name: Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl 2
detailed_description: Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl 2 lets you duke it out with the biggest and best fighting character roster yet, including all new characters like SpongeBob SquarePants, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Squidward Tentacles, Jimmy Neutron, and more! Choose your favorite brawlers, master their unique move sets, and use all-new powerful Supers to land the finishing blow with friends or across a unique, roguelike player campaign! Featuring: • New Single-Player Campaign: Put your skills to the test as you fight to stop Danny Phantom archvillain Vlad Plasmius from taking over the Nickelodeon universe! • All-New Gameplay: New and revamped visuals meets new audio, animations, modes, stages, mechanics, taunts and move sets for all levels of play! • Cinematic Supers: Power up your fighters with incredible new animated supers to deal devastating blows to your opponents! • New & Improved Brawlers: Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl 2’s roster is better than ever, with even more variety in how each unique character plays. Battle with brand new Nickelodeon fighters as well as returning fan favorites!

_childDocuments_.review: The first game walked so this game could run a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ marathon.This is the perfect example of a sequel done right. If you can think of anything from the first game that needed improvement, this game has it covered. The characters all play wonderfully and their movesets are so well designed and creative, making each fighter a blast to play as. The stages look wonderful, and are flooding with detail, plus the myriad of competitive layouts add gameplay variety, the costumes are a massive step up, with 2 extra full costumes + 2 bonus shadow skins you can unlock for every fighter. The singleplayer content is nuts, featuring a super fun rougelike campaign that encourages replayability. Think of it like a souped up arcade mode with enemy horde battles and bosses mixed inbetween. The voice acting is not only even better this time around, but all the cute dialogue interactions and jokes included in the story mode are a joy to listen to, giving so much soul to all these beloved characters.All this, and I still haven't mentioned the real All-Star of the show, the Slime meter. To put it simply, this meter singlehandedly makes this game one of the most interesting and unique platform fighters out right now. It gives players of all skill levels an immense amount of options on top of the already packed movesets, making gameplay even more frantic and dynamic. Competitive players are going to have a blast with the many options that it opens up, but even if you're just a casual player who doesn't want to learn bursting, slime dashing, cancels, or EX Specials... you can simply save up your slime for each character's super move, which are very charming and feature so many cute references.My favorite aspect is that for the online... when it works, it works WONDERFULLY. I will warn that currently online does have some bugs currently and there will be an occasional softlock or disconnect, but aside from the occasional issues, the netcode is surprisingly solid!To list a few criticisms, the lack of replays is very strange, not being able to remap movement controls on all platforms sucks, and the game really needs Multi-man or an endless enemy horde mode.Overall, this game turned out way better than I think anyone expected, and I can't recommend it enough to people who love Nickelodeon or Platform Fighters!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, but I feel like there's a lot of harsh truths and reasonable concerns with it that are getting drowned out by the typical wave of public approval or disapproval I want to make clear.On the bright side, this game is much better designed than it's predecessor. My only real issue is I feel certain aspects of the movement could be faster, like it's predecessor, but the slower speed and better designed movements are overall a net positive that makes the game much more interesting than the Nair central that was NASB 1. Character movesets have gone from boring flavors of youtube highlight reel to actual archetypes and gameplans, and a lot of them like Plankton or Angry Beavers especially have that Ludosity flair to them that made Slap City so special. This doesn't come at the expense of combos or hype moments either, and the expansion of movesets and reintroduction of mechanics like shield breaking makes this super mechanically solid compared to how the average non-smash platform fighter tends to give characters less options in their moveset like Rivals.  The slime meter is also an amazing inclusion most people are probably wondering why nobody else tried yet.Additionally, the online is great, the singleplayer is... not necessarily my thing, but at least probably the most fun platformer fighter single player aside from Subspace Emissary I've played due to trying to give the gameplay loop some extra meat with the roguelike item systems and pathing, and the visuals stand out as not amazing but great. Some characters look incredible like El Tigre or Ren and Stimpy, whereas there are a lot of assets that just feel crusty like Zim's render or Danny's model.The flaws: I could not blame someone for not wanting to support this on principle. Taking the money of both a full priced previous entry and DLC and effectively running to make a sequel that has another $50 price tag is painful. It's especially frustrating because this feels like the game that 1 should have been, so as much as I'd love to ask people to try it and hope the game stays alive, I could never say feeling scammed is wrong. Similarly, it has some release bugs and jank. I personally have not run into any gamebreaking ones, but for a list of the most notable ones:- No explicit way to rebind controls in single player (it uses the last profile you configured to P1)- Online will constantly and randomly boot me from lobbies during the matchmaking part. Not during matches, but I usually have to repeatedly attempt to get into matches until it finally works properly.- Unranked options are not good. It's a lot like smash where you just don't have any sort of executive control over what kind of maps or rules you'll be dealing with, which isn't bad as it's own thing but I believe there should always be an equivalent 1v1 queue for both ranked and unranked.- The training mode is way better than any other platform fighter I've tried in a lot of areas, yet has utterly bizarre blindspots. No way to force the AI to do specific actions (jump, run, shield, dodge) and I'm not sure if I'm missing something but even on characters with specific gimmicks the character-specific options just do not seem to open. It might be reserved to only a couple of characters and just not apply to the ones I've tried, but considering the characters I've tried have their own mechanics, like Zim, I would call that a flaw.Overall, I think you do get what you paid for if you're coming into it fresh, but for someone who played 1 it'd be a really hard sell and I wouldn't blame you for it. I'm hoping this game can survive till the point where sales can make it more manageable or something nice like a discount for 1 owners could be worked out.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is Fair Play Labs second attempt at a brawl; it is definitely a step in the right direction; the game play feels much smoother this time around, and the combat feels very much like Smash itself; however, there is something new here that changes the Smash gameplay, which we were all used to up a bit.That being the slime o'meter, a gameplay addition that slowly fills up overtime during combat that allows you to strengthen base moves and/or completely fill up for a “final smash” rather than everyone fighting over a smash ball.The game also has a nice attempt at a campaign mode, which is surprisingly good. It's sort of like a brawl roguelike with randomly generated paths (the maps themselves you'll fight on aren’t randomly generated, though), but that’s expected and probably for the best. The maps themselves, though, are beautifully detailed and filled with small references here and there.I also noticed that there is a fair bit of dialogue here; however, you won’t get to see it all if you only play one brawler. Each character has dialogue lines when talking to characters from their respective series or unique dialogue with bosses or NPCs.There’s also a returning arcade mode from the first game, although this time around we have branching paths we can choose after each match, letting you choose who you’ll fight or what minigame you’ll do. This new arcade mode also has mini bosses as well.There’s also a single-player boss gauntlet mode, allowing you to take on all bosses one after the other. I haven’t really played this yet.The online multiplayer unfortunately seems dead. I’ve tried numerous times to get a game in any of the vs modes but couldn’t find a single one, which is very unfortunate as this game definitely has a lot of potential. EDIT correction  there is an contingent of players online however you have to change your region most players seem to be in the USA region i got a lot of matches doing this.I now want to address some concerns.I’ve seen a lot of people very dissuaded from the game due to its price tag, as the first game was much cheaper, and while I can understand that perspective as someone who doesn’t like buying a lot of new games due to their $100+ asking prices nowadays, I have to admit I can sort of understand why this is 50 dollars. There is so much more effort put into the production of this game; the first one felt very cheap, jank, and stiff; however, the second entry is far more polished and completely remade from the ground up; the move sets have mostly been tinkered and changed, and the level designs have also been remade.With the added campaign and the depth of it, I can see why they’re asking for this price. The game has a lot more depth and a much higher budget this time around, and, to be honest, $50 is nothing compared to what most triple AAA developers are asking for a bug-ridden, unfinished game at launch, and at least you’re getting a game with no microtransactions like Multiverses, which will easily see you pay over $50 if you want to unlock anything fast.The complaint I'm probably most sympathetic to though is the removal of some previous fighters, which I do agree does stink. I don’t mind them removing some and replacing them with new characters from their series, i.e., Hey Arnold and/or Jimmy Neutron, but the removal of Cat Dog and Oblina now means there are no representatives for these particular series.I do hope that in further DLC (if we get a season 2) they add either these two characters back or a character from either series and hopefully two more from Nickelodeon series that don’t have representation yet.All in all, the game is probably one of the best smashlikes out there right now, and I honestly recommend getting it on sale. It's way better than the Janky first game, and if you’re a reoccurring smash player like myself, then this game will feel much more at home for you than the first game.Note: The game does have some small bugs, but I haven’t encountered anything major or game-breaking yet, so hopefully these will get patched out eventually.All n all i give this game a 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to see games like this come out, since I know they will be fantastic, and this one definitely is. It's probably the closest I've seen to my dream fighting game, a unification of Smash's movement and the mechanical complexity of trad fighters like Street Fighter or Guilty Gear. It's got meter, supers, ♥♥♥♥♥♥' Roman Cancels, the works. The production quality is far better than the first entry, which, while good, had a permeating stench of shovelware to it. Now all it needs is a functional training mode and a combo counter (seriously, why the hell do platform fighters never have combo counters in normal play, that ♥♥♥♥ is fighting game 101)The problem is that people just seem to refuse to give a ♥♥♥♥ about non-Smash platform fighters, regardless of how much they improve upon Smash's gameplay or how strong their character lineup is. Whether that's a testament to the closemindedness of the Smash community or Smash's sheer quality is up to you, but, with what seems to be the end of the Smash series, or at least a very long hiatus that will likely never see the series return to its former glory, new platformer fighters like this, Fraymakers, and the upcoming Rivals 2 can finally break their way out into popularity.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good; but way too expensive. Imagine having such a massive flop that was NASB 1 and then expecting people to A: Come back to the NASB series to begin with, and then B: Charge an already weak and wary fanbase 50 DOLLARS for a mediocre party game that is too competitive for it's own good. Most people don't play platform fighters for the competitive aspect, some normal-ass drunk college kids aren't going to understand how to slime cancel, or do anything remotely satisfying for that matter (I'd say the game is harder to pick up than something like Smash, and is just generally lacking in "party-game-esque" content). Little kids who pick up this game to play as Spongebob after a long day of school are going to get throttled by the measly 50 active players who are long-time veterans of the genre and find slime canceling to be a cool gimmick, those are the only people who would play this game. Almost every game they strap into, even in casual, will be an almost guaranteed loss. Trust me, I've played hundreds of hours of various platform fighters at high ranks (including this game) and I can tell that the majority of people who play the game know what they're doing, at least somewhat.  It sucks the game was basically dead on arrival because it is actually good. They should have went the MultiVersus route and made it FTP with microtransactions. 50 bucks is insane, if ur going to buy at all, buy at a massive discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a huge step up in every way from the first game. It looks better, moves better, sounds better and is a great platform fighter for any fan of the genre.The game has shifted more towards Smash Bros mechanics while maintaining it's own unique spin on things. Shields and throws are more akin to Smash while teetering on edges and arial strong attacks remain.A new spin on things that I love is the Slime Mechanic which is a very versatile new addition. Using a Slime Meter which builds up on hit and being hit you can cancel moves, save yourself from death (akin to an anime fighter Burst) as well as power-up your attacks among other things. Slime gives the player a very valuable resource which they must think on what to spend it on and where.The game has a surprisingly fun single player content for those who don't want to invest loads of time into getting better at the competitive side of things. The Story mode has a rougelite element to it which means you can give your character unique abilities on a playthrough to make each experience unique. There's a break the slime balloons (basically break the targets) that is different for every character and a breezy Arcade mode for those who just want to sink 10 minutes every now and then per character.If I was talking about this game 2 months ago I could say that the online was a well built but only mildly active game. Today I have to caution that this is a discord game for online play. Even using crossplay which is a lovely addition I struggle to find games and when I do it's often against new players who probably won't have a great experience with even mildly experienced players. It's a shame because 99% of the time when you play a game it is as smooth as butter, one of the best online fighting game experience I've had. It does show that you do often need an absurd player base so that those remaining after launch are enough to sustain the online. Join a Discord group and have fun.This game has eaten a good amount of my time and I've enjoyed just about every moment with it. It's rough around the edges but the foundation is very solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Ha ha. Funny Sponge Go BrrrrrrrrrrrrrWe wanted SpongeBob in Smash, we got Smash in SpongeBob.Smash gave us memories, but this is gonna give us memes.I've been having some of the most fun l've ever had in a platform fighter while playing this. The devs really improved from the first game where it doesn't feel like a simple cash grab. The first game feels like a tech demo next to this one, like the level of improvement is kind of incredible all around. One thing I liked about this game is that not only does it feel like an improvement over the original, but it also feels like a true evolution of Ludosity's original platform fighter Slap City.The effort put into these games is very much apparent. I adored all of the fun little references and faithfulness to the characters' personalities and their source material. Nickelodeon fans will have a blast for sure. This game got all the little things missing from the first game like story mode, voice acting, but most importantly, smoothed out the fighting mechanics. Honestly a few cut characters is a small price to pay for a massively better experience. Proof you don't need to abandon a series just because the game doesn't blow up.I think the biggest problem with platform fighters is we always go into them with smash in mind and judge everything based on what smash did/does. I feel we need to see these games as their own individual games with their own things to offer, it will definitely help you appreciate them alot more. Hopefully they keep the hype train going and not let it die like the original game. All in all; A really great game with fun characters, interesting mechanics, creative stages, and amusing game modes. The battles are fun, there’s good music and the moves don't feel generic. More fun with friends. Got what I hoped for and  more. The pricing is odd and some of the removed characters do bum me out, but still, great game. Cant wait for what the future holds for it. Definitely recommend, specially on a sale.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far one of the BEST non-Smash mascot platform fighters I've played in a long time. The Slime mechanic gives me PlayStation All-Stars vibes, but without it being required to KO an opponent... so good job devs! I like that the Jukebox feature returned, because this game's soundtrack is also leagues above the original's (you cannot tell me the main theme isn't inspired by that one Dragon Bal Super song, it just sounds like it so much). And the campaign... my goodness, the campaign... that has scratched my Subspace Emissary itch that I've had for so long now (and dare I say, it's BETTER than SSBU's "World of Light" campaign). The voice acting makes the characters feel like they occupy the same space, especially in the campaign, which is another thing Smash really doesn't do all that well... again, good job devs.Now, there are SOME things I did NOT like this game doing. For starters, the roster: Yes, you have a solid selection here, but some of the cuts from Game 1 are incredibly baffling (Lucy but no Lincoln? Where's the other two Turtles? Why are Powdered Toastman and Hugh Heutron dangled in front of me as NPCs when they were playable previously? And why pray tell is Grandma Gertie here but not Helga?). I love the newcomers and even how the veterans got reworked, but those omissions still sting even though I know game development is not simply "copy-and-paste" when making a sequel.Secondly, there's one major flaw in the gameplay I noticed during my time with it:Momentum does NOT carry after jumping from platform to platform!I'm hoping this is something that can be fixed in a patch, but it sucks having my sprint motion not carry over after landing from a jump. It has stumped me more times than I care to admit.Aside from minor audio bugs, the game is FAR from a mixed bag. To say it's middling would be a lie. It is such a robust improvement over the original that it's apparent far more resources were pumped into it. I do enjoy the way the Campaign is structured, and really hope more platform fighters improve upon this concept... especially with character interactions (I'm sorry Smash players, but it's important for ANY CROSSOVER to make it feel like characters occupy the same space and aren't just simply standing next to each other with no awareness).I'd give this game a 7 out of 10 at the moment. With the momentum issue and audio bugs ironed out, I'd boost this to an 8. Here's hoping the devs come through on these two bits, because this game IS GREAT so far. Please keep doing whatever it was you were doing during development post-launch. Please.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Be wary, this game has been on a very sharp downward trend in player count. The most recent averages have been less than 200 player peaks, which means there's likely to be times of days you're fighting a lot of the same people or having a hard time finding people in your rank. Everything I said about the quality & content of the game itself still stands, but it's likely you'll need to join a community for the game (like its Discord channel) to find reliable matches.---This game makes the original All-Star Brawl feel like an unfinished tech demo. This game absolutely oozes charm with every single attack, voice-line, & menu.Despite the original already feeling good mechanically for competitive players, there was no staying power for casuals. This has been changed perfectly with the new single player modes, one of which being a full rouge-like campaign. Also, there's great systems in place to unlock new skins, borders, & icons to have a sense of progression & completion for those not interesting in playing ranked. Of course, on the competitive side, the addition of the slime meter for cancels, boosted moves, & supers adds an absurd amount of depth to every match. Slime radically changes the way the game is played in a way I've never felt in a platform fighter before and I absolutely love it.The online has some of the best net-code I've ever seen in a platform fighter. From the 40 or so games I've played launch day with a friend & vs randoms, I haven't noticed a single bit of lag. No eaten inputs, no stutter, no visual confusion from rollback, just straight game.In the day & age of free-to-play smashlikes, the pricetag can seem intimidating, however if you enjoy platform fighters, you will not be disappointed. With all the new characters, reworked movesets, significantly higher visual polish, new modes, new mechanics, & better online, this absolutely feels like a warranted sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: While the first game was really fun, there's no doubt that its launch was quite rough. It got better over time, though unfortunately most people moved on. NASB2 instantly is a massive upgrade from the first title, giving it more refined gameplay, drastically improving the visuals, and best of all -- single player content, which the first game absolutely lacked.Arcade mode is actually much better this time around, and the campaign layout being rouge-like gives a lot of incentives for multiple runs. With bosses, more modes, minigames, the game definitely feels like a complete product this time around.A lot of people may be upset over the cuts -- but keep in mind that this game had a limited development time and they focused on reworking pretty much every character and spent time adding more modes.I do think the costume pack price is quite hefty, and the game could be WAY better optimized on other platforms, but NASB2 on Steam is absolutely a great game and I think those who didn't like the first game would probably enjoy this one a lot more.

_childDocuments_.review: Massive, and I mean MASSIVE step up from the first game, but a few key issues that need addressing.  +  Slime meter is a groundbreaking mechanic for platform fighters and has been implemented incredibly well. –  Slime meter's capabilities are not explained at all by the game.      — You can spend a bar of meter to enhance special move in the game for a more powerful variant or to improve your recovery.     — You can use some meter to enhance your shield (meter gradually depletes while holding shield+slime) and make it temporarily unbreakable.     — You can spend a bar to cancel any move at any time whether it hits or not, allowing for some crazy movement options and mixup potential, and of course making the combo game immensely deep, dynamic, and creative.     — You can spend two bars of meter to burst like in GGST, cancelling all knockback and making you instantly actionable. +  Movement is simple and intuitive while still having massive depth through interactions with each character's unique movement options and how they interact with the slime meter. –  Character's movesets are not explained by the game, like at all.  E.g: Azula's side special can be angled down much like Bayonetta's Afterburner Kick (ABK) in Smash Ultimate, but it's never mentioned in her move list.  +  Rollback netcode! Yes, this game has rollback, crossplay between platforms, and dedicated regional servers for online play, and most of the time they work great. –  Ranked is mostly dead outside of the USA servers, likely in part because crossplay is off by default for some reason. +  Campaign! And it's actually pretty good, although could still use a lot of quality of life improvements. –  Probably the worst training mode I've ever seen. Worse than Smash Ultimate's, somehow.This is quite possibly the best core game system of any platform fighter on the market right now, but definitely held back by lots of weird bugs and a lack of quality of life features.However, it is very clear from reading the patch notes that the developers are dedicated to improving the game, going as far as to make core game engine changes to address core balance issues. One can only hope they direct some of that energy towards quality of life improvements so this game can grow an audience without frustrating its players and become the incredible game I know it can be.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game to recommend. It's buggy, mashy, and has a small player-base. But when it works, it works well. It has very fun mechanics that give you opportunities to freestyle reads and combos like crazy if you want. Often-times while playing you encounter a situation where you think "maybe this will work" and it likely will. It's very rewarding if you put up with all the flaws. Also it's fast and input heavy but not hard to control, which is hard to do and many other platform fighters feel less snappy/responsive. Most of the typical character archetypes are represented here with many creative liberties that spice up the game-play. The online is also good(when it works). It has bugs and queue times can be long due to the smaller player-base but I always end up finding people. Worth checking out for any platform fighter enthusiast.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying this: If you're having trouble finding an online match, there's a Discord server called "Nick Brawl Grinders" dedicated to matchmaking and general chatting. I highly recommend joining it if you're new to the game.As for the game itself, I absolutely adore it despite all its faults. THIS is the kind of Nicktoons-themed platform fighter I've been wanting to see for years. It plays well, looks nice, has a solid roster, innovates the genre in a fun way with the Slime Meter, and has plenty of single-player content to keep even the biggest loners busy for a while. It also has an incredibly fun roguelike campaign mode, featuring the first original story for a Nicktoons crossover game in 15 years. This is where a lot of my hours of play went into.Yes, there are some bugs here and there, but I can look past a lot of them because I know this was made by a small development team that did the best with what they had. It's a labor of love by fans of the source material and I will gladly support their work as much as I can, especially if it gets us a 3rd game with a better budget and more time to cook.Even this late into its life, I highly recommend giving this a shot if you haven't. It's frequently on sale, has a small but dedicated community, and (unlike a certain other IP-driven platform fighter) is available to play offline as long as you want, even well after support has stopped. There should be at least one last big patch on the way at the time I'm writing this. Pick up the game then if you're still unsure now.EDIT: The patch has been out since the start of November and it's fantastic. Many of the issues have been addressed and fixed, making this game the best it's ever been. This is THE time to give NASB2 a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing gameplay. There's so much room for creativity and self-expression, and the combo strings are endless feeling, especially at high level. Also hoping for a rework or tuning of the matchmaking system (not that I would even pretend to understand any of it myself lol). I say that because often times I am immediately matched with the same person that just left me or that I left after playing with them; I would like to see some sort of cooldown or something to avoid the instant rematches (it often leads to the opponent seeing it's me again, leaving, and then rejoining my lobby AGAIN and repeating until inevitably just settling to play more with each other, or waiting some amount of time before requeueing, which disrupts the vibe). It also can take a little longer than I'd like to find a match in general, only ever able to find matches in Ranked 1v1 -- only once or twice ever with Quickplay 1v1 lol. It could just be harder to find matches at higher ranks, and perhaps the online playerbase is mostly playing ranked or something, but I still feel it's a bit much and I should be able to find matches sooner much more regularly than what currently happens. Ultimate and Melee (the speed feels somewhere in the middle, which feels great in my opinion! It's no Smash Killer like lots of people meme it to be, but in all honesty Smash needs some actual competition, and this game could definitely fit the bill in time.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface, I love Smash Bros. Have played it competitively for years, and casually for years before that. I've played pretty much every platform fighter out there, including all sorts of Smash mods, fan games, and indie projects like Rivals.Nick All-Star Brawl 1 (NASB) was a cute little fighting game that I played for a few hours with friends and then never touched again. It was a fun premise with cool ideas, but clearly did not have the budget required to create a good game. Ultimately, it was mechanically shallow and characters tended to play pretty similarly.Fast-forward two (?) years and behold, Nick All-Star Brawl 2 (NASB2) appeared. In every possible way it improved over the original, from audio to visuals to mechanics, online, and singleplayer-content, NASB2 excels. Mechanically, it takes the tried-and-true formula established by Melee and refined by Project M and Rivals to create a game with so much depth that every character feels like a brand-new game. Case in point: I hopped into local play with a friend, and picked Donatello (they cut my mains from the previous game). I tried a couple of games of Reptar, and then went back to Donatello. I was having so much fun playing this one character (who is apparently low-tier), that I literally have not touched anyone else for the 4 hours I've played this game. There's so much versatility in every character's kit that I'm constantly discovering new ways to use moves, new combo routes, and new neutral tools, just playing ONE character. And this is just the beginning. As time goes on, platform fighters tend to gain more depth and complexity. I could probably just play Donatello for the next 100 hours and still feel like I've only scratched the surface of what he can do. I can't recommend this game more if you enjoy platform fighters like Smash Bros. The NASB2 team really outdid themselves with this game. Props to learning from the failures of the past game and the Smash-like genre as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Vast Oversights, But  PotentialI basically never write reviews but I feel compelled to here. The lack of movement binds being available is baffling to me and an incredible oversight, and there's definitely annoying bugs. But with that being said, the devs stated such fixes are incoming, and I don't want to let such overshadow a game with amazing potential once we get past these initial bugs. The quality and gameplay of this game is so much better than the first. I'll update this review after I play some more campaign, but it seems solid and better than most platform fighter offline content. But online play, and competitively, once you get past the bugs and are actually in a match, it's freakin' great. I'm addicted, I'm invested, and I want to see this game be the cross-play smash-like that we need.Additions I want to see the most are of course movement binds, autorun toggle, other flexibility toggles for controls, and BUG FIXES. But some personal stuff I'd love to see are:Crew battle options would be . A cross-platform friends list where you can see online status, invite, and follow and spectate (depending on settings)! A 3D replay viewer (ideally with timeline scrubbing) where we can change camera axis and everything (montages, clips, etc skyrocket in potential if we get a good replay tool). Also, for the ranked algorithm, I kind of want a good blend of per character elo, and overall elo, that makes the most sense to me. As a very experienced player in other platform fighters, I definitely want to see much better AI (note to devs: take a look at Brawlhalla AI implementations?). And for max difficulty to be much harder, dark souls hard, because I believe we should always have the option to be challenged, and everyone always has the ability to just not choose the higher difficulties.Quick section of bugs that need to be fixed and a couple suggestions:Needing cross-play option to be on even when you're on the same platform, to join rooms, cross-play option turning off itself, needing workarounds to use the controls you want in campaign and I've heard they can reset during runs, I've heard you can become soft locked as well but don't know if that's on PC, players should have no invincibility after they miss ultimate it's very annoying, rematch should be the first option after a game not the second, you should be able to edit lobby size while a lobby is still live, max lobby size could be higherOh I'll quickly say this, while at first the roster and character cuts did seem weird to me, I've learned I care about character movesets far more. I'll take movesets I love over characters I enjoy with mid movesets any day of the week. I don't even remember a lot about many of these shows, don't remember Avatar yet I'm in love with Korra's playstyle and moveset. So the same extends to the DLC characters for me, the names don't excite me but the playstyles definitely may.I could make this review far more thorough, and perhaps I will when I feel like it (unless character limit lol), but more than anything I'm writing this because I truly want people to give the devs a chance to fix some of these glaring issues, because gameplay wise, this is great. I'm sure we'll need balancing, move fixes and etc, but it's a blast. This game should  have shipped with the problems I mentioned even if it meant a delay. But it's here, and I'm hopeful that the sore spots will be addressed soon and this game becomes a casual and competitive mainstay.

_childDocuments_.review: *note: this is more for people looking wanting more out of the gameplay. if you're looking for a fun nickelodeon game to mess with friends or yourself and don't care about techincal stuff pick this upwhat if super smash bros melee didn't have directional influence? Nick all star 2 feels like it sets out to answer the question. This game is aggressively designed around letting you land combos to the point where it affects the design of bossfights and the single player rougelike mode. This might appeal to some, but I believe it comes with more issues than it's worth.Nick all star 2 has a roster of characters who feel the same as many characters from other games with a Nick coat of paint. A lack of creativity is in almost every moveset where if you removed the aesthetics of the character they'd be indistinguishable. A good goal for any fighting game is to have characters whose movesets are unique to stand out amongst itself and against it's competition. Nick doesn't really have this. Alot of these cartoon characters tend to have a variety of normal attacks that the audience will have seen before in many games.  This issue could be excused if the system's mechanics allowed generic characters to shine, but it doesn't. Hitstun is a term referring to the momentary freeze a player will experience upon being attacked. Usually this is done for flair or pacing, but in platform fighters it will be slightly exaggerated to prevent an instant recovery from attacks that launch the other player. Nick 2 takes this concept and runs a football field with it. You WILL wait for your velocity to reach 0 for nearly every attack whether it pops you up for a juggling opportunity or if its intended to KO. In other platform fighters, this is often something you can influence greatly by tilting the stick in a direction you'd like to push yourself. This prevents your aggressor from getting into a position to land a follow-up attack. You also often can press a button to quickly regain normal control of your character, preventing them from tumbling forever. Nick 2 barely allows for DI and disallows you to regain control until the hitstun has completely ended. This results in a snowballing effect. My successful matches against other players always resulted in going for combos, and my failures often resulted in me trying to do another strategy. If one player lands a combo starter, the other player will be unable to respond (besides a rare combo breaker) and have to eat all the damage they need to take. This means getting poked once can you leave you on Death's door. Combos in fighting games are fun but Nick 2's systems don't seem to be aware of how far they can go. Getting a very strong combo in a fighting game often requires you to burn through resources (Tekken 8 with wall crashing/heat), be very low on health (Street Fighter 6 with critical arts), or require a ton of setup to really work. Nick 2 allows for these nearly game ending combos off of random pokes. If that wasn't already tilting the balance towards offense blocking attacks near a ledge instantly stuns you. There's no ability to get a big jump off a ledge, meaning your options are extremely limited if you manage to get back to the ledge. If you preform a recovery move onto the stage, the endlag is longer than in other platform fighters. These choices are often present in platform fighters to prevent a steamroll from happening once one player is knocked off the main platform. Nick 2 removes all of this to allow combo based strategies to run wild. This also means attacks are often incredibly fast and easy to chain into themselves. I will not be going into movesets in depth as that's outside of the scope of this review, but it does trivialize bossfights if you're playing as an average speed character. Take Rocko for example, his light up attack has his brain come out as a gag, but it's super fast. You can run under a boss and keep doing that move to take away nearly all their health  before their first attack is done. Vlad Plasimus, the final boss, is a complete joke specifically to strategies like this. Campaign's main challenge are these bossfights...You can see the issue. By forcing their characters to have very fast moves, the game trivialized. (Side note: I played through the game as Donatello once I realized this because I wanted to have some fun, and he's probably one of the least combo focused characters. he's also one of the worst competitvely lol)Some bonus modes of hitting balloons and training dummies. There's a rogue like campaign but as mentioned earlier it's made very easy due to how attacks are handled. In conclusion: IF You like NICK and have no wanting to get good - no,  at this game, pick it up on sale. There's not alot of content but it is a great time. However, if you want to practice and learn the mechanics you will quickly realize that doing anything to get a combo started is the only way to win, since defensive options are kaput and other offensive strategies such as playing with slow big attacks is pointless compared to the ease of combos. It's not a very depthful game as a result. It's like a Mortal Kombat game for platform fighters. If that appeals to you, get it. If not you won't find anything else here.

That was a rough gem, and i felt "cheated" when they announced NASB 2 instead of making NASB 1 somewhat a normal game, yes it was that bad. NASB 2 is what NASB 1 should have been from the start:+ NASB 2 has a functional campaign mode in form of rougelite that you can unlock characters gradually. _childDocuments_.review: -This is Fair Play Labs' second attempt at a brawler-style game. It is all-in-all a step in the right direction after playing the first game. The gameplay is much smoother. Combat and levels, for better or for worse, becomes quite similiar to a smash you can get on a non-nintendo console. It eventually got to a point where I refer to Jenny as a Meta-Knight agility fighter, Lucy Loud as Pokemon Trainer with 3 mode mids, Riptar as a better Bowser heavyweight, Jimmy Neutron's basement is Pokemon Statium, and a temple-like stage, etc. There's an sub optimal target smash too.  The game has clear inspiration from Smash with two major exceptions. One improvement is the similarities in light/heavy/special attacks across all characters. A lot of fighting games seem to give character all different movesets, but no matter which character you choose in Brawl they are all similiar. Where they differ is in how well those movesets string together, like a fighting game where you go light-light-heavy-heavy. Spongebob prefers going special-light to a heavy, while Lucy Loud might prefer doing heavy to rebounc an enemy to special light to string into offense. This was really fun to explore without the frustration of finding a fighting game character can't do this move. Another improvement is the slime-o-meter. Rather than a smash ball to fight, there is a meter that slowly fills up overtime during combat to give you option to strengthen base moves or fill a "final smash". This can be amusing or strategic for longer games.-The game also features two single player modes: campaign and arcade. In campaign, you enter a brawl rogue-lite where you go through 12 matches up to 3 times on randomly generated maps. Matches can be minigames, upgrades, shops, enemy mobs, or CPU brawl opponents, the latter two being the most common. At the end of each map, you face a boss with a patterned moveset. If you lose, you start over but get to keep green and purple slime to buy upgrades (WHICH YOU ABSOLUTELY SHOULD DO EVEN IF YOU DIE ON THE FIRST STAGE AS THE GAME IS VERY UNFORGIVING AND AUTOSAVES). (You can also save and quit if you're doing poorly to restart the match). Arcade is a mini version of this, but you only have 12 stages to fight CPU bosses and Vlad Plasmius as the final boss. In the campaign, Vlad Plasmius from Danny Phantom has kidnapped various Nickelodeon characters and wants to brainwash them to do his bidding. It's up to the brawler and the Clockwork, a time-manipulating character from the same franchise,to stop Vlad. I write this not to give spoilers but to note that you should ideally play characters from the same franchise (Danny Phantom or Ember) to get unique dialogue you would not get otherwise.-Single player matches give the opportunities to face CPU opponents. You can do this brawler style or a gauntlet style. thee CPU opponent is generally fun. However, note that it is still not a human and there are times you can cheese the same move and win. The CPU tends to block anytime a projectile is thrown, so you can use this to your advantage. Spongebob has this weird move where you can special light and lock your opponents in a near infinite damage distributor. And sometimes the CPU will just jump into a pit and die or just hang on a ledge waiting for you to hit them and die. -Online multiplayer is OK. Switch to USA. Reviews and Reddit posit that Europe is dead, or at least everyone migrates to the US. There's few toxic players or people vying to be t1. It's just good fun from what I played.. -As for the $50 price tag.... considering all the fun this is and how it basically doubles the fun of 1, it's well worth the price.I got this on sale, and would recommend getting this the moment it's on sale, even if it's just $10 off. The first game felt like polished IP insertion into a popular game genre, like a lot of Nickelodean games. This feels like a game I could continue to play and repeatedly challenge friends to play if they can ever put down Smash. Released in 2023, the game having $50 price tag is in a weird place. In one regard, it's $10 lower than the AAA price then. But that's also $20 less than the AAA price in 2024, at which is which this game is well worth the value.You can feel the effort the developers put into this, and there are plenty less bugs here than in the previous game. And I cannot stress this enough; it is a game you can easily sink dozens of hours into, and feel satisfied sinking a dozen hours into. -One criticism I have is the game is not optimized and I wish there were a way to lower settings. I am playing on a mid-high 2021 gaming PC, and the game still takes a while to load and lags during loading. The same issue is on the switch.Gameplay is fine. -Another criticism that only matters to those who played the first game is that some previous fighters were removed. Hugh Neutron was removed but his NPC is in the Powerup menu, which hurts more when you see they kept his animations. This is only something to be upset over if you played the previous games. -I give this game an 8.5/10. I really want to recommend this, and I spent a while writing this review to get my thoughts out. There's things I like about this but don't love. It's probably me not enjoying the Viacom era nick starting in the 2010s, it's a part of me that's a little disappointed it went from being original in 1 to being a smashlike in 2, but a very good smashlike. Buy it if it's on sale or a friend wants to play. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that Steam's "Would you recommend this game to others Y/N?" system is a bit too black and white for what I want to say here. While I do think the game could be considered "good" in a sense it is clear that this game is dead on arrival. Also, I have not played the original so this review will be in a vacuum from that. Also I had no expectations going in. Did anyone actually unironically expect this game to be good? I don't think so.Probably the biggest part. As the title for this section suggests the roster isn't very good. There were cuts from the last game which I am fine with the IDEA of, but who they chose to cut and who to keep is baffling. Why isn't Sandy here? Why don't we have all 4 turtles, but ****ing April is still in? You cut Lincoln, the protagonist of the Loud House and kept Lucy? The newcomers are also a very mixed bag. You do have good picks like Jimmy Neutron, Squidward, and the Angry Beavers, but they also traded Leo and Mikey for Raph and Donnie. Azula is a strange choice considering that there were like 2-4 Avatar characters that should have taken priority. Ember? I mean... Vlad was right there. Bosses also being playable characters is not a foreign idea, especially with Vlad's smaller size compared to the other bosses and moveset potential. Gerald and Grandma Gertie? Aren't there better characters for Hey Arnold like... I dunno... Arnold himself? "But he's a pacifist!" So are Iron Giant (Multiversus) and Isabelle (SSBU) yet they still showed up to throw hands in their respective games. Oh and your telling me that dlc characters have been shown? Well lets see... Zuko and Mr. Krabs good, good,... Uncle Iroh and Rocksteady!? Who came up with this roster, an AI program? Now I for one like the addition of an oddball character but there are just to many strange picks here. There were more important and more fan favorite characters that just are not here. All so that they can make a couple of unfunny roster jokes. Which is literally the whole reason that Garfield is here. "Oh but they own the rights to him now!" I do not care. Garfield is not a nicktoon. At least TMNT had a couple of shows made specifically for the network before their inclusion. Garfield was never funny, neither are the millennials who meme him. tl;dr: The roster kinda sucks which is a shame considering the roster is the biggest draw for a crossover game.Holy cow, There are enough bugs here to rival a Bethesda game. Not on the level of something like F76 or starfield, but wew. I have had my game soft lock just by trying to change my character in the campaign. Dialog boxes in the campaign will get confused and display the wrong character while someone is talking. I have had, after an offline singles mach, my character indefinitely fall in the results screen void while the camera was zoomed out to an almost hilarious degree. Sartana's ai just giving up 3/4ths the way in her fight. Among other things. Selling this for 50$ is a move that only someone like Mr. Krabs could make. This game is barely worth 29.99 let alone the actual price tag. I pray every night for the poor suckers that bought the 80$ version of this. Also, DLC! Uh question. Weren't those costumes in the costume dlc supposed to be rewards for completing arcade mode with the characters? And you're now selling them to me for 20$? The ♥♥♥♥??? Hell, some of the characters' costumes aren't even worth any price tag. Mainly Spongebob's, April's, Reptar's and the Beavers'. Also 20$!? WTF? I could get an entire indie game or two with that money! And a season pass day 1 as well? Screw me with a rusty sippy cup. I just know some executive crap is behind this mess.One of the biggest draws for this came compared to the original is the voice acting. It's... a mixed bag. A lot of the characters have weird line delivery. Some don't even sound like they're trying (I'm looking at you Aang, Jimmy, and Korra). Squidward's voice actor sounded like he was struggling to do the role so much that at one point I thought they used an ai voice for him. There is still a good amount of actors who sound like they're trying though. The writing also sucks. Even if all the voice actors were at the top of their game, the dialog sucks. Characters, most of the time, will not acknowledge another character's presence If they are not from the same show. Like, you'd think that Jimmy would have a nice chat with Nora about science, but no. The only exceptions to this are Bosses, Clockwork, and a one time per character interaction with Gary where the majority of the cast will be surprised that a snail meow'd. The dialogue that is written for these interactions however feel awkward and disjointed. Characters feel like they can see the other guy's lips moving but have to make a guess at what their saying. Clockwork says "TMI" at one point, which for a wise, otherworldly figure such as himslf is out of character.After all that complaining, there is but one thing to ask. A question that some gamers say is the defining factor in a game. That question is: . Yes. Yes it is. The gameplay loop is solid. The characters are fun to play, not to mention are generally on point with a few notible exceptions, one example of which being Garfield. Such a fat, lazy character should not be rushdown. Perhaps a more defensive playstyle would be more fitting for the character? It is fun to use Jimmy's air down strong to bounce around like in the movie. It's fun to switch between Daggett and Norbert and having the non active brother assist you. It's fun to see a heavy character that doesn't completely suck (Plankton) This is why it's so hard for me to decide whether or not I would or wouldn't recommend. Because there IS something here. I just don't think that most people will see it.-The advertising for this game is abysmal. The only reason I remembered that this was coming out was because an L.S. Mark video of this game showed up in my youtube feed-Where Multiversus felt like it was made by people that would rather be making a moba, this game feels like it was made by people who would rather be developing the actual super smash bros melee itself than this. Case and point half of Gertie's moveset is literally just a ripoff of Captain Falchon's and wave-dashing is an intended mechanic.-Whoever composed the music deserves a raise. Particularly noteworthy tracks include the loudhouse graveyard stage music, the tremorton stage music, and the minigame music.-Graphically the game looks pretty alright all things considered.-The campaign mode being rougelike is an intresting way to do a crossover platform fighter story mode and a good alternative for one that does not have the budget for an actual Subspace Emisary-esqe campaign.-The online  I've had a few matches where I was able to play normally and I have had it break and freeze on me multiple times. My internet sucks, but it doesn't suck that bad for the latter to happen. 6/10Overall this game is the textbook definition of a mixed bag. I think the concept of a Nickelodeon platform fighter could work, but I don't think the people who are calling the shots on this project are what it needs to work. Again, the roster picks are weird, the bugs are plentiful, the writing and the delivery on the voice acting sucks, the online is unstable at times and the experience itself is overpriced. And again the game does have its merits. The majority of this review being negative is mostly because it's easier to say the things you DON'T like about something than it is to say the things you DO like. I just hope we get a good Nick platform fighter one day.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl, I got so excited when it was first revealed. A Nickelodeon crossover fighting game akin to Super Smash Bros. definitely sounded like a dream come true for someone like me who has loved both since childhood. And while the first game wasn't considerably bad, there were a LOT of stuff holding it back. For one, there were NO items or voice-acting at launch, and considering the single-player content, outside of the arcade mode, there was NOTHING for casual single-player people like me. NASB was an unfortunate case of too much hype, in my opinion.But when it comes to Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl 2, every single problem I had with the game has been addressed, fixed, AND improved. The graphics as well had a massive overhaul as well, looking much more sleek and stylish. The single-player content on offer is a major improvement; while the arcade mode returns, we also have a mini-game mode much like the Target Test in Smash Bros, as well as a boss rush mode, AND an amazing rogue-like campaign mode where you face off against main Danny Phantom bad guy Vlad Plasmius. While the roster this time around has seen some considerable (and some devastating, in my opinion) cuts, the new additions definitely make up for it, with some underappreciated series like El Tigre and the Angry Beavers making their grand return here, with more characters periodically coming out as DLC, such as the recently released Mr. Krabs. The voice-acting is another highlight, with a lot of the famous voice talents such as Tom Kenny, Frank Welker, and Clancy Brown (just to name a few) delivering some of their best performances, especially in the campaign's story.If there are any complaints to discuss, most of the issues come from a technical standpoint. There are some visual glitches that, while they don't completely ruin the game, do cause a hindrance to the experience. The audio mixing can also be a big problem, especially in the campaign. You could barely hear some of the voice clips over the loud, blaring music. Other than that, the game is still very much functional.Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl 2 is a major improvement over the first in every single way imaginable. If you're in the mood for a good Smash Bros-style platform fighting game, or a good Nickelodeon crossover title, then this is definitely a high recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very well crafted from a general standpoint. Every character has a unique and fun move set, full of interesting mechanics and solid general feel, and they all represent the shows they originate from pretty well. It visually looks quite nice, outside of the super moves and victory animations which often look strangely unfinished. The sound design is solid, and the voice lines from characters strike the balance of being fun and giving them a personality without being too frequent or repetitive to the point of being annoying. The soundtrack is perfectly fine, although none of the songs really stand out as being particularly memorable or catchy.The casual-oriented content is where this game really shines. Booting up games to mess around with friends is a lot of fun, even based solely on the absurdity of being able to "lasagna install" or "squid-dash". Stages offer good variety, although several of them feel overly large and empty, particularly with how far the blast zones sometimes extend beyond the screen border. Items feel a bit too imbalanced, with some like the anchor being able to solo an opponent for multiple stocks, but overall they do offer a nice change to gameplay when you feel like turning them on.In terms of solely singleplayer content, I think this game has the best campaign mode of any platform fighter. The roguelike structure makes it fun to do repeated runs, even if there aren't all that many variables, and there was clearly a lot of effort put in. Every character is fully voiced, including NPCs and bosses, and generally speaking the presentation is solid. There are some glitches, like some of the enemies behaving oddly when interacting with grabs or supers, and the cutscenes being oddly loud to the point of unfortunately drowning out the dialogue audio. However, the simple structure of platform fighter mechanics with a series of unique challenges, combined with ability to earn random power-ups that have a genuine impact on how you approach things, makes this mode easily the most fun I've had in this game.Unfortunately, it seems to be the online where corners had to be cut, and I just have to hope it gets fixed in the future. I've had genuinely baffling experiences, like my opponent having an invisible clone who counted as a third player that technically won the match, my meter not getting consumed when it should, animations not playing correctly, and other bizarre scenarios that, as far as I can tell, only occur when playing online. Even ignoring glitches, the connection is often poor, and lobbies have to be closed and reopened after every match in order to keep playing with friends. When playing on ranked, it feels like there isn't a great matchmaking algorithm, as I have generally ended up against players far beyond my skill level, despite me being at a low rank. The stock count being 4 feels too high, as matches drag on, particularly against defensive players (which seems to be the most common type of player to encounter). The rematch button being the default option is annoying, as I've ended up having to fight the same annoying player again because I hit it by accident before, and there's no time to cancel if they've already chosen the same option. When playing on quickplay, it's rare to end up queued with another player at all, which I imagine is just due to a small player base that primarily prefers a more competitive format, but it's still unfortunate. In general, if you want to get this game primarily to play online, I can't recommend it in its current state.Overall, I can at least say that the good outweighs the bad in NASB2. You can play as Squidward.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a week since free play weekend and I still have no idea what to think of this. On one hand, it does what it needs to do with some big and small setbacks from a casual perspective, thus the recommendation. On the other, there are several reasons why Super Smash Brothers is as big as it is and why no game really replicates that as far as I am aware.Here's how I'd put it, if you don't have high expectations and one of those low expectations is a game... , then it's good if you get it on sale. My opinion here on price is mainly because I usually don't pay full price for any game with my own money at all outside of indies, especially with digital games, but this game in particular just isn't one I would want to pay full price regardless. Personally, if it wasn't for the fact that far better games exist that I want to get, I might just get it used on Playstation or on sale here on Steam. The are reasons for this.The control scheme combined with the mechanics was my biggest gripe with this, as it is not as pick up and play like Smash. I was able to get the controls to be closer to Smash, but it still doesn't feel as right as a Smash game; doesn't matter as the default is forced in the campaign until you are able to change your character in the hub. Since I'm talking about controls, might as well mention that this version only has the icons for Xbox controls. This definitely won't affect players using Xbox controllers, but I used a DualSense controller for most of my playthrough, which makes things really weird, especially the face buttons on the default control scheme. There is not even the option to use Nintendo controller icons in the pc version which is quite baffling for the type of game that this is (fyi I didn't use a Nintendo controller during the weekend, so maybe they are there and I haven't seen them at all).The roster is a bit odd. Garfield is especially odd, since he never had a Nickelodeon show at all. Like, I know Garfield is now owned by Viacom and thus Nickelodeon, but I personally remember Garfield having a show on Cartoon Network as well as just being it's own thing separate from Nickelodeon, so it's quite the odd placement. There's also a bigger focus on older shows that have stopped airing (prior to 2010), but I only have this concern for both children who may of not had the opportunity to watch most of the shows featured and the lack of Harvey Beaks which was strangely a show that I think should of been included despite never watching it in my life (maybe those who watched it can chime in here idk). Can't say I dislike it though, especially since the former concern in terms of rep has been minimized because of the existence of streaming services and the general internet. The characters that I tried were fun as well, regardless of the issues this game has and if I recognized them or not (Ember was the only one I didn't prior to this game and I still had fun playing as her in the campaign).To at least give the game another positive, it has quite a unique campaign, being somewhat of a roguelike and all. While it is short, it was an okay use of my time and the inclusion of it is nice.Like I said, it's good if you get it on sale (or used on consoles). Preferably, if you never had the chance to play a fighting game, play Super Smash Bros Ultimate first or any Smash game for that matter. Super Smash Bros for 3DS is how I got into fighting games in the first place. However, this game was good for the 9+ hours I played it during the free play weekend. Just don't go in with high expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm no expert in platform fightings, NASB 1 was literally my first and only one before this one. I enjoyed it, so decided to give it's sequel a shot when it was on sale.At first, everything seems great. More voicelines, better music, improved stages (except Tommy's playground, I miss it), more mechanics for characters, and most importantly - Campaign mode with bosses. But then you run into some issues...1. Technical stuff. Easily the worst part of NASB 2 is it's big poll of bugs and weird limitations. Characters can sometimes ignore inputs, especially during platforming in Campaign. You always have to start the Campaign with default key settings and only switch them when you save Patrick and lose after. The main menu sometimes gets laggy and doesn't allow you to switch to extras. You can sometimes get stuck in textures. No cloud saves means you will lose all your progress if removing the game from your device. However, the one that bugs me the most - Arcade mode is literally unplayable. Some people say that it only works fine if your OS is set to English, which is wild. And from what I understand, there have been much more bugs before - weird hitboxes, inability to swich the keys and so on. And I'm only talking about offline - afraid to even imagine what people face playing with each other.2. Character selection. Not a big deal, but something that bugs me a bit. This game is a crossover, so it's appeal is having more franchises smashed up together. In comparison with NASB 1, we got 2 new ones with El Tigre and the Beavers, but lost 2 with Oblina and Catdog. And the main sinner of the story is Season Pass. The main appeal of NASB 1's Brawler pack was  the fact that they were mostly brand new IP's - out of 5 post-launch additions 4 represent new franchises. Here, all four belong to already the most represented ones. Do we really need 5 SpongeBob or Avatar characters? Have to be fair, I would better see Plankton and Azula as bosses, especially considering there's a very small amount of those.In the end...I don't regret getting the game on sale, but I cannot recommend it, especially at full price, which is a bretty big one. The Campaign is still really fun (when you finally get to play with your settings), but the tech stuff is just frustrating. Maybe those will be fixed some day, can't say. But right now, sadly, no.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Addressed every issue I had from the 1st game and delivered. One of the best platform fighters out right now especially if we're talking just Steam (in the top 3). The only things that drag this game down are the bugs (which are said to be addressed) and a lot of (albeit personal) nitpicks that add up but the positives really outweigh the negatives. If you're a fan of the genre or was disappointed with the 1st game, this is it. It's almost insane what they've accomplished in the time span they were given honestly.For some details:I am really happy that there is a dedicated single player mode with actual substance this time. There is some joy to be had hearing these characters talk to the different bosses and characters. Really appreciate that some characters even have special interactions with each other like with Jenny and her mom, or the Danny Phantom crew bantering with each other. (I wish there was a lot more of that and that it just wasn't in the campaign mode but I digress). While it may seem negligible to have small platforming stages and side modes like pop the balloons appear throughout a run, I again can't say how much I love that they're in this game. It is kind of crazy how much single player content gets shafted (even in the latest Smash game) in favor of the competitive aspects of the game in this genre (I get why sometimes but it still sucks) but this is one of the few games in the genre to have a decent offering which is nice to see and adds more value to the whole package. Despite all that I've said so far, I do have a couple issues with the single player modes. While the campaign was a blast playing through it the first couple of times it did get start to get very repetitive especially near the end. Making you repeat each zone every time you made to the next story beat felt like unnecessary padding. I would have much preferred if they just had more zones instead of having you repeat them but I sort of understand why it is the way it is. The whole run would have been really long like an hour each run had they had 2 additional zones, and that could get really repetitive if you wanted to do a run with each character but I think on the hardest difficulty this should have been a thing. While including platforming stage are great they're pretty mediocre. They only have a few themes and they're borrowed from already existing stages and the only obstacles are moving spikes and bottom less pits. It would have been cool (even if it was only on harder difficulties) to have some relevant enemies show up in the stage or give each stage a unique gimmick like finding a key to open a door or a race to the finish or just make certain stages that make use of the slime mechanic or wall jumping ability (could have a served as another to teach players to use those mechanics in certain situations). The whack a robot mini game I honestly hate now, idk if it's cause I suck (most likely) or the hit box don't match up but it never feels satisfying trying to get a high score whenever it comes up. I am glad it's there for variety sake but I kind of wish there was something else besides it. One thing that annoyed me while going through the campaign was that if you face a normal version of a character with any character that doesn't have a special dialogue with the character you picked, you essentially missed your chance for the WHOLE campaign to see/hear that dialogue. Since the character's don't talk to each other in campaign mode your just gonna have to start your campaign all over and make sure you know who has special dialogue with when picking your routes. Granted I think there's enough special dialogue between playable and npc characters that this doesn't bite too much but it still annoyed me.  It's also a missed opportunity that when a character faces their clone version self they don't talk with/have anything to say back to them. I will say that I'm not really into rouge/ or rouge-lite games so that may have to due with some of my complaints but I wish there was more unique aspects to the runs. Other small things about the campaign; I wish the hub had more NPCs and that it was a bit bigger and had more things to do in it other than buy perks and look at decorations (though I appreciate the 2 secret chests, while that's very little an attempt was made and I wish there were more secrets in the hub area). Would have been cool to have a coop mode so that a friend could play through the campaign with you.I think arcade mode could have been done a little better, it's basically a stripped down campaign run but there are no perks, mob fights, or platforming stages. I think having even a metal fight or even a stamina fight (which never gets used despite being a rule set in the game) would have helped a lot. I sort of see the reason to keep certain things exclusive to one mode to differentiate them, but it makes arcade feel more like a chore. Also would have been nice to have the option for coop in this mode to as well as with the boss rush mode. While I like the new stages, a lot of them either don't have a tournament friendly variant and/or aren't tournament legal which typically wouldn't be an issue for me (since I'm more of a casual) but when you play ranked you can only play on tournament legal stages and most of them are just the same stages from the first game. This with the combination of most stages having similar/the same music (I know they're redone but the point still stands) and most of the new stages being relegated to casual only modes kind of deflates my enthusiasm for the new stages (while I'm at it, should have included the music from the first game so each stage could have 2 alternating tracks instead of only having 1). Having all the old stages (the good ones) come back would have made for a cool unlockable imo though. I really hope the DLC characters also come with new stages similar to the DLC the first game had despite everything pointing to answer being no. I kind of dislike that the costume pack is a DLC when it should have been in the base game imo, I wouldn't be salty if the base game had 4 alt costumes (those dark clone variants don't cut it) or 4 recolored alts and they then had a paid DLC costume pack with 1 unique alt for each character but it could have been worse I guess (I am just thankful we have more than 1 alt unlike the first game). Cause right now it feels like they're being held hostage behind expensive paywalls. I appreciate that those clone alts are unlockables and something you have work to get but they're pretty lame, would have taken simple color variants.I think that's all I have to say but in the end despite my bickering the last few paragraphs, I get that this game was probably rushed and it's a miracle that the game turned out as good as it did. It really feels like that really wanted to make things right coming from the 1st game and that there was a lot of effort put in to make this game as good as it could have been despite the time constraints placed on them. Even though I complained about the heavy reuse, it was done in a smart way to maximize the amount of content available.Despite a lot of characters from the first not being playable here I've come to really enjoy some of the new characters (like Azula, Ember, Jimmy, and the Beavers) and the reworked moves of the veterans that the sting of some of them not returning doesn't sting too much. I honestly hope this game does well cause I think it deserves it, the team should be proud, and if/when the 3rd game comes around I hope they can expand the solid foundation they've made with this one and address the lingering issues like more reps from post 90's Nick that aren't from already rep'd shows and more unique single player content.

The gameplay is a more refined version of a fighting game, it takes aspects of what makes Smash so good, and then other traditional fighters, puts them in a pot, and mixes them together. For example they have MOVE CANCELING! It's literally on par with, say, Turbo mode in Project M in levels of how it can extend combos. They even have a balanced version of a Final Smash, where it doesn't just kill you in one hit and is blockable, meaning competitively it's a very fair move, and super stylish for a game like this! I cannot recommend this game enough, if you're still weary of it because of how the first game failed, wait for this game to get on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: It has good ideas, and graphically is an improvement over the previous game, but that's about all i can praise about the game.Aside from technical issues, such as crashes, freezing on loading screens, and queue times being absurdly long due to how frequently the servers are unavailable, i'm mostly frustrated by how this game *feels* to play. I have 9 hours on record, but at least six of those is just me waiting in queue over the last couple days.The game fees unresponsive, i've attempted using different controllers, but no matter what i use, all my inputs feel delayed to the point where i find myself double tapping or even mashing at times, because i can't rely on my singular button presses to perform the function i wanted to do, the control options in the game are also rather limited, and while steam big picture controller support exists, i shouldn't have to depend on it for a fighting game.Gameplay wise i think the meter is cool, but i'm not a fan of how they've handled projectiles. I don't have anything against zoners, and in fact am a fan of some of them, but every projectile in the game is really slow, which for a character or two can be a cool tool to work with (see Laura SFV, or A.K.I. SF6), but when applied to the whole cast for the majority of projectiles, combined with the unresponsive, unprecise control of the game, it make navigating through them a nightmare. Another thing i noticed was that hitboxes feel small while hurtboxes feel large (at least for the characters i've played), which leads to this awkward combination where it's hard to land a hit when it looks like a move should hit, but it's easy to get hit when there are visible gaps. I don't know why they did it that way but it's not fun.Overall the game feels like Flash Party with the addition of an interesting meter system. I'd still rather play the former though because at the very least that game didn't cost me $79. (i bought the dlc)

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying that I absolutely fell in love with nasb1 and was so excited for nasb2 after the first game's immediate death.1. I've been teleported from mid stage to the bottom blast zone.2. I've fallen through the stage.3. I've gotten stuck in the loading screen.4. I've gotten stuck in the losing screen.5. I've gotten stuck in the winning screen.6. I've gotten stuck in the screen.9. I've been invisible.10. They've been invisible.My pc is juiced and the game works properly maybe half the time.But let's ignore that and talk about the combat.It's straight up just hit stun and gimmicks. On top of that you can run through each other which makes grabbing so horribly wonky and ineffective. I appreciate their effort with trying something new with the slime mechanic, but it is just NOT it. It doesn't work properly half the time if trying to recover with it. That being said, almost every recovery is designed to be bad in order for slime to be relevant in using it to recover. Subsequently nearly every character has a built in flying side special attack that can be used to get back towards the stage, changing many character's movesets that were unique in nasb1, to generic cookie cutter movesets in nasb2 that are clearly built completely around the slime system. Also being able to hit someone mid air, hold them in place with slime mid-air, and follow it up with an instant strong attack for kills feels so disgustingly cheesy. Like, slab of cheese dragging off the pizza kind of disgustingly cheesy. That was but 1 example out of hundreds of broken setups that are possible with the slime. There's already insane amounts of hit stun as it is with no DI options. (I might be wrong on the DI, but it doesn't seem that you can.) There's also slime shielding, slime attack power ups. Pretty much anything you can think of can be effected by the slime. The combat is obsessively built around the slime system, so if you thought you were getting a melee-type game like nasb1, that is the opposite of what this game is. It's almost as if they were recreating nasb1 just with better netcode, but then SF6 released, and they decided to reverse course to copy their Drive mechanic.General rule: If the mechanic you're implementing is forcing you to make the rest of what you built systematically worse, then you probably shouldn't implement that mechanic.Anyways. I was excited for nasb2 but god is it awful. The netcode really isn't even that much better. Patch or not, i'm confident this game will suffer the same fate as the first.Devs. All you had to do was make nasb1 but with a better netcode and bigger cast (11 of the characters that were in nasb1 were removed). You had it perfect.Just sad.
