_childDocuments_.review: Edit after 1.1 patch and 70+ hours - Devs addressed pretty much all of the UX issues I had with the game, and are proceeding with many updates that address player feedback and introduce new functionalities. The game has an incredibly tight core, and seems to be in great hands. Very optimistic about its future. Some thoughts after 17h:Lots of "one more turn" energy. I got pulled in for literally the entire Saturday and couldn't stop (17h on clock after 1 day...). Not for everyone though, you must enjoy micromanging your cities.4 X-es:Exploration is pretty decent.Expansion is goodExploitation is the meat of the game - really addicting.Extermination (war) is meh.Building the industry, setting up all chains so tha they are balanced - this is where the meat of the game's at. UI could be a bit better, but it's not bad.Difficulty is hard to get right - you must be close to the top to not get wiped out after an Era ends, but If you are too high it appears too easy. No rubberbanding mechanic that I've seen yet, snowballing may be a problem.Nice graphics, lots of eyecandy, make sure you don't go too high or you will fry your machine. Though the battle "recaps" are silly as hell and IMO were a waste of engineering resources.No technical problems during gameplay, no performance issues. Had a problem with installation via Steam, had to reinstall (tbh I even refunded and then bought again).
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I have been pleasantly surprised by Ara. I expected it to be another Cov type clone but found that t was far from it. It is a real mix of a Civ style game, Anno or Victoria from Paradox. It is far more involved in production chains and the economy than say Civilization. If you enjoy Civ style games Anno or Victoria this is a mix of all 3. I am veryMuch enjoy this game and it is the only game to give me that just one more turn feeling since Civ 4 at least in civ style games.Plenty of things to improve, UI as micro can become a lot in the later game, AI needs some work but expect to be fighting AI early on if you get some aggressive cigs spawn nearby. I love the graphics, can zoom right in and see the people. I know some have performance issues but I have a high end PC so no crashes or issues for me, running on Mac settings at 150fps. So yes if you enjoy the games I listed then you should really enjoy Ara. I think it is a real gem and will grow into m popularity over time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Ara: History Untold has compelled me to play 1 more turn many times, lol.** This review is after me only playing 10 hours so forgive me if I am grossly incorrect. I just think it's a travesty to see so many negative reviews so quickly. So, I thought I'd share my 2 cents even if it's in haste.As a Civ fan having played over 4,000 hours of Civ V and Civ VI combined I thought I'd give this game a shot while I wait for the next Civ.While far from perfect and refined it offers some new ideas that I really like such as the city building design system. City improvements need resources, which you then can turn into other resources and/or amenities which can either enhance certain aspects of your city improvements or be used in other cool ways. ARA's "crafting system" is a great enhancement for planning.Watching battles is pointless and inaccurate. The battle progress and results stats are nice though. But, opting to watch a battle play out needs much improvement. I can understand though why it's not up to par because it isn't that important when compared to other facets of the game. I imagine this facet will be phased out, this game isn't Total War.Battle formation options are a step up from Civ VI. More formations with different perks and restrictions, which is cool.The graphics are great at all zoom levels, but that isn't as important IMO, more like the icing on the cake. Beauty is only skin deep they say.The tech tree is very plan and thus offers less planning, diversity, and strategy IMO. Basically you can research any tech you want in your current ERA, or BOX I would say. It feels very boxed in that you can't pursue tech's outside of your current era regardless if that's your desire or not. You're literally boxed in.Diplomacy seems promising but so far I'd say average. Close to on par with Civ VI perhaps but Civ V's diplomacy system is much better, IMO.Paragons in ARA is pretty cool. Think of them as great people that can be utilized many different ways. Not just a one time bonus or perk.  Paragons are an improvement over Civ's great people IMO because they are so diverse and can be used in different ways.Map creation needs to be improved and a better definition given to each option. For now though since the game is so new it's not a big deal, but hopefully this will happen.In such a beautiful world it's missing Natural Wonders, a nice touch that any world would Naturally have! Right??I'll revise this review as I gain more play time, I just wanted to make this quick review to point out that while imperfect, ARA is very promising too!It's hard to be a perfectionist while also held to deadlines. Nothing is ever perfect, but this release seems to be very smooth. I've had no issues with glitches or crashes, etc. Granted I haven't reached the end game yet, but I'm playing with the max Civ's on the biggest map size to see how the endgame reacts and performs.If you're a Civ fan give it a shot. You've got what 2 hours to decide if you want a refund? Granted this game is on the more expensive side but by the time I had to think if I wanted a refund or not 6 hours had already passed and I still wanted to play 1 more turn.....
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Ara is best described as a mix of a 4x/City builder game. Don’t listen to those people saying this is the next “civ killer” they are only doing that for clicks. If you understand how this game works and how Civ works you would understand there are  a lot of things that make them different and both can exist on the market. Now that we got that out of the way. I think Ara is a pretty good game. You can see the devs put a lot of work into it with its crafting system, the living world, etc. The leader choices are interesting and I am pretty happy with them. The prestige system is great since you don’t have to 100% focus in one area to win like in the Civ series and other 4x games. Overall I think it's fun.Though what's hurting Ara a lot is we have certain gameplay elements that need some more work. Biggest being diplomacy, religion, and trade. Diplomacy feels very barebones and there are a few ways to expand this in the future. Religion verses system needs some changes because it is all random in what you get and some options are just way better than other  is very strange because you can “ask” for resource from the AI  or the AI can “ask” for resource from you that neither you nor the AI can produce. At the same time I said “ask” because there is no asking really. You just click on a resource and you get it. Those areas need work.In terms of balance tech pacing does feel slightly fast why city building can be slow at times. Some leaders are clearly very strong while others seem pretty weak. Cities in low food areas really can not grow after a certain point. The supply system for building is too much micro and rather boring.For me though the UI issues are the biggest issues atm. I'll link my post I made for this when I am done because I am not going to get into it all, but the UI needs a lot of work. From lack of notifications for important information, Information being buried in different tabs, or information just not being available in areas that would make the most sense. I am going to recommend it because this game does not deserve a negative review and it is still enjoyable, but all the issues I brought up need to be fixed. Once all these issues are fix it a solid 10/10 for me.Link to my post for a lot more details:

_childDocuments_.review: Please combine Humankind with this game with  less micromanagement.I believe the diplomacy system in Humankind is the best compared to other history based 4X game.Economy system in Ara is also pretty compelling and fun, but there is a little bit too many micoro-management.In addition, Ideally, based on the environments and what they have done in the past, each leaders should have develop strength and weakness, even appearance.I need compelling mechanics to emerge in.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: A fresh new take on the Civ franchise! The requirements of materials to keep your cities and civilization running smoothly and into the future keeps things exciting and challenging. I very much like the idea of how buildings / resources play an important role in the development of your cities and unites. The game itself does need some polishing and updates to make it even better than what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Hell I like it.  It's a bit more micromanage-y when it comes to the production which kinda threw me off at first but after I got the hang of it it was pretty simple to keep track of. I also like the ideas of formations being used for certain types of units though it could use a *bit* of polishIt's kind of meh that units can't be directly upgraded (must be disbanded and recreated as their more powerful counterpart) though I got over that really quickly honestly. _childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I have a great time with this game. Something I always disliked about Civ was how many turns were just clicking end turn for a bunch of rounds because you're already set up. You can always tweak something here. You can specialize in different kinds of industries and just making huge cities isn't necessarily a benefit because trying to keep up with the needs of a growing population means you have to keep reinvesting into the food production which doesn't leave you a lot of space for much else. Making use of the space has a lot of interesting dynamics.Right now the only downside I see is building wide is very painful because managing many cities is very tedious and since you individually equip/upgrade buildings its easy to miss some things. It is also, surprisingly, not worth to try and keep everything to a modern degree of development simply because you can only produce so much in a turn. There is a lot of detail in here that requires a serious rethinking and while I think the UI can be improved, this game is already really cool to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Game is solid, rough around the edges but the core gameplay being somewhere between Civilization and Anno is very good. Supply chain is engaging and fun, and makes progression through the game exciting both with new technology, exploration, and expansion. If you like 4X, this game will probably be worth your money. Time will tell with replay value, but right now I am more likely to play this than Civ 5, 6, Humankind, or Millennia.The game has some lacking elements, as others note warfare is pretty rudimentary, but the core design of forces with certain structures getting bonuses is fun and should probably be made even more impactful. I think walls and city HP need to be reworked, especially by the late game. Air units are currently high investment for low output, and would be fixed by massive range increases, especially for late game aircraft (the high end bombers have similar striking range to first-gen aircraft in civ 5). I broadly think that the later eras need to focus more on globalization of trade and warfare, and was surprised by the lack of satellites or a space race prestige system because it would have been a perfect endgame of supply chain management.I worry slightly about replay value, each civilization and leader has bonuses that will make them specialize differently, but I think the game would benefit from civ-specific units and buildings, or some other form of specialization that makes different games feel different. Civ 5 had ideologies for this, and I think the government system in this game has an opportunity to be that if it became something to be invested in.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It offers a great combination out of Civ, city builder and Anno. It is definitely very complex and you need to love micro management, but if that is the mix you are looking for, it is the game you should go for. It goes exactly in the opposite direction of Civ7 and confronts you with even more complexity. That´s great... it gives you all the choices and possbilities and so much depth.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I've been surprised by the depth of game play. This is not Civ! I'm really enjoying the city management, especially as I figure out the UI (which wasn't easy to navigate on day 1). There's a lot of options for viewing information, e.g. a city's zones, harvesters, and improvements, which is not initially obvious, but critical once your cities begin to scale up and you have dozens of production queues. I'm really liking the crafting elements and how the outputs are used by farms, etc. to improve their yields. I've played a game across three nights and am only in the Medieval era. Can't wait to see what things look like once I get to the modern age.Other things I'm really appreciating: - Not having to micromanage battles (though I've only been in one war), which compensates for the fact that cities require more management.- Not feeling like I'm in a race to claim *territory* while competing against a city-spamming AI. This is a game about building and expanding cities and not as much about walling off an area of territory to prevent the AI from moving in.Things I'd like to see improved: diplomacy.Note that I've had Steam in offline mode for the past two days, so all in all I've played for about 14 hours as of the time  of this reivew.

_childDocuments_.review: At first i was not sure so i got the game on pc gamepass and the more i play it the more i like it.it's not a civ competitor nor a civ killer,  the basic is similar but there is so much content that is different that they cannot compare to civ.the Pro  :  simultanous turn,  you never wait for AI  :)  there is no hex grid making the world more organic  Complex production chain with hundreds goods  when building triumph ( wonders )  you need to craft the mats first and it's so satisfying  it's much easier to move military on the map than other historical 4x game  with the deluxe edition there is 42 leaders to chose fromThe Con  cannot upgrade units  ( but the dev are working on a patch to make it possible )  steep learning curve  the ui is not the best it can be
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a turn based 4x and Anno series combined. Ara is mainly an economic sim that focuses on production chains and producing goods. Those goods are necessary to build units / buildings, or improve them. While overall its a very satisfying gameplay loop, it can get overly tedious going back through all your cities and all their buildings to place new or swap out old tools / goods. It also is not optimized very well, but I've managed to get it playing at about 40-60 fps, which is at least playable for a turn based game. Overall I'm pretty damn happy with it, but then I love the 4x genre; I'm not sure I'd recommend it to someone who's not.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Take AOE and mix that with Rise of Nations and what do you have? ARA: history untold.  I am a big Sid Miers Civ fan, but I must admit this one is the closest thing to beating Civ I have ever played.  Do be aware that it takes a pretty stout graphics card to run this game, but even though my graphics card is not as stout as I would like for it to be, and after the GPU shaders finished there compilation which usually takes around 20 mins the game runs great, I have never had it crash as of yet and I have really been enjoying Microsoft and Oxide's take on a large scale CIV building game.  Highly recommend this one to all you history fans out there!
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: They seem to have done some back end fixes, because my framerate is now up over 40 fps on average. It's performing way better now :)After playing for a while, I definitely like this game. There are still some issues that need fixed, but overall it's good. The progression pace seems fine, and I don't have to micromanage anything (unless I want to!). The limited amount of units forces you to be smarter about how you use your troops, and limited number of cities makes you be more strategic about placement.The good: The graphics look pretty good, and resources are pretty clearly marked. I love that each event or larger accomplishment has a history fact attached to it. The AI seems to be smart (Hubby and I are on lower level to learn the game, so they weren't *too* smart). There's a nice box that tells you how many of what materials you have, total you're making per turn, and total you're consuming per turn, so that makes it a little easier to balance out. You can zoom close to your city and see your people going about their daily lives (or running around like crazy if you're seiging a city!)The bad: I do have major fps problems. I have an I9-11900K processor, so a few years old but not ancient. I have RTX 3070 and 32GB of ram. My graphics are not maxed out, and I sit on average 6-23 fps (8 as I am typing this), so pretty bad. My game freezes often - super annoying! But since this is a turn based game, it doesn't affect my gameplay, just annoys me. This DOES need fixed! When researching, if you advance to the next age without learning something, you lose the option to research that thing, which I think is pretty dumb. You should be able to go back and learn something if you want to!Overall, the good outweighs the bad. If you just can't handle fps/freezing problems,  probably give this game a while to see if they fix it. If you can live with that, definitely get it now!
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lovely mix of Civ and Anno in a great way. I like the knock out feature. For anyone that has played a civ game for hours then lost in the end because they forgot to check their standings knows that feeling of time wasted and this helps you know that hey, pick it up or loose the game. I do have a gripe of having an army disengage or retreat from a battle engaged in to reduce casualties. Overall worth the money just for the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game receives some of its negative reviews because of the comparison with civ. It's much more of a management game.The simultaneous game turn is so comfortable that I don't think I'll be able to play a turn-base game that doesn't implement it. I mean just for this I recommend people to give it a try. It's like there so down time even in the latest part of the game.Also It's worth mentioning that - day 1 - the game is working smoothly. _childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable game, especially if you enjoy details, processes and long-term strategizing, both military and economic. _childDocuments_.review: #--- SummaryCurrently "Ara: History Untold" is crushingly broken/unbalanced and insanely time-consuming.Due to a 'maximum capacity of combat units' you can never survive (notice that I don't even talk about winning) on the highest difficulty, since the AI cheats like an apocalyptic demon on steroids.All of this ensures that approximately 95% of players will find this game tedious, unfulfilling and to be honest will never play this game multiple times. Such a shame... really... because I expected this game to be bloody awesome. The game developers are grand master artists, only the balance lags behind and requires fine-tuning.#--- Current status of the game"Ara: History Untold" is a huge time killer, since you have to micro-manage everything to the tiniest detail. Furthermore, each building has slots which need to be filled, not once, but every new era (otherwise you will lag behind your opponents). Don't get me wrong this is fun.However be aware Ara is currently catastrophically unbalanced:1. The starting civilisations (you can choose from) are NOT created equally at all.    With Mexico - Benito Juárez - you can easily outpace everyone else in the entire game with crafting.2. The spawn locations for each civilisation are also NOT created equally at all.     To grow cities quickly you need to plug-in 'feasts' and 'grain stores' in the amenities city tab.    However 'grain' only spawns in grassland areas, in desert areas you're simply screwed.3. Combat... sigh...  you can attack in formations, retreat is no option in this game (attack is the only option).    Furthermore, due to the 'maximum capacity of combat units' you will have almost always have insufficient combat units AND can't build combat units fast enough to replenish destroyed combat units.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game so far. There are soooo many different ways that you can customize your empire which can be a bit overwhelming at first but I personally like having those "a-ha!" moments in a game when I figure out a better way to do things. If you're looking to purchase this game and you like "Civ" and "Humankind" I think you'll like this too. My only complaint (which may be a deal breaker for some} is that you can't upgrade your military units. I'm holding out hope that they fix that eventually. I'm in act 3 right now and it IS getting a little tedious between turns but we all know how it goes in this genre, I haven't come across one yet that's figured out how to keep up the pace once the Empire gets huge. The late game is still less tedious than Civ 6 in my opinion. 100% i'm gonna binge this one for awhile
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, so much so I feel I gotta write a rare review about it.I hate the term "Civ-killer", people want something unique, NOT a Civilization clone or something that does Civ better than Civ does. Ara: History Untold has a lot of smaller, and large details wrapped up in a nice bow which, given time to cook, will come out to be a spectacular feast. A small note I want to make is that this game has some of the most diverse leader & civilization options and abilities I've seen in a 4X game when it comes to historical 4x, with 36 different leaders at launch and around 30ish? Civilizations.Do you like supply systems? They're required here however the developers have done a good job making it simultaneously important whilst not micro-managy to the extreme as you use tools and other amendities and the like to build off and supply each other.Do you like building cities that make sense and aren't clustered "districts" with little uniformity? Cities require planning and location is quite important, along with the unique way tiles are broken down (Into smaller "Zones", you get bonuses keeping certain buildings grouped together, such as a farm & granary as an example.)Even it's war system is unique in the genre, forming casus belli's against your neighbors & the battle system (Of which army organization & structure is important) more reminiscent of a Paradox game rather than others in the 4X genre.The only concerns I have, which will absolutely and definitely be mitigated overtime, is the lack of diplomacy options (It exists and has a good base, but bare bones atm) & performance issues which I won't go into as other reviews already have.tl;dr, You'll like Ara if any of these things interest you.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves better reviews.So far, I absolutely love it and it is my favorite 4X game of all time based on the limited playtime I have. First, a few negatives. The performance is a little rough. It chugs a bit on my very high end PC, but turning down a couple key settings made it totally acceptable. I'm sure this will be improved. Certain elements of the UI need improvement, and more automation of some tasks is probably necessary. While the depth of the crafting system is one of the game's strengths, as your civ expands it gets overwhelming and too fiddly having to check which of your buildings has available supplies or upgrades. This should be broadcast by the game, and probably it should allow you to automatically supply buildings with items, or at least supply all buildings of a type with items at once.On the other side is just about everything else. Diplomacy and Religion are a bit barebones, but probably will be expanded and are my least favorite element of these games anyway. The visuals are incredible, and I love the irregular, more natural tile shapes and the ability to zoom in and look at your people and buildings close up. The simultaneous turns element is a complete game changer and revolutionary for the genre. I can't imagine why I'd ever want to play a 4X game that slowly cycles through opponent turns ever again. The crafting system is also fairly unique, more similar to something like Victoria than anything else. Your workshops and other production buildings can produce numerous Supply and Amenity items, which can be allocated to other production buildings to improve their output, or allocated to cities to improve Health, Happiness, etc. As you progress, many of these items are also needed to build or upgrade higher level buildings. Again, this system is very interesting but can be a bit cumbersome later in the game. With some automation and UI streamlining, it will be excellent.Ara does a number of unique things to push the genre forward. As it stands, it's a very solid, groundbreaking 4X game with a couple of rough edges. I truly hope this game succeeds and the devs have the ability to improve and expand it over time. With that sort of support it could easily become the best game in the genre, ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: It is a wonderful 4X game, much different from the vein of Civ - there is a sense of grandness in how it looks at concepts such as settling, building production chains, and war. I wish there would be some significant difference between leaders/cultures, but it certainly has the framework to be an amazing entry!

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are real good, makes me feel that I'm looking at something real, not cartoonish.  Has essentially 12 ages (within three acts) and the clear losers are dropped instead of going on for hundreds of terms only to lose.  On the negative side, I often don't have the space to build what I want and need to build.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Ara has a healthy mix of new and old things from the 4x genre, and the beginning to the midgame of each game are fantastic. However, once you hit the second half of a game, you'll start slogging through a lot of micro and a lot of clicking. This is because every improvement (read: buildings on the map) and every city can have things "slotted" or "equipped" to them, that you yourself craft by building workshops/breweries/factories/etc or that you get via trade or conquest. The thing is, this is great and all at the beginning of the game, when you don't have as many cities or improvements. But as the game progresses, you get (maybe) exponentially more things you can slot to buildings, and many more buildings to slot items to.If not for that, ARA is a fantastic take on civ-like 4x games, and I'm excited to see where this game ends with future patches, hopefully they'll introduce ways to reduce the micro and make the second half smoother to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: A different take on the 4x genre. If you want a "Civ" game this probably isn't for you, while they are in the same genre they are very different in the way they play. With that said, this game has heaps of unique takes on different mechanics and is definitely a fun experience. I enjoy the process of building up a city, different production lines, and frankly the level of detail in the map and the cities is, in my opinion, some of the best in the genre. The game has also ran great for me on nearly maxed out settings. Also, in my opinion, while the game is more "micromanage-y" than other 4x games the game gives you several tools to manage that to the point that it is not overwhelming i.e. a menu that shows you what everything is crafting that can be changed with a click, the ability to infinitely make a resource. All-in-all, while not perfect if you are a fan of the genre and want a fresh take it is worth a try, especially considering you can play it on gamepass for a few bucks and see if you like it.General pros:Graphics - the map generally and the people in your city and armies being represented as actual people and not giant monstersThinking ahead is rewarded wellA unique take on armiesCivilizations dying out as the game goes on is (in my opinion) unique flavor and adds some tension not found in other 4x games - this can be turned off for the playerPrestige being an overall win condition feels less pigeon-holey than some other 4x games"Leaving behind" tech that can be discovered later is a fresh take on research in a 4x gameManaging different quality of life modifiers with different bonuses is engagingDiplomacy and AI diplomatic actions make senseThe game is more feature complete on launch than any other modern 4x game I have playedGeneral cons:The game has a pretty steep learning curve - expect to read lots of tooltipsThe ui can be a little clunky at times Early game hunting feels underdevelopedPlaying "fast" can send you down a hole that can often be difficult to recover from by the time you realize what you have missedThe tutorial exists, but could definitely be betterBattle cinematics could use some workUnits or buildings to make leaders/civilizations feel more unique would be welcomeOverall, I'd say its a 7.5/10 for me with lots of potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions: 1. Thumbs up for what is here on Day 1, and for the potential this game has, that I hope it fully realizes with updates and / or dlc. I love the map, the graphics are gorgeous, I'm sure the performance will be improved, but I've got it running between 30-40fps on an i7-11700 with an RTX 3060Ti and 32GB of RAM. 2. In the current version, the ration of "Work / Management" to "Play / Fun" is too heavily weighted to the Work / Management / Micro side for my taste. This is due to the systems of Resources / Amenities, which I like overall, but becomes very micro-heavy very early in the game. 3. Tech Tree unlocks may need a nerf, I feel like I'm unlocking Techs faster than I can implement then either due to other unlocks, or it feels like my Tech inventions are outpacing my cities production and growth. I just entered the 3rd Era of Act 1 and I only just founded my 3rd city and am still using Archers. What do I need War Chariots or Elephants already for? Other than that, I really like the slow(er) pace of this game, but much of that slow pace is due to micro-management of buildings, chains and aforementioned Resources / Amenities. Thanks to the devs for their dedication and thoughtful design on most of it! I really hope MSFT and the devs continue to invest in this game over the next couple years, build a community, get some modding going, the potential for this one is huge!
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: good start, finally after many competitors who tried to copy all of the faults of civ series, without giving much new stuff, we have a game that  has seemingly focused on removing the faults instead. So far so good, enjoyng the game, even if some UI things feel a bit rough around the edges, there is nothing that a patch or two wont fix in the future. Good stuff
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the negative reviews are legit, some are just bad. Late game micro and UI issues are legit. The game does what humankind wanted to do better, and does what milenia couldnt do. This feels more like a PDX 4x than any of the others. This is more what I wanted civ 6 to be before they released that garbage.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is not very experinced in 4x strategies, I find Ara very exciting! It is not too complex to understand, but at the same time it is quite challenging (playing on normal difficulty). Perhaphs people who have over 1000+ hours in this genre might find this game too simple and limited, but for me this is the best combination of challenge and simplicity in one. A small tip for beginners: this trategy is more about crafting than building, so keep a closer eye on your crafted items and ways to boost them.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: The game has exceeded my expectations so far, Im at the end of act1. It runs smooth on my PC (Ryzen9 5900x, 32GB & 3080 Ti) with all maxed out except for shadows that I decreased 1 notch to high, 4K resolution. The AI is indeed not very threatening, I recommend you start high on "difficulty" as many suggests, especially if ur familiar with the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Need more optimization, but mechanics are quite good and addicting. The potential is definitely there and should be given the chance if you are a fan of 4x games.Pros- Placing buildings are a puzzle that's quite fun to optimize- Scouting and hunting is quite good, can be better but good.- Combat formations cool (hoping for flanking bonus in the future)- Nice variety of leaders, lore accurate and flavorful- Good overall system(crafting and acts)Cons- Some civs have 5 positive buffs and some civs has only 3 buffs or 1 nerf, thats kinda bad balancing.- I was kinda hoping for some buffs on certain buildings like blacksmith being close to a mine.- Where unique units?- Some wonders are too weak to even consider building- lagging even when playing on recommended pc requirements unless go very low on settings- civs do not compete for wonders (AI is not utilizing crafting mechanic)Notes:For all the games I've played Ghengis Khan is always declaring war early then getting too strong in the midgame lolNobody likes Jean De Arc xdI have quite a few maps where I started in a bad placement (no food, no resources)
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't even finished the tutorial on my first run, so take this for whatever it's worth.  Just what I've seen so far offers new, unique, and very deep mechanics.  The tutorial is exceptional.  It's entirely possible that I have yet to discover some highly negative issues; but so far I haven't.  If I do I will update this review and reevaluate my recommended rating as appropriate.  But for now, this game is very definitely scratching that civilization itch for me, so it's a thumbs up from me until further notice.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a somewhat casual CIV player. I get the basics, I play versus normal AIs. I really like ARA. I was a bit overwhelmed with the possibilities and it is likely I'll never truly master it. But it's so much fun! Trying to min-max, looking for resources on the map, creating vast industries, and seeing my little people walk around.I also believe I understand some of the other frustrations I've seen in the comments. It's likely they are substantiated. The game could run a lot better, but I haven't encountered any crashes so far. What I don't believe I agree with is the fact that this game isn't worth the full price; in my opinion, it is.I'm having a lot of fun!L.E. 1: OK, needed to come back and vent a bit. I triggered the end of the game without realizing it was a condition. If this was explained somewhere in the game, I certainly missed it. Once you gather a certain amount of prestige, you are informed that the first nation reaching 47k will trigger the last 25 turns. I was generating a substantial amount of prestige per turn and I only got to about 470 turns. I was frustrated because I had just started moving into producing the late game stuff and I didn't get the chance to really use any of it. That is why I wanted to play a long game of 1,000 turns. ARA team, if you see this, please make it an option that I can turn off. I wouldn't have been generating prestige had I known I was going to be penalized for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: This is a unique mix of empire builder and supply chain management, as others have pointed out. There is a lot of information when you get started...I felt more comfortable after watching a few "let's play" guides on youtube (mole undermanagement is a good one). An important - but not explained - tip is that various buildings benefit from being in the same region (the small sections of the map for your city) as same types....i.e. farms with farms and wells etc. I am enjoying it so far, but I like management games, so that was not a turn off. I do think they should incorporate some way to automate many processes for those who want it. Ultimately, I appreciate that this adds a new approach and is not simply a Civilization clone. Really like the roster of leaders, a good mix of classic and unique options. I have not experienced any crashes so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I like it, and I'm not among the haters club of Civ VII, I will buy that as well. So I'm not saying this is good as a vendetta for CIV VII decisions. This game is funny, it's much better than Millenia and Human Kind. Much better graphics than CIV VI and V. Overall, I think we are having some progress in this kind of games, which I appreciate.I've seen people complaining on the battle animations? CIV series does not have control on battles. Well the only one of the genre that has it is Human Kind, but the game is terrible, including the combat. So for me, not an issue, I like it.The only con would be that I am not sure any game should cost 60 EUR. That's a super robbery overall. I paid them because I can, but come on, that's a lot of money.Will be sharing more in short, loving it so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: So im having a hard time understanding the amount of negetive reviews. I am playing the game on a 2019 Acer Predator Laptop with a GTX1660ti. With a mix of low and medium settings the game is FAR from "unplayable". Does it need performance updates to fix slowdowns and lags? Ye, absolutely. Does the AI, especially when it comes to war, need some work done on it? Yes, absolutely. But, the underlying game is freakin awesome. This is what i always wished Civ would be like. Resource management i don't find that difficult, love it. Naturally expanding cities across an area of land instead of just having a 1 single hexagon that is "a city". Love it. Im 10 hours in so far and i cant stop playing. awesome game that needs some polishing issues fixed. If your on the fence about getting it, i feel ya, so was I after reading the reviews but im SO glad i just went for it. If you were a fan of both civilization games, and resource management games, it would be criminal not to play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very promising game. Not just visually beautiful and impressive what they have done with the zooming and the map, but actually has a deep economic system and some really good ideas.I can see why for so many people it feels overwhelming - there is a LOT to customize and optimize here. If you hate min-maxing or you hate micromanagement, then it can be discouraging or even confusing what to do.But I'd argue that you don't have to do any of that, if you don't want to. Sure, you'll play suboptimally and won't beat the hardest AIs, but you can still enjoy the game. The UI actually helps with that, and there is literally everywhere an info button or tooltip to help explain things. The tons of options and optimizations however can be really enjoyed by the more "hardcore" strategists and builders.Regarding performance, I'm astonished. The game runs smoothly, it's responsive, barely any bugs, loads incredibly fast, constantly above 50-60 FPS, all by having a middle-high tier laptop, running medium-high settings. Not to mention thanks to simultaneous Turns, you don't have to wait anything basically, even with 36 players.It's far from perfect, some systems and features are still quite rudimentary or rather in a "backbone state", I personally find the style of the UI as kinda ugly, but overall the game has a very solid start and stays on good grounds, in my opinion. Add extra contents (both DLCs and free updates, the latter which was already confirmed by developers that they have the financing for a long time) that will be coming, add modding on top (which was said many times by developers that it's a priority for them) and this game has the potential to be truly incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying it greatly so far.It plays more like a city builder 4x than any Civ.The economy is very deep.Supply,crafting,setting up production lines for what you're consuming.With good management you can set it up without all the crazy micro that I have seen reviews talk about,you just build one crafting station per resource and let it be mostly but you wont get dead turns in this game....There is a learning curve here.The non economic 4x elements are pretty basic.War,diplomacy are standard 4x.The graphics are great.The little details of the map.The diorama feel of the cities.Best I have seen. Performance issues were fixed when I set shadows to direct shading only everything else is maxed out.Runs 90fps at 1440p with  I5 12600K,32RAM,RX7800XT.The game has some issues like not being able to upgrade units,no nukes,UI could be better.AI military logic hopefully gets improved.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I read the reviews, about the performance issues and optimization, but decided to buy it anyway. I'm seeing no issues or problems - but I'm running a 4090, so your mileage may vary. Still, I'm really enjoying it. It's a nice departure from the Civ series in all the right ways. It's entertaining and engaging and without the boredom of a Humankind. Combat is very much who has the bigger stack, but that is also very Civ-like, at least the older Civs. All in all a very good alternative to Civ, bit pricey though... seems like a lot of games are creeping north of $60 these days... an unwelcome trend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: A really good civ competitor with a mix of anno logistics. I love Anno and I like civ style games so it was a perfect combo. My only gripes are war can be cheezed really hard making the game very easy and the animations areound battles and just things happening around the world I wish were more fleshed out. the second thing isnt a big deal but the first one is for multiplayer. I run this on an all amd system with no problems. It actually runs amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: A solid advancement on the 4x genre. The production chain for resources and overlapping aspects of tech is a fun innovation. I also like that they don't over-complicate combat with a mini-battle field or per-unit customization, but they do allow interesting army compositions and a neat little visualization of the battles. The rest of the game is on par with competitors in the genre. The only thing I found annoying was that the terrain wasn't very readable at a glance. But that's pretty nit-picky.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: So far so Good!Only  played about 9 hours at this time. So In other words I've barley scratched the top of the iceberg so to say.I've thrown myself into the deep end with huge map 4 continents, and I've so far had the impression that my starting locations have been varied enough to give different challenges each time. Regarding NPC players, resources, biomes and general feel. The pacing feels on point, and it seems that effects from lost tech can be picked up later from similar but better tech. AI is as I've come to expect from a 4x game, and atleast for me it is good enough for now, but I would not complain if improvements arrives in the future.UI got a paradox games feel, and thusly is familiar, atleast for me. The production line thingy, yes it's there. But I'm starting to lean into trying to not overthink it. It can fast spiral out of control if one is a tad impatient and starts to add alot of boosters to the production. Slow is fast or something....Acts and Tech-stages. Feels fine so far. Nothing out of the ordinary for other similar games, the lost civilisation for the lowest scores between acts is also a nice thing  that can create a certain Atlantis/lost citiy ruins mystery hehe. General short feel is as many have pointed out a CIVish game with some Anno elements. But I woud ad "And a Paradox game presentation".  And for myself this is a sweet package that I can't keep my fingers away from for now. -Might update later :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Don't normally review, but honestly want to just counter some of the low tier negative reviews. Don't get me wrong, there are definitely performance issues for lower end PCs (I have had 0 performance issues at all so far personally), but that kind of stuff is usually patched quickly, and most of those reviews will likely not change.The only other gripe I've really seen is the UI. Honestly, I expected it to be bad, and kinda thought it was at first too, but once I actually looked through the menus, the UI actually gives a lot of information where and when I need it. Every time I was like "Oh I wish I had a way to look at this" I found something for it. Take the time to look through each menu, especially the ones in the top right corner. There is a LOT of information there and you can manage much of your civilization that way.Otherwise, the game is great. It is more complex imo than Civilization, but not crazy complex. There is a bit of micro managing with crafting, but not frustratingly so. There may be some balance issues later (I have only gone to the second act so far, which is 4 ages in), but so far the game has honestly exceeded my expectations. I expect with a few patches and possible future updates that it will be an extremely good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I personally liked it, sure there are some things that are annoying with the UI and lack of map selection but there are a lot of new things that make this game fun. I liked the balance that they have achieved with the micromanagement of resources and having specialists generating masterpieces.  The battle system is nice addition and the road system at first is kinda weird as you can only connect your cities, in order to connect with other civs you need improve your technology and research Hospitality which makes sense. For me it is a good starting point for the game and  looking forward to playing new patches of it
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I originally wrote a positive review for this game, thinking it was heading in a good direction. After the 1.1 update with the new empire-wide economy screen... I think I'm comfortable flipping this from a positive to a negative review. I'll explain it in detail.Ara history untold has drawn a lot of comparisons to Civ and Humankind and the paradox games for obvious reasons. It's a 4X game with a different take on history, with a more board-game like feel through intensive resource management that can be rewarding when you get just right. It also imparts a bit of realism to it, with the culling at the end of each era giving other nations more room to expand which is a neat idea, and the organic, very nice way city expansion works. Unfortunately, though, the aforementioned resource management system is also the game's biggest curse. I originally found it interesting if cumbersome to deal with. After seeing what the developers came up with to help mitigate the difficulty and tedium of intense micromanagement that was required to play the game well and navigate its many, many, complex nuances for slotting components and resources into place, it just left me asking. Is this really the best they've got?The problem with the way the system works is that it's very unintuitive. If I have an excess of wheels, why do I, the king (emperor, take your pick) of this empire need to personally slot it into place in every granary, workshop, mill, or other building that can use it? Putting all the granaries and houses on one window where I can see them in the list goes a little bit of the way to make this easier, but it really obscures much of the real issue which is just how tedious this micromanagement gets as the game wears on, especially in the lategame when you've got hundreds of different resource types, corresponding buildings and projects of higher complexity that need supply chains to function. The sheer number of choices becomes utterly paralyzing and tedious, leaving the player begging for a more efficient way to offload some of the work. This new economics screen is really just a reorganization of the old one into a grouped list style, it still doesn't give the player any resources to help cut down on micromanagement.And it's a shame, really, that the developers don't seem to have a clue how to make their game more fun or approachable for those of us who don't want to feel like we're playing what amounts to a GUI over a spreadsheet with pretty city building tools on top. Plenty of people directly suggested to them that they should reform the screen into more of an "inventory management" system where the different resource producers rather than needing to be individually managed automatically produced resources up to set caps empire-wide. For instance, I need 10 glass to complete a university, I could queue up the order within my system and have the computer automatically delegate the necessary production across the appropriate buildings within my empire, with settings to tweak that production to my own needs. That way I'm not still clicking through menus individually to queue up the specified number across each of my 5 ceramics shops, the game is doing that busywork for me. It's an obvious solution that I know was suggested to them multiple times in the discord, but it appears to have fallen on deaf ears.I still have some hope the developers will get their heads out of their butts and stop assuming what the players want and instead just give it to us. I think Ara has something special, but it unequivocally needs more time in the oven to really develop the polish where it becomes a fun game. Right now unfortunately it's just disappointing how much micromanagement you have to do. For the right person this will be the best game ever, but for your average person it will be hard to have much fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: As of now I haven't gone too far into the game, but i would say its good. All characters from early game strong, too building up to become a prestige powerhouse give you unique objectives on how you want to invest your nation. For some advice, the ai will jump you as all of them will suddenly decide to kill you, so keep some soldiers on hand.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Have not played this game for many hours. But I have played a lot of strategy games before. Such as Cilivization III to Civilization VI, Anno Series, Paradox strategy games, Rise of nation, humankind, Old world, Total war, Galactic cilivization seie etc.  ARA History Untold is a good game and if you like strategy you will probably like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting new approach for an old concept of 4X games.Graphics is awesome and give you a much better feeling for scale.Music is really good.Gameplay is a little more complicated compared to the biggest genre game, but is fun when you get the drill in it.What would be needed would be more options in the game creation, like victory conditions and other things.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Could definitely use some optimization. The only mechanics that I think need improvement with future content are diplomacy and religion. This game makes a lot of bold choices to shake up the 4x genre and I already enjoy it more than Civ 6. There is plenty of content here to work with and as long as you keep an open mind and drop any expectations coming from Civ, there are plenty of worthwhile ideas and mechanics that make this fun and engaging (even if you have to hit "next turn" a few times in a row).
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: Early review, but game seems promising. I can see an emerging issue with the UI, which does not bode well with the complex gameplay. However, the economy has depth, the agregate advantage of a strong economy help lift your empire faster and the graphics are what Civ should have gone a long time ago. Indeed, the beautiful landscape makes you FEEL like you are building an ascending civilization. The management of military units is great, as is the management of expansion, which is intuitive and allows for a strong expansion.If the devs fix some of the highlighted issue (frame rate, UI management, AI issues - the latter have not encountered yet) this can, indeed, be the Civilization killer.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually cautious about these games as there can be some real hit or miss attempts but this however is pretty fantastic I adore the art style,the living world and the army sizes that actually look like armies it is awesome! truly in my opinion an innovative new chapter in the 4X grand strategy turn based genre I love it! I'm switching to gamepass to continue playing (for anyone who goes hurr durr about ours spent in the future) as of release date, bar some small frame rate drops ARA looks like it is a real labour of love and a thoroughly enjoyable experience so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Ara: History Untold

_childDocuments_.review:
Ara: History Untold, built by a team that includes many of the leads behind one of the most popular historical grand strategy games of all time, invites players to build and lead a nation throughout global history as they explore new lands, develop arts and culture, conduct diplomacy, and go head-to-head with rivals to prove they are the greatest leader ever known.

Players will become the architect of a dynamic, living world fully rendered and brought to life through the power of Oxide's proprietary Nitrous Engine, where their play style and decisions will shape the world they create, the lives of their people, and their legacy as a leader.

There is a pattern with every boss, including the final bosses in both normal and Trips story. But I'll still recommend playing the normal story, Trips story is difficult and really challenges the player. (If you say this game is as worse as Sonic Forces, that's a genuine skill issue.)
_childDocuments_.name: SONIC SUPERSTARS

_childDocuments_.review: The first half is pretty good, except for the lag and stuttering in single player. I cannot get 60 fps consistently on my 2060, even on low settings and all windows closed. Once you get to Golden Capital Zone the game falls apart and the bad level design shows. The bosses are just being difficult, not actually difficult and go on too long. The game runs worse than Sonic Frontiers on my 2060, even with all other windows closed. I cannot recommend this game. It might not be Sonic 2006 bad, but it's not worth more than maybe $10.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars are a great and amazing game after Mania, but.... the bosses are really long and boring, and sometimes can be frustrating if you died and re-play again. However, the zones are good, the special stages and bonus stages are great, expect the 5th Special Stages can be a little difficult. After you earn an Emerald and want to earn more just like the classic Sonic games, you'll only get 1 Emerald per Zone, not Acts. The Final Boss is really, really hard but manage it. _childDocuments_.review: Well I figured since I'm on the hardmode now I've played it enough to leave a reviewFirst and foremost I want to get this out of the way since unfortunately the steam review system is binary in just yes or no. All my issues with the game are entirely outside the game itself. It requires an epic account to play online and it requires the epic launcher to run for some ungodly reason? I literally don't know why they did this but it explains why the newsletter took so long to have steam listed as an option. I imagine it was some deal between sega and epic but regardless that's kinda stupid since I got it on steam to avoid epic. The other thing is it has denuvo, so if you're already pretty anti that then yeah. With those 2 combined I can understand why one may not want to support the game. That being said if you don't care about those things and the shady fact that it wasn't mentioned in the store page then you may move onto the rest of the review.Ok now to actually talk about the game itself, this is very much a classic sonic game within it's gameplay. Though I've seen some other reviews not clarify what that really means to them seeing as how not all classic games were even the same. The classic games for the most part are a platformer with momentum physics that allow you to do some interesting platforming and give you the ability to zoom through levels after mastering the layout/understanding of physics in general.I've been seeing a lot of people say it doesn't feel classic cause it doesn't have that "sense of speed" which I think is baffling to me cause you have to earn it in classic games. It's not modern sonic where you can just press a boost button and "go fast". It's made me think that the people who say this don't actually have an idea of game design and have sonic 2 as their favorite classic game and yes, that is definitely me calling them simple to some extent.So let me give you an actual closer comparison as opposed to just saying "classic". The gameplay in superstars is much closer to sonic 1 and sonic cd. If you find you're a fan of those 2 specifically then there's a good chance you'll actually really like this game's gameplay. If your favorite is sonic 2 then your mileage may vary quite a bit. The physics in this game are at the very least comparable if not a near perfect recreation of the classic physics. Looks like they finally took some notes from mania in this regard.The game's collectibles on the other hand leave much to be desired. You can get the chaos emeralds which give you cool powers and the ability to see the true ending at least on the hard mode, but every other thing you can get in the game feels pretty meaningless. You can acquire medals which are used mostly to unlock parts for your mp avatar which apparently has crossplay? I haven't tried the online myself at least but idk how long it is going to last anyway which makes the medals feel pretty pointless. It's an interesting idea but they probably could've spent their time and resources elsewhere. Other than that though there is fruit, which you can get via boss capsule rng or hidden throughout the levels... which also seems quite pointless. They allow you to access a special "fruit" act which is basically just a bonus stage to get a bunch of rings in. Normally this would be fine but there's no live system so what exactly is the point of getting these?Sound design is alright, which is something to be concerned with as sonic's sound design/ost is usually really good. This time around I'd say it's just serviceable. There are a few tracks I really ended up liking, but a good amount that just kind of faded into the background for me. It's a bit of a grab bag in the ost department. That aside though the sounds aren't bad in the game either but I feel like the balancing on certain ones are off. The barrels actually made me think someone was knocking on my door in the late hours which confused me at first. The fact it stood out so much from the rest is a clear sign to me at least that something is off.Ik I mentioned the gameplay earlier but I want to add that the level design is actually pretty good as well, though some levels can be a bit gimmicky. There were only a very few moments where I had questioned if they thought something was fun or not. The easiest example that comes to mind for me is in the Amy Act where you have to spend some time occasionally pushing boxes... somewhat slowly might I add. I imagine this to be quite annoying on repeat playthroughs. Bosses are actually pretty unique this time around. They actually feel like legitimate bosses that ask you to at least learn them a bit to combat them instead of just damage boosting like you could in the original. This is a double edged sword though imo cause it means there's also a large amount of time that you can't speed up the encounter. Emerald powers can also trivialize the bosses a bit too so if you don't like them you can just kinda skip them anyway. It's in a weird spot but I prefer this way mostly.Last thing I can mention are the characters and their abilities. They all feel unique in how they traverse the levels. Sonic is exactly how you imagine. He can go fast due to maintaining the drop dash from mania allowing him to keep going as long as you know what you're doing. Tails got some upgrades in this one with his flight. He is now able to hit enemies above him and hold down to descend faster making him a lot more fun to play as. Knuckles remains mostly unchanged, a bit of a delay when landing, climbs up walls as usual. It seems like they took his jump height penalty away at least which is good. At least I didn't notice it being shorter this time around. Amy is a new addition to the playable cast... technically since she was later added to origins. She gets a double jump that allows her to have more verticality than sonic at the cost of a drop dash. She can however use her hammer while jumping to hit enemies the rest of the cast wouldn't have been able to hit normally since the hammer extends the hitbox. For those unaware you can hold the hammer out for longer by holding jump after her 2nd jump. This allows her to take routes the others wouldn't be able to take due to how well she can bounce off of basically any enemy she pleases. Her abilities also allow her to be pretty good at taking down bosses, in case you don't want to use emerald powers anyway.Overall I enjoyed the game at least and can/will recommend it to those who don't care about the stuff outside the game. Even though I did enjoy it though I do have to question if $60 is a reasonable price and part of me is conflicted on that. I think 40/50 might be closer to how I actually feel but it's a bit arbitrary anyway. Especially when you consider that a lot of other big named games are making the jump to 70 unfortunately. Take that as you will as that's going to be entirely subjective and I hope you found this review somewhat helpful in your decision making.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 4/5. Good game, if you're into platformers and couch CoOp.Detailed:One of the best Sonic Games since Sonic Adventure.Pros:+ Absolutely responsive controls and controller feedback. I personally don't remember Sonic games controls being as smooth yet responsive (excluding Mania). Generally, Sonic was simply too fast to catch up with high-speed paced environment and was generally stuck in textures or throw himself out of level bounds. Here, it is masterfully great.+ Camera in CoOp/Multiplayer. While many people will say that it "works weird" - the reality is actually quite transparent - whoever goes first gets the camera. If you're farther into the level than your friend(s) - the camera will stay focused on you and will switch to other people when they take the lead. This is actually a wise decision since attaching camera to one player would be not very beneficial to the game overall, resulting in too much responsibility on one exact person skill.+ Characters. Each character does deliver a unique experience to level completion. Since you can do 4 various characters  every level can be beaten up to four time, while not obliging a player to do that. This game does not oblige, it only offers an opportunity.+ Fantastic Nintendo-like level design. High-paced highways are intersected with classic platforming experience, boss fights and reaction-based episodes. That makes player don't get bored easily, always providing something fun and unique every 30 seconds.Cons:- When playing CoOp with friends, everyone has to point a lot of attention to where they are on the screen, as sometimes it may get frustrating when playing with all 4 characters. But playing with 1-2 friends feels much better.- Deluxe edition is not worth it. it's just cosmetics for a rabbit skin, which I only suggest you purchasing if you really want to. It provides 0 additional value to the story, only giving a couple lego skins and an in-game wallpaper. Just get the base game, really.- Chaos Emeralds powers feel fun, but sometimes may feel a bit odd. Lowkey - the game is played well enough without them most of the time, except for the episodes when using emeralds' power is necessary.- Compared to other badass and really outstanding characters, Sonic himself  I mean, having an additional spindash is cool, not gonna lie, but I'd love to see something else on top of it, as he deserves this as a main character.Overall:The game doesn't feel "BIG", for sure. However, imo this game can definitely stand up in line with AAA-releases, due to the facts that it it very detail-oriented. I suggest you taking a look at least at Sonic's ears animation on windy levels, this is insane :DI do recommend this game for most sonic fans, as it is fulfilled with creativity, and extrapolates new ideas, not trying to completely stand on their predecessors' legacy. Don't get me wrong, it is still a platformer, but not anymore the one you knew on those old Sega consoles. It's a completely new game with tons of new fun stuff to check out.Some people tend to ruin the rates as they added Epic Store authorization and Denuvo security. My call - rate the game itself, not the things that it's pre set up to. I highly doubt it was Sonic team's direct choice to add those things, and not the SEGA as the distributor. Also, it only took me 1 minute to register an Epic account on my steam deck and then I went right into the game. And the game itself - solid.I'm sorry if this is a bit watery, I'm not much of a reviewer, but I do recommend you checking it out. Don't fall into "Sonic was never good" pit, it was and HE IS BACK :)

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of this franchise I can safely say Superstars is a massive disappointment. The game starts off really strong with its really well 2D animated intro by Tyson and his team. Bridge zone is a great little nod to the actual Bridge zone from the 8-bit version of Sonic 1 and a original enough zone that it doesn't feel like a copy of Green Hill zone. Yet despite its strong first impression issues quickly crop up. There is simply just way to much automation or moments where control is taken away from the player.  The classic games are known for these moments where you just hold forward and you watch Sonic and friends blast through a cool set piece, but this is totally different. One moment you are playing through a stage normally then you are forced into a little mini game in order to progress. Something that completely goes against Sonic's design philosophy where the flow of your movements is completely dependent on your skill not how fast you can figure out whatever little distraction the developers throw at you to slow you down.Special stages seem entirely built around the concept of 4-player co-op. I get why they did this its just weird they didn't design a single player version of the game. Compared to Manias' special stages alone Superstars' are laughable.Boss fights are by far the single worst aspect of this game. The waits between openings is way to long and was clearly designed with 4 players in mind. Again why wasn't a single player version of this experience considered? Sonic has always been a solo game first multiplayer aspects were always secondary. The story is light, which is normal for a classic game. However there are certain aspects of it that just seem forgotten or flat out rushed. The True final boss being the prime example of this. You get one hint of its existence unless you watched the trailers for the game. You don't get an indication of what makes it a threat or why Eggman wants it. The boss is also one of the most frustrating final bosses I have ever had the displeasure of taking down. Probably the single worst final boss in the entire franchise.The new playable character they added actually plays really well in comparison to the others. One negative aspect is having to play the whole game again with the new character in a "hard mode" version of the game to unlock the true final boss. The hard mode final boss is also a very frustrating experience with its one hit kill attacks that make you restart the entire boss fight over if you die.The music reminds me of Sonic 4. Utterly astounding that they thought it was a good idea to have anything even remotely comparable to the complete garbage that is Sonic 4's music. All in all this game claims to be a classic game, but in reality its a pathetic attempt on Sega's part to cash in on the 4 player co-op platformer that the classic Sonic games was NEVER intended to be designed around. If you sincerely intend on buying it please get it on sale it's not worth its price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Before getting into the game itself, why the hell does a  game require an Epic Games account? There's absolutely no reason for it. And Denuvo is bad as always.Moving on. The one big question on your mind is likely "Is this as good as Mania?" No. Not even close. It's not a bad game, but it has several major problems.First, the level design is just not as good as the classic games (Genesis + Mania). It feels less cleverly designed overall and has fewer interesting new level mechanics, but the big problem is that the camera doesn't follow you as it should. There are many,  times throughout the game where you'll get hit by an obstacle that you have no chance of knowing is there. And I'm not talking about "you forgot to roll when going down a slope", I'm talking about problems the classic games didn't have like "the game tells you to use a certain ability to move yourself straight upward and when you do, the camera pushes you to the top of the screen where an enemy is just offscreen during the moment where you're literally unable to defend yourself without cancelling the ability in the exact spot where the game explicitly told you to use the ability". Vertical camera movement in particular just feels wrong and doesn't center on the player as much as it should, though horizontal movement also has its problems. Or how you get an ability that's supposed to slow time to slow down everything around you, but some specific things just... don't get slowed down, and you have to find that out on your own.Or how a lot of the bosses have attacks with effects that you have no way of expecting unless you've seen them before. You can learn through repetition and then they're not so bad, but they lack the intuitive design of Mania's bosses. Speaking of which, the boss fights in Superstars drag on... and on... and ... and ... Nearly every. Single. One. Even if you play perfectly, they just take too freaking long. They're designed like Mario bosses that have a lot of buildup to taking three hits, but a lot of them take the usual 6-8 hits. Even the ones that do take only three hits are a slog to get through. Not helped at all by the short, generic boss music. But I'll get to that later.A minor issue about the special stages: You're supposed to be able to latch onto nearby objects to swing your way to the emerald, but the triggers feel random. Sometimes I can grab something that looks way too far away, and other times I can't grab something that's right next to me. It feels like whether you can grab an object depends on its proximity to the camera. Not the player, the .Finally, the music... "mixed bag" doesn't even begin to describe it. Some of the music is amazing and may even be around Mania quality. It makes sense; Tee Lopes worked on it. A lot of the music is good but not great. And then there's Jun Senoue. Please Sega, do NOT let this man near a synthesizer, he can't make Genesis-style music to save his life. If you told me half of this game's music was Sonic 4 Episode 3's unused OST, I'd believe you. Unfortunately, that includes very common songs like boss and menu themes, so you'll be hearing "okay" music much more often than great music.Really, the whole game feels like a mixed bag. Some parts of it are classic Sonic quality, while others are pretty forgettable. Get it at a discount.(Oh, and I haven't played the battle mode much, but it's fun. But spraypaints are consumable? Are you kidding me?!)

_childDocuments_.review: Gosh, it hurts to say I don't recommend this. I really wanted this to be the "real Sonic 4." And it really looked like it would be. Then I played the game. First warning sign was when it notified me that I needed an Epic Games account to play the game. I don't have one and, being that I bought the game on Steam, I shouldn't need one. So that multiplayer that the game advertised so much requires you to use an account you didn't buy the game on. I’ll mention the vile Denuvo by name only, as we all know every new Sonic game seems to always have it…The levels are all decent. I really liked having new areas for once, instead of visiting Green Hill for the umpteenth time. Feels like classic Sonic gameplay and the level layouts and momentum feel good to mess with. I even really liked some of the gimmicks. The bosses were a pretty easy, but I expected that for the first boss or two. Bosses never got harder until the very end of the game, and not in a fun way either. Having the player wait about a minute or so between hits on a boss that goes down in less than 6 hits (often only 3 hits) is boring, even if the design of the boss is cool. The music is so middle of the road; one track will be really good and then the next few sound like they were ripped from Sonic 4 (which, need I remind you, has some of the worst-sounding music in the franchise). Having mid Sonic music is a cardinal sin, as it’s one of the best things about this series.I really wanted to like this; after Frontiers, it looked like it was a good time to be a Sonic fan again. The game isn't horrible, but with the current asking price and the nickel-and-diming practice of the DLC, your money is better spent elsewhere. Maybe pick it up on a sale? I hope they fix this game up some, because it could be a really good one if they iron out the problems. I was more excited for this than Super Mario Wonder and SEGA dropped the ball again. A real shame.
