_childDocuments_.review: For a game I truly looked forward to since its first trailer, this game is a disappointment. For starters, this game felt slow for a Sonic the Hedgehog game. The controls for all the playable characters both felt slippery and without proper acceleration. Every special stage was too easy, for both the chaos emeralds and medals. The "Battle Mode" is extremely underwhelming. I know the creators are proud of their work but did almost every stage need a cut-scene? No. This game is not balanced when it comes to difficulty.Sonic the hedgehog is well known to be a fast paced games. This game does not measure up. Using the spin dash at any point starts quick for a second, then back to zero miles per hour in 5 seconds with nothing in the way. Only time I personally felt the game went fast is when it was over. I may have 19 hours of game play as of publishing this review, but this game is too short.All the characters movement was slow and sluggish, almost like the playable characters had weights in their shoes. At some points I wanted to make evasive maneuvers, but the controls were restricting. Sometimes the game would feel as if all stages had ice on the ground, sometimes glue. Again about the spin dash and speed, the movement speed was inconsistent. I will say, not all the time I disliked the controls but it felt it varied at some points.Not too much to say about ALL the special stages. None of these side stages felt difficult, no challenge. I know there was some nostalgia from the spinning Sonic 1 special stages but they were incredibly easy. The "George of the Jungle" like special stages are boring too. Also the special stages felt like the game was holding you hand along the way. Also obtaining medals felt underwhelming and a waste of time.Speaking of the Medals, "Battle Mode". Battle Mode could have been bigger than it was. maybe more competitive or extended somehow. I played a few times and it got boring way too fast. It's fun to try once but that's it. The medals being used for customization really sucks. Again like earlier, could have been used for something bigger or a way to extend the game or more to unlock for the main game. Medals are useless, change my mind.There are so many cut-scenes it is not funny. Before and after there is a boss, between stages, the Sonic 1 special stages. It felt like every few seconds, cut-scene. One main time the cut-scenes annoyed me was retrying the final bosses.Why did I have to watch the cut-scenes for the final boss so much? The difficulty. The main story from beginning to the end was an easy cake walk. The second story? the difficulty ramps up to a setting this game should have been at. The main game left me treating this game like a fidget toy and not trying to hard to play. When I played the second story, I felt like I was bullied. Not complaining about the challenge, I'm complaining that the whole game should have been this way. On a side note, the stories final boss is something else. No matter how many rings you have, you could get one shot by lasers. I had to skip the two cut-scenes just the restart. Two phases took me 9 minutes to beat. Most of my play time was sunk into this boss. The difficulty went from tolerable to why is he trying harder than Eggman? Also the True final boss sucks. All I have to say about this is "Have an indicator that you are suppose to charge at the homing rocks at the end" the game does not hint at this.Now the good things I liked about this game. many playable characters. All the characters feel unique in their own way, not copy and pasted. Even the new fifth playable character is fun to play as. The chaos emerald super powers are fun to use as well. Had the main game been harder like the second story, I would have utilized the chaos emeralds far more. Also turning super is always fun too. I did not mind the fresh new look of this game I liked it. However honestly, I prefer the original 16-bit look better. As a final remark, Overall I give this game a solid 3/10. This game should not be priced where it is. Too many bugs I've encountered. Not much content in this game. Game is too short. Playing with a friend does not make the game better. This game does not have much replay value. There are much better Sonic the Hedgehog games listed out there for cheaper.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best 2D Sonic SEGA’s in-house talent (with some help) has produced since Sonic & Knuckles. Yes, it does feel like playing a proper Classic Sonic game and SEGA finally “gets” Sonic again. Now that I’ve finished the main story, I can appreciate what Sonic Team has done with this one. It grew on me and now I kind of love it. If they can iron out some of this game’s flaws in the next entry, Classic Sonic is finally in good hands at home. The main issue with Superstars is the same issue with almost all of Sonic Team’s games: It’s a bit inconsistent in quality. Sonic Mania was revelatory in its thorough greatness and it seems like the people at Sonic Team wanted to prove themselves, which is likely why they brought back Ohshima-san. While Mania’s music and level design were a bit more inspired and memorable than Superstars (down to using the elemental shields in certain stages), Sonic Team has mostly recaptured the feel of the Genesis / Mega Drive games. The passion of super fans getting a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity edges out the old devs recapturing lightning in a bottle. Yet unlike Sonic 4, Superstars can sit alongside the first four games. Classic Sonic has a very particular vibe. Being honest, the first few games were a fun, hot mess held up high by a strong, unique audiovisual design. With Ohshima on board, Superstars of course nails the look of the older games and the new character fits right in. The soundtrack however is a bit inconsistent, with the worst offenders being the tunes you will hear the most often: the sleepy bonus stage theme and the quickly repetitive Act 2 boss theme. In Sonic 4, it seemed as though Jun Senoe was trying to emulate the sound of the Mega Drive’s YM2612 without actually using one. While his Eggman theme doesn’t quite work, his synths and compositions in Superstars overall come much closer to that Mega Drive sound, with his Press Factory themes almost sounding like something out of Sonic 3D Blast. Of course Tee Lopes graces this game with his usual bangers. The other composers provide some standout tracks as well, with Tails’ Frozen Base and Pinball Carnival being particular highlights that are up to the high Sonic music standard. It’s not as consistently awesome as Mania’s soundtrack but it’s quite good. As for the gameplay, it’s not up there with Sonic 3 or Mania, but it sits above Sonic 2. Sacrilege? No. Each zone in Sonic 2 has its gimmicks, but there’s honestly not much going on in Hilltop or Mystic Cave. Meanwhile, Sonic 3 and Mania have unique gimmicks in every . In Superstars the level layouts remind me of Sonic 2 and CD, but without the need to account for time travel, and with thirty years of hindsight to make each stage feel more unique and have things flow better. With stage gimmicks, Mania is again more varied and inspired, but Superstars still has some fun level mechanics I’ve never seen in a Sonic game. And like Mania, Superstars also features a boss that’s a throwback to a classic SEGA game. When you get to it, if you know, you’ll know. It put a huge smile on my face. Sonic Superstars is a  Sonic game with some great moments. The only real flaws are an underpowered spin dash and poor sound mixing with insanely loud effects that can drown out the music. The special stages also aren’t great. Everything else is nitpicking. If you love Classic Sonic, you’ll enjoy Superstars. Is it worth $60? It depends on how badly you want your Classic Sonic fix. If you grew up with the Genesis games and can’t get enough of them, you’ll get your money’s worth with 8 hours out of fun out of this. Otherwise I can easily recommend this when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable Stylist Classic Sonic... if you can get it for £20 or lessTLDR: The game is a great transformation from the original 2D classics and captures the original handling of SEGA sonic impressively well. The gameplay remains fast, but the bosses slow the pace down considerably and cannot be multi-hit in succession. The final boss initially felt extremely frustrating and cheap, but with enough attempts it becomes clear to player what they will need to achieve. This however did little to sway my initial opinion.I really like how the chaos emeralds now have individual purpose rather than just a collection task for the end goal of obtaining the super form or true ending and will make your run far easier depending on the emeralds you collect, I found the blue, red and yellow emeralds the most useful out of the bunch. Though collecting all seven will allow you to use the classic super forms for all characters which grant you extra speed, jump height, and in 90% of cases invincibility.You'll hear complaints about the music, although I felt I couldn't relate to this one without direct comparisons. The music is very good in some areas, but I also acknowledge it falls off hard in others.The game has the main sonic base story and a new character story for you to run through which did make the repeat run through less taxing on my withering attention spanThe developers IMO hit the style of classic sonic on the head. Giving a vibrant pop to each level as you'd expect. With performance being impressive even whilst at 4K.--- Things I didn't Like ---Whilst there is much to like about the game, let's talk about the first thing a player will notice about the game. £60 price tag? Absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ not. The game tries to justify its price tag with an online multiplayer feature, where you play as sonic avatar bots in random battles in an arena . I do not think about this when I think sonic multiplayer. The OG SEGA classic at least understood that sonic games were about going fast and racing your opponents to the end goal. With the content you get it's far from AAA value, but nonetheless its still worth a reasonable price tag.The gold coin currency is useless in single-player, which is what you're buying the game for. There is nothing else to be added here, its used to get skins for the multiplayer mode which I will never touch.The characters all possess some kind of trait which grants them a differing play styles over others, for example Tails can fly, Amy has a double jump, Knuckles can climb and glide. Sonic... can go... fast? Yes despite being on the poster, Sonic appears to be the weakest character out of all of them. Even the new character introduced, can climb walls and turn into a fire breathing dragon on super form (which can move in any direction). - I want remind you that every character will have access to the emerald powers you pick up, so there really isn't much incentive to play sonic other than the fact his name and face is on the "box", I'm aware of sonic's " ground dash" ability but i never found a universal use case for it. They are slow, they cannot be "skilled" in the traditional sense, I.e. someone with great mechanics and understanding cannot kill a boss quickly due to I-frames and "waiting" which makes some bosses feel like they overstay their welcome massively. _childDocuments_.review: This game is almost there, but there are some major issues that need to be fixed before I give a positive review and actually recommend to friends (Dev Team, Please Read)Necessary changes the game needs as soon as possible:1. Co-op needs to be changed. Give us a splitscreen option in the settings menu that is on by default or make the game zoom out when someone is left behind. Please don't teleport people around so much. Sonic games are so fast that this just does not work well. I really want to play this game with my friends and family but the experience is terrible right now.2. Boss battles need serious changes. For one, getting killed in one hit should not mean needlessly redoing a 3 minute fight, please add more checkpoints! The fights should also go by faster with less invincibility frames (for attacks other than chaos emerald ones) or significantly less delay in between boss moves. The fun of classic Sonic boss fights was getting good at the fights and sneaking in a lot of extra hits to get better win times. Also, players want to spend mostly the entire fight playing, not watching the boss fly into the background and get frustrated between every hit again and again. The final boss of the main and second campaign both take hours and hours and hours to beat which is not fun.Things the game does well:1. The art direction is vibrant and beautiful. My favorite level is the haunted carnival.2. The physics are great! The characters all play like they used to, with the nice touch of the drop dash from mania on Sonic. Amy is a blast!3. The time attack skips bosses, that is a very good idea.4. The world map and quality of life features are amazing, the multiplayer battle mode is really fun.5. The new special stages are well made and the coin minigames at checkpoints are also a blast.6. The little character levels are charming, love the Fang Chase and Amy carrying around Trip.7. Most of the bosses are really good. Just need to make those tweaks to how they work and they'll be perfect.8. The chaos emerald powers are amazing! I love this feature and want to see it return in other games!Other changes that would be nice later:1. The story is confusing, we need more story context. The true final boss has zero explanation and zero cinematics leading up to it so it's hard to feel invested in the fight. Trip's reason for following eggman is unexplained in the game, and we don't even know everyone arrived on a new island or why.Changes for the future of the series:1. You got the physics right but please do not design levels like Sonic 1 or CD. Most Sonic fans prefer levels like Sonic 2, Sonic 3, or Sonic Mania. Slopes and building speed in the level design itself is the reason classic sonic physics are so good.2. The music should not replicate the Genesis using the same instruments, with all due respect it does not sound pleasant. Please stop doing this.Sincerely, a big Sonic fan, thank you for keeping the franchise going strong after all of these years! ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely not worth a dime of its full price unless you absolutely want a fix of a new 2D Sonic game. Pick Mania over this, or many of the other 2D Sonic games that exist. I literally played this game with a roommate on their account, 100%ed it through family share on my own, and then bought it just to reaffirm to others that this is a very poor execution of what 2D Sonic could and should be and that they should look elsewhere.The gameplay is pretty standard for Sonic, you go fast toward the right side of the screen. The problems, however, begin when you attempt to perform this feat. Level design is very unappealing and gimmicky, and riddled with obstacles that are placed in such a way that it's entirely unfun to hit something that you would not have reacted to while running at mach 20. At the very least, we should have a more zoomed-out camera so that it's fair game to see and dodge things that are placed directly in your way. This all becomes 10x worse in the second story, where they just spam spikes and bottomless pits and more dangerous enemies far more frequently than before. IF you play the game enough to know the levels, then a clean playthrough can look and even feel pretty convincing, but the road to that memorization of each level is not pleasant.Of the five characters, only two are anything to write home about. Sonic plays about as well as you'd expect. Tails is very good, and has more horizontal movement speed when descending during flight, which you can take advantage of. Amy is fine, and her double jump can be welcome, but she's not going to keep up with the previous two. Knuckles was torn apart in this game, and is horrendous to play as, and will have you wondering why they even allowed him to remain the way he is. The new character is fun, and a welcome addition to the cast.Boss design is baaaad. A couple exceptions exist, they're not all terrible, but by and large the bosses are unfun to fight, take forever to allow you to hurt them, and are painfully long as a result. Several just have instakill attacks because why not, including the late and/or final bosses which are 10-minute-long slogs with narrow damage windows and potentially minutes-long downtime between being able to hurt them in the first place.The music is largely forgettable, though you'll probably find yourself unable to forget the title screen and/or super theme after playing for long enough, which are a lengthy 30 seconds before looping for you to get your fix.The multiplayer is ridiculously poor. Singleplayer is already rough enough just for playing through the game, but when you add more people the camera can't figure out who to follow. I've played with two, three, and four people locally, through the entire game, multiple times, and the camera never understands the assignment. You'll be booted offscreen for being last in line about as often as you'll be booted offscreen for being first in line. During any automated sections, only one person will remain visible as the others mash A in order to attempt respawning over and over and over again only to fly offscreen again within a second or two.This is the second-worst game I've ever played and completed.

_childDocuments_.review: I would cautiously recommend this game. It's good, but not $60 good. They're charging full price for what is clearly a budget title. Wait for a sale.Many people have complained about the mandatory Epic Games integration for playing online, and the fact they hid Denuvo being in this game. These will not affect my review, since they are outside the game, but I don't blame anyone for not wanted to buy this game for those reasons.The core gameplay is classic Sonic, fully intact. This isn't a Sonic 4 situation, you can do anything you could in those old games. The key deciding factor in this game's quality, then, is level design. I want to make it clear that all levels have a degree of competence no matter how bad they get. There's good places to build up speed, low automation, and several available paths to keep subsequent playthroughs fresh. That being said, the levels are hit and miss. They start out as fun levels with moments of frustration and slowly transition to frustrating levels with moments of fun. This is usually takes the form of cheap ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ you would never know was there without playing the level several time before (classic Sonic, I know). It gets really bad near the end, where your basically required to tiptoe through the level. It's as if they don't know how to make Sonic hard without pranking the player. Many of these cheap moments would be fixed if the zoomed out the camera a little. Since multiplayer has a more zoomed out camera, it makes me think that they designed all these levels with multiplayer without testing singleplayer.This game's main gimmick is the new emerald powers. Collecting a chaos emerald will grant you a new power to mess around with. They are activated on a radial menu, and they grant you a certain ability for a limited time, or until you get hit. I liked these abilities more than I thought I would. Since they only last so long, you'll be rushing through the level as fast possible to make the most of it, but you can't go too fast, or else you'll get hit by an enemy or stage hazard and lose it. The abilities themselves are fine, they have their situational uses. The minigame to get the emeralds suck. You grapple across points in a void, and it's as shallow as a puddle. They're all incredibly easy, with the bizarre exception of the green emerald, which randomly requires a very specific strategy and good luck. After that, it's back to baby mode for the rest.There are four playable characters. Yup. Four. Sonic is the one that generally plays best, with his playstyle seeming to be the basis for most levels. The only thing I don't like, and this is something that baffles me, is the new(?) delay on his drop dash. You have to hold the jump button for maybe a half-second before it comes out. This makes his ability much less responsive, and there are times when you simply do not have enough airtime to initiate his ability, a problem no other character has. Now, I haven't played Sonic Mania in a while, so it's possible his drop dash was always like this. If that's the case, it didn't bother me nearly as much back then. Tails is alright, he's what you expect. He's just who you pick to make navigation easier. Knuckles is where we start getting into problems. None of the levels (aside from the one specifically made for him) feel like they accommodate his ability to climb and glide. I could not tell you how many times I tried to explore with him only to hit a ceiling, or the times I tried to glide over a chunk of level design only to glide away from the level and into the endless bottomless pit that surround it. This, combined with his lower jump, made playing as him feel detrimental compared to anyone else. Amy is fine, but a bit lame. She can double jump, and she's swings her hammer around when jumping, allowing her to destroy badniks she normally couldn't. If she holds the jump button after a double jump until she hits the ground, she can swing her hammer repeatedly while freely moving. The hammer based parts of her moveset are unengaging, they simply let her kill bad guys a little easier, it doesn't change the way she actually  The only reason to use her, then, is her double jump, which is one of the most boring abilities possible in a platformer. There's nothing really wrong with Amy, she just has missed potential.After the first few zones, the bosses suck. They're the genre of boss where you have to wait for an opportunity to attack, and these fights go on for far too long. They take the same number of hits as Genesis bosses, but can't be attacked freely. Emerald powers help a bit, but only so much. There's more I'd like to say that I'll have to save for the spoiler section. It is because of the bosses that I think this game is best enjoyed in time attack mode, where bosses are skipped.Presentation is generally okay. The characters look good and are well animated. Some of the levels have interesting themes, like a haunted carnival or a golden palace. The art style is boring, and some assets are shockingly low poly. Sound design is lacking,  There are many times when it feels like a sound should be playing, but doesn't. Music quality is all over the place. Most of it is fine, some of it is incredible, and some (particularly the boss themes) are horrible. Jun Sunoue's compositions aren't bad, but he insists on these dinky-ass synths. He needs to be kept away from classic Sonic. The above three points lead to the whole game feeling very cheap.Sonic Superstars is essentially good. There's clearly a good understanding of the essence of classic Sonic, but it fumbles in some key areas. The core gameplay and some good levels are just enough for me to recommend this game, albeit at a reduced price. $60 is wack. I saw someone on Twitter compare this game to the Advance games, and I think the comparison is apt. With some more polish, this game could have been fantastic. I guess that's nothing new for Sonic.

_childDocuments_.review: "Sonic Superstars" is the best 2D Sonic since the Sega Genesis, and it's the best overall Sonic game since "Sonic Adventure 2". I have logged over 100 hours on the Switch version and 10+ hours so far on Steam. No, It's not a long "epic" game like "Sonic Frontiers". All those hours are sheer replay value. Like the classic Sonic games, Superstars is effortlessly replayable with giant levels that offer a variety of paths. In true Sonic fashion, I will sometimes take an odd turn and find myself in an area I've never seen before despite playing the level dozens of times. Sometimes I stick to a tried and true path, and sometimes I like to see what happens if I veer off course.This is a good time to talk about the new Emerald Powers. In the original Sonic games, the Chaos Emeralds were collectables that didn't do anything until you got them all. In Superstars, you now unlock new powers for each emerald that you collect. These open up new options for mobility or strategy. Earlier I talked about selecting paths. If I miss a jump, the new emerald powers can help me course correct. The red emerald can let you shoot through the air like a meteor until the timer runs out, and the green emerald grows a beanstalk that lets you reach high places. Other powers are useful only situationally, but are nifty. The yellow emerald can slow down time to make certain areas and obstacles more manageable. You ever get paranoid about drowning in a Sonic game? The light blue emerald lets you breath underwater while also letting you swim. One emeralds reveals hidden platforms and items for a time, and another generates clones of Sonic that can collect items, clear the screen of enemies, and even damage bosses when they are out of reach. The game is nice enough to "prime" certain emerald powers automatically when they might be useful, so you often don't even have to select them manually. The new powers aren't really a "core" gameplay feature. You can beat the game without using these powers, but once you unlock them they open up new gameplay possibilities on replay.There are 11 "zones" in the game, and 23 stages (or "acts") between those 11 areas. There's a good mix of tried and true Sonic ideas and new gimmicks. For me the highlights of the game are a factory level with a giant hydraulic press that is constantly hammering the ground, a cyberspace level that transforms everything into voxels, and a space station level with a time flow gimmick straight out of "Tenet" or "Dr. Strange". I never found myself growing bored of a particular gimmick. Once you get to Speed Jungle, Superstars doesn't let up with introducing new ideas and directions in each level. Everything makes an impression and nothing overstays its welcome.That creative approach extends to the roster of bosses and mid-bosses, which might be the strongest in the history of the series. If you've heard anyone griping about the bosses in Superstars, it's because many of the boss battles are mean and uncompromising. These are bosses in the truest, old-school sense of the term: straight up gatekeepers who will skill check you. You get a few soft balls in the earlier parts of the game, but once you get into the latter half you WILL have your skills tested. The final bosses, all three of them, are particularly brutal. This is not a game where you march towards an inevitable victory. You've got to earn it, and in this age of "soft" casualized gaming I find this uncompromising approach refreshing.I said there were three final bosses. That's because there are three "story modes," although one of them is literally just a boss battle. The first story mode is your standard relatively "chill" normal difficulty level, while the second story mode is downright MEAN. Without spoiling anything, the character you play as in the hard story mode has a useful moveset that you will want to familiarize yourself with. This is the only bone the game tosses you in this mode, and it expects you to use it to the fullest. The main story mode can be played through as one of four (later five) characters, but you only need to beat it as one character for the sake of completion. You know who they are, you know what they can do, and you've seen their faces plastered on the game's cover. Each of the four main characters has an optional level that only they can play through during the main story mode, which is catered to their particular skillset. If you're not playing as that character, you will temporarily switch to them if you decide to play that particular "act." An usual choice for a Sonic game, but I like how it breaks things up and adds a little variety to a playthrough.The story modes are the meat of the game, with a couple of multiplayer modes functioning as a mild gravy. Multiplayer is often an afterthought in Sonic, and that continues to be the case here. There's co-op play in the main story mode, but I haven't touched it. Co-op in platformers is not my cup of tea. There's also a Battle Mode that's pretty okay. You can build a custom robot character by purchasing components with medals that you've collected in the story modes. One nice touch is your custom robot becomes the boss of Cyber Station Zone. If you want to fight Metal Sonic during the main game, you can unlock his parts and build him. There are also parts for building "metal" versions of the other playable characters, and you can even make a robot Nights from "Nights Into Dreams". All that said, I think a traditional versus mode in the style of Sonic 2 or 3 would have been better. Each round of Battle Mode is pretty short and you only have one round where you actually get to race people in a stage. I mainly like building a robot and seeing it show up in the "real" game.I honestly don't have a lot of gripes with Superstars. Frozen Base Zone Act 2 was the only part that disappointed me. Instead of being a proper level, it's just a short shoot 'em up segment. The following level more than makes up for it, though. From a graphical standpoint, I think they went a little too hard on the depth-of-field effect. The unlockable fifth playable character also has a cool super form that is unfortunately underutilized in the game. One thing I won't knock is the music. A lot of people have been throwing shade at this game's soundtrack, but I honestly love it. I don't even mind the unusual mix of "arranged" and "Sega Genesis" tracks. The YM2612 songs are strangely appropriate.If you're wondering how Superstars will perform on your computer, it doesn't require much in the way of resources. My computer was built a decade ago and was basically meant to run games from 2013, and it can handle "Sonic Superstars" just fine. With 720p and all graphical effects disabled except for shadows, my old PC gets a stable 60FPS for most of the game. Like the Switch version, Super Sonic tends to cause a drop in FPS, but not to an unplayable degree. This might not be an issue on modern systems. Basically, any computer from the past decade should be able to run this game smoothly on low settings. Even on high settings, older PCs might not encounter performance issues until Egg Fortress Zone, which is the most demanding part of the game. If you own some sort of modern super computer, you can ignore the contents of this paragraph.(UPDATE: This game runs GREAT on the Steam Deck and deserves "Verified" status. Performance is basically flawless at 720p with High settings. 1080p/High also works nicely, but you will see some frame drops with Super Sonic during Last Story Mode and some smaller frame drops here and there in the other story modes.)This game is getting a lot of mixed reviews at the moment. I feel like I'm caught in the Mandela Effect. Is everyone else playing the same game I'm playing? Have I slipped into the Twilight Zone? When a game as innocuous as this gets such a strong negative response, it's usually a sign of a "narrative." I say ignore the narrative and give "Sonic Superstars" a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: The game launched with Denuvo DRM after a lengthy pre-order period where it wasn't mentioned on the store page. It has now been added to the store page several hours after release. I've confirmed that without a valid Denuvo phone-home token, the game will not start (the error window also blames Steam for being offline, which is a cheap way for Denuvo to shift the blame). This is all the more galling considering it's a Unity game and Denuvo on Unity is notoriously easy to pirate. Paying customers are going to be inconvenienced for nothing.Upon startup the game screams at you to log into an Epic Games account, interrupting the game's intro movie. It says you "need" the account to play; you do not; if you click the almost hidden X in the login prompt, you can play the entire game except the online version of its multiplayer Battle Mode. Even players that do have an Epic Games account are demanded to log in every time they start the game up, which is a nuisance design.By default the game automatically installs Epic Online Services to your PC, without warning or acceptance. This manner of installation is borderline malware. It can be prevented if you rename or delete the installer prior to launching the game, but it will return if the game is reinstalled, or updates, or if you use Steam's "Verify integrity of game files" feature.It's a lot of frustration and upset for players considering it's completely unnecessary; I've played other cross-platform EOS-using games that needed no personally-identifying Epic Games account or the installation of any EOS software on my PC.Lastly the game has upset players by making one of its DLCs - the Comic Book Skin Pack - available for a ridiculously short 24 minutes and 3 seconds when it launched. After that the DLC has been made inaccessible and most players who've spent upwards of $60 on the "Superstar Deluxe Edition" have been unfairly left with an incomplete product.

_childDocuments_.review: Way better than the reviews would lead you to believe. Looks beautiful, controls great, sounds great, good classic sonic level design, S3K type story telling and level transitions, hallelujah. Lot's of people don't like the music, and I guess it isn't anything you'll have stuck in your head after playing (save for a couple songs), but it all sounds great. Emerald powers are a really interesting and fun addition to the classic sonic formula that you don't have to use if you don't want to. Special stages are fairly good. The biggest complaint I see thrown around is the bosses and honestly I don't get it. Classic sonic bosses have been infamously really easy to tank through and kill quickly, so making bosses with more i-frames and more complex move sets feels like a natural evolution of the formula. They feel like boss fights now, not just a quick enemy to beat at the end of a stage. The end game ones even get difficult which is a novelty for classic sonic games. You can still obliterate most of them with the chaos emerald powers, so if you really hate them you don't have to bother. Fang returning is awesome and they really go all out with his boss fights. Trip gets the knuckles treatment with a harder campaign with alternate level design using her abilities. They pull from the 3D games by having a "Last Story" which contains the super sonic final boss, it's honestly pretty good and harder than Doomsday and Egg Reverie combined, really strict on rings but the boss itself has a neat move set. All of this wrapped together with beautiful animated cutscenes. Honestly 2D sonic now confidently holds a place right next to 3D sonic in the coming era, and I'm all here for it. This game deserves to sit next to the classic trilogy and mania in the pantheon of classic sonic games. But of course I'm cursed to like all the sonic games that most people are mixed on.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 25.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 10 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 10 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realise that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: I've haven't played a Sonic Game in quite some time that is so close to being a new classic, yet at the same consistently it fumbles on it's feet to try and innovate. Sonic Superstars is the most mixed bag Classic Sonic game I've ever played.  Pro's- Half of the soundtrack hits hard. (Bridge Island Act 1, and 2, Golden Capital Act 2, Sky Temple, Pinball Carnival Act 1 &2- The controls are fine tuned to perfection. They nailed the controls here.- The level design is sincerely great and fun as heck to explore. - Game oozes with so much charm with character animations and level aestheticsCon's- The other half of the soundtrack, just plain sucks. Not a single one is fun or entertaining. All are waiting games, with most of the final bosses having WAYYYYYY TO MANY INSTA-KILL moments, and most take way too long for there own good. - Multiplayer is horribly designed with its horrific camera for local. Missed opportunity not having online co-op.- Not enough content to warrant a $59 dollar price tags.- Special stages are ok, but the fact we are only relegated to one emerald per stage kinda sucks. I want to love superstars so much. But those horrific boss fights, especially the late game ones, along with the meh special stages, mixed soundtrack with half that reminds of games made 10-12 years prior, Sonic Superstars is just a mixed bag. At its worst, I'll never run through it ever again. At it's best, its a fun distraction every now and then, that has some great level design and control.

It worked great as a marketing gimmick in the early 90's - 'blast processing', remember? - but we are a lot more educated about what makes good video games work than we were back then, and, well, the game doing loop-de-loops for you and bouncing you all over the place aren't gameplay mechanics this cynical old bastard isn't impressed by anymore.But perhaps, my innocently virginal 14-year old self might have been,

poor boss design, likely done to keep a full team of 4 from clowning on every fight, bosses have elongated periods of inalienability, this makes the fights drag on for upwards of 8 minutes which is an unacceptable length, the bosses are also plagued by cheap shots that leave the player unable to get any rings back or worse instantly kill the player, for some bosses the powers are a saving grace that trivialise the fight but im not giving points for the game having 2 broken mechanics somewhat balance each other out.its possible this game improves dramatically in co-op but the game has no online co-op, couch only. this is baffling, a co-op focused game developed during the pandemic and which already has PVP with online functionality (why?) is like a car being made without an engine but extra reigns for more horses.what wouldn't be fixed in co-op would be the games awful OST. despite getting Tee Lopes back from mania the games score lacks all identity, instead hearkening back to the sonic 4 soundtrack which sounded like a Megadrive being hurled down the stairs and its not much better here.the games sole bright spots are the graphics and physics model. sonic and co handle beautifully and look incredible in motion. all the characters have traits that set them apart without prioritising any one over the rest, the only exception might be amy as her hammer allows her to hit bosses when no other character can which easily makes her the best only matched by sonics drop dash which both have the benefit of making the game go by faster.100% completion is a nightmare, I might have recommend the game on a steep discount after the first run through but my journey to the true final boss made me change that perspective.The rumour is the mania team was disbanded because they utterly clowned on sonic team and made them salty. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up on Sonic games since the Genesis, I cannot really suggest this game.  I have over 30 minutes at the time of this review and that means I'm about 3 worlds in right now, and all I can do for the most part is echo the concerns others have about this game.  Sega has done as Sega will always do and that means they've included Denuvo (please search as to what Denuvo is and how it can affect your performance of games when it's installed) but this time they made things even more of a nuisance by  Epic Games Store services to handle online multiplayer so Cross Play can be achieved.  Maybe that's not so bad to you but I personally cannot see the online play being something you or your kids will come back to here because it's just a simple "Collect the stars" mode.  The real multiplayer   You're having EGS installed on launch everytime against your consent and get a browser opening to register on Epic every.  Single.  Time.  It's annoying to deal with and a waste.  I don't want EGS on my PC more than I absolutely need to in order to play with my friends as I'm one of the many who HATE Epic and their politics and practices.  As for the game though?  Sega  isn't aware of the "K.I.S.S." method and once again they've made some changes to the physics of how you would expect a side scrolling platormer Sonic to handle and it feels sluggish and gross.  I would even amost dare say Sonic 4's physics were better.  Of course I'm a bit upset at this so take this with a grain of salt as the game plays fine.  Fine is about as good as I can put it really as it doesn't really wow me or feel great to play with.  The lives system is not present in this game like many games are making optional or doing away with, and they've replaced earning lives at 100 rings with medals.  These medals are only good for earning cosmetics for the super lack luster battle mode and do nothing cool for you in local play (single or multiplayer).  Special stages are strange too this time around in that you're swinging around from point to point to earn medals or the usual chaos emeralds, but it feels too, off.  You can't particularly target where you wanna go in the 3D space, which means you can't turn the camera or your character to try and target a more advantageous swinging point, making things more frustrating.  Chaos Emeralds are in their usual giant golden rings hidden across stages and now there are giant blue rings to earn medals, so if you don't care abnout battle mode just save yourself the time and avoid the blue ones.  At the time of this review I'm HEAVILY considering a refund.  Game is SEVERELY overpriced for what it is at $60 .  Wait for a sale of 50% or better so you don't feel entirely like you wasted money.

There were 2 things that actually made me hate this game, 1 inconstancy, and 2 bad level design.   There was inconsistency everywhere, one song sounds great and then the next one from sonic 4 ep1, sometimes I clipped though the ground, sometimes there was alot of care in certain graphical assets and then non in another. The best example I can think of is hitting an enemy or even a boss the same way and both times getting different results, one where you get hit anotherThis inconsistency bleed into the level design which includes the bosses (more about them later). now one thing before I explain why the level design suck  I would to note that the LEVEL GIMMICKS ARE GOOD, HOWEVER THE LEVEL SURROUNDING THEM ARE BAD.  The level design of this game is  very close to sonic 1 and Knuckle's Chaotix  but worse. Every stage is just paced like marble zone, fun gimmick or set piece followed by auto scrolling or annoying platform section that doesn't allow you to preserve the momentum you earned. You mat be wondering why did I include Knuckle's Chaotix as an inspiration and that is because this game is infatuated with vertical platforming sections, but with worse vertical mobility. You know what else this game is infatuated with WAITING both in level and in the bosses. THE EASIEST WORST BOSSES IN SONIC HISTORY WITH mostly BELLOW AVERAGE MUSIC. Hey you know when sonic games reward you for being tricky and getting extra hits on bosses, well you get punished for that in this game and have to watch lengthy cutscene long animation of attacks that you can't really interact with until the boss presents themselves for another hit. Also a lot of info on how to defeat or fight these bosses are very poorly conveyed which is saying a lot since usually you just have to jump on them and ya good. Nah you have to hit this enemy that the boss spawned but you have to hit them before they land and there is no visual cue telling you this, so you trial and error the bosses since you have infinite live and the designer don't have to worry if something is a lives sink. I know I am one of the few people that thinks lives are a good mechanic that has great potential that no one see but  you can't just ignore how they make the game more bs just because there is less to lose on death. Which reminds me that after around the halfway point of the game they just decide to throw insta-deaths every where so much so that having super sonic on sometimes was more of a liability that I earned. Another this is that the game constantly takes you out of super sonic at random time but also right before the boss. So if you activate super sonic before a boss and their cutscene loads, congrats you now have 49 ring for the boss fight and no super sonic.Lastly let me talk about the final bosses. The normal final bosses is like one of the worst bosses in the game. No way to really speed up this boss (in phase 1) and you are constantly at the mercy of RNG. You don't really have a way to be proactive in this fight  so you fell like you have less control while fighting it. The extra story boss does this in reverse but is in my opinion is a lot better. You have more control on the pace of the fight compared to the normal one and you have the slower phase as phase 2 rather than phase one. There are a couple of ways to make the fight faster and easier if you think a little bit. the true final boss however is THE WORST BOSS IN THE GAME. It has mechanic it never explains so you think that most of it is RNG. The dash they give you takes rings and unless you figure out the mechanics, congrats you can't even use it effectively. Also the fight ends with a quick time event and dodge sequence that if you mess up you have to redo that sequence. I didn't also address the most important factor to the true final boss, because the game is super stalling in the super sonic fight you are just going to timeout in very inopportune times cause animations that will make you lose more rings than getting knocked back. In the end the thing that hurt more than all thing points above was that anytime there was something I liked about this game I got 5 things I didn't like about this game. I really wanted to like this game and beat it through hoping it would get better. Unfortunately that didn't happen and under the best of conditions I can not recommend this game. If you don't have sonic mania, just get mania it is a 1/3 of the price and one of the best 2D sonic games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is bad. They managed to capture the physics of the Retro Engine perfectly, which is really cool to see in 3D. Level themes and design are alright. Definitely not close to the beautiful, creative, and fun original levels in Mania, but good enough. One thing that definitely sucks is how they handle save files. They have moved from the Sonic 3 and Mania system to something akin to New Super Mario Bros. It really kills replay-ability. After completing the campaign as Sonic, I had no desire to restart and try again as another character. Also, the placement of Special Stage rings suck. One per Zone? Why?Music is hit or miss. Most songs arranged (and some compositions) by Jun Senoue sound awful. It's not really the quality of his synths, because I'd argue that most of his Sonic 4 compositions sound nice on the ears. This feels like half-assed work. Along with this, there is no cohesive sound design. Songs differ in composition and arrangement style between acts. Playing Speed Jungle gives you whiplash of getting into multiple car accidents every 2 minutes.There is nothing in a video game that makes you despise it more than an awful, un-fun, miserable final boss. Sonic's boss is tolerable, but to get the Super Sonic ending, you have to beat Trip's boss. Trip's final boss is one of the worst designed boss fights I've ever encountered in a video game. Janky hitboxes, a plethora of instant kill attacks, pretty much any aspect that could make a Classic Sonic boss awful.EDIT: I'm editing this review due to me learning you can glitch out of bounds as Trip to beat Egg Fortress Act 2 without beating the boss. Now there's a final final final boss, and oh boy is this one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ too. Out of the 5 attack phases it has, you can damage it in 2 of them. Each phase is like half a minute. This boss legit takes longer than 10 minutes to beat. Plus, there a cool bonus at the end where you have to learn a new mechanic while no longer getting any rings. So good luck as you struggle to figure out unexplained controls while you slowly deplete rings. Don't worry if you lose, rest assured you'll wish you put those previous 10 minutes into literally anything else in the world. As an added bonus, this fight also has instant kill attacks! While playing as Super Sonic! If that doesn't sound fun, then I don't know what is. If you haven't yet, before purchasing this game, do a little thought experiment with me. You learn the rhythm of the final boss. You're 5 minutes into the fight, and you get every hit you possibly can on this fatass dragon. 5 minutes you could literally spend on absolutely anything else in life. Your body drains as you watch this ♥♥♥♥♥♥'s flapping animation for the 30th time. You fly ahead to get your 20th consecutive hit on him, and a black hole suddenly appears exactly where you are from offscreen, and you die instantly. This game was not playtested lmao. There is no actual way that a casual player beat this boss in playtesting, let alone thought it was fun. I don't believe it. Miserable game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a couch co-op game you can play with your kids or friends and have fun, this is definitely not the one. When one of the players falls 'behind', they respawn at the lead character's location, without enough speed, so cycle repeats. It's a very poor mechanic, which instantly disrupts the pace of the game: the leader ends up playing solo, while the 'extra' players are constantly respawning. Other players are somewhat useful during boss fights, but that's pretty much it. Unfortunately, my main motivation was to have a nice co-op game from the Sonic franchise that I could easily enjoy with kids, and this title fails miserably.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked it up for £22, wouldn't have gotten it for the full £55.I have beat the main story and got all the emeralds and it's pretty fun! It reminds me a lot of the advance series of games.The first good chunk of levels are awesome and varied, accompanied by great music (mostly when its's Tee Lopes or Yasayuki Nagata).The latter levels are fun too, but the music definitely drops when you get a lot more Sonic 4 style stuff, which also coincides with some weaker level design at times.Sonic, Tails, Amy and an additional unlock later on are all really fun to play, mostly just differing in a small ability (drop dash, flight and double jump respectively for the first three)It has its issues, three of the boss fights had weird bugs that occurred (such as having my ground physics with no need to breathe during an underwater boss fight), and Knuckles honestly feels kinda horrid to play with how his glide doesn't take any momentum into account.Overall not perfect, but no Sonic game is, and this was a good bit of fun.Probably wait for a sale though, it's relatively short (like most sonic games).Don't bother with the battle mode stuff by the way, unless you're going to play with friends, the online is completely dead.The shop is also bizarre, they made the character customisation very tedious and slow to unlock cosmetics in for not much point, and you can recolour parts but you use up sprays which you need to repurchase to do it, with each spray costing roughly two(!) bonus levels worth of coins.Trip is also very cute.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars is the franchise's New Super Mario Bros. Wii.It's a modern re-translation of the classic formula for home consoles with some solid gameplay, a buncha new powerups, and 4-player simultaneous co-op that... uh......Honestly, I have no idea how to properly describe the experience without just flat-out saying that the co-op has the  same energy as New Soup Wii's, to the letter. Mechanically, it differs in that players do not collide with each other or get bubbled, but this lack of ""cooperative"" tools is made up for with grabbing players that go offscreen unless the game feels like following them and grabbing everyone else instead. This does not stop it from feeling  like playing New Soup Wii co-op.So, if you enjoy the Monopoly-esque chaos of that flavor of co-op, you will adore this game. If not, then, uh... play singleplayer, I guess.The game itself is really good as well. I feel obligated to say "It's no Mania, obviously", but if while I don't disagree, I would feel kinda gross actually saying that. They did a  good job on this one; the physics are on point, the special stages are engaging, the new powers range from "okay, I guess" to being way too much fun, and there's even a tacked-on competitive mode just like New Soup Wii! The online's completely deserted though so if you want them sweet meaningless gamer ranks you'll have to grab a friend to be on at the same time as you.So, uh, yeah. I honestly feel like a lot of the negative feedback is overblown, especially since its Shadow the Hedgehog is one of the most beloved games on the Nintendo Wii.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so I haven't read or seen any reviews for this game. I don't know what people's takes are, so these are my thoughts alone.Just... ugh. What a slog. For the first two zones, I was pleasantly surprised. It seemed as though Sega had nailed it without the assistance of the Sonic Mania team. The visuals and music are better than I expected, the level design is decently nonlinear, and there's very little automation. To its credit, that last point remains consistent throughout the game. Otherwise, Sonic Superstars is a slow decline throughout.The bosses,  I'm gonna scroll down the Steam page and see a highly rated negative review that reads "good bosses!" or something, because damn, there is no way in hell that this problem is getting past anyone. It is the biggest problem with the game. You know how some games have "that boss"? 80% of Sonic Superstars' bosses are "that boss". You see, in the 16-bit Sonic games, bosses functioned as a damage sponge. They typically didn't last longer than a minute, and that's stretching it. Attack patterns were mere seconds long and there were little optimizations you could discover to speed up the fight. 2D Sonic games (partially) revolve around speed and optimizing your skill through replays, so this approach to boss design made sense.In contrast, Sonic Superstars' bosses typically last over a minute long, if not multiple. They tend to revolve around waiting 15-20+ seconds for their attack to end while they are completely invulnerable, followed by their weak spot opening. There is little to no room for optimizing/speeding up these boss fights. Even if the boss opens their weak spot and you bounce off it multiple times, the game only counts the first hit. Tons of waiting around for the boss to stop shooting projectiles or doing an insignificant animation. You'll get bored and start drop dashing compulsively, and then you'll die. The optimal way to play these bosses is to go at their slow pace. There's a decent amount of poorly telegraphed attacks and a few fights with some badly needed checkpoints. Every time I entered a boss fight I was thinking, "it's gonna be decent this time", and a few minutes later I'm miserable. A significant amount of my playtime in each act were spent on the boss. What happened?The level theming and graphics are also pretty middling. Again, the first few zones were a pleasant surprise in this regard. The second zone, Speed Jungle, has some cool visual elements that give it a sense of scale. The background will change depending on your elevation in the level and the zone transitions to nighttime in the second act. However, it feels as if the budget was not distributed equally among the zones. Some of them lack enough foreground and background detail, and feel vacuous as a result (the carnival, factory, and golden zones come to mind). Background details in particular are sparse and graphically low-fidelity; they're often low-poly models or just 2D textures. I was constantly noticing low-poly objects everywhere. Strong art direction would mitigate this, but Sonic Superstars' visual style is just very basic. Zones tend to blend into each other as a result. Some of them are memorable, but others lack enough interesting gimmicks/visuals/spectacle/music to make an impact. The lack of a second act for some zones may also contribute to them blending in, as the concepts introduced in said zones are disregarded faster than they would be if there were a whole second level to iterate on them. I suspect that the Nintendo Switch and an AA budget visually bottlenecked Sonic Superstars, just as I feel Sonic Forces and Sonic Frontiers were. The game's multiplayer may also contribute to this problem, but it could've been mitigated with, again, better art direction, or completely 2D visuals. In the past couple of years, the Sonic franchise has experienced two successful theatrical films, a Netflix show, and the best selling 3D game in the series. It's about time for a budget increase.Finally, the cutscenes. They're barely there and don't matter too much, but I still take issue with them. First, while I appreciate the return of 2D animated cutscenes from Sonic Origins, they're not up to the standard that game set. Take a look at Sonic Origins' 2D animated cutscenes and compare them with the ones in Sonic Superstars, which have worse linework, less fluid animation, CG shortcuts taken, and too much bloom. Sega's YouTube exclusive Sonic Superstars cartoon, Trio of Trouble, looks better than the 2D animation in the actual game. Perhaps these were being produced at the same time and one studio wasn't enough to handle both projects, or was it a case of saving money?I also question the inclusion of two characters, Fang and his sidekick(?) Trip. The way the game was marketed would have you think they'd be antagonists second to Eggman, like minibosses or something, but I think you fight Fang literally once. You only see Fang and Trip a few times after that and they never pose a threat to you. It makes me wonder if these characters were added late in development.Okay, but what about the actual platforming, the most important part of the game? Well, the movement and physics are thankfully much closer to the 16-bit games than the likes of Sonic 4, Generations, or Forces. It feels ever so slightly different, but I suspect this may be due to the 2.5D visuals or character animations. If you loved Sonic Mania, you'll feel right at home here. The level design, on the other hand, is a mixed bag. There's a good balance of new and old level mechanics/gimmicks from previous games, and most of them work quite well. The game isn't just lifting elements from previous games but introducing its own, which I very much appreciate. The aforementioned (relative) lack of automation is also a major plus. There are some moments where the game takes control from you for spectacle, but this isn't a huge problem. The game respects the player's agency in a way the more automated Sonic titles don't, and it's refreshing. However, some zones don't contain enough interesting level mechanics/gimmicks to feel distinct from other zones. I do wonder how much of my issue with Sonic Superstars' levels has to do with how they look rather than how they are designed. Sonic Superstars raises an interesting question of just how much visuals actually matter in a game. Are visuals the most important aspect of a game? Generally, no, but they help contextualize what we are doing in a game. If you removed all the level artwork from Sonic Mania and made it look like a series of test levels, I think I'd still have fun with it. However, I can't say the same about Sonic Superstars. Maybe it's the 2.5D, but I'm open to that visual approach if done well enough. Unfortunately, Sonic Superstars isn't that visually interesting. All in all, some of the game's levels just don't make a strong impression.Overall, Sonic Superstars is a decent game held back by tedious boss fights, unimpressive environments, and level design that can fail to feel unique. Thankfully, one of the game's biggest flaws is far from a fatal one. Reduce the amount of hit points bosses have and/or remove a few of their cycles. Giving the player more opportunities to damage bosses would also help in speeding up their pace. This is something that could easily be fixed with a patch, and if adequate, would bump Sonic Superstars up to a comfortable 7/10 in my eyes. As it is, the experience is far too uneven for me to call it consistently good. If you're not a Sonic fan, wait for a price drop and hope for a patch. If this game irritated someone experienced with this series, it'll probably be a lot more frustrating for you. I appreciate the game's inventiveness and willingness to introduce new ideas to the Classic Sonic formula, rather than completely revisiting the past. It's not a failure, but it doesn't quite live up to its Classic Sonic predecessors.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR this game is forgettable and has technical issues, but has a certain degree of charm in the character design and mostly proper 2D Sonic Physics, definitely not worth full price, wait for a deep sale.This game likes to softlock, and there are issues with the collision detection, getting pinch killed while not under whatever pinched me, I fell through stages, got locked into animations until quitting out and resetting. The sound design is abysmal, SEs are often mixed way too loud and feel out of place like they picked out of a hat for what sound goes whereTechnical issues aside, this game is very very forgettable, from the soundtrack to the level design, I feel like I'm playing Sonic Team's answer to New Super Mario Brothers, but like, ten years too late. While there are new stages, which for a new Sonic game is somewhat groundbreaking, those new levels are, however, mostly either recolors of previous games' stages, or aesthetic amalgamations of two older levels. The level design is passable, really nothing special, no new memorable stage hazards or platforming challenges, much like the visual design, forgettable, especially considering that each character plays through the same stages with no alterations until you unlock the new character's story, which is the same, but with a lot more enemies. Not going to spend much time on it but the special stages are boring, one is a worse version of the Sonic 1 emerald stage with an early 2000s flash game adaptation of the level theme, and the other is this lame swinging game that's super duper easy, add to the list of forgettable things in this game The physics are honestly pretty nice, while not a 1:1 with the classic titles, the nerfed spindash and weightier jump definitely stick out, despite that, the characters feel mostly like an old Sonic game. The soundtrack... uh... not great, feels a bit like the sonic 4 soundtrack, honestly none of the songs are downright bad, but none of it is anywhere near the quality I expect from a Sonic game, really really feels like a mobile game ost and that's really disappointing, especially when composed by Jun Senoue who has composed some of the best Sonic osts to date, even bad Sonic games usually have a good ost, but this mediocre slog has a similarly mediocre soundtrack.The character models are actually quite nice, I think the team translated the classic aesthetic into 3D very well; stretchy, bouncy animation on cutesy character models just works for the aesthetic they went for on this one, unfortunately putting nice looking model files into an otherwise mid game doesn't "do it" for meThe new power mechanic is cumbersome, would be better if you could set them to a context based command but that's not a feature. It's also irritating that they're either necessary for progression or, say it with me now, a forgettable feature you rarely use until the game prompts you to do so. Super forms are playable, which is nice and should be a feature in all Sonic games, I mention it here since it's tied to the power wheel I didn't play the multiplayer, what footage I've seen tells me it varies from, "Sonic 2 co-op" to a race/battle mode that's definitely not worth buying this game over

_childDocuments_.review: Amidst all the mixed reception, I've quite enjoyed my time with this game everything considered! In terms of ranking compared to previous classic 2D games, I'd put it firmly here: 1 < CD = Superstars < 2 < 3&K. Let's break it down.Core Gameplay: 9/10. The physics feel perfectly accurate and fun, and the level design is surprisingly good !! I was hesitant at first when the Emerald Abilities were shown off, but they're very supplementary and add some fun little things on top of the gameplay. The levels make me want to come back and replay them over and over again. Amy is super fun to play as, and the secret character is more than welcome too !! Super enjoyable all around.Aesthetics: 7.5/10. Finally, we're getting some fun level themes !! The graphics are serviceable, and some levels do really neat things with the aesthetics such as Cyber Station. The Lego DLC is very fun and silly which I appreciate, and the Comic Book skins are downright better than the vanilla game. The new badnik designs are especially fun !!Music: 7/10. Tee Lopes tracks are bangers as always, and even the supplemental tracks are pretty tight !! Jun needs to get off the damn Sonic 4 synths though, they hold back so many of these compositions and they can become so grating after a while. The boss music sucks ass. But some highlights from me are definitely Lagoon City Act 2, Speed Jungle, and Pinball Carnival.Bosses: 3.5/10. The BIG issue with this game. Most of the bosses in the game are fine, some have neat mechanics and ideas, but jesus some of them are AWFUL. Multi-phase bosses with unfair insta-kill attacks, long amounts of waiting, and no time to react. The final boss nearly made me stop playing altogether, which sucks because the rest of the game was drawing me back in !! A patch could easily fix these issues, and I hope it does.Additionally, I'll say that the customizable Battle Mode robots are a fun little addition. The mode itself doesn't add anything meaningful for me, but it's a nice addition.Overall, I'd give the game a solid 7.5/10. The bosses suck, but surrounding them are a wonderful little game that I adored to bits during my time with it. I wouldn't say it's worth $60, but definitely pick it up when it goes on sale. Very hopeful to see what this team does next.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good. Plain and simple.Before I actually start talking about the game's pros, I should mention the two elephants in the room. I don't need to elaborate that much on the inclusion of Denuvo, as for the Epic Games account being required to play the game's Battle Mode, yes it is stupid. Even though I've yet to play Battle Mode as of typing this, it is stupid that you need to need an Epic Games account to actually play this mode even though I brought this game on Steam. At the very least, you don't need one if you just want to play the game's main story. These two inclusions are stupid, but I wouldn't let them change my opinion of the overall game.Edit: As of writing this, the Epic Games problem has been resolved. However, the Denuvo situation is still thereThe game itself is very fun. The locations are actually original (even though some aesthetics are borrowed from previous games), the visuals are great, the physics are almost identical to the classic games, the characters all play and control very nicely, and level design is solid. One of the only few times where I felt the game suffer a bit were the bosses. Due to the game having a co-op mode, the bosses were mostly likely designed with that mode in mind. Because of this, it can take a couple of minutes to actually beat some of them. It can get very tedious at times, especially when some of the later bosses have you restart from the beginning of the first phase. The story of the game is also just as simple as some of the previous classic games' stories, so don't expect too much when going in.Another thing I should bring up is the game's music. It's pretty good (I mean it's a Sonic game why wouldn't it be). There were some songs that I really enjoyed listening to, but others not so much. It might be due to the fact that some of the songs use the original Sega Genesis sound font.The game's price of $60-70 is a little too much for a game like this. While I would recommend waiting for the game to go on sale, it's really up to you whether or not the game is worth the $60-70. Speaking of the $70 Deluxe version, it is a little better for what you get. The extra Main Menu backgrounds are meh, the Mecha-Sonic parts for Battle Mode are neat, the Lego character skins are somewhat decent, Sonic's original design in the form of the Rabbit Skin is very cool, and the Digital Artbook+Mini Soundtrack are fine as well.Overall, while this game isn't the successor to Sonic Mania that some of us wanted, it is still a very solid game. Despite the fact that this game does have mixed reviews (mostly due to the people who are mostly giving it a negative review for the inclusion of Denuvo and the Epic Games account requirement for Battle Mode), this is one of my favorite 2D Sonic games below Sonic Mania and Sonic 3 & Knuckles. If you like some of the previous Classic Sonic games, I think you'll like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a 7.9/10. This game has a lot going for it, the positives still outweigh the negatives, but the negatives really bring it down. I never thought I'd say this, but for the first time in awhile, a Modern Sonic game turned out to be better than a Classic Sonic game! Frontiers is definitely better than Superstars, and I'd recommend playing Frontiers over Superstars. Maybe this will convince SEGA and Sonic Team to ditch classic games and fully focus on Modern Sonic games for good.First, the Positives; The art style of the game is really good, the graphics are great and it really compliments the art style. The pre-order skins are worth it, it makes me so happy that they're finally implementing fully fledged skins as opposed to simple shoe/glove changes and accessories (looking at you Frontiers & Colors Ultimate). Also, Trip, despite not having much of a character or even a voice (seriously, is it too much to add voice-acting to these classic-styled games?), she's such an adorable character with an awesome character design. Don't even get me started on her Super/True form, SO BADASS!! She probably has the best super form in the game. Then there is the battle mode and it's customization, it's definitely not much, with only 4 or 5 game modes. But it's a really fun side game to play with friends, and it's pretty awesome how you can customize your robot in any way you like. It still needs to be tweaked a bit, but it definitely has potential. Now for the negatives, and oh boy...; first of all, the Comic-book skins, WHY ARE THEY EXCLUSIVE TO JAPAN?!? WHY DO THEY GET THE COOLER SKINS!? Second, the gameplay, it feels so freaking sluggish. It feels like Sonic Generations' classic gameplay, it takes Sonic and the others way too long to get going. If anything, it seems like everybody besides Amy feels sluggish. I know Frontiers didn't have the best physics in their Cyberspace levels, but this is way worse! Then there is the Level Design and holy crap! Every levels feels so cramped and doesn't give the player enough room to run at full speed for more than 5 seconds. That, and there is WAY TOO MANY ENEMIES!! You don't get enough time to recover before getting hit by another enemy 2 seconds later, this is also where the gameplay screws you over, you take forever to recover before the next enemy screws you over. There's no point in using the Super forms because you'll your 50 Rings literally seconds after you collected them. Last but DEFINITELY least, the Boss battles, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WHAT WERE THEY DOING?! They take WAY TOO LONG to beat, they're poorly designed, they're even rigged at some points. There was a point where I hit a boss, and they took damage, but I STILL lost rings, despite the boss not having ANY defenses on them, WHAT IS THAT?!?P.S. anybody who is crying about requiring Epic Games for online capabilities should be invalid. It literally takes 2 minutes to make a free Epic Games account, get over it, and doesn't go against the quality of the game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine you lived in the 1970s and for whatever reason you LOVED bell-bottom pants.  Then the 1980s comes along and you still love them but everyone around you tells you how lame you are for liking them because they are so "outdated" according to everyone.  Being a 46 year old longtime fan of platformers in this day and age feels a lot like that. No matter how good a platformer may be they don't seem to be cool and hip with the kids these days.  It's odd that First Person Shooters never receive the same criticism of being old fashioned despite the fact they too have now been around for over 30 years.  Yet as early as the early 2000s I've heard nothing but how "outdated" and "ancient" platformers (2D or 3D) are despite not being nearly as old as First Person Shooters are now back at that point in time.  With that context in mind, if you love Platformers like I do, there's much to enjoy here!  The Boss fights are fine and enjoyable.  There's a simple pattern to figure out and once you do you can take them out.  It gives a little brain tease but that's about all; it's otherwise fun to watch the set pieces play out!  Lots of good variety in the environments, there's shmup sections too.  I can't complain!  Very happy with the game.  The way that game reviews are these days is it's very similar to something like the "Academy Awards".  We all know that the ONLY kind of movie that can ever win "Best Picture" will always be some heartfelt drama.  A comedy film for instance, no matter how good it might be, can never win "Best Picture".  There's an unwritten convention that makes it impossible for anything else to win.  Gaming is like that now.  This is a great platformer, but it can never win "Game of the Year" or even be considered good because there's this unwritten rule in gaming that everything has to be some sort of dark gritty, poe-faced, serious story based game to be considered "good" for the modern audience.  Personally I prefer more whimsical fare like this.  Highly recommended.
