_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: This was a strictly single player review.  I've only watched the multiplayer, but it looks absolutely atrocious.Remember when I said Sonic Frontiers was a mixed bag in that game's review?  Well, Sonic Superstars has officially become the biggest mixed bag in the series for me.   For everything this game does right, it does something completely awful.  Starting with the positives:- The controls are solid, at least for the most part.  Not as good as mania, sure, but nowhere near as bad as the classic stages from forces.  I think there's a pretty good sense of speed, and (outside of bosses and post game content, but I'll get there), There was never a time where a death DIDN'T feel like my fault.- The special stages are pretty great overall.  The Sonic 1 special stages return, but I genuinely think this is the best they've been, with decent enough control and even original obstacles.  As for the other, brand new stages you play for the emeralds, I love these.  Swinging towards the emerald to catch up or taking a shortcut to cut it off is really fun.  It's even better in co op, where it's a hot potato game of everyone taking turns cooperatively making moves to reach the emerald.  - The emerald powers.  This was probably the most advertised part of the game besides the co op, and I think it's a good idea that could use improvement.  The powers aren't all winners, but the ones that are winners are extremely fun to use.  The first emerald gives you an attack that's helpful against bosses, the second one gives you a valuable tool for exploration as ANY character, and so on.- Fang gets a major role again, even if it wasn't perfect in execution.  Also, the new character. Trip, is a great addition to the cast, and I hope we see them return in future games.And now that I'm done with the positives, it's unfortunately time for the negatives.  WARNING: Getting into the negatives requires me to maybe spoil some stuff.  Consider yourself warned.- This game has Denuvo.  Again.  I'm sure anyone who's played another Sonic game on PC knows why this is a bad thing.- The pacing.  Superstars' pacing is all over the place.  There are 11 zones total, but they aren't all made equal.  Some zones have 3 acts, but some only have one.  This is kind of weird, since it means some ideas don't get enough time to be fully showcased, and some have the opposite problem of becoming boring and repetitive.- The playable characters.  Specifically, Knuckles and Amy.  Knuckles' movement is pretty jank, since his gliding has a speed cap, and without levels built specifically around his movement like in 3K and Mania (Yes, I know he gets a stage for himself, but it doesn't really do anything special), he's not really worth using compared to Sonic or Tails.  Now as for Amy, as cool as it is that we can play as her in a classic game, she's just nothing special, which is also a feeling I had in Origins Plus.  All she has is a double jump, which is inferior to Tails' flight, and a hammer attack that is inferior to Sonic's drop dash.  Not helping matters overall is the fact that the extra character you unlock for the post game (no spoilers) can double jump AND climb walls, making Amy and Knuckles completely obsolete.EDIT: In retrospect Amy's double jump is better than I made it out to be.  It keeps speed better than Tails' flight, which is nice, but doesn't really change the fact that I'd rather play as Tails or the extra character making her obsolete.- The bosses.  These are some of the worst boss fights in series history.  Now, it's actually okay for the first two zones.  The first zone is expected to be pretty straightforward, and the fight at the end of the second zone is actually something different.  Unfortunately, by the time you reach zone 3, almost every boss becomes an annoying waiting game to expose a weak point, and not a short one either.  The boss fights can actually last longer than the actual levels sometimes!  The fights in zones 8, 9 and 11 are by far the worst of the lot, since all of those are also pretty hard in addition to being very long.  The emerald powers are great and all, but they only get you so far with these.- The extra story.  A second story becomes available after finishing the game once, which is strictly single player as the aforementioned new character.  It's god awful.  The new character is really cool and all, but how can I enjoy that when enemies and spikes are spammed all over the place for a ton of cheap shots, and the fact that BOSSES ARE EVEN LONGER THAN THEY ALREADY WERE, since someone at Sonic Team decided they should have MORE HEALTH.  This all reaches it's peak in the final boss, where it goes on for a good 10 MINUTES, and almost all of it's attacks INSTANTLY KILL YOU, with NO checkpoints!Overall, while I had enough fun with Sonic Superstars to leave a positive review, this game is NOT WORTH $60.  Wait for a sale, or wait for stuff to get fixed, because as of right now that $60 is better spent on Mario Wonder, which released mere DAYS after Superstars.  (Seriously, how did SEGA mess up that bad?)P.S: Digital deluxe is, as expected, a total waste of money.  Don't buy it.  Get the standard edition and save $10.

_childDocuments_.review: To address the elephant in the room, the multiplayer functionality is completely useless. No one plays the Battle Royale mode and the co-op is considered one of the worst features in the game due to it conflicting with the main gameplay loop. What's more is that it's very much an excuse for SEGA to charge full price for what's essentially a 30-40 dollar game. You're better off waiting for a discount if you want to buy this game.The game maintains the classic gameplay formula as best as it could. There are only a few issues when it comes to the movement and physics department such as the starting speed feeling a tad slower, Knuckles; glide not gaining speed as it goes on, not being able to do your second jump ability out of certain level gimmicks such as Speed Jungle's vines or Sandy Sanctuary's booster lines for example.The quality of the bosses range from creatively designed or alright, to being such a bore, or excruciatingly frustrating. The latter being the ones you encounter in the later half of the game. And the problem worsens with high amounts of invincibility frames. The I frames were likely brought in as a means to counter the clone ability however it'll still decimate half of the game's bosses anyways. However on the opposite side of the spectrum another chunk of the game's bosses are capable of game ending players without preparation (and one boss in particular only has moves that can quite literally OHKO the player.)Speaking of the clone ability mentioned before, the Chaos abilities are an necessary inclusion for a variety of reasons: They're either too situational, or they're too overpowered too the point of breaking bosses or skipping chunks of Acts or they're completely useless in comparison to the other abilities. They're also the main reason the elemental shields aren't present this time around, they're meant to be an evolution of that concept. The problem is that the Chaos abilities are implemented in a way that it feels more like a limitation. You have a limited time for each ability and they're only replenished when you touch a checkpoint. If I had to compare all of this to another game series, the Chaos Abilities are to the Elemental Shields as Halo's sprint and "abilities" and the equipment from that series' third entry.Another knock I have to give to this game is it's soundtrack. While there are some good tracks, they're unfortunately mixed in with some very bad ones as well. The main issues stems from the lack of cohesion of what the tracks want to be. For instance, Bridge Island, Speed Jungle and Sandy Sanctuary mostly use CD quality instruments heard in Tee Lopes' other works, meanwhile Press Factory and Golden Capital uses the ever-so iconic "dying cats" synth that plagued the Sonic 4 duology, thanks to Jun Senoue of course. Listen, that man has made a ton of good tracks throughout the years, be it in the Adventure era titles or even in spin-off titles afterwards. However, the moment you lend him the aux cord to the fake OPN2, that's when he'll lose the plot, and in the worst cases, his tracks will tear your eardrums into shreds such as the beginning part of Press Factory Act 1. (Note: these tracks were so bad I held myself off from playing the game until mods were made that included better renditions for those tracks. Yes I'm that picky.) The next time Jun returns to work on music, keep him away from the (fake) Genesis font. It didn't work for Sonic 4, it didn't work for Forces, then Origins. and it didn't work here as well.Anyways, despite all the issues the game has, it's still a very solid game if you can get behind a glitch or two. Despite how decent the game is, the fanbase has chosen this game as it's main target to pick apart and destroy all sense of worth for the product. If it has slightly differing physics from the original games, it's bad. If it has ties to lore bits that Ian 'Kino' Flynn wrote up, it's sacrilege. Anyhow, relying Sonic fans and SonicTubers to justify whether or not you should buy the game is more counter-intuitive than buying the game itself at full price. In my eyes, Sonic Superstars is basically the 'Sonic Heroes' of Classic Sonic games, you'll either enjoy it for what it is or you'll absolutely hate it for even the smallest of reasons.

It just isn't fun but that could also just be me, and maybe others would like it. Lastly the new emerald powers are broken and make the game not fun and too easy. The game feels heavily focused for multiplayer, and maybe it's better with multiplayer, but for me personally I don't want to play multiplayer in a classic Sonic game, and as someone who enjoys Sonic more than Mario, if i wanted to play a multiplayer platformer i would just play NSMB, or Mario 3D World instead.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're interested in this game, buy Sonic Mania. You'll get a far more consistent and fun experience there.There are a lot of good parts of Sonic Superstars. Expect unbalanced sound effects, music that feels straight out of Sonic 4, and bosses that have you waiting for your turn so long that they may take as much time as the rest of the level they're in. Paying full price for this game is not a good decision.Once again, there are a lot of good parts. The game really is pretty fun past the issues, and some of the levels have a lot of replay value. But when there are not only more full experiences for the same price, but better sonic games for a fraction of this one's price, Sonic Superstars is just not worth it.Don't be fooled by the recent successes in this franchise. _childDocuments_.review: NOTE: Do not buy this game at full price, it is not worth it, wait for sale (you can thank me later). If you want to experience this game and get most most of your money, cop the game when it is at least 50% off. Review:Sonic Superstars is basically a dollar store version of Sonic Mania. It wants to replicate what Mania did in 2017 so bad, but it attempts to do so without the same team that worked on Mania and because of that, the team struggles to understand what made Mania good in the first place. The game lacks all of the charm, passion, fan-fare, and stellar game & level design that Sonic Mania excelled in. Superstars ditches the beautiful pixel art style from Sonic Mania and instead goes for a boring 3D Generations styled look for its character models and level assets in a 2D game. The result is an uncanny look for Classic Sonic that just doesn't work when trying to scratch that Classic Sonic feel and itch. Why Sonic Team/SEGA decided that this was a better art direction than what Mania did will forever puzzle me. What was wrong with Mania's pixel art style? If it ain't broke, don't fix it.  The level design is questionable, the boss fights drag on for far too long (especially the final fights), boss fights ruin the pacing of the main levels (the bosses should have been separate levels similar to Sonic 4), Emerald Powers and Co-Op Play feel like an afterthought and are poorly implemented into the game's design. The game physics feel slightly feel off compared to Mania, and the playable characters control sub-optionally for speed running/time attacking. The animated cut-scenes are a noticeable downgrade from the Mania and Origins. Similar to every modern SEGA Steam release, Sonic Superstars has Denuvo DRM built-in, so don't buy if you computer barely meets the minimum requirements or is a potato. You will need a constant internet connection to play this game without being blocked from playing after a certain amount of time without being online, so playing on Steam Deck Offline is pretty much a no go, unless you have hot-spot capabilities on your phone. The multiplayer Battle Mode was dead on arrival and still is to my knowledge. There is no incentive to explore/optimize time attacks on the levels due to them feeling very lifeless and generic and the collectibles only earn you cosmetics for the aforementioned dead multiplayer. The game is constantly held back by the fact that it is trying way too hard to be a traditional Classic Sonic game, because of this, the game fails to innovate on the Classic 2D Sonic formula. 2D Sonic has never been this lifeless and boring, go play any other highly regarded 2D Sonic game and you'll have a much better time. If your curious about how much this game fumbles the bag or just want a Sonic game to play to pass the time, pick the game up while on sale, but otherwise this game is pretty uninspired, forgettable, skip-able, and generally not worth experiencing. This is coming from a pretty hardcore Sonic fan too.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars is an excellent example of what a 2D Sonic game should be. Is it perfect? No, but it's still a great Sonic game.Graphics are amazing, it's a really good art style. The characters all look amazing in this style.  the only real complaint I can think of is that the backgrounds don't always loop properly on boss fights that have you running in a circle, so there's a point where you can see the background warp back to it's starting point.Music is good and i'm sure most people will find something they like. But it's not Sonic Frontiers level amazing. So no promises that you'll find a song that's worth the price of admission all by it's self.Game Play is amazing. All the characters control really well. I never felt like any of the characters did anything unexpected, everything just worked as I expected it would.Level Design was amazing, nothing felt like a copy-paste from older games, yet almost everything felt like it belonged in a Sonic game. Plenty of paths to follow and secrets to find. over all a good balance of fast paths for blazing though the level and things to explore for. (with one minor problem but that's not a level design issue.)Story is what you'd expect (a basic adventure story) but the innovations are worthy of note and praise. In particular the character specific acts and and background appearances do a wonderful job of helping you piece together the real story in a game that accommodates letting you play as anyone.The only flaw in the story I can mention is that the final enemy just shows up out of nowhere. And nothing stands out as the reason for "why is this happening now?"The individual emerald powers are a fun addition to the game. Although three of them amount to, "Anyone can go places normally meant for Tails." And seeing as the Bullet power does it the best, The Water and Ivy powers feel redundant to me, and good candidates to swap out for other ideas in the next game.That said I really liked the "Extra" power that changes for whoever you are playing as. It was a fun idea and might make since to apply to more of the emeralds.Last power I wanted to comment on was that the sight power felt under utilized and it might have been better to have actual visual clues in the level's themselves as to when there would be something to be relieved. The just have an icon pop up saying this power will do something here just made it feel more like a key that opens a locked door then finding something hidden.The biggest issue I have with the game is the reward structure. pretty much all of the special things to find are ways to get meddles and the meddles are only used to unlock cosmetics for the multi-player battle-bot. So once you've built the one you want, the only reason to find all the hidden stuff is just for the fun of it. And while that might be enough for me, it's a shame that there isn't anything interesting to use the exploration rewards on. Like cosmetics for the characters in the actual game.The other complaint I have would be that there isn't a way to speed up the ending credits in a game that's meant to be beaten many times. And while the mini game they let you play during the ending credits as nice, one again the only reward for doing it is more meddles. Why they didn't have the credits speed up a little everything you collect a ring is beyond me. You better believe I'd engage with your mini game if it got the credits over with faster. But as it stands you beat the game walk away and do other things while you wait for them to be over.Edit: I have since found the option to just skip the credits by returning to the main menu so strike that complaint. The patch that added the Santa costume for Sonic also fixed a few bugs. Most notably the bug found in the last two levels that gave away the ghost on how the game's code handled crushing deaths. So thank you dev team and good job on that. end editOn the upside Tails can't be called easy mode anymore. Amy's balance of mobility and combat power made her's the easiest play through by a long shot. Still fun though and it fits, so I can't actually suggest changing it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so *so close* to being a home run. The gameplay's as fun as I'd hope for a 2D Sonic game, a lot of the new environments are pretty cool, and Trip is a fantastic addition to the cast. Really hoping she becomes a bit of a mainstay. Not to mention all the deep cuts like Feels (Rabbit) finally appearing in a game (which is still insane to me), Fang finally have a prominent role again, and Mecha Sonic MK1 and Metal Knuckles returning in addition to there being an official Metal Tails and Amy outside of the archie comics now. There clearly was a lot of passion going into this game, and I think they *mostly* succeeded in making a great Classic Sonic game.However, for all the things this game does right, there's still a lot of oddities that're too prominent for me to ignore or gloss over, and I hope get addressed if/when another Sonic game in this style is made in the future, Biggest one being the music. I think a lot of the tracks in the games are fantastic, but there's just as many that sound straight out of Sonic 4. The compositions of said tracks aren't even inherently bad, it's just the instruments used to make said tracks they really bring them down in execution. On top of that, it's very inconsistent as to what songs do or don't use the genesis samples. It honestly makes it sound like they were work-in-progress arrangements that somehow never got finished, especially when you go from a track that doesn't use those genesis samples into one that does (For example, Speed Jungle: Act Sonic. It's extremely jarring hearing that fantastic level music periodically interrupted by Fang's theme, which sounds very unfinished in comparison to the level's theme). If they fully committed to not using those instruments like most of the great songs in the OST do, OR if they had composers who had a better handle on how to make those genesis samples shine, I think Superstars would be up there for having yet another fantastic OST.There's also more minor things that could've been handled better like whatever's going on with the Comic skins, more options for Co-op beyond just sharing a screen (such as including split screen or online as an option for those who don't enjoy how often they get outran), the execution of the emerald abilities, and the way the Prototypes in the battle mode were handled (Touched up animations, and maybe an option to change what their ability is instead of having all of them functionally be Sonic clones).All in all, Superstars is a solid game and I'm definitely enjoying it. If you're like me, someone who is a longtime fan but doesn't need a game to be as solid as say, the Genesis trilogy and/or Mania to enjoy it, then by all means give the game a go. But, if you aren't and/or are a more casual enjoyer of Sonic or platformers in general, I'd say to wait for a sale before getting the game instead of blowing $60 on it.

_childDocuments_.review: We've taken steps forward since Sonic 4, which is good, but we've also taken a handful of steps back. A lot of this game's mechanics feel like they're at war with each other, like the Mania devs were trying to make something fun but Sega kept butting in to add new bloat for (probably) marketing reasons. This game definitely takes the title for "Worst Bosses in Sonic history" though, and honestly the game as a whole felt like such an amazing idea on paper, but was executed poorly, it really needed a bit more polish before release. (Also releasing this on the same week as Mario Wonder was probably the dumbest executive decision I've ever seen.) The soul is definitely there, but it needed a couple more months of tweaking to make all the mechanics work better together, such as the later level design and bosses. This game tricks you into thinking it's single player when realistically they designed the whole game around 4 players, which makes it a bit miserable when you're alone. _childDocuments_.review: If I want this review to leave on one message and one message only, it's this:Good game, bad PC port.Forcing Epic onto the consumers, especially without telling them until they already purchased it, is definitely really shady and they should face all the backlash they're getting currently, but one thing I do have to respect, is the hustle to give the game cross platform online play for it's battle mode, which is where the Epic launcher comes into play. Something that should be standard with online multiplat games. .....just wish it wasn't EpicAnd that is also ignoring that the game is unstable on higher framerates and resolutions, I suggest watching OhNoItsAlexx's video on that for deeper insight.On the game itself.........yeah, it's Classic Sonic. Physics, controls, level design, it all feels ripped from the Genesis games and Mania, just given a New Super Mario Bros. Wii level of multiplayer. Sonic and co. (Trip excluded) definitely play like how they did in the past.Sonic is the speedy one with the Drop-Dash, Tails can fly and carry others, Knuckles can glide and climb walls, Amy can double jump and use her hammer.....everything is accounted for with what feels like minimal compromise. If that is your thing, this game will treat you well on that front.And all of this while not reusing a single zone from the past in it's campaign. Green Hill is still here, but as a bonus stage for Battle mode, but the campaign is wholly original, and thank God for that.The Chaos Emerald abilities are definitely a neat add-on, and gives the feeling of getting even one Emerald worth your time, something that has always fell kinda flat in the past. Some of the powers, like vine and water, feel rather under utilized, and it would benefit from having Rings slowly recharge Emerald abilities, or just put them all on cool-downs. Still keep checkpoints immediately refresh these abilities, but one time uses before checkpoints feels too strict.The bosses are alright, save for Fang and the final boss of the main campaign. They're not hard. just too slow/too tanky, and on each death, you have to start from the very top.In short, the game is pretty good, just avoid the PC port until it goes on sale or gets fixed (namely it's stability and outright performance. I don't see Epic getting phased out at any point) and get it on another platform.Edit: As of November 8th 2023, SEGA has removed the forced Epic Install for Online Battle Mode. The game still has the boot file and the EOS folder in its Directory, but the fact that Epic is no longer forced on you wi a MASSIVE improvement. SEGA deserves all the props in the world for taking the feedback to heart and doing something about it. (There is still Denuvo, but one battle at a time)

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars has returned Sonic back to its roots.Physics are the first and most important thing and I'm happy to report they they are very close to being 1:1 the real thing. The one elephant in the room being how you rebound from objects and badnicks, sadly it has not been recreated faithfully. Otherwise it's pristine and if you find this a non issue - you'll be delightfully pleased.  Level Design is closely on par to Sonic 3K which in turn has been surpassed by Mania. I was very surprised to see how good it is. When I heard Naoto Oshima would make a comeback, I was happy the game would look great but for those who are in the know, he designed levels for the Platform heavy Sonic 1. He also worked on Sonic CD which featured level designs which were a mess to navigate in. I am happy to report that albeit there's a bigger focus on Stage Verticality, it doesn't at all harm levels. They keep you on your toes, are fast paced and packed with explorability. Featuring all new stages, albeit with tropes not alien to anyone who has been keeping up to speed with the Classics, it does however have a mixture of tropes already present in the past and they are all for the most part very interesting to play. Level mechanics are new and interesting to play, all the while intuitive.As for characters movesets:- Sonic works as you'd expect. Elemental shields are sadly replaced with emerald powers. Now rocking the Drop Dash from Mania, which works exactly as you'd expect. Spindash works well for all characters, albeit sadly only two buttons function to rev up the Spindash (down from 3).- Tails, which I am happy to report plays even better than what he used to, featuring a longer sustained flight and being able to descend faster, these small benefits add to the experience. - Knuckles, which is for the most part well translated with his glide and climbing walls, albeit I am sad to report his super glide is dead, no longer able to glide way up in the air as his genesis counterpart. This is due to how rebound has been programmed as pointed above.- Amy has her Origins moveset. Included is the double jump which helps a lot transverse the land and makes it more familiar ground for mayhap someone new to the Classic formula. However her ability to turn one a dime with her hammer Dash, doesn't carry over the speed last present in Origins. This I feel is a step inferior, but it won't be harmful as she is still pretty fun to play.On to the presentation. Presentation wise this game is the definition of what a Sonic Game should be. Colourful, appeasing, vibrant. Animations for all the models are crisp, smooth, very unique and expressive.Spindash, jumping, idle animations, attack animations, everything is just so welll done I can't help but be in awe at the amount of time and effort put into it. All and all, for a 3D Classic Game, presentation-wise, It's wonderfully crafted.  As a new add-in mechanic, we have Chaos Powers. Collecting Emeralds awards you with unique abilities to transverse the land. And while this came at a cost (Elemental shields) they offer something new to the formula.These abilities range from explorability powers such as Vines to climb, the ability to swim in water at ease (without worrying for air) and combat abilities, I.E: avatar, burst, etc. These abilities are decent, I personally don't like how you select them too much, as I feel with a game such as Sonic, I'm mostly worried about going fast. Still, it doesn't harm the experience and are sometimes useful. You'll often be looking into using combat powers for reasons we will discuss later and these can help you progress and smoothen things down a notch.Music is for the most part phenomenal. Tee Lopes makes a comeback and you will instantly pick up on his tracks which are: I must say, an absolute joy. All is not sun and sunshine however as I must report Jun Senoue is a legend with his guitar but his track record at creating tracks for classic Sonic hasn't been great. Those who played Sonic 4 and Origins will immediately recognize the issue here. It all comes down to his obsession with the genesis drums, because his composition is good, you can really feel what he is going for but then you hear the genesis drums and you can't help but feel at odds as to why a game which has such nice live instruments soundtracks suddenly goes back to the Genesis drums. Alienating at best and tragic at worst.Now on to the Bosses. You might either love it or hate it. Bosses start off being fun, filled with energy, not too tense but definitely unique. Fun designs. Sometimes they are a part of the level itself, taking new liberties while retaining the fun of what Bosses should be. They were on to something great, however I must report this trope didn't last the entire game.I'm looking at Sand Sanctuary's Boss as the first to really heavily start this trend (albeit there were glimpses of this present already) start this pattern where we last saw in Sonic 4. By this I mean you are waiting for your queue to attack. You start this dance where the boss is fun, you get one attack in only to find the repetitiveness of waiting 20-30s for your next move. This makes bosses just tedious instead of encouraging the player to take risks to get a few more attacks in before waiting for your next opportunity to attack. Furthermore, and this is where I can't help but feel that they went a step too far is where you have multiple phases to a boss and there's no checkpoint. Look - I get it. They wanted Sonic Bosses to be more than bounce 7x to win. Nothing against it. But let players keep their progress. Encourage them to do a boss unscathed or deathless. Players will want to do that if they like the game. As it is now, players might not want to replay Sonic Superstars after a few playthroughts. And here personally I am sad because I can feel they made the game with soo much passion (And it shows!) but they overshot themselves. Still fun! But I would advise people to be weary of this.THIS is where the combat abilities shine. They provide an ok solution as a jail-free card to (some) bosses and might even add a layer of timing and opportunity once you understand the bosses patterns. Expect to die a lot, watch for hidden queues, they are there - but don't think you'll one shot everything without prior knowledge is my suggestion.Now, without spoiling too much. There is an extra mode on the game which I love, but be warned. For this mode is merciless. It WILL put you to the test. And I don't say this as a negative, much au contraire, extra gameplay! I'm all in for it! But it is NOT a mode I'd recommend picking up unless you are ready to steel yourself - The game will test you!  For its content, quality and fun aspect I must report that I find its demanding price tag too steep. This is a game that shouldn't have been priced at more than 40$ (at most!) and I can't help but feel Sega overshot themselves recollecting how cheap Mania was considering how much it ended up selling. Origins suffered from the same exact problem, too steep for what it was worth. I would personally recommend waiting for a sale on this one unless you are really craving and itching for some Classic Sonic action, which I must say, this game delivers.  Arzest has done a wonderful job translating the "Sonic feel". It feels Classic to its very core. There are many Easter eggs, nods, references, small details that once you pick on will make you so happy to see the attention to detail. It's a game that you can feel took some of the best notes from all classic games up to now and expanded on them. And albeit there are faults, you can feel they were really trying their best to create the best game possible, and I am eagerly awaiting for a chance for them to flesh out their next Classic Sonic game. I feel we have finally found sustained ground to keep the momentum going. May you roll fast and I'll catch you on Bridge Island. That track slaps!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting a sequel to Sonic Mania and Origins, this isn't it. If anything, its closest comparison is the Classic stages of Sonic Generations and Forces (though it's more polished than Forces).The physics are kinda floaty, which can be frustrating if you're familiar with the 16-bit style games; if anything, the characters feel far too slow and unresponsive. The game is very short for the price tag, and aside from a New Game Plus, there's not much replayability. There are no Ranks or Time Trials, and you have infinite lives, so there's no reward for improving. That being said, you die from off-screen objects quite a lot, so maybe this is a blessing in disguise. The main new mechanic of this one is the special abilities you get for collecting each Emerald, which act similar to the Wisps in the Modern games; you can activate them at any time, but in practice this makes you stop in your tracks and I only found myself using them when there was an on-screen prompt. Even then, using them feels like I'm going against the speed/momentum physics that the Sonic games are supposedly based around. You also have to restart each level to attempt a Special Stage for some reason, as if this mechanic somehow peaked in the Mega Drive era; it's frustrating to say the least, and I would honestly take a 2 minute countdown over having to restart the level like this. The Special Stages even manage to incorporate the Homing Attack that's been broken since Sonic Heroes.But the bosses are ridiculous. After some very forgiving platforming, each Stage ends with a rage-inducingly punishing (and often badly designed) boss. It doesn't matter how many hundreds of rings you collected in the level, you will not have the chance to recover them if you are hit once. You can't take risks to beat them faster either, because they have invincibility frames for days and immediately bugger off the screen. Oh, and there are no visuals to go with the invincibility frames either, so have fun jumping into bosses and bouncing off for no apparent reason. With the older games, you could improve yourself and beat the boss faster, but here it's either perfection or you get sent back five minutes. Of course, this has the knock-on effect of breaking the game's pacing, because you'll spend most of your playtime on incomplete runs of a boss fight.I beat Sonic Forces, with all the S Ranks and Red Star Rings. But I gave up on the New Game Plus of Sonic Superstars. It just isn't fun.This game was such a huge step backwards for Classic Sonic. It doesn't carry over what made Sonic special, and I can't imagine it's going to feel very fresh to general platforming fans either. The only good to come out of this game is that maybe Trip (the new villain) will show up somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh well, I hate to give a Sonic game that was looking promising a negative review but here I am. I played only single-player mode because I do not have friends that are autistic enough to pay that much for a mediocre Sonic game. In general I am quite disappointed the more I play it. I wanted to complete story mode for each character but I had enough. The game just now irritates me, I will explain later why. Here are some pros and cons:Pros: - Game does look rather nice.- There are some stage parts that are nicely implemented (like running sideways on the first level). - You can play as the whole cast from mega drive Sonic series and more.- Kind of, you feel some Soul coming out from this game... too bad it is not there.- Some new emerald powers are quite nice, you can skip some part of the level thanks to it.- New character has some potential, I hope that Sega won't forget about her too fast.- Story. I wish they could add some more story points. That was nice but sparse.Cons:- Game is very slow in comparison to other 2D sonic games.  There are only a few moments that I felt I am going fast. Game focuses more on platforming instead of speed. - Bosses are uninspired and boring. In previous games you could tell that Eggman creations were quite cool and were designed to what that machine should do (like attacking sonic in a specific way). Here designs do not make much sense. - Bosses take too long to beat. On normal play-though it is not so bad but when you unlock "Hard mode" then those bosses are very annoying since you have to endure even more. Why can't I "gotta go fast" on those bosses in the Sonic game? Yeah sure you can sometimes use chaos emeralds powers to make some additional fast hits but I feel like it is a design oversight instead of the intended way of dealing with the boss. - Sonic is no longer cool. I do not know... I feel like Sonic has the same energy as Mega man. Serious, ready to go instead of cocky and having fun. Sure, Tails and Amy give a good energy but this is a Sonic game so Sonic should be at least done correctly. - Medals. In the game you can collect medals so you can buy parts for a robot that you fight in one of the stages (I guess you can also play as it but who cares). Some parts are expensive and to get them all you will have to grind a lot. It is a waste of time in my opinion. Sometimes to get medals there are portals that appear on the stage that you can fall into by mistake. It disturbs the flow of the game. Why big rings where you get emeralds after getting all of them you do not get 50 rings but you replay stages but instead of emeralds you get those medals?- Emeralds powers. Some of the powers are nice but a bigger part of them are useless. When I get green emerald I was sure that there will be some chaos control stuff there but no, you get power to grow a plant that can elevate up, yey.- Music is very meh. Usually, one of the redeeming qualities of Sonic games was music. None of the tracks stayed with me longer after completing a level. Boss music is especially bad... perhaps it is due to bosses taking too long and track loops too often. - Games forces you to get some Epic Games store plugins or something. I almost refunded the game but my love for Sonic games was too strong this time. I bought it on Steam, why I have to create another account from a different store. Denuvo is enough Sega. If the next Sonic game will have it I will not even consider buying it.- Game has a lot of bugs. I do not know if someone tested it. In the main menu or main map you can screw the index of selecting options. In the main menu, I entered options and then I wanted to start the game but instead of game start I was returned to options. On stage select I selected Act 1 but it took me to Act 2.- 2D game in 3D design. I had a lot of problems determining when I could attack the enemy or what the hit boxes were. It really shows on the "Hard mode".- Super forms are death wishes. In short, super forms do not fit into the design of the maps. For example as Sonic you go fast and then either you fall to death or you get crushed by something. Super forms can be useful only during bosses if you have enough rings to cover the whole fight.- Game UI and UI sfx feels like taken from Mania. I had fun with Mania, why is this game trying to alert those memories? I am sure that I would list even more negatives but I feel that is enough. My breaking point was playing a hard mode. I just felt tired and irritated while playing those levels. All of the game's flaws just scream here. After beating the boss on stage 10 I just said that it is. To be honest, that's all there is I guess. Nothing to unlock after finishing the story with all the characters but who knows.I do not know... game feels like Balan Wonderworld, The same level of disappointment and regret. Do not buy this game, -50% is a must if you want to play it.I wanted to "gotta go fast"... instead I have returned to rethinking my life choices... again :<

_childDocuments_.review: I am about to blow a lot of my friend's minds by posting a negative review of a Sonic game. I'm usually known for being lenient with this franchise.There will be "spoilers" ahead that I will be sure to mark.I was decently excited for Superstars. Growing up with 3D Sonic, Mania turned me into a 2D convert. While I was not expecting something of Mania's quality, the more I play it the more I realize this is just... not acceptable for a $60 game.I started out having fun. It (mostly) feels like the original trilogy. Sure, the level design was nothing to write home about, but it still had enough classic Sonic charm. It was modernized pretty well, and I'm a big fan of the removal of lives (which makes things far less frustrating as you go on). The new special stages are also pretty fun too. I'm impartial to the emerald powers, but they do (one in particular) make bosses a lot easier in some cases. I never got to try co-op for myself, but I'm happy we at least have a proper co-op Sonic game at the very least. Even if responses to that co-op have seemed mixed. I'd love to give this game another try with a friend at some point.Here we get to my first massive complaint: Bosses.Bosses in this game drag on for far, far too long. I get it. It's a multiplayer game. If bosses were just as easy to hit as they were in the original games, they would be over in seconds. But they often have a tendency to drag on. And on. And on. And on. Some of them are about a third or half the length of a stage. That being said, most of them aren't too bad. Until you get towards the end of the game. The final boss goes on forever. It takes a while to figure out how to even beat the first phase, and then comes back far more difficult in the second. Spending over 5 minutes, even up to 10 minutes, on a run of this final boss only to end up dying was infuriating. There is far too much waiting involved in bosses.My second complaint: Collision and obstacle placement.I didn't have a hard time with this game's collision at first. By the time you reach the final act, it's bad. There were several moments where I got crushed by something I wasn't even under. My rings would clip into the ground sometimes. There's an on rails boss at one point that has you dodging things you can't see yet. The final stage is super cool and ambitious, I will give them that, but it's also probably the least polished and has the most issues.My final complaint: Post game. This is going to be a lengthy section. I don't think "spoilers" for a 2D platformer are a big deal, but I'll mark it as a spoiler so I don't ruin anyone's first experience.The events that inspired me to write this review involve all 3 of these issues combined.This is the most broken thing I've ever experienced in a $60 game. I'm currently debating as to whether or not trying to finish this would even be worth it.This game seemed fine at first, and to be fair the first half is. But the more I played, the more bugs I encountered and the more tedious the bosses became.I'm not even mentioning how completely unnecessary it is for Epic Games's online services to even need to be a thing here, or how completely bland and forgettable the multiplayer they're trying to pedal is.And while I'm at it, this was Fang's first big appearance in years outside of a few cameos and he's barely even in the game. This game should have been $30. I would even settle for $40. It's probably less than 15 hours of gameplay here, unless you're achievement hunting. There is just not a lot here, and what is here breaks the more you play it. It's not the worst thing I've ever played, but it's incredibly underwhelming and not as polished as it should be.Say what you will about Sonic 4, but the Sonic 4 games at least knew what they were. Short, cheap games made for digital storefronts. There are things to like about Superstars, moreso than Sonic 4, but I would take a mediocre $15 game over a mediocre $60 game.Maybe I'll come around on this game in another playthrough and after patches. But for now I cannot recommend it in its current state. I feel pretty burnt.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun. Out of all the zones, I didn't like Press Factory, and the first act of Golden Capital was a little too long for my liking, but the rest are all really good. The music is amazing for the most part, but Jun Senoue should stick to modern Sonic. His compositions are good in this game (minus the boss fights), but the instruments he's using to mimic the Genesis music sound boring and awful. The stage gimmicks and the emerald's power are really fun to use. The boss fights SUCK; they're HORRIBLE and go on for way too long, it really feels like some of them were made for specific characters using specific Chaos Emerald powers. I didn't try local multiplayer, but the game definitely wasn't made for it. The game isn't as good as Mania or 3&K, but it's a great classic Sonic game. Making it 2.5D just so SEGA charges 60 dollars for it is a joke. This game is worth 25-30 dollars max. ARZEST did a good job, I hope to see them collaborate with Christian Whitehead in the future to make a new classic game in the style of Mania. The game is a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr Its half baked, the right ingredients are there but it should have been QA'd, given more treatment and focus in some aspects, and needs a lot of improvement overall.Pros:+Mechanics feel right for 'Classic Sonic' gameplay.+Character choices for different playstyles that you can freely switch between levels if you so choose.+Emerald powers are a nice additional feature to vary up your playstyle.+Graphics overall looks pleasing.+Zones and acts have a good variety of mechanics to keep gameplay fresh.+Infinite lives (You will be glad you have them)+Tee Lopes.Cons:Some obvious ones:-Minor bugs.-Slowdown can occur when certain events are triggered.-Denuvo.-Epic games account required for online play.-Microtransactions. Nothing to put past Sega's recent practices, but still disappointing to see.Gameplay-wise:-Emerald powers really become forgettable until the game prompts you for the niche opportunities to utilize them.-Bosses are full of time-wasting segments that you will find yourself standing around waiting for the next chance to attack if not dodging. Unlike in previous 'classic' titles you will sparsely find opportunities to attack more than once during an opening. -Some bosses also have very cheap attacks (some that will one-shot you) that, coupled with above, can waste 5-10 minutes of your time each try, just for not being able to know those attacks exist. One in particular has a mechanic never used previously and will throw you off completely unless you looked up a guide.-Single-player gamemode gives you a narrower field of view meaning you can get blindsided by traps/enemies, which forces you to play  a Sonic game. This is worsened when playing a certain mode.-Stage pacing feels a little inconsistent when some zones have 3 acts, and others are balanced to only have one.-Medals and bonus stages serve very little purpose other than for customizing a robot you can use for online play, which you may or may not play.-Without going into spoilers, this game feels very lacking in storytelling, especially justifying why Fang even exists (other than for fan nostalgia-baiting), Trip is given little background, and the final boss...is not very well explained either.-Long credits that makes you wonder if selecting "Go back to the main menu" will result in missed content, (It won't.)-Jun Senoue.-All for $60 upfront.And if you're wondering why I have so many hours in this game, the majority was spent on bosses. They are THAT much of a timewaster. All in all, I'd say if the more glaring problems could be fixed with a little more quality-of-life improvements implemented (Just make bosses faster, please.) I would recommend it. But for now, maybe hold off for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars is more than just a game; it's a thrilling journey that beautifully marries the nostalgia of classic Sonic with innovative elements, creating an experience that feels both familiar and refreshingly new.One of the standout features is the intro and ending animations, there is a general intro and then an unique intro and ending for every character,  adding a unique touch to each character. The return to an environmental theme, last seen in Sonic Adventure 1 and more vaguely in Sonic Adventure 2, was a welcome surprise. Sonic Superstars brings back the influence of Naoto Ohshima, the original Sonic' character designer, that can be seen on the influence Sonic 1 and Sonic CD had on Superstars philosophy and design.Character-specific extra acts, such as Sonic's act in Speed Jungle or Knuckles Act in Golden Capital, are noteworthy. They're not needed to play to clear the games, so adding animated scenes or more narrative layers within these levels could further enhance the narrative without imposing on players who prefer a more straightforward approach.While the story has many positive aspects, there are areas for improvement. The reason behind the Black Dragon's awakening could be more clear, offering a more satisfying conclusion. Trip's Story narrative feels a bit disjointed in the game flow, especially after the confrontation with Fang's Robot, raising questions about the sequence of events.Moving on to characters and graphics, Sonic Superstars shines with impressively animated and expressive character models. The attention to detail, evident in unique animations for actions like jumping on rocks in Bridge Island Act 1, sets the game apart. Notably, Trip emerges as a standout character, conveying important messages like Courage that align with the series' character-driven approach. Easter eggs, like Sonic enjoying a chilidog in Bridge Island Act 1, showcase the team's love for the game.However, some environments lack the distinctive Sonic style, particularly in characters' attitude and environment design. For example, Bridge Island and Jungle Speed are full detailed, but other stages like Lagoon City and Golden Capital lacks this super detailed art. To enhance future projects, maintaining character attitudes and avoiding excessive simplicity in environmental art could contribute to a more detailed vision, aligning with the series' roots in dreamlike and surreal aesthetics. For characters, Sonic's running expression might benefit from a cooler, less cute demeanor, aligning with the classic image of Sonic as a character with attitude.Turning to Sound and Music, Sonic Superstars excels with notable sound effects reminiscent of Sonic 1, adding an extra layer of nostalgia for classic game enthusiasts. Musical nods to Hydrocity from Sonic 3 in Lagoon City and Sky Sanctuary in Golden Capital showcase thoughtful touches for dedicated fans. However, the game could benefit from greater cohesion between music tracks, addressing the noticeable contrast in styles within certain acts that should retain the same theme. In terms of controls, Sonic Superstars stands out with its polished and improved controls, surpassing other classic Sonic games. The decision to make Emerald Powers optional allows old-school players the freedom to explore at their own pace. The cooperative mode, while not my personal favorite, does offer a different dynamic for those who enjoy playing with friends. Designating a primary player and ensuring the camera follows them could alleviate frustrations in cooperative play.Despite certain areas for improvement, Sonic Superstars proves to be a well-crafted and enjoyable addition to the Sonic franchise. The game's true evolution of the classics, thoughtful level design, appropriate references to classic games organically integrated in game's design, and rewarding exploration make it a must-play for Sonic fans. The game's future could benefit from addressing some narrative inconsistencies, refining character personalities and expressions (specially Sonic!), and ensuring a more cohesive musical experience. Nonetheless, Sonic Superstars is a commendable installment, showcasing the team's dedication to crafting a Sonic experience that both honors the past and looks towards the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Even ignoring the Epic Games and Denuvo stuff, this game isn't very good, especially when compared to Sonic Mania. Here's what's up: either that or the level design just isn't very tight, I never feel like I can discover alternate paths and things without just blindly jumping. It was definitely made for the co-op mode they've been putting at the center of the advertising, which... Covid set that as a precedent, and I don't always have opportunities to meet up with even my nearby friends in person, much less any of us have the desire to plug in multiple controllers to my PC and huddle around the monitor. And I'd rather not be forced to rely on figuring out how to set up Parsec. And what if I just wanna play with random people, or Internet/long distance friends? Totally betrays the rest of the classic series where you can beat bosses quicker once you learn their patterns and such, as well as the energy of absolutely wailing on a boss. Now you're forced to patiently wait inbetween hits for bosses to get a gleam in their eye and move to a different room, or do some long animation to switch to a different attack mode. There's so much fluff that you end up spending as much time on the bosses as you do the actual levels, sometimes even more. The most difficult ones don't even have checkpoints inbetween phases, so die, and you have to do all five to ten minutes all over again. Don't get me started on the true final boss, it's literally luck . It just sucks because there's a lot of good ideas here and I even sort of enjoyed the challenge, but they're just so tedious - I think if they just opened up the damage windows and sped up the transitions, it'd work way better. and this is coming from an idiot with bad taste who actually likes Sonic 4's soundtracks... it's basically Sonic 4 Episode 3, except in an effort to be more Genesis-accurate, most songs are bland and use overly basic and boring synths that make them absolutely grating. There ARE non-Genesis styled tracks that are better, but they're few and far between. With the exception of those, there just isn't that classic Sonic charm. They're all way too easy, except for the fourth one (I think?) where all the grappling points send you high in the sky, but not far enough to actually grab the emerald. It's a crapshoot whether you get it or not. They're boring and unsatisfying. the mechanic itself is fundamentally flawed. I never ONCE used the water power or the special attack power. I think the main problem is that they're at odds with classic Sonic design in regards to the emeralds... they put the special rings in obvious places so you can access the Special Stages, but they design every level with the possibility that somebody won't have all the powers, and none of the final bosses or sections of the game test your skills with the powers. They're useless. You can't even use them in Time Attack. Back in Sonic Mania, the game would keep track of the blue sphere stages you completed (and even if you got a perfect or not), and depending on how many you beat, you can unlock new moves and modes and stuff. It seems like they wanted to do something similar, since they bother to check if you've gotten a perfect in the stages or not, but all you get out of it are medals which are used to buy the multiplayer cosmetics. No peel-out, no insta-shield, no Fantasy Zone minigame mode (like Mania had for Mean Bean)... it's pointless. The physics are also weird and not faithful at all... why can't you jump when you're on diamonds?!?!?!?I actually don't hate the graphics and the level design's emphasis on platforming and such, but the camera issue and especially the bosses are preventing me from wanting to replay the game. I might do it out of sheer boredom as a Sonic fan, but aside from that, , which I was thinking about at almost every turn playing this. I'm talking $20. $60 is absolute robbery for such a serious lack of bonus content, and even at $40 I'd only recommend for hardcore Sonic fans. I think they're justifying it with the multiple playable characters and multiplayer stuff, but it's not enough like Mania's plethora of extra stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars is a frustrating case of a game that’s ‘core’ is pretty decent, but has some glaring flaws and a lack of substantial content that it cannot justify its price.Sonic Superstars was marketed around it’s co-op mechanics, said co-op mechanics feel very tacked on and are just absolutely miserable to play. You can make very little progress in a level without you or someone else you’re playing with having to get respawned because they were off screen for 2 seconds. Also the lack of traditional online co-op is annoying, as the only way to currently play this game with your friends is through Steam’s ‘remote play’ feature, which is prone to crashing and making the players who aren’t hosting the game’s experience miserable, as it tends to be quite laggy.The level design in Sonic Superstars is honestly pretty decent with the exception of a very small minority of acts not being that great. I’d say most of the levels give you just about what you’d expect out of a 2D Sonic game; Lots of various paths and ways to progress the same level, with you being rewarded for your curiosity and exploration quite often.The game’s playable characters are a mixed bag. Sonic plays exactly as you’d expect him to, with the drop dash from Mania returning yet again, it feels like Sega has a pretty good idea on how they want Classic Sonic to play and I’d say he feels just as good as in other games. Tails plays like how Tails has always played, nothing much to say about him. Knuckles on the other hand… dear god is he clunky, his gliding has fixed momentum and glide canceling is painfully slow, I do not know how they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ him up so much. Amy has a double jump and a pretty useless Hammer dash thing, it also sucks for Amy that this game’s secret character also has a double jump and is overall just better, making Amy feel pretty obsolete after unlocking the secret character.The new power ups you get after collecting each chaos emerald in this game are fun and I think should be a permanent fixture of this series. It feels more rewarding going after the chaos emeralds, because each one you get offers you a new power. Yes, a lot of the powers aren’t that good and have some niche points of application but I feel like with a bit of tweaking these powers could become a beloved feature of future 2D sonic games.The bosses in this game are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AWFUL, a lot of the later bosses take 6-8 minutes to beat, and have the most monotonous gameplay loops and patterns. I do not get any joy or challenge out of fighting them, they’re slow slogs that really take away from the pace of the game. The bosses are the worst part of this game, and if you take anything away from this review it should be that.The game isn’t super buggy, but I ran into a fair share of bugs during my 9 hours of playtime, I’ve clipped through floors and walls a few times, and I have even fallen through a stage once (There was no death zone, so I had to restart the entire act because of it). These aren’t awfully common but they happened enough to be an issue. You are almost guaranteed to run into one of these bugs if you use the superforms.The game has a general sense of charm, and I didn’t think the music was bad. A lot of the characters that appear in the story like Robotnik, Trip and Fang have a lot of personality portrayed through their animations and I think that is worth commending.I may have 9 hours in this game, but I spent A LOT of time ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around and replaying levels as different characters, this game can easily be beaten in 3 hours if you put your mind to it, and because of that, I think the 60$ price tag is ridiculous, especially with the abundance of issues I’ve listed.When this game is great, it really is great but when this game is bad, it is painfully awful. I hope Sega rebalances the bosses and fixes some of the issues with this game, and I could easily see my opinion of this game improving, but as it stands, you should only get this game at a reduced price, it is not worth 60$ in the state it's currently in.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, pretty much what Sonic 4 should have been.Shame the guys who did Mania didn’t stay to create something original with Sonic, but at least some of their ideas were used in Superstars.My gripes with the game is 1. Let Tee Lopes compose the music, he seems to understand classic Sonic vibes more than Jun Senoue does. Jun can write tunes no doubt about it, but my god he needs to step back from composing unless it’s for SA 1 and 2 remakes.2. Difficulty. This is by far the hardest Classic Style Sonic game made. In some parts it’s like I’m playing the oldies again, and then they crank up the difficulty out of nowhere and it becomes less enjoyable. Trip’s final boss is a perfect example of this. Raged quit the game because of some bull instant death lasers.Is this game a 10/10? No, but I would give it a 7/10. It’s good, and fun to play at times, but the difficulty and soundtrack let it down. Wait for this to come on sale, don’t pay full price for it.

_childDocuments_.review: ++- Graphic (best graphic ever)- Controls (in many Sonic games, the controls of 2D Sonic are bad, but in Superstars, it is perfect)- 4-player mode (first time possible)+- Music- Bonus levels (but Bonus level 5 is a little bit too hard)- Shooter zone- - No setting to get 50 rings for big rings after collecting all Chaos Emeralds (there is a mod to change that)- Transforming back from Super Sonic when reaching a boss or cutscene (there is a mod to change that)- Level design (second half of the game and the whole Trip story - too many obstacles and too little flow, too many death traps)- Boss design and long invulnerability frames of bosses- It is not possibe, to get a Chaos Emerald each act (need to wait until zone 7)- No Fire, Lightning, or Bubble Shield (could be activated with an extra button for all characters)- Not 2 acts per zone- Fog of war in Speed Jungle 2- The mini portal bonus levels are bad (should be removed)- Story gap in the "Last Story"- Chaos Emerald powers (they are unnecessary and only needed at specific points; better if only Super Sonic)--- Camera focus (is good in multiplayer, but bad in single player; there is a mod, but the mod is not really good)- Transformations in Cyber Station (they are not fun and also stop Super Sonic)- Last Story boss design (there is also a bug that you don't get enough rings on screen resolution 5120x1440)I recommend buying and playing this game, but it could be much better.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like proper classic 2d Sonic in all the best ways. Incredible soundtrack, diverse environmental aesthetic with unique Zone mechanics for each level... its got it all. I even wanna give Superstars bonus points for a Special Stage design that was actually fun.2D Sonic hasn't felt this good to me since the Sonic Advance series on GBA, some of the BEST 2D sonic games in the whole franchise. I put those games ahead of Rush on the DS, and Superstars might have just jumped up to the top spot.I get what people mean when they say the bosses are too easy or it goes by too quick. But honestly, classic Sonic has always kinda been that way. Mania included. Short and sweet high-speed platforming. It's either your thing or it isn't. No way to majorly lengthen that formula without plots with depth, which classic Sonic never had. Length usually came from replaying and finding ways to get through levels even faster.Battle mode is fun, if very inactive (I've only found one other player in queue ONCE, all other times its all bots). The story you unlock after beating the game (i think you need all the emeralds, too) is some genuinely creative and pleasantly challenging level design, especially with the hidden character's unique abilities. Each chaos emerald you get unlocking a new power to find weird paths through levels with is one the only times collecting the emeralds had an actual meaningful impact on gameplay BEFORE the ending. And I love it.I understand why some people might find it unsatisfying or overpriced, I understand absolutely.I just had way too much fun to agree with you.

_childDocuments_.review: While not as good as Mania or Frontiers, Superstars is a fun and competent Sonic game that sits comfortably as one of the better outings of 2D Sonic we have seen. With the exception of the last Zone in the game, the level design remains fair, enjoyable and full of creative and fun ideas which compliment the core gameplay seemlessly, rather than just serving as cheap, throwaway gimmicks.The bosses are an obvious and unfortunate sour spot of the game, being overly drawn out, boring timewasters that have more than their fair share of unforseeable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and cheap instant-death traps that serve to frustrate the player rather than to challenge them.I am also torn on the newly introduced Emerald Powers. While Bullet is an amazing tool for both exploration and combat, helping to significantly speed up some, but unfortunately not all, boss-fights of the game, the other abilties are far less useful. Avatar can help with speeding up certain boss battles, but remains fairly useless outside of that context. Water is very useful for one specific Zone and then never again. Slow, Vision and Ivy pretty much only find any usage in spots that are specifically designed to make use of them and I have never once found a situation in which Extra proved to be of any use whatsoever.Still, this is classic Sonic at it's core and when in those plentiful moments where you get to enjoy the all too familiar gameplay this series provides, you will experience the same kind of fun you'd expect from something like Sonic 2, even rivaling the likes of Sonic 3 or Mania in those rare moments when Superstars' is at it's very best.

_childDocuments_.review: I would happily place Sonic Superstars on my list of "great 2D Sonic games" alongside with Genesis Sonic 1-3K, Sonic Advanced 1-3, Sonic Mania, and the recent fan games [Sonic 3D in 2D] and [Sonic Triple Trouble 16-bit].Classic feel? Yes! (Physics approved!)Level design? Great!Boss fights? Love them!Music? It's keeping the Sonic standard!You can really smell inspirations from all over the Sonic franchise, but they mixed and matched things into interesting new themes and mechanics.Boss fights could be challenging if you play as Sonic and don't use any of the emerald powers. I like it. If you want an easier time, I suggest playing as Amy and do use the emerald powers.Each character has his/her own charm in this game and the level design makes them all fun to try out. Sonic is good for time attack, Tails and Knuckles are good for exploration, Amy has an easy time with platforming and boss, and the 5th character is kind of a mix Amy and Knuckles.I didn't try the local co-op myself, but from watching others play, I feel like it is not working very well at high speeds. I would suggest either adding an option for the team to manually select a lead player, or adding an option for split screen.One small complaint that carried from Mania though: I prefer the bonus stage at checkpoints to give instant power-ups (shields, speed shoes, invincibility, etc) instead of medals. Mania Plus solved this for me, but the issue now returns. What I like about the bonus stage in Sonic 2 and Sonic 3K is that it rewards you with something that actually helps you in the main game, so playing the bonus stage does not feel like a side-track from the adventure. Otherwise, you gradually lose interest in the bonus stage when you don't need the reward anymore. Though, I am okay with a medal system that lets you buy stuff.Anyway.All in all, Sonic Superstars is great. I am happy.

_childDocuments_.review: TL: DR: Platforming is good but not very "classic Sonic" and the bosses are atrocious due to being designed around 4 player co-op. Can recommend only if you can put up with them or potentially if you plan on playing with friends (I have not tried out the co-op). They really dropped the ball on this one. I'll start by saying the actual platforming is for the most part pretty fun even if it's not very "classic Sonic", not having characters locked to separate save files should have been a thing with Mania and Origins, and the Chaos Emerald powers were fun for a bit. The bosses however are hands down some of the worst in all of the classic series. ESPECIALLY the final bosses of each story and the multiple auto-scroller bosses. Classic Sonic bosses are usually pretty bad but it really feels like all of the bosses here besides the first few just go on forever and some just abuse instant kill attacks which just isn't fun. The special stages are really bad too and having the emeralds locked to 7 specific stages is so weird. Everything feels really handicapped by the fact they designed it first and foremost as a co-op game which is honestly the most confusing thing about Superstars. It's such a backwards way to followup Mania and Origins. I really hope this is not the future of the classic Sonic series.If you can put up with the terrible bosses, then I can recommend it for the platforming but if you're a classic Sonic fan looking for a good momentum platformer look to the fan game scene instead

_childDocuments_.review: For the purposes of this review, I will not be factoring in the Epic Online Services and Denuvo issues. While I do believe those are very scummy, I want to highlight that there is a good but flawed game here.Sonic Superstars is good. I enjoyed most of it. The level designs are fun and their themes are really cool. The physics (minus some hiccups I'll mention later on) were almost spot-on. The visual presentation is also great with a fitting artstyle and very expressive animations for the entire cast. Trip's also a really cute character, and I enjoy her immensely.Now for the problems. Firstly, Jun Senoue should be banned from composing for anything classic Sonic-related until he realizes what he did wrong. While I do not know who composed what for the entire soundtrack, I do know he brought back the Sonic 4 synths for his contributions and he did this while others were going for more of Mania's feel. Jun's compositions from what I can tell are still good. The instrumentation is just bad. My favorite track in the game has to be Sand Sanctuary, which has to be one of the best desert level themes I have ever heard. Tee Lopes went all in for that track.Another big problem with this game is the bosses. Most of them have too much downtime. I know that these bosses were made with multiplayer in mind (which I cannot comment on since I don't have anyone here to play it with), but they could've used better balancing for singleplayer. I feel like if there was different balancing to account for how many players there are, it would go a long way to help the game's replayability. The final bossSo, there are a few minor issues with the physics. Knuckles' glide doesn't accelerate like in 3&K, Mania, and any classic game he was backported to. I've also heard that Sonic feels a little heavier than he does in Mania, but I did my playthrough with the Rabbit skin (which has unique physics, apparently), so I am unsure about that.Overall, Sonic Superstars is a good game with issues I honestly believe that can be remedied with a good patch or two. Knowing Sega, they're going to wait until "Sonic Superstars Plus" or whatever to actually deal with that (or not at all, considering Origins Plus and Colors Ultimate). Also, Edit:  Honestly, this game doesn't tell its story as well as 3&K and Mania. It has the silent storytelling approach from those games, but there's not enough to it to convey what exactly is going on.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars is a blast from the past! I grew up with the original Sonic games, including up to the much praised classic Sonic 3 & Knuckles! Remember that weird lock-on cartridge?Let's get this out of the way: The game, for some reason, requires Epic Games launcher. I already have it installed since I'm gearing up to get Alan Wake 2... and that is clearly not coming to Steam so of course I have Epic Games installed. If this is a big problem for you, stay away from Sonic Superstars until they disconnect it from needing the Epic service.The very first thing this game gets right are the controls, they are very responsive and tight. There is nothing more important to a Sonic game than having split second reaction times, and good controls help with that here. They are shockingly tight, I wasn't expecting the controls to be this good!The character selection is great! There is a decent amount of replay value, including one more character who I love and is a pretty decent addition to the cast. She's cute! All the characters have unique abilities, including the Chaos Emerald abilities which change up gameplay and allow for screen clearing attacks so you can zoom on through safely, or traverse through water more effectively. You can recharge these abilities at checkpoints, and they never felt overpowering or never made the game TOO EASY. I still haven't gotten ALL the Emeralds ( or maybe I will, I plan on replaying the game some more ), that damned Green Chaos Emerald is very hard to get in its bonus stage.Speaking of bonus stages... there's a good selection of them! There's one that is very retro and takes me all the way back to the first Sonic game. Then there's one that requires you to use fruits to access. Finally, the Chaos Emerald bonus stages which are a fun romp that feels like it came straight from the past in terms of gameplay and ideas.The bosses are the best in the Sonic series to date, at least in my opinion. They are often multi-phase, with fun mechanics, and the final boss WILL give you an excellent challenge even if you're a veteran. The final boss might be too brutal in fact.The level design isn't actually too bad, I just wish they were more detailed and full of stuff to look at, but there's still plenty of fun mechanics or stage gimmicks. Hey, at least these aren't Sonic CD levels, don't get me started on Wacky Workbench!The music is hit or miss, there are some standout tracks I really like, and some I really don't like. A certain bonus stage track is probably the most childish sounding thing I've ever heard. I appreciate the nostalgic Sega Genesis soundfonts, but more effort was needed to make these tracks really shine besides the couple or so that I like.The graphics aren't all that amazing, but honestly the style is still quite good, smooth, and runs excellent. This is definitely a game for potato PCs!There are some very good animated scenes, and they really add to the charm of this game. The in-game cutscenes are also cute and convey what they have to convey via visuals rather than words which is just like the classic games.As for the overall speed... it's pretty good! But you will run into some slow, annoying obstacles or segments like pushing heavy objects which really isn't fun.I get it, we Sonic fans are never happy. We compare any new game to Sonic Mania or the classic games especially the venerable Sonic 3 & Knuckles. Any new 3D Sonic game, even if it tries to experiment or set itself apart, is ripped apart instantly and compared to Sonic Generations. Any new 2D Sonic game, like Superstars, is heavily scrutinized. I know, we want something innovative... but wait, they already tried that with several Sonic games and you were disappointed with them. You can argue that maybe Sonic Team should just stop making games if they can't even innovate correctly, but it makes me wonder if Sonic is a formula that can even be done right to begin with. Like, it needs to be a solid platformer, but it also needs to be fast, yet they can't just have you hold one button and move forward constantly. So what is it you exactly want? I don't know. I admit, I just want good fun Sonic games, and that is exactly what Sonic Superstars is, a nostalgic and good bit of Sonic fun that celebrates the past while looking to the future!

_childDocuments_.review: The positive:I decided to pick this up today since it's 60% off and wow I'm astonished at how much I love Sonic Superstars.  I love the graphics, the controls, the music and most importantly the level design and flow!  Because Sonic games are all about speed and flying through levels it's really important to me that I'm not constantly stopped by obstructions.  Thankfully, these levels were designed really great and flow nicely.  The boss battles and extra levels are fun to play which is an added bonus.  The hidden coins and areas are nice to see and a welcome addition that adds replay ability.The negative:Overall this game was review bombed because people don't want to pay $60+ for a Sonic game that has DLC from day one.  I can't say I totally blame them as that's one of the reasons I've waited so long to play this game but I think Sonic Superstars deserves a review beyond price gauging.  On Steam we should have a way to provide our review for both the game and the price separately.  I think there's a certain expectation for the amount of content you should be getting for that $60 price range and sadly a simple platformer just don't fall into that category.  Conclusion:If you've been on the fence about buying this game because of how bad the reviews are don't be.  It's absolutely a fantastic game and I would say it's equal to Sonic Mania and in some cases surpasses it in level design.  Sonic Superstars is worth $30 including the DLC all day long.  At the $23.99 I paid today it's a steal!  Sonic Team please keep making games like this but re-consider what you charge for them.  Perhaps make massive level packs for $20.  Then you could charge $25 for the full game and $20 for say an additional 10 worlds that each have 10 levels.  Wouldn't that make more sense versus constantly making new engines that take years to develop for games that don't sell well at $60?  Following this method as long as the original game feels full and complete I think you'll do really well.
