_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars has the framework of an excellent game but is really let down by its okay level design and badly handled bosses and I can't really recommend the game.Every character controls near-perfectly and honestly that's the best thing about this game. The physics are on-point and Amy is handled better than in Origins, giving her a double jump and allowing her hammer dash to last a lot longer. The game is also visually stunning and performs well even with Denuvo.Unfortunately, that's where the good ends for me.Like I just said, the game has Denuvo, which is annoying if you want to play the game offline (this kind of game is great for the Steam Deck but you're shackled to wherever you can get wi-fi). On top of this, the game also REQUIRES you to sign into an Epic Games account (??????????????) even though this is the Steam version. It doesn't negatively affect gameplay but it is an annoying extra step.The level design is mostly inoffensive but I didn't find them nearly as fun or memorable as those in 3K or Mania. The zones are all original with a distinct lack of Green Hill which is refreshing but some zones felt a little bland, such as Press Factory and Egg Fortress, and wouldn't have seemed out of place in Sonic 4. One standout however is Cyber Station, which is a completely unique level theme in the series so far and is fun to go through.The game structure is the same as the series standard but with some exceptions. Most zones have two main acts save for Cyber Station, which strangely only has one. However many zones have additional acts that are optional, including one act for each character (total, not per zone) meaning no matter who you play as you can play as all four characters, which is a nice way to keep things from getting stale.The bosses, however, are my single biggest problem with the game. Most early bosses are standard Sonic fare but as the game progresses they become much more difficult and overly punishing. It's very easy to get hit and when you die, replaying the bosses can take several minutes per attempt (especially since one of them is an autoscroller). I imagine they're easier in co-op since one person dying won't kill the attempt but in singleplayer it's absolutely brutal and completely killed my enjoyment. By the end of the game I just wanted it to be over.Finally I should probably talk about the soundtrack. Some tracks are fine, however all of the tracks that try to recreate the feel of the Mega Drive/Genesis sound chip are absolutely AWFUL. They wouldn't feel out of place in Sonic 4's ear bleeding soundtrack. Unfortunately none of the soundtrack was particularly memorable and the only one that stuck with me was the incredibly annoying and repetitive boss music.I wouldn't recommend this game, definitely not for full price. Maybe half price or more, but not full price.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been around since the Genesis and was coming off of the high from Sonic Frontiers, it pains me greatly to say I'm heartbroken with this game becoming the newest monkey's paw...but then again, Sega ♥♥♥♥♥♥ it up themselves by having literally anyone but the teams behind Sonic Mania make this game. It really screams that the game is a product by committee: a release put out to the public for a quick buck and profit for SegaSammy this Q3 2023, quality assurance be damned.Some of this is going to be intermixed with my own previously posted thoughts on the Steam discussions, but I will add to them considering how much time I've spent on the game.- Holy piss these Special Stages are , at all. A confusing yet simple mechanic of locking onto an object and swinging doesn't seem to really guarantee or convey well how to get closer to an Emerald faster. The camera is always honed in and staring at the Emerald (and how far it is from you). You may want to lock on and homing attack onto another floating point in the Special Stage void, but ♥♥♥♥ you, you can't, because it's not centered enough on the screen to matter. You could be close enough to bump noses with the floating blue orbs or yellow/ring orbs and it won't matter if that homing reticule doesn't appear at all. It feels like Sonic Team/Arzest wanted to do another Chaos Emerald chase sequence, saw what Mania had, and wanted to make the most un-fun and pure trial/error based one yet. I feel like a good way to gauge a 2D Sonic's game longevity partially involves whether or not the ability to get the Chaos Emeralds is as fun/enjoyable as the journey throughout the stages. If it isn't, then if it's not hard by a large margin, then the game is still good. (see: Genesis 3D Blast. Super easy to do, but at least the rest of the stages/game is enjoyable) - SOUNDTRACK IS mostly good for everything  the starting Dr.Robotnik theme. For some reason the developers wanted to be quirky and make any boss tune that isn't done by Jun to not absolutely suck ass. You can argue until you're blue in the face that it's only the instrumentation that makes that starting boss tune bad, and you're wrong. It's just bad by all accounts. I want whoever composed it to be given a lego to step on for every 10 steps for at least a week for burning my ears with this travesty composition when the other "Genesis" like tracks I've heard so far have been pretty enjoyable. There's several other composers that came onto this project who knew exactly what to do when it comes to mimicking the old chipset the Genesis had back in the day. Those tracks immediately stand out as more of a "Look at what the Genesis can sound like!" rather than Jun's pathetic "Hey guys, remember the Sega Genesis?! ;)". This problem is made even more worse when so many tracks don't follow the restriction of trying to sound like it's from a 16-bit system and follow Sonic CD and Mania's steps for composing/arranging gorgeous sounding tunes. Whoever made Lagoon City Act 2's track needs to be treated to dinner AND promoted.There's clearly a distinction of decent to really enjoyable 'classic' music here but we have >got< to stop allowing Jun Senoue onto Genesis synths where the Sonic 1 snare drum and 10 second loops are all that makes a song. For god's sake, S3/S&K and 3D Blast had songs that LASTED 30 seconds to *over a minute* relatively for both of those games, and those were on 16 MB game cartridges. What's the damn excuse here and now?I want to shake the person who makes these songs and ask "Are you not ashamed of yourself? Do you not have any self respect?" for thinking something like this is excusable. Furthermore I am insulted that Sonic Team wants so badly to be able to allow their head director, Iizuka, to lambaste the longevity of things like retro pixel art in gaming but then turn around and give us flaccid faux-Genesis boss music. Sorry but miss me with that ♥♥♥♥. You can't play both sides here and think we don't see it.- These stages are insanely stingy on Shields or any power-ups whatsoever, making some stages feel incredibly fun to still run through but kind of bland when it comes to the exhilaration of exploration. Gone is the joy in finding a hidden location by pure accident and being rewarded with a Lightning Shield + 1 up + Speed Shoes.Now that same sense of discovery is supposed to be instilled when we find a hidden pathway and we get......a medal. For a mode I'm never going to use, ever.Thanks, it's worthless to me.If this were isolated by just the lack of shields or power ups it would be one thing but it's also the fact that:- Golden City insists on showering you with Rings when lives (or score counters) are useless, making me question why the stages are designed this way. - Special Stage Rings being the '1 Chaos Emerald per World' just to pad out the game is bad design that not even Sonic 1 did this. Removing the reward or agency from the player is not something I consider a fun gimmick. Matter of fact, the gimmicks in this game turn up to 11 once entering Press Factory Zone, where blocky, stop-and-go platforming is all that remains and you will be showered with rings, but maybe you won't care for that once Arzest is shoving yet another stage specific gimmick down your throat like a stage that makes you bounce every few seconds, several by-the-second transformations in Cyber Station zone, or a Fantasy Zone stage straight from the Master System.- Boss fights are the one main reason I will not be replaying this game nearly as often as (quite frankly) any other Sonic game I have in my library. Slow, telegraphed, full of one-hit-death attacks that are meant to prolong the fight as long as possible is the name of the game here. You are not meant to take down these boss fights quickly. Even if you get more than a hit in during a period where you CAN, the boss only registers the first at any given time. It's one thing in a Sonic game when a boss encounter has openings amidst its traps, leaving you seconds to attack it. You can see the opening, you just simply need the moment to strike. Sonic Mania understood this and expanded on what a boss design can include in order to heighten creativity in a player-vs-CPU fight by throwing constant twists from start to finish.Sonic Superstars insists that you truly must sit there and navigate through Fang's near-minute-long auto-scroller segment without getting hit a single time, and Dr.Robotnik's boss fights are no different. Each fight has so much needless downtime that the presentation loses its 'ah!' factor quickly. It'd be so cool if it wasn't built within minutes-long boss sequences in a game where, for some insane reason, Arzest/Sonic Team . So if you don't like sitting through stages that already repeatedly hit upwards of 5-7 minutes, then tough luck, kiddo, you gotta open wide and swallow what's given to you anyways. The hypocrisy behind this entire game from top to bottom is not lost on me, and we've had over 13 years since Sonic 4 Episode 1 to get away from this garbage. We had the example right in front of us with Sonic Mania, and if it comes out that this had little dev time, then it's all the more absurd.Knock it off already, Sega. We're tired of this, and so am I. You burned me, being a Classic fan at heart. How did you make me love your modern Sonic game far more than one that was supposedly aimed right at my heart? You said this game was FOR ME! But you lied.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people will see Sonic Superstars as just a bad, incompetent game, but it's more that this is a rage game.Arzest is a developer known for their spiteful and incomplete game design on top of their love of kaizo traps.Just about every complaint about this game is identical to the complaints about all their other ones, especially the (3)ds Yoshi's Island games.This game isn't too bad as a sonic title, assuming you aren't going for achievements and don't mind a total lack of polish.  Bosses are inexcusable however, and the final, final boss is possibly the least enjoyable experience I have ever had in a video game.A lot of the difficulty would be lessened if certain quirks were not here:1) Every level reuses room layouts repeatedly, so at first you will think you've gone backwards when in reality the same set-piece or loop or jumping puzzle is block-for-block and model-for-model repeated sometimes up to three times in one level.  The final level is utterly incomprehensible because of this.2) Hitboxes were not so strange.  It's not hard to fall through world geometry or get hit by things you didn't even touch.3) Hits did not bounce you right into other enemies or stage hazards.  The main story last boss will bounce you into pits constantly every time you hit him if you don't know the tricks to manage that.The difficult bosses that take ages to even be made vulnerable and the constant "surprise" hits throughout the levels are staples of arzest games, as they are known for being influenced by mario kaizo levels.  It's not an arzest game if you don't get launched off a platform and right into spikes, nor if enemies don't just spawn right at your feet at the worst moment, or you hit a very inconveniently placed bit of scenery just over a pit.All of the above is tolerable, but having decided to get 100% achievements just laid bare all the bs and I couldn't take it anymore.For casual play it might be worth a try on a generous sale.  I personally got 1 hour of playtime per dollar I spent on it (23 hours) to get all achievements.Might replay it one day just for fun, but it won't be anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not the best of habits to start talking about a game by comparing it to other games, but I get the feeling we wouldn't necessarily be playing Sonic Superstars as it is if Sonic Mania hadn't happened, to which this is a roundabout spiritual successor to. And the thing is... I never really got into Mania, which to me felt like a tribute band's first album of their own material. It looked and sounded great but I found it hollow as a play experience, like a decent fangame you give a quick intrigued go but which'll never replace the games it pays homage to. And so I was... uncertain, to some extent, about Superstars. But I gave it a punt - and I'm glad I did.In summary, Superstars is good fun. It's a "classic" Sonic game through and through but it has its original ideas and it leans onto them - the fact that it's not a straightforward 2D sprite entry in the footsteps of the Mega Drive games is in hindsight a clear signal that it wants to establish its own identity even if it wears its inspirations on its sleeves. The new powers tied to the Chaos Emeralds isn't a groundbreaking new gameplay mechanic but it feels like a fresh take on the skill upgrades the series occasionally brings out; it also makes hunting down the Emeralds more engaging because you never know what kind of new trick you can learn next. The basic gameplay also flows well and the level design manages to achieve the balance between easy to navigate and open for countless side paths, and the levels do not feel overly convoluted or labyrinthine (see also: Mania), even though it sometimes feels like you've barely scratched the surface of a zone while zooming through it.And... you know what this game really reminds me of, more than the Mega Drive games? The Sonic Advance series. The more I play Superstars the more I get the same feel that I did out of the SAdv games: between the multiple character choices and the expanded navigation options they all bring as well as the overall level design principles, it's almost deliberate. The Advance games weren't my favourites but they were fun, neat little games with their decidedly own vibe in contrast to the mainline Sonic series - and I like how Superstars echoes back to that idea of creating something with its own vision after all the other recent attempts at 2D Sonic games have been so trapped in the shadow of franchise nostalgia. It's clear that this is a 2D Sonic game, with everything that comes in the packages of both 2D and Sonic, but it wants to be *Sonic Superstars* above all.(I do however give credit where it's due and appreciate how Mania effectively turned the Sonic CD-style anime cinematics into a fixed part of the series' 2D entries. I still love them)The downsides can be summarised by saying that while the gameplay and overall design ethos are extremely solid, the overall experience - the *je ne sais quoi* oomph - falls a bit flat. A big part of it is that the music is really lacklustre and the game's biggest flaw. The Sonic the Hedgehog series is synonymous with great soundtracks, even as it's gone through so many stylistic direction shifts, and in that department Sonic Superstars is completely unmemorable. There isn't a single memorable zone theme, the boss themes are barely there and the game's main theme is pathetically flimsy. I've completed the Story Mode once, gone back to certain levels to sightsee and I'm currently in the middle of the post-game "hard mode" playthrough, so I've been going through these levels a lot - and nothing sticks. At first I was a little annoyed that there doesn't seem to be a physical soundtrack release for this game to go into my collection, but in all honesty I'm not too fussed anymore.The other main downside is the recycling of level concepts. It's nothing new to the Sonic series and especially its 2D entries - each game *has* to have its own "green hill" as a tradition by now - but Superstars feels particularly bereft of coming up with original ideas on where Sonic and the gang adventure in. Every single level is a trope and usually with nothing of their own to add. A few levels do finally figure out their own style (Golden Capital's final parts, Egg Fortress' twist reversal) and they're, to no one's surprise, the most memorable segments of the entire game. Despite the downsides and the fact that I haven't 100%'d this yet and I'm sure to tear off some hairs in the next few weeks judging by how the post-game mode seems to be advancing in difficulty, I'm having a good time with Superstars. It's not a milestone entry for the series (and by no means is it worth the absurdly high asking price), but... well, I go back to my point about this having the general feel of a GBA Sonic game title. Those games weren't *great* either but they were fun and breezy to play, like little palate cleansers in-between the bigger titles, and they were memorable in their own quirky ways. I think Sonic Superstars will eventually fall in that category too.P.S. I've no thoughts on the multiplayer aspect. I have no desire to play 2D Sonic platforming on multiplayer and I feel like as time goes by, people at large are going to forget it was even a selling point (ish) for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has really, really good moments. The entirely new levels, themes, music, all of its presentation visually and audibly is good. But, the rest of this game is a hit or miss, which is why I'm reviewing it with a recommendation against immediately purchasing it. The physics, whilst somewhat like the classic Genesis games, are very weird in some places, and there were three things with this game I noticed were very apparent.First of all, this game punishes you for wanting to go fast. Y'know, the fastest thing alive? Especially in the latter half of the zones, you won't know to slow down on some sections that require platforming or waiting for literal platforms to spawn. If you're going fast you'll plummet into a pit otherwise and it had me so aggravated. I was getting upset because all I wanted to do was blaze some stages. This becomes so much more annoying when you unlock the super form. You can't even do half of this game as it's designed for the normal characters in your super form. Especially if you've beaten the main story and are doing the new character's story, their super form is literally so big half of the things don't work.Second of all, this game has very janky collision issues. I would reach something like a falling platform, and be standing on the far right of it, and if its rubbing against a wall with a gap in it, the game will treat it as if you were crushed, and you'll insta-die. You have to be so conscious on where the player is even standing to proceed and I hated that too. It got annoying quick, especially in the final zone where it happened SIX TIMES.Third and last, this game is overall just hard. The bosses are ridiculous sometimes with their phases and attempting to hit them sometimes is impossible unless you're playing a careful game of precise buttons... or you've died 10 times and figure out that it does the same phases so you adapt. Especially that they rescinded the way bosses worked on the Genesis, you have to wait until after they stop flashing after you hit them and then some. You can only get one hit in per time they're attackable and its annoying. This game doesn't feel like Sonic in some spots and that makes me upset...This game is not worth the $60 dollars, especially when you consider Mania was only half of what this game was in price. Also, EGS? Really? I'm not fussed because I already use Epic for other games but it feels cheap to have this in here for an online service. Very redundant and sort of turns me off of the Battle Mode entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: I think Sonic Superstars is a good game, but is held back by many things that can make it reach it's full potential.First, even though I don't like Epic Games, I didn't care for the account link, especially since I already had an account. I can understand why that would turn off some people, but I personally didn't care.The gameplay was really good. I enjoyed playing every character, and the physics felt accurate to other Classic Sonic games I've played. I didn't necessarily hate any zone either.The new Emerald Powers were really fun to use as well. Even though I  used them a lot when I was prompted to by the game, I found myself using them more than I thought I would.In terms of co-op, I've only played with one other person and it was really fun. _childDocuments_.review: Something to keep in mind is that I've only dabbled in the single-player experience for this game. I've not touched the multiplayer yet, be it the local co-op or online battle mode (though the lack of online co-op baffles me).That said, I don't consider this to be the "perfect" Sonic game, or as close to as perfect as it can get, but I found it enjoyable to the point that I don't care if this game was admittedly overcharged. I don't fault anyone wanting to wait for a price drop before buying, but whether you do or not, you'll squeeze some fun out of this charming title.I DO want to point out that the spin dash feels weird on the PC version. I would sometimes tap the button to charge it, and the game alternates between charging it and...not charging it. Meanwhile when you play it on console, it functions normally. What's up with that?I'm also confused as to why some zones have only one act. Cyber Station was such a good stage and I wanted to play more of it, but only one act?! Maaaaaaaan!On the flip side, I give a thumbs-up to the boss designs, even if some are...time-consuming, but I imagine that will become less of an issue as we play the game more. The stage layouts are great too, but Superstars reminds me of Sonic 1 in that many of the stages lean more towards platforming rather than striking a balance between platforming and speed, which is usually when a Sonic game is at its best. I DO enjoy platforming, though, so this isn't a loss at all.For anyone curious about the soundtrack, there are some gems here (as usual), but I suspect you will find a lot of tracks that'll cause you to scratch your head in confusion. The return of the poorly coordinated Sonic 4-esque music rears its ugly head here, and I dearly wish it hadn't. But it isn't always a recipe for disaster - once you get to the third zone, you'll see what I mean.All in all, not necessarily perfect, but an acceptable addition to a Sonic fan's library. Go buy, go play!P.S. SEGA/SONIC TEAM, I DEMAND A MODERN TRIP GAME RIGHT THIS INSTANT! SHE'S TOO ADORABLE!

_childDocuments_.review: Worse than I could have imagined. It controls correctly, but that's the only good thing you can say about it. All the levels are terrible and full of annoying gimmicks that only get more annoying in the mandatory second playthrough they make you do before letting you fight the true final boss. On top of that, they're boring to explore because they had to make all the special stage entrances obvious to let people get the emerald powers, relegating every reward for exploration to being currency to buy parts for your robot in the online multiplayer Fall Guys mode, that they thought people would want for some reason?All the emerald powers are gimmicky and mostly useless because even though the special stages are obviously placed, they're still optional and not something you're guaranteed to have so they can't actually design levels around you having them. The special stages themselves are a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mess and among the worst in the franchise. I don't know how they made a worse version of Sonic 1's special stage but they sure did it!Maybe the worst part of the game is every single boss fight. They're all a slog with eternal waiting periods until they're vulnerable and 1000000000 invincibility frames after being hit, and they only get more and more sloggy as the game goes on. This game has three final bosses and somehow they're all progressively more nightmarish. That's the main reason why I significantly enjoyed this game.However it's safe to say this game has far more rough edges than it should considering it's price point. It makes the game feel somewhat undercooked or not very well playtested. I'll list off the main complaints I have as a list first and foremost.1. The music is highly inconsistent because there's plenty of great tracks but a lot of rough genesis-ey ones2. The game is often noticeably too zoomed in for comfort which results in far too much blindsiding3. The Multiplayer barely works and often feels more like you're fighting each other and the camera rather than the game4. The game shouldn't be priced 60 dollars. Mania was priced at 20 for a similar and more polished experience for example.5. The bosses often take way too long and the final two bosses are AWFUL. They're a bad mixture of cheap and boring.6. The story is confusing? It feels like they were trying to tell a story but stripped out all of it's substance at some pointSo while I very much enjoyed the game's levels and day to day moments, the game has too many sour spots to be worth 60 bucks so it's more worth it on a significant discount.Also I enjoyed the game far more with a mod that changes much of the soundtrack and allows you to zoom out the camera manually. _childDocuments_.review: Played and beat the game on Switch prior to this review but wanted to address a few things since before beating it on PC as I've been seeing an abundance of negative reviews over something not even related to the game itself. The negative reviews are not doing justice to this game. While the Denuvo and Epic Games login(s) can be annoying and frankly not ideal, it is not reflective at all to the game itself, and honestly, this situation isn't even a rare occurrence with gaming nowadays anyways. Game is super fun. Plays akin to Sonic Mania while not feeling exactly 1:1 with it. Game gives you a good sense of speed and each level brings some sort of new thing that keeps the experience fresh while not making it overwhelming, such as grinding on a vine, switching between the background and foreground of a level, pinball segments, turning into a rocket, and even turning into a shoot-em up for a small section. The game presents so many wacky and stupid ideas but they work to the games' benefit and I found myself having a lot of fun with each level because of it. Each character has a unique move set that makes each level a blast to explore and you can always come back with another character and have a complete different experience with it, especially with the new Chaos Emerald powers. The game generally has a lot of replay-ability and very good gameplay to back it up. Story is fairly simple, not a lot going on here besides some cute little animations every now and then. It's a classic Sonic game so honestly you shouldn't be here for story but it's entertaining enough for what it does. The game visually looks pretty good, each level has a unique theme to it that stands out, and while some definitely look better than others, it never is bad or an ugly aesthetic. Sonic and the rest of the cast look great and have a lot of charm to their models and move very fluidly, resulting in something as simple as running or spindashing feeling pretty satisfying.The music will be pretty mixed for most I can imagine. This game has a lot of composers for it, including the likes of Tee Lopes, who worked on Sonic Mania, TMNT Shredders Revenge, Streets of Rage 4, etc. Jun Senoue, long time producer for Sonic, and more. Each level theme due to how many composers are on the soundtrack, are all pretty different sounding resulting in some themes definitely sounding much better/worse than others. Some of my favorites are definitely Sand Sanctuary, and Pinball Carnival Act 2. Difficulty for this game is pretty consistent but there are times where it can be pretty difficult out of nowhere. I would say at its hardest that this might be one of the hardest 2D Sonic games to date. Overall, while the Denuvo situation is wack as hell and Epic Games login shenanigans are annoying, I would say to still give this game a chance. If $60 seems too much, wait for a price drop. The game could use some polish in areas and some aspects of this game are definitely more enjoyable than others, but this game is still very fun, it's very replayable, feels like a breath of fresh air, and this isn't even getting into the multiplayer aspect of the game, which I found very enjoyable too so this game can even be enjoyed with friends. I give this game a good 8/10. Would recommend.Edit: I've seen people use this link to help Epic Games stuff go away, so use it if you want:

_childDocuments_.review: One of the worst 2D Sonic games, easily. Relies heavily on nostalgia, while just being objectively worse than the original trilogy of games it tries to copy. Movement startup speed is way too slow, boss fights go on way longer than any other 2D Sonic game and have plenty of one hit kills/holes to get knocked into/fall into when glitch through the boss into them.Numerous bugs experienced throughout my play through including:- Drowning when not in water- Spawning at the final level in the overworld when I'm not supposed to then falling through the map endlessly- Glitching through bosses and instantly dying- Getting killed by touching a corner of the world while falling down an elevator (no way I was being crushed)- Having the game pause every time a new level/section was loaded after my controller fell asleep onceIt's embarrassing that this game released a week before Super Mario Bros. Wonder and at the same price. Where Mario innovates in nearly every level, this game has such innovations like:- Hitting fruit with a hammer (guess they are big Gallagher fans)- Literally just doing a Fantasy Zone- Split screen battle mode where if played with two players 50% of the screen is grayed out and you have two tiny screens side by side in the center- A core collectible currency that's spread throughout the story mode (in repetitive mini-games that pop up constantly, as well as in golden enemies and just floating in levels) that can only be used in the awful battlemode- A story mode that is light on story and personality, even less so than previous titles.- A bunch of useless powers granted by each Chaos Emerald- A level where the visuals change (good actually) and everything else in the level is wildly creative, as if they put all their decent ideas into a single place- A story mode where at times you're forced to play as other characters for seemingly no reason.- Same screen co-op that is objectively worse than the old school titles because the camera randomly decides who it is going to follow.I almost always buy Sonic games at launch, because I think its funny that they are so bad and like the idea of continuing that, but I'm finding it hard to find it laughable anymore. It's just bad. And I mean I expected as much from the Balan Wonderland devs (yes it was done by them, minus the one who did the insider trading.)If you held a gun to my head I'd maybe give them a 5/10 to save my life. 4.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely did not like the inclusion of Denuvo and Epic Online Services, especially the giant prompt when you open the game to sign into said services that completely covers up the opening cinematic. This was at least a partial reason for refunding. The other reason is it’s just not a $60 game, not in any way, shape or form. I will praise Arzest for getting the physics mostly right. Flying as Tails and turning around at just the right moment to tail whip enemies in the air feels just like it did in the Genesis games. The main issue for me is the level designs are somewhat bland overall and bereft of enemies and traps. I’m not saying I necessarily want something to slow me down every 5 seconds, but I’m passing most of these levels on my first try without much issue. This game loses a lot of points for me in the music department. Jun Senoue should never be allowed near a Genesis soundfont again. Somehow this music is at times even WORSE than Sonic 4, which is a real feat. There are a couple pleasant tracks, but they don’t balance out the rest of the garbage soundtrack. Of particular mention is the terrible co-op. A friend invited me to do Remote Play Together after I refunded the game which is where the bulk of my play time came from. Co-op is unbelievably bad. The screen gives priority to whomever is furthest right on the screen regardless of elevation, so if two characters take separate paths, but the one on the bottom route is slightly further right, the top screen player will get caught off screen while the bottom path player continues. This can be especially frustrating when you’re trying to get giant rings or just explore the level. It’s also extremely annoying how the literal moment you go off screen, you just turn into a bubble à la NSMB and have to press A to respawn at whichever character has priority. This will happen so frequently that you’re almost better off just staying that way the whole level and only jumping back in when you reach the boss. The co-op implementation is just so mind-bogglingly bad. Why they didn’t just implement split screen like the Genesis games is beyond me. It’s also worth mentioning the boss fights are pretty boring, too. Many of them are of the variety of waiting for the boss to do a thing so you can actually hit it, and they feel designed to just waste your rings in Super form so you have to fight them normally. They’re almost always the weakest part of the respective Acts they are in. Ultimately, while Sonic Superstars does get the feeling and speed of a classic Sonic experience right, it fumbles almost everything else. The paucity of content and other issues inherent to the game make me recommend getting it on a steep discount of at least 50% off if not more. This is especially true if Denuvo and Epic Online Services don’t get removed. There just isn’t enough content here to justify paying any more for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the negative reviews pushed me away at first, and even with all stellar reviews, I would not have paid 59.99 for this.But it's a good sonic game. Some people gripe about "stage design" but I saw no problem with the stages that I wouldn't have had with Sonic 2's designs. The hazards don't catch you by surprise if you can keep up with the speed of the game. Just like any of the classics.Graphics are near perfect with the only thing missing being anti-aliasing. Music is very reminiscent of Sonic CD's JP soundtrack, and gameplay is tight and responsive. And they brought back my new favorite move, the drop dash.The different types of special stages deepen the game a bit too.What really stands out for me is the co-op and the Emerald powers. They really encourage you to revisit the special stages and see what you missed. Sonic Mania is a better game, and it's way less expensive.If this didn't go on sale for half its regular price, I would have skipped it.

_childDocuments_.review: They managed to recreate the classic physics pretty well, and the game puts forth some neat gameplay ideas, but overall the levels feel like a less thoughtful or interesting facsimile of the pixel art games. The soundtrack has a few songs that are fun to listen to, like Speed Jungle and Pinball Carnival's tracks, but most of it just feels phoned-in and uninspired.The bosses are the worst part of the game, full stop. Every single one is overly scripted and long-winded to the point where I was begging the game to just stop. Not all of the bosses in the pixel art games were winners, but at least they were generally brisk and could be taken down quickly with enough skill. Even if you've mastered this game, I imagine half of your typical playthrough will be waiting for the bosses to go through their excessively long attack cycles until they *finally* give you an opportunity to hit their weak point *once*, before starting their cycle all over again. After two playthroughs (Sonic and the extra story), the misery of dealing with these bosses pushed me to give this game a thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah... I finally beat the game and decided to update my review.  It is a big ol NOPE in my book.  I will list the Good, Neutral, and Bad.The Good1. The graphics are pretty decent.  Yes, I have seen far better, but it worked for me.2. Bonus stages - for the emeralds are fun and different, although the emerald ones aren't all that challenging (besides one maybe) but I don't necessarily mid that.  It could be a turn-off for some.3. We see a rework of the original Sonic the Hedgehog bonus stage, which is used to collect medals to unlock things in the shop.  I actually like the puzzle aspect of this bonus stage a lot!4. I also thought it was cool that the robot you create becomes a boss toward the end of the game.  That was pretty awesome!5. This should be number one probably, but the physics feel mostly right!  I had a small issue with inertia at times, but it wasn’t THAT big of a deal.  It was mostly noticeable with Knuckles while gliding and trying to land in a spot with any precision and underwater.  I am so thankful it didn't feel like Sonic 4's physics… especially episode 1!6. The ability to play as Sonic, Tails, Knuckles and Amy. I really like being able to freely change between characters from the world screen and appreciated each character for what they brought to the table.The Neutral1. The music.  This is all personal preference, I get it. I really do!  However, the track was as bland to me as Sonic 4.  I didn’t like the “sound” of Sonic 4’s OST.  That being said, I grew up with the genesis games and I thoroughly enjoy many of the BGMs from Sonic 1-3&K.  Each game has at least one or two levels that stick out.  The compositions were not only fitting, but quite nice.  Most recognize Green Hill Zone, but how about Spring Yard Zone?  Sonic 3 had bangers like Mystic Cave Zone and Metropolis Zone.  Sonic 3&K?  Well… where do we begin there?  Angel Island, Ice Cap, Flying Battery, Carnival Night… that game was full of good tracks.  But Superstars?  The carnival/casino one was good, but not great IMO.  The others were either Okay or meh.  Music is one of the things I really love about Sonic games and the game’s OST was a huge letdown to me.  I am sure some loved it though.  Was half tempted to list this under “the bad” section.4. The level map looks nice.  It doesn’t serve a lot of functionality, but it works as a graphical representation.  I think it could have been done a lot better.  I guess they decided to take the Sonic Generations route with it.5. Emerald Powers - My experience with the game so far is that they aren't really all that useful.  A couple are handy for certain situations, but I pretty much never bothered with them for 99% of the game.  I don't think they should be mandatory by any means, but bothering with them often slows down the game for me for all the more benefit they provide.The Bad1. Sonic seemed very mediocre as a character.  Sonic just plays like a normal character besides his “dropdash.”  It would have been nice to see an insta-shield, homing attack, or had elemental shields he could take advantage of.  Why would you want to be Sonic in this game?  He feels bland when compared to Tails’ flying (which is OP in this game), Knuckles climbing and gliding, and Amy’s hammer and double-jump.  I wish they gave him something besides dropdash.  From what I saw, he did not have anything else.  (Someone please correct me if I am wrong here.  I would love to be.)2. Boss fights feel so slow.  The bosses are largely cinematic.  You watch the boss attack while being largely invulnerable (besides if maybe you have all seven emeralds and have gone super). I think it was a good thing that they wanted the boss fights to stick out more, but IMO they went the wrong way with it.  Over half the fight is generally watching the boss do something and moving to avoid attacks.  There were times I got so bored and was distracted by something else and forgot I was even in a boss fight and died.  (LOL Yes, I know that is largely a ME problem probably.)  I also found some of the bosses unnecessarily difficult.  I guess the fact that you get unlimited lives gave them license to make them a pain and take forever to fight.3. No “bounce” on boss hit.  IMO it was a good system in older games when you bounced off the boss a bit after hitting them.  I don’t like feeling like I just smashed into them and fell straight down.  This actually got me killed in the custom robo boss until I switched to tails so I could just fly after landing the final hit on the boss so I could avoid the pitfall.4. The Price – Look, It is an okay game.  It isn’t worth $60.  I’m sorry.  It just isn’t.  I could see $40 for it for all the longer it is.  Maaaybe you could do $50, but $60?  You have to be out of your mind!5. Denuvo – Anyone that has looked into Denuvo knows it is at best useless, at worst, something that will tax your computer system and cause performance degrade.  Why any company wastes money on this crap is beyond me…  It isn’t a deal-breaker for me, but many won’t like this.6. Steam Version Requires Epic Games – Why should a game on Steam require Epic Games?  They are two different platforms.  They couldn’t make it work with just the Steam launcher?  Again, it isn’t a deal-breaker for me, but many won’t like this.7. Fruit Levels – Am I the only unlucky person that never got fruit from the post-boss reward capsule? (This is why I don’t play slot machines in Sonic or IRL.)8. Level Design - Oh my goodness.  The first zone was so fun, then it just becomes a slog.  Levels get a bit slower with a lot of enemies and hazards, (sometimes enemies that sit in the background and shoot you that you can't actually destroy) and these parts really slow down the act.  Some acts are nothing but these.  Furthermore, did you get super?  Well, fortunately the game can take you out of sure (like boss intro) and if you were below 50 rings, sucks to be you.  I also had an issue on the second story, with the new character's super form and with tails because some levels have you switch between the foreground and background by interacting with certain objects.  So if you wanted to transform and just skip over stuff on certain acts... well you will get stuck or end up dead.  It is very obvious they didn't really test these things very well.9. Super Form - It is just so underwhelming in this game.  Going super helps to SOME degree in the acts, but is almost useless in some bosses and going super can kill you.  Why, you may ask?  Because the boss will take anywhere from 15-30 seconds to be invulnerable while your rings tick away at times.  Unless you had A LOT of rings, you are going to be stuck leaving super form for at least part of the boss fight.  You also aren't immune to some insta-death mechanics in super form as well.  Like the emerald powers, it leave me asking why bother to use it?Overall, I think the game is pretty terrible, which hurts me to say because I have been a long-time Sonic player.  This is the status quo, though.  Sonic games have been pretty shaky, and even things like Frontiers lack any real depth or particularly great design.  IMO this game isn't worth the $60 price tag.  If you really want to punish yourself, get it on sale for $20-$30.  In all honesty, I would say skip this game and buy something better.

_childDocuments_.review: Denuvo bad, forced Epic Games Online Services bad. Not disclosing it until later terrible.With the obvious out of the way, this is quite a good classic Sonic game. My two biggest concerns, the physics and level design, both ended up being quite good! This is further proof that you don't need Genesis-accurate physics in a 2D Sonic game (though if you're arguing otherwise, you've clearly never played Sonic Advance or Rush).Sadly the bosses all destroy the pacing and are simply not good. They all suffer from the Sonic 4 Problem™ where they take way too long to reveal their weak points, or otherwise just have really long animations. The only good boss imo is the final boss, and I wouldn't even say it's good mechanically, it's just the spectacle of it that won me over (sounds similar to Sonic Frontiers, almost, doesn't it?). Especially near the end of the game they end up taking waaaay too long. I had a red timer multiple times.The zones... ohh, the zones! They're all so, so good! Possibly some of the best designed zones in the series can be found here. My absolute favorite is Pinball Carnival - it combines the carnival aesthetic with Eggman's signature industrial factories, and it's just perfect. The one zone I don't really like is the cyber one, with the pixel character gimmicks. That one felt kind of forced, there was no level transition into it and it felt "video gamey" to me, which I don't like. The rest are good, though - shoutouts to the final zone, which The soundtrack is pretty good, though the regular boss themes don't really fit. It overall reminded me of Sonic 4 at times, so if you aren't a fan of that soundtrack then that's something to keep in mind. The instrumentation is better here at least - I just wish there was more Mania-inspired (or I guess Tee Lopes-inspired?) music here rather than Genesis-inspired since much of the time that ends up falling a little flat.Note: I've not fully played  yet. I also played the game entirely on Steam Deck and it worked quite well (with frame drops, though that's probably moreso due to shader compilation and not a fault of the game).Why does one of the top reviews call this Sonic 4 Episode 3? It very much isn't.This probably isn't worth full price - I'd say this is more of a $45-50 USD game. It's not bad, but it's not Mania level quality. Still, I'd recommend it to others, if they can put up with the bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: *Note - this game barely gets the recommended rating. I would give it a mixed review if the option was available*Sonic Superstars is a return to 2D classic Sonic and thankfully, much like Sonic Mania before it, it inherits the 2D classic titles physics and gameplay. If you've played the classic titles on the Mega Drive/Genesis, Sonic Origins or Sonic Mania, you know exactly what to expect. If not, classic Sonic titles feature momentum based platforming where speed is the reward and the name of the game. The gameplay still feels just as satisfying as the older titles, you can explore and take multiple pathways throughout the levels with the higher paths often leading to faster traversal through the levels. You can also pick multiple different playable characters, each with their own unique attributes. Sonic, Tails and Knuckles all perform exactly as you would expect from Sonic 3+K and Sonic Mania, with Amy for the first time being available at launch in a 2D Sonic title rounding off the pack, with a unique double jump and huge hitbox, making her feel unique in her own way. All the characters are fun to play and regardless of who you pick, you will be able to play a unique special act, which makes you play as one of the characters specifically. There is also a 5th playable character, available once you beat the main story but I will not go into detail for this due to spoiling the game.This time round, Sonic Superstars tries to take a page out of the New Super Mario Bros book and introduces 4 player multiplayer for you to play with your friends. While this sounds like a good idea on paper, the execution leaves much to be desired. The camera cannot decide who to focus on, meaning players will frequently be thrown off screen and forced to respawn as the camera constantly switches and jumps around from player to player in an erratic fashion. Frustratingly, this issue could likely have been solved by focusing on the top right player or by further zooming out the screen and adding a 'P1, P2, P3, P4' icon. In addition, for some bizarre reason there is no online multiplayer for this game. You can get around this with remote play and it's a mess to set up but it can work. Sadly, as it stands right now, unless you are specifically co-ordinating and going slower, multiplayer is nothing but a chaotic, unpolished experience. Unlike Sonic Mania before it, Sonic Superstars takes the 2.5D approach to its graphics, similar to the NSMB series. While some would prefer the pixel artstyle of the Classic titles, Sonic Superstars still manages to look great. This also extends to the completely unique levels, which is a bonus when compared to Sonic Mania's reimaginings taking up a considerable portion of the levels. This makes the game feel fresher than Sonic Mania, though this is not to Sonic Mania's discredit.The story is poorly explained. While the cutscenes at the beginning of the game and the ending look great, it's really not explained how some things happen. This problem is exacerbated by the final boss for the 'Last' story appearing out of what is essentially nowhere and the ending having it sealed in what appears to be an egg by the hidden playable character. There are small hints, hidden during the character acts but frankly, the story is a disjointed mess, which is a shame because a handful more of the animated cutscenes sprinkled throughout could have helped the cohesion.While the gameplay overall is fantastic and the graphics and levels are all interesting and look great, the game is sadly let down by the very frustrating boss designs. In classic Sonic titles, you are allowed to hit the bosses as many times as you like, the risk/reward being that you may take a hit whilst doing so, which could lead to a death. In Sonic Superstars, unfortunately Sonic Team made the decision to give bosses invincible frames (I-frames, boss cannot take any damage) after you hit it once, forcing you to wait whilst an animation plays out and an attack sequence happens again. The waiting really drags out the boss fights and can make them feel tedious. This problem is made even worse in the late game, where bosses often can take 5+ minutes to fight. One of the bosses is an annoying sidescroller where for half the fight you literally just sit there and wait. If you die, you end up going all the way back and having to sit through it again, waiting for ages to be given the chance to attack. This problem is made worse when the later bosses also incorporate insta kill mechanics, which means that you will die and end up having to wait a lot, making the whole experience even more frustrating.The instant kill mechanics also feel incredibly cheap. Take a game like the Souls series, those games manage to not feel cheap because a lot of the time if you fail, it feels like the players fault, fair enough. In Sonic Superstars, you will not feel like it is fair. For example, another boss requires you to consistently run to the right whilst it drops explosives on you. The player is already being skill checked for their speed and momentum platforming. While this is happening, the level behind you is disappearing, leading to bottomless pits. Take a single hit during this fight, regardless of rings, you will more than likely fall into the pit and have to restart.Another example is the final boss of the hidden characters story and the 'Last' story. The boss in the hidden character's story gives you rings but they are all but utterly useless since the overwhelming majority of the attacks will insta kill you regardless of your ring count. This is made even worse by having a badly choreographed final attack that again, you guessed it, can insta kill you. As this boss is a two stage fight, it can really drag on and lead to many frustrating restarts unless played flawlessly. This is not fun and difficult for the sake of being artificially difficult and badly telegraphed to the player. Likewise, the 'Last' story boss suffers from the same badly telegraphed attack issue in the final stage of the fight, which also incorporates QTE's that do NOT explain when you are supposed to press the dash button (it's the circumference by the way, not when it changes colour like every other game in the industry...). There is absolutely no indication given to the player, leading to frustrating deaths and restarts. Combine this with the complete RNG of the ring drops required during the Super Sonic fight and you may well be at the mercy of RNG and not have enough rings to even complete the final stage. When you hear or read about how the bosses in this game are a joke, to be fair to the game, it's only really a huge problem in the last quarter or so of the game. Unfortunately, as this is the part gamers will likely remember the most, it leaves a very bitter taste and sours the whole experience of the game.There is a good game buried in Sonic Superstars but as always with Sonic games, it's buried under very poor design choices. If Sonic Team and Sega release a patch that does the following then the game could potentially sit there with the likes of Sonic Mania:- Remove I-frames and allow the player to attack the bosses multiple times- Add in online co-op- Fix the camera in multiplayer, either by focusing on the 'lead' player or by pulling the camera out further to show more of the levels dynamically- Remove/rework the bosses to remove RNG and the multiple insta kill mechanics (one or two in the final bosses are fine)Right now, this is a game that has potential and may be worth a look but you really have to be prepared to potentially have your experience ruined by the bosses. For now, it just about gets a 'recommended' rating because I still had a great time with the levels themselves but just exercise caution if you're considering this title.

_childDocuments_.review: SEGA decided to finally give us a new 2D Classic Sonic game after 6 years, but this time developed by Arzest, known for plenty of titles, most notably one of the worst games of 2021 "Balan Wonderworld", but hey, maybe that was an accident.First, of course, the graphics.This is the first proper 2D Sonic game that doesn't use pixel art since Sonic 4, and it looks okay.The character models are pretty well animated for the most part, it's also pretty colorful, however the zones themselves have fairly generic themes and the graphics don't help them convey anything else. They almost feel totally empty foreground and background-wise, it's odd how the Sonic games with pixel art have way more detail and charm.The music is also subpar, especially for a Sonic game.They hired the Avengers of composers to make one of the most forgettable soundtracks imaginable, the only memorable track is the Zone clear theme that they ripped straight from Mania, and it sticks out, cause the rest of the OST doesn't have that style. Jun Senoue went to work and whipped out that synth and drums to desperately make music that sounds like the old Classic Sonic games to no avail, it ends up being forgettable with a complete lack of identity.Now to the gameplay, you don't need to worry about the physics, they are almost a 1:1 copy of the physics from Sonic Mania, but good physics doesn't mean good level design.The level design completely misses the mark, in concept it understands that multiple paths = Sonic game, but in its execution it feels more like Sonic CD where half the act is a literal labyrinth. It's very stop & go, you can only really go fast when the game allows you to do so, and it doesn't help that the camera is so zoomed in that you have trouble seeing what's ahead of you. Sure, this is a critique that many Classic Sonic games have had over the years, but in this game it especially rings true. Furthermore, getting the optimal path is synonymous with automation, there are so many moments where you just watch stuff happen, or you hold to the right with nothing happening, but when something happens oh well, it's over. This game LOVES instant death traps that crush you. Let me tell you, making your later zones harder doesn't mean making them full of instant deaths, it's cheap and unavoidable, after all, you got that limited vision to deal with. Even cheaper are deaths caused by going too fast, due to the gimmick being the floor "spawning in".What's even more embarrassing is how Sonic Superstars boasted about having original zones, and then decides to instead rip-off gimmicks from older games. You aren't being original, you just moved your copy & paste problem to another part of the levels. Now we have the bubbles, ice and the weird spinning balls from Titanic Monarch from Mania in this game, and it's just such a blatant rip-off that I can't even consider this a "nod to the series". Additionally, we have a worse drill than the drill Wisp from Sonic Colors.Another issue is the pacing. Some zones have 1 act, some have 2, and some even 3. They already figured out in 1993 that 2 acts are more than enough for a zone, after that it drags on, despite that they even made 1 act long zones drag on. There's no reason for a Sonic game to have levels that take 5–8 minutes to complete, even with the perfect route. The levels aren't even that interesting, why do they take so long?The answer is: The bosses. These are some of the worst bosses in the series. Some of them take two minutes, but there are even ones that take longer than the act they're in, with one of them clocking in at 5 minutes. You can't even speed up the process. They removed the option to do multiple hits during a boss' phase, so it's just a game of how long you have to wait 'til you get another hit in. They take the wind out of the sails and make you want to replay the game less and less.Let's move on to the Special Stages, cause at least they aren't the worst.They aren't good, they aren't bad, just kind of there. You have to homing attack floating objects and swing yourself to the Emerald. There are occasionally springs sprinkled throughout the stage that help you get to your destination faster, but that's it. Just press A and you will make it eventually.Chaos Emeralds not only grant you Super Sonic, but you also get a Special Ability from each Emerald. These range from fine to being so situational that you won't use them even once during your playthrough. The only useful ones are the ones that help you speed up the bosses or go to another path, although they still are so optional that you don't even need to use them at all, they could've been a neat mechanic, but they end up being more of an underutilized gimmick.The worst part about the Chaos Emeralds, though, is that you need to finish the game twice to actually fight the true final boss. Why change something that’s been a staple of this franchise for decades? You’re just trying to make me play that shoehorned in slightly harder mode that barely has any merit.However, the worst part of this game is easily the Coop. They marketed it so much and it’s so undercooked, it’s one of the worst cooperative multiplayer experiences I, and my friend ever had.The game does NOT let you leave the screen for even a millisecond. The moment you go off-screen, you despawn and have to respawn next to your mate. The bigger issue is that it doesn’t even zoom out when you’re far apart. This is not intuitive for a Sonic game, where you can be on the other half of the screen by simply touching a spring or bounce pad.Even the gimmicks in the level are controlled by the player the game currently considers the “main player” which you can’t know. There’s for example a torch gimmick in Speed Jungle Act 2, surprisingly only one player gets the torch and the other stays in the dark, the light isn’t even that bright, so you easily end up staying in the dark, not knowing where you're at.To add insult to injury, there are SINGLEPLAYER ACTS IN THE COOP, so you have to tell your friend to sit in the cuck chair while you’re busy for the next 5 minutes or so. These acts are character specific ones that are designed after the character’s abilities, but why couldn’t you just add 4 different colors for each character to ensure that your as coop advertised experience is actually coop? It's a punch to the gut, since I think the character specific levels are a neat idea.Obviously, to make this the least cooperative coop, the game simply doesn't allow you using the Chaos Emerald abilities individually, including Super forms, leading to your friend enjoying a speed and jump distance boost, while you keep respawning for being too slow.I am not someone who encounters bugs often, even in buggy games. Sonic Superstars differs, by being undoubtedly one of the most unpolished and buggy 2D Sonic games ever conceived.There are so many glitches that I had to open a text file to keep track of them. The most obvious one was simply falling through the floor during the final boss, even the rings did that on occasion, meaning I had to retry it multiple times for something that isn’t my fault.Other bugs include not being able to respawn, getting soft locked, music stops playing after using an Emerald power, drowning through air, enemies not spawning in, except for their projectiles, enemies thinking the floor is a suggestion and clipping right through it, them crediting people, but there's literally no name, and other visual glitches like the pause UI not appearing.The one thing that wasted the everyone's time wasn't a bug, it was the devs forgetting about a skip credits button. These are 10 minutes long, and if you want to fully finish the game you need to sit through them thrice, enough for me to go out and get some groceries.Superstars is at best mediocre & at worst atrocious to play. It does everything wrong that Mania perfected 6 years prior. 4/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars was SEGA, Sonic Team, and Arzest's attempt to continue from the success and praise of Evening Star's 2017 throwback, Sonic Mania. The question is...did they do it? In my opinion, yes. They did. Superstars feels like a natural continuation of the classic titles on the Mega Drive, picking up elements like Mini-Bosses, One Act Zones, Transitions and more. The controls are almost, if not fully exactly the same as the originals, which is a huge achievement. Sonic Mania was for the longest time the closest we got to the original slope controls. 2.5D games were believed to never get it right, as Generations, Forces, Sonic 4 and etc. always featuring a issue. But Superstars finally proves that it can be, and has been done. The level design is the true and tested formula of multiple routes depending on your skill level, but now much bigger and in some cases, kept in one single act, like Sand Sanctuary. I really like the level design, nuff said. Bosses do take effort to beat this time. Sonic bosses usually go how an act goes, depending on how much your persistent, you can bash your way through, but this time, the opposite is true. You now have to wait and learn the enemy attacks, and be patient, and for a Sonic game, it's appreciated and mostly done well, but some waits can be...long. The big new addition are Co-Op and the Emerald Powers. I played Co-Op with a friend and while very chaotic and almost stupid in some cases, we had loads of fun, the the degree that now we're doing a full playthough throughout Uni class breaks. While online would have been awesome, I do really enjoy couch co-op, and sharing the fun with my best friend for the first time with Sonic, it'll be memories that I'll hold forever, and that will never be left out of my thoughts of the game.The emerald powers remind me of the double gear system in Mega Man 11, not fully needed to play the game, but when used effectively, can be your best friend, and it's the case here. Slowdown, Bullet, and more are super helpful and can either save you from a mess up or exploration, so overall, I really like em. One element that might go unnoticed is presentation, and I'm impressed. Character models, stage visuals and etc. are all very well done, and while some acts can seem more generic that others, I still feel many stages are memorable, like Bridge Island, Cyber Station and Pinball Carnival. Music overall is very good, like any Sonic game, and features some first time Sonic composers from across SEGA's Sound Team, who worked on Yakuza/Like A Dragon, Judgement and Super Monkey Ball, and one track comes right from the 80's with a song based on the music from Fantasy Zone!Superstars really is an amazing game, and it's clear there is areas of improvement, but that's good, because it shows where we can go from here, and with what we already have here, I'd me more than happy for the new team to take on a follow up. Sonic The Hedgehog 6 anyone?Some Steam/Steam Deck notes - Epic Game Login is...interesting? I understand it isn't a requirement, but it's a bizarre choice. Also, it is a shame the PC release had a weird launch, and the inclusion of Denuvo risks this game being worse performance wise than it needs to be. Good News tho, Sonic Superstars worked amazingly on Steam Deck, if it wasn't for the login for EGS, it'd be verified. The only issue is when you turn Super Sonic, it can hang around low to mid 50's fps and also when a lot of particle effects are going on a once, but they're a small issue and the drop isn't that noticeable until it's actually passed, so it's still great overall. Sonic Superstars in it's current form is, for me at least, a 9/10. It might end up being my favourite classic sonic game, or at the very least, the one I'll be finding myself go back to out of any classic title. Which is funny since every mainline 2D Sonic game is on Steam! So, yeah, pick this game up, it's amazing and made of pure love, and I'm excited for where the future of 2D Classic Sonic goes.

_childDocuments_.review: Forget about Denuvo, Forget about Epic Games stuff, it doesn't bother me. What bothers me is the actual game itself. This game suffers from two very big problems, two problems that I believe let the entire experience down. I'm talking about:1: The boss fights.2: The level design. The boss fights are some of the worst ever in a Sonic game, and believe me, I've played nearly all of them. How we can go from some of the most exciting, fun bosses in Sonic Frontiers to the absolute snooze fest this game offers is staggering. The bosses go on far too long. Every single boss in the game requires a huge amount of waiting that it makes them so boring. It just comes down to attack once, wait 20 seconds, attack again, wait 20 seconds, atta-oh no you missed, wait another 20 seconds. It's terrible. That's not even mentioning that some of their attack patterns are needlessly strict and some bosses have cheap instant kill moves - gotta love it! >:IThe level design is awful, just awful. The best comparison is to the Advance titles but not the good zones in Advance 1 and 2, I'm talking about the really bad ones from Advance 3. Constant examples of the level automatically throwing you into enemies after speed sections. The game punishes you so many times for going fast, bottomless pits, cheap enemies (many suffer from the same waiting problem as the bosses) and just overall boring design. No level stuck out to me when I finished the game, no real good music tracks accompany them either which is so disappointing for Sonic which always has great level themes. Overall, the game is dull, the art style is cute and fun but when the game is just so painfully average, it just sucks. I was really looking forward to this but unfortunately this is not the successor to Mania I was looking for. Definitely not worth full price! Wait for sale and even then, be cautious.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, when I heard a new Classic Sonic game was announced I was pretty excited!I mean, a new 3D Classic Sonic with Multiplayer and Emerald Powers, that sounds pretty neat right?For me yes, specially now that I am kinda discovering the Sonic franchise, and playing some pretty decent Sonic titles, and this one is the most recent Sonic game I have played yet.When it released I heard good things about it, so I was expecting a pretty good experience.I have almost completed this game 100%, having the last 2 bossfights left, so I thought writing a review for it would be a good idea to say...I don't like this game.I will start with the good things.The game honestly looks pretty nice, it's cool to see Classic Sonic in such colorful world and in 3D (without counting Generations or Forces), seeing Classic Sonic always in 2D pixelated graphics was starting to feel kinda tiring for me, but i think they managed to maintain the same feel as the other games with this one with how good it looks! I hope more Classic Sonic games look like this!The cutscenes and animations of the characters also look pretty good, feels like I am watching a cartoon, which fits Classic Sonic and the others. The art direction as a whole is pretty good in this game.And the characters also control very well, some people say that characters felt too heavy, but I don't know, they felt to me, and moving around with them is pretty nice.Plus, all of them have their different abilities, like Tails being able to fly for a period of time, or Amy being able to use her hammer, making all of them distinct and fun to play and choose between all characters.And I also like the new character, Trip, hope I see her in future games!Aaaaand, yeah that's it, that's everything I liked for the most part, the presentation is very good and the characters are fun...The rest of the game... Ranges from meh, to bad, to terrible, and from this point and onward, I will list these things that are not so good.Like the music, I don't think it's THAT bad, it's bad for Sonic standards, which that I do agree, but still wish the music was a bit better because nothing stands out. It's a shame because usually the most consistently good thing about Sonic games is the music but oh welp.I also wish that more stages were like Cyberspace Station, because most of them feel kinda whatever in theme and in gimmicks. Some of them are ok like Bridge Island or Speed Jungle, but the rest of them didn't stand out in any way, which Zone 9 did because of its different artstyle and different gameplay mechanics. At least these are original but still, I wish they were a bit better. They are not bad, but I felt like they could have done a bit more with it.There are acts that are kinda just... there, i guess... The character acts, which apparently, you don't have to complete to get to the next zones and are only singleplayer, so what's the point?And same could be said for act FRUIT, which you can play if you have 1 fruit or more, but let's be honest... Do you play this more than 2 times? Because personally I could see this only being replayable for achievements.These fruits are already hidden pretty well, but they are always in the same spot in every act, so you can kinda farm them, making this restriction kinda pointless. But even with it, you just get a few medals and nothing else.Maybe act FRUITs are good for trying to get a high-score with friends or so, but other than that, it felt like missed potential with these.I mentioned friends. Which is because this game heavily advertised as a multiplayer experience.Now look, personally multiplayer and Sonic sounds weird together, because Sonic is a game where you usually like going fast. The problem is that the multiplayer is very broken.Thankfully I didn't get to experience it that well, but a lot of it was very disappointing.There is a camera where all 4 players should be, this camera follow the player that is the most advanced in the level, so the "camera player" cant go too far from the others, or basically the other players will despawn from the level and spawn after a moment where the "camera player" is. In practise, there are way too many times where there are players spawning and despawning almost every 5 seconds, which isn't very fun, but you know what would fix it?Going slow. In a Sonic game. That's the problem with it, game-pacing is more important for multiplayer than people give it credit for, and if you say: "What's the problem with going slow in Sonic games?"The problem is that what makes Sonic standout from other platformers (or at least it is from a general sense), is going fast, if I do not go fast, what makes me want to play a Sonic game besides being another platformer with multiplayer.And also, remember those character acts i just mentioned a moment ago, those cant be played multiplayer, which sure, fair enough, but there is one separate mode where you cannot play multiplayer either, and that is Trip's Story, and I have no idea why you can't play this section in multiplayer if you want to play harder stages.There is also no Online Co-op which sure, usually in platformers is not a good experience, but having the option would still be nice.And there are some very game-breaking bugs if you play multiplayer, I didn't get to experience them myself, but still, things that should not happen, like players not appearing once they despawn from not being in the camera, to weird deaths and ring-loses for... no reason?It's broken and while it can be fun, it is a mess, which sucks because they put emphasis on the multiplayer for this game.One thing I also was disappointed, which the game also put a lot of emphasis into, are the Chaos Emerald powers.Once you get them, you unlock new powers, and I'll give a quick thought on them.Blue - Clone - Situational in actual levels, good for cheesing bossfights.Red - Bullet - Easily the best one, and in my opinion, should be the standard for all of them because it's pretty fun.Cyan - Water - Useful for like 1 level, shouldnt have been a Power.Green - Ivy - This one is also good, specially for vertical levels and making some platforms for yourself.Purple - Vision - Completely ruined by the game telling you where to use it, ok for getting secrets like medals.Yellow - Slow - It's ok, useful for a couple of stages and for the bossfights, this one gets a pass.White - Extra - This should not have been it's own Emerald, why can you use an extra character-unique move for 20 seconds?After getting all Emeralds, you also unlock the Super ability, which is cool.Overall, the Emeralds are a mix-bag, and I wish they impacted gameplay more, because you kinda dont have to use them except for some brief moments, sometimes I forget I have those Emeralds.Trip's story was also kinda disappointing for me. Long-story-short, this is a hard mode, which hey, I like when games get tough. I was expecting something else however, newer levels, maybe some sections being very different, but the way they made it is basically: "Pick this act, put more enemies, put more spikes, done."I do not like that. Yes, it is a harder version of the original act, but they could have made it more than that.You also can't play as the other characters, which sure, it's TRIP's story, but it would be nice if you could play as others.I am not even going to mention bossfights being the way they are, everyone has complained about them.I wanted to like this game seriously, and I was so excited for it, but there are just so many missed opportunities and bad game design decisions putted into this game (in my opinion), which makes it very fundamentaly flawed in many areas.If you don't care about most of these, that is fine, my reviews tend to cover everything for a game, specially what is trying to make the game special.You can still have a lot of fun with this game, but for me, it isn't very good, specially for 60$.Not recommended3.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game, even with its few problems. I'm going to ignore the elephant in the room with the whole Denuvo/EGS fiasco since it doesn't affect me. Simply put, I do not care and have yet to be given a reason to.For the game itself, it's pretty neat. It's not perfect and a lot of level design (especially during a certain character's unlockable campaign) is VERY hit or miss. But as far as the main cast goes, the level design is pretty smooth and fun. It moreso takes the design philosophy of Sonic 1/CD where speeding through the levels and getting a good time is moreso a result of memorization and knowledge of the stage, instead of 2/3s way of just railroading you along the fast route.Each character has an act exclusive to them as well. Nothing fancy, but a stage dedicated to a character and their moveset is appreciated. Would love to have seen more of these though.The biggest downside I'd say are the bosses. Mainly, the stage bosses. They're very "wait for your turn, then get 1 hit off". If you know how they work, they're pretty fast and you can quickly learn how to get a few cheap hits in with the emerald powers to speed them up. But regardless, you are still waiting through simple patterns for a chance to do that.The exception to this, are the final bosses. I adore these. They aren't over in minutes like most sonic bosses are, put up a good challenge, and don't let you gorilla your way through by living forever with 1 ring.They're a lot more about correct positioning and managing your speed/momentum. Their attacks are simple, and even their OHKO attacks are extremely easy to dodge if you know how they work. The final bosses don't ask for much, just your attention and for you to actually watch and observe how their attacks work. I've seen a lot of people chalk them up to being unfair with unpredictability, when really just watching their attacks will show you exactly how they work and what the safe methods for them are.Basically, the final bosses of this game expect you to play well. It will not take sloppy play as an acceptable answer.The music is kind of whatever. It has its great tracks like Lagoon City act 2, but also has its forgettable/bad tracks like Sky Temple. The ost is what it is. They really need to keep Jun away from classic osts. Just give them to someone else at this point.TL;DR: Boring/mediocre stage bosses but great ending bosses. Great stages for the most part, held back by trying to make them more difficult for a certain repeat playthrough. Okay music, but nothing outstanding with a few hits.Grab on sale, probably not full price. If one enjoys classic sonic then this will fill the classic-sized hole in their heart that mania tried to fill but ran out of bandages halfway through the operation.This game is the other half of what mania tried to be, basically.
