_childDocuments_.review: The Red Flag went up when I was asked to make an Epic AccountThat Red Flag started to violently twist in the wind when the How To Play/Controls option just displayed a QR codeThe Disaster Alarm Sounded when I realized there was no option for dedicated Online  Co opI bought this mostly to play through the main game with friends.  All the marketing and trailers seemed to show the game was built for this. As it turned out, the only way to do so was through Remote Play.  This meant that everyone would need to share the same screen. In a game built for moving fast and taking multiple routes through a stage, this choice was... suboptimal. It left us fighting for control of the camera, and the game never seemed to be consistent about who the camera would follow and who would be forced to respawn once off screen. This is to say nothing of how during Remote Play, there were input delays of almost a full second, when the game was in between crashes and booting players from the session.The single player mode was... fine. Not $60 fine, but fine.Eventually asked for a refund. I wanted a seamless co op experience, but that wasn't what I got. That's okay, this game just wasn't for me.I'm not angryI'm just disappointed

_childDocuments_.review: This game leaves me so conflicted.  On one hand, I generally like the levels and their designs, the emerald powers are a solid way to give this game identity and shake up the classic Sonic formula, and it generally feels nice to play as a result.  The music (barring some Sonic 4-sounding tracks) is generally enjoyable, and had the game just stuck with the same kind of boss design as the previous games, I'd be willing to recommend it.But oh my god, the bosses just absolutely tank the game for me.  They're too damn long and that length comes from simply waiting.  I get they had to balance them around multiplayer, but wouldn't the better move be to increase their health accordingly?The second story (which I will not spoil for the sake of review) is also inundated with terrible level design packed with spikes and horrible enemy placement, honestly even worse than Sonic 2 in that regard it's awful, and the last two bosses in this game (both the second story final boss and the final story final boss) genuinely left me frustrated and enraged in a way I haven't experienced in a game in a long time, spending hours and hours on these fights that just won't end or relent with the unnecessary difficulty that's all ultimately in service of a decent Sonic game at best, when I could replay any of the other classic games and be done with them in the time it took for me to beat either of the last two bosses.Don't buy this game at 60 dollars.  Wait for a sale, and even then I can't even recommend it at that.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixed bag. I'm enjoying the return to classic platforming and I think they do that well, with some unique mechanics, and some ripped from Sonic Mania. The physics are supposed to be 1:1 to Sonic Mania, but I don't buy it. There are some things that seem off;  the spindash feels really quite slow, and I find the drop-dash more effective?  I just found out if you have your framerate uncapped or above 60 fps, it'll break the spin-dash. I changed the settings and capped it to 60 fps and it works as intended. Strange bug. The graphics look OK. I would honestly prefer pixel graphics, but this is good enough. I think comparing this games graphics with other platformers coming out this year, you can clearly see how behind the curve they are. I find the lighting on the character models quite distracting. The graphics and level themes are quite nice. Level design feels pretty good. I'd compare this with Sonic CD but with the mechanic of having power-ups from the chaos emeralds, it makes exploring a quite fun with the vertical level design. I really enjoyed the  acts. Some really nice game mechanics to match the level themes. The special stages are awful and quite infuriating - felt on some occasions that there I didn't have any control and that it's purely based on luck. I dislike how you can't attempt to re-try them, I had to reload the level and try again a couple of times. The music is quite poor - I was expecting some bangers but most of them are quite forgettable which is a real shame. I think they should've just got Tee Lopes to compose most of the tracks and forget about Jun Senoue. I don't know why they keep asking for him to compose music for games when his music has been criticised and disliked in previous games. I find also the music mixing is odd. In some stages the BGM is quite loud, and the SF are louder. I tried to go to settings and mess around by turning up the BGM (so I could listen to it a bit better) but it ended up turning up the SF which was strange. I like the themes for the chaos emerald power-ups, but they sometimes get a bit repetitive; I hate how it cuts the background music and restarts the track when its done. I've found myself avoiding using them so I can listen to the full tracks. I tried multiplayer with my other half, it sucked and was a real disappointment. The game can't seem to decide who's the leader or not on most sections, making for some awkward moments where you have to respawn even though you where in-front. I couldn't care less for the battle mode.Overall, the game is not better than Sonic Mania, but is serviceable. It's not terrible, but it's incredibly safe and sadly the bare minimum of what we should expect. Take a look at how Super Mario Wonder and then come back to this. Sonic used to be the platforming rival to the Mario. How far Sonic has fallen. Overall, don't pay for full price. Pick this one up when it goes on sale. Not sure what SEGA was smoking thinking that the price for this game was fair.

_childDocuments_.review: A game with amazing level design that is held back by absolutely horrible boss design in almost every zone. The bosses hold this back immensely, either being too difficult for no good reason, far too long, or as is very often in the endgame, both. The act of running through levels is immensely fun, until you reach the end of the act and realize that it's time to fight something for multiple minutes.  The new character of 'Trip' is underutilized in the main story, though the interactions she does have are very pleasant. All in all, I recommend the main story as it still gives a large amount of fun, but the final bosses should really, /really/ be made easier in order to be more welcoming for the child audience and novice gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, under no circumstances should anyone ever pay full price for this game. £55 is an utterly deranged price point.As for the actual game, it's kinda ok. The physics are better than Sonic 4 or the 2D sections of Sonic Forces, but not by a huge amount. I would still regularly be confused about suddenly losing almost all my speed after trying to spin dash up a ramp, or not really gaining any speed after falling into curved ground. There's also far too much stuff that's basically on-rails, and honestly I don't really like the drop dash. It trivialises gaining speed far too much, and while I can just not use it, they should probably just... Not add things that remove or ruin the fun part of the game?Overall it feels very amateurish. Visually it looks far worse than the 2D levels of Sonic Generations, which came out 12 years ago. The music is mostly awful, and I'm not even one of those people that hates the Sonic 1 snare, in fact I quite like it, it's one of the best bits of the Sonic 1 boss music for example. The music in this game is just not well written, and at this point there's no actual reason to not be using much better samples.Honestly after Sonic Mania this game feels like a pretty cynical attempt to cheaply cash in on nostalgia, rather than a game made by people who actually love and respect the series. If you've not played all the classic Sonic games, definitely play those first. If you've not played Sonic Mania, it's infinitely better and almost a quarter of the price. If you've played every 2D Sonic game and are absolutely desperate for more, it's maybe worth it once it's 50% off, but I wouldn't get your hopes up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really bad game. Like, seriously, this makes Sonic Lost World look like a blast. The gameplay is horrendous. The game tends to punish you for going too fast, and there are plenty of spots that you will get hit out of pure luck, meaning there is no way to know if you will take damage or die until it is too late. The studio that developed this game seems to have no clue on good level design practices. In addition, the spin dash makes you go very slow, so if you are using a character that doesn't have the drop dash, have fun turning back around to gain momentum. Oh, and the bosses take an eternity to beat because you can only hit them once every 30 seconds. It feels like every other Sonic game that comes out turns out to be abysmal at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: (SPOILER WARNING)The game for the First story is an 8/10, its very solid and I like the new chaos emerald powers and levels. Everything seems very fine, boss fights are pretty easy because of the powers, but some require you to actually think. The music is a little weird, by weird I mean inconsistent, we go from all these cool instruments and cool songs, then we go straight into genesis sounding music. Which is very confusing. For instance the Title screen if very jump and sounds good, then you press start game and suddenly its like youre playing sonic 4...This doesnt mean music is bad, music is great its just inconsistent. Now Trips story is where this game gets very good. The issue of bosses and stages being too easy, are instantly gone when playing Trips story. Levels are remixed and are harder to complete. Boss's are much harder and take a lot longer to beat, the issue of boss's being easy because of chaos emerald powers are taken away. You actually need these powers to stand a chance against some of these boss's otherwise its just very hard. Im sure someone who is very skilled can do it but its very hard. Trips story is basically the first story but juts harder. The final boss's of this game...they made me lose my mind. When making to the final boss on the first story, it took me about 3 hours to beat it, no youtube guide or anything just learning from trial and error. its beatable, just very hard.Trips story final boss is where I really lost it though. Its similar to the first story final boss, except the arena is remixed, and instead of fighting eggman you fight Fang. And this final boss battle makes it seem like Fang really hates you and hes not doing it for the money anymore. The boss is A LOT harder, i took me about 4-5 hours to beat. and thats using a guide. beating it is satisfying as hell. now the "last story" is just the True final boss, where you play as super sonic and fight a dragon. The fight is pretty hard, but its like any other super sonic final boss just collect rings and attack when you can. Its not hard, but its not easy either. Its fun to learn and play.thats basically the whole game summed up. My final rating for the full game is a 9/10, I do think $60 is a bit pricey, so maybe wait for when its on sale, but if youre desperate to play and it seems funs then sure spend $60.

_childDocuments_.review: I like to think of myself as someone who tries to be positive about the sonic series overall, no matter the style of game, whether it's Classic 2D, Adventure Era, Advance 2D, Rush 2D, Boost Era, whatever it is, i like to try and find the positives in it, and the positives for superstars is that some of the music is good, trip is cute as heck and probably the best thing to come from this game, and some of the levels are pretty greatSadly, something in this game, drags it so low, that i can't even justify telling someone to try it, and that's pretty much every single boss in the game, the later bosses especially, can last upwards of 6 minutes, and most of that unlike the classic games where you make your own opportunities to attack, and then the speed comes from your own skill at it, there is no speed to these bosses, the game decidess when you are allowed to do damage and SOMETIMES those are in situations where you are already dodging their previous attack and cannot capitalise on this, leading to the bossfight lasting an extra 3-4 minutes depending on how often this happens. the worst offender of this was the super sonic bossfight at the end, where the rings you get are pretty much all RNG dependant, and you'll find yourself dying not to anything like the bosses patterns being difficult, but just due to the fact the boss stands there doing nothing for 20 seconds, making you lose 20 rings in the processs, but also in a situation where you can't hit it, this is going to kill you in MANY situations, and is just not a good design, whoever designed these fights around waiting, really should re-evaluate what they think makes a fun sonic boss fight and maybe research some of the older games or even some from the adventure or boost era. Waiting, especially in a game series where historically you are on the offensive, just isn't fun, especially when ring drain is a mechanic in probably the worst offender of these.3/10 trip and the early game levels carry

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this game knowing it was meant to be a successor to Sonic Mania. A game with great level design, great music, and a really good overall charm that I've missed from sonic games of the past. Needless to say, this game did not meet my expectations. I was mostly excited for this game's music because of Tee.     Don't get me wrong, Tee Lopes can and will never make a bad music track, no matter what game he composes for. It's always an absolute blast and I'm happy to say he delivers in this game as well... however, as soon as I got to that factory themed level, my already pretty low view of this game got lowered, from the start I noticed there was a required Epic Games account necessity, Denuvo DRM once again tanking game's performance, and overall pretty bad level design, such as poor direction () cheam enemy locations, underwhelming boss fights, and sluggish movement... it seems Senoue has tainted this game's soundtrack with the grating Sonic 4 "genesis" soundfont. Tee Lopes should have went all in on the soundtrack, the music would have been in perfect hands.     When I first installed the game, I got my friends to play with me because of the marketing that this was a game meant to be played with friends. Hoo boy... NEVER play the multiplayer in this game. It's laughable how abysmal the multiplayer is. Tail's ability to fly practically kills every other player, I'm surprised any of the multiplayer has passed QC, There's a shared camera (that isn't implemented well for multiplayer in the slightest). Even when you get those breaks from the spastic camera, you're frequently thrust into special stages and bonus stages, to the point where it feels more akin to a Warioware game than the Sonic game I was hoping to play with my buddies.     SEGA should learn from Mania and let their fans make their games. Since apparently whenever a 2D Sonic game is made in-house it always falls short of everyone's expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic once again returns and builds upon his earliest installments with a brand new adventure through the Northstar Islands.I love how the game is styled. The graphics look great as per usual. The characters are animated well. I love the way the Chaos Emeralds were implemented into the gameplay. Instead of having to collect all seven to become virtually invincible, you can use one of the seven emeralds, each with unique traits. The Slow power makes me think of Chaos Control, which it basically is.I also appreciate the choice to add Amy's modern outfit as DLC, which I may say is very cute. Those comic book skins look interesting, however I wasn't able to get them before they were taken down.The soundtrack can vary, but it hits most of the time for me. The new Shadow costume is pretty funny.At the time of writing the review, I had just beaten the main story and hadn't played  There is a big issue with boss fights in this game. They seem to drag on without being too engaging,  They are also sometimes frustrating and unfair, Let's see here.Sonic Superstars earns a(n): for...its style, gameplay, and ideas. It is weighed down by its long and sometimes unfair boss fights, its steep price for its shorter length, and occasional unfair level design.I originally gave this game an A, but after playing through Trip's story, I decided to bump it down to C due to the downsides I see.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars is a wonderful return to the franchise's roots, evolving and iterating off of traditions with unique stages with unique gimmicks, rather than primarily repurposing preexisting stages like how Mania and Generations did it. Fang's long-awaited return is welcomed, and new villain Trip is simply adorable. Each of the four playable characters have a unique ability that makes swapping out between stages worthwhile.So why am I giving such a wonderful game a negative review? Because Sega has once again betrayed fans' trust with anti-consumer practices. Denuvo DRM causes framerate issues on Steam Deck while it loads level chunks, and that's only if you can get even that far, because the game relies on Epic Games Services for online cross-platform play. This latter fact wouldn't be too big of an issue, except that the game installs Epic launcher without your consent, and if you wish to decline, you are *completely* locked out of online play, and the prompt will obscure your game (and is difficult to navigate on Steam Deck) every. single. time you launch the game. This was not a major issue for me personally, as I already have my Epic account linked with Steam, but many people are understandable opposed to Epic Games as a company. And even if you do decline to sign in, you're still forced to play the game with the Epic overlay running in the background unless you open task manager to forcequit the program.In summary: great game, terrible DRM. Unless you're a diehard fan of the franchise like myself, wait for Sega to at least remove Denuvo (should only take a few months if Frontiers is any indication) or wait for a price drop; unfortunately, I don't think much can be done about the EGS integration unless they add an option to reconsider your decline in the multiplayer options or something.

_childDocuments_.review: It says a lot about a game and it's level design when it's difficulty often lies on how many cheap sucker shots it can throw at a player without them being able to see it coming or do anything about it, rather than actually engaging with the player by challenging them with situations that genuinely test their cunning wits and skilful abilities. This in turn leads to a lacklustre of game-play that once it's novelty wears off, the only feeling one might have aside from the usual boredom when playing, is that of annoyance and/or frustration. RIP Replay value.The acceleration speed from a stationary position or when switching direction has such a slow start that it feels like you have to wade through quicksand before you can even start to get moving. This can often make any incoming danger that may be heading your way tough or even inescapable at some moments. Then there's the length of time that the boss fights take, especially nearing to the end of the game. They have many different stages to them and when you put them all together they become so very bloated and tedious. Also there's no checkpoint so if you screw up and die, you have start over from the very beginning again and because of that it can become very old very fast.As well as that, I just get the impression at times that some aspects of this game were rushed in development. The background details feel like they are are missing something, the lighting feels off on some stages, the music is uninspiring and there are a few bugs still left to be ironed out here and there.Also the Epic Games scandal that they snuck in there was a bit of an unwelcome surprise too. Yet another sucker punch we didn't see coming.On the better side of things though, it's the first sonic game that you can play alongside 4 other players with and that does look fun, though I haven't tried it just yet. Some of the artwork regarding cut scenes and model animations are really well done. The characters and story are pretty good too, and the new character makes a very welcomed addition to the crew.Overall though it's about a 5 out of 10, let down by a few of those fatal flaws I mentioned earlier.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars is a really great 2D platformer, and most complaints from other players is actually just skill issue. If you get frustrated when playing Sonic Advance then this game is probably not for you. The game plays like a classic game and the layouts of the stages feel inspired by the classics, but the hazard placement is similar to the first Advance game. However, bosses are actually just as pathetic as in the classic trilogy if you utilize the emerald powers. BTW, I do not think people not enjoying the game because they're bad at this game to be a flaw on their part. Platformers as a genre have failed to provide substantial difficulty options, and through that there has not been a standard difficulty to expect from a platformer. Mario has done well by making more difficult challenges optional, but rewarding for the player. However, Sonic has not found a solution still. Slowing the game down as punishment for poor performance only makes the game boring and/or frustrating for unskilled players.However, this is not a multiplayer or co-op game. You'll get a better experience of co-op from playing Knuckles' Chaotix because Sonic Superstars has not done anything to improve upon the little brother experience of player 2 in the classic trilogy.It is also unfortunate that the multiplayer competitive mode is so lackluster because the robot customization is actually incredible. The game is stringent on when it rewards players tokens to spend on parts for customization, but generally after playing through the main story as Sonic, Tails, Knuckles, and Amy you should have enough parts to fully customize at least one robot to your liking: potentially two if you're going out of your way for the tokens. Unfortunately, your robot can only be used in the lackluster competitive mode. Which means you will never use them. The robot does show up twice in the main story, but I do not think the average player would find that satisfying reason to customize their robot.The soundtrack is also hit & miss. Some really amazing tracks, and some tracks that are so bad one of the first mods of this game was to replace them.The story is not coherent. It exists, I guess, but it is impossible to follow on a first playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I was worried about getting this game because of how polarized it seemed people were about it. I bought the steam version so that if I didn't like it I could refund it.  I did not so and am almost 4 hours into the game so I guess that means I liked it enough to keep it. I was never expecting a contender for Super Mario Wonder but I am failing to see the "New Super Mario Bros" of Sonic. I would play this over any New Super Mario Bros game any day.  This to me was more like the Mega Man 11 of Sonic. I liked what I was playing but I could definitely tell you this is no where close to my favorite 2D Sonic game. It ranks above Sonic CD and it is miles better than anything that Sonic 4 ep 1 & 2 had to offer. Sonic and co control exactly how I want them to in the classic format, the physics felt on point which is weird since this game has a 3d aesthetic, so you would expect it to control like in Generations or *shudders* Forces.The music is music.  When Tee Lopes stuff came on, it was great, Jun's stuff came on, it was hit or miss for me. The boss music was definitely a far cry from boss music of old. Press Factory definitely sounds like it has that "Genesis twang" but the funny thing about the genesis Sonic music music, they didn't have that twang except for Spinball.The boss fights, these were what I was seeing a lot of complaints about and I gotta be honest.  With the exception of one or two, I had fun with these.  I like just bopping Eggman 8 times in a row before touching the ground as much as the next guy but I also like it when a boss fight makes me...   actually fight the boss.  And these bosses don't take full 8 hits to beat other.  Mario and Donkey Kong bosses have been doing this shtick for years plus if you want actual boss fights that drag on forever, fight Chaos 4 or Iblis Worm.Level design was hit or miss for me, more hit than miss but ♥♥♥♥ Golden City act 2.  I was seeing people compare the levels in this game to Sonic CD and Sonic 1 but I would take just about any level in here over what those had to offer.The multiplayer, I will be honest, I played solo  all the way but I have played New Super Mario Bros, Rayman Origins & Legends, Donkey Kong Country Returns and Tropical Freeze, Kirby Super Star allies, etc, and when I saw that multiplayer, which was one of the major selling points on the box granted, was one of the weaker parts of the game, I was like "Yeah that sounds about right."   I am just glad that the game was not at all like Kirby Star Allies where the levels were so streamlined and empty to accommodate for the multiplayer gimmick. I guess my major complaint is this game definitely feels pricey for what it is.  $30-40 seems better fitted for the production values and the length of the game here.Edit: I forgot about the chaos powers...  They aight. There's only like a couple that I go out of my way to use but I don't find that they really add or subtract from the overall experience.TLDR: I enjoyed this game though it is not gonna be in my top 10 Sonic games, the negatives I have seen felt blown way out of proportion, if you already enjoy Sonic, I think you will still enjoy this title. I recommend waiting for a price drop or a sale. I don't give games number ratings because number ratings are stupid.Update: At the time of my original review, I was only done with the main story of the game.  It wasn't until the later half of Trip's story where all the criticisms about the bosses clicked in.  Namely Trip's final boss and the Super Sonic final boss are the lowest of the low I have seen in terms of Sonic boss fights I have seen.  Still leaving it as a recommended because I do think the main story is a perfectly fine 2D Sonic experience(Single player) but do beware of how long and tedious the final 2 bosses of the game are.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic SuperstarsThe level-design is good. The levels aren't as open as in Sonic CD, but they have multiple paths to encourage exploration, which usually leads to a warp ring or some other collectible items. The pacing of each level was good for a Sonic game.The playable characters all felt accurate in terms of physics and gameplay. Sonic, Tails, and Knuckles all play the same way as they do in Mania. Amy can do a double jump, and her hammer extends her attack range when she's jumping. Unlike in the Genesis games, the characters can be swapped at any time between levels on the level-select map without losing any progress.The Emerald Powers are a good way to make the gameplay unique. Each Chaos Emerald gives a new power, which can change how the players strategize as they move through levels or fight bosses. I used the Red Emerald Power the most often, since it's a dash-move that can be used for both combat, exploration, and helping with some harder platforming sections. Other powers are borderline useless, like the Cyan Power, which can only be used in like 2 of the 12 zones.The bosses were alright. Most of the boss fights are just waiting around until it becomes possible to attack it. When attacking the bosses, they have too many invincibility frames, so they can only be hit once per cycle. Some of the later bosses have attacks that immediately kill the player regardless of how many rings they had.There aren't very many collectibles in the game. Exploring the levels can warp rings or medals. The warp rings are used to access the Chaos Emerald Special Stages, just like in Sonic 3 and Sonic Mania. Medals are used to buy robot parts for the multiplayer mode. There are also fruits that can be collected, which are used to access bonus stages to earn more medals. Each level also has a hidden Golden Badnik that drops medals when it's defeated, and there's an achievement for finding all of them. These are the only collectible items in the game.Overall, if you like the 2D Sonic Games, then I'd recommend getting Sonic Superstars.

_childDocuments_.review: If your a fan of classic sonic, you definitely will like this game. I tend to explain each point sometimes so bare with me! I have played all of the classic sonic games and if your a fan of those games, I do recommend this game despite its flaws.The Pros:+ It has the same momentum as the classics+ Controls feel great and very responsive. Feels exactly like the classic games and isn't as restrictive+ Rewards you for knowing the map since...+ Speed is Earned and not given, you need to know the map and route and keep up momentum instead of free boosters.+ Emerald powers lets you explore every route and experiment a lot. Some are situational but still are fun in their own right!+ Progression is great and it has a slightly better and improved saving system than Sonic 3 & Knuckles+ The game utilized its new engine and 3D background to give it a nice twist. You can find more secrets and paths on the background that adds a new layer to a lot of zones.The Ok:o The Music is a mix bag due to more than 1 composer. You can tell the quality of the music goes all over the placeo The difficulty is harder than most classic sonic games, especially at the bosses. I personally like it but I know a some wouldn'to The Co-op is different. Whoever is in the lead will have the camera and everyone either has to catch up or be forced to teleport. This is great if you have a little cousin who isn't so great and needs to help to catch up but if both players know what they are doing, it can be rather annoying but its hard to make co-op work in a fast plat formero The Boss battles can be a hit or miss. Some bosses are great and fun and rewarding while others feel cheap with instant kill attacks, which feels like artificial difficulty.The Cons:- The bosses last a rather excessive amount of time. Your unable rewarded for risking yourself to hit the boss multiple times or during risky moments most of the time because the game doesn't let you get consecutive hits. Due to this, some bosses last around 7-10 minutes, which is rather odd since it takes around 5 minutes to beat a a level and less once you learn the levels. Once you start fighting "that boss" and die a lot, it starts to feel like a chore to repeat a boss battle.- The new multiplayer game mode is bare bones and wants you to grind excessively just to change your look. There are also barley any players playing this mode so you either get 2-3 real players and have the rest be bots or just have bots. Another issue I notice is if someone leaves early, everyone is booted and no one is rewarded.- The debug menu is bare bones and lacks option. Its just a level select and a music player. Your unable to place enemies or entities around the map, play player exclusive levels or bosses with different characters and with all the bosses this game has, A simple boss rush would had been a nice touch, even if some hate the bosses.- There is a special mode in the game but it forced only 1 player to play the game. So if you finished the game with a buddy, you literally have to either force him to watch you play or take turns with the controller rather than enjoy it together. Really is a poor game decision.- For a 60$ game, its underwhelming for its price tag. It only lasts 8-10 hours to beat the game (twice) and do everything the game offers.

_childDocuments_.review: Is the constant pandering to die-hard 90s Sonic fans cute? Yes. Is Sonic Superstars a worthwhile game? No. People describing it as "Sonic the Hedgehog 4: Episode 3" aren't far from the mark, but at least Sonic 4 Episode 2 had some modicum of ambition. This is the epitome of a franchise treading water, and the visuals are awful. I haven't seen anti-aliasing this bad in years, and some of the bloom effects are straight out of 2008.We've been treated to two truly remarkable Sonic games in the last six years and the best Sega could come up with for 2023 is... this? Really? It's a travesty that Superstars seems to have somehow garnered better critical reviews than Sonic Frontiers, despite the latter being in a completely different league. I find the idea that this is a $60 game utterly baffling. I got Sonic Superstars for 44% off with the Humble Choice subscriber discount, and I'm not sure it was even worth the $33. It's infuriating that we got this instead of Sonic Mania 2 solely due to Sonic Team's arrogant narcissism.I'm also displeased by Sega's anti-consumer decision to obfuscate that the game was primarily developed by Arzest, creators of Balan Wonderworld (not to mention the insipid Yoshi's New Island). Steam natively supports listing multiple developers, there is nothing stopping them from listing "Arzest, Sonic Team" instead of Sega. They just don't want you to know that you're buying into one of Japan's worst support studios.For 90s Sonic fans its worth $20, but if you're just looking for a high quality 2D platformer - look elsewhere. The quality differential between this and Mario Wonder is embarrassing.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright it is time to revise my original review from the highly negative review that I posted when I was roughly 30 minutes in. So I will address the elephant in the room. The reality is that I should have paid closer attention and looked at news and information of the game before I bought it for both me and my partner, this was a fault on me and I will accept that. Second this is that the local co-op is doable, just not in the way that I intended. I have one keyboard & mouse, and one controller that I use for games that require local coop, what I did not know is that K&M is always classified as player one, but it will also identify the first controller as player one too. Me and my boyfriend were able to play through remote play and have my roommates join via local play, but we required 4 controllers for all of us to join when only 3 of us would realistically use the controllers. So you would need at least 2 controllers if you plan to play the game with a friend. So a correction from my original statement "don't buy if you want to play with other people," turns out it is possible, you just need several controllers. In the end I did end up refunding my boyfriend's copy of the game since it was not even needed for us to play together.So now this runs into one of my first complaints of the game: The refusal to implement an online coop mode. I do see potential in a multiplayer sonic game of this type working, since even in coop mode through remote play it worked decently. The only complaint is not quite always being able to keep up with others due to frame drops on the remote play stream, which could be remedied with online support. I know their excuse was latency issues, and that points to my next issue with the game.Latency, this is an issue that is prominent in any online game. Now as a mostly offline game, one would think that this would never be an issue. However, when playing alone and in the other story modes, it seems that issues with delayed reactions, oddly sluggish or unresponsive movements, and downright incorrect calculations of hit boxes points to at least latency like issues. With these issues, some bosses later on become RNG of rather of not you can beat them. Not because you haven't learned the pattern, but because there is a chance that game play will turn temporarily inconsistent. OG sonic bosses were always pretty hard, but when you get the pattern down and learn how to beat them you get that feeling of YEEESSSSS. Though with the underlying issues like these, it makes the bosses of this game make me feel like "Freaking finally"Now you may be wondering why I could possibly recommend this game despite my complaining, well it has a lot of silver linings. To start off, what me and my partner managed to salvage out by setting up coop through remote play ended up being a very good experience once we figured out how we needed to set up. The stages were not too difficult, but I personally could say that they are not too easy either. The perception of difficulty could be obscured by the fact that there is no limited life system in this game, and personally I like that a lot. When the "latency" issues didn't impact performance, the bosses felt very fun to fight and I loved learning about the mysterious new characters while discover old forgotten characters that had always been my favorites. I never thought I would see an official sonic game with Metal Knuckles, Tails Doll, and Mecha Sonic all in the same place. I felt very giddy about seeing these old characters get some spotlight once again.In relation to the bots though, I think there is much to be improved with the online battle mode. Considering the game has not been out for even a month, and absolutely no body plays this mode shows that there is little incentive to. I think drastically increasing medal rewards could be a way to fix this issue, since playing with bots is boring and yields no medals to begin with. On the topic of bots, they seem to have two sides. They are rather pin perfect with every movement on stages to the point it is extremely hard to get close to them, or their path-finding bugs out and they just stare at a wall or off themselves. Eitherway, it does not seem intuitive and and oversight on sonic team. Overall, I am very glad I got the game. It was a pretty fun experience, and kinda brought me back to a place I was in when I used to play the old sonic games in the Sega mega collection gamecube game. I hope that we will continue to get more games that play into the classic sonic characters and their backstories. I would definitely like to see more of Tails Doll and the Metal villains take a more important role especially.

_childDocuments_.review: As of November 9, 2023, the forced EOS installation and Epic Games login requirements have been completely removed. So I'm redoing this review now. Even with that aside, I can't recommend this game,  at full price. Who at Sega thought charging AAA prices for this was a good idea, especially when it's launching the same week as a far superior 2D platformer?The main campaaign is... fine, I guess? It's still one of the weaker Classic games, but it can be fun enough. The characters don't exactly control like the originals, but it's close enough that I can look past it. The level design is actually pretty fun for the first half of the game. But the second half starts to become a slog with boring/annoying gimmicks, long level lengths, cheap traps that you have no way of avoiding, and overly long boss fights.And then there's the unlockable second campaign, where the devs take all the things that are already bad about this game and make them  Cap that off with one of the worst, most poorly designed boss fights in platformer history, and you've got yourself a recipe for pain. This wouldn't be as much of an issue if it was optional, but for some god-forsaken reason, you're required to complete it in order to unlock the Super Sonic boss fight. Because everybody loved that decision in Sonic Heroes 20 years ago... But you wouldn't be missing much anyway because said fight itself, like most of the bosses in this game, is pretty terrible and comes completely out of nowhere.Also, bugs. Lots of bugs. I've clipped through the map numerous times, had issues climbing walls that should otherwise work, and the spin dash doesn't work properly at frame rates above 60fps. Further proof that Sega hasn't learned a thing from previous Sonic games and continues to pull the same practices that nearly killed the franchise over a decade ago.This game pulled back most of my optimism that was gained with Frontiers. I'd say it's worth a go if you can get it around $30 or less and only care about a single playthrough, but at that price, Mania and even Origins are better purchases. This is not the 2D Sonic game that we deserve. Though I probably should've expected that from the team that brought us such classics as Yoshi's New Island, Hey! Pikmin, and Balan Wonderworld...P.S. Never let Jun Senoue near a classic Sonic game ever again.

_childDocuments_.review: I was extremely excited for this game when it was announced, as I've been a huge sonic fan for most of my life. I'm very sorry to say that I've found this game immensely disappointing, and just a plain bad experience. At the time of writing this, I've done two full playthroughs, first one in singleplayer and all emeralds, and the second one in 4 player multiplayer with all emeralds, beginning to end. The game starts out very promising, with a very solid first couple zones. The bosses are a lot more annoying in this game than previous classic sonic entries due to the abundance of waiting you have to do before you hit them, but are otherwise inoffensive. Things begin to nosedive around the game's midpoint. Level design begins to resemble that of Sonic Advance's lategame levels (not very good), and the bosses become straight up terrible. Bosses in classic sonic games were never really all that good, but at the very least you could beat them really quickly. These bosses involve lots of waiting and trial and error. The final boss is especially egregious with this, and in my opinion is one of the worst bosses classic sonic has to offer. I'm not really sure who played these bosses and thought it was okay to ship the game with how unfun they are. They bring down the entirety of the game for me, and I know I'm not the only one who shares that sentiment. In general, it really feels like this game lacks quality control.Speaking of lack of quality control, the game's multiplayer. In almost every single act of the game when my friends and I played multiplayer, we encountered some sort of bug or glitch that got in the way of our enjoyment (mostly. with how messed up it was, we did at least get a lot of good laughs from how poorly this game kept itself together in multiplayer). Despite the fact that this game was advertised with a heavy coop focus, it doesn't really feel like the game was designed for multiplayer at a certain point. In the game's defense, I don't think it's really possible to make a cooperative multiplayer game out of classic sonic that holds up well, but that just means they shouldn't have attempted it to begin with. Players are constantly being despawned and having to respawn (or in some cases due to a glitch we frequently encountered, ♥♥♥♥ outta luck altogether and unable to respawn for seemingly no reason). Even though my friends and I had fun with the coop, it was because of external reasons. The design itself does not lend itself well to multiplayer at all and is just fairly miserable.The game does have some positives, I find trip to be a cute character, and  . The control feels pretty good too, not 1-to-1 with mania or the classics, but pretty close! I also found some of the music pretty enjoyable. I usually find sonic soundtracks in their entirety enjoyable, so it's a little disappointing that isn't the case this time around, but there are standout tracks still!I really wanted to love this game, but it just did not stick the landing unfortunately. It face planted, and it face planted  At best, get this when it's on sale for really cheap, it's not worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Superstars has a lot of good ideas, and often some pretty damn good execution, but sometimes (for example Egg Fortress Act 2) the ideas don't feel like they were fully envisioned, and in Gold Capital's case, the level felt like it had way too many ideas at once that they couldn't give to their own levels. The level design (with exception for Gold Capital Zone) felt very solid overall, giving equal senses of speed, platforming, and exploration at a very good pace.The final boss is a huge letdown, the first phase is a huge slog, and the second phase feels way too similar to the final boss of Sonic 3 and Knuckles, or Metal Sonic Kai in Sonic Mania. Sometimes there are throwbacks (the Hydro City motif in the water level's music, the Sonic 2 Game Gear bubble gimmick in that same zone, the Death Egg Robot) that feel like they would've hit much harder if it hadn't been for Mania doing the same exact thingsThe soundtrack, while perfectly fine and very enjoyable overall, has a large issue with consistency. Some tracks use real instruments that give a vibe of what a SEGA Saturn Sonic game would've had music like, but other tracks take the Sonic 4/Sonic Forces Classic Sonic music route and try to use the sound of the Genesis. Granted, these tracks do it much better than either of those games do, but it still makes the overall OST feel very unsteadyOverall it feels like a 7/10 Wii U game, which is NOT necessarily bad, but it's nothing absolutely spectacular. Not sure on the $60 price tag, though, but at a discount or after a price drop (...hopefully) it'd likely be more reasonable.EDIT: After having played Trip's Story (which features harder levels...which boils down to enemy spam and spike spam, and a different final boss) and the true final boss, I can definitely say...Yeah, they suck, lol. Overall I still like the game a lot but these parts absolutely drag on the experience.

I'm not surprised the game has Denuvo, I wholeheartedly expected it to (though, admittedly, I shouldn't!), but once again, loopholing Steam's ToS that requires publishers to dictate that their game has Denuvo before launch and waiting  should be unanimously reprimanded.It is sad and aggravating how SEGA lightfootingly treats their PC consumer base. It was upsetting that Sonic Colors Ultimate had a period of Epic exclusivity, but their handling of Sonic Superstars feels not just anti-consumer but borderline evasive of Steam's ToS. _childDocuments_.review: This is my third revision for this review. It has taken a lot of soul searching on my part to make any kind of decision, but here's what I think, both good and bad.First, you're probably going to have a lot of fun on your first play-through. The levels are fun, and have an emphasis on exploration. I personally love taking in the colorful and well designed sight as Tails, making exploration a whimsical walk in the park.The gameplay, however, is a little slower than the typical classic-style Sonic fare. It seems just a notch below the speed one would expect from a Sonic game that draws so much influence from the classic titles.The bonus stages are a welcome treat, and obtaining the chaos emeralds is an enjoyable experience. It's just challenging and rewarding enough to have a player commit to the task.The bosses are a mixed bag. There are some very inventive mechanics involved with some of these battles, but just be aware that the good-old bouncing-on-them-'til-they-die trick won't work in this outing. Additionally, some of the boss battles seem to linger longer than necessary, especially during Trip's Story.You will get hit. A lot. There are times when the level design pulls you along by the nose, leaving you vulnerable to attack.The multiplayer mechanic is flawed - the camera is fickle in its decision as to whom it will follow, making it difficult to control your character at times.The music and sound design are top notch!The game's price point is entirely too high. It's worth the investment if you can grab it during a sale, but at it's sticker price of $60 there's just not enough to justify taking the plunge.All-in-all, it's a fine Sonic game. Maybe one of the most fun and enjoyable Sonic games in years! It is, however, flawed. Still, I recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, and it does start out pretty okay. The first couple of zones are decent enough, moderately pacey and the sort of romp one would expect from a 2d Sonic game.However, it's pretty much downhill from there. There's one overtly pinball stage and a second that's trying to hide the fact that it is one. They're always terrible, so having to endure the annoying bouncing around the bumpers uncontrollably twice is pretty bad. I'll never understand Sonic Team's obsession with these kinds of Zones. Christian Whitehead and Headcannon did get it right in Mania's Studiopolis Zone, but alas, their fingerprints are nowhere to be seen in this game.The emerald powers are pretty much lacklustre. One of them is good for skipping terrible platforming sections and another is good for dealing damage during boss fights when you can't be bothered to wait for the over-long attack cycle to end. The other two I found were completely pointless. I don't know about the reaming three because I couldn't be bothered to endure finding the special stages in the correct zones to get them. Trip's campaign is the same as the main campaign, save for a couple of additional badniks that simply serve to make everything more annoying. The boss battles are also ramped up a bit, making already tedious encounters largely unbearable. (Every bad thing anyone has said about the boss battles is correct. They're excruciatingly bad and all over long).The game does look very nice, but it's all style over substance here. Give me a worse looking game that has way better level design and fewer silly gimmicks.I paid over £20 for this game, hoping it was was worth the money; only a fool would think that the full £50+ price tag could be. But alas, I was wrong. If you absolutely must buy this game, wait for ages for it to get deeply discounted to about £10.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10, 8/10 BARE MINIMUM.There is now better way to say it; this game just knocked it out of the park with what it means to be a 2D Sonic game.This game hits every mark on the head in terms of what fans wanted from a new 2D entry after Sonic Mania. It has over 10 new, 100% original zones, filled to the bursting point with all new mechanics and fun ideas. The characters and areas all have super pleasing colors and aesthetics, and truly captivate you with how even though it's not pushing the graphics to their limit, the game is stylized and visually euphoric (exactly like Zelda: Link's Awakening HD).The controls are PHENOMENAL, since it is literally Mania's code just copy pasted, which is 100% fine, because why fix what isn't broke. This game no only delivers on what people loved about Mania, but dashes forward with new ideas and beautiful looking levels. Who would've thought an entire level about GRINDING, the thing that games like Lost World and 06 ruined in the eyes of some fans, would be FUN in a 2D styled game???And that is what I love about this game, it not only learned from Mania, but also pushed forward on what we loved about it, and wanted more of. For those who are already calling the game bad just for using Denuvo, it's actually hilarious that something so trivial like that is causing you to miss out on a genuinely beautiful game.You also have tons of new Power Ups with EACH new Emerald you obtain, and a handful of chances to obtain the Chaos Emeralds in each stage (for those who weren't lucky enough to get it on the first go blind). It's actually pretty cool how each of the Emeralds abilities not only can help you in combat situations when properly utilized, but also encourages you to EXPLORE the zones for more rewards instead of just blitzing through the whole stage.This game is not only for the speed demons who love to speed run a stage and try to get a faster time, but also introduces so many new mechanics and powers for those who want to stop, explore, and experiment with the game they bought. Which is perfect, because that is exactly what SEGA set out to do with this game, to not only have it please long time and experienced fans, but to also provide a more family friendly experience.Which brings me to another thing I LOVE about this game; the difficulty it has implemented. I would say for most Sonic games, the true difficulty comes into the stages and your want to replay them. That feeling of getting a new best time and improving not only your score, but also your own skill in the game you are obsessed with, is a feeling I think anyone can relate to. And that is what defines the difficulty throughout most of Sonic Superstars. The game's stages are well constructed, fast, and push you to learn the faster routes, just like the games of old. But, here's the interesting change;They found a way to make the bosses keep you on your toes, even with Super Sonic. The bosses are all designed to not be a complete cake walk after getting the legendary form, which is a welcomed change in my personal opinion. How many times have you played a Sonic game, gotten all of the Emeralds, and then just stood in place as Super Sonic for the rest of the now trivialized boss fights? If you are well experienced with the games, then you would know that unless the boss has some crush or insta death pits (Big Arm for example), the bosses became REALLY boring after getting all 7 Emeralds. Superstars throws a wrench into this mechanic, by not only giving the bosses invulnerability phases so you can't just kill it in 5 seconds, but also has the bosses require you to THINK about how you attack them. You can completely waste not only an entire opening to hit a boss, but also WASTE the rings that Super Sonic consumes during the boss. Meaning that if you wrecklessly try to abuse Super Sonic in a boss fight, you can not only leave yourself in a bad situation where you have lost an opening for attack, but also ticking closer and closer to dropping out of the form entirely. There is now some strategy to using Super Sonic in the fights. You can activate and deactivate the form on command, and this is a cool idea. Have a hard part of the boss that you haven't nailed down the dodging time for? Go Super, negate the attacks, and drop out. You sort of have a time management factor to the form now, and combined with the new extra powers that the Emeralds now bring to the table, there is a wide assortment of ways to approach how you fight the bosses in this game, which is so cool and a nice change to the formula. Super Sonic is a strong and OP reward, but it doesn't mean that the game is now brain dead easy, and I for one, LOVE that change.And the bosses, while not some Dark Souls level of challenging, are also a cool change. More bosses have ways of threatening you, and almost all of them bring some now gimmick or stage interaction to keep you on your toes. It is nice to finally have a Final Boss in a Sonic game that actually took a couple of attempts and memorization to finally take down, not to mention the CRAZY COOL idea the final zone had for it's gimmick and theme. The previously mentioned Emeralds also, as stated before add a TON of ways to attack and evade the bosses now, each of which having some form of value to them, whether that be for exploration or combat.All of this combines to not only give an awesome, casual experience, but actually adds new stuff to not only keep seasoned veterans of the series a new experience, but also refines the formula to remind you of WHY we love these types of games. It is a game made for a family, whether that be the speed running gamer, or the younger brother who you hand a second controller and carry through the experience.Sonic Superstars was NOT a game I was heavily anticipating, but it sure is one that surprised me with how much love and passion was put into this next entry in the series. Both Frontiers and Superstars show that SEGA/Sonic Team are trying to learn from their previous mistakes, and don't intend to pull another Boom or Forces any time soon. We have finally hit another good era for the series, where we can look at this gaming icon, and be proud of what comes out in the series. Whether that be a 3D modern game that involves the Boost, or a 2D classic game that rejuvenates our love for the Genesis styled games, Sonic is once again back and running to a brighter tomorrow.At the end of the day, I truly do believe that this game, at bare minimum is an 8/10. Outside of the Denuvo thing (which is such an arbitrary and forced reason to call it BAD), I genuinely can't name any negatives with this game. It was a passion project that only pleased me the entire way through. No game breaking bugs, and all around just pack with new and fun ideas for both the gameplay, zones, and characters. So while I say that this is a bare minimum 8/10, my personal enjoyment for it is DEFINITELY a very high 9.5/10. Even if you're not a super big Sonic fan, I can guarantee you will have a great time playing it and enjoy it immensely. And if you are a fan of the series? Then it hits every mark in terms of what we wanted.So yeah, check it out and decide for yourself! Don't let people who haven't even PLAYED the game and instantly uninstalled turn you away from what could be an amazing experience. It really is a shame that such an incredible game that aimed to please the fans first, is just being brushed aside by some and not even given a fair chance. Sonic has always had an unfair, hate filled bias against his series, and this game is another definitive example of something amazing being bandwagoned against.2022-2023 has been a Sonic Renaissance, and I can't think of a better way to end of this year with another banger of the series. A PROUD 9.5/10 is what I give this game, and I highly encourage you to give it a chance and experience return to what we all loved about Sonic Mania; Classic Sonic DONE RIGHT.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game for three reasons:1. I have been wanting to play a new sonic game for a while2. The inclusion of Fang and Trip had me intrigued.3. I have been saying for years that if they made a game with Amy as a main playable character again, I'd buy that game.The Story:I really wanted to like the story, the advertising bragged about this being a show-don't-tell type of story, but there was virtually no story at all and there weren't many cut-scenes between all of the acts. This is a huge disappointment because I was hoping for a decent amount of exposition. No motives for any of the three villains and absolutely nothing about Trip's background. Did they run out of time for writing the story??? I learned so much more from the trailers than the actual game!The Music:I have always been a fan of Sonic OSTs and there were a few excellent tracks in this game. Some that stood out to me were: Speed Jungle Zone Act 2 for zen-like ambiance, Pinball Carnival Zone Act 1 for funky beats, Lagoon City Zone Act 2 for Sonic CD vibes, and of course the Super Form song for its cheery, I-can-do-anything tunes. Unfortunately some songs are so short that they end up looping too much on the longer-than-usual stages and some were not particularly inspiring. The Gameplay: It feels like a proper 2D sonic game and I really enjoyed playing as Amy for my first go-around. One thing that really stood out to me was that, unlike in older 2D games, the water levels were actually enjoyable. At no point did I feel like I was rushing through just for an air bubble. They run a little long (5-7 minutes apiece on average for a first run) so be prepared for that. They do give you the ability to go back to previous stages through a hub world if you missed an emerald or just want to play it again. Props to SEGA for not just trying to nostalgia-bait us with Green Hill, Chemical Plant, or Angel Island Zone! The stages were pretty decent up until Press Factory where it seemed to just be cheap gimmicks and punishing enemy/spike placement. While I can appreciate the attempt to slow down gameplay for exploration and platforming, the unlockables aren't really worth it. The Unlockables:Its your standard Get 7 Chaos Emeralds for that awesome super form. In my opinion, they are much easier and enjoyable to get than in Sonic 3. They added new "abilities" that you can activate once each per checkpoint post, but I found myself completely ignoring them unless they were necessary for a certain platforming section. There's also Medals to collect thru Sonic 1 style special stages, but they are truly worthless, only buying cosmetics for the "Battle" mini-games which you'll get tired of almost immediately.Bosses:Oh boy, this is why the game gets a negative review: If you aren't playing as Tails, Amy, or (Secret Character), boss fights lag on for way too long because there's usually 30 seconds to a minute between when you can hit them again, and because they require so many hits, levels can drag on for over ten minutes (which would usually kill you in a classic sonic game but doesn't in this one.) Its a test of patience and endurance and far more than a test of reflexes and experimentation. I dread having to do bosses when I replay the game, something that isn't true of most other sonic games. Also, the final boss is like 10 minutes with no checkpoints or spare rings. Better not mess it up!The "Secret Character"If you don't already know who it is, then you clearly haven't been paying attention to the marketing of this game. But in case you don't want to know, I won't spoil it for you. They have double jump, wall climb, and ceiling climb, making Knuckles and Amy effectively obsolete. You'd think "Gee, I'll bet that makes the game easy now huh?" WELL YOU'D BE WRONG!!! The new character gets their own "Campaign" which is just the same stages as the others, but remixed with spike traps galore and completely saturated with enemies and unfair platforming situations. IT WAS NOT ENJOYABLE AT ALL. It did not feel like a reward. And if you're thinking: "Why not just use their super form, you collected all the emeralds in the previous play-through, right?" That's true, you could do that, but their super form is not like the others, its slow and doesn't play well with the mechanics of the game (i.e. bumpers, cannons, loops and other Sonic staples.) Then when you get to the boss, you'd better hope you have enough rings to go super again, because your super form turns off when the cut-scene starts. I still haven't completed this campaign because of how difficult and not fun it is. At least you get unlimited lives...In short: The main story plays like a proper 2D sonic game should, and having 4 characters to choose from is cool. The music was nice, and the nostalgia-gauge wasn't screaming "LOOK AT ME!!!" all the time like in Sonic Generations. The bosses were too tedious and the later stages were frustrating. The story was non-existent, and most of the collectibles were a wasted effort. The Mixed rating this game has is well deserved. There are good and bad parts, but it is up to you to decide if the good outweighs the bad.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not worth £60.Now see the graphics are ok with the animations, but that's the only good thing about this stupid game. The reason i have issues with this game are the following reasons (please note spoilers will be ahead)1: the chaos emerald powers. Now in sonic superstars you get powers from the emeralds that's "suppose" to change the game. However, within the game you barely use these abilities and it's not massively game changing if you do get these powers. There are two main chaos emerald abilities that break boss fights entirely, this being the fire ball attack and the clone attacks, which break boss fights down so fast its barely even a challenge. and the rest of the powers from the emeralds are so god danm useless its unreal.This is because you have to "recharge" the emeralds powers at a checkpoint, so its a one time use. So throughout my play through, i never ever use the powers of the emeralds unless its super forms or boss fights which i only use 2 of the 7 powers.2: Super sonic cancels the every other power. Now this one pisses me off, because if you are within a super form after having all 7 chaos emeralds, you can't even use the other powers of the emeralds, which makes this games branding entirely useless. the ENTIRE point of getting the emeralds in this game 1 by 1, is to gain elemental powers for certain environments on certain stages, like water or using the ivy etc. What's worse though, is IF your playing co-op with people and you wish to use a super form, you cancel everybody else's use to the emeralds. so apart from the characters move set, they become useless in story mode, as they don't have emerald powers if somebody is in a super form. And even worse, they can't even use the super forms alongside you, meaning that the branding for this game is even more pointless.3: The multiplayer. Now this one is just so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ frustrating. Sega has decided that playing a 2D sonic game with multiplayer on a single screen was a great idea. Well people, its not. I have suffered with my partner throughout the entire time we played, and it was not great. The camera focuses on one player and if the other goes off screen (very easy to do so due to the speed of the game) then you have to respawn near them every time. In my play through i have been zapped around because of this problem, and every time my friend hit a boost panel then it zaps me every time or him. this happens frequently throughout the ENTIRE game.4: Horrible camera and controls. This is one of my main problems. Now, when you play through this game single player, the camera likes to stay very close to sonic in nearly any level, and this is NOT a great thing for 2D sonic. Because your moving so quickly or your platforming across a level, you cant see ANYTHING! It makes playing the game harder because of how close the camera is to sonic, and if you are running at high speeds and you bump into an enemy then you can't see it. Which makes you lose rings for your super form or score. I find the camera very annoying in this game, more so then any other classic sonic game because of how close it is to the player.The second part is the controls. Now i wont lie, its not like sonic 4 where it feels like there is no momentum at all. However, the spindash feels terrible in this game. I find myself contently using the drop dash more then spindash because of how terrible it is. When using the spindash, i feel no gain to speed and it feels so sluggish compared to other titles. The momentum in this game is not great, but its not the worst thing ever.5: Online multiplayer. Jesus don't even get me started on this crap. You need to make an epic games account to play online battle modes on pc, which is stupid due to steam having its own online platform. After doing all the requirements to play online battle mode and you go to find a match there is barely anybody within lobbies ready to play, making the online dead in this game. I only encountered 1 real person in the entire online matches, and i was sat waiting for a good 10 minutes.Do not do the online its terrible.6: Remote play. So everybody, Sega can make an online battle mode, but can't make an online storymode. Which would have made the multiplayer so much better, as players wouldn't have had to share a screen or have the same camera, which would have fixed a huge amount of multiplayer issues. _childDocuments_.review: The DRM is bad, yes lmao. But I'm going to talk about the merits of the game (for someone who has beat most of the game, except the endgame final boss).First off, I'll talk multiplayer. The co-op should be online, but the online multiplayer is a bit barebones but seems to be fun (once people start playing it). Level design and physics are actually really accurate to the Genesis games. It gets super platform heavy mostly (which I prefer), and isn't afraid to filter to you. The power-ups are fun, some of it is situational but experimenting with them have been a lot of fun, and has saved my ass. Trip's story is a bit filtering but it's really fun to play in general. Bosses are cool, although my biggest issue is a lot of stop and go, and really cheap hits in the later bosses.Visuals are 50/50. You can't wipe off that cheap filling to some of the stages. Stages like Golden Capital, Speed Jungle and Frozen Base Zone being highlights imo. Just remove the depth of field in the settings, it really improves it visual wise. Badniks are awesomely designed and the characters themselves are really expressive.Music is one of the weaker aspects, because Mania was 100% peak and this was not. There are great tracks (like Speed Jungle Act 1, Pinball Carnival Act 1, Lagoon City Act 2) and some real Sonic 4 tier duds (Press Factory, Main Menu theme). Still not as bad as some would describe, but Jun Senoue should get off the Genesis synth.In conclusion, there are some cool surprises, good physics, and level design which will definitely filter you. It's just not worth $60 though, especially with the poor presentation (visually and music consistency wise) and DRM issues. 7.5/10 overall, 2nd best Classic game imo in terms of level design and the content it provides. So it's definitely in the more game-play over graphics sort of thing (although I look for that more then spectacle like a lot of Modern fans, no offence it's a preference thing). Sonic 3 and Knuckles will still never be beat though.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is crafted with extreme knowledge of every single other Sonic game and is aimed to be the most extensive review of this game as possible. Sonic Superstars is a game that nails the original ideas of Classic Sonic. Different path game play with varying difficulties and rewards based on your path. The speed and pacing of the game is back to feeling like Sonic 2, with a major focus on speed and lots of things in levels to achieve that. The best way to describe this game to a major Classic Sonic fan is that it is Sonic 2 that takes a lot of things from Mania.They nailed how Sonic feels but the spindash feels weaker than the other games, luckily the dropdash from Mania helps with this problem a lot. The Zones in this game started out feeling absolutely excellent but far too short. Luckily, the progression in this game also fixes this problem and levels start feeling about the same as Sonic 3&K level lengths, not as long as Mania levels though (for better or for worse). The Zone designs are definitely a bit more basic than the other games but that's to be expected when SEGA's last 2D game made in house was Sonic 4. Sonic 3&K introduced Act based mechanics which Mania further explored but sadly, it seems that these are sort of absent in many ways leaving the Act 1 and 2s (sometimes only Act 1s) to feel just like Sonic 2 Zones. Pretty much the Act 1 introduces the level and its gameplay style and the Act 2 is just more of Act 1. The amount of Zones are comparable to Sonic 3&K but since there are so many 1 Act Zones, it ends up making the game have a similar main game length to Sonic 2. Levels do lack some of the identity other zones in Classic Sonic games have, Bridge Island's half pipe gimmick is the most reminiscent to a memorable Classic Sonic gimmick. Lots of levels feel like a mix of Sonic 1 and 2 or 2 and CD.Levels have these sort of multiplayer gimmicks that get in the way like spinning in a loop 10 times or hitting the jump button a set amount of times on a hanging block. These are in most levels when I wish there was just more freedom around them. There are also these warp portals that open up around levels that skip you through them a decent amount. Personally, I like to avoid these because I like knowing a level inside and out to completion. I really wish I could turn these and those other gimmicks off but it doesn't negatively impact gameplay much. The special stages in this game feel a little bit weaker than the special stages in 2 and 3&K but I would say they have a similar difficulty to the Sonic CD special stages (which to me are pretty easy but get hard fast). All in all, they are a new experience and are still interesting but a bit basic in comparison to every other special stage. Emeralds have become progression based which doesn't allow you to get more than 1 Emerald in a world but the special stages still appear and allow you to practice them. Personally, I loved trying to get all the Emeralds as fast as I could to test myself but this was a good decision due to how Emeralds were reworked. Each Emerald unlocking a new power is interesting but you wont find yourself using them on your first run too much unless you fall off top path and wanna get back or miss a special stage you really want. Some like water are way too situational, while fireball makes exploration very easy. I think they are excellent for replay value and adds more depth than a lot of other sonic games.The depth of the game is also very comparable to Sonic 2, while exploration is something that the game humors, I never feel like it is the main focus, sorry Sonic 3&K Enjoyers. Getting to point A to point B was a journey in Sonic 3&K and Mania but I cannot stress enough how much of an extended Sonic 2 this game feels with its huge focus on speed. The boss fights opt for a more cinematic experience and while they are tough fights and have strategy, some even more than any of the other Classic games, they often feel way too long and slow. This doesn't stop them from being fun, but I often wish I could deal with them 8 hits old school style instead of needing to wait between attacks. I am not going into the OST too much because it sadly isn't as notable as the other games. It isn't as bad as it's made out to be I swear, but it is a little "too lacking" for Sonic.If you aren't someone who gets turned off by corporate companies getting their claws on some part of development (I'm looking at you Denuvo and Epic Games) then Sonic Superstars is a very strong return to form that anyone who knows a lot about the original games can very easily enjoy. It is the true extension of the Classic games and does very little wrong. Sure it can be buggy at times but we live in a time where these will probably fixed at some point. It doesn't reach what Sonic 3&K does for me but I find myself enjoying the levels of this game more than the likes of Sonic 1 and CD hell, even more than many Sonic 2 and Mania Zones. It's a weird in between of CD and Sonic 2, just like how Mania was an in between of Sonic 3&K and CD. Sonic Superstars is nearly a perfect return to form while feeling completely new and I cannot wait to see a perfected form using everything they learn from this game for their next title.

TLDR: You have to switch the input template from "Controller with Touchpad" to "Mouse Only" and then back again every time you run the game!First time running the game it starts up the Epic Games Launcher which then goes and downloads a bunch of stuff independently from Steam. Then after the game starts an overlay pop-up shows from from the Epic Games Services that asks you to login to the Epic Games Store and give some app called "Aero" access to your Epic Account. This pop-up doesn't respond to controller input and doesn't work with the Steam Deck's touchscreen, making it almost impossible to dismiss! To get rid of it, you have to switch the input template from "Controller with Touchpad" to "Mouse Only", use the touchpad to dismiss the pop-up, and then go back to "Gamepad with Touchpad" afterwards. You have to do this EVERY TIME YOU RUN THE GAME!All of that just to use Epic's matchmaking service... which is totally redundant since Steam comes with a matchmaking service. In the post-Steam Deck era, this kind of behavior is now completely unacceptable.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best fully original 2D Sonic game Sega has released since the Sonic Advance era. It might even be better than those games.The level design is very evocative of the Genesis era. They even have new game mechanics for a 2D Sonic game, which are very cool. For example, one of the zones has you hopping between fast moving roller coasters. Another has you grinding on vines. Some of the levels are a bit too long though, especially the boss battles. The later bosses are not just long, but too difficult. In the 2nd story mode, this is taken to the extreme, which the final boss having some moves that will kill you instantly. There are no checkpoints between the forms of the bosses, so you may have to replay minutes of tedious gamepaly, just to get back to where you died. Also, if you quit the game, you will have to replay the entire long level, leading up to the boss. It's too bad that most PC games don't have a suspend mode.Otherwise, a lot of the challenge in the later levels trivialized by the ease at collecting all of the Chaos Emeralds. You can turn super and just plow through everything, provided you maintain enough rings. The emeralds stay unlocked, even in the 2nd story, only mitigated by the tedium of controlling the secret character's super form. Another annoyance with the super form is that certain parts of the levels will automatically change you back. If your ring count had dropped below 50, you will be unable to reactivate the super form.I like that, in the main story, you can switch characters between levels. The fact that each Chaos Emerald gives you a unique ability, is also an interesting mechanic. However, some of the abilities have very limited uses, such as the water ability.The online Battle Mode is a nice bonus, but there don't seem to be that many players. Unfortunately, most of the collectables in the levels only server to unlock cosmetics for said mode. This is a missed opportunity to have more unlockable content, such as cosmetics for the other modes or maybe even extra levels and music.The soundtrack is good, but not great, which is weird for a Sonic game. There are a few standout tracks, my favorites being Sand Sanctuary and Press Garden Act 1. The rest were not as memorable to me, but still good.I also had a few technical issues with the PC port. If using VSync, the game would often slow down to 30 FPS, after a loading screen. This would not stop, unless I enter a new loading screen, alt tab out of the program, or switch to window mode. The solution was to disable VSync. However, this caused screen tearing, even in borderless window mode. There were also some occasional frame rate hiccups, but nothing as severe.Another issue was that the boss music would sometimes not play, if I was in a super form, prior to a boss fight. The character would transform back, as mentioned earlier, and the regular level music would play instead. Also, if my controller disconnected 1 time, the game would automatically pause at certain points in the level. This happened even after reconnecting the controller. Restarting the game resolved the issue.Overall, I would recommend this game, but maybe wait for a sale. It really should be more like $30 or $40 for the light amount of content. I am also hoping that the technical issues are addressed soon.
