_childDocuments_.review: How do I explain this game? I finished it out of sheer stubbornness and malice and I got all the achievements. I hate this game. I didn't even pay money for this game and I still hate it. I have no respect for it and you should not play it. With that said, I'mma discuss stuff nonchalantly without caring about spoilers. Don't worry, the only impact the story has is the palm of your hand hitting your forehead, but just once.If you're gonna ignore me and get the game, then get it on sale and plop a new save at the start of every chapter (unless you don't care about achievements). The game won't let you access old chapters without starting a brand new game. Also, importantly, the bad ending is in chapter 6.I ended up cutting down on my review by a lot to fit. Turns out, you can run out characters in a steam review.With that said, think of the worst possible Persona game. Okay, now make it worse somehow and that's this game. It mishandles any and all ideas - most stolen from Persona - it to the point that it lost me. It isn't that I can't handle convoluted and stupid plots, because I very much can. I can go on and on about Blazblue lore until you lose interest in it as a game and as a fighting game. The main problem with this game refuses to commit to the idea of something happening and it messes around with "Did that happen? Hmmmaaaaybeeeee." It just doesn't work. Commit to your freakin' ideas! A HUGE reveal pops along at one point and it's "THIS GUY AND THE MAIN CHARACTER ARE THE SAME PERSON ALL ALONG!" And I was like "okay." Not only did I see it coming, but it had zero impact because it doesn't change anything.* On top of that, the game points out the plothole it created for that plot twist and decides "EXCEPTION!" which kills any reason as to why I should bother caring.*okay, full disclosure, it does allow a fake version of the main character to pop up in the final dungeon and belittle the every ally. After the battle, the characters get to discuss how they've changed over time. That's a breath of fresh air of good game design out of a sea of bad bad bad stupid game.Okay, I spent longer on that thing so let's keep walking and compare the game to Persona. Like Persona, you are Mr. Main Character - bland every man with nothing interesting going for you and you're thrown into the plot with the stakes against you. However, instead of being a good person, you're kinda just doing a job for money because you're a detective. A detective who is really absurdly bad at being a detective and gets called out for it; but instead of caring, they just shrug and continue.Speaking of characters, you enlist a bunch of allies. Poorly written allies.The first dude you get is also the main character, but he doesn't act the same except for the occasional hint.The second person you get is a fan of Robin Hood. You save her life from a trap that she has been trapped in for *YEARS* and she verifies that it is true. She decides to team up with you to get revenge. You do get the revenge, hooray! It baffled me at one point where main character says something completely normal and in sequence with the serious cutscene that was ongoing -> and she suddenly yells "PERV" at him. I was like "huh?" I pulled up the log to look and find out what happened, but I couldn't figure it out. What is this stupid gag in the middle of a serious cutscene?The third person is an old vet with a taunt button who serves as your main tank, but he excessively sucks at being a tank. Imagine your main tank having a weakness. Fourth is a celebrity with a 3 minute music video of her singing - which I refuse to watch. Fifth is some leader of delinquents who seem to have ire against "the man" man, but uh... it seems to be less of a serious life and death situation and more of a "hey, you splashed me with water!" in-a-swimming-pool kind of situation. And finally, sixth is a little messenger boy who I thought would be the second ally.Some of these allies have no a reason to stick around, but "it is a video game," so they do. You can improve your relationship with these character for almost zero gameplay impact when an icon appears on the map. Go to them, press the button, watch a cutscene, and done. There is no input. "Almost?" Well, there is a rare minigame in this game: Slay the Spire. Yes, really. You get a basic deck from each ally and you unlock the advanced version after you improve your relationship enough. You cannot edit these decks, just pick which deck to use (also, basic or advanced) and it's fairly easy... then again I have hundreds of hours in StS so I'm biased.Like Persona, you have a normal (albeit small) city to walk around in. Thing is, the city is a dreamscape of sorts where time is entirely frozen. The entire plot really revolves around this city. It starts off on some drug called "HANDOUT" but that unravels in an unimportant way and stops being important. Time is technically still in the city, despite people feeling time going by. I think we destroy the city in the "normal ending" which sounds significant but again the game mishandles it due to aforementioned reasons of refusing to care and commit - so it is vague. I would've respected the game if it had ZERO post-game saying "you destroyed that world. What'd you expect?" There are optional dungeons for harder fights and loot, so you can do more difficult fights for more loot. This leads me to combat. You get 6 party members in total but you can only use 4. Why? Combat isn't even balanced properly to have any valid excuse. The only reason is "because it is a video game." That's literally it. It's a trope from other games where 4 people parties exist so this game must follow that too. Canonically, all six of you are always together, fighting together. It could've been a selling point - along with no-post game because you destroyed the world - but nope.That aside, you have 3 main types of damage, slash, pierce and crush. Every enemy is 20% weak to one, endured to another, and 0% neutral to a third. Thing is, there is nearly zero benefit for hitting a weakness other than "more damage." There is no flare or fancy happenings to be done for hitting a weakness, so combat is boring. It does one thing well: abilities do not cost any resources. Instead they go on cooldown. This forces tactics and strategic thinking. It's not a high bar.Also, auto-battle sucks and is completely unreliable. I ran through old random dungeons for the achievement with auto-battle; turn 2 rolled around with 1 enemy with tiny amount of HP. Literally any basic hit will kill the enemy. What does the auto-battler do? Literally all four of them activate buffs and don't hit the enemy... sigh. Importantly, this game loves wasting time. Just half a second here and half a second there. It adds up ya know. Animations in battle can be sped up in the settings - and even skipped by mashing right click/B/Circle. You cannot speed up nor skip the animations of the camera moving to the next ally (even in auto-battle) and importantly: enemies taking DoT (poison/bleed) and enemies dying. There is other time wasting in this game, including transitions screens, pressing a button in dungeons and slowly watching the game showing us what changed even if it is so painfully obvious (like 3 feet away), etc. Without the time wasting, my 33 hours in this game would be closer to 27 hours. Yes, I believe I lost 6 hours on useless time wasting in this game. That's not hyperbole.Also, this game runs really well for being poorly optimized. I was low on money at one so I went to sell my junk. Selling stuff is one item at a time, how many of that item and are you sure? That's THREE button presses per item to sell. It took me 5 minutes of mashing to sell all my level 1 and level 2 gear. Again, I only beat this game through sheer stubbornness and malice towards it. Don't play this game. Please. I don't even have space to talk about all the stupid things I hate. Character limit.

_childDocuments_.review: For full view, go to: Mato Anomalies is a JRPG developed by the Chinese studio Arrowiz, stands out as a well-crafted game.  I appreciate its successful execution in combat, pacing, and voice acting—areas where other indie games(and even AAA) often falter. The game blends a 1920s aesthetic with a futuristic cyberpunk setting, following the detective Doe's investigation into a drug called HANDOUT. The narrative unfolds through a dual perspective, with Doe solving crimes in the overworld and Gram navigating 'Lairs' using the MondoShaman device. While the story starts small, it intensifies into a complex cyberpunk conspiracy.The character-focused moments, particularly addressing themes of trauma and humanity, are some of the game's strongest moments. Combat is well-done, employing a rock-paper-scissors approach with different damage types and incorporating strategic elements. I loved the designs of the enemies, as well as the bosses and their ability to morph during fights, however I do want to point out the final boss offered a huge difficulty spike, especially in comparison to a number of other bosses.Despite the last hour's difficulty, this game is worth the experience, with special mention given to commendable voice acting. Overall, this is easily an 8/10. If you're a fan of classic JRPGs, comparing it to Final Fantasy, Dragon Quest, and Persona, noting its closer alignment with modern Persona games in terms of difficulty and world design.

_childDocuments_.review: Mato Anomalies is a captivating and immersive experience that had me hooked from the very beginning. As someone who enjoys exploring mysteries and unraveling secrets, I knew I had to purchase this game on my Switch with the DLC, and I'm so glad I did.One of the most striking aspects of Mato Anomalies is its richly detailed world and atmosphere. From the moment I stepped into the shoes of the protagonist, I was transported to a realm filled with intrigue, wonder, and danger. The game's art style is stunning, with vibrant colors and imaginative designs that bring the world to life in breathtaking detail. Whether I was exploring ancient ruins, delving into dark dungeons, or encountering bizarre creatures, every moment felt like a journey into the unknown.But what truly sets Mato Anomalies apart is its compelling storyline and deep lore. As I uncovered the mysteries of the world and pieced together the truth behind the anomalies, I found myself drawn deeper into the narrative with each passing moment. The game's characters are well-developed and memorable, each with their own motivations and secrets waiting to be discovered. And the DLC only enhances the experience, offering additional content and insights into the game's rich mythology.Of course, no adventure game would be complete without its fair share of challenges, and Mato Anomalies delivers in spades. From intricate puzzles to intense battles, the game offers a satisfying blend of gameplay elements that kept me engaged and entertained throughout my journey. And with multiple endings to discover, there's plenty of replay value to be found as well.In conclusion, Mato Anomalies is a must-have experience for fans of adventure games and mystery enthusiasts alike. With its captivating storyline, stunning visuals, and challenging gameplay, it's a journey that will keep you enthralled from start to finish. Whether you're playing on Switch or any other platform, I highly recommend picking up this gem of a game. You won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I very much wish that Steam had mixed recommendations because I do think Mato Anomalies is pretty good? But I also feel like there are some quality of life changes that would improve the game.So first, I like the mash-up of different genres/styles. I think it's pretty fun to have the visual novel with some other elements. The VN aspect is really what drew me to it (along with the detective nature of the story), but it seems pretty nice to mix it with turn-based combat and Persona-esque dungeon crawling. I also really like the art style of the game, especially the mixture of 3D environments to run around, the traditional animated VN elements of conversation screens, the cinematics, and the comic strip scenes. It sounds like a lot and like it should clash, but it all works together really well.That said... I don't feel like Doe needs to do anything beyond be the detective protagonist. The mind-hacking card game is tedious and clunky and feels like it was added as a means to give Doe something to do (kind of like an afterthought). It often feels really cumbersome and slow, which doesn't match the narrative that's happening around it. Usually, Doe's scenes have provided a sense of urgency, a sense that things need to be done quickly... and then you do the tedious mind-hacking, and it just... slows everything down? I appreciate that there's a skip-after-3 option, but I really feel like there should be a full-on skip option from the jump. I personally don't appreciate this aspect of the game, and I'd rather just waste time failing 3 times to skip it instead of doing it (with few exceptions, it feels faster to do that). Seriously, as much as I hate wire puzzles, I'd rather do those than play this card game. (I also felt like some of the descriptions in the card game were vague and unclear, which contributed to me giving up, not caring, and just skipping turns to fail.)I also think the danger-level scaling in the dungeons on normal is a bit weird? Like they're super easy for the first couple dungeons where you only have one character (Gram), then the difficulty scales up a lot until you get Butterfly... where it scales down again... but then scales up dramatically once you get Smoker? And it feels really inconsistent. Even upgrading and changing things doesn't really make it that much better; the changes (gears, talents, weapons) just feel incremental at best, so it doesn't really feel that great when you get a new weapon (and actually kind of makes it feel pointless to buy them because they are so costly and money is so scarce unless you run dungeons on repeat to get more weapons/gears to sell to the travelling merchant).Like, I enjoyed a good chunk of time with this, but it also does a lot of stuff that makes me give up before even finishing because I just get bored of having to grind things out to get minimal improvements. I'm getting older, and I have stuff to do in my normal life... Games that start feeling like work, even if I like them to start, feel unappealing.

_childDocuments_.review: My feelings are all mixed up.  There are a number of interesting ideas in here, but my recommendation is more to advocate for the potential that's in here.  The battle system is interesting, the card game is interesting, the characters and setting are interesting, the plot is interesting, etc.  However, there's a reason why almost 94% of players never finish it, and it's not the difficulty.This game is LONG and it FEELS long.  The scope of the game appears to far exceed its budget.  Some sequences use normal cutscenes or comic-book-style cutscenes to show what's going on, but the vast majority of dialogue happens with the same character portraits with the same backgrounds without voices for a LONG time.  Normally not a big problem, but it's difficult to properly emphasize HOW MUCH of it there is.  And while a good turn-based battle system like this can balance things out for a while, it can only go so far.  On top of that, it's not like you can skim and catch up at the bigger story events, because the decision on what's important enough for a cutscene vs normal dialogue was made by throwing darts at a wall.  Example: at the end of one party member's character events, they get a FULL 3-MINUTE MUSIC VIDEO.  What does the rest of the party get?  NOTHING.All that being said, I'm still hopeful to see what Arrowiz makes next, because I see the potential for something truly great.  There are sparks of brilliance in here that I hope to see more of in a future title that's more dense/focused.

Mato Anomalies is a turn-based RPG that takes players on a journey across Mato, a fantasized neo-futuristic version of a bygone oriental city. Take control of the Dual Protagonists Doe and Gram to investigate strange anomalies around the city, or venture into rifts to battle demonic abominations determined to bring about the city's downfall.

Team up with unlikely companions and unravel the dark secrets in this story of Duty, Hope and Justice.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game worth the money? Yes, Absolutely. Its a 10/10 remake hands down. BUT, with that being said.. I didn't necessarily want just a "Remake". I mean they already changed some stuff from 4. So why not stop being lazy af DEVS and go the distance to make this game truly something special. I mean this game came out what? 15 years ago or something crazy like that. So in 15 years.. What? 10 RE games? You're telling me what passes for a remake these days is just remaking the game with better graphics. Then slapping a few quality of life updates to the game? Thats it? Idk maybe its just me being critical here. But I'm just tired of game company giving us the short end of the stick. Dont get me wrong I'm grateful this game was made and they added some stuff from RE4 so its better. I get that. I just dont get why they stopped there lol.For instance.. Why cant we prime our guns? I mean Leon will do it by himself from time to time. So why couldn't you take the code from the other RE games and simply tweak the values for RE4. So anytime we want to we can press "Square" or "Reload" and if our gun has full ammo we can see Leon do his gun check animation. That alone is such a small thing.. But in reality goes a very very long way in making the game feel good. Same thing with the flashlight... Or the movement... Like RE Village just came out and the movement in that game is perfect. So why on earth give us this janky running movement half as good as RE7+. Lets see... I can't mark my map. No compass. No Map button like RE5.. So once again why have you released other RE games with these features but not this one? Makes no sense to me. Idk this game just feels like its missing a lot of little things. BUT, its a good "Remake" LOL.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil has a very unique gameplay style that works really well for them. There are some things that I am going to chalk up to cultural differences, as RE games are made by Japanese developers. For example the voice acting, and story always seems to be just a little off. While us westerners like our realism in our stories, CAPCOM kind've go for bending reality as much as they need to suit the story. I think the best thing I can compare it to is anime; Of course it isn't going to be as realistic as TLOU. So if you can get behind the obvious scenes where plot armor is put on steroids, you can enjoy the amazing gameplay resident evil 4 has to offer.

As for the PC port, it is solid as rock and ran flawlessly. The mouse and k/b controls are excellent. The autosaves and manual saves are very generous. The game is a great mix of action, scares, suspense, adventure, humor, and fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, strap in for a wild ride down memory lane with the Resident Evil 4 Remake! This game takes you back to a time when "tank controls" were a thing, and our hero Leon Kennedy could take on entire villages armed with just a few herbs and a sassy attitude.The graphics are so good that you can practically see the fear in Leon's eyes as he realizes he's about to be chased by a boulder again. And speaking of chasing, the villagers are now more persistent than ever, giving you a cardio workout you didn't sign up for. I mean, who needs a gym membership when you can just run away from chainsaw-wielding maniacs, am I right?And let's not forget the merchant. He's like the ultimate one-stop shop for all your apocalyptic needs. Need a rocket launcher? He's got it. Running low on first aid sprays? No worries. Just don't expect him to accept credit cards – it's all about those precious shiny gems.But let's be real, the best part of the game is still the president's daughter, Ashley. She's the queen of getting into trouble, but hey, at least she's resourceful enough to hide in dumpsters. A true survivalist in the making.All in all, Resident Evil 4 Remake is a hilarious and heart-pounding trip down memory lane. So grab your green herbs, ready your puny knives, and get ready to yell "Oh my God!" as you dodge boulders and dodge death. It's survival horror, old-school style!

I never feel too pressured to keep pushing forward and actually makes overcoming the fear and killing the zombies really fun and satisfying. Ammo and materials are just scarce enough to keep you being careful with your resources and feels like the difficulty is always just right. Can't wait to do a second playthrough on Hardcore mode.

_childDocuments_.review: pretty good. think i like res e 2 remake more, however i do like this also. separate ways dlc should have been included rather than a 10$ dlc, and doesn't improve the base game much, but just gives you a bit more re4r, if that's what you're looking for. english vas are inferior to the originals, so i prefer to run the audio in japanese. would not call the dialogue differences are better here than the original, but do have differences fwiw. runs well on older hardware (running on a 7 year old ryzen 7 system as of 2024, vega 56 gpu, and get solid framerates). this game honestly kinda imho is likely a preview of what an eventual re5 remake will look/feel like, though i hope that capcom will do code veronica before they go further down the remake path; re3 remake was quite disappointing in that it feels like half the original, if not less, because they cut a lot of content from that one. anyone familiar with re5 can probably likely also see how easily capcom can remake re5 similar to how they did this, using more or less the same tech, and keep a lot of the feel of the original in tact; only major change will be how the newer tank controls allow some small amount of movement vs having your feet planted while aiming. the other aspect would be would they choose to make it one big open map like this rather than the level based approach in the original, and how might they implement a multiplayer component - i do think that re4 remake is a good example of what to expect gameplay wise, as well as look/feel, from any further potential remakes in the series. capcom is apparently working on a new game rather than a remake at the moment, but i expect more of these in the future. 2 was good. 3 was meh. 4 was good. hope they don't repeat the pattern that's developing here.anyway, re: re4r - plenty of replayability here, ng+ and various difficulty modes. shooting gallery is fun. game looks good visually as well.lastly, don't buy the treasure map dlc unless you want to have lots of extra treasures which kind of trivialize the difficulty, imho. tldr: 8/10, recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this series for a long time. RE 4, I've played a ton on multiple consoles. The gamecube original, the Wii port, the terrible original PC port, Ultimate HD with mod pack and the VR version. Resident Evil is one of my favorite series no matter how goofy. The B movie experience has always enhanced the best parts of this series and I'm very happy with this remake. Without saying anything about the story, I will just say the remake changes just enough so it's familiar but also changes context, adds lore and cleans up the plot. As far as graphics, animation and characters go, I love that RE Engine is so well optimized without sacrificing the looks. I've always been amazed by Capcom's animation. Leon's animations are slick, enemies are much more intimidating this time around and bosses are nasty looking. The body horror looks fantastic. I do think Ada and Ashley look nice.My one complaint, Ada's voice. Her actress really put no effort into it. Everytime she's on screen, she looks good but sounds bored, so out of place and each delivery sounds like a bad first take. In comparison to every other character in the game, she sticks out like a crying baby in a movie theater. As far as gameplay goes, I don't mind the knife durability as the game gives you weaker knives to hold out. It's another resource in this resource management survival horror game. With how easy it is to parry in this game on any other difficulty other than pro, this game would be a huge joke if knife was unlimited and yes, you can parry unarmed enemies if they go for a punch rather than a grab. It will literally slice their arm off. Speaking of enemies, they are FAR more aggressive this time around to compensate for Leon's extended movement. You can move and shoot, run in any direction and can quick kill many enemies. Flash bangs can be used to get knife insta-kills, perfect parries can stun enemies to open for a crowd controlling roundhouse kick and can now suplex from the very beginning. Much like how the original was made to overwhelm the player just enough to reward skill, this does the same with the extended move sets. Overall, I absolutely love the remake as much as I love the original. The cuts are outweighed by what they extended. For example, it's been stated in interviews that the original cut a lot of the castle to fit the game on the discs of the hardware at the time. The castle in this game is largely extended with new setpieces and a little more to explore. The remake stays familiar to veterans while changing just enough to feel different. Fully recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The Resident Evil 4 Remake is something a lot of people looked forward to after the original trilogy got remastered, and it was absolutely worth the wait. Resident Evil 4 (2005) has always been one of my favorite classic titles and even my favorite of the Resident Evil franchise, it really capitalized on "open world" exploration while keeping the horror elements intact. I remember being scared of the verdugo for the first time, or the anxiety growing as Dr. Salvador slowly got closer to me, those moments are re-captured in this game beautifully and the mechanics updated to go with it. This remake was very well put together and the moments I found myself in were never the games fault, but my own for being in a place at the wrong time. The weapons are responsive, bloom is a ♥♥♥♥♥, grabbing ganados are the hardest enemy in the game. Jokes aside, the difficulties feel like actual levels of intensity rather than them just becoming bullet sponges - they evolve. While I don't agree with the purchasable exclusive tickets (I own one for an easier time), there isn't a reason to be anal about it and honestly enhances the early game experience. Looking forward to see what gets developed next, I know this game isn't done producing content yet.

_childDocuments_.review: How to improve an already fun game into a narrative rich and chaotic masterpieceThis game is not without its flaws but this review is coming from the heart of someone who played every version of the RE4 title (except that weird mobile one).So about the original title: It was a fun, guns ablazing type of gameplay where you could just mow down waves of enemies with your shotguns, deal absurd amounts of damage with a fully upgraded TMP, min-max the treasures and get a bunch of money to fully upgrade the best weapons of the game. It was just a fun game all and all. The story was a bit lacking, having to relay on files and pop-up characters interactions like a visual novel and even then Leon only had one personality of being snarky and throw quips at the other characters when they interacted. So what about the remake improved from the original version? ------SPOILERS BEYOND THIS MARK--------This remake brings a new narative and additional plot elements to characters, more personality overall. Luis is not just there for plot convenience, he's now his own character and actually have a good ammount of screen time! He's not just the lady's man anymore, he's not as shallow. This all goes the same for Leon, Ashley, Ada, Salazar, Saddler and Krauser.Leon finally gets to shine as a hero who's not just a oneliner machine. He actually gets narrative and you can see where he's coming from this time. RE2 Leon's build up as a character shines in this remake and you can see he's actually trying to go through some ♥♥♥♥ unlike the original where he just shoots and one-lines.Ashley is grown up!!!!! She's more than a escort mission now! She actually helps a couple of times, her section is way more fun and interesting to explore, she doesnt need you to catch her from the stairs every single time and her commands are actually useful this time. She gained a lot of character as well! She comments on things, she doesn't need to rely on you for anything besides guiding her through the hordes, she actually shows personality now making it a fun exchange between the two of them.Ada shows growth from the last couple of remakes. Saddler is an actual character now! He has screen time and it bacame an actual terrfying villain and gives us reason to kill him this time. Same goes for Krauser! If it wasnt for the early exchange between you and krauser and having him killed Luis he wouldnt have a depth. They actually give you some revenge juice to go after him and that's great!! Storywise, this game improves immensily and I'm so happy to see how it's been turning out!! Now for the gamplay! I think it improves on things the original game lacked, such as crowd controld.Getting rid of some of the treasure improved the curve immensily. All the catseye you used to collect in the original are gone and spinels are now actually useful! Changing them to their own currency and grabbing specific gear from their own separate menu is so much better, gives a reason for the player to go hunting them down and do subquests!Subquests on their own are a HUGE IMPROVEMENT for those who want to explore the game! In the OG it was cool going back to the same areas but there was no real meaning besides lack of tech. Now you can go back and explore those areas! Making the backtrack less of a chore and more of a seek and reward kind of deal! The merchant giving you quests to kill mini bosses and kill rats and blue medallion hunting is a great incentive for the player to keep exploring, specially with the rewards! The weapon roaster is still amazing! I love how each one feels compared to the OG. The kick back is strong, the sound design is great! One personal weapon that kinda got ruined to me was the mine thrower. I like the mine thrower, it used to be a satisfying gimmicky weapon, now with the bolts AND attachable mines kinda makes it  unworthy to use, takes too much inventory space and it doesnt reward the player as much. The crafting system is a great addition makes it less unbrearable to have enemies drop piles and piles of ammo each wave of enemies, it makes you conserve and think about your choices. Like any other resident evil game. I found myself running out of ammo and having to rely on my knife a couple of times, which was challanging and fun! The knife on itself is an AMAZING addition! Gives the player a way to block attacks since this game is a bit more chaotic than the other ones, rewards you for doing so and gives you a way of insta killing enemies with stealth or just prompting a command to insta kill them once they are stunned on the floor. In the OG game you'd have a knife for cheesing a lot of enemies, you'd stun them, knife them, conserve all your ammo and that was it. Now you actually have to think when to use it since it has durability!The case mods is a fun addition allowing you to actually choose what the game drops this time! Such as gunpowder and ammo.The enemies placement is great, nothing feels out of place unlike the OG game. Enemies actually feel they are supposed to be there. Like removing the random giant in the chasm, making him an actual weapon of war and placing him in the castle with the other two. Same for the wolves, much better placements compared to the OG game. The map is just amazing to go through. Things I missed overall in this game were nitpicks:-Kicking down doors to stun and damage enemies was fun and satisfying, they removed it here-A couple of optional maps, such as the ruins maze, was removed-The entire container section was removed, now became a reference in one of the files. Hopefully in the DLC-Having the keychains is cool, gives a reason to play shooting range besides having fun but NOT when you can drop duplicates. I get it, stacking buffs is fun, makes for interesting gameplay, but c'mon i dont want to waste my gold coins and get a duplicate of a common thats just awful.-RIP Mecha Salazar :( (I loved the clock tower section tho, major improvent)---------SPOILERS ENDS HERE---------TL;DR;Overall this game is really fun specially for those coming to Resident Evil franchise this late in the run. Imrpoves a lot from the OG title and makes for a really immersive experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying the game!- This seems to be the first game in the series that offers a pseudo-open-world experience with an order of magnitude more freedom, and with more degrees of freedom. Although it also feels similar to the previous remakes, but more arcade while also complex.- I didn't get immersed into the story as much as I did with RE2, for example, but I played that on PS1 as a kid, so I'm biased here. It's not bad, however, just not that engaging: nothing explains to me why I should have stake in what is happening to the protagonist (except that it's the same one from RE2), or to the person he's protecting.- Shooting effects feel good and satisfying, but the mechanics are not realistic; still, the series never was that much about realism, because it's a Japanese fantasy world that is _similar_ to the real world.- I like that this seems to mock religious fanaticism, and sort of reminds me of my country of origin: "ссы в глаза, всё божъя роса"; those who know will understand. There quite a variety of guns in this game, and even different ammo types for some; although it seems totally possible to beat the game with just a handgun, provided there's enough ammo.- I liked the way the levels were crafted: although simple and mostly linear, they are full of secrets, and the beautifully lit interiors impress with their detail.- The villains could use more depth, but their character and concepts are quite varied and they appear to invoke the emotions one could expect in this context.- When I saw a killed enemy seize and then get up, I legit went "Whatthefff....." as I unleashed my then limited firepower onto them. Since then, my firepower has grown a couple orders of magnitude (as has the strength of my enemies), yet I still had the same reaction just now towards probably the end of the game, when a very strong and mostly immortal bullet sponge mini boss got up after I killed them, and transformed into a hellraiser version with another heart in their throat. And I had that reaction several times during the game. Breaking a cold sweat is a normal thing, but there's a lot of dopamine and joy in it.- This is my first playthrough, but with the things I have learned this run, I already can't wait to start again, but stronger, wiser, and wealthier. I don't know how good it will be really, but there seems to be at least some good potential for engaging replayability. If I understood the grading correctly, it's possible to beat the game in 4 hours, which seems challenging but I can see a few things I could already do to do it faster than my current ~30 hour run, where I try to find every treasure and buy every ticket.- There are some cool minigames.- The interface is much better, and still relatively simple with much more to display and do.The one thing that is still annoying me is: the video settings keep changing all the time on their own, every launch is different, and almost always in a bad way. Sometimes, even if window mode says Full Screen, it's still a bordered window, and that setting as well as refresh rate and maybe some others is locked. Sometimes, it changes the resolution to something else. Sometimes it runs at no more than 30 fps, and at other times I have to turn on VSync to prevent it from trying to reach 80.Another thing that was quite disappointing is that only some items can be stored in saferooms, and it's not the kind that you'll have a real lot of for a good part of the game. I can see how this pushes the player to buy inventory size upgrades, but they are cheap anyway, and it could simply be smaller. to begin with and then also scale proportionally.And, why, why is Crouch mapped to E, and the follower controls - to Ctrl???But seriously, great game, money well spent, eye candy, thrills, replayability. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This may be the best RE game to blend the action and survival horror elements perfectly. It surpasses the original in just about every way. With Separate Ways now released and the game fully complete, I can confidently say that this may very well be the best RE game in the series, although I still have a soft spot for RE2 and its remake. RE7 barely felt like an RE game to me, but RE2 Remake showed what classic RE would look like with that modern feel and I got excited again. But then RE3 Remake and RE8 came out and were just okay. But this game showed that Capcom really did just need the time to work out the right game mechanics to build a fun RE again. In an ideal world, we'd be able to get both survival horror and action RE games. I still hold out hope that a Code: Veronica Remake with the style and pacing of RE2 Remake eventually releases. But if RE9 and a possible RE5 Remake do release using this blend of action and survival horror, I'd still be more than satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: The remake and the original are comparable to the original Evil Dead movies and the newer movies that have come out in recent years. I feel like if you had a tutorial where Krauser had taught you some skills it would have helped his character have more importance in the story and it would have removed a lot of exposition from parts in the story where he appears. I also feel like another missed opportunity is not making more horrific moments with the plaga messing with Leon's mind. Again. these aren't *problems* with the game as the original didn't have these either and I still enjoy that game very much, but the remake had a chance to improve in those aspects and instead stayed the same.Overall, I recommend this but I do recommend playing the original first as you may enjoy that game as well, if not even more.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 4 was one of my favorite games for the PlayStation 2, and from what I have gathered over the few years it has since its release, is that I'm not the only one. So to say the least, Capcom had big shoes to fill is quite an understatement.Did they fill them? I'd say that's impossible, as the sixth-generation RE4 changed drastically the third-person genre and paved the way for some of the best games of all time. What this remake manages to do is reintroduce and reshape the old title into a new mold that is approachable to far more people with its much tighter and easily maneuverable controls, satisfying gunplay, and introduce new mechanics along the way, like the newly added parry which is fun to use and the unnecessary bad stealth that plagues nearly every triple-A game, which is a sin we all have to live with.A lot more has changed, not just the core gameplay, the story and characters are revamped to serve the different design directions which the majority of recent Resident Evils have undertaken. It is much more serious at its core, although some of its rather charming bits can be noticed to have remained from its original predecessor as part of a homage.The question I believe everyone has to ask is, are you looking for a modern take on Resident Evil 4 or are you looking to relive the impact Resident Evil 4 had on you when you first played it? Because the latter will never happen and that's okay. You'll always have the memories and that's where all the love lies.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I want to give some first impressions. I will update once complete if I feel it's needed. Putting it simply I think it's an amazing game. One of if not the best game of the Resident Evil revival (7 and onward). Combat is good. The initial worry some people had of it being too easy with a bit of extra mobility was very quickly fixed with the release of the demo and the full game proves this further. The enemies and their AI are perfectly tailored to match what you can bring to the table creating a very good balance. Not limiting the player to the point of frustration like 5, and not over the top control making it a complete action game like 6. Closer to 8 meets RE2make, which I guess makes sense. However, I'm not blind to the potential criticisms. It's a weird case. I feel every component of the game as a whole has 3 pieces to them. These permeate through everything; The weapons, the set pieces, the world, story, enemies, and so on.Again this is a first impressions, but it's leaving one hell of an impression.

_childDocuments_.review: What is a good remake?We all have probably wondered that at some point, specially after the many fiascos and cash grabs with remasters and remakes we've seen.The very word: Remake, has now become synonym for cash grab, for "we don't know what game to make so we'll reuse what worked in the past to make some money today".Yet, from time to time a company shows that it understands what made it's game what it was, that it understands what the players liked and what they didn't, and what the sequels taught them.Resident Evil 4 is, without a doubt, a good remake. It takes the original game and presents it with modern technology and game design, removes the dated things and implements modern gameplay mechanics, the story remains the same but with changes to the space between point A and point B, but with respect to the original material by making these changes feel like something that the original should've had instead of a "we added it simply because we wanted to change it for the sake of changing it".After 10 hours with the game, I can say that it's just as good as the original, and somehow even better. The graphics, art direction and level design are just as amazing as they were back in the day. Leon now can shoot and walk and the enemies were made to be more aggressive to match, the guns feel powerful and sound amazing (much better than in previous modern REs), the way the levels are expanded upon from the original game feel natural and not simply filing.Overall, a 10/10 as a Remake. Respectful of it's source material, and builds upon the strong pillars it created, if you liked the original then you'll like this, if you like RE7 and RE8, then you'll like it, if you liked the 2 Remake (let's forget about the 3rd...) then you'll like it.I hope Capcom remakes 5 and 6, and give them the change to become good RE games. R5 wasn't that far away from being great but it was held back by it's excessive focus on shooting, and RE6... well, they went all in with the action and forgot what a RE game is.

_childDocuments_.review: **Title: The Ada Wong Chronicles: A Quirky Analysis of Her Importance in Resident Evil 4 (2023) and Beyond!**Welcome, fellow gamers, horror aficionados, and Ada Wong fanatics, to the ultimate review extravaganza centered around Resident Evil 4 (2023)! Buckle up your bulletproof vests because we are about to dive deep into the picturesque terrors of rural Spain and unravel the enigma wrapped inside a red dress - that’s right, it's Ada Wong time!**A Glimpse into the Chaos**  Ah, the beauty of Resident Evil 4 (2023), where the only thing more elaborate than the plot twists is Leon Kennedy’s hair care routine. And while our boy Leon is out doing dramatic hero things (seriously, that hair flips when he kicks), Ada Wong glides through the shadows like a fabulous ninja in a sequined gown, reminding us all that looking good while fighting evil is indeed an art form.But why, you may ask, do I wax poetic over Ada Wong? Isn’t she just another femme fatale in a franchise overflowing with them? Well, let me tell you, dear reader, she’s not just *any* femme fatale; she’s the crème de la crème of mysterious, knowledgeable, and occasionally duplicitous characters—competition for Queen of the Gaudy Handgun notwithstanding. **The Clean-Up Crew in Heels**  In Resident Evil 4, Ada appears to be the ultimate multitasker—more versatile than a Swiss Army knife armed with a can of hairspray. She’s on a secret mission for an organization known as “The American Government” (or something like that), which, let’s face it, is as vague as Leon’s relationship status. While Leon is off rescuing the president’s daughter, Ada is out here picking up the pieces, playing both sides like a banjo in an off-key country song.What makes Ada’s role vital is that she embodies that everlasting tension in the game. Picture this: Leon is out there battling hordes of Ganados, thinking he’s the star of the show, while Ada is a closet diva, occasionally popping out like your weird neighbor who inexplicably has the ability to juggle flaming swords. She swoops in, provides critical intel and support, and leaves behind a trail of confusion as to whether she’s friend or foe.**Ladies and Gents, the Queen of Stealth**  Let’s take a moment to appreciate how Ada struts through danger like she's on a catwalk. While Leon fumbles with his shotgun like a clumsy toddler during a birthday party piñata, Ada gracefully takes down enemies with a nod and a wink—and probably a well-aimed silent shotgun blast. It’s not that Leon doesn’t know how to handle himself; it’s just that he’s doing it in frantically panicked bursts, whereas Ada is carrying the dual machine guns of coolness and cunning.As players, we often find ourselves reflecting on our fantasy selves, right? “If I were a video game character, what would I be?” Well, *I* would strut into villages with the finesse of Ada Wong, casually inspecting hidden treasures while simultaneously flirting with death… and maybe even Leon. **A Mystery Wrapped in Bondage Gear**  The alluring complexity of Ada’s character deepens her significance beyond the confines of Resident Evil 4. She raises the stakes—not only does she push Leon to make questionable decisions that lead him into truly precarious predicaments (thank you, Ada), but she also manages to challenge the male-dominated milieu that often saturates video games. Her character leads you to constantly question her motives—does she really care about Leon, or is it all just a ploy to peek behind the curtain of his overly stoic demeanor? Let's be honest, she’s the one giving Leon that much-needed character development. Ada challenges him not only with her sharp wit but also with her unpredictability. And as every relationship expert will tell you (Hi, Dr. Phil), unpredictable relationships keep life spicy—like adding hot sauce to your hot Cheetos! **The Power of the Dress**  Ada Wong’s iconic crimson dress—dear readers, it’s not just fabric; it’s a *statement*. It signifies danger, allure, and said “please don’t eat me, I’m fabulous” as she navigates through the chainsaw-wielding fiends and giant monsters. It’s this dichotomy of glamour and horror that embodies the essence of the franchise. And let’s face it, there’s nothing more scary than submitting to the scary reality that you collectively resemble the fashion sense of post-apocalyptic zombies while “Miss Wong” manages to strut out looking like she’s on the cover of Vogue. The power she exudes gives hope to every gamer who has ever played in sweatpants: one day, I too could look fierce while dodging a chainsaw!**Summary of Epic Proportions**  In conclusion, Ada Wong is not just a prominent character in Resident Evil 4 (2023); she’s the heartbeat behind the drama, the enigma wrapped in leather and sass, and a perennial mystery in the wild world of survival horror. Her allure is as intoxicating as the delightfully weird monsters chasing our beloved protagonists. She brings style, complex depth, and a much-needed sprinkle of drama to the narrative, making her significance to the game—and the franchise—absolutely paramount.So, the next time you find yourself fighting off hordes in Resident Evil 4 (2023), remember to appreciate the epitome of elegance and chaos that is Ada Wong—because in the world of survival horror, she’s here to save both Leon and your fashion sense! And who knows? You might find yourself turning into a bit of a smooth criminal with every playthrough. Now go on, suit up, and embrace your inner Ada Wong, minus the heart-stopping danger (please, for the love of all things good, minus that).

_childDocuments_.review: Technical production values are great. The setting is wonderfully created. Performance is great on 4090. It puts you into a setting where there are LOTS of enemies and if one of them notices you, it's extremely unlikely you'll survive. Looked online for a solution and there's a very specific place to go that is not obvious. If this is just the start of the game that puts you into impossible situations where the only way out is to save-scum, then this is not really a game. It's a save-scum where as soon as the villagers (see screenshots, that village) notice you, you MUST immediately load the previous auto-save. There's no point in doing the actual battle. Maybe one in two hundred chance of winning. That's a wild guess.   This is not a real game. It's a masochistic save-scum interactive movie that's presented very well.   Also the combat while on the surface seems well implemented, it's over the line in frustrating moments where what you want to happen and what actually happens are not the same. That makes combat tension artificial because the game forces you to be bad, except when the cut scene engages and suddenly you are an amazing combat soldier who can do moves you can't do otherwise. Yes the combat is frustrating. They show no fear at all, instead relentlessly moving towards you while your ammo runs out. The FOV os too narrow as well, on max FOV setting with my ultrawide screen. That makes combat also more difficult.Wait for a $10 sale play it for a few minutes then forget you have it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the original RE4. This was a faithful remake of the original. I was pleased that this wasnt just a 1 to 1 overhaul with improve graphics. The story is somewhat retconned and rewritten to make more sense and clear up plot holes from the original. The overall envoirment stays more of less the same, with some extra areas either added or replacing old ones. In short they kept the good things and improve on the bad ones from the original (some boss fights were reworked or nerfed to make it less annoying to play, for example the first El gigante was far easier to beat than in the orginial Re4, even on hardcore difficulty). Overall bossfights are less tidious but the difficulty dealing with ordinary enemies has gone up. The game employs a physics system adding delay and weight to your movements. This is annoying but also lends to the survival aspect of the game. This can lead to frankly unfair situations where Leon is simply stunlocked untill you die, as you have to wait for Leon's wrighting animation to finish before you can access your briefcase and heal.There is a high risk of softlocking yourself in the game, especially in the later stages on the island and halfway through the castle, as ammo and healing are very sparce. For whatever reason they didnt rework the part of the game where ashley needs to turn two cranks inorder to raise a bridge. You HAVE to use ranged weapons inorder to defend her, of which there are very few ammo. This was a problem in the orignial as well and i feel like they should have somehow reworked this part. Even with the bolt thrower you run out of ammo, and the bolt thrower is woefully inept at taking on several enemies at once.My biggest grievence with the remake is by far the voice actors. Aside form Leon and Ashley all of the voice actors are worse compared to the original RE4, ESPECIALLY ADA WONG! Ada sounds like she has a flue constantly and the voice actor puts in NO effort! Do better CAPCOM!Overall a good game, 8/10, not worth buying at fullprice, but if you can get it for below 30 euros definetly go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: What have they done to my boy? Words cannot begin to describe my overall disappointment what they have done to my favorite video game ever, but as they are the only medium in which a human can express anything i will deign to try.Lets start with Tone, the tone of this game is completely all over the place, the one line left in about bingo is all that remains from the first game. The game takes itself so very seriously now, everything is gritty, darker, "realistic" with leon being the worst offender, whereas before he was hyper competent goofball, now leon is a void of a personality, i would go as far as to say that there is no personality left for Leon to fill other than uber serious cop guy. Ironic that if this version of leon was the one presented on PS2 there would probably be zero love for the character at all. because while re4 remake leon "completes" alot of the same events as the original he does so with absolutely zero style, zero charm no stupid quips or absurd humor, whereas the the original RE4 leon would be running away from a giant mech of the antagonist, narrowly escape with his life before turning around and delivering the cheesiest line possible. Leon in RE4 felt like a charcter who belonged in the absurdity that surrounded him, and him being completely unfazed by everything thrown at him made him the memorable character he is today. This is the whole reason that the game was remade in the first place to capitalize on nostalgia for a vastly superior game. Capcom sanded Leon down to perfectly average video game protagonist #78.I have to ask who is this for? New players aren't going to remember this version of leon, he's a wet noodle with no charm.But aside from our leading Man, the world has changed alot too, someone at capcom went down the list and struck off every set piece that they deemed too goofy and in the process contributed to making re4 significantly less memorable. the boulder run in the village, the lava room, the bulldozer, the speeding car, mecha salazar, the spike room, the laser room, cable car sniping, and so many more. Its these critical moments where i kept asking myself surely this will be in the game right? No it will not, without all of these amazing varied set pieces the game feels less like RE4 and more like another bland third person shooter that apes the combat mechanics and nothing else. By removing these set pieces capcom has effectively removed the soul of the game.Okay So what do we get in return?They put durability on the knife (why?)because there is a parry (why?)because all of the cool game have parrying (how will you balance it?)Your knife breaks and you have to pay to get it fixed or you can't use it. (WHHHYYY)Parrying is honestly a cheapo trick they coudn't figure out how to balance in the RE4 sandbox without a band aid fix. Most of the time my knife was broken while playing, in the original it was a really poor fallback option baked into your kit that could be used to escape some tight situations.In this game parrying is at the core of a lot of encounters and those moments where you are without your knife you are basically playing original RE4 at that point anyway, running to avoid attacks and not being able to block.There had to be a better way to balance this, i had to have spent 10% of my run's currency on the damn knife repairs.Then we have sidequests, which are literally the most boring copy paste objectives ever. Remember the blue medallions in the first game? Get ready to do that 6 more times across different areas of the game, or kill 3 rats in different hallways or areas, or fight a slightly powered up version of a normal enemy, no thank you.This game fails to capture the originals charm in almost every conceivable way, this at the end of the day was product created with money in mind. All of the removed content has been supplanted with non-memorable generic third person shooter drivel.I'm so very disappointed to say that no one will talking about this game in 20 years, I can't even tell you what happened in the castle in this game as i literally cannot picture it. This game will not create ravenous fans the way the first did because it lacks the originals energy and charm.The Gameplay is the only thing that has "improved" and even that is debatable.What a waste, i could easily see people playing this and not understanding what all of the hype about the original was.

_childDocuments_.review: Of the Resident Evil games that I have played (RE2R, RE3R, this one, RE7 and RE8), I think that Resident Evil 4 Remake is probably my favorite of the bunch. I have not played the original version of this game, so I can't give you a comparison of the two, but I can say as a first-time player that this game was an absolute blast. It isn't as tuned into the horror aspect as RE2R, RE7 or RE8 were, but the action is more satisfying in this game than in any of those other titles.The campy fun which the series did so well in Village is present here as well, since the story is a bunch of nonsense and the game seems to be aware of that. Leon is such a good protagonist for this sort of story, since he's both no-nonsense while also being open and willing to crack jokes about the strange situation he's found himself in. He gives off the goofy everyman vibes that Ethan Winters did while simultaneously being essentially a cartoon superhero at times with his acrobatics and strength and such. Also, for a game-spanning escort mission character, I really liked Ashley. I thought she and Leon had good chemistry with one another, and Ashley even had a nice little arc about becoming more confident in herself. Difficulty-wise, this game is definitely not easy, but it is very fair. You're going to have to manage your inventory like every Resident Evil game, but you likely won't ever be short on ammo or other weaponry. The game encourages you to fight back and to fight back hard. Enemies will do a good amount of damage to you if you're not careful, but you can dish it right back to them in kind. The boss fights were pretty good (outside of the big lake fish one), none of them too similar to one another to feel boring. If you have played a game in this series before, you should give this one a try. Even if you haven't played a game in this series before, I would still recommend this game to you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is single handedly what the entire Resident Evil series has been working up to. I love this franchise I have enjoyed every game that I've booted up (Mainline) from RE. RE5 came up a little short and RE6 was shaky but both I think are serviceable titles even if nowhere near the best the series has to offer. But after recently beating RE4 original I came into this with high expectations and wondering how they would handle the campiness and cheesiness and downright silly undertones of the original and where they would take RE4 in the remake. I am not the biggest fan of the overly cheesiness and 80s action movie style as that's not what attracts me to the franchise so I was ecstatic to see that they decided to take it to a more serious and darker tone a standard set by newer titles (Biohazard, Village)Well they took a diamond and polished it even further. Everything in this game looks stunning, every cutscene in Resident Evil since 2017 has been stellar but RE4 remake is easily the most jaw dropping the graphics have been yet. As for the gameplay they took the weaker spots in the original and managed to make them some of my favorites. The island as most can agree was the most controversial section in RE4 but they handled it extremely well  without removing content they just slightly tweaked it and made it very fun and enjoyable as well as making sure it did not overstay its welcome. Salazar in the original I found a little boring and thought his design was a little underwhelming but how creepy he was in the remake and how they remade his boss fight was another instance how this game made RE4 even better. My all time favorite fight in RE4 Krauser, was handled so well and felt intense the entire 20 minutes it lasted. My least favorite fight in the original the 2 Gigantes was made much easier since you could just drop them both in the lava unlike the OG where you just pour bullets into them. Ashley now not having a seperate health bar is also a huge plus. Escort missions will always be tedious yet they are less so in this remake. This is easily my GOTY and I don't think that will change. This isn't just the best Resident Evil game I played but the best game I've played EVER.  Truly as close as I've played to a 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: For the AAA game buyer and enjoyer with a surface level depth into games, (shallow formulaic games like TLoU) they'll probably love this remake, but as someone with over a couple hundred hours played in the original who liked the core gameplay mechanics and combat, this remake is awful.Leon moves slow and running in during an opening for a melee attack prompt takes way longer. Putting enemies in that "open for a melee attack" staggered state is way less consistent and it feels like a shorter window, made worse with Leon's slow speed. On top of that it will take 1 head shot or up to 5, and its totally random, and I've had a few of my melees totally whiff and go through the enemy like air, leaving me open to get my health drained in hardcore mode. Its very common for explosions to not interrupt a zombie as it has you grabbed. I've had grenades totally disappear if I was grabbed mid-throw, even as I watched my nade fall to the floor at the zombie's feet. I've had the game crash to desktop over 8 times with modern hardware, even when not exceeding my max VRAM. The knife durability disincentivizes the original games really fun melee focus for those who got really familiar with the gameplay in professional mode, tho upgrading it's durability makes it less bad, but still worse than RE4 2005. Repairing and upgrading it to be useful drains your money supply for other weapon upgrades all playthrough. Also the QTE's to avoid boss mechanics are either removed entirely or don't work as consistently as the original game as well. Salazar is an awful boss fight I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy, tho there are cheese strats online for it. Since staggering him will take between 1 shot and 5 shots to his weak spot, just pray the game chooses to be nice cuz its just luck at that point, and bad gameplay.I replayed RE4 2005 and immediately I was reminded how that game encouraged frantic fun gameplay with enemy stuns with head or leg shots to follow up with melee and knife attacks, taking 1 shot to put them in their staggered state and with Leon not running as if he's 300 lbs and running through tar. It was a fun action game with fun gameplay, like Godhand with guns. RE4 remake is a very polished, bog standard modern game that is totally unnecessary for people who like the deeper gameplay of the original. Having fully collected my thoughts since I wrote this a week ago, the old game was very rigid but expertly designed in its combat gameplay, making mastering the rules it set extremely rewarding and fun. It was peak PS2 era gaming with tight controls and satisfying mechanics. A great Japanese-made classic that felt unique and purposeful. In the remake though, you have to worry about all these different random elements that shouldn't even be there. Will this shot stagger, or is the game gonna want 3 more bullets this time randomly? Can I make it to the enemy to kick in time, or is the new sadistic AI gonna make zombies interrupt me as i slowly shamble to the staggered guy, essentially pushing Leon forward through all this moddern, muddy inertia BS making me run at a snails pace. I would really like to knife this guy but the knife is just gonna break in half if I use it so I better just run away and make space and use my gun, even though that's way less fun. I have the ability to shoot this guy in the head, i could have in 2005, but the new forced weapon sway realism might screw me, like other modern games force in at the cost of fun. The remake is just more modern trash with hints of OG RE4 sprinkled in that are too marred by modern and generic trends.

"no thanks bro" "little rough don't you think?" and so on, some of the changes left me a little sad like Luis first line in the game Leon going "women…" as Ada leaves the boat and so many others left me saying "aww come on man I loved that line" but it is not something I would say ruins the game, the voice acting in the game is very good, I still prefer the OG voices over the remake, but there were some voices that really did not make it for me, Ada as many people have said had a really bland delivery to her lines, and for me the Krauser voice actor did not feel nearly as good as the old one, I do not think he did a bad job, not at all he did great I just love the OG Krauser, while I'm at the topic of Krauser I liked the first knife fight, I think they did a good job making a cutscene as iconic as that one playable, but then at the same time that cutscene is so iconic and the dialog is so embedded into my brain that when I saw it changed it left me kind of sad.Other than that I thought the requirements for S+ in professional were a little arbitrary like the number of saves and no checkpoints, it felt like a chore to have to use limited save points and repeat some chapters due to not having checkpoints while trying to leave some saves for hard parts of the game or for the endgame.I believe those would be it, now for the things I liked more in this game, I think that the boss fight themes are better in this one, the OGs are great, but it felt really intense replaying those boss fights in a new way with the new tracks, Ashley overall is better here, not having her life bar to worry about, her being able to make jumps go down ladders and the possibility of stabbing the guy carrying her in the neck for a one-shot made me appreciate this Ashley more than the old one.With that said I think this was a great and refreshing take on and old classic like re4, none is better or worse than the other, they are just different, and I love them both equally even if remake went for a more serious vibe and left some content out it did a great job on everything As stated before I could go on and on, so I'm leaving it at great job easy 10/10 in my book.I loved when Leon said it's residenting time and killed all spanish people.

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥' amazing. They managed to re-capture the core, the essence of the original RE4. The story elements are mostly kept the same, minus no laser scene and some small parts cut out and replaced with other parts (QTE's are still there, just not in cutscenes but rather in the gameplay) the game is still very much RE4. I wasn't a huge fan of requests, they're pretty much side challenges/quests but they always give you a chunk of them at the very end of the area, meaning you need to backtrack through the entire ♥♥♥♥♥♥' level to get to it. A bit more care could've been given, but hey it wasn't in the original game so it's still a plus.I think there's more weapons than the original, more upgrade options, the firing range minigame was pretty fun (good luck to you plebs playing on a controller, you're gonna have a swell time with that one), graphics are superb minus the fact that RAY TRACING CAUSES YOUR GAME TO CRASH FREQUENTLY which is dumb so I couldn't play with ray-tracing unless I was prepared to crash every ~15-30 minutes. There was a point where I crashed about 7 or 8 times in quick succession (this is the point where I gave up and disabled ray tracing if you didn't know). It's amazing, the nostalgia, all of it just flooding back to me was an insanely euphoric feeling. That being said, even if you have no nostalgia/have not played the original RE4 either back in the day or before RE4 Remake you'll still very much enjoy this game. The story is kind of a continuation from RE2, it's not necessary to play the original but I'd still recommend it just so you're relatively familiar with the characters. There is definitely extra content missing (Mercenaries, Separate Ways/Ada stuff etc.) so lets hope Capcom will add them without making us pay a fortune. Other than that there's not much else I can really say, I'm kinda speechless. Buy it and play it yourself if you wanna know how great this game is, but for me it's as perfect as an RE4 remake could be. I was a bit scared since the RE3 Remake (Tons of cuts, no added content, full priced game, story was quite short) but hey, looks like they've definitely learned from that nightmare (pun intended).

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 4 remake is an astonishing game that does justice to the original. Despite the content cuts, the level structure and presentation are still excellent, and the gameplay is simply breathtaking. The graphics are great, and the game runs smoothly on both high-end and mid-range machines, unlike some other remakes (looking at you The Last of Us Part 1 PC)Most of the new voice actors in the game do an excellent job, but the voice actor for Ada Wong is a bit lackluster. However, I'm hoping that the upcoming DLC "Separate Ways" will redeem her character. The developers added so many details that show how much they care about this remake. The smart player's discovery of ways to skip some sections or boss battles is a testament to the game's depth.The game mechanics have been tweaked to make Leon more responsive, and the addition of new abilities, such as parrying attacks and stealth kills, adds a new level of excitement to the gameplay. These changes make the game feel like a brand new game rather than just a remake.I've already completed the game twice and doing my third playthrough now - also eagerly awaiting the release of the Mercenaries DLC this weekend. If you're a fan of the old games or want to know why Resident Evil 4 is one of the best games ever, you must play this remake. It's a game that shows how much care and attention the developers put into it, and it's a must-play for anyone who loves survival horror.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very aggravating game.  There are a lot of rough edges making for an overall rocky experience, especially if you like to challenge yourself on the higher difficulties.  Having played many versions of the original RE4, there are a lot of improvements (the game looks fantastic, larger emphasis on horror, vastly more engaging castle, more cohesive themes, better characterization of Ashley and the Leon/Ashley relationship).  I also feel like there are some major roadbumps to being a fantastic game (poor checkpointing, many more sequences requiring cutscenes to trigger events you have little way of preparing for on your terms, too much grappling from enemies and animation-locked attacks making you sit and watch some sequence for a few seconds each time you take a hit).I think the combat is pretty good.  Stealth is buggy so if an enemy takes any damage while you are stealthed (such as walking into a bear trap THEY placed), you lose your stealth.  I think removal of laser sites from most guns, instead putting the emphasis on reticle bloom takes away the ability for certain players to master recoil control.  A few weapons are graced with the laser site, but my favorite weapon the Red9 is not.  They've also made melee a far more integral component, with the ability to parry and dodge attacks.  I like the parry, but the dodge is trash.  Dodging is only available when prompted by certain enemy attacks.  It is challenging to know what attacks can be dodged or parried or neither.  I would like dodging if it were more like Dark Souls, something you can always do which provides i-frames as protection, though the game would probably be way too easy and way too mobile.  Thus I would then prefer dodging was removed entirely. It's overall okay.  If you liked Doom Eternal you'll probably like this: both made you buy into their updated combat loop.  You also might like the game playing on easier difficulties where a lot of the roadbumps are far less noticable.  On a side note, a mod that vastly improves the game is the manual flashlight mod on Nexus.  You have a flashlight, but Leon only pulls it out when Leon cannot see.  I am not Leon.  I like my horror games dark, but I like the ability to see when I cannot via an in-game mechanic versus cranking up the brightness.

_childDocuments_.review: May contain spoilersTL: DR - Never in my adult life has a video game genuinely brought me back to my childhood in such a way. If you enjoyed the 2005 release, you'll surely love this one.I've already played the hell out of this game and have beaten it both on Hardcore and Professional, and I have quite a lot to say.  I'll make it easy and break this up into sections. (Also S ranked all shooting gallery stages!)Difficulty - Off the bat, I want to say Resident Evil 4 has struck a good balance on Hardcore (at least for me) when it comes to difficulty. Capcom has almost regressed and moved back to the original Resident Evil format with how scarce resources can be. Resident Evil 4 leaves the player constantly weighing their options in fights and picking their battles wisely. Most importantly Hardcore is fair to the player and typically gives them enough to survive assuming they don't waste it. It's the perfect difficulty to play the game in my opinion.Now we get to Pro which is functionally nothing like Hardcore. This mode limits you to ONLY typewriter saves, perfect parries, near instant death, little to no resources, and makes the final 2 bosses absolutely insane to fight. Like the original game, your Pro runs will be GREATLY affected by RNG, and some areas can be literally impossible on Professional. An example is the infamous water room where you can soft lock yourself with no ammo or crafting materials. Professional mode ramps everything up to 12 and is ridiculously hard in some areas. It definitely doesn't feel as fair as it did in the original, and it makes a point to show you just how unfair it can be. However, even though Pro is much harder it is still a fun experience. (Excluding Novis...they're absolutely not fun at all on Pro.) Enemies can be quite a challenge to take down and it can be very frustrating in some situations. Especially when they eat 3 shotgun shells point blank and don't die. One section of the game in particular where you're holding off waves of enemies is extremely tough on both Pro and HC. Ganados typically take upwards of 4 headshots to stun reliably on Pro and so close quarters fighting is often an extreme RNG gamble. Grapples are also extremely rough as a single Ganado can remove 95% of your HP with one grab. This leads to you being wombo-combo'd quite often.AI - Enemy AI in this game is actually somewhat nuts. Every enemy type in the game fights in a unique style and will flank you, grapple you for other enemies to hit you, set up traps, and even feint their attacks to keep you guessing. They're incredibly good at catching you off guard and on Professional they can be ruthless when it comes to setting up sandwiches.(Looking at you Water Room Ganados.)Gameplay - Here's where I have some issues. The biggest issue I have with RE4 remake is the bloom found on most handguns that aren't compatible with the laser. The bloom found on most weapons is awful. It makes some weapons like the TMP absolutely worthless outside of 5 feet and shooting gallery stages horrible to complete. You will often find yourself fighting the guns more than the enemies. Movement is also a big factor for some people with a lot of people saying it's too "weighty." Personally, I like this change but to each their own. Bosses- Bosses have been massively improved and majority of them no longer stand in one spot. They all typically have a unique mechanic that you have to be aware of when fighting and it makes them much more interesting. That being said....late game bosses in particular on Pro are absolutely maddening. Ashley - Ashley has been massively improved and is genuinely a like-able and fun character to be around. She's also surprisingly helpful in later stages of the game and is much more capable than she used to be. Her not being able to stay like in the original game though is somewhat frustrating as you have to juggle her position alongside enemies. Overall though? She's a massive improvement and is very enjoyable in this game with her quips and dialogue.Story - The story of RE4 is much more fleshed out with more in-depth documents and lore scattered throughout all the areas. You'll find more lore on the big bads, their families, minor characters, and others who were previously not in the games or not as pronounced. Overall, the story is solid and does a good job.Visuals - Playing the game at 1440 (4K for half the game but rip that monitor) Ultra is an absolute joy. The games fidelity is crazy and this game pushes the absolute limit of the RE engine in some aspects. Graphics are a definite 10/10. On a 2080, I7-9700K, and 32 Gigs of ram the game ran great with very few hiccups. Controversial takes - Voice acting overall is great... but Ada's voice actor does not fit the character. She almost sounds like Jennifer Tilly. Another issue I have with the game is how some scripted events happen. In some instances enemies will teleport directly to Ashley in an attempt to capture her even though you've cleared out every enemy that was en-route to her. Removed/Cut Content - This might be my most controversial take. Personally, I feel like the content that was removed from the MAIN game was for the better. I know some people were not happy about the removal of a certain boss-fight and areas but it genuinely made the game flow much better. A big complaint of the old RE4 was that it was too drawn out, and some areas, namely the island, were just a slog to get through. Excluding Mercs, (Which we get later)I definitely think not having Assignment Ada or Seperate Ways at launch was a bad move by Capcom especially with the game being $70+ in some areas. Granted, it will most likely be sold as DLC but it should have come with the game. Overall, the game is a solid 9.5/10.  Personally, I just cannot get past the removed bonus campaigns when they added so much to the game.
