_childDocuments_.review: This game is an 8/10 for the first half of the game and a 5/10 for the second half.Truly a remake for fans who praise the original despite so so so many problems. For every improvement, there is something they've doubled down on that was in desperate need of changing. If you think you'll like this because you enjoyed RE2R, RE3R, RE7 and Village like I did, you won't. It shares almost no qualities with those games other than the sluggish movement and bad controls. I have lost track of the amount of times I've taken damage due to input delay and missed button prompts. Despite being able to literally take baddies to suplex city, Leon handles like he's got buckets filled with concrete attached to both feet. You either stagger enemies at a safe distance and fail to reach them to melee because of how slow he is or you risk it all and let them get as close as possible.Cringe tier writing. Leon acts like a complete moron for no other reason than to serve the plot. Enjoy the cyclical nature of rescuing ashley, dealing with an escort mission for a chapter (WHY IS THERE FRIENDLY FIRE IN A GAME LIKE THIS), just to lose her to the enemy. Rinse and repeat. Every character has a massive yapping problem in this too, and Leon has a tourretes-like tendency to quip regardless of whether the situation calls for it or not.Boss battles are painfully easy and gimicky as hell. Painfully cliched. If I had a nickel for every time they pulled the you-thought-you-killed-the-boss-but-no-wait-there's-more stunt I'd have 0.05 x how ever many forgettable bosses there are in this game.Gee I wonder why RE5 and RE6 went such a bad way....

_childDocuments_.review: “This time… it can be different.”RE3. That’s what I would’ve said if you asked me my favorite RE game before this. The original 3rd game has always been my favorite. But now? I think it’s RE4make. I love the original 4, but this surpasses it in nearly every way for me. It’s engaging, changes the story in good ways, along with characters. The fact that Leon has much more of an actual arc over the game is great, he becomes less brooding as it goes on as he finally does what he never could in Raccoon City: save someone. Marvin died on him, and so did everyone else with him, and he believed Ada to be dead. Claire managed to rescue Sherry on her own, he didn’t have anything to do with it. He just lost people. Now he changes that, and you can see it in his attitude in the final cutscene. I love Ashley and Leon’s relationship in this version, they play off each other really well and I’d love to see Ash return again in another game. Gameplay wise it’s amazing. RE2make but much more action focused, even more so than 3make. The new parry system is one of the best implementations in the series, giving thrilling encounters and ways to defend, and ways to escape, while a choice in every situation with it. Waste some durability for protection and lose a chance to attack or just take the hit? This along with the much harder to find ammo in the last half makes it much more intense, especially on hardcore. Ashley is fine, as I believe she’s always been in combat. The new command system does help a bit, keeping her from danger easier and she doesn’t have a health bar which gets rid of an extra worry that was in the original, instead she gets incapacitated if hit and you have to pick her up before she’s hit again. It’s a good change that still has you watch her, but it’s not as stressful with healing items.Your first playthrough will be long. But from there it will be shorter as you memorize more and more and get more used to combat. Can’t recommend it enough, have very few complaints

_childDocuments_.review: TO THE HELL GREEN MAN GAMING, I lost the pre load. Dear CAPCOM, Please develop Resident Evil: Code Veronica (Remake), Dino Crisis (Remake) please, for the love of god. Ashley you can sit on my face whenever you want and as long as you want. I was looking forward to playing this game, since the trailers were a success, I hope they don't do the same thing with resident evil 3, because there they killed a lot of the content. I hope Capcom doesn't screw up that wonderful game.Resident Evil 4 Remake, called by Capcom only Resident Evil 4, is extremely faithful to the 2005 classic. There are identical camera angles in some cinematic scenes, very familiar scenarios and enemies both traditional and new.Overall, it's very likely that our favorite bits from the original Resident Evil 4 are exactly the same as the new version.First of all, it should be noted the already expected improvement in gameplay, Leon seems to have the same gameplay as resident evil 2 which I really liked.There is no shortage of headshot and kick to the face combos. Leg shot and wrestling strike. As the demo already indicated, our favorite special agent has, in fact, become John Wick himself.By the way, don't think that Resident Evil 4 Remake is far from being a horror game, as many fans said about the original. Darker from the beginning, the new version managed to balance the most intense action with memorable scares and an atmosphere that doesn't take so long to become worthy of what we call horror.Whether for the decoration of the scenarios, with bones and signs of sacrifices scattered everywhere, or for the resistance of specific enemies, such as the chainsaw, many will be the moments in which players will despair and will not know how to choose between combat and escape and I think I'm going to ♥♥♥♥ myself when I see Regenerator.The number of enemies in the scenarios contributes to increasing the tension. There are situations in which Leon needs to deal with dozens of Ganados, some of which transform before dying, and the ideal is to be able to eliminate the maximum number of enemies while losing the minimum amount of ammunition — even though there is much more ammunition available than in other games of the series.Realize that almost everything that has been said so far also exists in the original Resident Evil 4, with the difference that the horror dosage is now greater. It doesn't matter if martial arts shooting and striking combinations have become more frequent. The game's tone is still arguably suited to what's expected from the series.I couldn't fail to mention the immeasurable improvement in the way characters interact with each other. Ashley specifically is much more active in this new version and there are more conversations between her and Leon or even between Leon and other characters.I think there will be huge nostalgia and one of the most memorable knife battles between Leon and Jack Krauser, it won't just be in the cutscene, but we will be able to move and fight.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review written after completing the game multiple times and tackling most in-game challenges.This contains no major spoilers, just minor ones that are marked as such.The gunplay is satisfying and feels much better than in previous recent entries. The animation work of the player has weight to it, with every shot not sounding like a pea shooter anymore, while the enemies have varied responses upon impact ranging from gore decals, staggers to even dismemberment. Weapon recoil drives the point home, but also requires getting used to.The burning desire to know about the game's duration and the amount of retained content is likely going to be an unavoidable topic, so I'm going to mention that I've spent 28 hours during my first playthrough on Standard difficulty. That's thorough exploration with all the treasures, challenge completion, with occasional restarts and whatnot. If you're going in without guides, then you're likely to get similar times, granted I did do some sightseeing during the scenic parts.The game has been re-imagined, so familiar areas are likely to have entirely different layouts and connect in unexpected ways. The nonsensical filler parts have been merged into other areas, some segments are expanded, and the progression is made slightly more linear so that constant tiresome backtracking is not a necessity. Speaking of tiresome, the challenging areas are still present, but feel less of a chore to get through, and this kind of design philosophy is applied throughout the whole game. There is occasional objective branching that can be tackled in any order, along with optional surprises and treasure hunt, in case I made it sound too linear.Throwing Ashley into a dumpster is no longer a necessity anymore, because not only there are no empty dumpsters around, but the Remake Ashley ain't a bratty damsel in distress to begin with.Ashley is more versatile and can actively avoid enemies to a degree. It's up to you if you want her to follow you closely or try avoiding the battle. The latter is not a magic bullet, as corridors and lots of enemies can still corner her.It's not possible to accidentally harm other characters outside of battles, but that doesn't mean that you can be careless. The system reminds me of Revelations 2, because when she receives damage, it incapacitates and requires you to pick her up again. That doesn't mean that you can throw grenades or use piercing guns through her, though, as strong attacks like that will cause an immediate game over.The player animation system is placed somewhere in between being responsive and preferring animations to inputs. Actions have momentum and velocity to them, even bringing your gun up takes time, so some players might call these controls "heavy". Contrary to that, the parry system is immediate and can be initiated even from an aiming stance. It's a concept similar to Resident Evil 6, where pressing action right before being hit executes a devastating counter-attack, but rather than doing damage, a perfect parry staggers an enemy and a more loose-timed parry is essentially a block. It'll take time to figure out and master parrying, since the timing window varies per each attack, but on regular difficulties it's possible to mash the button with only a slight possibility of it not working. After a couple of playthroughs you're likely to develop muscle memory for it and start using it without thinking.There are a few notable ways of avoiding enemy attacks: attacking in hopes to cancel or stagger, parrying, running away, ducking, and dodging.Evasion by ducking was the most difficult tactic to master, as enemy grabs cannot be parried, a charging enemy can really catch you off guard if you're not prepared or used to it, especially since ducking takes time, and you cannot attack from this position.Climbing animations are no longer the go-to cheese strategy, as in RE4R the enemies are no longer shy to Sparta kick you down the ladder, thus causing some unintentional comedy in my case. Well, not literal Sparta kicks, but gone are the days of safe ladders against bosses, and it's best to make sure that your destination won't greet you with force.My issue with the parry system is that pressing it almost during impact is a bit too late, and there were times when I felt that my perfect parry input was "eaten" by the game. Because of that, I think RE6's counter system is more snappy.The same button that is used for ducking is also your dedicated dodge button, a direct replacement for the QTEs that appeared during very specific enemy attacks. My biggest gripe with the dodging is that certain player actions, like being in the middle of a knife slash, prevent dodging altogether, and even though there's a prompt for it and the button is pressed, absolutely nothing happens, and you get obliterated by the attack, which is definitely bound to cause frustration. I think that a dodging prompt should take priority no matter what the player is currently doing.Uncertainty is a great element of horror, something that I really like about the original Resident Evil. RE4R, on the other hand, tries real hard to over-explain absolutely everything that is happening in the game. The documents scattered throughout the game give little to no headroom for any speculation or headcanon. It's definitely exciting to have more backstory, but the amount and placement of it could have been better.Aiming for the highest ranking rewards, but don't vibe with rushing through the whole game? Sucks to be you, 'cause the time limits here are worse than in RE2R. Be prepared to run past enemies, skip all side events, and not bother with some of the items or treasures. Best part? You can't use a New Game+ save, so no upgraded gear to help you rip through enemies faster.Not only the rewards of the shooting range have changed, but so did the range itself. More challenges, more gun variety and if you're going for a perfect round, the difficulty is likely going to frustrate. The courses are designed to be tackled in a very particular pattern, with little wiggle room to begin with. Trial and error it is, with the added variable of your weapons having randomized bullet spread, a few gotchas of hidden bonuses, fast-disappearing targets and now the original shooting range looks like a walk in the park. However, if you're going "just" for completion, then you're not required to do perfect rounds, as achieving S rank is enough. It's impossible to get all the rewards within one playthrough and, luckily, collecting all of them is not necessary for completion anyway.Good stability, no crashes, adequate performance even on an GTX1070, considering the visuals the game is pushing.FSR2 is recommended, you can push most settings mid-high with 1080p60 in most areas, while there's only two notable areas that go below 60 throughout the whole game.Sadly, there seems to be traversal stutter.I like Resident Evil 4 Remake because it refined the parts of the original that aged the worst. The combat is on par with the best action-oriented survival horror titles, the QTEs are eradicated, Ashley is better than ever, the presentation is more down to earth, tedious sections have been appropriately handled, all that while this being the longest RE Remake title by far.The duration should satisfy anyone who was concerned about it to begin with, and the game remains fresh throughout thanks to the location variety. The ranking system is one of the few things that could have been better, as not everyone wants to be forced in that kind of play style.In the end, most of the game is preserved and feels complete.Review copy provided by Capcom Co., Ltd.

_childDocuments_.review: A stellar remake of an already stellar game. They’ve really nailed it on the head with this one. Not only with the changes they’ve introduced, but also the content they’ve cut. It’s a lot more streamlined. It makes more sense from a design perspective. It’s just generally tighter and smoother of an experience, without sacrificing any of the bravado that made the original game so good.I absolutely love it. I don’t think it surpasses the Resident Evil 2 remake -- that one holds a very special place in my heart. And despite all the new shiny bits, the sense of “first love” isn’t there for me either. I suspect because I already had that going into the first game, all those years ago.But who cares, right? I mean, you can’t go wrong with this one. _childDocuments_.review: If you have played the original game all those years ago and even remotely enjoyed it, this is a must buy! I very much enjoyed the similar but new level design, it is more cohesive and makes sense now compared to the original. The enemies are no longer pushovers with their upgraded AI, and they cannot be rolled over instantly all the time either, which is a welcome change.There is not much I could think of if I had to think of flaws... they would probably be minor nitpicks but what game doesn't have those? In my opinion, a game can be a 10/10 and still have things wrong with it. And this game deserves a 10/10 for sure. Super enjoyable to play, the replay value is very high with all the customization. If you enjoy survival horror, this is one of the best new games I have played in a long time, and that is saying something.

_childDocuments_.review: The 2023 remake of Resident Evil 4 will go down as one of the best remakes of all time.Granted, it helps that the original version is both readily available and already one of the most influential games ever made, but even so - the team at Capcom looked at every encounter and mechanic, then did as much as possible with said encounters and mechanics. It's amazing that none of these expansions feel bloated or drag the pacing down, but they don't - while the 2004 original sometimes felt like the developers were so excited to move from one idea to the next, the 2023 version looks at all of those ideas and tries to figure out how to use them in new ways.RE4 2023 does stand on its own, though - the updated gameplay of the RE2 & 3 remakes, combined with a few well-implemented mechanics, provide extra layers of depth to account for the increased focus on action and combat. It would have been easy (in big air quotes) for the developers to simply drop RE2 Leon into new maps, but they didn't - instead, they made meaningful changes that feel appropriate to the kind of game RE4 is.And now that Separate Ways is available, the few moments of "aw, I wish they had brought that back" are a thing of the past. Ada's campaign is improved in all ways except voice acting - the mix of returning areas from the 2004 version, remixed areas of the main campaign and entirely new stuff makes for a great little addition. At $10 for the expansion, it's well worth taking a look at...even if Ada's voice actor sounds like they're either about to fall asleep or just waking up from a nap.Buy Resident Evil 4. It's one of the few games in existence that was pretty much perfect...twice!

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 4 Remake: A Master Class in Game design.	Resident Evil 4 Remake is a theme park populated by all the classic horror movie monsters that we all know and love. One second you are exploring the decrepit rooms of the village. Next you are running for dear life down the corridors of a castle straight out of Castlevania. If Resident Evil 4 has anything.  It has variety. Moment to moment gameplay feels good due to the host of players options available. The ability to sprint, couching, and mantling seamlessly over obstacles what you would expect a Super agent to do so. Switching from melee attacks to firearms without so much a hitch is so gratifying. Now only if this knife would not break. Many, if not all combat scenarios, can be tackled in various ways. Observant players will spot opportunities for stealth kills, shoot an explosive, or lure enemies to a trap. Mix in the upgrade systems, passive skills, and multiply loadout possibilities makes it feels like a game from the minds of From Software, but with that Capcom panache for insanely fun action.	For a game about bloody chainsaw maniacs and terrifying monsters it surely has a lot of charm laying around. Take everybody’s favorite Weapon merchant. Everytime he speaks it is an absolute treat. “What are you buying stranger.” Will never get old. We have the scene-stealing Luis. He was plucked from a Saturday morning cartoon with the cringiest one liners to slapstick humor. Then, there are the enemies of Resident Evil 4 themselves. My favorite boss fight in the game is with a towering monstrosity. The fight keeps me on the edge of my seat. Attacks and evade prompts coming from every direction, but I was holding my own with this monster. I am ♥♥♥♥-talking as we are rampaging.  There is a sudden break in the action. It stops for a sec to stare at me. Come I got you, I said and at that moment it reaches its arm forward and waves me in like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Bruce Lee! Apparently, the  boss was enjoying this skirmish as much as I was. When was the last time you felt like a game was alive? There were many moments that highlighted Resident Evil 4’s excellent game design..	The one time I felt that the game stumbled for me was facing a mid game boss . Now up to this point the boss encounters were awesome with the appropriate difficulty. Not this bastard. At first, I didn’t understand how to evade the it’s attacks. Then I was sure if any damage was being inflicted was making a dent.  The player is bombarded by the ungodly trio of a fast moving boss, environment hazards, and disorienting stage design. Eventually, I figured out a gameplan to beat the boss, but we when it was all said and done. I felt a sense of dread not relief because I was worried the remaining boss fights would be harder than this one. Seriously, I contemplated switching to an easier difficulty a few times, but I am glad to say it was smooth sailing from there.Bottomline: this game is worth your money. I cannot recommend this game highly enough. You will constantly be challenged and rewarded with something worthwhile. This game begs for you to replay it over and over again. Multiple playthroughs are built inherently into the game. I have played over 100+ hours. Completed the game 8x times and counting. Add in the Mercenaries mode, which will steal hours away from you and the upcoming “Seperate Ways.” DLC. There will be no shortage of monster slaying in your foreseeable future.

_childDocuments_.review: Younger brother bought this as a christmas gift since he knows the original RE4 is one of my favourite games. This version is an excellent remake of one of the greatest games of all time. The visuals are stunning, the environment is appropriately creepy and the gameplay foundation is still exhilarating. Building off the excellent RE2 remake (rather than the barebones RE3), the game has so far recreated the OG RE4 feeling, while remixing all aspects of puzzles, combat, and exploration. While veterans of the original game will feel at home, there is no doubt that Leon's new movement options, combined with your enemies' new tricks livens up the experience. A slightly stronger emphasis on survival horror elements makes this game feel like a logical sequel to the Leon in RE2. He's more experienced, more trained, but the challenges you face don't allow you to just go in guns blazing always (although that is much easier than in RE2). The game's audio is excellent. The rev of a far off chainsaw causes you to whip Leon's head around to locate the source, creepy gooey sounds have you second guess dipping into that dark corridor, and far off wolves announce their presence like hounds from hell. The voice acting has been tightened up, with a script and tone that is more polished and a bit more serious than RE2. However, the spirit of Leon the "action hero" is well preserved.If you loved the OG , give this a try. Everyone else, you owe it to yourself to play RE4.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first Resident Evil game, recommended by a friend and fan of the series. And I have to say, I really enjoyed it! I even did the Separate Ways DLC with Ada.I'm a total sucker for a good culty creepy kinda story so the lore had me gripped from the start. The mechanics took a little getting-used to, but once you understand the rhythm of the action sequences, it quickly becomes insanely fun and you feel like such a badass when you take down a wave of enemies. The game punishes using too much ammo too quickly before you can restock, forcing you to be resourceful which I liked. Makes the ammo feel actually valuable. But I almost never felt *too* backed into a corner, so good balance.I'm also big on collectables, and I always found myself instinctively looking upwards when I would hear the iconic dangly sound from the metal containers holding shiny goodies. I LOVE the marketplace guy, just felt like a buddy that kept you company throughout the entire game, cheering you on while he sells you upgrades and new weapons. He even has a shooting range to practice weapons that rewards you if you get high scores. Different weapons also affect different enemies or are better for certain situations so the game makes you experiment to figure out what works.The boss fights often took me a few tries to beat, but I never got particularly frustrated with them. If anything they felt exciting, the enemies are terrifying and you feel like you really accomplished something when you beat them. Even killing regular enemies is immensely satisfying in a way that's difficult to describe. All of the characters were fantastic, and I loved the synergy between Leon and Ashley, seeing them work together and become friends.All in all - this game is a masterpiece and I can see why so many people love it! I'm happy to join that crowd.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've played. I hadn't played and other Resident Evil games before and I have to say that this was an amazing introductions to the series. Some pros and cons:Pro:- The game is graphically amazing. Its very atmospheric, with high-quality animations as well. It ran very well on my decently good gaming laptop, which was a nice surprise.- The combat is really cool. You can tell that the developers put lots of effort in the handling of the firearms, the melee attacks and the grenades. What I find most impressive is how the enemies act when closeby. You always feel like you were cornered, but somehow fought your way out, which is an amazing feeling.- The enemy variety is excellent. Nearly all enemies have unique ways in which you have to approach them, which really helps with spicing up the combat. - There's a variety between combat, fun traversal and puzzles. - The companions you travel with are a lot of fun. You miss them when they are not there.- The DLC is good. Separate Ways is worth the money.- BingoCons:- Sometimes, especially during boss fights, you can press E to evade an attack. This will have a pop-up on the screen. However, sometimes you need to parry an attack or simply sprint out of the way. These counters won't really have a pop-up, which can make some boss fights feel like there's no counter to their attacks. I recommend just sprinting out of the way most of the time :)- I was kinda disappointed that there was no "chapter replay" option after you've beaten the game. To get back to a specific chapter you must be lucky to have a save of that chapter, or you must play the game from the start again. I recommend saving at a different save-slot after every chapter.- I felt kind-of punished for taking a long time to explore during my first playthrough. You get a score for the entire run at the end, and rewards are handed out for a higher score. This made me think to myself: "If only I had played a bit faster I would've unlocked the funny hat." Its not a big deal, but be aware of this.In conclusion: highly recommended :)

_childDocuments_.review: A Masterful Recreation - Resident Evil 4 Remake (2023) ReviewCapcom's remake of the 2005 classic, Resident Evil 4, stands as an impressive testament to the potential of revisiting a beloved title with modern sensibilities, while still paying homage to its original roots. Not only does the 2023 version resurrect the timeless thrill and horror of the original, it further enhances the experience with brilliant gameplay mechanics and audio-visual enhancements.At the heart of this refreshed experience is the delicate balance between nostalgia and modern gameplay. Capcom has done a remarkable job in maintaining the core essence of the original game, while introducing elements that align with contemporary expectations. The game stays true to its roots, not veering off into unnecessary story add-ins, thus preserving the core narrative that fans have loved over the years​.The game's combat system has also undergone a substantial revamp, with the integration of new knife combat. A significant upgrade is the replacement of the Quick Time Events (QTEs) with quick time prompts, a change that maintains the excitement of the original QTEs, while eliminating the harsh penalties for failure. The fight with Kruger stands as a notable example of this new system, with parries and knife attacks occurring in real-time, adding a layer of skill and strategy to the combat.What truly stands out in this remake is the remarkable implementation of spatial 3D audio using 7.1.4. The careful attention to audio detail adds a new level of immersion, enhancing the overall horror experience and making every moment within the game feel even more lifelike.Capcom has outdone themselves with the internal development of the RE Engine and it carries over to the other games as well!Overall, the Resident Evil 4 Remake stands as an impressive example of how to effectively modernize a classic, enhancing its gameplay and technical aspects while preserving the spirit that made the original game so beloved. Capcom has not only breathed new life into a classic title but has also set a high bar for future remakes in the industry.

_childDocuments_.review: =================Resident Evil 4 is a fantastic remake of the 2005 GameCube title that runs well and looks great on the PC, provided you've got a beefy enough system, or can make compromises with the resolution and ray-tracing.There's so much here to like that it's hard to think of any gamer who wouldn't find a high degree of enjoyment from this game. Action? Check. Adventure? Check. Horror? Check? Replay value? Check.Resident Evil 4 has it all.=================- Absolutely gorgeous environments.- Extremely satisfying action.- Guns are a joy to buy and upgrade.- Treasures are still here in all their glory.- New side quests provide extra incentives to fully explore the world.- Great enemy variety.- New stealth kills to help you reserve ammo.- Ashley's AI seems improved compared to her 2005 version.- New game play segments added to the campaign.- A campaign that lasts around 15 hours on first play though.- Lots of unlockables, meaning you'll want to replay the campaign.- One boss fight was removed, which I did find myself missing.- Not sure I like how the cases you carried impacted the drop rate of certain items.- Not enough Saddler.- Some dumb changes to Luis.- Some of the camp was toned down, which was a part of the original's charm.=================

_childDocuments_.review: Owch... This sucks for me to write. I'm conflicted at the moment, and I'm aware I'm only a short way into the play time, but so far my overwhelming gut feeling is I want to return this product. Let me be very clear, I adore RE4 (the original), it is my absolute favourite RE game, I have completed it many times on multiple platforms, and have been a fan of the series itself since it's genesis, so this isn't a lighthearted take on what I have played so far, but I can't deny my personal feelings and experiences towards this product I have been waiting for for years. Presentation-wise this product delivers, this looks, and sounds great so far. There is decent VO work (even though the script is typically kitch RE, which you either love or hate). The return of MY most hated, unrealistic mechanic for the modern RE games is back again: knife-durability! Yay... This is admittedly a personal stance on this, and I know some people enjoy the aspect of  limited resource on the knife, I however, abhor it as it feels like a cheap, uninspired way to artificially create the sense of horror in these survival horror games. Stabbing the soft, supple throat of a Ganado should not take of 1/4 to 1/3 of a knife's durability, I just don't buy it.So what are the actual problems I have with this release? To be blunt it is the controls, more precisely, the combat controls. This feels borderline awful to play. (For reference I played on a game-pad, AND mouse & keyboard, they both feel stiff and slow)Aiming and movement are unrealistically sluggish, both the weapon draw and Leon's inability to move quicker than a stoned paraplegic while aiming. As for the aiming itself, it feels similarly slow (yes, even with increased sens). The crosshair (which I also dislike, I feel the laser pointer from the original was less immersion breaking) often feels like it's not a true indicator of where you're shooting, as I've had enemies at point blank range slip my shots in the same way Fortune from MGS2 slips bullets, i.e. just standing still or slowly moving forward, all the while mounting non-stop offence. The bullets themselves feel like they have limited to no effect when they impact, head and leg shots don't feel satisfying or as effective like in the original game, with enemies often needing 2-4 shots before entering any sort of reaction or stun animation giving the enemies a very spongy feel that reeks of artificial difficulty. The recoil (on game-pad) has a truly terrible feel to it as it effectively does not recoil in a realistic way. Instead, after each shot Leon's aim is moved off-center usually upwards, but does not realign, meaning if you are not constantly realigning your cross-hair after each shot you will quickly have you shooting into thin air.The game recommends running if the odds are not in your favour which would be fine were it not for enemies that seem to possess FTL capabilities when your back is turned as they immediately gain on you, often executing far reaching charge or throw attacks, so when you do make space to fight it's all been for naught as the moment you quick-turn you get skewered, or catch a flying axe in the face. The slash action on the knife also feels weak and ineffectual, and while I've yet to test it more the arc of the slash has felt (to me) as if it does not connect with all the targets in the arc. I've even experienced the bull (from the town square fight) stand still after being set on fire, allowing the ganado to saunter around untrampled, only to be bulldozed myself the second I got in view of it, where it immediately ran directly into me and no one else then promptly died... Admittedly this was actually as funny as it was frustrating, so I've not lost my sense of humor yet, but I may have lost my desire to play RE which truly saddens me. I hate feeling this way about my personal darling of the franchise, however, the new combat system is truly killing my enjoyment of this title. It's as if they are trying to impose RE2's combat on to the game that redefined combat in the first place. It's an ill fit for me. Perhaps it get's better when you have more weapons or better gear, but 60 Euros is a steep wager on something that has yet to make me feel like I'm having fun. So ultimately I think I'll refund for now. This is not the game I was hoping for, but I hope it is for you.If you have similar feelings about the combat of the modern RE-make games then give this a miss until it's cheaper. The way it played so far I cannot in good conscience recommend it. For those who do enjoy it, I envy you getting to play this gem in all it's revamped glory, have fun since I can't <3

_childDocuments_.review: The last time I enjoyed a resident evil game was RE2 remake. Now, it’s RE4 remake. Overall, this remake balances between new and old while still retaining that sweet combat/horror balance that the original was known for. For that reason, I think that the remake is better because it adds a very clean visual experience to really take in the horror and environment in the RE engine. This is not a perfect game, mainly due to missing campaigns and mercenaries characters, as well as some other bosses. Unlike many though, I think there is enough replayabilty in this game (challenges,S+, new game plus) to keep me occupied until the campaigns are added if they will be. The MAIN game is what I was looking for in the first place and I think the removal of some bosses actually allowed for better pacing between bosses.Pros:-cinematic story-improved experience with Ashley -side quests-RE engine quality -fun combat-neat controls-Nice HUD and menu-Horror/action balance-replay ability Cons:-Heavily action focused at times-Still some weird VA-Missing bosses-missing campaigns and mercenaries characters -felt less interest in story and horror compared to re2 remake

You may notice familiar areas from the original, but they have been retuned just a tad to make them look better and different. _childDocuments_.review: I played the hell out of the original RE4 in multiple devices including PC. I loved that game so much it is one of the few games I keep going back to. I was a little nervous about the remake since RE4 was a big game with a lot of content. I am glad some of the things they cut out were mechanics such as quick time events and other minor things. I am a little disappointed about removing the cheesy dialog because it was fun and memorable, but I can understand why they did it. This remake nailed how a remake should be made and how a game like this needs to be in terms of pacing. Each area you visit doesn't overstay its presence and moves on very well. I also like Ashley's and Luis's improvements to their characters. They turned Separate Ways into a DLC, but the original release did not even get it on GC. The base game still has plenty of content to replay just like the original did. As for the "microtransactions" the game is more forgiving than the original, specially when unlocking things, so you don't need them like in other games where they purposely nerf your progress.Well done Capcom.

_childDocuments_.review: The original RE4 is one of my all time favourite games, if not just flat-out my all time favourite. When this was announced, I had no intention of picking it up, as I thought "how can you improve on something already so perfect in almost every aspect". Then I saw the first gameplay.Then I replayed the original for the umpteenth time and started thinking of ways that it could be improved.Then I played the demo.And then I played the game.And I realised that the Resident Evil game I'd been pining for for years was what I thought I'd never wanted in the first place. Whether you're a long time fan or a newcomer, this is peak Resident Evil in every form. Spending the weekend playing this on Hardcore took me back to playing this game for the first time on the Wii in my parents' basement late at night during summer vacation. A true love letter to survival horror, the Resident Evil franchise, and one of the greatest games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: An improvement over the original in nearly every way, this game is a masterclass in how to make a good remake.PROS+I feel like a broken record saying how amazing the RE Engine is, but it's genuinely beautiful in every scene! I love it!+Likewise, a great deal of explanation is hidden in the files for those who are interested. Similarly to how RE8's twist could be seen in 7 if you think it through, you can pick up on the backstories of many of these characters by reading the files and thinking it through.+Just like RE2R, the story is the same, but tweaked to be logical rather than a B-Movie. As the original story was pretty solid, this one is genuinely good!+The characters are dramatically improved over the original in every measurable sense. Leon has a wonderful character arc, Ada feels like a natural extension from her appearance in RE2R, Luis is a sympathetic ally with a tragic past, Krauser actually feels like a former mentor-ally to Leon (as opposed to his stereotypical tough-guy merc attitude in the original), Salazar is a wonderfully theatrical monster who needs a wake-up call, Mendez is a badass who makes the "evil priest" stereotype (which I'm sick of tbh) actually work, and Saddler became a charismatic cult leader who actually feels like a menace, as opposed to his original "B-Movie villain" writing.+While the character improvements in this are wonderful, the glow-up that Ashley received is well-worth mentioning on its own sheerly for how incredible her improvement is. She's a literal polar opposite to her original writing: going from annoying, whiny, and idiotic to desperate, inexperienced, yet capable of learning. She's no longer a chore, but an actually valuable ally to Leon. She's not a badass like Ada, Claire, Helena, or RE6 Sherry, but she's doing her best and actually being effective in doing so. Her banter with Leon feels realistic and funny: a vast improvement from the "No way!/Way!" dumpster-diving scenes from the original. She no longer feels like the quintessential annoying escort mission, but the exception where it's actually fun to escort her, not unlike Elizabeth in Bioshock Infinite. I couldn't wait to be rid of classic Ashley, but I can't wait to see this Ashley again.+The new voice actors are almost 100% improvements over the original. Particular stand-outs include Leon (same actor as RE2R!), Ashley (no longer whiny teenager), Salazar (menacing and funny, not just funny), and the Merchant (familiar to classic, but not the same!).+The gameplay is improved over the original by a significant margin. Just being able to move-and-shoot makes it much more fun, and the handful of new enemies are welcome additions to the game.+Speaking of gameplay, the introduction of the Parry system is a fantastic way to show that Leon is on the same skill level as Chris or Jill, but still have his own flavor of it. Instead of the Krauser knifefight feeling like a cutscene without much meaning to it, it serves as a natural way for these two masters to fight it out. +The Merchant is a very welcome return, and feels like a port in a storm before a serious moment. I've heard some people badmouth his bantering, but I like it.+Also, adding Item Box functionality to the typewriters is a nice way to strengthen that "completionist" attitude and get me to buy and own every maxed-out gun in the game.+Also-also, the new shooting range is probably the best minigame I've played in a long time! It's a genuine challenge with good fun, great atmosphere, a fun pirate theme, and some wonderful bonding with Ashley and Luis! Not to mention: The Drive (Remix) goes so hard I kept coming back for more, even after getting all the unlocks I wanted.+The new crafting system is welcome as an evolution from its RE2R and RE3R counterparts!+Some new weapons with fun, interesting roles! The not-MP5 is a good sidegrade to the TMP, the not-M4 is useful for mag-dumping Regeneradors, and the mine thrower has been repurposed into a bolt thrower which is a remarkably useful weapon on higher difficulties when you don't have ammo for your main weapons!+I wasn't expecting to love the new music as much as I did, but the motifs and themes to each track are wonderful! They feel like a perfect balance between horror, action, and Spain, depending on what's going on.+With other RE games (especially RE3R and RE7), the highest difficulties are balanced around needing to use the rewards for beating the lower difficulties (like items which give more health, better weapons, etc). This one isn't, and even has unique rewards to beating the game on the highest difficulty without using any bonus items!+Mods!+DLC: The Mercenaries is different from its original incarnation, but better in a lot of ways. Each character plays differently, yet thematically appropriate to their characters. Leon feels familiar to the campaign, Luis is a glass cannon, Krauser is a big, bad brawler, and HUNK is a cold-blooded professional. Incredibly fun FreeLC!CONS-I know I love the new parry system, but I have to admit that parrying a chainsaw, while cool in appearance, is a bit much for me.-On that topic, I don't like the returning knife durability system. It's not very fun to be dumping pesetas into keeping my knife in functional shape, and the Primal/Fighting Knives would work well as sidegrades to the default without needing to make Durability a reason to take one over the others.-I don't know why, but they butchered the not-MP5 so much in this. The poor thing looks like a cursed Call of Duty Vanguard-version of itself. Which is odd, considering how good it looked in RE2R.-DLC: I'll be honest, the new Mercenaries music is pretty bland and heartless when compared to the original.As of right now, this game is a work of art and a must-buy. I'll update this as new DLC comes out, but this is going to stay as a must-buy in my book!

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played any of the Resident Evil games and are looking to start to get into the series this is the perfect game to start with in my opinion. You don't feel like you missed much of the series because you are brought up to speed in the intro. The combat is pretty straight forward you'll just have to practice a little bit but I think that's the fun part because as you are learning you are being chased around! The story is what makes this game one of the best in my opinion. It's fun, scary and creative with some amazing boss fights! The puzzles are fairly easy but to a younger mind they might struggle hahaa. That's why this game should be for 18+ you need some common sense and awareness of your surroundings. If you find yourself debating whether to give this game a try or not like I did, I say if you like horror games you won't be disappointed. There's no other game like it and it has replayability value in my opinion. The story and graphics are so rich and unique that it makes me want to go through the story at least 2 -3 times and I'm only on chapter 6.

There is a lot of blood in the game, for this a separate respect, the developers have not caved in to a society that has become too tolerant that now does not like blood in games.  Shooting is the coolest thing here.   The graphics look like you're watching a movie; each boss is drawn in its own unique style.  For me personally, the game was not scary, there was no effect of surprise, and very rarely enemies came out suddenly, so anyone can play it. Splendid game, now I have a lot of work to complete all the games from this story.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it a good game? Yes! Do I like it? No.If interested read on.I have been a fan of RE games since RE2 as it was my introduction into the franchise and have fallen in love with it... However, RE4 was built up to be the high on silver platter golden shelf monumental video game. But I didn't like it. #1: "Who tf is shooting at me syndrome" You can't tell where ranged enemies are at times and it makes combat infuriating. #2: "Action>Horror" Resident Evil started as a horror game & got revived by a horror game and SHOULD STAY A HORROR GAME. RE3 Is pure action movie and RE4 feels too run & gun for my liking. #3: "One Way Only" This game really punishes you for trying to go a certain way when the game wants you to go another way (EX: Ashley's bit if you didn't go to the library first) almost as if the game punishes you for thinking differently from the creators. #4: Ammo doesn't matter, part of the fun of RE games is resource management, but in this game where enemies are birthed from air the game showers you with them like a Utah mom on Christmas day. #5 Bullet sponges, I've seen people review RE2 & RE3 for being bullet sponges cause zombies take 5-8 shots before dying in the head, but they don't mention it for RE4. One could make the argument that since these El Zombozos are a different variant it makes them tougher, but I think that is a weak explination. #6 Gotta be honest I hate the chapters & the over abundance of cut scenes. This game is chapter'ed in way that ultimately pauses the game FOR you and it really pulls you out of the experience. And with every cutscene entering and exiting with a (cool cutscene) it pulls me out. RE2, RE7, and RE8 did the cutscenes perfectly by making em snappy or making them a part of the gameplay smoothly, but here it feels like RE3 but with weird interludes. What is positive about the game?QUITE LITERALLY EVERYTHING ELSE! While I may not like the game, it is incredibly well put together and designed beautifully. This game truly is a work of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ art, and I do love aspects of it. But the absence of horror, the emphasis on weird chapters, and punishing you for thinking differently then the developers makes the game feel far more out of place for me. It sucks cause I want to like it, I really do, it apparently the GOLD STANDARD of Resident Evil games (even for remake standards), but I just couldn't get behind it.I really hope Capcom does not repeat the mistake they did all those years ago with Resident Evil 5 when they turned to action/adventure and nearly killed the series until the horror game RE7 brought it back to life.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I wouldn't give a feedback on a game i bought and played, mostly because nowadays these tend to be released in very poor condition, for full price tags or aren't that much big of a deal. This is not the case with this Title and for that i feel like I should post this for everyone to see.I've played this game for 19 hours, i am yet to find any kind of bug or crash/freeze. the game seems well optimized, has been running smoothly with no framedrops ever, and trust me there are times things go really hectic (Explosions, super gory dismemberments in all sorts of ways, bloody explosions) in this game. The game is astonishingly gorgeous, I can only imagine how it must be like to play it on a  Top of the line rig with ray tracing and everything maxed out.In terms of gameplay i find it to be a challenging game in normal difficulty (can only imagine how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nightmarish it must be if you crank it up), it feels like a true survival game, you're never fully out of ammo, but you're never swimming in it either, i've noticed there's somewhat an abundance of healing items throughout the game (i have like 6 first aid sprays, 3 herb mixes and some fishes) i find it to be slightly game breaking. The gun play is SUPER good, they look awesome, only thing i'd change in them would be SFX by making them louder (might be a hardware problem on my end, since i play on a Laptop though) and tighten the shotgun spread, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it feels like you're shooting a sawed-off shotgun 10-20 meters  away from target.You can now use your knife while moving nimbly to CQC enemies: Wide cuts, stabs, parrys, blocks, stealth kills.Ashley isn't as useless anymore! she'll rarely get on your way, she's more autonomous and won't scream "LEEEEEEOOOOOOOON" every 5 seconds anymore and she struggles with the Plagas for about 5 seconds before they can get a hold of her, giving you time to knife them in the face.The only thing i didnt really like in the game was the Camera. Personally i find it to be WAY TOO CLOSE to Leon, even at max FOV, even worse when you aim your weapons. But in the end this ends up not being an issue since you can take care of it with mods and create your own Camera offsets.This game is super easy to mod: I'd recommend to anyone who buys it, to mess around mostly with camera mods. There IS a way for you to make that Sniper Rifle of yours to toggle between iron sights and 3rd person view while ADSing and its AWESOME.Installing and uninstalling mods on this game takes literally seconds, and never breaks the game nor your savefiles (well atleast in my case)To conclude; It's a breathe of fresh air considering these past game releases. They picked up an already awesome game, and made it like 10 times more fun. STRONGLY RECOMMEND IT, wether you buy it full price, or on sale, it is worth every cent. Most off the issues it has are minor and can be fixed with mods. You're bound to replay the Sh** out of it as you did with Resident Evil 4.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played OG RE4 (2005), you won't miss anything by jumping straight to RE4R (2023). The remake surpasses the original in every way, right down to the story and characterisation.Ashley is less annoying and has better chemistry with Leon, while Luis and Krauser have more fleshed out motivations that tie in to Leon's character arc. Even the backstories of the main villains have been updated to form a more cohesive narrative in the RE canon.Unfortunately, Ada is the only cast member that suffers in the remake due to a lousy and miscast actor. Remake-Ada exudes none of the mystique and panache that made her such an iconic and popular character. Now she feels like a generic female "Black Widow" secret agent — with none of Scarlett Johansson's charisma.Gameplay-wise, many of the signature set-pieces and monsters have been updated with new twists or variations. This is one of the very few remakes where the developer deliberately uses the player's foreknowledge of the original to throw in some unexpected surprises.Gone are quick-time events during cutscenes, however you will still be prompted with QTEs during most of the boss encounters. The updated controls feel more fluid, modernising RE4's combat into what you've come to expect from a 2023 title.Does RE4R justify its existence for this remake? Absolutely yes. Is it the best game in the series? Nope. That honour goes to Resident Evil 7 (if you can play it in VR).

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, Resident Evil 4, where your one job is to babysit an American president's daughter, Ashley. Because, of course, in the vast universe of game plots, “The President's daughter has been kidnapped!” seems as cliché as “Did you try turning it off and on again?”Graphics: Leon S. Kennedy, our favorite wisecracking hero, sports that "I just left a 2005 boy band" look. Hair more emo than a teenager's Tumblr page, jacket swankier than a Vegas magician's, and that aura of "I might be in over my head, but look at my hair!" The ganados, our main enemies, are grumpy farmers with some serious anger issues. Maybe they’re mad because their crops keep failing, or maybe they just can't find their chickens.Gameplay: Ah, the good old "stop and shoot." For those unaware, that means Leon, with all his training, has the motor skills of a toddler on a sugar rush when trying to walk and shoot at the same time. A moment of silence for all the times we've yelled, "Move, Leon, MOVE!"Aiming: Let's not forget the laser sight. It's like a futuristic cat toy. I half-expected a cat to jump out and chase the red dot. Would’ve made for a great addition to the game. You know, Zombie Cats. Just an idea, Capcom.Inventory Management: The Tetris-style suitcase is a masterclass in teaching players the importance of space optimization. Who knew that, amidst a zombie outbreak, the real challenge would be trying to fit a rocket launcher next to an herb?Plot: Ah, Spanish villages, mysterious cults, oversized sea monsters, and oh, did I mention Napoleon? Resident Evil 4 somehow throws it all in a blender, adds a dash of sinister laughter, and still manages to serve a palatable storyline cocktail.Thought for the day: In a world infested with zombies, cults, and chainsaw-wielding maniacs, perhaps the real Resident Evil is mankind's inability to coexist, the real monsters being our inner demons. Or maybe it's just about shooting stuff and saving Ashley.Overall: If you ever thought life's too predictable, give Resident Evil 4 a whirl. It teaches you important life skills like how to deal with lousy village welcoming committees and how to maintain perfect hair amidst chaos.Remember, it's not just about survival; it's about style. Leon knows it. So should you. 10/10 - would run from villagers again!Go out and buy this ♥♥♥♥ now! It's 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best game among the newer Resident Evils simply because of its slick combat.I am not kidding when I say this is the Dark Souls of Resident Evil Remakes.It doesn't waste its time with item fetching puzzles, and being combat heavy makes it immensely more replayable than the other entries.Still, there are things the original Resident Evil 4 did better:-The levels were much cleaner and easier to navigate.-The enemies were more responsive and predictable, when you shot at them you knew they would flinch:This was RE:Village's worst mistake, everything became tanky and less interactive, the difficulty made the game less fun, but here they managed to dial it down on a very acceptable level.Still, I think the Hardcore difficulty message is intentionally disdainful, like "You played the old one? Then come try this one ♥♥♥♥♥." and it is actually more difficult than the old one. It's funny but definitely misdirecting.-Removing the gunpowder mechanic made sense. It made you switch around your weapons.-New side quests are alright, but they make you wander off quite a bit too much, they basically waste your time and make you get a lower ranking at the final results.-Small keys are completely needless and something that should've been shaken off from the 2 and 3 Remakes, it fit them more because they're more "survival". Like who cares about retraversing the whole level for some measly cash, same goes for the special keys in the village and the castle. They're not very well thought, even shooting glimmering stones off the walls were more engaging than getting a key and opening a drawer.But overall the new additions make up for it:+Parry mechanic is absolutely fun. Making the main knife break so easily is a little redundant, having to play with kitchen knives, especially just when the game just started is a little annoying. But the Krauser fight became more intense in general.+There's stealth. I'm not really one for it, but getting easy knife kills from behind is satisfying and it makes sense.+New Salazar boss-fight is way better than the old one.+Luis and Mendez got some love with additional scenes.+Animation quality is top notch. Enemies have some wicked attack animations.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 4's remake is an excellent game that is superior in many ways to the original and just different in others. Though, it is a shame that all the years later both games never are as enjoyable, tense, and good at maintaining that survival feel after that first village fight.The remake of RE4 gives us most of what was in the original with some setting alterations, allows you to move while aiming, shooting, and reloading, makes mostly positive changes to boss fights, adds additional weapons and extras (costumes, an infinite ammo for all guns attachment, etc), minor stealth mechanics you can make use of or ignore, crafting options, mostly all positive story and character alterations, and makes your knife a much more important tool.The new movement system where you can aim and move at the same time is somewhat balanced out by the enemies being more aggressive, seemingly being more likely to attempt to or to come into the area trying to surround you, and that your guns might take some time to aim well making quickly moving and shooting leading to a minor to severe accuracy loss depending on the gun you are using. The new movement system works well, not always better, just in a different way than the original. On the negative side, being able to reload while moving has taken the tension out of the moments where you run out of ammo, and the increased realism of movement and more lifelike graphics do tend to naturally raise obvious annoyances when you are damaged or killed when Leon suddenly can't drop off a small ledge to an area you can access by moving in a different direction, can't climb or vault small obstacles, and when certain sections do allow you to do things like vault over objects while other similar sized parts of the environment don't allow that. Reloading also has the odd issue that is in a lot of games where, when it comes to weapons that reload one bullet at a time, Leon will not stop reloading until the gun is full or he is out of extra ammo. You want to load one bullet into the bolt action rifle to shoot the guy guy charging you? No, Leon will not stop until he loads all four, so you better run away while reloading, or swap your gun. The realistic look of the game also makes it a bit ridiculous that those weapons that load one bullet/shell/bolt at a time have their reload speed upgrades tied to Leon magically loading more and more bullets at once until you end up with a sawed off shotgun that hold six bullets and loads up to six bullets when he puts one in.There are now on the fly weapon swaps with up to eight assignable slots for guns and grenades, a nice change from having to go to the inventory screen all the time (still an option). Finding gunpowder and resources to craft ammo or grenades allows for a bit more control over what guns you want to use along with the great new option to store any weapons, weapon attachments, and first aid sprays at any save location. Allowing you to build up an arsenal of weapons over time or over multiple playthroughs without always having to rebuy and upgrade the guns you want to use to save inventory space in the current playthrough. Beating one playthrough will allow you to start a new game plus with pretty much everything other than key items carried over to your next game, on whatever of the four difficulty settings you choose to play on, though the highest ranking and some challenges with their own unlockables might require you to do a fresh playthrough or at least one without any powerful unlockable items like not useable in a normal first playthrough.Blows from the more aggressive enemies look, feel, and sound a lot more impactful and to those enemies from your own weapons when your guns can blow off arms or shotguns can cut them in half (which can make aiming your shotgun at the body instead of the head a way to prevent them from getting back up if the parasite in them takes over, a nice change from the earlier titles where blowing off zombie heads preventing reanimation). There is wider variety of movement animations for enemies as well as for the movements of allied characters when they are following you as well as different dialogue lines depending on how well you handle combat and your health status. For those that speak or understand some Spanish the use of and accent of the language has been improved from the original, though if you don't speak Spanish you are unfortunately mostly out of luck when it comes to understanding what anyone is saying as it isn't subtitled.Your knife has become a more useful and varied tool. Stealth kills can be useful and at times a fun and tense mix, stealth killed enemies seem to drop about twice of the random loot they would normally drop but doing so will damage your knives and if you damage your main knife the repair cost might basically be taking that extra money from you. This cost can be negated by using weaker disposable kitchen and boot knives you can find around the environment, or if you take down a more powerful enemy that would have required you to use a lot of ammo to kill. Stealth can be made more difficult than it has to be at times because there is no way to switch which shoulder the camera is is over so taking left corners always puts you at an aiming and sight line disadvantage (on top of not having this feature being a potentially large disability issue for some). There are a limited number of areas you can get through by relying on total stealth, usually it is more to pick off a few enemies, but there are a few cases where you can instant stealth kill a mini boss fairly easily. I was able to backstab three of the large sledgehammer wielding brute types in my first playthrough.When it comes to new weapons, the boltgun is fun to use and, with the silent nature of the weapon and reusable bolts that can also be fitted with proximity mines, comes with a few new strategies of its own to make use when attempting stealth, trying to save ammo, or dealing with enemies that are blind and attack only what they hear. Another new weapon is an automatic rifle that can still equip scopes, and the two old rifles are changed a bit by giving a first person style iron sight aiming mode when you don't have the scope attachment equipped when they used to just have a scope with a more limited zoom. There is a new SMG in the LE 5 that is also able to equip a rifle scope as an attachment, and while weaker and able to hold slightly less ammo than the old TMP it unlocks the ability to penetrate multiple enemies or through shields. There are two deluxe edition only weapons with the new pistol being about the same as the main gun but with higher capacity and firing rate and slightly less damage and the more interesting sawed off shotgun that offers a wide shot spread while also giving you a shotgun that takes up very little inventory space and that has it's own entertaining Terminator 2 style flip animation.The game seems to have been designed with a variety cool little skips and speedrun strategies in mind. Using a sniper rifle to shoot the church bell to stop the game's first big fight early, grenades and rocket launchers being able to destroy or weaken walls or defenses you need to progress through, locks and devices that can be shot through windows, bars, or cracks in walls to access areas faster, being able to stun or kill enemies before they can activate devices to hinder you because the cutscenes run in real time, killing a boss by hitting him with golden eggs, etc.There is a more serious nature to some of the scenes and characterizations. Jill in Resident Evil 3 and now Leon here seems to have PTSD from both Raccoon City as well as the jobs the US government have forced him into since. Being a bit angrier and Leon being taken advantage of by the government feel at odds with the moments they put in to -Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so, the game is good. Really good. This is the kind of gameplay you would remember after playing the original and trying to upscale the graphics in your head. I totally stand by that comment.The game feels...fresh....both for someone who experienced the previous remakes and/or the series as a whole, RE4R takes the series in a more action-oriented direction. The game most definitely feels more like a 1:1 remake of the original rather than a re-imagining of the whole game. Some map layouts are identical to the original game, and some are changed. There are also instances where you have to go through a map backwards - comparing it to the original. So additionally some areas are flipped to keep the old gamers feeling confused as to where they have to go.Safe to say that the cast did a phenomenal job. All characters feel alive in the game. If I were to be a picky eater, I would probably find some issues with the voice of Salazar and Ada, the latter of two actually having a bit of a controversy when it comes to voice acting at the time of the games release. Personally, I really enjoy the new Ada's voice. The older games (RE2R included) tried to portray Ada as a seductive agent who tries to get into Leons head. Here, in the remake of RE4 she sounds much more as a experienced field operator who is almost tired with the things she has to do, additionally trying to keep up the facade of a fem fatale to Leon. I really dig that.Now, the gameplay. Yeah it's fun, for the most part. In this game, there's a big emphasis on the parrying mechanic with Leon's knife, which could save you from some nasty trouble. I personally am NOT a fan of those type of mechanics. Especially in the type of games which DO. NOT. NEED. this mechanic. I'm fine with a parrying mechanic being in a medieval game, or something more akin to a melee-orientated games. The Jedi game series (Fallen Order, Survior) come to mind. But in a game where most of the time you'd spend trying to desperately shoot some zombies, a tiny indicator which tells you when to press the parry button is not a good mechanic to put in-game. My advice would be to:-make the opening window for a successful parry bigger-make the indicator more visible as supposed to a tiny button in a corner of your hud-be able to select different types of the parrying mechanic ON TOP of the games difficultyI'm not saying that the game doesn't necessarily reward you for hitting the parry at the right time. It does, stunning your enemy for a brief second. But in my opinion it's really not worth it to try and get it "in the perfect time". You'll end up equipping and un-equipping your knife, making Leon jump up and down as if he's having an intense beatbox battle.I just remembered something. In the original game, to get to the castle you had to fight the big preacher guy to get his glass eye and take it to some gate for it to open. That segment, along with a few more were cut out from the remake. I actually appreciate that because it felt kind of overdone in the first place. You CAN however still get the glass eye after your fight with him and sell it to the merchant.That's the neat thing about the merchant. After using some items that are required for the story to progress, you can sell them for coins. It's a nice addition to get something out of items you no longer need.Now, my other point. Ammo management. I personally had to kill the final boss, Sadler, with grenades and sniper rifle ammo because I ran out of bullets moments before. Now to be frank, this was the only moment in the whole game where I had to rely on some wacky weapon I wouldn't typically use to progress the story. BUT, that being said, I wouldn't call having to constantly watch out for your ammo IN A BOSS BATTLE as a good game decision."uUh bUt IT's A sUrViVal HorRor GamE" yeah, I know. I know that one of the games appeals is inventory management. I really have no issue with that. It's just that in some areas you might find yourself out of luck with nothing but a flash grenade to your name. And if you do...you better clutch that.I won't speak much on the games optimisation. It's definitely made for the newer generation of consoles, so I can't say that the game is bad because it ran badly on my pc. However...the game presents you with multiple graphical presets meant to help the player with settings. In my mind, when a game tells you "you can and will run the game in this mode, but the models will be kind of wonky" I expect that the settings it's giving me WILL make the game run at a solid framerate, taking away from the visual aspect of the game. For the most part, I ran the game on the "Performance" and "Ultra Performance" modes. Even then, in some chapters, I could get roughly 9 fps for a good bit. This is the thing I have a problem with.Now I could ramble on about how the game gives you the minimal requirements to run it on the games store page, but "a minimal requirement" and an in-game graphical mode are two different things in my opinion. Minimum MEANS minimum. So no matter how crappy the game will run, it. will. run. The same can't be said for the presets in-game.As for the story...Well, it wasn't changed much. Most of the main story beats stay the same. I haven't played the original RE4 in a good while so I can't exactly compare it directly, but there are some changes like WHEN in the story Leon and Ashley get stuff out of their system. That being said, the main change in the games story I COULD feel was how Ashley got seemingly kidnapped over and over again. Let me reiterate that the same thing COULD have been in the original game, but here it seems like the story follows this plan:-Leon fights enemies-Leon finds Ashley-Both go on about their mission-Ashley gets kidnapped by a miniboss-Leon rescues Ashleyrinse and repeatResident Evil games have this sort of appeal to it, that it drags you into the game with the first act of it. The setting, the atmosphere, the characters relationship. Like for RE2 you have the RPD with just you and a single wounded police officer in it. In RE8 you have the beginning village and the tall vampire lady stalking you. In RE4 you obviously have the village (again) with just you, Hunnigan and the feeling of loneliness in the middle of this remote place in ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, Nowhere. When you finally get comfortable in your surroundings, the game flips the switch on you for better or for worse, changing the whole games dynamic. In RE2, suddenly you're in the Umbrellas Labs with Ada and/or Sherry by your side. In RE8 you're running around this complex of multiple locations just getting from checkpoint to checkpoint for....actually I don't remember that. I'll have to play through that game at some point. In RE4, you're in the castle and later on, the island with Ashley, Luis and Ada. The whole mystery about the area you found yourself in is now gone for the sake of shooting zombies. I don't have the problem with RE games being action-packed (RE5 and RE6 come to mind) but I would like a game of this calibre to have one persistent theme throughout it. RE2 sort of achieved that, making you feel like you're helpless throughout the whole game, no matter how hard you fight back. I think RE7 takes a similar approach, but I know the least amount of things about that game, so I won't speak on it.My verdict is that Resident Evil 4: Remake is a solid adaptation of the original game. It polishes the experience and builds onto it, creating a much more pleasant version of the game which fits in the newly, more serious tone of the games. I recommend it for people to play AFTER experiencing the original from 2005. I really like it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be perfectly honest. I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate the inspid, overblown, poorly written, anime-esque writing of Resident Evil. The Resident Evil 3 remake was laughably bad with only brief moments of sanity. The original Resident Evil 4 did well because it distanced itself from the awful Resident Evil story and was a great cheesy romp. So understand the compliment when I say that Resident Evil 4 remake is actually well written. Leon carries with him the weight of his failure to protect people in Raccoon City. Even his design backs this up with bags under his eyes, his face looking a little older, and his eyes often seeming exhausted. The game still has moments of levity with some of the poorly written lines of the original omitted. (Such as Luis commenting on the President's Daughter's 'ballistics' or Ashley's constant flirting with Leon.) The writing honestly manages to walk that fine line of having both comedic, cheesy lines but never undermining the drama.The sound design is understated, with little to no music often, the guns sound perfectly fine but none sound amazig, and the voice actors all do a good job. Your real mileage in the sound design is the quiet moments, the chanting in the distance, unalerted enemies mumbling to themselves, the wind howling, storms raging. It's all very effective at setting a mood even if the whining from Ashley every time you bring her out into the rain grates after a while.The gameplay is Resident Evil 4, the same Resi 4 style gameplay from the other remakes but with the ability to move and therefore insanely easier. The chaotic nature of Resident Evil 4, and some very clever AI, will still find ways to challenge you. There are various challenges to unlock more costumes and weapons, unlockables, treasures to find, and everything you could expect from the original. The game feels like a love letter to the original touching on the same beats but improving in certain areas.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 4 is my favorite game, and the remake outdoes the original in many ways.Unfortunately I cannt say I own this game on multiple consoles, but I have beaten it on ps4 and pc, and gotten every achievement except dlc, and I beaten it on professional. I have enjoyed this game thoroughly, and it is a masterpiece. I want to compare it to the original Resident evil 4 by itself, but that wouldn't be a good review. This remake is a 2023 video game, and it has to be compared not to only the game it is remaking, but whether it is good compared to the games it is released in its time. The point is to see whether the remake is jsutified according to the 80$ price tag in a sea of other games in its category. In this way, I would contend that Resident Evil 4 is a worthy nominator for 2023 game of the year.Firstly, the game does update that old game design to a more modern sensibilities. This means you can walk and shoot and you can auto-sort your attache case, which are nice additions, but the game does far more with it's combat. It basically remakes that old game combat to more in line of what a expert actually plays like. If you play that old game long enough, you start to be more aggressive and tactful, and turn this horror game into an action game, but one that has tank controls.  It is like if you were playing Doom, but with tank controls. In the remake, you can move freely and enemies are more aggressive, allowing that play style to come more naturally.  The perfect mode that exemplifies this play style is mercenaries mode, which shows what this combat system can do. The story mode still restricts you, so it's not like doom in it's insane action. It's a better blend of horror and action then the original had, which is a rarity in today comapre to other video games. If you want to play Spiderman 2, you could jsut play Batman Arkham games for a similar experience. If you want to play Resident Evil 4, you have to play Resident Evil 4. Resident Evil 4 is stillone of the few games that blends action and horror together in a enjoyable way. As for the story, it's phenomenal. In nine hours, the game narrates a darker, unsettling, depressing, and hopeful story that has gripped my heart many times throughout.  It's a simple story, about a knight sent by the king to save the princess, and you might think that I am writting about a different game, but no we are stilll talking about Resident Evil 4. The story has  wonderful symbollism throughout, where the story is a modern day representation of those tales of knights. You have Leon, who is a agent (knight) sent by the president (King) to save his daughter (princess), and his tale of killing the monsters (las plagas). I won't spoil anything, but you definately leave the story feeling good and uplifted by the act of Heroism that Leon displays many times, which I quite franckly miss. I think it's a rather crude and dark time we live in when we're inundated with dark depressing stories, like Last of Us, where the protagonist commit flat out evil, and we're supposed to pretend that it's a "serious story about the frailty of man" or some other nonsense like that. One could say that it's meant to be a much more serious reflection of character study, but since we live in such selfish and turbulent times, where women will kill their own children, or men abandone their children because of personal reason, at what point does it cease to be "character study"and an opportunity to say for ourselves, "Well i guess it's ok to kill  someone for whom I love". How much of it is it just us trying to justify great moral evil to make us, "deep and complex".  I appreciate a story like Resident Evil 4 where I'm moved by the "simple" virtuous hero overcoming the  "deep and complex" evil S.O.B's. It's an uplifting story that refreshes my soul after playing it.If your thinking of buying it, please do. It's a fantastic game.
