_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has completed the original RE4 countless times across various platforms, I’ll admit I was a bit nervous when the rumor train starting running about a 4 REmake. Could they really capture lightning in a bottle twice?By god they did it.In comparison to recent remakes like Dead Space, RE4 isn’t as strict in copy pasting the original game with enhanced graphics and minor changes. No, this is very much a different game, but that really works in it’s favor. Fans of the original will have their expectations subverted throughout it’s relatively lengthy campaign. While I’d say 80% of the content from the original is still there, it always feels like there is a twist to it, or a different order, or something added to it that sets it apart from the original. That missing 20% of content shockingly doesn’t feel missed, since the new stuff outweighs what is missing in my opinion.The gameplay is absolutely fantastic. They do a genuinely good job making you feel like an action hero by parrying and ducking attacks, reacting to stuns, constantly changing your weapons as fights evolve etc. I feel like I can get into a psychological flow state when playing this game, and it looks and feels amazing once you do. Next to MGSV, the is easily the most fun I’ve had playing a third person shooter of sorts.The game of course still has nods to the quirkiness of the original, while till retaining an overall darker tone. It’s a fine line they are treading, but they do it well. Leon’s quips are on point, and his relationship with Ashley throughout the game is much improved. A minor gripe I have with the game is that I don’t find the voice acting for Ada and Krauser to be very good. Also, they cut out a lot of Ada’s appearances in the original game, but hopefully that will be made up for in a DLC. On a more positive note, the story is way more cohesive and makes much more sense than the original.On top of everything, this game is loaded with an in-game achievement system with about 100 challenges to do that gives you points for an extra shop (similar to the RE2 and 3 remakes). With the additional free mercenaries mode coming, you get a lot for your dollar here. I’ve always found the Resident Evil franchise to be one of the most replayable franchises of all time, and I fully believe this remake will be something I will revisit time and time again like I did with the original for the last 15+ years It’s near perfect so far, and I can’t wait to start speed running it.

_childDocuments_.review: As I sat down to play the Resident Evil 4 remake, a flood of memories came rushing back. I remembered the days when I was just a kid, watching my older brother, John, masterfully navigate through the eerie and thrilling world of the original Resident Evil 4. He made it look so easy, effortlessly taking down hordes of infected villagers and towering monstrosities.John was my hero, my protector, and my gaming mentor. Those nights spent on the couch, watching him play, were some of the best moments of my childhood. He would laugh at my squeals of fear and reassure me that it was just a game, but his bravery and skill were anything but imaginary.The remake was a bittersweet experience. On one hand, I was reliving a cherished part of my childhood, but on the other, the absence of John was a painful reminder of the void he had left in my life. He had passed away just a year before the game's release, and the fact that he couldn't share this new adventure with me was a cruel twist of fate.As I delved deeper into the game, I couldn't help but imagine how John would have reacted to the updated graphics, the refined gameplay, and the nostalgia that washed over me. I could almost hear his voice, offering guidance and tips as if he were right there beside me.With every zombie that I encountered, I felt a mix of excitement and sorrow. Excitement for the game's amazing recreation of a classic, and sorrow for the brother I had lost. It was as if the game had become a bridge between my past and the present, a way for me to connect with John one more time.The final boss battle in the game was an emotional climax. It was a moment of triumph mixed with tears, as I couldn't help but wish John were there to witness it. I could almost hear his proud voice saying, "You did it, little brother."As the credits rolled and I put the controller down, I realized that Resident Evil 4, both the original and the remake, had given me a gift. It allowed me to relive precious memories and pay tribute to the brother who had introduced me to the world of gaming. The sadness of his absence would never fade, but through the game, I found a way to keep his memory alive, even in the face of a bittersweet and poignant journey.I miss you John.

_childDocuments_.review: A slight deviation from the previous Resident Evil formula, diving more into Action and a little less Horror, but don't let that scare you away. Giving it a fresh breath of air while still dealing with the same looming threat and adding to the overall lore. With this RE being a more action focused title than the last ones, the gameplay is also improved. Feeling responsive and high stakes. It's not sluggish anywhere in the game despite not being completely fast paced.It's a much longer experience than the first two remakes. Easily clocking in 9 hours from start to finish, longer if you go around collecting secrets which you might end up doing thanks to the beautiful level design and the game rewarding your exploration.A shop along with a shopkeeper is introduced where you can buy and upgrade new weapons as you progress through the game allowing for a customizable arsenal and gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: In an age of disappointing and sometimes outright insulting remakes or reboots of old games and movies, this was actually surprisingly really enjoyable. I recommend it, you can stop reading here if you want.I'm going to preface the rest of this by saying i did my first (and only) play-through on hardcore difficulty and i did a semi-completionist run (going back to old areas and making sure i got everything, beating all the optional "bosses", etc). So keep that in mind. This Segways into my only negative point:Provided you manage your cash effectively the difficulty was a bit lacking i felt. I feel like i only died like a handful of times the entire play-through and i defeated every boss but major krauser and the twin giants in the foundry first try. I'm not saying that to show off or anything. I just feel like most of the games difficulty even on hardcore revolved around the games shop and crafting system. As long as you think your purchases through, dont waste ammo and dont sell incomplete jewellery you'll probably be well-equipped to able to deal with any situation the game throws at you and you'll never really feel challenged as a player all that much. If you didnt manage your money properly i can see it being a bit of a struggle. but personally I would have preferred the difficulty be more to do with player skill than a players purchasing choices and willingness to to side-quests and treasure hunts.Other than that if you have a graphics card powerful enough to max the graphics out it looks amazing. Lighting is top-tier indoors especially.The gameplay was re-worked making it new and interesting but it was still being faithful to the original. So points for that too.all in all I enjoyed it, it was fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I entered the series back then with RE2. Huge fan, loved the way the game worked. Also played RE3 a lot and loved it. Went on to Code Veronica and loved it. And then RE4 came and I lost interest in the series. The shift in gameplay and atmosphere was just too big and too crass. Also I never liked Leon or Ashley much tbh.The remake doesnt invent the generic story new, nor does it change the horribly flat characters Leon and Ashley, nor their non-existent chemistry or interactions (but honestly I blame games like Last of Us, The Telltale Walking Dead and A Plague Tale for that. You cant beat any of those duos easily.) But they gameplay is fun, the graphics are good, I did not encounter a single bug in my entire playthrough. Yes, the mechanics are clunky. Yes, in the endgame every boss gotta have his predictable mutations. Yes, none of the antagonists have a real story. (Village did that much better)BUT, I still enjoyed coming back to it every time. And also foreshadowing: The DLC Seperate Ways is really, really good and made it obvious they learned from some mistakes they did in the maingame.Excited to see where they are gonna take RE next.

_childDocuments_.review: The Separate Ways DLC fixed many problems I had with the base game. Despite my lingering feelings about how the base game handled some things, the full package of RE4R with Separate Ways is a 10/10. For me, it still doesn't replace the original game, but it's an excellent product on its own.Resident Evil 4 2005 is my favorite game in the series, so I went in with some high expectations.  They weren’t all met, but overall, Resident Evil 4 Remake is a very good game.  I don’t think it outdoes the original (although it came close) due to a few key areas where the developers just didn’t really understand why the original was so good.  The serious, grisly tone of the remakes does away with too much of the character and pizazz that made the originals so beloved.  Here are some pros and cons to hopefully highlight why I felt that way.-The gameplay has been refined to a T.  It feels so good to play.  I love the addition of the possibility of stealth if you want.  Feels great.-They did a great job of making the game feel scary, despite the original game’s reputation of being action-horror.  It feels like a great blend of RE2, RE3, and RE7.  I really enjoyed that.-Lots of homages to the classic game in really cool ways, expressed through level design and lines of dialogue.-Ashley is awesome, the new version of her character is a refreshing change and I would love to see her come back in a future RE game.-The Merchant’s shooting range has been given so much love, it’s fantastic.-The village portion of the game has been expanded in all the right ways, I thought it was great.  Really awesome.- has been massively improved this time around!  It felt like kind of an afterthought in the original, but in this game it’s really good.-As with Resident Evil 2 Remake and Resident Evil 3 Remake, too much content has been cut/changed for my liking.  They did add some new content as well which is awesome.  But, they cut some iconic stuff, dude… That hurt.  On that note… Capcom… why isn’t Ramon wearing his hat, yet statues of him have it?  Why doesn’t Leon ask Ramon if his right hand comes off??   You’re gonna make me cry!  Here are a couple of lists of things they removed, : -Some character redesigns just didn't vibe with me, with Ramon being the biggest offender.-Ada suffers a bad case of character assassination.  I'm not a fan of her new voice or personality.  She comes across as cold and uninterested instead of mysterious and playful like every single other time she appears in the franchise.  She's also missing her iconic red dress.  This just ain’t it, chief. -On the subject of Ada, her unlockable "Seperate Ways" campaign isn't included in the game and is probably going to be DLC.  This is something I'm kind of mixed on, but ultimately it's a con because it's content they're removing and selling back to us later.-I felt that the antagonists really weren’t given enough of a spotlight in the remake, to the point where I’d almost recommend you should play the original version of the game first just to get a full sense of their characters.  Here, they feel more like typical bad guys who show up a few times.  In the original, they were more present in the story.  They would call Leon on his radio and have conversations with him.  You felt more of a connection to them/vendetta against them.  That’s been reduced to occasional taunting, and a short conversation here and there.  Meh.-I think it would be funny if you could still upskirt Ashley, even if you couldn't see anything.  It was a funny detail in the original game with her calling Leon a pervert.  They could’ve made it so you get an achievement if you do it at one specific part of the game or something, leaving a permanent stamp on your account like Nier Automata. Oh well, not a big deal. But a missed opportunity imo.-The Merchant’s voice acting is great, but just can’t compete with the original Merchant’s.  Also, I don’t like how infrequently the Merchant says “What’re ya buyin’?”  It feels like just an easter egg even though it’s supposed to be one of his main lines.-Some weapons have been neutered, like how you can’t give the Red9, my fav RE4 pistol, -A silly 'cinematic' sequence where you're forced to move really slow in a dramatic story moment.  I can't stand parts like this in games.  It's alright the first time, but it's annoying on replays.Resident Evil 4 is a flawed but very fun remake.  I enjoyed my time with it.  I feel similarly to how I felt with the other remakes.  Great games in their own right, but they don’t seem to fully understand what made the originals so enjoyable.  I love the first half of the game.  But, the second half left me disappointed enough by the ending that I just can’t give it the perfect 10/10 I gave the original.  9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like remakes. Maybe you'll "recapture the magic" or whatever, but you'll probably just ruin something great for future generations. Well, I was wrong. This time. RE4 Remake takes the 2004 original and translates it perfectly into a shooter from 2023. Does it reinvent the genre, the way the original did? No. But it was never going to do that. It isn't *trying* to do that. Leon is a different guy in the remake. Still sexy, still funny, but younger and less of a smirking badass. Something lost, something gained; he's more believable, and it's easier to imagine him never getting over his experiences with Ada. Every location and set piece from the original is here, except U-3, which sucked anyway, and you know it. Some parts, like the shooting gallery, are significantly improved. Other things, like hiding ulockables behind speedruns -- "remember, don't play the game, just run past it" I had to keep reminding myself -- are worse. There's a tendency to suggest that the art is muted and "soulless" in the remake, but it's not. Watch all the comparisons you want, but when you're playing the actual game, the art fits the atmosphere and that atmosphere is immersive and, unlike the original, occasionally stressful and scary. Also, Ashley is so much better in the remake I feel like Capcom deserves a reward of some kind. A medal. Maybe some kind of plaque. "Fixed Ashely," it would say. New Ashley is neither a helpless damsel nor a shrewish jerk, and when Leon bends to help her up over a ledge or catches her after a big jump, you really care about her. When she fights to save you and screams in terror after you take a big hit, you really feel like she cares about you. Really, a medal. A statuette, maybe, like at the Oscars. RE4R is harder than the original. The two difficulties: "normal" and "professional" are traded for four very different experiences: Easy, Normal, Hardcore, and Professional. All the best stuff requires doing Professional, and doing it quickly. And professional sucks. I mean, no, it's great I guess, but it's *hard*. And if, like me, you suck at video games, you'll probably end up playing parts of the game over and over again. I've put over 200 hours into a game you can *technically* beat in 4. Do the math. Anyway, it's doable, but it's a huge jump in difficulty over the original. Finally, do yourself a favor and download two mods from Nexus. One that mutes Leon's cough -- he makes this little noise when he aims, over and over again, it's baffling and irritating -- and another that cuts Ashley's sex noises. What sex noises, you ask? Well, when she runs, she makes endless little hentai sounds that are fun for about 2 minutes, but after that are just distracting. Muting these noises will *dramatically* improve your gameplay experience, and won't take away from the actual game. I promise. Anyway, go ahead and drop the money on this one, if you liked the original. All the jokes and stuff are in here. You won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll be honest: when I heard that they were remaking , I wasn’t sure about it. I mean, the original is one of my favorite games and, since I play it every couple of years, I believe the old one still holds up to this day. I thought remaking it would be “gilding the lily”, as they say.But, I’m glad to report that I was wrong. I still think that the original is fantastic, but the quality-of-life improvements made to the remake were needed to make it relevant in the modern age of games. This game is drop-dead gorgeous, the action is more fluid than ever, and the story has been improved by a lot. It somehow has something for everyone – modern gamers that haven’t played the original and fans of the original that needed an excuse to play it again.A lot has been changed. There are almost no QTEs in the game anymore. Sections that seemed to stretch on have been shortened or combined with other lengthy sections. The island (considered by many to be the weakest point in the game) has been optimized so that it doesn’t feel like it drags on. Ashley’s mechanics have been improved to the point that she’s not really a burden anymore – she doesn’t even need yellow herbs this time around, thank god!It’s not all coming up roses, though. There are memorable parts of the original that didn’t make the cut. The lava-filled rooms in the castle, for one. The gondola in village, for another. Oh, and all of the times that trucks come barreling at Leon and he has to shoot them to death before he gets run over? Those are gone, too. I kind of feel like getting rid of those parts was unnecessary… But I’m not a game developer, so I don’t can’t say ♥♥♥♥ about it.But, really, those are the only things I can think of that are missing. Everything else is here and it’s ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ great! And, some of the things that were cut were replaced with new sequences that are totally badass in their own right.They absolutely outdid themselves when it comes to the game’s tone, too. I’d say it’s much scarier than before. (To be fair, I didn’t think the original was all that scary to begin with…) In the original, the castle was a bright and shiny spectacle of extravagance but, in the remake, everything is dingier and darker and covered in blood. Somehow, though, in making the game darker, they didn’t compromise the game’s humor. Leon interjects with dad jokes at the perfect times. And, I won’t spoil anything, but the best of his one-liners comes right as the player beats the final boss. I’ll remember that for a long, long time. I could go on about this game for hours. I’ve already decided that it’s my Game of the Year and very possibly my GOAT. Instead, though, I’m going to go bask in the afterglow of having beaten this one again for the first time. Play it if you can – you won’t regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: As one of the numerous people who considers the original RE4 to be one of the greatest games of all time, I was skeptical going into the remake. _childDocuments_.review: It's fine, yeah? It's totally fine. Playable, no bugs, looks good, performance is fine. Now releasing RE4 again is just plain. DOOM knew this and modernized the genre like the original did back in the day. And to top it all off, at least the Dead Space Remake did necessary improvements to the game. This is just closer to a remaster than to a RE2 type remake.It's obviously worse than its predecessors who already improved on its own formula years back. Setting is more boring than Village, so is its enemy roster. Horror and atmosphere is worse than RE7. Gameplay mecanics and uniqueness is miles below Dead Space original limb dismemberment and weapon design. You get me ? And to top it all off, the game is too bloody long. Several times I think it's gonna finally end and it proceeds to take me to a new map.EDIT: NO! ITS NOT FINE! 20 hours later this stupid game is still going with Ashely being kidnapped a 4th time. At this point I'm powering though it out of spite. _childDocuments_.review: [Early impressions]I played the ♥♥♥♥ out of the original RE4 and had it on both GameCube and PC. I've beaten it numerous times. When I fired up the game for the first time, it advised me if I played the 2005 release, then pick hardcore.Do not pick hardcore.Hardcore restricts your resources hard. The village was a stiff challenge but manageable. By the time I got to the castle, I was getting reduced to zero ammo in every room that had enemies. I don't know what my accuracy stat was, but I know I wasn't missing THAT many shots. There are a lot of significant changes to the gameplay (none of which I'd consider bad), so there's a big learning curve. In fact, someone who's used to how the original works may find their habits are working against them in this game. Finding treasures wasn't a nice bonus--I HAD to. I shudder to think how much harder it would've been otherwise.Is hardcore _unfair_? I suppose not. But what it did was push me to my absolute limit and with some games when you up the difficulty enough, you start needing to play the meta game in order to progress. I found myself doing things like manipulating the distance at which enemies would aggro me, spending crafting resources in such a way that I could control what items would drop from a crate/vase/whatever. I started to git gud, but I didn't like the experience it was giving me. I fired up a brand new game, set it to the standard difficulty, and now I'm enjoying myself.Is it too easy? Maybe. I have more than enough bullets to get the job done, and the last time I checked I have an abundant supply of grenades, far more than I would get in the original. However, if I fool around, I die. I haven't looked up the specifics of how each difficulty works, so I don't know what kinds of things, if any, the game is doing to adjust the difficulty on the fly, but I'll tell you this: it's FUN. It feels like RE4 again. So I like that the option to play the hardcore mode is in the game, but even if you're familiar with the original, I wouldn't recommend this difficulty the first time through. You need to get acquainted with how the remake plays, unless you like your level of challenge to be SADISTIC.Anyway, the original is a classic, and the remake captures the essence. Changes have been made for the better, such as Ashely's previously awkward dialogue to something more fitting. Additionally, the remake clarifies that Ashley's actions, like running away from Leon in the castle, are due to the plagas, addressing the original's ambiguity.A possible flaw in this game is as I'm exploring areas for goodies, I feel like I'm often running in circles and checking the map. That might be a me thing, but I'm not so sure I agree with some of the changes to the layout of this game. In the original, I thought the game flowed really smoothly and I didn't have to check the map but a couple times--throughout the entire game. I won't pass judgement on it yet, but I'm not sure if I'm completely onboard with needing to backtrack in order to unlock drawers and chests.

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike RE2 and RE3, RE4 is actually good and is a nearly perfect remake of the original game, but it does come with some serious problems that some people, like myself, are frustrated at+The game is a near perfect remake, even adding some new areas that feel organic and good to traverse+Gameplay is faster and more responsive, in most ways+A few bosses have been entirely reworked and for the better+Challenges return from the last few games and remakes, with unlockable items such as guns and accessories with unique buffs+The soundtrack updates and improves upon the original OST in many good waysWith all these upsides, there are downsides that I cannot overlook-It follows the same trend of the last two remakes, though not as much, of just removing content for no reason, or at least a good reason-Professional is just unfair at many points in the game, especially with how aggressive the enemies are-Ashley, while so much better in this game, gets grabbed way too often because of the aggressive enemies, even if there are none nearby, they'll just seemingly teleport and pick her up, they're that fast-The difficulty can spike drastically early on, even just in Hardcore-The hit detection is quite buggy, especially with dodging just not working, and even getting stunlocked to deathI like RE4, way more than the OG, but it's missing that charm and just further proves that Capcom doesn't really understand what made the original games so perfect. Yes, these games look and play so much better, but the constant cutting of content, big or small, for no discernible reason, is getting on peoples nerves. Removing U3, the PRL, and the sewers with the Novistadors doesn't make sense, since they were pretty good parts of the original. Yes, some people hated the sewers, but the creepy atmosphere and introduction to the Novi's was memorableFinal verdict, the game is amazingly good, but Capcom needs to stop removing content from these remakes. What ever happened to RE1's style of remakes, being completely faithful down to the letter?8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Capcom was risking a lot remaking RE4, one of the most beloved entries in the series.Yet they were able not only in respecting the original, but also to improve it!Absolutely recommend, one of the best Resident evil!Spoilers Ahead:A lot has changed since the original, making for a better pacing and a better experience fitting of the more serious tone of the remakes.There is still the right amount of campiness and Leon is full of cheesy one-liners but it never goes over the top. So no more rolling boulders or self moving 40mts statues and magma filled rooms. The gameplay has improved drastically, no more tank movements that means leon can shoot while moving, but that also mean way more aggresive and fast enemies that will swarm you and keep you on your toes.The resource managements is one of the best in the seires, forcing you to choose not only what weapons and ammo to bring around, but also what bullet to craft and how you want to use your knife. Sometimes it might be worth to keep an extra knife for protection, instead of dispatching an enemy faster.I know that a lot of people will have something bad to say about this chapter, it is granted with a title that made the history of both the franchise and gaming as a whole, but Capcom did not miss.They really did something amazing and this game deserves to be played.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 4 Remake (RE4R) takes place a couple years post events of Raccoon City. Leon, one of the protagonists of RE2R, is part of a U.S. government agency. His task: save the president’s daughter, Ashely Graham from a sketchy village in Spain. It doesn’t take long to realize that this is far from a normal search and rescue mission as Leon finds that villagers are all affected by some sort of parasite. The villagers are affected by the infection known as Las Plagas. Leons sneaking suspicion is proved true when he meets Luis Serra and finds out this is another Umbrella outbreak. Soon after Leon is infected with Las Plagas. During his adventure he eventually finds Ashley but is burdened with the task to not only heal himself but foil another Umbrella outbreak. Throughout the journey you will run into some familiar faces and witness the typical action story foibles. Losing the cure, your escape not working out, and world domination. The story here isn’t anything revolutionary, but the production makes for a fun ride.  RE4R was revolutionary back in 2004 for its turn into a 3rd person survival shooter. But just going off what we have here, the RE Engine really lets this gameplay style shine. RE4R still has a more action like feel compared to its previous counterparts. This isn’t necessarily a negative though. With the new technology comes the re-envisioning of the enemies. RE4R may not be as scary as the previous titles but its shooting and arcade-y play make it standout. Although the game feels VERY heavy, it forces you to be intentional with your movement. You CAN move and shoot in this iteration of the game but its so slow that you’re practically stuck in place when shooting. This forces you to be purposeful in your positioning and movement. To help with this heaviness, RE4R introduces the parrying mechanic. Parrying allows you to counter various melee attacks and throwables to give you more of a fighting chance when planted to shoot. Understanding this is extremely important when it comes to bosses and what I’ll call heavy enemies. Although there was a boss/enemy or two that flustered me, I enjoyed the challenge presented. All the tools in your arsenal are good at dealing with some enemies to an extent, and its important to exploit that to the fullest. Leon’s arsenal can be upgraded but is still limited in resident evil fashion to a grid-based storage case. If it fits, you can keep it. Ammo, grenades, etc. can be crafted if the game isn’t being generous enough with its drops. All of this culminates in a tight feeling ride through Leon’s very unfortunate situation which you get to blast your way through and solve. To no one’s surprise RE4R is a mostly linear, chapter-based game. There is some freedom on your exploration, but mainly get from point A to B. The limited amount of freedom is to complete bounties offered by the lovable merchant. Completing his request will net you with currency to trade-in for some valuable that’ll help you along in your travels. Every so often when you visit him, he’ll have an elevator behind him that will take you to a carnival style shooting range that will test your trigger finger. Having a steady trigger finger rewards you with tokens that you use on a gumball machine that gives charms for your briefcase. The keychains give small effects that improve a gameplay mechanic in some way. Lastly, since this game is supposed to be run multiple times, there are plenty of challenges to complete. It is technically impossible to get them all done in the first run. Therefore, you’ll be running the game multiple times. As intimidating as that may sound, if you break down the challenges you’re trying to complete, your NewGame+ run becomes stronger and faster. Before you know it, you’ll be beating the game on the hardest difficulty because you maxed out all weapons and have an infinite rocket launcher. The music didn’t really do much for me in this title. I wasn’t aware of any eerie or ominous background music. If I recall correctly, I feel as though most of the time was filled with silence. The only time there was any musical scores worth noticing was in boss battle. Even then, they felt generic. RE4R is more of a technical marvel. One could say the art direction here naturally improves because of that technical step. Enemies are fleshed out to look more threatening. And certain areas instill a bit more anxiety because of the lighting, or lack thereof. In the end the animators struck gold with RE Engine. If this graphics suite continues to improve over time, Capcom will be a video game giant for the foreseeable future.

Weapon balancing is a slight negative due to nostalgia of the original and bullsh*t RNG bullet spread in some weapons. _childDocuments_.review: Did I like everything about this remake? No, I did not. But when looking at all of the things they had to get right and so many things that could have gone horribly wrong, I struggle to call RE4 Remake anything other than a triumph. Some of the things I did not like were some atmosphere changes, dialogue changes, the gutting of certain characters such as Ramon Salazar, and the cardinal sin of making Serenity only audible in the Merchant Menu. Despite this, they absolutely nailed the most crucial part: the gameplay. The gameplay stays true to the foundation of the original while adding much more depth and fluidity with the new added mechanics. Not only does it not get even remotely stale after a full playthrough, but I felt like I had only scratched the surface after beating the game on Professional. I will undoubtedly spend many more playthroughs trying to get a higher campaign rank while mastering the game's mechanics. In terms of the story, most changes made were very reasonable and made sense. I also felt that character changes made to Leon, Ashley, and Luis were very well done. Leon is less like an alphabro who never takes anything seriously and is now a deeper character that at times uses humor to cope with present and past trauma. Ashley feels much less like a hyper-annoying damsel and now feels like an innocent girl who shows she can be capable when it counts. Luis is for the most part the same, but his role in the campaign is expanded with a brand new section where you fight with him and his character is further fleshed out.Overall, the changes made RE4 Remake into a more serious story with likable characters and a fantastic combat loop, while still capturing the essence of the original. I honestly couldn't have asked for anything more than that. For those who still prefer the atmosphere of the original or the campy, cheesy dialogue, the OG is still there for you to play. TL;DR: Great Remake with mostly reasonable changes. 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game during my first playthrough (mostly). But the more I replay the worse I actually feel about this game. Read on (contains spoilers). Written after 5 completions across all difficulties.Story:I miss the whimsy and cheesy dialog in the original; I think it's a shame they dropped that but I enjoyed the story changes although once again we fail to get any justifiable reason Krauser has such a grudge against Leon (explanation is awfully weak). Given the more serious tone of the game this time around, Ashley is far too positive sounding and acting, like some kind of valley girl at the mall. She is seeing people all around have their heads explode, why is she like this? Voice acting is overall decent otherwise, although Ada is bland as hell.Visuals: Looks stunning, although why is everything so dark that post-village I have to wack the various brightness settings up to their absolute limit just to see anything. Following the setup instructions for the 'best experience' correctly achieved nothing except let me miss out of so many gorgeous details. Multiple monitors exhibited the same thing.Audio:Love it; soundtrack is excellent, there was a lot of love here clearly. Covered Ashley's voice above; the voice actress does a good job, ignoring the fact the character as a whole is utterly unbelievable in her actions and voice lines.Gameplay:Honestly it's extremely medicore and riddled with small-to-medium issues. This is basically just a list of all my gripes.* First and foremost is this game suffers from so, so many softlock areas, mostly in the second half. If you don't have enough of the right ammunition for the next fight, it becomes a frustrating 'hope for crit or reset' experience.* Your knife and body armor wearing out feels like another one of those copy-minecraft gameplay additions that doesn't seem to serve any purpose beyond 'longer gameplay feature list=better'. It adds nothing pleasant to the gameplay.* Plagas infected enemies have no consistency. From the get-go we are told that plagas die to Flash grenades. However there are plenty that just don't, who knows why? Knights have to to knock the head off, despite the plagas already being visible. Confusing visual cue. Iron maiden/regenerator with exposed plagas are also uanffected even though the plagas is exposed. El Gigante also has exposed plagas and nothing happens.* Why do chainsaw villagers not get staggered like normal enemies? There is no setup for them being inherently tougher than anyone else. Except now you learn the hard (and confusing) way they a shotgun to the face doesn't stop them like the other enemies they look alike and are surrounded by. It seems to be damage based to make them stagger now?, so just keep unloading into them.* Parrying, while a nice idea, feels half-baked (like the original melee actions fwiw). By this I mean that everything just stops while parrying a chainsaw villager, and you're immune to explosives during that time. It lacks any immersion and feels poorly implemented; no Iframes when climbing a ladder, but Iframes when stabbing someone?* El Gigantes can stun lock you in the first encounter.* The 3 big baddies as a whole are uninspired and boring fights. Mendes has 2 attacks total which he just loops on a timer in stage 1. Stage 2 is just run back and forwards waiting for a barrel. It feels like sonic '06 level depth gameplay. Salazar is just a boring 'try not to have line of sight' fight where he basically does the same attack over and over. Saddler was fine I guess, but the 'summon bugs' attack is so lazy honestly. Instead of doing anything interesting lets just have a bunch of enemies from earlier in the game spawn again.* Some of the puzzle rooms are designed in such an impossibly unrealistic way. It's RE, I don't expect 'real world' type stuff. But the brief sewer puzzle on the island with Ashley holding the door is so laughably bad. You can see the challenge from a mile away, but its compounded with a room layout so laughably unusable for its purpose that it loses all immersion again. Also all the island electronic lock puzzles are just awful; who playtested those and said "yeah that's good"?* Enemy AI seems to be tethered or cordoned to certain areas. You can be chased by certain enemies in many areas, and they will just stand and watch you once you pass through many doorways rather than continue to chase. Is this an AI limitation? There is a surprise Iron Maiden fight in the sewers (right before the previous bullet point) where you can just walk back through the doorframe that led to the arena and the Iron Maiden just wanders away until you step back in.* Typewriters are awfully located. There are multiple areas where the Typewriter is placed at the start of a long, EMPTY, corridor that leads to a tough fight. This creates a straight up waste of time if you die and need to retry; you have to keep walking the same path over and over.* Ashley incapacitation feels like it was implemented AFTER most of the set-pieces. Her incapacitation often just leads to a reset in these sequences; its too hard to recover her quickly enough after a random axe flies across the screen and cleaves her head open* Mercenaries updates are awesome. I miss Waterworld and the double chainsaw guys though.* The Mine cart section feels way too scripted now that villagers don't get on your cart. It's also so long and the environment so massive that I can no longer suspend disbelief that it exists, or that anyone ever even found the Plagas nest in the caves. Seriously; the discovery lore dates back far enough that anyone who found their way in would never have been able to get back out (far too many cliffs, chasms and combined with the cart ride several miles of total darkness).* Good effort with the merchant. I wish he kept his iconic lines, although I like his new ones too. The side quest tasks are a good addition, although most are quite repetitive (Shoot the Medallion #6 anyone? Really, they couldn't be more creative than that? Especially when they had the great sidequest of backtracking to take down the golden knight).* Wtf is the point of the Striker exclusive upgrade now ammunition is much harder to conserve, and upgrades don't refill the clip like in the original.* The environment is filled with 'theres a fallen tree at knee height that blocks your path' type things. The most ridiculous part I am referring to is the Dynamite room in the mines. Given that in the very next room Leon boosts Luis higher than the ledge you are forced to walk around in the dynamite room it's hilariously badly designed; can't boost a guy 6ft, but 8ft in the next room is totally fine.* If you click load game and choose auto-save after dying your in-game timer isn't reset to the time in the loaded auto-save, but it is if you quit to menu. Another obvious lack of attention to detail that leads to confusing inconsistencies in-game and wasting time avoiding this (bug?).* Want to add a special note for the cabin; it's the ultimate representative of problems with the game for a more casual player (purely anecdoatally, but none of my friends who didn't player the original much enjoyed this; they found it to be a frustrating experience of RNG; some experienced players enjoyed it more). I'm glad this sequence was kept in, but it's the ultimate soft-lock point in the game, made worse by the drops from the crates in the house being random. Have no heavy artillery left for the finale? Better keep loading then quitting to menu at the start of the fight until you get a decent ammo drop. There are too many enemies when combined with the bad aim and random stun mechanics (cool 3 headshots didn't break their charge or stagger them now I'm stunlocked...)* Dude still taking a wizz in Mendez's toilet even after ~17 years. Glad they kept that.SummaryIt's not a terrible game, but it really needs it's flaws recognised; summarized in 1 word: "Inconsistency".8000 characters.

There is nothing more annoying than having a target dead in your crosshairs, pulling the trigger, and watching the shot somehow land nowhere near what you were aiming for. Why is this in the game? The second, is the knife execution mechanic. Capcom decided to bind the knife attack key and the execution key to the same input. This means that every time you attempt to get the one-hit kill on an enemy (Which is crucial on higher difficulties) you may miss it and instead watch Leon awkwardly slash at the enemy and do next to no damage, and by the time you've recovered, the prompt is gone. This is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ infuriating, and it's entirely unnecessary. Capcom, let us rebind the execution key. Please.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game with gripes. I enjoyed a lot the combat mechanics and changes in the game. The Ashley alone segment is a bit better but it comes at the cost of an intense firefight I loved in the original.- Most the ham of the game has been cut off and worse lines have been put in their place. One involving the K***hts was disappointing, as was a chunk of Ramon Salazar's character. Character development was more towards making you sympathetic towards the Big Cheese and Luis. I preferred Luis being a lying little sack trying to redeem himself a little. This forced stuff? No thanks, Bro.- Ada Wong is more like Ada Wrong, Wesker is more like Wisker. As is the main character she's speaking to at the end, it's just badly directed like they didn't care about it.So, some things I really don't like, however it's a very good remake of the game. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best games of all time. Again.When this Remake was announced, I was actually very sceptical, as the original RE4 is one of the most impactful games of the last 20 years and I think it aged actually very well and is totally worth playing today. So I was unsure if a complete remake is actually that good of an idea. Luckily, I was very wrong. This game is at the same time faithful to the original title and its intentions, while updating graphics, gameplay and presentation to (and above) modern standards. The overall tone is a bit less "cheesy" than the original, which can remove a bit of the B-movie factor, but it also straightens out the few more... questionable scenes in the original that have aged less gracefully than the rest.The setpieces work just as well as in the original in almost all cases. Only the often copied scene and the final boss can be slightly more frustrating than they were before. I am a bit saddened that one of the bosses of the original game was cut, but I can see that it would have been a bit of an awkward fit...Overall just a great game. Fantastic presentation, great voice acting, fun gameplay, the best setpieces in the business and an enganging (if slightly simple) story. The prime example of what the RE series can be. No matter if you are an old fan or have never played Resident Evil, you do not want to miss this.

_childDocuments_.review: No, this game is disappointing. I mean, it is good to see Leon return for another adventure in the series and the game itself is quite a playable action game. Once you have reached the village, things turn quite mechanical from that point onwards. I just felt I was turning up at these locations, shooting zombies before they got near me, finding door keys, and then on my way again.Also, the story was weak. I got why the villages were zombified, from the earlier games, but I did not understand why I was encountering Plate Armour springing into life. _childDocuments_.review: RE4 Remake is the best 3rd person action shooter ever made. Which is saying a lot, because the original game that was it's basis and inspiration was also the best 3rd person action shooter of it's time back in 2004. I have played this game many times through, and even played it with friends on stream (despite it being single player) and have even inspired friends to do the more challenging modes and runs and settings of this game. I could write about it all day, it's that good, but I'll narrow down why I like this game so much with this: Every enemy, every gun, every door, every window, every bear trap, every treasure, every document and photo, all the locations, all the upgrades--- Everything, serves a purpose that is deeper than what first meets the eyes, which makes completing the various levels on different difficulty settings and acquiring achievements requires creativity and attention to detail and a WILL to explore and learn. I love this game, it's a good thing too, because if Capcom didn't make this game as good as it is (which is perfect) there would have been hell to be raised by fans of the old one... And by god I am a huge fan of the old one. And now this one. Please, for your sake, play this game. Also, Don't quit, it's very difficult. But with some practice and research into the mechanics-- I think you'll be able to rightfully pass or conquer all foes and challenges you meet here. And then you'll want to do it again, because it's so much fun. Thanks for reading. Have a great day whatever you may be doing. Tell your loved ones-- everyday- that you love them. Trust me, if something happens and you don't get the chance-- you'll be kicking yourself. Thanks againRyderP.s. I love you Anne.

_childDocuments_.review: RE4 is an awesome action survival horror game with lots of replay-ability through the different difficulties and rewards the player greatly for accomplishing S+ ranks for it. I could not enjoy the original RE4 due to motion sickness and I am glad that they remade this game with motion sickness accessibility in the options. _childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly really enjoyed this title and feel it is true and genuine to the original. I feel if you enjoyed the original then this is a must-have for sure no questions asked Mercenaries felt pretty good too, shame Ada wasn't in originally, maybe in the future and being able to bob and weave with Krauser and his stance animations was pretty awesome to sorta feel like he did during the knife fights with Leon.EDIT: I saw the store page and had to comment on this. DO NOT BUY EXCLUSIVE UPGRADE TICKETS FROM THE STORE. Everyone knows the site for modding (idk if it's allowed to specify so I won't but rhymes with Lexus. You can download any of the plentiful merchant mods and have a field day with tokens and upgrade tickets if you cannot be bothered to ♥♥♥♥ with it all.) I don't care if you like modding or a vanilla experience. The exclusive upgrade tickets are not hard to get and even if you don't like them, do not go out of your way to spend money and be charged for ♥♥♥♥ like this.I'll start with the downsides I (personally) feel about this game and want to start off that I played the original many times over on gamecube, wii, ps2, ps3/ps4.  Edit: And the stupid exclusive tickets in the store page.As far as downsides go there are some areas that have been removed from the game that will be added soon like Separate Ways.-The U3 fight is no longer featured in the remake-QTE's are removed-Incen grenades are removed-The laser room is removed-The lava/fire room in the castle is removed.There may be a few more things removed or missing but nothing super obvious right off the bat. You could consider that not being able to send every item to storage could be considered a bad thing but I feel it's pretty much like the original and forces you to choose what you want to keep and of course upgrade the size of your case. (I think it's good but it's something I've had friends gripe about.)I think that the charm system (Most notably the method of acquiring them) is just not ideal and maybe I'm whining but it's tied to save/playthru and you can't save/reload and get different charms if you don't like what you get. The only differences when it comes to what charms you'll acquire on your playthru is the amount of coins you use and their rarities therein. So for example using one silver and two gold coins compared to using 3 gold coins. You'll get the same results when you reload your game, though it does at least allow you to chart down your results and pick and choose from there if you're not happy with the first outcomes. You will have to start an entirely different playthru or ng+ to my knowledge to have new rolls, so I would recommend you save your tokens if you don't like grinding the shooting minigame until you are completely satisfied with your outcomes as they can take a while to rack up I feel.-A few weapons were somewhat nerfed in this remake but I won't say them just for the sake of spoilers and I'd like to mention it's not that big of a deal being the type of weapons they are and what you'd be using them for but it is noticeable.I didn't have many other dislikes as the game held firm towards most of the mechanics and I'll get straight into the positives.-Loot in my experiences lasts forever on the floor (I've only had instances where in the intro to the village if you kill Dr. Salvador and don't pick up his gem right away, it may not be there after the church bell rings. Not sure why.)-Melee combat along with being able to parry feels smooth (krauser fight included as you would hope it would) and allows for a lot of ways to save ammo and deal with enemies in a creative way that while may only result in a few kicks and suplex's, they do end up saving ammo and deal hefty damage and some crowd control. You can parry most attacks and duck under lunging enemies if you can react appropriately.-The upgrades and tuning for weapons feels good as well as combining the gems with your treasures and even appreciating combining them in ways for squeezing out that extra bit of cash with multipliers.All in all the game felt smooth and I only had two separate crashes when I tried streaming the game with some pretty intensive settings turned up to max but to the games credit, it did warn me that with my system it may be unstable with the settings turned up. Tldr: Great game and pretty true to the original, had a few new mechanics like parrying and if you enjoyed the 2005 version then I would feel comfortable saying you'd enjoy this one too. Deluxe version has a nice pistol that is only slightly worse in terms of damage than the starting pistol but the other stats are better (same exclusive) and the treasure map is nice but definitely spoils where loot is so avoid it if you're not into that. Hope you all enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: Well, Capcom did it. They actually remade one of their greatest classics of all time.Unlike the other Resident Evil games Capcom remade with the RE Engine, not only has the original aged remarkably well, but it's actually available here on Steam. So it's much easier for people to compare this to the original.So... ... ... no pressure then.Let's see, The iconic village square has been faithfully recreated, the water hall is still an irritating nightmare to get through, Ashley's cries for help are still annoying as hell, and Leon is still a dorky badass shooting off bullets and corny one liners.Is this better than the original though? Well... The knife now has limited durability and can only be fixed by the merchant, but it can now be used to perform stealth kills, break free from grabs instantly and parry melee attacks including our old insta-killing friend the chainsaw.Luis Serra's backstory has been expanded on, but Osmund Saddler's subtle hatred of America is gone.Leon's a little smarter, doing things in cutscenes that fans criticised him for not doing in the original game, (like speaking Spanish to the first villager he meets) but he doesn't mock Salazar as much as he used to.The fight with the monster in the cable car is gone, but the Final boss now has a second phase.Set pieces like the giant statue that chases you and the laser hall are also completely gone, but the minecart section now has Luis for company and there's a section where Ashley pilots a demolition crane. (because drivers ed apparently *shrug*) The Regeneradors now have a much more terrifying introduction, but the flaming man in the oven jumpscare is exactly the same so you can see it coming a mile away.You know what? In the end, I recommend you get both the original and the remake and judge which one is better for yourself.One things for certain though, they're both good for the same reason.The RE4 remake maintains the familiar gameplay that rewards both clever planning ahead and awareness of your surroundings.While putting you into desperate crowd control situations with unpredictable enemies both familiar and new. You can still shoot an enemy in the head to stun them, then run up and give them a good kick and you can still lure enemies into their own traps.Well, at least they were smart enough to take Leon's weapons as well as his jacket this time.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish someone made me play this game sooner. In sum, it was amazing.For context, my only other Resident Evil experience was 5 co-op which was fun.. but I wasn't entirely invested in the story, world, characters or even setting. I was incredibly invested in Leon and Ashley's journey and felt the tidbits of world-building we received were fascinating. It was just enough to make you both understand and crave more from the overarching plot. Story was simple enough but had some amazing beats such as Major Krausser, Luis, Ramon, that were effective in execution. Set pieces were wonderful and each location felt deliberate and purposeful. Gun play was so addictive. And as I've been made aware the shooting range was allegedly not in the original? If true, what a fun addition. Devs were clearly very confident in what they achieved here, as they should be. There isn't anything negative to say. This is a beautiful game and Leon is HIM.Actually I also must admit, a big part of my enjoyment was associating each gun with their Girls Frontline counterpart because I'm a weeb. I'm happy to say VP70, no matter which game it is, continues to come in clutch.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a hard one. I would rate this a neutral overall but since Steam doesn't give that option, I'll go with the negative and here is why:First of all, I grew up with RE4 (the original obviously) and I loved the game. For me this was also the best RE game that was ever made. It felt fairly unique story wise and the gameplay was very unique as well for its time.The environments and lighting were awesome and felt like they were created with care.I find all of this somewhat missing in the remake. It almost feels like a soulless shell to me.Don't get me wrong here; I think RE4 Remake is a good game and also a somewhat faithful one. The graphics are awesome and the sound is great too.Now here comes why I feel like it's not as good as it could be:The reason why this kinda felt soulless to me was, because they cut so much stuff out of the environmental diversity. For example the Freezer room, where you fight the first Regenerator. The room in the remake had only body bags hanging from the ceiling, while the original had all the failed versions of the regenerator hanging from it. The original had environmental storytelling going on, the remake didn't.This also goes for the animations. Not only had the original what felt like 100 different death animations for lean, but also cool animations for bosses were missing. Most notably was the ripping in half from the first boss (Chief Mendez). In the original you were able to see the process of him ripping apart for his second phase and the remake just had him spawn like that basically.The gameplay feels like the generic 3rd person shooter that you know of all the other games of this type. The original game did not have any movement while ADSing which made the whole experience way more scary imo, because you had to commit to fighting and be a bit more tactical about what you do. The remake completely got rid of it, which made it almost feel like a horde shooter at some points.All of the main characters look extremely weird to me. Something is wrong with their faces and Leon especially looks really ugly, so does Ada. When I compared it to the original, I was shocked how much better the faces looked in the original.There is also some cut content. They basically cut the whole U-3 boss out of the main game that was in the original. This was the only content they cut out, that I could really tell though, but there is probably more.This game shows that games are produced to make money and are no more products made with passion sadly. It's the small things that make a good game a great game, like animations for every possible death or showing how an enemy rips apart for his second stage. The remake just feels more generic because of all the points above and all the remakes and games they did in the RE universe (besides RE7 which is awesome btw) feel like reskins of each other which is sad af.Overall this is an okay game that lacks the small details and feels way more generic because of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you Capcom for not letting me regret a full price purchase for once. This is how you remake a game properly & let your community enjoy every minute of it. This Resident Evil game's story is pretty simple and self-explanatory. 6 years after the events in Racoon City, the presidents daughter Ashley Graham is kidnapped by an insane sect and brought to an isolated province somewhere in spain. You will play as Leon S. Kennedy who was given the task to rescue her. Simpler said than done because one obstacle awaits the other.If you played any other game of this series the gameplay will feel familiar. Typical for this franchise you will find yourself in placed in a specific area and in order to progress to the following location, you must either seek the required item needed to open the door or solve a puzzle. However, the sect's member will not be pleased with Leon's presence and intend to stop him at all costs. In contrast to the other remake titles (RE2+RE3), the enemies are not the classical George Romero type zombies.  In Resident Evil 4 they have maintained some of their humanity and are able to wield weapons such as pitchforks, torches, throwable dynamite and molotov cocktails. Brutes can prove especially difficult since they are strong enough to carry chainsaws and big hammers. There exist many more types of infected you will encounter and i will not spoiler much here. However, be sure expect some screwed up creatures! You must  act quickly and use your environment to your advantage to save as much ammo as possible. Starting with a meek pistol, Leon will encounter a mysterious traveling merchant who provides him with guns, ammunition and a limited supply of consumables in exchange for either money or gems that can be traded for special items. Several pistols, rifles, shotguns and automatic weapons, the choice is yours and you have to manage your suitcase as you like. Obviously a shotgun will take up bigger space than your pistol. Like i mentioned earlier, Leon's first priority is to protect Ashley. She cannot protect herself on her own and fully depends on  you. Ashley can be killed or picked up and taken away from you which will result in a game over screen. Don't worry she is not half as annoying as she was in the original game from 2005. LEON! This game is fantastic. From the environmental to the sound design. The cheesiness in the dialogues. The creepiness of the infected & the bosses. This remake is joyful fan-service for veterans of the franchise as well as a thrilling horror experience for new players. Capcom has restored my faith in the gaming history. After countless of disappointing launches in the last couple of years, we received a title which is fully worth the full price. It's properly optimized for PC, fleshed out and neither too long or too short. You can expect 15-20 hours of pure horror.9/10

_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: Capcom decided to task itself with capturing lighting in a bottle for a second time. Not an easy feat and I'm happy to say they mostly accomplished that.Playing Resident Evil 4 Remake is a surreal experience for me because I have played the original soooo many times across multiple platforms and you cannot convince me that the Wii Edition isn't the best version, I will actually fight you on that. Going through each area of the remake, I'm cast back to the original game and making comparisons everywhere, some locations in the remake are almost so identical to the original that I found it jarring but in a good way because I got giddy about it.My expectations for this game as a remake was that they had to follow the original closely since I will argue the original is an almost perfect game in terms of gameplay, pacing and sound design, and some other things. I'm really happy with how it turned out, the plot follows almost beat for beat, the locations are familiar, fresh and changed around sometimes in ways the compliment the game as a remake but don't feel so drastically out of place next to the original, everything in this remake feels like it would have been right at home in the original. The visuals are outstanding! The RE Engine has always been beautiful and RE4R is no exception, there are some areas in the village arc that just made me stop and engage in photo mode. The attention to environmental detail and visual story telling is immaculate! I'm especially impressed with how the castle was remade. All enemies encountered are too recreated with a lot of love and care and hands down much scarier than their original counterparts, some highlights would be the dogs, Garrador and Verdugo.The gameplay is what shines in this remake the most, if you played the chainsaw demo then you will know what I am talking about. The shooting is responsive and feels impactful and it is so damn satisfying to stun an enemy then go up for that sweet round house kick, even better when you knock down a whole group. Sometimes, Leon's response from walking to running feels a bit sluggish, like I'm not entirely sure if he is in a walking or running animation right after performing a melee attack for example but it was not much of a hindrance. My absolute favourite addition to the gameplay from the original is knife parrying, hot damn this makes for some tense and rewarding gameplay and the stuff Leon can deflect is questionable yet awesome. Should you time a parry just right, you can follow up with a melee attack which I just adore and the amount of times, hitting space to deflect an attack or instant kill makes group battles very intense and well above the original. But be careful as the knife has durability, which I know is a point of contention for a lot of gamers but it can be repaired and there are other knives you can acquire too.The enemy AI has also had an upgrade too. Enemies will now group up en masse and be waiting for you around corners. Not only that but should you get grabbed by one and another is nearby they will turn you in that direction so they can do a combo attack on you, it's impressive and once more adds to the tension.Ashley is now a lot easier to manage, thankfully. Instead of having to share you healing items and scarce yellow herbs with her, they now just remove her health bar entirely in favour of a new system. If she gets hit, she gets downed but can be recovered by Leon via a simple interaction but if she is hit while downed, she dies. It is also much easier to take down any enemies who try to carry her away, you can of course still knee cap them to make them drop her or you can run up and use your knife at the cost of some durability.The sound design is an area I start to have a problem with sadly. The environmental sound, gun sounds and all that are brilliant, i love the sound Leon's starting pistol makes when you are popping off but I feel like it's the little things Capcom dropped the ball here on compared to the original, not all the time but only in certain places. For example, you don't hear the castle zealots chanting as much as you used to, they definitely do but it just doesn't have the same effect as the original. And the soundtrack is something I have mixed feelings on. Out of all the RE remakes, RE1R to me has the best soundtrack because it is very omnipresent and silence is used rarely but when it is, it is used to great effect and there are so many good tracks I can rattle off the RE1R, such as Neptune, Guardhouse theme and of course, the save room theme. But ever since RE2R, I feel like Capcom have dropped the ball on the soundtrack. Sure, you can argue they are going for a more ambient approach, where you only listen to the sounds of the environment and I get that, really. I can totally appreciate it too but there are times when they do have tracks playing in the background but the whole track is just a subtle theme that you can barely hear because half the track itself is just silence or a low drone and that seemed to carry through RE2R, RE3R, and sadly RE4R. The track that plays during the first village shootout is what I wanted from the whole games soundtrack, it's loud, it's catchy and it is tense but after that section, there was not really another track that caught my attention. I recognised boss battle tracks instantly and they have echoes of their original version in the which I appreciate but outside of those, I was pretty let down, especially by my favourite track; Infiltration. That is hands down my favourite from the original and they did indeed remake that for this game but it's far too subtle, which again, probably what they were going for but given how some other tracks sound, I was let down by this. This doesn't ruin the game at all, I'm just a massive admirer of video game soundtracks.If you have yet to finish the game, you could consider this some light spoilers but it has to be talked about.In the original after you beat the game you got access to The Mercenaries, Separate Ways and Assignment Ada. At the time of writing this, The Mercenaries came out yesterday which allows you to play as Leon, Luis, Krauser and Hunk. There is no Ada or Wesker, my two personal favs to play as. And that's all the extra content. There is no Assignment Ada or Separate Ways which was a major bummer for me. I loved Ada's campaign in the original and I had a little inkling before finishing the game that told me there would be no Ada campaign and that came in the form of one of her cutscenes being used in the main campaign. This definitely detracts from the replay value for me personally especially since the rewards you can unlock from replaying the game on different difficulties for a better rank just don't seem worth it to me.In the end, I say RE4R is on the same level as the original, I don't think the game does anything worse than the original and in some instances, does a lot of stuff better than the original. but perhaps since I've played the original so many times, I do find a lack of replay value and it is sorely disappointing that there is no Ada campaign to play through but despite this, if you are a fan of the original, then I still implore you to check out this remake, which sits well above the RE2R and RE3R but sits comfortably next to the RE1R which still holds the crown on remakes for the game industry.

_childDocuments_.review: This setting produces the odorous chi of a krokodil den. Already a long-time customer, I joyfully crash on its rotten mattress with needles sticking out of it. One look at these muddy roads, hairy soups, and filthy barns promises a dive in familiar trouble. It looks as good as it feels, yet not in the same sense as some otherworldly grandeur of God of War. The beauty is in the slick particle effects and lighting, the liminal qualities of gloomy corridors and barren vistas, bristling with insurmountable thicket, where brown foliage adorns the edges of dark ponds. The sky is murky and ravens feast on piles of carcasses. You're here to make bigger piles. Shoot the ravens, eat all the fish, blow someone's head off - there goes a squelchy alien parasite in its full graphical glory. Gross! But almost real.So are their hosts, the unkempt locals with off-putting mannerisms. Inhospitable as they are, even being a cop, Leon couldn't get away with a murderous rampage through an impoverished Ass European village without winning our hearts first. We love to root for a youthful underdog with a witty sense of humour and a heartbreaker haircut. Even Ada harbours a soft spot for our hero, and I betcha she has high standards. But what I love about Leon the most is that, no matter how much tragedy fell on his shoulders, he hasn't turned into another "stoic veteran" archetype. He retains a spring in his step, high hopes, and a set of childishly pure morals. And he still doesn't have the patience for villains' monologues, straight-up shooting them in the face in the middle of a sentence.But Leon was always good. What's new is that the rest of the crew went through a complicated humanisation treatment without muddying the story, which is as clear-cut as ever. Considering that the franchise has been constantly expanded upon for decades, that's a huge praise. Capcom takes a subtle erotic approach to character interrelationships in place of blatant emotion porn. It doesn't turn its actors into puppets for soap opera affairs, doesn't knock them together like toys, saying "Now kiss". A mere proclamation of friendship here is considered a big deal. Pairs have to do with all kinds of covert tensions, which give local stories a playful tragicomedic tone without bogging them down with melodrama.They toned down the sex appeal, too. Judging by the public's reaction, getting rid of Ada's hot evening gown or Ashley's pantsu shots didn't diminish them, allowing for their personalities to shine through without heavily relying on the hormonal manipulation of coomers. Ada hasn't changed much, although, I found her performance... not bad but unusual. Ashley's transformation, on the other hand, is major. She used to be a low-tier anime cliché and a flasher. Now, she comes off as capable and sympathetic, acting her age. Adventuring alongside her provided me with a sense of comradery. Luis is a Chad for my own heart, their friendship dynamic with Leon is more fleshed out now. Ramon Salazar wears no tricorne, but he's still hilarious. Annoying him never ceases to amuse.Overall, they managed to enhance the series with wisdom and restraint. The Merchant, thankfully, hasn't changed much. Instead, he dispenses an even bigger array of side challenges, not to mention the classic shooting range where you win neat baubles. The puzzles are as simple as they always were, no one cares. The grid inventory is a non-issue, albeit I wish it was. I'm compelled to accentuate juiced-up bossfights, easily the best ones in the series, and an improved mine kart ride, which isn't just another shooting gallery. Finally, the water scooter victory lap doesn't spoil the climax by obliterating you out of the blue. Most of the fresh takes are good. Getting rid of the giant Lilliput statue chase is a crime, though. Why? You already jump ten sharks by that point!Luckily, one of the main attractions to die for, exploration, remains intact. To see these alluring little pillars of light, emanated by constantly drip-fed pickups, or hear the ringing of pesetas has a therapeutic effect. I'd be hard-pressed to name a game with a comfier flow. Of course, milking every location for hidden treasures and resources is only half of the beloved loop. Peaceful moments wouldn't be as precious if they weren't frequently interrupted by volatile Panic Horror, the hallmark of the series, which saturates the game's pacing with contrasting patterns. Getting trapped and ambushed is always exciting. Shoot, kick, suplex. Then, when the last body hits the floor or blows up spectacularly and everything goes quiet, go back to the delightful looting again. To happily start anew in a few minutes.Starting off, I felt suspicious upon seeing a stealth mechanic. Turns out, it's only used to get a few free kills before it hits the fan. Most of the time-tested arms are present for that occasion. Grenades explode with power, tearing bodies apart and throwing them all over the place, enemies react to each bullet, burn spectacularly, get mutilated, and the headsplosions are gorgeous! This series always provided weapons that kicked hard. The shootouts feel smoother now that you can swap weapons on the fly, which is a welcome change from the archaic necessity to rummage in a non-diegetic suitcase. Like before, ammo scarcity presents a problem only in the beginning. You are free to enjoy your arsenal to the fullest, including knives that got buffed big time.To curb it, their durability depletes on use. Sounds cancerous, but they're worth it. An easy parry can fully negate an attack, and knife executions look like what I only imagine doing to a driver who honks outside while I lay in bed sleepless. Enemies return the favour, shoving their fingers in Leon's mouth, poking his eyes out, and impaling him on pitchforks. These gory sights reminded me of Dangerous Dave in the Haunted Mansion. Fortunately, we don't have those vile slimes here. But there's a plethora of other threats, things that can still bite your head off at full health, as well as traditional staples: insects, weird cartoon dogs, abominable super-mutant giants, and the infamous Regenerators. Due to their nightmarish movement patterns, they keep being a menace even after you get a thermal scope.Leon's own movement clearly was an important point during development. He smoothly bumps into obstacles, performing slick animations, and has just enough weight to his every turn. Controls, especially aiming, are more precise than before, reflecting the agility he displays during cutscenes. To compensate, the enemies are faster and deadlier, too, turning each encounter blood-pumping and personal. Most of the combat happens in the same compact locations where you fight for a breather. Counter-intuitively, when you see a crowd - you run at it, not from it. RE4 is all about making Leon johnwick and gunkata through his foes. No matter how strong, those are still too clumsy for our boy, tripping and falling, whereas Leon floats among them like a butterfly. Yeah, RE4 has always been a horror-themed brawler with guns.Unsurprisingly, the remake offers quite a challenge and high replay value with an unlockable difficulty and a badass Mercenaries mode. Boasting improved characters, expanded melee, obvious cosmetic superiority, and complete abolition of QTEs, it's an upgrade. My main concern was Capcom's ability to maintain that wacky Evil Dead atmosphere. Admittedly, it's a less goofy game, toned down in its art direction and acting. But the offbeat wit and playfulness were transplanted carefully, only corrected to correlate with other revamped chapters. We can't have things exactly like they used to be. Must we cry about it while trying to calculate how much "soul" was lost during this transition? No thanks, bro.My curator
