_childDocuments_.review: This definitely is the highest quality Resident Evil game to date. As for if it's faithful to the original, both yes and no. With a few changes here and there with outfits and diologue and a few plot choices that really expand some characters from the original, this is definitely very close to the OG 2005 title. The value here for DLC offerings comes more to taste than anything else and is worth considering at the very least. Overall, a solid entry and a very high quality title that shows alot of love for the franchise and it's roots. 9.5/10I feel that RE4R has taken a page from every previous RE game and made it into the perfect entry. The partner AI feels like a more streamlined version of RE5. Fights feel frantic and high energy like RE8. The in between combat mechanics of crafting and inventory management have taken inspirations from RE2/3R while building on the originals' systems. The enemies feel like an update swarm system from the 2010a era titles. The 'melee' mechanic definitely feels like a love letter to RE5.RE4R is by far the finest work Capcom has done with the franchise. Guns feel powerful, enemies are threatening, bosses are fun, and the dialogue, while still a tad cringey and definitely changed from the original, at times is still very funny. The DLC outfits are very hit or miss in my opinion. Romantic and Hero/Villain are a hell no from me. Casual doesn't feel too out of place though, and I think they're my favorites. I don't personally like the orange jacket that has been added to Ashley's model. A jacketless version is an option, but only after beating the game once and for 500CP. Debatable value  terms of length, this is a long game relatively for the series. The 2005 original was about 15-20 hours with the remake falling to about 12-16 hours. Not quite as long, but very much a solid length. The flow of the game is slightly different from recent RE titles, opting for a chapter system and forgoing the more seamless style of recent titles. A slightly welcome choice, making it easy to know when a good time for a break is. 2R and 3R being much shorter titles, this lengthy entry definitely feels like it warrants a few trips to grab snacks and a drink before continuing.The file size is massive, for an RE game, clocking in at over 50gb, easily twice the size of the other remakes and understandably so. With such high detailed models and textures, fantastic lighting, and so many massive environments, this game really warrants the massive install. At launch, sadly we won't have the Mercenaries mode available, coming for free in early April. A welcome return of the PvE mode for long time fans. At 60$ USD for base game, it's nice to see Capcom hasn't yet hopped on the increased price choice of other AAA studios. The Deluxe Edition offerings are definitely a matter of personal taste on their value as I've mentioned, but at only 10$ USD more, it's worth considering at the minimum.Hopefully Capcom keeps up the sky high quality we've seen here in future titles, because this is a fantastic display and what they're capable of. RE4R is without a doubt my personal preferred way to experience the game, followed closely by the GameCube version, if only for nostalgia sake. Easily a 9.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR at bottomBeing a huge fan of the original RE4, infact it possibly being my favourite game of all time and basically a large portion of my childhood I was extremely scared for this game's release, that was until the chainsaw demo when I realised this legacy was in safe hands and I was absolutely right.While the original still holds a very dear place in my heart I genuinely do believe the remake has both remade and surpassed the original, they absolutely nailed this, the gameplay if phenomenal and addicting, the story is the same old but modernised while also expanding on Luis so we actually care about him more than 3 lines and improving Ashley to make her feel more like an actual person, though I didn't rly have alot of problems w OG Ashley tbf. The new mechanics add alot and the parry mechanic is a blast to try master. Tbh I have only a single criticism of this game and it's that they pretty much entirely removed the relationship between Leon and the Antagonists of the game, while I understand they wanted a slightly more serious tone, I really do miss the radio calls between Leon and the games numerous villains, particularly Salazar, I ADORED their back and forth in the original and that is sadly missing here. Otherwise though, I really do believe this game is close to perfect.Onto Seperate Ways, I wanted to wait to post a review for this game til AFTER Seperate Ways was announced and released as it felt almost inevitable and one of my biggest if not my biggest gripe with OG RE4 was actually the Ada side story, the pacing felt awful and outside of a few moments it felt extremely lack luster and like Ada really had very little impact to actually change the outcome of RE4 OG, however with the remake they again ABSOLUTELY NAILED IT. The new Seperate Ways feels like a mini-campaign and honestly Ada feels so much more normal, in a sense that, in OG RE4 she really just felt completely chaotic, doing whatever she pleased with 0 reasoning and while I enjoyed that character they really brought Ada some much needed morality in this remake imo. They also added alot of the "cut content" from OG RE4 here in this DLC and it actually fits alot more, I especially LOVE what they have done with a certain boss and the larger presence of a certain super villain within the story to overall just gel RE4 with the rest of the universe so much neater. TLDR; They completely and utterly nailed this game, every addition and change was phenomenal bar the removal of Salazar and Leon's back and forth, Seperate Ways is INFINITELY better and this is truly the greatest remake of a game ever done.10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: it's a good modern game, but a bad remake. If you don't care about the original that much, you'll have a great time.When Capcom announced Resident Evil 4 Remake, I thought to myself that if they transfer the combat mechanics from Remake 2 and Remake 3, i.e. headshots not having 100% stagger chance, clumsier movement, imprecise aiming, and so on, they're going to ruin it. All of these aspects work for a survival horror, a slower type of game. Original Resi 4 is an action/arcade game which boasts predictability, crisp and precise movement and aiming.I wanted to give RE4R a chance. I lowered all my expectations and opened my mind. Surprisingly, for the first few chapters, I got sucked into the game. I grew to like parrying, even though it can be unreliable at times. Unfortunately, as the time went on, chapters passed, a feeling started to creep in. A question. Am I enjoying RE4R on its own merits, or because it's a remake of Resident Evil 4?......and so began the downwards spiral. I started noticing changes to encounters and mechanics not because they would improve the game, but for the sake of it:At least they removed QTEs, right? Not really, they reduced them, but let's be honest: parrying is a sort of QTE. Evading literally is one, as a prompt is displayed on the screen.But oh, they added stealth! Except it works exactly like in The Evil Within, which was criticized for the simplistic, low effort way it was implemented. Back in 2014.There are some good changes, but most of them are tied to atmosphere and character writing.Completely unnecessary remake. A product of remake culture, purely for the money. I didn't even bother playing Separate Ways DLC. It can be fun, since it's Resident Evil 4 at heart. Good game, but a bad remake. Buy only on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 4 Remake is a masterpiece. It is a faithful remake of the original game, but it also updates the game with modern graphics, gameplay, and controls. The game is still scary, but it is also more action-packed and exciting than ever before.Here are some of the things that I loved about Resident Evil 4 Remake:The graphics are stunning. The game looks absolutely gorgeous, with detailed environments and realistic character models.The gameplay is improved. The game is still a survival horror game, but it is also more action-packed than the original. The controls are tight and responsive, and the combat is satisfying.The story is engaging. The game tells the same story as the original, but it is told in a more engaging way. The characters are more likable, and the plot is more suspenseful.Overall, Resident Evil 4 Remake is a must-play for fans of the original game and fans of survival horror games in general. It is a faithful remake that updates the game with modern graphics, gameplay, and controls. If you haven't played Resident Evil 4 Remake yet, I highly recommend checking it out.Here are some additional things that I loved about Resident Evil 4 Remake:The atmosphere is terrifying. The game does a great job of creating a sense of dread and suspense.The puzzles are challenging. The puzzles in the game are not too easy, but they are not too difficult either. They are just the right level of challenge to keep you engaged.The boss fights are epic. The boss fights in the game are some of the best I have ever seen in a survival horror game. They are challenging, exciting, and visually stunning.If you are looking for a scary, action-packed, and suspenseful survival horror game, then Resident Evil 4 Remake is the game for you. I highly recommend checking it out.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely incredible REmake of RE4, with a great PC port (with a few fixable issues) and some nice modern quality-of-life changes.Fans of the OG RE4 will find a lot to like here. A few things were cut, but also a lot of new stuff was added. It feels familiar enough, with plenty of fresh changes to keep you on your toes. The campy dialogue is back in full force, and Leon is a quip-machine. Overall, it remains very faithful to the original. Almost all of the story beats and environments happen the same as before, just with more added detail, some better lore cohesion, and things feel a little more grounded, similar to REmake 2.The environments are lush and extremely detailed. Exploring the village, castle and labs are a real treat. Things are constantly changing and progressing, so things don't get too stale, and the RE Engine has some noticeable upgrades compared to older games like Village and RE2. New shadow rendering with far more detail and distance-based softening, foliage deformation as you walk through it, destructible environments and props when you thrown enemies through them, and simulated hair strands for more swishy looking characters - to name a few. Resident Evil has never looked so good!The game is far more action-heavy compared to RE2, but at the same time, REmake 4 introduces a lot more puzzle and survival-horror elements compared to the original. Supplies on the harder difficulties can be pretty scarce if you don't manage them well enough, making combat encounters a lot more tense. There are more puzzles throughout, and some of them can be quite tricky - they also change depending on the difficulty you play at. Combat is extremely satisfying with beefy sounding weapons, lots of detailed gore and dismemberment (blowing enemies in half with a shotgun never gets old) and all the round-house kicks you could want. Enemy counts are heavily increased and you can be swarmed by around 10 enemies at a time. Things can get very hectic and challenging at times.The PC port is overall fantastic, with incredible optimisation. On an ageing i7 6700K, 2080 Super with 32gb, at 2560x1440, I've cranked the game up to the max and had 100-144fps most of the time. It looks fantastic and feels even better. Mouse and keyboard controls for combat and inventory management are smooth and feel great.Now, the issues. The game's antialiasing (TAA) is basically useless. The game looks like a jittery aliased mess no matter what resolution or settings you use. AMD's FSR 2.0 just blurs the hell out of the image. Thankfully, the community stepped in and with the 'RE Framework' mod, you can enable DLSS on Nvidia RTX GPU's (and XeSS on Intel) to instantly clean up the visuals, for a sharper, cleaner image, while also boosting frame rates a bunch. The game has an FOV slider, but the max setting is still only 70 degrees and uncomfortably zoomed in. Again, the 'RE Framework' mod adds a much-needed FOV slider with higher limits, making the camera and gameplay much more comfortable.For fans of Resident Evil, this is some of the best it has ever been.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel insane for leaving the a negative review for a game like this, especially one with overwhelmingly positive reviews.My play through is/was on Professional difficulty, since that's what it recommended for people who played the original game.THE GOOD:I LOVE the original and I was super stoked to play the remake. The game looks incredible and I really enjoy the much darker atmosphere compared to the original. The Gore is fun, visceral, and makes your guns feel like they really have some punch to them most of the time (especially the shotgun). The campy-ness has been dialed back quite a bit, but Leon still makes his quips and some interactions are still silly. So that doesn't bother me as much as other reviewers. Most of the iconic parts (that I've seen so far) are still in the game/have been expanded upon (The lake with the big fish is my favorite example). Inventory management is still oddly fun just like it was in the original. Managing Ashley isn't as annoying in this game as she was in the original IMO, so thats a bonus too. I could go on and on about how there are a ton of really cool things in this game that really make it a great modern remake of an incredible classic, but I have one major complaint that makes this game hard for me to enjoy (plus a few extra qualms).THE BAD:LEON MOVES AND FEELS LIKE A 60yo MAN DRENCHED IN TARwalking feels slow,running feels slow,switching weapons feels slowLeon is stunned for A LOT LONGER when he is hit and he doesn't get I Frames after being hit like he did in the original. So not only can you be hacked to death extremely quickly if you find yourself surrounded, you also wont be allowed to reload or swap weapons after the initial hit due to the stun. This is supposedly remedied by the fact that you can parry with your knife darksouls style if you time it just right. If you don't time it right, you'll still block the attack, but it eats the durability of your knife and it only sets them up to swing at you again (hopefully you parry it this time). The Zombies also have much improved AI (which I actually appreciate) and move A LOT faster. They also don't flinch after every shot and head-shots don't guarantee a melee follow-up anymore.Melee follow-ups aren't as good as they were in the original as they are a lot narrower and you aren't going to knock down 100+ zombies in a single kick like in the original. (I KNOW melee was stupid busted in the original, but it adds to the overall point I'm going to make).  Attacking prone zombies is harder and more risky because not only is Leon slower to follow-up, but attacking with your knife also eats its durability a bit. So, by themselves these things seem like good difficulty changes to make a very cheese-able game a lot less cheesy and give the fights a much needed dose of stress and urgency.But together, it creates a crowd control nightmare. if you find yourself in close quarters/surrounded (which will happen often due to the plentiful ambushes and enemies spawning behind you at the start of fights):1. you will have difficulty moving around them due to Leon being slow as hell and the zombies having better AI and being faster2. you will not be able to reliably Head-shot+melee like the old game to get them off your ass (due to slow follow-up/non-guaranteed melee).3. if you try to be a parry god, the various grabs, thrown weapons, insta-kill attacks and knife mechanics will put you in downward spiral.So in reality the only real solution is to either bust out the precious shotgun and blow everything away, or don't ever miss shots at the beginning of a fight.Again, I know that difficulty needed to be added to make it not a cakewalk, but I don't think the shotgun or explosives should be the answer to every cluster-f*ck in the game.ALSO WHY ARE ALL THE GOOD AMMO TYPES MADE WITH SMALL RESOURCES?!?Handgun, shotgun, magnum and bolt mines are all made with small resources. While Large resources make TMP ammo, rifle ammo crossbow bolts  and flashbangs. Don't get me wrong, the rifle and flashbangs are amazing, but flashbangs are situational and rifle ammo is efficient due to how powerful the rifles are. plus, since these all take gunpowder (another limited item), I would much sooner make the small-resource equivalent (pistol ammo instead of TMP, Shotgun instead of rifle, etc.). OVERALL, this game is like if you recreated your favorite childhood food in a 5-star gourmet restaurant, but all of your silverware was sharpened to cut your mouth with every bite to make it as difficult to enjoy as possible. Every bite is rich and delicious but at the same time- exactly as you remembered it. However you'll need a bib for all the blood you'll be spilling over yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, but my god I would like us to move away from clunky controls and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ aim in horror games and whatever genre this would be called. I played it on Hardcore and I can't tell you how many times I would have an incredibly frustrating death and be like "I hate this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game". It was good enough that I kept playing though. There's just two major things you're gonna want to be aware of before playing this:Leon, while not a full tank in this remake, is still partially a tank. There was noticeable lag time between when I started and ended input and when the game would register that. On top of that, Leon doesn't move that fast and has ramp up time, especially after shooting (even with a pistol), so I struggled to reliably melee enemies, even if they were quite close when I stunned them. If you've played the other remakes, this one is way clunkier. If you played Resistance, this one is not as bad but is closer to that than the other remakes on the clunkiness scale.As for the gunplay, I get it, a bunch of factors affect accuracy and recoil, but the number of times I would miss point-blank while stationary with a pistol or the bolt thrower was astounding. Want to use an SMG reliably? Good luck with that. You can't aim while crouching either for some reason.All in all, I still liked it and will play more. I just think purposeful ♥♥♥♥♥♥ design choices that seem to be there just to force you to use the new knife parrying system really hold it back from its full potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing I can say about this game is that, if you have no nostalgia for it whatsoever, this game is still one of the better games you will have played in your life. The gameplay is just that good, and now the visuals have been brought up to today's standard as well. I don't think anyone can fully explain why the gameplay feels so good. It is very simplistic in theory, but it is just plain fun. It totally works.I highly recommend you play on Standard difficulty. It feels like you have to put in effort, and yet you won't die that much at all. You will never get stuck on anything, even bosses. But it still feels like you're putting in the work. Minor nitpick: the game doesn't really tell you all that clearly to go for Headshots or Legshots so that you can get enemies to stagger or fall down which enables a powerful melee strike. Use it!But this feels like you are sort of John Wick with your assortment of guns, importance of reload speed and accuracy, some minor gun (and knife) porn in here. Flashy cutscenes, fantastic boss battles. Especially 'you know the one'. Just a super fun game.Yes, even for you, guy who hasn't ever played the original and feels like this is just fans appreciating fan-service. No, it really is one of the best games you, too, will play.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is poorly optimized.Wild FPS swings, the game will run at 120 fps majority of the time, occasionally dipping to 80 or 90, which is fine. But in certain areas it will go all the way down to 25 fps (unplayable)Also, if using scope you are guaranteed to take an fps hit, which makes the scoped rifle absolutely unusable sometimes. If the game already drops to say 40 fps and you try scoping... well now you are watching a slideshow at 15 fps, good luck and trying to score a hit.There is no official DLSS support or FSR 2.1... I ended up using REFramework (mod) to get DLSS running and the game not only works better (keeping it playable at all times, no more slideshows)... but with DLSS (quality) it also LOOKS better as well (native AA and FSR 2 look objectively worse).Since it is a mod and not an implementation by Capcom - DLSS doesn't separate 2D UI stuff (like map, inventory etc.) from the rest of the game, so expect ghosting and reduced quality for those. I'd take smooth gameplay and better looking game over prettier menus and text every time, so it doesn't bother me so much... but the fact I had to resort to modding to get a playable game = not recommending it (at least for now, and at this price).

_childDocuments_.review: Let's be honest, calling this a "review" feels generous. It's more like a desperate plea for someone, anyone, to fix this unholy abomination before it consumes my soul. But before I exorcise this buggy beast, let's talk turkey.The gameplay itself? It's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece. Shooting Ganado heads feels oh-so-satisfying, and the knife parry system is a thrilling game of digital roulette (minus the self-inflicted headshots). It's like tangoing with a chainsaw-wielding maniac, if the tango somehow involved screaming and praying to invisible tech gods.But then there's the save data. Oh, the save data. It's more fragile than a porcelain doll in a mosh pit. Crashes lurk around every corner, waiting to pounce and send your progress to the netherworld. My save file has committed more suicides than a soap opera character, leaving me in a constant state of paranoid save-scumming. Capcom, I think your game needs a priest, not a programmer.And Ashley? Don't even get me started. She's the world's most talented damsel-in-distress, capable of tripping over her own shadow while simultaneously attracting every undead villager within a 50-mile radius. I've spent more time rescuing this walking liability than Leon has spent with hair product.But amidst the crashing despair, there's a glimmer of hope. Leon's wit is still as sharp as his knives, delivering cheesy one-liners that make you question whether to laugh or cry. And then there's Salazar: the scenery-chewing villain who's so over-the-top, you can't help but cackle at his melodramatic speeches. He's basically every telenovela villain rolled into one glorious, hammy package.So, Resident Evil 4 Remake (PC): would I recommend it? Honestly, NO. The gameplay is fantastic, but the save system could give Cthulhu nightmares. If you're a masochist with a penchant for digital roulette, go for it. Just have a priest and a therapist on speed dial. As for me, I'm going to go cleanse my PC with holy water and hope the nightmares of Ashley's screams fade soon.

_childDocuments_.review: "You don't seriously think a conservative mind can chart a new course for the world, do you?"Six years have passed since the biological disaster in Raccoon City. Agent Leon S. Kennedy, one of the sole survivors, has been sent as part of an elite special forces operation to rescue the president's kidnapped daughter. He tracks her to a secluded village in Spain where there is something terribly wrong with the locals.Yet another incredible remake.  The remastered graphics are gorgeous and feel so much more authentic and believable than the original, especially because a lot of the ridiculous scenes from the original game were redesigned and cut together to provide a much more cinematic experience.  They updated so many of the mechanics just enough so that you get the same story, characters, and plot points but with a new and improved gameplay experience while still retaining the same DNA as the original game.  To me, this game combined all the dark and creepy jumpscare-type moments of Resident Evil 2 with all the over-the-top, action-packed moments of Resident Evil 3.  There’s also a ton of new replay value with all the new unlockables, difficulties, and Ada Wong’s Separate Ways DLC.The newly remastered Resident Evil 4 remains the same incredible, gore-infested horror experience that everyone loved the first time around and I’m so glad they finally got around to remastering the best game in the series.  If you loved the original game, you’ll love this one even more.  9/10

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10RE4 remake takes the formula established by the RE2 and RE3 remakes and improves upon it even further. While both the remake and the original shine in their own ways, the remake excels in reimagining certain moments. For instance, Krauser's iconic fight starts and ends in a different way. The QTE-driven cutscene from the original is transformed into a fast close-quarters knife fight full of parrying. Separate Ways is also among the best DLC's I have ever played. Though Ada's DLC came free with the original, the remakes is well worth the $10 it costs. Coming into the game, I knew it would be good considering how well the RE2 and RE3 remakes were, but I didn't realize just how good it would be. This game is for sure a must-play for any Resident Evil fan and even a great entry point for newcomers to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, i really do. But because Capcom is rolling out ENIGMA Protection on both old and new titles heres a few things you need to be aware of before buying any capcom title.- No Mod support, this is cause people see modding as cheating which isn't true- 10-15 drop in FPS with stuttering- Various virus and Malware flags showing up, this DRM is coming out of Moscow btwIts not just Resident Evil but all capcom titles, and while there are lists out there that tell you what games have it capcom will sneakily slip it in without you knowing. so please do the right thing and just sail the seven seas cause as Gabe Newell put it "piracy isn't a pricing problem, its a service problem" and the service were receiving is less than poor given a pirated copy can run the game better than a legit copy.And and D riders that comment trying to defend this then you better show some proof with your statement otherwise im not going to give you the time and day.Below is my old review from when i played it and gave it a few weeks for the launch hype to die downWell I'm glad i held off on writing my review as quick reviews tend to only focus on their first impressions so with mine i wanted to dive into the whole picture of this Remake telling you why you should play this but to not get your hopes up or to be blinded by nostalgia.While you'd assume i'd say the game half-asses it compared to the original, that's not the case here. The Remake captures a lot of the original in terms of scenes and events while changing it up a bit to keep veteran players on their toes.One of the biggest improvements to this would have to be the combat/encounters as enemies can easily swarm you if not at times outright spawn in behind you to give that feeling of being surrounded by a bunch of Spanish denizens out to kill you in the name of their lord and savior.Being able to stealth kill a ganado or outright go full John Wick on a group of them just leaves you feeling a special type of satisfaction to be desired all the time. Parrying an enemy's attack while being low on health giving you that stroke of luck to survive feels great.The new puzzles and even the extended Ashley section was nice to play through as it expanded a somewhat short section from the Original version and the village layout stayed the same while shuffling the rooms connecting to them to give a familiar yet different feeling. Moving on to the castle it does feel a bit more touched up from the original in terms of graphical quality as can be said about everything in this game.I did like the improvement to Salazars boss fight both making him mobile and having him and Leon exchange their lines mid fight.I wont lie when i say that while the castle looks better in terms of looks it definitely took a fall from design as it's no longer a death trap filled fun house (at least for Salazar it was a fun house) and even the man of the castle Ramon Salazar and even all the main baddies of the game have minimal screen time, Salazar in the original would constantly taunt you over the radio with him and Leon exchanging lines back to one another in a cheesy fashion.The game definitely feels a bit more linear than the original as it'll be like 5 chapters before you back track to a spot you missed something and while the original was linear in terms of progression there were moments where you could backtrack mainly for a merchant who while I like his quips he gives when you see him I feel there's never a moment  where i had to backtrack to him aside from finding a gem to socket into a treasure.Separate Ways/Another Order was rumored but so far nothing has been shown for it or even hinted at it aside from a folder found in the games files and mystery achievements that the fanbase has tied to it being potential DLC.Much like the other Remakes this game would fall into the challenge run type of game as thats the most you'll get out of replaying it aside from achievement hunters.Another issue with at least the PC version is the lack of a VR mode for both this and RE:VIII as its exclusive to PS5 with no promise of it coming to PC much like 7 did. The only legit way to playing RE4 in VR is either buying a PS5 and PSVR2 AND the game, or buying a quest 2 and buying RE4VR.Mercenaries mode felt too easy to get that S rank and the leader boards are crap as you'll spend hours just trying to get out of the 10,000 place mark and of course the lack of challenges as it literally only serves to be fan service with its own twist and having Luis added in as a playable character. Meanwhile RE4VR actually had challenge missions included in it's Mercenaries update and the same can be said for Mercenaries Additional Orders in Village. I'm not saying Mercenaries is outright bad but it is lacking those extra additions prior games added to theirs.I think this game should be played but not with rose tinted glasses as your love for the original will turn your experience with this into a sour one, it's okay to admire the changes as most people did at first and thats what the devs intended to do for players and it's to give them a fresh yet familiar experience.Honestly if you're just getting into RE and you played the Remakes and not the original then none of these changes will probably bother you.If you're one who fancied the original games and didn't like this from its changes then just take into consideration that the remakes are more like Re-imaginings of the story and applying the OG timeline to the Remake timeline will lead to inconsistencies.So without further ado id say get this while its on sale unless you have the extra cash then by all means snag this up for your collection and if you already played this and not the UHD version then definitely check that out as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I am currently on my third playthrough (Hardcore) in NG+ and I am loving it.It has everything right... Of course it's not perfect and the AI can be a bit frustrating at times. It's clear they could improve on it a bit.In my personal opinion, some of the "encounters" were poorly made. The "Twin-Garrador" and "Ramon" fights are long and drawn out on the first playthrough. They aren't hard, but nothing about them screams satisfying upon defeating them.Although, I want to mention the most crucial piece of evidence to why this game is amazing. Why I can play this game repeatedly and don't want to touch RE2... There is no Mr. X gimmick! I hate with a burning passion any game that invites me to explore than proceeds to say, "hurry up!" Not to mention this enemy being immortal.In RE4R you have a singular scripted event where you are chased by a Mr. X like enemy, but it's extremely short. If anything my first time through I loved the chase and having to run while dodging enemies. Even in the second playthrough I found myself enjoying the encounter. Why, what's different? Not only is it shorter by a mile, but soon after you get to face this enemy as a boss. A boss that is killable!Overall, RE4R does a brilliant job in using a Mr. X like character. It's not drawn out nor is it annoying. It's an enjoyable encounter every time.In my opinion the "Regenerators" are the perfect Mr. X enemy. They are horrifying and extremely difficult to kill on a first playthrough. Of course once you get the right gear they are trivial, but for a first playthrough they do the job of instilling fear into the player perfectly. Even though I can kill them easily, there appearance is still terrifying! Where as Mr X is basically a meme. You don't want an enemy designed to be terrifying to become a joke and that is why RE2 and RE3 failed in my opinion. Side note for those who enjoy parrying in games. This has a bit of a funky one. You basically can just spam the space bar to parry without consequence. Also I found it to be really inconsistent at times. Where you'll have someone trying to grab you and you go to press space just as they are coming and yet you still get grabbed. Other times you successfully parry them. I whole heatedly see why people install a parry mod because after doing enough mercenaries I strongly feel annoyed at times with how the enemies can just grab you regardless. If you find that you agree with what I've said and enjoy a game that gives you the freedom you want to explore... pick up a copy of RE4R and you wont regret it. I thought at first my computer probably wont be able to handle it, but it runs smoother than you might expect.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: For anybody who loved the original, no review necessary. This is the same game modernised and it's better, just get it.For anybody who hasn't played the original, this is a horror/action third person shooter with some RPG elements.The combat may feel somewhat claustrophobic and difficult to adjust to at first, but this is entirely by design. The game's mechanics are primarily built around managing your limited resources effectively in high intensity and stressful situations. It has a difficulty setting, so I've only played on Hardcore and I can confirm that there is definitely some challenge in this mode. I haven't played the lower difficulties, but judging from previous RE games, they should make it a lot easier for new comers. This plays best on Mouse and Keyboard, despite originally wanting to play it on gamepad, the shooting mechanics are perfect for a mouse.The game takes place in a rural setting in Spain where a cult has infected all the residents with a parasite known as Las Plagas, transforming them into zombie like creatures. You play as Leon Kennedy who has been sent there to rescue the daughter of the US president who has been kidnapped by the aforementioned cult. It's a pretty good story, can be a little cheesy at times, but I often find too much nuance and realism in a horror story will nullify the horror aspect.I've played 10 hours so far and I'd say I'm about 25% through. I am a completionist, however. So I leave no stone unturned. For your average casual player who's not interested in exploring every corner and finishing every challenge, I would say you'll likely be finished in around 15 hours.The game is worth full price and is definitely within the top 5 resident evil games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first run on Resident Evil 4 Remake. And let's straight go to the point, this remake is excellent. I never played the original game so it's total discovery for me.The updated graphics and sound design are impressive, bringing the game's environments and characters to life in a way that was not possible in the original version. The controls have also been refined, making the gameplay smoother and more intuitive, without sacrificing the challenge and tension that made the original so memorable.A couple of bad sides however : I feel sometime RE4R is more action shooter than a proper Resident Evil game. On my first run, I killed exactly 753 mobs according to chapters stats... Furthermore some puzzles are utterly boring.Gameplay is a bit clunky in some sequences when being outnumbered by enemies.Also as the previous game, Resident Evil 4 Remake can accept mods with Fluffy Mod Manager. Some mods are quite interesting.I do recommend  ! Resident Evil 4 Remake is a fantastic update to a classic game that is sure to delight both old and new fans of the series. With its improved visuals, sound design, and gameplay mechanics, it's a worthy addition to the Resident Evil saga. Now CAPCOM, you know what you have to do : start the remake of Resident Evil Code Veronica ! We want it !

_childDocuments_.review: RE4 is a genre defining game of a generation that has generally stood the test of time over the years, staying both iconic and incredible to go back to, even after the slew of sequels and remakes that have come for RE over the last few years. Has this remake done the original justice? Has it messed up the formula? Or has it somehow risen above the original? This game is gorgeous. It runs like a dream and looks incredible with ray tracing and water textures really being a standout.The combat is heavy and meaty, being altered from the original so that you can move instead of being a turret like in the original. Is this as good as the original? To me, yes. But to a purist, no. It was never going to completely change horror like the original did, and it was never going to be this paradigm shifting game, inspiring the likes of Dead Space. But is this a fantastic game in its own right? Oh yes. A solid buy!

_childDocuments_.review: Best RE game ever created. I have hundreds of hours in the original RE4, starting as a kid and playing a couple times a year, every year. This game is just as much of a masterpiece as the original. It took everything that the original did well and improved upon it. It then took everything that was old/dated from the original, and modernized it to be more appropriate for modern systems/gaming. It is perfect and I cannot say anything negative about it.Edit: Separate Ways was well worth the money. Capcom went above and beyond in this remastered DLC. It certainly has some big changes from the original version, but I think the changes are for the better and help it make more sense both chronologically and in terms of the flow of Ada's story. Things that were removed got replaced with new things that were imo better than the original. Things that remained were re-imagined and executed very well. My only complaint is that this was a great opportunity for Capcom to add the PRL-412, but they didn't (for whatever reason). Maybe it'll come in the future if they add new, original DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: All the Resident Evil remakes are simply the best.I only regret losing time playing something else when this was released.Update after finishing 1st run:As a wise person once said, “Escort missions are scientifically proven to spoil the fun for every game that is not Resident Evil 4,” I can only agree.It’s the only game where escorting another NPC not only works but is even truly enjoyable. The story, graphics, and gameplay are all amazing. It gets a little bit repetitive in the 2nd half, and the regenerators are pretty disgusting, but still, it’s an amazing game. It’s the least scary of the remakes, I would say, with plenty of action as you play as a specially trained policeman/soldier. On Normal difficulty I found it on the easier end and using rocket launcher only once during the entire playthrough kept me well supplied for the rest of the game.Fun fact - tuned Red 9 was my default weapon as it's pretty powerful with plenty of ammo, only switching to something stronger when things got a bit hairy. The only annoying thing is the shooting range, which would be fun if it didn’t require perfecting of every task there with nearly 0 chance to get something useful for the silver and gold tokens you win by this lengthy process.Village is still the best Resident Evil, then 2 or 4 remakes, maybe sharing the spot, followed by 3 remake.Overall, RE remakes are among (if not) the best games ever made, and they deserve every award they keep receiving.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: As a devoted fan of the Resident Evil franchise, I approached the highly anticipated RE4 Remake with a mix of excitement and scepticism. After immersing myself in the REimagined into it, I can confidently say that the Resident Evil 4 Remake not only lives up to the legacy of the original but surpasses it in ways that redefine the standard for remakes in the gaming industry.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: This remake is a masterpiece! From the suspensful scary beginning to the action-packed craziness in the end. Definitely a GOTY in my book.To start things of, I like this remake the most of the 3. I'm a huge fan of the more action-like approach. I wasn't very keen on all the puzzles and backtracking in RE2R and RE3R was just a bit short for my taste - but that's just a fact.I haven't played the original RE4, so I'm gonna talk about the remake as a completely new game (to me).Six years have passed since the biological disaster in Raccoon City. Leon S. Kennedy, one of the survivors, tracks the president's kidnapped daughter to a secluded European village, where there is something terribly wrong with the locals...The story is very well paced. Your placed in Leon's shoes as you uncover the truth about what this strange place you're currently on is and what happened here... And of course there's Ashley.All characters are very well written. They feel human, showing their emotions - telling jokes, acting frightened, having sincere dialogues between each other. And of course they are many great and badass one-liners!Ashley and Luis went through a great upgrade from what I've seen from the original. To all those Ada haters, just get over it. Her voice is completely fine.The gameplay is once again more action packed just like RE3R. Well except there's no slowmotion this time around. Gun play feels good and the best of all is the balance of every single weapon. Capcom managed to hit the nail right on the head. It just feels so good to switch the weapons around and really have fun with them... Yes even the TMP. Even though I'm personally a sucker for the Red9. The only inconvenience I can think of is there is no dodge button, but I get that the game would be too easy with a parry button AND a dodge button. It's just that it sometimes feels weird that running away from enemies is the only "dodge" movement you can do.I LOVED playing through this DLC. The way it ties parts of the main story together is just amazing. I already did multiple playthroughs as I really enjoy it. Another great thing about this exceptional remake!
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: I was about to give them a thumbs down as I saw no mercenaries. OG players like myself at a young age found out about the S rank in Mercenaries mode on every character to unlock the hand cannon back in the day as it was one of the only items in the original with the infinite ammo perk to unlock. Seeing it not ingame on day one had be a big disappointment, but 2 weeks later they released the Mercenaries mode allowing players to follow in the same path as the OG game to unlock the hand cannon. Lastly thank you CAPCOM for learning your mistakes with the RE3 remake and deciding against emasculating Leon or updating the game for a "Modern Audience". You listened to your fans/customers instead of the Game Journalists and now you reap the benefits with a nice blue Overwhelmingly Positive review score which will lead to more future sales.

_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best remakes ever made. It must be hard to make such a good remake for such a good game, but Capcom nailed it. This is an example to be followed, specially now that remakes are becoming so popular. Some parts were removed, some parts were added, some parts were extremely changed, but every modification was well thought and well implemented. There is literally nothing wrong with Resident Evil 4 Remake, nothing to complain about. We have the base game, we have mercenaries, we have Separate Ways, and everything was clearly done with love and care. The graphics are stunning, the optimization is excellent, the atmosphere is perfect and the gameplay is awesome. This is a must have for every Resident Evil fan, and if you liked the original, you are going to love this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: Came for the rescue, stayed for bingo. This is the best remake Capcom has done. A perfect remake of a legendary and perfect game that changed gaming forever. I love how many things have been kept the same and also changed, which makes it feel a bit like playing RE4 for the first time. If they continue making these, I'm hoping they do Code Veronica or Dino Crisis next.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best paced games i have played. Start to finish tight level design, great shooting. The depth in progression , weapons, inventory management everything is so well done. The level design , exploration , the enemy variety & complexity , puzzles everything was so varied and kept me engaged till the end. These are the perks of a linear level based game design which just cannot be matched in open worlds. The gameplay and difficulty felt perfectly balanced. Great job Capcom !!Visually the game presents great atmosphere and mood fit for the setting. RE Engine shines perfectly optimized , controls flawlessly a treat to play. My main complaint are the dialogues and characters. I get it that this is supposed to be a 2000's action movie kind of feel. But lot of times i felt the dialogues were just characters telling one another's name, speaking very brief 1 or sentences , never felt like real characters talking to one another. If the characters actually "talk" lot of the plot points would have been better. In terms of level design the island levels in later part of game felt rushed with mostly similar looking blocky buildings and corridors, I just loved the Spanish village and those levels more.8.5/10 . I havent played original RE games and having played RE2, 3, 4 remake I prefer these RE remakes over the new first person style and hope Capcom continues to make some third person RE games.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: I scoffed at this game even up until the release, thinking "Resident Evil 4 doesn't need a remake, it's still one of the greatest of all time!" I didn't think this looked bad by any measure--I think it honestly looked like the best game yet in terms of raw playability and content--but similar to the Dead Space 2023 remake, I just couldn't bring myself to buy it on release. Even now, I look at something like Dead Space 2023 and think, sure it looks way, way better but what else does it do, if anything? The original is still perfectly playable and looks great if you squint.But after finishing RE4 2023 for the first time, I have a new favorite. Not just in the Resident Evil franchise, but Of All Time. Every fiber of the original game is perfectly in tact: Leon is still cracking jokes; the Merchant is mysterious and fun; the story is campy and well-written; the combat is frenetic but tactical, even with moving and shooting; the list goes on and on. If there's something about the original you loved, it's still fully baked into this remake.I was surprised at not only how much original DNA and heart was carried over, but how well the gameplay worked, too, even taking into consideration the perfectly tuned original. While you can move and shoot, standing still to let the reticule shrink to its smallest for critical hits is a wonderful way to still make it feel "classic" without being dated. Roundhouse kicking enemies still feels powerful and hilariously fun, and even the animations are touched up but still very much what I'd expect form Los Illuminados villains. I could envision all the original tenants on a white board at Capcom's offices with little arrows saying, "do this, but modern". And ♥♥♥♥, Ashley is a WONDERFUL character this time around. I want more Leon and Ashley team ups, they work extremely well--maybe RE5 Reimagined, or a new spin off series? Luis, too, is no longer a throwaway gray character to let the plot remove your parasites, but someone with an understandable motivation and likable personality--the actor for him (and, frankly, everyone else) knock it out of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ park. His death actually meant something, and made me feel things alongside Leon.Move over RE2 Remake and Village, there's a new favorite on the podium!

_childDocuments_.review: In this sense, following the great trend of Resident Evil 2 Remake and, more recently, Dead Space Remake (pretending Resident Evil 3 Remake does not exist for obvious reasons), Resident Evil 4 Remake (RE4) can be rightfully considered another perfect example of how you remake one of the highest and most iconic points of a franchise. every single aspect of RE4 has been carefully reimagined and adapted to today's standards. While the graphics speak for themselves (and the graphics options menu is one of the best ones around - with tons of options, each showcasing comparison pictures, explaining exactly what it does, which parts of your PC affects and what part of the visuals it will improve/hinder), Leon and the other characters have tons of situational and conditional animations and comments that make them look truly alive. A couple examples: Is it raining? The characters will visibly be annoyed. Running too much? Leon will be holding his side and be winded for a bit. A crossbow bolt flies next to Leon's ear? He'll react (alongside you doing the same on your gaming chair).There's just so much going on, and the best part is that none of this affects gameplay: it's there for immersion, because "why not?".Certain sections and encounters have been rearranged or expanded while making sure who played the original feels right at home and those players, like myself, will find themselves smiling and grinning at the screen whenever certain memories are unlocked or expectations are met.There's only one big encounter missing from the original game, although its absence is objectively painless and, that aside, every single pixel of the original was taken into account for this remake - puzzles included - unlike Resident Evil 3 Remake.But don't worry: while being more grounded to a "highly improbable, but plausible reality", the game keeps all the cheesiness that made the original great, although now there's far fewer plot holes, characters have far more depth and everything plays out and is overall explained better, on top of having a great pacing. they have been integrated into the gameplay flawlessly, allowing for dodging certain attacks and parrying with your trusty knife (which can also defend you from insta-kills for as long as it's not broken).Basically: anything that was in a cutscene that could be integrated into gameplay instead, it's now a playable part of the game, giving the player a fair chance to fight back.This definitely helps with giving you the feeling you're not that helpless in situations where you had to face a Game Over screen in the original. Leon does feel like a trained super-agent of sorts, despite having to face a nightmare. from concept arts, to costumes, to special weapons and suitcase customizations (your inventory). And don't be fooled by the shower of paid DLCs Capcom released alongside the game: if you really feel you're lacking something, aside from the two extra weapons and the extra treasure map (and the original sound effects and music, if you're into a nostalgia trip) they're all completely useless and unnecessary.Also, the most important one (the extra game mode "The Mercenaries") is free. Although players are rightfully concerned regarding "Separate Ways", a story DLC following the main plot from the perspective of a different character, which is still missing as of writing this. If exploration was rewarding in the original game, you can be sure this remake got you covered. The legendary Merchant is back with his arsenal of weapons, his "Welcome!", "Stranger!", "Aahh!" and any other "excited RE4 Merchant noise" you can imagine, and he's eager to buy everything you sell him... "at a high price!".Also, the dynamic loot will make sure you're always ALMOST out of everything, but got just enough to keep going (regardless of difficulty - for as long as you know at least half of what you're doing). Long story short: if you ever find yourself in a situation where you have a bit more ammo/healing than usual, it means you're about to throw your whole suitcase at a boss or a tough encounter.And if all of the above didn't convince you this is a masterpiece of a remake, then pay close attention to the suitcase charms: they use the 3D models of the original game from 2005. What's more to say?

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, inferior to the original.I actually replayed the original RE4 pretty recently as I had a urge to revisit the game, and when you compare the remake and the original, I feel like the original comes out on top.The main reason why I personally feel like the original is much better than the remake, is the tone of the writing. They made some major changes to the story, rewriting dialogue and changing up the major beats. I wont spoil anything, but overall, if you played the original, you know that its super campy and it leans into the silliness of the writing and characters yet still managed to be somewhat serious at times. The remake's writing seems like they are trying WAY too hard to be realistic and grounded, it feels like any bit of silliness and camp are taboo.I know that there has been talk about Ada's new voice acting. I am in agreement that the new voiceacting is bad. I dont really have a problem that she has a very different voice to the original, the problem is the direction. Im guessing whoever was directing the voice actor, had no idea what the heck they were doing, so she has the most deadpan, lifeless VO ive heard in a long time. The original had campy silly characters, without that, Ada becomes this stiff wooden doll (ive seen more dynamic and interesting figures and dolls).The gameplay and combat overall, is a step up from the original. The guns feel more meaty to use, and the ability to actually move while aiming using modern controls is great. There are some changes made that are somewhat annoying though. They added reticule blooming, which I hate. This makes it so that, as an example, the Red 9 is worthless without the stock. The street sweeper also is mostly worthless as well, since its as if the gun has a duck bill choke but you are working with a barrel that isnt even the length of the shell. The spread of the street sweeper is half the screen or more from what it seems. The new knife mechanics are pretty good too, but its annoying to continually have to pay to repair your gear.The biggest positive for the remake, is the decision to completely cut out the quick time events, That is the biggest negative thing for the original game. No matter how good you are at shooting, managing your resources, nothing is more annoying than missing a button prompt in a cutscene and just instantly dying.The inclusion of crafting and the new changed ammo system are bad though. The crafting ability makes it so you have a problem with inventory bloat, and its a band-aid solution to the bad ammo spawn system. The ammo system trys to be dynamic and keep the difficulty up to a moderate level by adjusting the ammo drops. The original game had a system as well. The new ammo drop system tries to keep your ammo UNDER a certain amount (total in your inventory) with an example of something like a total of about 25 rounds of handgun ammo in your inventory at all times (this includes inside your gun). This makes guns like the matilda and the streetsweeper worthless, as the system denies you ammo to the point where you cant even keep the gun fully topped up reliably. The crafting allows a bit of a bandaid to the problem, as you can craft ammo, but the crafting parts take up space in your inventory, making you feel like you are always short on space. This drastic change in the ammo drop system mad it so that I was always feeling like I was low on ammo, and was actively discouraged from using any other weapons outside of my handgun due to the shortage of ammo (your default suitcase increases handgun ammo drops). It felt like of all the shots through the entire game I made, 95% of them were with the handgun or the bolt caster. I was hesitant to use anything else, even when going against hard enemies, I didnt want to use my shotgun/rifle/magnum, since ammo was so stupidly scarce (I picked up a grand total of 6 magnum rounds in my entire first playthrough). The original, at least from my experience, has a ammo drop system that works better. it almost exclusively drops ammo for the guns in your inventory, and goes off of the spare ammo. you always have a chance of ammo, but it increases the drop if you are low, so you can actually stockpile ammo if you are skilled.As a complete package its not as good as the original, its fun, dont get me wrong, but the writing and direction really feel like it was all redone without understanding why people loved the original, if anything, it feels like the writers actively detested the original script and story. Even the ending credits is a weaker, as it just doesnt hit as hard with the visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:If you like action, Dead Space, and/or the original RE4, then you’ll like this game. Do you like slow paced survival-focused gameplay? Do you like item management, backtracking, not having enough ammo to kill all the enemies? Do you like tension and actually being scared? Do you prefer the RE1 remake, RE0, and/or the RE2 Remake over RE4 and Dead Space? If so then you might not like this game.-------------------------Resident Evil games come in 3 flavors. Games that focus on survival:RE1 RemakeRE0RE2 RemakeGames that focus on horror:RE7(I assume RE8 but I haven’t played it yet.)And games that focus on action:RE4RE5The RE4 Remake, like the game it’s based on, focuses on action.Out of all the games that focus on action, it’s probably the best one. But I don’t like these games. Is it a good game? Yes. Do I like it? Not really.I feel like if the game would have just ended at the village I would have liked the game more. That was by far the best section of the game.Was the castle good? Yes. It was much, much improved over the original RE4 castle. They took out most of the dumb stuff. They removed the lava room. The giant Salazar statue chasing you. The rooms where there were gun turrets inside of the castle (why would you put a gatling gun in your own building? If you ever used it you would tear your own building apart).Was the Island good? Not really. I feel like it overstayed its welcome. By the time I got to the island I didn’t want to do the spinel side missions anymore. I didn’t care about the environmental storytelling. I didn’t even bother looking for the treasures. I just wanted to get the game over with. I liked the first few enemy encounters. They were much improved with the addition of the stealth mechanic. I liked the very first Regenerator encounter. That was great. But I didn’t really enjoy much else of this section.I spent my time trying to figure out how to make this into a survival game. I wanted it to play like the RE1 Remake on Real Survival mode with no ink ribbons, but you can’t really play the RE4 Remake like this because there are just too many 1 hit deaths and the game is too long. There are also dumb sections (like the mine cart section) that use completely different mechanics from the rest of the game. It’s a fast paced on-rails shooting section where you are given infinite ammo and a set amount of health. You cannot use healing items.I wouldn’t want to play a no save play through and then die at this gimmicky part that has nothing to do with resource management, navigating the environment, or close quarters combat. I’d say this game is better than the original, mostly because there were some great additions to the Village section, removal of dumb sections from the castle section, and some overall great additions to the game mechanics.Stealth: The addition of stealth fit so well, and it was completely optional. Knife parrying: It’s very cool, but it makes the game less intense. Especially when there is a chainsaw enemy in the vicinity. I got myself caught between a dead end and a chainsaw guy, and I was able to just parry his attack then run away. This makes the game less tense since you can just parry yourself out of a bad situation. I personally feel like I should have died for being so unaware of my environment and making such bad decisions as to get myself trapped like that. Removal of QTEs (for the most part): Great.Spinels system: There are now sub quests that you can complete in order to obtain spinels, which can be traded for items, which cannot otherwise be purchased. I loved the side missions in the village, and I liked the extra strategy of deciding how to spend your rewards.Conclusion:My “Not recommended” review is just a matter of preference. I don’t like action horror. If you like action horror, then you’ll like this game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games in my collection that has inspired me to play through more than once.One of the even fewer games that inspires me to post a review and I'm happy that I can - for once - rave instead of rant.In a world that has seen so many disappointing releases; _this_ game has renewed my faith in the industry.A compelling story combined with great visuals, action and some puzzles (not too many as to be obnoxious) kept my interest throughout. The adventuring companions one encounters are both fun and interesting and there's a great chemistry between them all.The pacing is good and there are additional mini-games (optional) that provide a bit of levity to take a break from what is otherwise quite a dark atmosphere.Combat is extremely satisfying and enemies will react quite realistically depending on hit location. While the genre does encourage a bit of an over the top kind of feel at times this game does a great job of keeping things to where one can suspend disbelief during the entire ride.While some of CAPCOM's other titles have flopped in my opinion (especially on PC) this title deserves to be what I see now on steam as "Overwhelmingly Positive". It is my pleasure and honor to recommend this game, without reservation, to the fellow gamers out there :)

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't touched the Resident Evil games prior to playing the RE4 remake. And holy s#!t, I was missing out so much.Between the dorky dialogue delivered perfectly by the actors, superbly crafted survival horror mechanics, and the downright ridiculous plot that this game somehow had me invested in from the first minutes, Resident Evil 4 is just so damn fun.This game feels like a love letter to horror/action media as a whole. It dares to throw every single cliché, every cheesy line, every single trope, and yet it manages to establish itself as something unique from other franchises. It does all that while challenging the player in the simplest way possible by displaying their stats. This, combined with the additional Pro difficulty unlocked after beating the game, and the challenge bucket list available in the extras menu was enough to keep me invested for way longer than I thought I'd ever be - in a horror game released in the current gaming market.As a final note, I deeply appreciate games that aren't over after you finish them, and this one doesn't fail to meet that expectation. If you share the same sentiment as I do, then good luck on your S+ runs ;)

I like to run and gun John Wick style and don't have the patience for stealth or timed attacks.  I was afraid the remake version would have the same punishing gameplay and was excited to see that I could lower the difficulty and actually have a good time with this version of the game. I honestly steered away from any idea of purchasing RE4 again because of my past experiences, I'm glad I caved in. I really thought I'd be refunding it. I know I'm still early in at chapter 4 but I'm having a blast and recommend this game for gamers that might be afraid of picking up this title due to it's challenging reputation. It's definitely approachable for less skilled players. As a side note I've been playing on my Legion GO and Asus Rog Ally and it's been running great.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best game I had played this year. Just like RE2 Remake, Capcom came back and delivered another good remake with RE4. I am personally very surprised at how well the game managed to hook me.Unlike the OG RE4 the story here ties to RE2 Remake. It also actually has a plot unlike the original where it was just there to fill a void. The remakes fixes alot of the original story while also enhancing it by fleshing out the characters. Gameplay wise it keeps alot of parts from the original while either changing some parts or removing them. Most of the parts that were removed honestly were annoying anyway and I also don't miss the cut boss either. The parts they did changed were done in a way that made them alot more enjoyable from the original. For example the Ashley or the minecart section felt alot more fun to do in the remake then the original. The changes to Luis are also great. Overall I can't say the game felt shorter than the OG did, infact I took longer to finish my first playthrough of the Remake compared to the OG.Gunplay and movement been updated to a modern standard. Unlike the OG where movement was slower, here you have a more action oriented gameplay with faster enemies running at you and also there just being more in general.What I do miss is the ada separate way dlc from the OG. It was a great addition to the OG in terms of fleshing out their story and I would have loved to see that remade. Also Adas Eng VA in the remake is honestly so bad I really wish they would have kept the one from RE2 Remake or took someone else.Overall a very good game, can definitely recommend this game over the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: The somehow took one of the best entries in the series and made it even better. The gunplay is so satifying. Movement feels weighty but not clunky. The story is much more grounded with to fall in line with the newer games but again somehow its even better for it. For those who are familiar with the 2005 release be prepared to have alot of familiarity ripped from you in terms of map layouts, enemies and more. Especailly did the one thing most companies don't seem to want to bother with, THEY ADDED ORIGINALLY CUT CONTENT INTO THE GAME! ¡Mis hermanos y hermanas, regocíjense!  ¡Porque la hora de nuestro regreso finalmente ha llegado y es hermoso!Also, detrás de ti idiota!

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Pros: Engaging gameplayImmersive GraphicsTight ControlsCons:Unengaging StoryVoice ActingWith those basics out of the way anyone may be wondering why "7/10" my pros and cons seem more suited to a 5/10.  Well the short answer is that unlike the original RE4 I actually finished the Remake. The big reason for this were the controls which felt more natural and intuitive than RE4'S original PC port.Outside of the controls I found the gameplay loop far more engaging, and while the story wasn't that great I enjoyed my time with the characters a lot more.  To put it simply everyone was an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the original version and here they are not.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: 8.9/10. High quality product.Only issue I found was not being able to look around while driving the boat. Could only look in the direction I was travelling, which was a right pain in the a.. .For me, everything else was without complaint, bar not being able to store some inventory items like  ammunition or herbs. Additionally it would have been extremely helpful to have had upgrade values for weapons while in game. Having to google to figure out which weapon would have the highest stats once upgraded, was inconvenient. As was to a lesser degree, not being able to tune-up weapons in storage.I played the original RE4 HD Edition in 2015. While I liked that game it was overshadowed by poor movement controls. Granted after some time it was possible to adapt to the control format. However it put me off replaying, which is not funny.The remake was in that respect more immersive. I was totally into playing. Undeniably RE4 HD Edition was they said, 'lightning in a bottle'. Such a shame it was hampered by controls, where the remake shines with it's modern take on controls. The remake is something else in a bottle, but just not sure what - maybe thunder.I loved every minute of playing RE4 remake. I was never bored. I regularly felt that this was a brilliant game. That I was playing one of the 'the best games'. As I played it doing all side quests and searching out all treasures, it took me 34.5 hours to play. Value for money, as I will replay more than once.Solidly brilliant game.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: After 22 hours of playtime and %100 done, what can I say? It's a masterpiece.Incredible reimagining of the original with some extra scenarios to keep the experience fresh. Although they do remove some scenes and plot points, they aren't very iconic or impactful which keeps the game from straying away too far from the original. Although I may not enjoy some of the rewritten dialogue, especially regarding Luis’ character and how all of a sudden everyone is rude to him, as apposed to the original where he’s meant to be seen as charming yet somewhat untrustworthy and mysterious, to the new dialogue is faithful and different enough to be unique. The resident evil team did an incredible job recreating this incredible classic and I hope the remake becomes just as iconic, despite nerfing Ashley’s ballistics. Definitely rooting for this one to be game of the year!
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better remakes there have been for games in general, not even just in recent years. The gameplay of the original is captured near perfectly and definitely improved upon, removed some of the most annoying aspects of the original while adding it's own unique touch that does enough to separate the remake from the original, and best of all the original is still available to purchase and play instead of being replaced and de-listed. My only gripes for the game would be the toning down of the personality and interactions between characters, mainly between Leon and the villains of the story, it hardly feels like they interact at all between fights, while in the original there was near constant, albeit cheesy banter between them. Would have loved to see some of the old radio conversations with Salazar and Saddler, but the improved writing between Leon and Ashley makes up for it I suppose. Overall the game is definitely worth a buy, whether you enjoyed the original or not, it stands on it's own two feet very well.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: After playing 130 hours, completing game over 10+ times and unlocking tons of stuff, I can't S+ run the game on Veteran, because of Twin Garradors.I'm not new to RE, platinumed RE7, RE8, RE2+RE3 Remakes, but this difficulty just f**ks your brain stupid.It's not fun anymore, it has become pure frustration.If Capcom thinks they can make me play another 130 hours, they are wrong. Next game I won't preorder, but wait to see what people say about difficulty and then either buy or don't buy it.Final assessment: 90/100 for the game itself, 70/100 als final one because of the crazy difficulty.

_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: Good game like all the recent RE games, good graphics, runs well, no technical issues really. Seems to mostly be the same as the original game though so you don't necessarily need to play this one if you played the original. It does have quite a few issues that are a bit annoying.First of all yeah Ada's voice acting really isn't that great but she doesn't really appear that often so you don't really need to worry about it. The main issues I have with the game are just the gameplay and how much worse it is than the other RE games. I was playing on hardcore mode so a bit of a challenge is understandable however a lot of the game just felt like trial and error. On top of that most of the combat when you're not shooting relies on you using your knife to parry but a lot of the time you just end up getting hit anyway and there's no dodge button so you pretty much have to just sluggishly move out of the way out of certain attacks. There are dodge prompts once in a while but they are extremely inconsistent, a lot of the time when you're fighting bigger enemies its pretty much impossible to avoid their attacks especially when the character movement is so slow. A lot of the enemies are BS as well, there's times with the long range enemies where they'll pre-fire you as you're coming around a corner so that's really annoying and overall there's just so many unnavoidable attacks. Didn't really have a problem with the combat in any of the other RE games but this one its just really bad and not fun compared to the others. The shooting range in this really isn't that good, a lot of the time it seems like especially in the later challenges that instead of requiring skill to beat they just require repetition so its just not fun trying to figure out which weapon to use, how long to wait to shoot specific targets and where all the bonus things are and then combining all that its just a pain really. Also the rewards you get are coins you can use on a machine that gives you trinkets you can use to get certain buffs but most of them are absolutely useless, most of it is just stuff like you get more money for selling specific items or you get more ammo for crafting specific ammo, most of it is just duplicates of the same thing and you really don't need to use most of them, you can get by just fine, most of the game I had atleast 100k cash to spare. Aside from all that though yeah decent game if you like more RE games of the same quality of the other recent ones you'll enjoy it, lots of things to unlock, challenges to beat and all that. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another game ported with DRM that causes constant crashing, stuttering issues, and people rushing to the defense claiming that it is anything but DRM.  This was proven false with the last two Resident Evils, as soon as the DRM was removed system issues magically were removed and fixed not because of any kind of magical patch.My advise.  The game is decent if you can get it to work without crashing.  (FYI I have a system that should be able to run two instances of the game on max settings no issue whatsoever, but can't even speak to the merchant in a latter chapter because soon as I walk into the door it crashes after a few seconds.)Wait until a sale, they remove DRM, and then enjoy the game.  If I had not been over the limit I would request a refund and just wait.  10 hours at the time of this review to run into crashing.  Thank everything that is holy I waited until Resident Evil 7 removed DRM to buy it, I missed the crap with that, but wanted to give capcom a try with DRM since they typically remove it.  Do yourself a favor and just wait.  You should not have to lower your graphics or do any work around to play a game.Want 100% proof DRM is cancer?  Go look up PC version of Operation Red River.  It can take upwards of 6 hours of 'work arounds' to play a game that you own legitly, yet because of DRM rendered 100% broken.  Even the old RE games suffer from this like RE5 and what not.  Yeah it may require a single download but it is just further proof that this anti-consumerism needs to stop.Wait for a sale, DRM removal, and then enjoy the game.  When pirates get a better working version of a game then people who paid $60 or more, you know how much the company cares about your money.  (Spoilers, they do not give a crap about you just how much profit they make, not the experience.)

_childDocuments_.review: There is definitely room for improvement; some bosses near the end are way to easy, Ada's voice is flat (not the actors fault, but that of casting and directing). I think the best part of it for me was seeing how much the creators loved the original, You'll find yourself smiling over and over at all the details and references to the original. All in all it's worth it, I don't regret getting it and imagine I'll have hundreds of hours on it before I'm done with it. But OMG please try again with that voice. Maybe mix things up and use Sandy Cheeks for Ada this time, I would totally pay for that DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Resident Evil 4

_childDocuments_.review: I spent a ton of time as a kid discussing secrets from the original Resident Evil 4. I would spend hours watching videos online talking about the best weapons and the locations of hidden treasures. This game makes me feel like that kid again. I loved the original and I love this game. There are so many amazing areas that return in this game and look they exactly as I thought they would look like when I was a kid imagining a more modern version of the original. If you are like me and hold the original close to your heart then I would highly suggest you pick this up. This game should be used as the standard that all other remakes from any series in gaming should follow. I've beaten it on every difficulty now and have done the same with the DLC. As of now, I'm currently on my fourth play-through of the main story and plan to 100% this game in a few weeks. I highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 4, 2005’s legendary survival horror, is brought fully up-to-date in this ground-up remake. Six years after the events of Resident Evil 2, Raccoon City survivor Leon Kennedy has been dispatched to a secluded European village to investigate the disappearance of the US president’s daughter. What he discovers there is unlike anything he has faced before. Every aspect of the classic game has been updated for the current generation, from modernized graphics and controls, to a reimagined storyline that may surprise even hardened fans of the original game.
