_childDocuments_.review: I've been liking it a lot so far. I don't like that it still limits you to just one character and save file, and I've definitely had fps drops in the capital city down as low as 30fps at times, but out in the open world where I'm doing most of my questing and fighting, it runs pretty steady. I feel like the Pawns are smarter and more useful in this game than the last one. I like that they can be specialized to gain new abilities like using items on others rather than just themselves or finding and combining ingredients to drown you in an ocean of Salubrious Droughts and other potions. Even better than any of that, Pawns that have discovered something in another world will try to physically lead you to hidden chests and locations they know about, but your other Pawns don't. Conversely, if you're exploring and find a hidden thing, the hired Pawns will remark about needing to relay that back to their own masters-presumably implying they will lead other players to it if those players get close in their worlds. There's a Pawn quest and badge system where you can request other players complete a specified quest with your Pawn if they hire it and offer a reward from your inventory or some gold as thanks. Quests as easy as just adventuring together for an in game day or hunting a specific monster like a cyclops. Cause if my Pawn hunts 30 cyclops for example, it will get a badge for that and presumably be able to offer more useful methods of hunting them for me and other players who might hire it. At least according to the tooltip about it in the game, anyway. You can also gift equipment to other players' Pawns by equipping it to them. It sends their currently equipped gear to that player's inventory and gifts then equips the new piece each time. This allows you to try out new gear and upgrade it for random players or friends' Pawns. In addition, you can find these golden beetles out in the world and when used, they permanently increase yours or your main Pawn's carrying capacity by a set amount each time.As far as the combat goes, I've been playing the Archer vocation and liking it a lot. I have to craft or buy the various special arrows I'd need for those related skills. To use my explosive arrow skill for example, I need to combine withered branches and a sunbloom to make 5 of them, or buy them from a vendor. I like it cause it feels like you're not relying on or spamming them and instead using other skills more. Ones that fire in a wide area, or rapidly in succession-stuff like that. I made a Mage Pawn to keep my party healed and enchant our weapons with fire or lightning. It feels like it's more active about all of that stuff. Instead of getting my weapons enchanted as the combat's already over, they're on it usually by the time I've fired my 2nd or 3rd shot and will change it seemingly to the situation. It could have been coincidence, but as an example, they don't use fire when it's raining it seems. They use lightning cause everything is drenched and weaker to lightning. The other 2 Pawns I currently have hired are a another Archer to help me hit flying enemies, and a big brute warrior to bully things around and help carry a bunch of stuff. Cause now you have to carry a camping kit if you wanna make use of the many camping sites dotted around the map and recover lost max hp.The game has something called a loss gauge and you'll be losing max hp as you take damage and the longer you go without resting, the more of your total hp is capped by the lost gauge, making all forms of healing less worth using and combat overall more dangerous. I've had all the way up to half my max hp lost from stupidly wandering around without bringing a camping kit. I could've used a ferrystone to fast travel back to town, but that would've been a waste of 10k.Speaking of, there are some vendors who sell the fast travel items and you can get them as quest rewards or find them out in the world, but they are half the price of the house I just bought in game before writing this review. I watched some lady's house in game for a week getting free night's stay and a place to access my items like an inn, then she sold it to me for 20k, the price of 2 ferrystones, or a couple pieces of decent gear from a shop, Chest gear and weapons have been costing over 10k each and the average helmet and pants are 5k and up unless you wanna buy inferior gear for some reason. You can upgrade armor and weapons and doing so also makes them weigh less so definitely do that as much as you can. A lighter inventory helps with stamina and move speed. You don't wanna be caught in combat with a heavy inventory. That said, the couple of times I had a heavy inventory, the Pawns in my group came up to me and distributed things among themselves to lighten my load. Did they do that in the last game? No, right? I can't remember.Anyway, the intro to this game-I also think it's better than the last one's was. Starting out, playing your newly created character, being introduced to the Pawns, and going all the way to the capital for the first time-everything about it, I feel has been done better in this game than the original. I hated the intro in the first game. I always felt like the game really only got worth investing time into once you made it to the capital for the first and it really opens up. This one starts letting you get lost in side quests and exploration pretty much immediately upon getting the Pawns. I think the first little town I went to was the one where I got a side quest teaching me how to combine items using recipes in this game and make or buy an item for this girl who wanted to learn how to make them for her family's apothecary shop in the capital. Later when I got to the capital, she gave me the specialization chirurgeon for my Pawn that lets it use items on others of it's own accord. I'm curious to see what other specializations and what conditions unlock them. It feels like there's so much more hidden stuff in the opening area leading up to the capital in this game. I know it's over a decade later and technology has improved a lot, but still. Technology didn't force the original's intro to be that boring and linear.If you liked the original, you probably will like this one too. If you never played the original, I still recommend this game. Don't take it the wrong way, but I liken it to Elden Ring in that it is probably a great entry for newcomers to the kind of game this is. I think within the first few hours of playing this game and having someone's Pawn encourage you to follow it to random locations and treasure, plus all of them helping you fight in combat, you'll know whether or not this is the kind of game you'd wanna keep putting more hours into. By the time you've got a dozen or so hours into it, you'll probably have already made over 100k gold in game, replaced and upgraded all your gear and your Pawn's gear as much as possible, and collected 4 or 5 fast travel items, a couple wakestones (revive items) and a couple fast travel locations to warp between. You might also have taken the ox cart fast travel system a couple times as well. Whatever you've done, hopefully it was entertaining enough to wanna keep playing because this one feels much more like an adventure game than the last one in that you're resting up til morning or night and then heading off to do a quest or 2 before you rinse and repeat and feels more like you're living the life of an adventurer in the game than the last one. I know you're supposed to be the Arisen and have a grand destiny to fight the dragon like in the last game-but I care more about all the fun you have in the game along the way to that final fight than that ultimate fight itself, usually. This feels already like a more memorable adventure than the last one just from all these side quests I've done and how they've ultimately been impacting things in other ways. (Like getting a house or Pawn specialization.)(Out of room for more review.)

_childDocuments_.review: Alright.  is not a lot of fun in my opinion. I want it to be, and I will revisit the game again in a couple months and see if my opinion has changed, but what it is right now is a janky mess with gameplay mechanics designed to encourage you to buy MTX. The story starts off kind of ridiculous, and so far as I've played, that hasn't changed. Combat is not as much fun as I'd hoped and the random encounters every fifteen feet is as unnecessary as things get.Also, you get weighed down via the encumbrance system with a nominal amount of items to begin with. Which is annoying AF.The NPCs. Oh man, the NPCs. Some are likable, but as a rule, they fall into two categories: NPCs that really want nothing to do with you and NPCs that absolutely won't stop talking. The overexplaining in this game is over the top.The Pawns are even worse about this. They never stop talking and always want you to follow them, even when all they are doing is walking into the face of a cliff, a thing that happens very frequently. They are the epitome of 'know it alls'. Dude. Aren't you supposed to be working for me? STFU please. Pretty please. With a cherry on top.I did try playing this on the Steam Deck and it obviously was unplayable. On my PC, it handled mostly okay, although the random drops into soupiness (sub 20 FPS) are definitely still a thing.Things I did enjoy:The crafting system.The amount of detail, annoying as it may be, within the scope of the game's dialogue.To some extent the quests, even if the premise for getting you to do them is generally stupid and they're mostly fetch or escort style.When the game looks good, it looks really good.I realize a lot of people enjoy this game, but in my opinion, Capcom handcuffed themselves with this game's development in order to monetize in game items and gameplay mechanics, and for some reason, they thought releasing a PS3 era style game with a $70 base price tag was a good idea. I had to laugh after the intro where the game introduces itself as Dragon's Dogma rather than Dragon's Dogma 2. I think I know where their mind was at lol. Also, the developers don't bother offering a changelog when they announce updates on Steam. What's up with that?

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Absolutely amazing game. It is good because it is different. The game don't need any of the microtransactions. Especially not on PC. You can just mod your game.All in all, a fantastic game, just like its predecessor. Anyone who loved it will also love Dragons Dogma 2. I'm also pleased that this game is now getting a bit more attention than the first instalment. The great thing about Dragons Dogma is that it breaks with the conventions of other games and does almost everything a little differently. It's a lot of fun to explore the game world here, almost reminiscent of Breath of the Wild and Elden Ring. And there are fun and useful things and enemies to discover in many places.Another brilliant thing about Dragons Dogma: the mastery skills of the classes are absolutely overpowered. And that's not wrong, because it's fun. Whilst one class can oneshot fat dragons, but then has to rest, the other is almost invulnerable and shreds his way through everything. And: The skills are not only available late, you get them relatively early from the respective teachers. The individual teachers are usually only available late in the game, but if you want to, you can get there at level 1. It's just a long and dangerous way ;)Regarding the microtransactions: Capcom has more than earned the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. However, they are completely uninteresting. I didn't even think about spending money on them. And among the monetarization of games, this is a fair one. You can just buy for your money if you want to. No advertising in game. No in game currency. No money left over after you buy. Lets get to it:Rift crystals: You get more than enough and you don't actually need them at all.Lazarus stones: You get more than enough. And even if they mean a "continue" when you die, that's how meaningless it is in the end. If I die, I just reload and play the 2 minutes until then again. The game saves very often. Also: Healing/stamina potions and food have an instant effect here. So I can still drink a healing potion when I die and stay alive. I think I revived an NPC with it 4 times and used one for myself 5-6 times and in the end I still had 17 left over, which I received in the course of the game.Art of Metamorphosis: The item with which you can change your appearance. Why should you actually? Other games don't offer that either. Except for hairstyle and make-up - and in Dragons Dogma 2 you can do that in-game with an NPC.Everything else: You don't need it, you get it in the game anyway, at the latest when you need it in the course of the game.So: zero influence on the course of the game. I also can't see that this will be patched in the future to make it more important.Nonetheless, this nonsense has not to be there.However, there were a few things that I didn't like quite so much:- Limited fast travel. Not too bad for the first 10-15 hours, but then the distances gradually get longer. The items for teleporting are unfortunately very limited, so you always have to think about whether you'd rather teleport or walk around for 4 minutes. Unfortunately, this is a decision that is not much fun.- The technology really isn't that great, especially in the towns and 2-3 areas outside.- Very limited carrying weight, which also has a significant impact on combat and running. Some people like it, I hate it. I often spend far too long on the tedious task of constantly rearranging the inventory between myself, the three companions and the storage chest. Takes too much time.- Only 2 save states, only one permanent one.The good thing about all the negative points: On the PC there is a remedy through modders. There are already a lot of useful mods and there are more and more. Except for the frame generation mod (which is actually already built into the game but not unlocked). Even with lots of tips from the community, I couldn't get it to run permanently without crashing.9/10. If it wasn't for the technical issues, it would be a 10. And apart from the Elden Ring DLC, I don't see anything coming close to it this year.Addendum: I think the monster density is too high, especially on the roads. The roads should be safer. I remember it differently from part 1. There you could travel along the roads relatively safely. In the second part, you also have to fight every few metres on the paths. Another pity: At some point during the game, I received a helmet with the description that small monsters are afraid of it. I thought I would be able to travel better with it because they would then run away. Unfortunately, it was just fluff text.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, but not yet polished; it should have undergo another 6-12 months of development before release.Pros:- Vast world with extensive exploration opportunities.- Phenomenal combat with numerous classes and skills, highly dynamic and engaging.- Evokes the feeling of a Lord of the Rings adventure.- Minimal loading times.- Efficient travel via ox carts.- Numerous caves that will give you the creeps.- Graphics that are easy on the eyes.- Exciting griffin riding.- Many fun and challenging enemies.- Epic-looking spells (if you choose to be a mage or sorc).- Discovery of new and interesting allies roaming the world.- Offers numerous gameplay options, providing a sense of freedom.Cons:- Performance issues, including FPS drops in large cities and random crashes and freezes.- Game save system is cumbersome and restrictive.- Can’t create a new character without deleting the old one.- Followers often die or disappear unexpectedly.- Ox carts are fragile and prone to destruction.- Stamina mechanics can be frustrating sometimes.- Casting spells feels excessively slow.- Some reviewers complain about microtransactions, though this may not be a significant concern for all players. You can ignore micros altogether.TL/DR: Consider purchasing this game for a good ARPG experience, or wait another year for a potentially smoother experience (hoping for bug and performance fixes).

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to edit my review now that I'm ~30 hours into my first play through.I love the game play. It fits my preferences perfectly. I'm a game master who runs games that are open world hex crawls - needless to say travel is a big part of my campaigns. The travel in DD2, especially early game - is dangerous and exciting. The quick travel options you slowly unlock are limited to certain points - traveling by cart from settlement to settlement, and limited teleport to specific locations - just feels good. Do I want to use this teleport and save a bunch of time, journey back, etc. Planning your inventory, and the inventory of your pawns, is part of the intended experience and personally, its just what I like.The story is pretty bad. The main NPCs are fine but they just don't really matter that much. The writing of the story is pretty bad too, like some real high school stuff if I'm being honest. Its a shame, but I don't think thats the focus from the developers side. The world however is much more interesting. This is a video game about details, and this game has a lot of it.While I played Dragons Dogma Dark Arisen I was not as into it as I am with DD2 so I can't make any specific comparisons. That being said, from what I've read from bigger fans of the original game the step up from 1 -> 2 isn't what they we're hoping for. I encourage you to go read some reddit threads if you're curious for more.I've had one crash and experienced some minor bugs, but nothing too crazy personally.Performance is unacceptable. 3080 with a 5900X - not top of the line obviously but by no means bad..cant hold 60 FPS in open world depending on the location/situation, and cities forget about it LOL more like 30-50. I understand that this is a brand new AAA game and my hardware isn't top of the line anymore: I was never expecting 120fps maxed out settings. But a constant 60 in 2024? That should be the bare minimum. And the frame drops - gosh the frame drops are so horrible in the city. What makes it even more frustrating is that clearly all the NPC load bogs down performance, but the NPC popup is still insanely bad. Like what are they even doing?? It may seriously be better for me to lock the fps at 40 and just be done with it until a performance patch thats supposedly coming.All of the micro transactions confuse me. Everything there you can get in game and its not really that hard or time consuming - I don't know why they would even bother adding them. I mean - ok I do - because some suit is greedy over at capcom - but its just weird and out of place. Just ignore them don't let them win.Despite me personally having fun, with the massive performance issues I can't give this game a recommendation until they are fixed. Proceed with caution. Look at some benchmarks on youtube with your hardware, and see if the performance is acceptable enough for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played Dragon's Dogma Dark Arisen on multiple platforms for years, I was stoked beyond belief for the sequel.  Didn't think it was going to happen after 12 years.  And then the unthinkable happened:  Bizarre design decisions, atrocious performance, and a world worse than the first time - which was never fully completed in that game, apparently.  So rather than an evolution we got a devolution, at best with some lateral changes but also some major flaws.  It isn't ALL bad but considering the foundation it was built upon, the game is a disappointment.The good - character customization/creation, combat, leveling up vocations.The bad - performance, especially on PC.  My PC is more powerful than my PS5 but even on potato mode, this game's performance on PC is inexcusable.  The quests are mostly boring fetch quests.  This was the case in the original but you would think that would be an easy improvement on this one.  The world feels all wrong and is a pain to navigate, especially the beginning area.  Desert area is ok.  Additional areas are too brief.  The loot hunt is abysmal.  Too little interesting loot and you can buy it in vendors.  Chests give you garbage.  Jumping sucks, there is no double jump and navigating cliffs and edges is a massive downgrade over the cool parkour you could do in the original.Game needs a really solid expansion like Dark Arisen to save it.  As it is, for me it's a 5/10 on PC (I would rate 6/10 on console due to performance).  There's better, and more re-playable games out there, sadly...

_childDocuments_.review: Man, its a rough one. I really wanted to like it, but so much feels off in the game its a grind just to play.The combat and responsiveness has improved over the first game, its more pretty, its mechanics make sense... but everything else feels like its missing something one way or another. I've just made it past the first locked story bit, (the gate to the new area).Half the game hours i am pretty sure i spent running from one place to the other.. and back again.Not to mention every 100ft on the main road you will run into: goblins, +100ft pack of wolves, +100ft pack of harpys, +100ft pack of goblins, +100ft... oh! pack of bandits this time. Movement is okay, as long as its flat, randomly some surfaces you will slide off of, others you can just walk or sprint up. Other than that it sucks so bad to go from one place to another on the *what should be the safe route*.. Your stamina ticking down while sprinting even outside of combat, an endless amount of low effort combat in combination that just drags your pace down to a slog.Pawns being locked to the starter vocations except warrior and sorcerer.The fact that the pawn specialization you get is a one time use item, so keep it as the item healer or just brick your pawn with it moving stuff around between party members constantly. its certainly a choice that they completely forget what you taught them before and that its not added to a library you can swap between freely.Gaining access to all the vocations except one being locked behind story progress is nice.. until you find you cant really progress any, or get new things past rank 10 in that vocation, just start over on a new one.Everything costs an arm and a leg. Want that new chest armor? 34k. Want that new weapon? 23k. Want to not run so much and buy teleportation? 10k a single use item. Want to rest at an inn? 3k. Want to buy some rift crystals? 1$-5$ usd :)The two new vocations... are.. something. Spearhand is bootleg Jedi in every way imaginable. it just feels out of place. Trickster is cool, if you want to play support for your Pawns ai doing weird things as they try to kill the monsters.The pop in for inside cities is the most aggressive i have ever experienced. Legitimately 5ft to a NPC bumping into them they pop in and materialize out of thin air. that whole cart? you didn't see it? nono it was there we swear.One step forward, two steps back. The motto for this entire game.

_childDocuments_.review: The performance issues are the least of this game’s problems. In the opening section, DD2 seems incredible- every new place you find has something to discover or a cool boss enemy. Then after hour ten you realize that there really is no reason to explore, each area has the exact same enemies, rewards, and caves copy pasted. There's a couple interesting quests, but the majority have you finding items or doing escort missions that make you backtrack for almost no reward.The combat's flashy, but there’s no staying power to it. You can’t perform combos, and only have a regular attack along with four special moves. Eventually, you realize the best way to approach fights is to spam attack and one or two abilities until you kill the enemy. This game really needs cooldowns on special moves and some combos to give it more depth.I think the core of Dragon's Dogma 2 is amazing, the random encounters, the pawn system, and open world all come together in first ten hours and it feels unlike anything else I've ever played. Maybe a DLC release will fix it like the first, but for now just wait for a deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I''ll try to keep this concise.I do not think this game is worth 70 to 80 dollars.I think this is an unfinished game with many features not added as to make the game harder.The first game, as someone who has played it recently and not upon release, Was good but id rank it no higher than an 8/10 and that is me considering when it was released and how it holds up. This game can't be ranked higher than a 6.5 for me but realistically id say a 5.5. The only thing this game has going for it is the combat. I think its exciting, fast paced, and most (not all) combats are fun and don't drag on too long.That being said this game is just a newer port of the first game, No new major mechanics, same/more restrictions, and the story is the same thing but instead they have a twist in the plot that they just divulge to the player in a long text within 2 hours of game play.Most characters have little to no personality. and the ones you may like don't seem to be romance-able. and even if you manage to find a character you like, if they have an escort quest, they will likely die and you cant res them right then and there and must wait days for them to appear in a morgue if you are unfortunate enough for them to die in a location where their body auto despawns like off a cliff into nothingness and into the water.Now speaking of dying, theres a disease in which a pawn (The bland and copy paste companions with no discernible personality) can get that risks them killing an entire towns npc's whenever you sleep at an inn there. There is no simple cure for it, (only known cure is spreading it and then dismissing the pawn its spread to).Around every corner there is a quest that is inconvenient whether is doesn't have a marker and will have to have listened to every word said, or look it up. There are quests in which can be failed and never to be fixed that can have SERIOUS implications for the game state (avoiding spoilers) and the game only has one save file that you cant access in game so youre stuck with what has happened or close the game without saving hoping it didn't auto save, which is an issue when you need to trouble shoot.It feels like the developers actively try to extort the player through game play around every corner and is only difficult due to lack of implemented mechanics that should be in any RPG worth its salt. There are classes that literally are just there to make the game arbitrarily harder because they are not good and don't work in every situation (I'm looking at you trickster) they removed fan favourite classes like Strider and Magic Knight and replaced them with par to sub par classes making options and possibilities for a class more divisive. There is only one support class that can actively heal and many classes they feel built like they are for co op instead of a single player world. (why would anyone play a support class in a solo game where you'd be reliant on you AI for damage) Pawns are restricted to one of the 4 default classes and then warrior and sorcerer when you unlock them even though Sorc is literally just a more DPS focused Mage with less options for utility.I will wrap up by saying I believe the game is unbalanced, frustrating around every corner, restrictive, and honestly is a worse version that looks better than the first game. This game is a far cry from what it could be. The only thing I liked about this game was the fluid and fully loaded nature of the character creator and was disappointed from the first moments following the Finish Character button.I think with a newer game like this, restriction of a players choices in the last thing you wanna do, whether for combat, or story. but in a game with little to no story, near to 0 characters with personality and development, I think the developers shot themselves in the foot and were left to bleed out in the chains they made for themselves.This game is not worth the amount they are asking for and you should likely go play the first game. sure it doesn't look as good visually but honestly not by the much and it has better mechanics and an identical story with more content.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally do reviews... but this is such a great looking game, that feels super shallow when you play it. Luckily I received it as a gift and didn't pay the full price.Performance: At first this game looked incredible and ran pretty well on my old setup, but as soon as you get near any form of civilization, the performance takes a dive. From 120 FPS in the wilds down to around 30 within city limits.Gameplay and controls: The gameplay feels sluggish. It feels as if you are having an input delay and the character does not listen to your inputs fully. A lot of times items are hidden under broken barrels or other rubble and in order to grab it, you need to go really close to it, which makes your character automatically enter the climbing animation and blocking you from picking it up. It happens so often, that I mostly ignore loot.Fighting on the other hand feels really nice. There are a few classes, to pick from, but most are locked at the start. The only problem I have with the combat system is, that my followers seem to do 90% of the work. I play mage/sorcerer and it takes AGES for me to finish casting a spell... enemies are either dead by then or are about to be dead. Don't even try fighting multiple enemies as a mage alone to see how strong you are... even the weakest enemies keep you stunlocked 24/7.Questing and Information: The game is TERRIBLE at telling you what to do. It gives you a quest that says "Find a place with lots of books for this guy." but what it really wants you to do is to go somewhere, find a boy... yatta yatta yatta. The main story had me attending a masquerade ball and find information... but what I really had to do was go somewhere COMPLETELY different. I only solved this due to my girlfriend telling me what to do. I had to go out of the marked quest zone... to do the quest...This game feels very medieval, but a little bit too much so imo. It makes you walk almost anywhere while having a gigantic map. No mounts, very clunky quicktravel. If you want to get from one city to another quick, you have to ride an ox cart. Like in skyrim back in the days. The only downside is that you can get attacked by huge monsters on the way... which happened almost every time to me so far. So you basically quick travel into boss monsters.All in all this game feels like it should have been much more. It feels like a shell of a AAA-Game that was never finished.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is clearly and painfully unfinished, and I am not even taking optimisation into account.Long explanation (rant?) ahead, TLDR: Quests are frontloaded and unfinished, no satisfying resolutions to many stories and NPCs, many mechanics to artificially prolong game time, bad progression and loot, jank pawn AI and really jank combat mechanics and difficulty. Only saving grace are the really satisfying skills and gameplay of the vocations/classes which carry the enjoyment of the game in the otherwise barren world (minus lack of dodging/blocking).The quests are extremely frontloaded, the vast majority of interesting main and side story quests are in the first half of the map and around the first capital city. The moment the main story takes you out of the first capital city, everything grinds to a halt, the main story is barely present and side quests are extremely sparse and for the most part not even remotely interesting (Rescue person A, escort person B, slay monster C, but with a few dialogue lines. Yay.) Most of the quests that do exist seemingly end in a way where you'd expect a followup quest for further development or payoff but it just never happens, and I am starting to harbor a fear that this may happen with the main story too, seeing as I'm almost at the end and haven't seen any of the NPCs that have been built up in the first bit of the game again. This alone would be enough for me not to recommend.With that in mind it is abundantly clear to me that the restricted fast travel is here not because "the world is interesting to traverse" but exactly the opposite, it is actually very empty, the majority of your gameplay is going to be sprinting around. Besides the lack of quests for the size of the map, the enemy variety is not great either. I can count on one hand the number of times I received a gear upgrade from a chest or a boss enemy - it's all money materials and consumables, with gear coming from vendor purchases. While I suppose this is sort of more realistic, realism doth not a fun game make (mileage may vary). On top of everything else, most of the materials were worthless for me because I got better armor from vendors faster than I got the materials to upgrade my old armor, and that was while being quite diligent to explore most of the map as I went. Inventory management is unnecessarily punishing with the weight limitations so another huge chunk of gameplay is constantly giving stuff to your pawns and coming back to town to store the materials and consumables you will likely never use.Combat carries this game, easily. The vocations and skills that they have (at least the ones I tried so far) were all really fun to use and exceptionally satisfying. Because of how satisfying it is, it took me way longer than it should have to realise how empty the game is, as running around killing the 30th pack of goblins is still somewhat fun when it's done so well. That said, f*ck me the combat is unbearable sometimes too. There is no dodge and no block for most vocations(classes) so the only way to dodge attacks is to run away, and for a lot of smaller enemies the animations are too fast to do that in time. If you do get hit, you get stunned for an eternity and will likely get hit by a followup or by another enemy (stunlocks are very possible, there are no i-frames whatsoever). Combat on the whole becomes very easy once you get a few skills unlocked and a proper set of armor and weapon for the first time, you are only ever in danger of dying to BS like stunlocks, one-shots, or your pawns abandoning you at that point. Might as well mention that pawns get stuck on everything, with the game refusing to teleport them to you until you're like 2km apart from eachother, and this happens multiple times per play session. They will often kill themselves by accident too.Mystic spearhand vocation has a skill that makes them invincible for a few seconds and is spammable. This is the kind of thing they need to give to account for no dodging and no blocking I suppose, but like why at that point. The magic archer gets their ultimate ability at the same time as the class itself gets unlocked (why?) and that ability can one-shot or almost one-shot the most powerful bosses you've seen in the game up until that point. The concept of breaking the game with strong builds is nothing new in RPGs but this game just breaks itself with its own skills with no effort required at all from the player.To be clear, if the game was exactly as is but had a finished story and more quests around the place, I would be singing its praises. But with how insultingly bad that part turned out to be, I was compelled to rant about just about everything that bothered me while playing, because it just feels like they put all their effort into the beginning of the game to fool players into thinking they were playing an AAA game that's worth the absurd price and microtransactions on top. It is not. And given my trust in CAPCOM has now fallen off a cliff they are probably going to add in the quests that should have been there to start off with as paid DLC too. It has the beginnings of an amazing game, and that just makes it feel so much worse.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stellar followup to Dragon's Dogma. They've improved the gameplay experience in every way while keeping its core identity fully intact. This is the most engrossing open world RPG experience I have played in some time, there's so much to do and see! I'm 12 hours in and haven't even managed the second step on the main quest. Something bad happened to an early quest NPC and he died, leaving me to find the capital on my own. This was awesome, because it took me on such unexpected twists and turns, venturing through unexplored territory and into the thick of danger. Bandit dens, goblin caves, saurian spawning pools, even a chimera nest (after one fraught attempt that ended in utter defeat, I left that one sleeping and got the heck out of there). I even found an ancient pedestal guarded by a wight! Stole his book and ran the heck out of there, couldn't hurt him at all yet. I haven't been this knocked out and impressed by an open world title since The Witcher III, or Skyrim before that. Really it feels more like Oblivion felt all those years ago, or maybe even Morrowind. Feels like the start of an amazing journey. I highly recommend it.Note: The DLC is unnecessary but you can buy it if you want. Don't think they're tuning the game to suck without it. They had the same kinds of DLC for Dragon's Dogma 1 at launch in 2012.

_childDocuments_.review: sonic colors: "ultimate" is a BAFFLING release.just for the sake of transparency, i'm not a fan of the writing style or shorter level structure of the original release, but things like this are a matter of opinion, and i decided to pick this up on a deep sale to double dip and see if it changed my mind. what i wasn't expecting was the worst version of this game.for starters, the materials on characters look super scuffed, and the newly done lighting is, while this is a matter of opinion, a lot less clear and consistent than the original, and to most, looks a lot worse. the cutscenes are AI upscaled, and have this awful wobbly effect for the entire duration. it feels like a fever dream to watch.the controls aren't as responsive, and there are LOADS of new bugs. i didn't run into anything utterly game breaking in my time, but launch pads that send you the wrong direction into a kill plane, dash panels that play sound effects but dont work, and sonic randomly completely halting are all pretty notable issues. the biggest offense of all though, in my opinion, is the rework of the double jump.in this release, the double hop triggers every time you hold down the jump button for anything longer than a VERY fast strike. i play platformers all of the time, but this caused me to misinput and double jump CONSTANTLY, and there's no option to toggle this off. most annoyingly, the double jump in the original release is a fun way to course correct and shift momentum mid jump, but, if you use the new feature of activating it while holding the button, you can no longer time it at the peak of the first jump's height, which is what the levels in the game are *built* around. due to this change and the fact that the double jump is *mostly* a corrective option in the original, the act of jumping itself feels sluggish, inconsistent, and just...bad. there are mods to fix the lighting, and i used those. but unless you want to get this game specifically for mod support, PLEASE do yourself a favor and just play the original in dolphin.it looks better, runs better, has FAR less bugs, and still has the movement the game was built upon. none of the new additions to this release are meaningful, and the whole package feels cheap and rushed. coupling this with the much much less consistent writing and characterization (which makes sense as an entry point for younger audiences on the original hardware considering that there were multiple more coherent adventures before this one, not so much here) this is the worst version (aside from the switch port of ultimate, which is this same release but with a lower framerate and more bugs) of an already not ideal game, and i just can't figure out who this release is for. the nicest thing i can say about it is that i didn't experience anything game breaking in my time with it, but i doubt i will stick around to finish this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Colors is a good game, I recommend it. Not through this though. The gross lighting, forced Tails save, graphics constantly flickering, stuttering, and the general lack of polish makes this hard to recommend. It's a pretty bad remaster of a good game, it's still fun, but the bar needs to be higher than "They didn't completely ruin it!". Play Sonic Colors DX instead. It's a fan project that gives the original HD textures and it runs on a custom build of Dolphin that fixes many of the issues with playing the game at 60fps. It's not perfect, but it runs and looks better than this.EDIT: I actually do recommend Colors Ultimate now, specifically because of Bluwolf's Project Re-Rainbow mod. It fixes most graphical and sound issues, and makes the game look closer to Hedgehog Engine 1 games like Generations and Unleashed. Get this game on the steepest sale you can though, because Sega deserves as little as possible for this awful remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: It's finally on Steam! Disappointing how a lot of the issues the game launched with are still here, but with mods, I'd still take this as the best way to play Colors. Colors was already a fun game, and the remaster's shortcomings doesn't take away from what the game is at it's core. Coming from someone who nearly 100%'d pre-patch Ultimate on an original Xbox One back in September 2021, I very much recommend this new Steam version lol (as long you get it on sale ofc). I got the digital deluxe version from GameBillet for 27 bucks, not bad.I'm gonna link the mods I personally use:Sonic Team Animation 2022 (Caio Natsune): I just really like the new splash screen from Frontiers lol. Improved Lighting (Micah33088): I chose this over PTKickass's Environmental Tweaks mod, mostly due to my doubt that Ultimate will ever look exactly like the Wii version. There are too many differences for it to look 1:1. So instead of trying to go half way with the original's aesthetic, I prefer Improved Lighting for doing it's own thing. I think it looks really nice, and fits with the new game's models n' such. Better Tails Materials (Taku): Tails lighting looks awful in-game and this fixes that. Better Sonic Textures & Materials (Wailful): Same thing can be said the for the blue rat himself. Sonic Model and Animation Fixes (SonicHyuga): By default, SCU Sonic looks pretty off. And some of his animations are broken, such as him not moving his pupils, and the infamous floating down in Starlight Carnival. This fixes that, and it even has him open his mouth. How fun! Tweaked Motion Blur (PTKIckass): Fixes that disgusting default boosting motion blur with one that looks a lot better. 3D Wisps in Capsules (Dario): I think it looks better than having those crunchy sprites. Aquarium Park Act 1 Fix (AllyJax): Fixes draw distance issues in that stage. I also swapped the B and X buttons (Xbox layout) to be more like the other Boost Style games. You can do this in the options menu.All in all, I recommend it. It's lazy as all hell, but its still fun. Have fun Coloring the Universe, at Dr. Eggman's Incredible Interstellar Amusement Park!

_childDocuments_.review: This remaster is an embarrassment and a sad reminder of how poorly Sonic has been treated in the last 5 years. The current state of the mod is already a massive upgrade and I highly recommend it to anyone who owns this game.Would I recommend Sonic Colours Ultimate? _childDocuments_.review: Currently at time of writing, Sonic Colors: Ultimate is very difficult to recommend. Is it a port of a good Sonic game? Yeah, it sure is. But hooo boy does this rerelease have it's problems.Let's start with the deal breakers and work our way down.- There's an obscene amount of bloom on every light source and object, including Sonic himself. Some areas this is passable, but for worlds such as Starlight Carnival, which is almost entirely neon lights on a pitch black background, it can render the game uncomfortable to play to near unplayable. Potentially able to be modded out.- There's an obscene amount of stutter during active gameplay. I don't think it's because of my machine, I've got a 3070 and it's held up incredibly well on other games that, believe it or not, aren't ports of Wii games. Heck, it even runs games on Dolphin like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ champ. So I can't tell if it's an optimization error or if the game is struggling under these very lenient conditions. But for a Sonic game, it can be absolutely unbearable to deal with.- The cutscenes are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ strange to me as someone who's played the Wii version before. They're clearly upscaled, but to a really weird and disgusting degree. Character edges shake like a mess and lips desync easily. It's honestly a little hard to watch Sonic and Tails interact in them, although most of Eggman's are okay.- The customizations seem to be a last minute duct tape addition with how aggressive they are with the currency needed to get them. It doesn't help that all of them can be boiled down to "Neat, but you'll never be able to tell you have them on in actual gameplay." Not a deal breaker, but certainly annoying.- Extra Lives are replaced with Tails Pickups (as an aside it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up that you pick up his disembodied head as a life) where if you fall down a pit then he'll help you back up, saving you your rings in exchange for a life. Neat for a Sonic game where 1 hit loses all of your rings, but the put down animation takes an eternity and a half.- The remixed music for a Sonic game is profoundly bad. I'm sorry if it's not awful to you, but when most of the remixes sound like a group of elementary school students copying the tracks with Kazoos, Vuvuzelas, and Otomatones. In comparison to the original tracks you're really scraping the bottom of the barrel calling these inferior versions "Remixes". It's this low on the list because unlike everything else listed here you can actually turn it off.The rest of the problems lie with the original too. It's oddly too floaty, it's hard to get into a flow state, the red rings are remarkably annoying, sometimes the game just breaks going from 2D to 3D or from a scripted sequence to a nonscripted sequence or vice versa. But at the very least I didn't have the displeasure of being blinded while playing it. If you do pick it up, try to find some sort of mod that cuts the bloom and fixes the stuttering issues. Otherwise you're in for a bad time instead of just a time.

_childDocuments_.review: Me personally, I do find this game to be SLIGHTLY overhated. Truthfully, yes. This game has many flaws. For starters (And what's most talked about)The bugs and glitches are here, and can be quite annoying, even after a few YEARS of this being released. There is still lag in the cosmetic menu (And multiple other areas at times) and a lot of the new additions in this game were incredible lazy. I will say, this is a very lazy port. And it was clearly rushed by the devs, without the proper time to replay it and fix the major issues being dealt here.Also, yes, the lighting is worse than the original. The bloom effect looks off, but I personally got used to the style it brought. Its not good, its not horrible looking either though. The cutscenes though, look like garbage. They just took the old cutscenes from Colors and upscaled them a bit, which was lazy as FRICK. They look off because of this. I legit skipped most of the cutscenes due to this issue.Also, the music is significantly worse than the original. Oh my GOSH, What did they do to this soundtrack? Some of these songs sound like they were composed by people that never composed songs before. The compositions can sound very disjointed, and downright awful sometimes.There are multiple other issues as well. The list goes on and on.With all of that being said, this is still Sonic Colors at its core. This game feels AMAZING at 60 fps, and the controls in this game were significantly enhanced to feel better than the original. Sonic is more floaty in this one, and his double jump is a MILLION times more accurate.The level design feels way better at 144fps than I thought it would. This plays beautifully (When it works right) and thats the big highlight for me. More people should acknowledge that about this game.This is worth the 12$ I paid for it. I beat it all in one sitting in 3 and a half hours, and had a good time with it. This was only because of the game play and level design that work WELL at 60 fps. And seeing Sonic Colors ported to modern hardware was a treat to behold, despite the major noticeable issues that downgrade this game by a LOT.Don't buy this at 40$. You could get MUCH better, at 40$, even is you like the original Sonic Colors. Get this on a deal. This is an alright experience, with HIGH highs for me, and some pretty LOW lows at times. This game has merit, despite its problems. That is all.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to give this game a "negative" review, but I really do feel guilty giving it a "positive" review. I wish there was a "mixed" opinion option.The reason I'm leaving a positive review is for the sake of its playability and accessibility; Sonic Colors: Ultimate is just *fine*. It works. If you're looking to buy this for your kid, then go ahead; they'll have a good time. If you're one who's particular for quality, then I have some things to say (ignore my playtime; I've experienced this game on Switch and EGS).SCU was clearly bogged-down by a messy development cycle and was likely rushed, but it works. You can play through the entire game, collect Red Rings, wear newly-added unlockables, etc. Its notorious (and sometimes exaggerated) GLITCHES (not to be confused with issues) from launch have mostly been patched, so what's the problem?Firstly, the art style has been completely overhauled; not because the developers wanted to try something new, but because they didn't know how to get the original Wii game's rendering functioning on a modern hardware (at least, that's my understanding of the situation). You can prefer the new style to the old, but for Tropical Resort, the "Color" in Sonic Colors, is very much toned down. It's a bit of a shame, but not a deal-breaker.The newly remixed songs are a hit and miss. Planet Wisp's beautiful, tone-setting tune is now cranked up to 10, and sounds more like a rave that completely misses the point of the original song. If you're familiar with this game's soundtrack, feel free to keep the new music on, but if you're looking for the original experience, there's a DLC for that (laugh track except I'm serious).As for attention to detail - Sonic's blinking animation feels stilted. The newly-added menus are unreasonably laggy. The A.I. upscaled cutscenes are very poorly considered, and Sonic's walk-cycle on the world map doesn't play at the proper speed. These are all things that can be overlooked, but when there's so many issues, it starts to hurt this game's identity. Sonic Colors was cherished despite being a simpler entry to the series, and this "remaster" doesn't prove to be definitive. It's so sad that I beat the original game on emulator, and when the remaster came out, it was the laughing stock of gaming media. SEGA really hasn't learned their lesson.If you're looking to play Sonic Colors exactly how you remember it, I'd recommend emulation over this any day. If you're like me and enjoy collecting achievements and unlockables, and can tolerate occasional oddities, then this is just "okay". It's fine. It'll pad your Steam collection. I refuse to pay full price for this, but on sale with achievements, I bit the bullet.I got Sonic Colors: Ultimate to play it on Steam Deck. Right away, I want to warn that despite it's "Verified" status, it performs horrendously. You'll be getting 60fps @ 1080p and 720p, broken by immense, random stutters. This isn't the case on PC, so I'm unsure what's causing the problem. If you're looking to play SCU on your Steam Deck, wait until a solution is found.TL;DRPros:-Accessible if you're afraid of emulation-Unlockables-Achievements-Metal races can be challengingCons:-Original art style is lost-New music is a hit/miss-Tons of visual issues that weren't present in the original-Cutscenes look messy-Performs terribly on Steam Deck despite Verified status

Just barely after a minute of playing, I already encountered a bug that launched me literally backwards in the stage, dropping me to my death, after doing the very simple action of just switching a grind rail. And my playthrough was capped off with the game crashing mid-credits, barely even three minutes into it. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, at least in my experience, the remaster in it's current state is nowhere near as bad as many people try to say. I have encountered some minor bugs here and there, but it's overall performing much better for me than I had been lead to believe it would. There are also some things that are worse about it compared to the original Wii version, but not enough to the point that I would outright just say to play that version instead. In fact, quite the opposite. I feel like overall, the benefits of playing Ultimate outweigh the negatives. The controls are generally very nice feeling as well, and I've not experienced any significant audio issues aside from the game being a bit too loud when I started it up for the first time.Others have reported issues such as Mono Audio, Long Loading Times, etc. However, I have not experienced these issues. A friend of mine also showed me the game working really well on his Steam Deck.The inclusion of Denuvo on release is quite puzzling here. Pirate versions of the game have been available for quite some time now, so I'm not really quite sure what it is they're intending to accomplish by including it in this release. It's hard to predict if it will ever be removed either, as Mania did eventually get an update removing it but other Sonic games with it on Steam so far have not. However, I can report that Denuvo does not appear to be messing with performance much if at all. I've had some small stutters during gameplay, but it's hard to say for sure whether this is the game itself or Denuvo, and it's a minor enough issue as to hardly even be an inconvenience.The new content compared to the original release on Wii isn't huge in scope, but it is neat for what it is. Firstly, there's an entirely new Wisp which first appeared in Team Sonic Racing: The Jade Ghost. It allows you to travel through walls by grabbing onto grapple points, and gives you a brief period of flying. Collecting some of the Red Star Rings is tied to using this, so old Wii guides on locating these will be a bit outdated.There's also a new move in Sonic's moveset: The Sweet Spot Attack. When the homing reticle first appears on a target, there's a brief window of time visualized by a green circle in which you can do a sort of perfect homing attack. Doing this successfully plays a sound and gives Sonic's homing trail a rainbow aesthetic, and will reward you with a little bit of boost for your meter. It's very fun and satisfying to pull off chains of this.There's also the Tails Assist System, which can rescue Sonic from bottomless pits and the like and restore him to nearby stable ground. I opted to mod this out in favor of the original lives system, so I don't have much to comment on it, but my understanding of it is that it basically functions as infinite lives.The only other outright gameplay change I'm aware of is the addition of the new rival races against Metal Sonic. These are unlocked by getting enough Red Star Rings, and are basically just normal runs through stages, except under the time limit of reaching the goal ring before Metal Sonic.There's also a number of new cosmetic changes you can make to Sonic. You can unlock alternative looks for his gloves, shoes, boost, and even give him an aura. Aside from the ones unlocked from the start, these are unlocked via collecting Park Tokens in the stages and spending them on the cosmetics. The only exception is the Dark Aura and the Dark Boost, which are unlocked by beating the Metal Sonic races.Overall, while the remaster is a little bit buggy and has some visuals at times that are a bit worse than the original game due to too much bloom or etc. It's not as bad as people say, has some fun and generally harmless new additions compared to the original game, and appears to have had its more egregious issues patched out since it first came to PC. This will likely vary from hardware to hardware, but overall I've been having a lot more fun with it than I have frustration, and I have encountered nothing game breaking, and some of the issues that do exist can be fixed with mods.If you're interested in playing Sonic Colors, my personal opinion on the matter is that this is worth grabbing. Do expect there to be some bugs and glitches from time to time, and you might want to look into the modding scene if you have some nitpicks with certain details like the missing lives system and the overuse of bloom, but overall it's nowhere near as bad as some people would have you believe.

_childDocuments_.review: Its been a while since I played this, but I wanted to review now, because I got reminded of it and it really stings...This game is much MUCH worse than the original Wii version of Colors... It somehow made a lot of things worse.The gameplay itself and how the movement of sonic feels, is fine for the most part, but all the wisps somehow don't play right anymore. Their physics have been broken or something, dunno. Anyway onto everything I encountered while playing trying to get 100%!The sound doesn't let you change the voices in cutscenes individually. In general, none of the sound options really make sense, the eggman who speaks on the planet map is extremely loud, while everything else will be very quiet. But in the cutscenes the voices will be way too quiet instead using the same settings. Very weird.Wisps physics got broken.For example the drillwisp always had a radius you had to follow when turning, but in this game, you simply instantly turn to whichever direction you hold your stick. Feels very clunky, even though its easier. Not fun though, since it defeats the purpose of this wisp.The frenzy wisp also controls incredibly bad. I mean it never was meant to be simple and it definitely is supposed to be a bit clunky, but there is a part in which you need to time your jumps while chomping through blocks to get a red ring, but while it chomps through the blocks he grows in size and always has a little stopanimation to show him grow. You can't instantly jump after that, which will make you fail this jump over and over and over again. I had to restart like 30 times, just to get it once. Super annoying.The spike wisp works, but somehow lets you break the game completely. There are many moments in which you'll get to places you weren't supposed to get to. To be fair, that also was possible in the original, like climbing up invisible walls and stuff, but this game has even MORE of it... HOW? Isn't it supposed to get better if you call your game "ultimate"?(So yeah, there are invisible walls.. lots of em)I said Sonics movement is fine "for the most part" well, there is indeed one problem. If you kept running to the right and turn around, wanting to go to the left, you already start moving left and boost, you will still boost to the right, as the character still hasn't fully turned around. VERY annoying if you're used to how quickly it worked before and in other boost games.The Quick-Side-Step was kept on the controlstick instead of letting you put it on the shoulderbuttons. There is no point in having that on a system other than the Wii...It also has other problems with the buttonconfig, like how the drift is the same button as the boost and depending on where you are, you do one or the other. This could also easily be different buttons, like the seocnd set of shoulerbuttons... its what made unleasheds daystages feel so great, being able to drift and boost at the same time!Also the Homing Attack and Double Jump are on the same button! This makes no sense whatsoever, since you constantly run into the problem of wanting to doublejump, while sonic targets something on the very other side of the screen behind a wall, letting you Homing Attack the wall and fall to your death. Great!...In addition to invisible walls, you also constantly get blocked of from the rest of the level you already ran past... using more invisible walls! You have a game that wants you to collect all the red rings, but you punish your players constantly by blocking off a path, by just moving past it by 3 steps? Very annoying. Leave it open, what purpose does that even serve?If you try to get all S ranks, you want to farm points, as being fast won't give you an S rank in this game, you need to have enough points. However, if you're too slow, you can't get an S rank anymore and there is no timer showing at which point that'll be the case. Its different for every level too! So you'll randomly get an "Time-Out" at the edge of your screen, this too is very frustrating, because you don't even have fun farming points, but need to do it and if you do it, you still get punished.. argh.Automated passages don't work anymore... This game has lots of bumpers and loopings, usually Sonic runs through them elegantly, in this game however, Sonic does not... he gets thrown around by the boostpads as if they were bumpers and just hits his head in the loops without running them most of the time. Also some bumpers will sometimes randomly throw you the wrong way into the void. FUN!Even the camera doesn't always work correctly. In asteroid coaster there are parts in the coaster with the cam being zoomed in too much and the game running at what feels like 10 fps for no reason. The Wii never had this problem before.Some bosses are bugged aswell, the most annoying one being the boss in the water. If you activate a drillwisp, that boss will teleport away from you all the time, making you unable to hit him at all. I read that it only works correctly if you force the game in 30fps, anything higher will make him teleport and almost impossible to hit with the drill, which is required for an achievement and an S rank. (I reset like 50 times for this to hope he just flies into me on its own)And lastly... sometimes you just get hit without reason. You jump, you're in your spinattack, use it to jump on an enemy to destroy them like any other... aaaand you get hit. Sometimes it just doesn't work. If you want to make sure, homing attack onto everything, because otherwise the game sometimes just doesn't want to work. Especially annoying if you're trying to get your S-ranks.And thats it! Incredible how much bad stuff I've encountered... and almost none of these problems existed in the original on the Wii! I don't understand how you can make an "ultimate" port this badly.... Can't recommend...

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, shoddy remaster. If you don't mind a few glitches and issues, then you'll probably enjoy this port, since it does have cool new features and upgrades over the original. If you can't handle the glitches, then just emulate the original on Dolphin. Keep in mind that some of the more serious glitches from the original release of this remaster, such as the seizure glitches, have been patched out, so it is better than before. Still not perfect, but a solid port nonetheless. Runs well and looks good, for the most part. It appears that some of the cutscenes were AI upscaled, which works to mixed results, whilst other scenes were actually given higher resolutions, which look great. The new remixed soundtrack is also pretty good, and offers a new experience over the original. The game runs at a stable 60 fps, which is very nice, but it does stutter every now and then. The loading times are good too.Concerning the game itself, it's fun as hell. Not the best Sonic game, but it's certainly one of the best. Good level design and controls, good story and soundtrack, and good visuals for a Wii game. Between the original and this remaster, it is the 3D Sonic game I've beaten the most times. This game is similar to Sonic Forces in it's level design, but I don't believe that's a bad thing, since I love both of these games. If you've never played Sonic Colours before, I would implore you to give it a shot. 8/10 for the original game, 7/10 for this remaster. Also, check out the DS version too. It's a separate game, and it's also great!

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'd like to say I am very happy that this is now on Steam. This game was the sole reason I had the Epic Games Store installed on my computer, and now that this is on Steam I am able to uninstall that. Thanks Sega.Anyway, the game is good. Sonic Colors was my first 3D Sonic game and it's always held a soft spot in my mind. I 100%'d this game twice on Epic, and countless times back on the Wii. It's fun, especially if you like Sonic games. It's also just a solid platformer in general. The base game is solid and worth giving a shot.As for the remaster itself. I am not especially impressed. There are several changes to the game compared to the original release that are very questionable. First of all, the graphics. The game is very bright. The bloom has been turned up to 11, which I believe is how they chose to hide certain unpolished graphics. Secondly, the music. Every theme in the game has a remix (except Game Land I believe?). These remixes are toggleable, however the Planet Wisp remixes are locked behind a pay wall. This is a horrid choice. Very cash grabby. They are decent remixes though, the new soundtrack is worth a listen. Thirdly, there are a couple gameplay changes such as the Tails save. Lives have been removed and in their place is the Tails save. If you fall down a pit Tails will save you and put you back on the stage, simple as that. It's a little wonky and he holds on to you for longer than necessary, but it's overall fine.Lot's of people do not recommend this remaster. There are several reasons for this. The initial launch was absolutely horrible. Several issues on other platforms caused public opinion to sour for Sonic Colors as a whole. The PC version, for me, has always been fairly stable aside from some audio issues. I recommend this solely because it is the only proper way to play Sonic Colors on PC. Wait for a sale though, I don't think it's worth the price they ask for. If you have the ability, play the Wii release on Dolphin. Other than the remaster changes, it is the superior way to play Sonic Colors.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the original Wii game when it first came out, I didn't really need much to be happy. Yet, I'm not happy.Not only is this buggier than the Wii version, the extra content and changes feel unnecessary. The new wisp in particular was very poorly implemented, and was clearly not well thought out. There were several times I got myself stuck out of bounds using it, and had to restart the level to get myself out. Planet Wisp had this weird bug where half the skybox simply wouldn't load in sometimes. I had this happen twice in my 17 hours of playtime (in which time I 100%ed the game, loading that area several times. It makes me wonder how this didn't get caught in testing)The cosmetics, while easy to ignore and not problematic for gameplay, didn't add anything of value to the experience for me. The new music remixes, while not nearly as bad as I feared they would be, still don't compare to the original 2010 soundtrack. But this isn't an issue since the original soundtrack can be toggled from the options menu.The core gameplay is about as good as it is in the original Wii version. Not as good as I remember, though I was a child back then. But it's faithful to the original. (minus the Jade Wisp being awkwardly added into random levels with a dozen rings in a formerly out-of-bounds area)If you've been SUPER EAGER to play Sonic Colours of all things and haven't yet, maybe give this a shot. But for anyone who played the original, I say if you still have a working Wii or Wii U on hand, and a copy of the game for the Wii, just play that. _childDocuments_.review: Sonic Colors was really good in my memories but replaying it made me realise it wasn't THAT good. It's not a bad game in itself though, but it's supposed to be a 3D Sonic game. There's way too much 2D moments in the game, with entire 2D levels. I would play the game on the DS if i wanted that. I'm not against it from time to time in a 3D game, but that's too much. We have levels beginning with 15 seconds of 3D gameplay, then the rest is 2D. Even on locations like Starlight Carnival where there's a little more 3D, the game just lets you run in a straight line just to dodge 2 robots shooting lasers and then shows you big spaceships for 30 seconds while you just continue to run without even seeing Sonic. I wanted to have real 3D levels, but all i had were 2 lasers, some rails from time to time (the coasters on Asteroid Coaster are the same as rails with coasters skins), 10 seconds of drift every world, and bad side steps sequences (using the joystick above that.). There's 7 bosses, and abive the 6 normal bosses (not counting the final boss), 3 were reskins of the previous bosses, and 2 contained 3D parts wich are just running in a straight line dodging machine guns that shoots in a straight line.Then you have Game Land levels wich are just useless levels. Before that you had the music that helped appreciating the game, but Game Land levels are just 2D uninspired levels (with sometimes 5 seconds of running in a straight line in 3D) that feels like a 10 year old would create these on Super Mario Maker. If it was still not enough, you need to collect the 180 red rings, just to unlock those 21 bad levels wich you need to complete to have the Chaos Emeralds.This """Ultimate""" edition is a missed opportunity to make the original game better. Instead, we have freezes, crashes, graphical glitches, and Sega thinking removing instruments from the original music will make good remixes.Sega added some things but they are kinda useless and there to give some impression like "look, we added some things":-Sonic's personalisation with his gloves, shoes, aura and profile icons (wich are for most of them on Google Images since at least 10 years) that doesn't even give some special effects.-Metal Sonic races that would be a great addition if only it was to replace the way Game Land gives you Chaos Emeralds, here it's just the same level but with a time limit, the same could be done by just having a time limit.Just play the Wii version if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: Just place in a few mods to polish up the visuals and BADDABING BADDABOOM, you get what I consider one of the best Sonic games to ever exist. Dare I say, the best Boost game in terms of gameplay. It offers high-speeds, exploration, and lotta fun in going for full completion. The Wisps are some of the best power-ups in the franchise and encourages exploring the levels for Red Rings, Tails Saves, Tokens, and other goodies. While I know the more child-oriented writing isn't for everyone, I really enjoy the plot of the game. A simple Sonic and Tails VS Dr. Eggman adventure that goes for the classic tale of rescuing critters from being used as batteries for an evil scheme. Only this time, you're saving intergalactic aliens instead of woodland animals. I really like the Rival Race with Metal Sonic, and while more could've been done with the concept, it's good to see the Blue Blur racing against his greatest rival yet again. The Jade Wisp is also fun to use in exploring new level layouts exclusive to Ultimate. All in all, Colors remains one of the greatest Sonic games to ever exist. Just like Sonic...I'M GONNA REACH FOR THE STARS!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Graphical effects and camera angles gave me motion sickness and eye strain. The bloom is turned up so ridiculously high that the game looks smothered in vaseline. Performance is also odd, going from 60 to dropped frames for small instances. As far as boost Sonic games go it has better control in 2D sections (where ST usually struggles in their modern games) but the 3D sections are overly sensitive when it comes to turning. Sonic will turn almost 90 degrees with a small tilt of the stick. Level design has some fun mini-puzzles designed around the Wisp abilities, but the game is visually so busy and un-clear that its hard to even play, on top of it's sensitive turning. Stories also painfully boring and childish but you can skip it.Overall a decent game hindered by awful decisions when it came to this port job. Instead of overthinking their graphical ideas they should've just put that focus where it mattered, especially seeing how buggy the game was on all platforms for so long. No longer stuck on EG$ but it honestly could've stayed on there.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Colours Ultimate is after 1.5 years out on Steam, and while they did fix most of the game breaking, or epilepsy-inducing bugs, this remaster still has lots of issues, but are these issues a dealbreaker, or can you still enjoy the game that people used to call one of the better Sonic games?First, let's talk about the stuff "Ultimate" stands for.The most obvious things are the visuals, higher poly models, UI changes that make this game look like a fan game, and a blinding amount of bloom that makes Discord light mode look like a saint. Bloom in this game is obnoxious. Instead of just implementing better lighting and shadows, Colours Ultimate instead aims to illuminate every single object in the room, even Sonic glows. It really bothers me how the entire color palette looks like it's washed out. Very few levels look better, most of the "Colours" fade away.Whenever you enter a cutscene, you really see the difference the bloom makes, because the cutscenes weren't remade. They reuse the old ones from the Wii, which are lower poly, but much more colorful. It's kind of jarring to see how unreasonably bright the remaster is.Additionally, you can't even turn off the bloom. You can't even change your graphics settings, except your game's resolution and if Vsync should be on or off. The PC port is the definition of bare bones, so if your game doesn't run well, then you only have 2 options 'til you can give up or refund it.However, the biggest issues were the glitches. Faulty collision detection, visual bugs, like Sonic hovering while doing his little start animation, or the game stuttering whenever you collect a 1-up. Luckily, most other glitches were fixed, but there are still many left, and I doubt they care about them.All this could've been prevented if they hadn't implemented additional content that you can barely see, or even play.They added the Jade wisp from Team Sonic Racing to the game. Unsurprisingly, the game wasn't made with the Jade wisp in mind, so it hardly works, gets you soft locked, or simply feels out of place.Cosmetics were also added. They usually change Sonic's aura, gloves or shoe color. Unfortunately, it doesn't matter, because Sonic is most of the time so tiny on the screen, that you cannot see your new skins.Overall, the Ultimate part of this game is a joke, and if they hadn't spent so much time on cosmetics and implementing an out-of-place Wisp, then they would've had plenty of workforce to address the most basic of issues.SEGA didn't remake the game for no reason, though. Maybe the essence of the game still reigns supreme?Sonic Colours' theming is wonderful. It's one of the last times we had interesting Sonic themes that weren't blatant nostalgia pandering for the 5th time. Tropical Resort, Planet Wisp, Aquarium Park are all places that really look nice. They still have somewhat basic themes, but they make them look astonishing and memorable. Whenever you run past a section, you actually feel like you're going on a tourist trip to see the different places and sights, which is amazing.The level design on the other hand is pretty messy. Padding is Sonic Colours' cornerstone. Each world has 6 levels and 1 boss, but there are only 4 unique bosses, and 2  or 3 levels that actually feel fleshed out. Most of the other ones are mandatory challenge levels that keep the game slow and uninteresting. Most levels heavily rely on their stop & go aspects, meaning you have 5 seconds of spectacle and 1 minute of mindlessly jumping from A to B or simply waiting. You will wait a lot in this game. Lasers that slowly circle around when you keep standing on a switch, platforms that slowly move upwards when you stand on a switch, auto-scrolling levels that let you wait around for way too long. They treat waiting as their unique gimmick, to the point that my mate and I acted hype whenever we had to wait for 5 seconds to go past a laser.The issue is that boost levels go through areas really quickly, but it's not better to force the player to wait or go past the same landmarks multiple times in the same world, as if you aren't progressing. The challenge levels to pad out time are either the shortest levels in the entire game, or the lengthiest. As an example, I had to run around a ring for 2 minutes and kill enemies. Most of the level design elements in these levels look like they were made in some kind of "Sonic Maker" mod.Wisps too are not well implemented. I get the idea of freeing Wisps the more you progress, and getting them in older levels to try and find new ways to save time, but if I want to grind a level then I'll just do it. I don't want to be restricted 'til I get another Wisp.Writing-wise, this game is god awful. It's the Dora the Explorer of Sonic games. I can't even see a kid finding half of the stuff in this game funny or clever. I played Murder of Sonic before that, and the quality difference gives me whiplash.Sonic Colours Ultimate isn't a great remaster, and after the consensus shifted over the last few years, it's a mediocre game at best. Sonic Colours DS still reigns supreme, but we will probably never see a remaster of the supposed lesser version. 6/10.
