_childDocuments_.review: To be clear, this is NOT a review for Sonic Colors, simply a review of the Ultimate Port, I very much like Sonic Colors and think its a great game. With that out of the way, lets start off with the good. Having easy access to this game on modern platforms is awesome. Being able to rebind the controls to my liking was also very useful and a nice in game addition. The increased frame rate on PC is spectacular, seeing this game in 144 FPS makes it look a whole lot better, the higher resolution is a bit more of a double edged sword however, as for most of the time it looks super great, however with this newfound clarity, some visual trickery/low detail backgrounds become a lot more apparent now you can see everything so clearly. Also with this game being on PC, modding capability is applied much more to it. However, the huge caveat to all of these up sides is that literally all of them apply to emulating the game. Higher resolution, Higher FPS, Rebindable controls, Modding, all viable with "free" emulators. But ofcourse, those additions are not the only things added to this "REMASTER", unfortunately as I will soon explain, all the additions are, to put it lightly, ♥♥♥♥. The new Menus replacing the old ones look atrocious and the newly created Menus look even worse! The newly implemented UI is just terrible, it looks cheap and lacks any style. The new visuals, being the lighting overhaul is abhorrent its as if Sonic is made of some Neon material or something, it just looks bad. In terms of gameplay additions, the new "Metal Sonic races" are a joke, the previously mentioned UI and newly added Metal Sonic prompts look like a poorly made mod, and the actual race itself is just replaying the level with a flying static model chasing after you. The cosmetics are a complete joke, ridiculously ugly recolours of gloves/shoes/boost aura, why not add some actual costumes or model swaps instead of these super gross looking recolors. The life system has been replaced with this rather strange Tails save mechanic, which is basically just lives, but for pits, and if you die by anyway thats not a pit, you just go to the checkpoint as normal, its stupid and unnecessary and when Tails respawns you, he holds onto you for way to long. They also added in random Tails voice lines telling you about upcoming danger for literally no reason, like Sonic Colors is not known as a hard game, we didnt need these random hand holding additions. The newly added "Ghost Wisp" is just a Hover Wisp clone, but can take you to completely out of place looking and poorly designed "hidden areas" that totally stand out and take you out of the level, again it feels like a low tier mod somebody put into the game. The cutscenes for some god forsaken reason have had this absolutely awful upscaling done to them that makes Sonic look like some blob half the time, the cutscenes are literally in-engine, just either play them unrendered or re render them??? Its truly bizarre. The new music remixes are all OK, but a lot worse than the originals, thankfully there is now an option to switch the music back to the original tracks, which I dont believe was in the game at launch. I did not experience any real glitches, although the game does not like being tabbed out of in true fullscreen, and some particle effects were a bit buggy, mainly some confetti in Tropical Resort and the score breaking apart in the results screen. Overall, it would have been better if they just didnt add anything to begin with, and just straight ported the game, not one of the additions actually adds anything and simply makes the port look tacky. With that said however, none of the problems are "game-breaking" or ruin the experience to that much of a degree, they just make the game look worse for the most part.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, look at that. After almost two years, Colors Ultimate finally made it to Steam.SEGA, no more Epic exclusives if you please. We no like those.Now, while I am giving this game a thumbs-up because I enjoyed playing it, I have to say that this is not the most ideal remaster for a 2010 title. Visual changes are a hit or miss depending on which stages you're talking about, but I (mostly) dig the remastered soundtrack and had a decent time playing through many of the stages, especially Starlight Carnival and Planet Wisp.Performance-wise, no issues for me...except for the slight freeze that occurred whenever I picked up a Tails Save, but that can probably be attributed to me playing the game in 144 FPS. Apart from that, it's pretty much the same game as on consoles and Epic, and it ran fine for me.However, the best option to play Sonic Colors remains with either using the Dolphin emulator with upgrades, or a Nintendo Wii with a physical copy of the game. If you cannot use either method, then Colors Ultimate is an acceptable alternative, be it on console or PC.I think the one thing that's going to keep many players from reverting back to the original Sonic Colors is the upgraded homing attack in Ultimate. When timed right, you get boost gauge with each attack. This did not exist originally, and most people who play this game love to be understandably boost-happy so there you go.To summarize: if you have Colors for Wii and/or Dolphin, stick to that. If not, then go ahead and try Colors Ultimate. It's pretty much the game as you remember it, with the additions being barely meaningful.

_childDocuments_.review: When it first came out, Sonic Colors was seen as a beacon of hope as a return of the Sonic franchise. No werehog, no bad motion controls, no kissing a human and everything else bad sonic reviewers of the 2010s have already mentioned. Heck, even mentioning how bad that era of sonic critique was is pretty cliche at this point. Now over a decade later, a remaster has come out and it looked like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. But that’s okay, because sonic fans grew up and are now capable enough of fixing everything Sonic Team screwed up on. Truly, there’s never been a better time to be a sonic fan than right now. But how does the actual game stack up in retrospect? Funnily enough, a gradual shift has occurred within the reception of certain sonic games. Sonic Unleashed used to be seen as a mediocre entry with the werehog stages dragging down what would otherwise be a pretty good game, but nowadays it's universally beloved among Sonic fans. The inverse has occurred with Sonic Colors where its flaws seem to be more visible in the eyes of many with the abundance of 2D sections and the bloated 6 act structure of every level. Although 6 acts does make it a tad weird as some of it can feel stretched, knowing that it's just chopped up pieces of an act 2 helps knowing that each act is more of an exploration of the different gimmicks of the level with the accompanying wisps that can be used. In this regard, I think Sonic Colors level design is actually brilliant in how much variety it has and how it accompanies the player in exploring its different aspects. In addition to its accommodating level design, sonic control really well in this iteration with the double jump coming in clutch for a lot of the platforming but also the fact its abundance in 2D sections creates less room for error. People hark on said 2D sections but honestly it really isn’t that bad as they both maintain the challenge and the spectacle I expect from my sonic game. The appeal of this game though, the wisps, is what really brings these strong design elements together. I love that Sonic took a page from Mario’s book in getting different power-ups that can help explore these new terrains. Each of the new wisps are surprisingly unique and well-integrated without ever feeling forced onto you as a lot of stages don’t even really rely on using the wisps. This is essentially how I want a sonic game’s gimmick to be incorporated into the game.With the Re-Rainbow Mod, this game looks outstanding. I’m still going to give a negative rating overall for this game because the base game is honestly just a downgrade of the original, but the folks working on the mod really deserve me giving credit to them as every stage is even more visually beautiful with the restoration of its original colors and lighting brought to HD. With a game with such gorgeous level themes being that of different planets, Sonic Colors is stunning on another level with the Re-Rainbow mod. It also makes the wisp powers pop out more with the cool spectacle they are with better textures in a better looking environment. Sonic Colors Ultimate with the Project Re-Rainbow mod might be the best looking 3D sonic game in my humble opinion so far.So should you drop the cash to buy Sonic Colors Ultimate now that there’s a mod that fixes everything? It depends. Feels wrong to essentially reward Sega for the work modders did, but ultimately Sonic Colors was their game that they originally developed. If you’ve never played Sonic Colors, then you might as well jump in here and install the mod to witness one of the best 3D sonic games that isn’t Sonic Generations. If you have played the original game, then only get this if you really want to see what the game should look like in HD if you don’t mind giving that money to Sega’s half-assed attempt at it. Either way, I had a good time at the very least with replaying the game this way.

It's one of the more acclaimed Sonic titles and for good reason, the original had colourful and creative environments, good gameplay that carried on the Boost stages of Unleashed, and a more simpler, light-hearted title. The stigma the game has rightfully garnered is expired as Blind Squirrel have provided several patches throughout 2021, which are all included in this version. The game runs very smoothly, at a nice 60fps. The controls feel good, and overall is a pleasant experience. The bugs that were originally present have all been either managed to be fixed entirely or are minor to where it wont hinder your experience. The main bugs present in this version are minor graphical glitches with pop-in of objects and geometry, however they are always placed far away to where it doesn't break immersion. There are also very, very rare frame dips, but after my first session, I never ran into such dips again and any crashes are gone. This is a very stable version and very enjoyable.If i was to provide any advice, I'd say wait for a sale. The port is good, and while in a perfect world it would be better, Ultimate is a very fine and acceptable way to play one of Sonic's most brightest and charming adventures. _childDocuments_.review: I heard from a few people that the previous patches improved Colors Ultimate a fair bit, but I was still pretty skeptical and not super willing to part with $40 to find out. Fortunately, the recent sale has dropped it down to about $12 and I can say the game, while not perfect, is much better and more stable than at launch. It's faster to load, runs at 60 FPS, and feels better than I remembered! The Jade Ghost Wisp is also less shoehorned in than I expected and adds new sections of level design, both to increase replay value, and skip over some parts of slower-paced levels. I can honestly say I had a good time!Most of my complaints were either nitpicks, like sound effects not consistently playing for some things or Starlight Carnival's color palette looking duller than it used to. The only major complaints I have with Colors Ultimate partially stem from issues I had with the original release not being fixed, such as the Double Jump and Homing Attack being on the same button, which led to some collectibles being a pain. The Homing Attack ALWAYS takes priority over the Double Jump, which gets frustrating at times, and I was really hoping there would be an option to separate the two, but no such luck. Another issue I have is that they didn't fix the audio issue from the base game with Eggman's PA Announcements. Despite Colors having my least favorite Sonic script (until we got Lost World), the PA Announcements were the one thing I could always count on for a good laugh, but they're just as hard to hear as they were before unless you stand still and do nothing in certain spots, but who the heck wants to do that in an action game, much less a Sonic game? That shouldn't be a thing you have to do.The only other complaint I have, and it's also true of the original release, is the scoring system in Colors is DUMB. Man alive, as someone who struggles to find any sense of purpose or use for score in 99% of the video games I have played, this game did NOT do anything to change my stance on it. I say this only because I actually put effort into getting all the S Ranks in Asteroid Coaster, which is my favorite zone from this game, and a few other specific levels from different locales.The best way to rack up points in most of these levels I've attempted seems to be to spam Wisps and stay in their forms (excluding the one-and-done Wisps like Rocket and Laser) for as long as possible without going over the time limit. This means you're hovering near the goal ring a decent amount of the time either sitting around doing nothing or going in circles with the Drill Wisp. If a level or boss has a quick step gimmick in it, you're spamming left, right, left, right, left, right, left, right over and over and over again and it looks so weird and unnatural. You HAVE to do it, too, if you want S Ranks on the Frigate bosses and the Final Boss, and man does it take you out of the fight something fierce. This is not a competent way of handling things, it doesn't feel good or look good. Just... no. Ignore score, you get nothing out of getting all the S Ranks besides some achievements. It's not needed, useful, or fun.Honestly, for the price it's at now, I think it's a worthwhile experience. I think enough has been improved that I'm willing to stick with this over the original release, though I admit I didn't have much attachment to the game before my recent playthrough, which I had a shockingly good time with compared to when I played the Wii release at launch! I think Colors holds up better than I remembered. It's not clearing any of my favorites, but it's still a mostly fun time! I'd call it an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Colors; I had gone into this game expecting to be disappointed after hearing lots of negative things about it. Instead what I found was a very interesting take on modern Sonic. One I enjoyed greatly for the most part.Given time the release on Steam seems heavily patched and most of the bugs (not ALL mind) seem to be patched out. I only ran into a really bad bug once that caused sonic to clip through the map in an odd slope and fall, setting me back to my checkpoint... but I could never replicate it so I guess this was a fluke.Gameplay wise the game shines in my opinion. Your sense of speed is definitely there and favors memorizing the levels to max out the rank and collectibles. Atop this though you have some really innovative design choices in the aliens which can give Sonic a cool powerup. These can be used in a variety of ways but I enjoyed most of them a lot. Some really cool ideas here that ALSO work quite well in the level design department. Big thumbs up.I gotta make a comment about music: You get the original soundtrack here as well as the remixed soundtrack. Both are nice but most will probably dig the remixed variant more overall-- it definitely has more polish. The vast bulk of music here really fits the series and enhances the levels in a neat way. I found myself really resonating with a lot of the tracks and it brought back some memories of classic sonic at times.The weakest point here has to be the story but I imagine this won't really be the attraction for any but the most diehard sonic fans. It is very servicable even if a bit more on the silly side. The overtly goofy moment did have me grinning though, nothing is exactly out of place. Characters act as you expect them to which can only be a good thing. Just don't expect any real plot twists or anything this time around.The only overt complain I really have is more of a personal gripe about maxing out certain missions. Most missions are okay and it is more of a memorization game with the level layout and all that, providing a good challenge... However a few can be all over the place, or have such a specific route of success that they can get frustrating countless restarts later-- but this isn't exclusive to this game and I found Sonic Adventure a lot more cruel in this regard and I enjoyed that game a lot as well.Overall if you're a Sonic fan I highly recommend this one and it wouldn't even be bad as a starting point for some. Just bear in mind it isn't like the classics and does take a few liberties with the formula... But I personally see this as a good thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Colours. With a 'U'.The original brought the franchise back to its roots, despite being a Nintendo exclusive. But then that changed 10 years later when it became available for modern gen consoles and PC, in the form of Sonic Colours Ultimate. I find Colours decent, but not one of my favourite Sonic games, mainly for how levels are split into multiple acts, with half of them being "small puzzle acts", just to pad out the game length. The Wisps are a neat and cool game mechanic that changes how you progress through the levels, with each Wisp giving you different abilities. Personally, I prefer Ultimate over the original. It looks cleaner with higher resolution textures and lighting, and the majority of the remixed soundtrack knocks it out of the park. Being able to play it at 60fps is also a neat bonus. Ultimate added numerous things; a new Wisp, which also tweaked certain levels to include the new add-on Wisp, and is pretty cool to use. Rival Rush, where you race against Metal Sonic in certain stages. A cool idea which does add replayability, however I do wish it was added to other levels, instead of a grand total of 6. Tails Save was added to help new players get back after falling off the level, which replaces the lives; an outdated system that NOBODY asked to get rid of. Let newbies play without having the game hold their hand, especially when the game isn't even that hard. Yes it had a bit of a rough launch with numerous bugs and issues, but majority of them have been fixed, further improving the experience. If you never got to play Sonic Colours in 2011, then I would recommend Ultimate as it is now more accessible. If you have played Sonic Colours before, then I'll still recommend Ultimate, but I totally understand if you rather play the original.It may not have been the perfect remaster port everyone was hoping for, but at the end of the day and at the core, it's still Sonic Colours with a new coat of paint... for better or for worse.

_childDocuments_.review: All things considered, this isn't that bad of a port at all honestly. It's not great, but nowhere near as problematic as Sonic Origins or as downright egregious as Sonic Adventure DX. The lighting changes are really only noticeable in Tropical Resort, which I adjusted to quickly. Generally, there is a little too much bloom but this was something I also adjusted to, and isn't something that drastically alters the look of the stages. Additionally, I think that the new mechanic of timing your homing attacks to increase your boost gauge is a great addition, and introduces an increased level of engagement to attacking enemies. The sound that plays when you correctly time it does get annoying, though. Maybe there could've been some visual indicator of a correctly timed homing attack instead, or at least an option for it.Regardless, we absolutely should've been given the option to choose the original Sonic Colors experience, without the Tails saves, park tokens, Jade Wisps, or any of the other adjustments to the level design. This is one of my biggest problems with Sonic Origins as well (which I do not own), where you absolutely cannot play the games as they were originally designed. These games were designed with lives in mind. I'm pretty sure this is a matter of a menu toggle that switches a few variables around. Lives are not so incredibly antiquated and inaccessible that we can't even give people the option to play these games as they were originally intended. I suspect that Sonic Colors Ultimate is a rerelease geared more towards kids, but why can't fans be catered to as well? That's what Sonic Colors originally did for Classic Sonic fans back in 2010.Also, the options menu is horrendous. It doesn't fade in when you select it and navigation is super laggy. How do you screw up a menu system this badly? Maybe it has to do with Sonic being rendered in real-time in the cosmetics section, but either way there's no excuse for it. Also, the landing animation is still broken in Starlight Carnival 3, and the Wisp capsule at the beginning of Asteroid Coaster 1 is still impossible to collide with.I don't expect any of these things to be fixed. I think Sega published a few tweets announcing bug fixes post-launch and then cut their losses. I know there are probably passionate people in this company that want to make these Sonic releases better, and some higher-ups are telling them, "no, we're cutting our losses". If the Sonic Origins launch is anything to go by then there are people impeding the work of these developers. That lack of polish is the difference between a Sonic release and a Nintendo release. Ideally, Sonic releases should be just as polished as Nintendo's output on the Switch. Sega, you set those expectations over 30 years ago and I will forever hold you to them.What is most frustrating about Sonic Colors Ultimate is that it's a part of a pattern I'm seeing with how Sega treats these Sonic rereleases. Sonic Adventure DX, Sonic Origins, and Sonic Colors Ultimate are all available on Steam and are flawed to varying degrees. Sega, these are rereleases of some of your most critically acclaimed and beloved Sonic titles, and when the most accessible versions of them are problematic then it tells me you don't value preserving this franchise's legacy.If you want to play Sonic Colors on Steam, then I can recommend this. In all fairness, I think that the issues fans take issue with might not concern most people. However, that extra polish really does matter, and this rerelease is a bit lacking in that regard. I will be giving a thumbs down because I'd like Sega to do better on preserving their legacy content.

NO. i absolutely do not recommend buying this game AT ALL. please save your money and buy something else, just because sonic is in this game does not mean it must be bought.and the fact this game has not been fully fixed yet since its release almost 3 years ago is mind boggling. i mean, they fixed like 2 or 3 major issues but left everything else alone abandoning this game and letting it rot.i have nothing else to say about this game. its just a really bad remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird game to review so im gonna start off by saying:Sonic Colors itself is a GREAT game. whichever way you want to play it, it is so, so fun. The wisps, the different level themes, the gimmicks all stand out and are exactly what makes sonic fun. You can go fast as ♥♥♥♥ and going back to levels is legitimately rewarding, because there are other pathways to discover, places you can only reach with wisp usage. It's a game that truly stands out because of this gameplay mechanic, in Sonic and in the wider Platforming genre.But this remaster has issues. i dont think it has enough issues to warrant the *mixed* score, as it's pretty obviously good at its core - but it has issues. I played it on epic and on switch so dont mind the half an hour of playtime, I know what I'm talking about.The bad things, ill break them down here:- random screen stuttering? Idk, sometimes its perfect, at times its not. It seems to get better after you've been playing for a bit. Still inexcusable.- Lighting system ranges from ok to bad to glowstick and sonic's model is awful. This is a very big problem, he also has this drawn on smile. I get what look they were going for, but there are areas that have arguably worse lighting than the original, so it makes it feel cheap, and it shouldn't even be a point of contention. its the type of thing that shouldn't be a debate.- New UI is horrendous. it just does NOT fit with the rest of the game (i mean in terms of they added in, not what was there before.)- Lack of options for graphics - you can only add vsync, change resolution or make it fullscreen, etc. which is ♥♥♥♥ for a pc game, this isn't 2009. this isnt games for windows, let me change settings i don't understand.- Occasional glitches (i didnt really get them, but they are a thing and a flaw of the game). Just straight up shouldn't be a thing like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It's a remaster. Remasters should be definitive, not DIVISIVE. it can ruin your experience. it didnt ruin mine, but I have seen clips and its very annoying.- Cutscenes are not bad but not good? they look like they were ai upscaled, but at the same time, more or less fine.- They took away the multiple save system. what the ♥♥♥♥ was the point of that? it was integrated with the mii stuff? thats all i can assume - but sonic simulator wasn't killed. so its just dumb they removed that.- DRM is still here, and it can make performance worse, but I'm not clear on it.So there is a fair amount of negatives, and it sounds like I HATE the game but TBF there are good things that this remaster does:+ 60fps, 4k quality. It didn't look this crisp on Wii, and it's a clean output that we've never officially seen for Colours.+ Better overall controls, wall jumping and 3D movement both feel more accurate than the original.+ Changeable controls, decent on keyboard.+ Homing attack sweet spot is great, and not talked about enough - this function adds more speed to the game and rewards good timing with more of a thrill, you can boost so much more than you could in the original, and playing the OG game without feels very strange.+ Rival rush content - its a glorified time trial but legitimately is a fun addition that gives you something to strive for, not in the original game. Racing against Metal Sonic with that funky music is cool.+ Graphically enhanced assets - textures look a large degree better than the original game. this is not a simple upscale and it shows when you do a side by side. it makes a difference in presentation.+ Jade wisp is a cool change and a fun addition, as it allows for a new way to explore levels, going through walls.+ Lots of new customisation options, even if they're very surface level, do offer more replayability and are a nice option. the boost auras are actually really damn cool.+ A brand new remixed soundtrack that you can toggle. I personally love it, but get that it's about preference. You can even put a mixed version on with both old and new.+ Other small things, new invincibility ring, tutorial voiced by Tails, Tails life system.+ It's still a good game.TLDR: It's a good game worth buying even considering Dolphin, as the steam version already has mods that let you fix the lighting system and other things. I have the game on dolphin AND on Wii. trying to mod and hack an emulated game doesn't always end up well.You also miss out on the extra content (if you care about it) - so there is absolutely worth in this remaster, even with the things it ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up on. it isn't a simple upscale. I highly recommend Sonic Colors, and even recommend Ultimate. It may be that none of the issues are a problem for you, even though they are there.If you dont care about this extra content and just want the core game, get it on Wii or emulate it. If you want it in your steam library, there's nothing I can say to sway you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not worth a penny above 20$. It is 2-3 hrs long, dominated by mediocre gameplay, and the remaster teeters between unremarkable upscaling to just straight up visual downgrades. It is a solid meh game.Gameplay is divided into 2D and 3D sections. The 3D sections are more like interactive cutscenes, because you dont actually do very much during them. You hold boost and the homing attack button, and sonic does most of the work for you. For some levels, the game actually does the whole running  thing automatically, leaving dodging as your only form of interaction. 2D dominates the majority of this game's runtime. This wouldn't be a problem if the 2D sections were faster paced, but they aren't, and you spend what feels like eons in what is essentially stop'n'go platforming, which would be fine for a mario game, but the entire premise of sonic is going fast, and that is something that sonic colors fails at for the majority of the game. As I mentioned before, the game is criminally short for its price tag. The game is 2-3 hrs long, and each individual level is 2-5 minutes long. However, there are filler levels in between the proper ones that are literally 1 minute long and have you collecting a bunch of rings/shiny things, so I'd say the actual meat of this game is MAYBE* about 2hrs long. The whole "ultimate edition" part of its name is sorta just a lie. The game, ironically, ♥♥♥♥♥ up the colors of the original wii version and turns up the bloom so high that the game looks like it has the color pallete and lighting of a gmod animation from 2009. The in-game cutscenes are AI upscaled, so there are awful warping effects on objects in the background, or ones that are out of focus. Overall, it is nothing more than a below average 'remaster' .None of the things mentioned in this review would be that bad if the game were priced accordingly, but Sega insists on having it be nearly full price, even though, at heart, it is a half-baked remaster of an average sonic game from 2010. There is nothing remarkable about this game, and there is nothing here worth buying at this price. If I were to put a number on this game, i'd give it a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: After a long wait as an exclusive over on Epic Games, Sonic Colors: Ultimate finally makes its way over to Steam. For those who skipped the Wii back in the late 2000s and early 2010s, this is a great method to finally experience what's arguably one of the best modern Sonic games. There's a lot more than just a basic HD coat of paint. Mainly, you have customization options for Sonic's appearance, options to pick between classic and remixed music, and time trials on some levels against Metal Sonic.The primary downside from the Wii version is that this remaster only uses one save file, as opposed to the Wii version having multiple save files. So if you ever want to replay the game, you'll have to delete your save file. Annoying, but given that this is PC, there's likely the option to just manually back-up your current save if needed. There is also the fact that if you start the game with Tails providing a tutorial, you can't disable him later. Make sure to start your game without him providing a tutorial, or he'll keep interrupting you with text boxes with advice you already learned about when replaying levels.As for any major bugs, I'm not sure what other reviewers are experiencing that's causing problems. The only notable bug so far was a one-time mistake with a homing attack that hasn't happened since. I temporarily got stuck because the homing attack was triggered from a weird angle on the side of a wall.

A theme park full of varied sections was a PHENOMENAL idea for a setting, I enjoy it a lot! However, the writing and humour this time is so dang weak and annoying. It even leads to entirely pointless cutscenes that do not progress the story at all, but instead attempts (and fails) to make people laugh.

People mentioned that the game is fine currently but through out my experience, I am here to deny this fact. This port feels low effort with all the querks that I had to deal with. _childDocuments_.review: A genuine joy ride from start to finish, with a few bumps along the way. Everything about this game is so creative, and the sheer spectacle makes me feel like I'm in an amusement park like Sonic. The setting is so pretty and detailed, made even better by the funny commentary Eggman gives to parkgoers in every level. Would recommend, but only if you play Sonic games for the exploration element. Because a lot of this game is slower paced and more puzzle centric opposed to being purely built for maintaining speed which other boost games focus on.The introduction of wisps makes for some really fun and unique challenges, and gives you a ton of options on how you want to tackle platforming. Spike, Laser, and Drill are all snappy and fun to use. Although there is an issue of some of them like hover feeling really really slow, and there's no way to cancel them early so you have to wait it out. The new ghost wisp is alright, it feels fun enough to slingshot between ghost points.The levels overall are very fun, with some of the coolest and most creative themes thus far. A bakery planet with cake layers instead of dirt layers to drill through, a dome full of water and samurai, and a roller coaster through asteroids. The egg pawns have cute little outfits to match the worlds. But while there is a nice mix of fast pace running and slow paced puzzle sections, some sections of levels can be way too slow and tedious, like buttons you have to stand on for 5 seconds just to cross and autoscrollers that move really slowly.The biggest problem with this game is how it handles platforming. There are a lot of basic platforming sections in every world, which would be fine if Sonic didn't rely so much on the double jump. Because for some reason, in spite of this being a remake, the biggest problem with Sonic's double jump in the wii version wasn't fixed, that being it shares the button with homing attack. This means if you have to use a second jump to save your life or reach a platform, and there is even a single target on screen, you will forfeit your jump... and possibly even your life. Seriously, this should get a fix, at least a setting or something.Overall, this game is fun to play and REALLY fun to fully complete, with all of the red star rings that unlock bonus levels and s ranks. It offers some nice new cosmetic features over the wii version and the appreciated removal of limited lives. Although it still needs some common sense fixes like making the restart button at the end of the level not delete progress.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so weird to review.It's Sonic Colors but a remaster and port to PC.While i do appreciate that they ported this game to PC (which SEGA should keep doing with the rest of Sonic games), this game does the minimum for a remaster.It is neat that there is customization on Sonic, and the new Rival Rush races are very cool too, the game does look better in some areas to me...And Sonic Colors was a completely fine game to beging with.It is a very well-known game that introduce the wisps, which give Sonic new ways to play, they are pretty creative in their own ways and very cute and friendly, and the game does revolve around them for pretty much like 90% of the levels.The levels are also very cool and well-structured. There are some levels that could be better tho.It is a pretty good Sonic game overall...But the remaster part of it left me kinda disappointed.The things above are pretty good but the rest of it are kinda whatever.The new ghost wisp is cool but... it just doesnt do anything outside of some secret areas with lots of rings or just secret red rings.Those areas are visually bugged because Sonic was not intended to be in there in the original.The cutscenes are also the same, the game is visually different but not the cutscenes which is... weird.I also am not a big fan of the new music, imo the old music was SO much better, but it is cool that they left the old music in the game.It is also kinda weird that this game has 1 save file, which for example in the Wii version there are 6 of them, which is kinda weird, I feel like having the option for more than 1 save file is nice but this one does not have it.The game also crushed here and there for me, and is not a me thing when other users have this problem too.Overall, this remaster was really disappointing to me.The game itself is fine, still is Sonic Colors and Sonic Colors is a great game, and the fact that you can play this game in your PC is very good.I like this game because of the game itself, the remaster as a whole kinda sucked.So this game it's ok.6.2/10

_childDocuments_.review: Disregarding the BLOOOOOM, fanmade "rerainbowed" project, poor cutscene quality, and the glitches, I played through the entire game on Nintendo Switch (which I 100%ed) and it's really not as bad as people thinkIs it the definitive way to play Colors? No, not by a large margin. However, it's a port nontheless that adds a couple new things.Customization, "sweet spot" homing attack, and a new wispMany levels require more exploration due to some red ring locations being rehidden, only being found by the new ghost wisp.The gameplay is still the exact same, boosting Sonic with a heavy empthasis on platforming. This isn't a Sonic Origins situation where the physics are noticeably different to the point where it jacks your muscle memory, they thankfully didn't try messing with that this time around.The new visuals may be an off putter, but I got used to it myself. Yes, it is better with the older style, don't get me wrong, but even if the game looks like a game from the PS1, if it plays well that's all it needs to be good.You can have the prettiest visuals ever made, but if the gameplay is unfun, you lost.Sonic Colors shouldn't be anywhere near the conversation of best 3D Sonic gameplay, but in speedruns, it is pretty satisfying utilizing Sonic's moves to make shortcuts on platforming, managing boost, and choosing what wisps to use and at what moment.Overall, Colors Ultimate isn't that offensive if you're looking for a fun Sonic game, however if you'd rather spare your eyes and ears, you should probably get the rerainbow mod to enhance the experience.So yeah, that's what I got to say on the matter of this port, 5ish years later.... man I'm old.

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of performance, I haven't experienced any issues as the game runs at a solid 60 fps and looks even incredibly smooth. Moreover, I didn't run into any real bugs or glitches upon completing the game and getting all achievements. The only issues I did encounter were the Starlight Carnival Act 3 intro as well as the Sweet Mountain boss cannons floating during the ship's animation sequence.In my opinion, I would say most areas look great and beat out the original with only a few instances. The environments are some of the most creative areas I have seen in a Sonic game and the fantastic soundtracks (original and remixed) compliment these areas perfectly. , one issue with the game that I have to mention is that all the background music is set a mono. This essentially means you will not be able enjoy the game's soundtrack, at least not to its full capacity. The game's cutscenes are also unfortunately just upscaled versions of the original on the Wii which makes them clash with the remaster's new look. It's not a major problem, but it's worth noting.In terms of gameplay, the primary focus is on the wisps, small aliens that give Sonic abilities that can be used to solve puzzles, defeat enemies, and explore areas. The wisps all function differently and some are definitely better to use than others but I'd say they compliment the game very well. Some levels are longer with more scope while other levels are shorter and mainly focus on a single gimmick. The only sections of the game I would say are a drag are the areas that don't focus on the wisps (e.g. yellow springs levels, fire bars, moving platforms, etc...). These areas aren't common throughout the game but I'd figure I should mention them.With the game's backdrop being a colorful amusement park, the story takes on a light-hearted theme with multiple instance of jokes and quips. In regards to the game's humor, most of the jokes are not really that great with there being a few exceptions. The dialogue between Sonic and Tails is pretty good and Eggman's character is great as well. Overall, I'd say Sonic Colors Ultimate is a fine way to experience the original game. The game runs, looks, and plays great with there only being a few problems such as the mono audio and animation issues. Overall, I'd still recommend this game to those who want to try it out or never got to experience the original.Final rating: 77/100

_childDocuments_.review: After 100%ing the game, I do not understand why Sonic Colors' reputation has gotten worse recently.Does the game have issues? Yes.Does the port have issues? VERY MUCH SO YES. However, the game itself is very well-crafted. The level design is really good for the most part. Some levels suffer from too much automation (Starlight Carnival is my least favourite for this reason) but as a whole it's a great bunch of levels. There's an abundance of 2D sections, which is a big point of criticism. And while I do agree that there should've been a stronger focus on 3D platforming, the sections themselves are good, so is it really a negative? The wisps, although gimmicks, are still pretty fun and open up some pretty clever secrets.The bosses are... very bad. There are only 4 unique bosses in a game with 7 areas, and they are miserable to fight because of the janky hitboxes and poor telegraphs.The story is nonexistent. This is the era of Sonic where SEGA managed to hire some of the worst writers in existence to make the scripts, so it's full of poorly landed jokes and horrid one-liners. Zero stakes.The music is exceptional, as is the norm with Sonic. Asteroid Coaster, Terminal Velocity, Planet Wisp, Sweet Mountain. All absolute masterpieces.The extra content is quite minimal and tacked on, which is a shame when you consider how replayable Sonic games usually are. I did enjoy running through all the levels in a single gauntlet (although REALLY wish there were no bosses), but it didn't add much to my experience.I wish SEGA would let the devs spend enough time to polish the game/port for once in Sonic's history, but as a whole the game is just a great time with a banger OST.

The Project Re-Rainbow mod helps improve a lot of things at the cost of some stability due to being a work in-progress.Don't buy it if you don't have an SSD to install it onto. _childDocuments_.review: Sonic Colours: Ultimate, or as I like to call it Seizure Colours: Ultimate - Epilepsy Edition, is one of the worst games. Ever.No, seriously. Easily worse than 06 and Boom: RoL.Sonic Colours itself is a Sonic Forces tier game, which is fine enough as I do enjoy it. But this "Remaster" is a joke.It originally came out and was announced as a Pig Store Exclusive for a good reason because the game is completely broken. The game released back in 2021 with a huge amount of bugs- Broken Audio (some audio just refuses to play)- Broken Audio mixing (left and right channels were messed up)- Major graphical glitches (like random textures popping in, stuff popping in and out constantly)- Gameplay Glitches (like rails sending you flying back, or the jade wisp sending you into OoB)- Stuttering (unplayable levels of it)- Missing Localisation (fine on PS4)This tiny list is just scratching the surface of the issues in this game, you can easily find videos online showcasing how bad it is.None of this is fixed apart from the Left and Right Channels which they "fixed" by making all the audio Mono instead of Stereo. The game was left to rot.In fact with each update they pushed out over 2021 the game got into an even worse state with more stuff breaking (most notable for me is an Aquarium Park and Terminal Velocity boss missing its laser charge up effect making you need to have insane reaction time)They have the audacity to even show up on Steam with none of this fixed and charge 40 quid for it, include Denuvo in it (it is a horrendous remaster of a Wii game!!!) and it is laughable.The "remaster" side of the game is also not great, some textures look a lot better for modern displays but then there are some which look absolutely horrendous, mix this with the new terrible lighting and you have a overwhelmingly inferior experience to the original you can find at charity shops for a quid. It does't help that playing the original in a modern way you can get fan textures that do the game a lot more justice.and while patched this should still be mentioned to give you an idea of how this game was treated and to explain my nickname for the game. On Day 1 on NSW the game had an extreme graphical glitch that resulted in extreme graphical glitches which is now known as the Seizure glitch due to how severe the extreme the effects of it where. It took IIRC about 20 days for them to release a fix for it which is embarrassing.In conclusion, Sonic Colours: Ultimate is a joke and a very unfunny one at that. You shouldn't buy it or consider buying it. Save your money.Edit: THEY FIXED 3 BUGS (I've noticed) WITH THE STEAM RELEASE!!!- The wisps on the main menu don't flicker on first start up- AP and TV Stage Boss Bug I mentioned is fixed now- Asteroid Coaster Act 1 Goal Ring is opaqueand everything else is still busted...

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Colors Ultimate… man, where do I even start? This game just feels off. The story leans way too hard into comedy, and Sonic himself doesn’t feel like the Sonic I grew up with. Tails is even worse. And don’t get me started on the Wisps. They’re just a bad mechanic shoved in to replace the other characters Sonic games used to be known for. This was the beginning of Sonic turning into a series aimed strictly at 6-12-year-olds (thanks, Iizuka), and it shows. That era was one of Sonic’s worst until Frontiers came around.Sure, the graphics are technically good, but they’re just… too much. I love vibrant colors, but this game cranks it up to where it feels like it’s just going 'ooo, colors!' without any real depth. Even Planet Wisp, which looks decent, suffers from this problem. It’s flashy but feels empty at the same time. For comparison, games like Sonic 06 and Unleashed had a much better sense of style and atmosphere.And then there’s the port itself. Oh boy, it’s a mess. The glitches are everywhere, from game-breaking bugs to seizure-inducing graphical errors. Not to mention the save data deletion bug. It’s like they didn’t even try to polish it up. Honestly, this version just isn’t worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't care what people say to me for thinking this, but this is definitely, without a doubt, the definitive version of Sonic Colors. However, is Sonic Colors actually good? Weeeelll... Everyone else seems to think Colors is good. Maybe not Colors Ultimate, but regular Colors. Do I agree? No. No I do not.Story: 5/10The story is as about simplistic and average as one can get. There is only 5 characters (arguably 6) in the game. Sonic, Tails, Eggman, and his 2 new robots, Orbot and Cubot. Eggman has built a galactic amusement park, and when Sonic and Tails find out about it, they go to find that Eggman has enslaved an alien race known as Wisps. So Sonic and Tails go to stop him.Orbot and Cubot add nothing to the story and only serve as comedic relief. I don't mind comedic relief characters, but they should at least add 1 thing to the story. But these guys don't. The Wisps are never portrayed as people of an alien race, they are just there as an excuse to give Sonic mundane and unfun power-ups.Writing: 3/10This is the first game written by Ken Pontac and Warren Graff. Before writing this game, they had never played or seen a Sonic game before, and it shows. They turned Sonic from a cocky teenager, who knew when to be serious, was kind-hearted, compassionate, and treated all of his friends with respect, into an arrogant, dumb loser who tries to be "cool" and fails miserably, who thinks that his friends are too weak to take care of themselves. Remember when Tails stopped a missile from blowing up a city and stopped Eggman all by himself? Remember when Tails thought he saw Sonic die before his eyes and did everything in his power to avenge him? Remember when tails was actually useful? Well, Sonic doesn't. Tails is completely useless in this game, aside from in Ultimate, where for whatever reason, he can take you back to certain checkpoints, even though the game was already easy enough. Eggman is a complete joke. He doesn't feel threatening and spends most of his time yelling at his minions in anger like a really dumb and bad cartoon villain. He never even has a reason for yelling at them all the time. Like, for example, Megatron from Transformers, only ever yells and belittles his minions whenever they have a royal screw-up or are being really stupid. Eggman's belittlement of Orbot and Cubot just makes him seem like an abusive boss, and not a person.Gameplay: 6/10Ehhh... it's... fine, I guess. I want to say it's mostly boost to win, and while that is true sometimes, it also isn't. The Wisps aren't fun to use, and they never should have been in any other Sonic game after this one, yet it's like they're an invasive species.Level Design: 6/10Again, just... fine, I guess. Act 1 of each world is usually really good, but always too easy, and then everything after that is either too short, or just not fun to play.Overall, this is the game that killed the franchise until Frontiers came to dig the grave.5/10 + 3/10 + 6/10 + 6/10 = 20/4020/40 divided by 4 equals 5/10Not terrible. But not impressive.

_childDocuments_.review: I won’t deny that I had fun playing it, but it’s just horrendous. It also highlights the hypocrisy of the Sonic fanbase once again. They hate Forces because it’s a hallway simulator and has short levels. Yet they praise ♥♥♥♥ like this. Most stages consist of short challenges that are quite literally a small portion of the 1st or 2nd act. And they even go as far as to recycle the same few bosses because they couldn’t come up with much variety. Over half of my playtime was probably dedicated to gathering collectibles. Being the game that introduced these red rings as collectible items already encourages me to chug it into the bin as this feature was unfortunately carried over to future titles. Some of these are quite obnoxious to get. Others require you to do some cryptic nonsense to even see them. In a game where speed should be the main focus, I don’t appreciate strolling through every stage at snail’s pace to find these. I was actually so desperate that I had to look up a guide for some of them as their hiding spot was just absurd. It doesn’t help that some of the later stages turn into a literal maze.But while we are on the subject of speed, don’t expect to win a pot of gold with that here. Because the requirement for an S rank has never been this terrible. Gotta go fast? No! You must goof around in every stage. Take it slow to rack up those points for using wisps. This was especially bad in two instances. One being a boss fight in which you quite literally have to rely on luck to give you a wisp twice while still maintaining your rings and meeting time expectations. The other one being so absurd that I figured out a neat way to cheese it. Thank you devs for the moronic feature of Tails saves, it was infuriating throughout the whole game, but actually saved me the trouble of gathering enough points.Allow me to squeeze in a minor complaint that becomes quite annoying on multiple replays. There are various segments in this game that are the equivalent of watching a cutscene play out. These scripted sections go on for far too long sometimes and only serve to show off some mediocre visuals. I can picture how the devs were rubbing their nipples as they implemented these into the game, expecting us to be amazed. I don’t play a game so you can stroke your tiny wieners, I play a game to escape the uneventful and miserable reality that is my life.What else is there? Oh right, let’s talk about Super Sonic. In every other Sonic game you would have to collect 7 Chaos Emeralds to get access to him. But not here. This time you’re obligated to get ALL of the red rings, 180 collectibles! This isn’t even the worst part. After going through all that ♥♥♥♥, you come to the realization that Super Sonic is extremely underwhelming and can’t even be used in boss stages. The issue is that the entire game is designed around wisps, they are intended to be used. But with Super Sonic, they are no longer usable, making the game actually harder in certain cases. The developers were actually aware of this, hence why they occasionally added bounce pads in certain stages if accessed as Super Sonic.There is one more thing I wish to rant about. It’s an achievement that you unlock for finishing challenge mode. This mode takes close to an hour to finish as it’s essentially just all the stages glued together back to back. Now why is this an issue? The issue itself lies not within the mode itself. It’s actually quite unchallenging and a literal walk in the park. The only problem is that the game has a tendency to crash while playing this mode. I don’t appreciate losing 20 minutes of progress and not being able to continue where I left off. You’re forced to do this entire achievement in one sitting and can’t even save your progression. Practically an achievement tied to luck.Overall a forgettable experience. I honestly can’t tell the difference between this and Forces. Come to think of it, the cutscenes in this game are not only worse but also less frequent. If you took all of them away, nothing would change. As for the remaster aspect, I have no strong opinion on it as I never played the original. Although I will admit that the characters, especially Sonic, look horrible. The added character customization is a fine addition, although the Metal Sonic races feel truly out of place and unnecessary. The only positive I can give this game is that the achievement completion itself wasn't difficult and straightforward. Thank you Sonic Team, too bad this game is the founding father for some terrible practices that would inevitably be carried into future games. I'm so tired of being in a state where I have to pick between boost formula or classic. What happened to adventure-like games where you could actually control your character for the majority of the game?

_childDocuments_.review: I do not understand why this game has a Mixed score on Steam. Maybe because I never played the original on the Wii? Other people keep mentioning this mod that is the "definitive experience" or something but after looking into it, it looked like just graphical upscaling. That's cool and all, and if you want that all the power to you, but the game looks fine without it and it didn't seem to impact gameplay in any way (which matters to me FAR more than graphics) so I didn't even bother. Un-modded, this was a solid 8.5/10 experience. It played well, was a lot of fun, and was incredibly replayable. I even went out of my way to collect every red ring and I'm even interested in getting every S rank for the fun of it.It's somewhat short, but that's not uncommon for Sonic games. You really get your moneys worth if you go out of your way to hunt for secrets, but I realize that isn't for everyone so take that into account. I'd say like 9-10 hours casual and like 15-20 completionist, maybe more. I'm writing this at 12 hours and like I said I got all 180 red rings, unlocked Super Sonic, got the credits, and I'd say I've got like half of the 44 Acts S ranked.I ran into a small handful of glitches, like "I could count on one hand how many" small. Bummer, but from what I've seen of the original in YouTube videos the glitches I experienced weren't new additions to this remaster. (Plus... I mean... it is a Sonic game... so yeah.)If you are interested in this game but on the fence and the only thing dissuading you is the mixed score and the negative reviews calling this game a "crime against remasters"... I'm telling you I either got a different build of the game than they did or they've got nostalgia glasses on because I don't regret this purchase in any way. Granted I did get it on sale, so take that into account.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always held a soft spot for Sonic Colors personally, as it was my first '3D'/'modern' Sonic game that I really played, and while it admittedly isn't perfect, I still really enjoy going back to the game due to it's (mostly) solid level design and Sonic's movement feeling particularly agile and fluid, both in 2D and 3D. Not to mention creative stage themes, really nice visuals and one of if not my favorite soundtracks in the franchise.As far as Ultimate goes, I've pretty much held the same opinion on it that I had when it launched back in 2021. In a nutshell, I do think the hate it got did feel a bit overblown, but at the same time was justified. There are improvements made to the base game that I think were rather good - particularly the Perfect Homing Attack which I think added an extra layer of 'skill' to the original game by rewarding the player for timing their homing attacks just right, as well as the Jade Ghost Wisp which while pretty situational does allow for some neat exploration elements and shortcuts - and there is obviously the added visual fidelity as well. That being said it does have it's issues - the laggy options menu, pop-in, and whatever the hell was going on with the Switch version at launch - and overall just feels pretty lacking as a remaster in of itself. Ultimate's a fine enough way to play Sonic Colors, but I definitely can't say it's an 'upgrade' from the original, especially for the $40 price tag.If you are interesting in playing Sonic Colors and picking up Ultimate, I have two suggestions - one, buy it on sale (for at least 50% off), and two, download and install the Re-Rainbow mod. In a lot of ways Re-Rainbow really feels like what Colors Ultimate should've been to begin with. The visuals look A LOT 'cleaner', the cutscenes are re-animated and look a lot better than the weird AI upscaled cutscenes of base Ultimate, the menus look better and most if not all of the visual glitchiness of base Ultimate is fixed with the mod. It definitely makes Colors Ultimate feel more like a remaster rather than just a 'fine' way to play Sonic Colors with some extra visual fidelity.

_childDocuments_.review: 2.4 hours later, finished the game, only 2 restarts because Alt+Tabbing crashes the game, and I never learn sometimes.I kinda wish Steam actually has a feature to make a "mixed" review of itself, because half of me wants to say that this is a somewhat decent port with bare minimum execution.Other than that though, as someone who actually grew up playing on the Wii version, I noticed a couple of minor glitches/annoyances that kinda sets me off every time I noticed it.-Every time Sonic walks on the field map, his running animation doesn't sync up with the sound like how it was originally was, making him look slower than usual.-Every time you beat the stage and come back to the field map, Sonic is always showing up bouncing in place, where as originally, he was meant to be invisible and *then* appear on screen for the next act to roll up.-Initially, my game lagged *really* bad as I started the first act, around the 20fps mark for at least a couple of seconds before it shot back up to normal, never went down so far since.-Starlight Carnival Act 3, The moment you boot up the level, Sonic doesn't land on the ground before running off as the stage begins.-Sound effects either cut off at random or never overlap with the others, so if you have multiple effects going off at the same time, only one will play.-Any time you press a button and summon enemies, even if you have the navigator (a.k.a, tutorial rings) off, Tails will always point it out. He never does this in the original and it's annoying.-There's an off-chance that there will be leftover spike effects after using Spike, nothing major.As for the art style, I can tolerate it at best, but I honestly wish it could look a little bit better than how it is presented.Some music from the original has carried over like the field maps, but most of the music had been remade, which I just take it as a "take it or leave it" response.What I wished was a thing is to have the ability to actually swap music over for the original soundtrack of the Wii version, considering other remasters like Xenoblade Chronicles Definitive Edition and the Final Fantasy Pixel Remaster series (just now) actually give you the ability to swap the music for the original renditions, but I guess with Sonic Colors: Ultimate, you're going to have to mod that one in...All-in-all, I'm somewhat glad to see that Sonic Colors *has* actually improved compared to the launch images I've seen, but I'm still disappointed over the features they actually give and the bugs that remained unpatched. Your best bet is to get this on sale, 70% at the very least, or play the original on the Wii.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest technical issues have been fixed since launch and the game now plays ok. I did still encounter some bugs causing me to restart the level as well as one crash, but nothing too bad – just some minutes were lost. Sonic fanbase has kind of mixed stance on Sonic Colors, sometimes criticizing shortness of levels, lots of 2D segments at the expense of 3D, cheesy story and dialogues, or wisp gameplay. I can personally agree on the story/dialogues part as this game does probably have the cringiest writing in the entire series. Other elements I learned to like over time to the point that Colors is, gameplay-wise, among the top Sonic games for me. It is true that boosting was done better in Generations, but levels in Colors try to be something different, emphasizing exploration and experimentation (sort of a nod to the old 2D games). The art on the levels is unique and fits well to the traditional colorful feel-good palette of Sonic (or how should I call it). The game also offers decent challenge in finishing levels for S ranks, rival battles, or challenge mode.Now, as for the remaster/port itself, it does not bring much extra over the original game and is technically sloppy, as is lately tradition with SEGA. The most annoying persisting things are micro stutters (Denuvo?) and fps drops. Animations could have used improvement… For those who have the means to play the original version, there is no reason to buy this remaster.  Those who never played Colors or do not have access to any copy might pick this up. It is a good Sonic game as is.My rating of game itself: 8.5/10Rating of the remaster/port: 5.5/10Overall rating:

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very Sonic game.A Sonic game with all the good and ugly of old titles, with elements of platforming that try to mimic more traditional style, and with some ultra experimental moments. The game swings from amazing fluidity and consistency in some acts and stages to crippling identity crisis in others.A Sonic game with a very basic yet cute story that doesn't try to be anything special, a kind of story that can be written in a game booklet and deemed sufficient. A story that makes as much sense as required and not a bit more.A Sonic game with popping colors and timeless design. I disagree with the popular opinion that it looks worse than Wii, they decided to go with a bit different art style, and it suits it perfectly.A Sonic game that, despite stumbling at times, leaves you with an overwhelming feeling of accomplishment, the game that, after exhausting you, rewards you by genuinely making you feel like you've done something absolutely epic.A Sonic game that puts its best effort into making you remember the good.Last note: in the current iteration, I haven't encountered a single visual or physical bug, the game didn't crash a single time.If you're new to Sonic, this game is a litmus paper if the franchise is for you. If you are not, and you got turned off by reviews and opinions of YouTubers... Still give it a shot. You might get surprised.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is better than passable, but stops short of spectacular. Definitely managed to enjoy this as if I was playing Colors for the first time all over again. (Colors does not have a U, by the way :P)The Good:- The 8th Wisp. Compared to the OG you might honestly think that the wisp was shoved in, but no! There are legitimately thought out additional areas because of the 8th wisp, and I can only give this positive marks for additional things to do in certain levels.- The additional flashiness of playing as a cosmetically different Sonic is cool I suppose. You can even play as Movie Sonic if you want, if you get the Cosmetic DLC.- They've also added "Park Tokens" to buy the aforementioned cosmetics in-game, and this part was done right imo. Lot of places where they spotted tokens in the levels, and it takes a good full playthrough+ to be able to buy all the cosmetics.- The game has stayed largely unchanged besides the 8th Wisp (and 100 ring items!), and it's great to see that. Hopefully more people get to appreciate such things as the scoring system of this game - it's unique for Sonic, and is very underappreciated.- The achievement set actually had some decent thought put into it, and is pretty engaging.- The "Sweet Spot" mechanic might seem pointless at first, until you realize it gives you more boost, creating potentially interesting situations where there normally is low or no boost.- The Rival Rush concept was a nice side addition! I do wonder what every (non-Terminal Velocity) level would have been like under Rival Rush, though.The Bad:- Lives being replaced by Tails heads. This system of Tails rescuing you from a pit (upward pits apparently don't count, and I cite the end of Asteroid Coaster 2 as the example) honestly was not a necessary addition at all. It also creates situations where objects respawn in full, so you can wind up recollecting things and make it even easier to S rank, which is a big negative imo. That's not how the game was designed. #BringBackExtraLives- There are some unfortunate stutters and oddities that deserve mention. Slight stutters occur when collecting Tails heads (Tails has a big head joke here), when 3 tokens drop at the results after getting an S, at the end-of-stage wisp capsules, and during some prompts. Additionally, the word SCORE can just straight up disappear sometimes, Planet Wisp 1's road to the first Red Ring does not line you up with the first set of rings, a spring noise always occurs when going through rings, dash panels, etc. (literally why?), and there are some areas in Aquarium Park that don't seem to work as they should (like AP6 when you get out of the water using the spring after the first major area), to name a few. None of these make the game unplayable per se, but they do dampen the experience a tiny bit.- Obligatory Denuvo comment. - The credits are something I wish they changed for the better, but no, the credits are LONGER. You could probably run an errand or two in the time it takes for the credits to finish. I like the concept of the credits, but having credits longer than 10 minutes is a sin.Overall, pretty good game. If you played Colors before, it's worth the sale price. If you haven't, I'd still lean towards sale price. If the remixes seem a bit off to you, I recommend the OG music.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite Ichiban's introduction after this game and multiple new playable characters in Yakuza 4 and 5, Yagami stands out as the most utilized character who seamlessly fits into the modern setting. Without the sequel baggage, the story can finally have the freedom to be unique and creative. It has a light Ace Attorney-style narrative that I enjoy. Unlike Yakuza 3, Judgment maintains the line between over-the-top storytelling and a sense of realism. The story is well-paced to keep you interested throughout.Although the combat offers a lighter depth, it brings back the beloved style-switching mechanic from Yakuza 0. While enjoyable, it doesn't reach the level of being amazing. The mortal wound mechanic is a questionable addition. Its goal is to prevent players from constantly relying on healing items. In my experience, I still guzzle down food to heal. The wound can become frustrating since there is only one spot in town to treat it. The friendship mechanic returns and stands out as the best iteration I have ever experienced. It's a mix of easy tasks such as purchasing items to side-quest story content. While the overall number of side-quests may be fewer compared to other Yakuza games, they are well spread within the friendship mechanic and side-cases. On a related note, the girlfriend mechanic is arduous and morally questionable as you are dating 4 girlfriends simultaneously.The new mini-games don't hit it for me. They end up taking a lot of your time, and the rewards they offer are pretty underwhelming. Even if the payoff is great, the mechanics themselves can be a chore. The number of new major mini-games included is disappointingly limited, with only two notable additions.To conclude, Judgment is a fantastic game that handles its main story well but stumbles a bit in its side content. Conversely, its sequel stumbles with the pacing of the main story but manages to deliver remarkable side content. What sets it apart from the mainline Yakuza series is its laser focus on the main story, which makes it stand out.

_childDocuments_.review: This was, technically, my first introduction to the Yakuza series (If you can count this game as one, which personally i do), and honestly, wow. When i was first jumping into this, i was expecting something like, L.A Noire, but with fist fighting, which i was mostly correct minus the fact that the detectiveness part wasnt exactly polished (Though spotting cats was a neat treat). Though despite that, there are couple of flaws within this game, like any other game has really.Pros:- The story is amazing. Despite the fact that sometimes the story does side track, one reason or another, the main story is just amazing.- The fighting. At first, the fighting feels... Eh, but once you start unlocking some fun stuff, by fun stuff i mean new battle EXs and such, then it becomes really neat, specially when some skills are nearly "must have" (In quotation marks), like double quickstep, Tiger Drop (Not needed but badass if you pull it off), and some other stuff like the Flux.- The graphics are really neat too. I, during the entire playthrough, never noticed i was playing with low Graphs (Prolly because i am just used to running a lesser end PCs in my life), but even with the said low Graphs, its really pretty. Though again, i am not much of a Graphics person. (Aka Gameplay over Graphics type of a person)- Side Cases & Majority of Friend Events, on the gameplay side, these two are also neat and are mostly your main source of money and SP, and trust me, you will need a decent amount of money, specially for 100%- OST, just simply look it up on Youtube, nuff said.Cons:- 100%, as much as i would LOVE to 100% the game, there are few things that are holding me back and that specific things are 1 Friendship where you need to play a game of Mahjong with special rules, Poker objectives and Shogi. Its less of a game issue and more of a skill issue, problem is, even if i knew how to play any of those, i am mostly relying on luck, as (For Poker for example) you need to win a number of chips, which absolutely relies on luck as opponents may waste their chips or play it very safe.- Mortal Wounds mechanic, its not exactly a con, its a good feature, whats not good feature is Firearms. It doesnt help that EVENTUALLY, normal enemies have guns too, and they hurt. Doesnt help that Yagami takes his time to get up (Though understandable lol).- Threat Level, god forbid whoever thought this was exactly a good idea. On paper, it sounds fine, but in practice, its annoying. To explain Threat level, after beating up a good amount of enemies or waiting some time, the Threat level will be at 100%, in order to lower it, you have either defeat the Keihin leaders (There are 4 of them, each of them having their own abilities). While Threat it up, alongside the leaders, Keihin enemies will become A LOT more common... And i mean, A LOT. To the point of annoyance. Again on paper, this sounds fine, the problem is, this feature appears on Chapter 4, and on top of that, the 100% Threat are very random and can happen pretty much any time, and boy oh boy, that any time is A LOT of time. (Also ♥♥♥♥ Koga, bro has 2 guns at 50% HP. >:( )- Tailing Missions. I dont want to put this to either a con or pro so i will just put it here as a Neutral. The Tailing missions are pretty fun at first, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, does the game overuse them. And majority of the times, they feel the same. The couple of times that it felt different is tailing more paranoid or aware characters, which trust me, its less than you think. Overall: 9/10Remember, this is all my personal opinion, some people may not share the same issues (Like my problem with Mahjong and Poker). But even so, i personally recommend getting the game. Is it worth 40$? Can be arguable, but if you are like me (A person that like to scrape by with sales), then wait out for Sale.Note: Despite it being a "2022" game, it actually came out 2021 (Remaster, not the OG that would be 2018), therefor threat this game as a 2021 game when it comes to sales.

_childDocuments_.review: Story: 6/10Gameplay: 8/10Graphics: 9/10The reason for my story rating is that I came from Yakuza looking for a similar Yakuza story. What I got was an ex-attorney turned detective solving a murder case. Typical of cold cases. If you want more cold case files or murder stories, I'd go watch a real series on a cold case or murder mystery. Its way better than this game's story even with the slight plot-twists which is to be expected of solving murder cases. What I'm saying is you might enjoy the story if you haven't binged a bunch of Cold Case stories in your life. I was able to predict most of the story and in my honest opinion, the story doesn't get good until chapter 8 or 9 out of the 13 chapters. You'll find yourself doing more of the side quests aka "case files" than the actual story where the side stories are more fun and entertaining than half the game's main story line. So I guess that makes up for it.As for the gameplay, I hated the "stalking" missions aka Pursuits. They were very boring! I felt the devs were very lazy with these missions and decided not to re-work them. If they ever update this game (which I doubt nowadays) but a mechanic needs to be added to add some fun and variety to these missions to either distract the suspect or speed up the pursuit. I felt like I was wasting my time with these missions. Personally, I'm not a fan of stealth unless they add certain mechanics to make it fun instead of playing simple stalk-hide-seek. The graphics are super clean and the game is very well optimized. I ran this game at 1440p at 120fps max settings with Nvidia DLSS at Quality with a 3090 and Ryzen 5800x3D all while recording with no hiccups. Its a beautiful game but the color tone can throw some people off as most of it is cool. There are some minor lighting issues. ex. Too bright in some areas.

_childDocuments_.review: A Fantastic Work of ArtI'm incredibly grateful to have been given a chance to experience all the hard work, mastery, artistry, and inspiration that went into Judgment. It really was a journey worth taking.I particularly appreciated the dramatic character moments, the way the story twisted and turned, and the excellently realized Kamurocho and all of its hustle and bustle.I found the battle system to be somewhat lackluster compared to some of the other entries in the Yakuza game world. The progression system in particular felt a little too free for my liking. I would love to have a leveling system that allows my character to become better at certain skills based on how often they practice and use said skills in fights. I'd also like to rely on my own mastery of these skills more often. Fights against large numbers usually devolved into grabbing and pressing triangle repeatedly. Fights against stronger opponents usually devolved into picking up objects and pressing triangle repeatedly. Sometimes I might have had to dodge and sometimes press R1. Maybe I should have set the game to a harder mode than normal. That said, I never really felt that bored by the battle system. I did feel a bit bored playing through some of the monotonous tailing missions. At first they are an interesting way to explore the city. But after a while it just becomes too tedious. The mini-games in this entry were lacking compared to the other two Yakuza games I've played, 0 and Like a Dragon. Big props for the dating simulation in the game though. The three that I played through felt really inspired and well-written. I do kind of wish that Yagami's love interest would have played a role in the main story line but, oh well. Speaking of the story, I'm pretty pleased by it. Some of it was maybe a bit too predictable, while other parts not as much. At the end of the game, though, I was thoroughly enthused by how everything came together. Except why did it have to be alzheimers? I would think that a cancer drug might have been a bit more important. Either way, it provided enough of a cover for our villains to do what they ultimately weren't actually justified in doing.The story of Yagami is one for people who haven't given up on doing their best to change the world for the better. It's not for the cynical. Sure, maybe it's also a power fantasy for those of us who might be able to change the world if we didn't have to worry about the retribution of violence from evil. If we could fight our way out of every conflict maybe we would. But even though Yagami has to fight many times, he never really becomes consumed by violence or a need for revenge. His fights are righteous and he never even so much as picks up a knife or sword. Maybe in that way, Yagami might even be a little too good in that he never even seems tempted to listen to the possibility of darker actions. But then the story would be something entirely different.Thanks for the huge discount. It was worth every baht. Now, I've got a cat to catch.
