_childDocuments_.review: Tldr; main story 2/10, side content 8/10I hated this story, worst one out of the 5 yakuza games i've played and generally liked for their main stories. Yakuza games are normally pretty realistic with the drama presented in their main stories (or at least that is the impression that i got), but I could not stand how unrealistic any of the court situations were in this game. Some examples: People literally monologuing from the audience, evidence being brought in mid case and ACCEPTED???, the attorneys cutting each other off in the middle of the opposing side's statements, attorneys unaware that there even was certain pieces of evidence submitted, etc... the list goes on and on and on about how cringe worthy these scenarios were.This story also had the worst pacing i've seen in a Yakuza game leading me to not care about the characters. My main gripe is from the way the beginning of the game was structured. There was a flashback that was half way through the story, but i wish it was put into the beginning of the game because it tells you no new information and gave more of a backstory to the main character.BUT i still give this game my recommendation because all of the side content was great (except for the tailing portions of the missions, not a fan). _childDocuments_.review: Judgment proves itself as a standout addition to the Yakuza series, with its most prominent strength lying in its gripping narrative. It strikes a balance, delivering complexity and unexpected twists without veering into the labyrinthine territory of some mainline Yakuza titles.The side quests, an integral part of the Yakuza experience, are also mostly very enjoyable. The sub-stories revolve around Yagami, taking on various detective cases and making you feel like a man with work to do rather than just being a local errand boy. While Judgment excels in many areas, it does stumble slightly in its boss fights. These encounters lack the dramatic flair that you might expect from a Yakuza game, and the accompanying soundtracks fail to leave a lasting impression. Nonetheless, it's important to note that Yagami's identity leans more towards that of a detective rather than a brawler, and this aspect is reflected in the gameplay. Sadly, the detective elements suffer from an excessive amount of hand-holding, making them feel less challenging than they could have been.Overall Judgement is a game with great characters, a great story, and is an entry to the franchise that should not be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil 8 manages to be a beautiful, visual masterpiece, while including overwhelmingly campy writing. With these factors in mind, it personally sorted itself out for me as a horror/comedy in its story. Take that as you will; personally I loved.However, one thing that I must stress to my very core is the very real passion, love, and care that went into crafting this game. It may not have enough horror, depending on your taste, and some people may dislike the heavy emphasis on the action aspect of the game.But as continue to play through the game, you'll realize the delicate structuring of every detail that was put into this piece of art. Every area within this game is so stupidly detailed with the new RE engine, and it can't be praised enough for it's style. And, personally, I think its cheesy writing makes a hilariously bad/good story.Could it have done better in some spots, definitely, but when you compare this game to overwhelming amount of cash grabs out there, you'll learn to cherish this fun and replayable experience!I should also mention that I played this game on a Dell Inspiron laptop with integrated graphics and a Ryzen 7, and it still looked visually stunning (with 60 fps in closed, indoor areas, and slightly dipping in outdoor areas). This really speaks about Capcom's desire to optimize this game as much as they could for their audience, and I think that should be well known.

_childDocuments_.review: Judgment, a spin-off from the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series, takes a decidedly different approach to the usual crime-brawling hijinks by placing you on the other side of the law. As Takayuki Yagami, a formerly successful attorney turned private investigator, you are tasked with investigating and attempting to keep the peace in the rowdy streets of Kamurocho.The story quickly evolves into a grand conspiracy involving wonder drugs, government handouts, real estate tycoons, and hitmen. Despite the grandiose plot threads, the overall narrative is more grounded in its presentation than past Yakuza/Like a Dragon games. Yagami is not Kiryu; his reputation doesn't strike fear in the faces of the Yakuza, so the whole experience feels a bit tamer. You're not partaking in over-the-top ritualistic duels of honor, but rather investigating crime scenes and fighting street thugs. I enjoyed this take, but personally missed the larger-than-life personalities and intense set pieces of the Yakuza series, although the cast of Judgment is still very likable.The beat-em-up brawler style combat returns, feeling classic and a bit wild at times. Yagami has two fighting styles: the Crane style for more group-oriented fights, which feels a lot like Majima's Y0 overall acrobatic stylings, and the Tiger style, which is unique to Yagami. Slower with hard strikes, the Tiger style's combo speed escalates as you progress. Both styles feel good, but the overall combat feels floaty, and you can lose control of the flow as Yagami bounces around the combat scenario, off walls and through the air. In some ways, it feels like an improvement from past Yakuza games, with enhanced animations and a more rhythm-based feel as you build combos. However, it also feels less grounded as fights can get away from you due to Yagami's wilder, floatier movements.A few new gameplay additions provide freshness to the overall experience. The city reputation and relationship levels are a nice way to introduce staggered story arcs for the interesting new characters around Kamurocho. Maxing out these friendships and relationships, and by association leveling your city reputation, introduces novel ways to change the city. Friends will be found roaming the streets, jumping in to assist you in combat, or giving you gifts. It's a clever way to alter the city based on your actions, and it is satisfying.Also present are a few new mini-games, notably a drone racing mini-game. The drone also plays a part in navigating through Kamurocho to complete investigations. Furthermore, there are some lock-picking-like mini-games and tailing mechanics that complement the detective/investigative aspect of the game. Overall, the side content is a bit of a letdown; there are fewer mini-games and an overabundance of forgettable side-cases.In conclusion, Judgment is good. I respect that RGG attempted to do something different and steer away from the baggage of the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series. It's a testament to their ability to take the familiar and reinvent it. However, I don't think Judgment did enough to stand on its own against its predecessors.

_childDocuments_.review: Judgment is easily the worst Yakuza/Like A Dragon game, with a lot of repetitive busy work that really doesn't add anything to the game and combat that just feels objectively worse than even Yakuza 6, which this game is effectively a mod for. I'd rate it even under Yakuza 5, which is saying something.The main problem, as I mentioned, is the busy work. There are a couple of frequently used minigames, some of which I have a hard time understanding why they exist. A good example is the keyring minigame: any time you have to unlock a door with a key, you have to sort through the protagonist's key ring to find the right key.. even if you've already opened that door before. The problem is that one of the doors you need a key for is the door to the protagonist's office... which is kind of laughable. Granted, there is an upgrade you can buy for fairly cheap that removes the key minigame on doors you've already nlocked, but it's baffling that anyone at Sega thought it was a good idea. Similarly annoying is the tailing minigame, which is used pretty frequently and consists of moving from cover to cover and then falling asleep because even though most of them are a couple of minutes long, they feel like they drag on forever.The combat is also not great - it's very floaty, and every time your character gets hit, he ragdolls to the ground and you have to mash X to get back up. The ragdoll animation takes approximately forever, and it's just annoying as hell to watch after the first couple of times. There is also an upgrade that makes it much harder to get ragdolled, but again, it's a question of why they'd even put that in the game in the first place. On top of that, the boss fights all kind of suck because of the addition of "deadly attacks", which are unblockable and reduce your maximum HP until you see a doctor or use a specific item you can only carry two of. The intended counter to this is to use "extreme heat mode" or whatever it's called where you can press R2 and become invincible, which honestly kinda sucks. Granted, you can get the Tiger Drop as early as the middle of Chapter 1 if you feel like it, and the Tiger Drop does in fact work against deadly attacks (because it's the best move in every Yakuza game it's been in) but the whole thing just feels like a dumb and bad idea.I'd say only consider getting this one on sale, and only if you've already exhausted every other game in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Judgement is a mixed bag for me. I like a lot of what it does, but it has a few big issues that stop it from being one of my favourite RGG titles.For the good: The story is fantastic once it gets going. It's a nice mystery story with some amazing moments near the end. However, there is A LOT of filler. The main story is stuffed with cutscenes where our main cast sits down and sloooooowly discusses what you just heard from a different character, and the first half of the game is so slow with very little progression towards the actual mystery. The finale is one of the best in the series, but the lead up to it is painful.The gameplay is great. It may have taken a few games but RGG finally figured out how to make combat on the Dragon Engine work. The only negative is the annoying "mortal wounds" system. Basically, if you take a hit or get shot, you get a chunk of your health bar permanently removed until you use a med kit or see a doctor. It's not a big deal, but it still adds more running around you have to do.The only other bad thing I can say is that the encounter rate is WAY TOO HIGH. The game has a system where everyone once in a while, the city will be put on "high alert" and encounter rates will triple until you beat a few bosses. It was fun at first but as the hours dragged on it got very annoying very quickly, and there's no way to disable it.Overall, if you liked the Yakuza series, you'll probably like this one too. It's got the same style and presentation, just with a more mature story.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is set in the  Extended Universe and very much follows on from the previous  titles with real-time combat. What I'm trying to say is that whether or not you like the  "formula" is almost certainly going to determine whether or not you like this game. If not, you are unlikely to get any enjoyment out of this title. If you do though, it's really more of the same good stuff you like. The "investigation" elements, if you can call them that, feel extremely shallow. None of the dialogue choices actually make any difference; getting the wrong answer in the main story just prompts Yagami to try again. Apart from getting to zero health, the only other way to get a Game Over is if one gets caught during a tailing/photograph sequence. As you can imagine, the tailing sequences themselves are somewhat tedious, involving walking behind someone and taking cover when they look backwards. So, it's safe to say that this is definitely not a big genre-bend from the previous  games.Of course, the most important things in the  "formula" are enjoyable fighting, plentiful side quests/mini games, and side-splitting sub stories. Well, this certainly doesn't disappoint in that regard. The fighting has been tweaked somewhat so that Yagami is more of a glass cannon than previous fighting characters, and so are the enemies. This means fewer health bars to break through, but equally it means your own health must be kept in check. It makes for a faster-paced gameplay style, and I do quite like it, even if it is more challenging. As with the characters in the recent  titles, Yagami is able to switch between fighting styles. There are only two of them here, which reduces the variety somewhat, but also makes things a bit simpler. The "mortal wounds" element is an attempt to mix things up, but it's just a bit of a pain in all honesty. It's all too easy to get hit with one from a gunman right after the start of a random battle, forcing a trip to the underground doctor and goodbye to 20 grand. The Keihin Gang is also somewhat annoying. I wouldn't mind fighting these guys every so often, but it seems you're getting a call from Kim about them every 5 minutes or so that they're back in town. There's no real story arc with them either; it's basically just a way of farming materials needed for making "extracts," which is another new thing added into this game. At least extracts do have their uses, so it may be worth collecting the materials for them if you find they help you out, or you are just a completionist.Any slight disappointments in the battle system though are made up by the fantastic story this game has, including all the various investigations you can do, with genuine laugh-out-loud moments. All of the characters are really nicely written, and I just think they did a really fantastic job of it. In conclusion, this game is absolutely worth getting if you want a slight twist on the old  formula with a great story and enjoyable gameplay. Steer clear however, if you are wanting to play a game that's truly in the "investigation" genre. Recommended, 75%.

_childDocuments_.review: (full review with screenshots:  ) Judgment is the beginning of the Yakuza series' move away from that name and its focus on, well, the yakuza. You play as a private detective/lawyer who is not and has never been an actual yakuza member, but who still has close ties with one particular family. The story and gameplay similarly sit somewhere between being about and not about the yakuza - they play a major role in the plot and much of the gameplay revolves around beating them up, but at the same time you can play for hours just doing detective tasks and dealing with civilians. The two main shakeups to the gameplay are the addition of various detective-y activities and a bunch of new minigames. The detective stuff consists of activities like tailing suspects, looking for clues in the environment, and dialogue-based interrogations. None of this stuff is ever very hard, and it honestly probably wouldn't have been interesting at all if not for the series' trademark bonkers writing constantly intervening to surprise you. The minigames, meanwhile, are a very eclectic bunch. Drone racing and a VR Mario Party-esque games are the main ones, and the latter is meant to be your main source of income since there's no business minigame. I found both of these a bit tedious because of slow movement in VR and excessive grinding for crafting resources with drones, but they're fun for a bit. Most of my time with minigames was with the batting cages, darts, and Outrun! cabinet. Outside of those changes, you'd be hard pressed to notice that this wasn't another normal Yakuza game just from watching gameplay. Most of your time will be spent on crazy sidequests that almost always end in combat or in street encounters against the bizarrely combative denizens of Kamurocho. The sidequests are nearly all fun, but several of them are frustratingly locked behind completing grindy NPC quests that require finding random resources or grinding casino chips to buy paintings. Combat is similarly fun when its new, but random events that spawn Keihin Gang leaders all over the map happen maddeningly frequently in the later stages of the game. Beating up those leaders is fun the first few times, but it's a lot less entertaining when you're fighting the same guy for the 30th time. It'd get a lot easier to differentiate the games if a cutscene starts playing, though. Most of the major characters in Judgment are either lawyers at the Genda Law Office or prosecutors working opposite you on a case, and typically your immediate concern is collecting evidence to exonerate your client on a case. The result is something that's half Phoenix Wright and half Yakuza. It's definitely not realistic, but it is thoroughly entertaining.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Rush through story mode when playing, ignore minigames, avoid any uninteresting friendships and substories, and make sure to upgrade attack and abuse exheat to avoid all the slop and slog. And always take taxis everywhere to avoid random encountersMight be my least favorite RGG game to date. Story and main characters are good but I genuinely hated playing this game past the halfway mark and the gameplay only gets worse as you play more. Yagami (theoretically) has a great repertoire of moves but then you'll get punished for doing something as basic as your rush combo because he'll randomly get staggered and enemies will shrug off his attacks. Block staggering is also still in from Y6 and K2. Crane style.Throws, unlike most Yakuza games, leave you vulnerable and have poor crowd control so you will get punished for attempting to throw one guy at a group of guys. Game has some of the driest and least entertaining side content since Yakuza 1 on the PS2. Most of it is either bland or outright sucks. Tailing missions, Dice and Cube, lock picking, choosing your key to open doors, tailing missions again. Only standout thing is Drone racing, which is okay. Mortal wounds are probably one of the worst mechanics ever devised. In theory, it makes sense to punish players for reckless play and going through whole setpieces by thugging them out with healing items. In practice? Oop, you got shot once in a random encounter so you know have to either fork up tens of thousands of yen for medkits or go to the most remote corner of the map for a check up. Why did they do it like this? This was a problem in the original game, you'd think a remaster would make medkits purchasable at more places, let you carry more of them/make them cheaper, let Yagami heal up at home, or have wounds not persist through street encounters. And speaking of street encounters, the Keihin gang makes walking through town a slog because there will be boss stationed in several parts of the map and goons will be at literally every corner. No way to mitigate this, so I hope you like running away from goons or fighting every few feet.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a must-play if you enjoy the Yakuza franchise. Although it deviates slightly from the normal Yakuza formula, the changes and unique gameplay make it worth your time.The main strong point of Judgment is definitely the story. Although technically a spin-off from the Yakuza games, it still manages to have one of the most immersive, enjoyable, and strongest story in the whole franchise. I was entirely immersed and invested from the introduction all the way to the credits. The story was so enjoyable to experience that I neglected parts of the game like the drone racing mini-game just to progress through and see what happens next. While Judgment doesn't feature the beloved characters of the main games, it adds a whole new cast of memorable and in-depth characters which really make the story come to life and adds a new fresh feel to the game. Combat is also very enjoyable and has a different feel and pace to the main Yakuza games. Yagami has two fighting styles that can be used in combat, both being very unique and different to Kiryu's fighting style. Rather than a strong and grounded playstyle, Yagami favours speed and agility similarly to Majima. Very fun to use Yagami's moveset while jumping on enemies and walls.Visuals are also stunning and really top off the experience. The dragon engine allows the game to look realistic and have beautiful lighting and graphics while not being that intensive. Really breathes life into Kamurocho. However, physics can be questionable at times.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily my favorite game that I've played from Ryu Ga Gotoku so far. Having played the Yakuza games from 0 to 5 Remastered, it's clear that RGG really wanted to push the mold with this game and they executed it really well. The story is the best I've seen from the franchise so far, with each chapter feeling like an episode in a season-long detective/mystery series. With some of the Yakuza games, the plot was either too predictable at times or relied on sudden plot twists that seemed to only exist for the sake of progressing the story without any prior set up; Judgement in my opinion doesn't have this flaw and has a coherent story the whole way through. Also, the humor in this game is legitimately some of RGG's best work yet, as there were a lot of times I burst out laughing at what was on screen, both in the main story and the side cases. The Dragon Engine they use for the game makes everything look stunning at maxed settings, and I found the combat really enjoyable all the way through. Side note: RGG usually has a heavy fight-choreo segments during boss battles, but they tend to put quick time events in said segments which prevented me from actually enjoying the moves the characters were making; from what I remember every fight-choreo segment for the bosses only had a single button input at the end of them so it feels like you're watching an action movie. Also the Yakuza bosses typically feel like shield/combo maniacs, ie impossible to hit unless you cheese them (tiger drop), but I never felt that being a huge issue in this game. Where I think the game really shines is the world-building, as there are so many side cases and friends to meet with many of them actually having great stories to tell/experience. RGG has always had a plethora of interesting substories in the Yakuza games, and the side cases are for the most part very engaging and worth going through. Overall enjoyed every minute till the end, and making this the first RGG game that I plan on 100% completing.(Edit): Recently found out that in chapter 5  Just some neat subtle characterization that I really appreciated.

_childDocuments_.review: Judgement is a curious addition to the Like A Dragon series.The first spin off to make it to the West. Although technically not the first new leading man to hit the streets of Kamuro. It had some pretty serious shoes to fill even before Ichiban came to fill them proper. On top of that, it was a serious expansion to the world, being entirely from the perspective of one very much on the side of the law.To say that Takayuki Yagami had a big dragon shaped shadow over him is... honestly a bit of a over-dramatization. Yagami is very much is own character, with his own game plan. And most importantly a vastly different game play.To start things off, I'd like to firmly state that the Story of this game was a ride I thoroughly enjoyed, the ups and downs of the games plot were kept consistent and entertaining the entire ride. and frankly I enjoyed seeing a protagonist try to fight and live through Kamuro's worst without being Legendarily strong like Kiryu, Majima, Saejima and Akiyama. It felt like the story could end for Yagami at any turn. (well, sort of, it is a LaD game afterall)The Mystery and detective game play had me hooked in between fights. I liked deducting the truth out of a situation, it genuinely felt like I was playing an Ace Attorney game at some points! Although honestly, I could do without the safe cracking mini-game. I have tourettes and that ♥♥♥♥ makes my thumbs want to seppuku. This is easily remedied with simply swapping to a mouse on low sensitivity however. As well, having to use key's with the key ring mechanic was simply unnecessary and a really dumb idea. Otherwise, I have definitely had worse experiences with a mystery themed game, I could probably play a whole game of just detecting through buildings like this.As far as the combat goes, honestly, it wasn't terrible. Yagami's Tiger style carried the entire game on it's back, frankly. By end game, the Tiger Style had so many exclusive upgrades, techniques and strengths, that Crane's entire purpose became 'Heat Mode' clean up of low HP mooks. Thanks to the Dragon Engine, used in Kiwami 2 and Yakuza 6, every action and movement is heavy, sluggish, and punishes you heavily for landing hits on blocking opponents. This leads to the Crane, in it's woefully under-powered state, effectively incapable of taking on 1 enemy, let alone it's purpose of taking on large crowds; simply because by the time you are evn half way into a string, you'll likely get blocked by one of the many enemies and another will hit you out of your combo. Something the Tiger style also performs better in, given it's state of basically being Brawler and Dragon Style if it had a baby; packed with counter attacks and more guard crushing power as it gets upgraded.Continuing on with the system, I turn to the ugly step-child of the mechanics, the Mortal Wound system. Or as I called it 'HP Tax'. When attacked by a boss during an enrage mechanic or when simply shot with a gun. Yagami gets blown away, and with it, anywhere between a chip, to over half his health bar is cut away and left un-healable without a shockingly pricey purchase of direct healing or even more ludicrously expensive first aid kits (nearly a quarter million Yen for a full heal?? you srrs??). These first aid kits are only obtained from a merchant in the sewers, which is an annoyingly repetitive trip to do if you don't wish to pony up double the cost for a first aid kit. I sincerely hope Lost Judgement has scrapped this obnoxious tax mechanic. With a note of the combat system, the upgrade system has once again changed massively from it's predecessors (probably the only justified reason for it, given its spin off status). Seeing Yagami investing Skill Points (SP) he gains from basically everything into skills of three catagories. Raw Stats, Combat Skills and Life Skills. Raw stats are required to unlock most skills, at least to the 2nd of three tiers, they are essential to have to make your admittedly lacking power quickly get a boost. Combat skills are techniques, style specific (read: Tiger Style Only) power ups, and of course Heat Actions. Which there are admittedly a lot of very lovely heat actions Yagami can pull off, given his much swifter nature than Kiryu, or even Akiyama for a better comparison. Finally, Life Skills, ranging from improved control with your drone, improved detective skills, better charisma with friends and girlfriends (There is four options and the game does not punish nor rewards being monogamous or making a harem (to my knowledge) out side of achievements) and the most pointless skills, like smoking. My biggest gripe with the games upgrades is simply: there is not enough SP in the world. The amount of SP you gain from just about everything is a pittance of a pittance; we are talking 100 SP at a time sometimes where some of the late game upgrades are 10k or more! The game actively expect you to grind to get the last few expensive skills, or for you to avoid the smaller options and save up. It's insane. It's almost Kiwami 2 levels of grindy because of that. I simply refused to play the board game side content to pay for SP drinks to round out my skills.Weird nitpick before moving on: There is a weird lack of healing items in this game. I had to rely on many small food items simply because there was no upgrades to the usual heal and heat drinks. The only 'upgrades' to heals were the pointlessly expensive first aid kits; and weirdly the aforementioned SP drinks. Why the sudden shortage of fancy drinks? The game already limited the usuals to 6 per slot, and by end game they barely heal a 3rd of Yagami's health bar. It's bizarre. To summarize this of my many long winded reviews of the Like a Dragon Series: Judgement is a very good game among it's peers. It has it's own identity, and as much as I hated the system, the wounds did make Yagami feel like less of an unstoppable fighting machine, and more like a skilled detective, one shot or stab wound away from critical injury. I still think the system needs to be dropped or refined though. This story of a Mystery surrounded by a theme of being true to your justice, to your companions and ultimately too yourself; it's an instant classic, that earns it's place beside it's titan of a cousin. The combat system is inherently flawed, a trait I hold firmly to the janky, sluggish nature of the Dragon Engine more than not. But fun, and makes you feel like a badass, fighting hordes, with a true friend at your side through most of the story and side content.This game's Amon was a stupid boss tho. it turned a game of patience into a tedious DBZ back and forth trying to juggly your heat bar. Really stupid.Kaito is best daddy/10

_childDocuments_.review: Judgment is a third person action game, and a spin off from the Yakuza series, which again takes place in the Kamurocho area of Tokyo. When a Tojo clan captain is accused of murdering a rival gang member, player character Takayuki Yagami, an ex-lawyer turned private investigator, is hired to find evidence proving his innocence, only to become drawn into a much larger conspiracy.•	Gameplay is very similar to the Yakuza games, so if you’ve already played any of those, this will feel familiar.•	Combat takes place in real time (like Kiryu’s games, not Like a Dragon’s turn based system). You’ll have to beat up enemies with combos of punches and kicks, you can grab and throw enemies, pick up objects like bikes and traffic cones to use as weapons, dodge or block enemy attacks, and successful hits will build up your special meter allowing you to perform various powerful finishing moves.•	Combat is easier than most of the Yakuza games. After a couple of hours I put the difficulty up to hard, and even then the mobs that wander Kamurocho were quite trivial to defeat. The scripted story encounters and boss fights were more challenging, but I was able to win most fights on the first try.•	As Yagami investigates the case you’ll need to use his detective skills in various ways. Search crime scenes for clues, reveal evidence during interrogations, stealthily follow suspects as they slowly walk around half the city, and perform QTEs during chase sequences.•	In addition to main story quests, the open world contains lots of other content. There are side missions where Yagami takes PI cases such as investigating a cheating husband, protecting a client from creepy stalkers, or finding a missing person. Meanwhile many of the shop owners will ask you to help them deal with their problems.•	If you want to take a break from beating up thugs, there are lots of fun minigames to play. Many of them have appeared in the Yakuza games, including darts, baseball, poker, blackjack, shogi, mahjong and classic Sega arcade games. Judgment also contains a few new games such as drone racing, an on rails shooter called Kamuro Of The Dead, and a VR dice game.•	As usual the story is excellent, and well written. Yagami is a strong main character, his companions are all very likeable, and there are lots of other interesting characters including Yakuza, lawyers, cops, journalists and scientists. There’s so much detail, honestly the storytelling in these games is better than a lot of TV shows.•	Main story cutscenes look very cinematic.•	Main quest is fully voiced, and the voice acting is high quality, but the side quests are text only.•	While the main story has a serious tone, many of the side quests feature the Yakuza games’ typical wacky scenarios.•	It took me 57 hours to finish the main story and around 70% of side quests.•	I didn’t have any problems with crashes or framerate.•	Controls work well most of the time on my Xbox 360 gamepad, although it took me a while to get used to dodge / quick step requiring you to press both RB + A (I’m sure in previous games it was just the A button). And the two lockpicking minigames are almost impossible using gamepad thumbsticks, so I had to use mouse and keyboard for more precise control.•	While searching crime scenes, a couple of the clues where so small that these scenes turned into pixel hunts as I moved the cursor over every inch of the screen, still didn’t find anything (even with the ability which makes the gamepad vibrate when you’re hovering over the correct area) and I actually had to consult a guide to progress.•	The game seems to be in a permanent tutorial mode, as after every fight you’ll see a message appear in the bottom corner of the screen offering you hints about things you’ve already done dozens of times, and I couldn’t find any way to disable this.Judgment is a great game, the gameplay is mostly enjoyable despite a few small annoyances, and the story is excellent. There’s plenty of content to justify a full price purchase.There’s no connection to story or characters of the main Yakuza series, so if you’re interested in these games but don’t want to catch up on 8 games worth of lore, this would be a good starting point.

_childDocuments_.review: "Hey guys, what haven't we done better than Shenmue yet?""...Detective work?""Great idea! Let's make a whole game out of it!"This is the best RGG game since Yakuza 0. It feels like all the best minds at RGG got together, listed out all the cool thing a past Yakuza game has done, and iterated on all of it in one game. Every element of this game feeds into other elements. The friend mechanic from Yakuza 2 is taken to its logical conclusion here. Friends help you out around town, give you discounts, and even lead you to additional friends with their own substories. Remember the "Murder at Cafe Alps" substory in Yakuza 3, where you had to link people, places, and information together to figure out what happened? This entire game is built around that idea. I've had several instances where I didn't know where to go, so I talked to someone I had met in a past substory or friend mission, and they actually gave me useful advice. This is a detective game that actively rewards my intuition. If you're somewhat familiar with Kamurocho, try playing with the minimap turned off. The game often gives you enough details to figure out where to go without the marker.The core of the combat here is really good. Your moves usually have great impact, the animations are extremely fluid, and the heat actions are satisfying. Yagami's Crane style is the coolest thing since Majima's Slugger style in 0. The combat is more slow and deliberate than past titles. Your rush combo loops indefinitely, and every finisher has multiple parts. This encourages you to slow down and think about which attacks you're using, rather than spamming a full rush combo and whatever the last finisher is.I do have several criticisms.Context sensitive combat actions don't always work right. Wall jumps sometimes result in Yagami just flying off and attacking nothing. Flux fissures sometimes just don't trigger. This seems most common after an enemy is staggered, which is particularly annoying because that feels like the best opening for a flux fissure.Mortal wounds just shouldn't exist. They only slow down the combat, waste your money, and waste your time running across town to get them fixed. Wall jumps are recommended to attack through them, which makes it doubly annoying when your wall jump just doesn't hit the enemy.The English voice acting isn't great. One, a lot of the background and combat voices are still in Japanese. Two, some of the casting choices are questionable, most notably Yagami himself. Yagami's Japanese voice is husky and tired sounding, which fits his character. His English voice is the most generic white dude imaginable. Three, when the casting choice is good (like with Nanami), the direction isn't great. Scenes that should be full of emotion come off as awkward and stilted. I wouldn't normally even mention the voice acting, but English is enabled by default in this game (unlike previous titles, where it wasn't even an option).All that said, the only thing stopping this from being my favorite game in the franchise is the combat being a little sloppy in places. This game is incredible, and if you've enjoyed any other Yakuza game, you need to try this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Judgement is what it looks like - you play as a Japanese detective, who rolls around Tokyo in his leather jacket and bounces thugs on his way to solving a murder mystery together with his buddies. But how does it play?An ambitious title emerging from Sega's acclaimed Yakuza pedigree, Judgement combines many things, mostly with success.The core story is a neo-Noir tale of grizzly violence, personal conflict, hard choices, and high corruption; and the core gameplay is a stylized beat-them-up. Both are a joy to play and experience. The protagonist oozes kakkoii (Japanese cool), and the combat stays crunchy well beyond the 20 hours of the main plot.In addition to the streamlined Noir story, we have an off-beat open world along the lines of GTA but without driving or guns. You run around urban Tokyo, play mini-games, recharge health at restaurants, collect cats, make friends, date waifus, and solve wacky side quests. Though I enjoyed a few of the side quests, I was not quite sold on this open world adventure, since it diluted and padded the playthrough and introduced some tonal dissonance.In terms of graphics and performance, the Yakuza engine runs great on mid-range machines including the Deck, with the characters looking excellent and the world decent. Though the English dubbing is top notch, it's fun to switch to the Japanese voicing.So overall, I rate the core game 10/10, the open world padding 8/10, and Judgement as a package a solid 9/10. Looking forward to checking out the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: One of RGG's best games to date. Judgment takes the best parts from Yakuza/Like A Dragon series and add its own touch, with detective gadgets, investigation sections, etc. While the detective sections can be better, it does a good job in making players into Yagami's line of thinking.The combat is somewhat perfected in Judgment with lots of combos, varied enemies and just generally great feel to it. While it does feel slow at first, when certain skills are unlocked, Yagami becomes really enjoyable to play, becoming a master martial artist from just a rookie in the earlier chapters.Kamurocho is much more fleshed out now due to Friend Events where a huge numbers of npc can be befriended, some tells their own stories, some act like its own substories and some can even be teammates in random battles. This and with the usual substories (now named side cases) make Kamurocho such a well-crafted city. Judgment's story it one of RGG's best. It starts quite slow and eventually one case turns to another and then turns into a huge conspiracy where everything is gray, not really knowing what's really right and wrong. It's such a great well written, directed and acted story. The games does an amazing job in fleshing out its characters with believable motivations so when later on they clash with one another, the tension is believable. It makes the fights a battle of ideologies. As a detective story, it is amazing. As a thriller crime game, what a phenomenal one at that.Yagami is also the most fitting protagonist for Judgment. an ex lawyer turned detective, he gives the game much more grounded feeling and his actions are believable. All the other supporting characters have their own highlights that they become like a real person with flaws and motivations.Judgment, however, does stumble a bit when it comes to tailing missions and its implementations of Mortal Wounds, but its strengths far outweighs its weakness. Judgment makes me think about what is right and wrong ethically while also makes me feel sympathy, anger, sadness and guilt in its characters. Incredible game

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun spinoff of the Yakuza (Ryu ga Gotoku) series that puts you into the shoes of an ex-lawyer turned detective in Kamurocho. Yagami has 2 unique fighting styles that, in my opinion, feel quite smooth to use in comparison to the standard Yakuza gameplay.  An overall engaging story, dialogue, and characters makes this an entertaining entry into the series, but unfortunately the game dissuaded me from participating in the side content as much.That is because of the new tailing mechanic they added, where you follow someone without being spotted.  Many if the side missions/cases you can deal with require you to tail someone, and it is quite boring.  You'll spend much time walking slowly, angling the camera around walls, staring at an NPC while they glance behind themselves over and over or walk around a corner and wait to trick you into failing the mission.  It really is dull, and made me prioritize completing the main story over interacting with the side content.  Luckily, it is not necessary to complete much of it to be able to complete the game, even on Hard.  Despite the boring tailing challenges, I mainly enjoyed my time with the game and found it fresh enough to enjoy, regardless of this being merely the most recent in a long line of Yakuza games I have completed.

_childDocuments_.review: Judgment is a brilliant effort in forging a new path forwards for Kamurocho and its denizens post-Yakuza, with not only a new protagonist and story, but an entirely new genre and look at the world. I can't help but laugh at some of the ridiculous things that these developers come up with for side quests.To be honest, I wasn't sure how I'd feel playing a completely new protagonist in Yagami, as I've been so attached to the Yakuza series for a long time now, and getting to experience this world through Kiryu throughout the last few years, I was worried that I might feel a little biased in that regard, and possibly not enjoy this game as much due to this. I'm happy to say that I was wrong. Yagami shows so much character and personality, and to see how strong of a bond he shares with those around him, as well as how he chooses to bear the weight of responsibility of his past, was extremely moving at the most critical moments, to say the least. This is such a fresh experience, and easily is able to stand on its own as a standalone series. I only have a couple of gripes about the game in general, but they're nothing that ever discouraged me from wanting to play the game. First off, though I'll say the vast majority of the detective aspect of this game was super fun and appealing, the tailing missions are a little bit...awkward. In the sense that maybe it could have been designed slightly differently as far as being punished when an NPC realizes that you're tailing them. You can in most instances, literally run up to someone, they'll notice you and start watching you nonstop, until you find a hiding spot. As long as you find a hiding spot, it didn't matter how close you were to the person, if you were running at them or not, everything would be OK. They'll say something like "Must've just been my imagination...", and eventually be on their merry way, and the tracking bar eventually goes back down to zero like nothing ever happened. It was always just a little too easy to get through these, is all. I still enjoyed the experience, as it's something that was entirely new, but it was a little bit awkwardly executed, I feel.My other gripe is how often a certain group of people come to Kamurocho, and how often a certain someone texts you to let you know, "Oh, they're here! It's awful!" "We need you to stop them!", so on and so forth. Didn't matter how many times you took care of these guys, this stuff here is the only thing that got particularly annoying and repetitive, and I wish it would have been approached slightly differently. Maybe eventually this stops? I'm not sure because as of the point that I finished the main story (the time of writing this review), I haven't done all side quests, etc, so I can't be for certain. I guess more than anything being texted by the same individual over and over for the exact same thing while doing other quests and such was a bit frustrating, particularly when I was going through the main story, as it always felt quite distracting at those times.All in all, I have to say that if you enjoy the Yakuza series/world in general, and are eyeing this series as a possible purchase, absolutely do so. It's strong enough to easily hold on its own, and I'm looking forward to enjoying more from the Judgment series in the future. Speaking of...about to get into Lost Judgment today, absolutely can't wait.

_childDocuments_.review: Judgment is slightly different than the usual Yakuza games and I loved it. Main differences are the "crime drama" tone of the story, the detective's different kind of activities (such as tailing, lockpicking, drone flying, taking pictures etc.), substories becoming side cases and the fact that getting money is harder and more realistic. It took me some time to get used to the new protagonist, Takayuki Yagami, but he turned out to be a fantastic character (Kiryu is still the n.1 though). The story was very intriguing until the last chapter. I'm not going to spoil anything, those who completed the story will understand what I'm talking about, but there are a lot of poorly staged twists at the end (some don't even make sense) as well few characters changing their motivations in a split second. Another surprisingly bad thing is combat, which only features two styles (for 1vs1 and vs multiple enemies) and doesn't include enough skills, so it really becomes repetitive in the long run. While not perfect, it's way better than the latest Yakuza - Like a Dragon in my opinion. I really enjoyed my time exploring Kamurocho as a sexy detective.

_childDocuments_.review: Similar in the style to the other Yakuza/Like a Dragon games, Judgement instead follows disgraced-ex-lawyer-now-detective Yagami as he tries to unravel the cause behind serial killings in Kamurocho. Along the way, with the support of a large variety of characters and in typical RGG fashion, his sleuthing reveals that the reason behind the killings isn't as simple as originally thought.The game is honestly a 10/10 in the body of an 8/10. The story is fantastic, characters are all equally as fantastic, and this is the best the city has looked so far. However, the game has several fundamental issues that drag the score down. Combat is a big mixed bag for me. When you first start the game, the combat is likely the second least enjoyable in the series just under Yakuza 3. It is significantly improved with upgrades to speed and EX moves, but that takes several hours to finally collect. OST wasn't as impactful as some from the prior games, but I did like a lot of the jazzy detective beats. The general story as a whole has some issues. Funny enough, it has the same issues Yakuza 3 had. The main story is very, very intriguing, but the devs have no scruples in completely veering you off course to force you to do some other side story out of the blue. Say, you’re trying to get ready to hunt a certain character down, but the devs randomly force you to figure out who ate the cake in the fridge first. These side stories are very well written, but it definitely puts the brakes on the main story’s momentum. And that happens many times throughout the game. Just like in Yakuza 3 with the orphanage sections -  being forced to do them is more tedious than anything. And it doesn't help that the game heavily reuses the tailing and chase sequences for these as well as other side cases. On their own, these sequences are pretty enjoyable. However, by the end of the game, you’ll likely end up doing them all together for dozens of times. By then, they became eye-rolling.So, issues with combat, mission structure, and the pacing of the main plot sort of drag the overall experience down. Still, the game kicks a ton of ass.

_childDocuments_.review: Another game by Ryuu Ga Gotoku studio (RGG), much like its better known "Yakuza" series.Overall, more of the same so if you liked Yakuzas this will not be a miss.Action game with a lot of fighting, and a lot less detective/lawyer-work.It is nice to see the studio try to branch into different game styles, but personally, I just found this to be more or less like the other Yakuza games.There is a big overarching conspiracy that the protagonist is trying to solve, and the main way protagonist does that is through being a basically unstoppable fighter.You would think they would tone it down with the protagonist being a lawyer/detective, but that does not seem to be the case as Yagami (the protagonist) is honestly comparable to Kiryu, and even learns one of his signature moves just like that.Most of the answers Yagami has to beat out of others, yet the game tries to play his combat prowess off.There are a few cases where Yagami tries to avoid danger by saying "but they have an army in there" or "it's too dangerous", despite having a proven track record of being basically unstoppable, and the game basically throwing you into such situations anyway.Really, the only thing holding him back is the new mechanic of "mortal wounds" which is a type of permanent damage that requires a doctor or an actual medkit to heal (of which you get a very limited amount you can carry), but on a normal casual playthrough it does not seem to be a very limiting factor, so carrying a whole shop's worth of food is still a viable strat.I guess on this note, I will also mention that I was not particularly sold on fighting in this game neither, it just felt janky.Like one of your best attacks is a charged light attack, which tends to work at the start, but then bosses just shake it off, even if you can perfectly see that it should have connected.Some skills and critically, dodging, are reliant on lock-on which honestly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks, as it seems to more lock your character's view than lock you onto an enemy.I found myself walking back-first into the boss multiple times because I tried using the lock-on, so in the end, I would really rather not have to use it, but alas.Detective/Lawyer side felt a lot weaker compared to the action.Sure, there is evidence-gathering and such, but it feels kinda barebones, and there are like only 3 cases, which all get rolled into one by the end of the game, anyway.Game labels a lot of things as "cases", but realistically, those are more information storage and fancier side quests than actual mysteries.Some also get abruptly "solved" at some point, too, at least according to the UI.I want to draw a parallel to Danganronpa here - in that game, there are clear cases, you go gather evidence for them as they occur, and with some effort it is even possible to put all the pieces together before the game tells you how it all actually went down.Here, I found myself figuring out the first 2 cases easily enough, and the last one was basically the whole story that became clear like 1/2 or 2/3 into the story, with the rest of it going about trying to collect proof.Gameplay-wise, this game feels and plays like any other RGG game.Kamurocho is open for the player to explore, and has more activities than necessary with a touch of some Japanese bs.There are great graphics and motion provided by the modern Dragon Engine.Of note this time, I guess there are drone races that I completely skipped, but heard are really brutal, and the "VR game".The latter is just a virtual Kamurocho that Yagami can plunge himself into to play a simple board game that puts him into various minigames depending on the tile he lands, of which more interesting are again, fights.Those fights can, and will have challenges in them that can be actually challenging (like going against an enemy that has all its attacks count as "mortal wounds" and limit your HP bar) to fun spins like "kill everything with a railgun".This VR thing also pays an absolutely stupid amount of money, playing it for like 5 times has given me more than enough funds to go through the rest of the game.It also has an annoyingly catchy BGM.To summarize, this is an okay spin on the usual formula RGG employs.People who are already familiar with Kamurocho get another excuse to delve into it, and those who are not are in for an okay introduction into the franchise (though, probably Yakuza 0 is a better start).

_childDocuments_.review: Judgment is a really successful spinoff of the Yakuza / Like a Dragon series, just as fun as a Kiryu story but renewed due to Yagami's fresh face at the helm.  That said, this is not an entirely different experience from the mainline, this is just a different flavor of the same formula.  "Yakuza-adjacent hero street-fights his way to the bottom of a massive conspiracy threatening to destroy Kamurocho" describes almost every RGG Studio project, and this is no different.  There are nods to Rockstar's L.A. Noire in the way Yagami searches crime scenes and tails suspects, but it should be understood that this game will feel very familiar to series fans, sometimes to its detriment.  The new things Judgment brings to the table are generally positive - I enjoyed Drone Racing more than I expected and rank it highly among the series' flagship minigames like the Hostess Club and Pocket Circuit.  VR Paradise (Mario Party), Lockpicking, Disguises and the crime scene investigation minigames were positive inclusions, too.  Suspect tailing, however, is so dull and impossible to fail at that the game would be better off without it.  And it is a huge part of the game, accounting for at least 15 missions.  Interrogating story characters is likewise questionable, with some truly baffling "correct" choices requiring reloads if you want to accomplish certain missable hidden achievements.  Added on top of that, almost all of the legacy minigames are bringing down what should have been a fresh, new experience.  The UFO catcher is perhaps the worst it has ever been in Judgment, and I do not want to play Space Harrier or Fantasy Zone again for as long as I live.  That brings me nicely to the next point - completion of this game is long, it's tedious, and it's not worth your time.  Insulting missable achievements (wait 3 minutes before saving Sugiura??  For what purpose?) pair with unnecessary endgame grinds to make for an unpleasant post-story experience.  And because this is such a low-power Yakuza title, with no equipment or inventory weapons to augment Yagami's modest combat abilities, a Legend mode playthrough is an exercise in frustration and essence-gulping.  I just thank my lucky stars that this entry does not have additional combat challenge missions.  While parts of this review may sound critical, I highly recommend that Yakuza fans play the game through on Normal, complete the excellent sidestories, become the Drone Racing champion, and leave it at that.

_childDocuments_.review: IT'S FINALLY ON STEAM! Judgment is a proper successor to the original Yakuza games (considering that Yakuza: Like A Dragon turned the series into a JRPG series, which I don't hate, far from it, but it's not a genre I'm into). Coming off Yakuza 6 (and Kiwami 2), Judgment feels like a proper upgrade from the series it originated. Gameplay wise, while it does still have some jank to it, the new combat mechanics such as juggling are a fantastic addition, pulling off long juggles on enemies is some of the most fun things you can do here. Soundtrack and the side content are also some of RGGS' best, I like the "quality > quantity" approach here much more than what the PS3 era Yakuza games did, which had TONS of filler and boring content in which felt INSANELY tedious to complete. However, Judgment's best aspect is it's fantastic story. I won't go into detail here because of spoilers, but I can say that thing might be the best story this studio ever wrote (and they wrote some amazing stuff before this). Overall, a fantastic game and one of my personal favorites of the past few years, definitely go check it out. If you've never played a Judgment or a Yakuza game in general, you are can play this without going through the Yakuza series, as the Yakuza stories are not connected to the Judgment games.

_childDocuments_.review: A great port of a great game. If it wasn't for the somewhat slow start before the main plot really kicks off and for the tedious and unreasonably abundant tailing missions, it would be up for consideration as the best in the series. The story is fantastic, the characters are very interesting, has some beautiful visuals at times, a RIDICULOUSLY good soundtrack, fantastic voice work and a surprisingly solid English dub for their first time since the series' recent popularity boom, combat becomes hilarious fun, and its packed full with tons of fun side content. It's easy to get hooked into the main story once it starts to really kick off early on. But its also just as easy to get hooked into ignoring the main story so you can go play darts with your weeaboo ninja friend Ryan Acosta, or going through the drone racing grand prix, or solving side cases about a pervert named Ass Catchem. Love this game. Also does not need any prior knowledge of the mainline Yakuza series to get into.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr i would hold off on buying this until some more performance patches are released. slowdowns, lockups, and crashes occur quite often and i don't think the game is good enough to make up for that. wait about a month or so and then buy. you could also get the game on sale if that occurs beforehand.PREFACE:At the time of writing this game has only been updated once. As the TL;DR indicates the technical complaints may go away in the future (hopefully) but as it stands right now this is my assessment.TECHNICAL:Out of all the video games I have ever played this one has had the most frequent technical problems. Every time a new area loads the game locks up for a while, sometimes a minute, and sometimes a "not responding" prompt from Windows even pops up. Very rarely the game shows mercy and instead lets the framerate drop. The game has crashed many times while loading new areas and there were two cases where a save file corrupted and caused an infinite loading screen. I believe my PC is good, and it was able to run Yakuza: Like a Dragon, which features a considerably larger map, with no real issues compared to this. The Drone Racing minigame goes to a black screen very often for some reason.GRAPHICS/SOUND:The graphics aim for realism and do it well. I'm pretty sure that most of the people in this game are modeled after real people. I don't think the soundtrack has as many memorable songs as some of the past games though. Overall there is nothing to think too hard about let alone complain.COMBAT:The combat is in general okay but a bit weird at times. Wall jumps can lead into attacks but these often cause the player to rocket off in a random direction and getting the aim right requires more finesse than should be needed for a game in which combat takes place primarily on narrow streets and indoors. The criteria for a wall jump is also inconsistent. Sometimes running at a wall does nothing and sometimes you can initiate a wall jump while standing still. There are two styles in this game, somewhat of a return to form to 0 and Kiwami's style. Unlike in those games there are only two styles. There is the good style and the other style. The good style is called Tiger. It's the good style because it is faster, does more damage, and has unlockable perks unique to it, whereas the other style doesn't. The other style, Crane, is slow and if a hit is blocked, it stuns you for a second. The only reason to use Crane is to break up a crowd of enemies so you can switch to Tiger and start the real beatdown. I feel like the developers gave more love to Tiger than Crane which is quite sad because a crowd-control style was done quite well with 0's Breaker.Thankfully, the Tiger Drop is shared by both styles.Something I don't like is how items are distributed. There is only one variant of the healing drinks (e.g. there is Staminan X but no Staminan Spark) and you can only carry a maximum of six which seems like a bit of an unneeded restriction. There are medical kits that heal a lot of HP but only one guy sells them and it's very inconvenient to have to go to him for this basically essential set of items.Medical kits also are important because some attacks leave "mortal wounds" that decrease max HP, and the kits bring it back to normal. The idea of enemies that could semi-permanently decrease max HP was cool when bosses and a few enemies with guns could do it, but it became very annoying once these gun-toters started showing up on the street because, again, only one guy in the whole map sells medical kits.The last thing is Extracts. They're potions that cause various effects like making you fight better or reducing the number of enemies on the map. They're interesting as an idea but I didn't use them too often.EXPLORATION AND SIDE CONTENT:You are limited to Kamurocho in this game. You will not be going to Sotenbori, Onomichi, or any other district within urban Japan. That's fine because I don't think the plot gives any opportunities for that, and I don't know if this game could handle multiple cities with its technical performance. You have the typical minigames like batting, mahjong, and the arcade games, with some new additions like a rail shooter and a VR fight zone. This is the Dragon Engine, though, so no fishing. There's a special important minigame called the Drone Race. You collect materials and buy parts for it and it's a big part of the side content. It's ultimately not too interesting however, because all you do is steer the drone around a route within Kamurocho and hit booster pads. It's not very involved and half of the tracks are literally the other half but backwards and with some changes to the booster pads.Another thing that returns from 0 is friends you meet on the street. The benefits are a bit more tangible here, since your friends grant you access to rare items, new Heat (or rather, EX) Actions, and even come to your aid to fight on the streets, which is a real improvement. There are a few people you can romance as well, but unfortunately love has no gameplay benefits.The system for substories is slightly revamped in that the majority of them are found by going up to someone who pulls up a list of substories for you to pick, similar to how you unlock a sidequest in the Witcher. It's a bit annoying because you will frequently check these rather than encountering the substories organically on the street (which still happens but at a greatly reduced rate).The piece of side stuff I really don't like is the Keihin Gang. Every now and again you get a text message alerting you that the Gang is coming and then the enemy encounter rate quintuples until you find and defeat a bunch of street bosses who are all really far from each other or until you wait 20 minutes or so. There is no way to stop it and it gets very very annoying after the third or so time. It's like a bad version of the Powerful Foes from 6. At least the Powerful Foes only showed up one at a time.PLOT:The storyline follows a model set by some of the later Yakuza games, working with the ideas of vast conspiratorial webs incorporating politics, organized crime, and things that on the surface have nothing to do with either. The difference here is that instead of seeing this through the lens of the criminal underworld itself you are a law-abiding (for the most part) detective, and hence this is more like a noir film than a crime drama. There is convolution but not a lot of it. It's interesting to see how the style of the previous games fits into this new skin and I enjoyed some of the hardboiled detective flairs they added. They even have an opening monologue ruminating about the city and its crime and all that. I enjoy it a lot and it gets real weighty at times but not soul-crushing, a balance Yakuza is good at striking.Despite the stylistic similarities and a shared universe, you do not need to play any previous Yakuza/RGG game to follow the plot, and the game does not have spoilers for such.
_childDocuments_.name: Judgment

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the top games in the franchise.The story was outstanding and the best written in the series imo even if there were not many iconic scenes like yakuza 0's for example  it was simply too addicting and near perfectly executed.The combat was also heavily improved compared to the previous dragon engine installments with cool additions to the extreme (heat) mode,flux fissure,fast style switching and mobility.Side content was satisfying enough with frienships,dating,sidecases and 2 new minigames to keep you entertained while completing the main storyline.On the downside,there are not a lot to say but the tailing missions were really boring as you pretty much do nothing but walk and some times hide behind an object for 5 seconds.Lockpicking and thumbturning were also annoying.That doesnt hold the game back thought since all these detective mechanics rarely appear and you can buy some cheap upgrades with SP to make them a tiny bit better.Lastly as with most of the games in the franchise the completion can get tedious.I would recommend Judgment to anyone especially to Yakuza,beat em up or crime / mystery fans , the devs keep evolving on every single game and totally delivered with this one.9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Judgment

_childDocuments_.review: I'll just say that I really enjoyed this different sense of the Yakuza franchise. Rya Ga Gotoku is a one-of-a-kind type of developer that release damn good games.Basically, you're an ex-lawyer turned detective trying to understand why there is a mysterious serial killer targeting a certain Yakuza family. Obviously, in classic yakuza fashion, it goes deeper into multiple plot twists that will all come together in what I think is a very good finale. Personally, my favorite story arc is , and my favorite villain is .The characters are unique all in their own way. Yagami {the main protag) is a much more realistic type of "Yakuza" character. He possesses the fighting style to defend himself, but he is no Kiryu or Ichiban, or Majima. He needs to use his brain and the power of friendship in order to get through situations. Such as Kaito or his lawyer colleagues.I will not be responsible for any damages you had towards your experience since I warned you.Anyways I will say some things that I didn't like.First off no karaoke. I have no idea why they wouldn't include it, but for whatever reason, I hope it was worth it.Secondly, I thought the whole side quests were pretty bland compared to the rest of the Yakuza franchise. I understand this is mostly detective work, but I only had very few side cases that I thought were memorable. Though most have a sort of plot twist and some were funny, it just didn't leave a considerable impact compared to its previous ones.Thirdly the tailing sections in some missions were the most generic and boring ♥♥♥♥ I have experienced in Yakuza history.Side activities like drone racing and VR were pretty meh, but I appreciate it when developers try new stuff. (Though they have house of the dead arcade game. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ best minigame).Overall I like the direction Ryu Ga Gotoku took with this installment instead of focusing on a heavily involved Yakuza character and I really have high hopes for the future Yakuza games.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a breath of fresh air for the Ryu Ga Gotoku series. Compared to Kiryu and his fists, Yagami and his palm strikes feels truly different. It's always great when they manage to make things different while keeping others the same. It's a shame karaoke couldn't come back, but i know there's reasons behind that decision. _childDocuments_.review: Originally this game was only sepposed to be sold on PlayStation4 as a spin-off to the original Yakuza/Lad-series. However, when Judgment got first announced that it was going to be ported to pc I had my hopes up. After all, this will probably be "the" only franchise that will have actual combat based street fighting. It seems that RGG studios only have plans to do RPG-styled combat in their future Yakuza/Lad or other spinn-off games. So this looked pretty promising to the fans that Judgment will see a new light of day on pc. Only to discover a month later, that the agency for Yagami's actor: Jhonnys, had allegidly debunked that announcement made by Sega and claimed that the game will not be avalible on steam due to the privacy for their talents and actors. Which by then Sega had no choice but to own up to that word. This came as a pretty big shock to the community as evryone who loved yakuza games or liked the combat based fighting mechanics specifically had to go home empty handed. However here we are, not just Judgment but also Lost Judgment have both been released to steam. This meant that RGG studios has seen the cries of the fandom and blessed them by talking things through with Jhonny's to finalize this negotiation. So if you are one of the people who still enjoy the old combat system from previous Yakuza games and want to see something new and refreshing, then this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Judgment

_childDocuments_.review: For as much as they wanted this to be NOT like yakuza, it at least feels it takes place within the world, but gameplay it still yakuza. The whole detective shebang either overstays its welcome or is super underdeveloped, there is really no inbetween. Story is atleast interesting, twist villain is really cool and the characters and interactions are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good, the characters do feel like they've known eachother for years and have had their difficult moments in life, plus the banter is so fun, especially with the decent english voice acting. If you're lookin for a new experience different to yakuza from RGG, this isnt that much of a giant leap away from it, but the characters and story are atleast fun and decent.
_childDocuments_.name: Judgment

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend Judgment, at first I was bored but as story went by it kept getting more and more interesting, story pacing was well done. Characters are memorable and lovable especially your close buddys, almost on par with Y: LAD characters. Story is one of the best in Y/LAD series, it's more serious then your avarage Yakuza. Side content was meh, lacking and repeatable, you have your funny and qurky side cases(substories) and standart side content like baseball, casino etc. New stuff; street rep(buddy system) that unlocks new events, side cases and allies that help you with street fights, girlfriends, money making ''Paradisu VR'' board game, and a very hard drone racing. Your MC, Yagami utilizes two fighting styles; Crane crowd control style which has no upgrade tree and powerfull Tiger for single enemy, but you can easly finish game using tiger only, Yagami can also leap over enemy and wall jump, the second one is crucial if you want to stop 'mortal wound' strike from boss type enemy, MC can also use extracts that e.g. gives him ability to break enemy guard or throw em around like they are nothing. Now the bad and ugly, lack of interesting  side content so you will be mainly doing main story and side cases, mortal wounds mechanic - it does not add anything, just makes you take a long trip to sewers so you can heal or buy medkit for a very expensive price, this exist only to waste time, Keihin gang - ''Majima everywhere'' system but 3x worse, atleast you can pull out your drone to reset random encounter spawn. Assassin's Creed style tailing missions that are slow and boring just horrible, especially the final one, it's like 15-20 minutes of walking in circle. Chases are not great either, at least they are quick, always funny when Yagami does some unnecessary goofy jump/dodge, still better then Y3 chases though. I will give it a score of 8/10 Main story carry this game, oh and also one of the best last bosses in the series

_childDocuments_.review: Judgement is yakuza game with detective plot and minigamesFighting is fun and that¨s kinda all there is for JudgementDont get me wrong, i like the story but there are so many other factors in playForced minigamesLockpicking for example, I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HATE THIS ONE, you have to be so precise and its not even fun, using mouse even a single flick will reset the whole minigames, and controller is so much worse.That minigame where you have to follow that yellow thing with your joystickAgain, this minigame isnt the worst but its still bad, its okay with an mouse but controller on the other hand makes me want to kill myself, i use 20 years old ps2 controller so 0.2 second joystick disconnection will reset the minigame.FightingThere are 2 fighting styles for yagami, and thats it. i have heard that lost judgement has more but its kinda pointless if i cant get myself to complete judgement.Mortal woundsYou will get limited hp if you get shot or stabbedTo remove mortal wounds you have to use a medkit (costs a lot of money in early game) or run into the sewers for a doctorPointless mechanicI have tried to play this game for half an year but i just cant do it just because of those minigames littered over the story and every other side activityMaybe i will try to play this on ps5 when i get one eventually but for pc port, i cannot recommend itJust play the mainline titles and ignore this one

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing spin-off to Yakuza playing the side of the law instead of the side of the criminal. What a wonderful idea that they executed with fine precision. If you are looking for some good games, play Judgment, and play Lost Judgment afterwards, Beat this on PS4 just recently and it was great on that platform... But daaaammmnnnn, 60fps for this game is pretty damn great.
_childDocuments_.name: Judgment

_childDocuments_.review: Judgment is a fantastic spin-off game of the yakuza series this time you take the roll of a detective meaning there is a lot of new mechanics implemented in order to actually put you in said role like tailing or using a drone to get information and as a plus to that this game has one of the best stories in the yakuza franchise period i would honestly say you should avoid looking up any plot points of this game for a full experience just like i did however the game is not perfect and i would say one of the more weaker aspects of the game is actually the gameplay, compared to the rest of games in the yakuza series the combat actually feels a bit slow too slow for my taste even with full upgrades but you will get used to it after a while and this was fixed in the sequel, besides that i actually also felt there was a big lack of minigames in the game but my guess is that was done on purpose considering this game is a lot more serious, so yea those are some of the more weaker aspects of this game, besides that i had a blast with the game having a lot of interesting side cases, great supporting characters and a great ost making this a fantastic experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Judgment

_childDocuments_.review: Whoever you are, play this, and play it especially for the story, the characters and the overarching meaning. I don't know how this studio does it but each time they provide a world you can immerse yourself in. The fighting mechanics are very fun & addictive, the world of Kamurocho is filed with activities, friends and fun, and the writing is excellent. Plus when you have a whole side case which has you chasing/apprehending a panty professor it shows the game knows when to provide a certain level of comedy.What really makes it stand out is its protagonist. Yagami is a great midpoint between the excessively stoic Kiryu and the lovable Ichiban. He's charming, snarky, and shines as his own distinct character. As a standalone adventure, it's an excellent action RPG, boasting some outstanding storytelling and a brilliant cast of characters. And as a Yakuza spinoff, it's arguably the perfect gateway into SEGA's stellar series. If you're looking for another entry in the brilliant Yakuza franchise, then Judgment is the way to go.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10, the "perfect storm" of a Yakuza spin-off. Mature tone, crime drama story, fun detective gameplay, great combat, good minigames, interesting substories (Side Cases). It's like they took that core Yakuza formula and peeled off everything that made it un-enjoyable, leaving nothing but the juicy insides.
_childDocuments_.name: Judgment

_childDocuments_.review: JudgmentTakes place in the same universe/town as Yakuza (Kamurocho) . We play as an investigator (Yagami). A guy who holds his phone in his back pocket, makes me nervous to see him run. We tail people (stealth missions) capture ppl, and observe our surroundings and stuff as part of the gameplay. Plenty of QTE. The general feel of the game reminded me a lot of "like a dragon". There's plenty of unique game mechanics in this title. Flying drones to spot the targets/security cameras and stuff. Friendship system this one is pretty weird. Involves friend events, gifting. Mortal wounds, you cant replenish ur whole hp unless u visit a doctor or use medkits that can be used from a doctor. I disliked that quite a lot.  I didn't find chapter 1 too engaging. It dragged out way too much. The story rly gets rolling at the end of ch 4, and I rly rly loved the plot starting from ch9.The last fight was hype, the plot was satisfying and complete, and Saori is the best girl.The overall vibe was a lot more dark/serious compared to the yakuza games.

_childDocuments_.review: The best Detective/mystery story I've witnessed in a video game . It has it's problems and is missing a lot of fun side activities like Cabaret club, karaoke. dancing, fishing etc and the Combat could be a little deeper. But regardless of these the Pros of the Game greatly outweigh the cons. Amazing mystery plot, really amazing characters and their developments that even made me tear up in a couple of places and the fun combat. If you like doing side activities with a lot of dialogue  but with no voice acting, then you'll absolutely love this game. I personally can't get immersed if the side quests are not voiced. So mostly I skipped most of the side quests' dialogue. Now this game is not perfect , not the best yakuza game but it's at least top 5. Only if it didn't have those god awful tailing missions , could clearly tell that was for padding purposes as most of the time there needn't be any tailing required. even if you had to do it, you have a drone you can freely control. Why waste time hiding and following slowly. This is the most frustrating tailing mission in any game period. Also those god awful thumb lockpicking sections. hope they did a little more play testing with the controls as the sensitivity for the sticks were awful and no option to set the said sensitivity. Verdict: Great detective game with a twist where the story twists and turns, courtroom drama , fun fighting , bustling atmosphere . A game with a lot of hits and few misses. It was a fun ride to the end, can't wait to play the sequel.
