_childDocuments_.review: Great game on controller, I imagine. However, If you want to play this game on PC, I guarantee that you will have a more pleasant experience shoving your keyboard up your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horizontally, whether you're into that or not. If you're wondering what's so physically painful about this game, it's mostly the lockpicking mechanic. You're supposed to use either the left stick or right stick to slowly raise the lockpick thing to push the pins to the shear line. If you're on mouse, there are set parameters to where the lockpick thing can go. These parameters do not always include the shear line, so if you can't get it first try (assuming the insanely high sensitivity doesn't make it impossible for you to get it at all, my normal DPI is 1600 and I have to move my mouse about a tenth of an inch before it goes too far, and at 200 DPI I sometimes still accidentally overshoot at mach speed) as far as I'm aware, you're just kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥, and eventually if you keep retrying it you should get it after half an hour or so. Aside from the lockpicking, which is equally impossible, and significantly more frequent, there's another weird, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ minigame for unlocking doors where you use your left stick and right stick to do some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I don't really know, and I don't think the developers know either. The fun part is, even if you're on PC, you still have to use your left stick and right stick. In other words, you have to use your mouse to simulate the left stick and right stick, making what's normally a fairly difficult minigame genuinely the worst experience I have had in the entire Yakuza series so far (0-6), and yes, I did finish Yakuza 3. If you do not have a controller, do not get the game. If you already have the game, and don't have a controller, refund it. If you can't refund it, go ♥♥♥♥ yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: I have fairly mixed feelings on this game. On one hand, it's one of the best stories RGG has put out to-date - it's not quite as emotionally heavy as Yakuza 0 or 7, but Judgement makes up for it by having overall excellent story structure and delivering extremely well on the crime investigation aspects. If you're a fan of Ace Attorney or the times the Yakuza games get into that territory, you'll be right at home.On the other hand, I'm conflicted on the side content. The game reintroduces the Friend System, where you do things for people around town to increase your rep. In the Yakuza games that used it, you could befriend shopkeepers and they'd give you access to a special attack while you're fighting near their shop, like stuffing a goon's mouth full of spicy chicken. Judgement expands on that by adding more possible outcomes, such as additional locations and facilities for you to use, as well as people that'll roam the city and help you out in fights directly. This is a genuinely good expansion on the friend system, which is more than I can say for the other additions.The sidequest quality is just below 0, 7 and Kiwami 2. Good, but not great. My absolute biggest gripe is with the minigames; hardly any new additions, tons of removals (THERE'S NO KARAOKE) and one of the new additions is both the most-frequently-required minigame as well as one of the worst minigames RGG has ever put out. The tailing minigame gets old extremely quickly and I genuinely hope this game gets a mod that lets you skip it. It's an incredibly low-stakes stealth minigame that is far too forgiving and does nothing but slow the game down. There's also a Mario Party-ish board game minigame that becomes your primary source of money and EXP once you're done with the game, but I largely ignored it and I haven't gotten around to the meat of it. At a glance it's alright.The combat isn't perfect, but it's still pretty damn good. Unlike previous titles using the Dragon Engine, you've actually got multiple fighting styles - Crane, which is for dealing with crowds, and Tiger, which is for single-target fights and small groups. They both feel great once you expand their movesets a bit, but there's a very noticeable lack of upgrades specialized for the Crane style. Most upgrades augment both styles and behave differently depending on which one you're using, but Tiger has a bunch of upgrades that drastically alter what it can do. Eventually you'll be spending all but a few fights entirely in Tiger style, it just becomes that much better. Tiger style alone still plays better than Kiryu's Dragon style in Yakuza Kiwami 2 and 6 though, the focus on agility feels great.Overall the game's excellent with some fairly large holes in it.Edit: It's worth mentioning that every single issue this game has is fixed in its sequel, Lost Judgement; fighting styles are more distinct and have a large amount of upgrades for each, the tailing minigame has gotten a massive overhaul, the sidequests are mostly-excellent and there's far more minigame variety.

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all the Yakuza games, this one slapped the most. Completely separate from the main line titles makes this game easy to jump into for new players not immersed in the universe and the whole design premise of the style switching combat from Yakuza 0, in the funny and slick physics engine already had me sold.Gameplay - In my opinion the previous entries within this new engine (Yakuza 6, and Kiwami 2) never really fully utilized the crazy tech you would be able to pull off in previous titles, and boiled down to spam punching combos till enemy dies. The previous games were carried by their funny wacky physics of punch guys into space and objects and watch them clip over the place (which not at all makes the those games bad, in fact I enjoyed 6 and its craziest physics). However, during Kiwami 2's collesium side content, some bosses would put me through the mix with unbreakable action moves happening in real time and I wondered how those moves would operate if they were actual techniques you could pull off yourself in game. Well, this game manages that, it gives you tech off the wazoo. You wanna throw yourself off a wall and swing on enemies like a monkey? You can do that. You wanna play hop scotch and reverse suplex enemies into the ground? You can do that. You wanna insta kill blast opponents with a simple open palm move that makes a funny bass noise? You can do that. Hell, remember me talking about those moves in kiwami 2 that bosses pulled on ya? You can actually deploy those moves from extraction potions that you craft and completely alter your fighting style. I haven't even talked about the two main styles you can switch to, and honestly I have already said too much. The best part about the two new styles (crane, and tiger), was figuring out what they do, and where to use them. So ill leave it off there.Setting - For returning players we see the return of Kamurocho from the eyes of a disgraced lawyer turned small time detective. Now, even halfway through the game I knew that this was one of the best iterations of Kamurocho in the entire series (previous qualifiers were Yakuza 0's time switch, and Yakuza 4's verticality). What makes this Kamurocho so great is the friend's system. Its the best version of previous title's reputation grind, but its actually good this time cuz unlike previous titles where you would do a citizen's rep meter, and would never see them again or hear from them. In this game, you not only see them wandering the streets, you see them aiding you with crafting materials, boosting your EX meter, or aiding you in fights whether with ally heat animations, or tagging along in fights. The new northern part of Kamurocho being the "Hills Garden" area was really beautiful and the new areas within the city that makes it easy to traverse thanks to Yagami's parkour god skills, makes carving shortcuts through point A to B, fun. The story was also one of the best this series has to offer, and is carried by the cast of characters you that surround yourself with throughout the game. At the credit screen I was already wanting to jump back into that iconic detective's office that you come love by the end of the game. Its that good.Mini games - Now I will admit, this is the weakest lineup of mini games within the series. Now does that mean the side content in this game is bad? No. You have your basic mini games that you've come to expect in previous titles like baseball, returning sega arcade games, mahjong, etc. Even with the returning mini games, they manage to spice things up, shogi now has a much needed mini feature of having checkmate problems to solve presented as "puzzle shogi" which to me was insanely addicting to solve, along with mahjong getting a whole new parlor named "Tachibana" which was mahjong on crack, which was high rated nuts to butts action with the "wareme" rule. This game had my favorite sega arcade lineup in awhile simply because of the amount of fun I had with "Fighting Vipers" which is now my definitive favorite fighting game ever. Unfortunately no karaoke, that seems to be specific to the mainline titles, but the brand new exclusive mini games to Judgment weren't exciting to me ON PAPER, but ended up being pretty damn fun. Drone racing was a blast, and in my opinion was better than Yakuza 7's dragon kart mini game. Simply because of the deep amount of customization you can apply to your drone and the 3D racing environment giving you more exhilarating, high octane, ball sack quenching moments maneuvering through tight corroders within cafes, and buildings. Finally, we have Paradise VR which is a single player mario party type game that has you avoiding black cats, conquering challenges, and scoring big. This was my main money maker throughout the game and though it did get a little bit boring near endgame with constantly running this mini game for cash it definitely was fresh air from the meta in previous titles which had you just go to the casino or gambling hall to win big and I am thankful nonetheless for the change in scenery.I haven't had that much fun with a Yakuza game since the first one I played which was Yakuza 0. Def. a must have for people getting into the series or fans who have money to burn.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend Judgment to any non-Yakuza diehard, the story and characters are intriguing and fun, but the rest of the game is ROUGH. The combat is terrible, possibly worse than Yakuza 3s combat. Enemies constantly have a combination of super armor and blocking, If you hit an enemy with super armor or they're blocking, Yagami goes into a recoil state that lasts entirely too long for an already slow combat system. This makes Yagami's Crane style borderline useless, because that is the "crowd clearing" style, but because of the recoil mechanic if any random goon you're fighting blocks you go into the recoil animation and then get whopped. Hitboxes are also laughably bad in many places of the game (possibly because it was early days of the Dragon Engine.) I would highly recommend using one of the combat overhaul mod packs you can get on Nexus Mods, they make the combat feel significantly smoother and more fun to play. It also seems like RGG just gave you a bunch of cheesy win buttons with extracts instead of actually fixing the combat (which modders were able to do,) so that's a bummer. Reminder, combat isn't hard (on Hard mode at least,) its just very annoying and unfun because of the jankiness of infinite super armor and blocking.Judgment introduces a Wall Leap attack and a Leap Frog attack outside of the standard Yakuza combat. Leap Frog is pretty useful, as there are some solid attacks tied to it, although larger enemies and bosses will generally throw you off when you try. The Wall Leap attack is a hilarious joke and whoever designed it should feel bad, it misses extremely often and is very janky to even activate because of object clutter, uneven walls, and random walls you just can't leap attack off of. On top of that, the light, heavy and throw attacks you get from wall leap do tiny amounts of damage compared to normal combat. The side stories are very mediocre, they lack the goofy/whimsical nature of your normal Yakuza side stories and so, so many of them are incredibly boring tailing missions. Tailing missions are strictly just worse versions of escort missions. You slowly follow a target and the missions are borderline unfailable, or impossible to fail if you've invested skillpoints into the tailing skills. These missions last anywhere from 3-10 minutes, and they're just awful wastes of time with no fun or interesting game mechanics. The drone is pretty cool, even though it is very rough around the edges its still fun to play. Not being able to rebind brake to whatever you want for drone races is a huge troll, but workable. The drone races are fun but also very poorly balanced. The drone is apparently made out of the same material as a bouncy ball, so you can pretty easily make a small mistake and lose 30-50% of your health in one crash during a drone race because damage taken is based on impacting an object and you bounce all over the place when you hit something. The CPUs also cheat because they run into ♥♥♥♥ all the time and don't have to worry about durability which is extremely dumb. The VR minigame is pretty solid too, it is slightly unfortunate it's basically the only way to make money in the game, as that made it a bit stale for me after a while (you can gamble but its not nearly as lucrative.) This minigame has some fun strategy but some rough RNG, and the skill to slow down the dice is ridiculously expensive, so smoothing out the RNG takes major investment. The tigers you can fight in the VR minigame are basically a showcase of everything that is wrong with the combat in the game. You can't combo them outside of EX mode because of the super armor recoil, the hitbox on their leap attack is hilariously disjointed and much larger than the tiger model, the tiger is low enough to the ground that a ton of attacks go above it AND all of its attacks cause mortal wounds and do a very silly amount of damage in a mode where you can't heal unless you run into King Kyoronan. Mortal Wounds is a terrible system, and doesn't really show how awful it is until the last 20-25% of the game. At this point you run into a few boss fights where multiple enemies can cause them, and they also incorporate enemies with guns into normal enemy packs that open fire almost immediately in combat and delete about 1/5-1/6th of your health (with the highest health upgrade.) It's a truly braindead call to put these enemies into a game with already bad combat, just to force you to either spend insane amount of Yen (which you can only farm in the VR game) or run around with a severely debuffed healthbar until you're forced to go and heal at the doctor.Overall game is worth playing if you like the RGG Yakuza world, but the actual gameplay is very middling to downright bad. For Yakuza buffs I would put this game below Yakuza 3 as it has a lot of the same problems with bad combat but good story. Buy on sale, use one of the combat rework mods (I didn't for my playthrough, but then tried one after I cleared the game and it was much more enjoyable.)

_childDocuments_.review: Judgment is like a cross between a gritty crime thriller and a choose-your-own-adventure book, except you're not really choosing the adventure - you're just along for the ride. But hey, who needs control when you can watch your character make questionable life decisions and get involved in shady deals?The graphics are great, and the game really captures the feeling of being a private investigator in the mean streets of Japan. But let's be real, the real star of the show is the main character, Takayuki Yagami. He's like a brooding anime hero come to life, with a tragic past and a sense of justice that only applies when it's convenient for the plot.The game is packed with mini-games and side quests, from tailing suspects to playing arcade games to solving puzzles. And don't forget about the fighting - nothing says "private investigator" like beating up random thugs on the street.But be warned, the game can be pretty slow-paced at times, and you might find yourself getting a bit too invested in the fictional world of Kamurocho. Just remember to take breaks and step outside every once in a while, or you might end up like Takayuki, wandering the streets in a perpetual state of existential crisis.Overall, Judgement is a fun and entertaining game that will keep you hooked for hours. Just don't expect too much realism, and be prepared to suspend your disbelief a few times. And who knows, maybe you'll discover a new love for private investigation - or at least, for wearing a cool leather jacket.

_childDocuments_.review: Judgment is a familiar game if you have played any of the previous Yakuza games but this spin off to the main series does well in differentiating itself. Yagami has to be the smartest main character since the start of the series, he also is an actual human capable of having emotions unlike Kiriyu. The story is centred around exploring the gray zones of your mortality but Yagami is very strong with conviction for what is right.The game unlocks side stories (cases) differently by having a  which you level up by befriending people around the city. As you continue through the story you unlock more people who you befriend by sometimes simply talking to them each time or there might be a short mission you have to do. I loved how these were done since they were a bit like mini-side cases but not really? It felt like Kamurocho was alive with a community of people you have helped out.The combat in this game is enjoyable and felt really good when playing on Hard. I felt like it was missing some Akiyama air combos since Yagami's fighting style is similar to Akiyama's. There is a new mechanic in combat called mortal wounds which is where the enemy powers up and if you don't go into EX mode or dodge your health bar actually gets destroyed. I was sceptical about it but the game gives you enough options to avoid it.Overall, Judgment is definitely a series I want to see more of in the coming years. It advances the plot in a different way to your usual Yakuza (Like A Dragon) game by being  lawful. Yagami is a character I want to see more.

_childDocuments_.review: Now I finally was able to beat judgement after almost an entire week taking 31 hours of my life and I do not regret it for a second. The game has a lot to offer compared to other games I have played not surprising since this is from the same people who made Yakuza.So If I could rate this game out of ten I would give it a 8.5/10. It takes itself seriously and then at the same point you will be forced to bond with a child. It is stupid sometimes and over the top but honestly that is the charm of the game. I just want to say the pros and cons real quick.Pros:Combat - Unique with two unique styles which change the style of combat instead of Yakuza where it usually has more impact, this focuses on speed and movement. SO you will be moving around quickly in the air like a monkey pouncing onto dudes constantly. It is addictive.Story - Quite unique following a ongoing elaborate case of "what you would do to justify your goals?" However most of the time with some of these segments you will be interrupted from a serious scene to a music tone shift which focuses on comedy. It happens often in the early game and it can be quite jarring.Soundtrack - Very unique soundtrack especially the theme for "the mole" but honestly with the amount of reused tracks there are for certain sequences, They have a lot of variety. I suggest listening to a couple of spotify, since some are absoulte gems.Side Content - It is Yakuza side content, silly, wacky and weird however not necessary to complete (most of the time)Clan Encounters - At random points you will be contacted that a rival gang is out on the streets looking for you, why is it good. Well if you need higher chances of being in encounters plus the luck potion you can have a easy time farming. However it can get annoying when you are on other important missions like main quests and they pop up.Now THE CONS:First 6 Chapters - I have no idea how but this introduction is so weak. It helps you get to characters and settings but after your first tailing mission it sends you on a  bunch of meaningless fetch quests and just when something intresting is about to happen you are pulled back to do a mandatory side quest. Here is my  It is the only way to progress and sometimes you have to do an additional 2 or 3 which take 20 or more minutes. Look I understanding waiting around for info but this is ridiculous.If it happened once in the introduction I wouldn't mind but this happens for at least the first 6 chapters before it starts to ignore it. I dislike it extremely.Trailing Missions, Lock Picking, etc. - Now I understand trying to diverse a game's options and mechanics but sometimes it feels pointless and unwanted. If these were only used sparingly or well optimized maybe it would have been better but sometimes you have to be close to pixel perfect in order to pull off some of these missions. As side content that makes sense but as most of the mechanics it feels annoying when it pops up for the 50th time.but other than that the game works as intended and is really fun...I just wish you know some of these methods didn't keep prompting up. Also I listened to this game through its english dub and subtiltes I think it is fine, if you disagree fight me.Hope this will help you if you ever think about buying it. Personally I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite games in the Yakuza series (even though it is a spin-off). Combat is great and manages to feel like a natural progression of previous Yakuza games while also being able to feel unique with the addition of new specialised moves to fit the newly introduced protagonist you play as in Judgment, Takayuki Yagami. The story is another classic for the Yakuza series involving many plot twists that keep the player engaged to find out what happens next. Unfortunately, the pacing also receives the same treatment as other games in the series with big story beats being mixed up with side cases that you cannot skip. This does not take away from the story in any massive way but it does impact the player experience. I would recommend Judgment to anyone who is a fan of action/beat 'em up games or to anyone who is interested in the Yakuza series. Overall Rating:  4/5

_childDocuments_.review: Kamige.The Yakuza series, or Like A Dragon, or Ryu Ga Gotoku if you prefer) have formed a critical part of my life at this point. I started Yakuza 0 during the start of the COVID pandemic, and have been on a binging spree since then. I didn't own a Playstation however, so imagine my absolute joy when they just announced Judgement/Lost Judgement for PC. More Yakuza!Judgement or Judge Eyes is an absolutely amazing spinoff that I really wouldn't mind seeing more of. It's clear that the devs didn't wish to be locked into just the traditional Kiryu plotline with these entries (despite going back to him anyway with the recent announcements lol). If you're wondering if the characters in this one are just as lovable as the old Yakuza games, don't worry, Toshihiro Nagoshi's got your back. If you're looking for more critical reviews, there's plenty out there. But if you ask me to list what I love about this series; -the Japanese aesthetic.-the art direction of the locations (seriously, Kamurocho at night in the Dragon Engine looks absolutely )-the action beat 'em up gameplay (I still liked Yakuza 7 despite not enjoying turn based gameplay as much)-Buff, muscly men beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of goons, sometimes shirtless, in almost every game, charming female sidekicks.... Hot characters in general, really. Obviously subjective.-the minigames. THE MINIGAMES. They form 50% of the actual game. You can get lost in any one of the minigames as if they're actual games. You can play SEGA's arcade games in the game because SEGA's the publisher for the Yakuza series and they got the rights for it.-the plots. Quite frankly the plots are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane in every single game, and it goes so wild at times that after a certain point you slowly accept that these games really are just a fantasy version of reality, just so your suspension of disbelief doesn't shatter completely.Honestly, despite the flaws in each of these games, the innovations they try with each new entry that both please and piss off fans, each of them is  a treat that really, you owe it yourself to try at least one of the entries in this series.

_childDocuments_.review: It's still unbelievable that RGG announced 3 games in one day and also decided to drop Judgment on steam just as a cherry on top, best company ever.edit: I'm now very close to actually beating the game so I need to get this out of my chest. This is, by far, the best story RGG has written as of yet. At least in my opinion.I was honestly thinking that nothing would ever top Yakuza 0 but I am so happy to be proven wrong. RGG can write brilliant stories and engaging characters if they try hard enough. Additionally, I've totally fallen in love with the combat mechanics. Despite this not technically being released this year, It's probably my GOTY for 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through this on PS4 and am going through it again. An amazing Yakuza spin-off game that takes place in the same universe as the mainline games. The Yakuza series has always been heavily story driven and I've enjoyed the stories present in every game in the series despite their flaws. However, Judgement takes the story aspect of the franchise to a new level. It's such an amazing tale filled with many twists and turns. On top of that the game delivers what you expect from other Yakuza games: tons of mini games, plenty of side quests, cathartic combat with a ton of unlockable abilities, beautiful graphics, and a banger soundtrack. Highly recommended if you enjoy the Yakuza games or if the trailer looks interesting to you. You don't need to play the other Yakuza games to understand this one. It's a completely stand-alone story and the saga continues in its sequel: Lost Judgement.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really know what to expect going into this as this is the first yakuza spin-off that I've played, but it ended but being an excellent game. Quite an interesting story with some crazy plots. The combat feels a little stiff from time to time, but I like the animations and martial art techniques. I'm also glad it wasn't the abominable turn-based combat system that Like A Dragon had. Unfortunately, I ran into some game-breaking bugs where I couldn't interact with some parts of the environment. During the main chapters, there have been times when I couldn't open doors and/or interact with something that I had to in order to proceed. Through trial and errors from reloading older saves, I somehow got through it. All in all, apart from the irritating bugs, definitely a nice experience for a spin-off and I'd highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I´ve never written a review for anything before, but this game was just so good that I had to talk about it ( a bit ;) )First things first: Yes, this game is a Yakuza Game in its core! It uses the same dragon engine from Yakuza 6 and Kiwami 2 and thats really great in my opinion! The combat is smooth as ever, the two new combat styles are refreshing (just a quick info: Ive played through Yakuza 1-6), but the fights are still challenging enough.As you may know from the info material, the story is set in the same universe as the Yakuza Games, but (to my surprise) manages to tell a new engaging story with lots of twists and turns and some great side characters. The protagonist Takayuki Yagami is such an interesting and complex character and the detective aspects of the story gave me a well needed break from the Yakuza type stories with all its clans and stuff (dont get me wrong, I absolutely love the Yakuza games!!!).When I heard that the game was sort of a combination of Yakuza gameplay with visual novel elements (I´m also a huuuuuge Ace Attorney fan, which was one of the main reasons) and even some puzzles (in the sidestories) I was instantly hooked and decided to buy it in a steam sale. After completing it (about 67 hours with all friends and sidestories) I was so glad I did! The story is great and memorable, the gameplay is just fun and if you already like the Yakuza games, even better :) Even if you are new to the Yakuza/ Like a dragon- franchise, Judgement is an awesome way to start!For me, this game is clearly a 10/10 experience. Get it during a sale or not, its worth your money either way!

There are a few situations that make you question the developers and some fights feel like Elden Ring on steroids but overall it was very enjoyable. Also, long live the Dragon engine!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be completely honest - I haven't progressed very far into the game, and I'm only on chapter two.However: This game just isn't as fun as any other Yakuza game.Yes, I'm a major sucker for Kiryu, Majima etc. but that has 0 impact on why I'm not a huge fan of this iteration.I wasn't a big fan of Like a Dragon, but surprisingly enough I've sunk more hours into that game than any other Yakuza game.I can't see myself throwing as many hours into this one as any of the others.Kamurucho is glorious - Further more it's nice being able to "parkour" around the town, and take some of the small "shortcuts" into side alleys that we've never been able to before.Whenever I played a new game, it was always one of the top things for me to figure out: "What has changed this time around" and for the most part it hasn't disappointed me.The major grief I have with the town is the removal of Karaoke - Why couldn't they have left out Mahjong instead? xDTailing is probably the worst "game mechanic" I've ever experienced in this universe since they turned the series into a flawed RPG game (Holy ♥♥♥♥ it's flawed). It seems pointless, slow and it's just plain horrible.It's even worse than unskipable cutscenes/dialogue.Next up is the entire investigation crap...I get it - We're a detective yada yada yada. But why does it have to be so horrible?! And now we have to present our case to convince people of A, B and C?!?The fighting styles suck - Yes, I haven't unlocked that many skills yet, but they're so clunky and slow. After finishing a combo he'll just stand there for 2 hours while being open to attacks.The lock-on system is a major downgrade compared to any of the previous games and the new EX meter sucks.And don't get me started on the freakin' drones.. I thought I wasn't a fan of the toy-car races but seriously.. ♥♥♥♥ that drone - And ♥♥♥♥ having to scout out areas with it too!While not having a real impact yet, even on hard, I can't see any reason why the new wound system is in place. It seems weird and horrible at the same time.Some of the, few, things I welcome in this game is some of the new mini games (zombie shooter is amazing!), the more nimble character (actually being slim enough to go through narrow paths lol) and the removal of weapons/gear but sadly that's about all the positives I can come up with at this point.When I noticed the game got released, I basically blew my budget to get the collection and sadly I have to admit that I deeply regret it.I thought I disliked the new direction of Like a Dragon, but honestly I hope this spin-off dies. The sooner the better.TL:DR - BRING BACK MAH KARAOKE!!!

_childDocuments_.review: First half of Judgment: B-Second half: A+Seriously, this game isn't the best of the best when it comes to RGG Studio's output, with mechanics such as the tailing wearing out their welcome real quick, but Judgment benefits from a great cast of characters throughout, a truly loathsome villain, and a second half that takes the training wheels off and just goes freakin' nuts. It's got some of my favourite moments in any RGG game, and a lot of that has to do with the main pair of characters. Yagami and Kaito both bring their own great flavour to proceedings within the oh so familiar streets of Kamourocho, and though only Yagami is playable throughout the story, Kaito immediately takes a head seat within the council of ABSOLUTE HOMIES.Great game, in spite of a few little issues. From chapter 8 onwards, I don't think the grin left my face for a second.Judgment 3 WHEN?

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, this game loves to circle back to information we already know regarding the plot but yet present it to us like such profound new info. The Keihin gang was annoying to all hell. They were like roaches—easy to kill but impossible to exterminate. They will spam your playthrough with encounters, like the SMT Nocturne Encounter rate. Ok, maybe not that bad, but still pretty bad. lol And whose bean head bright idea was to remove the load save option that was in your menu?! Also, constantly displaying your tips on how to play is like, wow. If I wanted to be babied, then I would have played a Nintendo game instead. Also, I find it so pointless to have to look through keys to open a door; it is just so stupid and boring, even with the skill that identifies the exact key to opening the door. Should be removed altogether. Also, this developer must love making stupid decisions in game development because of also restricting your max HP and only being able to recover it by only paying 20 to 40 grand to fix it, da ♥♥♥♥!? Now for non-spoilers, but story critiques (just piece it together if you know the story)-Conveniently taking sleeping pills-Trusted Hamura over the middle man.-The very important death scene of a certain man was so cringeworthy.-Story loves to conveniently pick and choose who to kill.

_childDocuments_.review: Given the overwhelmingly positive review, I just want to give an alternative opinion here. The game is overall ok. Solid 6/10. At least it is better than Yakuza Kiwami, which is pretty much just recycled/water-downed Yakuza 0. But also note that this game is nowhere better than Yakuza 0.I'm very intrigued by the plot, except the game decides to pause the main story mid-game and force you to do boring side-stories. I assume this is because the main story is too short on its own to carry this game. A lot of these side-stories involve you being a detective to either stalk people and/or play "find the object in the room/image" game, both of which feel kinda meh and a slightly annoying. I do enjoy the deductions. But sometimes I feel like the game wants you to deduct in a very specific order. At times you know what happened but you have to kinda guess how the game wants you reach a conclusion and select dialogues (show evidence) in a specific order. The combat feels really fresh. It does not feel like recycled content. But beware that the main character really loves walls. Apparently a lot of his moves are designed around running toward a wall and doing some sort of jump-kick. In my opinion this design just makes the combat feel less "open" than Yakuza 0. And since it is kinda difficult to pull off the jump-kick, mostly I just end up getting lazy and grabbing a bike to bash enemies. I'm also kinda annoyed by the Japanese audio. Not sure why but the English dialogue audio version of this game feels a lot more crisp than the Japanese one. In the Japanese dialogue audio, it almost feels like the voice actors are speaking through a thin blanket.

_childDocuments_.review: I made a severe and continuous lapse in my judgement, and I don’t expect to be forgiven. I’m simply here to apologize. What we came across that day in the woods was obviously unplanned. The reactions you saw on tape were raw; they were unfiltered. None of us knew how to react or how to feel. I should have never posted the video. I should have put the cameras down and stopped recording what we were going through. There's a lot of things I should have done differently but I didn't. And for that, from the bottom of my heart, I am sorry. I want to apologize to the internet. I want to apologize to anyone who has seen the video. I want to apologize to anyone who has been affected or touched by mental illness, or depression, or suicide. But most importantly I want to apologize to the victim and his family. For my fans who are defending my actions, please don't. I don’t deserve to be defended. The goal with my content is always to entertain; to push the boundaries, to be all-inclusive. In the world I live in, I share almost everything I do. The intent is never to be heartless, cruel, or malicious. Like I said I made a huge mistake. I don’t expect to be forgiven, I’m just here to apologize. I'm ashamed of myself. I’m disappointed in myself. And I promise to be better. I will be better. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: After the awesome journey of Like a Dragon: Gaiden, this game was my obvious next foray into the 'you as a suit wearing guy see some ugly mfs and beat em up' genre, and now maybe I can say I'm a real RGG(Ryu Ga Gotoku) fan.For starters, I rue the fact that this game was brought up to me this late due to release cadence, it is important to note that at the time RGG studio games have a JP exclusive time window, that window is often spent on PS platforms only. For the same reason the series might be hard to continue from the side of the devs due to disagreements with the Actor's management group from Japan, thanks to the devs tho, playing on pc now is still a perfectly whole experience.This game has the same basic legs of the main RGG yakuza games, only this game sees the Dragon Engine shine like never before (just don't be fooled because the wacky physics and confusing ragdolls are not gone). The story blows everything you've seen out of the water but closely resembles J-drama (in this genre some of the contemporary story lines borrow and refine from Agatha Christie novels, you'll see some of those here), although maybe the story relies a little bit too much on yakuza knowledge from the main series, but still can be enjoyed as the protagonist you play really is his own thing.Combat wise this has lots of jank that would be fixed in the sequel Lost Judgement, there are skills you can pick up early on to sidestep the difficulty, but playing the game normally while you abuse your ability to release the fist of JUSTICE after bouncing from walls should make it a smooth and fun experience.Be wary of the length, don't try to beat the it one go, and go play the next game when the amazing story is still in your brain.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game that builds a bit on the Yakuza games' formula while doing some new things. Some things work really well, others not so much, but the important thing here is that, in my opinion, this is a solid first game on a series, that already shows so much promise.Like most Yakuza games, there's a lot to do here - some series staples may be missing, but there are a few new things too to compensate for them. Some of the added elements kinda feel like padding - like picking the keys for certain doors - but, well, it's all part of it being an experiment based on the series.Well worth playing for fans of the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series. For completionists, it's a pain to complete, like most games in this series.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Yakuza/Like a Dragon games, but this game disappointingly IS NOT Steam Deck-friendly enough to be falsely-advertised as "Verified". After getting to the point in the story where you unlock Essence Concoctions all Heat Actions have an extremely high chance of flat out crashing the game, and at worst making the Steam Deck restart itself. No amount of graphical settings seemed to make this problem less prominent. The Heat Action where you use it on an enemy on the ground to make Yagami kick them off the ground and into the air is the worst one which crashes 9/10 times, with the only times it doesn't seemingly have no logic to it. I use this Heat Action often in Judgement, so I can definitely say it was working fine up until that point where the game does a mini-tutorial on how Essences worked.I know it's not anything to do with a corrupted saved game or anything on my end because I swapped over to my PC and ran it there and I spent an hour or so doing as many Heat Actions as possible and not a single one had any crashes or issues with the same save file and everything. Then I go back to it on Steam Deck and it goes back to crashing frequently on using Heat Actions, especially the basic kick one. So this makes Judgement on Steam Deck unplayable for me because even if I don't use any Heat Actions, boss battles that are required to fight in the story force you into scripted Heat Actions, and there's no guarantee if those will crash on me or not. That sucks a lot because I bought Judgement and its sequels specifically to play on my Steam Deck, and them having the Verified by Steam would mean they work.Judgement might be an amazing game, but a massive Buyer Beware * on this game, especially if you are wanting to buy this specifically on a Steam Deck. Especially since this game-breaking bug was introduced to me 20 hours into the game which for other buyers translates to no easy refund. This game is by no means a safe "Steam Deck Verified" purchase, and if Valve happens to chance upon this review definitely change that at least until RGG patches stuff like this, because with stuff like this the game isn't even Playable status.If RGG happens to fix this I'll happily change my review, but as of right now the game is unplayable to me on what I was advertised to it would work on.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll try to keep this absolutely spoiler free, I hate receiving even the slightest spoilers about gameplay, story, even about the length of the game, so I'm not doing it to you. I'll not spoil yakuza either.Judgment, also known as Judge Eyes, and some other titles, is a spinoff to the yakuza series. If you haven't played the yakuza series, you really should, when I bought my first yakuza game years ago, I started basically non-stop playing more and more yakuza content for hundreds of hours until I ran out. This is that moment. I ran out. All of it was amazing, it reminded me of something that I almost forgot in the modern gaming industry: Games can be good, and full of passion and meaning, videogames can teach you something about life, and they can make you love people that don't even exist. The Judgment spinoff series does the same thing, but from a different perspective.This game advertises itself as a detective game, just like the sequel "Lost Judgment" does. I played Lost Judgement first, for some reason. In Lost Judgment, I felt disappointed with how little thinking it really requires of the player, how many crutches it gives you and how it never, not even once, actually requires you to do any real investigating. Somehow, the first game does this far better. I really enjoyed immersing myself into it.If you are interested in playing as a guy in a leather jacket who looks scary but has a good heart, and who is also a detective, you should buy this. You might just feel like I did when I started playing yakuza games, you might just get a new perspective on life, all while having a blast playing this game.Once you're done, maybe you could give the Yakuza/Like a Dragon mainline series a go, too. Now, here's a small spoiler unless you've already played the sequel, something of a warning if you, like me, play this after already having played Lost Judgment:The chase sequences are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ garbage. Really, they are complete ass. Remember how in Lost Judgment you had these super cool, energetic chase sequences where you had to exhaust the guy you're chasing and then catch them? Well this game has chase sequences too, but it doesn't matter whether you ♥♥♥♥ up and run into every single obstacle, or dodge them all. In this game, the guy running from you will slow down and even stop to wait for you if you fall behind, and if you're about to catch up to them, the guy you're chasing will simply speed up. They don't have a stamina bar, and you're not actually required to do anything. Almost every single chase sequence I had encountered during my 57 hours of playing, you didn't have to catch the target. Instead, the chase would just end once the guy you're chasing arrived at a certain position, the game would fade into a cutscene of you catching them. I saw the "catch" button prompt exactly once ingame and it didn't even work. Why the ♥♥♥♥??

_childDocuments_.review: Being locked out of the game due to Denuvo is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrible.TLDR; 7.5/10 for a RGG game but the story more than makes up for the lackluster side content.With that out of the way, this game is a mixed bag. The side cases are ok at best, tedious at worst, the friends system is nice but locking side cases behind friend progression makes it very tedious. The combat can feel stiff. The only thing holding this game together is the story. However, even then, you can't escape from the obnoxious tailing missions. _childDocuments_.review: i do recommend trying judgement if you’re already a fan of the yakuza series; however if you want to try an rgg game,, i still think yakuza 0 is your best betjudgement failed to really keep my interest in both its characters and its story. i was able to predict alot of the smaller twist and you often have to sit through what feels like hours of dialogue just to get a simple point acrossthe story and most side missions really failed to give me a reason to care for most of the characters, as i can’t really pinpoint how yagami or others have changed throughout the story. obviously yagami overcomes,, but i don’t feel any sort of connection to yagami in the slightest. besides repetitive story relays, the pacing is really screwed over by forced minigame sequences that help further the plot. which doesn’t sound all so bad, however these modes are super slow and not even that well fleshed out.  investigation sequences are the best and most immersive part of the game, but it loses its charm. the other two forced minigames are drone investigations and tailing sequences,, these are super super slow and often made me put the game down once i was done. while they’re a better alternative and more immersive way of storytelling than just plain cutscenes, it’s hard to enjoy these segments. judgement—like most of the other yakuza games— have a stellar soundtrack with excellently animated cutscenes and voice actingkamurochos friend/girlfriend system is one of the best additions of judgement, as more side content opens up and also really grounds you into the world. there are also a few real cameos from store owners, which really makes the world feel lived in. my only complaint with the girlfriend system is that it’s super bland, after they confess their love there is nothing to do with them furtherthe combat for this game had already been a bit spoiled for me, as i have already played The Man Who Sold His Name. However it’s still enjoyable for the most part. the game isn’t really balanced well around switching styles, as tiger style just does everything crane does, but better; as well as major upgrades to your fighting 99% of the time benefit tiger over crane. there are no specific upgrades for crane style, unlike tiger which has 3 specific upgrades that correlate with your damage boost.non of the minigames kept my interest as well. i will admit i am spoiled, y7 and others set such a high bar for side content,, but the drone racing minigame and [something] clan/gang were both boring and annoying at times. besides their specific minigames, theres only really gambling, darts, majong, and batting cages. i probably would’ve loved the combat if i had played judgement right after yakuza 6my thoughts on the ending: the court cases really were lackluster as i’m a huge fan of lawyer shows, we didn’t get nearly enough time doing some of the most fun and interactive parts of the game.the gimmicky incense system has its moments but ultimately just not a fun system to mess around with; id say it’s equivalent to the weapon searching family from yakuza 0definitely one of my least favorite rgg games, compares to y3 in terms of engagement and storythis game makes me not look forward to lost judgement, so my playthrough on that will be put on hold,, i’ll refine this review later but it’s super late and im so tired nightynight 🤙🤙

_childDocuments_.review: God I don't even know how I can describe Judgment from the other Yakuza games, because as much as I could recommend people to start with Yakuza 0 to start this series, Judgment might be an even better solution to the whole confusion of which one to start with."You never know where your choices will take you in life, Not giving up on it is the most important part"First of all, the opening song is just breath taking, It gets you into the game before you even know what to expect from it, it feels as if the game won't rise to the expectations that it is setting, and with the other installments of the series you'd think it could be kind of hard to top it, right?, Well you'd be proven wrong! The combat is better than the main series in my opinion and they even made it easier to get to 100% than the other games, the mini games are quite fun as expected (I'm at hour 56 of Mahjong, please help)"You ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, you think you can just say boobs all the time and not sound like a total jackass?"The side stories, or well, cases, in this game, are a riot yet again, They are not as goofy as some other Yakuza side quests, but they are up there, these are more on the wholesome side, there's quite a few hilarious but repeating ones, but that was something that I can deal with, well, besides the tailing missions, I was going to gouge my own eyes out if I had to do any more tailing mission after the main story and all the side stories. "We haven't had a job in a while, Let's do it right!" I'm gonna be honest, the story kind of lost me halfway, but then it picks up in force and drags you with it, and with that ending... man, it all ties up so nicely, then you get that beautiful ED sequence, which cannot be skipped, but I must tell you that if it was skippable and any of you skipped it, you would be dead to me.And when I realised it's all over, that's when this game really hit me, I kept setting such high expectations for it and going through it like "yeah it's fun but the others had this which was better and so and so".But no... man... the ending credits rolling made me realise how much I love this game. And now it has to amaze me yet again in Lost Judgment! I cannot wait!

_childDocuments_.review: Im writing my review as new player to the Yakuza franchise so please understand (Sorry in advance!)My issue with this game was that the story didnt start becoming interesting until chapter 11. I felt like I was tied to the back of a truck and dragged through the streets of Kamurochi against my will. I had to really fight through the story building. This feeling mainly stemmed from not having any connection to Tak, the protagonist. I felt more affinity to Kaito than Tak in early game. Because his backstory is left in the dark and we dont really seem much of it until late game, I was left wondering "Why does he care this much?". i felt like I was plopped into a drama that I had no business running in. For someone who spent much of his time doing odd jobs and such I didnt see why he felt so strongly about THIS case. Granted the story did end up becoming more interesting, by that time I was already exhausted by playing 18 hours of side missions and Keihin gang antics. I truly wish I could have enjoyed this game more. The combat was decent and the overall story was very well written , but for me the pacing was very off. I reached out to friends who loved the game to see if I was missing something and was told to just be patient but GYATDANG. For a 13 chapter story, to only really see the fruition of the plot in the last two chapters is mad. In the previous Yakuza games I played, what made me love them was the feeling of vengeance I was chasing all game. Whether it be a murder off rip or a betrayal, I would chase to the end of the game for my MC's retribution. I felt that this was missing for Tak. I didnt really care to see through the story UNTIL chapter 11 where more info is revealed. I will likely still continue to play through to Lost Judgement just to have all the Yakuza games complete but I am bummed that I seemed to have missed something of a gem here..

_childDocuments_.review: Really intriguing story and some of the best combat that the RGG games have to offer. Yagami is a cool guy. Kaito is a cool guy. The part where the game kind falls apart for me is the side content, substories, and specific game mechanics that are kind of smelly. The side content and minigames available are barebones, not very fun, and there isnt much variety.While the sidecases are entertaining and funny, the "friend" missions are tedious, boring, and unneeded, and i found myself near the end completing ignoring the friend missions altogether.certain mechanics like the mortal wounds and Keihin Threat meter sound good and interesting on paper but feel extremely lackluster and annoying in practice. The Keihin fights start off extremely easy and kind of just exist to minorly annoy you between substories, but by the later chapters the keihin fights are relentless onslaughts of high level enemies with firearms that either one shot you out of the blue on your way between objectives, or simply waste your time strong enemies with multiple healthbars who take away YOUR maximum HP that you can only recover by going to a specific location that is so out of way and cumbersome you might as well not even bother. other gameplay segments like the detective tailing are so mindnumbingly boring that its almost astonishing how much it gets reused and the game never shakes up the formula or does anything interesting with it. regardless, its a pretty good entry to the RGG world and a really solid 8.5/10 game, and despite my criticisms i still think the postives outweigh the effects of the negatives

They are quite boring and ruin the pacing a bit.Old fans of the series who didn't have the chance to play this on PC will definitely enjoy this. _childDocuments_.review: Judgment is a spinoff of the Yakuza game series, this time putting you into the role of a detective solving crimes revolving yakuzas.Action gameplay is rather similar to your Yakuza games. Game is set in Kamurocho and you'll fight small time crooks while playing optional mini games like baseball, darts, crane machine and more. What set this game apart is it also includes tailing and investigation elements. The main cases which progresses the story, and the side cases, often involves tailing suspects while trying to not let them discover you. At times, you might also have to look around the surrounding and find clues to your investigation. Game runs superb on the Steam Deck at near 60fps too, and great graphics. So why not?

_childDocuments_.review: The story is definitely not far of being a masterpice, as it manages to keep you engaged, and at the edge of your seat until the very end. The combat, while having its flaws, its enjoyable, and fun for the most part. Beating enemies while you style on them with flashy and powerful moves, while you break enviroments with their faces never gets old. The music is great, it immerses you into the situations that you are dealing with. From beating the ass of a yakuza on the street, to beating the ass of a prosecutor in court. The "weakest" aspect of the game would be the side stories. Some of them are hit or miss, depending on what you are looking for, and the game even forces some of said side stories, if you want to continue with the story, which kind of kills the pace if you ask me. The game also offers a lot of minigames, such as: Drone races, a Mario Party-like game, mahjong (idk why you would unironically want to play this), darts, and some others that I can't think of rn.Overall, the game manages to have a good balance in all of its aspects. While far from perfect, it's definitly worth a try if you are trying to get into the RGG way of doing games, if you are just looking for a game with a great story about crime, and mistery, or if you just want a game that doesn't end when the story ends.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the story it was coherent for the most part; a complot regarding a serial kiler that goes deeper the more you progress in the game, the combat is one of the best but it has few minor issues (enemies stop your combos if they block attacks).Things i disliked: Instead of making an entire new soundtrack sometimes they re-use tracks from previous games like Yakuza 6, the substories are not that interesting they lack variety, it almost feels formulaic; talk, tail then fight.Also the tailing missions become boring the mechanic gets shared between the campaign and substories, and they make less sense since you have a drone, why don't use that instead?!The campaign it's overall very good but it's very inconsistent with its pacing; One minute you are running to gather clues about a possible killer but first you need to figure out who ate a cake in the refrigerator or trying to fix a broken marriage of a random couple. _childDocuments_.review: One of the weakest games in the entire Yakuza series. It has some of the best combat and finishers in the entire series. It's has a great story that is actually connected better than some of the mainline games but the open world aspect of it feels forced in some ways. The game feels stretched out which is especially apparent in the later chapters. Things from having to wait for a phone call to progress or being forced to do boring side missions in order to wait for the main story missions to become available are annoying and gets old really quick. The game is also plagued with endless tailing missions which just make the game feel more boring and empty. The scripted dungeons in the streets and dungeons leaded to boss fights are repetitive and get old quick. There is even one level where you fight the same boss with a cane over 5 times and he just runs away to the next room with backup. The pacing of the story is also really bad thanks to those factors and the story doesn't really get fully engaging until the later chapters. You just get pulled from the main story when it starts to get interesting and get forced to do some pointless annoying side quest. These may seem like small little nit picks but they add up quickly and it took my over 8 months to fully finish this 30 hour game. Don't get me wrong it is a decent game but I don't think it deserves all the praise it gets. I only played the game so I can play Lost Judgement which as I have heard has fixed all these issued I have mentioned, with a better story and a more engaging open world and less annoying features. I think it would be better to skip this game and watch a youtube video summarizing it than buy to it for $11.99 on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Judgment

_childDocuments_.review: Having now played about 10 hours of Lost Judgment, I feel fairly confident that people should just start there and maybe come back to this one later. They recap enough of Judgment at the start of LJ to let you know who everyone is without spoiling the whole game. At least so far.Judgment feels like a transitional game very similar to Yakuza 3, where a lot of new features are being introduced and they don't really click until later entries in the series. Far too much of the game consists of boring tailing and running sections, the combat is pretty limited and the plot is all over the place. The game also has problems running above 60fps, where some minigames don't seem to work properly.It's not terrible, but unless you really fall in love with the characters of Lost Judgment and want to see where it all began, or are committed to playing every game RGG Studios release, this one can be skipped.

_childDocuments_.review: To quickly sum this game up. If you have ever played any of the Yakuza games, then you already know what you are getting into. The only difference is this game is less fighting and more strategy/matching. If you have never played one of those games, then consider this a detective game where everyone in the city hates you guts and you end up in a small fight every 5 minutes while doing favors for everyone while trying to solve several murder cases.The Yakuza line of games is a larger set of mini games in a collection. Sega has placed several of their own FULL games in the arcades and many others throughout the city. We are talking Outrun, Virtua Fighter 5, VR board games, Mahjong, and many many more.You play a detective who is helping out with a murder case. You are tasked with collecting evidence to prove the client is innocent. As you go through the events, you notice a larger issue that ultimately affects several groups, Yakuza, and citizens. With you partner in tow, you traverse the city streets looking for clues pummeling all who get in your way.The actual game does not take long to go through. However, the fun of this type of game is in the side missions. You will spend a considerable amount of time doing these and playing through all the arcade games.If you are looking for a a recommendation... I have played a Yakuza game and this one. I enjoyed this more as I was not fighting some super powerful Yakuza lieutenant every hour.

_childDocuments_.review: What starts out as a mystery story about a serial killer who gruesomely removes the eyes of their victims quickly turns into a compelling story of how much people are willing to sacrifice for the 'greater good'.Gameplay's good, though it's a little bit weaker than the main Yakuza game series.  In combat Yagami has two different stances he can use but only one's really worth using.  Furthermore 'SP', the currency used to upgrade and acquire skills, gets a bit difficult to acquire later in the game which can lead to some frustration.Still, the game's plenty of fun, there's lots to see and do.  There's a couple of rather creepy parts where you play as someone not Yagami, but on some level I feel like making the player feel a little creeped out was part of the point.  Overall, a very good action RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part, it's a pretty decent detective movie, but there are a lot of uninspired and irrelevant text-only side plots that interrupt the main story. As for when you're not leaning back eating popcorn, the combat runs with the traditional light/heavy/block/dodge setup and remains unremarkable even when the unlockable skills kick in. The detective mini-games are derivative and boring at best. In just the first few hours, the game reveals all the mechanics and limitations of its beyond-basic detecting gameplay. There's also way too much empty on-foot commuting. You're honestly better off watching the cutscenes on youtube than slogging through all of Judgment's tedium for bites of its whodunit story.

_childDocuments_.review: General tipsMoney seems tight at first, but a little ways into the plot, you'll unlock the VR mini-game (not real VR, the character goes into VR) and that can make you mad cash really fast.Unlike Yakuza, some of the side stories aren't found on the street. You'll unlock three location where you can check for detective jobs and you should visit them between every plot event.Tiger Style is better than Crane Style in almost every situation and gets a lot of upgrades from the skill tree. Unless you're trying to 100% the challenges checklist, you can stick to Tiger Style for pretty much the whole game.You can carry a limited amount of healing drinks and first-aid kits. The healing drinks don't really heal all that much so don't forget that you can hoard convenience store sushi, bento boxes, and ramen cups to help get through tough boss fights.Drone RacingDrone parts:Use the 250 point frame, not the QR one.The QR Code reward engine.Not the QR code propeller but the one with the highest speed.Use the lowest rank boost.Use the QR Code ESC unit.The Boost Start ability really helps. To trigger it hold down accelerate just before the 1 in the countdown appears. Not sure if the wind one has any effect in races. I had it maxed before I started seriously trying.Also there is a shortcut in one of the tracks. Whatever the 5th one in the Single Race listing is. After you come out of Millenium Tower you can hang a right through Little Asia. This is required for the Time Trial. This shortcut is not open on the reverse course.I'm not sure this does anything, but for me I found using the boost AFTER going through a ring was more effective. You have a few seconds while you are still sped up to hit the boost and get the barrel roll, effectively giving you an additional amount of time at top speed.Using the listed parts should put you at 250 points exactly. With this I was able to clear every Time Trial with a bunch of extra time. I was also able to finish the final GP in first reliably except for the final track, which has no boost rings. You can take a few hits, but still have to be careful in tight areas.Obviously you still have to have at least a little skill. Memorizing the courses and doing the Time Trials first is advised.You can exit and save between races.

_childDocuments_.review: Judgment is a spin-off of the Like A Dragon Series, where you play as Takayuki Yagami, an ex-lawyer-turned-private-investigator. The story of this game is really well-done. I can't spoil anything about it, but it does have a climactic ending, a captivating narrative along the way and interesting and memorable characters. For a spin-off, it's insanely good. The only noteworthy thing about the story is that neither Kazuma Kiryu, nor any of the other more known characters of the Like A Dragon universe make any appearance in the game. And since it plays out in 2018, you might spot some interesting changes around Kamurocho.The visuals are fantastic. The Dragon Engine really kicks off with particles, lighting and physics here just like it did in Yakuza Kiwami 2. Not much has changed in graphics apart from every menu looking somewhat "modernized" to give off a bit of a futuristic feel. The music is also pretty atmospheric and accurate to the situation. Since Yagami is a private investigator, most of the music will have a tune of figuring something out, thinking, revealing new information or simply investigating. And the fighting soundtrack is also very on-point.The gameplay really sticks out in this game. Yagami has two fighting styles: Crane and Tiger style. The blue Crane style is a group fighting style with foot-sweeps and broad roundhouse kicks to hit multiple enemies, while the Tiger style is a one-on-one fighting style with fast and powerful punches. Being able to use both styles at the same time makes for very fluid combat as well as being able to use all the unlocked fighting skills at all times. They even made a Crane and Tiger theme when fighting on the streets like in Yakuza 0!The skill tree is also very interesting. You have three trees to skill out: Abilities, Battle and Special. The red Abilities tree is the most essential tree for survival, damage-dealing and EX-charging. Yeah, it's called EX Action here, not Heat Action anymore. Hence, why the skills here are pretty expensive. You can unlock new moves and individual EX Actions in the purple Battle tree. And to cap it off, the green Special tree houses all other miscellaneous skills, like better friendship influence, easier Tailing, better Lockpicking and whatnot.Exploration has also become a thing in this game, as after a certain two chapters, you'll be able to find miscellaneous items lying around in Kamurocho, which can be used as crafting materials to make new Drone Parts as upgrades for Drone Races or several other miscellaneous items to create a variety of Extracts.Extracts are this games way of compensation for not being able to carry Gear or Weapons. Yagami doesn't uses blades or guns, but he can buff himself temporarily with devastating movesets or battle effects. But listing them all here wouldn't do it justice. There a quite a lot of extracts and they usually spice up the already known moves of Yagami a bit.Since this is a Like A Dragon title, there's also a Completion List, sort of. It's called KamuroGo and is an app on Yagami's phone. There, you can check for what you have already completed and what you still haven't done toward the 100% checkmark. This includes eating every dish in every restaurant, playing every minigame and achieving certain feats and so on.The only scary thing about 100%-ing this game is not knowing when to do what. There are three unique Mahjong establishments with their own completion requests as well as 3 in-game-emulated fighting games which you have to somewhat master. But the difficulty curve isn't as bad as it used to be. If you're already familiar with straight up ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this game's minigames should be a breeze. There's just a lot to do.Also do me a favor and find those cats, alright?

_childDocuments_.review: The Yakuza series had massive success with its spinoff Like a Dragon. While it had flaws it was entertaining and had great characters and a detailed story. The entire Yakuza franchise excels in the storytelling and character development department. Judgment is no different. You play as the lawyer turned-detective Tavo Kagami trying to rid of his demons and upturn a bunch of corrupt politicians. An Alzheimer's cure and a murder mystery are at the center of this. The story is well constructed and kept me on the edge of my seat at every turn. The entire story has chapters ending on cliffhangers like addictive binge-worthy TV shows. I always wanted to know what was going to come next. At many points, it felt that Yagami and co. were backed into a corner and I didn't see any way out only for the story to twist and turn in crazy ways.I don't want to say too much about the story as any small detail can spoil it. Just know that this is the strongest point of the game and what makes it worth sticking through the 30+ hour game for. The second reason is the characters. There are many and they are well-acted and have great backstories. They are slowly introduced throughout the game and by the end, I either loved them or hated them. Tavo himself is a well-rounded character that's stubborn and unwilling to back down from anything. I really liked the personalities of each character. They were unique and interesting and they all stood out in their own way. For such a large cast this is usually hard to pull off or not done well enough. As for the gameplay, this is where Judgment falters and the entire Yakuza series lacks here in every entry in some way. You get to run around in this open...map called Kamarucho. I don't want to say open world because it's just a small city that can be run across in about 2-3 minutes. It's a city full of crime and underground misdeeds. What's the point of the open city? I don't really know. Mostly for side quests, but I always found these to be underwhelming and repetitive in the Yakuza series. There are a few types. First off are actual side cases which net you more SP and cash. That's bout it. They are mostly uninteresting and don't advance the story or characters at all. There are friend events spread throughout which net you skills that can be unlocked, SP, and cash. These are the two main types of side quests you can partake in and I did finish most side cases just for the SP and cash. You really need cash to buy healing items and stay stocked up.There are taxis spread throughout to help with fast travel. With such a small area you would think it's pointless but it's great to avoid fights on the streets. These are randomly occurring and you can usually run from them and you should. I felt it hindered progress and after the third chapter, it didn't net enough SP to be worth bothering with. Eventually, you will be wanted by street gangs and your threat level will increase unless you stop a boss-type enemy. This never goes away and will always go back to 100% so I just ignored them. There are also side activities that are mostly used for dating. That's another side quest that I didn't find interesting. You can meet girls through friend events or side cases and later date them by presenting presents. Side mini-games like batting, darts, and gambling can be fun to an extent, but when are mini-games like this ever fun to go back to? It's just filler content and for achievement hunters really. It doesn't advance the story or add to it in any way I just felt like all of these side activities/missions were chores to complete.Let's get into combat. It's flawed for sure. While it looks cool and it's simple to understand it suffers from unresponsive controls and animations that don't interrupt when you input a command. I always felt like my button presses were delayed. There are two fighting stances. Tiger for one-to-one fights and Crane for multiple enemies. You can pick up objects and hit people with them and there's a special EX finishing move that you can perform which is key to winning tougher fights. You also have an EX boost which unlocks more powerful combos and increases your defense. Again, a key thing to use to win fights. I just felt like no matter what I did I couldn't master the system. There is a block and dodge button, but it seems that the enemies are magnetized to you because no matter how much I dodge or run away they always follow me and connect their attacks. It makes boss fights especially infuriating. While I had plenty of items I could use at my disposal to help I wish I could rely more on my skill, but the fighting system just doesn't allow it.There are other small annoyances such as mortal wounds. These lockout parts of your health bar and the only thing in the game that can fix this are med-kits which are rare and cost a lot of money. There's only one person that can heal you and they're sold underground in a sewer. Of course, you have to go through the animation of opening the sewer great, sliding down a ladder, running down the sewer, and then the same thing going back up. Just cut all of this out! I also found the game way too long. It's padded with a ton of fights throughout the main story and I wish a lot of this was cut out. There are easily 10 hours of fights just in the main story. Nothing breaks this up, however. There are repetitive detective events like searching for objects in first-person, chase scenes and tailing people. My god, do these get old quickly. Tailing missions are never fun in games and these are dragged out for sometimes over five minutes. You can hide behind objects and that's about it. Just don't fill the suspicion meter. All of these mini-games are just incredibly repetitive and could have been cut out.The game at least looks decent. It's a PS4 port so some parts look rough. There are some textures that look like PS3-era stuff, but at least the facial animations and character models are really good. There's lots of detail everywhere, but don't expect this to push your hardware to its limits. It mostly looks very realistic and sterile with not much in the way of artistic flair. It looks like a modern-day Japanese city.Overall, Judgment excels in storytelling and character development but falters in gameplay. The fighting is stiff and unresponsive, the mini-games are repetitive and pad out the hours, and I felt the detective work in the courtroom was a missed opportunity. The open city is an excuse to throw side cases and missions at you that are meaningless and just pad gameplay. Random city fights are annoying and get in the way of progress, and the visuals aren't much of an upgrade. What's here works, but I mostly stayed for the story. If it had a bad story this game would be barely above average, however, it's one of the best and most detailed video game stories I've seen in recent years.

_childDocuments_.review: The game I was waiting for RGG to port with the fear of it never seeing the light of day. With all the drama revolving around a PC port I'm glad it happened.Judgement's story is very reminiscent of japanese crime thrillers that I have watched in the past and this is definitely not a short coming. I loved the layers of the story that continue to unravel as you progress. The game's story starts off slowly until it just turns into one this one huge finale that just gets the heart pumping. I love the bond that Yagami and the boys form and the collaboration between them to solve the case is probably one of my favourite story tropes. I just love a good brotherhood. The tailing missions are probably the worst part of this game. Although the feel of it is cool it can quickly get repetitive and frustrating. I think they would have been better if there were more QTE sections and more cinematic moments to make it feel more slicker rather than just slowly walking behind a target that takes forever to reach their destination. Minor issues aside, I have nothing but praise for this series. It is definitely solid game to pick up. The final part of the game was so damn good! The judge men truly judged with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let people tell you this game has good combat, because it doesn't. It feels like Yagami weighs about 400lbs and he's as responsive as a man who is heavily drunk.God help me, I'm never buying another RGG game in my life. Every single time I go in with my expectations on the floor in terms of mechanics, and every time the game stomps them into the tiles to get them just a bit lower than I thought was possible. How is it that a studio that has been around this long has never made a beat-em-up system that's even half as good as something like the Batman or AC games? Those aren't even that good, they're just simple, but this is both SIMPLE and CLUNKY at the same time. If you want the combat to have weight and commitment, it needs to be consistent so the player can make good choices. If you want the combat to be skill-based, it needs to be responsive and feel good to use or else nobody is going to want to play it. These are simple ideas that nearly every game studio understands, but apparently not RGG.Judgment's combat doesn't understand any of this. Yagami takes inputs more like suggestions half the time and his slow action speed paradoxically makes avoiding mashing very hard. Hitting the buttons too slowly will interrupt your combo, but hitting them too fast will end up queuing more attacks than you intended if you want to play technically, so the best option is just to mash and build your basic strategy around that. Worse still, Judgment eats inputs sometimes, killing the responsiveness. One of the first upgrades to cancel a combo with a dash barely functions at all because it only works at specific timings that are probably very tight based on what I experienced in my hour of play.I get why Y0 was a bit clunky, the engine was old, but this is not an old engine. Yet, it's even worse than Y0, and I returned Y0 because the combat was bad. I dunno man, I want to like these games. On paper, they sound like games I would like. However in practice, every time I've played one of RGG's games my only takeaways have been shock at their mechanical incompetence and disappointment at the wasted potential.As I said for Y0, for the story, there's always Youtube.
