_childDocuments_.review: Lost Judgment is the sequel to Judgment, and another spin off from the Yakuza series. While investigating accusations of student bullying at a high school, player character Takayuki Yagami is asked to look into a murder case which might also have links to the school.•	Lost Judgment mostly takes place in the Ijincho area of Yokohama, which was the setting for the Like A Dragon game starring Ichiban Kasuga, but you’ll get to spend some time back in Kamurocho as well.•	Like the previous game, the third person melee combat is played in real time. There are now four different fighting styles (tiger, crane, snake and boxer), which are intended to be used in different situations, but honestly I just stuck with snake for most of the game, while playing on the hard difficulty. It feels kinda similar to the Arkham games, where pressing block at the correct time leaves enemies vulnerable to a counter attack. There’s also a very useful move where you can grab enemies who are wielding weapons to disarm them. And some special moves can be triggered on enemies who are scared of you, which causes Yagami to punch or kick the air beside their head to make them faint in terror, which looks really funny.•	Main story, which focuses on bullying and flaws in the legal system, is well written, fully voiced, and voice acting is excellent. Yagami continues to be a very likeable protagonist, while his allies who return from the first game are also interesting characters.•	In addition to the main story, there are lots of substories featuring PI cases and wacky situations, some of which involve hour long investigations, or have multiple parts.•	Many of the entertainment minigames seen previously in the Yakuza series are included again such as golf, baseball, darts, VR dice game, House of the Dead style shooter, and various Sega arcade games. Plus there’s a new Geometry Wars style twin stick shooter, and Yagami has a Master System console in his office in Kamurocho where you can play 10+ old games.•	I didn’t have any problems with bugs, crashes or framerate, and the controls work well most of the time on my xbox 360 gamepad.•	Lost Judgment also features a lot of content related to a secondary investigation, where Yagami is asked to join 10 different clubs that all have a connection to school students, and a criminal mastermind called the Professor. These clubs all have their own lengthy storylines and contain unique minigames.•	This secondary storyline is significantly longer than the main story, but this isn’t necessarily a good thing. Most clubs take around 4-5 hours each to complete, which eventually made the game feel bloated, while also hurting the flow of the main story. In total it took me 83 hours to finish the game, and I haven’t started the Kaito Files DLC yet. •	For example, to complete the boxing club storyline you need to defeat more than 20 opponents. To complete the motorcycle club storyline you need to win 16 races. The dance, robotics and skateboard clubs all require you to do multiple practice matches before each round of their tournaments. In robotics you can customise your robots with various parts and you’ll probably need to grind a few more practice matches to earn crafting components. Its really excessive and feels repetitive.•	Some of the minigames are quite easy. Dance is a rhythm game similar to Haruka’s in Yakuza 5. In skateboarding you have to ride around a skate park and perform tricks to earn points. In Esports you’ll play the Sega arcades version of Virtua Fighter 5 Showdown. Boxing (more challenging but thankfully I did win every fight on my first attempt) is like a 3D Street Fighter.•	However, the robotics and motorcycle clubs both have poorly designed control schemes and feature difficult opponents. Robotics is a 3v3 battle where you have to collect and place tetris blocks to capture territory on a grid, and motorcycle involves death races where you have to knock several other riders off their bikes while they attack you with molotovs, baseball bats, etc, and then race a boss to the finish line. Any time I lost a match more than once I quickly started to feel frustrated, knowing that I was still quite far from completing the game.•	Meanwhile, these school club storylines feature a lot of dialogue related to unnecessary subplots. Every club has multiple members, there’s usually a rival club which also has multiple members, every one of these characters has a tragic backstory, or an issue with a family member or a romantic interest or an internal club conflict, and in between every round of the minigames, yet another of these dozens of minor characters wants to spend several minutes discussing their feelings with you. I value story more than many gamers, but even for me these storylines started to lose my interest because of how much they dragged on with pointless conversations that didn’t connect in any way to my actual investigation of the Professor. Lost Judgment does have some good moments and I still recommend playing it if you’re a fan of the series, but if I had to rank all the Yakuza and Judgment games, I’d put Lost Judgment near the bottom of the list.While the combat is fun and the variety of different activities is interesting for a while, the number of times you need to play and win each minigame eventually feels repetitive and grindy, while the number of hours it takes to do so has a negative impact on the pacing of the main story, which is usually a key strength of this franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Goes unbelievably hard, buy it and play it nowHaving not beaten Lost Judgment on console so I could wait for it on PC, I'm very happy with my choice, as Lost Judgment improves on the gameplay presented in Judgment in almost every single way. Combat might be at its peak across the whole Yakuza/Like a Dragon/Judgment series, with four styles to choose from, fleshed out upgrades, and amazing animation it feels incredible. I've never looked out for fights as much in other games in the series like I do in Lost Judgment. You also spend a good amount of time early on beating up school kids (amazing). It's absolutely PACKED full with content, with most returning activities given extra polish and depth and a ton of new activities that are all fun and engaging. Side stories, clubs, school stories, mini games, you can even buy old Sega master system carts and play a variety of games in your office. Tons of quality of life features like the skateboard especially are very welcome. Alongside that, a lot of the stuff that received criticism from the first game for over staying their welcome like the Tailing missions are surprisingly improved and also a lot less frequent. The detective features in this game are much more fleshed out in comparison to Judgment. You can start investigation at any time even in the open world and in missions, and you have new tools including a sound amp, a noise detector, and a dog to carry out your detective work. Ijincho from Yakuza: Like a Dragon returns as the main city this time, however you have the ability to go back to Kamurocho at any time. Both of them are looking better than ever with updated lighting, effects, and density, making this the best looking game in the series bar none. Audio is great, with both quality English and Japanese voices. The soundtrack in this game is INSANE though, with some of the best music from the entire series. I've played every mainline game in the series to completion except for this one and this game's OST sets a high bar.PC Port is great, but has some stability issues. Runs great and looks great but for some reason when I play the VR mini game, I've crashed 3 times alone just in that mode, and never crashed outside of that. There's also a weird black flickering only during night time that is rare but noticeable. Both can be easily patched soon I'm sure but just making it known.The story is the only thing comparable in quality to the first Judgment game, which is a fairly solid bar to reach for. The first Judgment had a lot more moments that stand out as great set pieces with events unfolding through the entire game and constantly evolving until the very last second of the story even if it did have a lot of moments where it was taking a while to get going or it felt like they tried to pad out the story length. Lost Judgment's story on the other hand feels more emotionally intense. It grabs you from the get go and feels like the developers are making this game to say a lot of things that they truly feel strongly about, which is very refreshing to experience, even if the latter third of the game feels like it might run out of steam after all the secrets and plot points are revealed. I'd say it's very subjective as to which story is better, even if they are both great stories. But I prefer the faster pace, the character arcs, the themes, and the villains in Lost Judgment over the original myself. I wouldn't hold it against anyone for preferring the first though. I'm a humongous fan of the Yakuza/Like a Dragon/Judgment series, they're all great fun without an outright terrible entry to be found. However playing Lost Judgment makes the original Judgment look like a proof of concept demo in comparison, and even makes some of the other Yakuza games look like ancient relics. Cannot recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: It is infuriating to me that RGG studios goes on to make one of the best combat systems ever and then does everything it possibly can to divert player's attention and total playtime from that.Lost Judgment is a game full of varied content to do and it is what this game suffers from the most. It is obvious that this is the product of cultivation of both years of preceding RGG games and a great effort. There are more than 30 minigames in this game and tons of other things to do. So, what is the problem then?1- Minigames are hardly play-tested or ever balanced. In any minigame with AI opponents, from classics like Mahjong or Poker to new minigames like drone racing or motorcycle races, AI will cheat %100 of the time and you have to use specific anti-AI tactics to win. It does not matter how good you play the minigames, if you don't specifically play around AI's cheats, you are going to lose.2- Even if you don't wish to complete everything and it's just that you want to see every cutscene instead, you are going to play a good chunk of those 30 minigames. Now, look, let's say that they were all perfectly made minigames (They are not); no one is going to like every single one of them. If you lock certain content behind those minigames, you have to make sure that every single one of them are as enjoyable as rest of the game. Unfortunately, they are not and although there were some of them I liked to play as much as the base game, there were an equal amount of, perhaps even more, minigames I absolutely detested playing. And that will be the case for a lot of people. You can't expect people to like all of those minigames.3- After all those complaining about abundance of minigames, this might sound ironic but: Lost Judgment needed another minigame, or I should say, a content where you actually can play the game's brilliantly made fun combat system. RGG studios, in their infinite wisdom, decided to remove Arena from Judgment series albeit it was present in its predecessors. Hell, Like a Dragon: Gaiden has just came out and Arena plays a major role in that game. Why wouldn't they just let us play the game in an environment tailored to test our skills? Currently, if you wish to play the game itself after finishing the main story, there are only 2 options: You either have to go around streets, beating up laughably weak punks or you have to go into Gauntlet mode from main menu, in which you are limited in all aspects (Which items you may use, which combat styles you may use etc.). Ironically, in this game that is full of content to do, there is no content to fight against strong enemies, using everything we have farmed for so far.I know the first 2 points are present in all RGG studios' games but I have not written a review for them so I'm mentioning them here, since they also apply to Lost Judgment. As for third point, it's truly unfortunate that they withhold such content from us in the game that's considered to have the best combat of the entire series by majority of the RGG fanbase. And rightfully so, Lost Judgment has 4 vastly differing combat styles, all fleshed out and fun-to-play with. Although they could have done a better job with style-switching buttons. It was far better in Yakuza 0 whereas styles were assigned to all different buttons rather than a single button to switch to them in-order, one-by-one.That all being said, I wrote all these because I truly like this game and I would have loved it if they had added the missing pieces because all the potential was there. Lost Judgment is a great game and worth both your time and money. In case you may want to skip all the side content, you still have 35 hours of main story to play to your heart's content.

_childDocuments_.review: So much better than Judgment but not there at the top with Yakuza 0 and 7.I felt like GTO Onizuka for a part of it, this was so good, i wished Ryu Ga Gotoku woud make such a game where the High school part is the main focus.    ---- Lost Judgment does everything better than Judgment. Right from the beginning , fighting feels faster and more responsive, and the change of scenery for Yokohama is more than welcome.   No more being stuck in the tiny and oppressive Kamurocho. Secondly, the game is split between the main story and the optional School story, so there's a good deal of content if you don't skip it.  Before writing about the story, i want to mention some of the other changes, improvements and new things that have been added.  _An entirely optional Story tied to the School that takes a bit of grinding _Plenty of new side quests, and several new gadget that are needed for them, like a signal detector._2 new fighting style, Snake and Boxing (included DLC ); Snake being so strong that i almost only used it past a certain point. _Lots of new minigames related to the School, some of them being good, some of them very tedious._Drone racing has been improved. The drone on the other hand has barely any use during the main story._Yokohama being much larger than Kamurocho, you can use a Skateboard to move around faster, with the ability to do some tricks._The Keyholder has been completely removed, and one the lockpiciking minigame too._There is humor from time to time, but this is still far from Yakuza._The events of Judgment are barely mentioned,  making it a lot more optional to play it prior._There's tons of minigames like in every other games from the same studio that are completely optional !About the high school/main story ; _Despite being a bit grindy and tedious, the High School part of the game is what i liked the most ! Some of the clubs were engaging, some of the mini games where actually quite fun, some not and the whole plot surrounding this was enjoyable. I felt very attached to the students near the end, and the last part , to unravel the mystery was very heartwarming !_The main story is better, but also has a pacing problem. Unlike in Judgment though, here, things are going too fast. Probably not to make a game too long i think, but i felt most of the chapters were very short !From the beginning, with the informations you are given, you can very quickly find what the end goal for the whole situation is, so it is more about finding all the steps and means that served to create such situation, and there was some good surprises here, which is something the first game is missing a lot.Near the end, the focus is once more about questioning the player about their perception of Justice.  This time though, several events in the game pushes you very hard on one side, which i found a bit disappointing.The characters implicated in the events felt much move likable and relatable too.Conclusion : I liked this game to the point i would recommend it without having played Judgment. The story is nice, a bit on the short side, but it is compensated by the optional storyline tied to the High School. Some clutter has been removed, some added, tons of side content and minigames, all that bundled in the quality that this studio is known for. A very good game !

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games that RGG made. They improved the game's combat by reworking the Crane style and refining the juggling system from the first Judgment game and in addition with the two new styles: Snake and Boxer. Boxer is more of an optional style since it's part of the School Stories Expansion DLC and it's toggleable in the options. Nevertheless, it's still a pretty good style for initiating juggle combos.Compared to Judgment the game is way larger, it has a new city region Ijincho, a separate side story named "School Stories" which consists 10 different clubs with each having their own unique story. The lowlights for School Stories are Biker Gang and Photography Club. Completing Photography Club forces you to be Stealth mode to get to the designated destination before taking a photo and it's not a one time occurrence. Biker Gang takes too much time to complete it and the camera placement in the minigame is such a weird choice. Speaking of minigames, there are plenty of them that you can do here and it's much easier to get cheat items while completing achievements.The story overall is not as great as Judgment's but it's still decent compared to other Yakuza games' . As mentioned previously, the stealth sections ruin the flow progressing through the story and you can still fail them pretty easily. The boss fights and long battles here are awesome with the game's improved combat. _childDocuments_.review: Another Yakuza game down in the 100% books. While not as annoying to do as a Yakuza 5 this game was tedious in many completion regards like the 50 hour professor side case lmao. Anyway this review will be about the game itself and not as a completionist. Spoilers belowFirst of all, the story. - While not my favourite game due to repetitive tasks, this is my favourite plot line in the yakuza series so far, beating like a dragon, 0 and 2 for me. The continuous theme of bullying and suicide is something that yakuza usually doesn't tackle as its main focus is usually on bizarre evil yakuza plot twists or corrupted police. This game also has my new favourite yakuza villain in Kuwana as he is genuinely the most grey shaded antagonists in terms of motives and desires. The line of good and evil is so blurred that your main bro Kaito even says he doesn't know who is right at the start of the final battle and he leaves you to it. Not to mention that masterpiece of a tear jerker send off where everything he tried to protect falls apart and the characters around him apologise for making him keep such a dark secret for 13 years. Him crying out is heartwrenching as he just balls with tears post Yagami fight.- Yagami is also here but his character development is not as deep as the previous title and kaito takes much more of a backseat as well, but i think this is what makes Kuwana shine the most. Another massive positive is how they dont do the bad guy turns good then dies trope at the end, bro doesnt even get arrested, he just walks off into the shadows, i loved it.- Literal Only complaint with the story is how Soma has Yagami and Kaito dead as ♥♥♥♥ in the bar but he just leaves after the bar owner calls and there is just no good defence for that (yes i know its Kuwana dad).- Also Soma goes on a mad killing spree. Gotta be the most deaths in any yakuza game including the Kaito files. I like it, feels like they took Saejimas advice to Kido from 4 and got their balls outContent/Gameplay:- While there is no karoke there are plenty of activities for you to partake in with yagami. A lot of the dumb detective trailing stuff is back but it was toned down from the first game. Some of the questionable observation gimmicks return like "turn on the lights" lol. In my opinion the school professor storyline, while fun, was not worth taking up 40ish hours as it ate up side quests. Of the 42 side quests 13 have to do with one illegal detective agency as well which was very boring. Some quests ended after literally 1 minute, no joke. School def ate development here. While i sound harsh here its because this is all my complaints, i got nothing else besides some of the tedious side content as a completionist and some boring side cases.- Also, Snake style is the best style in the series, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. so cool.Kaito Files:- Idk how much this dlc cost on release but for the sale bundle i got it was worth it as i enjoyed it more than the yakuza 2 majima story dlc. Nice to see old fighting styles return with kaito and i love how on stealth missions you can get caught and still knock the guy out unlike yamagi because you are a brute. Also, instead of running around crowds kaito pushed them away in chase missions XD. Made me laughConclusion/Summary- Game is excellent, my fav yakuza story and second fav overall yakuza game after 0. While not my top 3 protagonist, Yagami has the best side cast in the series hands down. I hope they will release a third game down the road or have these characters make a return in a mainline game. If you like judgement 1 this is a must buy since it has improved the formula in every regard.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Judgment is, without a doubt, one of the best RGG games available on Steam. Being a sequel to Judgment, a Yakuza spinoff, it brings back the brawler style with revamped gameplay, flow and freedom. With 3 main styles to switch from (Crane, focused on AOE and mobility; Tiger, focused on one on one fights with devastating charge attacks; and Snake, focused on parryin and style) and an extra previously DLC only style (Boxing, focused on dodges and combo freedom), there's a lot to mess with. Returning from Like a Dragon is Yokohama, with the newly added Senryo High, and a slightly tweaked Kamurocho. Overall, the sequel is a pretty good improvement on gameplay, sound, mechanics (for the most part) and minigames.A lot of the extra content in the first game was cut: the friend system was removed, the girlfriend is only half implemented and side cases are also fewer. However, where the development teams cuts in content, they make it up in gameplay. Yagami's moveset has been improved, with pretty much every style being excellent in any fight, specially with the increased attack speed, instant style swapping, easier juggling and buffs that are awarded for style variety. The combat improvement makes Yokohama a playground for Tekken style fights, where the Boxing style shines the most, with it's freedom of combos: no longer is Yagami restrained to specific moves and sequences in styles, now Yagami can just do a variety of different attacks based on buytton prompt and not on X X Y Y sequences.Story isn't as good as the first Judgment, but it's still a pretty good mistery, with a lot of twists and one of the best villains in a videogame.Soundtrack is excellent, with a great variety of genres, with the main composers from previous Yakuza games returning to deliver some of the best beasts in the series.Overall, Lost Judgment may very well be the best "brawler" game from RGG, but needs to be played after Judgment, due to how good the combat is compared to the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: Old Review: while i did do a full review for Judgment, this game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing that you should just buy the game right away.Actual Review:So continuing from the first game Judgment (Judge Eyes), they decided to absolutely hit the ball out of the park with Lost Judgment, with a location change from Kamurocho to Ijincho from Yakuza: Like A Dragon (Yakuza 7) as well!Getting into gameplay, the Crane and Tiger Styles return from the first game, with some new improvements, Crane has gotten buffed to the point that it's actually now really good, and it actually has upgrades instead of being left out because of the other upgrades going to Tiger in the first game. Tiger also gets improved with some new skills and charged attacks being apart of the base style instead of a separate skill like the first game, however flux fissure isn't as broken as it was in the first game but still pretty good. The Snake Style is one of the new styles being added to the mix, which is basically Tanimura's style from Yakuza 4 but improved upon and more focused on parrying and the opening you can make with that, you can also disarm opponents that have weapons (unless they're a boss enemy) but sometimes I wished that if you failed it, you just grab them instead. The Boxer Style that was originally DLC in the Console Release is now an actual style that comes with the game, and it's really good for stunning your opponents and just laying waste on to them. but you can turn it off in the settings if you like having 3 styles instead. Each style has their own Secrets and Counters which is pretty nice, Crane has a counter that launches enemies into the air opening a juggle combo, and the secret allows you to dodge an attack and gain temporary boost in combo speed, Tiger has Crushing Tiger Fist which is definitely not Tiger Drop renamed and reanimated, and the secret allows you to do extra damage after a charged hit, Snake has the worst counter as you can only use it when your EX is empty, the secret makes you immune to being knockdowned after a parry, Boxer has THREE counters for jabs, hooks, and straights, which they all do their own ailments as well, the secret makes it so your EX meter charges more faster after a counter, oh and btw each secret can be used outside their styles, so you can use crane to dodge an attack then switch to tiger and do a charge attack and vice versa.The story of Lost Judgment is fantastic, while most people will definitely enjoy Judgment's story more than this game's, this story shouldn't be slept on since its one of RGG's best stories out there at the moment, the school is interesting part of the story (you also get to beat up high school children) and yeah there is some pacing issues in the middle, and a certain someone getting mentioned by Yagami every 15 seconds in the finale, but the villains of the story are incredible, and the final boss goes REALLY HARD in terms of both characters, atmosphere, moral, and it's music.The Side Content of Lost Judgment is definitely some of the best Side Content we have gotten as well, while there isn't as much Side Cases in Kamurocho since the game takes place mostly in Ijincho, the School Stories are a great addition to the bunch. Each School Story has it's own minigame that you can play to progress through them, and they all have their own respective characters as well, it's a really fun time, my favorite being the Boxing Story, and my least favorite being Robotics Story (i hate it alot). There are 42 Side Cases in Base Lost Judgment, but since the PC release includes all of the DLC (except Kaito Files) it goes up to 54, but you only need to do the base Side Cases and all School Stories to fight this game's secret boss, as the other 12 cases from the DLC are connected to Girlfriends.So talking about detective stuff, they pretty much took out half of the gimmicks from Judgment, no more rotating lockpicking, there's only one Tailing Segment in the story, Active Search Mode is a lot more better, Chasing is more like Yakuza 4 and 5, with the draining health bar and comically large Staminan X on the streets. Overall most of the detective stuff has been improved in this game, and they also dialed down them in the main story, even improving Tailing Segments to have a nice new Act Natural button that you can hold, but they also made it so you can't make that many mistakes anymore, and then they pretty much threw every single one they made into the Side Content.Now talking about the PC Port as I played this game on PS4 and then PS5, basically you get all of the DLC except kaito files, so you're getting the best experience of the game with no extra cost, and just like Judgment you also have pretty good optimization.Overall, for those who have never played a yakuza game and returning fans of the series, I would 100% recommend this, however I recommend also to play Judgment first so you have a better understanding of the characters. also soundtrack is a banger

_childDocuments_.review: (Everything I talked about in my review for Judgment still applies here.)Here's the thing about Lost Judgment. Yes, there is a fair amount of tonal whiplash between the silly and serious parts of the game.But do you know what it also has? One of the best hand-to-hand combat systems in any game, a densely-packed open world full of experiences every corner with no room left for boredom, and a very powerful narrative carried by a memorable cast that will take you from start to finish holding your interest the whole way.The gameplay is worth it, the story is worth it, and you will walk away from this game not only having had a lot of fun, but also having experienced a real ride of emotions that few other games of this genre can give you.Play it. _childDocuments_.review: Lost Judgment is another masterpiece in a string of them by RGG Studio. It's the absolute pinnacle of brawler combat, the story is unbelievably engaging, the side content is deep, varied, and almost always incredibly fun, and the total package the game offers is basically unparalleled by anything else the studio has ever made. It's good.The combat is probably the biggest, brightest selling point - Yagami's three base styles mesh together extremely well, and you can find situations to maximize them all throughout the game. Tiger is as good as ever with the addition of charged moves, Crane is actually very useful now in its intended crowd setting, and Snake is maybe the most satisfying combat style RGG has ever put together. Even with Tiger and Crane being great, I had to force myself to use them from time to time and not just sit in Snake from the moment I unlocked it. The flow of it is just amazing, and you're given fantastic combat situations throughout, too - powerful, tricky bosses that make you feel accomplished for figuring out how to get around them, while you can simply smoke regular encounters on demand, and with mortal wounds gone (thank God), you don't have to worry about putting the game on hold to go restore your full health bar after getting randomly shot by some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the street. Perfect!The story...easily one of the best, of course, with a great deal of nuance and grey areas for the player to mull over as the story progresses. I'd say it's not quite as satisfying or viscerally gripping as Judgment's, but it's hard to live up to the strongest, most focused story RGG Studio's ever made, and even then, Lost Judgment does an admirable job in keeping me engaged. The returning characters develop, the new characters fascinate, and there are plenty of amazing twists and moments of absolute satisfaction that kept me locked in for hours and hours. The primary antagonist has a ton of layers, and the supplementary antagonists all spiral outwards from them in myriad ways that conveyed a strong, clear message about the story RGG Studio was telling here. Even if I personally find the antagonist a lot more reprehensible than others do, they were written astoundingly well, and the game hinges on that success.I LOVE the side content this time around - most of it is centered on the School Stories, which basically functions as a second campaign meant to be played through alongside the main story. Amasawa is such a sweet girl, and the stories told through each of the clubs you explore tie pretty well into the game's core themes of the price of bullying and who gets to pass judgment on wrongdoers. Each club has its own minigame associated with it, and while most of these are fun and well-developed, a couple of them were significantly more frustrating and needed better balance. This is about the Robotics Club. It should have been deleted. There's no salvaging it. The rest of the clubs, though? Great. Skateboarding, love it. Boxing, AMAZING. Dancing that's mechanically similar to Haruka's idol minigame? Fantastic. Cooking the CPU in Virtua Fighter? Perfect.Honestly, there's just SO MUCH to love about Lost Judgment, and its highs are so high that I can barely even remember the lows. I think the way Yagami is written can get a little one-note sometimes, especially in comparison to the antagonist, and as previously mentioned there are minigames necessary for School Stories progression that are absolute torture to get through. Stealth missions suck ass, the parkour segments are interesting but ultimately tedious, tailing is still horrendous even though it was downplayed significantly, and, frustratingly, the female characters get pigeonholed into passive roles more than I'd like (as usual). Even with all that, though? Lost Judgment is one of the best games I've ever played. No qualifiers. Play it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a slight improvement to its prequel but there are some caveats to this game. I will say that the fighting for this game has improved a bit. The new gadgets give more options when finding side content, making you feel like an actual detective. The side content is packed, making free roam much fun and having to do more. There is just a lot more to do in this game but still having the simplicity of giving players where to find this or that. And, a lot of quality of life improvements.As for the caveats, when I said simplicity, what I mean is that finding what you need to do and there are less hurdles to go through. The problem is the side content itself. The school stories for example, all the activities are there and it tells you what it needs. Personally, i like this style of objective finding, making it easier to be organized. What I hate is how the first 5 of the stories is long and exhausting, especially the ROBOTICS CLUB, and the rest are easy to do. The school stories is fun, turning side cases into minigames but they are really exhausting, just to find out who the culprit is. There are less side cases because half of the content is in the school stories, which is great but the content itself is just tiring.The main story is really confusing. In the first game, the structure is pretty similar, you handle a current case but it somehow branches off to another case years ago, branches off to something that seems irrelevant but then it all connects, and everything unfolds, and close to the end, you understand everything, then everything makes sense, giving closure to everything. But the story telling for the second game is really confusing, and it also leaves you in a cliffhanger. This one has no closure, which i hope there will be a continuation for this game. The reasons for murder, the bully hunter's purpose, legality, and etc make zero sense whatsoever. At the very end, I've pretty much connected all the dots and the missing holes this game offered. As for the scenes, It didn't make much of an impact in terms of emotion and action. The death scene of the innocent didn't feel much heartbreaking and the characters have very limited back story to it but they're all connected to it.But, I will still recommend this game for those who like the yakuza series or for those who are fans. The prequel will still be my favorite and my highly recommended game. The sequel is still a great game but falls a bit short. You won't be disappointed on the quality of the game regardless of the short rant I've made.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic sequel to a fantastic game part of a fantastic world.Your role is detective and former Lawyer Takayuki Yagami. Called to Ijincho to investigate a suicide at Seijo High School your case quickly begins to tangle itself with a few other plotlines which I won;t talk about for spoilers.Lost Judgment is an absolutely gorgeous game. I don't know how RGG does it but they are on top of it in the graphics department. It's easy to see the beautifully crafted world around you but small details such as pants wrinkling as you move creates a highly detailed world.The combat is excellent and fluid. You are given 2 fighting styles and unlock 2 more for a total of 4 fighting styles. Crane and Tiger return giving hefty upgrades and REAL utility to the crane style while nerfing Tiger so it's not busted easy to beat foes (seriously, that 1-inch punch-like move made the game a cake walk). Snake is a style that has you focusing only effectively catching attacks and and swiftly striking back although most of this is done through heat button prompts. Boxing is a style borrowing moves from the later unlockable boxing side quest. The fact that you can juggle most bosses makes this style head and shoulders above the rest. All are fun to play and have their utility throughout the game.I won't talk a lot about the story but it's well crafted, detailed and puts you through a rollercoaster of emotions.As of now I have not completed Kaito Files, will update my review when completed.This is genuinely one of the best games I've played. Sale or full price, with all of the typical RGG filler of side quests, stories and mini games, or just breezing through the 25 hour story (you'll find at least 1 side activity you'll end up enjoying, trust me), this is another RGG game that offers so much bang for your buck with all the high quality of a Japanese AAA game.

_childDocuments_.review: Judgment was a pretty good game, but wow, this is such a massive improvement over the first that I can't see myself going back to it after playing this. Other than having a story that is slightly better paced, there is nothing JE does that LJ doesn't do a 100x better.The biggest improvement, by far, is the combat system. After years of playing through the Yakuza series, I can finally say there is a Yakuza game whose combat system has surpassed Yakuza 0's. So much more fluid, so many options, no more mortal blows, the returning styles got major tweaks and the new styles are fantastic in their own rights, and being able to mix them up and juggle enemies like it was Tekken is exhilarating. From this point forward, every beat-em-up style Yakuza title should strive to reach this level. If you can't juggle enemies in newer titles, it's immediately inferior to this game.The story is also fantastic, and while it's not quite as compelling as JE's story was, LJ more than makes up for it with who is probably the best antagonist in the entire series. Yakuza games have always had a tendency to adopt a very black and white moral view throughout their storyline, and this is the first time we've gotten such a morally gray character and dilemma in the series, I loved it. All the new characters and antagonists introduced are so memorable.Technical aspects are also vastly improved. This is, without question, the best looking any game in the Yakuza series has ever been. The Dragon Engine has been perfected so that the prerendered cutscenes look worse than actual in-game cutscenes, and the lighting has also been improved drastically (especially from Y7's awful lighting). The soundtrack is great, and the new QOL improvements are welcome. I can't believe it took this long to be able to fast travel from anywhere.If I had to point out some flaws in the game though, it would definitely be the school subplot with the MRC, because some of the minigames are definitely better than others. Boxing, robot club, dancing, girl's bar, they were fun and interesting. The others, not so much, and some of them, especially the biker race, just got really repetitive and frustrating. The substories were also pretty lacking for the most part although there were still some wacky and hilarious ones. However, I'm really glad they removed the text messages about the Neo Keihin Gang, that was one of the worst parts of the original JE because it was so annoying. The flaws overall are minor however, and this is easily one of the best games that RGG has ever put out, and I genuinely hope a third game is in the works somewhere down the line. Powerful story, memorable and interesting characters, a fantastic antagonist that acts as a dark mirror to the protagonist, an extremely fluid combat system that makes me want to engage in random battles instead of running away, and some great minigames, this game has almost everything I could ever want in an RGG title.

_childDocuments_.review: is an action-adventure beat 'em up/detective game developed by Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio and published by Sega. It was released for PS4/PS5 and Xbox consoles and a year later received a PC release via Steam.   instead of a positive one because that’s exactly how I felt after finishing the sequel to what I consider one of the best games in its genre. “Judgment” was such a blockbuster to me and seeing how the sequel underperforms in several aspects really lowered my overall score for it, but I’ll fill y’all in on it later., our old buddy detective we’re familiar with from the first game, as he receives an invitation from old acquaintances who have opened their own detective agency. He travels to  to help with the investigation. Seemingly something grandiose like serial murders, but alas, a simple school bullying. Meanwhile, Yagami's former colleagues at the bar predictably lose their case in court. Their client was caught harassing a woman on the subway, and all evidence points to him. However, Ehara challenges the justice system: he names a murder victim who has just been discovered in Yokohama. The investigation finds out that the crime occurred exactly on the same morning when the defendant was arrested in the Tokyo subway—that is, the guilty verdict became his alibi. But he also had a motive: the murdered young man drove Ehara’s son to suicide during his school years. In addition, they studied at the same school where Yagami deals with the problem of bullying. filled with new areas and interiors. The main story is the strong suit of this game as it’s gotten bigger and vaster. However, it really lacks some high-stakes moments, dramatic confrontations, or intrigues that the Yakuza series was famous for, at least for half of the game, until the plot decides to finally unbutton its shirt and show all that it’s got. But even then, most of the time is spent watching cutscenes, unlike the first game that managed to balance the  and  really well. Lost Judgment introduces some new mechanics like Stealth and Parkour; however, they were left half-baked and hugely underutilized, like many of the new additions in Lost Judgment. Every stealth and parkour section is highly linear and can basically be seen as a cutscene where you press a few buttons on some occasions. , now featuring new combat styles and moves that you can pull off. However, all that improvement is overshadowed by the fact that there’s very little to no combat throughout the story missions, so constantly upgrading Yagami’s moves seems like a waste of time because you barely fight anyone other than occasional bosses, of which there are only a few. Every single one can be cheesed by using the special extracts and brews which you’ll receive plenty of for buying the deluxe edition of the game. While it’s a great system, I’m just totally bummed by the fact that I barely got to use all these moves and abilities.Many minigames and side activities were , which isn’t necessarily bad since there’s only a two-year gap between the games, but in my opinion, some of them could’ve been improved, especially the boring Paradise VR game. More stuff that left mostly underutilized were, believe it or not, some of the main characters like Kaito, who is mostly absent for half of the game and only appears closer towards the end to fight off some baddies, throw a couple of appropriate quips, and watch some credits. Afaik, they made a DLC about him, but I’ll write a separate review on it.What can I say,  that tops the first one story-wise but really lacks behind a hundred more things. It runs smoothly on PC and there weren’t any issues or bugs that I encountered, which just shows how much quality RGG pushes out every year or so. And while the story is deep and comprehensive and I’d probably replay it just to catch on more details that I missed given more free time, the gameplay factor really falls flat in Lost Judgment as you spend about 80% of your time watching expository cutscenes which are important to the plot as a whole (many may even call it a ). This is exactly why I can’t recommend the sequel over the first game, which was probably, if not the best, then one of the greatest games RGG ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll get straight to the point, i think this may be one of the top 3 RGG games period. One of the few games i have been supremely and fully invested and enraptured by. Stellar combat (miles better than Judgment, lemme tell you), in that you have so many options and tools as your disposal to demolish your enemies that you may end up wishing you had a training room to practice some combos on. One thing about the combat however, to balance out the positive, is Snake Style. The parry can make some fights become downright trivial, so i only used it sparingly. You can do the same if you wish to challenge yourself, but don't let me tell you how to play. When you don't wanna beat anybody up, rest assured there is a plethora of activities to sink some hours into. You can easily forget about the main story by getting caught up in the new School Stories. 9 whole sub-plots that have their own set of unique characters to get tangled up with. Some come with new minigames to try, such as the Dance Club rhythm game, the Biker Gang racing game, and the Robotics Club's tower defense(?) game. Some are less intricate, but they are all still very fun to look into. As is standard with Judgment games, you can wile away your time in arcades, Drone Racing, golf, the Batting Cages and so on. The usual suspects. That is not to say that they have become any less fun. There are some very minor gripes, such as Mafuyu (once again) not being a very important character at all, despite her history with Yagami, the kind of at-times clunky skateboarding controls, just to name a few, however those are very minor nitpicks that barely affect the overall quality of the game. All in all, if you haven't touched the Judgment series, you are doing yourself a disservice by not doing so. It is an amazing narrative that can even teach you some things if you're willing look into things a little deeper than what's on the surface. RGG Studios does it once more and knocks it well out of the park. Keep it up guys. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the previous game (Judgement), you get more of what you enjoyed from that game here in lost judgement. Insane combat with a return of the tiger and crane styles but with an additional two styles, characters that you will vibe with or hate, an engaging plot, outlandish side quests, emotional roller coasters, and yes, four girlfriends. Now a harem might be condoned IRL but, this is why we play video games :V This time we get two maps to stomp around in, Kamurocho and Yokohama. The theme of this game is influenced by bullying and how it can affect people. You join the local high school in Yokohama as an advisor and help troubled kids in their own mysteries in the form of "school quests". This is entirely optional to beat but I recommend that you do. Besides, the best way to teach delinquent children is through pain.... I mean constructive lectures.... But as you progress through the story, you will find out why the game is called "Lost Judgment" because I was torn between what was right and what was not. My cons are the same as the first games, no Karaoke and you can't romance Saori-chan and Mafuyu chan because of plot. Like the previous game, all DLCs are included. All in all a worthy addition from Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio. So do yourself a favor and BUY IT!!! WE NEED A THIRD GAME!!!! >:V

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Recently tested the game again after a system upgrade, and I noticed SEGA added DLSS support! Awesome! The game looks better than ever, and runs at stable 120 FPS @4K (DLDSR 2.25 on native 2k), probably more if I'd set it higher.i9 13900k, 32 GB, RTX3080ti----------------------------------------At last, we can enjoy the Judgment games on PC. SEGA dropped both titles on Steam without much fuss in the wake of the teaser for Like a Dragon: Ishin!Both games look and perform better than the PS5 versions if you got a medium range PC (RTX2070) - with stronger cards and CPUs you can boost graphics considerably. I run both games all maxed in 2K with DLDSR 2.25x (4k) and FSR 2.1 in quality mode at sharpness level 1.0 and get stable 60 FPS. Sadly DLSS is no option, but I recommend to use FSR 2.1. It boosts performance and for some parts increases level of detail too (most noticable: leaves on trees).You might want to disable Depth of Field, in some cutscenes it's not very effective but just muddens visuals too much for my taste (at least in Judgment, Lost Judgment has a sharper overall look).While Lost Judgment is a bit more demanding than Judgment, I still got stable 60 FPS using FSR 2.1. Lost Judgment's graphics were an upgrade on PS5 and so they are on PC. Textures are a bit sharper and lighting has improved too. Strangely, the graphics look way better than the screenshots on the store page. I only wish they'd paid for a DLSS license too.Both games are my favourites in the Yakuza series (it's more of a spin-off but shares the same universe and regions). You play a small time detective in Tokyo's red light district Kamurocho (strongly based on the RL Kabukicho). You were a promising lawyer but dropped the career due to a dramatic event. You were part of a Yakuza family (your former boss financed your studies) and still got ties to the Japanese mafia.The general tone is a bit more serious and down to earth than the Yakuza titles but the games share all the silly side missions and activities Yakuza games are known for. The Judgment games also share the typical street brawling action (no round based escapades as in Yakuza:Like a Dragon).With time you learn martial arts and general skills to help you on your way.Awesome music, solid English voice actors. Still the heavy American accent isn't my cup of tea, I highly recommend to give the Japanese actors a try. I don't understand no word (well, more like 99,99% - what a coincidence: that's the conviction rate in Japanese courts too ;) ), but the cadences and the leading actor's (Takuya Kimura) soothing voice feel way more natural and obstrusive to me.You can easily sink 50-80+ hours in each title (no idea about the Lost Judgment DLC "The Kaito Files" yet) depending on how much time you spend on the side missions and activities. If you're interested in both games, I also recommend getting the collection edition.i7-8700k, 32 GB, RTX3080ti, M2 SSD, Soundblaster Z

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Judgment is a downgrade compared to its prequel. The story and characters are not nearly as good, and the school stories side-content is not well paced while often using mini-games that should have been more polished. The interconnected plot of school stories is a good idea on paper, but ultimately is not as satisfying as traditional sub stories. That said, the combat and overall gameplay flow is much better, with two additional battle styles and new abilities and streamlined tailing missions. Despite the fact that the game is much larger with a whole new map, it rarely makes good use of Kamurocho and dumps almost everything into Ijincho. _childDocuments_.review: As someone else said about the first game, stop reading the reviews and play the game yourself! But if you're stubborn like I am, keep reading! If you've played any of the previous Yakuza games, you'll like this one. It's among my favourites already! If you haven't played the others, I'd still recommend it. Depends on how cautious you want to be regarding certain changes in the lore of the Yakuza series. Anyways, be warned of general side content spoilers, as well as an extremely vague overview of the story (no details whatsoever). Firstly, this game is awesome! Everything about it. If the first Judgment was the Dragon Engine's Kiwami, then in the reverse order of things; this is Dragon Engine's 0. In almost every way possible. From the four fighting styles, to the absurd amount of deep mini-games, to the endlessly entertaining side cases; this game has it all. Great graphics, beautiful music, an amazing presentation overall. You won't want to stop playing!Secondly, it's a huge game. I have 107 hours at the time of this review. I've only completed around 60% of the game. That's including the main story and all the side cases, some general stuff too. There's so much more to do if you want to be a completionist. It's an addictive game! You can join a robotics club, a biker gang, a boxing gym, a dancing club, etc. There's photography, arcade games in arcades and at home, skateboarding, gambling, darts, batting, VR games, etc. You can even get four different girlfriends! In the game, probably not for real! My favourites are the side cases, dancing, boxing, and robotics. The side cases are a lot of fun. Hilarious, and almost always bigger than they initially seem. A lot of them are interconnected with each other, and are related to the various mini games. That's a trademark of this series, how everything you do is made bigger through the characters you play, and the ones you encounter. So let's talk of these characters. Overall, a similar cast. But with some remarkable additions that make the story more engaging. Yagami is cool as always, tries to be sensible, he's fairly believable though naive at times in terms of his beliefs. Kaito is hilarious, clumsy, and awesome. Made even better with his own story, the Kaito files were epic! Sugiura is still a nuisance, but he's part of the team. Tsukumo is the ultimate problem solver. Genda law office people are still there, and oh man Saori-san! The antagonists of the game will be made well known to you, and they're among the most memorable ones in the series. You'll just have to see for yourself.The story itself covers a wide range of sensitive topics in a fair and balanced way. Those being sexual harassment, bullying, suicide, murder, justice, corruption, etc. They give way for nuance rather than sticking to stereotypes, which is what makes the story interesting. How they managed to connect so many different facets of life together in a believable and well put manner is beyond me. Some moments have becomes memes, however serious they may have been intended to be initially. The death of the author, look it up! How about the main gameplay loop? It's a bit different to the first game. The first one really hammered in the detective side of things, and that was something I enjoyed a lot. But in this game, it's more varied.As usual, the game weaves together the gameplay with the main story, linking it to side content when it can. Tailing has improved, being much more free flow than it was in the first game. Which makes it more believable. Inspection mode has also been improved thanks to the new gadgets that add more layers to the experience. Makes a lot of sense for a modern detective!Fighting is contender for the best in the series so far, rivalling 0 easily. Four fighting styles that are all distinct but can be switched between at will, leading to endless creative options for you to explore, with the most insane juggles the games have seen so far. It's ridiculous, in a good way. The best thing that they did here is they've made Crane useful! Man, it was a meme in the first game. Now it's actually insanely good! Mainly due to its own counter that allows you to combo the opponent. Each style has its own purpose, which I like. Snake allows you to parry everything and forever. Get those weapons outta here! But you can't move for ♥♥♥♥. Tiger has tiger drop, of course. Flux tissure is tough, but still super good. Boxing allows for so many counters, charge moves, launching attacks, stun links, and the ability to sway in and out. Though it's fairly limited in terms of EX moves, and its movement is not as good as Crane or Tiger.They've also added stealth and parkour, which feel like mechanics that could/should have been here before. Rather basic, but they do the job. A problem is how they're only used when they game wants you to use them, you have no choice of doing them freely. I'd prefer that they weren't so basic, since they appear more often than lockpicking does. Which has also been simplified, no more thumb turn bypasses. No lockpicking jobs either. A little strange.Contender for best soundtrack. From the songs in each fighting style, to the main menu theme and how dynamic it is, to the boss themes, even the old substory music we've grown to love since ancient times. Man, the boss themes are epic. Viper, Unwavering Belief, Liumang's Chant, K.O.G, even the generic boss theme Vorarephilia is sick! Of course, the Kaito files has awesome stuff too! The Crimson Devil, A Duel for Love, epic stuff! Special mention to Amon's theme Lineage of Clan.RGG know what they're doing. They know what we want, and they keep giving it to us. Is it perfect? No. But is it as close to that as they can do in almost every game? Pretty much. Still some work to be done to flesh out certain things that are too basic or simply outdated. Some of that is part of the charm, while the rest is a bit annoying. Overall, it's incredible how they managed to make so many good games in this series. And how this spin off feels right at home. As if this is the 10th Judgment game, and not the second one. Fantastic achievement on their part! I hope that there are no more problems, and that they can go ahead and make another one!9/10 - "Tabo"

_childDocuments_.review: The story is confused. It lacks footwork, and is lost in what it tries to do. It ends up doing justice to none of the morals it tries to present because they don't really go anywhere, and it ends up feeling flanderized in almost every aspect. Rather than Yagami pushing his views in any stronger way (Kuwana being called a serial killer is laughed off, which I found embarassing from a writing perspective.) he just clings onto muh sawa, muh sawa, muh sawa, muh sawa. It's not endearing, and it makes Kuwana look like he's in the right, which he shouldn't be. He doesn't achieve anything by hunting down and murdering PAST bullies. All he achieves is some form of minor catharsis for the victims, but it doesn't achieve anything in the slightest. The fact the characters cross their arms and go "Hmmmmm, this guy has a point." Is actually infuriating, and I could not find myself stomaching a large part of the plot past the first five chapters. The game struggles constantly with empty characters spouting trivia and moral debates for the sake of trying to emulate the feeling of an actual story where things happen, when in reality you're backtracking the same info, coming to the same conclusions and nothing is truly happening until you're giving a payoff with no build up, that feels unsatisfying. While Judgment at least tried to be a new idea, Lost Judgment is just a Yakuza game dressed up as a detective simulator, but it falls prey to the same mistakes of overcomplicated conspiracies, mixed messaging which is afraid to commit to a single stance without coming off extreme and charismatic characters misused by the authors.Besides that, Kaito Files is kino and this game by far rivals Yakuza 5 in terms of fleshed out side content. The School Investigation is the best part of the game and is insanely endearing, with a lovable teenage cast and fun minigames which don't overstay their welcome.They have the classic Yakuza charm, good sense of humor and have genuine wholehearted things to say to the player without becoming pretentious about it. It feels like what the game was intended to be, and not what it is in the final state.The combat is also the best the series has to offer, the amount of effort put into making every style feel different down to the simple details like each one having a differently working quickstep, the extreme focus on defense mechanics (perfect guard, quickstep crane arts and jumping/wallrunning specials, parrying, attack reflection, resolute counter) combined with the super high damage output of enemies makes the game thrilling, especially since the game is actually designed with that in mind. Bosses finally play around you on equal footing, and duck out of the way of your attacks just as you do theirs. It becomes thrilling to go through anime-tier combat segments no longer just restrained to the dynamic intros, as you and the guy you're fighting both roll and slide out of attacks, locking into grabs and throws, hurling one another around the arena and trading hits. It's extremely fun, and never got boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down--this is one of my all time favorite game plots.I came into Lost Judgment mildly interested in the plot-to give as little background without spoiling anything it's basically this...Mystery, Crime, Legal, Drama with Kung Fu actionThe plot has moments where it's funny, and moments where it deals with some SERIOUS ♥♥♥♥, like, the Yakuza series is a bit more over the top, this is slightly more grounded in realism-there's a lot of over the top ♥♥♥♥ that happens, but this is just a bit less insane than how the Yakuza games get. I really had a hard time finding a bad character, everyone is well written for what they should be and wonderfully voice acted.Combat is just the way Yakuza 0, Kiwami 1, and Kiwami 2 work, closer to Yakuza 0 and Kiwami 1 if I'm going for an accurate comparison, Yagami (the protagonist) fights nothing like Kiryu, he moves fast and does various martial arts moves, but the combat is pretty fun. _childDocuments_.review: After finishing this game, I can't say I'm all that excited for any potential Judgment 3 game.Sure, the game is a high quality game but for the sake of an A-list Japanese actor, they've changed too much in the game to make it feel bland, boring and a chore to play through.Perhaps it's the fact that the game is played from the viewpoint of a detective. Even the side cases aren't as fun and memorable. As Kiryu, side stories were about helping others out of kindness and getting involved with all kinds of goofiness, whereas Yagami's side cases feel like work, needing to do these tedious evidence searches which involve scanning every virtual inch for clues or tailing suspects and then quick-time chasing them around town.A lot of content was also gatekept behind stat checks. With all the previous games, you get up to a certain point in the story and new content becomes accessible, some side quests are chain quests which is fine but you don't have to waste time raising some pointless non-combat stats just to unlock content. In Lost Judgment, you're forced to do various activities repeatedly to raise stats to arbitrary levels to unlock content. I don't want to do 1000 dances just to raise my "Appeal" stat to level 4 just to unlock a tiny bit of content thank you very much.I also have no idea why they had to show us a maggot infested corpse so many times. I get the picture. Someone's been murdered. Looking at a rotting corpse a few more times isn't going to do anything other than make me want to turn off the game and play something else. Also playing an adult constantly beating up high-school kids just doesn't feel right.I enjoyed the Kaito Files DLC a lot more than the main game. Whereas Lost Judgment, you are playing a guy doing his job, with a weak excuse for emotional investment into the case and basically no character development for Yagami, in Kaito Files, you get to learn a lot more about Kaito and his past and he is emotionally involved with the story too.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Judgment is an excellent sequel to 2018's Judgment. With a more fluid and deep combat system, tons of extra content, and another great story, Lost Judgment is everything you want from a sequel. Along with this, some of the side content, such as the school stories, brings a new and unique twist to the typical side missions. However, even though Lost Judgment does a lot right, it does have a few issues. The biggest, in my opinion, is that there is just too much content thrown at the player. For example, even though the school stories are great, they drag on way too long and end up becoming a chore to finish. _childDocuments_.review: After 100+ hours of playing Lost Judgment and 100%'ing it, I can safely say that this is probably the best game RGG has ever done.The story of Lost Judgment starts off with a seemingly innocent normal RGG game (totally normal) then proceeds to drop a critical point of the story right off the bat and it's Yagami's job to solve it. To refrain from spoiling any story elements, Lost Judgment's story leans toward the emotional side vs. Judgment. Despite that one meme of Yagami screaming, with context it was really heart-wrenching seeing what actually happened. The story revolves around between two beliefs that the protagonists and antagonists strongly and desperately want to believe in which I really like how it was executed, it shows how good and bad each side is but what is truly right or wrong? That's for us to interpret (to judge so to speak). While Judgment felt like a really good roller coaster ride for me (Despite my dumb ass spoiling the final boss), Lost Judgment felt pretty much the same for me but add a bit of emotion into it. I love Judgment's story even though there were some scenes that kind off not made sense for me or I just didn't like how it was executed, but Lost Judgment really kept me hooked despite doing a ton of side content before the really good chapters. The combat system is a huge step up compared to Judgment's, everything in Lost Judgment's system is just satisfying to play, watch, even grind whatever you need in your TownGo. You can never go back to Judgment's combat system ever again unless you mod it. The combat system offers 4 styles, 2 returning and 2 new ones with one being a DLC.Crane Style has a huge glow-up comparing to Judgment as the combat system removed the annoying guard bounce that no one wants and the combo speed in LJ is the same as the max upgrade in Judgment. With the addition of "Secret Arts", The "Secret Arts" makes it by far the strongest and best styles in the game as it amps up your combo speed (to all styles) which is great for juggling making it by far one of the best styles to fight enemies or even bosses. Crane counter is pretty neat too but once you bought all the +ATK skills, it just one shots any enemy. Tiger also got buffed as the 'Press Y/Triangle' to kill or do big damage is already built in which is great. Tiger style is just the same old style to just deal giga-damage to everyone. A nice addition to Tiger is the super armor it gives when you do the Y/Triangle combo in EX Boost, insanely OP and could really help you in the Amon fight. Tiger did get a somewhat new counter, the 'Dragon Crushing Fist' which is is basically just Tiger Drop but with a different animation. The "Secret Arts" is just more damage as you hit your empowered Y/Triangle attack which is pretty good.This style is one of the most fun ones I've ever played. The Snake style combines two of my favorite move sets in Yakuza which is Tanimura and Shinada. Snake style offers a parry window similar to Tanimura's, a rush combo into a grab that kinda feels like Shinada minus the rush combo into tackle. Snake also gives you the ability to disarm weak enemies with weapons by grabbing them and hitting the QTE or doing an EX Action. It also gives you one of the best additions to this game which is EX Surrender. Instead of Yagami just beating them senseless, he can peform a fake-out so hard that the enemy just faints. It can only work on frightened weak enemies as it can literally one shot them. The "Secret Arts" isn't too special but it does help you not get ragdoll'd all around the map. The EX Boost makes you the ultimate defense machine as you can auto parry and not flinch. Parrying makes you hit them after the parry and Y/Triangle lets you tackle + grab whether the opponents standing or ragdoll'd. A defensive stance with very good offensive capabilities.This style is okay, it's not as relevant as the other 3 but it is a fun style regardless. The way you unlock skills is to first unlock the 'Todoroki Boxing Gym' for School Stories and then spar opponents to unlock skills and buy them using money. After that you can learn each skill unlocked from the gym for 100 SP which isn't too bad when you compare the unlocked ones. The style reuses Kiryu's style switch to 'Rush' and it's pretty much literally boxing. The thing I love in Boxer is the 1-2-Launch it offers for an easy launch or guard break. The Mortal Reversal on this style is so satisfying to end any encounter or boss with. Lost Judgment's "School Stories" offered a lot of exciting minigames to play and to have fun in (maybe even rage at some). Dancing, Death Racing, Boxing, Mech Battles, Play VF5 and beating up High Schoolers (in-game), the return of Drone Racing, and other classic RGG minigames like Baseball, Mahjong, Shogi, and more. If you get bored or you just wanna complete some TownGo missions while you're in a middle of a chapter, or you just wanna have fun at school then by all means go for it. School Stories is an interesting system compared to the 'Friend' system in Judgment, while the 'Friend' side story was okay but it felt weird where you can just put it as "The power of friendship" sorta thing. "School Stories" in the other hand made feel more immersed as I play and as the story went on because some school stories were pretty long and it actually gets interesting here and there and of course a cameo group from Judgment. Lost Judgment did a better job with everything in graphics and audio. The graphics in this game really captures what PS4's Judgment's supposed to be in the PC port. Judgment's blue filter after coming back really feels different comparing it to Lost Judgment. The story cutscenes, dynamic intros were all great. The lighting, the effects are really just better. The audio in Lost Judgment is pretty much the standard in any RGG game. The OST is an absolute banger. Viper, Dig in your Heels, Unwavering Belief, even the battle style themes are great. Snake being my favorite one. Lost Judgment is a massive upgrade in graphics, a better story (imo), the best combat system overall, OST is fire as usual. There was never a dull moment in playing and it was a fun ride.Lost Judgment is a 10/10 for me and nothing will change my mind.SPOILER: My thoughts on the antagonists of Judgment vs. Lost Judgment

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: performance is not that bad but is not up to par with other installments, combat and general gameplay is vastly improved over its predecessor and resurrects some good ideas from other RGG games, plot is marginally more restrained than the typical RGG game and is better for it. there is a major spoiler for yakuza: like a dragon in the game's plot.TECHNICAL:I'm pretty sure the performance improved as I was playing the game by virtue of me buying the game on release and important patches being released within a few months while I was actively playing it. That being said the performance was fine but not good. You can obviously tell when a new area is being loaded because the game freezes for a couple seconds, and this was a thing until the very end of the game. Also, whenever you boot the game up, the first fight I would get into would have titanic frame drops. There were also a couple of crashes in the early and mid game but as said before this was probably because of things that were patched.COMBAT:The combat is way better than in Judgment. For one, Crane style has a reason to exist now due to various buffs and unique moves that Tiger doesn't have. Tiger was punched up a bit with some new moves, and a new style was added, Snake, which is throw and counter based, akin to how Tanimura would fight in Yakuza 4, except improved. Snake also has the bonus of having a set of "instant-kill" EX actions to compensate for its slower speed and middling damage output (compared to the other styles). This particular port comes with most (not all) DLC pre-packaged so you also get the Boxer style which I used maybe twice in the whole game.Yagami can equip gear in this game, which is great. He still can't equip weapons or pick up guns, though, which is unfortunate. SIDE CONTENT/EXPLORING:You get to go to Ijincho in this game. It's not significantly different than it was when it was first introduced. Same with Kamurocho. The new area is Seiryo High School, which is obviously not a city but a campus you can walk around.The bulk of the side content is in the "School Stories" which are in Seiryo High. Unlike substories/side cases these have overarching plot lines and unique minigames akin to the side stories in Yakuza 5. They vary in depth and quality: the Robotics Club has a massive slate of parts you need to build and a bunch of robot battles, and the ESports Club is just you playing one of the arcade games against a weak AI.Minigames mostly are the same. Kamuro of the Dead is now Hama of the Dead and is set in Ijincho, the Drone Race is easier, and Dice and Cube is now a race against an AI rival instead of you wandering around grabbing money until you run out of dice. The "Celios" in-universe franchise also returns after having been unseen since Yakuza 5. Aircelios is 90% not being able to see what is going on because enemies are indistinguishable for debris. Boxcelios and its spin-offs always were the arcade's weak points. OTHER GAMEPLAY:There's some story stuff revolving around tailing, parkour, and stealth. Tailing has some mechanical changes but it is still very boring to follow someone around for a long time with nothing else happening. Parkour and stealth are new. Parkour is not particularly in depth and the sections don't last very long. I wouldn't call it bad but I wouldn't call it fun either. The stealth sections are very restrictive; you have to go to particular spots to hide and throw things in particular spots or else you can't progress. It lacks any degree of choice and feels more like pushing a cart down an aisle than playing a game.PLOT:Remarkably, this game does not have a lot of insane out-of-the-blue twists. It's quite grounded even when the conspiracy plot engines start revving up. The plot has school bullying as one of its themes, which is certainly closer to home for many than the majority of RGG games. It seems that Yakuza: Like a Dragon has started a sort of trend within the franchise of more directly discussing and centering around specific societal problems. Speaking of Yakuza: Like a Dragon, there is a major plot spoiler for that game within the first twenty minutes or so of this one, and mentioned several times after that twenty minute mark. It's an offhand remark but it reveals an integral twist. It's not avoidable, so if you want to dodge that spoiler you may have to hold off this game for a while. Some cameos and organizations also return from Yakuza: LAD but that's not a spoiler.

_childDocuments_.review: If people say Yakuza 0 is the best Yakuza game, then this is the greatest game ever conceptualized by humanity. It's got everything.Gameplay: Easily the best in the entire series. Lost Judgment's combat makes the rest of the series look like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tech demo. Each of Yagami's main 3 styles has more depth than any style in the series prior, and Boxer style is an awesome addition on top of them. On top of that, any enemy who has a presence in the story has a unique moveset this time around, unlike the first Judgment which suffered from a lot of copied movesets. The detective-esque minigames from the prior Judgment have also been improved as well, with tailing being actually somewhat enjoyable. The only part of the gameplay I don't like is the stealth missions. ♥♥♥♥ the stealth missions.Plot: Without saying anything spoilery, the plot is bold. It focuses on actual issues in the real world and handles them with maturity. The characters are also all written extremely well and seem like actual people you could meet or hear about in the news.Music and Sound: It's a Sega game. The soundtrack is not only phenomenal, but also extremely varied and has something for everyone. The sounds themselves are also great, with big hits having big impacts and small hits not deafening you. In addition, the English dub is incredibly well done and probably the best in the series as of now (though there's only 2 others to really compete with for now). I'd even say I prefer a good chunk of the English voices to the Japanese voices.Side Content: Being a game in the Yakuza series, of course the game is loaded with tons of enjoyable side content. Though there are only 42 side cases listed in the completion list, this is only because there are 10 whole storylines through the introduction of School Stories, where Yagami becomes an advisor for clubs in the school and tries to solve the mystery of an anonymous individual called "the professor" who has been causing huge amounts of delinquency in Yokohama. Definitely some of the best side content I've ever played in a game, and probably the best in the Yakuza series.The Kaito Files: An additional paid DLC that takes place after the main game, focusing mainly on Kaito and his past life. Even though it is much less serious and significantly shorter than the main story, it is still a very nice epilogue-esque addition to the game. His combat features two upgraded versions of Kiryu's Brawler and Beast styles that are both very fun to use. Though the DLC only adds 6 new tracks, each of them is just as good as any of the main game's music, if not even better. There is almost no side content with the Kaito Files outside of a superboss and some nice references. Also, Kaito's stealth is actually pretty okay. Still not that good, but it's not bad.Final review:Lost Judgment (Base game): 9.5/10, definitely worth the $60 if you're a fan of the Yakuza series. (Although you should play 7/Like a Dragon before this one, because Lost Judgment's plot has a lot to do with a significant event that occurs in it.)Kaito Files DLC: 8/10, if you really liked the base game and don't want to wait for a sale, it's worth the full $30. However, for anyone else who just plays casually, I'd say wait for at least a 30% sale so you can get it for around $20 or less.
