_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 8.5/10Story:Set three years after the events of the first game, Lost Judgment places you back in the very tight skinny jeans of Kamurocho's finest private detective, Takayuki Yagami. The main story begins with a seemingly simple case of high school bullying, but it soon uncovers a much larger conspiracy involving murder, cover-ups, and deep-seated societal issues. Throughout the narrative, Yagami navigates legal and moral challenges, exposing hidden truths while also confronting his own sense of justice in a world where right and wrong are not as black and white as one would hope. The most accurate description of the story is, while Judgment starts off rather slow and builds into a "whodunit" style story where you are presented a mystery and the goal is to reveal the perpetrator, Lost Judgment is more of a "howcatchem" where Yagami's goal is to prove the guilt of someone who is already suspected. I personally did not know this going in, and after Judgment ended up being one of my favorite narratives in gaming, my expectations were high. Despite getting off to a hot start and in fact being very intriguing, What I ended up realizing by the third chapter or so was that I wasn't really feeling the same sense of suspense as in the previous title. For all the pacing issues present in Judgment's narrative, Lost Judgment has the same problems, but due to the nature of the story and how it's told, it feels like the game loses a LOT of steam before critical and truly interesting plot points happen... which are around halfway through the game or so...While I will say Lost Judgment's narrative is better in terms of realism, social commentary, and raw emotion, It didn't really deliver on its premise as effectively or captivate me the way the first Judgment did. Visuals: I thought and Judgment had some of the best visuals in the series, but without even realizing the original release date of either game, the visuals and cinematics in Lost Judgment were immediately noticeably smoother and crisper looking, definitely a result of releasing on current gen consoles whereas Judgment came out as a PS4 game.While I don't believe the visuals are as flashy and over the top as some moments in Judgment, Lost Judgment truly takes everything done exceptionally well in regards to visual storytelling, detailed character models, expressive animations, and masterfully placed shots during cinematics, and does them just as good if not better in some moments. The atmospheric design of Kamurocho stands on its own per usual, full of the usual neon-lit streets and crime-ridden environments, but so does the second explorable city of Ijincho, which beautifully portrays a more grounded vibe while blending commercial, residential, and entertainment areas. The vibe you get from each city are similar enough to feel familiar, but different enough to stand on their own visually. Music/Sound Design:Lost Judgment definitely continues RGG's trend of phenomenal soundtracks and sound design. The music throughout the main story and the side cases/general world is tremendously successful at continuing to give the Judgment games their own vibe, while not straying too far from the mainline series OST's vibes. RGG knows how to compose tracks to perfectly complement their game's emotional moments, and their effort is arguably more effective here, given the nature of LJ's narrative. The boss fight tracks too are of course each uniquely entertaining and compliment the combat especially well with their chaotic beats and dynamic compositions, very positively contributing to some of the Yakuza series' best fights.Gameplay:Combat wise, Lost Judgment takes the most fluid combat in the entire series, being that of Judgment's, and does it better in every way. Yagami's unique Tiger and Crane Kung Fu styles return much more fleshed out, and expertly complimented by the new defense-focused style, Snake, and the traditional Boxer style. The combat mechanics are smoother and more responsive, allowing for seamless combos and satisfying transitions between moves. Additionally, enhanced mobility, including wall-running and aerial attacks, adds a dynamic layer to fights. Despite Yagami still not being able to pick up dropped weapons, the environments are also more interactive, offering creative ways to engage enemies which in turn makes the overall combat experience more polished and exhilarating. All this to say, sometimes the combat felt way too easy in some significant moments, especially once you really start unlocking upgrades and master the combat flow. In my opinion, this was an issue that plagued the game even on Hard, but not quite so much on Legend. Regarding side activities and side quests, a significant portion of them take place within Seiryo High School as the various "School Stories." This was actually something that I really did not like, as I personally was not drawn into the school, or the things going on within it. If you enjoy doing the side quests in Yakuza games, then you better get used to the high school, because that's where about 90% of them take place in LJ. These school-related quests mainly involve interacting with various clubs and students to uncover different mysteries and challenges. While there are many side activities outside the school, such as drone racing, VR minigames, Arcade games, etc., the school stories form a substantial and definitely unique part of the overall side quest experience, but it makes the high school setting a central hub for most of the game's optional content, whether you like it or not..  World:Kamurocho returns again as the setting in Lost Judgment, and its neon-lit, crime ridden streets are just as beautifully presented as in the previous title, with of course the occasional minor improvement/tweak here and there. The most significant change to the world is actually that you're now also able to explore the city of Ijincho. Unlike the compact and densely packed vibe of Kamurocho, Ijincho offers a more expansive and varied urban landscape, blending modern skyscrapers with traditional neighborhood vibes. The mix of different architectural styles and atmospheres creates a sense of diversity and depth, making it feel like a living, breathing city and it fits into the narrative's plot very well.However, while I did really like the city of Ijincho, it absolutely feels bloated at times. Pretty early on, you're given a skateboard to traverse around the city, but even with this speed boost it can feel tiresome to go from place to place during longer gaming sessions. Thankfully, you're able to fast travel to any cab on either map from your phone while free roaming, but this point still stands if your destination is in the center of the map. TL;DR:Despite my minor personal gripes with the game, I think Lost Judgment improves on almost everything done previously in Judgment. The narrative, while maybe not as suspenseful, is still rather intriguing, excellently acted, and thought-provoking. The combat in LJ is also some of the best in the series, if not THE best, and while the side stories didn't particularly resonate with me, I could still tell there was true effort put forth for the most part, and they were, at the very least, incredibly unique.All in all, I definitely recommend Lost Judgment to anyone who is a fan of the mainline Yakuza series, looking for a new single-player narrative experience, or thinks the combat looks potentially interesting because yes, it is 100% that good!

_childDocuments_.review: (While i haven't made an actual review of the first judgment, mostly due to being unable to write a better one compared to other people, i'll still make some passing mentions of it in this review.) (Just skip past my story intro if you want to get to gameplay parts.)Story:Lost Judgment has you step into the shoes (again.) of  Takayuki Yagami, a  detective operating his own agency (only 2 people mind you.) in the RGG  series iconic tokyo district - Kamurocho. Many years have passed since the agency has gotten any important jobs (cough cough events of judgment), and Yagami has grown quite bored  of getting cats out of trees and catching cheaters at love hotels.Following a mundane job of helping a female client get her money back from a scam bar, Yagami receives a call from his close friends: they've opened an detective agency of their own in Isezaki Ijincho! (Yokohama)Wishing to get help from an expert on their first big case, they ask Yagami and his Partner Kaito  to  come to Ijincho and help them with the case: a  string of bullying incidents in Seiryo high school. Meanwhile a sexual assault case sweeps the nation, an police officer has been  caught groping a woman on a packed train. What's meant to be a simple clear and cut case ends up turning sour:  After his successful conviction the police officer discloses the location of the student teacher who bullied his son to suicide. This leads to genda law office, owned by the man who mentored Yagami in his youth. To ask Yagami  for help to solve the mystery of this murder.But as Yagami  investigates these cases, the secrets start to leak out: the groping, murder and bullying cases are all connected in a way even Yagami cannot comprehend.In this case nothing is black and white. And Yagami must face this question:  "What is Justice?" and if his way of enforcing the law can change people for the better.Styles:While the fighting is simillar to the combat the series is known for, Yagami himself is a speedy fighter relying on technique and speed over raw strength, he prevails in combat using his self taught fighting styles:Tiger: A returning style from the original Judgment. It's high damage output makes it excel in dealing with  singular opponents, while it's charged attacks let you breeze through hordes of weaker grunts without breaking a sweat. It's exclusive secret art allows you to gain even more attack power after a successful charge attack knocks out  an enemy.Crane: The second style from the original Judgment. Heavily upgraded compared to it's weaker version in the original game, this Crane is not afraid to deal high damaging AOE attacks against hordes of enemies, even changing certain heat actions into multi target ones + it's newly added ability to let yagami leap into the air to avoid attacks and gunfire from all around! It's secret art is my personal favorite: Increased combo speed after perfectly dodging an enemy attack in crane style, the true basis of all combos.Snake: A newly introduced style based off Aikido: focusing  on grabbing opponents and disarming their weapons and punishing them for even trying to use them on you.Snake also comes with a neat mechanic that tanimura from yakuza 4 is known for: perfect guarding.Simply guard at the right time and the enemy will stumble away like a moron, giving you free heat and even disarming them with the correct upgrades. With it comes a new type of heat action: EX surrender: Scared an enemy by perfect guarding with snake or wailing on enough enemies in time? Aslong as he is not a boss then you can simply "convince" him into passing out regardless of health! It's secret art is quite  useful but not the most intresting: You simply cannot get knocked down after performing a perfect guard.As the  PC version of the game comes with  all the DLC (except Kaito files) You also get access to the fourth fighting style: Boxer. After reaching Ijincho and progressing the storyline.Boxer: Right what it says on the tin: Yagami has no grab in this style, but an uppercut that launches his enemies into the air. This style relies heavily on dodging and countering attacks, it's secret arts giving you a heat gain boost if you do it correctly!  While it's upgrades rely on you progressing through a certain line of side stories, in the end it's damage output can even outperform  charged tiger hits!Gameplay: While the Judgment games follow the same format as other RGG titles, with Yagami's speed come certain mechanics exclusive to the Judgment series: Leaping off walls to catch enemies off guard, letting you perform unique heat actions dependant on the style you use!In this game, hitting enemies into the air doesn't make them immediately fall down: with proper attacks and proper timing  knowledge, you can simply juggle them in the air like in a tekken game and watch them squirm (till they eventually fall since the damage gets lower the more you juggle someone).Ex boost:  An ability rarely used in the main line games, activate your heat meter to  use exclusive heavy attack combos and extremely damaging EX boost heat actions to help you turn the tide in battle!Side Cases: While the original Judgment has a focus on Yagami receiving jobs from clients visiting his office, Lost Judgment  Changes this quite heavily by turning Yagami  into a school counselor  of the mystery club.While this may seem mundane..... Yagami  ends up investigating all other manner of clubs!  Each with their own exclusive mini games:From dancing all night in the dance club, having robo battles in the robotics club, having some good sparring matches in boxing, joining a biker gang?????This format ends up making the side case experience quite thrilling and a fun time to go through, especially since some of them are even voice acted!Overall i think Lost Judgment is a hefty improvement over the original.While some may consider the story worse, or the villains not that intimidating.I, myself enjoyed all the 122 hours i spent on 100% this game.Highly Recommend every Yakuza fan to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to JRPGs, nobody does it better than Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio and this game may be their best one yet. The story, characters, plot, minigames, side stories, music, and everything are top notch. This is the sequel to Judgment though so I would recommend playing Judgment first if you haven't already to get to know the characters and enjoy the quality of life updates added to this game. This is like Season 2 of a TV Show when they get a higher budget and everything is more polished all around. Sure, you can technically start here but Season 1 was also really good and some of the improvements added to this sequel blow the original out of the water in gameplay. The combat in this game is fantastic with 5 different fighting styles to master that you can switch to on the fly, the main story is an exceptional drama/mystery, but... my favorite part of this game has to be the side quests. I have never played a game with a single side quest that is just as long and good in terms of narrative as the main story but this game has done exactly that. I seriously spent over 30 hours of gameplay on a single side quest alone. This is the first Ryu Ga Gotoku game that creates an overarching side quest that is interconnected with, and requires you to complete, 8 other overarching side quests that each have their own unique gameplay, stories, characters, plots, and mysteries to solve. The amount of content in this game is staggering and it makes you wonder what other companies like Square Enix are doing when this level of detail and quality exists.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS BEWAREI have not played it's prequel Judgment but I have played Yakuza 0, Kiwami, Kiwami 2, and Like a Dragon. Overall, the game is okay. As for the story, usual Yakuza stuff where it just escalates into higher ups and police and top gangs and what not. Compared to other Yakuza stories, it was pretty low-tier. Maybe it was because Sawa-sensei was getting a ♥♥♥♥ ton of attention and focus despite being such a ♥♥♥♥♥. It was weird how some cutscenes allowed you to skip dialogue and some didn't, also it would bug out where you actually had to let them say a couple of words otherwise you don't get to skip the next line of dialogue. I think it was me but when the game introduces the character for the first time, it lasts for 20 seconds for me.For most of the game, I played on Hard difficulty but the combat was still quite easy. I switched between Simple and Hard and the difference was that enemies had less health, hits you with a feather, and the AI uses combat moves for you such as activating skills and switching between stances. The extracts that you get are extremely overpowered but fits well for how difficult and annoying they are to acquire and store, I never had to use these extracts until the last couple of fights and legit swept them. The EX skills were quite annoying as they take a long time to finish animating. Combat is easily the strong point of this game and carries it pretty hard. The few side missions that I have done were interesting but nothing note-worthy in my opinion, they were better in Yakuza.The annoying parts of the game:The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ school stories, I swear this section took up at least a third of my play time. It was extremely annoying just navigating through the school because you would do a mission for a club and then you have to return to the MCR to talk to the wanna-be detective hoe.The Dance Club was actually pretty fun because it was just stepmania.The Robotics Club was interesting but a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time sink if you actually play this above Simple difficulty because the enemy AI are nuts and you actually need to have materials to upgrade your robot parts so you have to play practice matches as well as buy mats at other places to win.The Boxing Gym was cool but repetitive and also hard as ♥♥♥♥ on Hard difficulty. I managed to get through most of the opponents on Hard by just spamming buttons but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Kenya is a beast who parries and blocks 95% of your ♥♥♥♥ and I had to tone it down to Simple.The Biker Gang is probably the one I hate the most because it doesn't even feel like a race. You have to drive into and hit 10-20 other bikers before you actually get to race and when you're finally racing with the last guy, you can't outpace him, no matter what, he's a set distance away from you so if you happen to make a couple of mistakes at the end, you're done for. So you have around 4 boss races that you have to win and each boss has 3 lackies so you have to race for around 16 times to complete this garbage.The Photography Club, you just take pictures.The eSports Club, spam buttons in street fighter, win.The Casino, you don't actually get to play for real, you auto lose and then auto win.The Girls' Bar is another grind. You have to drink and talk to 4 girls and complete their side missions in order to complete this section. If you don't have the drunkenness limit, it'll take a long time since the only way to quickly get rid of being drunk is to go into a fight and use the EX drunk skill with 6+ drunk and get rid of the whole meter or drink a bunch of liquids.That's all for the school stories which is a huge part of this game. I dislike the stealth, climbing, and chasing mechanics because it just feels like they waste time. There's no real skill, it's a pretty linear path for the direction that you're going in, all it does is waste your time. Because of the physics of this game, you would sometimes just fall off when you're in a climbing section and you also have to investigate the route that you have to take before you start climbing which is just a HUGE waste of time. I don't know if it was buggy or what but several times during chase scenes, I would miss the grab at the end even though I was spamming the button and time was slowing down but the button prompt wouldn't show up at all.A lot of the previous minigames are still here such as the batting center and darts. They have added a new VR minigame which you can get a bunch of money from and it's basically mario party with more mini games inside.The investigation tools that you get also feel like a waste of time. You get a sound amplifier, an emp detector, a drone, and a detective dog. I don't think I have ever used the drone and the detective dog was part of a story. They give you these so you can go off and do your side missions which you have to first find based off of another mechanic: buzzwords.Buzzwords shows you a bunch of tweets around the map and you basically have to run to each relevant tweet and listen to start the quest and you don't know which tweet is relevant until you're there and have listened to their conversation.The game looks fine, doesn't pop out or anything but runs well. I only like this game because its reminiscent of Yakuza and I severely disliked Like a Dragon because it was a turn-based game.

_childDocuments_.review: These are excellent games from RGG Studio - the developer behind the Yakuza series, which will be called the Like a Dragon series going forward. This series has a completely different cast of characters, but takes place in some of the same cities as the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series. These games introduce detective work and stealth, but otherwise are very similar to the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series, aside from the fact that these games include magical spells called "extracts" instead of equipable weapons. You can play Judgment whenever you want, but be aware that Lost Judgment contains a major spoiler for Yakuza: Like a Dragon, due to something major that happened in that game that affects the games' shared universe in a big way. I can't recommend this series more highly, and the bundle of both games + all DLC, including the Kaito Files, is the best deal you're going to get for the series on any platform, and obviously the Steam version is going to look better and allow you to use the input device of your choice. The performance for both games is superb due to the implementation of FSR 2.1. There's also a mod that replaces it with DLSS 2.0, if you prefer it.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Judgment - an action masterpiece that you do not want to miss.Lost Judgment is a gem that should not be missed by anyone liking action games, especially by those adoring CQC. It´s a beautiful game that reflects one of the biggest society problems in Japan - bullying at schools. This is a real deal in Japan and it´s great Ryu Ga Gotoku Studios decided to focus on this topic that is very rarily seen in video games. Yes, there is the game Bully by Rockstar, but Lost Judgment is not a parody or a funny game. Lost Judgment takes the topic very seriously as the problem that big should be taken.Lost Judgment improves basically everything what Judgment failed at. There is much much less tailing missions and chasing missions tho even these two mission types were enhanced and they are frankly interesting this time around. It´s maybe because they are less frequent. The battle system were enhanced - now it´s more responsive, quicker, there are tons of battle skills, new weapons to fight with, enemies often fall on the ground and give up and Yagami shows them mercy many times. There is a huge list of moves and actions that you can do in battles in order to gain as much SP as possible and after fights you can check the list to see which actions you managed to perform. You have several fighting styles including boxing and aikido, of which I fell in love with aikido especially. It´s wonderful how those styles are perfectly captured. Each fighting style has even its own battle music theme.The story is at least as good as in Judgment. At first it does not seem as dark and sinister but later on you find that Lost Judgment is pretty ominous. There is a lot of beauty in the story just like gruesome scenes that are very hard to watch (you know the scenes I am talking about). Camera never moves away and that´s good! Characters are superb, their chemistry is amazing, everything is glued together masterily. Tho I would like to nitpick one thing - Higashi! We need more of him in Judgment 3!There are tons of sideactivities that are worth playing. Judgment just pales in comparison with Lost Judgment in this area. You have two big districts to explore, you have Sega Master System in your office with plenty of games to find, you have a sequel to Kamaro of the Dead, you have the arcade machines from Judgment here, girlfriends, interesting sidequests, and mainly you have the monster called School Stories. These completely optional side missions connected together with one goal is so robust is basically a game within the game. In the school there 10 school clubs you can be a part of and each will provide you with unique minigames like dancing, robot battles, boxing, skateboarding or bikes. There are not just some minigames as they contain also funny stories, you can compete in competitions etc. Great stuff.Now you can climb in this game and also stealth. Well, these two new things are not particularly well made. I mean climbing the pipes and whatnot is good, you have even a strenght meter which depletes, but the problem is you can only climb in some specific missions. It´s not like you decide to climb a random building you see, not possible. That´s a pity as I was looking forward to this kind of exploration - basically Zelda/Tomb Raider-like exploration. The stealth passages are also just forced and you cannot do a stealthy approach on your own will. Stealth here is superbasic and not interesting at all. I mean, often they are laughably easy and stupid. But on the other hand stealth is a total minority here so it does not affect the overal experience. These passages are short so they do not annoy at all.Lost Judgment contains over 180 unlockable skills and you can wear various things that can improve your attack, defense or whatnot. This RPG element was not present in the previous Judgment. You can buy the stuff to wear or you can win it as a price for playing various minigames - you have to beat certain score or similar thing though in order to gain it so there is actually a reason for you to spend your free time playing minigames.The PC version is as good as Judgment´s PC version. Both ports are basically the same -  equally good. Lost Judgment supports a mouse cursor, there are plenty of PC settings, previously prerendered cutscenes locked at 30 fps were patched by the 60 fps versions, tho they only run in 1080p. K+M playing works wonderfully here. The graphics in this game is very good, tho many textures are really low-res but in general the game looks better than Judgment. I have to appraise the OST as the music here is masterfully crafted.I have written several things I did not like as much as the other content but I also have to adress that the game suffers from a lot of cutscenes. I do not mind cutscenes when they are well made and not so frequent but Lost Judgment can become annoying by how little you can play before another cutscene starts. This is the problem that appears mainly during story missions.The game can be brutal, can be emotional, can be funny, can be thoughtful. A real masterpiece and one of THE BEST action games I have ever played. Highly recommended.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as the first Judgment, which I thought was excellent, but still a good sequel. I think the story overall was not well done, though it has plenty of great moments. It sort of has two halves to it.The first half is better and closer to what I expected with the detective aspects and discovering all the elements surrounding the main case. I feel the mystery here is good and on par with the first game.The latter half feels less natural, as if redeveloped afterwards where they couldn't figure out how to take the story further to make something longer and more climactic. There's some good stuff here, but my biggest issue with it is that it adds little new and very slowly compared to the first half. You're constantly location hopping just to hear the same conversations and names drop in attempts to get slightly new information. The mystery and detective elements feel dead where you're instead either beating around the bush or just pressuring others until someone finally gives you something new or some new event occurs.Other stuff:The evidence selection and questioning this time around feels more tacked on than something where you're needing to make meaningful, thought out choices. For me it tended to usually be either completely obvious what to pick where it's  the latest piece of evidence you just obtained moments ago (why is there even a choice here?), or sometimes confusingly ambiguous (many of these could technically apply).The trailing, sneaking, and photography were minimally used as gameplay elements. The climbing stuff which I believe is new felt unwelcome a lot of times since they were long and slowed down the pacing.The school setting was something new and neat, but I was disappointed with  The school stories, which is sort of a primary sidequest not connected to the main story, is way too long, unbalanced in how time is divided between the clubs, heavily padded with repetitive minigame requirements, and does not fit at all chronologically when doing them in the middle of the main story (where some of the activities are likely taking place over at least several weeks). Some of the minigames are pretty fun and had a lot of development put into them, but I was exhausted at the end due to how many times they make you do them to progress.The game is, for me at least, unwelcomely more violent. Despite being rated M, Judgment and the Yakuza games (though I've only played 2 of all of them) were comparatively tame. _childDocuments_.review: Detective Takayuki Yagami is back in the gripping sequel to Judgment. Lost Judgment drops you into another gripping tale from the developers behind Yakuza. After a police officer mentions the murder of a student teacher who bullied his son to suicide, Yagami must go undercover as a high school club advisor to uncover the truth behind the vicious cycle of bullying and the worrying increase in victims. Now with 3 fighting styles and the ability to join the Dance Club, it is up to you to end this horrible repeat of events.Lost Judgment runs around the same as its predecessor, being able to hit 40 FPS 95% of the time with drops occurring when loading in the environment quickly. It feels really smooth most of the time though and looks fantastic on the screen. The temps generally stay below 70c and can get around 3 - 3.5 hours of battery life thanks to a mix of medium/low settings, FSR 2.0, and a TDP set to 8.The one big difference with Lost Judgment is the FSR 2.0 blur is a bit more noticeable. It wasn't enough to deter my enjoyment of the game, but it was something to note. In some scenes, when you were far away from a person in a cutscene, the face looked a little bit blurry. But the worst was pausing when a cutscene was going and every person who was moving would look smudged. Unpausing immediately returned everything to normal though.Even with all of this, I genuinely am enjoying the experience so far. The 40 FPS sacrifices are completely worth it thanks to how smooth the game feels. I will be testing out a new build to counteract the blurring, though it will eat more battery, and try implementing FSR 2.1 files to see if they help. The settings/build we used are on our website below!

_childDocuments_.review: When I played the first Judgment, I thought that it couldn't be topped. The first game compared to the other Yakuza games within the new flashy dragon engine (Kiwami 2, and Yakuza 6) looked like a tech demo compared to Judgment. But I am shocked and astonished to admit that the sequel not only expands on the gameplay in the first game but also makes Judgment look like a demo.Gameplay - Even without the new and technique heavy snake style which straight up slaps, the two previous styles have been massively fine tuned. Tiger is still bursty as ever, and crane is no longer complete garbage. They gave crane that juicy attack speed buff when you evade that the whole style desperately needed, along with a new mechanic called "Crane Dance" which flips Yagami in the air to either evade or pull off special combos or EX actions. Where in the previous game I would be permanently in tiger style, here you really do have to switch to crane at least once in a fight to get some nice damage in. But onto the snake style, just whoever came up with the combos, and system for snake ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ i love them. If you time your guard just right you can just completely parry an enemies attacks and fear them into a 1 shot EX action just like that. Hell, they even re-did previous reused EX actions in the last game and gave it a brand new fresh coat of paint and im all for it, helps keeps things exciting! Im happy to also see that toned down trailing missions which really wore their welcome in the previous game after the first few, but also reworked it a bit to where you can now hide just about anywhere and you dont have to go to scripted areas to shelter yourself from the enemies site. They also added two new sections you can run into being stealth and parkour. Now stealth is an amazing idea for Yagami on paper. It makes more sense for a detective to sneak around enemy locations than the typical long fight brawl and bashing your way into enemy territory like a yakuza. Dont get me wrong the long fights are still spectacular, but from a logic standpoint its like the ♥♥♥♥. But actually doing stealth is really janky, sometimes enemies just decide they have a sixth sense and can look behind them at random while you're crossing from them and when they spot you, thats it you're toast, and sometimes there are just kill barriers that instantly get you spotted whenever going to a specific spot, and its just overall janky. The parkour segments on the other hand, are handled quite nicely and have different mechanics like wall running and pipe swinging to keep things spiced up. Overall, great gameplay switch ups aside from a few hickups.Setting - You travel between two cities in this game, Kamurocho which was the main location of the last game, and Isezaki Ijincho of Yokohama! Its great to see the funny rpg game map from Yakuza: Like a Dragon shown to us in real time combat, and im also happy to see both cities get equal enough game time to keep you entertained. Isezaki Ijincho was a little weird tho, with some places like the bottom half of the redlight district, and commercial district being cut off by objects and sometimes invisible walls that was accessible in Yakuza: Like a dragon, but in turn adding a brand new area being the Seriyo School acting as a sort of hub for a bit of the side content of the game.Mini games - I am was anticipating this game's side content quite a bit because i've heard that there were quite a bit of different things to do within Yokohama, but wow I was just blown away at how much that was just thrown at me. Not talking about the elephant in the room being the "Side Content" which ill explain below this point, the normal mini games we have are still quite a blast. VR paradise and drone racing return from Judgment with a new fresh coat of paint with new coarses or a complete new overhaul to how the game works. Arcelios is brand new and is found within the VR paradise location where you blast different enemy types as fast as you can while surviving with different abilities, and wow was it surprisingly addicting, I swear its always the mini games that im least excited for that catch me off guard and gets me wanting more.Side Content - Usually these games give you a side content story cultivating with usually a big mini game, like business mini game in Yakuza 7, and 0, or cabaret mini game in Yakuza Kiwami 2, and 0, but this game really took it to the next level and gave us a whole bunch of mini games connected to each other through a story that progresses the more and more you complete different mini games. Going back to the Seriyo School hub that they added to the game, reason I said hub is because this is where most of the mini games to this side story take place, if not start here. Mini games ranging from different school activities like robotics (which was super addicting customizing a robot team and then heading into pve combat arenas) or dance club (with a complete banger ost and dancing combos that hit you with straight dopamine), or to boxing (which the more you progress through the boxing story and more skills you learn within the boxing mini game, the more those moves can be applied into outdoors combat in a whole new 4th style just called "boxer"), and thats just half of it. None of the different mini games within the side story felt like filler or bloat, I found everything enjoyable whether it was instantly or took some growing on to.Extras - Im happy to see the return of the proving grounds or ultimate battles renamed as "The Gauntlet" in the brand new dragon engine and yep its def. a challenge giving you spins on fights, focusing on a specific technique, or showing off a gameplay switchup like that 10 minute stealth section that can go ♥♥♥♥ itself. A new cool thing with the gauntlet is that you can get items from first time completions like either extraction potions to help buff you, gear, or completely cosmetically items, and collectibles such as records. Honestly was just really cool to look forward to after completing a chapter, and acted as a sort of break from the story and tear fest.This game not only improves on its predecessor in every way possible, but also is the best title in the Ryu Ga Gotoku series, if you're looking for beat em up combat.

_childDocuments_.review: It might be a bit early but Lost Judgement is very much likely to be my GOTY 2024.Lost Judgement is the sequel to Judgement (originally titled Judge Eyes), where you play as private detective Takayuki Yagami looking into all kinds of cases in a fictional city in Japan. Lost Judgement features new cases, new characters in new places but if you play Judgement first, you'll have a better understanding of background and relationships. I personally recommend play in order, thumb up for both games.There is quite a lot of stuff you can do, I'll start with the main story. Lost Judgement is a highly story-driven game, I enjoy this game so much mostly because the story reveals in a very delicate and well-designed way with excellent pace, gets me so interested yet never sees what's coming next, and the game never ceases to surprise me. It starts from unimportant case and you investigate bully events at a local high school, based on your findings and news given within process, you'll know something bigger is hidden underneath and you might be the only person capable to reveal the truth, flip a floating ice to see what's the rest 9/10 underneath water. Why? Because similar to the first game, the government authorities and police force are either slow, unreliable, corrupted or don't see what you can and can be misled, making Yagami a lonely hero to take risks to uncover the truth and fight for justice.However, sometimes justice can be beyond reach, even the most sounding legal system can fail the weak and harmed, then people start to take actions to execute what they think is justice. Those are what Lost Judgement heavily focused on and why the game is named this. Characters like Ehara is to humiliate the . Standing in the center of this swirl of chaos is you as Yagami.The more I play, the more authentic I feel. Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio did a stunning work on character building, giving each person an authentic look, voice, personality and reaction. It feels like what happened in the game is actually happening in real life and I can relate to. A couple times I ask myself what I'd do in the situation, countless times I found the lines thoughtful and profound. In the end, it is very hard not to feel for .Speaking of the final boss fight, both Judgement and Lost Judgement features 2 stages, but in the former you know you are fighting against the villain, however in Lost Judgement I don't think there's a conclusion who is right but from my understanding, what keeps Yagami pursue the case is to bring justice to . At the beginning I was bored because Yagami cued her too many times, later I understand Yagami means more innocents can get hurt if he does not stop.The final fight is awfully satisfying and a visual feast. Once the fight's done, I was deeply moved by the following cutscene when Yagami saw it coming but didn't dodge , if I were in a cinema I'd applaud. This reminds me of classic/golden action movies Hong Kong made in the 90s, making Yagami a man of power and with understanding that beyounds words could explain.Honestly, the main story requires a certain level of concentration to understand because of twists and turns, but gameplay is made crystal clear so I always have a good idea of what happened and what to do next, Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio surely knows how to let players enjoy a relatively complicated story.I've written this review far too long. I'll skip the side quests, the convenience of one click to the taxi to go anywhere, and tons of things Yagami could do at school. Just don't miss the dance club, you won't regret seeing those fancy moves.One more thing I'd like to mention is that I discovered that Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio made two sets of English subtitles for both English voice and Japanese voice version. I was surprised because being a regular gamer I have never heard of it. A quick comparison is when Kuwana told Yagami he has planted , Yagami replied You can't do it. Kuwana's answer in the English voice version is: But I can. In the Japanese voice version he said: Of course I can. The difference is everyone's to see and I definitely prefer the latter. After the fight came long dialogues were almost completely different and I was astonished, it felt like watching Behind the Scenes of a movie.In an article the language localization supervisor talked about it, turned out the English Subtitle for Japanese voice stays true to the original meaning and the other version is made to suit the habit of English speaking players. He also added: 'I do hope that after your first playthrough, you’ll give the other language a shot! It’s not like you’re going to find all the hidden cats in one playthrough anyway.'I have over 2500 games in the Steam inventory and I don't play a game twice. However, now I have genuine respect for Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio, and Lost Judgment as my GOTY, I will try the Japan voice version in the future for a full experience.In addition, I really wish there will be Judgement 3.On March 18, 2024 I finished the DLC Kaito Files, I left an review on the DLC store page.

_childDocuments_.review:
SEIZE THE TRUTH - December 2021, Tokyo district court. Akihiro Ehara stands accused of groping a woman on a crowded train. A bystander’s video footage of his attempt to flee the scene and subsequent apprehension is all over the news, and public outcry demands a maximum sentence. “Three days ago, a dead body was found in an abandoned building in Yokohama. Have you identified it yet?” he proclaims as confusion cuts through the court room. His defense lawyer, Saori Shirosaki, has no doubt that crucial details of the situation have been overlooked, as Ehara was not even tried for the murder. She contacts detective Takayuki Yagami to investigate this further.

How could Ehara have committed two crimes at once? Was the sexual battery just a cover up? Has Ehara gamed the entire justice system? As victims surface and Yagami digs farther into the truth, he is faced with a question: Defend the law, or enact justice?

From just a single stumble, one can become a monster…

BRINGING JUSTICE AT THE EDGE OF THE LAW

Put Yagami’s distinct martial arts forms to the test in order get to the bottom of the case. Harness the Crane, Tiger, and new Snake stance, a graceful style that can deflect and return an opponent’s strikes, using their energy against them.

EVERYONE’S GOT A STORY

Employ Yagami’s arsenal of detective tricks with new gadgets, stealthily tracking suspects, and crafty methods of infiltration. Leave no stone unturned in pursuit of the truth as you take on cases in both Tokyo and Yokohama.

name: Monster Energy Supercross - The Official Videogame 6
detailed_description: Mud, sweat, fun and adrenaline: find the rider in you and jump into the action with Monster Energy Supercross 6! Live all the emotions of the Monster Energy Supercross 2022 Championship with the official bikes, riders, and tracks. Take advantage of the wide range of settings to customize every detail of your game experience, freely choosing the amount of realism and riding ease. This year, Supercross 6 follows an entirely new and unique perspective – yours! YOUR PERSONAL COACH Leave your mark in the Supercross world with the aid of your coach and mentor, the legendary Jeremy McGrath! Learn all of his tricks in the Supercross Academy and rely on his teachings to reach the peak of the Championship in a Career mode that is more immersive than ever. Rack up successes, impress the sponsors, race through unique rivalries, and become the Supercross world champion! LET'S GO FOR A RIDE From the airport to the mine, from the mountain to the stadium, the new Supercross Park offers unique locations to explore on your own or with friends! Every area is connected by Supercross circuits and motocross tracks that you can use to practice, perform stunts, or simply take in the view. RHYTHM ATTACK You. Your opponent. A straight road. Everything else is superfluous. Open the throttle and follow the flow to cross the finish line first in the new Rhythm Attack mode. Prove your worth, race after race, in the single elimination tournaments that take place in breathtaking locations like canyons and forests. YOUR CHALLENGE, YOUR JOURNEY Customize every part of your climb until you become the world champion! Ride your bike with an ultra-realistic feel, or take advantage of the riding aids. This way, you will always be able to approach each race with a style that suits your needs. Choose how to develop your rider's skills and adjust each detail of your bike's setup. And that’s not all! Build your ideal track with the Track Editor, create an unmistakable style with the Helmet Editor and customize the rider and the bike thanks to a wide range of accessories. FIRST TIME IN THE SADDLE? Don't let the turns and bumps scare you – the new riding aids will pull you right into the action from the first race. Thanks to Assisted Braking, Steering, and Acceleration, you will be able to become familiar with the track and discover the best trajectories to follow in order to reach the goal – winning! RACE ONLINE Crossing the finish line before everyone else, performing perfect maneuvers, riding for hundreds of miles on your bike – thanks to the new online ranking system, you can earn points and climb the leaderboards with these or other activities, or even by specializing in the ones you prefer.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this game. It is exactly the same as Supercross 5, which has been downgraded in every area from previous games (physics, graphics, animations, customization, etc.) The camera angles are bad, the gear and liveries are still recycled from Supercross 3; this game is literally just a roster update using last year's riders. Supercross 3 is still the best Milestone game, and this game is just as bad as Supercross 5. There is no improvement to any area of the game. Milestone has officially become Madden. This game's only redeeming qualities are scrub-turning being removed and the compound being better than SX5.

_childDocuments_.review: The game had potential, but if the devs would not listen to the active members in their community. The gameplay is very stiff and restrictive, but it doesn't feel too unrealistic. Racing online was pretty good for the most part, but desync became an issue on multiple occasions and trolls are abundant in public lobbies.Pros: Plenty of track options, great graphics, and some of the best net code of any of the milestone games.Cons: Very stiff rider movements and steering, terrible corner anticipation on 1st person camera, leaning back slows you down, front end tucks incredibly easy, terrible global ranking system, dev team doesn't listen to their community, track builder is trash, sticker editor is misleading and nearly useless, AI are awful even after patch, track scaling is inconsistent, bike sounds are awful for some bikes, can't time attack custom tracks, and multiplayer lobbies are non-existent after only 4 months after release.I was ranked #1 globally for the first 4 months of the game, competed in esports leagues and was active in the official MESX 6 discord, but even after all of the time I put into this game and my involvement in this community, I cannot recommend this game. Too much of this game is either copy-paste from previous editions, or just completely unpolished and unusable. Milestone, if you ever catch wind of this, reach out to me. I manage an esports team that competes exclusively in your games, and we're pretty in-tune with the community. We can provide a lot of insight on the current version of MESX, as well as suggestions for future editions of MESX that would satisfy many members of the community on both the casual and competitive sides.

_childDocuments_.review: Im going to attempt to give a good, thorough review of this game due to the hate it is receiving. I find it unwarranted. The Good- Its fun. Its really nice just to be able to sit back and rip around the tracks and not think about to much. Its just a fun thing to do to kill time.  - It looks nice. This pairs hand in hand with the previous. Its really nice to have a good looking SX game that you can enjoy as eye candy. You dont get that with any other MX games. - It Doesnt take a lot to pick it up and play. With how they setup the career mode, by the time you get around to racing in the championship you are used to how the game feels. Its nice for it to not be overly hard. If you wanted to play a sim then go buy MXBikes or TrackDay.- The gear and bikes are really nice. Sure a lot of it was in the last game, but blame the companies who make gear. Not the company who puts the gear in the game. I really like all the options you have. Custom helmets is a cool feature. The Bad- Small things that would be huge quality of life improvements. Being able to do small things like customize your rider a little more, or customize the suit a little more would greatly benefit the game. Just give a little more customization and control to the player. - Some things really are the same since 3. The player options are the same, and the tattoos and cosmetic options are the same. We need to get new things in this department. Its lazy at this rate. I feel like we need more depth in the career mode. Maybe throw some dialogue options in there in the form of a interview post race etc etc. It feels stale at this point when its just race, race, and race. I will add that they DID incorporate the fitness function in there and there is more to it than say, SX3. Cant knock it super hard because of this. But it does need further help.Overall the hate is unwarranted. Its a good GAME. You want something that really mimics real life go get MXBikes or TrackDay. Thats not what this is. Id buy it again, and for full price like I did this time. get the game, go race dirtbikes and have fun. Dont take it to seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I have never seen a group of developers progressively get worse at developing a game year after year. I really did not like SX4. Did not even buy SX5 after seeing it maintain all the clunkyness introduced to 4. I will say this one is an improvement in a lot of ways regarding bike physics and handling, as in its closer to SX3 than the previous two, but the way the jumps are built in this game is beyond excusable. I absolutely for the life of me cannot reason why the jumps are designed the way they are in this game. It's laughable that there are INDIVIDUALS on MX Bikes creating track height maps that are not only more accurate to reality, but actually function like normal jumps that send you into the air above the height of the landings (which are taller than the takeoffs for some reason??????). And do not even start on me with these corners. So much for "battling" with people online (like the AI will provide anyone over the age of 4 with competition....), they have put premade mini berms in no less than half of all the bowl turns on this game, effectively eliminating any option to race or battle for position. Might as well turn collisions of as well. The rhythms are not glorified whoop sections like in previous titles. Instead they basically laid them out to have exactly one functional rhythm that is either easy peasy on the outside berm or next to impossible from the inside berm. If you don't hit that specific rhythm with the added space between jumps to continue to gain speed to make the next 3, you are just going to double-skim your way through it. The goober whip animation remains to cover up the fact that they still cannot build a functioning physics engine for the game. And make sure to buy the credits multiplier if you don't prefer spending 12 hours grinding to get one singular bike to full stats on equipment if you refrain from buying any other cosmetic upgrades or gear. Like always, instead of designing a game that is challenging and rewards effort through skill obtained playing the game, you get a rudimentary point and shoot preload simulator that incentivises you to grind out career mode where you can lap the field 8 times in your first "realistic" difficulty main event. I would be able to get over many of these issues if I had a realistic option to create my own tracks and avoid their stock made tracks, but the changes made to the editor (from 3 really, I didn't spend much time on SX4's track editor because my initial impressions were quite frustrating with the change of controls) have made creating custom tracks completely unnecessarily difficult. Plus every single tuff block sits at an angle of the somehow sloped off jumps. I hate to hammer this point and come off as grandizing, but my first track in MXB was more meticulously shaped than anything on this game. It's truly pathetic. Please, unless you're completely unfamiliar with the sport, avoid this game. I tried my best to support a franchise that attempts to develop and grow this sport but I simply cannot continue having it thrown back in my face by a continual regression of every single detail within this franchise. Did anyone at Milestone play any of their last 3 games?? Do any of them have any familiarity with the sport of supercross? Has anyone at Milestone ever seen a dirt bike in person before?? These were the questions I had playing 4, and I was really somewhat joking, but at this point I'm actually curious. I'm returning to MX Bikes. For sure checking reviews out before purchasing another one of these games. Wow. Just wow.

_childDocuments_.review: Always look to see how much time a reviewer has spent on a game prior to reviewing before you find a review "helpful".This is a good game. No errors. Smooth frame rate. Good physics. Realistic track mapping. First of all, if you're not playing the game on "Advanced" physics, you're missing out. It takes more precise control and is more difficult at first, but once you get the hang of it, you will be faster.Jumps. Jumps can be tricky - you can't just mash the gas, jump as high and far as you can and expect to be fast. Go through the tutorial, experience the Supercross Academy lessons and you will understand.Many of the complaints I read from reviewers who give this game a thumb down, are just silly.  One person complained that the jump spacing was screwed up and wasn't realistic - in reality they probably just need to practice the track's "flow".Another complaint was that there were "mini berms" in a bunch of the "bowl turns". What??  OK, first of all, there are two types of turns: 1) banked turns, and 2) flat turns. I have no idea what a "bowl turn" is. I can only assume they meant "banked turn". Obviously this person doesn't know the first thing about, well, motor vehicle racing.  Second, those "mini berms" are actually called 'ruts' and they are extremely realistic. Watch any SX event on tv and you will start to see them develop after a few heats - specifically in hairpin turns where riders typically spin their rear tire and "drift" through the turn middle.  If you learn to use ruts properly, you can actually be quite fast.The Advanced physics are good.  The right stick controls your rider's weight, while the left stick controls the bike's weight.  As in real life, scooting your butt back (shifting your weight back) under acceleration helps to "plant" the rear tire.  There are many ways to control the height and distance of your jumps using the combination of these two functions during a jump.  You'll have to play around with it and practice in order to be fast. But in general, if you are going for a triple (the mound you launch from is 1, then you fly over a second mound, that's 2; then land on the downslope of a third mound, that's 3 mounds: i.e. a triple) so this is a longer jump than a double so, yes, you need more speed.  But also, you may need to "launch" off of the first mound.  You do this by pulling back both L and R sticks as you approach the jump and accelerate, then, still accelerating, push both sticks forward just as your front tire clear's the crest - this will lurch the bike in a flatter trajectory that will carry you farther. By contrast, if you want to jump a shorter distance (for instance to make sure that you land on the downslope of the next mound thus gaining the maximum gravity assist) you shouldn't jump higher, you just launch with less speed.  It is a deep and complex system that is much more cerebral than just mashing the gas and going for broke.Cheers

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from MESX 3 and wanted to see the new features and challenges as well as a roster update. Mostly, i wanted to support the sport as a whole and help it grow. As for the game, first and foremost, Milestone: Fix the tunnel jump slide out issue. How has the game been out this long and you haven’t patched it? Better yet, how did this issue get past testing? Did you even test the game? If you are not perfectly upright and both wheels straight forward when hitting the tunnel jumps you will either slide out or you will be sent flying in some random direction off course. If the tunnel jump is directly out of a corner, you basically have to stop and straighten out or crash.. This could be ignored if there was only one or two tunnel jumps in the game but there is a tunnel jump in NEARLY EVERY TRACK. Come on Milestone…WTHI started with futures because why not? And jeez. The tracks are just awful and graphics look like playstation 2 quality. I was so disappointed. Luckily, i stuck with the game until I got into the amateur ranks and raced the official tracks because the game and dirt looked really good again. How does a game start out looking like lego graphics and then get better an hour in?Now the corners…i dont mind that they added inside berms. But the way the work is just dumb. They basically grab you and pull you around the turn. In many instances, I come into a corner a little too fast and overshoot the inside berm and have to go to the outside. Well, if you have too much momentum and your front wheel touches any part of the inside berm,  the game will pull your character around berm with your front wheel and forks over the inside berm and rear wheel following the inside berm, all the while your rear wheel is perpendicular to the actual turn. Almost like your playing Tony Hawk and grinding the berm. All bad.Also, the brakes suck in MESX6. In MESX 3, you actually had a front brake! And when you used the front brake, it acted how a front brake should and it was predictable. As for the rear brake, you were able to slide your rear wheel around a corner and really cut inside corners. Using the front and rear brakes in conjunction, you were able to pivot your bike around a 180 degree turn. In MESX6, you cant do that. Even though they give the option to have individual brakes, it does not function like they are independent at all. They have basically removed the ability to steer with your rear tire. All the turns are basically push the right stick in the direction of the turn and let the game take you. LAME! Lastly, the AI issue. I have seen a lot of complaints about the AI. Yes they are easily cheesed. If you ride wide open all the time in an unrealistic fashion, the AI will obviously not be able to keep up with you. If you ride the track how you are supposed to (jumping the rhythms and timing your jumps) rather then just pinning it and taking rhythm sections as whoops, then the AI has a better chance of keeping up with you. They do ride as if you are not there though. I wish Milestone would address that issue. This is coming from someone who does not play online races. In racing games in general, I see too much opportunities for people to take cheater lines that the game doesn't recognize as cheater lines and not jumping sections properly. So I just avoid online.Other then these obnoxious issues, I actually do enjoy playing. Maybe it’s because I am biased as a someone who grew up riding dirt bikes and love that there is a Supercross game. But, jeez Milestone. Maybe spend more money on making sure the game functions properly and less money on having Ricky Carmichael or Jermey McGrath voice in their awkward and off key narration. Ralph Sheheen actually sounded believable in MESX 3. Daniel Blair is not too bad. I prefer his narration over Ricky all day. Asking $50 is too much. Not with this many issues. Get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Played just under 2 hours of it so far, enough to do a couple full events and some free roam. So here's a quick first impression:Gameplay is good, and getting a nice flow going is quite easy, and the controls feel responsive and fluid. Rider animations are very stiff though, annoyingly more stiff than in the earlier MESX games, there's also some texture flickering and pop-in issues, as well as poor optimisation on the free roam map, but I assume that will get patched.  The AI aren't great, they are much slower than in older titles, and I found myself winning by over 20 seconds in a short race on the hardest settings. The tracks are great, might even say my favourites of the series so far, they are well recreated and a joy to ride, I also really like the inclusion of inside berms in some corners, they're really satisfying to rail and make up for the lack of proper ruts these games have.I hadn't played one of these Supercross games since the 3rd one, so if you've held out for a few years I say buy it, but if you played last year's one you might want to wait for a sale, as from what I can see there's not a whole lot different.Oh yeah and what's up with the camera? The default FOV is so low, and you can only edit the chase view, I would love it if Milestone added an FOV slider for the first person view!

_childDocuments_.review: Like many, I went into this game predisposed to critique it as a "cut and paste" version of 4 & 5. And while it does share many similarities to the two previous MESX versions, after 30 hours on the game, I'm finding it entertaining. I describe it to people as "looks like 4 & 5, plays like 3."? The Ice Capades slide outs of 5 are all but gone; so that's a huge plus. The biggest draw for me is always the public lobby racing, and to my surprise (and this could change overnight) most of the lobbies have been for the most part, toxic-free; or at least toxic-light. Oh sure there are the usual a-holes we've all seen for years; the guys who get some kind of adolescent, twisted joy out of ruining the racing for everyone in the lobby, but overall, the battles have been very good. Get the game at a discount from one of the 3rd party sites, and give it a fair try -- 20 hrs minimum -- and I think you might be surprised. Relax and race clean. It's only a video game!

_childDocuments_.review: The last game I played (which was the first I played) in the series was number 4, and the steam reviews for that one had a lot of controversy with a mix of love and hate depending on which game they played last. Personally, I enjoyed game number 4, but noted the game had a steep learning curve and they didn't teach you how to do everything well. Not to mention the AI was broken and the "Very easy" AI was barely any different from the hardest setting, punishing new players hard. In spite of that, I gave it an 8/10 in my  review  because ultimately, I had a lot of fun with it and it felt well put together in spite of the learning curve. Back to game #6, while it's not a whole lot different from 4, everything that has changed is an improvement. The basic tutorial is about the same as before but the game follows this up with a choice of how serious you want the simulation to be, and offers a lot more tutorials and help to get you in the game. The AI difficulty is also much more accurately reflected by the setting you choose, with very easy actually being very easy and "realistic" (the hardest setting) being well, crazy hard.I'm seeing a lot of strong reccomends and strong not-reccomends in the user reviews for this game, and what i've noticed is that players who have been with the series since the first few games are less likely to like the current direction. But newer / less experienced users like me seem to be enjoying it far more. I see a lot of complaints about the DLC too, but quite frankly in this game, I really don't care that much about the customization, I just want to race, so none of that bothers me. I have no intention of buying any DLC outfits in this game, to me all the race outfits basically look the same. And that's fine, because it wasn't that important to me anyway.I had a lot of fun with this and if you aren't really really petty and/or nitpicky, you will too.

The camera views are trash, "Hey lets make two mostly the same chase cameras, and two first person cameras where you can't see your bike or handlebars and have no idea what direction the bike is going to go. " and this is only made worse by the HORRIBLE handling in this game, which is then made even WORSE by the fact that in this game you need to "level up rider skills" to be able to brake better / turn better / everything basically. I guess we don't go "Oh you're as good as you are" anymore, now it's "you're as good as the grinding you've put into this game" And incase you're wondering, you will absolutely have to put more hours into this garbage to get even the most basic rider skills than you're allowed on the steam refund window before you realize what a trash game this is. _childDocuments_.review: Milestone sports has successfully done what EA has done for years with the Madden franchise. However, there is no excuse for Milestone's lack of change and development from year to year (particularly ranging from MESX3 to the current MESX6). EA is too focused on their Ultimate Team cash grab, while Milestone is just lazy. This is a re-skinned, and re-tuned version of last years title. When I say re-tuned, I mean re-tuned. They clearly did not change the physics in any capacity, at least of any positive significance. However, it just feels like they simply changed the tuning of the bikes default feel across the board through settings a user could change in-game, instead of actually changing the base physics. All they did was add inside berms to tracks that are copy and pasted from last year, with more to come I'm assuming in the form of $15-30 per track/compound/pack/etc. Furthermore, it's riddled with bugs, and feels unfinished upon release. Refunded after an hour.I would rather spend my $50 on Raid: Shadow Legends and 2 already opened jars of expired Vegemite.

name: Cavern of Dreams
detailed_description: MORE FROM US About the Game Cavern of Dreams is a surreal 3D platformer with collectathon elements, created in the style of N64-era platforming gems. Play as Fynn, the young dragon who enters the Cavern of Dreams in search of his unhatched siblings stolen away by a mysterious villain. Explore densely packed worlds full of puzzles to solve, challenges to overcome, and treasures to collect as you get closer to solving who stole your siblings… and why . Secrets and surprises lurk around every corner in the Cavern of Dreams. Discover four open-ended, densely packed worlds, all with their own unique themes, each connected to a main hub world full of secrets of its own. Search every nook and cranny to not miss any of the secrets the Cavern holds. Acquire abilities from the Sage to access new worlds. Put your platforming and puzzle-solving skills to the test to find your siblings and treasures! ◼ COLLECT THEM ALL: Each world is full of goodies to find - 40 eggs placed in perilous situations, mushrooms to feed your siblings once they hatch, collectible cards to fill out an Encyclopedia, and more! ◼ ACQUIRE NEW ABILITIES: Collecting eggs allows the Sage to grant Fynn new body parts, which give him new abilities! Use your tail, wings, and more to reach areas you couldn’t before and move super fast! ◼ NON-VIOLENT APPROACH: Fynn is a peaceful little guy, so there’s no combat in the game. Instead, the focus is on exploration, puzzle-solving, and platforming. This, however, does not mean there are no dangers lurking in the Cavern of Dreams, so best be careful. ◼ MEET A WHIMSICAL CAST OF CHARACTERS: Each world is populated with strange characters who need your help. You may chat up a tree, assist a mermaid, or free a sentient soup dumpling! ◼ THE NOSTALGIC OST: Fully immerse yourself in Cavern of Dreams through a nostalgic and mysterious soundtrack, with each world having multiple versions of its theme based on where you are.

short_description: Embark on a magical quest as Fynn the dragon to rescue your unhatched siblings from the mysterious Cavern of Dreams in this N64-style 3D platformer. Gain new abilities, meet unique characters, solve puzzles, and beware of the mysterious villain.

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams places you in control of Flynn, a young dragon. Your mission is to explore a strange, colorful environment in pursuit of your siblings, who have been stolen by an unknown evil. This includes traversing 3D settings, figuring out how to get to new places, and learning new skills as you go. If you enjoy old-school 3D platforming games like Banjo-Kazooie and others from the Nintendo 64 era, you should keep Cavern of Dreams on your radar. Although it is fresh and new, this colorful game resembles classic platforming games - for better or worse.We are greeted by Sage, the fairy-like creature residing in Cavern of Dreams, as soon as we can directly manage our small dragon after a short cutscene. She invites us to go through a brief tutorial and then offers us our first ability. After a quick chat, we can immediately enter the first world and complete practically all available worlds 100%, as long as we think carefully about the puzzles located there. You can obviously complete the puzzles there with the next ability in some circumstances, but it can also be avoided if you use your head and explore for alternatives. The narrative is sparse, focusing more on exploration and unraveling the puzzles scattered throughout its game world. It carries a lot of rewards when it comes to figuring things out. The worlds are small and intimate, more in line with the original Banjo-Kazooie rather than the bloated latter-day N64 platformers.The nicest part is that it's a game that you can recommend to everyone, regardless of age. You don't get hurt, you fall down in places, but you're set back down where you came out before, and so on. There is no blood, and the mechanics are relatively simple, making it ideal for families. You can also discover items other than your siblings or eggs on your adventure. Every world contains encyclopedia cards that provide further information on objects and/or foes. Furthermore, you come across mushrooms everywhere that you can collect and feed to your younger upcoming siblings, who should also grow big and strong, right? They even give you something after you have fed the little ones the required quantity of mushrooms, but you can find out for yourself what that is.The game's design that I liked the most was how accommodating it was to my curiosity. Poking around corners, exploring the whole cavern, attempting to get the most out of my glides, and experimenting with in-game fruits nearly always resulted in some sort of prize or entry to a new location. You can even collect stuff in one world and carry it over to another one and I loved how different tasks would fold back and interlink to one another, like when I met a turtle who had lost his fish food, only to find the box of it halfway across the level at the end of a birdhouse platforming section. When I returned the box to him, he thanked me by feeding the fish in the pond, which gave me way to another new location in the previous Next Fest Demo. That kind of interlinking design reminded me a lot of Banjo-Kazooie's Treasure Trove Cove. Why am I talking about the demo here? Not to spoil any actual content in the game, because that's what puzzles and finding out ist all about.Cavern of Dreams is being created by the solo developer Tyler McMaster, who works under Bynine Studio. While it inevitably lacks the funding or polish of some of its indie peers like Yooka-Laylee and Super Lucky's Tale, the passion and admiration for the Nintendo 64 era of gaming is on exhibit here. You enter a mysterious realm, are warmly welcomed, the worlds all feel rational, open and filled with lots of secrets, and you just want to explore. Sure, some gameplay difficulties and settings aren't saved when you restart the game, but who cares when the foundation is so incredibly good? The only issue is that the journey is over way too quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: The highest compliment you can pay to this sort of game is that it looks like lost media - ie a game that if you told me it was an unreleased N64 game from 1995 I would probably not know any better and believe you. There's really not much else to say about Cavern of Dreams, you can take one look at the screenshots and know if you'll like it or not.As someone who loved Banjo Kazooie/Tooie and the recent Yooka Laylee among others, this game felt very comfortable and pleasant, and I kept finding myself drawn back by the stellar models and texture work and the incredible sense of immersion that came with it all. Really well done by the developer, this is laser-focused on what it was trying to do and very successful at it! Really my only complaints were a bit of an unexpected difficulty spike towards the end with some stuff that was definitely on the more sadistic end of what you'd see in an old Rareware platformer. That really didn't bother me much though. Also I would've liked it to be a bit longer and maybe leaned on the creepypasta angle that was kinda there, kinda not a little bit more. I'll definitely be supporting anything else this dev does either way! I fell in love with this game right from the first Next Fest demo and feel compelled to get the word out about how great it is.

_childDocuments_.review: What a cute game! Kinda a bit spooky sometimes, has an underlying bit of lore to scratch the brain, and just a good time with a chill vibe. It did make me tear up a bit, too.It was only 6 hours for me to 100%, but platformers are kinda my thing, so it might be longer for others. Still, I really enjoyed it. I'd rather have 6 hours of charming, heartfelt game than 40 hours of copy pasted triple A shlock.Also I would die for Mr. Kerrington.
