_childDocuments_.review: I love 3D Platformer Collect-a-thons. They are my jam.This one is pretty good. About 5 hours, short enough to marathon in a day. There's a few parts that could be peak nightmare fuel if you trick your child into playing it.You can probably solve everything naturally except for one well hidden collectible but there's an easy timestamped video in the guides section for it.I can recommend this for $10 sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, Spyro Kazooie.This is some dirty, FILTHY 90s nostalgia porn... and I bloody LOVE it!This is what you call nostalgia bait……there’s genuinely a good game beneath the “bait" though so I don't mind! That nostalgia hit me in the gut! The Banjo is STRONG with this one. This will fill the Banjo Kazooie sized hole left on my wife’s boyfriend heart. Caverns of Dreams is an N64-inspired platformer. Feels very similar to games from that era. You're this little dragon that's trying to rescue/find all his siblings and care for them to help them hatch by collecting stuff in the levels.The game is like a beautiful melding of Spyro and Banjo. Spyro for the obvious main character ties, but the atmosphere reminded me so much of Banjo, being quite charming mostly with hints of a sinister undertone later on. At first the game is supposed to be cute, and sweet, but something about the music, the atmosphere, and the graphics kept making me think it was going to turn into a horror situation real fast. Definitely my favourite kind of atmosphere.I got really immersed in the Cavern of Dreams world. I think it having all those landscapes to explore and lore that is lightly sprinkled in if you're looking for it really built it up. It had a very cozy feeling that felt like home. Had a blast with this one, and the emphasis on exploration and puzzles was a genius move to keep the flow going smoothly. The dev also left in multiple ways to solve puzzles and the platforming. Some of the puzzles could’ve been better but it was still enjoyable. I wish there had been some more like this with just a bit more polish. At the end of the day though, it's still a fun game with a great atmosphere and vibe to it. And as someone who has great fondness for Banjo Kazooie, I happily welcome more games like this.I honestly just love the N64 blocky art style. I know there's a lot of people who criticize the N64 era graphics but there's something so charming about it to me. Maybe it's just nostalgia, but I hope we see more games with this type of style to it. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: A charming little 3D-platformer with distinct and unique controls.It's neither too hard nor too long, not at all complicated and confusing like its 90s "contemporaries" - something I very much appreciate here in this case. The game feels very relaxing, it's almost like falling asleep in  childhood bed.Really liked the dreamy vibes, the "historically"-accurate lo-fi art and kinda eerie, liminal feeling levels. I also loved how the game turned to the darker tone near the end, I really like that kind of the final stretches in games in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Late 2023 saw a bumper crop of N64-style 3D platformers; Pseudoregalia, Corn Kidz 64, and Cavern of Dreams among them. Each offers its own take on the platforming genre and of the three Cavern of Dreams is certainly the zippiest. Psuedoregalia is definitely crisper and easier to control but the frantic speed and absurd momentum you can get trivially in CoD is something to behold. It's short, sweet, and knows what it's trying to do but is more than happy for you to break it in half and do something else. That's all I could ask.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a cute little adventure. The movement is fun and often presents several options for exploring the levels and world, that said however there is some slight clunkyness to it. There seems to be no jump buffer which is a standard Quality of Life improvement made in modern platformers. Lacking this means it can feel sometimes as though the game swallows your jump input without your character responding at all. That said its a pretty minor complaint, seeing as the game was a "dream" to play. The only other complaint I have is that the game is short! I was having fun, and am left wanting more. I would say that's a compliment though.

_childDocuments_.review: Update (around 6 hours played):After several hours of playing, I want to point out some extra things that might not have been clear in my original review:- Later levels do have enemies. But more often than not, they're the invincible kind. They can "damage" you and push you around, but not directly kill you (although they can drop you off cliffs). Think of them as obstacles rather than enemies. Despite there being no health bars, the game is far from mindless and easy, with some enemy ridden areas being quite tricky.- Haven't reached the final stage there, but based on a menu and other reviews, the game is indeed on the short side, with one big Hub area and (at least) 3 detailed levels. While the first one felt small and cozy, second is awe inspiring and third is enormous.- A later skill makes high-jumping easier, although a bit more clunky in closed environments.- I'm still liking the game a lot, despite some minor jankiness in a few closed environments.- CON: Someone pointed out there are no real resolution options. Can confirm, and as far as I can tell, the game doesn't save your settings for inverted controls or removing the Blut filter. Minor annoyances for me (game plays perfectly on Steam Deck), but I can believe that the lack of resolution options can be a deal-breaker.Original review (around 2 hours played):A retro 3D platformer that trims the fat and emphasizes the aspects that made so many people fall in love with the genre back in the day. Without arbitrary scattered enemies, health bars or lives, the game focuses on a vibrant world ripe with puzzles to solve and varied locations to explore.Since it's a platforming game, the platforming better be good, right? Cavern of Dreams delivers, thanks to an inspired selection for a protagonist. As a small amphibious-like dragon, and as new skills are unlocked, the player can roll, glide, swim and walk underwater. Aside from the varied mobility tools, what I like the most is that, if you want to, the game allows for a lot of speedy maneuvers. While it can take a hot second to get used to rolling and Tail-Spinning the ground, once you get the hang of it, getting from one point to another takes no more than a few seconds.So far, the levels have felt less like "big enormous areas to explore and go wild" and more like "small and personal locations dense with things to find". Collectibles boil down to eggs (the main McGuffins to collect to unlock skills and advance with the game), mushrooms (a few dozens of them per level, used to feed some of the eggs) and secret cards (just a fun thing to collect). With the size of maps and it's cozy intentions, this helps the game feel more streamlined and straight to the point rather than padded with forceful exploration. Also, some gimmicks available on each level, like throwing fruit that grow into trees or boots that allow for hovering, allow for fun and innovative puzzles.If I have a complaint about the game it'd be the same that has haunted this genre for generations: The camera. For the most part, it's fine, but on some specific tight areas, it can get problematic. Not a deal breaker, but still needs to get pointed out.For anyone that misses the era of mascot-based retro-platformers, this one is a great homeage to the likes ot Spyro and Banjo-Kazooie. Expecting it to be on the short side, but so far, it's been a blast. Even as a low-stakes game with no losing condition, it finds ways to innovate on its puzzles, spice the game with thrills, and keep one curious about what else is there to each world.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. Cavern of Dreams might be THE best 64-bit inspired 3D platformer on all of Steam. It nails the otherworldly, dreamlike vibe those games had better than any of its contempories. Fynn is an adorable protagonist, and I look forward to pouring in many hours to 100% this game.Couldn't recommend more highly.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: cavern of dreams replicates and perfects the n64 platformer experience thanks to its reduced but tight movement mechanics. the floaty quality some protagonists of yore had is not here, and that's a blessing because some jumps are dependent on fynn landing on a small and moving platform and if the model slides just one milimeter to the left he'll fall and i'll scream.this game is a joy to play from the very start, the art direction is off the charts both in the successful emulation of the games it was inspired it and the game's own identity, ochre and warm tones lead you to different levels with strong color palettes that represent their themes. the sound direction takes you on a nostalgic trip you won't want to come back from with its mystical notes and lullabies.and the level design, my god. there is no unnecesary vastness. the levels are compact and dense with content, every space has a purpose, reminiscing of banjo kazooie's tight design. i missed this. i needed this.this is the good stuff.hopefully, cavern of dreams will be a success and we'll have more of it or whatever else the dev feels like creating next.Find me on my curator page
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright. The main appeal is the artstyle and the textures/lighting which have that perfect N64 look, which is hard to pull off hence why hacks typically go for PS1 style instead. The devs knuckling down and getting their hands dirty is an admirable quality. The gameplay is somewhat mixed. The main mode of platforming becomes a bounce move which is time consuming to have to repeat over and over to get anywhere, and it easily bounces you off walls and ruins your progress, so a lot of the pace is pretty glacial. Some puzzles are obtuse but I'm also practically handicapped so who knows. Lots of sections that require speed and precision from a roll move that has oddly inconsistent momentum. Weird difficulty spike at the end. It's also very short, four levels. I 100%'d it so what can I really complain about? Pick it up on sale or smth
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Starting playing PC games in the late 90s, Cavern of Dreams brings back some precious memories. Within the release of RTX 4090 many devs pursue graphics performances - of course graphics is important, but for me graphics is an extra score for a game rather than a score item. Cavern of Dreams is not much about graphics performances but lay heavily about exploration and puzzle solving, and so much fun to play.The purpose is simple - collect dragon eggs that scatter around the world. You learn new skills including double jump, gliding etc. when you gain a certain amount of eggs. Sometimes player needs to be creative especially before acquiring special skills - A bit like The Legend of Zelda Game series and it's huge satisfaction when you get there without using the regular/normal way. e.p player get a jump boost when get hit or burnt and that is how I reach some higher platforms. Also not all eggs require puzzle solving, some are tested for good eyes, and you get to walk around doing some actions.The art style is relaxing but the game style is kinda hardcore, some places ask for precious landings and one failure means a restart from the beginning. The characters are all cute, humors all over the place like the first sign I encounter reads "There's nothing to read, since this is the back of the sign" . Somehow I find it hilarious.I got stuck and didn't finish the game, collecting 22 eggs I believe I'm halfway. I'm not familiar with puzzle solving games and I suck at click and point, I accidentally found "dragon airplane" could rotate and its eyes can be hit. It would be wonderful if hints could be provided and the fast travel could be more straightforward, but this might be the original purpose as to make players on their own. I probably will pick this game up again once a guidebook or walkthrough is provided, but the rich and fun content won't stop me from giving a positive review.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is a delightful gem that transports you back to the golden era of gaming with its charming N64-style aesthetics. This game effortlessly captures the essence of a new classic, creating an experience that is as endearing as it is immersive. Everything, from the style to the music to the quests to the characters, feels incredibly nostalgic while still being fresh and new.One of the standout strengths lies in its ability to create an atmosphere that is both cozy and contemplative. Every corner of the cavern is filled with small, meaningful moments that encourage you to slow down, explore, and truly soak in the experience. It's a testament to the developer's skill that they've managed to infuse the game with such a sense of wonder and discovery. It's clear that they poured their heart and soul into this project.Could not recommend it more. Absolutely adored this experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Having just 100% the game in a little under 9 hours, I feel it is the perfect time to give my thoughts on this game.I'll play my hand open-faced here; I think you should play this game. It's a charming little bite sized collectathon by a small dev team, an indie project that I think should receive more attention and support.As for what I think, I'm going to start with the vibes.Imagine with me, for a moment, that it is 1998. You are in elementary school, 10 years old, just a few months into 5th grade. You've made a new friend this year, the two of you having bonded over a shared love for video games. They have an N64, while you own a PS1. It is the evening, well after school. You've just gotten home from your new friend's house, where the two of you had spent all your time glued to the CRT TV. The two of you had passed the controller back and forth for Banjo-Kazooie and Super Mario 64 happily. When their older brother finally got home, the two of you had set upon him immediately like ravenous dogs, hounding him for help with the levels you just can't beat and begging to borrow his brand new copy of LoZ Ocarina of Time for But that excitement is passed, now. Upon your return, you'd promptly parked yourself on the floor directly in front of your TV, much too close as your parents often tell you. You dusted the screen down with your forearm, just to entertain yourself with the feel of static prickling your hairs. There you while away the dwindling daylight playing Spyro the Dragon, until you feel yourself begin to grow tired with the encroaching darkness. Unwilling to surrender a moment of free time, you retreat back onto the couch to continue playing while you lie down. You're on your side, head propped up by a firm, scratchy throw pillow at an angle that you don't think much of now, but would feel murderous on your neck when you're older. Although your efforts to fight it are valiant, sleep finds you there on the itchy sofa, controller still in hand. Behind closed eyes you bare witness to an amalgam of the day's fixations; a cute, colorful character navigating worlds of puzzles to uncover secrets. Slowly progressing and retracing his steps with each new skill learned, all set to a twinkling soundtrack. Just when those soft, dreamy and warm, bright color palettes give way to a world of shadows that instills you with a sense of unease like teetering on the edge of a nightmare, you are shaken awake by your parents.Though scolded and sent to bed under the looming inevitability of school in the morning, you can't help but think of those fuzzy glimpses of a phantom game. The prospect of possibly seeing it again in your sleep entices you into bed. Most of all, you can't wait to tell your friend all about this cool new video game you thought of tomorrow.Truthfully I don't know that I have the right words to describe this game's comfy, dreamy atmosphere. The whole time playing it felt nostalgic for me despite being an entirely new experience. I must say the dev team perfectly captured the feel of a 90s platformer, it's a wonderful love letter clearly crafted with passion.I do feel the need to be fully honest with you on the game play front. The controls can feel a bit off; Fynn is rather slow and your methods of speeding up (ie rolling around to gain momentum) feel very unwieldy. I'm not going to harp on the jump/swim/fly mechanics too much, it'd be unfair as my controller's button is worn out so I don't feel I got an accurate experience. I did still have a fun time even struggling against my controller, so do with that what you will I suppose. This game also struggles with the age old problem of 3D platformers; the camera. I wouldn't call it any worse than usual, however. Just an occasional annoyance.While I do enjoy when a game doesn't hold your hand through every step of the process, some of the puzzles and secrets felt just a bit obtuse and vague on instructions. Ultimately they're not impossible to decipher, and there are full guides for the collectibles if you feel too stuck. All and all it may not be a perfect experience -and a rather short one- but it is a very comfortable one. Give it a try, if only to support small indie devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I may be pushing it too far, but it could be possible if the developer wishes to expand on this IP. They have all the ingredients here for it: loveable characters, some cool problem-solving puzzles, and a unique aesthetic, with each location looking entirely different from the others, like a horror-themed museum or an ice palace. Fourthly, there are some platforming challenges where you can use the skills you earned to go where you want to go by putting all the mechanics you learned to the test.However, I need to reiterate this is a platforming and puzzle-solving focus game first and foremost, so don't expect many combats if that's your thing. To the other who stuck around, I also say this isn't as child-friendly a game as it may seem upon first impression. From what I mean by that not all puzzles may not have an apparent solution unless you are unable to read between the lines of dialogues. Buy this for your kids or a younger friend or family member if you feel they don't mind being unable to complete a game in one and play it again years after forming a new appreciation for it. I'm sure we can relate when we were younger if you owned games like The Simpsons: Hit and Run or Lara Croft's Legend.Still, I applaud the developer for gifting us this delightful experience inspired by the time when 3D retro games were making a name for themselves. Kiddo for them for keeping the spirit of these sorts of games alive.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, and I just don't. The visuals are a really great facsimile of the n64 era games, and I can tell they are going for a Banjo Kazooie or Spyro vibe, but the controls play a lot more like Glover. Clumsy movement, and awkward platforming had me turning it off and requesting a refund in less than an hour. I hope they make more stuff like this, but they need a lot more buttery controls in whatever comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly all in all its extremely well made but just not what I wanted from this game. It was a bit of a slog to get through the castle at the end of the game and I just can't help but wish we got more of the forest or snow globe palace style of levels. They filled you with wonder but instead the tone shifts, and I just can't say I'm a fan of it.It's entirely subjective of course, there's a depth here with the story and context clues spelled out to you about the world and the characters that inhabit it it just isn't really what drew me to this game and I'm left a little unsatisfied.If you go in with the expectation that its a little more story/lore heavy I think you'll really enjoy this. It's extremely well made for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cute! I liked it a lot! I'm a big fan of Spyro the Dragon. It really scratched that itch for me, so if you're looking for something like that, definitely give this a try.Levels are fun to explore. Theres 5 levels including the overworld, but they're all densely packed with content. Because there's few of them and they're close together, going back to an earlier level with new powers or insight is not bothersome at all~Controls are smooth and satisfying. It has some neat speed tech. Very clearly had thought and care put into it. Even if youre not interested in speed tech and the like, I felt this game was very accessible to people with a low skill level as there were very few timer challenges and very few moving platforms that you had to time. There are few enemies, and there is no HP mechanic, just knockback from damage and bottomless pit death. Because of that most of the technical challenge comes from methodical, low pressure platforming which I found to be well executed.One place this game really shines is the puzzles! They were brain teasers for sure! It was really satisfying to me to do the puzzles and have my "A-HA!" moment; I've played the Spyro games so many dang times that I practically have them memorized, especially when it comes to puzzles. So this game really stretched my brain with its puzzles in a way that a game I'm more familiar with just can't deliver on. There weren't any that I found to be offensively cryptic or nonsensical. If you're not a brainy gamer, it might not be for you.Another thing this game excels at is ATMOSPHERE, ATMOSPHERE, ATMOSPHERE! It really nails that, well... dream-like quality. The character and environment designs are perfect for this, music and sign text is used to EXCELLENT effect. It's cozy and encouraging while also having a sort of spooky and somber undercurrent..... Delicious.... As a kid this would probably be a game that I couldn't tear myself away from even though it gave me nightmares. As an adult its just the perfect treat.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels like it would have been a well loved classic collectathon on N64, and I feel that that style of game is a nice change of pace from the norm. I would highly recommend this game, if N64 style 3d platformer that has just enough challenge, is what you're looking for. Also it is an incredibly charming experience, and I look forward to what this studio makes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! It's got incredibly fun platforming, and simple, but fun little puzzles. It's got just enough variety to keep the experience fresh, but not so much that it feels stuffed. The combination of music, and visuals create an atmosphere constantly and meticulously tilting from dreamy and cozy, to eerie and mysterious. I've never seen an n64-style game nail that aspect quite like this one.I'd highly recommend it to anyone who likes those 90's 3D-platformers. Especially if you enjoy that dreamy nostalgic feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely N64 style platformer, got a lot of charm and a good length. Got a few interesting mobility mechanics, like momentum based rolling, and doing an attack before landing on the ground to lunge forwards and help cross larger gaps. Visual are very nice and mostly fit the era well, and it's got a lot of the crazy colored vertex lighting we used to see more back then which makes for a lot of striking contrasts. Just a nice and chill time to go around exploring and finding collectibles.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Great little 3D platformer, lots of neat ideas, good level design, and controls well. A couple of puzzles are definitely as obtuse as what you'd find in the 64 classics it takes its inspiration from, but not so much so to be a problem. The story/premise is straightforward and believable enough (you typically don't need much for a platformer after all) and the game encourages exploration, with general progression being quite flexible, and several easter eggs throughout all of the major areas, including in places that at face value seem totally out of bounds (but are indeed accessible in some way or another...). The game overall is on the shorter side, and does a good job of staying fresh throughout. For achievement minded players, Cavern of Dreams only has 2, both of which being to find all of a specific macguffin. These are reasonable enough to attain throughout regular gameplay (as long as you explore a bit, and I mean, if you're not exploring, why are you playing a 3D platformer?) and none are missable. There was a bug on launch that made unlocking one or both seemingly impossible for some players (myself included), however as of editing this review (edit on Dec. 8, 2023) a new patch has dropped and achievements seem to unlock again, so make sure you play the latest version if that matters to ya! I strongly suggest all who play to immediately disable the blur filter in the settings as, personally, it does not really add to the experience. But to each their own. tldr, Fun game, great (and short) 3D platformer, plays well but check your settings anyway, buggy achievements so beware if you care.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. The visuals were pleasing, ambient soundtrack beautiful, and gameplay mechanics were fun to learn and use around the different environments. A true-to-form homage to the classic era of N64 style games. I especially appreciated the quirky character designs, colorful environments, and the fact that once you get enough eggs, you can actually fly, not just glide or have a specific level designed to fly, but truly revisit old locations and REALLY explore all they have to offer (looking at you Spyro.) The developer truly went to great effort to put little easter eggs everywhere (some meaningful to actual gameplay progression and some more of obscure personal messages I believe meaningful to the developer themselves. Overall, a really excellent experience and would definitely recommend if you enjoyed games such as Spyro series and old N64 3D platformers. You will not be disappointed. Well, the only disappointment (which is not neccessarily a con or shortcoming of the game) is that I wish it was longer and had more levels to explore and enjoy. The developer expressly stated that they had wished they could have put more into the game but this was the best they could do with their time and resources. I can appreciate that honesty. Regardless, give it a try as what the developer has created for you to explore is truly an experience worth playing and putting some time in.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams was a big disappointment for me and sort of a tragedy in that context. The character design/art is very charming, and the initial movement challenges feel quite inviting, but the level and world design becomes incredibly gated and linear very quickly, to the extent that there is basically no room for player expression. I've spent a lot of time thinking about what it is that makes the difference between a good 3D platformer level and a bad one and I'm pretty sure one of the main culprits is omnipresent death planes. In Super Mario 64 there are between 5 and 8 omnipresent death planes, depending on your definition, and 5 of those are in end game areas. In every other stage, when you miss a jump, your only punishment is lost time or health. You do not lose control of your character and have to sit for three seconds while the game respawns you at the beginning of the level. This happens incredibly quickly into Cavern of Dreams, and the level that does this also features wind physics and a mechanic involving height manipulation of terrain that feels like a tortured gimmick even if it worked properly (it doesn't). The notion of finding eggs to unlock abilities and having a bunch of extra eggs to give yourself room to explore is great, but my experience was that I very quickly ran into one or two eggs that were the only ones available and I didn't want to do the stupid challenges the game was presenting me to unlock them because they had nothing to do with fun movement or challenging platforming... they're gimmicks that involve carrying an item across a level or knowing which direction to hit a lever.Huge miss for me, but maybe more tolerable if your standards for platforming aren't as high.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is not a perfect game.It's rather short - it took me just over 5 hours to get 100% completion, currently glitched encyclopedia achievement notwithstanding. People on the fence about this sort of game or seeking a higher money-to-time ratio might want to look at something like Pseudoregalia instead.A handful of segments, like Heaven's Path, the hoop- and swimming-related sections of the Gallery of Nightmares, and the area behind the 4-heart door, were more punishing and/or annoying than they really needed to be.Despite the aesthetic and inspirations, the game isn't really suitable for children, mostly because the Gallery of Nightmares fits the name a bit  well. Teens should be fine.The in-game hint system spent most of my playthrough locked on a hub world egg that I straight up wouldn't have the moves to reach until just before the final level.Also, the camera control settings reset every time you visit the title screen, which led to me repeatedly failing to realize why the camera was embedded in the floor....And apart from everything I just listed, Cavern of Dreams absolutely  everything it's going for. The visuals, sound, level design, controls, challenges, and writing all come together to make the game feel like just like its inspirations, while being modernized in just the right ways to not feel dated in the slightest. A Rare achievement indeed.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of THE best platformers of the year, I had been waiting for it ever since I saw it being worked on and it was so, so worth the wait!Very much feels like buying a brand new N64 game and playing away a comfy rainy day, mostly having a spirit close to that of Banjo Kazooie.Honestly can't recommend enough, it knows what it's doing, the protagonist is both cute and has an incredible moveset and the puzzles and levels are just that amount of difficult that don't feel too on the nose, but also not infuriatingly difficult!Also reminded me how horribly scared I was of Glover back in the day. Not something I expected, but this game is doing everything right in injecting that fear right back into me. Wouldn't be a good N64-esque Platformer without that uncanny horror somewhere in there.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played a game that yanked me right back to being ten years old and playing games like Mario 64 and Banjo-Kazooie for the first time like this game did. It captures the N64 vibes perfectly, down to the graphics, the dreamy atmosphere, and the way it occasionally hits that feeling of being incredibly unnerving and leaving you unsure of what to expect. There's even some mysteries like the ones you'd find in those old games that leave you wondering. It stands out from those old games though by having a more involved story. It's nothing groundbreaking--not near to the narrative level of something like, say, Psychonauts--but there's little bits of lore you slowly pick up throughout the game, and as you piece them together, it paints a pretty good picture of the game's world and history. It's really satisfying being able to link the pieces together. It also stands out in that there's no combat--and, honestly, the game does so well without it that I didn't even think of the fact that there wasn't any until after I'd beaten the game and saw someone else bring it up.I also adore how much this game rewards exploration, especially in the late- and post-game. There's a lot to discover--stuff that's not required for completion, but that's really nifty to find regardless.The game is not perfect--there's a few puzzles I struggled with and on a few occasions the controls got a bit fiddly--but they did little to detract from the overall experience. If you enjoyed old N64 or PS1-style collect-a-thon platformers, you NEED to play this game. At the time of my writing this it's on sale for about $8 USD and it's well worth it. It's short, sweet, and a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful and surprisingly contemplative journey through spaces that feel liminal mostly because they aren't rendered the way we're accustomed to; leave the default shaders ON and resist your visual cortex's initial grasping for the crispness and fidelity it's accustomed to!In no time at all you'll begin to feel the artistic intent work its dreamlike charms and as soon as you meet Mr. Kerrington you'll be hooked.Don't SLEEP on this game just because you lack nostalgia for N64 era graphics; we can learn a lot from being transported back to simple exploration, movement, and wonder-based design.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is probably one of the most charming games I've played in 2024. Its cute protagonist, retro artstyle, and relaxing and oddly nostalgic soundtrack makes me feel like a kid again.You're looking at a 3D Platformer Collectathon that advertises itself as being heavily inspired by the N64, and it truly does live up to that vibe, albeit with a few new bells and whistles that the N64 couldn't handle. but those hardly take away from the experience. You play as a cute little dragon named "Fynn" whose primary goal is to locate the lost eggs of his dragon family and bring them all back home.There are 3 types of collectables in this game: The unhatched eggs of your dragon siblings, mushrooms that you'll use to feed hatched baby dragons, and cards that fill up an in-game encyclopedia of objects and characters. Every set amount of eggs you collect will unlock a new ability that will help you navigate the worlds and solve puzzles more effectively.There is no real combat in Cavern of Dreams, and therefore no health or lives system. When you die, you are quickly set back to the last door you entered. This may sound odd, but I stated before that the game feels kinda relaxing, so it actually works pretty well here. The most frustrating thing you'll probably run into is some of the puzzles. Most of which in my experience are easier than they look. If you have trouble getting to one place and find yourself doing the same thing over and over and missing, there's probably another thing you can activate somewhere that makes it easier. Otherwise most of the puzzles are pretty straightforward and satisfying.It may not be long, it may not be perfect, but it has a lot of character and charm, is (mostly) smooth, and I love it. It's a fun romp and if you love old-school 3D Platformers, you should play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games ever. If you like Spyro or Banjo you'll love this so much, I got kind of sad when I 100% / collected everything so I spent some time looking at all the secrets! I watched the credits all the way through and almost cried, I need to replay it I guess LOL!I wish there was a second one, or they would extend the game even more. Its cozy, cute, fun and easy to pick up, kinda creepy, and full of so many little surprises. Thank you to the people who worked on something so special, I had so much fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is an absolute gem of a game.It's a charming and magically wonderful collectathon platformer. The world is densely packed with puzzles, secrets and platforming challenges, where you can also upgrade your abilities and giving you access to new mobility options. The game's cute, but it's never mindless often times platforming challenges and puzzles require careful thought rather than being execution tests (though that being said, I do think that could also work very well for this type of game).It also features one of the most adorable mascots to ever exist for anything: Fynn the dragon. HE'S JUST TOO FRICKIN' CUTE AND THE NOISES THAT HE MAKES AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAHH!!! His moveset is also really robust, being mostly momentum based. From basic rolling to go insanely fast, clawing the ground to get a quick burst of speed, to doing a dive-glide from a high vantage point, the insane speed you can build up underwater. It's SO fun to experiment around with Fynn's movement. All in all the game handles like a dream! Honestly I would have liked more obstacle course segments in the game to fully take advantage Fynn's moveset, The atmosphere too! This game feels like a love letter to that weird essence and charm many N64 games had, down to its blur filter. It's also super surreal, as you'd probably expect for a a game based around dreams. There's a certain magic to the areas in this game that just cannot be described, you just have to experience it for yourself. That said though... that N64 surreal-ness also can be kinda... eerie and unsettling at times? Not like diving into full on horror, but it does also take inspiration from nightmares towards the end of the game, which I found a little creepy honestly. All of it is wonderfully done.If I do have mixed feelings on something... it's the puzzles. The game always gives you some sort of subtle hint somewhere to a puzzle... however when I say subtle... I mean it  degree at times. Many times, a solution may require going into an entirely different area altogether just to get an item you need, and hints to solutions are also often placed a bit far away from the puzzle itself. Point is, many of the puzzles aren't "convenient" to solve. In a way that makes the puzzles that much more satisfying to solve, but you can also waste a bunch of time being stuck on a single puzzle.Overall though, this game is a like dream come true.It's an absolutely whimsical and magical experience every step of the way, and it's pretty cheap and it's a fairly short game so it's not that huge of an investment or commitment. I highly recommend giving this game a shot.*Also shout outs to Nitro Rad for putting this game on my radar. This game did not disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've played a 3D platformer with a less enjoyable movement kit. It's sluggish, floaty, the environment doesn't feel built around it. As others have said, there is no room for self expression here. After having played Yellow Taxi Goes Vroom, Orbo's Odyssey, Big Catch Tacklebox, Frogun Encore and Lunistice, I couldn't think of a more opposite experience. The music and VFX in this game is ear piercing, wondering if there's been any mixing, and if the dev made all the noises in the game with their mouth and increased the pitch ten fold.The art is nice I guess, but it's all very noisy, too bright, and does a very poor job and guiding your eyes to points of interest, because the color contrast and saturation is all over the place.I also just got lost at some point in the game, because of how many side passages there are, and backtracking is slow and painful.Genuinely surprised this has such good reviews because the nostalgia can only go so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings on this game, but I don't want to be too harsh on it due to its small developer and scope. I don't think it's a great example of a retro-inspired platformer, but it's not a bad game either. I would have given it mixed rating if that were an option. My biggest gripe mostly stems from a few obtuse mechanics and level design choices, as well as some questionable controls. The story isn't really well told either. When the game starts, it never really explains why the main character and their siblings ended up where they did. Some of the character motivations are not entirely clear either. There does seem to be some inkling of lore that's both dark and intriguing, but it's never really told or expanded on in any meaningful way, and it's mostly left for the player to theorize or deduce. The Encyclopedia is the primary source of lore that you gain access to, and it doesn't give up much information.The camera can be a nightmare at times. I fought with it quite a bit, especially during trickier sections. It has a tendency to want to rotate around the character in the direction you're moving, which is fine or desirable in most  situations, but if you're trying to do some side-scrolling platforming in a 3D space, it can be infuriating. It really needs to be contextual or have the ability to be shifted in mode.The controls, especially when rolling, are not particularly precise or fun. You slow down when rolling up hills. You can get caught on ledges and fall when trying to climb and jump over them from vines. The double jump is an extremely slow and painful move to make. I could keep going, but the good news is most if not all the bad move-sets are made obsolete by the end of the game with the introduction of new abilities and ultimately the capacity to fly. Other peeves are that moving up/down and left/right through menus is done through TWO SEPARATE sticks, instead of all being tied to the singular directional pad or one stick, which is incredibly annoying and unintuitive. Backing out of the menu when holding an item makes you toss it. Making a non-standard random button for the text prompts but tying the back button to attack is baffling to me, as opposed to just making it a normal contextual select.Finally, about half way through the game there's a bit of a difficulty spike. The game becomes incredibly obtuse with its level design and puzzles once you make it to the palace. The things you can do are poorly explained, and hints for puzzles are given in cryptic messaging. I was forced to look up a few solutions, and it was never clear to me how I was expect to discover that solution without just trying to brute force it. Anyway, I will say the character design is good, the sound design is compelling and strangely nostalgic, and there are hints of good level and game design, It just didn't work for me as an entire whole. So I'm lukewarm at best on this.

However, it’s not all bleak. I did encounter a handful of puzzles that were quite enjoyable, but there were too many so far that were too obtuse. It all boils down to . It tries too hard to be something else and doesn't bring in any originality of its own which ultimately resulted in me asking for a refund.

Despite it's replication of a gaming era I never got the opportunity to be apart of it still brings me back to my childhood with it's whimsy and charming designs. _childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite genres of games is 3D collectathon platformers. Mario, Banjo, Spyro, love these games, however this one though okay, is not good or great. The positives, characters are cute and colorful if a bit busy but that's okay especially since it is the style they are going for. I appreciate the classic retro style the game is made in and the filter is a cool touch. The first little bit of the game is nice and having to get an item to get more abilities is a great idea. This is where it ends though as the rest of the game gets odd. One of the biggest things about 3D platformers is the smooth controls, this game doesn't have those. The speed to walk is slow, the rolling and jumping are inconsistent and I understand the choice of not having combat, but it is odd. I've never had a good game in this genre where the jumping just doesn't feel good in any way. The jumps are short and the only way to get them higher by only a fraction is an ability you must earn, same for gliding. The last level is also just not enjoyable at all, same for the last "boss fight". As for other levels they tend to have lots of weird sections that just lead to dead ends suddenly, are maze like and hard to traverse. They don't have many characteristics to tell the difference between paths. Granted these sections aren't very long but there were a few times where I'd end up getting turned around and have to correct my direction. There are just a lot of really weird choices that don't make complete sense in the game. Some things just frustrated me to where the only thing making me 100% the game is the fact that the only achievements are for 100%'ing the game. Is it okay for a short game, sure, its just not good in my opinion though.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing more platformers lately and ended up 100% this one.Entertainment: 35/40 + It is oh so enchanting.Design: 13/20 + You can move so fast! + I haven't played many collectathons, but this one by far had the best level design. + Levels are densely packed with characters and collectables alike. + Has one of my favorite levels in any platformer in the form of the Prismatic Palace. - Fynn (The player character) is purely momentum based, making him difficult to control.Presentation: 19/20 + This in one of the best looking games I have played in a long while. It's just so stylized and nostalgic. + A+ Character design. Everyone looks unique from not only each other, but characters from other games.Story: 14/20 + The inspiration for Fynn is that he is rescuing his unhatched siblings and that is simply adorable. + Probably my favorite character out of the bunch is Lady Opal.Total: 81/100Statement: A charming adventure that I thoroughly enjoyed the whole way through. P.S. I want plushies for this game so badly!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: cavern of dreams is an extremely well made game in the style of a n64 game. it controls really well and the music and visuals are excellent. the progression really works and it s really reasonable to find everything the game has to offer. i really like moving my little dragon guy and i especially had fun seeing what the game would let me get away with! a game like this doesnt need to be massive to be good, and i think that the smallness really allows you to keep track of everything in a way that would be harder if the game was even twice as big.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Took my time with this lil' fella. Flynn's a dragon and he's trying to protect his eggs by recovering them in this wonderful world.The game is a mega nostalgia trip to the N64-archetype platformers era (Banjo, DK64, SM64, ...). The game offers some gimmicks, but I'm giving this massive positive review for it because it's a simple game, it's not overly complicated, it's charming and it has some very loveable designs.That being said, if I had to summarise it properly. It's Banjo, but shorter and messier than Banjo. You see, a ton of things in this game can go super wrong, but those same things allows you to be creative with things. Sometimes you need an item to go at special place... or a lot of platforming skills to make up not having it.Will say, some things are a little frustrating. I think your character should move a little faster by default, it takes too long outside of the roll ability to do things at time (maybe adding a running bind would help).Otherwise, this is a solid 9/10, it's not perfect, but it has the right things for an N64 platformer, just not as memorable as Banjo or DK64, but it's fine for a newer short game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely little game and relatively easy. It's a great time for all ages, or if you've got a youngin' that's just getting into gaming and you're looking for something that might bring you some nostalgia. Nice little puzzles, hidden collectables, pretty basic story but the message is still very solid. Quite short, but I didn't feel it overstayed it's welcome, nor made me thirst for more.If I had one Wish for it though, it would be to have more reasons to use the roll mechanic. It's a fun action that works really well, but the levels are just not very designed for it, and maybe only two puzzles had any use for it (though you could complete it without the ability). Such a shame for a rather fun mechanic that had a good amount of thought put into it. Overall, a solid recommendation if you're looking for a "keep the kids busy" weekend. I know I would've had a blast with it when I was younger <3
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. If you're looking for a N64-era collectathon platformer, definitely give this a try. The controls are easy to pick up, but challenging to master. Slowly you uncover different maneuvers that make the platforming so much fun. Pretty simple puzzles for a good chunk of the game, but some of them can be challenging if you aren't paying attention. The art direction and world design provide a nostalgic backdrop for you to explore. The hub world is fun to explore, and you'll find little secrets tucked away in every corner.Would love a Cavern of Dreams 2!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great game, there are more movement options than I expected based on trailers. There is even an OP move that I'm not even sure is meant to be there. I won't give it away directly but let's just say if you slap the ground (not the ground pound move) after doing a certain combo of 2 other moves it sends you flying straight up. Sometimes this move just gives you a decent sized boost in the air and other times it sends you way high up and I'm not sure if it's random or because of momentum or the timing of how you combine the moves but you can sequence break the hell out of this game using this move. If it isn't intentional and gets patched out at least I got a playthrough using it! It was fun to experiment with getting around a level and avoid the intended route. Kinda felt like mario 64 hacks that give you an extended or new moveset and get you to think about the new ways you can navigate a level. At times it felt like it made the game too easy tho so I might consider a playthrough not using it whether it gets patched or not. So movement is awesome, visuals are awesome, there's a whole lotta charm, and level design is also awesome... for the most part. As much as I love this game I do have some criticisms and complaints. The spoiler free short version is that there are just some areas that don't feel up to quality compared to the rest of the game.Now mild spoilers ahead...The last level was a complete change up and was a negative experience for me. It felt like everything before it was that s-tier banjo kazooie quality, and then the last level reminded me of rare's mistakes in games like banjo tooie and dk64. Completing it just wasnt much fun in my experience - cryptic puzzles that leave you wandering around a lot and scratching your head, weak level design overall compared to previous levels, and a lot of empty space with the collectibles being too spread out leaving the level feel very disjointed. It wasn't terrible but it wasn't nearly as enjoyable as the rest of the game, and some parts of the level weren't enjoyable at all. Then the final boss/challenge was more of a nuisance/chore than it was a fun challenge. Half the time I got knocked off the course because of some janky BS and by the end of it I was just thinking "jeesh finally that's over" instead "hell ya I did it" - it really didn't take that long but it just wasn't fun... at all. It's sad because up until the last level and the final boss I was infatuated with the game and was thinking "this is 10/10 for sure"But after beating the final boss/challenge that 10/10 got brought down to an 8/10. I really don't wanna dismiss how great the rest of the game is, and hopefully the ending is a better experience for most people. I love bynine - this dev is going places and I appreciate all that they've done for the bk rom hacking community so I don't want to diminish the great things here.... just wanted to vent a bit lolSo let me reiterate- there is A LOT to love about this game and if you're a fan of the n64 visuals and/or 3d platformers then this is a must play. It's well worth the price even with its flaws. It just felt like one of those movies you are so captivated by because of how good it is and then the ending just isn't up to par with the rest of the movie and leaves you feeling a bit disappointed/confused
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable N64-style platformer, with an atmosphere that oscillates between "cheerful" and "unsettling" with surprising smoothness. It made me feel a sense of nostalgic wonder in a way that games haven't in a while, wondering what secrets or cute scenery was waiting for me as I delved deeper... and it also made my skin crawl in certain segments with outstanding tension building (no cheap scares; it's pure atmosphere and context).Overall, it's short and sweet; absolutely worth the price and time I took to fully complete it. And c'mon, just LOOK at Fynn. How could you even resist helping him find his family?
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is a good example of a game that does one thing very well: it's an unapologetic love letter to N64-era 3D platformers/collectathons and just gives you a very polished experience of that. And I don't even really like the N64 aesthetic that much, so that goes to show this game is onto something.The character's moveset looks underwhelming at first, but there's actually a lot of strategy and tech that goes into the movement and the stages are a blast to jump through. It's a surprisingly challenging game in that regard, and some of the puzzles left me genuinely stumped for a while too. Thankfully finding all of the eggs (this game's version of jiggies) isn't mandatory so there's no pressure to pursue a puzzle if you really don't want to.Tonally the game tends to be fairly cheery, though there's also a healthy helping of spooky stuff. However, it never feels overdone or tasteless- it very accurately mimics the unexplained creepiness games like Mario 64 or Ocarina of Time had and in the age of creepypastas it's very impressive that it manages to tread that fine line while still feeling like it firmly belongs in that era.All in all if you like 3D platformers at all it's a must play. There are a couple eggs and cards that are way harder than they should be though, so don't be afraid to use a guide if it comes to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: It's the N64 game that formed a culture in the recesses of your subconscious. Fully germinating into a work of living nostalgia. All through the dedicated hard work and tallent of Bynine. There are so many little references and nods to events, areas, and puzzles of those old platformers, but never to its detriment or loss of identity. It controls great, the visuals are spot on perfect, and the level design really captures the appeal of exploring early 3D game environments without the frustration and tedium that would sometimes come with it. I'm only missing one card somewhere in the main lobby, and I think I may have broken an easter egg quest, but I don't think it's vital for completion. It's a perfect weekend game, 100% worth the price
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun nostalgia-fueled adventure that's clearly inspired by Banjo Kazooie and Spyro. _childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet, a fantastic 3D platforming experience. This game is crafted beautifully and perfectly encompasses the N64 era of platformers with its art style, sound design, and atmosphere. Every minute I felt immersed, back in my childhood playing the classics on my old CRT. I very much appreciate the Blur option to give even more of that feeling, though you're more than welcome to turn it off if it's not your thing, which is great to have a choice.The levels in this game are all unique and offer fun challenges both in puzzle and platforming, and I felt very satisfied whenever I was able to complete any given level. I will also commend the game in its immaculate ability to present the player with eerie and unsettling areas very reminiscent of the kinds of things you'd find in these kinds of games in the past. Overall, if you're a fan of classic 3D platformers, this is a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great throwback to the Nintendo 64 collectathons of yesteryear, with lovingly blocky, 64 bit graphics to boot. It's not a long game, only about two hours if you know what you're doing, and a little simple, but the atmosphere is very chill and the puzzles are fun to solve. If you want a simple game to kick back with, this could be right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is definitely a must play for Collectathon obsessed gamers. The game is accurate to the N64 era even down to its faults.Things I liked:> Solid platforming and unique feel > Some good jingles and sound FX> The Roll ability > Charming atmosphere and aesthetics> Cute character designs> Well hidden secrets Things I didn't like:> The way some of the levels link together (why are there 3 entrances to the forest?)> The camera could be a little more modern> Too few puzzles require the use of the roll or the bubble> Some puzzles are just too cryptic> The octopus puzzle (nobody liked that ♥♥♥♥ in Spyro idk why you copied it)> The living airship was a great character/setting but the level was far too short> The idea of turning the airship at an angle is a great game mechanic but I only needed it for 1 collectible> Certain areas are too big only having one egg> The constant tone shift of certain areas into uncanny and creepy is a weird choice (We all remember finding weird and surreal areas in old games when we were kids but what made them impactful is how hidden and rare they were in contrast with the rest of the happy-go-lucky style)> The jester boots are a cool idea but they just seemed like an unnecessary mechanic when your character has a glide ability.> Some of the sound FX are too repetitive or just downright bad (Your little dragon siblings cheeping is annoying and hitting  ice sounds unpleasant)> The music is too sleepy (Get Kent Kercher for your next game)> Towards the end of the game certain assets and textures are kinda ugly > Stunlocked by enemies> Gallery of Nightmares was the worst part of the game (frustrating puzzles, lack of direction, ugly level design)It might sound like I'm tearing into this game but pretty much all of these cons can be overlooked if you're an N64/Collectathon veteran as it is fairly short and reasonably priced. I wanted to point out the issues I have with this game because I really enjoyed it and am looking forward to the Dev's next project, which will likely blow this out of the water.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This review is being written after 100% Completion of the game (just above 5 hours playtime).Are you a big fan of 3D Platformer Collect-a-thons? I am, I grew up on the likes of Spyro and Croc. So when I saw this, I was immediately taken back, and excited to have a similar experience again with Cavern of Dreams.Take my "Yes" Recommendation with a grain of salt. I believe if this game was any higher priced, it could very well be a no from me. Here are some of my thoughts and reasoning after completing the game.For what it costs, this was absolutely worth it. The first hour or two I absolutely loved it. It's cute, charming, and took me right back to what I loved about Spyro and Croc (more leaning towards Croc with this one). There was also a hint of Frogger Swampy's Revenge, but maybe that was just me.However as I played, I grew more impatient with the game, controls, secrets, you name it. And I couldn't wait to be done.The biggest issue for me, is the controls. Fynn feels *really* slow, and I mean *REALLY* slow. You can go pretty fast with the roll move, but getting it going consistently was quite the hassle in my experience. Building any kind of momentum was either extremely sluggish, or full throttle. There was no in-between. And don't even get me started on SLOPES. Heaven forbid you have to go up an incline, no matter the size. It's going to take you a while.And that brings me into my next issue. The game starts cute, great puzzles, it was simplistic and felt fun. But the later levels give cryptic a whole new meaning. Speaking on the inclines, there is a level later in the game where you can peer down a few hallways, and at the end of one of them, is absolutely nothing! Why is that an issue? Because now you have to walk back up a massive incline. There's no fast travel, no "end life" option, nothing like that. If you get stuck somewhere, you have to get out of it. Or save and quit I guess, not even sure if that would work.The game just feels slightly unfinished. Lacking polish. And maybe that's just me. For the price, I definitely recommend trying it out if you love games like Spyro, Banjo, and Croc. But if you aren't too desperate for a new experience like those, I'd pass on this one and buy something else.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: really, really solid 3d collectathon in the spirit of classics like Banjo-Kazooie. The movement in the game is amazing, even allowing you to do a few skips IF you're good enough to pull them off. only possible flaws I can think of is the game could be a bit longer (I don't mind though, allows me to actually finish the game :p) and the camera can be a bit hard to work with at times. other than that, this game is fantastic, and if you're craving a new 3D collectathon with fantastic movement, I cannot recommend this game enough!

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful, condensed 3D puzzle platformer with charm.Loved this title, spent around 6 hours 100% completing it. A nice value for the price tag, IMO. The controls are smooth and responsive, the levels are very well designed and the puzzles are intuitive, and the game oozes charm - with memorable characters and a great pacing to the story and tension that builds in the final world. Took me forever to finally get around to playing it, but I'm soo glad I did :) Love the N64 style graphics too, and if the blur isn't your thing, they have an option to disable it to make the whole game look a tad bit sharper than the trailers show too.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: The highs are high, but the lows, when they happen, are also very low. I can't overlook that, even though I ended on a positive note.To be blunt, playing on keyboard controls made everything feel clunky, awkward, and unintuitive; and combining that with aspects that are needlessly, disproportionately punishing (e.g. "instant-death, respawn-at-the-last-loading-zone", when it could have just been a minor setback) made parts of the game exactly the opposite of fun. In particular, the final-boss sequence, with its lack of checkpoints, felt unpolished, and didn't "feel" achievable, even though it very much is.WITH ALL OF THAT HAVING BEEN SAID,There is a fantastic game in here; it just jostles for space alongside those unfortunate aspects. It's cute, it's captivating, it's endearing, it's charming, it's atmospheric, it's emotional, and it's very visibly a labour of love on the part of its creators. This is in no world a "bad" game. It's a brilliant game with a few "but"s attached.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is a game that touches on N64 3D platformer games' style and aesthetic for better and for worse, and I absolutely love it!It's a game filled with whimsy and cheer that will embrace you with both arms from the very start. Fynn, the player character, is so adorable that I actually have to give the game a point on that alone because it was a driving force to see the little dragon reach his goal! He controls very well and simply, though there are a couple tricky techniques (such as the roll launch and Ecco-style diving) the player will have to become proficient with to truly tap into Fynn's surprising amount of mobility. It's actually easy to overthink obstacles by implementing your full suite of maneuvers which can make them more challenging to overcome than necessary, but at the same time, the fact that it's still possible to do so your own way makes it all the more satisfying when you ultimately do. Again, something that is in spirit of the games that provided inspiration for Cavern of Dreams.The graphics excellently capture the blocky models and over-stretched textures the N64 was so well known for while keeping the world vibrant, decorative, colorful, and even not! I say "even not" because there are moments when the game brings in a distinct lack of color, a pitch black void, or downright dreary or lonely surroundings for atmospheric effect, once again hearkening to the moments in older games when we didn't know if we the developers knew they were making a place feel so unwelcoming and haunting. Those places really make you feel like a small vulnerable dragon in a big dangerous world, but be brave, little one!Now, when I said "for worse" in the beginning, it's because that "worse" (namely the occasional crypticness and backtracking) seems artistically implemented to only touch on some of the frustrating aspects of those old N64 3D platformers just enough bring back the feelings of playing those games while keeping them on a leash. It actually put me back in the skin and a state of mind of when I was younger, when my homework was done, and the next run of the gauntlet was sure to be the one that I'd see the end. Challenging though they'd be, they were better days, and it made me smile to relive them without forcing them out of retirement, all in a brand new adventure.• Platformers from the era of gaming when 3D was first becoming common, like Banjo-Kazooie, Spyro the Dragon, and Super Mario 64• An enchanting world and characters that tap into your childlike sense of wonder, adventure, friendship, and playful danger• An absolutely adorable player character you wish you could hug• Gameplay that rewards maneuverability, timing, and spatial awareness more than twitch reaction• Exploration and collectible hunting that isn't overly demanding or drawn out• A game that is inexpensive and lengthed appropriately• A game for all ages• A deep story• Any form of combat (seriously, of the few "enemies" that exist in the game, your goal is to avoid them rather than fight them)• Crisp and realistic textures on detailed models• No backtracking• A lot of replayability• Markers or notes that tell you exactly where to go or how to solve puzzles• A game that makes you feel macho when others see you playing itCavern of Dreams is an abundantly charming game filled with heart that is beautiful in how quaint it is without sacrificing anything to make it an actual game. It knows exactly what it is, it succeeds in capturing a distinct time and theme, and it does so with perfection by respecting that time and theme, the player, and itself. Though it may not be a particularly expansive or cerebral game, if it tried to be any more than what it is, it'd be trying to be something it's not, and it would be a disservice to itself and the experience. And what a delightful experience it is!So, uh... When can I buy a Fynn plush?
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a cute, sincere homage to early 3D collectathons! If you enjoyed M64 and BK back in the day, and love how Lunistice and Toree expand on low-poly 3D platformers now, then Cavern of Dreams hits a sweet-spot I never thought I'd experience again. The mechanics take time to get a feel for, but they expand into really fun depths the further you dive into the Cavern. Charming characters and interesting worlds, beating the game doesn't take much time but 100% is worth it for the care and detail poured into every edge and corner.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is the 3D platformer with really good aesthetics that you need. It controls really well, the main areas are really nice designed with collectables placed carefully (not just thrown around), the enviroment is always on point being beautiful, creppy or a mix of both, a interesting but not intrusive story and even fun easter eggs!.The game is in the shorter side tho, you can finish it in one sitting, which I personally find it great, concentrating the good aspects into a consistent good time that never lets down. Basically it's a really good Banjo with a mix of Kirby Crystal Shards and Majora's Mask aesthetic

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game while browsing social media and the dev posted a release trailer and after I had watched it I was very interested in what the game had to offer. After only a few minutes of owning the game it just clicked with me. It holds true to a lot of what you'd see of platformers of the 64 bit era. I got many reminders of Glover, Mario64, and Banjo from this game.I'm no great at reviews but things that I took from this game that I hope others find value in too:-Its not a long game, the collectibles are very contained and 100% completion values your time with well designed goals. I loved that I could enjoy the entire experience to 100% completion in about 4 days of playing on and off. So many games now are extremely long and padded with content that I cant bring myself to finish them.-The game has a momentum mechanic that you can mess with to speed through levels. A lot of games I've played that do this often make levels very centered around this and they're unreasonably huge. However Cavern of Dreams levels are sized perfectly to have this mechanic not be central to its design but instead adds to its puzzles and traversal.-A lot of the puzzles and platforming challenges can be tackled in more than one way if you're willing to try different things with the physics or get clever with your jumps. There were some eggs that i collected that when i got it I saw the likely intended means of getting there and was happy that I found my way there in my own way.-The levels have a handful of shortcuts to other worlds instead of having to always navigate through the hub. You'll also find out that items do not despawn between world transitions which comes in handy!Things that I wish were better:-The game introduces a simple attack that can be used in the air and on the ground implying there will be a few enemy encounters. The game is almost entirely devoid of enemies outside of things that visually are enemies, but act more so as obstacles. The attack is used primarily for puzzle solving and movement which is great! Though a handful of simple enemies would have added some life to the worlds.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a cute game!It took all the right lessons on how to design a satisfying collect-a-thon that even classics didn't always get right.The different worlds are all very striking in their own unique way. Unlocking new abilities and exploring every nook and cranny was a joy with Fynn's almost Sonic-like physics and rolling ability. Navigating was also very pleasant and I basically never got lost with how detailed every bit of the game felt.In terms of platforming challenge, this is definitely on the easier side. Most hazards just knock you back and falling in a pit never sets you back far. Go into this expecting more Banjo-Kazooie with Sonic physics, and less Crash Bandicoot or Mario.Had the game crash on me just once, but with autosaving I never lost any progress.Was able to 100% the game in I think 7~ hours-ish (a bit of time was spent afk), and the reward for doing so is I think very worth it.All in all, highly reccommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely precious 3D platformer. Good controls, good level designs, good puzzles, great vibe all around. Also some creepy undertones and spooky lore if you dig deep enough. It's not very challenging tho. No lives, no health, damage only sends you flying and pitfalls bring you to the last doorway. Very casual and forgiving, but not to the point of insulting. If you are looking for a very relaxed 3D collect-a-thon platformer, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: After laying a few of these retro-inspired 3D platformers, Cavern of Dreams stands above basically all of them by heads and shoulders. It doesn't set out to frustrate you for no reason, its world is well-thought out and appropriately mixes the whimsy with the darkness in a way I can actually compare with some of those old N64 games, the controls feel great and progressively get better as you unlock continuous upgrades, and there's plenty of option stuff to explore once you finish the main bulk of the game.The only complaint I have is that it's a pretty short game. I only wish there was more of it. Every individual level is packed with charm and care, and I'm anxious to see what comes next from the dev.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: A solid and straight forward game in the style of Banjo-Kazooie, Mario 64, A Hat in Time, and other collectathon type games. You can complete and collect everything without any power-up beyond what you have when you enter each zone which is nice, and some of the eggs have that extra degree of complexity which is really nice. It's a bit buggy and the camera's weird at times, but for a game that's largely made by one person it's pretty solid.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: A very charming and entertaining game, reminiscent of classic 3D collectathon titles such as Banjo-Kazooie and the original Spyro trilogy. The game sports a beautiful art style along with unique and interesting locations that the player can explore. Alongside the games visuals, the gameplay itself is both fun and fluid, with momentum based movement that makes traversing through late game zones fast and exciting, especially once most if not all of the available power-ups have been unlocked.Cavern of Dreams is a fairly short game, taking me only about 6 hours to 100%. The game contains 3 different types of collectibles for you to seek out: the eggs of your dragon siblings, Cards which contain fun little details about the various characters in the game, and mushrooms that you can feed to your little hatchling brothers and sisters. Despite the game's relatively short time to complete, it manages to find ways to stay challenging and test the player's mastery of the game while still not overstaying its welcome. If the player chooses to challenge themselves to gather every Dragon egg, the payoff is VERY rewarding. I don't want to spoil the reward, but I will say that it encouraged me to spend an extra hour of my time in game despite already 100%-ing it.That all being said, I'm very happy I purchased this game. It was short, sweet, and exactly what I wanted out of a collectathon. I highly recommend for others to check it out, especially with it being offered for the criminally low price that it is. I'm really looking forward to what the Developer has planned for the future, be it Cavern of Dreams related or otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just the thing you need when you're a bit tired of all the super dark and mature games that are so common nowadays. Don't get me wrong, a dark and serious game can be awesome, but sometimes, all you want is a cozy and wholesome little adventure with a cute baby dragon in search of its little siblings.Cavern of Dreams is an adorable reimagining of the usual 3D platforming collectathon, with a greater emphasis on puzzling than on action, and this adorable child-friendly dreamy atmosphere that goes perfectly with the gameplay. You play as a cute little dragon who, with the help of a mysterious entity called Sage, needs to save all its little siblings from an evil bat called Luna in the titular cavern. Your adventure will take you through a small selection of adorably crafted 3D platforming worlds full of collectibles, puzzles, and charm.Many collectathons from back in the day were content with having a rather "edgy" tone to it, with characters being straight up jerks for the sake of comedy (think Kazooie, Laylee, etc), but this game is unapologetically wholesome and ethereal. Every world has a character to be helped, and once they're helped, they're thankful and call you their friend. But not everything is what it seems, as there is always this rather sorrowful undertone to the whole thing, even right from the start. As you approach the end, it starts becoming ever more obvious that something is up. I still haven't reached the point where the proverbial other shoe drops, but I can definitely feel it coming.The one huge complaint I have about this game is that there isn't more of it. I'd so love more of it. It's much too short, I want mooooooore :(
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams
