_childDocuments_.review: A Dream-like game, but not always in the best waysCavern of Dreams is an N64 inspired puzzle platformer that is trying to change up the platforming genre by creating a unique movement mechanic that helps it stand out, but not always in a good way.There isn't much story here, but what story exists is enough to keep the plot coherent.  The main pull of this game is the nostalgia and level designs.Each level is visually interesting and compelling, and each world has at least one character in it to interact with, which is always a nice touch.  The levels are large enough to require exploring, but not so large that they become tedious to navigate, which is great considering the higher power of modern consoles often lead platformers to become bloated.  There are 3 main collectibles in this game; eggs, mushrooms, and cards.  The eggs are your siblings and tie into obtaining character abilites, the mushrooms allow you to open shortcuts to each level, and the cards unlock gallery entries giving you insight into the different "characters" in the game.  These collectibles are usually easy to find but require skill to obtain, which is a great way of setting up a platformer.The main thing that sets Cavern of Dreams apart from other platformers is the actual platforming you'll be doing.  In this game, rather than having a double jump, to reach greater hights you must jump on the ground twice with proper timing.  This is what I find to be the greatest issue to the fun of this game.  The reason this is a problem is two fold: 1. it makes platforming take longer than neccessary because you have to stop in place and jump twice constantly to reach the height you need, and 2. the game also has a glide mechanic that uses the jump button, so if you mistime the jump, you'll begin gliding and it'll prevent a double jump, or worse, take you off a ledge.Honestly, the movement mechanics in this game as a whole appear to be aiming at making the game a high skill floor and high skill ceiling kind of game, but it ends up just making the platforming imprecise and annoying.Having said that, I do recommend this game if you're willing to put up with some annoying controls, because it's a fun game that really leans into its aesthetic and that aesthetic is a good one.  However, this game, while it looks kid friendly, will likely frustrate a child too much, so it should be reserved for nostalgia seekers only.

_childDocuments_.review: This one bummed me out a bit. It was missing 2 things that kept it from being great for me, and left me bored and contemplating a refund after just a little while playing.#1 The contorls feel floaty and not precise at all. Platformers should be fun to control. Period. Spyro, crash bandicoot, super mario 64, all had tight controls. Those games were fun even just to run around in the starting area doing nothing at all. This game felt more like I was suggesting movement to the character than actively controlling the character.#2 the music doesn't grab me. It makes me feel sleepy. Not relaxed. Sleepy. It makes me feel bored. Platformers like the ones I mentioned above have catchy music that burrows into your head like an earwig. I felt weird leaving this game a negative review when its so highly rated, and I know its a small developer (and I do like indy developers and indy games) but floaty controls on a platformer are a no for me. There are too many other great games to play. ~PR0XIDIAN

_childDocuments_.review: This game has left me speechless. It has scratched every nostalgia box from my old N64 platforming days and even outdoing those games. _childDocuments_.review: If you love simple 3D platformers, you'll love this onean N64-styled indie game that packed full of whimsical charm and wonderthe game has a strong sense of atmosphere, bringing both dreams (and nightmares) to life!Pros:-Varied Moveset, with hidden techniques keen for speedrunning- Dense Levels, no getting lost with how close together things are and how fast your roll can get- Charming characters and Locations- Music is Dynamic and shifts when changing areasCons:- Basic jump is a little too stumpy, despite the great speeds you can get. I've fallen down pits from what could have been basic jumps but I fell just short of it. the game could use a more consistent ledge grab too- Finding the last few remaining collectables, like mushrooms and cards, could use a hints system too- Final Boss is VERY unforgiving but also very braindead if you got all the eggs and unlocked the final ability, it's a doomed if you do doomed if you don't scenario. I suggest check points at each phase of the final stretch- while the camera is good, it could use some fine tuning so it doesn't drift up so much when I'm trying to land on something while falling. this was notable during the tile puzzles when I was trying to ground pound under a time limit.- personal negative but this is because of my personal tastes: the final world was a bit too scary for a game like this, it was shockingly unnerving near the end.Great game, would play again but it could use a touch up or two to be truly a perfect indie N64 game

_childDocuments_.review: im almost done with this game so i thought i'd begin talking about my thoughts.so, the first thing i want to talk about is the mood of the game. i thought it was just going to be a fun, good vibes game all the way through, but there's actually a handful of segments that range from nerve-inducing to downright disturbing or even scary. so, if you want to grab this game, expect some disturbing locations and/or music. it probably won't do as a cozy platforming game if you're easily frightened.there were some puzzles i had to brute force through. i probably missed the hints, but i feel like they could have given you the information you need to solve them in a better way.there's no enemies in this game, so this game is a lot more about puzzle solving and figuring out ways to get those collectables. so, be warned if you were wanting a platformer with some combat in it. on the brighter side, though, the game really does a good job at getting that n64 feel, and the blur filter is a nice touch. the environments are well made, and when the music isn't getting pitched and tempoed down, its pretty good. i like how it even sounds like n64 music! the controls feel good, as well. the camera could be better, but it didn't impede my enjoyment from the game. its very fun! you'll enjoy this if you like spyro games.

_childDocuments_.review: When I randomly found out about this game I was extremely excited to buy it and check it out because games like Banjo Kazooie, SM64, Spyro, etc... were my childhood and games in that genre are just not made anymore or not quite as often at least which is sad. I enjoyed playing Yooka Laylee when it came out as a Spiritual successor to Banjo Kazooie as well.That being said I have to say this game does not dissapoint at all. And I 100%'ed the game in 7 hoursIt's cute, it's fun;the controls are tight; smooth and responsive; the platforming, exploration and gameplay is fun and feels rewarding.I maybe just wish it was a little bit longer, but for the very low price I can not complain at all. In fact I would have paid even more for this. Nintendo brings games with less content for more money.This game does a very good job as a spiritual successor to some of my favorite games and I hope the developers will make more like this.I will however note here that this game despite it's cute exterior becomes rather challenging real quickly and while I didn't mind this it might put some people off. That being said the challenge doesn't just come from platforming, there's some very random and hard to figure out secrets or puzzles in the game. Early on you get some hints and riddles that are pretty intuitive and not that hard to solve, but later on you get less and less hints or they become incredibly cryptic. I had to look up at least 2 things online in order to find them because I just got stuck trying to 100% the game.

_childDocuments_.review: If I was to rate Cavern of Dreams out of 10 it would be a 5. I will cover 3 main issues I had with the game that stopped it scoring higher to me.MovementSo lets break down why I personally feel its a 5 starting with movement. The movement is your classic 3d platformer movement with a few unlock-able upgrades which I wont spoil outside the first one but needless to say they where rather generic. So to start with you have a roll ability you can use to gain momentum and run slightly faster with. The issue is any degree of slope kills the momentum slowing you down to a crawl. The other issue is that wall hit box's can feel sticky at times and despite not touching them the game treats it like you are so again kills your momentum and if you try to jump you can end up bonking your head on invisible lips on the wall. As i previously mentioned you do get upgrades the first being your tail attack that if you time it right when you do it in the air you can launch yourself forward repeatedly which can be very fun. However, just like rolling any slight alteration in terrain height or just being a little to close to a wall for the games liking and your tail attack will hit it sending you off in an unintended direction or flat out killing momentum. These two issues coupled with the rather small feeling levels hinder the movement from truly shining.SoundtrackNext to touch upon would be the soundtrack. Personally I found it rather boring and forgettable and honestly lacking something to make it stand out. However, I will say the theme for the main hub area works well for setting the area's tone and vibe and is the only track that I can remember.Level designThe levels are like Marmite to me I liked 2 of them and found the other 2 Boring and lacking. Starting with the negative The final 2 levels an ice themed one and a spooky gallery just felt like they undelivered on there location. Starting with the ice level I will say they nailed the ice physics not to slippery that you can't control it but not so little it may as not it exist. However, the level overall just felt lacking in a real personality coupled with a location that was moved there from the demo it left me feeling that not enough love was put into the world.Onto the the final level a spooky gallery themed level It starts good with the basement sequence before just falling into feeling like I've seen it all before in the outside section with a janky hitbox dead fish enemy that can knock you into the water sending you back into the basement. Or if you go the other way a fire themed room which leads into another location moved from the demo which worked better where it originally was in my opinion . The issue of the previous ice level still continue's here as overall a level called gallery of nightmares just didn't live up to its name there was no real feeling of unease produced.On the other hand the first 2 levels are very good the first level perfectly captures that retro first level in a 3d platformer vibes and getting the player to explore . Meanwhile, the second level an airship reminiscent of a certain metal shark/fish from banjo kazooie builds on it by having the player tilt the airship to gain access to different area's and being the only level i found i had to leave and return to with another power despite collecting what i felt was all possible eggs up to that point which is both a positive and negative depending on personal preference. In closing on the levels it may have helped switching the 2nd and 3rd levels round to give the impression of building mechanics on the levels as you progress through the game as well as again personal preference I feel the airship leads better into the gallery tonally.SummaryThe game is neither good or bad but just average  if you are craving and N64 styled collectathon to kill a few hours you can do worse so go ahead and give it a try. However, if you what something longer lasting or memorable I'd say skip or wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and fast movement with a cute retro design, but the second half of the game is a mess.Cavern of Dreams nails the N64 platformer style while also playing like a smoother, more modern platformer. Once you've unlocked a few power-ups, moving around gets to be pretty enjoyable, which is good since there can be a lot of distance between points of interest on any given level.Sadly, the later levels are dishearteningly disorganized. The number of dead-end offshoots and back-to-back puzzles the final few areas provide is exhausting. The solution to some puzzles is often provided somewhere completely different, creating a sense of doubt and disinterest whenever a suspicious landmark rolls into view. The game fails to establish a consistent or respectable range of how far a puzzle can reach. When a door says “a mechanism somewhere around here”, ‘here’ starts to feel like ‘anywhere’. Furthermore, many environmental details suggest the presence of a puzzle but offer no visible interactivity to confirm that this is a place that can be altered or that it’s at least somewhere to remember. The finale was also a prolonged camera-angle nightmare with a sprinkling of randomness to keep it nice and agonizing.Had I called it at the two/three-hour mark, I probably would’ve left with a wonderful impression of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard review to leave. On one hand, the care and attention is there, and I see that. But the game has flaws in my opinion that outweigh nostalgic pros for me. I grew up with this era of games that this emulates, 64/PS1 games. This does a lot right in that regard, it nails the music, and the graphics. But the momentum is all wrong in the movement. And movement is crucial in a platformer. When rolling you will start to roll and start super slow then go fast all of a sudden, no ramp up in speed. There are no enemies, other than obstacle type enemies. This is a con in my opinion. I want the satisfaction of beating an enemy. Also, the obstacles send you flying ,which once again in a platformer stinks, as you lose all progress. There are no checkpoints. There is also no fast travel or map, and it gets confusing to keep up with this stuff. Some of the puzzles are super obtuse. I mean randomly obtuse. I know once again, it's trying to be like the games of the era, but some are just bad. I actually gave up on the final boss, as the final boss, is a long narrow platformer full of obstacles, with one enemy spamming you with projectiles. This knocks you off, and you have to start all over. This just gets tiring, its not even difficult, its just annoying and not fun. Its a shame, as like I said, this does a lot right and is clearly a love letter, but a platformer should entice you to want to play and collect everything, not get lost in a labyritnth of obtuse puzzles and hazards that knock you off of platforms nonstop without actually hurting you. I would be interested in a sequel to this game, that said, as like I said, I didn't hate it, I just think I didn't like it as the cons outweighed the pros for me. I'd also say if the puzzles are like they are here, I'd legit get an old school strategy guide on it if the dev had it bundled, as like I said, some puzzles are just out there, and not really making sense, I say this as an avid puzzle game fan too.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: I think this game is alright if you're thinking of getting it, but I would recommend you buy Corn Kidz 64 over this (yes I am advertising another game in this review).This is one of those times that I would really like to have a mixed/unsure/"thumbs middle" option for a Steam review. I don't think Cavern of Dreams is "bad", and thus I wouldn't give it a negative review, but I don't think it's particularly great either. Like in terms of gameplay I thought it was good enough: the controls were fine, and the various movement options you start with and unlock throughout the game were enjoyable for the most part. The one exception being the "slam", or more specifically, the "swipe" you need to do before you can do the slam, as that can knock you away from the platform you're on if you hit a wall or something with it, which was a consistent annoyance. Thankfully death in this game has essentially no consequences, so it wasn't super annoying, just mildly.Really it was more or less everything else that dragged the game down for me. The general aesthetics (like character and "world" designs) to me was a generic, "cutesy" style, the sort of safe, clean thing you might make for children. That's not inherently a bad thing, but it didn't particularly appeal to me. The story and characters (what few there) didn't have much going on with them. Again, not inherently a bad thing, especially for a platformer like this, but a more fleshed out story and/or characters I think would've helped keep me interested in the game. Then there's the soundtrack, which outside of a few songs, I thought was largely forgettable. It's unfortunate to me because a good soundtrack can really help elevate a game, in fact part of why I like Corn Kidz is that it has such a quality soundtrack. If one or more of these aspects were better, I'm sure I would've enjoyed the game a lot more.So what's my ultimate recommendation? Obviously it's that you should buy Corn Kidz 64, because I believe it's a much better game. Didn't you read the tl;dr? I even put it at the top! But, if you're not interested in that game, then I don't think you'll have a bad time if you decide to get this game. Or you could get both games. Or neither! The options are not limitless, but they are yours to make.

Your basic jump feels way too short, and while you can do a second higher jump with some timing after you land from the first jump, the timing is a bit strict for how little extra height you gain.Its a fun little game, but definitely wait until its 50% off.I dont really want to draw comparisons on a review of all places, but Corn Kidz 64 is another similar indie game that costs half the price, is WAY more polished and oozing with style and flair with controls that feel great.

_childDocuments_.review: Cannot say enough good things about this game. It's like the devs took all the problems I had with YookaLaylee and a Hat in Time and just fixed them. One of the hardest parts of making these types of games is just making it fun to run around in the worlds and they nailed it. The weight, physics, jumping, and moveset all work together extremely well. It just feels really good to play. The levels are appropriately sized for the amount of content in them; they don't feel empty at all and it's a joy to just explore. I'm mixed on the absence of enemies to kill, but the devs make it work. The enemies that are present are more like stage hazards. I don't think the game would be necessarily improved by the addition of mobs. Music and sound design are also on point here.Challenge is appropriate and it feels really good to piece together context clues to figure out challenges, but it does get significantly more difficult in the (spoilers) ice level. This game has a ton of charm and is super well designed and thought out. If you've been underwhelmed by 3D collectathons that have come out in the past decade GET THIS.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

The only thing that I haven't gotten used to is the camera, which fights with me just a little bit. I use a controller to play it and that's the only thing that messes with me. There's also a bit in the game and I know other people don't get this way, but I experienced a tiny bit of motion sickness (probably not motion sickness, just similar dizzy spell) from the camera angle. I get the same way when I play Banjo-Kazooie. But overall, the game is still a really fun time and I recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't get myself to even try finishing this game and simply got a refund. I was pretty excited for the game and foolishly assumed that it having a higher price tag than similar games meant that it'd have a certain level of polish and creativity with competent devs.... Hooooo boy was I wrong.The game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lies to you before you enter the first area. It says that you can get all the eggs in a world when you first unlock it, but it'll be easier to get them if you get more abilities... The airship literally has an egg that requires an ability from later and I had to look up a guide to learn that the game just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lied to me and I wasn't stupid.The game doesn't have the greatest start from sound design to general gameplay. I can't actually remember if there was even any music in the game or just ambient noises... The fact that they're asking 12.99 for it at full price feels like way too much for the quality of what you're getting. You can get Super Kiwi 64 for less than a third of that price, and it got a full free DLC addition that took its overall length to about 90 minutes which doesn't overstay its welcome while feeling very fun and refreshing to play. Cavern of Dreams gets stale very quickly since none of the upgrades make gameplay any smoother or more fun.This game feels a bit clunky control-wise, and even considering how I can see it being plausible to have speedrunning-type tech with optimized routes for some areas, most of it's just painfully slow. The fact that your ability to glide can only move at a snail's pace and kills all your momentum makes it even worse. Lots of the "Greats" of the N64 area had controls that feel much tighter than this game's despite having been made 30 years ago on dated hardware. I really feel that movement is a huge factor of how enjoyable a game can be regardless of the end game design, and that's sadly a missed note in this title. An example of something really frustrating is that you can only break breakable walls if you're on the ground using a ground attack... Even though you can use attacks in the air as well. If the jank physics decide to put you off the ground, you'll use an air attack and it'll look like the object wasn't breakable after all unless you decide to reposition because you know you're right and able to break the wall. It doesn't help that there's knock-back from aerial attacks so sometimes when you try to attack and it decides you're "not on the ground" it'll end up knocking you back and possibly off of the platform you were standing on...To make matters worse, the game has mushrooms that are PRESUMABLY supposed to send you back to where you were, but the physics are so awful that some of them will literally kill you instead which sends you back to the start of the level and makes you spend multiple minutes trekking back to where you were PURELY because of incompetent devs... Yeah, great. There are multiple areas with "super-bouncy" mushrooms like that which feel like the devs just said, "Eh, that'll send them vaguely in the correct direction" and just let you suffer.It also doesn't help that the game defaults to having a disgusting blurred filter on launch which you need to turn off.Oh, I almost forgot... I don't even know why this game has an antagonist bat thing... It's served next to no purpose and is terribly written for what it has done/said. The game would have somehow been slightly more meaningful if they'd just randomly said that some magic went wrong and teleported the eggs randomly places instead of having the bat exist. Maybe it was added because they want to market plushies or something, I don't know.

_childDocuments_.review: "This can't be better than The Last (s)Tinker" - Friend No. 1"I can smell the stinky from a mile away" - Friend No. 2"...one more game rejected" - Friend No. 3You might have a problem if three friends, independent of each other, send you such messages when they see you're playing Cavern of Dreams. Undeterred, I continued to blast through CoD and even got 100% of the achievements, putting me up there with the top 16% of CoD players. It's not surprising that this number is so low considering that most people don't actually finish games they start. However in the case of CoD, it's probably wiser to drop it, count your losses and move on while you're still ahead.There are so many issues with the game that make it a clear "do not recommend" for me. The sound design is simply irritating, death awaits you at every corner in unfair, unexpected ways and the platforming is simply finnicky. Even the wide FOV which you'd assume would be a good thing ends up creating a fish eye lens effect, which made me feel nauseous at times. At best, the level design is half-baked, making it very difficult to engage with unless you have been diagnosed with EOBKM (Early Onset Banjo-Kazooie Madness).I really liked the idea of unlocking abilities after collecting a certain number of items (eggs). I kept expecting the abilities to get better but here's a shocker: They didn't! That is, until you collect all of the eggs and unlock the ultimate ability - a pair of little dragon wings. At that point, you can fly anywhere, breaking the game and finally allowing you to get the rest of collectibles you couldn't get due to the impossible, finnicky platforming mentioned above. This "highlight" made up about 30 minutes of my 7.5 hour playthrough.I'm sure enthusiasts/manchildren of the N64 3D platformer era will probably love this game. Maybe the experience is more authentic/better if you crop the screen to 4:3, play it on a CRT and have another CRT blasting M.V.P. (Most Valuable Primate) on VHS in the background. Add some caffeinated water to the mix and you'll probably also be diagnosed with EOBKM shortly thereafter.I did enjoy some of the enemy names like The Gobbler! and the personification of "Heartburn" itself. All things considered, I'd say skip this one and play a big boy game like Balan Wonderworld instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Old school to a fault. The controls are barely responsive, it feels like I'm still using my N64 controller... y'know... old, clunky, slightly broken, misshapen analogue stick. Maybe I need to unplug my keyboard, hold down, then plug it in? Because honestly, this game could use some work. The control scheme is awkward. Mouse to look around is fine, click to attack is fine, middle mouse button to focus is fine. But you cannot use the mouse in menus... That's weird.The character or the camera sways a lot when you move. Expect motion sickness.I know it's replicating games from ye olde times. But games like Croc or Ocarina of Time / Majora's Mask, play better than this. The control feels more accurate. Secondly, you cannot rebind controls. I have a friend with disabilities who'd probably be completely unable to play the game based on this. Why can't you rebind controls? That seems like a pretty basic feature to any game.You can only view the controls when you get into the game, they're not in the options menu before you get in, they're actually within the game... which... is strange.More on the controls, double jump is incredibly awkward. I don't know if I'm doing it wrong, but I can only really double jump a split second before the little cutey hits the ground. (And yes, the character is adorable, that much I cannot fault the game on, if you release a plushy I will buy it. He will guard over the eggs in the kitchen.) The game does have it's positives, it runs in windowed mode, it runs smoothly and doesn't appear to be glitchy, unless that double jump issue is a glitch maybe? It's well made, but the lack of control customisation leads me to not be able to recommend it. Even though I dislike the camera angle and sway, if the controls were customisable, I'd recommend the game to people who like things like this.The game is inexpensive and often seems to go on sale. So I cannot fault the price, if you want to give it a go yourself and decide that you enjoy it. Good. I'm glad. But for myself, I found a lot of issues with the control and camera. It made me feel ill to play it and I couldn't rebind.I suspect it's designed for gamepads more than keyboards, which... fair enough. If I ever get a gamepad that doesn't break in the first month, then I'll try that. (I always leave the comments open, if anyone can suggest a durable gamepad, that'd be great, I don't mean to break things, I'm just a bit accident prone / clumsy, also the controllers bought off amazon are usually very poor quality. Even if brand new, it's a roll of the dice whether or not it's going to last long.)Finally, I'll state as I always do on my reviews. Just because I don't recommend the game, doesn't mean I'm attacking the game, or hating on the players. The game just wasn't for me. Yes, I have low play time, because the issue I had with the game was discovered fairly quickly.  If you play the game and enjoy it? Good. I'm glad. I want people to have fun. I personally just don't recommend it.So please spare me silly comments like "You just don't like the game, so no reason to review bomb it!" yes, I really got that as a comment once... What steam is doing is asking if I personally recommend the game. Currently, no. I don't. If it had control customisation? I'd change to a yes. While I don't enjoy the game for a couple other reasons, timing, camera, I'd still recommend it for people who like this type of game.So, if you don't buy the game based on my review, I hope you can find something to satisfy that itch to play something soon! If you do buy the game despite my review. I hope you enjoy it more than I did. P.S: Devs, seriously, if you make a plushy, I will buy it, your protagonist is adorable.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat it non-100% in one sitting. I'll start by talking about the overall quality. I liked the start of the game, it felt friendly and fun and like a classic Rare game with colorful characters. It takes many interesting inspirations, obviously from N64 games but surprisingly uses mechanics from Super Mario 64 romhacks (like jumping onto fire so you bounce higher). I enjoyed that bc I've always wanted to play, but only watched videos.Mixed feelings: I liked the overall level variety; up until the end of the game I thought the puzzles and mechanics were usually not that taxing. It really ramps up in difficulty when you get to the "Nightmares" stage. I thought the hints on where to find more eggs were kind of useless. I didn't get all the eggs, but partway through the game I didn't care about 100% anymore, because of what I'll talk about next.The voices are creepy, but not in a way that helps the game, it just feels bad. The movement is clunky -- why do i lose momentum on everything? why is jumping such a chore? -- the story tries to be a Souls-style, fragmented narrative about bad parenting, but misses spectacularly at the end; the final stage and the ending are pathetic, and when you play it, you'll feel frustrated by the camera and the controls.But even if you ignore all of the other points I said, one of the last levels (a "Pit" level) is a complete showstopper in my opinion. This level is designed and plays like a creepy death scene. This was beyond uncomfortable, in a setting where you are playing as a baby dragon rescuing his unhatched egg siblings -- in a retro, Rare-style collectathon. Just please don't play this game, you're smart enough to use your time doing things that make you happy instead.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of 3D platformers and the era this pays homage to, it really pains me to give this a negative review. If I could I would give this a middle review, negative seems too harsh, but as it stand I am going with negative.The game does a great job capturing the N64 3D platformer aesthetic, which is it's main draw and may be enough to sell you. That's fine, it was enough for me. I really enjoyed the character mechanics, you unlock several abilities as you progress and there is some really cool momentum build up and preservation mechanics to play with.Lack of polish, world design, and level layout are where this game suffers the most. Too rarely do you have an open area and large space to explore. Which is a shame because the aforementioned momentum mechanics could really shine in spaces like that. Instead we get a lot of cramped and interior spaces. They weren't kidding with the name  of Dreams. The vibes are odd in this game. The level themes, visuals, sounds, characters are strange and feel somewhat off, sometimes creepy, and mostly otherworldly. For some this might be a draw, there is a uniqueness to it, but it didn't work for me.Level layouts are often baffling and confusing, while not unintelligible, I often found myself wandering aimlessly until stumbling onto something that made a piece of the level make sense. It is a bit hard to describe but the levels flow are unintuitive and will have you turning a corner to find another door that you aren't ready for because you haven't fully explored and understood the space you would be leaving. It plays closer to Banjo Tooie in that way.Overall I can't be too harsh, the game was made by one person and by that standard it is impressive. There is great character mechanic design and aesthetics. The level layouts is where the game loses me and makes me wish there were a more dedicated level designer on board. I hope to see the developer succeed and maybe follow this up with a sequel that explores more depth in the character's design and movement while tightening up the level layouts and flow. I think there is a great game waiting. However, between the hard to parse levels and off putting world themes, this Cavern of Dreams too frequently became a Cavern of Nightmares.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: only played ten minutes. The reason for that, though, is because it's *really* uncomfortable to control, and has some blatant choices that disrupt a player's ability to gauge the environment. IE - you can't look up or down. That's fine when you're in an open area with no real threats, but when there's a pit of death in a little dungeon? You kinda need to be able to look down. Not to mention the fact that there's a Sonic the Hedgehog roll that goes *way* too fast for how compact the level design seems to be. The controls beyond that are super floaty and a bit slidey, with jumps that are too short. The most confuddling aspect, though, is the key binding. The "talk" button is X, and you can't proceed dialogue with "A" even once you've started it, you keep having to hit X. In addition, the *attack* button is "B," which I don't think I've ever seen in a video game. "B" is a defensive button, hence why it's usually associated with dodging. It moves away from the direction the thumb is pointing and in toward the hand which, therefore, feels more like a retreat. "B" would've been a better dialogue selector/item interaction button. It seems like a small thing, but it forces you to rewire your muscle memory from decades of platforming experience, and a game shouldn't try to change up things like this if it wants to also be nostalgic. There's no way to rebind the keys at time of writing, either.The graphics are good, though. Presentation, not so much. The camera definitely clipped through several items in cutscenes, and the text boxes are *really* hard to look at and can clutter the screen. The voice acting (what little there is of it because, hey, it's a retro 3D platformer, it ain't that important) stands out as just a bit amateurish for some reason that I can't pinpoint. Audio quality, maybe?3D models and environmental design - 9/10, very nice. 6/10 for the main character, because it looks like a mix between a Chao and that guy from Night into Dreams, and that's not incredibly compelling. Lotta Sonic connections, here. Game feel - 4/10, not great. Not my cup of tea, but I'm just not willing to give up vertical aim, sensible button placement, and high jumps in a 3D platformer. Those are *pretty* big barriers of entry to me. The fact that it just doesn't seem to have much if any polish makes it a really hard sell, as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little Nintendo 64-esque 3D puzzle platformer and collectathon.You take control of Fynn the dragon, who enters the cavern of dreams in search of his unhatched siblings. Shortly after entering the cavern you'll meet Sage, who offers Fynn help by granting new abilities once a sufficient number of eggs has been collected, unlocking more areas to explore and making reaching certain eggs easier.The gameplay revolves around exploring the various, colorful areas and worlds within the cavern of dreams, trying to find all eggs and other collectibles spread throughout. The game gives you a handy checklist and also notifies you once a world has been completed. A lot of the eggs require you to observe your surroundings and pick up on little hints to solve puzzles. As you rescue your siblings, Sage will offer you more and more abilities to help you navigate those worlds while also giving you access to previously inaccessible areas. While progressing through each world you will learn more about the inhabitants of the cavern of dreams as well as some of their backstory, giving you some lore to piece together if you are into that kind of thing. However, the game is very short, taking about 5 hours, give or take, to 100%. But the game does offer some more optional post-game content, making you revisit those worlds and reaching previously unreachable areas for more tidbits of lore and other fun and interesting content.The controls are very responsive and Fynn's moveset is fun to use and very satisfying once mastered. I will say that I do like the control scheme used in the Nintendo Switch version of this game better. As such I have created a community layout that reflects the control scheme of the Nintendo Switch version. However, since the game does not use the Steam Input API the controller glyphs in game won't match up with your customized layout. Other than that this game does support high refresh rates as well as non-16:9 aspect ratios such as 21:9 or the 16:10 aspect ratio used by the Steam Deck. However, while I appreciate those QoL features I wish the game had some options to limit framerate to 30 or 60 fps, aspect ratio to 4:3, render resolution to 240p, as well as draw distance. While you can do most of those within your GPU drivers it would be neat if the game had options for those things to get a more old school N64-like experience for less tech savvy people. The game runs well on the Deck does show proper controller glyphs as long as you don't remap your controls.tl;dr: while short it is a well crafted game with a lot of care put into it. The worlds are colorful with quirky inhabitants and lots of little secrets to find, accompanied by a dynamic soundtrack that changes depending on the area you are in. The controls are responsive and the abilities fun to use and master. If you enjoyed those older Nintendo 64 collectathons this game took inspiration from and don't mind a shorter experience then this game is for you and worth the 13 euro asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly cute 3D Collectathon Platformer with inspiration from all over the place. The game can be played with keyboard and mouse, which is how I started out, but it feels so much better with a controller. The controls feel good, though I did have a bit of a problem on controlling Fynn after he would dive since you start to run after you hit the ground. This is fine, but there were times that platforms were a bit small and I would end up nearly or totally running off a platform when I didn't mean to. It also took a bit to get the second higher jump timing down, it kind of feels like it needs a slightly bigger time window to pull it off easier. The puzzles in the Snow World were also incredibly harder than the rest of the game,. I especially had trouble with the statue puzzle (I think it has to do with orientation?) and the star room puzzle. I needed a guide to figure out those. And the final fight with the main villain was much harder than it needed to be because the way the camera is panned out, it's hard to tell depth. _childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Donkey Kong 64 and Super Mario 64 as a kid, I really appreciate the retro style along with the open-zone Collectathon gameplay. I only ever got to play Banjo-Kazooie later on when I downloaded an emulator, but I see the DNA of those games in this title as well.Inspirations aside, this game stands on its own with a distinct style and smooth gameplay. I love the movement options that you start out with and unlock through the course of the game. Sage does a good job of teaching the player how to use basic controls and maneuvers, but you can also learn a bit of advanced "Schmoovement" on your own with a bit of experimentation and expert timing. The platforming aspects give enough room for both beginners and veterans to complete the game at their own pace. The puzzles are great too, but the only one I really got stuck on was the one in Prismatic Palace. Each of the four worlds exterior to the Cavern of Dreams have a distinct theme to them, and each have a friendly resident that you help along the way. You'll collect eggs, mushrooms, and Encyclopedia pages through each world and even the main hub with little sub-sections here and there. Each world also has a more challenging egg to grab that you'll probably save for last before exiting the world. In some of the later sections, you'll even open up shortcuts to the other worlds to solve puzzles and even find secrets. Overall, this game has amazingly good design to it, and I am glad I got to play it all the way through.P.S. Even when you've collected everything, there's still more optional secrets to find using a certain endgame upgrade. If you pay enough attention to the Encyclopedia and your environment, you can also catch some backstory to this world. I had fun piecing together what happened before Fynn arrives in the Caverns, and I hope you do too.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: A charming 3D platformer with phenomenal atmosphere. There's a ton of stuff to do in each level, and finding the eggs or encyclopedia entries is often satisfying. Combing each world is a ton of fun thanks to Fynn's movement, as you're able to achieve a ton of speed and mobility with enough practice. Each world is quite whimsical, but they can dive into unnerving territory at the drop of a hat.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty short runtime for full price and I wish there was just a bit more to round it out like an extra level or two, but a really chill and fun little experience regardless! Rolling around is fun, all the little animations and use of squash and stretch is adorable, and it really does give off that "dreamy" vibe that a bunch of early platformers gave off. Each zone has its own vibe and challenge, and the puzzles are intuitive without being too in your face obvious.There's a nice amount of secrets to find in the postgame once you've gotten all the eggs and abilities, which adds a nice little bit of extra value and playtime just experimenting and seeing what you can find. It even comes with some simple but interesting background "lore" that doesn't get too esoteric or weird with it. The story is very simple and straightforward, but it didn't NEED to be anything more than that.I just wish the rolling mechanic was used in the gameplay more - there's only like one or two times the levels actually make use of it, which is a shame since it feels like so much work was put into it. This feels like one of those games that could lead to an incredible sequel or successor - I hope Bynine doesn't stop making games after this!

_childDocuments_.review: It is HONESTLY a breath of fresh air to play a cutesy game WITHOUT it turning into an analog horror game. The difficulty was pretty beginner-friendly for a 3D platformer. I do think there were some difficulties with grabbing onto hanging items like chains or vines. Jumping off sometimes would just drop you straight down, or you would fly right through the thing to grab. There were also some areas that could be cheesed a little bit. I remember breaking the game a little early by taking a pair of Jester boots (REALLY cool mechanic, by the way, I've never seen a puzzle mechanic like that before, personally) outside of their designated area. _childDocuments_.review: I heavily enjoyed Cavern of Dreams.First off, I have always personally enjoyed games that feature a rich world. Cavern of Dreams presents a blend of themes: Wonder, etherealism, magic, coziness, mystery, sorrow, spookiness, and charm. And, it mixes these themes in a delightfully tasteful way through all aspects of its presentation, with no part going too far to disturb the mixture. The characters, the world design, the music, the lighting, the level design, the story, the set dressing, the secrets, the mechanics of movement and the collect-a-thon gameplay all come together to create this mixture. I read that the dev had wanted to create the feeling that the game world always felt like there were more secrets to it and I think they really nailed it.Gameplay:Cavern of Dreams is a 3D platforming collect-a-thon where you're tasked with finding your fellow dragon siblings (in unhatched egg form) and mushrooms to feed them with after some hatch. There's also encyclopedia entries to be found too, and each card you find gives a little information on the world you're exploring.The character movement controls work fairly well with some caveats. Let's get them out of the way. One issue is that you use a ground pound to get to higher areas, but the ground pound involves an attack move that hits things in front of you as well. This means that if you're too close to a wall you're trying to scale, you may accidentally hit the wall and bounce away instead.Secondly, I feel the game could use more 'coyote time'. Fortunately this was a minor issue, as most jumps have a lot of leeway, but this came up once or twice.Thirdly, this is less of a critique and more of a desire, but the game includes a fun rolling mechanic that's great for getting around. I only wish that the level designs emphasized its use more though. It would have been nice to have more locations featuring large slopes and paths that are focused on rolling.Other than that though, I really enjoyed the movement mechanics quite a lot, and these critiques mostly apply to the beginning parts of the game. Later abilities you unlock for your character create a lot of platforming possibilities that are fun to execute.Music:The overall amount of music is a little short, but they fit the locations they're in very well and they're well done. The tunes loop a lot but you'll never notice this unless you think about it - they're composed in a way where they're not repetitive.Characters:There aren't many characters you speak to, but the ones that are there don't overextend their stay and the dialog they have is charming. They also have fun and interesting designs.Story:The story is a simple but charming plot with a thread of mystery to uncover as you go along. When the main story beats began to unfold I was ready to be disappointed with how it would handle certain characters, but I was very happy with how it was wrapped up. I felt like the characters stuck to actions and character development I rooted for, and in the end it presented a nice moral message you don't often see.In addition to the main plot, there's background lore that forms its own narrative if you can do enough exploring to figure out what's up.Sound:I do wish the sound mixing was handled a little differently, but this wasn't a large gripe. Some sound effects seemed to play much more loudly than others, and I found the game sounded "nicer" when I turned down the main sound effects and turned up the game music. Before I felt the music was too quiet.Visuals:It has an "N64" art style that's executed in a very tasteful way. It's easy for devs to use a visual style like this to disguise a lack of skill in craftsmanship, but it's clear the developers really know what they're doing. Because, they know how to create an image that evokes just the right feelings to create the mixture of themes mentioned at the start of this review. There's no lack of craftsmanship here.Also, I recommend leaving the "blur" filter on. Unlike retro filters in other games, this filter is done in a tasteful way that enhances the look of the game rather than hiding it.-------In summary, Cavern of Dreams sets out to be a charming and mysterious 3D adventure game, and I think it perfectly achieves that goal. I hope its audience continues to grow.

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is a great vibes-based platformer. Early 3d games had to work within their graphical limitations to try and create areas that felt real, but were often a bit uncanny as a result of low-res textures and low poly counts. CoD masterfully recreates this aesthetic with great sound design & music to craft some beautiful and mysterious levels and secrets within them. Many times in this game I felt I was stumbling upon something I shouldn't have or that didn't quite feel real, like I was recalling vague memories of areas from other games I played ages ago, trying to stitch them together into something coherent. Paired with a fun albeit limited momentum focused movement system and a quickly expanding moveset, CoD is a rewarding game in its own right with a retro charm that pulls the whole experience together.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a nostalgic delight. The aesthetics and atmosphere are on point, feels like a lost N64 game, although some of the environments are way moodier and darker than you'd expect, and it's awesome to discover! It's got all the charm and collectathon goodness of Banjo-Kazooie, just compressed into a smaller package.There are 5 open levels that you can explore freely, and it feels great discovering things at your own pace and soaking in the vibes, finding lore, solving puzzles, and doing easy platforming. It's almost cozy, EXCEPT for the final level! The 5th level is frustrating and cruel -- there is no combat, but enemies and hazards can still push you around and knock you into bottomless pits, and some traps teleport you to different parts of the level, sucking up a bunch of your time. It's not overly hard, just frustrating, like the game is poking fun at you, which lines up with the antagonist this level is based around, but it feels out of place compared to the rest of the game. That said, the other 4 levels are wonderful and totally worth playing!My favourite time spent with this game was in the first half. There were 3 levels available to me, and I could explore self-directed wherever I want, and I felt like I could really do what I wanted, and there was no pressure. The places and things I discovered, especially throughout the entire 3rd level, were genuinely unexpected, and I had a blast hunting for eggs -- the main collectable. The problem is, the last 2 levels only unlock once you find EVERY egg you possibly can in the first 3! And I missed a couple, so I had to go back through every single level and scour them for the few I missed. There is a hint system to help with this search, but I still had trouble finding one that involved breaking through a subtly-suspicious wall. It would be nice if more of the eggs were optional, at least for the sake of unlocking all the levels.My only other gripe is that the controls can be awkward (I played on an Xbox controller). There are several moves mapped to the B button, when the left triggers are left unused. Felt like an oversight, as I regularly smacked myself away from walls when I was trying to do a ground-pound-bounce. Also, the encyclopedia menu doesn't work with a controller, but you can operate it with the keyboard arrow keys.It may sound like I'm coming down on this game, but I had a great time with it overall! I just want to give the dev feedback on where they can improve for next time, because I'm definitely waiting for whatever comes next :) I gladly recommend this game to anyone who likes (mostly) chill, atmospheric platformers!

_childDocuments_.review: I would best describe this game as feeling like a mix of the first two Rayman games and Banjo Kazooie, I think.  It's got that colourful and quaint cosy ambience with some unsettling enemies and creepy places sprinkled through it.  If you grew up enjoying collectathon platformers I think this'd be up your alley, there's only 2 collectible types in the game but it's a good time.  It also feels great picking up momentum and zooming around levels.There's no health or numbered lives to worry about, your patience and approach is the only thing stopping you from getting any collectible you see.  If you get hit you'll be sent flying and usually lose your footing, while falling off of ledges into pits or lava pops you back at the last entrance you walked through.  There's no boss fights but there are upgrades and secrets you can find in post-game.Unrelated author's note: I've never played a game where the falling-to-your-death noise the character makes is so adorable. _childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is a cutesy 3D platformer with a Nintendo 64 era aesthetic that really nails that sort of unique atmosphere, while also having its own discernible identity. If you liked Banjo-Kazooie, Spyro, and games of that sort, you will enjoy this one.Story's kind of simple and I barely paid attention to it, essentially you're this cute little dragon fella and you're saving all your siblings (as eggs, the main collectable) from an evil bat. As you get more eggs, you gain new abilities, things like gliding, a ground pound, and etc, which help you progress through the world and discover new areas. It's a pretty fun game to explore, and I liked discovering new things using the new found abilities.The controls are a bit of a source of controversy for a lot of people. Fynn (the player character) is largely a momentum based character. His base jump height is laughable, and he walks fairly slowly too. The main way you gain speed is by rolling around, like Sonic. Except it takes Fynn quite a while to build up that speed. And if it's uphill, you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Personally though, the controls grew on me. At the start it's kind of a slog, but as you play the game more, you get more used to how it feels and it starts to feel a lot better. It's really rewarding rolling around a lot, then jumping over a gigantic area. It's a very unique control scheme and I like it a lot.Difficulty-wise... I mean come on, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ look at it. You're a fool if you're expecting a challenge from this. Granted there are a select few puzzles that can take a bit to figure out, as well as some platforming sections that are decently tight, but for the most part the challenges are a cakewalk. Spoilers for the final boss: Overall, like I said, if you're a fan of this sort of thing, you'll like it! Pick it up whenever you can, definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fantastic exploration based 3D platformer with movement that starts out fun and interesting and becomes even more so as you collect new abilities. _childDocuments_.review: I can point to exactly three things I don't like about the game:- Two puzzles were confusing to me and I had to look at a walkthrough.- One of the collectible cards is listed as in the Cavern (overworld), when it's actually in the Prismic Palace level, and I had to check a walkthrough to figure it out.Otherwise, I really like it. _childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams understands the aesthetic of retro 3D platformers better than most throwback attempts. The slow platforming can have uncharacteristic moments of speed, blurry textures get stretched across massive triangles, and the large levels often have collectables / puzzle hints stashed in weird nooks. However, because of those surface-level imperfections this game is able to do something that none of its contemporaries can emulate: It feels like a dream. Exploring this game's various worlds gave me a sense of unease, due in large part to how often the low-fidelity art style is used for both charming characters and foreboding vignettes. The narrative presentation compliments that unease, with most of the individual stories beings suggested but never completely unraveled. All that stuff will definitely scare off players who cannot tolerate early 3D platformer trappings, but the end result is uniquely captivating.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and only wish there was more!  It has a very dreamy vibe to it, which initially comes off as basic and childish but by the end of the game feels almost haunting and unsettling.  It's a game that gets more interesting and involving the further you get into the game, which I always appreciate!There are four worlds to explore, with a hub world and a few secret areas tucked away for good measure.  The first world is pretty basic but the others are elaborate and rewarding for fans of the genre.  Fynn has a very satisfying moveset to use that is almost a little too good for the game--you're going to find yourself wishing there were more opportunities to put the moveset into action!There's a very interesting mythos in the background that the developers smartly explore very little.  Forgotten races, mysterious statues, and weapons of war hint at a very dark past that the world has moved on from, but which remain afloat in the time capsule-esque Cavern of Dreams.  The game gives you little hints of lore through collector cards and excellent environmental storytelling and it is just enough to make you wonder and hunger for more without bogging you down with lore dumps.It is clear that the game takes heavy inspiration from Spyro the Dragon and Banjo-Kazooie in its level design and movement.  However, tonally it is very different from those games.  Cavern of Dreams surprisingly took me back to Glover, which I'm not sure was a coincidence--one of the main characters is very reminiscent of the wizard from Glover.  Like Glover, it seems there is much bigger things at play in the world, but you are a simple resident just trying to get by and get your work done.One weak spot for the game is its soundtrack.  In a bubble, it is pretty good.  There's a few tracks that are memorable, enhance the mood of the area, and stick with you after playing the game.  It does what it needs to do.  However, this is a genre full of bops and Cavern of Dreams has a theme and atmosphere that lends itself to really dark and captivating music (think of End of the World from Kingdom Hearts 1, Castle Oblivion from Chain of Memories, or The World that Never Was from Kingdom Hearts 2).  So in that regard, it is a disappointment.  I like the soundtrack of Cavern of Dreams but it isn't winning any awards.I can't wait to see what these devs make next!  Cavern of Dreams for me may be the standard that I judge future 3D platformers against.  It's not the best of its genre but it is very solid and it really makes me appreciate how far indie developers and gaming in general have come.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is a pretty standard Nintendo64 style 3D platformer. You play a little dragon that try to save his siblings (which are eggs). The movement feels very nice and you unlock different abilities throughout the game by rescuing more and more siblings.The game basically tries to emulate a classic N64 platformer and it does it pretty well, the different aeras are very colorfull and fun and the character design is overall very good (especially Sage i love their design). Cavern of Dreams is a really small but very good 3D platformer. If you like exploring and searching through levels for little collectables you'de probably like it.

The rest of the game wasn't like this so it was a bit jarring.Highly recommend despite this if you want a cosy relaxing game to chill out and play!

_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I was drawn to this game by the fact that it is a N64 style platformer which was some of the first games I played when I was a child. This game was played entirely on my Steam Deck, so my points will be based on that. The game is playable on Steam Deck 100% and from what I could tell there was no real issue with it. The one thing I did struggle with was the double jump ability. But it was difficult to tell if it was either just timing or a delay with the Steam Deck. But other than my own potential skill issue there, the game ran smoothly on the Deck and was enjoyable to play. I don't think I'd have enjoyed it as much if I had to play on my Laptop. The game is short and sweet. There's 4 main areas to explore with one big hub area along with a few smaller miniature areas to explore. Everything is close together so you aren't running about for long to get to each area. You'll find yourself jumping between worlds with each upgrade you get so that you can collect things you previously couldn't collect. It does help that in game you do unlock shortcuts to worlds which makes jumping between everything very easy.Some items are a little difficult to locate, but with a bit of looking you do end up finding everything. The story is very simple. You're a young dragon called Fynn who is looking to find his siblings. There isn't much more to the story than that. The characters that you meet all have unique designs to make them stand out. However most of them aren't very memorable either with how quick you can finish a world and with the minimal amount of contact you have with them. I couldn't tell you most of the names because of that.In game, I only struggled with one thing and that was technically the only boss area in game which is a long stretch with various hazards in the way. This was for some reason, almost a deal breaker for me with quitting the game due to how easy it was to misplace a jump and hit a hazard or with how your default movement is a slow walk and getting hit by the attacks. It didn't make this part of the game enjoyable for me in the slightest. It was the most rage inducing part of the game which made the ending very anti-climatic to me as I was just that annoyed over the boss of the game.One fault I noticed was the achievements. I had to completely shut the game down and reopen it to obtain them when they should have been an automatic thing. I noticed a few others have had this issue, so I do hope that it will be fixed in the near future.This is a game that I do recommend if you're looking for something quick to pass the time. It's easy to complete in one sitting and doesn't requite much time to complete nor does it have much story or lore in game that you have to remember if you're just looking for a simple game to play. It took me just over 5 hours to complete the game and then another couple to go around and finish looking for everything that I hadn't collected. However, If you're not interested in platformers, short games or games without much story or lore? Then this wouldn't be a good choice for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game! I love the art style, character design, environments, gameplay, and story! It really captures the cozy feeling of playing a 3D platformer as a kid! The length of the game is perfect and 100% isnt insanely difficult either which I appreciate.Honestly a great game which I plan on replaying :]
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a charming nostalgia trip and it's fun to get immersed in the world. The graphics and music are great, and the controls work as well as they would if you dusted off your N64 and tried playing from the older catalog...which is to say, less responsive than a modern game and sometimes a little janky. But it's such a weird, delightful gem of a game that is substantial and fun enough to stand on its own merits.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: There's a handy helping of throwback platformers out there but this one might be my favorite, perfectly captures the N64 era Rareware visuals while having a unique, dreamlike quality all its own and playing in a fairly distinct fashion. It's short in a pleasant way that doesn't outstay its welcome, with a relatively low level of difficulty to match. A good, chill time.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to be able to suggest that you buy and play this, but I just can't.  Unless you just absolutely MUST have one more platformer with N64-clone graphics, this game is just mediocre at best.The character and level design definitely evokes the nostalgia that they were going for, but it absolutely does not live up to the same charm of something like Banjo-Kazooie or SM64.  Characters are bland with almost no personality to speak of.  Level design is about a 6/10 at best.  There are some high points for sure, but some objectives are just too obscure to reasonably discover on your own while others are just painfully obvious to the point of not being fun.The controls are....fine...at best?  They work ok, but the abilities you learn are incredibly cliche' for the genre and worse, most of them are generally useless except maybe to solve a single puzzle.  There's no real combat to speak of even though you have moves that imply the ability to attack.  There's no health bar, no death.  Falling off a cliff just loads you back in at the latest entrance that you crossed through.  It means that there are no real "stakes", you just bash your head against the wall to figure stuff out.I think I'm about halfway through and I just can't bring myself to finish it right now.  The thought of going back to the world that I was exploring is boring as heck.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing "nostalgia collectathon platformer". So many references, hints and nods at old nostangic titles of the past. But new and well done.It has its flaws, no game is perfect. But this ones up there and well worth a play for someone looking to get a little taste of the good old days but new. Often caused an ear to ear grin and I enjoyed every minute.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the closest experience to Banjo Kazooie that I have seen. For what it's worth I played Super Kiwi 64 and found that one very disappointing. Not the case here.Graphically, it is incredibly true to the N64 collectathons, and Banjo Kazooie most of all. It is really impressive how well they recaptured that look.Gameplay - movement feels great, a handful of upgrades that make your character stronger and able to access more areas.The areas where it is lacking compared to the N64 area - music and humor. The music in this one feels pretty subtle. The game has charm, but not that cheeky humor that Rare were known for, and I kinda miss that.OVERALL - the game is a delight. Highly recommend to anyone, and I think it can stand on its own as a fun experience without needing the warm nostalgic feel for the collectathons of yore.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I found out about this game through youtuber Nitrorad's video on indie platformers. Me and my boyfriend were charmed by the visuals and good ol' Fynn that we had to check it out! And now, I'm sitting here, having just 100%'s the game (Though the achievement for getting all the cards doesn't work) that was just... SO CUTE and cozy that it actually made me and my partner tear up. No other game has done that to me before aside from Undertale. If that's not a sell for you, then how about this!The controls have a nice, weighty feel to it that makes it feel like your fault any time you fail to reach platforms and the like, with its focus on maintainable momentum making for moments where you zoom through areas, feeling incredible, a feeling that increases with each move you get. The levels you get to use the moveset in are not only are perfect for said moves with some really clever environmental puzzles, but are so distinct and memorable with how strong their vibes are, instantly creating feelings of massive unease or unshakeable comfort, the music being the cheery cherry on top of it- That and how each level interconnects so nicely!Another amazing aspect of this game is the surprising amount of lore you can find through the cards. Now, don't get me wrong, it's not a huge focus but what we do have is certainly intriguing, with this world only being a corner of larger picture. Idk if Bynine will return to Fynn's adventures anytime in the future but if they do, I'm CERTAINLY going to be there for it. If I had any problems with this game, the game is so substantially cute that I forgot them all. Only one persisting is that there aren't plushies of the characters I can buy.So with all of that in mind, please, PLEASE, give this game a shot! If you're one for the cute and whimsical, well you're about to get the sweetest, most courageous adventure the indie platforming genre has to offer you!(Also, if that wasn't enough, Tasch Ritter worked on this game! Shout outs to The Grifters!... I know probably nobody reading through these reviews would get the reference but sometimes, you just gotta make them for yourself to enjoy. If you're reading this Tasch, amazing work! If you worked on the Gallery, you legit scared me and honestly, I wouldn't have wanted it any other way lmao)
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid little game, here!  I would say getting it on sale, as I did, is a good value.  Cavern of Dreams is fairly short, though it did take me about 9 hours or so to play through 100%, perhaps slower than average for total completion.  If you were to just go through it quickly without a desire to 100% the game or find any secrets, I reckon a couple hours would be plenty.Cavern of Dreams faithfully recreates the feel of N64 era collectathon games, with charming and cute characters.  There's a lot of little hidden easter eggs to find, with a nice sprinkling of spooky atmosphere.  I found the gameplay easy, but not to the point of being boring.  The difficulty curve through the game is good, with each upgrade to Fynn increasing the complexity of your platforming tasks.  My biggest gripe with the game is the peculiar choice to make the highest jump require holding a button down, which makes it kind of clunky - it also requires you to do a tail swing attack which will often send you bouncing off a wall when you did not intend to, losing you progress.  Fortunately, there's not really any major drawbacks to taking damage or 'dying', the worst cases just sending you back to the beginning of an area.  Most areas are not terribly expansive though, so getting back to where you were isn't that time consuming.Sometimes the momentum of Fynn's movement can feel somewhat inconsistent where it can be kind of hard to get the right speed to launch as far as you need to for certain collectibles, or doing what you assumed was the same thing will yield different results due to the inconsistent physics.  It's not so bad that it makes the game unplayable, but it did lend itself to a few frustrating moments where I died because I bounced strangely for seemingly no reason.  Some of the puzzles are also a little obtuse, though I appreciate that many puzzles do require some real thought.  Very minor gripes for an overall extremely enjoyable and nostalgic-feeling experience.  The soundtrack was good, though fairly relaxed in tone, especially compared to its classic contemporaries. Overall, I really enjoyed this game and would very much like a sequel.  It gave me all the warm fuzzy feelings of replaying my favorite N64 titles from my childhood, and I think it is a true love letter to the genre.  Anyone who enjoyed those types of games will undoubtedly enjoy this title, too!  Props to the developers for their hard work making a game that feels very genuine!
