_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is an excellent, adorable little game. While it has a little bit of cruft that comes from something designed by a small team, the game more than makes up for its flaws through its incredible world design, surprisingly deep lore, and fun movement.The game is a “traditional” N64-style collectathon, designed intentionally to be a (mostly) non-violent, purely exploration-based game. As the dragon Fynn, you collect the eggs of your dragon siblings and even hatch a few, and saving more siblings unlocks new abilities which get reflected on your character model directly. Each level features some character in distress you can help and befriend, and many of the levels force you to really pay attention to the interconnectivity of the environment in ways that you wouldn’t normally think of.The game is relatively short, and you can 100% beat everything in a weekend, although the game does distinguish its normal ending from the one where you’ve found all your siblings. In fact, finishing the game in this way unlocks even more fun places to explore, although nothing new to collect.At first, I’ll be honest that I was a bit put off by the movement. Part of these are genuine criticisms, like the lack of coyote timing and input buffering, but mainly, I think that one of the first platforming challenges of the game accidentally amplified all of these issues. When you enter the first level, Lostleaf Lake, you have the option of climbing up a tree to save one of your siblings and get a card for the encyclopedia. Here, we have a tight space with narrow, winding platforms; a constantly rotating camera; and weird geometry that causes Fynn to occasionally hop up over small “ledges” during which you’re not able to jump any further. These kinds of situations aren’t really good for showing off the game’s movement, which does better in much larger areas, although the theming of the first area really does benefit from having the tree.The game’s movement is incredibly simple, mostly relying on rolling to build up momentum and then using this to your advantage one way or another. Due to some quirks of how the game’s physics engine works, you can exploit this momentum to make ridiculously high jumps and far leaps, and the game has a lot of potential for sequence-breaking, even when there aren’t many sequences to break. If this game had a native Linux version, I’d love to make a TAS, but at least for now, I’ll have to deal with just my own playthrough.One of my biggest criticisms of the game are the lack of control rebinding and the hint system not being very good, but again, I think that the game makes up for its flaws more than enough. The hint system sorts all the siblings’ eggs into nests of four and lets you ask any nests with two or three eggs where the other eggs are. It doesn’t tell you anything about the cards or mushrooms (admittedly, the latter not even having any dedicated achievements), and I often found myself with a bunch of single-egg nests and no further help.I actually got frustrated and looked up multiple egg locations before I found the numerous hints that would have helped. The game does a great job leaving clues everywhere and there’s really nothing that’s overly obscure, but again, I got frustrated. I’ll elaborate a bit more in the spoilery section at the end, but sufficed to say, have a bit more patience than me.Thank you for making this game.----SPOILERY ADDENDUM BELOW----By far, the thing I struggled with the most was all the puzzles in the Gallery of Nightmares, which required carrying objects from different areas to other places. Once I had done the puzzle where you bring an apple to The Gobbler and then later realised that one of the items was Lady Opal’s head, it all clicked for me.It turns out that a lot of these puzzles have multiple solutions to help you out. For example, I thought that the burning egg required the water upgrade, but you can also throw a health potion on the egg to get it earlier. To cure Sniffles’ illness, you could give them a health potion, or you could just blow some water at them. One thing that the game doesn’t reveal that I wished it did was that you can blow water in the first-person camera, although ultimately, the game doesn’t require it.My favourite part by far, and what honestly elevates this from a good game to a masterpiece, is the post-game content. I love the fact that the game gives you boundary breaking as an end-game reward. And on top of this, it adds in all sorts of lovely timing challenges in areas where you can just fly outside the map. My only disappointment was the fact that the secret in the Airborne Armada is accessible just with Mr. Kerrington’s wings, and by trying to climb the lonely Pom in the middle, I had to get the wings again for the puzzle. I loved exploring this area after I learned to fly.The game even has some particularly dark secrets if you explore Luna’s room in the Gallery of Nightmares, alongside some silly secrets there too.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: A little rough around the edges but this is a respectable little colectathon. Mechanics are introduced a good pace and the majority of the level design is cute and functionally good. Fynn the little dragon you get to control I'd say is quite unique feeling. There are multiple ways to gain momentum allowing you to move surprisingly fast, but when you are simply walking around things are nice and slow. Fynn has really short legs so obviously walking up hills is an issue for him. He crawls up even the smallest of slope, if you ever played Sonic 1-3 you'll know the feeling. This game also does not have any real fail states. You have no health bar and falling into pits resets you to the last load zone you entered. You'll lose at most a minute of progress as many of the areas are small. The final area of the game is a bit of a misstep. I'd say about half of what the final zone has to offer is more annoying than fun, but it's not anything that will make you want to quit the game. It's like a slightly worn feather pillow. Most of the time its simple and cozy, but every now and then you get poked in the face by something. This is a nice 7/10 game. Nothing crazy but I think it succeeds at everything it was trying to accomplish, take any overly excited 10/10 reviews with a grain of salt. Oh, also, yes your jump sucks at first, don't worry it teaches you how to jump higher among other things. Spend a little time with the game. It's a fun little romp, and quite kid friendly to boot.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun! It feels like an N64 game, but with all the extra empty space removed. Each world is a collection of rooms that feel like little super compact dioramas. You won't wast time traversing across any space like Hyrule Field, though there are a few places where rolling can really pick up some speed! Vertical movement is very limited, which makes it feel more like Zelda or Spyro, and using a controller is a MUST for best feel. Puzzles are very common, mostly one way doors that open shortcuts and simple riddles, but many are proper teasers and test your memory or observation skills about what you've seen in the world. My biggest critique is that some of the sound balancing seems off. Some sound effects startled me with their volume.This quickly became one of my favorites in my library. If you're looking for a bite-sized throwback that's more than just a nibble (looking at you, Super Kiwi 64), then this is a must-play!!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: played almost 2 hours straight, haven't enjoyed a good platformer for a long time. this one feels like an n64/psx classic. The story is minimal and just throws you in without wasting any time, a huge plus imo. There's plenty of hints if you look around the levels, the puzzles are fun and so is figuring out where to go next. Very little to complain about 2 hours in, I will say that controlling the roll and jumps can take some getting used to. You may find yourself repeating challenges even tho you know what to do. Lastly I'll add that it works perfectly on steamdeck!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game with a lot of heart, had a great time all the way through and was surprised at all the little secrets the developer sneaked in. This really is a labor of love from the developer.It's worth every one of the thirteen dollars you'll pay for it, so GET IT ALREADY... and have a good time :^)
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend the game while by all mean it not a big game but I enjoy it so much as well as the character you play as. I did crave for more and I really hope Fynn do get more games as I can see more adventurer await for him. If you love collecting things and platforming and such then this is a game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute, fun, albeit short game to pick up and play. The gameplay is quite simple, but it really doesn't need to be complex to be fun. Rolling is a great ability I found myself using to get around, but not abusing it as it could cause me to launch myself off if I wasn't careful in some spots. It definitely gets the N64 style down very well.The final boss, from what I've heard, is hard, but only if you don't get the extra powerup from getting all the eggs. It would be nice if it was possible to completely miss powerups, but that's a nitpick, I'd say.Again, the only true negative is, it's quite short. I might've been able to complete the game in half the playtime I have, but I enjoyed messing around in some of the worlds a little (and I may have spent too long on some parts that, in hindsight, were obvious). But this doesn't take away from the experience, and it's a solid price for the length.The only thing I really needed to post to recommend this is you can make Fynn sleep, and that's enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: i adore this game so much! i love the world, the characters, the gameplay, the graphics, the music, the story, the details, and everything else about it! i had so much fun playing!! it really felt like i was playing a game from the n64 era! i wish there were more games like this made today. highly recommend if you love old school platformers!!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game it reminded me a lot of Spyro which is still one of my favorite Series and i can say that this game definitely felt a lot like Spyro. One big thing about this game is that its very simplistic. From the N64 style graphics to a simple level and sound design and i really liked that. It wasn't bloated with a lot of things and its fairly straight forward. The puzzles do sometimes require some thinking but its not incredible frustrating. The characters and their interactions are really cute fun to watch. I now have 100% in the game and it took me almost 8 hours, so the length isn't too long so that it gets tiring or annoying but its also not too short.If you are a fan of Spyro like games or just want to have a chill gaming experience after a stressful day of work, then i would definitely recommend trying this game
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun and replayable game.This takes me back to the good old days of Banjo Kazooie and Super Mario 64, games that helped deepen my love for puzzle-solving, platforming collectathons.  The unlockable powerups make exploring so much fun, and the visuals are amazing, whether they be stunningly beautiful or harrowingly creepy and depressing.  Plus, there's the fact that there's some major undertones that make the characters deeper than they appear, and hidden lore behind this fantastical world.Plus, the fact that there's no real combat in this game makes it so that you don't feel the pressure of worrying about horrible nightmare creatures to fight.  In fact, besides some major end-game things that I won't spoil, there's almost literally no high-stakes pressure.  You can really take your time, exploring every nook and cranny.  Plus, there's so many secrets and easter-eggs to find once you've saved all of your adorable siblings.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: this game is absolutely adorable, and is the best purchase of a game i've made this year. filled to the brim with nostalgia, really feels like you've been taken in a time machine back to when games were much simpler in the N64 era. the charm and everything is all there, whilst also delivering a full-on refreshing experience.definitely my personal game of the year as well, there's no beating this cute little red dragon boi from saving his siblings. this game combines everything i love from a platformer, and the soundtrack sounds incredible too. highly recommend this game to anyone who is looking into it, you won't be disappointed if you're a platformer enthusiast like myself.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Some call this game "A Banjo Kazooie spiritual successor".It's more like "A third party N64 game from back in the day that tries to capitalize on the success of Banjo Kazooie and does so successfully but doesn't quite reach the quality level of that game".Let's just say, if someone had it running on a CRT with an N64 controller hooked up, I would have 100% believed it was an actual N64 game from that period.It looks and feels just like one.It's been said that nostalgia is a powerful drug and for me this game is like getting a generic prescription of nostalgia.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Of all the throwback N64 platformers out there, this sure was one of them.It has heart, and it succeeds in capturing the feel of games from that era. Unfortunately, the feel of games from that era is Bad, and it also succeeds in capturing everything that frustrated me about them. Never wished more for a 'mixed' option on here instead of just a yes or no.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks, sounds and plays great. Platforming is a lot more forgiving than some of the old games this game was inspired by, which results in a game a bit on the shorter side. There's also a small amount of jank that allows you to complete sections in an unintended way.That said, those are minor complaints, this game is absolutely perfect for a lazy weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This game embodies exactly what this genre(collectathon platformers) should be. Its got fun and unique level design, engaging and rewarding exploration, and satisfying movement and progression. Its only downside is the short length of the game(took me about 15-20 hours for 100%) but what is there is of the highest quality. For clarification: Steam says I only have 0.9 hours on this game but I have well over 20, not sure whats going on there. 10/10 definitely would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely game. Even though it's a new game, in 2023, I had such a nostalgia trip playing this, taking me back to my childhood when I played the classic platformers such as Spyro & Crash. The blur filter definitely aided in this nostalgia, although I had to turn it off a couple times during the playthrough, especially in the Ice world due to visibility. For a puzzle platformer released in 2023, there's not much of a forced direction that the game tries to put you on, you are free to do most things in any order you want, which feels amazing. Platformers nowadays normally have a set path, so it's quite surprising that Cavern of Dreams is practically free-roam. The puzzling aspect of the game gets more challenging as you progress in the game, it never gets impossibly hard though, but figuring out all of the complicated puzzles felt incredibly rewarding. There's so much variety for an indy game, in my opinion matching that of a Spyro game.Thanks for releasing such a lovely game, I don't normally replay games or suggest games to friends, but I'll be doing both with Cavern of Dreams, I don't understand how this game is relatively unknown. I feel so lucky to get to experience and enjoy this game so early on in it's life-cycle. Thanks again devs for releasing this game! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Another brilliant little throwback 3D platformer in 2023. It truly captures both the visual flair and design of the old Nintendo 64 classics. No combat, fun movement and beautiful locations makes this a relaxingly terrific experience. The final area has deviously tricky puzzles though and presented a bit of a surprising difficulty spike that some might find too daunting.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is a stellar game to relive the old mascot collectathon platformers of yesteryear. With a low poly, early Nintendo 64 look, the closest comparison would be Banjo Kazooie, and I couldn't help but feel a wave of nostalgia flow over me when I first started playing.The visuals of the game looks wonderful. Imaginative scenery decorates each of the levels, and the character designs look charming as well. Most of the collectible eggs are simple enough to get, but there are a few here and there that provide quite a bit of challenge as well, or will completely stump you if you fail to keep in mind some mechanics or items the game world has available.The game is not without it's flaws, however. For one, the game feels far too short, clocking shy of 6 hours myself to beat the game and get all the collectibles. I found myself wishing dearly that there was more to this game.With how short the game is, the pacing feels a bit off as well. Early on you're introduced to a mechanic where you get more moves as you collect eggs, growing new appendages for each in what I found to be an enjoyable visual change showing progress. However, after just the first world I had nearly all but one unlocked. Compare to say the banjo games, where you are learning moves throughout the entire game at points scattered throughout each of the levels. A minor gripe, but one that stuck with me nonetheless.The boss 'fight' of the game is rather punishing. You basically rush down a narrow floating platform dodging attacks and environmental hazards, and any mistake taking damage will surely send you off the edge with no chance of recovery, sending you back to the beginning.Despite that, what you have here in Cavern of Dreams is a charming adventure with adorable creatures in what is clearly a love letter to the old mascot platformers of Nintendo's 64 console. If you have any love whatsoever for that era/genre of gaming, definitely consider picking this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly love this game. It's so fun and cute. Some of the game design can be obtuse at times and other times it can be just a bit slow. Although, I only looked up a answers twice. I honestly love this game though and it made me smile and feel so happy playing through it. I think I only have a few levels left. I don't want it to end.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This a cute and short collection platformer. Find your siblings, help out the residents, stop the bad guy. It controls pretty well, the areas are fairly distinct, and honestly nothing was frustrating at all. It took me 7 hours to 100% it, a majority of collectibles are quick to get with a couple of well hidden ones. Would definitely recommend if you are itching for a ps1/n64 style platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: the dev set out for an n46-style platformer, and while i wasn't an n64 kid, i *was* a ps2 kid, and i can confidently say they nailed the old games style. every time i play it i remember playing spyro or jak and daxter when i was 7 or 8.the baby dragons are also extremely cute. im happy i found it. i want more like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I was really impressed with Cavern of Dreams! It manages to do an excellent job harkening back to Rare's 3D platformer games, but more importantly (IMO) it does it in a way that still feels fresh. It definitely does owe a lot to those Rare games, but the designers have totally earned it - they clearly understood what made those games great and how to execute on it themselves, but they bring their own ideas and designs to the table, and they generally work just as well. Regardless of inspiration, though - at it's core the game is just well-designed and fun to play!I think that part in particular is worth emphasizing - I have played a fair number of 3D platformers both old and new, and it seems like getting the core level designs and game mechanics to feel good is one of the hardest things to get right, especially consistently throughout a whole game. There are games which are, like, completely unabashed clones of classic games which still fail to get this right. But I felt like the entire time I played Cavern of Dreams, the levels were fun to explore, the puzzles were just the right level of challenging, the mechanics all clicked - it all worked well together.Aside from the gameplay - you can probably tell from the trailer that the visuals are really well done (given that, of course, you're into the N64 vibes). I also appreciated that they went for a different general mood overall - more, I don't know, eerie (or perhaps...... dreamlike) and with touches of backstory to uncover. I'm really tempted to compare it to Anodyne, another game I loved, though Anodyne definitely gets a lot closer to straight-up horror at times. But like, if you appreciated Anodyne's vibe, I think you'll like this. (And hey, Anodyne is also a game which is heavily inspired by a retro game but executes it well, with it's own flair. So maybe it's an apt comparison.)I think the biggest weakness of the game is just some general clunkiness with the controls - rolling doesn't feel quite satisfying, and certain moves are difficult to pull off - but I never felt like it was enough that it seriously got in the way of my enjoyment.So in short - I highly recommend Cavern of Dreams! It will definitely tickle the nostalgia centers of your brain but more importantly, it totally stands on it's own as a well-designed 3D platformer. I look forward to whatever it is Bynine decides to do next!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up playing Banjo-Kazooie, Spyro the Dragon, and Super Mario 64 a long time ago in the only home I was ever happy in, thank you for letting me go home for a little while. You play as the adorable dragon Fynn as you platform around 4 stages and a hub world to collect 40 of your missing siblings eggs. You acquire upgrades the more eggs you collect, such as a tail to swipe objects with, and wings to glide. The visuals, models, and animations perfectly emulate playing an old platformer on the N64 or PS1. There are no traditional enemies and you don't need to worry about anything like lives or health. Eggs are comparable in difficulty to collecting a moon in Super Mario Odyssey, making for a very cozy experience. I loved Cavern of Dreams to bits and only wish it was longer. The final upgrade for collecting all 40/40 eggs was very fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is easily one of the best 3D platformers I've played to date. Taking control of a young dragon name Fynn, you embark on a quest to rescue his young siblings as he travels across the zany, unique worlds within the Cavern of Dreams. For those craving for a modern-day Banjo-Kazooie/Conker's Bad Fur Day, this game will certainly scratch that "classic, old-school" itch. While there were a few hiccups along the way, I had an overall excellent experience with this title, and would certainly look forward to a sequel if that's ever in the works.Using a PS4 controller, I really noted how well-responsive the controls felt while playing the young dragon. When you start, Fynn is only capable of jumping and rolling into a ball to build momentum across flat surfaces and slopes. Most of the worlds are rather spacious, so being able to quickly cut through the terrain helps shave time when you need to backtrack, (Side note: I personally enjoyed it for giving that 2D Sonic feel in a 3D environment, sue me :p.)  As you rescue your siblings, you unlock certain abilities that expands Fynn’s move set, including gaining wings to glide, and a tail that both break’s objects and lets you fly forward if you slam your tail right before you land on the ground. These tools really helped enhanced the gameplay for me, especially when returning back to world’s you’ve previously explored and utilizing these abilities to find new pathways/secrets.There is a healthy amount of puzzle challenges within the game. Some are easy to solve, while others may require you to pause and think for a bit. If you are ever stuck, it helps if you look carefully at your surroundings, whether it’s a room or even in the world itself, as those can provide hints as well. That said, sometimes there are hints the game provides that are so vague that its almost up to personal interpretation on how to solve it. This issue was especially apparent when I entered “Prismic Palace”, and had a frustrating time going back and forth in the world, thinking I was missing an obvious hint to solve a puzzle. (Side note: I was so frustrated that I inadvertently found a glitch with the “Jester Boots” power up, an item that lets you walk in the air if you ever walk off a flat surface. Normally the powerup disappears if you leave a designated room, but I bumbled out a way to leave the room while keeping the boots on, which led to many funny game breaking moments admittedly.)For 100% completionists, this game may put you in a sour mood at times when trying to find all collectibles. Collectibles includes finding all of Fynn’s siblings in their eggs and collectible cards that updates the encyclopedia within the game. I highly recommend a guide if only for looking for the cards, since there’s just a few so obscurely hidden that it gives original NES Legend of Zelda flashbacks, and that game at least came with a guide. For casual gamers not interested in 100% completion, this will not pose an issue at all to your experience.Special note for parents: Despite the “cutesy” look of this game, I would not recommend this game for younger audiences below 12 years old personally. The sometimes unsettling imagery of this game may be too upsetting for younger minds, especially in the last world.Cavern of Dreams is a much welcome callback to classic 3D platformers of the late 90s/early 2000s. With that said, it certainly sets out to establish its own unique identity with its psychedelic and frankly bizarre world design; as well as the silly yet sometimes unnerving enemies that you will encounter during your journey. I could not state any better how much I enjoyed my time with this game, and I look forward to seeing any future content with this game series.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely delighted by this one!While other retro/nostalgia platformers have felt lacking in certain features, this one has everything I've been looking for:- Perfect length (5 hours to 100% for me)- Player ability progression- Satisfying movement (including one of the best solutions for underwater movement I've ever seen)- Puzzles that are easy enough to not get stuck, but hard enough to make you feel smart- Level gimmicks that are well thought out and come full circle in the final levelDefinitely worth checking out!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a fun little platformer, and I certainly got that, but I was surprised by the subtle storytelling and worldbuilding that underlie the whole thing. It really sells the idea of exploring this little world, learning its secrets, and making friends with its inhabitants. It's a neat game with a great bit of personality! Glad I played.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: A very authentic feeling N64 style platformer, that feels like it easily could have come out back then. It's actually got a nice amount of challenge in it, and the hand-painted vertex lighting is gorgeous.This game is helplessly cute and the movement is surprisingly fun and smooth.  I loved every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little game. Leans heavily into the N64 aesthetic whilst also carving its own identity with dream-like environments. It has a solid collectathon formula complete with cute characters and interesting puzzles. If you enjoy collectathons or dreamy aesthetics, I strongly recommend. If you enjoy both, it's a must have.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: BUY THIS GAME, ITS CHEAP AND EVERYTHING ABOUT IT IS AMAZING!I got all of the eggs and beat the game so I thought I should say something. I LOVE this game, definitely one of my favorite games I played this year, props to everyone involved. This is genuinely one of the most well crafted and detailed worlds I have experienced in a long time. All the moves are fun to use, the sound design is great, the characters had amazing designs and were really fun (I love Kerrington), the music is great and add a lot to the world, and just the world design and the variety of them were absolutely stellar. And the art direction is amazing OH MY GOD! Even though I'm not old enough to have any nostalgia connected to the games this is (seems) to be inspired of like Banjo and Kazzoie, and Mario 64, when I played this I still got a feeling of warmth and familiarity like I did, thats how you know they got the style down to a T. And its not like the game's design doesn't hold up on its own, everything is so colorful and charming I was literally aw struck when I first got into some of these worlds, but at the same time there is a few unsettling areas that got me from the shear tonal shift.The only thing I have a tiny problem with is that sometimes the camera didn't want to corroborate with me sometimes but that may be a me issue.Other than that the only REAL problem I have with this game is that I wish it was longer, and if that's the only  "complaint" I have then you know you made something special. I can't wait to see what else these developers cook up in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I originally picked this up from watching a streamer and having my backseat gamer kick in. This is such a charming puzzle platformer game that harks back to the old school style games on the n64 and early cd rom. Think breakable walls, hidden areas, riddles to solve. It's movement is also very fun and could lend itself to speedrunning very well if you are inclined.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice and relaxing game that's perfect for playing at night, or whenever you're tired. I love the feeling of exploring the various locations, especially the mysterious, uninhabited rooms, like the bedroom in Lostleaf Lake. I also love the graphics, character designs, music, etc. You captured the N64 vibe perfectly!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute and addictive platformer that recalls its predecessors from the N64 era. I love the games sense of exploration and the freedom to "mess around and find out" it takes me back to first time playing Banjo or LOZ, and Spyro, trying things over and over until you realize the real  solution. The game has a few puzzles that I would have loved a guide for, and a few platforming skill spikes, but overall its a treat for anyone who loves collect-a-thons and platformers! the blur filter was a fun addition, and I found myself using it quite a lot! overall cute, fun, and really understands its inspirations.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy classic platforming and adventure games, then I can't really fault this.  Obviously if those types of games aren't your thing then I doubt this will change your mind.  One thing I loved about Cavern of Dreams was that fact that, despite feeling familiar and having influence from a number of classic games; it still felt very unique.  Level Design and Graphics -The stages themselves are very varied and despite as mentioned having some nods to games of the genre, they still feel special and memorable in their own way.  I like the graphical and art style, I understand 64 bit graphics aren't for everyone, but I still felt the game looked like it would have pushed the N64 hard and is frequently full of colour.  Another thing to mention is the music is excellent and really helps to immerse you into the worlds.Performance and controls - Except for a few glitches - that were fixed very quickly I might add... the game runs very smoothly.  Both on steam deck and PC the performance was fantastic.  I get that obviously with the games design, it shouldn't be taxing to run, but sadly that doesn't stop a lot of games falling short in this area.The controls are very unique and without giving too much away, all the moves that are earned are actually useful.  This is where I feel a lot of these games fall short, they make themselves far too similar to other platformers.  While there are some moves you would expect from a dragon character, for the most part Fynn's moves are unique and feel very different to other platformers.  They may take a little while to get used to, I did die to a certain move a number of times... but overall I though they were great.Summary - Cavern of Dreams is a colourful well presented platform/adventure game that will transport you right back to the N64/PS1 era.  The gameplay while familiar, certainly has it's unique quirks to make it stand out from the crowd.  My only criticism is the length of the game and its replay-ability value.  However, I am really hoping that a sequel or additional content is created as I am eager to see more of Fynn!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute game that will make anyone who loved exploration collectathons from the N64 era nostalgic. The low poly graphics and atmosphere are my favorite aspects of the game. There are varied locations, but keep in mind that this is a small indie project so the scope isn't that huge! The controls aren't complicated, but they're deeper than I was expecting - they also feel much better if you use a controller, so keep that in mind if you usually go for keyboard & mouse. My biggest gripe with the game is the final sequence- it frustrated me so much that I turned on a hidden ability through the secret debug menu just so I could finish it and continue playing past it.The game isn't perfect, but is still absolutely worth checking out if you're a fan of throwback titles or cute games in general. I hope Bynine makes more games!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game. It promises a N64 style experience and absolutely delivers on that promise. The levels look great, it was fun picking out what games it may be inspired by: "oh thats clanker's cavern" "oh that's mad monster mansion" "oh that's gerudo desert". The movement has a nice amount of depth to it, so I can't wait to see what the speedruns for this game will look like. There's also momentum based curl-up-into-a-ball button that is reminiscent of glover that is fun to play around with. There's no health, if you get hit, you get knocked pretty far away. If you fall into a pit, you void out and start back at the entrance of the room. The more I played the more I really liked this system. It felt more casual, but honestly didn't really impact the difficulty. There's still consequences for failing a platforming sequence, but removes the tedium of dying, restarting at the entrance to a level, and trekking all the way back through to where you died. It's a pretty small difference, but I appreciate it.The music is great and has just as much personality as the levels themselves.My only complaint is the final fight is a bit rough. The camera starts facing the wrong way every time you void out, the enemies are resized which messed with my depth perception so i had to slow down to avoid hitting them, and overall the fight was a massive difficulty spike compared to the rest of the game. Difficulty itself isn't bad, but I had to quickly git gud with the variety of movement options to get through. but this is a very minor complaint in an otherwise amazing game.Finally, I loved the post-game secret hunting. It was such a fun, satisfying, and chill way to make one last quick loop through the game before saying goodbye.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up playing banjo and dk64 and dearly missed the collectathon genre this game scratches an itch that hasn’t been scratched in so long, I’ve played yooka Laylee and a hat in time, and enjoyed both but neither really recaptured the feeling of playing the collectathon platformers I loved as a kid until now. _childDocuments_.review: Great game! _childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: A cute love letter to the days of N64 3D platforming with collect-a-thon gameplay akin to that of the classic rare-ware games formula.While a shorter experience that could take an average player around 4-5 hours to complete, the music, atmosphere and the gameplay were quite satisfying. the music feeling like a nice calming theme for each level and the general atmosphere and level design of each world accompanying it. the gameplay felt competent enough. giving you a few extra abilities along the adventure like rolling across distances very fast with well timed ground pounds and has one of the most satisfying rewards for 100% all the game's collectibles by offering a little more to explore in each level and giving you a chance to discover a little more about the characters in this world.A lot of the puzzles feel straightforward enough, save for a handful of others that have stumped lots of players, a 'star' puzzle especially. while each puzzle does have some hint hidden somewhere either through environmental detail or dialogue, sometimes they aren't the most straight forward. one map has you running around a wasteland to just happen upon an egg which even looking around the area after the weather cleared still left me wondering if there was a clue that somehow was suppose to guide me to the egg's randomly placed location. another such puzzle has you map out a shape in a 5x5 tile in a small room with the clue "Match with us" the clue being to look at a higher resolution wall texture than the 5x5 tiles and be expected to translate the wall texture to the tiles. what could save this room is having a clear to see portrait frame in the center of the room to focus on when given the clue. aside from those, a lot of the puzzles are fun and sometimes intriguing enough that when you solve it you may feel the dopamine kick in.The story was a little quick with not much going on similar to mario 64 in which the only dialogue you recieve are at the beginning with your goal, dialogue with the antagonist anytime they arrive, the ending fight and any hidden lore you find exploring the worlds and reading signs.The music is a wonderful soundtrack that fit each environment. sometimes playing in my head every now and then.it's a pleasant game i highly recommend to anyone that's a fan of collect-a-thons, cute games, nostalgia chasing, a good soundtrack and art design reminiscent of the N64 days! definitely worth the price and i wish the team that made this game well and look forward to seeing what they do next!
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a callback to my childhood N64 days. Controls weren't great and moving around didn't feel as tight as games like Mario 64 and Banjo-Kazooie, but you can tell that's the vibe they were going for. Taking into account the team size that made this, it's great what they managed to accomplish.Sound balancing needs work. Didn't realize the game even had music because the sound effects were so loud I had it turned down to make those reasonable. I also had to play the game to completion twice before eventually giving up and poking the code to get the achievement for all encyclopedia entries to pop. _childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Looks and plays like a forgotten Rare game of from the late 90's, which is a good thing!! It captures the ambiance and atmosphere of the 3D platformers of the N64 era perfectly. As someone who is obsessed with playing mods of old N64 games (My Mario 64 mod folder is massive LOL) I wonder if it would be possible to add support for a USB N64 controller? DK64, Banjo Kazooie, Konker's Bad Fur Day and ESPECIALLY Banjo Tooie took full advantage of the N64 controller combinations, and many mods/hacks of N64 games have done even moreso. There are wonderful mods of Mario 64 for example that make him feel as modern as Super Mario Odyssey, similar to how fluid it feels to play your game! It's amazing!My only main complaint here is that camera control, ironically enough, is either too fast or too slow for mouse/keyboard and makes balancing between controlling the character and camera either too slippery or too sluggish.Really excited to delve more into this as the days progress, as well as seeing your future releases. I'm so happy that there are devs out there that continue to make (and mod) games of a long forgotten, yet sorely missed, era of gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Perfectly captures the mystical atmosphere and design of Nintendo 64/gen 5 collectathons and puzzle platformers. Every part of the experience hearkens back to an era where exploring a mysterious and dream-like place was enough for a game to be interesting. The graphics are exactly what you'd see in games from the mid-to-late 90s and the music is just INCREDIBLE. It's also a nice length; it doesn't overstay its welcome but didn't feel too short either.The movement in general is quite engaging; after getting accustomed to the abilities, launching yourself around (and even sort of cheating a few of the platforming challenges) becomes second nature and never stops being fun. Even swimming is pretty palette-able. Part of what works in Cavern of Dreams is what isn't included: No lengthy tutorials to disturb the pacing, no lives or even a health system, in turn there is no fall damage or breathing meter under water (which imo very few games actually benefit from), no real combat, and few arbitrary boundaries in levels that obstruct you from just exploring and finding your way out-of-bounds to your heart's content.A few small drawbacks: the character controller doesn't deal well with steep inclines, and some of the mini-puzzles might be a little too cryptic for some. The camera is also a little troublesome when you roll at high speeds, which is mostly only a pain point at the finale. Drawing players' attention to the breakable eggs in the lobby when they are there would also be nice, it tripped me up for a bit since they're mostly identical to all the other eggs.All in all, it's a 8.5/10. really accomplishes what it sets out to do, and if you grew up in the 90s, it should transport you back to your childhood.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: a 4-8 hour game, and very well-curated level design makes the gameplay available very enjoyable - and the secrets you can find in post-game are also a treat.Every egg being collectable on your first visit to an area is very encouraging! The more you do, find, and collect, the more the game changes into a playground. Some of the bonus cards, though, are plenty tougher on you - and sometimes are just darn tough to find. The checklist managed to make me spend more time than i needed to on scrounging - I'd given up at first, just to find them later on somewhere i didn't think of or know about.Rarely, the clues for puzzles are hard to understand or find - the third and fourth area have one or two instances of this each. Thankfully, it isn't that frustrating! just pay careful attention to what's close by, and you'll eventually pick up on them.the only concern I have is the first area being the worst optimized - either that, or it's dense/big enough to cause lag on old computers, such as mine. it's interesting that pretty much everywhere else doesn't have this problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is a great example that a consistent art style goes farther than hyper realistic graphics and physics which require a lot of hardware resources while they offer little in return.Pretty chill game with lovable characters, consistent art style and dreamy looking levels which reminded me of some parts of Rayman 2 and 3 so it's a must have in my book. _childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: A true gem of nostalgic platformers. The graphics are straight out of the N64/PS1 era and the gameplay is just as simple but just as fun. It's short, but makes the most out of its time with lovingly made worlds and characters. You'll get plenty of mileage out of each ability as you're gathering eggs, cards, and mushrooms. It really feels like a game that managed to trim almost all the fat. There's no real combat to speak of, enemies are usually invincible in the few worlds they appear, but that's not a huge drawback when you're bouncing between collectibles. Also the music and sound design are great, fitting and punchy it was an excellent match. All that gushing aside, I do have a couple bugaboos.The puzzles are generally on the simple side. One world has two different "hit things in the order of the conspicuous poster" objectives. This isn't a deal breaker, just go in knowing the game's more about having fun and exploring than challenging your platforming or puzzle skills. The final segment kinda honks. It's easy to be forced to restart this segment over and over because it's real easy to fall off the edge (or be blown off). The challenge doesn't feel super satisfying to beat, and while it's visually interesting there isn't much variance in what it asks of you. That's really it though. Just two issues that I don't think will ruin the experience for you. Though I will say I'm extremely biased, 3D platformers and *especially* collectathons are my favorite genre of game. If you grew up on old-school 3D platformers, or if it's just a genre you're a fan of, give this game a try. It's like a more chill Banjo-Kazooie by way of Spyro 3. Good fun and a hearty recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cute retro-3D puzzle platformed adventure with heavy inspiration from N64 games like Banjo-Kazooie and Mario 64, but it reminds me of a PS1 or PC game from that time. You can see the influence, but feels different enough that it stands on it own.Controls on Fynn don't feel as smooth as I might hope. Horn bouncing near a wall can push you off where you were landing and pulling off a hi-jump never felt consistent. Probably a "me" thing but it did kinda annoy me that Fynn would run after a roll or drive, but you can jump to stop it though. Those might be nit-picks because the game is easy enough. There were a few eggs and cards you could find laying in the openly in some of the worlds. However the actual puzzle and/or platforming was actually very well done, with the puzzles being what I few are the real interesting challenge of the game. Also They give you a nice bonus when you collect a the eggs.Overall Cavern of Dreams is an enjoyable game and one I would highly recommend if you liked the old school puzzle platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent little throwback to the platformers of old.  If you enjoyed the Mario 64s and the Banjo Kazooies of the 90s, then you'll enjoy this little gem.Unlike some modern games that have almost too much content (think Mario Odyssey) this game keeps it simple.  There are a few different collectibles and in just the right quantities to not be too much of a chore to collect.  Level design is simple yet interesting and beautiful.  Music fits the levels great and adapts to whatever is happening.Pros: Beautiful interesting levels.   Lots of post game "content" to explore.  Terrific music.  Some clever puzzles.  No lives or health to worry about so you can just focus on completing the game.  Main character is awful cute!Cons: Controls are a bit cumbersome at first, but get better as the game goes on.  Some puzzles are a little more tricky than they need to be.  Hints given are sometimes a bit too cryptic.  Not very many NPCs which made the game feel a little bit lonely... A tad on the short side.  It took me about 8 hours to finish and find everything.For $13, its well worth it!

_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Loved every second of this game! The way that you explore some areas that can be both cheery and also have some creepy aspects within them really hooked me in. _childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so where to start with this.This may contain SPOILERS so consider yourself warned!The game as a whole is pretty solid, it's a nice little collectathon platformer with some well hidden secrets and collectibles. I really enjoyed having to go through multiple levels to unlock some eggs and the overall mechanics are pretty fun. I also really enjoyed the movement, especially being able to chain some movements to get more height or more speed. I like being able to solve problems by using my movement instead of using a mechanic thats given to me. There is one negative thing though, which unfortunately made me ragequit the game and that was the end boss level which was just unnecessarily over challenging and unfair.So here goes: 1. The boss is sending projectiles at you from the front... in a game where depth perception is already very hard. So you never really know when exactly the projectile is going to hit you. This could have easily been avoided by having something on the floor that shows where the projectile is at, like the drop shadows on the character, which follows a similar concept.2. If you do manage to hit the projectile, depending on where you stand in the level, the projectile will hit the floor in front of you and the explosion will send you flying anyway... so that's just straight up punishing the player by doing something he is supposed to do... 3. Almost at the end there's an upstream that's supposed to send you upwards to reach the next stage, and you're supposed to use your momentum to get enough speed to cross the gap.... the issue is... the boss keeps sending projectiles at you that you literally can't avoid.. I fell off there 4 times because the boss hit me while I was in that upstream, granted there is a jumppad in that area but...4. The jumppad mushrooms dont disable player input when hitting them, so if you dont let go of the joystick the moment you hit the jumppad, you might not get send back, but you fly god knows where.. also: one of the jumppads sends you straight through a saw mill at one point which sometimes makes you get hit by it.. so theres the save thats supposed to help me get back on track...5. Theres no checkpoint at all... Now this point is very debatable, I feel like the only reason I was missing checkpoints in that level was, because it was so unbelievably hard to get through due to all these aforementioned issues... Now thats it.. I can still recommend the game for everything that happened before that endboss, I had great fun trying to get the collectibles and solving puzzles and I think that the developer did a great job on the game, especially for it being a solo project. I might pick the game up again and 100% it but for now, i need to restore my sanity.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, this game is a masterpiece.The aesthetic of a surrealist take on the signature N64 look is captivating and delightful.The storytelling is simple, yet completely brilliant.The controls are tight and responsive, with an elegance to the flow of everything.The reward for 100% completion is simply perfect.I simply cannot recommend Cavern of Dreams enough.

_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Cavern of Dreams is absolutely adorable and enchanting on every level. The world is unique and thoughtful, both in its mechanical construction and its creative conception. Its inspirations are obvious and worn proudly but they come together in ways that are always cute, novel, imaginative, and original. It’s impossible not to smile about something while playing this. The movement is delightful and truly makes every space feel more like a puzzle-rich playground than an obstacle course (with intentional and memorable exceptions) and you truly feel almost constantly rewarded for sniffing around and exploring to your heart’s content. The optional collectibles are extremely rewarding as well. Collecting mushrooms to feed to Fynn’s baby siblings is precious and it also gives you the ability access new areas. The encyclopedia cards are my favorite part, though. They’re always hidden in fun spots and each one of them gives you a tiny snippet of lore/flavor text about an inhabitant of the world, injecting even the smallest environmental details and obstacles with personality, love, and a place in a world that feels crafted with care. I’d really encourage anybody to try and 100% the game. It’s short and sweet enough that I can’t imagine anybody would find it to be a chore.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the development of this game for a while now and I'm so glad it played as good as it looked. This is a wonderful 3D platformer. _childDocuments_.review: "Cavern of Dreams" is a charming, but rather short (around 7 hours to 100% it) 3D-retro-platformer in the veins of the classics like Rare's "Banjo Kazooie".You play as a young dragonling trying to rescue his unhatched siblings in a dreamy and whimsical world. _childDocuments_.review: I had a blast playing this game. I got all the collectables and ended up sitting and playing through the whole game in a day. I loved all the nods to the 64 era adored the music and the controls. Minor things; the camera was bugged in some sections which made me feel like I was fighting the camera. This only happened twice for me. The settings also reset every time you exit and enter the game again. I did not like the blur effect and had to turn that off every time. Minor annoyance. As of writing this the achievements are also bugged but it looks like the Dev is listening to all the feedback and we should hopefully see these issues resolved in a future update.The reward for completing the game was also a wonderful surprise and really opened the world. I wish other games rewarded the player in that way. Overall this game is easily worth the $15 price tag and was such a love letter to the late 90's platformers. 8.5/10 you should give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: • Great and fluid movement, almost of that of Super Mario Odyssey  • A Atmosphere to trigger your nostalgia of Nintendo Era platformer games, especially original Banjo-Kazooie fans • Only $11.97 USD!?Cons: • Short Game, short, and small levels making you want more at the end of each one • Frustrating final Boss fightOverall for a $11.97 USD game, Cavern of Dreams is a great old school Nintendo 64 platformer game, and well worth the price to the point of being a steal, and the developer should have priced it higher. If you have an itch that has not been scratched since playing Banjo-Kazooie, either it being the atmosphere, or game play, there's a chance it might scratch it.Unfortunately the game might not satisfy you for long or fully, it's a short game if the price did not tell you that already, lasting around 4 hours to finish the game, and additional 3 hours of collectable hunting. The levels feel small, with not much to do in them compared to the classics, as well having a small selection of levels to play through, ending each level never truly satisfied me, wanting to demand more of it. But the biggest issue I have with the game is the beginning and end of the game. When you start the first Banjo-Kazooie game, you are treated with an introduction cinematic, showing you the protagonist's goal, Banjo's sister has been kidnapped by Gruntilda, showing you your goal. Meanwhile in Cavern of Dreams, you start the game in the Hub world, where you talk to Sage and she tells you your goal, during the game you see cinematic clips of antagonists getting in your way, taunting you. A cinematic that played at the beginning of starting a new game would have done the game well, instead of telling the player what they have to do. And finally at the end, the boss fight against the antagonist is memorable, and not in a good way, a check or save points would have made the level much more tolerable, but as it is, it will make you frustrated when you die, and realise you have to start the boss fight again.Even with the block of text of criticism I wrote up, I wrote it due to the joy I got from the game, even with its flaws, and the want of the developer(s) to improve. Playing the game and taking in the atmosphere you can tell the developer(s) have a special place for the old school Nintendo 64 era of games, especially Banjo-Kazooie, this game is pure passion, and deserves more attention with its fair share of criticism, it's not a perfect game, but it's passion is far greater than its small size would make you think. If you have $12, I strongly suggest buying this game, it's well worth the price, especially if you grew up with the Nintendo 64 console.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Super solid ode to Nintendo 64 platformers. Though it's short (managed to 100% it in around 6 hours), there's a lot to explore both in terms of finding collectibles and well-hidden secrets. Loved reading the encyclopedia, loved solving the cute platforming puzzles, and loved the constantly upgrading moveset that still keeps things simple. A wonderful little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a huge fan of the movement in this game. It's bearable in the sense that it works well with the game world but I didn't find it fun or satisfying to control throughout my initial playthrough. That's my only major complaint. The art direction & overall presentation is absolutely stunning. There's a lot of areas that tastefully pay homage to games from the N64 / PS1 era (Banjo, Glover & Klonoa etc) while also managing to retain its own identity. The whimsical music does a fantastic job at building the atmosphere along with the detailed environments & there's so many standout areas & secrets throughout the game where you can tell they were made with love. This game hit all the right notes for me & it left me feeling happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, short experience. A few areas are a bit challenging if you are going for everything, but only 1 or 2 frustrating parts towards the end that are mostly a matter of having to go a bit roundabout to get something. The atmosphere is very nice, and I appreciate the subtleties in some of the storytelling. Good luck to the devs in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

_childDocuments_.review: Embark on a magical quest as Fynn the dragon to rescue your unhatched siblings from the mysterious Cavern of Dreams in this N64-style 3D platformer. Gain new abilities, meet unique characters, solve puzzles, and beware of the mysterious villain.
_childDocuments_.name: Cavern of Dreams

name: Moss: Book II
detailed_description: Winner of The Game Awards' 'Best VR/AR Game,' the VR Awards' 'VR Game of the Year,' and so many more! Quill is back—and she’s being hunted. Those who seek to unmake this world are desperate for the Glass she holds, and they’ll stop at nothing to claw it from her grasp. To stand a chance, Quill will need a true partner by her side—and we hope that partner is you. With her, you’ll venture deep inside the hexed castle of the Arcane where dangerous terrain, challenging puzzles, and enemies twisted in fire and steel await.The journey will be trying—filled with triumph and heartbreak alike—but new allies, old friends, and the very nature of the castle itself can offer help along the way. Yet in the end, it is you alone who can lift Quill up to save this world, and together, rise to legend. Gameplay Reach into The World of Moss Your every action has even more meaning in Moss: Book II, as we take full advantage of today’s virtual reality technology, letting you move objects, battle enemies, and manipulate the field of play as the key ally to our hero, Quill. Adventure to Fantastic Places Travel back to a lively world that hums with wonder and legend. Explore the castle where her uncle was held captive, caves beneath, snow covered mountain tops to the depths below filled with ancient artifacts, mysterious creatures, and sprawling views. Form a Unique Bond Your abilities are complementary to Quill’s in an alliance for the ages. Combine classic, action-adventure controls with a world that responds to your touch. Solve puzzles, combat evil, and achieve victory together. A Story Told Unlike Any Before From its opening pages, Moss: Book II continues to draw you into a first-of-its-kind fully immersive world of myth and magic. Enjoy a rich tale of intriguing characters, illustrious artifacts, and legends old and new.
