_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Fully refunded, I hope they fix it in the future and I will get it again if it gets updated to be the re-release it deserves, but frankly it should have been good from day 1 and not whatever this is. And to add onto these things the game is 16:9 with no 4:3 option or balancing to accomodate for this, so it actually alters combos on some characters and is not arcade accurate as a result.I sadly absolutely CANNOT recommend this in it's current state, the game itself is awesome and has a legacy built up for a reason but this is such a bad look for the game's first ever home release. $30 is sort of a whatever price point on it's own, kind of iffy, but it gets worse when you take a look at the port itself and see how absolutely barebones it is with things such as ZERO keyboard support and quite frankly awful training and online menus, and realize it jumps up to $40 when you add the 3 "DLC" characters who have been playable for no extra cost in the arcade versions since 2005. Also I bought this and was instantly greeted by it running at like 200fps, I had to fix the framerate with a third party frame limiter program. I really sincerely hope the devs take a good look at this and patch the game with the proper QoL features it deserves because this game is legendary and this is just really unacceptable for an almost 2023 fighting game release, just having good netcode doesn't make your port good. The one good thing I can say is that this port is based off the latest balancing NESICA version of the game, but that's pretty much all the good I have to say at the moment and in the future if nothing is done to fix this rerelease.
_childDocuments_.name: The Rumble Fish 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Training Mode+ Has RollbackCons:-No Lobby system, you have to manually invite your friends through Steam or play a quick match-No rematch system, you get booted to the main menu after the match-Hazama, Greed, and Beatrice are DLC characters that are 4 USD each, despite being available in the Arcade port from about 17 years ago-The game is 30 USD. You're paying for a $40 game if you include the characters that shouldn't be DLC-When you win a match online, you're forced to sit through the win screen and then the game over screen before you can queue another match (or just the game over screen if you lose)?:Despite what the game's Steam page says, there is keyboard supportThe game feels fun to play but these, plus many other issues that were mentioned by other reviewers makes this port very barebones and I'm reluctant to recommend the game right now until it gets fixed. Wait until it goes on sale at the very least if you still want to pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Rumble Fish 2

_childDocuments_.review: Despite it initial release, 3goo have been doing this game justice by releasing tons of QoL fixes to the game. While its still annoying that all 3 boss character that was unlockable in the original arcade version and are fully playable in the nesicaxlive version of the game are STILL paid dlcs; the game overall quality is still a lot better as of now. Things about reviews, most folks don't go back to update them when something changes. Despite my steam hours I have put a lot of time in this game on the original Naomi version and the updated NesicaXLive version that this is based on. TRF2 is a good game that deserves all the love and attention it can get.Do I recommend this game: Yes, especially rn during the Winter Sale where the game is half off as of writing. I can't bring myself to recommend it at the 29.99 USD price tag because of the boss being excluded from the base game. So if you happen to see this after the sale, just hold off on it or get it from somewhere else cheaper.
_childDocuments_.name: The Rumble Fish 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a lot better now that most if not all of its launch issues have been fixed. You can turn off widescreen and enable 4:3 mode with sidebars to play the game as you're supposed to, matches against other players no longer kick you back to the title screen and let you rematch, and lobbies have been added. As for changes to balance, this port is actually based off the NESiCAxLive rerelease of the game, which came with a balance patch that is regarded as being better balanced than the Atomiswave original (at least according to the Mizuumi wiki).That's all good, but making Greed, Hazama, and Beatrice DLC when they were unlockable in the arcade versions for free with the flip of a switch is still a very scummy move. It does not replicate the arcade experience of having to "enable" them but rather cuts three characters who were in the game before and resells them to you for no good reason. The game's also a bit too expensive for a game that originally came out in 2005 and doesn't have much content beyond arcade, time attack, survival, training, and online. The publisher is quite frankly incompetent, both with the DLC practices and for botching this port's launch in the first place, and it very well might have ruined this port's chances of being popular and successful thanks to a negative first impression. At least they handled the launch of The Rumble Fish + a whole lot better from what I've seen. So in conclusion, the game is fixed. It's a well-balanced and very fun hidden gem that's well worth a buy if you like fighting games (though not at $30, but it tends to go on sale somewhat often), but although this is a positive review, I can't really forgive the publishers for the abysmal launch and the presence of DLC characters who should've already been in the game by default. At least they're $4 each, but still.
_childDocuments_.name: The Rumble Fish 2

_childDocuments_.review: The Rumble Fish 2 is a very neat fighting game. Since the first release on Atomiswave, the NESiCAxLive version had two updates that genuinely improved the game. There's definitely more that could still be improved, but the game has a cool cast and mechanics.This port of the NESiCA version is sorely incomplete and flawed. Based on my testing, it seems like this port is actually just of the NESiCA 1.0 version and not the more updated 1.1 version. In addition, the game has a huge change from its arcade versions, in that its in 16:9 perspective instead of 4:3, which significantly changes the gameplay for many characters and messes up many combos and strategies. I'm totally fine with them making additional changes to the previous version, but they should've honestly gone further to add more additional balance changes from even 1.1, which I think could be improved upon. As I stated earlier, in my testing, this appears to even be based on the old NESiCA verison and not even the 1.1 update. EDIT: After doing more testing, I can confirm that this *is* working off of the 1.1 version and not 1.0 like I previously thought, a few interactions I was using as a testing basis were functioning differently because of the view change. That's my mistake. I do still believe the point stands in that this is functionally a distinct (and worse) offshoot of NESiCA 1.1 because the view change messes a lot of things up. If they wanted to change stuff about the game, they should've gone further to improve various characters, moves, etc. None of this is to mention the predatory locking off of characters freely available in the 12 year old NESiCA version, aka Hazama, Greed, and Beatrice. Instead the developers are trying to charge extra money for them as "DLC," even though they are already present in the game. In addition, the game is missing essential features for a fighting game, including: damage data, stun data, hitstun/recovery data, damage scaling data, frame data, recording, *working* auto guard, and more in training mode. There's also the fact that there's no lobbies for online play (a staple for growing the scene and ensuring enjoyable play for groups) and no rematch option (besides just kicking players out to a game over screen after the match is over). It really feels like the developers had no idea what standard users expect in a fighting game.I highly recommend the developers communicate directly with competitive fighting game players *BEFORE* attempting to make improvements, as it's clear they don't know what they're doing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Rumble Fish 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself isn't bad, but this port isn't doing justice for this game in the current state that it is in.  The only major reason to get this right now is if you wanted a dedicated training mode where you can grind labbing uninterrupted due to Flycast/Fightcade limitations where you can't properly lab this game.  Even then though, there's no reset position button and no guard after 1st hit function that works properly in training mode.  The game works when you boot it up, but unless you're some kind of training mode/lab fiend there's nothing this port will offer in it's current state where I would say it is worth buying since online is screwed and one match will send you back to main menu as though you were playing Event Mode on an arcade cabinet for...reasons.TLDR; game good, port bad.  Will update review if/when devs patch/update the game since they said that there are planned updates for online lobbies and training mode options people asked about.  Game is a tad bit expensive for what you get currently unless you're going to lab hard af in training mode.03/02/2023 Edit: The first substantial patch came out today on steam since the game's release almost three months ago.  The biggest change is that "combat range" in the game's options main menu was added which lets you play with the original 4:3 aspect ratio the game originally played in, but instead of banners to show where walls are like in the Nesica version, it's just invisible walls.  It's weird but it's still a step in the right direction to where the game was originally.  Multiplayer online lobbies now exist for up to three(needs more testing?) people in one room and will keep players there after a match ends unlike previously.  As good as these updates really are though, the fact this game sells 3 of the hidden characters as DLC at ~50% of the game's base price is still awful and the game is still overpriced for what you get.  Fightcade and port versions are now distinct with balance updates added to the port version however, so this might be worth getting on sale in the longrun if this game manages to pick up some momentum later on.  It still feels too expensive at base + DLC prices..Edit: 12/22/2023: Color me SURPRISED AS HELL, the game is legitimately in a much better state now, pretty much up to the point I expected it to be when it first launched last year.  They added new recording/playback options in training mode, and added sidebars as a new option for short range battle style and the ability to have a command list show in the sidebars if you want.  I would highly recommend playing short range with side bars as this is the Nesica standard me and others were expecting when this game launched originally.  This game can be worth it on sale IMO, at full price it's a little iffy and the DLC will always suck, but I can't imagine what else could be put into the game at this point after the last update.  It is a bit too late with bigger things like SF6 and Granblue Rising now out, along with Tekken 8 and Under Night 2 on the way in the next few weeks, but if you really want this get everything on sale instead of spending the $45 for everything like I did in the past.
_childDocuments_.name: The Rumble Fish 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. The fighting is fast and fluid, and the system mechanics are an absolute joy to mess around and play with. It creates a unique, expressive game that makes me want to play for hours.This port however, has terrible issues.  Even if it's a port of a game from 2005, I've seen other ports of fighting games done way better. This game has Rollback netcode, and that's great. Everything else about the online is terrible.You cannot see the opponent's ping.You cannot deny matches in case the opponent does have high ping.There's only a single random search mode, and it's "ranked" only.No lobbies, which also means no spectating.And worst of all? No instant rematching. Oh wait, there's no rematching at all? Why?!It just gives you a game over screen after your match, and before that you have to sit through the character victory screen. Then you get booted to the title screen, and you have to queue all over again. This would be acceptable if this port came out in 2005, but no, it's 2022 and it launched with this? And it asks for $30? With all the bosses as DLC as well???EDIT: Oh right, I forgot. You indeed can see the Ping display, but only during the character select screen! You know, when it's too late to back out of a match you know will be horrifically laggy or not. Even then, I don't think you can back out of matches at all. Please give us that option in the future if you'll let us see player names in the random queue anyway.Save yourself the $30 and play it on Fightcade. You'll be in and out of matches much quicker, and you don't have to buy the boss characters that are already in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Rumble Fish 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good but yeah it should not have been this pricy and the DLC should have been free.Also for those who are wondering why some combos don't work, is because this is based on the 2011 acrade re release which had balance changes as well as the wide screen, so making the game 4:3 wont be an option.For the people who give this game a negative review, yeah you have every right to be upset and I'm not going to try to change your mind, if you plan on buying this game, wait for a sale like I did, don't buy it at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Rumble Fish 2

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT - Refunded and went to fightcade instead.It shouldn't have been released in this state. Im judging this shoddy port more than I am the game itself though because it's been around for over a decade and still rocks. But yh, the port on the other hand has problems.Sure it FUNCTIONS most of the time, but that's not enough when you're charging $30 for an old fighting game with such a niche following. Especially with the DLC issue that does it no favours. Probably just puts newcomers off the purchase, in fact that's part of the reason why I felt a refund was a better option even though i was hyped to support this one.Rollback works well though. (Although this can be experienced on fightcade for free so do with that info what you will.)The game has enjoyable mechanics to mess around with, rewarding practice and experimentation. Players who haven't played fighters of old with slightly more strict inputs and execution than more recent fighting games, may feel its a little jarring to get used to. Personally i like it this way cuz it makes combos feel more like the damage they deal has been earned rather than handed to me for a fraction of the effort like in Stri-ANYWAY~ My main issues here are - No rematch option. Instead you get thrown into a GAME OVER screen which you cant skip, to then be thrown back to the main menu until you get your buddy to invite you all over again. This is apparently being dealt with in a later patch but the fact that this wasn't applied by launch means that every single match is followed by frustration and tedium till that promised date.- No position reset in training mode. There's other missing and buggy features like the auto block not working properly, and you cant record like others have said. That's all a shame, but for me, having to reposition the characters myself, turns me off practising for long periods entirely. I hope this is something else they add into training mode because to me its essential. I understand that this game is old, but this port is brand new and should show that in its presentation. Letting me reposition with SELECT + 4/1/2/3/6 would be great.- The price of this lacklustre port, and the "DLC" marketed alongside it.$30 for a port this devoid of basic polish is too steep Imo. The game itself is fantastic but that doesn't change the fact that its still ancient. Right now you're essentially paying for a buggy training mode since anyone can hop onto fightcade and play online there like i mentioned. But to salt the wound, it looks like 3 characters have been gutted from the roster just to be marketed as DLC for $4 each. The console version had these characters readily available to you years before, i think one needed a code but regardless. Marketing team would rather you fork over another $11.97 for $42.96 overall. "They have to make a profit" or "Other games do it too so its fine" are popular arguments people tend to hide behind to defend this type of thing (for reasons beyond me). But nah, it doesn't change that a greedy marketing tactic is just that. All its done here is put a negative stank over the port. It wasn't necessary and shouldn't have been done.Overall Im pretty disappointed in this ports release despite how hyped i was to play it on steam with friends. If time was an issue to give it more polish, then more should have been given to at least fix what they're saying will be done in the patch. I know that's super easy for me to say without knowing anything about game development, but its how i feel when im the one whose paying for it. These are all problems that didn't need to be here at launch. But yeah, rather than just sit and complain i got a full refund instead. I doubt the patch will make buying this game more appealing because those ripped characters are definitely staying behind that DLC paywall. But who knows, maybe if it all goes on sale for a the right price ill jump back on.

_childDocuments_.review: A cult classic fighting game that was originally released during the "Dark Ages" of fighting games by the OG SNK Team now under "Dimps" right before SF4 revived the FGC which you could argue at the time was on life support. This port when it released here on Steam was unfortunately completely botched from the pricing including the DLC monetization, bare bones touch ups for PC play, and things like the stages not having arcade perfect spacing in 16:9 so certain combos wouldn't work as they should. I mean you could argue at least there's rollback so online play is decent (If you could get matches here lol). But this seems like a lesson in how not to release/re-release a fighting game. Now RF2 is sitting at a "Mostly Negative" rating and has been left to dry. I will commend the devs for at least addressing most of the problems if you look at the series of patches they released over time, and finally marking down the MSRP down to 14.99 USD and the DLC characters at .99 cents a pop. How the game is listed today is how it should have been on launch, but it's too little too late in a way. Now the default place to play if you want to run sets is fightcade. Glad this exists even though it was sadly DOA, but hopefully this is a learning lesson for everyone involved. I think for fighting game devs they should really run a  early access period for players to test and then during that time get feedback and fix any issues/add certain highly requested features/QoL before doing a true "official"/Final release when trying to bring back old games like The Rumble Fish 2. This is just my 2 cents. - Cult Classic from the "Dark Ages" of the FGC that everyone who likes fighting games should try, unique cast and system mechanics. Cool yet sometimes uncanny character animations. Completely botched release by the publisher and devs that destroyed any momentum this official port could have had, but the most important issues seem to be fixed now including the pricing. Unless some notable FGC streamer tries to revive this official release fightcade is the only way to get online matches now and for the foreseeable future.

_childDocuments_.review: - UPDATE -Since my initial review, the game has seen a couple of huge updates that brought about a lot of QoL changes and then some. Unfortunately, these changes have come a little too late as now there's hardly anyone playing this game so it's very hard to find ANY matches. Spectating lobbies only allow up to 3 people (room host can decide to spectate and host a spectate only room). This update was shadow dropped and was never advertised to the people who bought the game so no one probably knows it's up. The 4:3 screen ratio is also added but if you play in ranked matches, the game will default to the 16:9 ratio.On Playstation, PS4 arcade sticks now work on the PS5 version (BOUT TIME).Overall, the updates have been okay and need but they just came too late. So with that being said, I'll change my review verdict but it probably won't change how everyone else feels about this title as of now. In its current state, the game is worth picking up but to some degree but with no one playing online, I wouldn't bother unless you want to support the devs or have the game in your collection.-----::: ORIGINAL REVIEW :::I'm sorry but I'm not going to hold back on this review because there is some stuff that needs to be said and the devs need to get their $#!t together and stop these kinds of practices and players need to call them out on their BS. With that being said, let's talk about "The Rumble Fish 2"The Rumble Fish 2 is a port of an arcade game that came out back in 2005 and has never seen a home release on any console or system until now. This is wonderful....finally we all get to play this wonderful classic while supporting the devs.....if only it was that simple. This port is bad....hella bad......VERY BAD....FFS IT'S SO GAWD AWFUL that it gives other bad "ports" from other developers a run for their money. Barebones doesn't even describe this game and it gives the meaning to "barebones" a whole new meaning when you compare this to modern day fighting game ports. What you get in this port are the following modes:- Modes -ArcadeSurvivalTime AttackVersus (both for local & online)TrainingGalleryRankingOptionsThese are your staple modes in any fighting game. Cool....but this is where it ends. There are so many glaring issues with this game that you can't give the devs a pass for this by allowing them to say their going to "patch" fixes in when this crap should have been in the game "DAY 1". Here are things you need to know that are going to be "patched" into the game:1. There is no online lobbies or spectator mode for online play.2. There is no replay mode to view your previous matches3. There are no practice mode options4. The game is stuck in a 16:9 full screen ratio when it's originally 4:3 in the arcade version. This screws over a lot of characters over that rely on wall bounces for their combos. Those combos are now useless since the wall is farther out5. No keyboard movement binding support for those who don't have controllers (PC Only)6. There is no option for rematches. After a fight, you go straight to the game over screen and do it all over again (WTF!?)7. Not being able to see the ping of the opponent you're facing against online nor the option to deny a match with said person.8. There is no Legacy Control support for console versions of this game (I have the PS5 version also and I can't use my Quanba Dragon arcade stick on it since it's a PS4 stick - Playstation 5 Console Only Issue)(I need verification for Xbox)9. For the Playstation players, There is no cross-platform purchase option for this game on consoles. If you buy one version and want the other, you'll need to pay another $29 for whichever version you want (this was my mistake when I bought the PS5 version and found that I couldn't use my Quanba arcade stick on it). The DLC is the only thing that's cross-platform purchaseable.Truth be told, the PS2 version of The Rumble Fish 1 seems more complete than this version and it has no online play so that's telling. The kicker to all of this is the following which EVERYONE is pissed about:"The 3 unlockable bosses are locked behind a paywall. They're DLC which totals around $12. This is such a greedy part on the devs because these characters are unlocked either by code (on the Atomiswave version) or by default (on the Nesica version). There is no other way to get them other than paying for them."I want to love this game, I really do and after having to wait for so long for a home version only to be greeted with a "NOT EVEN BAREBONES" & cash grab version of a game, there is no way in heck that I can recommend this port to anyone.....let alone my friends. Even if they do patch everything in, it doesn't make up for allowing this to be released as is to the public. With that being said, if you want a better gaming experience with this title, I implore everyone to go play on FIGHTCADE rather than this disaster of a release.3goo (never heard of this publisher till now) and DIMPS should be frickin ashamed of themselves for this BS release. <_<

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so this is based on my first impressions, I am familiar with Dimp's other fighting game Street fighter 4. So I went into this one thinking it had the same type of gameplay. Safe to say it isn't a street fighter if i had to compare it's more akin to a king of fighters. 4 buttons with bonus options for quick inputs (like 2 punches or 2 kicks). The gameplay is 2000s fighting game, a specific kind of jank I both love and understand has its limitations. The character models are very detailed which kinda makes them a bit uncanny against the kinda static backgrounds. Again I am aware this is an older game that has been ported so I wasnt expecting anything too extensive. What I like:Game has a sense of style and all the characters fill their respective fighting game "functions"I love the music, its up beat and very... mid 2000s? I feel like I am saying that a lotWhat I would like to see:More graphics options would be nice, as right now there is full screen or alt+enter window. That being said you can click and drag the window size but thats a bit odd to do for graphics options in 2023Also overall quality settings in the graphics would be welcomed. _childDocuments_.review: The game's alright. And that's most I can say about it. Is it worth 30 bucks? Yes and no. Yes, if you're into Rumble Fish and want to support its official release in the West, or just like fighting games a lot. After all, it is a very solid fighting game with unique mechanics, art-style and sound design.But then again, it's not worth the 30 if you're unfamiliar with this title and don't know if its accessible enough for you. The mechanics are unique and difficult to master. With that being said, there's lot of difficulty options so that the AI will be fit for your skills. I have a feeling the online won't be blooming with players, so buying this for online play alone is not recommended.With that being said though, the game offers lot of different offline modes for solo play or for couch versus with a friend.And that's something they definitely improved for this modernized version of Rumble Fish 2. The original was an arcade release exclusively and had no game-modes outside of the arcade mode. Here you have all kinds of stuff to play, and with online Rollback net-code too. On top of that you unlock some never-before-seen concept art that you can view in Gallery. I think this gives players nice incentive to go and play through the arcade with each character.. Assuming that the player has interest over the lore and the character designs.It's a solid release of the original, with some changes and additions that definitely add to the experience in terms of quality of life. Personally, having played the original releases and enjoying them thoroughly, I'll recommend this purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: (EDIT 1/5/2024 - Changed to Positive)I'm glad to say that finally, with the addition of sidebars, all of the big outstanding issues with this port have been solved. I would now fully recommend playing this game via the Steam port for any fighting game fan. The lack of an expansive story mode or anything of the like might still be a sticking point for a casual fan, but it's a truly excellent fighting game finally done the justice it deserves.Bonus points to 3goo for their more recent communication not having the same condescending tone as they did initially. Their developer response on my review got my hopes up, and they delivered in full.My original negative review as of 7/13/2023 is left mostly intact as follows below, but **please keep in mind that many of these older issues have been addressed!** For instance, TRF1 is now available on Steam with online play, as a better port than the original LRG-exclusive port, and you can now play on keyboard if you so choose.=====An update launched that addressed some of the many issues. Crucially, the online play appears to have lobbies now, fixing what is probably the biggest overall problem with this port. Additionally, the original 4:3 version's wall distances are now available in the options as "combat range: short" but with no sidebars, still displayed in 16:9, with bizarre invisible walls following the characters around. Not ideal, but at least the resolution concern was acknowledged in some way.But the fact is that resolution issues make this a straight-up useless port for competitive players, and the premium price point (with chunks ripped out and sold as DLC) make it a poor choice for casual players. On top of that I don't have a lot of faith in the developer of this port, and I'll tell you why.To any longtime fighting game fan, every issue with this port is something we'd already learned from the history of the genre. We've HAD wack ports with problematic widescreen modes and even ones that behave like this port's new "short" option, way back in 2008, and they were all rightly derided every single time.The developer's messages addressing all the patently obvious shortcomings of this port are transparent lies covering up "we made this on the cheap and we knew it wasn't gonna be a big hit so we're gouging the ones who do buy it."See also: porting TRF1 as well without any new features, but locking it away behind the purchase of a Limited Run Games collectors edition.See also: not having keyboard controls because they wanted to "preserve the arcade feel."See also: ripping out characters to sell as DLC because it's just like when the arcade operator had to put in codes to unlock the bosses.TLDR, as I see it, the market for porting an old fighting game that never came to the home market is two kinds of people:1) hardcore fighting game fans who want to play it competitively, for whom this is useless.2) casual fighting game fans, who would just be getting an barebones port of the arcade version.If it's fixed up to be useful for the hardcore fans, it'll still be overpriced and barebones.If it's not fixed, you're just being ripped off.Given how good the core fighting game here is and how little availability it's had historically, that's a crying shame.

_childDocuments_.review:
At the close of the 20th century... A large-scale natural disaster struck the eastern area of a certain country. The disaster wiped out the financial sector and toppled high-rise buildings over a wide area, even as far as the main functions of the capital. This resulted in the loss of a staggering 158,000 lives.

At the dawn of the 21st century... Conglomerate PROBE-NEXUS, commonly known as Probe, begins reconstruction efforts in the eastern area of said country. Probe relocates its own base of operations to the ruined sector and builds a massive city run by the corporation. Lavished with colossal capital and cutting-edge technology, the modern-day Babylon is made up of skyscrapers that put the old high-rises to shame, the biggest shopping mall in the world, and recreational facilities one might mistake for a theme park.

This was the dazzling birth of a symbol for the new century. It became the most essential place on the planet and was christened Zone Prime.

The Rumble Fish is a 2D fighting game. The arcade version was developed in 2004. The arcade version of The Rumble Fish 2 came out in 2005, introducing new game mechanics and characters. It gained popularity with its sleek 2D visuals powered by S.M.A. (Smooth Model Animation), fascinating characters and strategic gameplay using 2 types of gauges.

name: Return to Monkey Island
detailed_description: Return to Monkey Island is an unexpected, thrilling return of series creator Ron Gilbert that continues the story of the legendary adventure games The Secret of Monkey Island and Monkey Island 2: LeChuck’s Revenge developed in collaboration with Lucasfilm Games. It’s been many years since Guybrush Threepwood was last locked in a battle of wits with his nemesis, the zombie pirate LeChuck. His true love, Elaine Marley, has turned her focus away from governing and Guybrush himself is adrift and unfulfilled, having never found the Secret of Monkey Island. Hip, young pirate leaders led by Captain Madison have shuffled the old guard from power, Melee Island has taken a turn for the worse, and famed businessman Stan has been imprisoned for ‘marketing-related crimes’. Banter with old friends and new faces on familiar islands now under dangerous new leadership. Then, take to the high seas and explore the new and unknown as you work your way out of tough predicaments. Clever puzzles, bizarre situations, and devastating ripostes are all that stand between Guybrush and glory. Return to Point & Click Swashbuckling Bringing classic point and click gameplay to the modern-day, intrepid pirates will solve puzzles and explore the islands with a clever evolution of classic adventure game controls. Context-sensitive interactions, reactive dialog trees, and an easy-to-use inventory system make pirating a breeze. Embark on Archipelago Adventures Navigate the sometimes-friendly confines of Melee Island, a familiar place that finds itself under new management by leaders who have put the squeeze on old friends and new faces. Venture out into uncharted lands like the aptly named Terror Island and the chilling outposts of Brrr Muda to make allies and enemies alike. Created by a Legendary Crew The new chapter in the Monkey Island series marks the return of the iconic series’ creator Ron Gilbert, joined by game co-writer Dave Grossman, art director Rex Crowle (Knights & Bikes, Tearaway) and composers Peter McConnell, Michael Land, and Clint Bajakian (Monkey Island, Monkey Island 2: LeChuck’s Revenge).

_childDocuments_.review: It's more Monkey Island, and it has the most Murray of any Monkey Island game to date! Storybook art is a little different from prior iterations, but it works well and still has lots of character.Update: Having finished the game, I can say the ending will be a bit divisive. I thought it worked fine, and depending on your actions in the last act, it can actually play out in a couple majorly different ways, and in several different flavors on top of that. If you're used to thinking these sorts of games are on rails and you're railroaded into "the one" ending, experiment a bit - you may be pleasantly surprised.This ties into one of the other fun bits that's new to the series - there's many things you can do that aren't actually required to advance the game, but unlock achievements and change the experience a bit along the way. I won't spoil any of them, but definitely play around with stuff - there's several little moments where you're rewarded for forward-thinking and experimenting.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing return to the good ol' Monkey Island games. _childDocuments_.review: For a lot of people the original Monkey Island titles mean a lot. And for the game industry as a whole, not just the adventure titles, these games have had (and still have) a lot of influence. For me? I respect them and admire them, but the first time I’ve actually completed the first two entries was only after the Special Editions came out a bit over 10 years ago. I did encounter these titles as a kid, of course, but had far more experience with other LucasArts titles and adventures from other companies. The first game in the franchise I’ve completed was actually Tales from Monkey Island and I’ve still never bothered to play Escape and Curse.Why is this important? Well, it is undeniable that your enjoyment from Return to Monkey Island will depend greatly on your experience with the previous games. But what I can say for sure, is that if I’m anything to go by – you can still have a lot of fun with this game, even if you don’t know the classic titles by heart.Another important thing to establish, is that this title was designed, directed and co-written by Ron Gilbert – the creator of the series and one of the key developers of the first two entries, who left LucasArts in the 90s and hasn’t been involved with any of the sequels. So even though this game is well aware that it’s the sixth entry in the series, it has most similarities with the first two.Though, gameplay-wise, it surprisingly completely goes away with the classic selection of verbs – in the classic LucasArts games you always had a number of verbs-actions that you could choose to perform on an object or person. It was kind of a re-imagining of the classic text-based adventure approach with the text parser, where the designers got rid of complex constructions and kept just the most important verbs available as a selection the player can make. Even later LucasArts titles, despite simplifying the list of actions even further, kept the concept alive. Yet, Return doesn’t have even the most common modern approach, with “left click to do contextual action, right click to examine” and makes all interactions entirely contextual.This means that some objects may have two interaction options (and interestingly, the options are usually swapped – right click for action, left for examining), some may have just one, some may have one until examined, some may have one that changes many times… It’s entirely dependent on the object or a person what you can or cannot do, comment, examine, muse about. Strangely enough, even though it does mean that puzzles will have a more hands on approach, as you don’t need to juggle 10 different verb actions that can all be potentially correct, it not only doesn’t hurt the flow of the game, it mostly improves it. At least – if you like the adventuring bits, not the puzzle bits of these types of games.Oh and yeah, what type of point and click adventure game Return to Monkey Island even is? Because in the modern market, adventure titles are usually heavily leaning into specific niches, pushing boundaries in a specialized way – be it new ways of telling a story, or creating a feeling of freeform investigation, or being a puzzle-focused title, or whatever else it may be. But Return does feel more like a classic 90s adventure game from LucasArts, for better and for worse. On one hand, it means that this title is about just having fun and adventuring, looking at cool visual style and laughing at the jokes. On the other hand, it does mean that logical consistency, “good” storytelling and truly engaging story take a back seat and you will pick up and carry around items, because you can, not because it makes sense to do it.It’s hard to pull off a game, where it’s more fun to “hang out” with the game, rather than consider it a completed narrative or gameplay-driven experience. But luckily Return has enough charm to do it well enough. How well – that’s where that previous experience with the series comes into play. For people in love with the franchise, it’s probably an especially exciting and touching experience. For people who don’t have any emotional ties to the previous entries, it’s a jolly good time with lots of laughs and some occasional hiccups. Most of which are, luckily, easily overcome with the fantastic built-in hint book that I didn’t use as much as I expected based on my experience with the original titles.There are a few oddities, though. The game has several settings that will impact your experience that are quite uncommon for games in general. For one – there’s a difficulty setting that makes some sections/problems to solve more complex. I’ve decided to play on Hard and enjoyed most of my time with it, but there were a couple of puzzles that felt a bit too convoluted that seem to have been simplified on the easier mode. That said, some of the puzzles seem to be less fun on easy and some make less sense. Another option is to enable a “Writer’s cut” in the options which, apparently, adds more optional dialogues and even more encounters with the characters in the game. Which I didn’t have on and not sure if enabling it would’ve made it better or could make the pacing too slow.In general, Return to Monkey Island really is a fun silly adventure game. It has weaker moments, it has annoying gross-out humour that I never liked, it does feel a bit too personal and meta-commentary at times, something that might mean something to people who love the series, but to me felt recognizable but pointless. But it is pretty fun and good. Oh and also it apparently has some new game plus elements too, which is unexpected from the genre. But the genre is called “adventure game” and Return to Monkey Island sure is an adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Monkey Island since I was 2 years old. I named my first dog Mêlée. My wedding cake was built to look like Mêlée Island. In short, I have strong feelings about this series, and to get another outing some 30 years later with the same heart, wit, and humor as the original games AND a much smoother, more accessible interface is nothing short of a dream. This is a good, good game, genuinely, with clever puzzles, a really clever built-in hint system that you can easily choose to use or ignore, references for longtime players, hooks for new players, and an aesthetically pleasing world worth deep exploration. Completely charming, warm without being cheesy, sharp without being overly cynical. I am restored on a spiritual level and also I really want limes.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what to say about this game. It kind of had it all. It was a worthy successor of the Monkey Island series - although it felt a bit sad to play at the same time. I got very nostalgic and felt quite old. It reminded me of all the time that has passed and I suppose this was the intentions from the creators. I love how the came connected all the previous five game in one or another way since I was afraid they would just continue from where MI2 ended and ignore all the other games. CMI is still my favorite game of all times, but this was totally as good as all the other MI games.A plus was the in-game hint book. Then there was no need of googling outside the game and spoil unnecessary details.As an extremely big MI fan, this get 10/10 from me - but I got kind of more happy by the other games, this made me a bit sad - but in a good way. It's hard to explain, buy it and play it!

_childDocuments_.review: A well written adventure that both takes you back to what made the first games great, while the humor holds up and is funny on its own.Puzzles are a bit on the easy side even in hard mode, and to me the ending was a bit of a dissapoitment, not because its not what i expected, but because it didnt feel fleshed out enough.All and all, a very fitting addition to the adventures of guybrush threepwood.

_childDocuments_.review: While I love the return to form for a Monkey Island game, I can only recommend it to die-hard Monkey Island fans. The latter chapters feel rushed. The collectables are frustratingly stupid in how they're handled. The achievements are monotonously specific. The ending is downright lazy and BAD. Recommended for franchise fans only.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Once again we get an absolute gem of a game.It has everything the original Monkey Island games had: Puzzles, fun, amazing dialogues and a great story.Unfortunately there were tons of haters before the game was even released complaining about the art style while calling themselves "true Monkey Island fans".Well, the game is here and it feels like true Monkey Island.Once again I can relive that amazing experience I missed so much in point and click games.The game is an absolute gem.Yes, the art style is different and yes, everyone has their own taste in art. But the game is 100% Monkey Island and people that hate about the art, probably never understood what makes Monkey Island so amazing.If you're one of these haters, don't play the game, it's just not for you. Go buy some crazy 4K DLSS Raytracing graphics festival and make your 3090 sweat hard.But if you actually ARE a true Monkey Island fan, don't wait any longer! Get it and play it. You won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: The series has become way more sanitized and childish with this one I feel.This would be something I'd try to play with my own child, and he or she would probably get crazy bored with within ten minutes, as would I. I don't really enjoy the humor, every gag is predictable and also mostly pretty lame.It tries to play the nostalgia card, but that one never worked for me. I still want a good game.I also don't enjoy the artstyle.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Return to Monkey Island felt like the embrace of an old friend. I'm nearly 40, and the early games were some of my earliest gaming memories. While I "enjoyed" the other games in the series beyond the first two, they never felt quite right to me. Return feels "right" in all the best possible ways.The new art style is gorgeous and a perfect companion to the original Pixel Art. The music is beautiful, and the puzzles are some of the best non "moon logic" puzzles I've seen come from an adventure game, let alone the LucasFilm Games alumni. By the time I the game had ended I had caught feelings, so they say, and even now, hours later I'm still sitting with it.Monkey Island has always meant a lot to me. And this game, whether it is the last in the series or the start of something new and beautiful, was a tremendous entry into that legacy.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Sure this game can be divisive, but to be frank, just the fact that it exists makes me happy.Is that its greatest merit then, just to exist? No. I feel its mostly divisive because it makes BIG choices.Some of them are bold, but all of them fit the Monkey Island mold. Unlike some stuff in Tales of Monkey Island or Escape from Monkey Island which felt (totally) out of place. This game is a genuine and lovingly made Monkey Island game. It also recaptures the extra Ron Gilbert cynical madness that slightly left the series over the years, as he stopped working on them.Return strikes a great balance between nostalgia, easter eggs, nods to old jokes, fresh ideas and new/returning characters and overall is still one of the few genuinely funny games out there. The puzzles where challenging enough, but never obscure or frustrating. With the hint system in place, which a seasoned player wouldn't need, maybe some puzzles could be a bit more challenging. (I played on harder difficulty) Whatever you may think of the choice of art style, a lot of the expressive animations and drizzles of details happening on every aspect of the screen where awe inspiring. So much was "brought to life" on every scene, it amazed even when compared to way more tech-advanced games. I'd spend a few minutes regularly just to check it out. The music is also great, again a wonderful remix of the familiar and the new. The delivery of the voice acting is spot on, as always in the monkey island games. I guess its an age thing as well, as time goes on and there is less time to play a game and truely enjoy it, Return to Monkey Island was one of the games that makes me glad I still play a few real gems now and again.As far as a recommendation goes then:  100% recommended, like the first 3 games is part of a series that shaped what videogames can be and have become.  AHOY!

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time MI fan (played the original back in the 90's) this was a lot of fun.  The writing was clever and the puzzles nice. Over all I am very glad it came out and that I could play it.But I have two major gripes with it.  First the art style is god awful.  I usually do not have a problem with art style changes or weird art designs but this one specifically just is bad to me.  I am no stranger to images of an art style looking way worse than the art when in motion and suspected this was going to be the case again.  Plenty of things I've enjoyed where the art looked bad in previews but was fine once you got into it.  Not this one.  The second and far worse gripe though is the ending.  I was aware it had a bad ending but I didn't expect it to actually make me upset.  I was completely on the side of the devs and want to encourage them to tell the story they want to tell.  I usually can groan through an ending I didn't like and still enjoy the journey.  This ending just rubbed me so wrong I almost regret playing it.  Spoilers ahead:I didn't care what the secret was.  I would have laughed digging up that shirt.  It was the story of Guybrush and LeChuck that I was engrossed in.  But that story was completely abandoned.  A whole three way stand off against the pirate leaders, LeChuck, and Guybrush could have given me a nice finale to the story the game told to that point.  Instead just chucking the plot in the garbage to end on the Carnival joke again actually irritated me.    As time goes on and I digest it more, that is the thing that is sticking with me.  The interesting story it was telling was just thrown away for a gag.  I fear that will be my main point when I think back on this game, my sense of severe frustration and disappointment.   I try to remind myself of the fun getting there but it's being overshadowed...

_childDocuments_.review: is the first computer game my parents bought for me, and I’ve been a  fan since. So when Ron Gilbert and Dave Grossman, two of the designers of the first game, announced that they’ve been working on a new  title in secret (pun intended), I was absolutely elated. I knew then that  was not to be missed. did not disappoint. While the game’s story is set after the events of , and references characters and events of previous games, it’s written in such a way that you can treat this game as the direct sequel to  should you choose to do so. Gilbert and Grossman’s flexibility with adhering to series’ canon allows you to enjoy this game regardless of your opinions of the  titles that followed . It’s hard to review  without spoiling the little, surprising bits that make the game special. I loved how the game’s prelude ended with a twist  before transitioning to the proper tale. The setup of Guybrush’s return to Monkey Island being an embedded narrative informs the game’s artistic design. I really appreciate the chosen art style. While the character designs may look simple at first glance, the characters are drawn to emote effectively when the occasion calls for it.The story of  is an allegory: it pokes fun of recent events, reflects on the creators’ and fans’ relationships with and memories of  games, and comments on some fans’ devotion to (or even obsession with) finding out the Secret of Monkey Island. One of my favourite bits in the game involves pirates refusing to eat lime . The way Gilbert and Grossman designed the ending of  truly showcases their intelligence, humour, and perceptiveness. I have no doubt they knew a segment of the  fan base will have things to say about how they told their story.I finished this game at Hard difficulty level so I can appreciate the game as the developers intended. The puzzles weren’t challenging to solve, though I did need a hint or two for a couple of them. They were well designed and made sense within the game world. I actually found puzzles in previous games to be trickier, so novice adventure gamers may want to give the Hard difficulty level a try. I also turned on the Writers’ Cut option for extra dialogues and jokes. Even with that option toggled, the story didn’t drag. If anything, it’s the fun side quest of finding trivia cards, and answering 100 questions about  games that hindered my progress.When I finished , I was happy, satisfied, yet slightly wistful. At my age, I found myself really connected to the narrator , who by extension represents Gilbert and Grossman.  is not just another entry in the  series – it’s a tale about  being nostalgic, returning to unfinished business, tempering expectations, and accepting reality. There’s a mature voice beneath all the witty writing in .Although I’d love for Gilbert and Grossman to make another  game,  feels like their swansong. If this were to be their last  game, I’m happy that they gave us this game. The series has become bigger than the original creators, and the door has been left open for future stories be told, whether by Gilbert and/or Grossman, or by other developers. With that, the legacy of  can live on. (Oooh, that’s a good title for the next game!)

_childDocuments_.review: Big, BIG monkey island fan here. Played the first game on my dad's amiga back in the 90s, and was a giant fan ever since.After playing this game, I was incredibly saddened- the game really pales in comparison to its predecessors (especially the first three) in so many ways; And not just via the graphics. I know there were a lot of complaints about the graphics in this game, and I was one of the people offput by them when I first saw the trailers as well, but I didn't let it bother me because monkey island is so much more than graphics- and to be honest, I kind of got used to the graphics after about 20 minutes in the game anyways.The biggest disappointment was that the monkey island writers never bothered to answer any questions or give the game series any sort of conclusion- I was SO happy to see Ron Gilbert back in the saddle, and was really hoping to get some kind of proper, Ron-Approved ending... but this game ends up not providing an ending at all, and it feels like the final answer to all of the wonder, hope, and lore that I was interested in was "The story is unimportant as long as you have fun". I was really insulted by that, since in most of the previous games, the world of monkey island felt so ALIVE.Looking at each of the islands you go to in this game- they all feel so EMPTY! Maybe 2-3 places per island, or location, and mostly a big expanse of nothing. Compare the locales of this game vs the islands of MI2, or MI3- like phatt island, scabb island, or Plunder Island... vs the vast empty islands of brr-muda, or terror island (which was a huge letdown). Even melee island had its locations cut in half from the first game, and what we did get was (mostly) empty! Stan's place on melee stood out to me as a great example of this - once a bright, colorful place with a ton of stuff to see and interesting ideas, vs a sad empty reminder of better times (with only two items to grab and no other interactions other than for guybrush to reminisce about older days). To me, that kind of sums up the game too- it's so empty and lifeless compared to previous games.Also, I really didn't like how many times they focused on hand shots. What was the need for a closeup of people's hands reaching out to exchange something? That was weird.Anyways, I did get the messages that the team were trying to send, and I also read the note at the end of the game, but as a long time fan, I was really saddened that we got no real closure or answers to all of the wonderful story that the writers had created in the past. It felt like they kind of just gave up on this wonderful gem of a series, and that's depressing.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this is a very enjoyable revisit of the classic series.  Is it worth the $25 purchase price? Yes and no.For me, I grew up with point-and-click adventures. I played MI4 with my parents when it came out, which made me revisit the originals when they came out with the remastered versions.  Return to Monkey Island captures the feel, nostalgia, and goofy logic puzzles of the original. With the original team on board, it was honestly a foregone conclusion this was going to be a joy to me - I have spent far more than $2.50/hour on nostalgia before.Now, if you haven't played the previous games... My husband, who really isn't the casual gamer type, heard my squeal of excitement when I saw this release. After listening patiently to me rant about how amazing this series is to me (as I was frantically throwing money at this now Disney owned game), I think he expected something above and beyond. About 20 minutes later he walked behind me, looked at the art, and said, "um, how much did you pay for this game?" As others have mentioned, the art is cheaply done. This might be a problem for some, but I think the cartoony style fits the series. The value in the series has always been the writing, puzzles, and where applicable, the voice acting. Did it meet those three requirements? For the writing, there is a setting to turn on a less edited version of the game. I enjoyed it, and didn't feel like the plot was too slow. For the voice acting - yes, absolutely spot on. For the puzzles... I certainly didn't feel cheated (especially with all the things to keep track of in Act IV), but some parts felt a little rushed, as if there was more planned that wasn't included, or as if they had an "Act" just to handle the change of scenery. However, compared to many of the more modern point and click adventures, certainly more complexity and enjoyment than those puzzles.So back to the question, is this game worth $25? If you enjoyed the original, 100%. If you are generally a fan of point and click adventures, or generally a fan of cartoony silliness in games, I'd also wager yes. If you're coming into this expecting something groundbreaking, you're about 32 years behind the curve.

_childDocuments_.review: Neat! But only for old time fans.Positive: the humor is still the same old silly stuff. the art style is a pretty unique mix of all Monkey Island titles - from DOS pixel art to ugly 3D. They also managed to stay true to certain character mannerism that already were there in part 1 (Stan's clothing texture for instance). It made me again appricate how insanely good part 1 and 2 were, with the limited resources back then. But I guess that's what made the old stuff so beautifully condensed - every frame a painting, because every pixel mattered. Negative: 'point and click' has died for a very good reason. It feels like a chore rather than fun or even challanging gameplay. The hint book is a nice idea but really making it even more obvious - when you have to include the cheat codes right into the game. At least the interface and general moveability is good - not a thing one can say about previous Monkey Island games.Hmm, I think it's one of those classic 'you had to be there' kind of things.If you grew up with crude but lovely 2D DOS games, it's a nice final point to the francise but that's about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just about old enough to have played Monkey Island (and other point and click games) the first time around. Though, because I was quite young at the time, the difficulty of the puzzles was often beyond me.Many, many years later, and finding myself somewhat disenchanted with the games industry of the present day, I was excited to get into this game and see what it had to offer.Disappointingly, though, what it has to offer is mostly nostalgia. On the plus side, the game runs exceptionally well and is basically jank-free, which was not something I remember being the case back in the day. But on the down side, the game adds basically nothing to the successful format, so many years after the genre peaked.Of course, its not completely fair to expect every game released to be pushing boundaries and evolving the nature of gameplay, but when you're using a gameplay loop from basically 30 years ago and adding nothing new to it, you perhaps disappoint some (but not all) of your audience. Personally, I found the tone and gameplay too childish and simplistic, considering how old I am now. And just like the original games, so of the solutions to puzzles just feel arbitrary; solving them can be attritional instead of logical.  Overall, I'm sure players of the original games will get something out of this one, but I definitely wouldn't recommend it to anyone else.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is a bit of a mixed bag for me. On the one hand, it was as enjoyable throughout and it kept me glued to my computer for a good 10.6 hours (Bedtime and walking my dog, took up a lot of that time). On the other hand, I'm pretty certain I found the Mass Effect 3 of Graphic Adventure Games...Despite not having played ME1-3, I've just heard a thing or two in web comics. Anyway, here's my hit-miss index.Hit: The callback to the second game's ending to introduce Guybrush's son before we see the man himself was a nice twist, the rest of the game was pretty great from story to puzzles.Miss: The framing device could've been used a little more sparingly, the narrative seems to have forgotten Herman Toothrot's story arc, no pay-off with the Voodoo Lady's overall role that was built up in Tales, and then there's the ending. I won't spoil the formula for those of you who haven't played the other games, but I as a fan expected better from this series than how they treated the final act! Worst of all (And this tore it for me), It's a Disney game! Not that I didn't expect that, but, I was hoping against hope this was going to be a separate project, given my current feelings towards modern Disney.In conclusion: My highest recommendation for this game, sadly, is to MI completionists, like me.

_childDocuments_.review: i grew up with Monkey Island 1 & 2. If I had to compose some kind of a list of my all time favorite games, they would likely be on it.Return to Monkey Island is not only a fantastic trip down memory lane but also holds its own as both an adventure game and a Monkey Island. I consider this Monkey Island 3.The humor, the puzzles, the dialogue, the characters, the over-all MI feel - it´s all there.Fantastic game. Not to be missed by any adventure game fan, old or new.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game was excellent, the story was even better than expected. I love the puzzles; they were so well thought out! My only gripe was with the art design of the character's faces; it was too abstract for my personal preference. It had me laughing at the end, wow the ending was so great, it was so realistic and funny! I love Return to Monkey Island, and I am looking forward to the next game already!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write a ton of reviews, but as a fan of the Monkey Island series since I was a child (30 years ago), I had to play this one, and was not disappointed.  Very rarely can a point and click goofy adventure game make you think and feel nostalgic like this one.  And go one step further to even make you question your nostalgia.  And whether or not the end goal was even worth it, or was it the journey?  And extremely great, and most likely final entry to the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Has a clear goal of making this game accessible to the mainstream. They have two levels of difficulty, so people can choose the puzzle difficulty, but even on hard mode, you are very strongly led towards the correct path so you never are unsure what your goal is or where you are trying to go. The game even comes with its own hint book, which I never used, but there were several times I spent a LONG time trying to figure out the puzzle. A complete lack of moon logic, so you can probably figure it out if you just try everything possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen this game through, and although at first I didn't like the art style, I've chosen to ignore it and play with an open mind. I'll concede that eventually it showed some charm, but as I played on, I wasn't convinced by the story, the characterization (Guybrush was never a sociopath, and yet in this game he has more in common with Rufus from Deponia than his previous more good-natured iterations) and some of the puzzles that felt repetitive or out of place. But I pressed on, because we'd finally get to see the story to conclusion and learn what the secret of Monkey Island was all about, right? Instead all we got was a meta ending that, personally, left me unfulfilled. This was not worth thirty years of waiting for me, but subjectivity plays a role in all of the above. Oh, and I also had to borrow a computer that supports DirectX 12 to even launch this, because apparently the game's groundbreaking 2D graphics couldn't be handled by lower API levels (or the developers were just lazy and didn't bother to make it compatible with graphics cards older than 6 years or so). The only plus side is that the music is fantastic, although it's mostly due to the fact that they tend to be covers of beloved tunes from the first two games, rearranged by the original composers.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely homage to the earlier games and an overall almost perfect point-and-click adventure game.The puzzles are great, the dialogue is well written and the music is perfect fitting.However, the inventory might get a bit clustered with a lot of stuff to pick up and the artstyle is not for everyone.You should not let that avert you from this gem of a game though.Welcome back Guyrbrush! We've missed you so much!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked it.The puzzles all made sense to me besides maybe 2 or so which isn't too much of a problem if you're using the hint book.The ending dragged on just a little bit for me.But other than that I thoroughly enjoyed it. It is funny, nostalgic and just a good time - just the way you remember the series to be.I would give it a 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: So going into Return of Monkey Island I was hoping to see that same sort of humor, storytelling, clever inventory puzzles, and witty dialog as previous games. I got none of that. The humor was incredibly lackluster, a few lines got a tiny "heh" chuckle while many previous games, especially Curse of Monkey Island were fantastic and had me rolling with laughter. One of the most fun things you could do in the older games was getting unique responses from Guybrush or other characters when you combined something wrong or showed the wrong thing to people. In this game you CAN'T even combine them wrong, the game just has a big X over combinations that won't work.As far as the storytelling, none of the new characters were fun or interesting, the returning ones had minimal dialog and nothing really stoodd out with no memorable or quoteable lines. Whilr I still to this day can remember many great lines from Secret and Curse, as well as almost every insult sword fighting response.The returning voice actors did a good job with a lackluster script. However the new voice actors for Stan and LeChuck don't come even CLOSE to the quality they had in Curse and the remasters of Secret of Monkey Island and LeChuck's Revenge.The graphics, I have to talk about them. After how gorgeous the pixelized version of the hand drawn marker art from Secret and LeChuck's Revenge were, or the hand painted cell art of Curse. This game's graphics feel like a lazy insult to the series. They don't even hold up to the 3d models of Tales of Monkey Island. They at BEST look like a indie game made in a year by 3 people. Not like the 6th game in a long running series made by supposed industry veterans over a multi year period.Plot spoilers, but I doubt it matters since the plot is so bad. The main plot feels really weak and contrived, the game both pretends like it starts right after LeChuck's Revenge, then says "nope we are just kidding, that ending is still nonsense, Guybrush's kid is playing it out as a pretend scenario, and getting it wrong" The main plot is told by Guybrush on a bench to his kid after this. It slowly drags without being funny or interesting. When you finally get to the last part of the game, you find out the secret of monkey island was actually a giant box. But when you open it, it's just a map back to Monkey Island. So you go back down below the island. It is then during the ending where the game falls apart completely. It acts like it's building to something, then just STOPS, after acting like this was going to be some big reveal after all this time of what the Secret of Monkey Island is, Guybrush walks through into a REALLY crappy looking diorama theme park and turns the power off and leaves. THAT'S IT! The game developers might as well have said "we just did this to cash in and don't give a crap, so why should you? Oh you wanted a good game after all this time and hype? HAHAHAHAHAHA Suckers! We got your money. So go screw yourself."All in all this game is an insult to fans of the series, I would HIGHLY recommend not playing it as it is by FAR the worst of the 6. If you are new to the series, Play the MUCH MUCH better Secret of Monkey Island, and if you like that play LeChuck's Revenge, then the wonderful Curse of Monkey Island.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: well done you guys!  this ticks all the nostalgia boxes,  has the same quirky comedy, the same goofy charm.  and the new art style is great!  fantastic voice acting, sounded so similar to the og.  i even caught a bunch of feels in the end.  AND it's got some great QoL stuff for a PnC game.  like the dialogue rewinds, or the double click run, or the recap if you don't play for a bit.  and chievos!  i loved every moment.  if u are an oldschool Monkey Island fan, pick this one up!  they did awesome
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Classic flavor; the dialogues in the line of the first two Monkey Island. The controversial (for some) art design complies perfectly and doesn't take you out of the game at any time. In fact some of the backgrounds reminded me of Day of the Tentacle or Sam & Max Hit the Road, so in the end the design was not so far from other similar products of the time. For me it's a YES. Buy it, enjoy it. The puzzles are 100% frustration free. If you played the previous games it will bring back many pleasant memories. Just released and already an instant classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great adventure game, and a great addition to the Monkey Island saga. The game sprinkles in a good dose of MI nostalgia, without falling in cheesy cliches. Its puzzles are smart (particularly on Hard mode) and logical, meaning you'll never get stuck in a place for very long.The graphics, which came under intense scrutiny before release, I found very charming; they work! LeChuck looks amazing, and so do the other ghosts/demons of his crew. The environments also look great, and so do dynamic objects like flames. The only thing I didn't like about the new graphics is unfortunately Guybrush's face! I understand they wanted to achieve a Guybrush-esque goofy look, but maybe they went a bit too far. The ending of course will have people talking and criticising, but I liked its maturity as Guybrush has clearly learnt the important things in life.... or has he?
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Friends, this is not just a game. This is a love letter. A love letter to the entire monkey island series, crafted with great care and affection and respect for everything that has been done concerning this series.And even if you don't know monkey island, this game is very much worth it. It has a metric tonne of references to the old games, but it's also a fun game in and of itself, providing fun puzzles in a swashbuckling way.Finally. Elaine is the best character in monkey island. Change my mind, you can't.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Very short version is that Ron Gilbert overall still has it (applies to Thimbleweed Park as well). There's still certain feel that other adventure games have. It just that he has gotten older, which is thematically present in this game. As for the ending, .As for the art, you'll probably get used to it. Some scenes kind of look nice because of the fitting color scheme for the scene. Store page has plenty of examples if you haven't seen the screenshots and videos already. I would like bit more of the Monkey Island 3 style, but in higher resolution. But I guess it's impossible to please everybody. Puzzle design is mostly OK. Dialog even has some hints. For the cases where the puzzle seems bit too obtuse, there's integrated hint system. The book glows in the inventory inviting you to open it...I feel like in overall puzzle design is bit easier than the old ones at cost of having the bit more clever puzzles that some like in the old ones. In summary, if you don't get hung on that things are not like they used to and enjoy Ron Gilberts writing in general, Return to Monkey Island is good fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: If you are as old as i am and grew up with monkey island, then this is a wonderful, fun and entertaining trip down memory lane. But even if you haven't played the older games (which i recommend), then you are still left with a solid Adventure, even if you'll miss out on a lot of little references and jokes to the previous titles.The puzzles are solid, difficulty was (for me) just right and for the 11 hours it took me to finish the game the price is absolutely justified. I haven't encountered a single bug, the sounddesign is great, the graphics.. well.. not my cup of tea to be honest, but it fits the vibe of the story and i got used to it within minutes. Return to Monkey Island gave me a great weekend. And that's all (and more than) i wished for.
