_childDocuments_.review: I played Monkey Island 1 and 2 when they were new, loved Curse but always wondered where Gilbert and Grossman would've gone with their version of 3. This is not that game, but it would be weird to make that game now -- instead, this is an exploration of the themes of what Monkey Island 2's ending was doing, and a unification of all the different storytelling styles in Secret, Revenge, Curse, Escape, and Tales. For me, it was a perfect capstone on the "uncertain reality" aspect to the series, while leaving room to tell further stories -- or to simply imagine them, if this ends up being the finale. I loved it.Mechanically, it was the easiest Monkey Island game for me, but part of that was due to some smart choices in the UI and travel systems. Backtracking is as painless as it's ever been, and the interface is as simple as it's ever been, for better and worse. You can highlight interactable objects on the background, get a text description of what interacting with them will do, and most notably, instantly see whether using an item on them is possible by hovering the item over them. This reduces the number of "I can't use these two things together" type responses, but also cuts short a ton of experimentation and shows you a lot of red-slashed-circle icons. It's not my favorite, but I got used to it over time.I think my series ranking at this point would be something like: 1/2 > 3 > 6 >>> 5 >>>>>>> 4.This isn't my favorite Monkey Island, but it made me appreciate the many different approaches this series has taken, and treats them all with respect. I had a great time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This was pure nostalgia for me but with a fresh art style and awesome soundtrack. It still retains the wit of the first three. (I haven't played 4 or 5.) What was the most fun for me was solving puzzles for the first time as I played the others multiple times and the puzzles are just a formality at this point. I loved the inclusion of collectible trivia cards and the achievements. I am about to start my attempt at the Speed Runner Achievement. I feel like I have been doing this for years with the other games. This is already an instant classic and I highly recommend it to everyone. If you love point and click adventure games with fun puzzles and well written humor, this game is for you! And the secret was, in fact, the friends we made along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun, very much in the spirit of earlier Ron Gilbert led projects, with a fair bit of meta commentary. Puzzles are a bit on the simple side, but still are entertaining. The voice acting is terrific, with Dominic Armato knocking it out of the park as per usual. If you're a fan of the other MI games, particularly 1 and 2, you'll enjoy this just for the number of callbacks and references alone. Is it a good conclusion to the series? That's going to be very much up to the individual, but for me I feel it's appropriate.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I'm a huge Monkey Island fan, I've played every iteration and consider MI2 to be my favourite game of all time.  I was very excited to play this new adventure, and while it was enjoyable, I'm hesitantly giving it a thumbs-up, as I mostly found it to be pretty mediocre.The puzzles are way too easy, and part of that fault rests on the control system; with a maximum of two actions for every item, there isn't nearly enough to experiment with.  I finished the game easily on "hard" mode without using any hints, and pretty much every puzzle solution was rote and obvious; tasks are basically spoon-fed to the player by way of a to-do list, which makes them a monotonous chore.  Certain "puzzles" are repeated for no reason other than seemingly just to pad the length of the game, requiring revisiting the same locations over and over.  Fan-service is fine, but became gratuitous due to how many locations are pulled from previous games in the series.  The dialog is decent, but merely elicits the occasional smirk rather than a proper guffaw. It's all a bit re-hashed and ho-hum.With that said, the voice acting is fantastic, the music is expectedly wonderful (though not much different from previous games), and while the artwork is divisive, it's colourful and whimsical, and I didn't find it distracting (other than Guybrush's nose looking like a flaccid member).  It's a good casual time-waster but I don't really feel like it's worth the full price I paid for it.  Maybe wait for it to go on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Although I'm only just into Chapter 2 this game is easily worth recommending. It's almost like a love letter to the original games. It follows on directly from Monkey Island 2, while still recognising the other games as well and i does so in a way I never would have thought of and one that makes perfect sense as well.The interface is simple and easy to use and I love the new art style as well. It's no as "flat" as it looks in screenshots, but actually has light that reflects off characters and and scenery and everything is bright and colourful. Sound is excellent as well, with top notch voice acting and music which will be familiar to fans of the series. Speaking of which, there are so many easter eggs to be found here that fans will instantly remember.Puzzles are interesting. Simple, yet challenging and with two difficuly modes and hidden trivia cards to find, there's plenty to go back for too.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: An ode to growing old and wiser but also about missing the dreams and the vigor of youth. Game is brimming with nostalgia of course, and is made much better if you've played 1 & 2 in particular. (And why wouldn't you have??)The humor remains great, and I LOL'ed IRL quite a few times, there's one particular reference to the pandemic (which the team faced during dev) that's just pure genius.Adventure-game-wise it's very solid, no puzzles that are too cryptic or far-fetched and there's even a progressive in-game hint system which really should just be an industry standard going forward.The acting is great and the music is as delicious as expected, and the art style ends up working great, although I had my qualms with it to start.It is indeed short, but when your only criticism is that something is short it's because it's good, as I always say. Also the price tag matches its brevity.So turns out the Toybox isn't Terrible after all, here's to hoping for many more games from Ron & Co!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I played all Monkey Island games several times. Did I liked this one? Yes! Is this better than the original Monkey Island 3, the "Curse of Monkey Island"? No, it's different. Even if Ron Gilbert did not work on "Curse of Monkey Island", that game is still amazing nowadays. "Return to Monkey Island" is an hommage to the saga, a third and closing chapter to the original Monkey Island 1 and 2. The art direction is nice and the jokes are still there, but I disliked few things:- It's pretty easy, probably the easiest of the serie. I finished it in just 6 hours. - The atmosphere and musics are too calm and not as expressive as "Curse of Monkey Island". - There are no big happening within the story or stressful puzzle where timing is crucial for example.- I could not find the rubber chicken and the pulley...!?- There is not a single monkey in the game...
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: For those who grew up with Monkey Island or played them later, this is a wonderful revisiting of that original vibe. Stick with it to the end if you are indeed one of those fans. It's worth it.Thanks Mr. Ron Gilbert and team, for that time capsule. Right in the feels, as some other reviewers point out. Right in the feels.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Ron, Dave and all involved - you made an absolutely stunning and beautiful adventure game that fits right in with the original Monkey Island series without skipping a beat.It was a real pleasure to play this one, thank you for making this! And the little gift at the end was really heartwarming to read.To fans of the old Monkey Island games, you will love this one. To new fans, maybe this game will inspire you to pick up the other titles in the series.All in all, a truly great game! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is pure, old-school Monkey Island at its best. The art style may rub you the wrong way (it's not my favorite), but it really doesn't matter...the game set out to capture the magic of the original games, and I think it succeeds at that flawlessly. That said, it doesn't necessarily innovate the genre, so if you're looking for that, it's not here. The ending was also somewhat of a letdown.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: That's the 2nd bestest Monkey Island game I've ever played! (tied with the original game.) Ron Gilbert didn't just mark his Monkey Island return with "Return", he brought back the spirit of Monkey Island, which I felt was missing in varying degrees with each sequel after Monkey 2. That said, the team also made sure the game didn't feel like a product of the past, adopting a confidence and even some commentary that resonates well with 2022's sensibilities. I could also see Gilbert's growth as a storyteller here, especially with how he incorporates themes from his latest games like Thimbleweed Park, which was basically a love letter to video games and game design. Long after the end credits cut back to the main menu, I was struck with a profound feeling that this game that I've grown up with have grown up with me, too. TLDR, they really made the most of this opportunity to make a new Monkey Island. "Return" is a bonafide Monkey Island game, and more.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Return to Monkey Island is an excellent game. It is very easy for me to recommend this to old fans and newcomers alike.The game is the product of creator Ron Gilbert's first proper return (he did a bit of consulting for Tales) to the franchise since Monkey Island 2, some 30 years ago. In that time he's clearly developed a wealth of ideas for the new game, and this is perhaps the boldest departure from what game before of any game in the series. There is a radical new art style, with sharp angles and visible brushstrokes aplenty. There is an unusual narrative framing device which was toyed with in Monkey Island 2, but leaned into heavily here, to great effect. There is also a novel UI - mouse buttons are tied to bespoke actions for each item, and this leads to a wealth of worldbuilding.But it's not all new. Fans of the series will find an experience which is very much in the mould established by the older Monkey Island games. The writing is charming and witty, and with a slight edginess that had drifted from the series in later games. The music and voice acting are, as always, perfect. You'll find yourself wanting to prompt characters for certain responses, because the delivery is just so fun to listen to. It's also nice to see an enjoyable version of Elaine again, after she drifted between useless and abusive in the later games. Fan favourites Stan and Murray are also brilliantly written. Overall, the whole thing really "feels" like monkey island. It's a delightful, swashbuckling adventure which put a smile on my face and kept it there.One thing that really shows is the huge amount of love and care which has gone into the game. If you don't know the previous games, that's fine. You'll get a scrapbook feature which gets you up to date with the story so far. If you're a fan of previous games, you'll find many little comments and references about whichever one is your favourite. The devs really wanted to reach everyone, which is great. The game is also full to the brim with easter eggs and little things you can do and try out. It rewards you for experimenting and trying things which are wrong - the common adventure game frustration of the character saying "I don't want to do that" over and over is keenly avoided here. A final example is the "previously on" feature which updates you on your progress if you load the game having not played it for a while. These are just three examples, but there are many, many more.The game is, of course, flawed. The puzzles, in a successful attempt to avoid the moon-logic sometimes seen in the first four games, err on the easy side. They are still satisfying, and nicely designed, but I think most fans would prefer something more difficult. Secondly, the art style received lots of complaints early on, but while playing it's honestly really nice to look at (especially on Ren & Stimpy style close ups). The only issue with the art style is it doesn't always draw attention to key items that well, so you may end up using the hotspot highlighter habitually. Finally, the ending may disappoint people. I absolutely loved it, but it's definitely controversial. Ultimately, it will be talked about far more than the "happily ever after" endings of the previous 3 games, and that's great, but in order to get that discussion it will be provoking a lot of strong emotions, and many people will outright hate it.Overall, a thoroughly brilliant game, and a wonderful addition to the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game, but it's a no from me.-The art belongs to a budget children's book: it's cute, but too simplistic and looks rushed.-The plot is barely serviceable, and very run-of-the mill: can't really say it was at any point gripping or memorable.-The puzzles are a bit too simple.-There is no insult-sword-fighting, which is an absolute shame as it's one of the most humorous things in the franchise, and one of its defining elements.-Collectibles and achievements don't really add any replay value, since this kind of game has inherently none, especially with such straightforward puzzles and simplistic plot.-The meta ending was really underwhelming and ruined what little mood and atmosphere there game had going.I can't think of anything positive to say other than "it's a Monkey Island" game, which might hold some sentimental value to some (and it had, for me, but that can't be the only thing that a game has got going for itself).
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I finished , and...It's here, and it's good: another instalment of the Monkey Island series with everything it's known for. Fun times, adventure, puzzling, people to talk to, storytelling, good jokes, bad jokes. I finished the game in 15 hours (on hard mode, with ) and had a great time.Monkey Island games have always been very forgiving and user-friendly, even in the brutal 90's.  even more so. It's all point-and-click, any frustrating quality-of-life issues have been polished away, there's a very straightforward hint system (that you can ignore) and a Casual Mode which takes away some harder puzzles. Best of all the puzzle solutions are very logical and give you regular "ah-ha!" moments! No cheapness here. And no way you can put the game into a "dead end" state, plus you can't die (with one exception, and that's Monkey Island tradition).If you've played previous Monkey Island games, there's enough continuity and fan service to feel rewarding. Like meeting old friends. If you haven't, you don't need to; there's enough fun right here to keep you looking for more.The art style is polarising. Some love it; some hate it. I think it looks excellent and plays well both at 4K and on smaller Steam Deck-size screens. Don't let the screenshots put you off; in gameplay it comes to life. However if you try it and it still bugs you, it unfortunately won't get better.The game itself can be a bit "weird". It's super-polished but in places breaks the fourth wall, goes all meta, and gets strange. It's done well and adds to the game (and is par for the course for Monkey Island titles)... It's a labour of love that very much reflects the personalities and experiences of series creators Ron Gilbert and Dave Grossman. It's 30 years since the original games; they could have just let them stand for themselves, but then they never addressed the "Secret" of . So in writing this game they have both nothing, and everything to prove.Well they proved it. If adventure games are your thing,  is for you....N.B. Linux players, I can report that this game works pretty well on Linux, but you'll want to check the  as there may be some tweaks required. Laptop users, I can report that this game runs well on integrated graphics; you don't need a huge GPU.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A new Monkey Island game... very unexpected but very welcome. First and foremost, thank you to everyone involved in making this happen!Playing this game really was a joy. Both on Steamdeck where you can control Guybrush directly instead of by clicking, which works surprisingly well, as well as on a stationary PC with mouse and keyboard where it really feels like the old games, except very streamlined (which is a good thing, mind you!). This is what adventure gaming in 2022 should be. Amazing.As for the story and puzzles, I loved them. It could have been a tad harder for my taste, but at least it never was frustrating.  But not too simple as well. Quite a delicate balance to strike which for me worked out very well.Hunting for trivia cards that are hidden around the world was actually quite fun, even if it had nothing to do with the game's story and required multiple playthroughs to find them all. There are some really fun achievements as well (*cough* Cogg island *Cough*).Not sure I really completely understood the ending... but then again it feels like this might not be the end of Guybrush and Elaine's story after all. I may be wrong, but I certainly hope I'm not. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving it.  I've been a huge fan since playing the first game when I was a kid in the early 1990s.  Monkey Island is the game that made me a "PC Gamer."  This game has all the charm and wit of the early games (I hated 4 and 5).  Much has been made about the art style.  Well, I'm a classically trained artist and studied at some of the finest art schools around and I think the art looks great.  Interesting shapes, nice color and tonal harmonies, etc.  I can tell you that anyone who thinks the art is "bad" either hasn't had good art instruction or simply has bad taste (or both).  Taste is like talent in that it's something you develop over time.  It's not something you're born with.  Anyone that has studied at a school like Art Center (which is one of the finest schools around and where all the best artists working in movies and games went) would be able to appreciate the art in this game.If you enjoyed the first 3 games, you will love this game.  I've had a genuine non-stop smile on my face since I started playing.  I do agree with those who say that people who actually played the older games may appreciate this game more, as it does hit a lot of nostalgia buttons.  I have no idea how someone who's never played a Monkey Island game will feel about it.  Monkey Island has been a part of my DNA for about 30 years, so I can't even relate to being any other way.Update:  I've nominated this game for Outstanding Visual Style in the Steam Game Awards.  This game has a unique vision and voice that most other games are lacking.  They took a lot of chances with this game and stuck to their guns even when the angry internet mobs went after them.  They are the creators.  They know what's best for their game better than any plebeian that doesn't create and knows nothing of art and just wants their childhood regurgitated to them like a narcissistic wet-brain.  Most other companies just cave in to their childish demands of internet nerds and I applaud Ron Gilbert and the rest for sticking to their vision because the game is beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Finished the game. I'm so happy with how they treated the series in this new game. But also sad that I've completed it. Buy it!Original review:4 hours in, and so far I am loving it. I'm a die-hard Monkey Island fan, and this game has hit me square in the nostalgia.Play on hard-mode, if you've beaten one or more of the earlier games.Also, don't worry if you think the art style is strange. I did. It really grows on you, as soon as you start playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic nostalgia trip. The visuals, music and voice acting have you thinking back on old adventures with Guybrush all the way. I have had a great time as a casual gamer with this on easy mode. It provides a hint book, that speeds things along. It feels wrong to use the first time, but it really is a quality of life thing. Most puzzles are more straight forward than earlier MI games, when you play on easy/casual, so you don't use it much. New players should know that you can access the sea-map directly from your inventory, no need to travel to your boat every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: At first I didn't like the art style, bet eventually it started to grow on me, it helps that it looks much better in motion.The story, the jokes, the dialog and the puzzles are as great as they've ever been, they really make this game something special.That being said, I didn't like the ending but I still think the game is definitely still worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Arrrrr, My name is Guybrush Threepwood, Mighty Pirate. The Monkey Island games have been my absolute favourite games (I & II) since I first played them in the early 90's. So for me, returning to Monkey Island in a proper way was almost a religious experience. When I first saw the graphics in the trailer I was a bit turned off since I thought it looked childish. Monkey Island might be a humerous game but it's themes were never childish. But as soon as I started playing the game I felt like I was back in my childhood with Monkey Island I and II and for me, that's the whole point with this game, this is Nostalgia to the teeth. Sure the exterior looked a bit more modern but overall I had a great time. If you're a fan of the series, this game is a must play. If not, You should perhaps start with the originals to get the 'full' story. Overall, this was the best Monkey Island game since the original two, it beats The Curse of Monkey Island as well as the Tales of Monkey Island series. For me this gets 8 'three headed monkeys' out of 10. Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first 4 Monkey Island games when they came out, back in the day. This one is similar in style, but with less frustrating puzzles. (Partly due to being able to see everything that's clickable, and partly due to the convenient built-in hint book.)It was great to revisit old game locations and interact with the old characters again.The ending was a little bit of a let-down, but was a reasonable choice.(I played the "include all the writers dialog" version of the game, with hard-mode puzzles. Not sure how the game differs, if I had chosen to play another way.)
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Just a delightful game in the Monkey Island series. I was actually impressed how beefy the game was compared to other titles. It took me about ten hours to beat when I could probably take on Monkey Island 1 or 2 in half that time. Tales still holes the longest length due to the nature of it's episodic releases. I wasn't too disappointed by the ending. Ron Gilbert's games always tend to have these meta endings, and the thank you letter in the scrapbook and the last dialogue option made me a little teary eyed about the franchise. If this was the last ever game in the Monkey Island Franchise, I feel that I would be completely satisfied, even if the story from Tales never reached a proper conclusion. The voice acting is spectacular as always. Dominic Armado is JUST Guybrush. I can't imagine him with any other voice, and seeing him back for this along with Alexandra Boyd is a delight. Also some big name surprises like Robert Paulson show up!  If I could make a few criticisms though, I feel this game is really making a lot of commentary on Nostalgia, without anything else. For the first three parts of the game, it's really familiar ground, even solving some of the same puzzle structure in the same structured order. "Do these three things to beat the chapter in the same locations we've seen before" Not to mention the trivia card collectibles that are hidden throughout the game. I think it's really unfair how the trivia cards vanish if you misremember or get an answer wrong, almost requiring a walk through if you want that achievement hunter high. I didn't start having real fun until we got to new locations and interacted with more new characters in chapter four. But there's a decent chunk of the game that is just going over old story beats. And given the ending, I feel the  game is a lot like Guybrush himself... Washed up, and trying to recapture the magic of 1 and 2 and relive the glory days. I feel the game could have benefited a lot from going on it's own adventure with new characters and new locations, instead of just wondering around Monkey Island and Melle again for the millionth time. All in all, I enjoyed my experience, and I'll be sure to revisit the game for a second playthrough to get all the achievements I missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A great showing and a return to form for one of the best series in the genre. Not perfect by any means, if anything I'd say it leans a bit too hard on the fan service and it only gets to a decent difficulty level in Act 4 when the world opens up. But it's a worthy sequel and I'd put it only a bit below the classics
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: For a second, I thought I was a sucker for nostalgia traps when I click Buy.Then I played, and it's just a great game on its own.Sure the references and fan service is really nice when you get the jokes, but the game on its own has a great story, great dialogues and a splendid artistic direction.Loved the hint system. The game designers are aware that the solution can easily be found online, so they give it to you drop by drop and you choose how much you want from it. But in general you should not need it that much, the puzzles make sense (it was not the case for Monkey Island 2).
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: They actually did it! It is a modern continuation of the Monkey island Franchise. It was everything I'd hoped it would be and more. I'm happy if they end it here, but would gladly play more MI games from this team. The art style takes only a second to get used to, especially after you see what they can do with it. Gorgeous and versatile, I was pleasantly surprised with what they were able to pull off with it!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: (Disclaimer: I've adored this franchise ever since I was a small child, so expect to encounter less than objective views)Alright, here goes. After so many years, I was honestly not expecting this to actually happen, much less to happen with Ron Gilbert and Dave Grossman involved.Let's address the elephant in the room first: Is it ugly? Well, that's up to the beholder I suppose. I will admit that I was thinking, at points, that I might have preferred a different one, but on the whole it's mostly just that screenshots don't flatter it, it's  in motion. It's a coherent style that, all in all, pretty much just works, and not in the Bethesda way, thankyouverymuch.On to the Gone is the SCUMM interface of yore, but in fairness that was on its way out by Curse and it doesn't work particularly well in widescreen anyway. What it does mean, however, is somewhat reduced complexity in the gameplay. Now, there's only the mouse buttons. Is that bad? Not really, though it does remove such moments as trying to "Pick Up" characters because the option simply isn't there anymore. Alas.On the whole, it works, and it works well.And for the Well, not to spoil anything, I'll say this: It's pretty much exactly what I wanted from a new Monkey Island game made by Ron Gilbert. And that, frankly, is the highest praise I can give it.Lastly, the There were a few areas where the performance was, strangely, not entirely stable. Definitely not what you'd expect from a game like this.Outside of that, in the entire playthrough I've encountered a grand total of one bug, which was only an animation loop glitch that didn't do anything to impede progress.Of course, that point is subject to change and even as I type this, an update is queued.Overall, an easy recommendation for fellow Monkey Island fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: SpoilersWhen i told my friend "the secret is gonna be the friends you made along the way" i was joking :(I was really excited for this game, probably the most excited ive ever been for a game. That probably played into my dissapointment when it wasnt great.I didnt expect much, i wanted a fun adventure, good humor and a witty resolution (and for it to be better than MI 4 & 5, in which it succeed imo)And... it was good, some cool puzzles, way less laughs than i was expecting, but also a few really loud laughs, charm, and a fun enough storyThis has been a controversial topic (ridiculously enough) but i personally loved the new artstyle, and i like not knowing what the secret is, because i think the point the ending makes is a good, important one. I was worried about learning the Secret because unless it was something mindblowing (which lets be fair, after 30+ years of buildup, nothing was ever going to measure up) then all the magic would be gone. But then again... maybe spending 8 hours working to learn the secret with no other payoff whatsoever isnt a great idea. At least give me a B plot that ends up taking over and giving me a satisfying resolution. We could have had Guybrush finally finish LeChuck for good or something, but there isnt anything.I also thought a couple of choices to make the MI2 ending make sense were written pretty hastily and felt sort of like a copout, didnt love the whole thing with the sonGood game, sadly not the adventure i had hoped forMaybe my love for it will grow in the future, after another replay and some pondering on what the game was going forEdit: Been reading a few of the reviews from other players and i must say theyre warming my heart, im really glad so many people were able to find such enjoyment here. It makes me want to give it a bit of time and tackle the game again with a different perspective
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It's a well crafted, solid and worthy return to monkey island. While I'd still recommend the game for fans of the genre, the ending was rather underwhelming, dumb (not in a good way) and came out of nowhere. It seemed like a (possibly warranted) commentary about the entertainment industry but felt totally out of place.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I had lots of fun, really liked it.The puzzles were just right in terms of difficulty and I really dig the artstyle. Fully voiced and charming, funny dialogue. Also the world and characters respond to your previously chosen dialogue options and there are some optional puzzles or little "side quests" which unlock additional content.Unfortunately, the ending really was disappointing.I already suspected something during the course of the game, because there are some (very subtle, but more obvious if you played the previous games) hints. However, the ending still surprised me (in a negative way). I'll just say this: if you didn't like the ending of Monley Island 2 or Thimbleweed Park (like I did, especially Thimbleweed Park - god was that ending sh*tty) you almost certainly won't like this one either.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Review is based on what's important to me in adventure games.Art style 7/10Not my favorite in the series, but it works and has some charm. A lot better than Tales and Escape.Puzzles/puzzle design 9/10Except for a few dumb ones, they are usually very good and engaging.Story 1/10Whatever they were trying, it doesn't make sense. It's apparently not a story based game anymore, sadly. Lets face it. The characters I like, but no story here. It's a anti-story game even.  Sense of place/exploration/atmosphere 6/10This is really important! You want to explore the islands and meet the characters. Mostly fine in this game, but there were a few pointless wastelands of islands. You went there just to solve a puzzle or two. It didn't have "world-building", very hurried and shallow stuff at times, compared to previous games. Voice acting/music 9/10Great, as expected.So the game has its moments. Puzzles are great. Overall  an enjoyable game, but somewhat disappointing story-wise. I would love it if they actually attempted to tell a story.. still would recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: ... then I ran into the announcement of Return to Monkey Island. I instantly knew that I had to pre-order the game, because something special was about to happen. And I was ! Monkey Island has been a troubled ongoing series of six games with only the first two involving the original creators. As you may think, this led to inconsistencies throughout these titles, or at the very least incongruences with the original intended style. Ron Gilbert and his crew at Terrible Toybox managed to rearrange this quite difficult puzzle into the culmination that is Return to Monkey Island. Because yes, from what I've seen and played, this for me is an important milestone in gaming and storytelling, and acts as a parable of life in many ways. If you're a long-time MI fan, this is where you sould stop reading. Play this game and let yourself immerse in the flow that is this melancholic journey. Because yes, this is a good game, but it's a game made for an audience which grew up with the series, and it shows.The compositions in this game are so well made that they deserved to be talked about before anything else. As you open up RTMI, you'll come across the main menu theme. For me, it has been an instant win. It manages to capture what the previous themes from MI did, but with a somewhat melancholic twist which fills you with feelings of nostalgia, particularly so if you've been a fan of the series over the years. I'd say that it captures in a way the coziness which Thimbleweed Park had. The feeling that you're seeing something new, but it's just as you left it.And then, after the initial part, the intro rolls in with the classic Meleé Island landscape and the original music. This was masterfully done by the team, and it's obviously a nostalgic move. But then again, this game is all about that (and I loved it).The artstyle. To be honest, when I first saw the reveal trailer I thought that nothing was wrong with how the game looked. It was modern, fresh and yet nostalgic with an accurate selection of colors to represent that. This  Monkey Island, visually and audibly, and I couldn't be more sure of it. In the end, you have to play it to confirm if this suits or not your likings. I think that the art direction for this game has been astonishing, with an actual intent to bring the nostalgic old style to new grounds while keeping the core elements which made the original series great. As Ron Gilbert said in an interview made a few years ago, the games he created then weren't . They were state-of-the-art graphics which, at the time, were all they could work with. There's no such thing as a Pixel Art for Monkey Island, because the developers always wanted to convey their artistical vision with the most advanced techniques available. And this is no different. I strongly agree with Ron when he says that this is the Monkey Island he wanted to create, because there's so much to see and cherish, with the animation portraying what is an alive and fun world. If you don't like what you see and don't see it coherent with the game, that's okay, everyone's different. But the backlash that the artsyle got, for me, made no sense. I've seen reviews here on steam which praised the game while costructively criticizing the style. They sounded reasonable, and as I've said that's perfectly fine.Ultimately, I highly suggest playing this to confirm or dismiss your ideas about the artstyle.On a more positive note, dialogues were well written as always. They lacked the Thimbleweed edgy vibe, but mantained the jokey, lightweight Monkey Island one. I've enabled the director's cut content, with more dialogues to please the obnoxious minds of the players who like to read a lot of dialogue, and I wasn't disappointed.The constant throwbacks to previous games in dialogues were much appreciated too, and I've got to say that they managed to put a big smile of my face a couple of times. For the most part, this is the writing you're used to. Ron and the team didn't change everything all of a sudden. It's just... the same old dialogue structure. And I've been really happy with it, .I haven't talked about the gameplay yet since there's not much to say. It's a point and click adventure with an inventory system. What I am going to talk about is the additional content, though. In the menu, you'll get access to a scrapbook containing all the information about previous entries in the series. A good addition, which lets new players stay on track with what's going on, although they will inevitably miss many dialogue snippets here and there.Oh, and there are trivia cards scattered across the game which let you do a sort of quiz game with questions based on the story so far. Really nice to pass some time, honestly, but I've constantly failed...........Other than that, nothing to say. The game plays out well and the UI is intuitive, modern and fluid.If you're a long time fan, this will hit hard. It's a must have classic, and it acts as a milestone for the Monkey Island series. I can't say anything else.If you're new to the series, I would recommend playing the previous ones first. Or, at the very least, the first two games (as RTMI relies heavily on these two). It's not that you wouldn't be able to enjoy the game, but you'd miss many things and it would be a shame, since everything is expressely made to be remembered through old dialogue snippets or returning characters. Heavily recommended.: :
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a classic point and click fan, avoid this game.The first games used verbs, and you really had to think and move the mouse around to solve puzzles. They were engaging and fun.The third game introduced a wheel with three action options. It was dumbed down but still challenging and fun. You had to move the mouse around to find interactive items on the screen. Some were really well hidden or unexpected. You still had to think.This... you just hold tab to see the interactive bits. Move the mouse there and a big pop up will tell you what it is and what you can do, before you've even had a chance to think about what it might be. It tells you which mouse button to click to do what thing.It's absolutely infantile, utterly dumbed down. A monkey could get through this game by spamming tab and clicking everything.What a shame, what a pointless end to a franchise that started so well.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: if I can sum up my thoughts in one word i guess it has to be: conflicted... while the the humor and majority of the story is genuine, the ending certainly feels out of place...reading the final parts of the scrapbook after completion makes it a bit clearer while making it more meta at the same time... not the ending i was hoping for, but i had a great ride playing the game nonetheless!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A sequel to the old & original two Monkey Island that's actually pretty good, I had to get used to new graphics design, I still love the original style better, but I can live with the new style, it's still funny to revisit Monkey Island, I played the originals a lot of times and miss point n click adventures, so I'm glad it came, overall a decent chapter in the MI universe
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a charming adventure with some witty writing and inspired art direction. The quality of the puzzles however varies compared the the old Dos games and other Lucas Arts Adventure highlights most solutions are either too simple, solved in only a couple of steps or too obscure. Given the fact that the amount of items to pick up and interactions are relatively limited it didn't tease my brain in a fully satisfying way. The main reason however why I can''t recommend this is the ending. Quite frankly it is insulting, uninspired, dumb and a giant middle finger to the fans that played Monkey Island 2. There are some fun themes about fatherhood in the narrative structure, but the way the plot and story are resolved is a complete cop-out. If this would have been the first time doing it I would give Ron Gilbert a pass, but basically reusing the ending of Monkey Island 2 without adding anything significant to the meta narrative is either equal part lazy and creatively bankrupt.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Return to Monkey Island is like hanging out with an old friend:PROS: The game is just filled with joy! The story was riddled with nostalgia of the previous games & it truly felt like it was a true continuation to the series. Puzzles were tough as nails but not frustrating at all. Art style was very pleasant.CONS: The soundtrack was a bit forgettable. It didn't have those charming Caribbean tunes of the previous games that got stuck in my head. CONCLUSION: Return to Monkey Island is everything I wanted and more. Daft humour with plenty of dad-worthy gags, puzzles to both frustrate and delight you, lovable throwbacks around every corner, and all the while being effortlessly enjoyable. It feels like Monkey Island has fittingly come full circle with this title in many ways, and yet I can’t help but be selfish and want more of this legendary franchise! To the developers of this game I salute you. Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It gives me great sadness to hit the "not recommended" button. Perhaps there are rose-tinted glasses from growing up with the original gems, but I just couldn't find a huge amount of enjoyment from this final instalment. Pros:*the voice acting, especially Dominic's. On point throughout.*Some gags were good and made me smile.*I enjoyed the little diversions away to Guybrush and his son.*the music.Cons:*Far too easy. No puzzles presented anything of challenge. A lot of stuff felt like going on fetch quests. There was no sense of exploration with trying out items. You just get a "cannot use" icon unless it's something that you *can* use. Half the fun of the originals was wondering what humorous dialogue would emerge from trying out combinations of interactions, either within your inventory or with items in the world.*Lack of life in the locales. Everything felt sparse and barren.*The ending. I understand the sentiment and metaphor from the devs, but this didn't land.Neutrals:*The art style. I neither love it nor hate it.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fine adventure, and more fun than it had any right to be. Tip of the hat to Gilbert/Grossman/Crowle for a fine conclusion of the series.The puzzles are well-crafted and balanced, not too easy but also not to illogical (that is to say they are mostly congruent with the story's internal 'logic'). The visuals and the sounds were immersive, captivating, and enjoyable (for my taste). I would like to applaud the team for selecting a 'novel' graphical style, but honestly after playing a short while I could not imagine how else to illustrate it.  So again great work by its creators, well worth the time and expense...
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Really mixed on this one. I don't mind the art style, I don't mind them constantly referring to old games. The story isn't particularly interesting but I did like some of the puzzles and how the game evolves from act to act. I wouldn't say the puzzles are too difficult but some left me scratching my head for a good amount of time, enough for me to feel happy with figuring it out, not enough for me to get frustrated.I found a fair amount of the dialogue and puzzle solving quite funny.However I really didn't like the ending, I didn't like how LeChuck is just not scary anymore (If anything he was incredibly scared of Guybrush!), and also didn't really like the trail of destruction left in your wake, it was just a bit too much compared to the other games... it's enough for me to give it a 5 or 6/10 rather than 7 or 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The magic is back!This is Monkey Island again. Now with new updated graphics and a little more politically correct as everything else... The magic and feeling of the original Monkey Island 1 & 2 is right here also. Don't understand all the childish rant about the graphics? The graphics are really nice and cosy and warm. It gives the feeling of nostalgia also right away with a touch of something new at the same time. It's really impressive that they manage to make this kind of game after all these years! Many others have tried to relive the magic of the old and failed, but not this people. They managed to continue the magic from the old days and bring it into the present! Thanks ❤️
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Final Vote: 100%Graphics: 10/10Music: 10/10Story: 11/10This game is a reboot and is also the ending. A full meta experience. In fact is  the game that is playing with you most of the time!Longevity: between 2,5 hours and 1 year.Nostalgia impact: MEDIUM - Luckily is not only about Nostalgia but used it as a starting point (and to play with the player).Best longplay ever (around 16 hours):I buyed a computer on a refurbished site and give it back after completed this game 2 and an half day later because I was waiting 11 years to know what the amusement park was. And now I’m happy. I’m a 33 years old player who quit gaming like 5-6 years ago to start to do sport and composing. I don’t play regularly anymore.Monkey Island with Legacy of Kain, Portal, monument Valley 1-2, Braid, Bioschock 1-2-3 , Valiant Hearts, The Stanley Parable and few less games is a videogame that are narrating a story in a very unique way. Not a lot of games can achieve this level of storytelling.Return To Monkey Island, the sixth chapter of this saga (like Saw or Fast and Furious, wow) is going a step further the ludic experience: is going deeper in the meaning of why gaming exists. And in doing this is still remaining a valid playable game for a 12 years old first time graphic adventure player.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Haha oh god, I've been wondering for weeks how Ron Gilbert will pick up the ending of part 2. The first 15 minutes of RtMI expertly continue the ending of 2, just hilarious. Buy the game - it's a masterpiece! I love the artstyle, the music (which changes dynamically as you walk through a screen), the humor..... stop reading reviews buy it!!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for fine leather jackets, then this is the right game for you! Oh, wait ... that's not quite it, but you can't go wrong with any Monkey Island title - even that Escape one, although that's the only one I never played till the end. This one here, however, is fun and entertaining. You will definitely want to play this till the end, it's not going to end up in your library as one of those games "that are actually not that good and I will definitely continue playing this..."Something that has to be addressed is the visual style though. There was never anything wrong with the visual style of the first two games and Timbleweed is proof that this style still works nowadays. The devs went for a different visual style anyway. It doesn't necessarily hurt the experience, but it certainly doesn't add to it either.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Everything I could ask for.Mechanics, puzzle style, framing... all technical aspects are at a pinnacle.The art style has matured since the disappointing Double Fine Adventure; it's really good now, and made into a perfect fit to the setting.The meta commentary makes me feel that we are in the same wavelength, once again after all this years.And in the end it's a fine fun romp in nostalgia land -and it feels to me (due to the said technical polish) it can grip a modern audience as well.Of course it does not have the epic feeling of LeChuck's Revenge or Grim Fandango; but then again, what does?
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This was a nice dive back into a franchise that made me fall in love with video games back in my younger days. Some will find the lack of sword/insult-fighting to be disappointing, and it is. Coupled with a more streamlined interaction with inventory and environment that removes any possibility of Guybrush saying things like "I can't pick that up," some staples of quirkiness are missing. But this also doesn't feel like it's trying to be a fleshed out MI game. It's rather a nice love-letter to the fans. And if you are a fan, make sure you enable Writers Cut in the settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I was pretty apprehensive about this game with all of the pre-release stuff.  It looked goofy (in the wrong way) and off-putting and I almost didn't buy it.  I'm glad I bit the bullet and went for it anyway because it is Monkey Island through and through.  Playing with nostalgia in a new context, viewing it through cracked rose-colored glasses, it knows its history without making it carved in stone.  I still don't love the new art style, mainly the heads and faces being the problem, but the game itself it so darn good, it is easy to get over it.  One hundred percent worthwhile and if you were nervous like me, you'll almost certainly love this.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my, what should I say. I'm an old guy who played MI1 and MI2 dozens of times. Return to Monkey Island is a dream come true. All the charm and love of the old games are alive again. On one side I can't wait to finally find out the secret of Monkey Island, on the other hand I don't want this game to end. I'm enjoying every second of it. This game is a 11 out of 10. Thank you Ron and everyone else who was involved in this masterpiece. I love it!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: If I recall correctly Monkey Island  I+II were my first two PC games I owned as a child back then in the early 90s... and loved! I don't know why exactly because there were so much great Point & Click adventures out there that time. but I always loved Guybrush's exaggerations, and any character was described with so much love! I think I just love good pirate stories!Return to Monkey Island was a great experience. In some moments it just threw me back 30 years back to my childhood. I felt all the love to the characters I felt back then. I strongly hope the story continues but I also am happy about the game as it is although the end does not feel like the REAL ending, again (besides of knowing the SECRET) ;) I also have to admit that I miss the old Pixel Art some how, but I also loved the 3rd game with more Disney like optics back then. I would have liked to see something in between but everything is still drawn very beautifully/detailed! Also the puzzles weren’t as hard/crazy as back then I guess but I initially played the easy path. Somehow that is good so, I love the story and breaking my teeth out on some puzzle would discourage me today. That’s also why I love the new “hint-book”. I think it benefits the game for players like me who can not think of such crazy puzzles as the developers (although they were really funny back then!).I also can relate to Guybrush growing up/old(er) having my own kids around me now and sometime surely begin telling some old stories about good games I played back then 😉. I am awaiting the day my kids are old enough to enjoy the games (with me again).I love the German sync with the original cast of the third part. It is really great! But maybe now that I am capable of I will replay the game in English to get maybe even more jokes.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Having played all the MI games, some multiple times, I would consider this game as the second best in the series. (The original being the best.)I know a lot of people have been questioning the art style, but I think a lot of them are just experiencing a shock to their expectations, and holding onto the negativity of that shock. Possibly swayed by some of the few, negative voices out there. While I personally also would've loved to see this in classic, pixelated graphics, I found the new graphics style actually really feels like it makes sense when you actually play the game. It's honestly pretty good, despite being different. (Also, it's better than both Secret's remake graphics or the 3D graphics of both Escape and Tales, in my opinion.) I do acknowledge that it might not be to everyone's taste, but neither is pixelated 90s graphics, or hand drawn animation á la Curse.The music is absolutely excellent, and so is all the voice acting! With some returning talent, which is very nice.The game ought to be played on Hard mode in my opinion, as that adds some extra steps to many puzzles, and makes them be on par with the old games. Again, some people are crying about how the puzzles are much easier compared to the old games, but they're either playing on Casual mode or completely misremembering the puzzles of the old games as more difficult than they were. I personally played through Secret and Revenge(and most of Curse) again as a warmup to this game, and the puzzles in those games are not any more difficult than those in Return. In fact, they're almost all quite easy.The story in Return to Monkey Island manages to make sense of the combined story of all the MI games together, including that strange ending to Revenge! And it's a pretty solid MI story otherwise, as well.All in all: Ignore the "fans" that can't deal with this not being a carbon copy of the old games, as they're so focused on hating on the art style of a game that very much has the soul of the original two Monkey Island games, and has been made by the same developers, but with 30 years more knowledge and experience than when they made the original. Certainly, The Secret of Monkey Island hit a special sweet spot that none of the sequels really managed to come close to, but with decades of honing their talents, the original developers have been able to make Return to Monkey Island the second best game in the series. (And there are definitely ways it's better than the original as well, even if not overall.)Don't miss out on this excellent entry in the series!100% in about 24 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Avid Monkey Island fans will definitely enjoy this, and it will be fully worth the ~23 €! Folks new to the franchise should probably try the first part of the series (Secret) or the third (Curse) to know if they'll like this one.I liked the art style a lot more in-game than I did in the trailers and promotional materials. If this is the last in the series, I wouldn't be mad at all. A very good send off. Only Monkey Island ever made me chuckle and laugh out loud while gaming, and this entry in the series is absolutely no different. Take your time to enjoy it though.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this Return to the great series ! The story, the chars, gameplay - everything reminds me of the good old adventures with Guybrush, LeChuck, Elaine and all and at the same time, it offered new aspects, a new look on all this. I had great fun and highly recommend it - for fans a must and all others have the chance to become fans !
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Great successor to the Monkey Island franchise.  I love the original games and this felt like a great return to form.  It has lots of laughs, silliness, and Guybrush causing havoc and wrecking the lives of other characters in the game.  The difficulty level is much easier than the original games, which is a good thing.  The puzzles are fun and challenging without being unfair or impossible.  I thought I wasn't going to like the vector art but it was actually a perfect way to get the hand drawn style of the old games onto modern displays.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most unfulfilling point and click adventure game in a long time. The game play and puzzles are fine but kind of bland and hardly challenging even on hard mode. Biggest issue is that from a story telling perspective it fails to deliver a cohesive story that can work as a standalone experience.Overall it just feels like Gilbert wanted to have a one more "Gotcha!" moment and cash in on the nostalgia rather than to make a wholesome fun adventure game on par with some of the great LucasArts classics. Maybe my expectations were too high considering the price tag but I was nonetheless disappointed in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan who played several times all the games in the series, I should say I was very excited at first, when I knew it would be a new Monkey Island game, but in the end I was very disappointed. Far too easy, uninspired story and a lot of loose end plots. I tried hard to like this game as most of people, but I couldn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The game felt like a big joke to fans of the series, especially because of the ending. Felt like the creator was lazy and just rushed to make a game for the sake of making a game. Very disappointed. I already felt like giving up on it early on, because something about the style or the dialogue or SOMETHING just felt off, but I kept going for the sake of nostalgia. The ending though, made me really wish I could turn back time and return this game. I should have trusted my instincts!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A good combo of familiar and new. My attention span for games is definitely shorter than a zillion years ago, so I appreciate that with some things, once you've figured it out once they don't make you do it every time you return to that place. The art style is obviously new, but you get used to it and then it's good, and the music and voices are 'right'. Elaine is a very patient pirate-wife of a kind of bumbling pirate!The Secret probably would make good merch.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Return to Monkey Island is filled to the brim with nostalgia references to Monkey Island 1, 2, and to some extent 3. Most of its humor is inside humor for those familiar with the aforementioned games, leading me to believe the game is designed to be played after at least the first two games. However, the game is incredibly easy, incredibly short, and the humor is more miss than hit.If you're a Monkey Island fan, then this game will sorely disappoint. If you've never played any game in the series, then just play 1, 2, and 3 and forget this game exists.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is by no means a terrible game, just a very bland and uninspired sequel to the old Monkey Island games. If all you need is a decent adventure to keep you going, by all means buy this game.But if you are a veteran of the series don't expect any of the humour and creativity that made the classic games so enjoyable.I personally don't mind the graphics, I don't love them but they look alright and have some charme to them. What I can't forgive however is the severe lack of really funny moments. And this is not nostalgia speaking, I went back to the old games to compare the writing: I could laugh at the dialogues from decades ago where a slight smirk is the best this game can get out of me.This game is like the Monkey Island of old if the original's locations felt tinier and way more cramped and with 90% of its fun sucked out of it. Not terrible but expectations certainly were a lot higher.Edit: Finished now. Nothing really there to change about my review. A decentish game, nothing to write home about compared to the old games. The game is kinda short, feels very limited in scope and doesn't really have a satisfying ending. The meta plot about Guybrush telling a story to his son doesn't really lead to anything and is mostly there to take you out of the game and hinder immersion.A wasted opportunity more than anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Could have used a slight bit more challenge, which we know Ron Gilbert is capable of after Thimbleweed Park. But it's a solid return. Well-written as ever, and MAN is the soundtrack on point. As for the visuals... I was fine with them, but they're specific enough to put some people off. Use the trailer to determine whether they're something you're okay with. It's an entirely personal thing when your art becomes this abstract.I'm not going to spoil the ending but you should know up-front that you might not find it satisfying. Ron Gilbert clearly takes a lot of pages from David Lynch's season 3 of Twin Peaks. If you watched that and ended up being one of the people who was upset about it, this is probably going to be the same thing all over again. How you feel about this kind of conclusion is very philosophical and hardly anything I could do any justice to in this little blurb.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game series was introduced to me as a child and sparked my lifelong love for absurd comedies and point-and-click adventures. I was apprehensive to start this in fear that it wouldn't live up to the grand image in my head. Luckily those fears were completely unfounded; this is everything you'd want and expect from a Monkey Island game and more (save for no insult sword-fighting, RIP) Amazing script with puzzles that challenge and reward! If you liked any of the previous entries to the series, you will not be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It is not like, that I think, it is a bad game. It has its pros, but I am just not satisfied with this. Actually I liked the game to a certain point, but then it just gets really boring and some mechanics are outdated. Like you can skip some stuff but not all and you have to replay it, if you want to have all questions. First, there is this cog wheel on the right up screen, which functions as the escape button and this was really unnecessary. I do not get why the devs included this, I even sometimes clicked on it without purpose. Then there is this boring ending, where you . I think that The Curse of Monkey Island is way better than this game. Some mechanics are great and really are groundbreaking for future adventure games in some ways, but the story lacks interesting stuff and this may be the only Monkey Island game, I probably will never replay, because all others (at least the 2D ones), I like to replay every now and then.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It is good. I got what I wanted, but not what I expected. A few notes:1.) Art- a lot of blather about the art direction online in months leading to release. I too am a pixel art fan. However, the art is lovely and grows on you as you play. It ends up stealing your heart. Atmospheric and enchanting.  2.) Music- WOWZA. They knocked this out of the park. I heard lots of remixes from the other monkey games as well as new stuff that is equally captivating. 3.) Puzzles- There is some puzzle progression from the easy early chapters to the more complex final chapter. It might seem unbalanced to an adventure game junky, but to those less initiated, the mounting difficulty will make more sense. There was only one puzzle that didn't make sense to me.  The best puzzle that gave me all the feels was 4.) Story- Grabs you and reels you into the game. I adored  The ending caught me completely off guard, and at first I was confused and maybe even a bit angry? Upon my own reflection, I kind of think maybe that was some of the point of the ending. I've liked it more with subsequent replays. There is room for interpretation and that is pretty cool. Gilbert, Grossman, et al did a fantastic job threading the needle on the story. It was nostalgic, but new. It gave some answers, but asked more questions. Just all around good stuff. It isn't your typical rodeo and I was glad for the journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth the wait. The new graphic design does not disapoint, and the achivments and trivia cards makes me want to play all over again. Well done Ron and Dave. One last thing: As a super fan, I pre-ordered the game, hence I have the most beautiful horse armor ever. It should have some utility in the game even if it was just for fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Huge MI 1/2 Fan since I was sprogg back in the 90s.Was sceptical at first with the art style, but really glad I got this game as it brings it all back.I am not disappointed!!! The ART grew on me fast and the story and gameplay is just like the old days. Up to Part II and having a great time.Big Thanks to Ron and the team!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Guybrush returns to finally find The Secret of Monkey Island!Return to Monkey Island is a classic-style point and click Adventure Game, and why wouldn't it be with Ron Gilbert returning to the series? As an Adventure game, it really comes down to two things: Good writing, and good puzzles. And thankfully, Return to Monkey Island delivers both.The game has Guybrush Threepwood, Mighty Pirate set out to fine the Secret once and for all, but his nemesis, the evil undead scourge of the seas LeChuck, is having similar ideas. And so the race is on, or at least that's how it seems. The game also features an interesting narrative framing, but I won't spoil it.Puzzle quality is good, a few puzzles share the same solution, which gets a little repetetive, but there are also some quite clever ones as well. And of course, the Book of Hints is there in case the sometimes bizarre logic you need to apply doesn't quite land with you, it can offer incereasingly specific hints from vague nudges to outright spoiling the puzzle for you.Overall, Return to Monkey Island feels like a worthy successor to the series, both MI1 and 2 that Ron Gilbert worked on and the rest of the games as well. If the series were to end here, I wouldn't mind it. But if another Monkey Island shows up, I'd buy it, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a die-hard fan of the Monkey Island games for years (see piratey username). I was super excited for this to come out.  Positives: The artwork (know some people dislike this), the UI was intuitive and easy to use (and funny), the puzzles were generally a good balance of challenging but not impossible (I played on hard mode, naturally), the length, the story as a whole.Not-so-positives: Some of the puzzles used the same item again and again which made it frustrating, and some were so easy I overlooked them to be something more complicated. The ending was a big let down, which is ironic considering the game was meant to pick up from the 'bad' ending of Monkey Island Two.Overall I'm glad I bought it and would absolutely buy the next installment!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface, I was apprehensive with the art style at first but it was very well presented in the game. It has its charm and I do not hate it.I can compare this game to the original release of Mass Effect 3. A magnificent adventure from start to before-the-end, a 10/10 in the first 95% of the game. But because of the way the ending was done, I cannot recommend this game to anyone.Spoilers ahead, my problems with the ending:The new pirate leaders just die off off screen. What the hell, they are the antagonists we had to face off for the majority of the game and they are just written off between the Meanwhile-at-the-baddies scenes. It felt like the ending had to be rushed.We do not face off with LeChuck. The entire ending arc was Guybrush catching up to LeChuck for a final confrontation. After finally catching up, we are rug-pulled the "it was all an amusement park attraction all this time" ending. Unlike the ending of Monkey Island 2, this does not lead up to a twist ending with a twist that raises questions for the next game, it is a one note gag used as an ending.The final puzzle was text heavy and has an extra step which each component is up to interpretation. The two extra turns on each wheel is a terrible puzzle clue. The code wheel also does not move backwards so that was an unnecessary amount of spinning.It is such a shame, the entire adventure was an enjoyable classic Monkey Island game and it leads up to a terribly written ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot say in all honesty that I didn't like playing Return to Monkey Island, but at the same time I believe we're very far from Secret of Monkey Island and Le Chuck's Revenge. I didn't really dig the art style, the Flashgame-like animations, or the fact that even the Hard Mode is extremely easy. I finished the game in 10 hours without ever using the hintbook. Except for Act IV (which is by no means hard) you always have the solution to a certain puzzle 10 clicks away, and it's always extremely clear how to proceed further into the game. Some characters are there for no reason, way too many easter eggs/fanservice. The writing is there. Dialogue is funny and witty, story is somewhat engaging and fun to discover. It might be the perfect entry point for kids or newcomers to the adventure games, but if you're looking for a true 90s experience... look elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 100% fanservice for old farts like me. Unfortunately mediocre at it. Also this game does not contain anything new, it is just exactly same as old games, albeit with worse graphic style. Puzzles are also little bit too easy.When I played this I actually figured out things that are explained in last sealed envelope you open and it cast sad mood for rest of the game. This is aging developers pastiche of their younger self creations and they emphasize it too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: ... well, except that they obviously did!This game is a historic landmark - and a goofy pirate adventure. Ron & Dave (and the rest of the crew) crafted a nice story with good puzzles, gorgeous art, skilled animations, great music, cool dialogues, slapstick moments and more. It made me laugh, and it made me ponder (even about reality). Recommended to old and new adventurers.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun experience for those who grew up with the original games... unfortunately, if you didn't, you'll really feel left out of the joke. There are a lot of callbacks to the first two Monkey Island games where, if you didn't play them, you'll either be waiting for the joke, or miss it completely. So, if you did enjoy the first two point n' clickers, you'll probably have a ball with this. The humour is still on point, mixing a perfect blend of nostalgia and new and the gameplay is still as simple as it once was. If you didn't grow up with the games, I'd really recommend getting through those first... and why not? They're great games! Why haven't you played them yet!?
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good!I'm so excited for a new Monkey Island and it warms my heart seeing so many people playing it!If you are a Monkey Island fan I definitely recommend it; unless something completely ruins it, I doubt I'm going to change my recommendation.The artstyle felt a bit weird when the game was announced but I kept an open mind and now that I'm playing it, does it still feel weird? At first, maybe. After a while, it does grow on you.In conclusion, I really love this series and that's why I might be slightly biased... but pressing that play button just made feel like a kid again, starting my journey to become a mighty pirate!Update: wasn't a big fan of the ending tbh but overall it's still a pretty good game and a much needed return to the Monkey Island universe! Long time fans will definitely enjoy returning as Guybrush.I'll give it a 8/10, could have been higher but the ending lowered the score a bit.And since this chapter has been successful, perhaps we'll get some more games in the future?
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Not a fan of the art style at all. Would have liked a return to VGA 640x480-like pixel art, like Thimbleweed park if this was going to be the last Monkey Island like the preachy and lacklustre ending implies. . Rest of the game was ok,but the childish scribbles of 'art' really knocked it down for me.Music was good though.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A nostalgic journey with familiar voices and humour with a new look.This sums up most of my feeling after playing this game, and I will be honest, I had this game on my wishlist for a while, waiting for it to go down in price because I was a bit wary about the artwork. Artwork that quickly didn't bother me once the game started.The first game in the Monkey Island series that I played myself and made me a fan was "Curse of Monkey Island", and you always remember your first love. Which is why I was happy to hear the voices of Dominic Armato (Guybrush), Alexandra Boyd (Elaine), and Denny Delk (Murray). Familiar voices from my tween-age years that sucked me right into the atmosphere.Unfortunately, I can't say the same thing about other iconic characters. LeChuck and our ever-flailing salesman Stan. In Curse of MI LeChuck was voiced by Earl Boen and Stan by Patrick Pinney both of which brought the best kind of over-the-top energy that made their characters iconic. I will say that Jess Harnell (LeChuck) and Gavin Hammon (Stan) are doing a good job and both are seasoned voice actors, with Gavin being the voice of Kenny in TellTales "Walking Dead" series, a character so alive that you can feel, sympathy, love and hate towards the character, so I'm sad that the energy in both Stan and LeChuck feels a bit flat.The gameplay goes back to point and click and I do agree with some critiques I've seen that it can be a bit too easy compared to the original games in the series, but I did have to use the hint book (loved that feature) on points where I just blanked out, playing even at "easy". I've yet to play on hard since I wanted to save that after getting to experience the story and humour.And speaking of story and humour! The game starts with the abstract ending of Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge... sort of. We do start at the Big Whoop theme park with two kids serving as a tutorial, and an appetizer for the weird world of Guybrush Threepwood. A world where they make jabs at previous game mechanics that didn't make sense to being with, but they keep the meta jokes on a low level and not too over the top, where they could break the fourth wall and destroy the immersion of the game.The ending was perfect if you ask me. It made sense to end it that way for this series and the story.If you like abstract puzzle games and/or are a fan of the Monkey Island series, then I would recommend playing this game. Other people have said, it made them want to play the other games and I agree with that.PS if you are interested in character design or animation then you'll probably get a kick out of watching the credits and what get's unlocked when completing the game. It gives a brief insight into the thoughs behind the series and the development of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It is a new Monkey Island!By Ron Gilbert and the dream team, Dave Grossman, David Fox, Michael Land, Peter McConnell and Clint Bajakian!Awesome graphics by Rex Crowle and the beloved voice of Guybrush by Dominic Armato!It even adheres to Guybrush's rule, “Never pay more than 20 bucks for a computer game”.So what are you waiting for, still reading this review, go buy and play it now!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Well I knew the franchise, but I never played any of the its predecessors. So I went in blind and discovered a very well crafted game for only 25 bucks. I had no expectations and so far I was really surprised by the art design. The purchase was an instant decision once I saw the game popping onto a steam banner.What to say about the game. Never played any point & click adventure in my almost 40 yrs and I loved it. Its well written with a lot of hints to older titles. Whereas ashamed I did not understand all of them due to missing predecessors, but anyway its a perfect game nowadays of around 10-12 hrs. Relaxing, having a good time and keep the game carrying you during some beautiful hours. Puzzles are no that difficult and if one exceeds there is a hint book giving useful on point advices. A very welcome surprise and a refreshing game. Solid 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the Monkey Island classics, especially Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge. I've played all the other Monkey Island games released later as well.Of course, I was delighted to see this latest one being made and released. While I feel that there could be lots of improvements to it, I can say it's good enough for old fans to feel nostalgic about this series.Have a go at it, especially if you've played the previous games!
