_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a Monkey Island fan from the very beginning and I finished this game today! It was a lot of pleasure and I highly recommend it!Ron Gilbert and Dave Grossman know how to entertain adventure gamers and especially Monkey Island fans.My tribute also goes to David Fox, Kenny Sun, Dominic Armato, Craig Derrick, Jenn Sendercock, Rex Crowl, Robert Megone, Michael Land, Peter McConnell, Clint Bajakian and everyone who was involved in this game in any way.Wonderful story with original puzzles and good old and new characters! It's worth to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending it because I did enjoy it and I'd like to see more OG team MI games, There were some issues and the user Booleanbling left a review here on Steam that sums up my thoughts exactly so if you'd like more nuance than that check out the Booleanbling review in the replies. I only slightly disagree in saying that I didn't actually like the ending;
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Although I was a little put off by the art style at first, it grew on me quickly. Some character designs were weaker than others but in general the environments were beautiful! I played on the standard difficulty and unlike most Point and Click games (including every other MI title) this one didn't seem to have a puzzle that was obtuse for the sake of being obtuse. I did find a few puzzles which felt poorly explained meaning I didn't even know the puzzle let alone figure out the solution, but for the most part everything was hinted at through dialogue or environmental design. Probably one of the smoothest P&C Adventure game experiences I've had puzzle wise and the hint system was well setup to drip feed you hints instead of just ruining the puzzle by instantly giving away the solution.Voice Acting and Music were all top notch and it was so nice to hear classic characters return with their VA behind them!The story was kind of the weakest point. Not the writing, that was as funny as I've come to expect from the MI series, but the motivations of the characters seemed a little more childish than in past games, especially the original 2 games. It felt less like a big pirate adventure, and more like a childish squabble between Guybrush and LeChuck which let me down a little but it was still a good enough vehicle for funny jokes, fun puzzles, and enjoyable characters!No spoilers but I have fallen into the 'I don't like the ending' camp. I see what they were going for, and I appreciate the attempt, but it felt a bit flat and poorly explained which let me down a lot. This was very much a Journey Not the Destination kind of game to me, but it wasn't weak enough to stop me recommending the game!Last thing; people are saying you don't need to play previous MI titles to enjoy this one, and they're not totally wrong, but I would recommend playing MI 1, 2, and 3 first as there are subtle and not so subtle call backs through the whole game which you'll enjoy a lot more if you know the context (and the scrapbook in the main menu does it's best to address this, but it's such a small sum up it really doesn't do anything to help you understand already established characters and world).
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic return to a series i've loved. A lot of new jokes... a lot of old jokes, but all flavored in R.G's special way. If you're a fan of the old games, you'll love this one, and if you've never played the old ones, you should find quite a bit of enjoyment here as well. I played 'hard mode' but only a few puzzles seemed harder than most. Overall, it's great to be back to Monkey Island (tm)
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The weakest of all Monkey Island entries by a long shot. It follows the unfortunate trend of recent adventure games that oversimplifies the interface and resolves everything with a click. The puzzles are unimaginative and repetitive (how many times you opened a lock using the exact same process?). And the plot is barebones and too focused on nostalgia. But if I wanted nostalgia, I'd simply play the original games to bring me back to the 90's. As for the characters and dialogue, I found them boring, and lacking on the typical Monkey Island humor. The art style is too abstract and inexpressive to be funny. And in general, I had a feeling of the game being rushed and empty.There are rare occasions where you get glimpses of what these games used to be, but for the most part, this isn't on par with the other MI games.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to rate this game, it has some good points about it but the story is... well, ♥♥♥♥.I don't mind games that don't take itself too seriously, but still there needs to be a story in there somewhere, something exciting and unpredictable to keep you on the edge of your seat. What we got instead was a parody of itself, where nothing matters, just a nostalgia trip, and that ending...
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to the Monkey Island franchise and to adventure games as a whole. A masterpiece that made me laugh, cry and feel childlike joy. The puzzles were not as tough as for example in Monkey Island 2, but always fair and fun. The hint book is very well done too, if you need it. It will guide you through the puzzles with hints without spoiling too much. Very well thought out. The animations and design really work well together and I grew to love it in the first minutes of the game. Don't let Screenshots fool you. The music and voice acting is outstanding, too!I fully recommend this to any Monkey Island fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you so much Ron Gilbert for returning me to monkey island. It's one of my most beloved gaming stories. This game is perfect so far. I got giddy seeing some familiar faces and exploring how the world has changed since we last left it. I'm really enjoying the art style so far with the exception of Guybrush (just wish the face was a bit different and I think specifically his nose). Also a bit of a bummer we couldn't get the original LeChuck voice actor back but that's okay. It's great to be back!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is a 30 year old series that, while succesfull, wasn´t ever the sales juggernaut other stablish franchises are, it´s from a genre considered long gone from it´s golden age and now a nitche little thing, from a defunct compny that while legendary is gone, from a creator who shifted his career into educational games and though about leaving developing games all together for years as long as not having being involved with the saga for more than 20 of those 30 years. While do I say all this on a review? Because to say this game existance is a miracle is something we all should be aware when discussing it.Return to Monkey Island is a return to true form, the humor from 1 and 2 is back and so it´s the meta comentary, which takes it´s final form on a game that is all about it and on the series itself. This is quite the divisive premise since for many years Guybrush story was halt, the idea of seeing the character grow and progress was replaced with a corporate desire to squish the name of the franchise and just keep chugging sequel after sequel where Guybrush, LeChuck and Elaine just keep having adventure after adventure trying to bring up as many jokes from the older games as they could. And I do have appreciation for those games and enjoy them very much, but it´s impossible for me not to make a distinct separation between Ron´s Monkey Island, and the other Monkey Island. This is Ron´s Monkey Island, and if that´s not what you wanted from this, the game makes it very clear why it made that choice, why it always made that choice, in the final lines of Guybrush "I though you liked silly endings".I have no doubt Monkey Island will return in some form or another, even when the games were reviewed badly and sold porly they found their audience, and the legacy of each game keeps gowing strong due to the strenghts of the series, but I doubt any future or past installements will have something as deep as to say as this one. In the final moments, with Guybrush alone reflecting, there´s a sense of pourpose to his character that is being fulfilled, he wanted an adventure and he had many, perhaps hundreds, but it was never about how they ended or what he plunged from his travels, it was the journey itself that keep him pushing  to set sails once again every single time. And if you´re still to young to get it, trust me, wait a few decades, fire up the game, and you will; your most vivid memories are never about the first or final act of most of your own adventures.It´s beautiful, it´s cathartic, and it´s bitter-sweet to say goodbye to an old friend (or at least a part of him we know for sure will be gone) but knowing he goes happy and having meet the goals of his life.I rate it 2022 out of 1990, a true piece of art from the media from a true master of it. And if you still angry about the art style I suggest therapy, the same one people who complained 3, 4 or 5 did previously, and the same one people will go after 7,8,9 or how many there may exist, because it´s a not a true Monkey Island if you don´t get people who grow up on a previous one crying about art direction for a whole decade.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played the game for 8 hours now and it's the perfect mix of new with a lot of nostalgia. It has a lot of fun puzzles and Dominic Armato coming back as Guybrush is clearly the only way to go. He is just perfect as Guybrush and he keeps his same hilarious blunderous ways, thanks to the writers. Great game! Definitely worth the play for someone who has played all the previous games, for sure! If you haven't played the other games, (what's wrong with you?) you really should, this one too!**SPOILERS BELOW***MURRAY, STAN, AND WALLY, YAY!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10What a wonderful return to this amazing gem of a series. The Monkey Island games have always had a special place in my heart as some of the most creative, hilarious, and exciting adventure games ever. Although the ending of this game is my only critique and a bit silly in a great way, I loved so many elements of this game. After playing all the Monkey Island games before this one, it's super touching following Guybrush again on one more adventure. Thank you Ron Gilbert and the original Lucasfilm Games team for sparking an idea that has touched the hearts of so many people ever since the original 1990 release. If you've never played any of the Monkey Island games, I highly recommend playing them.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: How can I put this...I grew up playing the 90s era Lucas Arts adventure games.  Yes, I am over 40.This ain't that.  This is a mockery of Monkey Island, and every great Lucas Arts adventure ever made.  I can't even believe this made it past the drawing board.Do yourself a favor.  If you're looking for a GOOD point and click adventure game, get an original (not remastered) edition of one of the 90s Lucas Arts adventure games (check Wikipedia for a list) and download the free ScummVM application, and chose a CRT shader to give you that classic DOS game experience on modern hardware. (I suggest starting with the "CRT Consumer" shader for realism)Do that, and I promise you'll have a BETTER experience than if you buy/play this wretched excuse for a Monkey Island game.  Play Secret (1), Revenge (1), and Curse (3), and stop... Escape (4) and Return (5) are horrible games and should be forgotten along side games like E.T. the extra-terrestrial.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of these games, you're a part of something beautiful and unprecedented - a 30+ year journey that culminates in one of the most moving finales in video game history.A beautifully soul-filled, heartwarming finale that was worth the wait.You're doing yourself a disservice if you don't play Return to Monkey Island, finish it, and then discuss it with your friends and internally with yourself.Thank you Ron, Dave and the entire team.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game in the Monkey Island series, it's anchored on the original ideas, characters, and humor while allowing the characters to grow and show their flaws. It's clear that the team really cares about the characters. While I'm not a huge fan of the art style, I don't dislike it and it worked well with the game play.The game never felt too hard, but it is possible to get stuck because you haven't circled back to that 1 character you have to talk to. An in-game hint book is an elegant solution to this problem, and I'll admit I used it a few times in my play-through.The ending works well for the game and can stand as a comfortable end if another game is never made.Solid B+ from a longtime fan of the series
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I had played an original Monkey Island game or two and loved them, although if I recall, the navigation in that game could sometimes be a bit slow.  I just played Return to Monkey Island with my family, and we absolutely loved it!   We had so much fun solving the puzzles.  Sure the animation isn't the same as before, but actually we didn't care.  The only thing we really did hate was the ending.  I'm sorry--it was really horrible (I know there are multiple endings, but we even managed to fall upon the potentially best ending--lame.  However, still worth it and we had a super fun time playing it!  (My 14-year-old is pretty hard to please but loved this one, except the ending, of course).  Please make more, but don't quit at the end of the game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It's Pirate Paperwork Simulator. I really wanted to love this, and parts of it are very charming. I enjoy the new characters and the score is fantastic as well. I'm currently in Part IV with lots of game ahead of me, but so far it's been too many dry, easy "riddles" based around doing office chores and handling paperwork. A character couldn't reveal a secret to me and said "Sorry but I'm all NDA'd up with this one", and that's pretty much how every NPC's dialogue is. All the while you revisit old settings and get reminded of more challenging and piratey things you did there. The interface is very reductive so that you can only drag and drop things on each other and don't even get as many funny messages when something doesn't work, only a little stop sign when things are incompatible. After a while, this made me feel like a kindergarden kid sorting building blocks but office-themed. Another thing is the writing, which seems pretty lazy and not very creative at times. Just an example: As a MI player, you know how hard it is to get a crew to man your ship... which is a problem in this one too. Then the game decides you don't need one anymore and sail your ship alone. Monkey Island was the source of all funny pirate content there is today... and this is all they did with it? All in all, for me it's sadly a let-down and writing this rewiew hurts my heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Well this was a disappointment.As a long time fan of the series, I was hesitantly excited for this. at first like most people, i wasn't a huge fan of the art style change, but having the original voice actor was enough for me to try it out.  Some thoughts:Vocals for the game mostly had good, with some odd VA decisions, was not a fan of the new Stan, but the rest were fine.Puzzles were mostly consistent, your opinions may differ also how you logically solve them. But for me, i had some issues with the eating test logic requiring you to do it in a different order, or the doors at the end requiring you to backtrack (I assumed they would need the items to stay open).Art style was fine, it took a little to adjust to it, but it was consistent with itself.But the overall reason why this is a negative review: the ending, it just felt lazy,Overall: Amazing game right up until they ruined it with a bad ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: In case anyone with an older Macintosh computer is wondering whether Return To Monkey Island will work or not (the graphic card section alone wasn't helpful here), my 2012 Mac Mini Server (2012 Quad Core i7 with 16GB of RAM and a newer SSD drive but Intel Graphics from 2012...) appear to run it just fine thus far full screen at 1920x1200 resolution (my old 24" monitor's native resolution). It's smooth as can be so far, which admittedly is just the first scene of the game, but I had no idea what to expect since the Intel Graphics chipset isn't even mentioned.I've played all the previous Monkey Island games (first one was on an Amiga 500 and the 2nd on an Amiga 3000) back in the early 1990s and played Curse originally on a family member's 1995 Windows machine (since it wasn't released for the Amiga) so I'm looking forward to it, but not expecting too much.  All previous versions run fine on the same Mac from the Deluxe versions (only Apple store had the 1st one for the Mac Deluxe and I had to play the 2nd one in Windows 10 on the same machine, where it worked fine) and all the Tales games ran natively and I had the old Mac versions, which will run under SCUMM just fine (original ran on my old PowerMac Digital Audio under MacOS9 and X under emulation).  I just wish Maniac Mansion had gotten a Deluxe release.  I first played that one a Commodore 64 and later the Amiga version, which looked slightly better.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: What... what was this? I waited 25 years for Ron to make another Monkey Island game. Listened to him wax on and on about how other creators simply didn't do the series justice.... Even listened to his ridiculous bashing of Curse (the best game in the series). After all those years, and all his yelling this is what he delivers to us? Let me be clear, I don't give two ♥♥♥♥♥ about the art style. It is what it is. Every game since MI2 in the series has taken artistic leaps and i'm ok with that. I don't expect modern games in 2022 to try to look retro just for fan service. What absolute SUCKS about this game is that it doesn't trust it's audience AT ALL.Every single minute of this game absolutely bludgeons you with hints. Even in hard mode. Even when you don't ask for them. I can think of multiple times when the game outright told me to go talk to a character or do a specific thing to progress completely unprompted. At so many points in the game they airdropped nuclear bombs of hints on your head. I beat this game in ten hours. No hints. On hard mode. And some of that time was padded by me streaming it to twitch. I wanted to cry when it ended... not because it was a good journey, but because after sticking up for Ron being a pompous ass about how much better of a game he could make if given the IP back for two decades, I expected a treatment befitting the lucasarts days of glory. I wanted a hard, challenging puzzle around every corner. The story was lame, predictable, and not funny. Completely lacking the humor that made the series popular. The ending was the least fulfilling ending of any piece of media i've consumed this year as well. In conclusion I expected the stars, and I fell face first into the mud. After playing the not perfect but extremely excellent Thimbleweed Park, I guess I had high expectations that Ron had not lost his flair for adventure games, let alone doing justice to the one that made him a household name. I was wrong. I am disappointed, and I hate that this is what he chose to deliver after all these years. Monkey Island peaked with Curse, and has never had a good entry since. Maybe in another 20....
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: NO SPOILERS AHEAD, I PROMISE-----------------------------------A stunning return from Ron Gilbert and Co.Don't listen to the haters, they're just scared that the art style has changed but I'll tell you what hasn't...The humourThe charactersThe puzzlesEverything you could wish for, very carefully crafted to fit in with everything that was made after Ron's departure from Lucasfilm back in the day. I was personally touched by how well he's handled the previous games, it follows on perfectly from MI2 without letting any of the good bits from Curse, Escape and Tales. If anything it embraces what the other teams have brought to the table through the years.The new art style works really well, the animation that goes alongside it is quite the beautiful thing. I was a little sceptical when I first saw the teaser screenshots but nothing could stop me from pre-ordering and downloading it on release minute.I can't give this anything less than a solid 10/10 and I'm only 3 hours in.Now you've read what a Monkey Island fanboy (Escape wasn't the best) has to say, but it, install it, play it, love it. Ron and his team worked their arses off to craft this beast and it shows!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I thoroughly enjoyed RtmI. I grew up with Monkey Island 1 and 2, which I replay every couple of years. Also have fondness for MI 3. I think Return is everything a Monkey Island fan should want it to be. It's incredibly funny, well acted and fun puzzles. Especially the first three parts are maybe a bit on the easy side, but I couldn't really care, I was enjoying being back in this world too much. Puzzles can sometimes be a bit finnicky (I used item A on item B instead of item B on item A and it wouldn't work) but that was just a couple of times and the hint system is great. Loved it!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent art, good writing, great puns! A very good Monkey Island adventure.After playing through this I thank the team behind it for daring to set sail once more. Truly a worthy sequel and possibly the best adventure game I've played in a decade. The vibe throughout is so very Monkey Island, and all the throwbacks and in-jokes definitely hit home. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: No bad, gameplay and story is subpar with Monkey 1 & 2. And some parts have pretty lazy writing (don't want to spoil anything but if you play, you will know). Graphics ... I get why they go with that style, but a little bit less abstract/minimalist would have been better. Some places just look poor and unfinished. There isn't one background that make you love it. It ain't Monkey 2 landscapes, that's for sure. And characters lack so much detail that you don't have any memorable one.Better wait for sale. I mean, it's fun, but pretty forgettable.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I have played through the game once on Hard Mode.Pros:+Art style is great+Voice acting is terrific+No Monkey KombatCons:-None of the puzzles are memorable-None of the dialog or gags are particularly funny-Multiple sub-plots and characters are dropped without resolution-Worst ending to a video game since Thimbleweed Park-So many callbacks for nostalgia's sake that it got tiring-No funny remarks for trying to use the wrong item on something or someone
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Borderline not recommended.I've played through all of the Monkey Island games and this was the weakest entry yet.  I can tell the team wanted to do it justice but it just seems like they're out of ideas.  Some of the classic humour is there and shines through but very seldom.  The new characters are very dull and the old characters are executed less effectively than in the past.  There's nothing offensive or necessarily objectionable, just very underwhelming so a long-time fan.  For context, my favourite was MI2, followed by MI1 and MI3.  MI4 was ok, then Tales was subpar and then this was below that.  I was hoping that the involvement on Ron Gilbert would elevate the end product but I can't say it seems to have made much difference.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: An utterly wonderful addition to the Monkey Island series! I loved this game! Everything about it is wonderful! Another point and click classic by Ron Gilbert! If you are one of the people who don't like the game's graphics, I would advise you to try it anyway! The graphics look a lot better in motion. I wasn't totally sold on them prior to release, but I got used to them during my playthrough. The music, the dialogue and the story are all spellbinding! I can't get enough of this game, I already played through it three times on hard mode! I would give it a 9/10 rating! Another evergreen by Ron Gilbert and Dave Grossman!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Play it in hard mode.This game is way to easy and lazy. I like the new visual style (3rd MI was the best for me), the engine works OK, but is extremely obvious it was like reading/following a story instead of having to interact with the game and figuring out what to do next.If you played previous Monkey Island games when you were a child, don't have much time to spent on a game and want a quick trip down memory lane, this is the right game for you, but don't expect it to be what Monkey Island 1, 2, 3, ..., Grim Fandango, Full throttle, or others are (never played Day of the tentacle, so I might look for a remastered version of it next)Regarding the ending, it is just a little bit depressing, but the correct one, not greatly executed, but not a bad one either.I know there are like 10+ endings scenes, but I mean the whole final act and twist, not just the different last scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I did not get through the beginning credits before the younger version of myself, still very much alive under my aged skin, started jumping up and down for joy. As the music queued and my lips formed to whistle along, I was taken back to much simpler times when all I had to worry about was learning the best sword fighting insults. Props to Gilbert and Grossman for for yet another amazing installment of a much loved series.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Super funny, super fun to play, genius puzzles, great music and voice acting. Overall, this is one of the greatest point-and-clicks of all time. The only problem, of course, is that this is based on a 30 year old franchise, so it's impossible not to compare it to the originals, in which case I think there is a *hair* too much fan service going on here. But, it's still good, it's still weird, it's still irreverent, the humor is biting and sarcastic as ever, and the spirit of the originals is here 100%. So. Yeah. I just hope they make more.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Especially for fans of the first two games this is a must buy. It's got the humor and witty dialogues of the original games. Puzzle difficulty can be selected in easy and difficult, while difficult is probably the right choice for every seasoned point and click player. There is an on-demand in-game help system available, if needed. The game never patronizes you by throwing hints at you while you still want to figure it out on your own.Good pacing, funny jokes that frequently borderline fourth wall breaking and a very clever way to make it a sequel to all Monkey Island games yet still making it a dedicated true sequel to Monkey Island 2 at the same time.Not much more to add. Liked it very, very much.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited at the thought of returning to Monkey Island after all these years but as much as  I hate to say it,  if this had been the first chapter, I never would have made it to the sequels.  The clever dialog is gone and the best words I can use to describe Return to Monkey Island are tedious and boring.  There is no depth to the characters,  the story line is weak at best and the different locations are empty compared to what they once were.  This might be acceptable for those who never played any of the prior Monkey Island games but I can't imagine veterans enjoying this at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I love Monkey Island. All of them. Yes, even Escape and Tales. It's my favorite adventure game series, and I was thrilled when Return was announced.Right off the bat, I have to address the art style, since it gave this game a lot of bad press. Well, it looks way better once you actually play the game. Every screen is colorful and vibrant, and it is a joy to watch and play.Return is very accessible. There is a recap of previous games (ALL of them are canon), multitude of accessibility options, checklist of current tasks and even a hidden tutorial.I'll update this review once I finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately this is the worst Monkey Island game by some way. The world feels empty and half-finished. There are major issues with the writing that I won't go into to avoid spoilers. Let's just say the script really could have done with a rework and what we got feels a bit like an unfinished draft.They've also streamlined the point and click adventure formula to to the point where there's very little challenge left in the gameplay. At times, you feel like you're just going through the motions on rails, which would be more tolerable if the writing was more interesting and satisfying. It's great to have Dominic Armato back as Guybrush and there are some nice moments and laughs but it's not enough. The overall package is very disappointing and it really feels a bit like the devs got bored or ran out of cash. This was a must buy for me as a fan of the series but I genuinely regret the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: i have been playing this series since the first game. And every time, the story, writing and characters shine. This time around we get the full Monkey Island experience with renewed visuals, a story matching the legacy and amazing puzzles that never feel unfair. For new players it's sure to be a fun romp, but for those who've been following Guybrush from the start, get ready for another amazing three-headed story worthy of the Monkey Island franchise. Loved the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Very snappy, modernized old school point & click adventure. Well-written, funny. Difficulty levels and the in-game hintbook minimize frustration, though of course one should try to solve the game on Hard and without hints... like a REAL pirate. Played for 4 hours now. If the game holds up till the end, I shall rate it eight out of eight pieces of eight.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10The game is alright, humor is there, it feels like monkey island game, it has the good soundtrack, great voice actors, and still it feels like so much wasted potential. So yeah it's good but it's not really a monkey island game in my books, If I had to rank the games this one would be the worse one, the puzzles are insultingly easy, the character artstyle is atrocious, especially the eyes and noses of humanoid characters, rest of the art is passable at best. the writing feels really bad too. but I did still enjoy it cause Monkey island is still one of the best series and I can't get enough of these games.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I really appreciate the effort Ron and his Terrible Toybox studio brought into the Monkey Island series. The dialog is great, the puzzles are fun and the graphics style is the best yet in a MI game! The graphics style is not only nice to look at, it also serves a functional purpose as it doesn't clutter the screen with non-essentials that hamper the gaming experience. For adventure fans, this game is a steal for its roughly 20 dollars!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Great to see a return of the Monkey Island series and even better to see it done so well with the humor and story being a continuation of two and clearing up that whole ending while pushing the story forward. The scrapbook feature is a great way to catch up to the story if you haven't played before and the art style while different from all the other games didn't bother me at all but the longer I played the more I like it because during cutscenes it helped make the 2d environments feel 3d with there movement and I thought that was cool! 9/10 could have been longer and while I thought the ending was a nice way to wrap it all up I still want more.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: We've been waiting to Return to Monkey Island for too long. Well, the time is now, and we have Ron Gilbert and Dave Grossman leading the journey this time. While the originals are said to be the best of all time in the genre, this one somehow manages to transcend and elevate the game. With it's daring, different and fresh beautiful art style, and slick rich animation, the visuals will quickly capture your heart. The facial animation and emotions delivery is very well done as well. In terms of story, it picks up where MI 2 stopped, while still paying respect to the sequels, and giving enough space for personal interpretation. It was really challenging to come up with a story to continue from that cliffhanger, without completely cancelling every other game that came after it. I can't think of any possibly better option than what they went with. Wonder how long they had to plan this direction.Voice acting is top notch as always, and the music is good as always, only much more dynamic now, and with far stronger sound effects that at times made me shiver.The UI and game controls are the best I've tried in any video game perhaps. Very intuitive, explains the action, minimizes clicks, and you don't need to try combining each and every item to see if it works. It will simply tell you if it's possible by hovering. There is key to skip dialogue line, and one to bring up the dialogue history so you never miss a thing. You can walk or pace faster to where you want to go, so it's never boring or tedious task.The game puzzles I thought were good and funny. Nothing too hard, and it's not too easy either. If you get stuck, there is a very good hint system that will give you small snippets one by one until you're good to go on your own. Another neat thing is the trivia cards which tests your Monkeyology knowledge. They pop up at random places again and again, so you don't have to be too worried about missing them. Murray is a star in comedy as usual, and I feel they improved on some other characters compared to previous games. I'm 42 now, and don't easily get excited like when I was a kid. Yet this game got me laughing hard, and clapping like I was 30 years ago. I finished the game fighting the tear and dealing with a mix of emotions.They have done it again. Definitely a masterpiece, and a game we will probably be playing and admiring 30 years from now. I'm so glad I got the Horse Armor for me and my kids so we get to brag about it by then. It definitely isn't without a purpose see?
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The art and visual design of this game is fantastic, which is what kept me playing.  I played the Curse of Monkey Island as a kid, and was reminded of how tedious the gameplay can be while playing Return to Monkey Island.  So much dialogue to click through.  You think you retrieved the correct item to complete a task, but then a character tells you that you need something else from a place you literally just came from.  It can be annoying.On top of that, I nearly felt like asking for a refund when .  I mean, seriously, what a horrible character.  Was he always like that?  I realize someone thought this was funny, but it just turns him into a monster, in my opinion.  Maybe if Boybrush interrupted the story to tell Guybrush how mean that was, it would have made it less terrible.Still, I kept playing cause the voice acting, music, and artwork are gorgeous.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun and definitely triggers nostalgia for the series. That being said, I'd rate it as one of the weaker entries. The story is okay-ish but somehow disappointing (including a typical Ron Gilbert ending), the riddles surprisingly easy. The humor is good but not as great as in the earlier entries. Voice acting, gameplay and music are top notch as always. While the new art style is beautiful and well crafted, it definitely needs some getting used to. The only thing I really didn't enjoy at all, are the spawn rates for the trivia cards you can find across the game, which result in tedious grinding.The Monkey Island series is like pizza, even a bad one is still pretty good. So I'd recommend this one to fans of the series, but you should lower your expectations. If you're new to the series, go play the original ones instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Gloriously done adventure game that does justice to one of the best, most loved adventure games ever.It achieves this feeling you got when playing the original games that  is hard to describe.The new visual style works really well, and gives it a refreshing aesthetic while respecting the original's artwork.Not only the game's story has matured along with the gamers, but the mechanics have improved in a way that feels like a natural progression for adventure games.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: On the technical side, mainly the interface, it is a great step forward. The story is fun, but sometimes also very meta, but this could just be me, being 30 years older. I a way it is also a very sad story.The puzzles are mainly good, for me only some of them were annoying, because of the back tracking, but that's the adventure genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Is it as good as Monkey Island 1 or 2?  In many ways, yes.It's got all of the charm, wit, and cleverness of those games.  The interface has been streamlined.  The puzzles, while challenging, don't seem as obtuse as those from the original games.  There seem to be more hints in the dialogue to set you on the right path.  Or maybe I'm just older and wiser now.It is definitely a worthy successor to the first two Monkey Island games.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start by saying my recommendation of this game is more mixed than negative. It has good and bad points.First of all, I'm speaking from the perspective of a lifelong Monkey Island and I've played all the games both in their original and remastered forms - even the awkward 3D ones. Despite the varying quality of the games over the years, every time I hear that theme song and see Guybrush on screen it warms my heart and puts a smile on my face.Return is a great nostalgia trip for seasoned Monkey Island fans. Lots of returning characters, references and of course gags. You'll revisit familiar places but everything has moved on now; the Pirate Lords are trendy youngsters, no one's drinking Grog anymore and the Voodoo Lady is going out of business. It's all a bit sad but appropriate given how much time has passed. It's also - I imagine - a reflection on Ron Gilbert's opinion of the game industry and how it's changed.The biggest problem I have with Monkey Island is actually Gilbert himself. He seems unable to resist the desire to put in fourth wall-breaking meta commentary, even going back to the first games and this trope gives him a way to avoid writing any satisfactory conclusions to the story because they're just video games. It's a trick he has pulled a few times now, starting with Monkey Island 2, continuing with Thimbleweed Park and finally in it's most egregious form here in the ending of Return to Monkey Island.Up until the ending of this game, I was on board with it. Although I don't care for the art style, I felt the music, voice acting and writing more than made up for it. The story was chugging along nicely, centred around Guybrush and LeChuck's ongoing rivalry in finding the Secret of Monkey Island (tm) amid a changing world with changing ways. The characters are for the most part very charismatic and likeable and I enjoyed the trivia cards and playing "spot the reference".However, all of that does not matter in the face of the ending, which is without a doubt the worst and most disappointing ending to any story I've ever encountered. In fact, to call it an ending is inaccurate because endings are planned. This was a brick wall, a sudden drop, this was just turning the lights off, locking the door and simply leaving. It was in short, unacceptable and once again I get the impression Gilbert either wrote himself into a corner or decided to subvert expectations by making the ending abrupt and confusing.So, if you're desperate for a taste of that old Monkey Island magic, maybe wait for a sale and give it a go. The music is superb, Dominic Armato hasn't missed a step and still shines as Guybrush and LeChuck is still comically menacing. Puzzles are fairly straightforward (even on Advanced mode) and the game gives you a hint book now which I have mixed feelings about...Also, there's no insult swordfighting which is a huge disappointment because I loved that.

I could write a page on why I disliked it, but as a life-long Monkey Island fan, suffice to say this one is a real downer. I wanted to say "at least it's *more* Monkey Island. _childDocuments_.review: No finished the game yet.  In Part V.  Highly recommended.  Will rewrite this when I've finished the game.===============================Have now finished the game, some time ago.  See below original review, for additional comment.  The stuff I wrote originally has not been changed since I've completed the game.===============================The intro had me a bit concerned, it was very Knights & Bikes, which is a game I quickly wearied of, and to which I doubt I'll ever return.Entering the official Part One of the game, however, that K&B flavour quickly receded, I am thrilled to report.The music is excellent, the jokes are bloody well brilliant, and if you're a fan of Ron Gilbert, you are sure to have a blast!  The words of this review will likely get deleted and completely rewritten once am finished, outwith the warning about the intro, and the reassurance the actual game, once it starts, is delightful and fun.  I've had several LOL moments, at least half a dozen, and Ron has worked in post-2020 cultural quips that will defo bring a smile to yr face.Feel free to creep my profile: I played the Secret of Monkey Island when it came out in 1990, MI2 in 1992.  I loathe the Special Edition re-imaginings (there's a review).  I've never played Curse or Escape, I probably never will, however, I intend to play Tales one day. My complaints about RtMI are few, the primary being, don't let the intro scare you, if you're a first gen player.  The very, very beginning is beautiful, but they use the intro as a bit of a learn-by-playing tutorial/guide, it quickly veers away from a Ron Gilbert style (which happily comes back once the actual game begins).  idk if Rex Crowle has been a Kricfalusi fan, but I'd put a tenner on it.  I've been especially entertained by the digs Ron makes at his detractors, to the point I wonder how much was foreshadowing and how much was him mebbe adding to the script between April and July  :)===============================(now December 2022, last played game in October)Months  after I finished it the first 3 or 4 times, additional remarks:Still have not played Casual Mode, but warning to anyone, it is a different game, as reported to me by others who have played both.  If you were around in 1991/92 for Monkey Island 2, to me it sounds like Casual Mode is very much like MI2 Lite.  I made the mistake of playing MI2 Lite first.  When my pals found out, one of them quit talking to me for over a week.  When I set about playing the actual Monkey Island 2, I pretty quickly understood why he quit talking to me. The Lite game left so much out and it was so much easier, in many ways it was hardly the same game.  Only go in Casual Mode if you really don't like puzzles.  When I finally get around to playing Casual Mode, I'll update.  Being perfectly honest, there are only two "difficult" puzzles in the full-on version of RtMI, and of the two, only one did I find especially challenging.  You will likely not spend the 2 weeks (months?) it took for you to figure out a couple of MI2 puzzles back in 91/92, but it may be a week.  Maybe. Regardless, you lose a lot of fun going Casual, imo, based on reports from my friends who've played both.The only other thing I'll add is I actually cried at the end, from good feels, not sadness, not disappointment.  I found the ending beautiful and poignant.  I have now cried, while playing exactly two computer games, both Ron Gilbert written.  The first was Thimbleweed Park, and I really thought that was a once in a lifetime cry; it took me by total surprise.  I quite famously avoid and eschew games/film/etc. meant to bring out the tissues, as they are, imo, tiresome, so crying for me, regarding entertainment of any sort, is a massive deal.  Despite being aware of the importance SoMI holds in my life, and in my gaming life, I still never expected to turn all emotional at the end of RtMI.  Even knowing what happened at the end of TWP.  Did not see it coming--tbh, all the game play previous to it, perhaps because it didn't look the same (whereas TWP, very very retro in appearance, theme, content, and completely plugged into my early gaming experiences), I never expected a cry--overwhelming emotional reacts of love was defo not a reason I played RtMI: it was not what I wanted, never a thing I'd choose, but I'm glad it happened, it was all good feels.  Sake, am about to tear up writing this, and it's been months.  So that's Ron Gilbert, 2 for 2 in the crying game for me.  Important note: Gilbert has done this with respect, unlike someone such as Steven Spielberg, who is willfully a tedious manipulator of emotion.  i.e., I really don't think Gilbert intended this to have a cry at the end; he was merely telling the story, not seeking a tear-jerker.  I'd prolly never have played another of his games, if he had ever come off to me as that kind of writer.  ===============================

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a lifelong Monkey Island fan and was SOOO excited to hear that some original team members were coming back to make this. But I shouldn't have been. It's just not good. ART - This is good. I had no complaints here. It's charming!PUZZLES - They were good! Satisfying, challenging, and balanced. They start a little overly easy for someone experienced at point-and-clicks like this, but I figured that was by design, so newcomers to the series could jump in since it was getting a lot of hype. The pacing is odd but fine.DESIGN - A little empty. Gone are the days of combining random things or showing items to NPCs to get unique lines or jokes. Most things have only 1 or 2 possible ways to interact, and a lot of the maps and scenes are just empty.VOICE ACTING - Fine. Some sound a little out of character but having Dominic Armato makes it all OK to me. He's wonderful as always.STORY -  Waste of time. It was self-indulgent, pretentious, and soulless. The game feels unfinished. They explain in a post-game letter that this was essentially a mid-life crisis work slash series farewell and it's meant to be disappointing and hollow-- but if you don't know how to write an ending, just admit it.  I used this game to introduce Monkey Island to someone new to the series and fully regret it.  It's just a disingenuous and bitter-feeling approach to the series that leaves (by design) a sour and tired taste in your mouth.Imagine you launched a new Pokemon game and the first line was, "Welcome to the world of Pokemon. Did you know your parents will die someday? Here's your stupid Pikachu I guess."

It's fun to stroll down memory lane with Guybrush here, so if you're new to the series, I would recommend playing "The Secret of Monkey Island" and "Monkey Island 2" first. _childDocuments_.review: A nice send off to a legendary series. The art direction is booming with charisma and personality you want to see from a Monkey Island game. The puzzles are well balanced, leaving enough room for head scratchers. The game simply demands you interact with as much of the environment and it's items as possible. The excellent writing and humor remains rock solid, and the new addition of trivia cards adds a new standard to collectibles that I never knew I wanted. There's plenty to experiment and discover with. Don't be afraid to replay the game, as you might miss some stuff, and remember that Monkey Island above all else is about having fun. I do hope we get another game down the line, perhaps a remake or two, but I'm confident most Monkey Island fans will feel right at home.

_childDocuments_.review: We've been waiting for 31 long years. Another chapter of the original saga, another episode of the old fashioned series, interrupted with an idea in Gilbert's mind.And here we are, finally, talking about a game that nobody expected, but it's a good damn reality.So, what is Return to Monkey Island??The game follows the Big Whoop story, starting where Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge ended, in the amusement park on what seemed to be Monkey Island.I'm not gonna do spoiler, since i think that if you're here, maybe you're not certain to buy it or not, and if you do, you don't want to know how things go and how Gilbert and friends thought it could have been. I just want you to remember that this game features Ron Gilbert, Dave Grossman and David B. Fox (the original chief programmer) at programming and designing, Rex Crowle at graphics, all the original dubbing crew (without Earl Boen as LeChuck, but nicely substituted) and the amazing trio Michael Land, Clint Bajakian and Peter McConnell at sound design and music.Many of the old characters are still here (Guybrush, Elaine, LeChuck, Herman Toothrot, the Voodoo Lady, Stan, Otis, Carla...) and then we have many many other new characters.The story is so well written, and follows exactly the same path as the first game, with some additions (Scurvy Island, Terror Island, Brrr Muda, Barebones Island, Cogg Island and others), starting from Meleé Island, going to Monkey Island, back to Meleé Island and back again to Monkey Island, and everything is about the search for the SECRET of MONKEY ISLAND.A classic point and click with a hint book to help you (the game it's not difficult, even selecting hard mode), and a trivia system to make things so much more interesting.39 amazing achievements (some of them require multiple runs) to enhance longevity and stimulate the player to play it over and over again.Many people hated the art style before playing it, and then loved it, so my suggestion is to not think about it and play the game, maybe you're gonna love it too.Pros:+ Amazing cartoonish art style+ Original but seemingly old fashion plot+ Classic point and click gameplay+ Fantastic soundtrack and sound design+ Quite long for a Monkey Island game!+ Smart puzzles, require some skill but they're never frustrating+ Proton compatible (for Linux users)Cons:- Some characters deserved a better treatment (Herman?)- Require Directx 12 which is a shame for a game like this- No native Linux client (they promise it's gonna come soon)Return to Monkey Island is the right and deserved conclusion to the saga. The ending was quite expected, but still is nicely told. It's fun, good looking, quite challenging but not frustrating, it has everything that a point-and-click adventure game should have.I think it's a masterpiece, and everyone, especially Monkey Island fans, should play and enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Monkey Island has been around forever.  It's been around so long that it outlasted the genre it belonged to!  For the jaded fans, the series has overstayed it's welcome but for the optimistic fans another pirate adventure was a pipe dream.  Once the optimistic ones awoke from their slumber, they discovered that against all odds, the grumpy Ron Gilbert managed to put something together.  Whether optimistic or jaded, Return to Monkey Island has something for you but the question is: Do you really want what it offers?For the uninitiated, Return to Monkey Island continues the tradition of LucasArts style adventure games but manages to make interactions with the environment and items very one dimensional.  Long gone are verbs and the much simplified (but better) verb coin.  In lieu, we get the sinful no verb left click.  The player is tasked with finally finding the much maligned titular secret treasure before the zombie pirate LeChuck.  To get the treasure you need to left click your way through fairly easy puzzles (even in hard mode), a lot of witty NPC dialog and eye offending nu-corporate memphis art.  Games like this live and die on their writing so I thank God that Ron was able to deliver otherwise Return would have walked the plank.Along with puzzle difficulty, puzzle complexity and player expression being reigned in big league so has the size and scope of the game world. A few puzzles suffer from the age old problem of laying out the puzzle logic with the player such that a path to the solution can be gleamed.  An early example of this is having to cut a flower off with a knife from your inventory instead of being able to just pick the flower.  When you attempt to pick a flower, the feedback from Guybrush does not give you a clue as to why you can't pick it with your hands.  This results in puzzle fatigue as finding the common sense solution gets old fast while the player attempts to use every item in their inventory in a last ditch attempt to brute force the solution.  Thankfully, there are only a couple of these in the whole game;  The hint system is robust and sensitive enough to track your progress on the odd chance you encounter puzzle fatigue.Each island that you visit is quite small with very little to interact with when compared to games of the past.  The tech and craft behind the game is equally as meager: seemingly ancient animation techniques produce disjointed movement from characters and the environment; little use of visual depth; missed opportunity to bring back full screen realistic close-ups of characters when speaking with them (lots of animated close ups in the corp. memphis style, however); missed opportunity to build on top of the art style of Curse.  This is my jaded side rearing it's ugly head.Since jaded heads are unsightly, allow me to lop that off before it grows back so my optimistic head can shine for a moment.  What the game seriously lacks in beauty the writing almost makes up for it.  Maybe, 80% worth.  If you pay attention you can pick up on the major themes of the game.  One such theme is change but they don't hit you over the head with it and instead opt for sublety.  Dialog is rarely laugh out loud funny but it's humorous none the less in a sarcastic, cynical, ironic, cunning and thoughtful Monkey Island way; it's obvious Ron has stepped back into the room when you play it.  Often, the sudden situations the game provides are more knee slapping than the dialog: situations where dialog wasn't necessary.  The new trio of hipster pirate antagonists were a clever touch along with our ironic friends of the enemy's ship.  Classic characters make many appearances too if you care about that sort of thing; they were fine.  I was a little sad there wasn't so much as a cameo by Edward Vangelgen, Haggis and Cutthroat Bill.  With the exception of LeChuck, the voice acting is top notch and helps keep the player engaged.  With that said, the voice of some of those actors are really showing their vocal age.Now, this is the real kicker but I'll keep it pithy.  If you're a long time player of Monkey Island you know that Ron famously kept the secret of Monkey Island a mystery not too dissimilar to the brief case in Pulp Fiction.  The end of this game is very predictable if you have followed and read about Ron Gilbert over the last couple decades.  As you progress through the game and try to predict the ending, you will certainly be correct only to laugh at how absurd that would be to only dismiss it as you try to keep an open mind. The jaded will become more jaded while the optimistic might have their third eye finally open.  I'm in the jaded camp so that's why the writing only covers 80% of the games technical and craft issues: I hate the ending.Return to Monkey Island may have it's issues but it's the last of the Ron Gilbert Monkey Island games.  It's worth a play for that alone no matter what camp you are in.  If a monkey wrote history books, this game would be in it.  7.2/10, would not play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, it's a legit, old school Monkey Island game, so of course I'm going to recommend it. I did hate the ending, because it left so many game threads unresolved. It's a legit old school Monkey Island game, and I am grateful that it exists 30+ years after the original.

_childDocuments_.review: a love letter to Monkey Island. Before playing this game I replayed in a row all the games from the franchise. It took me quite a long time, but it was worth it. Return to monkey island has a great art style. Together with the first game I consider this to be the best looking monkey island until now. About the dialogues and the general meaning of the game, Ron Gilbert is back at his best. Just like the first monkey island, this chapter is an adventure game that reflects on what adventure games are. A must play if you believe that games can be works of art. It's deep, it makes you think. And it's light, it constantly reminds you that all in all, it's just a game. Thank you Ron, we missed you!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Well... how do I start this review? It is with a lot of pain that I am not recommending this game. At the beginning, I have a lot of doubts about the art decision. I didn't like what I saw in the trailers. At all. However, how happy was I, when, after playing the game for literally 5 minutes the art grown on me. I loved it! All the characters, the screens, everything is beautiful. Great job guys!However, there are a lot of things that make me not recommending this game, and be careful, some minor spoilers ahead.[Game interface]First of all, the controls. Why did the developers decided to have only two actions? Why in Earth? That makes the game completely easy, it's ridiculous. I understand that having a list of 15 verbs (specially when most of them do something similar) was unnecessary (specially when your are in that part of the game where you don't know what to do and start trying every single combination in case you missed something). That's why I loved when they introduced the new interface in games like Full Throttle, The Curse of Monkey Island, Grim Fandango, etc. Simple, intuitive, 3 - 4 possible actions. You didn't have to choose between Pull and Push, just pick the little hand and that did the trick. Easier, but at least it have you the chance to think about it, should I use the hand, the eyes, the mouth? With RtMI only 2  actions, to see and everything else. That's ridiculous, the game's offers 0 challenge in terms of interactions with objects, characters and landscape. This leads to a super easy game, with puzzles that are so easy that you know what you will need to do, 5 or 6 steps before anything happens. Like if you've been to a location and there was something to interact with, you know exactly what do you need to do next, that combined with the "only one button for actions" makes everything too easy.[Puzzles]All of them super easy, the game presented 0 difficulty at all. I only had one moment that I got stuck, but only because the puzzle was bad. I never had that feeling when you are stuck and when you solve the puzzle you go "Of course it was that, how did I miss it!?". Nope, in RtMI, all the puzzles are easy and there is one, maybe two, that are badly written, the game doesn't give you any hint on what you need to do. When I get a graphic adventure, I want a challenge. When I saw that there were 2 modes, like in other Monkey Islands, I thought it was a good sign, but then, playing it in hard mode, the challenge wasn't there. It was more like a to do list. Which brings me to the To-Do list. Seriously do we need that? Then why do you also introduce the Hints book!? Why on Earth do you have to provide me with a To-Do list!? I know that it's not mandatory to use it, same as the hint book, but I think that everything combined ruin the experience.[Locations]It's fine, a lot of existing locations which are nice to see in this new art style. However, most of the island introduced are useless. You barely have any puzzles there and the only reason why they exist is for you to pick up a few items that you can use somewhere else. I was expecting more locations, more things to do.[Characters]I would be writing for hours if I express all what I think about them. First of all Elaine. Oh my gosh... What have they done with her. They totally ruined her. She is there only to support Guybrush and to tell him nice words, even when he does really bad stuff. I understand all the different theories about it, I don't want to go there so I don't spoil the game, but I haven't read a single post that convinces me why she is like that. My only theory is that there is going to be a DLC in the future where you play with her and you can see the "real" story.LeChuck, useless, the worst LeChuck in the saga. The voice is wrong, his actions and decisions make no sense at all. He is just there to fill the place of bad guy.I could keep going with the Voodoo Lady, Wally, Carla, Otis (this is the worst fan service), etc. The only character that is ok is Stan.[Story]The story is ok, half of the game when it becomes rushed and pointless. There is Elaine's arc that goes nowhere, literally nowhere (which adds up to my theory that she's coming back in form of DLC). There are actions that have a big impact on other people with 0 consequences. And the ending is bad. I have seen this in the past, so I think it's a Ron Gilbert's signature, to have goofy or bad ending. Like the goal is not important but all the steps to get there. But this ending is too much.Anyways, if you reached here and still have some doubts, you love graphic adventures and you have money to spend, go ahead and get this game. It's an ok game, it's a Monkey Island, it has nice graphics. But I would wait until it's on sale. There are better graphics adventures out there. ;(
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Thimbleweed Park is a better Monkey Island 3 than Monkey Island 3.Everything's there. The art style perfectly recaptures the originals while improving it. The ending is zany yet satisfying in its own controversial way. It's hilarious, unpredictable, and comically long, much like this review and The Curse of MI, which makes it so good. It’s a unique, Gilbertesque blend of humor, horror, mystery, sadness, and cartoonish stupidity, miraculously getting you emotionally invested despite its silliness. Gilbert's narrative is something of a signature—he is an incredible storyteller and gifted writer.Return, on the other hand, feels safe and predictable most of the time. You've got to wait til the 4th act to get things moving. The first three fly by before you even realize it and the countdown in your head becomes very hard to ignore. Then, finally, a glimpse of the true adventure, sailing the seas, twisted puzzles between different islands, plethora of objects and characters, an overall plot implying keys and a cinematographic build-up to the conclusion you've waited for years. As it gets closer and closer, with an epic act dragging you above and below, you try to bury all the negative sides, because the ending will obviously make them vanish…Then, of course, the ending sucks.It doesn't suck because it misses the mark or feels incoherent (TP for some of you folks). It sucks because they didn’t try. At all. It really ends with a letter saying, "we're not the same people as a few years ago, and the ending reflects the fact that the things that mattered to us in the 90s… doesn’t really anymore."Which begs the question: if you feel this way, why create a new Monkey Island game in the first place ?Think about it. You decide to return with a new entry in your beloved saga, but you do so with absolute pandering to modern audiences. You decide to indulge in all its whims. You tone everything down like a Netflix show, convinced it's the right thing to do, while repeatedly claiming the game is for die-hard fans first.The main thing left from Monkey Island are references—everywhere, for everyone. It's kind of a "we put everything we had in the blend, so you’re not allowed to complain" situation, when you're mostly looking at an empty shell. The message is something along the lines of: "after all these years of crazy fan theories, it has become impossible to craft a satisfying ending anymore, so there won't be any ending at all."The thing is, I agree with Gilbert. Crafting a fitting ending got harder each year. But that doesn't mean he shouldn't have tried, especially for a game that only exists by some miracle.The thanks you get for playing are authentic, but this absolute act of cowardice of an ending remains unworthy of a pirate. Any ending would have feel better, even the infamous TP one, which is kind of the same. It's sad that after all these years seeking the secret of Monkey Island, the least remembered thing about MI3 will  be the secret itself. I get it—the journey, not the destination. But while Gilbert awkwardly shoves this message in the end-game letter, I feel no less sad and disappointed. And I don't think I should.I don't think the game is bad. It's fun, hilarious at times. The humor is similar to the old titles, if toned down. You'll laugh, have fun, think the ending is nothing expected and move on. But I think MI deserves a little more than that - at least a spot in your brain. Two things: nobody would have talked about this game if it wasn't carrying the Monkey Island IP, and above all, this game wouldn't have been created this way if it wasn't carrying the Monkey Island IP. It's so, so shy. So protective of its own heritage yet so distanced from it. If it was a brand-new game, if it had been created from the ground up, I know for a fact it would have been fiercer, braver, less bland, less paralyzed by the possibility of displeasing. It would have been... Thimbleweed Park.The game is not bad by any means, but it's paradoxical at heart and I try to share my frustration here. It is ultra-referential yet reinventing everything, as if trying to appeal to a modern audience. A modern audience? With a point-and-click? With a 30-year-old saga? My question is, why, why choose your beloved saga to experiment with ? And why make Thimbleweed Park, a new IP, everything a new MI should have been? If this game is for die-hard fans, why not bring a good conclusion and move on? It doesn't make sense to me that Gilbert decided to start everything over for a 30-year-old saga's conclusion. If you want to be the master of the ship, which I understand, why choose your old IP with its unresolved twist? And if you want more MI games, why not bring a fitting conclusion first? How can you think diminishing interactions and making the game waaay easier is a good idea ? Is modern audience reticent to fun ? Does being complacent with modern audience means making the game as least memorable as possible ? What the ♥♥♥♥ is wrong with the character of Elaine (why does she looks like a one-faced robot, why is she acting like Guybrush's mother, why does she always appear from nowhere to give weird, Jiminy Cricket-like advices ??)  WHY CHOOSE MONKEY ISLAND TO EXPERIMENT WITH ??? WHY DIGGING IT OUT OF ITS GRAVE TO STATE THAT THERE WON'T BE ANY ENDING AT ALL ??? Especially when Gilbert seemed to have figured it out years ago and it was apparently different ?It was supposed to be a bittersweet farewell, right? Monkey Island never held back from bringing a tear in an ocean of jokes. However, this particular farewell give the terrible impression of a creator waking up one day to contemplate his work with the cold distance of 30 years and deciding that it is time to smooth things over to ensure his legacy. This is a cruel thing to do to fans who praised your work for being the way it was. I get that time have changed. We all get it. No need to wake up Threepwood from his slumber to teach us a lesson we all know about.(I don't really mind the art style but it surely does nothing to lessen the feeling of blandness.)I've had my fun with this game. But I speak as someone whose favorite game ever is MI2 - I have the right. I thought the game was for me. And I know for a fact that during the vast majority of my playthrough, I was fighting with all my heart a growing feeling of disappointment. My mind was emphasizing the good aspects of the game to make me fall in love with it, which is never a good sign, but also a sign of your investment in a work. And there's something to love here. The humor. The surprising first act. The nostalgia. Not the message of the ending, but the very last sequence, possibly the very last Monkey Island image we'll ever get, which made me sad, in a good way, because it actually looks like a proper farewell.I don't know what to add. I don't think this game is a cashgrab - I think one quality of this game is its sincerity. But at least, Return is not a fatal mistake. Gilbert is at least right when he says the ending is less important than the journey, even if MI is the one saga you can't say that about. (Too bad.) This statement, though, is only valid if Return isn't the last of its kind. You don't bring MI back from the dead, subvert everyone expectations in a mid way, only to forget everything again. You only do it if you want to build something new from the ground up. So this game at least made me curious for the rest.While not bad, I think Return is only a down in a saga which had its shares of ups and downs. In my dreams, Gilbert makes a sequel to Return which doesn't even need to be the proper MI3 : just its own thing. Not limiting itself for a weird, misplaced, half-imaginary new audience. (You know, kinda like TP didn't give a ♥♥♥♥ about pleasing anyone because it knew how sparse the demand is for point-and-clicks today). So, the first MI ark is over and I'm fine with it - but only in the prospect of sailing stranger seas.

_childDocuments_.review: Been a huge fan of the series, especially the first two, since the beginning when I loaded it from 5.25" floppy disks...and I think this one is the worst in series by far.  Everything feels wrong, from the plot to the art; even the inventory system feels like a weird step backwards.  The puzzles aren't difficult or clever.  I was really excited to hear Ron Gilbert would be back on board, I figured we'd get the characters' original personalities and humor back with one of the original team on board.  But that's not at all the case, if anything it feels even further from the original games.  Maybe Ron forgot how to make a Monkey Island game, or maybe he wasn't the key to begin with and it was other members who really brought the magic.  Who knows.  There's word of a Maniac Mansion re-boot, which is a shame because that's another classic that will probably be ruined just like this one.What a disappointment.  I'm thinking the real Secret of Monkey Island is that Ron isn't the secret sauce to the franchise.(if you're looking for a Secret of Monkey Island experience that's true to the originals, check out the DLC for Sea of Thieves.  it's not a point and click adventure but it's outstanding)

_childDocuments_.review: Curse of Monkey Island was already the best ending to this series. Everything after it really hasn't lived up to the legend of the first two, or the greatness of Curse.
