_childDocuments_.review: What can i say about this game? It exceeded all my expectations. I loved the graphics, plot, puzzle, music and jokes. This made me feel like a little child again as if i was playing the first game so many years ago. I`m sure the ending will be received mixed by many but i absolutely loved it! It was kind off what i had theorized many years ago and it also allows that all the games in the sage to exist, be explained and coexist in the same universe and this is beautiful. Hope to see the teased sequel at the end soon!Highly recommended game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Ron Gilbert did it again!We finally get the conclusion of the vision he had for The Secret of Monkey Island and Monkey Island 2 - LeChuck's Revenge. Is it the ending we were waiting for? Probably not, but I am so happy to finally have his idea for this trilogy.Guybrush Threepwood is back, voiced brilliantly by Dominic Armato, who gives him incredible charm and charisma. He wanted to become a pirate in previous games, even though he looks more like a flooring inspector. Now he is decided to finally uncover The Secret of Monkey Island.As soon as I started playing the game I was immediately brought back to the Monkey Island world. There is a lot of nostalgia involved, but at the same time things are different. But most importantly this is Monkey Island, with its usual sense humor and fun gameplay.Being back to Mêlée Island is like being back home, and although the graphical style was controversial at first, it actually works well in motion, with lots of small details and funny close-ups. I am glad they went back to 2d graphics with this game, especially because they are modernized with lots of beautiful animation and effects, such as zooming in.The gameplay seems streamlined, but it still retains that feeling of discovery and joy when you solve a puzzle. Point and click gameplay is back, streamlined and faster, but playing with a gamepad is also quite effective. I miss some more silly interactions between the objects though. I consider this game has a lot of potential for having DLC that will include more stuff.But the best thing about this game is the music! Simply masterful and familiar, while fresh and new. There is interactive music as you move from place to place, but nothing at the same level of Woodtick in MI2, but it's still amazing.The ending is going to be incredibly controversial and I am still figuring it out. Inititally I was very disappointed, but after thinking about it some more I think it is quite brilliant. Anyway, it is unique, but people will be talking about it for a long time.This is definitely a worthwhile closure to The Secret of Monkey Island trilogy. Thank you, Ron Gilbert and everyone involved for bringing back this amazing series.How appropriate! You fight like a cow!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is my selected title for the GOTY on the Steam Awards 2022, this is how much I loved this game.No surprise, I'm a LOOONG time fan of the series, since it's original debut that I have played on Amiga 500.This is what hardcore fans have waited patiently for decades. Ron Gilbert was able to be respectful of all the other titles in the series (inlcuding the ones not developed by him) but still be coherent with his first two games (and the pecular ending of the second chapter) and craft a game that is fun but is also aware that time has passed and fans of the game are grown too. This lead also to the only limit of the game: you can play it without having played the other games before and still get some enjoyment but it's pretty clear that you have to play the other titles before this one to get the best experience from it.Apart that, the game have a simple interface and the art stile is not bad as I though when I've seen the first screenshots, you get used to it. Some people say it's too simple and I can understand that but to me wasn't really a prominent thing and I think that the "book of progressive hint system" inserted in the game is a good idea.Maybe it can't be equally loved by everyone but this game is truly a love letter to fans of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to fans of the Monkey Island series.  In the beginning I wasn't happy with the art direction but that all faded away in a comfortable nostalgic vapor.  I began to remember when I played that first Monkey Island game so many years ago.  Looking up on the top of my bookshelf I saw the big box copy of Curse of Monkey Island and all those memories came flooding back as well.  This is a series that in many ways began my gaming career that has lasted 30+ years now.  Each time a game would release I would revisit all these wonderful characters again that somehow feel like family.    Through college, marriage, having kids, and empty nest syndrome - these games provided something special at each step throughout the years and this game really hit home with closure I wasn't expecting.  I sense this is the end for this series and I am both happy and sad.  All good things come to an end and this was a fitting conclusion to the story and all the meaning behind it.  For those who think gaming is merely for fun, a momentary respite from whatever is bothering you that day I am here to tell you that is wrong.  Games like these touch you and bond with you, almost like a silent companion through the years.  If this is truly the end, I feel blessed to have been there are the beginning marveling at those amazing pixelated graphics cursing trying to get my PC to run it.If for some reason you are buying this game before playing all the others, but it, but don't play it.  Yet.  Just do yourself a favor and take the time to play through the previous 5 games.  This will mean so much more if you do.I tip my hat to all the developers who worked on these games through the years.May the secret live on forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Love it so far and I expected nothing less, music and story so far everything has been wonderful I look forward to the rest of the game.UPDATE:Just finished the game and I loved every second of it I'm really glad Ron and his fellow cohorts made another game with a powerful message too top it off, well done i'm probably gonna play the entire series now thanks for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original back Monkey Islands back in the day on the day and loved them.   I know that's the demographic for these games, the nostalgia of the older games for those who played them.  Perhaps it's probably just me but I don't find these point and click games quite as much fun as I used to.  It still is worthwhile if you are a fan of the older games for sure.   Same witty Guybrush Threepwood humour.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Waited for this half a lifespan (hopefully at least). It's colorfull & fun & easier than former parts. Not salvaging it is an act of crime boodthirsty pirates!Some Issues I have with the plot, but this game is about the ride (joy of life) not the picky details. _childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The good: It's Monkey Island, lots of old characters, good dialogue, memorable settings.The bad: The new art style, they took away they "talk/take/look" coin and it just decided what to do for you, the art style, the game is too easy and the puzzles aren't hard because the dialogue basically gives everything away and they also give you a hint book on top of that, the art style.I am giving it a thumbs up because I love this franchise and would love to see another made in the future. Hopefully one that fixes some of the mistakes this one made.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A tentative yes. Between an unpolished ending and reliance on older entries for some of its narrative beats, Return to Monkey Island is best enjoyed by long-time fans of the adventure game genre and Monkey Island itself.With that said, I enjoyed the game while playing it, and had several laugh out loud moments while playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Having played pretty much all older MIs, I genuinely liked it and had fun playing it three (four?) times to get all achievements, yay. Humor, characters, voiceover (english), all nicely done. The ending though. Well, a lot has been said already. It felt rushed and inappropriate to say the least. This would cost at least a star or two but since Steam only allows Yes/No recommendations, I will go with a firm yes.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing to see Guybrush return, after all these long years.Its fantastic to see how Ron & Dave have weaved the stories in such a fashion that it respects the non Ron iterations by gently touching upon the better bits of them, and simply ignoring the parts that aren't useful to the plot.Amazingly well done, tying up loose ends that have gained a cult status of their own.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It was everything I expected and then some. The visual style is perfect, the narrative is witty and funny as any of the previous games and most of all, the game is just so fluid, the controls (a small innovation, but a great one) and the gameplay were so comfortable and enjoyable. Props to Ron and his team, and I hope we have many more to come!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Very disappointing, it pains me to write a negative review for this as I had been waiting and excited for this game for a long time but I have too be honest, I am a bit confused by all the positive reviews after playing this and after checking some of the negative ones I agree with many of what they have pointed out. This doesn't feel like a Monkey Island game, the story is lacklustre and feels rushed at times and incomplete. The overall tone is depressing and devoid of the fun excitement the original games elicited. The art style is fine and you get used to it but the story and writing is just terrible and feels like a very hollow game with not enough to do or explore compared to the originals.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: For now, it's everything I ever wanted it to be!Art, music, dialogs and voice actors are incredibly well done and simply on point, just what you'd expect from Monkey Island.If you're a fan of the series you'll feel right at home.Besides that: It plays perfectly well on the Steam Deck too!You can even lower the TDP and GPU clock _way_ down to save some battery while still hitting 30 frames (locked) with ease, even in docked mode.Well done folks!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: After 30 years, it's unbelievable to witness a game as pleasant to play as the first two.If you are a long time Monkey Island fan, play this game until the end, then read the scrapbook.This game is good for newcomers too, you will enjoy sharp humour, funny dialogues and smart puzzles.Thank you guys for this unexpected gem.9/10Oh and the music, the music is 11/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the art style.Loved how Elaine and Guybrush interacted.Loved the beginning, ending and the middle part. It's adorable all steps on the way.It's perhaps not for everyone and that's okay. But everyone who hates this masterpiece, for it's art style or how it doesn't fit their "head canon" or whatever is an idiot.Would buy the T-Shirt.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is the Monkey Island I have been waiting for! I somehow missed the announcement in April, and only just found out a new Monkey Island game had been released. I bought it immediately. Chose "hard mode" and started playing. I'm only a bit into the game, but this is exactly what Monkey Island was, and should be. Thank you Ron for taking on this game once again, and delivering sublime work! Anyone who has played Monkey Island 1 & 2 original and/or remakes should buy this immediately. Anyone new to Monkey Island, buy the 1 & 2 remakes, and play them! There is also Monkey Island 3, which is also great but was never remade into modern graphics, and Monkey Island 4, which you can safely skip. Play the 1 & 2 remakes, then this game and you will be right where you need to be, including all the history you need!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic entry in the series. I've played the first three games repeatedly over the years, and playing a new entry that feels as good as the others is a pretty great experience.I wish it was a bit longer (my wife and I both played our own games, so it took us an average of 8.5 hours to finish the game), but only because I didn't want the game to finish, not because I felt it was actually short.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Monkey Island fan that's been playing these games since the 90s, I had extremely high expectations for this game. After playing it this week my expectations were absolutely blow away. Man.... I loved this game! Clever, engaging, absolutely gorgeous, and so much fun! And not to give anything away, but I really liked how they tied up the whole series plus gave us plenty more to think about for the next 30 years!I don't know how else to describe it, but this game is a masterpiece!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: What a great return. Monkey Island was the first game I bought back in 1998 after playing the demo from a now discontinued PC Gaming Magazine. It would be very hard for me to not like a Monkey Island game and I loved it.I would have been happier if the art style was like Curse of the Monkey Island (MI3) but this doesn't mean the current one isn't enjoyable.If you like goofy adventure games, very easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't love the ending, art style grew on me, but didn't love it, voice acting is fantastic, puzzles were good, but felt there were a bit too many "find 3 of these things" type ones, game spends a bit too much time on LeChucks ship.But overall liked it a lot, was surprised how much is felt like the original games. PLOT SPOILERS BELOWFelt like the creators were annoyed at me for wanting to know what the secret was, I agree that whatever it is (not that I think they have defined what it is) probably won't live up to expectations, but in that case don't make a game centred around it, the other games managed to have a solid plot without using Monkey Island at all.Another gripe I have with the plot is that is makes a point to show Guybrush's trail of destruction in his relentless pursuit of the secret, and Elaine calls him up on it, only for nothing to happen? Thought we might get a kind of Last Crusade type ending where Guybrush gives up the secret in order to save himself or Elaine or something, but just nothing happened, we get a weird meta ending of being at a theme park again. Was all a bit anti climatic.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: As an homage to Monkey Island 2 (1991), the game tries really hard to copy the humour of its predecessor. IMHO it only partly worked. If you like this kind of humour, you will find this one ok or sometimes too absurd to be funny.While being a homage, it fails to try somehting new and fresh within the Monky Island "universe", but only warms-up old ideas and themes.My biggest gripe are the graphics or art style. It's something between lazy and plain ugly, mostly without any details and with strange comic-ish proportions. Yes, it's a humorous adventure, but why make it look like a game for preschoolers??
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful and incredibly fulfilling experience. To put it in perspective, Secret has been one of my favorite games since playing it as a young child in the very early '90s. Revenge was great, Curse was fantastic, Escape... let's just not talk about it, and Tales were fun. I'm not usually one to write reviews, but having just finished this game I feel I need to get some things off my chest and record some thoughts for posterity, mostly addressing what I think are some of the most contentious points of the game.To start with, the art. The screenshots looked awful. They reminded me of Flash games. However, after the initial in-game shock, the art grew on me until I cannot visualize this chapter of the Monkey Island saga in any other way. I have no qualms with the art direction for this game, and in hindsight I think it turned out wonderful, and truly lent the game a whimsical and fun atmosphere.Next, the puzzles. These were maybe too much on the easy side, but I do appreciate that there weren't any that were overly obtuse or incoherent- I never felt that my time was being wasted. That being said, I never really once had to sit and wonder what the solution to an issue was going to be- it was always somewhat obvious, and solving the puzzle just became a matter of clicking through to execute the right steps in the right order. But again, on the flip side, the writing was clever and fun, and I thoroughly enjoyed the ride and the challenges along the way.The interface is probably over-simplified. I don't want to say "dumbed down", but as an avid adventure gamer, it seemed far too straight forward and hand-holdy (even more so when you consider the "highlight objects" key!). This certainly contributes to the less-than-challenging puzzles, as mentioned above. But, it was clean and it works for what it needs to do.The overall environment and story were fantastic. Some of the islands are pretty bare, but the game certainly already has enough to do. The ending is great. The message at the end is great. I absolutely appreciate what they are doing and saying, and I feel it works. It works enough that I felt I needed to write this. Again, what a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: First of all i'm a huge fan of Monkey island saga once it was probably the first game I played on a desktop, so yes im playing monkey island saga since the very first one. Second I'd really like to give congratulations to the devs that spend time building this. Third, a review to the game, IMHO I'd say that all the mechanics, story, humour and the puzzles kept the original way it was. I really didn't thought it was possible, but it is! The art is different but I got used to it very fast, for sure not disapointed. Thanks once again to every single person envolved in game to give me the opportunity to travel more than 30 years in time :D. I'll be anxious expecting a continuation! Please don't give up on this masterpiece saga.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A long time ago, in 1988, mother of all adventure games was made, the magnum opus of Ron Gilbert, what I would like to call, the best adventure game of all time - Secret of Monkey Island. A couple of years later, a sequel came out, and for those of you who played it, you know how it ends, and you know many questions were asked. But those questions were left unanswered for decades...Until this game was announcedReturn To Monkey Island is one of the few games I actually pre ordered it, simply because to me, Monkey Island series holds a special place in myself. It is more than a game, it's an experience. As soon as I heard Ron Gilbert made this, I rushed to buy it.And honestly, I don't regret a single bit. I don't really care about the art style, I even like it to some extent. This game is a love letter to Monkey Island fans. Even if Rob Gilbert wasn't involved in Curse, Escape and Tales, I love that he at least acknowledged them.IMO every monkey island fan should play this game. It continues where Monkey Island 2 left off and you get to finally find out the secret of monkey island. I won't spoil the ending but I can say, it is a good ending.Thank you Ron Gilbert, for this epic return! Full thumbs up to this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely recommended. An near-excellent level of polished point and click adventure with good humor and fun dialogue, a good continuation to the story of Guybrush and a nice epilogue for his search for the Secret of Monkey Island. Great music, very reminiscent of the original tracks of the first games in the series. I would just leave the game on the main screen on some other game locations just to listen to the music playing in the background -- probably why I have so many hours logged in the game.I've mainly played in Hard Mode, with the Writer's Cut enabled, and the game did not feel short at all. I'd say it's just about the right length for me. It also didn't seem to have its pace ruined by the Writer's Cut, not for me anyway, so I'd recommend enabling that too.Puzzles are decent. No absurd solutions. Only one puzzle really gave me a bit of a hard time, but in the end it was solvable without hints. However, since there's also a hint book integrated in-game, I don't expect people will get stuck anywhere.All in all a great addition to the Monkey Island series.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: As a kid, I played the original Monkey Island games (along with pretty much every other Lucasfilm adventure puzzle game like Loom and Indiana Jones).  Fast forward 30 years later, and I bought this game so that I could play with my daughter, and hopefully show her how games were when I was a kid (rather than the Roblox crap that she plays now).  I am not sure if it was intentional or not, but one of the things that we enjoy most about this game is how the game is told through the eyes of Guybrush's kid.  By starting the game playing as the kid, it got my daughter interested in the game, and then when the "real" game started she was like "oh now we get to play the dad".
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: What a loving and appropriate tribute to the original games this was. Not only is it funny, charming and enjoyable throughout, it does something I didn't think possible - it rescues the series from the strange limbo the ending of Monkey Island 2 left us in all those years ago and it does so with grace and humour. Considered in isolation this probably isn't the best video game you could spend your money on. It took me 12 hours to get through, and not all of those were perfect. The occasional puzzle falls flat and the humour is more chuckle-worthy than it is riotously funny. But if you are in any way a fan of the original Monkey Island games and have the time and cash to spare on a dozen hours of closure, then this is a beautiful love letter to the series and I'll recommend it in a heartbeat. I'm so delighted this was made.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This wasn't the adventure I had hoped for. Return to Monkey Island reuses a lot of old locations, but most of them feel small and limited. Places on the map that you could explore in Monkey Island 1 are now gone. The new islands in this game are very small and feature only a couple rooms. The puzzles feel very straightforward and end up being simple fetch quests half of the time. You spend a lot of time getting keys, but most of them you can just pick up without a puzzle. That doesn't feel rewarding. There's also a whole island that features only a single simple maze puzzle. Some of the story lines are unfinished. Characters are just forgotten or ignored towards the end and plot lines dropped without a satisfying resolution.The game takes the ending of MI2 (which I absolutely hated) and made it a main part of the story. Unfortunatelly the game constantly pulls you out of the main story, which breaks the immersion. I had hoped for an adventure game that could stand on its own, like Curse of Monkey Island. Instead I got a game that overly relies on nostalgia and is average at best on its own. Overall the game felt a bit rushed and it could have been much better if more effort had been put in to flesh out the locations, dialogues, puzzles and story lines. I can only recommend this game to people who loved the idea of MI2's ending and want a quick and easy nostalgia fix featuring Monkey Island 1's location and characters. Don't pay more than 20 bucks for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Once again, the dialogues are fantastic with great flow and absolutely awesome sense of humor. There are some brilliant moments here and there of genuine Monkey Island entertainment.- Crazy story full of twists, unexpected events and dozens of obstacles in Guybrush's way to succession. Exactly what someone would expect from an episode of the series.- Amazing voice acting performances that fit perfectly each character. Of course it's great that Dominic Armato is back as Guybrush Threepwood.- Responsive controls with fast walking and double click for running. You can cancel any action by clicking somewhere else, you can skip dialogues or roll back. Everything feels smooth unlike many slow burn (controlwise) point and click adventures out there.- The iconic Monkey Island theme is here along with some more well known music scores (e.g. LeChuck's theme). Awesome music.- Although I think that these minimalistic, geometric visuals are not the best fit for the series they are absolutely gorgeous. The neon chromatic palette is great and some frames are pieces of pure art.- A lot of beloved characters and tons of references to the previous episodes of the series. If you 've played them, you 'll probably love it. If not, this may be a problem.- The overall design is pretty clear in order to help you find all the clickable objects and avoid annoying pixel hunting. In addition, if you need it, there's a button that reveals all the possible on screen interactions.- The sketchbook that briefly tells you about Guybrush's previous adventures is a nice, well designed addition.- Well built hint system that helps you in several stages instead of instantly telling you the whole solution. Better find it on your own, but it's there if you need a small push.- Although trivia cards don't really add anything to the gameplay, I found it pretty enjoyable to collect and answer them.- Emotional, allegoric, surreal ending. You won't see it coming but, if you love this series, you will find it pretty touching.The bad- Way to many old characters and references to evets of previous episodes. In fact if you 're new in the series I doubt that you 'll manage to enjoy it or even understand most of it. Also new characters are shallow and new locations aren't that remarkable making the game even more unbalanced. It's more of a throwback or an emotional ending from the series' original creators than a real new episode.- The most simplistic puzzles that have ever existed in a Monkey Island game with too many obvious helping hints. Especially during the first three parts everything is so linear and pretty straight forward and even the combinations between the objects in your inventory are rare. I expected something more clever and inspirational.- Interactions are shallow. First thing first, you can only perform one specific suggested action with each interactive object. Forget multiple options like "push", "pull" etc. that were giving many alternatives and deeper gameplay. Also you can interact with only two or three objects in most of the screens so the world feels much less alive. Guybrush doesn't react at all when you try various wrong combinations (there's usually just a visual "X") or gives you some simplistic, generic comments. These answers were usually the most enjoyable. A lot of fun is missing here.- Visuals are artistic for sure, but I felt that they ruined the game's atmosphere and personality. It's more about fancy, pop or even childish aesthetics than pirate dirtiness and grog beer. Most of the characters feel cold and distant like they have missed their pirate soul. I pretty much liked Guybrush though, but this has probably more to do with the voice.- I don't really get the easy mode especially when there is already a hints book. It just alters the game's personality. Let the new gamers have the full point and click adventure experience or even stack somewhere for a while. We played the first episodes back then without even having an internet connection.- This is not a really crucial element of the game, but animations are a bit clunky and cheap like they were made in some old flash application.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished it and I loved it! It is a great game!I am one of those old fans who played Monkey Island and lots of point-and-click adventure games in the 90s (and always preferred the LucasArts ones). I am not a gamer; in the last few years, the only games I played were Broken Age and Thimbleweed Park. I liked them both, but I think RtMI is the best of the three. Certainly, there is some nostalgia influence here, but not only that. All three are equally funny, but the mechanics, the somewhat nuanced story, the connection between puzzles, and the puzzles themselves are all perfected in RtMI.There are a lot of small, good ideas in the game that adds up; I'll list a few. The scrapbook, for those of us who didn't replay the old games, is an excellent reminder of the stories -- and has a great addition once you finish the game, don't miss it! The hint book; it is well done, useful to keep you going. I used it twice. Once I had the right reasoning, but I didn't get a hint of what I should do precisely in the dialog. The other time, I also had the right reasoning but didn't know I could expand an item in the inventory. Much glad the hint book was there so I could just continue with the game (and since I had the right reasoning, I felt it was a cheat, I felt good completing the puzzles). The dialogs guiding you on what you have to do are great too. The action stated in the cursor, great idea! The tab key for showing clickable spots; very handy! Multiple uses of the same inventory items in different puzzles, I like that! The trivia book is an interesting meta-game, but I wasn't getting many correct answers. Probably fun for some people, but I wasn't caring much about it in the end -- but I still picked up every trivia card I saw.  The to-do list is great for keeping track of what you are doing and have to do.Production-wise, art is great and really works; voice-acting is awesome. Really good job!Story-wise, I loved it! The first half, or even the first two-thirds, it is a good story but as good as other good adventure games (comparing mostly to Thimbleweed Park and Broken Age). But when you start to reach the end, you notice some very interesting nuances in the story; what the characters are saying starts to get some layers. Not only meta comments, typical of Ron Gilbert, but deeper nuanced meta comments. The game gets a bit closer to us, older people, playing it. The end is very connected to that and I liked it a lot. I won't comment on the ending to not spoil anyone, but it is an ending that lets you appreciate some things while purposefully not corresponding to some common expectations. It is a choice that I respect as art, intrinsically, but also I really enjoyed it myself. The last addition to the scrapbook after you finish the game also adds to that, giving more meaning to the end, I felt. Well worth taking a look.Summary: the mechanics are perfected for point-and-click adventure games! After decades of learning, this really is it! It would be nice to get other games from other creators using Ron Gilbert's Dinky engine. The art and voice-acting are phenomenal, great at giving awe and immersion at all times. The story is funny as expected, starts more of the same, but gets an interesting, nuanced turn at the end that puts it to a new level compared to other adventure games. The puzzles are at the correct level of difficulty to match my personal taste. Not too hard, not too easy (I played the complete version). Mostly satisfying. Sometimes I would see they were adding just one too many steps to solve a particular but never crossed the line of being annoying.Overall, 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is ALMOST everything I could have ever wanted in a new Monkey Island game. 2D point and click, good puzzles, funny, well-written, original voice cast (aside from Earl Boen as LeChuck who has now retired, Jess Harnell does a great job) a fun new art style (don't act like this isn't a series staple) and let's not forget an ending that will keep people talking.But ever since Curse, I've wanted another open seas piracy minigame. Some kind of new twist on insult swordfighting and ship-to-ship combat. Maybe I should count my blessings in case we got another Monkey Kombat somehow, but that one little extra touch would have made this perfect in my eyes.BUT that's not what this game is about. This game is about the folly of regret. Revisiting the past and wondering what you're supposed to do when you get there. It's about being old and looking back.I relate.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It captivated me from the beginning to the end. Art style is wonderful, looks amazing in motion and will get awards despite what people who don't understand what pixel art is are saying. This game has so much warmth, that playing it makes you feel at home and you don't want it to end. It's also incredibly self aware and it communicates its message not through dialogues or the story but through what it is - if you will get it, you will get it, just like it is with art. If you won't, you will write a negative review.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It think this game is a little gem in times of too many expensive but repetitive AAA titles and never finished early access stuff. The humor, the puzzles, dialogue, music and voice acting. All are exquisitely done with tons of love. This is a trip back to the good old days of gaming.And yes, personally, I love the unconventional graphics as well. This cranky graphic novel style is normally not really my thing, but when I gave it a chance I found the vivid colors and clear lines kinda .. expressionist. It carries the ambiance and feelings of locations and characters extremely well.All in all, definitely worth playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I finally finished and it was a blast.Indeed the trip down memory lane was the main selling point, but in the end it's indeed the good game that was announced.The music is there (of course up to these times in quality).The game is there: simple point and click,  slick and intuitive interface, a pleasure to go around the locations.The cartoony art fits the theme perfectly, although at first I felt it "odd".The wit and humor is there - now with voices!The hint book ... it's a bit the "meh" part, in these days of internet it probably wasn't needed, but at the same time it was just feeding you the same hints that 30 years ago friends playing the game would do to push you to the end, without spoiling too much.Thank you mr Gilbert, thank you all at Terrible Toybox.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure Ron Gilbert had fun making this, I did not enjoy it as much.As many others who came across this title I played the first and second chapters of Monkey Island when they came out some years ago. I fell in love with the perfect formula: amazing new computer games, pirates, funny mechanics and great puzzles. Guybrush and friends are still with me o consoles. mobiles and any device where I can get my copies of the game to run.I got very frustrated as games on Monkey Island were developed and looked less and less of what I loved in the first two chapters. The Curse of Monkey Island was still ok but I can barely remember the names of the others that YES I did buy and played hoping for a comeback of the series.Then Ron Gilbert came back on with Thimbleweed Park: a game that I truly loved, made me smile and presented some cool cameos from the Monkey Island series that I loved and when The Return was announced was full of hope. Eventually I got to see the "new" art style in a youtube video and man I was disappointed. No I don't like the new characters, they are just ghosts of what MK 1-2 was and as consumer I feel totally entitled to express my opinion (which you should care about if you are reading this otherwise why bother?). Still as fan of the game I did buy this and had some fun with few puzzles even though they all seemed pretty straightforward and in many cases very shallow. The game in general seems more a cruel way to show how this was all a child play. The ending is simply unbearable and make me think that this is the last game from Mr R. Gilbert I'll ever play.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Watch out, a three headed monkey! Happy me! It is great to go back in time and remeber all the good stuff of Monkey Island. Overall it is a great game, but some fact are a bit ... strange?!? I miss the humor of the old days. There could be more sarcassm!I love the new graphic style. It fits the time. But I do know, that many people dislike the style.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a looooong time MI fan! I even played through all 3 of the first ones leading up to playing return to MI... Wow, what a disappointment.Firstly, the art direction. What were they thinking?! Compared to MI 3, which had so much imagination and visual detail, this feels like a barren and creatively bankrupt made-for-Netflix kids cartoon. Why does Guybrush look like a red nose alcoholic? Why did Le Chuck's voice change? Why did you replace the pirate leaders with an obnoxious group of characters that don't seem to thematically fit within the world they've built. I was hoping I'd get used to it, but wow. Terrible.Then the puzzles. The first half is a breeze to the point where it's kinda boring. The story line meanders and there's no over arching goal that motivates one to play. Then the 2nd half of the game (once it opens up) is full of obtuse "why would I think to combine those things" puzzles and the storyline gets even more muddled.Realistically, they were never going to live up to expectations. But quite frankly they did an even worse job than I would have expected.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't quite achieve the glory days of the old point and click adventures but is a fun and satisfying experience that if you are a Monkey Island fan will tick all the essential boxes from humour to obscure puzzles.Just wish there was more insult sword fighting and some of the puzzles had more steps you had to put together like games of old.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the prologue and I am already in love with it. The art style flows well and the humor is already showing how cheeky it can be. Return to Monkey Island tells a wholesome and compelling tale of swashbuckling shenanigans that should appeal to anyone seeking a hearty adventure on the high seas.It is a game for the series' fans. There's a scrapbook on the main menu that recounts the events of past games, but it's light on specifics and feels more like a refresher course than a vital tool for newcomers to catch up on previous adventures. Returning players will adore the fan service and familiar sense of warmth that permeates the whole experience, yet it still strives to make itself somewhat approachable for beginners. There's no denying that certain elements will be lost without that decades-old connection, but having a history with the series isn't essential to enjoy Guybrush Threepwood's latest escapade. 5 previous games. All are available on Steam. The first two were pixel games but we're remastered and voice added. The third game is traditional animation. It has a new creative team. The fourth game has a new creative team again and the series moved into 3D. It's generally considered the worst. The fifth game was a co production with Telltale and is made up of 5 episodes. It sort of trades a sequel but around about that time the Lucasarts was bought by Disney so no follow up was worked on.This game is helmet by the original creator of the first two games.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge fan of Monkey Island since I was a kid, and I was VERY excited for a new installment -- and it did not disappoint. The puzzles were excellent, the writing and humor were true to the series, and they got the voice actors back.Any nitpicks I have are pretty minor (there are a couple of meta moments, where the developers are essentially speaking to the fans, that I found annoying). But they are far outweighed by the excellence of the rest of the game.I highly recommend this game to Monkey Island fans and people who haven't played a Monkey Island before.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

Because I was getting into it like... 7/10 getting into. I expected more from the way the story was being told. It left me with a weird sense of disappointment and tiredness. Even Escape didn't make me feel this wronged hence the low scoreI had a few laughs. I'll take that with me and move on to the next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I had been thinking Thimbleweed Park might be Ron's best game.  I am now thinking Monkey Island 3 (aka Return to Monkey Island) is probably his best.  The whole team knocked it out of the park.  The fan service is real, but new folks will love it just as much.  What a one-two nostalgia punch so strong even newbies will kind of get it.I am on part 3, and I'm an adventure game veteran, also a Monkey Island veteran (have played 1 countless times and seem to replay both 1 and 2 every 5-10 years).  I am not using the hint book, if I can help it.  Usually when I do need a hint, it's something that was obvious that I missed.DON'T USE THE HINTS!I'll be back after I finish the game, although I may also want to play it in Writer's Cut mode first too.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Here it is, the sequel to the legendary adventure series Monkey Island and the question is: Was it worth the wait?To me, the answer is a yes. A mild one, but nevertheless it's positive.Which wasn't a given, as i wasn't a fan of the new look of Guybrush. With his blocky face, red nose-tip (a kind of phallic nose in general) and his stubble beard he resembled a drunkard more than the character i fell in love with all those years ago.But in-game it turned out to be less of an issue to me, i got used to it and the humour, the characters and world made up for that design decision.It's most definitely also a more divisive game, considering some design and story-decisions, but personally i think they have found a way to make it work (mostly).Now, while i've already mentioned Guybrush's design, i'd say the overall artstyle, is quite fine. I do think some characters look a bit weird or clash a bit with the style, but it's few and far in between and overall i quite enjoyed it.As for the gameplay, you probably already noticed that there's no verb interface. Gone are the days where you clicked on "Talk", "Open", "Use" or others, now it's either right or left-click on items, characters and other hotspots.It's streamlined and i'd say it works in favour of a proper pacing, even though you might lose some funny commentary when trying out different, not obvious combinations.I'd say the difficulty of puzzles is mostly fin but even if you're stuck, you do get a hint book you can use. There was however one situation in the very last puzzle where i was stuck for longer than i'd like to admit, because i didn't see an item that helped with solving a puzzle.As for the world and characters, you will see a lot of familiar faces and they're all brought to life through fantastic voice acting and animations.The world itself and the different islands and places you visit look fine, though you also do visit familiar places you already know from the series. I would have loved to see a few more new things i haven't already been to.So, how does the story hold up and can it bring the series to a satisfying end?Well, i guess this is the part where players might have a very differing opinion.Personally, i think they did something that a lot of players might not have been expected, but in my eyes tied things together quite neatly. It might not been what people wanted or expected, but then again, i doubt anything could have satisfied all or the vast majority of them.I can see how what they did is divisive, but i also did smile at the end and was glad i could have a last "Goodbye", a last ride with the characters in the world of Guybrush Threepwood, LeChuck, Elaine Marley, Murray, the Voodoo Lady, Stan, Otis and all the others.I guess the journey IS more important than the end itself.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game that pays homage to the old games without just feeling like giant fan service. As someone who played the old games as a teenager, Return to Monkey Island feels solid!  And if you're curious, you can turn off the voice acting and just do text to get that old graphic adventure feel. Will give you both a "casual" and "hardcore" option for puzzle difficulties.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long time fan of the Monkey Island series. For Monkey island 6, I  Love The humour, story telling, voice acting and all the puzzles.  The art style is also very cute and pleasing, not quite as good MI 3, but I'm glad they stuck with it. _childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I whole wholeheartedly recommend this game.  Return To Monkey Island captures everything about the series that one would expect.  The humor, the puzzles, the music, everything is great about it in my opinion.  Challenging without being frustratingly difficult.  If you are looking for a nostalgic return to the point and click games of old, Return To Monkey Island definitely scratches that itch.  The complaints about the art style are complete nonsense.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Gaming back in the 90s was a bit more intimate, closer, and something more special than today's affairs. Monkey Island feels like a passage of time, an adventure for the ages that's been told for over 30 years - It's very much your favourite series of books, you've finished them - but did you really want to reach the end? Monkey Island has always had a very self-reflective, meta angle to its storytelling, the framework is unfailingly genuine and surprising. Having played this in my early teens on my trusty Commodore Amiga I am now finally getting to play what I consider the true third chapter into my late 30s. Will I finally discover the secret of Monkey Island? Chasing that golden monkey, a treasure I've discussed time and time again, only I didn't have a map, it was internet forums, I didn't have a compass, It was a dial-up modem. I didn't have the three trials it was 14 floppy discs and a wish the original team would grace us with a sequel. These stories, adventures, characters mean so much more to us than pixels on a screen, their progression and lives arc with ours. A truly great adventure. Thank you MI team - its been emotional.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It's tragic I have to do this, but I can't recommend this game for one simple reason: the ending is not only terrible, but it is abrupt and nonsensical.Before the end, the game is slow to start (the intro really turned me off), but it gets progressively better and better, leading to some really brilliant Monkey Island moments.There's bags of nostalgia, brilliant puzzles, fantastic dialogue and plenty of varied items and locations.The art style wasn't really my thing at first, but it really grows on you, the animation however leaves a lot to be desired and in a lot of places feels cheap and lazy (I'm sure it wasn't, but it comes across that way).Along the way you start to get the impression that the game was never finished. There are huge areas with nothing in them, and things that seem completely unfinished. There's glyphs on walls that you notice and comment on, but never come into the game (unless I just missed it?), items that seem like they should come in to play at a later time and never do, areas that seem like they should have a meaning later, but never do. It doesn't really take away from what IS there, but it starts to paint a picture of a game that was never properly finished.All-in-all, I was a solid 8/10 before the last 10 minutes. But then - it's just... Awful.I get what they were going for, and there's even a little easter-egg in the menu at the end that tries to explain their thinking behind the direction, but it didn't work on any level.There are multiple endings, but they are basically all derived from the same abrupt, ridiculous scene at the end, and can all be played through by re-loading the very end and making slightly different choices. They are all very brief, boring, and in no way satisfying or fulfilling. I was  couch-playing this with 3 other people, and all of us were completely shocked and in disbelief by how terribly shoehorned the ending was.It's tragic. It shouldn't have happened. This game was going to be a strong recommendation, but I just can't.I just can't.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I believe I'm about 3/4 through the game at this point, and I am loving every second of it. This is just about the perfect Monkey Island game to me. It has all of the trademark humor, music, sound, puzzle style, dialogue... Everything basically!It's extremely well crafted! And it oozes of love for the series. You can really tell that the entire team working on it has poured their hearts and souls into it. I love the art style! The attention to detail in the environments and the animations is next level.I love how, when you load a save game, you are presented with a "Do you remember where you're at" scene that, if you choose to hear it out, tells you what's going on at the point you're at. You might think that you would know this, right? Well, yes, but if it's been a couple days between sessions, it's really nice with that little reminder. And it's implemented so damn well!Same goes for the hint system. If won't outright give you the answer. Instead it will kind of nudge you in the right direction. Then you can ask it for another hint, and it will get more detailed as you keep asking, until it finally just tells you what to do. I love that! It's sooooo much better than getting stuck and searching the web for the answer. Next level!I'm crossing my fingers for more!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I like a lot of Ron Gilbert's work, and I'm glad a lot of fans seemed to enjoy this game. But for me it was a crushing disappointment. Mild story spoilers to follow... I think Gilbert may have taken message board criticisms / questions about MI1 and 2 a bit too seriously and made Return to Monkey Island into a very personal response to that stuff. It feels a bit like he made the game about himself.Also, the story just doesn't make sense unless you interpret the ending to mean that it's not supposed to make sense, which just comes off to me as lazy or cheap storytelling (Note: I'm trying to describe the ending vaguely on purpose to be as light on spoilers as possible). [Early game spoilers] It's as if none of the previous games' stories mattered and Gilbert was happy to just kick them to the side. If we're to believe that none of the stories are supposed to make sense as the ending suggests, then why did all of the other games at least try to follow the main continuity, whereas this game ignores or changes so much of what happened in previous games? The ending of Tales of Monkey Island was ignored, which is ironic, since this game is supposedly meant to address the ending of MI2 as if it wasn't resolved properly.  So once again, we have a new MI in which the previous game (or parts of it) never happened.  I'm glad at the very least that Gilbert incorporated some of the fan favorite characters that he wasn't involved in creating. But other than that, he virtually ignored every game other than MI 1 and 2.I played through the full series the month before Return to MI came out, but Return made me appreciate Escape from MI even more (previously the black sheep of the series). Honestly the writing in Return to MI is inexplicable. At times it feels like a Monkey Island game, but more often it barely feels like a genuine entry in the series, even if we only count MI1 and 2.  It has a new tone that sort of feels like a kid's cartoon.  I'm sure people might have said that about Curse of Monkey Island, but it is far more true here.I also agree with a lot of the complaints about the art style but I was ready to completely overlook that for a great new MI story, or some good new jokes, or anything. But unfortunately for me, the story is one of the weakest in the series, if not the weakest. The series seems to be basically finished with this game, which I am okay with since there is no elegant way to salvage the continuity. I'd be happy to be proven wrong, though.  But with Ron's awful writing, I wouldn't be surprised if he dragged this dead horse along for another game, since this one has been so successful.To me, MI as a series was about hilarious stories and characters, crazy puzzles, and often cinematic piratey adventures that could only be told through a point and click format. Not a story about Ron Gilbert talking to message board fans through a game and trying to explain why the divisive ending of MI2 was good actually (I was fine with MI2's ending, but Return to MI kind of retcons it anyway). But unfortunately, it felt like the latter to me. Hoping it is better for a lot of other fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: R2MI Is exactly what I expected as a revamp of MI series. It's funny, fun adventures, never was much for achievements but even those were fun to do. Overall it was an incredible ride! IMHO Do the hard mode. it makes the entire game feel fuller.Regarding the design decisions music/sound and graphics... I really enjoyed them! Good Job Ron and team! You did not disappoint!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: First of, let's address the biggest complains I have seen: The Artstyle.Yes, I can understand, that this isn't for everyones taste. I for my part was rather sceptical pre-release, only from the screenshots and trailers etc.However, it really grew on me over the course. When first starting, my first reaction was, that it looks much better when playing then from the screenshots etc.You can also tell, that despite other claims a lot of care and work went into the artwork and animations for this game. Still in my Eyes it doesn't beat the original MI1 and 2 artwork (though admittedly it is hard to beat the nostalgia associated in that for me), but I would place it at a solid 3rd place in the franchise, even before the special editions.The puzzles have been very fair. They all made sense, though I used the hintbook a couple of times, because I just couldn't get the right idea. However, they were very fun, and there was the one or other curveball thrown at me (in a positive sense), as someone coming from the classic games, which I very much enjoyed.The Story itself...my first impression when starting the game was "what a cheap copout" for a continuation after mi2, however, after finishing the game, I have to say, it really feels well rounded, and a carefully crafted story, which nicely wraps up. Especially in combination with the scrapbook unlock.The music was beautiful. maybe not completely on the same level as the originals, however, that would be really nitpicky. I did enjoy it.Voiceacting was well done and the soundfx overall nicely done.But the most important achievement they managed to capture for me, was the same experience I had with the originals way back when, taking me back to my own youth, while still feeling a somewhat more "adult" experience. This was one of the things I really was afraid of...being excited for the game but then being let down by another ruined childhood ip, as we all experienced countless times before. And I have to say, especially in that regard this game is a masterpiece.Yes, there are certainly some callbacks, but they didn't feel forced etc.I won't drag this further out, all I have left to say is thank you a lot. Not only for this game, but for a life full of adventures. And here's to hope a new generation can pick something up from this and carry on with new adventures from Boybrush!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Return to Monkey island... what I wanted it to be, what it could be, and what it is...Let's start with the art. ... Well it's not pretty... But it's still nicer to look at than Tales of MI or Escape from MI xD!Then again art was never the point.i've decided to go on hard mode, because i wanted to see how frustrating it will get getting stuck on puzzles.Except... Well the puzzles weren't really that hard... not as hard as the old games. They were somewhat entertaining, but lacking. "Too easy" i thought. I also thought "Have i been playing the other MI titles too much and seem to have gotten too into the groove of them? I guess so..."The hintbook is waaaay too tempting to use. I don't like it! (i still used it, lol).The game felt kinda short. About 8 hrs... and i really went to check for funny lines or repetitions in the pre-story.And the ending... Well d#m#it, i felt disappointed! Swindled! BETRAYED even! But then again... It was so Monkey Island that it fit darn too well...I really missed some good "battles" like insult sword fighting... or a Banjo duel... Or some other challenges that would take some time to build up the "skills" to become the "fearsome" mighty pirate and overcome adversity like in any good adventure game. But that never came...but... but...Did i enjoy the game?YES! Yes, i DID! From the title scene onwards there was a nostalgic throwback moment, i enjoyed the scene, the colors, the music! My heart danced with the theme song and anticipation what lies ahead.The "Boybrush" intro into it all took me back into the ending of MI2... The references of old characters, some meta-jokes and homages to old items made me chuckle every time.I played it, i got immersed in it, got time to slip past me (and my bed time) and it left me yearning for more.Now in my book... that's a thumbs-up. Can't say it's the same for everyone.But now to the ideas that i found about this game...It's a homage, a tribute, a (not good) wrap-up that leaves a lot open to the imagination of the player and for the player to connect the dots or assume what actually happened.I learned in the past that Monkey Island has always been a kind of parallel to being a game-developer, or a developer in general. And it reflected the age of the devs and story-tellers quite well. Even in this game.The whole point of the game is pretty similar to what i find the point of life... "it's not what's at the end of it, it's about the journey" and that has been true for all of MI games so far i find.As a player playing the old monkey islands, spending hours and days pondering over the puzzle solutions the frustrations behind them and not knowing how to finally slide forward in the story and gameplay... and finding that "torture" enjoyable... it seemed on-par for a young player with little worries in life and abundant of time on one's hands easy to grin at a corny joke...And with Return... you get a feeling of looking into the past, some jokes worth making, some worth forgetting, some people left behind, some people staying to keep enrichening your lif... erm gameplay... but "damn man, you're old(er) now... Things have changed a lot, you might not agree with the changes, but here they are. People are more competitive, in your eyes quirky and weird... On top of that... Free time is sacred, you probably don't want to spend too much of it solving silly puzzles, measuring against your arch nemesis... You have better things to do" seems like what the whole lack of hard puzzles, long gameplay and in a way, the ending, wanted us to take along as a message. And i don't resent it, as it does so with the playful style of a Monkey Island game.TL;DR: I missed some harder puzzles, more game content and a more meaningful ending, but i had fun with what i got!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I've always found point and click adventure games to be pretty intimidating. Something about the logic of putting together items really just never jived with my thoughts. I'm happy to say that Return to Monkey Island greatly alleviates this with a dynamic clue book, which gradually gives your more and more indepth hints as needed. That along with a automatic populating checklist of objectives makes Return to Monkey Island a blast to play as a new comer to the genre, even on the hard puzzle difficulty.QoL changes aside, I find the game to be very charming from the music down to the dialogue. If you're looking for a wholesome care free experience and dont mind the point and clicking, I would recommend this game without hestitation.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful, nostalgic experience.  Just as witty and fun to explore as the rest of the series. I recommend playing on Hard - it's not too challenging, especially if you have experience with the first 5 games.  No moon logic to be found and there are a good few achievements and bonus/secret puzzles to complete adding to the replay value.Also the music is absolutely fantastic!!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The Monkey Island series always brings me back to my childhood.  I love each and every game and this one is no exception.  If you are just discovering the MI series for the first time or re-discovering it for the 20th time, this game will make you laugh, think, and enjoy the life of being a mighty pirate! 10 out of 10, will plunder again!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: (spoiler free) Return to Monkey Island: I did not rush through the game, I just haven't stepped away from my computer, I tried but I couldn't, and I have just completed it. I can honestly say it truly is everything I had hoped it would be, and more! Full disclosure, I am a huge MI fan, played all the games, yada yada yada, so I had high hopes and expectation for this game. The story, voices, settings, animations, colours, comedy, dialogue, puzzles, inventory items, all of it; absolutely wonderful! I don't know the creators come up with these games but they're all geniuses and I'm forever thankful that they decided to revisit Guybrush and his story after two decades, it was WELL worth it. Monkey Island is still living up to it's reputation as the BEST point & click adventure game series EVER. I'm on a huge high right now!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the journey, I waited a long time for this. The ending may not have been what I expected, but it might have been what I needed.EDIT with potential spoilers: Actually no, I'm angry - the ending feels like a slap in the face, as if someone made fun of you for getting emotionally involved. Thimbleweed Park was the same, as if Gilbert hates you for trying to finish his games and for expecting a satisfying conclusion.I really enjoyed the game right until its ending, then I started to see its flaws throughout. It feels wrong somehow, even despite the letter found in the menu afterwards.I still enjoyed it, I still had fun playing, I was feeling nostalgic, and I'll probably play the next one if they ever make it. But I feel weird.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is by every measure a worthy entry to the franchise. Here are a few standout things, in my mind:Gameplay wise, it's a modernization of the classic point & click, inventory focused adventure genre, introducing all kinds of quality of life improvements and streamlining without loosing the core of what makes these games fun. For the story, while I don't think it's really the game you'd want to start on for Monkey Island, it's respectful to the legacy of the previous games wile adding new elements and resolving some plot-holes along the way. The writing is top notch and is everything it should be.As someone that holds the MI series deep in their childhood memories, I'm glad this game exists and lives up to what I wanted out of it. It's an easy recommendation in my book for anyone that likes the series. While you can jump in here, you'd get a lot more out of it with the context of the previous games (that still hold up and are playable today).
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, I haven't felt this joyful when playing a game for a long time. It is the best combination of new and old, and it is a love letter to all the series' fans. Unfortunately this means that it cannot be enjoyed by people who haven't played the previous games (expecially the first two), but I did :)Despite what people says I love the artwork, it's so fresh and colourful and detailed. Everything is perfect, from the locations to the scores, to the puzzles, to the characters, to the dialogues, to the humour. Someone could say that it's too easy, and in fact I think it's the easiest of the series, but I think that this is only because all the puzzles make 100% sense and everything is straight to the point and makes it easier for the player to enjoy himself; there is none of that unimmaginable bs puzzles that make no sense, it is made just to be an enjoyable fun cozy adventure. And it's perfect.The ending, 10/10 absolute masterpiece
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I got a bit of dejavu. What more can I say, i've never played the game before, it's clearly not the same, yet it picks up a lot of things that made the original game great when i was a kid. As an older person who played the original when released, this game is great, i'm just about to go back in and complete for the first time.A strong recommendation from me for those that played the original. :) Enjoy the nostalgia wave whilst playing a good game. ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is the weirdest series for people to be all like "muh lore!" lol. I liked it. My tiniest complaint might be that it's not too much of a tonal departure from MI 1 & 2 whereas Curse and Escape both do some interesting new things (I didn't get around to playing the Telltale one, and also I think Escape is hella underrated). The tonal consistency does makes it work well as the ending to a little trilogy of MI 1 & 2, but it is not a good entry point if you are new to the series; you have to play the first two games from the 1990/1991 to really get this. Thimbleweed Park (2017) by the same team is a good starting point if you are completely unfamiliar with Lucasarts-style adventure games, as are the relatively recent remasters of the Tim Schafer games from the 90s (Full Throttle, Grim Fandango, Day of the Tentacle). Nevertheless, game's got a lot of heart and does have that magic the older games in the series have.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The story is great, I loved it. The puzzles are good fun. I was really disappointed by the graphics, of course a matter of personal taste. Every time I moved on to another scene I could not help myself from thinking: why on earth would they spoil such an amazing game with so lousy graphics. So look at the screenshots, if you can live with them go ahead and play the game, it's great fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first Monkey Island on my Commodore Amiga, about 25 years ago. I think I'm in a special position to appreciate this game after so long, a kind of time capsule to my childhood. I'm not going to spoil anything, but I'm deeply satisfied to finally know what the secret of Monkey Island is. I know that might be going against the grain - a lot of the reviews are unhappy with the reveal - but for me, as someone looking at this with older eyes, I think it's perfect. I totally get what Ron and Dave are saying with the way they ended it. In fact, the secret of Monkey Island couldn't have been anything else. The secret encapsulates exactly what Monkey Island is all about, and it says something about what it means to look back at a younger time. I can't say more than that, without giving anything away. If you want to know what it is, go and play the game. The secret of Monkey Island awaits.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for the whole ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ family, or just playing it if ur single is fun as hell. The new puzzles are great.The only thing i see as a "negative" is the hint book. U can always refuse to use it. But not always easy when it's already there. I think they could included it in the standard mode, and left it out in the harder mode with more puzzles. It kind of takes away the fun knowing it's there. But enough of that, it's a great game, nostalgic and really takes me back to my youth, and it's cheap considering the content.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't bother with this game unless you're already a fan of the franchise. A lot of the storytelling feels like cheap nostalgia bait (constant reminders of past storylines and puzzles, hardly any new characters, a bunch of pointless cameos), the characters are flat and uninteresting (I was looking forward to Elaine in this game because I know Gilbert has complained in the past about how soft she got in Curse etc and in this game somehow she's WORSE), puzzles are simple and the story beats are almost all retreads. I thought the art style was fine (though the really short legs were offputting), and while Dominic Armato sounds great as always a lot of character voices had this weird hoarse quality that I didn't care for.The whole thing really just showed me that I could be playing the better game I was being reminded of instead of this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: (Multiple) Ending(s) might set off some people, but don't let that discourage you. The game is a blast to play, there's both a to-do-list if you're not sure or remember what you were up to. Also, upon loading the game, half of the time there's the occasion the game let's you have the option to remind what happened before, perfect if you don't have time to play it all at once. There is also a very nice hint-system for when you get stuck, ranging from subtles hints of what to do, to (if you really ain't got a clue ) straight forward telling what needs to be done.Wish more adventure-games had this in the pre(or extremely limited) internet 90's when you could be totally stuck and didn't have a magazine with the walkthrough (anymore).Had my doubts about the artstyle, but 2 minutes into playing completely ignored that issue.Still wouldn't mind a "curse of monkey island" engine though.Finished this in about 12 hours , with a little help from the hint system now and then.At this price point one cannot complain though.Recommended to all wannabe pirates !!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion the game is well made and it is truly the Successor to part 2. When you play the game you will deeply sink in the word of monkey Island. Expecially when you are over 30 years old you will enjoy it because it will remember you to your childhood, so it is a nostalgic game in a grafical modern way. Another good thing is you dont need any solutions from the internet, here you have always the choice to solve the secret all by your own or if you want one or more hints. The secrets self are good solvable and funny as we expect it from Monkey island. So if you have some time left after work and you want to relax yourself by playing a video game, play this game. You also loved the old parts of monkey island and  you want have a nostalgical moment of your chieldhood, then I especialy can recommend this game for you. And as a tip do not read spoilers, then you will have the greatest experience, .I also recommend you to have much time to play the game, try to solve as much secrets by yourself as possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing video games my entire life, but you could say the first time I fell in love with a video game universe was Monkey Island 2 and The Curse of Monkey Island. I have so many fond memories of my dad helping me through if I got stuck or I just need a little push or idea on what I could try next. I was so obsessed with the world of these characters, the amazing music and the hilariously funny dialogue that even if I got stuck, the 8 year old me didn't care to go and try every possible solution or try every dialogue option again as to see if they give off any clues because I was just enjoying my time in the world so much. I can perfectly remember my dad bringing me a copy of Escape from Monkey Island (which I never knew existed) and installing it on his laptop for me and the amount of excitement and joy I felt starting up the game the first time knowing I will be able to spend more time in this world with things I have not seen before.I am 32 now, engaged and having a 6 year old daughter. I lost my dad to cancer last year so seeing the announcement video that a new Monkey Island is happening brought me such excitement and fear. Fear cause I was scared of how it would turn out, as I am sure lots of people like me have fond memories with these games. I found comfort in knowing Ron Gilbert was back behind the wheel and I was a fan of his later Thimbleweed Park as well. The art style did concern me at first, but after seeing and especially playing the game myself I can easily see why this art style works, why it was decided on and I absolutely grew to love it.The prelude to the game stunned me with the reveal, and I loved it. When I reached the ending I was confused and trying to figure out what is happening but until the last few seconds of Guybrush staring into the distance, its like a truck hit me. All those emotions, memories came back. This game took me back to when I was a kid, having those special memories with my father. It honestly feels like this game never went away all this many years but rather grew up alongside me. Having a kid of my own and Guybrush's story really resonated to me on a very personal level and for that I will treasure this game and Ron Gilbert forever and hopefully I will be able to share this amazing world and characters with my own some day. All I can wish for now, is for another Monkey Island (Guybrush) adventure to be able to go through this amazing experience again, but if not, I am so very glad this was the way it ended. This game is amazing and I do hope people give it a chance, It might change your life. It surely did mine. <3

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10What a great game, and what a nice entry in the Monkey Island-series, over 30 years since it's first entry released. Clever puzzles, charming visuals and a lighthearted but gripping story that lasts just long enough, what more could you wish for? Well, let me tell you about the good and the bad of Return to Monkey Island.The game is set years after the last game, with Guybrush telling his son about one of his adventures, the time when he found the secret of Monkey Island (the title of the first game, coincidence?). Safe to say, you should absolutely play the five games that came before this in order to fully appreciate this game. You will understand what is going on, but 100% miss out on a lot of jokes and references that enchance the experience. in the Story that Guybrush tells hos son, he wants to set out on a voyage to find the secret. Sadly, LeChuck is one step ahead and is planning a voyage for himself. That is the premise and the only story-explanation you need. Along the way you trevel between islands in the Caribbean, solve puzzles (mainly inventory-based ones) and chat with a ton of characters, new and old. The humor is the centerpiece, bringing a smile to my face every now and then. The story itself is fun and nostalgic in a good way.The game can be played on two difficulty-settings, casual and hard. Hard seems to be the intended experience, but I played through the game twice and either one is "fine", although I believe that you engage more with the world and the characters on the harder settings. Also, if you want achievements, hard is the only way to go. There are achievements you cannot get on casual, due to some elements being REMOVED from the game on that setting.Another "fun" feature is the trivia book, a book of över 150 trivia-questions that you can answer throughout the game. The twist is, you need to look for the questions (in the form of collectible cards) around the game. The are not necessary for the story but 100% mandatory for achievements, as you need to collect and answer at least 100 questions in order to get all of them (maybe more if you do not find question 9.2 in these first 100). The thing is, these are not in set locations. There are spots in which they can spawn and they can also respawn, which means that one spot could yeild you all of the cards if you wait long enough (it takes some real time for the cards to respawn at every location). This is time-consuming as hell, but I like trivia and achievements so I still did it and enjoyed it.It is time to list the good and bad about this game before we wrap things up:+ Fun and lighthearted story with a big focus on nostalgia+ Charming visuals+ Great voice-acting+ Mostly fun puzzles- The ending is not for everyone. Unless you have played the prior games, you will probably hate it.- Some achievements are highly missable due to poor design, causing players to have to replay large chunks of the game to get them.All in all, I highly recommend this game to fans of the series. Play this last and lean back and feel good about yourself. The score comes from the game not being anything revolutionary and the ending, which I personally did not enjoy. Apart from that, it is a very enjoyable experience!
