_childDocuments_.review: A wholesome meditation on storytelling within an old beloved franchise. Fun puzzles, fun characters, a bit of unfinished storytelling, or to some, mystery left at the end. I spent many hours in my youth playing Monkey Island 1-3, and this fits alongside those memories. I played this game straight through 14 hours in one go. Very much felt like a book you pick up and blink, finishing reading as the sun rises the next day.Music, Writing, Art, Voiceacting - all 5/5Thanks for making this one, Devs

_childDocuments_.review: This game felt like nearly the best of all worlds, Monkey Island-wise.I actually want to start with what I thought was the absolute best thing about the game: The silky smoothe new game engine (Dinky Engine) Ron Gilbert made. Point-and-click adventure games have always been kind of a chore to play on a gamepad. A mouse is usually just way easier to help you walk around and find objects on screen. But I played this both on my deck and on a PC with an XBox controller, and it was clear that they identified all of the pain points and specifically took steps to improve the user experience.For instance, the white circles that appear when you're near-ish interactable objects and the ability to cycle through them with the shoulder buttons made it very easy to use a gamepad. And I was worried at first that without a mouse I'd miss items on screen that I could interact with, but it was not difficult at all because of the circles that appeared to highlight anything you could interact with. Some might complain that made it too "easy," but to me pixel-hunting was frustrating more than fun. It was never exciting to spend 20 minutes trying to figure out a puzzle only to realize you simply didn't notice that there was an object you missed on a screen.I also liked that when you had an inventory object selected and hovered that object over other interactable objects the engine overtly indicated a "No" crossed circle when the objects wouldn't interact with each other. I never loved that when I was stuck I'd have to select objects and try them out on every other object, so this made it much easier because I could quickly select an object and cycle hovering over every other object in my inventory to see if anything could be used with other items.Adding in a "quest log" (your checklist) was a phenomenal idea. Not only did it help you get back into the swing of things if you spent a few days away, but it helped you change course when you were stuck on one of the paths you were going down. ("Maybe I'm not ready for this one yet, which other things am I trying to do again? I'll switch to one of those.") Plus, the checklist was yet another avenue to inject some humor.The literal navigation itself -- ie. traveling from one place to another -- was the best I've seen in an adventure game. Having a run function that actually made you move REALLY fast was very nice. And being able to get to your ship from any screen by using your ship map was much appreciated. I found myself being able to go from a specific point on one island to a location on an entirely different island within 10 seconds, which eased the pain of having to decide "Hmm ... I wonder if the next step of this puzzle is in Location X" and then getting there and being wrong. It only took you 10 seconds to get there and test a theory, as opposed to other adventure games where you have to spend minutes going from X to Y to check a hypothesis.I also loved being able to see a dialog log at the tap of a button.And finally, I don't use hint systems in adventure games, but if I ever did I'd always prefer it be incorporated. Reading an online walkthrough is the worse way to get a hint, but that's all you really get online. They used to create UHS (universal hint systems) for adventure games back in the day, which would let you get a more subtle hint after the hint system asked some questions to figure out exactly where you were stuck in the game. It helped you get a nudge but still feel accomplished at solving something. They included an official hint system just like that in this game, so you know that the hints are more subtle and are creator-approved.Seriously, just everything about the engine was an improvement on all adventure game engines I've come across.The story absolutely kept me interested, and I loved how they were able to organically make callbacks to so many of my favorite characters and locations from the old games. I'd play on my Steam Deck with headphones on, and my girlfriend would comment, "I love hearing you just randomly laugh playing that game." So yeah, the writing is solid. I'll admit that my favorite writing is still from Curse, but this is a very close second, and I was not disappointed in the least.Perhaps the  (minor) complaint I have is that the puzzles were pretty easy. I only really got caught up once. That could also be because the new game engine removed a lot of needless friction from puzzle solving. So, the controversial part. I know a vocal set of people don't love the art direction. I wasn't one of them; I thought it was an interesting, cool visual style from the first time I saw it. Frankly, I'm still the biggest fan of the actual hand-drawn style of Curse most, but this is easily my second favorite of the series. One thing I will say is that whatever you thought from the trailers / screenshots, it  even better "in person." Playing through the game, there are moments of pure beauty in the art, especially in some of the cutscenes. They did some really, really cool stuff with it.I was disappointed they couldn't get the original LeChuck back, but the new voice actor did such a good job that if I hadn't known ahead of time, I think I would have had to really pay attention to figure it out. (Plus, I love that it was Jess Harnell, who had already done voice acting for characters in previous Monkey Island games ... felt nice to keep it in the "family.") And as for the rest of the voice cast, they were wonderful as always. Dominic Armato (Guybrush) and Alexandra Boyd (Elaine) returned and were great, as well as the actors for Stan, Murray, and Wally.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Frankly a bit of a slog seemingly content with wallowing in nostalgia. A comedy whose attempts at humour come in the form of re-heated bits, locales and characters from the first two games. Adds nothing and nobody of value to the series while engaging in point & click adventure game design that ignores the advances the genre has made in the last 30 years, venturing to improve on its own past formula by chipping away at the gratifying aspects of where the genre used to exist in the 90s and acknowledging none of the clever puzzle design associated with it now.The art style is the only wholly successful thing about it. Absolutely, utterly gorgeous from top to bottom, quite frankly. What seemed like expressionless characters in screenshots come alive plenty once they animate and talk, and although MI3 obviously took a different path, visually, this establishes a kinship with the more impressionistic backgrounds of the first two games in a way I find very, very charming. Some locales in this are simply breathtaking, and the way it has complete command of the mood of a scene is magnificent. It's not enough to elevate the experience when it's being weighed down by endless chores where puzzles should be, a supremely forgettable cast of new characters and situations only barely padding the dutiful rolling out of old characters and references to old situations, and a "story" and a to-do list menu item that more or less feel like the same thing.Please, I implore you not to play this as your only adventure game in the last 25 years and judge the state of the genre based on it. There are wonderful, *wonderful* adventure games to play. Please play those.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very indecisive on this... This is definitely a good game... I had a lot of fun with it, until the end... I used to play Monkey Island when I was a really little kid, and attempted going through them a few times as I grew up. I always remembered spending days just trying to figure out what the puzzles actually worked... and despite never managing to finish on my own accord, they were always fun. This installment... okay, there is definitely some of the old mojo in there, but... it's just a little off somehow (maybe it was the ending that did it in for me).I'd say buy it on sale, and you will be happy.Pros:- Some of the old mojo is definitely in there, great atmosphere for the most part- Pretty decent jokes!- Story is pretty decent until the end- The interface is well thought out, control is easy to get used to and pretty fluent. Cons:- No insult swordfighting... :( - Just a little too easy/short for anyone with half a brain and some familiarity with the genre (took roughtly 13 hours to finish on full-monkey, without using the hintbook at all)- The ending... a little too meta... - The graphic design choices are a matter of taste... I only put this down as a con, because old Guybrush looks like a bad drunk honestly, though I'm not such a big fan of the angular designs in general.

_childDocuments_.review: I had taken a break from gaming for the past year or so as there were no good games to play - I occasionally played a few multiplayer games or some of the older titles but the recently released games were simply not interesting to me. Return to Monkey Island is the first new game I've bought in over a year. I'm a huge fan of the series and when I heard it was in development and I saw the pre-order on steam, I went ahead and bought it. Background -I first played the Monkey Island games when I was in school (yes I'm that old) and fell in love with the genre. I've played and finished all of the games in the series and simply love the music, characters, story lines, puzzles, game play and the art style. The art style has varied over the years, but I'm happy to say I like what every game had to offer.Quick Summary -For the people who have played Monkey Island before, PLAY this one - you may have a few complaints but overall, I feel it's a fun game and you'll get what you expect from a Monkey Island game. I played and finished it (casual mode) in about seven hours and I used the guide about four times. Some of the puzzles will take time to figure out, but most of them are fun and you'll enjoy solving them. The art style is different but in a good way. For people who haven't played Monkey Island before, I would say, buy the first game (it's been remastered and it's on steam for dirt cheap) and if you like it, buy the second one and then get this one. The story line will fall in place and you'll get an introduction to all the characters. I highly recommend that you pick up the other titles in this series first as they are a lot more enjoyable and you'll have a proper introduction to the series. Also, this game, right off the bat, may not be the type of game you like to play - it's a point and click adventure game and you may not like it. What I liked about this game?It's remained true to the Monkey Island style - characters, music, voice acting, funny dialogues, story lines and puzzles. Felt right at home when I started playing and the game got progressively tougher. While the art style was not what I expected, I ended up liking it - it's different and an acquired taste - but I think they did a good job.  What I didn't like about this game?I wish they filled the game with a lot more - it's a relatively short game and they could have included more variety in the puzzles. I wish they included the insult sword fighting challenge and or something along the lines of Monkey combat. The puzzles were fun but similar in nature. They could have added a lot more variety. The game felt like it lacked content and they didn't flesh out the dialogues of all the characters or give enough backstory. The story, while most of it was fun, I didn't like how they bridged the gap between the second game and this one and didn't enjoy the "flash back" approach they took.   Closing comments -I'm really happy that a new Monkey Island game came out and I got to experience it. I missed the characters a lot and I'm glad they are all back. I'll start my second play through soon and will try to complete the game in hard mode. This is a must buy for Monkey Island fans!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic follow-up to one of my favourite franchises, and a direct continuation of one of the most frustrating cliffhanger endings.Gameplay is streamlined but not to the point of oversimplification, and the wit is as strong as ever with this one. The art style is different, but beautiful. Personally I prefer it over the style of the first game's special edition. Achievements add some welcome extra interactions into the game to cunningly distract you from the real puzzle solutions. And the trivia book is a great way to offer collectables while giving them a small purpose at the same time.The point-and-click adventure genre has never been more accessible.Now, that ending... Let's just say I don't see how it could have ended any differently.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A long awaited return of arguably the best adventure game franchise of all time!It's a bit different now, slightly modernised, but at it's core it's still good old guybrush.Kind, funny, childish fantasy. A small escape to the best pirate theme park you ever visit.If you're a fan of the franchise or adventure genre in general, this game is definitely worth cheking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Phew. Right. Okay. Yes, I recommend Return to Monkey Island, but not to everyone.This is far from my favourite Monkey Island. It's not funny; I solved too many puzzles by accident; and I have to admit, I still hate the art style. The constant head-bobbing made me queasy, and the incessant dialog that some characters spew is infuriating.It's not a great game, but it is a meaningful one.Flicking through Guybrush's scrapbook before I started playing brought a tear to my eye. Then, eleven hours later,  had me sobbing. I don't understand the ending in any literal sense, but emotionally it was perfect.If Monkey Island is already special to you, if you're open-minded to an alternative interpretation of that world, and if texture is more important to you than closure then please, get Return to Monkey Island and I hope you love it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Secret of Monkey Island was one of the first games i've played as a kid and until today it's still one of my favorites. I also liked Monkey Island 2 and 3 a lot and i still love the point & click adventure genre. So i guess my expectations for Return to Monkey Island were quite high.Was it as good as i hoped it would be? No, definitely not. But after more than 30 years expectations can grow huge and it's not very realistic to think a new game can meet all the expectations that built up over such a long, long time.Return to Monkey Island was a nice point & click adventure game. Not more, not less. I liked it, but i liked Monkey Island 1, 2 and 3 and Thimbleweed Park a few years ago more.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all the monkey island games. and everytime I hear the theme song, my heart warms up. Forgetting the confusing disaster of the ending, this game is a teeribly empty puzzle that hasnt evolved from the last century when the francise first started. The islands mostly empty, the puzzles mundane and straightforward. the only joy was meeting lechuck's crew.Do yourself and wallet a favor, and play some flash puzzle games. you will have more satisfactory headscratchers for free.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game - one part it's own, new Monkey Island adventure and one part a love letter to the first two games, but not in an overbearing way that makes the game feel unoriginal.The puzzles are good and the characters are fun. There aren't many "total bs" puzzles that leave you going "how the hell was I meant to work that out??" but a hint book is there in your inventory for when you need it and it's well implemented (it'll give you a series of more blatant clues before finally telling you the answer, there might be the odd puzzle where you need one or two but the clues are vague enough that you still feel like you mostly worked it out yourself.)Overall, an excellent adventure game and very worthy addition to this acclaimed series. If you enjoy adventure games but are daunted by the long life of this series then this is a fine place to start - you don't need much prior knowledge to understand what's happening but it provides a recap of previous games if you feel like it. If you're already a Monkey Island veteran, or even if you only count the first two games as "true" Monkey Island adventures, then definitely pick this one up; you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the original two Monkey Island Games. Now to the 2020's..... Basically they take the character you know and love and chastise and belittle the character for his actions and decisions in earlier game. Making the story about a life lesson asked for by literally... no one. Makes the player feel like they are controlling a character who has been careless and done wrong. Yuck. Turns out the lead character is not always right and neither is the customer... thanks current owner of Lucas Arts... thank you so much for bending another one over to your narative. PS. love to know where my first, longer review from a while ago disappeared too? ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing actually. Well done guys! I actually thought the art was cool in the end. Nice length game. Good story. Would have liked a few more zany characters and scenarios, with slightly more complicated puzzles. The best Monkey Island since Curse of Monkey Island (which I thought is perhaps the best, or MI2).
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is an art piece that tries to evoke a feeling of melancholic nostalgia.If the game's message resonates with you, you'll like the experience, ending and all. If it doesn't - then you won't. Both valid takes.While there is a lot of revisiting going on in the game, it isn't is pure nostalgia bait and has new things to say.Mechanically the puzzles aren't difficult, wish they did more here.The runtime for the game is around 15 hours, it doesn't have time to get boring at that length. There's some limited replay value in the form of collecting trivia cards and achievements but it's not very compelling for the time required and the amount of new content you would see.TLDR If monkey island is one of your early gaming experiences give this a try, this was made for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of the series this is a true return to adventuring form. Sure, at the core, this is a classic inventory puzzle game. The story is what makes it so much more. There are layered and metaphorical ideas at work. The humor still holds up and I got quite a few belly laughs out of the ludicrous situations Guybrush Threepwood finds himself in. I do recommend you go back and finish the first 3 games of the series to really get the most out of this. Look a three-headed monkey!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I expected way more for such a famous classic game. Its nice, but it lacks good jokes, feels like a game for little kids and it completely lacks the feeling of the old games, especially with all the hint systems. Yes they are helpful in some cases, but Id rather google a solution, then just have it at hand during the game (especially in the double way that there is a hint book, characters help you and you can see what objects are clickable by pressing a key) I am a little disappointed, but still great this game has been done.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game and I do like some parts of it, but I can't recommend it. The game has a very different art style compared to the previous games. I don't necessarily hate it but I don't love it either. It really just doesn't feel like a MI game, it has none of the charm of especially the three first ones. The character design for many of the characters however is just plain ugly, with Guybrush himself being the worst. They've for some reason decided to depict him like some deformed monster with dead eyes, I really can't understand that decision at all.The story was fine, that at least did feel like it belonged in a MI game, not a high point in the series though. The ending however was a major disappointment, it felt like the dev team didn't know how to finish their game and just went for the easiest and cheapest option. Without spoiling anything the ending has basically been recycled from a previous game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Being a Monkey Island fan since my childhood I've had to wait many years for a new part and was not disappointed. I got used to the new graphic style within an hour. The puzzles start out very simple and become more difficult and abstract over time. You can notice a clear nostalgia factor and the signature of Ron Gilbert. Let's hope there will be another sequel! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... the swan song.  I hated the art style, but got used to it, I hated the limited dumb puzzles, but got through them.  If you are the fan of Monkey Island, you should definitely play it.  If you are not a fan, or were born in the curent century - consider playing original remastered versions first, those are the undying classic puzzle-adventure games.  And then, perhaps, come back to this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The Return to Monkey Island feels just right for a new game in the series. High quality on puzzles, humor and dialogue makes it a very entertaining experience worth your time(and money). The puzzles can be a tad far-fetched at times, which is tradition for the Monkey Island games, but a handy hint book can provide you with just enough voodoo to get a grip of what you're supposed to do. Just don't use it too often or you'll spoil the fun in solving puzzles on your own.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed going back to the world of Monkey Island. I am exactly the target audience, having played the original Monkey Island games on floppy disk back in the day. For me this was a great step back into the world the world of Gybrush Threepweed, LeChuck and more. I loved getting to go back to Melee Island, visit the SCUMM Bar and more. I liked the context-sensitive cursor system, I thought that was an intuitive change to the point and click format. It's simple to use and the wording attached to the cursor changes to let you know what will happen when you click on something in the game world. For me, this was a great time back in Monkey Island, with enough humour to keep me laughing until the end. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. Just fn loved it.Awesome story, puzzles, humour.You get used to the art style. Kind of goes with the "Children Storybook" vibe set at the beginning with Boybrush. Weird that heads shake so much while talking.The ending left me a bit empty.Don´t get me wrong, I understand it, and it`s the same feeling a lifelong chase for a McGuffin would leave you... But still, it is strangely moving and thoughtful.Cheers for a more mature and philosophical childhood hero.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I didn’t expect this to be any good, and yet here it is. An excellent entry in the series, one that frames its story well, looks great,, and unexpectedly actually has something to say.It’s funny, easier than the originals in a way that keeps it’s pacing up, and plays extremely well on the steamdeck / console controls to the point that I didn’t even know this is also still a point and click game.It’s not my perfect Monkey Island game - not all the characters or locations are hits - but it didn’t need to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I was sceptic about the graphic at first, but now I must say, it fits this marvellous saga perfectly. I finished it in a few days and now playing it again to catch more trivial cards and achievements of course... and because... it ended too soon T_T I actually wanted to playing it forever! The plot, the old-but-gold point&click, the characters, everything takes you back to the 90s. AH SO MANY HEARTWARMING MEMORIES!!  <3
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge Monkey island fan but this game just wasn't for me. This is just not nearly as good as any of the old games. I don't like the opening.There hasn't been any well written humor.The art style is ugly and weird. Everything is surrealist and looks like it has no soul. All of the NPCs don't even look like people, they look almost like abstract paintings. Guybrush just looks extremely weird, like his face is carved out of a bar of soap or something.Of course, the voice acting for Guybrush is phenomenal at least. The new characters are not memorable. Even the music is not memorable like the older games. And to top it all off, the gameplay feels linear, hand holdy and dumbed down from older entries. Not really a very great game.Maybe I'm just getting old and this game just wasn't for me.I'll keep playing it and if I change my mind I'll come back and update this review.Updates:-So far I've atleast been able to laugh at the -I really can't get over how much I dislike the art style.-I would literally choose escape from monkey island with tank controls on the playstation over this uninspired mess, at least that game had charm, despite all of it's flaws.-I'm honestly not sure who the target audience is for this game, it doesn't feel targeted at fans of the original games.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. A great introduction to point and click adventure games for me, having never played one before. The graphics, story, characters, voice acting and music are all top notch. Stan and Wally were highlights and their voices left me hoping for as much conversation with them as possible. The zombie pirate crew were very good too. There were also several moments and lines from npcs in the game that were genuinely funny, which is rare in the games I've played. The only negative is I would have liked a bit more from its ending but even that fits the vibe that this game has. I finished the game in 8 hours on casual and will be going back for a play through on the higher difficulty setting as I'm led to believe that there's more to the puzzles and game in general in that mode. I'll definitely be checking out the other games from the Monkey Island series in time. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute.  We're taking our time as we go, savoring the moment, just as Guybrush wanted.  All the early naysayers on the art style can suck it, because there's no way this was the "cheap" option; it looks so much better in HD motion as you play.  Tons of quality of life improvements 'borrowed' from PnC adventures over the years: double-click for fast travel being one of them, hold Tab to see clickable hotspots, and all the old "space to pause," "period to skip," etc. from LucasArts games of old.  Very excited and hopeful that this could possibly help reinvigorate old franchises for new generations.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked almost everything about this game. The music is beautiful, the characters and backgrounds feel lively and detailed and the voice acting is excellent. It is also well written. I guess the reason why I still feel like something is missing must be due to the fact that this game is just way too easy. Whereas I would consistently get stuck in Monkey Island 1 and 2, which allows you to really take a good look at all the different places and try every item on every little obscure corner of all the islands this is not the case here. There still were a few fun side stories but the grand overarching quest seemed more important this time because everything went by so fast. Maybe just try and play very slowly. I would still kind of recommend playing it but not if this is your first one.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Not my favorite game in the franchise, but imo still worth a play.But three warnings are imo quite important:1) It's quite short (~10 hours)2) The graphics style might not be for everyone3) The ending might disappoint and anger people. If you want to spoiler yourself and are interested you can read about in the forums - i won't go into it here.Now what is to say about the game itself.The Soundtrack is great, though it's mostly a remix of existing tracks from Monkey Island I+II. Still a new version of the Scummbar theme surprised me quite positively. The general audio quality felt fine to me and the quality of the english voice acting also felt good. So Sounds: 9/10The graphics have been criticised as early as the first trailer dropped. And it certainly is a switch from the comic 3D graphics. And while people act as if it's the first switch, it really isn't (Pixel > Comic 2D > Bad 3D > good comic 3D > angular planes abstract comic style now).The colour palette feels quite similar to Monkey Island 1 + 2 and the animations are good enough. While it definately could have been a more complex thing, it is a rather smal and cheap game. So in the end such complexity is neither nessecary, nor would it fit the production budget. Also it works fine in getting the characters and world across and even making old known characters spotable quite easily.So the Graphics are definately good for what they try to do, which in my book would be a 7/10.The gameplay is your typical point'n'click adventure. With puzzles written by some of the veterans of the industry. It's standing in the modern tradition of LucasArts Adventures. (Nearly) Non-Killable Protagonist, who can combine items (mostly two), and solves a few different types of puzzles.The control of the game can be done with two mouse buttons and as with most modern point'n'click adventures, you don't have dozens of different verbs to use things or combine much more than two items within your inventory. For anyone never having played a point'n'clikc adventure - you control a 2D (sometimes 3d) Character within a sideview world, experiencing the narratively quite linear story the characters find himself in. To progress towards the characters goal you've got to speak to characters, collect and combines items to solve puzzles (some are rather actual puzzles than usage chains of items). You're prettty free in visiting different spots in Return to Monkey Island and the enjoyment depends mostly upon the storytelling itself.The basic formular will work great imo, for everyone who loves Point'n'Click adventure games. So for fans of such it' give it a 9/10. Most puzzles felt quite logical, though perhaps a tad to easy for quite a few people.The story told isn't as connected (sequentially) towards the other Monkey Island stories. We still play (mostly) as Guybrush Threepwood, who's telling the story of how he searched for the Secret of Monkey Island again. Guybrush feels like good ol' Guybrush. He's still a somewhat clumsy, gullible, reckless, guy who cares little about personal property of others, when it comes towards getting closer to his big goal.During the story we'll meet old known characters - who themselves felt true to their old characters - and we'll meet a few new ones. All with their own fitting personality. The world itself is back to its themepark-esque Voodoo Pirate Caribean feeling. The bad old (Monkey Island 4) overdoing of franchise companies and easily spotable standins for real people seems to be a thing a of the past. And it generally felt enjoyable, though sometimes still a bit on the nose. There are still quite a lot of jokes and it's definately still a quite silly world. As always, jokes don't work equally for everyone, so beware me thinking it's funny. Though i definately wasn't laughing out loud that often, but i wouldn't remember having done so with Monkey Island I + II either. Then again my frist playthrough of those was 30 years ago.As the story is something to experience, it's hard telling why i think it's good without giving things away. If you need to see story elements, you'll likely find things on youtube...Now as i've warned the ending might not be everyones thing. I personally didn't like it especially. It wasn't that fulfilling and it likely doesn't deliver on everything that people thought it would deliver. And to a lot of people this might be a deal breaker. But if you don't need a great ending to enjoy the hours and gameplay beforehand, i can only advice you to get it.So personally i'd rate it at 8/10. But having seen a lot of people voicing their dislike of the ending, that's truly a very subjective thing!So in the end i see 33/40 points. Which means i'd personally say it's definately a game you should play if you like point and click adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It's Monkey Island as you know and love with a new story. Absolutely worth buying if you're familiar with the games, or like point and click adventure games.While it was nice to see familiar returning characters and places, the only criticism I would have to this fantastic game is there was a bit too much of the familiar, and a little lacking in the new places. However this is an extremely minor complaint as the game as a whole is another masterpiece.The art style and animations suit Monkey Island perfectly, and I'm so glad they went with the traditional 2D over the rather clunky 3D of Escape and Tales.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: When I return to my admired first video game franchise after 25 years, I´d expect more of the funny dialogs and charming puzzles as it used to be. Not boring dialogues, just to warm up memory of well-known, way too easy puzzles and the game telling me where to go first and what to do. Also it does not feel "piratey" anymore. The Prelude is a waste of time and replacing old side-characters to jump on the woke-train is which ultimately leads me to refund the game.Pity, I was so excited to return to Monkey Island.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw the announcement trailer for Return To Monkey Island and that it was being done by the original team I knew immediately that it was a must-buy for me. So my overwhelmingly positive review of this game relies heavily on the nostalgia that aches my heart when I think of all the wonderful times that I had playing the first two Monkey Island games as a boy.From that perspective, this game does not disappoint and has the same charm and goofy humour (read as Dad jokes) that made the first games a treasure in puzzle games.I am very grateful to have had the opportunity to experience this adventure one last time. For these few hours, I truly felt like a kid again...
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I always loved the Monkey Series, I first played on my Amiga 500, yeah, I am that old. I am glad that they managed to maintain the same type of humour and that the story bring back old characters. My only regret is the new graphics, I found them too squarey. The first Monkey was so ahead of its time graphically, that I feel a little rob by it. But Overall, it's a very good game especially if you have old school game nostalgia like me.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The artstyle is actually pretty great, it just takes a little taking used to. On top of that, the game is lovingly crafted, contains tons of great humor. The puzzles might be a little simpler than previous games but that's ok. The only negative thing I would say about the game is that some of the hotkeys are a bit weird and that you cannot currently rebind them without editing a config file.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Return to Monkey Island is a perfect and wonderful conclusion to this story for me.I am going through a difficult time and this game has given me joy and some light.It brought back memories of old carefree times and touched my heart.I would like to thank Ron Gilbert, Dave Grossman, David Fox, Rex Crowle, Michael Land, Michael McConnell, Clint Bajakian (for the wonderful music) and the rest of the team.I can recommend this title to anyone who likes beautiful stories and has an open heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This was overall a really great nod to the other Monkey Island games. I was fine with the "blocky" graphics -- Honestly, I think it was the best graphics of the updated versions! The ending of the game is... interesting, but there's a huge twist to it. Do a google search to find out. Overall, I loved it!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. So many insider jokes (including trivia), such an easy handling and I also dig the new artwork. It feels right and for me personally, takes me back 20 years when I played the old ones on PC. Thanks for all the work that went into this! And now watch out, there is a 3 headed monkey behind you!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: “Look behind you, a three-headed monkey!”The nostalgia factor is definitely strong with this one! , the beginning of the franchise, has a truly special place in my heart. It was the very first adventure game, one of the first PC games and, in general, one of the first video games I ever played as a kid, and also one of the main reasons why I started taking my English studies way more seriously – I had to understand all those jokes, after all! :DEver since Guybrush walked into my life, I’ve been obsessed with point ‘n’ click adventures, and, naturally, I played through all the sequels (with  being my favorite). When they announced yet another (and probably the last) installment, I could hardly contain my joy – and now, finally, the time has come for me to return to my beloved Monkey Island.I think it’s safe to say that  is all that fans of the series could have hoped for. Yes, the art style is quite different from what we’re used to, but trust me, if you start playing, you’ll quickly realize how great everything looks. The characters move smoothly, the locations are detailed and vibrant with colors, and nothing or no one looks out of place. The writing is just as superb as it was in the old days, the puzzles are challenging (or not, if you choose casual mode), and the voice acting is stellar. This is how you modernize a classic genre!For me, this isn’t simply a game, but a way to relive my childhood all over again. A huge thanks to everyone involved for making this trip down memory lane possible!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The Monkey Island series is a pillar of PC gaming history. This (final?) addition is the culmination of years of perfecting the art of the point-and-click adventure. The return to 2D did for this series what it did for Metroidvania-style games, in that it was a choice that revived the spirit of the franchise. The art style is perfect for this series. I'm on my second playthrough of this. I did the story mode first and am now on hard mode. Both are incredibly enjoyable, though I do recommend hard mode for its extended gameplay and additional puzzles. There's an option in the settings to turn on Writer's Mode, which adds tons of additional dialogue, that I insist every player turns on. The ending is bittersweet and fun. I've played all but the first game, and I think I might have to go back and play that one now too.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very nice return trip to Monkey Island! Humor was sharp and witty, and difficulty level seemed appropriate. I used the hint book only once. The graphics - well I got used to them. Everything looks pretty, but nothing looks really spectacular. Still, I was entertained and even moved at some points.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who'd been playing through the franchise when this game was announced I can say this is a worthy addition to the Monkey Island line-up.As much as people complained about the art style is has proven to be charming and quite impressive at times and the rest of the presentation measures up as well.The only 'drawback' I could name would be that LeChuck's original VA was too sick to reprise the role but his replacement does a good job instead, even if the audio balancing is a bit low whenever he's screaming.Furthermore the game has a ton of references back to the previous games, all of them and not just the original two. As someone who really liked Curse and Tales I highly appreciate that and it shows the devs appreciate them even if they had no real hand in their creation.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Great addition to the Monkey Island series.  Really like some of the new additions of the to-do list and chat history.  I was a little apprehensive about the art style but quickly climatised, feels so so good to be back in Scumm Bar and the music takes me right back to being a kid.  My 7yr old daughter would also like to make clear this is her favourite game too!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Boy this game took me back to my childhood when I couldn't wait for my cousin to visit us to tell me how to move past a specific part...Thank you for taking the time to provide me with some closure devs! there are few games that are made with a purpose of creating something you like and not just profit.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Finally back to Monkey Island - feel like 14 again :). This game really lives up to the spirit and has got me into MI again after the first few seconds.Awesome graphics & UI (y I like it)  only downside is that they broke linux with the latest update - but I've a mac too :). If you've played MI 1&2 this is a must have. Thanks to the team to make a sequel that improves the franchise rather than destroying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This was a real fanservice! My initial response to art style was same with many others: it doesn't look like Monkey Island! Fortunately I can say that art sits really well in to game. As for the game itself, it's as oldschool Lucasarts game as any. Puzzles have just the proper difficulty. In-game-tipbook is a great addition. Recommended for those who have played Monkey 1 & 2
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Hello,I simple love it, it's clever & funny and totally contemporary in terms of how it picks you up, whenever you find the time, and takes you on the journey to Monkey Island(tm)! Its a well made porting of the classic into 2022 and a lot of reminiscing going on while strolling through the game, besides people complaining about the non pixel(art) graphics, I find it brilliant. <3 job well done.have *arrrgh* fun!!! Guybr....Alex
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Whats not to love about a passion project made 30 years after its initial release. Game was fun and engaging I don't typically play this genre of game since i was a child but i just had to pick it up when it has Guybrush in it. Definitely worth checking out puzzles were fun and the hint book gave you exactly what you needed but not more than you needed when you felt stuck it only helped you but didn't spoil the entire puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I don´t know why, but it was a strange feeling flipping the switches in the end. Although wistful, yet satisfied.That´s probalby because I played The Secret of Monkey Island as a kid, and I was drawn into that world of adventure gaming. Hours of puzzling, to the point of despair, without help from the Internet (did not really exist kids!) Only the buddies in the schoolyrad might know a tip. What great memories.The best thing about Return to Monkey Island is, that it is not a cheap cash grab by creating yet another sequel. I enjoyed playing ever minute, and spilled my grog over the keyboard laughing a few times. It really catches the feeling of the first two games.The way the whole story is wrapped up is just great for me, being a father myself now.And I´m sure, every other younger person will have fun with this games as well ;-)
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Press <TAB> you'll thank me later...Was a really wonderful experience reminiscing. It had just the right kind of fan service, puzzles on hard were fun and just the right amount of challenge without being too abstruse. Stan is back waving his arms and making great deals! There were a couple of slightly clunky puzzles (Terror island, I'm looking at you). And the trivia card spawning is a little annoying. My best advice is to save at a few places both before and after certain events since the landscape changes a bit, that way, if you're planning on grinding out the trivia or achievements, it makes it much easier to search all spawn locations since it's a random spawn across save games.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Ron Gilbert did not surprise me, again. Monkey Island has always been and will remain one of the best point-and-click adventure games I've played. I've read a lot of people's negative comments: These comments were about both the puzzles and its humor. However, there is no forced storytelling or boring puzzles. It's a pretty decent game that anyone can play.If you're starting the Monkey Island series for the first time, I recommend playing the previous games, as you can see a lot of spoilers in Return to Monkey Island.The ending though... It made me laugh a lot. The last information Elaine gave was really pleasing.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Another entry in my favorite point and click adventure game.Some good parts, some frustation, some... I don't know if it's fair to call it retcons?First of all, hands down the cutest depiction of Elaine and Guybrush relationship.I enjoyed the game, it wasn't to hard, short and sweet.I can definitly relate to the letter in the recap having grown up with the series and all.I do however have to add that there's a fair few things that were not good or lazy.Gameplay spoiler: Not letting me pick up items until I get specific triggers, I'll assume I can't pick that up if there is no option.Atleast make a "why do I want to pick that up?" dialogue or something.Finale spoiler
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A great Return of a franchise with plenty of Tales where Guybrush can't Escape from his Curse of forever being at the receiving end of LeChuck's Revenge since never finding the Secret of Monkey Island... Bad anti-jokes caused by sleep depravity aside, I really loved my time with this game. I know people have complained about the ending, but I thought it was pretty good finale to the series(but still open enough for further stories to happen.)
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a fan of Monkey Island since the first game, and I loved all of them including the non-Ron Gilbert ones. Monkey Island was the game that got me into point and click adventures, but very few other adventure games match the quality and humour of Monkey Island. I was initially a bit hesitant about the odd choice of art style, but I was so distracted by the the sharp, witty and excellent writing that the art style ended up not bothering me. It helped that Guybrush Threepwood's voice is still the same voice. I love how they have made the point and click much more intuitive, so now the point and click doesn't get in the way of the story. I recently replayed Monkey Island 1 and 2 in preparation for this (and I still needed walkthrough help!), and I'm glad I did it as this made Return to Monkey Island fresh, as it takes place immediately after Monkey Island 2. Plus it made "hard mode" more palatable after playing the first two which contains many more illogical puzzles. The jokes are just as funny in Return, and the excitement feels familiar, which is a great thing. I was so sure of this game I pre-ordered it on Steam before release, and I'm glad I did. A masterpiece...

_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It gives me absolutely no pleasure to leave a bad review for something I've so longingly waited for but dang, the ending of this story just up and fizzles out. The central question the story asks is: "If you spend enough time pursuing something, will the satisfaction of the prize live up to the thrill of the chase?" Sadly, the game does not provide satisfying closure. The game seems content to ask you that question, and let you make up your own answer. Don't get me wrong, there's weight and meaning in that philosophy but... to have people wait 20+ years to be told that? I feel bad for the old timers who grew up with this series playing this just to be told something they can read after biting into a fortune cookie. It just feels cheap and awkward to do considering the honest to god legacy of the series. If this series continues in the future, I just ask that Ron Gilbert moves past "meta", "gotcha" endings; as the point was made at great cost.

_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A return to the classics of point and click adventure! Witty writing, twisted puzzles, and more items snatch than you can find ways to use them. For those concerned about missing the intervening years of Monkey Island Misadventures, don't be. There is a nice "scrapbook style" refresher. Guybrush happily revisits all his achievements and follies to get you up to speed, or just as a nice reminder.The game itself is full of the kinds of characters Ron Gilbert and crew have grown famous for. Friends and foes, both old and new, return. Whether updating you on their whereabouts since the last voyage or to trade items, send of fetch quests, or just prod you in the right direction for the next puzzle. Everything you'd expect from the classic adventuring is here.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the revious installments of the Monkey Island series, Especially the older installments back in the SCUMM days, you'll love this game. You get used to the unique artstyle pretty quickly, and it doesn't hamper the fun at all. I first played Secret of Monkey Island 20 years ago, fell in love with it, and continued playing the series for the next 20 years, over and over again. Playing this game from start to finish feels like a love letter to the classic Monkey Island adventures, while still maintaining an identity of its own. If you've never heard of the series before, you should probably go pick up the other installments first (all available on Steam, with remastered editions for the first 2 as well!) or you may get a little lost playing this newest installment. The Monkey Island series is a major staple in video game history, and this plays to the strengths of the entire series, with its clever puzzles, funny jokes, humorous references, and the heart the developers poured into every bit of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: My feature-length, spoiler-free review can be found at Ars Technica, and while I won't hotlink it here, it's not hard to search for. A snippet from that piece:Return to Monkey Island is nearly everything I'd hoped for in a modern return to the series. Its interface and controls split the difference between the expectations of hardcore genre fans and those of point-and-click novices. Its presentation and voice acting pair nicely to set an approachable and fiendishly hilarious tone. And the game's full journey, from bumpy waters to smooth, silly sailing, consistently feels personal, vulnerable, and reflective of its creators—which is to say, this is the opposite of a nostalgia-reeking cash-in.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game took me back to a very special place. People tend to remember the good parts of an experience better. This game feels like exactly the Monkey Island of my memories.The art is familiar but crispier and shinier, with all the playfulness of the previous games. The dialogues are a delight to explore, every character is well written, I really loved the crew of LeShip. The puzzles manage to be logically and intuitively integrated in the story logic and at the same time retain the wonderful wackiness signature to Monkey Island series. The gameplay was flawless, painstakingly polished down to every single detail. It's a joy to experience in every aspect.Games are art and good art is very hard to make pleasing everyone. For me it delivered everything i wished for and more. I'm thankful for all the hard work that went into making this gem of a game. I hope it will spark inspiration in new creators as the originals did and the Return to Monkey Island will in the end mark the beginning of the return of the great genre of adventure games as such.

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are kind of too easy. I don't know if it's because there doesn't seem to be that many things to interact with in general or because all puzzles actually make sense for once (well, at least I could finish the game without any hint/cheating). Also, there's a bit too much of fan service in my opinion (unnecessary references to past games).The fact that a lot of places and characters are directly taken from the original game sure adds some nostalgia, but also hinders its ability to make you discover a new universe (which is what made the Monkey Island series exciting). The game has also been somehow "modernized" by introducing new features like the "book of hints" and the "checklist", which bring the game closer to a more casual audience, drifting away from the niche point&click adventure it used to be (which can be a good or bad thing depending on your preferences). However, if you liked the games of the series, you will certainly enjoy it ! All its atmosphere and humor has subsisted while giving you something fresh. Even if some people can't seem to fully appreciate the cartoon graphics, I think they really fit the game.I highly recommend playing the first Monkey Island games before trying this one, as you will probably not be able to enjoy it fully otherwise. Also, I highly recommend playing the "hard" difficulty, as you probably won't start it all over again after completing the "easy" one and you will probably miss out on some stuff (I don't know what, though, as I only completed the "hard" difficulty).

_childDocuments_.review: I've decided that, for me, this game doesn't exist... me playing it never happened... the Monkey Island series is just Secret, Revenge, and Curse; with Curse being the best out of the three.Why have I decided to forget this game? It's not because of the art style; which did take some time to get used to... even when they made Guybrush look like a hobo.It's not because of the puzzles; which were far too easy and simplified for more "casual" players of the genre.It's not even the story overall; which was average, not very funny, and left a lot on the table (many of the new islands had such high potentials but ended up being wasted).So what was it that made me despise this game? THE ENDING! This game has one of the WORST endings to a series I have ever seen!*** SPOILERS ***At the climax of the story, Ron Gilbert (creator of MI) basically slaps the player in the face and says, "You know the story you've come to love? the cool characters you grew up liking? The adventures you've went on? The world you've immersed yourself in? Yeah... it's all fake, never happened. Everything is just a buch of stories a guy made up to tell his kid. Oh by the way, stop idolizing the past, stop trying to relive any happy memories you may have, move on. META ENDING! THE END!"The ending is like having the rug pulled out from underneath you and have you asking yourself, "Why did I spend all of that time playing the MI games only to be told none of it mattered in the end?" This stupid meta ending is literally the worst buzzkill EVER!The ending is also one of the biggest cop-outs in term of storytelling. All of the plot lines, character arcs, unresolved issues, etc... ALL OF IT gets swept off the table like they never existed. What's left is a scrapbook letter with Ron Gilbert lecturing the player about life.And you know what? This game basically ruined any potential sequel to the MI series (for me) because any MI game(s) that comes out after this one will have me saying, "why bother playing it? it doesn't really matter anyways." Thanks Ron.so in summary, whenever someone asks me about the Monkey Island series? I will tell them to play Secret (MI1), Revenge (MI2), and my favorite Curse (MI3); which funny enough was the one WITHOUT Ron Gilbert's involvement.P.S. - Don't play "Thimbleweed Park", another one of Ron's game, either. It also has a meta ending (apparently bad endings are Ron's forte).
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Fun! Keeps a lot of the original MI1+2 humor and doesn't pretend 3+4+5 never happened. The environment visuals are somehow a very satisfying evolution from the low resolution SCUMM era to high resolution vector art feel. The character visuals have that paper puppet look that isn't for everyone, but still feels lovingly drawn, surprisingly expressive, and I suspect will age quite well -- far better than the 3D of Escape and Tales have aged.The music is exactly what you want it to be, and even continues the tradition of doing slight changes to the instruments from room to room that made such an impression back in MI2. The voice acting is strong, and I personally think they did a great job casting for LeChuck, as daunting a task as that must've been.The best part, though? The horse armor, of course. Who would've expected one little piece of armor could unlock so many secrets?

_childDocuments_.review: I am a longtime Monkey Island fan and I was looking forward to this new episode of the saga. In spite of Return of Monkey Island's many positive aspects, the finale completely spoiled the game experience for me, to the point where I cannot recommend the game. The ending of the game is not just bad: it is insulting to the players and particularly the series' fans, as if it was giving them the middle finger for having wasted their time on it.Return of Monkey Island is essentially an old-school point-and-click adventure, but with a very simplified interface. The most substantial departure from traditional adventure games is that it's mostly impossible to perform wrong actions: the game just won't allow the player to try something that doesn't work (or that at least makes some sense, in which case it will provide an appropriate response). This, together with the relative scarcity of content, makes the puzzles much easier than in previous games, causing Return to Monkey Island to be quite short and not very challenging (even at the highest difficulty level and without using the in-game hint system).Although it caused quite a lot of controversy, I like the visual style of Return to Monkey Island. It's certainly unconventional and a departure from both the original pixel graphics and the cartoonish style of Course of Monkey Island, but it fits the tone of the game well. I also loved the score, sound effects and dubbing, which features the return of original voice actors such as Dominic Armato for Guybrush.So far, so good: Return of Monkey Island provides an enjoyable and smooth experience full of piratesque humor and good puzzles (although on the easy side), featuring a cast of returning beloved characters plus a few interesting additions. The plot proceeds smoothly, with a Guybrush obsessing over the still undiscovered secret of Monkey Island while having to deal with a changing world. Though, something feels off: the game's world is half empty and a bit dull, as if the production was rushed off and plenty of content never made it to the final version.I will now spoil the ending and what the secret of Monkey Island is, don't read on if you don't want to have it revealed.I feel sorry for all the people who worked at Return to Monkey Island, as they did plenty of good work (especially in the art and audio departments). Unfortunately, the game betrays the contempt Ron Gilbert has for his own players. This much is clear: I'm done with his games, since he despises me so much for playing them!

_childDocuments_.review: It's no good! yet, I can't not recommend a game of Monkey Island, BUTI entered with open mind regarding the art design, but boy oh boy the character design of Guybrush gives memories of "Escape" and MI1 special edition a run for its money! look what have they done to my boy! :DWhy on earth he has a penis for a nose?! what look they were going? an alcoholic? and to his son, I mean fine that they had to address ending of MI2, but constantly cutting back to the son really destroys the mood and story and any shred of immersion. it's really insufferable and tediousStill it's a freaking monkey island! just to hear Dominic Armato's voice worths the trouble!P.S: the ending is so obnoxious and cynical, ultimately too meta and depressing.
