_childDocuments_.review: Truly a canonical sequel to LeChuck's Revenge at last, after - as 90 percent of other reviews have pointed out - 30 years.The game is in itself a worthy installment of the 2D series. It defied expectations in that it was actually good, when i expected it to be mostly nostalgia bait.Spoilers below.I could tell from the beginning the symbolic nature of the game; written the same creators of the classic ones, now aged 30 years older. Having played LeChucks revenge, the beginning itself is sure to immediately make yourself reflect on the series.  Guybrush is older and his children are running around, pulling pranks and playing pirates, their minds full of imagination. They cannot wait to themselves set out on adventure, like in all those stories Guybrush has told them. Our man sits on a bench, seemingly reflecting on the past, which for us is, the past of the series and the implied in-between happenings of Guybrush' life. It was a comforting opener for a long time fan. Strangely, 30 years is an apt time for this game to finally come into our lives. I imagine most of us registered monkey island enjoyers (judging by the reviews here on steam) are at least past our early twenties and can relate to reflections of what youth, hope and imagination promised and how different it all turned out to be, for good and bad. It is hard not to become sentimental when this game opens. However, it is only in the opening and in the end it has this effect.The adventure begins and its proper a monkey island game, in all its monkey island-ness. That will suffice to describe the experience. Some parts dragged, other parts were fun and exciting. Call-backs, sure to confuse any new player of the series, can be found almost everywhere, but like previously stated the game is surprisingly not just cheap nostalgia bait. There is inspiration and love in the writing, amusing humor and puzzles in the gameplay, but it is not a flawless gem. It is more of a mixed bag of passion project and modern game design pitfalls, in a word: casualisation. The game is easier than earlier installments. The "hard mode" includes more puzzles, but they are quite obvious all of them, except for one including a temporarily distracted head of state. I dare not think of just how easy the easy mode must be. The strategy is no longer try every item with everyone and every interactable object, as used to be the case. Items cannot be interacted with people or objects where they will have no effect. Aside from the latter point, this is not necessarily bad. A staple of the point-and click adventures from this team and adjacent developers of its era are filled with far-fetched nonsense puzzles, that once theyre solved, most of the time with a guide, make you shake your head in annoyance rather than admire how clever they are. My experience, atleast. An hour or so into the game, i was planning on writing a sarcastic review about melee island being ahead of its time with diversity hires, but that would have been unfair. There was a moment of it seeming to be the case, that a focus group had handed in a list of bullet points on what must be included to sell a modern game as far as the design and traits the human characters must have, but i quickly realised this is in fact not the case. There appears to have been a genuine concern with making the game as timeless as the classic ones, not opting for topical satire applicable to the early 2020s.That is my main critique of the game. The "shut the lights off" segment at the end took me right back to the reflecting of the beginning, but tinged with more melancholy. I had hoped this was but a new kickstart of more 2D Monkey island adventures, but i dont think thats the case. The ending is as much of a perfect ending as there could be to Monkey Island, or any adventure series.  As far as the humor goes, they may have exaggerated a little with the amount of beurocracy jokes.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I'd downvote a MI by Ron Gilbert, but here we are.The wonderful music is still there, Dominic is as great as ever, and many beloved characters and locations are back. Personally I am not a fan of the visuals, but I suppose that is a matter of taste and they don't make or brake the game anyway.My main qualm with RMI is that it feels rushed and unfinished. Islands have very few locations, and rooms are mostly empty but for the few things you'll need to use. There are possibly more items in Woodtick town in Monkey Island 2 alone than in this whole game put together. There's less NPCs, less locations, less items, which means less puzzles that are also easier to solve. I am not exactly a genius and I completed the game in about 10 hours, taking my time and exploring every dialogue choice. I didn't get stuck even once. Also, much of the humour in previous games came from commentary on stuff that was just lying about for fun's sake. You would Look At, try to Pick Up, or Use this with that not because you thought it would forward you in the game but to see what would Guybrush comment on it. Now all that is mostly gone. Just as an example, in MI2 Phatt Island had a whole library of books, each of them a joke; now we are given Carla's library with... six or seven books, and the titles are not even funny. We waited for this game for 30 years, why couldn't they take a little more time to flesh it out? It could have been great.The writing and the story are not great either. I get what the devs tried to convey (it is very clearly stated in the final letter in the scrapbook after the ending), but there has to be a better way of putting that feeling into a game. Personally I thought it was bland and lazy.For old Monkey Island fans this is a bittersweet walk down Memory Lane, but I don't think there is much in this game to recommend it to players who are new to the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game, in the second chapter so far. Long time monkey island fan, I have the limited run games re-release with guybrush threepwood statue and a book with trivia about the series so when I heard there was a new one I was super excited. Classic comedy so far. Ron Gilbert and company knocked it out of the park.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Played the first Monkey Island the year it was released and dozens of other point-and-click adventures since then. Ron Gilbert and Co. have played the "the ending does not matter" card in at least other four games now. But in his previous titles the story arcs lead to a sense of conclusion, even if the overall ending did not. I gave Gilbert the benefit of doubt regarding regarding the five meta-endings of Thimbleweed Park. But the doubts dissipated after listening to one of his interviews where he tells he actually never had a complete story in his mind while developing the game and that the endings were simply ad libbed.Return to Monkey Island repeats the "nothing really matters" trick. The game starts by establishing rapport and tension while keeping the audience engaged. Then Guybrush morphs into an unnecessarily cruel character that wrecks everything and everyone without any comeuppance. Yes, Guybrush screwed up dozens of things in previous MI titles, but he always owned them: the major story arcs in previous games are actually about Guybrush fixing them. Not here. Guybrush's actions are simply remorseless, incoherent and not entertaining. And the ending is simply egotistic and selfish. It is not "meta" and not "clever". If Gilbert and the rest of the team are having some sort of mid-life crisis and are unable to provide their audience a sense of closure to the stories they create, then they should invest in some therapist instead of spending time developing games. If you are immune to incoherence and disappointments then play this. Otherwise, there are plenty of rewarding point-and-click adventure out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Now that I have finished the game I will revise my original review. The tonal oddness which I complained about fortunately changes to a lighter, more entertaining narrative. In the end, I forgave the game the grotesk hiccups from earlier scenes. I'd now give it a neutral review, which isn't possible, but overall my experience was more positive than negative so I'll go with the thumbs up.Here's my original review:I'm a Monkey Island fan since I was a teenager and was more than thrilled when I read about the comeback of the franchise. Indeed, after a few hours of playing I can say that a lot of the old charm is back. And I don't mind the new graphics at all. They are playful and fun. Most importantly, the voice actors have returned and do a terrific job as always.However, something has changed about the game's tone that I really dislike... and find even somewhat upsetting. Monkey Island has (in a few scenes) become mean-spirited and cynical. And that is something I would never have expected. How the heck did that even happen? There are a couple of scenes where Guybrush's actions bring harm to other creatures and all of this is celebrated as if it was funny. Unfortunately, it isn't. Not here. Not in this fictional universe. This isn't the nihilistic Rick and Morty where some sort of self-reflective meta-storytelling is key. It's Monkey Island. You know, the point and click game about funny pirates... I wonder if the creators somehow felt the urge to be a bit "edgy" now that LucasArts isn't involved anymore. Some feeling of finally being allowed to go a bit bonkers. But that edginess only resulted in a a weird and incoherent tone that isn't enjoyable to follow anymore. It's just not the contract that the player thought to have entered in with a game that offers escapism and cartoonish, childish fun. The cynicism jumps at us as a surprise and irritates. That's a real weakness in storytelling that left me and my girlfriend literally speechless, until we looked at each other, shaking our heads, and both saying at the same time: "Was that supped to be funny??"No, I definitely don't think that Monkey Island needed to be darker and more post-modern. It doesn't fit the world, tone and content. And all that's left is... how do kids call it these days again? Ah, yeah... "cringe".
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is very much in the vain of the usual Monkey Island games and that would make you think i'd recommend it.  I'm not bothered with the art style, thats not why either.  The reason i don't recommend this game is that it has no ending.  The game does end and pretends to have an ending but story wise there is no pay off.  None of the open threads get resolved.  I'm not upset that a certain important thread is unresolved, i'm disappointed that none of the threads get resolved.  The game builds up to a crescendo and then just ends, not a cliff hanger, it ends.A game like this is so heavily narrative driven, for it to just end that's a waste of my mental investment.  I'm all for clever endings or well thought out subversions but this one is neither.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Cartoon animal cruelty broke my heart. Also, a few gripes with the game.I was a huge fan of the original series, and I bought this as soon as it came out. I have not finished this game yet, but wanted to comment on one of the quests I just completed because it really bothered me. A group of happy animals were living in a forest until Guybrush recklessly destroys it. The animals are all left crying, homeless, and some are even on fire. There was no reason for this part of the story -- it was just cruel. I wasn't a huge fan of this game before that, but now I definitely don't recommend it. Some other issues with the game (spoilers ahead): 1) Sometimes you are able to pick things up without having a reason, but sometimes you cannot because "I don't need that." This bothers me because I'm playing the game on the hard difficulty (which is surprisingly easy) and would welcome some red herrings in my inventory. 2) You can't call up the aerial map of the island (for fast travel) from just anywhere. You have to walk to one particular scene, which (depending on where you are) takes just as long as if you were to walk to the scene you're trying to get to.3) The to-do list changes independently of the dialog/gameplay. For example the first quest was to get a ship, but then it updated to getting onto LeChuck's ship instead. This would be fine if it aligned with the progressing story, but I was still wandering around asking people to help me get a ship until I looked at the list and noticed it had changed. It's a clunky (and confusing) experience to have one goal but have dialog options for the original one.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful new entry to the series. At first the changes in the gameplay may upset some of the fans but in the end I felt like nothing was missing, the distinctive puzzles and humour of the classics are there.  Recommendend for who enjoyed the Monkey Island series, a bit less for the newcomers that will miss much of the references
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Long time Monkey Island fan (starting with MI2 back in the 90's).Up to this point the only entry in the franchise I bumped up against negatively was MI4 but even that had its merits however based purely on the trailer I had a series of concerns about "Return to".1. The Art style (I could not tell how it would jive with the game play)2. Armato's voice sounded weak (tired) in places 3. The lip sync seemed off4. The replacement actor for LeChuck didn't seem to fit 5. A generic concern about new characters over old characters In hindsight (during play) none of these turned out to be issues and I am enjoying myself immensely !!!A. I acclimatised to the art style in just a few minutes B. The break in Armato's voice is few and far between (and he has earned the odd off note)C. Can't tell if it is accurate but the lip sync does not bother me during play D. The new voice fits this even pettier (if you can believe that) LeChuck variant well (though I would like to know how he is kicking about)E. I like the new characters and thus far I am not pining for missing entries (MI3-5)Curiously (given RG being a stickler for improvements) my only complaint is regarding the interaction controls e.g. having to go into the inventory to grab an item  just picked up, having to keep going into inventory to use an item more then once, lack of interaction with inventory items (you see the red NO sign a lot in this one), no ESC command for the main menu, and of course the lack of teleportation (although it turns out the sea map can be used on land). Good job Ron and crew !
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that manages to be more than nostalgia bait. I was among those who was uncertain of the new art style, but it works for the game in action. The puzzles are sensible and fun. The story is well written, and I loved the framing device. The only complaint I have is that the trio of new villains, while appropriate to the game's theme of the struggle between old and new, were not of themselves particularly interesting (even if Alix Wilton Regan happens to be my favorite VA--she was kind of wasted on the role). What I did love was Le Chuck's crew. All told, this is a worthy addition to the Monkey Island legacy.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I could not love this game more. It is a tremendous gift to fans of Monkey Island and adventure games as a whole, crafted by consummate professionals of the genre, demonstrating not only their expertise but their desire to consistently evolve the medium.I also applaud the bold art direction of Rex Crowle, which is so rich in personality and atmosphere. The character designs convey a humor and whimsy that is such an intrinsic part of the series, and brilliantly compliment the incredible performances by the voice cast. And the ENVIRONMENTS! The environments are all beautifully rich and immersive, constructing a fantastical world which I wish I could spend far more time in. I greatly appreciate that Gilbert and Grossman embraced such a distinct and unique art style for their triumphant collective return to the series, which does not play it safe but is as expressive and creative as the game itself. It's fresh as hell and so fun to spend time in.Playing this game truly warmed by heart, from discovering the Scrapbook in the main menu which acknowledges and honors all the games in the franchise, till the very end of the credits. This is in very many ways a love letter to the series, and something which us fans are so lucky to be able to play.More!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was very pessimistic, but then I heard the title melody and it reminded me of old times, good times. And even though everything is different, it felt so familiar. As if I had come back home and pick up where I left off as a child. Back to Monkey Island. I mean...Return to Monkey Island. Lovin' it!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Monkey Island fans will be severely disappointed.In past Monkey Island games the developers spiced up the game play by sending players to brand new locations in each new title, that were all full of beautiful scenery, wonderfully interesting characters and fantastic puzzles. Not so in this game.In Return to Monkey Island you literally return to what you already know. The game plays like a creatively bankrupt revisiting or reimagining of (mostly) the first Monkey Island game. The developers apparently took "Return" to Monkey Island too literally and it goes a bit like this: Oh hi <character from former game> in <location from former game that looks just slightly different>.Now don't misunderstand me, revisiting characters and locales from former games is great, but that is the key element of Return to Monkey Island, which is absolutely absurd.On to puzzles, of which there is only one in the first two hours or so. ONE. Otherwise the game is almost on rails instead of giving the player a major objective and letting them figure what to do themselves. That said, I'd say that developers were more influenced by Telltale story games than by Monkey Island itself.As if this all weren't bad enough, there is figuratively speaking of course a cherry on top as garnish, which is obviously the extremely controversial art style that has been at the center of discussion.The art style in Monkey Island 1 to 3 was absolutely wonderful. One of the greatest things about Monkey Island is finding a new scene to enjoy. You would always stop just to admire the artists beautiful rendition of the world, with all of it satisfying nooks, crannies and enjoyable tidbits. Some of my best memories of Monkey Island are doing just that. This marvelous and charming art was the framework for the story and adventures you had with Guybrush. When it all fell into place, there was a special spot in this overarching scheme for every wonderful experience you ever had, like discovering the mystery of the El Chupacabra chicken demon.This art style, however, is not beautiful. It is not interesting, appealing or charming in any way. I could possibly live with that, but the art style in Return to Monkey Island is in fact incredibly irritating and just plain appalling. The characters are just barely acceptable, but the scenery is made up of wildly garbled geometric shapes that are completely out of any logical or coherent proportion. It is probably the most atrocious art style I ever laid my eyes upon in a video game. I am absolutely astonished how it could have ever possibly been greenlighted.All said, this game feels like it was churned out the with the least amount of effort, by a development team that does not care about Monkey Island or understand what made it so great in the first place. The game play and art style are absolutely preposterous, which is why I give this game the lowest rating of any Monkey Island game. As you might suspect, I am indeed a huge Monkey Island fan and have therefore played every single title in this series. Some are great, some are forgettable, but none of them are unacceptable. That was until today.4/10And remember: Never pay more than 20 bucks for a video game.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Hooray! OK so Monkey Island 1 and 2 are the best games on planet earth agreed? Then the others came along and I wish they hadn't. But.... Return to Monkey Island is exactly what we needed so thankyou Ron Gilbert and Co. Amazing and lets just pretend that this is Monkey Island 3 and everything after Money Island 2 didn't happen.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing Return! Guybrush Threepwood looks and moves better than ever and this time he's after the legendary Secret of Monkey Island! Are you as excited as I am?? Checkout my  review!I'm an old time fan of the series, so this review is specially written for fans like me. The game should be accessible enough for the new public, but I´m not among that audience so can't really judge without bias.Let's start with the . Yeah, I feel you all, it's not what we had been wishing for, right? But after 10 minutes of playing it started to grow on me. The scenarios are so beautiful and full of life and details, the characters move also incredible, I must say I still don't like Guybrush face that much but oh boy, check out Lechuck! That guy is scary and so well designed!Now the , well, there's nothing revolutionary about them if you have been playing adventure games for the last 10 years. But they are very well designed! You'll get stuck, I got stuck! But taking a break, looking at all the clues again, trying some things... managed to solve the game in hard mode without using the hintbook. I was expecting some kind of achivement, but I guess that was not a thing for Ron. I liked a lot the new UI as well, I wasn't sure at first, but the 2 button UI is pretty clever!Let´s end with the . The game starts right after MI2 finished and then moves quickly to find the Secret of Monkey Island. Expect a lot of old scenarios and characters to appear and challenge you again. The writing is, as expected, very high quality and the story feels rewarding as you play it. I didn´t find myself bored or lost, not a single time!To wrap up, I´m very happy this game came out, I wasn´t expecting it at all and it has given me so much happiness since I started playing it. The ending... I'll leave it there. The ending is a thing to discuss. Maybe a story for some other day?Stay stafe you little salty pirates!

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly fan service for previous games. The "puzzles" are boring and fairly plain with most time in the game being navigation. What little of an ending there was felt unfinished as it had the easiest puzzles and would have served better as the intro to the game. The actual ending is just bad. Much akin to the 'it was all a dream' trope for when you cant write a proper ending in 6th grade.*edit* Anyone who says its mostly about the story telling is both right and wrong. That's all the game really has but due to the end being so bad, just leaves a sour taste in your mouth. I would refund my time and money if I could as this game wasn't worth either.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I'll do my best to explain my disappointment in this game without spoilers. The gameplay is fine, there are some good puzzles and jokes—it's entertaining enough while it lasts. But ultimately, the story adds nothing worthwhile to the series. The ending is just bad. Let me be clear: I'm not disappointed that the secret of Monkey Island didn't turn out to be something original and amazing. I wasn't expecting it to: it's only ever been a Macguffin, after all. No, even if the revelation of what the secret of Monkey Island actually is had completely blown my mind, I would still be disappointed in the conclusion of this game, or perhaps I should say, the lack of a conclusion. The story follows Guybrush and LeChuck racing to be the first to find the Secret, but in the final act, the plot is simply abandoned without any resolution. Again, let me be clear: I don't mind that the ending is weird and ambiguous. I loved the weird and ambiguous ending of Monkey Island 2, but that ending came  the resolution of the plot. Guybrush defeated LeChuck in a final showdown, and then Gilbert and Co sprang that crazy ending on us with its "it was all just a dream" suggestion. If that ending had instead come immediately after Guybrush landed on Dinky island, Monkey Island 2 would have felt just as incomplete and disappointing as this game. Even a story that turns out to be just the overactive imagination of a kid in an amusement park needs to be brought to a proper conclusion. Although it has some good qualities, I'm sorry to say I can't really recommend this game as being worth your time or your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: After "Thimbleweed Park", Terrible Toybox makes its Return to a beloved classic. The pirate humor sets this game apart and you can sense that it bears the original creators' handwriting. (In my opinion, the other sequels never really got there 100%, even if they were excellent games in their own right.)While Guybrush recounted most of MI II to Elaine, he is telling the current adventure to their son. A nice trait for all the original fans who were kids back then and are now playing this adventure with their children.The whole game is teeming with allusions to Monkey Island I and II, even most puzzles are reminiscent of things you had to do in these earlier parts of the series. They are never too hard for somebody who loves to play this kind of game. For my personal taste, they could have been even more convoluted at times, but they are always very well crafted.The whole point&click-interface is really userfriendly and polished to make the gameplay intuitive.Played the "hard" (=normal) mode with more blather, of course (you have to tick the box in the menu options). Who would possibly want to miss out on some free extra blather?The ending is something quite special and about living up to unrealistic expectations...
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy instalment in the Monkey Island franchise, it features many of the old characters, locations, familiar theme music and voice overs by the original voice actors, which gives the game a real feel of authenticity and nostalgia. But it also introduces enough new content and variation to keep things fresh.You get to pick between a normal and hard mode for the puzzles and I selected hard, which I thought was very well balanced for seasoned puzzle gamers, it gave the game a good length. There's a good ramp up in difficulty, starting very simple to introduce the mechanics to you, and increasingly gets harder, as you progress the number of puzzles you're solving in parallel expands quite significantly, but they also have a to-do list which helps you keep track of your objectives and their relationship as part of the bigger picture. I'm also very pleasantly surprised to see there are some distraction in the environment and inventory designed to throw you off, items never used to solve puzzles. The inventory itself becomes very large near the end game, as you keep most of what you find. This means you have to think, you can't randomly combine stuff.It also sports an incredibly good hints system, it's entirely optional to use and gives extremely fine grain hints in order of importance. They start with pointing you roughly in the right direction and getting more and more specific the more you request help. If you feel like you want to use a hint because progress has slowed and become frustrating, then you can get the absolutely minimum help without being given the answer, which means puzzles retain a sense of accomplishment, often all you need is a tiny nudge in the right direction.Murray returns, enough said really, this was a joy in and of itself.Sadly the graphics did not do much for me. They aren't bad by any stretch of the imagination, there's a well thought out style and it would work extremely well for a new adventure game, unrelated to this series. But Monkey Island artistically peaked with the absolutely beautiful hand drawn art in the Curse of Monkey island in 1997, and since then has struggled to replace it with something as good, this is sadly no exception. Even the hand drawn special edition remakes were nicer. I'd hoped they'd grow on me but it remained distracting throughout. This is a solid 9/10 for a puzzle game and could have been a 10/10 with a more suitable art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I have to recommend this game because it is Monkey Island, and I've been a fan of the series since the very start. I want there to be more of them. I have liked/loved all of the other games in the series, including the much-maligned Escape. However this one is by far my lowest-ranked game in the series for many reasons.First, the positives. The music is great and most of the voice actors that make a return are great as always. There are many funny jokes and gags, and Guybrush is the same lovable borderline-sociopath as before. The puzzles make sense and the game flows fairly well without any really boring pixel-hunting. The plot/story (up to a point) is typical Monkey Island pirate adventure fare, and therefore perfectly fine for me. I want a funny pirate-themed adventure, and for the most part I got that. I enjoyed exploring the different islands and hearing Guybrush's comments on everything.Now on to the... less positive. Some of the new actors sound a bit like someone's relative reading lines rather than acting, but it isn't so bad that it takes you out of the game.The puzzles almost all make sense (which is rare for any adventure game), but they are very easy to solve. I played on the "hard" mode and I can't even imagine what the casual/easy mode is like.The game is a good length, but a lot of my play time is leaving the game running while doing tasks around the house and The art style is something that each person will have to make their own decision on. The best way I can describe the effect the art style had on me is that it is the visual equivalent of putting crackling and popping sounds in audio on purpose and calling it an audio style. It detracted from my enjoyment of the game. Everything looks extra disgusting and it was very difficult for me to tell what some objects were or what most facial expressions were trying to convey. On the same topic, the animations, for the most part, were very basic. The whole effect was unpleasant and came across as cheap/amateurish. Some people have described it as old Newgrounds flash-game level, and I think that is being mean to some of the nice work people did on those games in the past.On to the writing. At its best, it was clever and entertaining. For the most part, it was serviceable. However, there were some pretty big problems with it.LeChuck felt less menacing than ever. He was barely an adversary. Elaine felt very flat and boring. She was barely a character. The three new bad guys are barely fleshed out. They have some new kind of dark magic, but not much is said about what it is or how it is different from voodoo. They are well voice acted, however, and work well as enemies to both Guybrush and LeChuck. The rest of the characters were okay. Nothing else really stood out to me except maybe Stan, who always carries the games on his expressive shoulders.The endings, whoo boy. All spoilers from here on out.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all of the Monkey Island games (and yes that includes Escape); and this is probably my new second favorite in the whole series.  It was great to see this series finally make a return, and with a fun new art style to boot!  Sure, some of the puzzles were meh, but the good far out weighed the bad.  And yes, I actually DID like the ending, which is hilarious that people were getting upset about it.  I won't spoil it, but as someone who loves the series and has played them; it makes sense and I honestly think it was the best way for them to handle it.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, this turned out to be a mediocre attempt at pulling some nostalgia strings with a big raised middlefinger towards the fans as its finale.To get this out of the way, because it has been discussed unnecessarily much, the game is ugly. I dislike the children picture book style and the cut out paper doll animations. It prevented me from getting immersed and I think except for a few, well,  exceptions, the characters look horrible, especially Guybrush. But I knew that before I bought the game and decided I could live with it in exchange for a new Monkey Island.Only to find out it was hardly worth it.The story's pretty bad. Guybrush, for no particular reason, wants to go find that Secret of Monkey Island and by pure random chance, LeChuck  a bunch of nobodies you are supposed to accept as your new antagonists you'll hardly even deal with decide they want to do the same thing at the same time. Some of the sub-scenarios are alright, but the overall arc lacks any form of urgency, motivation or at least character development. The story meanders aimlessly from one plotpoint to the next without any build-up to anything.However, it was a neat idea to have this game's structure resemble the first two games, but it could've been implemented better.The game attempts a few times to do some heavy-handed commentary and self-reflection, but drops those questions immediately and moves on without any resolutions.This ship was still on its way into thumbs up harbour, though, because, sure, not great, but okay enough plus Monkey Island coziness for the feels. But then came the ending. It's exactly the sort of feces-like ending I feared they'd give this. It's : Hoped through the whole credits there would at least be another scene to turn this train wreck around at the last moment, but no, they really did it. Ruined the whole game.What's on the good side? The game is of decent length and the puzzles/riddles are mostly nice and fun, even if it takes a bit too long until they finally get more complex and difficult. You do a lot of brainless busywork until it gets more interesting, but when it does, it's good. The humor is entertaining and well-dosed. The music is nice. Not as good as in the previous games, but those classic themes can't do much wrong.This thumbs down doesn't mean it's a horrible game. It's a slightly above average game with the bonus of revisiting a beloved franchise that gets pulled down to somewhere below average by it's extraordinarilly incompetent and audience trolling ending. There's still fun to be had along the way, but it does too many things wrong or mediocrely to warrant a recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers and emotions ahead!So .... here I am .. in my 40th.I just finished this game.At first I was surprised about the set up of the end scene.Then I saw Elaine standing there waiting for guybrush.And I completely understood.The secret of monkey islandTM? I dont care... all I wanted is to make guybrush go home with Elaine. So I turned of the lights...no turning back..."I am ready to go  home" And so they went.And then there is Guybrush talking to his son again..Elaine comes in and I am happy for this family somewehere in the ficitonal caribean.. She is off.Guybruhs..is looking me straight in the eyes. Breaking the forth wall with nothing but along stare. I feel strange. What is going on?The credits roll. Back to the main menu.I browse through the new content of the album.Read the letter from Ron Gilbert (and the other guy)The music plays and I am in tears. Sobbing. Remembering that moment when i finished MI 1 in the 90th. 12 years old. Now im 42, two kids, a life of ups and downs, like most of us.Im so thankfull for reminding me what the secret of monkey island realy is.Where ever you are out there. Have a good life and take care.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a Monkey Island fan, you will be satisfied. Many reviewers wanted the old graphic style of Monkey Island, which I honestly love. However, I do find this new style refreshing and intuitive. MI is the reference for all point-and-click adventure games. I can't wait for the next one. This story should not finish; it is nostalgic, wonderful, and entertaining.

Kind of like in Ren & Stimpy or similar cartoons (only missing the Valentino foghorn sound effect).- puzzle design is mediocre, leading to a short to medium lenght gamethere were only 1 or 2 unfair puzzles that took me a while; on harder difficulty it essentially boils down to more backtracking and more inventory puzzleswhat I disliked:- the ending is a letdown for me; however I will admit that I don't think that any ending would have satisfied everybody, especially after 30 years and different sequels from different creators that all added to the lore and therefore raised the stakes for Gilbert and Grossmann to respect everything that the people liked about the other gamesAll in all I would recommend Return to Monkey Island, if only for the characters and dialogues as well as the music.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a new SCUMM game from LucasArts. It's the real deal.The new art style might be jarring at first glance, but once you get into the game, you quickly realize this is a 4k analog of a hybrid of the classic Monkey 1+2+3 artstyle with much heavier emphasis of the first two.The writing is f*****g splendid. It's genuinely as funny as the originals, nay, funnier even.Michael Land made more beautiful miracles with the music. I've listened to Curse OST to hell and back so it's super nice to have new tracks and renditions of old beloved tracks. I gushed listening to the forest music on Melee island. Now to get ahold of the score. Hope to get a big box physical of the game including it.If you ever liked the original Monkey Island games, or any adventure games, and you haven't played this yet, you're wasting your life away. _childDocuments_.review: perfect addition to a majestic seriesit's point'n click at it's corejust like i remember it from back in the day when i first played Day of, the lucas arts Indiana Jones games orMonkey Islandthe voice over is spot on, the soundtrack fits the series like it was always there and the new art-style works and especialy characters look incrediblethe level of detail has been slightly detailed due to the art-style, but the picture, aka characters+backrounds and lighting just looks great.some of the "new" additional game-elements like the trivia cards or the hintbook have been included in a way that is very organic. you can engage with these mechanics and if you do they feel natural, or you can just ignore em and not lose anything special. very happy with the gameeven more happy when looking at the pricing: they could've milked the series name, yet they have chose to be customer friendly (and looking at all the voice-over i don't think the game was cheap to produce).

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece!Maybe a little too short, maybe with an unexpected ending, maybe feeling a bit rushed in the final chapters... but it is a masterpiece nonetheless.Some people say they don't like the Art style and would prefer something else (pixel, "remaster" style, etc.), but I liked it from the first teaser up to the final credits. It doesn't live up to my expectations.I recommend the first three MI games, but I can't really recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+True Monkey Island!! From the original creator, Ron Gilbert!!+Art style and direction, colors, character designs and animations are all fun and perfect for the setting.+UI is smooth, simple and does not detract from the visuals+Music is amazing and is equal parts nostalgia and new.+Puzzles (hard mode) are what any fans of the series have come to expect and range from easy to very difficult (but logical and with little to no frustration). Very satisfying to finally solve the harder ones that have been blocking your progress for awhile+Solid voice acting (for the most part). The returning cast--Guybrush (Dominic Armato!!), Carla, Voodoo Lady, Murray, Elaine, Wally, etc.--are all very good...buuuuut (see cons)...Cons:-Some of the voice acting is a little flat and uninspired. Also I also would have loved Earl Boen's LeChuck and Patrick Pinney's Stan to return to their roles here! (New LeChuck is ok, Stan is...oi...)-Script, story, and humor take a little while to get going. I realized this con was probably being influenced by my love for the "laugh-a-minute" humor in Curse (which wasn't Ron Gilbert's game)...once I recalibrated my expectations to be more in line with 1 and 2, in which the humor was more subtle, I relaxed a little. And to those just starting out: Stay with it! It gets funnier! :DOverall:I would definitely recommend this game to anyone! I'm just really glad to have a new chapter of Monkey Island...those of us who grew up with this series know the special feeling when those games were released, and are undoubtedly feeling that same feeling now! Those new to the series will definitely want to go check out the earlier entries as well!

_childDocuments_.review: My husband and I remember playing the Monkey Island series as children.  When they got remastered, we introduced the series to our children. _childDocuments_.review: Context: I've played all the Monkey Island games when they were released, and I waited 30+ years for Ron's version of Monkey 3.Pros:- Cutting edge adventure gaming!- Virtually flawless, this is a fairly large game and I only found one minor bug with the inventory and left/right clicking.- Lovely art style- Amazing music- Captures the Monkey Island atmosphere perfectly.- Variety of well thought out puzzles- The Monkey Island brand of humorCons (but really nitpicks): - Not really a con, but I wish there was a way to create ultra hard mode. The puzzles are so well made that they are never too hard to figure out. It's a compromise between dificulty and accessibility, I guess.- The pacing is uneven, as if there's been some late editing to cut content, and there's a bit of too much reuse of scenarios.- The new pirate bosses don't really have any purpose to the story.- The game gets too meta for its own good at times, especially towards the end.- No three headed monkeys? (That I've seen)- No post ending advice on how much to spend on a game.- Not a lot of new "instantly classic" Monkey Island characters.- It's a real game instead of a potentially perfect Monkey 3a each of us had in our heads. That's sadly the real price we had to pay to Return to Monkey Island.Rating: 3 out of 3 Monkey heads.

_childDocuments_.review: Secret to Monkey Island has a very special place in my heart, as it's one of the first "real" games I remember playing as a very, very young child, back in the days of AOL and Windows 95/98. The game engendered in me a love of puzzles that's continued on to this day in my gaming habits. Eventually I would add LeChuck's Revenge and Curse of Monkey Island to my repertoire, as well as other LucasArts and point-and-click games. I'd replay them, year after year after year. So needless to say, I know the series. I love the series, though that's not to say there haven't been disappointments.Escape and Tales are shlock. They are sad stains on the lovingly crafted t-shirt that is the series as a whole. With shoddy graphics, rancid controls, and embarrassing writing - not to mention gameplay that I wouldn't call puzzles, for various reasons, if a cutlass was held to my throat - I wasn't sure what I felt when I heard there would be a Return to Monkey Island. Trepidation, perhaps.The first I heard was all the hullabaloo over the art style. When the site came out, I meandered that way, and was pleasantly... surprised. The style was certainly not what I expected, but it somehow seemed to capture the charm of the series (at least the charm held by the first three games). The writing on the site had that Monkey Island pizzazz I had come to know and love. I found my trepidation turned to excitement. I pre-purchased, and my husband and I set down to tackle the trilogy together.And then the day came. I downloaded the game. I installed it. I took a deep breath and pressed play.The scrapbook was a charming way to recap the previous games, but that wasn't what I was here for. I started a new game.We played through the prelude, and both my husband and I were quick to see that the shortsighted numskulls decrying the art style were entirely wrong. It just *fits*. Fits the world, the story, the characters. The movements and miniature cut-scenes during dialogue and such are done with love and care (and reminded us, vaguely, of Ren and Stimpy). It was unique and yet somehow reminiscent of the pixel art. Not only the characters, but the backgrounds were feasts for the eyes. If you love the series and for some reason think you need to pass this one over because of the art style, you're objectively wrong. Sorry, I don't make the rules! (Am I being hyperbolic? Who cares! There are people out there that made the graphics designers/artists feel so bad that they stopped posting screenshots... you're not cool people for that, yanno? You're, actually, really terrible!)I, being a lover of puzzles, went hard mode/writer's cut. Best decision of my life. I never opened the hint book, though a few times I felt sorely tempted. But when I figured out the puzzles - and I mean EVERY SINGLE ONE - I felt that rewarding AH-HAH! moment. Not a SINGLE PUZZLE annoyed me. Every one was EXCEPTIONALLY well done. So many of them were based on PAYING ATTENTION - something I adore. And so many of them had that quirky, LucasArts puzzle logic we've come to love so much. Of course, I don't want to take ages playing a puzzle-based game - I have limited free time, but I've never had that issue with the Monkey series (at least the good ones). Even back in the day when I was 7-8 playing Secret, I finished that game first time, no walkthroughs (had no idea how to search for one!) in about a week, and that was only because I had limited time as a grade-school kid. So it felt right that this one didn't throw any SUPER MEGA DIFFICULT puzzles into the ring, because the GOOD Monkey Island games have NEVER had those.The characters were entirely 100% themselves, something I hated about the Tales series.The writing and jokes were snappy and pure Monkey Island. My husband and I were always either charmed or amused by the writing. The many references were appreciated.The interface is pure joy. It's simple drag and drop. Not the "put two items in two bubbles and click the plus button" trash from Tales. Not the tank controls from Escape, which have NEVER been good.The music is crisp and absolutely an audio treat for the ears. There are several times when themes are reused and it works perfectly, or the instrumentation changes. It's all just... chef's kiss.And finally, the story. Wow... what a story.!!! SPOILERS AHEAD !!!Conclusion: My favorite game in the series, from a long-time Monkey Island aficionado. 20/10.  But of course - it wouldn't be so good if it didn't have the foundation built by the first two games. (Psst - please add a borderless fullscreen mode, though! It's nearly 2023... seems really antiquated to not have that as an option!)
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: In brief: If you're a monkey island fan, you definitely want to play this game.I was thrilled to learn of a Monkey Island sequel, and everything about this game seemed really promising, except for the art style. Finished the game in 14 hours and this is very much a game worthy of the Monkey island legacy. The voice acting, featuring the original cast is top notch. The superb soundtrack by the original composers is on par with the fírst three MI games, and really makes the atmosphere and mood happen. I will probably go back to this game just to listen to the music, which uses the established motifs and instrumentations from past MI games, while having fresh arrangements and new themes in place as well. The game really shines on these two fronts.Writing is much in line with the first two games' silliness and the story has quite good pacing. Dialogue is well written and funny. I felt the game could have been a bit longer, but at 14 hours I can't really say it was short either.Puzzles are well done. Not too obvious, and you do get the occasional head-scratcher here and there. The middle part of the game is really where the game excels. Because of the multiple locations available you have many options to explore and if you get stuck at one place you can head to another.After finishing the game, I'm still not quite sold on the art style, even though it was functional and okay in the end. (I feel that the beauty and atmosphere of Curse of Monkey Island's art can't really be beat) Some of the characters just look a bit too simplified to my taste. This is pretty much my only gripe though!The game really does justice to the Monkey Island legacy on all fronts. Recommended for adventure game fans looking for a polished light hearted pirate adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Return to Monkey Island is a delightful game both for longtime fans of the franchise and new players alike. A lot of effort was taken to make improvements on the previous formula and control schemes to encourage convenience without taking away from the charm, exploration, or problem-solving of the originals. The humor, writing, and voice talent are all there, and the surprisingly few voice replacements do very well. There is no lack of witty dialogue. My favorite gag was I do have a few criticisms which I believe hold RtMI back a little, but I do not believe they take away from the enjoyability or nostalgia the game has to offer. Firstly: the art direction (not to be confused with the art STYLE). Like past MI games, the artwork takes a stylized approach only this time, it almost has a childrens storybook feel to it. The colors are beautiful and the environments especially are filled with life. The character designs look great, but I feel that they lack in expressiveness, which in my opinion, hinder visual gags. For example, past games, both originals and remakes have the hilarious bug-eyed expression on Guybrush's face. I feel that the characters' black beady eyes do not compliment Monkey Island's slapstick humor very well, but it could be easily worked around with a few more extreme facial expressions/eye illustrations used sparingly. Additionally, I felt that there was less visual humor entirely. eg. Guybrush's pants falling down in MI2. Comedic timing is there and it is brilliant as always, but more visual gags was just a personal wish of mine. Again, this certainly wasnt enough to ruin the game for me, and it didn't stop the game from feeling like a true Monkey Island game. My biggest praise for RtMI is  its VERY clever means of modernizing the point-and-click adventure formula to be user-friendly and convenient. Further, they provide really helpful tools and simple dialogue features to help players get on the right track whereas with older adventure games, you were pretty much thrown to the wind. My favorite feature is if it's been a day or two since you've used a save, youre provided with a very natural narration offering you a reminder as to what you were working on previously. Very lovely game with a lot of heart. Very welcoming to new players or players who need some reminding. Fun challenges for long time players.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting art style, and somewhat nice scenery. The game mechanics and dialogue engine work great. It's actually quite strange how each subplot in RtMI starts out really interesting and intriguing only to be a complete let down, and this trend continues for the overall story arc. Don't waste your time with this game unless you want your impression of the MI franchise to be washed away.Curse of Monkey Island is definitely still the best MI game. Hands down.
