_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to review.Thinking back on all the wonderful elements of M1&2- the story, the amazing team with a shared vision and sense of humor - of writers, super talented artists and musicians, programmers, etc., to masterful technological maneuvering for the time (SCUMM engine, solutions for limited file size capacities, transitional environment midi scoring, color cycling, etc.) to LucasArts and Skywalker Ranch… Return pays tribute to all of this- it's entertaining, satisfies an itch, might even make you tear up a bit, but it does so in a way that’s sappy, heavily capitalizing on nostalgia and fandom to create a homage to the series within the series. While you can feel the decades of lore and love backing it, Return ultimately gives the feeling of a rushed production with good intentions, attempting to appeal to a broader audience at the expense of some of the series' integrity and true magic. Real fans of Monkey Island don’t need to be spoon fed with in-game Trivia cards to unlock Steam Achievements, and constant reminders of running gags and characters- even if the ultimate message of the game is heavily meta driven. M1&2 were real works of art. Purcell, Ferrari, and the original team really put so much love and detail into each scene, and were absolutely crucial to the games collaborative development and sense of humor. With Return, we enter a lackluster world that feels like a cheap Flash game- overly cutesy, flat Shag inspired art that lacks any refinement and feels factory-cut, executed as a graphic gig rather than with any of the passion or artistic vision we saw in M1&2. Attention to detail -  - was what made the first two games so masterful, and what is completely lacking in Return. Everything is there for you, bright, ugly, overly defined cartoon characters, leaving no space for fantasy. The entire production felt watered down, puzzles included. I never looked at hints, and finished it faster than I have any other MI game, without feeling stumped for very long at any point. I was confused by how uninspired and easy to string together the puzzles were for the most part. Getting rid of the original SCUMM UI and replacing it with an item bag wasn’t satisfying either, and the red icon that pops up over items when attempting to make an incorrect combination made everything feel too easy.If you grew up with these games, it’s hard to completely dismiss Return and Ron’s sweet sentiment- it feel like a warm blanket somehow, especially with Land, McConnell, and Bajakian's wonderful music (aside from the awful electric guitar bit in the SCUMM bar). But one can’t help but feel it’s a bit of a cheap send off, when it could have been a masterful third installment.I wish this was the light Disney version. I wish the original team could have just continued where 2 left off, and we’d have another classic. But I guess that’s part of what Ron is saying with this game. It’s a different time, it’s about the journey, and it’s been a fun one. I can appreciate that, and all criticism aside, I did enjoy playing, I just can’t help but feel let down. I am proud to say I play M1&2. They are masterpieces. I’m not proud to say I play Return, though I will likely continue to explore it out of curiosity from time to time in…secrecy.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game but was totally miserable about the ending.Beautifully animated, great voice acting, very funny.  Totally captures the atmosphere of the original games and improves on the GUI in many ways......At least that's how I'd describe the first 99% of the game.  The ending is a very hard slap in the face for all loyal fans of this franchise.  The game builds you up to expecting something wonderful as the payoff but you just get fobbed off with a cop-out ending that ruins EVERYTHING that came before it.If you've already bought this and don't want to be disappointed, then play up to the point where you're at the large "wheel" puzzle at the end.  Then simply stop playing the game, and remember the fun you've had up to that point.  That's about the best ending this game has to offer.The game devs should make a proper ending to this game and give everyone a free update.  A disgrace.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: So, I don;t like the graphics. I particularly dislike the artwork for  Guybrush, Le Chuck and Carla.  I like the old-school, pixellated graphics, so it would be nice to see an update at some time which enables that option, much as they did when they remastered the original, and introduced the new artwork. Trivia cards could have been a bit more easily seen, especially as they have to be triggered to appear.But those my only complaints. Everything else I absolutely loved! Played it straight off in one sitting, and I couldn't have enjoyed it more.  Well done to the guys for such a fantastic new instalment.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A Point and click adventure that in a certain way "wraps up" the Monkey Island saga.The art style is very fitting and works very well in the game. The gameplay is what you would expect from a modern point and click game, with easy interactions, interactable object highlights and even a built-in hintbook in case you are stuck.For any Monkey Island fan, this is going to be an extremely fun adventure, filled with nostalgia, walks down memory lane and a lot of laughs. From this point of view, the game certainly does not disappoint.If you are not a Monkey Island fan and this is the first Monkey Island game you play, there is a section of the menu that recaps very quickly the story so far, but I think the overall experience is going to be filled with references you might miss.The ending is something that I think fans will debate for years to come so be prepared for something you will like or not like in a fairly polarizing way.8/10 would have waited 20 years again
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I played 1, 2, and 3, with 3 being my favorite (couldn't finish 4 because I didn't like the controls and movement).I will say that if you are a fan of the series as a whole, give it a go. I didn't find the puzzles as hard as the earlier games but that's alright. Art style was nice, music instantly took me back to the classics, and the wit and humor were there. There is some replay-ability too with all the achievements there are to earn.  While it definitely had that monkey island feel, just wasn't my favorite of the series. I didn't mind the ending, its not bad, and it is explained a bit in the a letter from the devs after completion. But like I said, if you liked the other games, I'd recommend this one, but if you were already a fan of those, I doubt you need my recommendation. Now, if only I could get a curse of monkey island remastered version. Thats what I am really waiting for
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant about this game the first few hours I started playing it but it just got better and better. I think my hesitancy was from the many criticisms of the ending but I have to say that those people who didn't like the ending just didn't get it. They explain it in the final letter in the scrapbook and it couldn't have been any other way. Ron Gilbert made a funny and thoughtful game that had just as much heart or even moreso than the first game. When you're young, life is like an amusement park and everything is magical. When you're an adult and you've experienced a lot of hardships in your life, the magic is still there but sometimes it's hard to find and maybe it's not quite what you dreamed of when you were younger. Things are just different now and places I visited as a child don't feel the same, just like Melee wasn't the same place when he came back to it. The point is that the journey of this game was the magic I was hoping for and it brought me back to the magic I had playing the first game when I was 9 years old.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: So many loose ends. Ending did not feel like an ending (felt more as if they ran out of time/money and just gave up on it). Nothing really stood out or shone in terms of story, gameplay, art style, etc.Most of the game wasn't horrible but not great. The ending definitely pushed it into the negative, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly well designed and thoughtful adventure game. I was initially hesitant on the choice of art design as I really liked the aesthetic of Ron's previous title, Thimbleweed Park. That being said; this style grows on you as you play and having a new experience within the confines of Monkey Island was a really satisfying experience. I'm not nearly as concerned with canon as I think some players were and honestly what matters more to me is "Did they get the characters right?". Monkey Island was never a franchise that was driven by epic story but rather the characters and humor found within it. The game got me to laugh and got me through a nasty virus. They knocked it out of the park and I would love to see more from this team.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fantastic. I hope there will be another part anytime soon. The graphics, the jokes and the story were great. I have just a few little remarks. I missed the "pick up, pull, push etc. section". The puzzles were fairly easy, I little more like Thimbleweed Park would be better. But I understand this game had to be for everyone, so I'm very happy it came out at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Return to Monkey Island is a quality, modern point 'n' click adventure that should appeal to fans of the Monkey Island franchise and newcomers alike. An intuitive, easy-to-use interface, an easy difficulty setting and an in-game hints system will be welcome to those unfamiliar with point 'n' click adventures and everyone can appreciate the crisp visuals, professional voice acting, beautiful soundtrack and funny humour.The ending is the only thing I had mixed feelings about. It doesn't detract from the fun I had playing the actual game but I did feel it could've been wrapped up better (just don't ask me how).
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Not much of a game.All the funny things are missing, like the sour and funny comments of the characters when you try to give them the wrong items or when you perform the wrong actions.The puzzles are easy, even in the difficult version.The ending is outrageous...i was hoping for an adventure at least as good as monkey island 3 (or Deepoina); but i was disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I played through to the ending.Right off the bat things seemed abit disjointed with events not strictly fitting the time line. I thought it might be foreshadowing for a big plot twist that took into account the ending of MI2, the beginning seemed to heavily hint at that. I was expecting something incredibly clever and satisfying because the scrapbook seemed so well thought out. Other than that it played like a decent Monkey Islands game... until the ending.I won't spoil it for you, all I'm going to do is say this. If you have any positive memories of this franchise, if you can even half accept the ending of Tales of Monkey Island as being the end then do so. You'll still be able to think of Guybrush Threepwood as a mighty pirate going on swashbuckling adventures.Monkey Islands was the first game I ever played and since I was... I want to say eight, thats the image I had in my mind. This game will snatch that from you and leave in its place a vanity project. Because if theres one thing writers love to do its to get meta, it reminds you they exist at the expense of the story. It makes them larger than the characters. I regret playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Great to be immersed into the Monkey Island world again.  Can remember as a pre-teen the struggles to solve the puzzles and complete these adventures (Monkey 1 & 2).  Have played through the whole MI series and this one felt a little easy in comparison, but maybe I am a lot wiser now as a 40 year old.  Still great to play through, but can't help feeling I should have been stuck for a couple of weeks at least, trying to solve some of the puzzles.  In a way, a good thing for new (young) adventurers so I am not being too critical.  Do miss the insult sword-fighting though.  7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing old school Point & Click adventure!Fun & colorful graphics and animations, great riddles, amazing characters and story.The music is one of the best in the history of video games. The voice acting is perfect.This game is all about heart and good time. It took me about 13 hours to finish it. Worth every dollar.So, if you love point & click adventures, or have kids you want to play with them a great funny game - this is the one for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I love love love a new misadventure of Guywood! Yes, some of us are not fan of new art style- but please look pass the art! Story, humor, and puzzles are still great and funny- there's no shame to look the Book of Hints. Anyway, we will find a REAL Secret of Monkey Island(tm) and meet both new and old friends and rivals!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. Read all the flack the game received prior to launch over the art direction and it really highlights how toxic gamers and the Internet can be. Makes you wonder why half of these people play games if all it does is continuously disappoint them. Not to say you can’t critique a game, but often a line gets crossed. Overall, I thought the game was fun and great to see a return to this series. I have always loved the Monkey Island games and I thought this was a solid addition.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: For longtime Monkey Island fans, this is a must buy. As a game, it is funny, witty, clever, and fun to play, but IMO does not belong in the upper echelons of the MI games. I'd slot it solidly in the middle: below Secret, Monkey 2, and Curse, but well above Escape and Tales. The true value comes in the nostalgia of seeing old locations on Melee and Monkey Islands, familiar characters (mainly from the first 2 games), familiar voice actors (other than Stan and LeChuck), and FINALLY getting a 3rd MI game from Ron and team after 30 years. The one they wanted to make. If you're new to the series, they do summarize events of the past games for you so you're not completely clueless (but a lot of jokes and references will go over your head). If you're on the fence, buy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Return to Monkey Island is a fantastic blending of nostalgia and fresh ideas, moving forward while celebrating the past. The jokes are laugh out loud funny, the puzzles interesting without being too far fetched, and both the voice acting and soundtrack are absolutely on point. The visual style is one of the biggest changes, but in motion in the game is far more dynamic and engaging than it might appear in screenshots.If you're a fan of the franchise, you've probably already bought this. If you've not played the games before, and are interested, Return to Monkey Island works incredibly well as a gateway to the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: It's OK, can't really rate it above that. The game is fun in places, but the game play starts off very easy and linear and doesn't really ramp up until the middle of the game before dropping back down again towards the end. The art style is terrible and feels cheap, it's the worst looking game in the series and it is too short and easy, especially for the price. The ending was also a massive letdown. The writing and puzzles are a step up from the talltale series but it mostly plays on the nostalgia factor; it just doesn't feel like a well rounded, fun and complete Monkey Island game when you look at the others in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up on this series and I've got a lot of fond memories with it. From learning insult sword fighting with aunts and uncles, to me and my cousins working our way through Curse with only our own wits and persistence to guide us. So despite not gelling with the new art style when it was revealed I was looking forward to exploring a new adventure with Guybrush and seeing where the story went.You're probably on this store page because you like puzzles, and you can see the big Not Recommended above, so what went wrong?Setting out its stall both in game and from Ron Gilbert himself as the story to finally answer the question  'What is the Secret of Monkey Island?' and unfortunately after so many years, decades even, its a near impossible expectation to live to and resolve in a satisfying way and the game even acknowledges this. It turns out the correct answer is the LucasArts point and click adventure game from 1990 (and Special Edition from 2009). Not only is it a more satisfying story, the humour feels fresher there and isn't reliant overly on nostalgia.The game feels like it doesn't quite know what it wants to do. It wants to hit so many nostalgic points such as familiar characters, Mêlée island and all its locations, insult sword fighting, etc but it also doesn't give enough time or focus on those characters over new ones, Mêlée feels like a shell of itself and then most of the game is spent in new locations, you don't really feel like you got some satisfying insult sword fighting in. The new locations lack memorable characters, or much to explore with one island in particular just feeling like a load of atmospheric empty clearings instead of giving an interesting fluid walk to the important place, or integrating it into somewhere else and having it feel like a sinister part of somewhere bigger. The puzzles are fine for the most part, and the in-game hint book does a serviceable job of feeding progressive hints to keep things moving without having to look up guides. Late in the game where puzzles that span multiple islands appear though puzzles start to feel like they were padding out the game and overstaying their welcome by a journey or two. There's also an issue of some puzzles are interesting and unique, while others are essentially repeated over and over.TL;DR – Return to Monkey Island can't pick a wind to sail in. It wants to hit nostalgia frequently but can't decide between going all in or breaking out into something new. It cuts between taking you to iconic places but also focuses on new, broadly empty locations. It unsteadily walks a plank of balancing unique puzzles with overuse of the same puzzles. Ultimately it feels like it never really wanted to  and was content to stay in its own footsteps.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect send-off for the Monkey Island™ series of games. Great for long time fans, and especially for nostalgic parents to introduce their kids to the series.It returns to the point and click of its roots, with friendly faces, familiar faces, references, and gags galore.Easily leagues better than the last 2 installments of the now 6 game franchise, and ends with enough nostalgia to consider it on par with the remaster of the original. It's much larger game to explore, has a longer story, and feels like it has more puzzles and optional things to do compared with previous games.It is easier than most of the games before it though, with multiple optional ways to reduce difficulty as well. There is an in-game hint book that will straight up tell you what to do next if you're lost (after enough prompting), a button you can press to locate all interact-able items on screen, and a dedicated "Easy" mode option. My only real complaints are related to there being almost too many puzzles and items and locations. You can feel lost quite easily, and using hints becomes almost necessary for you to actually figure out where you need to go. Perhaps because of there being so many puzzles and requiring so many items, the game only lets you "use" an item on things that are related to the puzzle they are needed for, which might be a bit of a bummer to hardcore fans who try pretty much every silly combination of objects to see if Guybrush has anything funny to say about them. (No more attempting to use a rubber chicken with a pulley in the middle on every new thing)
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Love the new art style and the game engine. It feels like the most logical and thought through progression from the pixel era. And the game… beautiful written, it has all this Ron Gilbert charateristics that made the two first games great. I’m amazed by all the imagination and wittiness going into the plot and dialouge. A must play if you love the earlier games, point and click in general and appreciate humour at a the same level as the best cartoon sitcoms.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Did you enjoy  and its sequels? You'll probably enjoy this one, too. Same goofy humor. Same obscure puzzles. Just with some modern polish and a very, very heavy dollop of nostalgia. But ... is it necessary to play this? Is it necessary for this game to even exist?You see, the game does exactly what it says on the tin: takes you back. But here's the thing: the original  still exists. You can go play it right now, and that's the elephant in the room that keeps swishing at you awkwardly with its trunk while you play  game, prompting the question: What is the point of it? In  you revisit many of the same locales and meet many of the same characters. The graphics are updated, but the music is pretty much identical. And, yes, of course there is a new story and new puzzles. But, really, why do this? Why not create a new adventure with new characters in new places? Were there any loose ends that needed tying up from twenty years ago?It turns out that there were none.I didn't dislike it. But I would have been perfectly satisfied without it. Possibly even more satisfied, because I'm a bit annoyed at how hard it tries to make me feel something that I'm already perfectly good at feeling. I can't in good conscience give it a thumbs down because it's not a bad game, but I'm here to tell you that even if you're a fan of the series, like me, skipping  is totally fine.I do have to dish out one complaint: the achievements are horrible. Many of them involve mindless repetition, are fragile, and are generally very not fun. Why would you put a feature in your game that is not fun? Do you not understand the point of games? Hugely bad design here.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: A tired feeling damp squib with the kind of dragging resignation endemic to once-great creators who have come off the boil, and seek to drag the adoration of their fans through the mire with them. An exhausted sigh of a game that doesn't care about what you loved about its predecessors, and thinks you're an idiot for having done so.A crushingly depressing waste of money.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Even though the ending ruined my childhood (sort of), playing this brought back a huge part of the joy I experienced as a kid when playing with the predecessors. I thought at first that the new artwork wasn't really suitable for a Monkey Island game, but after a couple of hours you get used to it, and it helps a lot that most of the main characters have the same voices as in the prequels. I played the hard version and at times the puzzles felt over-complicated (like when you know what you will have to do with something later on, but the algorithm would not let you do anything until you had that particular piece of conversation beforehand) - or when one has to travel around a lot for the same reason - to make the puzzles more "difficult", but overall it was quite a nostalgic time I spent with the game, and I am glad I could. Monkey Island is one of the best games there ever was, and even though the latest ones were not really up to the first ones, this one still gives me a warm, fuzzy feeling to be able to go back to that world I spent a great time at as a kid. DESPITE the ending.We sort of got what we wanted, but it wasn't what we expected...
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: There are no words for everything I would like to say.Monkey Island was my childhood and this felt like coming home after so many years of longing.It's beautifully crafted, the story that just had to be, even though we didn't exactly know what was missing.Thank you Ron and Dave (and Dominic for the world's best voice acting). Thank you to the whole team. Hope we'll get to go with you on your next adventures :)
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Never pay more than twenty dollars for a computer game.After finishing the game, you receive a letter from Ron Gilbert admitting this project was the result of his middle-aged ennui. Even if this confession hadn't been included, it's present all throughout the game. There is an overarching obsession with with reminding you about Monkey 1 at every corner, but only as a memory that has lost its luster, not as the ground of a new and interesting story. The game engages in nostalgia-baiting as it tells you nostalgia is wrong and you can't relive your glory days. The characters never develop or deepen their relationships, in a sort of rebuke to the melodramatic turn taken in some of the sequels. The art design is okay and executed well, except for the characters, who are ugly. Ugliest is Guybrush, with his red alcoholic's nose that extends up to his eyebrows. This is very unfortunate, as he's on screen most of the time. The plot is pure shaggy dog. Not "surprising but compelling" like Monkey 2, it just gives up and tells you the game is over. The music is nice, though.I'd rank this below the first three Monkey games. I have to replay Escape and Tales, but it may well be below them, too. Buy on sale and manage your expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I don't like the art style, I think they should have gone with the art style of the remastered versions of 1 and 2 if they insisted on making it a point and click adventure rather than a 3D one like "Tales". But it is a terrific Monkey Island game with a good story, some good jokes, fun puzzles, and a heap of nostalgia for all of us 90's kids. So yeah, if you are a Monkey Island / Lucas Arts/ Sierra/ point and click adventure fan - this game is definitely for you! My only real complaint is that while they do treat it as a sequel, they ignore the way we defeated Lechuck in the previous game and the after credits scene where we saw him trapped in a jar by the voodoo lady. Would have been nice to use that as a jumping board into this story.Edit: (SPOILERS)I hate the ending, even with the note from the developers. Basically it's the same ending they had for Monkey 2. Which is no ending. No secret. I mean, even a joke secret (like the shirt bit) was better than that. Sorry, you created a terrific series and characters that were a part of my childhood (and adult life apparently), but 3 and Tales were better written.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: So much feelings, this game was all about giving the perfect ending to an amazing chronicle that was Monkey Island. Like all good things, we never want it to end... But it always comes the time when it does, thank you so much for the amazing team that put together this game to give us this final chapter. I loved it and I highly recommend it to everyone who played the previous ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great look back at the world of Guybrush and the Monkey Island cinematic universe. Its a solid sequel to the original two games and the new style works really well. The puzzles are ok but if you've played the originals then start on hard mode or i doubt you'll get much of the challenge. Well worth a buy if you love the series or point and click in general. Makes you feel old though by the end - thanks for the games guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Great entry into the series, if you've been waiting all this time for the next Monkey Island, this is pretty much everything you'd hope it would be. Good blend of original characters and locations and nostalgic reappearances from the other games, with pretty much every single one of them being called out or referenced in some way as you go along. Also: Go into settings and turn on the 'Writer's Cut', it adds more dialogue and even certain characters that were cut from the normal version!
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: The Secret of Monkey Island is the first videogame I ever played (and finished). Since then, I've enjoyed all of the entries in the series to varying degrees. Return to Monkey Island surpasses the past few entries and stands comfortably besides the original three as a classic in the adventure game genre. The puzzles are well designed (I got briefly stuck several times, although I always managed to figure out the solution without resorting to the in-game hintbook), the new art style grew on me considerably, the dialogue is as sharp as ever, and the story has a nostalgic and melancholy edge to it that I wasn't expecting. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

_childDocuments_.review: Announcing Return to Monkey Island, the long-awaited follow-up to the legendary Secret of Monkey Island and Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge by Ron Gilbert's Terrible Toybox in collaboration with Devolver Digital and Lucasfilm Games, coming 2022.
_childDocuments_.name: Return to Monkey Island

name: Wilmot Works It Out
detailed_description: Wilmot Works It Out is a puzzle building game about completing beautiful images and hanging them in your house. You play as Wilmot, who likes to unwind from sorting out a warehouse by sorting out puzzle pieces. Yesterday’s puzzle was a snake wearing a hat, but today’s looks like it might be an octopus?  …or maybe that’s a hamburger? Once complete, you decide where to hang it. Then the mail person delivers a brand new puzzle! Oh dear, this one has a few extra pieces - I hope there wasn’t a mix-up at the puzzle delivery service! Complete a series of puzzles to unlock new customisation options for your house, including colours, wallpapers, bookcases, and cats. This house is going to feel like a home in no time at all! Features Assemble more than 60 original puzzles by Richard Hogg ( Hohokum, Flock ) Unlock 7 additional rooms in Wilmot's house Decorate each room to your liking with 20+ additional unlockable items Adopt a cat or a dog Sequel to beloved organization game Wilmot’s Warehouse Enjoy hours of extra organizing fun, Wilmot's Warehouse-style, when you unlock Marathon Mode A gentle and slightly jazzy electronic soundtrack to listen to as you ponder and solve, brought to you by composer and sound artist Eli Rainsberry ( Wilmot's Warehouse, Flock )

_childDocuments_.review: yea, wilmot, my man, this time we'll work it out!!i honestly don't know what they put in these games. that's a second Wilmot game, it's about sorting out the space and solving puzzles, and it's super chill and relaxing, in the way that I can't stop playing. this game really does something to the autistic part of my brain. it's comforting in a way that it's comforting to rename folders on your computer, and to arrange books in order that makes sense only to you, and to show someone photos of birds on your phonethe loop is genius: you get a package with details, it has some pieces of the puzzle and maybe some from the other puzzle. you solve what you can, put it on a wall and get a new package. it has a new puzzle and some more details from the previous puzzle or maybe from the next one. so it really gets you going. i'm stopping just because it's 2am and i completed first two chapters of the gamei love the feeling of figuring out what i can solve, i love the feeling of things clicking together, and i love that while you play every 5 minutes you get the feeling that things make more sense than they did beforethe art is beautiful and fun, the soundtrack is just PERFECT and jazzy and gives the ~vibes~ and super comfortable for your head while playing. awesome tunes, i'll listen to them while working too!so yea, if you're looking for a chill lil game, check it out. it might not change your life, but it made my life better for sure. warm hugs to the team, you are the best!!
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play the other Wilmot game, so from the perspective of a jigsaw fan...This game *gets* what makes jigsaw puzzles fun.  It’s about observing the finer details of a colorful image, and recognizing surprising patterns as they emerge.  The game achieves this through a tightly curated selection of puzzles, with similar textures from separate puzzles playfully mixed together.The puzzles are fairly small, making them fast-paced and lacking the contemplative quality of a larger puzzle.  But marathon mode mixes all of them together, so it becomes like one big puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Instead of taking place in the warehouse again, Wilmot Works It Out takes place in a home. Wilmot’s home to be exact. We got to see what he did for work and now we get to see what he does when he’s off of work. After a long day of work at the warehouse, Wilmot comes home to unwind and do some puzzles. Time seems to just pass by when he’s doing puzzles and he likes doing them so much he joined a subscription service called Puzzle Club. Puzzle Club sends boxes with puzzle pieces every week and Wilmot is locked in for the full eight season release. Plus, this does give him an excuse to talk to Postwoman Sam (who I like to think is his friend) every time he gets a Puzzle Club package. Sam strikes up some small talk every time Wilmot gets a package and sometimes, you’ll get the option to ask a question to get some more details if you want to.The game starts with you hearing a knock at the door and receive your first Puzzle Club package. Wilmot does all of his puzzles in his hallway so you’ll be unpacking them there. You can pick any spot you want, as long as there’s nothing obstructing the outline, and you get to see all the pieces that Wilmot received. If you played Wilmot’s Warehouse, even if it’s been years, you’ll already be quite familiar with the gameplay here. Wilmot can pick up any pieces that are around him, pick up multiple pieces if needed, carry them wherever you need them to be, and rotate them around you if you need to. You can also just push the pieces around. Each piece are squares like Wilmot, but instead of each square representing a warehouse item, they are just a part of a bigger picture. All you have to do is put them together to form the complete image just like a jigsaw puzzle. You also do get a subtle confirmation when you have pieces that fit together in the form of a flash and a confirmation ding sound. Which is helpful considering these are purely squares without the tabs and blanks. It’s also pretty helpful that Wilmot, by default, picks up clicked together pieces as a group.It seems easy, but it does bring in a surprising challenge. It comes from various aspects and the difficulty of the puzzles do increase as you progress. Each puzzle do vary in how many pieces there are, some are four while some have a lot of pieces. Some have a simple image while some are more complicated. You’ll get various themes and it is easy to tell if pieces do belong in the same image, but there are some tricky ones. There were two instances where I thought a group of pieces belonged to the same image, but came to realize they didn’t. Or I thought they belonged to different images, but they were from the same image. You’ll find yourself analyzing all the pieces longer than you think; or putting two pieces together hoping they’ll fit together as sometimes the shared part of the artwork can be subtle. It also doesn’t help that a package won’t just have pieces to one puzzle, but will have pieces for a future puzzle that you’ll get the rest of soon. You are guaranteed to be able to complete one puzzle per package, with it tripping you up with being able to complete two once in a while, before Sam comes with the next package. Luckily, all the pieces are always in their correct orientation so that’s one less thing to worry about.But oh man, does it bring in so many different satisfying moments. Like when it just clicks and you put all the pieces together in a row like a pro, finally being able to see the full picture after struggling, and when you finally find the piece that clicks to another.Once you finish a season, excluding the last one, there are a few things that happen. You get a nice screen where you get a view of all the framed puzzles on the wall, how many puzzles you solved, and how long it took you. You’ll also be able to unlock a room, giving you a choice between two options. There are eight rooms in Wilmot’s house, including the hallway, and you’ll unlock seven as you progress. Don’t worry, this only dictates their position as you won’t miss out on a room. Once you pick, you’ll be able to choose the wallpaper pattern, the color of the room, and if you want to put all the puzzles you just completed in there. That’s not all, though. You can also add accessories to decorate the room, like plants or a bookshelf. As you unlock more and more rooms, you’ll also unlock more room customization options. While you only get a limited list when you first unlock the room, you’ll be able to pick from the whole list when you go to edit the room afterwards, more accessories are added, and you can rearrange the framed puzzles on the wall and between rooms. I didn’t realize this until the last season, but you can also change the frame style of a framed puzzle and tilt them. Wilmot even adopts a pet and you can pick who you want.Don’t worry, you can rearrange and decorate these rooms at any time and you can stay in a save file for as long as you want.Once you put together all the puzzles through all eight seasons, and thus finish the game, you unlock another mode. This acts as the game’s New Game+ and is called Marathon Mode. I didn’t look at what this was beforehand, so I thought this was sort of a speedrun mode, but nope. This puts us in a more Wilmot Warehouse style of gameplay and the hallway room is much bigger. Instead of getting deliveries from Sam the Postwoman and being drip feed the puzzles, you get a slip where you can request deliveries at any time and packages will have randomized puzzle pieces. Yep, you’ll be tasked to complete all the puzzles together. Since all the pieces are in the draw pool, there’s no telling what you’ll get and you’re not guaranteed to have a complete puzzle in a package. Not to mention there’s no way to tell when you’ll get another piece for a specific image if you’re going to focus on completing one puzzle at a time rather than keeping track of multiple ones.This mode is definitely harder as it does require you to generally know what pieces belong to the same puzzle. I’m also sure it helps when you know what each completed puzzle looks like and how many pieces. This mode can also be pretty stressful and overwhelming. I know it was for me.I do have a few complaints that were just minor inconveniences. I found the knocking to blend into the music, enough tow here you can miss it. Granted, I was always ready at the door after completing a puzzle so I didn’t have any trouble. Either way, there’s no penalty to missing a delivery as a slip will be pushed through allowing you to schedule a re-delivery. Which spawns Sam immediately. Other than that, it can be a pain decorating or redecorating the rooms. It can be a pain trying to select what painting or decoration you want to move or remove (and it’s especially so when you want to do it for more than one item and the selection or position resets).I really enjoyed Wilmot Works It Out. Every element works together well in making a chill and relaxing experience, even with some difficulty sprinkled in. It was also great to see Wilmot again and learning more about him when Sam comes to deliver his Puzzle Club packages. The music is relaxing and makes for a good “doing jigsaws at home” vibe, the gameplay was simple and satisfying, the game did well balancing the puzzle difficulty, it was great talking to Sam the Postwoman and learning what’s happening around Wilmot, I liked the inclusion of being able decorating Wilmot’s house, and the art was cute, charming, and every piece was unique. It was a great idea to make a Wilmot puzzle game and I definitely recommend it for anyone that likes doing jigsaw puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: You construct (small) jigsaws from a bunch of similar looking paintings at one time, with a delivery of 16-25 new pieces delivered every time you solve a puzzle. Its simple and fun, and the characters have a lot of heart and charm. (yes, there is a plot. its cute and charming, but not particularly grandiose.)There is no timeframe or timelimit like there is in its predecessor.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: this is a very simple game. unlike Wilmot's Warehouse, there really is no progression or upgrades, just a seemingly never-ending supply of jigsaw puzzles that need solving. as long as you're not looking for something challenging or "thinky", there's a lot to love here and a wonderful soundtrack to vibe out to :)
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable, and all of the artwork is beautiful. I really wish I could decorate my real home with a lot of them! If you like jigsaw puzzles, you will like this game. I think I was expecting other mechanics to be introduced as you play, but once I realized that wasn't going to happen I was still content with what they game is. I would recommend only playing a season or two in a sitting, otherwise you'll blow through them pretty fast. Great job Finji!
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Wilmot's Warehouse, but you're making slide puzzles.If you liked sorting in that game, you'll like this. There is no time limit/management, so if that was the aspect of WW you liked, you might not like this one.If you haven't played the first game and you're just a fan of puzzle games in general, you'll probably enjoy this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: A much more lax version of the addicting gameplay to Wilmot's warehouse. Very simple, but just the perfect amount of puzzling puzzles you'd want out of a jigsaw game! I will say this is drastically different from warehouse of course. And if you were expecting anything like that (you should really play the demo before you buy, thats the point!) but you will be dissapointed. But if you love wilmot and love puzzles this will be no issue turning that organization brain off and getting into the puzzle groove
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Plays great on my Steam Deck!A fun, relaxing game that feels just like doing jigsaw puzzles. Getting pieces for multiple puzzles in a delivery makes it fun to sort them out, and adds some guess work when putting the puzzles together. The way the cut up the pictures for their puzzles are A+.The one thing I wish it had was multiplayer! (like Wilmot's Warehouse has). But my wife and I play together and we point out when we see pieces that match.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciated the design of Wilmot's Warehouse, but found the time limits and queues more stressful than I want in a puzzle game.  Wilmot Works It Out tweaks things to remove the stressors and lets you just relax with a bunch of puzzle pieces on the floor and arrange them into pictures.  Perfect cozy game, with a little background story and some surprises as you go.  Works great on the Steam Deck, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very fun puzzle game! It’s very easy to pick up and super difficult to put down. It’s so satisfying when the pieces start to click together and form the picture. My only gripe with the game is that I wish it was longer. I would gladly pay for a dlc in the future. Overall, if you’re a fan of games like A Little To The Left or any other organization games, you’ll love this as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly loading this up on my Steamdeck and gently solving puzzles in front of the TV is one of the most relaxing gameplay experiences I've had this year. I love the gameplay of Wilmot's Warehouse and this is all that joy with a lovely story but none of the stress of deadlines and clocks. Perfect autumnal vibes game and no spoilers but the last puzzle is a delight of playful genius which sums up the whole experience nicely.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Positively fantastic. I love jigsaw puzzles and I loved Wilmot's Warehouse so I was excited about this game. It's pretty, peaceful, and fun. I love that you don't know how large the puzzles are as you put them together. I can't wait to finish all the puzzles and I hope they add more! Thanks for this lovely game!! PS it works perfectly on Steam deck!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved Wilmot's Warehouse, so I knew this game was going to be what I enjoy, and it's even better than I expected.The story of Wilmot receiving puzzle boxes in the mail was very sweet, and it's nice he has work/life balance after working at the warehouse. I played through the main story pretty quickly, and got right into the newly unlocked Marathon Mode right away. It was delightful getting big batches of puzzle pieces and organizing them into groups like I do for the warehouse.I was thrilled to find there are pictures here in my marathon puzzles that I didn't have in the story mode. Replay value for sure, knowing I haven't seen it all. This game is pure joy and relaxation for me. I love Wilmot's games.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Played the tutorial so far, it's already a bit addicting ^^But I noticed several things, I play in German, with a QWERTZ keyboard (that's the normal german one), but Z and Y are always showing switched up in the UI. So when it says press Z you have to press Y and the other way around (after I tried re-binding the keys)Other language issue: althoug the game is (so far) correctly translated to German, the Umlaut "ö" is just replaced by the regular version, so instead of "schön" it's "schon" and so on.EDIT: Also "Küchenzimmer" should just be "Küche"Also it's a bit weird that to let go of a puzzle piece you press Ctrl, but when placing a picture you have to press Esc. (Feels inconsistent and it's one button more, when there is already a let go action/button)No dealbreakers, but would be nice if it was fixed, especially the mixed up Y-Z letters, because it shows incorrect in the UI and people could get frustated by it.All the customization options you unlock are also nice, some of the achievements are also like small puzzles and the marathon mode is quite the challenge too.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Wilmot's Warehouse, so I had high hopes for this one--and it didn't disappoint. The adorable graphics and cozy vibe are so great for a puzzle game. HOWEVER!!!!! It drives me crazy that finished images don't automatically align. Some of them, especially in the corners on the wall, leaves gaps, and there's no way to adjust it. It'd be great to have an option that lets players to choose whether pictures on the wall should stick together. Please consider about it it's a matter of life and death.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing, cute and just challenging enough to keep me playing. The postwoman's mundane anecdotes were fun. The formula doesn't really deepen, but there are a couple of small epiphanies that made me chuckle.It's not quite as clever as Wilmot's Warehouse where you basically had to create a sorting system in your head. The marathon mode that unlocks after the credits scratches some of that itch, but since I already beat most of these puzzles, usually the sorting abstraction doesn't go past "this piece was from this puzzle".Anyway I played 15 hours total in 2 days which I guess should be my review.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long time fan of Wilmot's Warehouse. I played 45 hours of it on the Switch and I played 12ish hours of it on Steam, bought the board game, streamed the game a ton over the pandemic, found a bug in 2-player mode with a friend where you can make blocks disappear (I have time lapse and video footage proof if you don't believe me), and the devs sent me a sweet pin that you can't find anywhere online.The whole game is different. Before you look at me without having played both games and say "but they look the same?" let me explain. In the original game you are supposed to organize blocks with the same contents next to each other, you also are supposed to remember where you place all these blocks and there's a timer to pressure you to act quick in organizing and serving customers. The story of the first game as well is how your boss doesn't treat you right even though you do more work than literally every other non-existent employee at the company and then in the end In this game, it's a more chill and relaxed experience. I literally got a key for the game yesterday and I casually completed it this morning, it took 4.6ish hours to complete. Every block is different, you get incomplete/complete puzzles in packages and you gotta put the pieces together to make photos. The mechanic for the puzzles pieces are nice, if you slide a block next to a block it's supposed to connect with then the blocks will automatically connect with each other. If you select a block and move it around other blocks and you have it in the right spot, it'll play an SFX to tell you that it's in the right spot in the puzzle and you can drop it to connect it with the other blocks. There is NO TIMER in this game so you don't have to be stressed about anything. Every time you complete a puzzle and/or finished connecting all the possible pieces you get in a shipment, Sam the mailwoman will come to your door and deliver another package. The final thing to wrap up this game review is your friend, Sam. I think this game wouldn't really have a point if there was no story, and Sam brings light to storytelling. After each shipment she gives you updates on her life, whatever is happening in your neighborhood, or news. When you go to complete puzzles you think about what she talked about, letting it sink in, and then when you get a new shipment you have something new to think about. I think there is a slight commentary in the story on how you only stay indoors to complete puzzles but there's a world to explore outside of your house, even if your house is super cozy to be in all the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Wilmot Works It Out is such a soothing and cosey game. You get sent a shipment box full of puzzle pieces and have to assemble them. Simple! However there's a catch - some of the pieces in the box don't fit together, and there's some puzzles that can only be completed after receiving assorted pieces from multiple different boxes.Essentially the game revolves around getting a box of mixed up puzzles pieces and finding out how to put them back together again. You're not just trying to solve a single puzzle, but also having to work out which puzzle the pieces actually belong to in the first place.There's no time pressure, and the puzzles are never 'too' difficult, so it's a very enjoyable and smooth experience from start to finish. Also if you want a real challenge, there's a new game + mode that is sure to keep you busy for many hours. I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes jigsaw puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: A thoroughly charming little game - I really wasn't expecting this after Wilmot's Warehouse, but it's a lovely direction for Wilmot. The amount of little aha moments where I realised "oh this piece goes in THIS puzzle" or "oh these two separate puzzles are actually the SAME puzzle" was really satisfying. I don't think I would have ever classed a jigsaw puzzle game as slice-of-life but the writing was genuinely charming, and without spoiling anything the final puzzle made me tear up a little :')
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: You may have played Wilmot's Warehouse and wondered, what happens when this obsessive little square goes home at night?  Well, now you know.  He endlessly builds puzzles and expands his home to hold all the puzzles he's building.  But wait ... do these puzzles tell the future?  They seem to.  And maybe that means Wilmot's organizational obsession isn't just madness.  Or maybe it is.  Maybe if you look deep enough you'll see where the proper things go in the proper places.  Does he get the girl?  Does he care to?  Or does he just want to keep playing puzzles all day?  Either way, it's fun to make puzzles and hang them on your wall... and wait... should we sort those paintings?  Hmmm...
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the gameplay of Wilmot's Warehouse but wanted something low stress, congratulations, they made a game just for you!I keep gasping as I realise that a puzzle piece is actually for a completely different puzzle, or that the two parts I've been assembling across the room from each other fit together, it's delightful.ALSO it works flawlessly on steam deck! It's a great way to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: the game starts extremely cozy, with fun and interesting puzzle designs. at first, i was bothered that the puzzles weren't traditional jigsaw shapes, but i got over that qualm pretty quickly.as you progress through the story, your inability (playing as Wilmot) to meaningfully answer the other characters in the game with any dialogue options other than "give me my puzzle" was mildly stressful - the characters have a decent level of development, and not being able to interact with them felt rudeand, for truly crazy people, the game mode unlocked after beating the game is a REAL challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a delightful puzzle game. It scratches the same itch that Wilmot's Warehouse scratched, but this one is much more suitable for a relaxed experience. I like the fact that there's still a bit of an organizational aspect when it comes to putting aside puzzle pieces for incomplete puzzles, but that I don't have to rush around to try to find the right piece. I'm definitely taking my time with it, because this isn't the type of game to rush through, but I find that when I start up the game it's very easy to keep playing and opening the door time after time for more puzzle packages.The small snippets of story you get with each delivery are nice too. I think even without the small chats at the door it would have been a nice game, but this adds a cute touch. I think it gives Wilmot some more depth, despite the fact that Wilmot doesn't ever speak. It's nice to get some Wilmot Cinematic Universe lore.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Wilmot Works It Out has been my favourite puzzle game of the year, which is a bit surprising as I don't consider myself a huge jigsaw puzzle fan. The art style is so charming and the atmosphere so chill I found myself obsessed with the gameloop. Despite Wilmot being largely silent in their interactions aside from a few lines, I found the friendship between them and Sam the postie so endearing and realistic.This game is just full to the brim with a cozy warmth, invited in to your friend Wilmots' home to assemble colourful puzzles that slowly fill the walls with art as time goes by. Also there's a dog, really what more can I ask for?Thank you Wilmot you're my favourite lil guy :)
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it as much or even more than the previous Wilmot game (Wilmot's Warehouse).This one is even cozier and more relaxing, while still super fun.The perfect game to play while listening to a podcast or watching your favorite streamer.PD: the game's "marathon" mode is the best! don't miss it after your first "standard" play.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure how I feel about this one. On the one hand maybe I should be disappointed in  because I really enjoyed the previous game, , and I can't help but feel this is a step or two down from . There really isn't much to say about this game, it's a series of jigsaw puzzles where the only design connection to the previous game is that you move the pieces around like you would move your inventory around.On the other hand, I don't know what I would have expected from a sequel to  really. More of the same wouldn't have been all that exciting either, and I will say that  still carries a similar amount of charm to it that the last game had. Is that enough of a reason for those who liked the original to check this out?You know what? Sure. I enjoy doing a jigsaw every now and then, so I had a good enough time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly cute game about sorting out puzzles. The pieces from different puzzles are made to look very similar to make it trickier, along with a cute bit of story every time you get a new box of pieces. It's a fun experience, but the base game is never too hard. The marathon mode is where this game really shines, giving you unlimited pieces from completely random puzzles. You have to sort hundreds of pieces throughout the room, slowly working through each puzzle. One corner will become your "Pieces with clouds section" while somewhere else you're putting any piece that has a hot dog or a burger. And don't get me started on the "I dunno" corner. It's a true extension of the Wilmot's Warehouse experience, but instead of having to remember where icons are, you have to go shopping for each piece you might need for the puzzle you're trying to solve. As someone who loves puzzle games this game made my brain work in a way no game has before, and I cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy a nice afternoon with puzzles, good music, and the company of a funny cube guy then you're in luck! Wimot Works It Out is a calming jigsaw-solving puzzle game that lets you solve charming jigsaws, decorate your expanding house and enjoy the company of a lovely postwoman named Sam. (There's even a dog/cat depending on which one you choose!) When you're finished you end up with a wonderfully decorated house filled with beautiful images and all sorts of knick-knacks and a load of plants. There's also some plot thread about a moon landing... wonder what's up with that?
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game. I love puzzles in real life and was looking for something to play while chilling with an audiobook or podcast. Wilmot is such a cute little square and I love decorating his little home with all the different puzzles I finished. The art style is so comforting too. I have played both PC and Steam Deck and I much prefer PC , keyboard and mouse. Calming gameplay to wind down with and amazing art to put together.I love Wilmot and will be watching to see if he makes more appearances in different games in the future and will be checking out his other warehouse game because of this title.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, it is just so chill and relaxing. I've worked through the main game and am now embarking on the level where it seems to just throw all the levels at you at once. This is genuinely one of the most relaxing and enjoyable puzzle games I have ever played. I just hope there will be some DLC in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much. I swear it's been a long time since I've been that engrossed in a game and can't stop playing it. It's so addicting and really hooks you in. 'I'm sleepy but just 1 more puzzle. Juuust 1 more. OH, the post lady's here with a new package with more puzzle pieces. Ok ok just 1 more and that's it'. This is what I look for in a game. Immersion. It's just puzzles and putting pieces together to make a portrait but manages to be exciting, fun and wholesome.There's 8 chapters and as you progress through the game you unlock 7 different rooms in the house. You can decorate your rooms like wallpaper type, colours and add small furniture pieces and accessories. You can move pictures around each room if you want to categorise each room with different kinds of pictures. There's achievements for this as well. After you finish the main game, you unlock a challenge mode too. Overall this is a 9/10 solid game and genuinely recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: A very cozy experience! The controls are oddly complicated and it feels like there are actions bound on unique keys that feel like they could've been combined with other bindings, but this didn't prevent enjoying the game too much. The art is delightful and the little story is very enjoyable; do check this out if you'd like to relax with some jigsaw solving!
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Really neat puzzle game. The controls take some getting used to compared to other games where you can move the pieces more freely and moving completed puzzles around the house feels a bit clunky.Love that there are "traps" where you get pieces at the same time for 2 different puzzles but with the same color schemes or seemingly the same elements, and that you get leftover pieces you don't know what they belong to yet and have to organize them.Haven't played Marathon mode yet, getting all the puzzles like that at once feels a bit overwhelming after the rhythm of the main game.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Richard Hogg did an incredible job of designing artwork for the puzzles. Each puzzle piece feels like candy for your eyeballs. The task is challenging enough to keep my mind tingly, but it never pushes me in0to the stress zone. Love the idea to have "rounds" of puzzle solving broken up by decorating a room with your creations. 10/10, would look at a cowboy snake playing a banjo again.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Wilmot works it out is an amazing second entry in the Wilmot series!Its definitely less stressful than the last Wilmot game, and it has so much personality! I loved seeing the story unfold in the background, and I found myself wanting to draw out the playing experience as long as possible. Currently playing in the remixed mode and I really can't get enough of out boxy guy :D
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: There’s something fun about scattering a jigsaw puzzle all over the floor and putting it together, but because it's a game, it doesn’t make the house messy. Once the puzzle is completed, it needs to be stored somewhere, but again, because it's a game, it doesn’t take up space in the house. All of these desires are perfectly fulfilled. And the feeling of collecting each colorful illustration one by one is incredibly satisfying.In just three days, Wilmot Works It Out became one of my all-time favorite puzzle games. I keep playing it, and I want to keep playing it. It's endlessly fun. This is the game of the year for me.Thank you, Wilmot, and thank you, Sam!
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Wilmot Works It Out has a simple concept where you receive puzzle pieces each day and you have to complete the puzzle. However, it can be challenging to figure out where the pieces go and you can also receive extra pieces that are used for puzzles on another day. If you do like puzzle games, I do recommend checking out Wilmot Works It Out.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Wilmot Works It Out is more parts casual cozy game, than puzzle game. (But that's not a bad thing, just keep expectations in check)I will shout out the NG+ / Marathon Mode for providing some challenge, but you must complete the short campaign before unlocking it. There isn't much story, but the one sided dialogue between the mailwoman and Wilmot is cute.This game plays great on steam deck and is enjoyable both in short bursts, and looking at the clock and realizing hours have melted away.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: With Wilmot’s Warehouse, Wilmot Works It Out, and the recently released board game, I’m all in for this adorable cube and its expanding universe. Wilmot Works It Out brings vibrant, colorful puzzles to life with a clean, intuitive design. Its jazzy, relaxing soundtrack creates a pleasant, seamless experience from start to finish. It’s a must-play and has officially become one of my favorite games of 2024. Hollow Ponds has done it again this year with Flock released this past summer and Wilmot Works It Out. Both are fantastic games.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE PUZZLES! Really cute game with some fun jigsaws and lovely art. It controls so well and is just generally a great chill zone out game. Put on a podcast and enjoy!Was genuinely invested with the relationship with Sam. However absolutely devastated I could not pet the dog. Now I need more puzzles! Please make a DLC with more art please pleaseNote - I had a couple of crashes on the steam deck but otherwise played well
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Delivery lady keeps getting between me and my puzzles with her friendly chatter. Shut up and give me the puzzles, Sam. I'm a busy little square, I don't have time for things like "establishing a sense of place", "character development", or "personal connections"Life isn't about that kind of shiz. It's about puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly when I first heard about this game I was quite apprehensive, as I'm not much of a jigsaw puzzle fan. But I really liked Wilmot's Warehouse so I was like why not give this one a try? I trust the developers to deliver a cute and chill experience :DAnd it delivers, the puzzles are really pretty and small enough that putting them together isn't a chore, but rather a satisfying process where you can bring stories to life while just matching patterns. The surrounding atmosphere is also great, I love how you gradually get pieces of story over time, really makes you value taking your time to enjoy the moment, relaxing to the soothing music and sound effects. I finished my first playthrough today and just started the marathon mode, which will prove to be quite challenging but surely as satisfying, as the puzzles will come together piece by piece.Anyway, thanks for bringing us such a great game!! I'll be sure to check out Wilmot's future experiences :D

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly fantastic game. Beautiful in its simplicity. A satisfying control system used to build satisfying (and at times deliberately confusing (in a fun way)) puzzles, with a cute little story weaved in for good measure.I especially loved how the only character you interact with seemingly got confused by the same puzzles that you did and in the same way. Genius.In short - Beautiful soundtrack, art style, control system and story.I'd easily pay for every DLC/Expansion/Sequel this game ever gets.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Adore this game. I already loved Wilmot’s Warehouse, and this is the perfect companion piece. The lovely art style, phenomenal Eli Rainsberry OST, the goofy art, and the subtle design choices that went into pacing the puzzles out just right over the course of the game… and the marathon mode is just the cherry on top! Is it too far to say this is the perfect puzzle game?
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Fun 6 hours of gameplay! I loved the intentionally misleading pieces of puzzles! The gameplay was mostly cozy and relaxing. Putting puzzles on the walls and decorating rooms with them was however tedious, as you could only move finished puzzles to a different room if they fit on the wall of the current room? _childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute delight! Simple enough to hook you into the gameplay loop but with enough challenge where none of the puzzles feel trivial. Throughout the game I felt myself slipping into a flow state, feeling like an amateur speedrunner and relishing in the satisfaction of clicking the pieces together. Very cute and pretty lookin' game. Would recommend if you are looking to relax, zone out, and think about nothing except the task at hand.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: this game is very good! The way the puzzles are designed feels really unique. It's quite relaxing and I would recommend it for sureEDITAfter playing and 100%ing this game, I think it's one of my favourites of all time. The puzzles feel intelligently designed, and nothing was ever too difficult or too easy. Overall a relaxing experience, and I genuinely hope the developer makes more unique games like this <3
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: This game delivers more than expected from a simple premise. By removing the classical expectations of a jigsaw puzzle, you end up with an exceedingly novel experience. The primary twist is that you don't know what the puzzle will look like when completed, so you'll need to use more mental skill in recognizing objects and then deducing the appearance of the next parts. There's additional challenge in the fact that you don't have easy edge pieces to focus on first, and you also won't even know if you have all the pieces you need or if you may even have too many. This may sound purely like added challenge or frustration, but in reality it makes each step of the solving into a greater thought exercise. There is a satisfying brilliance in the mental leap that is required to predict the unknown, and this game provides that in a constant stream.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever posted a review on Steam. I own hundreds of games and have been on the platform a long time. But I felt compelled to type something.This game is: SO. DANG. GOOD.Took me about 8 hours in total, and I basically completed it within 24 hours of launching. And I don't even like jigsaw puzzles much in real life.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Just good vibes. To preserve some level of difficulty, every so often the puzzles get a bit devious and you can also end up missing parts in another shipment so you must work around and store ones in progress. It's always satisfying to finish a puzzle and the game is just a delightful experience. Being able to decorate the different rooms is a nice touch too!
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: The Wilmot-shaped hole in my heart was indeed filled by this game with a satisfying click. I'd highly recommend this game to any and all puzzle lovers! Also, I feel like this may be a better introduction to Wilmot for some. The pace of this game is very chill, and marathon mode may ease more anxious players into the style of Warehouse without the addition of time pressure.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: wilmot works it out is not an autobiographical narrative adventure by gary wilmot, mbe. it is a game where you must assemble a series of jigsaws by pushing blocks around. the vibe is relaxed and cozy, except when the postlady knocks on your door incessantly and tells you about things you're not interested in.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Did I get so distracted by puzzling that I zoned out and missed a knock at the door? Yes.Did I get so paranoid about missing a knock at the door that I checked it repeatedly, hallucinated knocks, and focussed my puzzle assembly toward the front of the room? Also yes.The simple conceit of meshing jigsaw puzzles with logistics has managed to plumb the depths of my psyche. Am I missing a piece, did I misplace a piece, why does my floor look like my desktop? Why is this game a mirror into my soul? Thank goodness I don't also have to make a cup of tea!Lovely pictures, too.10/10. Would lose my mind again.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: A really cosy casual game that is all about puzzles!Wilmot takes a break from his somewhat stressful warehouse job to solve puzzles, game is a breeze to control and incredibly well designed with the ramp up in difficulty and the red herrings Game is a bargain and you'll get your moneys worth in my opinion.My single and only complaint is it's a bit fiddly to move your paintings around and decorate, but nevertheless I had an incredible time with this. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Wilmot's Warehouse which built up anxiety and stress as you try to keep things organised whilst under time pressure but I'm really pleased how well this works as a gentle chill game without that pressure.There is still satisfaction from keeping your space organised as you try and sort the various puzzle pieces on the floor but with that pressure removed you can just take your time whilst you put together the puzzles.I don't really do jigsaw puzzles in real life but this evokes my memory of the satisfaction of sorting through the pieces and slowly putting together a picture. At this point I've done the first batch of puzzles and whilst I haven't found any particularly difficult I can feel the difficulty increasing so I'm intrigued to see what the later ones are like.I'm also enjoying the little insights I get into the delivery person every time they deliver a new package and talk to me.If you want a nice chill time whilst doing some puzzles I don't think you can go far wrong with this.
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: It's the perfect jigsaw puzzle game, it's fun and relaxing. The music is impeccable, it helps fill the background with some jazzy tunes. Wilmot's a cutie, and the side story was interesting. I wholeheartedly recommend it.I could play this for a lifetime if they sold more intricate puzzles in packs. Hope to see what Wilmot does next after the warehouse gig and puzzle club membership!
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Great combination of jigsaw puzzle and organization! No time limit; you might feel space pressure but no time pressure, very cozy and relaxing. The controls are just as smooth as the original, and the art is beautiful. I'm very tempted to see if this artist sells printsI will say I noticed a fair amount of slowdown, which felt fairly random; it was worse when doing Marathon mode, as I might expect, but it also happened during normal play; it would fix itself after a couple seconds, but it would hang during that time. It did not put me off the experience.Playing the whole game fully took me 17 hours but I would say there's lots of wiggle room depending on your skill
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Are you good at puzzles? Do you love organizing stuff? This is the game for you. I bought this game for a family member who loved the wilmot warehouse game. This game breathes an air of nostalgia, if you’ve ever played those tile puzzle games when you were younger, (for example the rollercoaster tycoon games that had playable mini games) this puzzle setup reminds me of those. While being nostalgic it’s also something new that I haven’t seen with puzzle games. It’s refreshing, minimal style is incredibly captivating. I love the interactions with the mail lady too!!
_childDocuments_.name: Wilmot Works It Out

_childDocuments_.review: Every time I revisit Wilmot's Warehouse, I am reminded of how charming and stylish it is, so I came into this sequel with high expectations. This game hooked me within the first round of puzzles, easily. I am so impressed by both its continual stylish charm and how elegantly and smartly the puzzles are designed - I literally gasped out loud at the reveal in Season 3. This game feels like how putting together a puzzle on the floor of my living room feels and I mean that as the highest of compliments.

name: Hauntii
detailed_description: Play as Hauntii, a naïve ghost on a journey to ascend beyond the afterlife. Explore with your angelic partner, solve challenges, and collect starry fragments to reveal glimpses of your past life. Use the unique Haunt mechanic to possess and take control over almost anything (even trees)! Dash, jump, blast, glide and shake your way through the intricate world of Eternity . Haunt As a ghost, use your haunting powers to command both creatures and the environment itself. Craft an array of solutions to puzzles, and devise various approaches to combat scenarios. Explore An expansive hand-crafted world, with tight yet open-ended environments. Whichever path you take, there'll always be something around the corner, waiting to be discovered. Collect Build the Constellations and uncover the story of Hauntii's past life. Find the pieces you'll need by exploring, solving challenges, and trading with other ghosts. The game employs a unique hand-crafted art style, making use of line art, animation and a striking two-tone palette. Meanwhile, Hauntii’s dynamic soundtrack sways and swells with the action on-screen, creating a captivating audiovisual experience.
