_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Hauntii is an indie title very worth playing with a high level of artistry.The gameplay uses twin stick mechanics but it is a more slow paced, methodical game so don't go into it expecting bullet-hell high speed madness. Instead, think Mario Odyssey: you haunt objects to unlock abilities to defeat enemies or solve puzzles that reward you with stars. The stars are used to progress the story through showing your memories of your past life - as well as giving you options to upgrade health, "stamina" (dashes), or "ammo" (essence).The visuals - hand line-drawings and animation - are incredible.The soundtrack is the absolute standout here. Get the OST - it really stands well on its own, but it also brings you through all the emotional changes of pace within the game. The story is told in a cryptic or impressionistic way. There is little direct exposition. The game does tell you what your current objective is but it is up to you to absorb everything the game shows you and piece together what it is trying to tell about the ghost's past life and the important lessons. There are occasional NPCs who establish the themes of the game through your interactions, and the rest is out there for you to experience. Take your time, explore everything, interact with every npc... just really drink it up.Really impressive that this game came from such a small team. Every single one of them clearly sets a high standard for themselves with the art they create. The game can be beaten in under 10 hours - so you have the time necessary to enjoy it. No performance issues, runs great on the steam deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: For a game about being a dead little guy without the ability to speak properly being attacked by ghosts significantly bigger than them, I ended my time with  feeling surprisingly chipper and upbeat about the game. That didn’t come without a few gripes, but no game is going to be perfect, let alone the debut title from a small indie team. What it might lack in corporate polish and shine,  more than makes up for in pure heart, charm, and gorgeous artwork. Now, my total time spent playing shows about 27 hours for me to get all the achievements. I promise it’s not that long of a game. I work from home, and I’d sometimes boot the game up for a little session during my shift, and I’d usually forget about it running since it doesn’t get crazy about hogging my PC’s resources. If a long game is what you’re looking for,  isn’t going to be that, though it’s not short either. Getting all the achievements probably took me around 15 hours of actual time played to complete. Visually, it’s a beautiful game in that way that’s propped up by strong art design and direction, not with the realistic graphics that show every pimple on a character and will melt your GPU into molten slag in your case. The art clearly had tons of love and care put into it, giving us characters, enemies, and environments that are all fully realized and brought to life. There’s this nice two-tone style that gives each area a unique feeling, which is likely the result of some color psychology that goes beyond what I’m consciously aware of. That said, the art design can sometimes be ’s enemy. While the two-tone style and filters make for a very striking and visually appealing game, there are instances when it can be hard to tell exactly where you are in a specific area. It can also make ledges difficult to see in exact relation to where you are, which gets substantially worse when the camera pulls out for certain parts of the game. It’s not a good thing when I have to lean closer to my screen and start squinting just to try and distinguish my character in a cluttered battle or set piece. While this isn’t exactly an art choice, it’s adjacent enough that I feel like it’s worth mentioning. Moonloop, please, I am begging you to do more QA testing on winding staircases if you make another game like this. They do not work in , and it’s especially annoying at the end of the game when , with the camera being pulled back obnoxiously far again. I straight up could not see what I needed to see, so unless it was a metaphor for something, consider adjusting how the environment interacts or interferes with crucial visual information we need. In more than just graphics and art direction, the visual information is the core of ’s storytelling. You gather up stars you get for completing puzzles, defeating enemies, and wrapping up various challenges in each area. By combining those stars into constellations, you get a backstory told without words in charming little cutscenes that tell you a little about who Hauntii was before their journey in the afterlife. You’re accompanied most of the game by an Eternian, the white angelic being who acts as a sort of “guide” and friend for Hauntii, existing in the narrative to help ghosts gather up their memories to  I like this as a storytelling tool. At first, I was disappointed that I didn’t feel many of the NPCs had much staying power, despite a lot of their designs being fun and interesting. Then I realized it made perfect sense. The entire theme of the game, or at least my interpretation of it, is to  It’s revealed early on in the game that the ghosts don’t like Eternians and that Hauntii shouldn’t look for his guide or trust her should they find her. With the purpose of the Eternians being clear as the game progresses, it makes sense that NPCs wouldn’t just follow you around.  Moving to the gameplay side of things, things generally click, and most things hit. The first two areas of the game are the highlights. You get to haunt a cute, cozy little forest, and the second area is this grand amusement park area. Both areas have fun enemies to fight, puzzles to solve by haunting, and cool environmental interactions with haunting things like trees. You shoot your way through the bad guys, haunt the things to progress, and gather up stars to complete constellations that let you gain stat increases. It does fall off in the third major area of the game. The area is huge with a specific intended traversal mechanic you gain by haunting a certain creature. You lose out on some of the fun puzzles and great environments by doing that, turning it into a vast, featureless, and largely lifeless desert area. Come on, the ghosts have shown they can party it up with an amusement park. We can do better than trudging across a boring desert for a whole area. In general, the gameplay takes its biggest bonk on the head in the third area. The creature you haunt is annoying and frustrating to control, and an entire boss fight ends up revolving around that mechanic. If there was a part of the game that felt half-baked, it was that area and its core mechanics. I don’t want to say it was a “nothing” area, as that seems way too mean for something not that big of a deal, but I do legitimately believe it could have been removed or replaced and not a lot would have been lost in the experience. Moving past that, you get to the last area of the game, which strikes a balance between the first two areas and the third one. The last main area didn’t feel like it was losing steam in it like the third area did, with a few fun puzzles and challenges wrapped up in a cool, oppressive, melancholic vibe. While it lacked the charm and joy of the first two areas, I felt like it got the game back on track for its ending. Which, as expected,   did have me leaving satisfied, though the experience was somewhat uneven. The most unwelcome area in the game felt like it went by in the shortest amount of time, but it’s hard to feel like Moonloop wasn’t struggling to fill out those last two areas somewhat. Still, it’s a beautiful game with cute characters and a nice little story that’s told a lot without words, with gameplay that sticks the landing more than it misses. For $20, I think it’s worth someone’s time, and I think it’s worth it to see it all the way through to the end. As a debut title, I think Moonloop did a fine job with their project they clearly adored to pieces. But if you do get  and want to get all the achievements, keep track of your hats! Once you get one, you can’t see the name again, and make sure you reload the area where the shops are. They’re usually going to be restocked with new hats to buy. Moonloop, if you read this, PLEASE consider adding a better way to track hats in the game. I will buy every  soundtrack and artbook I can find if you do.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is aesthetically beautiful, excellent score and has some great cinematic set pieces with a great core game loop, it kinda fell flat at the end for me.  I really enjoyed the game in the first ~2/3 of my play through, but the last 1/3 of the game became frustrating and soured my desire to play.  I definitely rage-quit a few times from frustrating mechanics.  It really just felt like a slog at the end.  Which is a shame because I was excited to play.-Great core game loop: Dash, shoot, haunt-Beautiful aesthetics-Fantastic score-Stellar cinematic set pieces-Satisfying difficulty spikes, toho/bullet hell etc-Open dyslexic font!-The last 1/3 of the game felt like they were padding for time with needless mechanics   If the game was shorter and more focused I would have enjoyed it more.-Some mechanics aren't well explained and frustrating to figure out.  And when you do figure them out, you never use or see it again.  And you don't have a sense of accomplishment when you do figure it out, but a sense of relief, like, "Thank god that nonsense is done" -For having a lot of nice accessibility features I wish it had inverted controls separated for the sand whales.  The Sand Whales are supposed to control like a plane or submarine where pushing the control stick forward would dive, and pull back to climb.  This is however opposite and cumbersome.-Some areas you couldn't get a star even when using different mechanics.  Like, "It makes sense to use that ability here" it doesn't work, even the backup mechanic doesn't work.  -Sometimes the high contrast aesthetic made it very difficult to determine the edge of a platform-Enemies bosses sometimes glitch preventing progression-UI doesn't update past 5 essence.  I did glass cannon build, and it didn't show the progression past lvl 5.-Max ghost fire at 2999.  And there aren't enough things to use the fire on, so you're always left with an excess.-Sometimes ghost fires would block the path if you had max-A lot of level specific collectibles that don't seem to have a purpose?  Each level had a specific blue collectible, but what's it used for?-can't skip dialog if you've been through it once--The NPCs felt inconsequential to the story.  The Wizard in the castle and Glasses ghost were the only ones that felt like an antagonist.  But they're quickly dispatched.I'm sure I'm being overly critical, I feel that if the game had been shorter and more focused it would have been better for it.  I was feeling burnt out by the end, and I just wanted to get the game over with.  The fact that you can beat the game without needing to get all the stars, to me, say that those stars and locations shouldn't have been added in the first place.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game marred by horrible design decisions and poor controls. Played on Steam Deck and thus is reviewed as such.First, the good: The two-tone art style is incredibly pretty and hauntingly beautiful, as is the animation, and music and sound design. This game is incredible to look at. The story is simple but works to its advantage, telling a short and sweet tale. The game also runs extremely well on Steam Deck.Unfortunately, that is where the good ends and the bad begins. There are so many questionable design decisions in this game that I can't help but feel frustrated at the waste of time it all adds up to.Needing to gather purple energy to use the haunted objects' special actions feels like such a tacked on aspect. You never needed to collect anything special for Cappy to do its thing in Mario Odyssey; and running out of energy during a crucial moment just destroys whatever semblance of progress you've made.The feedback design on controls are also pretty poor. It's impossible to tell where your sandwhale is going to steer/jump during the Vortex battle of the game, for instance, and the cowboy shootout portions doesn't give any sort of aiming reticule, so you have to "best guess" it for a precision shooting activity and end up missing most of the time.Other incredulous pieces of bad design include the coaster battle in Wickland, where it's impossible to see where the first bombs are on the track until a split second before you collide into them (the camera is shifted far too much behind you rather than showing what's ahead), and i ended up having to just not use the boost at all to be even able to make it through the section, which is a pretty anticlimactic end to what is otherwise a very unique and cool boss fight.You also, inexplicably, can be hit by things when still in the "coming down" animation from putting stars into the night sky. I've died several times when i still didn't have control of my character from it being hit by things when the camera was still panning back down.There is much to like about this game, but unfortunately it's let down by the fact that you'll be battling a lot of the design choices they made, in the process of going through it.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! The art style is amazing and I love the story. I really struggle with the idea of death and the fact that I will die one day. I love that this game gives me a cute, new way to think about the afterlife. I will say, this game is definitely challenging at times, but I enjoy that! I do wish it was easier to move around to the different locations. I'm someone who likes to double check that I haven't missed anything and it's time consuming to retrace my steps if I want to go back to an area.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals by far are my most favourite thing about this game as they strike out with such beauty. The visuals seem so effortlessly simple with minimalistic use of colour but overall creates this world with so much personality and charm. The game is a beautifully crafted work of art where it sets a monochromatic tone with quite sketched, point-like art style. Even though there is so much simplicity to the game it brings so much life through its pleasing and charming animations. The animations carry out great bodily expression and actions that bring everything together.What truly sets this game apart from other games is the exploration and puzzle mechanics which drive the player into really focusing on using Hauntii’s ability to haunt objects to interact with the environment in a clever way. This gameplay style I found to be so much fun because you could also haunt everything in the world and use it to your advantage. The progression of the game followed you exploring one area which led to the next and unlocking gates by completing constellations, each area having a select number of stars for Hauntii to collect in order to complete constellations.Another thing I quite enjoyed was the combat in this game, it felt somewhat like a bullet-hell at times, where there was constant shooting but I felt the difficulty of the enemies increased more and more as time went on. Personally, I found the combat to be pretty balanced and being able to haunt enemies that can momentarily upgrade your damage allowed players to play smart.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: ProsAesthetically pleasing and has some cute character/creature designs with great animation.Interesting take on the afterlife with spirits having to let go of the memories from when they were alive to pass on/ascend and the angel like creatures who act as their guides being treated as monsters.Beautiful soundtrack ConsThe high contrast black and white visuals and automatically changing perspectives make the game disorientating at times as you cannot make out where you are or where enemies are.Clunky movement as going near the edge of something will sometimes throw you over or you get suck on things in the environmentThere are some clunky mechanics in the game like some of the objects/creatures you haunt  or the mini games you have to play to unlock starsThe map for the game only shows you what area you are in but not where you are in the area or what’s in the area.Not much of an incentive for collecting all collectibles except for having the bare minimum stars for each area to ascend and complete the gameCombat becomes boring as there is a lack of interesting things to haunt and be used during combat.No form of fast travel until near the end of the game but the fast travel only works near stones and will only take you to an area not a specific location.There is no indication on the map of where the fast travel stone are either so you have to remember.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game certainly isn't without its flaws, it nonetheless manages to be a fun, magical, and deeply emotional experience, with a very strong identity to it that sets it apart from any other game.The gorgeous artstyle and heart-tugging story are definitely the most striking aspects here. Everything in this game is super pretty to look at, and I simply cannot believe how much detail, and especially how much raw emotion this game is able to portray using its extremely limited colours and simplistic shape language. And I do mean RAW EMOTION. The story had me in absolute shambles at several points, making me question what I believed about the world and characters, and in the end delivering a truly unique and powerful message through a combination of heavy symbolism and interaction with gameplay elements. In that regard, this game is something special.The gameplay is great as well, though it does have its issues at times. For the vast majority of the game, it plays really well. The haunting mechanic is very fun to interact with, and the methods of obtaining stars (the major collectible) are somewhat repetitive in concept but each usually has some fun twist that makes it enjoyable to collect nonetheless. It's nothing special, but it carries itself along well with its heavily Super Mario Odyssey-inspired format, merged with a twin-stick shooter gameplay style, and is more than enough to keep you engaged through the story and wanting to explore each area to the fullest. Like I said though, it is not without its problems, especially in its last quarter. While most stars are fun to collect, there are definitely a few frustrating ones, or ones that DO feel repetitive, but that's bound to happen in a game with this many of its major collectible, so I can forgive this. There are other smaller issues too, like the camera making gameplay harder than it needs to be at times, the map not being very helpful for navigating areas, a bit of an annoying difficulty spike in , and generally a number of bugs and oversights (immediately taking damage when un-haunting some enemies, the camera panning up to the sky for seemingly no reason, the fast-moving shuttle enemies in the final area being a bit too fast to react to them coming on-screen, etc.). These issues did not do much to bog down my experience personally, but they are worth mentioning.Hauntii is not a perfect game, but it touched my heart in a way few others have managed to do. I truly think Hauntii is special, and I hope that others can look past its flaws to see the beauty that I see in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: I originally backed the game on Kickstarter in 2022, but it was unsuccessful in raising money. However that did not stop the devs in pursing their vision for this game. I joined the discord and watched the various updates over the next 2 years, and did not hesitate in buying the game when it finally released after so long.This is one of those games that has a story to tell, and uses a very unique artstyle and world in which to tell it. I think this game is an absolute masterpiece that does everything it set out to do. Everything from the artstyle to its music is absolutely beautiful.I streamed it on my Twitch channel and have stated multiple times just how much I adore this game. _childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Hauntii is a gorgeous, hand-drawn game about acceptance and moving on, told through an afterlife setting. It’s been done many times before, but Hauntii conveys it with a subtle grace that left a serious pang in my heart. The story is simple, but beautiful and well-told. The art may be cute, but more importantly it is a functional aesthetic that supports the message the game is trying to convey. The music, too, supports the aesthetic. It’s unobtrusive and ethereal where necessary, but turns to convey the decadence of those still chained to their desires just as quickly. It’s been a long time since I critiqued music, but the saxophone was an excellent choice for the main themes.Hauntii’s gameplay is fun and light-hearted. This is a casual game with some light collectathon aspects. The focus is on the linear story, but there are plenty of little things to collect. However, they are careful not to make you feel obligated to collect everything, either. Despite being prone to completionism, I found myself perfectly happy to let go with having simply collected all the stars (of which there are far more than is actually necessary to complete the main story and even the bonus upgrades). They’ve added token rewards for collectors in the form of little hats, and a token punishment for death — enough so that you feel you want to avoid dying while collecting things, but not so much that you feel burdened. For those who like material reward, such token gestures might be more irritating than anything, but in the context of what the game is trying to convey, that in itself is meaningful.There are very few negatives to the game. These are mostly in the form of minor bugs that can easily be patched out in the coming weeks after launch, like the occasional ‘triangle’ (currency) failing to be picked up, or getting stuck in a wall while haunting a jumper, which was easily resolved by simply un-haunting it. A couple of the more significant issues were certain puzzles for stars that didn’t seem to work as intended; they are still completable, but took more brute force than should have been necessary. The one true negative in my mind is one that plagues 2.5D and 3D platformers in general: problems with spatial perception, especially height and depth. There are several puzzles and boss fights that require you to jump through rings or otherwise hit things that are floating, but the perspective makes it painfully hard to tell where the target actually is.As I came to the end of my journey with Hauntii, I found myself pleasantly surprised that the game didn’t hold my hand. From start to finish, the most you get is a single written next objective and a flag on the map indicating your next destination. And, in what I consider a stroke of brilliance, [minor aesthetic spoiler]  You are the one to decide when to leave it all behind.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: This is a twin-stick shooter collectathon with massive amounts of soul, in every sense of the word. The game seems relatively laid-back and casual at first, but it's modestly challenging. On top of that, the game was longer and more open than I was expecting. It's an impressive feat how I wasn't bored; simplistic games that are long can get stale easily. Although this does recycle some gimmicks like any other collectathon (races, shooting galleries, etc.), even those usually had enough noticeable variation, and the levels still introduced all-new gimmicks. The brief animated cutscenes attached to your upgrades were also a clever way to make that repetition less bothersome, as they of course flesh out the narrative. In concert with the solid game design, there's great art direction, smart writing, and excellent music. I don't often buy the bonus art books or soundtracks to games, but everybody knocked it out of the park here.While there are a few things that I felt could've seen tweaking and improving, such as the camera angles in certain areas, on a moment-to-moment basis this game is fairly polished.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: A Hauntingly Beautiful Experience!After seeing the trailer I had to try out this game! I love games where you haunt (possess) other characters/objects but I wasn't so sure about the dual-stick aspect as I'm not really good at them. But I must say, it’s been an unexpectedly delightful experience. As someone who isn’t typically drawn to dual stick games, I found Hauntii to be refreshingly accessible and easy to get into.The first thing that struck me about the game was the artwork. The visuals are not just beautiful, but they also contribute to the overall atmosphere of the game, enhancing the haunting theme that runs throughout. Not to mention the music and sound design which is truly captivating, adding another layer of immersion to the gameplay. The sound effects are spot-on, and the music perfectly complements the game’s aesthetic.Despite my initial reservations about the dual stick controls, I was pleasantly surprised by how quickly I was able to pick up the game and start haunting. The controls are intuitive and responsive, making the gameplay smooth and enjoyable.Whether you’re a fan of dual stick games or not, I highly recommend giving Hauntii a try. It’s a hauntingly beautiful experience so far... Thumbs up for Moonloop. They did a great job! Gotta get back to finish the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Its a 10/10 on all counts.The visuals in this game are like no other and it has perfected every aspect of what makes a game great. The soundtrack is one of the best and it really stirs emotion in you during impactful cut scenes. The 2d hand drawn art style gives a really cozy and easy on the eyes experience, It also super unique with its colour schemes and it manages to stand out. Some of the places in this game have honestly had me pause my gameplay for a moment and just take it all in, you cannot help but admire it will always catch your eye. The storyline is also pretty well written, i really love the way the main character's past is narrated and it's journey throughout everything till the very end, though its simple its super heartfelt. the game mechanics are super easy to understand as well and the levels are pretty unique.One of the most memorable games I've ever played and I'm recommending it to everyone i know.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Would like to recommend as game has strong music and visuals, but too many other issues that led to a poor quality of my playthrough of the game. Traversal of areas is a bit tiring. Its fine if its your first visit to an area, but if you get lost or are trying to look for missing stars, its just not fun at all. A lot of the game is exploration to find stars and whatever the blue collectible is in an area, but so many of them are simply too massive. I had initially dumped my upgrades initially into getting more dashes until I had 6 but this was still a problem for many large areas. As well, I was hoping to get a feature to allow me to visit any room I wanted, but I also did not get that as there are only a select number of places you can teleport to. Its a bit difficult for me to imagine slogging through the world to get every star, let alone every collectible.The primarily monochromatic color choices do cause problems at times with determining position or depth. Additionally, the camera being too zoomed in or out combined with resolution issues has led to some problems trying to pick up some things during challenges.Story is a bit thin, which is a bit odd as there are multiple threads to work with, unless theres just additional lore I missed. For the protagonist's memories:  For the protagonist's journey through Eternity: It just seems like you're collecting stars. Some antagonists pop up, but eventually you just stop dealing with them anymore and the conflict between you seems kinda unresolved. For the greater story of the world: EDIT: Was originally going to not recommend this, but the soundtrack has stuck in my head so I've bought it and changed my mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased this game last night and immediately played a solid 2 hours and the picked it up again first thing this morning. Plays great on the Steam Deck. The visuals and VFX are amazing and although I don't quite understand what is going on yet (intentional) I'm compelled to keep playing to find out.Really enjoying this one so far
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Captivating, beautiful, but anticlimactic.Bringing the Odyssey-style bite-sized missions and enemy capture systems into an isometric perspective seems like a strange match up, but the combo works remarkably well. The pleasant cute-spooky aesthetic, serene music, and overall dream-like tone of Hauntii provide a distinguishing flavor throughout the experience. It’s easy to feel motivated to find different locations and secrets as new ideas and visual themes unfold.As I began to wonder how the story would wrap up, I ran into a roadblock that appeared to require some sort of key hunt or a new completionist approach to a game that was thus far generous with its commitment to sightseeing. I nearly gave up, but a while later I figured out what I was missing. But the damage had been done and I felt like my success in filling out all the constellations had been shot down right at the end.Regardless of whether my unexpected pre-ending bump was a near softlock or just a symptom of idiocy, I still really enjoyed exploring through Hauntii. It's pretty, it evokes curiosity, and it's a clever reinterpretation with plenty of identity.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Practically a collection of mini-games with a world, story and ocassional boss battles. But when the story strikes - it strikes hard. Plus art and music are just beautiful.On the downside: mouse and keyboard controlls are a bit awkward and some locations have narrow paths with a weird for a keyboard angle, you'll have to constantly tap to adjust yourself in these moments
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and stellar in its art direction and music.Lots to discover and collect, in a sorta Mario Odyssey style of possessing things to fight or reveal items.Writing is charming, with it's dialogue and characters. The whole game is just full of heart and hard work put into it.More people need to know about this hidden gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with amazing presentation. The gameplay is pretty basic but they really stretch the mechanics to their limits for climactic moments. It was really buggy on release, but the devs have taken feedback and patched out most of the serious ones just recently, so I flipped my review. Overall a good purchase, but...In the end it felt like the story ended before it was even halfway realized, but the game is still enjoyable from start to finish. Maybe there's more I'm missing that requires 100%'ing the game, but nobody knows because 100% was bugged until recently, so we'll see.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: I went into playing Hauntii without any expectations really. It just looked like a cute, little indie game.As I played, I was so impressed with how much care was put into this game. I did not expect the monochromatic level design to not overstay its welcome, but it is so well done and actually such a plus. I was also very excited by how large the whole map and game actually are.As an avid map explorer, I was very thrilled over the sheer amount of collectible stars (with each having a name to subtly hint at where they can be found if any prove to be a challenge) that existed to reward exploring the map.What especially came as such a pleasant surprise was the difficulty level of some of the combat and bosses. Going in, I was mainly concerned that the cute indie aesthetic would mean that the game would prove unchallenging and inevitably boring. It was like Christmas discovering that some of the bosses would prove to need at least two if not three attempts to beat. The slight increased difficulty of those fights are what really make the game and bring it to that next level of enjoyable and memorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Its good. Its short. Its sweet.The game lives by its art and music, gameplay is pretty simple and easy, and you don't really have to engage in any challenge you don't want to.Collectibles are overabundant, so it'll take away from your experience if you hyperfixate on getting all of them instead of just progressing.Just beat the game, and load the previous save, you can go backtrack and collect all that you missed.If you like how the game looks and sounds in the trailer, you'll like the game. The story is interesting and has an emotional core, but overall everything remains light and simple.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Usually, I don't leave reviews, but I just couldn't pass by this masterpiece. From the art style to music, to puzzles and story, every single element has found its way into the depths of my heart and kept me raving for days. Even though I tend to avoid games with any type of combat in it, this game grabbed my breath from the moment I saw it, and I am so, so glad I picked it up. Once-in-a-lifetime experience, and I thank the developers for allowing me to experience it. I will miss my biblically accurate girlfriend whom I nicknamed 'Airfryer', it's been a wonderful journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game with a charming art style and great music, with a sound gameplay style. Definitely has influences by games like Mario 64, Banjo Kazooie, classic platformers etc. in terms of the stars collecting nature and visiting/ exploring hub worlds. It’s not a perfect game though, I feel like its length is slight a detriment to itself and the amount of worlds/places to explore is a bit much. Also would like to see some more quality of life improvements such as being able to warp around the map at a much earlier stage of the game and another zoom function on the map, to be able to have a closer inspection of the location that I’m exploring, as it can be be quite crating to travel around every corner of the entire area, numerous times, which can be quite confusing to remember sometimes. Especially when I’m trying to find exits, which there are usually multiple in each area, so it can be a little overwhelming.Overall though, underrated little game, would recommend and hope to see more from this team! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: The artstyle of Hauntii is incredibly pretty and is even further elevated by the hauntingly (haha) beautiful piano soundtrack playing most of the time.You are a little ghost, that seems to have recently passed on.Now you're being guided by a little angel, trying to ascend.But before you can do that, you need to collect your lost memories, in the form of stars, that are all over the place. Some easier to find, while others require puzzles to be solved or combat trials to be won to release them.The gameplay loop and story is pretty simple, but the overall presentation of Hauntii alone was enough to keep me playing as I wanted to find out what the next area may look like and how the story of our little ghost and angle duo may end.Don't expect particularly challenging combat or puzzles, but more of a pretty and relaxing little game.Nice, short and sweet, like a little treat. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games where you wish it were longer, even though it's perfect the way it is! The art style is so visually striking! Each area's monochrome color pallette accentuates the intricately textured backgrounds and stage objects; it has the same, cozy vibes of a hand-illustrated storybook.The soundtrack is wonderful as well! I personally wouldn't listen to it on its own or anything, but it absolutely works with the games atmosphere. Also, enemies(?) in the stages each have a subtle variation on their area's theme, which is so cute!!While I wouldn't say the core gameplay is ground-breaking, it's a really solid collectathon that felt really solid to play. There's a healthy variety of challenges to obtain said collectables, and none of them ever left me truly frustrated or bored.There wasn't really anything that got in the way of enjoying the game, but I have just a few little nitpicks nonetheless. The first is that the story is largely advanced via short animations, and these story bits are only viewable once. It'd be neat to have a menu or something to rewatch them...The other is that the number of total collectible stars far outpaces the amount needed to complete the story. To be clear, I absolutely am a completionist and would've collected them anyway, but it does feel just a bit empty when there's no in-game motivation for it (I guess that's what achievements are for, tho)Bottom line: if you enjoy collectathon games a la the 3D Mario games, Banjo Kazooie, Crash, etc, absolutely give this game a look! It's a short n sweet game in the same vein :)))
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't beaten the game yet, but I felt that I needed to leave a review because THIS GAME IS INCREDIBLE. I haven't felt such a jaw-dropping sense of awe over the visuals of a game since I played Manifold Garden; the artistry behind the environment is something that never ceases to amaze me while playing. The gameplay is also excellent- the stars are often really fun to collect, and the expansive environment always keeps things fresh. My only complaint is that the ladybug is a bit tricky to navigate depth with, particularly without the ability to move rotationally around the trees.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: This one's up there with Hollow Knight, Hyper Light Drifter, TUNIC... I'm really hooked! Almost 8 hours in, and I don't think I'm anywhere close to halfway completing this game. I'm obsessed with the art style in this game (it's SO nice <3), and it tickles my brain that the color palette totally changes according to which area you're in. I'm definitely going to spend many more hours here trying to uncover all the little secrets this game has hidden away :]
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous artwork, enchanting music, a story that's simple yet enthralling.  While the gameplay isn't particularly deep or nuanced, the game itself is enjoyable the whole way through and short enough to finish in a few sittings, so the lack of any real difficulty doesn't hold it down.If there's a game that deserves to be more well known, it's Hauntii.  An experience you'll never forget.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable experience that's smooth for players that want something easy to relax to. The music is very chill, the combat isn't frustrating or annoying. I highly recommend this game to anyone that wants to give it a shot. And to any streamers concerned that their audience might not like it, then you might be surprised. This game makes for very awesome chill sessions. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so pretty and chill, but there are still boss fights that challenge me enough that I get that hit of satisfaction when I overcome them. I could also imagine a parent playing it with a younger kid with the parent on the move stick and kid  on the aim (though the visuals can also get deliciously spooky at times too, so be aware). Overall, I think the trailer is a pretty accurate portrayal of the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game, the visual is absolutely stunning and the gameplay is very fun, haunting all kind of objects gives a lot of variaty in terms of loop.The story is really interesting, subtle and touching too, I went through some health challenges with my wife last year, so some passages in the story made me really get attached to the little ghost
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a beautiful game. Wonderful art with a lovely soundtrack and an interesting visual story. The downsides - the ending gets quite tedious. Requires going back through some of the map and there isn’t really a fast travel option. In one end game portion I kept falling off the map with no understanding how I actually stayed on the path once I did succeed where previous runs hadn’t due to a weird fixed camera angle. Sometimes the camera leaves something to be desired. It wasn’t an obstacle most of the time. There are some challenges I felt are too hard, at least for me, but you aren’t required to complete every little piece of this game unless you are trying to hit achievements in steam. I don’t think it has much replay value, but that’s common with this sort of story based game. I don’t regret supporting this game or the money it cost. I thoroughly enjoyed most of my play through with some spots of frustration (half required and half optional tasks). I would and have recommended this game to friends. I got a bit stuck in places, took my time, and did try for some of the extra achievements. That said I got a solid 18 hours from this little game. I’d give it an A or A-.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Simply beautiful, Hauntii keeps you engaged during its 10 hour runtime.Though the game could have launched in a better state with some heavy game breaking bugs and the inability to 100% the game, the devs have been hard at work and responding quickly to bug reports and thats more than anybody can ask for.Thank you for this beautiful game and I am excited to see more from this dev team.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning. A little wonky at times but some patches have fixed major issues. Amazing music. Gameplay ranges from easy item collection and exploration to panicked twin-stick. Bosses were mostly a blast. The story is simple but I'm definitely going to need a minute to just let the conclusion digest. Emotionally satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterpiece. Charming characters, beautifully simplistic graphics, and cozy gameplay. It's been a light year so far, but right now this is my GOTY. The storytelling is perfect, I love the characters, and the haunting music is definitely becoming a part of my regular playlists. Please play this game - you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games I’ve played so far in 2024 <3 absolutely amazing, cute and beautiful art style and world. The soundtrack is phenomenal and the game was so soooo chill. The story really had me feeling and thinking in a good way. Very fun to explore and find stars etc. Absolutely worth it to pick this up
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and I'm left speechless. A beautiful experience - narratively, visually, and especially aurally. Hard to describe just how much love was poured into every square inch of this game and its presentation. Extra shout out to the musicians behind the soundtrack - excellent performances and composition all the way through.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is great! I love the character designs and storyboard, but I'm having a bit of an issue with the part where you need to ring the bells to set the guardian free. I can't seem to ring the bells since they seem "too slow" and won't pick up momentum when pressing a and d or s and w? Is anyone else having this issue?
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: The music and story carried me through to the end here. The graphics are beautiful but ultimately become a bit of a stumbling block by making navigation tricky as everything ultimately blends together. The gameplay is also a bit in on the clunky side but was improving through updates even while I was playing.But both graphics and gameplay are serviceable to carry you through a surprisingly emotional but very minimalist story with an absolutely beautiful soundtrack in the background.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: I'm hooked!The game already enticed me with it's charming visuals but I'm really happy that the Gameplay feels just right :). All the sweet gimmicky puzzles that you experience when posessing creature and the colletathon aspect left me still within the first third of the game.As for the story. It's well captured, making use of sweet cutscenes to get you in, but don't take away too much time for you to get back playing.I will continue to write, in case there's any change of pace in the latter part of the game, but so far I can really recommend it, if you are looking for a sweet Puzzle game with a bit of action^^ and a charming world and story.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Artistically this game is absolutely beautiful! There were TONS of times when I was awestruck by the set pieces and music. I stopped moving my character just to admire all the scenery! The puzzles and challenges here are also wonderful! And you are most definitely rewarded for just taking the time to explore! I would highly recommend this game if you enjoy puzzles! Also the ladybug has an umbrella
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: 5 hours in and have loved every minute - I was expecting a fairly brief story and have been so pleasantly surprised by the map size, pacing, and depth!  Every 'memory' recovered by filling out constellations tugs at my heart strings, and the question of where your angel friend's loyalties lie have me eager to reach the conclusion.  The moments of scope shift where the camera pulls back to let you drink in a huge background setting that dwarfs you in comparison have me in awe, and it's so fun to discover new things to haunt and ways to use them.  Combat is usually pretty easy, but admittedly I've hit a couple bosses or challenges (or very mean rollercoaster bombs) that have required a couple of attempts; so while it's overall fairly relaxed, I don't feel entirely coddled.  Very, very happy with this game and can't wait to jump back in!
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: The art and music deserve the highest praises, but I wish there was  more to gameplay. There's nothing wrong with it per se,  it's just too basic. The upgrade system is not interesting, haunting interactions are rarely complex or intricate, you hoard currency, but barely get to spend it on anything tangible. Yet despite the aforementioned flaws, it's easy to recommend this game, because it has charm and personality in spades, I enjoyed my time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Immensely beautiful in both art and music. As for gameplay, its like if you took the exploration/simple puzzle overworld thing that mario odyssey or paper mario origami king has, with a combat system involving shooting bullets and dashing, as well getting creative by possessing nearby creatures or objects to help out. If that sounds like your deal, I can't recommend the game enough. I did see a few things here and there that could be tightened up a bit, but it wasn't enough to harm my enjoyment any.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game, melding twin stick shooter and puzzle adventure in something I know I’m going to devote hours of playtime to. Whimsical and light hearted most of the time, you can never forget the heavy chains that bind you from ascending or the dangers that linger in the darkness. Blast enemies and haunt your environment to solve puzzles and uncover the truth of who are and who you where.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art style, poignant story.There are plenty of gameplay elements taken from Mario Odyssey (possessing enemies and environment elements to solve puzzles, losing currency upon dying, each area having their special tokens, you can collect more Stars than you actually need, ). It's not a bad thing at all, especially if you are not into Mario, or platformers, nor you can't be bothered to get a Switch. Just something worth pointing out imo.Some Stars are pretty cryptic though. At the beginning there are hints everywhere, but later on, especially in the Void (third area) i had no idea what to look for. I kept exploring the Vortex and couldn't find anything, it gets tiring after a while.8/10, will be waiting for merch.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be finishing this one for sure. A very stylized and graphically interesting game paired with fantastic music - unless you don't like jazz - and generally calm gameplay mixed in with some combat makes for a good time. The worldbuilding reminds me of Hollow Knight, which says a lot about how good the game world is. Play it!
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: I have been very very surprised by this game so far. It is the definition of a fun, relaxing, charming and inspiring experience. The difficulty hasn't been very high so far, but I can see how some of its puzzle aspects could become quite challenging as I progress through the game. Its twin stick shooter elements haven't been relatively easy, so don't let this aspect of the game scare you if you are not too much into heavy twin stick combat. Special kudos to the soundtrack and the overall sound design. This OST is going to stay with us for a while, that's for sure!Final verdict: I RECOMMEND
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! Hauntii is amazing. The art style accompanied with a beautiful soundtrack is a must have experience. It is as if you were to play a game in a painting. There is so much depth to the visual storytelling and frequently left me amazed. This game is super fun with satisfying mechanics that are well developed. Hauntii is definitely a highlight!!
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: I would compare Hauntii as a game to Mario Odyssey in terms of feeling, it does a consistently good thing in game design where it rewards you for any kind of exploring or experimentation you do and constantly teases you that there is more to do in the background, this is good game design. It also looks and sounds great and is telling an interesting story at the same time. It is strange to have such a relaxing game that controls like a twin-stick shooter, but it works well and manages to escalate in difficulty and challenge as it goes to keep it interesting. Overall a pretty high quality game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: Stunningly beautiful details and an exciting indie game with an engaging story.  The game is really well finished, works really smoothly and at least no bugs have been encountered yet.  Graphically and in terms of soundtrack, the game is a work of art.  Really relaxing to play and collect material that the fields are full of.  At least the game wasn't challenging yet, but it was already some kind of nut for the brain during the first hour.  This is not a quick response game, but rather a slower puzzle-type story adventure where a cute ghost is looking for a route through the fields from one place to another.  And you can buy hats for the ghost!  What's better than that.  I would say that steam deck as a travel game is exactly 10/10.  Relaxing, and definitely worth a try :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to begin. The graphics, the MUSIC, the game play. Every single aspect of Hauntii is magnificent. The cute characters make me giggle, the memories make me tear up (every time!), and don't even get me started on how satisfying picking up those little prisms are! I am desperate to find out more about the little ghost's previous life, who that angel is and what they are saying. I haven't even got halfway through, yet I cannot recommend Hauntii highly enough. Prepare to chuckle, gasp out loud, and shed a tear as you wander through eternity with your little ghost.EDIT*Have just completed the game and I am completely speechless and in tears lol
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying Hauntii so far. The hand-drawn art is stunning and the environments look fantastic with lots of little details hidden away. The little odd-ball characters and enemies you find dotted throughout the world are really well done and keep making me smile. The actual gameplay is pretty relaxed, a nice gentle mix of puzzle-solving, exploration, and twin-stick shooting that works well together and lets you enjoy the atmosphere. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Hauntii

_childDocuments_.review:
Eternity. A place that exists outside of space, where all souls eventually end up. No ghost can truly die in Eternity, but all can be led astray, corrupted into hellish versions of their former selves.

A mysterious race of glowing creatures, known as Eternians, guides lost souls to an ominous central tower where they appear to ascend to a higher plane. They look like angels, but no one really knows who they are, nor where they came from.

As Hauntii, you'll traverse this mysterious world - using your ghostly powers to possess both its inhabitants and the environment itself, leading to a wide range of solutions to combat and puzzle scenarios.

name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve
detailed_description: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve is the first original Invincible game from Skybound Games , the creator-led company behind Invincible and The Walking Dead. Experience an original story with striking art directed by Rossi Gifford and creative direction by award-winning writer Jill Murray, and explore the life of Atom Eve in a world filled with beloved characters. Based on the comic book by Robert Kirkman, Cory Walker, and Ryan Ottley. Atomic, With Agency Play as Atom Eve, the fan-favorite superhero from the Invincible universe! Get to know Eve like never before as she navigates her life with the Teen Team, her family, and her friends while figuring out the best way to use her incredible powers as a force for good. Determine Your Destiny Doing the right thing sounds easy until you’re the one making the decisions. Your choices shape your relationships with the people around you and will define what kind of hero you want to be. Choose how to develop Atom Eve’s skills and increase her power, unlock special combat skills, or choose to unlock unique dialogue options to further play your story, your way. Comic Book Combat Take on new and familiar foes in light, turn-based combat woven into visual novel gameplay and wield the powers of Atom Eve as your story flows seamlessly into vivid action that feels like a comic book come to life.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neat little game with a reasonable price tag and surprisingly fun turn-based combat. If you enjoyed Amazon’s Invincible series or the comics, you’ll probably enjoy this as well, although, as you can imagine, the tone is less diabolical and has more of a feminine appeal. _childDocuments_.review: any piece of invincible media is always fun, it's a choose your own choices and dialogue based game and it was surprisingly good, i finished my play through in 5 hoursthe story is engaging, taking place before (i believe) & during season 1 of the show with a ton of characters you will recognize if you have seen the show (definitely check out the show if this game interests you, because you'll be lost without it) as a big fan of the show this has kept me busy for a little while waiting for new episodes of season 2 to dropthe gameplay and combat is good, but easily exploitable (you can just spam your shield move, and cripple enemies with some moves) but it's a really nice touch, some fights were actually challenging when its you versus multiple people because you have to manage your little HP, and energy, there are 3 skill trees you can branch into while you level up and earn skill points, each one has it's own advantage, i went with mostly dodging and counter attacking and stuff if u are a fan of invincible, check this game out it's like an interactive invincible comic book

_childDocuments_.review: If you've read the comic or been following the excellent show on Prime Video, this is a nice little side story from Atom Eves point of view and the events of the first season. Presented as a visual novel, there's also a simplified turn-based tactics game seamlessly attached to it - skill tree included, and it's all rather well done. Get it if you're a fan of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: So this is my first foray into the Invincible series, and having completed this, I can say that I have had a great time and am definitely keen on watching the show now.The game subverts expectations by being more about Eve and the struggles she faces trying to balance being a superhero as well as a teenager instead of the same tired beats of every superhero offering. It is a breath of fresh air in a market that is very samey and I am glad that it exists (and hope they make sequels).The game will also be interesting to an Invincible fan as it gives perspective of what she has been up to during the events of the main series.Speaking of the game on its own, the art-style is charming, the background music is great and the story-line is pretty good.  I think its great that they added turn-based combat to the mix so its not just a plain visual novel, sort of mixes things up that way. There are some interesting choices that you can make too, so there is some replayability value to it as well.All in all, I had a great time and can definitely recommend it, even at the full price (a reasonable one at that) which they are asking.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a great game. I'm not particularly interested in Invincible, but I really love Atom Eve as a character, so I had to pick this up. It's a steal for the price, and a great casual game that still keeps you really engaged. I found myself genuinely intrigued by the plot and wanting to play the next episode to figure out the outcome. It took me about four hours and some change to finish, which is not insubstantial in my opinion.My only real criticism of the game is that the devs were set on the game adhering mostly to canon, which I understand, but I would love their next venture to allow a little more freedom even if it ends the game early/on some wild notes. The fun of a CYOA-kind of visual novel is that it doesn't have to be canon. Semi-related, let me romance Universa you cowards. I sincerely hope this is successful enough to encourage them to make more of these types of games, as I loved it. The fact that I liked it so much despite being set in a universe that I don't really have any interest in should speak for itself.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Invincible, the comic, the show, and now the whole Universe in general? This game is perfect for what it is.I'm not a big visual novel player but this game hearkens back to the Telltale Walking Dead days,  there are a number of choices you make throughout the game which have varying degrees of impact later on in the story. And on the combat side of things, while it seems shallow at first there's a depth to it which makes it less of a 'rock paper scissors' type of combat and more of a puzzle to solve, and it makes it all the more rewarding when you find the right solution to it.I guess if there's anything against it I have, it's that I wish it was longer. I beat this in about four and a half hours over the course of a week, and that was due to me dying a bunch in combat encounters. But considering the price of the game I think it's worth that much at least. I hope that this game doing well means we'll get more Invincible games. But this is still a great entry point for fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: Exceeded my expectations. If you think of this as an interactive comic book you won't be disappointed, assuming you're a fan of the show. If you haven't seen  season one major portions of the plot of this will make absolutely no sense to you. There is just enough 'your choices matter' to  you're having an impact as it will effect relationships, dialogue, resolution of minor plot points, etc. The writing was overall a lot better than I was braced for. You need to play through twice to 100% but you can do things differently enough that it doesn't feel like you're exactly repeating yourself so it didn't feel like a chore.The characters and setting felt more vibrant than I was expecting as well, especially Eve herself. Also as someone who found the art in the store preview uninspiring, after playing through I felt like that's the worst the art gets in the game and it's frequently much better. Why they chose to put that front and center I don't know.Other than Eve the only other character that gets much more depth than the show was Rex.  The other characters are all portrayed faithfully, but you don't get much more into them than the show did.This dips to $4 during every sale it seems, so no reason not to wishlist and wait. For $5 it's definitely worth if you're a fan of the show, especially if you think of it as a next-gen virtual comic book. If that's not what you're looking for, this might not be the best choice for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: This is Visual Novel set in the Invicible comic universe. The story follows Atom Eve and seems to be a mix of original content and basic retelling of first parts of the comics (goes to about end of first season of the Amazon TV show adapation I think). There's also simple and fairly easy turn based combat mini-games in between the traditional VN gameplay.First playthrough will take about ~-4-5 hours, not a very long story. The story is split into 10 small chapters. A secondary playthrough or two will be required to get 100% achievements. Dialog and story decent over all, some pretty comic style cutscenes. As you progress, you will gain experience which you can use to unlock upgrades in three trees. The upgrades give buffs to the combat mini-game and unlock additional dialog options. The story follows one overall arc. The different dialog options can change minor elements of the story and do events with different characters but no major story arc changes or different real routes. On subsequent playthroughs you gain bonus exp which lets you level up Eve earlier and progress through the combat faster.One thing that is lacking is 'Extras'. Unless I missed it there's no Art Gallery or Music Box. Why can't you review CGs you've seen or listen to music? These are pretty standard VN features. There's doesn't seem to be a 'Quick Skip' option to speed through seen dialog and only one save file per playthrough. You can restart a chapter that you're currently playing and I think roll back to a past checkpoint in the chapter but can't keep multiple saves if you want to test out different flows, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: I got my hands on Atom Eve: Unleashed when it came out in 2023, and I have to say, I absolutely loved it. There are no dislikes to be found here, and I wholeheartedly recommend it.The game's story, characters, and interactive elements are like reading a comic book come to life. Being able to make choices in the story adds an exciting layer of interactivity that keeps things fresh and engaging. I've been playing it one episode at a time, and each installment feels like a breath of fresh air.The serialized theme adds to the overall appeal, making it feel like you're part of an ongoing superhero saga. If you're a fan of comics and enjoy immersive storytelling with interactive elements, Atom Eve: Unleashed is a must-try. It's pretty cool and highly recommended for comic book enthusiasts like me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun little game about learning to be yourself and to cope with the transition to adulthood.  I like how they managed to work both the story from the show and a legit combat system into a pretty basic visual novel.  I found the whole thing compelling and identified with the main character.  The art style and audio design are both well-done and they manage to capture the essence of the show really well, considering the medium.A steal at the price.  A few caveats- one, it was pretty easy to get overpowered by the end, to the point that I breezed through the final chapter without a single defeat.  Two, it would have been nice to have some voice acting, as there is a LOT of text in this one.  Three, the amount of control you actually have over the story is pretty limited, with the chapters playing out basically the same way for everyone with only slight differences.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: Short and simple, but I enjoyed this a lot. The perk and combat system is just flexible enough to encourage tactical thinking, and over all three playthroughs, I was finding new story scenes to explore. The music has a nice vibe and I love this art style (though expect to hear a lot of griping about Eve's looks from the usual crowd). As far as a cliffnote's version of these events, roughly analogous to Season 1 of the Amazon cartoon, it hits the major beats while mixing in a couple original plotlines. Not sure if it'll hold up for people not already familiar with the source material, though. I don't usually play Visual Novel type games, but for this price (especially if you can get it on sale), it's a solid way to spend an afternoon.

_childDocuments_.review: As for current, there is a big problem: The dialogues or descriptions spilled out of their word balloons from times to times, making reading experience quite disjointing especially when background is too dark to distinguish the words from it. _childDocuments_.review: Very cool game!  Very well done, excellent comic graphics, engaging story and a nicely challenging fight mechanic. _childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of Invincible, so I definitely wanted to check this out and I am glad I did. _childDocuments_.review: A unique way to re-experience the world of Invincible through the eyes of another character! It isn't very long or expansive, but instead focuses on giving a fun and short story told through the player's eyes using material from the comics as well as adding some of its own! Its style and care for the cast is notable in every moment, and does a wonderful job humanizing characters that didn't get enough focus in other media!That being said, for what it is, it doesn't commit to being a visual novel or rpg with much depth. Choices don't have almost any impact, but dialogue does branch out slightly. Pretty much every event won't be missed if you pay attention, and replaying the game would really only be for achievements since you can take back your decisions at any time in game if there were something else you wanted to do/see.Overall, I would definitely recommend playing it if you're interested in experiencing the story as a fan!

I will say though, I'm very disappointed at the fact that this game could've been keyboard accessible but it doesn't appear to be at all. It's so simple, it's a huge missed opportunity on the developer's part. I just stumbled upon this title but overall I'm glad that I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Female prot in a super hero game (not many games like that, sadly)-Good art and music-Nice simple rpg and story elements-Combat mechanics and level progression are interesting enoughCons:-Can get a bit grindy at times-Probably not a ton of difference in main story upon replay A wonderful foray into the Invincible Universe starring every one's favorite character Atom Eve. Overall, this visual novel reminded me a bit of a Tell Tale Game, as it had a similar look and functionality, which was awesome. While I'd probably agree with some of the criticism that some of the choices don't really matter to much, that's kind of how that style of game often works - the look and tone of the game might change a little based on your choices, but you can't really go to far off the track of the planned story line. While we'd all love a game where you're choices make a ton of changes to the story each time you play, honestly, those games, while wonderful, are few and special . . . this is a very good game if you disregard that some of the plot you will be stuck on regardless of what you do. While the choices may not do a lot, they keep the story interesting and help define your version of Eve personality and back story wise a little, and the story that is there is great - it differs a little from the tv series, but not by a lot.  The characters seem well defined and interesting, and balancing the prots relationships with family, friends, and potential romantic interests had enough tension to be interesting but not so much as to detract from the generally fun tone of the game. Dialogues were fun and engaging, plot reveals were fun too. Level progression was fun and fast, opening up new dialogue options and powers fairly often.Idk....kind of hoping they do a sequel or something, but if not, I'll say this game is solid all the way through. Its got a strong theme and tone, orchestrated by the strength and challenges of Eve's character and her story. While it's nice to leave Atom Eve with an optimistic ending, like the end of the last episode says, this isn't the end - I'm sure there's a lot more story.Anyway, I'd recommend this game for fans of super hero games as well as visual novel players that like light role playing elements - this is one of those games I wish Steam had a star rating, as I'm gonna give it a like/recommend of course, but it deserves a higher star rating than some of the other games I've liked or recommended. I'd happily give this one 4 out of 5 atoms.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a total blast. My only complaint (and it's a serious one) is that the game is disturbing in a "woke" way if that makes any sense. It almost seems as if the game handles various difficult issues such as teen sex, cheating, family abuse, death etc. in an almost frivolous way in order to appear edgy and progressive while some people like myself just can't process emotions associated with those issues so quickly and carelessly.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: HUGE REQUEST: the game NEEDS a New Game Plus mode, as that would be the best case scenario for a second or even third playthrough (achievement hunting, perhaps) to try some different things and power through the fights/get through conversations in a little different way.A very commendable effort in bridging the gap between an animated TV show, a legacy of comic books and the world of video games, all on a very tight production budget it seems. It has that "we did our best and put ourselves out there, check it out" vibe. It's also priced 'just right' in my opinion. Well worth your money if you are not allergic to turn-based combat (which is pretty simple puzzle to solve, nothing crazy or really difficult) or the visual novel approach.Definitely a fun experience if you really liked the show's season 1 and wanted to revisit it from a different perspective, through the eyes of Atom Eve.Some choices let you slightly bend the canon of the show which is very nice. There's an extensive skill tree and you can roleplay a slightly different Atom Eve but ultimately you're still the same character playing the same story.The relationships can be affected by your actions and dialogue which isn't going to completely change the story but it does give you enough to feel like your first playthrough was your own.It's like an extra re-telling of the coming of age story of Atom Eve and that's fine by me.

_childDocuments_.review: This was an interesting game—really short but has a good chance of being replayable 1~2 more times.This is more of an interactive comic book with very, very soft turntable RPG fighting with a neat little build path (3 in total). The story is kind of all over the place; you really need to be a fan and have already watched Invicible S1 and S2 before playing this; it will make the story really more immersive. The game was good and was a nice little side game while waiting in between seasons. Please note that this story and game are focused on ATOM EVE. This also means it's a bit more emotional and girly—not a big deal, but something to note for all the bro's that prefer more darker/masculine tones. However, it's still in the invincible universe. Please note: this isn't the comic characters; it is 100% based off the show's versions, which is good and even better, imho. The fighting is fun; the animations aren't something to brag about; they're just like 3 to 4 frames of action, but they are all well designed. The fighting is great, but I hate how I have to keep spamming the mouse button or controller rather than the battles going automatically. I also wish you could speed up the dialouge and speed of attacks and have something more in depth. This is a great game, however, the music is a bit overbearing and just seems like a placeholder. The story was good. Wish there were more battles or a way to grind all 3 tree paths. As silly as it sounds, a NG+ mode would be really neat.Going to take off some points because this did feel more like a novel, also didn't like the  . I do wish they would have animated the game, though, or at least had the voice actors read the dialogue. Definitely a must-play for any Invicnble fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: I knew nothing about Atom Eve before this.  Now i want to see the show and read the books! Over all it was just a fun and light superhero story, with a bit of depth with relationships and the roller-coaster of being a young adult. Unlike many VN's, it had some combat and you choose where to go or skip. You have some agency of what you do or choose not to do as far as choices and how you went about it. It was rather deep on the choices mater side of things which was nice as often in VN's you are sort of along for the ride.  The story's art and comic book styling was a nice change of pace from the typical slide show scenes where they just change poses. The comic book chat bubbles and picking how to end sentences was also a nice touch.  Fan's of VN's and RPG's could enjoy this short little romp in the world of Atom Eve.  I hope there is more to come.

My biggest negative would be that they NEED to add a new game+ option
