_childDocuments_.review: This was a really fun visual novel type game.  I'm a huge fan of Invincible and the television series and this game was a nice spin on the material and another way to experience the story the show tells.  Really solid game and not too expensive for the time you get out of it.  It gets my recommendation!
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: Sort of like the usual visual novel, but with as much focus on graphics as on text (maybe even more). Set throughout season 1 of the television series, there are 10 episodes that took me around 20 to 30 minutes each to complete. The game takes place strictly from Eve's point of view, so there are familiar moments from the show as well as entirely new ones. I really enjoyed playing through it; I think my only complaint is the lack of an option to fast-skip through dialogue like in visual novels made with Ren'Py. This isn't a big issue, though, as it only matters if you're doing multiple playthroughs to see the differences your choices can make (or to get the Steam achievements).
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of the comics since about mid-run. Atom Eve has always been a top fave superhero so to have a game all about her feels surreal and its nice to have a game that almost feels like its for the female fans. I think its fun even if you are a huge comic nerd and if you only know the show you may not recognize a few characters just yet but nothing spoilery. Its actually surprisingly hard but in a challenging way. Worth playing :D
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: As a casual fan of the show and someone who doesn't play games like this, i found it enjoyable. I was surprised that a game with a skill tree would have so few battles. Without multiple playthroughs it is difficult to know what impact your choices make. That all said, its a fun side story for any fans of the universe.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: Nice visual novel with RPG elements set in Invincible universe (not to mistake with The Invincible).  The game has a good comic book stylization and music, sadly it is not voiced. Gameplay is solid, fights were interesting. RPG skills affects conversations as well by offering new choices. Specialization into different trees can change the gameplay and personality of Eve.  The story runs parallel to the series and slightly diverge to alternate timeline. It was fun and an interesting expansion on the main character.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of Invincible and see the potential and OP-ness of Atom Eve, this game is for you. A mix of RPG and Choice-driven game-play and just a quick game just to feed your gamer soul. This is for you. Plus, replayability is good to try skills and choices not made in the your game run through. For it's price its a win for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: Atom Eve is a fun, brief venture into the world of Invincible left behind by the show. It covers a brief period that spans the first season.If you watched Eve's origin episode, this game is a great way to get more time with her. Likewise, if you enjoy visual novels, it's a great, quick adventure with two romance paths.While the game can be a little too quick (approximately 4 hours for a full playthrough), there is a degree of replayability to it that can double that time if you want to see how different things can get.The combat learning curve is pretty direct, so you won't usually struggle in fights; its system lays out a nice, interesting formula for other games like it in the future. Would love to see more games set in the Invincible universe or from these devs in general.Great singleplayer game to stream or to take a partner through.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Atomic Eve on Steam last week and I have been hooked ever since. It is a turn based adventure game that lets you explore a normal world with your super hero powers.. The game is fun, flexible, and challenging. You can choose from different  skills, and personality traits for your Atom Eve. You can also make decisions that affect the story and the outcome of the game. The game has great soundtrack and interesting gameplay. The combat is turn based and challenging at some stages of the game., the side quests is rewarding and immersive, and the puzzles are clever and varied. The game is not too easy or too hard, but just right. It is a great entertainment for a weekend or two, or even more if you want to replay it and see different endings. I highly recommend Atomic Eve to anyone who loves turn based adventure games with different stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: I've never seen Invincible, so I didn't know what I was getting into. The choice aspect of the game interested me, so I gave it a try. I'm happy to say I was pleasantly surprised. The art style is beautiful and the dialogue is great too. The length is not too long and not too short. The price is very cheap, so no complaints.I would be interested in more games like this. Maybe one day they could make a The Walking Dead based on the show or comics or something. I think TWD game would be great if it had the same artwork and mechanics as this game.The creators have done a great job and can be proud of this game. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: This is what a comic would look like in game form, a twist on the story of Invincible season 1, with some elements of the Atom Eve bonus episode and season 2, introducing a character straight from the comics who might just get introduced to the series as time goes on, who knows? It has the elements of a visual novel, and the battle elements of an RPG, plus a skill tree. Fights are relatively simple once you figure out the mechanics, making a deathless run go smoothly. If you haven't gotten into the animated series yet, this game could be a good introduction to a demographic who want more of this dark saga. A short, simple and definitely love-stricken little gift for the Invincible franchise's 20th anniversary, a second season of the animated show, and Nolan Grayson, or as we better know him, Omni-Man now in Mortal Kombat 1, it is quite a time to a fan of....

_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: Took me three hours to go through, so it's not terribly long, but for the price I think it's fair.The game is like an interactive comic, you go through the first couple of issues of Invincible but from Eve's perspective, there are elements of dating sim and visual novel but it's slightly more than that, there's a combat system (turn based), there's a leveling system with different classes (and the ability to multi-class). I'd recommend it to any fan of the comic (or the show).
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: The game was cheap and pretty cool looking into the perspective of Atom Eve a little closer. As a fan of both the comics and the show, this was pretty cool imo. A little short and not necessarily needed, but as a new form of comics this was kind of ground breaking for it to be interactive. It takes about 4 hours to complete, nothing really difficult and the art for the main character was really off putting at times. But I'm glad I played it, it's not even the cost of a movie ticket and if you're into the show, why not?
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review: As a Big Fan of the Invincible comics and the show, this game is an amazing extension. Following the same outline of the comic plot and show modifications, this game keeps the general feel while also changing the order of events and pacing, which is brilliant for this game since it keeps the story as we know it, but with twists that are in no other Invincible media. The story is further altered by the player's choices, which can be as small as tiny dialogue change to as big as Eve never dating Rex in the first place. The combat isn't flashy but I never found it boring. There's also a skill tree that has both combat and dialogue options to unlock, however it's a bit too large and can't be completed in one play-through which also sucks because there is no new game plus as of yet. But for 10 dollars, this game is a steal for visual novel fans and invincible fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Invincible Presents: Atom Eve

_childDocuments_.review:
Invincible Presents: Atom Eve is the first original Invincible game from Skybound Games, the creator-led company behind Invincible and The Walking Dead. 

Experience an original story with striking art directed by Rossi Gifford and creative direction by award-winning writer Jill Murray, and explore the life of Atom Eve in a world filled with beloved characters. Based on the comic book by Robert Kirkman, Cory Walker, and Ryan Ottley.

Play as Atom Eve, the fan-favorite superhero from the Invincible universe! Get to know Eve like never before as she navigates her life with the Teen Team, her family, and her friends while figuring out the best way to use her incredible powers as a force for good.

name: Tower of Fantasy
detailed_description: Embark together on your fantasy adventure! Set hundreds of years in the future on the distant planet of Aida, the shared open-world MMORPG, anime-infused sci-fi adventure Tower of Fantasy from developer Hotta Studio and publisher Level Infinite, is now available on PC and mobile platforms globally. Players will be able to experience an anime-inspired post-apocalyptic sci-fi art style, freeform character development, and exciting combat through thrilling battles and exciting open-world exploration. In Tower of Fantasy, dwindling resources and a lack of energy have forced mankind to leave earth and migrate to Aida, a lush and habitable alien world. There, they observed the comet Mara and discovered an unknown but powerful energy called 'Omnium' contained in it. They built the Omnium Tower to capture Mara, but due to the influence of Omnium radiation, a catastrophic disaster occurred on their new homeworld. Immersive Open-World Experience a vast alien world full of beautiful open vistas and imposing futuristic structures. Unique Characters Wield the unique weapons of each character that grant different gameplay styles as you explore their compelling backstories. Grow and Explore Together Party up with friends online and take on new adventures in the shared open world. Epic Combat Engage in epic battles against enemies of all shapes and sizes as you switch weapons and gameplay styles on the fly to unlock your own personal fighting style. Explore and Interact Explore and interact with a vibrant living world as you discover your own journey through it. To learn more about Tower of Fantasy, go to or check out our other official channels: Facebook: Instagram: Twitter: YouTube: Discord:

_childDocuments_.review: i downloaded it on steam so you can actually read and see an honest and true review about this game!i am a day1 player and since launch i have never skipped a single day so you can feel free to call me nolife ^^ but its really just for the daily tasks mostly!so lets wrap up first the pros of the game!PROS: -Good graphics also there will be RTX features in the near future!-Complex yet simple and easy to learn combat mechanics (phantasia or bullet time you can call it whatever) relic usage,weapon rotations etc!-Huge open world with different regions and places to explore and immerse yourself!-Decent enough character customisation-heaps of content (will get to it on my initial thoughts)-Very forgiving gacha system unlike in genshin the pity not resetting if you pull early SSR doesnt matter how many times!also if you get unlucky on limited banner after 120 pulls you can just buy your desired weapon/character!and now to the sad reality!Cons: -Way to many servers and different channels it makes you feel you playing a single player game at times! (will be server merges transfer options in the near future tho)-PVP is laggy,cluncky and at times unfair if you dont own certain weapons that can stun the living **** out of you! also there is still hackers in the game but fortunately its being less and less time to time!-altho its very rare but there is still some bugs like you being launced to a random direction when you grappling ledges but really its kinda rare these days but still happens so i still include this!-Chat system very bare bones and definetly needs a rework! (it works tho)-Some bosses in joint operations is kinda buggy like floating 10meters above ground or random teleportingI could include some more pros and cons but they are so minor stuff you wont be even noticing it while you playing it so it doesnt even worht mentioning it!So my initial thoughts on the game!First of all please take it into consideration that TOF is a gacha game and there will be always 4 type of players!-Whales-Dolphins-Very low spenders-F2PI hope that i dont have to explain the meaning of these players but in a nutshell Whale spends thousands,the Dolphin spends sometimes hundreds on the game the very low spender buys the monthly card and battle pass which is like 15 to 25 USD depends if they buy advanced or basic pass,and also the F2P who dont even spend a dime on the game!Now thats all out of the way lets go down to the main topic aka the F2P experience!As mentioned above in pros the gacha system is very forgiving compared to many other gacha games and as an F2P you can grind out hella amount of pulls,darck crystals (premium currency) and on top of that if you get very lucky you can easily 6star a standard banner character which is huge!Also you may ask is the game grindy as an F2P the answer is yes its grindy but as you expect its an mmo rpg game its supposed to be grindy so its not very casual friendly!Also you may ask which category i am out of 4 type of players! I am a dolphin i am occasionally 3star a limited unit and get at least 2pc matrice set and if i get lucky i top it off with 1star advancement! (not every time)and being a dolphin player i still do the grinding every single day because playing the game getting gear and trying to farm for matrices,weapon mats etc is the stuff every player do on a daily basis! even whales!I could literally write a book worth of opinion about the game but i dont wanna bore you to much so here is what i can say about the game!regardless of your status whale or f2p the game can be fun and its adviced to play with friends also form a crew or join a crew and if you are an f2p then you can always find stronger players to beat harder content so you ll be never left behind!Just download the game start playing it grind it and time to time you will get stronger and stronger,so just enjoy the game to the fullest!thank you for taking your time reading my ♥♥♥♥ maybe kinda based review and i hope you will have your fun times in the game and maybe become a TOF enjoyer just like me ^^hugs and kisses #nohomo oh btw i forgot about the actual in game content! yes there is plenty and sometimes it even feels to much! there is raids,joint ops,frontier clash for coop gameplay also the occasional world boss runs people do on a daily basis some just farm for the sake of extra mats or just test their damage on bosses! there is also solo content like bygone phantasm and wormhole where you get both one time and weekly rewards as well! there is also the PVP part if you into it! there is also your daily routine like bountys,collecting gifts for awakening traits,mini games in vera for the gachapon currency and the list so goes on! so if you know what you doing content will be never an issue it might get repetetive but lets be real every game is repetetive if u played the game to much and every game needs an update for fresh content and in this case TOF will be not lacking of content we are 10 days away from version 2.1 by the time i am editing my review so it will be even more to do and explore ^^i hope my review was convincing enough for you to think about life choices and finally stop listening to negative people instead just jump in play the game and enjoy yourself ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Touted at it's early stage as the Genshin Killer by imbeciles (read influencers/youtubers) did not give this game a good rapport. If you take it in an isolated light, this game is okay. It's not as polished as Genshin but it has done a lot of things better in some regards that i find lacking in Genshin (mostly QoL related rather than story)TLDR: a solid game around 7 - 8 out of 10 if you don't take it too seriously. Pros:+ Your own character. (Wanted to play Traveller but with different weapons/elements in Genshin? here you can)+ Anime style (dress up your waifu and husbando to your hearts content)+ Lots of weapons to choose from (Gacha player haven)+ Most weapons are viable (no they are not going to top the DPS charts unless you whale/lucky)+ Fast paced combat (land and aerial combat, some weapons have better combos than others , Genshin lacked the aerial combat but has the better element combo -reaction system)+ open - world (can be a con if you don't like it)+ Multiplayer! (cannot stress this enough, Genshin lack proper multi player QoL and i am not talking about dungeons or raids, just the system that supports playing with friends without being locked out of buying items from npc or interacting with the statue of seven)+ Lots of content update (not a dead game)+ you can skip story (i hate genshin unskippable dialogues, waste of time when in a hurry)Cons:- Gacha (for people that don't like to spend money, this is kinda obvious, but still enjoyable as f2p)- server issues (sometimes crashes, sometimes lagged, roll the dice)- older weapon are less useful in the DPS (support weapons might still be useful, like the standard Zero is still pretty good for supporting)- story (mid, not bad but nothing great)- graphic (not as polished as Genshin or Honkai)- UI (feels too much like a mobile game, of course it is made for mobile as well, so there's that)+- Extrano idea about Customer support if in regards to billing or any cash issues as i don't spend much here (occasional monthly pass early on but haven't bought any recently)i had bad experience with hoyoverse in terms of billing before, so i don't have good things to say about their CS too.Verdict: Worth a try if you like this kind of games or have friend to play with.Don't bother if it isn't your cup of tea. If you're into story, probably stick to Genshin.

_childDocuments_.review: Recent Update:I cannot recommend this game anymore.  I was willing to tolerate the questionable choice of running Lin into the Tian and Lyra banners for the sake of catching up with the CN version faster but then they decided to not add Nemesis to standard after her rerun.  One of the main reasons I was willing to tolerate this game over Genshin is because limited characters enter the standard pool but seeing as that didn't happen I'm done with this game until my black and gold pulls are good for something again.  If you're considering trying to play this game F2P I would recommend you stay away until the standard pool starts getting expanded.  As is trying to keep up as F2P is miserable because of how few limited pulls you get for free.Note: I have many more hours playing this game than my Steam playtime suggests.  I started playing this game a few months ago when the developers launched the standalone client and have generally played daily since then.Tower of Fantasy is an Anime-themed open-world sandbox ARPG with Gatcha elements.  Realistically you will not get every single character without paying and people who have bought more pulls will do more damage than you.  If you're not cool with those things, this game probably isn't for you.  Do you need to spend money to enjoy this game?  No.  As long as you pull strategically you'll eventually have enough characters to make a few competent teams. You've probably heard ToF compared to Genshin Impact and for the most part both games are pretty similar to one another, so if you enjoy Genshin's style of gameplay you'll probably enjoy this game too. I enjoy this game more than Genshin for these reasons:If you haven't played Genshin you can think of this game as a typical open world game with fun combat.  The open world is full of simple activities, enemies and chests.  Most of what you earn from exploring the world can only be used for the standard banner, but you will also earn a lot of "black crystals" that can be turned into limited banner pulls for free.ToF also has a neat 'relic' system.  Relics do various things and are generally useful in either combat or exploration.  You can unlock things like a jetpack, grappling hook, missile launcher or blackhole generator.   Character balance for the most part is OK and much better than on the game's Chinese version.  Limited characters were notoriously OP on the Chinese version, but have been reasonably nerfed on this version.  They are still better/more useful than standard characters but without doing WAY more damage.The daily and activity loop is similar to other F2P games with the most important progression related resources being limited to weekly tasks.  I'm not going to claim the daily loop is great, but it's quick and painless for the most part and 'pays' reasonably well.The story in this game is just kinda there.  I found it enjoyable but it didn't leave an impression on me.

_childDocuments_.review: Day 1 pre steam release player, participated in closed beta too.The good:Personal character customisation is good.Exploration feels good and rewarding.Global version has japanese dub.Gameplay is fun, if you have money for it.Vera region and mirroria are a huge step up in quality over 1.x version.Gacha pity doesn't reset on SSR drop.A lot of endgame activities such as wormhole, raids, world bosses and coop dungeons.The Bad:Gear substats are rng, which leads to potentially being stuck on trying to optimize your build for very extended periods of time.Most events are boring and not enough rewarding.Hotta decided to speed up patches schedule to allow the global client to catch up with CN version, problem with this approach is that rewards didn't scale up accordingly leading to a clear lack of resources and time needed to get new characters and build gear strong enough to tackle content unless heavy spending is involved.To give an idea CN had a total of around 8 months between release and 2.0, global had barely 3 months. Speedup is so bad they started to overlap banners causing further pressure on spending.Shop bundles have way lower value compared to CN for the same amount of premium currency.As F2P you will be practically forced to prioritize only 1 element, low spenders can somehow manage with 2 on a total of 4.This clearly isn't fun because most of the appeal of these type of games is getting new characters to play with, something the game heavily restricts out of greed.Characters are not added to standard pool after their banner ends, not until they get at least another rerun which might take months. Lin is classified as a limited character meaning she will never get added to standard pool ever, hinting at future limited characters.Characters/Weapons are too reliant on getting dupes to feel rewarding to use, example is Nemesis which is worthless as a healer unless you manage to obtain 2 copies.On top of resources being scarce Hotta releases gachapon 'events' lasting barely a week fairly often to obtain limited outfits and accessories to customize your custom made character, these gachapons are paid only and hypothetically can cost you up to 100+ euro.Most high end content requires a whale to carry you to completion unless you are willing to spend minimum 10 times the amount of time and effort required to clear.The Hotta:Hotta rebalanced a lot of scaling for global compared to CN, while this has clear positives it also comes with some subtle negatives.Some content such as Joint Operation 8 and elite enemies in the map are not scaled properly leading to bloated hp pools and huge amount of damage if you get hit.As a personal opinion this rebalance is just a way to shuffle the meta around making some characters more appealing compared to their position to CN meta which is taken as a point of reference.Security and bugs are practically a joke to the development team, hacks and exploits run rampant and bugs that were supposed to be fixed in the CN client didn't get a backported patch to global.Conclusion:Tower of Fantasy is a good game at its core with some nice ideas and clear improvement over new patches, however is also a game that is difficult to like because of the dev team clear laser focus on squeezing as much money out of their whales as possible leaving normal players to deal with the aftermath.My advice is to not play this game unless you have a lot of free time and money to spend and some friends to tackle more difficult content together.

_childDocuments_.review: So I played This Game a while back when it first came out, Deemed as the "Genshin Impact killer". After a few days i got a bit bored and left it alone or just simply forgot to get back on it, Now that i have gotten back on it today, i can say with full confidence, That yes...This game has so much things it does better than Genshin does. For starters: The combat. It seems that the combat is actually more based off the combat from Honkai 3rd Impact. Another game of Mahoyo that was popular prior to before genshin impact. The story and characterizations of the cast of playable characters are also very well written. Now...this is a gacha game but what i find most surprising, is that while the 5 star weapons are indeed quite fancy (do not care about the lacryma or whatever it is called to morph into the characters you get), you can still be better off with the 3 star weapons you receive. This game Depends purely on skill for you to do well on the long run and less on gacha meta. In fact I'd argue that you could ignore the gacha all together and just play the game as it is.What i find great though, is that this game has more of MMO RPG elements than it does for a gacha game, which i feel is another thing setting it apart from Genshin Impact. Making it quite easier to grind in little time or just exploration in general to receive points to unlock gacha rolls as a F2P Player.Oh Also the Aeshtetics are just much more better. Kinda giving me a borderlands type of feel. This game is just pretty good overall in my opinion. My only issue being the lip sync in some of the scenes because of how the original langauge is in chinese that sometimes after they are done talking, their mouths still move and wave their hands around in awkward silence.ALSO some advice for new players: The story will move you automatically from now on to the latest story for some reason rather than you doing the OG quests when you start off. Do the Quests in the memory section. That's where you need to go. Sadly i have broken the immersion myself because of this which is my second gripe...why do this? what's the point of it? _childDocuments_.review: It was fun for a while, have more time than listed due to playing before it was brought to Steam.Now I'm somewhat conflicted in giving it a bad review because even though it's PvE and extremely pay to win... I'd have minimal problems with that as long as it's pretty honest and ToF is quite honest about you needing to pay to be good and get stuff.To put things into perspective quickly: a whale can hard carry a typical group since they'll be doing 3-4x as much damage as free to play/cheap players while also being beefy enough to survive much more easily.Where it does get my negative review is that it just isn't free player friendly at all. Big new event? Better bust out the credit card because the entire event revolves around spending actual money with the free/low budget players being left out in the cold.A lot of free to play games have a balance of stringing along the free players with enough stuff to keep them happy while also letting whales give them huge stacks of cash to lord over the free players - that's the basic idea of most mobile games. The problem here is that there's very little incentive to be a free player and almost nothing keeping them around. Typically mobile game events have ways out for free players which are like "just grind for 200 hours over the next 2 weeks to get the stuff you need!" but that route is straight up nonexistent here, pay up or nothing.Usually what happens in cases like this where they're trying to run a mobile game with only whale content there ends up with nobody for the whales to lord over and it sorta loses the appeal for them too. Mobile game design classes 101 right there.The game itself is also stuck in the mindset of "I'm a mobile game" but "I'm also a MMO" without adjusting for a healthy mix. There's still a stamina system and although you can run missions multiple times, you only get the main rewards when you spend the stamina... which takes exactly 24h to cap out. Want to play the game with your friends every night around 6pm? better not be late or you'll be burning stamina and get slowly pushed back later and later every day.Still, better than Genshin and Breath of the Wild!

_childDocuments_.review: It's essentially your online multiplayer version of Genshin Impact open world with Honkai combat. Less polished and janky, but 10x more fun since you can actually play with friends. But the game is developed to be as annoying as can possibly be and hinder progress every step of the way to the point where you have to fight tooth and nail for every combat score to even progress through the game.Global release got shoved 10 months worth of content from the Chinese release within the span of 3 months with no compensation to gear up with the speed we were leveling at. At the beginning the game's progress was time gated and every few days and you would get a few more levels so day one players were leveling at a controlled pace and had breathing room to gear up but when we reached around the level 50-70 mark, any new players who just started were given a 500% exp boost to help catch them up but by doing that the devs actively ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over all those players because to even kill a single open world mob would feel like fighting a world boss. So you would have a ton of level 50-60s that can barely kill an open world trash mob let alone do end game content queue up for the level 50-60 dungeons that would give you the best gear available because why would anyone in their right minds want to waste their limited resources and queue for the dungeons that are recommended for their actual combat scores of like 7360 that only drops blue tier gear when they can just queue for the level 60 ones that will drop legendary gear but have the recommended combat score be 39900. It was a huge oversight and probably one of the worst new player experience I've seen in an MMO. New players will just have to queue up and hope there's a whale who will carry them or bite the bullet and do the lower level content to not overcap on their resources.But when the game has to rely on whales to help carry the majority of the playerbase because the devs failed to properly tune player progression. I don't see this game thriving if the new player experience is this bad. It'll just be another typical gacha to pull in a few whales, make a quick buck and call it a day which is a shame.tl;dr Decent mmo with a fun combat system that you can actually play with friends. It's just plagued by gacha and clueless devs.

Additionally, I have not spent a single dollar on this game and I don't feel like I'm at a disadvantage for it.I do have 2 gripes: the vehicles get stuck on EVERYTHING. You can't even drive over a bush and if you try, you'll get stuck and have to back up and go around. Not only can you not drive over anything, it basically has to be feet away from you or you'll get stuck on it. The second is that weapon set swapping can't be done in battle and there's no easy way to switch sets out of combat. You basically have to observe your enemy and swap weapon sets before you get near them. This might seem like a no brainer but the puzzles in the game require their own weapon sets so say you're out farming puzzles and run into enemies, you're stuck using whatever weapons you were using on the puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: Overall the game has great gameplay and a lot of exploring to do. However I have to give it a downvote due to a lot of problems. - The game is extremely buggy. Cutscenes are for absolutely no reason either skipping or bugging a lot. During cutscenes the characters most of the times talk on top of each other, skipping the cutscene and making it unbearable to watch. The story is already mid as it is but this bugs are making things worse. I reached vera and most people tell you that the story doesn't have this bugs around there. Let me tell you some. That was a damn lie. The same things happened even further on. - Gacha is very bad. The game bombards you with pulls after clearing zones however the reason for that is because the gacha is extremely bad and unforgiving in this game. I did over 500 yellow pulls, 200 red ones and not even once I got an SSR without the pity. Out of all the pulls you almost NEVER get an SSR unless you hit the 80 pity mark. The problem is that pity also gives you something random which can be copies for a character that you don't even like or use (got 4 copies of the same character I don't like instead of different ones for more play style). Another problem is that at some point you won't be able to get as many pulls after clearing the game. You either get lucky enough to get good characters that you like or you have to completely reset the account if you end up with colossal bad luck like me.- There's also bugs while travelling around the map. Invisible fall dmg even though you don't hit the ground from a high place and completely die, using a mount sometimes glitches you for no reason. If you pass by a single small rock that somehow manages to glitch you, it keeps teleporting you back constantly until you either travel to a waypoint or you waste a relic cd to get out of the spesific spot which is also really annoying. Bosses glitch you as well. Fought the Aesperia boss in story to finish the planet and somehow I completely glitched out of the map while jumping after her and had to completely restart the mission cause I couldn't get back in or use the unstuck option. I could do dmg either.I did some research and apparently most of this bugs have been around for quite some time yet the developers still didn't fix anything. All I can say, if you are the type to like gameplay, you might like this but other than that I don't really recommend this game for someone that likes stories and doesn't wanna bother with annoying bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always almost instinctively shied away from free-to-play gacha MMOs of this sort, given my personal history of loving the heck out of games like Final Fantasy XI which only ever reward you for effort put in rather than what's in your bank account. I decided to set aside my prejudice and give this game a shot at the invitation of a friend, and I haven't regretted it. It's quite pretty visually. It's a good deal of fun to play as the combat is simple enough yet engaging enough to be entertaining and the game seems to take significant inspiration from Breath of the Wild in terms of exploration and gathering/cooking mechanics, which I like quite a bit. The story is engaging so far and I'm rather excited to log back in and keep playing, which is more than I can say for some games I've paid for years of subscription to (looking at you, WoW). My only gripe might be that I wish there was more customization in terms of clothing appearance, as I'm a pretty big glamour addict in FFXIV and was a transmog addict in WoW once upon a time. I even go pretty far out of my way for /lockstyle outfits in FFXI. I'd say give it a shot if you have enough self control not to spend all of your money on gacha pulls.

_childDocuments_.review: Background: Played ToF since global release. Played Genshin Impact since 1.0. Dabble in some other games, but not much times in MMO's (lost ark, FFXIV)Overall: don't start. Honestly, if I could go back and never start the game, I probably would. The honeymoon effect (prevalent in basically every other gacha in existence) is pretty strong compared to the normal gameplay cycle. Do not expect to do serious dmg as a F2P. English localization is clearly neglected, the UI is made for mobile, the UX is abhorrent. Combat: 2.5/5. Decent skill expression in gameplay mechanics (e.g. "perfect" dodges), although the weapon elements don't really react with each other. As such, mono element teams are currently the most resource efficient, until you run into combat that arbitrarily has "65% frost resist" and greatly reduced energy gain, etc. You'll either take a massive fat L until the resisted element changes, or you have to switch to weapons you haven't invested in. Combat relics are fun (similar to Genshin gadgets, but much more diverse), but they take a while to acquire.Leveling on the other hand, is sad. You can be overleveled, since overworld combat scales with your player level, and your enemies will get stronger faster than you can get better gear. It's a sad feeling to use your weapon discharge burst on a wild boar. If you're anything less than a monthly/BP spender (<$15/mo), you will have to be carried through group combat. And who would want to rely on a whale to get on just so you can get better-than-copium rewards? It's fun the first time, annoying for the 10th week.Story: 1.5/5. Honestly, I get where the devs wanted to take the story. The execution however, is terribly rushed. You meet a character 5 minutes in, spend 10 minutes with them, and are apparently supposed to care about them for the rest of the story of this game. Story NPC's sound like google TTS. Skip button is there, until it isn't. Hell, even loading screen art spoils the story. If you've had the misfourtune to read/watch Isekai Cheat Magician, this is worse.UI/UX: 2/5. Obviously this game was made first for Asian mobile markets, but even worse is the fact that this game is unplayable on controller (not all abilities are mapped to a controller button). Some menus can only be accessed through Alt-hold+cursor click. PC controls still mention "tap anywhere on the screen". Text overlaps with UI elements. Mandarin is still present in sub-menus and gameplay mode descriptions even when the game language is set to English. Text chat doesn't work in certain *group* game modes, so you can't even request team buffs that the one random is hogging. If you hate Genshin's red [!] when you didn't want to C6 your Benny, oh boy there's 5 times as many here, and they keep on popping up a couple minutes after you dismiss them.Endgame: 2/5. The thing that keeps players going back to online live-service games is the gameplay loop. In ToF, it looks like: Doing your 4 dailies, spending your vitality (time limited resource), and doing the myraid of weekly activities. While at first it may be a breath of fresh air from Genshin, beneath the facade of choice is the sameness of it all: Do little things here and there, and beat up a buffed boss that is either a punching bag (Void Rifts), is a beefcake that will one shot you (Frontier Clash hard bosses), or is simply a chore (Artificial Island base combat; the boars simply won't die in any reasonable time). You get better resources, gear upgrade materials, but for what?Developers: 1/5. Literally Tencent, under different names they own. For spenders, Chinese markets get better rewards for their money. For customer service, it's abhorrent when you really need it. 2FA doesn't exist, so make your game account under anything but your email account. Hackers topping leaderboards is a very common sight, and hackers stealing other player's inventories has happened *multiple* times. Honestly, many other people have touched on this topic. Gacha: 2/5. Compared to Genshin Impact, it's better in a couple respects, and worse in other aspects. A single copy of an limited banner SSR (Genshin equivalent: 5 star) is inferior to a standard banner SSR with a couple copies. One healer (zero) doesn't even heal until you get your first duplicate, while some limiteds aren't even worth rolling for unless you're going to get 3 or even 6 duplicates. Rolls are relatively easier to come by, but the rates outside of guarantees feel much lower. The honeymoon will have you excited because you got your first SSR after spending less than 30 standard rolls until you realize that is hard coded for your first time. 80 rolls will get you to a 50/50, but there is no 100% until you roll 120 times *on a single limited banner*. Matricies (Genshin equivalent: weapons) are the second banner you can roll on, and they're just as bait-y, if not more. Weapons can hold 4 matricies, 40 matrix rolls gets you one. Realistically, you'll need to roll 160 times for a complete set. Events: 1/5. Do not expect genshin-like events, with a mini story and unique combat. Either they're daily log in for extra rolls, double rewards when you spend your vitality, or beat up overworld bosses to spend in an event shop for you guessed it, rolls and materials. Can't forget the literal gachapons (in a gacha game no less!), where they bait you with a character skin, but realistically you'll need to deplete the gachapon pool for the equivalent of $100/60 limited banner rolls.2.0 (steam release) was supposed to be the big thing to improve the game, but honestly I'm just seeing more of the same.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a serial gacha game enthusiast. I play multiple gacha games and I spend hundreds/thousands of dollars on gacha games each month. I am a "whale". My experiences are vastly different compared to a F2P player. I also play on NA Solaris. I believe it to be the most populated NA server. It has majority of the ToF streamers and content creators.To sum up Tower of Fantasy in one word: I've been playing since the day 1 global release back in early August. I have had a ton of fun playing this game. I play it for multiple hours a day and have never missed a day. I have done almost every piece of content in this game up to this current 2.0 update/Steam release. Everything except PvP. I will never play PvP in any gacha game even If I am a whale. In my opinion, I believe ToF as a F2P game does a pretty good job to keep you interested and engaged with a huge amount of content. I often get asked why don't I just go play Genshin Impact? Well, its a simple answer. Tower of Fantasy does things that Genshin doesn't do. To start, it has a pretty decent character creator. I love character creation in any game. I could spend hours on most character creators. To be honest, ToF's character creation surprised me the most. It has more depth to it than I originally thought. It's not as robust as Phantasy Star Online 2 but Its not so simple either. Another thing I really appreciate about ToF is the fact that it is a "". The activities in this game are centered around group play. I can meet with people in the overworld doing world bosses then I can add them and party up to do a joint operation (dungeon). Even if majority of people don't chat in this game, I just enjoy how lively it can feel. Another thing that sets the two apart for me would be the fluidity of the movement and combat. I enjoy the ability to dodge, double jump, use relics, and just have more control over my combos. The phantasia system (timed dodge before a attack to slow time around you) is just the cherry on top. Sometimes everything just works out and you just end up having a really satisfying flashy anime-esque fight.(To be completely fair, I have not played Genshin Impact since the global closed beta test before its launch. My experience of the game should be completely different to how it plays now.)I listed my favorite aspects, well, what are the downsides you ask? It's listed as a MMORPG on Steam but I can tell you this is a gacha game through and through. There's no point sugarcoating it. You will have a much easier/enjoyable time if you spend money in this game. You will outperform majority of players in basically every aspect. For example, I can outheal, outdamage, and outtank every F2P player even if I am not playing the healer role or tank role. I can buy more vitality potions to keep refreshing my vitality instead of having to wait hours to continue farming content. I can farm more content because I have more than one strong elemental team. The game just fully unlocks for you if you are a whale. I wouldn't say its impossible to do content as a F2P player, it just takes more effort and more time. You think your only paywall is characters/weapons & gear progression? Guess again. Another thing locked behind paywalls would be cosmetics. Going forward, majority of the new accessories and outfits released will be locked behind another gacha or just paid in a bundle/battlepass. These aren't cheap either. So far as of the time of this review, global has had two additional outfits locked behind gacha events. The odds of rolling the featured outfit is extremely low. Majority of players would need to clear the entire gacha event inventory to get the outfit. How much does it cost? A whopping $150 USD for an outfit that does nothing for you besides make you stand out a bit more from the F2P crowd. There are very few events that will reward you with cosmetics for free.As a whale, these issues don't bother me. I just swipe my card to overcome these hurdles. My biggest problem with this game is the amount of bugs there are. This game has a ton of bugs. It's always has. Its just a huge shame that the devs decided to launch the game as is and not include all the QoL features and fixed bugs the 2.0 update delivered in the original CN server. There were so many bugs that have been around since launch that have only just been resolved now. Months later. Its unacceptable to just keep these bugs in the game until a major content update.The only bugs that they prioritize fixing are bugs that affect their revenue. The bugs do get annoying but I have not come across a single gamebreaking bug since day 1. Most bugs that occur are just graphical/audio glitches and the really really terrible English localization. When I say terrible English localization, I mean it. There were so many submenus and important text that were just copy and pasted from the Chinese server that were never translated. Majority of them have been fixed now but now a few new ones appeared. There are cutscenes that are out of sync with the audio/video and are just riddled with framerate lag. This should not happen on my beefy PC setup. I play with Japanese dubbing because I'm a filthy weeb. 80% of the time a name is said, it does not match the name spelled on screen. For example, in 2.0, you meet a character named "Shelly". The voice actors/actresses call her Cecily. Its a minor mistranslation but this is just a single example. A more disruptive example would be the fact that characters will start a new dialogue line before their voice has the chance to finish the previous sentence.The only bugs that I've come across every so often that actually affects gameplay have to deal with teleportation. One is when I try to teleport to a new location and my character does the animation to dial in the new coordinates and nothing happens. I just keep looping the animation over and over until I select the location again on my map. A minor bug but annoying time consuming bug. The next one is more disruptive. There are times when I use Crow's double daggers and use his teleportation dash combos and I noclip into the side of a hill/cliff/wall and I just teleport and load across the map. Usually very far from my original location. Again, very annoying.There are many things that could improve this game but at the end of the day, it all depends if the developers of Hotta Studios can actually deliver what the community wants. My main gacha game was a game that didn't have any pity in it at all so this game has just been terrific for my wallet. I am an avid player and I will likely continue playing this game for quite awhile.P.S. Please for the love of god, Hotta Studios, toggle the option to turn off the splash screen intro. It is the most ear bleed inducing loudest intro I have heard in a long time. My ears have bled every day since launch. Gacha game is a gacha game but multiplayer poggers.

_childDocuments_.review: People tend to hate on this game because they say it's a clone of Genshin Impact, but it's actually quite different, and better in a lot of ways imo.Genshin is an RPG game with instanced multiplayer, while Tower of Fantasy is an MMO. Their similarities lies in them both being a anime artstyle gacha game.I have played Tower of Fantasy since day one and have logged on every single day to play the game ever since (from their standalone launcher) so will try and give my best takes and both positives and negatives about the game so maybe you will try it, or even avoid it.Positives:The graphics look really nice, with beautiful character design and world creation.You can customize the ''main'' character of the game, to your own liking, with a ton of sliders for bodyparts, hair and even cosmetics which can be earned in-game.Content at a pretty good pace, with a bunch of events to participate in for in-game cosmetics, gacha currency and more.Great rewards for exploring the world and taking the game at your own pace.Combat is okay with beautiful animations and a variety of weapons (easy to obtain as F2P, more on upgrading weapons in the negatives.)When pulling an SSR, you get both a new character you can use instead of your own avatar, and also a new weapon.You can mix and match weapons with certain elements and characters you've gotten in the past, so you're not forced to rock a certain character if you need a weapon with ice element etc. It has a good pity system which means that you are guaranteed a SSR character after 80 rolls, and one of your own choice if too unlucky,  at 120 rolls.The PvP is balanced and not Pay2Win.Soundtrack is really nice balanced and nice on your ears, from soothing while exploring and collecting materials, to pumping and intense while slaying a boss.The game seem to run decently on low-end builds at 60FPS at least, based on my own experience with my budget PC.Progression between PC and mobile phoneNegatives:It is a gacha game, so expect some pay2win. Every weapon has 6 stars, and when you first get a new weapon, it is at 0 stars, which means you would need the same weapon from gacha 7 times, which would take you a very long time to save up for as a F2P player. This only really applies to limited banners, because you will eventually get 6 star weapons from the ''normal'' banner by just playing, but if a weapon from the limited banner seems interesting to you, good luck trying to max it without spending  money or saving currency for years.Matrices, items that essentially makes your weapon or element of a certain type stronger, is in a seperate gacha, while also having limited time banners.A stamina system that makes certain types of content in the game limited, mainly XP grinding for equipment and weapons.Cutscenes come across as buggy and voices of characters are almost never in sync. Some servers are filled with non english speakers, even when selecting europe, so be careful that you find a server where people in the world chat speak or even understand english (I play on estrela and there are 98% russians.)Sometimes connection errors, although not sure if it's being me or a common issue. I would recommend you trying the game out yourself to see if it's something for you. I have had a ton of fun in this game which is why I wanted to write a review here on Steam, hopefully bringing in some new players!

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a mobile game for Steam. Decent time waster. 2 hours in and still getting ridiculously long, unskippable, hyper boring, drowsy, tutorial chunks. If you can't explain the basis of a game to the point that it's playable in 15 minutes or less and by just moving forward and learning as you go, maybe your game isn't setup properly. Let me play the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. If I wanted to read a novel or listen to one I'd go buy a book or listen to audible.Beyond that, a few additional notes1 : Enemy Balancing is horrible. In a zone where you have say level 15 enemies, they'll suddenly start outleveling you. Or being your level and taking eons to kill with fully upgraded weapons.2 : Dungeon difficulty makes no sense. A dungeon that you went through on the first difficulty with zero problem at level 40, the moment you switch it to "normal" difficulty it becomes something that is impossible without a party of people. 3 : There is >too much< going on. Every time you open a chest you have a million red pings in your submenus that you have to go to individually to clear. There should be a collect all/clear all option or something. This is infuriating especially for people who like their HUD clean.4 : There is an issue with mission tracking. Say you want to go to a dungeon location. You'll get halfway there and the mission tracking ping will just vanish. You have to go back through the multi-menu process of selecting that dungeon again to get the ping back on your map.5 : Equipment upgrading feels horrible. You'll upgrade a weapon/armor piece several times and notice little to no change in it's effectiveness.6 : Storyline is all over the place. It'll take you from one map location to the next and then you'll be circling that area for about an hour before suddenly you're back to the other location and the storyline splits causing you to need to run back and forth between the areas. It's irritating to say the least. 7 : Dialog is bad. While the voice acting is good many words are mispronounced and horrid grammar is all over the place. If you actually don't hit the Skip button (which only appears after you listen to two lines of dialog at every single interaction) and listen it's a laughable situation honestly. This game has no real clear direction. It's like it can't decide if it wants to be a Mobile Game or a PC game. It also can't decide if it wants to be it's own MMO or if it wants to copy Genshin Impact. It can't decide if it wants to be a hack and slash or an MMO. Because of this it suffers from the harmful effects of having a huge identity crisis where it just feels sloppy, messy, and jumbled together. It's like the developers took every single idea that people in the think-tank that came up with this and just shoved them into the game with no regard for what went where, just that it was in the game. This could be good but it really needs everything mapped out and polished up better. Of course the game is F2P with the option of buying items in game (and don't get me wrong they do a good job making F2P not feel like a punishment) but the game really, really, needs some clarity adjustments done before anyone should feel tempted to actually spend money on it. Right now it's just, really, a mess. A pretty nice looking, decent feeling mess....but a mess nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty sure I have over 500 hours in this game at this point, playing every day since release and as a F2P I could get into top100 rankings on my servers so I think I'm doing good.This games premise and it's core is good, it's satisfying when it works, but oh boi does it NOT work majority of times. First of all, if you decide to start playing after launch, be ready to for an absolutely awful experience. Always weak, not able to do most of coop because nobody plays it and you can't solo carry it, the only catch up mechanic for new players is getting 500% more EXP, sounds great, doesn't it? Only if levels gave meaningful power, they are only there as gate for content that you have to do to gain power and as a new player, you won't be able to do this content when you unlock it because you gain levels way too fast and not actual power. Oh and I was even holding the worst about levels untill now, enemies strenght scales with your level, so leveling up fast means the enemies get stronger than you because they are getting so much more stats with each level than you. If you want to somehow catch up to current players, you need to get carried everyday and also spend, I don't believe there's any other way. But how does my experience look like so far and what can you expect if you somehow catch up? Bugs. I saw bugs, more bugs and again bugs (for clarification, a bug for me is anything that doesn't seem to work properly) Graphic bugs, hitbox bugs on every weapon, mobs with junky hitboxes and the worst in PVP where melee weapons can hit you while you fly 20 meters above them (Meryl spin), bosses that can only count as one giant bug (Interdimensional Dragon), the most annoying bug so far that I'm pretty sure is still not fixed and is happening for the last 2 weeks is players that want to join an instance in a 4 player dungeon or 8 player raid just randomly get disconnect and are not able to connect for half an hour, some had it good and only got disconnected a couple of times in a week, some players say they get disconnected over 5 times a day.The gameplay was never challenging so far, it looks like the devs idea of challenge or harder difficulty is giving mobs 3 times more health, boom it's hard now, go and fight that timer after which you fail. Atleast it does seem to change now with the new big expansion (except for a big flying whale that you can't target with 99% of weapons, impossible to do when you are not maxing that weapon or abusing bugs).Okay since I started this by stating I'm doing good as a F2P, people reading this for sure wonder how it looks in terms of balance, resources, materials and the most important thing, getting the waifus. I have higher standards than a typical casual, if you want to feel strong in this game as a F2P, be ready to give away your life, your soul, your friendships, your grass touching, all that for the grind. I have not played Genshin, but my friend tells me it's 1 hour at most and you are done with dailies, If anyone cares how does my day look if I do it mostly optimally (note I have bad PC so long loading screens): 4 daily missions taking me around 25 minutes for all, minigames in Aesperia another 15 minutes, 3-4 JO runs (4 player dungeons) each around 25 minutes counting in queue times (if you don't fail any of them), 15 minutes for mini games in Mirroria, 6 Grayspace exploration (limited daily exploration) each taking me over 10 minutes to get to and make, in total over 3 and a half hours. This is only dailies not counting in things that you can do whenever during the week like raids, bygone, wormhole, frontier clash, void rifts and the most time sucking world exploration. All of that and this games does feel like it's F2P friendly. But don't get me wrong, P2Ws are still much stronger than you and you won't be able to get every single limited character no matter what. I'm not a gacha player and this games predatory system sickens me, I can't believe how people are able to spend 150 dollars on a RNG slot machine to get a single or maybe 2 cosmetic items, getting a single limited character with just money and in time would be around 150 dollars as well. I get that games have to make money, but atleast in my opinion this is just too expensive for really basic stuff, not even something extraordinery.I have one good thing to say, devs atleast try to make the game more balanced and more player friendly (except for the real money prices) on global compared to Chinese servers. For example limited characters are weaker making standard characters fall out less, the new gear is universal instead of one for each element making it easier to get a good one (so getting a flame engine with frost attack doesn't happen, you only need to get the right elemental attack once).I'm not good at reviews so I'm wrap this up with this:I hope this game becomes better, I like to play it, but there's a ♥♥♥♥ ton of problems I can't ignore and the game is completely unpolished in many aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: My expectations were low, but holy crap.I knew what I was getting into when downloading this game, both with it being a gacha game and with the general perception of ToF being a Genshin Impact clone. And I've played both Genshin as well as other gacha games before. But I did not expect to be bombarded this much with tabs upon tabs of menus, calendars, rewards, events, shops, currency exchanges, and so on, nor did I expect this game to require access to the registry editor for some reason. It feels extremely predatory.I think what would summarize my experience the most is clunkiness and bloat. I say this knowing that gamedev is hard and that the devs are working in the kind of monetization culture where the goal is to confuse the user into spending money, but man... Somehow mechanics get both overexplained and underexplained; you get items and you won't even notice; the freedom of movement is there but only on paper since none of the movement options feel smooth, and in some cases, they feel like they don’t even work properly. Apparently, as of the time of writing, the game is in its 3.5 version, yet within the first hour or so, I glitched into geometry and T-posed. I got unstuck without using the unstuck option, but it's still an early sign of what was to come.To the game's credit, the first world and what I got to see of the second one do look nice and do give you the feeling of some wonder and like you'd want to explore them, but you're not really given tools to do that. And again, don't get me wrong, there's plenty of tools to move around; you get to walk, run, dash, jump, double jump, air dash, fly with your jetpack, use the grappling hook, use some biome-specific traversal options, ride a bike, and so on. I have never felt like I had so many options to move around, yet I wanted to use none of them. Most of them are artificially limited in some way, feel somehow both slow and too sensitive, or are simply buggy. The multitude of traversal options and the fact that they simply don't feel satisfying to use results in the world seeming smaller and emptier than it actually is.The only two ladders I tried using simply did not work (you get clipped out when you're done climbing), grappling into the ground sometimes damages you and sometimes doesn't, and most animations cancel into each other, so you can sometimes just plop out of your grapple, which can be useful but just feels bad. Another thing is that none of the movement options feel like they have any momentum. I was legitimately confused about the bike being faster than your run since it just simply feels slower. This point applies to the fights too, but I'm getting ahead of myself here. All around, it's just kind of wild; it somehow copied the climbing formula from Breath of the Wild and Genshin Impact but didn't get the memo about it feeling good or being used as a dynamic element in the whole traversal thing; it somehow introduced a grappling hook that is fast and precise but also unwieldy and clunky. While I'm at it, the game is kind of a bugfest, and the optimization leaves a little to be desired. What's more interesting, though, is how it handles client-server side stuff. It appears as though there's some rollback or desync when you lag. I lagged once when grappling, and after it stopped lagging, the game thought I had already reached my destination and simply dropped me to the ground.I think the main issue is that it just all lacks impact, no pun intended. The attack animations look flashy, but it's only surface level because there's no pacing in them; the bike is relatively fast, but the animations don't do anything to indicate or support that; the cutscenes are dynamic but are all over the place (I honestly felt a QTE incoming at any time during the first few cutscenes; they really felt messy, and my brain interpreted that as "you'll need to do a thing in just a second." They gave off that Uncharted or Tomb Raider vibe in this sense, but probably not in the way the developer might have wanted); you get more and more powerful by the literal second, but everything is just spongy and weak and barely interactive, it feels like.I've got to give props for the character creator, though; it's genuinely one of the better, if not the best, in the gacha genre. It's probably the most fun I've had in this game, apart from poking fun at it with a friend during our session. The coop experience also felt a bit better than what other gacha games offer. There's some QoL improvements if you're coming over from Genshin Impact, namely a dedicated button for consuming healing items or food, quick equip of items from alt click, a cutscene skip button if you're not particularly interested in the story, and probably some others. I don't think they fix the overall experience, but they are nice. The game looks good enough, and I really enjoyed some of the enemy designs, like the little goblin guys or the octopi with arms instead of tentacles. The same goes for the environments; I really like the desert planet. I won't say much about the story since it didn't really grip me in the first few moments. I played it with a friend and just didn't really pay attention much, and I kind of completely lost interest when the game threw me between NPCs right next to each other over and over for consequential cutscenes and dialogues. I really dislike when the game doesn't value your time or attention like this.At the end of the day, this game offers very little to players like me, and it just all feels cheap, surface-level, undercooked, and overdesigned. Honestly, I feel like it doesn't even do the FOMO thing right. It doesn't even sneak up on you, it simply bombards you with options, hoping something sticks. I am severely and utterly disappointed, especially since there's some potential here, especially in the visuals department.My playtime may be low, and there may be interesting content, experiences to be had, and a decent story later on, but I don’t think the game has much to offer in the meantime, especially to a new player. If 4 or so hours is not enough for a game to get decent, I won’t play the thousands it will need to get good; there’s experiences I’d rather have out there.To wrap it all up, this game made me write a review for the first time, and that's something. I know this is a lot of ranting, and while I dislike this game a good chunk, I honestly hope the developers turn it around into something good at some point. It's not a completely uninteresting product, and there's talent utilized here.Have a nice day, y'all o7

_childDocuments_.review: Tower of Fantasy pulls you into a visually stunning world that feels as if it could rival any top-tier open-world game out there. The graphics are truly breathtaking, with vibrant environments, rich textures, and attention to detail that make exploring a joy. It’s no secret that Tower of Fantasy borrows quite a bit from Genshin Impact, but that’s not a downside. In fact, it incorporates many of the beloved features of its predecessor while adding its own unique twist and even streamlining several functions, making gameplay smoother.The combat system is flexible, allowing you to build and customize your characters and weapon combinations in ways that feel personal and strategic. While certain weapons are undoubtedly more powerful, the game still offers enough flexibility that you can tailor your characters to your preferred play style without feeling forced to follow a meta. Progression is fast-paced, and that’s a good thing considering there’s no server transfer for scores, so you want to get through the early content quickly and efficiently.One thing I found missing is a cooking or fishing minigame, which feels like a bit of a missed opportunity. These types of casual features would have added a relaxing side activity to break up the high-energy combat and exploration. For fans of fan service, there’s plenty here; the game features a largely female cast, and many of the characters are designed with bold, revealing outfits that are quite eye-catching (although this may not be everyone’s cup of tea).The story itself is straightforward, and while it can feel like you're breezing through bosses, it’s accessible and makes progression feel fast. However, the side quests can sometimes feel redundant, with a lot of backtracking and running from point A to point B, occasionally dragging on even with the help of fast-travel.Lastly, the community stands out as a positive aspect of Tower of Fantasy. Players are welcoming and eager to help out, partly because they’re rewarded with in-game resources, but the vibe is genuinely supportive. And for those looking for a game with staying power, there’s engaging late-game content to keep you coming back even after the main story wraps up.

_childDocuments_.review: So; this is my second account due to the nature of the game and RNG that are Gacha games. Having played ~400 hours in total, I believe I have an informed enough opinion and can see the general direction of the game from this point having played from day 1. Flame me if you want, or tell me to post it on Reddit. I don't care, the Reddit Mods remove any posts that even remotely criticize the game.Bugs;Lots. And Lots. Of Bugs. Very few fixes and more time spent monetizing things. Plenty of other reviews have gone over a better curated list, but the most recent being bugged Suppressor levels.Roles;This game features Tank, DPS and Healing roles as a large focal point for content. Due to the nature of the game and how power is, Tank and Healers are completely irrelevant. Whales can carry and solo any content, which is nice from a F2P stand point, but really, REALLY bad for everything else. The fact that there's built in DPS meters to show you exactly how far behind you are from paid players is massively discouraging. Another problem is being a Tank or Healer (if you choose to do those roles or you get REALLY unlucky pulling) is the damage. DPS characters do amazing values, where as tanks and healers are just shafted, taking ages to kill anything even on open world at your level.Gear;Gear is basically the same as Artifacts from Genshin. If you don't know what that is, then allow me to explain. Each piece of gear can roll 4 lines from a curated list. Completely random, it means gear that is actually good for your role is hard to come by. Not including the rarity value of gear from end-game content. It's so low that it's absurd. Sure, there's a pity to get a piece, but when you use a limited resource for a sub 2% chance to drop a piece, it's not well designed.Monetization;The game started a bit monetized as all Gacha does, and considering that other games like this have paid options, the game is only becoming paid options. "Events" either cater to whales or spending money while the rest of the game is in shambles. The care for F2P options is becoming less and less.Events;These events... they offer amazing rewards. Let's face it, they're great. The problems being, unless you're a whale or you can manage to get on within the specific window that events run at (which is typically a few hours a day, ONCE a day) you won't be able to fill out or even participate. Outfits and cosmetics are tied to these events, making F2P options non-existent.Optional Game Modes;Much like the events with their limited time windows, Break from Destiny (Battle Royale) and PvP are tied to a limited time window to play them. They seemed to have dropped these additional game modes to keep game play fresh, but were immediately forgotten about. Really bad Lag and bugs make these game modes unplayable.Relics;Oh boy. These things are... REALLY Good actually. I can't honestly say anything bad about them. Enjoy the click bait because I really enjoy how relics work in this game and how they function.RNG;So! Earlier I mentioned Roles. This is completely random as for what roles you can get. Your pulls from Gacha dictate what you can run reasonably, and if you have terrible luck, enjoy the tank or healer life. If there was a mild way to sway RNG to go for a specific role or weapon, it'd be fine. But since most of the weapons are tied to limited banners and the basic weapons are pretty spread as for roles, you can't be sure what you get.All in all, if you enjoy this game, you do you. Keep playing and keep enjoying what the game has to offer, because the combat and exploration are actually enjoyable. Everything else is just... bad. There's a reason we get no new players. And it's not because the game doesn't have advertisements or good graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: Tower of Fantasy has always had mixed feedback. It tried to market itself as a "Genshin killer", but was later mocked for falling short and the surplus of bugs at launch. My playtime is much higher than Steam suggests (usually play in non-steam version). Basically I've played every day since launch. It was quite fun. Battle system is fast paced, gacha system seems fair, and for a while it seemed to fix many of the issues I had with Genshin which caused me stop playing. After playing both Genshin, I had more fun playing ToF with the the fast paced nature, even if Genshin has many elements that make it overall a better game. But here's the thing. The dev just do whatever they want and it becomes increasingly apparent the game is simply a money grab. * 99% characters are excessively big-boobed waifus. Virtually no male characters, and the ones that do exist are no longer relevant. Characters are teased and never added. * Powercreep is exponential, leaving no real incentive for investing in characters. The game launch talked some heavy game about keeping balance, but balance no longer exists. There's zero reason to A6 a character when it's lifespan is a handful of weeks and the next generation has a 40-60% gain on the previous. * After initial exploring, rewards are lackluster, especially to the cost of everything. For a game marketed as a "f2p", it's anything but. I don't mind the paid element, in fact I've spent several hundred. But the value of everything has decreased over time. You do get TONS of standard pulls. I'm sure i've done 2000+ from the free elements of the game, but the issue is standard characters are thoroughly useless, minus some niche situations (and needing a healing comp). * Devs decided to merge all the servers which caused splits among the playerbase. Some are happy to be able to play with friends on other servers. For many others, there's name issues, congestion issues, and language issues. World chat full of toxic players, to where it has to be fully muted and completely ignored. All sense of community is lost. There's no more recognition of a familiar face. Just a sea of faces.* Leaderboards, as expected, are exclusive to day 1 leviathans. The power difference between low end players and high end players is astronomical. The difference between high end players and leviathans/giga-whales, and whales is also astronomical, making the difference between a low end player and a leviathan laughable. * The game is expensive. Which falls back to the other points. Powercreep and low rewards disincentivize investment.I've played this game for hundreds of hours over the last year. Despite some of the technical flaws, it was a lot of fun. But the game is devolving. It no longer has it's luster. I want to like and recommend this game, but I fail to find reasons to.

_childDocuments_.review: I was highly anticipating this game while playing the Beta and once released it was fun for the first few weeks. If you're someone who wants to play TOF after getting burnt out of Genshin Impacts daily repetition and slow updates, this game will give you exactly what you want until it doesn't. The main issue with TOF is that if you aren't going to open your wallet, you will never be a top player. This may not be an issue for some however you may not even be able to beat most content without hard carries. There are clans for this reason and it isn't necessarily hard to find willing people however being on the lower end and dependent on others can feel quite burdening and imo would get boring fast. if you decide to open up your wallet (or if you are f2p and save for months), prepare to be spending anytime a new character drops because there is insane power creep in this game and compared to a game like Genshin where even 4 star characters are viable and frankly- some even OP - til endgame, the SRs in this game will immediately be discarded and never used again. If youre f2p this creates a problem where you will pretty much never have the most optimal team and all your pulls will be focused on your main DPS and getting their copies. Swapping up main DPS later on may not be feasible because it may require a completely new team.Thats not to say all is bad. the combat in this game has a different feel then Genshin but with a lot of the same core mechanics. its easy to learn combos and rotations and personally it felt more smooth and mobile. exploration is also great as far as mobility. Visually and combat wise this game is an ocean but story and puzzle wise, its a puddle.Overall i don't hate this game. It was extremely fun while i was burnt out. if you're looking for that it will do the trick. As for getting really invested, i wouldn't really recommend for F2P
