_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for 6 - 9 months so far. Here is my review: TL;DR - I do not recommend this game as a main MMORPG to any player out there. Breakdown: Community: I always measure community in online games in three forms.Interaction outside of guilds - There is virtually none. What you see is usually the same members of a top 10 guild just post in world chat. Ask a question, you will get an answer, but hardly will anyone play with you. I literally have less than 1% of my total time in this game playing with other people.  Interaction through a friendlist - Almost none due to how content plays out in this game. Interaction through guilds - Joining guilds usually has guild leaders force you into a Discord Server where they get to manipulate and con you out of time, money, energy. Some guilds push you into websites too. Depending on the region, you also deal with the usual jingoism found in SEA guilds. I was surprised at how toxic this game can be. ---------------------------------------------------------Game Strength: This game is story-based. The key to playing this game is to focus only on the story. Luckily you do not need anyone due to the concept of Dimensional Level. Dimensional Level is simply that every creature in the world is set to the same level. This means a player can run through the entire story set to the lowest level and be done with it. If you want Golds, the minimum level in which I have visually seen myself get an SSR weapon has been 55. Once you finish the story, there is actually no point in playing until the game story is updated. The rewards for getting all your gear maxed out and three weapons to six stars is that you can drop the Dimensional Level to 55 and never have to play with anyone again outside the raid content. If all you care about is the story, just never raise the Dimensional Level at all. -------------------------------------------------Events: Events tend to be what I call "Fluff and Grind"Rather than focus your time on how to be most efficient in gaming, the events in this game encourage wasting as much time as possible for little to no returns. Like said earlier, what kind of return to you get if you can already at lowest dimensional level see through the story and the extra content isn't really worth that much?It's a lot of fluff, and worse is that its temporary fluff that gives the illusion of content. Rather than focus on making permanent content. You will regions and that is commendable, but outside of the main story and some exploration to uncover them all, they are really quite empty and even void. ---------------------------------------------------Story I liked the story even though it follows a common ground with a lot of SEA games in which they introduce the player to a female character that ascends to the role of female lead character and then before long, more female characters are introduced in their typical soft-core cute/sexualized form. I am not against it as I like pretty characters, but the system is designed to make males fall in love with a digital female character in hopes males spend their savings on that virtual female character to get maximum power on a weapon and gets some matrices. What this game does is have the female lead character of the story share the role with a regional female lead character. Each region has its top female character that stands above the rest. if anything I approve of is the fact that you do get the different environments. You do get Snow Areas, Desert Areas, Underwater Areas etc....------------------------------------------------------Fashion The initial look of the character is pretty strong in terms of having an identity. This identity goes away with the simulacrum system. Rather than make a unique look for yourself, you can get the look of another character you've unlocked in sacrifice of your own look that is switched on and off. The majority of the fashion is pretty much behind Gatcha, while all your weapons are in a Gatcha. -------------------------------------------Cash Shop The cash shop and in-game interfaces for buying items leave much to be desired. In fact, this was the first game in which its cash shop creeped me out to the point that it encouraged me not to spend a lot on this game. In fact, it feels like visiting some Dark Web site and its not welcoming or friendly.--------------------------------------------Gameplay Combat is fun with some things deliberately copied and replicated from Genshin Impact. However, once you get used to the combat, you will realize that the only way to balance the freedom of combat is to HP-PAD enemies later. You will find that the #1 reason you can't beat an area is not because of your own gameplay ability as you will survive and live, but primarily because they will multiply the HP of enemies to astronomical proportions that you will need a P2W weapon at least in 1 - 3 stars to be able to cause enough damage to win.-----------------------------------------------------Graphic Intensity I like that the graphics are decent and low key. Mirroria uses the most graphic power in the game so far unless that has changed. This is a game I can play on a PC I deliberately set up as a solar power system running as an APU on low settings and it plays fine and under 50w. However, this game can also be cranked up using a high end spec and show decent visuals. However, the scale of visuals on your character is not major from lowest to maximum setting, but affects the environment on a much greater scale. ---------------------------------------------Minimalist Rating This is a game where a player can run dailies very quickly. This is true with weeklies as well.Weeklies are about accumulating 900 points. Once you accumulate 900 points, you get nothing more. Even with 1200 - 1300 points you do not get rewards for anything over 900 points. Once you claim 900 points its best to not login unless you wish to spend your 360 Vitality Points . ---------------------------------------------Personality This is a game where there is a voice actor/actress for the protagonist (your character) which is a welcome change to the whole silent protagonist thing. It gives strength to the story and its welcomed. ---------------------------------------------Warnings: Ipad Warning - I have this on an iPad 8 and it crashes a lot. Most of my other games do not have the problems this game has. Many people have this problem...CCP Warning - Hotta Studio is the Developer of this game. The parent company of Hotta Studio is Perfect World located in Beijing, China. In short, by their authority and government, all companies located in Mainland China regardless of their industry or product answer to the will and demands of the Chinese Communist Party. This means if you wish to stay clear of products that may have their touch and influence upon them, this is a game to skip. I enjoyed the story. Community was non-existent Motivation to play beyond the story as this game lacks a decent endgame is almost non-existent.Its fun to hear how players are willing to spend 500 - 1000 dollars to get a Level 6 weapon in a game one can control the Level Scaling of all enemies and bosses in the world (to the point I can solo world bosses due to Dimensional Level being 55 for me). ----------------------------Conclusion I had my fun with this game and enjoyed the story very much. The story was refreshing for me, and I liked the simple character designs. Outside of that, the game has a lot of fluff to try to hide its largest problem, its design for mobile focuses on a single player design that forces you to play online to finish the story. ------------------------------------Advice: Play through the game at the lowest dimensional level and stay for the story, and then uninstall and go back to your main MMORPG. This game is not main-MMORPG material as its a Gatcha Game. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short, I don't recommend people to play this game.For most people, even if you want to play, don't get too deep with it, as open world and story is still manageable for F2P and low spenders.Now let's dive deeper into it:Before I talk about the bad, let's talk about the good. The way how you move and fight, it got many diversity, you can do some pretty creative thing about it... And speaking of creative, you can also create your own waifu or husbando. Which is good!Now the bad, which mainly goes into these two part: HUGE P2W and bugs.About bug, there are A LOT, memory leak, crashes, RGB textures, black skybox... etc. You name it, there are just too many bugs, very few of them are being fixed and most of them will be reappear after EVERY major update. Even in optimisation and network wise, it's one the worse, FPS drop and desync is very common in regular play.About P2W, oh boy, the latest update literally made part of the game to be whale's playground, F2P and low spenders HAS to be a support (tank and healer), otherwise don't think to do events like VA and OOW. You'll at least need a team of 2 mega whale DPS with one tank and healer, otherwise you ain't even going to get enough damage.You don't want to do it? Hell no, you literally need to do it for A SINGLE PIECE of one of your equipment. (equipment is basically Gensin equivalent of artifact) And plus, you need to do it over and over, because you need to fight multiple times to get a single one AND there are a lots of RNG on substat rolls.This part is basically either get extremely lucky or pay a lot.In summary, play casually or use your entire life saving.Or, don't touch it.Edit: Since someone in the comment has doubt about the P2W element, I will make short answer to that and reinforce my statement about P2W with the following point: Roles, Weapons, Matrices and Equipment. For the sake of giving the sense of how bad it is, I will sometimes use Genshin for comparing, which is also wildly consider bad of some of it's department.About how F2P and low spenders are able to clear hardest content now, it is basically in these two situation... 1. That F2P or low spender player are very lucky, getting insane equipment sub stats and good weapon/matrices pulls.2. Whales are getting better and better on time, hard carrying majority of population of F2P and low spender players, hence giving the illusion of difficulty is good enough.I would agree that giving more time will make people have easier time, but look, for some F2P and low spender that has below average luck like me, we sometimes even have difficulty to clear JO10/11 on time (with full team) without a whale helping. That's regular farming for equipment and standard matrices, to make everyone to actually able to clear hardest content like OOW and VA normally may need like half year or so, and by that time, new hardest content would've been released already.The idea to have whale to carry us at all time is just... weird.In tof, there are Attack, Fortitude and Benediction role, for the sake of ease of understanding, I will call them DPS, tank and healer.DPS is for the role that deals damage, typical whales' role that requires a lots of investment and luck.Healer is the role that heals people, in tof, heals are scale based out of ATK and able to crit, therefore healers will have same build as a DPS. In that sense, healers still requires a decent amount of investment which has their weapons at higher Advancement (basically Constellation in Genshin) with full 4pc of their matrices.Tank is the role for survival... of yourself. In tof, enemies often has AoE attacks that will usually hit many players, which could make 'taking damage for you team' to be non-existent. It's aggro nature is currently most useful for Gaia, since as tank, if you got it's aggro and run around it, Gaia will not attack at all. However aggro is usually attracted by player who deal the most damage, therefore tanks usually have struggle to keep aggro on themselves due to their (usually) low recharge and damage. The only actual goods from tank is the bonus shatter and it's pretty F2P friendly due to equipment would usually roll to resistance and HP.Weapons are Genshin equivalent of characters. While it looks good on surface, which it has lower pity counter and you can exchange the limited (or standard if you are pulling standard banner) weapon directly from shop if you pulled enough. However there are some catch:- Most SR (basically 4* in Genshin) weapons are useless, while Bai Ling and Ene are probably the only weapon that is still consider as relevant.- You could lose 50/50 for indefinite times.- Weapons usually doesn't have full kit without any advancement, therefore you will usually need to get the same weapon twice to be functional.Even though it has bad, however due to tof is very generous for giving out free pulls, especially free weapons pulls. Therefore this part is actually equal to Genshin.Just keep it in mind you better save 240 pulls before each banner.Matrices are Genshin equivalent of weapons. It's consider as one of the worse design in tof due to these:- For SSRs, you need to pull for at least two of them to make it work, four of them on 'full potential'.- You cannot get an extra currency for shop even if you already own that matrix already.- There is a high chance that you will get a same piece too many times to be consider as waste, which could make you unable to get or buff the set bonus.- All SRs are irrelevant due to their max level are way lower than SSRs.- All SRs only have 3pc bonus while SSRs has 2pc and 4pc bonus.- You could lose 50/50 for indefinite times, just like weapon banner.- For DPS, standard matrices usually able to utilize the 2pc bonus (with very few exception), while there are not much matrix choice for Healer and Tank.There are not many free pulls for matrices, therefore if you say Genshin weapon banner is a scam, then tof matrix banner is a head on robbery.Equipment are Genshin equivalent of artifact. In both game, it's consider as the worse design in the game. (all example will use 5* artifact/SSR equipment)For genshin, you have to worry about these:- In each artifact domain, you need 20 and you will get at least 1 of 5* artifact.- Choose which artifact domain you need to farm- Which one of the two artifact set you get- Which one out of five artifact piece you get- For Sand, goblet and ciclet, worry about which main stat you get- 3 or 4 lines of substats- Which 4/9 substat you going to get (not 10 cuz you can't get the same substat as main stat)- High or low rolls for each sub stat, using crit rate% as example, it has 43% difference for highest and lowest roll. (2.72% - 3.89% each roll)Now for tof, you have to worry about these:- For JO, you need to cost 30 for each opening, 90 to opening all- For JO/FCH/World boxes, you can only get the basic 8 equipment- You won't get SSR equipment all the time in each JO boxes, first and second box will have lower drop rate- For basic 8 equipment, you have 14 different sub stat, while 7 for Tank, another 7 for healer and DPS.- Which 4 out of 14 sub stats you going to get. (basic equipment)- 4 speical equipment that can only be obtain in the special mean, 2 are easier, the other 2 are extremely hard to get even one of them.- In additional from the 14 sub stats from the basic 8 equipment, these 4 speical equipment will have 17 additional sub stats. Which is 31 different sub stats.- Which 4 out of 31 sub stats you going to get. (special equipment)- High or low rolls for each sub stat, using crit as example, it has 500% difference for highest and lowest roll. (from my experience: 200 - 1200 each roll)- UR rarity on future update, all previous work will be gone to waste unless you can carry the sub stats.

_childDocuments_.review: Well well well, I’ve spent a thousand hours and then some playing this. I think it’s time to get some things off my chest.I first started playing Tower of Fantasy almost immediately after global servers opened. In its early state there was nothing I hadn’t already seen in other games, and it wasn’t long before I lost interest. Three months later the first character to pique my interest was close to being released, and I returned to the game and have basically played every day since. Within my three month absence, the content, character designs, open world and soundtrack had already greatly improved.For the first six months, I actually had a blast playing this. For a gacha, I never felt like it was too hard to get what I wanted or that the rewards were too stingy. On limited banners, pity is at 80 pulls, doesn’t reset if you get an early SSR, and carries over to the next banner. Every SSR has only a 50% chance of being the limited one, but it can be bought directly with tokens obtained from pulling 110-120 times on that banner. And because it’s recommended to main one element (volt, flame, frost, or physical), as a F2P there’s plenty of time between banners to save for the next new weapon of that element and get copies. On that note, the weapons and gameplay are definitely ToF’s strong point. The elaborate kits, flashy animations and niche features of each weapon make them all appealing and completely unique from each other. Every weapon has a character associated with it, and you can choose to use the character skin or your own customizable MC, which has quite a bit of appearance options. Sadly the nice MC outfits are all monetized in some way, but even so I’ve had the resources to get three from outfit gachas without spending money. The last aspect that’s kept me playing is the ton of things to do and work towards completing. It features the typical fishing, pet raising and housing modes; racing, CLUBBING, a card game; many, many things to farm resources for or upgrade through exploration, and of course daily, monthly and seasonal PvE modes to challenge, team and solo. If you complain about having no end game content or nothing to do in ToF, I don’t know what you want in a game.Here’s the thing that makes me mad. ToF has so much potential to actually be better than and as popular as other games in its genre but shoots itself in the foot by being greedy and unambitious. There are two things I really wish the developers would learn from certain massively successful gachas:- Players don’t need to be forced by constant powercreep to invest in new units.Do you enjoy trying various team combinations to see how much damage you can dish out with your own ideas? Do you pick what units to use based on their playstyle, but don’t want to sacrifice a huge amount of damage for that enjoyment? If yes, then you would probably hate ToF. Your only choice is what color you want your damage numbers to be, because there are only three units max of an element that are relevant at the same time. The best team for an element has always been its last two weapons with the latest “altered” element weapon. Despite limited weapons eventually going to the permanent banner, if you’re F2P you’ll never catch up with people spending to instantly max new weapons. If you invest money, it will eventually be a waste unless you continue to spend. I don’t know why they put so much effort into making weapons unique and interesting when they twist your arm to pull regardless. The entire reason I became a volt main was because I built my team around a weapon that is appealing and fun for me, and now I’m being expected to ditch it even before it’s been banished to the permanent banner. Speaking of which, I’d even prefer if limited weapons never went to standard if it meant they would stay relevant, because maxing out my favorite weapon is just going to feel like I’m getting a whale’s outdated hand-me-down and not as exciting as it would’ve been five months ago. Balance is nonexistent, this is the one problem most of the playerbase can agree on.- Male characters DO sell.The ratio of female to male playable characters is ridiculous. Right now there are 34 females and 6 males. They make well designed male NPCs and confirm them to never be playable. What makes this even more ridiculous is that characters and weapons in this game are separate, which means the waifu enjoyers can continue to run around with a waifu or their own custom character and completely ignore the male character associated with the weapon they’re using. And it’s even further ridiculous when every new character becomes part of the meta; the three limited male characters we’ve had were all meta when they were released, and I saw no decrease of people using and whaling for their weapons. More playable guys won’t affect people who don’t care for them, and it will make everyone who wants them happy. Hotta has nothing to lose, there is no excuse for this. If another cookie cutter waifu simulator in a genre oversaturated with them is what they wanted to make, they should have never added any guys to end up disappointing the players who were drawn to their few crumbs and expected more.On a side note, Hotta ironically seems to really hate the in-game equivalent of their target audience. Whoever made that horrid animation for the male rig with the bubble mount needs to be slapped. At some point they stopped making separate attack animations for male and female, and lately the weapons all have extremely feminine animations. The male and female MC in cutscenes never had separate animations and it’s very obvious they were made for the female.I dare say even the female characters lack creativity, most of them look the same (tall, big bust, long hair, pale) and 11 of 13 monetized skins are either a swimsuit, a wedding dress, or a Halloween costume.My conclusion from all this? The devs have some extremely basic tactics for getting money, they know what’s sure to make people open their wallets and don’t deviate from their tried and true practices. Even when not displeasing their current players and opening the game to a wider market would potentially be even more profitable and make the game look less like a half-assed cash grab.Moving on, the open world exploration is kind of awful. It’s so extremely braindead and boring, everything entails nothing more than hitting an object or bringing one object to another. I can only think of two times there were actual puzzles to make me feel accomplished for figuring out. The underwater area is a huge pain, so much going back and forth up and down to reach exploration points, and half of that giant area is just empty water... Exploration in the new region is almost exclusively running through orbs to collect them, of which there are far too many.The story… oooh boy… this is subjective matter now, but in my humble opinion, the story is very boring to play through. It has potential but is lamely executed. There’s supposed to be a mystery but they never drop any hints to theorize with or plot twists to stir things up. And this is the only game I’ve seen that MAKES you skip its story. That’s right, not long into your playthrough you will be shown a spoiler-ridden cutscene badly summarizing five chapters that it does an abrupt timeskip over. You are able to go back and play it chronologically, but at that point you’ve already been spoiled, and you won’t unlock important game features until beyond the point in the story it skips to. I have no words.I keep playing because of the good things I named off and because the new stuff every update activates that “ooo, shiny!” part of my brain, but it’s only a matter of time before I get too annoyed to keep tolerating Hotta’s bs. The next volt weapon will undoubtedly be another waifu that makes the damage of old weapons I still like even more pathetic in comparison, and I don't see myself being excited for that.

Like the language would display a different one at times. There are also bugs in the cutscenes were the pacing is off a lot of times. The dialogue gets cut off and didn't go well with what is happening ingame.The story is fun. It's not a masterpiece but it is definitely enjoyable and I was often waiting until it continued because I wanted to know what happens next. The graphics are okayish. The music is really good as well as the english voices. In some parts of the game it felt like sound effects were missing when you would expect something.The world and exploration part is good and rewarding too, you get orbs for pulls or dark crystals (currency to buy orbs).Gameplay modes are nice. You got those missions to grind for upgrade materials and gold and "dungeons" you play in a group for gear drops. All of that is gated by an energy system costing 30 energy and caps out at 180. Then there are sort of challenge missions where you solo levels with always increasing difficulty for reward. These don't need energy but at some point you won't be able to progress since the enemies get too strong. Raid is unlocked at level 60 which is 8 player beating bosses.I can recommend to play this game but not on  because:You get stutters nonstop and cutscenes stutter even more to the point it makes it just annoying and not enjoyable!If you want to give this game a shot download the standalone installer by clicking "windows" on their website. My PC is average at best and i can play this game maxed out without issues.Also the ingame gacha currency is expensive af but you can thank the greedy *** at apple for that. They changed the pricing tiers so those prices in my region increased by around 20% to what it was before. The same happens with all other gacha on Android/iOS so it an universal issue.7.5/10 enjoyableIt is a good fun game to play and a game i frequently like to come back to. Not a masterpiece and not terrible either.

_childDocuments_.review: I know that gamers this days has builds far too powerful than they need. Like some guys play CSGO with gtx3090. _childDocuments_.review: You know, I was originally planning to give this game a positive review. I've been with it since the closed beta, and ever since the initial launch. I've played the Artificial Island update, and now that Vera's here I was assuming I'd be happier for the game, however as someone who plays nearly F2P this game is super inhospitable. Ever since the initial launch the game felt very generous, but with Vera's release this has seemingly changed. Within Tower of Fantasy there is a currency called "Dark Crystals" which are used to roll for the designated highlighted banner characters, so these are extremely important to F2P players. During the initial game and Artificial Island you're capable of getting these from every single chest, but with the release of Vera they've seemingly removed any way to acquire them from the landscapes you're exploring, making it nearly impossible outside of events for F2P players to accrue large amounts of these to roll for characters which they most likely will need 120 rolls for. For newcomers to the game it's incredibly generous with the Dark Crystals you'll acquire and the area you're capable of playing within is expansive, mobility is amazing, and combat feels diverse and fun compared to something such as Genshin. For someone who's been playing for quite some time, outside of events it feels like a drought and nearly impossible to scrounge up enough to roll for characters, and as this is one of the key biggest features with Gacha games, it's the main thing that needs to be said.Outside of that, I've not got many qualms about the game other than how characters seemingly need copies to be good, which is the opposite of how many Genshin characters seemingly work. Features which should be given to players from the start for weapons aren't typically accessible, and sometimes unless you're far into the tree the weapon isn't worth using if you've already got something like Huma's Axe. Combat's fun, mobility's great, the story is laughably bad with some of the worst translation work I've seen in years, being something like what I'd see for a fan translation of a game which doesn't have an official translation.Overall: Unless you're someone willing to spend money and a lot of time, I'd say this game isn't really worth playing past a certain point.

_childDocuments_.review: ok so i come from WoW since wrath and played starwars TOR before and after it went FTP also played ESO before and after it went FTP.PROs: -Its free, very minor punishment for being FTP meaning stamina plays a minor role on this game (if you play gatcha games u know if u have no stamina u cant play at all until u pay or wait hours to play again) you will always have things to do here that meaningfully affect ur progression.-Questing/leveling is fun!This game is a GEM for what you pay for, even if you were to pay a one time AAA price is still worth your time as a single player game the world is HUGE! so u will be lost doing quest and exploring (the game demands you explore as a FTP as u get rewarded for doing so (this is not a negative, in all my live in MMOs one thing i have hated the most is leveling and chore like activities..) this game i am actually looking forward both, one huge part is the great DUB! main quest is fully VA! i am a sub elitest but i played a huge part of the game dub because its that good (not cringe) i recently tried about 10-15 hours in sub and is even better! however going back to dub to appreciate the in game cut scenes and appreciate better the art and animation (since dub is not bad i am 100% ok with this).-CombatIs really fleshed out (PC) this game is so rewarding when u fight it reminds me so much of Monster hunter series. you actually feel like a bad ass when u hit and dodge attacks the progression when you upgrade your gear is very noticeable too so a ftp player can kill anything a whale can (it will just take you days) unless there is a timer.CONs:-lets address the elephant in the room.... the game is a gatcha game if u know the game type u know the negatives, however this game is very generous for new players and if u like exploring u will be rolling with decent gear thought some strategies are always good to know before u go spending your currencies.-You like to be competitive? look for another game! this game is not meant for you to try to be on the top of the leader boards..... it will not happen unless u Willy your self to the top ranks. however if you stay in ur bubble with other players who also FTP u can find it very enjoyable to do raids/dungeons with them since you both will be on the same page the game is actually fun however even thought you both are FTP RNG can ruin this gap but its still nice to be able to play with other FTP players so far co-op has been fun for me.-Combat I know i added this on the Pros but there is a gripe i got with combat but it has nothing to do with your character (you) when u play with others their animations are set to low by default to not spam ur screen with so many effects u can fix this by setting all effects to 100% the problem is they dont do impact animation or sound... this is very noticeable as they look like they are striking thin air no sound from their attack hits no animation showing their attacks hit, this may not bother most people it bothers me a lot.TLDNR: make a noob friend get on discord and do stuff with them, make a pinky promise to stay FTP and help each other do puzzles and explore the hugmongus world and doing elites/world bosses i believe thats where this game shines is not only a perfect exploration single player game but u can share the adventure with friends. Support if you can.if you believe after sinking hours of ur life playing their game for free and feel compel to reward the devs i believe you should pay a micro trans here and there just make sure you make a budget. and stop.... like pay for AAA game (spend 50-60 bucks) or sub to their monthly fee i think its 5 bucks a month. something along these lines will support the game (you like playing) and will keep ur pockets healthy.the devs have really made an amazing game it feels bad this is a gatcha game because i would of easiliy paid a 15-20 buck monthly sub plus AAA price tag (like wow) to be able to be competitive and have full access to the game (characters) for a 1 time fee plus sub.That being said the game has been made with love you can feel this oozing anime lore/vibes and despite being a gatcha game in my 100+ hours of playing i have not felt like i am being preyed on by micro transactions. This is a non endgame/content review this could very easily change then but for what i have played this far its a 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: The main reason why I don't recommend this game is because it's a gatcha game. Playing ToF is a guilty pleasure of mine. The story is passable at times and downright awful at others. Power creep is toned down from the Chinese version but is still pretty bad if you want to keep up with people who spend money. You can clear most all of the content as a F2P and you definitely can get some whales to carry you through the rest, as long as you're on a server that's actually active. The music is pretty boilerplate. The exploration is kind of bland at times but Mirroria (cyberpunk city), the Confounding Abyss (underground alien cave), and Innars (ocean/underwater area) are definitely stand outs, featuring a lot of verticality and terrain that leverages the high mobility your character has compared to other games like Genshin Impact. There are bonuses for teaming up with friends and new players, and being an MMO means it's got a lot more things to do with your friends than just "have the overleveled friend carry you".Is it worth your time? Maybe. But be prepared to put up with a lot of jank and of course the random BS that comes with being a gatcha game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really want to downvote, if I could I would put neutral. But there are too many issues to really recommend this game.Pros:- Combat is loads of fun and there are plenty of weapons and builds to cater to all play styles.- The Gacha system is very generous, both in free packs and statistically speaking. In the sixty-some odd hours I have at the time of this review, I have half the available 15 weapons plus an event exclusive, all f2p.- I'm including this as a pro; The bad translations are just hilariously bad.- Plenty of waifus and weapons.Cons:-  For context, the world and main story enemies match your character's level. The overabundance of events give out tons of EXP and very few materials, resulting in a high level character with low level weapons. Fights become more and more of a grind, and while I enjoy a good challenge, the last 20-30 minute boss fight consisting of dodging the same three attacks was anything but. The weapon materials you need are locked behind daily energy, so as time goes on, there is only so much you can do and play in a day before you have to wait to get materials again the next day.- Pay2Win is prevalent, my primary issue is that the prices are so. damn. high. It costs $200 USD to guarantee one SSR weapon, which each have five tiers. Meaning if you want to max an event weapon pay2win style, I came into this game wanting to spend money to show my support, but at that price there is no point in even trying my luck.Overall, a fun game at its heart and I've met some really nice people on here. Unfortunately, even with other player's help, the fights are getting so grindy to the point where it is not fun to play. Would recommend playing over an empty weekend or two with a couple of friends, but don't plan on playing for very long.

_childDocuments_.review: Your typical open world anime rpg. I was looking for something with game play similar to Genshin and this game checked all the boxes for me. I really enjoy the storyline, it really made me care about people of Astra and Baden (two first areas of the game, the ones i went through so far). I like how the side quests deepen the ambiance of the game's world. Enemies actually feel malicious and like you have to defeat them (in comparison to Hilichurls having to be exterminated for sport in Genshin...). I enjoy exploring the map and getting my 100% exploration checks, really satiates the completionist in me. The background music is often relaxing and pleasant to listen to, enhancing the experience of exploring the map. Game features many puzzles and objects that have to be interacted with in specific ways beyond just pressing a button all around which i really enjoy.The game, although a gacha, can be played without paying for it at all which most of my friends do. I however allowed myself to get a premium battle pass and it's of a really good value for the price! The community, although small, is very welcoming and helpful. There is always someone to donate resources, accept you into a crew (guild) or help with a world boss. World chat makes me feel more connected to other players.There are some issues with localisation. Voices not matching the subtitles or missing completely at times, which interfered with my immersion in critical moments. Some minor bugs include notifications about new features not disappearing long after unlocking them. But in the end it didn't stop me from sinking hours upon hours into this game in the last few days.

_childDocuments_.review: The most free to play friendly gacha game in the market and the only worthy successor of Honkai Impact 3rd.I've been a gacha (gambling) enjoyer since 2014 and day one player of TOF with over 800 hours of gameplay (mostly played outside of Steam) and have experienced all the content this game offers, which, compared to any other of it's competitors, it's gargantuan and has an actual endgame reachable by both whales and F2P players. I've spent less than €100 since launch (2 battle passes and the €5 monthly sub) and have enough resources to last for months, while having all the characters for my element, multiple rare cosmetic outfits and mounts, all with usually some pretty terrible luck from my side as i hit pity almost every time. There is simply no better game in this category in terms of rewarding for raw playtime instead of spending money.First and foremost, this game is an actual MMO with hubs and players roaming around doing stuff together, not a glorified single player with RPG components like Mihoyo's (or any other gacha) games, which means you are required to play with other people in different types of activities, fortunately matchmaking and LFG aid in this and the community is also very friendly. The game can be played solo apart from the endgame content.Combat is great and every single character has its own style, set of animations and unique weapon, giving an immense amount of variety which is definitely an upgrade over the "pull this new character that uses a shared weapon type" which you already played for hundreds of hours, you also only need to pull the weapon to get the respective character skin which you can use with any other weapon, which, when paired with your custom MC, brings this games customization to another level compared to any other in the genre.Powercreep has also been an issue since the original CN launch that has been toned down but not eliminated, making almost all vanilla SSR weapons useless for anything endgame.Exploration is unmatched due to the freedom of movement you have with grappling hooks, jetpacks, wall-running boots and mounts and the maps are simply gigantic with each having a completely different theme, refreshing to say the least.Graphics, thanks to UE4, are a step above any other competitor as they all use Unity and the difference is massive, the game's soundtrack is also excellent and the terrible english dub (literally the same incompetent VAs that worked for Genshin) can be replaced for the amazing japanese one with a single click. The game also supports 120 FPS and has both DLSS and Ray Tracing. Performance wise, it's well optimized but has some stuttering issues especially in Domain 9.UE4 also means that the mobile version needs a lot of raw horsepower to play and i wouldn't recommend touching it if you don't have one of the latest gaming smartphones as even my ROG 6 struggles in some areas.The story is unfortunately a convoluted mess, but it's been improving with every single version and you now actually have a reason to care for the characters.There are tons of different currencies and upgrade materials, which can be extremely confusing for new or returning players, and the developers don't seem to slow down instead of unifying them into one or less at least.Events are constantly being pumped out and many of them force you to play minigames which is a standard in this genre of games, but many of these activities are PvP and people might skip or afk farm them as they require a fair amount of grinding (usually 3-5 hours of playtime)With all of this in mind, this is objectively the best gacha game out there if you're looking for pure gameplay flow and want an actual online MMO with content, if you prefer an amazing story with flashy gameplay but less f2p friendly, singleplayer and with dated graphics you always have Honkai Impact 3rd waiting for you.(Just don't download it off Steam as you won't be playing on HI3s global servers)You could also just play Genshin or Star Rail if you like chasing trends more than playing a good videogame.

_childDocuments_.review: Tower of Fantasy begs to use a controller, but as an all-time Dualshock player, I'm very unlucky because it doesn't work by default. Using just DS4Windows was NOT enough so after following few tips, I finally got it to work (). Nevertheless, I still ran into few bugs/inconveniences:1. Jumping as well as quick menu keeps disabling at times (mostly after cutscenes/conversations).2. Attack and interaction actions are mapped to the same controller button which makes fighting really annoying while between hitting a combo you keep interacting with stuff/characters.3. Shooting a bow/pistol requires you to hold LT and press O while moving right stick to move the camera, genius! xD4. Not every action is mapped to a controller i.e. crouching or choosing which object/character you want to interact with (by default it's Z to crouch, scroll to choose with keyboard and mouse).5. For some f-ing reason it double-taps while interacting with things, what makes you skip convos, exit from cooking etc.6. You can't customize any mappings on the controller. It claims "coming soon" while the game is out on PC since June.7. Overall UI is a disaster. Lots of missing settings. Far from the bar Genshin Impact had set.The list keeps going but I stop there. In summary, I really want to enjoy this game. Comparing it to GI, it already has better smooth movement, you can do and chain combos (not just spam attack and do special occasionally), and it allows you to create and dress your own "adventurer". There is a lot to be desired and for now, I cannot recommend to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: ToF is more or less a,,better''genshin.Like many others,i started with genshin aswell before ToF was a thing.And one thing always bothered me about genshin,which was the lack of multiplayer content,i wanted it to be a mmo.Tower of fantasy is fixing this.You play online with other people all the time,there are various modes like raids,dungeons,open world duels or ranked arena matchmaking(equalized gear),you also have little events sometimes,like a racing competition.-Combat: Pretty good,you get to make your own build with 3 different weapons,each having their own special attacks and combos.You can juggle,air dash/combo,switch weapons while attacking,and you can also do a perfect dodge,which makes the time around you(so including nearbie enemies too)freeze for a few seconds.In addition to this,you can also equip 2 different relics at the same time to make your setup more unique.You can use a jetpack,grappling hook,a magnetic force field,or even a freakin mech wich guns and rockets!-Story and voice acting: The  short,is about altering time itself,after experiments with a newly discovered ressource called,,omnium''went south.People got to use,,suppressors'',to shield themselves from the omniums radiation,which turns people into abberants who are hostile to everyone.The story takes place in the far future and has a somewhat post apocalyptic feel to it.Its not the best storytelling ive seen and its very linear,but its also not the worst,pretty mediocre.There is voice acting for cutscenes and some enemies,but sadly not for talking with random npc,s outside of the cutscenes.I know there are mixed oppinions regarding the quality of the VA,but often it just comes down to personal preference,and i liked it.Sometimes voice lines are skipped because of some bugs,no idea if they fixed it yet.-Mounts and exploring: All mounts are futuristic,so instead of traveling on a horse,you get to use a bike,a robot unicorn,a floating giant cube,a floating car and other stuff like that.You can also use relics for getting around easier and faster,like a jetpack,a grappling hook or a surfboard.If neither of those are for you,you can also just sprint or climb on walls/trees/whatever.-Music: Usually very chill,combat music isnt that great.Not much else to say about it,but the new music for vera sounds nice.-Character customization: This is where the game really shines compared to genshin impact.You can not only play as the characters you collect,but also make your very own char.There are various things to choose,like front/back hair,color of skin,height,clothes with different dyes,you have sliders for customizing the face,and you can also have different eye shapes and seperate colors/pupils for each eye(so for most people,thats 2 eyes)Alright,now some things that are NOT so great:-While the arena is equalized,you still have a big advantage if you got access to,,premium''weapons.You can unlock them theoretically for free too,but only if youre lucky with the gacha pulls.If not,you got to pay.It was mentioned that all weapons will later be available for everyone,without needing premium currency,but as of now,this didnt happen.-Performance isnt that great in the open world sometimes,and the arena(especially the 2vs2 arena they had in the past) can be very laggy sometimes.-Linear story.Im kinda spoiled by ESO,where you get to choose different answers and alter the outcome of quests.In ToF,thats not the case.-Lack of a male castAlmost everyone that actually matters in the story and gets enough screentime,is female.There are also only a few male characters to collect and it doesnt look like this will change much in the future.Its more of a,,waifu collector'' -Multiplayer content is way too easy.Dungeons are cool and all,but they are very simple.You usually just rush trough mobs and kill everything,and after a few minutes,youre done.Id like to see more puzzles and traps,stuff that makes people actually communicate and cooperate instead of just killing everything.TLDR: Genshin 2.0,its great.If multiplayer isnt your thing though,you might find more fun in playing genshin.PS:We got a crew on the server futuria,called,,Midori Ken''If youre new and need some help,consider joining us or also just hang out with us if you want,discord is available.Have fun with the game!

_childDocuments_.review: I played Tower of Fantasy since day 1 of its release so my hours hasn't been counted till today but I played every day since launch (8/10/2022) and today I just downloaded the game on steam and already got 16.9hours. At this point, you can tell that I really like this game and I will tell you why with this simple review.Just astonishing especially when you enter Mirroria for the first time with RTX on. Incredible, fluid, fancy, flashy, exciting, and really enjoyable. Interesting mechanics too, artifacts are a big plus, exploration is awesome.It's not that amazing but it's fine. You get to listen to new soundtracks when changing area and it's nice to listen to.I heard a lot of people didn't really like it. On my side, I really love the relationship between Shirlie and Zeke and since the story is basically focusing on this, i'm lucky and I have never skipped a single cutscene.The answer is P2A (pay to accelerate). This game can definitely be played (endgame included) without spending money at all. Monthly pass ($5) has 1,100% value that's the best value in game and it isn't expensive, especially for a free game. I know many people and I follow F2P streamers that are totally F2P and they're doing totally fine. Sure, you can't pull for every single events (unless you're blessed by the Goddess of Gacha) but if you are organized it won't be a problem at all.A lot of people compare this game to Genshin. Here's my thought about it:They are both amazing and none is better.Genshin Impact is focused on solo and it's a fantasy world.Tower of Fantasy is a MMORPG and it isn't a fantasy world but a cyberpunk one.Comparing those two games is a mistake to me because some prefer solo adventure and others prefer co-op content. They may be both gacha but they are too different and you shouldn't say one is better than the other.If you have any questions regarding the game feel free to message me. Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Terrible game.This is suppose to be genshin killer game but the only thing it kill is itself.This game offer what genshin didn't, an MMO end game combat. You have tough raid, daily quest, world boss. Everything is challenging and it give you reason to upgrade your gear and spend real money to get awakening (constellation in Genshin)That is the reason i draw to this game, however, this game also have ton of flaw1) Biggest flaw of all time, it is full of bugs. Annoying bug like constantly disconnect to serious bug where hacker can delete other player inventory. I kid you not, i thought it is just some paranoid player report false stuff in the first place but the developer confirm it and...they wait until the next day to fix it. Many player lost their entire inventory.As at this point, they still waiting to get back their stuff. Its already 2-3 weeks.2) Translation/port-over issue: It can be a small thing like missing space and text over the border to misleading such as "Equipment in this dungeon is consider max level" but it isn't. However the biggest error is the translation error in Weapon Awakening. Player spend hundred of dollar for each sentence in awakening but the game developer didn't bother to double check the translation. E.g. Cobalt B 6-star awakening have a missing line that state "Any DOT from dodge attack will trigger the skill CD reduction as well". This is a big impact because without this line, you can only reduce CD with dodge attack and it is not really impactful. We know the China version have this line but global has been nerfing every character in the game, they might nerf this 6-star effect.Turn out they realize their mistake after 15 days into the banner and fixed it in 2.0, 5 days before the banner is finish. Great job there..oh and they added more issue with cobalt matrix where they nerf it in 2.0..and then said they will change the text to show the nerfed state. Then they revert it in 5 days and said it is an announcement mistakeAs a paying customer, you going to suffer a lot playing this game. You won't know if the awakening is working properly or it is nerfed. They might even nerf it after release, while the banner is still up.3) While above issue is enough to make anyone quit, they also have a bunch of smaller issue that no time to address.Discharge attack sometimes do not trigger, grappling hook sometimes teleport you to other area, flying boss cannot be reach by most weapon and those boss usually can fly to outer space and reset hp bar. Overall, this game have good potential however the publisher really drop the ball.They make a lot of changes from CN > Global version, mostly nerfing the damage to prevent powercreep but they also make the gacha more expensive. Cobalt matrix suppose to help trigger burn effect at 2 set but they swap it to 4set, now you need ~160 rolls to get 4 set for QOL instead of ~80 rolls.Global limited pack is also give less nuclears compare to CN. They didn't reset x2 for first purchase while Korea and China did. It just hard to find anything positive to talk about this game. Every 1 good thing about the game is counter by 5 bad things. If I haven't put that much money in this game, i would have uninstall it by now. I just hope miracle happen and they improve the service , fix all bugs and provide better quality game in future.

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting much from a free game like this that I had never even heard of before. It has been a happy surprise to discover one of my favorite games.Beautiful graphics! Smooth combat and movement! Characters that are interesting, who I actually care about helping! Characters can climb things! Even ladders! Characters can pick things up! You can customize characters, upgrade weapons, collect vehicles, try on different avatars, play with friends. So many cool ways of interacting with the world that I have not seen in other games I've played. Did I mention the graphics are gorgeous? It's like the developers have been eavesdropping on all the things about games that I love and hate and actually working those thoughts into the game to make it better.And then...There are some serious story discrepancies that happen because you get sent to a certain area too early? Maybe? Not sure why the glaring story fracture happens, but it does and it is jarring and upsetting and seemingly completely unnecessary and it really trashes the immersion that the beginning of the game was so great at.I'm hoping to be able to forget that bit as I re-oriented to the original story line, but we'll see.But anyway, It's free!!! Definitely worth checking out as it gives other games I paid real money for something to live up to in so many ways.

_childDocuments_.review: Played many hours unrecorded before steam release and during the Vera update.Lackluster in the things that it needs to do right: the social/MMORPG aspect. The multiplayer aspect is what sets it apart. The obvious comparison to Genshin is irrelevant due to the fact that one is that one is meant to be a shared world MMO, and the other is designed to be a single player experience. It would be foolish to compare this to Genshin. But overall, it's okay to like both games. Liking one doesn't mean you have to hate  the other. ToF has potential, might be good in the future if the devs properly support it. However, I have a good bet that this game will never reach it's full potential. Don't get me wrong, ToF does a lot of things well, but I think it lacks staying power and polish. For an "MMO" style open world game, the world and servers and channels within the servers can feel quite empty. It feels like a side game you play when you need a break from something else. At times it can feel like a chore to play. The gameplay can be quite engaging and methodical while at other times feel quite jank, for lack of a better word. I also find the monetization rather predatory, as most gacha games tend to be. I find that hardcore fans and/or elitists will often praise the game while willfully ignoring the downfalls and red flags. ToF is a free to play game, so give it a shot. If you're a weeb, or enjoy collecting waifu's, you'll probably enjoy it. It's not a bad game at all, I just think it has a lot it can improve on. I want the game to get better and succeed. Invest your time and money wisely.

_childDocuments_.review: To address the elephant in the room, it seems like a lot of the reviews I see on this game are detractors of Genshin Impact, saying TOF is just it but better, and Genshin Impact stans, who say this is a pile of hot garbage. To state my biases right off the bat, I play Genshin Impact. I sometimes even like it. A year ago I was one of those people who hated all things Gacha, and Genshin for all its faults showed me you could still have a fun game behind it all. Genshin scratches the grinding urge in my monkey brain, and playing it casually I think it's great. I say all of this because in my opinion, TOF can entirely be described as "Genshin but..." In no particular order:It's Genshin, but it inexplicably takes 3 seconds to open a chest or interact with anything. Something you do a lot and that gets grating over time.It's Genshin, but while in Genshin to collect a dandelion you use an anemo skill and then collect it, here you have to hit the dandelion, then hit and collect another three things that burst off from it. Every. Single. Time.It's Genshin, but the pulling animation is extra long and annoying.It's Genshin, but we've added vehicles because...Well because it's Genshin, but we made the world extra big, empty and tiresome to travel around.It's Genshin but we added boring turret segments and...vehicle driving minigames where you dodge obstacles? Like, why? Who decided that was what would improve the experience? It's total scatterbrained game design.It's Genshin, but the combat is even more reliant on dodge spam because doing so lets you use your more powerful moves. I've seen a lot of people saying the combat is "better" than Genshin and while I don't think Genshin is very deep or complex, this ain't it either, chief. You group and juggle people to avoid taking damage, and when you're not doing that, you're dodging so you can spam your weapon swap specials. Maybe it gets better in the late game, but if you're asking me to grind through an unfun combat experience to get there in a gacha game, you've got another thing coming. The movement and attacks in general also just feel a bit stilted, like a worse version of PSO2's combat.It's Genshin, but it's even stingier with rolls and doesn't even seem to subscribe to the mindset of "The First Hit's free".  Mostly you just get the currency to roll on the weapon banners which give you barely anything and a few on the limited banners. I don't even think I got 10 gold whatever rolls in 6 hours of playing. Maybe I wasn't playing optimally, but if I can't find the slot machines because you hid them in the back of the casino, that's on you.It's Genshin, but super buggy and unpolished. I've had chests disappear from in front of me. I've gotten stuck in looping teleport animations and screen filters. I've fallen off cliffs because the game decided that particular bit of cliff is ethereal. I set the game to Japanese and some of the cutscenes are still in English. When I went to set the game to Japanese, the confirmation dialogue box has the "confirm" button in another language entirely. How does this get past testing? It's so insubstantial but it really demonstrates a lack of care.It's Genshin but the performance is abysmal. I do not have the best PC, but I could play Cyberpunk 2077 on high settings and a steady 60FPS. This game on anything above "Fine" should not be making my frames dip into the single digits while using dlss.If you didn't like Genshin, you will hate this game because it's too much like Genshin. If you love Genshin, you'll also hate this game because you could just be playing Genshin instead.All I can really praise is everything but the gameplay. I love the design of the world and characters, the music is great and atmospheric. The instant I stepped into Mirroria I was gobsmacked at how great it looked. I suddenly wished I was exploring these locations in a better game.If you like this game that's cool, I'm going to keep playing until I unlock another what I assume is the equivalent of a Genshin 4 star to see if it magically spices up the game, but I'm not holding my breath.Edit: Future me here, I got another 4 star (SR? I think in this game). Through some quest or event completion. I think my main issue with the system here is that getting a new character in this game does not feel as game-changing as getting a new character in GenshinIf I whale away 90 (Or 180) of my wishes in Genshin, it hurts, but at the end I have some really dope character like Raiden Shogun where I can dish out huge DPS with my Q,and an E that is benefited from all my other characters. In TOF, I get a new character and...I equip their new weapon to my wanderer MC and have ONE, count it, ONE new ability (which is shared between weapons of its type, and I guess the weapon swap special).It's ironic that letting you design your own MC is a detriment. I love that they let you do that, but it means that I don't see any reason to actually use Simulacrum. I honestly do not even know if there's some benefit to using it, but I'd rather use my custom OC donut steel MC than any of the characters you roll for, since you can access their weapons and abilities anyhow and keep your unique look.I think Genshin stomps out TOF in regards to reasons to whale for characters. In Genshin, I have four characters with two abilities each. That's eight abilities with (potentially) four different auto attack sets. In TOF, I have one character with potentially three different weapons, and the resonances seem to encourage you to use two of a single weapon. We're going to ignore that and pretend you're using three weapons. That's 12 variations for Genshin and only 9 for TOF.For Vets reading this I may sound like a total moron right now, but as a new person who has looked up nothing on the game, this is the impression it gives me. This is how it's encouraged me to play, and this is what I take away from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Had potential to be a good game that would make for a better multiplayer experience than Genshin. But as it stands now it will most likely just fade into obscurity in a year. Bad communication from the global devs, poor translations in game everywhere, buggy, laggy to the point you can't do group content in the open world, powercreep like you never seen before (older characters ends up unusable), barely gives you anything at all for playing (if you wan't to actually progress, you have to spend or don't mind being a third wheel). Game is also hyper focused on player retention and you will have to log in every day to do menial tasks to progress. Even weekly/monthly tasks will require you to log in several times to complete it in a timely fashion which ends up being extremely time consuming (especially when you have to make groups for a lot of the content, most of your playtime will be staring at the chat window trying to either make a group or find a group. every. single. day).Recent news are pretty bad and indicate they have cut their budget for the global version of the game. Their plans was to catch up to the CN version originally, but they have now decided to stay not 1 version behind, but 2.This might not sound like a big deal, but when you consider each update for this game takes months, global version will always be +4 months behind at all times. Nothing will be new to you as the CN version is basically what global will get with only adjusted numbers.Since the F2P experience is so bad in this game and now recently even long time players will have issues finding groups to do content with. I would steer away and spend my time somewhere else.Not to mention i doubt this game will exist 2 years down the line with how little has been done since launch to improve the experience and new players rarely makes it to the end game anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: don't let me steam playtime confuse you, i've been playing this game every day since it first released outside of steam. i have at least 100 hours total hours in tower of fantasy off of steam, so i've seen pretty much everything this game has to offer and then some.this game is bad. it's worse than bad, it's awful. it has the makings of a good game, but all of its shortcomings weigh it down so much that i just can't forgive any of it. i'll start with the pros, the mehs, and then move on to the cons.pros:-CUSTOMIZABLE PLAYER CHARACTER: the main character is completely customizable and the character creator is great. it's a ton of fun to mess around in and you can make some really unique and fun character designs in it-GRAPHICS AND ARTSTYLE: it's easy to say "this is a genshin rip-off trying to cash in on genshin's success" which, yes, it certainly is, but that doesn't change the fact that the game is nice to look at. genshin looks way better, but tower of fantasy is still a "pretty" game on the surface-EXPLORATION: i personally enjoyed the exploration aspect of tower of fantasy, so much so that i have most of the outfits you unlock for completing 80% of all exploration tasks in every region. there's a lot of things to do while exploring and there are little markers on your map to point you in the directions of points-of-interest. also, you get currency that is required for pulling in the gacha simply by exploring and completing points-of-interest!-SIMULACRA: the simulacra system is the same as every other gacha game, where you roll in gacha and get characters. the way this system differs in tower of fantasy is that simulacra, at least to my knowledge, are only cosmetic and don't have any unique abilities or stats. honestly, this bit could go in the "cons" section depending on who you ask, but i personally like it. it removes something from genshin that i absolutely hated: the constellation system and the need for dupe characters. instead, when you get a character, you get their unique weapon which you level up and awaken instead and you can wear them like a skin in the place of your customized player character, but why would you want to do that?-MINIGAMES: these are very few and far between, but what's there is a pretty enjoyable change of pace from normal gameplay. there's a racing minigame, a mario-esque sidescrolling platformer where you rush to the end while also collecting items to improve your overall score and the rewards you get from it, a regular platformer where you do the same thing (this one is way more fun than the sidescroller version), and a maze that you run through collecting items before the time runs out. the last three are from this 'dream projection' thing you can encounter out in the world randomly, and they sadly begin to wear out their welcome after a whilemeh:-THE COMBAT: the combat is fine. it's not great, it's not bad, it's just fine. completely serviceable and can be fun at times-THE RUINS: ruins are little mini-dungeons a la genshin's domains. they're alright, they're usually just mini-areas you run through and defeat enemies but sometimes there are puzzles. nothing special, but sometimes there are little data logs that you can read usually in the form of research notes from long-deceased researchers and those can be pretty interesting-THE LORE: i'll be real, the lore isn't all the interesting but it can be at times. lore is communicated to you mostly via the data logs i mentioned in the previous note but sometimes it'll be talked about in the story, but only briefly. it's basically nonexistent but what is there can be cool at times-THE RELICS: relics are collectibles that you get in ruins that allow you to complete certain puzzles in certain ruins and complete points-of-interest while out exploring. these range from hover boards that allow you to surf across bodies of water to... cubes that let you blow away other cubes..? they're either pretty good or strange. they all have certain utilities that you /will/ needcons:-THE SOUND DESIGN: my god, the sound design is terrible. it's actually impressive how bad the sound design is in this game. there are no sound effects in cutscenes, the audio mixing is abysmal, and it actively hinders your ability to take the story at least a little bit seriously-THE STORY: the story has potential, but the way its executed is /rough/. i'm not going to explain the story because i don't want to include spoilers in this review, but the story is an absolute mess and borders on nonsensical at times. it's not well written at all and can be a slog to get through-THE CUTSCENES: characters show no emotion on their faces, there are no sound effects, the sound design is ESPECIALLY bad in cutscenes, and it's just... ugh.-THE VOICE ACTING: the voicework in both english and japanese is... it's passable? but it's not good. the japanese dub in particular surprises me with how bad it is because they have some very high profile and skilled seiyuu like ayane sakura, yuichi nakamura, and yoshitsugu matsuoka among the cast. the voice direction is terrible which lowers the quality of the voice acting as a whole, even with good voice actors-THE CHARACTERS: i wouldn't consider all of the characters unlikable, but they're all flat and boring. i only like one character out of a decently sized cast of characters and even *he's* flat and boring. the generic npcs you come across that are involved in the plot for a short while are, however, grating and actually caused me to have to put the game down for a bit. all of the side-characters introduced in the third area's main story, which is also the worst part of the story in my opinion, are obnoxious and genuinely miserable to be around. playable characters are very blatantly designed and created for the sole purpose of making money via the gacha. which brings me into my next point-THE GACHA: obviously gacha isn't good in any game, it's predatory and dampens the experience of anyone playing a game that has gacha in it, but there are games that have relatively forgiving and decent gacha systems. tower of fantasy is not that game. the rates of getting SSR characters is so low that you'd be lucky to get anything above an SR character before hitting the amount of pulls before the game pities you and gives you a guaranteed SSR, which takes a ridiculous amount of pulls-CHARACTER DESIGNS: the character designs in this game are messy and unappealing. the best character design comes from a character that isn't even playable (zeke). there are some decent ones, but 90% of them are generic, boring, or just plain lazy.-THE MUSIC: the ost has a major identity crisis and it shows. it doesn't know what it wants to be, and it's the most apparent with what i'm assuming is the games theme song, which plays at night in an area that, once you hear the song, you can tell is clearly inspired by NieR: Automata's amusement park, and the song plays at no other part of the game. the reason i point this out is because the song is trying HARD to be Weight of the World from NieR: Automata and it's /very/ obvious. it's a pretty song, don't get me wrong, but it wears its 'inspiration' on its sleeve to the point that it seems like a rip-off. it carries no emotional weight or impact, which makes it nowhere comparable to Weight of the Worlddon't let the amount of pros and mehs fool you into thinking that tower of fantasy isn't "that bad". it is. it's that bad. it starts out as a fun experience that you really, really enjoy, but once you leave the first area it all goes downhill from there. tower of fantasy was a huge letdown for me as someone who had excitedly waited for months for it's 1.0 release.also, i found out recently that to "bolster player numbers" and generate fake positive reviews at launch, they registered accounts under the names of ACTUAL DECEASED PEOPLE and used those deceased individuals' information

_childDocuments_.review: Tower of Fantasy (ToF) is by all means a fun game to play; however, like many gacha games, it requires you to set limited, obtainable goals to prevent your game experience from becoming not fun.Having started my ToF journey on its release day through the launcher, and continuing the journey after its Steam version was released, this game has continued to provide content and updates that do improve the overall game experience. While most (if not all) patches were solely created with the original Chinese (CN) server in mind, the global server has benefited from the improvements the developer, Hotta, has made to the game since the CN server first opened. However, the roll out of said improved content by the publisher, Level Infinite (LI), has been rough to say the least. Initially, they had aimed for the global server to catch up to where the original CN server was at. This resulted in several patches worth of content, in addition to all the gacha characters that came alongside them, to be squeezed into less than a year. While there were benefits to this system, such as a minimal delay between content drops, this also meant gacha characters that were destined to be overshadowed by newer ones of the same element and type became irrelevant much sooner than in the original CN server. It was only after several months, with the release of 2.5, that LI decided to keep the global server about two patches behind the CN server. Now, while players have a larger window to play with newer gacha characters before they eventually become overshadowed, there is a longer period of delay between substantial content drops. Paired with the poorly received events/minigames (developed by Hotta) that were handed down from the original CN server, most of which have been plagued with AFK farmers not participating, there is not much reason to stay online any longer than you have to.Contrary to most gacha games, where simply logging on to do daily content does not affect the overall game negatively, ToF is hurt greatly by this practice. Yes, there are a certain amount of players that can clear harder group-focused content without much assistance; unfortunately, that cannot be said about the majority of players, especially casual and newer players. ToF is by all means a "carry or be carried" game, in the sense that you will have to be carried by players that are stronger than you until you are strong enough to carry players weaker than you. It's this cycle that drives the small, but passionate community in this game to keep playing long after most of them reach whatever they consider endgame. If a chunk of players strong enough to carry others decide to log off after completing their daily content regularly enough, then another chunk of players are affected negatively. The only option to help remedy this is matchmaking, which sadly falls short to the task.To Hotta's credit, matchmaking does not only pair you with players in your own server, but also with players of the same region as your server. This means that even low populated servers that have yet to be merged with other servers can still tackle harder content with players strong enough to carry them. While every group-based mode uses a same-region matchmaking system, the only mode that fully utilizes the benefits of such a system is Joint Operation (JO). What makes JOs stand out over the rest is the Support Match option; when pressed, the game will search for a player or a group of players matchmaking for a JO of any level (1 through 9) that needs a spot with a specific type filled (i.e. Fortitude) and place the Support Match-er in a party with them. This allows for those who have a high enough level (giving them access JOs 1 through 9) to assist someone whose level is only high enough to access, say, JO 4. This minor, yet beneficial system, which allows strong players to (with little to no hassle) greatly benefit weaker players, is unfortunately locked to JOs alone. The sole matchmaking system available to other group-based modes features a more limited system that makes it difficult to assist players with ease. This system requires the player to lock in 1 to 2 roles (i.e. Fortitude, Benediction), then wait while the system finds 1 to 7 other players that meet the recommend team requirement (2 Attack, 1 Fortitude, 1 Benediction for 4-Person Teams or 4 Attack, 2 Fortitude, 2 Benediction for 8-Person Teams). If the system does not find enough players to go within about 2 minutes, it will then stop matchmaking and ask the player if they want to go alone or resume matchmaking. Deciding the latter will forcefully make you create an empty party and post an automated message about the party in the Recruit chat before starting the cycle again for another 2 minutes or so. Both the locking in of (a) role(s) and the timer on matchmaking are not present when using JO's Support Match option, making that mode much easier to assist casual and newer players in than the other equally important modes.With all the issues in ToF I felt needed to be shared in this review, you're probably wondering why I'm leaving a thumbs-up, or even still playing the game all these months later. The only reason I can give is that I've successfully accomplished what I mentioned at the beginning of this review that a game like this requires of you: set limited, obtainable goals. For every gacha game I've played, no matter the length of time with it, I made a commitment never to spent a single cent in it; instead, I wanted to "give back" to the gachas I enjoyed by using my account to help other players in-game. This looks different for every gacha I've played, but for ToF, that meant hosting World Boss taxis, assisting with group-based modes, and sharing info with players who were asking in World chat. Since I never spent any money, I was pretty much locked into being carried by stronger players (i.e. those who did spend money) for the first couple of months. Accepting this reality, I focused on becoming a Tank main; my main duties were to keep aggro (while managing my HP), activate Phantasia by dodging specific boss attacks at the correct time, and shred through shields when they popped up. Soon enough, with two standard, but fully-ascended Healer weapons, I was also providing heals and buffs that allowed DPS-ers to deal even more damage. In addition, since I only needed to use my limited gacha currency on two banners out of the dozen that have been released, I was able to use what I had left over to obtain a cosmetic outfit that fit my Wanderer's cosplay. Now, on the doorstep to the next largest patch (3.0), I've gotten to the point where I can not only help stronger players get stronger, but also help weaker players get stronger. For me, that's the only reason I continue to log back in day after day, despite the many shortcomings this game has on both the development and publishing side.At the end of the day, if you're someone who is okay with setting limited, obtainable goals for yourself to achieve, I'd recommend giving Tower of Fantasy, or any gacha game for that matter, a try.And don't worry, you probably won't have to put in 500+ hours into the game to reach them.I just like to chill on the bench in Mirroria.
