_childDocuments_.review: Played hundreds of hours before steam launcher. Day 1 player here.Game had so much promise, unique weapon system for build variety. Great customizability of your on-field character cosmetics, fun world exploration e.g. grappling hook, wings. Does lots of things that G-Game doesn't do in terms of world exploration.Time gating of world exploration has pissed off lots of players. Sometimes in boss battles, server lag makes the game literally unplayable and stalled. An MMO that struggles to run when there are other players around is a huge red flag. Unfortunately the game is very pay to win, and requires constant ongoing grinding to get currency to roll for new characters. Older characters are power-crept very easily. People who return from playing months ago will find the new characters released are much stronger. This incentives people to pay for rolls to keep up.While the game has some fun character gameplay, good customization, and decent looking worlds (the new zones look way better than the old zones), the power creep and some actual gameplay jank (stalling on world bosses etc) make the game struggle to stay afloat. Players come and go once they realize what the game is really like. Fun to get started but hard to keep it up.It shouldn't be thrown away and discarded, it's a decent game on its own, but it has some pretty big drawbacks that just make it hard to keep playing as a main game; and it's hard to play as a side game due to power creep.PVP uses equalized stats, which makes PVP reasonably fun and balanced, however if you don't have the meta characters, you will get facerolled. So on the one hand it is balanced if you have meta players but on the other hand, if you don't, you can't compete. Unfortunate.It's free, so it's worth trying, but, I'm done playing this game and don't intend to return, and don't recommend the game.WHAT WOULD MAKE IT BETTER?-stop power creep, balance units-more pulls-fix server lag issues-fix chat spam problems-get rid of outfit gatcha, be more forgiving and get out skins/oufits easierOf course, they won't do any of those things, because they think that will cut into their profit. So, unfortunately, they are choosing greed over gameplay. Unfortunate.

_childDocuments_.review: A polished title with tons of content and it hasn't been out on PC for even one year. Recommended with WARNINGS.Overwhelming amount of minigames thrown at you and even more that's level-locked. Keeps people busy after the story is done, so if you like a wide variety of things to repeat instead of story, then Tower of Fantasy is a good choice.If you need to chase battle passes and try to max them, then it probably isn't for you. On a daily and weekly basis they entice you to play a lot and do a dizzying amount of content. You can easily let the game monopolize your time. But you may be actually fine with this if Tower of Fantasy becomes the only game you just play for 4+ hours a day.Other than the battle passes / reward tracks, pretty much all the minigames reward you with something relevant, so that can make you feel like you need to do them all. As you level up, more systems appear and there's more and more to track and eat up your time.Of course there's gacha randomness. You can earn quite a lot of free rolls just doing overland exploration but if that's all you are using, you're likely in for a frustrating time. Your combat style is determined basically by what you can get randomly. Don't get anything good for the minigames where you get swarmed by enemies? Too bad.And sometimes random draws can result in edge case weirdness like 8 copies of The Terminator SR cannon weapon and not much else.Main story chapters have an "unlock time". WTF? I got to Cetus Island and after a very tiny bit of story there was a 15 hours unlock time before I could continue. I guess they expect you to fill in that time doing side activities like wandering the world and doing minigames. If you are here for the story, don't bother and go watch a youtube instead.Sometimes an enemy will have resistance except to one type of weapon, and if you don't happen to have a proper one to dps it down, too bad. You can easily end up flunking an instance trial. It's not so bad for overland since you can often disengage and swap weapons -- if you have a useful one of the correct element.

You will get hundreds of free draws in the regular and premium shop to work with, and a pity mechanic of 80 draws to fall back on. Word of caution: Avoid combat whenever possible. Low levels get an XP boost, which levels monsters with you, but your strength is only dependent on your equipment. You thus get loot-starved and incentivized to spend more on gambling just to survive. Now why do I still not recommend it on the long run? Well, after you have collected and spent your starting loot from all over the map, there really is not much to do. Literally everything is time-gated. Everything. Well, everything except the means of spending money, of course. So even if you want to grind resources as a F2P player, you can't. If you spend 30-45 minutes a day on your dailies, you get everything you can get. Then spend an afternoon on mondays on your weekly recharge things, and you are basically done. Important resources like gold orbs, and dark crystals are kept at a trickle. Red orbs(event currency) is only available with dark crystals, which are also kept to a trickle. There are constantly events to spend red orbs on, but there is no way for a free player to participate in all of them. It takes months to save up enough for a single guaranteed event SSR draw. And even then, there is only a chance that it will actually be the event item you want.Additionally, the P2W-F2P divide. In any PvP event, you stand no chance whatsoever against someone who paid for extra stuff. The upgrates to gear are just so significant that a P2W player can melt a boss in seconds. This also means that in PVE events, you basically dont do anything. If you can, CC the mobs together so the guy with a million DPS can kill them all even faster. Meanwhile, since the bosses are more balanced towards these people, a F2P player can easily get one-shot by most. To have any hope of catching up to a P2W player, you would need *years*. During which they got more and more of the fresh good stuff.Speaking of, the bosses: These are some of the worst boss designs I have seen in my 20+ years of gaming. The two general branch are: whole-arena AOEs that you cant really avoid, and bullet-sponges that defy any expectation. I have literally gone AFK in the middle of some fights with 10-20 people killing a boss(which results in massive lag), had lunch, took a ♥♥♥♥, returned, and the boss was not even at phase 2 of the fight... Of course, both of these issues can be alleviated by paying for more resistance and DPS. And on the topic of DPS, its king. There are sooo many activities that are solely based on DPS. You simply cannot do them any other way, you just need to increase DPS at any cost. No matter your skill at anything else, even if you can solo a world-boss with technique instead(and yes, very much possible), There are many important solo things you simply cannot do without ridiculous DPS.And finally, chat. 50 character limit per message, 10 sec cooldown between messages. And it fills literally half the screen. Oh, and half the english dictionary, and then some word combinations are censored. We recently became able to speak the name of the colour red without being roundabout.Yeah, I think that about sums it up. Play it for like a month, then throw it away. Its probably even more fun if you play with that in mind and spend resources accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I've been playing this since it initially launched back on August 10th. Here are some of my thoughts on the experience I've had on the game. I'll start with the cons since I feel they are more significant and why I wouldn't recommend this game to just any random person, there are pros but text limit, so tl;dr with that is if you like exploring you'll have fun but otherwise it's nothing special. Now wall of text incoming...Cons:- Hotta is an incompetent studio. That's the nicest way I can put it, the team for the global version of this game just doesn't seem to know what they're doing. We've had hackers on the top of nearly all leaderboards since the launch of the game (and are still there as of writing this), hackers in PvP one-shotting people, and a little over a week ago people were too afraid to play due to people being able to delete all the items in other player's inventories. There are translation errors that have existed since launch. We constantly need hotfixes because they forgot to change the scaling of an enemy from CN to Global values or batch fixing the translation errors that are everywhere. Most matrix and character star effects cannot be trusted since they don't do what you think they would by reading them. We are also the only region where top-up bonus wasn't refreshed with the release of 2.0 and have the highest prices for premium currency out of all regions. All of these things can be found easily by searching and have been the source  of major drama among the players. - Customer service is nearly non-existent. I sincerely hope nobody ever has issues that force you to go through them.- The design of the combat and gear systems leads to shallow choices in team building, and end-game content is not engaging. The game railroads you into playing mono-element DPS teams for nearly all content, where characters can largely be viewed as strictly better than each other. This has lead to powercreep being a constant feature of the game, there aren't any niche rolls for them to fill like how elemental teams work in Genshin. In Tower of Fantasy you have your main DPS, a shieldbreaker, and a buffer and you do not deviate from that formula. At least not if you want to get through the harder content in the game. This isn't exactly new for a gacha game, but you get punished for trying to commit to waifu > meta harder than a game like Genshin. All hard content is just a DPS race as of writing this, tank and healer roles aren't needed. Especially if you're around whales.- Touching on end-game content being shallow for a second - Raids, World Bosses, Bygone, Wormholes, etc... All rarely go beyond having a mechanic of "Don't stand in the red AoEs". Bosses and mobs are constantly recycled between those and other content such as Joint Operations. It looks like you have a lot of options available to you, but in practice it's all the same content with slight twists that don't do enough to make them feel unique from each other. - Combat is just ok. If you enjoy fast paced combat that rewards perfect dodging, I would recommend you go play Punishing: Gray Raven instead. This game has issues with lag, desyncs, certain characters heavily reward being macro'd due to buggy animations, and if you aren't playing with a character that has high super armor uptime you will grow to hate certain enemies / content because CC can last forever in this game. If you aren't doing solo content, only the person tanking has to know how to dodge and you're mostly just beating into damage sponges if you aren't. - The story is also just ok. Not much to talk about here without spoiling parts of it, but there are some incredibly annoying characters  that stick around way too long. Cinematics have definitely improved in 2.0 I will say.- Acquiring gear is timegates on top of RNG on top of timegates. Have you played Genshin? Did you enjoy farming for artifacts every day once you ran out of story? Because even though they try to make it seem like there are more activities, this is essentially all you will be doing here as well. Except the new gear takes the RNG to a place Genshin could only ever dream of (you get maybe 1 chance per week at rolling it, and the pool of stats is insane at over 20 options. You want 3/4 of your rolls to be useful for your DPS. Then you have to actually hit non-min rolls if you finally get a usable one...). Additionally, the way you upgrade armor is one of the most heavily timegated resources in the game. Anyone starting now will be months behind players who started on launch. There is currently no catch-up mechanic for this. Even worse, there's kind of a snowball where people with the best gear get rewarded with more materials to upgrade it (leaderboard ranking rewards every week in Bygone). - The game is only generous at the start. Yeah, this is kind of a "no duh" thing, but the game really does shower you in rolls and SSRs at the start. It wouldn't be hard for a player to hit 3 SSRs in their first week of playing, and that's without hitting anything off-pity or getting lucky at a world boss. Once you exhaust that though, it feels like you're just limping along waiting for the next major content release. As more limited characters get released, those easily attainable SSRs also crater in value. It is definitely possible to max units as a f2p or light spender in this game, but most new limited units have more power than most of the 6-starred base units at 3-star or even 1-star in some cases. Which makes sense, they have to get people tempted to roll on the new hotness. - The game is balanced for the whales. Some content is extremely difficult or outright impossible to full clear without whales or at least a majority dolphins being present. There's also a large gap between a true f2p - battlepass + daily crystal package buyer - dolphin buying monthly bundle deals - true whale who just spends until max. If you pay for power, you will feel it, but it you get heavily diminishing returns after BP + daily deal.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat seems fun so far, each weapon plays differently and the world is quite diverse. unfortunately, the game doesn't want you to play to it's strengths.there is an utter mess of inconsistent systems and terrible ui. for example, it has at least 3 menus where daily login rewards need to be claimed. it feels like typical feature creep in a badly managed software project. instead of integrating new features into the existing framework, they slap another menu and another one on top of each other. I think the game is pretty F2P friendly, but the overall UX is horrible.the game also can't seem to figure out how to guide players in terms of equipment. there's a character level, weapon level, equipment level, matrix level, relic level and probably a few more. CS is an overall score of your gear they try to use as a general benchmark of your power level, but the recommended CS of ruins doesn't seem to work at all. a 2.4k CS ruin can have you fight tooth and nail for 15 minutes against a boss despite being at 4k CS and simply leaving - then at 5k it suddenly dies within seconds. the power progression is just not intuitive and you never know if you stand a chance. as someone that doesn't like dragging others down, it turned me away from any group play options, as I have no idea if I could even help or just be a useless carry that can't do more than 1% of the overall damage. even a simple, potential dps with basic attacks would be a better guideline this CS. the only way it helps is if it says 50k, I know I won't even need to attempt something and that it's probably endgame content.the story and ingame characters are also really horrible, especially the atrocious girls and lolis with their "endeering" characters - a friendly fire option would've been apreciated. _childDocuments_.review: This is the first time I have felt the need to leave a review for anything on Steam. I played Tower of Fantasy at release using its stand alone client. Just played casually as I usually find open world games relaxing to mess about in and I'm not adverse to gacha games as long as they are not too predatory and there is actually stuff to do in the game to earn whatever currency the game uses. I initially created a character on a server that soon filled up with mostly SEA players (not sure why, I believe it was a European server) so I hopped onto another server that was predominantly English speaking and created a new character there. I played the second character off and on over a couple of months, downloaded the client off Steam when it released and got quite a few of the limited simulacra as well as multiple of copies of the standard characters and completed the Mirraria (is that what it was called? The sci-fi pyramid city in the desert?) storyline.  I grew a bit tired of the chase for Nucleus to roll with and took a break until a few days ago (it had been over 600 days since the last login according to the clients welcome back screen). I initially thought everything was fine, I agreed to the transfer of my account to a Level Infinite account and logged into the game to find I only had one character and their name had been changed. "Oh okay, they probably merged some of the servers" I thought. However the one character that remains available to me without creating a new one no longer has any of the map clear and is missing almost all of the simulacra I had pulled. I thought maybe I just missed seeing the other server where my longer played char was parked but no, nothing on any other server on any of the regions. I opened a ticket and explained that I appeared to be missing a character and all of the guff I had accumulated on them and submitted screenshots taken in Steam showing me using both the simulacra I had and them using their weapons.Now this is where I can't understand what has happened, the screenshots I had taken (before I stopped playing) have a different UID than my account has now, BUT, it is literally the same account I was using before. All the login credentials are the same. I can only imagine that something went wrong on Hottas end at some point, either when (if) they had server merges or during account transfer to Level Infinite (but why would only 1 character have transferred?). So Customer service refuse to look into the matter any further unless I can provide them with details that most people would probably find difficult to come up with, date and time of account creation, when I linked to social media etc. I never spent any money on the game so no transaction history. So that's that.For what it's worth, I enjoyed the game when I was playing. The graphics, animation and music are quite good. The world is fairly attractive to wander around in. The combat is mindlessly okay. The gacha isn't too onerous and is quite generous with the pulls it gives out or lets you earn, There is probably by now a wealth of content to wade through even though the story is forgettable. So if your thinking of playing and don't mind the anime aesthetic or gachas in general its a nice way to kill some time.But if something happens to your account through no fault of your own (that I can see anyway) you can probably kiss your stuff goodbye as customer support are essentially useless. I didn't spend any money at all on the game, maybe things would be different if I had, but then again maybe not and I would be pissed if I had.Anyway just thought I would add my experience in case it sways anyone on the fence about the game. I wont be committing any more time to the game and I'm not really bothered about that, all I lost is meaningless stuff and the time it took to gather it all. Somebody else might end up losing quite a bit of cash.

Banner hard pity (80) carries over to the next and does not reset when you get SSR's before the hard pity. Banners rerun about every 2-3 months so you can save up for what you want and spend it then to further max your character of choice. Problem is actually being committed to holding your pulls and being realistic about what you can actually obtain.PS: Stay away from PVP content, servers are laggy and effects don't show, it always ends up in a battle of luck or mechanic abuse. Do not frustrate yourself playing it unless it's somehow your cup of tea.Whale only if you really enjoy the gameplay loop and squading up with your crew (clan in tof) and beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of bosses together. Else just F2P the game and ask for whales which are in abundance to carry and then return to solo (SP) content which requires 0 spending or whaling. _childDocuments_.review: I took quite a long time to review this game because I didn't know how to properly go about it and how to evaluate it. But after spending 289 hours with it, I more or less know how to go about it.The game itself is very good so I can't rate it negatively, but this system of drawing characters and other things (gacha system) in my opinion is not good because it rewards people with big wallets, which is obvious and I shouldn't be surprised, however, everyone wants to have we want to enjoy the game as much as possible and have fun, and this system is a bit disturbing here, and on the other hand, it helps because when we learn how it works, we more or less know how to act. However, if we want to really achieve something here, we must have friends to play with, who will support us in crossing borders and improving the character, and it is also good to have money that we will spend in the game itself to strengthen ourselvesBeside that, the combat system should be really praised, it's very well done, it's really interesting and it combines well with various combos in this game. I really like to fight in this game. As for the story, I think it's very good and interesting (as for a network game, it's very good).It is also important in this review that I am writing it as a player who plays both ToF and G:I at the same time. That's why I know what both games do and how they do that's why I can say that both are good and worth playing, and if you get bored which is the most possible because often G:I players have something that can be called burnout, you can just put it aside for a while and, for example, play Sekiro or something else and then return to them againIt's hard for me to point out any specific flaws because all in all the games are good, maybe they're not perfect and sometimes you can get tired of them like I had with G:I and sometimes even with ToF but I kept coming back to them after a while.My rating for this game is 9 / 10

No ones can afford to try any weird off-meta meme build at all.How to be a meta player as a damage dealer role in TOF ?It's simple just follow this patternWeapon slot 1 : Newest Flame/Frost/Volt/Physical  element weaponWeapon slot 2 : Second newest weapon of the same element as slot 1Weapon slot 3 : Newest Altered element weaponYou need to save ALL of your premium currency for the newest unit of the same element you main onlyMost weapons need to have multiple copies to unlock extra effectso you might need to spend pull even more than you think and cannot afford to try any other element weaponsaside from altered element weapons 90% of weapons in this game do not work at all outside of their own elementif you pull random weapon it will be completely useless and waste of pull.Whenever the new unit of the same element drop you replace the oldest one with the new oneNever look back at those old weapon because it's gonna be completely outclassed by new weapon in every case scenario.No utility or any niche usage.Sure, they may give you more than enough pull to pull the newest unit of the same element you main but this is not what I really wantI'm not a one trick pony who play one element for the rest of my life I want to try multiple things.Waifu over Meta doesn't work if you want to do endgame contents properly without leeching whale.== Powercreep fiesta ==Some might say powercreep is normal in gacha gamesbut this is really really REALLY bad compare to other gachas out there.Don't be deceived by anyone who says "B-But... TOF Global is different from TOF CN"The whole "Global Nerf" is just a propaganda.TOF CN : Old units deal 100 damage / new units deal 1500 damageTOF Global : Old units deal 100 damage / new units deal 500 damageTHIS is their so-called Global Nerf. Old units are still absolutely useless.I don't even know why they even bother do all of this "Global Nerf"It doesn't do anything at all only exists to kill anticipation.Yes, I'm looking at you the one who intentionally sabotage the interaction between Lin A6 and Fiona Torrential Force on Skill1 and brush it off as a "bug".SR weapons are completely uselessSSR standard weapons are also useless (aside from some healer-buffslave weapons)If you want to keep up your damage you MUST PULL newest weapons only.Do NOT touch any rerun banner. It's a bait.== Should you play the game? ==If you are meta player who doesn't care about waifu ?Sure, Just make sure to pull the newest unit of the same element you main whenever they drop and bench the oldest of the same element in your setup and never look back at them.If you are super casual player who doesn't care about endgame contents?Sure, play however you want the game got so many mini-games and stuff, have fun.If you are 50% waifu 50% meta player (want to play whatever I want but still want to do endgame contents properly) ?No, TOF is not for you. _childDocuments_.review: After dedicating over 100 hours to this game, I’m left deeply disappointed. The storyline is lackluster, making it tempting to skip through it entirely. Combat is underwhelming—you can easily one-shot enemies, and while the difficulty can be increased, doing so offers negligible rewards and comes with a penalty if you choose to revert it. Much of the gameplay involves traversing the map at an agonizingly slow pace, repeatedly performing mundane tasks, interspersed with cutscenes that add little value due to the poor narrative. Most of the “Game” is running across the map, ok good job, now what? DO IT AGAIN. Sadly the storyline is the fastest way to progress your character and there's next to no content outside of it. If you aren't holding down W your typically skipping through slow paced cringe dialog. Dialogue is excessive and largely irrelevant. Occasionally, you’re presented with multiple-choice options, but these have no meaningful impact on the story, reducing the experience to a shallow, poorly constructed roleplay idk. On top of this skipping dialogue is a tedious process, often taking 10 full seconds, which hints at just how time it would be to experience the game as intended. The game’s content in general is sparse, consisting of the main storyline and a few side quests, most of which involve clearing areas of enemies that pose 0 challenge. The limited combat is flashy and enjoyable in theory, but it’s undermined by the ease with which you clear every mod presented. The gacha system is prominent, and although you can play for free, the pay-to-win mechanics are blatant. Yet, considering the lackluster gameplay, it’s baffling why anyone would spend money to excel. Speaking of “anyone” there is actually NO ONE. The online community is nearly nonexistent, and the world feels desolate. Players log in primarily to assist friends with monotonous routine tasks or to chat, making the game more of a background distraction than a captivating experience. Dungeons, which should be a highlight, are hidden away in a sidebar and require teleportation. They are disappointingly short and single player only. The puzzles within are uninspired busywork, failing to match even the oldest Zelda titles. These dungeons would benefit from being longer, multiplayer, and integrated into the open world, with improved puzzles and more substantial rewards. Unfortunately, the game feels like a low-effort attempt, banking on its attractive visuals reminiscent of a lesser Breath of the Wild and flashy combat to draw players in. However, the experience quickly becomes a monotonous grind, driven by the promise of better weapons that ultimately do nothing to enhance the gameplay. The gacha elements are poorly executed, serving primarily as a funnel to extract money from players.Moreover, the game’s interface is needlessly complex, requiring navigation through roughly 50 tabs just to collect every reward. This could be easily streamlined with a single button to collect everything at once, but instead, it’s designed to bombard players with countless prompts to spend money. The plethora of currencies is poorly explained, adding to the confusion and reinforcing the game’s focus on monetization. The visual design, while appealing, raises some concerns. The art style borrows heavily from Breath of the Wild but with an overemphasis on sexualized anime characters, which feels incongruent with the presence of a child like character who inexplicably follows you throughout the entire game. This juxtaposition is unsettling, especially in light of the studio’s upcoming title, which just based on the trailer alone seems to double down on this questionable approach, In the trailer they show what looks to be a very young child, in a very short skirt being chased around by a drooling demon. I don't know, maybe i'm over thinking it but something about that just seems off no? In conclusion, this game is a significant waste of time. Despite its attractive exterior the gameplay is shallow, easy, repetitive, boring, slow and ultimately feels like a low effort cash grab. Save yourself the frustration and invest your time elsewhere.

Swipe your credit card to spend more money on a myriad ways of advancing your character or be on the dead-end of progression.The open world is not truly "shared" as they had claimed, instead it is designed in layers that you oftentimes won't bump into other players. _childDocuments_.review: A very unpolished game. It feels like those spinoff mobile games that copies another game and tries to take all your money.The amount of glitches, bugging character movements, unnecessary travelling for dialogue, lack of optimized organization of UI(UI is a lot easier to access on mobile), lack of explaining of currencies/mechanics, amount of real money needed for loadouts..Has only made one this real clear about the game, is it's design to siphon as much money out of the users as possible before they leave. If you sit in town for long enough the music will BLAST your ears out. Doing side quests with multiple parts is annoying to track as it redirects to the main quests. Calling your mount sometimes turns your character in a random direction(not ideal when near cliffs), and many more lol.The game places A LOT of orbs you can collect around the map to spin for the Gatcha system. It is fun to collect them, but it does become overwhealming at the speed you are introduced to new areas. The orbs you can collect basically only roll you garbage materials with a 000.30% of rolling of the most valuable weapons but even then if it is not the weapon you want to choose for your loadout it also becomes garbage. The game doesn't give you enough resources to fully upgrade all the weapons you acquire so you have to be specific on which weapons you want to focus all of your resources on... or spend money to deck out all of the high tier equipment you acquire.  These orbs around the world is another marketing scheme to get users addicted to rolling the gacha system and also make the user feel more invested in game, but really has little value.As you get higher level the game the quests start to outgrow character. Monsters and bosses in the stroyline has become a lot longer to kill, but also do almost 0 damage to me which is very confusing. A more difficult challenge is fun but can't help but notice it's the games way of trying to make you spend more money to feel stronger for the quests again. The co-op system leaves a lot to be desired. It is better co-op than Genshin but still restricts you from a lot of content. I am playing with my girlfriend and it would be nice to help and be there w/ her for the quests. Most co-op content is either collect the low-value orbs around the map or do end game content together.You can tell they spent more time polishing the beginning of the game. The story line is dry sprinkled with interesting moments. You can tell the voice actors recorded their lines separately and not together in a session.I do enjoy the combat system and fighting with different weapons and using different relics to get around the map. There are some things that I like about the game but the negatives outweighs the positive heavily that it makes it hard to remember. I'll be using this game as a placeholder til Blue Protocol comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game may not be as polished as others  "Gacha" type games, I genuinely enjoy playing this game, and to be frank, that's all that matters at the end of the day.What really captivated me was the world/level design, some parts of the world are absolutely stunning and i find myself immersed in just enjoying the views around me, i'm convinced if the budget was larger, and the game was polished as much as the environments are, the game would be on the apex of ftp games, especially considering how generous they are with resources.Again i want to give huge props to the world/environment designers, it has made the game visually stunning, and exploration a delightful experience. I love the inclusion of different relic variations that adds to the excitement of traversing the world as well, like the grappling hook, glider, mounts, hover boards and much more! I see heaps of potential here.Now sure the game isn't without it's flaws, the animations are pretty bad, i'd even say some cut scene animations are so awful they are comical. The mounts feel stiff and awkward, and movement overall is pretty clunky.but putting that aside there are things to make up for that, as clunky as the combat may be, it actually is one of the games strong points. The storytelling is engaging enough to keep me invested (though barely.) Other content such as raids, PvP, and world bosses greatly enhances the end-game content.Overall, I am genuinely glad that I decided to check this game out, but i'm left with a bitter sweet taste of lost potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: + Plenty of ways to earn summons for new SSR characters/weapons.    (VERY F2P friendly)+ A lot of Multiplayer PVE/PVP content for you and your friends to do together.    (In comparison to something like Genshin Impact)+ A lot of story and exploration content for a new player.   (Almost overwhelming at times with how much stuff there is to do.)+ Fun Gameplay Mechanics and the fighting itself feels really good on both KBM and Controller.+ Helpful and active community (INSIDE the game through Global chat)+ New major content every 2-3 months + Really great character creation and clothing/accesories (With the option to look like other characters you obtain)Cons:- The graphics look slightly dated compared to the likes of Genshin Impact or Honkai Star-rail. - The community outside of the game itself is non-existent making it hard to find how-to videos or build videos that are relevant at the time of writing this review.- Customer support is awful and isn't the quickest at helping resolve issues. - There are a few game breaking bugs that need to be fixed because they can full on halt progress until you can get a hold of support. - The UI can be a lot at first and could frustrate controller players. - The story isn't all that great overall very cookie cutter with some really great parts sprinkled in. (Just wish there was more of them) If 1 is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and 10 is utter perfection. This game can sit comfortably at a 7. If you like Gacha games, aren't a whale and wanna play with your friends this is your game. Though Isn't winning any awards at this moment but has great potential to.

_childDocuments_.review: -Combat that's more interesting than just "short click" and "long click". At times, it feels only a step below Naraka Bladepoint.-Customization of your main player character. As someone who loves character customization and was a bit disappointed by the lack of this in Genshin, ToF certainly does it justice. Just make sure you create the character you want when you begin the game, or you'll literally pay later.-Impossibly hefty rewards for...getting a life?!? I've never felt so honored for going outside to touch grass in my entire existence. Jokes aside, this is sadly both a blessing and a curse. I'll explain more later.-A daily grind that doesn't require you spending 30 minutes to an hour running around like an errand boy, doing the same quests over and over again. Unless you want to take part in an event, it literally just consists of collecting some shinies from a couple different menus and upgrading your gear.-Way too many gacha. Even for a gacha game. Genshin usually has four options you can order from at any one time, but ToF currently has about ten, and most of them you need unique currency for. I'm not kidding.-Lack of diversity in unlockable player characters. 90% are waifus, 5% are boring husbandos (though this may change in the future), and 5% are children clad in clothing that would make even an anime fan like me blush. The worst part is, I don't even feel attached enough to bother playing as any of these characters, even the one or two I really like. The bonuses you get for playing as them are really insignificant.-Translations and voiceovers. I'll cut some slack for the devs here, since they definitely don't have as much time, money, and people on board as MiHoyo does. Just be aware that there is plenty of engrishy text and inconsistent voiceovers in ToF, which may be immersion-breaking for some people.-Meh storyline. It provides the framework for a fun roleplay with your friends, but in itself is pretty mundane. You almost never have any meaningful interactions or decisions, and... -Lack of an active player base. This part really, really sucks. More likely than not, you won't see ANY players at all until you reach Mirroria later in the game. Part of this is because players are more inclined to explore new maps, but I think it's also because there's just not any reason to play longer than collecting your daily shinies, MAYBE hitting a few events, and then logging out. The amount of rewards they give you for taking a break from the game for a couple of weeks certainly doesn't help, either.Conclusion:If neutral reviews existed, I would give this game one. However, I'm pretty bored of the constant pressure from Genshin to keep up with the storyline or else your friends and everyone else will leave you eating their dust, so I'm more inclined to leave this world better than I found it rather than dumping on the devs. :)

_childDocuments_.review: First things first this is a GATCHA game. A gatcha game is defined as : Gacha games are video games which encourage players to spend in-game currency for virtual items as they progress. In gacha games, items such as cards, weapons and characters can be won through a mechanism, similar to a prize machine, in which players pull, spin, or roll using in-game currency to receive a random itemNow that we understand that down to the review. Concept: You are an elite officer investigating a particular disturbance in the world regarding a super mineral. This mineral is highly toxic but powerful. You pull/roll for weapons, each weapon has a character model that you can switch to if you like the design or you can use your own character with the  weapon and  other character's passives.Pros:-good combat-anime style graphics that are well polished-open world, free explore-custom character creations - gatcha mechanic has generous rolls of compared to any other game in the genre. You are guaranteed a SSR character every 80 rolls. Game keeps tracks for you so you Know when you are close. You can save it for limited characters at 79 and they carry over to new banners( limited window characters). - Upgrades are easy to obtain for regular weapons and normal banner( you can pick the weapon you want after 120 pulls)- gatcha currency is abundant, you earn free Pulls everyday. - good return rate for Free-2-play users-subjective but characters are all feel and look unique, cute, sexy etc. -mounts -lots of freebies-incentives for multplayer, 8 man raids, group exploration, more exp. per party member, material donating to guild members-lots of activesCons: - story is generic, don't expect a complex level of story- PVP isn't balanced for casual players. There is a full meta where your favorite  PVE weapon might be useless. There is scaling of dmg and hp but not Upgrades and gear passives.- Events are uninteresting -everything is scaled for team play, activities are better in team/squad or group, you cannot solo World bosses unless you have invested some real $$$ for upgrades or have grind a decent amount of time- not great for causal first time gamers to this type of genre-SSRs or gold weapons/ characters are everything. regular SR are for beginner areas and are useless after outside of puzzles -out of user control: low server population, finding people or a dense populated servers can be difficult -time gate, some content gated by time. This can be good or bad. One you don't have to push so hard to the next level of upgrades and feel left behind. 2) if you live, eat and breath videogames you might feel frustrated on waiting if you like to binge everything. Conclusion: It is fun, dailies are quick and can be done in less than 30mins. Systems are very f2p friendly. Emphasis on muiltiplayer. Every activity progresses your character but you don't have to do them all.

_childDocuments_.review: Answer is... No... MC loses his memory at the start of the game, some people find you, heal you and for thanking them you do chore missions and then magically start bonding with them, one of them becomes sick, and his brother takes her and goes with some dangerous people to cure her sickness and you do everything you can do for finding them even they don't want to be found and even you saw them they do beat you up and go again and you try to find them again and again and do chore quests and sometimes, just sometimes some cool main quests along the way... As you can see story and story-telling are not good and the main quests are not that different either. Sadly most of the main quests are nothing more than doing some chores for learning some info about people we want to find and it's just plain boring... I totally understand MMO games having classic attend/delivery boy kind of quests, that's a normal thing but I hate it when the game actually does this for main quests... Why do I need to attend boy quests while I'm doing main quests? That's just boring and totally out of context with what the main story quest means. I wish there wasn't a lot of attend/delivery boy type of quest we have to do for progressing the main story. I mean there are some cool quests as well like the quest you disguise yourself as a guard and try to not take attention to yourself and try to save someone but their number is not good enough compared to those boring ass quests. It has a kind of similar open-world style to Genshin and there is a lot of box having loot and honestly, their numbers and items you got from them are annoying... They don't give anything important and they give a very less amount and their number is a lot... Nearly in every corner, you will see them and for opening, most of them you need to kill a bunch of enemy groups, at first it's not annoying but after some point, you just want to leave them and don't bother and do the main quest and stuff instead and it's very bad design, their number should be less and they should give more important items. And aside from that, the open world is full of the same boring collectibles like flowers, shells, etc. I mean design is cool sure but it doesn't feel like living open-world nor enjoyable to be inside of it. BTW we have some mounts you can use while exploring the open world but they do feel very slow and riding them feels like riding nothing, there is no feeling behind it and it's just weird.We have different weapons you can get with gacha pulls along with characters you can get and every weapon has different combos and gameplay mechanics which is cool and might be the reason can carry you while doing those boring quests and roaming around boring open-world. For me, it didn't work well enough because the enemy variety is bad... Aside from that base game mechanics are quite fast and sometimes the hit feeling feels a little bit weak but generally, it's good.Yes, the game let you create your own character which is cool and we have a system called Simulacra as well and it's actually pretty good. With this system, you can play as an NPC you got from gacha pulls and interestingly they have their own quests as well.Enemy variety is bad, I mean from the outside of look we have a lot of enemies looking different for sure but fighting with different enemies nearly always feels the same and BOSS'es are not that different either. Most of the BOSS fights feel the same and it's boring. And if it's not enough a lot of BOSS fight is literally scripted so even if you play like a chad you still gonna lose in the end... Yeah very cool...The game doesn't have pretty darn good or realistic-looking graphics, they do look good in their own style for sure but they don't look like needing a lot of hardware, but you are still getting a lot of FPS drop, that's annoying and it's not the only problem, there is a lot of things you might get crash like trying to enter star gates, etc.  Or most of the time character's voice lines and mouth movements don't even match, considering this is one of the rare games MC actually has a voice line and this bug exist just makes that good feature darn annoying... Long story short this game is not stable at all and they should have optimized this game better. Especially releasing 2.0 and having this poorly optimized game is darn nonsense... They should have made better optimization before adding more content, if players can't have stable gameplay then what's the point of adding more content?Honestly, I tried my best for sticking more but nearly all of my playtime was boring AF with those chore-styled so-called ''main quests'' and boring open-world. If you really, really, really love these anime-style games with hot and cute-looking girls, etc, and don't care even if it's boring and needs MMO to play then you might enjoy but if you are not that into these types of games this game is not for you. Even I, a guy who like these type of games couldn't enjoy them because of reasons I told. I can't say I had big hopes, I started with very low expectations, but I was kind of hoping this could be MMO I can spend at least 100 hours and not drop after 10-15 hours...

_childDocuments_.review: is frequently frustrating, unpolished and suffering from generally poor design, but it's an audacious effort you can't help but applaud. It's a hilariously stupid idea cobbled together into some bastard child of  and, somehow, . I have no idea what the story is about, but I would expect that many will begin to power-scale the awe-inspiring feats of the squirrel in the coming weeks of online discourse (spoiler: he's like the rodent Goku). Despite obvious flaws, like the poor controls, short and repetitive gameplay, and the "instructions unclear" sandbox experience that had me confused constantly - I still enjoyed it. It's a collectathon puzzle-platformer game that does very little to impress and lacks a cohesive artistic vision to tie together its ridiculously high-quality UE5 assets. But whatever, it's a game about a squirrel with a gun. I got exactly what I paid for and even a few surprises. The indie scene never fails to amaze me.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost: Is this a fun game? Yeah, it's alright.More information: This game is alright and also please note that the tags are wrong. This is mainly a puzzle platformer that allows you to cause more and different chaos as you unlock more tools to get more places. Do you shoot people? Absolutely. Do you do stuff like climb on top of agents and kill them? Without question. And also the game is mainly a puzzle platformer where you use the guns to get to different locations and you can also use your squirrel abilities to do the same.Problems: Boy are these controls floaty and don't even try playing with keyboard and mouse. The camera moves way too fast for the mouse and that makes it even harder to aim your jumps. If you're playing with a controller then it's a fair bit easier. It solves the camera problem - more or less, it's still awkward sometimes - but it's still a little hard to aim your jumps. The guns are really hard to use as weapons, too. The camera and the floaty controls make it hard to aim and then the kickback of each shot means you have to re-align the shots. And when you throw things you have to hold the trigger button and slowly aim where you want to hit. This is why I say it's more a puzzle platformer than it is an open world shooter.Also: IT DOES NOT HAVE AN AUTO-SAVE FUNCTION. REPEAT, IT DOES NOT HAVE AN AUTOSAVE FUNCTION. In order to save you have to go to a birdfeeder and you'll get a prompt to use it. If you don't do this then you won't save your progress.Things that would fix the problems: First, the floaty controls. The squirrel needs to have a little bit of weight to it. Secondly the fighting needs some smoothing. I'd love to see an actual lock-on method - if it has one I haven't figured it out - because it would fix the weapon problem entirely. Also, auto-save and/or immediate save rather than having to find a specific locationOverall: Like I said, the game's alright. I've paid more for games I liked a lot, lot less. And also if I said it's not because of the entire ability to be a squirrel and have a gun I would be a liar. The level to which I love squirrels overcomes many of these problems and if you don't also love squirrels then the game might be a little less than alright for you. If you're looking for a game that's *only* open world chaos then you'll also be disappointed. But if you're looking for a neat little puzzle platformer that has a ridiculous premise then yeah, this is solid enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and funny game, though rough around the edges and way too short. It's like if Goat Simulator actually had good mechanics. It is a very short game, you'll only get 5-7 hours of gameplay out of it realistically. Given that and its general lack of polish, it really isn't worth $20. I honestly figured this game had a team less than half the size that it actually did, and I still expected it to be over twice as long. 128 people helped make this, and the game has been in development for at least two years, which just makes me wonder where all of that effort went.Wait for a sale below $15 and pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny, but not as funny as I would have figured. Also incredibly short in duration. I expected a lot more neighborhood to explore and general content. This seems more like an early access offering. As it is now there's just a few blocks of town and a water slide park which is an odd choice here but whatever. Honestly this is one of those situations where I would prefer to give the game a middle of the road recommendation not that great, not that bad either. Once the game is completed there isn't much in the way of replay value. Hopefully the dev team will spend some more time expanding the world as I think there is plenty of potential here.

_childDocuments_.review: There is definitely some polish needed for this game when it comes to the audio or an NPC bugging out, but the game is solid, simple, and fun and does it job amazingly. If you enjoyed Super Mario Odyssey, this is basically that, but you're a squirrel that gets to shoot three letter agents. What's not to love? The boss fight music is hilariously awful, and the first boss definitely could have been less tedious, but the second boss was great. Again, this game was solid, the environments were surprisingly varied for what the game is. Game is 100%able in about 11 hours, so factor that in to the price. Either way, I had a lot of fun, and wouldn't be against a sequel of sorts.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Squirrel with a Gun wears its ridiculous concepts as a badge of honor. It gives you what it says it will in a package that’s familiar and fun in a way that I assume would meet everyone’s expectations. However, this game, and some like it, do this in a way where it’s hard to tell what is just silly design, and what is non-functional design and/or bugs. Which makes me wish, in this case, I could provide more of a “maybe” than a real recommendation.Abbreviated Review: Despite its name, the guns in Squirrel with a Gun are mostly a secondary aspect of the overall game. There are plenty of them available and they can be used for more than simply shooting at the many agents that come after you with their respective weapons, but they’re only a portion of the gameplay. Especially since you can’t climb while holding one and, as a squirrel, that’s a pretty important skill.The bulk of the gameplay is a combination of platforming and puzzle solving to collect both the large and small acorns that are scattered around the relatively small open-world map. The small acorns are plentiful and are produced from practically every activity – whether it’s taking out an agent or just being photographed by a random friendly NPC. The larger acorns are typically awarded for solving a puzzle, climbing to a lofty location, or a combination of both. These are the foundation of your progression in the game and unlock new regions through various means.Unlocking new areas typically involves an introduction to a boss or a boss fight, each of which is one of the more compelling parts of the game. Here, you’ll use your gun far more than other points in the game. So much so that I had to switch from my controller to keyboard and mouse just to facilitate more precise aiming. Yet, the fights themselves were generally forgiving enough that they didn’t disrupt the flow of the game. There are plenty of disruptions to the flow of Squirrel with a Gun. While it does take advantage of the sillier animations and quirky physics in its design, several bugs compromise the gameplay. For instance, there are parts where you need to place objects on the ground or in certain areas, but NPCs that randomly follow you around will kick them out of that placement. There are also RC cars and boats that are challenging to maneuver in any productive way but are required to be used in many locations. And all of that is a backdrop to the constant issue of simply being able to control your squirrel avatar with any reliability. Here, the touchy, loose controls make the persistent platforming that comprises the bulk of the game excessively difficult for challenges that would be a breeze in other platformer games.Yet, the most egregious interruption to the flow of the game is the save system. It has prompted save options after key events like boss fights, but predominantly you’re required to go to static save points to do all of the rest of your saving. That’s not a huge problem in itself, but it is an issue that leaving the game and returning to those saves will respawn all enemies and, surprisingly, erase various parts of the progress you’ve made. Not only will it erase the partial progress you’ve made on puzzles, but it will reset completed puzzle areas for seemingly no reason. The latter doesn’t affect your ability to move forward, but it’s just an annoyance to have gone through the processes to accomplish something only to not have that reflected in the world after loading a save.The issues that I had with Squirrel with a Gun are notable, but they didn’t completely destroy the game for me. They certainly made it annoying, but I think they’re issues that can be resolved. And even if they aren’t all addressed, there’s still some really fun stuff in the game that does work. I loved most of the puzzle designs, even when the solutions were a bit too obfuscated, and it made a collectathon-style game that didn’t feel as ‘by the numbers’ as they typically are. Plus, the boss fights were solid.The only other complaints I have are that the game’s performance is inconsistent and overall, not very good for something that isn’t all that visually impressive. It could definitely use some optimization. The soundtrack is also a little repetitive. It uses different twists on a core motif, but the main song is extremely prominent, and it got old within the first hour of playing.So while this review does state that it’s recommended, be aware that it is not a great game. Without some noteworthy fixes and perhaps fundamental changes to the way saving in the progression system is handled, it’s barely more than an “Ok” experience. However, there is a lot of charm to it and if you can get it on sale (and perhaps after some patches) it might be worth your time and money.

Go eat some more acorns.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a funny and novel concept with some unique gameplay ideas but it’s marred by some pretty bad controls, uninspired level design, and shallow gameplay depth.The squirrel is the only thing that looks good in this game, while everything else looks cheap and unpolished. Each weapon you use has 1 finishing animation. The controls for our squirrel hero are floaty and imprecise. I found myself dying repeatedly in areas of the game that I’m certain were not meant to be difficult. If not for the wonky controls, this game would be pretty easy. There are some delays as well which is especially noticeable when trying to bounce on the umbrellas. M&k is all-around pretty awful to play given the floaty controls and shooting feels really weird on a controller, but I think I'd recommend  a controller.The world is small and exploration is rather minimal if you’re comparing the sandbox, open-world platforming-style gameplay to something like Goat Simulator. It’s sometimes funny, and it can be fun if you like very minimalist gameplay. But those of us who have been around the block and played a game or 2 in our life will find that the game reveals itself to be a bit shallow in depth and the novelty wears thin after a short while.I don’t want to say it’s a bad game, it’s just not great. I didn’t expect much, but I was hoping it to be as engaging as something like Goat Sim, which is by far and wide a better game.Another game not making it past the refund window.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this almost as a joke with fairly low expectations. I honestly thought it was going to suck, to my surprise this game blew me away with its humour, graphics, and detail. This game is made with more love and care by its developers then most modern triple A titles and it really shows. The soundtrack is incredible and truly makes you feel like badass. Right when you load up the game there's a original song for the title screen, I've only fought the first boss but there's an original (and quite awesome may I add) song for that too and I imagine the other bosses have original music in them as well. The cutscenes like the one where you first obtain a gun and the one when you beat the first boss are awesome and hilarious. The animations when you do a takedown on an enemy are different for each weapon you use and every one of them (that I have seen thus far) are epic.However, I do have some slight critiques with the game. The currency which you collect by casually playing the game (standard/bronze acorns) are used for most things you can unlock (weapons, vehicles, ext). They aren't too difficult to obtain but most things are priced very highly and the only way that I've come across to quickly get a lot of them is taking out enemies and robbing civilians you find around the town. The problem with this is after a while the combat gets pretty old and it feels a little grindy. A couple ways I could see this problem being solved is lowering the price of items you find around town considering they are already locked behind the amount of gold acorns you have obtained (this games equivalent of stars in a Mario game), or give the player bronze acorns for doing things such as beating bosses or obtaining all collectables in an area (Mean Streets, Spice House, ext). I've seen some people complaining about the movement and/or controls of the game but I personally have had no problem with them. The platforming for me has been a fun and enjoyable experience.Overall I'd definitely recommend this game for anyone looking for a laugh and feeling of badassery. I think it's fairly priced and I can't wait to finish the game and to see more content being added from the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, so, where to start...I've followed this game for a while and was really interested in it, when I got the notification this morning that it was available finally I bought it right away, I was /excited/, I'd been looking forward to this for a /while/, I had a group of people /excited/ about this game who also wanted to buy it, they were looking forward to watching a quick stream of it before buying it.I opened the game, ignored a few red flags I'll get to later, started a new save and after a fairly cute cutscene.... I was instantly confused with what was going on with the game play.The game is first and foremost a "puzzle platformer" as it makes painfully obvious in the tutorial, and once the shock of what the game actually is wears off, you'll immediately notice that the controls are horrific, the worst, they're clunky yet floaty, the camera is offset but only sometimes, its all just.... weird and feels wrong, frustrating, bad and wrong.  Maybe the controls were only playtested with a controller? I have no idea but mouse and keyboard controls are just horrendious and you'd think that would be the default in a game where you are a squirrel that has a gun to shoot, you know... aim? Oh boy, speaking of aiming, yeah, you are severely limited in the vertical range you can aim, another aspect that seems to support that this game was made for controllers possibly?The entire 'feel' of the movement and controls is bad, but its made worse by way of not being able to change keybindings, etc.  If you are someone who's really used to doing things like, oh, you know, pressing shift to sprint you'll be constantly randomly throwing things because shift is... throw? Why? You want to reload? That Q.... excuse me what? The controls very mcuh seem like they were laid out by someone who really isn't familiar with or plays a lot of the rooty-tooty-shooty games and that brings me back to the first problem.Its a platform puzzle game, NOT A SHOOTING GAME, most of the time you aren't even allowed to hold the gun if you want to do things, you are constantly forced by the game to put down whatever you are holding to do something that forces you to leave it behind in order to continue the platforming and puzzle stuff, which is the core of the game.  You can't call a game "Squirrel with a Gun" and then have the "with a Gun" part be such an after thought that the game actively has mechanics to discourage you from the "with a Gun" part of the game, what is the point? I genuinely am just /mystified/ at how something like this could happen, its like the developers didn't understand the appealing part of the product, the 'with a Gun' part, they focused completely on the 'platform puzzle' part which is the part that wasn't openly advertised or shown off in the marketing.During the tutorial, I was able to /accidentally/ soft lock myself time and time again, this shouldn't happen in a tutorial.... I had enemies constantly getting stuck in the floor unable to move in the exceedingly few times they're even featured, on top of that there's little to no bones in explaining things in the tutorial which makes the unexpected and frankly unwelcome style of game play that much more jarring to experience. A game like this shouldn't need a tutorial like this, it should be a wacky fun sandbox game with organic silly fun things to discover and screw around with tool tops that pop up when you first encounter different things, it shouldn't be platforming sections with targets to shoot to open doors, what? The layout of the tutorial its self is just bad because you are in a fairly dark area most of the time, the squirrel is dark, and the edges of the platforms are dark/black... so you are thrown into a worse case scenario for a third person platform game since the tutorial, the thing thats supposed to be easy and inviting puts you in a situation where judging where you are at the edge of a platform is inherently difficult, this coupled with the just atrocious controls makes for some mightly unsatisfying play.The enemies are bullet sponges and it doesn't seem to matter where you hit them, they just have a health bar, shooing someone nearly point blank in the head makes a green bar go down a bit.... its so immensely unsatisfying, you are a squirrel with a gun, the gun play should be weighty and satisfying, when I shoot the gun and it send my flying back a bit only for it to barely stagger the person I'm shooting and do almost no real damage is so... so... /so/... SO.... just /bad/, its actively unsatisfying.Ok, I have to stop here, I have a lot I could say, a lot I still want to say, there's just... a lot that's wrong, a lot that needs some big time critique but its going to seem like I'm punching down.I don't want to punch down on the developer, I don't want to be mean, I want indie developers and studios to succeed and I wish them well, but this game feels like a very strange bait and switch, it feels like it was advertised to be one thing and its a whole other thing entirely, I have never... EVER refunded a game on Steam, if a game is 'bad' and I bought it, I'll just say "meh, my bad I guess" and move on, but this game is the first game I've requested a refund on and I'm kinda sad to say that.This is a game I watched and waited for a pretty long time, its jolting to buy something you've been following along with and get what feels like something else entirely.I wanted to play a wacky open world game where a squirrel has a gun and the squirrel having guns and causing chaos was the focus, I didn't want a game about jumping puzzles and the marketing didn't seem to try and sell me one either, it seemed to try and sell me a game... about a squirrel... with a gun.... causing chaos...I'm so confused and disappointed with what ever happened, how the game shifted focus or lost its track is just really disappointing.Again, developer, I'm not trying to be mean, I wish you the best, but... I don't think you understood the appealing part of the equation for most people?

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of a "Squirrel with a Gun" serves as an intriguing metaphor that invites exploration into themes of power, survival, and the subversion of traditional hierarchies in nature. This imagery juxtaposes the typically innocuous and playful characteristics associated with squirrels against the violent connotation of firearms. The result is a striking representation of how even the most seemingly benign creatures can embody unexpected forms of agency when placed in precarious circumstances. Through this lens, one can examine how environmental pressures may drive animals to adapt behaviors that challenge their stereotypical roles within ecosystems.Moreover, the notion of a squirrel wielding a gun raises questions about anthropomorphism and our tendency to project human qualities onto animals. This phenomenon is particularly relevant in contemporary discussions surrounding wildlife conservation and animal rights. By attributing weaponry to such a creature, we implicate ourselves in a narrative that critiques human dominance over nature. It highlights the absurdity of equating power with violence while simultaneously encouraging empathy towards animals often perceived as mere pests or nuisances within urban settings.In conclusion, the "Squirrel with a Gun" operates on multiple levels; it serves not only as an emblematic critique of societal norms but also as an invitation for deeper reflection on our relationship with wildlife. As we navigate issues related to habitat destruction and climate change, this image compels us to reconsider our understanding of agency within non-human species. Ultimately, it challenges us to recognize that vulnerability does not preclude strength and that all creatures possess unique strategies for survival in an increasingly complex world.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for almost a year for this and I'm rather disappointed.- No option to keybind or even view controls- Main Menu / Menu system has no mouse control, feels very plain and just a few widgets thrown together.- Sensitivity and general controls are very touchy and overly sensitive (even with sensitivity turned out)- The target when choosing to throw an item is clear and practically invisible when on the main streets.- Even when you hide in bushes and run away the AI will hunt you down and kill you regardless of you being stealthed.- The camera snaps are not smooth and incredibly annoying.- Once the tutorial level is done you're just left in a sandbox mode with no side quests, no objectives nothing... pretty boring.- The AI moves very oddly, non-smooth.- Huge lack of content/lore/objectivesThe pro's would be:- Squirrel animals are great- The bones for the squirrel have been rigged really nicely when holding weapons, interacting with objects/vehicles.This feels like the developer worked their butts off then rushed at the last moment.I'd honestly say this is 90% complete but there's a few major issues that need to be resolved.Unfortunately I can't recommend the game with the state it's in, maybe in a few months ill check back at any progress.but for now, there's too many bugs and lack of content for me to enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial game play takes:I'll admit, I was following this game on twitter and was looking forward to it. I bought it pretty quick after launch. Because of the tutorials, and I'll get back to them, I was desperately trying to figure out how some of this stuff worked and what buttons to press.Tutorials: It's either random button prompt icons on the screen or short descriptions that don't include the button prompts.Scripted events: In an open world game, I understand scripted events aren't ideal. But, for a tutorial they are necessary. I had to figure out how to throw things accurately by looking at a game play video! (again, just a button map to tell me what controls does would have saved me some time!) And the scripted event to teach me how to break someones neck? What is the point of a tutorial if you can't teach someone how things are supposed to work?Lack of an aim: I'm not going to complain about lack of a goal, it's open world. Yeah, collecting Golden Acorns is cool, and apparently one of the things squirrel me wants to do is brake open all these glass cases and kill people/joy ride with whats in them. _childDocuments_.review: for too long has traditional media painted rodents as either pest or prey, willfully playing into untrue stereotypes about these beautiful creatures. mice need to be saved from cats. all rats are dirty. youve heard it all before. its a tired rhetoric made and perpetuated by people who know nothing about actual rodents. however, squirrel with a gun takes that narrative and flips it on its head. this game stands in stark contrast to the ignorant anti-rodent slander, instead choosing to empower a squirrel. in this story, rodents finally have a sense of agency over their lives. does the squirrel stand by helplessly, waiting to be exterminated? ♥♥♥♥ no. the rodents in this media are strong and have the tools they need to defend themselves and their caches. sometimes that tool is a shotgun, other times its a charmingly small car. but the fact remains that in the world of squirrel with a gun, rodents are not to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥ with. finally, a piece of media that does justice to a class of animal so brave, resilient, and intelligent. rodents are getting the respect they deserve in this game. while the controls are clunky and the game has its flaws, i will continue to support such an important work in the fight for rodent empowerment. i stand by and even applaud the message portrayed in squirrel with a gun. it is a long overdue critique of anti-rodentism and should be celebrated as such.tldr; 9/10 driving the car is so ♥♥♥ hard but i will always support pro-rodent media

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - This is not release-ready for the price point. I applaud the devs for being bold and sticking to a higher price, and if they shoot for the quality required for that, this can be a great and fun casual game. Game Breaking==============As of now there are a lot of bugs that result in "LowLevel" crashes despite any settings. Coupling this behavior with the lack of any autosave mechanics means that you need to be saving every minute minimum to even progress, which makes this practically unplayable imo.Mildly Annoying==============the controls need work as the camera movements are very janky, but you can get used to it. Speaking of the camera you can easily get disoriented near surfaces due to the way the depth of field focuses solely on the character, blurring out everything else (which can be a pain if you are trying to throw something and use the targeting arc). To be honest I really think that even the crashes could be manageable if there was some sort of periodic autosave so you don't need to completely redo what is already a repetitive format. And again, if the price was closer to $5 I could probably look beyond even the crashes since it is an indie game. I will wait before coming back to this.

_childDocuments_.review: Squirrel with a Gun has its charms, it's got a squirrel, it's got guns, so it's definitely got that part right, but for me, the controls just feel way too floaty for me. For a game which seems to feature platforming quite heavily, there just isn't enough accuracy in the movement and jumping for it to feel fair.The game looks great, thanks to it being made in the Unreal Engine, and the little cutscenes during the tutorial are nice, but the breaks in gameplay go on for far too long. The game will stop to explain a mechanic and forces you to wait too long whilst it spins around showing you the thing you just picked up.Little QoL changes need to be introduced as well, for example, having centred crosshairs instead of having it towards the top of the screen, as well not having the throw curve be transparent. The pole climbing makes sense gameplay wise, but personally, it would make sense to have a small bit of magnetism so I'm not killed by a slight angle miscalculation.Overall, a pretty fun idea, just needs that last bit of polish before it's a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ funny. You are a squirrel, you have a gun. You can shoot folks, you can rob folks, you can ride a car, you can break into houses. It is a visceral crossover between GTA and mario. I have been waiting for this game for a very long time. I had my expectations, I had my fears. _childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to recommend this game at its price point. It's a quirky and silly game with issues that add up.The humour of the game lands for me personally, so I still found enjoyment playing the game. I think one of the best parts were the enemy ragdolls. The gunplay is serviceable at best. It does its job.The platforming and camera felt atrocious. Movement had no feel of drag or acceleration and finding a good angle for the camera was difficult. Many collectables were extremely high up and the camera in many cases wouldn't pan that high. In other cases, walls were so close that the camera was obstructed, pushing it so close to the squirrel that I couldn't see anything, even in the middle of jumps.The game suffers from terrible performance and isn't visually very interesting. Turning down graphics settings seems to mess up LOD of guns so badly that even up close they look broken. Fused trigger guards, large gaps between edges, etc.I can appreciate the novelty of Squirrel with a Gun and it's not a punishing game in the slightest which offsets the faults it has. It's difficult for me to say would I recommend it or not, though if anyone comes up to me asking if this game is worth their 20€ without more context, I would say no. I would pick Squirrel with a Gun over almost any AAA title these days though that's for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Reminiscent of games like Goat Simulator, Squirrel with a Gun allows you to terrorize civilians and enemies alike with all sorts of weapons. I will say, it is very bare bones in the sense that it doesn't feel like there is any real objective to the game other than collecting golden acorns and outfits. I did, however, enjoy the tank boss fight underground. Another issue I have with this game is you can't really customize any of the graphical settings nor the keybinds. I have had this game wishlisted since 2020, and now that it is finally out, it offered a bit more than I expected of it (which is good). Another issue I have is the fact that you can't sprint. If you want to go fast, you need to use the car, which is unnecessarily difficult to maneuver. The saving mechanic doesn't really make sense - you have to go to a specific location to save your progress and there is absolutely no indication if your game has autosaved or not. Lastly, I think the movement mechanics are a bit annoying. There were times when I was doing parkour where I would click jump and I would not jump at all. All in all, the game needs more polishing, and I have yet to complete it, but I think it is a fun singleplayer experience overall.

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT IS THIS GAME?!? WHO's INSANE IDEA WAS THIS?!? Because that person is amazing and deserves to be paid more.
