_childDocuments_.review: I've played for a while and essentially it's an unlock-a-thon before meeting up to defeat the boss for that stage and moving on unlocking other areas, costumes, guns, and so on. Here's the thing, it's fun! Don't expect anything crazy here or reinventing the wheel, it's a 3D platform shooter with puzzles. Some are easy to understand and others are not so easy, but overall it's a fun game.The not so good is the controls take some getting used to. The puzzles sometimes can be frustrating. The save system is not fun at all. The level reset each time you load can be frustrating because it also resets the puzzles themselves even if the puzzle is completed. There are some things that can be improved upon, but I'm already looking forward to a squeekquel.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually really fun. You wouldn't expect it to be particularly fun outside of exploiting jank, like with Goat Simulator, but that's not what you'll get with this game. Starting out it can be difficult to figure out the weapon recoil and how the squirrel controls, but you get used to it pretty quickly. Plus, despite there being some jank in the game, it's mostly related to animations and not the gameplay itself, I've not once actually encountered a bug that prevented me from progressing or got me stuck, though that could change as I continue to play.I really appreciate that you can redo all of the content in the game too without having to make a new save like in most games. All you do is reload your save and everything in the map is refreshed, but your progress is the same. The way it works reminds me of Super Mario 64 or Galaxy. I think the devs are actually pretty big nintendo fans, given the credits sequence as well. The Looney Toons-esque sense of humor is a great addition as well.I'd recommend this game, I had a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: this game is addictively good! idk how to put into words, it really is as the title suggests and as good if not better than the initial trailer for the game! it has met expectations and then some, i love how it exposes you to various mechanics and concepts as you play along, some things arent even tutorialised, its just.. oh turns out you can perform takedowns on enemies! discovering new ways to play is very fun!if you mix small elements of gta, with some parkour/platforming, and slight collectafun elements.. then you have this game of awesomeness! it doesnt take itself serious at all its very aware its a jokey comedy game and that really works well in its favor!i was admittedly a lil confused at first, the golden acorns at vendor points were slightly confusing but i realised that they are only for collection purposes (so far) and wont take away from your total found/earned compared to the actual currency!i also love how the healing works! that was a nice touch i onyl realised as i played more!the enemies remind me of a cross between the matrix agents, and the enemies in saints row... i dont knwo fully why but its hilarious! 10/10 game found it hard to put down.also final note: dont forget you can only save at bird feeders, or after defeating a boss!

_childDocuments_.review: first of all, i had been looking forward to it for a while, and from what i had seen, was going to be something akin to goat simulator but just a squirrel with a gun, this is not the case but instead feels like a ps1/2 era game (not the good ones) where you just collect stuff and the shooting gun part is more-so an afterthought.controls are also an annoying combination of clunky and floaty, meaning more than once you will see yourself dead, and all the accorns you got until a certain point between ''checkpoints'' will now respawn and you'll have to collect them againi might have missed the visual cue, but i could not find a save option *anywhere*, and instead hoped it had frequent checkpoints/auto saves, and since i couldnt find a manual save option i decided to quit and hope the aforementioned checkpoint/auto was the case, it was not and i lost all my progress.from commercials/ads leading up to it i was also lead to believe that the squirrel could kill ALL characters, aside from the people pursuing it, but after unloading an entire 2 magazines of SMG into a passerby and said passerby getting up like it was no problem, im now quite dissapointed.it feels like they tried to make the next untitled goose game, but it just is not hitting that same sweet niche spotmaking it story-driven instead of sandbox driven (like goat simulator) is a huge mistake in my opinion, and its $17 WITH a launch discount? just buy some better games with that, since its story driven it means they have already made everything, and something like lethal company ($15 base] keeps getting updated and keeps things fresh, thats a anecdote ofc but i digress, the point being i do NOT think Squirrel with a gun is worth the nearly regular price of $20on a positive note, the cinematics and executions are pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good, i just really wish it didnt try a half-baked 50% story 50% sandbox (which isnt even real sandbox)

_childDocuments_.review: I have waited for this game since day F$#)-ing one! Knowing that when this game comes out, it will take parts from what I love from suburban areas games like goat simulator, Postal 2, and Over the Edge the game, and take the free-to-roam collectathon games like Mario 64, and Conkers Bad Fur Day. To which it totally did, except the more I play the game, the more humor you wouldn't expect to get from playing it. Squirrel with a gun is similar to goat simulator in premise, but refined with third-person 3D shooters. Sure you get the standard simulation squirrel physics, but its more of let's do that but give the squirrel a literal gun and see what happens, the game has this open sense of freedom when trying to complete a mission. Take for example; one mission where you get to collect one golden acorn in a land mine field, you can try to find a costume or you could use a shotgun to propel yourself up-word to get it. Freedom is what this game gives you. It's like the freedom you get from games like Grand Theft Auto where you cause destruction and drive around cars and kill random by standards, trying to beat objectives with platforming games like Mario 64 which also provides you the freedom to roam and explore and collect coins but you do other ways to get collectibles.  but you get all of that with a squirrel firing a gun into a tank causing it to explode to get a golden acorn collectible. Sure, the game needs more polish, it does tend to have the standard slowdowns when agents pile on the screen when you toss a grenade. But to where it stands this is the most fun I have had with a game in a long time! I genuinely mean it! After experiencing games that I have been hyped for over and over only to be meant with disappointment. Genuinely I'm surprised to finally get a game I was hyped for, before coming out, had defined my expectations and then some. This is not just a squirrel simulator, this is what if we gave the squirrel a gun and then the squirrel said: "HELL YEAH, I HAVE THE POWER OF GOD!" simulator.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: So far, so good.  Really enjoy the game play and concept.  Puzzles are not overly challenging but enough to keep you interested in moving forward. I still recommend it with the hopeful assumption more is on the way.  Maybe develop some co-operative missions and pvp arenas to go with it???
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I've gotten through the tutorial section and have to say I like how the squirrel can use the gun for combat and puzzle solving and platforming. Sometimes you may need to shoot targets, sometimes you may need to use the gun to help perform a double or triple jump across a gap, or you can use an SMG to I guess to SMG jump to help the squirrel go high into the sky. It's also funny when the squirrel falls from a high distance and hits the ground with enough force to bounce off the ground. I also like the idea that to navigate sometimes the squirrel needs a gun while, while others the squirrel needs to be unarmed so you can climb. So far the game is pretty fun, looks good, the music is enjoyable and is just overall silly. Within the first opening moments of the game the squirrel breaks in somewhere it shouldn't be, steals a golden acorn, pisses off some agents, learns to use a gun to take out agents and perform platform jumping and escapes a base where the floor is actual lava. If that isn't a strong intro to a game I don't know what is, looking forward to playing more.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game for free to stream, but was going to buy it anyway even if I hadn't. My comments below are NOT affected by the fact that it was free.Absolutely awesome game. Hilarious silliness, a cute squirrel, big guns, silly abuse of physics, bosses that take some proper fighting, tons of outfits to collect (some with special effects), vehicles, and lots more... There's too many good points to list them all!Yes, there are one or two glitches, but far fewer than many other games, and the ones I've found are very easy to ignore in favour of the absolute insanity and fun factor.I don't think another game has made me smile as much as this one does. Certainly not in the last couple of years, and possibly ever...100% recommended. Don't even think about it. Just go and buy it already.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing the trailers I thought it would be an instant fun game that's about doing silly things with a squirrel, kind of like "Untitled Goose Game with guns". Turns out it's a hard punitive platformer puzzling game where you die every 20 seconds and the death screen lasts for 5 more. What the heck? The controls are far too random to allow for anything as precise as the platforming and gunslinging of the game. Many games have invisible tricks to make platforming easier but here you just fail by an unknown distance because the camera makes it hard to see whether or not you are on the platform yet, and then you end up in lava and you die.I would maybe be up if there was an easy mode, the death screen took under 1 second and the game supported keyboard rebinding.Gotta shoutout whoever did the music though.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright?Like, lots of parts of this game are pretty frustrating. Hardly any bullets are one hit kills. The finishers are just, one per gun.The game needs high graphical requirements despite literally hardly being anything more than graphics from 2012 unless you max out the fur and ray tracing (which my 3090 struggles to utilize at > 15 FPS). The controls are sucky on PC. I'd recommend a controller. The mouse doesn't interact with the menus at all and your menus are 100% keyboard options. The options menu has very few options which leaves a lot to be desired.Enemies either always hit you or barely miss you. A headshot doesn't kill, but rather stuns enemies. Doing finishers is the most reliable way to kill an enemy, but again, it's the same ones over and over.The game revolves around getting acorns, but most of the tasks to get acorns are platforming or grindy. The binary input of a keyboard makes this extremely difficult.Overall, it's Squirrel goat simulator but much much less polished at a similar price point as the original goat simulator. After you get passed the jokes and laughs of "haha it's a squirrel with a gun" you're stuck with a janky repetitive mess of a game unlike goat simulator that has other level options and a lot more to do with significantly more polish. For $15 on sale, I can see people liking it, but I wouldn't expect to get more than a few hours out of this one and I can't imagine paying full price for this either.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, I expected a funny game like Goat Simulator. This is not. It's a frustrating puzzler with sandbox areas—it's just tedious. WTF was that tank fight? Why are there puzzles in the first place? Why are the controls so tedious to use and janky? Once the funny effect wears off, this game is janky, tedious, and just not fun. And with no autosave, if you forget to save at the bird feeders, say goodbye to all that progress. Autosave or checkpoints should be the bare minimum.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun novelty game. Like, what to expect from a game with this premise? Probably not much. It doesn't take itself seriously, it's a way better 'Goat Simulator', with decent platform segments, a few puzzles and a good amount of collectibles. The overall design of the game and the many different 'areas' are great, it's a bit barebones but for an indie project it has a decent open-world, mostly lacking some sound design. I dislike the bosses but well it's not like there are a bunch of them anyways. I played with graphics on High and the performance was fine, the game itself is one big glitch from time to time but it feels a lot more like it was a design choice more than anything else (hence the Goat Simulator comparison).Overall, the word here is fun, I had a lot of fun, the squirrel is super cute, it's not a fantastic game by any means and I'd maybe recommend to wait a sale to get it (it's a bit short), but I don't really regret buying full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, the concept was funny, and the gameplay did show promise. However, just like my parents' marriage, my excitement for this game was not meant to last. The guns did not feel very good to shoot, driving the car or the boat was very clunky, and a lot of assets in the game don't look as if they had much time put into them. In the end, the game was very short, with little to no story, and I don't see much replay value in it. Was good for a couple of quick laughs, but that devolved into a repetitive acid trip that didn't feel very rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ridiculously cute, very entertaining and endlessly frustrating all at the same time. The clothes and accessories you find for the squirrel are adorable. The idea of a squirrel mugging someone with a double barrel shotgun is hysterical. The puzzles are challenging, and it doesn't hold your hand to get you through things. Very much reminds me of the Untitled Goose Game. The only real issue I have with the game is the controls are atrocious. Vague and drifty. They don't work until they do. For a game that has as much platforming as this does I'd like the controls to be tightened up. But overall, good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a generally fun puzzle platformer, hard carried by the title concept. Gun selection is limited but for how short the game is, but not bad. The shenanigans you can pull throughout the game were great (especially loved rocket jumping on people's heads) and the overkill nature of the finishers were a nice touch. I do have some concerns though. The vehicle controls are very touchy, and combined with the odd camera angles it makes for a tough time seeing where you are going or even getting there when you can see your target (especially if said target is up a ramp). I encountered 3 glitches during gameplay, two of which I was able to escape but one that was hard locked once activated. All in all, I'd give Squirrel with a Gun a 7/10 for what you get. Certainly worth playing on a slow day.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Progress breaking bug in the tutorial level.  in the part where you have to drop the gun to climb the pole there is a gun pickup station at the top where you need to pick up a gun to preform a series of double jumps. You can't pick up the replacement gun. Pressing the key the gun spawns but you cannot interact with it; the only way to progress is to reload from a checkpoint.  However once you get to the end of the double jump section there is an opportunity to buy an SMG and after paying for it the same issue happens where the gun spawns but you cannot interact. Also, mouse input doesn't work at the menus, no manual save and when you exit the game when you start it again your save is reset to the beginning. I suggest giving this a little while longer to cook since you really can't progress with this bug in place. I do not recommend this game at this time. I submitted a bug report on the discord bug report channel.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a $10 game at most. Unfortunately the novelty wears off pretty fast and the gameplay loop becomes very grindy within minutes of exiting the opening level. The devs placed prices (in-game currency, no mtx) around every weapon or key item with the exception of a few cosmetics. This wouldn't be so bad if the cost of some of these wasn't so outrageously large. I genuinely feel like I'm playing a free to play grind fest at the start. There are sections of the first level I literally couldn't figure out what the game wanted me to do as well. Like climb a tower. No clue how. Am I supposed to unlock the rocket launcher for 25 Gold Acorns and 1000 Bronze Acorns? No idea, but that would literally take me hours of grinding while also having to get enough to pay for a little toy car, which I'm assuming opens the level more for 12 Gold Acorns and 400 Bronze Acorns. All of this institutes a sense of false longevity that the game wouldn't be more than a few hours if the grind were removed. Which ultimately makes it all feel like a vast waste of time. I'd rather some thought had gone into level design and story around literally a Squirrel with a Gun, like even the opening music suggests. I'd rather there be more enemies to ease the grind even. But this feels more like a less expensive Ubisoft game and I can't stand Ubisoft games.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this a funny game? Of course.Is this a good game? Not at all.Within seconds of booting this up, I was sad to find that the funny lil' meme game we'd all been waiting for was in fact not good. The controls, and the camera, are abysmal. This game consists of the worst platforming you've ever played, poor visuals, and some of the worst combat you've ever played, all rolled into one. The camera and player character movement are both so janky and hard to control that it makes the platforming an imprecise mess. The combat is near nonexistent; each weapon only having one take-down animation that is quite funny and charming at first, but then you're forced to watch it over and over again in nauseam. This game is definitely charming, and funny, and has some great gags all hinged on what I consider to be a really great premise; a squirrel with a gun. Sadly though, it is so amateurishly made and poorly put together that you are left with a great premise wasted on a horrible game. Simply as a goof, this game would be fine, but charging upwards of $20 is ridiculous. It's not longer just a joke, meme-game at that point, it's robbery. At $5 I'd recommend it just for maybe an hour or two at most of laughs, at $20 it is a complete waste of money and you're better just watching someone play it and getting the jokes that way.My gameplay and impressions from the first half hour:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not what it claims to be. The title and videos show off "Squirrel with a GUN!!!" like it's going to be this crazy, silly shooter. But after 30 minutes, it felt more like a frustrating platformer with some shooting elements thrown in. The balance is all wrong.There is shooting, but it feels janky and unsatisfying. Janky shooting can be fun if that's the main focus, but here it's more like "kill 2 enemies with a pistol, now go platform some more." It doesn't work when it's just a small part of a mostly platforming game.The movement is hard to control, and you often can't tell how far you're jumping or where you'll land. You move almost too fast, and with the camera angle its so easy to miss a jump. Oh, and if you are close to a wall you can barely see what you are aiming at. Respawns/falls are annoying - fall off a platform, time to carefully walk back to a riser and not fall into the inexplicable lava which would set you back even further. There's barely any tutorial, so you're left to figure things out yourself.And get this - no unlimited ammo in a game that's supposed to be about a squirrel... with a gun...? No idea what you're even supposed to do if you run out. It's like they missed the whole point of their own concept.There is no option for anything other than full screen. In the forums a dev told people to use the Alt-Enter which puts it in windowed mode... not borderless.  Not even Borderless Gaming worked; well, it did make it borderless, but it refused to go fullscreen borderless. I'm not usually this annoyed by a game, but when something promises fun and delivers frustration, it's really disappointing. If this was $5, maybe I would have kept it. Absolutely not at $20. First time I've ever refunded a game, but I couldn't justify keeping it after 30 minutes of play.

_childDocuments_.review: has a great concept, but the concept just fails when trying to create gameplay with it. It tries to blend a collect-a-thon style with those of an action shooter, yet it is not very engaging. If it targeted one genre only, using action shooter might have still worked better—at least the shooting mechanics, tsk tsk. The controls are pretty standard, if not bland design-wise. You can use either a controller or keyboard/mouse, but the interface does not feel good for either. Missing a button remap option is quite a big miss. Where the camera does work, it tends to move off position randomly, which is a nuisance. The graphics seem as if they were made from premade Epic Games graphics, so the game is void of a graphic style. Even though I understand why the depth of field is changing with the movement of the mouse, it was simply irritating rather than enjoyable. The animations aren’t high-end either. Prior to quitting, I can vividly recall using a few different guns. While they weren’t the worst, it was just a bad feeling aiming. The open level structure isn’t too good either—all you basically do is just bore yourself grinding for acorns in order to get the next upgrade. That ends up getting stale pretty rapidly. Another big problem is the most obvious and most necessary feature:  (Edit: My bad, there is a save system, I just worded this wrong. I’m just copying and pasting this from a comment I made correcting this statement).  I’ve seen people getting very frustrated because they can’t find a save button in the menu and there’s no auto-save. This should have been fixed before the game released. At $20, the game is cheap, but there are other “♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥” games on Steam that are actually fun for half the price. Most of the positive reviews seem like jokes because the game itself feels like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The idea is funny, but the execution just doesn’t make for a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd love to write a proper review, but I can't due to the absolutely insane DOF and motion blur that CANNOT be individually disabled without hunting down configuration files. Both DOF and motion blur make me super nauseous. DOF is fine in moderation, but simply cranking it all the way up is far too much, especially in a shooter.On top of that, the movement is INCREDIBLY floaty, even with a controller. It feels like the environments were designed with default Unreal Engine movement in mind, then had the squirrel movement replace the default UE movement with zero testing and tweaking done.Other things that are missing include:- A fullscreen toggle (no Unreal Engine's default behaviour isn't a toggle)- Borderless fullscreen- A resolution selection dropdown- More granular control over video settings (as mentioned, no way to toggle DOF/motion blur)- DLSS/FSR- Mouse support in the menus (which as an Unreal Engine developer myself is painfully easy to implement)Once all of these are fixed/added (DLSS/FSR are simply just plugins), it'd be a VERY easy recommendation for meEDIT (9/11/2024): DOR and motion blur toggles have been added!

_childDocuments_.review: I do not give many reviews. I have played many games, and still so much more to play. I focus myself on anything with a good story, good artistry, or just about anything with soul in it.I'm not too fussy on the quality of gameplay, so long as I can tolerate it, it could be objectively awful gameplay, so long as the story, or art, or soul is strong enough.This game was supposed to be just a dumb thing to kill time and have fun with... it is so much more. This game thrives in it's absurdity, in it's goofiness. And yet, provide a style, a factor, an idea, that provides it more than just the goofy foundation. So many games focus on just one thing for it's foundation, and hope that all they add on top doesn't break it. But this game uses untold confidence as it's foundation, a very risky choice as it is always a coin flip as to what may come of it. But they won the coin flip, and created an art piece that mixes the nature of the badass, a chunk of the goofiness of Goat Simulator, and the surprisingly rad music that any action packed boss fight would need.There has been talk about publishers closing studios to keep a cookie cutter assurance they will always make money, to avoid experimental games that aren't even coin flips, but cower from them anyways. They would never- COULD NEVER .... create such a testament to creation itself. This game is the epitome of being a creator, an artist even ... to make for the sake of making in one's own mental image. Without politics, without greed, and most importantly, without compromise. I paid for this game twice, as a friend must have it, and I may find myself buying it a third time for another.Also, you do not take fall damage so the game is also squirrel lore accurate. NOW GIVE THAT SQUIRREL A GUN!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - The entire game is shown in the trailer, this is not worth 20 bucks. Get it when its 4-8 dollars. 2 boss fights. 40 Golden Acorns, 500 Mini Acorns. 9 guns. One Car, one boat, one Drone. I regret buying this game after how long I waited for it.EDIT - I have since finished the game and I gotta say - this is not worth 20 dollars. It's not worth 18 dollars. At best this is an 8 dollar game for some silly fun, running around a neighborhood firing guns and driving an rc car. The boss fights are not enjoyable by any means, the game is drowning in constant buggy terrain and the controls are awful. I really really wanted to enojy this game. I was so excited for its release and all I get is a game with terrible controls, false lengthening via "unlock with enough currency", and 2 measly boss fights.Now to be fair, the boss fights are interesting on paper. The final fight is even fun for a moment before the horrid controls and mechanics ruin it.Did you watch the trailer for the game? Congrats, you've experienced everything available. That's right, every level in the game is shown in the trailer. That is the entirety of the content you are getting for TWENTY DOLLARS. The final boss fight is gated by needing to have 40 golden acorns and 500 basic acorns. Just to make you wander around the map and fight a subpar pain the ass final boss that I didn't even realize was the final fight until the credits started rolling.[Original Review]I want to enjoy this game for what it is - a silly experience of a squirrel collecting nuts with various guns. It's very much like Goat Simulator in that way. The controls are far from perfect and it takes a while to get used to how slidey the squirrel can be when it comes to basic platforming. The number of times I have fallen in lava or off a ledge because there is zero precision control on this creature is absurd.SPOILER FOR FIRST BOSSThis is where the game started to lose me. The first boss is a fight against a tank, which SOUNDS cool until you get into the fight. You can get your hands on a grenade launcher and the game tells you "shoot the treads!" and once you stun the tank by doing this it says "whats going on in the back??" which lets you slide under the tank to remove its bulldozer chunk from the front and enter the next phase.All this time you are being chased by Agents who punch and kick and get mowed down by the turret on the Tank. Also the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cannon on the tank. Any form of ragdoll makes you throw your weapon in a random direction and flings you helplessly in another and zero inputs work during ragdoll. Used your slow mo and got hit? Well have fun waiting 10 agonizing seconds while you fall slowly and roll around unable to disable your slow mo and waste it entirely.During the tank fight you can have a little car you drive around which is of course, jank to control. So you are trying to aim at tires, drive the car, and avoid being shot. This combination of controls is a normal thing in several games. Grand Theft Auto for example, hell, even Jack and Daxter got this right. When you aim with a gun in the car, you go into cruise control and just have to worry about turning right and left. These directions are based on where the front of the car is, not where your camera is facing.Oh and that grenade launcher? Great for stunning the boss, so long as no one runs in front of you while using it. Like those 6 constant agents surrounding you. One grenade kills you instantly and starts the boss fight from the beginning.After all of this, the tank wants you to jump on top of it and open a hatch to damage the boss. But the turret gunner will spin, ragdoll you, and waste the stun time, forcing you to redo all the previous actions for one change to do damage. The game expects you to see the bombs on the back of the tank, grab one, and hurl it into the hatch. With everything going on, I never saw the bombs and wasted several attempts trying to shoot into the hatch only to get spun off, staggered, and blown up.Upon finally realizing I need to use the bombs on the back of the tank I lost several attempts to spam spin that only actually hit me half of the time and other times the spin was done but I got flung off anyway by an invisible hitbox.I was very tempted to demand a refund but I am choosing to give this game another chance. The rest of the experience is silly and enjoyable to a fault.Collect the acorns, do the parkour, experience the guns, yada yada. The boss fight, in short, is absolute trash.Really cool concept on paper, but with these controls, very poorly executed.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay. I've been waiting for this for awhile. It looked like a lot of fun in the trailers and previews. Sadly, I have to agree with others...the game's a bit of a letdown. * Controls are very loose and sloppy, and your squirrel can be hard to control. Now, I get it, it's part platformer, and thus needs some muscle memory. But this goes beyond that. The controls are just bad, they are so imprecise and when you add how the camera works makes things really frustrating at times. There were times where the camera really works against you to the point where it kind of 'punches the player'. This makes me wonder how much, if any independent play testing the developer did. * The target reticle is so faint...at first I didn't realize it had one. Again, this makes me wonder if this game was really play tested. * The on-boarding/tutorial is pretty awful. I didn't even realize you could charge a throw and see the throwing arc till I found a video to see what I was doing wrong on the first level. * The save system is pretty terrible. The checkpoints seem arbitrary, and if you quit, prepare to lose progress. There's a serious lack of options when it comes to controls. For instance, you cannot remap keys, etc. In summation, I think this could wind up being a really good game at some point. But right now, it's not there. My advice is: wait a year, and see how things come along. Right now, even at 10% off, it's not worth the frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: TIMES GAME IS SIMPLY *A*M*A*Z*I*N*G* !!!** The following contains some spoilers so... read at your own discretion **(++) Very original idea : A squirrel with a gun !(++) Hilarious scenario, missions, characters, ...(++) Relatively relaxed/brainless game-play, but not without its own (sometimes serious) challenges(++) Lots of weapons, collectables, ...(++) A lot of subtle references to (and/or inspiration taken from) other games and/or cultural landmarks :> Goat Simulator > Assassin's Creed > Tony Hawk's Pro Skater > Need for Speed > DOOM > American Pie > Jackass > Pokemon > James Bond > The Matrix > ... (++) The credits (++) Decent amount of (funny and silly) achievements(++) ... (At this point I probably have already forgotten some other things I like about this game)(-) Some minor glitches here and there, namely clipping and projection issues when interacting with destroyed items at odd angles(-) No possibility to remap input for either keyboard/mouse or controllers(-) Can't adjust camera distance, sometimes it gets a little problematic(-) The game-play might feel a bit repetitive after a while(--) Controller experience is a bit clunky (XBOX, PLAYSTATION, ...) :> Inferior precision vs. keyboard + mouse experience, which is a bit of a shame for this kind of game-play, which I tend to prefer with a controller> There's a delay between input and action that is not (as) noticeable when using keyboard + mouse(--) Vehicles controls are a bit too reactive at times, especially while airborne with a car and especially with the controller (again)So yeah... for 15.99€ on sale it was well worth my time and I am extremely happy I bought this game, especially since my knee is broken and I am stuck at home for the better part of the remaining of the year, so... I needed some quality entertainment and boy did "Squirrel with a Gun" deliver ! That is, at least, for me :-)Hope it helps !

_childDocuments_.review: Squirrel With a Gun was honestly some of the most raw, humorous fun I've had on a game in a while. From the hilarious cut-scenes, even funnier lore, goofy mechanics, and great soundtrack I had a lot of fun. Squirrel with a gun is a goofy sandbox game that is very comparable to Goat Simulator. You go around town, blasting FBI agents with shotguns, snipers, all sorts of weapons. Your goal is to collect as many golden acorns as possible and defeat some main bosses (wont spoil them). Surprisingly, Squirrel With a Gun had a great soundtrack in my opinion. The main menu song, and the boss fight songs are amazing and to be going guns blazing as a squirrel with that playing in the background is awesome. I mean, who doesn't what to be a squirrel with a gun?? Come on! The humor is great, the mechanics are awesome, it's just such a goofy and fun game that you can just enjoy. I love how well made the game is, and how every part of the map has it's own unique theme, really brings in tons of different adventures you can go through as a badass blasting squirrel. I see people complaining that the game was too short, but I feel like it is a perfect length. It's a short goofy game, and has no need to be over 5 hours. I also saw a lot of negatives on performance issues/bugs but I really didn't encounter any, and if it was it was very minor. For a small studio, they did an amazing job with Squirrel With a Gun. It's a very unique, quirky, goofy game with great mechanics and is very well designed for what it is. I really enjoyed my time with it and give it an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: To call this game unfun would be a straight up lie. Between figuring out platform puzzles, killing agents, and just generally mucking about this game is a blast. _childDocuments_.review: Zany sandbox super rodent action or fans of games like GOATSDifficulty ★★★☆☆☆☆☆☆☆ (no big consequences when dying)* concept and sandbox is fun* good soundtrack (do like the fact that the main theme has different variation depending on the area your are, like the wedding theme)* boss fights were awesome* funny gameplay with lots of different tasks and intersting areas to explore* nice outfits and cosmetics* squirrel has a gun* really, squirrel has all sorts of big guns* squirrel is just imba :)* game performance is bad due to a lot of hefty post-processing shaders to beef visuals up artificially* overall polygon level of assets and objects is a little but too low, the shaders don't helpt to much* the sandbox world could be bigger and more detailed (game felt a little bit to fast to play through)* there is no real resolution setting (just a slider) or option to set fullscreen or borderless windows mode, that slider can also get stuck on low and medium, you need hotkeys of Windows to fix this. I would like to have more particular control over those two things* some clipping don't work out well* would like to have different fatality moves for the same weapon* climbing was bugged once until I reloaded the whole game* camera control and car control does not work out too well with controllerIf you are a fan of crazy sandbox games, or you played GOATS and loved that, Suirrel with a Gun is pretty much exactly for you. Though GOATS, especially GOATS 3 does offer more (and even multiplayer fun, locally or online). SwaG has a great concept, it needs more polishing, more areas, more to do, and a multiplayer, and it could really stand out of the masses.Don't get me wrong, the game is fun as it is, and you should really play it if you are interested in it, but it could be much much bigger. Hope this games get a proper sequel or some interesting new DLCs or other additions.

_childDocuments_.review: Squirrel with a Gun is an absolute gem in the indie action-adventure game genre! This game delivers a unique and whimsical experience, blending the wild antics of a gun-wielding squirrel with the charm and chaos reminiscent of Untitled Goose Game and Goat Simulator.The story line is delightfully absurd: a squirrel breaks into a top-secret lab, eats a hard drive shaped like an acorn, and embarks on a hilarious rampage through a suburban neighbourhood. The inspiration from the Yakuza franchise and Shadow of the Colossus is evident in the game's mix of combat and exploration.Players control a seemingly ordinary squirrel armed with a variety of firearms, from pistols to RPGs, navigating a sandbox world filled with interactive objects and NPCs. The combat is engaging, and the platforming puzzles are a fun challenge, rewarding players with golden acorns.What makes this game even more appealing are the non-violent activities and stealth elements. You can steal food, help NPCs with tasks, or sneak past enemies, adding layers of depth to the game play. The range of costumes for the squirrel is a delightful touch, making the game even more enjoyable.In short, Squirrel with a Gun is a must-play for anyone looking for a fresh, entertaining, and hilariously chaotic gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I finished playing Squirrel with a Gun, and I can’t stop smiling! This game is a whimsical blend of humor and action that had me hooked from the start. The concept alone—a squirrel armed with a variety of guns—is both hilarious and unique, and it’s executed brilliantly.The graphics are charming, with vibrant colors and detailed environments that perfectly capture the playful tone of the game. The controls are smooth, making it easy to navigate through the levels while executing some impressively fun moves. The gameplay itself is a delightful mix of platforming and combat, keeping me engaged and entertained throughout.I especially loved the variety of challenges and missions. Each level offers something new, from quirky enemies to clever puzzles that really test your skills. Plus, the soundtrack is catchy and upbeat, perfectly complementing the overall vibe.Overall, Squirrel with a Gun is a breath of fresh air in the indie game scene. It’s fun, lighthearted, and has a ton of charm. Whether you’re looking for a quick gaming session or something to dive into for hours, this game delivers. Highly recommend to anyone looking for a good time!

_childDocuments_.review: It should be obvious from the steam page, but the game is at its core a 3D collectathon first and foremost, and a third person shooter second. It took me about 10 hours total to collect everything the game currently has to offer, and it was very enjoyable for nearly the entire time. You get a fairly constant stream of new weapons to play around with, and every golden acorn has a largely unique and creative challenge or task you have to do to get them, with little repeats. There's also a ton of outfits and hats to find that also usually have their own little challenges too. The game really isn't too hard to 100%, as there are flagpoles everywhere that act as "ubisoft towers" that show you the location of all golden acorns, outfits, and upgrades in the nearby area.I only have two real gripes with the game. The first is that the two boss fights in the game are both massive slogs that boil down to: run in one direction for ten seconds to avoid the boss' attacks, then spend 5 seconds blindly firing towards their exposed point on repeat until you stun them and can do actual damage. Both fights feel super slow and feel like you are making little progress as a result.My other gripe is a very odd quirk with the aiming in the game that affects at least controllers. There's a weird smoothing thing with it where the aiming reticle will move a little bit in whatever direction you were last moving whenever you change direction. For example: You move the reticle to the right for a second and let go of the stick, and the camera will instantly stop as expected. But if you then move the stick to the left, the camera will start moving to the right for a split second before moving the actual direction of the stick. It's a very odd quirk that makes precise aiming infuriating.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about this game. It's quirky and entertaining and is exactly what's written on the tin. Overal, it's a GTA style sandboxer with various puzzles and challenges laid out. It's pretty to look at as it's utilizing the unreal engine in great ways. The non-dialogue narratives that pop up are delightfully silly.The one thing I don't like about the game are the movement controls. They're very loose and I find myself fighting with the movement more than I am the enemies, challenges, or puzzles, especially when many of the puzzles require precise movement to get through them. Whether it be "jump on a small platform" or "drive the car in a straight line", I find it extremely difficult and often lose control of the character as it twists and turns in unintended directions. I tried using a controller at first and completely ditched it immediately as it over-corrects for the thumb sticks causing you to overshoot and overextend every movement.Overall, the game would benefit if the character controls were tightened as you could then focus on the puzzle rather than randomly running, or driving, in completely unintended directions and falling into lava over and over and over and over and over and over and over.

Frustrating controls, especially the boat and car, they are an immense pain in the ass to control on PC, due to the over-correction and super sensitive turning. The guns can sometimes screw you over when platforming.2. No post-game content, so collecting everything in the game doesn't actually reward you with anything special, its just padding, which is very disappointing and kinda lazy, not even an achievement for it.3. _childDocuments_.review: It delivered everything it promised and more! Took me less than 9 hours to collect 100% of items and achievements, and I'm fine with that for a $20 sandbox experience. If that doesn't sound like a good enough value for your wallet then wishlist it for a sale, but if the trailer looked fun to you then you will definitely enjoy your time! The devs even announced a roadmap of seven free content updates by the end of 2025, so I'm glad to have a reason to pick this up again every few months and get up to some more nutty nonsense! exceeds expectations good, but the boss tracks will be hit/miss for folks (and you'll hear em loop a LOT while you learn the strategy)  around 8-9 hours;  probably like 6-7 hours you're a squirrel, and you have guns! Also a car (and later a drone) to ride! I only encountered one bug in my playthrough; got stuck in a wall after an explosion and had to reload. No issues otherwise or even any notable framedrops, so just don't forget to save often and you'll probably be fine.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR This feels like a cross between Grand Theft Auto and Conker's Bad Fur Day in most of the best ways... I think it's worth it.Full form:If you judge games by the best graphics or how long the game is, this game may not be for you. If you want a lighthearted romp through a world where a squirrel can pick up a gun and exact vengeance on the agents responsible for the way he is... you will enjoy this game.Difficulty seems to ramp up quickly at the boss fights compared with the rest, but it feels SO GOOD when you finish something. I love exploring interesting and creative world designs and this doesn't disappoint. Using the guns as a means of superjumping is well done, and while some aspects may seem repetitive (esp if you are like me and want to 100% the game), the payoff for the story is worth it.This is not a very long game, I could probably have finished it in a few hours if I sat down and powerhouse it.. but for me, I emerge myself in the world and the game.In my opinion, any negative in the game is outweighed by the sheer positives that come with the absurdly fun concept and executions.Worth a buy? Yes. Worth it on sale? VERY yes.

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical about this game at first. It looked like another half-baked indie game looking for funding, and for $18 (on sale) I didn't think it was going to be worth it. We happened across a Youtuber that was playing it and halfway through the video, I decided to give it a shot.During the opening "tutorial" the control scheme was a little tough to get used to. Having shift as a throw button instead of sprint threw me off and continued to mess with me for the entire game (but not terribly). However, once you get used to the controls and how sensitive the motion is, it turns into a REALLY fun Shooter/Platformer/Puzzle game. Each big battle got one trial run while I figured out my favorite weapon/strategy combo, then won the second round. Each weapon is well crafted in terms of aesthetics and functionality, and I had fun using every single one!One thing that I really like about this game is the vehicle controls. Using your aim button as a kind of [temporary] cruise control on the car and boat, as well as auto steering in the boat was a mechanic that I've not seen before. It made the vehicles a lot more fun to drive, since it allows you to focus more on all the ridiculousness of the game.The platforming aspect of the game was creative and just the right amount of difficulty.All in all, it took me just about 8.5 hours to 100% the game. I'm really looking forward to the updates they have already announced, as well as future plans. It may not be what some people are looking for for  $20; but with more development, this game (which is already worth it, personally) has incredible potential.Thank you to the dev team for making a creative, unique, and fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: My favourite game of 2024. Initially I thought the asking price was a little steep for what seemed like a single area of a janky Goat Simulator wannabe but there are two large sandbox levels with several mini levels integrated into them. I fully recommend, if for no other reason than this is a Goat Simulator simulator where you shoot CIA agents with guns as a squirrel.Pros:- it's a beautiful looking game, even if it is relatively unpolished. 60+ FPS is pretty easy for me on a 10700/4070 combo with a couple of settings turned down.- controls seem weird at first (mouse and keyboard) but once you get used to the "weight" of them it becomes very fluid- 10ish hours of play to clear achievements and 100% the game. A second playthough might only take 2-3- just the right amount of jank, this game is obviously inspired by Goat SimulatorCons- very unpolished. UI is keyboard only? Many of the finer mechanics aren't explained at all (did you know you can shoot locked doors to open them? Well now you do!). There are no graphics options to disable depth of field/motion blur or to set resolution. - very buggy. Many scripted things wouldn't trigger until I saved the game and restarted. My resolution scale is stuck on medium and nothing save from reinstalling will fix it. Map/physics get glitchy after an hour or two of playing and require you to save > quit to menu > reload. Squirrel will get stuck in things requiring you to quit and lose progress.- very unoptimized; performance leaves a lot to be desired. Unreal 5 looks great even with options turned down but there's no reason my solidly mid tier system should be hitting 30 FPS in certain situations.- save system needs work (but the dev did make some improvements in a recent patch).  but I feel like there should be an auto save every 15 minutes or something. On two occasions I lost progress, through no fault of my own, because the game glitched out. (edit: the save system was actually updated before I wrote this review but I had already completed the game at that point. It now has an autosave feature when you complete  goals/objectives)- currently not a lot of replay value and probably better ways to spend $20 if you're strapped for cash (unclear if more areas are being added but I hope so. I would even pay $5 for DLC maps/areas if they were the same size as one of the main areas currently in game)- instability: I did not have crash/hang issues but there are a number of people complaining about this on the forums/redditDo not let the cons scare you. Try it out, and if you don't like the game by the time you clear the first area, keep an eye on the refund window. I don't think you will want to use it, though.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - For $20 you get to run around and do silly things as a squirrel.It's fun, cute, funny, and more challenging that you'd think. It's got a lot of tongue in cheek satirization of some old gaming tropes, and some interesting puzzles.My only complaints: There are handful of spots that are challenging in a "oh, this is maybe badly designed" way. It walks the line between "requires more precision than you expected" and "made artificially difficult to pad the play time," and it stumbles to the wrong side of that in a way that feels bad. The tips can be surprising unhelpful (), navigating certain challenges () requires repeating the same kind of annoying car ramp a lot, etc. I'm pretty sure at least a couple hours of my 7 hours was just trying to figure out if I was doing something wrong and/or going up  repeatedly.Overall, I still liked it, it's not like the above complaints are true detriments, just worth saying.

_childDocuments_.review: I have just completed my playthrough of Squirrel with a Gun, and I feel compelled to give you a thorough review of this game. Starting out we all know what it looks like. This is just a crappy meme game with a niche gimmick and it's not gonna be worth $20, but the gimmick drives people like me to buy it, play it one time, and never look back. This is completely WRONG. Although the game doesn't really have any replay-ability factor for me now that I've got 100% in the game and on the achievements, the game is very fun and refreshing for a first time playthrough. The mechanics are fun and the "story" although basically non-existent locked me in the MOMENT I saw the first boss. I NEEDED to see where this went, and see I did. I can now say that I was 100% not disappointed in what I found. The game is quick fun and enjoyable, with amazing boss fights, and cool levels to explore. The overworld basically serves as a hub of mish-mashed gimmicks that are fun to explore. Although there is no real cohesion every level feels like it's own little area to explore with it's own self contained interactions. The world itself is also full of fun memes, funny moments, and well rounded quality gameplay. The game serves it's roll as a casual experience, but also offers exciting challenges for a more refined gamer in the form of fun quality 3D platforming assisted by the physics of your various guns, and in the form of actually very fun and interesting boss fights. This game also offers a variety of choices for both character customization and weapon loadouts, with every single weapon having an effect on combat as well as the platforming, and puzzle solving aspects of the game. This was a thoroughly enjoyable experience and I would happily recommend it to most people.

_childDocuments_.review: The premise of this game is far more enticing than the gameplay itself.  The game absolutely delivers on the promise of humor as I've been dying laughing from this thing and I'm only an hour or so in.  The developer has definitely not rested on their laurels thus far and the gags have not been repetitive.  Only time will tell if the joke will outstay its welcome, but so far I am in love and would recommend this to anyone who was delighted by the trailer and curious to give it a go.That all said, it does have a wonky control style that evokes similar feelings in me as when I played Octodad or Goat Simulator, but I have the impression that it was not exactly the intent of the developer this time around.  Nothing too major, but the biggest issue for me is aiming the gun.  When you press LT to aim, I often find that right as I sight in on what I'm shooting, even stationary targets, the squirrel will move at the last second, causing the reticle to jump in one direction or another.  It's made even basic "puzzles" more difficult than they needed to be, and getting headshots on baddies, even while in bullet time, a real challenge.  The other aspect of wonkiness to this game is the camera controls.  They have a similar issue when turning of suddenly jumping, causing me to fall off simple platforms and die.  This is hardly insurmountable as I've already grown accustomed to it, but these are pretty basic control issues which impact the game at every step of the way and should be patched out.  Additionally, either I just missed it or it doesn't make it very intuitive to save the game.  It also doesn't tell you how long it's been since your last save when you go to exit and as such, after my first time playing for 30-40 minutes, I quit, figuring it had auto-saved, only to find upon logging back in that it had never saved once, even after clearing an entire section.  I literally had to watch a youtube tutorial on how to save and the fact it exists the day after launch suggests that I'm not alone.Again, I very much recommend this game as at the price point, the problems are something I'm certainly willing to look past for the ability to enjoy the humor on my own without being spoiled by the endless memes and youtube suggestion thumbnails ruining it.

_childDocuments_.review: As the next entry in the "play as an animal and be an a$$hole" series, Squirrel with a Gun builds on a funny motif and executes somewhat well. Just don't expect $60 games' level of polish on this $20 game.The game starts from a tutorial level, teaching you to jump, shoot, throw, and extend jumps by shooting downward. The platforming feels more difficult than it should be due to the squirrel being floaty, the lack of a position indicator and the lack of coyote time, and I gotta admit it did not leave a good first impression. Thankfully combat is more passable, shooting is crisp, and it's quite a new experience to shoot from ground level and get ridiculous recoil from every shot. You can "takedown" a downed enemy, but the animation gets repetitive after a few times.After the tutorial you are taken to the main town and the game opens up. It took a while for me to grasp, but the game is structured somewhat like Super Mario 64. The map is divided into sections, each with a few golden acorns to collect, which is the overarching goal, used to unlock weapon spawners, vehicles, boss fights and new sections. In each section is a flag pole, once you climb to the top you can see the location and name of each golden acorn, providing a hint of how to get them. Not all golden acorns are immediately available to collect, many require you to interact with the environment or NPCs in some way to spawn. It can get cryptic at times, but I do appreciate some exploration and puzzle solving.It needs to be noted that there is no auto save. This is quite out of place in an age where every game warns you to not turn off your console when some icon appears. In this game you jump onto a bird feeder to save manually, which is entirely unavailable in the somewhat lengthy tutorial level. I hope this can be reevaluated in a future update.Another complaint is the constant need to find and spawn guns. You don't select guns from a weapon wheel; you spawn guns from specific locations and then carry them like an item. There are many occasions that forcibly remove your gun, such as climbing a pole, falling from height, taking a heavy hit, saving, and opening a costume chest; whenever this happens you better rush back to your gun because I've had it despawn a few times. If you ever want to switch to another weapon, good luck remembering where their spawners are.Overall, the game is funny enough to keep me playing, but there are pain points I wish can be addressed. 7 out of 10.

The extra cute touches from the designers add a delightful charm that makes every moment in the game a joy. It’s a thoroughly satisfying adventure that has me twitching with delight!
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a hilarious game, kinda reminds me of the nonsensical games you'd see during the PS2 era. The only problem I had with it was the controls not being displayed anywhere. Seriously, I couldn't even find them in the options menu. I spent a good 30-40 mins just trying to get out of the first room because playing on mouse and keyboard, there's soooo many possible button combinations.  Even though I got a refund for now. I'm still gonna give it an upvote and keep an eye out on the game, because it has great potential and I really hope the devs take the time to polish it up a bit more. And please, add a button layout manual, especially for those who are on keyboard. P.s. music is awesome and matches the theme perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played for very long but I'm loving it so far. Great humor, the game doesn't take itself too seriously, and who doesn't love a small goofy protagonist?However, the developers did seem to fall into a couple of common (and in my opinion bad) practices:1. For this current version, there's no way to modify the motion blur of the game. I've seen developers add this functionality later and I hope this can be the same case for Squirrel with a Gun.2. Jumping  is very floaty and imprecise. The jumping feels better when you have a gun (since guns give you some midair mobility), but it is still pretty imprecise. There are a lot of platform puzzles that require you to jump without a gun and this imprecise-ness causes unneeded headache in a platforming game.These gripes are extremely minor though and I want to reiterate that I am loving the game so far! Definitely pick this one up if you can :)
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Mannnnn, wish more game devs were able to pull off games like this ! It's makes no sense at all what so ever in a good way ! A challenging platform, mixed with open world elements for sandbox chaos with guns (I love the animations each weapon has for when the squirrel fires the guns, he like gets blown away when using a shotgun, jumps around when shooting a smg, it's great!) they really put a lot of thought into this game ! I really hope they continue to add more content and expand the open world even more ! I'd play this all day everyday. And it has boss battles !!

_childDocuments_.review: If you had a grand old time playing Goat Simulator or something in the same vein where you just cause chaos, use some problem-solving skills to unlock secrets, and just generally enjoy seeing a squirrel dome secret agents in the most merciless ways, then boy do I have a game for you. _childDocuments_.review: This game is Nucking Futs! Secret agent squirrel saving the neighborhood the only way a 00rodent knows how: Looking fabulous, and an obscene amount or recoil.  You want sploots? you got it. Sports? This little furry vandal has you covered. Stripping? The pole game is unmatched. Stuffing cheeks and clapping em at the same time. Controls took a little bit to get used to, but over all it plays well.  The tongue and cheek humor is great, and reminds me a great deal of Goat sim.  I'd been waiting for this to release for over a year, and I was not disappointed. If you like stupid, fun games with a touch of challenge behind it, buy it.  It's been great fun so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I saw "Untitled Goose Game" I wanted a squirrel game. AND NOW WE HAVE IT! There are a few minor issues that the devs are already working on but this isn't an alpha or a 'beta that we are releasing and patching into a full game' - this is a full and working game! And it is everything I could have wanted! You want a squirrel running around and causing mayhem? Check! That squirrel gets guns? Check! Rocket launchers? CHECK! The squirrel wears clothes and is customizable? CHECK! And the save spaces being bird feeders that fling you off once the save completes? OMG!!! _childDocuments_.review: ABSOLUTE riot of a a game.I have literally had to pause as i couldn't see from laughing so hard all because of just ludicrous things i've pulled off just because the game makes it available.There are a few world clipping issues they need to fix but they actually kind of add to the charm? (should be fixed though lol)The music is amazing.The humour is on point. I do love the spy angle to it all. Perfect for a squirrel.Gunplay is great, for being a tiny lil squirrel... so recoil is an actual issue and will launch you backwards.Controlls might be an issue for some folk, but because they're so punchy it makes it seem like you're playing as a squirrel, you dart about quite a lot. but you get used to them pretty fast. not sure what its like with a controller however.The world story telling is quite good too, you see a a sad lonely guy with a party hat? go steal the cake from the people partying currently mad they have no meat yet... they won't careI do wish there were more variants of finishers, even 3 or 4 for each weapon would be nice, as it stands uzi has one, pistol has one etc etc.its an easy 8/10 for me and i definitely recommend grabbing it.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe the game is good enough and fun enough for the asking price. If you are in the mood for a wacky/janky platformer with a lot of humor and absurdity this game is there for you. If you want a perfectly polished game with polished controls/mechanics you are in the wrong post code area. I really hope the game is successful enough that the devs make another, better and more polished game after this one. :)The good: - The setting of the game is really fun - Manages to induce laughter repeatedly.The bad: - Controls are bad, even for 2005 standards. - It is a 1.5A game. Levels are competently made with a strong reuse of what appears to be store assets. Animations and ragdoll physics are a little wonky.The maybe: - The game is 80-90% platformer and a little bit of shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: I unfortunately returned this game, the camera sensitivity was far too high (even on the lowest setting) and I cant change my DPI so it was impossible to aim. Additionally the character moves extremely fast (too fast to keep up with). So why is this a positive review? Because if I could put character movement to 75% and lower the DPI the desired amount I have no doubts this would be one of my favorite games. In its current state I cannot play it, but if you are able to keep up and control the game then I know this game will bring you hours of enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is easily a 10/10 for the money. I've been waiting for this game for nearly 2 years since it's announcement and it lived up to the hype!The only bad is that it's kinda quirky and the tutorials aren't the best. In order to save the game, you need to jump on the bird feeders and that's not explained. It's definitely the same save game approach in the ps1/ps2 era before autosave was a big thing. Regardless of these flaws, the game is still a 10/10. I never imagined squirrel gun violence would be so fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Squirrel with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t know how the developer meld so much retro game influences as it feels like playing Mario Odyssey’s coin (acorns) & star (golden acorn) collecting mechanic that has a character reminiscent of Conquer’s Bad Fur Day but silent, Chip N Dale’s item grabbing & holding, on Toy Story 2’s sandbox areas that has Goat Simulator’s tone & physics. It’s a great combination of ideas overall.I like the gunplay in this game as you can get creative with it on platforming that it feels like Toy Story 2 double jump but with actual guns😂 Physics & enemy animation in Unreal Engine 5 needs a bit more polish but for a solo development man this is beyond my expectations for its price. Well done. It works on launch day but I’m still expecting some updates mainly to fix some animations & performance issues specially when I boot it on Steam Deck. I don’t see the usual game graphics options & it was capped for 40 fps. On my PC & ROG Ally though that option is present & I can tweak it so I could get atleast 60 fps. Recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Game of the year. From the moment you launch Squirrel with a Gun, it’s clear you’re in for an exhilarating, boundary-pushing experience like no other. This game is a triumph of creativity and sheer joy that will leave you grinning from ear to ear and humming with excitement!Imagine this: you’re not just playing any ordinary game – you’re stepping into the shoes of a squirrel armed with a gun, navigating through vibrant, whimsically designed worlds. This premise is as wild as it is brilliant, and it’s executed with an irresistible charm that makes every moment feel like a celebration.The game’s graphics are nothing short of stunning. Each environment is a visual feast, brimming with color and intricate details that make every level a pleasure to explore. The animations are smooth, capturing the essence of our feisty little protagonist with such flair that you can’t help but fall in love with every quirky move and cheeky expression.The gameplay is where Squirrel with a Gun truly shines. The controls are tight and intuitive, making it easy to pick up and incredibly rewarding to master. The blend of platforming and action is executed with perfect balance, ensuring that each challenge is both thrilling and satisfying. Whether you’re darting through forests, dodging obstacles, or taking down enemies with your tiny but mighty arsenal, every moment is packed with adrenaline-pumping excitement.But what really sets this game apart is its unparalleled sense of fun. The developers have poured their hearts into crafting a world that’s not just playful, but downright hilarious. The witty dialogue, clever level design, and imaginative scenarios all combine to create a game that feels fresh, original, and utterly delightful.And let’s not forget the soundtrack – a perfect companion to the frenetic action onscreen. The music is upbeat and catchy, enhancing the overall experience and making you want to keep playing just to hear more.In a gaming landscape that often feels saturated with the same old tropes, Squirrel with a Gun stands out as a beacon of creativity and sheer joy. It’s a game that doesn’t just entertain but makes you appreciate the art of game design all over again. It’s a must-play for anyone who loves a great adventure, a good laugh, and a unique twist on the familiar.So grab your acorns, lock and load, and dive into this delightful escapade. Squirrel with a Gun is an absolute gem that will keep you coming back for more – it’s a nutty, exhilarating, and unforgettable ride that you simply cannot miss!

_childDocuments_.review: I am ALREADY loving this. Squirrel with a Gun is such a bizarre concept but oh my God it is so much fun to play as a squirrel shooting up agents and terrorizing an entire town. The platforming and shooting have the perfect amount of balance as well as challenge, so you'll have to use your wits to defeat the agents. The weapons have the perfect handling, and my God, that uzi is by far the best weapon in the game with how nearly, if not perfectly accurate it feels to use. But, by far, the best part of the entire game is, of course, the absurd concept. I mean, it's a squirrel, with a gun. A squirrel escapes a secret underground facility after an agent trips himself, and that's how you get your basic mechanics for the first time. But, the concept itself, the concept of a squirrel using lethal weapons and firearms, is so crazy and over the top there are no words in the English language that can describe just how crazy it is. This is literally Goat Simulator, but with a squirrel using shotguns, uzis, rocket launchers, and other guns. This is a truly unique sandbox game for what it is. I have never had this much fun with a sandbox game since Goat Simulator 3 came out in 2022. In fact, I know I'll be in the minority on this, but I think it is actually better than Goat Simulator due to adding brand new mechanics inside of the silly sandbox genre. I am actually seriously enjoying my time with this so much more than I have ever with any of the Goat Simulator games or its DLCs. Not throwing any shade on Goat Simulator or its sequel, but I have seriously been enjoying Squirrel with a Gun so much more than I have with Goat Sim. You made it just different enough so it doesn't just feel like a direct copy of any of the Goat Sim games, but you also added unique abilities and features that barely, if not at all is ever seen in the sandbox genre. I never thought that playing as a rodent that collects nuts that also wields firearms would end up being even more enjoyable than my favorite sandbox simulation game. I am actually awe you have managed to top this. It is, without a shadow of a doubt, my new favorite sandbox game. You have done everything right about this. Added features that made it just unique enough to be considered its own game, added Mario 64-like platforming, and you made it far more enjoyable and entertaining than Goat Simulator ever could be. I truly thought that Goat Simulator was the absolute Gold Standard of silly sandbox games. But this? This takes the cake, by a mile and a half. Completely nuked Goat Simulator's #1 spot on my "Top 10 Personal Favorite Sandbox Games" into the stratosphere. This is it, THIS is the Gold Standard now.This game gets a well-deserved 9.5/10, since there is no true 10/10 game in my eyes.

name: The King's Dilemma: Chronicles
detailed_description: Welcome to the Kingdom of Ankist: a place of daring expeditions, gruesome battles, and arcane mysteries. You play as the Head of the Council, the leader of the King’s inner circle. Listen to the advice of your Council of Houses, or overrule their decisions. Face hundreds of dilemmas where every choice you make may affect your relationship with the other Houses, influence the well-being and resources of the kingdom, and change the course of history itself. Discover the lands of Ankist over a story spanning across tens of generations. Form alliances, survive betrayals, and prepare for the final uprising foretold by an ancient prophecy. Will you act for the greater good, or will you think only of yourself? Explore the map of Ankist and see the Kindom’s problems currently at hand. Choose one, and the Council will be summoned to make a decision: do we send help to people hit by famine? Should we wage war against that northern tribe raiding the villages across our border? The Houses will cast their vote: “Aye” or “Nay” based on their personal interest and political stance. At that point, you might decide to influence the vote, spending your House’s finances to corrupt members of the council, or consuming some fo the limited “power” points you are given for the rule of each King. Each decision you make has consequences both on your relations with the other Houses and on the Kingdom’s resources, which in turn might result in the King abdicating or being overthrown. But they will also make more dilemmas become available on the map. Based on the resources standing at the end of the current King’s rule and your moral alignment, you will be awarded “greed” and “influence” points, which you’ll be able to spend to research technology, start expeditions, or build structures. Which of these will become available depends on the choices you made. Each of the above will award you money and resources during the rule of each King, in addition to changing the events of the final uprising you will be preparing for. Play as one of twelve different houses, each with their own narrative goal Discover 300+ story-driven dilemmas through Ankist and its neighboring kingdoms Choose branching narrative paths across six intertwined storylines Explore multiple endings, with each playthrough lasting 3 to 4 hours Use influence or corruption to control the Council Invest in research, technology and buildings Play across generations, choose your heir as well as their personality and goals Always be preparing for the final battle The King’s Dilemma: Chronicles tells the story of Ankist, a fictional medieval kingdom in the continent of Lywik. The structure of the kingdom is feudal: the Duchies and the Marks are managed by their ruling Houses, many of which also have their representatives sitting at the Council, a governing body ruling in the name of the King located in Lybra, the capital city of the Kingdom. As the leader of the Council, all social classes will come asking for your help: Merchants, Scholars, the Army, the Cult of the Mother, and of course, the People. It will be your task to drive the choices of the Council and satisfy their requests… but you’ll also have to manage the resources of the Kingdom, and keeping everyone happy won’t be easy. Your main interest is obviously to make Ankist prosper; however, you are also trying to increase the power and the prestige of your own family over the others. The campaign spans decades and generations, and you will assume the role of different representatives of your House over the course of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: So yeah, this game is pretty good.It's definitely worth it's asking price.It'll probably take you 4-6 hours to get through a single playthrough, and the game gives opportunities for multiple playthroughs thanks to it's replayability potential.It has no voice acting and no sound effects. Okay it has a few sound effects, but it's mostly music that you'll be listening to but the music is great.The gameplay itself is kinda simple and boring, at least to some. It's basically reading dialogue followed by clicking "yay" or "Nay". Then watching the sliders go up and down.It's not really much for strategy so don't expect any of that here. It's mostly political simulation by saying either yes or no. ANd that's it. So it's gameplay is kinda lacking in that department. Don't get me wrong, there's still a lot of good here and I still think the game is worth it, but it's not as deep as you may think.It KINDA has resource management but not really.It KINDA has strategy stuff but not really.It's mostly just guessing and gambling that the decisions you make are the right ones.yet somehow this game still manages to pull you in and immerse you into it's world. I was so into the game I lost track of time and realized I had to get off and do this review.Basically you play as the king's second in command and help him rule his kingdom by making choices. Ally yourself with other houses who serve the king, and do what you think is best for the kingdom. But make sure you don't get the king killed or whatever.It's a lot of dialogue and reading, it's mostly dialoge and reading actually. But it's very good reading and it's very well done. It's slow and to some could be considered boring, but as a political simulation game in medieval times it's actually a lot of fun, considering there isn't much you can do besides say yay or nay.If you want a more in depth look with gameplay then please check out my video on YouTube (link below).Otherwise, thanks for reading and I hope I managed to help some of you out there to spend your money wisely.
