_childDocuments_.review: After two playthroughs I feel like I have a decent idea of the game.It's an exceptionally poorly designed game, with occasionally great writing, but an incredibly disjointed narrative and totally pointless gameplay.For the most part the writing is solid, but it collapses entirely when taken as a whole.The idea of the game is a generations spanning tale of politics, but essentially it boils down to you flipping a coin with every decision on an event, where sometimes you might have an idea of what the result is, but often you don't. You're not making informed choices for the most part, I would say. Sometimes yes, mostly not, and ESPECIALLY at the finale you're not. It's literally just flipping a coin, but you have NO idea what's the correct choice(and indeed there is a correct choice which makes it very frustrating). Most of the time you're given zero contextual information as to what the decision you're making might mean or what it might affect, and it's very annoying. Sometimes the decisions are illusory and are immediately backpedaled on, but thankfully that's extremely rare. For the most part the choices do have a lot of consequence on the narrative, but you'll only understand this on a second playthrough by making opposite choices. It's just that they're self-contained into their story arcs, so it makes zero sense at the finale where everything supposedly comes together. I had an immortal god queen, yet she wasn't even mentioned in the finale which was absolutely insane narrative wise and totally destroyed the immersion.The game has a slew of absolutely pointless mechanics, and would be better off without them. They serve no purpose whatsoever, and are incredibly easy to abuse to your liking, or in fact complete ignore as they have ZERO impact on anything. None of the numbers mean anything, except the buildings you can make which give you more choices at the end(since it's a coin flip, it's not really an advantage). I suggest paying them no attention.And that's the problem. The game has several supposedly important gameplay elements that are just in the way. You have a bunch of houses that vote on things, and you can influence them with money or ignore them by using a power resource. Either is irrelevant as it has no effect on anything in practice. There are a bunch of sliders these choices affect, but again, they have no effect on anything. There are no dynamic checks that inspect where a slider is, and then change the narrative accordingly, they're just there for, well, I'm not sure why. To make it seem like a game?The whole game has the feeling that someone was forced to add three or so gameplay mechanics into it, or felt compelled to do so since that's what games have. Had it just been a game where you choose how the narrative goes, it could've been decent. As it is, I can't recommend it due to the mechanics getting in the way of enjoying the narrative. And no, I'm not some storytelling obsessed person who hates interesting game mechanics, quite the opposite, which is why these fake-mechanics are so aggravating.It seems this is a port of a board game, which presumably doesn't have those mechanics, and it definitely shows.As for the narrative, it has many problems too. It's structured into several self-contained story arcs that have nothing to do with each other, which makes for absolutely horrid continuity errors and a general feeling of meaningless. If my previous choices aren't taken into account with the future ones, why bother telling me a tale about what happened? I got an infinite gold generator and accepted slavery in my kingdom, and the next thing you're saying is that my peasants are too poor to buy bread so they're forced to eat corrupted bread? And there's no mention of the slaves anywhere, by the way. Absolute nonsense as far as an immersive narrative is concerned.Long story short, the game is a massive waste of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: For those not in the know, this game is based on a very popular board game, simply titled The King's Dilemma . It has a high ranking on most board game websites, and my own particular group had an excellent time with it for many sessions. When I heard it was being turned into a video game, I was quite hopeful. This isn't a board game review, so I won't get too bogged down with the game its based on, but I will say this: the board game was not perfect. A video game, I thought, might give the team a chance to fix some of the issues the board game had. However, I was also a bit worried. There was a lot that could go wrong. I'll be frank: almost everything I was worried about going wrong, went wrong.First off, if you're going to play the board game, . I was a bit stunned when I realized that the video game has the  as the board game. In fact, the scenarios in the video game are very often ripped directly off the cards in the board game. A lot of the fun of the board game came from the slow, but amazing exploration of the land and plot. That will be ripped from you if you play the video game. If you're in the opposite position, and you've already played the board game, there's still not much for you here. You can go back and find out what happened if you made X choice instead of Y, but that isn't all that exciting, sadly.The board game was also fun because each individual person played a council member. You would bribe, cajole, and threaten your friends to accomplish the shady goals of your house. Turning this into a single player experience completely robs you of the part of the game. This is just a mathy single player slog through the story. The hours and hours of combative fun of the board game are distilled into an exercise of spreadsheets and solitary reading. You don't feel any particular connection to your house in the game. Spoiler warning: . Finally, the ending. I don't want to comment too much, but I'll briefly sum up what I think (spoilers ahead, don't read if you plan to play the board game): . Some pros: -The story and writing itself is good. If you're looking for a good visual-novel esque experience, and never intend on playing the board game, then this is decent. -The world is still just really, really cool, no doubt about it.-Art assets are dank.-You can make choices. Pressing buttons that have different effects is fun. -One of the houses is a purple hedgehog. Some more cons:-Worth $15? Absolutely not, if you're a fast reader, you'll clear it in an hour and a half. Subsequent playthroughs are not as fun. -A lot of your choices will not matter in the way you anticipate they will. Once you see how the end up mattering, it will feel frustrating. I won't say more to avoid spoilers. -There isn't much "game" outside of the button clicking. Overall, this gets 3/10 from me, 4/10 if you never plan on playing the board. One final plea: seriously, do not play the video game first if you intend to play the board game. In fact, just get some friends and go play the board game. Save some money.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the boardgame. It did not translate well to a single player game I'm afraid. It looks nice and the events are still good. _childDocuments_.review: Good, but short ruler game. Played through twice in 3hrs. Very short game. You can literally play it through and still get a refund(not to say that is what you should do but you could) The game is similar to something like the Reigns series of games where you have to tossle diffrent columns like knowledge, money etc. they are interchangable and dont have much impact on anything. But the decisions themselves can end up leading you down seperate paths. For example decisions with the northerners can either lead to an alliance or war depending on choices you make. It isnt quite a "pick alliance or pick war" option, you can easily miss the important decision in the mission chain and end up going down path you dont want. Second playthrough is pretty much essential to get a hang of the mechanics. It is quite fun picking how you want the stories to play out, but they dont in the end matter much. Siding with Celestia or not has 0 impact on the ending slides for example. Kind of disappointing how generic the endings are.But main issue in all honesty is how the dethrone/abdication/mechanic works. It is fine as a boardgame but here in video game form it turns the entire thing into just picking the option that gives you the column you need (money, knowledge etc.) instead of being ideologically consistent with your playthrough otherwise. You can play as a diplomatic multicultural and equality type guy picking the right options and then you can just pick the option that says trading with slavers is A-OK. And again, this has no impact on anything.If I'm not completely mistaken there are 6 important decisions you get to make that actually has an impact on the story. Everything else is filler column jiggling. Just wish it was more focused on the narrative impact of your decisions instead of encouraging trying to minmax. For 15 bucks its tough. If you really liked the reigns games then check this out. But for the amount of content you actually get it is a tough sell for people who are on the edge

_childDocuments_.review: The setting is actually interesting, but the game is just bad designed.First of all, all the story paths are disjointed. Events appear in a confused order and many times it can happen to solve an event before the previous one in cronological order. On a text, story based games, this is a nonsense.That said, mechanics are simply not fun. Sometimes you are forced to take loss-loss decisions just because you have to balance poorly planned counters. It's not like you're compromising something to have something else (that's the very base of any political sims), it's just that you have to do something you don't want just to be able to keep playing. And, ofc, you also have to pay the consequences of your bad decision.When I play a political sim, I want to be able to shape the country as I want: I don't want to be forced to sabotage it just because my "tech" slider is too high and it is required to just be average to score a "crown".

_childDocuments_.review: I refunded the moment I realized that it felt like I was the kingdom itself, instead of a character within the game. I bought it despite the negative reviews and was upset to realize they were right. The fatal flaw of a game with such beautiful world building is that it lacks any *life*. By this, I mean that the details of this world are fascinating - I'm interested in the history and politics, and I'd love to get to know the people who live here. Unfortunately, there are no characters. You play as head of a house, but no members of that house are introduced, no personal goals established (outside of the cultural goals of your house, which are not really necessary or worthwhile to pursue - either narratively or gameplay wise). The 'history book' writing is interesting, but without the human drama it ends up feeling very dry.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR in case you don't want to watch the video:1. There is virtually no voice acting, and 90% of the game is reading text, and making decisions that affects resource balancing (in every sense of the word)2. The game’s tutorial and  tool tips are somewhat barebones - so its going to take a lot of trial and error; and again - reading the in game encyclopaedia  to help you to learn the complex and somewhat convoluted systems. Sometimes the ‘good’ decision, ends up being the  ‘bad’ decision. 5. Art and music are on point - nearly every story event / thread has its own unique hand drawn art. _childDocuments_.review: The biggest dilemma with the King's Dilemma is the fact that its a single player video game based on a multiplayer board game, and doesn't tweak its systems enough to handle what a giant change that is.It's a digitization where we needed an adaptation; with an actually rock solid presentation and kind of an interesting story/world doing a ton of lifting to compensate for a gameplay system that's too contrived to make sense of on a first playthrough but too 'solved' to be of any interest on a subsequent.It's not meritless, it's just hard to identify who this game is for.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I was torn between a positive and negative review. The story is interesting, and I enjoyed my time. I had some issues at the start as the game isn't compatible with my resolution, but you'll be fine for most monitors - mine is just wide. Once I figured that out, i enjoyed ambling along making choices. It took me a couple of hours, (which is annoying, because without technical difficulties I could've refunded the game). The real kicker is there just simply isn't enough gameplay. It takes around 2 hours to finish one playthrough and you quickly realise when you finish the game that there isn't really much to any of it. The choices don't really matter. There aren't any concequences to most actions and the game rewards you no matter what really. If this was a couple of quid, I could justify it as I do love these style of games, but for £12.99 for 2 hours, it really isn't worth it unfortunately. If you don't care about the money, or gameplay and just want a somewhat interactive story, I'd recommend. If you want any sort of gameplay that isn't a pointless coin toss - maybe avoid. It's a shame, as it has real potential. It's just poorly designed gameplay mechanics. Lose all your money? okay. Kill some children so the townspeople hate you? ok. Make enough bad decisions (or good ones?) that the king abdicates (why?)? No problem, we'll reset your economy, millitary, knowledge and happiness. In most cases you actually want to overextend your influence, loose all your money, etc. because you benefit from the reset.

_childDocuments_.review: The Board Game is fantastic. I played in full group of 5 and we all loved the game. Me and my group are avid gamers, and play a variety of games. Kings Dilemma is not a grand strategic game. Its a experience, that is centered around negotiation, politics, and role playing. When I saw this version, I immediately bought it and have been playing through it here and there. I do feel like the tutorial is a bit lacking... It took me a few dilemma's to understand how the advisor role worked, alliances, etc. It also wasn't immediately clear how voting worked, as far as seeing the NPC votes before you cast your vote. In the board game, the voting is done in order. There is a mechanic each vote round for a Leader, who always starts votes, and a Moderator who can break ties. I was definitely curious how they would alter this for solo play. Essentially, the power you commit is based on where the other houses land, which you can see before you cast your vote. So you always vote last. As I get into it, the vote mechanic works fine, and I am enjoying it. This game, board or digital, is not about things 'working out'. This is the point. You make a choice, with the best info you think you have, but things are not are they seem. Crucially, if you are gaming the advisor, e.g. extremist, opulent, etc.. that is, trying to get the most points per reign, you are constantly at odds with your perceived story goals, continuing plot threads in the way you think they 'should' go, and... your morals. In the board game, there is (should) be a role playing spirit, you play to your House and the evolution of your understanding of your and the other players House's grows through the campaign. In this version, most of that is lost, however I definitely so far feel the crunch, 'the dilemma' - insofar of my urge to min-max my points in each reign and watching the story sort of fall apart for my broader House goals or the kingdom at large for that matter. This is interesting to me and presents a solid puzzle. I know in advance that I am not going to 'win'. If you played the board game and liked it, I think you will like this too. Its quick, easy to quit and pick up where you left off, and you will have fun remembering some of the plot threads from the board game. I know I am....

_childDocuments_.review: Like many reviews, I’m barely giving this thumbs up because of the awesome story and world, but it was let down by lack of a ‘game’ and limited meaningful choices. I wanted to love this sooo much, was looking for a Yes, Your Grace or Suzerain type ruling adventure, especially as this was tauted as a multi-generational dynastic struggle.Only found out about the board game after and it was a horrible port from a scheming 5 player backstabbing fest to a single player interactive storybook. In hindsight, instead of cramming the board mechanics behind a computer screen, the developers should have borrowed the setting and plot points but made a separate game system to fit.The 5 resources military, money, morale, food and knowledge should have stayed persistent, instead of arbitrarily resetting every time the king changes. If I paid a fortune to upgrade my army then that should damn well reflect in a high soldier count or otherwise be incorporated in the final battle.There was a beautifully drawn map (probably taken from the board game), but I wish it would update over time to reflect my choices and how the kingdom developed.Despite the frustratingly meaningless mechanics, the game did manage to keep me torn between making a choice that sided with my personal morals vs what was better for my house vs what might be better for the kingdom in the long run.The heir system could have been so amazing if each generation gradually enhanced certain traits based on your historic choices and gene point allocations to make your descendants better at military vs finances vs diplomacy vs espionage etc.Most coin flip choices either didn’t matter or might affect the narrative in a cool way but have zero impact on the game. Instead, allying with a rival kingdom should provide their troops in a demonstrable way for the final battle. Currying favour with other houses should have provided elite special units like in Yes, Your Grace. Taking the time to build granaries early game should give extra tactical options to support a long siege. Researching forbidden magic should open dank ways to obliterate the enemy, but maybe the holy knights joined the other side because of it and so forth.Still a wonderfully dark and intriguing story that I enjoyed discovering. My house beliefs and quests really fit with my morals, so I enjoyed a second play through to figure out how to achieve them. Thank you to the devs and thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving my playthrough of The King's Dilemma (the board game) thus far and so this videogame version was definitely on my radar. I haven't played much yet since I've discovered that the story in the boardgame and videogame seem to be the same. Since that is the case, if you have a chance to play the boardgame, I HIGHLY recommend doing so with 3-4 friends that you can meet semi-regularly about 13 times. The boardgame experience is amazing, and uncovering the story amidst debating and arguing and ruling amongst your friends is a one-of-a-kind experience.I'm excited to see how some mechanics translated into a singleplayer experience, including relationships between many different families and the ability to select between multiple different story beats at a given time. In the boardgame, you draw from a deck and all answer that dilemma immediately. In the videogame, you have the opportunity to select certain dilemmas based on limited information, such as which values might rise or fall as a result of your decision. Since you never know if those will be positive or negative, you still have to play it by ear and that leads to exciting stories!Other reviewers condense the game down to "simple yes or no decisions" and while every dilemma is answered "Aye" or "Nay", they lose the depth of those decisions when ignoring the other participants, NPCs that have motives and desires of their own that you have to balance and sometimes hedge resources against in order for the decision to fall your way. An interesting addition to the videogame over the boardgame is how your relationship with other families can grow or worsen based on actions you take. Not just are the logistical results of each dilemma to be taken into account, so too are the relationships with your peers and the very real and very heavy narrative consequences that you can't take back... until you play again!Again, I highly recommend playing the boardgame first if you have the opportunity. I will be attempting to finish my playthrough of the boardgame before finishing the videogame, even if it seems a "run" in the videogame can be completed in mere hours. I don't want to spoil the fun I have as I discover the story of Ankst in realtime with my friends, but I'm excited for the ability to replay and relive epic story beats that have come to haunt us in our games and to see the other side of stories that were locked from us! Thank you Big Trouble for providing the opportunity to participate again in this wonderful story without having to rely on rounding up 3-4 friends to meet up every week for months!

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review.In this episode I check out the dark fantasy Strategy game called The Kings Dilemma: Chronicles, which was developed and published by Big Trouble. The Kings Dilemma is an Adaption of the Popular Boardgame series, taking place in the kingdom of Ankist, a land ruled by several kingdoms, each with their own politics and agendas. The player takes the role of a Councillor to the one of Ankists Kings, guiding the Kingdom through difficult events including war and famine. To do this youll need to manage the kingdoms recources, make difficult decisions and live with the consequences. The end goal is to stop the coming of the Apocalypse at the hands of the Black Sun, a Cult that has been prophesised to end the world in fire and blood.While im not familiar with the board game, i enjoyed the experience of playing the Kings Dilemma so much ive decided to try it out. If your a fan of unique games you should definately check out this interesting mix of Strategy Game and Visual Novel.Please note: All opinions in this video are my own. _childDocuments_.review: Very much recommended to players of the board game, in part for the nice jolt of nostalgia (with the images and text much more prominently displayed than they ever can be on a small card being read by someone on the opposite side of the table), in part because your decisions will likely deviate from choices a group of contradictory players made at the table. Game play, as a solo game, isn't entirely the same, as you get a bit more sway, and much more choice in determining what order you encounter events, but in that way it felt like a more serious solo play version of multi-player game King of the Castle. It was great to see behind the veil of a few elements that had not been witnessed before in my play through with friends, though I think I played as the same (or similar) House. The tide of war seemed stacked in the favour of the traitors this time and, although three phases of war allow you to make tactical decisions to aid your chosen side, loyalists or traitor, it was fun playing as the traitors this time, having won the board game as a loyalist (also the computer game makes the final battle feel a lot more engrossing).Not so much recommended to those who've not played the board game but, arguably, players of similar text based games like King of the Castle might also have fun with this.

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: There are many games out there that claim your choices matter and have a significant impact. In the majority of cases, the impact of your choices is minor at best and meaningless at worst. Few games have managed to really make you feel as though you are substantially impacting the world. In this game, every single choice can have a huge impact.Based on a board game, the screenshots make The King's Dilemma seem like a grand strategy game, but it's much more focused than that. This is a game entirely about making choices and watching the impacts of those choices play out. There are a lot of mechanics working together here, but it's not as daunting as it looks. You play a king who is trying to lead an empire under the looming threat of a prophecy that is predicting a major uprising in the future. You will be given different scenarios one after the other, and each requires a yes or no choice. You have to balance the impact to your kingdom's resources, the other members of your council and their opinion of you, how your people and other nation's will interpret them and all the while, also making choices that will keep you in power as long as possible and appeal to your assigned personality type. Eventually, your king will be replaced by an heir (who may lead very differently) and you have to do this through a number of generations, then try to lead the kingdom through the uprising.Unlike many "choices matter" games that tend to have very binary good or evil choices, many of those in The King's Dilemma are grey at best. Often, you will be given no win situations, where you either have to weigh which choice is the lesser of two evils or worse, make a choice you don't want to because it's what you need to do in order to keep things together. I had multiple choices in my playthrough where I started at the screen for several minutes because I really couldn't decide the optimal path forward. That is this game's greatest strength and I dare say, it's one of the most impactful "choices matter" games I've ever played.The other huge strength of this game is in its writing. It does a masterful job of conveying a lot of information and the weight of that information in few words. You won't ever have to read paragraphs of text between choices and despite the mechanical complexity, even the tutorials are quick, yet informative. You never feel that your time is being wasted with narrative padding and everything gets to the point, while still being pointed. Even though a run of this will probably only take 4 hours or so, you'll feel like you've accomplished a lot and there is tons of replayability available for those who want to play as a different type of ruler or see how scenarios play out with other choices.When I got my review code for this, I went into it very skeptical and came out with this being one of my biggest surprises of 2023 so far. If you like kingdom management games and especially, if you like a heavy narrative where your choices really matter, don't skip this one.

name: Ravenswatch
detailed_description: SUPPORTER EDITION Early Access Roadmap About the Game Ravenswatch is a top-down roguelike action game in which you play as heroes of tales and legends that must slay hordes of nightmarish creatures in nerve-racking fights. After the success of Curse of the Dead Gods©, Passtech Games returns with an improved formula and an addictive game experience with endless replay value. It can be played solo or with up to four players in co-op. Play as 9 heroes, each with a unique twist and individual gameplay, including Little Red Riding Hood, who suffers from lycanthropy; Sun Wukong, the fallen monkey king; the Snow Queen with her evil powers; and many other familiar characters who have a darker side and are more violent than you might remember. The Nightmare has invaded the world of dreams and is corrupting everything in its wake. Faced with this evil, the Ravenswatch is gathering heroes from tales and legends from all over the world to lead a crucial battle and restore the fragile balance. But the heroes themselves have been corrupted. How deep do the roots of this evil go? Explore 3 open maps filled with activities and inspired by enchanted forests and marshes, One Thousand and One Nights, and Arthurian legends respectively. Help the inhabitants of Reverie, such as the Three Little Pigs, Sinbad the Sailor and Morgan the fairy, and earn valuable rewards to help you in your future battles. Reveal the story of each character and Reverie, run after run. Ravenswatch is a meticulously crafted combination of a dark fantasy atmosphere with a comic book style. To defeat the Nightmare and reach the final chapter, you will need a strong build, focus and/or excellent teamwork. You have 3 days and 3 nights to increase your power. Face the chapter boss when you feel ready… or when you no longer have a choice. In the purest tradition of the roguelike genre, Ravenswatch is a challenging game but fair, balanced and refined thanks to community feedback. Epic boss battles and over 50 formidable, uniquely designed enemies. With each level completed, you earn the right to choose a new talent and improve your heroes' skills. Combine talents, items and dreams to craft the most powerful builds. Even more fun with friends or using the matchmaking feature: explore the synergies and relationships between heroes with up to four players in co-op. During your game, optimize your time and make the best use of the upgrades you earn. With each new run, explore a new map filled with activities and enemies. Unlock new heroes and new content from one run to the next. Over 200 talents, 50 magical items and endless build combinations. Randomly generated maps with a wide range of activities. 4 difficulty levels and customized game modes for an even greater challenge or to enjoy Ravenswatch at your own pace. Regular updates will add new free content.

_childDocuments_.review: The art, music, multiplayer and rogue lite concept is what makes this game worth buying. However, the content is right now severely lacking. There is no depth to the character progress. Every build feels pretty much the same. You can't really specialize your character meaningfully. The progress in between runs is insignificant, so you get to experience 80% of the game in the first 2 runs. And there is also no backstory, which I would be willing to get over, if the game mechanics were better thought through. However, in the current form, I don't believe the game is worth it's price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great Rouge-Like! Twisted and dark story book characters and level. Awesome gameplay, easy controls with excellent button mapping for controller support. Really hope the developers keep up with this game, there is alot of potential. keep pulling from fairy tales and working new characters in. Would definitely recommend to a friend! My only complaint is the connection with multiplayer lobbies seems to inexplicably crash on one person or anothers towards the end or right after the boss fight, then all xp for the run is lost for every person in party making it frustrating to play for long periods.other than that, great game! 8/10, Help the lobbying issue, would give 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying it so far, and I’v been playing by myself. All heroes are fun to play as and feel unique, despite some feeling better suited for multiplayer. My biggest qualms so far is there isn’t an option to change the color of enemy attack cones. Besides it being a dark game, I’m colorblind and the red blends in with the background (especially on the major boss). Would love to be able to adjust to any color we like. Obviously matchmaking would be awesome, but it’s a newer game so it’ll come with time. Add that accessibility option and a brightness adjuster and the game would be a huge improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: So the first thing that needs to be written  is that this game seems to actually not have a tutorial. Not "Not much of a tutorial", not "An inadequate tutorial", not even "A tutorial that isn't really practical to playing the game", the game actually . I just spent my first play session going "What the ♥♥♥♥ am I even trying to do?" interacting with as much of the game as possible in the hopes of being given an answer. I haven't found one yet.I'm not gonna stop trying yet, this is an "I've played for less than an hour so far" review, but that's a pretty noticeable red flag, that the only teaching this game is doing is putting button prompts on-screen so I don't have to just guess at how to use core game mechanics.So yeah. that's pretty baffling to me, that I haven't had literally any of the rules explained to me. We'll see if that changes, but its certainly making me ask "How good does this game have to be for me to keep trying?" and I don't think what I've seen so far is that good. I guess I have another hour or so before I start asking if this game is better off refunded.Edit: It did not take me an extra hour to decide.

_childDocuments_.review: Ravenswatch is a game that will leave you spellbound with it engaging interactions with enemies and diverse set of skillsets with each character. Each character comes with their own unique set of skills and abilities, making gameplay a dynamic and thrilling experience. (I am not sponsored at all)One of the things that sets Ravenswatch apart from the other games is the roguelike feature in the ARPG role. Although not as quick hack and slash as a game like Diablo or Torchlight. I find it extremely satisfying leveling up and going from struggling with an enemy to mowing down groups of enemies with the right types of different builds. Whether you prefer to play as a stealthy rogue with critical damage or a powerful mage with frost ability, each character really has a unique aspect into the game. While there isn't a public online match feature available just yet, I believe we are still in the Early Access part of the game. I did see the alot of people complaining about it just being a demo, but in my opinion I see this literally what it's called accessing this game early while it is still in development and testing out the waters while getting feedback from their players. In the meantime, the game has tons of replayability and actually is a blast to play. This is a game worth investing early into and seeing how it comes out especially if they start releasing different aspects or even like a weapon/armor system into the game. The options are honestly limitless. I hope that they do add a lobby function where players can gather and chat before starting a match and maybe even be able to have an alliance to bring a more social aspect part to the game. I do enjoy a good game with some online competition. (Maybe like different runs or a daily challenge with different modifiers) **(Adding custom modifiers into the game that maybe the host can enable i.e. Higher HP monsters, electric monsters, invisible monsters, some that pop like a balloon etc.) Overall, I think anyone trying to find maybe a hybrid to Hades, Diablo, and roguelike deck builders may enjoy this. I can't wait to see what the developers have in store for us in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very high quality, it bares extreme similarities to predecessors like Hades while keeping the gameplay fresh with well designed characters with abilities and skills that complement one another to form unique and pleasurable playstyles.I am not going to bother listing the Pros, because frankly if I do not list it as a con here, I think the developers have done a phenomenal job with the game...Cons:- Occasional bug that does not allow for the destruction of corrupted tumors on the map, can make it hard to efficiently farm XP and prevents damaging the level boss preemptively.- Level variety gets stale after a few consecutive runs, although the content that is here is extremely polished and entertaining, there just needs to be more of it.Overall the current state of the game is a great vertical slice, and if the devs continue doing exactly what they have been doing to this point, the game should go down in history as one of the greats of roguelite games.

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed this game and it is only in Early Access. I have soloed played the first chapter multiple times with all the heroes. _childDocuments_.review: Ravenswatch is a fun roguelike action RPG with good replayability and coop. Six characters, ten difficulties, and plenty of unlocks makes for a fair amount of content for the price. I've played for several hours, and it feels as if I have only scratched the surface. Many negative Steam reviews complain about a lack of content, but I disagree.No game is complete on day one of early access. Those who want more can always buy later. The studio's previous title, Curse of the Dead Gods, proves that they can put together a solid game. More levels, bosses, and characters are on the roadmap for later this year, and I'm sure the team will deliver.

After playing some more of this game i see they made beowulf and gepetto a lot better. they are now some of the best characters imo for ease to play and comfort where as i cannot say the same for the rest. Ice queen and melv the mermaid are really strong and probably should be held as the example of what the other characters should be. Carmilla is fun and has a good framework but everything she does relies on blood which is just exhausting to work with., she can do insane damage but getting to that point should be made easier. she dies do easily and honestly since she is a vampire should have vampirism. i think her q should not require blood and she should have passive heal from attack like wukong along with a bit more health. Wukong just needs more health and honestly should not take extra damage for switching stances he gets one shotted and the extra damage on top of low is just ridiculous. Pied piper needs to have one of his abilities generate rats because they just take too long to generate. He also needs more health and his defense ability should push back elites/ bosses. i dont know why his cant effect boss when other characters can straight block damage. The game is good but higher difficulties enemies have too much health and damage the boss becomes a boring slog on higher difficulties for low dmg characters like beowulf and there is not an obvious reason to do higher difficulties. I think it would be a nice feature if you could have a setup for a chartacter before you go in like pick 1 or 2 specific traits so you can have some control in what you are getting. the enemies that can heal should not be able to fully heal an elite, elite pigs hook is bigger than hitbox when close to it, enemies should take a second to find you so you can have more freedom in exploring. quests should pause the timer so lower damage characters can do them along with the pig quest straw and wood houses enemy waves being shorter or houses have more health as well as a feature of being able to start it without all the material instead of waiting would be nice. challenge boss that requires key should not be timed or at least have less health because they are unreasonable and the challenge would be fun if i could actually do it.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a ton but here are my thoughts so far.Having played Curse of the Dead Gods until I could parry in my sleep, I was VERY disappointed that there was no parry, but maybe there will be a character that can do so in the future. This is completely subjective, but games like this benefit GREATLY from a higher skill ceiling, and active defensive mechanics are a free way to raise that ceiling. I understand it comes with other balance issues, however. Each character has abilities that fill slots, a "power," "defense," "special," etc. None of them require much in the way of timing on a short scale. There's an evade/dash, but from what I can tell there are no iframes. Which is fine, but it makes me question why there's only one dash charge. You're not gonna know what the hell anything is or what it means. You can hit the menu button on an Xbox gamepad to see a description of your abilities and skills which is nice. That's it, though. Everything else is just there and you're expected to know whether you're making a mistake or not. It isn't completely cryptic, but it is a bit annoying. Although I am not always a fan of long tutorials. There are some "quests" so far on each run, but I think they aren't done yet. They involve gathering pickups for an NPC, I've seen 2 variations. On the first one, the pickups (or at least their general area) show up on the map and I missed that goal by 1 item. The other one, nothing on the map and I didn't see any on the ground except one that spawned immediately when I started the quest. The enemy mechanics are a bit baffling. There's a stun bar for some enemies and not others which makes sense, but you'll find yourself using the higher stun moves on enemies out of habit only to discover that while a hulking tree brute can be stunned with so many hits, knee-high spider enemies don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about being concussed and as a result you'll lose half your HP after the enemies in the encounter that drop health are long gone. The healing offered seems generous for a game like this, until you realize how absolutely unforgiving the enemies are. Not punishing, because "punishing" implies there's a perfect dance you can perform but will pay dearly for mistake. I say "unforgiving" because you don't really have to "make a mistake" to get your face smashed in. As I mentioned, there's no active defense mechanics and dodging only allows you to escape the telegraphed damage area of attacks. There's also a bunch of poorly explained mechanics. For instance, the warrior character has a shield bash that "prevents ALL incoming damage while held" (emphasis mine), and while using a certain ability heal you for 30% of damage blocked. But, joke's on you player, there are numerous attacks which completely ignore the block, and unlike other games that have similar mechanics, you don't get to know which ones are unblockable until you lose 2/3 your health from an unblockable attack that stuns you while 2 enemies attack at the same time. I have faith that passtech will develop this into a fantastic game, but right now it's not quite found it's legs. That said, it's still fun, and I plan on giving it a few more hours before I feel comfortable not recommending it, and I'm gonna say you should pick it up if you like these types of games.

_childDocuments_.review: EA Review:My thoughts to the Developers:I had high hopes for this game when I first played it in early EA.I thought, "With another year or two, this could be a fleshed out experience that could likely find great mainstream success due to the polish and the care put into the combat and the character / enemy design."Really, I thought the game could easily be more enjoyable than Hades (for me, at least).Fast forward to 1.0 launch, and I have to say I am fairly disappointed at the lack of variety run-to-run. The foundation is so strong, but the overworld needs more dynamic events and encounters. The enemy variety isn't quite there either. The bosses and the side-quests are always the exact same. More side quests / varients to side-quests, new bosses (or distinct variants of existing bosses), and a range of effects that could happen in the overworld for each chapter are some of the minimum things I feel the current game loop needs to feel fresh.For example, you could have a chance of a lightning storm event that lasts through the night, you could have dense fog event, an earthquake / fissure event to change the routing mid chapter, you could have a terrible elite variant mini-boss spawn worth extra $$ for a unique challenge.  You get the idea.The character design in this game is top-notch in my opinion, but in the end the game in its current state is not as strong as Curse of the Dead Gods (dev's last game)I hope that future development can lift this game up from where it stands today, but I am unsure if the studio has the funds for that much ongoing development. Best of luck Passtech. Despite what I wrote above, your  team's talent is evident.

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptionally fun early access experience. The procedural generation works well in the open-map style environment, meaning that even though there is only one stage available at this time it still feels fresh each run. Once the game gets fleshed out fully, this is a real masterpiece in the making.Pros: - Diverse characters and playstyles - Every button and ability is useful - At higher difficulties, each enemy is a real threat and needs to be respected - Music is great, and ties into gameplay nicelyCons: - Uses a lot of computer resources, for some reason - Early access, therefore only limited content is available (I'm happy with what is available, some may not be, beware)

_childDocuments_.review: I give the game a positive review, but I would like to point out that there are a lot of problems with the gameplay. As with most such games, luck factor is a thing in every aspect. There is not much you can do about it. But the fact that certain builds just not working is sad. There are skills where you have to hit two opponents to activate. With the end boss, this is quite problematic and difficult to implement. And other skills are too weak. For example, you get 12 shields or 4 life... The opponent hits you with 50 and you can recharge 4 after 10 sec cd. The characters are different and enjoyable in their own way, but one is clearly stronger than the other. A piper can't be compared to scarlet, who deals a lot of damage, heals herself and can completely avoid injuries in at least two ways, While our piper friend just runs around and shoots his weak auto attack. I would say that he is a support character, but he doesn't have many such skills that can be used apart from breaking the defense. Rats are funny and powerful, but they charge quite slowly even if you upgrade their ability. Geppetto is very strong and can always summon new puppets that can hit really hard, He is capable compared to the rats' one-time stunt. The direction is good, but much more diverse skills would be required to avoid the fact that you can only choose from 2 options also can only level till 6. The 24-minute playing time also makes the game a bit urgent and rushed. It is understandable that this is intended game design, but the fact that you are constantly running and racing against the clock greatly impairs the gaming experience. Despite this, the game is imaginative and enjoyable, but I hope they put a lot of work into it in the future and it doesn't become another Darksburg..UPDATE AFTER BETA TEST:15 minutes is very little and you won't reach half of the course before the boss appears. I didn't even get the ultimate at the end of the first level, and I couldn't pick up what I wanted even with the speedrun tactic of leaving the opponent behind. The opponents on the second court are brutal and not in a good way. AOE everywhere, flamethrower, tracking projectiles, armored crabs and the rest. It is understandable that the game is rouge-like, but this difficulty will frighten many players because you have to be a professional to do it and even then you need luck.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game Good things: + 8 heroes - 3 of them need to be unlocked - each is pretty unique+ Something new in Rogue-like genre - you have limited time till boss fight - so you need to gain as much xp and money to evolve in limited time. That creates new level of decisions - your party is alway like 'okay chest is worth a shot - while this bonus dungeon - nope' + another mechanic of globally limited revives for the whole team - is also something fresh and nice+ good optimization and good net-code - it is available for 4-players coop and it runs pretty smooth. + atmosphere and music are fine as well - characters of fairy tales fighting nightmares with the help and guidance of the Sandman - what's not to like here? + it is re-playable and you need to beat the game a few times to have all abilities unlocked for the character - it requires a few hours for each character+ new map released on September 2023 - showing that the project is not abandoned Negative things: - close combat heroes are feeling much more challenging - so it can be pretty frustrating for some players - you constantly die and waste team's revives (apologizing in front of you teammates for noobing around)- you should not expect TOO MUCH of a content YET. I'd say  so far it is extended demo maybe  (still worth your time exploring - it won't end in 2 hours - trust me)- bosses' design (mini-bosses and random encounters are great,but main bosses of each level look similar color-wise  - maybe rethink concept of how Nightmares should look like - gameplay mechanics of each boss are very different though)Verdict Solid good game - 10/10. The only serious negative - I want more content - more heroes, more monsters, more levels, more perks, more items. It is not yet-one-more-early-access-greedy-♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. It is a good product for somewhat of 20-30 hours of gameplay depending on your speed, which is totally fair for 15 bucks. And you are able to enjoy it with you friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I read a lot of the negative reviews around the game only being "one level" or boring because there is only "one boss" and the concerns about the timer being "too short". I decided to pick it up because with loops only being about 25 minutes, you can just play two runs in under an hour and then refund it. Here are my thoughts on these concerns: Buy it and play for an hour and then refund it if you don't enjoy the first few runs.1. Level is adequately sized for multiple replays. Paired with the timer it makes it hard to explore entire thing in one run, which again forces you to make choices that have real impacts on gameplay.2. The one boss fight is repetitive but it evolves over difficulty increases. Boss kill feels rewarding and is good payback at higher levels for all the fails it causes during early runs3. The timer is good. It could be a couple minutes longer 30 would be nice. Timer forces you to make  and choices are good. Doing multiple runs that last 45-60 min would feel long and grindy, 25-30 is a good feel for the loop.4. It's  and this "one level" has little to know bugs (that I personally experienced) and has plenty of characters with different playstyles from each other but also within themselves. You are getting a fair amount of game (with plenty more on the way) for $20 and then you get the full thing when it releases. 5. Some enemies need some balancing. Pigs are  strong and are unbalanced in mobs that are only them. In theme the "three little pigs" missions are horribly imbalanced, specifically for melee characters in single player. These are probably fine in multiplayer but solo they are awful to try and complete.- Only having one level: This is a valid concern to raise and initially it was a big deterrent to purchasing. Having played for almost 10 hours I can confidently say, it's hardly noticeable. Unless you are "pro-gamer" tier who 100%'s all content in a single day, then sure, it might be a drag. For a more casual player who only plays a couple of hours every day, there is so much to explore with each of the characters, learning different "builds" based on what you roll, you hardly notice. Also this is a rouge-lite. the purpose is to replay things again and again and again and again etc. Plus this  early access. There will be more levels upon full release, and their roadmap shows multiple new characters and levels to come in future updates.- "One Boss": This you'll probably just be split on no matter what. It is the same boss, and its generally the same mechanics every time. The harder difficulties you unlock the more mechanics unlock, so the boss fight does "evolve" but it is still fun and engaging so far. Again it creates that feeling that choices matter and that you get to test your choices to see how well you did.- Timer is "too short": Another good concern. I like to play games at my own pace and enjoy playing them however long I want, this sounded terrible. I like it a lot. It is  jarring, at first. However it creates a certain amount of "pressure" that keeps the game feeling tense and like there is something at stake. I love running through packs of dudes and hacking them to pieces, but that's also what games like diablo are for. The time forces you to make . What upgrades to get, how far to go and when to come back to other areas when you're higher level etc. Having to make choices keep each run fresh, and they also develop as you level each character and unlock more possibilities with traits, upgrades, etc.- Balancing: Some enemies feel a bit too tough. The pigs in general are ridiculously brutal. At almost all levels if you don't have a combo which allows you to 1-2 shot them, they will sync their combos and turn you to swiss cheese in 1s flat. Spiders are also a pretty tough and could use some minor tweaks.The three little pig events where you help them build a house are absolutely dogs***t though. That one things feels the least balanced, at least for solo play. Ranged characters seem to be able to complete them okay, but melee characters are too slow and the distance between nodes is too far or has too many mobs that prevent pickups. Generally speaking though if something is killing you though, run away gain a level, get a piece of gear, and then go back and you should be fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is simply great, combats smooth, progression in game is consistent and you feel rewarded with powerspikes for exploring as much as you can in your limited time period of an act (25 minutes until the boss). The time limit is definitely a good addition as it keeps the pace of the game up and rewards risky fights to time save with. Rogue-like wise, meta progression is a bit on the light side with you being rewarded more for you learning from your experiences. You instead unlock new heroes and new talents for your heroes to find in a run as your meta-progression, so no flat "you start stronger" progression if that's what you're looking for. However, run to run feels quite different due to the random map changes, random finds of talents causing changes to builds and playstyles.Hero design is also a big boon for the game, with each hero having a diverse playstyle, moveset, upgrade trees and traits; their are alot of traits that help your teamates if doing co-op, however as I was a solo player I can't say how the game plays in a group.However, the game is very much in early access; With 1 act, 9 difficulties (unlocked from beating the previous difficulty), 6 heroes (with multiple unlocks through meta progression) the game has a lot of replayabilty as of now but at the same time can feel lackluster with where your run ends abruptly.For the Devs, I found myself running through mobs half the time or trying to sneak objectives from beside them, as there's no rewards for killing them (besides experience), It'd be a good idea to find a reward system for killing the individual mobs or for killing a full camp of them (such as gold drops, or some objective around the map that requires killing 'x' many mobs to unlock). Would also be nice to have some sort of variation on the world boss with multiple phases or different aspects or something (I avoided the tumours as the boss was very one dimensional when I understood the gimmicks making it the easiest fight with the tumours just being timesinks rather than rewards). Other than that great game, look forward to playing it further :)

It seems like the world doesn't scale off of anything. Don't get me wrong, I love difficult and challenging games but this is to a point where it's unfunny and just suffering. There is a deadline and you need to get most out of it before the timer runs out. You can do only few easy events and a quest. You don't even get to explore the most parts of the map. Even If you manage to get bunch of best boons, you don't really feel like you're getting stronger. Some of you might think It's a skill issue but even tho abilities are well telegraphed, big groups of overlapping monsters just insta kills you most of the time because of how long the skill animation locks are. I love playing this game however, I feel like it just gets a bit more frustrating every attempt. I'll say avoid it for now.NEW REVIEW : They added longer timer to the game. You have enough time to explore and cleanse everything in the map If you wish. I haven't tested all the characters yet but some of them are really fun and scales pretty good with boons and allows you to be a lone wolf even in late game. I haven't checked If they buffed my boii Beowulf since I like playing warriors but I still recommend it anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: I was going to wait for 1.0 to actually review this, but I just don't think I need to anymore. I've put over 100 hours in over the last year of early access (about evenly split between solo and co-op) and I can say both ways to play this are really engaging, fun and often very difficult. There's still plenty left to accomplish with each character, and I'm still excited about doing it. It would be a mistake to compare Ravenswatch too much to a Hades...but I'm known for some good mistakes. I grabbed this because I wanted and action roguelike with co-op play and it's absolutely the best I've seen. This is much more about mechanics, and requires skill and focus even in the most "broken" combo run. Ironically, It's almost completely without narrative. For some, that may mean this feels a bit light on content, but if you engage with all the systems, there's plenty of depth, especially considering the resources behind this compared to what a team like Supergiant can do. It is not as frantically-paced in combat (co-op would be a nightmare at that speed), but timing is everything, and failing to use your abilities skillfully is also more punishing. I've introduced multiple groups and several solo players to this game, and I've not yet seen someone fail to enjoy it, so the current "Mixed" state of reviews honestly confuses me. There's certainly not shortage of good rogue-likes to choose from, but if you want to group up and get really cool combos going, this one is dream, despite the nightmare theme.

_childDocuments_.review: Game doesn't deserve the negative reviews it is getting. It is a very solid game with really superb skill and timing based combat. It only has one level currently true but it's a really really good level with multiple paths you can take. That's more a reason to give it a positive review but say wait to buy till out of early access imo. This game is quite hard, so don't go in expecting Diablo or something of similar difficulty. You have to keep moving because you are on a timer till the boss and you can't fight every monster. Also the combat is just a lot more challenging than Diablo. This is all very good, I'm not complaining, just describing it's a more challenging experience overall. Co-op is very decent.

_childDocuments_.review: An overall good rogue like with some refreshing mechanics and gameplay. It's a nice mix between a Hack'n'Slash and a Rogue like.The Fairy Tale setup is kinda unique and original even it has some similarities with existing media like Rise of the Guardians movie, or The Wolf Among Us games, but it has its own approach of the thing so it's really refreshing.Regarding the gameplay and diversity, all the characters have their own playstyle, and I didn't feel any redundancy in any of them, which is very likable. I do appreciate the unlocking system for the secret characters, which is very interesting and smart 'cause it makes you play at least once with every character so you can discover their kit and unique gameplay, so you can find your favorite. It's very nice and I'm glad that the devs didn't locked characters behind a +10h grind wall.+ I didn't feel one character to be overpowered in comparison of the other, the game is pretty well balanced in this aspect. I'd say it's more a question of affinity and playstyle that will make you play a character, and not his power so I appreciate.The coop part is a really nice idea, it add a nice social value to the game, and I hope to see more rogue like game with that feature in the future 'cause it's really fun, especially with some friends. However it might be a little bit unbalanced in regards of the difficulty, especially in the lower difficulty levels (with a friend of mine, we kinda destroyed the game in lower difficult, and we were only 2).And for the difficulty, I feel the game is pretty well balanced overall, at least in solo. Ennemies might have too much HP in Avalon, especialy if you messed up your build and don't have enough damage, but I guess it's part of the learning curve of the game and it encourages you to think about your build and adapt your game plan, depending of the character you play.In conclusion I'd would say this game will please aas equal people who appreciate a good rogue-like and people who enjoy original universes and cool Fairy tales stories.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of Curse of the Dead Gods and in many ways, this just feels like an upgrade. Combat is responsive and agile, with exceptional visuals indicating where to be and where to not be, which effects are good and which are bad, and where your teammates are. Balance seems reasonable so far. The heroes have really impactful and unique movesets, which I tremendously like. I'm an avid gamer and some of the characters have mechanics I've simply never seen before. While content is a bit short -- only act 1 is out right now -- and the game isn't perfect, I do strongly recommend this game. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lot of fun ! The characters all have a unique gameplay style, the enemies are diverse, and combat feels very satisfying. It looks pretty great, too. The customization options give it a lot of replay value even if you stick to one character, which is a pretty impressive feat IMO.I'm a big fan of Curse of the Dead Gods (the devs' previous game) and comparing the two games is pretty interesting. While Ravenswatch isn't as technical and deliberate than CODG, it's more focused on customizing your hero's abilities and powers to create unique effects and combos - it's arguably more interested in the strategic level than in the tactical aspect, but it works. It took me some time to get rid of my CODG reflexes ("why can't I dodge all the time ??") but once the game clicked, I got hooked.Regarding the Early Access thing - I have some experience with Passtech Games' Early Access releases and I'm confident they will deliver good updates. I got into CODG during the Alpha stage so I got to experience its whole Early Access journey, and I genuinely don't have anything to complain about. The updates were solid, on-time, and I don't even remember any major bug : it was Early Access done right IMO. As for Ravenswatch - I tried the game in Alpha too, and it has already received important updates (with some community-driven changes) before it even hit EA, so there's no reason to assume it will be any different.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has bought Curse of the Dead Gods from the beginning of early access, I know this game will also be a slam dunk.  Yes there is only one "map" (or chapter)in Ravenswatch at the moment, but there are still plenty of heroes, abilities, difficulty levels, and items to unlock and enjoy using. The amount of content/updates Passtech Games have proven they can add to a game within an early access period assures me that this game will be even more amazing at launch. Do not sleep on this game, the combat is too good and the characters are very unique and well designed. The timed nature of a run before the chapter boss begins means that player choice always feels deliberate and engaging. And while I can't speak for the multiplayer experience I can only imagine it feels even better if the characters (with combo-able abilities or buffs) feel great to play solo. I do have a few suggestions for things that I'm sure are being worked on, but will give people reading a reminder that this game is still very much an early access title. -A tutorial.-More detailed explanations of status effects and item bonuses.-Let the Bard activate his trait during his ult (or maybe even auto activate it upon ult press), it feels clunky and takes away from his power fantasy if the rats do nothing if the player forgets to activate it before hand.-Rewards (like more character xp, or a color variant for the character) when playing at or completing higher difficulty levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game from the devs of Curse of the Dead Gods. Like that game, this is a challenging top-down hack'n'slash game, but now with an emphasis on co-op play. I tend to play with two friends but the challenge is really nicely balanced if you decide to play 2 player, or solo.Character choices are diverse - every option feels COMPLETELY different from the others. Some focus on melee, some defence, while others feel like support roles, slowing enemies, providing shields, or delivering the "vulnerable" debuff on enemies. So far, every character has been incredibly satisfying to play, bringing unique mechanics to each choice.Characters level up as you defeat enemies and the mechanic is also extremely satisfying, granting additional capabilities to existing attacks, or changing the nature of an attack completely.Graphics are dark, but beautiful, voice lines are professional and fun. Full controller support.The only negative is the spartan content. Characters max out at level 5 in game, with a meta-level of 6 (unlocking new upgrades and objects). This means that the game ends after just the first boss. A second level and second boss is promised by end of Sep 2023, however, and this will also buff the in-game max level to 8, which will mean that eye-wateringly powerful builds will be feasible. I can't wait.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: It's got really great pillars to work with, but currently it's very lacking in content. The combat is mildly fast with very different characters with their own playstyles and upgrades, but the higher difficulties don't offer anything new, just less xp and tankier enemies which make the game more of a chore. The stage bosses are also very disappointing, considering the theme of the game you'd think they would put iconic fairy-tale bad guys like the big bad wolf or the evil queen, but they're just some random grey blob that shoots out lasers.6/10 as of Early Access 4/2024, it's fun but lacks content and some difficulty tweaks, but I really look forward to what might come in the full release

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very nice blend of ARPG and Roguelike. But that being said that's probably the best complaint to have for an early access game, wanting more!

_childDocuments_.review: (Updating from an Early Access review)A co-op pve rogue-like with tight MOBA combat mechanics, they nailed it. The art style is captivating and a perfect choice for the twisted fairy tale aesthetic. The character design is well done, there's something so satisfying about ripping nightmares apart as a little red riding hood. The horizontal progression, adding more choices and synergies, focuses on player skill over grinding for loot to do bigger numbers.I have a couple of hours into the game (I think 50+ of active play) and I still don't have all the characters fully leveled to 9. The maps are generated so don't be concerned with "there being enough content with only 3 maps"The game takes place over 3 days - each day is 20 minutes - so when you hit "play" a good run will last an hour.The action is so frenetic that I prefer a controller over mouse and keyboard but both work well.  DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME SOLO - you are not getting the intended/optimal experience. For a $20 to $25 price point you should get your money's worth

_childDocuments_.review: Like what Hades would be if it was co-op and based on European mythology (public domain characters) instead of Greek. Every character has a delightfully twisted alternate backstory as well.Been playing this since there was only one level and the game just keeps getting more fun. Every character feels totally unique and strong, each with many different viable builds and play-styles. This game is super challenging and rewards players for their skill and knowledge. _childDocuments_.review: This is an elite-level game, and if you haven't undergone some degree of specialized training or gained an in-depth understanding of the game, your experience will be quite painful and frustrating. Therefore, it's not recommended for casual players who aren't mentally prepared to play.10/02  The changes in version 1.0 seem to make the game much friendlier. When I first started playing, it was unimaginable to go solo (it was extremely painful), so I focused on mastering the mechanic’s operations, which allowed me to clear the initial difficulty. However, it was still quite challenging.Now, I can complete the initial difficulty with relative ease. _childDocuments_.review: Update review after a year of playing Ravenswatch:Pros: The game is in great condition to play if people are still reluctant to purchase it. They have a post-launch road map of what's to come. So new content ahead free and paid DLC (mostly new heroes.)Playing solo is fun, but doing it with your friends and even 3 random players gives your runs variety. Heroes has multiple play style for everyone. You could go tank, hitter, casting from far away, medic, etc. Fun and sometimes OP build for each hero (if RNG bless you.)CONS:They still hasnt fixed the ridiculous aggro of enemies outside of Point of Interest. You want to explore the map and when you find a new POI and you want to engage, you either have to deal with random mobs of enemies outside of it or risk gathering them with the other enemies inside of POI, making your run excruciating and not fun at all. Other players will say "oh gitgud in de aggro on the enemies." Sure, be my guest in doing that with a party of 4, when you did successfully take off the aggro from random mobs, your teammate will inadvertently aggro them again, thus, wasting your time fulfilling POI interest.Maybe come up with a better way of filling the map with environmental hazards instead of increasing mobs at random spots? I understand if they are guarding healing well and clump of dream shards. It's just bad game design. Imagine fighting a mob of enemies with 5 different enemy healers. IT IS NOT FUN.Can we get another slot for talent to choose from? even though you gave us the option to reroll, the talent that you didnt want will have a higher chance of appearing again after a 2nd reroll, make it make sense.Adding another pattern of attacks for existing enemies will make the game refreshing and not redundant, IMO.conclusion: The game is great despite of the overlooked cons. 10/10 will recommend to other players.

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically and structurally it is one of my favorite rogue-likes/lites I've ever played. There isn't that much content at the moment, but there are 6 VERY different characters that are basically an equivalent of playing a different game, so I'm more than okay with dropping 18 euros on the game. There's also 10 difficulty levels, and higher difficulties genuinely make the game more fun. The most interesting thing I feel though is the structure. Since every character is so different and they all have combos and different requirements to be efficient and fast, the game really punishes you for being suboptimal with your character's kits because there's a 20 minute limit, so if you don't get through enough of the map before the final boss spawns, you have to face the boss weaker, and the faster you are the more power you get. That structure combined with genuinely interesting character kits essentially makes you feel like you're playing a speed-run game with really fun Battlerite/V-rising like combat mechanics, and I am there for it. I made a video review too expanding on this take and comparing Ravenswatch to some classic roguelikes.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: After putting in a good 80+ hours into the game, I am still having a blast. This game has the possibility to be great with an already established game-style and art design. I've almost gotten all available characters to level 6, the map feels fun to play every time I step into a game. Monsters all feel like they have a unique way of interacting with player and the telegraphs feel like they are just enough to get out of a situation while still punishing poor placement and bad cool-down management. The 4 player Co-op can feels really good with little to no latency issues with other players for me. The diversity of Heroes is probably the thing that stands out the most for me so far, every character feels like they play a little bit differently than the next and the kits built into each one are also diverse and can play differently each game. That being said I think that going forward with content and updates to Heroes abilities I'll continue to have a ton of fun with my friends and I hope others stop and take a look at this diamond in the rough.My only con would be the lack of story narrative in the game, granted this is a unfinished game and I don't begin to know where the dev's plan to take things in the future but! As it stand right now, there is not much lore and that is something I'd like to see. I love the twist on each storybook character and I'd like to know more about them. :) Not a big con though, the game is great.Edit: 600+ Hours later and I'm still coming back for more. The difficulty change was well needed and I love the direction they are taking with the design and heroes they've decided to go with! Wukong, The Monkey King. is a lot of fun and playing this game while it evolves is something I am proud to be a part of! I'll be continuing to follow this game and watch it grow into something special to me!

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun already, and looks very promising for the future (i know we're at the end of the early access, but hopefully the development doesn't stop). The gameplay of each character feels distinctive and incredible, like an action RPG but with actual thought, where you have actual cooldowns and fluid, impactful skills that you must combo well, not just spam AOEs.Differently to some other reviewers, I don't mind the clock at all, makes the decisions matter - since every fight takes time, you must pick your fights and play them efficiently. It's a skill you learn as you play.As some cons, right now load times are eternal, both in solo and multi. I think some characters are quite unbalanced for solo play, being less mobile and/or inflicting less damage than others. Also, the bosses did already get repetitive and they're... uninteresting compared to the bosses from CotDG - honestly they could directly import some of those reskinned as Nightmares and make the boss random and it would bean improvement. Also, hopefully we get some more heroes. Multiplayer is very fun but it's pretty important to voice chat, and right now you can do it only on the discord server - actually you can't even write to others atm, which feels quite strange. Also it lags a bit at times.Still, great game, and very recommended even at this stage.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun! What else do I need to s-*reads the negative reviews*...if y'all would just read, a lot of those issues would be resolved... 1) There's a "defense" skill and a dodge for damage mitigation. Learn to use those and the balance will feel better. Of course it's balanced for party play, but you *can* solo once you've learned the character.2) You unlock characters by beating the first boss. You should be happy they let you try/test those characters for free before the game came out, not complaining that you actually have to work to get them now...3) "DEMO content" ...okay, so I might actually agree with this one. There is only the one level available atm, but here's a reason it's <$20 and released as Early Access. Beating the boss unlocks a character (progression and replayability) and they're promising Chapter 2 before EA is done, so... we'll see how long that takes.The debate on whether this is a rogue-lite or rogue-like will be strong. There are perma-death and random spawns, but also permanent progression in the form of better perks after dying (unique to each character). Doesn't really matter, tho. Think of it as an arcade or "party" game that still rewards you for the time you put in!

_childDocuments_.review: Truly great roguelite. Gameplay loop is super satisfying. I think my biggest takeaway currently is that every character is incredibly fun to play, and none stand out as over/under powered. This makes every run a ton a fun moment to moment as you kill enemies and work on completing quests in the open world. The objectives do get a little repetitive but it doesn't really impact my enjoyment of the game, and this is expected considering that there is only one available area currently. I also think that the day/night cycle and the timer are very interesting expansions on the roguelite formula - the day/night cycle affects gameplay in interesting ways, sometimes subtle and sometimes overt, and the timer keeps you on your toes but is not suffocating. It may seem like a lot at first, but after a few runs you'll have picked up on the flow and things will click into place.I also primarily play solo, but co-op, from my experience, works well and is a ton of fun. Characters compliment one another well, and resources are shared to avoid any possible annoyances. The exception is currency, which is shared when it comes to earning it, but you each get your own stash to spend, which is really great.The challenge is also very fun. There are 10 difficulty levels, and you unlock a new one every time you beat the game on the currently highest-unlocked difficulty.Highly recommend, but yes, it is in early access and you would be better to hold out if you aren't fully on board and want more content. I've put in around 25 hours with the current content and have no desire to stop playing, and can't wait for future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: For the price of a decent meal, you can enjoy many hours of excellent combat with 6 complete characters (in 30-minute run increments). Nothing about it feels unfinished.I would consider the replay value very-high, due to not only the meta-progression, but for the amount of fun I'm having combining unlockable skills and magic items.I really commend these devs for sticking to their vision. This game already blows me away. Looking forward to seeing more!*For those complaining about lack of content, I ask that you name a single early access game with as much polish on launch-day. The characters even have VOICE LINES. Consider the countless "full games" that have launched with much less care and quality.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial impressions are really positive:- Combat feels nice and chunky - might feel a little slow at first, but I think that's a deliberate decision to make it more methodical and less 'button-mashey'.
