_childDocuments_.review: For those reviews that you read from those who have played for 1 hour before getting a refund citing it's too unbalanced to play solo - ignore them. I've played about 3 1/2 hours co-op and 3 1/2 hours solo, both fun and both capable of achieving what you need to. Yes it's early access but here is a game that already feels very polished and for a roguelike co-op to play smoothly in EA is something to celebrate in and of itself. Yes, it's one map, and does it feel difficult at the start? Of course - it's a roguelike. Most people don't get their first Hades escape until 20+ runs, and yet I achieved back to back wins here solo, after completing relevant quests to help level me up. It's nowhere near as unbalanced as people will have you believe. The more you play, the more the game rewards you - same as Gungeon, Hades, Curse of the dead gods et al. Persistence in these games is key - you get rewarded for it and whilst the co-op is a big selling point I've also had a lot of fun playing solo (interesting to note I've yet to beat the boss on co-op so as far as unbalanced goes.... no.) So please don't let some 1 hour refund review put you off. This game is brimming with potential and already plays well. It's a fantastic foundation the devs have set themselves up on and I'm excited to see how they build on this. One final point - yes, I did get this game for free, but as far as entry price points go this is not a bad price at all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a thumbs up for the combat alone. They totally nailed it! It is as good if not better than Battlerite, which is a huge compliment. WASD movement, very snappy, buttery smooth animations, and weighty attacks. Plays well on controller too. Although it's a roguelite, it does feel like a full fledged ARPG for the 20 minute round. It's easy to discern what's happening because of the pacing and art style, so it's fun to watch as well. Coop is a blast. Heroes are really well designed and interesting. Scarlet is a rogue that turns into a tanky bruiser (werewolf) at night, and you really FEEL the power spike and playstyle change. The Piper is basically a ranger who can debuff and CC. Aladdin is a support-ey bruiser. Haven't tried the rest but there's an archetype for many playstyles. The hero design is really top notch.A lot of people are complaining about the timer. I disagree. 20 minutes is plenty of time to hit lvl 5 and power up. The map does need some additional work to vary up the quests, and fix up some balancing. Please add more quests! My main feedback is the minimap is terrible, and needs to be improved a lot. Rest of the UI is actually great. The stone collection quest is just ok, and we definitely need more quest variety.To me, the current EA is easily worth the admission price because I plan on mastering all of the heroes. I would say that's about 20-25 hours of entertainment. I understand the thumbs down because if you don't go deep on the heroes and just try to "beat it", there's less than 10 hours of content here. But given the dedication of these devs and the quality of their work for their previous title, I see this game being huge down the road. Fully recommended in its current form, with the caveat that it is early Early Access. So that needs to be well understood.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing about Ravenswatch, it REALLY seems like it has all the building blocks to make it a roguelike icon like Hades 2 or Risk of Rain 2, but the more you play it, the more you realize their core design ideology just isn't the same. Hades 2 and Risk of Rain 2 are designed around making encounters fun, making builds fun, and making long runs FUN especially by having you scale out of control, with difficulty as a secondary objective or in service of the game being fun, Ravenswatch is the opposite. By the end of a Ravenswatch run, you can technically 'be' overpowered, but it'll still take forever to fight certain enemies, and you'll never feel as if you've truly outscaled the enemies like you would looping in Risk of Rain or late into a Hades run.  In your first 5-10 hours with the game, you'll have a ton of fun, and I think the game is incredibly polished. But then, you'll start trying to unlock specific skins or start jumping up the difficulty ladder and you'll start to notice little things one by one: This is all to say that slowly and steadily you'll find that most of the enemies in this game aren't enjoyable to fight and don't feel rewarding to overcome, they just end up feeling tedious to deal with.  The game was built around the timer mechanic, but for the most part you're ignoring all the enemies in the open areas of the map and PRAYING they leash and go away without following you into the next objective, and especially in 1.0 they rarely do and will sometimes just spawn into an area out of nowhere after you've already cleared it. In a game designed around a timer, you can't make each encounter feel so painfully slow. You might have like 20 minutes per stage, but you'll realize that unless you really get lucky with items and upgrades, each objective is going to take anywhere from 2-4 minutes, giving you time to get like 5ish upgrades max per stage, not including buying from the Well or Dream Shard shop.Enemy leashing in particular in 1.0 has made it even harder to get a good amount of things done in any sort of real time constraint, as most enemies will follow you the distance of two objectives, and will sometimes even spawn in later on only to instantly leash but bug out your combat encounter icon regardless.There's not much to actually say about the boss fights, other than the fact that  in that there are 5 different attacks and attack types overlapping on each other at the same time. I could go another 5 paragraphs just describing the total fun oversight that is giving enemies attacks that can't be mitigated in anyway and just need to be avoided (visually seen by a yellow telegraph on the ground), but it wouldn't be worth the time. Giving most characters the ability to become intangible but not letting that intangibility avoid these yellow telegraphs is a gigantic oversight and leads to situations where you literally don't have enough time to escape the area of effect in time due to an attack animation and just have to accept death.ADDITIONALLY, Boss Health in Darkness 3 especially is absurd. If your build is great but not overpowered, you're going to be spending 10+ minutes fighting the bosses of the third stage (and even more time fighting the secret boss). And, with the bosses of stage 3 especially that just means you're gonna spend more time dealing with (what feels like 10+) constant attacks coming your way and overlapping with each other. Ravenswatch is a game I've followed for over a year now, and I've played a lot of it, and these are all complaints I've had since the beginning. The developers obviously care about the game and have added a lot of content into it, but I think on a core level they don't understand what makes the best roguelike games fun, especially so in games where runs take 60+ minutes. I can't recommend this game to anyone who is a roguelike fan and enjoys learning intricate mechanics, as the more you try to work with this game on its mechanics, the more frustrated you'll be about the mechanics not working with you. I know the roguelike community shares a lot of overlap with the soulslike community in terms of just assuming all of someone's issues with a game have to do with their skill level, but my bald ass has the Darkness skins with 7/9 characters, so you don't want this smoke, I promise.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so I want to kick this review off with one statement:It has more content than you probably think.Okay, maybe I'm lying a bit, but at the same time its a roguelike.  It's meant to be played like hundreds of times over.  Although it only has one boss, its variety of characters and difficulties makes it worth playing again.  My favorite characters are by far Aladdin and Scarlet, both playing as fast paced assassin type characters, sneaking in and out of combat.  Or perhaps you would like Snow Queen or Melusine, which are unique mage characters, with Mel having a controllable wisp that can do damage to enemies.  Beowulf is a heavy damage character, which has an unforgiving playstyle, making him a hard character to play.  And the Pied Piper, who does crazy single target damage, but struggles without the use of his powerful rats.I have played about ten hours, completed normal mode on all characters, and nightmare 1 on a couple.  The difficulties go up to Nightmare 9, allowing for ten difficulties on six characters at the least.  It could use more content, but right now I'm satisfied with it.  Anyways, Ravenswatch is an absolute masterpiece, and I haven't even tried co-op yet.  Being someone who has dumped over 500 hours into various roguelikes, I would recommend 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Thumb sideways. My impression after 10 hours, is that the game is just OK.I've played many roguelites/roguelikes and frankly, I'm questioning a lot of the design choices that are presented in Ravenswatch. Here is my short list:- A lot of enemies feel like damage sponges, especially early on when you're lacking in upgrades. Early game SHOULD be the point in the game where you can roll over most enemies that aren't of a special variety (bosses/elites). Instead, you get events that you will simply fail and not get rewarded if you don't meet the damage requirement. Every time I saw an enemy with the little armor symbol, I was cringing, because of how much of a chore they are to fight. I'm not saying early enemies shouldn't still feel threatening, but I shouldn't have to be hitting the same guy so many times that I'm falling asleep holding down my auto attack. Kills the pacing. - Speaking of pacing, trudging around the map at a snail's pace with enemies trailing me is awkward. They want you to go fast to pick up as many resources + upgrades, yet you also need to deal with the enemies that you encounter, because you can't interact with objects/upgrades if you're in combat. - Since enemies are often so spongy in nature, there are many times that I would fight a group but end up kiting into a fresh pack of monsters, thanks to the open nature of the map. - The game being the same 'open' map really adds nothing to the experience. There is a reason that games like Hades + Enter The Gungeon + Binding of Isaac offer small arenas with specific numbers of enemies. The only thing I could think of is that MAYBE they wanted players to feel like they're exploring to find upgrades... but the three chapter maps are always the same layout, with only the placement of things that are randomized. - Further building on the last point is that the maps don't offer a variety of interesting quests or special locations or rare events. Take act 1 for example. You always get one quest to help the swine guy gather materials, then defending his home. And that's about it. Where is the variety? Rare spawns? Cool unique quests that pop up from time to time?- While the game does offer some interesting talents to upgrade the abilities of your hero, a lot of these options are gated behind unlocks you can only get from grinding games on the same hero. This is even more of a problem when you realize that these unlocks are the only kind of meta-progression in the game. - A lot of items are very boring. Wow, +20% more damage to my auto attack. This one gives me more flat health. Oh but how about this one... it adds armor. None of these open up new ways to play my character or diversify how each run plays out. And I always feel like I have to take the damage options when presented because of how damage spongy enemies are and how punished you are for not killing things quickly and efficiently. - No invincibility frames on using dodge? Just... why?- Could we maybe get a reward for beating end of chapter bosses? You know, something besides a splash of xp? Like every other game in the genre?- Enemies that root you in place for lengthy amounts of time. News flash, players don't like being CCed in games. You might as well slap on an additional 100+ damage dealt as well, because that's how much you're going to take if you get rooted.Now, with all that out of the way, I will say that I think the playable characters are cool, and each offer their own unique playstyles. The combat and skills generally feel fun and snappy. But with all of the problems I listed, I struggle to think of why I would want to play this over other games in the same genre -- games that offer superior replayability and variance from run to run. It clearly tries to do its own thing to stand out, yet what it brings to the table often just leaves me scratching my head and wondering "Why?"I'll probably still dabble with the game to see if my opinion changes, but I don't expect the game to change much from now to it's 1.0 release in a few months time.edit: Played it more since the review, including the 1.0 release. All of my points still stand. If anything I've developed even more gripes.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: After having played Curse of the Dead Gods a lot, and having enjoyed the f**k out of it, I am so glad to see that the next game by Passtech Games is just as good -- and with the huge added benefit of being a co-op game. Ravenswatch is not even fully released yet, it's still in early access but I've already found myself dropping every other game I've been playing recently so I can binge this one.Just like Curse of the Dead Gods, the combat design in Ravenswatch is really good and it feels incredibly rewarding -- just as much as it is punishing when you don't do it right. That being said, it is definitely a difficult game more catered towards hardcore audiences. You WILL die. You WILL get frustrated. But it will only make you want to go for another run so you can get better.The art style and the overall theme is gorgeous and captivating. I can't believe I get to play as Aladdin in a dark fantasy setting -- how cool is that?! I also really enjoy the banter between characters in-game; I only wish there was more of it. It adds a lot of flavour to the game and it's possibly the most important vehicle for communicating its narrative in-game, which is why I'd like to have more of it in the future. I wanna know what happened between Aladdin and Melusine in that sparring contest they had! Did Melusine let him win? She did, didn't she?My personal favorite thing about this game, which incidentally was my favorite about Curse of the Dead Gods too, is the sound design. It's such an underrated aspect of game design. A game with good sound design immerses players so much more, it adds to the visceral feel that one gets when playing, it really makes one feel like they are part of the game's world. And Ravenswatch does exactly that. Everything, from Melusine's and Pied Piper's musical notes, Wukong's HOO-WAH-YAH and Snow Queen's freezy crunchy sounds, to the battle cries of the enemies and the sounds they produce when they die, it all adds up to create a very immersive soundscape of a fantasy battlefield.I am super stoked for the release of the game and future content updates!

Each of the 6 characters available feels completely different and fun in their own ways with upgrades you can unlock that transform their abilities in interesting ways, granting all-new effects or even changing the nature of the ability from melee to ranged. As of launch the content is fairly limited, with only 1 map, but the 6 characters are all fun to experiment with and there is a scaling difficulty option in which you can push the difficulty higher and higher to see how much you can handle.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the gameplay is solid and all characters feel unique. I didn’t play co-op yet, but intend to do so. I also want to complete higher difficulties, but I might give up on that as the game is not motivating me or helping me in doing so. But even without that I had lots of fun and recommend the game. Especially if you like to try out different characters and play styles.- Plenty of characters and play styles: Each characters play differently. It is generally fun to try them all out and figure out how to play them.- Smooth gameplay: I didn’t encounter major bugs and the controls are very responsive.- Progression of characters: All heroes start with all skills available and ranking them up only unlocks new choices to pick from when leveling up. It doesn’t feel like this makes the characters better and sometimes it is even bad, as the new choice wastes a choice slot with often a worse talent than the starting ones.- Weird Dash: Dash does not make the hero invulnerable like in most games, instead the player must use the “defense skill”. Which is just another button to press. It could be simply the dash button and give the heroes more abilities instead.- Combat Balancing: The enemies overall have high health and high damage output and often an insane range. This makes many battles feel like boss fights even they are trash mobs. This is a choice of the devs, but I prefer games where trash mobs are trash, like in Gauntlet.- Time Limit Overall: This is imho the worst mechanic in the game. It is clear what the point of it is, to limit the rewards the player can get before fighting the boss. There are games out there, which solved this mechanic in a much better way (see Hades). With the time limit the best strategy is to skip trash mobs and focus only on reward spots.- Time Limit Rewards: And because it is such a bad mechanic the game even uses it for quests and the reward spots. If the enemies are not defeated in the time limit, not only the reward is lost, but it wasted time, which could be spend for other rewards. The most interesting enemies cannot be fought, because they “cost” too much time to beat.- No Variety: Higher difficulties do add some mini-bosses and corrupted versions of regular mobs. But that doesn’t change much, as the bosses are ignored due to the time limit and the corrupted enemies feel like the regular version just with more health and damage. Bosses are the same on each run. Choosing a path and getting a different boss every now and then is what other games do to make the grinding more fun. This is completely not the case in this game.- Each hero rank up should add 30-60s of additional time until the boss must be fought. This would fix my biggest issues with the game: The time limit and the not meaningful ranking up of the characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Sitting at having played a little over 300 hours I genuinely believe this is a fantastic game and I often find myself coming back to it for a new run; however it is a pretty hard game until you come to truly understand the mechanics--then it's fairly easy.  All of the characters have unique and enjoyable playstyles with a strong degree of variety which is appropriate for a rouge-like and I find there to be plenty of replay ability. It's a solid 8 or 9 out of 10. The only things that bump the game out of being 10/10 is Multiplayer and the amount of Content.Starting off with multiplayer, the difficulty is spiked up per player (which is fine) but some people can't handle it so the instant anyone dies or does anything unfavorable the host might just leave and boom, you're back to searching for a new group. I believe the game's built in matchmaking is global so there are many times where you'll just dc because the host is in Timbuktu, literally. I recommend playing with friends or using the discord's matchmaking.Now if you're coming from a game like Risk of Rain like I am, you'll probably feel that Ravenswatch doesn't have much content. There's four main maps with a set number of objectives and specific enemies that spawn on each. After a while I came to understand that what Ravenswatch trades for enemy and map variety is a strong amount of build variety. Unless you're the type to always go for a specific build every run on only one character you'll quickly get bored, but if you open yourself to somewhat letting RNG takeover(responsibly) you'll find some funny builds that can (usually) be insanely strong. However with all that being said I still believe the game could use a little more variation to the maps; at least one alternative per section of a run. More talents, heroes, and enemies would be appreciated, all of which they are confirmed to be working on with a roadmap but at the pace of two heroes over the next year, it'll be slow.TL;DR: Great game but it can be very challenging (especially in multiplayer). Rouge-like features are slightly lacking and multiplayer sometimes suffers from connection issues but neither issue truly brings the game down too much if you truly enjoy the gameplay. I strongly recommend this game you like games that challenge you or require skill/game knowledge.

_childDocuments_.review: So, after 1.0 release and 400hours (most of those hours in EA) spent in the game, I think I can give a pretty honest review of Ravenswatch (in it's current state).Let start with the positive things about the game:- has a beautiful art / visual style and animations- has an awesome soundtrack- very nice voice acting & fun dialogues between heroes- gameplay is very good, superior to other rogue likes / lites I've played so farNow the negative things about the game:- biggest issue right now is the balancing of the game, especially in multiplayer. - enemies have gotten way too strong / tanky and their numbers have been increased to the   point, where players are easily overwhelmed and crushed, it's very frustrating- some magical items have been nerfed, others are still useless, only a few are really good   and considerable- even after 1.0 release, still only 3 completely identical stages / biomes with no variation at all   (a 4th stage or biome would have been fantastic)If you're going to play this game mainly in singleplayer mode, I would recommend it, you're going to have fun  and it's worth it.If you're going mainly for multiplayer (which is the heart of the game) I would not suggest getting the game right now, due to very bad balancing status (in every difficulty mode!).It's a pitty, because the game is so beautiful and has so much potential.I hope that PassTech team will look into this as quickly as possible and roll back some changes they've made for they've hurt the game badly.

_childDocuments_.review: Hades but co-op and you have a full moba-like set of cooldowns. The cooldowns keep the game from being a "spam the button you've invested into" simulator because it'll go on cooldown and you'll have to use your other abilities in the meantime. The items and talents give enough build diversity that you can play the same hero over and over without just doing the same thing every time. Combined, it makes sure there's variety both within runs and between them.The dash not providing I-frames takes some getting used to, but makes it so you don't just have a "Getting attacked? Press the invincible button" play pattern and instead have to learn the ranges of enemy attacks. The timer makes this a little difficult to play in co-op if you don't have a good chunk of time set aside (no way to go grab your pizza delivery mid-game without just losing because there isn't a way to pause the timer after starting a biome), though there is the option to turn it off if needed. The runs can be a little long since the timers make it about an hour for a full run, but when you're bad like me you'll only get that far when you're playing a build so broken that you want it to go that long anyway. I'd love to see a few new characters and talents added over time (give me a Merlin hero please) alongside more barks and integrated story content, but hopefully that'll come naturally as it approaches full release.

_childDocuments_.review: Immediate disclaimer for potential buyers: similar to Curse of the Dead Gods, this early early access is only the first stage - aka like 30 minutes of gameplay per run.As a proud EA supporter of Curse of the Dead Gods (someone who got terribly addicted and beat the game 3 times post release on various platforms) - my interest was immediately piqued when I discovered this game was also made by Passtech.  Unlike Dead Gods this game seems to resemble more of a Roguelike than a Roguelite but with the more open-worldish environment, more deliberate combat and a class system, I am really optimistic for this new title.  The aesthetic is familiar but fresh, awesome soundtrack and engaging combat (I've claimed in the past that Dead Gods had the best combat of any game, we'll see if this remains true once this game releases).Only 3 hours in but I haven't experienced any bugs, similar to my Dead Gods experience which makes me cautiously optimistic for another smooth release.  All-in-all, I'm hopeful I'll be able to be proud of supporting this game as well, only time will tell.  Thumbs up for now

I have only played this game for 2 hours, but I have successfully beaten the content that there is available 3 times on different characters on escalating difficulties. The amount of content currently available isn't much but it's to be expected as the game is still in early access. The gameplay is quite fun, being a mashup of several games that I enjoy. The exploration of Tribes of Midgard (on a smaller scale), the level progression from Heroes of the Storm, and combat that feels somewhat similar to Diablo 4, the game is very fun. The amount of content there is available is multiplied when considering the fact that each character plays very differently from what I've experienced so far. Each combat encounter has to be approached in a different manner based on your character and what build you're going to try. There's more variations to builds once you've unlock more upgrades and items which adds a lot to the fun of the game.Overall, I would absolutely recommend this game. The content is currently limited so it's understandable if you want to wait, but if you're looking for something that feels a bit like Diablo with a roguelite twist, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing.Curse of the Dead Gods was criminally under rated. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not here to talk about the lack of content or bugs due to it being in early access, I've come here to talk about one crucial thing. (Get rid of the damn timer that forces us into the chapter boss fight)So the gameplay is good, the couple characters i played felt good. The overall gameplay loop seems like it would be really fun, but the 1 thing that makes me not recommend the game and it's a completely biased reason so take this review with a grain of salt. It's simply the fact that you are on a timer and when that time is over (which is a really short timer) you have to fight the chapter boss, there's no way around this. so unless you play sweaty af you are probably going into the boss fight under leveled. you have a relatively large map to scour, albeit, with waypoints at your disposal. I guess my gripe with this mechanic is that you don't get anytime to actually enjoy playing the game, hell even every time you level up and try to make a choice with the ability power up you want the timer still ticks down? like why??? its idle time. I'm forced to play this game a speed that is not enjoyable at all. Please get rid of this timer, keep the day night cycle, just get rid of this timer... let us initiate the boss when were done with the map to proceed to the next chapter or however its going to work, let me enjoy this game at my speed....
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay of Bloodline Champions/Battlerite, mixed with the strategy of a MOBA but with co-op as an added bonus. You pick a hero and do your best to get as powerful as possible in the time given to you. The game is fairly casual but there is a decently high skill ceiling and there is almost always something you could have done better whether that's with game knowledge, reaction time, or just general strategy.As it is a roguelite it is not the kind of game that can be beaten just by playing it; it will require adaptation on the part of the player and, unfortunately, it seems some players are reluctant to do so. I hope the devs stick to their vision of the game.The game is fairly cheap and I don't regret my purchase in the slightest. The only thing the game needs is more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if the negative reviews are because people want to treat this casually like a Diablo ARPG, but this is one of the best coop games I've played in years. Strong recommend for 3-4 player groups, especially so with a consistent friend group. Single player is a weaker recommendation. Fun on occasion but not the draw.Here's what I like about it (some of which others deride):+ The timer forces players to make strategic decisions on how to best spend their. Route planning a key skill in the game that you improve at over time.+ Horizontal roguelite progression instead of vertical. Basically, instead of the typical +attack, +defense, etc, you just get access to more builds which WILL increase your overall power, but this again requires player skill to make use of. + You really feel when a build comes together, enemies can just melt...the downside of this is enemies have a longer time to kill if you don't, but I like that my choices feel impactful.+ While there aren't many biomes/bosses, I don't mind, largely because of how it impacts the strategic decision making. I know what I need to plan for at the start of each run, and given how challenging the game can be. Variety comes from builds/characters.+ Speaking of the characters, they all feel so different. It's hard to imagine players not finding at least 2-3 they really like to play.+ Runs take about an hour, which is a good length. Lets do about 3/session until we're overloaded on the focus required.+ Controls feel responsive, at least once you realize several moves root you+ I LOVE THE BANTER...I grew up playing CRPGs and loving companion banter and this has tons of great dialogue (though I seem to hear Pied Paper and Carmilla's flirting constantly).Honestly, the only negative I can think of is the learning curve. The game can feel good but not special for several runs before things click and you see how well put together it is. That said, if you don't like games that are challenging from the get go or want a pure single player experience, it might not be the best for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello everyone, given the amount of mixed reviews i would like to add something.THIS IS NOT A LOOT GAME. Please dont get this mixed up because i have seen a lot of negativ reviews saying "its not diablo". Welp- they dont try to be. What you are looking at is similar to a ROGUELITE BRAWLER. You play 1 of 6 very different and unique characters and find different upgrades to your skills each run. With completing a run and leveling your heroes (hero levels persists outside of each run) you get access to new unlockable skillupgrades. Roguelite 101.The characters itself are very fun and different in design. Playstiles very hugly if you play Beowulf (Barbarian) to a summoning naga enchantress which locks itself on spot while casting. The skillevels is very high as you get multiple skills to evade damage and every hit in the game can be dodged. In higher difficulties thats very important to get the map done.The artstyle is amazingly well done. From the general feel of the world, to character design and even menu work it is done with great attention to detail and craftmanship.A major point which i see people complaining about is that right now there is only 1 map and 1 boss. That is in part wrong. Yes there is only the first act (therefor only the first map) available. But there are multiple bosses on this first map, and 1 endboss which when u beat the map ends. Given that the roguelite nature of the game randomizes the map and the random events you can find on it each turn it does not (!) feel stale. Something not a single review mentioned is that there are 10 difficulties right now, which you have to unlock by beating the previews one. Enemies get upgraded and revival items reduced as they increase, so the game does not simply oneshot you with strongers mobs but rather tactically increases the difficulty by other factors. I believe this to be well thought out.Lastly the developers have posted their roadmap which you can always take a look at.To summarize:This is a true gem. Its crafted with great love and attention to detail. What is available right now is of great quality and performs almost bug free. The art direction and characters are lots of fun to look at and play. It takes a good amount of skill to get to the higher difficulties. I do in good heart advice you to give this a try- just dont jump into it thinking you play a looter game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, rightly priced. It has a pretty nice DA, runs smoothly with low end computers, and good class design.It's a roguelike, meaning your progression is tied to your understanding of the game as much as your unlocks. Pretty solid as it is, but I'm waiting full release to review endgame and unlocks.Some reviews blame  lack of i-frames when dashing. This is intended, however every character has a Defense skill, with a block / invulnerable mechanic. Some have i-frames in other skills as well, mainly melee heroes and Melusine. Managing these defensive cooldowns (roughly 5 sec base) to evade non telegraphed attacks is part of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT LET THE BAD REVIEWS DISSUADE YOU!This game oozes charm and polish and is super rewarding to get good at all the characters. People are complaining about the balancing in this game and while some characters feel a little under powered or some situations feel a little unfair there's a big-ass banner on the store page that says EARLY ACCESS. _childDocuments_.review: As of writing, I've yet to finish the nightmare, but I was able to reach the final boss and was so very close to beating it. But despite my loss, I was satisfied with my run, and am excited to try again and again until I beat it, and then beat it again with my friends.The game has been nothing but fun and exhilirating, each character is so unique in playstyle and in builds, combat is frankly, amazing, exploration decent enough given its roguelike nature, since its the same 3 maps but different placement of objectives. I also greatly appreciate the different ways in each each of the character's stories are told, like how Melusine's is in the form of a song. One thing to note in particular is multiplayer scaling - being in a 4 man party, sticking and coordinating together is extremely important, as going solo is borderline suicide, but even then its still a matter of individual skill, because you don't exactly need to work together and do teamwork synergy per se, you just need to build well and keep up with the game's scaling. So if a couple of people are lagging behind, you're gonna have a tough time trying to carry. Overall though, amazing game! Super highly recommended, especially with friends! And that's before even considering its more than fair price point!UPDATE: I've completed the memoirs of all characters in the game, and I'm glad to say, still an amazing game, and very fun. All points above are still valid. A very solid 8.5 or 9 out of 10, definitely recommend, especially with friends

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game at launch, it was rough, but I was extremely interested in what they were cooking up, and was following the updates throughout the months. after completing two runs, one solo, and one multiplayer, I can safely say that this game is a great addition to my rogue-like collection. Large variety in character builds. Challenging combat. Great sound design. Amazing music. and an actual interesting story (Lesbian vampire my beloved). Some people may not like the time restriction part of the game, but it adds a lot to the loop of the game. You have to actively choose between where you want to go. Do you do the side quest and get a legendary item in exchange for 5 minutes spent? Do you search around looking for money to buy upgrades and items? Do you look for grimoires and chests for guaranteed items and passives? Do you fight tumors to lower the HP of the area boss? etc. Lots of choices and you do this 3 times per run for each area. While the boss doesn't change, that doesn't matter as they require enough attention to not be boring to fight every time. Especially since you usually won't have the same build.Overall I recommend this game if you enjoy fast paced action rogue-like games. As there are lots of content to go for, and lots of variety between characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is mostly good, but too many things bother me and make the experience way less enjoyable that it could be. Important note, I'm a huge roguelike/lite fan in general and played this game exclusively solo, never gonna touch coop. Here is what bothers me :- Huge lack of variety (only 3 maps, not many enemies, only a few bosses that you always fight in the exact same order). Honestly all runs just feel the same, which is bad for a roguelite. The game clearly needs atleast 6-7 maps and 15 bosses.- Exploration and combat are painfully slow, you can barely visit half the map and many monsters are dmg sponges. After 18hours I tried a run with a trainer to double all dmg I dealt, and the game instantly felt WAY better, it tells a lot.- Progression sucks. All you get are new talents that are added to the pool for later runs, which just dilutes the good ones you may want, I just despise that system in general.- I got used to it, but honestly playing under a timer is never fun.On the bright side, the game is very aesthetically pleasing (love this style a lot) and the gameplay in itself is great. Each character has a unique skillset, they are all very different, even if some of them are probably more oriented toward coop. Just give it a shot if you're interested, but beware that it may not be a game you will play for dozens of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Game better now (patch 0.15.01)New character needs some learning to play effectively. Plenty of additions and fixes to existing problems (or at least acknowledged)Some of my personal gripes still persist As of patch 0.15.01 the game has been improved massively and seems to be going in the right direction, great improvements on horizon as well.The addition of Sun Wukong, who is at least at a glance seems higher skill ceiling character than other heroes due to how his defensive works, which in my opinion is nice change of pace. There are still same issues as stated below with the character (and seems more prevalent with him, especially while leveling)'In current state, you might have fun couple of the first runs you do. If you keep playing till Nightmare (current hardest difficulty, 0.15.01) you slowly start to realize that there are only few truly viable builds that you need to  roll into. If you don’t want to play on the higher difficulties, you’re more than free to do so, and the game on the lower difficulties is fine and you will (if you want to level up all characters) get around at least 20-30 hours of game play in it's current state (patch 0.15.01). Performance is alright, I haven't really run into any huge issues or have hiccups on my PC or Steam deck. In some points FPS might drop below optimal, but it is still playable.In the group that I've been playing with we haven't encountered any disconnects, but your mileage might wary.The premise and characters are truly captivating for me and makes me want to learn more of the setting. I truly love the twists and spins they’ve made with the fantasy novel characters and how they’re portrayed (and sometimes interact with each other). Visual style fits the theme (and I must give props to the artists).The characters all have unique and fun gameplay with most of them having build defining talents. Problems start to arise once you reach “meta progression” end (currently at the time of review level 6 of character and item unlocks from certain conditions). Once you gain access to all the talents you can acquire on character the RNG of getting a “good” talent increases exponentially (also getting decent items is RNG hell sometimes). Currently if you were to have really bad luck you can for example get following talents on Aladdin: Starter Aerial catch or Wish of omnipotence, Air Dash, Healing Blades, Major Enchantment, Dive (in short 2-3 support abilities and in this example 1 damage talent), sure you can kill the stage boss with this but that will take some time and feel awful all the way there. Additionally, to bad talents you can get useless items where I’m left with the feeling of wasted time and not enjoying playing the game.I’ve finished multiple runs with every hero on Nightmare 9* (solo and co-op) and I have to say most heroes feel great to play and can finish the run. Exception being Snow queen (even after the rework) she just doesn’t feel fun to play and needs something else than her current kit.*previously the hardest difficulty in the game, but pretty much equal of current Nightmare difficultyAddressing the timer, in my opinion the timer adds good amount of urgency in choosing your way of dealing the stage. Without the timer the game would feel even more monotone of checking every single crook and cranny to get all of the loot and levels making all encounters truly trivial without much effort ( of course standard RNG talent choices would affect this). If the devs were to remove it, please create different game mode for it.•	I know the idea of the game is to deal with the cards you’re dealt as best of your ability but allow picking any of the starting talents (or at the very least allow us pick from 3 of them), some of the characters currently have (in my opinion) only few truly viable starter talents. _childDocuments_.review: Throwing my two cents in here to counteract some of the (in my opinion) unfair negative reviews. It's early access, that's not up for debate. However, there are tons of unlocks, 6 characters, and a lot to try even in this first release of the game. This "24 minutes of content" complaint would be like saying Hades or Risk of Rain 2 have 30 minutes to 1 hour of content, because you can fight the final boss at that point and then quit the game win or lose, never to come back and do a different build or play another character. Sure, when the game is fully out and all 3 chapters are in, I imagine runs can span the 3 stages and be up to 72(?) minutes long, but even then there will be a major stress in the time constraint. Bottom line, I'm excited to keep playing this and watch it grow over time. If they can stick to the roadmap they laid out, at this time next year this is going to be at the very top of the list of good roguelikes. Even if there's a delay in the roadmap, I think once chapter 2 is out it'll already be getting to that point. The combat is just so smooth. I hope this game sees content and DLCs even after launch.

_childDocuments_.review: I played solo for a bit and got my first impressions.What feels good- The visuals and sounds are top-notch — shoutout to those artists for absolutely nailing it.- Combat and controls are smooth and responsive.- The dark atmosphere and the overall vibe are authentic and unique, which is one of the most sought-after features.What feels weird/bad- A ticking timer does not contribute significantly to the fun, as when it runs out, you get immediately teleported to the boss. Your time is always ticking no matter where or what you are doing, except if you are on the map menu. So there's really no room to safely consider your options. Picking up an upgrade? Pick it up quicker as you're on a timer. Considering items in the shop? C'mon, move already, time runs out.- I still have no clue what recovering the black raven statue does. Everything stays the same visually, and no explanation is given, or I missed something.- There's no point in breaking down surroundings - tables, barrels, boxes, etc. - as, sadly, there's not even a tiny loot from it.- I played almost exclusively with Snow Queen, and it felt rather punishing. She's slow and clunky, though she might wipe the entire packs of mobs if positioned well. Some mobs (like fat worms with ray attack) may get you no matter how skillful you move, rendering you unable to avoid the attack.- The boss fight is so frustrating. It's nowhere near the feeling of boss fights in Curse of the Dead Gods, where bosses present a solid challenge, but their patterns are well-readable, and they're totally beatable. Even with destroying a tumor and reducing the boss's HP by 20%, I couldn't get it close to being defeated. Sometimes, I had a feeling of getting killed w/o noticing what hit me. Regular tendrils hit hard; the central tendril one-shots you. Plus, you need to dodge bullets, lightning bolts, and ground attacks during the fight. It's not fun and feels too much for the first boss, especially with a hero like Snow Queen.- Adding some condition icons or other visual cues to enemies with chilled status would be great. Playing Snow Queen revolves around chilling and shattering enemies, which requires you to distinguish visually who's chilled to attack/shatter them effectively. And those tiny little snowing animation isn't enough, obviously.- Cooldowns for skills should be stated in the skill description.- From what I've seen, there are just a few upgrades, just differing in order. Even though there was only one character in Curse of the Dead Gods, the variety of weapons adds to replayability and the feeling of interesting, fresh runs. Here, it starts feeling samey pretty fast. This is crucial since that's what makes roguelikes like The Binding of Isaac a timeless classic — its variety of possible item/skills/set/trinket combos. You can play for 100 hours and then suddenly get surprised with something unexpected and exciting. And it goes on and on for every room you enter.- I tried the beta branch to see the next chapter and after defeating the boss and choosing to go next, the game has closed. So there's not much to see here for the given price.Hopefully, all the bad will be refined, and the game gets better.

_childDocuments_.review: I've bought the early access as a sign of confidence in the final product, but i'm just not having fun with it, at least as a solo gamer. To get it out of the way, I am not criticizing the lack of content, as I understand the concept of early access. But I will compare this game with other similar titles that just do it better by comparison and hope some of my feedback can be incorporate in some way down the road:1)	Play cycle feel super rushed, mainly because of the timer. There is too much exploring to do and the combat is too tactical in order to accomplish much at a reasonable pace. One of the selling points of the game is the aesthetic, but good luck taking a breather to admire anything around you or to tactically approach an encounter. I feel I am on a treadmill, I am forced to rush the exploration and most of the time I get killed for it. Proposed solution: at least for solo gaming, an option to remove the clock; keep the day/night cycle, but let less die-hard players to enjoy the game mechanics at their own pace.2)	There is no meta progression. I was hoping for something here that takes inspiration from Hades, Roboquest or Vampire Survivors, but there isn’t any. Outside of unlocking and increasing the pool of potential abilities for each character, there is 0 reward to benefit from in subsequent plays. Some players probably enjoy not having this, but consider this train of thought: if the meta progression is there, casual players can benefit from it and die-hard players can just ignore it if they want the current flavor of the game. There is no reason to advocate against having this option. Example rewards that can be provided as meta progression:•	Extra raven feathers•	Extra dashes•	Boosts to the primary stats (ATK, vitality, armor)•	Bonus shards at the start of the game•	Rerolls to abilities when leveling up•	More abilities provided to chose from when leveling up•	% speed boost (just to cover the map at a more decent rate)•	EtcI will keep my opinion as negative for now, as I believe I gave the game more than enough time for a fair shake, but I am worried that the things stated in the roadmap (Extra stages, characters and monsters) do not address at all any of the things that I dislike. EDIT: As there is now a no clock mode, changing review to a positive.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, it's polished, everything works and the gameplay is good. BUT, I can't say it's a good Roguelike / Roguelite. A good roguelike is about how varied the runs can be, and how replayable the game is. This game has a lot of characters, but not a lot of variety. You can play each character enough to unlock more of that character's upgrades to find during your runs, but eventually you just unlock all of those upgrades. SO, when you play, while the upgrade options you find are randomized, there is a VERY small pool of upgrades that you will be offered, and multiple upgrades with VERY clear synergies that you must pair together to do well. The point of all that is in this example: So I start a run playing Aladdin. This run will only be different from my last run depending if I pick to upgrade my E ability instead of my RMB ability. So there is NO feeling of "oh boy i wonder what this run will be like! Is this the run??". NONE. It is all, "what will I choose this run to be of my 3-4 build options, and will I find items that are good for that build or not. That right there, is bad roguelike design imo, compared to the best ones like Dead Cells and Risk of Rain 2. Even after 100s of hours in those two games, I still get that sense of excitement when starting a run and seeing different whacky builds come together during the run. This one is just, start out weak, get slightly stronger on a linear and very limited upgrade path, then find stat upgrades for the upgrades that you already found to make them even stronger. And I think the most talent levels you can have is 10, so you kinda just get 10 upgrades with some additional items on the side. Just imagine if the upgrades in Risk of Rain 2 were JUST improvements to the character abilities, like "Huntress arrows do 10% more damage after jumping" - it'd be f**ing lame.It sucks because the gameplay and polish is really freakin good, and does Diablo 4/V Rising type combat but even better. The characters are cool and learning them is fun, but the gameplay loop overall is very clearly not something with the insane replayability that roguelikes/lites depend on for success.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, I appreciate how Ravenswatch is basically an evolution of the first game from this studio. They managed to improve many aspects that felt a bit lackluster in Curse of the Dead Gods, such as enemy variation, combat mechanics, music and especially your character, as now you can choose from a wide variety of heroes to play with. From the few hours that I played Ravenswatch, which I think gave me a broad idea of what the game is about, I will point out the following:1. The map feels a little too big to explore, which comes with the downside that a lot of what you see while playing is barren, empty space. Now I know that you're not supposed to explore everything, and actually it's impossible to do this given the time constraint, but I would appreciate if they reduced the size of the map to about 2/3 of what it is now and make everything more condensed2. The heroes feel really good to play, each of them having unique skills that make the gameplay feel fresh each time you start a run. I haven't gotten the chance to play with each of them, but I do need to say that some are clearly more powerful than others.3. They need to tone down the HP of enemies. Most of what I fight is basically a bullet sponge (or in this case a magic spell sponge) and it just doesn't feel right to pump multiple abilities into one enemy before it goes down. I know you can do combos and you are encouraged to maximize your output damage, but they could have just as well reduced the enemies' HP and decrease the timer until the next boss so that fights don't feel like they drag on for so long. This is further accentuated in the second chapter where enemies start to become actually dangerous and you encounter more "elite" enemies. I need to mention that I played Ravenswatch solo, so I understand that it might be a better experience with more players involved, but I don't have anyone to play with and this game is marketed as being playable both co-op and solo.4. Now for the elephant in the room. The god forsaken DASH mechanic in this game. I don't know who thought it was a good idea to give you a single dash with a recharge of 4 seconds in a game in which you get swarmed by enemies and fight bosses you are more or less a glorified bullet hell with little room to maneouver. Even in CotDg your dash had multiple charges as I remember, so it still gave you  some room to breath. But here, dashing is like an afterthought. I can't tell you how many times I died just because I couldn't avoid incoming damage because my dash was recharging. And let's not forget that it DOES NOT give you invincibilty frames (just WHY?). It makes 0 sense. Now I get that a typical dash mechanic wouldn't work well here because it would trivialize most of the encounters, since enemies have clearly telegraphed attacks. But it doesn't need to be that way. They could just give it multiple charges or IE frames or something that can make it more viable, just take your pick and bam, problem solved. As I mentioned earlier, most of the enemies you fight have clear attacks, but there are some exceptions, like those annoying snakes that shoot lasers which are more or less mini-bosses. Try to dodge that when both are shooting from different angles and they are accompanied by other mobs as well. And the bosses are self explanatory. I always end up losing a couple of feathers simply because I can't pay attention to 5 different attacks at once, while my only method of dodging is to dash every once in a while or walk slowly.So that's that for now. Since it is still in early access, I am confident that they will add more content in the future and fix some of the issues I mentioned. I will recommend it as it is for people who are confident that they will enjoy this kind of experience, but keep in my mind that what awaits you is a tough experience which requires a lot of patience and learning from your mistakes if you wish to try this game out.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth playing if you're a fan of the genre. Coop is working really well, no hiccups there. Difficulty seems about right, the higher difficulty levels are - understandably - very punishing when you're new, but I think that's justified.Definitely looking forward to seeing more content. So far, the only negative, imo, is lack of content - which I hope we'll see remedied throughout the Early Access period.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: That's a 10/10 from meWhile the game has limited content, what is present in the game is extremely polished content, with very few glitches, incredible optimization, and highly satisfying gameplay which controls really well. it's hard to describe how much polish went into it without playing it.It's honestly the best choice to guarantee a incredible finished product, because the foundation for the rest of the game is so polished, and really shows that passtech really loves what they're doing and simply never disappointPlus you realistically have a good 20 hours of content available in its current state, which I am 100% sure will be more than tripled in the final release.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game.A lot.And I really want to like the harder difficulties. But as it is balanced right now, I can't. Nightmare difficulty is a slog, enemies aren't more difficult, they just have more hp and are in greater numbers, so that means that everything just takes longer and you're bound to make mistakes. I also often feel punished for using my ultimates, since most of those have an uncancellable wind up animation that more often than not ends with me dead because an elite begins with a one-shot attack (I'm looking at you, big trees).Also, I also concur with some other review that say "less xp = less fun".Please please please balance the latter difficulties, I really want to like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write a review, but I decided to do it for this game for two reasons:1) The majority of other reviews barely hit the 3 hour played mark. For reference, 2-3 hours is like a maximum of 5 runs in the game, if you manage to make it to the Nightmare - that is if you're not rushing it or die early. With 5 runs, you can hit like level 3 on one out of six characters, unlocking about a third of their new abilities and unlocking about a fifth of magical items - all of this is that of what is currently available.2) If you have some friends and don't know what to play, play this. I think the balance is just right, it is challenging if you don't get the perfect combination of skills and magical items, but that is how it should be. You are not supposed to one-hit every mob and survive every hit if you have a dumb build. Roguelikes are especially about this, looking at the opportunities and making the most out of what you have available. Most of the time, it's not going to be the strongest build, and it shouldn't. Devs, please keep this in mind and don't appeal 100% to the people who only play games on easy and can't make it if it gets a bit rough.So here is my opinion about the game - added to what I already mentioned above:- Graphics are nice, the art style, design, ability effects look great.- Gameplay is fun, especially if you are playing co-op - but be ready to hard carry if your mates suck. :)- Current highest difficulty is Nightmare 9 with peaks in difficulty at certain Nightmare levels.- Enemy diversity for one map is alright, it gets kind of boring if you are playing this single map a lot, but as more content gets added, it won't feel like that. Also, you gotta get used to enemy attack patterns, etc. if you wanna git gud anyways.- Replayability is more than okay, even with this one map and "only" six characters. The characters play very differently compared to each other, can't wait what the devs can come up with then it comes to new ones.- Ability upgrades and magical items diversity and map variability is great for an early access game - if you are putting in the effort. You have to understand that a lot of unlockables are behind difficulty levels and character progression (ranks outside of the map). So by the time you get to Nightmare 9 and Rank 5 with a character, you will have plenty of choices when it comes to building your character even on this one map, to level 5.Hands down one of the best surprises this year and a fresh new addition to the pool of co-op games. Can't wait for the updates and additional content. Do yourself a favor and play it. ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: What to say, I love this game ! I was a bit skeptical because of the comments saying it was impossible to play in solo because it was too hard (which is not the case, you just got to git gud, which I'm not). I played the first 30h on solo, it's a blast. The coop is incredibly smooth, enough people are on discord looking to play it's decently easy to find at least one other person, and the game just gets sooo much better in coop.The timer isn't a bother at all since you get too know the skills fast enough and it doesn't take that long to pick anyway. Whilst playing coop it would totally break the game if every time someone has to pick it would pause the game. It's very fast paced and this would kill the rythm. I wouldn't mind seeing a pause option for solo play however.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: After the update I do feel there's enough content to justify the price tag even if you never play it again after it's fully finished. Very solid co-op experience with interesting and varied builds for every character and quite a few that play off each other nicely. Definitely worth picking up and trying even for the solo player as well, but I do think co-op is just far more enjoyable. There's enough here now as well that I'm far more confident that development is going to continue in a very positive direction. If you're at all a fan of this style of game I'd definitely recommend picking it up.Leaving this up 'cause it feels weird to completely remove my original impression.Original thoughts -- In its current state I wouldn't bother picking it up unless you're a hardcore Roguelite fan, but what is here is very solid. I expect this to be a super easy recommend within 4-12 months after it has more than 1 area and 1 final boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly i dont get the game's popularity. It feels like a tech demo or a concept art, but the tech is not that fun and while the art looks great in form i dont think its up to par in essence.First of all, the idea is alright - a roguelite bite-sized diablo is what i would say it is. The randomly generated map with different POIs sounds cool and would really add to the replayability, if those werent so dull. Most of the POIs are just "go there, kill a bunch of enemies, one of your numbers goes up slightly" - i mostly dont care if its a fountain, a grimoire, a chest - its pretty much all the same. The only somewhat interesting points of interest are quests, but after you play through once, you have seen them all, and even those dont really go besides "go and kill a bunch of enemies on timer". Traveling/killing enemies between POIs was just a nuisance, so in the end it all felt like we took rooms from Hades, made them arguably less interesting and then added some meaningless slog between each room.Speaking of enemies: faceless damage sponges that sometimes lay down void zones, thats pretty much it, and while im aware that you could probably fit that to most games, i would say that this game's most interesting normal enemy is a crab that you have to turn over to deal any meaningful damage to - and that being your most interesting enemy says a lot. However, i could look past the faceless mooks, but the bosses are the same, just bigger (also, all red void zones and red effects on a red field, really?).While the playable characters are pretty cool and have some interesting ideas, the best case scenario for me was that one ability felt actually impactful and the rest were just kinda there - i think it has to do with even regular enemies being damage sponges. The upgrades, both from leveling up and from items, didnt feel meaningful either - oh alright, my aoe tickle is going to tickle for 20% more, wow! I did not really feel any major difference between a 'built up' character and a starting one. I didnt find any major exciting or gamechanging upgrades that i could make a real build around either.The combat itself felt pretty sluggish. Maybe, again, it has to do with too much hp even on regular enemies, or long animations without a lot of ability to animation cancel, or long cooldowns. Again, i want to point out that most abilities dont feel impactful. I've seen the other reviews comparing Ravenswatch to Battlerite - and in the latter, if i hit my spider egg bounce, or hunter trap or whatever (its been a while), i knew that it would definitely change the game. In this game, i hit my full rotation, whether thats building/spending CP, freezing and shattering, or whatever else; i deal 30 to 80% damage to the enemy and then im locked to basic attacks, and nothing really kinda happened. Overall, i would make combat 30 to 50% faster (maybe a turbo option like in other games), and i would definitely prefer more unique and less numerous enemies over the sheer number of faceless mooks now.I played a couple games in coop too - i dont really have much to say about it, its the base game but together. It doesnt have a lot of interaction between the players, but i didnt really have any problems playing coop - no lags or whatever.All in all, the idea is cool and the game looks great visually, its pretty polished and it could already be a full game that you play for an evening or two, maybe with your friends, and then forget about it. However, i wasnt excited or looking forward to anything in my time playing it. Curious to see how it shapes up.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: About 2 hours in and the game is completed (I took the time to test out characters). Although VERY limited with content as of now, the game still offers awesome gameplay mechanics as well as unique distinctive heroes, each with their own playstyle and difficulty. As of present, it is a thumbs up for me because beside the lack of content, I don't have any other negative thing I can say about the game, the graphics are amazing, the music is awesome, the gameplay is smooth, etc... However, I must say that for those of you doubting whether or not you want to buy this game, I would recommend you wait for a few more months when additional contents are added.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Seems great so far. combat feels really good and each character is unique. The graphic style is beautiful, and the dark fairy tale setting is great. It is very well polished. I haven't run in to any bugs yet and the game play is really smooth. Ignore all the brain dead people complaining about lack of content. They clearly state what you get in the description so to buy it and then complain about it makes zero sense. Between the 6 characters currently in the game you could still sink plenty of time into the game to make it worth the $18. The only bad thing i could say about it at the moment is it seems really difficult for solo-players and there is no matchmaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, with a very unique approach to the roguelike genre. The devs are really active with the community, and the changes they've made throughout the early access period have all been positive to the playing experience.Each character (there are 9 in total currently) plays in a very unique way. I've used them all but really enjoy Gepetto, who uses constructs in the form of puppets to deal his damage, and Melusine, who was a unique playstyle that is best in coop as it requires standing still to deal damage/shield allies.Playing with friends and finding different combinations is really fun.Highly recommend getting this game. If you liked Curse of the Dead Gods, Hades, or other games of that ilk, it's likely you may enjoy this one. The playstyle may take a while to get used to but give it some times and I think you'll really have a lot of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: have only played single player so far!Pro:- Great feeling to the game. Very polished for an early access game. In 25+ hrs, I have not encountered any bugs. Cool soundtrack, nice visuals.- Surprising amount of replayability. 6 characters all feel very different and even though it's only one map, playing through it again and again with different characters and growing difficulty (Ascension system) gives plenty of play fun even for just one mapCons:- This is an early access where the content still needs to come. Even though there is great replayability, a second map (announced for summer 23) would go a long way. More characters to unlock stuck with would also be nice.- Not much story, if any. There isn't an underlying story like with Hades for example. This is just a roguelike where you play the same map over and over again and the only progress is stuff you unlock.- Not really a tutorial, and very little guidance. There are mechanics you really need to know but the game doesn't really tell you this, for example what to do with dream shards (in starting area there is a vendor...).Verdict:Worth $20 for me, easily. You'll get 20+ hours of fun even in the current state. If the devs keep their promise and release more content, maybe even post release, this will be a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Game is genuinely just fun to play. The sounds and visuals are satisfying and impactful.The characters are quite unique and don't fit neatly into the archetypal system. Each character can be built differently. Most heals/shields in the game are group heals so you heal yourself and your friends, it allows you to focus on damage and mechanics while keeping the group up. Definitely coming back to this as it gets more content. There are 9 characters total dozens of items and talents that can be mixed to change how you play.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: (+) The game is really tightly designed, every character is unique with their own gimmick and different ways to build them with talents that actually give you new abilities on top of your existing ones with starter talents that determine the flavor of the run. The artstyle is very atmospheric with great character designs with their more grim takes of folkore characters. It takes a few runs but once you get it its really fun to become a monster blender on wheels as you blitz through the map.(-) The game is very much not finished, since its early access. It has a hard time keeping up with 4 player lobbies and theres plenty of bugs in coop specifically. It is also very short, only one map that youll get through in exactly 25 minutes.Most of its problems will be patched in the following weeks with more content added, but currently it lacks anything more substantial than character unlockables to keep players in, making the price tag a bit steep. Even with all the shortcomings I reccomend the game because Im still having a total blast figuring out character quirks and builds on one 25 minute map.It has that certain mix of risk of rain, hades and battlerite, so if you liked those keep Ravenswatch on your radar. By the time the next map patch drops it should mature into an amazing co-op roguelite.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

You have to get stronger by beating Cthulu a bunch of times, then you are ready to move up to Giga Cthulu. Giga Cthulu 2 is actually the little brother of Giga Cthulu. _childDocuments_.review: I think a lot of the dislike surrounding this game is justified: complaints of "samey" feeling runs with no variability in mob types, boss types, NPCs, and universal magical objects for characters. I seriously enjoy this game and would highly recommend it. The game play is very enjoyable and it is fun to try out different builds on each of the characters.
