_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Great feel, Seems like they really put the time into making the game feel good over the content available. Im going to be playing a lot in the future. I really think this is going to get amazing. I cant wait to see what they do with it. I have only played through about 4 times and it feels super nice. Graphically looks great and its freaking coop! The sense of urgency with the day/nights and trying to get everything done in order to kill the big bad feels great. People saying pacing is goofy I highly disagree, everything that you're doing you have to do with intent or you die. Not a lot of button mashing in here which feels like a breath of fresh air. There is only 1 map right now but it feels like there is a lot to do on it. You never really get to explore the whole thing on a run. Side quests and prioritizing are key. What do you want to do to get tougher and kill the big bad??? ITS SO COOL! Biggest surprise in a long long while. Didnt think it would hook me like it has. If you buy it for $20 schmeckals at this point is a little steep if you dont know what you're getting into. However if it helps the devs make a bigger/better game im here for it. Im guessing with how strong the foundation of the game is they will start blasting content out like a machine gun. THIS GAME IS FREAKING RAD AND I CANT WAIT TO PLAY MORE!
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me to Heroes of the storm. You currently have two maps (which have points of interest and time cooldown until boss spawn) and  7 heroes, all of them have different playstyle and as you level, you can chose between two random skill upgrades. This game is not arpg so you can't button mash. All your skills, enemy attacks and overall physics have weight so you need to know what are you doing in specific time. If you played last Passtech game "Curse of Dead Gods" then you know the drill. Gameplay loop goes - roam the map, kill the monsters and level up, take as much as you can point if interest (for example you can have a chest which give you items that have boost to your hero, part map reveal, reduce healt to boss fights etc) and when time is up - fight the map boss. It is ok solo, but it is more fun with friends.  Currently it have not much content but it still have enough to have hours of fun and that you can see that this game have bright future.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: It definitely needs more content, but the game is rock solid from a design stand point. The game looks great, performs well and is stable (have crashed once and DC'd once in 30+ games). Characters feel great and play completely different from each other. I wish the map was more procedural as far as layout, as only the events/enemies are randomized. Defintely has a Tribes of Midgard season 1 feel currently, with much more technical combat.You can't just face tank enemies, you must dodge and use your abilities to succeed. You will go down incredibly fast at higher difficulties with poor play/builds. Looking forward to more with updates!
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is from the developers of Curse of the Dead Gods, and it feels very similar.After playing for just a couple hours, I now remember the main issue I had with CotDG: enemies attack you all the time, and you have very few openings to deal damage. And it's even more prominent here. Coupled with how much HP the enemies have and ticking timer, the gameplay feels extremely unfun. Hades has so much better fight and progression dynamics, I'd rather stick to it.Moreover, the three heroes I played feel extremely similar. Light attack, heavy attack, aoe attack, defense ability and evade - like we haven't seen that in a million other ARPGs and roguelites. Oh, and an ultimate ability that recharges so long and makes so little impact that it's almost non-existent. Again, compared to what Hades has, this game is very basic and unimaginative. So I guess the only reason to play this is if you don't like Hades or played it too much and look for another roguelite with a similar combat flow. But keep in mind: while it may look similar, the dynamic is very different.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly writing this review because people are dogpiling the negatives for absurd reasons. Virtually every single negative review I've seen has said one of the following:1 - I mean, yes. It's early access. There are plenty of things one could pick apart early access formats for but "the game isn't done yet" is a baffling complaint.2 - I'm not sure what these people expected when walking into what is clearly advertised as a roguelike/lite. In all fairness, I don't see anything mentioning the time limit on the store page but even still, this genre is all about restarting and playing over and over. The unique premise is what drew me to the game to begin with. I'm thrilled it's doing something new rather than just being Diablo again.3 - I beat it solo on the fourth attempt. I realize not everyone is at the same skill level but, again, roguelikes/lites are known for their high level of challenge. I enjoy the difficulty and most others that come to the roguelite subgenre do too. I get bored if they're too easy.The game is fun. The concept of dropping into a Diablo/Hades-esque game and having to scramble to gain power before the final challenge (à la Kirby Air Ride's City Trial mode) instantly caught my attention and sounded like a really cool idea. It's a promising premise and I love that it's bringing something new to the table so I don't see the point in getting mad that it isn't a traditional Diablo clone. There are plenty of other apples in the world, let me have my damn orange.Yes, there's only one level right now. What IS there feels very polished and there's 6 characters to play, on top of the inherent replayability that multiplayer brings. Do I wish there was more? Sure, but the game isn't done yet. I have high hopes for this game and it will live or die by its replayability factor. I wouldn't mind seeing alternate options for movesets the way Risk of Rain 2 does it, where you can swap them individually. The current characters are fairly simplistic, often revolving around a single standout mechanic (Scarlet builds and spends Combo, the Pied Piper passively gains rats and can cash them all out, etc). The trickle of level-ups and items keeps it fresh enough to last through the 30-minute run. Some modifiers change the way your abilities work and are arguably the most fun to get, but they do feel like they come slowly (from a solo viewpoint, at least). The biggest draw to replaying over and over in the current state is swapping between the different characters and playing with friends.I think the devs have a really great concept on their hands and it's already proven to be fun. At this point it just needs more of everything. More levels, characters, enemies, world events, items, etc. Depending on how long they plan to support the game, it seems like they have a nice setup to where they can just add a new boss, level, or character here and there to prolong the future of the game, should they choose to do so. The foundation is solid and successful. Now just jam pack it with more "stuff" all over the place.TL;DR - Despite only one level, the game concept is very fun and what's here is already nicely polished. The vast majority of people giving negative reviews are either saying "the game isn't done yet" or "I wish it was just like Diablo/Hades instead of being something unique" and it bothers me. If you don't like the fact that the game is lacking content in its unfinished state, just wait to buy it instead of review-bombing a good thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by the negative reviews, the game is well worth the price. Cool art, gameplay and content with more to come. They chose to give all the content in an honest way and not gated by grind like some other rogue-lite devs. Please encourage this behaviour and enjoy a soon to be masterpiece.Crisp controls, cool builds to experiment with and 6 very different characters. Ramping difficulty level and good replayability. Good simple multiplayer with minor bugs as expected of an early access.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: so far i have finished succesfully two runs (Scarlett and Snow Queen), and i have played with all the characters.  My opinion as follows:I feel like when iam buying an early access is knowing that it might not have enough content, and iam ok with it, because i am actually buying to get to play something that i want to support early so it gets better and better.  This game's potential? absolutely amazing, is very polished in my opinion,  it just lacks content, which i knew when i decided to buy.  The only thing bad that i could say is on the road map, which it says that we get the new map in the Summer, so yeah kind of a long wait.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Right of the bat i think Ravenswatch is a fun game in its early access release state, though i think the asking price is a bit high given what it has to offer. Personally i would price it around 10-15 euro. Personally i rarely purchase early access games but this game has a lot of potential, which made me buy it to support the devs and follow the development.The heroes are unique and the combat is challenging providing a fun gameplay experience. The artstyle is awesome with nice animations and the UI has a creative design. The map is quite big and a run takes 24 min before you fight the boss, leaving little time to explore the map. A side note: People calling this a demo, expects too much from a demo. If this was a demo you would only have 1 playable character, fewer enemies, smaller map and less objectives/ points of interest and likely a simple boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: "Wow! Where do I even begin? This game is an absolute masterpiece in every sense of the word. From the stunning visuals that transport you to breathtaking landscapes to the intricately crafted gameplay that keeps you hooked for hours on end, every aspect of this game is pure brilliance. The attention to detail is unparalleled, and the passion poured into every pixel is palpable.But it's not just the technical aspects that shine; it's the heart and soul of the game that truly sets it apart. And the soundtrack? Oh my goodness, it's like music straight from somewherelse..Perfectly complementing every moment of gameplay.But perhaps what's most remarkable is the way this game makes you feel. It's not just entertainment; it's an experience. Whether you're engaging in epic battles, or simply running around, there's a sense of wonder and joy that permeates every moment.In short, this game is a triumph for an early access game. It's the kind of experience that reminds you why you fell in love with gaming in the first place, and leaves you eagerly awaiting whatever the developers have in store next. JUST Bravo Peeps!"10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and original take as a roguelike, if development continues well I can see this becoming a staple of the genre. Keep in mind that it is early access. I would say VERY early access. It's more than a demo, but definitely not a full game (yet).The gameplay is relatively similar to Hades, so If you like Hades you'll probably like the combat in this game. There are a lot of original ideas here, especially in the characters, which are all very unique and fun in their own ways.Word of warning, however: I would not say that this game is worth $20 currently. It definitely will be worth that and more when the game is done, but as it stands there is only 1 stage and the encounters seem to be the same on every run, just randomly placed differently on the map. The boss seems like a first stage boss and isn't very difficult, and it becomes less and less of a threat as you learn it's moveset more and more each time you fight it.Overall very well polished and original game, every aspect currently in the game is fantastic. As an early access title it will continue to get more and more content, so the lack of content will obviously be less and less of an issue. I love this kind of game, and will easily get $20 worth out of it, but if you aren't already a fan of this genre, probably steer clear for now (but you should wishlist it).
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game!I was already excited when I saw that the developers from Curse of the Dead Gods were releasing a new game, and I must say, I'm quite happy with what I've played so far! There's so much depth in every single character that I think I'll be hooked on it until the next update. Great job, Passtech!
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Solid foundation: a base for a gaming loop to add upon (with endless runs they confirmed to be working on) An extreamly well made multiplayer (which is hard to do and rare) Crisp combat, Six well rounded and thoughtfully designed characters to play instead of a pletora of decent ones, with more to come.Enough difficulty levels to match and challenge your skill level for quite some time already.Good Graphism, Audio and Music.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly fun, even in the early stage it's at. The recent Geppetto update has made the game much more fun and each play through more unique with additional ultimates and upgrades. Even in this early stage I consider this game a good choice for any fan of rogue likes or Diablo, but if you are undecided just wait until more content is released, Definitely a new favorite of mine!
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very, very fun. HOWEVER, it is unfinished at the time of this review! I'll try to remember to edit it when the full game comes out. That being said, there is still enough gameplay that it is worth the asking price as it is right now.PROS: The game is really, really fun. If you like top down action games, this is amazing. Multiplayer is smooth, and makes the game even more interesting, and singleplayer is still plenty fun already! DESPITE WHAT YOU SEE IN CONS, it still has a decent amount of all of the things it's not done with.CONS: There is no narrative conclusion yet, no Final set of Talents for each character, and no 3rd act. Also, it does not have all the characters it will release with. THE GAME IS WORTH IT RIGHT NOW, even though it is incomplete.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is incredible. Most of the negative reviews are because they want more content, which is backwards because the devs get less support if the game has bad reviews which = less funding for new content. It's insanely fun already with only 1 chapter and there's so much to come. Big recommend. Lots of fun with a friend (or 3!)

_childDocuments_.review: A very big disappointment for me.I will never buy a game as soon as it comes out again and instead wait for reviews.The game is shorter than a demo. It ends in 25 minutes. There is a countdown and ready or not you fight the boss in 25 minutes. If you loose you try again. If you win Game Over. If I hadn't left my computer on while eating it would have said less than an hour of gameplay instead of 2.2 hours for me.I thought I was buying something that plays like Diablo. If you have similar assumptions this game may not be for you either.On a personal note I find it to be very predatory to hide behind Diablo like short videos taken out of context.These mechanics are not at all appealing to me, even if there had been content. Long story short you play a map, unlock upgrades, fight the boss in 25 minutes, and then everything resets to zero. Even if you add new maps in the future this is not an appealing gameplay for me. Neither is it common within similar games. Normally you keep your upgrades, fight bigger bosses, get better weapons, see more biomes, etc. Here it is completely worthless to level up your skills or to get upgrades. Win or loose the game is over in 25 minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: To me, this game is a perfect example of Early Access done well. It's already a lot of fun, the gameplay loop is tight and well-developed, and all of the characters currently available feel really good to play.It just needs more of what it already has: more levels, more enemies, maybe even more characters. I'd also love some cutscenes, because the world seems amazingly fun in a League of Extraordinary Gentlemen-gone-Lovecraft way.FWIW, I bought Hades very early in EA on that other storefront, and this feels very similair to the state that was in at the time: great fun, but lacking much content and replayability.If you want a fully fleshed out game with lots of content, look elsewhere for now. Come back in a few months or a year and buy it then.But I'm happy to play this a bit, move on to other games, and dip back in after the devs add more content (and to suport the devs in the meantime).I've been playing on the Steam Deck, which works great as long as you switch to Proton Experimental (just trying to launch without that change was goving me a DX12 error).For more thoughts on the gameplay itself: It feels kind of like the old Gauntlet games mixed up with more standard roguelites (Hades or the devs' own Curse of the Dead Gods). The different feel of each character means that each can play a very different role in a team composition. They're also all fun solo, though some play better solo than others currently. And the shared raven feathers (essentially lives) and level timer give that feeling of always being under-resourced and under the gun as you explore the level (hence, Gauntlet vibes). The different abilities each character has makes them control a lot like League of Legends characters (no bad thing, IMO).I would like to see the devs expose some of the settings as levers that the player can control, even just in an "easy setting" or a "custom" mode that doesn't award achievements. For example, though I think the timer should stay as the default for balance reasons, the ability to lengthen or remove it would go a long way toward providing folks a more accessible experience (or just treat it as a chillout game with friends), letting them take their time and possibly overlevel before facing the boss. Similarly, the option to start with more raven feathers would make it more accessible.Overall, though, really loving what the devs have so far and excited to see more content drop in the coming months.

_childDocuments_.review: HUGE potential in this game. A little light on content right now, but a heavy amount of polish in terms of game feel, the overall gameplay loop, and the variety between the six currently playable characters and how creatively they've been implemented.That being said, it might not be worth the price to some people based on the current amount of content, and that's totally fair. I'm personally a huge fan of everything this game has going for it, even in it's current state, and the direction it's headed in, so I think it's well worth the price of admission.Also, don't trust the people bashing the solo experience. I've played mostly solo and it's all very much doable, even the sidequests a lot of people are complaining about. It can all use some balance changes, of course, but that's the whole point of this early access period, and game balance is one of those things that takes a lot of time and feedback to get right.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is lacking content it is still the best purchase I've made in YEARS, especially an early access game purchase. The road map shows promise and the development team is very active within the community. All good signs and shows a lot of the good I see will come with time. The graphics are smooth and fit well with the combat style, reminding me of a multiplayer Hades style cross Diablo game. Currently only has one map, but the randomized events, layout and enemy spawns keep it feeling fresh and fun. The controls are responsive and smooth, never feels like I'm not doing what I want it to do when I want it to. For an early access game it's well worth the price tag. I'd even go so far to say it's being sold undervalue. The game has a very fun and engaging replay to it. Especially fun in groups with friends. Highly recommend.Edit: Okay, one nitpick I can add. While I was upgrading my skills after leveling I was about to be hit by an ability and instinctively pressed spacebar to dodge. Which accepted whatever upgrade I was currently mousing over. I don't see a way to unbind spacebar being an accept key for things like this, but it's a minor annoyance I can attempt to avoid in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was middle ground somewhere but I'm giving this game a thumbs up for its quality. Great casting, fluid animations, fleshed out synergies, crunchy combat mechanics, and a beautiful set piece.It's just too short! My buddy and I played the game after the coop fix and we finally beat the chapter two boss. We wanted to explore the map. do the other events on the map but is time gated. Gamer brain just wants to see what's beyond that fog of war but with the time limit set for speedrunning, it's mostly divide and conquer. It feels like Dead Cells Malaise system at tier 5 difficulty where the game expects you to finish a biome as fast as possible before it corrupts you, but for Ravenswatch it's the time. If you're not a fan of countdown time based games this is not for you.An extra game mode where there is no time limit for the more casual players would be nice, or an endless run with more bosses. Waiting for the full release!

_childDocuments_.review: with good support this game will probably be a lot of fun eventually. but right now it's too short for the price or any price really, once you start charging for the game it needs to be longer than what you expect from a free demo. according to the road map the second map isn't coming until the second major update which is an issue, the devs really need to extend the length of runs as soon as possible even if it's under baked, hell you could just re-roll the first map after killing the boss and continue run to it's intended length without having to design anymore areas. it's probably the length of the run that's the problem rather than the amount of content, in most roguelites it's not really until later in the run you feel your build coming together. my main other gripe is the long dash cooldown, your going to take damage when there's lots of enemies on screen, dash just lets you choose which enemy gets to hit you. too compensate for this the game is very generous with healing tools, enemies drop healing orbs and some upgrades have healing on them, but this makes the game play much like you expect from an arpg which i guess isn't a bad thing, maybe it's just personal taste but i'd rather have a very generous spam-able dodge than lots of healing to compensate for inadequate evasiveness.

_childDocuments_.review: Ravenwatch review :Goods : - Great art direction- Voice actor and music choice is great- Smooth gameplay and synergy with perk along with 6 unique characters ( for now ) - Combat feel great and meaningful for each encounters , event or special places on the map - The game really challenge even with Solo and Co-op- Its a easy to learn , hard to master kind of game- Many difficulties to play ( each difficult will add up 1 more buff perks for monster in  the  run , max to 9 ) Cons :- Minor bugs so far ( mostly with cannot damage Wraith and ghosts mobs )- Some character have pretty low on base damage scaling ( Aladin mostly feel less impactful for base damage but his kit is great if lucky )- Pricing still some what expensive a bit ( due to country pricing change ) Recommend : - is good to pick it up right away with friends but in case you want to have more experience to play then i would suggest wait til the game update chapter 2 for longer play time on each run ( current run would only cost you 30 mins each run at any difficulty ). _childDocuments_.review: Playing this after Curse of the Dead Gods feels like a major downgrade in every aspect. While CotDG revolves around skillful gameplay, precise timings and positioning, this game just throws tons of damaging projectiles at you while only giving you ONE dash every few seconds and an extremely weak defensive ability. Due to this, gameplay very often turns into a boring mess where you just run around a group of enemies, and only engage when your strongest AOE skill is off cooldown. The majority of upgrades and talents are boring and uninspired, they surely increase your damage output, but sadly do not change your gameplay in any meaningful way. You still use the same abilities in the same order, they do not interact with each other and don't empower each other. Map exploration feels fine at best, points of interest are located haphazardly and without any logic. Overall, this game is a pretty miserable experience that just disrespects the legacy of CotDG and falls short in every gameplay aspect. Don't play this.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. Even after winning runs I feel more frustrated than accomplished. That is compounded by the timer, increasing the frustration over lost time.I find myself running past as much as possible to only get to points of interest. The best way to play the game is to engage with it as little as needed.

_childDocuments_.review: i'll try to give a rough overview of the game from the time ive put in so far..Gameplay- The general idea of the game is a roguelike but with the idea that your on one static map and level up your character you choose like a very short term RPG experience gaining levels and skills to fight the boss at the end. Through the map you'll have monsters and quests and little events you can do until time runs out and you have to fight the end boss the complete the stage. Currently theres only one stage for early access and from my experience it feels very short. I'm sure the general idea is not for games to last long periods of time and hence the timer but it does feel like given the way the game is designed..if it was longer and more fleshed out per map ( as more get added down the road ); you'd have a pretty neat experience making your run(s) feel engaging as you put time into it.*Note*The game is able to be played either solo or with other players. Currently its limited to friends only and not thru a match making system but is able to be played by yourself and still have a enjoyable experience. I will say the way the game is designed..it does feel more designed for CO-OP in mind to get the most out of the experience and how some of the characters skills have effects that affect allies; so is something to keep in mind while playing. Personally i've just been playing solo and seems fun enough but you often dont have enough time in the game to ever go through the whole map so you have to cherry pick what you do per run in the way its currently designed..which is where my opinion of the game feeling short comes from.Music/Sounds- Nothing to much to say here. The music is pretty casual really and the SFX sound pretty good.Characters- Overall they feel ok and each have their own theme. Currently you got 6 i believe to choose from? At first play-thru i admit some did feel a bit clunky but was more from the lack of playtime and the more i tried some of them the more i could see there was some depth to be had with the characters and how their skills compliment them. Currently though there isn't too many skills to choose from and the leveling is VERY limited so your really just looking at making a small little build to get you through the map to get a feel for the character you pick. Basically for anyone that hasnt played the game; essentially you have a set of starter skills you pick from ( you get 2 random choices to start and per level up; currently isnt a way to re-roll or affect the likely hood of one skill showing up more than another.. ). You level to 5; at what time you get a ultimate skill and your character is maxed out. You can continue to kill mobs on the map but it wont offer anything level wise or growth wise outside of doing any events that you have time for on the map to scale your character more.For anyone that picks up the game i would say be patient and give the characters a few runs to get the jist for how they play before getting frustrated as some just take some time to get the hang of.*Overall impressions*In general i would say i like the game and do look forward to where it ends up going from the small sample size available to start from. My hope is personally is they add more systems to the game beyond just the leveling system and have more depth to how to upgrade your character. I do think as more content comes out and the level cap goes up with new maps the game will feel alot different though. I do still feel more time on the map to really double down on the RPG elements to go along with the roguelike elements their going for as well would be amazing. Add more quests or little events to do or see and make exploring feel fun and engaging, over it feeling like you have to speedrun the content since your on a limited timer. Personal feeling would be maybe make the end boss a adventure to get too that is paced on how much content you do on the map to say unlock the fight or go to it etc..Otherwise i think the game has alot of potential with the general design they have going for it but only time will tell if it adds much to it to feel immersive and expand upon what they got now or if it sorta falls flat.Regardless, i'd say give the game a shot to anyone that this may appeal too when you see it; just bare in mind it isnt alot of content right now so be aware of that if the price point seems a bit hefty to you at the moment until more content comes out to test.

_childDocuments_.review: Current state is pretty bad. I feel I can boil it down to 3 things Lack of content- This is to be expected, its early access The timer- This mechanic feels completely anti-fun. If you die a few times in a grimoire event or a tumor kill you basically have to start all over again. The game does not respect your time by forcing you to grab as much as you can but then rewards you with little to show for it. I have learned to ignore certain events because they just aren't ever worth it, my time is too precious and even with a build that hits hard I do not feel like the pithy reward I get is worth losing a raven feather. The rules- The games gives you several abilities and each one have rules along side it. some abilities are for stunning an enemy when you cannot move out of its way, but the game presents several choreographed attacks that all seem to indicate that the enemy can be stunned out of them, but some cannot. This is frustrating to me as a player because I think " nice I have an emergency button when I am overwhelmed to get me out of tight situations' nope because it will only stun some enemies not all. There are other issues like unlimited spawning of adds that I think is just a stupid designed choice, and hopefully it will be fixed. Right now every time I pick up this game it does something to frustrate me and I am not going to stick with a game that does that.  I will check it out in a year and if something has changed I will give it another shot. I am disappointed because Curse of the Dead Gods nailed the combat/encounters/bosses that Ravenswatch is failing to pull off

_childDocuments_.review: things I think are great about the game:Combat System:- core combat system is designed very good with normal attack into charged attack and one offensive and one defensive slot with seperate slot for ultimate, just using ultimate feels good and I'm glad it's not locked behind some slot managment bsEnemies:- enemies at the start are too easy to kill with just one type of attack thats easly avoidable, only after first chapter they matched requirements of me using my brain and combat system to the fullest Bosses:- first boss is great starter to teach player how to navigate around stronger enemies while being attacked by other "weaker" foes, - second boss is more focused around that bullet-hell playstyle where player need to dodge projectiles while watching boss melee attacks to not get squashed- I like more second boss bcs of bullhell style but both bosses are very well designed except some players might think they are too shallow with briefly 2-3 attacks on first boss and second had around 4-5 but even with that much they still can be quite challengingCharacter progression: - main source of exp and abilities are objectives thrown around the map, you complete them by killing some enemies in specific areas and thats all there is - there are side quest that are completely diff from smaller objectives on maps they can varry from collecting resources to build house to defeating whole siege with boss- you collect exp and "coins" to upgrade those abilities in main hub on map and I like that you can upgrade which ability you want to be better rather than putting that under RNG bracket - overall small encounters coupled with one side-quest for every chapter is great way of creating progression for the game - only thing that I think could be improved is that its pointless to kill enemies that are not in these objectives zones bcs they only give exp nothing more and objectives gives you just more rewards Map objectives:- most fun objectives must be these where you fight a bunch of waves of enemies or with one strong boss/elite mob - very good mechanic is one type objective where you fight few waves of enemies where in the end reward is that main boss of chapter has less HP when fought, its very unique idea and encourages people to explore more of the map to get that easier fight with boss but doesn't punish more hardcore players bcs only reward is less boss hp not coins/exp Overall opinion after only 2 hours of gameplay:- in the state that the game is I didn't think it would be that much fun with its Super designed core combat system that just feels smooth like butter then you attack enemies,progression around the map is like sprinkles on cupcake for this combat system, only thing that I didn't like very much is how easy its to kill bosses even without that less % from objective they are just too easy only obstacle for me was getting ganked by 10 and more enemies where around that number you cant do anythingI recommend game for everyone that likes souls-like games and especialy HADES bcs I think it was BIG inspiration for this game <3

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the deal, right now the game only has the first zone in it, which will only take about 20-25 minutes to complete during a run. The meta progression is a bit low, so its more of a roguelike than a rougelite. There is a lot of stuff to unlock, but they're possible upgrades to find during a run, and not just adding raw power to your character.  (Also as a note each time you clear a difficulty it slowly builds up more modifiers, similar to how the crucibles slowly stack up in monster train for those who have played that.That said, I'm perfectly happy with my purchase as the game is fun, it uses those awesome WASD isometric controls you see in games battlerite, the characters feel good to play, and I know this dev does a solid job with early access as seen with their previous game, so while the amount of content is low right now, I'm happy with whats there and I know that this dev updates at a reasonable pace, so even if I'm probably only going to get 10-20 hours out of it right now I know I'm going to sink plenty of time into it in the future.

The fact that it's CO-OP  enhances the experience tremendously.   I'm already loving this game, and I can't wait to see how much further the game will go.   Definitely my favorite purchase of the year. I'm looking forward to seeing how far this game will evolve.

_childDocuments_.review: I played on Early Access with my friends and we enjoyed the game! It's hard to come by any co-op roguelike with this beautiful art style and not so buggy (actually any co-op roguelike all seem quite elusive to us; why must they all be single player). I had desynchronization issue going on a few times but not sure if it was on their end or mine since the friends I played with all live in different parts of the world.Anyway, this game is great and it should gain more popularity. Playing solo is fun; and with friends, even more so! I would definitely recommend this to any roguelike lover. One minor dissatisfaction I find is that despite being in roguelike genre, this game isn't quite strong on the 'viability of randomness' (i.e. "let's try this with this and wow it works!") and 'build diversity' (i.e. "in how many styles can I play this character... hmmm not so many"), which are essentially the heart, I suppose, of any roguelike games. Surely, this affects replayability. I don't think I will reach 100 hours with this game. But well I might be wrong; this game is just in Early Access stage and I've invested but 20 hours or so so far. Still yeah, totally recommend it though.Final verdict: play it! It's fun!

_childDocuments_.review: I love the isometric action genre. The combat is so good, this game is doing great with this familiar set of tools that I've personally experienced in MOBAs, Battlerite and V Rising. The music in this game is this epic war drum tune, reminds me of Thronefall. I like the combat, and I really like that these characters are complex. There are some great ideas floating around competitive with the MOST complex league of legends characters. I like that the magic isn't based on D&D, it's based on folk tales. Aladdin, Gepetto, Red Riding Hood, etc. The enemies are unique, too!So my caveat is that the game is rogue-like or roguelite or whatever. You do sessions from start to failure or finishing 1, 2, 3 levels in a row. The layout changes a bit each time in a deep way. There's a bit of randomness in all kinds of items and talents etc. Feels a lot like Risk of Rain, maybe a bit less of that exponential power increase it's really more incremental most of the time. I don't like that? I feel like I'm failing, or that I've not done good enough. Every run there's some goal I wish I was powerful enough to reach. I'm refining my skill and strategy, but never rewarded. Eh. It's gotten repetitive so quickly. I am not building towards anything. So the gamemode is not my favorite, but the game itself shows that it was made by extremely talented creators.

_childDocuments_.review: Easy Recommend.(Pre storm island update)The art style is amazing, the game-play loop is perfect, and it runs better than most AAA games, while in early access. Each run has felt different and unique, and becomes even more so when you rank up your characters and add more upgrades to the pool of items to use. It is definitely worth supporting the developers now so they can keep making this game even better! As for content? I feel a lot of dislikes misrepresent the game by stating a lack of content, just because it has 1 level. There are 6 characters, each can be ranked up to 5 currently, which unlocks new and different abilities to use in future runs, a total of 14 upgrades per character. There are also 9!! difficulties to get through, requiring wins on the previous difficulties. Aside from general character upgrades, there are 44 collectable items you can gain during a run offering more unique experiences during your run to find play styles that suit you. For an EARLY ACCESS, this is a huge amount of content, and 14 hours in I'm still invested in playing.Minor downsides I've seen so far, players who have joined my game cannot do damage to certain enemies sometimes, and rarely one of us might not be able to collect an item. Aside from that, It feels like a complete game, even with 1 level.Its early access, so definitely read more reviews, and check the roadmap the devs have set up to conclude if its right for you(post Avalon Update)Edit: The devs are just doing everything right atm. This new update is amazing, from the changes to the quests, and even the grimore 'nerf'. It just feels like an overall more balanced experience where your choices have to come into play more. The re-roll system is amazing, allowing you chances to go for the exact build you're after, and the new island is perfect.Quests: Previously, it never,EVER, felt worth going for the quest, especially on the first chapter. but now it seems to be only the stone house, and the time to gether the materials is shorter, and you need less. With this, it no longer takes up 2 POI's, and it much easier to get started. With this being more worth it to go after, getting that legendary item from it, it makes going to future quests much easier to go after. Not to mention being able to re-roll your legendary choices is a HUGE deal.Edit: after playing some solo games I got different Quests, the straw house, and the wood house. Don't yet know if it's a solo-to-multiplayer thing or not yet, but either way, the change from 25 items to 15 is big enough that they're still viable, though the straw house is easily the most difficult, and likely in higher difficulty runs still be a Passover, even with the POI's having an item there nowGrimore: The nerf this got, at first i didn't like it too much, however with the current balance of the game it's perfect. Unlike before when it was 'only pick upgrades' and then everything gets to legendary, saving tons of money and allowing you to buy out everything else, you get very nice, varied options that have value based on what character you are, granting a lot more choice with what you have. Plus the option to get more re-rolls is amazing for build hunting.Re-rolls: Amazing. Perfect for building specific builds, or hunting for that one more object you need to complete a set. Goes a long way even just with the few you start with. The best change they've added so farAvalon: The best map. It couldn't be more perfect in my eyes, (though I'm super biased to castle designs) on top of that, the enemies are so fun and engaging to fight, and still unique from everything else encountered so far up until that point.This early access progression has been Incredible, and I cant wait to see what else they have in store!

_childDocuments_.review: ** I'll be updating this review with more updates on the game **This one caught my attention for its unique gameplay and cooperative aspect. I must say, the game is a lot of fun, and the cooperative gameplay is one of the most enjoyable aspects of it. Playing with friends, exploring the game's intricacies, and taking on challenging enemies together makes for a genuinely thrilling experience.However, I do have to say that I was disappointed by the fact that the early access version only has one map. While the map is well-designed and offers a lot of replay value, it feels like the game should have been released as a free demo instead. It's tough to justify paying for a game that only offers one map, even if that map is incredibly well-done.Despite my reservations about the price point, I do have to say that the game is worth playing, especially if you have a group of friends to play with. The co-op aspect is where the game really shines, and it's clear that the developers have put a lot of thought into creating a cooperative experience that is both challenging and fun. Overall, I would recommend giving Ravenswatch a try, but be aware that it's still very much a work in progress.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like such a wasted opportunity. No, I'm not saying the game is bad - this game is solidly built, mechanisms are moderately fun, distinct characters with very different play styles, enemy design is not bad, music on point, all that. BUT there are just so many things that takes the FUN and REPLAYABILITY out of an ACTION ROGUELIKE. I'll break this down further below.On top of everything: what do you mean I can't change difficulty? Maybe if I can't change difficulty because the feature is not implemented yet, then don't put that difficulty selector in my face as a joke? Yes I get the whole GET GUD aspect because yes a good game is worth spending time and becoming experienced with, but again, it's beyond natural that when I just bought the game, I know nothing about it, and I need at least some way to see and learn what the game has in store for me. How about starting new players off on regular/easy/relaxed mode and when they beat the whole thing in that difficulty, THEN ramp it up to normal?OK, now breaking down the "so many things that takes the FUN and REPLAYABILITY out of an ACTION ROGUELIKE" point.- Enemies within one area/map (yeah I might be wrong and that's because I was never able to beat the first boss, duh) does not seem to have life/defense leveling - meaning the enemy of the same type that's right next to the safe zone versus one that's at the furthest point of the map, they are likely to have the same amount of health and armor/stance. You might say "well as you play through the map you gain skills and upgrades and those make the same enemies weaker" - well if you call dealing 5 damage to 7 damage per hit to an enemy with 200 hp an upgrade. How about we make the character deal 10 damage instead of 5 when they gain a certain upgrade, then strengthen the enemy from 200 to 275 hp or something like that? And the amount of "XP" (if there even is an XP setting) you gain grows as the enemy gets harder? I thought this game is all about the countdown thing, so why is this mechanism so difficult to have? Won't this make the level boss easier to approach?- just like many other reviews have mentioned, every run feels almost the same. Can we please have 3 options at the beginning of each run out of a pool of maybe 5 or 6 options, instead of the same 2 option at the beginning of every single run for a character?- Is this game actually meant for solo play? I am honestly not sure. I am ok ~ pretty bad at playing games, but some moves of mobs/boss in this game feels so punishing that it just discourages me. Also - the 6 raven feather respawn system feels so weird. When I'm playing alone I get 6 feathers, and when I'm playing with 3 others the team also only get 6 feathers? So who gets to respawn and who stays dead? I typically am a solo gamer so this does not really concerns me, but it feels so weird and I wonder if this has caused any problems within teams of players of this game.- Yes, when I like a game and am invested enough in a game, I will passively pick up and remember things about a game - but hey, when I'm like 3 hours in, maybe don't try to make me straight up hard remember "trait" "defense" "skill" and whatever there is out there? Give me a hint by showing a small icon of the skill that the upgrade is going to empower, or even just a key hint, does not sound that hard, isn't it? Especially when (1) there's no tutorial at the beginning of - really, anything, not the first run, not when you just got into the game, not anywhere, and (2) when I hover over skill icons at the bottom of the screen, there's no tooltip whatsoever telling me what skill I'm looking at. This really hurts the replayability on the long run.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish it had more characters, since you're rather limited in terms of unique personalities. I wish the balance between individual builds was a lot better. Some characters are just too powerful, regardless of their builds or modes, compared to others. For some characters, you need hyper-specific rolls and some luck.I wish the UI was a tad bit better. For example, when you get a lot of relics, it starts to go off screen, and you can't even view the effects of said relics. Lastly, I wish they took another look at interactions. Why can't some skills target crystals? It severely reduces the amount of time you get to move around. Outside of those small critiques, this is definitely a game I'd recommend for others to enjoy. There is a lot of build versatility (though some builds are just not good compared to others).  Great lore, beautiful aesthetics, fun conceptsGameplay-wise, it's rather smooth, and depending on the character and personal playstyle, learning the game can be quite entertaining. I'd also recommend enjoying this game with a friend since you can cover more ground, learn characters at a faster pace, and it guarantees more laughs.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a refreshing new take on a "Hack and Slash" genre where the story, the characters, and the style merge into a great experience of gameplay. As a fan of the fairy tale concept, the game accomplishes its intended atmosphere through its art style and its interface. Its animation and coding feel smooth and polished. After playing it since its debut, I am always looking forward to new updates and new heroes that keep the game challenging and fun but casual and relaxed. Compared to the original "grind" concept which makes a person work for hours and hours for loot and gear, the developers shifted the attention to grinding that does not feel daunting or obligatory. Each game feels like a run for excitement and when it's done, it's done and you feel accomplished after each one.I highly recommend this game for those people who only have a few hours a day to play. Each game finished provides a grind that allows new things to look forward to. Giving the next scheduled game time something exciting to be expected.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty solid. It has a lot of things roguelike fans will enjoy. It’s fairly polished and bug-free, but that is probably something you should expect from a game that went through a lengthy Early Access cycle.I think the best thing about this game is the character roster and the combat mechanics.The character pool is very mechanically diverse: every character feels unique to play, has their own gimmicks, playstyles, and builds that will cater to a wide variety of players. I think you will almost certainly find a character or two on the roster whose playstyle you really mesh with.The combat is pretty punishing, but rewarding when mastered. There is a good variety of enemies that each pose a unique threat that has to be dealt with. Unfortunately, that variety doesn’t extend to bosses: Each level only has one boss that never changes and always has the same moves. This feels somewhat lacking, especially compared to the best games in the genre, that offer more variety in that particular aspect.As an aside, another thing that hurts the variety is that the maps never change. You have the same layouts every time, all that cnanges are the rewards for clearing particular modules. This feels like missed potential to a certain extent.And while the mechanics are good, there are frustrating things about the game’s combat, too. The main culprit are the somewhat inconsistent hitboxes, particularly on enemy AoE attacks. And some enemies are just plain annoying to fight, with their moveset either being too relentless and oppressive or their HP pool being too big.With all that being said, I still enjoy the combat in this game quite a bit, especially when everything comes together. Which brings me to the next portion of the review: items, builds, and RNG.I feel like the game doesn’t quite strike a perfect balance there. You start with only a portion of your Talents unlocked, and unlock more as you level up a character, but the issue is that while unlocking new Talents gives you more room to play and experiment with, at the end of the day you will find that some of the Talents you unlock are somewhat lacklustre. What ends up happening is that your Talent pool becomes diluted with Talents you don’t really want. I  say that the game doesn’t have a lot of bad Talents, though. It’s just that a lot of them are either very “meh”, or just simply too niche, and don’t fit into many builds.And this does lead to frustration, when you’re just not getting the things you want, and it feels like the run is doomed and you’re just going through the motions. And the way the game works is that there is almost never a chance for you to clear a run when your build is crap.The game does, however, provide you with a few ways to control your run, like rerolls and item shops. I’ve found that the best way to play the game is to know what build you’re going with before starting the run, and play accordingly. Because letting the RNG decide often ends up in a build that is a mishmash of everything, and doesn’t really work. I feel that in other games “going with the flow” is a lot more fun than it is here.This issue is very prominent in multiplayer. Since MP games scale the difficulty, now you’re even more reliant on RNG. Not only do you have to get a nice build going yourself, you have to hope whoever you’re playing with does as well, which too often just doesn’t happen.I feel like about half of that are actual design issues with the game, and half are skill issue on my part.Despite all those frustrating elements, I’d still recommend the game. It’s a solid 6,5/10 for the overall experience. Excellent combat somewhat dragged down by punishing RNG and the lack of variety in certain areas of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game with plenty of content even for Early Access. Ramping difficulty levels, character, item, and skill unlocks, provide tons of replayability despite there being one level at this stage of development. Every character is unique and plays a different way. The negative reviews are largely due to complaints that there's not enough content (only one level). _childDocuments_.review: I picked this up in April. 2023, and have played it off and on since, mostly around content releases.After reading some of the other reviews around here I found myself wanting to counter one of the critiques of this game.Granted, playing games is a subjective experience, so this is merely how and why my point of view differs.A recurring point I'm seeing is that this game lacks meaningful progression and there isn't much point to playing a character more than once or twice other than to say you beat the run with them.I wholeheartedly disagree, both the progression of your character during the match and the progression of the character outside of the match are mechanically tied into playing the character repeatedly. Mid-game you level up to earn talents, which change or enhance the mechanics of your abilities. These talents are rng-selected and can come out at various times and at varying strengths. The selection of talents you have access to increases by leveling the character outside of the match, including access to an alternative ultimate ability after several levels.Out of match XP is granted by completing runs. So, the more runs you complete, the more variety of talents and abilities that can come out during a run. These talents can lead to different combo's becoming possible, synergies with other characters changing, and sometimes can completely change the play style of a character during the run. Since these talents are rng-influenced, every run requires you to think flexibly and keep track of what other talents you have access to. Depending on circumstances and preferences, a bad build could become a great build by changing your playstyle or coordinating with teammates differently.I think those that claimed the game lacked progression depth actually did not play any character enough to unlock meaningful variety. If you only play a character once or twice and think you've seen everything it has to offer, you are likely really missing out on some stuff, or perhaps misunderstanding what the progression system is.The characters all have meaningful variety between them, so progressing each one, or even half, up to the point where you unlock their 2nd Ultimate is a decent amount of playtime. Each character continues progression beyond that point as well, so that's not the end-all by any means.Now, the game is still very much an early access experience. It is explicitly not complete. A standard run will be a 3 act (map/boss) affair, as of writing (2-2024) the game only has up to Act 2 released. However, the dev's are nailing their roadmap, each content release has been solid, meaningful additions to the game, be it gameplay mechanics, lore, back-end, networking, etc.This game, to me, feels like it was aimed at a weird intersection of Diablo, rougelike, and Dota 2 event mode fans who wanted something that can range from a casual hack'n'slash experience to a grueling race against the clock to optimize yourself for an ass-kicking. If you like the devs and like supporting good early access titles, and enjoy a pick-up experience of adjustable difficulty that will never demand more than about an hour of your time for a complete run, I can't recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:  -A multiplayer roguelike that is challenging and doesn't trivialize itself by giving you raw stats with meta-progression is really unique. Basically treat it like deep rock galactic.-Some performance issues if you have a 3+ party and aren't all on the same screen. _childDocuments_.review: Another case of 'Steam should allow neutral reviews'.The game has a pretty decent foundation, mechanically and thematically. The combat is deliberate and well-paced, with an emphasis on managing the cooldowns of your abilities, particularly those that allow you to iframe through the bullet/AoE hell the enemies will happily throw at you. The game is surprisingly tough in the first few runs, even on lowest difficulty, as there's a lot of basic mobs that will absolutely delete your healthbar if you don't deal with them properly.What turns this from a straight positive review into a mixed one (translating into negative given the current average score) is quite simply the lack of content. There's only 3 chapters, that you will play through in the same order each run, with the exact same enemies around and the exact same secondary quests and almost the same map layouts. The number of traits and perks available is likewise heavily limited, to the point that there's barely enough to kit you out in a full run (you get to pick 10 talents, and afaik the base amount is 11 to chose from, with a few more to unlock by meta progression). With this narrow a scope of upgrades, there's no real way to differentiate your build, so each character will always play almost the same. (Kudos to the different characters having significantly different playstyles though, that part is done well.)I'm 7 hours in, beat the game in a few runs with different characters, but are already bored of fighting through the same set-up again and again. At least the game isn't expensive, and it's EA status suggests more content might be added later...but I wouldn't recommend buying into it just yet.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, the game rocks. Its crazy good, and you should play it if you like Roguelikes and are okay with feeling a little bit of pressure. Since buying this game, I've beaten the hardest difficulty on my favorite character (Scarlet), and will attempt to do the same for all of the other characters. All of my experience speaks for solo play. The character variety is one of the game's strongest suits. All of the heroes are completely unique, strong, and FUN, with a play-style to match anyone. If a hero doesn't feel strong, it's not necessarily because they are weak, but because they need to be understood by the player piloting them. The game heavily rewards understanding the heroes abilities and investing time into them. In my case, Scarlet immediately clicked for me, but I could not play The Pied Piper at first to save my life, until I eventually understood his basic strategy. Each hero has a variety of different builds to pursue that are all very powerful. Almost anything seems to work for most of them, and character modifiers (talents) work together in sometimes unexpected ways, and more are unlocked as you play. The enemies are fun, fair, well telegraphed and identifiable at a glance. Understanding which enemy needs to be targeted first in a group is an important skill that is heavily rewarded. I hate the cyclops' grab though.The map, for the most part, could be better. It can be sort of hard to read sometimes, sometimes an activity can be on a hill, but you have no idea where the way up the hill is, and you end up wasting some time. And some of the events can be a little unclear; I still don't know where the mini-boss key is supposed to spawn. Close to the mini-boss door? Randomly around the map? Things like this could be explained better in-game, and I hope they are in the future. I also simply wish there were more activities and more variety for existing activities. I honestly think the game difficulty is nearly perfect. I do not think it is nearly as hard as many people say it is; extra lives are very forgiving and all of the characters have plenty of outs for getting out of a bad situation. Easily the most controversial thing about the game is the fact that it runs on a timer. Frankly, I don't really have much of a problem with it at all; it is not much different from understanding that you only have 30 minutes in an Isaac run to fight Hush. The game immediately presents you with the idea that you have a timer to work around; everything you do in this time-frame is done to make you stronger to prepare for the boss. Its an easy to understand format that presents you with plenty of time. Not enough time to do EVERYTHING on the map, but enough time to make meaningful choices and get noticeably stronger using the route through the map you took. That said, it would be a nice quality of life change to have time freeze if you teleport back to the Sandman's circle, just for players to be able to catch their breath and consider their build/other options. A lot more could be said about this game, and frankly I am not the best at writing reviews, but to put it bluntly, this game is phenomenal and extremely fun. I love everything Passtech Games is doing with it and will be following this game for as long as its development cycle lasts and beyond, and I encourage anyone reading this to do the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite roguelikes and it pains me to see how much better it could have been if feedback from early access has been taken into account. It is still fun but it feels like game is actively trying to frustrate you for no reason whatsoever.The indisputable positive of Ravenswatch is time management based biom exploration and class design. The timer forces you to spend your time as productively as possible and rewards you for doing so. Each character feels unique and has multiple build options. Becoming op by third chapter and absolutely destroying enemies and bosses is very satisfying. However, there are a lot of minor problems that pile up and turn your runs into unfair and frustrating mess. These problems were in the game during early access and it's shocking to see them not fixed in full release. 1) Enemy agro range. If you agro enemies you don't want to fight (and there are plenty of enemies you don't want to fight because you want to save your time) they will keep following you for eternity until they decide to finally ♥♥♥♥ off. While enemies are agroed you can't interact with chests or any other activities on map and damage to gold crystals is significantly reduced. This often leads to situations where you enter a POI arena hoping for a quick fight and reward but instead enemies follow you all the way to the arena and pollute the encounter. Now what was supposed to be a 30 second fight turns into a 2 minute nightmare of you running circles around enemies, waiting for your cooldowns to reset, and chip damaging a giant crowd that NEVER STOPS SPAMMING AOE attacks. I have no idea how an issue so glaring made it into 1.0 patch.2) Combat. I keep seeing people praise combat system. Don't get me wrong, when you managed to make a good build with all the right talents and items combat can rock. But early level gameplay is just miserable and I think the main reason why is the fact that enemy attacks often overlap. If you played Curse of The Dead Gods (a previous game from devs of Ravenswatch) you know that every single hit you took was your fault. There were never situations where enemy crowd spammed you to death. But in Ravenswatch this happens all the time. And again, this is not a big deal in late game where you kill enemies before they even have a chance to attack. But I swear most of your deaths in early game will be a result of overlapping attacks and AOE spam. Many enemies have unavoidable chip damage attacks (like small ghoul bite attacks) and I have no idea why they are in the game to begin with? They add nothing of value and only frustrate you. 3) Feathers. But the worst thing about this game is feathers. Feathers allow you to revive after death and even on highest difficulty you get to revive twice. Why feathers are bad? Because it contradicts the whole point of death in roguelikes. Permadeath is a core mechanic of roguelike games and in a good roguelike death is always a player's fault. But it seems to me that devs are aware of the fact that in Ravenswatch death is often a result of a situation where player couldn't avoid damage. And instead of making sure that these situation don't happen they decided to just give you revives so you can continue leveling up until you become overpowered. Hell, you can even buy additional feather in bioms and doing so also rewards you experience. That is the biggest issue for me. Every time I die in this game I wonder if it was my mistakes or game's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Whereas in CoTD, Slay the Spire, Dead Cells I know that my deaths are results of my mistakes.I'll keep playing this game. I'll even buy DLCs that are already announced because despite its flaws I like Ravenswatch. But many problems that were present during early access are still plaguing the game and at this point I doubt they will be fixed. It's a shame because Ravenswatch has a very unique concept that currently lacks the polish it desperately needs.

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions after playing 2 player coop with a friend: Very competent for an Early Access, will be playing it more with friends.The Bad:1. The minimap is difficult to read at first because the little blips showing players' positions are "standing", mimicking the isometric camera view. This means only their pointy bottom is where the players actually are.2. Most attacks do not stagger enemies, even though enemies will spasm out as they react to hits - if a player goes to town with only basic Attacks on even the lowest tier enemies, that enemy will start trading hits without any visible windup to their attacks. This gets particularly annoying with characters who have longer attack animations as part of their combos.3. Sometimes an enemy will stop registering attacks from Guest Clients. So far it has only happened with non-boss enemies, but I don't even want to imagine how frustrating this would be vs the Master Nightmare.4. The characters' abilities radically changing with the Day and Night transitions (often times mid-fight) feels punitive and frustrating if one only like one particular side of the character's kit. Scarlet and the Pied Piper being prime examples of this.5. Baseline cooldowns feel a bit too long, especially if you tackle a map solo.The (very) Good:1. The game loop looks very healthy with the randomized spawns, powerup locations. A good coop rogue-lite ARPG.2. The music is superb, and fits the tone and mood of the game.3. The characters' visual design is great - with a bit of extra voice work they could be nicely fleshed out.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Ravenswatch is a good game with the potential to be great over time. For $20 ($18 at the time of writing) I believe it is still worth the price.Ravenswatch is the weird love child of Grimm, Diablo, and Hades. Between its clever retelling of common children's folktales, art style reminiscent of Darkest Dungeon and Hades, and crisp / clean gameplay is the heart and soul of a great game...it's just missing some of the content to go from good to great. However, that isn't a ding on the developers or the game itself, but rather the nature of early access. If we look at what the early access pricing is providing, I feel this is on par CONTENT WISE with the initial Early Access releases for many other titles while providing a level of polish that outshines many AAA releases today. For an Early Access title, my friends and I could find only one bug, combat and progression felt smooth, and all we wanted to do was just keep playing. All I can say, is that this game is worth supporting. It's worth the $18 I paid, and I can't wait for the next few months to see what new content gets added.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend it on steam so you read it (I know you searched the ,,not recommended section)Here are my thoughts:I love this game!However, I agree with most of dislikes - even for an early access (I like that they decided to release it so soon to hear the feedback) there's too little content. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you like arcade style multiplayer, roguelikes, or breathe air, you should buy this game.Overall, it is quite fun and very re-playable. I'm 8 hours in and having a blast. Each run is different and each character quite unique and fun to engage with. I can't imagine this game not blowing up. I enjoy the combat, sound fx, voice lines, enemies, mechanics, and the graphics. No complaints.I feel it has the right level of difficulty to keep me feeling challenged, but not frustrated. I have a 4 person play group most of the time, but it's fun solo, coop, or 3 person. In our play, we find ourselves working together in a variety of ways, scrambling to the end, and often someone is saying something frantic. Some fights and boss runs are pretty epic and we end up exploding into cheers, laughter, and spouting crude inappropriate things at the enemies.On a more technical note, the character builds you wind up making up as you go is a huge part of the fun. You find yourself choosing various powers as you level and unlock items. The combinations are interesting and create unique experiences. Thanks to this build variety, there are many different ways to play each character, and each run winds up playing out differently. Some combinations work better than others perhaps, yet all seem to end up feeling fun and powerful if you play into them. I feel like it's similar to Risk of Rain though less overwhelming as there are a bit less items and powers to juggle, and it's more accessible overall. There is enough player agency to keep you involved and feel like choices are meaningful, but not so much as to slow down the action or become a burden. Likewise, you can't really choose wrong and ruin the experience.I do feel there is content that needs added. More is very likely to be added based on the history and the road-map. At the time of this review, the game is currently in beta and there are two 'chapters' and maybe 6 or so characters, but the road-map indicates a third chapter and more characters are on the way. Personally I feel that could be plenty if there were more bosses, and perhaps some sort of uber boss challenge at the end. I'd also like to see alternative game modes.I honestly recommend everyone buy this game. It's in beta, not even finished, and I'm telling you it's worth the spend in it's current state. It feels very polished, which is a rarity lately in gaming.*40 hours in now, and it's at full release.*This game is fun. I stand by my review. New bosses and characters have been added among other things. Pretty solid game. Could use more levels to mix it up a bit more, but generally it's a fun game.Cheers,Luckymod13

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, but there are some problems. - difficulty. Current difficulty system is just more enemy’s damage and health, less player’s XP and feathers. Nothing else, there are no gameplay changes, only different numbers.  - convenience. Mark of the new talent or item in the book will disappear only if you click at this talent or item and after that on another one. Also there is a problem with Scarlet wolf abilities, you can read their description only in game, there are only Scarlet human abilities in the book.  - items swap. If you don't want to take any of current items from chest, quest or grimoire you can replace them with another set of items. BUT, there may be already replaced items in the new set. New content such as enemies, their attacks, and quests can solve this problem. At least higher difficulty can give more gold and XP to be more powerful as your enemies. _childDocuments_.review: A pretty neat take on the roguelike / roguelite formula where you control reimagined storybook characters across a few of the popular 'realms' in their stories. Each 'realm' IS timegated, which can feel restrictive initially, but the aspect of choice in what events you want to complete adds to the strategy of the game. Do you weaken the acts final boss, making the hardest fight easier, or do you farm money to boost your damage for the rest of the game? Maybe you grab a talent instead to boost your abilities? I can see some people hating the time aspect, and I personally prefer Curse of the Dead Gods take vs. this, but it's still enjoyable. - Ability diversity is great, each hero can have 4-5 different builds. Considering there are 9 heroes here, you're getting a decent amount of variety. - Realm diversity is great, it's randomized each time. There are also quests in each which can vary between runs. - Character diversity is great, Pierre plays NOTHING like Scarlett. Also, this is a really weird thing that appeals to me, but the sound design in this game is so satisfyingly.. musical? Like, for instance, when I play Scarlet in werewolf form she can get a 3-hit combo that just sounds.. rewarding? It's a great touch that I don't know how to vocalize. I just know when I right-click, then attack, I'll hear this satisfying 'Whoop Whoop Whoop whopp whoop whoop whoop. I know, I'm weird.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, very smooth and satisfying gameplay, super crunchy controls and animations. Every hero has its own different unique playstyle and "feel" to it, with many ways to build and experiment. Some of them feel better than others, especially once you understand how they work. Things aren't as simple in this game as they may look at the beginning, and that's awesome.Menus, music, visuals, all of them are stunning. They did a great job with everything.I didn't expect a lot of lore from an action focused roguelike, but they even have cool backstories and lore to read if interested.Characters have unique interactions between each other. They speak, they joke, give hints about their stories and personal relationships. Adds some nice flavor into the game.Some people say you can't "break" the game with extra strong builds in late-game, I'd like to correct them them and say you can. It's just not as easy and you still have to be aware of your enemy attacks most of the times..  Unless you build into crazy amount of armor/vitality.. Which you also can.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the game very much. I've only play solo so far, but I've read that coop is even more fun.It's a rogue-like action game, very well executed:- Good strategy: you must establish a path dynamically, and build your character (skills and upgrades, objects to stack).- Good class design, with most skills having dual effects, so offering a highly mechanical / optimized way of playing, to maximize these effects. Plus day/night have side effects on both heroes and enemies, so this must be taken into account as well.- Challenging, you need to scale up fast, and make sure you don't fail (be methodical), otherwise you'll feel weak and die miserably. It's possible (and not that hard) to become strong/overpowered and one-shot mobs, though.The art is great, and the OST / sound effects are good too, which gives a pleasant atmosphere. Like in Curse of the Dead Gods, there is some story, but no narration at all: you must read it in the compendium. It may be a good point or bad point, depending on what you desire.The game is not for everyone, but if you're into roguelike action games, and are looking for some challenge (no casual skill spamming gets you to the end), then this is a great one.
