_childDocuments_.review: In an article I posted back in , I described Ravenswatch as potentially one of the best titles to come out when it was ready.  The title was in an Early Access state, freshly adding content on a quarterly basis over the course of nearly 18 months, with its 1.0 build releasing this past September.  The isometric style gameplay akin to games like Diablo and the developer’s previous title, Curse of the Dead Gods provided a fun spin on the ARPG genre, so long as the content provided to make the complete game was enough to keep fans happy over the many hours it expected you to play.  Lets, uh.  Let’s talk about that.Ravenswatch tasks 9 heroes to choose from, all ranging from different fairy tales and folklore legends to tackle the hordes of devilish creatures known as The Nightmare that is plaguing the lands of dreams.  You and up to 3 other players will tackle different worlds on a time-limited venture, powering up to be ready to face the Boss of each world before moving on.  If at any point you die and run through all of your continues, known as Raven Feathers, it’s Game Over and back to square one: no checkpoints, no saves.You’ll take charge of your heroes in a control scheme that feels like a blend between your favorite isometric ARPG and your favorite MOBA.  Movement is handled via mouse clicks and your abilities are tabbed to your keyboard, with certain abilities being offensively or defensively minded: dashes, CC, debuffs and buffs and the like.  Each world gives players 3 days and 3 nights, roughly 18-20 minutes in real time, to collect as much money, XP, and items as they can before heading into that world’s boss battle.  Maps are specifically made so you won’t be able to do everything in a world so you must choose your route in terms of gambling and efficiency: do you want to run multiple easy objectives or try your luck on the harder tasks knowing a failure to complete could spell big trouble?The speed and tempo of Ravenswatch lies solely within this chasm of manufactured busyness and benefits greatly as you really do not have much time to waste if you want a fleeting chance at defeating the bosses of each world, so routing a specific path and being on the same wavelength as your teammates is crucial.  Each map starts with a couple hints to where certain objectives are and the rest of the map is covered in Fog of War, so finding and completing objectives, which different colors indicate varying levels of difficulty, is done on the fly and those decisions on taking on the harder objectives can mean the difference between a comfy run and a dead one.But the time limit on each world feels like a blessing so you don’t recognize the curse.  Each world feels very empty and lacks character, especially with the size of each world being inflated to add that sense of mystery requiring multiple playthroughs to see everything available.  Most of your time will be spent running from key objective to key objective with the occasional mob in between but nothing on the run feels memorable or interesting to look forward to.  A lot of the objectives themselves fall flat as well since quests divulge into “clear this base of minions for cash/perks/etc.” or “complete this objective from a NPC for cash/perks/etc.” and don’t go much farther than that.Upgrading your character is handled on a leveling and bartering scale.  Defeating minions and finishing quests earns XP to level up your stats and choose from one of two upgrades to your abilities.  These ability upgrades can range from adding additional stat bonuses to your ability to changing the structure of the whole ability in itself.  You can push for quicker attacks but sacrifice damage but this would combine well with “every X hit” upgrades or go for slower but chunkier attacks that can do AOE damage to help clear minions quicker.  The instances where there feels like some genuine crafting of builds happens within these level ups, though with only two options per level and most runs you will level less than 10 times, the amount of tinkering can feel minimal.Stats can also be boosted by obtaining perks from completing objectives and also upgrading said perks in the world’s shop at home base.  These perks do help your character become more powerful but the plentiful amount of items available don’t do much outside of flat stat boosts to your desired ability.  The shop also has multiple items that provide short-term boosts that are good for extra strength on a harder area or a refill of HP before heading back out into the world or to tackle one of Ravenswatch’s world bosses.World bosses are your marquee, bread and butter spectacles in Ravenswatch.  These bosses mirror raid bosses in your favorite MMO with sprawling area-based attacks and a circular arena to chip away at.  These battles will test your mental dexterity and actions per minute as you have to be constantly moving and on your toes or these bosses will tear you apart.  They are  but they are  and provide the best example of what Ravenswatch is really trying to sell you.  Which makes it so much more disappointing that of the 4 main world bosses, one of the bosses is a dual-boss fight with rehashed abilities from the other bosses.  Really?    I can’t explain the audible groan our team had when we finally reached this boss and started recognizing patterns from previous bosses.  There’s only 4!  This either is a complete lack of imagination to supply another interesting and specific boss type or the development team ran out of time before their 1.0 release and had to pivot to assets already made.  It’s a shame since this boss takes some time to get to and knowing that’s your ultimate reward for about an hour's work is brutal.Once you complete a run, you gain permanent XP for the character you played where level ups to the overall character unlock additional ability upgrades for when you level up in game, an additional Ultimate ability, or pages of lore for the character.  Completing the first chapter with the standard characters will unlock additional characters so you don’t need to go far in order to extend your character range for who you want to start the next game with.And then, if you’re willing, it’s time to do it all over again.  The foundations of what is provided by Ravenswatch did show promise, the time management focus is a brilliant idea to hyper-focus team concentration and split-second detours within each world and the characters all do provide some interesting mechanics that are enjoyable to play.  But even as Ravenswatch turns the 1.0 page, it feels like it’s missing a lot.  The worlds feel empty, there’s very little variety to the objectives, the bosses are wildly hit and miss, and the rewards for a run well done don’t feel plentiful enough to run through the lusterless hour or so of leveling up your character.

_childDocuments_.review: Negative reviews that just state "There's too little content" should be ignored on all early access titles..THE POSITIVE¬ Controlls, abilities, artstyle, animations, sound design, voice acting - all REALLY great.¬ There are multiple heroes to choose from, each with their very own unique play style. I've tried them all and every single one plays the game differently, which is great fun.¬ Many different viable builds for each character. It's RNG but you can still pick which ones you want to upgrade, and you also get a chance to re-roll talents if you're not happy. ¬ Having one hero I enjoy more than the others, I get rewarded more and better talents when ranking up that hero. Not getting punished for playing the same hero I enjoy over and over again is so good. ¬ Good variety on enemies, and their corrupted/harder versions are done correctly! Instead of just getting X% more health/damage, the harder versions of enemies gain new abilities, different animations, and look more menacing. Also they reward more xp! Feels really good to defeat them.¬ Custom modifiers to the game!!!! You don't like the "rush-against-time" aspect? REMOVE IT! Great job devs.THE NEGATIVE¬ The game promotes you splitting up with your team mates to cover more ground faster, and since the currency used for upgrades is rewarded to everyone even if you pick them up on the other side of the map, it removes alot of the co-op. Naturally you don't HAVE to split up, but then you lose some of the possible advantages. When playing in higher difficulties it becomes a necessity to split up.¬ Playing on higher difficulties punish the player the "wrong" way; by limiting the one thing that generates the most dopamine: Leveling up and getting new talents. Playing on higher difficulty reduces the amount of XP you get by X%. ¬ Only way to get currency ("dream shards", used to buy upgrades) is rewarded from smashing certain objects that take a few amount of hits, and then having to manually walk over the debris. It's boring, especially for ranged heroes. Even if Dream Shards are the most important thing to smash/loot, I tend to skip them when I see them randomly on the map, because the few seconds you have to dedicate to the task breaks the flow of the action in the game. Personally I believe it would just add to the already present satisfaction of killing monsters if monsters also rewarded dream shards depending of the difficulty of the enemy (rule of thumb in this game is bigger enemies = harder enemies). It's currently dividing my matches; Some players want to fight monsters because it's where the fun is at; and some just skip all the monsters and run to the dream shard static spawns.Thanks for reading!P.S: @devs PLEASE remove the animation when transforming into/from werewolf.. it's so annoying EVERY. SINGLE. TIME xD

_childDocuments_.review: The reviews of this game are far worse than it deserves. Ravenswatch is a hard rogue-like, no doubt, and that may be off-putting for many players. But it's extremely deep and engaging once you have a grasp of its mechanics. The dark fairy tale art style is fun, the different characters make you engange with the game differently, progression, mixing and matching - it's all really great. The balance in the release version is much improved compared to Early Access. Hades II is flashier, fluffier and hornier, but this game is really not that far behind.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Difficult yet fun game to play by yourself or with friends. The fleshed out map is  nice to have. Combat is skill based and not spam to win (note that missing a skill in higher difficulties may result in death). This game also features a revive system that makes the experience more enjoyable, as you wont have to restart if the enemy kills you in 2 hits (again only in higher difficulties). Talent system works nicely with items, of which there are multiple including legendary and cursed items. Overall a very good roguelite with a dark fairy tale theme, of which there are few out there. Can't wait for the coming updates and more heroes and areas to come.

This is clearly communicated tho and the roadmap looks reasonable. Getting feedback and player data is of course nice, but sometimes it's a shame that Early Access is often financially necessary. _childDocuments_.review: You know, overall, I'd say I'm decently luke warm, BUT.. Positive review for one reason more than any other - ACTUAL interesting character design. Each hero doesn't just play differently in a general since, as most games claim while having the same boring sword+shield melee, heal-y priest, elemental mage, and other uncreative tropes we've seen done over and over and over..Each hero plays differently in reasonably unique ways and it's a bit telling just how unique it feels just for putting in some effort to go beyond the usual trinity of classes as the base design! _childDocuments_.review: Great game, especially for a roguelite junky like mePros:-amazing dynamic combat-huge number of unique characters and builds-super fun as a coop game-the artstyle is greatCons:- Balance issues. Some characters aren't made for solo playthroughs (like Beowulf) and rely a lot on others to dish out dmg. His kit is great, but it's pretty much impossible to beat the game on higher difficulties as solo Beo. Unless ur a tryhard, that is. On the other hand, Scarlet always feels great to play with almost any build, I would even call her overtuned. Healing, insane single-target and aoe dmg, etc. If u get lucky and pick up Excal, the run is pretty much done as Scarlet.-Confusing mechanics. Maybe it's just me, but I really struggled the first couple hours, because I didn't get the fact that the farther u go from spawn, the stronger the enemies get. Enemies are also super aggresive at night and there are "milestones" to completing certain tasks on the map (for example- u shouldn't try to do the first quest until ur at least lvl3. The second quest needs to be done at lvl7 minimum and the game doesn't really tell u that). If you don't understand those things quickly enough, the game will become a chore to play, ur gonna kill 3 enemies in 5 minutes due to their large healthpools.The second negative point can probably be circumvented by reading the in-game guide, but I digress.Overall, the game has huge potential, I am really interested to see what the devs come up with next.

_childDocuments_.review: This Games Design is beautyfull and made with lots of Love, I really like the Theme and Characters in it.The Music is alright but nothing i'd pay for to get the soundtrack but it fits the dreary dark atmosphere. Looking at this Game with a bare eye I would say i really love it. But i just can't help myself to enjoy playing this.Most of the time it just feels like you are accomplishing nothing. It's all pretty cool when you start, you'll unlock the characters one after another and everyone of these characters have a very unique feel to them. But once you have them all, decided on 2 or 3 Favorites that you will play, thats pretty much when it starts to become quite the drag.The Problem here is it's repetitivness, there arent many maps or bosses, and it all playes out the same each and every run. Only that the maps are randomly generated. It could be ok like this, the Problem is the progress you make. I find most of the Upgrades you can get while leveling up really dont feel as if they had any impact. Only a few abilities seem very usefull and make a difference on how you play your character. The rest of them you will bearly notice, if you notice them at all. It makes it frustrating , as when you aren't very lucky enemies quickly become sponges that take forever to kill. Im not saying i find the game to difficult , it's just that your pool of abilities seldomly makes you keep up with the rising difficulty. That being said, to me the combat itself also feels like a bit of a drag. In my opinion its all a little slow in movement. It all feels like its in a bit of a slowmotion. you get one dash at the start which is bound to a cooldown so it wont help you speeding things up a little. The more of the map you uncover while exploring the more teleporters you will find, making it easier to navigate from one point of the map to another which would be far away. But that doesnt make the movement itself fun. You will have 20 Minutes on each Map until the final boss of that area appears. That sounds a lot but it isnt at all. You only aim is to rush from one point of interesst to another until that timer runs out, you'll constantly feel pressured by time. Now i do get that this game is more about the Multiplayer, and enemies are spongie cause you need a fitting set of characters and fight coordinated with your teammates to focus one enemie after another. I like the idea and when my friends get this game i will try playing it with them and see how it gets. But playing with the public pool is like fishing in  a toilet bowl. Why you cant blame the Game for the behaviour of some people in the community, it just happens a lot that players become toxic, abandon the game (which pretty much means restart for you). There is so many times that people just cant decide on a common goal and youll end up with a devided group. That is bad because alone there is no way you'll be effective. (basically another reason to restart) I think the overall gameplay is often a frustrating expirience due to the upgrade system which doesn't allow much variety or improvement. And i think this is one of the reasons for the bad multiplayer as well. Getting into Multiplayer itself is a hasstle, its managed over a public lobby instead of just giving you the option to quickplay. Yes the set of characters abilities should play well together, thats why the lobby function is good, but youll never get on terms with other people on that. Everyone will just play what they like anyhow, and often enough insist on a character, then another one leaves and it goes on and on until finally 4 ppl manage to hit that ready button at the same time. Again its more like behaviour from the community. Stuff like that also happens alot in other games, overwatch for an example. But that is pretty extreme in this game. Then the loading times until everybody is ready, take forever.Summarising this, the generall expirience you get each run is: youll take 10 minutes to get into a game with 4 people. Then you start out with abilities that dont make much of a difference, you'll fight uncoordinated frustrating battles against very spongie enemies. Your teammates start to argue on where to go , someone leaves. you now had 10 minutes playtime and can now wait 10 minutes or longer to get into the next game. That loop is what destroyes the game for me sadly.Like i said im still looking forward to play this in a coordinated fashion with some friends, and expect it might be more fun then. But the game mechanics remain and the repetitiveness and the lack of reward for playing wont allow much longevity for it. Really wish i could love this game as much as looking at it, since it is clear to me that the developers put much thought and love into this project. And at it's core this is a great game idea.

_childDocuments_.review: So far (as an early access) it provides a very fun and engaging game-play loop, although with a limited amount of content (being a very early access game). This game has a roadmap, unlike even some fully released unfinished AAA games (DARKTIDE), and several playable characters from the get-go (with two more unlockable). Only a single map design exists now, although it's completely randomized, with randomized event's and locations.Graphics are reminiscent of a Diablo-esque game, with a tell-tale game graphics twist. Controls are good, responsive, game-play is addictive and fun. Even in it's early access state it's a very enjoyable game, especially with a group of friends.Will add more info down the line when more content is released.

_childDocuments_.review: I would 100% recommend getting this game,sure there is a lack of different maps because this is the first week of release, but to say there isnt enough content is just crazy.  It's a roguelite it'll probably take 20+ hours to get all 5 current characters to max level, and on top of that it has an increasing difficulty rating each time you succeed.  The different classes literally all bring such a different style of play to the game.  It has a merciful time system, preventing a poor rng run keeping you in a game for what feels like a waste, if you have bad RNG it'll take much more finesse to pull out the W. _childDocuments_.review: Number one problem: the entire game is FAR too bullet-spongy. Even common trash enemies require you to spam your entire skillset multiple times to clear them, and this is at low difficulties. When you get up to the hardest mode, combined with its experience deduction making your character weaker at every point through the game, this becomes absolutely infuriating to deal with. Multiplayer enemy scaling is also bananas - I don't know the exact numbers, but if you're playing with a full party of 4 people, it definitely feels like they simply have 4x their already ballooned HP.The aggro system needs a lot of work, too. Enemies will see you and follow you for several screens, often times still counting you as "in combat" despite having nothing visibly attacking you for several seconds. This prevents you from triggering interactables or collecting any dream shards (gold), adding to the frustration of "waste a ton of time on trash mobs or you're not allowed to do anything!" In my opinion, there isn't any good reason to lock interactables or prevent dream shard collection in the first place.Boss fights have some clear attack patterns, but the design is tarnished by the over abundant bullet hell aspects, which also works directly against the multiplayer mechanic of reviving teammates. The interaction timer is JUST long enough so that many cycles of attacks perfectly ♥♥♥♥ you for trying, as they knock you out of the revive progress bar with nothing to show for it, so more often than not when a teammate goes down it's actually a trap to even try. The only real safe time to revive someone is when you've just staggered the boss, and that takes up almost all of the time you're allowed to do any damage, because every boss has tons of armor when it's not knocked down.By the way, did I mention that if you don't revive your teammate within a very short time frame, it costs your team one of their limited auto-revives, and if there are none they're just dead for the rest of the stage, and if it's still during the stage itself and not in the boss, they get to fall behind further as a consequence of no longer being able to pick up relics? Yeah. Great.On top of all this, the roguelike elements are laughable to the point of being inconsequential. You get two talent choices per level up (except at levels 5 and 10, which are locked into being your 'ult' and 'ult booster'), of which you'll only see around 5 per run on average. More often than not they're tiny DPS increases that you hardly notice, sometimes with janky requirements. Because of that, most characters feel stale, never really evolving their gameplay from their base kits.The relics you can find have similar problems, providing negligible bonuses and requiring you to find a ton of copies of the same one to get bonus effects, but even those are often pretty bad. I've played a lot and not once have I felt like my character ever gets to that juicy point where I feel my build really comes together. You're simply not given enough power, and the little you do get tends to come out in the wash of enemies getting stronger as you go. You never catch up.All around, very frustrating gameplay with not nearly enough payoff. I'm the type of person who challenges themselves with high ascension/max difficulty/tons of bad modifiers/etc type of gameplay in all sorts of other games, so don't mistake this for complaining out of a lack of skill or something. I don't mind failure, as part of the fun is not knowing whether a run is going to be successful or not, but there is a difference between something being difficult and something being poorly designed, frustrating, and unfun.

_childDocuments_.review: Now when I first got this game it only had minimal reviews and it was "mixed." After reading through some of them it appeared most players were upset due to lack of content rather than bad mechanics or poor development. In fact, they almost seemed like good reactions because the players liked what they experienced so much they angrily craved more. Which brings us to my thoughts on this. MORE! Seriously, playing this has been a blast. From discovering new enemies and points of interest, to experimenting with the different play styles of each unique character. Even though there is only one level to play as of this review and I'm only a few hours in, there's quite a bit to explore and unlock. This is on track to be an excellent title and I can't wait to see what the other worlds hold. I know the price tag may seem a bit steep for a game that is still missing the bulk of its content, but don't let that deter you from getting this fantastic gem. I know it will be more than worth it upon full release! And If you like slashing your way through ghouls, monstrous gluttons, and other wretched creatures of the night then I can't recommend this enough. Especially if you are a fan of games like Hades and Diablo. Pros: Multiple Characters to play with unique abilities         Amazing art style         Fluid combat that's well balanced          Shredding demonic night beasts          Eldritch horror tentacle abomination Boss Battle          Good upgrade and progression system          Solid replay value Cons: Having to wait for full release and more content

_childDocuments_.review: After the major update, the game became better. I am changing the negative review to positive.The developers have solved or at least smoothed out the main problems:1. There is much more armor, which greatly increases the dynamics of the game, especially for melee classes. Enemies no longer kill with one hit, if you prudently took armor (better a couple of times).2. "Inconvenient" perks can now be easily rerolled using a new mechanic - stars. Stars are given in rewards in large numbers, at least 3, so there are always enough of them.3. The store itself has become more interesting due to the fact that now, in addition to improving perks, they offer not just "+5% damage", but something more substantial.4. It has become more interesting to play in co-op (we played in pairs). Due to the scaling of monster characteristics, it is better to stick together, focusing on the same group of enemies. It will be more effective.Of the obvious "minuses" so far I have only noticed a sharp difficulty curve at the 3rd stage, compared to the first two. In fact, this can be solved with good builds and armor (I got up to 65% resistance by the end of the game). So this is not really a minus. I played with a hat, which was previously called very thin and quickly dying in reviews.THANKS to the development team! :)

_childDocuments_.review: One important thing first: Keep in mind this game is (VERY) early access with limited content right now (just one chapter with a seeded/randomized map, several heroes (4 from the start and 2 more are unlocked when completing the chapter with different heroes) and several difficulties (unlocked one by one when completing the chapter). No bugs or crashes, just limited content at the moment.Anyways - I really like this game. All heroes feel really different, the combat feels good (at least with the heroes I played so far), the sound is really good, graphics are cartoonish (Torchlight comes to mind) but I like them.What is this game about (so far):It's a rogue lite action adventure(?). You play one of different heroes (co-op possible, but I'm more of a solo gamer), like Scarlet (which turns into the Wolf (with total different skills and playstyle) at night), Aladin, Beowulf and more to come. All with different playstyle. All heroes have fixed skills and there are no items. Since it's a rogue lite intented for mastering your skills this is to be expected.Maps are seeded/randomized with day/night cycle and you have only some few days to level up (each level up gives an unlocked/randomized selection of upgrades for your skills) until time runs out - when this happens it's time to fight the chapter boss. (The last seconds are very nice sound and graphics wise) You have some different options (and can't do all of them) like doing a quest, searching for chests (containing a selection of skill upgrades), fighting a miniboss (beating him reduces the health of the final boss) - and slaying tons of monsters on the way. You goal (or mine at least) is to get as much upgrades as possible while also reaching level 5 (maximum level at the moment). After you beat the chapter (or die) your played heroe gets XP and might level up (which unlocks upgrades).Speaking about dying: you have multiple lifes - so it's not game over after one death. But the lifes are shared in co-op and you have less and less of them with increasing difficulty levels.Only thing I would complain about is the minimap - it's very hard to spot where you are EXACTLY and what is a passage and what is blocked - since it's timed content this sometimes really sucks. Also the "house" quest is really difficult to complete in time (at least for me) because you need too much stone/wood which is pretty impossible to complete. (You can win anyway when you collect just enough and fight the monsters in a clever way)Is it a game where you can spend dozens of hours RIGHT NOW? Probably not.Is it fun? YesHas it potential? Definitely Looking forward for the next content - roadmap is public and shown at the store page.Update: Coming back after half a year: 2 new Heroes and they are (again) both very fun and different. The only concern I have about the game is maybe the long term replayability. We are now at 2 chapters and both are pretty much the same with a different theme. There are 2 more chapters to come and a story update. So it looks like it's more about increasing difficulty levels and the heroes. But on the other hand - we are talking about a 20eur game here.

_childDocuments_.review: In the early access with 2 of the 3 stages planned for release, Ravenswatch is a very promising multiplayer roguelike. Each of the 8 characters (with 2 more planned for the full release) play uniquely from one another, and as you dedicate play time to a single character you unlock more talents for them to create new builds in your next run. The time based system, paired with a map that is perfectly just too large to explore all of in 20 minutes, means players have to make choices on what activities they will participate in before they are forced to face the boss of the stage. Changing the gameplay loop from "skip content to get to the end as fast as possible" to "get as much content done in the time that I have" is a refreshing change from other roguelikes with a timer system, like the time trial doors in Dead Cells or the tight schedule modifier in Hades. I'm hoping in the future to see more changes to the difficulty system, and possibly a way to reward future runs based on your performance in previous runs. Even in early access, I recommend giving the game a try if you enjoyed Hades or Curse of the Dead Gods, as Ravenswatch plays very similar to the two.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS REVIEW IS TO COUNTER THE NEGATIVESFirst of all. READ the "why early access?" Then place your judgement.You know it's one Chapter, containing one boss being a rough 30min run. Yet you still buy the game only to give it a negative review?? You should only blame yourself being impatient still buying the game cause you couldn't wait yet you're saying how the devs should just wait until full release or until there's more content before making it early access. It's here at this stage for a reason. For US who actually appreciate the game and want to help shape the game into something beautiful. The negative reviews is only hurting the game even more. It's better off not leaving a review at all. And with the mixed review there's still a solid 3k+ people actively playing and that means something.Okay enough of that. Lets talk about gameplay. You start off picking from 4 characters the other 2 will be unlocked after a run. Aladdin first then Melusine. You start off on Normal Difficulty. It gets higher up to nightmare 9 after a completed Run. Once you're in you get a free upgrade towards your abilities. Upon spawning there'll be Sandman who you can use currency to get buffs or upgrade your abilities which comes from the Crystals you break out on the field. You'll occasionally see enemies you can kill for Xp to level up and upgrade your Abilities. Being Level 5 the max and that's when you'll get your ultimate. All Interactions require that you kill enemies that are within range so dont think you can go around getting upgrades or healing with a bunch of mobs around. There's also side quests you can do for some solid upgrades if you can complete it. A tip on that. IF you run into the Collect Wood/Stone side quest LOOK around first and find the mine, preferably TWO for Stone to make it easier when playing SOLO. For Wood you can just kill the TREE enemies for wood if you can't find any around on the floor. Last on the map you can find a Tumor that you can engage and do the challenge in order to reduce the bosses health by 20% if you want to make it a bit easier on your end.What I spend my time doing? I'll run around looking for points of interest so I can kill AND take care of objectives to get upgrades or complete quests. While looking for currency for Sandman so I can teleport back to upgrade my skills. After I heat at LEAST level 3 I'll do the Side quest, that way I'm relatively strong enough to defend the house no problem. After that I'll practically do what I first was doing and depending on Time I'll Then take out a Tumor and by the time I'm finished I'll probably have time for one more Objective then I Should already be at Max Level and it's boss time. And based on how I do it's GG. Run Successful. Back to doing it again With either the same or different character and it's still fun so if you like this then you'll have no problem whatsoever. Also I encountered no problems playing alone.

The game is as I remember:- Style, look, and feel are great.- Game balance is bad.I really want to enjoy this game, but the dev seems to be locked in some masochists-only mindset, and prefers to nerf nerf nerf the player in a singleplayer PvE game (I refuse to try multiplayer again). This nerfed nerfed nerfed my enjoyment. No, I don't have any difficulty beating the game. It just isn't rewarding. If I wanted to do a painful, unrewarding grind, I'd just get a soul-crushing job instead.Original review:Trash.Bought with the idea to play with a friend.Played solo, leveling up for the second ultimate ability. The grind was boring, but bearable.And then finally I got the chance to play with my friend  -  and I was so sorely disappointed. The enemies have more HP when playing with more people. So. Lazy. In 2023, a developer has no other options than to just give enemies more HP instead of other difficulty options. Changed my whole game experience. Now enemies are just damage sponges. I get adding more HP to the final boss, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, every enemy is now a snooze fest when I have to stand 2x the time in front of them to kill them.What is even the point? The multiplayer feels bad, slow, and pointless.I wish I could refund, as after ONE multiplayer session it's clear I won't play this ever again. Shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: A very fresh take on the roguelike.I wish diablo 4 was more like this, each encounter feels meaningful and the controls are spot on. Every skill you wield in your arsenal has synergies with the other skills and defines the patterns of your attack.The upgrades and unlocks you get are meaningful and impactfull, no filler material or useless progression.On the steamdeck there are currently still some minor issues (some visual effects aren't always visible etc.) but it is fully working and a blast to play.Highly recommend it, its a lot of fun and if you like challenging games with meaningful progression, it is a fantastic enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, a little easy, about 7 hours to 100% the game (beat nightmare 9) until they come out with the new chapter. Runs become quite similar once you figure out the game play loop, hopefully that will change with more variety though, the core mechanics are solid though and you can tell it took a lot of work.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: I need to put this review out there, just to try to counter the sheer amount of dumb-founding takes in some of the negative reviews.The game has great potential. You can see it from the second you start playing. It has an amazing atmosphere, it has fun and tight combat and the rogue-like elements are fun. What is already there is good. This title is in early access, of course there is less content. That is what you are signing up for when you buy an early access game. The developers are already working on the second chapter (a second map) which will come in "Spring" (i.e. very soon). When you pay those "20 bucks" you are buying the whole game, NOT just what is currently there, so people giving this a negative review "because there isn't enough content" is baffling to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most instantly addicting game I've played in a long time.Bear in mind it's early access but it's a lot of fun and the devs are constantly updating it. The gameplay loop of murder-hoboing your way across a grim fairytale land really works for me. I should get therapy, but until then, this game will have to do.A thing that's a triumph with this kind of game is that a) there's a hero for everyone b) the heroes don't suck c) there are heroes you'll like more due to your play style but that doesn't make them OP. And what's not to like about a Little Red Riding Hood who turns into a frickin' werewolf?!About the only negative aspect I can think of at the moment (early access!) is the netcode. If someone's at the end of 56k dial-up you'll feel it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: The combat doesn't feel nearly as good as the devs' last game, Curse of the Dead Gods. It's got very MOBA-like abilities and hit feedback which doesn't come off very satisfying with the Risk of Rain-style stage progression and enemy layouts. There's only one area in the game so far and there's barely enough time for you to level up to your Ult before the bossfight.The art style and music are fantastic as usual from the studio, very striking comic book colors and great menacing violin tracks. I like the inclusion of voice lines and NPC's with dialogue, gives the game some personality that I think Dead Gods really lacked.Not gonna refund it yet since it could potentially turn out more fun as it goes through Early Access, but the core game feel so far is a bit disappointing and currently there's about as much content in here as a Warcraft 3 or Dota 2 custom map.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing. Action roguelike with multiplayer, and it's extremely fun to play. Quite a few different classes, all have different roguelike-style upgrades to choose from on level-up, so it's always a different experience. I can't believe I waited until full release to play this, but it's a masterpiece now. HIGHLY recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: It is alright with game play, and you should always play it alone.Multiplayer is utter pile of crap. It is like game from 1999. You cannot see ping to other players, there is not host session swap, meaning once host leaves the game is gone. Game has like 3 stages that can take each up to 20ish minutes, so if host loses connection near end, bye bye. All random hosts are crap, because the moment they die they will leave. Other players cannot join your session in progress. You cannot see lobbies, you are just aware you have some sessions for each difficulty. You cannot pre-select your hero then join a session, you will join sessions with double heroes and it is first come first ready.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: I had about 150hrs during early access and already 200 in total after the relase.this game provides a really fresh take on roguelikes. It focuses more on getting new runs with multiple characters to see & try new builds rather than on a long and tiring progression path. It has a very refreshing art-style and enjoyable music. It is extremely fun in Multiplayer.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Geez solo player here and damn this was painful. In terms of the visuals they are stunning, lovely artwork, interesting enemy design and the voice acting work is very good indeed. However those are the only positives I really have. Combat is underwhelming and clunky with certain characters and enemies are incredibly tanky, unlike other games where you take less damage and the enemies take more because they outnumber you with this it's equal if not outbalanced in the enemies favour, am I expecting to kill enemies in a single hit? Absolutely not but im also not expecting to put next weeks plans on halt when I start a combat encounter. Another problem is the unneeded time restraint which just adds unneeded rush to an already unforgiving combat system and like I said at the start im a solo player now I can't speak for multiplayer obviously but if you're playing solo don't bother it is not balanced in solo and very single player unfriendly. First ever review and that's because this is genuinely a roller coaster of a game so go in at your own judgement.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: 3 Open maps, you weren't kidding.  One hour playthrough and you've seen everything. (Unless to do the same hour on a different character, to be fair, but come on.) That's it! Wow!  $25.  There are definitely games like this that offer more for the price or less.  I'm disappointed that release is one hour playthrough and that's it!  I guess the developers just wanted to be done with it or something, roadmap is extremely disappointing with no hope of actual things to go experience.  I was just recommending it to someone, then realized that I can't, actually, and it made me frustrated enough to come write this review.Not worth the money as much as much as it pains me to say.  Great character/build designs though, genius even, just so little content to play with them in.Update: Embarrassing new statistics released claiming 13 million "unique runs" but the same statistics show that characters are picking the same talents 80% of the time. No new levels planned. Tragic.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: I dont care for this game very much but full disclosure: i suck at it and have yet to beat the normal mode after about ten hours of gameplay.  I find it punishing, frankly cheap and frustrating.  The game makes me feel dumb.  Maybe I am but I've played seemingly more comlex games with ease so something just isn't working with me here.That said, what is presented with Ravenswatch is a very original product.  You get your money's worth in the sense that it's clearly $20 worth of work thus far.  I am not good at the game so I've gotten around 10 hours of gameplay to date without beating it.  Sorry but as a kid in the arcade days if you get 2 bucks an hour of video gaming thats a fair deal.  If you go back for 9 more of those hours...there must have been something that compelled you.The game makes me feel dumb. Maybe I am but I dont care for that feeling thus I dont care for the game any longer.  So why did I come back? I dont know.  I think it's just it's original spirit and how it's quite unlike anything else I've played.  It evokes memories of games I've played but doesnt rip off any one of them.  I could have stopped after hour two and gotten a refund but I dont like doing that to an early access project. To me, unless they outright scammed me, I chose to take that risk and support their project and all told, to me, $20 to an artist presenting something original isn't a whole lot to ask.  Even if I never enjoy another second of this game, and I likely will someday, I STILL dont mind supporting this project because it's something different.  Something that tries to break outside of the norm.  Something that stands out. I didn't see it at first but I see it now.I cant say I personally love it, but I see why others do and can step aside and objectively recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Let me comment on some of the 'reviews' (with 30 minutes playtime etc.) first:Obviously, many people do not understand the concept behind an early access. With that out of the way:The heroes are pretty unique and fun to play. I like it how the game transfers basic skills you might know from other games (like a simple ranged attack for example) into the theme of folklore legends. Attacks/skills have good feedback and upgrading them really feels like upgrades. Ravenswatch is not always clear with the abilities though - I wish the devs would add detailed tooltips: game keeps you guessing sometimes.Fighting feels great and is somewhat challenging. Killing a group, taking out a strong enemy, getting upgrades: that's being commented with voicelines, and thank god no cheesy ones. Sound is good, music fits the action quite well. The graphics are decent, ultra wide support, runs smooth, no visual bugs so far.I like the events you encounter, like time limited quests. Mind you some of them require a group due to the time limit.The final boss isn't too hard, if you figure out how to fight him - I think he should be more of a challenge.I do not know, how co-op plays - might try that later.Keep in mind: that's just a 1st impression after 3 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: I've played quite a bit, had input into the beta that got addressed, and I can safely say that the negative comments of difficulty and scaling? Since the last dev update have been addressed. The game is not easy, as I would hope not. As it scales, it gets increasingly difficult for a multitude of reasons. The descriptions for each scale really lend a lot of expectations, which is ideal when progressing through, collecting new skills, and honing your own personal play style. The game is set in a wonderful world known as Reverie, a dream world where the Sandman is your shopkeep, and characters from the fairy tales and stories of past come to life. The common enemy, the corruption in the form of Nightmares, are what is causing the issues, your job is to defend your home, Reverie. There is still much planned, and this development team cares deeply about their game. They constantly communicate through steam, discord, and community updates for how things are progressing. I have nothing but respect for this team bringing us a wonderful game, and sharing it with the world. If you've been on the fence about trying the game, and want to wait? Go ahead. The game will cost more at launch, but when it does, it will be worth it. Pick it up now and get hooked? Play with friends? Explore the setting, the world, and the gameplay loop, and you won't be disappointed. The replayability is high, and the level of satisfaction is also there. More end game is going to be added, so if you find yourself at a stopping point, that's going to be addressed as well. Cannot recommend enough for lovers of rogue-likes, RTS, and MOBA's alike. It's fun and challenging, thats what games should be like, and I appreciate it for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: the game is good but the multiplayer part sucks cause it has to be a friend. need to make it so you can either quick-match or open servers list or something. hope they do something for the multiplayer aspect cause it would be a pretty dope game is they did that. so only buy if you going to do solo or if you have a friend to play with otherwise i wouldn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of Ravenswatch is great. It's execution is still Early Access levels. I shall build and add to this review the more I play.- There is NO text Chat.- NOT even Emotes.- Recent Players list DOES NOT WORK.- Client side hosting WITHOUT host migration. (If the host leaves, y'all are kicked. Game's over)- Since games go sequentially it is SUCH a time commitment that people often leave after you win the second boss. ie. You've been playing for 45 minutes already.- Why is the person with  Deaths highlighted on the end screen? It should obviously be the one with the least.- You can't do anything while searching for a game. It cancels the matchmaking.- Playing on ultrawide 100% render scale yet the main menu's red tab icons are low resolution , and 3D characters are too.- Content is present but lacks incentives. Reward players for playing different characters, modifiers, and challenges.- Have a rolling "Challenge of the Day" / Daily Quests. Quests that everyone shares so that it doesn't dilute matchmaking pools.- Custom modes are neat and underused.- Display all the achievements in The Compendium. Creating more incentives to play the game.- Expand on the endscreen and have fun titles like "Elite Killer" (most damage to elites) "Trash Clearer" (killed most normal enemies) "Globe Gobbler" (collected most health globes) "Path Finder" (uncovered most map %) etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Me and my friends have been looking for a good Action Roguelike that we can all play togethere and this really scratched the itch! Made by the Developers who made Curse of the Dead Gods. This game follows a familiar formula that delivers! With the state of the current game and more to still to come! I have high expectations while I continue to enjoy this game. It is a must have!
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Played some before the release and already knew what kind of reviews game will sadly get after seeing "Currently available content is over" window after killing first boss not even one hour in.But there are 6 characters to try and maybe even to spend time to git gud with, upgrades for those characters (some of which you need to unlock first), different difficulties - usual Roguelite stuff that will increase your playtime a lot if you are into that kind of games. Tried all characters and while I'm on difficulty level 7 currently (apparently 9 is the max?) I had no problems doing stuff solo, even though some characters seem like a better fit for co-op environment it's still fun to play them, albeit more challenging. Quest with resource collection doesn't require you to collect all 26 pieces, you can return with less, goal is to defend the house, which is of course easier with more resources, but still possible with less.Was enjoying Hades as much on Early Access EGS release when only Meg and Hydra were available (maybe a bit longer run than here right now) so I will still recommend it, just calculate if it's in your price/content ratio range considering Roguelite nature of the game, otherwise wait for more updates with content. Everything else in this game is really solid already.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay/Mechanics: 10/10 tight, responsive and fun. creative and skill based. Looks, animations, readability: 10/10 art style, all characters and voice are polishedQuality for price atm way better than normal imo, if quality persists till after EA game will be standout winner, probably goty.Recommend now if your the type to beat all 10 difficulties with all characters, try diff builds and get all unlocks/play for fun.Else keep an eye for when game has more content atm only one map/boss, average winning run ~25 mins but expect failuresgg
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review: The game is clunky.The game is unintuitive.The game is CLUNKY.The movements feel sluggish. The dodge reset timing feels off.The worldbuilding is lazy - I have no idea why should I care about what's happening, and I've already unlocked a character. The intro is crypticly boring, and it doesn't help that the story seems to be locked behind character progressions. This ain't Dark Souls, I'm not gonna go out of my way to figure out what's happening in the story if the gameplay doesn't hook me first. And it doesn't hook me at all, so at least give me story! Tutorials/tooltips are absolute garbage - your level-ups give you upgrades to your SPECIAL, DEFENSE, and such, but you have all of them from the start, and you have no idea what's what, unless you specifically look for it. After a couple of runs I still confuse what's POWER, and what's SPECIAL on a same character, and I play a lot of more complicated games on a regular. It's just bad UX.Some abilities move you or hit in the direction of the cursor, some where your character faces - no info which is which, and in case of Scarlet, for example - it feels incredibly inconsistent, like with her grenade.There are exactly two positives about this game - the music and that it has ravens in it.I wouldn't have bought it if it was in this state as a 1.0 release.P.S. Ah, forgot the worst part. The minimap and the map are ABYSMALLY bad. The exploration of this mud-stained nothingness is boring and tedious. Also it is infuriating how bad the Werewolf form of Scarlet feels to play. I'm done. This game's garbage.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

_childDocuments_.review:
Ravenswatch is a top-down roguelike action game that combines intense real-time combat with deep gameplay and high replay value.

After the success of Curse of the Dead Gods, Passtech returns with a new formula and game experience that can be played solo or with up to four players in co-op.

To defeat the Nightmare and reach the final chapter, you will need a strong build, focus and excellent teamwork. Increase your fighting power in battles then face the level boss when you feel ready... or when you no longer have a choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Ravenswatch

name: Islands of Insight
detailed_description: DELUXE EDITION For Seekers keen to expand their horizons, the Islands of Insight Deluxe Edition bears a trove of exclusive gifts designed to celebrate the beauty of the islands. Don rare creations left behind by the ancients with the Sterling Cosmetic Set and download exclusive backgrounds for Desktop and Mobile. Islands of Insight Deluxe Edition includes: • Standard Game • Premium Cosmetic Set (Includes 2 sets of Costumes, Gloves, Headpieces, Wings and Trails) • Desktop & Mobile Wallpapers WISHLIST NOW About the Game Welcome to Islands of Insight: a sublime puzzle game set in a fantasy realm of ancient wonders and natural beauty. Brimming with mysterious puzzles to solve, secrets to uncover, and vibrant landscapes to explore, this peaceful world of floating islands is the perfect place to unwind. Embark on a puzzle adventure of your choice, all at your own pace. Seek out and solve an unparalleled collection of over 10,000 puzzles divided across 24 puzzle types. Every corner of the world holds a new eureka moment for you to discover. From enigmas of perspective to logic problems, environmental challenges and more, the puzzles you’ll encounter vary in difficulty and have been crafted by some of the best minds in puzzle design to create an engaging experience for both newcomers and seasoned puzzle fans. Freely explore the main island’s expansive open world where most of the puzzles and secrets are found. Wander the vibrant landscapes and architecture of its 5 distinct biomes or spread your wings to glide above them. Navigate the environment’s verticality and take your game to new heights. Unlock puzzle types and new areas in the campaign by completing 20+ Enclaves housing curated puzzle challenges. Go where you want. Solve what you want. The only path here is the one you make. ‎‎‏‏‎ Play as a Seeker on a peaceful journey rich in exploration and puzzle-solving. Embark on the Path of Discovery and let your curiosity guide you through a breathtaking open world where the answer is always in sight. Customize your character. Increase your puzzle masteries to level them up while earning sparks to unlock new abilities. Complete daily quests. With puzzles that refresh over time, a new discovery awaits with every visit to the islands. Age restrictions may apply to access this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like puzzle platformers, open world game play and hidden lore, then you may just find yourself loving this game as it's a beautifully crafted open world with inspiration taken from all around the world, as you will find everything from the Great Pyramids of Giza to Chinese temples with the Foo Lions in front. And with the offline mode coming in a few short weeks as of writing, if you don't like MMOs you can simply buy it now and wait to play once it's out.[Edited as I saw a typo.]
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: To quote a review out of many similar ones:In my case, even games such as Cyberpunk played on maximum settings had not resulted in my computer becoming a heating brick. Island of Insight does. Some more… concerned voices say  crypto-mining malware is involved, but the more plausible explanation is that the game is simply horribly unoptimised.As for the puzzles, they are disappointingly monotonous, though on other hand, pleasantly challenging and yielding the much craved dopamine rush upon completion. I find it refreshing to see a game like this aside hundreds upon hundreds of FPS titles. A shame it is superficial and potentially hazardous to run.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: This game is weird. A puzzle game, but MMO. It doesn't make sense, nor will I defend the lack of social features.But ignoring the MMO part, it's the only game in the world that scratches a very specific itch I didn't know I had: a stunning open world littered with puzzles to solve. Like The Witness, but with a main questline and a map, so you don't get lost or do puzzles out of order.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: The online mode doesn't function and load times and optimization for the game/fps is terrible.Additionally there are only a handful of puzzle types, many of which are just "click here"s or "walk here"s .Furthermore you cannot reset your online progress without going to their official website and requesting it personally instead of other games that allow you to do it by yourself.While the game's online did function at launch, it has since become unplayable, pretty much requiring the offline mode that they only just now released (as you previously HAD to play online, despite the game logically having all resources you'd need to play being local, as other players are not required, much less even interact, with the gameplay cycle.)
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute paradise playground for puzzle lovers! Massive and gorgeous open world that's super fun to explore and find all different kinds of puzzles accompanied by soothing and meditative music! Great range of difficulty for puzzles, too!I see no problem with it being online like other reviews mention. Definitely doesn't kill or detract at all from the game. It's nice to occasionally come across other players and do a little bit of emoting with them! Or to see someone still working on a puzzle after you breeze through it! XD So what if you can't solve puzzles with other players Haven't really come across any major problem glitches. Very rarely a few small blips but never anything worth really mentioning that will prevent you from playing the game at all.There's so much content in this game that for even $30 it's a steal! So easy to get lost in this game only to realize 6+ hours have passed already!If you love puzzles, you'll definitely love this game! An absolute hot recommend! A new favorite puzzle game of mine for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: After 3 hours, I get it and I'm bored!  There is a saying "Quality over Quantity" - The Quantity of puzzles means unfortunately in my opinion far too many are dull, and repetitive.  The world concept in nice, but looks like it may have been rushed or assets where just randomly placed all over the place, with foliage clipping through some assets. and odd gaps or holes around rock formations, where you can see rocks were separate assets placed together.  Smaller slightly more refined islands which you could fly between may have worked better and seemed less crowded.  some puzzle also don't seem very clever, with blocks resized and wedged into the landscape or between other assets that don't seem to conform or make sense, meaning some puzzles are not solved with standard logic but more luck of exploration and spending hours just looking around at not very interesting representative assets.  The character creation seems far too basic and almost irreverent.  I really wanted to like and enjoy this game but I found my self completing puzzle felt more of a burden rather than enjoyable, and the world become boring very quickly as assets repeat and are scattered all over the place.Great Idea but I just think it missed the mark.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: Good - the puzzlesBad - it's online onlyI just want to quietly solve puzzles, absolutely not interact with people. Having an in game appearance at all is optional and something to be ignored. I'll be ignoring this game until offline mode is a thing,which is sad, the bit of it I've played was good, I just don't want to remember other people exist while I solve puzzles. I want to actually immerse and not feel like I have to be in any way sociable.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: Let's keep this simple. Super fun puzzle game, the base game is about 20 something type of puzzles that you encounter in the open-world. Within those types, you also get some basic variations. The main idea is simple, you explore a world in which puzzles are everywhere. While exploring you discover some areas or puzzles cannot be solve because you need to move the main storyline forward for that to occur. As you unlock those new puzzles types and areas, you learn a bit more about the lore.As a puzzle game, highly recommended, super fun and the puzzles are really well balanced. I'm really not sure about the multiplayer or cosmetics etc... within this game. I feel this was an afterthought or something they didn't have time to complete before release. The thing is while it is lacklusting on the coop/multiplayer area, it doesn't remove anything from the core game itself, so I won't consider negative, but maybe a missed opportunity to even better game.All in all well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: This game offers a delightful puzzle-solving experience with a variety of unique and handcrafted puzzles that keep the dopamine flowing. The massive central area, filled with different puzzle types that reset periodically, and the numerous “Enclaves” or floating islands, each focusing on specific puzzle types, provide a perfect balance for both casual and completionist players.The story may not be compelling, but it’s optional, so you can focus solely on the puzzles if you prefer. The game stands out as one of the few open-world experiences that feels vibrant and engaging, instead of empty and lifeless, offering constant stimulation and variety.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most impressive games I've ever played.  Teaching how to teach.  They took a puzzle game integrated so many different types of puzzles (everything from visual to exploration puzzles).  Brought a social aspect to it.  Although I strongly wish I could chat, but obviously some people would cheat.  I think we should let the cheaters cheat and understand them better.  Brought a leveling system with talents and skills.  The skins are a combination of skill and bought.  They turned a puzzle game into a reflection of people.  I've barely gotten started but I'm blown away.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good puzzle game. The game can be played both in first person and third person view. One downside is the bad graphical optimisation but on the other hand, game world is breathtakingly beautiful. Interactivity with the UI shows that it is an indie project (climbing is a bit frustrating as our character doesn't try to grab onto stone ledges while jumping). Puzzles are amazing and devs have actually made use of open world in some of the puzzle structures.Overall, the game is very addictive.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this game after watching a VoD of someone’s stream of it (and cause it’s currently £15 on Steam) who described it as “an open world of puzzles scattered everywhere with live service elements” which is pretty on point really. The main part of the game is a black & white grid puzzle, where the rules change depending on the area. Sometimes you can’t do certain shapes, or you need to have a certain number of bricks in the number’s colour, or the block is equal to a music sound. A good mix. But there’s also loads of environmental puzzles about the world too. Finding hidden arches & rings, making connections of blocks with the same symbols, markings that you have to stand at certain angles to collect. Reminds me of the alt ending to The Witness and it scratches a really nice itch in my brain, just running around pointing at puzzles and solving them.My only issue currently is that some times the game server can get a bit too busy and then keeps kicking me out without any warning or messages saying why. I originally thought "Maybe it’s the game telling me “you’re solving too many puzzles sir!” haha" but after being kicked off whiles I was just stood still and checking the game map, the silly thought stopped. Luckily, the devs have made an annoucement about an offline mode, which might help with this issue
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: Will recommend the game as the puzzles are quite good, and the world is ok. I reveived the game for free, but my only grip with the game is, why does it need to be an MMO? Connection is always unstable for me, and some puzzles are really hard with the lag. You really should add a Single Player option

_childDocuments_.review: Expansive, beautifully crafted open world islands of discovery filled with a wide variety of individual puzzles. The only real issues with this game that I have encountered so far are related to connecting to a server. At times it takes a number of attempts, waiting through the crash, UE5 error reporting, and relaunching before you can join and play. Also, quite often, once you do join not all of the assets have fully loaded and you can not interact with them initially. On occasion, you might suddenly get warped back to a previous location you were at, while the server tries to synchronize your location in the environment.These are annoyances, but once you do get in, the game is worth the wait. And I do have to admit that I struggle with some of the later logic puzzles that you encounter, because I do not quite follow their logic. Fortunately, you can always work around those puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Second update 15th November 2024:This is really not meant to sound mean, but:On October 30th the game went permanently offline and now the game is better than ever.The performance, while still not impressive, is much better. And the stuttering is also massively improved.---Original Review 13th March 2024Pro:+ Really good puzzles+ Huge and beautiful world+ Devs have added more puzzles and improved existing onesCon:- Always online / no offline mode- Pretty bad performance / visuals ratio- Sometimes stutter and rubberbanding -> Makes challenges based on speed and/or precision frustrating- Bugs that reset progress, or just reset the unlocks (meaning the puzzles are solved, but not counted as such) making it frustrating to 100% challenges and areas.Neutral:- Story is presented in a non linear way with mostly unvoiced single text lines. (Like reading a book out of order one line at a time)- Soundtrack isn't bad, but the humongous scope of the game manages to make it feel repetitive- The insane amount of puzzles makes many of them feel samey- Most of the puzzles are on a timed rotation, since the game cannot load all of them. _childDocuments_.review: I expect I probably have more hours in this game than most reviewers which should give my words some weight and I intend to keep it quite fair. $30 is quite high for a puzzle game and Island's of Insight was quite ambitious. Multiplayer is a feature that shouldn't be implemented if it doesn't enhance the end product and not a single puzzle in this game required two people. As of two days ago multiplayer was removed and all save-data for those who did not log-on between Sept. 30th, 2024 and Oct. 30th, 2024 has been deleted. As a result of this many reviews will be understandably upset as they lost their entire save. I am not as I previously completed 100% of mainline content(all enclaves, secrets, challenges, monoliths, etc.) This game has a massive puzzle count and truly solving all of them without assistance is a massive undertaking, with that said puzzle types can become stale and you may not want to complete many of the easier puzzles of a certain type after trying out the toughest. If you play through slowly over the course of years this game will be fantastic to revisit and slowly master. If you tend to get absorbed into a game and dump dozens of hours within a month you will get bored quite quickly and never touch 95% of the games 10,000 puzzles the game claims to offer. This game is truly one of a kind but the high graphical demands and failed multiplayer have tainted my perception of the game. I would recommend this over the Witness for example but even a simple puzzle game like "A Good Snowman Is Hard to Build" might be a better experience, despite having far less content. This game has good puzzles but you need to find them, some players may enjoy this others may view most of the game play as busywork.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably the most addicting puzzle game I have ever played. The puzzles themselves are nothing special so far. So what's the idea here?1. The world is big and there is puzzles EVERYWHERE. All of them are optional, all of them reward you with metaprogression. You feel good for A: finding the puzzle, B: solving the puzzle, C: unlocking upgrades and new areas. Being stuck never happens because it never feels bad to give up.2. The variety in types of puzzles gives a work/play duality that allows for not needing breaks. In most puzzle games you feel great after solving something hard but then you need a break. In this game, the game is also the break. Go hike up a mountain or do some platforming puzzles to take a break from the logic grids.3. The world looks good, exploring is exciting. The game has a bit of a zelda feel why not solving the puzzles. I like how some of the enclaves (subworlds) feel like zelda temples, you might need to navigate a maze or think outside the box to reach some places... and finding them rewards you with a puzzle!

_childDocuments_.review: 20h (+13h Demo)I've never been interested in puzzle games, as they're usually too quick and too expensive for the time it takes to complete them.But when I was recommended Islands of Insight Demo during the Steam Next Fest by a friend, the game immediately hooked me. You just land in the middle of this big open world, without any loading screens and you're surrounded by dozens of puzzles.You can go wherever you want, choose which puzzles you want to do and just explore the beautiful world.No cooldowns, no daily limits, no fall damage and if you get stuck, just move on to the next puzzle and come back later.I don't understand all this whining about multiplayer/co-op...Yes, you can't solve puzzles "directly" with a friend, but on the other hand you can. You go off together and solve the same puzzles in the group at the same time, if you get stuck you can either help each other with markers or via Discord & co. Nowadays you are usually somewhere in a 3rd party app to communicate with friends.Of course I would be happy if later in the game there are puzzles that you can/must solve together or maybe you can play against each other for time or something.The only thing I've noticed so far after 20 hours is that some puzzles are repetitive or relatively similar if you solve a lot of them in one area over a period of days. Also that the quests send you directly from one region to the next, which again contributes to the point of how "free" you are. You can just go to the next region without having to fulfill any requirements (like solve X puzzles of this type and X puzzles of the others to unlock the next region)All in all, I am very happy with the game and recommend it to any puzzle enthusiast. You can spend at least 100h+ here and as a completionist if not 3 times as much time.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the gameplay is fun, the puzzles are pretty good.But I just can't recommend this game as is with the online component. It takes almost 5 minutes to load into the game. So either wait for it to die entirely or for them to just remove this 'feature' but as is, it's a headache to actually launch the game. And sometimes the servers go down, which would be more forgivable it had Palworld tier success (though it is at it's core just a single player game, so it's still not great) but according to steamdb there's only around 1k concurrent players. _childDocuments_.review: I am genuinely having a good time with this game, even 90 hours in.People are disappointed or curious on why the game is multiplayer when there's no multiplayer puzzles or benefits. Josh Strife Hayes I believe once said, regarding the majority of players treating an MMO like a single player game, "playing the game alone, together" or something to that effect. This game is that statement taken literally.Being able to see other people going about their puzzle business has a sort of charm in itself, and it's not necessary, but it's nice. I'd love multiplayer puzzles, but that is not what this game is.There's a few bugs, nothing game breaking so far for me. Fast traveling failing and having the game lock up is annoying, but alt+f4 and a relaunch fixes that quickly.The demo version is very solid, and you'll easily be able to decide if you'll enjoy the game or not from it. Give it a shot, there's nothing to lose.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't think the quantity of puzzles dilutes quality here - this is a passion project, that doesn't hit every mark, but rarely delivers a poorly considered puzzle.  Even when they're easy, they're a rush to blitz through, which I've found to be usually satisfying.  The pacing here is great.  You'll feel like an idiot; you'll feel like a genius.Things I don't like - some of the puzzles are just misses for me - basically anything that is more of a "guess what I was thinking" puzzle than reaching a logical conclusion.  Some of the mysteries are halfway bad by that definition, and several other classes of puzzle.  But guess what - you can usually just skip classes of puzzle you have a distaste for. And when they are part of a "main" (i.e. mirabilis) objective/bonus, they're usually made with more care as to be enjoyable - with the notable exception of late-game music puzzles on the mosaic/music island which I feel were made by an imagination-less robot who doesn't understand what people that enjoy music could possibly be enjoying.Overall, if you know you like a few of the 24 puzzle classes this game offers, especially logic grids, you'll like this game.  It's exceptionally good content and, as I'm doing an end-game retrospective/revisit, it really has been a fantastic ride.  Thanks to the devs for giving the focus on quality puzzles, and leaving less puzzle-lover-centric cares (yes, like performance and glitches) their appropriate role in the back seat.  Not that it couldn't have been better, but you made something truly special here, and I loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have around 18 hours in the game, plus another 12 in the demo, and so far I am absolutely loving the game.It's a lot for everyone. Especially if you're into exploring, finding hidden stuff, platforming and logic puzzles. It's so many types of puzzles that I still find all new puzzle types I haven't seen before 18 hours into the game.The world looks beautiful.What's worth noticing is that this game, even though it's an MMO, is not really a multiplayer game. So far. I have yet to encounter anything that needs to be done with others. So I can see why it's a dealbreaker for some, since you can't play it offline. But then again: it's a big world, and I do like the fact that it feels populated.If you played the demo, and you're concerned about rubber banding: I haven't encountered it once after the release.Big thumbs up!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving it so far, and will fill in this review more later, but I want to throw out that this game REALLY needs a single player mode. I don't mind so much being in a world with others, except that when one of the "puzzles" is chasing a squirrelly glowing orb around the map, it's infuriating when server lag decides the client needs to glitch you back 20 yards and facing the wrong direction, for minutes at a time. _childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It looks beautiful, the riddles go all the way from super easy to super frustrating and everything in-between, so there's something for everyone here.I also feel like it shows in the programming that the game was made by very intelligent people who love logic puzzles because I haven't found any major bugs and even when I found bugs the game has recovery options, e.g. there's the "I'm stuck" option that teleports you to a safe place from which you can continue to play, and if you fall down quickly 3 times in a row you will respawn much higher up so that you can actually land on solid ground again.Sometimes I had to ask in the forums as to what I was supposed to do because you often don't get tutorials on how the puzzles work, and when you play in over-the-shoulder view instead of first person it'll be a lot more difficult to figure out how to solve e.g. Skydrops or light motifs. And Crystal Labyrinths are also a lot more user-friendly in first person view because you can see the walls more easily.The support is very quick and very competent to respond, which is a rarity for games of this calibre.Of course some of the puzzles are not my type, but that's to be expected when there's so many different types. Sometimes I like to just stroll around the beautiful landscape and maybe solve a logic grid or match some boxes here and there.The story is a pleasant, low-tension one, and it's more philosophical than engaging, but I think that's a good thing for a game that wants you to just enjoy it regardless of whether or not you want to progress the campaign.Daily Quests play a small role, i.e. you can do a bunch of small quests that don't time out no matter how long  you take and get a small amount of rewards in exchange, so they're really not grindy, they're just there in case you feel like doing them.
