_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the second play-test and the demo (for about 30 hours for both), just looking around the first area, trying to solve the random daily puzzles, I was overall satisfied with the quality of the puzzles in the new areas of the map and the different enclaves. Some puzzles, like the matchboxes in the 2nd area, ramp up in difficulty (in the sense of finding the angle in which to see both boxes), and the logic grids' rules and symbols you can unlock make them pretty fun and diverse (in the sense that the approach in logic changes). The hidden things (ring, archway and cube) are kinda fun on their own regard, and make you explore the map to find more puzzles, oftentimes I find the star puzzles that way, and I enjoy hunting the cubes the most from the hidden group. The perspective puzzles are also fun to find (Light Motif my beloved).A few caveats about the online: It might mostly be to avoid piracy, and people have reported rubber-banding, which I also experienced in the demo, but I've never felt it in release (AKA in my 9 hours registered at review time), so it seems the issue might be fixed or I got 3 good servers (I launched the game that many times). Also, I can take or leave the online, it doesn't really bother me, and I sometimes have fun looking at other players doing the flow orbs, and their different paths to get good times.I also stopped experiencing main menu crashes, which there were a few in the demo. I haven't found any game-breaking bugs (though I have found ways to get stuck under the map, by some obscure maneuvering) but there is always the "I'm stuck" feature to handle it, so nothing much there.The music I like, it fits with the theme of the game, and doesn't really distract from the puzzles (except maybe for some jingles in the music, which I confuse with the hidden cube jingle). Soothing, relaxing, that's all I can say, really.The visuals are really good: The structures are divided into themes, and the fantastical feeling of floating islands and the mix of a type of architecture from one country with the type of flora or natural phenomenon  from another make for some really good ideas.Overall, the price is good for the content it gives to you (I felt it was on the cheap side, so take my opinion on price with a grain of salt), and I believe the content itself offers something unique for every puzzle enjoyer.(Review subject to change on game completion, although it will most likely stay positive)

_childDocuments_.review: the game is beautiful. the puzzles are also pristine and have ten different difficulties, ranging from taking several seconds to upwards of at least an hour. there are dozens of different puzzles, and has a lot of things similar to the talos principle where there are different regions filled with puzzles. so why do i not recommend it? well...there's a few sad, unfortunate reasons why i don't recommend this game. first off, is performance. god...no matter what settings, what graphics, even if it looks like it's a 3d game from the early 2000s by the time i finish changing video settings...it runs like garbage. i suspect this is due to it loading the entire map at once, as well as the puzzles, in an inefficient manner. you'd think it would be unity engine or something with struggles with performance regardless of graphics. the second reason is online-offline play and how it works. the game used to be online where you could help others with puzzles, interact with other players, and see a live feed of what puzzles people were solving. i was looking forward to seeing how you could interact with others, but...a couple things caught my eye pretty quickly. for one, there doesn't seem to be any direct way to communicate with people besides markers and emotes. no text chat or anything. you could add people and message them that way, but that makes it harder to find help. it hits more as though it's meant to be a game you play with friends instead of playing online on the servers with random people, helping each other as you progress. the other thing i noticed was the utterly terrible server lag. i'm talking like a server that no matter where you are in the world, it just stutters and occasionally rubber-bands you all over. normally this would be fine, no big deal, but there's whole mechanics and puzzles involving movement, speed, precision...you can't do any of those when the connection is that bad. in addition to that, they have recently announced they will be shutting down online servers, encouraging players to migrate their save progress to offline play. people have frequently warned in the reviews about how bad this game is for your storage because of how often it saves, which doesn't seem to be the case anymore; they decreased the save frequency. this comes with another catch, where you can't really force it to save, and oftentimes when you load back in your progress will be weird, like negatives amounts of sparks. as far as i can find there's no manual save options.i eventually have made it to the end of the game, and honestly anticipated there would be some sort of ending towards the vault of the vitric like it implies because of how much you must do to unlock it. unfortunately, despite clearing it...there doesn't seem to be any ending. it seems to be more of a game with lore you unlock and discover, but without an actual ending. i'm unsure if i missed something or the ending never triggered(unless you have to solve every single puzzle on the island, which would take several hundred hours of playtime) but it felt underwhelming. it's what had me so eager to progress in the first place.all in all, this game isn't worth the money. it was free for a little bit, but now they returned it back to its price. it's right up your alley if you just want to go around solving various puzzles, and killing time. if you want anything else more than that, i wouldn't recommend it because it falls short of doing so.

_childDocuments_.review: What a cool concept, a puzzle MMO. Honestly surprised it hasn't been attempted before (I suppose  is the closest but that was kinda different)Very ethereal and celestial, huge open world filled to the brim with lil neat puzzles and doodads. Imagine BOTW, but you only looked for the Korok puzzles / shrines, except the puzzles were actual challenging well-made puzzles, the rewards were actually rewarding, and the shrines not instanced.Great sense of progression, very rewarding to do the puzzles since the reward is tangible gameplay upgrades like a double-jump/giga-jump, QOL tools for the puzzles, changes to puzzle rewards (giant boost if you perform a puzzle perfectly for example), etc etc., so you're actually motivated to continue doin more puzzles, instead of seeing them as chores. The puzzles themselves are really neat too, great variety (I still haven't discovered 50% of them), with each type also having lots of different spins. The world itself is gorgeous, lots of pretty visual things like fractals and waterfalls and statues -- reminds me of The Witness in the best way possible. On top of all this, there's the MMO aspect, where you unlock cosmetics and titles, and you help eachother out with hidden secrets by pointing/pinging. There's no text-chat, so it's all just emotes and pointing -- which is absolutely great imo. There are daily quests, friendlists, parties etc. Honestly I was very pleasantly surprised, the puzzles are really well-thought-out and range from easy to "ok I'll come back to this later". There are "end-game" puzzles that are really tricky, but if you're stubborn enough you can gettem done right out the gate. OR you can keep playing through the quests and unlock "insights", ie. tips from the designers, on how to solve more complex puzzles. GOOD STUFF

_childDocuments_.review: is essentially a theme park adaptation of   It’s not about the thoughtfulness and observation required in that earlier game to discern the rules—or even to see the puzzle in the first place.  It’s just not interested in being abstruse and clever in that way.  Instead, it drops you into a playground where you constantly walk up to puzzles that are clearly marked as puzzles and whose rules are simply stated, solving them to tick off a box in your massive completion checklist and earn a bit of progress towards more elaborate clothes.  Even its hidden objects and perspective puzzles are distinct forms placed upon the environment rather than being a part of it.  So  doesn't have the depth and mindfulness and philosophical care of —but I still enjoy it quite a lot.The best parts are the enclaves, themed ‘dungeons’ that exist separately from the open world and contain finite, set puzzles rather than an endless cycle of randomly spawning optional challenges.  They have a nice sense of progression and exploration to them, owing to their stable, handcrafted layouts.  I’ve been through some of these that I wish I could reset and play again.  Early on, The Empyrean Journey strings you through an ascending sequence of floating islands to get your wings and then sets you loose to chase a wandering echo through descending rings in a cinematic climax.  The Glass Temple is all about navigating a dense, illusory space as you solve mazes with multiple exits, seek out hidden archways, and work through paths that can lead you to objects tantalizingly teased on the other side of crystal walls.  These sections have unique identities that make for a refreshing change from the thick soup of the open world.  If  is a theme park, enclaves are the rides.But, even when you’ve run out of that type of content or are merely taking your time to reach the next area, you’ll find plenty to do.  There’s a wide variety ranging from strong logic boards to bite-sized spatial queries that can barely even be considered puzzles.  Certainly some of these formats are better than others, but it’s really more about the relaxing overall experience formed by the endless pull of their myriad distractions rather than the quality of any individual challenge.   is absolutely not an essential play like  is, but, if you can be satisfied with a pleasant and very moreish world that lets you lazily wander around while chaining together rapid dopamine hits of diverse intellectual intensity, then you’ll have a great time with it.  I see skydrops in my sleep.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is exactly what it says it is.  Thousands of puzzles in an open world map.  Think Talos Principle, but with a focus on many more, much smaller puzzles.  The game does a good job at both scratching that itch of "just one more" but also lets me stop whenever I want and pick up pretty much wherever I left off.  It's very consumable for short play sessions and different skill levels.One of the things that I think was undersold was progression.  Each region has a checklist of puzzles and milestones.  Each domain has core objectives and bonus objectives.  And while some puzzles rotate, many are fixed in the environment, and there's this constant sense of progression as you unlock new abilities and bonuses, new equipment, etc.There are a couple problems the developers could improve upon.* The fractal puzzles are extremely frustrating in controls, and require overly precise accuracy* Some puzzles that should have a hint system, do not.* The always-online nature of the game is novel, but it adds very little value or substance.Overall though, these faults are things that the devs can tackle with patches down the road.  Hopefully they will.  In the mean time, the core foundation of the game is there, and it's something really interesting to me.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game is fabulous.  I could hardly stop playing from when I bought it and have gone on for 10 hours. I will say that unlike the Witness, none of the puzzle types I've seen so far have been something completely unique or required too much out of the box thinking.  Instead how I'd describe the game is sort of like all the puzzle parts of things like Arkham Asylum or Zelda without any of the repetitive combat.  It also does not have a very strong story to pull you through.  You do find bit of lore or god-like beings talking to you now and then, but I have no idea what any of it has to do with the gameplay.I would recommend this game to people who like the exploring and puzzle solving aspects of action adventure games.  (with the action limited to occasional races and flight challenges).  It's for people who like to explore every bit of an area in those types of games and check off every single achievement.  Most puzzles in the main world are pretty easy to the point that eventually I get bored and just search for the hard puzzles and completing mysteries, which are like scavenger hunt riddles.  The best and hardest puzzles are once you open up the pyramid and there are some real doozies there.

_childDocuments_.review: Something like 70% easy/trivial puzzles and diversions and 30% interesting/hard/very hard puzzles, which honestly seems like about the right balance. Puzzle types are interesting, but the primary focus is definitely the Logic Grids. The grid rules are simple to understand on the surface, but the emergent complexity of larger puzzles and different combinations of rules clearly had a lot of thought put into it. I like the clever use of existing rules to implicitly create special circumstances and patterns without just adding an excessive amount of brand new rules to make it happen.The overall environment aesthetic is gorgeous. Just finding nice vistas makes it worth exploring all over the place, and then there's the puzzles tucked in every corner to make it that much more rewarding. Shoutout to the Reflections in the Sky enclave specifically; that place was a distinct pleasure to explore, fabulous environment design around the theme while also inherently sort of guiding you to the puzzles you haven't found yet just by its very nature.The multiplayer bit can be completely ignored, it's effectively a single-player game that just happens to also have other people running around it. Maybe they'll wave at you, but that's about it.Overall an excellent way to spend your free time, though obviously it's not gonna be everybody's cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: This game activates a "flow state" more than any other game I have ever played; it seems to have been made for exactly me specifically. Whenever I log on, hours magically seem to fly by.If you are the target audience for this game, you will feel the same way. Islands of Insight is a predictable, cozy, beautiful, peaceful world. It is also a carefully crafted puzzle game, but if you're expecting life-changing "eureka moments" a la The Witness or Baba is You or Stephen's Sausage Roll or Portal, you will be sorely disappointed. This game is not trying to amaze you (albeit you will make many cool discoveries!) Rather, it's a chill vibe--a world you can retreat to after a long day at work or school.Download the demo before you buy. You'll know whether you are the target audience for this game within the first hour.

Why ? So you can get a log of what the others players are doing. Oh and probably also so the studio can get your email and other valuable datas. It's completely useless, the log is infuriating and you can't disable it. No, IDC that "XYZ has solved a puzzle". The one in this game feels like "hey look, this is cool, let's do the same, but not the same because we don't understand why it was cool"Then, you can't restart the game ? WTF ? Oh sorry actually you can. You simply have to submit a ticket to their support. Imagine for one second being a support engineer, paid 6 figures, to reset players games. How come someone thought it was a good idea ?Also, no controller support ?And overall many, many UI/UX issues, such as it's dificult to know if a puzzle was solved or not, untold rules (it's ok if the gameplay is made around this, but if you tell 75% of the rules, it's a bad idea to not tell 100% of them etc)Overall it's sad, as I feel it's an interesting and potentially good game, but this smell like a case of "we want that shinny light that Unreal can do and don't care about actual devs/qa team inputs about the game"

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something I have been searching for a long time - I absolutely love it.I installed it because I got it for free and since there have been a lot of negative reviews, I didn't expect much. I was proven wrong from the first minute I played.This game is packed full with diverse puzzles in a beautiful open world setting. The movement is satisfying and smooth as you fly between enclaves and the main islands. I have a graphics card and CPU from 2019 (5 years old) and I rarely have lags and if I do they're minor when I get into a big area that needs to be rendered. There are 24 puzzle types, of which 4 are variations of the same concept. The rest are fun and unique puzzles that include action in the map, perspective, audio clues and many more. With this amount of objectives you're never bored. The puzzles in the main islands are reset periodically to insure replayability. Progressing is exciting as well, as you are rewarded with points to unlock skills and abilities as well as customizations. One thing I want to mention is accessibility: There are some puzzle concepts that use audio clues which cannot (or only with added difficulty) be solved in another way. People who have issues with hearing will have to focus on the other 22 (or 23) puzzle types instead. Since you get to choose which puzzles you solve, this should not be a huge issue. However some enclaves won't be able to be finished completely. I found the community to be friendly and helpful. With only a limited set of pings and emotes that can be used, we helped each other with especially tough puzzles and could show our gratitude as well. I have spent around 40 hours in the game and can whole-heartedly recommend it. With the offline update around the corner I think even more people will enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Loving the game.The puzzles have a nice variety, which helps 'cleanse the palate' so to speak, so if you get frustrated with one type you can give another one a go.The open world is nice, with some beautiful vistas and a few neat secrets if you go exploring.I quite liked the cheeky 'Clever Seeker, getting to this enclave before unlocking it' acknowledgement of me gliding in from another enclave to one I hadn't unlocked yet. The way the enclaves basically act as advanced tutorials to teach you the basic strategies for solving the specific puzzle types, intermixed with a few lore tidbits giving some context about what this place is, was quite pleasant too.I've had quite some time pass trying to figure out some of the 5 difficulty puzzles, and have yet to even meet the 'Star' graded puzzles (Met a Grandmaster one in the demo, took me nearly an hour to figure that one out).There's quite a few interesting and creative ways they make some of the enclaves work, and a few meta-puzzles too (I always loved those from Talos).The only negative is probably the Always Online aspect, as this game feels like it will have awesome replayability for years to come, if only because it's neat to jump in and warm the brain up on a few puzzles. And the Always Online part threatens the possibility of the servers one day shutting down. Hopefully the game gets enough success that an offline mode with a fixed set of puzzles becomes an option if that ever happens. (The rubber banding and lag some have complained about was entirely absent for me, but I'm on a wired Fiber optics connection, so that might help)

_childDocuments_.review: After mulling it over a bit and playing Islands Of Insight for a couple days, I think the game is genuinely fantastic, if not without it's flaws (for now). If you are puzzle enthusiast who can go solving puzzles for hours on end without much direction or guidance, this is the game for you and will keep you busy for a long time. It is addictive, having the "one more puzzle" effect coupled with a chill soundtrack and gorgeous art direction.The game is touted as multiplayer - what that means is that, on whichever server you are in, you will see other players walking around and solving the puzzles that dot the landscape. The multiplayer aspects are a bit thin, there is no chat and there are only a few puzzle types where you can really "help" each other (such as labyrinths or the pillar puzzles), as other puzzles are locked to their specific screen, but it is a neat idea and I appreciate the vision. Sadly, this vision also leads to the usual always-online plagues - rubberbanding, disconnects (very rarely, admittedly) and being unable to play should the server go down.The game does not really *need* to be multiplayer and I hope they will expand on this aspect since the vision of the game clearly includes this multiplayer aspect. The game should definitely have some sort of chat function that goes beyond basic pings and if the game needs multiplayer, there should be some puzzle type that requires or at least heavily incentivizes Co-Op play. As for now, it is just a big playground with characters running around and while I find it cool to see when people solve puzzles or struggle with the same puzzles I do, it doesn't really do much for the game as of now.As for the way the game works, you walk around an open world with several biomes. The game is essentially divided into two sections: the open world and enclaves. The open world has puzzles dotted everywhere that reset every day. In the menu, you can see how many of the total available puzzles (that rotate in and out every day, as mentioned) you solved and claim rewards for specific milestones. Enclaves, on the other hand, are fixed and come with their own set of puzzles that stay solved after you finish them, and unlock after specific milestones. It is a cool mix that will keep you playing and exploring even after you are done with the many enclaves in this game. In the open world there are also random quests and some locked-off challenge areas with their own set of fixed puzzles that offer additional challenges. Solving more puzzles also raises your rank in the respective puzzles, granting insights and titles, but also your overall progress, unlocking more cosmetics. It's quite an addictive and rewarding system.The customization with the unlockables is good and moving around the world is fun - you can glide, jump high and unlock more abilities with sparks you gain from puzzles. The game still has some bugs as of now - puzzle counts randomly reset in enclaves (showing 0 solved puzzles even though you already finished, the puzzles are still solved, but it is a visual bug), some puzzles may appear unsolved even though you already solved them and I spotted some other minor visual bugs as well.Overall, I hope the rough patches and some of the multiplayer issues will be ironed out in time. What is there, though, is incredible to a puzzle lover such as myself. 24 different types of puzzles (some easier ones you can knock out in a minute, like skydrops and rings, and harder ones like logic grids or fractals), rotating puzzles that keep you busy and some really good difficulty balancing, allowing you to choose what puzzles you want to tackle and how difficult you want them to be. The game has a chill soundtrack, looks gorgeous and is perfect to vibe away the hours while teasing your brain. While the game is a bit rough around the edges, I am having a ton of fun and if you like puzzles, you can't go wrong with Islands of Insight if you can look past the forced multiplayer aspect that I hope will be built on in the future. Puzzle on!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I'm going to start with the Cons here. This game does not need to be online. I get what they were going for, but the way it's implemented has missed the mark. There is very little player to player interaction if any. There's a scrolling chat always on screen that such-and-such as solved *this* type of puzzle or *that* type of puzzle, but this information is completely useless to everybody who can see it. There is nothing that tells you where that puzzle is, there is no chat function to ask where it is or how to solve it. Thereby making it completely irrelevant. Coupled with issues with it being online, I have owned this game two days, and have had the servers crash about 12 times. This comes with additional challenges if you're trying to play with a friend, as you cannot choose what server you load into, nor can you join your friend through steam or through the (non-interactive) friends menu. You also cannot quit to main menu, which means attempting to rejoin your friend involves closing and reopening the game and then loading into the server over and over again, hoping to just get lucky.The devs have stated that they are working to make it offline compatible. Which is a huge step in the right direction. My only hope with this is that it can be locally hosted to play with a friend, as that would make it the perfect game in my eyes. Now, why do I still recommend this game?It is absolutely stunning. I've only explored a small portion of the world but it is gorgeous.The variety of puzzles is incredible, I could sit and do the logic boxes for hours, but if that's not your taste, there's at least 10 other types of puzzles right next to it for you to pick from. The movement is fun. For such a large world it does not feel like a trek to get around, with quick sprinting, gliding, and air lifts.No in game purchases. I cannot emphasize enough how nice that is in this day and age. There are many cosmetics to mess with, and you don't need to spend an extra cent. There is a demo that I highly recommend trying if this game interests you even a little. I played it for quite a while before realizing I was hooked, and needed to buy it in case my progress reset. Thankfully it did not. My friend, who is not typically a puzzle game enjoyer, also bought it after the demo, and has also been enjoying it, despite the issues we've encountered.If you enjoyed The Witness, The Talos Principle, Myst, or any number of similar puzzle games, I highly suggest checking this one out.

_childDocuments_.review: Islands of Insight could have been a fantastic game, but unfortunately, it falls short in several key areas. The game suffers from technical issues, a lack of developer engagement with the community, and poor communication from those maintaining it.On the positive side, the puzzle design is genuinely well done. However, the online mode is a frustrating experience, and the offline mode becomes nearly unplayable once you've solved a significant number of unique hub puzzles.The only thing that has kept me going is the desire to achieve 100% completion and the small but dedicated and friendly community behind the game. But as it stands, I can’t recommend the game until major fixes are made—which, unfortunately, seems unlikely at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm delighted to update my review to say:  as of the "offline only" update, both of the show-stopper bugs appear to no longer be an issue!  (Offline mode can now safely use steam cloud sync without corrupting your save, and online mode... no longer exists, so its bugs are no longer relevant, heh!)   So with those warnings out of the picture, it's finally time for an actual review....The short version is:  this is a *phenomenal* collection of puzzles, wrapped in a needlessly-complex 3D environment, with a somewhat ADHD-brain-candy format (for better or worse!).   It feels absolutely silly to launch a GPU-fan-blowing environment to spend 99% of my playtime staring at a 2D grid of numbers that I'd rather be playing on my phone (and yes, your GPU fans will *keep* blowing hot air the entire time your screen is filled with the 2D puzzles too!), but the fact is, these puzzles are worth it.   I do wish you could go through them in order with a checklist, rather than having them thrown at you at random, but admittedly the random aspect *does* encourage moving on to something new rather than beating your head against tough puzzles constantly, so it's really not a bad format either tbh.   The random puzzles *not remembering* whether or not you've solved them really got under my skin at first, but from what I hear on the forums, there's a mod to change that...  and tbh, I got used to it after a while anyway.To describe the puzzles themselves:  there's all sorts, some more interesting than others, but something like 75% of the game's puzzle content is all variations on a puzzle that feels like a cross between minesweeper and nonograms (and a little reminiscent of Hexcells too); it builds up an *amazing* variety of rules over time, but the short version is, given a handful of clues, you gradually narrow down whether each tile in the board is black or white, and every new tile that you narrow down allows you to narrow down something else next.   From what I can tell, these *appear* to all be human-authored puzzles -- at the very least, a large number of them give aesthetic suggestions that they were, and some of them seem much too clever to be the output of a script -- and none of them ever require guesswork, they're all perfectly solvable just from carefully thinking the rules through.Frankly, it's my sincerest hope that all of these 'tile' puzzles get ported to a phone app that isn't full of battery-killing 3D graphics; but in the meantime, it's worth plodding around the (very pretty, admittedly) 3D environments to find more of them.A note for Steam Deck players:  I *have* gotten it to run once or twice, but on *most* of my attempts, it crashed on launch.   Launching it as the first thing after you reboot your Steam Deck seems to help, but tbh it felt flaky enough that I haven't given it serious investigation, as much as I'd like to play this on the couch.

_childDocuments_.review: You may notice reading other reviews that the online servers for the game were shut down and that many people permanently lost their save files, and I agree that the game deserves some negative attention for that. However, I think a review should be an opinion piece addressed towards people who are interested in purchasing a game and what their experience playing the game might look like going forward, so this controversy will not impact my final recommendation.That being said, I think it should still be talked about to some degree. I believe that (after the final update fixing the SSD wear issues) the offline mode is genuinely better than the online mode was while the servers were still active. While an interesting idea conceptually, the online mode didn't actually add to my enjoyment of the game, nor did it really detract from it. It felt like an unnecessary addition. There were no cooperative puzzles to complete, no way to speak to other players, and barely any way to communicate to other players at all (small ping system with a few options, a couple emotes).So where does that leave the game? From my viewpoint, exactly the way it probably should have been when it was released. Islands of Insight is an extraordinary puzzle game with a massive variety of puzzles to complete. Not all puzzles are created equal, but I actually think that adds to the appeal. The game is a perfect balance of challenging and interesting puzzles alongside more relaxing puzzles with only minor thought required to complete, which allow your brain to take a small break in preparation for the next challenge. The open world itself adds another layer of depth to the game; instead of simply navigating menus, which actually detracts from that perfect balance I was talking about earlier, each puzzle must be interacted with as an object in a world (not to mention several of the puzzle types would not work in a game where puzzles were accessed via menu).All there is left to mention is precisely who am I recommending this game to. I truly do believe that if you enjoy puzzle games at all, you will find some enjoyment in Islands of Insight. Despite the decision to make the game online only on release, despite the half-baked implementation of an offline mode to the game that destroyed people's SSDs until it was fixed months later, despite the death of the online servers mere months after the game's release, Islands of Insight is one of the greatest puzzle games to ever exist and I cannot recommend it enough. None of the controversies are relevant to new players of the game, so give it a try.P.S. Download rushin and team's Offline Restoration Mod (available in the discussions as of writing this review). It fixes some of the lingering bugs the developers failed to fix before leaving the game behind. Disclaimer: My opinions of the offline mode may have been influenced by the use of this mod.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot going for it. It's got ndlessly inventive puzzles, with new ones introduced regularly, new rulesets to increase the diversity of the puzzles you already know, and tons of space to explore, always jam packed with a dozen new freshly generated puzzles around each bend. It's also got creative, curated "dungeons", called Enclaves, with specially tailored challenges that remain always the same, sometimes to introduce concepts and puzzles, other times to offer the nastiest challenges to really prove your mettle. It's got movement, hidden objects, exploration, speedrunning, and loads of logic puzzles as well. These are generally all great.It's also an always-online "MMO", where it sure is Multiplayer, but the only thing that happens in Multiplayer is that sometimes someone solves a basic generated puzzle locking you out (Armillary Rings or Skydrops seem to be the only ones that others can take) that will respawn in a short while, and emote or ping others to help guide people to solutions or hidden objects. The issue here is that, especially in the Enclaves, half the puzzles aren't even something the super limited communication can help with and you can't discern what someone is missing when trying to 100% a location anyway, so it's very hard to help others (seriously, please devs: When you finish all the main challenges of an Enclave, it's genuinely not fun to not be told what KINDS of puzzles remain. Every single Enclave ends this way and it's an endless frustration for me as I aim to 100% each one. Please. Give some guidance, since so many of the remaining puzzles are incredibly hidden.)It leaves the multiplayer aspect as almost a vestigial element - it's there and it exists, but it doesn't really offer any additional value. Sometimes it even causes lag or rubberbanding. Yay!With all this in mind though, the puzzles are generally phenomenal, the constant access to puzzles does an amazing job of offering a "just one more" solving experience, keeping you up late (I'm writing this at 5am) and cracking clues, and it offers an engaging progression each step of the way. The lore tidbits are just fine, but the hidden Mysteries are cryptic and intriguing, offering even more layers atop the already rich puzzling experience.If you're willing to ignore or just lightly engage with the multiplayer aspect, you get some extra hustle and bustle in the world at most, but also get a really engaging puzzle sandbox to explore, and for that, I absolutely do recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: Don't play this game! I haven't slept since I started!Jokes aside - engaging minipuzzles in various difficulties and loads of hidden objects to find in a beautiful environment. Customization and upgrades for your char. Responsive movement that allows you to correct your trajectory in midjump and wings for gliding.I love it and would say it's a must-have for puzzle-lovers.Nothing for achievement hunters: At least for now, there are no steam achievements.They still have to shake out some bugs (some of them major like not always saving progress correctly), but even so the game is already a joy to play. Definitely worth getting on a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems to have a ubisoft size world and amount of content. Anywhere you go you will get surrounded by content. One step to the right - a hidden pathway, one step to the left - a labyrinth and so on.Probably the best way to play is as a mental gymnastics. You launch the game for 20-30 minutes, solve a couple dozens of puzzles and go on with your day.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2: Never played online mode, but the attitude of the company makes me unable to recommand this. (Also the save file takes up so much space, even with their sort of fix).Edit: played more now. Only in offline mode. It's a really good puzzle game, I like it a lot. The puzzles are varied, easy to challenging with a couple of really difficult ones, and you can choose which ones you do. The hint system in logic grids is great. The puzzles in the mainland reset, but I don't mind, as it always gives you something to do. The puzzles in the enclaves don't, which gives me a sense of progress, as wel las the unlocked puzzles. There's 5 'lands' and I'm at land 3 currently. I enjoy it a lot, it runs smooth, there's a nice atmosphere, love that you can change your outfit and skin whenever. Some upgrades from the upgrade tree are good - and help in not giving you all the things all at once which can be a bit much - but I wish I could turn some off.Maybe 30 bucks is a bit much, but with a small discount I'd say it's worth it.Sure, it has some meh-things. I wish I could wear all outfits on my character, not just the male (sorry - 'square') outfits on the male character. I wish I could turn the quest markers off. The 'story-line' is okay, but a bit unesecary and pretentious/vague, but there's some nice sayings in there and it doesn't really play a big part so it's not a bother. It takes  a bit of time to load, but it's playable.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow I got this game free of charge, but it is one of the BEST puzzle games I've encountered.The good old Pandora's Box came to mind when I played Islands of Insight, with its absolutely clever puzzles and "just one more, promise" , hooked feeling which just wants you to continue on and on with solving puzzles endlessly. And you basically can :) I thank the developers for creating this beautiful piece!
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: Islands of Insight is a great game for fans of the witness, the talos principle, and other puzzle heavy gamers.The Good:Great puzzle design. Puzzles I hadn't seen before. In a linear way.The plot, while terrible, is so easy to skip!The environments you jump around from puzzle to puzzle is extremely relaxing and beautiful.The Bad:If the game only had cube puzzles, and no other distractions, it would be a huge improvement. What feels like 50% of the puzzles in the game are filler puzzles that are either random-ish, or take less than 10 seconds to solve. In addition, some environmental puzzles are incredibly frustrating, though do require some out-of-the-box thinking.I actually really like the hidden cubes (you just listen for a tinkling then hit the cube) but because there's a percent complete on each section, finding that last one is torture :)The game has cut most of their dev team, so I'm not expecting a ton of additional content, though they have already added some.My recommendation: Definitely, definitely buy it! But, ignore all puzzles that aren't cubes. Just do the "main" enclaves (follow the waypoints). If you start to hit dead ends, move on to the next enclave. Interact with the freebee puzzles as you see fit. I found many enjoyable... but I wish I could traverse the land with a bit more emptiness and go from cube to cube. I think that would have further enhanced the beauty.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: In its current state, I don't love it.Plenty of puzzles are good, the logic grids and pattern completion is all great. But there are a LOT that feel like filler. "Look at this from the right angle and press M1" is repeated over at least 4 'different' puzzle types and I'm still early in the game.There's also a tonne of "puzzles" which are just invisible objects you can't see until you're close to them. Not a puzzle, not fun. Even worse when the only hint to finding many is a high pitched ringing noise many players can't seem to hear, myself included as it seems to be masked by my tinnitus. There are no accessibility options for such things. A high pitched ringing as your only hint is terrible game design.Areas are broken up so you can see how many puzzles are in an area, but once you've solved most of them, finding the last few is an absolute nightmare. Finding an invisible little box SOMEWHERE on a large island isn't a puzzle. It isn't fun, it isn't rewarding. FINDING the puzzle should not BE the puzzle in a puzzle game.The online stuff is, at best, intrusive for what is a single-player game. I don't want a constant popup on my screen telling me Xz-L33tSn1p3r-zX solved a puzzle in their game every 12 seconds. You have no option to opt out of the always-online ♥♥♥♥, and no option to hide the visual spam that comes with it. Worse, you can be chugging along in your single-player game, and be unable to progress, because random lag spikes keep sending you back to the bottom of the launch-pad thing, or jump you around inside a transparent maze so you have no idea where you are any more.For the moment, I would hold off on buying this until player numbers dwindle and they can't afford to keep it as an always-online experience.Edit:All of the things I mentioned are still annoying.There are some late-game puzzle types that are just unenjoyable to play. Music grids are nice when they're smaller, but they reach a point where it's just a cacophony of noise with like 12 instruments being played at random points over 1 second where it asks you to pick out which is being played in which order.There's also some time-based challenges which ask you to solve 20 hard candy-crush-style match three games in 60 seconds. If you actually want to pass it, it has nothing to do with solving the puzzles. It's sitting down for literally several hours, memorising the exact sequence of moves which adds up to about 100 movements, and then just playing the same 20 puzzles ad nauseum until you can successfully make all the moves flawlessly and fast enough.Many players also dislike the Morphic Fractal puzzles, where you essentially drag your mouse around until a picture matches the example. They are so wildly unpredictable that there isn't a lot of strategy beyond just moving your mouse randomly until things look right.Overall, it is a good game, but it just has these constant thorns in your side to remind you that there are problems with it.Edit 2:At this point I've completed all the enclaves. They are the small islands with a set number of fixed puzzles. That means what's left is the 'open world.' It is filled with hundreds of puzzles that rotate every few hours, so the puzzle you found in a place one day might be absent the next. To progress through rewards, you need to do a set number of a type of puzzle in a region. ie. You might need to do 200 logic grids to get an ugly hat. I'm not set on doing everything. In each region there are THOUSANDS of puzzles in each category. However, the big disappointment for me comes from the fact that you can get duplicates. I KNOW I solved a siteseer puzzle in the exact same place with the exact same view. I remember that yesterday I found a hidden ring in the same place because I noted that its placement was unusual. I followed a wandering echo that jumped between those same 4 pillars.Sure, I can play more and avoid the dupes, but it's not really fun to just tick up an exorbitantly large number for the sake of it when they don't even put in the effort to make them unique. The store page brags about 10,000 puzzles or whatever but when today alone I've played 3 different logic grids, all with a solution that I recognise I've done before, and I can check my stats to see all three counted as a new puzzle, well what's the point?
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: Was incredibly fun to play this game, especially if you love puzzles and mind-games, this felt like i was a child again solving puzzles and little kooky games with my mother, sister, and father. thank you Behaviour Interactive, this game is incredibly fun, and i hope to see more to it in the future when playing it :]
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a tribute to Bigfish Games.Not anywhere near 10000 puzzles, but still good casual fun while listening to podcasts or music.It's a decent sized open world with several types of puzzles (e.g., grid puzzles, match 3, sokoban) and several collectathons (e.g., hidden objects).The vast majority of these seem to be procedurally generated, and take only a few seconds to solve (e.g., look through all floating rings in a bunch, look at all floating spheres from the right angle).There are also a few handmade, more complex puzzles, which are much more fun. Some of the grid based puzzles have multiple rules to keep in mind, and can take 10 minutes or longer to solve.Exploring the open world gets repetitive fast. It took me 20 hours to unlock all puzzle types and all areas except a couple high level dungeons.There are a few complex exploration puzzles called mysteries, but most of the exploration is the same from the beginning to the endgame. You stumble upon hundreds of hidden objects and short puzzles, and level up without much effort.There is some lore, but it might as well be generated by a chatbot. Bland inspirational quotes, generic 2-3 sentence memos, nothing memorable.The graphics are sometimes nice, and sometimes a jumble of basics from an asset store.The performance is bad. This is not a high-end looking game, but it runs like one.Overall, I recommend checking a review video or two. The gameplay doesn't change much, so if you like what you see, and you like the price, you're in for a good time despite the lack of polish.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very nice "puzzle MMO", somewhere between Uru: Ages Beyond Myst and Talos Principle, but only with puzzles and no storyline or philosophical aspect. It's all about solving simple but well-thought puzzles (match-3, perspectives, labyrinths, objects to connect, hidden objects, etc.) in an open world environment while unlocking new abilities allowing to access more puzzles. It's addictive, with a wide range of difficulty levels and consistent design quality. Also, did I tell you about puzzles? Puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Online is being shut down this month, Offline may get a minor performance fix. Puzzles will respawn, but there's an excessive amount of puzzle grind to get through a single player passive story. Still can't recommend.They applied progression bars and open world  elements to the puzzle genre, there are some good potential points but it's lacking. The overwhelming majority of "puzzles" are small interactions and clicking hidden objects. These are satisfying for awhile,  The puzzle XP chart is primarily for unlocking everything in the skill tree, but most of the skill tree should've been default stats instead of upgrades. After the skill tree is full, you'd be grinding puzzles for cosmetic points in a game with no cosmetic satisfaction.I played pretty consistently at first, dipping more as server issues sprung up more, which got BAD after the free redemption day. The offline mode update did seem to help more players offline and I stayed online to finish up the main quest. After doing some of the Mystery content, I realized I was just grinding to complete some more checklists. I never cared about the story or much of anything else. The dopamine puzzle mine wasn't worth it anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, just rough around the edges.There are tons of puzzles and activities. But you have to ask yourself, will the puzzles feel meaningful when there are that many?With typical puzzle games you have a gradual progression of hand crafted puzzles that lead to something. In Islands of insight, you stop playing when you lose interest. There may be a narrative, but if there is that's a puzzle too as you have to piece together lore fragments.  I kept playing thinking something would happen, but it didn't. Just more of the same puzzles. And there is a nice variety. I remember the wonder of discovering different puzzle types. But that wore off quickly as most of the "puzzles" are just curiosities that amount to busy work. And this is always online, for no conceivable reason. This is made worse by frequent disconnects from their server. For some reason you also get updates every time someone completes a puzzle, in a game where it's possible to complete 10 puzzles in a second by walking into them. You eventually blank out the updates from your perception, but I do have to wonder what the devs were thinking. They could have at least limited it to less frequent milestones. And the worst part is there is no chat feature to justify the online aspect.Puzzle games typically give me a zen feeling. This game is over stimulating. If you do play it I suggest not worrying about accomplishing anything in particular, and maybe sticking to the main puzzles. Otherwise this game is a a completionists koightmare.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore all the comments going "servers are lagging downvote." The game itself is amazing it lacks co-op currently, but that can be added in later. The servers are getting better each day as they make adjustments and get things situated. The puzzle variety has gone up tons since the beta, and there are much more challenging puzzles than before. FPS is much better than beta as well, but still low sitting around 60-75fps on my PC which is high end. Low or max settings give the same fps, so might as well stick with max if you have a strong PC because the game is beautiful. I hope this game ends up fully co-op with a VR option. Exploring around a beautiful world while solving puzzles with some friends is the peak of what VR is made for. Though that will be years down the line if they decide to do it.

Shouldn't need internet for a game like this, which is no doubt a breaking point for people who would otherwise play.Score: 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Islands of Insight is a tough game to recommend, I've now spent over twenty hours in it and, for the most part, enjoyed my time in it yet I still find myself wondering if I should advise against playing this game, let me explain why...Firstly the game itself is a fairly simple concept, you awaken on a series of floating islands and every corner of every one is covered in hundreds of puzzles, you're never more than a second or two from the nearest puzzle and if you enjoy the puzzles in this game you'll likely enjoy the game as a whole. Likewise, if you're not fussed by the puzzles you almost certainly won't enjoy this game.There are a number of different puzzle types in the game, though the most common one seems to be a variation of a 'logic grid' - where you're given a sudoku-looking grid and a rule or two to follow to help split the grid into black and white squares. These puzzles are well designed, the islands that specifically teach these rules are done in a really accessible way though by the harder ones they can be overwhelmingly difficult. Luckily these specific puzzle types come with a time-based hint system that tells you if a square you've coloured in is wrong, or points to the next solvable square. These puzzles are well made and make up the backbone of the game.Other puzzles include chasing lights, flying through rings, finding locations from screenshots, lining up patterns on the environment, discovering lines through a collection of wings, music puzzles, mazes, creating rings of orbs by standing in the right place, uncovering invisible things among others - this hint system hasn't been implemented for many of these, which is a shame if you get stuck. There also seems to be riddles to solve that lead you back to old puzzles and tell you to solve them in a different way, which is cool.Basically, if you enjoy puzzles like these you'll likely enjoy this game.So why am I so torn about giving it a recommend rating? It's always online but I wouldn't say it was multiplayer.The game insists on connecting you to a server, as you run around the world you can see other people running around doing the same. Only that's about it. I -think- there might be a chat system but I've never seen it used, I once had someone wave at me but that's it for player interaction. I've yet to find a puzzle that requires coop, you can't actually see another player solve a puzzle, just where they're stood in the world. I've yet to see a reason to communicate, everyone seems to be playing the game as a single player game and the whole system seems underused.Which would be find in a Dark Souls echoes of other players sort of way but by forcing connection to a server there seems to be small but persistent amounts of lag that still affects the game a couple months after release. Again, not a huge problem until you're trying to complete an agility puzzle and the game teleports you past a target or rubber-bands you back.If multiplayer added meaningful gameplay to the game I wouldn't mind so much, but as it is forcing online seems to just cause lag and that's about it. One of two things need to happen to this game at this point, either they need to make it a single player game, or add features that make the multiplayer worth suffering the server issues for. Unfortunately, two months after release, there doesn't seem to be movement in either direction.The game plays great, looks great, sounds great. It is relaxing like a puzzle game should be, has some sort of story I'm not really paying attention to and, despite the issues, I've enjoyed the couple dozen hours I've put into it, I think I'll be playing more - so it seems wrong to give it anything other than a 'recommend'.BUT you should be aware there's some avoidable issues that I really hope the devs are working on in one way or another.And no, if you don't like the looks of the puzzles, you won't like this game - if you do, however, I recommend checking it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhere between the open-ended design of The Witness and the vibes of The Talos Principe (but far less introspective, which here is good). Can't say that I care much for the lore, but the open world is chock full of puzzles at every corner, to a dizzying degree, If you're trying to finish EVERY puzzle, finding them is gonna be a serious challenge on its own.  The movement abilites you unlock like absurdly high jumps and the floating wings make it a lot more fun than expected.I'd classify puzzles in two categories, main and secondary. Main puzzles ask you to really use what you've learned through other similar puzzles so far and can be particularly tricky, like the tile puzzles, similar to TTP's sigil puzzles, with more and more interesting variables as the game progresses. Some of them are more about looking around and spatial exploration, like matching pairs of hidden symbols in the environment, or floating rings where you need to find a direct line between all yellow rings while avoiding purple rings. Secondary puzzles get repetitive rapidly, but main ones offer a lot of variety and are well worth the effort. Overall, you just need to know one thing. If you usually like puzzle games, like The Witness and The Talos Principle, this one is going to become a classic and you should jump on it asap. If puzzle games aren't your thing, well this game is just non-stop puzzles. Maybe not your best bet.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, intriguing, addicting, very odd game. The original pitch seems to have been "MMO ," which struck me as a bizarre notion when I first heard about it a couple years ago. How could puzzle gameplay possibly benefit from being MMO? What does "multiplayer puzzle" even mean, really? I'd just have to wait and see.Well, now it's here, and the answer seems to be: "um, we're still not sure... but look at all this other stuff we made! SO much stuff!" And it's true. There's an enormous amount of puzzle content, littered densely throughout a sprawling landscape. It's a giant grab-bag, without any particular voice or personality, and some of it is just randomized filler... but there are many hundreds of genuinely excellent handcrafted puzzles here, most of them delightfully bite-sized. Is that good enough? It might be. I've definitely been having fun with it.As it currently stands, shared-world multiplayer is basically just a vibe: instead of the typical wandering alone in an eerily abandoned puzzle-world, you're aware of being in company with lots of other players, who can be seen leaping and flying nearby, or at least milling around on the map. If you've got friends among them, you could, I guess, choose to go around together from puzzle to puzzle, though you'll still be solving individually. And... that's all there is to it! I've never played a game that put so much networking to such inessential use. It certainly feels like a developer's crazy dream that hit some hard realities and ended up weirdly stunted. So is the online aspect worth all the technical demands and headaches that come with it? Probably not, and yet... I have to admit that I've been really enjoying the feeling that I'm playing within a living, populated space. It may be just a vibe but it's a vibe I've never gotten from a puzzle game before and, yeah, there's something thrilling about it. Will it evolve? Will the developers eventually make good on their wildest ambitions, crack the problem of co-op puzzling in a rewarding way, and add it to the game? I have no idea. But now that I'm here, I'm rooting for them. Until then, I'll be more than content to play through a solo campaign of mostly-great puzzles, explore a vast generically-gorgeous dreamworld for secrets, and enjoy the constantly rotating selection of "sandbox" content. All that plus the huge potential for future expansion seems to me worth the asking price.(For what it's worth: the lore and the costume upgrades and the customizable characters hold no charm at all for me, aesthetically or otherwise. It all strikes me as pretty silly and unrewarding. Plus the elaborate progress-tallying systems and upgrade trees etc. etc. feel like a lot of noise inherited senselessly from other games. In my opinion, that sort of stuff contributes to addiction without contributing to actual fun. Luckily it doesn't really matter: you can just do the puzzles and ignore the noise.)[Reviewed after about 16 hours in the demo and another 4 in the full game.]

Some puzzles require audio.No singleplayer mode (and sometimes the servers are down so you can't play). Furthermore no reason for this game to be an MMO at all. Not even multiplayer. _childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: Islands of insight is one of the easiest games to misunderstand, and not in the normal way games are misunderstood "no you are not supposed to fight the monsters" etc but just the way the whole game is presented lets you think it's a pay-to-win, cashgrab, multiple subscription models, gatcha MMORPG with stupid minigames and a gazillion metrics to keep track of. Especially back when it was 100% online. But ... it's quite frankly not any of that (tho some of the minigames are indeed a bit stupid) You can't even buy anything with realworld currency. Everything is just unlocked through gameplay and exploration. And it turns out all those metres that fill up ... thats just passively tracking how many of X puzzletype you solved and will give you some Cosmetics or ingame currency. So once you realized that you can just roam around Ancient Floating Islands and do Sudokus as long as you want, which is really ... nice. It's just a nice chill game. I don't know what made the devs think 100% online was a good idea and why they designed the game as if it were the mess I described above. But the game itself is a nice relaxed puzzle session in a nice ambiente, reminiscent of Talos Principle (1). There is no relevant story to speak of tho, so keep that in mind.Also Character customization is insane. Every piece of clothing looks like the stuff whales wear in MMOs, you even start with spectral wings and trail effects. And what's up with the skin?!? There are like 4 layers to skin texture with glow, sheen etc. and offcourse all colours of the rainbow. So go nuts :D
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a co-op puzzle game, you've come to the wrong place.I was really looking forward to playing a massive multiplayer puzzle game with my friends, having enjoyed playing other titles such as Portal and Escape Simulator. Sadly this was not the outcome...This game claims to be an MMO and was marketed as having co-op, but you cannot interact with anyone in-game in any meaningful way. Your friends can join your "party", but I have no idea why - you cannot solve puzzles together, the only thing that makes this an online "multiplayer" game is that you can see other people around you. There is not even a voice or text chat to speak to other players.Apparently in early play testing there were elements of co-op, but these were scrapped.As a side note: my friends and I were kicked to the main menu several times during our very brief time on the game, which I assume was due to server issues, but there were no messages to let us know why we were back there. This game currently has a very small player-base, so the servers shouldn't be having issues.I am genuinely saddened that this game wasn't what I expected. It could have been amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: I fully intended to leave a positive review.  Though I hadn't played in some time, I played and enjoyed a large amount of this game, starting back in beta.  It's a beautiful puzzle game with some fantastic features, and some rather pointless ones.  There was never much value to the online features; there could've been, had the game been allowed to grow, but as it was, there was no real collaboration or communication supported, so it was just a silly thing, being able to see other people running around the same world without much meaningful interaction.It's also a mixed blessing that there are "infinite" puzzles which regenerate.  While this hints at the idea of endless value, in practice you can often tell the difference between a randomly-generated vs. a lovingly hand-crafted puzzle, and furthermore the fact that these regenerating puzzles create the nagging feeling that you can never  complete  will diminish the zeal of completionists.But the variety and quality of the puzzles - especially the hand-crafted ones, of which there are still a great many - is absolutely enough to constitute a solid, even exceptional puzzle game.  And I really love the "insights" feature - they make this an actual  experience, to the point that I would feel happy to see this being used as part of some kind of school program.Yes, this game would've ranked highly among the many puzzle games I've played...But, I just logged in and... did they really lose my save file?    I feel such contempt for whatever greedy management staff made the knee-jerk decision to hastily abandon a game which had such potential, which was so unique.  Clearly a talented team was presided over by morons with no idea of, or appreciation for, what they had.I'll change my review to Positive if it turns out my progress can be recovered, but my cynicism for so-called "management" will remain.**EDIT**: It looks like I was able to recover my progress, on a second attempt to download it from Online Mode.  It's something the user should never have to worry about, frankly, and presumably if I had waited a bit longer - past the imminent shutdown of the Online Mode - I would've lost it forever.  Brutal.  Hopefully if I ever decide to return to the game and finish some more of it, I won't be blocked by any game-breaking bugs, which presumably will never be fixed given the game's apparent abandonment.Still, I will change the review to Positive - for all its flaws, and despite being mismanaged to death, what's here is worth playing if you enjoy logic puzzles.  But it's sad to reflect on the fate of this game, and what might've been.

_childDocuments_.review: Unable to play the game beyond the main menu, probably due to memory issues: the 8GB minimum requirements are nowhere near enough to actually play the game, and even 16 are insufficient, without a quite sizeable pagefile. All the time the game crashed it was allocating more than 19GB of memory, between physical and virtual.edit: definitely a memory issue: tried installing it on a PC with more memory and more disk space, and now it is at least able to launch. In order to be able to launch the game you need 25-27GB of combined space between free RAM and free space on and SSD disk.The concept of the game is good, the implementation, not so much. The multiplayer part had absolutely no reason to exists, it doesn't add anything to the game and it serves only to draw additional resources and add more points of failure.The game suffers from a lot of crashes, I still have to experience a session without crashing to desktop at least a couple times. In addition, you will need quite a beefy setup in order to be able to play the game without constantly juggling the settings: hidden objects puzzles are almost impossible to solve without having the graphics set to at least "middle", while you will need all the possible fps for the running, flying and parcour settings. The janky camera doesn't help either.The game has plenty of sound cues (good idea), but all the cues sound like being affected by tinnitus.Hidden penthads, flow chases and running echoes are just a pain in the ass

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that delivers on everything that it promises. It's an endless dopamine mine and you can play as little or as much as you want. There's a good variety of puzzles which keeps the game fresh and they're refreshed all the time. It's like an all you can eat buffet for puzzles. The difficulty varies for each puzzle type and there's no obligation to do any of the puzzles so it's as easy or as difficult as you want it to be. There are lots of individual enclaves for overall progression as well as overarching targets and endgame stuff that make it so there's always objectives if you want to work towards things. You can also just solve puzzles aimlessly if you prefer that. The open world is great and elevates the experience in every way.The game performs perfectly fine below minimum specs for me, though there is the occasional glitch. Probably most of the issues it has will get fixed with the offline mode. It's a bit baffling to me why it is even an MMO in the first place but it's funny seeing other people darting around doing puzzles I guess. Got for free during the 24hr giveaway but it's more than worth the price and I hope the game starts to get the attention it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: The world is absolutely gorgeous, and there is no shortage of things to do. Gliding around is a lot of fun and easily the fastest way to travel. The map size is large, but not to the point of excess, and I'm very grateful for the offline mode. The character customizer is a fun bit as well, especially as several rewards for leveling are items for your character. Everything from new clothes, wings, effects, and more! Ultimately, a very relaxing environment.All that said, the puzzles themselves feel somewhat lacking. With a lot of puzzle games I've played, the puzzles fit in to the world around you, unlocking new areas, secrets, or information as you play. Not with Islands. Here, the puzzles exist for their own sake and this can lead to a lot of repetition and similarity. There are only about 5 kinds of real puzzles with a few variations, while the rest are more fun mechanics (flying through rings, finding invisible archways, lining up orbs in the sky so they make a shape, etc.)There is some attempt at lore, but the game items that give it are vague and try to feign being insightful, but are just generally off-putting. You're also not given any rewards or motivation to find these bits of lore. Mechanically, everything works as intended, but there definitely comes a point where it gets tedious.All-in-all, it's a fun way to spend an hour or two, but I definitely recommend waiting for the price to drop. It gets about a 6.5/10 from me. Maybe 7/10 if I'm feeling generous.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really sure how to rate this game. First, I will admit that knew nothing of this game but only got it because there was a 24 hour giveaway that I happened to catch, so I got it.  This was just before offline mode was introduced. The online mode was rather annoying and I'm not sure why they marketed the game as some MMORPG puzzle game when the actual interaction with others was so, so minimal.  Offline mode has fixed that.Overall the game is beautiful and rather addictive as the game is absolutely massive, not only with a kind of planned progression of objectives throughout the game, but also with "overworld" puzzles resetting daily.  There's just tons of stuff to do.  Many call it a leisurely puzzle game, but that is kind of what you make of it. Yes, you can just go through at your own pace, but if you are trying to do 100% on the quests and enclaves, you might get a bit frustrated trying to find, much less complete all the puzzles in an area. And, like I said, the game is massive, boasting around 10,000 puzzles.  So, I would say you will definitely get your money's worth even at full price.  But given it has already gone on sale during the Steam Summer Sale, and they've even given it away for a 24 hour period, it might be worth waiting for a sale.  Especially when there still seem to be some bugs.  Some have complained of performance issues, and I have had an issue with negative sparks showing up (sort of the in game "currency" for advancing on the skill tree) when I reload a save even though I had thousands of sparks when I ended the last session.  Seems more prevalent in the offline mode from what I have read. But overall, I would recommend the game.  It just needs a bit more work to iron some things out, however it is very playable, and aside from a few minor issues, I have enjoyed my time playing it, and it has gotten a lot more of my play time than I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying I LOVED this game (I also have around 30 hrs in the demo before launch). _childDocuments_.review: Gonna start this off by saying that IOI is easily one of the best puzzle games I've ever played. The amount of content seems endless but not in an overwhelming way. It's very possible to almost entirely ignore puzzle types that don't interest you and still complete the main story line, nothing feels like it's shoved in your face, and even after you finish the main quests there's still at least a few hundred hours worth of content with loads of variety. There are still some bugs in it's current stage but nothing too game breaking.Pros:Literally thousands of puzzles ranging in difficulty, separated by both puzzle class and puzzle type The puzzle class you come across the most has a hint system that guides you in the right direction instead of just telling you how to do itVery well made skill tree No combat whatsoeverThe lore is there but it's not long or boring, just a few little lines of text as you choose to collect themGreat mastery system for each puzzle typeScenery is amazing and it's very easy to forget about the puzzles entirely and run around admiring the areasEasy UI with a fully functioning map that includes waypoints and a summary of what you have and haven't completed in each areaCons:It's definitely more multiplayer than co-opQuite a few bugs, random disconnects, and some glitched cosmeticsPretty big game that occasionally has trouble with optimisationOverall, if you don't mind a single player online game and getting disconnected here and there, then this is definitely a buy. It's super relaxing and absolutely worth every hour you'll end up pouring into the game
_childDocuments_.name: Islands of Insight

_childDocuments_.review: I played both the beta and open playtest for this game. I wanted so badly for it to be good, and it come so close to being amazing. But it falls so far off. Flight lag. I have ethernet and between 16 and 20 ping. This should not be a thing. But it is. Makes any movement puzzle impossible, and the only fix I have found is to restart the game.The monolith in the fourth area has no beams of light showing me where the fragments are, but isn't complete. Hilarious.Enclaves. Not only does it not tell you how many of each puzzle is left in each one (not a bug but super annoying when you are hunting down the last puzzle and have no clue if it is a puzzle grid or a hidden archway) but when you load into the game, the map resets your progress. So it visually shows 0/107 puzzles done. When you enter the enclave, ta da! 107/107. Unless it's a bigger enclave, then you need to go further in to let the puzzles load I guess? Horrid design.The pyramid. I have all but 3 mysteries unlocked. It should open the entire thing, but it isn't. Just the main floor.Fast travel. About 1 time in 5, it fails. And when it does, oh boy! The next 3 attempts also fail! Nothing I can do makes them work. Waiting, restarting the game, nothing. Excellent variety, good difficulty. Not a fan of the timed match 3s, but there are not many of those. The fractals can go away. No clue if I'm close, how close is good enough to win, or how to get closer. Move mouse at random.I do wish that in the open world (which is super small, if I'm being completely honest) the puzzles respawned at a much faster rate. Like every hour, new rolling blocks spawned in 1 of the 5 areas. The upgrades you get are quite nice. But you can get them all pretty quickly. And once you do, all that currency you are grinding? Transmog, when you play in 1st person most of the time. The upgrade tree should be 10x the size, at least.Unlocking different puzzles can be done by exploring each of the enclaves in each area. Once you do, those puzzles spawn in the open world. 10/10. Perfect, stops you from being overwhelmed. Wouldn't change anything about it.Overall, the puzzles are fun and challenging. But the bugs make it nearly unplayable. It feels like it never left Beta testing.Do not buy games that are released at full price in the condition. This is not acceptable in any way. Do not reward releasing buggy titles with the promise of "we will patch it later, promise"9/10 for gameplay. With the world being pretty small, and all the bugs, 3/10. And I feel generous on that

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Steam Deck. Experience might be different on normal PC.First impression is... Not good. Puzzles are boring and uninspiring, visuals are... Well, fine but could be better. Game crashed once in half an hour. No gamepad support (seriously?). Always online for no reason. Optimization is quite bad, game have a FSR Upscaling implementation but only FSR 1.0. Without FSR frame rate is 25 FPS on low settings. With FSR it's around 40 with drops to 30, but because there's no sharpening game looks really blurry with FSR enabled. Of course, maybe further into the game it might become better, maybe patches will fix optimization problems, but for now I can't really recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: This game has made me say "Woah" so many times, it's design is gorgeous and mystifying, and the puzzles are extremely varied and range from simple to very difficult. You're not forced to complete everything to progress, but it's also open for you to do so. The ability to customize everything about your character on the fly is also amazing, even your gender if you want, there's no limit. I had nothing to do yesterday so spent 12 hours in this game, because it's really addictive. So far I've played almost entirely in offline mode, I like solo play, but what I've seen of online mode has a lot of possibility to it. _childDocuments_.review: I got this game while it was 100% off. After today, i can no longer recommend it.First major issue, the quest for perfection puzzles, where you're only allowed to make 2 mistakes. Once you make your third, you have to start over from the beginning. It's rage inducing, especially considering that you have to consciously keep in mind which button colours the squares black or white, otherwise you end up accidentally placing the wrong colour and giving yourself a strike.Second major problem, the game keeps failing to record your progress with certain things, such as the mastery level rewards, which you have to reclaim over and over again, or the upgrades panel, where I bought the "Dual Luminous Quests" upgrade, but subsequently lost on rebooting the game, along with about 2000 upgrade points. I've even had some puzzle progress reset in areas I've 100% completed before, like Vanishing Point.Third major problem, if you happen to save in the wrong location, say inside the Vault of the Vitric, then you might as well kiss your progress goodbye, because the game crashes every time you try to log in. It took me 14 attempts to get in, and crashed on each attempt except the last one, where I'd set the game to the lowest graphical settings and the smallest window size possible.Fourth major problem: this game is an MMO, which means you should be able to meet up with your friends and solve puzzles together, but that's not the case. Meeting up with your friends is basically luck, you have to exit and enter the game in the hopes of being placed into the same instance as each other, and even then, the best you can do is to explore the world together. You can't assist in helping each other solve logic grid puzzles. You're also limited in game to 10 emotes and no text chat.Going into this game, I was enjoying it so much, but over time, my enjoyment waned as problems kept appearing, and it's just reached the point where I'm pretty much done with the game. If there's no guarantee that my puzzle progress is saved, what's the point in continuing?
