_childDocuments_.review: THE FINALS is a fantastic addition to the world of FPS games. It offers a unique blend of strategic gameplay and high-octane action, set within destructible environments that bring a fresh dynamic to each match. The game's emphasis on team play, combined with the ability to creatively use the terrain, elevates the experience beyond the usual run-and-gun style. It's not just about shooting; it's about outsmarting your opponents in clever, unexpected ways. The community on kik.gg enhances this experience by providing a space for players to connect, strategize, and share their most memorable moments. Overall, THE FINALS is a must-try for anyone seeking a thrilling, team-oriented shooter with a twist.

_childDocuments_.review: Imma be honest. This game is addicting, the gameplay is really unique, and the playstyles are very diverse, and that sets this game apart from a lot of arena shooters. The abilities are cool, and the concept is great. The only issue I have is that the in-game currency is limited to 3k at a time (kind of lame), and you can't use any in-game currency to buy cosmetics, despite some of them being kind of low-tier. I get it; the dev team needs the money, but come on, we can agree some of these skins should be for in-game currency. It's still a super-new game that's rising in popularity. Aside from some things being insanely overpriced in the store (understandable), the dev's need money, but it's not very welcoming to people who don't have deep pockets. At least add more skins to the battle pass that are free in this case so the everyday player who may not be earning enough in this economy can at least get something other than default clothing, and before someone thinks I'm referring to myself, I'm not. I have already spent money on this game, but I do see how this can be slightly unfair in a way to those who may not be well off.

People keep popping in and out of games all the time, presumably because their teammates couldn't carry their heavy posteriors to the victory AND with no consequence in casuals so even casuals only care about winning. _childDocuments_.review: As a casual player, I have to say, the game is great, and you can feel the devs care about it. Movement feels great, weapons too ( most of them at least ), maps are fun, pretty and everything being destructible is even better. But what lacks the most is balancing. It's not awful, but some weapons and / or gadgets can feel either over or under powered, especially if you're playing for fun like I am.Turrets and perma healed Heavies can be very annoying if you're playing light or medium, while some weapons like the dagger or grenade launcher can feel underwhelming. This is still a very good game but depending on loadout there are some games where it feels like you cannot contest objectives at all because of it. And while it could use more content, it's understandable there only so much from an indie dev team and the work they put into it, especially the maps. The only problem i'd have with content is gamemodes. I feel like we could use more.TL;DR Game is fun but needs more time on balancing in my opinionTry it out with friends you'll have a good time, definitely try out if you're searching for a competitive FPSSubjectively, Düne :)

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game has potential but gets boring pretty fast and game play is unbalanced. SO initially the game was a lot of fun. It if different than any other game i've played and is very fast paced (when not playing in a tournament). I progressed very quickly and got the hang of the game pretty easily. This is where the issues start coming in. You will reach your max progression very fast and they cap your money. All of the cosmetics are locked behind a paywall. There is no way to get them without paying. I have money but nothing to buy in the game. In order to win or be competitive in the game it is heavily reliant on your teammates and LUCK. If you get to the payout at the last few seconds you can easily win. And you will beat teams who have been defending and brought the money to the deposit . All you have to do is wait. This has happened to me about a dozen times on both sides. When I am defending getting double digit kills and still loose because I got team wiped by a random toxic gas and the other team with 4 total kills comes in at the last 10 seconds diffuses and wins the entire game. We cant come back and try and steal it back, the time is just over.  The timer needs to start over every time a new team steals the cashout. The game is literally punishing you for playing. Melee weapons are also extremely unbalanced. The heavy can come in with a hammer take down a building in 3 swings taking you out with it in 1 swing. The lights can become invisible and 3 swing you with a katana before you empty your entire clip. Makes guns almost unnecessary and will often put you at a disadvantage if you choose a gun over melee weapons. Shotguns are much stronger than any other gun.  You wont win against a shotgun melee or a heavy if you only have a gun.  Now lets talk about the solo mode and tournament. The solo mode is terrible and I didnt have fun playing it. It suffers from the same issues of gameplay but now you have to get to the cashout and deposit the money before the timer expires. Even if you are at the cashout depositing the money the timer can still expire? Why? I just fought off 4 other players now I have to run across the entire map again for another cashout just to get shot in the back by a re-spawned player. Tournaments take so long like to load and setup. There are two cashouts and 4 teams also you loose almost 10k everytime you get teamwiped. You run out of re-spawns so if your teammates don't want to revive you goodluck or wait for a teamwipe. Teams dont go negative so again you are punished for playing the actual game and getting killed. If you get team wiped a team who has no points can come in at the last second steal your cashout and kick you out of the tournament even though they put in very very minimal effort and honestly just got lucky being at the right place at the right time. If someone backs-out you will lose.  In conclusion I believe the game has potential but in its current state it is not very fun for me. It seems unfair and more like gambling than a game of skill and effort. I kept playing even after I began to feel this way to ensure it wasn't just a few games I wasn't enjoying. No I really just dont like the game all that much.

Then you realize you've just been angry for the past 2 hours and your time isn't worth this.Stealing the objective is a very real thing. You wait for the right time, steal it and that's the game. Out of an 8 minute game only 30 seconds matter. The 15 seconds before the first cash out, and the 15 seconds before the second.The double barrel shotgun deserves a mention. It 2 shots literally anyone. Combine that with either invis or a taser and there is no counterplay.Crossplay (console) has some of the most aggressive tracking I've seen in my life. Playing on PC? Use a controller, it will dramatically improve your aim/tracking unless you're on a professional, tournament winning CSGO team.If you're on the losing team you're  to the game. You die, (if your team wipes you respawn can double in length if you were 1 sec away from respawning) you then have to crawl across the map. In some cases it's not so bad, but in others you spawn 200m away and you just have to s l o w l y C R A W L over. You can also win with pure stall. Capture the cashout, gas grenades, fire, (edit: these can be countered by fire and smoke respectively to neutralize) dome shield, turret. There isn't counterplay to this aside from have one of your teammates be a medic. Even that's assuming the enemy team just lets you capture and d o es n 't shoot you.Overall, don't recommend. _childDocuments_.review: Make a name for yourself and get paid in THE FINALS, a free-to-play first-person-shooter game show where you'll face off in teams of three in a virtual arena. THE FINALS offers a unique game show take on the FPS genre, similar to Rainbow Six Siege's Road To S.I. 2020-2022 events.Featuring environmental destruction, it's possible to steal the objective right out from underneath an opponent in an outright disrespectful play. That's not all, THE FINALS also presents the player with a choice of specializations. Employ stealth with the cloaking ability, assert your value to the team with the healing beam, or bring the building down around you using the dash ability - just to name a few of these specializations. How you utilize the tools in your arsenal can completely change the course of the round.This game unfortunately suffers from a lack of variety. More weapon customization or upgrades along with more game modes would be a fantastic addition. I would also like to see an improved ping system for better communication and coordination between teammates. I don't foresee THE FINALS maintaining the top of the player charts unless they continue to stoke the flames ignited from its initial release. I am optimistic for the future of this game though.

_childDocuments_.review: The Finals has emerged as a groundbreaking title in the competitive shooter genre, captivating players with its unique blend of high-octane gameplay and innovative features. Set in a futuristic game show, it combines intense action with a strategic depth that challenges players to think and react quickly. The game's emphasis on destructible environments and dynamic movement adds a layer of complexity and excitement, making each match unpredictable and thrilling. With continuous updates and enhancements, The Finals keeps evolving, offering fresh experiences to both new and seasoned players.The Finals is set in a vibrant, futuristic world where players participate in a high-stakes game show. In this setting, contenders from various backgrounds come together to compete in intense, action-packed battles. The game's storyline is more about creating a thematic backdrop for the gameplay rather than a traditional narrative. This setting provides a unique and exciting atmosphere that enhances the competitive and strategic elements of the game, making each match not just a battle for survival, but also a performance on a grand, televised stage.This game is rich in gameplay mechanics and features. Let me break down the vital ones:In The Finals, movement is a pivotal aspect of gameplay, characterized by fluidity and agility. The game allows players to seamlessly navigate the environment, bolstered by advanced parkour elements like running, jumping, and climbing. These capabilities enable creative map traversal. Recent updates have honed these mechanics, especially in movements such as vaulting and zipline usage, making them more intuitive and responsive. This mobility not only contributes to the game's pace but also introduces new tactical and strategic layers. Positioning and environmental awareness become crucial for success. Furthermore, the game differentiates contenders based on build types - Light, Medium, and Heavy - each with distinct movement speeds. Light contenders are the quickest, fostering an agile playstyle, while Heavy contenders, though slower, offer increased resilience. This variety in mobility among different builds injects strategic depth into the game, prompting players to choose a contender that aligns with their preferred gameplay approach.The Finals features a versatile loadout system that allows players to customize their gameplay experience according to their preferred playstyle. Here's a breakdown of how the loadout system works:As of now, we are offered a total of 3 game modes:In my opinion, the visuals are quite striking. The game showcases clean and colorful maps, with settings like Las Vegas standing out for their visual appeal. The use of virtual renditions of real-world locations adds an intriguing layer to the futuristic game show theme. What really impresses me visually is the game's destruction technology. Watching environments collapse in real-time during the chaos of combat is not only visually stunning but also adds a dynamic element to the gameplay. However, I do feel that, while aesthetically pleasing, the maps could benefit from a more distinctive identity to make them truly memorable.On the audio front, this title makes an interesting choice with its AI voiceovers. The game features AI-generated commentators who react and respond to in-game events, which is an innovative concept in a multiplayer shooter. However, I find that the execution is a bit mixed. The AI voices, while a novel idea, lack depth and personality, sometimes coming across as rather dull and not adding much to the game's atmosphere. Additionally, while the overall sound design is decent, I think improvements, especially in directional audio, could enhance the player's ability to locate other players by sound, which is crucial in a fast-paced game like this.In conclusion, The Finals stands out as an innovative addition to the competitive shooter genre. Its dynamic gameplay, characterized by highly destructible environments and diverse class options, offers a thrilling and tactical experience. While the visuals are generally impressive, there's room for improvement in giving the maps a more distinctive identity. The audio aspect, particularly the AI voiceovers, is an innovative attempt but falls short in terms of depth and engagement. Despite these minor drawbacks, the game's commitment to fair play with a focus on cosmetic microtransactions is commendable. Overall, this is a promising title that delivers a unique and engaging experience, especially for those who enjoy teamwork and strategic gameplay. MidplayzI still suck at this game. 8.5/10

The destructible environments aren't just for show; they play a pivotal role in the strategy of each match. Players can create new pathways or destroy hiding spots, making every match feel dynamic and unique. The parkour and grappling elements add a vertical dimension to the gameplay, expanding the tactical options available to players.Enjoyability: This game is an absolute blast to play. The balance between strategic planning and fast-paced action keeps the adrenaline pumping throughout each match. The thrill of breaching through walls or collapsing an entire building to gain an advantage is unmatched. The variety of weapons and tools at your disposal ensures that no two matches feel the same.Future Prospects: Looking ahead, the game has the potential to redefine the multiplayer shooter genre. With its strong foundation, the game can evolve with new maps, modes, and destructible environments. The prospect of community-driven content and regular updates from the developers promises a continually updated experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have about 100hrs on PS5 on this game, and i am so happy it exists, its a needed breath of fresh air in the FPS industry.It has a great dev team behind it and i really hope it is here to stay, all it needs to be up the with other popular FPS titles like Apex, CoD, etc. is if it gets a well organized E-sport scene along with great content creator focused on this game. Appart from that i do not see anything holding this game back from become well respected and liked by most FPS fans.There are VERY frequent events with free rewards along with an LTM, seasons last long enough to finish the battle pass (which pays for the next), it is filled with creativ and well designed items that fit the great artistic direct this game has going on.I really enjoy this game and wish it and its devs the best of luck in this overfilled industry of live service FPS games, if you are on the fence about getting into it, give it a try, its free ! If you have friends to hop on with you i doubt you will have a bad time if you enjoy FPS games.So let me list the pros and cons in my opinion:PROS:- Great premise, heist style main game mode that encourages clutch plays, is very rewarding and requires to outsmart opponents in a 100% destructible environment, its great.- Art direction is remarkable, the lore is just interesting enough to be followed without being intrusiv or predominant (like Overwatch for example (no hate)).- Graphics are insanely good on every platform i have tried the game on (PS5, Series S, PC).- Monetizaion is very well present but due to the structur of the character costumization (not skins but parts of outfits, shirts, pants, gloves, etc.) it is worth it to mix and match if you care about consmetics in an FPS game.- Battle pass pays for the next one (*cough* cough* Destiny 2 (again, no hate i love D2)) and is full of creativ and well modeled items.- There are 3 classes, heavy, medium and light, they all have their pros and cons and there is plenty of choice for builds but it is not overwhelming and you generally know what you are going up against in a game.CONS:- No E-Sport scene yet, i think in 2024 where twitch is very known to mainstream and e-sports are also getting more and more attention it is important to have a good scene for your game if you are serious about it in the long run.- Balancing is good ovgerall but not perfect and it is unfortunatly console dependent, which makes it very hard to patch so good luck to the dev team, what i mean by console dependent is that in my opinion the games biggest balancing issue is lights, on PC that is, because snipers can be very strong if used correctly and there are simply more good snipers on PC due to M&K being more suited for FPS, especially fast paced sniping, on the other hand, lights are almost not a problem at all on PS5 for that same reason, if you understand invisibilty and other light tricks they are trivial if they are not played by a great player and those seem to be rare (at least in my current rank). So balancing seems to be tricky for those kind of reasons, should they nerf them ? buff them ? Do one on PC and one on Console ? i don't know, but all in all balancing is very good for such a young game.- Ranked is good, it is a tournament so very adrenaline heavy and once more emphasizes clutch gameplay, but i wish there was a way to see your MMR, right now the game has a system where after a ranked game they show you your current rank (Gold 1 for example) with 3 arrows above and 3 arrows below it, they can be filled or empty to indicat how much you progressed or regressed towards the rank above or below respectively. Its very basic and still way more complicated and confusing than just showing you a good ol' number like an XP bar.- Melee weapon hitboxes seem off on the recieving end, especially the mace for heavies look like they hit you via bluetooth.SUGGESTIONS:- I would like to be able to go into the shooting range with friends, to practice strategies etc., there is a private mode for private matches tho so its just a knit pick.- Make is possible to have custom team names like Rocket League for example, i know the AI comentators say the teams names pretty often but since they are AI they could learn to read custom team names, and if not, just make them say "red team", etc. but thats probably just me and way more complicated than i think anyways lol.- Discord quests and Twitch drops are great, keep em goingThats it folks, try THE FINALS and have a great day!

_childDocuments_.review: On console, I'm a CoD and BF veteran, did not like BRs like Fortnite or extraction games like Tarkov/Shadowhunt, because it seemed to complex or slow paced...However, since I m now on PC I just tried The Finals by chance and it felt like Battlefield 1. Weapongame, movement etc. So I feel like I am at home in this game, however the gameplay itself is very fast forward and "simple but complex at the same time". Why? Because the objective itself is very simple, but there are literally infinity ways to kill ur opponent or to steal the money. It is a good mix of nearly all genres I would say but they just mixed the good aspects together.With foam you can somehow build up some cover or climb up to some nice positions, you can destroy nearly the whole environment with explosives and teamplay is key here. PTFO is rewarding and round-times are between 12-20min I would say. Graphics are perfect, no bugs or glitches so far from my perspective. So the game is in a good state.What I dont like: - no minimap  (you need some time to learn the maps...)- no weapon upgrades/settings (yet?)- some skills/perks/weapons seem to be a little bit overpowered (invisibility or RPG), but that counts just for 1on1s All negative points are less relevant with a good team. So if you have at least one buddy this game is an absolute banger, Solo it is still enjoyable, but you need a good mindset ;)I think that this game is easy to learn but hard to master, so this could be a game with 1000s of hours in for a lot of FPS-Fans. And last point: it has a high ttk that suits at least my playstile very well. With good movement and aiming to can give some nice turn-ons and you really have duels in that game like 1vs1, 2vs2 and teamfights. Very often! I would rate it a 9/10 and I am excited for future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics and World Design:GTA VI is a visual feast that showcases the cutting-edge capabilities of modern gaming hardware. The attention to detail in Vice City is nothing short of breathtaking, from the neon-soaked streets of South Beach to the gritty alleyways of Little Havana. The game's dynamic weather and day-night cycle add an extra layer of realism, making the virtual world feel alive and constantly evolving.Character Design and Voice Acting:Rockstar has once again raised the bar in character design and voice acting. The protagonists are richly developed, each with their own compelling backstory and motivations. The voice performances, led by an ensemble cast of talented actors, breathe life into the characters, making them feel like genuine inhabitants of the criminal underworld. The witty dialogue and memorable one-liners that have become synonymous with the series are abundant, providing players with a truly immersive experience.Storyline:GTA VI's narrative is a rollercoaster of crime, betrayal, and redemption. The intertwining storylines of multiple protagonists keep players engaged and invested in the fate of Vice City. The plot tackles contemporary social issues and explores the consequences of a life lived on the wrong side of the law. The narrative is a testament to Rockstar's ability to weave a complex and engaging tale within the framework of an open-world game.Gameplay and Mechanics:Grand Theft Auto VI introduces several gameplay innovations that enhance the overall experience. The improved combat system offers a more responsive and fluid feel, making shootouts intense and satisfying. The addition of new vehicles, including motorcycles and boats, expands the range of transportation options, while the revamped AI ensures that both allies and adversaries behave more realistically.The open-world structure allows for unprecedented freedom, enabling players to choose their paths through the narrative and explore the vast city at their own pace. The plethora of side activities, ranging from heists and street races to casino gambling, ensures there's always something to do beyond the main storyline.Multiplayer:GTA Online returns in GTA VI, offering a robust multiplayer experience that seamlessly integrates with the single-player world. The multiplayer component features a variety of cooperative and competitive modes, as well as an array of customization options for characters and vehicles. The persistent nature of the online world ensures that players can continue to build their criminal empires alongside friends or rivals.Conclusion:Grand Theft Auto VI stands as a testament to Rockstar Games' commitment to delivering groundbreaking gaming experiences. With its stunning visuals, captivating narrative, and an expansive, living world to explore, GTA VI cements itself as a must-play title for fans of the series and newcomers alike. Whether causing chaos in the streets, engaging in epic heists, or simply soaking in the vibrant atmosphere of Vice City, this game is a triumph that sets a new standard for open-world gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my favorite FPS of the past few years. After years of playing half-baked multiplayer FPS games and games ruined by developers (Looking at you Overwatch), this game is very a breath of fresh air. Is it the most amazing FPS ever made? Certainly not. But is it fun? Absolutely. And that is the point.I would take most of the negative reviews with a grain of salt. The game is free and you lose absolutely nothing from giving it a try. Most of the negative reviews are just complaining about balancing they did after the beta. Which is just silly because that is what betas are for. They complain about silly things like how they lowered the movement speed a little bit (Which they didn't. They just changed the default FOV so it looks like you move slower. It's literally one of the first things i change when i play a new FPS game).The destruction in this game is really well done and the gun play can feel very satisfying. With the different guns, tool, and environments this game makes really easy to pull of pretty amazing combat. The environmental destructing allows each match to unfold into a completely different experience very regularly. The game is not complicated and the mechanics are very easy to understand. There are no complicated objectives of over designed game mechanics. The game doesn't take itself too seriously and you shouldn't take it too seriously either. It's a game that is fun for the sake of being fun without wasting your time with an unnecessary amount of features, gimmicks, and "innovative game-play." The Finals thrives in it's simplicity and that's what makes it so great. The Finals is just stupid fun. Especially with friends.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game has 2 issues to me, Enemies walking around just don't make any audible noise you can hear(meaning you are constantly rounding corners, just to be taken out by a team of 3 people), and the existence of the light unit. The light unit is designed with 1 ability that makes them nearly perfectly invisible, and another ability that allows them to dodge any damage 3 times, which acts as the most OP mobility option in the game. Not that they need it because they are also the fastest unit in the game. In my experience, what this had led to is the light units literally just spawning in without me knowing they are anywhere nearby, they then kill me in literally 1 second (All of their weapons have the best DPS in the game), and then they move on to ruin someone else's day. If I even try to run away from them (say we have a good distance between us), because of their objectively better kit and better speed, they WILL catch up to me and kill me no matter what I do. _childDocuments_.review: As of September 7, 2024, in light of the changes the devs have announced for season 4, I am tentatively changing my review from "not recommended" to "recommended" simply because I want to give the devs another shot. While the reasons for why I wrote my original negative review below and chose "not recommended" are still around as of this writing, because I enjoyed seasons 1 and 2 so much, I am hopeful that season 4 will bring the game back into a state that I will find fun (most specifically, the re-introduction of Cash Out as a/the ranked mode). If I could, I'd change my recommendation to "undecided," but since that's not an option and a "not recommended" can significantly damage a game's reputation, I'm going with "recommended" so as to not unduly affect the game's score on Steam when the devs have said they'll be changing a lot of what I and many others didn't like about season 3.I've also been playing the game a little bit after taking about two months off, mostly because I want to finish out the battle pass since I went to the trouble of buying it. Doing so has re-affirmed my belief that this game has really good bones, although again season 3 introduced many, many flaws that made things very un-fun for me (while largely failing to fix flaws that had existed before the season). So I have high hopes for season 4. If anyone's reading this who hasn't played before, go ahead and give the Finals a try, screw around and get your sea legs, and then see if the changes in the soon-to-be-started season 4 make this a game you like or not.For now, I'll leave the text of my original negative interview below. After I get a feel for season 4, I'll try to remember to delete this review and write a new one, good or bad.________________________________________________________________________I would have recommended this game in season 1 or 2, but as things are going in season 3, for me, I can't anymore.My issues are those of someone who has played the game more or less since the beginning (excluding the betas) and who came to love what the game was. I am no longer enjoying the game due to the drastic changes implemented in season 3. Another player coming in from season 3 for the very first time, for example, my love how the game is today.At any rate, here are some of my issues:-Most guns and other projectile weapons outside of the light class have been heavily nerfed in terms of either damage, recoil, or both. Several of the light class's weapons, meanwhile, are now overpowered. The movement style and low health of the light class encourages solo play, flanking, and surprise attacks. Lights also have numerous other items and abilities that make facing them unfun, including instant dashes, invisibility, a stun gun, and sonar grenades (i.e., wall hacks) with a very large radius, enabling them to almost always decide how and when they are going to fight you and withdraw if you are any class other than light as well. Most matches are now filled with light players mostly playing team death match instead of focusing on the objective, creating an atmosphere in most games that is completely different from that of season 1 and 2.-The introduction of Terminal Attack, a watered-down search and destroy mode, as the only ranked mode in place of Cash Out, the ranked mode the entire game was designed around from the game out. I really enjoyed ranked Cash Out, and the ranking system, while not perfect, generally resulted in you playing against players around your skill level, especially in season 2. Terminal Attack, with it's single life play, two teams of five, and no healing, etc., is a completely different game and one that I don't like at all. And to boot, since The FInals wasn't designed around Terminal Attack, the mode is extremely broken, with an extremely slanted meta heavily favoring lights. The maps being used weren't even designed for Terminal Attack, either, enabling snipers (also a light weapon) extreme lines of sight in most situations. (Quick overview of ranked Cash Out: Four teams of three players each compete to collect cash boxes, of which two spawn at any given time. You take a cash box to a cash out point and defend it for 120 seconds to claim the cash inside. You can steal an enemy's cash out if you can get close enough to it and interact with it for six seconds. The two teams with the most cash at the end of a round proceed to the next round. Cash boxes increase in amount as a round progresses, making it potentially possible for a team in last place to swoop in and steal second or even first place either by grabbing one or both of the last cash boxes in a round or stealing another team's.)-World Tour is a crappy replacement for ranked Cash Out. Ostensibly the rules are similar, but there is virtually no skill-based matchmaking, meaning either you are completely crushing the other teams or are being crushed. It's a completely different feel from the previous seasons. Each tour "leg" also includes only three of the already limited selection of maps in the game, an apparently in the coming weeks will also feature limited equipment loadouts. It's not at all like the ranked Cash Out I loved in season 1 and 2.-Almost all of the new weapons introduced this season are melee weapons. Coupled with the extreme nerfing that has been applied to most projectile weapons (except for lights, who got heavy buffs to already extremely powerful weapons), apparently Embark wants to turn this into a more melee-focused game. For heavies, right now, basically the only really viable weapon feels like the sledgehammer. I'm not opposed to weapon variety, but I also don't like melee weapons, so the slant of the game has shifted even further away from what I liked in season 1 and 2.I could go on, but I'm just tired of this game, now. The game mode I enjoyed is gone, the weapons I liked are all garbage now, the style of play has completely shifted, everything feels blegh. Embark keeps making bizarre choice after bizarre choice. Embark said they're going to "work on ranked Cash Out" and that Terminal Attack is just a temporary replacement, but that just sounds like so much corporate lying to me. And even if they brought back ranked Cash Out in season 4, I don't know if I'd want to play anymore considering how heavily everything else about the gameplay has shifted.At any rate, it's a free-to-play game, so feel free to install it, give it a try, and see if it tickles your fancy in its current state. It certainly doesn't for me, but maybe you'll like the way it is now.

_childDocuments_.review: A great idea executed poorly. great gun-play, the destructable environments lend to unique encounters on every stage, and a unique approach to challenging targets. The Light/Medium/Heavy setup is also very fun, and the customization is a fun addition on top. However, this is marred by the games many issues. Poor player matchmaking, poor balancing, poor community insight and support, rampant toxicity and cheating all throughout the game, and elitism as the cherry on top.the match you're placed in whether it be power shift or any other casual game-mode will be 1 of a few things. -a stomp where you have no fun because your teammates had 18 kills and spawn-camped the enemy-a stomp where you have no fun because you were killed 12 times, and spawn-camped for 8 minutesAnd, the rarest 3rd type, -a fun fair match where everyone's about evenly matched and no bull-honky is going on. You'll also get lots of AFK players, leavers, and farmers who aren't there to play the same game as you, they're in your way to collect a reward and f*&^ off. none of them are fun. Competitive is a travesty, and terminal attack feels like going to the casino except you're going in knowing every machine you touch will be rigged. This game is not a fun experience unless you're already invested into it, or are able to somehow engross yourself into the ever-shifting, neurotic community. Anyone shilling real money out for this game is an idiot.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the positives. "The Finals" truly shines when it comes to graphics. The developers at Embark Studios have crafted a visually stunning world, providing players with a feast for the eyes. From the intricately designed maps to the detailed character models, the game immerses you in a visually captivating environment. The attention to detail is commendable, creating a world that feels both realistic and fantastical.Gameplay follows suit, offering a smooth and engaging experience. The controls are intuitive, allowing players to seamlessly navigate the game world while executing complex maneuvers. The team-based matches add an extra layer of strategy, encouraging coordination and communication among players. The destructible environment adds an innovative twist, forcing players to think on their feet and adapt to the changing landscape, which is a refreshing departure from conventional FPS titles. It's disheartening to acknowledge that a game with such potential is marred by the presence of aimbotters and wallhackers. Despite the fantastic graphics and smooth gameplay, the experience is tarnished by these unscrupulous players who undermine the integrity of fair competition.The cheater issue raises questions about the effectiveness of the game's anti-cheat measures. It's imperative for the developers to take swift and decisive action to maintain the game's credibility and ensure an enjoyable experience for the majority of players who adhere to fair play.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember when you first launched Quake III online ? Your First Unreal Tournament in an obscure Asian Cybercafe ? The Battlefield Bad Company 2 destructibility experience ? Team Fortress 1 and 2 ? The thrill of playing Counter-Strike with the boys at a LAN or at home ? Now take all those experiences, heighten all the emotions incurred by x10, put it all in 3v3vPLUS style game play on super polished maps, an incredible vertical style game play, where everyone can be the leading man or team on the field, and get ready for blast off !First of all, I would like to point out that a game release in 2023, with what seems like not too  many game breaking bugs so far, pretty balanced, a nice selection of maps and different instances, all that for free !? INCREDIBLE Second, this is for me, the most fun I have had in a while playing a multiplayer game/shooter. It is nice to see the Arena style fighter back but with a more open feel, thanks to the destructibility of the environment and the movements of all three different classes, along with the abilities. I have enjoyed playing with the Light, Medium, or Heavy Class so far, and unlocking their abilities, gadgets, and weapons. Every game feels fresh and different, I don t know what the opposing team will be doing and I m not sure how I will get out of it either, it is like a game based around Brazilian Jiu Jitsu  - except the ground below you is not so sure anymore. The game feels perfect almost right now and I hope the devs won t add too many new classes - if at all, and improve incrementally without any game breaking gadgets, tools, weapons, or pay to win items like we can see in other games out. Seriously give it a try while the game is fresh and close to perfect, I pray it stays the same, that would be another miracle. As a Arena shooter and an FPS fan in general, try it, you wont regret it. The game play is simple but there is a learning curve and the possibilities of attack, defence are huge. Enjoy, 6/5 Stars for Me !!!

_childDocuments_.review: I played the beta pretty extensively, and I have to say that when I hopped in on the Light, I didn't notice a movement speed drop. Maybe it's because of the gap in time where I played a lot of other games where the movement speed is extremely slow compared to the high-octane movement of the Light in the beta, but I didn't feel like the "drop" was really an issue. Additionally, while the heavy is difficult to play against as a Light, if you play properly it's not impossible. Some of the Light's weapons were nerfed; I felt like it was a little fair to nerf the pistol, as I found myself not really playing anything other than the pistol or the sword if I needed to win. I can't comment on the taser as I never used it (I just didn't vibe with its playstyle). I still really enjoy the game. It's one of the only FPS multiplayer games I have where I don't feel pressured into being sweaty 24/7, I can chill and relax and take it easy while still having a good time. I have seen many people complaining about the movement speed, and honestly I 1. Don't believe it and 2. I don't care even if they did. As the Light, you're still moving at a ridiculous speed, and the other classes don't feel any slower than they did before. Embark themselves say they haven't changed the movement speed, just the animations and FOV, so perhaps it's not a problem of actual speed but of perception? Like how in a small car you feel fast at slower speeds while in a big car you feel slower at high speeds? I'm really not sure. I'd say, if you're looking for a fun FPS to play with or without friends, take a look at this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. This is the most exciting release we've seen in a long time, probably the best FPS out there right now, and it's free. Sadly, I can't recommend it in its current state due to several major issues.1. Rampant AA Cheesing: The controller AA in this is nastily overtuned... worse so than other games with this issue. The Finals has a "snap-to-target" on ADS, so you're effectively punished for actually aiming on controller vice just getting in the general vicinity of the target and cheesing ADS snaps. It's just free hits and headshots at the press of a button. Expect your experience with the game to go like this - Do as well as you normally would in an FPS > SBMM up to the point where every match is all just people who know how to abuse the game's egregious controller AA > turn crossplay off > go back to doing as well as you normally would > SBMM up to where it's entirely PC players playing on controller (or using reWASD) to abuse the game's egregious AA. 2. Rampant Cheating: On top of the AA issue, which becomes indistinguishable from outright aimbotting at higher SBMM, cheating in this game is currently run amok. As you SBMM up, recoil script usage becomes increasingly common as well. Anytime you die, the game tells you exactly what all the damage sources were so it's quite obvious when another player is cheating based on their weapon and range and it really ruins the experience.3. Latency Obfuscation: The game doesn't tell you your, or anyone else's, ping. If it's really bad, there's a lil red icon that'll appear at the side of the screen but you have no way of knowing how your connection is relative to the other players. I'm waiting to see how they address these issues and will amend the review if they manage to get at least the first two points better under wraps.

The use of AI VA is not only a lazy cost saving measure that shouldn't be needed by how much monetization is in this game, but it's not even used in an innovative or interesting way. The dialogue is turned off for me, so I don't have to listen to this machine spew out ♥♥♥♥♥♥ dialogue that adds little to nothing to the experience.TL;DR:  Good Game, Bad Devs, Enjoy it while it lasts.  Also, turn off your dialogue volume, you'll thank me later. -- Original Post: I want to recommend this game, it's really good.  One of the best multiplayer games I've played in quite a while. _childDocuments_.review: This game is the absolute culmination of everything wrong with current multiplayer gaming.  Worst solo queue experience ever.  Literally the most disappointing multiplayer gaming experience I've ever had.Let me preface this by saying that I have been waiting for this game since the minute it was announced, eagerly anticipating it.  Finally something new and fresh and potentially incredible.  That is not this game.If you try to solo queue in this game, you're going to have a bad time.  AAA multiplayer gaming had a plague set upon it years ago during the early days of Halo 2 called skill-based matchmaking (SBMM) and things have never been the same since.  SBMM is built to protect the lowest common denominator to ensure that thumbless goofballs that "just want to have fun" (read: goof off and completely disregard the experience of the other players on their "team") get to experience a win every now and then by doing close to nothing as far as investing time and effort into building skill and/or understanding the mechanics of the game they're playing.  While this occurs, the rest of us (what I like to call the "middle class" of multiplayer gaming) have to carry the weight of the team, and be continually matched up against teams that are triple-stacked with players that are either A. unemployed and play the game 24/7, B. Paid to play the game 24/7, or C. Are just as good as us, so we are constantly in a state of absolute teeth-grinding, white knuckle effort to just eek out a win one out of every 5-10 games.  Meanwhile, that lowest common denominator (that will likely move on to the next game without a care in the word) just flounders through the game, never bothering to improve or even learn from their peers.  That being said, even if they were improving, how would they know?  The SBMM will constantly ensure they are SWEATING TO THE MAX and there is no in-game experience to gauge your improvement by.  Just ass-stomping losses and a complete sweep by your team every 5-10 games.  It's the same roller coaster of peaks and valleys you see at a casino.  Keep the addict sitting in front of the slot machine by feeding them a win about every 30 minutes.  Give 'em that ol' dopamine hit and watch them drop another pay check of quarters into the machine.  SBMM is a cancer on gaming and the players need to stop supporting devs that utilize it.Edit#2: Ok, uninstalling.  The game just plays so disappointingly.  The matchmaking is atrocious, the bugs and glitches plenty, cheaters everywhere, braindead teammates constantly filling my team while the enemy team is nothing but clanned-up TTV squads.  HUGE disappointment.  Maybe Arc Raiders will be better, but I sure as hell won't be buying it without seeing a LOT of gameplay videos and reviews first.  This ain't it.Edit#3: Re-installed to give it one last chance.  I now have additional complaints about the game. 1 - The game STRICTLY REQUIRES you to play as a team, yet gives full agency for your team to build out their characters any way they like.  Want to be a healer?  Good.  You better be VERY good at it.  Want to be a tank?  Good, then you better be damn good at it.  Want to do anything but WORK the whole game and have a good time?  Forget it.  As a solo player, almost every match you join will be 2 Lights (an arguably worthless, out of place class), and they will not be specced to do anything but run around and try to "gank" opponents.  No utility for the team, whatsoever.  So, you try to "be the change you want to see" and play the medium class with healing and revives.  The problem of being teamed up with 2 light class players still exists, and you will be busting your ass the whole match to keep them alive.  To still lose.  If another team has an actual balanced makeup of classes, (or worse, are ALL HEAVY) you will lose.  You will lose dearly, and likely be fairly frustrated by the end of the game.  That's if the balanced enemy team that the SBMM has selected to win doesn't farm you and the other team for kills for 15 minutes.  In that case, you'll be pissed....if you actually stick around through that B.S.2 - Class items/equipment are all over the place.  There's too much variance in utility of items for each class.  You'll have one item that's damn near REQUIRED to use, and several others that are arguably near-worthless.3 - Damage registration doesn't make a lot of sense on some items.  For example, playing the  heavy class, you can shoot someone with the rocket launcher at point blank range, and the rocket launcher will kill YOU, but not the enemy.  What sense does this make?  How does that work?4 - The environment destruction is a fantastic element, but unfortunately the game is really built around it, and there's not much substance there besides that "neat" element.  It also ends up being rather annoying when you've finished a huge firefight with both other teams, and you can't even steal the objective because you can't get to it, because there's so much rubble all around that's blocking your path.5 - As many others have stated, nothing you do in the game makes any real difference, until the last 30 seconds of each vault or "cashout" process.  Sit back, wait for the last 30 seconds, then both other teams descend on the objective and whoever lives, wins the game.I can say one good thing about the game.  They don't penalize you for leaving matches over and over again, as far as I can see.  By day 2 after this game's release, I was already leaving 4/5 matches.  You either get matched up with 2 lights that are running around the map completely oblivious to any objective, or  you get paired with a team that is literally throwing themselves into gunfire and wiping as fast as the game will allow them.  GG.Again, this ain't it.  This game actually made me go back to Battlefield 2042, which is suddenly fun as hell after playing this jet-fueled aggravation machine. This game is a failed idea.New edit: As of 2/4/2024, I've dumped many more hours into this game.  The game is actually getting worse before it's getting better.  The matchmaking is atrocious, the balance is only getting worse with each patch, and all the developer does is roll out new skins for you to buy.  Bad game is bad.  The beta was exciting and fun, but the full game was not great at launch and terrible post-launch.New edit 6/21/2024: The game continues to become even worse than it was at launch, the longer it lives.  As I asked a close friend, "How many professional sports games do you know of that have more than two active teams playing at the same time"?  The game is a bad design from the ground up.  It's built around addiction mechanics based on the constant up/down, left/right/ win/loss ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that SBMM brings, and it's extremely clear in this game if you play more than 2 matches as a solo player.  I solo queued to diamond in season two, and it was EASILY the worst gaming experience i've ever endured.  I didn't go into season three with too great of expectations, but the first week of the season seemed bright and positive as far as design and development direction go.  I was SWIFTLY shown that I was incorrect by ~week two, as the SBMM ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and terrible mechanics of the game quickly showed themselves.  The game is not designed well at all, given that the developers refuse to relinquish the whole 3-4 team foundation, which is a complete failure from inception.  Add in a bunch of players riding the meta weapons / builds with an absolutely unwavering, bloodthirsty stringency. The game is disappointing at best, and absolutely soul-crushingly boring and oppressive, most commonly.New edit 7/27/2024: I keep trying to make this POS game work for me, but it's just not.  I just about burned myself out on multiplayer gaming in general, with solo queuing to Diamond rank in the ranked mode in this game's 2nd season.  My god, it was the worst grind I've ever experienced in any game.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit - Just a few weeks later almost EVERYTHING I mentioned below has been fixed or adjusted. Additionally I have never seen game devs be so fast with anticheat updates. Great signs for the longevity of this game. Shockingly few flaws for how many new concepts this game brings to the table. I have massive respect for the devs and there is no other competitive FPS I would pick over this. This is not meant to take away from the game, and is intended as feedback.- Queue bugs -Cancelling matchmaking does not work a majority of the time.Some infinite loading screen glitchesParty members load into game but you don't (this even results in mm penalties for tournament modes)- Physics bugs / issues -Goo can have some weird physical interactions with the map especially in instances of vaulting in crumpled buildingsThere are a few instances of getting completely stuck in debris, however it is super impressively rare given the destruction.- Balancing (Subjective obv) -One shot barrel (w/ C4) is wayyyy too powerful.Double barrel shotgun and invis cloak are individually extremely balanced, but in combination I would argue too powerful.I'm ok with the stun gun range increase, but I believe the stunned hipfire accuracy needs to be increased a bit.Stun duration is too long, I don't think it should last much longer than an SMG mag dumpGas duration is a little too longMines need some quantity restriction, a team running triple mines is like playing floor is lava on objectivesThrowing knives could use a minor buff- Maps - Elevators need to be looked at DEEPLY, either make them breakable or force them to stop at each floor.- Integrity -Cheaters... _childDocuments_.review: I am writing this review with over 100hrs in the game between the last Closed Beta and the Open Beta, and the current game. Pros:The game is amazing, the destruction adds an element I have not found in a game since Rainbow Six Siege. Unique visual style set in a world where things can be silly and it still aligns with the world itself. Simple systems and UI that work very well for the most part.Overall I love the game and the energy and the tense and exciting moments. Free to Play game with no P2W whatsoever. Insanely responsive devs (they patched animations one day after launch to help the movement feel faster again, ONE DAY) Cons: Balancing is in an interesting state, weapon bullets do not follow their recoil (If you put a dot on your screen, shots are always laser straight which can make people feel like there is bad hit reg also) The main game mode is broken in a sense, people may start to realize this over time. I proved in the last beta that you can do absolutely nothing until the last minute and a half and still qualify, the first cashout has very little impact even if you don't get a single team wipe. This is my biggest concern for the longevity of the game in all honesty, as people get more competitive and figure this out, it will change the meta playstyle and likely create some frustration and undesired effects. These are my points! I love the game overall and I have high hopes for its longevity. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 200 hours on PS5, my gametime here in comparison is just the free time I spend playing during breaks on my Steam Deck.I have never been the biggest player of any competitive games. I've dabbled in some over the years, but it has mainly been just me having a good time with friends. Overwatch (2), some Call of Duty here and there, PUBG, I've played quite a few PvP games but have spent somewhere around 100 hours at most over the years.The game show aesthetic, the gunplay, the higher TTK leading to more intense fights, the destructive nature of each map, it all culminates into one of the greatest experiences I've ever had in gaming. That feeling of winning a tournament after an intense match, your teammates all celebrating the victory as the jingle begins to play. That high is right there next to the feeling of beating an incredibly difficult boss the first time in any Souls-like game. I f**king love this game, haha.I can't forget to mention the damn soundtrack. Holy hell, the music team over at Embark are geniuses at keeping those musical ear worms in your head (please Embark, let me play those old tracks in the lobby again).If you want a competitive shooter where you can cause mass chaos on the map, requires teamwork for success, and you can relax on stressful days with some casual matches, I'd highly recommend giving this game a try.There's a lot more I can say, but I think it's best for the game to let it speak for itself. Seek me out if you want a fun clown as a teammate in the arena ;).

_childDocuments_.review: Remember when games were simple, but fun af? I remember. And so will you, after you buy this game.PRO/CON (depending on you): there is no gunsmith; there are no weapon customization; no attachments; no cosmetic decals; no armor; no perk packages. You can customize your loadout within the limits of your class, and then play. That's it. Enjoy. PRO: Game looks great. Game feels great. The battle space is completely destructable, creating a new experience each time that you play, despite the limited customization options, maps, and game modes. It's a ton of fun; and it's free. What do you have to lose?

In The Finals, maps encourages both head on approaches ala COD and long thought ambushes build on rotation as those seen in PUBG. As there are always three other teams, choosing when and how to fight is the key to victory.When looking to compete, multiple loadouts from your classic AR to katanas, sensor granades and Feudal spears will allow every player to find their style, all weapons spread along three main archetypes with different abilities to ensure stylish and clip-worthy wins. _childDocuments_.review: This esport-based service game is depressing... On the plus side, these are former Dice employees, so the buildings are destructible.Nevertheless, it's a lobby simulator of cheaters, and there's already been quite a bit of talk about it in articles, as well as controversy about the servers.The game is "poor" (2 modes, 3 characters with different abilities) but the gameplay is nervous, the characters are not memorable, they're similar to default skins that you could find on make Human (addon blender).I'm not used to these sprays (I'm more COD/CSGO/DOOM), so I can't say if it's due to the gunplay, or probably to Dice gunplay... others manage their aim better.The main mode, is a "search and destroy" (but for THE THUNE), while the second is a sort of concealed capture the flag, but with the possibility of breaking walls, etc. It changes the style.We're not reinventing the wheel: there are special abilities, Overwatch-style shields, grapnels and so on.Foam grenades are really cool when the going gets tough.So gameplay that's likely to interest you, if you like edgy FPSs.A nice game at first glance, but it doesn't appeal to me, because the universe is a kind of prefabs that you'd find on the unity store, i.e. lifeless... and its microtransaction-oriented aspect (the items are horrible)... the game's 1st intention is clear: to create a service game with simple Esport loop gameplay to engage your  available brain time to make you pay. But I understand people who like this game, try it, it's free.

_childDocuments_.review: The level/building destruction in this game is completely on another level. Absolutely an 11/10 on speed and intensity in the combat. Melee weapons do absolutely MONSTROUS damage and it feels stupidly satisfying when you ace an entire team of gun-toting plebs with the sledgehammer, sword or dagger. If you've ever wanted to finally actually feel like the Hulk or Superman or Goku just smashing through literally anything in your way, play Heavy class and you'll be hooked. You think you're the fastest ninja who has ever existed? Play Light class with the evasive dodge and a sword/dagger and you become speed incarnate. REALLY, really satisfying gameplay for sure. Needs more game types but I'm sure that will happen with time. More importantly, the foundations for mind-blowing gameplay are already in place. Game is pretty much a 9/10 until it gets more content, then it'll likely be a 10/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game, but my gosh is it unbalanced rn. Noticed it during the beta too. It is a very teamwork driven game which is great, but it's to a point where if even 1 of your teammates is dead, you're really in trouble. Like in other teamwork focused shooters like Siege and CSGO, you can clutch up if your placement, aim, and map knowledge are good. The spawn times that feel like an eternity in such as fast paced game play into this, but in someways it's necessary. Maybe these aren't even complaints, so much but the play style you need to win games feels very different and is hard to get used to. It's super fast and you constantly feel like you're under a shot clock having to run to the cashout, but at the same time, you have to play patiently. Super unique, the destructible environment is wild, and the arena style feel in it is awesome. Just hope they balance out the weapons, items, and abilities over time

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most fun I've had in a PvP FPS since Titanfall 2. High mobility, high flexibility, good gunplay, and good maps.The content is a bit slim, two gamemodes and a small handful of maps with alternative versions for each map- it's not a lot. However, each map is thick with detail and extremely freeform- there aren't lanes here, you truly do not know where someone is going to come from or how you'll route to somewhere. Watching corners becomes harder when someone can blow through the corner behind you, immobility is punished in this game. It's probably the most plastic map I've ever seen in a game. Every wall is optional. For negatives- With teams of 3, having a bad teammate really hurts. They recently changed mics to be on by default, which is a huge boost to comms- it used to be opt-in, which meant 90% of the time you'd be sitting in silence in matchmaking. There's not much to do about this unfortunately. Balance is still in a tricky spot, each player having 3 gadget slots and ~15 options for gadgets, however most of these have varying usefulness to useless compared to a small handful of options. Unfortunate, because some of them would be fun to use. One or two gadgets are usually considered mandatory for a given class, so that doesn't give as much flexibility as there maybe should be. The game theme is kind of goofy- the announcers are AI-voiced, and it's a "vr arena" for fighters. I hope they make better use of this but it comes off a bit poorly. This really doesn't matter too much I suppose. The cosmetics largely look fairly bad too. Just not very appealing, imo. But damn if I'm not having fun. Even when losing I can't really be too mad about it most of the time, and pulling off a clean team wipe is exhilarating.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for something unique in the battle royale/team based shooter genre The Finals is worth a shot. "Quick Cash" the main game mode, pits three teams of three players against each other as they fight for a vault (digital wallet) that must be brought to an ATM and guarded as its decrypted over several minutes. The first team to get two cash outs wins. Breakdown:Graphics- The game is gorgeous, full stop. Those with lower end specs may have issues.Gun-play- I'd describe gun-play as snappy...however some guns don't hit as hard you'd expect. Map Design- Nearly fully destructible maps with creative hazards and usable items such as poison gas tanks and exploding canisters add greatly to matches. At certain points special modes like "Low gravity"or a meteor shower will activate, impacting the course of play.  Classes- Light, medium and heavy classes are basically just as they sound. Each class has a different kit tailored to play-style with more you can unlock as you play. Monetization- strictly cosmetic, battle passes, the usual. Overall The Finals is a well made game that I would suggest to anyone who likes Battle Royales or Team-Based Shooters. If you're not a fan of those  types of games this likely won't win you over but may still be worth trying (it is FREE). As usual with this type of game it's highly recommended to play with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game because it's free. If it had even a $10 price tag, I would not recommend for most people but because it is free, its great fun for the first 25-50 hours or so. this game has some big issues tho, and I think if they arent addressed it will kill this game. #1. the gameplay while fun, is incredibly stale. there are only 2 modes, and they're basically just the same mode anyway. in Ranked and tournament games, you can only play one mode, and with the way the game is balanced, every game plays out pretty similarly. there are also only like 4 maps. and while they all feel fresh at first, it gets pretty boring just playing the same 4 maps over and over again.#2. the balance. the balance in this game i think is actually quite bad. for every class, you pretty much have 1 ability that is a lot better than the others, for example, if you play light class you have to take invis if you want to be competitive as Light is way too squishy any other way. and with each class, there are very limited viable options for weapons. for the light, you have to use either the pistol, shotgun, or MAYBE the smg, and the shotgun+ invis combo does not feel super satisfying to play with, and is extremely infuriating to play against. for the medium you can basically only use the Fcar and the Ak, and the heavy pretty much just has the lewis gun. #3. this one i think is more personal than the other 2 points, but i dont really love the gun play all that much. when it comes to automatic weapons, the time to kill feels oddly long, and the "recoil" is a weird mix of traditional recoil with some random bloom which makes it feel like they were trying to dumb down the gun play to help lessen the skill gap i guess. I come from a more competitive shooter backround, my most played game being rainbow six seige, and while that still has more than enough of its own issues, the gunplay is much more rewarding and skill based feeling. #4 this is also a balancing thing, but for some reason all the super cool and fun stuff just sucks in this game. want to be able to zip around the map with a grappling hook? it sucks and you'll die in like 2 seconds. want to use a sniper cause you love sniping in games? you're pretty much useless to your team because most of the objectives revolve around a small enclosed space. plus it does no damage. want to use sick throwing knifes and feel like a ninja? those just plain suck. want to use a cool revolver and feel like your one tapping people with a deagle or the apex wingman? good luck. that one can actually work *sometimes*, but the risk vs reward for it just is not worth it. want to use an awesome hammer that can smash through buildings? well you dont get a secondary gun so its just completely unviable due to the automatic weapons. I had fun overall with this game, but the mixture of stale gameplay, poor balance, and overall lack of identity outside of the destruction mechanic has kind of turned me off of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not an FPS enthusiast, and although I tend to try and play them all, I never play them for more than 100 hours. Everything offered is not slapped in your face once you boot up the game, and the store has some impressive stuff. They really do listen to player feedback. I don't recommend listening to what streamers and YouTubers are saying about the game, as they are complaining about the game's new ranked system and trying to overshadow how impressive and promising the game's overall direction is.For the casual player experience, The Finals is enjoyable with your friends and solo. However, I have to say the lack of communication from the players hurts the experience of the game a lot, as people tend to not speak at all. The weapons are great with some being more significant and overpowered than others. These things are inevitable in an online shooter game, but the game never feels like it's unfair.Overall, The Finals is a great game for competitive and casual audiences. _childDocuments_.review: The Finals is one of the best live service, first person shooters out right now. The game has a high skill ceiling which allows for new players to competitive pros the ability to enjoy it's wonderful sandbox. I think where The Finals shines is in three aspects: destructibility, movement, and gameplay mechanics.DestructibilityBecause the game is built by a lot of Battlefield ex-developers, the game has an incredible amount of destruction that can occur during a game. I've seen matches where players specifically try and destroy as much of the surrounding buildings as possible in the match. It can become a chaotic mess of rubble and rebar concrete pillars that you are jumping over. But it's amazing and allows for dynamic fights between the two teams throughout a match.MovementThe movement is very fresh and fluid. The light build has wonderful and fluid movement as you can have a grapple hook or dash special ability allowing you freely move across maps fairly quickly. The mediums has jump pads or zip-lines that can allow for even heavy classes to get on rooftops or jump across the map quicker than just running. I think the only class lacking any mobility ability is the heavy but it's expected that a tank character can't just go from one side to another in a second.Gameplay mechanicsEmbark gets to have a lot of fun with gameplay mechanics ranging from goo guns that allow you to climb or barricade yourself in. Or the dematerializer, which allows you to make holes in walls, roofs, or floors which allows you to jump through or shoot enemies unexpectedly. All in all there is a lot of fun and exploration happening by Embark here on The Finals. It's refreshing to see new takes on a familiar format.Overall, I highly recommend anyone to The Finals. It doesn't have that familiar of game types but it's worth learning and exploring this fun shooter. My favorite game of 2023 and most of 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: Most fun I have had in a multiplayer FPS since Titanfall 2.From the same developers that brought us Bad Company 2, and you can really feel it.  The full level destruction feels like where the battlefield games should have gone after Battlefield 3.  It really keeps each match dynamic, since the entire building you are trying to defend can be blown up in different ways, each objective rarely plays out the same each time.What actually is the Game?In quickplay there are two modes, `Quick Cash` and `Bank It`.  Both modes are 3v3v3 team based matches.In Quick cash you have to take a 'cash box' to a 'cashout station' and defend it until a timer expires.  Other teams can steal the cashout from you and whichever team is in control of it when the timer expires gets the cash.  Do this twice to win the round.  It sort of plays out like king of the hill, except it only matters who is in control at the end, not who held it the longest.In bank it, you will collect coins from around the map rather than a cash box.  When you defeat a player you can then pick up any coins they were carrying.  If you manage to bring these coins to a cashout you can deposit them (takes about 3 seconds of holding an interact key) and this will add them to your teams score.  First team to hit the score limit wins.Overall, I much prefer quick cash, and I think the 3v3v3 nature really helps keep things interesting, since all teams are constantly attacking and defending, sometimes at the same time, rather than the more simple attack/defend system most games have.  There can be a lot of strategy around when to attack to let the other teams weaken each other first.There is also a tournament mode, which is very similar to Quick Cash, except with no score limit so the team with the most money at the end of the timer wins.  There are also some other differences, like limited respawns and bonus money for things like kills.  I don't really play this mode as much because I find it a lot more sweaty and I am just here to have fun.I find this game great to just mess around and have fun in, and if you enjoyed the likes of Bad Company 2 or other early battlefield games then you will probably enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi my name is Omnirock and I like to smash things with hammer, sometimes head. The Finals scratches that destructive FPS itch in spades with fully destructive levels and chaotic gameplay that is easy to pick up with a high skill ceiling. It's an objective based game that very much focuses on team work to make the dream work. A dynamic push and pull of attacking, defending, escort and making hail mary plays. Very friendly F2P model with some brilliant cosmetics available for those looking to spend some dosh. Season Pass is split into free and premium tiers with the ability to earn back what you put in for the in game currency cost (Multibucks are the in game currency and it costs about $13.49 CAD for the 1150 MB required).  All in all, a fun game that can be a lot of fun when vibing in a decent team or with friends. Not the kind of game for those looking to TDM or just mindlessly frag (although a couple modes do lean in this direction more than others, it's not the main focus). Give it a shot, it's free, and deserves more attention.

_childDocuments_.review: SKILL BASED MATCHMAKING SUCKSHere's my honest review of the game based on different categories: Gameplay: The movement is as good as it gets. I don't think I've played a better game in terms of movement. Same goes for gun gameplay. Weapons are cool and the feel of shooting is great. I like the idea of the classes according to the rock paper scissors principle. Some abilities are anti-fun but that's alright. Some abilities are really creative and fun. I'll talk about the game modes later. 9/10Maps: I think the maps are decent. Ranked maps are a bit too complicated in my opinion since the buildings have so many floors, it can get frustrating at times. I like SYS$HORIZON since it is a more simplistic map. Spawn points are too far away sometimes. However, overall decent. 7/10Game Modes: There are three game modes as of right now: cash out, power shift, bank it.- cash out: I think it's great they are trying something new but I feel like the gameplay in this mode is too chaotic. It feels so random and it's unplayable solo. You need to have a good team and good team coordination to win, however it feels sooooo random a lot of the times. This is especially true for ranked. Once the vault is deposited people just camp around it with all of their gadgets. There is some counterplay such as the light emp grenade but i really dislike the gameplay once the vault is deposited. - power shift: similiar to hardpoint from CoD but the hardpoint is moving. It's a more casual game mode which is fun at times.- bank it: In my opinion, it's the best game mode so far, as the team composition isn't as important as in cash-out and it's less about defending. Killing enemies is more rewarding since they drop money which you can deposit into the cash out. I am hoping for many more casual game modes such as snd, tdm, domination. I think they would really do a favor to the game and its players if they would introduce them. I've seen that they will add a new mode early May similar to the normal game mode in cs2 which is great. Let's see how that goes. Overall 5.5/10Skill based matchmaking: In my opinion skill based matchmaking is the biggest critique of the game along the games modes. I don't have too many hours in this game, less than a hundred, but as of late I can really feel the skill based matchmaking which makes the game so anti-fun. The devs announced that there is sbmm across all game modes which I really don't understand. I consider myself a decent player, I was global in csgo and had a fairly high level in faceit all solo so I think I can assess it fairly. In literally all game modes I have to sweat to win games and have a decent score. This is so not fun. I want to play the game casual at times and not play an esports tournament. Why does the game not just divide the gameplay into casual games with no sbmm and ranked gameplay with sbmm. That's how it should be. Recently, they have upped the sbmm ensuring that the games will be more "exciting" but that's the wrong approach in my opinion and it really stops me from playing the game more frequently. big minus pointIncentives: There are no real incentives to keep playing the game. Yes there is ranked, but it doesn't feel like csgo/cs2 or League but that's also correlating to the game mode cash out which I simply don't like. There are skins for weapons and gadgets, however it's just farming exp and playing the game nonstop, no tasks or anything. There are tasks in your career which grant you skins, emotes and stuff which is decent. My rating of the game so far: decent 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: While thinking about what I was going to write in this review I have determined that this game's main selling point above all else is providing a squad based shooter game set in maps that are both large and highly destructible. It's hard to overstate how important this is - as this is something that differentiates it from most shooters which are quite frankly uninteresting to me. No two games are the same, and there's a lot of breadth to strategies you can run. What would be hard obstacles in other games are more opportunities here.The cashout gamemode is brilliant in how it so often boils down to extremely tense moments which can be very satisfying, it struck the balance perfectly of having a clear likely winner / looser but still allowing for last minute reversals and unexpected comebacks. Terminal attack lacks this for the whole game but per-round it gets this feeling right on the smaller scale, power shift does not have much of this but it's fun to mess around with all sorts of gimmicky strategies there. With good teamwork being integral to every gamemode of course.You can theoretically get pretty much any cosmetic for free as well, which I appreciate. Granted, you'd need to grind multibucks for at least 3 seasons from the free battle pass in order to get into the premium pass loop to get a good income of coins and cosmetics - but the point is you don't have to spend much or even anything to look good. Shame that you can't customise the colours of your cosmetics but I think tabg has spoiled me there as many other shooters I've seen, you can't even mix together different items of clothing.The game's gunplay and movement are not that interesting but they're better than a majority of comparable games I've played. There's nothing really  about this game, so definite reccomend.Half the reviews seem to be complaining about chinese cheaters... I've had exactly one run in with that so far. Not a big deal. Balance by and large is improving every update, I feel like the people complaining about bad balance decisions are either new players or have a short memory, as things used to be far, far worse.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided I'd give the game a try, and I played it for a short amount of time before I had my fill of it.The gameplay itself is fun. The gunplay feels good, the enviromental destruction isn't extensive but it is satisfying and it helps in creating defensive positions or eliminating them (Can also end up stuck in place if you aren't careful) and graphically it looks good.That being said, it feels like the most soulless kind of free to play game you can find. And this isn't just in regards to the monetization (Which is pretty extreme), but also in the core game design being "By the book modern gaming" as you can get, removing any and all charm from the final product.You got the standardized character customization that does not let you have male and female exclusive options, all thrown together. You got a bunch of cosmetics that aren't made with the thought of "Is this aesthetically fitting?" being replaced with "Is this something that will sell?" and a distinct lack of any kind of charm to it. Oh, and also AI voice acting, which probably makes the whole thing worse, but at least they gave the game some good sounding AI voices, though frankly it'd have been vastly improved if they had Dagoth Ur being the announcer if you're going with AI.Overall, I will say this: It is a "Functional" game. It's fun enough to play, it works, it's expensive, and it lacks any kind of soul. A perfect "Modern Day" game.
