name: The First Descendant
detailed_description: PLAY FREE NOW About the Game The First Descendant is a free third-person cooperative action RPG shooter featuring high-quality graphics. Experience the fun of strategic boss fights through 4-player co-op and various unique characters, exciting gunplay, and looting. A variety of equipment is necessary for growth, and you can obtain them through clearing scenario missions within the game or in the World Missions where cooperation is crucial and battles with huge bosses. The player becomes a Descendant in the game and is given a mission to fight against the invaders for the survival of humans and to protect the ‘Ingris continent’. The player can experience a spectacular story by growing stronger through various missions and stories to finally discover the Descendants' secret. You can also feel the First Descendant’s unique atmosphere through high-quality fields developed with Unreal Engine 5 and gain a new experience of reality and SF fantasy coexisting in one place. Charming and Unique Characters You can play various characters with distinctive concepts and battle styles. We plan to add various customizable elements such as skins for each character to support character decoration. Exciting Battles and Dynamic Action Using Various Skills and Firearms Experience the First Descendant’s exciting battles composed of various characters with unique skill sets, free movements, and chain actions through Grappling Hooks, colorful firearms, and additional effects. With these, the player can create any battle style they desire. Battles With Huge Boss Monsters Through Cooperative Play You can target huge boss monsters with different appearances and abilities through 4 player co-op play. The various difficulties will stimulate your competitive spirit, and you can destroy or extract various parts of the huge bosses through 4-player cooperative play. By targeting the huge boss’s gimmicks, you will be able to experience a more compact team play. Motivating Play and Growth You can equip a character with 3 guns, 4 secondary accessories, and various sub-weapons. Of course, there will also be items to enhance a character or their firearm stats or add a new ability all together. A variety of equipment is a necessary element for growth, and you can obtain them through clearing scenario missions within the game, or in the World Missions where cooperation is crucial and battles with huge bosses. We provide equipment so you can develop the characters to play continuously through character growth and acquiring and combining the various equipment. Use it to challenge yourself with more difficult tasks and enjoy the thrill of clearing them.

I spent my first free upgrades poorly not knowing how games like this work.  So after the season pass and buying Enzo instead of grinding for him, I broke down and bought Ultimate Lepic plus 4 Energy Activators and spent the rest of the $200 in Caliber on Crystallization Catalysts.  Now the game is fun again after $220 plus tax.  I hope during the second 300 hours I get more than 1 Energy Activator blueprint and 2 Crystallization Catalyst blueprints.  They do drop, even though I thought it was impossible.  I guess with more power it all goes faster.  I thought Viessa would be my main, but now I'm liking Enzo.  Enzo might get the next 4 crystallization catalysts.  My Bunny still kind of sucks at anything besides open world farming.  So I have Viessa with chill, Bunny with electric, Sharen with electric, Enzo with non attribute, and Lepic with fire.  That's one character to do each reactor type.  I won't get anymore characters except by accident.  I wish I had upgraded long distance maneuvering instead of multiple grapples.  I had millions of gold and didn't know what to spend it on, but now its all gone.  Third update.... With the real dollars I spent, I was able to get a 500K+ DPS white ammo weapon based on critical hit rate.  The white/common ammo weapons will always scale higher than orange/green/purple ammo weapons because of critical hit rate and critical hit damage modules available.  Weak point damage on other white ammo weapons won't ever be as good as having critical hit chance and damage first.  So the Tamer will never scale as high as Enduring Legacy.  With my high DPS high critical chance white ammo weapon I was able to open tons of amorphous materials that I had collected, very rapidly, to get more of the Energy Activator blueprints and Crystallization Catalyst blueprints.  Most of the "transcendent" descendant modules in this game are worse than having no transcendent module, they were obviously not play tested.  Once you have one white ammo high critical chance base weapon maxed out, then you can slap some defensive mods onto any descendant that you unlock, and go bossing.  Once the DPS is present, you only need team coordination with randoms in public matchmaking (who do not go down all the time) in order to beat Hanged Man, Obstructor, Frost Walker, Molten Fortress, etc.  Descendant skill based solo bossing requires high investment, high resources, and getting lucky with a glass cannon build.  But any descendant can solo all of the solo bosses once you have a maxed out high critical chance white ammo weapon.  The highest rewards come from repeating the content that is beneath you many times quickly.  Being able to open amorphous materials in 10 seconds instead of 10 minutes allows you to grow the account exponentially.  Being able to dungeon run in 2 minutes instead of 10 minutes no matter how (upgrading a Bunny first, rewards the most).  Being able to clear Outposts with Sharen in less than a minute instead of 5 minutes rewards the most.  Killing reactor elites in less than 60 seconds unlocks everything for you.  And Enzo doesn't even need to be upgraded, he just needs to be on the account or in the group to unlock all of the treasure.  You need Bunny, Sharen, Enzo, and that maxed out white ammo weapon (there aren't many viable purple options, so I maxed Thunder Cage first and Enduring Legacy second).  Everything else you grow is not going to add as much value to the account, even if it is more fun to play and Bunny is boring.  Enzo is my Enduring Legacy team bosser with his matching transcendent.  Viessa and Lepic are mostly for mobbing but worse than Bunny.  Lepic will become a niche solo bosser only.  This game rewards you for smashing the lowest hanging fruit the fastest and repeatedly.  Repeating trivial content faster will negate any and all skill checks.  Above is a 44 hour review and a 300 hour review.  Now I'm sitting at 600 hours with Ultimate Gley and Ultimate Valby farmed approaching mastery rank 20.  Problems with this game is that any time/money upgrades you spend on normal non-ultimate descendant characters is wasted because you will want full access to all transcendent modules and the higher base stats.  I should have maxed my Ultimate Lepic first, but fell in love with Enzo and the transcendent "supply firearm enhancement."  In fact I have all of the Ultimate Lepic materials gathered from just upgrading Enzo, so that was money wasted.  I also have a selfish Enzo build where I run around with infinite rockets.  Reactor drops in this game are also terrible because 3 things have to match to be useful, the weapons type, the skill type, and the sub stats.  All non ultimate characters are for is progressing the mastery rank by getting them to level 40 for the first time.  I will probably eventually delete all non-ultimate versions of each character, especially because when you craft new characters you have to buy slots for them.  Besides the Ultimate versions wasting your non ultimate upgrades, and the terribly impossible time farming reactors that drop with unmatched useless stats, you also acquire tons of amorphous drops of things you have already collected and don't need anymore, and there is nothing to do with copies of the stuff you already have.  Fully building out a Bunny first will probably help you unlock all other content in half the time.  I just didn't want to play Bunny because she is boring and has a schizophrenic always running requirement. Plus she is not the Ultimate version.  If you're going to buy one Ultimate, buy the bunny one and make it your starting character to unlock everything else.  Instead of buying any Ultimate, you could more cheaply max a normal Descendant like Enzo or Bunny, who will unlock every other character and weapon in the game.  I basically used my Ultimate Lepic to farm flame void shards.  And Ultimate Lepic boss farms faster than Enzo, but Enzo gets it done.  I actually acquired the parts for building an Ultimate Lepic before getting the Blair pieces which did not drop for me for the longest time.  I'm glad they fixed Frost Walker so that you can gather flames from his frenzied state.  This will be one of my main games that I come back to for the new content. I could have kicked off my account progress with $40-$70 instead of $220 if I knew how to play these types of game to begin with.  So I wasted $150, I feel like this game deserved $70.... but its too soon to tell.  They need a way to absorb non-ultimate progress and slots into the ultimate versions, they need to eliminate useless reactor RNG, they need to let everyone reclass and respec without penalty, they need a positive use for all of that amorphous material farmed that you simply don't need anymore because you already have it.  Because as it is now your build is rigid and mistakes cost days.  Rebuilding or respecing a character would take weeks if you didn't know what you were doing.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Gameplay is pretty fun, monetization is nuts but not necessary. For a free game it's worth playing and then walking away from whenever you hit your limit. There was a lot of discussion around this game as a Destiny like looter shooter when in reality it's infinitely more like Warframe. Gunplay feels good, not great though as the combat really excels when using your abilities. There's a great amount of different weapons to choose from to fit your playstyle. The Descendants all feel very unique and have their own satisfying gameplay loop whether you want to be a tank, ice caster-type, or speedy glass cannon. From what I've seen, most of the Mixed reviews come from the incredibly aggressive monetization/MTX from Nexon. Fair criticism considering things like power upgrades are about 5x more expensive than a game like Warframe. That being said, you can absolutely grind out the additional Descendant including the Ultimates if you're patient and willing to grind. The paywall is really if you just can't gut out the grind anymore. For a free-to-play game it's absolutely worth downloading and trying out to see if you like it. I can absolutely say you can spend 20-30 hours in this game having fun with zero money spent if that's your issue.

_childDocuments_.review: With enough wrangling, you can get a solid gameplay experience.Frame generation adds a lot of input latency however, so avoid that.A bit of warframe, a bit of destiny. Micro transactions are pricy for what they are so avoid those.Gameplay is solid and simple, unfortunately too simple for some missions.Being able to dynamically join in to active missions is neat, really like this feature for swinging by and helping strangers out.Build theory crafting options are really solid, systems for what to farm and where are built in well, drop rates too. I would say it’s on par with warframe drops from what I recall.The real challenge is behind hard mode after a career clear.Bouncing between pc and console requires third party account, but works great.For steam deck, expect 30 fps, messy in some areas and situations.HUGE PLUS For free to play, time delays for building stuff is usually about a half to a third of what warframe does.Instead of 3 day waits on things, it’s a more reasonable 1.5 days being the worst I have seen so far.Overall verdict:It’s fine, it’s free.It shines in some areas, and needs work on some rough edges. There’s a roadmap, and the devs have been receptive to criticism. Kinda want to see how this one rolls out, gives me early days warfame nostalgia. Jank and all.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game and I find myself having fun but then I hit issues like the bosses. Colossi feel boring as they're just bullet sponges, The bosses that aren't Colossi are just regular units but with boss health bars and they get 3 orbs that after beating one health bar you have to defeat the orbs before you can damage the next health bar. This is on EVERY BOSS. It gets boring after the 4th one and the orbs only slightly change after the 40th-ish one where now you have to defeat them in a certain order. Bosses (even colossi) should have phases to them to make them unique instead of just the same thing over and over. Not to mention that the Colossi fights all happen in practically the same area with no unique looks which doesn't look cool at all. It looks bland compared to the rest of the game's environments.There's a part in the game where you have to hunt down a enemy with a cool ability (not gonna spoil the story) but you expect there to be a fun boss fight. Well dreams are made to be crushed I guess. Instead you get a cut scene (which looks cool IMO) of what happens to that specific character but with every cut scene and dialogue in this game the audio is not synced with it. Imagine watching an action movie but all sound is about 2-3 seconds late. Not fun at all and this is a constant problem throughout the game. Annoying when characters lips aren't synced with what they're saying but worst when guns muzzle flash isn't linked with the gun shot sound.The world looks pretty but its also dead. There's usually 1 to 3 other descendants in the same zone as you at a time which would be fun but you usually go to the zone to do the "main quest" which feel like side quests and if they're already running it then you either choose to do the one closest to you or try and find which quest they're doing so that you can do them as a group. If you're not doing the quests then there is nothing really happening in the environment. Maybe there's 3 really weak enemies walking together but on each area there's probably only like 4 of those patrols max.Overall the characters feel fun to move and shoot with and the world looks nice but for content within the game it's pretty dead. The game feels like it had more artist then it did programmers and designers.

_childDocuments_.review: OK so I've tested this on my PC and on the SteamDeck on another account.Pros: Crossplay & Linux/SteamDeck Support. I honestly didn't think this game would run at all on the deck. Was pleasantly surprised that using FSR we were able to get 60fps with a mixture of medium and low base settings. With destiny not being available on Linux for anti cheat red tape, this leaves the platform missing a good, ACCESSIBLE, looter shooter. Where Warframe in its current state is harder for new players to get into. No secondary launcher. This one speaks for itself if you know what I'm talking about.Real Free 2 play; I was worried this game was going to be forcing purchases down my throat. While there is a shop, battlepass, and premium currency in the game. They took a page out of Warframe's book and let you use earned gold from just playing to purchase blueprints in order to craft premium weapons & Descendants.UI; The UI and controls are relatively simple to understand & borrows from similar games so its not overly complex.Combat; combat feels similar to other 3rd person shooters like; Remnant, and Gears of War.Cons:Constant crashes that seem to be caused by the server.Bugs using DLSS and FSR sometimes making the server never connect.Gameplay; the gameplay feels like a mix of Destiny & Helldivers but the way point and marker system can get confusing. That and sometimes finding your party members is difficult because the text doesn't stand out.All in all this game can become very great. If they solve some of the performance issues and crashes I could see this game nabbing a chunk of the gaming community that destiny hasn't touched. Linux gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: I have 97.3 hours in the beta. I was one of if not the player with the highest MR in the game at 23.I know this game. It is fantastic. If you want strats or a guide, I'll leave the basics at the bottom. Edit:I'm 11 hours in, (Now 29 hours) just past Devo. He dropped a lot faster than in the beta. Currently, I'm worried about the challenge of the game. (it picks up alot just after devo, pyro was a big bottle neck, I am seeing zones with just me in it for hours now.) I'm assuming it hits around lvl 100 since that's what Hard-mode looks to target.Let's all dive into this without worrying about how we compare to others. The fastest players might sprint through everything, but the grind will slow them down enough that a mildly jogging player will catch up quickly. Expect a grind, btw. I grinded for 20 hours for a single mod in the beta. Drop rates get rather nuts:One mod dropped for something like 1000 total players from the data I found on it. It was a 1/10000 drop chance on a mob that spawned in about 1 in 20 packs. No player actively farming got it; it was an accidental drop.With all of that said, bunny and range plus power is the fastest farmer. Gley was broken in the beta; she will be broken again. If you get her in time, you will have her long enough to clear the entire set of bosses and farm for your chosen bossing set.I have only completed the Dead Bride set in the beta; it was something like 1.5k extra hp, which is very worth it. I know Pyro also had a set, but I never completed it. Primes or Ultimates are good. You want them. But the farm was around 20 hours per Ulti. Probably more now. I assume you will see players getting their first farmed set on day 3 to 4. Those will be the top players in the game, so don't expect to keep up unless you have 70-ish hours by then.I'm rewriting my guns portion:Guns are ruled by the legionaries at launch, my Thunder Cage is already hitting in the 50 to 55k range at around lvl 50 (gun-wise), so seriously, look into keeping them up to date when you hit milestone levels. (For an everyday player, this would be closer to the hard mode section than the campaign.)Re-roll for Crit dmg/chance, and %damage, try and get the yellow stats.Mods section is being reworked:Range and damage are the name of the game for the campaign. I wouldn't worry about anything else until hard mode. These two will help you clear large packs and 1 to 5-tap mini bosses or challenge enemies. Skills do ♥♥♥♥ all to raids in the early game but ramp up like crazy. Do not waste your Crystal cats or the extra 20 mod slot thingos I forgot their names lol.They are both about double what I remember them costing in the beta. So a 20 to 30 hour farm.Watch Reddit for the best mods. Players will find them much faster than YouTubers will. Upvote good builds, help everyone see what works. If their is a market, its good for the players if its broken early. You can make money late game for now we want everyone prepped to farm their hearts out.My final notes, Gley is a boss killer but Jayber was OP as ♥♥♥♥ for bossing in the beta, he solos everything. Bunny is ass at bossing, Most other characters were not optimal for every boss. But they can work if you let them breath. Dont steal the bosses attention from your tanks, and if you cant kill a boss stop fighting it and farm hard and fast. Seriously 3 or 4 tries should be enough to see if you dont DPS it hard enough. If you are out DPSed then move on.*Tl:dr *Watch Reddit for mod drops. Guns will be wild; don't trust "this is the best gun in the game videos." Don't waste your Forma. When bossing, don't waste time losing to it, just go farm high-level mods.*End of Tl:dr*Forgive my grammar; Grammarly is yelling at me for something like 30 missed commas, but I don't care to clean this all up. I hope my info helps. You could very well see my builds on the Reddit. I have a whole week off and some money for the game. Happy grinding fellas!

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiralling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I stopped playing this game because it simply is not fun once you reach the endgame and start with pretty much endless grinding because there is nothing else to do in this game.Normally I am not against grinding in games, when you grind towards something that actually feels worth it. In this game you grind to get characters and weapons, that you can farm other characters and weapons faster by doing pretty much the same content again just faster.Then when you have the character or weapon, you grind to make it better by grinding again for upgrade materials and in many cases you even farm the same contents over and over again just to do the same again once this character or weapon is done and you move to the next one.Or you have to farm for a character because this character has one ability that you need to farm something specific like Sharen for example, so what if I do not want to play Sharen ? Well good luck getting those specific Amorphus Materials.The best thing about this game is the combat combined with the movement, I did not play all characters but every single character I played [Jayber, Ult. Bunny & Ghley, Lepic, Frenya, Enzo]  was fun to try out and get used to.The story is nothing special, after a while I started skipping because I lost interest in all the generic dialogs and when you are not "slapping the serpent" to some of the character models I see no way to get attached to any of them.The cash shop is another argument against this game, everything is overpriced and with the endless grind they try to force you to buy either the characters or the upgrade materials to avoid countless hours of monotone repetitive grinding. I bought 2 Ultimate Decendents myself to skip the boring grind. But in the end what did I get ? Just two more characters that had to be upgraded by grinding the same content again just to start farming for the next weapon or character afterwards.I know that they have to make money somehow, but there are better ways than going full scammy sammy mode.Without a story and content that keep people playing even after they geared up I see no reason to keep playing this game at all, which is pretty sad because I really enjoyed the beta's and the launch of the game. But at it's current state it's just your average google play store waifu collector with good combat gameplay managed by Nexon....

_childDocuments_.review: Let me first of all say that the only reason I'm recommending it is because it is free. If it was paid, I would not. I played a bit of the beta back in October and I've about caught up to where I was then, so I feel like it's an okay time to write this.I would say that this feels like a love child between Destiny and Warframe, except there wasn't enough love and it was just a surprise pregnancy after one month of dating and the parents decided to stick it out and see what happens. There's technically potential for it to turn out okay, but probably not a lot. Let's start with the pros.-Character design of the actual Descendants is solid. I think this is where the most attention went.-Some mechanics have some nice quality of life perks to them, like weapons keeping mods slotted when you swap for the same weapon of a higher level.-Gunplay is okay, not amazing, not particularly great, but it could have been worse. Definitely developing some weapon preferences early, especially with the Auto Rifle.-Voice acting is decent for what it is. Just the voice acting though.-Enemy design is pretty okay. Nothing super memorable, only issue I take is the Cabal Phalanx ripoff but they're not the only ones to do it so meh.-A lot of the similar elements from Destiny, Warframe, and Division actually do well. The weapon gear system, the mod system, the Mastery system. I hope they have more weapons and more Descendants over time. I think it could be a less successful but still decent Warframe style game.-There's been day 1 hotfix and maintenance compensation handed out! It'd be nice if they kept that up beyond day 1.Cons:-Script writing is atrocious. I can't tell if they're lining up the Guide to be a villain or if the writing is just so bad it just sounds like it is. Either way it's a bad time. Voice lines are predictable after knowing hardly anything about the characters. It sounds like a 15 year old wrote it.-The subtitles often don't actually line up with what the characters say, either using different words or having grammatical errors. Haven't noticed any spelling errors yet.-The lip sync on the characters is awful. Either being completely out of sync or just so lazy with the animations, I've seen better out of Skyrim.-The default poses and animations of some of the characters are so strange for creative choices. Alpha always has his hand on his chin, like he's trying to subtly cover some strange bald spots. Nobody actually talks like that for minutes at a time. Guide has a computer hacking looking animation, but it's only like a 2 second loop. Super repetitive.-I hate Jeremy. Not like a douche-y character that's designed to be a douche, but like I'm not sure there's enough of a brain behind the design to even really call it a character. Also his voice acting is actually pretty bad.-Not a big fan of some parts of the UI. Having the character health and ammo count right next to the character isn't great. I know The Division did that too and it was okay there, but it was also orange. Here it's just white and a faded red for the health, so it's not nearly as noticeable or easy to see. I actually was several hours into the game before I knew where my health bar was even at.-The NPC that doesn't actually talk and just has subtitles for tutorial sort of things for Descendant and weapon upgrades goes way too fast. I can barely read what they're saying before it's moved on, and if I stop to think at all about what I've read then I fall behind. Not great for reading comprehension.-I immediately don't care about the story. I want to care, but there's not really any exposition on why any of this stuff matters. "The Ancestors are great people that were really smart" Who are they to me? "Oh no! He's got the Iron Heart!" So? What does it even do? Just the world building outside of the immediate "crisis" is non-existent. I don't understand why I need to care about any of this? Also I don't understand what makes Descendants special. They kinda seem to be a halfway between Guardians and Tenno, but not in a good way.-Servers have not been great with performance, dealing with some massive lag spikes. It is also day 1 so it's not a serious problem at this point. If it's still a problem in a month, then it's serious.-Season pass is awful. I didn't buy it, so not actually a problem for me, but the free track is bad and the paid track is somehow worse? Like I thought at the end they might have a Descendant skin or something to unlock. Nope, just colors for armor and weapons. Not sure if they're consumable or toggled.-One again it's impossible to buy just enough premium currency to get what you what, you have to get a little extra. This is typical in the industry but I still hate to see it. Also $70 for a singular skin is really dumb, idc what it looks like.Tech cons:-No screen border option-No option to change reticle colorI'm sure I'll find more things to say but the essences are there. Because it's free to play, feel free to give it a shot, but it's really not great. You want the same scratch for that itch, play Warframe, play Destiny, hell even play Division. There's a lot of games out there that are more deserving of your time and especially of your money. I'll keep at it for a while longer just because I'm a leveling addict, but that's about it for me.Thanks for reading, have yourselves a good one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game brings back childhood memories.Remember those times where you would get up early in the morning and the first thing you do is head to your console, turn it on and play one of your favorite game? or those late night gaming where you thought just another hour, then it ends up being 4hrs later? This game has made me do all of that in the past 3 days.I was not excited or had any idea what this game was. All i knew was that, it was a game made by Nexon who i know are very greedy. But also made some of the best childhood games (combat arms, Maplestory, Dragonnest)Then i thought, "great another heavy micro transaction game" oh boy was i right on that one. Once i heard about all the micro transaction people complained about on youtube, and said how bad the game was. I was ready to look for another game to play, until i remembered about all those valid complaints were the same complaints I had with many of their other games that i played, yet those games i played were FUN. So I took a look at some gameplay and noticed how smooth the gameplay looked and how nice every was and decided to give the game a shot. I'm glad i tried it.PROS-you can unlock Almost Everything just by playing the game. (the only thing that is locked behind a paywall, are cosmetics and emotes)-the gameplay is smooth and felt really good-A decent amount of cutscenes-amazing graphics-characters looks great-good waypoints and easy to follow any quest-pacing for the game was well done-there are no enemy scaling-you unlock some of the best stuff early on-all future content is free (at least at the time of writing this)-a decent amount of locations and enemy types-they explain a lot of things step by step over time on how to do things (not like other games that just throw all the tutorial stuff at once and overwhelm the player or throw you in the world and have you "figure it out")-Beginning of game, player lvls actually matters all the way to late game and late game actually requires skills and good builds-haven't encountered any game breaking bugs-every characters can use any and all weapons/equipment that you have (at least at the time of writing this)-Grappling hook is fun and you can grapple on everything-friendly fire is not a thing-there is no vote to kick (at the time of writing this review)-have not encountered any cheaters (at the time of writing this review)-Everyone gets their own loot/rewards. (no need to fight for loot)-easy to find out how and where to get materials/gear/skill and stats mods (all in game, no need to look for guides or ask for help)-There are no crazy amount of ads for their micro transaction in your face (comparing it to many of their past titles and many other companies games that are made these days)CONS-Disconnection issues, from time to time. (not often)-Rendering Shaders can take a long time randomly (usually around peak hours, but not often)-Cosmetics and emotes being locked behind paywall (and super expensive)-you can get ahead by paying money to skip some of the grind-drop rate is really bad-the grind is real with this one-need more different mission types-Bunny can make the game really easy and not that fun for those who are not playing as her, and have her on your team on some missions. (I'm a Bunny Main and im not asking for a nerf and guilty for this)-weapons and gear levels are locked behind locations and progression of game areas. (you can level up your gear to the level of the area you have unlocked, but you can not level them past that, until you beat that boss gate keeping you)-there is no way to remove someone from afk farming in your team without having to leave the match. (thankfully i have not encountered this but have heard it is slowly becoming a problem)-community has been pretty nice and helpful (if you are stuck with a boss or mission some higher levels can assist you, usually)-needs more unique locations to explore-needs more enemy types (maybe some that can require more teamwork to beat but not impossible for solo)-game does feel repetitive after 3-5hours in. (I lost track of time)overall the game is Fun and very good, but not the best. Many of the complaints ive seen are a lot of small nitpick and jabs at the games and many with very little playtime. I would suggest playing this game and see if this is the right game for you, everyone has their own style of games they like to play, and this is the type of game for me.Try this game, It's Good and FUN but most importantly FREE.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game with a few meh implementations and a couple of very very predatory practices in an otherwise ok microtransaction store.So the long and short first: Energy Activators (a consumable, core part of late game progression that you will need for every character and weapon you plan to use) is TERRIBLY priced and locked behind an untenable grind. The best drop rate is a 3% chance early (6% with a shape stabilizer that is also a 3% drop item and 6% base late game after a point where you need a few of them already) or $24!!!! worth of premium currency. In Warframe (the benchmark FTP looter shooter this is half modeled after) these "potatoes" are a much easier drop with less grind or about $5 premium currency.  While I have no problem with $50 Ultimate characters (prime bundles in Warframe are about the same, although they do come with more accessories) the activator are outrageously priced and are the thing to bring the entire experience to a grinding halt. They also use the unfortunately too common model of only selling premium currency in amounts just less than you actually need for purchaes forcing you to "buy up" and spend more, then have a bulk of excess without actually having the ability to buy much more.Lastly on the predatory money side, the cosmetic "paints" are horribly implemented, requiring you to purchase additional cosmetic skins to even use, then locking themselves to the skin you use them on. They even require a 2nd purchase to use on the head and chest of a character as they are treated as different slots. Again referencing the benchmark of warframe, you purchase a palette (or individual colors if you want) and they are available for all items and skins. Outside of the monetization, it's a very ok game that, as everyone else has said, is basically copying Destiny's gameplay with Warframe's character building and farming, but less well in both cases glossed over with an Anime/Asian art style reminiscent of a sci-fi Monster Hunter World. Gameplay is fun and engaging, if uninspired and occasionally clunky. Movement is very Destiny with an added grappling hook. Which works fine, until the very out of place platforming missions and sections that really want to be Warframe and just stand to show how much better Warframe's movement system is. Character and weapon modding and building is also good albeit, like the rest of the game, an obviously less well built knock off of a better game's system. Modding is good but frustrating due to lack of full stat visibility while doing so, having to scroll over each mod for full details is annoying and the whole UI feels scrunched up. Gearing is fine and mostly straight forward with one glaring issue. Each character requires a unique reactor and external parts for optimum build. While you can assign them to a preset so the correct parts are assigned when you pull that particular character out of the drawer, all those items have nowhere to sit except your inventory.  So if you are the collector or like the idea of building and playing every character to its max, be prepared for a very cluttered inventory. Furthermore, while this may only be a mild inconvenience now with a limited stable of about 15 standard characters, if/when more are added, this is going to quickly reduce looter/shooter to inventory full/shooter.I'm not even going to comment on the story and voice acting as it's been beaten to death how bad it is overall. In total, ok game, decent systems, fun-ish grind with some extremely bad monetization among an otherwise livable microtransaction store. Definitely not a "Destiny killer" but an ok alternative when you want a change and bad Warframe knockoff that is much more beginner/low skill approachable due to simpler, slower movement so you might get more friends on together.

The story is uninteresting, the gunplay falls flat, and the act of farming for materials to craft new Descendants, despite being one of the few remaining reasons for playing it, is superfluously multi-layered to either force you to farm for that item that will give you a % chance of a % chance of finding the last component you need, or nudge you towards ending your misery by spending real money in the shamelessly-predatory cash shop. After putting far too much time into the game and seeing everything it lacks to offer, I can say with certainty that nobody should play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from games like Warframe, Destiny, and even previous Nexon games I just can't anymore. Nexon would at this point let me buy my gun I deleted on accident back for real money but I'm surprised thats not in the game yet. Further more the gun play and clunky movement does not warrant the slog through campaign with bad scaling where bosses become just bullet sponge time sinks, specifically the mechanics where you have to destroy the floating orbs or shield in certain order or dps check them fast enough. The devs had to have been smoking thinking this game should have jumping puzzles/parkour missions. Am I the one bad at the game? No not at all, I actually loved the beta I had fun playing and even did The Devourer fight. The issue is that we were scammed. In the beta obviously they let us get strong quick to do the content within the short time, but now that the full game is out it feels pointlessly stretched out into artificial difficulty. Let alone the micro-transactions which I haven't brought up because my friends played Vindi and I as well aware. But this is just another point to make where First Descendant doesn't get right, look at the model Warframe uses. Plat discounts literally all the time, ability to trade and actually make the premium currency in game creating a trading economy, a way to purchase mods to save time from atrocious drop rates these games are known for. In the end, this is looter shooter slop I don't see it lasting nor do I care if it does. Typical Nexon.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:      Gun play isn't something outstanding, similar to its counterparts such as Destiny 2 and Warframe, the game has a variety of weapon to choose from. Personally, the best part would be the sound design.      Graphics is second to none, but thats to be expected developed using Unreal Engine 5. However, there are some hiccups here and there with the game freezing up and recovering or just entirely crashes. Hopefully it gets polished out in later QoL updates.      Characters, each characters have their own unique ability kit, dare I say better than Warframe. Old Warframes get reworked to bring it up to par with others but a lot of them still revolve around the capability of armor stripping. Hydroid got reworked, has armor strip. Hildryn has armor strip. Styanax has armor strip. Jade, a new Warframe just added, has armor strip.      Target looting, one of the most convenient thing this game has to offer since it narrows down loot pool to specific missions and be repeated over and over again. Expect it to be repetitive, but most of the missions are quite fast to complete.      Resources, the quantity of resources dropped is quite generous, it simply just gets better once you finish the campaign and unlock Hard mode.The Bad:      Wait time for things to be crafted, not new for someone who came from Warframe and played Destiny 2 in the past. Destiny 2 has no wait time for crafting weapons, great. In Warframe, you have to wait 3 days for your Warframe to be crafted, and this isnt counting the additional time that goes in to crafting the parts for your Warframe. I can agree that people want things ASAP but I view the time on crafting as a way to take a break.      Microtransactions, I don't mind microtransactions in a game as long as it's not gambling. I am not alone in saying that some of the microtransactions in this game are a quite expensive. Ultimately, it's free to play. You'll have to grind to get what you want or pray to RNGesus. Though the shop sells cosmetics, resource bundles, and descendants, there are some leveling resources that cannot be bought and you'll have to put time into the game and get the materials to craft them. Fret not, both normal descendants and ultimate descendants can be obtained for free by playing the game. A grind? Yes, but it's free.      Inventory, compared to Destiny 2 and Warframe, this game has the worst inventory system as it caps out how many items you can hold which includes, but not limited to: Weapons, External Components, Reactors, Modules, etc. It doesn't make it any better as you can buy additional inventory slots which ties into the ludicrous microtransactions.      UI, The UI during gameplay is pretty good, some can argue that the ability bar should be placed at a corner of the screen to make it visually cleaner, but it's grown on me, and it feels like glancing at your car's dashboard and then looking back up. The menu UI however, is a different story. It'll take some time to get used to it but it is NOT beginner friendly by any means.      Missions: It's no different compared to most other games since if you're grinding for something, it will be the same repetitive stuff over and over again. Just go into auto pilot mode and listen to a podcast or something.      "Hard Mode" is not hard at all. By the time you unlock it, you are getting level 100 reward drops across the board which basically makes you at level with most of the enemies you encounter. Only exceptions in this case are the Void Intercepts as the boss can scale up to lvl.120.      As much as I appreciate this game in implementing something similar to Destiny 2's Raids, Void Intercepts is nothing but DPS check, if you do enough damage before the timer runs out, you win.Overall, I like the game more than I am disliking it. It's new, it's going to have a lot of issues, as well as a lot of room for improvements. Hopefully the devs listen to the changes the community has voiced about and make the game better over time. The First Descendant has a lot of potential for a game that is Free to Play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fine. It isn't the worse thing out there and for it being free, you can definitely get a few hours of mid entertainment from it. It's the "We got Warframe at home" of games. Moment to moment gameplay is good, abilities feel decent, if a bit clunky and light. The gunplay is fine. Nothing spectacular that makes you feel anything special. Guns look cool and some even have fun game mechanics. The general gameplay loop is repetitive and gets stale quickly. Enter a zone, do 3-4 missions from a pool of types (defend an area, kill enemies, pick up items and move them, etc). Once those are done, you enter a dungeon, do more of the same objectives and then fight a boss. Rinse and repeat. Enemies are stupid and will often stand there and let you shoot them and bosses have multiple health bars, after each one they will teleport away and summon ads that you have to kill before you can start dealing damage to the boss again. No real interesting mechanics to be found in the fights. Story is basic as hell, no interesting characters and everyone does what you'd expect. Voice acting is Monster Hunter levels. The movement is...fine again. The grapple hook is a fun gimmick but you can't really do much with it. It really just made me wish it was a mechanic in destiny or Warframe which have better movement to support it rather than it being wasted here. The fact you can just travel the maps and start missions without having to go back to the hub constantly is cool and easy waypoint travel is also good. The monetization is what you'd expect from this company. There is definitely pay to win and the battle pass (the free version at least) levels up VERY slowly. They also have the classic scum tactic where no currency bundle is exactly the amount you'd need for a character or a cosmetic, forcing you to buy more than you need. You don't have to spend any money to play, you get a free character to start and unlock another from the first few missions. You can also farm additional characters but of course, it'll be a grind and you also have to wait real world time to unlock them after you've gathered all the parts. None of the currently available characters made me WANT to get them or pursue them. Some of them are cool and they clearly occupy different playstyles but they just feel lackluster. On the plus side, missions are labeled which the parts needed for a character and it seems like they are guaranteed drops so no having to pray for RNGsus to bless you. That may change in the later levels. Overall, I was left wanting for a game like this that was just better designed and had some actual care put behind it. Shame but not unexpected.

_childDocuments_.review: The end-game here is absolutely terrible. It is garbage and it is intentionally designed to be so. You know how this works, the developers purposefully put problems in the game to sell you back the solution. When drop rates cooperate the gameplay is fun and can be reasonably rewarding. Some of the activities even resemble something you might do for actual fun rather than for shiny pixels. Some of them do not. There are times you are forced into one of the most terribly designed loops I have ever experienced in a video game of farming outposts, shard farming, and then killing a reactor boss. Enemies at a shard, which you need to kill thousands of, are the only enemies in the game that purposefully do not drop anything - not gold, or any other material. It is designed to make sure you would never want to do this for any reason other than to open this games version of loot boxes. Do all that for a 6% chance to get what you want. Spend 10 hours doing that and have literally nothing to show for it. The game is fun to play, but the game is fun solely for the purpose of  getting you committed and then make everything at the end game bad enough to force to pay for something. While we are on the topic, paying for something would be fine if this game didn't follow the horrific industry trend of making everything in the cash shop as poorly priced as they could possible get away with. $50-$100 for the "ultimate" version of Descendants. $30 skins. Every other trick including such classics as: Buying other forms of currencies that are sold in bundles so you can never purchase the right amount needed for anything in the shop, some skins and ultimate Descendants are only available for a limited time so FOMO over and purchase them now, low drop rates and long time gating making purchasing the only option if you care at all about your sanity. These people do not deserve your money. Developers should be paid for the games they make and the game is reasonably fun - BUT - it is not designed to make it's money back or be able to make enough profit to continue operation for the long-term. It is designed to rake in as much money as humanly possible by employing every trick they can to take advantage of people. It is a delicate balance these people try to walk of making a game good enough to have people want to play it but bad enough that people want to pay to skip it.

Like doing missions, only to find out afterwards that you are missing an item needed to obtain a reward, this game is it!  Like enhancing a level 63 weapon with two clicks, expecting as weapon with 3 clicks, instead, its makes a level 1 weapon with two clicks by consuming the weapon you are enhancing and not adding the enhancement!   Apparently I screwed myself by following a logical path, thinking a level two enhanced gun would then be enhanced to a level three gun.  I picked the weapon to enhance (level 2 enhanced Thunder cage, and ended up with a level 1 thunder cage with two enhancements.  Basically I got screwed by selecting the gun to enhance, then selecting the newly made weapon.  Lets do the math 2+1 =2 and reduces the weapon to a level one, when it was a level 63.  Thanks for the clarity in that process!If you like a game that you spend 50% of your time with load screens, this game is for you!

But even then it is opportunity to level your gear and farm up resources while you run through. Overall I would say the game is a 6 or 7/10, if they optimized the game more, added in more mechanics for bosses instead of the balloons you need to shoot (the hoards of enemies that spawn and you need to kill is far more interesting to me), and bump up the values you get from mods, i would say this game would easily go up to 8/10 for me. I bought the battle pass to get some skins and new stuff and have progressed pretty quickly through it in that minimal time (level 64 as of this writing).  Its a F2P game, so the store sells absolutely everything, but, its all in the game too, and buying it just shortens the grind so, keep that in mind (plus its ridiculously over-priced!).  Currently, the end game seems to be quite a bit of grinding to upgrade or level and re-level guns, descendants and modules. I've only finished the story (very long!) a couple of days ago so I wont speak much on the end game. _childDocuments_.review: Pros - It has a lot of guns, fair selection of characters, Mod system, and Prestige system. Free to play and with no life all is achievable.Cons - There is no player economy and can use a better system to communicate with friends. If you have a wallet and don't mind using it the items are pricey.Strong similarity to Warframe and Outriders. Has an open world system similar to Destiny. Some hints of Division and Anthem as well.Opinion - This could easily become the new decade of success like Warframe, but it for the most part has already closed a big gap of the earlier struggles of Warframe, the mod and prestige systems are nearly one for one match in this sense. Ultimate weapons have bonus abilities that trigger much like unique guns in warframe, but it uses the looter shooter aspects for the bonus perks and for the ability to evolve the ultimate weapons to have stronger ability procs. Easily an 8 out of 10 in my book and enjoyably a community supported game.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great free to play game, but it has its issues. It does some things better than Warframe and it does some things better than Destiny, which are the two games its very clearly taking inspiration from. The gun play is smooth and responsive, the skills are unique and fun. I do like how it doesnt take an eternity to unlock new characters, and for the most part the characters are worth grinding for. I will say that i dont agree with the pay to win model, i.e. being able to spend real world money on ultra rare in game materials that are 100% required for leveling your character/weapons at end game. Thats my opinion though, probably not a popular one. The over monetization in the game is a bit obnoxious, but again, just my opinion. If you want a fun third person shooter to play and kill some time, this is it.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of comments are saying this game is " Destiny 2 x warframe with waifus" but honestly this plays nothing like destiny, i can't speak too much on its similarities of warframe as i have only played 3 hours of it. The gunplay is decent enough, the skills for the starting 3 characters aren't too good at selling people on buying more characters or "earning" them. This game is extremely PREDATORY with its monetization ($30 battlepass, almost $20 character unlocks, you can spend real money for premium currency to speed up time for your crafting), but the game is not pay to win, anyone who says that is retarded and has no impulse control. The way you unlock characters in this game is; each character costs 4 material specific to them to earn X material you need y(1), y(2), y(3), y(4), but you need to craft each of the y's, and to get the material for y you need the y blueprint. The Y blueprint can only be found in mission A but its only a 20% chance it drops, you farm mission A but need materials a,b,c,d (drops for those materials can be common to rare) then you have to wait for the crafting time for material Y to finish (could be up to 3 hours). With material Y(1-4) done you can finally craft your character, the queue time was 12 hours. The part i like the most about the game is its "void intercepts" (raids) the bosses have unique mechanics and areas that force you to learn them.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I can’t recommend this game to anyone as of right now. I understand this game just came out and that always comes with its own problems. However, this game has more cons than pros when it comes to gameplay, story, and replayability.5/10 It’s a game, it runs, you have stuff to do, and it’s inoffensively simple.Long Answer:	Overview-The gameplay is alright. There are plenty of characters to allow for a variety of playstyles. The gun variety is also nice, as it does feel like I keep finding new items with each new zone. However, they feel and sound the same as their counterparts. A sniper’s gonna sound like every other sniper, and a machine gun is going to sound like every other machine gun. The shooting is alright. The hitboxes are very good. The modding capability for descendants and weapons is also nice and feels like it makes a genuine impact with each upgrade. The gear selection is also good, as it helps make grinding easier with certain substats. Grinding out the gear for specific stats (so far) is okay too, and not too time consuming. During the “story”, I’ve managed to earn most of my gear just by playing through the main missions.	Loot- This is my biggest praise I’ll give to this game, drops are easier to get most of the time. It genuinely felt like the game was respecting my time. Like in warframe, there is Kuiper (endo), and amorphous materials (relics). In warframe, getting endo was a slog, especially for non-endgame players. Relics were also troublesome to get, let alone open. You had to grind and hope you got the right one. Grind to get mats to upgrade it to the right tier. Theeeen grind to open said relics and hope to goodness you got the right part. The alternative was buying platinum to buy the stuff you wanted. Even then, platinum costs were alright. In this game, grinding out Kuiper is much faster, there’s gear to boost it further, and it can be obtained fast. The same goes for the relics. You are guaranteed the exact same one  per run, which is awesome. Thought the loot contained has its own drop rates, they are still consistant with their probability. Plus, later on runs do get faster so you’re getting dozens of relics an hour. Enemy materials are also consistent in drop rate. The actual grinding can be accomplished by normies like myself who still have lives and jobs haha.	Loot cont.- As I said earlier, the guns are okay. They definitely look nice, but behave and sound the same, except for minor randomized substats. They drop often, allowing you to pick what you like most of the time. And you almost always can get a good gun at the current enemy level within a few encounters. Plus, you can level up your guns using other ones to keep ones that you like, which is also nice. The gear is okay too, I haven’t played with it much, but when there’s a big change in main and substats, it’s impactful.Enemies-The normal enemies are actually pretty decent! I enjoyed fighting them. Like I said, their hitboxes are well made, there’s plenty to fulfill an enjoyable power fantasy too. It’s nowhere near turning on ‘The only thing they fear is you’ and going nuts as a titan in destiny; or getting your energy filled and using your warframe’s abilities and weapons en masse, jumping around like a murderous ballerina while classical music plays; but it’s still okay. Characters/descendants- The character abilities are also okay, but I haven’t played with enough to give you a fair evaluation. Of the two I’ve played, they are fun and their abilities make a difference in a fight, and can provide decent team synergy tactics. 	Bosses- They suck. No better way to put it. All except for the unique-ish colossus bosses (they get reskins too) are just reskins of existing enemies. So far, every boss has 2-3 health bars. After lowering one, they will enter a shield phase where they are invulnerable. During this phase, you have to shoot floating orbs (meatballs) above their head. The bosses are already tanky bullet sponges, and the same goes for the meatballs. After 70 hours, I only just found a semi unique boss fight, because he has 4, then 5 meatballs as opposed to 3 for every phase. You can’t avoid these guys either, as they’re who you need to fight to get the relics you desire. Meaning, meatballs for days. All in all, the devs cheaped out on the bosses and made them bland, copy-pasted enemies you’ve already fought many times before. And they only get tankier and stronger as you progress. 	Mission/Level design- All levels are linear,  wavy paths to the boss. In between you usually follow these quests, run here, kill dudes, run here, kill more dudes, stand in circle for x-amount of time while shooting dudes, then fight boss. That’s all the missions! Shooting dudes, sometimes picking up items after shooting dudes, or standing in a circle while fending off dudes, by shooting them. Standard looter shooter stuff. There’s nothing special to it, it’s a run of the mill objective system. Here and there, there is a unique mission, which is terrible. It is a parkour mission where you collect orbs. You are expected to use your traversal skill to get them all. However, this is not titanfall, let alone warframe. No bullet jumps, wall rides, or fancy gear apart from the jankiest grapple known to man. You get 2 slowly recharging uses, it is very short ranged, and it doesn’t hook what you look at! You aim at something, hope that the retical locks onto it and it works. More often than not, the grapple’s “assist” feature will attach to the wrong object and ruin your flow.	Open-world design- Very pretty. But graphics don’t make good gameplay. The worlds are small, divided into even smaller instances, and have near nothing to do accept copy-pasted missions (patrols from destiny), shooting dudes, or looking for records you’ll probably never read. There’s one more thing, hidden boxes with a hacking minigame! In theory, may be fun. Especially with good hacking minigames to look back on (Like automota’s or warframe’s). However, it too sucks. Think of the grineer hacking, but far worse. If you misclick, you lose a third of the time allotted. Also, to hack you need a consumable which is burnt upon any use. And, getting them will require a grind. These boxes also hold essential materials for making the game easier for you too. Besides the pretty landscapes, the open world is uninteresting and merely on the way to you unlocking the correct boss mission to grind for relics.Story- I am not able to make any true comments about the story or characters, as it was very uninteresting to me and I shut the volume down to get back to grinding after a few missions. The characters are okay too. Their voice acting is pretty good, some better than others. But, overall, got bored with the story right away and shut the volume down.Music- I also can’t comment on this as I heard the same battle soundtrack for multiple regions and fights and turned the volume down for music because it got old fast. Plus, it’s not the most “re-listenable” song, but that may just be me. Microtransactions- Oof. Warframe prices may’ve been pricey, but you got permanent stuff which could be used for a variety of things for fashion-frame. The currency is miles more expensive than warframe’s too. I get it, it’s F2P, but man it’s still high. The paint took a page out of destiny’s book too, it’s consumed upon use! Not a large pallete you can use infinitely, one use. One use of paint, costs you 50 cents. Even worse, you can get free paint, but you can’t use it because the base character’s aren’t colorable. So you’ll still have to fork over your doubloons to use the paint. The bundles cost as much as a full priced game, with one character and one outfit. 60 bucks, and it doesn’t even come with paint. Overall, the microtransactions are ludicrous.Maybe keep an eye on this, but just go play another looter game for now, this one ain’t worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: After The First Descendant servers shut down, I found myself in a state of utter despair. The game had been my escape from the harsh realities of life, and now that it was gone, I felt lost and adrift.I tried to distract myself with other activities, but nothing could fill the void left by the game. I found myself constantly thinking about the characters and the world I had come to love so much. I began to lose touch with reality, unable to distinguish between the game and the real world.I started to exhibit strange behaviors, talking to myself and acting out scenes from the game. My friends and family grew concerned, but I couldn't bring myself to stop. The game had become my entire world, and without it, I felt like I was slowly losing my mind.As the days passed, my mental state deteriorated further. I began to have vivid hallucinations, seeing characters from the game in my everyday life. I couldn't sleep, couldn't eat, couldn't focus on anything but the game that was no longer there.Eventually, my friends and family intervened, urging me to seek help. I was admitted to a psychiatric hospital, where I underwent intensive therapy and medication to help me cope with the loss of the game.Slowly, with the help of my doctors and loved ones, I began to come to terms with the fact that The First Descendant was just a game, and that my obsession with it had spiraled out of control. I learned to let go of the past and focus on the present, finding new ways to cope with my emotions and find joy in other aspects of life.Though the memory of The First Descendant will always hold a special place in my heart, I now understand that it's important to live in the real world and not let a game consume me. I am grateful for the support I received during my darkest days, and I am determined to move forward with a healthier mindset, knowing that I am not defined by a virtual world.

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone wants to compare this game to Warframe and Destiny 2 so lets do that. (I have over 600 hours in Destiny 2 and Warframe each)Destiny 2 resets your level and makes you regrind and buy an expansion every season or so. The first descendant is free with no expansions.Warframe makes you buy forma or grind days to get forma. When I had beaten The First Descendant campaign I randomly had enough resources to buy 2 of this games version of forma by the end of the campaign and gave me 3 for free for beating the campaign, beating the final normal difficulty boss and for beating bunny's quest. Destiny 2 cuts content from the game (including that you paid for in expansions) on a whim. (The First Descendant hasen't been out long enough for that to be a thing but I have literally never seen another game do that.)In both Warframe and Destiny 2 when a class or build is considered "meta" it gets nerfed to the absolute ground next patch. The First Descendant devs not only havent nerfed the meta builds into the ground but made other builds more fun and powerful to compensate. I've put easily 100+ dollars in Destiny 2 and 200+ dollars in warframe and admittedly got hundreds of hours of playtime out of them. I have put 20$ dollars into The First Descendant (just to buy the premium season pass which isnt necessary outside of cosmetics/boosters/resources you can easily build) and its been insanely fun thus far and I still feel the need to play it more and have a good time. Farming is enjoyable and the player base is actually retaining the knowledge on those farming routes and character builds. _childDocuments_.review: 100+ hours in. I think this game is a solid 8/10. I will explain below.I played with my irl friends and made a couple friends in the game. I will be playing this game as long as they keep making content.My pc: 3070ti, 12th gen intel cpu, 32gb RAM, WIN11.Graphics: 10. Amazing lighting quality. Amazing details, meshes and textures. The game runs amazingly smooth above 60fps with ultra graphics on my rig.Story: 6. Basic copy and paste story of dire circumstances and having to fight off an army of invaders, etc. However, the enemies are varied and interesting, well done and look good. The world is unique but it lacks lore.Controls: 9. Superb controller support and everything feels smooth and how it should be. The grappling could be better and sometimes the jumping is janky.Sounds: 8. Distance gunshots sound like I am downrange again. As someone who has spent thousands of hours behind a firing weapon, or downrange from one, or near one, I can say the sounds are fairly realistic. All other sounds make me feel immersed. Voice acting is great, even if some is AI.Fun: 9. Like i said, my friends and I had a lot of fun coming over to this from Helldivers2 and it was worth it. Negatives: I will say that the game maps are a bit small or limited and I wish they were much larger, had more points of interest, or just had more objectives. Maybe more open areas to traverse, i don't know, but I feel like that was a negative for me. Content: I wish there was a lot more customization options. A LOT more. The game is very grindy for just about everything ULTIMATE, and I wish there was higher drop percentages is all. And then when you craft, you must wait again. I do not like that, and I wish it was a quicker wait than 18 hours on some of the things. Positives: bringing my friends into the game, we had a blast and hopefully we will continue to do so. Gorgeous lighting and textures, character models look fabulous. Gun play and overall gameplay is FAST, FUN and engaging. I love playing this game. It is a top notch looter shooter, similar to Destiny, very much so. Recommendations: I HIGHLY recommend they release a full photomode, where you can pose your characters, change outfits, add items, change lighting, etc etc. Some vistas were just beautiful and I would have loved to make them into screensavers. I recommend more content like customization options. I would like to see more areas, and maybe some unique games or puzzles. Disclaimer: I did spend money inside of the game and purchased their in-game currency. I spent maybe a total of $50 on this game, but I had so much fun and played so much. I think it is very worth it.Favorite part of the game is the horde modes, they are called DEFEND missions. I love running around those and listening to spotify playlists or podcasts.

_childDocuments_.review: Mediocre. Warframe/DestinyIts like they chopped up destiny warframe and diablo and tried to make their own coherent game out of it. they however ended being unable to separate the good from the bad. They EYEgor and Fronkenstiened this  Abby Normal monster of a game you basically have destiny's map and travel without a mount. Combat is straight up meh. Warframe works with your set character skills because there's so much more to your missions, the movement system the massive variation in weapons the pure chaos amount of enemies. same for destiny there's a lot of weapon variety and skill variation in the skill trees for your class and mobility is key, not to mentions meaningful unique equipment. all of these make those games combat engaging and meaningful. Descendant lets you stand there with a machine gun and just stun lock enemies. if it wasnt for other enemies spawning and moving around you it would just be a game of carnival target practice. wanna try and focus your weapon on an enemies head. well good luck because except the fodder and boss enemies have some form of whole body interrupt animation that makes them double over or fling their head back like they got slapped with a brick breaking any form of head tracking. Mobility is also meh.  In TFD you have a double jump and a grappling hook (which is very clunky) other than that the only other mobility oyu have is if your character has a skill that gives you that. bunny sprint ability should of just been the sprint mechanic for everyone. but the sprint and walk are basically the same just with a speed filter like Mass Effect. the grapple will have a red circle around your cross hair for any point you can grapple to to let you know when you can use it. well except for the things you cant that have a red circle anyway. wanna climb up that ledge after. well you can but you need to try half a dozen times to hit the right spot with the grapple otherwise your character will not go into the proper climb animation. and often times the climb animation will be fine but you will be kicked backwards because of the geometry of the ledge and have to try again. see clunky. UI is also meh. i had my UI lose my quest marker at least a dozen times, markers disappeared while heading towards them, skill name in the character preview and the buff description from that skill weren't even translated similarly. your health and ammo count is in the most asinine of places above your skill bar but not attached and just floating the the bottom right of your crosshair. far enough away to lose sight of it regularly but close enough to not be immediately readable when looking at other ui elements.Items are pretty meh. Youve got the parts farming of warframe, youve got the random equipment drops of diablo and guess what stats and bonuses that make very little sense unless you are activly paying attention to audio in game and converastions while in a fire fight.Story is kinda meh. anyone remember Anthem's story? if not take a look its pretty mediocre. but take the big bad from there put him in charge of the vex and fallen where he mashes the two species together and there ya go you have the entire enemy force summed up in one. sneaky advisor to the big bad, pretty sure thats just a freaking Exo from destiny. there is one character specifically who tells you how to do things in large text form but speak audio is a couple beeps. that text goes even faster than someone who reads quite fast could pick up. everything is just MEH. is it bad. yes, but playable. its just another game made to get attention and money from people without putting to much effort in refining the product into something great. play it for a couple hours. have a little mediocre fun. then ditch it for something more fufilling.

_childDocuments_.review: After 250 hours in The First Descendant, I can't confidently recommend others to play it. Starting with what I like, the combat and movement attribute to a "gamefeel" that I can only describe as satisfying and engaging. The character abilities only add to this, and playing a new descendant genuinely feels like an entirely different experience to the last. Unfortunately, "what I like" pretty much ends there.... As the base game has a stale repetitive mission structure, that offers no fresh ideas, mechanics, or challenges to keep someone invested in the gameplay. The story is even worse, unbearably obnoxious dialog filled to the brim with convoluted sci-fi vomit and exposition, that as a player I was never made interested in learning about. Does it get better in the end game? NO, I have 10 level 40 Descendants 4 of which are prestiged to their full builds for what feels like absolutely no reason, as there's no endgame content that requires characters that strong, 70% of the "raid bosses" (calling them that feels like an insult to raid bosses) are just bullet sponges, with no real mechanics barring point and shoot at the big guy, and as for the other 30% they have 1 or 2 mechanics that you as a team have to overcome to beat the boss, the mechanics are pretty basic, but its fun the first few times you kill the boss. the rest of the endgame content consists of the same boring missions from the base game with boring modifiers smacked ontop to disguise them as new content, things like "enemy HP up" or "player defense down" don't change the mission at all, and they're so easy that you can complete them with your eyes closed. There's little to no incentive to grind for new guns as there's no challenge in the game that requires you to have them, cant hunt for armor or transmog because the vast majority of cosmetics are behind a paywall, and while sure you can keep prestiging your character to make them stronger and apply more mods, for one, its not fun leveling in this game and it becomes a huge chore after 3 prestiges and two, there's no need to, as everything dies so easily to you without a full build. By the way, I keep hearing about an "invasive monetization system" that "ruins the game" and that's simply just not true the game is monetized almost identically to warframe, and anything you can buy you can get from just playing (and quite easily might I add) apart from cosmetics. There's some potential here for sure, but only time will tell. As of right now I don't think this game is worth investing your time into when Warframe and Destiny exist.

_childDocuments_.review: Never left a review for a game before. I love looter shooters, but this game just feels tacky to play. The forced anti-aliasing is awful and lack of options in the graphics menu is terrible in 2024. There is no lip sync for the English dub, which in itself sounds over the top corny and I'm personally not in to it. Poor English translation for subtitles and game tutorials, they seemed rushed and inconsistent. Subtitles very often overlapped tutorial text so you just have a mish-mash of lines of text on screen. Store/micro-transactions system is overly convoluted and undoubtedly a huge cash grab.I see people comparing this game heavily to Warframe, which I'll admit I have not played. But I will say the shooting/gun-play did not feel satisfying, the same goes for Descendant abilities and movement. When selecting your "first" Descendant the abilities "descriptions" use terminology that has not been explained to the player. This means you have to chose a character based on what you "think" their abilities do, based on lack of clarity. The first things I notice when loading into a new game is the initial feel, look and responsiveness. I felt uninterested in learning the mechanics and general gameplay loop purely based on my experience in the tutorial right at the start. The game randomly closed without an error pop-up multiple times in succession, even in the short amount of time that I played.I tried to like the game, but I was simply put off by all of the above. I acknowledge that playing it on release day means there's going to be growing pains, and the devs will need to tweak things, but I simply did not enjoy my experience playing the game.
