_childDocuments_.review: Free to play, can earn everything except for some purely cosmetic stuff in game. You can shortcut your way to more characters and ultimate characters with money as well but you can earn them through in game "research". The game has a surprising amount of end game content from what i see, with trials that go up to level 130. (The max level for a character is 40, so idk how that would work).The gameplay is very fun, all the characters have their own unique abilities and gimmicks to them. The boss fights are usually pretty interesting, the beginning of the game is too easy but it ramps up. While some bosses just get a lot more health and are spongy, it has made for some fun encounters when its a tough battle with people going down. There are trial bosses in the game, where you are placed in a massive arena against a 50ft monster and can grapple onto weakened points and smash them, while making sure to hang on when they try to throw you off. I do not see any type of PvP combat/missions.The variety of enemies is actually really impressive, i have been in 5 maps now and they have felt fresh. Even the drop ships look different. The map designs are pretty cool and you are able to use a grappling hook and do some spiderman stuff.There is a heavy warframe influence on this game (which i like). There are research projects as i mentioned, which are time gated and require materials that are obtained through in game missions with different drop chances. There are modifications you obtain for your weapons and descendants. There is a wide variety of weapons, where it seems that i find new ones in each new map. (Started finding beam rifles, thats fun). Also mastery rank system from warframe is back in this game, if you are familiar with it. Your account levels up seperately from your characters which grants you bonuses and further unlocks new research and other options. There are also those fun warframe missions where you can see how long you can survive and risk going further waves for better loot or losing it all if failing to extract.The visuals are great, even on low settings. The soundtrack is really good too. The voice acting is ok. Map design is nice and each map feels different with different weather, structures and such.Overall, i would say that its better than some full priced games, such as outriders and the recent helldivers. There is just so much more variety and a much deeper endgame than some of these games, while i have yet to reach it (17 hours in), they have so many trial bosses that you can view from the menus. I may update this review after i spend sometime in end game.Its not a perfect game, but as far as free to play games go, its reminding me very much like a warframe experience, except not so overwhelming with so much catch up that there is in that game. There I have probably experienced about 7 times where for a few seconds my frames would dip severly, but it happened every few hours and didnt make it unplayable. One point i joined my friend and it kept lagging like crazy. Idk if the game has some kind of peer-hosting system, but when i lead the squad again, there was no more lagging for the rest of the game session (6 hours later).As of day 2 the game's server has had so many unexpected players that they have been down almost all day. Not surprised when the game is very good and they didnt expect this amount of players. They gave out compensation for the issues on day 1 and I would be surprised to see more of that with server crashes on day 2.As far as a F2P game goes i would give it a 9/10 with the current impressions that it has left me in this amount of time. I still felt that it was fair to give it a review at this point as i have experienced quite a bit with so much much more left to offer.I look forward to future updates and maybe seeing some of you around the hub or in a match.

_childDocuments_.review: So after beating the main story of the game and grinding out a few things i do have to say I wish this was not a free to play game because it gives the dev's an excuse to make some wild Microtransactions that should not exist, A big problem i have is you do have to Buy Character slots to have all the characters because you start with 10 and need 19 to have all the Decscendants (Plus any new ones they may add in the future) and there is no other way to get slots other then buying them with real money which is very stupid, i understand it isn't much for them but the fact that you have to buy them to begin with is very stupid. some of the best skins can cost from 20 to 100$ which is insane, you can buy the characters but i feel grinding them for free is far more worth the time, though you do have to buy character slots if you buy to many characters. And there is no way to get premium currency other then buying it and you don't unlock skins or grind for them at all. you can unlock colors, emotes, and titles but not much of anything else.The story was far to predictable, after all if you put a main playable character in a tight or death like scenario 99% of the time they will be alright especially in a multiplayer MMO-ish game and i know we would not fight the main boss dude because that might be the end of the game in an endless war like game, after all the players always need an enemy to fight in an all PVE game. Some of the characters have good personalities but the story kind of beats them down and makes me not care.The Grind is reasonable but like Warframe when you get everything for the research for the character or item you have to wait several hours to be able to use it, like a character can be researched for 16 hours before you can use them which i personally hate, and once you beat every area of the story then you are made to go through every area again on hard mode, i also hate that you have to do an intercept battle after every zone because you are stuck at a gear level in till you get past it and on the harder intercept battles people never seem to be able to do enough DPS before the time runs out and most of the time you need all 4 people to be there to get the job done with in the 10 minutes you have to fight the boss, so one random that is under level or dps could drag the whole thing down and waste your time. also there is a lot of repeat missions in each area and some things you cant do without a character of a specific element.This game might get better in the future but at the moment most of what you do in the game is Grind and pay money for things, i understand that a few dollars for a free to play game is totally reasonable but it does put a few walls in front of you, and the battle pass only gives you like 6$ in premium currency back if you complete it, the battle pass does not have many good things in it either. I understand the game has good graphics and sexy characters but a game cant run on that alone. I honestly cant recommend this game because at the moment its just a "listen to music and grind" kind of game and i don't see many people continuing to play this game after the first time through it.(Edit) So after reaching end game and trying to farm for Ultimate bunny, I've been through more then 150 Pattern 082's and still have not gotten the Ultimate bunny code, as far as I'm concerned the 6% it says for the drop is not real, I feel as if I'm being scammed for my time.

_childDocuments_.review: Another dime a dozen, live service FPS. It clones a lot of Destiny, but gives you a cast of hero characters to play as instead of your own. It's visual cohesion is questionable out the gate with it's skins... Including following a character you meet Bunny in the first minute of the game. Who you can then later buy a booba outfit for in the cash shop, who looks exactly like you probably imagine she does. Hard iron clad looking characters with little critter backpacks. Their character influence seems straight out of the BDO character creator. They know what they're doing, and much like other knockoffs like Outriders it'll have it's plug pulled in a year or two when the new player rush dries up and the battle pass doesn't make enough money for the corpos.Honestly didn't get to play long. Slogged through a crash or two barely getting through the opening, only to get halfway through a mission later and have a mission point objective just... Not work. Maybe if this game gave you a character creator like Destiny I would have been more invested, but I don't want to play an PvE exploration type game using someones stock characters who only exist to sell skins... Otherwise, combat performance was fine aside from some weird animations here or there. Shooting is fine. No FPS drops on a 2070 on a mix of medium-high+RTX.You get two weapons and a heavy. The only mild mechanic you could say that gives it a draw outside of hero characters, with a handful of skills each, is a grappling hook. I don't think this is the content Titanfall 2 fans are looking for, and this won't touch the newer Halo audience. Destiny is still going strong. Apex is going strong. I guess the argument is filling a niche for PvE, but man none of these studios come close to understanding the playerbase they're trying to target. Who is this for? This game will end as just a skin cash shop in a ghost town server. Just watch it's steamdb player counts.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm always wary of anything F2P, but I thought I'd give this a try given the reviews were saying it was fun. And well here I am 20 hours in and I'm having a blast. Is it like Warframe? Kinda - but not really.  Combat feels a lot less floaty than WF to me. more like half way between Destiny 2 and WF.Combat is fun and engaging with the different classes (Descendants) plus much like Destiny 2 there's a huge bunch of weapon types to mix things up in combination with your class abilities.Traversal is a real highlight with the grapple and the maps are varied, vertical, and really pretty.I like how I can mix things up easily between doing solo missions, group missions, dungeon runs, and special events.Plus the actual story - whilst no Pulitzer - is just meaty enough to vaguely keep me interested (with extremely pretty cutscenes to help it along).As for the P2W elements - I haven't come across any yet. There's an optional Battle Pass (just like every other live service shooter) plus a bunch of cosmetics on the store, but I've unlocked a bunch of extras and haven't spent a single cent so far. I'll probably grab the BP as a 'thanks' to the devs eventually.Should you play it? Hell yes - there's literally nothing to lose but some time if it's not your cup of tea, but if you enjoyed Destiny 2 (Social hub w/ multiple planets (maps) and dozens of dungeon and event runs, plus loads of build customisation) then you can't go wrong. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I have so far been hooked on this game since launch day! I've been a huge fan of Destiny, Warframe and Division over the past years and have put many hours into each of them. So if you like those games, then you will love this game! It's grindy, it's fun, graphics are great, characters are good looking, movement is fluid, gunplay is second to none. There are endless character build possibilities, quests and reasons to keep playing. Ignore all the pathetic comments about having to spend money in game, its all absolute garbage! You don't "NEED" to spend anything if you don't want to! If you've played Warframe, this is a very similar progression system. Considering that it's free to play (with optional in game purchases for cosmetics), and most games nowadays cost £50 - £60 to buy, this isn't such a bad deal! I myself will be supporting the devs by making a couple of in game purchases, they've been amazing so far, and they've worked hard for years to give us a great shooter game that we've long been waiting for! Give them a break from all the toxic comments, download the game and ENJOY!

_childDocuments_.review: As it is right now, you're better off playing Warframe, it respects your time a lot more, giving you more value for everything you do, and also giving more value to your money.To be more specific, while farming in Warframe, you will always get more resources and drops that you could sell, and then buy the item you were looking for from another player, or sell drops that you don't want, to then buy skins, inventory slots, or palettes to customize your equimpent, while in TFD, you can't trade, and colours are items for single use, so you would need to buy a lot of them... They've said they'll add trade, but we don't know the extend of it, and also they've said a trader will be added so we can sell items to the NPC, and get something back for it, unless that is premium currency, or items that you can only get through the shop, I would still recommend to better play Warframe.Since TFD copies almost every system they have from Warframe, and to this point, they didn't copy some of the systems that make Warframe fair to players, at this point in time, I can't recommend this game over Warframe, since it's literally a worse version of it, and no one should really do so.My biggest problems with the game, are:    1. There is no way for free players to expand inventory slots for Descendants, and so, you'll eventually find     yourself having to decide on which ones to keep, unless you buy slots from the shop.    2. Since there is no trade, whenever you do quests to farm for low % parts, and you end up with 10x of     other parts you don't need, you can only keep them in your inventory, and those have no value at all, so     most of the time  you just feel like you're loosing time.    3. Customization is very restricted to paid items, most skins are shop only, which is not a problem,     Warframe is the same, but since there is no way for us to get premium currency via trading, that's a down     point that makes me just recommend Warframe to people that enjoy this type of game.    4. And lastly, colours, colours are a 1 time use item, that you get some for free doing some achievemnts in     the game, and also in the battle pass, but still, since they're a one time use item, you will need to buy     more if you want to customize everything, it's ridduculous to me that colour is a consumable item, and not     just something you unlock once.I'll change this review if at some point, they add trade to the extent that I think gives us enough to be able to play the game fully, without having the need to pay, meaning we can get all the customization, and utilities like buffs or inventory slots by playing the game, and not only by paying, basically, I won't recommend this game until it's at least as F2P friendly as Warframe is, because it's exactly the same genre, and it's just superior on everything except maybe graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Multiple characters to choose from with 4 abilities to use that vary in single target or AOE, offensive or defensive, and different elemental damage types- Multiple map regions with sub regions within, offering plenty of missions and different scenery- Modules, weapons, equipment are shared between characters so you don't have to farm multiple pieces, only swap parts to keep each character optimal- Lets you swap to a hard mode after completing the main story for better drops and a bit more of a challenge- Matchmaking for bossing and missions are quick, making it easy for solo players to get harder content doneCons:- Some characters are free to play with from the start, another is basically handed to you at the start, but if you choose not to grind and want to buy them it can get expensive...especially the ultimate versions- Buying currency in the shop is sketch through steam, it will deny your transaction and you'll have to open a support ticket and hope they fix it- Stuttering issues can take the immersiveness out of the game, unclear if it'll ever be fixedI would slightly recommend this game more than i don't, and with it being a free game i would say give it a try, you have nothing to lose.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a "recommend with stipulations" option, I'd select it, but here's the general gist:Pros:-Story missions are fun and relatively easy to progress even if the story itself is painfully mid.-Colossus fights are fun with the destructable and removable parts.-Gunplay is excellent as is the looting and gearing phase of the game.-The open world co-op is really interesting, as you can just pop into a mission someone is doing and help them with it, and vice versa, without joining a party or anything like that, you can just join at the mission marker or better yet, start clapping enemies in the mission area. I really enjoyed this aspect of the multiplayer.Cons:-Encrypted Vaults suck fat ♥♥♥♥. They don't show up on the map, the timing minigame is awful, and if you fail it, you lose the resource that you need to open them. The resources in Vaults are required for several necessary items. The vaults are bad and need to be completely overhauled or removed entirely.-Infiltration missions suck fat ♥♥♥♥. Unless you've unlocked Sharen and have stacks of Skill Duration, they're borderline impossible.-Laughably bad monetization, but it's Nexon so it's not like any of us expected it to be anything but."Meh"s-Zone Recon missions. They're short missions that give materials that countless items and Ultimate weapons need as well as Amorphous Materials (potatoes from Warframe), but the drop rates are excruciatingly low and the mission goes on a 5 minute timer after you've completed it, which takes about 6 seconds. Chances are you'll need one specific resource so you'll be inclined to just wait out the timer, but ideally you'll just rotate through the other Recon missions so that you're actively farming while waiting for the one you actually want. Kind of sucks, but manageable.-Tracking which potatoes and materials you want to farm is a bit tedious and not really helpful as it currently exists in game. You're better off throwing something up on your second monitor to see what will get you what you need.It's a good bit of fun, but there's room for a TON of quality of life changes that, frankly, should have been there in the first place. They just simply cannot shake the "grindy Korean MMO" aspect of the early 2000's.

_childDocuments_.review: Right now (~200 hours) here is how I enjoy TFD**Comfort Food:** Freyna in 400% dungeons  **Challenge:** Hard bosses, starting from Frost Walker and beyond.**Explore**: Build new Descendants to see how the content feels. I've added Hailey, Luna, Gley, Lepic and Valby for this purpose, although (except for Hailey with bosses) are all still very weak compared to Freyna.**Recent Highlights:**- Hailey taking down Pyromaniac in under 10 seconds! A fantastic way to farm Slayer components. A nice feeling of accomplishment.- Ultimate Gley with a fully kitted Vestigial Organ – happy to carry in Molten Fortress fights. She is also fun in dungeons without Freyna or Bunny.- Playing Hailey in a 400% dungeon with Lepic, Luna and Gley. It was much slower than with Freyna, but more interesting and fun as there was a lot of interplay and synergies between characters. I see a few distinct phases:**Phase 1: Confusion**  In the beginning, there's a lot to learn. The mechanics don’t make sense at first as you progress through the main story. You don’t know what the weapons, attributes, or modules do, or how they interact. At the same time, limited access to descendants adds to the confusion. The story is also not very good. What keeps you going is the fun combat!**Phase 2: Mastery**  This is when everything clicks. At the end of this phase you get a fully built Descendant (in my case, Freyna) fully equipped, and you start to understand key elements like Outposts (and get a Sharen) and materials (and get an Enzo). There's a satisfying feedback loop where leveling and bossing become easier as you get stronger, which, in turn, helps you get even stronger.**Phase 3: Plateau**  This is where I am now. You start to question why you’re still playing the game after conquering all the hard bosses and can breeze through 400% dungeons with 1-2 characters. One possible answer lies in exploring the content from different perspectives – trying out other descendants, experimenting with different weapons, and gearing them up. I chose Hailey to tackle bosses that my Freyna struggles with (I think of them as “Hard 1” or H1 bosses and “Hard 2” or H2 bosses, H2 roughly starting with Frost Walker and up). Hailey lets me breeze through H1 bosses with ease, which is satisfying and a great way to farm useful gear, like Slayer components from Pyromaniac.H2 bosses are more team-oriented, and they can be frustrating and generally not very enjoyable. The challenge often lies in the fact that players, including yourself, may not know what to do. The game doesn’t do a great job explaining complex mechanics. For instance, I had no idea what the little flames in Frost Walker did until I watched a YouTube video. The same goes for the switches in Molten Fortress (MF). MF is especially frustrating because public groups often don’t know how to handle the immunity phase. I didn’t either, until I watched a video on it. I don’t think it’s reasonable to expect players to study videos just to understand a boss fight. Instead of simplifying the mechanics, I suggest adding in-game tutorials. For MF, for example, players could practice the button mechanic without the boss present to get a feel for it. This same idea could be applied to _The Hanged Man_, whose mechanic is so opaque it wipes the team without explanation. Players are left with no clear path to success other than searching online.**The Plateau Phase: A Critical Point**  I believe the Plateau phase is perhaps the most dangerous for the game's longevity, from Nexon’s perspective. This is where players like me might start to lose interest. The challenges of this phase are many, including finding a descendant whose playstyle suits you without feeling underpowered. During this exploration phase, managing reactor and component farming becomes increasingly mentally taxing, especially with multiple descendants requiring different gear combinations and substats. Additionally this expanded interest can quickly strain inventory space, leading to a poor experience where you're constantly sorting through and deleting gear during missions, breaking the flow. Personally, I don’t think buying more space is the solution, as it just creates more clutter. A better solution would be a simple scripting language for filtering gear – if an item doesn’t meet your criteria, it could be automatically dismantled. This would also help players stay focused on what they actually need and not get overwhelmed or break their game flow.**Mental Models of Descendants and Stats**  Another challenge is the mental model required to adjust your descendants, weapons and their stats. There’s a wealth of videos and spreadsheets out there explaining how stats affect final damage calculations, but I think it’s Nexon’s responsibility to make this information more simpler and more accessible. A spreadsheet might be useful for min-maxers designing a build, but it doesn’t help the average player when you're in the middle of a game session, your inventory is full, and you need to decide what gear is worth keeping. I foresee this becoming even more of a problem as new descendants are introduced. A Nexon-authored tutorial or blog post on understanding and thinking about damage stats would be a great start. This content should focus on helping players understanding how the stats work, with their actual, human brain.**The "Stick with One or Two Descendants" Solution**  The obvious solution to many of these challenges (and one that seems to align with TFD’s design philosophy) is to focus on one or two descendants and ignore the rest. The problem with this approach, though, is that with descendants like Freyna, the content becomes either stale (dungeons) or perpetually out of reach (H2 bosses). Even branching out to build up Hailey doesn’t fully solve this, as H2 bosses are still mostly beyond my reach (though H1 is now trivial). Perhaps the real final challenge lies in socializing – finding serious players to team up with for H2 bosses. But again, this has to happen outside the game’s systems, and I wish Nexon would address this issue directly.**Weapon Balance and Storage Issues**  Lastly, it’s unfortunate that entire categories of weapons, like shotguns, beam rifles, and launchers, are essentially useless. While this simplifies the game to some degree, it also creates storage issues, especially when ultimate versions of these weapons take up valuable space. I’m reluctant to dismantle them, as I assume they may be buffed in the future or gain niche utility (like the Vestigial Organ with Gley in Molten Fortress). My preference would be for Nexon to either remove these weapon categories or make them relevant again.Thank you for reading my notes on my experience with TFD. It's a great game and I hope it thrives like Warframe and Destiny 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Warframe's (maybe like 15 days of play time as I never got into trading) near unlimited options for activities to do always caused me to get off after an hour or so every time I went back from being overwhelmed. Big fan of Destiny 2(played since D1 beta) so I feel I can say looter shooters are a genre I enjoy to say the least. This game provides a way to experience games similar to Warframe from day 1 where there isn't too much content to choose from(I know I sound crazy saying that about an mmo looter shooter). The mtx can be a bit much but honestly if you are not impatient and can see yourself being okay with farming for a few days to get parts to build other descendants or weapons this could be a good fit for you. The movement is super simple and not anything we haven't seen before but the grapple hook still feels fun when using to get momentum when racing your friends/party members to a destination.  Drop rates while not the most bountiful I feel; are still pretty fair. Live and die by the 1.6% drop chance. I do feel that paints should not be a "Buy or earn from Battlepass" only situation I think I saw another review mention they were also craftable in a beta for FD which having a free alternative is always something to be grateful for. I'm hopeful for the future of FD as the road map that is currently available for all to see seems extremely promising for the content to expect for the rest of this year. With Games like Destiny 2 winding down story-wise for the moment this game is a welcomed time waster to say the least. If there comes a time where I need a break or no longer wish to play FD I imagine I will go back to Warframe to try again.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying this game. I've been playing for 11 hours and I've already unlocked 2 additional characters (fairly easily I might add). Yes there are some F2P components, such as skins, that you have to pay to receive. Also, colors are expensive and you have to buy them for each component you wish to edit. However, the game itself can be grinded pretty quickly (so far anyway). Apparently, Nexon has no plans to change this which is a good thing. The performance is okay if you use DLSS or FSR with Frame Gen. It doesn't look "too bad" when using these. Still, it should be considered that UE5 is still relatively new with "limited plug-ins" as my friend pointed out. The story is decent but not spectacular. However, it's still more enjoyable compared to other looter shooters' (Borderlands, Destiny). The gameplay is similar Destiny for sure. I have never really played Warframe so I can't compare it. However, I hear it's similar to that as well. The cool thing about this game is the grappling hook it utilizes for traversal as well as offensive measures. It can also give you great vantage points to utilize high ground to eliminate bosses/foes. The mission types are varied enough not to become stale. The negative reactions to this game are astounding considering everything that you get for free. I'm enjoying playing this game with both community members and friends. I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is decent, but unless you want to farm all day for mods with .01% chance, I would stay clear. Pros: -Super fun with friends-intricate frame and weapon customization-content is somewhat challenging (but not optimized. will explain in cons)-graphics are great, but too demanding-Crafting is fun. Honestly was very similar to warframe. Very comprehensive and easy to navigateCons:-Story is laughable at best. -False drop rates. 38% drop rates on crap items seems to be more like 99%. farmed the dead bride for about 67 kills (Im lvl 100 on weapons so it was 15-20sec kills) and the damn mod to upgrade my frame didnt drop once. even with a 3% drop rate, it shouldnt take 70+ kills to drop. I have a good feeling this game is lieing about drop rates!-If you have no friends be prepared to hate the game. Matchmaking is a joke and maps have a VERY limited amount of players in it. -90% of the community is in Hard Mode so maps WILL BE Dead if you are new-Bunny spam everywhere. Meta frame with speed and insane clears. gl trying to enjoy missions/content-lag is crazy. I play Star Citizen with max graphics and I have never experienced lag like this. Actually, i have lol but doesnt make it right!-Haigos+ is a literal dead zone. 1 to 2 players in the zone max. The content starts off fine and fun with any frame (Or Descendant, but w/e) but once you get to Haigos, it goes from "Yea my frame is fun and amazing" to "wtf, how am I supposed to solo this?" The game takes a hard dive from challenging to hard in 1 map, and it gets worst from there on. -Mod drops are abyssal. Spent 6hrs trying to farm Mid-Air Maneuverability and best mod i got was a random weapon. Seriously, the grind is real in this game, even worst than Warframe.-Cash shop. I will admit that Every frame is available and you get bunny within the 1st hour or so, but farming for ever frame will take some time, effort, and sacrifice to RNGeezus.  Not to mention that everything in the cash shop is over priced. There is literally more stuff in the shop than content!-Community is kinda quiet unless you join the discord. They have a fun and innovation VOip in game, but no one uses it. Overall the game is solid if you spend 0 cash on it and need a time waster. The frames are pretty unique and fun to play but modding them is impossible with the RNG. I dont want mods to drop instantly, but 6+ hrs for 1 mod is where i draw the line.   I spent a good $500 on this getting some frames and mats for items, but overall, i got my moneys worth. However, if I had to redo, I wouldnt have spent money on this game and just stick to Warframe. Edit for Season 1: Stay clear. You have to SERIOUSLY invest in weapons and a descendant to even do the story. Its dumb and not worth to even try. Intercepts have absolutely 0 aggro mechanics. The new frame "Hailey" is ridiculous to farm and snag w/o spending money so most people buy it. And, even if you do use it, for some reason the bosses will instantly target you. Tested this with several friends and i have 80% aggro the entire time. Overall, I will say its a fun game, but STAY AWAY!!!! This game is predatory with cash shop and just not worth it. I cant Downvote this game enough!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: It appears they've solved the optimization issue for my particular setup, either through patches or otherwise (yes, I did some tinkering, but was still lagging after that, but that appears solved).The monetization is unbelievably expensive, but you can at least zero out your currency in this game, where in 99.9% of others, you can't. Also, it's your choice on if you're spending the money.F2P review.Two big problems so far.The first: The PC port from console seems to be *extremely* poorly optimized. I have at/above the recommended system requirements - with everything on low - and I *still* hit huge lag spikes with my 7700 and 3060Ti (admittedly not the brightest star in the sky, but it's not bad) running at 100% the whole time. I've done research, I've done my best to optimize my system and it's still a joke. I run other games at 160+ frames and 30-60% CPU use, no problem. This one? I can't even begin to explain why. (I'm turning on comments in the hopes that someone can educate me on this issue)The second and far more egregious problem: The incredibly predatory monetization tactics that only get worse as the game progresses (I'm going to explain that rq. This isn't an exaggeration for the sake of a review. As endgame content becomes harder to overcome, they want you to reach for your wallet. Their actual plan is to bottleneck you at endgame [because, remember, you've already invested a lot of time and maybe some $, so what's $30-100 more on a F2P you enjoy? See how they get you? Frog in a pot.] so that you are damn near forced to spend money, especially as the upgrade options become fewer, rarer and far more valuable, it's quite literally their business model to bottleneck you into paying at endgame. You get a lot and progress and whoopsie, after all the fun, here comes the paywall). If the prices were closer to the $5-80 range, I'd have already spent money a few times. I'm happy to support a F2P game (games aren't free) that's a decent use of my time. But minimum $30 for a single-use item? Screw THAT and screw them. Good games are worth supporting, but not this one.I would have supported the game with more reasonable pricing and I knew this was a gatcha mobile game for PC going into it, but the amount of greed is ludicrous. To get a single ultimate descendant you have to 1. Grind to get the equivalent to a loot chest. 2. Grind a boss to open it and hope you get the 3% drop. 3. Grind to get enough materials and currency to craft the item. Repeat 4 times to get all 4 items required to craft the ultimate. Is it fair for a free game to be grindy? Maybe. I accept that argument and probably agree with it. That doesn't change the fact that it is extremely grindy. Free games are often incredibly insidious. this certainly feels like one of those games.UPDATE: Since I got further in the game I realized that you can get higher drop rates by doing harder content. It is still grindy, but it does make a difference.Lack of content: There are like 5-10 different types of objectives and every mission is one of these or a chain of these. It can get old fast.Don't let the time I've played this game fool you. I like  grinding if I have a goal. I'm fine with spending all day trying to get one item. I realize that most people don't like  grinding, which is partly why I don't recommend the game even though I'm having  fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Seems like a pretty solid Warframe-esque spin on a Destiny-like looter shooter.  For anyone familiar with Warframe's mod systems for weapons and frames, they pretty much know what to expect here, that's basically identical, down to the relics for containing materials that you have to open.  While those progression mechanics are satisfying in general, I feel they could've fleshed that out a bit more with in-game lore and story... but at the same time, they clearly focused more on getting the core gameplay loops and progression mechanics right - and in the long run, that is probably more important.As far as the gameplay is concerned, I was worried the grappling hook mechanic would be a bit janky from watching trailers.  I'm happy to report that, at least with a keyboard and mouse (that's all I've used so far) it works pretty well - definitely feels better than I expected.  From going to weak points on the colossus to scaling the environment, it seems to work well.Seems to run fine with a 3060, and no crashes to report so far (4 hours in on launch day).  Didn't have to create an account to play, that's always good, no launcher that I've noticed.  So I've gotta say, it's looking promising.Criticisms from other reviews so far are relatively minor:1. Negative reviews around item delivery: Note that it's normal in some games like this for delays around item delivery to be encountered, and it currently looks like it can take a few hours to receive based on forum posts.  Not a huge deal, as long as you expect it.2. Reviews saying it's easy or boring after spending less than 1 hour in the game.  I don't think those reviews can be taken seriously, as most games are much easier to start out and ramp up the challenge and mechanics to consider as it goes on.  That's... normal, though I am still expecting it to get more challenging later.  People who are familiar with Warframe progression systems may have a legitimate concern if they find that boring, because that's basically what this is, but I don't think that's what they're talking about.

_childDocuments_.review: "The First Descendant: Where Warframe and Destiny Had a Space Baby"Are you ready to embark on an epic journey through the cosmos that feels like a fusion of your favorite space shooters? Look no further than "The First Descendant," a game that blends the fast-paced action of Warframe with the looter-shooter vibes of Destiny.As you dive into this galactic adventure, you'll immediately notice the sleek, futuristic visuals reminiscent of Warframe, complete with dazzling neon lights and intricate armor designs that make you feel like a space ninja on a quest for loot. The combat mechanics are as smooth as a freshly polished Excalibur sword, allowing you to unleash devastating combos and powers with the finesse of a Guardian wielding a Golden Gun.But fear not, dear space traveler, for "The First Descendant" also pays homage to Destiny's addictive loot grind. Prepare yourself for endless hours of chasing rare weapons and gear that will make your fellow teammates green with envy – or maybe just a little blue, depending on the shader.And let's not forget the multiplayer aspect, where you can team up with friends to tackle challenging raids and missions that will test your skills and teamwork. It's like forming your own Fireteam, except with a few more cosmic twists and turns thrown in for good measure.So, strap in, get ready to blast off, and prepare for a gaming experience that will have you saying, "Wait, is this Warframe or Destiny?" Because in "The First Descendant," the line between the two is as blurry as a drunken Grineer stumbling through the Tower of Babble.Overall, "The First Descendant" offers a delightful blend of familiar gameplay elements from Warframe and Destiny, wrapped up in a shiny new package that's sure to keep you entertained for light years to come. Just remember: in space, no one can hear you scream – but they might hear you laughing at the quirky jokes sprinkled throughout this out-of-this-world adventure.Rating: 4.5/5 stars – For when you can't decide between being a space ninja or a space cowboy, "The First Descendant" has got you covered.

_childDocuments_.review: *ANOTHER GAME REVIEW, LETS GOO!!!!*For starters I've been playing this game since (Beta) and yes it has had it's issues with the early start, however the game is becoming a icon of MMO game play. From characters, Maps, Dungeons, Bosses and a STRONG COMMUNITY that is willing to assist you throughout your experience. I will say a lot of players are complaining about (DROP RATES), but let me express to you that the drop rates in the game all come down to RNG (Random Number Generator), in which many similar games that use the same feature all have the same experience. If your dedicated, stubborn and just don't give up you will get your item's in no time. I think the creators developed the game for such a purpose. We tend to realize in life that getting something with little to no effort doesn't have the same fortitude to that which is a challenge and a struggle. Once you accomplish something you have a inner emotion of accomplishment. I'm getting off topic, so lets lock right back in. The Community is astonishing, you can easily find friends and others to play with. Just join the (The First Descendant Discord) channel and you will be making friends in no time. To the Developing team, I applaud you and must say "Thank you for listening", because no many Game Developing Teams will go out of their way to do a (QA) with their Consumers & Community. They are listening Ladies & Gentlemen so if you assume they're not, then I will correct you and say they are. From each season they're adding unreal new content, new dungeons, new bosses and characters/descendants. Many people have told me this game is similar to that of Warframe & Destiny to which I've never played the too, but if you're from those communities I will just go out and say that those individuals have bias opinions of this game.  The Shop is outstanding in remarks to the amount of content, they're really making the in-game shop to reflect on what the community wishes to buy. So instead of just wasting your money on something they designed they're starting to listen to the community. For a example, the Nun outfit had the two strips in the back and they removed it and game you a free other outfit so you can bounce between each outfit if you like only if you purchased it. That was really kind of them to do that. Plus they have the ETA Shop which gives you the ability to get other key components for the items your grinding and struggling with. Gives you a little edge especially when you have certain materials that are building up in your consumer inventory that you just need to get rid of. This game has a lot of potential seriously, there is already discussion on have a In-Game Trading system that many players wish Nexon to implore. It would make it a true community game. If you got the Cheddar to buy a difficult item off someone that why not if you can get Gold/Kupier very quickly or just trade one item for the next. I would highly implore those who are either (New) to the game to just be patient while playing. Not all games are supposed to be easy and just give you everything at the start. If you're (Old) to this game and have a biased opinion about the game, please give it another try because I think Nexon has learned from their failures and successes to give us all such a incredible game. _childDocuments_.review: Overall it's a 5/10.Edit: So their game plan due to rapidly dropping player numbers is to add FOMO in order to get whales and streamers to buy their skins and bundles.As my review below said, it has the foundations of a solid game. However, if their plan is to lean even more into microtransaction hell this quickly, then I don't see the game lasting much longer.Even Ubisoft learned from its mistakes after Outlaws was a bust.Season 1 of this game was worse than season 1 of Diablo 4... and that's saying a LOT.I changed my overall to a 5/10, and I do not recommend this game.I haven't played too much, but what I have played is pretty damn okay, and sometimes it's even pretty good.Those are indeed compliments, because in truth I don't like grindy games like Destiny, or The Division. The latter had really good lore and atmosphere, but the grind just isn't my thing.This game has a lot of grind. It also has the tendency to make you feel sooooo close to unlocking a part or research ingredient but it ends up taking up a half hour of time for you to even get it... then you have to research the whatsitwhosit which literally takes hours.I get the purpose is to make it so damn annoying for those who want to breeze through the game so that they feel compelled to buy the dumb characters or weapons... but come on now. I guess it's not as annoying as it could be since I do have a full time job so I can grind a bit before bed, then when I get home from work all of the stuff is researched, but eeeh it still feels scummy.The story feels almost ai generated, along with many of the characters and layout of Albion. It's too damn clean and corny. The lore is legit interesting and I do like the different locations. Don't get me wrong, I love corny science fiction. It's my bread and butter. When I saw that the first mini-boss was named Greg I literally couldn't stop laughing throughout the fight. It was very entertaining.The objectives are pretty uuuhhh... generic and repetitive. They all consist of "kill these guys", "defend this terminal", "Escort this bot" and the worst of them all "Collect the orbs". The game needs more variety, especially since there is no actual endgame, so the grind is about just collecting materials and unlocking characters. Even the battlepass is pretty mediocre with only a few really interesting unlocks.Which is wild to me since it's meant to bring in money, but how do you expect to entice people into buying the battlepass if it takes hours to unlock the levels and the unlocks are pretty "okay" overall?I guess the focus is to get people to buy the characters, as I mentioned before.If left to cook a bit, I think the game could actually do some good things. I've mostly complained so far, so here are some really good positives:I genuinely like the boss fights. It's one of the strongest aspects of the game in my opinion. I like how their weaknesses and strengths, along with the fighting patterns emphasize planning and teamwork. Both are aspects that many other games of this ilk kind of lack.I like how easy it is to pick up and play. The benefits of having a fairly generic story is that I don't have to worry too much about the dialog when grinding for loot.The different Descendants are enjoyable. Yes, there is a meta, but from my understanding the meta is mostly about speeding up the grind over actual numbers so it doesn't feel like my starter character is any less capable than Bunny or Valby.The lore is pretty interesting, and it's neither obstructive nor too hidden. The world is generally explained through the dialog and story, but there is in-game information you can learn yourself if you want to actually know more about the game's setting which is fun.Bottomline: It's free, and it's a run n gun kinda looter shooter. It's a certified brain off, guns out kinda game imo. Yes, Nexon is pretty much a leech on the industry, but as long as the game is still given love and care overtime, then it can be more than the sum of its research parts.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very much inspired by Warframe and other looter shooter games. There is plenty of content, a lot of Descendants at launch, weapons, a full campaign and enough end game content to keep you occupied.Pros+ Great looking game, characters, maps, locations etc.+ Performance and Optimisation is pretty solid too for me (1st Gen Ryzen 5 Cpu, Radeon 6600 GPU, 16GB RAM)+ Plenty of Descendants with different playstyles to choose from.+ They can all be unlocked free (even if a bit grindy).+ More Updates and Roadmap revealed and all looks promising.Cons- Monetization needs a bit of rework. Battlepass isn't good. No descendant skins in the BP, lots of emotes etc. It costs the equivalent of $10 which is fine but you don't get enough currency back to buy the next one as is the case in other games. Current selection of skins is also a bit limited. Basically 3-4 outfits for all of them pretty much.- Buying ultimate skins is very expensive. Sold in bundles priced $60-$100 !- a few other minor issues like robototic voice acting etc but not a big enough con.Overall I am pretty happy with how this game has turned out at launch. I had played the previous betas of this game starting from the first one in late 2022. I had played that a lot (15+ Hours) and only briefly tried the later betas. My main issue with the betas was the performance. Happy to report that is all sorted and  works very well even on my modest system now.One thing I do feel is important to note here is that if you have played Looter Shooter games previously you are bound to enjoy and understand the game more. I had a few hundred hours in Warframe but I joined it in 2017-2018.  Always felt like starting at episode 586 of the world's longest Soap Opera.Here I felt more at home since I was here right from the beginning. There are a lot of things borrowed and systems that work like Warframe. Fast paced movement, grappling, farming missions quickly over and over to get drops etc.There is a lot of grinding but its not as bad as some may say. As for the repetitive nature of missions etc I feel that is once again something that is only an issue for people who don't like Looter Shooters or other games with a similar gameplay loop. I even liked Outriders, so maybe that explains why I am liking this.They also provide all the information for grinding and obtaining materials in the game. May take a little time to fully understand but everything is available in game.So overall I would recommend this game but keep in mind you have to like the looter shooter genre to enjoy this properly. The only issue is probably some of the drop rates and prices for cosmetics etc. I feel a little fine tuning there and it should be something the does well. Lets see how this game is a few months from now but player numbers are good and game is fun for now.UPDATE after almost 400 Hours :Still enjoying and still plan to play more. A few things worth mentioning.+Devs have been great so far. 7 patches released so far since launch in less than 2 months. They are listening to the feedback and improving things. Lots of improvements already which have helped reduce grind and made things a lot smoother.There is a lot of comparison to Warframe online from other reviews on YT. Makes sense but most of the comments are along the line of "this is a poor clone of WF, I am going back to WF".I don't think this is meant to be a replacement to Warframe. I feel its for those who tried WF and did not like it because it was too vast and difficult to understand. I had approx 250 hours and I barely understood how to do the basic things. Kept constantly asking friends about how to do certain things. With TFD I am already making simple guides to help out people because its easier to understand. I hope TFD does well long term and holds an active playerbase but if it doesn't that's ok too because I have thoroughly enjoyed my time with it so far and in this crowded market its done alright.Full Guide on Farming Ultimate Bunny for Free : Ultimate Bunny Build Guide : Ultimate Freyna Build Guide :

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I can recommend any looter shooter right now. I have 900-ish hours in Warframe, and I never got into Destiny because of the contraversies, so I've been waiting a long time to have something fun to play. I'll just make a generalized list of what my complaints are. Cash Store currency: not being able to earn some currency in the game feels bad. But I am mostly okay with microtransactions. Drop rates. It's bad.The lack of customization or keybinds. I don't know why, in every MMO or loot shooter, we seem to get less and less customization. In particular, I like to keybind them based on their format; defensives go on my mouse buttons, and combat ones I usually bind elsewhere. Which works great to a point. I started with Ajax, but as soon as I got Bunny, they chose to change all the abilities, so what I thought would be static (the same skills in the same spot, defensives and offensives in the same position) turned out not to be.The story is okay; I like it so far.Game play is bad; I've played Warframe for around 900 hours. On their client, and then later on steam. It's a very boring format of 3–4 missions: do the zone dungeon, move to the next area. They really need to expand on this desperately. It's pretty much why I am writing this at 28 hours into the game. I do a map, get bored, and go play Warzone for a bit, then come back. Or just go out and touch the grass.The hot take: this game takes a fan service approach, but, uh, I'd like something more than copying pasta females. We got the cliche anime stereotypes, or it feels like it. I need a muscle mommy, haha, like Karlach from Bg3 and Astarion.Tooltips: we need better descriptions of mods and items.Melee combat, I don't care for it at all. I would like some melee options, like in Warframe, where my favorites are still Lacera and Mios.I plan to finish the story because I do enjoy it, but I think they could take a page out of Warframe and just have more to do in the game; it feels "short" in some weird way.What I like so far is that the game is free, and as of the current state, you can farm everything in the game without spending a dime other than skins.The grappling feature of the game provides a fresh take on the looter shooter genre and can create many different play styles. You can grapple onto walls to fly around, grapple to an enemy and melee for a free knockdown effect, grapple onto a boss's armor pieces to tear it down, etc. Though I would like more mobility, Obviously, take this with a grain of salt. It's just an opinion I have based on my experience so far.

_childDocuments_.review: My time is mostly from the beta where I had decent connection to the servers (rip new players). In the beta I unlocked all the characters and completed the full story, doing everything available in the period. Not much seems to have changed since the beta when I logged in again recently.we all know the cash shop sucks, but the rest of the game isnt special either. Sure its the latest looter shooter live-service game, but every part of this game feels like it lacks creativity and soul. People draw comparisons to destiny and warframe and they are right. go pick those games up instead. The modding system is ripped straight from warframe except its a bunch of stat increases and the ability to sort through them absolutely sucks and you need multiple versions of the same mods. they dont meaninfully impact gameplay in exciting ways and are mostly "increase X damage". theres a few augment mods that do a bit more but nothing that wow-ed me. Visually the game looks great, but my god is it souless. its more of an unreal tech demo than a game. none of the designs feel lovingly crafted. it looks like you typed "hot scifi girl" into midjourney and churned them out. Not a single mission has impact or importance beyond "kill x thing" 3 feet apart from the last place you did the same. The big arena fights look kinda cool, but outside of literally also being the warframe simulacrum in terms of environment, it just kinda is a big sponge to dump damage into. This isnt a game you are playing because you like it. this is a game you play because it reminds you of what you do like. but it will never be those things. The abilities feel stunted, movement doesnt feel great, cheese strategies arent fun but are effective (looking at you "running in circles as bunny and everything just dies" strat). They could add to this game for the next 10 years with meaningful updates, but it will never ever be good because it wasnt made to be good. there are too many structural problems to the gameplay system in this game to ever achieve that. The only goal this game was made with was to try to steal a bite of other's pie without any deep understanding of why they are successful and the first decendant doesnt try to do anything of its own or better in any way. Major pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat in  is undeniably its strongest suit. The thrill of wielding various weapons and experimenting with diverse abilities is exhilarating. The game offers a plethora of customization options, allowing players to tailor their combat style extensively. Whether you prefer close-quarters brawling or long-range precision, there's something for everyone.However, this excitement is marred by a significant flaw: the lack of variety in gameplay scenarios. Despite the myriad ways to configure your combat strategy, the repetitive nature of missions, especially defense missions, quickly becomes tiresome. It's disheartening to see such promising combat mechanics shackled to monotonous tasks that feel like filler content.If combat is the heart of , then crafting is its cumbersome backbone. Crafting in the game is an exercise in patience and frustration, designed to test the limits of even the most dedicated players. To create any significant item—be it a weapon, descendant (character), or their components—one must endure a multistep process that epitomizes grind.Firstly, acquiring the necessary materials involves repetitive grinding through missions, often requiring specific blueprint drops that are frustratingly rare. This gating mechanism artificially extends gameplay time, pushing players towards spending excessive hours farming for essential resources.Once materials are gathered, the crafting process itself introduces another layer of waiting. Components must be meticulously crafted, each step laden with timers that can stretch for hours or even days. The pinnacle of this waiting game is crafting descendants, which can demand an excruciating 36-hour wait for completion.Herein lies the crux of the issue:  doesn't respect players' time. It demands hours of grinding and waiting, teasing with the option to expedite progress through real-world currency. By monetizing the acceleration of crafting timers and material acquisition, the publisher undermines the integrity of gameplay, turning what should be a rewarding progression system into a cynical exercise in pay-to-progress.The insidious nature of monetization in  cannot be overstated. It's evident that the game's design deliberately introduces friction to coerce players into spending money. Whether it's bypassing lengthy crafting timers or securing rare materials through microtransactions, every aspect of progression seems calibrated to push players towards opening their wallets.This predatory approach not only tarnishes the player experience but also erodes trust in the game's longevity. The publisher's unwillingness to address fundamental gameplay frustrations in favor of monetizable solutions speaks volumes about their priorities. Players are left feeling exploited, their investment of time and money undervalued in a game that prioritizes profit margins over player satisfaction.In conclusion,  squanders its potential with a shortsighted focus on monetization strategies that disrespect players' time and financial investment. While the core combat mechanics shine brightly, they are overshadowed by repetitive missions and a punitive crafting system designed to extract maximum profit. For those seeking a fair and fulfilling gaming experience, look elsewhere until the publisher reevaluates its priorities and returns to honoring the player above all else.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface this review, after 80 hours in I'm still entirely a F2P player. I've completed the campaign, am deep into hard mode having killed several of the hard mode collosi (the major bosses), crafted 6 descendants and many ultimate weapons. There are expensive in-game purchases, but the fact I've made it this far without spending a dime is fairly impressive.TFD surprised me and I did not expect to enjoy it as much as I do. The gameplay holds up to some of the best in the genre and the guns, skills, and grapple feel satisfying to use. There's a lot of content here with many things to grind for, and the number of builds and gear available keeps it from feeling stale. If you've played Warframe, TFD is heavily inspired by it and even directly imitates some of it's systems such as modding i.e. how you customize and increase the power of your gear and character. It feels right at home here and I consider that a positive. It can be fairly grindy and you'll find yourself cursing RNG at times, but overall it does feel pretty comparable to D2, Warframe, etc. All that being said, I recommend The First Descendant. If you enjoy other games in the looter shooter genre there's a good chance you'll enjoy it. Give it a shot, it's free after all.

_childDocuments_.review: ~ Before you start reading i want you to understand that yes i am complaining about the current stat of the game, even though i like the game. ~ ~ I also don't think that anyone should complain about anything without at least coming up with one or two possible solutions to fix their complaint. which I have suggested in this overly worded review. ~I've got over 400*nearly 500* hours on this game but i don't play for the "meta" or with bunny.  I play under powered characters like Blair, Jayber, and esiemo... not because they are under powered but because i like those characters, they are just unfortunately not Bunny or gley or lepic, or valby  so they are trash by comparison.  Anyways, I was hoping that with this update i'd at least see some well deserved buffs to Blair since he feels like one of if not the most under preforming character on the roster but all the devs did was increase his range... and not even increase it but instead increase the maximum you could achieve.    look... with all the time i have sank into this game,  i have 9 catalysts on and a energy activator on blair.  i assembled the best possible SKILL DAMAGE build for the character and he still cannot hit enemies as hard as any other Ground AOE character.  Blair's ultimate *his 4*  at full potential hits only 1/10 the strength of a lepic's 4. . .   and yes i am using Crit on blair.Even worse is the Transcendent mod "Incendiary Bomb" which is an absolute joke.Its an absolute nerf to an already horrible skill.   I spammed the boss fight until i got this thing because from its description which read "throws a projectile forward that spawns a flame zone where it lands"  to me it sounded like what the skill should've done on Blair anyways but I'll grind for it because i believed he needed it.  Imagine my face when i saw what the mod actually did.You throw a small fireball *which doesn't do direct damage if you hit an enemy :( * That goes only a few meters away from you and explodes, mid travel,  without hitting anything or anyone and leaves a flame zone that is  massively reduced in size of the original skill. So There is absolutely no reason to ever run this card... or honestly this character outside of his "truly Deadly Cuisine" build which by comparison to every other bosser... isnt "truly deadly" at all unless you are solo.   *the big lonely sad*Or his   "backfire" gun build... and even then he is the worst of the gun builds because each of those other characters can still deal damage or provide assistance with their remaining skills.Blair is a Spell damage character with no spell damage.   He has no support skills to fall back on to be a full fledged gun character, he has no CC to atleast slow down or disrupt the enemies.   essentially if you wan't to be a gun build with blair you have to completely ignore his skills outside of just buffing your gun.   what a waste.   I like this game but Devs you really really need to considering both nerfing over preforming characters, which imo would help with the overall health of the game and promote challenging content for all characters not just for those that are under preforming. and, but only after this ^start buffing the STILL under preforming characters. that would ensure a level playing field for all characters,  sure there would still be a few OP characters, every game has the "Meta" AND understandably not every bit of content is made for each character's kit. but in the current state of the game,  There is No reason *outside of utility like enzo & sharen* to pick any character that isn't Lepic, Bunny, Gley, or Valby... other than "i like these characters even if i am an absolute detriment to my team," heres a few character suggestions... kindaBlair needs damage a base damage x% increase to all of his DoT skills. His 1 needs to be reworked to be "incendiary bomb" and that Mod can be converted into an actual Bomb version that could perhaps Explode on contact dealing Direct damage and leaving a DoT.His "burn taste" skill should be able to be canceled at any time.    being locked in that animation is awful and often times deadly for blair and not the enemy.it'd be nice if absorbing your flame zones gave blair some utility or survivablilty functions aswell.  like a temporary over shield or a pulsing damage aoe, similar to bunny, that's damage would be based on the amount of zones you absorbed.   just a thought.Jayber needs his base skill crit rate to be 10% or the Skill x % to be increased so that his turrets can actually be useful late game *hard Difficulty*  I also think his element should be changed to electric since his Arche Powers are to control Electronics... which are electric??? even one of his Red Mods turns his 4 intro a Lightning damage aoe.   why not just say electric?   we have no male electric character and we already have way way too many Non attribute characters.Esiemo... look the man has to do so much with his kit and setup just to deal less than half of any other bossing character than simply just presses a button or two and melt bosses.so why does he have to work so much harder and yet is still weaker than them?   thats a whole lotta work for nothing.   I couldn't even begin to suggest a fix for this character that isn't an entire rework. Even his Passive is an absolute stinker. i mean the simple *BuFf HiS DaMaGe* might help but really when other characters can simply just exist or run around and kill enemies without any effort at all... i don't think the real solution is just BUFF DAMAGE for this one.  I think his kit is interesting and definitely stands out from any of the other characters but he's working  far to hard for such little payout.*i do think his taunt Mod for his landmines is great... it actually made me use him as a farming character for quite a while.* so maybe more mods like this... things that dramatically change the function of a skill and the gameplay/role of that character.Even wtih these complaints i think that This is a great game and it has a good foundation to build upon.  but this "buff" for blair was just not it.

I've got 30 hours on record for the game, so not long when compared to games of the same type like destiny or warframe but not an insignificant amount of time either. I got the first part no problem from doing a dungeon but had to get the second from something called "zone recon". now this is a mission type that you have to "stealth" in order to complete, what they want you to do is kill all the enemies then hack a console to get the good loot at the end. But it REALLY means is go and farm sharen who has 3 spots you have a 20% chance to get from each. THEN you have to wait for 3 days or so for her to craft. Which isnt something that im opposed to BUT REMEMBER im not farming cause i want to PLAY sharen. im FARMING TO DO A SIDE OBJECTIVE TO GET THE ONE THAT I WANT. this isnt an issue in warframe or in destiny. On top of all that the progression in this game is whack. did you have a legendary weapon you really liked using but it took you a while to farm? too bad, you gotta go out there and farm that sucker a whole bunch more times to level up that weapon. did you have a purple tier weapon that you really liked but its falling off? too bad, you gotta go out there and farm for a level up slave for that weapon in order to make it viable. And on the topic of boss fights. Did they really have to be that problematic? Im not one for soulslike encounters but i dont mind trying to fight a boss thats tough but doable. _childDocuments_.review: Incredibly generic, derivative and uninteresting in almost all aspects, The First Descendant is a third-person looter shooter that tries to build an experience clearly inspired by the Destiny games by Bungie, but fails at all points to recreate anything worthwhile.Boring and completely replaceable missions follow one after the other, where you fight the same handful of a few visually completely incohesive enemy types, with no end in sight.Meanwhile the game metaphorically buries you in loot, where within minutes you're likely going to acquire the same weapon with different stats, making inventory management, or rather cleanup, mandatory.Not only does this worsen the value of getting new weapons, it also really doesn't help that most weapons are almost identical to others of the same class.And with the ammo system the game employs, those actually fun and interesting weapons you get every now and then, will run out of ammo constantly.You add the barrage of incredibly objectifying and wholly overpriced character skins for the female cast on top of this already barely mediocre game and you have something that doesn't even deserve to be called we-have-destiny-at-home.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. To be blunt, it's just Destiny 2 (general combat, guns, map designs) with all of the Warframe mechanics (crafting, weapon mods etc.). If you like that, you love it, if you don't, you hate it. As for how far I've gotten in 30 hours and my level of experience: I did not play the beta, but over 30 hours in I have hit max level on 2 characters so far, which isn't hard to do. I have hit ML11. I have done about 6 areas completely and have 2 left to finish in the story. I think I have done 5 Void bosses. I'm more than half way through the story, but have not unlocked hard mode or started the actual endgame grind yet, this is still the leveling phase, but fairly deep into it.As for the pros:* Solid combat* Decent story* Skippable cutscenes* A new grind to enjoy* SOMETIMES fun solo, very fun with friends* Great cosmetics if you like beautiful Asian womenAs for the cons:* It's Destiny combat, this isn't bad, unless you hate Destiny* The grind ranges from okay to kind of ridiculous. More so than even Warframe...* SOMETIMES solo is not fun with squishy frames and some deaths feel very unfair on harder stuff.* While the cosmetics are amazing, they are EXPENSIVE. Typical scummy currency models from NexonOverall, if you like Destiny and Warframe and looking for  anew game, this is it. If you do not want to support Nexon, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ business practices or get easily frustrated when soloing, this may be worth a pass even as a looter shooter fan. At the end of the day though, it's a free game and does not hurt to try it out. If anything, you playing and not spending money only costs them money in the end, so give it a shot and if you hate it, don't feel bad about uninstalling it.Warframe: 9/10Destiny 2: 8/10The First Descendant: 7/10 with potential to be a 6 or 8 based on changes and future experiences with even deeper endgame.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm a bit late to review this, but I'd still like to weigh in on it. As many of you already know, TFD is a blend of Destiny, Warframe, and Borderlands style mechanics. Overall, I think TFD strikes that balance/mix surprisingly well, and sometimes it even takes those mechanics and does them better. For example, for those familiar with Warframe, you can assign a polarity (symbol) to a mod slot, resetting your character's level but allowing you to halve the cost of mods with a matching polarity in that slot. In TFD, you only lose 10 mod capacity, regardless of your overall mastery rank, plus you don't lose access to your abilities (something which took the Warframe community years and years of asking to get). You can also activate/deactivate those polarities in your other loadout presets for that character. There are many examples like this, but I don't want to make the review too long.As for the microtransactions, well many of them aren't very 'micro', let's put it that way. The pricing on some stuff is honestly just goofy, I don't have a better way to describe it. However, the game is not pay-to-win, it is *pay-to-rush*, which is an important distinction I want to make. You do not gain any unfair advantage by buying things in the game, you only cut out the farm. If you want my honest suggestion, don't play this game if you don't have self-control when it comes to your wallet. I won't say not to buy anything, I did myself, but if you're going to, don't go buying your way through the game because it'll just become boring. Outside of maybe getting some cosmetics (everybody knows fashion is the TRUE endgame), the only things I can really recommend considering buying is the other two starter characters, and maybe the battle pass if you're into that.You choose one of three starter characters (Viessa, Ajax, and Lepic). There are plenty of guides online so I won't explain them, but then you can also unlock Bunny, Sharen, Freyna, and Blair through the Normal mode missions without having craft their parts, just collect all their pieces and do the final craft at the end. All of these are the characters that cost 300 Caliber in the store, the others are all 600 or 900. For this reason, I only recommend getting the two starters you didn't choose, as that will give you a character of every element to work with, and the starter characters aren't as simple as the other four you unlock through the Normal mode missions.This review is getting a bit long so I'll try to keep from saying too much more. The other thing I want to say is that I've been pleasantly surprised with how the devs have listened to the community so far. Each Thursday is patch day, and each week they've released a patch addressing multiple concerns or suggestions the community has had, and they've already fixed many problems the game had at launch. While it's certainly not perfect and still needs some work, I can say that I enjoy the game thoroughly and that it's worth giving a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: An Honest Review of The First DescendantAfter playing for nearly 55 hours and completing most of the campaign, I can say that this game is really enjoyable and not as bad as some of these reviews make it out to be. Sure, there are some obvious flaws and problems such as the monetization and AFK farmers that so many have brought up, but overall, for a newly released game, there have not been as many severe issues as I thought there would be. First of all, the monetization is definitely not as insane as some people are saying it is. From my experience so far, I have not felt like I needed to purchase anything to progress at all. Basically everything can be crafted and farmed for if you have the time and patience besides cosmetics, which is fair in my opinion, since they don't affect the gameplay anyway. The game doesn't really force microtransactions down your throat or fill your screen with them like some other games do. There main things you can purchase are entire descendants, starter packs with resources, or cosmetics. Like most other games these days, this game also has a standard 10 dollar battle pass with decent value, but if you are like me and have not considered purchasing anything so far, the free part of the battle pass offers plenty of loot and cosmetics. STORYStory wise, I think the game is a little weak, but for a looter shooter game where many people playing aren't going to care for the lore and story, it holds up. The story blends into the gameplay really well and the cutscenes are really well-made. As someone who likes fantasy and scifi, the plot was a little confusing at times but it was still followable and interesting. The voice acting was also not bad, certain characters were voiced better than others, but I'm pretty sure the english version was more of a dub, and the Korean version is much better and matched the mouth animations more accurately according to other people. GAMEPLAYTFD's gameplay is one of its stronger areas, as the movement and controls are pretty simple and smooth, with sprinting and rolling being the main movement mechanics. TFD's gameplay is also super similar to Warframe's gameplay, minus having the melee at your disposal at all times like Warframe does. In TFD, guns are the main weapons, so the melee is a one shot use that is rechargable while Warframe allows you to spam the melee. Although the movement in TFD is pretty basic, TFD eliminates the need for a complex movement system like that of Warframe's by introducing a grappling hook that you can use in a variety of ways, allowing for many possible playstyles. The gunplay in TFD is also really satisfying, as each weapon has its own traits and style of play. The recoil is reasonably balanced, and the guns feel powerful when you shoot, thanks to the great sound design. The gameplay loop is quite addictive, and the farming can get tiring at times. My personal favorite game mode so far are called Void Intercept Missions, which are basically boss fights. I love this mode since the bosses in the game are really different from one another, and can get quite challenging, requiring you and your team to strategize which weapons to use or which descendant composition to bring.CHARACTERSI think we all knew what to expect from the characters in the game knowing that it was made by Nexon... >:DJokes aside, the designs for each character are unique and detailed, and with a total of 21 descendants and ultimate variants, I'm sure everyone who plays will find a descendant with a playstyle that fits for them. There are also a lot of cosmetic options, but currently most of them are only available by paying real money. Hopefully Nexon will make them more F2P soon. Another thing I want to mention about the game is how it compares to similar titles such as Destiny 2 and Warframe which were definitely their main inspirations. Personally, I have only played Warframe, so I can't speak much on Destiny 2. First of all, I had a much harder time putting down TFD compared to Warframe, which I think I can attribute to the overall progression flow of the game. In the TFD, the campaign/story-mode is pretty easy to follow, and they set a clear path of missions for you to do, while in Warframe, I got lost a lot of the time and wasn't really sure what I wanted or needed to farm or what missions to do next. Another big factor was being able to play TFD without having to open a wiki the whole time whereas in Warframe, I was constantly searching things up to figure out what to do with a certain item or resource. Sure, there are some more complex things I had to search up while playing TFD such as weapon level transmission and crystallization catalysts, but for the most part, the game does teach you about them as you progress, and you have an access info menu that tells you very specifically where to acquire every resource and material in the game. What really put this game ahead of Warframe for me though was the charm and designs of the characters/descendants. In Warframe, I wasn't always that excited to unlock a new warframe and I never really found the designs that appealing due to the lack of a face or a distinct personality. In TFD, I love unlocking new descendants because they all have their own unique personalities, outfits, abilities, and designs which makes them a lot more fun for me to play. So far, the dev team have been very vocal and actively listening the community which surprised me and the playerbase because I have heard that Nexon has a bad reputation for not listening to their communities and using suspicious systems for the drop rates. However, in just the second week of release, the dev team fixed a big chunk of issues brought up on social media in such a quick fashion that gives me hope that this game is heading in the right direction. It certainly has a lot of potential as long as the devs continue to release new content and listen to their community, so if you are on the fence about playing, just give it a try, maybe it will be a great fit for you. Me personally, I think I will possibly play this long term because of how much I have enjoyed it in such a short span of time and how much endgame content there is. Thank you for reading :)
