_childDocuments_.review:
The First Descendant is a free third-person cooperative action RPG shooter featuring high-quality graphics. Experience the fun of strategic boss fights through 4-player co-op and various unique characters, exciting gunplay, and looting. A variety of equipment is necessary for growth, and you can obtain them through clearing scenario missions within the game or in the World Missions where cooperation is crucial and battles with huge bosses.

The player becomes a Descendant in the game and is given a mission to fight against the invaders for the survival of humans and to protect the 'Ingris continent'. The player can experience a spectacular story by growing stronger through various missions and stories to finally discover the Descendants' secret.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, now that the online is fixed I can give my opinion.The game itself is gorgeous. Superb music, incredible animation and splendid pixel art. In my opinion, this is top tier visually.Very good game, but sometimes I feel some of the combos are a bit too long, but the neutral game behind it is very enjoyable and the characters are very interesting.Where it's less enjoyable is the low amount of newcomers to the series online. So far, I very rarely see people at my level and as a consequence I get utterly destroyed to a point it's not really fun because I don't have much time to learn the game while I'm getting tenderized in the corner by 89 hits combos. You seem to have options to filter people by their rank, but so far everyone seem to be D rank no matter their skill level is. I assume that if most people stick to casual mode and/or lobbies, you won't be able to force the game to match you with people around your level. That said, this might be an issue that will resolve itself as time goes.Hopefully, more people will pick up the game, because when you fight someone at your level, this game is extremely fun. That said, I think the game is worth it to a point I'm willing to stick to it even if I must face much much stronger opponents.  If you want a game that has a rank system that is similar to Street Fighter 6, you will probably be disappointed. That said, I think Under Night In-Birth II is a much better game than Street Fighter 6. Its main flaw is literally that not much people are playing it right now.At the moment of writing this review there are 2,113 people playing Under Night In-Birth II. The game launched two days ago... For comparison: - Tekken 8 has 43,338 people playing (launched today)- Street Fighter 6 has 9639 people playing (launched about seven months ago)- Guilty Gears Strive has 2,145 people playing (launched in 2021)I really hope this game can survive its terrible launch due to buggy online (that is now fixed). It would be a shame if this game remains niche and underground because I really think it deserves to be much more on top.Edit: FFS Tekken 7 beats us.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm leaving this review cause I think the mass review bombing is unwarranted and turns away people who might be interested in this series.The game is a great improvement over CLR, the new characters and mechanics all feel great to play and use. Single Player and training mode work fine! In match the Rollback works great, and I have experienced no desync unlike MBTL's launch. The crashes and other networking errors are annoying but the Dev's have made multiple statements about how they are working to solve these issues and have already released 2 patches that have improved stability exponentially. I think some leniency should be given to the Devs as their team is only 14 people, and aren't massive like Bandai Namco (who are getting little backlash for Tekken 8 having many of the same issues). I think in the future French Bread shouldn't neglect having a PC beta to see these issues before launch, but I suspect Sony likely forced their hand on that front.TLDR;Game's great, just give the Dev's a week to fix the issues before writing off the game. This series deserves a bigger community.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite fighting game, and the series has been near and dear to my heart for nearly a decade. I'm so glad it finally has rollback netcode.It's an anime fighting game much more based on the ground game than anime fighters usually are. There is a universal "assault" mechanic that acts as a sort of air dash, but no actual air dashing per se for the most part. So the movement is not quite as fluid as Melty Blood Type Lumina, but in exchange you get the "grind grid" system which puts a tug of war at the bottom center of the screen, rewarding whichever player has superior positioning, movement, offense, and defense, on a moment-to-moment basis, awarding a buff every 9 seconds or so. Whoever has the buff can spend it for different things, or keep it for a blanket damage bonus.This is one of the last of the "old school" fighting games that doesn't have very much of an auto combo system, and has no easy inputs, even as an option. Characters have quarter circle, half circle, and dragon punch inputs, as well as single and double "full circles" for grapplers.This game is actively being developed post-release, and already has a cast of characters coming as DLC. It's not a Discord fighter, and ranked matches can be found at all skill levels at regular playing hours, at least in NA.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: This review was written (as positive) when the game launched with very, very broken functionality. The game is now completely playable online, with crashes being far less common. Can 100% recommend this now to anyone who's a fan of the genre.UNDER NIGHT IN-BIRTH II Sys:Celes is potentially the only mainstream 2D fighter that has been able to check every box on gameplay. Featuring a diverse cast with multiple different playstyles, and system mechanics that become more useful as you grow as a player, there is an insane amount of depth to the time you will spend playing this game and learning how to improve. Boasting a roster of 24 characters (with 3 more to be released as DLC over the next year and a half), there is bound to be a character for everyone to stick to.Now, let's get to the stuff that you fighting game players may want to know about, gameplay and mechanics. UNDER NIGHT IN-BIRTH II Sys:Celes (herein referred to as UNI2), while an anime / airdasher style fighter, is more ground-based akin to Street Fighter or King of Fighters. However, do not mistake the idea of a ground-based fighter with simplicity or slow gameplay. While you are lacking in traditional movement options (no double jumps, no super jumps, no airdashes), you have intense, fast-paced offense. Notably, UNI2 has Melty Blood's Reverse Beat mechanic. For those who don't know, Reverse Beat is a mechanic that allows you to, once per string, gatling (normal-to-normal cancel) backward, from heavies to lights. With a wide variety of normals and specials to mix throughout, offense is fast paced, yet far from shallow. You will be relying a lot on conditioning your opponent, and the way you open people up will depend on your play style and your attitude. Special moves are closer to something like Melty Blood (or Street Fighter) than they are Guilty Gear. Rather than a special being tied to a single input, or maybe two, a special is usually tied to the motion itself, giving you three* different variations of each special. A light version, a heavy version, and a metered or EX version. (* Some specials do not follow this rule exactly). Due to a focus on these EX specials, meter is not always saved for a super kill, but also used for defensive options, utility, and taking your turn back. Paired with the pace you gain meter, UNI2 is a game that forces you to be quick on your toes with resources, regardless of your character.Now, what makes UNI2 especially different from other fighting games? The GRD gauge. I'm mostly going to cut through the excess explanation with the expectation that if you're reading this far, you've played a good bit of fighting games and have a bit of know-how. The GRD gauge is a shared meter (segmented into 12 blocks, 6 on each side) between both the players that is influenced by every action you take. How you move, how you defend, how you press forward, the way you play shifts the gauge in or out of your favor. Think how Negative Penalty in GG punishes you for running away for too long, except its all measured, and there's equal rewards for successful risk taking, good decision-making, etc. Where does this lead? Why does it matter? There is a clock attached to the GRD gauge. Every approximately 16 seconds, the player with more of the gauge filled up wins the "cycle" and gains a buff known as GRD Vorpal (or simply "Vorpal"). Vorpal gives your character a buff to one of their unique traits, a 10% damage increase, and access to Chain Shift, a move that can cancel what you are doing, pause the screen and convert your GRD into meter. You cannot simply win the GRD cycle by winning neutral. You don't always win one by winning the other. GRD is crucial to mastering the game, being able to plan your actions to not only win the battle on the screen, but to win the cycle of the ongoing second battle in the meter, is a skill that many high-level players continue to hone even now.Past the gameplay, You get 40 colors, and 5 semi-customizable color slots for each character, online offers ranked and casual matchmaking, on top of simple player lobbies. UNI2 has implemented rollback netcode, allowing more stable connections from your region to people on the other end of the continent, if not beyond. (Your mileage may vary, depending on your location, connection, etc. Furthermore, read the beginning of the review.) Past that, the game has the widely desired Replay Takeover mechanic, allowing you to go back and play out certain situations from your matches over again to solve your problems in precise detail. And for the situations where you require maybe a bit less precision, the game still has a phenomenal training mode for you to practice combos, situations and setups.Now, I may be biased, I have been playing since early into UNDER NIGHT IN-BIRTH Exe:Late[cl-r] (the prior entry's) lifespan, and this is, or rather was my most anticipated game to release since before it was even announced. But regardless, if you've read this far, I'd say give the game an honest shot. Of course, it has flaws. The game is evidently rushed in a lot of spots, the PC port was released in poor condition thanks to Arc System Works' poor handling of publishing, and the regional pricing is so horrid that players in places like South America simply can't afford to get the game at launch price. Even so, this is one of the smoothest, cleanest, and most fun fighting game I have played in my entire time pressing buttons and landing combos.Would I recommend UNDER NIGHT IN-BIRTH II Sys:Celes? If you love fighting games, yes. If you're disappointed by the state of the current leading games in 2D fighters, yes. If you want a game that provides much to explore, a game that is still very unsolved, and a game that will continue to develop for a while, UNI2 is the game you are looking for. (P.S.  This is my first time writing an honest review. I've left comments open, so if I've made any mistakes or gotten anything wrong, let me know.)

_childDocuments_.review: UNDER NIGHT IN-BIRTH is back yet again. This time though, we went from changing the game’s subtitle to slapping a 2 on the name. And yeah, it’s still just as fun, and.. well, difficult.UNDER NIGHT IN-BIRTH is basically an anime fighter along the same vein as Guilty Gear or BlazBlue. I would say it’s more difficult than Strive, but maybe on par with BlazBlue. I don’t know - that’s all subjective anyways. That said, I liked the past two entries in this series and yeah, I like this one too, but it’s not without its issues.Starting with the good though: The movement. This is probably my favorite thing about the game. It just, flows so well, if that makes sense. You have so many options to dash, jump, and move around the screen that once you get the hang of things, it is a very fast-paced and satisfying experience. That and the characters themselves are pretty solid, for the most part. Plenty of variety there - grapplers, zoners, rushdowns, all of that - and I always like a good fighting game where more than a handful of characters click with me. That said, Merkava is still my favorite. He’s just so noodly and fun to play.The game also does a really good job with its tutorial system. There are over 100 different tutorials, each with demo videos and a walkthrough to help you through them. And then on top of that there are character combo guides and general strategy guides for each and every character. It goes to great lengths to get you into the experience, which is definitely warranted given just how hard a fighting game this is.If you’re looking to hop into the game and don’t already have friends to play it with - you’ll be subjected to the game’s online mode. On one hand, there’s actually rollback netcode which is super nice for a niche 2D fighter like this, but on the other, there are not that many active players just hanging out in the game’s online lobbies and when you do find a match, it’s likely going to be someone way higher rank than you. People call this series a Discord fighter - meaning you have to hop on servers dedicated to the game to find matches - and that still holds true with this sequel - even if the online playerbase is double that of the last game, averaging around 200 online at any one time.I spent some time in singleplayer, but honestly, those modes just aren’t that great. The arcade mode is pretty standard, but comes with a boring storyline and the time attack and score attacks are just vaguely different ways to play the arcade mode basically. Multiplayer is pretty much a necessity for this one and the most fun I had was duking it out with friends locally - and this is definitely one I’ll be keeping installed for that very reason.I’m still not a fan of how tight diagonal inputs are, it just doesn’t feel right to me, but pretty much everything else is solid. The art is just as great as its always been, the music is excellent, the stages are cool and really just remind me of the Fate series, and the level of polish on top of it all is really impressive given the size of its developer.UNDER NIGHT IN-BIRTH II Sys:Celes is worth a recommendation, but maybe not for the general audience. If you’re not already into fighting games, definitely pass on it, and if you’re not specifically into 2D anime fighters, then probably pass on it too. It’s got quite the learning curve, but is fun to play with friends and the addition of rollback netcode actually makes the game playable online too - even if the playerbase is small. The PC port apparently had issues on launch, but playing a couple months later, I can’t say I had any issues, so there’s that too.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

That means that I can't change my control type to circumvent the problem, and I have to restart my PC, which is a massive inconvenience. Having to restart my PC every time I run into this bug, which happens randomly and has yet to be fixed, is a pain in the ass. This should be fixed by now, 5 months after the game released on PC, but it's still not been fixed and I don't know why.Until it's fixed, this review is going to stay negative. I'm enjoying this game a lot, it's fun, satisfying and action packed, but this singular bug actively hampers my personal experience, which I can only fix through a ridiculous workaround.Please fix this bug.

_childDocuments_.review: The initial PC port issues aside (rolling back to the desktop and the like), there are technical issues that hamper the PC version that allegedly don't exist on the console one.  There are also problems with one-sided rollback, which seems to impact the person with the better connection/PC. Another easy to overlook problem is poor Steam integration: out of a casual/ranked match, there's no way to open a user's Steam page to add them as a friend. You'll have to search for them in the Steam client or find them in the rankings list. Oddly, player rooms and the rankings list do have Steam integration. I would expect consistency throughout but that is not the case.That said, I think the technical issues kind of pale in comparison to the other large issue, which is the small player base. Only a month into the game, the Steam version of the game is already down to less than 500 players per 24 hours, per SteamDB. The initial poor release really hamstrung the game in this regard. The end result is that the players who remain skew to being far more skilled than otherwise. If someone has very little experience in fighting games already, I'd probably recommend trying a different one first. This won't be an enjoyable experience. If one does have experience in fighting games, preferably anime fighters, it's definitely possible to get into the game, but it's going to be an uphill battle. I will note, however, that the players that are around are largely wonderful: this easily has one of the best communities, period. People are kind, supportive, and there are extremely skilled players who are more than happy to offer advice.I don't know what the future of this game will bring. It's possible that Evo will be the good press the game needs and will bring in some newer players. It's possible the weird issues with the PC port will be fixed eventually. As of now, though, unless you're someone very dedicated, I would recommend passing. If things get better, I'll plan on updating this review. I really, truly hope that they do.For what it's worth, as frustrating as the experience may be at times, I haven't given up on the game yet.EDIT 1: Okay, the latest update seems to have helped quite a bit with the input reader. I still don't think it's as good as PS, but it's definitely better than it was before. I really wish there was a "neutral" review instead of thumbs up or thumbs down at this point. I think it's worth reiterating the community side of things as well: if you have locals near you, I'd definitely give a thumbs up for the game.EDIT 2: I've started having a lot of fun with the game, finally. It took a while to click. I think I'll recommend it, but with a caveat:  That said, I think the game will probably get a few new players with Evo coming up and if you can pick it up on sale, I think it's a solid recommend. At full price, it's fine if it's a game that you really want to play, but otherwise, I'd recommend waiting for a discount. Hopefully things continue improving over time with the game and I can get to a point where I don't have any caveats or technical complaints!

_childDocuments_.review: if you like 2D fighting games, especially older ones, then you're likely to enjoy Under Night. It looks like an anime fighter, and it largely is, but doesn't have some of the genre's more egregious design habits, due to its more grounded focus. The GRD system adds a layer of complex decision making on top of almost every interaction, rewarding players with good reads on their opponents habits while on offense and defense.Characters are strong, diverse, dripping with personality, and are all viable. Almost every common archetype is represented in UNI's roster, with more to come in the season pass.The online part of this game was rocky at launch, but has since been fixed and works fine without issue. The rollback works very well, I've played matches from West to East Coast USA with only 1 frame of delay and no noticeable rollbacks. Speaking of delay, the game allows you to customize your input delay online, allowing players to customize what they'd rather deal with; more delay, or more visual rollbacks. All in all, UNI is a great series, and UNI2 is a great game. I started playing in uni1st, all through clr and now into uni2. It's the only other fighting game i've enjoyed since BBCF back in 2015, it feels untouched by some of the more modern and frustrating design decisions made by SFV, SF6, and GGST.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that the online functionality is working, I can confidently recommend giving the game a try. This means that I'm uncertain if anything is even canon at this point, as I've been assuming that Chronicle was the canon story, and that Arcade is a lot of what-if stories. After waiting for the story to update after a decade, it was one of the things I was legitimately looking forward to.I also have a mild frustration that this game still has no English subtitles. With the devs adding vastly more character voice interactions, I would love to know what they're actually saying.These issues are unlikely to make people not try the game entirely, as most people ONLY play online, but I wanted to give a warning to those who feel similarly.The gameplay *is* very fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by far my favorite game and it has so many good things going for it, however like any fighting game it is super hard to get into if you are not experienced with fighters, but the game offsets this with the best tutorial and combo trials I have ever seen.The tutorial teaches you the full game and about fighting games in general which is fantastic, the combo trials show off the characters and walks you into the character and ranks up the combos like most games typically do, but the Advanced and Expert level combos are genuinely super good and let you play the game just fine learning one of those to use as a BnB.The training mode also has tons of tools you can use for learning the game and the character you play and if you just spend some time labbing it will help you become a far better player.Outside of all the great learning tools the game offers for new and older players, the actual game is fantastic with a large variety of fun and unique characters and the game play is super on point, playing this game you will come to understand that there is a lot of long ranged attacks, the game is pretty grounded, and that the inputs are pretty simple, but this is just a trap. The skill floor is low to start playing right away with friends, but the skill ceiling gets very high very fast as you come to learn that there is so much going on in the game and the mechanics run deep.I highly recommend this game more as its amazing and if you want to use  to learn about the mechanics first I do recommend that, but the lab, trials, and tutorial are so good you can play without a wiki, which to me is mind blowing.When I first bought this game, I refunded it since my monitor was 1920 x 1200 which they did not support, the game looked super blurry and the black bars bugged me. The day just after I refunded it I bought it again since the game was way too good to just give up over something like that, it also I helped I changed monitors later anyways too.Biggest issue I have with this game now though is at launch the PC port was horrible, and Akatsuki does not say CHESTO loud enough, they fixed the PC port issue but still have not fixed making Akatsuki say CHESTO as loud as he can.

_childDocuments_.review: Please add Zohar to the game.This right now is the best current fighting game to exist. This game embodies what triple i gaming is to me.1- Independent2- Innovative3- InterestingThis game has all the fun fighting game single player modes that should come standard. Arcade, survival, time attack, and others.  The online is also great, as i experienced no lag.The loading times for fights are almost instant.The pixel art and music are amazing.The gameplay has the perfect speed for a 2d fighting game. The characters are unique and amazing. This game also takes "common" styles and adds more. One example would be a charge character that has a move from charging forward. This game has two sticks of butter to manage, and a middle gauge that players can use to add another layer for tug of war. If someone does not know what the middle gauge does, that is okay because it is just a reward for playing the game good. The middle gauge also slightly punishes what I call "turtle" styles.This game has unlockables, and other fun activities for replay ability. I have two cons for this game. 1st con- This is a very niche con for me in fighting games. I love it when a fighting game takes a risk and adds a minigame to the game. Some mini games are garbage, and some are fun. I will not mention in this review, which minigames were fun. But I would have loved to see them take a risk on a minigame. However, I understand this is a small team compared to other game companies. This is a nitpicking con.2nd con- The player base is small. However, there are solutions to fix this and I am not too proud to use them. But I have to be honest in my reviews. This is an issue that the developer has no control over. TLDR- This is a perfect 2d fighting game. It has beautiful pixel art and great music. The gameplay has the perfect sweet spot speed, and the load times are fast. This is a must have game for any gamers collection.

_childDocuments_.review: ayo they fixed netplayThis is what CLR should've been and I'm very surprised they fixed all the issues I had with that versiontl;dr it's much better than ST/CLR so whether you're new to the series or returning from those games you should get itFor newcomers: If you want to seriously get into anime fighters, this is THE game to start with, and with this version of the game I think it's also one well worth sticking with.For ST/CLR vets: Everything from the system mechanics to the character kits and overall balance feels much more dynamic. There are more ways to gain and lose GRD with the dodge, smart steer special, and many characters getting new FF moves. Celestial vorpal seemed like a meme at first but you're gonna be surprised how frequently it comes up in games where players know how to shield properly and tech throws, and when you combine this with VO being easier to use offensively and minimum damage on IW/IWEX being raised it creates situations where people will get blown tf up. And yet it doesn't feel cheap cause unlike a similar mechanic from blazblue called active flow, celestial vorpal doesn't feel completely random and getting it requires a lot of back and forth between players. Just like active flow it can be a comeback mechanic OR a snowball mechanic but the shifts in momentum feel earned. The new characters are cool (Kuon's flight mechanic is fun) and rest all got some cool new stuff. Many characters have a new FF move, some like Wagner even got two, some got new specials, etc. and they all contribute a meaningful piece in their characters' gameplans. From what I've played pretty much all the CLR routes still work but with the new moves and mechanics a lot of new routing potential has opened up, and experimenting with it is more fun than ever.If you give a ♥♥♥♥ about the story you're probably gonna be really disappointed, I definitely was, but that was always just a bonus and it doesn't really have any bearing on my enjoyment of the game cause it's really fun and for sure the best version of the game we've gottenUNI is back and it's really good this time

Very active on both defense and offense there's a lot of fun to be had on both sides if you can avoid raging. My biggest challenge to overcome in this game is being a pad player and learning to dash black constantly - there are MANY screen control characters in this game. Not quite zoners but they have so much range you have to learn to dash block a LOT. So if that sounds ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up to you, it is. But if you're willing to learn through it the game is very cool. My opinion on the Aesthetics: This is, IMO the biggest strength of the game. The soundtrack is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incredible. So many cool songs. The sprites are unbelievably sick for being 2D sprites like so expressive and stylish. Character designs are super cool and seem to have a longtime attachment to them from fans (this is my first uni)Overall: The game is hard. If you're a strive or sf6 player not at a super high level this game will be tough. I'd say it's similar in difficulty to Xrd or Blazblue. So it's doable you just have to put in work and be willing to get clapped for a while. 8/10 fighting game I recommend it

_childDocuments_.review: I had initially given a positive review of this game, when the online got fixed. However, I was a total beginner at the time, and by playing more I changed my mind. I just don't like this game that much and here are the reasons why. I must add that I played Blazblue quite a lot, and this game really looks like a Blazblue clone to me.- Either you don't have Blazblue Central Fiction (BBCF), and in that case, I recommend you buy that instead. You would think "UNI2 is new there are tons of noobs" and you would be mostly wrong. This game is full of veteran players who are at a large advantage because it's basically a rollback netcode update of the first game with a few new characters. You would also think "UNI2 is new so the player base is much bigger" and you would be mostly wrong, it's not even twice the current player base of BBCF. Worse than that, the room system is terrible, and the ranked and player matches do not allow to select opponents, so you are often stucked playing the same few people.- Or you have BBCF, and in that case, I stand by the opinion that every single aspect of UNI2 could be considered as "Blazblue, but worse". This game revolves entirely around the GRD system, which is a clock at the bottom of the screen, and by performing certain actions, you gain "vorpal state". Vorpal is basically overdrive + rapid cancel in Blazblue, mechanics which you can access all the time. All right, so what's wrong with this ? All the mechanics could be describe as "it's like in Blazblue, but you cannot do X in that situation". You cannot double jump, you cannot instant air dash, you cannot block in the air, if you tech in the air you can't do an air action, you have less defensive options, your moveset is half the size... You feel like you are in the same situations as in Blazblue, but you're just forced to take the mixups, and they aren't even original, because the characters just don't have moves to work with. The combos are very redundant as well. So on top of all this, you tell me you are constrained to choose certain options to win the GRD ? In the game which is a clone of another one with half the options of the game you cloned, I'm forced to choose depending on the clock ? In this game I just feel stuck playing the exact same situations over and over. Last detail, graphics are worse than in Blazblue, and I find the cast much more generic, but that's a matter of taste.Conclusion : my feeling is that if you're not coming from BBCF, go there, and if you are coming from BBCF, don't come.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be my favorite fighting game of all time. The system mechanics are daunting at first, but as you understand then GRD gauge and get used to how it works it's more than manageable. The characters are all well designed too, you're guaranteed to find at least one character you'll like. Something that I was unsure at first in this was the fact that most moves cannot be blocked in the air, if you're used to anime fighters like then this will be something of a hurdle at first. But over time I've grown to like it since it allows the game both fast and aggressive while also being slow and grounded, kind of like a Street Fighter anime fighter. The only I'll hold again the game right now is that is there is no crossplay with consoles. Hopefully French Bread adds this at some point, preferably soon, because the online can feel very barren at times. But regardless, the mechanics and character design of this game are a joy to play with and makes for some of the most fun I myself have ever had in a fighting game.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that they fixed the ranked and casual queues and the crashes (from my experience at least), the game is great. Probably has the most QoL features of any modern fighting game (resume from replay, launch the game into training mode or the online menu, queue in training, a very functional and smooth lobby system, choice of delay for rollback, having your stage and music online separate from your opponent, just off the top of my head). The rollback is good, even if it's not the best you can still play people from quite a distance without it falling apart. On top of all that, you have my personal favorite fighting game and one that deserves a lot of attention. The game manages to have very cool execution challenges without feeling obtuse or impossible through a huge number of different motion inputs, a unique feel due to being as fast as an anime game without many air options, extremely well thought out system mechanics that influence the game's strategy constantly without either causing aggression or defense to outright win, and all with a set of characters that maintain there individuality while being balanced.10/10, probably gonna be the only fighting game I play

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR. It’s an excellent game, but I’m a Mortal Kombat fan, and I don’t understand the appeal of this, so Under Night System Clear… sucks.Welcome back brawling game gurus, I’ve received a lot of fan requests to review this game that I want to get out of the way, so in this review, I’m reviewing Under Night System Clear.We’re busting this beat-em-up game wide open.Under Night System Clear is one of the most iconic entries of the Under Night franchise. It’s popular for having a clever roster of characters with their own special moves. However, if you’re looking for a good beat-em-up, then look elsewhere because this one deserves to be chucked into the nearest wood chipper. This one turned out to be just another run-of-the-mill rip-off of Mortal Kombat. Now before you send me your hate mail, listen to me for a while. I don’t really hate this game but, compared to Mortal Kombat, this one has the word ASS written all over it. Trust me, I’ve been playing beat-em-ups for well over 20 years, and I know all the ins and outs of it.When you start the game, the first thing you see is the Under Night System Clear title card, but when you start playing it comes the major downside of the game: This is just a boring brawling-type game where you punch a few times, and you win. There are no special moves, no combo moves, nothing. What a buzzkill. Is this supposed to be fun? Guys, if you’re going to copy the work of a literary genius like Mortal Kombat, at least keep the elements the same. Where is the blood? Where are the fatalities? Whatever happened to just picking up a controller and decapitating your foes, or exploding them in a gory fashion? *FACEPALM*And speaking of fatalities, what’s with the fighters in this game? There’s this pretty boy with a sword, this pretty girl with another sword, this other pretty girl with another sword… What the hell? Where’s the variety in this game? I thought this game was called Under Night System Clear, not Under SWORD System Clear. And look at this four-eyed dork with a book, gosh, even his moves look dorky. Go back to the library, you wimp. Well, at least we have Dr. Claw’s grandpa, this guy in a white tuxedo, and this little girl with giant metal arms. Hey, maybe she’s The Hulk’s little sister. *HULK SMASH* Take it easy, sweetheart.And you think that’s bad? (Yes, my humor is better than Family Guy) Take a look at this girl with two swords. This is another huge letdown. I mean, why is a little girl playing with oversized knives anyway? What a pixelated nightmare. And she’s accompanied by this bug creature that just floats there and does nothing to help. Can I do something? Can it attack? No! What a waste of pixels. It pisses me off so much that I’d like to throw it across the screen. *GET OVER HERE* After doing some research, I found out that this girl’s name is LYNE, but if you win, the bug creature does nothing, if you move it does nothing, if you’re hit it does nothing, if you attack it does nothing so, what’s the point? Didn’t they test this game before they released it to the public? This is so FUSTRATING and literally blows me up.And then we have characters you can’t do anything with, like this girl with a whip… A whip? I thought this game was about swords, this doesn’t make no sense whatsoever; I mean, are these characters really that much in-demand? Sorry, but I just can’t imagine a lot of players jumping at the chance of playing them. *DOUBLE FACEPALM*Ugh, somebody call 911, ‘cause I was PACHO’d. *This is where you laugh*Then there’s this dumb part where, if you pause the game, you can look at the character’s commands for their fighting attacks, but to hell with that. I mean, whoever reads these things anyway? I can’t waste my time reading about the characters’ moves, I just gotta play the game.And what’s with the character selection in this game? Why are there so many girls in this game? I don’t wanna play with girls. Gosh, this game sucks so hard that I wish a real fighter would appear and rip some guts around here. This is so FUSTRATING. Where are the badass military men? Where are the sub-zeros and scorpions and whatnot? Where are the Mortal Kombat barely dressed hot chicks? Time to montage this b!tch for two minutes with over dramatic music in the background. No way, this game still sucks.But the problems don’t end there because, after doing even more research, I found out that this is the sequel of another game called Under Late at Night but, if that’s the first game, I insist on playing that one first. I mean, what’s worse than having to play your games out of order? The very thought of doing such a thing is sickening, and I think it’s punishable by death in some countries. *TRIPLE FACEPALM?*Then there is the arcade mode, where you must beat up one bad guy per stage, and there are only 9 stages. What a bunch of ass-burgers with a side of fries. For crying out loud, would it have killed them to add some extra levels here? When I play a game I expect some side-scrolling action, and we’re not really doing anything besides fighting in this game. And the worst part is the ending, as the prize for beating the game is just a static image painted on the wall. A better prize would have been the chance to play as another character, like Goro, or Shang Tsung, because everybody knows all brawling-type games should be just like Mortal Kombat.Under Night System Clear is a perfect throwback and predecessor to the Under Night franchise and was made to compete with another title by the same company called “Guilty Gear 4: The Strike”, which was made months ago. So final verdict, it’s an excellent game, but I’m a Mortal Kombat fan, and I don’t understand the appeal of this. So, Under Night System Clear… is a piece of s#!t.Till next time, gamers. Game on. *TOASTY*

_childDocuments_.review: This game activates my combo neurons. I haven't run into many issues with the game. I ran into some roughness doing online sets with a friend but I don't trust either of our internet services to place that blame on the game. Others are reporting technical issues with the game's display settings and such as well as netplay problems. It seems that the devs are currently working to remedy these things.All that aside, Under Night is an excellent fighting game. It's fast enough to feel frantic but it's not full-on Marvel VS Capcom insano speed or anything like that. This game has some of the most wildly comprehensive tutorials I've ever seen. It starts from the ground up, teaching you not just what the goal of the game is and what the meters are, it teaches you fundamentals to the genre like frame advantage, block strings, spacing, punishing, you name it. If you put in the time even as a total newbie, this game can teach you how fighting games work. It's awesome. The game's kinda big unique mechanical feature is the GRD system that has you play a sort of meta-game tug-of-war where playing aggressively or successfully guessing your opponent's offense rewards you with extra damage and a powerful reset ability that gives you super meter. It's that extra layer that tugs on your decision making that can give you the slight edge you need in a fight once you get your legs under you and start interacting with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Netplay issues have been fixed, so I can feel good about actually recommending the PC port to people now. If it's not already obvious from the other recent reviews, the game launched with a glitchy port, but it's better now.Under night is one of the greatest fighting games of all time. For like 10 years, the only thing that's been holding it back has been the fact that each new version was technically just updates to an old game running on delay based netcode. Not only have they finally given under night the rollback that it deserves, but they've gone above and beyond by adding replay takeover (with an option to have the game automatically save every replay, in case you're like me and too stupid to remember to press "save replay" after games), ad hoc frame data in training mode (want to check how plus you are if you do assault slight delay j[C]? no problem), reaction tests to get used to teching gold throw on reaction, and like five other training mode options I can't remember right now. The tutorial for this game is also incredibly detailed and comprehensive, but it's been like that ever since uni[st]. Mission mode combos are (mostly) actually very good combos, as everyone's trials have been updated since uni[st] when the old combos were written.The three new characters are all very interesting, and all of the returning characters got new moves and buffs to keep them feeling fresh. Season 1 of DLC characters is free if you buy the game before March 31, because French Bread is the greatest fighting game dev of all time. Season 1 has large gaps between each character, which some people consider a downside, but I think is great because it guarantees the game will continue to receive support and updates.Literally the only thing I could want from this game that it doesn't have is crossplay, and the devs have stated that the only barrier to crossplay is money.Also nerf yuzu plz thanks

_childDocuments_.review: Not remotely a good sequel.Game mechanics changed the game from a methodical but tense back and forth of managing both resources and actively trying to win the game to all-ins nonstop for little punishment.The netcode doownright sucks. I can play street fighter 6 or guilty gear strive with people halfway across the world and ping upwards of 200 with no issues. In this game, the rollback starts becoming noticeable at 85, and by 120 it becomes unplayable, not to mention the sheer volume of poor connections you'll encounter online.There's next to nothing to do other than play online. All of the single player modes are the same thing repackaged as if they're different, but there's nothing making any of them worth touching.The tutorial is lacking. This franchise often gets praise for having a tutorial that shows the player optimal combo routes, but in terms of how to play neutral, how to escape certain blockstrings, etc? Nothing. You're completely on your own and you just have to pray your opponent shows you the same play twice if you want to try to figure out how to beat it. Overall, a complete waste of $50; as somebody who loved the previous iteration of this game, I can't believe I had to uninstall this one. I put in over 50 hours trying to FORCE myself to like this, but I just can't.

Every single design decision made in this game feels tailor made to make the game less fun and more of a pain to play. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The crash bug has been fixed! They're still fixing the the cross region problem.No news on the resolution and fullcreen problem yet though. Finally, the best version of Under Night so far as been released, because rollback has been added! After more than a decade of delay based netcode, the loyal fans of the game definitely deserve this version.I recommend this fighting game to both newer players and veterans in the genre, as there are lots of characters to choose from, each of them having set up a solid playstyle identity, no 2 characters are really the same, even the shotos in the game differ from each other thanks to the force function and vorpal trait system the game has in place which gives them different moves and special abilities/improved frame data depending on the character. Those are just 2 examples though, there are many more mechanics in this game that sets itself apart from other games. Speaking of mechanics, the GRD is one of a kind and rewards good defense by giving you offensive buffs after whats called  the vorpal cycle finishes, which kind of turns the game into a tug of war where each player is fighting each other but also keeping an eye on the gauge at the bottom, although nothing is also stopping you from completely ignoring this system at the start so even newbies dont have to worry about it. To add more to the game theres also the replay takeover which lets you take control of your character during a specific time in a replay, letting you test out what you could have alternatively done in that situation, a really handy tool for learning.Another positive in the game is the amazing soundtrack composed by Raito, each character's theme is a banger and definitely adds to the overall package of the game. Although I'm gonna miss the old character select theme, the new is also great especially when the guitar solo kicks in.Adding more to the positive in the game is its tutorial system. It's quite solid in my opinion and not only explains the mechanics and basics controls of a game that a complete newbie can understand, the mission modes also give optimal routes when youve finally reached the level where you want to learn combos to improve your play. This is coming from a Vatista player since  UNIST and I'm glad they added her optimal BnB combo from the previous titles to this game which makes for great practice, there's also the custom colours like in the old melty blood games which let you change the colours of every part of the character you play, this also affects the colours of the particle effects of the character itself so for example vatista's laser can be changed from blue to yellow if you really want to using custom colours, not just relying on the plethora of template they already have available.As for cons in the game, I would say that even though the game itself is welcoming to new player, it is still harder to pick up compared to other competing titles like the recently released granblue rising versus, which I also play. This might put off some people off the game but I assure you, the mechanics of this game really make it worthwhile and fun to play, especially when things start to click, its why I recommend it whether you are new or veteran to fighting games. :)

_childDocuments_.review: another great game from French Bread. UNI2 have interesting mechanics and something very unique that you don't see on any other fighting game: the Grind Grid (GRD) which allows you to be in Vorpal state, this was present on previous games as well, but got some small changes on this one as well some new mechanics added too. The characters have good design and they all play different, each of them having a large toolset for you to learn, and the roster keeps increasing. It have a good ammount of single player content as well, each character have their own story on the arcade route, giving you an unique art to unlock at the end, an extensive training mode with different tools for you to work on your practice. It also allows you to watch replays and take control, with that you can learn what you could have done in certain situation, and also a mode where you can learn a big ammount of combos for every character. The tutorial inside the game teachs you all the basics and advanced stuff, so it's a good place to actually learn some things if you're still confused about it. The other modes are just extras but you can have a separate progress for each character for time attack, score attack and survival. The online mode have a decent connection thanks to rollback, allowing you to play even with people from other countries.UNI2 is a very fun fighting game, with a beautiful pixel art on the character's sprites, it have everything from the previous games plus some new stuff, very good music and learning new combos with each character is rewarding and satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that the port is actually playable, this game is really great. It's just a perfected version of an already great fighting game. This game feels like the perfect panacea to the issues I have with modern fighting games, as it still rewards honing your execution, has a balanced approach to defense and offense in its mechanics, has a fun neutral game, and the characters are diverse and interesting in a very fun way. The best part is that they achieved this by not fixing what ain't broken. Sys:Celes doesn't really have any huge game-changing additions to the Under Night In-Birth's mechanics. It just further refines what made previous versions of the game already good. The more balanced approach to pacing of a match feels so much better than the heavy handed emphasis on aggression seen in other recent fighting games like Street Fighter 6 and Tekken 8 (I swear, drive and heat are literally the same mechanic), an emphasis that makes the games kinda boring as offense is so free and easy due to the reduced emphasis on executional skill. If you're like me, someone who likes fighting games but doesn't like the direction that modern fighting games are going, pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that my locals offer this game, I decided to pick it up and it's a surprisingly good pick for a lot of fighting game enjoyers looking for another game to try. Most characters don't make a strong first impression compared to some games but each have something fun to contribute to the game from their kit or just seeing them in motion. The single player is standard, the online currently runs great although I heard matchmaking is quiet, and the game itself has a wealth of resources built in that are above and beyond to help you learn and improve if it suits you. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: online works now, many new and cool changes compared to previous installments. Glory to the French Bread team.To address the immediate issue: yes, the game launched in a very poor state, at least online-wise. But now online is (mostly) fixed and you can get ranked/casual/private matches. If you're getting timeouts while doing quick match search (ranked/casual), try switching to custom search. This gives you a list of other players in the queue, and in my experience I can match with them fine. Rollback is smooth though there are some issues still (this issue has been fixed as of Feb 5).Regarding the game itself, as a fighting game newbie (roughly 1 year experience) I can say that this game is on the harder side of things, and some characters will require more effort to even grasp the basics for, as they incorporate some intermediate/advanced level stuff like negative edge, delayed rekkas, etc. However, there are some things that in my opinion has made this game a lot better than its predecessor in terms of newbie experience. Firstly, there's an autocombo system, which, while limited, always ends on a safe ender. Next, tutorials are even more robust in terms of teaching you the game's systems, including the unique GRD gauge that you might have heard of. Each character's combo trials also includr general strategies to help you get started with a character, including simple and safe blockstrings, anti-air attacks, key moves, etc. These were also in the previous edition but now they're moved up. Finally, features like replay takeover and frame data make it much more convenient to learn, revisit your matches and try to find out how you can get out of that pressure or block that wack mixup. Character-wise there's a wide range of play styles to choose from. As a newbie I recommend characters like Hyde, Nanase and Tsurugi, who have decent range and relatively simple combo structure to get started.Get this game if you liked its predecessors or you want to try an anime-style fighting game with cool mechanics and relatively more grounded neutral.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to preface this by saying that I absolutely love the Under Night In-Birth series, Uniclr was the game that really made me fall in love with the fighting game genre. If you're a newcomer to fighting games, particularly anime fighting games, I truly believe this to be an amazing starting point for you; there's an in-depth tutorial feature, and you're primarily only using three buttons to attack (with the fourth mostly being reserved for special actions), making combo structures noticeably easier to grasp if you've struggled with other anime FGs like blazblue or p4a. Not to mention, the mechanics that make this game unique have enough depth to keep veterans entertained, while also being simple enough for newcomers not to feel too overwhelmed. I genuinely believed that all Uniclr needed in order to become a (practically) perfect game was rollback netcode, and Unisc (or Uni2 if you prefer to abbreviate it that way) got that and more. All that said, the launch and (as of the time of writing this) current state of online has left a lot to be desired. You couldn't even queue for matches without the game crashing on steam launch, you had to create a Player Match room with a *unique* keyword. Emphasis on "unique" because if your room shared a keyword with another room, the same crash error would occur to anyone trying to join your room. And while that has been fixed, the game still crashes somewhat frequently, and I've had private lobbies break several times per session due to timeout errors. There's also still the issue where ping is displayed incorrectly, making it hard to guage how high you should set your input delay to avoid rollback frames, and making it just as hard to tell if the occasional lag spikes are because we didn't set input delay high enough, there's still a few kinks in the netcode to work out, or some third factor we haven't deduced. While French-Bread *does* have my full confidence that these problems will be (mostly) fixed eventually, most of these problems could've been solved with a PC beta. I would still recommend getting this game on pc, especially if that's the platform most of your friends are playing on; it's an incredibly fun game when it *does* run smoothly, just be prepared for semi-frequent hiccups. That or give it a few weeks, and most of the bugs will probably be fixed

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most fluid and fun fighting systems in games in my opinion. Anyone can pick it up and start mashing buttons and see something cool. Over time you will learn fun new combo routes as this is one of those fighting games that embrace self expression in your combo chains and move sets. As you get to know your character it just all feels intuitive and fun. It is mu favorite fighting game franchise period. They are having some difficulties at launch, be patient the Devs will figure it out. The graphics are stunning in my opinion. Top level animation of 2D sprites, hand drawn and gorgeous. Original character designs that cause each character to feel and look unique and interesting.The music is some of the best I've ever heard in a fighting game. As soon as I hear it I get psyched. I've heard a lot of content creators use the music in the background on videos that are not even fighting game related. They are catchy, melancholy, melodic and overall great jams. ...and no lyrics to get bored/annoyed by after the 200th time of hearing them. Sorry Daisuke.If you like beautiful art, fun mechanics and games that just feel good to play. Pick it up. The current problems will be worked out.

name: Tavern Talk
detailed_description: Kickstarter Info & Dev Roadmap About the Game You Walk into A Tavern… …and get to work! You are the owner of the Wayfarer’s Inn, a popular watering hole in the fantasy land of Asteria. But you’re no ordinary barkeep. Be it a potion of seething fury or prancing swords, the drinks you serve can change your customer’s destiny forever. You can also turn the rumours you hear at work into intrepid quests for your patrons! Befriend a colourful cast of adventurers as they brag about their latest triumph – or commiserate an utter failure. Whether it’s relaxation or a fresh thrill, you’re on hand to give each patron what they need. Beyond the walls of this cosy tavern, a world-threatening danger is brewing. Every quest, rumour and conversation is intertwined with the ultimate fate of the land. You will... Find Your Family The Wayfarer's Inn is a safe haven to a colourful cast of characters inspired by TTRPGs. Get to know their unique personalities, and help them find a place that feels like home. Brew Up A Storm Serve an ever-growing menu of magical drinks to your patrons, but choose carefully, as your choice will alter their fates. Whip Up Some Quests Gather rumours from the tavern-goers and use them to create quests for your adventurous guests. Connect the Dots Piece together the fragments in your little study and uncover the secrets of an ancient evil threatening the land. Cherish the Space As adventurers return from their mighty quests, they’ll bring back trinkets you can use to decorate your tavern. Your choices shape the snug interior of the Wayfarer’s Inn! Page localized by LocQuest Content Warning Like in every good Pen & Paper campaign, Tavern Talk touches topics that may hit right in the feels. Please be aware that there will be mentions of death, grief and violence.

short_description: A cozy visual novel about running a tavern in a D&D-inspired fantasy! Gather rumors, serve magical drinks, and meet adventurers on a life-changing quest.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Get it if you enjoy fantasy stories and reading. Don't get it if you're looking for creative fun creating and making drinks - if that's you, get Coffee Talk instead.I really enjoyed Coffee Talk and was excited to see this new game, but in my opinion Coffee Talk is better than Tavern Talk. The main reason is that in Coffee Talk you could use your creativity to create drinks and have fun discovering new ones. In Tavern Talk you can't. You have to follow the recipe and if you don't you just get an error. You can't create drinks outside of the story either.And while the quest system is fun, you can't be eagle-eyed and jump in to create a new quest once you have enough rumours, you have to wait until the story tells you too. This game has almost no creativity options for players. The only thing you can really do is to pick between two options on occasion to choose one story path over another.I do enjoy this game, I love the artwork and find the characters interesting, but I really wish I could have more input and creativity than offered. It holds your hand tightly and is largely just reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay, I'd like to give it a Meh, but it's on the low side of 5 out of 10.I was hoping for something a bit more like VA11-Hall-A, but there's not as much game here.The presentation is very nice, though some more voice acting wouldn't have gone amiss. Unfortunately the two gameplay elements (excluding the multiple choice moments) aren't failable, and can't really be played with.You can mix drinks to a recipe, but you can't make them up or have "Fun" with your patrons by screwing with them. I've been serving everyone, the same drink, regardless of what they ask for (when it doesn't change the plot, you're allowed to mix the wrong drink) and no one cares. They just say "You got it wrong, but whatever." I've been feeding the vampire sunjuice and fire chillies and he doesn't care. Come on, would a gag line be so much to ask for?You can also put together quests by assembling clues, except the clues are all colour coded so you don't have to do any deciphering, and if you try to muck them up the game says no until you get it right.But the real problem with the game is the writing. It's not awful, just overly verbose. It goes on, and on, and on, and you quickly end up wishing people would just get to the point instead of being "Quirky". It also doesn't help that they keep making references to DnD related pop-culture, it gets very tiresome to talk to someone who is just a meme fountain, constantly screaming at you "This is a game! I am an NPC!". And it's not a dialogue system, it's a monologue generator, you sit there, clicking, waiting for the scene to finish so the next collection of unfunny TTRPG references can walk in.Because the game doesn't care about the player decisions, what drinks you make or dialogue you pick, immediately closing all branches after they open, it just feels disrespectful to your time. Why bother to ask to pick from two dialogue options, if you're going to ignore it? Why bother getting the player to mix drinks, if your mistakes mean the same as your successes? I lost all interest in the story, which seemed to be going somewhere good, because I realised I was not playing a game, I was clicking through a very user unfriendly book.Overall, not much of a game, which is a shame, because there are examples of this exact premise done very well. If the Devs just wanted to make a kinetic novel, then they should have, the fake gameplay elements just slow the whole experience to a crawl.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: "Tavern Talk" is all about the conversations you have with your patrons. Like in the "Coffee Talk" series, you spend a lot of time chatting with different characters, each with their own stories and secrets. Your dialogue choices matter and will shape the direction of the story and your relationships with the patrons. Serving magical drinks adds a fun twist, as the right concoction can influence your patrons' moods and unlock new dialogue options.Gathering rumors is also key. By listening to the gossip and stories shared by your patrons, you can gather valuable information that might help adventurers on their quests. This adds a layer of strategy, as you decide which rumors to follow up on and how to use them to help your customers.: The sound design in "Tavern Talk" perfectly complements its cozy vibe. The soundtrack features soothing, melodic tunes that create a relaxing atmosphere. Ambient sounds like the chatter of patrons and the clinking of glasses help bring the tavern to life. Occasionally, you'll hear some voice acting, which adds an extra layer of immersion and helps to make the characters feel more real.^ Rating: 9/10"Tavern Talk" is a heartwarming and engaging experience that combines great storytelling with the cozy charm of managing a fantasy tavern. It's a must-play for fans of visual novels and D&D-inspired adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: The art is gorgeous and the character design is 11/10! However, the game doesn't allow you to make mistakes or be very creative at all. The drink making is fun at first, but gets boring after the same character asks for the same drink for the 7th time in a row, and you don't even get to choose what to make (the Innkeeper tells you when you've chosen the wrong drink, even if it meets the customers expectations). The most fun I have playing is deciding which drinks to make for quests, but that doesn't happen very often. The characters are fun, but a lot of times it feels like they've just come from a therapy session. On top of that, it feels like I'm overhearing other people's conversations. You don't get to choose your name (at least not as far as I've seen), you can choose your pronouns, but it doesn't really work if you choose they/them. You don't get to decide your relationship with other characters. Overall, you don't get a ton of agency or choice, despite the marketing.I'm sure this would be great for a younger audience that would rather read a cool story than make a ton of decisions, but it just doesn't do it for me as an adult.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a recommended because I think it would be a good game for players who want a cozy visual novel.  However, this isn't the right type of game for me.I love the concept of being a player character for a D&D innkeeper hearing rumors and giving quests, a role usually relegated to an npc.  I'd still love to see a game like that.Tavern Talk is click through reading with a minor diversion to mix a drink.  There isn't much more than that.  There's no economy.  I don't get paid for mixing drinks, and I don't need to order ingredients.  If I mix a wrong drink for a customer and throw it away, there's no penalty for wasted ingredients.The reason why I am giving this a recommended is because this could be the right type of game if you're just looking for a light, uncomplicated visual novel for Sunday afternoon reading.  The art style is lovely.  The characters are charming and have their quirks (I love Kyle, the neurotic yet charismatic vampire).  The characters pick up the quests from the board, ask for advice on which way they should approach the quest, go away for several days, then come back and tell you how it went.  Supposedly there is a consequence system if you give advice that is wrong for the quest, but I did not play this long enough to explore that.  If you grow attached to the characters, then this could give an emotional dimension to the game.I imagined being a player character for a D&D innkeeper would involve budgeting, pricing for the drinks, paying rent to the king, and a transactional component to doing the quests.  Like a quest giver would pay x amount for the job to get done, and the innkeeper takes a cut on completion.  Tavern Talk isn't that type of game, so this review is to help set what to expect.  If you like a click through novel from the point of view from a high fantasy innkeeper, then you might enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: *The small text issue mostly has been fixed in the recent patch. 32h (48/49 achievement, finished the game) 21.7h No. Yes (~29 achievements). No. is a visual novel set in a fantasy setting where you run a tavern, serving your customers drinks, listening to their stories, and sending them on a quest. It plays out just like  () and  () where you stand behind the counter and focus on mixing drinks and reading the dialogues.- Multiple endings, both for the story and the quests- Fast-forward button to skip already-read dialogues- Most text can be too small in Steam Deck- Making drinks can feel repetitive and boring: AMD Zen 2 4c/8t 2.4-3.5GHz, 16 GB RAM, 8 AMD RDNA 2 CUs is depicted in 2D visuals. The game tries to make characters look alive by giving them animations, though they are looped, leading to quick repetition. However, they still look stiff to me, as sometimes their expression might not match with the dialogue.As someone who likes fantasy settings, I enjoyed the story. The dialogues mostly revolve around the main plot and journey that the patrons experienced—their adventures, their worries, and their relationship with the other patrons. Quests will also change the outcome of these adventures, which will be determined by your decision prior to their departure.I liked to see how the characters had grown. The game might not make it subtle—it might look too obvious, but it's nice to see how they are striving towards the better person in the end. Strangers turn to friends, people fighting through their worries—things like that.On the negative side, the dialogue can be too boring sometimes. Some conversations are made in metaphors to make them look pretty, and you might not even understand what they mean, sometimes because they talk in a lingo that is exclusive to their world. This might also be caused by the fact that the game doesn't explain the worldbuilding well, though. Luckily, you can just skim over these parts and still understand the story.I like how your actions can influence the ending, especially the quests, but it seems that the result was too predictable and naive. The game seems to paint most quests in black and white, picturing the world to always work in your favor if you always try to understand the other side. Sometimes, this might even result in the story coming off as weird. I wish it would also showcase the dangerous side even if you try to be kind, making the quests to be harder to predict.The ending feels weak. Despite being the finale, what happened during the final act was treated just like another day in the tavern, just like how you solve the earlier quests. It might be because you are not the one doing the actual job, but I wish the conclusion was more impactful to the main character.You can categorize  as a visual novel with a little bit of mixing drinks gameplay: you'll listen to your customers' stories and give them drinks when they ask for them. That being said, I found the same characters to be asking for the same type of drinks most of the time, with only a difference in the wording.There are different types of drinks with different stat distribution, but the patrons seem not to care about that. The game makes it simpler to know what the customer wants by providing a note with the stat that they need, and that's all you need to know about. Giving drink A or B won't matter as long as it gives the same stat, which makes the drink variation itself useless. You can just introduce one type of drink in each stat and it won't make any difference.And then there is the infusion mechanic. It allows you to imbue a drink with skills and increase its stats. It can help to force you to choose which drink to aim for, especially since it will decrease other stat, which might make it impossible to make certain drinks. However, the infusions will only be requested during quests—you can add them to non-quest drinks, but there won't be any differences to the story.Speaking of quest drinks, yes, your choice matters. Through drinks. During quests, you'll be given two drink options to serve to your customer. The drink that you give will change the quest outcome. It won't be hard to make the drink that you need—you just need to look at the book for the infusion and stat distribution thoroughly.I finished the game in 21.7h. The rest of my playtime is to sweep the rest of the achievements. The game has four endings which are dependent on the quest results. It can be exhausting to get them all, especially since you need to redo the game from the beginning to reach them. Moreover, there aren’t many dialogues that were covered in the ending and you'll be wasting a lot of time just to read those dialogues.The game isn't difficult at all—you can even make drinks that the customer doesn't want and they'll still accept it. There is no currency or whatsoever that can make you fail the game early. Heck, even the ending doesn't rely on your drink-mixing skills.Some texts, especially the ones in the book, are too small in . Sure, you can adjust the font size in the settings, but that only works for the dialogue.There is also no option to skip the delay when the characters are speaking with punctuation. I set the dialogue speed to be the fastest, but it's still useless if I had to wait for the delay because the character was speaking with commas or dots.The game might not have the best dialogues, but  is still a good read for those who like to read fantasy stories. You'll listen to adventurer stories and get along with them—it's as if you are playing an RPG game, but you are not playing as the hero who saves the world. If you like a cozy story in a fantasy setting, you'll like this game, although I'd prefer to recommend buying it at a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I somehow didn't realize this was a visual novel when I kickstarted it, so this is from the point of view of someone who does not normally play visual novels. I played it enough to get all 4ish endings and all achievements. It takes around 22 hours to do a single playthrough for good/middle route. Less for the bad endings b/c you only get about half the story.Gameplay-wise, there's really just making drinks and building quests, but I feel like it doesn't happen frequently enough to actually be annoying, it's really focused more on the story. For drinks, there are recipes with set amounts of stats that you add with potions and/or infusions. For non-important choices, you can get the drinks wrong with no effect other than the person being a little annoyed. For important choices that change the story, you MUST give them one of the two options provided, it won't let you give them something wrong. I did not realize the first couple drinks that I made that you can open your recipe book and they actually show you what the person wanted--you don't have to guess based on the keywords that were bolded in their ask.You also have to build quests by sorting through sticky notes and selecting the three that go together. The first time I played, all the 3 matching would always match in color and design so it was really easy if you couldn't remember exactly what goes with what. They updated that part so the color/designs don't match anyway and instead added a hint button that you can use after failing once. I do not like that. If you're playing through just to experience the other parts of the story or get the achievements, I wish you could just turn on/off the matching designs. The writing is where this game shines and why I bothered to play it for all the endings when I don't really enjoy visual novels. It is a fantasy setting with DnD elements shining through in character races/types, the stat types, as well as the described fighting seeming to be similar. So many emotional moments leading up to all endings, though so much more for the non-bad endings. Some good LGBTQ+ representation with different characters (front-and-center, it's not a side thing you can just dismiss!!!!) and also your own pronoun choice. There is one quest that can result something real heavy that can happen in all playthoughs, and there is also the anxiety of not knowing the fate of some characters for a while, but most of the emotionally charged story is going to come in the middle/good endings where you get like 40% more of the story. I highly recommend watching the little scene changes during the credits b/c it conveys more story for each ending and it can still be pretty emotional. My first playthrough had me in tears on multiple occasions and actually worried about the fate of some of the characters at some parts. It ended in the middle ending. I thought it seemed like a good ending, but I learned from taking a look at the achievements that it was NOT the good ending and was determined to see both the good and bad after that, despite the long play time. The ending credits are a little bittersweet for the middle ending, with some sadness as well as some joy.Bad ending was next b/c I made a bad choice in my first quest drink. I played the bad ending as being the biggest jerk I could be the entire time and people were usually mad at me or annoyed at my responses. There are technically two bad endings achievement-wise, but there is a single dialog choice that determines which of the bad you get, so it only takes one save scum and you can get both bad ending achievements. Watching the bad ending credits scenes also brought me to tears. just to see the characters reactions as they go on as well as how some unknown things are handled. My last playthrough I did the "good" ending. There is only one major difference between the good and the middle, although it is a pretty emotional one. I was in happy tears when I got to the difference, but it would be a little heartbreaking if you do them the other way around. It was heartbreaking the first playthrough, but to know what happens in the good ending and then experience the middle ending, it would have hurt  so much worse. I think I would have been completely shocked if I had done it that way. The ending credits here are full of joy and add just a tiny bit more story of what happens after. My only gripe is probably more about the fact that it's a visual novel and not my typical kind of RPG/adventure game: you're stuck playing a character with existing history that is important to the story and it leads to situations that you can't avoid. When I have game-altering choice in a game, it just feels a little bad when you're NOT offered a choice and it's you're character's fault :(But that could just be b/c I don't normally play this kind of game. As far as story goes, it's a great read!

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but the finished product has the same hang-ups that I had with the demo: bad writing, very long dialogues up-front when you haven't bonded with the characters yet, awkward exchanges, no choice in what the innkeeper is like, very little challenge or diversity to the drink-making mini game, even taking out any challenge whatsoever to putting clues together into a quest because they're on color-coded pieces of paper...There is so much of just me clicking through the dialogue because it's in slow, short chunks at once (even at the speediest setting).
