_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Coffee Talk, so when I found this game in development I was really looking forward to it. The art and character designs looked gorgeous and I was sold on the fantasy/dnd world. But after about 4 hours of gameplay, it hasn't really met my expectations. It feels unfair to leave my rating on an incomplete playthrough, but I don't have the motivation to keep playing anymore.Story: So far, I'm not particularly invested in the storyline. To be fair, I haven't gotten to a point where it's totally cohesive yet, but given that the Steam refund period is only 2 hours, I think there should have been at least something within my 4-hour gameplay to pique my interest. The dialogue feels like it drags on forever before it gets to the point, the conversations aren't always that interesting, and overall it just hasn't been a fun reading experience.Drink Mixing: The drink mixing is extremely simple and one-dimensional. There are 5 attributes a drink can have (stealth, strength, intelligence, charisma, defence) and 5 main ingredients that only affect one attribute. Because of how simple the main ingredients are, the drink mixing is in turn extremely simple, even with the addition of infusions later. The characters constantly order the exact same drink and there's no challenge in trying to figure out what drink they want. The game doesn't allow you to experiment and discover your own recipes, instead you have to earn them through story progression, so there's basically no puzzle solving involved. It's just a click and drag game, at that point. Characters: They really killed it with the character design (and art direction in general, I think) but unfortunately their personalities don't really keep me interested. None of their personal storylines have me invested, and while I don't dislike any of the characters, I can't say I particularly like them either. Sometimes their personalities feel exaggerated and overly quirky, which makes their dialogue a pain to read because it seems like they're trying really hard to fit into a trope.Overall, this game was just really mediocre. It's fallen short on pretty much all the aspects I was looking forward to in a drink making visual novel. I see that they're updating and fixing parts of the game, such as the rumour minigame, so maybe if they change up the drink mixing game it'll be more enticing for me to play, but as of right now I can't say I particularly enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: A cozy fantasy visual novel game. The main way to move the story forward is through rumors/quests. They can be unlocked by talking to the various visitors. At the end of each level, you can add the info to add a quest to the board to be completed later.- Detailed artwork including characters and scenes. In the tavern, there is a cthulhu tentacle that ungulates as time goes by and adds to the magical tavern vibe. - When you are introduced to a new character, they have their unique personalities and preferred drinks.- Two conversation choices that lead to different outcome in the story and getting different Steam achievements.- Making drinks is clear with the pin recipe feature. - There is an option to let dialogue auto-run, so player does not need to confirm after each new statement. - Some of the conversations drag longer than expected and some editing would have helpful to make the conversations more crisp. I would take breaks and rotate with another game with more active player engagement. - There are no other locations to visit outside of the tavern. I hear about killing monsters and going on quests, but we do not see the scenes play out and only hear about them from visitors. - This game has bundles with similar Steam games like Coffee talk Episode 2 and Monster Prom 3.- Various DLC to for collectors and players that want a deeper experience. Conclusion: This game provides a realistic tavern experience, but the bloated dialogue bogs the story down at times. If the game had voice acting, it would have been more engaging. Thank you again to the devs for providing this review key. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I would only recommend this game to people who like storytelling!With visual novel games, I find that things tend to happen  you, but in Tavern Talk, things tend to happen  you. In other words, to grasp the plot, you'll need to rely on the characters you befriend to recount the events. The life of an innkeeper!At its core, I believe this game is about sonder (the realization that each random passerby is living a life as vivid and complex as your own), as you'll get to listen to the varying perspectives and opinions of the characters. Your friends will set off on journeys you won't get to see for yourself, but it's always you they come back to. Even that, they'll have strong opinions on. And speaking of strong opinions, here are more of mine!Why should you play this game? Because witnessing the telling of stories can only make you itch to go and experience your own to tell. This game instilled me with more than enough inspiration to do so! The world and its people (both in real life and in the game) are beautiful. Go forth and adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Soundtrack is amazing, gameplay is nonexistent, characters are interesting, story... not so much. It's not bad but not good enough to spend 12 hours on it.First of all soundtrack is amazing. I loved it and my favorite is the one plays when you make a drink.About gameplay... In Coffee Talk you have to figure out what your customer wants to drink on your own. It's like a simple puzzle game where you collect clues from the conversations, in here they just tell you what to make. Quest are the same, you just make the quest when the story tells you to do, there is no failure state just put the 3 same looking notes and you are done. This is not a bad thing, I think they just didn't want this game to be any stressful. I say this so you can adjust your expectations. You do make some decisions, but I'm not sure how much they affect the story.I didn't mind any of that because I played the demo and knew that was gonna happen. I still bought the game because I thought "they probably focused on story and that's all I care in a game like this" but I unfortunately didn't like the story. First of all lore is confusing (or I might be just dumb, so I won't focus on that) and second, the story... how should I say this… too naive…? I wouldn't even mind that if the tone didn't shift every second. One moment a huge catastrophe happens probably a lot of people just died and the next moment a character says "meh it's just Tuesday innit" like.. wtf. (It felt like character themself didn't care about the world so why should I)This happens throughout the story. A thief character says smt like "I love chaos and I want to steal sh*t" and at the next moment "I couldn't leave him like that so I saved him". The most drastic and ridiculous change happens to Assassin character, he is basically a more edgy version of Sasuke (one of the quests actually references this with its picture). He evolves from edgy comedic relief character to a character with a tragic backstory to a character from My Little Pony. And again that itself isn't a bad thing. I like My Little Pony and I do like those kinds of stories but it just needs to be consistent. I think Fable and Melli is a good example of this. Fable stays as the same person but more courageous and Melli stays as the same person just more smart and capable. They are also goody-two-shoes characters but at least they stay that way and that's why I like them.Overall I didn't like the game and I probably won't be able to finish it even though I'm near the end. But I do think this studio has potential. Maybe next time..

_childDocuments_.review: I do all my reviews solely based on hard of hearing and deaf accessibility, and Tavern Talk passes with flying colors. All dialogue is done via text and the customization is very accessible. There is an autoplay mode, and the text speed can be adjusted in the settings. Highest speed was a scooch too fast for me, second highest was a scooch too slow, but the story was good enough that my ADHD didn't wander very often. A full voice cast would have helped with the attention span and immersion, but game was still very solid without it and I can understand why that may have been a bit out of the developer's reach.

_childDocuments_.review: (I have to admit that I've always wanted to start a review like this, but now I'll get to the usual. XD) is a cozy, relaxing visual novel with magical potion-making elements developed and published by Gentle Troll Entertainment.  You take on the role of the Innkeeper (whose gender pronouns can be decided) who runs a tavern.  As travelers drop by for a drink and/or pick up a quest, you engage in friendly talk with them.  In regards to the potions, they aren't your usual liquid refreshments.  As they're magically infused, they can determine the fate of the traveler, and especially, if they embark on a quest, whether that quest ends up being successful.  Other have noted this, and it would be amiss of me to leave this out, but  is like  in a medieval fantasy setting.  You serve customers, hand out quests, and perhaps in the process, help to save the world from the big, bad villain.  However, I'll stop my synopsis here to avoid the usual spoilers and all that. ^^With the gameplay, there are the usual choices presented, like in visual novels.  They can influence how well you get along with the various travelers who frequent the tavern.  You can also assemble quests by listening to the various rumors that travelers will give you, and once the quests are assembled, you can put them on the quest board.  However, the main gameplay is the potion-making aspect.  You start off with six potions to choose from, but you'll get more potions as the story progresses.  Potions can enhance certain abilities, such as agility, intelligence, strength, etc.  Also, you'll have access to infusions a little later, which can help boost (or weaken) these abilities.  When it comes to quests, you'll be given one of two potion options.  Usually, one is the better option that results in the quest being successful, although either potion will result in a quest successfully completed.  Also, there are plenty of Steam achievements, and they count towards a user's global total.  However, at the time of this review, there are no Steam trading cards.Now that I've gone over the story and gameplay, I'll move onto my thoughts.  When I first heard about  coming to Steam, I couldn't help getting excited, as my thoughts immediately led me to both  games, which I enjoyed and I've written reviews for, so do check out the link to my curation to read those review and perhaps a follow would be wonderful. ;)  Thus, when I was offered a review key for this game, I knew I had to play it right away.  Without further delay, I'll give my thoughts on the story.  I love how it starts off, setting the scene as the Innkeeper and her patrons are in the world of Phesoa.  It starts off as a typical day, with the elf Fable entering the tavern and being their usual scared self.  However, it is the Innkeeper who gently helps Fable on their emotional journey (although you can choose to be mean to Fable, but I wouldn't recommend that lol), and it leads to Fable eventually taking on quests.  Other travelers enter the tavern, ordering drinks and taking quests.  All of this leads to the main story in which (major story spoilers here, so I'll put it in spoiler text) .  Depending on the drink choices made for quests, you can get one of four endings: good, normal, bad, or a hidden one.  I like that the story isn't linear in this regard.  I enjoyed the story, and I really loved the cast of characters.  There's such a variety of personalities, and the travelers have their own quirks.  I mentioned Fable earlier, and then there's Kyle, the forgetful vampire, as well as Rhea, the blacksmith who wants to beat her ex-husband in an upcoming blacksmith competition.  I especially liked the relationships that these characters developed, ranging from sweet, ever-lasting friendships to unexpected romances.  Even when it comes to the villain, I found it difficult to hate him although I certainly wouldn't condone his actions.  If I had to choose a couple of my favorite characters, they'd be Melli, the sweet cat detective, and Baya, the swamp monster who just wants to have close friends.With the gameplay, I found myself having to get used to the potion-making mechanic.  There's a tutorial that explains how to make the potions.  (You can use either the mouse or controller to do so.)  It's basically like following a blueprint to make the potion with right amount of ingredients.  Using infusions can make it easier or more difficult to make potions, but once you get the hang of this mechanic, it's quite easy to make them.  I do wish that there was a quick-making potion mechanic once you're able to make all the potions at least once since it would help save a bit of time, but this is a minor nitpick.  As for the achievements, I was able to obtain all of them, even getting all of the endings.  However, there is no "already read text" option even though you can choose to speed up text.  It would have been nice to have that option to save time on getting the other endings, which is why it took me quite a while to get all of the achievements.  A couple of achievements can be tricky to get without a guide, so I'd recommend this one:As for the writing, I found it brilliant.  The story flowed well, and there were no pacing issues, especially with the potion-making mechanic to provide a bit of a break from dialogue.  The characters come alive through the writing, and I found myself laughing and crying with/for them.  Oh, and before I forget, even the Innkeeper has a backstory, which is quite the shocker.  The only errors I noticed were that on the rare occasion, a couple of sentences were repeated in a row by the same character and a bit of coding errors, but they should be fixed in a future update.Regarding the art, it is beautiful.  I love how well the characters and backgrounds were well drawn and colored.  They really give off that medieval fantasy setting well.  Even during the ending credits, there's special art, so you can see what happens to the various characters.  I only wish that there was a CG gallery, so I can revisit these images whenever I want.With the music, the tracks are lovely to listen to.  I really like how each character has their own theme track, and they really fit well.  Voy's (the phantasm) track is my favorite since it's on the upbeat, fun side.  There's a very wonderful variety of tracks, fitting well with the events that they're placed in.  With voice acting, there's only the one female voice acting at the beginning of the game to introduce the story, but otherwise, there's none.  I don't think this is a negative since I'm one to enjoy the story and gameplay, and voice acting is just a bonus.Overall, would I recommend ?  If you like visual novels and especially like  but have always wanted to play in a more fantasy setting, then this is worth taking a look.  It was a pure joy getting to play this wonderful relaxing game with its many wonderful characters and the exciting adventurous story.  For the asking price, it's definitely worth getting, and it's also in a few Steam bundles, so you can save a bit of money.Finally, I want to give a major thank you to Gentle Troll Entertainment for the review key.  I'm happy to have had the chance to play , and I'm already wanting a . ^^

_childDocuments_.review: The visual novel part is really visually novelling -- so for roughtly $18, it *is* like buying a book. And if I think about it that way, the game feels less like a sunk cost. However, I did buy this game at a discount during a sale -- I wouldn't have otherwise. CONS:The game play experience is pretty repetitive and tedious in my honest opinion, which was my least favorite part. I'm trying to complete all the achievements and it feels needlessly more tedious than it needs to be, even with the fast forward. Additionally, I would have liked the game to be more queer since it has the LGTBQ+ tag on it; so I was pretty disappointed about that. It still felt comphet in many areas.There doesn't feel like a whole lot of variety when it comes to the story telling, even when you make different choices. It feels like the end is only where the convergences happen, but I think had there been some more different directions depending on drink choices, it would have made the overall gameplay more novel -- especially when you start over to try other things to collect the achievements. PROS:However, all that above, for me, is not enough to vote it as a no. At best, I'd rate it as a mixed yes/no, but since that's not an option, I'd rather lean more towards the positive. So like gradewise, I'd say this is a C+ to B-Overall, the game is cute. The characters all have their own personality. I personally like how much of a himbo Clay is, for example. And how Fable reveals different, contrasting emotions in her character development. Andu is a cutie, too.The tavern background is pretty. The overall art aspect of the game is pretty, maybe not *gorgeous* but still aesthetically pleasing enough. The drinks are fun to look at -- I always like seeing the cute end results of drink crafting.The drink mixing is also functionally pretty fun, but I think having more drink variations would have made the experience a little better. Using the coaster as a guide is very helpful and mentally stimulating enough for me, personally.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I had read the reviews before I threw down for the full game.  A lot of folks have already given really solid critiques on this one, which I really appreciate, but I'll echo as best I can.Artwork?  Stunning.  Cannot be said enough.  The detailing on tavern is beautiful.  The character design and little shifts in hair/fur are stellar.  It's lovely to look at.I played the demo and i really enjoyed the drink mixing and the introduction to quest building and thought this could be a nice little visual novel.  When I think of visual novels, I immediately think of games like Arcade Spirit where there are several aspects to the game: you can choose romantic paths  or not, you can effect the outcome of the story with your choice, your dialogue and your decision are a crucial part of the game, etc.That is not this game.  This is a click through book where after 500 clicks of dialogue that amounts to "this meeting could have been an email."  You make the same drink over and over again.  Per my play through, I reached act 1 scene 5, and I have made 3 of the 5 drink options. The dialogue is so incredibly long, drawn out, and pointless that I had to come to the reviews to see if it was just me, if it got better, or if I should bail now. The characters are bad.  They are as trope-y as possible and it's not a successful gag.  The elf is non-binary, UwU-level inept, but somehow completes a quest despite being ill prepared to take on one.  The furry-bait lady is obstinate and angry all the time because "lol isn't it funny that even her niceness is gurmpy coded?"  There is a rogue who shows up a few times and is "s u p e r   e m o   a n d   d r a m a t i c" for several scenes because rogue and "omg don't you love when rogues are dark and broody?"There is so much potential in this premise; the DND cozy core idea of running a tavern is really great and has a high marketability in today's world.  But there are so many visual novel GAMES out there that function as both novels and games.  And on a platform where gamers are coming to play, there needs to be more gameplay and less aimless dialogue.  Give us a paragraph that forwards the plot, gives us consequences for bad drinks, give us choices that affect the outcome and this could be a great game.  But it is not there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to a land where magic sways in the air, blessed by bits of stardust. Full of legends and heroes alongside exotic beverages and rumors.You’ll take the role of the owner of an inn, but as unappealing as that might sound, don’t get mistaken… Not only are you surrounded by mystery and interesting stories, but also the constant company of capable heroes in search of interesting quests to fulfill. And maybe, more often than not, in need of advice combined with your delightful and colorful drink section.You’ll be in charge of not only mixing drinks that will boost far more than the morale of your patrons, but also gathering rumors and relevant information to help assemble the quests and even assist in sorting out the adventures they’ll embark on.There are plenty of characters that will visit your tavern on a regular basis, each one of them with more than a story to tell, secrets to hide and their own personality. It is up to you to decide if you want to lend them more than "an ear" and let friendship flutter.Even so, you won’t be left alone since your faithful familiar, Andu, will always be at your side. Ready to assist in correcting certain mistakes and even maintaining your property clean.The game has 5 languages at your disposal, alongside the option of deciding about the pronouns you want to be addressed as.The overall plot is well written and quite intriguing from the beginning, whilst the display of witty humor, plagued more often than not, with some geek-culture-based references, won’t leave you indifferent… Personally, I’ve felt like the meme of Leonardo DiCaprio signaling in “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood”, more times than I probably would ever admit.Plenty of different magical creatures reside in this world: from vampires, werewolves, wizards... Even detectives in cat-shaped form and plenty more!Some of them will need a push in the right direction or even a helping hand to confront their fears, aside from the occasional drink. The appreciation for your support will end up decorating your walls and shelves, as they give you handmade mementos or little trinkets as a gift for your inn, whenever they come back from their travels!I was surprised when they even broke the fourth wall in a well scripted way, earning well-deserved praise.Every single character is unique. From race, personality traits, background or even affiliations. This colorful world is filled with personality and originality.The art style is really beautiful, vibrant and colorful. With Japanese anime-based style and well-made animation. The music quite complements the atmosphere the tavern portrays, or it befits certain situations unfolding. Whilst the entire cast of characters has their own theme to accompany their presence whenever they decide to visit your establishment.I fell in love with Jade’s and Skully’s character themes, even though the complete soundtrack was truly enjoyable.Your diary will be one of your best allies for keeping the notes about rumors organized, the recipes, list of ingredients and information gathered regarding every visitor that may set foot in your domain.Considering this game's length, I did miss having more chances to participate in the conversations unfolding. Even so, you can state your opinion with a variety of choices from time to time, and your words will impact some of the outcomes from quests and even the characters' growth. The beverages you recommend before an important mission can also have aftermath consequences, and in a way, some of the said outcomes can be more heartbreaking than others...In addition, the crafting system is not complicated, and you'll get the gist of it pretty fast, which made me also wish for more varied orders from customers. Instead of them all sticking to their favorite drinks whenever they just visit for leisure.The menu will expand as time goes by, and you will acquire new recipes and ingredients for your renowned concoctions. However, I reached a point where I no longer needed to check the recipes, even though drawing them on the board is a mandatory step to preparing the orders that you'll be entrusted with.The story, even if the quests at first may be seen as not related to one another, in the end are somehow connected, and that will help you assemble together the pieces of the puzzle about the threat looming over the entire world.Tavern Talk offers up to 17/20 hours of gaming plus 49 achievements to unlock. This adventure felt like a heartwarming and memorable trip that filled me with laughter. Also, it made me care about the characters I met along the way as well as made me grow attached to them. And more importantly, kept me intrigued by the world portrayed and the mysteries surrounding it till the very end.I would like to thank Gentle Troll Entertainment for the opportunity given to the group by providing a review copy of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've 100%ed it, I sort of feel like adding more nuance to my review. I did like the game, I just think it could've been even better. If you like DND and VNs, you'll probably like it. First off, the art is DELIGHTFUL. The game is gorgeous from top to bottom and I think the art and animation is easily its strongest suit. Second, I really really like most of the cast. The vast majority of characters I found charming and endearing, and some dynamics between them, I really enjoyed.While we're talking about things I liked: the setting. I love the cosmology of Phesoa, I think it's really really nice. To me as a DND player, it feels familiar yet refreshing and distinct. To non DND players, I think it's digestible and understandable without needing any prior knowledge. Finally, I am rather enamoured by the bad ending. Often times I find that bad endings, in their pursuit of being bad, are just plain unpleasant and unsatisfactory. Tavern Talk's bad ending scene, while sad and evidently a bad ending, still manages to feel cathartic. To me, that makes the bad ending worthwhile for its own sake rather than for completion's sake. Commendable writing in that scene!Now, things I find weaker. Not necessarily terrible, just things that really take the game down from being GREAT to just being good. The gameplay is nonexistant. Drink mixing is so constrained that the only difference between picking drinks from a list and mixing them is that the latter, which the game does, takes longer. There's no experimenting or messing about when crafting a drink, you HAVE to stick to a pre-established recipe, and you don't discover them. They're handed to you.Rumors are also only interesting in your first run, of course. On replays, they don't have any novelty because they're the same on every route. This, I didn't mind as much, because the story kept me playing, but I can see it being a real loss for some people. I see a lot of people saying that they feel like their choices don't matter, and I can understand why: the individual quest choices change a few lines of dialogue, but the major effects don't kick in until act 4's last part. Everything goes more or less the same in every route up until the last 10-20 minutes of the game,so it feels like your choices aren't all that relevant until the last minute. The game also presents you with the odd "illusion of choice" in the dialogue, which wouldn't be bad if it were in another context, but here it compounds the issue. It's not noticeable on your first run, which is the run I enjoyed the most, but a replay of the game to see another ending will have you realizing this very quickly. Thank God for the skip button!Lastly, and this is a minor writing peeve of mine: Fable feels like a writers' pet. Don't get me wrong, I like Fable as a character a lot! They're super endearing and the game succeeded in making me want to see them thrive. That being said, without spoiling anything, later plot developments feel sort of... handed to them, without much prior setup, and they sort of wind up feeling like a main character in what should clearly be an ensemble cast. I would like to reiterate that I enjoyed my time with the game, though! I think it's a good game that could've been even better, but is still really nice and enjoyable. I mean, I 100%ed it, I wouldn't have if I didn't like it!

_childDocuments_.review: Tavern Talk is kinda like "VA-11 Hall-A" meets "Strange Horticulture" with a Dungeons and Dragons setting. I enjoyed my time here, and I regard this game/VN as a bit of a flawed gem. -EDIT- The dev team actually listens to feedback, and they are addressing some of the "flawed" parts already. I am super excited to see a developer group making their game better so quickly, I feel that Tavern Talk is going to be a true gem when they get done polishing it!What I like:Plenty of characters to get to knowInteresting settingCool tavern vibeOverarching story is attention-grabbingYou "influence" the story with the drinks you serveThe Innkeeper actually has a back story that is revealed as you playAnimation and art is amazing. Bonus points for how freaking adorable Melina is.What I don't like:The user interface is a bit clunky (saving/loading could be a grid so you don't have to scroll a mile, and there could be a thumbnail pic of the save instead of a generic chapter marker)*being addressed!* No "skip read dialogue/skip to next choice" option. That makes replays really annoying and slow.The cameos and crossover characters really messed up the immersion for me (even though I am a fan of a "certain tavern" and the two people known to come from it!)*being addressed!* Limited drinks for certain characters/situations. I'm sorry, Fable, but you're getting a bunch of Swift Strikes...Almost too much dialogue at some points, it's like dang just tell the story already!All that said, it's fun watching the characters open up and grow. They even form their own relationships, and it's heartwarming to know that it is because of your tavern and efforts that it happens.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I have just finished my first playthrough and here are my thoughts:First and Foremost: The Comparison to Coffee Talk that I've seen and heard in my social circles when I've brought up this game. Yes, the premise is roughly similar in the fact that you are a member of a service industry where you provide beverages to your patrons and are expected to listen and offer encouragement/advice to aspects of their life.  That is sort of where the comparisons end. It is enough of an overlap that the playerbase of one should enjoy the other but you do not need to explicitly like Coffee Talk to enjoy this game.Next, a reminder: This is a Visual Novel. If you need gameplay loops or deep interaction, then this (like most Visual Novels) is will not be fun for  you.  Last thing to address as this seems to be relevant for the modern game playing / game buying market: Is there LGBT representation?  Yesn't.  There is potential for it based a couple of choices you make and how you read into certain dialogue choices you, the player as the Innkeeper, make (I personally just read it as the more racy end of banter any member of the service industry might engage in with their customers. If you've worked the field you know).  I wouldn't call it a major deal regardless if you're Pro or Against such subject matter, but is called out as some customers seem to need that subject matter included in their games and others cannot stand it in the slightest.With those big three things out of the way the things I liked and disliked about the game.The story: A charming story. The overarching plot involving the world didn't really challenge me or make me go 'wow'. It was a simple little adventure. It makes sense that there are DLC translating it to D&D, as the story arc of the game form the Adventurer's perspective would make a great campaign.    When going through this VN I was honestly more interested in learning about 'me' the Innkeeper than anything else going on. Well...that and petting Andu.The Art Style: Watching the videos on the store page: You get what you see. There is no hidden sudden style shift or anything. So if you like this comfy aesthetic of the Tavern's Interior and your Mixology lab, you'll enjoy it. If you need a little more variation in your gameplay...you'll struggle here.The Music: This is where I think the game shined the most. Overall I would call it "comfy". Most of the time it fits the sedate "I want to unwind after a hard adventure" vibe you, as the Innkeeper, tried to build. When tension does happen, the score shifts nicely.  I wouldn't say I need to listen to any of this music outside of the game or that it revolutionized a genre, but it fit the game wonderfully.The Mixing of Drinks: This is is where the game struggled to keep me. Some of your patrons want the same thing over and over, which is true to form for a regular. They know what they like. Sometimes you can recommend something similar to have them try it out and it works, but all in all they want what they want. Having to mix it each time by hand is a little tedious and a feature this game could use is a quick-mix option.  Would such an option remove one of the few 'gameplay' aspects of the game? Sure, but that's why you make it opt-in (such as a toggle feature in settings while having it default to off). The Dialogue Options, UI, and Progressing Text: So I tried some of the game on auto-progress at the highest text speed, and that felt way too slow. I simply read quickly, so I swapped to just hitting "confirm" a couple times with my controller to full print out the text and then progress. This is great...right up until you get into a loop on this and get a dialogue choice and the second "confirm" button press also sometimes registers as you choosing the first option in your dialogue choices. Not a fan. Perhaps even faster auto play speeds could help? Or an 'instantly' option for generating the text in any dialogue box so you are only hitting the confirm button to progress to the next one could fix this.Replayability: I'll probably get around to another playthrough to explore all the ending options/earn all the achievements, but in the game's current state it wont be for a while, maybe after another Slay The Princess run or three to work on those instead.  If the auto-mix and the instant text quality of life features get added? This will come to the top of my list as I do enjoy the story and my complaints are purely in how I, the player/reader, have to interact with the game aspects of it.Would I recommend this game?Yes with an asterisk.*If you come into it looking for Coffee Talk explicitly? No. Not really. Part of what defines that game are it's gameplay actions which this game sorely lacksIf you come into it looking for a fun Visual Novel where you will have some memorable characters and just the right amount of audio design and music to be ambient without distracting? Wholeheartedly yes.Having played the game do I think it was worth my investment of time and money?So I rate games (excluding Rogue-lite/Rogue-likes) on being "great' if I can get 1 hour of enjoyment out of a primary playthrough per dollar spent on the game (I don't like measuring a game being 'great' based on 100%-ing it if it can't be done in a single run).  As such...even on sale it did not reach that mark. Part of which is I am a faster than normal reader if the max text speed in game is to be a metric so I'm willing to believe that it should have padded itself out closer to the Introductory Offer Sale Price if I left it on auto-play, especially on the default text crawl speed.I would still call it a good game as I felt like I will get my money's worth with the second playthrough and it did inspire a few ideas for a Changeling the Dreaming game I intend to run in the future.All in all? 7/10.  Good bordering on Great, but not perfect. For the purposes of this platform I say "Yes" on Would you Recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a mediocre experience for me. The main problem being that there's not a lot of game here. The only gameplay mechanic is making drinks that are capable of enhancing the abilities of the guests visiting your tavern which then leads to different story outcomes. That's ultimately what makes this a slightly interactive experience instead of being a pure read-along visual novel. But there was just not enough depth to the drink mixing to hold my interest for more than the first few hours.Of course none of this secret. The developers are upfront about what their game is and isn't, including making a demo available. So I should've done a little more research before buying it. I would have quickly seen that it isn't really for me, despite the fantasy role-playing type setting. But if you are into relaxing, wholesome visual novels, this might still be worth a look for you as evidenced by the many other positive reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in this game seems to have a life of its own, from the characters, to the locations, to the lore, and Tavern Talk is all the richer for it. Cherry on top: the game is gorgeous. I could stare at the backgrounds and the characters for hours (and I have). I would recommend this game to all lovers of visual novels, it's a treat.

_childDocuments_.review: This game follows in the genre of other games like Coffee Talk and Valhalla.  Its stories are told through dialogue with and between a variety of very well written and compelling characters.   There is one overarching story that ties the other ones together.  Each of the characters have their own backstory and I liked all of them.  A lot of time, effort, and creativity was put into this game and it shows.  While things are linear, there are decision points in the game that affect the affect outcome.  I played through it twice, fast forwarding through dialogue I saw before but then taking time to experience the parts that were different.  It was a very entertaining, enjoyable, and worthwhile game.  I am glad I added it to my collection.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet, but my experience so far has been fantastic. The writing's snappy and really good at balancing both pretty solid humor and important emotional beats. There's tons of incredibly well-written exchanges littered throughout the game, to the point where I had to make a folder for all the screenshots I took from the quest log. So far the actual "consequences" part of a choices-and-consequences game hasn't been super obvious, but even the small stuff makes me feel like I have an impact on the characters.My favorite thing about the game, though, is just how deeply it captures the feeling of both a fantasy setting and a TTRPG. Even if the world isn't exactly in the D&D world, everything about it tells me the devs truly understand the experience. It manages to strike at the essence of that experience in basically every aspect, from visual presentation to character writing to background worldbuilding. It really feels like it was made with love for videogames and D&D, and pretty much everyone I  know who's played a TTRPG has heard me recommend Tavern Talk too many times to count.If you like D&D, or Pathfinder, or non-fantasy TTRPGs like CoC and Cyberpunk RED, or just fantasy in general, or visual novels as a whole, or just really well-written stories and characters and worlds, I can't recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I'm giving this a very tentative thumbs up so far. I've been a big fan of similar games in the past. Valhalla: Cyberpunk bartending action was crazy good and Coffee talk was a slightly inferior but still really good follow up to the genre. The writing in this game is... ok. I think the first few chapters were pretty good, and after that it's fallen off a little bit. Part of the fun of these types of games is listening to people and their problems, but honestly it doesn't feel like a lot of the people walking in the bar have problems. Maybe I just haven't gotten far enough for things to start fitting together, but it feels so disjointed so far. But honestly I think the biggest problem I have is the same problem I had with Coffee Talk, the innkeeper has some very slight personality, but they are basically just an everyman. No name, no strong personality, and maybe some slight story connection. It puts a LOT of the work on the characters coming in to be interesting and make an interesting plot rather than giving both sides of the dialogue spice. And, although learning and empathizing with the people coming in is important and fun, it feels bad that the character you are playing doesn't really have as much stake in anything. Also, this type of game is not supposed to nor should have a ton of gameplay elements, but tavern talk is lacking woefully. They basically give you the correct answer with every drink, there's not a large variety, and making them is just a little bit too much of a hassle for me. Coffee talk and Valhalla did a good job of at least giving a few times where you have to interpret what a customer might need rather than just telling you. Plus, the putting quests together mechanic is lackluster. It's just a story feature. I've seen many people say "they shouldn't be color coded" and I agree, but honestly I wish there was even a little more than that. I think it has so much potential in a game like this where you're the one posting rumors and quests and such, but it just doesn't deliver.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of these games that I simply cannot resist writing some kind of review for (even though it's incredibly late and I should be sleeping but this game's end kept me awake). Tavern Talk is a magical experience in my opinion - a journey filled with so many memorable moments that my heart immediately grew fond of it. I've been practically inhaling the game's content for the past few days and now that I have reached the end, I feel... Fulfilled. This certainly is a wholesome game indeed and very worthy of that title.For starters, I think it is quite easy to see how beautifully done the art is. The backgrounds are adorned with small details, bringing the world to life and keeping you entertained even though you see the tavern 24/7. The fact that characters can bring back keepsakes from their missions is such an adorable and great add-on too! I love how the story left its marks on the environment. The different weather changes or pieces of decorations always had me inspecting the background for any changes. Speaking about the art, I think we can all appreciate how clean it is, right? The characters are all gorgeously designed and their personalities are greatly executed through their clothing for example. Their idle animations and reactions to the plot were on point and I never got tired of staring at this stunning art on screen.I'm not a great music connoisseur but I know my fair share of tavern/medieval music, being able to form my verdict of how well-done this aspect of Tavern Talk was. It got me in the perfect mood for chilling in a tavern and listening to adventurers re-telling their vast experiences in a world full of fantasy. I usually get distracted while playing games and put on other music in the background (yes, shame on me) but I can proudly say it didn't happen in this case! I love how every character had a little tune of their own (once more adding to their amazing characterization).Speaking of the characters, let's just get to my favorite part, shall we? I want to gush over how much they grew on me and how I freaking adore them all!!! The writing was so incredibly good, I don't know how to properly explain it. We spend  al lot of time with the different adventurers during this journey that I actually learned to appreciate them all. Sure, starting out, I had my favorites () but as time passed, I loved each and every member of the cast. Their vast personalities and stories resonated with something deep in my heart, moving me greatly. I love how small parts of their designs and traits changed over time, proving they all developed as characters and grew to be different people. This game really feels like watching your friends evolve to their happiest selves and I know nothing more that compares to the beautiful warmth of a friend's embrace. This story and its characters hugged me tightly and definitely hasn't let go yet!The story itself was a very fitting plot of heroes saving the world but considering how beautifully every aspect of the game was done, I thought it was executed fairly charming. I didn't get tired of it, instead being very interested in what would happen next! There are clear cosnequences of certain plot lines seen in the game, which I can appreciate (even if it hurt; ).The UI of the game is pleasing to look at and everything is easy to understand/use. I liked the drink-making mini game as well, especially since new recipes and infusions were constantly added. Yay for versatility!Another small favorite feature of mine is the story told through drawings during the credits. It gave you such a welcomed conclusion to the story's end. Watching all characters interact almost made me tear up, especially after the hardships they had faced. I got so see several loose story ends tie up neatly and I couldn't be more grateful.I've seen someone in these reviews complain about the lack of gameplay and I would never judge anyone for that. Everyone's entitled to their own opinions. I think one should keep in mind that this is listed as a visual novel and those who are familiar with that type of game know that it's basically a book to read (, hence the name). For me, this game was a wonderful experience. I mostly value good characters and stories in a game and Tavern Talk delivered this very well.The only thing that was missing from the game in my opinion was a "skip the read text"-option. Sometimes I wished to go back and pick different options but going through some already viewed parts of the story was a very slow process. If that option would be added, I feel like the game would be easier to go through at times!Thank you Gentle Troll Entertainment for creating this wholesome game, which has filled my heart with a little more warmth and my mind with more memories of pleasant adventures with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, wish Steam had a way to give a middling review, but they don't, so I'm forced to pick between two options that I don't think the game really deserves either in. Tavern Talk is a lovely looking game, with fun music, but ultimately I'm just left with the impression that there was a fun concept here that just sort of got squandered. The story is kinda cute, but as with many projects these days, makes the cardinal sin of just forgoing actual comedy in favor of making references. Too many. The story occasionally gets good, but has a nasty habit of droning on and out and wearing out its welcome. But all that could be forgivable if it weren't for the fact that the drink mixing element is just hopelessly underutilized and handheld to the point of sucking all of the fun out of it. It can't even really generously be called a puzzle. Patrons more or less tell you exactly what they want "AGILE", "STRONG" and it bolded and repeated with synonyms just to really try to make it as mindless as possible. Furthermore, they basically never ask for any alternative drink either, so mix the proper drink for them once and you can pretty much be guaranteed that's what they'll want every single time. Sometimes they'll want it twice in the same conversation. There is basically no "puzzle' element to the game at all. This quickly turns the entire thing into just an unfun chore that you have to do to advance scenes. All in all, it was a solid concept, but just not well executed. The game and writing elements just feel sort of anemic. It feels like the drink mixing side was meant to help prop up the writing, but both sides end up feeling like they're undermining the other. Not quite willing to take itself seriously as either a true visual novel or be willing to push the player a little bit by being a puzzle game. Game would seriously benefit from a "hard" mode where the drink requests were just a bit more varied and more discerning. A shame too, the visuals are absolutely gorgeous and the world building seems neat.

_childDocuments_.review: As a partaker of the occasional Dungeons & Dragons game and a huge fan of Coffee Talk, I’ve had my eye on this game for a loong time. And the devs were kind enough to gift me a key to try it out early! Tavern Talk is at the end of the day a visual novel, so if you’re not into long conversations with recurring characters then this probably won’t be the game for you. But if you do like well-written dialogue and character development then keep reading. It's impossible not to fall in love with the fantasy world that the devs have created. It's filled with heart-warming characters, who you get to watch come out of their shells and change for the better as the story develops, some of the funniest (and fourth-wall breaking) dialogue I've read in a game, and beautiful artwork for every scene. My only downsides so far are that the potion-making gets a little repetitive as the game goes on, due to the limited number of potions (and why does everyone want a strength or dexterity potion?), as well as one aspect of the quest being a bit simple and redundant. But overall I really enjoyed this game and experienced only one teensy tiny bug throughout my playthrough. I'd definitely recommend it to fans of Coffee Talk and DND and it was much longer than I expected (in a good way)!Full thoughts:

_childDocuments_.review: Hello,I'm a huge fan of the "Coffee talk" game and I expected to get the same pleasure when playing "Tavern Talk". Alas, "Tavern Talk" didn't meet any of my expectations. I got bored after 4 hours of play (and 10 days of innkeeping IG) and I ended up uninstalling it. About the Gameplay : You don't have anything to do when preparing the drinks. You don't have to guess what drinks your customers want : the game tells you what to do. You can't improvise a drink either, you have to follow the recipe. It's pretty much the same about the quests you write for the adventurers. Indeed, the game tells you when you can combine 3 rumors into a quest. And you don't even have to chose wisely, for the rumors have different colors and shapes so you can recognize them. About the Story : I really miss the "Slice of life" aspect of "Coffee Talk" that I love so much. In Tavern Talk, you listen to adventurers telling you about their last quest. And you listen to them. And you listen to them... With almost no interaction with them. Which makes me wonder : Why do I have to listen to their quests when I could in any RPG play the quest at their stead ? Where is the small talk ? The 10 minute break after a rough day spent working at the hospital ? The lover quarrel ?In the end, I felt like the innkeeper wasnt part of the stories of Tavern Talk. I watched the game being played, and that wasnt interesting at all. Sincerely,22

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adored this game.It is the exact balance I needed for something cozy and relaxing I can play to unwind after work, but still having an interesting story that grabbed me completely. Some people might say the characters are a bit stereotypical, but I couldn't disagree more! They are my favorite part of the game, and getting to play through it and see how they grow and break expectations feels really rewarding. This story has captivated me completely and I absolutely will be replaying the game to try and see the alternate outcomes for the quests as much as possible.There's still more I'd like to see explored! Some characters who stop by the tavern we never end up learning much about, and I wish we did. As for the drink-making mechanic, I definitely feel like it could've been explored more. Outside of quest-specific drinks, all the requests felt a little repetitive. Moreover, since we're given the mechanic of mashing ingredients together, I would've loved it if we were able to discover the alternate drink recipes by mixing the ingredients ourselves, as we see fit. I think the gameplay would benefit of having to think more and consider the request for the drink, instead of just reproducing the recipes we get.The artstyle is also quite beautiful! I love how unique all of the character sprites are, and all of the assets look amazing. The music I don't love as much, some of the character themes startled me a lot when they started playing. It's still fairly good, but I've been spoiled by some of my other favorite indies!Overall, I'm very happy to have played this game, and I'm looking forward to more additional content for it! Please give it a try if you can, it's not overly long nor expensive, and there's great replay value from what I can see. It's definitely a lot of fun!

_childDocuments_.review: "Tavern Talk" by Gentle Troll Entertainment invites players into a cozy, whimsical world where they manage a bustling fantasy tavern. Let's dive into what makes this game a must-try, and where it could use a bit more seasoning.Pros:Humor: "Tavern Talk" shines with its witty dialogue and humorous interactions. The game's characters are vibrant and full of personality, providing endless entertainment as they share their outlandish stories and requests. The humor is cleverly integrated into the gameplay, making each tavern encounter a delightful experience.Art Direction: The game's art direction is nothing short of enchanting. The hand-drawn graphics and attention to detail create a warm, inviting atmosphere that immerses players in the fantasy tavern setting. Each character and environment is uniquely designed, adding to the overall charm and appeal of the game.Engaging Storytelling: Beyond the humor, "Tavern Talk" boasts an engaging storyline that unfolds as players interact with their patrons. The game cleverly weaves together various narratives, ensuring that players remain invested in the tales of their tavern's eclectic visitors.Cons:Limited Brewing Mechanic: One of the game’s few drawbacks is its limited brewing mechanic. While the idea of crafting unique drinks for patrons is intriguing, the execution feels somewhat shallow. The brewing system lacks depth and variety, which can make this aspect of the game feel repetitive over time.Lack of Voice Acting: "Tavern Talk" could significantly benefit from voice acting. The rich dialogues and humorous exchanges would be even more impactful with professional voiceovers, enhancing the overall immersion and bringing the characters to life in a more dynamic way.Repetitive Tasks: As stated before, Some players might find that the daily tasks in the tavern can become repetitive. While the storytelling and character interactions add variety, the core gameplay loop of serving drinks and managing the tavern could use additional layers of complexity to keep it engaging in the long term.Conclusion:"Tavern Talk" is a delightful blend of humor, artistry, and engaging storytelling that offers a unique and enjoyable experience. Despite its minor drawbacks, the game remains a charming escape into a fantastical world. Raise a glass to Gentle Troll Entertainment for creating a game that truly knows how to keep the conversation—and the fun—flowing.Rating: 9/10 – A Barrel of Laughs with a Dash of Magic!
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - The art style and animation is incredible and the music is beautiful. I wouldn't mind just playing it in the background whilst I work.- The character personalities, background and lore in general are well written. It's given me the urge to delve further in the world and create my own character.- It's very obvious this game has been made with a lot of love and care by the devs which is really nice to see.- It is very immersive, I felt the friendships and conversations were very real. It was also nice seeing other adventurers interact with each other.- The quests and story is fun, I kept wanting to know the mysteries, what the adventurers found out and curious to know more about us (the innkeep).Things to note:- I do feel like there needs to be some sort of game-play between the gap of making quests such as playing a card game with the adventurers or some sort of mini-game as it does feel exhausting reading so much at a time. I end up rushing through the text when it's been awhile to feel relieved when I can finally put a quest together so it would be good to have a fun break in-between.- I think the drinks could be more creative on how we discover and the way we make them. I like the idea of discovering a drink by yourself (like mixing different potions or adding fusions) would be quite rewarding and fun.Overall, I do recommend this game if you want to immerse yourself in a new, fun world, meet unique characters and enjoy a lot of reading with small game-play. However, I don't recommend it to those who expect a lot of game-play.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a solid 6/10 (and 7-8 if you enjoy the writing somehow), still giving it a thumbs up because it's a working game, decent price and it has heart and charm. As boring as it is, for me, still got me curious enough to want to finish it once. You know the German stereotype, which they don't understand humour? You'll get it why such thing exist after playing this game. Like "writing several Twilight jokes in 2024" levels of not funny. I didn't even cringe, I just shrugged. Lots of 4th wall breaking as well, none of which tickle the funny bone... so far.I was expecting the D&D table experience, where you all relax after a big fight and start quipping and laugh/chill for the rest of the night. Instead it's just boring small talk with characters I don't care and like. Biggest crime of this game is it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring, imagine reading a book for 90 minutes and not find a single interesting thing in it...  Even worse there is no choice, no branching dialogue options (and picking between 2 exposition dumps isn't choice) the only way is forward and only thing you can do is make drink A or drink B. It makes writing even more intolerable because since as the innkeeper we have no character and no agency, we just sit there and listen boring characters keep on yapping about their daily boring lives that we don't care and do nothing about it. For example, there is a character who keeps calling us npc, if we had a chance to call her out, or be mean to her, or at least tell her she's being annoying and ask her to leave, that would be great. Because that would be a choice. If only we had options to sabotage/fail the quests, give them wrong drinks, hell at least ask them to wrap it up because don't want to listen how you buckle your shoe for 15 minutes, for the 3rd time this week... But no, instead you keep on pressing left click/space very slowly (and there is no skip option so you just sit there check the pretty art work I guess) and hope maybe next character wouldn't be so bad. I had better random tavern RP sessions with strangers in WoW, with more excitement and joy.For the positives, everything pretty much works, had no technical issues, everyone and everything looks great. There are few fresh ideas like making quests/drinks but they played it so safe, so it's just few extra clicks before the next yapping session. I found the writing really boring and unfunny but your experience might be different. The lessons might be just what you need, who knows... It's not really preachy so far. One of the better things is that they don't shove 'the progressive' ideas to your face, like you don't get a 15 minute story about why they use what pronoun, it just happens naturally, like in real life, like with real people... Lack of voice acting also hurts the game but it's understandable, wish we had at least character grunts/laughters/etc. for at least have a reference in our minds. Even with the boring story and mostly terrible jokes/characters (so far), game still got me curious just enough to keep going, and got me invested enough to write a review. So buy this if you like VNs but this is less like your favourite D&D podcast session and more of walls of texts of people talking about their emotions or being extremely unfunny.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll recommend this game. However, there are a few things I'd have to point out. It's not perfect, but it's a fantastic attempt.The art is stunning, and every single character is unique, stands out and very clearly conveys who they are. They don't change just because the story calls for it, but because you watch them pick up a quest, go on it and come back with growth and a tale to tell.The drinks are beautifully designed and the mini-game to make them is simple and fun. There's also a neat little 'mini-game' that requires you to make a quest for the coming adventurers.This is where we have to be a little harsh. Unfortunately, both mini-games come up short very quickly.The quest-writing minigame is just boring after you realize it's all colour-coded, you can't get it wrong and because the story relies on them being completed, you never feel clever for quickly rushing to make one that you realized you had all the bits for. [As of a recent post, they realized this issue and might work to fix it]The drinks can't be made if they're wrong (so no critical fails here), and giving the wrong drink doesn't have any real affect beyond a simple, "you got it wrong". I understand the huge amount of writing, but think the focus should have been shifted there. If I walk into a bar and got the wrong order, you can be damn sure my dialogue changes that night. I think selling this game and highlighting the drink making, while in this state, is in poor taste.SPOILER WARNINGIf you're reading this, you've also likely seen other reviews say the writing is poor, which is mostly true in that it's incredibly bloated.If I was a GM, role-playing as an innkeeper and my players just had fun role-playing, chatting among themselves and doing what these characters do, it would be a delight.Sadly, in a game format, it comes across as just way too much of nothing. Characters walk in, and go, and if they aren't the literal main cast, they're not worth remembering.Please don't get me wrong here, sometimes those fun moments of silly banter and idle chatter make for great story-telling or reading in their own right, but I sometimes felt like a character was just there because they had the art for them, and needed to fill time, rather than digging into making the 'encounter' meaningful or build towards something.I quite like this game anyway. It's a VN in the style of VA-HALL-A and/or Coffee Talk, and we need more like them. It's mystical, has a lot of great potential to improve in another iteration, and the Dev team is clearly working on fixing the small issues they can, while noting the more pressing ones for the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent visual novel, and I recommend it, however;It needs another editing pass, especially in the final third of the game.I'll give an example; Throughout the game, the editing and proofreading has been relatively sound. In the final third, we start to get awful redundant misuse of terms like 'off of' (i.e. "I'll just get it off of them"), broken italics or pronoun coding, which is pretty sloppy, and highlights a huge difference between the well-edited and proof-read early story to the lack of care towards the end of it.(For me there's horrific whiplash of going from good editing to starting to use off of in the final third of the story ~ I really wish this crap ("off of") would stop taking off at indie studios, or even from mid studios using weaker translators... its dire.)Otherwise, this is a standard visual novel with some drinking mixes involved. You make drinks for your patrons ~ though the mechanic is dull by the 10th time of making the basic drinks, there's no real reason (that I've found) to mix any of the advanced stuff outside of the quest drinks.Occasionally you get to write quests, which your patrons take off (not off of) the quest board, and then they wax poetic about how they could approach the quest, and you then mix drinks based off (not off of) their summaries. Doing this, you'll influence their fates, and the outcomes of the quest, perhaps you help them slaughter entire monsters, perhaps you'll help them write a new novel based on (or off, but never OFF OF) their experiences?It is all very charming, there's a demo available on Steam, or you could get it off (but not off of, have I laboured this point enough yet?) Steam, to have a look at how the introduction plays out. It never gets any more complicated than that, and that's fine, this is very much a relationships game, a book to chill with as you listen to people's stories  in a game world. What I think is missing, is a codex or lore-dump for the history and mythical elements of the world ~ you do get a fantastic journal with recipes, character information and whatnot and a world map, but a readily available encyclopedia or something of the sort would be great to find information from.Additionally, on my first playthrough there was no option to skip previously read text, doesn't seem to be any option to do so on when you complete the game unfortunately.I completed the game with the best ending; is this a revolutionary game? Maybe not, but it is cute, and has a nice story to tell, and sometimes that's all we need as we take a break from other, more intense stuff, and that's okay too. The ending is fairly abrupt, however, which isn't ideal, and the conflict point between "you" and one of the characters is a bit weak, and resolves in a sort of sophomoric way.Overall if you're a fan of the genre, I'd definitely have a peek, it's a decent effort but not without several flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals of Tavern Talk are fantastic. Each character in the game is unique and distinct in their design, fitting perfectly with the game's charming theme. You'll spend most of your time looking at and interacting with just a few screens, but they are updated with new items frequently enough to keep things from getting stale.The game's music and sound effects enhance the cozy atmosphere of the tavern. Some dialogue is accompanied by fitting sound cues, the sound of pouring and mixing drinks is satisfying, and the background music perfectly complements the game's setting.Without giving away any spoilers, I can say that even after almost five hours of playtime, I still feel like I'm just scratching the surface. The story is engaging, and your decisions significantly impact how it progresses, making each playthrough feel unique.The majority of the gameplay is story-focused. However, you'll also spend a lot of time mixing drinks for your patrons, collecting rumors, and posting quests. The game offers a plethora of activities that keep you engaged and contribute to the overall narrative. If you are someone who enjoys world building and lore, the game is full of entries for you to read.Tavern Talk offers significant replayability with multiple story paths and outcomes based on your decisions. This encourages multiple playthroughs to explore different storylines and character interactions.The user interface is intuitive and easy to navigate. Mixing drinks, posting quests, and interacting with patrons is straightforward, contributing to the game's overall enjoyable experience. My only complaint would be that the map screen, which as far as I can tell is a completely optional screen used for world building and lore, is a little confusing to navigate.During my playthrough, the game ran smoothly with no noticeable bugs, performance issues, or crashes. The developers have clearly put effort into creating a polished and stable game.If you enjoy story-focused games, not being the main character, chill vibes, top-tier dialogue, and great art, then Tavern Talk is a perfect game to pick up. The combination of engaging visuals, an impactful story, and unique gameplay elements that really make you feel like you are a tavern keeper makes it a standout experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually play visual novels, but the idea of playing an Innkeeper in a D&D-themed game was too much to resist. This game is so, so wholesome. Rather than your words changing the course of the game, it's the drinks that you make for your patrons. It's a lovely, cozy game to play without stressing about anything. The gameplay is beautiful, but simple, you never leave your tavern - I actually hope that someone makes a more adventure-based RPG where you can leave your tavern, because I would have loved to see the world that was described to me and join some of the quests. I know the point is that the Innkeeper can't/won't because of their past, but it would be a cool thing to do in another game. I guess I want a D&D tavern simulator xDI have one small complaint about the drink for the quest "The Dead Parade." It's impossible to create the  Charisma and Defense drink. I tried multiple times with the two infusions that could be used, and could not make this drink at all. I think it's a bug, so I'd love to see that fixed because I want to know what the other result would be for that quest. Fable, Neil, and Melli deserve the world.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Coffee Talk, or really any visual novel, and you enjoy D&D-esque fantasy romps, then Tavern Talk should hit the spot! With beautiful visuals, a delightful soundtrack, and (eventually) compelling storyline, you'll be magically compelled to order another round! But more seriously, it's a very cute game. It took a bit longer than I'd expected for the story to really grip me, and there's a bit of inconsistencies in the storytelling, but all in all, definitely worth the price. (Caveat: I got it on discount during the launch period, so factor that in as you will.) I also love the diversity of characters! It's rare to see a game with such a wide variety of characters - not just good or pretty characters, but different body types, disabilities, and preferences. (My favorite is the swamp lady. ^^) I'll definitely be following this studio to see what else they come up with!
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Words cannot describe how bone-shattering hard I feel in love with this game!! The characters are all extremely charming with a far healthier take on common TTRPG stereotypes (i.e. edgy rouge, etc) where everyone is immediately treated with the respect they deserve from a truly accepting Y/N Innkeeper. The dialogue with the characters is very natural and they all bounce off of each other with as much fluidity as a river. What I think helps out the best in this case is the fact that no one spoon feeds you lore about certain areas of the map like Y/N is a sheltered monk and instead talk normally about the continent like how Americans would mention certain states in small talk. Instead the game chooses to handle world building by having little notes in the map tab that are completely optional to read. This the player isn't overwhelmed by a random exposition drop and can choose to learn as much of the world at their own pace or completely ignore the world building in favor of just playing the game.The art style matches the tone and narrative remarkably well with the character designs being peak 10/10 that match the character's vibes perfectly.I've heard people complain how often you make certain drinks for certain characters but that's actually something I will defend till my final breath. I say this because realistically a regular at any establishment will have developed an attachment to a certain menu item(s) and come back solely to experience the comfort of something they find pleasant and enjoyable. If you don't believe me then I dare you to go to a restaurant/fast food place you visit regularly and try not to order your "usual" for a month straight (while also not reordering the menu item(s) you ordered before).The drink recipes are easy to follow and even though there are numerous drinks that serve similar purposes there is usually enough subtlety in a character's specific needs and recipe descriptions to warrant a careful observation and mild concern whenever I fill out an order and wait for their feedback. I'm sure most people are going to complain about the lack of an ability to fail an order but that is something people can get over as I doubt many people would actually take pleasure in intentionally failing for reasons other than getting a 100% completion status.All in all, if you want a cozy game that's relaxing visually, narrative, and audibly with plenty of characters to hyper fixate on, then I highly recommend slapping Gentle Troll with an Andrew Jackson (guy on $20 bill) *\(^~^)/*

_childDocuments_.review: I was admittedly looking forward to this game as it advertised itself as being similar to the likes of Coffee Talk and VA-11-Hall-A. I even tried the demo and liked it initially. However, the actual drink-making portion of this game is nothing like Coffee Talk or VA-11-Hall-A. You don't get to experiment with different recipes, as every single drink must tie to a predefined recipe. You only get a grand total of five recipes to start with incredibly basic, simple requirements to make, and the game basically makes it child's play to determine what drink is needed, as you literally cannot give the wrong drink or the game won't progress. It took about 2-3 hours for me to get a different drink recipe besides the five, because they're all provided by the NPCs you meet. Why does an innkeeper/bartender need an NPC to give them new drink recipes? Why can't I just experiment with what I already have to unlock them?There's also a "quest board" system where you assemble quests for other NPCs based on rumors you obtain while talking to the characters, but like the drinks, you're railroaded into making quests only when you have enough matching rumors to actually make a quest, so there's no failure involved at all seemingly, and it's incredibly obvious which clues fit together.It seems like Tavern Talk relies on the NPC interactions and storylines to really carry it as a game, and to be honest, compared to the games that inspire it, I don't feel it accomplishes this with the cast it has. The characters don't have strong enough introductions or personalities to make me interested in them, and their designs are pretty bog-standard fantasy character designs.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully crafted visual novel experience with an inspiring fantasy story, set in a D&D style universe, with stunning diverse characters that we follow as we craft them drinks as they navigate through adventures and their personal relationships. This is a very laid back game with minimal and easy gameplay, so if you're not looking for a more relaxed experience, this might not be for you. I loved this game, I adored the characters (I relate to Fable quite a bit and might have shed a tear during one of their scenes), and I would love for there to be a sequel/another similar game made by this lovely group of people. My only suggestion would be to let people make the wrong drink, I felt the game (while I'm all for an easy experience) was a little too heavy on the hand-holding, I think it could have been fun to let the player make the completely wrong drink for the characters and have some different consequences from that. Other than that, it was a wonderful experience, and I know I'll replay it again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun cozy experience, with an exciting finale.If you enjoy games like Coffee Talk or VA-11 HALL-A this game is perfect for you!The art is very pretty, with lots of different facial expressions, even though they don't fit 100% of the time with what is said.Every character has his own unique music theme.It is pretty long for this kind of game, but the writing is good and the characters enjoyable, so the length wasn't an issue.All in all I enjoyed my time with this game and would be excited to play a sequel to this game, or even another game in the same world.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game to just relax and play in the evenings. Very resemblant of a storybook with a bit of interaction choosing innkeeper dialogue, and picking which drinks to mix for your patrons adventures. Replay-ability: There is some replay value in going back and choosing a different option of drink or words to see what happens but other then that its moreso like rereading a book.Graphics: Very charming, I love this art style and the "cozy" look of games in general.Dialogue: All of the npcs are their own unique characters and personalities which is great. Theres someone for everyone to like. Like Rogues? Theres a couple. Like anxious-ridden characters? Oh boy is there one for you!Music: It has some nice queues when different characters show up or different events happen. But I woulda loved more tavern music ambiance and variety.Price: Again this is very similar to an interactive storybook, and It seems to be a long storybook. So I'd be inclined to say its  a fair price given the cost of books nowadays. If you think the price is too steep - wishlist it and buy it on sale. Definitely give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A conditional thumbs up from me.While I enjoyed my play-through and thought it was worth the price, it's worth noting that this isn't really a game as such. There's not really any game-play here -- the drink mixing and quest composing "mini-games" are trivial and soon done by rote -- this is basically a story told through character dialogues that you click your way through. Occasionally you'll get to make a choice between two different solutions to a problem, but not in a way that really affects the overall story -- you'll just get one of two different variants of the same story beat. The story is nothing amazing, but works well enough for what it is, even if the ending isn't particularly strong. The presentation is strong though and makes this an enjoyable piece of "cozy fantasy." Recommended if you want to curl up with a fantasy story told through nice music and endearing character designs, but if you're looking for something with more interactivity or some form of challenging or interesting game-play this isn't it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Hello there.This game, may I say, it's a wonder.The art style is captivating, the characters are unique and easy to relate too, and the gameplay makes you ponder every time you make a drink.It's also incredibly emotional, I must have cried multiple time in my days of playing it.I cannot list any more reasons due to possible spoilers but I strongly recommend it.
