_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for 79 minutes and that was enough for me to have an opinion on it.The game has lots of positive reviews and running a tavern in a DnD inspired fantasy visual novel, intrigued me, but it disappointed me in many ways.Let me explain, in listing my positives and negatives:Positives:It's a pretty looking game visually.It runs very well, is fluid graphically, has very little demands on gaming hardware - it ran on average, around 760 FPS on my computer.The in game music is nice and quite atmospheric.Negatives:Video resolution:The highest is 2560x1440p.  No ultrawide  or 4k support.  In 2024!Woke Politics: I'm asked to confirm my pronouns at the beginning of the game, or I can't proceed! Character dialogue: Is by a text box at the bottom of the screen - you can click the mouse each time to progress each element of dialogue, or you can click the autoplay button.Could the creators not implement a more interesting and engaging way to interact with the characters, than a dialogue text box!? While focused on reading all the dialogue in the text box, you also miss the animations of the character you are engaging with, and that brings me on to my next point.Character animations:  They are facial only, and limited in variation, if you even see them whilst reading the dialogue!There is so much that could have been done here.  The characters were not brought to life, they were just like slightly animated cardboard cutouts.The Drinks Crafting:Nice interface but stupidly easy as there's diagrams for each drink and it seems in my limited play time, that you can't create a drink for someone unless it's specified by a recipe.In summary:The game is boring, the character stories aren't interesting and rather predicable in their outcome.There is no real adventure or excitement with the quests.Character animations are very limited, if you even see them from reading the text.As a note: The first character, Fable, is pathetic.  I felt rather like a mental health counsellor with that character., their story was so depressing, and that's the first character in the game!I would struggle to be honest, to call this an actual game.  It doesn't go much further than point and click.  However, it seems some people are so easily pleased by a a game called 'cozy', they don't see beyond that.

_childDocuments_.review: Having only played for an hour and a half, I feel confident and secure in saying this game is a wonderful experience. It brings a cozy, colorful, and charming atmosphere to life with its intriguing dialogue--of which you get many choices to become a part of the fantasy--as well as the enriching stories and adventures we get to participate in from a different side, from behind the tavern bar. The most comparable experience to playing this game is to read a cozy fantasy novel, which this game essentially already is but in a different format. What is most striking and memorable to me is how relatable the characters are; I saw parts of myself in them and actively connected to everything about them while playing. I'm very excited to keep playing this game and to explore it as much as I can.

_childDocuments_.review: Tavern Talk is largely what it purports to be; a visual novel with some fun drink mixing game play loops. (Yep, there is more than one ending!)I found myself getting emotional (positive) at some character interactions and how the story played out. If visual novels with lovable characters, witty banter, mixed in with profoundly deep and emotional conversations are your thing, get this game. Now the 'game play' is on the minimal side, mostly you have some dialogue choices, and what drinks you mix up effect certain outcomes, but again; this is a visual novel. The story, the characters, and dialogue are the key factor here. I would say it is definitely worth it's price. Highly recommend!!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was immediately pulled into drink-making visual novels thanks to titles like "Coffee Talk" and "VA-Hall-1A", and especially as someone with a love of high-fantasy, I've been eyeing Tavern Talk since its initial announcement trailer!After finally playing through the full game, I knew one specific thing--I HAD to hear these characters voiced. And so, over many months, I had created a livedub project with friends to not only get to share this game with an audience, but to also provide an entertaining creative outlet, as well!Suffice to say, all of the positives of this game shined even brighter as voices were given to each character! The writing and characterization of each patron was executed wonderfully, the overarching plot was an enchanting mix of comedy and drama, and best of all, by the final act, everyone was absolutely enthralled with the story, the characters, and the world as a whole.Add on the additional facets of a brilliantly-scored soundtrack and an expressive art design (both in the backgrounds and character sprites), and it all comes together to create a storytelling experience that one will never forget!If you're a fan of Dungeon and Dragons, and ESPECIALLY character-driven dramas, you owe it to yourself to check this brilliant gem of a game! I very much look forward to seeing what this team creates in the future! Hail and well-met, Gentle Troll!

_childDocuments_.review: A Charming, Cozy Narrative ExperienceTavern Talk is a delightful and cozy game that invites you into a charming medieval world where storytelling is the main focus. As the Inkeep, you engage with an array of unique characters, each with their own tales to tell, personality and flaws, creating a unique and yet immersive experience.GameplayThe gameplay is simple yet engaging, focusing primarily on conversations. You'll listen to stories, ask questions, and guide the flow of dialogue to learn more about the world and Characters. It’s less about action and more about choices, making it perfect for players who enjoy narrative-driven games and choices with impact your guests. The dialogue system is intuitive, and the branching conversations offer depth to keep things interesting without being overwhelming.Graphics and SoundThe hand-drawn art style is beautiful, creating a warm and welcoming atmosphere that perfectly suits the tavern setting. The sound design and music further enhance the cozy vibe, with soft medieval tunes playing in the background, making the world feel alive.In short:Unique and charming conceptEngaging narrative with branching dialoguesGorgeous hand-drawn art styleRelaxing and cozy atmosphereFinal Thoughts:If you’re looking for a laid-back, story-driven game with charming characters and a cozy medieval vibe, Tavern Talk is a fantastic choice. It’s perfect for unwinding with a hot tea and getting lost in the tales of this Perfectly crafted world.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh. My. Gods. If you enjoyed Coffee Talk + its sequel (or if you just enjoy fantasy-like games), I recommend this game highly. Not only are there some cute easter eggs regarding characters, but the plot overall had me wanting to come back to my computer constantly to finish it. I would say a minor critique I'd have is the overall assembly for drinks, however given the complexities of the infusions and drink-influencing-plot decisions, I could see why the devs chose to keep it as simplistic as they could. I also really liked how the Innkeeper is not a well-rounded/solid advice-giver MC in this game (as compared to CT/CT2:H+B). instead, we're more flawed and are more integrated in the other characters' lives as they pass through our tavern. The price for the game is somewhat reasonable considering the amount of plot divergences and playtime, however I would say wait for a sale to play if you're a little iffy on the price.

_childDocuments_.review: ngl i think u can tell i got this game 4 the ghost, stayed 4 the story i unexpectedly enjoyed and characters i didn't know i'd get attached to (despite rly loving certain dnd actual play podcasts, that was dumb on my end LMAO should've figured it'd vibe). what i was most concerned about in this game (getting polly Right) turned out to be a non-issue as she is perf and would definitely try to bump up any game's rating immediately. pleased that i got 2 like it divorced of monprom franchise, even gladder that i got to see my wife. i have Cerebral Palsy so traditional gaming is a bit of an issue for me;  this is why i tend to enjoy visual novels over the more traditional games, and while i understand that able-bodied people might take umbrage with the lack of meat to the gameplay (and even i wished i could've served different drinks every now and then, altho me n fable r trans autistic buds who want the same ♥♥♥♥ Every Time), for me i enjoy that the plot is basically going to continue on no matter what, as someone who's really struggled to play some games or even had to drop them 4 lack of accessibility to me. i could tell that Minthie was either written by someone disabled themselves or who knows someone disabled irl, as a wheelchair user myself. i rly appreciated her dialogue and the magical ways she had 2 deal w her own disability (and as someone whose wheelchair has had 2 go over cobblestones b4 yeah they r not the most convenient go off :/). i thought this game was quite cute and nice, and will be playing again. :) coming from MonProm fandom, i do wish there were romance options, but that's ok. this still scratched a v nice itch for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute visual novel that captures the essence of being an innkeeper in a fantasy RPG. All the characters have very distinctive and memorable personalities. You're tasked to make specific drinks, with there only being potentially a choice between two different goal recipes for quests, which then goes on to determine the outcome of the quest. Other than wanting a little more gameplay personally, it's all very neat and I have been enjoying the story quite a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game to come out for awhile and I wasn't disappointed. The levity from the beginning was a breath of fresh air as you, the Inn Keeper, served adventurers that were soon to be regulars. The concept for this game is sound and very unique. I was interesting to see how things played out and to get the aftermath information for completed quests. The interplay between characters is really well done and the backstories believable. _childDocuments_.review: Tavern Talk is such a beautiful game. _childDocuments_.review: This was a very lovely game!I like Visual novels, but I wasn't sure how I felt about the idea of being a character that can only do so much for the plot, considering I am roleplaying as an NPC. I had seen games with similar concepts that didn't click with me.Luckily, this game passes that test with flying colours!The gameplay isn't hard. Is easy to make potions, in part due to the fact that you can only make drinks you have a recipe for (aka not mixing random things and having a failing drink due to that;) this was something I didn't mind, finding it cozy and enjoyable. The mechanic to make quest felt a little bit wasted; the clue all have the same colours/designs, and you cannot make a quest unless is the right papers. I feel toggling with some of these options could create some different difficulties if they were interested in implementing said idea.Regardless, I don't feel there is any issue about this because the character and the story carry the show. I was fearing that because it was all dialogue without seeing the characters do anything, it could turn boring, to not said the fact that I wasn't sure if I would find the characters/conversations dull; but I was luckily mistaken. The characters are dripping with personality and ways to approach conversation are so fascinating; new discoveries and phases of the characters are discovered constantly, in a way that feels natural and appropriate with the story. The lore is also incredibly rich and fascinating, I recommend getting the lorebook, this world is worth immersing on it. I do recommend not checking the lore book until you had reached at least an ending, there are spoilers.Is not a very complex game, but I feel it doesn't have to be; is a nice, very heartwarming experience that I feel is better going blind and letting surprise you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: An overall amazing visual novel!!Pros: - beautiful art! : from the drinks to the tavern interior to the character designs, everything looks amazing!- characters+character design: I was invested in the stories of most if not all of the characters and I loved how they all played a part in the story. The different emotion animations and music themes were a nice touch as well. Baya is the best character btw :)- writing: the writing is mostly engaging and fun! There were some funny dialogue options as well. Some parts were a little cheesy, but I didn't mind- plot: it kept me engaged and wanting to know what would happen next. I stayed up until 4 AM to finish the game b/c I thought I accidentally sen† everyone to their untimely deaths lol....Things to keep in mind/Cons:- when they say it's a visual novel, it's definitely a visual novel. this is a very text-heavy narrative game, which I don't mind, but keep it in mind if u don't usually play visual novels. - the drink-making mechanic is pretty simple+easy. You just pour different amounts of liquids together and occasionally add a special ingredient. I personally would've wanted more involved drink-making, but that's just the cooking game-lover freak within me speaking. The drink-making is pretty well incorporated into the story, but I'm not sure just how much the drinks affect different outcomes. I also want more drinks to make!! - the text is way too small sometimes. There's an option to make the text bigger in settings, but even then I was straining to read many things within the game, especially inside the book, and I have no problems with my vision in real life. - the backstory of the tavern keeper (you) is kind of random and dumped onto the player out of nowhere imo. It made the ending feel rushed and left me a little unsatisfied. - extensive lore: the world building and lore is crazily detailed, which can be both good and bad at times. There were a ton of different terms and concepts that even at the end of the game I couldn't really remember or explain to you. However, this works to make you feel like you're definitely a tavern keeper with decades long experience. I wish there was a dictionary or something though to make me less confusedOverall:Awesome game! Buy this if you love reading, visual novels, and fantasy. I'm glad this was my first steam purchase :)

_childDocuments_.review: This cute little game doesn't offer the most compelling gameplay, and feels more like a visual novel with some minigames, but it certainly cares about your choices (or it's very good at making it seem that way), and the interactivity does break up the events just enough to provide a stimulating experience, at least for me.What I need to stress for anyone who feels like it might not be for them based on that description is that the writing is remarkable. It's not particularily clever or flowery, but you can tell that it really comes from the heart, and it offers vulnerable and real emotions and experiences in a way that is more grounded than one might expect from a fantasy game. If you need to take a break from hiding from your own emotions, then considder just sitting down and opening up to this charming and silly, but profound and heartfelt series of personal stories. Spoilers for a single snippet of dialogue below, I wan't to let the game speak for itself too:[Talking about a deity]Innkeep: "A reflection of what we believe deth to be. Death itself. He could be annything."Innkeep (cont.): "What would you like him to be? What hopes do you have?"Caer (fierce warrior): "I hope he's kind"Melli (10yr old detective): "Me too"Innkeep: "Then, I think he's kind. Maybe we should follow his example."

_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Starting off, I'd like to say I streamed this game and read everything aloud, so my playtime may be more or less than final for 1 (one) run-through of the game! I didn't restart or anything (and almost forgot to save, thank you auto-save!) I did receive a code for free after I played the demo - I wanted to play this game of my own free will, I wasn't paid to say or do anything specific! The TL;DR if you're considering purchasing Tavern Talk: If you like reading, visual novels, queer representation, DND style characters, deeply enriching and emotional dialogue between characters, and not to mention a unique visual style, you'd enjoy this game! It is about 90% reading and 10% drink making. The drinks you make and actions have consequences that affect the characters' lives, quest outcomes, and dialogue experience. You should get around 20 or so hours of gameplay, and definitely more if you want to re-do some runs (You will. You will want to re-do the run :) Haha...ha...) I will say, it is a visual NOVEL. I skimmed through some reviews a few weeks ago and was surprised to see people saying it was "long winded", or that there was a lot of text and little gameplay. A typical visual novels' gameplay is usually JUST reading, if there's any added gameplay other than choosing verbal responses it is usually secondary or even tertiary. This is pretty standard for most visual novel style games. I'll say again, if you like reading, this is a good game for you! END OF TL;DR REVIEW it is now time for me to gush about Tavern Talk. I adore this game. I adore the developers who made this. They very clearly love their characters, they love representation, and I feel extremely fulfilled having played this game to its fullest (well, just one run - I'm working my way up to the 2nd!) The writing is fantastic. The comedic timing of everything is hilarious, and the characters feel real. They have flaws and positive points and each has different feelings and quirks, and respond to events differently than each other. I am a crybaby, so the sad parts made me cry. That is something I wasn't super prepared for going into this game, so I will say - This is not ONLY wholesome moments. There are stakes. If you're a crybaby like me, this game will make you cry (happy or sad tears? Who knows! ;) )The character design is probably my favorite part. As an artist, everyone stands out on their own and also fits in perfectly as a cast/ motely crew. One of the artists was personally in my chat for much of my streaming playthrough of the game and was a delight the entire time (also stronger than anyone - you have to be to sit through 7 hours straight of me yapping). The little details of each characters' appearance, animations, and how they express themselves was extremely enriching to the experience. I could go on FOREVER. I'd like to leave you with this - Please try this game out. If you're even moderately interested in the characters, or the story at large, it is a worthwhile experience. I liken it to an interactive novel (which, you know, is what a visual novel... is...haha) and this one is definitely worth a read/ play. Thank you for reading if you've gotten this far! I hope you enjoy Tavern Talk as much as I have, and I hope the devs continue to make more content/ more games like it <3

_childDocuments_.review: I, like so many others, was very lucky to see the development of this game through dev posts in the Discord. It has been a lovely journey seeing it built from ground up and participating in idea discussions (like the appearance of the drinks!). The developers poured (hehe) their hearts into this incredible game, making it a quick cemented staple in my visual novel repertoire.I highly encourage anyone interested in fantasy VNs to pick this one up, at any time. Tavern Talk has successfully avoided the common issue that plagues VNs: uninteresting characters with uninteresting convos. I felt that each character had a distinct personality, not only by behavior, but stylized form of speech. With a full cast that Tavern Talk employs, it is a daunting task to perfect, and the writing team nailed it.The evolving design of the Innkeeper's tavern was delightful to see progress, with little reminders permeating through the game from past events. That touch of detail is appreciated! It felt like a real, lived in tavern by not only the Innkeeper, but the adventuring guests who come and go and the world they live in.My few personal downsides (that the developers have announced in the discord prior to me creating this review) are:* No auto-skip button for achievement hunting/visiting events not previously seen* The "rumors" were a little too easy to match. The devs did announce having a randomized system and an easy mode for those that want to enjoy the game with ease An unaddressed gripe I have (I do not know if this unlocks after finishing the game, I am currently in the begging of Act 3) is the lack of a main menu gallery. While we have the descriptions in the Innkeeper's journal of the characters, it would be nice to have previous events, full character design (you know, for cosplay and fanart purposes), scenes, visible from the main menu like a general VN would have. They did mention that there will be a future tab where we can see the heroic trinkets in full view within the Innkeeper's journal, so I think I can live with that for now.All in all, this is a solid 10 in my book. I look forward to what follows as far as this game or future games by Gentle Troll. Please support them, as they are a wonderful group who are actively invested in what the players encounter, think, and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game without really looking at it or the reviews - I saw that it was about mixing drinks in a fantasy tavern, thought it was a cool concept, and just went for it since it was part of the summer sale. VNs aren't really my thing, so if you're a hardcore fan of visual novels than this review might not be very useful for you.I thought the game was fun. It was well written, though I could see a lot of the twists coming ahead of time as things were a bit trope-y. I felt like the drink mixing minigame distracted from the flow of the narrative in some of the later portions, and sometimes it felt like a bit of a chore, but it was a neat concept. Over all, I'd say the game is worth the money if you want a light and easily digestible story.

_childDocuments_.review: Please play this game, it a beautiful cozy game turned into a??? Life lesson? Game I DON'T KNOW, all I know is I just finished it, I'm sobbing, I love my patrons and I love making my magical little drinks and I'm going to be recommending this to everyone I know. _childDocuments_.review: Go on a D&D inspired adventure in this visual novel. Known as Innkeep to the people of Asteria, you own a popular tavern in the area. This isn’t just any old tavern, because the drinks you create are magical and can boost different stats of your customers - possibly changing their fate. You’ll get to know and befriend many different individuals by listening to the stories of their many adventures. Not to mention, the rumors they discuss can be turned into new quests. Watch as these characters, and even yourself, grow and form new bonds with each other. To begin, I enjoyed Tavern Talk way more than Coffee Talk (I still haven’t gotten around to Coffee Talk 2). The art style and graphics were absolutely beautiful. Creating the drinks was a lot of fun and it was nice that there were recipes to help you create new drinks. I will admit, it got a bit boring that the customers would always request the same drinks and you could get away with making the original recipes throughout most of the game. I also enjoyed creating the quests, but I wish they had been a bit more challenging to formulate. The quests that went together were written on the same sheets of paper, and I would have enjoyed the challenge of having to read them and pair them on your own. The story was definitely interesting and I felt like I was the dungeon master of a D&D game. I felt more of a connection to the characters and genuinely cared how their story progressed. Now, I don’t know if I did something wrong, but I thought it was way too long - clocking in at about 18 hours for one play-through. There were some conversations I felt were unnecessary and some of the days could have been a lot shorter. I won’t spoil anything here (I’d like to hear your thoughts if you played), but I was so disappointed in the Innkeepers story! One of the things I really enjoyed about Coffee Talk and Tavern Talk is that you were sort of a mysterious figure with no background, but as the story came to a close there was a twist in who you really were and why you were so important. I thought of so many things, and was ready for the big twist - only to be severely let down. There were also a couple of things I thought could have enhanced the experience a lot more. As the Innkeep, you were gifted with different things from certain character quests. These would appear in your tavern as decorations. Some of them were difficult to tell where they had been placed - maybe if they had zoomed in or had a pop-up saying you had received this item, it would have been a nice touch. I also loved the intro to the game and wish the ending could have ended with a similar cut scene. All in all, I enjoyed Tavern Talk and would gladly recommend it to those out there who enjoy visual novels and fantasy worlds.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthrough and here are my initial thoughts, such a beautiful little gem of a game. Tavern talk is a very cozy fantasy visual novel. Some of them reminded me of memories of almost forgotten D&D game nights. The (magic) drink mixing was fun. My only complaint is that it gets a bit repetitive between the important quest drinks, I would have preferred that there would be a little more variation instead of making the same favorite drink over and over. But then that is typical for a regular in a bar always ordering the same, so I suppose I can live with that. I would wholehearted recommend this to anyone who likes visual novels, dungeons & dragons and the choice-matters kind of game. Although Tavern talk is a unique game in itself, if it were a drink it would be a base mix between  Dungeons & Dragons and Strange Horticulture, top it up with Coffee talk and a pinch of The Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood, and voila! a very charming and magical drink. _childDocuments_.review: When I heard of a successor to Coffee Talk, I maintained a skeptic optimism: those games have a firm hold on my heart, and while I'd love for the genre to expand on the concept, I feared anything else might dilute the formula. Imagine my surprise when Tavern Talk instead perfected the blend.So what ingredients gave us this potent product?1. A hefty dose of humor. The wit in this game hit every time. Each line not only expands on the world's lore, but exposes an additional layer to the character's heart – all whilst cracking you up. I can count on more than one hand the times I audibly cackled whilst reading. These writers know not only how to time their comedy, but how to arrange characters in such a way that it allows for dynamic conversations time and time again. The sign of good dialogue, for me, is when one person could take all sorts of lines out of context, present them to another person, and the other could guess with ease which character said what line. Give me any conversation in Tavern Talk and I assure you, I'd ace any dialogue guessing game – it's that distinct.2. A sprinkling of aestheticism. How could anyone not take even the slightest glimpse at this game without dropping their jaw? The artwork stuns, even when still, let alone when the characters maintain constant motion. They each felt so alive – including when they were sitting in silence. The number of expressions I screenshotted for the pure amusement they brought me has my computer's memory clogged, to say the least. These artists understood that staying in one location required making a home players wanted to dwell in. One made all the cozier by the countless trinkets you continue collecting. And the characters? Please. Minthie walked through the door and I unabashedly whistled. Grace has a vice grip on my soul, the way her clothes and eyes seem to radiate from her skin. Even Baya's design should win awards for ingenuity alone. Artists, y'all outdid yourselves. The musicians ought to be lauded too: each character's theme embodied them wholeheartedly (though I did feel that utilizing them every time they spoke occasionally clashed with their conversation's tone).3. A pinch of important decisions. While the game lacks any "secret routes" (ordinarily obtained through wrong orders or downright belligerent behavior), the Quest System does create considerably diverging timelines. Yes, there are technically "correct" choices, but I felt a genuine tug on my heart every time I was presented with a choice. Because I cared for these characters, I cared how well they fared in their quests! To have our potions directly impact their outcomes was a BRILLIANT way to let us feel important in this world, even from a distance.4. A heavy helping of lore. Worldbuilding? In MY cozy coffee sim??? It's more likely than you think. Imagine my surprise to find a whole trove of it right from the get-go! Each piece of information unearthed throughout the game made this world feel all the more alive, far beyond the walls of our establishment. How I long to go exploring on this planet in search of countless more mysteries and fantastical creatures. Not only did the world's intriguing nature aid in amplifying the game's quests, but it exacerbated the impact of (shockingly twist-ridden and, at times, poignantly dark) storyline all the more. I did NOT foresee the end to any act, nor have I seen anything akin to those surprises in this genre, but boy were they a welcome surprise.5. A hard-hitting message. From the outset, I found myself aching at the struggles and aspirations of these characters. From Fable's indecisiveness about her story's future to the Innkeeper's inability to absolve his past sins, each second of reflection stirred my heart. These characters – while undeniably dynamic to comical degrees – have a tendency to hit home with relevant and poignant insecurities that every player will face. The writing often forced me to face my own issues and ponder whether I was on an adventure to end them or indulge them. Thank you for the unexpected call to action, devs. What then, if anything, waters down its potency?1. Underwhelming orders. No, not the drinks themselves. I found them seamless to make, and even discovering what combination of ingredients and infusions were needed to make more challenging drinks excited me. Alas, you'll scarcely ever need these late-game elixirs, as the patrons ask for the same drinks. Over and over and over again. Basically, everyone has one basic drink that that they'll always ask for - UNLESS they're embarking on a quest. By the endgame, it became tedious to make drinks at all because I never had much of an incentive to experiment outside of the original lineup (once I'd gotten the achievement for making every drink/using every infusion in the game). I wish characters would have had more unique requests, especially since we couldn't give them the wrong drinks...except at first? That confused me, considering one achievement demanded a mismade drink.2. Overwhelming conversations. Listen, I am a novelist – and an overwriter at that (if you couldn't tell from this review alone). While I wildly enjoyed just about every character in the game, barring Iniko, the bits typically felt like they overstayed their welcome just a tad too long. Even when speedreading the dialogue, these people ramble. A LOT. Which is to be somewhat expected in a Visual Novel, but some paring down would have helped the pacing. You never want to sacrifice such clever writing's impact because you've strained your audience's stamina. This was highlighted all the more by the lack of any fast-forward option (or at least one that was apparent to me) for previously-read text. I love 100%-ing VNs, but I would give myself carpal tunnel clicking through everything a second time around. Devs: if that could be included in a QoL update down the line, I would love you forever.So should you play Tavern Talk? Absolutely. If you're down to fall in love with one of the most wholesomely-zany casts introduced this year, you're going to have a good time. Tune out the troubles of the world and sink your teeth into this one instead. It will refresh you tenfold – just as every elixir ought to.Who should NOT play Tavern Talk? Only if you're a gameplay-first player. This game's impact relies SIGNIFICANTLY on your connection to the characters, your intrigue in the story, and the awe you have in its world (both in terms of physical beauty and lore depth). If that's not your forte, then consider supporting a streamer or content creator who has walked through the game instead! Might as well tune into the adventures, even if you're not interested in executing them yourself, right?Thank you, devs, for a refreshing experience from start to finish. I sure enjoyed my stay in this tavern – and I'll be back for more adventures along the way, whenever you have further quests brewed up for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Tavern Talk is one of those games that brings you to a point of comfort, safety and wellbeing. Its art is visually stunning, with distinctive character designs that help distinguish one adventurer from the next, as well as brilliant cameos from other games such as Monster Prom.Overall, although I've not even finished Act 3, seeing the inclusivity of the cast (with many frontline characters being LGBTQIA+, disabled, or POC) throughout the game is beyond heartwarming, with important discussions had involving things like accessibility, fear, age, and overcoming one's greatest doubts. For fans of games such as Coffee Talk, this is sure to be a hit.The story flows beautifully, with well-written pacing and character development you can easily see over the course of the days you take your stand as the Innkeep - your choices matter, and it shows in such a wonderful way that it communicates a sense of purpose throughout the game beyond just taking drink orders and serving with a smile.I've been unable to put this game down for the last two days, and I guarantee I won't turn to anything else until I've finished my first playthrough - but, in the meantime? I cannot possibly recommend it enough. To the development team, kudos on a successful release and a beautiful work of art you've brought forward. To potential other innkeeps... take a second, curl up somewhere cozy, and give this one a try. Chances are, you'll like what you see.

The ending was a bit meh, and really didn't feel like much. maybe there could've been something with the sky in the window to show how the final quest was going? like the effects of the events in act 1 and 2? _childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fun cozy little game! It's perfect to come home to and just relax in a different world. _childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that is simple, enjoyable, and full of nerd culture references and jokes. From D&D to Monty Python to books and cinema, Tavern Talk is a cute and fun Visual Novel where you help adventurers find new quests and learn about their lives. While the drink making is simple, it is made all the better by having a cute little pet to give the drinks you screw up to!If you like games like Va-11 Hall-A then you will enjoy this! _childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely enjoyed this little game! It kept me entertained on a day when I wanted something fun but low-key.The characters are quirky and entertaining. Your choices affect how your customers approach their quests, and the stories they tell you afterwards.There are apparently a few different possible endings.I don't know when I'll play it again, but I really enjoyed the times I've spent with this game, and it will definitely be on my short list for days when I don't feel up to intense game mechanics, but do want some fun storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Cosy, story rich and oozing with charm. It has stellar art, music, and writing backing up a game that is centered around the unique patrons that frequent your tavern. I'm excited to see how the stories progress and what new character I'll meet.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little new to visual novels but am finding Tavern Talk very rewarding. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first play through, great game, lovable characters, I would definitely recommend this if you have played coffee talk or other games of that nature. _childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A truly interesting outside-looking-in perspective on an amazing adventure. Collecting rumors and mixing drinks is surprisingly entertaining; if you like hearing gossip that you'll (hopefully) never be involved in, this is definitely your game.Pros:- Story. Like a good tabletop campaign, there are many little details that all link together in the end - with a bang. There are multiple endings based on your choices, and the one I ended with was bittersweet and had me thinking for hours afterward.- Consequences. Your actions matter, and they matter A LOT. Making the right one could save someones life, and that's not something a lot of games (especially ones that are more visual novel in nature) offer.- TRINKETS!! Friends hang up little trinkets around the tavern with every adventure, and it's delightful.- You can pet your familiar. He's adorable.Cons:- Creativity. Admittedly I didn't experiment... at all... with the drink selection (it was important to get right, okay!!), but if you're able to mix your own drinks then that knowledge isn't made obvious. I also would've loved to access the mixing menu outside of patron requests just to mess around in what could've been a fun little sandbox, but oh well.- With regards to trinkets, you don't actually get an up-close look at them, which is agonizing. People bring you trinkets and they appear in the background, but I would've at least liked to look at them close up before they get placed somewhere across the room. Sometimes they even get placed out of frame (as the camera focuses on the patron you're talking to) and I'd have to wait for the day to end before seeing it.Personal gripes (not cons but things I would've liked to see):- We could've been busier!!!!! I know it's more of a story focused game with solid main characters, but I would've liked hosting more people than the ones our character either already knew or the ones that would eventually get involved in the story. Where are my fellow nameless adventurers passing by? Why is the bar empty until one of the main cast comes in? WHERE ARE WE GETTING MONEY FROM IF THE PLACE IS EMPTY?- If we could interact more with the set, that would be cool. Lemme move around the trinkets. I'll put them in a pile.All in all it's a great game. Once I stop being sad I'll try another playthrough - and hope there's a function to skip dialogue I've already heard in New Game+, because there's a lot of worldbuilding to click through.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A charming, cozy visual novel that's perfect to play a couple of in-game days after work to de-stress. I'm only a few hours in, but the dialogue is fun and engaging, the storylines have great hooks and the characters are super interesting and lovable. The art goes hard!(I'll write more once I've finished my first playthrough, but genuinely enjoying it thus far!)After completing all endings of Tavern Talk, I gotta say I thoroughly enjoyed myself! The characters have so much heart and the story is so thoughtful and heartbreaking at times. There are a bunch of good quotes that have stuck with me since I did my first pass of the game.I desperately wish this game was longer. I want to talk to the characters for many more hours and learn even more about them and the world. Thankfully there's a lot of great insight into the world if you read the codex entries in innkeeper's binder. Maybe one day we'll see another game based in this land :')
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

I think the conversations are fun, and worth reading, but I'd prefer to have more of the text at one time and less clicking and space-barring.  I can only play about an hour or so at a time max because I get frustrated.Also, I'd really like some hot key shortcuts for making the drinks.  Maybe I am missing something and they exist but I don't think so.  It's a cute game, and I am enjoying the mystery of who the Innkeeper is. _childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of DnD and similar games like Coffee Talk this is such a lovely mix of the two. The art, the music, and the general feeling is so familiar yet wholly unique. _childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a lot of fun and the story is great! Fun choices and a slew of unique characters, great chill vibes and lovely moments. Check it out!Only "drawback" for me (whilst definitely not enough for it to be a hindrance) is that drinks get slightly repetitive over time, you tend to serve the same thing to the same character most of the time, but it doesn't really detract from the experience :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Tavern Talk, eh? Solid game. Heavily reminiscent of Coffee Talk, but building on it and doing some of its own stuff. And that's no bad thing! This game's got a damn solid ensemble cast and a captivating narrative. If you want a cozy Fantasy VN, with just a touch of more serious moments here and there, this is absolutely worth a shot.Feedback wise, I think my one real complaint is that the game doesn't really take full advantage of its branching? Both Quest making and drink selection mostly felt pretty perfunctory - while key 'going on a quest' drinks offer you a decision, most of the time you're just able to choose anything with the desired stats and nothing really changes. Even unlocking new drinks didn't really feel that exciting or engaging - they just turned into vehicles to deliver infusions through.Plus the 'quest assembly' feature, something the game touted, felt like it wasn't really a feature at all. I wasn't unlocking unique quests or picking what adventurers would go on them. It's just a slightly more convoluted step in progressing the plot.Is that enough to call this game bad? Hell no! If you liked Coffee Talk or VA-11-Hall-A you'll likely have a good time with Tavern Talk. And the recc goes double if you're a D&D junkie. I just feel that it's a few steps shy of really doing something crazy and great. It's more a comfortable, well constructed but not too adventurous game. Sometimes that fits what people want better.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Being in the role of the innkeeper and serving guests, and quests, is a thing I don't remember seeing before. Tavern management isn't new, but Tavern Talk is more about the character relations and helping shape their stories rather then actually managing a tavern.I'm only a few hours in, but every single person who has walked into the tavern has been a distinct personality and so far I can't say I outright dislike any of them. I'm really excited to see where all the stories go and how my drinks help influence them.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful blend of classic fantasy style d&d and Coffee Talk, Tavern talk was absolutely worth the wait. The characters are charming, the art is gorgeous, the soundtrack is incredible and the story so far is gripping. While I do wish there was a little more freedom with the drink mixing, I still find joy in unlocking each new drink as the game progresses. I highly recommend this game if you like cozy visual novels, fantasy stories, and good character designs. <3 (I was gifted this game by my friend who knew it was on my radar for a while, thank you friend!)
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I am in LOVE! Amazing game!! I first played the demo and was immediately hooked by the fantasy story line as well as the charming characters! I just had to buy the full game. What I didn't expect was how thorough and detailed the game really is, every interaction had a role in painting the bigger picture. The amount of hours you could spend playing in this story-based game was also a big shock. I love the way all the characters interact with each other, and how they develop themselves (I'm a sucker for good found-family type stories haha). I can also really appreciate how our own character has a big role in the game as well, as usually with story-based games your character often feels flat with little to no personality, not only do you get to learn more about the wonderful (and chaotic) characters, but you get to learn more about your own as well. The story alone made me intrigued enough to commit to the game, but the mechanics were also very clean whether that be creating drinks or collecting rumors to set up quests. After having a long day I often found myself so excited to dive into in my own little fantasy world creating drinks for my customers as they retell me their wild and grand adventures. I definitely could go on and on about this game haha! I 100% recommend this game to those looking for a charming, wacky, mysterious, heart-warming, heart-breaking, but very fulfilling game! side note: You get the most adorable familiar pet to help you make drinks...CUTEST THING EVER!!! I love Andu! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 cannot recommend enoughAbsolutely wonderful game. The writing and sound track is so endearing and pleasant. Incredibly helpful for de-stressing after a crappy day. What stands out the most is the absolute love for the genre and dnd that bleeds from every character. No one is defined by stereotypes and you truly get to see them develop into worldly people as your interactions genuinely guide them down different paths. Additionally the world building just expands upon itself. You truly feel fully immersed in your role as an innkeep and immersed in the characters lives. And whatever crisis is going onI'd honestly recommend this game to any inspiring dnd/fantasy lover Or character designers, or artists, or writer I am absolutely going to be taking my experience playing and incorporate knowledge of character creation I saw in this game into my own works. Truly inspirational Additionally the consideration for every possible person. Incredibly heart-warming to people of any background or upbringing seeing how earnestly and genuine experiences are portrayed by characters in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only a couple hours into this game and the fact that I want to create a review due to the utter love and happiness that playing it has given me in such a short amount of time should be more than enough. I am someone who loves casual representation of gender non-conforming characters and this game... very much does just that. No remarks about a girl dwarf in a beard. (Which! Is very accurate, even female dwarfs have beards! I'm so happy the game sticks true to that fact.) Cute buff wolf woman. ADORABLE non-binary elf. Every single character I have met thus far are very easy to get attached to. I will admit I was weary of picking up this game as this genre is very much hit-or-miss with making me like or care about the characters I am attending to, however for Tavern Talk I have been so engaged and in love with everyone who shows up. I'm not impatiently waiting for a character I enjoy to come back due to the sheer fact that every character has such unique personalities, outlooks, conversations, etc. They all bounce off one another perfectly and so seamlessly. The quest system very much makes it very easy for said characters to connect with one another, it is such a genuine good idea to give a nice reason to make experiences overlap. Oh gosh, and not to mention how the drinks basically are apart of character choices and fates is so awesome. I have to actually think about what drink would be worth it to create. I want to see the characters I like to succeed! It also offers a lot of replay-ability which I'm very much excited to experience upon a rerun. This game is utterly lovely and I am so so so excited to finish it. I just had to stop midway to absolutely gush about how much I'm enjoying it so far, this is the first ever review I've left on Steam too! Thank you to the writers, creators, and team for making such a casual lgbtq+ and utterly amazing game. I hope this game overwhelmingly spikes in popularity because... wow.

_childDocuments_.review: Gentle Troll keep refining themselves in this new visual novel.The writing is good, the gameplay keeps you engaged.DND chose THEIR own adventure as you are the "trapped" ancient expresive mixologist I´d come to love.But the variety of adventurers will tell you all about it for a drink.No preachines or focus about lgbt stuff, the character, story and dialog come first.

_childDocuments_.review: My thoughts after finishing the game:If you've liked similar style games in the past, (Like Coffee Talk or Va-11 Hall-A), you'll like this one a lot, as it's the same style of visual novel. While the drink making aspect of the game isn't very interesting, the rest of the game makes up for it. The characters start off seeming rather bland, stereotypical, and uninteresting, but the major ones all end up undergoing some nice character development. While it's not ground breaking writing, and the characters all still tend to fit within their archtypes, the story is nonetheless enjoyable and memorable enough to leave a lasting positive impression. It's not a game or story that will change your life, but it is in my opinion worth the time and cost, and once you get past the first few days, is surprisingly engaging. The art style is also phenomenal,  characters are visually interesting and distinctive. The soundtrack is also quite good. My only major critiques of the game are the beginning isn't super engaging, and while the idea of the different drinks changing the story mechanic is interesting, I don't get the sense that your choices actually have much of an impact what so ever on the story. I similar games reward replaying the game and making different choices, but if I'm honest I'm not sure that is the case for Tavern Talk, and I also am satisfied after one play through, and don't have a strong desire to replay the game. All in all, if you like visual novels, you probably won't be disappointed with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: what a truly wonderful game.the demo immediately hooked me, so i was waiting excitedly for full release. i am not disappointed. the characters, worldbuilding, and story are all amazing. there is quite a lot of it! there is even a character i dislike -- in a good way. i think games should have characters so diverse there's opportunity for me to not like some. this game definitely does that. gorgeous and creative designs, with gorgeous (or not-so!) and creative personalities to match. such a wide array of patrons. they not only interact with you, but with each other as well. you get to watch them form relationships. you can influence how they go about their quests with the drink you choose to serve them. however...one thing i can say i am not satisfied with is the drinkmaking. it is definitely secondary to the game, coming from someone who really enjoyed the similar title VA-11 Hall-A. it's easy. too easy. there really isn't any guesswork or experimentation involved, and there also isn't any difficulty making the drinks to balance that out. in my opinion, either one of those should have been fleshed out more. you really only get one or sometimes two choices when deciding what to serve a customer, and those choices are made VERY blatantly clear. the character might say something like, "give me something that makes me agile!" so you serve them a Swift Strike. then the next time, the same character says, "i want to feel quick on my feet!" so you serve another Swift Strike. the next time, "i need to get home fast!"... you get the picture. even if the first time you serve this character they're an established regular that says "get me the usual," they'll still come back and go "hmm... maybe something like this?" which then always ends up being "the usual." but no customers order drinks by name. it kind of feels like they had the *idea* of making you do guesswork, but not the implementation.but that's okay. it doesn't totally kill enjoyment of the game. it is a visual novel after all -- the most important part is the "novel." and it nails that. i've been telling all my friends about how much i love this game. and i think you will too.

_childDocuments_.review: Tavern TalkA simple game about running a medieval fantasy inn and tavern. You are the innkeep...and that's all that you get as a name, would have preferred being able to name myself but that's neither here nor there. The game is very simpleA customer comes in....has some words with you...usually rumors or a tale to tell....and then requests a drink. You then have to mix the drink according to what they want5 mixers....intelligence, charisma, strength, dexterity, and defense.....mixing the drinks various outcomes....adding infusions later in the game change the outcomes even further. If you botch a drink, just feed it to your purple dragon blob, Andu...also, remember to pet him, he is best dragon friendYou also have to post quests...adventurers need adventures to go on...as you talk with the numerous and colorful cast of characters, you'll pick up rumors...placing the rumors together in order creates a new quest for another character to takeIt's all very easy to grasp and fun to do...but what really makes the game is the art style, music, and the lovely charactersEvery character has something to talk about...Fable wishes to be more outgoing....Kyle is a forgetful vampire (tried to go sunbathing....forgot that sunlight blows vampires up)....Caerlin tries to curse not knowing the makers above forbid swearing in the tavern. Every character has something to tell or talk about and soon start meeting up with each other on questsThe music and art style are appealing and set the story for each character's interaction with the innkeeper...Fable's music is gentle and soft whereas Caerlin's music has a strength behind it, emphasizing her warrior appearance. The artstyle itself is colorful and vibrant, bringing life to the inn and its varied customers....even Zephir, the rogue...despite his gloomy silent outlookIt's a simple game with lots of life to it and I haven't stopped smiling when playing it
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I helped Kickstart this game and am so pleased to see it come to fruition. The TLDR: Tavern Talk is a masterpiece of interactive storytelling.Review:Tavern Talk is a breathtaking journey into a world of captivating stories and vibrant characters, set in a cozy, atmospheric environment of a medieval style tavern. This game is a refreshing blend of storytelling, role-playing, and strategic decision-making, ensuring every moment is as engaging as it is enjoyable. From the moment you start up the tavern, the richly detailed graphics and immersive sound design pull you into a living, breathing world. The tavern feels alive with the chatter of patrons, the clinking of mugs, and the occasional bard strumming a melodic tune. Every character you encounter has a story to tell, and it's these interactions that the game truly shines.The dialogue system is one of Tavern Talk's standout features. It's deep, dynamic, and incredibly well-written. Offering players a chance to shape their narrative through choices that feel meaningful and impactful. Whether you're uncovering a patron's secret, resolving conflicts, or building alliances, every conversation feels authentic and consequential. Game play mechanics are intuitively designed making it accessible for both seasoned gamers and newcomers alike. The strategic elements such as managing relationships and gaining resources for drinks add layers of complexity that keep you invested in the long term. Each decision can have far-reaching effects, leading to a variety of potential outcomes and ensuring high replay value. The game's art style is another highlight, with its beautifully crafted environments and character designs that bring the medieval/DnD setting to life. Coupled with a hauntingly beautiful soundtrack, Tavern Talk creates an atmosphere that is both nostalgic for those who played Coffee time and readers alike. Moreover, the developers have shown a keen attention to detail, filling the game with easter eggs and subtle nods to classic fantasy tropes, which will delight fans of the genre. The community aspect with players who helped kickstart the game adding their own personal touch in ways some wouldn't have thought possible, adds an additional layer of enjoyment and engagement for the player base. Tavern Talk, is more than just a game; it's an experience. It is a testament to the power of interactive storytelling and world-building. Whether you're here for the intricate plots, the strategic gameplay, or simply to enjoy the ambience of the tavern while petting Andu, Tavern Talk delivers on all fronts. It's a must-play for anyone who loves a good story. I personally can't wait to finish the game (I'm currently on Act II Scene V).

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a visually pleasing and dialogue witty game. If you ever have been fascinated with the idea of being a bartender inside the D&D world, then look no further. I have only scratched the surface of this game, but I already adore my guests/adventurers. And let's not forget how adorable Andu is!
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo and absolutely loved it - it's a wholesome adventure with a great cast of characters. I'm also a huge fan of all the (subtle) accessibility feature that makes the game easy for people that get easily distracted (like a log of the conversations) or the different shapes of the rumours to easily see which ones belong together.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Obsessed with this game. Beautiful artwork, beautiful story lines, and some wonderful characters to meet and encourage on their path. Although I still feel bad picking mean dialogue options, I'm so determined to see every ending I can, with two under my belt already. On that note, good replay-ability, and even though I'm sad I can't romance the patrons, there's definitely a wonderful appeal to being a background character in this game.PS: The Monster Prom cameo was WILD.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Never left a steam review before but I needed to gush about this game. I've waited for this games release since the demo, so of course I had to buy and play it the second it dropped. I played the entire thing in one sitting (yes, 10 hours).When I tell you the writing and characters are phenomenal I mean it. You'll be taken on a rollercoaster of emotions, from sweet peace to absolute crushing revelations. The characters are endlessly charming and hard to dislike, and the story features some very well done twists and turns that you won't see coming.The fact that your drink choices matter and characters do stay away from the tavern for the appropriate amount of days really gives weight to the anxiety your choices can bring. Did they survive? Did you make the right choice?This is only amplified towards the end where the stakes are higher than ever. I dreaded seeing the achievement for the wrong drink pop up, but I somehow managed to avoid it! The artstyle is adorable and cozy, and endlessly expressive! Theres so many cute little details in everything, from the background to the characters sprites and animations. I honestly cannot recommend it enough. If you love narrative-focused games you will love Tavern Talk. The dev team did a fantastic job! Heres hoping they'll continue to put out amazing stories like this!I think my only complaint was trying to put it down was very, very difficult!
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Very sweet and cozy game, you listen to the stories of the Adventurers visiting your Tavern, and when they want mix them drinks. During these *heh* "Talks" you will learn about rumor snippets which (if you have enough fitting ones) you will then turn into Quests these Adventurers will go on. Before the Adventurers depart, you will influence with drinks, how they will go about their Quests. Will you mix them a Drink that gives them the strength to attack the werewolf sighted by the villagers, or will you mix them something to soothe their anxiety so they can attempt a diplomatic approach. What you decide for will have an impact, be it minor or major, and it feels really satisfying, when they come back and tell about their adventures. The Characters are a quite diverse and interesting cast and their interactions bring a smile on my lips. I recommend giving this game a try, I mean there is a free Demo, it costs you literally *nothing* to try it out. Have Fun ~
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this, the concept and visual design drew me in immediately but left me feeling lied to. You do NOT create quests or tease out the secrets of your patrons, instead everything is a strict railroad with only one solution and minimal actual thought or input from the player (even for a VN). The developers are more focused on servicing their OCs than delivering an engaging story as they repetitively spout bloated paragraph after paragraph that genuinely include quips such as "cringe fail", as well as a quirky self-insert whose anxiety is her entire personality and rants about it as though noone else has ever gone through it before. If you're interested in the same concept done better check out - Affogato.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly charming and cozy visual novel filled with eclectic characters and their ofttimes zany antics.It's your job as the innkeeper to keep your customers happy, and mix-up the right drinks to help your adventurous regulars on their quests as they take on tasks big and small beyond the cozy confines of your humble tavern.Gameplay is simple and relaxing, the characters are a diverse array of personalities that will surely win you over, and there's even a demo to wet your feet in before you buy.What's not to like? Give it a spin and see if you want to run your very own mildy-magical tavern.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Help fund on Kickstarter - this game looked very promising. I really enjoyed the demo and finally got to play the full game yesterday. It's brilliant! A fun cosy game to sit in a dark room and enjoy some enthralling story and dialogue that could've been taken straight out of my DnD campaigns! (Roll for Wisdom!)Beautifully written and the art style is very charming, with the little animations that bring the characters and the environment to life. You really get engrossed in the characters' little stories, help build quests, and have a good chin-wag with the many different and often quirky patrons.Also works well on the Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't gotten very far yet but I care so much for the beginner characters. Sent them off on dangerous quests and did worry about them returning in one piece. Story is very intriguing as is the Inkeeper. Game play is pretty much visual novel. Read the story and meet a wide variety of characters. The Innkeeper is their own character and seems to have their own story to tell, will see. Not much dialogue options to choose from, the prompt rarely pops up, and hard to tell how much of a difference they make to the story. Mostly just reading through what this established Innkeeper says. Crafting is very simple, just follow the recipe, not really the main focus, more like a mini game to give a break to the narrative. There are key points where you have two different drink options to make that do affect the story and the character(s) involved. Until I do a second playthrough, it's hard to say how drastically it changes things, but for one character, it's easy to imagine how much would change if I picked a different option.At 3 hrs in, it seems very promising. Very cute. Excited to see where the story takes me.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy playing this, although I'm not the cozy-ultra as they say. Reading text on screen usually is a turnoff for me, but the writing is so good and I've laughed many times already (we all know that a offline chuckle translates into LOL online). There's so many characters that truly feel different and make me curious about what the next story beat will be for them.The game has just such a pleasant vibe and funny writing, a great experience on Steam Deck. The music also really fits and carries the atmosphere.I played the demo a while ago and it really has come a long way. Also, my friends shall call me Innkeep from now on.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only 3 hours into the game and I've fallen in love. The characters are so cute, the gameplay is pretty simple yet fun, and the animations of everything in the tavern makes the world feels so alive. I feel like I could read a whole book series just about the history of Gaia. Every new patron to the tavern excites me. Highly recommend if you enjoy Coffee Talk and other cozy visual novels
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played Dnd sense they were a kid with their family, This game was refreashing and fun. It is simple and a lot of reading but the characters all make me want to hug them and remind me of so many diffrent dnd games i have played while still feeling unique in their own way.I have not finished the game but the mystories and learning of the lore of this world through the chats with the characters is a neat way to see dnd from another point of view.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: So far got in 3 hours. I can describe this game in a few words. Charming, whimsical, and a deeply welcoming experience. Every single character is well written and each day you just never know what is coming through your door. I ADORE the little in Dnd and RPG inside jokes that are included. I think what stunned me the most is the scope. When I took a step back I realized, we are the bartender at the beginning of an EPIC quest that is slowly unfolding (or at least thats my impression). I realized how much fun it is to see the story play out not at the central key character but as the one slinging drinks and listening to these people. The potion making is a neat little mechanic that I dig and the quest creation is such a genius idea. I love that we are building quests through rumors. Overall, I'm deeply impressed but also I feel a great sense of joy playing this. RPGs tend to make you the focus as the "chosen one" or something like that. Sometimes you loose yourself in the quests and you don't always get a chance to really explore the world and lore. As an innkeeper your whole existence is about obtaining as much lore as possible.  Love it!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I can't get enough of this game. The care that has gone into the aesthetics, the lovable characters - I genuinely care about all of them so far and am so invested in seeing them grow and succeed, and the music make me feel at home. I played the demo, and am so incredibly excited that this game is somehow even more amazing upon release. If you love the cozy vibes, great stories, and feeling like you're building your own peace in a chaotic world, this is a wonderfully amazing game to curl up with. The controller option is a bonus.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: At just over an hour of playtime, I am finding the game to be quite enjoyable. You meet and talk to people, gathering their backstory. You pick up rumors from around the surrounding continent. You piece together quests for adventurers. It really all reminds me of the Epic NPC Man series by Viva la Dirt League, only you are now operating from the POV of the self-aware NPC. Highly recommend to anyone who enjoys chill vibes, mixing potions, gathering lore, or all of the above.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo when it came out, backed the game on Kickstarter, and have been eagerly awaiting the full release! I'm really excited to say that the game on release day is very polished. It looks great, runs great, the sound design is so cozy, and the dialogue has had me laughing out loud at parts. The gameplay is pretty intuitive, and the only slight downside so far is that about 1.3 hours in, it doesn't feel like enough of a challenge. It might get a little more challenging as the game goes on, though, and I also don't mind a more relaxing cozy game. It leans a little more toward cozy visual novel, and the choices you make do matter for the outcomes, which is really fun. The characters are interesting and have me wanting to play more to learn more. If you're a fan of visual novels and cozy games, I would definitely recommend giving it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game to everyone, even if you aren't particularly familiar with visual novel games. The characters are all unique and bring their own flair to the conversations. The drink-making mechanic builds reasonably to introduce new aspects and unlock more difficult and intricate recipes. The decision making system allows for replayability, and really make you think about each character you're helping. The team clearly understands and loves this genre a lot, so much so that they even poke fun at the classic tropes we have all come to know and love. Seriously, if you haven't already, GET THIS GAME!
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to be a NPC quest-giver but other people keep sending you out to hunt dragons and solve mysteries? Well then Tavern Talk is the game for you!Jokes aside, Tavern Talk is brilliantly written. The story and dialogue flow naturally, which isn't always accomplished in visual novel style games. The characters are delightful and I look forward to them showing up at the inn. The active parts aren't too mechanically driven, which is great for someone like me who focuses on the story. and gets frustrated by complicated mechanics.  I enjoy learning about the characters through conversation, though I'll admit I'd like more dialogue options with the characters. I don't know if that will become more frequent later or if the level will be consistent throughout. I'm loving playing this game and I think anyone who likes visual novels and the fantasy/D&D setting will also enjoy it. I keep seeing Tavern Talk described as a combination of Coffee Talk and Legends & Lattes and that's a fair assessment. I loved both Coffee Talk and Legends and Lattes and this game hits all those notes of familiarity while also being it's own wonderful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game for months and am so excited it's finally here! It's even more delightful than I had dreamed! The music is beautiful, fitting, and adds so much. The characters are truly individuals you must get to know to best figure out how to aid them (or not!). The writing is witty and sharp and has some fun references. I'm about an hour in and looking forward to more time spent as the Innkeep!
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: This visual novel has good writing and a cast of quirky characters. It's got a dense amount of writing so if you just want to get to making drinks maybe this game isn't your cup of tea. One part of the game-play is gathering rumors through the story, which an hour in seems simple, but it has a good feel like organizing a desk to get it tidy. When customers request it, you make these characters drinks which is also simple task but has a pleasant quality as you pour brightly colored liquids into your mixing glass. The game has hinted at other mechanics being introduced later so as we unlock recipes the drinks should have more effects. The main bulk of the game is about getting to know these characters and helping them along their stories. It is implied that when given a decision to pick one of multiple types of drink that you can effect the outcomes of these stories, but I haven't gotten far enough to see how this will work. All in all, I find this game a fun and relaxing experience. Check it out if you are looking for a charming, low-pressure, fantasy setting visual novel.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid DnD player, this game is very much up my street. The characters are delightful and the occasional 4th wall breaking makes this a perfect cosy and fun game to play. The use of the drinks mechanic to affect the story is lovely touch which makes you feel like you are the Innkeeper and invested in the lore and people of Gaia.
_childDocuments_.name: Tavern Talk

name: Pepper Grinder
detailed_description: Pepper Grinder is an action-packed pirate adventure starring the titular Pepper, a seafaring soul with a passion for prospecting, and Grinder, her super-powered drilling device. Shipwrecked and robbed of her treasure, Pepper must spin up her trusty sidearm to reclaim what the mischievous Narlings stole. Armed with Grinder, Pepper burrows through terrain & water, controls machines, and pulverizes all enemies blocking the way towards recovering her missing fortune - with interest! Pepper's progress will not be that simple, however, as mysterious beings begin to emerge from the shadows... Gritty Gameplay Cruise through a colorfully animated world with precise movements, fluid drilling, and thrilling leaps. Thrilling Drilling Chew through the world with Grinder and find new drill bits to ramp up the chaos and solve clever puzzles. Conquer & Collect Pick up jewels and other riches during your adventure and cash them in at shops to power up Pepper, open up new paths on the world map, and snag collectible stickers for your sticker book.
