short_description: Pepper Grinder is an action-packed 2D adventure blending traditional platforming with an alternate drilling mode that allows you to dive in and out of the earth like a dolphin swims through water.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid, I remember walking into a Gamestop and seeing this GBA game with a girl with a drill on the cover. That game looked cool and I wanted it but I had never heard of it before. I passed on it, probably in favor of a Megaman Battle Network or something, but for years I always thought of that game and what it could have been. Now eventually I found out that game was Drill Dozer but by that point my imagination of what the game was had superseded the reality. Now, two decades later, I finally have that game.The flow of the movement of tunneling through the earth has the same feel as the excellent swimming in DKC:TF except you can't hit the breaks. Its satisfying to pull off long chains of burrowing and leaping out and the developers make great use of the mechanic. The sound design and art are great, and while I would have liked a bit more story context at the beginning, I can't fault a game for putting its gameplay first when that aspect is so strong. That said, I was always gonna love this game, its the game I always dreamed existed. I'm honestly kind of kicking myself that I didn't try to make it myself sooner, but it would be hard to do better than Pepper Grinder's execution.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I was so close to giving this a negative review. Really close. But overall the game is good, and due to steam's binary review system I'll give it a positive.The reason the intro to this review sounds so polarizing, is because the game is polarizing in its gameplay segments. Jarringly so.  The levels are really fun. I enjoyed them immensely. The boss fights are wildly unbalanced and ruin the flow of the game in many ways.  The first boss is very difficult. The last boss is unfairly difficult, due to the fact its bullet spam, and you don't really get a moment between hits where you are invulnerable. There is also a minute long cut scene between retrying the final boss that you can't skip, unless you just plan on doing it with no health buffs, which is a two stage fight where it takes you each stage probably a dozen hits to kill each, and you get 4 total hits, including falling off the second boss stage, which is easy to do. There are no difficulty modes. You can slow the game down, which I did find helped in the last boss to drop the speed to .7 instead of x1.  The middle bosses are really easy, and I only had to try once or twice on each one. It might be a personal thing, but I've beaten Celeste many times, I've beaten Super meat boy, elden ring, so on. In those I felt tough but fair. In the boss to this, I felt it was unfair, and that hurt the flow of the game. You don't expect the difficulty spike that you get for such a fun game. The difference in the difficulty between the levels, which are fun, whimsical, Nintendo like quality of levels. Then the bosses where they have a huge health bar and you die in 4 hits, is jarring. I hope they nerf them.Another thing, the game is very short. But I don't mind a short game for 14 dollars (though I paid 11 on sale). But please, I hope they fix the boss fights. I'm playing this a month after writing, and it says only 26% of players have beaten the final boss. Which for a 4 hour game is telling.Lastly, the costumes are boring. Just color swaps. Only 4 bonus levels, 4 worlds, about 7 or 8 levels each. So like I said, very short.Update: A week after I posted this an update came out addresing most of my concerns it sounds like.From the changelog"GAMEPLAY CHANGESchanged 1-Boss so that the Giant Beetle can be knocked down from a wider range of angles when on the ceilingchanged 1-Boss so that fewer ghost bullets are fired in the Phase 3 burst sequences, but with a larger gap between each one so the same area is covered but less densely.changed time attack requirements for stages 2-A, 3-2, and 3-4 to be more forgivingchanged the screen shake option so that at 0 hit stop is also disabledchanged sticker gacha machines so that drop rates are heavily weighted in favor of stickers missing from the player's collectionchanged the 4-Boss phase 2 arena so that grapple points now appear in the bottom corners to give players more chances to recover from a fallchanged Naro's skull projectiles in 4-Boss so that they all detonate when the player takes damage so that they'll never do an additional point of damage just as the player recovers"I'm not replaying it right now to confirm this, but this shows the devs listened to many people's feedback. Leaving my original review in tact for transperency, it was never negative so I don't have to change from negative to positive.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I played the Pepper Grinder demo during Next Fest and I really loved it and I was eagerly anticipating the games release, and I immediately picked it up once it launched. Despite some of the good that crops up during the game, overall Pepper Grinder is a massively, MASSIVELY underwhelming game.    Before I get into the issues I have with the game, I just want to mention that the art and the aesthetic of this game is pretty fantastic. The pixel art, the animation, the color palette, how diverse every level looks, it's all really impressive stuff. Drilling through mountains and volcanoes and icebergs and ruined cities all make for really fun settings for the game. It's just disappointing that all of that feels wasted on levels that don't take advantage of what makes this game great.    Pepper Grinder excels when it's just Pepper, the Grinder, and a whole lot of dirt. The movement is tight, its fun, it's fast and it's got a lot of personality to it. The game throws in some fun gimmicks too like dousing lava with water to allow you to quickly drill through the magma before it melts again, or ice that will break behind you as you drill creating exciting moments of platforming in really unique ways. The game just discards these ideas so quickly that with a run time of roughly 3-4 hours, they feel very underutilized. Some of these ideas only appear once, or maybe twice out of 23 total levels and I just wish there was more I could do with them. And it absolutely does not help that there's so many parts of other levels that focus on all the things that don't make the game fun. Having to shoot rockets at ice takes longer than it needs to, 'combat' sections get old after the first one in level 1, and World 4 is almost entirely focused around these slower, less drilling inspired things. One entire level in World 4 has an entire three places to actually drill, and the rest is filled with unfun autoscroller combat with a machine gun. There's just far too much in this pretty short game that's just frustrating or unsatisfying. But even still, there's a lot of fun to be had when the game isn't focused on all the things that aren't fun. If the whole game was like this, it wouldn't feel so bad, except for one giant glaring problem: the bosses.    The boss battle in this game are outright bad. There's unfortunately not a single one that is fun, they're tedious and frustrating to fight and show off every single flaw the game has on offering. This game is just not built for these, they don't add anything to the experience and actively detract from it. The final boss in particular is especially bad, the first phase is fine (even though halfway through the AI broke for me), but the 2nd phase is genuinely a slog to fight. It's like one of the worst combat arenas I've experienced in a game since the good old Capra Demon fight in Dark Souls.Just all round really frustrating bosses that do nothing to enhance the strengths of this game.    Maybe I went in expecting the wrong things, but this package has overall left me largely disappointed. So if you are like me, and you played the demo and really loved the fast paced drilling action and wanted to get this for more of that, I cannot recommend Pepper Grinder for how misused this games mechanics are that get focused on all the wrong things.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I thought the game would mainly be about digging/moving through the environment, but the developers wanted to switch up each world into something new, which unfortunately doesn't work out. Now its a 2d shooter, now its a jumping between trucks, now you got a grapple hook with awkward controls, now you got a mech.... I'd much rather the focus more on the central mechanic.Everything feels slightly off in some way. Bosses are more infuriating than fun to fight against. You can buy extra health, but it only lasts one life. You can heal at specific spots in a level, but if you reach a checkpoint with low health why not just kill yourself and continue with full health? So many small weird design choices that ends up bogging the game down. So beware that you may not get as much of the mechanic this game is promoted with, as you may think.

_childDocuments_.review: is a short and charming 2D platformer based on a digging mechanic similar to the one in . The game is quite short, I beat it in three hours of playtime. The structure is very classic Mario, you have a cute overworld that's drawn in a pirate map style, each world is a different map screen and has about five platforming levels and one boss level. Across the four worlds they play with the main drilling mechanic in a few interesting ways, but I did leave the experience thinking that they could've pushed a little further with it and had another few worlds. That being said, what's here is fun. The levels are stylish and exciting, although the bosses weren't my favorite. Similar to classic Mario games, each level has special coins you can collect, giving incentive to replay them. These coins are hidden quite well; there were only three or four levels where I manged to find every coin on my first run through. They also have a time attack/speedrun challenge for every level for those who enjoy time trials. The bosses are hit-or-miss, I enjoyed the first two, but the last two felt a little finicky with hitbox interactions; that being said, I certainly could've approached the fights with more patience. Overall, I had a good time with , the drilling mechanic is great fun, and the game doesn't wear out the novelty of the mechanic during its short runtime. It brought back memories of classic 2D platformers in its structure, but was distinctly contemporary in its gameplay and variety. While it was enjoyable, it didn't do anything over-the-top that compelled me to go for the 100% or sink more time into it after rolling credits. It's a good game that I'd recommend to platforming fans who are looking for a fun experience that they can knock out in a day or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder has been on my watchlist for many years. I was anticipating it highly since its main mechanic looked really engaging. The fact that Devolver was the publisher also increased the hype for me, thus, I purchased Pepper Grinder as soon as it was released.So what do we have here, is it a bad game? No, but it is a huge letdown for me. This game has been in development for 7 years and has a powerful publisher behind it. But the major issue with Pepper Grinder is throughout my journey, it felt like the game lacked content. By a lot. This mechanic could have been used way better, with way more varied level design. There are a few levels that have some ideas, but they wear out quickly. The music is nothing surprising. The pixel art looks good. The bosses are terrible, they lack any imagination and play very poorly. I liked the final boss though. The controls are not bad, but they aren't as responsive and smooth as they should be for a platformer-action game. And why is there this much action in this game? It surely doesn't fit the main mechanic of this game and doesn't play well. Pepper Grinder should have been a game solely focused on combat. There aren't any upgrades to purchase and we don't have any control over our tools/equipment, meaning we have no control over our playstyle. Overall, Pepper Grinder feels like a wasted potential with this little content. It just feels uninspiring in every aspect. I won't recommend it to anyone unless it's like at least 50% off. This is surely a miss from Devolver Digital for me. Follow My
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Boys and Girls, we have a thumbs in the middle Game here.No other option than thumbs down/up, but I'm leaning to up a little bit more.Pepper Grinder...I really, really wanted to absolutely like this Game but there are many issues here.First off, what's Pepper Grinder? It's a "Jump'n'Run" 2D-Sidescroller reminiscent of Ecco The Dolphin.At least that's what the Main Mechanic with the Grinder reminds me of.I think I'm gonna start with the positives here.The Pixel Graphics are not the best I have ever seen but they have their own charming style. Especially Pepper and the Enemies can look really cute.The Levels - while not chock full of detail - also look nice and varied enough.The Sound is also pretty cute, especially when Pepper jumps.Musically this Soundtrack is really good. As the kids say, "a banger" or "it slaps".Even though I didn't love every track, it really is extremely varied. There are Reggae Elements, Rock, Drum'n'Bass, even Hardstyle elements, jazzy elements, bassy elements and much more. Feels like a big mix of many genres but it's fitting, even though a bit strange when compared to the mostly cute artstyle.So, what didn't I like? Basically the Gameplay itself.. And that's the biggest bad here. The Levels are actually kind of easy and go over really quick. Collectibles are very easy to find and there is not much to explore. That's not bad per se BUT, I often felt that I didn't really have that much control of my character. Sometimes Pepper did what my inputs told her to, sometimes she was all over the place.As I said, it felt as if I wasn't a 100% in Control. And that lead to frustration in a handful of the later levels.Not gonna spoil how many worlds/bosses there are, but it's not much. It is over really quick.And oh boy, the last boss. The final boss....This was one of the most frustrating bosses (mainly because of the controls) I've ever encountered in a Game. Maybe not really that hard but since the controls felt off oftentimes, just frustrating.I even looked up how other people did it on YouTube, but I think they may have buffed the Boss more because every Video I watched, the Boss was missing attacks.The Final Boss alone took me as long as a whole world to complete. Yeah, not great. Also it was a BIG difficulty spike in the last level and also with the boss itself.But yeah, still, it was "only" 15€. There is also a Time Attack for every level (not really interested in that) and it probably has a bit of replay value.As someone mentioned, this Game could probably benefit from a built in level Editor.Somehow I get the feeling that many of Devolver Published Games, are really short, artsy, good but also kind of frustrating and annoying. Gee, I really have mixed feelings here.But ok, as I mentioned before, it still gets a thumbs up, but keep in mind that your enjoyment may be hindered because of the controls...
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's an okay game. The art is very well done and I had fun, but not sure I'd recommend it.The controls aren't great, mostly holding RT down the whole time but have to occasionally release and re-press to perform an action which sometimes isn't super intuitive since the X button is used to start the action, and pressing RT ends it (grapple). Also sometimes you continue digging if you clear a gap while not holding RT and sometimes you don't; This isn't a problem for 99% of the game until the final boss.There are jewels you collect throughout the levels, but can really only be used for stickers. It probably would've taken 5+ minutes to empty my jewel bank into the sticker machine. I guess they mostly just server as indicators on how to proceed through the level.You'll take damage on somethings that are confusing, like running into an enemy while you have your drill on, but sometimes not.The primary digging mechanic of the game is fun, but that doesn't really evolve in any meaningful way throughout the game so it's a good that this game doesn't go on any long than the 3-4 hours it is.I found the the game to be pretty easy overall with the final boss being a pretty big spike in difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: You see the main drill mechanic and you'd think how can this not be fun but I found myself more aggravated with it than anything. It just didn't translate that well as a core mechanic for a game. Something about the way it controlled was too chaotic. I felt the level of precision needed vs what the controls allowed just didn't align, especially the ability to change direction suddenly felt hit and miss. If you entered a small block at a bad angle, it didn't matter how quickly you could react, there was nothing you could do to correct it.Some areas verged on Super Meat Boy level tedium where you die until you remember the button timing and sequence to get through it and I'm just not a fan of that style of gameplay. Perhaps I just expected this to be something different than what it turned out to be.I found the shop element particularly disappointing. The temporary health boost was the only useful item but just wasn't worth getting. Both because of the hassle of needing to leave and re-enter a level but especially on the 2 stage bosses. If you died on the second stage of a boss you just restart from the second stage again. It was less annoying just to tough it out with lower health and keep doing that than it was to leave, get the temporary health boost then start from stage 1 again hoping you don't die because it would have been all for nothing. Then if you also don't care about the cosmetics or stickers (the only other items to spend gems on), collecting gems was rendered pointless. I would have love to have seen some upgrade mechanics.It did try to introduce a new mechanic in each level to keep the gameplay fresh but I felt they were all kind of lackluster. I found myself getting through levels just for the sake of getting to the next one and not really enjoying any particular level. I definitely didn't feel the urge to go back and play through any.The bosses were on a whole other level of annoying, at times it felt like there was nothing you can do to avoid getting hit, if you went in the wrong direction, accidentally came out of the ground at the wrong angle or were in the air at the wrong time, there was nothing you could do. On top of that there just straight up weren't fun or interesting to battle, they were all just jumping and drilling through the boss. The last boss especially was something else... his second stage can burn in hell.The ONLY reason I pushed through to the end of this game was because it's so short.I'm no stranger to challenging games, I don't shy away from building up the skill to overcome difficulty, when I feel like I'm still enjoying the experience. For some reason I just did not enjoy the experience this time.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: There are many games that include in their theme the function of digging, more or less prominently depending on the context, such as SteamWorld Dig, more of ole days as Dig Dug, or even Minecraft itself in a certain sense. But I don't think I've played anything that implements this aspect in the way Pepper Grinder does, integrating the digging mechanic as the main axis that makes the rest of the game turn; to mobilize, fight and solve the levels based on pure drilling. In this installment, we'll follow Pepper, armed with a grinder with which we can make our way through different biomes, facing various enemies in search of recovering what has been taken from us.The story of Pepper Grinder is simple and concise, with no missions or dialogues to distract us from the action. We start with a cinematic of Pepper, the game's protagonist, who ends up stranded on the shores of an island. There, a group of strange creatures rob the loot that fell from Pepper’s ship, and flee as she protests behind them. In pursuit of these ruffians, the adventuress falls down a ravine, but manages to get hold of a grinder (Pepper Grinder, eh, eh? that's pretty neat) that will be of help to her in pursuing the miscreants and making them pay. Without wanting to repeat myself, the narrative is to the point and leaves aside frills or complications, it lets us play without much preamble and it really suits the game very well. In terms of gameplay, Pepper Grinder is a very ingenious and entertaining platformer. We'll have only one tool, the grinder, but this fulfills several functions depending on the situation. Mainly, we can use it to perforate certain surfaces and thus dig through the ground, gaining speed to emerge like a dolphin from the earth. It doesn't sound so strange when the developers also took Echo the Dolphin as inspiration, does it? The grinder is our main means of movement, and I have to say that the mobility itself feels very fluid and fun, but we'll also find some interactables around the environment that will give us a little more variety, such as hoops where we can use a classic hook and rope to swing, or cannons with which we can shoot Pepper through the air. And we'll have to use everything we have at our disposal, as the difficulty of the levels rises gradually, adding new enemies, obstacles and challenges to keep the gameplay fresher. From brambles that will hurt us if we cross them, gates that we must push almost like puzzles, to of course the inevitable lava zones! Each scene has its own biome and characteristics, but they share a common point: hidden secrets, in the form of money and special coins.The money in Pepper Grinder is obtained by destroying interactables or defeating enemies, and is used to buy stickers and non-permanent but welcome life upgrades. The stickers have no impact on gameplay, but they do serve to create scenes in the game to our liking, either to take screenshots of them or to pass the time, all on album pages that are very reminiscent of albums from childhood days. The other in-game currency are some coins that are used to buy the said album pages, and also some items to customize Pepper, such as hair colors and clothing. This is a neat addition, it's a nice touch, and it encourages you to investigate the areas to find all the collectibles.Leaving aside the movement, the grinder can be used with several other gadgets, from keys to machine guns and giant robots, so that from time to time we can get a little of a change of pace. Related to this change of pace bit, the bosses, feel quite good and entertaining (except for the final one that I found somewhat tedious and frustrating, but that may be just me). And for those looking for a little more, we also have the classic time scores in every map, encouraging speedrunners and the like to beat their fastest times and challenge themselves.The aesthetics are very nice! We are presented with a colorful pixel art that makes use of varied color palettes for different biomes. I found the level and character designs to be very cute, and I like that everything blends in with the theme. The music is another fantastic addition, and features diverse tunes that range from relaxed to frantic. The tonal changes from zone to zone are very noticeable, thanks to a robust audiovisual section, what else is there to say? I really dig it. Heh.In conclusion, Pepper Grinder is a game that takes us straight to the point, demonstrating fun gameplay thanks to its curious choice of mobility. If I had to compare it to something I played recently-ish and enjoyed in a similar way, it would be Gunbrella, where the use of the umbrella was what I found very creative about the game. The levels here feel very good, and the additions that complement and keep the gameplay fresh, such as the machine gun or the different impediments in the areas, manage to keep one from getting bored as it doesn't get to feel repetitive. The only moment I felt frustrated was with the final boss, as it slows down the pace of the game a bit, and it's just that I had to take it slower and think my actions better. Overall this shouldn't be a bad thing, but having played the entire rest of the game in a frantic manner, the change of pace became noticeable to me. In defense of the boss, I'm also very bad at platforming, and even more so under pressure. But leaving this detail aside, I actually really liked Pepper Grinder, it feels very fun and witty, and to top it all off it looks super cute!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's like if you combined Donkey Kong Country's fluid level design with the drill mechanic from Drill Dozer.It's super fun. Like, EXTREMELY fun. This is one of those platformers that feels really satisfying to master! It has a short runtime, but the addition of time trials kept me coming back to Pepper Grinder. You just kinda drop into this 'flow' state when playing that not many modern platformers offer; the controls are responsive and finely tuned.Pepper Grinder is at it's weakest with the boss fights. While they offer creative ideas (especially the final boss) they are pretty tedious to do. Each one boils down to find a weak spot, hit it when it's exposed, but only if the level allows. They can drag on if you're waiting for a chance to attack.Besides that, all the levels and branching paths are really fun! They have a pick-up-n-play kinda nature to them while retaining a pinch of challenge to keep you on your toes. There are tons of gimmicks in each one and it was fun to discover them all. They aren't reused more than once or twice, and this means each level feels unique and memorable.If you enjoy fluid level design and unique mechanics, pick this one up! It's short, sweet, and a great way to end an evening.(Review shared from my Backloggd page)
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Take this as a recommendation (that I almost decided to review negative) with a lot of caveats attached.The game is not long (my playtime is 100%ed everything and it still felt on the shorter side).The bosses are not great, and the final boss is a new level of bad.Some gimmicks that show up will never show up ever again, most of the gimmicks were fun to play around (the grapple being an exception, and being one of the only gimmicks to appear in multiple levels).The time trials are not hard (not a negative towards the game).Cutscenes are not skipable in time trial mode, making you wait from 10 to 30 seconds for each boss fight attempt.Currency is practically useless, excluding the key for bonus levels and the cosmetics, you can only spend gold for temporary health boosts or stickers for the stickerbook (which i never touched ever and so will 99% of players).With the negatives listed, the gameplay is at the end of the day really fun and is fairly unique. I still had fun even though there are a lot of things that can and should be improved.I "recommend" it but do wait for a discount if you're on the fence about it. Don't buy the game if you don't plan on doing time trials or collecting secrets, you will beat the game in about 2-3 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: A charming platformer with a great central mechanic. However a combination of infuriating level design and bosses make it a tough sell. I frankly couldn't put up with all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game throws at you such as buggy grapple points, weird hitboxes, and the fact that you basically have no i-frames. I sadly do not recommend Pepper Grinder...
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Another game with Owlboy syndrome. (a game with a very long development cycle that had hype around it only for you to hear nothing about it when released, due to it not being bad enough to complain about but not being good enough to praise)Everything about it is painfully average. the art style, the soundtrack, the mechanics, the all could've been so much more. Also some of the most boring boss fights I've experienced in a long time.4-6 hours of content for a game that was in the oven for 7 years and backed by Devolver is very disappointing. Getting all the coins is tedious, and involves looking for a crack in a wall and drilling. And instead of putting more effort into more levels or a level editor, you get a stickerbook and gacha machines. Like come on.Again, not bad enough to thumbs down but only buy this on sale and if you need something to kill a couple hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly disappointed with this game. It's unfortunate because I have enjoyed every other game this publisher published. This game is incredibly short, I beat it in just under two hours, and that includes the time I left the game running to eat lunch. Normally I wouldn't say that’s necessarily a bad thing but this game could have been improved by a longer playtime. While each level has a unique gimmick its never expanded on. Pretty much at all. The only exception I can think of is the Machine Gun powerup which is used in a slightly more interesting towards the end of the game. Out of all the bosses only the first one was remotely interesting after the first attempt, all other bosses are just “Figure out the three different attacks.”Throughout the game I kept waiting in anticipation for the challenge levels which never came. There is a good basic game here but the final product feels more like a tech demo than anything else
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Although I would like to recommend this game after 100%ing the achievements I can't. Instead of further expanding on the movement the game introduces weird gimmicks per level in order to vary the movement. The vast majority of these gimmicks are god awful such as the giant slow robot. Besides casually playing the levels and collecting the coins as you go you can also speedrun levels. For this being an option and imo being the main content extender, getting gold on these levels was by no means fun. The final boss has a 35 second cut scene that you MUST watch each time you restart. Not to mention the lack of flow in some of these levels with slow platforms or weirdly timed stage hazards.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended! Neat movement mechanics, developed very well. The various levels continually offer new additions that keep the game interesting throughout the whole campaign. The duration is short but in my opinion is not a negative point at all. The game lasts just long enough to not overstay its welcome. The bosses are the only terrible aspect of the game: uninspired and difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: At the core of  is Pepper’s powerful drill, which is more than just a tool—it's your ticket to navigating and dominating the game’s colorful worlds. The drill allows you to burrow through terrain, uncover secrets, and tackle enemies with satisfying precision. The fluidity of the movement and the variety of challenges keep the gameplay fresh and engaging from start to finish.Visually,  is a knockout. The art style is bursting with color and personality, bringing each level to life with meticulous detail. The soundtrack complements the action perfectly, providing a peppy and upbeat backdrop to your drilling adventures.The narrative is straightforward: Pepper is on a quest for treasure and revenge against the pirates who wronged her. While the story won’t win any awards for originality, it’s peppered () with enough humor and charm to keep you invested. Plus, the gameplay is the real star here, and it more than makes up for the simplistic plot.With plenty of hidden collectibles and challenges scattered throughout the levels,  offers plenty of reasons to keep coming back. The controls are tight, and the gameplay is so enjoyable that replaying levels never feels like a chore. is a delightful blend of innovative mechanics, engaging gameplay, and stunning visuals. It’s a must-play for fans of action platformers and anyone looking for something fresh and exciting in the indie game scene.Innovative and fun drilling mechanicsSmooth, fast-paced gameplayGorgeous hand-drawn visuals and catchy soundtrackStory is pretty basicCan be challenging for some players drills its way into your heart with its unique charm and relentless fun. Don’t miss out on this indie powerhouse!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is a 2D platformer that is one of my favorites indies of the year so far. The drill controls take some getting used to, but once you do, you can soar out of the dirt like a majestic dolphin in the ocean. The level design is my favorite bit of this game and I can see the DNA of games like Donkey Kong Country and Rayman Legends. While the game is great, Pepper Grinder falls just shy of that pantheon. The game is (like its protagonist) on the shorter side and a reasonably skilled person could blast through it in 2-4 hours, however the collectibles are a lot of fun to look for but I am not yet sure if I want to commit to getting all the stickers from the various time trials. There are two things that hold Pepper Grinder back from being truly incredible. The first is that I wish the cutscenes could be trimmed away in boss battles if I have already seen them, especially if I am aiming for the time trial goals. The second is that the grappling hook is implemented a bit strangely and your direction of where you swing around a fixed point is dependant on what angle you hit the hooked point. It makes sense in terms of physics, but can be difficult if you mess up on your angle and are trying desperately to reach safety, requiring a degree of precision, the game really does not demand otherwise. Even with these two nitpicks, Pepper Grinder is probably the best 2D platformer I have played since Kaze and the Wild Masks. If you enjoy 2D platforming and want to play something other than a metroidvania, Pepper Grinder will whet your appetite.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder didn’t grind long enough on the game. This game feels so full of potential, it’s just sad to see what it actually is. It feels more like a game demo than a fully fleshed-out game. With only four worlds and about 5-6 levels per world, you play through it in a couple of hours, and I felt no real incentive to play more.This game is a platformer, but not a precision platformer, as most of the game is relatively easy, even in the time attack mode. The game feels like it’s slowly introducing new concepts that are all really well done and fun, but sadly, it never amps up the difficulty, even for the boss fights—until the last boss, where you finally get something that makes you have to try and learn how to really move your character and use the dash ability.This game has some extra add-ons like collectible coins that are more of a novelty than a challenge to collect, and nothing to really spend the in-game money on except for stickers, which basically do nothing except allow you to make a small sticker book, which just feels kind of whatever. This game needs more levels, more fine-tuning on the bosses and platforming, and a bit more difficulty scaling. As the game is now, I wouldn’t recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper grinder was basically everything I expected it to be and that means I had a lot of fun with it. I Haven't gone for 100% completion and I likely won't but this is the type of game that really elevates itself in getting that completion done level by level, challenge by challenge, every attempt shaving off those few precious seconds until you're so good at getting through this game that you can show it off and people will actually be impressed rather than just think you're a blowhard. Only point of critique is that I never did get quite used to the control scheme but ultimately that's more so on me than on the game itself.all in all you can already see it's a blue thumbs up, just know the game is pretty short if you don't go for the 100% not a downside to me but it could be to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, the game doesn't quite reach its full potential as it fails to evolve its core gameplay throughout each level and world. While new elements are introduced, they feel out of place instead of enhancing the core drilling ability. I strongly believe that it would have been more satisfying to encounter a variety of drill attachments that complemented the core gameplay, rather than adding a dozen okay-ish gimmicks.On top of that, the game is quite short and the movement both in and on the ground doesn't feel as tight as other games in this genre.Also, what is up with the world 2 boss which feels out of place and is super easy and boring to fight against?
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is a fun, charming little game with not a lot to say. It's a pretty short 2D platformer about Pepper, a girl who had all her treasure stolen by pirates and with the help of some mining equipment you'll venture across a land that has no reason to be this well compatible with a drill. It's the central mechanic of the game and it manages to find a new, novel way to mix it up every couple of levels or so. Whether that's mining through fallen debris or using it to control a giant fish mech and destroy half the town of Innsmouth, you'll be using that drill to do something because on her own Pepper is not very useful. Control wise I found the drill to be mostly solid though if the game wants you to do some really precise drilling I found it to be a tad too unwieldy for it. This was an incredibly rare occurrence though and the only other thing I have to say is that after awhile your hands might start hurting from holding down the drill button for long periods of time.The presentation was great with some nice pixel art and solid music. I gotta admit I wasn't expecting the soundtrack to be so... laid back? I was expecting a lot of frantic action music but a good chunk of it is atmospheric and mellow. There's even some jazz in the latter half. The heavy stuff is there when it's needed though so it's pretty well rounded. The story is about as simple as I explained it earlier though that's fine as it's the gameplay that takes centre stage here.The game overall took about 5 hours to play through it and it's not the hardest platformer out there. Outside of the final boss I didn't really struggle with much and the game is fairly forgiving for the most part. I'd say I personally got my money's worth out of it but I'd have a hard time recommending it to most people at full price. There's more stuff in the game like collecting scarfs, hairdos and a sticker album but they're really there for the completionists. If you ever see this game on sale and it interests you then I can definitely recommend it. It's a tightly crafted 2D platformer that's all quality with none of the fat.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, this was disappointing as I was eagerly anticipating this game.It has a fun core mechanic with the drill, but it never evolves. The last levels feel pretty much the same as the first, there is almost no challenge. It would be very cool if it borrowed some things from Pizza Tower like the combo and ranking system, so there could be SOME replayabilty. As it stands I see no reason to ever revisit this game. I quit at the final boss because it was so damn boring grinding it out. The whole game is mind-numbingly easy and then this terrible final boss is slapped onto the end. I wanted to see if there was some sort of hidden extra world or new game plus or something after the boss, but apparently there is not so I didn't bother.It's a shame. The game had promise, but it's so short and easy, and doesn't ever evolve its main mechanic, or demand anything of you.Not worth it at this price, buy Pizza Tower instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game! The controls, the way it plays, and general structure are good. Be aware, however:- This is not a long game. Most could clear the story and extra stages in about 3-4 hours.- Some of the end of the game is dedicated to a mech and a gun mechanic which are really clunky compared to the much more fun movement.- If you are not invested in the stickers and cosmetics, there is no use for money except for a health boost, which can be annoying to pull in and out of if you're using it to facetank damage for time attacks.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite level from Ori and the Will of the Wisps was the desert. Built around drilling through sand and leaping out at the right angle, it was nothing short of brilliant. I remember saying to myself, “They could probably make a whole game around that idea!”Pepper Grinder is that game. Back in May, I tried the demo on Switch and while I liked the drilling, the first few levels felt kinda samey. Six months later, a sale arrives on Steam. I picked it up, plugged in my GameCube controller adapter, and started drilling.I admire the choice to go full-throttle with a single mechanic. More platformers should try that. After achieving 100% though, I’m left conflicted. I’m not sure if developer Ahr Ech could not conceive of new ways to utilize the drill or if they got distracted during development, but not every stage uses the drill to a satisfying degree. A handful of them give you at least one of three tools that don’t compliment the core gameplay: a gatling gun that turns the experience into a 2D shooter, a snowboard that primarily consists of holding right to progress, or a lumbering mech for stampeding everything in your path. None of these sections were bad. In fact, they were fairly enjoyable, but I was hoping to see more complimentary drilling mechanics, like the switch platforms, Donkey Kong Country-inspired cannons, and special types of terrain. Grappling hooks are a dime a dozen nowadays, and Penny’s Big Breakaway already did a better job with swing momentum earlier this year. The implementation in Pepper Grinder is also fumbled by being a toggle input instead of a hold and release like the cannons, with no option to switch it.The skull coins were lazily done. Nearly all of them are just checking for small alcoves along the main path. Maybe that was done for the time trials. I still think Pizza Tower’s ranking system reigns supreme, but at least going for the gold here requires thorough knowledge of the stages and finding shortcuts by drill boosting. Most took me at least a few tries to clear. The bosses were surprisingly challenging. A little annoyed you can’t skip their intro cinematics (apart from the final boss for some reason), but great on the whole!Like my review, Pepper Grinder is all over the place. My initial impressions were both right and wrong, but I think this developer has the potential to make something great in the future. It took me 9 hours to achieve 100%. I’ll let you decide if that’s worth $15. Like actual pepper, the experience is enjoyable with the right dosage.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I was really excited for this game. I remember when I first found a video of Pepper Grinder on Reddit years ago. I had high hopes for this game, but sadly I would not recommended it.The visuals are amazing! I am a huge sucker for for pixel art and the game fully delivers on the art. Sadly the game lacks in other areas.The digging mechanic is great its a lot of fun and feel good to control. As you progress through the game and get through different environments things like ice and lava come into play. It pretty neat idea, but they are quickly discarded never to been seen again. The game is pretty short. Only about 3-4 hours of content. Which is a bummer I would have loved more levels to play as i quickly burned through the game. The bosses are all pretty awful. The last boss in particular is the worst. It has 2 phases and the 2nd phase is the worst of all the the boss fights. I was hoping this game would be as long and clever as Celeste, but with the main game play mechanic being similar to  burrow ability from Ori and the Will of the Wisps. Unfortunately it is not as good as those games. Honestly I would go recommend you spend your money on Celeste or Ori (1 and 2). Those games have great game play and amazing visual art styles. *I am not a paid reviewer. I won a free copy of the game from Devolver Digital's Booth PAX West 2023. They had a capsule machine and the capsule I got contained a code for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder was good. Not overwhelmingly great, but good and worth the price tag.My biggest gripe with the game are the unskippable intro scenes before bosses, which make it absolutely pointless to buy some extra health before starting a boss fight, because when I die, I can't quickly buy extra health again and start over without wasting time watching the cutscene again and again.

_childDocuments_.review: 3/5, probably wait for a sale in the future.Fun game but very short which means you don't often get to spend time with new mechanics. The bosses are very claustrophobic when this game wants you to have room to maneuver, particularly the final boss who is maddeningly difficult compared to the rest of the game (mostly because I kept killing myself due to the design of the arena). _childDocuments_.review: Got a key for this through their capsule machine at PAX, but I was clearly gonna buy this anyway. It's not quite the #1 game of the year, but it's damn near close. I wish there were a bit more difficulty in the levels or a special world to explore, it's a little light on content in that way. _childDocuments_.review: There is a solid set of mechanics at this games core, but the game woefully underutilizes them. The combat starts off fun with drilling bugs from below them, but that's as far as combat delves into the main mechanics of the game. And the final boss is just ridiculous. There is a difficulty spike that is frankly insane and asks so much more of the player beyond what the first 95% of the game did. Overall after playing, I still don't know if Pepper Grinder was trying to be a tight little 2d platformer, or a run and gun shooter. And unfortunately, it didn't do either as well as I was hoping it would have.

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the kind of game I love. It nails (or drills) the core gameplay mechanic--immediate, guaranteed satisfaction from the fluidity--and gives you creatively designed levels to never grow tired of that mechanic. Along the way, other gimmicks are introduced, with the difficulty gradually increasing at the same time as the fun factor. There probably could've been more side stages and optional challenges without compromising the overall quality of how fun and varied the game is. But I don't regret buying this, even if it's short. So much charm, and awesome music. The second-to-last boss glitched out on me, staying still in a corner vulnerable to attacks, and there are a few split seconds when the framerate dips from those early game explosions, though otherwise it's a very smooth and polished experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is a decent lil' adventure with 4 worlds to conquer and takes about 3-4 hours to complete. Definitely worth playing for the majority of gamers. I'm a real stickler for game feel and design so there's quite a few things this game executes well but doesn't stick and that soured the experience for me. If I were to rate it, it'd be like a 6.5-7 out of 10.This game is all about flow and when jumping between drill-able sections, it really works and feel great. Where it fails for me when grappling is used to transfer between sections. Being able to hold the drill and just press the interaction button when encountering these sections would have been a great QoL addition. Instead, you have to release drill, engage the grapple, and time the re-press when colliding with the drill-able section to continue the flow. This would be alright if they didn't have such small windows to perform. Prepare for lots of smacking into sections and taking damage or having to restart from a checkpoint.The levels are nicely designed and usually have some neat gimmicks involved. These are the real highlights of the game. My only complaint is how obscure collecting some of the major level coins are. They aren't super important unless you want to unlock the alternative route in each world or buy some cosmetics.The boss fights look cool but are forgettable, overstay their welcome, have a high difficulty spike, and don't incorporate the flow that makes the game awesome very well. The bosses play like fights from a Souls-like which don't really fit this well. I would have preferred them to play out like a classic Sonic or Mario boss where the boss goes down in a few hits but you need to survive until there a good window to strike.. There's very little space to drill, leading to you doing tight awkward rotations to stay in the ground, or risk losing control from entering and popping out frequently. Many times, I've tried drilling and immediately popped out to fall to my death or into a boss attack because of it.It has the foundation of an amazing title and I would love to play something like this again but with some major game-play changes.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most divisive game I've had to review. It almost makes me want to reevaluate how I even rate games. If I put all the parts of the game I liked on a pile, and all the things I disliked on another pile, the pile of things I liked would be much bigger. But the things I didn't like were so annoying to me that I'd really have a hard time recommending this game. The levels are all fun to play. The sound effects and music are generally super good. But all of the bosses except for the first one are pretty awful. Many of their attacks will go from their idle animation to an attack in a single frame, so there are many times where you'll think it's safe to attack, but they'll instantly put out a hurtbox and hit you. Because the fights are so long, you really need to gang on to your health, but because of how quickly these guys can suddenly spring into an attack, the only reliable way to kill them is by hitting them once in between their attacks, and never go for a hit if there's any chance they have the ability to throw out an attack. These fights would be so much more fun if they telegraphed their attacks, but a lot of the time they just don't. 90% of the game lets you just go go go, but the bosses bring everything to a crawl. I like their designs, and the final boss is satisfying to finally kill, but the frustration I went through was enough for me to reconsider my review entirely. To be fair, I didn't buy any of the extra temporary health from the shops, but that felt like  cheating to me. I can't help but feel like the developers were OK with the bosses in their current state because they knew players could buy their way to a smooth victory. When so much of the game is good, these bosses being as bad as they are is so disappointing. And while the rest of the game is pretty fun, it isn't doesn't do a lot to really stand out in the sea of 2d platformers. I really enjoyed most of my time with this game, but I came away disappointed. It doesn't help that I also encountered several bugs, one of which made me restart a level, and another which would keep the game from closing properly while it ate up my RAM running in the background, forcing me to restart my computer.Despite being disappointed with this game, I still gave it a thumbs up. Some might take issue with that, and I get it. But I feel like this game is so close to greatness. If the bosses were tuned up just a little more, and these bugs could be fixed, it'd be a game I'd happily return to many times for a quick burst of fun. But as it is in it's current state, it will be a long time before I come back for more, if ever. Steam says I played the game for 3.3 hours, which is how long it took me to beat the final boss with every coin in every level collected. For $15, that's kinda steep, but I still enjoyed myself overall, even considering the price. But with that said, I'm still so disappointed because I can't stop thinking about how good it could have been if the bosses were just better.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, before I go into details, I do recommend Pepper Grinder.Overall great game with an interesting combat/movement mechanic and great pixel art graphics.I have only 2 and a half complaints.1. It's too short. For the price and the amount of mechanics you are given, it almost feels like half a game (as others have suggested, a level editor would be amazing).2. There is the odd occasion where your inputs don't match what is happening on screen, but this isn't often - only really on the final boss was it notable.2.5. The difficulty spike on the final boss is RIDICULOUS. Pretty much every other level/boss in this game took me 4-5 attempts at most - the final boss took me around 30. And again, this might not be the case if the controls were slightly ironed out.But as I said - great game, and highly recommended to give a go.

The game successfully caters to collectors, completionists, and speed runners alike, without compromising the enjoyment of any one group for the benefit of another. _childDocuments_.review: Holy damn I was waiting for this one for a while and it didn't disappoint. This game feels like a trust exercise with a lifelong friend, you can think you can get away with something really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sick and chances are you probably can. Throwing caution to the wind and understanding that the game doesn't want you to slow down has lead to a feeling that has rarely been matched in a platformer and it's just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome. On top of that the drill finds so many interesting and unexpected use cases in every stage. From the common shortcut to movement mechanics such as skimming on the water like a flat stone, there's pretty much always at least a handful of cool ideas in every level.The whole game never feels dull (unless you go for certain gold time trials but that's more a skill issue), makes excellent use of the unique drill gameplay and literally the only major complaint I can think of is that it's fairly short. 4 worlds with 4-5 levels apiece, but I also would argue that each level being stand out different from every other level remedies this a bit. Besides, "I want more of this" is more of a selling point than a complaint in my books, cannot recommend it enough if you want a smaller game to chew on during a weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightful platformer with tight, energetic controls and mechanics, fun engaging and well paced level design, lots of treasure to satisfyingly collect and some tricky bosses. The secret coins specifically are well hidden, but also not too tricky to find making them all really fun to search for.The levels have a really nice flow to them, I can see why this would be a popular speedrunning game (while not my thing) so I'm glad they've including time attack modes and trophies to aim for.The games artwork has been beautifully drawn and is really distinct. This meshes with the fast paced mechanics to really come together nicely. The was everything animates and sounds also makes the whole process very satisfying (especially breaking pots and collecting treasure).The bosses are definitely on the harder side and do increase the difficulty as others have mentioned. I personally love a tricky boss, but I can see how this would be jarring for some. If you love some challenging platformer boss fights, this game is definitely for you.Everything is just so precise in this game, and its constantly introducing new ideas and mechanics to keep things fresh (in some cases to basically only use them for one stage!)Ultimately the core gameplay to Pepper Grinder is what makes it addictive and engaging, trying to maintain continuous movement as you make your way through this whacky world is just so satisfying and really a testament to the core mechanics here. The drill mechanic is fantastic and absolutely worthy of a full game like this (and maybe even a sequel please?)My only concerns with this game are the boss fight difficulty spikes, and also that sometimes the gaps between certain checkpoints were a little unforgiving, leading to a bit of frustration having to complete a larger portion of a difficult stage again to get back to where I was before. But ultimately, this is a small nit pick.This is a tight and fun 5-7 hour experience and I'd highly recommend checking it out. (Runs perfectly on Steam Deck btw).
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is by no means a bad game. The art, animations, and music are top notch and its drilling mechanic is polished and responsive. It's just everything outside of that core package that I feel like really misses the mark. If you played the demo, all of the levels play out mostly as you would expect them to: drill through terrain, be on the look out for hidden areas with golden coins, and kill a couple of enemies along the way. There are cannons and grappling points sprinkled throughout that help add some variety to levels and a handful of really interesting, if not a bit underutilized, terrain additions that were a lot of fun to play around with. I especially liked the blimps that you had to traverse around without popping them with your drill, the elastic purple goo that you could only get out of if you hit a drillable surface, and the destructible boats you drill right through the center of to sink. I wish there were a couple more stand out examples to point to overall, but what's there is pretty solid. I really wasn't a huge fan of the sections that deviated too much from the main formula; namely the gatling gun, rocket launcher, and giant mech areas. They were extremely straightforward and it was time spent that I wasn't using my drill to traverse areas. The majority of the frustrations I ran into during my playthrough were centered around enemy placement and combat encounters. Nothing super egregious, just sections that usually killed my flow.The bosses were my least favorite segments by far. It basically throws out the most fun part of the game and replaces it with encounters that focus primarily on combat in cramped spaces. When I got to the Magmaworm, I was convinced that there was something that I was missing. Some sort of hidden mechanic or strategy that I just wasn't seeing. But it just boiled down simply waiting for a chance to hit while the boss did the same basic movements over and over again. The rest of the bosses aren't much better, with the final boss being way more frustrating than fun for a lot of the same reasons. I know that auto-scroller boss fights are considered cop-outs in a lot of way since you're basically just doing what you would in a normal stage with a big goon pressuring you from the back, but I would have much preferred a few of those instead of these clunky combat encounters. The in-game store seemed promising at first, but I found it really lacking in a lot of ways. The only thing that was really worth investing in were the keys that opened up the hidden stages. There are also some costumes you can purchase with coins, which I didn't really care about since I liked the default look just fine. The rest of the selection includes temporary health (which is pretty useless since you lose it as soon as you get hit once in a level and it doesn't come back if you restart at a checkpoint), stickers, and a variety of sticker books. Personally speaking, there's nothing less inciting than collecting stickers and decorating sticker books in games. I just don't get the appeal. And with these as the only options you have to spend your treasure on, there's really no incentive to go out of your way to pick more than you'll automatically get while traversing the critical path of any given level.The narrative is as bare bones as it gets. While that really doesn't matter in a game like this, I just wish there was a little bit more here than what was delivered. Especially since they pull a foes-turned-friends twist in the final moments that may have hit a little harder if there was a bit more set up.The game also isn't very long. With all of the main areas, hidden areas, and going for most of the coins while not be obsessive about getting every single one, I clocked out at about 2.6 hours. This would be fine if there was more to do after the credits roll, but time trials really don't do it for me and once I had enough gold coins to unlock all of the hidden stages, I really didn't have any drive to go back and scour levels to find the ones that I had missed. I guess at the end of the day, with how refined the movement is, I was expecting/wanting more of a Celeste experience. Much less combat focused and more of an emphasis on stages and mechanics that evolved in interesting ways as you progressed through the game. While there were definitely glimpses of that throughout, there were a lot of distracting elements that kept this game from really reaching its full potential. I'm looking forward to what Ahr Ech puts out next. Even though I feel like this may have been a swing and a miss, the bones of this game are really good and I'm confident that they can knock it out of the park with another go.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review after beating the main game but not 100%ing the speedruns.In classic "published by Devolver Digital" fashion this game is more flare and fashion than substance and fun.The core mechanic of drilling through terrain is mid at best. Very floaty and for a platformer that requires a lot of precision not very precise. You can execute the same inputs and receive drastically different results. It even seems like the team behind Pepper Grinder wasn't very confident in what should be the games "core" mechanic because you spend more than half of the games run time not using it. Yes. I'm not lying. In a game about drilling you do more non drilling than drilling.The first two game worlds are decently solid in both design and feel but it very quickly falls apart. In the later half of the game you will be doing a lot of shooting guns and piloting vehicles in a test of your patience and willingness to put up with underbaked gameplay. The final level for Christ's sake is a shootout with a bad gun powerup that can only be aimed while moving.The boss fights are all pretty poor as well. Gimmicky and random in a game that should be about going fast and executing proper technique. Normally I don't think that's a problem in this type of platformer but the games that I let this type of boss battle slide usually win me back with spectacle. Something this game, I think, is trying to accomplish but it just doesn't hit the right marks. Full of "well this idea worked for other devs so we should do that."Buy it on sale or just skip all together. There are better games in Devolver's catalog that execute what this game is trying to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is pretty great! ....for what it is. The game is a brief experience (3-5 hours) but fun all the way through! The visual design and production values really help carry what are, ultimately, only a handful of mechanics - combined with the incredible soundtrack, each level felt fresh and novel throughout my entire playthrough. The music is a particular standout; many stages are scored perfectly with their settings and, from the moment you hear what plays at the main menu, you'll know right away the 'high-octane' vibe the game is going for! With the exception of one seemingly 'ska-inspired' track (which I had to mute as hearing it made me play worse), all the songs are fun and they don't repeat any!Although many of the other negative reviews focus on the short play time and lack of replayability, I found these elements of Pepper Grinder to be a boost to my overall enjoyment. Each level will probably take between 5-8 minutes to beat (maybe even less if you're focused on the 'time trial/speed-run' mode). That's the perfect amount of time to play a level or two in between chores or work tasks! Also, with a shorter overall time, the game wraps up neatly *JUST* as the whole drilling-based movement shtick starts to become a bit stale. Worth a buy!*I paid around <$10 USD on it when it was on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: 8 years after I first heard about Pepper Grinder it finally, finally releases. And thus, I can now report that the game is... fine.Using the drill feels incredible. It's fluid and responsive and lends itself really well to great level design. Everything else however, is not up to this standard. There is way too much in this game that is not the fun drill-based platforming. The combat in particular is pretty grim. Your shockingly small offensive range is coupled with overtly aggressive enemies that leverage questionable hitboxes against you. There is way too much of this, and it just isn’t fun. The enemies feel like padding to make the levels take longer, rather than actual substance in the levels. There are 2 90% combat levels that are completely miserable. If I made Pepper Grinder I would not have included them. The bosses are sick though they ruled.There are also quite a few sections of platforming where the drill is not used at all, or is only used as an interface with another mechanic. Few of these are fun; most feel stiff and over-simplified, assumingly so that attention could be placed upon the parts of the game where you’re actually using the drill. This is a questionable decision considering how many of these segments there are. Especially in the last 40% of the game these segments are absolutely too frequent. Couple this with a frustratingly limited standard jump and you do not exactly have the recipe for greatness.This game does have its highs, but they are not exceptional enough to counter it’s lows. Music is nice and has a really cohesive sound throughout the game, which is also nice. Every level has a decently unique mechanic that makes it different, which is inarguably impressive. But this means the quality of every level leans strongly upon how good this mechanic is, creating an almost binary system for each level. If the mechanic is fun or not fun, the same thing can be said of the entire level. I did have some fun but my socks remained firmly not knocked-off for the entire game. I would wait for a sale on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished with 65% completion.Pepper Grinder is a platformer built around leaping in and out of the ground using a speedy drill. The physics of momentum and angles are satisfying to learn, although occasionally finicky to manipulate. The presentation is colorful, detailed, and evocative, with excellent music to match. The bosses are largely successful and test the player's drilling techniques in creative ways. There also a lot of bonus content to engage with, such as time trials, secret challenges, and gacha collectibles. Overall this is a really fun execution of a strong concept that doesn't outstay its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a game I never thought I'd play. After Dunkey went over it in his Pax 2015 coverage, I thought it was awesome but didn't hear from it and just remembered it fondly as it faded into obscurity. I was delighted to see its resurgence and made it a priority buy. I blazed through the game over the course of a few days and while I was disappointed by its brevity, I could also recognize that there wasn't a single filler level in the whole game. It appears that they squeezed every bit of potential out of burrowing gameplay, while throwing in a few vehicles to break up the pacing. The collectibles are inherently tantalizing not for their worth, but through the environmental clues, puzzles, or extra challenges that stand in their way (although cosmetics are fun!) The pixel animations are so smooth at times that it looks like a different medium entirely. The smaller group of levels allows for a unique song for each one, and they're mushy and tepid at worst, and smooth or headbanging at their best. The bosses, as expected from a platformer, were underwhelming and incongruous with the core gameplay, especially the final boss. I would have preferred some really challenging levels as the final test for each world, with a boss integrated in the level similarly to Celeste. If you wait for a sale, you're getting more than your money's worth. It's a shame Antonblast is coming out the same year, because this would have been my game of the year otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper grinder is a fun albeit short game, you'll easily beat it in an afternoon. What you'll find in those three to five hours of gameplay is a solid platformer with interesting movement mechanics, with some feeling more lackluster than others. It would have been nice to see more attention to different 'drill-bits'but the pace of the game doesn't allow their mechanics to develop fully. This is most evident in the last stages where moving from the under-baked grapple into the DKC drill cannon, don't forget to retrigger your drill or else you'll end up in the bramble pit! I'm not the first to say this, but it would have been more intuitive to have the drill regrab not be the same trigger button as the drill, perhaps just the A button. Seeing the cannon was first an interesting concept to something that felt like a chore.The boss fights were a mixed bag, either having fluid and challenging fights such as the third and first boss to uninspired and trivial like the second. Lastly you fight one of the worst designed final boss fights in a game I've played in years, it baffles me that the first phase is so concise considering the absolute pile of crap that is the second phase. It would have been helpful if the game had explained we could wall jump or perhaps had less jank grapple mechanics.  Such a shame when the game up to this point does a great job of explaining mechanics through gameplay in a seamless manner is as the case with the chandeliers and drill-gun. For such a forgiving game, they really punish the player for any small misstep with the final boss, not a great way to end an enjoyable experience.Now listening to the game, you'll quickly pickup on the blustering breakbeats setting the mood that you're in for a fastpaced ride. Those being accompanied by chill hip hop and reggae tracks really round out the OST into a perfect listen. I found myself enjoying the gacha portion of the game, it would have been cooler to see more progression items say permanent health increase or drill damage instead of just cosmetics, but at least there's a small amount of customization.All in all, pepper grinder is worth the play, there was many moments in the game I was pleasantly surprised or just found joy in the cute world you grind your way through, unfortunately its hard to build on when being so compact. What pepper grinder does correctly it excels at which unfortunately highlights the negatives even moreso.Totally objective score 7/10
