_childDocuments_.review: There will be spoilers.    Putting the positive stuff aside, I want to remark on the problems I've come up with when playing this game notably in two areas, gameplay mechanics and the final boss, both of which have the same quality of being good and first and then being subject to bad design.    For the gameplay, a few notable irregularities pop up for mechanics like the swing and the cannon. The swing is way too snappy and has a weird side effect where it's possible to release and regrab the swing instantly. (This is also true for the staitionary hook.) Swinging as a mechanic might sound and look like a good thing, but no momentum goes into and out of the swing. I'm not a fan of these snappy mechanics especially when they go so fast that the sense of momentum moves off the charts unnaturally. For what it's worth its not a bad mechanic.  It could have been better. For instance allowing an exit from the swing by pressing X (Xbox controller) would make more sense than having to press drill all the time. However, I would really like the mechanic to have worked differently as it feels noncontiguous with the drilling.    The cannon's input requires a release of the same button to start the cannon, which is also the drill button. In order to drill, the player must regrab the drill button once fired out of the cannon, and to enter another cannon--which often comes extremely fast--a regrab is required. It would have been simpler to shoot out of the cannon with A. Regrabbing has to happen so fast that it feels completely inferior to any other game that copies Donkey Kong Country with this mechanic.    For a positive I have to say, it's possible to wall jump. When I realized this I couldn't believe what a great idea it was, how useful it could be in a situation, especially for the final boss. The wall jump should have been taught to the player by the game through a level that uses it in my opinion. I think it's worth mentioning.    As for the final boss, that dude is okay at first, but for the love of everything good why does the final phase have to be so badly designed? Most of the difficulty comes from the ridiculous stage, which has an endless pit and hooks to grab because it's so easy to misinput and launch yourself into annihilation. Maybe the endless pit is okay, but clearly the hooks are a crutch to balance the whole thing. I'm also tired of boss through ten or more projectiles at once. This is his most threatening attack. Once you know how to avoid it, the fight super easy and tedious. Hence the final phase of the final boss is artificially difficult given its stage and the decision to attack the player with more projectiles. This artificial difficulty is what killed all motivation in me until I could focus on time attacks and have fun again.    To bring up a few positives, the game makes its presence very concise and to point which works well in an experimental platformer and here adds to the fun with new ideas every time a new level pops up. Funny little enemies, good environments, good levels, exciting gimmicks, all coalesce together very well. Most of the mechanics do very well in this game. Overall fun. A bit short of its potential but very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great at all, but not at the price it is, i got for 12 bucks, and i feel like it should be at 5$ or something like that, because it's a really small game, i could have completed it in less than 2 hours, but im a completionist. What im trying to say with this is that is a good game, but get it on sale. Also, the difference of difficulty between the second and the third boss is abysmal, so you gotta be careful with that. The same with the final boss, but that one is actually cool, it took me a few tries, but it's okay. I'm currently trying to 100% it, but i dont think i'll do it, just because 5 of the 23 achievements it has is collecting stickers, you can get them from a type of gum machine that gives it, the problem is, they're random, and most of them you gotta earn them by speedrunning the levels. But overall, i give this game a 6 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10An enjoyable platformer with unique movement mechanics. The timed achievements give this game a real sense of challenge and accomplishment. Zooming through levels and finding secrets and shortcuts made the casual play-through very engaging. Pros: + Worth while 100% achievements + Fun movement + Decent replay value for speedrunning+ Challenging yet not impossible Cons:- Holding drill button down hurt my hand eventually- The final boss was frustrating for me (especially timed mode (GET GOOD I KNOW...))- Having to watch cutscenes after failing a timed trial was salt in the woundOverall I really liked how fun the platforming was. Zooming through levels and avoiding obstacles or enemies felt really good. The controls were a bit awkward at first but I got the hang of it. I'd also recommend maybe making it less inconvenient to buy max health after every death, at least so grinding the timed trials was less tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It’s platforming with a twist: dolphin-like movements with a drill. It’s a little hard to get used to at first, but with time, you start to feel incredibly satisfied as you seamlessly move through the levels. I know at first glance it seems like the game can’t possibly evolve and will feel repetitive, but it’s surprisingly not the case! The game is short and sweet, took me 3.5 hours to beat, and doesn’t overstay its welcome. It continuously and consistently introduces new ways to play the game, whether it be different platforming obstacles or weapons, along with evolving charming scenery. Exploring for all the collectibles is also very fun as it required you to use your skills. It’s a simple fun game. Pick it up and play for 20 min and go on with your day if you want, or binge it for 2 hours because you just know you can get a better time on that level. Highly recommend, extremely polished, very fun, and charming!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really on the fence with this one. The concept and art style is really cool, but the game is unfairly difficult in a non-fun way. It’s simply too janky and buggy to justify the difficulty, causing too much annoyance.EDIT: Changed to thumbs up because I still feel the urge to progress, and that's a good thing. World 3 is also much better, and shows what's fun about flowing around with the drill.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend, with caveats. The art is gorgeous, the traversal with the drill is fun, and the level design makes great use of both. If you liked that drill power up from Ori 2, this will probably be right up your alley. I would appreciate some more responsiveness in the drilling controls (you can't turn quite as sharp as in Ori) but overall the platforming challenges are a great time. The big problem for me is that the boss fights feel like they're made for another game. I almost quit on the final boss due to how many times I fell off a ledge and respawned into another free hit, or got locked into an aerial trajectory leading straight into a fall and wasn't allowed to recover, or jumped into the air to hit the boss only to get hit on the way down from an attack that started after I launched. Also the weird mechanics they introduce where you put the drill into something to make it run, while cute, felt like they subtracted from what could have been more of the solid drilling platforming stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great fun, it wont take that long to beat but its totally worth the price if you enjoy fast paced platformers. It took me a little over 8 hours total for full completion, 4 hours to beat all the levels and then an addition 4 to collect all of the stickers and to beat the speedrun times on each level. Only complaint I have is not being able to skip cutscenes since the final boss has a 40 second cutscene that plays each time you restart the fight.Other than that it is a really pretty and super enjoyable game!Edit: Cutscene skip for final boss has been added, thanks dev!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I first heard of Pepper Grinder many years ago, I thought it was a really neat looking concept but it sort of receded to the back of my mind until I saw it in a Switch partner showcase and immediately I was sold again on playing this. I think it was well worth the wait.A very polished game packed into a short yet flavorful playtime, Pepper Grinder constantly hops from one level to the next constantly putting new spins on the simple drill attack. Not a moment is wasted here and every level feels very unique from the rest, they really focused on making this one be a quality experience.Using a giant drill is definitely a fun spin on the platformer genre and there was a lot of effort into making you feel like you have a lot of control over Pepper's movement as you're constantly weaving in and out from dirt patches into enemies; movement benefits strongly with a controller. Levels experiment with many new mechanics and before any overstay their welcome, the level is over and you're moving on to the next cool thing.Definitely worth picking up if the gameplay looks even remotely intriguing to you, I can tell a lot of work went into this title and it shows. Very satisfying to play and I enjoyed seeing the end result of a lot of love for making a fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is a short but extremely enjoyable game. This game took me just over three hours to beat, after which I went back in and beat it again. Each stage is unique and memorable, and grinding through sand, snow, and water is very satisfying. The time attack modes feel fair, and it is a joy to whittle down your times and master each stage. Very memorable, and I'm definitely returning to this game again.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: A tad bit over-tuned in regards to it's controls and by extension what makes up most of the game, but still wonderfully unique and thrilling all the same.+ Varied level gimmicks and motifs that all make use of the titular Grinder- Over-sensitive turn radius during Grinding causes imprecision and constant overshooting
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: A great 3 hours in-and-out platformer.It gives you basically all you need in a game like this. Satisfying core movement coupled with fantastic level design, where each level offers a new twist on the establised mechanics. You'll know if you'll like the game during the first level and it only keeps building on the extremely well made drilling mechanic. The game doesn't attempt to pad anything out, just shoots original ideas at the player with very little time to slow down. So while the game is kinda short, it felt worth the money as I was having fun basically 99 % of the playtime - with only some frustration at the final boss.  After I died around 10 times to him, the game started kinda chugging like it was leaking RAM. I don't exactly have a slow PC (i7-12700, 4070, 64GB RAM, 2 GB SSD), so it felt really weird when the game started slowing down and the music cut out. A visit to the in-game level selection fixed the issue and I managed to beat him right after, so it might've just been a one time thing.Other than this little issue, the game is polished, mechanics are well executed and there's basically nothing to criticise. Great job to the developers!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: "What if we made a movement-based platformer, then designed a ton of gimmicks around Not that movement mechanic, including a bunch that just outright replace it with a gun or a missile launcher, and toss in a bunch of boss fights in a game without a proper combat system for good measure?" And they did. And it was not good.It's frustrating because the demo shows a LOT of promise and -does- focus on the movement... it's also got the only real puzzle level in the game where the rest of the game after almost immediately falls off a cliff. Even better is the decision to lock secret levels behind purchasable keys that cost coins... that are limited in number... some of which are in said secret levels... meaning it's more than possible to lock yourself out of them on accident. Didn't have this happen to -me- but that it -can- happen is inexcusable.Some of the time trials also seem... overly strict to borderline impossible, I gave up on them halfway through world 2 and since they're the only real thing padding game length, yeah, this one's quite short isn't it. I'm just upset because this so easily could've been a better game but it seems like the good ideas started and stopped with the base premise and never developed past that. And the levels focused around movement and going fast? They're fun! Shame that's, like, maybe a third of the game at best.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: First, the bad things: this game is way too short and the quality of some boss fights is questionable, with the second phase of the final boss being particularly terrible.As for the good things: everything else, from the level design and the enemies to the many gimmicks, not to mention the fast pacing: there's never a dull moment when you're grinding through the gorgeous levels that this game offers. It's a real shame that there isn't more of it. As it stands Pepper Grinder is a good game, but with more levels and better bosses it could have been even better. Still, if you like platformers don't miss it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A fun little package with fresh, exciting platforming, great pixel art, and a bangin' soundtrack. Minor issues don't prevent a pretty strong recommendation overall.I've heard this compared to that part in the latest Ori where you dive in and out of the sand, and well... yeah, mechanically, this is a lot of that. But I think that also sells this a bit short, because (beyond I think being in development since before that...?) Pepper Grinder further explores the concept with fun new mechanics in almost every stage. Drilling through falling cascades of ice, blasting in and out of Donkey Kong Country-style barrels, and some very cool vehicle sequences are just a couple examples.It also sets itself apart aesthetically with some beautifully-detailed pixel art. The stages are colorful and varied, and the enemies are cute and goofy. Pepper herself has plenty of personality for a silent protagonist, communicated through some slick animation and sound design, along with the briefest exposition possible (which I personally love - this is a straight down to brass tacks, all game play, no BS kind of game). And you gotta love that pirate treasure-looking world map!Also, sound is great. Lots of chainsaw revving and chill beats, overlaid with some smooth-as-butter jazz riffing. All that said... I actually agree with what some of the negative reviews have said about the bosses. The last two represent a weird difficulty spike, and their patterns seem to require an awkward, stilted play style that feels at odds with the fluidity of the rest of the game. Hit detection is also suspect on the last boss, and I also had the problem of diving through multiple dirt patches unexpectedly, even after releasing the trigger well before even exiting the first. Maybe I was technically doing something wrong, but the "feel" was off. This is also a very short game, pretty easy to finish in 4 hours or less (unless you're really into shaving down your time trial times). This is maybe a "back-handed criticism;" usually I actually appreciate the short and sweet games that don't overstay their welcome. But in this case I was enjoying the core game play and the stage variety enough that it could easily have held my attention for twice as long, if the content were there!So yeah, it's good, if imperfect. Once this starts going on sale, it'll be a great pick-up for just about any platformer enjoyer! (Side note: excellent Deck game!)
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I’ll start with one important thing - game does not have issues with controls. They are tight and responsive. It’s just the way the drilling works. You’re constantly moving forward and it needs to be taken in to account when doing any maneuvers and it’s part of the fun. Great action platformer with a lot of variety. It feels like dev wanted to do a mix of different types of 2d sidescrollers and it worked out. Drilling is satisfying especially in the more fluid moments. From time to time there are other activities that are super fun and do not overstay their welcome. Story and worlds don’t make sense but who cares. Graphic, animations and soundtrack are great and work very well together. Biggest complaint? Game is too short. And I’m not talking about stupid time/money ratio. There’s so much good material in there it could be at least twice as long. It took me 6h to complete the campaign, collect all coins (no guides) and try a little bit of speedruning. Other thing is final boss. With all that is happening on the screen sometimes you loose the track of the character and it can become annoying. To sum it up it’s a great experience that I wish was longer even if that would make game more expensive. Still really recommend it as it’s quality over quantity.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like the game, because I loved the idea of a fast paced platformer that is centered around digging and unique moves instead of normal jumping. But I was disappointed...tldr first; don't buy this game if you are like me, looking for a cool platformer. The game is way too short, frustrating and unpolished in terms of mechanics and movement. Pepper Grinder feels and plays like a combination of different game mechanics that don't match very well together.OK, now to the detailed review:First of all, the game is very short (beat it in about 3h, but 30 minutes of that was on the final boss alone - more on that later). Pepper Grinder also doesn't have any kind of storytelling or an overarching narrative. Which is - to be honest - not really needed in a game like this, but we literally know nothing about our character, the world or why we do what we do. The character just randomly finds the drill after her treasure got stolen(?) and then goes with it.There are also no upgrades, unlockable moves etc. The moves and mechanics you start with, are what you have until the end of the game. And while the initial hook of the game (or should I say the drill): the"digging"-mechanic is fun first and clearly the best part of the game, the game makes sure that it introduces weird gimmicks throughout the short 4 worlds, where you are mostly not digging through the ground but have to swim underwater, use a weird grappling hook (more on that soon), use a gatling gun, destroy blocks with a rocket launcher or activate donkey-kong country canons to reach another part of the level. This sounds good on paper in terms of variety, but in reality all these additional elements feel unpolished and ruin the flow of the small sections where you actually are able to dig your way through the level fast. And that's the point: The game design screams "speed" and "fast paced", but a lot of times you have to wait, stand still and shoot blocks or navigate through water, which slows down your movement. Pair that with clunky controls that at best feels very fluid, but at worst can get you easily killed because it can be unresponsive and shoots you in a direction you did not want to go and you have a very good chance of being frustrated. The grappling hook is the worst candidate here, because maybe I have missed it, but there is no way to know how to use it without trial and error. It is the X key on controller, but nowhere in the game does it tell you that. The grappling hook also completely deletes any momentum you had and does not even allow to change direction on the fly. You have to let go, turn around and hook back again. A lot of my deaths can be tracked back to this weird thing. To make things even worse, the game's checkpoints are rare and HP is low (you only have 4 HP and there is no invincibility, so getting hit by an enemy and then falling to your death leads to 2 HP already gone). Sometimes there are 1 minute long sections that you have to repeat again, if you fail! Literally the only way to increase your HP is to visit the merchant and buy temporary HP with the coins you collect in the levels. But die once and they are gone. This game is not HARD. It is just FRUSTRATING.Then there are the games bosses. Literally ALL of them are so badly designed, it feels like they belong into a different game. There is no real "combat" mechanic in this game, yet this game tries so hard to put combat-heavy bosses in your face. For a game like this puzzle bosses / gimmick bosses in the style of a Super Mario game would have been much better! The digging mechanic in the fights feels forced and is more hindering than helpful, cause only a very small part of the arena is ground you can actual dig into, causing you to weirdly stall underground or trying to change direction of travel without falling out (as there is no "turn around on the spot" button. Difficulty spikes alot in these fights (much harder than any of the normal levels and while definitely doable, they sucked out any fun I was having in the game). I think almost half of my playtime was spent in the boss fights, with the final boss taking almost 30 minutes alone (and that's only because of 2 things: first phase bugged out and froze, so I could just kill it after some time and in second phase I turned down the game's speed to 50%, otherwise it would have been longer - but not longer in terms of fun gameplay, just a boring trial and error).Without talking too much about the bosses: They are the worst examples of artificial difficulty. Small space for the player to navigate (sometimes it is easier to NOT use the digging mechanic and just jump around and damage with the drill), projectile spam, input tracking, parts where you just have to wait without being able to actually damage the boss, lots of HP, contact damage, weird or inconsistent hitboxes and almost no attack windups on bosses 3 and 4 (frame 1 of their attacks has an instant hitbox, so if you are unlucky, you get hit before even seing the moves)A lot of the game feels like if the devs came up with a cool core mechanic and then didn't know how to fill a game with it, so they added many different elemets that just didn't work together, which is sad, because the core can be really fun at times and should have been expanded more.To end this on a positive vibe, here is what I liked: Music is okay, core mechanic can be fun sometimes, levels are short and sweet and there are optional coins to collect, I liked the giant mech in world 4 (the only added gimmick that felt fun to use, even though it didn't really fit well into the game) and you can slightly customise your character with different hair colors and clothing colors. I don't know who this game is for, because for anything this game does, there is a much MUCH better game out there in the same type of game: if you want a tight platformer with cool mobility and nice tech jumps, get Celeste. If you want hard (but actually FAIR) bosses) in a 2D environment that you have to beat using your movement tools, play Hollow Knight. If you want a cool digging mechanic, play Ori and the Will of the Wisps. If you want to run and gun through levels, play Cuphead.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off real strong, but just can't stick the landing.Later levels are a slog and utilize mechanics that have frustratingly little to do with the primary mechanics of the game, that being the drill based platforming.Some of the time attacks levels are absurdly fast, but barely possible (level 3-2 still shows the pre-patch times for me)The player is able to permanently lock out a level for the save if they purchase shop items in the wrong order, meaning a fresh save may be required for 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING game!! Super fluid movement, excellent level design, surprisingly challenging (which is a positive in my eyes) and really fills in both the Speedrun AND the exploration aspects really really well! My only complaint is that it's so short! Right when things were getting REALLY really good the game just ended. Hopefully there will be DLC in the future for it?VERY happy with this other than that though :)
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but I simply just can't. Where the movement through terrain is smooth, everything else falls flat. There's no real risk or reward to the standard levels, they don't generally punish you for dying, although the distance between checkpoints gets a little... interesting? starting in world 2 (this is not a compliment). The difficulty for the bosses is a bit higher, but in a repetitive and annoying sort of way. The first boss overstayed his welcome after about the third time he killed me. The controls become janky and unreliable the second you need to use an addon for the drill, or the cannons in the secret world in world 1. TL;DR The controls vary from buttery smooth to completely unusable, bosses are mostly annoying, and the game stops feeling rewarding by world 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game, and I really did for the entirety of the first world. However, unnecessary add-on abilities, the final boss and the level before said boss really ruined this experience in my opinion. I collected all of the coins, but the final boss left such a sour taste that I no longer want to continue to do time trials. Unfortunate.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me excitedly say “Weeeeeeeee!” out loud, which is something I do not normally do. The controls are unlink anything I’ve ever experienced in a game, it feels like you’re playing as a roller coaster.The water levels in this game are so fun that it makes you wonder why they suck in most other platformers. Boss fights are mostly great, but I found the second world’s boss to be more frustrating than satisfying due to the extremely tiny patches of dirt you’re forced to use for the fight. Not too hard of a fight, but it didn’t feel as good as the others.Other than that, the unique art direction and breakcore banger songs that accompany every level elevate this game to an absolute must-play. Simply put, there’s no platformer like Pepper Grinder.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet, Pepper Grinder is great platformer with a neat gimmick. The gimmick of using a giant drill to move around certain parts of the terrain is fully utilized, basically every level introduced a new gimmick to play off the main gimmick as well, so it never gets stale and some of the uses for the drill are absurdly amusing and/or cool.  It is a joy to drill, and the buried treasure trails are great, they add a path that feels really good when you manage to follow and get them all in one go, but doesn't punish beginner players if they miss it, it's an easy to play, hard to master feel you usually only get from the highest polished Nintendo platformers, though that does fall off towards the end when it becomes a more precision focused platformer, requiring you to chain together all you learnt before just to survive, it was definitely a surprise compared to the demo levels how demanding some of the later ones can be, but thankfully it all works out in the end.A thing to keep in mind is that I managed to finish all levels and all secret levels as well in 4.3 hours according to Steam, and the only thing you can do after that is try to get the hidden golden coins (I got 90% of them first try) and a time attack mode, I definitely prefer games that don't overstay their welcome, so this is fine to me, but depending on your personal finances and how much you value playtime, you should definitely consider waiting for a sale.The only thing I would point out as a real flaw is a small one: I completed my first playthrough using only the secret levels route, each world has a secret level that serves as an alternative route to the end and allows you to skip the equivalent level, for example, if you complete the secret level in world 2 you don't have to play the second level of world 2, which is what I did, problem is, that level introduces the grapple hook mechanic, meaning I had no clue how the mechanic worked when I encountered it in later levels and had to trial and error my way into getting it, this could have been easily fixed by making it so the secret level of world 2 would skip level 3 or something similar, it's very weird you can easily skip a crucial level like that. Funny enough, when I went back level 2 of world 2 ended up being the last level I finished in the entire game, so, at least that makes for a funny story.Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game hurted my hand more than anything De to how the drill works. The initial gimmick is ok and it's used in different way, but it lack punch as a whole, especially vs the bosses that aren't super enjoyable to fight against. A functional game, but not one with tons of flavor even if it clearly tries at times. There's more enjoyable game around
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: "traditional platforming with an alternate drilling mode that allows you to dive in and out of the earth like a dolphin swims through water."thats how the game descripes itself. and i wish they doubled down on that mechanic. i played the demo and i was instantly in love with this game. yeah controls are kinda clunky but you could really learn to get used to it. i played all lvl in the demo and even got every gold medal in time attack. i longed for the release and now that its out it leaves me saddend. i wished they had done more with the drill mechanic. the grappling hook idea is nice but the implementation is bad. you have to press x to hook and RT to release. then there are sections that put you straight from hook mode into drill mode. now here we have a problem. drilling and releasing the hook are RT. so more than often you release the hook by accident and its annoying as heck. if you could hold x to kepp the hook attached and then release by releasing x the game would flow so much better.and flow is the key word here. if the game flows it feels really really good. but most of the time the game doesnt flow. the robot and the shooting aspects of the game destroy the flow of the game totally. as i said earlier i wish they would double down on drilling through more and more difficult level instead of shooting and robots. is the game bad? nah, but i wish it was what i had in mind while playing the demo. i still like it but i dont love it. i really dont know if i want to recommend it or not so a meh would be more accurate. and that after i annoyed my friends for days with "pepper grinder is going to release soon!" im sadedit: i changed to not recommend because the game didnt get better in the end but worse. i think i wont touch it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game- it was so surprising and fun. I loved all the different concepts for each level. The art and music were great, and the bosses felt very difficult but fair. My favorite little thing was how the secret coins were well hidden (but not so much that I needed a walkthrough), and if you missed one the counter would indicate which one you were missing, making it easier to pin down where in the level it was hiding.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: After enjoying the demo I thought this was going to be a fun and somewhat unique platformer, but it was the complete opposite. Don't get me wrong the levels are well designed, some of the mechanics are fun to figure out/use, the sound FX/music are very well done and go very well with the tone of the game, but that's it.This game doesn't feel cohesive; the mechanics/boss fights feel like they've been thrown together and they make for a very frustrating experience. The horned enemies are beyond annoying to deal with and they are basically the only enemy on every level of the game - no matter what biome you go to they're the only enemies you see apart from the boss fights. Not to mention the drill is way too sensitive.I haven't finished the game because I'm so frustrated with how annoying the enemies are.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I would only buy if it was under $5.00 and if you have nothing else to play.   DO NOT pay full price... this game is very short and mindless.I am disappointed since I usually love anything that Digital Revolver publishes,  but this one was a real let down.   The drill mechanic gets old quickly and compared to the dozens of other side scrolling indie games that I've played... this one is extremely dull and unmemorable.  I went through all the levels and found all the secrets in around 3 hours of play.   The levels are extremely easy and with frequent checkpoints it posed no challenge at all for me.  The bosses are do able once you learn the patterns of them which took about 5 trial and error attempts for each one.   I'm assuming others will complain about the final boss and his final form,  it's cheap and more of a trial and error then a battle that requires skill and timing.  I don't know what to say other then for a throw in game that's $2.00 it is sufficient,  but the current price of $15 is way to much for how little this game offers.   It needed another 30 levels that actually pose a challenge and more creative boss battles that are not super cheap.  5/10 game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder has some of the most variety I've seen in an indie platformer. The game constantly throws new things at you beyond just a new tileset. Stages with wholly unique gameplay mechanics are not nice surprises but the norm. Some enemies and stage hazards are used once in the entire game. Not even a stage-wide prescence but only are literally only interacted with once in the entire game. Then you take into account the above average pixel art which is gives the world consistent grit while remaining appropriately vivid for the game's cartoon-y premise and humor. The dynamic soundtrack which adds extra impact to stages while still delivering memorable tunes. The attention to detail that makes everything in Pepper Grinder feel cared for.  It truly feels like there was nothing in the developer's vision that could not be accomplished. This fits, the game has been in development for over 7 years and it feels like it. You can go back and watch the original reveal trailer from 2017 and see the same great foundational gameplay you get here and see that it was nailed early on. Since then, variety and polish have been stacked on top on this to make a game that's great on almost every metric.  You don't really go into an indie sidescroller expecting this much, many take that great foundational gameplay and solely rely on that to avoid repetition. Which does work frequently, and probably could have even worked here, but Pepper Grinder decided to be more than that.There's a part of me that kind of wishes there was less devotion to the variety. I became interested in the game due to its smooth drilling gameplay which at times can feel like secondary to the variety each stage brings. Adequate focus is placed on the core gameplay, but it's probably less than you're expecting. Pepper Grinder could have skated by with far less enjoyable fundamentals and could still be praised for its unique stages, but having both creates this weird divide where the new stage unique mechanics mean you spend less time with what you probably came here for.A rare issue for an indie game, and something I'm reluctant to call an issue in the first place. While I might have hoped for more stages that expand and refine the core mechanics instead of bringing some new to the table, the fact that that's the biggest issue I have with the game is a testament to how major of an accomplishment it is.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've beaten the main game (gonna 100% the speedrun stuff later) and I'd say that 85% of the game is that premium primo A1 wagyu good good. Keep this ^ in mind, because this is a f*cking awesome game most of the time, and most of the feedback below is for the dev in hopes of patches to fix things.15% of this game, is... not that. I'm gonna do my best to be very objective here because I *really* like this game, but the bosses are just flop after flop. In particular, the Driller and Final Boss are... not it lol. The beetle is just kinda forgettable and the Magma Worm was actually alright (I think I beat it in an unintended way though, by not drilling around and just sitting under its head jumping up with the drill spinning to damage it, very easy but probably not intended). The drill lady just cheats, like straight up she cheats. Its not even that hard of a fight, she has like 3 moves, they're easy if you can see them coming, but with the way momentum effects you while drilling and how you can't 180 on a dime, there's a lot of times you can see her start an attack, react to it, and still get hit anyways because your character can't react as fast as you can. She also chains her moves so sometimes the time from her starting to dig underground while you are underground is well under a second and then you've taken damage, and there was one instance where I got bounced around and hit 3 times because being hit bumper car'd me into being hit again twice lolThe final boss suffers from the same different issues, first of all being that he just straight up broke on me continually. The first phase froze, like he wouldn't move but I could beat him up FIVE separate times on me, and I kept restarting because I don't like winning off a bug. Then the second phase on like the third restart just had no audio but droning background ambiance. No music, no sounds effects, nothing, and restarting at that point to try and fix it meant risking the first phase freaking out on me again so I just stuck it out. (clip for reference:  )Reminder, this is not my microphone, the droning and hissing is just the only noise that would play for me.Beyond that, the final boss also suffered from a general pain point of damage causing more damage. There is no floor, so if you have a slightly wrong angle leaving one of the 4 ground zones on either side of the arena you fall off and die. If you happen to die as he is casting the lightning or there are skulls chasing you, thats a 100% hit as well because you can't move directly off spawn and there is no spawn protection (or it was short enough that it never stopped me getting hit). Thats 50% of your health bar gone in like a second, and that just feels bad. I'm fully ready to admit when its a skill issue in a game, and I don't think thats the case here, I think there is some tuning that needs to be done with the final boss arena and the way spawn protection works if there even is any, as well as fixing the awful droning noise that was my final boss soundtrack and the first phase freaking out.Beyond that, genuinely, the other 85% of this game was fantastic. I'm not kidding when I say this, if you remove the boss fights entirely and replace the final fight with like a mad dash or digging challenge, kinda like a platforming gauntlet just as a drill test ascending or descending, I think the game would be *much* stronger for it. It would be a waste of assets because the bosses look very cool but as they are right now they are very much a weak point. Zipping through the levels at 200MPH is the best, the music is a bop all the way through, the level design for the main levels is fantastic and while the game was short it felt like there was a fresh concept in pretty much every level. I'm hoping to return to the game again after some patching and 100% it, I really enjoy what this is for the most part and if the boss bullsh*t can get ironed out I think this is an easy recommend which is why I'm leaving this as a thumbs up. I'm not petty, just slightly salty lolAlso worth mentioning because it might happen to you, I can't run the game in fullscreen, I had to play it windowed. The visuals freeze up when I fullscreen it which doesn't happen for any other game with me, so I don't know where that originates but it happened in the demo too so I think its a Pepper Grinder specific issue. If you are on the fence after reading this, play the demo, that is representative of what most of this game is and what you can expect from it. Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Changing my review to Recommended now that most of my complaints have been addressed, original review below.CAVEAT: I don't recommend this FOR NOW. Reasons to follow.What I like:Drill movement and level design is quite fun in the beginning, a natural flow to everything, only broken when you're secret hunting and I'm sure a better player could incorporate that seamlessly. The music and graphics are great and I'm grabbing the OST for sure (with the exception of one track but oh well).What I don't like:The hitboxes. Without spoiling anything, some bosses have very specific hit areas and sometimes don't register. Said bosses can also hit you outside of the attack's visual range>The grappling mechanics. One would assume that jumping would jump off a grapple and you could hold drill to keep drilling,. But no, the jump button disengages the grapple with no momentum and the drill button makes you jump, meaning that you end up panic spamming in certain areas, or let go of drill once you're grappled, only to jump into the void.I'm also not too keen on the gun sections, but it's fun for a bit, also some amusing things at the end of one of the sections.A few patches can easily work the hitboxes and maybe add some options for the grappling if the devs are intent on keeping it the way it is. _childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet. 4 Worlds with 4/5 levels each (one optional) and a boss fight level at the end (no platforming on all except one of those - it's straight into the fight).5 well hidden skull coins in each level are used to unlock that one optional level per zone, a bunch of hair colours and outfits as well as sticker pages representing each level. The other unlimited gem currency can be traded in for random music or stickers you can place onto those pages or temporary bonus health.Besides digging (which is already greatly varied with a boost attack, trapdoors; growing, crumbling, falling and jelly materials to dig through) the grinder is also used for moving platforms, turning keys, shooting guns, rockets and cannons, riding snow mobiles and mechs. Great stuff.The few things that bother me are the difficult grapple hook mechanic being introduced before the simple one (a timed spin release versus a straight forward pull) and the sticker vending machine being terribly slow for the amount of gems you can aquire rather quickly. As with everything else you have to hold down your dril button - and with the rewarded stickers being random and others limited to time trials of completed levels, it's hard to tell how long you should keep going at it. You'll probably soon want to rubber bind your right trigger and go for lunch while the sticker machine does it's thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is a quick and creative platformer that heavily emphasizes non-traditional movement. The protag, Pepper, uses a drill to weave in and out of the ground, build momentum, and slingshot herself across imaginative levels. The developers succeed in creating level variety on par with some of the best platformers in gaming. I truly felt excited to complete each level, as I wanted to know what was coming next. The platforming itself is very forgiving. Plenty of checkpoints through each level allow for the player to make mistakes and never feel overly punished. The nature of the drill-based movement does cause some slips that feel out of the player's control, but it never feels overwhelmingly frustrating, as any defeat typically only sets the player back a minute or two.However, the boss fights at the end of each world were frustrating. They often felt much more punishing than the platforming stages, and I found myself spending more time on bosses than I did on progressing the game. This could have been solved with an option to permanently increase your health in shops, or if the bosses could drop health replenishments during their fights. These solutions may make the game too easy for some, but I still think it would have been a nice option.I also found very little replayability. Pepper Grinder expects the player to go back through old levels to find hidden coins, or collect currency to unlock stickers or character customizations. However I never found any desire to unlock those items. Completionist gamers might enjoy that gameplay loop, but I did not feel encouraged to go back. Lastly, the game is exceptionally short. From start to credits, I played for about 3.5 hours. In an ideal world, the game would have one or two extra worlds, but as it stands now, I believe the game is not worth full price.There is some real genius in the design of Pepper Grinder, but boss fights, boring collectables, and an exceptionally short run time force it to fall short of being truly great. Pepper Grinder is worth playing, but you should hold off until the game is on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Many have complained that this game is too short and while I vehemently disagree, there are ideas within the design here that weren't fully expanded upon. The final boss provides an incredibly unearned and steep difficulty increase, but it did make him really satisfying to defeat. I had tons of fun 100%ing this game and I highly recommend you do so aswell!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. Solid platformer with fairly unique core mechanic. Has enormous speed-running potential.My only complaint is that the game feels a little too short. It's low-priced and it's indie, I get it. A lot of work clearly went into this game, and I'm happy to pay for what there is because it's . But for as many mechanics as there are in the game (and there are ), it feels like there should be at least a handful of "advanced"-type levels (a la Star World in Super Mario World). _childDocuments_.review: + Graphics are pretty great, classic indie pixel-art with good art-direction to boot. The stages are great looking and unique (each with their own theme), the action is easy to follow (and it can get pretty frenetic at times) and there's personality in Pepper's and the enemies' animations.+ The main movement mechanic, drilling through the various surfaces with the Grinder, is well implemented. It's snappy, intuitive to control, has good feedback and is just fun. Exiting the drillable surface, especially after a boost, can be a bit unpredictable, but that definitely feels intended and part of the skill-check. You can also skip across water, by hitting its surface with the drill diagonally, which is very useful to speedrun. The game is at its best when the levels revolve solely around this mechanic.* There are 4 stages, each with a number of levels (one of which is secret and can be unlocked). Some of them revolve around a gimmick, a thing which I usually like, but it doesn't always land here.- Specifically, whenever you're handed a gun to shoot, it controls very poorly. Aiming with the left stick, which you also use to move, sucked all the fun out of the action. The last level is particularly tedious with this mechanic.* The grapple is also a mixed bag. It can add a lot to the levels, requiring some precise skill to ring around a grapple point and continue drilling through something and chaining that multiple times in a row is pretty exhilarating. But there were plenty of times where the input felt very imprecise, where I was certain I pressed the button and Pepper would immediately grapple only to miss completely and fly to her demise.+ The bosses can be a surprising difficulty spike compared to the levels that precede them and your HP might seem low the first time you fight a boss, but, after learning them, I thought they were pretty fair overall and  definitely fun to fight, an eventful finish to each one of the 4 stages. In case you are indeed stuck at a boss, the game also provides you with the ability to buy extra HP between levels with all the jewellery (you collect while playing) as the currency, so it also incentivizes picking everything up in the levels.+ There are 5 hidden coins in each level, as well as a time attack mode, so there's definitely some replayability there to compensate for the short length of the game.* The soundtrack is pretty good, fits the action really well, though none of the beats were bangers for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game as a platformer, but there's quite a bit of jank when it comes to its boss battles.Moving around with the drill can be strange at first, but once you get the hang of it, it becomes second nature. Even the grapple points aren't as cumbersome to deal with when you understand when to hold drill button, when not to, and when it's just better to jump mid swing. The biggest highlight of this game is moving around with the drill and trying to see if you can beat your own time. Some of the gimmick stages are also pretty fun.The main issue comes from the fact that once you're digging, you can't really stop, and when you're launching yourself off the ground and into the air, you have very little control of your movement. The first can be mitigated by spinning around in small circles, but the latter is more troublesome, especially when it comes to combat.Almost every boss battle in this game requires you to continuously launch yourself at the boss like your some ♥♥♥♥♥ up dolphin, and it just feels awkward as hell. The Last boss is especially aggravating since you have to deal with bottomless pits. On the plus side, both lava and pits don't kill you instantly, and the devs were nice enough to leave a checkpoint at the second phase of the final boss. Otherwise, I don't think anyone would have finished this game.If you don't mind the game being about 4 hours long, with very little to do outside of collecting all the Skull Coins and spending them on color swaps, unlock-able levels and...stickers, this is good platformer to play, at about $10. But, the boss battles can be pretty painful, and might even lock some people out from the rest of the game.
