_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful little gem of a game. Personally I love that it's not a very long game. Took me around 4 hours to finish the story and I think I'll put in a few more to get all the medals and try to get some time attack medals too. I'm looking forward to dlcs in the future but I'm also happy for what it is. If anyone is into driller games this one is not going to disappoint
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's beautiful, it's a fast paced GAME. It's a PURE GAME YOOOO. That kinda game that exists because it's a game trying to be a game and all it wants to do is be a good af game.They absolutely nailed the feeling of FLOW in this game, it's beautiful, fast paced, and highly speedrunner friendly (especially after some post release updates.)This game is short, sweet, and to the point. The scenery changes and they keep on giving you new stage gimmicks to engage with, they come, they go, and you move on, it's very nice and kept me interested to see what would be around every corner.It's fun to zip around the stages while trying to collect treasure and the special treasure (big gold pirate skull coins)Boss fights kind of remind me of Donkey Kong Country... both in the way they're animated... and the absurd difficulty... The difficulty is something many of the negative reviews mention but as I played after the adjustment patches I found them... something possible to overcome, is what I'll say. Boss difficulty is significantly higher than the difficulty of the stages and it's a little jarring but yeah, it reminds me of DKC a little and most of the bosses are very cool.tl;dr - fast, like a sonic game, if sonic games were actually good, because you get to go fast more often than just the first level. This game is very speedrun friendly. Beautiful and adorable graphics, constantly changing themes and new gimmicks around every corner. A few issues with the difficulty progression but this only applies to the bosses, 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I got this one through the Humble Store, which cut of another 2 bucks or something, but even with that it is kinda short if you think about. When you actually play through it there are some Ideas introduced early in the extra levels, in the last world it just is a whole new idea that did not get reused again. The process of completion took me 8 hours (Steam seems unsure, when I look at the game page it says 8 in the review for me 7), which is a little bit faster than what you would find on "How long to beat". To be honest especially for the last boss it gets really annoying to charge up your HP every time you die. Other than that most of the time trails are challenging but forgive one or two errors as to be not too harsh. I think I would say it is worth it for around 10 bucks and I am mildly interested in what the Developers behind it will do next.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: The main movement mechanic is fun, I enjoyed myself for part of my playthrough, but most of the level-specific gimmicks are awkward and/or unfun. There are several shoot-em-up segments that are just plain tedious, and the grapple hook mechanic is extremely inconsistent. On top of all that the game is extremely short, took me around 2.5 hours to beat (although admittedly I skipped the bonus levels and did not go back for all the hidden coins).
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Cool and fun, yet a little short. Very enjoyable game play, cute pixel graphics, and some head bobbin' music tracks. Has some challenging time trials and fun level design. I had a blast playing it and going for the 100% completion. Worth picking up.~ edit ~I do wish there were more levels or even something akin to Celeste's "B side tracks" where they take the original level and make it more difficult/add a unique twist. I definitely enjoyed the levels more than the bosses as the game shines when quickly blasting through levels and getting the good/perfect run.Just a two cents spitball idea here but maybe there could be a content update where you play as a different character like Mint? Could be interesting adding new mechanics with Mint's double drills.Anyway, cool game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is fun, but the game engine is quite poor. It has numerous bugs, such as missing collisions, faulty hitboxes, unregistered key presses, and random issues preventing jumps. These problems significantly impact the gameplay experience. While the joystick feedback and hitboxes should be excellent in theory, the game developers have unfortunately compromised the game’s quality. Although it is possible to complete most levels perfectly, it often takes over 100 attempts due to the persistent bugs. I’m very disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic platformer with good controls and smooth gameplay. Level design is creative and a joy to play through. Music is wonderful.My only complaint is that it's rather short. You'll definitely get more out of it than I did if you're the sort of person who loves Time Trials, but personally, replaying a level for a better time just isn't for me.Otherwise, a must-play if you enjoy this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding. Very fast gameplay and mechanics with a high skill ceiling, especially for completing time trials, which compared to the more exploratory mode will really teach you how to play. Superb pixel art and excellent ost. A must for any platform lover.PS. I've just 100 percent completed the game. Sadly, the last boss is completely out of point due to its excessive difficulty, and unprecise hitboxes throughout the whole game are a major issue.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is a fun and charming 2D platformer with easy to learn and hard to master gameplay much like the game Celest except instead of dashing through the air you are drilling through the ground. The art and characters are bright and colorful and have a lot of charm with each area of the game being themed differently. While the main story of the game is fairly short (Being able to complete it in Around 4 Hours) there is replay value in terms of collectibles and time trials. Pepper Grinder is a game definitely worth playing especially if you are a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet platformer with a fun hook. Yes, it's more challenging than it looks at first glance, but there are plenty of other easy platformers out there. Nearly every level has a unique gimmick that doesn't overstay its welcome. The whole game is about 3-5 hours if you don't do the speed running challenges on each level. Even so, it is fun enough to be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a treat.Though it is on the shorter side, I found the level design remained fresh front to back.The only part I found frustrating were the boss fights but then when retrying them on time trial I had a much smoother time with them.The games unique movement mechanics feel great but can have a bit of a learning curve that the boss fights necessitate. Also the soundtrack really bops. It uses a neat trick while the song will kick in right when a sequence or new mechanic starts up.All in all a strong recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game.  The main movement mechanic is fun to play with and has a good amount of room for your skill level to grow with it as you go through the game.  Music, graphics, and sound design are all good as well.The game is around 3 to 4 hours of playtime if you just go through the main levels and collect the golden skulls, but this can easily be doubled or tripled if you go for all the time attack medals on each level since the required times are difficult, but still pretty fair to get.There are a lot of different mechanics the game goes through in the different stages, and they're all mostly serviceable, but if you go for the time attack medals you might find some of them to be rather unwieldy.  Specifically I was not a fan of the level with the missile attachment for the drill, since the controls for aiming and shooting the missile don't feel great, and the mech has rather clunky movement controls, which isn't too much of an issue until you start doing time attack runs.  There's also a gatling gun attachment which I don't have any issues with controls wise, but the levels that used this attachment felt like they were just abandoning the drill-based gameplay entirely to be a run-and-gun shooter for a bit.  My favorite level was the one with the falling ice that you have to drill through, since it felt like it stayed true to the game's core game mechanic but also put a nice spin on it that makes it stand out from the standard drilling movement in the rest of the game.The last boss of the game is a multi-phase boss and casually it's not too bad since you get a checkpoint in-between phases but it was easily the hardest part of the game for me when doing the time attack run for it.  The first phase isn't too difficult and has a pretty consistent pattern, but one thing I didn't really like about it was how it wasn't visually well communicated where the boss's hitbox was.  It's at some point between it's head and shoulders, but there's no special coloring there or anything to show exactly where it is, so I found myself frustrated sometimes when I missed hits that I thought should've connected.  The second phase doesn't suffer from this issue since in that phase the entire head becomes the hitbox, but it does the thing that some platformers do where the boss battle takes place over a bottomless pit with floating platforms for you to stand on while you fight.  Luckily falling into the pit doesn't instantly kill you, but with how you're supposed to drill through the platforms to move through the stage during the fight (and with how small the platforms are) I found myself falling off the stage more often than not, since the drilling mechanic doesn't lend itself very well to precise movement in tight spaces.  I also found myself accidentally drilling into the platforms multiple times due to the slight inclines on them, which would make pepper automatically start drilling if she landed facing the incline while the drill is active.One issue I found with longer play sessions was that my right hand would get a bit sore sometimes from holding down the right-trigger for so long.  I get why it makes sense for the drill to be active when holding it down, but when you want the drill to be active about 90% of the time it can wear on the hand muscles to hold it for so long.  An option to change the drilling to a toggle on-off system might've helped with this.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool platformer with a fun gimmick that gets thoroughly explored through its runtime. The ability to do speed-runs of levels is also a really nice touch, and goes to show how much difference there is in 'playing the game well enough to clear it' and REALLY playing the game. Some of the boss fights were a little annoying, but a couple hit so  I guess it balances out.Also, the soundtrack rips.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo for this game at PAX West 2023, and I was excited to pick this game up once it came out.This game has a very unique gameplay loop. Ever played Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask? Ever played as the Zora Link in that game? This game is like that but in 2-D, swimming in and out of dirt sections and doing dolphin jumps for air and speed. That comparison may turn some people off, but I think it's a fun formula, encouraging speed and finesse. You run each level once for exploration purposes, with hidden nooks and crannies to find treasure in, then you can run it again later for speed. Both types of runs are a lot of fun.Bosses are hit and miss. Skip this section if you want to go in blind. This game is $15 (USD). Worth the price, just know that you're here for a fun time, not a long time. The demo covers all of World 1 except the boss, and the entire game is done after 4 Worlds. I was able to 100% complete the game in around 6 hours with all achievements. Good for a couple short-burst sessions over the week, or an all-day binge. I hope the devs can continue the momentum and possibly deliver a Pepper Grinder 2, or at least some similarly fast-paced game if not a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time spent with Pepper Grinder!I'd definitely recommend this game to someone that wants a short and sweet fun platforming experience. I'd agree with some of the criticisms, for example the first boss is very punishing and with some finicky hitboxes. Also the game struggles a little bit with pacing of mechanics. The bespoke mechanics in some levels are all genuinely fun and a nice break from the (very polished and good) core gameplay. However they all last potentially too long, with some exceptions. If they were shorter and more intense then they would have added some excitement to seeing them. When your core game is this fun, don't spend too long away from it!There are a lot of other lovely touches, the animations are full of charm and the music is needlessly good and jazzy!Lastly the collectables are well hidden but not frustratingly so which is a hard line to tread.Overall a good game that I'd have been proud to have worked on.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: It is not often that I won't recommend a game - usually there is enough redeeming factors to make a game worth buying.That's not the case with this game. The best part of this game is drilling and going fast, but for some reason the game is incredibly stingy with just letting you do that. Far too much (almost if not more than half) of the game is taken up by gimmick levels, which are broadly uninteresting and slow the game down to a crawl. The  hookshot is really interesting, but the game nerfs itself by only introducing it halfway through the game and then taking up that latter half with a bunch of boring combat/gimmick levels that don't let you use the hookshot! The currency system makes no sense - you get treasure from the levels, but you can only spend it on health upgrades that do not persist after death or between checkpoints (meaning if you buy it for a boss and lose, you have to go back to buy those upgrades again if you ever want to fight that boss with those health upgrades) and... stickers? I got to the final boss and had no motivation to beat it. I was really let down by this game from an otherwise stellar publisher, and I was looking forward to playing this game for a while.This game scratches the surface of what it could be, and demands too high a price for what it is.The best parts of this game are hidden behind some frustrating, confusing, and unfortunate design decisions. The music is great, and the art is nice. Some levels are super inventive (the level with the giant and the level with the falling icicles are really great), and there is a real charm to a lot the game has going on.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Man, as much as I love the movement mechanics in this game and WANT to recommend it, there is just so many little (and some big) annoyances that's holding it back. Tunneling around, being forced to always go forward and to figure out a path on the fly feels great and is super fun, and I really wish the game had a tighter focus on that with an equal split of puzzle and platforming challenges. Instead, for some reason they decided to chuck in exploration elements, bosses and enemies that you can't effectively fight because the only tool available to you the vast majority of the time is your drill with the range of a cocktail stick meaning you're bound to die over and over to enemies fighting you with any more range than that (I. E all of them).The game is structured into fairly linear levels with collectibles leading you through the main path of each level. Throughout the levels you can find 5 tokens to collect and sometimes these tokens are shown to you leaving you to figure out the path to get it (fun!), but other times they're completely off screen with the only way of finding them by taking random leaps of faith off the screen, usually sending you to your death and back to the last checkpoint (not fun! Go figure). And when the main gameplay is fast-paced going-with-the-flow pathfinding, randomly taking detours that often resets so much of your progress absolutely piledrives the momentum of the pace. Same goes for all the gems hidden in crates and jars and stuff, collecting them is just busywork that detracts from the main experience, and had they let you buy something cool with them, that could have been forgiven, but no, all they can get you are stickers for your sticker-collection.Enemies are also just there detracting from the experience. They usually don't block your path, they're not used to reach places and they're not even used to indicate where good stuff can be found. They're just kinda scattered around the levels as hazards and A Thing You Can Drill™. Since (most of the time) the only tool you have to fight them is your drill, combat VERY quickly turns into a tedious chore, especially when you die and all the enemies reset. Which, as previously established, will happen a lot because your drill is a melee weapon with range requiring you to stand a pixel perfect distance away from the enemy lest you take 1 of the 4 allowed damage before you're sent back to the last checkpoint. Again, had you been able to get something (ANYTHING) else to make the combat more varied, this could also have been forgiven, but 3 hours into the game the only tool available is still the drill and there's no signs of that changing.So far these are relatively small flaws in an otherwise fun game, the thing that makes me actively not recommend the game are the awful boss fights. Every single one (I've encountered) locks you in an arena with a boss that could not be less engaging to fight. All the arenas have a fairly limited area you can actually use your drill, they almost seem to have been put in there as an afterthought because they're barely used to actually fight the boss itself. And the bosses have a varied set of moves and paths they take, all of them equally impossible to predict because they're randomly chosen and not projected in the slightest. This in turn means bosses become less about reacting to their moves with the appropriate action and more about playing it stupidly safe in hopes that RNG doesn't ♥♥♥♥ you over. All of this is compounded by the fact that your drill with the incredibly short range, the only tool you have available during these fights, is deliberately hard to control meaning you often end up flinging yourself into the boss by accident taking away 1 of the 4 hits you're allowed to take before the entire encounter resets, again and again and again.There is a fun game in here and if you can get this game on sale, it's worth checking out to experience the very uniquely fun movement mechanic of the drill, but other than that I just cannot recommend. I can only hope the studio one day makes a sequel where they iron out these flaws
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder boasts amazingly satisfying and fluid movement similar to the sand level gimmick in Ori 2 but fine tuned to the absolute maximum. With a couple fun boss fights, some Crash Bandicoot style time trials and you certainly get your moneys worth... mostlyThe game is about 3-4 hours long and took me 9 hours to 100% it. It's paced very well and every level is super unique but I do wish it was longer after all these years of waiting; I even encountered a few bugs on the way. Throw a couple bug fixes and more post game similar to Celeste and we would've had a perfect game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Love the movement with the grinder, love the animations, love the stages, creative!Not a fan of the gacha mechanic for the stickers though, I'm not really willing to stay there and hold right trigger until I eventually get all the stickers, so that's one complaint.I did finish the game, got all the treasure, cosmetics, but I have yet to touch the time attack mode. Regardless, the normal campaign itself is very fun without having played the time attack, so I'd still give a recommend!8/10, great game
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper grinder is an incredibly smooth and fast paced action platformer that refrains from getting stale by adding new mechanics every level. This way each level is unique, posing distinct challenges and offering great variety. This gives the game incredible pacing untill it drags down to a halt during the bosses. This is because throughtout the levels you'll be constantly on the move, quickly adapting to what's next. But during bossfights you're just locked in one arena where you have to dodge attacks untill you can sneak a hit in. I think the game would've massively benifited from Ori style escape sequences for bosses rather than traditional bossfights. Speaking of Ori, pepper grinder's main burrow mechanic shares some similarities will of the wisps' namesake. And while neither inspired each other since both mechanics were conceived before being publicly shown there's still a huge satisfaction paired with having such a fun mechanic across both games. Obviously pepper grinder having built the whole game around it allows it to do more with the mechanic but that doesn't make it better. In my opinion both games used the ability to create genuinly fun and exciting platforming that is utterly addictive. But as my personal prefference lies with metroidvania's rather than level based platformers i'm just left wishing that pepper grinder was a fully fledged metroidvania. Perhaps something to consider for a sequel?That's also the thing with pepper grinder's level based approach. It wants you to go fast but at the same time there's hidden collectibles to look for? I think the skull coins would've been much better implemented if they were always easily visible but required a much tougher jump to reach. Sorta like a fork in the road between an easy and hard section. Most of the skull coins will be used on cosmetics but there's also 4 bonus levels to unlock this way which you won't want to miss as these are in my opinion the most fun levels in the game. The avalanche level especially was just chef's kiss.The whole movement mechanics and level design are delicious but so is the pixel art. It's not the prettiest or grittiest pixel art i've seen but it suits the game so well. Just like the soundtrack, although i would've liked a few rock/metal songs in there too (like doomblade). Regardless the whole experience clicks and just screams devolver. It's another great game in their already solid catalogue and a game i'll gladly revisit later to try my hand at the speedrun challenges. The game was obviously designed with these in mind so you'll have to forgive the shorter runtime of the campaign. Still though the game is cheap and pretty much worth it, especially if they could add a level editor later.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Having a setting where you can slow the game down is a brilliant difficulty slider that allows you to dynamically adjust the challenge on a moment by moment basisI've read a few other reviews, some of which mention a certain buggy-ness, but I myself never encountered any bugs or the like; the whole game felt super responsive and intuitive!Super big thumbs up
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Very short (4h, 23 levels), often pretty hard, but also fair platformer with a drill to it. Artstyle is somewhat janky, but also adorable and well animated.I don't mind the soundtrack, but it's not that great either.There's not much wrong with pepper grinder and is a well rounded, short experience. If you liked the gameplay of the "ori" games you might also like this game's gameplay, though it's not cute in any way.Great on steam deck!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great Level Design, Great Music, Great pixel art. There's plenty of stuff in the levels to keep the gameplay fresh. All of the bosses were fun to fight, especially the final one, but they weren't hard enough to sour the experience as others have said. The game is a bit short, but the game also doesn't dwell on any gameplay mechanics. Good game overall!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Very Polished, Very Good, Very Short.Definitely fairly priced. I really enjoyed every second of this game. Really explores ideas before they get even remotely played out and the overall tone is enjoyable. The trailer did make me expect a little more narrative, but the narrative is pretty much as deep as you would find in a Donkey Kong or Mario game.When considering Mario is over 3x the price and you can play this game while only have probably half the content it's really worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Inventive and fun, Pepper Grinder continually surprises with fun mechanical and level design. Worth trying to find every Gold Coin in each level to see the most of what the game has to offer.Most of the bosses do feel like a bit too harsh of a difficulty spike though. It feels like you don't quite do enough damage and have enough health to pull off a satisfying victory once you've learned the fight, so they can be a bit of a grind.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting little platformer, which in my opinion looks a little better than it plays. Not a bad game, but aside from the grinder mechanic there isn't much going on, say: there should be a much wider variety in level and enemy design and game mechanics to make it an actual good game. Every other mechanic aside from the grinder is just very underdeveloped. The boss fights were fun though, but they also need more variety, RNG, alternative attacks etc.I love to see more by the dev (solo dev, i think), because they did a solid work on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool game, and I hope the first of a series. The skill ceiling for movement is high, and when you get schmooving it feels really really good. The weakest part is the combat; a lot of weird hitboxes and i-frames, and 3 of the bosses play more or less the same. There are also a lot of gimmicky levels with vehicles and guns, which distract from the drilling mechanics, which should be the focus. Definitely enjoyed it over all.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Score w/o Context: Just Say When/10The Context:Pepper Grinder is the frenetic Dig-Dug that I didn't know I needed. A platformer with constant momentum pushing you forward, but much easier to learn than some counterparts in the 'time attack' genre due to the drilling cutting your momentum a bit. This leads to an approachable reflex-based design that rarely felt unfair. Constantly new, fresh ideas get thrown at you over the 4 worlds that you travel through, rarely being revisited. The only quibbles I had were the boss designs (shoutout to the World 3 chase though) and that I just want more of it (not a real knock, Id rather be left wanting more levels).
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Been following the development since 2016,  I'm so happy to say it lives up for me after seven years of hype :) I absolutely love every aspect from bottom to top, not a moment passed without thinking to myself that this belongs in a museum, it's also really inspired me greatly as a developer and it gives me so much hope for the future of gaming with masterpieces like this
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast playing this fluid platformer. The world's and levels are well designed, unique and fun. The boss fights are hard!! They are each a big step up from the easy levels but worth fighting through and dying a bunch. Is this game short? I beat it and collected all coins in about 8 hours of play and got my money's worth! Wish the devs responded more on Steam. I can't tell if they are still invested in the game but it's a buy for me regardless.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: So despite the hours it says, I actually completed this game, but it didn't sync with the steam cloud as my Steam Deck would not connect to the server and I had to do a factory reset losing all my progress. Anyway. It's a fun game with a cool traversal mechanic. I like the through back to the older style level based game play. The combat was the area I felt was lacking. Every boss felt a bit over powered.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: is a pretty cool take on the 2D platformer, it's extremely fast paced (almost to its detriment) and easy to learn, hard to master. It requires a lot of fine precision and move chaining by the end, and the final boss gets pretty difficult at times. I enjoyed this one a fair amount, but I didn't particularly blend with the speed of the game, oftentimes it led to frustration on account of being unable to chain moves with strict timing windows or see enemies/obstacles clearly at that pace. I know there's a game speed setting but it kind of ruins the unique pull of the title. By the end, I was a little fed up with it, which is honestly not the best way to feel when a game is only touching around a four hour runtime. Spent a little additional time doing time trials but gave up as difficulty increased. Still pretty happy with it. It's different and ended up being a good palate cleanser. Good fun. Also excellent on Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: A bit short for its price, it has an insane difficulty spike on the last stage and on the final boss, and the controls are sometimes a bit imprecise.Those things aside, the game is very funny, and with a beautiful accessibility feature which allows to decrease the game speed. The level designs is well structured, the secrets simple but clever, the animations are very pretty, and the game design and soundtracks are both good.Overall, a very enjoyable experience, definitely recommended for players who love platform games, and still recommended but at a lower price even for the other gamers.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is short. It took me 12 hours to 100% and see everything it has to offer. If that short length doesn't bother you, I absolutely recommend it. The movement in this game is absolutely electric and gratifying, the visual design is spectacular, and it's a thoroughly challenging experience. The sound mixing is not great at times, but the sound design and soundtrack are generally very good. Would recommend if you don't mind the length.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Delightfully refreshing little platformer. Really nails the "introduce concept, master concept, put a twist on it" level structure mastered by *all* good platformers in a super intuitive way, which makes it one of the most instantly enjoyable and engaging of its genre that I've played in a while. Just wish there was more!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: The actual traversal levels are super fun for the most part, but the boss battles are each more frustrating that the last Healing is super scarce and you will get hit, and while I'm all for a challenge, it often feels more unfair than challenging. Again the actual levels where you use the drill to move around a super fun and fluid, but the boss battles feel like they were almost designed for another game, it suddenly demands pixel perfect movement often while dodging multiple projectiles, and finding very small openings and for certain bosses and some dodgy hitboxes, I don't know if it's quite enough to ruin the experience, but it is enough to make not want to go back and attempt the last boss again.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I would say for its price the game is very much worth checking out, considering how satisfying the movement is, as well as how well the levels are built around the drill mechanic. The backgrounds were really pretty and detailed as well and the soundtrack slapped! I just wish the jump had a set distance (meaning the height is the same regardless of how long you press the jump button), as it sometimes broke my pace a little when doing the speedrun stuff. Otherwise, great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just a nice wrapped game with his art style.I feel like playing a borish plain game, i was excited before playing it.You get no upgrades, nothing to work for, just levels, which changes a little bit, it feels like someone gives you all progress and some dudes made some levels with the level editor. After reading some reviews i can see that this game can be done about 2 hours, and thats not okay, the price should be atleast 8-10 €.The only intresting thing in this game is the title screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I have beat this game 100% 3 times, this is an awesome pixel 2d platformer which when I first saw Grayfruit play I instantly knew I needed to play it. This game is genuinely a perfect 10/10 platformer, especially since they loosened the time constraints on level 3-2 (it used to be 1:58:00 minutes, but they changed it to be 2:35:00 for gold) Very cool, do recommend, play the funny Pepper Grinder game B)
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid game with a lot of very cool ideasA little rough around the edges at points (Final boss started to lose SFX and music over the course of the fight until it was just ambience, and third boss's AI broke to where she was just running back and forth across the screen), but would still highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cool little game with a really fun mechanicAll the levels are really good, I enjoyed all of them. the levels are all different.The problems are that the game is too short and the bosses are too easy (except the last one)for the rest the game is cool and not repetitive at all and with the time mode the game takes more quality.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: positives+ some bosses are cool, specifically the first and last ones+ works well on deck+ grinder surf like mechanic cool+ little additions to more mechanics as progressingnegatives- very short game about 3-4 hours long- would have been better to introduce mechanics to bosses as well to increase boss design- lack of enemy varietyoverall a cool game that is worth getting on sale
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is a fantastic game that I had been highly anticipating for years, and I am happy to say that it is, in fact, a great game. Its music, art direction and fundamental gameplay mechanic of drilling are all fantastic. I was shocked to learn that this was made by a solo dev too so no wonder it took so long to release. My only issues are the difficulty spike in the final boss and the fact it is very short. I probably spent around over an hour on the final boss which didn't feel quite right as the rest of the game does not follow the same difficulty curve. And as for its length, I was genuinely disappointed after realising my experience was coming to an end only after 4 worlds and around 3-4 hours of gameplay. I believe this game has so much potential and could easily have twice the amount of levels while remaining mechanically interesting. Although I was hoping for more, I understand that it would take a larger team to expand on this game and that if the solo dev were to make it twice as long, it would have been in development for years to come.  To conclude, despite its short length and overly challenging final boss I highly recommend this game. Keeping my fingers crossed for DLC in the future!!! :')
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's really good, but pretty short. If you don't have much interest in the time trial stuff it takes just over 2 hours to beat all the levels including "secret" levels. Time trials aren't that fun due to the number of levels that rely on a boring gimmick (slow robot, gun) or slow platforming. The only fun levels are the ones where you can dig non-stop, which are shockingly rare.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is a terrific game that is worth the asking price. It feels amazing to get into that natural flow state that you can't help but smile while playing. The art and music are top notch as well. The bosses can be frustrating but with quick resets they can be overcome without too much frustration. Also has some replay value if you enjoy getting better and better times as each level has a time attack version. I would love to see a DLC or even a Pepper Grinder 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: A sidescrolling platform game that feels like a Parkour - Donkey Kong Country. Not sure how much content there is, but it's fun to play for a while. Pixel Art and Soundtrack are pretty neat, controls are okay-ish, same goes for some of the hitbox detections when trying to hit enemies. My only gripe are the boss battles, which seem quite unbalanced, especially the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with a fantastic gameplay premise! The game is a fair bit shorter than I was hoping for, but the levels are designed as quality over quantity, so the levels it does have are quite well designed. In the future I'm hoping to see some more levels and perhaps a level editor with Steam Workshop, but I'd still highly recommend picking it up now.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic art, music, level design, and raw gameplay! The feeling of whizzing around with fast-paced digging action and grappling between dirt spots is beyond delightful! Takes my favorite mechanic of Ori and the WIll of the Wisps and expands upon it!However, similar to my experience with Shovel Knight Dig, this game just doesn't have enough content to be worth its price. 15 dollars for a 3 hour game is far beyond what I'm normally willing to pay. The game only has 4 sets of levels, but it needs like....12 to be honest. I've been following the progress of this game for a while now and was disappointed by how short it is.In short, the content this game DOES have is very enjoyable, but it is simply too short to be worth 15 dollars FOR ME. I'm still giving it a positive recommendation because I want people to support the devs and encourage them to make more of their fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is an awesome platformer. If you like 2D platformer, if you like time trials or speedrunning, this is a must buy. I lost myself into grinding the first level for at least 10-15 hours to get a better time. I hope there will be a decent speedrunning community and maybe some modding for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper is here to go fast with her grinder and to chew bubblegum. And she's all out of gum.Great little platformer that won't take too much of your time and has just the right amount of challenge. Cool pixel art, smooth movement, and a banger soundtrack. The time trials are a welcome addition to those who are looking for a bit more gameplay once the story is over.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my GOD this is so much fun. It's surprisingly simple, you only have buttons for drilling, jumping, and boosting while drilling. Even with those simple concepts plus digging through soil for mobility, so much can be done. The level design is top notch, and the Skull Coins(?) are surprisingly well-hidden sometimes. Time Attack is insanely fun to do- it's oh so satisfying to do things nearly flawlessly to get that sweet sweet Gold Skull.The story isn't much of note, it's pretty simple. I don't think there is a single line of dialogue, now that I think about it.I will say it is  on the shorter side though. You see these four hours I have (right now)? I beat the game, completed all the levels, and have now been working on getting all the Gold Skulls through time attack (I'm beaten up to all of World 2 right now). I beat the story in about 2 to 2 & 1/2 hours. Maybe I'm just really skilled, idk lolI will say that if you know Pizza Tower, this is definitely down your alley. It's similarly very fast paced, with tons of fluidity in speedrunning levels.Rating: 8.8/10Edit: So apparently due to some coding issues you can't actually 100% a save file if it's been taken from the demo. Some stickers and vinyls overlap in IDs, or something like that. I mean I love this game so I'd be fine playing it again I guess, but that fact harms my rating.Edited Rating: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game. I would have loved 1 or 2 more worlds as the game left me wanting more. But hard to fault it for that when it has:-Gorgeous pixel art. -Banger Music. -Fun Fluid Movement Gameplay.-The game constantly throws new cool ways to interact with the levels. -Bosses are actually challenging-Time Trials with medals for extra challenge after completing a level.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully crafted, poorly designed. If you have any expectations like I've manifested over the years since reveal, this is going to disappoint. Coming in blind, it's probably a blast.Desperately needs a level editor and/or mod support so the community can bring expectations to reality.Technically and aesthetically top tier though
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I was in from the very first Pepper Grinder trailer I saw. It's not exactly the same, granted, but the gameplay hook reminded me of Lorenzen's Soil in Earthworm Jim 2 for SNES. This way of designing platforming around "digging" has never stopped being fascinating to me, whether it was Jim, or Worms, or Steamworld Dig, to name a few.Pepper Grinder delivers exciting gameplay to the tune of a memorable soundtrack that's as versatile in the genres it hits as that mf KK Slider. Also I was delighted to see the inclusion of a gameplay speed option. It's a neat & elegant solution for anyone with accessibility concerns or for those wanting to tune down the difficulty a little. Conversely, it'd be interesting to see even HIGHER speeds added in the future. Still reading? Idk just buy the game--and the soundtrack too. This is another gem in Devolver's catalogue. They simply do not miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... okay at best...And the only reason (other than the boring bossfights) is the fact that the movement feels so, so lackingEverything this game has to offer screams "more speed!", and here's what I think this game exactly lacks.* A mid-air dash - I don't think I need to explain how frustrating it is to watch your character fall for its untimely death with absolutely ZERO control over it.* Your dash should refresh while jumping from one drilling area to another. - I fell atleast fifty times throughout my play-through because of that.* Keys, and  should also function as a drill.* Indicators where cannons send you.* COYOTE TIME FOR DRILLING AREAS.* Bosses should have been more chase-oriented and less about fighting them heads-on.* Some level redesigns. (gameplay, not theme)The reason I upvote this game is the amount of potential it has if some things get changed.Anyways, for now at least, if you are looking for a platformer game go play The End Is Nigh (same price) or Celeste (pricier).
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game to release for quite some time now, and I must say it was just as fun as I was hoping it would be. The controls are very satisfying and movement is very fun since you have great control (as long as you're not in the air). Level design is top notch and each level is packed with cool gimmicks, making them all memorable and keeping the playthrough fresh the entire way through.Unfortunately, the game is pretty short. Even while I was screwing around, it only took about 4 hours to beat every stage and get all the skull coins, and 12 hours to get every achievement and 100% the game. That being said, it's a great experience that was enjoyable enough for me to want to replay it again, so I'd say it's totally worth the price tag.There are a few nitpicks, such as the weird sticker system's existence (although it's kinda cute so I don't mind), a few bugs here and there (notably the final boss freezing up and not doing anything or getting trapped inside platforms and being softlocked), and level 3-2 apparently having incorrect time trial medal times making it way harder than it needs to be (took me about an hour), but I'm sure these things will be taken care of.Definitely give this game a shot, it's a pretty fun time.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is full of potential that never gets fully fleshed out. The actual platforming level feel great, especially early in the game, but it doesn't take long for the game to start hamfisting gimmicks in every level that only detract from the flow of the game. By the end of the game (under 3 hours, at that, and certainly not playing fast), I think only about half of the levels actually embrace the drill mechanic and demand you master it, the rest involve attaching something to the drill that severely limits your mobility and makes the game drag on. I wish the game leaned into it's strongest points more and expanded on the drill itself and it's speed rather than transforming the game into something it's not again and again.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome 2D action platformer where you don't grind peppers unfortunately. But what you get is a solid platformer with fast paced action, fantastic visuals and audio design, well designed levels, fluid controls, and satisfying boss fights all centered around one core mechanic which is the grinder. While one would think that this single mechanic would get quite stale after a while it's anything but that. They have executed this extremely well, even sprinkled in some unique gimmicks in between to keep things fresh and the fact that the game is quite short also helps I guess.Apart from the game being too short and the grinder hitbox being wonky on very rare instances, the only other negative I can think of is that the story is there? I guess?Overall it might not be the best platformer out now but it will give you a good 3-4 hours of non-stop fun ( probably even more if you're going for the 100%). That's honestly good enough for me to recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is fun, charming, and creative. The 2D platformer shakes up genre by using it's drilling mechanic instead of jumping as it's core loop. So, instead of running and jumping using face buttons, you'll be drilling (ZR Trigger Button) and boosting (face button) around the levels. It's novel and combined with constant introduction of new level gimmicks, it makes the ~5-10 hour journey a joy to play through. The speedrun challenges are balanced pretty well (besides from 3-2) which give you an opportunity to hone your skills.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been watching this game for a few years now. I had very high expectations when I saw it was released. TL,DR: I think it’s a very good game, and could be a great game with a few updates. It is very fun to zoom around each level. Some of the bonus coins are easier to find, but I’m almost 3 hours in and have not been able to find them all yet. I also haven’t even touched time trial mode.Each area comes with a set of unique tools and mechanics that keep the gameplay fresh and interesting. Some have felt these were tacked on, but I think there’s been a ton of thought put into the execution of each one. The grappling feels strange at first, until I realized it works differently than in other games like Flinthook and Grapple Dog. And that’s ok. It’s supposed to work differently. It works well for the kind of traversal mechanics that are in Peppergrinder. I knew this is subjective, but I vibe with the aesthetic of this game. I think the art style is just enough, not too flashy, so when things like fire breathing enemies show up, it really pops. Again, I can see the level of care that’s gone into making all the sprites and art for this game. Sound effects and music are good. Again, they fit this game very well. If we get more in updates, great. If not, totally fine too. I want to talk about game length for a moment. I can’t remember the last game I’ve finished completely. I think we have a culture in gaming that is very focused on collecting achievements, and 100% completing things. Some of these games can take over 100 hours to fully complete.For what this game is trying to be, I think the pacing is very good. It’s “achievable” in a way I think is very important. I’ll get into my thoughts on level editing in a moment, but if / when that day comes, the game could have almost unlimited replayability for me. Some things that could be considered for future updates: There are a few QOL tweaks like being able to skip the boss intros. I wanted more story building than the intro to the game had. I’d also want more and varied things to unlock. Finally, the biggest thing I think that would take this game into greatness and give it real staying power is a level builder / editor, and/or an official modding API. The inclusion of the sticker sheets is great, and shows some of the same toolset that a level editor might have. A level editor is a massive feature, not something easily tacked on. It would be much better to let that feature evolve over time, like it did with games like Rainworld and Celeste. I would give this game a solid 8.75/10, which is great for a launch title like this. Highly recommended, but do a little research first and get to know the game you’re about to drill into. It’s more than worth, if you want what this game is serving up.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Been following the game for a long time, and I'd say it was worth the wait.  It *is* very short, especially considering the game is very easy and straightforward, but it's also very polished with fluid controls, and pretty much every level offered new gameplay mechanics, cool setpieces, and so on.As far as negatives go, obviously the relative lack of content is the biggest thing, but for basically being developed by a single person, it's forgivable IMO, especially given the quality of what's there.  Also not a fan of time trials being tied to 100%ing the game (Not a fan of that in *any* game regardless of length).Overall, it's obviously not the most revolutionary, genre-defining game or whatever, but it's definitely a solid platformer, and I think it's worth the $15 price.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I wish this game was bad. Bad would be easy. "It's a platformer that doesn't live up to the promise of its mechanics" is an easy game to set aside. Pepper Grinder is almost good for its entire (bewilderingly short) runtime and for every glimmer of cleverness there's level after level that seems to fundamentally misunderstand what's fun about the game and the joy of the movement in the brief sections that flow well. I had hoped for Drilldozer 2. I would've settled for an exploration of the digging segments in Ori 2. What I got was a kind of okay Donkey Kong game with two hours of content and some absolutely atrocious boss battles. I don't want to mark this game as negative because it isn't bad it's just... not nearly as good as it could be or should be.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: A quick, fun game that sees you blasting through each level as a majestic dolphin might breach the waves of the ocean, if that majestic dolphin was bent on SPEED. While this is a short game, the price is well worth it as the music is great, the levels are all fun and original, and there are very few bugs. If you like platformers and VRRRRRRRM, you can't go wrong here.If I had to pick something negative to say, i'd say that the first and last bosses feel really wonky with how their hitboxes work, and while there is some signaling for how to handle it, it feels pretty inconsistent. Wasn't really a big fan of the boss levels, but aside from the last one they don't take very long so not a big thing. I also think this game could do with an option for "tap to hold" on drilling, so you can just tap the shoulder button (or whatever you map drill to) and have it continuously drill until you tap again. I spent a lot of time with my finger down on the trigger and came out a little sore.Neither of those are game breakers to me, and i did enjoy completing each of the speed challenges on the levels after I finished the game. One in particular (3-2) is a little overtuned I think, but honestly I enjoyed the challenge so maybe that's not such a bad thing.Overall, I'd say 8/10, definitely pick this up if you've got a free weekend to knock it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever felt the crushing feeling of waiting literal YEARS for something to come out, only for it to be incredibly middling on how you feel about it as a whole? That's this game for me. While there isn't too much that I can say that hasn't already been said, I'm still going to give my two cents as to what this game does right, and why you should still consider picking it up, even if I've got some heavy gripes with it.To preface, I'd been loosely watching this game's development over Twitter for the past few years, and was incredibly excited to dip my fingers into it day one. The steam nextfest demo absolutely fulfilled my expectations and then some when it dropped, so I had copped this game the second it came out. Not all that glitters is gold, as they say...While it's easy to notice that the criticisms listed stretch far beyond any praise I'd given this game above... I still believe it's worth picking up. The experience, when it's good, is REALLY good. That said, for every mountain so high, there's a valley just as low. The downfall comes with the lows of the game being excruciatingly demoralizing and sometimes outright frustrating, which is why some of the criticisms above are a lot more fleshed out. Buy this game, and its soundtrack, to support the developer if nothing else. It's a fun few hours, and despite the conflicting feelings, I can say I overall did enjoy the game at its core.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Product received for free via a draw at PAX WestGame is short and sweet and doesn't overstay it's welcome. However I do wish it was longer so it could have better shown off, or explored, some more of the neat game mechanics it introduces along the way.Would recommend checking it out.The dev is also a cool dude
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: You should play this game because the regular levels are awesome. With that said, holy crap would this be so much better if they had replaced the tedious, awful, no good, rotten boss battles with more levels that are actually fun. Did anyone actually play the boss levels before shipping? They're really really bad!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool indie game. I wish it was longer and it had more of the initial level's focused. The main weapon of the game is a saw/drill that you use to grind your way through levels. In the later levels, you use this drill onto other items and by doing that..create other kind of weapons. Like an actual gun. While that is cool at first, the drilling is what is what is special and most fun in the game. So I would recommend this game but I do think it gets worse the longer into the game you get. The first levels are by far the most fun. I also seem to have completed the game in about 3 hours. So I would be a bit careful with that as well. I really want to give a very strong and high recommendation. But I'd say this game reminds me of a more fun Celeste game. Just way shorter and unfortunately less focused on platforiming/drilling (especially the longer into it you go). So a weak recommendation..I guess. If you wanna try something new and don't mind the short game time..go for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder seemed to have a shot at being universally loved, with a great concept and demo. However, some issues have appeared in later stages that have caused some people to dislike the game. In my opinion, while it isn't perfect, it's a solid time. I'll try to explain why some complaints aren't that good.First off, the length of the game. Some people have somehow beat the game in two hours and have argued that the game is not worth 15 dollars because of this. A more average playtime seems to be between 3.5-4 hours, and if you had a good experience, the price isn't something that should matter that much (unless it's something egregious, like 2 hours of playtime for 60$). Doing a hour:dollar ratio seems silly to me, mostly because I enjoy short and sweet experiences, and there are a lot of long games that bore you to tears and don't deserve a penny.Another thing that comes up is how it's filled with gimmicks, and the main concept of the game (going through stages like a dolphin) didn't have as much time to be explored. I do feel like it's best for a game to end too soon than to end too late, but the gimmicks are actually really fun, with some rare issues.One issue that I kind of agree with is the boss fights. I thought the first two bosses are actually fantastic. The last two, however, have a major flaw: most of the times when you commit to hitting them, you essentially flip a coin on whether you get hit or not since you will be vulnerable for a long time, and the boss will most likely throw an attack in a direction. An example is the final boss's attacks. Some other issues I thought were exaggerated were the glitches. From my point of view it is exaggerated, because I only experienced one glitch, but that glitch can ruin a lot. It has to do with the final boss, because after dying some times, it stopped throwing attacks and stood still, making the boss obviously easy. I did restart the level and the boss started doing stuff again, but after dying a couple of times, it stopped working again. It could really leave you disappointed and leave a bad taste in you mouth.The gimmicks are consistently good, though some kind of bug me, like the gun, where your aiming is connected to your movement, so aiming up-right might make you walk right, for example. It could probably be better with twin-stick controls, but that would over-complicate the controls and would also be the only thing that controls differently, so I understand why it's presented this way. This also extends to the main concept of the game; holding down a button to drill through the dirt can be pretty uncomfortable, but changing the control to something toggle-able would probably be more awkward, since most people would accidentally drill and die.The game has a ton of highlights. Every single bonus level is a gem and worth the purchase in the shop. They are incredibly unique. My favorite levels, however, are the one in the last World, actually.  The game has consistently good standard levels, it just so happens that the quality peaks when the difficulty increases (excluding some bosses, as previously mentioned).TL;DR. At the end of the day, if you look at game-play and you think you might like it, you will like it. The controls are very responsive, and sometimes it feels like you enter a flow state where everything connects.Leaning towards an 8/10, personally.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Very short, but very fun, and charming!The base game only takes about 4 hours to beat, but if you're going for 100%, you're going to be playing for a lot more than that. There's 5 skull coins per level you have to find, plus there's time trials with bronze, silver, and gold rank for each level, and you have to get Gold on all of them if you want that 100%. currently going through it right now. The challenge is fun!Personally i think the game is worth the $15, but others might want to wait for a sale. Hope they add more to this game in the future, would love to come back to this! even if they don't, a $15 indie game you play for a week and never again is totally fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast to control. It feels super smooth to just fly through levels and collect stuff. My little goblin brain is pleased by the sensation of drilling through enemies and getting shinies. Moreover, there are plenty of secrets off the beaten path that are worth searching for. This game doesn't have to be any more complicated than that. Definitely recommended for platformer fans (or those who dabble). Not too tight, not too loose.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun! I especially love how every level has a time trial mode, encouraging you to go back and see how fast you can beat each one. The platforming is so satisfying, too. It's got this mechanic that lets you dash out of the ground, if you do it at the right time, which just feels great, perfectly dashing from one dune to the next. At 15$, this game is a steal! I definitely recommend it if you enjoy tight platformers and speedrunning.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game! The movement was fluid and fun. It wasn't a super difficult games but had a few moments here and there. My only complaint is that I wish it was longer, there's 4 worlds with 5 levels and 1 boss in each world, in each level (other than the boss) there's 5 medals hidden in the stages. My playtime (at the time of review is 4.6hrs) is completing the game and finding all medals as well. There is a time attack mode you can play as well but I can't really comment on that since I never tried it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, the level design is really creative, with some new surprise or mechanic in almost every one of them, and plenty of secrets to reward exploration and paying attention to your surroundings. There's a really good sense of speed and control, things feel very fast but you're able to react to them without problem and deaths practically never feel unfair.I wish it were longer but what's there is amazing, and for the price you really can't complain. And if you're a completionist, the time trials are a great incentive to replay the levels with a different approach.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: The movement in the game feels really good, and the game is short and sweet. I love the flow of going from place to place, chaining together drills and grapples. Everything flows really well! The soundtrack is also really good, lots of bangers.I hope that the game gets modded or has official level creation of some kind, this game has potential to be a fun platformer.I only have a few gripes, that being that the music will restart from the checkpoint in game. That sounds fine at first but when you keep dying at the same part, then it gets really grating. The second issue is that the combat is not really that good, enemies with melee weapons have the hurt box start the moment they wind up, not swinging to attack. Enemy hit boxes also feel very inconsistent and you will take damage when you feel like you shouldn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game with an amazing soundtrack that i cant get enough of you'll definitely get your moneys worth music alone. one thing people fail to mention is how re-playable levels can be trying to get a gold metal, most bad reviews on this game are really corny lmao "i really wanna like this game but but" at the end of the day to each there own so if you do end up buying this game i hope you enjoy it as much as i did.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder reminds me a lot of the kind of games you would see on the wii shop channel or early 3DS/Wii U eshop. A several-hour long game with a neat gimmick, fun gameplay, and a simple yet stylized artstyle. It’s not the most mind-blowing indie action platformer, but it’s a fun time for what it’s worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Game keeps it fresh by having different mechanics every stage, and don't get repetitive by not being too long. The accessibilty option to turn game speed down is probably the best accessibilty option that every 2D platformer need. The game was quite difficult for me but I turned it downn to 80% and it's fun & satisfying to play. And turning down to 50% actually makes boss battles bearable (I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate boss battles)Hope it get the recognition it deserves ^.^
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great game !Pepper grind is a short but geat game ! (around 5h~ish to finish the main stages) based on the trailers and screenshot, it looks like the main appeal is the grinding but there are a lot of small variants on the grinding power which are really cool to use !Did not expect the game to be this short but it's fine, I really enjoyed it while it lasted :D THE DIFFICULTY THO ! The regular stages can be tough BUT THE BOSSES are another story. They are ruthless, it took me so many tries to beat some of them, the moves are fair and all but it's still hard compared to the rest of the game.I encountered a few bugs but nothing really game breaking and i believe they will be patched soon enough !The environments and the characters are really cool, and some of the scenes are really funny, really did not expect that.Did not enjoy the shop at all. The collectibles in the stages are here only to buy keys to unlock 1 new stage per world or stickers for a photo mode and outfits (different colors, nothing fancy)Overall great little game that I could not recommend enough !
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: 7.7/10THE GOOD: Where does this game shine? The drilling. Core movement is some of the most fluid I'm come across. That's what carries the game. Finding coins and completing the times challenges is very satisfying. That and a very decent soundtrack. THE BAD: Everything else in this game is passable. The grappling mechanic feel like a quick time events. The Contra style run and gun levels are decent, but the sound of bullets gets pretty grating after a minute or so and completely overshadows the soundtrack. The Mech segments were cool, but I wouldn't say they were particularly fun. I would have appreciated if instead of all the divergent gameplay, there would have been more focus on drilling based puzzles.PLAYTIME: My first play through took 4 hours, finding 100% collectibles, but the time attack mode should double that time.SUMMARY: This might seem like a very negative review, but the drilling mechanics are so well done I would definitely recommend this game.
