_childDocuments_.review: Ah, yes, this is one of those just-one-more-level-at-2-AM types of games. If it was made back in the day for the PS1 or Sega Saturn, you can betchur arse it would've been a top seller and won the hearts of many players. There's a lot of greatness here for $15. What you can expect: charm, great pixel art, super smooth performance, very responsive controls, cool music, nice sfx, and an overworld map with plenty of replayable levels filled with hidden areas. If you enjoy games like Shovel Knight, Rayman Legends, or Yooka-Laylee, this might be up your alley.Here are the negatives that I found (which aren't big deals): 1) Loading up the game for the first time didn't use the max refresh rate of my monitor. The solution was to close and reopen the game. 2) In motion, the pixels shimmer a bit, due to the lack of integer scaling. The solution is... nothing afaik. It's just a nitpick. Hardly noticeable when I'm in the zone, making my way through the interesting levels and racing the clock. 3) By default, the drill function should be on RB (Xbox) / R1 (PS) instead of RT / R2. Holding down the trigger takes more effort than a button. Again, a nitpick. The solution is simple... go into the options and CHANGE THE GAHDDRILLIN' THING!Conclusion: Game's well-made and easily worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is an unrelentingly fun game. The developer takes a simple mechanic and expands upon it greatly, with ease and grace mostly only seen in AAA games. The moment to moment gameplay is constantly shifting and changing without becoming overwhelming or tedious. There are some really neat ideas here, like attaching different things to your drill (a key or cannon, and sometimes even a gun!! >:)), or the grappling hook which allowed for some interesting and high tension moments.It really does remind me a lot of the Donkey Kong Country Returns games. The exciting new levels, fresh ideas, challenging movement and level design never fail to amaze me. One thing I hope people praise endlessly are the visuals and ESPECIALLY the music. The pixel graphic style fits this game perfectly, and is extremely well done. Little things like the smoke trail behind your character or the lava bubbles growing and popping look incredible. And the music, oh man the music. There are so many different elements at play, like classic retro bitcrush style sounds, light jazz, and even some lo-fi and breakcore elements. The way they change and warp with the progression of the levels sounds incredible. I would highly, highly recommend this to any 2D platformer fan, or someone who can appreciate great graphics and sound/music. My personal score for this game would be an 8.5/10, which is astounding considering it came from a solo developer. I cannot wait to play more, and hopefully in the future, seeing what Ahr Ech has for us to play next!! Absolutely great work!!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and charming, albeit short. I completed all the achievements in the game, enjoyed it, and regret nothing.The game can be frustrating because of a few things, especially the control scheme. Like the toggle for the grapling hook and the fact that you must press the drill button to detach (I end up remapping the grapling hook button to the left trigger, making it much more comfortable).Right now, you can't manually aim your weapon with the right stick.Is it annoying? Yes.Managable? To some extent,.I hope that in the next update, we can skip the intro to every boss fight in the time attack mode. The final boss is the biggest culprit here. Also, please improve his first-phase hitbox. Sometimes I manage to hit him with two attacks; sometimes the attacks are not connected at all. (His attack hitbox is completely fine, though.)The World 3 Level 2 time attack is both challenging and entertaining. It was an absolute blast to grind. I heard that the time limits were set when the level was smaller, so it should be much easier to get the gold medal in the future and prevent migraines.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Mark my words. This drill will open a hole in the universe! And that hole will be a path for those behind us! The dreams of those who have fallen... The hopes of those who will follow! Those two sets of dreams weave together into a double helix, drilling a path towards tomorrow! And that's Tengen Toppa. That's Gurren Lagann! My drill is the drill... THAT CREATES THE HEAVENS!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler Free - Quick Summary:Fun mechanics, decent graphics/music but VERY short.Overall it has a solid foundation but only takes about 3-5 hours to complete (beat story + buy everything in the shop). While I do recommend the game "as-is".. by the end I couldn't help but feel I was playing an early access title.My biggest complaint with the game is the controls.  Things like the "hookshot swing" being overly clunky in execution and the final boss featuring inconsistent "bouncing" and low visibility.That said, I was a little surprised none of the capes or hair styles gave any bonuses.As far as I know there are no "power ups" in the game. You don't get stronger as you go and you cannot get permanent health upgrades. Leaving you stuck with 4HP upon death.If nothing else, it opens the door for the devs to update the game with future DLC granting unique gear/drills.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet platform game where you drill through things. It's sort of zen-like in the first couple levels until you get past the first world. It's really a game that tests your execution and precision with movement. It's got a pretty sick art style with impressive pixel graphics and animations. It's also a fresh can of new jams.If you want a platformer then you can't go wrong with this one. Especially since it has a demo.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: I finished every level and got most of the big coins in 4 hours. pretty solid experience, i wish the dev focused more on the "platforming" rather than the combat. combat was a lil wonky, the platforming and drill movement was pretty sick, wouldve loved for it to be more physics based i guess? idk a lot of things just halt your momentum and it can be a little jarring.considering there was i think one dev, id say its worth it to play Pepper Grinder, kinda bummed i had wait 7 years for it. the soundtrack is sweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a decent little game. The drilling is as fun as it seems and it's nice having all these different types of levels to experiment movement with. There are some QoL stuff that hopefully gets patched in like skipping boss cutscenes, changing how the swing hook works to holding grapple rather then having to press drill, and some other weird design choices. Overall I think it's worth playing and it's not that expensive so give it a shot!Update: Nice QoL update makes this game much fairer which gives even more reason to buy it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game!  Solid controls, inventive mechanics, each level offers something new!  There is so much in this game to break down and master and the time trials for each level are a great intensive for that, while the hidden coins encourage exploration.  The difficulty goes up quick, but the check points are forgiving. Very easy to learn, difficult to master. Very excited to see what the developer comes out with next!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: If you want the straight and simple answer: Buy it. Fantastic unique "platformer" with a killer soundtrack that you'll certainly see through the end. So many exciting things you can do with a drill and with no time wasted. That said, I have some gripes, and I hope the talented solo developer sees this.First off, the drill feels amazing, but when it comes to the grappling mechanic, it just doesn't feel right. It always seemed so clunky and took a lot of getting used, and I always seemed to mess it up. Possibly rebinding it would have been a better move, but it feels too calculated and patient to an otherwise fast-paced game. The way drilling would lead to grappling to drilling or other actions just often felt unnatural. Second, the bosses feel out of place. The in between levels and majority of the game? Immaculate level design. The bosses, save the first one and the second phase of the fourth boss? Not so much. Second, third, and first phase fourth boss don't feel like they fit into this game. They are trying to be metroidvania bosses in a game that doesn't suit that style. The first boss is probably the best one, and if there was ever more content made for this game, I would like to see a continuation off the idea there. I like the second phase of the final boss, besides the absurd VFX on the explosive attack (please patch it to be less because it genuinely makes it so hard to see what you are doing) (Edit: Though the VFX haven't changed, it is significantly less frustrating through a new patch).Third, and this could be a skill issue or not, but some of the checkpoints are absolutely killer. There are some, but not many, segments of the game that are difficult, or unforgiving and long, that make some of the levels a bit annoying on first playthrough (I'm looking at you, gun section of 4-4).Fourth, the money/gems being used for just a little gacha mechanic for stickers is a bit lame, and if someone wanted to 100% the game, they would have to spend a decent amount of time sitting there and holding one button. I also don't know why there is the ability to spend gems between every level for double the temporary health. Seems out of place, and the fact that someone COULD go and double their HP before every level or boss attempt doesn't seem right. If I were to have a suggestion for this part, drop the gacha machine entirely, make the stickers individually purchasable at an increased cost for the gems, and either make a permanent health upgrade system for a large cost of gems, or outright remove the ability to buy the temp hp. (Edit: There is now a weighing system that makes it significantly easier to obtain all stickers)
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent, albeit short, twist on the 2d platformer genre. Instead of jumping, you are drilling your way through most maps in this Devolver Digital published adventure. Pepper Grinder is extremely fun to control, despite not being that intuitive. With that being said, without typing a single word down, the game explains to you every single mechanic in a way that can be easily absorbed. The main mechanic is evolved, a few one-offs are added to keep the game fresh, and it all comes down to an honest boss fight where you have to drill to survive. Some constructive criticism, spoilers ahead:- It would've been nice to see the "one-off" mechanics stacking. Maps with vehicles are never have a mech, and vice versa.- Not using these mechanics in the bossfight for the world where you first learn them is a missed opportunity. It would've been great to do a bossfight using vehicles (at least partially). The game hinted at this with the car sequence that preludes one of the fights, but never comes through with it. Using the mech would've been harder, but IMO still possible. - Collecting stickers is a bore. Let us buy them in bulk instead of just standing there holding R2. With all that in mind, for 15€ this is a great product. It took me around 5 hours to complete, while collecting all skull-coins and trying a few time-attacks. If you're into platforming, Pepper Grinder is definitely worth buying.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is quite an interesting game. It takes the idea of digging from something like Dig Dug or Steamworld Dig but ditches the button mashing for a fluid movement system that has excellent physics and momentum. A lot of my concerns from the demo were easily kicked the curb as the game not only takes this excellent movement mechanic, but switches it up giving you other mechanics sporadically that break up the traditional game. This keeps it fresh and exciting.The game is quite easy, with the only challenge being the final boss. It's good difficulty though, it's the kind that forces you to teach yourself not to make the dumb, careless mistakes you might be prone to doing. For me, I had to learn to slow down and wait for my moments to strike. Once I did, it became fairly easy. It's also a short game but at $15, with the quality of this title, it's actually well worth it. I would have paid $20 for this experience, really an excellent indie game and one of the better releases from Devolver in recent memory. If you are at all interesting in a unique platformer with a wicked art style and fluid movement, give this a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pepper Grinder is a short platformer focused around a digging mechanic. Its intuitive controls and reasonably forgiving hitboxes for gems and interactive elements (e.g. grapple points) quickly put the player into a flow state as they zip through the levels. Every level features a new twist on the core mechanic and nothing overstays its welcome.The difficulty for most of the game is moderate (easier than Celeste, but harder than Mario), but checkpoints are generous. Each non-boss stage also features five hidden coins. These were fun to collect, although their hiding places were reasonably obvious, particularly towards the end of the game. A few more coins locked behind puzzles or more challenging platforming would have been nice.Once you beat a level you can also play in time attack mode. Advanced movement like skipping across the water and bouncing off enemies, in combination with the extra difficulty in one-shotting a level will make this mode engaging for anyone who likes to go fast.Bosses were OK and made reasonable use of the digging mechanic, but they certainly weren't the highlight. The final boss was a little annoying - figuring out the strategy to beat them was fun, but executing it for two minutes straight was not. The tiniest mistake in movement whilst drilling would often cause you to get hit, then fall, and then respawn somewhere unexpected causing you to get hit again.A few of the combat gauntlets in the last two stages were also frustrating. This is mostly due to it being a little tricky to tell whether you'll hit the enemy without them hitting you. Your grinder kills enemies on contact, unless they are at a certain point in their attack animation. This is fine when fighting small numbers of enemies but is a pain against hordes.The art style strikes the perfect balance between aesthetically pleasing, and visual clarity when moving at speed. The upbeat soundtrack is also fantastic - the drum and bass track that plays on the title screen is so good that I wished it played for the entire game.Overall pepper grinder is a fun game that makes the most of its unique mechanic. If you don't mind the short length and can look past a few issues with the last couple of levels, then this is definitely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Digging/movement feels really good in the game, it's just fun to move around, which is the most important part of a platformer. There are a couple of surprises in how you use the drill, but I would say the surprises were more charming than game-changing. The collecting feels good and the levels are built in such a way they really want you to complete time attacks.The controls feel very responsive, maybe too responsive for some people. It's because they want you to be able to adjust the drill on the fly and the game demands it at certain points. For me it's a huge plus because there's a lot of stuff you can get away with BUT they designed the game intentionally to let you discover this.I'm maybe a little less than halfway through at this review time is my guess but the game is pretty short. I had played the demo, as well, and finished it three times because I enjoyed exploring the levels and improving my times. If you like that, then the game's length won't bother you. I'm expecting to go back for time attack, the flow state feels a lot like something like Sonic or Solar Ash.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: An instant classic. Great art, very fun gameplay, creative level design, and unlocking character colors is a nice touch.That being said, I wish there was more of the game. A lot of concepts feel like they could have been expanded on. Hopefully a future DLC pack adds some new worlds or challenge levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun. I played on a controller rather than KB/M. I have only played World 1 so far in its entirety and I got Gold on all of the time trials on those levels. BUT... while its really fun to just play and enjoy the levels i played so far, the controls sometimes felt inconsistent. I am not sure how else to phrase it. It made the time trials slightly harder since Gold is already pretty difficult due to really tight times and feels like mistakes cannot be made even though it feels like the controls fight you and can cause mistakes. There are times that the controls feel great and there are cool tricks or skips that work great once you get used to them. So outside of the time trials I never really found the controls intrusive. Can easily recommend for casual fun.TL;DRGame is fun casually, but time trials are made more difficult by the controls fighting against you sometimes. Easy recommend for playing casually.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, VERY good.Bangin soundtrack, and a mix of fast paced platforming (a lot of dolphin-like swooping and diving) and occasional puzzle-ish sections.Very fun, polished.Only complaint is there's no borderless-window mode. So you either play windowed (with no 1440p option), or play fullscreen (matches your monitor resolution, even at 1440p) but alt-tabbing takes forever and streaming on (for example) discord can sometimes just not work. Borderless window would be nice.Also I have a high refresh-rate monitor and it seems the game doesn't take advantage of it. But frankly it doesn't need higher fps anyway.Although some effect-heavy sections definitely chug, its always fun light-hearted moments (like shooting a hoard of enemies). Performance never gets in the way of the challenging bits.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't realize how short this game was going to be, I still had a lot of fun with it though, and there's still plenty more to collect as far as achievements go! This is NOT your average platformer however! The levels aren't super long, I believe my longest stage was about 6 minutes, but there is a lot to the platforming than just the digging aspect, each level can feel pretty distinct and I love it! Although it took some getting used to after world 1. The bosses aren't too hard though. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute short game published by Devolver. They're one of my favorite publishers, so decided to grab this game since it's under their name and it's been a blast. Fast paced, high octane energy, secret-hunting, and even has some forgiving options for the more casual gamers if they're struggling. The movement feels super smooth and the platforming levels are really intuitive and sharp. Nice little hidden gem for sure. I plan on 100%ing it once I finish the "story".My only slight flaw I see with the game is some of the boss fights feel really simple while the regular levels are super fun to go through.

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much love and polish in this game and the ost that accompanies it is fantastic. The controls are tight, the levels are fun and varied, and the difficulty is just right. Mechanics are simple but effective in their use. My only complaint is that this game is too short. _childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to play a game built entirely around the Drill power up from Sonic Colors? Pepper Grinder is that game. As Pepper and her trusty drill Grinder you'll dive through 4 worlds each consisting of 4 or 5 levels collecting treasure, beating up pirate soldiers and drilling through all the soft dirt you see.The best parts of Pepper Grinder are when you get to chain a series of jumps by continuously leaping out of one patch of dirt into the next. Exiting any patch of dirt while pressing A grants you a boosted jump which has more than enough reach to keep a combo of jumps going. It's incredibly satisfying to pull off. In fact it's so satisfying that i'd argue Pepper Grinders weaker moments are when theres less dirt drilling to be done and the game instead throws one of its handful of other mechanics at you such as using a gatling gun to shoot enemies, or a mech suit to destroy buildings on a rampage. No mechanic overstays its welcome nor are any of them outright bad, but given the games already short length, giving up the dirt can be a bit of a downer.Controls are kept simple to a jump, grapple and drill button. Drilling feels buttery smooth and for the most part everything else works great. Grappling does come with some small issues though. Swinging in a circle as you try to line up your next jump can often feel difficult to pull off and when you need to pull a series of them off consecutively the controls may get frustrating as the game expects you to manually tap the grapple button for every subsequent grapple, as opposed to just holding the button down to lock in. As I constantly was holding down the right trigger (played on a 360 controller) to drill the whole time, the idea of releasing my finger to keep tapping to connect with grapple points, or one of the handful of barrel levels kind of akin to Donkey Kong Country, felt a bit off and I missed more then I wish. It's something that gets easier to adjust to, but one may still find weird if you're comfortable holding the buttons down as you drill.In each level there are also 5 skull coins alongside regular gems to keep you alert for cracks in the walls and other oddities. I consider myself fairly veteran when it comes to 2-D platformers and their secrets so I didn't particularly have a tough time finding all the skull coins, but just because they're easy to find is far from a detriment as they're hidden just well enough to elicit satisfaction from finding them all. These coins are used to buy keys for a hidden level in each world as well as hair and costume color changes for Pepper. There's also a gacha machine and sticker book if you want to decorate a still image of a level with stickers, though I didn't try this.Pepper Grinder isn't the toughest game out there by itself, but should you choose to pursue gold on each of its levels time attacks, you'll be in for a far different beast. Inviting you to clear each level and boss with no checkpoints in a time crunch is easily the toughest thing the game has to offer. I cleared gold in the first 2 worlds before the difficulty and time requirements both ramped up and I decided to ease off (for now anyways). In fact if you don't pursue the time attacks and just stick with clearing the levels (maybe trying for all the skull coins) you'll find that Pepper Grinders biggest crime might be in it's brevity. It took me 5 hours to collect every skull coin, and gold half the levels, but I imagine if I just gunned it straight for the end, the game would take closer to 3 or 4. As such If you plan to stick around and try for 100% the 15 dollar price tag is worth it, but if you're just aiming to clear the levels, then MAYBE a small sale would make sense.Every trailer for Pepper Grinder makes it look amazing, and i'm happy to report it plays just as well. As long as you've planned what you're going to play after it (because again you can beat it in an afternoon), there's no reason not to pick it up and go drilling.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game, makes the most of it's unique mechanics per level and has some really nice environments and setpieces. Great soundtrack too and lots of pretty art to look at. Main drill mechanic (what you use for most of the gameplay) is super smooth. Speedrun modes too if you're into that sort of thing.A little short though.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to thumbs down it because I rewlly do love so much about it. The drilling is great, the music is fantastic, it's gorgeous and it has personality. It's also super violent in a light hearted way...But. Its short. And that's ok, I'm happy to pay 15 bucks for a short but fantastic platformer...But. It's not fantastic. It has like... Half of the levels being fantastic. And some super fun set pieces.... But past boss 2, it's bosses are kinda annoying and not particularly special.And worse, it's levels have gimmicks that keep. Coming. Back. Shooting a gun? Super fun... The first time. Piloting a giant robot? Also fun... The first time. But then it keeps doing it. And these segments aren't really 'fun' they're just 'fine'. They're a power fantasy that involves basically holding right and shooting or maybe jumping every so often. It's fun... Once.And that's problem I think I have. World 1? Great, past the boss. World 2? Also great, past the boss. World 3? Ehhh.... Some good levels, some meh levels. And then world 4 which is just kinda.... Blah. It loses all of its steam and it's just 'gimmick you've seen before' or worse, 'boring gimmick' (the house stuff and smashing through it isn't particularly fun) Also, the controls are.... Good. Kinda. But they almost feel not precise enough at times and the momentum on the grapple is a pain to deal with.I think my main thing is that if it was all 'fantastic levels' it'd be an easy recommend, even with its short length. But when it's only 'half' fantastic levels, 1/4th gimmicks reused, and 1/4th boring gimmicks... It's a problem. And when the game has maybe 20 or so levels, beaten in 4-10 mins each... And at $15... I can't really recommend it.That said, the soundtrack is consistently great so there's that.
_childDocuments_.name: Pepper Grinder

_childDocuments_.review:
Pepper Grinder is an action-packed pirate adventure starring the titular Pepper, a seafaring soul with a passion for prospecting, and Grinder, her super-powered drilling device.

Shipwrecked and robbed of her treasure, Pepper must spin up her trusty sidearm to reclaim what the mischievous Narlings stole. Armed with Grinder, Pepper burrows through terrain & water, controls machines, and pulverises all enemies blocking the way towards recovering her missing fortune - with interest!

Pepper's progress will not be that simple, however, as mysterious beings begin to emerge from the shadows...

Gritty Gameplay
Cruise through a colorfully animated world with precise movements, fluid drilling, and thrilling leaps.

Thrilling Drilling
Chew through the world with Grinder and find new drill bits to ramp up the chaos and solve clever puzzles.

name: VANQUISH
detailed_description: VANQUISH your enemies in this deeply challenging isometric arcade shooter. Awaken ashore and enter the fray with reckless abandon as Gruegus, the furious close-quarters fighter—or take a more tactical approach with Zarus, the shamanic magician. Find new weapons and abilities to augment or overhaul each character's distinct playstyle, and fight to your last breath while unravelling the mystery of this uncanny, mist-mired island.

short_description: This is Vanquish! A top-down pixel art shooter where you play as either an Orc Warrior or a Gnome Magician which have both crashed onto a cursed island.

_childDocuments_.review: Directed by Shinji Mikami, VANQUISH is a sci-fi shooter of epic proportions with a fast, fluid and frenetic combat system, and an engaging and immersive storyline. Players take the role of Sam, a government agent kitted out with a futuristic battle suit, in a near future world where nations war over the planet's remaining energy resources. A versatile fighter with a huge arsenal of weaponry at his disposal, Sam also has an array of martial arts skills that he can use to take down his robot enemies.

name: VIDEOVERSE
detailed_description: Relive the days of past social gaming networks in VIDEOVERSE – A decision-based narrative adventure focusing on character development, friendship and love, from the developer behind One Night Stand . As Emmett, a young video game fan and aspiring artist, dive into this fictional video game era, where the Kinmoku Shark gaming system and its online social network, Videoverse , were still popular. Strengthen Emmett’s friendships, share fan art and browse the lively gaming communities. Make decisions that will change how Emmett grows, his approach to Videoverse and, ultimately, the final outcome! Will your actions help Videoverse thrive, or will you get caught up in teenage drama, video game fandoms and corporate conspiracies? Relive the Days of Retro Gaming VIDEOVERSE is inspired by Miiverse, MSN messenger, early internet forums and 00’s technology. The chill soundscape of the Kinmoku Shark, composed by Clark Aboud ( Slay the Spire, Kind Words ), will uncover memories of your favourite retro gaming consoles. Browse Videoverse Meet a huge cast of characters, unlock multiple side stories, enjoy the pixel doodles, and seek out the truth behind the troubled social gaming network! Personalise your Videoverse experience by choosing your avatar, personal quote and favourite theme. Join Feudal Fantasy Fans Accompany Emmett as he plays the Kinmoku Shark’s most popular JRPG, Feudal Fantasy. Swap theories and discover tips from other FF fans in its exclusive Videoverse community…and find out whether or not Hanzo will be able to stop the evil Nobunaga! VIDEOVERSE contains several accessibility options: Clear Font Closed Captions Colourblind Friendly Themes Content Warnings Sound, Music and Voice Volumes Tip Button

_childDocuments_.review: You know that dream when you go back to school knowing what you know now and crushing it? I got very similar feeling from Videoverse - it was in a way an opportunity to go back in time, use what you learned from your mistakes and be kinder to people, even if they are characters in a game. Also, kinda goes without saying, but gorgeously drawn and animated. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: (spoiler-free review) Game completed in 9 hours.I think this is my 2nd-most favourite game in the whole world.The atmosphere is so cozy and nostalgic. The music is dope (PLEASE let me buy the soundtrack), the art is so charming, and the characters are all so interesting/funny.I played through Videoverse in a "positive" way(?) Meaning, I did my best to show support and kindness to users who were struggling and I reported users who were being downright cruel/rude (tho tbh I gave some posts a pass if it gave me a laugh LOL). It was nice to see how my interactions on the virtual platform affects others and ultimately influenced the story. I'm honestly tempted to do another play-through just to see how much of a cesspool the platform could become and see how my friendships would be affected If I didn't care about bettering the community.I was kind of expecting something overly-dramatic, intense, and sensationalized for the climax/reveal of the story, but instead what you get is something  I'd recommend anyone and everyone to give it a try. It tells a very good story.

_childDocuments_.review: Videoverse is a decision-based visual novel filled with nostalgia of the internet in the early 2000’s. This is a game that will resonate mostly with those in their 30’s who experienced the early internet era, or those who were young and closely involved in the community of a dying MMO game. I am a bit younger than the target audience, but I still enjoyed the story and flashback to the golden days. Videoverse is a niche title, but one that can demonstrate both the wholesomeness and toxicity of the internet and how much of an impact video games and online friends from across the globe can have on people, especially teenagers.You play as Emmett, a 15-year-old from Germany who uses his gaming console the “Kinmoku Shark” to play his favourite game and interact with his online friends and gaming community. The game “Feudal Fantasy” quickly becomes his favourite game and in his spare time, he makes drawings on the Shark to share with other fellow fans. This quickly becomes an escape for Emmett, interacting with other people’s drawings, commenting, and chatting about the game. He already has many friends on the Shark and chats with them via the instant messaging option, also bundled with a blurry camera, although it is not able to be used in conversations as it does not feature any sound. He chats with his friends in English from across the world, learning of the language struggles some users have as they are from non-English speaking countries or may have different levels of fluency than him. He learns about the different slang associated with various parts of the world and also adopts some of it. Although he has not met most of these friends in-person, the game demonstrates how important these relationships are to him, and how much of an impact they had on his transition to adulthood. The communities quickly develop into further topics, moving slightly away from the game but mixing into every-day life topics from all different age groups. The Kinmoku Shark is being replaced with the new upgraded model, the Dolphin, and the Shark is soon to become obsolete. The moderators on the forums begin to disappear and internet trolls become more common. Not only this, but Emmett also forms a connection with a mysterious girl he met through the Feudal Fantasy community. Worried about the ever-impending shutdown of the Shark, Emmett eventually realises that not everyone has the financial means to simply upgrade to the Dolphin and melancholic feelings take over, realising he is about to lose his friends, crush, and an important past-time. Videoverse also encompasses deep conversations about game accessibility and the importance of this. It focuses on the significance of video games, and how they can be more than a hobby for many. How they can connect people to the world, to people from all diverse backgrounds, nationalities, wealth levels, ages etc. Although players can choose to behave in many ways through the different choices available, this nostalgic game helped me remember my early days on the internet, and that I too shared similar eye-opening moments online, just like Emmett. The amount of sexist comments I received in my first few years of being online was tremendously hurtful when I was a young girl, just starting to speak to the opposite sex. Seeing this replicated so well in the game with the female characters took me back to my early teens, and how I too thought this behaviour from men/boys was normal and that video games are for boys only. These moments were an important part of my growing up and whilst not every experience was a positive one, I loved seeing a game tackle this moment in time so effortlessly well. Emmett scrolls through the different forums such as “Art Corner,” “ Off Topic” or “Feudal Fantasy” and can interact with any of the posts. Choose to heart specific posts, comment on drawings, or write a new post. Reply directly to people and wait for a response. Choose to report trolls, or you can join in on the “trolling” as well. The main story revolves mainly around a girl named Vivi, but interacting through the forums provides ample side content too. Leave enough comments and you will unlock other new retro themes. Once you are finishing scrolling for the day and the story element has progressed, simply log off and when you log back in, new posts and content are available to search through. Reacting differently will unlock slightly new dialogue options and can manipulate Emmett’s personality as well as the final ending. Videoverse is split into 8 chapters and in between each chapter there is an animated version of Emmett with a few lines of voice over as he narrates and looks back on his past. The retro-style graphics match the early 2000’s era being portrayed although I must admit, many of the colour themes hurt my eyes and I had to stick to the same one to be able to enjoy the game. Characters are not voiced, except the small narration in-between chapters. The energetic retro music bounced along throughout my time exploring videoverse and helped set the atmosphere. 5 hours for one playthrough. No Yes, to see all the endings, explore further optional content and for completionists.Videoverse is a nostalgic game that helped me remember moments in time which I had completely forgotten. It highlights many important lessons that most teenagers experienced whilst growing up online. From a budding romantic interest to interacting with others from different backgrounds. Despite me being slightly younger than the target audience and not experiencing some of the main inspirations behind the game, I enjoyed my time with Videoverse and felt enough connections to the characters to keep me interested right to the very end.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: This game is lovely and you should play it...  if you still sometimes call 'emoji' 'smileys'. The extent to which this captures the feeling of a very certain time is incredible, and makes it an instant recommendation for any of those 30-somethings who had some of their most formative times on the bonkers internet of the early-mid 2000s. That's what I'll talk about first, because I fit the description to a tee (even specifically having been a regular of 'FF' forums).  I can barely express how good a job it does of recreating its period, in its own charming way. There were points when it was as if I could even feel the old muscle-memory coming back, fully returned to that IM-juggling, forum-F5-ing time that we all kinda just watched... melt away. So convincingly transportive is this forum-that-never-was that all it took was a crude drawing of a dancing badger to have me tearing up within the first 10 minutes, opening me up to a stream of such madeleine moments throughout the game that clearly underlined just how  these places were to me -  have been - to myself and everyone I shared them with, in ways I've carried with me to this day (for better or worse, consciously or otherwise).So there's that. Yes, the dressing is phenomenal - I'd heard as much, and that's why I picked it up - but that might not matter much for anyone who's never commissioned a vBulletin signature banner from XxDAGGERxX while waiting for their pals to get on MSN Messenger. Thankfully, this is all just the setting for a properly moving story about online interaction and what it can truly mean to people. I won't go into that story here, both because it'll be better if fresh and because there are no doubt plenty of other ending's I won't have seen, but I can say that it's more than strong enough to recommend the game even for those not so shamelessly smitten by the setting as I. I did encounter a couple of minor bugs, but nothing game-ruining. Just a few instances of repeating chat conversations, probably caused by my 2003-brain taking over and dragging me between forum posts and IMs too frequently for the chats to be properly recorded as 'finished' or something. Mildly immersion-breaking, but rare and easily forgotten. Other than that, though, I honestly can't fault the game. I think it achieves everything it set out to do, beautifully, and has given me something that I didn't know I needed while doing it. Thank you, Kinmoku.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Videoverse is a visual novel that encapsulates the feeling of being a teenager on the Internet, desperately waiting for your friends to appear online and refreshing forums for any sign of information. It's blended a little with the Miiverse and its inevitable closure, something that I wasn't quite a part of, but there's a lot of resonant feelings for anyone who's found solace in an online space that's doomed--as they all are--to the annals of history when it no longer becomes profitable or worth the time to support them.I think there's a few different outcomes, depending on the options you choose, and I tried my hardest to be the person I'd like to think I am, and the person I wish I could have been as a teenager--but being a teen is a time of emotional turmoil, and there's no perfect solution beyond offering as much empathy as you can to people in painful situations. I don't really know what else to say, beyond this was both nostalgic and immensely touching at the same time. Given that I have almost 4 hours in the game, it felt longer, and I'm a fast reader. It's nostalgic but nostalgic in a way that doesn't feel rose-tinted. I began using Internet communities in '02, at around the same time that this game is set (although I was a pre-teen at the time), and the game captures a lot of what that feels like. The freedom to talk to people from all different walks of life, united by a common interest--but so too are there trolls who care little for your wellbeing or adults who see you as a setback to their preferred space. It made me reminisce fondly of those days, but I don't long to be the person I was in those spaces, nor do I really want to go back to that time.What it did make me think about were my online friends, who I grew up with, who I lost contact with or grew closer to. I have one group who've managed to stay together for over 20 years, and so many of us have met each other despite the distance between us, seen one another get married, adopt pets, graduate, find their dream career--all sorts of wonderful things just from accidental meetings in a space that no longer exists on the Internet. And then there are those who I've lost, fell out of contact with, and I may not think about them daily, but I do think about them, who they might be now and what they might be doing with their lives and, sometimes, wonder if they ever think about me.Anyway--I think this game is a labour of love. It's emotionally moving, the pixel graphics are nostalgic and impressive, and I really think you'll enjoy it if you have any kind of nostalgia for a period of your youth that you spent online, for all the trials and tribulations that brought.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: "...I realised the importance of video games; how they can be a door into an otherwise inaccessible world......and how they can bring people together." After replaying this visual novel, I felt the need to leave a review.VIDEOVERSE is a heartwarming story of an aspiring young artist named Emmett, who is active in a community reminiscent of the older days of the Internet (or more specifically, Miiverse) and how his involvement with one particular member in the community would end up shaping his future.The story primarily takes place within a few months and with three characters in particular. Vivi's story was definitely my favorite from them and all the dialogue feels very genuine, relatable even. Some moments can feel rather tense or tragic, but it's important to stick with your friends and give them some time if needed. Some characters may not be fully likable in VIDEOVERSE, but its all part of the experience as not everyone is a pleasant person to be with lol. The ending is also really sweet.There's a lot of charm in VIDEOVERSE, the user interface feels rather simple and maybe even limited, but in a nostalgic way, the music further adds to this with some cozy tunes while you browse the boards. All the little stuff like being able to change the theme, customize your avatar, and even leave a custom drawing somewhere in between further adds to the experience. The accessibility options are also very much appreciated, given the overall message of the game.With all this even, there's replayability as certain dialogue choices will determine what the state of VIDEOVERSE will end up being, and even affect the relationships between the people there.As a huge visual novel fan, I was quite impressed with how much I enjoyed VIDEOVERSE, it left some food for thought and I still think about the overall message months later, as I also have some close friends I've met from the community of a game. The length is about 8 hours per playthrough, but you can get more out of it from replaying it, which I recommend as you're able to make some more connections with new knowledge in mind, and maybe some laughs as you try to unlock some of the achievements.tl;dr: VIDEOVERSE offers a nostalgic journey into an online community, containing relatable characters with impactful choices. With its replay value and charming story, I highly recommend this VN for any visual novel enthusiasts, or even those looking for a dosage of nostalgia.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: In less skilled hands, throwing about terms like 'nostalgic' and 'cosy' could easily be turned into negatives when describing 'VIDEOVERSE'. However, Lucy Blundell, the sole developer behind Kinmoku and 'VIDEOVERSE' has improved upon every aspect of her first title, the still very enjoyable 'One Night Stand'. The two games have little in common, but it is clear from the outset that it is a passion project of the developer, with many aspects of herself cleverly interwoven into the characters and the setting. Playing as Emmett in the early days of online forums in a world very close to the real one, the user can choose to make the community a more pleasant and safer space for fellow Shark owners, or do the precise opposite and add to the trolling and profanity that coarsened even forums 20 years ago and is certainly far more prevalent in today's (deliberately) polarised social media.The soundtrack complements the environment and narrative design, with some neat musical segues at particularly dramatic moments between the main characters. The art is very expressive where it makes sense for it to be, and purposefully Miiverse adjacent and equally expressive with the avatars. The characters themselves are plausible and interestingly flawed as teenagers are when discovering their own selves and the world around them. There are multiple endings to discover that hinge on choices made throughout each chapter, including how close Emmett is to his friends.I'd recommend this game to anyone who believes in seriously supporting indie game development, wants a fresh take on visual novels, and/or is of a certain age like the developer and myself who remembers what the internet was like at the turn of the century.For total transparency, I did do some beta testing on the game as a fellow narrative designer working in the industry, but all of these thoughts are my own. I also paid for a full release copy on the day it came out (today!) and I sincerely believe it's more than worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: It was an adorable and touching game; it felt authentic in its world and narrative to that early internet/2000s experience (visuals are stylized in different ways to lean into a retro feel, but I felt they fit in with the overall vibe). It is surprisingly touching in places, and there are some exciting bits of branching in the narrative as well - diving back in to see how choices affect the overall story. It was also an impressive effort for such a small team working on it - in presentation and going beyond the usual limitations of its engine. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful VN that captures the essence of connecting in online gaming communities 20-so years ago, especially for Miiverse notes (I'm from the vBulletin/phpBB days 😂)Much like One Night Stand, it's a beautiful tale about connecting and I'm going for a second playthrough NOW. Needless to say, this one hit very close to home, just when I needed it. Thanks for another gem, Kinmoku~
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: I bought a PS5 in January and have played a bunch of epic AAA titles and yet Videoverse is the best game I've played all year. I really loved the story and the characters. It captured a time that I didn't really ever experience - I was kind of too old for early internet messaging when it first became a thing and never had a handheld console growing up. However, I remember being obsessed with certain games growing up and most of all I remember a time when it seemed like that was all that mattered. The emotions this game provokes are so real I found myself feeling nostaglic for a console that never existed. There is so much going on in this story, it's not just about games but also about people and how we try to use technology to connect and how sometimes that's perfect and sometimes it really isn't. I'll be thinking about this game for a very long time.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to the heyday of internet forums. This made me so nostalgic for a couple of communities from back in the day (Storiesville and The  message board, I'm looking at you!) The community interactions really ring true.The graphics and music are great, it's fun to explore the forums and have a go at drawings. I loved unlocking themes for the Shark as the game progressed.The storyline is sweet without being too sentimental, and it feels like your choices matter in the game.My first playthrough was 5 hours and I have around half the achievements to unlock. I'd definitely go back to try and unlock more endings and artwork for the gallery.Overall, a delight!
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Without going into too many spoilers, in the age of a lot of games today starting to have a broader range of accessibility features, this is one of a few games I've seen that talks about the impacts a disability can have on enjoying them. As a person born with cerebral palsy, that's very important to me. I'm glad I was able to experience it. Play it a few times, if you want -- there are a few alternate routes and things to find. But I think I'll be happy with the ending I got my first time; I think it matters the most to me.

_childDocuments_.review: is one of the most moving games I've played in a long time. I stayed up way too late last night playing through it. It's a visual novel game told through the framing of a Mii-verse-like chat/community. I don't know how many of you harken to the days of the 3DS and Wii U having community-based drawings straight on the device itself.Communications is done with others through liking a post, commenting on them -- and the entire interface of the "Shark" device is 1-bit black and white with gorgeously done hand-dithering. The Shark device is something like a desktop dual-screen Gameboy-ish with grayscale graphics. It evoked strong feelings of nostalgia, of first loves and friendships online.There's also a RPG-story-game told within the game itself, quite a neat meta-narrative. I really liked how in this game, choices and the things you do actually matter and impact your interactions with others. As a disabled person, I especially appreciated how the creator touched upon disability and ableism.Now to go play through it again ...
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely well done visual novel, that has an interesting twist in how you play it, interacting on the fictional "Videoverse" platform. For everyone who grew up on the internet, it really catches the whirlwind of growing up online, being a cringy teenager and having experiences online that form you as a person. Loved it. Kudos to the developer!
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: I do not know where to begin or event how to fully express how this game made me feel. Growing up in a rural area in the early 2000s, I didn't have any friends. I was an awkward kid with a lot of trauma; PC games and early internet forums/chat rooms were my escape. I love this games theme of accessibility for those with disabilities. Such an important message. This game captured that early internet feeling. I, too, wonder where some of my early internet friends are now in life. I've lost contact with them all. I had friends from all across the world. I'm in my mid 30s now, so I don't have the chance to play video games like I used too. Some games are just ... hard to get into. I was fully immersed the moment I logged on as Emmett into Videoverse. Thank you developers for creating this wonderful game that made me feel all sorts of emotions. I can't wait to see what else this team can do.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really cute and possibly the most nostalgic game I've played. An idealised version of early internet and forum interactions and community that really shows the love the creator holds for that era. It left me feeling purely grateful for the experience in a way I can't think of another time I've really felt. The main character having the same name as me helps, lmaooooo~
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: A game seemingly made for my generation of proto-internet users, those people who've watched social networks form and grow and die and become the messy juggernauts we try to use today. This game so perfectly captures those nascent years of the immaturity of youth and the technology itself in a very moving story. In the same vain as the in-game art, the 1bit medium manages to capture such emotion in the characters along with its fantastic writing and an interesting reactive score.Absolute must play for anyone who grew up with this stuff
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: I was there for the real beginning of the internet in 1992-1993 when the public first got on.  I came from Compuserve and had an Apple Mac LC2 computer.This game is slightly more into the future.  It kind of melds the old days I remember with a little of the new, and I think it's absolutely charming.This is a one-of-a-kind experience.  Get this on sale, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: i will never get over how beautifully made this game is. thank you thank you thank you @kinmoku <3 many tears were shed.also, it makes me so sad to see this game only have 48 reviews. this game was made perfectly. the dialogue! the art! the story-telling! it was all top notch. give this game the love it deserves <3 sometimes i wish i was a famous gaming influencer just so i can help promote games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: I was not expecting to be so involved in the story, its characters and stakes. I also was not expecting the impact of the player's choices to be so important to the story (I only discovered that after completing the game and looking at the achievements).Sometimes the writing can lack a little bit of "oomf" especially at the begining, but that gets better and it didn't prevent me from being totally immersed in this online community story and its short-lived friendships. I'll remember these characters for quite a long time.It's full of smart narrative ideas, and the overall writing content is incredibly dense, varied and coherent for such a "small" game. What a triumph!
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: The internet of the early noughties was a very different landscape than today, and VIDEOVERSE captures its feeling perfectly. I think many people around my age (30-40) have experienced something similar to the central theme of VIDEOVERSE - an online community slowly fading away, leaving only a longing for times that have passed and can't be recreated.Populating this nostalgic fictional internet landscape are a wide variety of characters to interact with. All are well written, interesting, and unique, and genuinely feel like real people. It's up to you how much or little you want to interact with them, and how you want to treat them, and your choices do actually impact elements of the story.Some wonderful music and a variety of well-executed art styles round out an excellent game. There are tons of little references and easter eggs to find too!VIDEOVERSE really resonated with me, and I'm not ashamed to say I shed a few tears by the end of it. A wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: As other people have mentioned, "VIDEOVERSE" captures the experience of being in a close-knit online community (in the early 2000s) incredibly well, but that's certainly not its only quality: The characters are compelling and well-written, the game has a touching story offering different routes and endings depending on your choices, and the graphics and sound/music work really well together. I finished it in two sessions and thoroughly enjoyed my time with it. Highly recommended for everyone interested in story- and dialogue-heavy games with a lot of heart.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Since this game is being shown to even more people, I just want to give it the review it deserves and say that it's an adorable game that really captures you into this feeling of being in a tightly-knit online community! The VIDEOVERSE is the best possible medium for a visual novel so even if it's not your thing, I think you'll have an incredible time with it!!
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: A fresh, authentic and kind game that is 110% worth your time.  It feels so much like you're really participating in an online community and a lovely ongoing story that you don't even think about suspending disbelief, you just keep going and going, and interacting... and it's just a great experience!  Sometimes it moves on without you being able to see all the content, but it's not a big deal.VIDEOVERSE isn't flashy, fourth-wall shattering, or ripe for memes, but it might sincerely be the best game in the genre at depicting us.  It's my new favorite.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: VIDEOVERSE captures the early 2000 internet relationships in an honest and moving way that is irresistible.It really brings to the forefront our human need to connect with one another, even if our tools were simple then. It makes me feel grateful for having experienced that time when the internet was still in its early days, the games were impossibly huge in our imaginations, and the simple contours of these nascent digital spaces were burned into our memories.I binged the whole game in one sitting and highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: With this game’s brilliantly authentic and cosy design and heartfelt narrative, this is a true labour of love which I’m so glad I got chance to experience! It’s a really nice gateway into reminiscing on your adolescence, having fun just chatting with friends online and talking about video games.Full Video Review: *SPOILER-FREE*In what is such a comforting game to play, Videoverse delivers bags of nostalgia in a love letter to early 2000’s internet forums, messengers, and the technology. Personally, I grew up with MSN, Piczo and gaming magazines, so this game hit me right in the good place. The game boils down to playing on the Kinmoku Shark gaming system and losing yourself in Videoverse, its online social network. This is essentially a social media simulator from the early 00’s but trust me when I say there is a mature and relatable story at its core which is full of heart.Both the main and the side characters are all grounded and believably written, with folks from all walks of life to be found whilst surfing the forums of Videoverse. It’s honestly a case of the less I say the better, because due to this game’s heavy focus on narrative, interacting and learning about the community is one of the strongest aspects of the game. A lot of your time will be dived up into doing two things, surfing through the videoverse forums, and chatting with friends via private chat. Both of these feel incredibly authentic, and I sometimes forgot I was playing a game and felt like I was just using social media as I would in real life lol. You’re looking at about a 6–8-hour experience with this if you focus mainly on the core narrative, but with multiple endings, you could easily get up to double digits in terms of play time. This game is an EASY recommendation, and I hope you find time to sit back and enjoy Videoverse just as much as I did.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: A very well written game that perfectly encapsulates (an idealized version of) the early internet days of tight-knit niche hobby communities and everything they could mean to their members.The characters are very well-written, the plot nails the bittersweet nostalgic mood perfectly, and is presented in a very original manner. Everyone that grew up during these years will feel fuzzy and nostalgic while playing itOne very small criticism is that the music is a bit repetitive and not always matching the emotion conveyed by the scenes its in.Don't let it deter you from enjoying the game, it's really a small gem that made me feel like an akward teenager all over again.Thanks to the devs, wishing them a lot of success on their future projects, this was truly great stuff
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the most appealing character portraits I've ever seen. Emmett is the cutest boy in the universe. I haven't seen anyone get this much emotional mileage out of a handful of pixels since Undertale. Every expression, no matter how subtle, reads clearly and immediately. If you know how to read, you should check this game out, it's pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: It's like looking into my teenage years and have an opportunity to be a positive force, with all the knowlege I currently have. A very unique, peaceful and almost therapeuthic gaming experience, I loved playing it at night after work to disengage from my hectic life. Beautifully drawn and animated, with lovable characters. I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Videoverse is beautifully rendered depiction of the world of internet fan communities in a past not so long ago. If you’ve ever been someone who compulsively checked your friends list to see if a certain someone was online so you could maybe send them an awkward message, this game will speak to you.This is a story about being young, awkward and coming of age online. I found myself cheering for the protagonist Emmett as much as I was cringing with self-recognition at reminders of things I’d say in instant messages and fan forums as a teen who wholeheartedly believed there were kindred spirits on this new thing called the world wide web.And while Videoverse will especially strike a nerve for players with nostalgia for the early 00s pre-social media world of message boards and fan sites, I think anyone who’s ever found (and/or lost) friends online will feel touched by something in this story. Though draped in a retro aesthetic (which is beautifully handcrafted and often jaw dropping), this is really just a story about the struggles of finding identity and human connection as you’re figuring out your way in the world, and the ways technology can both help and hinder you on that journey. I've found myself thinking about this story and these characters a lot long after I finished playing. There's plenty to come back to -- this is a visual novel at its core, so you can expect that one playthrough won’t get you the same story as the next when you know what choices branch to what  -- but even if you just go through once, the game's mix of tech nostalgia and human drama will stick with you.In the interest of transparency: I playtested Videoverse during its development. One of my own game projects is playfully referenced in portions of the game as well.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: 2003 was a special time for a lot of people that were deeply involved in the internet. I was knee deep in AOL, Yahoo, and MSN messenger chat rooms, various Live and Deadjournals, Xangas, MUDs, Neopets, GaiaOnline, obscure builtin boards, forums, GameFAQS, God knows what else.  Had a laundry list of internet friends, some who I barely knew but still talked to a ton, others I knew waaaay too much for a 14 year old. It was the best of times, it was the worst of times. But all things come to an end eventually. We saw the rise and fall of so many internet communities over the last 20 years. Lost contact with more friends than I can count. And you know, for a brief few hours? This game put me right back into that space. Casuals friends that you enjoy talking to about whatever your latest obsessions are, showing off your (sometimes awful) fanart, sometimes getting a little too serious... Man. Thank you for making this game. As far as the game itself goes, it's a pretty neat little VERY lo-fi early 2000s internet culture aesthetic visual novel. While the cast isn't huge, you get to know and adore pretty much all of them over the time it takes for you to complete your first run. Sure, there's a few hiccups here and there. Stuff like certain chats not triggering until a minute or two later. But nothing that hampered my progress for too long. I look forward to a replay in the future to see how much different of an ending I can get on the second go around!
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully and carefully crafted tale, evoking the bygone age that never quite was of the Kinmoku Shark console's online community. The art's a lovely mix of the console's 1-bit graphics, combined with full-colour glimpses of the 'real world', the audio encapsulates the feel of a past era, and then the writing - it's all so well done. Characters feel *plausible*, there are motivations and desires to be discovered, egos to be reassured and trolling to be pushed back on.If there's any real 'negative' it's that you may find you end up with a very, VERY late bedtime, as the desire for 'just a little more' is so strong!Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic short video game experience. A cast of characters, many of whom you will likely recognise if you ever engaged in similar places. Even if you didn't its a great wee time machine to check out what it might have been like. Beautifully animated with a great interface which really sucked me in to the concept. It's not going to be for everybody but if you love visual novels told in a different way then I really recommend you give it a go. It's lovely.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Strong recommendation on this one. Positively heartfelt and downright bittersweet at points, and hits the spot for nostalgia that I'm too young to have really appreciated. This game is definitely one of the greatest releases of 2023, and it has multiple endings, even though the one I got first was the most satisfying.The soundtrack is also made by Clark Aboud, who composed the OST to Kind Words, another game I enjoy with a (extremely loosely) similar premise. Also present is voice acting by Mark Ota, who voiced four characters in the 2022 Live-A-Live remake. What's not to like?
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: A game packed in nice interface, but it's still a visual novel at the end of the day with zero quality of life features.What distinguishes the game is its presentation. And it's fantastic. A large portion of the game takes place on your desk, primarily on your video console. It involves a VIdeoverse interface or software, which is similar to today's gaming hubs. It offers a main screen that displays your profile, friends list, chat rooms, and a few more icons. The fact that practically everything can be clicked on adds to the fascination. You can, for example, update your profile and theme or visit your friends' pages. However, because the main genre of the game is visual novel, it doesn't really expand after the first few minutes. To advance the story, you must still click the appropriate icons and read a lot. Instead of monotonous squares with text and profile symbols, the story is told using a chat app and a webcam. Making the game feel authentic has one disadvantage. The pace is extremely slow. You need to wait every time the console boots up, there's a "person is typing" message during conversations that forces you to wait a few seconds, and so on. The story follows your character, a kid who wants to become a game artist. It primarily focuses on friends made in the Videoverse and how things will change when the next console is released. People are concerned that they may lose contact if the old platform is shut down.The gameplay is identical to that of any other visual novel, but there is a bit more interactivity, such as writing or liking forum messages, making new friends, and even reporting inappropriate posts. Various outcomes may result from how you respond to them. You have some control over how you approach something. However, while there are always at least three options for each post or comment, the majority of them aren't all that different. All take you down a similar path, but some allow you to tag various persons, which results in diverse responses on boards. Some, though, will be locked based on your choices throughout the game. In general, you can be helpful, neutral, or slightly mischievous.Once you've finished responding to and liking the comments, log out and move on to the following day. Every day, old threads are removed and replaced with new ones, so you must do everything you can to get the whole experience. Because there are so many various outcomes while dealing with your friends' troubles, you might want to play the game again. There are a number of achievements that may only be obtained by picking particular responses. However, the game likes to waste your time because you can't skip stuff you already saw on your first playthrough. I definitely won't be playing it again.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It feels really nostalgic for several eras of gaming - Dreamcast, Nintendo DS, Wii U - and scratches the same itch as something like Retro Game Challenge. But it's also about formative online interactions and the friends you make at a distance.For a decades long gamer like me it's really special. But I suspect this is relatable to any generation who has ever made friends online.The best thing about this game... It's not one of those visual novels where all you do is read. You're interacting and making fun choices all the time!Get this game!
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Videoverse is an excellent visual novel told through a computer console back in 2003. Many users of the Shark complained about how much of a dinosaur the Shark was.  Many friends were made through the Shark's Videoverse. The newest hype was the technologically advanced Dolphin. The Dolphin would cause many friendships to be lost made through the Shark's Videoverse. The 2 main characters were teenagers in love, and the interactions between the both of them were very interesting.Issues: On Chapter 2, I had issues and reported inappropriate posts and liked all the positive posts. I was led to a dead end twice. I restarted the game from the beginning twice. The third time, I progressed through the rest of the story, and although the developer claims that the bug was fixed, it still exists. The issue I found in Chapter 2 is that everything was procedurally generated, and if you reported a person more than once the game wouldn't let you continue. I noticed the main culprit was that I reported the same person too many times, and when it came time to report another person, the program said I reported too much, and it would take time to report again. The bug still exists. Once I past Chapter 2, the game and dialogue really opened up, and became very interesting. Overall, a very good visual novel, but yes that bug needs to be squashed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gorgeous and fun game about life in the early 2000s for kids who could be connected online. It pulls at the heartstrings, it reminds you of forums and private chats; although I have to say I was *sweating it* in a good way to play as a teenage boy. If you are a fan of immersive narrative games, this will be your jam too. The sound designers do a great job (Clark Aboud, Alexandre Carvalho), the Shark's loading music felt perfect and realLucy Blundell nd the rest of the team made a game I keep recommending to people, and I'll be replaying again soon for more the different storypaths.  I very much hope Lucy makes another game.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Very much 10/10 game in its niche.I was blown away by the atmosphere of hanging around Internet communities. The game replicates that perfectly, the good: chatting with friends and getting excited about games, oversharing personal life, jokes, and laughs, and the bad; trolls, haters, and drama.I love how, despite it being a Visual Novel game, it has a lot of gameplay elements like voting, posting, checking the desk, and deciding with whom we speak first. I discovered a lot of references and some hidden stuff (typing codes into the status panel!), but I'm sure I still missed plenty, so a second playthrough is definitely planned.The Visual Novel part; dialogues, characters, choices and consequences, as well as 2D art and animations, are very well done.Although one thing troubled me:
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: I was homeschooled throughout the entirety of middle school, starting right about when the pandemic started. During that time, I had very few people in my life. In real life, the only people I had were my parents and my dog, I didn't leave the house very much, I was chronically online, and spent most of my time wasting away on the internet. In that time though, I met a group of online friends that were there for me when not many others were. The original group chat was made on November 31, 2020, and we have all been best friends ever since.VIDEOVERSE is about making friends on the internet, and with all that given context, you could probably understand why it would hit close to home for me.There were so many times while playing this game where I felt personally attacked by how much I related to some of the characters, mostly the one you actually play as. The main character is introverted, awkward, and kinda nerdy, which was so easy for me to relate to when I could legitimately picture conversations I've had with my friends where I was doing the same ♥♥♥♥. There was also a ♥♥♥♥ ton of stuff that reminded me of my friends, but I won't talk about that because I don't think they would be comfortable with me just sharing it randomly. BUT KNOW THAT THERE WAS A LOT THAT REMINDED ME OF THEM.The only complaint that I might have about the game is that to get the full experience of the game, you actively need to have been through most of what the game talks about, but even then its still a compelling story line to follow.Towards the end of the game I was shedding tears left and right, especially since there was one friend in particular that I was reminded of so much. This game hit so close to home for me so many times, and I'm glad I got to experience it. Also, to the devs, props on doing such a good job capturing the awkward feeling of a chronically online teenage boy using the internet too much, because I was (and tbh, still am) one of those people and I felt legitimate second hand embarrassment at some of the things I was forced to say. Thank you for this game, 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful visual novel. The writing was excellent, and I really enjoyed the story. For people who are interested in this game because they want an experience similar to Hypnospace Outlaw, this game isn't quite the same sort of thing--it is much more "on rails" and is more of a visual novel. It is still really great and has a wistful, nostalgic feel.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely interesting game, that gave me the biggest feeling of reminiscence to a simpler time of online internet and forums, where we didn't know everyone, and we were part of smaller communities, full of random and mysterious people. I would never say I will fully be able to experience what the old internet was like but this game did remind me of the old communities I interacted, whether they were inside games or even in the internet before the boom of social media. Maybe it's nostalgia or whatever, but if this game is fantastic in anything is its presentation and the sensation you get by experiencing the 2000s.Other than that, I gotta give props to the message of the game, that while perhaps not having the most rigorously interesting characters with a lot of them feeling kinda mediocre, it still had a compelling story, that definitely hits hard and delivers in the end.TL;DR: Definitely recommend it if you want to experience how old internet forums/message boards were like.
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth giving this game a go to relieve the era of MSN. This game is such a nostalgia trip for the online culture of the 2000s. I had flashbacks to my youth playing this game, and for anyone who thinks that would be more fun than horrifying (it was a little of both for me) this is a game for you. The story is simple and sweet, and more branching than I expected. Give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: VIDEOVERSE

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of Hypnospace Outlaw, which has a similar type of premise - interact on a fake interface, make connections with people, learn about people's lives through the interface. This game is so beautiful. I feel really lucky I stumbled upon this game. Really touching story and I love all of the branching paths - definitely want to see how all of the scenarios play out now that I finished it! The art is gorgeous as well - it reminded me of my time on Flipnote Hatena as a kid.I could tell just by playing that the developers of this game clearly loved this game, and they really put their soul into it. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A heartwarming and nostalgic experience that takes you back to simpler times before social media. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful love letter to video games and online communities. _childDocuments_.review: There's not a game like this that I've ever played in my life.
