_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the last mission so wanted to write my review. Pros:- Fun tactical mechanics- Good variety of character types- Interesting world/settingCons:- Levels can feel like a puzzle with a fairly narrow way to win at times (though this was improved recently)- The story and characters are a little thin and you probably won't really care about them beyond what they can do during the level.Overall I enjoyed this game, a tactical turn-based superhero experience is basically like my perfect venn diagram for a game. And while Capes isn't perfect, I think it's worth playing if you've wanted to scratch that itch like I have.They recently did a balance update, which I think made the game overall less "puzzle-like" as a lot of people were criticizing it for. That isn't completely gone, but you don't feel like you HAVE to do every optional goal to get more upgrade points. By the end of the game I had way more upgrade points than I needed, so I would recommend people to just play the goals they think are fun and not try to 100% everything if they don't want to.The stealth missions are probably my least favorite part of this game. The way line of sight works feels very inconsistent, and if you're anything like me, you will get frustrated at times because an enemy saw you across the map because you didn't think they could see through a tiny crack between two walls. But to be fair, I don't think I've ever seen stealth in a tactical game work well.I thought the world building in this game was super cool. A city that's been secretly run by supervillains for years, and the superheroes of yesteryear grappling with their failures that led to it. With such a cool world, the character writing isn't really anything special. It tries to be an emotional story with big themes, but feels a little hollow and underdeveloped to me. Without spoiling anything, I felt like the final mission was VERY anticlimactic. I was surprised the game was over because the last mission felt more like a second-to-last mission and not the finale.So to sum up, if you want a tactical game that has some really fun mechanics (the power team-ups are great!) and you like superheroes, I'd recommend this game. If you get overly frustrated with puzzle-like levels  and some weak writing, probably skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: I do really like this game and I want to say that before I continue.The game itself is good, tactical x-com style game with superheroes. They have different abilities, different ways to "team up", terrain is interact-able, and overall the combat is fun.However, the game is also very hard. I found myself needing to bring the "tank" character for every mission, and every mission has the sub-goal of no heroes being downed.And when you're in a battle, sometimes you'll be completely swarmed by enemies with guns, and when one of your characters has 3 pips of health is isn't very sustainable.Granted, characters can give eachother shields, make line of sight terrain and taunt enemies, so you'd think "doesn't sound so bad!" But then enemies spawn behind you, or you have to disarm enemies which takes a whole turn.I'm sure if you read this you'll think "get good!" and I agree! Overall I've enjoyed my experience playing, I'll continue to play!  The combat is difficult but satisfying when you win, but the "get good scrub" inside me wishes there was an easier mode than there currently is.Overall I still recommend. Fun/fun

_childDocuments_.review: So a lot of people have talked about how the game is rather puzzle like, and how they don't like that because it's basically... not like X-Com.Well, I'm going to say something radical, not every strategy game needs to be like X-Com to be good.I think Capes is quite good from what I've played of it. The tactical combat is interesting, and I like how each character has not only their own "play style" but also how they all can "collaborate" to do combo moves with each other.The story is... OK. Not amazing, but not terrible. I genuinely like the character designs.

_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: I've beaten the game from start to finish.It definitely scratches the tactical-strategy itch I've been having for a while! While it's not exactly X-COM or Freedom Fighters, it does stand out as it's own simple tactical strategy.  If you're expecting character creation or base upgrades, I will tell you right now, this is NOT that kind of game and you're expecting something that shouldn't be expected in the first place.  However, that is not to say this can't be expected in a sequel or any future interpretation of this series.  So in full honesty:It's 8/10 with an opportunity to be better next time, (if the game has a future).The building blocks are all there and I recommend getting it on a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of Atlas Reactor a bit. Unique heroes in X-COM style grid combat.Sound needs work, voice acting varies between acceptable and atrocious. Gameplay is closer to puzzle than tactical; If that makes sense. You can see what range each enemy has and what threat they can bring to where next turn so it's less of a cover and tactical positioning and more of a puzzling out the right combo of abilities to let you get through the situation.Winning standard matches has been somewhat easy so far, getting all the challenges makes it harder, which you are going to want to do since those challenges let you improve your heroes.All up: Do recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: When I started I play through of this game I didn't really know what I was expecting, I've never played a game llke it.It is such an amazing game to learn how to play strategy, turn based games.I fell for the characters, the story and the whole message behind the game. It's a rollercoaster of emotions that you have to try. !00% would recommend to anyone
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: Three hours in and all I can say about this game is it's "okay."The good:* The game runs great. I've experienced zero technical issues running the game.* It has a great aesthetic. The game does a great job of making you feel like you're playing in a comic book.* Missions. Missions are decent and they give you a fair amount of tactical decision-making.* Game mechanics. Planning actions and using powers is probably the high point for this game (aside from the aesthetics).The bad:* The writing and story are just terrible. It's so bad that I'm just skipping cut scenes. Nothing about the characters are interesting. The storyline is cliche and boring. The dialog is downright atrocious. And of course the girl with blue hair is a lesbian (who couldn't see that coming from a mile away?).* No arena mode. Let me pick some heroes, select a map, define the bad guys, and just fight a battle. It's sad that so many tactical level games fail to give you this feature.If you're looking for a fantastic superhero tactical game, then go play Freedom Force vs the Third Reich. FF is so feature rich (including an arena mode), great characters, a fun storyline, and a great aesthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: 30 hrs in and I'm about halfway through Act 3.This is clearly a low budget indie game.... but it's not a bad game.The Gameplay is fantastic! A+! Love it! It's basically X-Com Chimera Squad with a Superhero paint job.The Story and setting is ok... 5/10 not great, not terrible. Writing is mediocre and the game is entirely linear which is a major weakness.Characters are hit and miss... the powers are all interesting and unique... but I didn't fall in love with any of the characters. I couldnt tell if one of the characters was suppose to be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Would have been nice if they had implemented a class system and allowed players to custom build their own characters and team.Probably the biggest drawback to this game are its cutscenes. 1/10. Every cutscene uses the in-game engine and reflects the low budget nature of this indie game. If the franchise continues hopefully they will get a bigger budget and have some nice cinematics. Call me old fashioned, but I like video game cutscenes. They improve the flow and story telling.

_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: So the actual meat of this game - the Turn-Base Combat is quite enjoyable. The setting and idea behind the story also not bad.  Where the game stumbles is in some other key areas.  Costume designs and even the graphical display of character powers is vastly underwhelming.  They seem bland and used abilities aren't as impressive as you might expect - at least not from the little I've seen so far.  Maybe that will change further down the road, too, hopefully. The first main villain you encounter is Crashdamage and he has possibly the most boring presentation and costume I've ever seen in a superhero game (a black tank top, wow, so cool...not)Voice-acting is mostly uneven or not great, with Rebound's (the purple-haired female) voice-work the most cringe-worthy at times.  I appreciate having the voice-acting but this is always a risk. Character graphics are odd, they look bizarrely plastic to the point you almost feel you're playing a game using plastic dolls. And the fact that you cannot create your own character is certainly a small disappointment as well.  I like the cool team-up abilities idea in combat so that was one nifty innovation, though Marvel Midnight Suns thought of this in a slightly similar way too albeit in a more minimalistic fashion. The game badly needs more background ambiance and audio and it could've really benefited from some sort of base-building feature, too.Another minor concern is that this seems like yet one more modern game that's flush with some DEI elements and it's something we see a lot with games from the UK area (annoyingly).  By DEI I'm referring to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion elements that feel extremely shoe-horned into the game to appease some woke expectation. The only other game that was as distracting in this way was from the same genre was Miasma Chronicles, which had laughably inappropriate demographics filling unrealistic roles in that game.  This one doesn't necessarily have that particular issue but it does seem like each character who shows up is meant to tick some DEI-approved boxes.  Which is a shame.Overall I'd recommend this however, because it's your only true super-hero TBS/X-Com style game and has great combat. Marvel Midnight Suns is the other but it's very much a hybrid arena-style game instead. I'd give this a 6 or 7 but it's sad because it could have and should have been so much more.
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

Boss fights at the end are a treat!You will probably like this game, if you like X-Com: Chimera Squad, Hard West 2, Showgunners, Tactical Breach Wizards

_childDocuments_.review: I already enjoyed the demos a lot, and couldn't wait to play the full game. And I was not disappointed! The visual art style reminds of comics, which fits in perfectly with the super hero setting. Personally, I find it refreshing to meet new, unknown super heros here. _childDocuments_.review: I liked the game just doing the intro missions, which were pretty linear and really what I wanted from a turn-based superhero game. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of this genre and greatly enjoyed this game. It is very similar to XCOM: Chimera Squad in style, but I think the execution is significantly better than Chimera Squad-- the game is more fun and feels like less of a grind because each mission is bespoke. In fact I was impressed with the sheer amount of content-- there are a lot of unique missions in this game! I will also say the game was 100% bug-free and ran like butter. Really appreciate the devs not wasting customer time with a half-finished product-- it's been a while since I played a game that ran so bug-free and smooth.I have seen people complaining about difficulty and "puzzle-likeness"-- let's address those complaints.Regarding difficulty: I played on the hardest difficulty all the way through and completed every optional objective. I was able to beat every mission with all optional objectives the first time I encountered it-- there was only one mission I had to go back to with a stronger team. The game felt  nearly perfectly balanced to me, with each mission posing a significant challenge to get all the optional objectives in one go. In fact I would say the balance here was the best I've encountered in the genre since XCOM 2-- the difficulty stayed just about right all the way through (if I didn't aim for all optional objectives in each mission it would've been too easy).Regarding puzzle-likeness: It is true that the missions are much more "puzzley" than something like XCOM. Especially early in the game, you need to play in a very specific way to hit all optional objectives. Personally this didn't bother me, it was still quite fun. Later on, when you have a variety of leveled up heroes, the "puzzle-likeness" fades as you have more options for each mission.My criticisms are minor:- The writing, story, and voice acting are very meh and medium-woke-- you lead a full United Colors of Benetton multi-ethnic team of heroes, complete with a genderqueer homeless youth, against an evil corporation. Despite the multicultural makeup of your squad, every single evil thug and supervillain is white. Make of that what you will. It was moderately grating but fortunately the game didn't do a bunch of sanctimonious lecturing, with a pretty standard comic book story. Overall it didn't much detract from the game.- Quality of life is mostly good, but there were a few times where I was a little unclear on a mechanic-- the game could do a better job of giving you more info in a few places. In particular:    - Seems like if you kill an unaware enemy with the extra half-point of damage from pushing them into a wall, this doesn't count as an "unaware" kill, which is not clear at all and can surprise you when X "unaware KOs" is an optional objective.    - Some enemies explode when you kill them and grant ultimate charge. The radius around them in which ultimate charge will be granted is not clear.But like I said, minor criticisms. If you are a skilled veteran of this genre and enjoy a polished challenge, I think you'll enjoy this!
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: Unexpectedly one of the best games I played this year.The mechanics are simple, but diverse and fun. The game is hard in a good way. I've had to retry most of my missions.The characters are really good, I liked all of them. The story is surprisingly good and interesting. The voice acting is phenomenal. I haven't skipped a single dialogue.All the heroes have very interesting mechanics and I enjoyed playing all of them. The art direction is awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: As an fan of the original Freedom Force, I was eager to see what Capes was all about. I'm happy to report that the Capes is a totally sound strategy title that has a lot of heart. Your controllable characters have a wide variety of abilities that all unique in the space and feel novel enough to feel different, for example a telekinetic that can't walk but uses his powers to hover around on missions. The game does a great job introducing the narrative to the player and slowly eases you into the gritty world it has established. Tonally, it's not too different from comics/shows like the Boys with characters swearing up a storm and civilians getting executed by the bad guys. There is no head popping yet, but I have about 40 hours left to play, so I'm guessing there will be some. Now for a few things that I'd like to see in the future. The character models and animations are a bit rough around the edges. Facial animations and some of the combat could use a bit more time in the oven. Having a single animation for moves like "backstab" is a real shame, as you see it often and a bit of variety would go a long way.  There is also very little in terms of character customization, gear and costumes. While it doesn't detract from the combat experience, I'd love to be able tweak my characters a bit as there is no character creator available. The voice acting and writing is sound and they managed teach the audience about a wide variety of characters in a short amount of time while giving them all nuance and personality which is incredibly challenging from a narrative perspective, Capes is a good game that is deserving of your time. Perhaps in the future it will add some more layers and depth to its characters and skill trees.
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: When writing a review, I don't necessarily think it's fair to judge a game by what it's not, and what this game is not is X-COM. But it's also impossible to escape the shadow of X-COM in the tactical RPG genre, and if you're playing something going, "Hm, this would be much better if it were more like X-COM," that is a relevant feeling to note.It seems like the premise of this game lends itself extremely well to an X-COM style of play, conceptually. You enter a dystopian, cape-punk world trying to topple the oppressive "Company" that hunts and captures/kills superhumans for their nefarious purposes. It seems like it would be fun to build up your superhero HQ, recruit a team of superheroes, and go out on missions trying to disrupt and destabilize the bad guys. and help out some civilians along the way. And while these are things that do happen during the story, the main difference here is that *you're* not doing it. The process itself is not game-ified. There's little if any management-style gameplay, discarded in favor of a more in-depth story. And while that's a whole side discussion on game design and what exactly we're trying to accomplish when making and playing them, it is hard not to feel a bit of disappointment that this isn't that game.So the question becomes, is what's here worth that initial (perhaps unfair) pang of disappointment?And I think the answer is absolutely yes.I expected, from the art style and promotional materials, a story that was a bit lighter and more camp and what we got instead is civilians being gunned down in the street, kidnapped supers being tortured to death, and plenty of swearing and blood. I don't mind camp and silliness, which is nearly impossible to avoid in the superhero genre anyway, but the older I get, the more I want stories that feel less like they're for children. This feels like a well-written, mature comic book for adults, with characters that are charming and likable, a world that does enough to justify itself, and even some sideways politics to give it depth. Despite not expecting to, I find myself looking forward to unlocking more interactions in the game's dossiers, and generally just enjoying listening to the characters exist. I look forward to seeing what's going on with Doctrine.(I do think it's a little funny how we've established that the Company is this brutal, supervillain-run coporatocracy that chews people up and spits them out, but the other characters are still suspicious of Doctrine and his "little vendetta" like it's a purely personal grudge. Just an odd bit of dissonance there.)As far as the gameplay goes, I see what other reviews are saying in that the tactical aspect of it can feel restrictive and "puzzle-y," and it definitely starts out that way, especially when you're trying to do all the optional objectives. That said, I think this mostly ends after Act 1, when there's still a lot of things being tutorialized for the player. And eventually, I stopped worrying about doing all the side objectives right off, since you can come back later and replay the missions anyway. Frankly, I'm not a completionist and if it's not essential, I'm not going to worry about it if I don't have to. It feels like playing with a noose around your neck, and I much prefer the gameplay if I don't torture myself like that.Graphics-wise, I think the art style is fantastic and evocative of comics, but the actual in-game 3D models leave something to be desired. They look a bit like lower-poly Champions Online models, and Rebound's horse face in the actual in-engine cutscenes gives me nightmares. Luckily, you're not subjected to that many close-ups compared to the character-art conversations, but I think the models themselves could have used a little more love.I have some quibbles with the UI, namely when you're selecting abilities to use. When you click on one, it greys the rest out, and gives you no obvious way to cancel. Now, the way to cancel is just to click on it again, but my natural instinct was to hit Escape, which instead just brings up the menu. I'm still doing this after several hours, so I wish that was a little more intuitive.All in all, I think Capes is a solid game, well worth your time, and especially fun if you're a fan of superhero media. It definitely deserves higher than the "Mixed Reviews" valley it's fallen into, and I can't help but wonder how many of those would change after the Player Freedom update. I didn't play before then, so I can't form a valid opinion.Easy 8/10.(Hands down better than Midnight Suns.)

_childDocuments_.review: Off the bat I will say that I understand some of the grievances people have with this game. Some missions feel more of a puzzle with a certain order to be solved than a tactical strategy game. And the dialogue could have used a little improvement.However I really enjoyed this game all the same. The concept felt really cool and the mechanics lead to some very rewarding moments. I would love to play a sequel to this.
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: As many other reviews have pointed out, this is indeed a puzzle like game.  Not only does every mission have a main objective there are optional objectives/ challenges that you need to do in order to get more skill points (SP).  These skill points are needed to purchase, well skills, which will be needed for later chapters.  The problem is, some of these optional objectives basically asks you to play the game sub-optimally.  Example, instead of outright defeating the enemies an optional objective might require you to disarm enemies an X amount of times.  Trust me when I say that you will eventually fight MANY enemies in the later missions, and the idea of disarming them instead of quickly reducing their numbers is kind of silly.  This is especially egregious when it comes to the stealth missions.  Fortunately there is not too many of those.When you gain levels and SP, you'll eventually be able to unlock more skills that will add a  bit more flexibility to the solutions in the later missions, which will make them a bit easier.I've noticed that there are particular questions that is often asked in MANY game forums here on Steam.  And those question are: Does this game have DEI and is this game woke?  There are 8 characters which consists of 50/50 men and women. There is a black dude who is straight and a white girl with purple hair who is a lesbian (possibly bi-sexual). There is a Caucasian male scientist who uses tech powers, a Hispanic looking male, an Indian male, an Asian female and another white girl that looks slightly chunky. But I think she looks chunky because she has big "assets." There is also a girl who sounds a bit like Nelson Muntz from The Simpsons and apparently she is gendered fluid, but this was hardly ever brought up.So yeah, it is pretty inclusive, but I wouldn't say that Capes is "woke" as there are no persistent lectures of  "white privilege," "the patriarchy," "racism," "sexism." etc, that is constantly being shoved in our faces. Sure, a good chunk of dialogue is a bit cheesy and the plot is kind of mediocre and predictable. But the game for the most part doesn't try to take itself too seriously.If you're looking for a strategy game with a lot of freedom, depth and with a good story, then this game is likely not for you.  But if you don't mind puzzle like battles where you can play as super heroes that beat the ever living crap out of people, them CAPES might be right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: I am sad to see all these negative reviews just for the game being hard. Just play on an easier difficulty? I think the problem is that is attracting "super hero" game fans instead of "turn based isometric RPG game fans". Its core gameplay is solid, the graphics are solid, and the story is good. That said, this game is woke. Though it does't feel intrusive given how woke all comics have been for the past couple decades.
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game so far. The characters have interesting abilities and common types of abilities, such as disarming enemies, are handled differently for different characters. I like that each character feels unique. The voice acting is also well done.I want to address the negative reviews calling this a "puzzle game". It is not a puzzle game. There are optional objectives, many of which ask you to use a certain ability a few times during the mission (or disarm an enemy etc). I think some players are getting frustrated thinking they need to use specific abilities in a specific sequence or else they can't win. This is not the case, there is plenty of flexibility. The game is designed for you to get good use out of your abilities. That's not the same as it being a "puzzle game".
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: With its unique "comic book" style, Capes stands out among the many other turn based strategy out there.Take control of a super hero team to tackle the super villain menace that has plagued the city, find and recruit new super heroes along the way, upgrade and customise your heroes.If you enjoyed other games like X-Com but always wanted a different theme then Capes is the game for you!Capes is a fun, exciting and SUPER-TASTIC game that's worth every penny!To watch the introduction, Tutorial and first main mission checkout my Plays & Chats on my YouTube Channel!
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: While the combat and puzzle aspects are great, the character models look like they're running on a PS2.  Animations outside of combat are terrible and there are serious frame drops every time the scene changes.  The worst are the cut scenes.  They use the outside world models and it's just horrific.Voice acting is ok, Dialogue can be a bit corny and stilted, but doesn't seriously detract.TLDR; Combat gameplay is fantastic, story/dialogue is ok, models are terrible.  Too expensive for what you're getting.  Buy on sale or if you're really big into puzzles and don't care about anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Splendid indiegame thats a must buy if you like the superhero of the golden eras.For those who played freedom force game back in 2002, this is what you been waiting for.Its on the harder side, and you need to treat every fight a sort of a puzzle a tad more then a tactical thing, so make sure you are prepared for that.The comic from the 60-ties design I guess will be of-putting for some as well, but you see that on the screenshots, so you cant really be surprised by that.Really good indie game, cant recomend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: The reviewers are right, this game is an avalanche of DEI and woke characters, but strangely enough the reviewers are totally wrong on the gameplay. The characters are all diversity cutouts, they have no personality outside of their race, or whether they’re gay (and there’s a lotta gay going around). I’m not even sure why they bother showing the character interactions, it’s obvious that once the writers established the character’s race and pronouns, they had no idea where to go from there, as most of the interactions revolve around, “boy, can you believe what we’re going through!” “yeah this is really hard!” “I mean we are really having a hard time here!” etc etc. The villains of course are all white, and all of the heroes I’ve collected so far are not (or they’re gay), to the point where the developers aren’t even trying to hide it anymore. They’re not artists, they’re anti-white race-obsessed activists. I haven’t finished the game yet but I’m halfway wondering if Weathervane, the sole white AND straight character on my team, is going to betray the team somehow.And the saddest part? The gameplay is actually awesome. I love tactical games, and I’ve been wanting a superhero tactics game like this. Of course, I would have preferred a strong story with interesting characters, but I’ll take what I can get. This game blows Marvel: Midnight Suns out of the water, since it doesn’t force you to wander around a map collecting trinkets.Also, the reviewers saying that this is not a tactics game, but a “puzzle” game with only one route through each level, are completely wrong. The first few levels have a lot of tutorials where they show how to specifically move a character, but that’s to be expected. After the tutorial stages, the training wheels come off and you can finish missions as you like. There are multiple characters to choose from, and since each character has multiple superpowers, and different team-up powers between characters, there are many, many ways to finish each stage. It’s crazy because that’s like the one thing this diversity propaganda actually got right.
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: Editing my response to a more objective one, game feels slow because the way skill selection and execution break up the flow of combat too much to be cohesive, to be expected to an extend on tactical game but when you have to repeat too many skills on a fight, maybe using cursor or skill memory to recast skills will feel more fluid.

_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed this game. It's a fun setting and the characters are interesting enough. The setting and siege-mentality of heroes coming back from a total defeat makes the limited amount of character depth come across more as people tense and with no real downtime to bond. Its well done enough that I'd suggest getting it at any discount .

_childDocuments_.review: I sat on the fence about this game since it released and finally took the plunge. I'm so glad I did. It's a fantastic game that I'm really enjoying playing. Once you get use to the tactics and team-ups it becomes a really enjoyable strategy game. Gets quite hard very quickly if you don't pay attention to hero/enemy abilities.Thumbs up!
_childDocuments_.name: Capes

_childDocuments_.review: I am over 12 hours into this game and so far I have enjoyed it a ton. There are some things thatI feel could've used more love and care. These are that I find the writing and Voice acting kind of stiff. After Mecurial, I find alot of the heroes you recruit to be kind of meh. Lastly is that I wish I had a way to play back a bad move instead of loading an earlier save.Those are what I have trouble liking. But aside from those semantics, I really like the story so far. I enjoy any moment the characters have heart to heart talks. Wish there were more however. The world building is gritty but grounded in the concept of the game.I enjoy the time I have spent so far tackling each mission in new ways. I have not seen anymaps get reused so points for keeping it fresh. It takes something I am poor at, puzzles and tactics, then puts them into a context I like. Super heroes and combat. I think it does this very well.My favorite is that the world and the characters are their own. While I love superheroes and comics they can get stale when you have seen them over and over. Midnight Suns was a great deal of fun! But I am also so, so tired of Marvel. It is incredibly fresh and encouraging to see a new take on the classic archetypes of the genre. I appreciate this most of the team from Spitfire I think. They took time to write some unique characters and give them specific strengths and weaknesses that feel impactful. I am, and never have been, big on the idea a character should be able to handle any challenge on their own. Especially in a squad or team context. Overall I find the game very fun and original in its world building and lore. I wish it were more robust but they did well for their first title. The gameplay is engaging and challenging for the diffculty of the same name. I wish progression were more impactful such as maybe letting your squishier characters get a bit tougher.If you're like me and enjoy a challenge as well as original superhero genre ideas then this game is fantastic. I may wait for a sale but thats only because I have not finished the game. If I can get 40 hours of gameplay out of this it would be more than worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic.Isometric turn-based superhero combat in the best vein of the Freedom Force series. A little more serious than those, with full normal language skills.  :)  The game features tons of meaningful meta progression, deep combat options (including cooperative abilities with other heroes), good writing, and good voice acting.Just started to play and the quality is obvious - these devs know what they are doing. Going to be a fun one.Note: Capes is mission-based, not free-form like an X-Com. It has the potential to be developed that way in the future. Given the solid main game, I hope DLC takes it in that direction.UPDATE: Capes *is* indeed a good game. But some caveats, many Missions into it.Missions are Main or Optional. Naturally, you'll be playing every Mission to be found - Mission objectives give upgrade points for your Heroes. So they aren't really "optional". The Objectives read reasonably, yet in-Mission are extremely difficult to achieve. Therefore, your Heroes will remain under-powered for the bulk of the game. Mission scenarios are tight, and despite quality in execution, more puzzles than free-form encounters; as good a game as Capes is, this means things are just going to get more 'crackerjack' (difficult) as you progress. Capes does not seem to give players a break.Winning a scenario means doing things right. Mistakes can torpedo the entirety of a Mission, they are so tightly designed.Opening up Mission structures, revamping the combat (be more liberal with hits, wounds, reviving, etc.), and generally relaxing the approach would be a welcome course to chart for Capes, whether in patches, DLC, or perhaps sequels.Still a good game, still well-done, but as aforementioned... .

name: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge
detailed_description: When a demon's castle darkens the land, two sisters challenge its halls. Together they can break the curse. In order to save their school after it turns into a massive demonic castle, two 'Demon Hunter' sisters slash and shoot their way through this 2D action adventure. Players can swap between control of both characters on the fly, each with entirely different skillsets. Proceed through the castle while confronting the demonic bosses that await deep within. Each boss yields new weapons to wield, allowing for more varied exploration and opening up new routes. ■Swap out on the fly as you traverse through the demonic castle! Take control of both the tag-team Kamizono siblings. Make the most of long-distance focused Shinobu and close-range brawler Maya Kamizono as you make your way through the castle. Each sibling has a range of unique sub-weapons, giving you a wealth of options to switch your strategy up whenever the time calls for it. Don’t hesitate to make use of them so long as you have Weapon Points in stock! In the event that one of the siblings falls in battle, they can be resuscitated freely with 'Sister Rescue'—provided you can make it back to where they fell. ■Defeat bosses to obtain new sub-weapons, opening up a whole new layer of exploration! Defeating bosses will yield new sub-weapons, providing the siblings with exciting new abilities. These sub-weapons also open up new routes and means of exploration in the castles. ■Enjoy the story your way with 'Pure' or 'Refined' voice tracks! Gal Guardians' story focuses on two main aspects: the mystery behind the school's transformation, and the whereabouts of the other students. Enjoy the original experience in 'Pure' mode with all of the original Japanese voices for story mode, or choose “Refined” for English voice acting focused on the action, tailored for fans of the genre. ■Adjust the difficulty to your playing needs with the unique Style system! A total of 3 different styles—'Casual', 'Veteran' and 'Legend'—are available for selection, allowing players to adjust the difficulty to their needs. This can be changed at any time after beginning the game with no drawbacks. What's more, co-op with both Shinobu and Maya will be possible should two controllers be available. It's possible to jump-in at any time during the game, so don't hesitate to invite friends along on your journey to conquer this mysterious demonic castle.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is mostly inspired by the older Castlevania titles which were linear. But with a modern feel to it, with a good punch and feel to the animations and attacks.I wanted to leave this quick review to address that since the game is getting negative reviews from people who thought the game was a metroidvania.I've only played the first 3 levels but essentially this is a spiritual sequel to their previous game Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 2, taking a lot of it's ideas when it comes to mechanics, character interactions, levels and structure, but without the restrictive controls of old Castlevania (which it is inspired by) and a lot more punch to the animations and feel of the game.This makes it not feel like old castlevania and probably won't scratch that ich as you don't engage with combat and levels in the same calculated manner, i would treat it as a modern action game that takes many elements from it instead. If you were looking for a more old castlevania type of experience check Bloodstained: Curse of the moon 1.Unless the game goes crazy later, you'll get a very good picture of the game from the first level or two, so give it a try and if it's not your cup of tea you can refund. Once again the purpose of this review was just to clarify the metroidvania thing.Edit: I was a little mean on the original review because i was frustrated at people leaving bad reviews just because the game isnt a metroidvania, i'm sorry, i edited the review to cut that out.

_childDocuments_.review: BE WARNED BEFORE YOU BUY!This is NOT a Metroidvania game! Its Castlevania classic. Stages, linear progression, that sort of thing. It resembles Symphony of the Night yes, but we're more talking the OG Castlevania on the NES.That being said its still a decent game. The characters are amusingly campy, the contrast between the two sisters is interesting, and the gameplay is solid... but if you're looking for an explorative game like the Castlevania GBA and DS titles... this ain't it.I'd recommend it, but with the caveat that you go in knowing precisely what kind of game you're getting.

_childDocuments_.review: Could call it Curse of the Moon 3. Another great Vania tribute, and while it takes a lot from the COTM games it includes mechanics from a ton of Inti's games. Some Gunvolt here, some Mighty Gunvolt Burst there, little Dragon MFD, and a bunch of Bloodstained. If you enjoy Castlevania and Bloodstained, get this. If you enjoy Inti's other games and aren't familiar with CV or BS, I'd still absolutely recommend this.Graphics are excellent. Amazing pixel art throughout, very fluid animations. Environmental effects are impressive, including reflections on some floors as well as enemy gore splattering on backgrounds. Can't think of many 2D games that do this, let alone this well. Some backgrounds and tiles admittedly look simple at times but it's not a negative. The entire game oozes charm but is also a treat on the eyes. Audio I'm uneven on. Sound effects are perfect, and this kind of sound design is missing from most games, AAA and indie. You get crunchy and satisfying slices and splatters when you kill an enemy, Giving the player rewarding feedback in combat is so important in making it engaging, and GG gets this. Footsteps sound different depending on the floor, cool for a 2D platformer. Weapon and monster sounds are all high quality too. I'm indifferent on the soundtrack. Its extremely well produced and fits the settings, it just doesn't really jump out. First stage and the cutscenes have the most memorable music. It's all good stuff, it all has effort put in for sure, but again it isn't too resonant. Gameplay is tight. Controls are tight, mechanics are tight, progressions tight. Like Bloodstained you restart to the beginning stage once you beat the final boss, replaying the stages but with increased difficulty and new powerups that let you explore previously unreachable routes. Difference is on your second playthrough you get a base with all the students you saved. Oh yea you also got students to save throughout the stages. Won't find em all on your first playthrough since, again, you have new powerups that allow access to new routes. Difficultys also nice. Its just challenging enough, where the game is overally pretty easy but you still have to pay attention to not fall down pits or lose your health quickly. Dying will restart you at a checkpoint with the character who didn't die and you have a chance to find your other character to revive them. If you die again you lose a life. Boss and enemy patterns are all well thoguht out, have proper telegraphs, and are a joy to fight. And while you can sometime tank you shouldn't, since you'll regret losing that health earlier. Seemed to learn from COTM 2, where yeah the game was extremely hard but for annoying reasons. They'd overwhelm you with enemies and boss attacks, which could be a problem if you don't have useful team members alive, and most of the difficulty was based on finding permanent upgrades Megaman X style. Checkpoint system was awful, sending you back tons of rooms for losing your whole team, which felt like padding. It was very not-Castlevania, and it made the game overly punishing if you didn't go out of your way to find all the upgrades. The game didn't feel as polished as COTM 1 or GG in terms of difficulty, just felt like "Hey they said the first was too easy? Let's kick their ♥♥♥♥ in this time". CV1 and 3 had their tough sections but it never got to the point that COTM2 did, where it felt like the game was wasting your time. IT felt designed against the player, not designed around mechanics.GG feels like a direct response to this, where they present you with your challenge of enemy and platform placements before you carefully navigate those situations with your mechanics. It's breezy and fun but, again, never too easy. It's rewarding to look before you leap, wait for an enemy to finish their attack before going in to kill. Boss patterns are also perfect, and a few mimic Vania bosses that fans will get a kick from. Games always keeping your attention whether you're having fun or completing a challenging section. Only irritating this they kept from COTM 2 was it's checkpoint system, where you'll sometimes go back pretty far from death. Don't wanna discredit COTM 2- it's a great game, just not very Castlevania once you get far into it. Castlevania shouldn't be Megaman X, and it's difficulty should never rely on hidden stage upgrades. Overall another great Vania tribute and another great game from Inti. I'd recommend this to basically anyone who enjoys platformers, but for fans of the series it's especially a treat. Safe to say we don't need Konami anymore. Inti and Iga have been providing new Castlevania games, and better than Konami could muster up now if they tried. Y'know, won;t just recommend GG, but also the three Bloodstaineds and the Castlevania collections. Can find em all on Steam, all pretty cheap, and all a ton of fun with incredible presentation.

_childDocuments_.review: The first thing you need to know is that this is not technically a metroidvania, nor is it advertised as one. That is to say, there is not one large interconnected map. However, the game does in effect play out similarly to a metroidvania in regards to both player upgrades and map traversal, which I will start explaining in the next paragraph. The gist of it is however that If you're the kind of person who enjoys metroidvania games, you're likely to end up enjoying this.You can break the game up into two different halves. The first half of the game is a more linear style of progression in which you follow a set path through a level until you reach the boss, you then eventually defeat the boss, unlock two new sub weapons (one for each of the two characters), and then progress to the next level. Once you reach the second half, you're able to return back to the levels you've previously beaten, except now alternate pathways are accessible in part due to your expanded mobility options and in part due to certain previously locked pathways now being unlocked. Sometimes these newly accessible areas will make their own unique spin on the level, such as a level that initially branches into an ice cave for the first half of the game instead later branching into a fire themed cave when you unlock that pathway later.In essence, you can think of the second half of the game as a pseudo-metroidvania in which the different individual areas you would typically find in such a title are split off into their own smaller maps. You will need to backtrack and explore through these a lot to find all of the hidden collectables and such if you're going for the completion ending.As for the gameplay itself, it feels like what you would get if you grabbed Castlevania Portrait of Ruin, Castlevania Rondo of Blood, Bloodstained Curse of the Moon 2, Mega Man X8, Mega Man ZX, and just dropped them all in a blender. There are two playable characters which you can swap between on the fly at any time; Maya and Shinobu. Shinobu has a longer attack range thanks to her "Anti-Demon Sub Machine Gun" which will trivialize many of the enemies, but has limited ammo clips that you need to keep track of. You will never actually run out of ammo, but you will need to reload which leaves you vulnerable. She also has the most health of the two, but does less damage. Maya has less health and relies primarily on melee range attacks, but does significantly more damage and can crawl. Effectively, the balance is very risk vs reward, and you will need to swap between both characters efficiently if you want to make the most of their individual capabilities.Sub-weapons are similar to Castlevania games in that you have a limited resource (shared between the two characters) that depletes a certain amount based on the sub-weapon that you used. This can be replenished via purple potions which drop from enemies and items on the walls similarly to collecting hearts in Castlevania.In addition to the sub-weapons that you can unlock, you also have access to a sort of team ultimate attack which acts as a sort of screen nuke if you can hit an enemy with it. It does not do enough damage to kill bosses or certain tankier enemies in one hit, so I would recommend trying to hold onto it until you've nearly finished a boss and then time your attack carefully to ensure it lands for a stylish finish. To use this attack at all, you'll need to build your pride meter, which is done by picking up colored badges that are part of the drop pool.The game can be played in either Single Player or two player local Co-op. As of the time of me writing this review, there is no proper Online Co-op, however you can simulate Online by using Steam's remote play feature, or via Parsec. Personally Parsec seems to work better for me between the two, but this may vary depending on the distance between players, how good your/their download and upload speeds are, etc. Co-op mode comes with additional risk of death due to both characters being on-screen at the same time, but also comes with unique perks such as being able to stand on each others heads to reach some areas earlier than in Single Player.There's two voice acting options for the game: Pure and Refined. Pure is the original Japanese voice acting, and includes fully voiced dialogue boxes during cutscenes. Refined is the English dub, with which everything is voiced with exception to the dialogue boxes which are silent. Many people at this point of their reviews will tell you outright which one you should use. I will not. Choose whichever of the two suits your tastes and preferences.Finally, your reward for beating the game (which ending you get doesn't matter, just get to the final boss and win) is Boss Rush mode. It is what it says on the tin, so to speak.Overall, I've found this to be a rather fun game all things considered. Despite not technically being a metroidvania, it's close enough in my opinion to scratch that itch if you're looking for that kind of experience, especially once things start opening up in the second half of the game. If you enjoy metroidvania games and games similar to them, this should be right down your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Very niche - unless you're an old school gamer looking for a 16-bit styling of an 8 bit Metroid-like (but NOT Metroidvania), or you're a die-hard Gal Gun franchise fan, you may find more confusion and annoyance than fun.Fortunately for me, I'm both of the above, so this fell right into my wheelhouse. I thoroughly enjoyed it, and am happy to support the series in hopes Inti will keep building on the franchise, but I can definitely see flaws that need to be addressed.I'll start with the big controversy that has dogged this game since launch, the question of if it is a metroidvania, and as above, I say no, or perhaps better to say, not quite. It has a lot of components of a metroidlike - multiple paths through areas, obtained upgrades and abilities that are required to open some of those paths, power-ups and collectibles and easter eggs that require exploration to find, secret rooms and triggers that those things are found in and through. It also has elements of a vanialike - room-by-room progression of platforming and stair climbing, annoying enemies that spawn offscreen and fly through screen in wave patterns to complicate jumps, wall-mounted breakables, and of course the faux-gothic aesthetics.  But a key element of the metroidvania genre, as found in seminal titles like Super Metroid and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, is FREEDOM, which this game sorely lacks. In old-school Castlevania fashion, everything is laid out in levels, not just in style, but in progress - every time you visit an area, you start at a beginning, work through mostly in one direction on only one of two or three routes (with a lot of one-way gates limiting ability to backtrack), then reach a boss, clear it, and exit the stage. There is no ability to do the first run of a stage out of order - though you can interrupt your progress by redoing a previously cleared stage, you cannot do a stage until beating the boss of the stage before it. And you cannot easily exit a stage - the only way out is either to reach the end, or to exit the game (it does give you the option to do this in a way that lets you keep items collected, but not your progress in the stage). As for revisiting prior stages, this WILL happen - to finish the game requires clearing each stage at least twice, and to 100% it will require at least thrice, but I think I did each stage at least four times, some more. So if you're looking for later-style, free roaming Castlevania, this isn't it. And the gameplay itself is often very reminiscent of the unforgiving mechanics and harsh penalties of the 8-bit era. While it is not overly hard per se, most deaths and failures feel cheap - either from being knocked into an instantly fatal fall, or succumbing to boss attack patterns you aren't given a fair opportunity to learn, aside from dying to them again and again and again until you finally see and understand them all, including the "death spell" each does as a final unique attempt to kill you after you empty its health bar. And jumping takes some getting used to, as I found the "falloff point" of ledges to be about six inches earlier than they visually appear to be.Meanwhile, the Gal Gun influence plays out in a very odd way, that may be very offputting for those not familiar with the franchise. From the start, the game assumes you already know everything about the characters - no exposition is offered for why Shinobu and Maya are schoolgirl demon hunters, why Kurona has such an odd definition of "prank" or why she's doing her thing, who the hell "Ho-nii" is, or any of the background history. It just drops all these random references and builds on the history as though you surely must know it (which I did, but relying on that knowledge emphasized for me how little of it this game was explaining). And at first, that won't really matter - it's just a basic video game premise, after all, and gameplay built upon it is just standard pixelated action. But as the story progresses, things will start getting weird, unless you're expecting Gal Gun style. One minute you're just killing demons, but suddenly you're hunting for a porno mag to excite a column (no, that is not a typo), having random schoolgirls say assorted off-colour remarks about being your maid, that she's unworthy vermin, wanting you to dominate her, or that she's a borderline cat, and you're collecting their panties from all over the castle.  If you've played other Gal Gun games this all makes sense, but to an outsider this level of comedic perviness will just seem out of place.So it is very niche. But it does what it aims to well, and once you learn the mechanics, the strategies, the ledge endpoints, and the boss tells and patterns, it's a tight, solid platformer. I enjoyed it, and so long as the oddball ecchi in the lategame doesn't bother you, an old-school platform gamer should enjoy it too. So yes, recommended.But I never want to hear the word "FEETZIEZ" ever again.....Also, game does not feature best waifu Saori Fujino :-( Had to be said.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an okay game but it's not up to the typical quality of Inti Creates.The game is very inspired by older Castlevanias, especially Symphony of the Night. It stops a few steps short of being a full metroidvania and frankly would have been a better game if it just committed.Like the game expects you to replay levels to discover new items with your newly unlocked skills, but makes the process a real pain.  The barely functioning item compass and an extremely vague intro map do very little to make exploration easier.   You also need to replay the FULL, labyrinth-like levels from start to finish when backtracking for items, complete with multiple paths and occasional 1-way doors.  I wanted to 100% the game but after a few hours of this, I just gave up and settled for the standard ending. Your powers also just don't feel fine-tuned (an item that creates platforms diagonally below you, a freeze spell you need to memorize the positioning for, etc.), which took a lot of the joy out of the combat.I'd just go pick up Curse of the Moon or Bloodstained if you're looking for a Castlevania experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Review :Finish the game and got the true ending, its a very fun experience even though its a short game.Back to topic, The game is a spin off from the main game of Inti Creates called Gal*Gun series in a more specific title the Gal*Gun Double peace, since it features the four main characters there being Kurona, Kamizono Shinobu, Kamizono Maya and Houdai Kudoki unlike the main title, this game follows a more retro style graphics with anime 2D style for cutscenes. The game itself feels similar to a castlevania game but  the usual metroidvania where you level up and back track for loots.Things to look out for :- The game starts with Shinobu and Maya and the ability to start solo isn't allowed.- The main gameplay is having you traverse the demon castle using Shinobu and Maya alternately.- Both Shinobu and Maya shares the same Weapon points which are used to cast sub-weapons.- Shinobu is a range character that can deflect projectile with her own but her attack power is weaker while Maya is a melee character that has higher attack than Shinobu but at the cost of a lower hp and range.- The two siblings can do a joint attack using the Purge gauge which can be filled by time or picking up Pride.- The castle has checkpoints(Birdcages lits up if you move towards it.) where you will re-spawn if one of the Kamizono dies or you reach a game over(-1 retry).- At the start only two difficulty is allowed being Casual and Veteran, Legend difficulty is unlock after clearing the game once and its difficulty increases with just having one of the sisters die which will result a game over(-1 retry).- The game lets you back track stages cleared(ex. Courtyard, Clocktower, etc.) after defeating the boss in its stage though it doesn't let you immediately spawn at the end but at the start of each stages.- Back tracking for HP up, WP up, Defense up, etc. can make exploring fun and rewarding.- Some items are needed since the game has multiple endings.- Some bosses are easier for Shinobu while some are easier for Maya.- - Sub-weapons can be upgraded later in the story(ex. Maya's Umbrella charges faster while Shinobu's Knife now throws three).- Later in the story, Shinobu gains a sub-weapon to summon hearts to restore HP making it easier to fight even during boss battles.- - Last Note : I thought I would enjoy Maya's gameplay more but felt that Shinobu's gameplay was more fun when she got all her sub-weapons especially the Grappling Hook and Anti-Demon Rocket Launcher.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon 3.  But it's got Gal Gun characters, instead of Bloodstained characters.  No, this doesn't actually affect the gameplay or design at all.  It's also gone from "8-bit" aesthetic to "16/early 32-bit" aesthetic.It is NOT a Metroidvania, and I don't know how people ever labelled it as such.  It is the same format as Curse of the Moon 1 and 2.  You have 7 stages, you go from start to finish, you kill a boss, next stage.  There are multiple paths thru each stage, which will have different power-ups and collectables.  Instead of up to 4 (8) characters to collect and swap between with their own abilities, you have 2 characters, each with their own quirks, who each get a collection of subweapons as you progress thru the stages (which just happen to mostly cover the traversal and utility weapons from Curse of the Moon 1/2).You get a new subweapon each stage for each character, subweapons can be freely selected at any time, and you can revisit previously stages at any time.  THIS IS AN AWFUL IDEA to do right as you're starting the game, is a waste of time in-genearl, and again, I don't know whoever started throwing the "Metroidvania" tag out there, because it is WRONG.  Whereas the format of the previous Curse of the Moon games was "beat game, new quest available with other characters/characters you didn't have at the start before", the format of Demon Purge is "beat all the stages, get booted back to the start with all your gear and upgrades for Lap 2, get ending depending on how much work you put into combing the stages for stuff".Read: there is almost zero reason to replay the stages until you've beaten them all once, and collected all the subweapons.  Don't make the same mistake I did.Did you like Curse of the Moon 1 and 2?  You'll probably like this.  Did you like Gal Gun?  They made a Curse of the Moon game in that setting, good for you.  The game itself is overall easier than those, to note, unless you go for the hardest options (which, again, mirror the other Curse of the Moon games).  After clearing the game outright, you have the option to do a collectathon, involving combing EVERY nook and cranny of every path of every stage, for an alternate ending, but that's really for the most dedicated people.  (No, really.)

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my favorite Inti Creates game in some time. The pixel art is a dead ringer for Castlevania and really looks fantastic. Unfortunately, the game can only be rendered up to 1080p, which is a shame. Changing the resolution also resets your voice settings. Do NOT set the voices to English as there's almost no English voice acting. Conversely, pretty much every line is voiced in Japanese. The basic gist of the game is that you switch between a character with a gun and one that fights at melee range. It's got a lives system but it's pretty meaningless on the medium difficulty, as one character dying resets the other character to a checkpoint where they can revive the other. On the hard difficulty, however, you lose a life once this happens. As such, if you're looking for a more old school challenge, you'll definitely want to set this to hard.There are eight levels and you go through the first seven sequentially. Once you beat the seventh one, you basically get told to go back through them again for fetch quests. But you get new abilities that make exploration easier after doing this and there are plenty of alternate pathways and secrets to find that you probably won't have seen on your first run, so this isn't as bad as it sounds. There's a good amount of playtime here, considering, although not as much as Curse of the Moon 2. You only unlock a boss rush for beating the game, so don't expect any extra characters. Although, there's more than one ending, but unlocking the other one seems to take a fair amount of busy work (I haven't unlocked it yet.)The gameplay feels pretty great as long as you're okay with using the ranged character a lot of the time. She has a lot more health and she's just safer in general, which can make her feel a bit overpowered and much more useful than the melee-range character. You get new subweapons after beating bosses and some of these aren't really weapons at all, as some are used for navigation, such as a grappling hook or umbrella that lets you glide. All of the subweapons can also be upgraded. I really enjoyed this one, as I adore Castlevania and this successfully scratches that itch. It's got more content than I expected, the level design is varied and features awesome environmental art, the platforming and controls are extremely tight, and it's just an all-around enjoyable action platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: It's nice that one of the key objectives is collecting panties, bloomers and tights. We need to keep the spirit of PS Vita games alive and games like this do a good job of that.Visually and aesthetically the game is an absolute treat. It's beautiful and the music is cool. I really enjoy that it's a Gal Gun spinoff with elements of classic Castlevania and other inti 2d action titles like Rockman Zero. I think this really shoots for a very specific niche since I bet lots of people who will enjoy the gameplay alone will be put off by the Gal Gun ecchi humour, but I personally loved that aspect and it added lots of soul to it for me.I will say one complaint I have is that it's almost impossible to get the true ending requirements without following a guide. It seems like adding a map or even just putting the secret collectables on the radar would make it less tedious. But it's well worth doing.

Other reviews don't do this game justice AT ALL. I read a lot about the game "only allowing assisting" but nay, both players are able to trigger dialogue or room change, etc. Both players are lead players and we can also stand on each other and gain jumping momentum, which may actually be a little of a cheat method at early stages but not in the long run. _childDocuments_.review: Gal Guardians wears its inspiration on its sleeves proudly. There's no mistaking where or what it borrows from or pays homage to. While definitely weaving a tale of pure satire (mixed with a dash of fanservice), it performs extremely well as a castlevania-like. However, unlike many of the current-era metroidvanias, it follows the playstyle and progression of past games like Rondo of Blood and Circle of the Moon much more. In addition, it also allows for coop play, as it borrows the moment to moment gameplay from Konami's Portrait of Ruin wherein you must hotswap between two characters to progress. All in all, a fun romp that only starts to become aggravating when achievement hunting. While I'd expect an extra playthrough or two, this title, to get 100%, requires quite a few things to be found. And like Rondo, it sadly has absolutely no in-game map to refer to while you're hunting. It's still fun, just forewarning if you're in a completionist.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, THIS IS NOT A METROIDVANIA GAME.With that out of the way, this game can be considered "Curse of the Moon 3", the game is very similar; you can switch characters on the fly, you can fight close or from a distance, and you have different paths you can explore after you gain new sub-weapons. Also, you have a "casual" mode that prevents the game from having the absurd and artificial difficulty from the old NES games its based on.The pixelart is great, although this might be the first problem this game has; the artstyle is not for everybody.It should be obvious just by seeing the store page, but this is basically "Castlevania III with waifus" (unless you consider Sypha a waifu).I personally dont have a problem with that, but some might, and is not only the characters in game, the images showing the game's story show very "interesting" angles, the game is not shy about this game being extremely "kawai".And this leads to the second problem, which is the biggest; the audio.I know the "people of culture" who like these types of anime is not only because of the art, but also for the voices, and for these people, well, the game delivers, the sisters are constantly screaming in really "weird" ways, while they also keep screaming things like "onii-chan" and that kind of stuff, you know, the "classics"...the game has the option to put english voices, but why would you play a game with this artstyle with english voices? what this game doesnt have are options when it comes to audio, while they should add an option to turn off the constant screaming, I think in this day and age is a given games should have an option to turn down the master audio...you better lower the speakers before starting this bad boy or your neighbors are calling the FBI.In short, amazing plataformer, just as good as the Curse of the Moon games, but is not for everybody...I would suggest trying it out before buying, or wait for a sale, considering I think is a matter of time before they put some audio options.edit: just finished it, the game its great, but it becomes EXTREMELY lewd near the end, so if you dont like or at least tolerate that kind of content...you should avoid it.I think Inti played us here, because they promoted the game as "Grim Guardians" since its announcement, and two weeks after release, they changed it to "Gal Guardians", revealing this game is part of the Gal Gun series, known for being, well, lewd AF...I still really like the game, but they should've been open about the type of game they were selling.

_childDocuments_.review: I played up to Stage 4 so far, but I'm having a great time. The challenge on Veteran mode feels perfect, it is tough - but not unfair. And it does give you quite a few chances if you're having issues with a particular boss fight.The main gameplay gimmick is being able to switch characters on the fly, each with their own style of attacking and health bar. The game slowly introduces more systems by way of secondary weapons you can utilize, but it never becomes too complex and despite the levels having multiple routes, it remains fairly linear - this isn't a Metroidvania game.While the music isn't particularly memorable, the game boasts great sprites, level designs, and outstanding characterization of the main heroines. The humor, likable characters, and creative boss encounters add to the overall charm.The screenshots on the store page look a bit washed out, but in-person on a Steam Deck the game is gorgeous and of course runs at 60fps with only 3TDP, so you'll have around 5 hours of battery life on a full charge.Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Can't say I can recommend this game. For a few reasons:The UI sounds and a small amount of the OST are pretty bad. Dissonance is a powerful tool when applied deliberately. This game makes use of it with all the subtlety of a punch to the face.The movement isn't very good. I was quite literally weaned on Castlevania for the NES which has slow and deliberate movement for everything and have built up a tolerance for movement in all sorts of games from that to Megaman and beyond to indie. This isn't that, nor is it the halfway point that Castlevania: The Adventure Rebirth pulled out. Let me explain. Jumping movement has aggressive acceleration. Reversing direction reverses the acceleration in the opposite direction. Put more succinctly, jumping backwards in attacking is awkward and clunky in a way it really shouldn't be. Enemy placement and variety is rather poor. The game doesn't do a good job for enemies with spawns or even properly use what it does have and so regularly sticks to spawning things 2 feet in front of you constantly for the entirety of the game that the stages become predictable despite being so different in actual design. e.g; a bunch of mooks that will constantly spawn 2 feet ahead of you, enemies hanging above you, 1 large "powerful" enemy blocking the exit. Powerful being in quotation marks for a reason. There aren't enemies or situations that threaten you with the exception of the bosses who themselves are also easy and only land hits on you through you not knowing what their attacks look like or even do. The spawns are honestly the worst part about this game. It's not challenging, it doesn't result in a hit. It's just annoying. If fleamen in Cv3 constantly spawned 2 feet in front of you in literally almost every map that would drive you insane, but here it doesn't matter because the enemy design is pretty whack.Exploration is a bit lackluster. The maps are relatively large and loop and intersect within themselves in a variety of ways but their intentional decision to omit a map/minimap from the game while still cramming it absolutely full stuff you constantly have to retread in addition to movement options for consistently moving forward being lackluster when combined with the poor enemy it leads to a rather mediocre experience. As a special note, there are way too many doors and despite this game being faster pace they barely open faster than the slow as sin ones in Castlevania II on the gameboy while having nearly 20x the number of them. This isn't a hyperbole.Character actions also aren't hot. The special attack while it does do "decent" damage takes way too long to pull off such that using it becomes a pain in the neck of being stuck in it's animation for 10 seconds, during which you can do more than that damage in the time you spent doing nothing. There's no jump cancelling and no angled shots. You don't even get the ability to shoot up until the game sends you back to the start and makes you refight all of the bosses again. The sub weapons are mostly boring and/or too strong with some being relatively useless until they get their upgrades. The basic attacks therefore have to hold most of the game. They don't do a very good job at that. I have no clue how this came out of the same studio that made Curse of the Moon 2. Like sure CotM 1 and 2 were rough at some points and Curse of the Moon 1 also had rather middling maps and enemy placements, but this game is an honestly downgrade in nearly every way. And unlike the first game it seemingly doesn't have an ultimate mode to rescue it. I wanted to like this game, but there's no way I could recommend this to anybody who grew up playing the same games as me.

_childDocuments_.review: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge is a 2D action platformer that has solid boss design and platforming with some questionable level design choices. Do not be misled by Steam's user tags- this is NOT a metroidvania. GGDP is far more similar to the Curse of the Moon games than Ritual of the Night. You play as two sisters, who find that their school has been taken over by demons. Fortunately said sisters are demon hunters and resolve to take it back. The elder sister, Shinobu, deals with ranged weapons whereas the younger sister. Maya, is melee focused. While the game offers co-op action, you can play through the game single player and swap between the sisters at will. Both get unique subweapons that both work for offense and level traversal. Each sister feels like she plays uniquely and has situations both in and out of combat where each excel. While the gameplay is level based, new subweapons are unlocked with each stage which opens alternate pathways within each stage upon replaying it. None of these, sadly, lead to unique levels or significantly new aspects to stages which is a missed opportunity. Each level ends in a boss encounter and this is where the game shines. INTI CREATES has fantastic boss design in the Curse of the Night games and GGDP keeps that streak alive. The bosses are varied and while not overly difficult, are certainly no pushovers.  However (at least on normal difficulty settings) if you die to a boss,  when you reenter the boss room after respawning, a decent portion of the boss's health is still missing due the efforts of your previous attempt. While I embrace the accessibility this brings, I think there should be an option to toggle it on/off. The game has a total of eight levels and to progress through the story you must play through these levels multiple times. The levels are solid but playing through them several times makes it feel a bit stale by the end. It should be worth noting that the story takes a huge left turn after your first run through these eight levels which may be a bit of a deal maker/breaker for players. The reason for this sudden swerve of the plot is due to the game being a part of the GalGun universe. I was not familiar with that series before the game and if you are not either, I would strongly recommend looking it up before buying. For me, the aspects of this shared universe and its tropes usually prompted an eyeroll, sigh or occasional shake of the head but did not really negatively impact my impression of the game. What does negatively impact my impression of the game is that when you replay it there are several collectibles that are tasked with picking up. In and of itself, that's not a bad thing. However there is no in-game map of each level, so it is impossible to tell which branching path you didn't take. Also there is nothing that indicates how much of each of the various collectibles you have actually picked up in each stage, and the names of a certain type of collectible are largely randomized so even using a guide is difficult. This caused me to loop through those same eight levels significantly more times that really should have been necessary and caused my good will towards the individual level design to quickly erode. Having an in-game map or even a vague checklist for each stage could have prevented so much frustration and I am flabbergasted this could have been overlooked. Questionable game design aside, I had a good time with GGDP but would have had a great time with a decent map and clear checklist of collectibles even if they were not marked on said map. Even with that frustration, I did enjoy the game enough to recommend it, even if it comes with a sizeable asterisk.

_childDocuments_.review: To keep things short, I think the game is good but it has major problems. If you like classic Castlevania or Curse of the Moon, and are fine with anime fanservice, I actually recommend this game. If you're just a casual platformer fan or looking for a true Metroidvania, you might want to skip this one.If you go in with those expectations in mind you will have a good time. Despite how it looks, this game is closer to an old school Castlevania than a Metroidvania.-Game doesn't have a real map. Levels are actually long as quite confusing to navigate at times.-Game doesn't keep track of collectibles. It becomes a problem in the end game when you need to collect 40 and don't know which one you are missing.-Padding with Backtracking. Over half the game is backtracking through completed areas, some paths lock you out of others so you'll have to clear stages upwards of 3-4 times to complete the game.-Game punishes early exploration. Even though you get platforming tools quite early, you will get roadblocked and sometimes stuck if you try to go back to stages right away. You need to beat all the stages once before exploring again.-Redundant tools. Some weapons are straight up redundant, the scythe and crane especially.-High difficulty. Bosses are incredibly quick and don't telegraph attacks much, which can be frustrating, you end up needing to predict patterns instead of reacting, enemy placement is also pretty tight.-The game overall feels pretty slow for the size of the map, you don't feel like you can move through the halls fast.Hopefully the sequel is better, I liked the game but I just didn't feel great after finishing everything. 15.8 hours at time of platinum, a bit steep even at sale's price, especially since more than half of that was backtracking.

Level design similar to Castelvania 3)- Story: Good (Meh)- Sound, Music, Voice: Good.I really enjoyed the game, although I was expecting a more metroidvania like game. _childDocuments_.review: I need to stress something at the start of this review. Gal Guardians: Demon Purge is not a Metroidvania even though it clearly feels like it was meant to be. I'm sure as you play through this you will notice this as well and the game would have done itself a favor by being a full Metroidvania...that being said...Gal Guardians: Demon Purge is a fun take on 2D Castlevania. The swapping between both girls reminds me of Portrait of Ruin and the difficulty...it's average and fair I would say. The game itself has 3 endings. 2 of the Endings can be gotten pretty easily but the alternate (3rd) ending is quite frustrating earning without a guide since, once again the game suffers from now going full Metroidvania + having no real map system. However the game itself is honestly incredibly fun!I love the level designs, music, enemies and the boss fights. Heck the sub weapons are really nice as well the further in you make it! You will even be given a chance to upgrade all of your sub weapons by the end of the game which can make traversal even more fun! Now yes of course the game has some fan service as it is set in the Gal Gun universe but I would argue it does not have that much outside of...uhh the (3rd ending) and all it's silliness. Yes the game has it's problems but overall I had way more fun with this game than I had frustration so I recommend this for fans of old school Castlevania with a touch of modern as well.
