_childDocuments_.review: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge is a spin-off of Gal Gun: Double Peace that re-uses that game's cast.  This is core to the game's identity and you are in for some sexual humor if you play this game, but it is not an eroge or "H-game".  Shinobu and Maya are literally the main "route" girls in GGDP, well the other GGDP, not this GGDP.   With that out of the way, GGDP is a linear traditional 2D Castlevania with defined stages that have branching paths and end in a boss fight.  You have 2 playable characters and you swap between them in single-player mode, but there is local co-op and simultaneous double character multiplayer.  As you progress through the game, you unlock different subweapons for both combat and traversal, and these allow you to open up new paths on previously played stages.  Some other stuff happens, but the general gameplay loop is that you will be able to return to any stage you've already played as often as you want: exploring to your heart's content and finding power ups and NPCs to rescue... among other things.  This game is NOT a Metroidvania, although it does have a sequel announced and that might be a Metroidvania.  This game is very similar to Castlevania 3, and also to IntiCreate's previous takes on that specific type of game: their 8-bit Bloodstained Spinoffs (Curse of the Moon).  The platforming is tight, the controls are snappy, but the enemies and knockback are unforgiving and the bosses are rough.  You have reasonable difficulty options to make the game easier or harder, including the return of Casual difficulty which negates enemy knockback.  The pixel art is pretty good but generally not mind-blowing, although there are some beautiful high-res 2D drawings of the characters as portraits and in cutscenes.  The music is fitting, with Ippo Yamada heading it up and making appropriate spooky gothic themes befitting a Castlevania-inspired game.  It's a good package overall.   It took me roughly 11 hours to 100% the game, but I played it a bit more after that and was looking at the Boss Rush mechanics and thinking about potential speedruns.  So yeah, this is a short and mostly linear game that will not fill the same true Metroidvania niche as something like Hollow Knight or Ender Lilies.  You know if you like this type of game or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Inti Creates does it again with a glorious 3-way baby of Castlevania 3, Portrait of Ruin and Gal*Gun! I was so hyped when I saw this announced and so far it doesn't disappoint. Inti Creates has been making the 2D Bloodstained games and plenty of their own platformers so they know what they're doing. Grim Guardians combines the linear-yet-branching level design of Castlevania 3 with the character switching of Portrait of Ruin ("But Castlevania 3 also had character switching.", yeah but it didn't have "JonathanCharlotteJonathanCharlotteJonathanCharlotte" =P) and the universe of Gal*Gun. If that sounds like your jam, GG doesn't disappoint. The only minor issue is that the cutscenes aren't dubbed in English. The in-game dialog is voiced in English but the cutscenes are silent. Most people are probably going to play with the amazing JP voices, so it's not a big deal, but it is a little weird. I'll update this review when I finish the game but I doubt my opinion will change much. Pick it up!Edit: It's even better than I first thought. Once you beat the game, that's when the REAL game begins. New characters, new objectives... This is awesome! Time to uncover all the secrets and unlock all the endings!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my experience with the game and the achievements being mostly exploratory, I completed all of them for my 100% showcase, yay!Some aspects I enjoyed was the different play style between the sister duo, the aesthetic of the stages, and the 2nd loop of the game is a bit of an EX mode (I was thinking of KIrby's Return to Dreamworld). I thought we would be unlocking more characters at some point, but NO, just a ton of sub weapons, such a diverse set too, my favorite probably being the grapply on Shinobu and the Umbrella on Maya. The stages being unique theme, with matching monsters and environmental hazards was cool. I think my favorite was the courtyard.Some annoying details was the lack of global tracking and map usage; however, there was some hint to the direction of important things like rescues, rare items, and boss via a local compass. Since I'd play the stages multiple time due to my curiosity and the 2nd loop, not having a map wasn't too bad, I got a good idea of the routes and looping rooms just by playing. I did also use a guide at the end to help me pin down some specific rescues though so I'm not going all over.I would recommend this game, there's a discount for it every so often, so buy it when it comes up! Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: Starting with presentation, because that is an easy one - game is gorgeous. From dialogue art of all characters, to character sprites in game, everything is clear and has that specific anime charm. I especially like the designs of our main characters. They have that spunk you look for in a protagonist of such game.Now to go into the gameplay - i enjoy the simple systems that grow more complex with time, and it works well here. You start with 2 very different characters, which works better than i thought it will - before trying out the demo, i was worried i would end up with Castlevania - Portrait of Ruin situation, where i stick to one, better character and only use the other one in more of a support role or when i am forced to. That doesn't happen here. Both Shinobu and Maya keep being equally useful for the entire game. Both start with one subweapon, unlocking more as we go - and i am again pleasantly suprised, because besides maybe one Shinobu sub that becomes less relevant after half-way point of the game, all of them keep being useful, and are not relegated to just being a way to progress into side paths.Difficulty is the good kind of challenging, but fair. There are some boss attacks that are harder to dodge, and sometimes you might be tempted to just tank through them, but other than that - very solid. I assume some would argue it is even too easy.There are permanent upgrades you can collect during your journey through the castle - but to be fair it wouldn't be that much harder to beat the game without them, and if you are going for 100% you are bound to find them anyways.I was wondering if i should even talk about the story, because it really isn't a focus in such games. I will just say that it is a very  plot, considering some developments later on (if you played the game and went for the collectibles - you know what i mean). As you would expect out of such title - yes, there are multiple endings.Last thing to mention - I, personally, noticed no technical problems with the game. No crashes, no bugs, game ran well. To be expected, but still worth mentioning.Being unable to access the map is a a big problem. You can see it during stage select, and when entering the stage, but it is really hard to read. Considering you will run each stage more than once if you intend to go for 100% completion, you will probably familiarize yourself with the layout of the stage enough to be able to navigate it. But still, it not being an option is simply a bizzare choice.Also, regarding the mentioned earlier collectibles - i can see how having no indicatior how many you are missing in general could be frustrating. By the time i am writing this i am pretty sure there are guides online where to find everything, but for players that don't want to look them up and do it themselves, a small counter either for each stage or in general would be most helpful. Compass is a fine and unique addition, but it rarely helps that much. Replacing it with rough map and small counter feels like a better idea to me.I am not a big fan of Sister Union attack. It is  but i rarely felt like i actually need to use it. It was too slow to use on bosses reliably, and when used on mobs it felt like a "I cannot be bothered" button. I don't know what i would do to fix it or change it up to be more useful but not overpowered, but i am not a fan of current form.Rest of my issues are spoilers, soooo...Grim Guardians : Demon Purge has flaws, but none harsh enough to distract from a very solid package it delivers. I recommend giving it a try, especially if you are a fan of recent 'modern-retro' games like Shovel Knight or Bloodstained - Curse of the Moon.
_childDocuments_.name: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually review stuff, but it seems there is a lot of confusion and misconceptions about this game.Is it a Metroidvania? YES. While the first 4 to 6 hours is very linear, the game opens up to exploration after seeing most of the levels. This exploration being quite necessary to finding the other endings and getting upgrades for your sub weapons.Is it a conventional Metroidvania? No. But does it have to be exactly like Symphony of the Night? I also don't think so. It's a great game and I think you'll find it really fun if you give it a chance, especially if you're a fan of games like Gal*Gun and other Inti Creates titles.

_childDocuments_.review: While Gal Guardians Demon Purge is a fun, if somewhat frustrating, game, this satire of Iga Castlevania games could have been one actually to equal up or surpass. Instead, it plays it safe and lazy, throws in some balancing issues (Maya being a glass cannon.), and you got yourself an Okay game but not a great one.
_childDocuments_.name: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge

_childDocuments_.review: If you played Curse of the Moon 1 or 2 you know what to expect in terms of gameplay.If you played Gal*Gun games you know what to expect in terms of story and general theme.In short: fantastic vania with wonderfully pervy sense of humor.The only gripe that I noticed is that if you are going for 100%, collectibles are a bit of a chore to collect since there is no information given how many are left per stage and map is more or less nonexistant so you are gonna have to look through every nook and cranny and replay some stages multiple times to go through every route.Still the game compass was enough for me to find everything without any guides so it wasn't that big of a problem and replaying the stages was enjoyable, so I can recommend this game as another Inti Creates classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge

_childDocuments_.review: Grim Guardians: demon Purge (GGDP from here on) is a game done in the classic style of castlevania...kind of, I can kind of see why it's tagged metroidvania despite needing to get to a certain point to see why but also the way it plays is both unique and very well done with that 2D style flair that inti does best like with it's megaman Z series and the like, the short of it you need to know is that it's a stellar game that in fact at least for me personally, fixes many of the issues with the classic castlevania games, granted back then it was limitations in all fairness but Inti did an outstanding job of taking a classic style and making it much much more in it's own way to make a great game dood.Okay onto the deep details of this game, so if anyone is up to date with Inti creates games you will be familiar with the heroine's of this story but for those not it follows the main gals of Gal gun double peace actually doing their job, what job? exorcism/demon hunting, Maya is the melee character who uses summoned weapons, she has low health, high damage and is very much a glass canon, Shinobu her sister is a ranged specialist who uses guns, she also doubles as a kind of tank as she has a lot more health and it seems defence than Maya, they both also have sub weapons much like the castlevania series does that have a myriad of uses both in and out of combat dood.Talking about how there are two characters let's get onto the fact that you get to play with both of them, you can switch at any time which is a great way to get Shinobu to tank a hit or safely get Maya up close to the boss for some major damage, you can even couch co-op and have both girls at the same time, although I can't say what that's like or how that's handled myself, that said having two characters has a massive perk and a fix for something that just never felt fun in old games, that being pits and that fix is the fact that if either of the girls get incapacitated by fall or attack, you revive at a checkpoint, lives in tact and you can go to where they fell and revive them, a maaaajor thing I loved about it dood.The level designs are great, having many great visual details and moving parts at times, I want to mention a particular visual tell you just don't see in games, especially 2D ones anymore that was a pleasant surprise for the style of game it was...okay I'll say it anyway! It's quite bloody and visceral, in fact depending on who you kill an enemy with the death animation for them, they managed to really outdo themselves and make the game look great dood.The game runs smooth as butter, it's a great PC port and movement both in general and for jumping is great which helps you traverse the areas and their different paths of which have a variety of things to find, in fact that's a part of what makes the game so great, it keeps on giving more so you don't feel bored as you have something new to help in combat or get around the stages even better than ever before dood. The story is an interesting one, more serious a tone than the galgun series in general in fact but not without some of it's humorous roots at points, the serious tone can be felt in the fantastic enemy design's too as enemies are nice and intimidating for sure dood!I guess I should also mention the lives system, thanks to the revive function it's nowhere near as intimidating as it sounds, they are easy to grind up (I ended up with 60 in the end) it's built up up by fighting enemies and getting pride points which also double up with making a special move charge up, one that although sort of difficult to land has to be one of the most fantastic looking special attacks when it lands I've seen in a long time, I literally can't spoil it not only for the fact I wouldn't want to ruin it for fans of the series but also it somewhat spoils an aspect of the series dood.Hmmm anything that could be improved on...although I was pretty methodical I have heard friends feel the game needs a map and although I didn't struggle myself I can understand their point with all the collectables, in fact some sort of in game counter that tells you what you have and what you're missing, even if it's only after you beat the game once would have been great, there are many twists and turns and it's easy to get lost if you aren't concentrating and no way to know if there is anything left in a level or not much less what you've done which can be annoying at times dood.Otherwise my end words are this is a fantastic surprise of a good times game and one that I am quite sad ended, I haven't enjoyed a game of this particular style in a long time and that means a lot to me as someone who's first ever game beaten was super castlevania IV as a child, thank you for reading and I hope you all enjoy the game as much as I have dood. ^-^/

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and challenging Castlevania-type game with a fun setting, a lighthearted tone, and an entertaining anime style.The challenge hits a sweet spot of where it will give your skills a good test without getting too frustrating or punishing if you fail.  The boss battles are particularly fun.  Each one refuses to go down without a fight, which makes it especially satisfying when you find a way to counter their dying strike, even if you just end up figuring out how to do so the second time around.Like any good game of this kind, it offers a lot to explore and rewards for exploring.  The sub-weapons you get from advancing also serve as ways to find secrets and reach new areas.  The game does make you go through twice, but it does so in a way that keeps it from being redundant.This game is definitely recommended if you're a fan of of the Bloodstained games, but lamented their glaring lack of slightly tawdry seinen anime.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall solid game. Borrows a bit from Classic Castlevania (Bloodlines/Rondo of Blood?), but there are elements from many other games - Ghost N' Goblins, Mega Man X to name a few.Both the girls do control differently if you are familiar with Inti's Curse of the Moon games, but still controls well enough as you'd expect. Subweapons are pretty fun to use, and with some knowledge of them, you can really tear through some of these levels and bosses. Speaking of those, the levels are well-designed; areas make use of each of the sister's strengths, but can also be done by the opposite character in the instance you lose one of them. The game can also adjusts the placement of a KO'd Maya or Shinobu to ensure that it is possible to revive them. The game is overall on the easier side, so I'd recommend Veteran if you are at all familiar with these types of games, and you can change it when you select your file without any problems.Only complaints is that you have the option to warp to previous stages on your first run through of the castle, and the optional sidequest after finishing the game. As for the first point, there is no reason for you to warp to previous stages before facing Kurona. If you do, you might find that a new path isn't completely doable yet as it may require more subweapons that you don't have, and you will have to finish the stage before being able to warp back as there is no "Escape" option - it just wastes time. And as for that optional sidequest, you will have to comb over EVERY path of every stage to find all the 'mcguffins' for 100%, and there is no way to track them at all. Not even the compass displays them if you are near one; I think the stage select should list how many items are in a stage and how many of them you have to make it more convenient. It is entirely optional, yes, but it still is part of the whole package.I'd recommend the game. Between the moment I started the game and the true ending, I had a good time. Just keep those two complaints in mind and you might have an even better time than I did. I would only 100% the game if you REALLY want to go that extra mile.
_childDocuments_.name: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge

_childDocuments_.review: It's a blast if you're into classic 2D side-scrolling action. The combat's surprisingly good, with epic boss battles that'll keep you hooked. It's all about replayability too, with secrets to uncover and challenges to tackle. Just a heads up though, it's not shy about its "ecchi" moments and over-the-top anime vibes. If you're cool with that, or you can just laugh it off then you're in for a treat.
_childDocuments_.name: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good!As most people have already pointed out, this ISN'T a metroidvania, but that doesn't make it any less fun.This game takes it's inspiration from older Castlevania titles, dividing it's content in stages that end up with a boss (not a big map like Symphony of the Night, where you can backtrack as you please). If I were to make a comparison with a recent game, I'd say that Grim Guardians is more akin to Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon than your good ol' Metroidvania. You do get new sub-weapons that you can use in previous stages to find extra stuff/routes, but nothing game changing like a double jump, teleport or Screw Attack (at least, I haven't found anything like it so far).I'm having an absolute blast playing this with my wife, the multiplayer aspect is really enjoyable. My only nitpick with it is that you can't play with keyboard + controller, both players need to have a gamepad (or maybe I'm just doing something wrong). The game only recognizes Player 2 when a second gamepad is plugged in, otherwise both the keyboard and gamepad will control one character.Also, another bad thing: the voices (both JP and EN) get kinda irritating after a while, there's no denying that.But all in all, If you are an old Castlevania fan, I'd say to give this game a chance. Also, if you got someone to play this with, then I ABSOLUTELY recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pixel Art Castlevania + Moe Anime Girls + Some cliché ecchi comedy = this game.Your reaction to that equation is pretty much enough to know if you will enjoy Gal Guardians. You want more info? Okay.Nowadays, we kinda assume all games inspired by the classic Konami series use the very popular "metroidvania" style. But this game doesn't exactly do that.While you are meant to backtrack and revisit locations with your new powers in order to find secrets, the castle isn't a seamless area to explore. There are levels. And all have a specific entry and exit point. But all have lots of nooks and crannies to find secrets in. And as said earlier, you HAVE to backtrack to older levels in order to find everything.I have heard some comparisons to Portrait of Ruin's "inside the paintings" areas, and that's pretty much on point. Comparing to that particular episode of Castlevania makes even more sense because of the "tag" system between the two heroines, which is a core mechanic in both games.The pixel art in this game is really good, BTW. Animations are very detailed, and you do get a "classic anime girls" feel from the sprites despite their very limited resolution. A feat I never really seen before. The monsters also share this level of detail, making it a very pretty pixelart game overall. Game is worth 7-10 hours to finish the first time, and about the double of that to get the true ending/all secrets. And considering all the backtracking and revisiting of old levels you must do for that, a fair criticism for Gal guardians is that it doesn't have a ton of content relative to its price. But if you play anime games, you know that's a pretty common thing with Japanese publishers. They just... sell games a bit more expensive than we do here in the west. And that's just how it is.As I said at the start, if the idea of "Castlevania, but even more anime and with lots of moe girls" seems good to you, just trust that feeling and get this game at the next sale. And if you want a good pixel platformer, you can also consider this purchase very safely.It's a good game. But not amazing enough to be something that will appeal to anyone either.  To like it, you have to be "already into" one of the things it can offer, aka anime and pixel platformers. But if you're not one of those people, you probably didn't read that review up to that point, now did you? ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Yes I would recommend this.  The castlevania experience is not so much rpgish but there are items to collect to increase your statistics.  The game plays well with many varied weapons that feel well catered to the experience.  The game is also not hard so it is pretty relaxing.  There are some flaws though.  I did not care for how you had to basically beat the first 5 stages again on a second loop with a few changes.  Also getting any different ending required something of a collectathon.  And then there seems to be yet another ending where it requires another collectathon.  After the first collectathon of saving students I did not bother with the second one.  Good game overall and I had fun.  Cute at times as well.  Hope they make some quality of life improvements like adding additional collectibles to the map on right press of the analog. Maybe a map you can access on start would be nice.  Some of the paths the first loop are not properly blocked off.  Very few glitches I encountered though so that was nice to see.8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying my time with this, it's a classic castlevania and since konami refuses to port castlevania adventure rebirth to anything, let alone steam, this is the best new classic castlevania game made in the last 20 years that you can actually purchase.Also liking cute anime girls will increase your enjoyment of this title about tenfold.Edit: Since there seems to be some confusion with the zoomer crowd.A "Metroidvania" is a castlevania game that plays like a metroid game (SotN)this is a game that plays like a classic castlevania game, which tend to play like castlevania games and not like metroid games.

_childDocuments_.review: Good castlevania style game set in the Gal*Gun universe with many character appearances from it. It features 1 or 2 player modes, with each character having their own unique weapon and 5 different sub weapons that are useful for different situations or taking shortcuts in the levels. If you play single player you can instantly switch between the two characters to make use of their individual weapons or sub weapons.There's a lot of hidden power upgrades, secret areas, stages and students needing to be rescued. Many of which you can only reach by revisiting the levels later after unlocking abilities or sub weapons. I played through the game on 1 player mode on a Steam deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge

_childDocuments_.review: Grim Guardians is a cute and fun Castlevania-like game where you play as the two protagonists, Shinobu and Maya, as you battle your way to the top of their school turned demon infested castle. Shinobu plays as a sturdy ranger with high hp and low attack, whereas Maya plays as a glass brawler with low hp and high attack. Switching as the situation calls for it is paramount to getting through the stages. The stage design is quite good, with sprawling levels that feature many hidden rooms and alternate paths, especially as you unlock more traversal options. There were some rooms in the levels that became a nightmare to traverse if you lost Shinobu, especially partway through said room where it becomes nearly impossible for Maya to actually traverse the platforms to get to her without ranged options. Bosses are quite fun to figure out and offer a great deal of challenge. There is a lot of incentive to go back through the stages to collect the rest of the items, especially as some endings are tied to them. The game is missing a map and item tracker, which does make it somewhat difficult to 100% it, especially if you were not keeping track of the items you obtained yourself. Overall, this is a great game that I recommend not only to those that have played GalGun before, but also to those looking for a Castlevania-like experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not an amazing game, but not a terrible one either. Get from point A to point B and fight a boss in 7 different stages, . Although the game teases you and makes it seem like you can explore, just don't. From my experience (and the main reason I do not recommend this game), whenever you try to explore in the first half of the game you are 90% of the time blueballed and met with a "mysterious door" that prevents you from exploring. They will open in the second half, but it just feels so counter-intuitive to punish the player for exploring just to have the doors magically open in the second half. It doesn't help that the first half of the game just feels like it was made to pad out the game due to it being extremely easy and the second half . The hardest part of the game for me ended up being a platforming section that makes heavy use of a sub-ability rather than a boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge

_childDocuments_.review: It's an enjoyable game but definetly not too good.It has hints of metroidvania despite being more like a classic castlevania adapted to modern gameplay, which is totally fine, but it doesn't commit to become a full metroidvania and it hinders the experience. There clearly are places to backtrack to, but the process to do so is too tedious and the skills a burden to use. Add a barely functioning compass, too many one way doors, having to do the ENTIRE level from the beggining for most secrets and a map you only see at the beggining of a stage and you get a terrible and boring exploration.Most of the skills you get are quite unusable, specially the ones that let you get to other places. The paper platform rarely sees any real use, and the freeze penguin requires you to already know the position of enemies to properly use it.And this ties into combat. The combat is simply bad. Shinobu is an afterthought in this game made to save Maya when you mess up, since the game clearly didn't take her into account when designing levels and enemies. Either enemies become too tedious to fight or are a joke that you slowly and boringly turn to dust from a distance.The 4th boss made me stop (and it's also the one you get the most prominent movement utility from). The platforms you need to get up to punish you for using your tools to more effectively defeat the boss, since most of them will hit them and lower them making the boss unreachable and most of its attacks able to hit you. Also, it's not funny to have to start over and over again while you have a student being sexually assaulted in the background, because tentacle is funny or something.And about starting over and over again, I played in the classic mode, with lives. May I say that this "difficulty" adds nothing? For bosses you can go in, mess up and die with one of the two (most of the time Maya, let's be real) and then come back with the other one and revive her quickly to just infinitely loop the boss room. I only had to use 1 extra life because I fell on a pit twice, and in all that time I only managed to get one extra life through collectibles despite killing all enemies I passed by and breaking special decorations. The special attack bar charges quite fast so, if this is the case, what's the use for these collectibles on the lifeless difficulty?The art and animations are great though. I loved both the artstyle and how fluid everything felt. It's what caught my eye the most when watching how this game played.And, for the love of god, add sound options and let me turn down the voices or make them less common. I was going crazy hearing them moan on every jump.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to play a cozy classicvania / metroidvania hybrid similar to rondo of blood but with fast paced snappy controls, this is pretty much the game for you.Both characters kit are quite fun but a bit limited in term of movements (no double jump / slide / back dash / dive / can't switch character mid-air) which is intentional by design but made me feel the game would have been a lots cooler as a fully fledged out metroidvania.Overall it was a fun cruise, and i'll definitely be checking the sequel out.
_childDocuments_.name: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge

_childDocuments_.review: okay so its sorta old school castlevania vibe (pre-metroid) - there are levels, you go through them, kill the boss, go to the next level.  there's a little bit of back tracking because levels will have areas you can't go into until you get some item, but its kinda annoying moreso than a good metroidvania where there's a single continguous world.the game has some pretty glaring problems in my opinion:- while you can switch between two characters, when one dies you warp the living character back to the most recent save point.  the character that died is still dead, but even though one character didn't die you'll have to replay some part of the level.  I think that if one character dies you should just automatically swap to the living character- the game has a lot of just *cheap* level design elements.  like, hard but not hard in a fun way.  hard in a way that makes the game feel like you have just do a bunch of work.  video games shouldn't feel like work.  like go play castlevania 3, that's hard in a way where you're like 'yea i wanna play more', whereas everytime i get hit by a demon painting or whatever i'm kinda just annoyed they're even there.- it's so close to castlevania it doesn't feel original, though some of the bosses do have some originality.- there are weird bugs, like on my system there's a vertical bar all the way on the right of the screen.can't say i recommend it, even as a castlevania fan.  you could probably have better luck with various fangames or just play the originals.  bloodstained maybe, depending on which title though.    gaurdian gals is not the worst game ever, but i can't give this game a 'meh' so it gets a thumbs down.  I'd give it a C to C-

_childDocuments_.review: While I am not a Gal Gun fan, i am a Castlevania fan. In fact, Castlevania is my favorite game series of all time, going back to when I was "little demondude777" playing Castlevania on NES. I grew up with the series and still love it.I picked this up expecting to have something Metroidvaniaish...but the game really isn't. Yes you can backtrack levels, but it is more like the old school Castlevania style of stages. It does have character switching a lot like Castlevania III or the Curse of the Moon series. And it handles the ranged character and melee characters pretty well to keep them balanced (and give you a reason to watn to switch other than one is dying). I do wish the melee one had more health though, but she packs a serious punch.Level design is passable. Its not super impressive, and pretty easy to cheap a lot of enemies with the guns that can't hit you back. But the character swapping fun makes up for the standard level design.I would say $25 is pretty steep asking price for this. So if you can find it on sale, and appreciate the stage Castlevania style...it might be worth dropping a few hours into it.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet game that is about 6-8 hours long+ Movement feels good and the sub weapons add to it, so naturally platforming feels fun+ Characters tool sets feel fun although some sub-weapons are very situational+ Presentation wise, the bosses and stages look pretty good, nothing stand out~ Its a tie in of Gal Gun so it can get a bit degen but its easy to ignore~ Some bosses were pretty ez and some were pretty difficult~ Minor smoiler but last boss can be made easier if you do certain things which is a bit annoying although it makes sense(?)- Game doesn't have much replay-ability once you run it twice, unless you want to try the 3rd difficulty which you have to unlockI highly recommend this game unless you can't stomach the Gal Gun fan service

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this as a coop game.The existence of a coop mode is nothing more than a footnote on the store page, and it’s a footnote in game as well, it is designed to be played solo.1. The second character’s move set is more like a temporary power boost than a full time job; more damage in melee but with less HP.2. The abilities the second character unlocks seem to be more “utility” than fun.3. Death pits kill one of the characters until the next checkpoint, leaving the fallen player with nothing to do. The death pits get especially numerous starting with stage 3.4. There is a system where you can jump on the other character to reach higher places. This is always active, which means you frequently accidentally jump onto your coop partner mid combat (and then sometimes continuing into the death pits mentioned above)5. Boss HP is not scaled for both characters to be doing damage at the same time. They die incredibly quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. It's neither a Metroidvania nor a Classic Castlevania, I'd say it's somewhat in between.The game is divided in stages, and you are able to freely explore each stage until you reach the boss, after that you can retry said stage or any previous stage. Some stuff will be unlocked by skills that you get further in the game, meaning that some backtracking is planned. I would have liked however if after the first time clearing a stage a map (like the map in Castlevania Symphiny of the Night for example) was implemented, either you remember the entire stage or either randomly walk around until you find what you were looking for.The gameplay feels good, the movement is nice, and the characters are fun to use (one much more than the other imo), I also love how the game is coop.I'm not yet sure if some things are locked behind coop (since character can step on each to reach high surfaces) or if it only makes some places easier to reach.The OST is nice, so is the art style.There is a story, but it's more of an excuse to introduce you to the characters and the game, nothing to die for but it's not a slog. It's a way to smash a couple fun dialogues here and there, I'd say it's appreciated.The game is not hard, you can decide to play with limited life and somewhat harder combat, or you can decide to have unlimited lifes. You can make copies of the same save anyway.The sub weapons use an ammo system similar to a Classic Castlevania, but instead of having to pick the up and drop the current one, you unlock more as you progress and you can switch freely between them, also the subweapons are what will allow you to go to certain places.It's a fun game, worth getting and playing, it doesn't take itself too seriously and it's fun to play with a friend. If you're looking for an "hardcore" classic Castlevania style challenge though, this is not it. If you're looking for the Symphony of the night experience, this is also not it.Note: Grim Guardians was a better name than Gal Guardians.

_childDocuments_.review: A great platformer based on the Gal Gun series, specifically the 2 female main characters, Shinobu and Maya Kamizono, from Gal Gun Double Peace.It plays like a solid 2D platformer, reminiscent of older Castlevania games, before the series became known for it's "metroidvania" style. Both characters are fun to play as and the game expects you to change often, as each character has strengths and weaknesses. There is a reason to replay old levels in the form of upgrades such as more health, defense upgrades, more ammo, etc. Each level also contains your classmates which you can rescue, giving more reasons to explore the multiple paths in each level. The game also expands upon a few things in the second half, including harder versions of bosses, ability to upgrade your subweapons, and another somewhat extensive collection aspect (though with no payout besides an achievement.)There are 3 endings, each tied to a different objective you must complete. You're not locked out, as you can replay levels and the final boss as much as you want.Gal Guardians: Demon Purge is a wonderfully fun 2D platformer with tons of nods and easter eggs to both Castlevania and Gal Gun. Definitely recommended for fans of Gal Gun, though you won't find an overly sexualized game (though it does have it's moments and some CGs). Co Op is tons of fun, though sadly only local/remote play.

_childDocuments_.review: What is a classicvania? it's a classic castlevania; you know anything before Symphony of the night. It's a successor to Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon using GalGun characters. If aren't familiar with GalGun; it is not required reading but will blindside you if you are unprepared. TL;DR; It's a solid 4/5 for a Inti Creates Game in the  style and we should be tagging it as such. The stages are small but dense with winding paths that all lead to the boss. Exploration and combat are choices made during the run with the stage select screen presenting a rudimentary stage layout. During your first play through you're probably going to be slow and methodical and probably re-explore stages; but in subsequent runs you'll learn how to be more aggressive with movement to weave between enemies and how to manipulate the stage/enemies to help you advance further faster.The game itself is short, don't get me wrong It's a very short game in a world where every game is either a 40-60 hour experience or a live service. If you play it you'll probably beat it in a sitting or two. I don't know like 4-6 hours if you're listening to the story, much less if you skip it. Though being a short game isn't bad, it means that it respects your time for a playthrough. I don't recommend 100% the game, it's really really not worth it and you should only do it if you genuinely appreciate the game. It's not a hard game unless you're trying to brute force it on the hardest difficulty. That said, you'll play the game your way, whether that be shooting from a distance with your anti-demon submachine gun or getting in close to cut them to shreds. The Enemy and lamp placements are somewhat based off the difficulty you choose and will become increasingly rude and punishing as you select a harder difficulty. Though they don't lock you into difficulty; so you can switch it during gameplay and continue on the same file. Don't be afraid of turning down the difficulty if you're just exploring, There is nothing to take pride in playing on the hardest difficulty in an area you've already cleared.Look okay, I'm not here to convince you to buy and play the game. If you're looking at this game you probably already have it in your mind that you want to buy it. I have 100% completed the game and can say that it's not for everyone. I like the pixel Art, CGs, game feel and general shortness of the game. It's just something that you can sit down and clear in a sitting.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR;+ level design is generally interesting, albeit maybe less so than CotM+ bosses are simple to figure out but very fun to clear the first time at least- characters are not fleshed out enough to justify all the switching- difficulty is too low, especially with revival mechanic-----Kurona's latest prank has turned the school into something of a demon's castle – an 'akumajou' if you will – and it's up to Shinobu and Maya to send her back to the HFIL.Based off the demo, I had a more negative opinion of the game, but I suspected the level design would become more interesting as the game progressed. That guess was about right. It's not on the level of Curse of the Moon, but it's good, and I'm always happy to play a retro-style platformer.Bosses also become more difficult, but I haven't lost a single life yet on account of the revival system. That's fine, I think the bad feeling of losing a character and consequently the boss regaining health is enough of a punishment to make you try to avert said loss. I would prefer if this was a little more... chewy? I like having to digest a boss fight. Curse of the Moon had more of this. Maybe this game becomes more difficult, but I feel like it's clearly going for a more breezy difficulty on account of it being a game partially for Gal*Gun fans.There's a bit of a furore here over the game not being a Metroidvania game despite some user-applied tags on the store page. It's fine by me, because I don't like Metroidvania games in general, but the approach to replayability here feels as if it borrows something from Metroidvania games as well as Curse of the Moon. That game used multiple routes that could be accessed by certain characters, sometimes only on certain playthroughs, as a means to make the game more replayable and also as a reward for keeping characters alive; the design was brilliant in both improving the game and adding some flavour, granting the levels an extra degree of mystique. Conversely, Grim Guardians grants you extra abilities, and multiple routes exist largely so you can explore and find more girls to rescue and more powerups. Unfortunately, it's not as holisticly applied as CotM, which would throw constant shortcuts and diverging routes, and it is no longer at all a reward for good play. Still, it adds replayability. It's FINE.The two characters aren't fleshed out well enough to justify the character switching mechanic. I know the game is designed for 2-player, but what fraction of players is going to be playing this game 2-player? Are all the Gal*Gun fans going to be passing off the second controller to their girlfriends and wives? Seriously though. Both characters have one main attack, and a range of subweapons. Shinobu is a ranged character, and generally you will only use her when: 1) there are lots of ranged or aerial enemies; 2) you don't want to risk Maya losing life, since she has less. I feel like she would work best as a summon who stands on the spot and shoots forward, so you could get some synergy with her as you might be able to in 2-player. In fact, if they added that ability without changing anything else, they would have a more interesting game instantly. Maybe you could remove the switching and bump Maya's health, give her all of Shinobu's subweapons... I feel like this would also improve the feeling of the two sisters working together, it would add flavour to give the characters this kind of synergy and clearly it's something that is possible for the few Gal*Gun fans who have someone to pass off a second controller to, so it should be possible in single player too.Graphically, the game is fine, but I keep fixating on the character sprites' faces. They look a little silly. Maya's face is particularly galling.Anyway, this is good. Not as good as Curse of the Moon, but it's enjoyable.Edit: after a few more hours... it's not bad, but the level design doesn't evolve enough and the enemies & gimmicks aren't used in interesting ways. _childDocuments_.review: Gal Guardians is a mixed bag that I ultimately cannot recommend.The best thing about this game is that the main feature of having two distinct characters really delivered. You get a unique pairing of a ranged tank and a melee glass cannon. This forces you to constantly switch characters because in any given situation you will be better off with one character over the other. Enemies, puzzles, traps, and even specific boss patterns are designed to be strong against one of your characters and weak against the other.Unfortunately, while the gameplay of the main characters is great, everything else about this game is below average. First off, this isn't a Metroidvania in the same sense of Super Metroid or SOTN where you explore a vast interconnected map. Instead this is a series of fairly linear levels where at the beginning and end of each level you can warp back to any level you've completed. There is an incentive to replay old levels because new powers will unlock secret areas, but I found that these were rarely worth the effort. Besides, The design in this game is extremely uninspired. Levels are about as straightforward and bland as it gets. Puzzles are very obvious and uninteresting. Enemies are very basic and don't pose much of a threat. Many enemies in this game just sit there and wait for you to kill them. In fact this game is very easy even on the veteran setting. The game gives you plenty of 1ups but you never need to use your lives since it is nearly impossible to die. If one of your two characters loses all their health you restart with the other character from the last checkpoint, but don't lose a life unless you die again as that character. As long as you make it back to where your other character died you can then revive them and keep going. This makes boss fights especially trivial because bosses will lose some of their max hp every time you die to them. That means you can die and revive your partner over and over without losing any lives, which will also cut the bosses max hp down low enough until they are easy to kill.Some other random complaints I have for this game is that your characters talk waaaay too much. Every time you attack they say a line. First thing I did was go to the options to mute this and I found that there's no audio settings at all. Also, really minor spoiler here but Fun gameplay stuck in a boring world. 2/5

_childDocuments_.review: Something odd I've noticed about Gal Guardians: Demon Purge (GG) is that the title changed at some point, replacing Grim for Gal. I guess there was a title dispute with another company, so they relinquished. Either way, when I was looking at the previews before it released, I was interested in what looked to be a promising Metroidvania. However, it wound up being quite different than I expected.  I don't think I'm entirely wrong for thinking GG would play like a Metroidvania with the visual style shown in the trailers. Especially since the after-image from characters walking is an iconic aspect of titles like Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. However, the gameplay is actually closer to the NES versions. Each section of the castle is essentially its own stage, shown with an image just like from the OG Castlevania. Instead of finding sub-weapons from candles, you unlock new ones from beating each stage boss, able to choose which one you want freely. Breaking candles to replenish how often you can use them remains the same though. Another new feature is a super attack, which takes quite a long time to charge up. It's not an attack you'd waste on basic foes, but would use on tough enemies and bosses. Frankly, I found the difficulty balancing unusual. Since you can revive the second character as long as you can return to the same place as where they died, it's better to keep one of them in good shape instead of getting both to near death. Because this also applies to bosses, who have checkpoints on their health bar, they can be less of a threat than the stages. I was very clumsy during my boss fights, but with such low stakes, my fumbling never even cost me a life. Instant death pits and annoying enemies came closer to snagging a life than the boss battles.  Despite being able to play as two different characters, their movesets don't make much difference to their controls. A simple example is tapping the attack button to swing origami blades compared to a burst of bullets. Additionally, even though you'll swap between them and their sub-weapons, the controls are mapped logically, without ever confusing me. The only thing I could see mixing someone up is recognizing which sub-weapon is represented by the icons as you switch between them. It seemed a hair sensitive with the down input, but that could be the X-box 360 controller's fault as well.  You play as two high schoolers who happen to be demon-slaying sisters. When they started referencing other students by name, I wondered if this was a sequel to a game I wasn't aware of, but it's actually a spin-off. GG utilizes characters from the Gal Gun series. Those games are highly suggestive and perverse, without quite crossing the line into a full-on sex game. Regardless, how many people would be that attentive to the potential lore of that series and want to see it expand in a tamer release?  Considering how GG plays like the NES Castlevania games, I don't know why they didn't use an art style more representative of that. When you replicate a style strongly affiliated with a specific kind of gameplay, you indirectly suggest your game will match it. Although a second playthrough allows you to explore and find secrets with the sub-weapons you get from beating bosses, that doesn't really capture the spirit of a Metroidvania. Regardless of my complaints about being misleading, it is a good-looking title, and some enemies or transformations can be startling and off-putting.  The use of classic instruments like the piano are used to good effect in the music. Orchestral tunes can set a variety of moods, and though a good amount of the songs focus on upbeat action, there's enough of them with a dash of Gothic moodiness. There aren't a ton of voice-overs since the story isn't that elaborate, but the Japanese voice acting sounded fine to my ignorant English ears. I did find some of the menu sound effects a trifle annoying, but at least there's no low health warning to drive me crazy.  🌟 The visual elements fit a horror game well. It's not obscene with buckets of entrails and gore, but still has a creepy vibe. 🌟 If you're going to copy other games, you might as well pick good ones.  ❌ Since enemies don't drop health on Veteran difficulty, and there's no money or XP either, you've no incentive to fight them. ❌ It feels like a slap in the face when your new sub-weapon would have resolved issues you had in the previous stage. ❌ Although the bosses look grand, they have very limited movesets and patterns. 🔍 After defeating each boss, you'll be in an area where you can try out the new sub-weapons with unlimited ammo. That way you can see their attributes and potential applications. 🔍 The firearm's reach doesn't quite extend to the other side of the screen. However, most enemies' reach and reaction distance is shorter than that.  For me, what sunk my enthusiasm for the game was how different elements didn't cohere together well. With Shinobu being able to attack enemies from a distance and tank a few hits, she becomes the more useful character. Being able to do more damage when up-close doesn't matter much when you die in only three hits. However, Maya is a good choice for handling a few pathetic enemies that die from only one of her attacks. In theory, a glass cannon can be an interesting character, but a super-safe, long-range alternative really undermines that utility. The bigger issue though comes from the level design. Some rooms in the castle have so little content they might as well not exist. Due to the stage layout, most enemies are either a complete non-issue or a nuisance. Because you're expected to play through GG once with minimal abilities, the level design has to account for how limited your jumps are. After seeing platforms you can't possibly reach, you just start zoning out and taking the path of least resistance. It makes the first playthrough seem like an intentional time waster, a way to evade Steam's refunding system. Otherwise, why start on a bland first step, expecting people to power through and get to a game worth playing? I'm not doing that, the game isn't worthwhile.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an okay at best game with a lot of shortcomings or odd decisions that makes this review negative for me. It really sells the Castlevania feeling with its art direction, music, and action, but it didn't fully commit to the metroidvania genre. Instead it's a level based game where you move from the start of the level to the end, fight the boss, and then you move to the next level to do the same.If you want to backtrack for collectibles you have to teleport to a previous level, and do everything from start to finish with no minimap, but only a bad compass. On top of that there are multiple 1 directional doors, and spots of "no return" unless you unlock some skills later to be able to go backwards which means you will have to clear the stage from start to finish multiple times. I wouldn't call that a fun replay value at all.There are 2 characters you can switch between, one with an SMG for a weapon, while the other one have the old reliable melee weapon. The melee weapon is amazing, and fun to play with while the SMG is just straight garbage.That's all I can say honestly, if you want to play this just wait for a sale, and keep one thing in mind which would be to backtrack at a much later stage when you have more abilities to avoid headaches.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR:  This game is a great time, if you're a big fan of both Megaman and Castlevania style games. Controls like a dream, and was so much fun that I decided to 100% all the achievements.-----Long version:  If you like solid action platformers that have the precision of both Megaman and Castlevania, then you will love not only the way this game controls - but the stage by stage nature of it as well.Don't be fooled by people calling this a "metroidvania", as that's not the case. It's more classicvania style game, and linear - but with some exploration elements in each of the different stages. So, the pace keeps going pretty smooth and fast. Though with utilizing some of the exploration, you can unlock a couple of alternate endings.The level design is very much akin to how the Megaman Zero games were, just with stairs instead of wall-jumping. And with how the two characters control, it's very easy to get a nice sense of flow going; once you've played through a couple of stages and mastered the precise but somewhat floaty controls.And the boss fights, some of them can seem brutal. But once you recognize the patterns you'll find yourself going: "Just one more, I know I can do this, I nearly had it!" As the loop hooks you, from feeling the progress you're making.Another thing in this game, that's more quality of life than necessity - is the fact that there's three different "styles" of how to play:Casual: Unlimited lives and no knockback on hits. Perfect for those who are just starting with this kind of game.Veteran: Limited lives that can be earned by playing well, and classic Castlevania and Megaman knockback is here. So mind them bottomless pits!Legened: Unlocked after beating the game the first time. All the elements of Veteran mode are here, BUT now if even just one of the two characters' HP hits zero, you lose a life. So, play carefully.All in all, this game is a great time. More than worth the price of admission, especially for action platformer enthusiasts like myself.

I'll nit pick a little, Just because nothing is 100% perfect.Limited Content:Was reading it can take around 12 hours to 100% Would like to see more content The game is around $25 and given that it is an indie, I feel the quality that is already here Is immaculate so more content should be a reasonable request.Sub Weapons: Most of the sub weapons are almost useless besides exploration, but I also tried to brute force most of the bosses So the Sub's probably played a bigger role than I give them credit for, it's my primary reason for comparing to Mega Man since 90% of his power ups are barely used outside Bosses.Revive:I understand having 2 characters is for the purpose of Co Op, but If you die you don't automatically switch so you can continue the fight, No, The other character starts back at a checkpoint(and on random occasions) the same room and you have to fight your way back to the body to do CPR. This by far is the thing I hate the most about the game, Besides there not being MORE game, Having to whittle the boss BACK down (you'll understand at the final boss) AND Revive my partner had me triggered like a MF at the end of my play through.All-in-all I'd say it's money well spent especially if you have a Co Op partner to cut through the game with, I believe that would remove 99.9% of the issues I faced on my play through.For $26 bucks I got a hell of a game and I'm glad I didn't get it on sale and that's saying a lot since this is the 2nd Game I paid full price for on my account and I don't regret it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the demo I expected to get a clone of Curse of the Moon. It could have been a really great clone tho, but in current state Grim Guardians feels average at best and unfinished at worst.It's not a metroidvania, but each area here has a lot of branching paths, some of which can be unlocked under certain conditions. So you'll revisit the same areas multiple times to collect everything and to save everyone. But there is no map, so I have to remember which route I took last time. This is not easy, given the repetitive design of some rooms. And to make things even worse - the Library stage is a fricking maze. Oh, and you have to beat the game twice, by the way. So yeah, you'll waste a LOT of time in this game. Level design feels unfinished. You may accidentally reach another route and head to the start of the stage, in the totally wrong direction (because you don't have a map), wasting more than 20 minutes for absolutely nothing. And sometimes you WANT to get to another route (to find collectibles or save the girls), but there is a one-way door, which blocks your path and forces you to restart the entire area from the very beginning in order to reach that one specific place.Oh, by the way... You'll lose you progress if you use teleportation room without visiting the next area first. I'm not even kidding! You have to leave teleportation room, visit the next area, return to the teleportation room and only then teleport wherever you want. Otherwise, progress will not be saved and you'll have to go through the recent area all over again. This. Is. Ridiculous.I think that galgun plot doesn't fit with the castlevania-ish atmosphere. Like, you're wandering through the grim demonic castle, destroying tons of scary demons - blood and meat all over the screen! And few hours later you're searching for schoolgirl's panties and naughty magazines... Is it just me or these things does not match together really well? I mean, I don't mind to see galgun characters in such setting and I don't mind jokes and references to other games. But it would be better if the plot of this specific game was less pervy.I really tried to enjoy this game - you can clearly see how much effort has gone into it. The art style is great as always. Music creates that spooky castlevania-ish atmosphere. Boss battles are really fun. Humor and references are good. Even each of the lost schoolgirls has their own unique portrait and personality - it was totally unnecessary, but it is here and it's good! Looks like Intis tried to create something bigger and more complex than Curse of the Moon, but instead the game feels unfinished and overcomplicated. So I can't recommend Grim Guardians, especially at this price.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'd wishlisted this game the moment I could. As a longtime Castlevania, metroidvania and platformer fanI'm always on the lookout for good games in those genres with a CV vibe and Grim Guardians looked promising... But when I finally got to play it my hopes and expectations were dashed as surely as if a herd of elephants were dropped on them. Inti Creates is unfortunately better at making trailers than games.So what's so bad about this game? It feels like they combined elements from Castlevania: Vampire's Kiss, Bloodlines and a bit from Portrait of Ruin as the core idea for the gameplay. It's not a metroidvania, more a linear platformer with in-stage branches. You can replay the stages to access new paths via your newly acquired subweapons that differ between the two sisters you play as. Only, they are unequal. Shinobu uses a submachine gun that at least hits what you're aiming at. Maya has extremely shortrange origami weapons and less health and seems to take more damage. Her weapon hitboxes are iffy at best and her subweapons are almost purely utility based.Which is not handy in a game that relies on enemy spam with questionable placements to give some semblance of difficulty. It's more frustrating than anything. Add in that the stages themselves are not quite what you'd hope for. Samey backgrounds for the entire stage, barely any enemy variety (mostly palette swaps) and fairly unmemorable music.As a -lite game it may not be bad, but at the price they are asking there's just too little content to justify the price. NVM that the English voices are poorly used. Every action you make gets a high-pitched voiceclip that sounds about as over the top as in the worst of Disgaea. Can't these sisters even fart without squealing out? Oh well.There is some good in the game though. The bosses and some parts of some stages do look beautifully done. But pretty pictures do not cover the holes in the game's walls. So for now, refund requested. I do hope that the dev team can fix these issues and others besides, but I cannot recommend it as is.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to like this game but.. it is a pain thanks to some design decisions:- No double jump. This is VERY ANNOYING as levels have many sightly-higher-than-what-you-can-reach platforms. Workarounds?   - A power-up which throws a temporal platform DOWNWARDS in front of you  - A power-up which, if used while airborne throws you BACKWARDS  - A 'chain' power-up to hang from some ceilings.All very cumbersome. Just put a damn double jump!- Bad sub weapons. Some sub weapons feel constrained or dedicated mostly to specific situations (like opening special doors). Sub weapon ammo is not that great either (upgrades do not help much) You end up using your main attacks mostly- Limited attack directions. Normal attacks only go forward (like 8 bit games). Later on, a power-up allows you to shoot (weak) bullets.. upwards... Yay!- Sword play issues, Some enemies have got small hit boxes: which makes you get very close to attack them. If an enemy just walks into you, you get hit as you were too close to begin with. And there's no dash-back / evade skill- Gun play issues. Bullets are weak. And maybe that's expected but... bullets also do not hit crawling enemies and you cannot jump while shooting (jump first then shoot..- No gun reload button. To reload, you MUST use up all your bullets... Sometimes reload will pick you at bad moments- Useless special attack. Fill a gauge and shoot a special SLOOOW bullet... which most likely won't hit a boss... Then the gauge fills so slowly you can't even think about using it twice on boss battles- No minimap / position tracking. You HAVE TO know where you're going, because there's no minimap while playing a level. A 'compass' feature points you to powerups ONLY IF you are close enough.- Checkpoints are not saved. If you 'reset the level' you return to your latest checkpoint but... if you exit the game (to resume playing later) checkpoints are not saved.- No exit level option: to exit a level you either WALK ALL the way to the start / finish or quit the  game- Pit-falls. Some falls are fatal, even if 'there's another room below' in that level- No sense of progression. There are a few power-ups to pick but those do not make a big difference on how many hp / armor / attack power you have- Sword girl has less hp / takes more damage. That's feels odd... why not make hp equal for both characters?- Boss battles... are a mixed bag. Some feel easy (once you know what to do) and others will have you re-trying over and over. You don't die at boss battles because of raw difficulty... but flawed battle designs.- Revive on Casual mode. You die on a boss fight, then you can re-enter the boss room with your other char, revive your fallen partner and resume the fight. Bosses sometimes even keep the damage you've made them... So.. DEVS KNOW boss battles are annoying and they even 'grant you' this handicap. You end with a 'fighting' char and a 'revive fighter' char.... not fun.This is a shame! The game has some good ideas but the execution was messy. Was the game rushed or what happened here? There is room for improvement here... but maybe changes are not even coming.I'd say, skip this one

_childDocuments_.review: To me, the game is a VERY bare bones action platformer. I understand my opinion is not popular, but this just how I honestly feel about it. You don't have to agree, and if you like the game, that's great. Read on if you like, but understand and respect that your opinion will probably not match mine. I don't understand why people have a hard time when one opinion doesn't match theirs.I kind of jumped the gun on this one. Bought it the moment it came out after watching one trailer, thinking it was one way, but the actual game is very different than I expected. The controls of the game are great and that's the only positive I have to say about the game. There isn't really much in the game to keep me engaged. There isn't usable items you can collect, or any currency, so killing off a bunch of enemies isn't very fulfilling. Just rush to the end. There are two big annoyances to me in this game. One is that this game is level based and not exploration based. Your progress isn't saved unless you complete the level, which feels kind of dated to me at this point. The levels can be kind of long, and unfortunately I don't have a lot of time to spend. I feel this game has so much potential, but falls short from odd design decisions.The next big annoyance is the voices. Oh my GOSH the voices! WHY is there no way to turn them off? I have the game nearly muted because it was driving me nuts straight out of the gate. The first thing my fiance said to me when she saw me playing to this was "is there a way to turn off their voices? That's the first thing I noticed and it isn't very comforting to the ear." There are just so many other better games out there that isn't much different to this one, making this game hardly stand out to me. It just doesn't bring anything new that has been done before. I'd imagine this game will be forgotten quickly over time. I'll hold onto it, and probably finish it someday, but right now I don't see that happening anytime soon.

Should have been a clue that there was no inventory screen nor map screen nor anyway to adjust the volume ingame without adjusting in windows.Edit:  It's important to note that this game had the Metroidvania tag yesterday (day of launch) and now the metroidvania tag is gone (which is good because it isn't)  Felt like the tag was used to trick metroidvania fans early on.  But that being said the graphics are amazing and if you want a Castlevania 1 NES experience it's great.

_childDocuments_.review: My review is short, simple, and to the point.gorgeous pixel graphics? sure. I'll gladly give the game that.what seems to be fun 2D action ala the original / earlier castlevania entries? sure. what I played was that too.But when I think 'metroidvania' I do NOT think of staged, discrete (IE separated and not continuous) levels that you can't openly back-track to, a lack of almost ANY form of RPG elements or upgrading ala the 'metroid' part of 'metroidvania', and a combat system that feels clunky and shallow.let me defend that - yes, the two characters get upgrades and power-ups, but if the closest comparison I could make would be to Castlevania - order of ecclesia, and Grim Guardians feels like someone took OoE and stripped it of almost any mechanical depth.I'm not saying GG is a bad game, I certainly didn't play it long enough to make that call adequately. _childDocuments_.review: Incredibly well polished and fun game to play. It's sorta a mix of old-school Castlevania with a more modern aspect to it. While it's not a true Metroidvania, it does include some stuff that does require you to do later.Weapons are very fun to use, and the character swap system is great. Each character has their strengths and weaknesses. There is also a sub-weapon system (think like the holy water and the crosses in Castlevania), though I didn't find much use.Which leads to my first point. The sub-weapon system is... okay. Later in the game, you unlock two weapons (one for each character) that does not consume mana points. They aren't used for combat directly, but more for mobility, and I've spent the vast majority of the game using them, outside a few things here and there that I had to use the other ones for some secret.Some of these sub-weapons are used to unlock new areas that you'll later can reach you that you weren't able before, giving the Metroidvania esque type. Other unlockables are also possible this way, but I don't wish to spoil too much.This game, however, has something that I absolutely adore. When you have weapons you can also use for mobility. Praise game devs that does this, because Minoria was another game that did this incredibly well. Here, it's not as straight-forward as that game, but you can still use attacks as mobility later in the game.Haven't found any glitches in the game whatsoever. Well, except one... There was one time that I died, and my character landed on a spinning platform, and the game ceased to work (it was stuck), and not even going to the Main Menu fixed it, I had to close it entirely and open again. It only happened once, though I don't know if this always happen with spinning platforms.The only thing I wish there was, is an option to disable voice acting. Guys, it's a little too much when your character is constantly shouting every single thing in every single action. I got used to it, I personally preferred the English VAs because it meant less voices in general (Japanese VAs include every dialogue and interaction, while English VAs is only interactions, not dialogue). I actually don't like when games don't have an option to disable voice acting, but I gave this game a chance, and I'm glad I did, because man, this is a good game. I do however feel like having an option could reach for other players that aren't really into the whole Gal Gun thing (myself included, since I never played it beforehand), or even the Animus (some still play even if there's an aesthetic to it, but would rather disable VAs).Oh, with that said, this is a spin-off of the Gal Gun series, and if you know at least a little bit, you'll know you're about to find some... suggestive stuff. But if you aren't that type of person, I'd say not to worry much, it's pretty tame.Heard that there is a sequel in the works. Here's hoping to be even better, and maybe Inti Creates, an option to disable Voice Acting? I have no issue for those who prefer to play with VA (either English or Japanese), but it would also be welcome to be able to disable them. The music in this game is very good, but... you can't listen it that much considering all the shouting and voices and stuff.Pretty much a perfect score for me. Still wish I could disable the Voice Acting, however.

_childDocuments_.review: ^ Played countless hours on PS4. The only difference to PC is that Up seems to double as an alternate Jump on PC only.It's Gal Gun characters in a pixel-art Castlevania game. It is a love letter to both those things.  Your two characters are well balanced for offensive or defensive play where you can switch between them at any time. The game is voiced in Japanese or partially in English. Great voice acting, though I do prefer the Japanese. The premise is entertaining slowly revealing little surprises along the way.The game offers a Casual difficulty which I appreciate, or a Veteran difficulty for seasoned Castlevania players. Depending on your skill level you may still find the game quite forgiving. The stages are relatively linear first time, but hint at alternate paths you might reach later on. The characters have special abilities unique to them that are super dynamic; able to combine in ways that reward experimentation and empower you while problem solving.Criticisms: Teleport destinations don't unlock until you walk through the door beyond them which, on your first playthrough, can fool you into replaying the last level fully to progress. The game only has an abstract map which appears at teleports or when entering a new stage for the first time, leaving the player to remember where they've been and what they've collected where. A difficulty higher than Veteran would be nice from the start for higher skilled players.My nitpicks are despite my opinion that this game is perfect! I love seeing new players (on Twitch for example) discover its quirks in their own unique ways and having a good time!

_childDocuments_.review: So yes, first thing's first, this game plays like old-style Castlevania but with modern gimmicks, .With that glaring issue out of the way, let's talk about the theme. The girls are obviously recurring characters from their Gal'Gun series, so if you were once invested in them, you'd definitely have fun seeing (a rather sizeable cast!) reprise their roles here. Japanese voice option is fully fleshed out, and that's where you get GGDP's quality in entertainment and voice acting. Sad to say, this is not the same for English, so I suggest that you do play in JP for the full experience, and listen to the great voice acting during dialogues. You will miss nothing at all from the EN side. NOTHING.I came in with expectations of a Gal'Gun player, not a platforming one.-PROS-There's actual replayability because the game expands itself midway. Think of it as your inverted castle moment, but with more options and places to explore now (The game cleverly positions/leads you and also "alerts" you to new paths). You even get to use your newfound abilities to the fullest once you understand in your first run that both girls are crucial to effective play.You are actually "forced" to employ both girls and their abilities effectively. The weakness of most Metroidvanias is the fact that the main character can get so strong because of equipment and levels, that good players can make 90% of any game's assets and inventory laughably useless at any time. The game makes sure that both sisters rely on each other in combat and mobility.Enemy placement can be perilous especially if you're down one sister, but otherwise the saturation is just right so that neither of the sisters get overwhelmed.-CONS-The pathfinding and navigation is where this game gets difficult, because it is linear but labyrinthine. Coupled with the vague map on the select screen, it is easy to be confused about where to go. The directions are approximate but not to size nor scale, so half the battle is guessing whether you're on the right path or not.All in all, I would absolutely recommend giving the game a go because it's actually pretty fun without taking itself too seriously. You don't need to know the characters at all to enjoy them.Lastly: Yes, unadjustable sound is an annoyance, but just go to your Volume Mixer in systray and manually adjust it to your comfort.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent game if you like classic castlevania style games. There is quite a lot of counterintuitive stuff in this game however with regards to controls. So you end up have a foothold so low, you can't even get on the other side. It's a real guessing game and you'll waste a lot of magic bumbling about with it.After getting the penguin freeze attack, i tried to open a special door and the attack went right through it. you're supposed to have the attack activate while its TOUCHING the door. Meaning you HAVE to stand a specific distance away from it.Last the purge attack, which you get when the pride gauge fills, is SUPER SLOW and DOES NOT freeze the action on screen. Meaning unless you know EXACTLY what the enemy/boss pattern is, the attack will more than likely miss. It's things like these that just make you say, "Really?" while playing the game and it happens a lot.its not a bad game. just frustrating with very little of the intuitiveness of the games its trying to emulate.

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoyed the game overall, there are some critical flaws that make me reluctant to 100% it, mainly connected to the difficulty of navigation.First, the game doesn't feature a map of any kind, which should be an essential feature of any Metroidvania. Second, navigating the levels is a pain - sometimes, thare are one-way doors, which prevent you from returning to the earlier parts of the level, forcing you to restart it. Finally, the game doesn't have an item counter of any kind, so it's imposible to tell how many items you still have to collect on a particular level - you'll have to remember that. I get it that this game was mainly inspired by earlier Castlevania titles, which didn't have any of those things... But they also didn't have a massive amount of collectibles on every level! This game encourages you to explore the levels to collect all the hidden items, but doing so is very frustrating due to the reasons I've mentioned above.Also, was it really necessary to force the player to go on a third loop through the castle just to collect everybody's panties? To me, it looks to be not only a way for the developers to scratch their kinks, but also to make the game artificially longer (it seems that the Japanese gamemakers are quite adept at both).
