_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted to play a classic Castlevania game with a buddy? Well this is it. This review will be based on the 2 Player mode of the game on Veteran difficulty, using Remote Play Together (Requires one player to be on a controller and be assigned to player 2 in Steam Remote Play.) Highly recommended to voice chat using Discord to effectively pull off some really stupid stuff that is only possible with proper teamplay.Play as Shinobu or Maya, 2 different characters with entirely different skill sets, playstyle, and sub weapons. Each character has their strengths and weaknesses and covering for the other character's shortcomings can create some really satisfying moments where you and your friend work together to go through the stages and bosses.Platform and fight your way through the stages, along with your friend. If one of you dies, the other can revive them assuming their body isn’t in a pit somewhere. Certain checkpoints can revive the other member, so don’t be too worried about losing out on the fun. Stages are linear but are filled with various alternate routes and secrets to discover and explore, giving a ton of replay value to go and hunt for them after the first playthrough. Bosses can be challenging the first time around, but their patterns are easy to learn and avoid. It’s honestly a really fun challenge, not too hard, not too easy. The game has many mechanics which make it a truly enjoyable experience, such as turning yourself into a familiar and teleporting to your friend. This allows you to catch up to them or avoid danger. Jump on each other's heads to gain that extra height to reach higher places that otherwise would be out of reach. Combine this with the various sub weapons that grant extra traversal options, there's some really interesting ways to explore the castle's many secrets.Either player character’s sub weapon arsenal are entirely unique to their characters, ranging from really versatile weapons to amazing exploration tools. For example, the grenade for Shinobu, giving her an arc projectile and a way to deal with low enemies. Or the hook shot, giving her a really useful tool to traverse the stages. Maya has a penguin that can freeze enemies (And some bosses), allowing the pair to easily dispatch tougher enemies with ease. And she has an umbrella that can be used to glide to various locations. With 6 sub weapons in total for each character, there's plenty of options and experimentation to be had. Both players share the same pool of weapon ammo, so be sure to not waste them or you’ll find yourselves unable to get certain secrets or deal with a boss easily.The story is all right, it’s entertaining enough. It doesn’t get in the way of a fun coop experience while also having enough to invest yourselves into what’s happening. If you’ve never played the Gal Gun games, a lot of characters and terms they throw around will probably confuse you, but my friend still enjoyed the story without ever having play those games. Shinobu and Maya have a really fun chemistry as the Demon Hunting siblings. Maya especially with her funny lines and cute mannerisms.Honestly, if you’re looking for a fun coop game, look no further. It’s just a fun game. In an era where coop games seem to be going extinct, this fills that void perfectly. It doesn’t have built in online coop, but remote player together worked perfectly during our playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this knowing nothing about the source material (Gal Gun) but it didn't stop me from having fun. Honestly, my only real gripes are that the game desperately needs SOME kind of map. One you can pull up with the Select button like SotN or at least a mini map or something, the little compass isn't enough to find things on its own. Also the characters voice lines are a bit too frequent. TO CLARIFY, I don't mind the voices, its just kind of annoying that every single action has a specific line and there's no cooldown. Perfect example is chaining jumps with the Grappling Hook. I'ts just YAH YAH YAH YAH YAHAYHAYAHYAHAYAHAYAH  every single button press and it starts to wear on you a bit. It's really nothing new though sadly. It's just like the Mega Man X4 memes with Zero spamming his voice lines during something like quick dashes or saber-cancels.Other than that, the story is kind of whatever. It starts off simple enough, get to the big bad (small bad?) at the top of the castle, but it gets really out there towards the end. Apparently that's what the Gal Gun games are normally like. The gameplay is solid enough that I just rolled with it. Probably my biggest takeaway playing the actual game after the demo, was finding out that the traversal sub weapons (like Grappling Hook and Umbrella) are free to use so you don't have to worry about not having access to them if you use up all of your Sub Weapon Energy.There are multiple loops, and you gain access to alternate paths after the first loop. There's a lot of backtracking as well but only if you're going for 100% and the secret ending. There are multiple difficulties, and it looks like on Casual you don't suffer knockback (I know thats a big complaint for people) I played through on Vet and am about to give Legend a try. The bosses are fun, the sub weapons get their uses though some feel a bit too OP, all in all its a pretty fun game. Plus there's a demo so you might as well try it out if you think it looks interesting. I was a big fan of CotM and this game didn't disappoint.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Inti Creates best game, and they live by a high standard. Strangely, at first I felt overwhelmed by this game, too many options maybe. This is when the game goes from cool/challenging, to excellent! The cheeky, "go collect girl's underpants" storyline is unfortunate/stupid. The game is better than its own storyline. _childDocuments_.review: Along with Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon, this game is one of my favourite games from Inti. If I were to sum up the game into one word, it would be "unique". While not a perfect game, Gal Guardians fits a unique in-between of both a Classicvania and Metroidvania mixed with inspirations from Castlevania, Mega Man, Ghosts and Goblins, and of course, anime clichés.Pros:++ Excels as a modern Classicvania, solid gameplay, allows for multiple playstyles.++ Fantastic art direction, character portraits, and spritework.+ Challenging, fair difficulty, multiple difficulties available.+ Fitting OST.+ Entertaining Boss fights.+ Boss Rush available for additional challenge and practice.+ 2 Player mode available.+ Clichés can give a good laugh to some.Cons:- Clichés can also be a turn off for some.- In-game VOs in JP or ENG can trigger too frequently.- Earlier Boss fights can be too easy on all difficulties.-- Weak Metroidvania experience, lack of backtracking convenience.In conclusion, panties.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game from Inti Creates, though one with a few issues. First, this game is NOT a metroidvania. A lot of people were disappointed because they thought they were getting something closer to SOTN, but this is a lot closer to Dracula X; more traditional levels with branching paths. This was more of a fan misunderstanding, though. As the developers never said anything about the game being a metroidvania, but people still used the metroidvania tag for the game's store page anyway (those are user generated, not the developer). If anything, I think Inti Creates should've checked the store page and tried to correct it, but they were busy making the game so, idk.With that out of the way, the game is still fantastic, with really cool bosses and enemies, fun anime characters (the game is a spin off of Gal Gun), and a pretty alright story that never takes itself seriously. My only issue with it is that the revival mechanic makes the whole game a bit too easy, since if one of the two girls dies, you can just revive her with the other one. But I really enjoyed switching between them, and using their unique abilities to find the crap-ton of secrets hidden in each level.Despite all the disappointment about the game not being a metroidvania, this is still another really solid entry from Inti Creates, and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Game's fun, I don't really know what else you'd want out of a game besides more freedom to explore. _childDocuments_.review: Magical Girls meet Old School Castlevania. Seriously that is the basis of this game. From super over the top corny anime dialogue, to magical girl transformation, to everything in old school Castlevania. This game is a ton of fun. Exploration Is rewarded, risks are risky, and gameplay feels plenty smooth. As a fan of Castlevania I was pleasantly surprised that there was no Metroid aspect to this game. A simpler, linear map, with the classic climb the tower mechanic with a neat twist at the end of each floor. Aesthetically, the music, art, and sound design really do well in this game. Everything feels in the right place. Also, the blood splatters? Super over the top but extremely satisfying. Both the English and Japanese versions of this game have good voice acting. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a Gal*Gun fan, I'm a classic Castlevania fan (Rondo of Blood is my all-time favorite), this game is a good middleground of the sensibilities of one with the gameplay of the other. It's hard to judge the whole experience based on your first time through the stages, because you kind of have to FIGHT your urge to backtrack. My advice is to wait until the game opens up a bit, and you'll enjoy the second run and level design a lot more when you have all your tools. It's not a cutting edge kind of game, but it is a lot of fun, looks and plays great, and it stands up to the quality of game that Inti Creates tend to make. 8/10, I recommend it if you like linear platformer Castlevania games. It also helps that it's a lot less frustrating than those.

_childDocuments_.review: Another banger from Inti Creates, this game is amazing through and through.For starters, the character art, sprites, and animations are all incredibly well done. The character design and voice acting is great too, and my friend and I had fun noticing some of the similarities between Shinobu's lines and Copen's lines in the Gunvolt games.Sound design is also phenomenal, but you'd come to expect that from Inti's other games. Hitting/killing enemies feels great because of it, and the music is top notch. All of the levels have a track that fits them perfectly, and it gives the game a lot of personality.Despite how good everything else is, the gameplay is definitely the highlight of the game though. The way both the co-op and single player are handled makes switching between the characters or teaming up to overcome different challenges a lot of fun, and the various abilities you unlock throughout the game feel great to use and allow for some fun alternate solutions to accessing certain areas you'd encounter throughout the game.The level design is really good, it's not hard to notice some extremely clever design choices here and there in all of them.Lastly the bossfights are great as well. They do exactly what they're supposed to by often getting you to make use of abilities you unlocked earlier in the story, and they're not too easy but also not too frustrating to do.I really hope they decide to make this a series, and that it doesn't end up being a one-off game. It does a great job of telling the story of the GalGun characters (and their connections to the Gunvolt universe) from a different perspective, and without having to play those games. They're not for everyone, obviously.All and all a 10/10. Definitely one of the best games Inti has put out.

_childDocuments_.review: Another fun and solid 2D platformer from Inticreates, and it's structured very similarly to their Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon games: a beautiful, pixel-style side-scroller through mostly linear stages with secrets and branching paths scattered around, and the ability to replay previous stages with new abilities to uncover more secrets.So far, it's also a more merciful experience compared to some of their other, similar outings; most enemies don't respawn in a level until you die, and even if you're not playing the easy mode, dying as one sister doesn't count as losing a life, so long as you reach & revive her with the other sister. It still gets hectic, especially the boss fights and other situations where you're swapping sisters & sub-weapons a lot, it just feels a bit less punishing for mistakes.All in all, I highly recommend this one. Just as a note: it's actually a spinoff of one of Inti's other series of the same acronym, and uhh, your mileage may vary wildly with the "source material". Don't let that stop you from enjoying this game, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Gal Guardians: Demon Purge

_childDocuments_.review: This game has it all: Megaman gameplay on your Castlevania motif, references to both games in the sprite work, skills and bosses, there is also some GalGun I guess. Movement is great once you get used to the floatiness and the walking speed. Gameplay is tight. You've read this already, this isn't a metroidvania in the usual sense, you have to replay stages but they're all self contained and always have a boss at the end. Every time you replay a level you can find new stuff provided you're advanced the plot enough. It's pretty good. Co-op is great. Remote play is great. There are different endings and I want to actually get the last one. Story is nonsense. Just figured out this game is the missing link between Gunvolt and GalGun, Copen is a descendant of these sisters. Some pretty stupid stuff. Wild.UPDATE: Finally got all the endings. Game could use an interactive map system, the only one you got is the one that's shown during level select. That's not good. But game was good regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: If Bloodstained: Curse of the Moon was revamped Castlevania; then Grim Guardians is a revamped Castlevania 3.The game is fun, the graphics are okay, the enemy designs are sufficient, and the boss designs are kind of nonsensical and don't really have a cohesive feel to them; but the fights themselves are alright. Slight spoilers but you play through the game normally, then you play through the game again to actually complete it. It's not bad. The controls are decent, the boss fights are decent, the sub-weapons are whatever. IMO they feel kind of weak overall so take that as you will.Shinobu is so much better than Maya is it kind of sucks The only reason you'll use Maya is for the double jump you get half-way through the game. Otherwise Shinobu is so much stronger and more versatile than Maya that you'll essentially forget Maya exists unless you need to double jump. I don't know why they made Shinobu so much better but at the end of the day Maya being useless doesn't matter.Pick this game up if you can get it on sale for like $15. It's not worth $25, so wait until a 40-50% sale to pick to pick it up unless you want to really support the devs.Bottom Line: What you can expect is essentially playing through Castlevania 3 twice, with some lame ass anime plotpoints and cringe ass dialogue thrown in. 4 hours in and it's a solid 6/10 game. **Will update tomorrow when I finish it completely.**

_childDocuments_.review:
Grim Guardians: Demon Purge centers around two demon hunters who return to their school after a mission only to find a demonic castle where it once stood.

Players control both of the demon hunting sisters in this 2D side-scrolling action game. Players must master each of the sisters' unique abilities and attributes to overcome the challenging stages with bosses awaiting their arrival. They'll also be able to find new routes through each stage using the two characters' abilities, keeping play throughs fresh.

Other features include two-player co-op with special actions, extensive difficulty options with the "Style System," unique changes on repeat plays, and most importantly the quality and challenge players have come to expect from Inti Creates titles, this time with a new gothic horror aesthetic.

name: Red Matter 2
detailed_description: Red Matter 2 is an immersive, puzzle-adventure game that will transport you to the far reaches of space in a dystopian cold war setting. Step into the shoes of Sasha, an agent awakened in a lunar base by an undercover operative and tasked with uncovering the secrets of the mysterious Red Matter. As you journey through the solar system following a trail left behind by someone from Sasha's past, you'll be challenged with mind-bending puzzles, stealth and platforming mechanics, and even intense combat sections. Explore visually stunning Volgravian bases, and experience a spine-chilling atmosphere that will keep you on the edge of your seat. About VR Gameplay: Embark on a journey of discovery and adventure as you explore a fully interactive world designed to enhance the feeling of immersion in virtual reality. Solve environmental, physics, and logic puzzles with the help of your tools, and be awestruck by the beautiful, fully physicalized environments that surround you. Use your jetpack to soar through the skies and move without limits as you traverse platforming sections, and hack into terminals to uncover secrets and clear your path. But be prepared for the unexpected, as Volgravia has taken great measures to protect the secrets you seek. Expect thrilling combat and unexpected encounters as you uncover the mysteries of this fully-realized world. Red Matter 2 is the ultimate VR adventure, and a must-play for anyone looking for a thrilling, immersive experience. About the PC version: The PC version of the game features: High-resolution textures Highest polycount mesh is always visible. No mesh lodding. Dynamic shadows Indirect Shadows Valve Index Controllers: If the game detects Valve Index Controllers being used, you will see a custom-made controller in-game.

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions 2.5 hours in. Great graphics that match the screenshots. Doesn't look downgraded for Quest at all. Very nice reflections, texture detail, and models. Very sharp visuals with MSAA on by default, no blurry TAA here. Performance is excellent using a 2080ti, running the game at a solid 90fps with 150% supersampling. Could probably drive it a bit higher if I wanted. Index support is good, with the in-game "controllers" to match. However there is no finger tracking. Sprint was set to thumbstick click by default, however I've posted a binding that changes this to right trackpad click.Smooth turn with plenty of speed adjustment. Smooth locomotion speed adjustment, head or controller forward. Optional vignetting. No graphics settings besides supersampling & dynamic shadows, but the game looks fantastic. Its a very atmospheric puzzle/adventure game. Fairly slow paced to start but I can feel the tension rising with turrets and a bit of stealth being introduced. The VR interactions are incredibly smooth and refined. Everything feels very intuitive and polished. Most items have physics too. So far theres been a good variety of puzzles and even some platforming sections with the booster pack. Soundtrack and voice acting are top notch!Look forward to playing more but so far I'm really impressed! It's like Half-Life Alyx meets Myst, in space, with a cool retro soviet theme. Beat the game in just over 7 hours. I'll add a few things;Most of the puzzles were good, a few stick out as particularly fun and 1 or 2 had me truly stumped for a while. Most felt pretty rewarding in the end, even if a bit obscure. I enjoyed the little physics puzzles and platforming sections a lot. I had one problem with inserting the battery into the rail car after you return from the mines, apparently I was putting it in upside-down. Took me about 45 minutes of trying to escape the level boundaries to realize that lol. No real bugs besides that I guess. The hacking mini-game is alright but I think it could be improved to make it more of a "puzzle" and less of "just find a random spot in 3d space". The stealth/tension with the turrets was great. The first enemies are awful and way too hard. The second drone-like enemies that get introduced later are better, however the gun play is pretty lackluster which makes the combat a weak point for this game. The bullets travel too slow and it overheats too fast. Some sections have enemies that spawn infinitely until you deactivate a control panel, that was a but frustrating too.The environments continued to impress throughout the game and had a good sense of exploration, even though its completely linear. There are TONS of things to scan and read. If you're big on lore, there seems to be a lot of it here.Also have to mention the soundtrack, it's phenomenal. Works so well with the ambience/vibe. Voice acting is excellent too. The sound design in general is pretty good but a few physics objects are missing impact sounds. Overall the audio provides a great atmosphere.The story had me really engaged throughout. The characters felt real and although the lip sync is bad the animations are good otherwise. They did a good job allowing you to build a connection with the characters which makes the story feel more significant and personal. I wont spoil the ending but it definitely gets weird and has a bit of a twist. I don't really know if a 3rd game would be... possible? But I absolutely want more Red Matter.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely the second best (half-life Alyx is the best game) VR game I have played in the last 5+ years.  Both RM1 and RM2 are fantastic, superb graphics, excellent story and game play.  I took my time and explored and the game time ended up just over 13 hours.  But the big diff is this game was developed by a very small non-AAA team while Half life Alyx was created with a large AAA dev team with unlimited budget.  The quality/game play of recently released VR games has been exceptionally poor and very disappointing to say the least.  But NOT THIS GAME, RED MATTER 2 excels in every area and is simply a great game that will keep you playing.     I played using Vive Pro 1 wireless with vive wands and had no issues with controllers or my HMD.  I am saddened that the game play for me is over now that I beat the game......i really enjoyed playing this game and can only hope that Vertical Robot will soon release another similar game........or MAYBE RM3!GREAT WORK DEVS..........this game must be selected as game of the year!

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions after completing the game in about 12 hours. Using RTX 3090, i9 10900K, 32GB, Win10 and Valve Index. (Note that the Steam version supports native Oculus drivers and works flawlessly with my great old Rift CV1 too - but I prefer Valve Index for this game.) The game is optimized for lcd hmds and now uses MSAA for antialiasing (Red Matter 1 used temporal antialiasing).  The game is a very clever Quest port, and if you don't know what to look for, it looks like a PCVR game made for a GTX 970 or close, like Red Matter 1. I started with an insane Index res 500% with the RTX 3090 - and I got nice 90 fps. I really only get such extreme performance in Quest ports - res 500% is 45 mill pixels per frame combining both eyes - nearly 50% more than 8K res, lol. But going further into the game, I could not keep 90 fps everywhere, but it was close - I ended lowering to res 400% (about 35 mill pixels) and now got solid 90 fps. I also ended up using Index res 400% for Cosmonius High, which just like Red Matter 2 is a Quest port with added dynamic shadows. So performance is same as Cosmonious High, and you do not need a fast gpu for Red Matter 2. I bet even an old GTX 1080 can do Index res 200% in Red Matter 2. You only have graphics options to set dynamic and indirect shadows on or off, so you cannot set antialiasing or other advanced options at all, only the shadows: It's normal for Quest games not to have any options for advanced graphics settings - and you really don't have many in this Quest port. Quest and PCVR versions have the same amount of objects, so you'll see no more objects (and furniture etc.) in a location or scene that the ultra-low-end XR2 SoC can handle. But Red Matter 1 was kinda an empty game like Myst - so not a bad choice with limited processing capabilities. The PCVR version has up to 16 times higher texture res than the Quest 2 version (1024 res vs 4096) res - and hands do look nice:- but Red Matter 1 does look awesome too - maybe even better?Devs also remade Index controllers inside the game - but no finger tracking. Devs even gave Index users the trackpad - pretty awesome:The right trackpad is used to cool down your gun, but the left trackpad is not used. Would be nice using the left trackpad to bring up the game menu?The game has some sort of barren feeling to it - like the interior of some space shuttle pods with very limited surface complexity - and I do suspect that's due to Quest 2 processing limitations. Another example, the rings of Saturn look nice - in Lone Echo 1-2 you did get many 3D rocks and debris, here in Red Matter 2 the rings look like a moving 2D pattern - but it looks fine and is high-res, I suspect this is one method devs used to reduce the poly levels for Quest 2.It also looks like the devs removed the awesome HDR-like lighting seen in Red Matter 1 - these 3 images are from Red Matter 1 showing the light:But there's no bloom, radiance nor anything special about the light in Red Matter 2:Feels like a big step backwards for the lighting. Does explain why I can run Red Matter 2 using an insane Index res 400% in solid 90 fps with the RTX 3090, while I had trouble getting much above res 200 - 250% in Red Matter. I'd so much love to get proper lighting back! Or just a setting to enable proper lighting.Still, being designed for a phone gpu (Quest 2 uses Adreno 650 gpu made for phones, part of the XR2 SoC), Red Matter 2 definitely is the best Quest port so far - but if this game was properly designed for current PCVR rigs, surely it could have been so extremely much more. That said, dynamic and indirect shadows do look great in the game, when they work. The Quest version has no dynamic or indirect shadows. The shadows are limited to certain objects though. Compared to Red Matter, which is a real PCVR game, your arms and hands do not cast shadows in Red Matter 2. And some surfaces don't work with shadows, and this may break immersion - never had that problem with the awesome shadows in Red Matter 1 - clearly showing the Quest origin of Red Matter 2. More info here:In spite of all the cons, I'm still going to rate the game 80 % (and Red Matter 92 %). I just finished Red Matter, and while Red Matter 2 looks fine, I'm not that impressed with the story and puzzles. The atmosphere in Red Matter felt much darker and more foreboding, while Red Matter 2 feels lighter. In the first half of the game, puzzles seem to require less IQ and some are repeated (felt close to a walking simulator), while several puzzles in Red Matter were difficult to solve. Feels like Red Matter 2 generally is more casual and easygoing than Red Matter 1, but Red Matter 2 does have some challenging puzzles during the last half of the game. Red Matter 2 also adds action sequences and no longer is a strict adventure game like Red Matter 1. The shooting feels like a chore and is mediocre at best, devs seem inexperienced with shooters and should have kept to adventure content. The reason for my 80 % rating has to do with the great voyage this game represents - the game will show you many different worlds and far more environments than Red Matter. On my Index box Valve wrote "Hello Worlds" - and these words kinda summarizes the journey in Red Matter 2 - even with some shortcomings.In short, I have no problem recommending the game, especially if you like Red Matter 1. If you have not finished Red Matter 1 then I recommend starting with that game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game restored my faith in PCVR.  Beautiful graphics that never dip from 144 fps with a 3080 on high settings, great voice acting, the physics engine is on point, writing is better-than-serviceable, I could go on.  I slept on the first Red Matter but saw enough Alyx comparisons in the reviews that I had to check it out and it absolutely lives up to it.  The PCVR scene needs more high quality games like this and this is an absolute steal at $29.99.  If you a) complain about a lack of decent new VR titles while b) sleeping on this game then you c) are probably are wearing clown make-up and large red shoes with big floppy yellow laces.  Amazing work Vertical Robot, I'll buy everything you ever make.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the sequel I was hoping for.  Firstly the atmosphere is ruined by the voiced protagonist and constant banter with Beta.  Weirdly enough you even see her in a hologram as the introduction to the game never to see her face again (why put all that effort and budget into that?).  Red Matter had a tangible loneliness which contributed to the atmosphere.  Here I feel like I'm being led around a kids themepark.  Beta constantly explains obvious plot points I already pieced together or could of done some scanning to figure out.  This game makes me feel stupid due to over-explaining everything.  The puzzles aren't even puzzles as the game gives you the solutions to everything right in your face.  Diagrams tell you exactly where to put things and scanning screens tells you exactly what you're looking for.In the first game there was a little bit of a sidekick voice over but they barely had dialogue.  Beta here is telling me things I already know every 2 minutes.  I walk into a new space and she tells me to solve the puzzle.  Gee what would I have done without her.The second main issue is the number of locations has expanded but as far as I can tell the game is still linear.  Red Matter had better atmosphere because it took place in a single location where you pieced together the plot yourself by exploring every inch of it.  Here Beta tells you everything while the environment plays at best a supporting role in story telling.  Due to the increase in scope each environment has less details to tell a story.Everything feels dumbed down.  I didn't get to the shooting but when I saw that in the trailer it wasn't something that excited me.  I wanted to explore a detailed lived in environment and piece together a story myself.  Instead I get my hand held everywhere and "puzzles" that solve themselves.  Judging from the reception so far on youtube and metacritic I'm just not the target audience here.  The audience is for Quest 2 owners looking for PC level graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial Impressions: Eye Candy Visuals that I wasn't expecting and ... wow!! They are good !!Interesting mechanics, you have 2 robotic claw hands that can pull objects similar to Alyx controls, and also keep objects on your wrists. You can pull out a very fast and practical screen with a laser that provides info on ANYTHING that it touches, and you have also a connector to use on specific spots. As a bonus you have a small/slow jet-pack that I love it how it is being used, I think is one of my favorite features and the locations that I used it were amazing.The game seems to be a smart story driven adventure. With mix of exploration and smart puzzles based on gathering parts around and understanding how activate or fix different retro sci-fi devices, while uncovering the main story.It has movement choices, also they have additional blinders to avoid sickness if needed (in my case I'm immune and I disable everything). Additionally the options allow the player to set the movement speed (!), so I guess this could also work if someone wants to practice with slow movements too.It is very early to give a detailed review but so far I like the game because of how it looks, how good it plays and how smart is .I will expand the review when I get more advanced in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: I am conflicted with Red Matter 2. Although the puzzles are more ingenious than Red Matter 1, where I was only stumped on a safe code. These puzzles are much more unique with the VR software. I also loved the improved movements and large scale of the game, and the fleshed out lore/story.However, there are some mini-games that seem pointless, the hacking mini-game had no skill. The combat was a welcome element, it soon overstayed its welcome. And became frustrating at the end where you had to fight through a horde with no save points. I also rage quit after I got soft locked during the reactor pipe platforming puzzle. Where I would respawn on the side of the pipe causing me to fall continuously. After reloading an auto save, the mini blimp got stuck on a shelving unit out of sight, causing me to reload another save.Red Matter 1 I can introduce VR to new people, but the difficulty of Red Matter 2 combat makes it so I can't use it to show off a fun puzzle game with an interesting story. If you are an experience VR user, then go for it. But I can only give this a thumbs up for the increased quality and wonderful story. But I can't really give it a glowing review either.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Only about an hour in but I can tell you already that the devs know exactly what they're doing and know what a vr game is supposed to be like. If half life alyx and lone echo had a baby..this would be it. If you liked red matter 1..then I would absolutely pick this game up. Only downside is For people new to the series that hate reading..you'll have to scan items and read text..also a little slower pace but those two issues are nothing and would be such a shame to skip for those reasons. If you're a shooter only player then I wouldn't recommend. For everyone else ..it should be a definite buy. Highly recommend!edit: Not sure why Index users are saying there's no picture or audio. I'm using the Index and everything is working just fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoted the first game then the second is essential, its better than the first in every way. Longer at 7 hours for me to finish it, better movement with options to increase movement speed and the jetpack is now built into the gameplay rather than being a different kind of teleportation.You have to use the jetpack to clear gaps and latter have to use it to do some platforming to get around the enviroment. You get a gun which add some variety to the gameplay. The puzzles are very well done with a focus on interactitivity and its very well paced with some stunning scenery.Its one of the best looking VR games out and you get to go to different locations with a much bigger scale and I found my self stopping to soak in the details and atmosphere alot.Overall its one of the best VR game available and my new favourite VR puzzler with Shadow Point and The Room VR close behind it.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Red Matter 1 was one of the first VR games to blow my mind, and the sequel doesn't disappoint. My only complaint is the combat: I'm a huge fan of VR shooters, but RD2 has the worst gunplay I've ever enountered. I wish they'd stuck a liiiittle closer to their roots as a puzzle game and hadn't tried to veer into action territory.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's overall, a better game that the first Red Matter. The environment is larger, the graphics are better, and the physics has improved too. It's a longer game too.  But, the puzzles in the first game were better. This game retained almost nothing on that front; no complex machines you have to figure out.  The game is more action oriented however: you get a gun, and you'll have 2 type of attack drones and turrets to shoot through the game. No diversity in enemy types, and quite basic/rudimentary gun play.  They also introduced some elements of a platformer with a new mobility suit but. Overall,  it's a significantly better game, but I still miss some of the puzzle elements the first game had.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely great and atmospheric story-driven exploration game with soviet vibes, light puzzles and incredible visuals and controlsPros:Incredible graphics and atmosphereAmazing environmentStrong and impressive story line with references to Red MatterNew mechanics and improved controlsGreat dialogues and puzzlesCons:Acceptable, but messy shooting/combat mechanicsNo way to enable smooth teleport with thrusters like in Red MatterA bit simplified lightning effectsRating: 4.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Red Matter 2 sets a new bar for VR mystery/suspense/story based games. I've thought about reaching out to the developer and thanking them it's that good. If you're a space lover like me, DON'T MISS THIS! Some very memorable moments in this, and the graphics are even better than Alyx sometimes. The music also is well done. Just enough to give you some atmosphere, but not overdone. If you also played the original this is worth getting for a continuation of the original story too. Very little is re-hashed so you've got to pay some attention to succeed. This also gets fairly creepy, more than the original, so if you're averse to horror games, this may not be for you. All in all, as I just finished this days ago, I'm still fairly blown away at how good it was. The developer has really found their niche. Still getting chills from the ending of this.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: No spoil.  Nice adventure, no motion sickness. lot of rooms to explore and game is 7h30 to finish all. success included. You have to see if you want to spend 30 euros for 7h30 of good game. You can do the game only once and after you know all. I hope they will do a 3rd one because i enjoyed redmatter 1 and 2. (Perfect play on quest 3 + 4080)
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Much like the first game I thought that this was amazing.  A great use of VR mechanics, a creepy story that'll keep you immersed in the game, and stunning scenery!  If you haven't played the first game I would recommend trying that first to add to the overall story and setting.  The puzzles are not all easy but not difficult to the point you want to hit your head off the wall and it's not as short as the first title but still under 10 hours depending on how much you explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: The story, puzzles, atmosphere and charm in this game are really good. It’s like a Mass Effect/Bioshock type of atmosphere, with a lot of really good puzzles and a small amount of combat and navigating. I can’t express enough, how fun- and hard, but in a good way- the puzzles are. They’re very creative and challenging but rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: "Polished" doesn't begin to do this game justiceThis is a peak AAA VR game right here, like Half Life: Alyx or Asgard's Wrath in terms of brand new and exciting interactions and effects.The puzzles are some of the best for this kind of game. Sometimes I would think "Damn! The game has soft-locked me here!" only to discover some ingenious solution minutes later.As with a lot of these games, it has to give bits of exposition via reading notes that are scattered around. This is a mechanic that I think most people will agree, should have died out in the 2000s. But for me, the mark of whether a developer has done it well or not, depends on whether the player is inspired to read all that fluff.Here, the writing is perfect. Exactly the right tone for the game and not too text heavy, so reading never feels like a chore. It always feels like you're looking for some crucial clue.The effects...brother...I've played a LOT of games, like, you have no idea, but here the game has shown me things that I couldn't have imagined possible on current technology.The animations, textures, liquid and particle effects are absolutely sublime and will stop you dead in your tracks every time just to gaze in awe at what is happening.I won't spoil anything, but there's a bit where you 'get' a 'thing' in the MOST ambitious and impressive way that I've ever seen a 'thing' like that 'got' in a game.You'll know when it happens.Great story, although a couple of the beats were painfully predictable. The use of environmental storytelling however, especially surrounding Irina and Stas' relationship actually made my heart ache at how well it conveyed the situation. It makes you CARE about characters that you may never actually meet.THAT is good story telling.  When a triple A VR game like this exists, it feels like an incredible labour of love. You can feel it in every detail.For balance, I think I'd have to say that 'back tracking' in games is never popular, but even here RM2 manages to alter paths so that going back through a section to solve a puzzle might present new challenges.Those hackneyed, semi-predictable story beats could have also used some work, as the horror of a situation hits much harder when you didn't see it coming two acts ago, i.e.: "Would you kindly?"Speaking of the devil; this did hit me as the closest thing we will ever get to a VR Bioshock game.TL:DR If you like games, get it. If you like innovation in VR, get it. This is a 10/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the better VR games I've played. It runs well even at very high-resolutions, has a decent story and good voice-acting, along with some very enjoyable gameplay. Note that it is extremely blurry out-of-the box, and you will definitely want to fix this: It is really the only negative for RM2; that the devs have applied an incredibly heavy amount of what I can only assume must be TAA, which blurs out all of the detail in the textures. I had to install Reshade and blast a massive amount of CAS into the title, and then it looked excellent. The textures actually have plenty of detail, you'll just never see it unless you sharpen the heck out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: a nice game at first, but at what i guess is half way through they switch to "red(matter)neck mode" and you suddenly have to shoot everything. very disappointing, i really liked red matter 1 and the first half of this game for their slow pace giving me time to think or just enjoy the scenery.being shot at makes me take off the headset and do something fun instead. i was under the impression that no jump scares, no shooting is a brand feature of red matter, i guess i was wrong :(update: thanks for the comment, VerticalRobot, i appreciate it. I do have the combat difficulty set to 'easy' - not 'normal', which are the only two modes. may i suggest a difficulty level 'story', where, much like in other games, e.g. mass effect, you still engage in combat, but don't take actual harm?also, my concern is not just with the difficulty of the bot encounters, it's the new game mechanic that suddenly i have to shoot everything to see if that's the solution. i mean, the first puzzle i did not figure out in all of red matter 1 & 2 and had to look up the solution for was the one where i had to shoot a button through a window right after i got the gun. it was too absurd for me shoot a button. now i'm shooting at gas fires and suddenly a crank i was trying to get to hovers in front of me and i don't even ask how it works anymore, i just shoot at stuff.update 2: i pushed through the parts with the nasty drones and continued playing because i was so addicted to the story. it's worth it. changed to a recommend - "pro" (lol) tip: do not use teleportation when in these drone fights, use the direct controls to get into and out of cover quickly. might update again if the shooting is getting too much (not finished yet)
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: 1) This game is a massive step up from Red Matter 1, in all areas (especially moving around).2) Go play Red Matter 1 anyway. It's short and still good. And it sets up the story for this game nicely. You'll burn through it, and then get excited for how much better this game is.+ Beautiful visuals+ Voice acting and music is overall A++ Fun puzzle mechanics+ Good story+ Jet pack- Also a bit short, but twice as long as the first title.- Linear, and strong lack of any side content whatsoever
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Review taken from my video. You can watch the video here : An alternate universe, cold war, espionage, puzzle space adventure. Even with a tagline like that it’s still difficult to truly grasp just how much Vertical Robot put into Red Matter 2. What makes it so difficult is that Red Matter 2 can stand shoulder to shoulder with the greats of VR like Half Life: Alyx, Boneworks and Lone Echo.I described Red Matter 1 as a space themed escape room that had a strong story, but was let down by its voice acting and anti-climatic ending.However in Red matter 2, any criticism I had of the first game was improved upon. Even things that I didn’t think needed criticism were improved. Voice acting was phenomenal, with the addition of a voiced player character. New puzzles were a blast and the addition of combat was a perfect choice for this adventure-puzzle game.Firstly, the visuals. My goodness they are great! You travel from The Moon to Saturn and later to Neptune, stopping at space bases hidden in moons and asteroids. Every time the scene opens up at the next location I was in awe of the absolutely stunning vista in front of me. The moons, the planets and their rings of dust and ice, the great abyss of space and its sparkling stars and galaxies - all of it was gob smackingly awesome to see. And then there were the interiors of the bases, the brutalist structures for the faux Russians and Sleek retro futurism for the faux Americans that just works so well. On top of that quest items and objects you have to interact with are large and obvious. Which is exactly what you want for an adventure-puzzle game that exists in large spaces.Speaking of the large spaces, the movement controls were improved. Smooth Locomotion is the primary method of movement but Teleport Locomotion can be selected in the settings. All the comfort settings you’d expect for VR are available in the settings, as such I’m certain everyone regardless of how strong their VR legs are, will be able to enjoy playing the game. Controls were great and I didn’t have any issues interacting with the world or my tools. If you’re using the Vive wands though you will have issues doing one and only action in the game, which is to vent your gun when it overheats, but it doesn’t get in the way of the game. Thankfully other controllers like the index or quest controllers won’t have this issue.And playing the game is a great joy indeed. Puzzles were improved upon from the first game with the addition of many new ones, some of them include piloting a small, remote controlled blimp. In any flat screen game this would have been a pain, but with the added dimension from VR it actually is a lot of fun. Having the Eureka moment for puzzles never got old as each puzzle was its own beast to tackle and some puzzles are beasts. There were some puzzles that were truly tricky but I loved every single one of them.And loving the game was an easy thing to do. Characters in the game are written well and it was easy to put yourself in the boots of the protagonist Agent Sasha. Interactions with other characters are mostly through radio communications, however at two points in the game you talk to floating heads, which are just projections thankfully, but they sit smack in the middle of the uncanny valley effect. They look great but the faces emote like robots and the lip sync is off especially with any word having the letter ‘p’ in it. Thankfully the floating faces are used at the start of the game to catch players up in the story.The biggest addition however is combat. Vertical Robot has added a gun in the form of a retro futurism laser pistol which is as cool as it sounds. It’s also a handy tool and I was using it to shoot buttons to open doors from afar. In some cases it's also the solution to puzzles. Though the shoot to solve puzzles tended to be much simpler than the other challenges in the game.The combat against actual enemies however, was really difficult and I found myself dying a lot to them. Enemies dodge constantly as you aim at them and later enemies are not shy to charge you down if you hide yourself behind cover. I felt that the projectile speed for the player was a little low in comparison to how fast the enemies can move, but I have it on great authority that Vertical Robot will tweak combat for the release version of the game.The story for this epic adventure game is a great story. I found myself 100% engrossed in the world and was finding and reading every bit of lore that I could find just so that I could grasp more of its story. Some sections of the game were terrifying as there is a long running theme of Cosmic Horror in the game. Coupling that with a world ending device means that our agent has actual agency in the game and reason to solve these puzzles. However at times the story could be a bit predictable but nonetheless still thoroughly enjoyable.If you’ve been waiting for another VR great, or have been itching to show off a VR game to your friends, family and internet dwellers that will wow them, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Currently 4.5 hours in. A really solid game TBH. I played Red Matter 1 a few months ago and refunded it cause, while it looked good, I didn't really enjoy it. But Red Matter 2 is really solid so far.Imagine Half Life: Alyx but just a lot more puzzles and less shooting in a Half Life 1 kinda vibe/setting. There's still shooting, but a lot less of it (at least so far). I kinda wanted more shooting but the puzzles are actually pretty fun to solve. That's kinda important since almost the entire game (so far) is solving puzzles and platforming. The puzzles aren't just fun to solve, but also (not to spoil to much) are cool to watch and do.Other things:Really cool set pieces. Good graphics. In game you hold devices that look like your controllers. It sounds kinda stupid, but actually immerses you into the game even more because it looks AND feels like you're holding the device. If you only care about blasting, this game probably isn't for you. But if you're down for really good puzzles with some shooting on the side then go for it. I was not disappointed.Also someone rated this game down because the protagonist has a voice??? I like half life too bro but stop being such a nerd.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the original Red Matter then you're certainly in for a treat with Red Matter 2.  It is better in every way to the original title.I loved exploring the environments and enjoyed the puzzles.  There is nothing here that requires a walkthrough.  All the puzzles are intuitive and relatively simple.  The combat scenarios towards the end of the game are welcome and fun.The presentation is top notch and the game ran super smooth for me on my system.Wonderful atmosphere and setting - Satisfying controls and mechanics - great story - lovely presentation.  Highly recommended!!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first one plays like a demo. A good experince, but short and feature lacking. The second installation is way more mature. It has around 8 hours of gameplay, good puzzles, excellent graphics and a good story. One of the best VR experiences so far. So, if you missed this one - I highly recommend giving it a chance
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I pirated the game on Quest and finished it there but I liked it SO MUCH that I felt bad about stealing from the developers with such a tremendous job they did in each and every one of its sections that I ended up buying it on steam. Excellent graphics, excellent puzzles, excellent physics, excellent story, excellent everything. Don't hesitate twice and buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR games to date. It's an incredibly slow and methodical exploration puzzler that makes you feel involved in the environments. The devs understood what makes VR special, and that is an emphasis on physics based interactions that sell the world for high-class immersion. Combat sections are far and few in-between, don't go in expecting amazing combat set pieces as that is not the game's goal. The minimal combat is only there to service the puzzle solving and gives you an extra obstacle to manage when solving puzzles. My only complaint would be that while the overall story was fantastic, the writing is sometimes just hilariously bad. Some lines of dialogue are the most generic, tropey nonsense that can sometime take you out of the experience for a second. Nothing too terrible but definitely worth mentioning.Overall I would give this game a solid 8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Overall an enjoyable sequel which has a bit more of an action-adventure bent than precursor with some new ways to interact and traverse. The shooting of the "dispensed" defense drones got a bit too much though. Favorite parts were some of the planetary vistas especially when landing on Neptune's moon. The score was also quite nice and had a certain John Williams/Star Wars-y vibe. If there is a Red Matter 3 at some point, I hope there will be a bigger focus on more space-goodness/exploration of alien vistas.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Played and enjoyed the first one and Red Matter 2 improves on every aspect of the first one. It looks gorgeous in VR, fun but not too challenging puzzles, and an interesting story. If you like a story driven puzzle game this should be in your VR library. It's set in space and in a space station so the environment is very enjoyable to play. It has some mystery to the story as well which is very nice. Haven't completed it yet but I can't wait to do so. I just wish you could walk faster, I have very strong "VR legs" and even at max speed I find it a bit slow.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Red Matter 2 is a crowning achievement in the VR gaming landscape, setting an incredibly high bar for immersive storytelling and visual splendor! The environments are masterfully crafted with a lot of attention to details. The storyline is another area where Red Matter 2 excels remarkably. It weaves a narrative that is both intelligent, mysterious, suspenseful and emotional. Its a fulfilling journey to be had!And lastly, Red Matter 2 has cleverly designed puzzles that are seamlessly integrated into the narrative and progression of the story!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: This was a good sequel. It was the first game I was looking forward to playing on the Quest 3, and it didn't disappoint.My one complaint is that the shooting mechanics weren't good, or rather they weren't accurate, even if you aimed properly. But this is a small issue with a game that is otherwise great.If you have played the original, then you are not going to find the puzzles in this one too different, but they offer enough of a challenge that it is still entertaining.The story seems more coherent than the first game, but both lean on your ability to connect the dots in your mind and find the little bits and pieces that add to the narrative throughout the game.Visually this is so stunning, I found myself jumping to death on purpose at times just to get better looks at some of the planets.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with very fun vr control ideas that actually work. There is a lot to interact and play around with in your evironment. No 'vr wonkiness', everything is solid here. Awesome puzzle design and a nice blend of gameplay elements altogether. More than once I felt like 'Now I am stuck for real', however, in the end I could figure everything out without cheating, so for me the difficulty level was just right. Like in the first game the outdoor locations were my favourites, I wish there would have been a bit more of them. The story is not mindblowing but enough to keep you invested, the ending is quite 'rewarding' :) Amazing this beautiful game was created by such a small team. I am very much looking forward to their next project.'Running' does not work out of the box on WMR headsets which does make the game harder during enemy encounters. As this is known for almost a month now it should get patched asap. Fortunately, it's not gamebreaking, and the normal walking speed is fitting for the exploration parts.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like the first Red Matter game because I enjoyed the puzzle elements, but I couldn't bring myself to play it all the way through because of the frustrating teleport controls. This game has full locomotion and is much more enjoyable because of it. Gameplay is similar to Half Life: Alyx but with more emphasis on puzzle solving and less on combat, although there are combat elements as well. I haven't been playing super long as of writing this, but I would already recommend it based on my experience so far. Puzzles vary in difficulty but most are challenging but not impossible to figure out.  Controls are smooth and easy to understand.  The graphics and environment look great and the voice acting is pretty decent as well.  If you are a fan of puzzle solving games definitely try this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Red Matter 2 is a puzzle adventure game set in an alternative reality Cold War scenario, where humanity has conquered the stars and created outposts all over the solar system. Somewhere out there, proud Volgravia found something, an alien substance, the “Red Matter”. As the player you visit several stations across the solar system in search for a long-lost friend while unraveling the secrets of the Volgravian Research Program. The game is strictly linear. There is only one way, not only through the entire game, but also to puzzle solutions. Puzzles are pretty easy and straight forward for the most part but I found them to be well-designed. There are stealth and combat sections that are pretty simple in scope, but manage to diversify gameplay enough to keep the experience engaging.Red Matter 2 has an incredible art style, it is stunningly beautiful at times. The game was designed to run on the Quest 2, and though the PC version has some advantages like dynamic shadows and higher resolution textures, it is still visible from time to time that they had to make some compromises to make it work on the Quest. The payoff for PC players is a very solid performance even on lower spec hardware. It took me about 7 hours to complete Red Matter 2. For a smaller indie studio the amount of content this game offers is pretty good. This is definitely one of the biggest VR puzzle games on the market to this day. Compared to the first part, every aspect of the game has improved, including writing, visuals, gameplay, mechanics, locomotion, voice acting and the general scope of the game, offering about three times the content. _childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Story wise a similar affair as with the previous game but to be honest felt like a repeat. Audio is good. Graphics nice to look at but just as in the movies nice fx/pictures are no longer special. But still there are some stunning vista's look at. What is a bit cheap is the trick to close blinders in rockets after liftoff to hide the immersion of travelling and then when "arriving" the open an voila some new planet.. a nice view but a bit old as a presentation trick.Controls are kind of ok for index VR, but to be honest the constant need to swap and watch the slow animation becomes irritating very soon. Also the text messages decode is sooooooo tedious-slow, like looking at a first generation fax machine.. Then I have set the walking speed to the fastest and still it feels like moving in mud. The jump/trusters have been made stupidly short (I know its a game but if this was reality the total amount that you could use in one trust the engineer who made this would be replaced.) So doesn't make sense in this story universeBut then we reach where it all falls apart.. The shooting.. this weak ass/stupid Star trek NG blaster type that take 5 seconds for a shot to travel across a room and then in the middle of the shooting you have to cool down your gun.. Because of the slow blast travel you end up guessing instead of aiming to shoot. Short verdict on shooting implementation=fail.Verdict, A flawed sequel to a masterful first game.--------------Reworked review 29-08 after the released fixes.So the gun is fixed, apart from this cooling down mech as this is still a cheap way to balance. The games still looks good and sound fine. text decoding of messages is still tedious and actually doesn't make any sense that people would leave paper cards with a question and others cards with answers.. So still believe an actual diary function (voiced or not) would work better. story wise still the same (game 1 redux so you can see the twist a mile away) so the 1st game still wins.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: A stunning follow-up to the original. Amazing attention to detail with great optimisation, good storyline and awesome visuals, sound and music. I like the addition of new game mechanics and tool. New enemies and an awesome jetpack. If you are new to the Red Matter series, they are basically a series of high-quality adventure escape room games. You move from environment to environment. Getting stuck in each section until you solve the puzzles and problems in each area. It is definitely a whole lot more fun than it sounds. I know people say this is a 5 to 6 hour game, but I'm 8 hours in and believe there is about 1 to 1.5 hrs left to go. So it's not as short as they say. I only go stuck once enough to need YT, so its the right level of difficulty, but not too taxing. This game is highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Played on a Reverb G2 with Valve Index controllers. RTX3080 + i7-9700kIt's hard to review this game because frankly speaking PC VR community rarely gets any treats that the Quest 2 community does. So it's understandable that the devs try to focus on Quest first, and PC second. So I'm grateful to them for the fact that we at least get a PC version from day 1.Having said that, for 30$ it's a banger of a game. This is my first RM game, so I'm not familiar with the plot and the universe. But the game reminded me heavily of Lone Echo series. In terms of the interactions and mechanics, the games feels like a mix between LE and HF: Alyx, even though the game truly never reaches both of those games' level of polish and fluidity. Performance-wise, I found it to be hit or miss. Some environments are very fluid, while others seem to be stuttering for no reason. Hopefully it's on the devs radar.In terms of bugs and improvements, I noticed that although Index controllers are physically present in the game, there's no finger tracking. Also, the haptics seem very weak. The collisions between your hands and the environment sometimes are inconsistent. Finally, why is there no body? It's very strange because the arms are visible, but the body is not. One bug I found is that if you open SteamVR menu while in between the environments (where the pink scanner scans you) - it will freeze the game and you'll have to restart.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: A fun sequel to the very good Red Matter. I played that one on PSVR so the upgrade in visuals here was very nice. I enjoyed the story, found the VR puzzles to be enjoyable and control well. The combat isn't great, but put it on easy and just get passed that part. Great VR experience overall and worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning! I love all the design work and the places the game takes you. The most polished environmental VR I've experienced yet, and by such a small team! Truly impressive work, I enjoyed the story and mechanics too. Saw some earlier issues posted about the Index but I didn't experience any on mine so it's all patched up. Puzzles were hard enough to make you think but not too hard I had to google. Only looked up a clue for one because I was overthinking it.It was a nice tie in to the first one but I wouldn't say playing the first is mandatory if you just want to skip to this one. But I also enjoyed the first one a lot too!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Pros Amazing immersive graphics High environmental interactivityNicely optimizedLenghty campaign { took me 10 hours to beat on my first run} these type of games are normally < 5 hours long ,so this on in particular having a run time of about 10 hours is amazingPuzzles are neither too easy nor are they too hard ,so well balanced difficulty-wiseConsLiterally l haven't found anything that l can consider to be a flaw
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Red Matter 2 fits into the long standing sci fi tradition of "alone in derelict environments while piecing together a story from audio transmissions, logs and recordings." Aside from that it is most definitely an adventure game with plenty of searching for items and solving puzzles, albeit with some action FPS sequences introduced later in the game.Pros:-Excellent use of haptic feedback and motion to simulate collisions, objects scraping, and exertion when lifting. This is one of the rare VR games I've played where it feels like objects have bulk and weight.-Some clever graphical tradeoffs in terms of environments: the rooms are often sparsely populated, but what's there is high resolution and many objects can be held right up to your face to see the details-Great atmosphere, and classic 80s sci fi orchestral soundtrack references-Some interesting puzzles especially later in the game-Decent length for a VR game (5-6 hours)-Minimal tutorials (I consider this a pro though perhaps not everyone would) which never break the immersion Cons:-I ran into one bug late in the game: one of the tools vanished from the menu/controller. Fortunately exiting and reopening from the last save fixed the issue.-There were some parts of the game where I found the puzzles far easier than finding the componentsIf you like the idea of an adventure game where you comb through atmospheric retro sci fi environments across the solar system and attempt to figure out a mystery, this might suit you.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: The only thing better about Red Matter 2 over the first game is the locomotion system.Oh, and now we have a gun with the accuracy of a home made potato launcher.The puzzles feel more like hidden object games. I am not sure where the physics description comes from in some of the pre release video reviews.I am just not feeling it like i was with the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I got total The Dig feels from this game, it has some brilliant scenery, gorgeous design, great atmospheric music, challenging puzzles, and even gets some action in there, believe it or not. Story is not too bad either!Highly recommended if you like adventure games in VR. My only tip, don't look down on books. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: More of the same from the first game, but that's not a bad thing. There is very little challenge involved, the puzzles are all very easy and the combat is simply serviceable, but it's all about the 'immersive experience' and that's where it excels. I thoroughly enjoyed it, as I did the first game, and I think the low price is enough for me to recommend it to any VR gamers out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: What an awesome game, graphics really surprised me with how good they are, and the physics are amazing also. The dev studio that made this is really becoming something, this is a top quality game the whole way through. I only wish it was a bit longer but I'll take the 8 hours of top quality over a longer game with less. Definitely recommend this. Cant wait to see what this studio comes out with next.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions: even better than the first one! I spent a good ten minutes just looking out the windows of the space station because the views were incredible. There's some obvious inspiration (and that's a good thing!) from Half-Life: Alyx in the hacking and circuit puzzles, as well as the gravity glove-like mechanics for grabbing things. The story is pretty intriguing so far and I can't wait to see where it goes. Stay tuned for the full review :)
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning scenery. a good story and relatively easily solvable puzzles (compared to some others) Some of the landscapes, such as the Saturn station are just amazing and I wish there was a way to load the game at a specific locations once finished.It's a great sequel to the original - and well worth a play through.  As others have mentioned, the combat is a little contrived but it is good fun and fits in well with the underlying tone of the rest of the janky Volgravian hardware :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Red Matter was brilliant and I thought this game would be at least good. (review for Red Matter The graphics is stunning, music is good, controls are great (better than in the first game), story is still good. The game is very well optimized for Quest. But unfortunately all this doesn't make the game good as the game play is bad or rather nonexistant. There are 'puzzles' but it is more of find object  and B and put them together or go fetch another object somehow while the instructions are there right in front of you. There are 'puzzles' that repeat that I did not even understand, like what is their purpose? While Half-Life: Alyx had either memorization or reflexes this game has pure luck (the game tried to implement a lot of things from Alyx). To even slow the walk through the game more they introduced combat. You get to shoot out of a weapon that has zero aim. I will just blame Index controller and wrong offset but I can shoot straight if the gun fits but this is not the case. The best is just walk to the drone and shoot and duck or move to the side since the projectiles or um energy shots are slow. The awesome lighting effects from Red Matter are gone. I loved those where are they now? (sad). Throughout the game you communicate with Beta who just tells you obvious things all the time and you are also forced to do things you'd certainly not do as any sane human being. The voice acting is bad and I just couldn't hear the voice anymore near the end of the game. Hearing the protagonist's voice did not help things much. This is something that is really bad in VR games. Too upset to write a proper review (later I will write it), but I am definitely not recommending this game to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: 3/5 OKSame as Red Matter 1 worth buying on sale just for the views.Gameplay and story are not great but not awful. I completed it in 4 hours and was not trying to speedrun it. 22/24 achievements, and the 2 missed would have taken 10 more seconds if I understood what to do at the time. In Red Matter 1 at the end of the game you are at least rewarded by one of the best and most atmospheric sci-fi locations in VR, but here all the views are in the first half. The second half is in the tunnels.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks awesome and has nice input mechanics that are build into the world.The story of the first game continues quite well. Some story elements are added a little bit lazy but I didn't mind.The game mechanics and riddles work well, some are quite obvious and none is really hard. But the game adds two elements that can be challenging: The first one being the shooting sections. They aren't unfair or anything like that but you have to be careful. And the next one is the height. You can float for a bit and there are sections where you have to cross gaps. If you are afraid of heights those can be quite challenging.But all in all Red Matter 2 is an awesome game I can recommend to anyone who likes riddles, story and some action sections.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: OK I am a VR veteran, I've played HL:Alyx more than 10 times now and pretty much every other top game out there I own a Cosmos Elite, Vive Pro, OG Vive, all with gear vr lens mods. My PC specs are i5 12600k, rtx ftw3 3090, 32gb 3600mhz ram.This gave me goosebumps the first hour of playing like Alyx did when I first played and that's saying alot. I've been waiting for this since playing the first one over 10 times already, and I've been waiting for another AAA feeling game comparable to Alyx and Lone Echo 1-2, and Stormland along with a few more and here it is thank the Lord!!!!The best part is not having to use an Oculus or meta headset anymore, the graphics and clarity on my cosmos elite with lens mod and the 3090 make this as clean as it gets, it is a night and day difference from the rift s and the quest2 that i just got rid of.The soundtrack is perfect and huge, it makes the whole experience so immersive that you are lost to it and that is the whole meaning of a great V R experience! Vertical Robot you have the talent and it shows, please don't drop the ball after this, I look so forward to your next creation because these two gems are on another level compared to so many VR titles out there. You have gained my trust and support after these two, I was in love with the first Red Matter and it was an experience I could easily and willingly go back to time and again. And this one will be also!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I'm desperate for single-player VR games of any coherent quality, I can't bring myself to finish Red Matter 2.I kept going back and forth between enjoying the atmosphere while exploring retro-sci-fi rooms and getting annoyed by some of the unimaginative puzzles and the generic combat that’s been shoehorned in. After taking a break, my interest in getting through the rest is at an all-time low. I no longer care about how the slow, unremarkable plot will unfold or wonder what new puzzle ideas, if any, the game will scrounge up.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2
