_childDocuments_.review: *minor spoilers* Played it, finished it, even found the little robot, so 100% on achievements too. Played the first one on meta, so I was really exited for the sequel, and when I picked it up, it seemed rightfully so. Looks great, we pick back up in the facility the old one ended in, a lot more vocal work, good callbacks, and personally I dug the story. So why the thumbs down then? Well, you get about mid way through and more and more puzzles seem a bit rushed and you start being able to solve the last steps of a few puzzles with good old brute force. But honestly I can forgive that, what I cannot forgive, is the gun, and the gunplay. To start off the gun is just the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gun you see in the game, from rapidly over heating and abysmal cool-down, to ♥♥♥♥♥♥ iron sights, to having one of the most unsatisfying effects, to feeling like I'm shooting crayons while everyone else is shooting slugs. Then comes the gunplay, I found the shooting sections ranging from feeling like a chore to down right inexcusable. The section coming out of the doctors office at the end being the prime example of inexcusable, first off there needs to be a save point at the end of the hallway coming out of his office, cause if you are going to make me use the annoying gun, repeating large sections of frustrating gun fights just highlights how annoying the gun is, and spawning more enemies as I come out of the kitchen, that should not have come out as an enemy was left alive in the room, and i specifically shut off the spawner in the kitchen (the spawner does not spawn more until the 2 drones in the room are killed) is lazy and obnoxious. The not eyeball drones are not fun to fight either, with tiny weak points that have to be exposed with a few shots then shot, as they constantly move around and your gun overheats, and you die when they bop you 3 times, and with the health rebound time, the shooting just makes huge chunks of the back half of this game an annoying slog that detracts so much from what it has going for it. If you make a Red Matter 3, I'll probably still buy it as I want to see where the story goes, but I'd personally advise either skipping on the gun, or having a come to jesus talk with the staff responsible for the shooting sections. Cause I didn't think this had to be said, but the gun should be fun to use, at the very least not annoying. The shootouts could've been cool breaks from the puzzle solving, throwing a bit of variety into the mix, something to look forward to, but for me, it ruined the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals for this game are really stunning, the art direction is really good. However, it's a disappointing sequel. I really enjoyed the first game and was expecting something similar, but while the game tries to improve, it felt like a downgrade. It is a puzzle game, after all, and the puzzles are really simple, to the point it makes the game feel like a walking simulator with a subpar story. It lost a bit of the charming mystery of the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly good, in almost any aspect. There is so much to love but I cannot suggest it to anyone.The game feels great until someone tought it was a good idea to add a terrible shooting mechanic to the game. It feels like a EA meeting where at some point, someone that does not have any idea of the videogame comes and says "I like you puzzle game, you know what it needs? More action!!! Shooting for our American customers!"It really is bad, in the worst way possible. Shooting challenges the performances, is not satisfying, is boring, done bad, targets are just annoying, the task cannot be simply completed brainlessly to keep having fun with the real game. No you need to hide, duck, try to aim without any good support or autoaim, or anything that really makes this mechanic better than frustrating. Enemies are annoying, if you die you have to face them again until you succeed in defeating them, they can come at your place some time, and all this in a DAMN PUZZLE.I really was feeling like this was going to be the new myst, the enigmas are super cool expecially at the beginning, scenarios incredible, but then shooting. Also the game is clearly not tested properly for all the options. The "teleport option" really does not work well in some positions where there is no way to aim at something to go on, so you are forced to use jetpack or get very inventive.For the future, if you are going to make a similiar kind of game, just do not add action, you want to make an action game just do it, but please focus on making a better game, instead of going for the shooting mechanic in a puzzle, no one deserve that thing, and no one should be forced to that torture to end the story.Really the game is great, the physics of objects is just great, but you may be forcecing yourself trough the shooting sections just to finish the game and see the end. A shame, hope for the future..
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Game progression isn't as clear as in the previous game, sometimes you might be in the same room for 5 minutes trying to figure out what to do, the minigames are even worse, having to balance a lever on a pixel perfect level.The first one was ok, the second one - after playing for 6h - I gave up, it tries to be more but it fails to do so.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's very well done. Personally, I got sick after about two hours of game time because of external movements, camera shaking when close to objects, and the smooth locomotion, but your mileage may vary.I felt the story kinda drag on once you reach the last planet.Nonetheless, the visuals are awesome and so is the music.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is bad.This game is in the exact same situation as Subnautica 1 and Subnautica Below Average.Red Matter 1 was pretty good. Immersive, with a short but intense story filled with mysteries, and a well-made, rich environment.Red Matter 2 is basically the opposite.First, the main protagonist is speaking. This is already nonsense for a supposedly immersive FPS game, but doing this in VR whole new level of stupidity. And "I" am not just speaking sometimes, "I" never shut up, preventing me from reading things, understanding where I am, and figuring out out what to do by myself.I tried to stick with it, hoping the endless verbal diarrhea would stop after the first hour, but after seeing the comments, I know it won't.Got it at -60% and still asked for a refund. This is not worth playing even if it were free. The story and the way it is narrated are way too lazy.Devs: you are making a game, not a film, not a book. Got a story? The player should experience it through gameplay. If you want to tell a story without engaging the player, make a damn film. If you want to narrate without showing or involving the player, write a book.What a mess, it could have been a great game, but it's pure garbage. It's sad.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the 4k textures fool you, this is clearly still a mobile game for children. Honestly bored out of my mind, the puzzles are super simplistic (I'm talking like connect the pipes minigame, and put thing in hole shaped like the thing) and most of the gameplay is just walking down corridors. The environments are made up of super small rooms connected with unnecessary loading "airlocks" between because its still the same game that had to run on mobile hardware. If this game wasn't in VR it definitely wouldn't have all the rave reviews. On the plus side I will admit a few of the effects look nice, especially the vintage-style circuit boards and screens with 3d-depth. And can say that while it won't challenge your wit it also wont challenge your hardware. A fully VR-capable PC has no issues hitting your headset's target framerate playing this mobile game.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe it was my fault to play this after Half-Life: Alyx and without having played Red Matter (I can't stand teleport movement, sorry), but Red Matter 2 didn't really grip me. I didn't play it for long because I had no more time left until the refund period ended, so my review is more of a "first impression".What I didn't like and what finally made me refund the game is:- The graphics and overall atmosphere felt unconvincing. It's a bit hard to describe, but if you compare it to HL:A, it's nowhere near that level. Maybe that gets better later in the game, but the first few rooms in the space station weren't that good.- The story didn't peak my interest at all. It seems to be pretty generic.- Being forced to scan all the texts to translate them makes no sense and felt like a chore just 30 minutes in.So, why am I still recommending the game? Well, I'm sure many others will enjoy it and since you can get a refund if you play it for less than 2 h, I'd say give it a go. I'm sure you'll notice soon enough if it is for you or not.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's every bit as good as the first game, and more. It remains a thrilling experience front-to-back. Just like the first game, it has the tension of a horror game through it's atmosphere and music, but none of the actual horror elements you would expect a horror game to have. You should feel a little uneasy at all times, but not because you're actually in any danger. There's no cheap jump scares, or monsters that you should be worried about.Ultimately it's a good puzzle game in some genuinely well made environments. I never found it too difficult. The addition of combat is probably it's weakest point. Not that I dislike combat, or that it holds the game back. It just isn't interesting enough to warrant it's inclusion.All in all, a good adventure that continues an interesting story.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Games looks really good and run greatMovement system is ok at best the character is really slow, the item grabbing mechanic is taken from Alyx but made really slow and boring just like the pathing of the game one hour in. nothing is explained and i found myself running back and fourth corridor, waiting 25 sec + at some decontamination (loading) areas just to found out brought the wrong Printed eye with me.I don't feel like walking back to the lab once again.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: This was very much a slow, methodical puzzle/adventure game with light combat. The combat was frustrating as I was mostly just blind shooting trying to murder stuff so it didnt murder me. ("Git gud", mmkay, whatever.) It was short. Like, SUPER short. Steam says I got this done in 6 hours. If this is on sale - like, maybe 50% off - then yeah I'd say go ahead and pick it up. There's a neat twist at the end that I enjoyed. But if it's not on a pretty steep sale, I'd say skip it, or wait for it to get bundled with the original - and get them both on sale, at the same time.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Basic puzzle solver/escape room gameplay with serviceable story that is almost completely hampered by unnecessary and poorly implemented shooting sections. You'll like this if you enjoyed the first one, but overall there are better puzzle solvers/escape room type games out there that don't try to shoehorn in mechanics to extend gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR games I've played.Game looks great with somewhat minimal artistic style and lots of great-looking indoor environments. Grabbing things feels very good and the world has many interactive objects. Some story bits are predictable for the players of the first one, but overall story is still interesting. There are quite varied puzzles usually revolving around repairing things (some puzzles are clearly inspired by Alyx). Also game has some combat scenarios, they are simplistic but do not overstay their welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very enjoyable storytelling game with some interesting puzzles, great graphics with perfect optimization, constant 90 FPS without any drops on the highest settings with Ryzen 5800X and RTX 3080 12GB, and with a lot of room to spare (according to fpsVR graphs). I really like that you're in a space suit that you control using controllers that look like your VR controllers (at least in case of Reverb G2 or Quest controllers), and when you press buttons or move your analog stick, the fingers in game do the same animations, which is great for immersion.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Very good, good story, good combat and voice acting is also good. The only complaint I have is that you have to press the trigger all the way in to the final click on the Index controllers(knuckles), I don't like that. Just look at what Valve did in Half-Life Alyx, that is better in my opinion.But that is just a minor critice, nothing that really matters, you get used to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, if somewhat simple adventure game.  They did very well with the graphics, and the puzzles are very intuitive.  I was a little disappointed the game was short, but it is standard for games of this type.  I will say that I don't think the arcade shooting added much to the experience, personally, especially since the enemies in certain situations infinitely respawn...  It wasn't much of a hurdle, just annoying.Definitely try and get it in the pack with the first game to get more value out of your purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished it yet, but I'm on the last bit.This game is great, just an improvement over the first part.However, as some others have mentioned, the gun controls are very weak. Unnecessary too. Just dodging the cams would've been more fun, I think.Puzzles are still much too easy, slightly more challenging than in part 1, but definitely still way too easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent VR sci-fi game, worked well with my HP Reverb G2. I played the first one then purchased the second, haven't been disappointed, with improved overall quality and game duration. Graphics, environments and gameplay is very good, puzzles are well balanced with increasing difficulty. I definitely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time since I took a risk on a game and could say "totally worth it" (or actually complete it). Puzzles were sometimes easier, sometimes harder but clues were scattered around to help you learn how to solve the puzzles (they never gave the answer, only how to solve which was neat.) Gun as a tool was alright, but as a combat mechanism I didn't like it very much. Was obvious this was designed as casual game, not action and so the combat with how tanky enemies were and how sluggish the controls were did not feel good. Story line was great. No BS, no hijacking the story to score "points" in any direction that I could tell, just good storytelling. Feels like forever on this point too. Based on this game and the story I may check out other titles from this company.Lastly, two things related to the VR experience. I could not bring up a menu midgame. Normally it's "hold down a B button" or "press both joysticks" but I found nothing. It would have been very beneficial to be able to adjust volume inside the game. In order to quit, I had to bring up the Steam VR menu and exit that way, felt kinda weird. I had to play this game in 60-90 minute intervals because I did get motion sick sometimes. I don't know that it was directly related to the game, There were some odd textures on occasion that were visually disorienting.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Works on Reverb G2 with custom controller bindings.Red Matter 2 is more than twice the size of the original and one of the best looking/optimized VR games, but its gameplay is just tolerable rather than exciting. Only superb visuals and atmosphere save it from being boring.Technical achievements of RM2 are undeniable: the game runs better than HL:Alyx while looking almost as nice. It has one of the best VR images of planets, and retro-futuristic soviet environments are breathtaking. And item interactions are still smooth, intuitive and incredibly immersive, just like in the original.But the gameplay is not as good: most puzzles are just mediocre, boring hacking minigames are repeated over and over, slow jetpack platforming and basic combat/stealth encounters feel like a padding. I still enjoyed most of my time with RM2, but it could have been something so much greater, if its puzzle design was on par with the visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cool sequel to Red Matter. If you liked the first one, you'll like this one.I simply love the world building, the puzzling is somewhat straight forward, but you do occasionally use your brain while never getting stuck.One new thing is combat which is well suited to slow VR motion (not everybody can stand fast action in VR, I tend to get motion sickness, but with Red Matter 2, that wasn't any issue, even in combat).The storyline is very cool and a worthy continuation of the first game.There were some minor technical issues for me, like hand tracking sometimes glitching out a bit, which I never had with other games. It also requires a rather beefy PC to play. My i9-12900KF and 3090 Ti with Index did not allow playing at my regular 150-200% resolution scale at the 120 FPS I prefer. But scaling that down a bit was well worth it to experience this game.All in all absolutely recommended if you're into VR Adventures at all.Slava Volgravia!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend however... the puzzles are not up to parIn general the game and experience is good, it lacked for me a little of the ghost experience of the 1st game but more than made up for it with more game play in the 2nd.The issue I had friction with was simply the puzzles were far too easy, and there was a bit of padding in there that made the game longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's kinda good puzzle game.Even though i liked 1st part more.Still, this one is good too.The storytaling, the gameplay, the puzzle stuff and etc - everything forces you to continue playing.What i didn't really like: shooting and speaking.I guess, the best part of RM1 was lack of human beings at all. Same feelings like in Subnautica 1.And when char and NPC always talking, drons are flying around - these things ruining all the suspense.Also i should mention "darkness": i didn't really enjoy those dark levels. It seemed like a horror and i questioned why would devs add such stuff in the game?This game bought me with suspense - i had no clue what was going on and i wanted to figure it out. But horror?...At least it was for about 5-10 mins.Still, i liked the game and can recommend it.And i hope there will be RM3 and it will more like RM1.P.S. Puzzles are too casual in RM2 than in RM1 though.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really solid game. It feels good to play a full and finished video game with a decent story an interesting gameplay. I just find it sad that so few people bothered to even play the tutorial. I found it was a great experience and I very much enjoyed 100%-ing it in the 8 hours I spent in it. It also doesn't require a PSN account which is nice to see.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most immersive and impressive VR games I've played. The atmosphere is chilling at times without being outright horror. The story is intriguing and the visuals are stunning, and do a fantastic job at imparting the awe-inspiring scale of the surrounding environments. The puzzles are not excessively difficult, and include some fun and innovative mechanics. Do yourself a favour and use the 'jetpack' method of movement - it's a bit slower than teleporting but really heightens the immersion. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics and the handling are insanely good! You can touch and move almost everything around and this hand-cable-thing is sooo satisfying to use. So from a technical standpoint a very good game. Also the story is interesting and well told.But the puzzles were very disappointing to me, I wouldn't even call them puzzles anymore. For most of the puzzles, the solution lies directly next to it. I mean really: You find a terminal with a broken fuse, so you already know you probably need a new one. On the terminal there is a written note that tells you that the terminal needs a fuse to work. Also, on the very same terminal, there is a schematic that shows that you need to put in a new fuse. And as if that weren't enough, Beta also tells you that you should look for a fuse. This makes me feel like the game thinks I'm 5 years old. These super obvious hints for obvious tasks really ruin the atmosphere.The only good thing about the puzzles are that they are very physical which is fun in VR.Oh and one more thing: The fighting levels and the gun are just annoying. The gun doesn't shoot where you aim using its sight (it's slightly of) which makes aiming impossible for me (so I just spam).I still recommend this game because it's one of the best story games I've played. Highly detailed levels, great visuals and haptics and a pretty good story. If you want to play challenging and rewarding puzzles, then this is not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Works well with Valve Index Controllers.  Engaging game that constantly tests your ability to figure out how to solve the next challenge and move on toward the end.  A GREAT game and multi-kudos to the 2 person team for coming up with such a playable, challenging and enjoyable game!  (Haven’t finished yet, am at the party room/kitchen scene now.)  I found myself “stuck” a few times in a room and had to REALLY look around to find the solution BUT (so far) it has always been there.  The only frustrating incident was trying to get the battery out of the radio.  I knew I needed a battery and the radio had one but using tools, twisting buttons and even shooting it did not dislodge the battery.  It kinda accidentally fell out, weird!   The pseudo AGI has a real welcome sense of dry humor and there are times you can trust it and times when you can’t, fortunately the game doesn't end when you “die” as a result of one of the times you shouldn’t have followed it BUT it is an entertaining addition that serves to lighten the story at appropriate places.  The only bug I found so far was at the beginning of the game when I tried to follow the rails and get on the other side, got “stuck” between the railing and the wall and could not move, ended up going back to start over.  Other than that there have been no bugs or glitches.  The gun site could be a little more accurate or a laser target red spot (like the one in Hubris) would really be helpful.  Other than that, no improvements needed!  Kudos again to the robot team authors! Oh, almost forgot: GREAT GRAPHICS!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great Game. The developer looks to have learned a lot from the first installment and found some inspiration from HL: Alyx, which is a good thing. Hopefully their next game will feature even more visual immersive and diverse locations and more clever puzzles and interactions, and will improve on the physics of the objects that you are interacting with. For example how the energy of a large object like a train realistically comes to a halt and how it drops its momentum in steps. Or the velocity of which heavy objects like chairs and crates would drop to the floor, etc. Besides that the immersion was perfect, some minor turning problems with textures that causes some spikes, but overal a great experience on an 78003D & 7800XT with an Index. Also,  thanks again for implementing the teleport option for those prone to locomotion sickness.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not finished with it yet but having a great time with this game. Even better than the first one. Great puzzles that make sense in the context of the situation. The couple times so far that I had trouble was because I wasn't as observant of my surroundings as I should be. A couple other times I thought I had more to do in the room because I accomplished the task quickly,so spent some unnecessary time looking for nothing.I would highly recommend this game (after playing the first one, of course).
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: A solid adventure. It's a bit more story and puzzle oriented than action, though there is action in parts, and it never felt dull or boring to me. Things move along nicely. The puzzles are generally basic. But They did stump me 4 or 5 times until I found the solution. A couple puzzles are pretty excellent. I'd say it's worth playing, especially for adventure lovers. I took 9.5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Combat was a nice addition but I wish there was an "ambidextrous" option that let you have your right hand set to dominant but put the blaster in your left hand and vice versa. I'm right handed but I shoot with my left and having to pick between moving with my left hand and turning with my right (which I'm used to) and being able to shoot properly is something I'm not a big fan of.Aside from that admittedly VERY specific nitpick, it's a suitable sequel to the original Red Matter that looks very pretty indeed. Puzzles require a good amount of brainpower and I found it to be quite charming overall.Story is good and all, but I just feel bad for the poor bastard whose body you end up possessing.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this game is like playing half life alyx for the first time, the story, the setting, the environments were all fantastic, the world felt so real I usually just spent time messing around in one room touching and interacting with everything to see how they interacted together and it blew my mind how much stuff fit together (You can remove and add on weights in the gym to make stuff lighter or heavier)This game really improved upon the first in so many ways it doesn't even feel like the same game anymore.However I do have a few cons yet that doesn't take away from the game all that much so feel free to ignore this part.The lip syncing needs a bit of work to be honest the mouth moves but the words don't fit.The line delivery is a bit lackluster in some cases however still a great story.I was a bit disappointed how some items don't make sounds when you drop them/bang them against stuff, add that and it would feel way better to pick up and drop items.Overall this game broke my mind in such a good way, the amount of times I just looked at the environment is probably one of the things I did the most other than touch stuff.This game feels so good to play in VR, overall best VR experience besides HLA8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: I was reading some people were comparing this game to Alyx in terms of VR masterpiece. Well I have to say that also for me this reaches a crazy level of immersion, similar to Alyx. Not only the design and graphics is great, but the interactions and rhythm between action, exploration and puzzles is just great. Everything is perfectly detailed with the same old mix of "cartoonish" feeling that the first game had.Definitely recommended and surely one of my top 5 (or top 3) VR games so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun VR experience, however it has some unnecessary filler that adds no value to the game. For example, large rooms that require jetpack navigation which is extremely slow and cumbersome. It's not difficult or challenging, it just takes forever to jump on one box. The story is somewhat interesting and the visuals are great! It runs pretty smoothly and worked flawlessly with Virtual Desktop on a Quest 3. I think it's worth it's asking price, but definitely a steal if you get it during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Better than the first one, even though there's a bit of shooting now and then. Some nice puzzle ideas, even though most times it's "find part/parts to progress. Graphics are nice and the overall experience is rather polished. Tip: If you find walkingspeed/jetpack flying movement too slow, switch to teleport in the options. Reduces immersion though.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not ideal, but very good.Positive moments:- excellent graphics and optimization- intuitive control system- some puzzles are interesting- the locations in space are magnificent. _childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Escape room for about six hours. It seamlessly follows on from the first part and is less spooky, but the resulting feeling is perhaps more pleasant. Nice locations, interesting music, good puzzles (Lysenko's are the best). I really enjoyed it with the exception of the final drone fight. Why do they have to "run and gun" in every game?
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Played it primarily on PSVR2, easily one of the best looking VR games out there, it was very impressive for a small team. For me the story wasn't very interesting, but the rest of the game was great. The combat was maybe a bit weak, but personally I'm already bored of shooters in VR, so this being more exploration-oriented is a plus.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute treat for VR, both visually and gameplay wise. Sure it's no Half Life Alyx in terms of Gameplay, but the visuals are certainly up there, if not a notch higher. The story is very interesting, and picks up right where the first part had left off (here's the moment you should start playing RM1 before considering playing RM2 :D), and nicely closes up the story.Highly recommended for anyone interested in story based VR games :D
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked Red Matter 1, but Red Matter 2 just elevated the gameplay even more.  It felt like its own story and not just more of the same, which is hard to do with a sequel but the developers did it.  The graphics are beautiful, the puzzles are still challenging, but not frustrating.  The puzzles are just fun.  And the story feels very original, and is really compelling and exciting.  Very atmospheric, awesome game.I have played a lot of games in my life, including a lot of VR games, but I have to say this might be one of the most enjoyable games (pancake or not) that I have played.  Loved it loved it.  Please make more!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first Red Matter was the very first VR game I played so this series holds a special place in my heart.  At the time I was blown away.  Since then I've played dozens of VR games so I'm now harder to impress.  Nevertheless I was not disappointed by part 2.  I decided to replay Part 1 right before playing this to refresh my memory.  The first one is a straight puzzle game and, from what I can tell, there is no way to die.  This one seems to be heavily influenced by Half Life Alyx with the inventory and hacking systems almost straight up copied.  Not that there is anything wrong with that.  There is now some platforming, stealth and combat sections thrown in so you can die but you usually reload seconds earlier and can retry an unlimited number of times so it's not too bad.  Gone is the teleport/jump and you now (slowly) move with the thumb stick so you need some VR legs.  The first one took me two and a half hours to complete recently but probably longer on my first try so maybe over three hours.  This one took me around 7 hours so it looks to be twice as long.  Maybe I'm just dumb but I got stuck a few times, didn't use any guides and stuck to normal difficulty.  The puzzles are mostly fairly straightforward with a few stand out ones that could only ever work in VR.  Usually when I was stuck it was because I missed an item and spent the next 10 minutes walking between different rooms trying to figure out what to do.  The platforming and stealth sections are a nice added element though very basic.  The combat is probably the weakest part.  You have one weapon, it's difficult to aim accurately, and the enemy AI is dumb. Enemies seem to move around predefined paths and fire at you when they see you.  They never seem to charge you so it's just a matter of peaking out, taking a few shots, ducking behind cover to recover, rinse and repeat.Graphically the game looks very good.  On Quest 2 these games are probably some of the best looking games out there, on PCVR the game looks very good but you can sort of tell it was made for Quest first and then upscaled for PCVR as there is no big showpiece scenes with high polygon counts, explosions, etc.  For example, when taking off on a ship the windows often close so you can't see a continuous shot of you leaving the planet.  Something that I'm sure the quest could not handle. Overall though 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: There are exceptionally good games and there are good vr only games. Sometimes, but very rarely there are exceptionally good vr only games. This is one of them.Red Matter 1 was okay. Not a masterpiece, but it was a good game overall with some issues with the movement controls. But this, this is miles ahead in every way. Controls, graphics, art design, music, puzzle design, story, pacing, balancing, performance... This is on the same quality level as Half-Life: Alyx. Impressive in every way. Not just because it's a great vr game: Because it's a great game overall.If you like scifi, adventure games and you feel overall comfortable in vr, this is imho a must-have title. Challenging, but never frustrating and you always want to know what happens next and what's around he next corner. Can't wait for the devs to announce their next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR experience I've had so far! Good story, beautiful graphics, well-optimized graphic engine, good mixture of puzzles, exploration, storytelling and action. I also had a lot of fun using the jetpack, it does induce a bit of nausea, but much less than I would have expected. I absolutely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: As many have said it is an improvement on the first, graphically is stunning with a lot of "wow" moment for design and sheer size of certain locations. I find the puzzle a bit more streamlined, however I am not a huge fan of very complex puzzle mostly due of time constraint when playing games. The story is also easier to follow in my opinion. A must have for any VR user out there, it works flawlessly with the Quest 2 in Airlink without any issue.We now need Red Matter 3!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding gameplay, breathtaking scenery, fun puzzles to solve, fascinating storyline, intuitive mechanics and usage of tools. What more could you ask for…. Just a few things….manual save would be nice so you don’t have to replay the last 20min of play when you ‘die’. The voice acting is ok, but could be better. The amount and depth of speech is something to be desired. It gets lonely in space! Beta’s interaction with you is very intermittent and, in the meantime, there is practically no inner dialogue.But, having said all this, this is a great sequel to red matter 1. Let’s hope they keep on making more like this….but take the comments into account.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Looks fantastic and runs really smooth.Liked all the puzzles.The combat is a good variation to the puzzling part. Yes it could be handled better but as it is not often the case it feels good. (The last "battle" was a bit tedious)Information for easily scared people like me: there are no jumpscares, although it is one hell of an atmosphere though. _childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: You get to find out what happened in the first game, more nice soundtrack, more VLAD, better locomotion, you get someone who talks with you every now and then which can be both a positive and negative, but that's it.The way the grabber was used in the trailer kinda lead me to believe you'd be able to, like, climb stuff, but alas, no.Puzzles are...And the flashlight is still a joke. _childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Dont sleep on this game.  its phenomenal!  the graphics are incredible.  it looks and feels AAA.  the puzzles are tricky but not frustrating.  i wanted to know how the story ended and was left feeling very satisfied at the end.its kinda like Half Life Alex' younger sibling in terms of graphics and depth and immersion.  i really loved it,  so much more than the OG red matter.  my only complaint is that i wish it was longer but i got a good 7-8hrs out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game! An Alyx-esque linear story with believable level structure, an interesting, physically active world to explore, many (many (possibly too many? idk I liked them)) puzzles and simple, but punishing and high-tension combat. Story's a bit predictable, and the protagonist's voice could use a bit of de-bassing (something the devs surely missed from observing HLA, it really pounds on the ears when the voice is still full on the low end), but they're honestly minor complaints for how engrossing and compelling the gameplay progression is.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: The attention to detail in this game is awesome, the retro-post-soviet ambiance and the intriging soundtrack make this game an incredible sc-fc experience. But this it's not a fast-action paced VR game, it's a mix between puzzling, exploring and discovering.Two thumbs up!!! 👍🏻👍🏻*Tested on a VALVE INDEX*
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great sequel to an already amazing sci-fi game. It's bigger, longer, more expensive with great graphics and completely remade controls to make it all nearly perfect. There's even light shooting combat now.Love the story, the mystery, the puzzles, the exploration.I wish there were achievements as well.Here's hoping for another sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Wow. Wow. I rarely write reviews, but I had to call out how much I'm enjoying this game. I was really worried that a sequel would be worse than the original. I need not have worried - this really lives up to the high standards set by its predecessor. I feel no need to rush through this game as it's incredibly beautiful and stopping to look at the little knick-knacks scattered throughout the area is amazing. Even the scratches and marks on the photographs. I'm appreciating every tiny detail and kudos to the devs for putting so much into the game, while still keeping it perform well. Great work and worth every cent.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is what a good VR game should look like. The story is good and well done.Gameplay is fun and can be challenging with some of the fights you have to get by but not enough to where you're going to give up because your not an expert at mario world. _childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: That was fun and interesting.  It has a few good spine-tingling moments with how it plays on dread about what could be around the corner, similar to the first game.  The environments are amazing,  There's a lot of stuff to look at and interact with.  The scanner occasionally has some snarky descriptions of the objects around.  Vertical movement via the jetpack is well handled and a welcome addition.  I'd love to see more exploration/discovery games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first Red Matter before the pandemic and was one of my favorite VR titles. I had no idea that they were making a second one and it did not disappoint. The game is beautiful with story, puzzles and some combat. A lot of other reviewers have already covered in detail about the game so I will not go over that here.Just know if you are looking for a Great VR Title to play your search is over.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game builds upon the original, with a longer story and much larger set pieces. There are some familiar puzzles, which make it fast to solve these, but enough new variety to keep it interesting. It has a much more linear story than the original, feeling more like a Lone Echo story than red matter 1, but has the stunning visuals and soundtrack of the original to make you feel at home. Some of the puzzles can be tricky, and there does, after a while, start to become a little fatigue of running around fetching things and repeating some processes, but not enough to leave you frustrated with the game. The visual and fluid controls, coupled with the visuals, really sell this game. Maybe it doesn't have quite the impact of the original, and therefore the twists and turns in the story aren't that surprising, but it is a worthy successor nonetheless
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal. Really enjoyed playing. I highly recommend. Many great puzzles and fps elements. Beautiful graphics. What more can I say, except I wish there was, or hope there will be, a third sequel? Great job to all the devs. Cannot wait to see what ya'll come up with next. I will certainly be purchasing it, whatever it is. Thank you for this experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: My hardware: nVidia RTX 3090; AMD Ryzen 7 5800x; 32 Giga of Ram; SSD hard drive; Oculus Rift CV1 with Supersampling at 1.7.If you are reading to find out if Red Matter 2 is a title to buy, you can stop at the first few lines and buy the game without any problems. Technically it is extremely accurate. The effects created with the shaders, the materials that make up the levels, the voices of the characters, the simple and fluid game mechanics, the effects and the soundtrack that are not too intrusive but effective are the strengths that testify, among other things, a notable technical growth of the developers. In fact, the first Red Matter, despite being a valid title, fails to compete with its sequel.Among other things, this is yet another game created with Unreal Engine. It's amazing how much space this game engine is gaining among Virtual Reality. And the quality that Unreal Engine is capable of delivering to the games is astounding.Returning to the game and its mechanics, the puzzles are well thought out, never extremely complicated and sufficiently varied. I've never felt blocked by a puzzle but I've often felt satisfied that I figured out how to proceed. The story is well thought out, perhaps a little too complex but still “plausible” and coherent. The “ethical principle” of freedom, if taken in general terms, can be shared.That said, this is the third VR title I've played in which "the villains", the ethically reprehensible people who try to disrupt the world with their evil plans, are Russian. Of course, the name that designates the old "Soviet" territory is another. However the references to culture and art, as well as the language of the "enemies", etc. refer with overwhelming clarity to Russia. It doesn't matter that the "heroes" of this story are also "Russians". The message, somehow, is that that part of the world embodies and interprets the idea of ​​absolute evil. And this saddens me and annoys me enormously. If any Russian is reading these lines, I would like to let him know that not everyone in the West is so simplistically inclined to create such a clear-cut dichotomy between good and evil, based on East and West. In our western societies there is so much that doesn't work. There is an amount of rot that would be enough to create endless dystopian games in which the part of the bad guys can be played by institutions of various degrees and levels, all rigorously Western. And I'm sorry that, with all the problems we have, our Western model of society can be taken as an example of freedom. It is not and it never will be because we are simply crushed and subjugated by corporations and powerful men just like in the rest of the world.Here, it is the second time that I am forced to write in a review that I would like politics to stay out of Steam and that game developers would commit to unite, to make it clear that we are in the same boat in the world and that after all only a few “elect”, a small elite, can truly be considered free regardless of their race or language. In the West if you are not rich you are nothing. I hope this review is read by the developers and contemplates dedicating their next chapter of Red Matter to western inspired dystopias with its many flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Played with Quest 2 + Virtual Desktop on Windows : perfect compatibilityI was a big fan of Red Matter 1. And this second game delivers! Fun atmosphere, nice controls, great visuals, a couple of puzzles, and a mysterious space building. It's not too long but it will keep you busy. You can finish the game in about 5 hours, I think. Together with Red Matter 1, this really creates a great pair of games.A relatively big change is that your character will talk from time to time. This sort of breaks with Red Matter 1's rather silent protagonist, but that is fine really. It does help with the story.Perhaps one thing I can say is that, I play with teleport instead of the jetpack, and there was one room where i had to use the jetpack, because i really could not see a way to teleport my way to my goal in any way. There was another moment like this. So keep it in mind, if you're like me, you might need to switch back to the jetpack once or twice.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: There is Alyx, Boneworks, Into the Radius, Blade and Sorcery, H3VR, Wanderer...heck you might as well through Red Matter 2 on the list of elite VR games that just seems to do everything right. No bugs, no cheesy puzzles, or shortcuts taken. Red Matter 2 looks and plays like a AAA VR title. The sound, gameplay, story, and  presentation are as good as it comes. Bit pricey at $40 and probably a better purchase for a sale, but still worth your money and time. I'll be back for Red Matter 3.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Red Matter 2 adds everything you might have wanted added to the original game, which was absolutely a top-shelf game itself. It is hands down the most polished game I've played next to Alyx. The story is as captivating as the visuals. Gameplay is smooth and intuitive and makes great use of VR space. This is the perfect sequel to a must-play franchise. I highly recommend playing Red Matter and Red Matter 2 in sequence. This game does not disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Played on a Pimax 8Kx, Index controllers.  Visually this game is top crust for VR, amazing to be inside this world this is what makes PCVR great.  No bugs, so i rate it as highly polished.  Puzzles were all solvable without the need for guides, story moved along at a nice pace.   I just didn't like the final shooty shooty part with the endless bots that part sucked.  But otherwise loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of areas to explore. Some of the puzzles are a bit too obvious and very easy to solve - but the solutions are not 'stupid' at least. Wish the challenges could be a bit more 'Myst' like; with the combination of graphics and story, this would have been very good. Never the less, I recommend this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Vertical Robot does it again! Daedelus, Red Matter 1, and now, Red Matter 2! I can't wait to get stuck back in and/or see what's to come next. This game is a must-play!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this for my PICO 4. Didn't expect much - oh boy was I wrong. I love this game - it's almost perfect! 6-7 hours of thinking mans puzzles and exploration. A little combat throw in - no tooo bad, just enough to annoy you slightly hahaha.The standouts are:1) GFX - simply stunning, art team has figured how to minimise aliasing and make everything look amazing.2) Soundtrack and atmosphere - top notch!3) Narrative - via voice acting (firewatch lady is great!), punch cards!!! and objects in the world, a compelling story that sucks you in right away.4) Puzzles have wide range of complexity - super simple or real head scratchers!I've played it thru 6 times so far, love it every time!Probably the best VR game made so far - Perfection!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished and WOW, really good graphics and controls (though I saw a video of someone storing item in left controller and couldn't duplicate on the Index. Anyone know a way?) Liked the story better than the 1st one and the graphics really made this trippy in some places. No spoilers but going towards the end was pretty trippy. Also liked the remote control vehicles you use to complete puzzles, especially the smaller 'blimp' later on in the game. The puzzles were good, I solved 98% without any walkthru help, though in one place looked a walkthru cause couldn't get back upstairs. Luckily the game provides enough objects I stacked them and found my own way out, so that was cool. Just stuck with what I had done. Had one puzzle thought was really stuck on cause didn't see any clues and even exited game to see if missed something. Nope! But you should be able to figure it out, by just watching how your trying to crack it and what is happening. That is all the info will give on it. But it felt pretty good to figure it out. Also really liked the scenes in the beginning of the game, the views are amazing being out there in space on the moon bases,..... The jet pack was pretty useful and absolutely fun!

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked RM 1, then you will also love this one. Outstanding space sceneries together with nice graphics will take your breath. Puzzles has normal difficulty, but you can stuck for a while sometimes. What I didn't like was action parts, which are unnecessary in this type of game. Shooting was kind of fun, but passing turrets was a nightmare. Anyway, it is a great game and I hope it will continue (and bring more facinating space sceneries).
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is how you make a sequel!The first game had great gameplay, but here its absolutely stellar! I love how the controls in the game are basically just extensions from the real life controllers, makes them super intuitive.The story perfectly complements the first one. It starts exactly from where the first part left off, which is basically at the main menu of the first game, it's a minor detail, but I think it was super cool.As I mentioned in my review of the first game, I still think the game should up the horror element. Compared to the first game it actually dials down to the point of not being scary but merely being mildly mysterious, which is a shame imo. I would love to play a horror game in this setting, I'm sure its not just me? Anyway, I really hope this is not the last title of this studio. I will definitely buy their next game and I can't wait to see what they turn out next.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Setup: HP Reverb G2, Nvidia 2080, smooth locomotion & turning.This game was WAY beyond my expectations. I'd played the first one, and it was fine, but had purchased both as a bundle. The 2nd one was mind-blowing. The story is just okay; but the setting and mechanics and attention to props & details are spectacular. I would rank this above Boneworks & Bonelabs.The fact that I can put a roll of toilet paper on the toilet paper holder (loose end over the top, of course) and use the toilet brush to clean the toilet is fantastic. The fact that there's a laundry machine, and not only when you try to open the door does it open... but the tumbler inside spins as well! The fact that these two things in no way relate to the storyline or literally anything about the game at all is the attention to detail that's awesome.Stepping into one of the space shuttles for the first time and flipping the switch and watching the door close to seal me in.. I really felt like I was in my own little shuttlepod. Again, it's all the attention to little details, smudges & scratches on the glass, reflective surfaces here & there. And speaking reflections... I don't want to give spoilers, but the reflections in this game were another time where my jaw hit the floor.And it's not just the puzzles and atmosphere. The way that movement and "VR hands" were implemented is the best implantation I've seen hands down (pun intended). The ability to switch between tools is genius and the animations exciting. The little plug that comes out the side to interact with terminals was a masterpiece in creative thinking. "Reloading" the gun was another genius mechanic that avoids the clunkyness of trying to insert magazines & stuff. 80% of the way through the game and I would still sometimes pause just to flip between hand tools and watch the smoothness and details of the animations. Spectacularly done! And the jetpack mechanic felt so natural & intuitive.For anyone like me who might be concerned about horror (it's one of the reasons I still haven't played HL:Alyx), this game doesn't have any jump scares or anything. There are some creepy parts, but very tame and nothing "jumpy". All in all, this is one of the best VR games I've played. The Devs innovative ideas for hand tools, movement mechanics, and everything just made this an absolute joy to play through and I really hope to see them get awards for this and for other Devs to pay attention. This is how to innovate in VR. I'd say it's a must-play for anyone who likes puzzle type VR games, and would highly recommend it to anyone else who's interested in seeing what types of mechanics and VR implementations are out there for immersing the player. I'm afraid to play other games now, because I'm not sure how they'll live up to the brilliant mechanics in this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Visually stunning, highly atmospheric and superior to the original game in almost every way, Red Matter 2 shows how to come up with a sequel and fully highlights the magic of VR. _childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: A great game. I had to look up one puzzle but everything else was mostly just a case of looking around. The scanner pretty much tells you what the puzzle wants. Combat was fun but not exactly challenging, it was enough to break up the puzzles though with a bit of action. Don't expect perfect, its not on par with HL:Alyx like some people are claiming. Your arms can get a little stretchy sometimes and the wrist flick is annoying temperamental and slow. Unless something was directly on the floor I found myself ignoring the mechanic. HL did this much better and I actually found myself wanting to use it in real life when leaving that game. RM this was my main annoyance. Movement was good, I had to turn up movement speed to full though. Worth the money for a solid game, some nice puzzles that at points make you have to consider several ideas. 8/10 if we are doing ratings, A good game with a few annoyances. Good story to drive the puzzling.PS. The game is not 47 hours long. The game didnt exit fully and ran for a good 30 hours in the background processes. Make sure it exits after you are done!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: YES! Everything that was missing within the first Red Matter game, comes with this one! Lokomotion, 9 hours of playtime and Enemies that you can fight! The very good graphics and the good controls are due to the HL-Alyx engine. A solute story, tricky as well as easy puzzles and pure soviet architecture porn make this one of the best recent VR title.All I have to say to the developers is: Guys, please start working on Red Matter 3!
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent VR game with silky smooth performance and stunning vistas. Largely linear and story driven, taking you from puzzle to puzzle with a few platforming and combat sections. Puzzles are sometimes simplistic, but are always a tactile experience that makes excellent use of VR mechanics. The combat is nothing to write home about and can be a bit frustrating at time, but that's not the main focus.Setting and story is somewhat reminiscent of 2001 A Space Odyssey, Event Horizon, and Interstellar with light horror elements set in an alt-history retro-future where a CCCP style superpower finds something unexpected in space. Direct continuation of Red Matter 1, which is almost as good as this entry and definitely a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Red Matter 1 better than 2 for have better atmosphere & presentation and not have unnecessary shallow gunplay mechanism that 2 have but still Red Matter 2 is one of the best VR game available now. Also I scanned almost every item include books and search everywhere and read everything and died few times but still finish game in 5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: Red Matter 1 is in my top 5 vr games. The sequel is beautiful. I loved almost every moment playing it. Great story, graphics, and puzzles (even though I enjoyed the puzzles in the first game a little bit more). The combat felt unnecessary and a bit clunky/underdeveloped, personally I think they should have left it as a straight puzzle game without these elements but it doesn't ruin the game. The only thing that did almost ruin the game was the last puzzle which without spoilers relies a bit on haptics. There are no other clues visual audio etc. My haptics are broken and I feel like its a bit of an accessibility issue when I was stumped for an hour then looked it up. Wish there was some way to adjust for disabilities/ use multiple senses.Overall though great game. Almost as good as the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute visual feast that performs beautifully. The amount of little interactions is so entertaining and the puzzles have some of the most unique solutions I've seen in any game that make full use of the VR controls. Story is nothing to write home about, but the atmosphere and immersion are top tier. Wish this little studio the best with whatever they decide to do next, and there are a lot of big studios that could learn a lot about VR game design from these guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Matter 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best story tellings in VR so far. I just finished it with almost 6 hours in. The graphics are amazing, it's not HL Alyx's levels of amazing, but it's almost there. They took a lot of inspiration from HL Alyx, like a Gravity Glove-like way of pushing objects, the way you can store the items under your controllers and how you can only shoot with the dominant hand (there's no reloading tho... you simply cool the weapon with the grip buttons).I ran into some problems, sure, like not being able to hold the safe combination buttons (kinda important if you want to put the password of the safe...), but for god sake, you can count in your two hand how many people worked on the project in the credits.

_childDocuments_.review: Exceptional - if you liked RM1 - this will tick all the boxes and many more. Its longer, more puzzles, more story, awesome. _childDocuments_.review: Having over 600 hours on the Quest 2 and half (or better) of that time with an Air Link connection, I've seen a lot,  but am I'm pretty amazed at the quality of this game. The puzzles are very creative, along with the controls, Character Acting, color, textures, ray trace, etc., etc., they  are excellent. The story line is believable, and it's the supporting puzzles (twists) that make the game so intriguing. If I were to think of a similar game it would be MYST but on steroids for all levels of play. As of now, I've only 3 or 4 hours of play time under my belt but I'm looking forward to picking the game up where I (it, lol) left off real soon. The one negative that came to mind for me is that you cannot save the game at will, the game does auto saves but rarely at the time you would like to exit. It's annoying but it can be made easier with a little effort. The puzzles are not as simple as you might expect, however, that’s a great part of the charm of this game… hop on board, enjoy…PS: I’m told that Red Matter (original) is a great deal of fun as well, but Red Matter 2 is a big step up for the hard(er) core enthusiasts looking for similar content but much nicer.

_childDocuments_.review:
Red Matter 2 is an adventure that takes place during a dystopian Cold War whose events unfold after Red Matter. It is the story of how people trapped in a reality created by their rulers, rebel against their destiny and fight to do the right thing.

Being subjected to a mental simulation in an enemy base, you are awakened by an infiltrated agent who has been sent to rescue you. Just as you are about to escape you intercept a distress signal belonging to an old friend. Determined to come to his rescue, you embark on the journey of a lifetime to the far reaches of the solar system to find him. 

That adventure will make you question your entire reality, not only because you will once again encounter the Red Matter more unleashed than ever, but also because Volgravia holds more secrets than you could have ever imagined.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd originally given this a positive review, but after playing it for longer I can't recommend this.This is a text based, sort of a choose your own adventure adult game. It plays similar to things like Corruption of Champions if you've ever played that, except you're more of the dominant sort in this title.This game is in rough shape at the moment, to say the least. The title screen always defaults to 1980x1080, so with my video settings it hangs off my screen. Text and options scroll down really far in ways that you're not used to seeing. Text boxes are sometimes too small for what they're displaying, so you've got this ugly scroll bar next to a button where you find out what such and such ability does. There are rooms which are listed but don't actually exist beyond their title yet. There are abilities which are the same way. Sometimes you have to look for a second to find out where a button is as the positions are not consistent from screen to screen. The dev really likes using the ellipsis (...) as an interactable object instead of saying something like 'continue' which can be hard to see at times and looks weird.I mean you get what I'm saying. But those things are interface based, and you can work around that if you enjoy the content which I do. The problem is that there are too many dead ends in this game which eat up your time, and there are few real paths to take which means you have to replay the same stuff again after each death.Like... you try a talent on the wrong person - Instant death.You get a random event and pick the wrong option (and it isn't obvious which is wrong) - Instant death. And by the way the instant death doesn't work on one of those events - it just says game over and then you continue playing.When you turn a person into a frenzied sex addict they then become useless to you. So, if you frenzy a key person it's like killing a main quest character in Skyrim. You're still playing, but your game is dead.Which reminds me... the game is very dependent on 'parasites'. Like if you don't infect someone with them, you're not doing much of anything. And the method used to get parasites is titillating the first time but it gets VERY repetitive.There's a lot of extra clicking. You start each day in your bedroom and then have to click click click to get to each location, and nothing happens on the way to these locations at least that I can see. It would make more sense to just have a list of useful locations that you can go to and perform one click to get to them.This has a great premise and I'm into it, and I want to see more games of this type on the market. But the truth is that Artifact isn't a decent playable game yet and the devs need to prove it to me before I repurchase or recommend. If I were you I'd check back in in 3 months.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a turn-based "strategy" (it's really mostly tactics) game in which you play one of several characters along the lines of ninja/samurai/judo master, etc. Each character has different starting tiles (tiles are essentially cards and each does a move, attack, or both), different ability, and a in one instance a different movement style. Every time you skip a turn, load a tile into your queue (3 tiles max), or play the tiles in your queue, it ends your turn. The enemies have the same constraints also.It's a very simple yet elegant and well-designed game. I've had a LOT of fun playing it, and although the metagame roguelight elements are not that strong, the replayability is high, there are plenty of things to unlock for a while, and the difficulty of the ramping game days (each day is like a difficulty level you choose before a game begins) is quite well balanced.The average run lasts perhaps 30-45 minutes unless you make one mistake too many and then of course it's shorter. The music and art are both great, fit the style of game, and are pleasing to the eye/ear. The sound effects are also great and suited to what's happening on-screen. The way the turns work is really quite strange at first, but once you get used to it (in about 5 minutes or so most likely) it becomes clear that planning when you load versus use tiles or move vs attack, etc becomes the focal point of both the fun and challenge in this game. If you have two attacks that total 3 damage, it'll take you 2 turns just to load those tiles, which may be too slow to kill an enemy with 3 health. Luckily, there are plenty of solutions to that kind of situation beyond the obvious solution of a single attack that deals 3 or more damage. Depending on your character you can push, throw, or move past enemies, and there are also tiles that allow for these same types of movements as well. There are upgrade shops and you draft new tiles like you'd expect from a roguelight card game, but one cool thing different than most games in this genre is that each tile has a number of pips you can use to add upgrades, and once you run out, you either have to add another pip or you can't upgrade it further. This adds another fun element to the game of having to make tough choices of which attacks to make stronger or faster, add pips for further upgrades, or to enchant with special abilities.I've got over 100 hours into the game so far, and I think that's above average for this game in its current state, but I think anyone who enjoys this game will get at least 40 hours out of it currently, and there seems to be an endless amount of significant content coming out fairly regularly from the devs, so I'm sure that number will go up soon and probably at least 1-2 more times this year if the current speed of updates continues into the future.I'd say this game is a great value proposition because it's really fun (most important), reasonably-priced, and you get a lot of playtime per $ spent. I play a lot of games and enjoy some and don't enjoy others, but it's rare that I actually take the time to pay attention to the studio behind the game. I've enjoyed this game to the point where I'm very interested in anything developed in the future from the same team because they've done such an exceptional job of balancing the various pitfalls a game like this could fall into. It's fun, it's a bit addictive, runs are a great length, it sounds and looks good, and has plenty of replay value.  I had a few minor gripes initially but they've all been addressed by early updates not too long after initial release so I can say with confidence that it's a game very much worth checking out if this type of game in interesting to you. I love it and hope that some other game developers make knockoffs of it like what happened with vampire survivors recently or Slay the Spire a few years ago. This style of game needs to flourish, there's something really neat here, design-wise.

_childDocuments_.review: It's as if Fights in Tight Spaces and Katana Zero had a child. Positioning is key, mistakes are severely punished, the gameplay is rhythmic and elegant. Move, turn, wait, queue your cooldown-based skills in a fast-paced tactical frenzy. The graphics, while plain, convey the setting and possess the oomph. A well-timed twitch and a swoosh effect coupled with a little bit of screenshake make a mace to the face feel as it should. The UI is really helpful by showing you enemy intents so you could strategize around them to your heart's content. Alas, it only thinks one step ahead, you need to be better than that. This game is deeper than it looks, challenging without relying on randomness. As a way to mitigate the hardships, it provides profound skill modification options that feel truly impactful. This is easily Shogun Showdown's crown feature, which makes it stand out big time.Every skill has a number of upgrade slots you can utilize after every other fight or at the shops, and you can occasionally raise the cap. The system allows you to create overpowered monstrosities out of anything by adding damage, enchants like poison and double-hit, or lowering cooldowns in a mostly unrestrained manner. That creative freedom puts Shogun Showdown in the no-run-feels-the-same category. Given how short and eventful those runs are, you'll keep coming back for one more over and over again. If I had to name a flaw, that would be a rather stingy meta-progression. The unlocks really make a difference, though. Overall, this game deserves its rating. It's tight, snappy, and thought-out mechanically. A steal for the money. I feel like I barely scratched the surface by killing the Shogun a couple of times. I yet have so much stuff to get done, but I can already tell I'm having a blast.P.S. Them archers, am I right?My curator

_childDocuments_.review: If Slay the Spire and Into the Breach had a child on a 2D plane, it would be this game. Even though at first people may think Darkest Dungeon, it's far from it. Like StS, you can see your opponents actions and react with tiles. Unlike StS, your hand is always the same as you build your "deck", which are called tiles in this game, although every action has cooldowns. Where it becomes a little bit like Into the Breach (And that may be a bad example since the way the turn goes, its 1 action for you, 1 action for the enemy) is that where you move actually matters. I appreciate the variety of the characters available (So far, 4) which each have their own playstyle. I also appreciate that skill is far more of a factor than luck when playing this game. Sure, some games you draft tiles that just work very cohesively where you're just obliterating the game. The difficulty balance I think is just right, although I've just unlocked Day 2 (the 2nd tier) with all the characters just now. Each complete run is about 30-45 min but it's addicting. What impresses me most is that this is in EA. I paid $10 for it and it's been worth it so far. I'm hoping the dev adds more characters and playstyles, more tiles, etc etc. More content really. The core of the game is more or less completely playable.  Some minor bugs that I encountered but nothing gamebreaking. There could be some better balance on tiles as some of them just have a too long natural cooldown to be effective. And some get ridiculously overpowered once you stack the right buffs.

_childDocuments_.review: Shogun Showdown is truly a breath of fresh air and a shining gem in the rogue-like line of games that have come out in recent years. As someone who has poured many hours into most other games of this kind (from Nuclear Throne, FTL,  Binding of Isaac, Gungeon, Slay the Spire, Spelunky and many others), Shogun Showdown still manages to stand on its own through beautifully crafted and thoroughly considered simplicity. Simplicity that nevertheless manages to offer you a myriad of strategic opportunities for you to exploit and fully utilize to your advantage to win. One aspect I feel most other games of this type eventually fall into and become a sore and thoroughly unenjoyable part of the game for me, is their RNG based mechanics. You'd play run after run where the game either gives you the most mediocre of items for hours on end, making the experience either tedious due to the items' lack of synergy or utility. Or you get every rare and broken item in the game in a row and sleep through to the finish because the game lost all semblance of challenge. Or you may get items you're sure would win you the game, but the game decides to present you a random enemy or boss, or multiple of them in a row, that directly counters your entire build and you just die in the end. Of course, that's a matter of skill about whether or not you'll score a victory, but fact is, in the end, I dont feel like I had earned that victory or loss one way or the other.Shogun Showdown manages to surprise in this aspect. Instead of going the usual route of adding uncountable amounts of items to the game to increase variety and then retroactively balance them so that they don't become either game-winning or nigh useless, it instead goes the minimalist route. The game offers a whole variety of weapons for you to choose and make each run distinct with, as well as a variety of characters to start each run with. Each that plays incredibly distinctly from each other and with their strengths and weaknesses to consider. Yet the maps and enemies remain consistently predictable. Each stage is pre-defined, their tiles as well. But, you may still pick which way to go on the map screen when a path branches out, each path offering distinct benefits for you to pick from. Even the seemingly most useless weapon you may pick up, you can still manage to find a way to make it wreck havoc through upgrades and enchantments. Sure, the shuriken may only do one damage at the start, but if you add the Curse effect to it, making the enemy take double damage on next hit once you hit them with it, and since it's ranged, it opens up a lot of opportunities for the rest of your loadout all of a sudden. The whole arsenal has this potential and that's truly refreshing and a playground to experiement with.With the later difficulties, each of the decisions you make play incredibly very significant roles that must be considered in full for you to even get near a victory. Carelessness isn't easily forgiven and each single action you take is something you really have to mull over before committing to, lest you get punished and straight up die as a result.Positioning and forward-thinking and planning are here of bigger importance than the individual weapons you pick up. That in itself negates a lot of the experience I grew irritated with other games of this kind, like I mentioned. No run feels like I had done everything right and still lost, or done everything wrong and still managed to eek out a victory. And that's truly refreshing. With the aforementioned thought that's necessary to have given before committing to each individual action you do, makes this a pleasure to play.On the design side of things, the game looks and feels truly wonderful, evident in the screenshots. The music is atmospheric and calm to keep you fully engaged, with some tracks being absolutely catchy bangers that had me bobbing my head while I played every time they came on (Theatre of Illusions and Spirit Gateway being notable mentions) The controls are tight, and the animations bouncy and full of life and character. Colour palette is also well considered so that each character stands out and everything's clear. I thoroughly recommend Shogun Showdown to anyone even mildly interested in this genre and most others, really. It's more than well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Another entry in the Slay the Spire-like genre, but rather than acquiring and upgrading cards in a deck, here you are acquiring and upgrading abilities with cooldowns.  It's got tactical positioning along a one-dimensional line, and you get the opportunity to manipulate enemies such that their telegraphed attacks will damage each other in a manner reminiscent of Into the Breach.The core gameplay here is really excellent - exactly what I want from the genre.  As you play, the game consistently makes you feel clever for setting up a multi-kill combo.My complaints are that the current content is somewhat limited - only five ascension levels and only four classes, each of which has a unique special ability and starting moves, but the classes are similar enough that the run-to-run experience feels more samey than some other entries in the genre.  Still, the price is right, and the core gameplay is really a bullseye, so I'm recommending.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆Shogun Showdown, currently in Early Access, seamlessly merges the strategic depth of "Into the Breach" with the addictive deck-building mechanics found in "Slay The Spire." Despite being in its developmental phase, the game manages to provide a compelling and engaging experience that held my attention for a substantial 35+ hours.The strategic depth of positioning and timing in battles, reminiscent of "Into the Breach," is combined with the accessible yet nuanced deck-building elements. This makes the game suitable for both newcomers and seasoned players, offering a satisfying blend of simplicity and depth.While the game is on the right track, the roadmap highlights areas for improvement. One notable suggestion is the introduction of more varied music to prevent potential monotony during extended play sessions. Additionally, expanding the variety of in-game shops and introducing a system to manipulate the shop type could enhance the strategic depth, adding to the game's replayability.In conclusion, Shogun Showdown successfully combines the strengths of "Into the Breach" and "Slay The Spire," offering a satisfying and addictive gameplay experience. With a few adjustments and additions, the game has the potential to stand out in the turn-based strategy and deck-building genres. If you're a fan of either of the aforementioned games, exploring this Early Access title is a solid investment

_childDocuments_.review: If it's not obvious from my playtime (which isn't accurate, but I have easily played 30 hours), and my 100% completion, I am mad for this game.
