_childDocuments_.review: Really pleased with this game.  Although it's a very different beast, the general vibe of Shogun reminds me of when I first picked up Slay the Spire - cute graphics, easy to play, mechanics that you can readily get the feel of, but increasingly complex as you dig into it.  My first few runs didn't go well, but making a little bit of progress let me unlock some new abilities that could be selected during runs, and by about my 6-7th run, I was able to put together a nice mix of skills and abilities to grab a win.Which felt a bit disappointing... as in, wait, was that it?  But the game immediately made clear that all I'd managed to do was unlock more content, harder runs, and increased variety.  In fact, looking at the achievements in-game, it seems like I'm really just at the beginning.Really fun, good price point, can play without a mouse if you want.  Hopefully they never port it to mobile else I won't get anything done.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is super fun.  There are so many turns where the outcome puts a smile on my face.  Here is an example: I was between two pike wielders both ready to attack.  I thought for sure I'd get stabbed, and being early on on day seven probably meant eventually death.  I did have a move where I could swap positions the second pike wielder.  However, this would turn him around and he'd still stab me, or so I thought.  I tried it anyway, and miraculously the second pike wielder died before he stabbed me!  What happened?  Well, the first pike wielder went first, and since I swapped places, he stabbed the second pike wielder.  But that shouldn't have been enough damage ... wait, earlier I had used a curse card that caused double damage!  I didn't even think about it applying to the enemy damage as well.Anyway, surprising turns like that make this game really fun.  The vibe is also top notch, although I wish there was more to the story ... it's mostly just characters you don't really recognize saying cryptic messages you don't understand.  But still definitely worth a buy if you at all like the genres involved.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been out only a few weeks and it's already one of my favourite games. The flow is smooth; the game is so simple yet so complex. There are so many different builds you can run; I've literally never had the same build twice. The difficulty jumps are still difficult, but they don't feel impossible. The soundtrack is perfect and very tasteful, so it's not overbearing or distracting, but it adds to the experience very well. I'm very keen to see what future updates hold and the sheer amount of content that the game seems to have/will have in future. I'm really enjoying what these developers have made. With that, the only things I would change to the mechanics of the game is, a buff to bosses in a balanced way as they feel like a break after the enemy levels before them, a way for enemy's to break infinities if a player is using one, and I think when an enemy uses a mirror to take a card the enemy should gets all the added upgrades, enchantments, etc. Otherwise that everything was almost literal perfection, I was shocked as I played the game just after release and before any updates,I hope this was helpful if you are considering it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of my favorite roguelikes, up there with the greats. It was a lot of fun coming up with good builds and even when you feel like you've solved it, there are so many modifiers to keep making it fun. I enjoyed each character and the playstyle it provided. As someone who has played for so long, id love to have some more enemy variants added to the game but I enjoyed my time with the game so far and look forward to seeing how this game develops in the future if at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I love it when games get super creative (especially in a genre so over-saturated as the deck roguelike). This game didn't grab me at first but I gave it another shot and everything just *CLICKED*. It's addictive, and extremely satisfying trying to work out numbers in your head, trying to hit combos like a mega gaming Stephen Hawking (RIP).The only thing I really want to see are palette swaps. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the simplicity of the premise fool you — it is an ever evolving puzzle with strategic depth and complexity of Fisher's chess. While easy to pick up, it will continue to surprise you with fun builds you can pick up along the way.Unlike chess though (which is the most boring game on planet Earth), it's fun and engaging. I haven't played any turn-based genres in ages and was hesitant to pick up, but after 60 hours spent in the game — it's money well spent. If I had anything bad to say — some UI decisions are... Let's say a bit questionable and confusing at times. Stores and map are a bit challenging to remember at first, but after getting through the game a few times, you're learning the names of shops, the tiles and getting through quite nicely. But I wish it a bit more explicit explaining what each store offers beforehand.The more you play, the more you start to see what will happen on the board — feels clever and rewarding. Runs are not quick — on average it takes me about 60 minute for a complete run. I'm sure there are smart people running through it, but I'm a dummy. Friendly warning — returning to real life after playing a few sessions will get you thinking in turns.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neat and tidy little deck-builder fighting game that nestles snugly within the archetypes of ninja-n-samurai feudal Japan-fueled comic books. Games are pretty fast, there's a well done (and standard issue) run, die, build, repeat kind of dynamic. The play is smooth and clicks along smartly. Maybe too smartly? After 15-20 hours of play, the rhythms of the game go from familiar to numbing, and the levels and enemies start to feel a bit samey. I wish this game had been bigger and messier, with weirder builds and outcomes, and more of a sense of world-building and exploration - as opposed to the same little island chain that you walk over and over and over again with increasingly nasty conditions imposed upon you (fewer bonuses, suped-up enemies minus suped-up rewards, etc.) Still: It's a nicely wrought package with some really clever cards and moves, and the developers deserve kudos for how smooth and skillful the whole thing feels. Absolutely guaranteed to be quite entertaining up to a certain point, and that's the most we can ask of nearly anything out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: After finally unlocking every skill and weapon, I've already got my money's worth. Currently on Day 5 with the final 2 characters, my favorite being the purple hair one.  I love the little animation details, the music and the boss designs.The combat is challenging but it flows in such a way that is more satisfying than frustrating, even with the added difficulty day to day. I love how many different builds I've stumbled into and just start clearing out waves of enemies. I am now going to mention things I'd like to see changed. Let me say first that I'm giving this game a 8/10.One criticism I have is I often go a long time without seeing certain weapons I want. I try to go for variety, but weapons with pierce, or kunai which can stack to great effect with any skill that says '+1'  have distinct advantages. One of the best combos is perfect strike kunai, if it kills ANY enemy in it's path, get it back free oh also it has infinite range. The skills are mostly balanced and all can be useful, 'Combo Deal' which gives you +50% more consumables should cost 20 gold it's a very good skill and I would still buy it for 20 but 10 is insanely cheap.Now that I've unlocked the feather and the scale (and haven't seen either once) I actually wish those were permanent effects that I can just have. Why else am I paying 99 skulls just to rarely see them and pay more gold?? Looking forward to beating Day 7 and then trying for a zero hit run. I'll keep an eye out for new skill updates, weapons or maybe a new character!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game, is incredible. I would wake up almost every day since purchasing, excited to play more. This is a phenomenal Roguelike.The game starts off feeling insurmountable. It seems so difficult, and you look at the Achievements, and think... man, there is no way in hell I'll ever be able to do all of that. But then you learn, and get better, and every win, improvement, and combo you make feels so incredibly satisfying. Each step further you take, leaves you wanting more. And that is exactly what I love in a Roguelike.If you are looking for a strategy Roguelike that pulls you in similar to "Into the Breach" you NEED to play Shogun Showdown. This is a no brainer pick up. One of the best games I have played all year.As a Completionist, I like to talk about what mastering a game is like. And as I mentioned while the Achievements feel insurmountable at first, they definitely aren't. Every step you take, you feel more and more capable of fully completing the game. However capability is not what stopped me from achieving 100%.This is where my one and only real issue I have with the game comes from, and if you aren't someone who strives for 100% in games you play, just go play Shogun Showdown already! However, if you are, I would read on.During your runs, you can complete certain objectives, that give you Stamps. I think this is an awesome system. Beating a run in a certain time frame, performing a specific number of combos, taking as little damage as possible, etc. This is all fantastic design, and it initially had me excited to collect these. However, these are character dependent, and they are same for all 5 of the Characters.The issue is, none of the Characters are different enough, to warrant having to collect each stamp, five separate times, in my opinion.What makes each character unique, doesn't necessarily make one character easier or harder than another. And their special abilities *can* be performed *by the other characters with specific tiles*.So getting all of the "Ultimate" Stamps a single time, is a really fun challenge (which, for the record, I did do). But having to do it four different times for the final Steam Achievement, isn't something I particularly felt like doing, it feels very *same-y*.On top of that, the game's "Story Mode", has you complete 7 "Days", and completing one Day with one character, does not unlock the next day for all of them. Which makes sense from a story perspective, but when I tell you one of the "Ultimate" Stamps is to beat Day 7... not only do you have to get each other Stamp with each character (which can all be done on Day 1 and is objectively smarter to do so), you also have to complete each and every day, with each and every character. Which is a *minimum* of 35 runs.The Roguelike aspect is great. The *runs* themselves do feel different enough, and are a lot of fun. But I don't feel like the Stamp system should be tied to each character independently, and should just be a set of challenges that can be done on any character. And if that were the case, I would have achieved 100% Completion of Shogun Showdown. And I had a phenomenal time doing so!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: There's a point, once you understand the mechanics, that you truly feel like you are developing a fighting style in a martial arts movie. It is exhilarating. And when you miscalculate, you WILL sit there and try to calculate any way out. You WILL spend 3 minutes just thinking, staring death in the face and conclude: ♥♥♥♥ I should have turned around 3 turns ago.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Fun experience that's worth it's price tag.Your ability to do well leans more towards your own skill, knowledge, and thinking ability, though not completely without a little luck/rng.If you're a completionist like myself you'll find a good amount of challenge in clearing runs over various difficulties and with particular goals such has winning a run without getting hit once, and with numerous characters and loadouts.   It also feels like a very fair game, 9 times out of 10 my losses were my own fault rather than the game throwing something at me that felt just a little unreasonable in certain circumstances, even that rare occasion only stands out in the more challenging run attempts.All in all, I strongly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great! Roguelite strategy with a cool aesthetic and surprisingly deep gameplay. It may seem easy at first, but the challenge really ramps up if you want it to. As of writing, only 2.4% of players have beaten the final "day" or level of challenge. I honestly didn't think I was going to, when I watched a streamer play through it, I wasn't sure it seemed fair. But I thought I'd give it a try anyway, and I was able to use all of the strategy I'd picked up over 50 hours of play to just barely secure the victory. It was extremely satisfying, and a good sign that even people who struggle to see more than one move ahead can figure out a way to win. I absolutely recommend picking this one up!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Got instantly hooked by the gameplay, the art, the theme.I feared the game would be too easy as I completed my first run but the difficulty ramps up nicely afterwards.There's some RNG involved regarding your weapons upgrades but you still get to focus on what you need since you're able to see which type of shop you're heading to.Once you're done with the max difficulty mode, there are still achivements to unlock. Some of them are quite interesting. Others are a bit too RNG.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: You know an indie game is good when it can distract you from all the "AAA" games in your library. This is on the same level as  when it comes to making something amazing with as few pixels as possible. The music, fluidity of tactics and replay value are peak quality. Great for quick gaming sessions inbetween doing life things!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna go on a long review, but gotta leave something positive as the game deserves it.It has great roguelike tactical gameplay that you can play fast like a speedy ninja or take it slow like a cunning tactician, there's some good ludonarrative resonance in that sense.Overall a must try for roguelike tactics fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: If you are like me and absolutely adore games like FTL, Into the Breach, Monster Train, you will love this game. The gameplay is fairly simple, and the difficulty ramp is fair. When I lose a run, it is often because of mistakes I made and not the game being unfair. Sometimes you get yourself stuck in lose lose situations, but they can often be avoided. I've had a blast with this game and it will easily end up as a game I jump into for a few runs every few months. Until them, this is all I'm playing right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much every part of his game is amazing. From mechanics, to art, to music, to themes. Would absolutely recommend it to anyone even partially interested in the tactical greed combat or roguelikes. The only real downside is because of the sheer amount of decision the game offers it's really easy to kill your run because of wrong input. It happened to me, it happened to other people who i watched playing, it will also most likely happen to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Easy to get started and it seems so simple, but every run feels so different. Even though it seems like you are facing the same enemies over and over again the challenge stays fresh because their positioning and your available weapons make all the difference.Reminds me of Into The Breach but in a simpler format.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I love these kinds of games, I play them almost exclusively. Coming across a well balanced, fresh, and incredibly well executed strategy rogue-lite is a rare treat.Shogun Showdown takes that a step further by also offering tantalizing progression. The difficulty ramps up quickly after your first run, and offers a slew of challenges to explore at your own pace. Too often rogue-lites burn everything on your first, second or maybe third completed run, with little motivation to keep playing afterward. Not so here.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun roguelike. You need to think couple steps ahead to beat a run. That said, lower difficulties allow for many mistakes. On the highest difficulty a bad move or two can end your run just like that. I think the difficulty curve in this game is great, it really forces you to think about which attacks to pick, how you upgrade them and what shop to visit. There's an enourmous amount of weapon combinations you can try. Planning your moves a couple turns ahead and then executing it and clearing the whole board is awesome. Unless you miss something in the process and it comes back to bite you. The game also looks great (if you enjoy pixel art) and the soundtrack bangs pretty hard.One thing, if you'd like to 100% this, it'll take a pretty long time. The game will require you to beat the highest difficulty on all playable characters (5) and also get all ultimate stamps on them (some of which are pretty hard to get).9/10 overall
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun, but i want to criticize just due to the 40+ lock skills and tiles. Seriously? Why are there so many things to be unlocked? Not to mention that your shop in run also need to be unlocked.  Also the skull is a long term to collect. It is boring to have great experience by using the same and less skills in the early stage. I have played <Alina of the arena>, <into the breach>, <slay the spire>, <fight in tight spaces>, no one force me to unlock so many things, which is definitely waste my time. Yet it is easier and shorter game, but i still can't bear the 40+ lock things and you have only 5 at the game beginning. 轻量且简单，但是40+个解锁项+商店全要解锁真的是司马了
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: The presentation and UI is top notch. A lot of care has gone into the basics.Its like a turn based dance where you can see your opponents moves and you need to react with your own. You can queue your own attacks and execute elaborate combos, which is very satisfying.At first I thought this game requires the ability to really think ahead, and couldnt be played too carelessly. But it is very forgiving in the sense that a lot of heals are provided. When you get the combos together it is very satisfying.It absolutely nails what it was going for.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Great variety of gameplay options, lovely difficulty curve with the "Day" system slowly adding difficulty multipliers to your run  (a more refined option than Hades's skulls), all wrapped in a neat little package.I don't think it's a roguelike with 2000 hours of play in it, but only because the very quick feedback loops allow you to learn more about the game terrifyingly quickly: Only played 20 hours (for now !), and I feel - in a good way - like I've played 80.Very, very highly recommended !
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute must-have if you're a fan of any other turn-based roguelikes ala Slay the Spire. It's not a deckbuilder but it plays a bit like one with its tile-based skill system. Combat is strategically dense and it's deeply satisfying learning its mechanics. Easier to learn than a deckbuilding game but with the high skill ceiling you want from a roguelike.I've only scratched the surface with a single day 1 win, and already It's clear this game has way more to offer beyond your first successful run. I'm seeing lots of interesting new areas, bosses and skills on day 2, and there's plenty left to unlock. Pretty sure I will be playing at least 100 hours of this if not more.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: If you like "Into The Breach", "Wildfrost" or Maybe "Dicey" dungeon then I strongly encourage you to get this.If you like deck building roguelikes in general I believe this is a safe purchase.If you like stacking complexity onto a simple foundation then this could be for you.If none of the above apply this review isn't for you, sorry!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game's great. Just beat the highest difficulty progression as I write this, and I had a blast the whole time. The formula is simple, but very very fun, and makes the common indie-roguelite formula feel fresh. Hard to put down, with bite-size runs that feel different in each build you try. New characters don't make a huge difference, but their special moves and starting equipment also keep things varied. I love this, it's a great example of what a solo dev can do if they're smart. Great damn game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: 4 hours in and I can already tell this is a roguelike that is gonna have its hooks in me. So far most of the metagame between runs is unlocking new tiles, skills, etc., but there's a great feeling of being able to chain together different moves and play a high-risk, high-reward type of way. But the game both rewards you for putting pressure on, but also knowing your enemy and being patient for an opening. It's crazy how this game at times creates this feeling of what classic samurai showdowns look like (despite looking nothing like them.).
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: The game unfolds wonderfully with early fights teaching you the basics before new ability, character and passive unlocks & ascension levels blow things open.High recommendation for fans of games that make you feel smart when you do something cool, and immediately punish you (fairly) for your own mistakes.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute delight. You can sit with it for hours while you have a podcast or a movie on in the background. Perfect multitasking game.  If you only have 5 mins, easy to get a stage or two done in a run. Outstanding work devs, can't recommend this highly enough. If you liked Into The Breach, this will be extremely up your alley. I hope more bosses, more islands, more tiles, more characters are on the way, even as a paid DLC. Let me throw money at you Roboatino!!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I've been gaming my entire life and this has got to be one of the best games I've ever played. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: A turn based Roguelite with a unique combat system, unlocks that actually matter, classes that all feel unique and balanced, and a fair difficulty curve. Despite some design choices I don't personally agree with (e.g. timed challenges in a turn-based game, enemy actions you have to remember to be able to react to) I really enjoy this game. Also, the soundtrack is very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute joy of a game! It tickles the joys of a deckbuilder without getting bogged down in a meta or relying on unlikely card combos and overstuffed decks. It tickles the joys of a tactics game, with the enemies telegraphing their next move - on your first run, you'll be relying on this, on your fiftieth, you'll be able to predict many moves in advance  how the enemies will respond, and slaughter the lot of them without getting a single scratch. The game actively rewards high-level play, without mandating it, and you can muddle through just fine on the lower difficulties that you'll need to pass in order to unlock the harder runs. The achievements offer alternative twists on the ruleset if you're looking for entirely optional further challenges (e.g. finish a run without ever turning around, for instance).
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Shogun Shodown is best described as a turn based puzzle rogue like. You know for certain what your enemies next move is (and often several moves past that) so you need to plan out your turns accordingly. A run takes about 30min to an hour, and you will go from combat to combat with upgrades in between and you gain a meta upgrades at the end like more skills and characters. Typical rogue like formula honestly. What sets this game apart is the incredibly tight, simple to understand but hard to master turn based combat. You will understand the game within 5 minutes of playing it: you spend your turn either moving, adding an attack to your queue or execute all attacks. You can tell however that the creators sat down and tried to think about all the creatives ways skills could use this. Attacks that pull or push enemies or you, attacks that hit one space away, rushes, ranged attacks. And they also spent the time to balance them, with every move being helpful or fitting some fighting style. It all comes together for incredibly satisfying gameplay. With game knowledge and smarts you can work your way out of any scenario.The game also looks and sounds ok. Honestly, I am not in love with the aesthetic, it does not wow me by any means, but the graphics convey information cleanly and well, and it isn't ugly. That part is all fine.There really isn't much story, just a small bit of lore.So in the end the game is solely carried by its gameplay, so good thing its so stellar. If you are a turn based roguelike fan, I would highly recommend Shogun Showdown
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding game, refreshing take on the roguelite genre.A lot of motivation to keep playing due to a lot of unlocks, different stamps and achievements that can be collected with each class and build variety of each run. Length of one run is perfect for me as well, takes about 30-60 minutes depending on how fast one plays.Plays like a charm on the Steamdeck with very low battery usage.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is way more fun than it has any right to be.  It's like Darkest Dungeon if you took away all the annoying parts and added in a touch of super lightweight deckbuildery stuff.  Intensely engaging moment-to-moment combat loop without ever actually melting your brain, so it doesn't ever get exhausting.You can save and quit at absolutely any point on any run, the fights are quick enough that it works great regardless of whether you have 5 minutes or 2 hours, and it's a phenomenal Steam Deck title.Thank the powers for the Discovery Queue, or I never would have seen this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: As a roguelike fan, I find it hard to find fault with Shogun Showdown. The battles feel intense and thought provoking, bringing an air of chess with the visceral excitement of a kino movie fight scene. Setting up a 4+ enemy combo and hitting the attack button feels so good. The difficulty starts out nice and easy but quickly ramps up the challenge with each day.The music is top-notch as well, it helps bring you into the theme of the game in a beautiful way. The visuals also play in, from pulling in an enemy with the grappling hook or watching multiple fall from a scar strike. Excellent game, I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic. The gameplay loop is addictive and everything feels great. The music won't get out of my head. Each new skill, weapon, and upgrade completely changes the way I approach each scenario. I honestly can't tell if the enemy waves are programmed to be perfectly solvable with the options available or if it's a testament to the balancing that I always feel like it's my fault when I can't correctly unravel an encounter.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. The core gameplay loop is satisfying and there are enough unlocks to keep you going. I think fights have a good length which always makes me play another one to finish a run in one sitting. I think the ascension system has a good scale which motivates me to finish it. The original one in StS just was too much for me. Different characters and the build options also keep it fresh. Using other tiles changes the gameplay is not just cosmetic. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Turn-based roguelike with fun combat mechanics that involves spacing out yourself and your enemies, timing out your attacks, and finding ways to make a good weapon into a legendary relic by the time you're face-to-face with The Shogun. While there's not a timer that forces you to make your moves, I feel like the flow of gameplay is at it's best when played at a hastened pace--there's even a few achievements tied to getting a 'Speedrunner Stamp' for completing the run in under 30 (in-game combat) minutes, which isn't as difficult as it may sound! I've had a lot of satisfying moments from being able to string together a smart combo of moves and clear the fight in under a minute. Though it may feel intimidating to rush into a situation at times and I'm glad that I also have the ability to stop and think through a series of actions before pulling it off.Each character has a special ability that influences you and/or your enemy's position on the battlefield in unique ways, changing up the core strategy of how you move with each characters and maybe even what weapons you consider taking throughout the run. This, alongside the large variety of weapon choices & upgrades, has made the game feel exciting and fresh to me everytime I've sat down to play it so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue-like games aren't my first or second pick of genre usually but I was hungering for some classic rogue-like gameplay, so I decided to try out this and Fighting in Tight Spaces.This game is an easy 10/10 for me. Music, rhythm, pace, visuals and gameplay is just top notch. And also quite easy to get into once you get the rhythm on keyboard controls (took me maybe 15-20min).Fantastic game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an incredible blend of turn-based strategy and roguelike elements that I have not really seen before and I've played it so much the last few days that I'm seeing tiles in my sleep...When I first tried the game I was very skeptical that I would like it as strategy games are not my thing, but I found that the mechanics (which mostly revolve around positioning and understanding of enemy behavior) are very straightforward. Each character has their own unique movement-related mechanic that you usually form your entire strategy around and having now played all 5 characters a bit I can say that there isn't a boring one!Another thing this game does particularly well is ramping up the difficulty in a smooth and consistent fashion. I never felt like the next stage was a significant jump in difficulty from the last. However, I do think this goes both ways as you aren't really going to find a single item that suddenly makes the game trivial like you do in some other roguelikes.If you aren't sure that this game is for you, definitely give the demo a shot. You might be surprised!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Shogun Showdown is utterly addictive. I bought it after literally about 5 seconds looking at the trailer told me that this was a game made by a developer with a passion and a vision.This is a game that is essentially perfect within its own framework. The game is sort of a "deckbuilder" roguelike, but it's mechanics are very different from usual deckbuilders. There is no deck, no drawing cards, and therefore you are building a stategic package of abilities that are completely predictable. Every enemy action, and their future actions, are also perfectly predictable. Every weapon has unique mechanics, upsides, and downsides, and the gameplay is entirely based around positioning yourself and comboing these weapons in creative ways to deal with problems. Because of that, this game often plays like an intensely satisfying puzzle game: you are presented a problem in the form of a crowd of people with different weapons all trying to kill you at once, and you are left to figure out how to leverage your own weapons and tools in such a way that you don't leave with 3 arrows sticking out of your face. Crucially, the games art comes in here to make the process of becoming better, faster, and smarter at dispatching your enemies LOOK and FEEL really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool.Every run feels different, and I have never had a run where I have felt that the tools I was being given were insufficient for the task as opposed to my strategy and brain being insufficient instead. The difficulty scaling is perfect, and I have rarely seen a game like this where it is so satisfying to just pause, think for a minute about how the next few turns will play out, and then execute a creative combo kill.If you like strategy games at all, give this a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing graphics, gameplay loop, tons of fun ways to play, great music, each boss is fun- I could go on. This has to be one, if not my favorite rogue like out there. It's literally just that in every aspect and just makes me yearn for more in the best way- if you are reading this, you NEED to try this. You won't regret it

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good, one of the few games in the "Roguelike Deckbuilding" adjacent genre where when you lose you can definitively see why and where you ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up rather than "Oh I just could not have won this fight"Would really prefer more enemies/bosses/locations over more characters though, runs out of steam and feels repetitive pretty quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Shogun is a great little roguelike, especially for the $15 price tag. I found myself to be addicted to it for the first 20 hours. That 'one more run' feeling would just not go away. The combination of so many attacks and abilities make for a large variety of interesting combos. You can certainly try to get your favorite combination of weapons/abilities, but there is just enough randomness that you may be forced to trying a new strategy.If you like Slay the Spire or similar puzzle-based games, this is a no-brainer of a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: IMO the trailer doesn't do a super great job of showing what the game really is. They are playing turns very quickly and it almost looks like an action game. This is a very unique game with some deckbuilding and great strategy / planning. As simple as the 2D grid seems, the amount of different actions you can take in this confined space leads to some surprisingly complex gameplay.It runs amazingly on Steam Deck, and with 1.0 out now this is a no-brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

The moves the strategy THE GOOFYNESS (yes i'm talking to you vine attack XD) It's the greatest blend of everything you would want from a game like this. I HIGHLY recommend this to anyone (if you are already here reading this just buy the game. Let creators make more content. ;3)
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Good grief, there aren't a lot of nearly-perfect roguelites out there, but this is one of them.There's nothing not to love. The action of the game is extremely evocative of kung-fu flicks with bullet-time shenanigans left and right. Ability tiles come off cooldown just in time to spin and kill the guy walking up behind you before sheathing your sword. Ninja-swap with an archer who proceeds to be killed by his own arrow. Rapid-transmission around a battlefield with an antagonist a-la DBZ. Throw a dude and hit him with another dude and then kick another dude into a whole bunch of dudes. It's fantastic.Buuut there's also the souls-esque aesthetic of some kind of terrible sin committed by the Shogun which put the world in its current state, with lines of unsettling lore here and there. It's exactly the right mixture of campy and creepy, and it lands at hardcore. That, plus the stage design, and absolutely incredible electronic soundtrack are evocative of the era of old-school Mortal Kombat.It's genuinely fun, sleek, mostly fair, strategic, and there's tons of stuff to unlock. It's stylistic, well-designed, and extremely fairly priced. It's art, it's clearly somebody's passion, and it's fire.If you're on the fence, hop over. This is lit.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Great strategy game with a lot of replay value, good aesthetic, and a great soundtrack.Saw a little bit of Shogun Showdown back when it was in early-access, but didn't play it myself until it released. Really happy with the gameplay so far, the rules are pretty simple but allow for a lot of complexity when combo-ing your kit.My one minor nitpick is that I wish bosses and a few enemies which don't have health bars had a more clear health representation; I think it's a little weird that you have to guess it yourself.Overall, 9/10 game, would highly recommend!.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Very fast and responsive fully polished GEM of an almost deck building rogue-like. There was no point in the game where I felt cheated from the games mechanics and everything is explained very well through the tutorial. This game is very fun and I will be playing much more, attempting to climb through the difficulty levels and unlock more tiles and upgrades to use on future runs.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful game! It's very puzzle like once you get good... you can get through most fights without damage if you think enough, but it takes a while to get there.I felt like every run was "winnable" but it was still challenging. This means it's a roguelite where you don't have to fully rely on RNG of items/buffs.Additionally, the challenging increase flavored as "Day 1-7" was a great idea... even a small thing like that feels less like choosing difficult and more like you are progressing through a story.My class recommendation would probably be jujitsuka. Collision damage in this game is very good, as is repositioning,This is a really good game.
