_childDocuments_.review: Simply brilliant. The core mechanic is building up a queue of combat moves over multiple turns, then unleashing them all at once. The result is that 90% of the time while playing, you're standing perfectly still thinking over your next move, but it still feels like you're slicing through hordes of enemies at lightning speed. It's really cool how it manages to combine the logic/puzzle based gameplay with the warrior power fantasy in a way that feels natural and satisfying. Definitely play this if you enjoyed Into the Breach.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: There's a simple, yet clever combat puzzle in this rogue-like system, with a MUCH reduced deck to a few combat tiles you'll develop a strategy around. Intuiting enemy movements, patterns, and trying to counter & combo them is SUPER satisfying.Only about 5hrs into gameplay and feels like there's a lot of life & love in here. Great animations, stellar Japanese lo-fi, with an intuitive control set which streamlines action. Great sense of exploration as you discover / unlock new tiles or skills, quintessential to rogue-likes, but even so for the backdrops and the art. Turn-based lovers, give this a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on this game for a while now but waited because I don't really do early access. Now that it's out in 1.0 I picked it up and I'm so glad that I did. The game is fantastic. I'm a huge roguelite and roguelike fan, I've played dozens and dozens of them at this point, and so far this is already high in the list of the greats. I can't speak to the longevity of the game since I'm only a few hours in - I suspect this will be closer to a 15 hour experience than a 1000 hour experience like some other rogue's can be. That's not a problem for me, but if you're looking for your "forever game", this might not be the one. But it is a fantastic game nonetheless.If I had ONE major complaint with this game, it would be that the controls using a controller are a little awkward. The game is perfect on keyboard and mouse, but things are a little weird with a controller. Being able to move tiles up and down using the right stick or d-pad would go a long way towards making things feel less weird. Right, you have weird stuff like having to press left to move tiles down and right to move them up, which is very counter-intuitive IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This review is 64 hours in with all difficulties beat and I must say Shogun Showdown is an absolute masterpiece as a rogue-like and tactics game. Runs are short and sweet and the difficulty scaling is perfect as each previous level of difficulty adequately prepares you for the next. Each character's uniqueness comes from their special skill and their starting ability load out which adds a ton of replayability without the feeling of staleness. The only improvement I would suggest to the developers is rework the economy system to allow for more consistent shop upgrades. When I leave a shop I either come out feeling like a god or leave with nothing but the shirt on my back.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, so entertaining and tactical. Many unlocks to chase, different levels of challenges to take on. Fun achievements to hunt, while runs are fast to do if you want or you can take your time and sit for hours since it's completely turn based.I hope for more content in the future and strongly recommend Shogun Showdown!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games of the genre I've ever played.Feels like something fresh and engaging that hasn't been done to death by many devs hoping to capture the success of StS.100% worth the price, if you're on the fence try out the demo; but if you're a fan of similar games then there's a good chance you'll love this.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: All my hours as of review time are from an early access iteration, and even back then it was fantastic! They spent a lot of time getting the difficulty balance just right: the result is a fair challenge that makes you feel like a badass to boot. I never get tired of making a big goon obliterate one of their allies with a sword strike meant for me, or queuing up 3 different moves in just the right order to wipe the map in one go. The boss fights are well-designed and feel more like a duel, or a puzzle/chess match to gain an advantage. It's a 2D-port of the action from games like DMC or Ninja Gaiden without the need for reflexes to pull off sick moves, like Fights in Tight Spaces with a better deck system or Five Finger Death Punch with turns.As others are saying: tight, tough, rewarding, addictive, and fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game quickly became one of my favorite rogue-likes. Brilliant game design and mechanics. The soundtrack really gets you on a upbeat mode while executing combos.It may need a bit of rebalancing weapons, but in general the game feels pretty fun with great replayability. After 25 hours, I think I still going to need some time to unlocking everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!Pros:- Amazing pixel art and UI design.- Fun minimalistic gameplay loop.- Good satisfying sound design.- A lot of enemy variations and all of them are cleverly made, especially the bosses.Cons:- Personally I'd love if the starting loadouts could be more customizable.- Unlocking new tiles kind of does more harm to you in the long run if the unlocked tiles are not good or doesn't benefit your character/build and they keep appearing as the end of stage rewards. Wish the player has more control over it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing, absolutely deserves its overwhelmingly positive rating. Graphics and music are great, the game is super polished, but the crown jewel is the gameplay. It's the essence of "easy to learn, hard to master".My only minor gripe is that map order isn't really randomized. So if you get stuck at a boss, you'll get to know the previous ones VERY well.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute blast of a rogue-like.  This game is entirely based on positional combat, which is a plus and a minus.  It's a ton of fun to make neat builds and see combos come together, but it's easy to nearly ruin a run because you turned at the wrong moment, which can easily kill you at later levels. Cool characters, cool powers, a KILLER soundtrack (huge props to the composer), and a very addictive gameplay loop.  Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo and got hooked. It's a fun rouge like that feels fast paced even though it is turned based! Two things I don't like about it; If your stuck on the first day it feels very repetitive, same enemies spawning on the same floor with very little change other then your attacks. Once you get past day one enemies spawn with buffs that are indicated by icons, there is no explanation on what the icons mean so it is trail and error. That being said I really enjoy this game and highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun rogue-like. So many challenges and quests to do. Runs are challenging but seem completely fair and I can only blame myself for not paying attention.These devs know exactly how to balance their game and because of it, it becomes incredibly replayable.A no-fat straight to the point rogue-like that you will love if you like Crypt of the Necrodancer and Slay the Spire.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: A time devourer. Runs only take about half an hour, but you're not just gonna do ONE run. Even though the action is constant, with very little downtime between battles, I never felt burnt out, no matter how long I've been playing. It's INCREDIBLY easy to just lose yourself to the game. When a run is going well, it's not just because I got lucky with the rewards, I actually FEEL like I'm playing well, almost like a flow state, which I didn't really think was possible with turn-based games until now. The moment-to-moment decision-making, both in combat (you and the enemies gradually commit actions, instead of all at once) and on the map screen (you can preview the next rest stops, but not the whole map) keep you from getting overwhelmed with choices while still giving you plenty to think about.Combine all that with a presentation that's incredibly pleasing and polished (the pixel art is lively and colorful, and the samurai aesthetic is something I personally adore), and you've got a game that's hard to put down, and before you know it the sun's coming up...
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible! Scratches that tactics/card game-y itch like no other.It's like Into the Breach, but from a different view and you can actually dodge ~95% of hits, so most of the damage taken is actually your fault and you could've calculated beforehand and avoided the mistakeReally clever and really fun. The music slaps and combined with the setting really makes you feel like a badass ninja dodging hits and outplaying enemies left and rightOverall the EA left me wanting more content because this game is the real ♥♥♥♥
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: A clever rogue-like deck builder with turn based combat. Thinking a few steps ahead to outmaneuver your enemy (and even make them attack each other) is really fun. Great presentation, nicely polished, love the art style.Shogun Showdown definitely has that "one more round" feeling that every rogue-like should have.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: When I played the demo I thought "What a fun little game". 200 Hours later, and this game is by no means "Little". The overall strategy is fun to master and does not get boring once you know what to expect. A full run to the end (Defeating the Shogun) usually takes 30 - 40 minutes while Character upgrades and stage progress are both saved (until either you or The Shogun is defeated), which is something I have come to appreciate in arcade "Rogue-like" games. Multiple player character options and a variety of ability choices keep the game fresh and make achievements fun to unlock. The MUSIC is (for lack of a better word) perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: For me, a sign of a good roguelike is a short tutorial. The mechanics are intuitive and easy to learn,  and within just a couple short minutes you're ready to go. That's this game; you can move, turn around, attack, and acquire skills and upgrades as you go. There you have it. However, the simplicity hides a depth of strategy and skills that makes the game endlessly replayable. Easy to learn, hard to master. At the time of writing this review, I have just over 50 hours into the game, and my appreciation for it is only growing. It's alongside Balatro for Game of the Year. Seriously, just give it go! Well within the 2 hour refund period it will be immediately clear how intuitive and rewarding the game is.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Not a Gamer, But This Game Has Me Hooked for 450 Hours—and Counting!What started as a casual dive has become a 450-hour journey that I can't seem to put down—and I don't want to! The gameplay is engaging,  but what really seals the deal for me is the soundtrack. It's addictive, mesmerizing, and perfectly complements every moment of the game. If you're on the fence about picking this up, just do it. I'll be playing this one for a long time to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so wonderful. The strategy involved in immediately understood and once you have a few 4D chess moves it becomes very addictive. Ive enjoyed loading it up and doing a run when I dont know what else to play. I find rogue-likes of this type the most enjoyable.Needs more characters, needs more moves, needs more modes. I hope the devs find success and can expand on this game or iterate in the next one they create
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: this game is so beautiful and challenging, and as frustrating as some of the cards (? day 6, no hits, etc) for each character can be, i always find myself coming back to polish the skill to beat it. i don't know how you put the feeling of mental flow state into this game so efficiently, but it works so well. can't wait for the new updates!!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Positional deck builder (as i call it). Really good and fun. The design is awesome too. The base music is okay, but i recommend finding your own and use different for each character, it helps a ton with immersion.Reminds me of a lot of things, but not one thing, which is a really hard ballance to get and they done it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I am probably 40+ hours into Shogun Showdown and cannot recommend it enough. Very cute, lightweight game (works GREAT on steamdeck) - lots of replay-ability to unlock all the tiles, characters, and "stamps". Great demo too- i'd suggest trying the demo and playing around with the combat style. If it clicks you'll absolutely love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly satisfying little roguelite that rewards versatility and planning ahead.  The arsenal seems limited at first, but after a few runs it's easy to stack up some unlocks and learn to appreciate how flexible each of the starting options can be.  The visuals are solid, the soundtrack is killer, and there's enough build variety to keep runs interesting.  Buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Turn based with cool down abilities and mobs and pc all in a row. It's basically a game of sequence and logic, but the music and graphics give it a very fun feeling. Sometimes when I get a really good combo I feel like I'm engaged in movie action kung fu. The settings are perfect- bamboo forest, moonlit port and spirit gate remind me of the best visual aspects of games like mortal kombat. It's addictive! I can't speak for others, but I'm not the best at this and I dont mind. The challenge hasn't gotten old after about 17 hours. Music is the sort of 8-bit, medieval Japan lo-fi jam you'd want and expect from a game like this. I hope they add more content, but the devs clearly care a lot about this and the price has gone up so they can keep at it- power to them! About 20 bucks CAD was a steal imo. Love itUpdate: (after playing several more hours, I was delighted to find the extra locations that unlock along the path. A good amount of content, more than my original review would make it seem, but I am greedy and want more ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: It's a tactical turn-based roguelike. Very tactical, very roguelike, and a little less turn-based.At the beginning I was a bit unaccustomed to the simultaneous turn system. And I was losing in the 1st or 2nd location, but after 20 minutes I got the hang of it and everything went well.Metaprogression in such games is the thing I’m not very fond of, but that's just the way the genre works. Everything is nicely stylized.Most importantly, the number of enemies and different attacks, both yours and enemies’ do not let you get bored, but at the same time do not let you get confused, and in general, the game is just fun to play.I'm a bit tired of this type of graphics, but this is subjective - just my eyes get tired of this a little faster than from less large pixels.In general, the game is still in early access, but I can already recommend it for fans of turn-based puzzle combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: "Shogun showdown" is a game centered around tactical, turn-based combats with a martial arts/samurai movies vibe that I received for my birthday.It's been rightly compared to "into the breach" for its brain-picking gameplay, but it's a lot more forgiving on starter difficulties, thanks to a generous amount of health potions and life saving items. Once a combat starts there is no luck involved, but picking up skills and power ups are randomized, making each run different and fresh. Still, the game feels pretty fair and that's what makes it engaging. That, and being able to unleash satisfying multi kills combo zapping through opponents like in an anime.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I'm absolutely hooked. This game plays as well as any of the great games cited as their inspiration like Into the Breach and Crypt of the Necrodancer. But unlike the plethora of clones we often see, Shogun Showdown is cohesive and stands on its own ideas. I especially love how you acquire new attack tiles and upgrade them as you progress through the run. There are four playable characters in total, each with their own characteristics. As a bonus, the game comes with a banging soundtrack too.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this is one of the funnest games I have played in a very long time. If you have a big brain you will have an easy time, me with my small brain still had a great time but it took me a while before I could win my first run. I honestly lost myself playing this game, and I will do so again. Give the demo a try if you aren't sure like I did. That's what hooked me.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. I disagree with the reviews comparing this to StS though. This game is more about learning and exploiting enemy movement patterns. Also, fully optimal play in this game entails playing very very slowly and methodically, killing off strong enemies one cooldown at a time and leaving the weaker ones behind to serve as meat shields so that they get in the way of the new strong enemies that spawn in. But that sort of play isn't at all necessary to get wins.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and well-paced tactical rogue-like. I see a couple comparisons to Into the Breach, but I'd actually compare this game to Crypt of the Necrodancer. A lot of the player skill comes from learning the enemy movement patterns and using those movement patterns against them to trick them into attacking empty tiles or other enemies.There's also a decent amount of replay value in the tile (a tile is basically an attack or move) and enemy variety. Throughout a run, I find myself often considering which enemies my build is effective against to decide which routes through the map make the most sense. The upgrades also have a similar reactive feel to Slay The Spire - every upgrade has me asking "Where is a blind spot in my build? What do I need to clear the next encounter in front of me?" instead of trying to accomplish some sort of preconceived build.I'm also happy with the difficulty curve of this game. The Days system introduces a gradually increasing difficulty for subsequent runs, kind of like Ascension in Slay The Spire, only with a more comfortable ramp-up in difficulty.The only complaint against Shogun Showdown I can think of is that the balance seems a little off still. Some tiles, enemy types, and bosses feel quite a bit stronger or weaker than others. This might just be related to my play preferences, and I'd still say the overall experience is balanced enough that it isn't game breaking.I'd definitely recommend this game. The tactical combat feels both fresh and familiar, the music and art are excellent, and the game is replayable and strikes a comfortable level of challenge without being too easy or too difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: 185 hours on record. I do not have enough words to say how much I personally love this game. It’s so fun and has plenty of challenge for the average rouge-like enjoyer. Right not the games has a lot to offer but as a beta tester I can assure you it is about to offer a whole lot more. Buy this gem asap if you find it on sale. Please be sure to check out the prologue or demo (imma be honest no clue what the difference is) if you want to try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Glad to have seen this game through EA all the way to the official release! Shogun Showdown is a fun, tactical 2d turn-based combat with increasing dificulty where you'll want to play through quickly but also take your time to evaluate your positioning and incoming threats. Art style and music are appealing and gameplay will leave you itching for more. The characters feel different enough to make you want to try out different approaches. Overall a really generous buy for its listing price.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I played this a bunch when it was just on Ich.io so I had to part with some money eventually :) It's beautifully simple, the right amount of juice and SFX for a satisfying combat. Compared the itch.io version I can see that they've added a few quality of life things and a better tutorial for new players without ruining the core game loop.Strongly recommended. I would say that I would expect it to be in the <£7 section, I paid £8 and I probably wouldn't go up to £15 for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this, I was immediately hooked. Fun upgrades, challenging enemies and bosses, and enough variety between characters to keep you entertained. I worked my way through a lot of the content early on, so I'm eagerly awaiting it to come out of early access before I return to complete it fully.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Shogun Showdown has a balanced and unique puzzle combat system that you won't find in any other rouge like on the market. The aesthetic is great, the rougelike elements are well implemented and greatly improve the replay-ability of the game , and the game has that polish "X" factor where you can tell the developers care about the product they are making.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Re-reviewing this game after 1.0 because  is it wayyyyyy harder now, the normal game (i'd say from day 1-4) is still a really fun turn based strategy game, and although the later half of the game (day 5-6) is a LOT harder it still is possible and i managed to 100% complete it, before 1.0 that is.With the added day 7 which adds a new boss, it is wayyyyy harder to 100% complete this now, took me about 2-3 hours just to complete it  and you need to do it with all characters to get the "true mastery" achievement. Overall, i'm not saying that the game's bad, i'm just warning all the completionists out there that this will take a while to 100%, so you better have some good determination and brain power if you want to complete this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable turn based tactics.  Similar to Into the Breach in that you get forewarning of your enemy's actions and manipulating them to your advantage is key.  The roguelite progression is a little off as I write this; I thought the game was overall too easy but day 5 showed me otherwise.Edit: Endgame play is nicely balanced.  Day 7 is no joke.  Kudos.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I've had it for 3 days and already played 17 hrs. The gameplay is turn based, you can see what your opponents are going to do and plan accordingly. There are 4 unlockable characters and tons of unlockable moves and abilities. I love the pixel graphics as well. My only downside for this game is that sometimes you lose a run for really frustrating reasons but a 9/10 overall. (I am an actual human who eats, drinks, and breaths btw)
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: If you're reading reviews because you're considering buying this game, then play its demo!I thought the game was slightly more expensive than it should be, however, after "beating" it for the first time, a number of things were unlocked that made the run different and a lot harder. After "beating" it a second time, it happened again. There's more to Shogun Showdown than it meets the eye and it is indeed worth its full price. Great game, very pog.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo for this and was almost immediately sold on the idea of buying it. it reminds me of the great game HUNTDOWN, also an indie pixel-art goldmine -- it's not only FUN, it's got SOUL. it reeks of being the product of hard work by someone who gave a spit about gaming. it's simple, it's gorgeously designed, and the music is legitimately some of the most instantly memorable music I can remember hearing in a video game. each of the first four stages or so (that's as far as I've been able to get, I suck and blow at this game) each have their own killer, vibing and CLEVER music themes. I can't remember the last time I was this immediately impressed with an Indie game. probably not since Huntdown, actually. (maybe Vampire Survivors.) an instant classic in that "One more go" sort of way. it leaves you smiling. simple tactics, but a really good challenge. and again, just really REALLY great music. kudos, developer. kudos. thanks for this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly fun.  It is one of only 7 roguelite games on steam with an overwhelmingly positive reviews for a reason. I played the entire demo on a website that feels better if you scratch it (if you know what I mean - I'm not sure if I can put links or website names here) and completed absolutely everything there was to do.  But I didn't even realise that was just a demo (it was really long) and that there was a full game with a load more levels, characters, items, abilities etc!  Happy times!If I had one very tiny complaint it's just that the runs are quite long, and around 75% of the run my brain must get tired or something and I end up making stupid mistakes that usually kills me. But that's my stupid brain rather than a problem with the game.  I bloody love it. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: What's not to like about Shogun Showdown? I was originally here because I love games featuring a feudal Japanese aesthetic and I stayed because of the brilliant combat system. While I was initially unnerved by short turns, waits, and move queues, I grew to love the snappy action. This game is surprisingly complex despite its simple mechanics. It encourages increasingly elaborate moves and combos, allowing your avatar to dance across the field of battle. Nothing is more satisfying than killing three or four enemies in a turn with a few well-placed abilities. Or better yet, why not set your ENEMIES up to kill each other? Smoke bomb the attacking yumi sniper to taste his own medicine; yeet the spear man behind you into the wardens on the other side of the map. The possibilities are endless. Shogun Showdown is a fascinating game that rewards creative strategic thinking and forces the player to always think one step ahead of their adversaries. I would highly encourage this game to anyone that enjoys a good turn-based roguelike, a cool samurai game, or anyone looking to introduce a new friend to their favorites collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little strategy game. It is still early access and is lacking in story, but there's lots to like: - Lovely music and graphics. - Unusual combat system that enables satisfying combos. - Upgrade one of your weapons every few minutes. - Pleasantly minimalist, with gradually increasing complexity and difficulty. - Lots of achievement to encourage a variety of fun playstyles (speedrunning, combo killing, and no-hit runs). - Less bloated than Slay the Spire. There's only 6 (soon 7) difficulty levels, with 5 characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's addicting.I'm sad there is no co-op but I understand the gameplay would be hard to adapt for it. But devs, if you have an idea to adapt it, I'd love it and have a couple of friend who would buy this game.Basically, it's a turn-based roguelite strategy game. You take action at the same time as your enemies but you see what they are about to do.Everything is an action and there's a great diversity for it. You can even stack up to 3 action applied all at once. It feels like you are in a cqc fight.While in a run, you will get upgrades for your action applied only for the run like: freeze enemies, reduce cooldown, increase damage, damage nearby enemies, etc...The bosses are good enough for an early access and I keep forgetting it is an early access. It's that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I keep forgetting that changing direction costs a turn.  Wish there was the ability to toggle confirm actions.Otherwise really good, fun and fair roguelite.  Like a 2d and less RNG than fights in tight spaces.  You know what moves you have, when you can use them, and when they will be available.  No "deck" just actions and upgrades.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I've gotten to day 3 of 6 on the starting character. Days are like madness levels with extra content - they're harder and longer (ahem).It's fun, I like it, it's well worth playing a little of. The content (enemies, attributes, tiles (cards), relics) is all a bit limited, not suitable for tons of replay. There is a strong deck-building component, but the play itself is turn-based amd deterministic. It's like solving a little puzzle each turn.The puzzle nature is also because it's much more discrete - health pools for enemies start at 1-3 & you typically have 2-7 tiles, which feels very different than 60 health and a 30 card deck. I do prefer the bigger decks, but small has it's own flavor & is nice for variety.I enjoy it way more than Balatro personally, the content may be limited but it's still a lot more than endlessly tuning an addition/multiplication equation. Play-wise, I enjoy Roguebook more, and Obelisk less, although the latter's multiplayer & large content pool definitely help make up for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Has aspects of Slay the Spire and Into the Breach, but to me the combat feels stripped down to essentials and more satisfying and physical than in either of the others. I love the gorgeous pixel art, and the tricky choices it presents at every juncture. Good variety in weapons and enemies without getting bogged down in hard to understand mechanisms.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth it.  It scratches that FTL, Slay the Spire, vibe while doing something different.  Each fight is a puzzle, and with careful planning just about any situation is solvable.  Each time I die I am able to recognize where I went wrong, and then later on improve.  If you are considering, just get the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: During one of Steams special sales events I was looking to add a DLC from one of my favourite AAA titles.  By blind luck I stumbled upon this gem.  Two weeks later I don't even remember the DLC I was planning to play.Its considered Early Release, but I don't see any bugs.  It could use a story line to round off the game, but otherwise the combat system is amazing and extremely enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. I am a big fan of tactical roguelikes and this is by far one of the best that has come out in the last 3 years. Desperatley needs more content, but only because its so good i want to keep playing more. It is still in early access so hopefully, alot more coming. The game is very simple at its core, but very tactical the further along you get. Multiple builds, characters and is adaptable to beat any run you get into, no matter how bad it looks.Please buy this game, its incredible, polished and super fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I have played hours, upon hours, of Slay the Spire. This scratched an itch for a game for me I didn't know I had, the roguelite deck builder genre. Ever since, I have tried looking for that addictive '1 more run' game. I have found it, in Shogun Showdown. Experimenting with the tiles (abilities) to create the best combinations of them is a lot of fun, with different difficulty levels and characters to try out your strategies in. In short, a fun soundtrack, tight game play with a lot of depth to try out combinations and also the ascension system makes the game progressively more difficult so that you're consistently challenged, which adds to the high replayability of the game. Overall a really well polished game
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely well polished and tactical roguelite. If you like puzzling through turns and then puzzling through shops, this is the game for you. I picked this up on sale and immediately sunk 15 hours into it, making it well worth the money, and was a little surprised that I hadn't heard of it before. I can't stress enough how good the gameplay is, and the fact that it's got good pixel art and music with some snappy UI stuff is only a plus.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Very addictive! It ramps up the complexity as you delve deeper into the game. Whether you're repeating the first run before you beat the final boss (if you die you can buy tiles to appear in the next run via the initial shop keeper on the left of the screen) or unlocking the "second day" after defeating the final boss, you encounter tougher foes and more intricate mechanics. The art style and music are also really neat. The real challenge lies in crafting your tile deck (which controls your active abilities which are largely separate from your movement (as some affect that too), to match your preferred playstyle. Whether you're focusing on beefing up attack damage from a distance or leaning heavily into movement-based effects, flexibility is key. You've got to think on your feet, adapting to the upgrades available in shops and the choices presented at the end of each combat level.Highly recommend to turn based puzzle combat fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing turn based tactics game. Each attack tile feels unique and viable in its own way and the upgrades/relics let you further customise your build to really take advantage of their unique effects. Could definitely use some more content but with 6 difficulties, 4 characters and a bunch of new tiles you can unlock you get a solid 15+ hours of content which is pretty good for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: A turn-based strategy game with easy-to-learn mechanics and fantastic depth. Despite being early access right now, this game will already give you a full game's worth of enjoyment, and it's only getting better from here. I personally consider this a must-buy if you enjoy strategy and roguelite elements.Every action, movement and turnaround(!) takes a turn, after which enemies will also move. This seemingly simple principle creates a lot of opportunities for different types of attacks - they will move your character, they can be ranged, they can displace or turn around enemies, they may hit in front or behind you (or both). With the ability to also power up your weapons (reducing cooldown, adding poison or frost, increasing damage, etc.) and collect equipment, and the unique abilities of the different characters, there's a lot of different playstyles to work with and things to try.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, well made, simple, turn-based game. Wasn't quite my style to start but quickly grew on me. Music and sounds are great. Lots of fun tactics. Throwing enemies around with a jujitsu build was a blast. Only complaint is that 20 hours in and it's kinda run it's course. There are still plenty achievements to grind for, but it's getting repetitive. I guess you can gauge if that's worth 15 dollars to you. You will enjoy what they made for most of that time.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This outstanding title, while adhering to core tenets of the contemporary tactical roguelike genre, transcends its peers and establishes a new paradigm for the genre's future development. Having traversed a multitude of esteemed entries within this subgenre, I can confidently assert that this gem stands as the exemplar closest to achieving an idealized state of gameplay. The game's non-obvious synergies won me over.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible, simply incredible.A great little game at a reasonable price that manages to hold you for hours. It has a nice learning curve and the difficulty increases make you think it’s impossible at first but you still push through and defeat the Shogun. The updates they’ve done so far were nothing but awesome and I can’t wait for what they have to deliver next.The gameplay is truly unique, the soundtrack is an absolute banger and the pixel art is beautiful.Without wanting to get too technical with the gameplay (as I believe it should be experienced first hand) the game is missing some features other rogue likes offer such as customising a run and getting a bit more control of your luck when it comes to abilities. But that’s hopefully getting resolved in the upcoming updates.But even that is just a nitpick showing how little is missing from the complete package that this game is.Achievement hunting is also very fun
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: The game is built on very simple principles, but actually hides a lot of tactical depth.A great take on the roguelike genre. Already the first stages of the game make you feel that your character is becoming stronger, and the mechanics of upgrades and perks are clear and allow you to simply enjoy the game.Since pixel art holds a special place in my heart (I like it), I have absolutely no objections to the way the game looks. Because it just looks good!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best strategy indie game I've played. The mechanics are easy to understand, and so are the tiles or the enemy attack patters, nevertheless, it still represent quite a challenge sometimes, where you have to rely  mostly on your maths skill in order to create the perfect combo or to prevent getting hit. Every enemy is unique and so is the music, as they all correspond to the land they're assigned to. Overall, my favourite part of the game is by far the combination of the music while beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of a boss.It's only early access and I already love the whole game. I don't really have any complains, as in my 60h of gameplay I haven't found any bugs that affect the gameplay (Just one visual). So I'd say it's 100% recommendable if you are into this kind of base turn games
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: An innovative approach to the roguelike deckbuilder concept that doesn't require comparison to Slay The Spire (shocking!). It recreates the flow of martial arts movies by situation your character on a 2D board and requiring you to plan your position and attacks several moves in advance. Success feels like mastery, failure feels like utter defeat. Not one that I will sink hundreds of hours into, but absolutely an extremely fun game that I enjoyed. 4/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Shogun Showdown is up there with Slay the Spire and Into the Breach as one of the best roguelikes to date. Each combat is a wonderful series of decisions. You can manipulate enemies, dodge out of danger, and chain attacks together to pull off satisfying combos. Even after unlocking all the skills and characters, every run feels fresh, thanks to the variety of attacks and the clever upgrade system. The challenge is also there, especially at the highest difficulty level, where game knowledge and careful planning are essential to victory. The different achievements encourage you to try different styles of play, which drastically change how you have to approach the game. Aesthetically, the pixel art is on point. Each enemy and attack is instantly recognizable, and the UI is flawless. It's really a perfect game in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Slay the Spire but with movement? Yeah kind of. Shogun Showdown is a great roguelike and superb on the Steam Deck. Controller controls take a little bit of getting used to but it's one of those great on-the-go games as it's not too demanding on the SD's battery,For full thoughts in video format, consider checking out my review here:
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: A very well-polished game. Lower difficulties are a nice power trip, harder difficulties definitely require one to be careful but do not feel unfair or impossible. The different skills you can unlock over a run lead to interesting playstyles and combos. It's easy to pick up and drop if I'm just looking for a 15 minute break, but it's also fun to stick and complete a run if I have more time. New favorite.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers for unlocks ahead.This game is great, even being in early access it already feels complete. The game starts off deceptively simple. but quickly you will learn the depth of its systems.It feels amazing learning how to manipulate the enemies into moving where you want them to, it has a feeling of carefully setting up dominos, then with a flick of the finger they all fall down.  Cut to ribbons on their allies' blades.Every one of the tiles feels distinct. They all have their nuances that set them apart from all the others, even if some serve similar roles.I love how upgrades work in this game. Upgrades can slotted onto a tile that boost their damage, reduce cooldown, greatly raise one at the cost of the other. Other upgrades add secondary effects like freezing enemies, poisoning them, shocking all adjacent enemies in row.(Pro-tip, the Shock upgrade is AMAZING on tiles that hit multiple enemies at a time, like Spear or Scar Strike. Each enemy hit applies the shock damage)Each of the four characters all feel distinct from each other, even though they all share the same pool of tiles. Each character has their own starting load out, with a second you can unlock after completing some challenges, as well as their own unique movement ability.The wanderer can swap positions with the enemy in front of them. The Ronin can push the enemy in front of them, dealing damage if they hit something. The Shadow moves as far forward as possible whenever moving, and can phase through entire lines of enemies. The Shadow feels a bit finicky to me, but when he cooks its some of the sickest movement you will get.My personal favourite is the Jujitsuka (probably spelled wrong, sue me). She can throw the enemy behind her forward. Its very similar to the Ronin, but different enough to be very distinct. Her starting load out is also my favourite because of her Scar Strike Tile.Scar Strike hits every enemy that isn't at full health. This encourages a fighting style where you "tag" as many enemies as you can, then striking them all down at once with Scar Strike with 4 damage upgrades.The music is very good, but I do wish there was some more boss music. Even the final fight with the Shogun uses the same boss theme as every other one.Speaking of bosses, they are also very good. Every boss has a distinct way of fighting that sets them apart. Though sometimes they will hit you with something you have no chance of avoiding, such as as attack that lets them sprint across the stage and stab you. The only real way to counter some of these is to always be ready for the boss to throw out the ONE attack.The only serious criticism I have is the game doesn't do a great job teaching you how to slot your tiles into the attack queue. For the first few days I played Shogun Showdown, I thought you had to drag the tiles into the Queue, but actually you just click the tile and it will slot itself in.This doesn't SOUND like a big deal, but an issue I kept having was that if i didn't PERFECTLY line it up with the tile slot, it would advance the enemy turns without even slotting the tile in, and this caused multiple deaths.I haven't struggled with this issue for a while, but I don't know if that's because the game was patched, or I just got gud.Overall, solid 8 out of 10 game. I will keep playing it and greatly look forward to future updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: It's a gem of a tactical roguelike, challenging and fair that will put your brain to work. You will need to build right to get all the tools you need to deal with various situations. But most importantly plan each of your actions in combat, prepare your weapons and position yourself right to kill without being hit.The gameply loop is simple: you attack cards you can put in a queue (spend a turn), move, turn around in 2D battlefield, or spend all attacks in queue at the same time. Use combo right to prevent enemies in the backline to hit you after the front line is down and get bonuses. Through the game upgrade tiles with CD, damage and other effects.Music is cool, visual style works well, and overall a very interesting idea.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I've played 30 hours of this over the last four days... send help. It's great on steam deck! This game is an excellent Roguelite; probably the best one I've played since StS. It's a great roguelite deckbuilder with a focus on movement and orientation relative to something like StS or Vault of the Void. The other reviews document the gameplay well, so I'll just talk about how long it took me to do everything since that's what I care about when I buy a game.So far, I think it's reasonable to expect at least 20 hours of really fun gameplay out of this even for someone who doesn't like roguelites, but I imagine my playtime will get much higher as I like the repetition.10h: first win15h: unlocked all characters25h: unlocked all tiles and skills(I'll update it if/when I win day 6 or get 100%)There are some features I'd like to see implemented:- The game is missing a run statistic page, it would be nice to review my winning decks as it helps me learn what works and think about why it worked. It can be hard to remember what exactly happened over dozens of runs. Also, statistics are fun in general. - Mod SupportLastly, and this is the only "con", but it might be too easy? I've gotten a few of more difficult accomplishments in only a few dozen hours. I may have been spoiled by StS, as that game kept me occupied with it's ascensions for hundreds of hours, but I'm worried that once I get really good at this game it won't be as challenging as it is now. I am only at day 4 (out of 6) and I am missing the no consumable and one-way achievements, so I'm hoping that the higher difficultly levels will be more challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 19 hours in. Do I have enough of this game? Not at all. Did I think I'd play 19 hours of this when I started? Not at all. This gem of a game is VERY addicting. Doing nice plays and combos feels VERY satisfying and rewarding. Play it, and keep playing for at least 1 1/2 hours. At first I thought it was too easy, and not complex at all. That changed quickly. Amazing game, I hope they will update this a lot. 100% reccomend.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, has decent amount of content now, but could use some more variety IMO. The different classes are too similar (they do not have different decks/tiles a la. STS) overall. For the most part this is a puzzle game, which is great IMO, but also can get a bit easy when you figure things out. The days (ie ascension a la STS) don't really bring the difficulty up much until Day 6.  which really just drops your health in a way where any one major mistake or two small mistakes is a run ender.The jump in difficulty at Day 5 (enemies have +1 hp) is pretty obnoxious as it makes most run beginnings tedious (you just have to rinse repeat multiple times since your tiles dont do enough damage to kill enemies).  Lastly, a warning overall, but your chars feel MUCH WEAKER after Day 5 because enemy HP goes up. this was pretty disappointing as some run RNG just doesnt give you damage upgrades and can lead to some really...slow...game....play. I would recommend a 10x bump in numbers here so tiles can do a bit more damage relative to enemy HP, while still keeping the ergonomics of the game. Lastly, there are other options for increasing the difficulty without bumping up enemy HP like this (for example more damage, or higher rate of quick elites which can put a lot of pressure on players, etc.)Good game overall though, will be coming back to it especially if they add more days and content.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing concept of a game with a great aesthetic. Simple to understand but deep with complexity, the perfect pick up n’ play on the go that was made for the steam deck. A 2-d grid game with emphasis on position mechanics through cards, I really appreciate how you do not get punished for having "excess" cards. I also really appreciate this game supporting fast game play
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: The simplicity of Shogun Showdown has everything to please: simple to start with and incredibly satisfying when your plan executes as you've calculated. Don't let its simplicity fool you though, the game is not as easy as it seems. If you are hesitating because the game is in Early Access, sincerely just don't think twice and get it now! It's already pretty good and quite addictive! I play it on mostly on my Steamdeck and it's a perfect tactical games for that platform! Strongly recommended if you look for a satisfying turn-based combat game such as Fights in Tight Spaces, minus the deckbuilder part and a faster pacing.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Play the demo.I already think this a full game.Suggestions:Super fast replay mode at the end of matches.Giving the characters some actual identity beyond their special skills and starting tiles. Increasing difficulties are really trivial because if you're winning you've probably already broken the game. I'd suggest introducing damage types or something to mix things up.Workshop, some way to make a custom tile or something. Random character. Dailies. Etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great so far! The combat uses a few simple elements to create a large amount of tactical depth. I had a LOT of fun creating combo attacks and making my enemies accidentally hit each other. Not to mention, it also manages to be faster-paced than other turn-based tactics games (slow gameplay won't turn me off a game per say, but it can get annoying after a while)The rogue-like elements are also fun. During my first run alone, there were many a decision to be made; which attack should get this upgrade? should i reroll the upgrade instead? which one of these attacks should i pick up? and more.Overall, this game is already looking to be great and I'm happy I brought it on a whim. Congrats to the developers!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: i have played since the alpha on itch (i reccomend you go there to try it, then maybe the demo to see the vision for the game) and i instantly fell in love. i like turn based stuff, easy to learn hard to master, japanese-style weapons & character designs and ways to create op combos, this game has it all. i highly reccomend this game and cannot say how much i reccomend you try it, it has 6 difficulties, the next one being unlocked after you defeat the previous one. i have not yet done the 6th "day" and am still playing this game, i have been here pretty much for the whole ride, got the game the same week it launched and this is all to say:give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Might be too early a review as I only have a couple hours in the game. First impressions is the gameplay loop is fantastic. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: A game that perfectly shows the impact of having a clear indication of actions. As I played the game and balanced out weapon cooldown and attacks, the strategy of having friends kill friends felt really clean and natural. Even as the game went on every enemy had a pattern that could be easily found and used against them. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This is an awesome game. I've never played a turn based strategy game of this kind before. Very well made. Even though it's early access, it feels like a finished game. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent a lot of time  playing the Demo version of this on itch.io before it ever came to Steam, so my hours aren't really representative of my time with the game.It's a solid, lightweight, puzzley deck-builder tactics game. Not my top choice, but it's still pretty great.There's nothing much to complain about here -- the genre it's in is simply very competitive, and this title isn't among the absolute best entries, imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Plenty to love about this game, fun weapons, combos, and the turn design is fun. once you get the hang of it, you can feel the combat flow, its fun to upgrade weapons and see what new combos, you can pull off. the different characters add some complexity to the flow of combat. looking forward to updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, Like everyone else wrote, it evokes Into the Breach while maintaining its own unique flavor. Shogun Showdown is challenging to learn and feels impossible at first, but once you start to pick up on enemy patterns the game really opens up. Some of the bosses and achievements that looked impossible at first start to feel doable and it's great. The game is still small but there's plenty to do. I finally beat day 5 with each of the characters and I'm working on getting some of the crazier achievements. The achievements are all challenging and varied. Can't wait to see where the game goes!I would eventually love to see more variety in everything: enemy design, day difficulty, bosses, weapons, and shop items. I also hope we can do something interesting with all that skulls we collect. Given that the game is in early access I'm excited to see all of the above and more! Even if this is all we get it's an absolute gem and worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Very well designed a simple game mechanics, no bugs after 24 hours, very challenging but not impossible, fun and enjoyable, a lot of replay value despite the content is not as rich yet as Dead Cells. Hopefully the game is still early access so we can expect a little bit more. Highly recommended even in its current stage.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Not a lot of content, so I recommend getting this game during a sale, but very fun and addicting game. Going into this blind is very fun, and it takes time to get used to the concept of the game, making a perfect challenge. There is also a lot of extra content after the first time you beat the game, like more optional levels, different modifiers that get harder as you beat them, and more characters that have different starting weapons and different support moves, kind of like you have to re-learn the game in a new character.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awsome and anyone that says its bad or "repetitive" bc they keep dying is just bad at the game. There are some things i'd love to see in the game quite soon like widescreen resolution cuz now its limited to 1920x 1080 but i got no other complaints. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game play, amazing progression and replay-ability, literally my only complaint is it's too rng which is easily fixable with something like a more detailed warning on unit type or placement when a wave comes in, or something similar. Other wise it's a really fun strategy game. A few things I wish they would add would be some sandbox mode since tiles and stuff are completely rng and more characters/achievements (game is fairly short all things considered, went from never played a game like this to 100% in less than 40 hours) these things aren't required but would definitely add to the game.Overall I would score it an 8/10As of 1.0 release I can say the game has a lot of content with tons of variety now so game length is not a problem any more but the final boss on day 7 is just straight up unfair, pretty much requiring certain tiles/skills to win so please nerf it a little devs. Also please fix the spawning, Garanteed damage or death on day 6/7 isn't fun. I can win 99% of the time on day 5 but only like 60% on day 6 and it's almost always because there was nothing I could do, please fix this.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I ASSUME!!! They will add infinite runs at some point but the base mechanics are VERY solid. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: As a Slay the Spire, Tower Tactics Liberation and Dicey Dungeon fan, this game may be my new favorite.  It's a blast to play, where you can play a perfect run only to get sloppy last minute in your hubris and burn the end of your run, which you would deserve.  The game doesn't cheat you, it's not unfair, and the challenge is always there.  Cannot recommend enough, if you like roguelike games with a card aspect, this is the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: So it feels like a very simple game at first, but to get anywhere at all requires you to think about the next move and at least the one after that. I’m not brilliant at this game, but a death always feels like it was your own fault - and so round you go again! I’ll definitely be double dipping if it comes to console as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the greatest roguelike is you are looking for quick action, the average run won't last much more than 30-40 minutes. Pleasing visuals, amazing soundtrack, and plenty of fun builds to make.However, there ARE times when RNG wills crew you over, and there won't be anything that you can do about the situation with your current deck and cooldowns, other than to accept taking damage, or even straight up losing the game. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this when I was sick for a few days and it's the deepest a video game has infiltrated my brain stem since I was  a child.  It's like if chess was a super nintendo swordfight. One of the best things I've ever played.  Feels like you're composing choreography instead of executing a fight scene, which, for a sleepy dork with no reflexes, is exactly my speed.  I will say tho, this, like most great roguelites, is genuinely a little too hard for me and I'm probably gonna plateau and give up without accessing half the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what to say other than it's a great game. It's very addictive, there's plenty of replayability and it has a free demo! Plus it runs great on the Steam Deck and can easily be picked up and be starting a run in less than a minute. I only just realised that this is in early access so I think that says something for the quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Very good title! I'm probably gonna pour hours into this. The controls on controller are somewhat finnicky and every misplay is punishing, so there's definitely a learning curve (at least on controller) to not do unintended actions. But it's fun and so far I always felt like I lost due to my own bad plays.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: It's a simple, but highly polished experience. It's easy to understand the basics, and all the info needed to learn and improve is simple to access and review. Difficulty is lower than average for a roguelike, enough so that winning your first run is doable, but there are a lot of different characters to play as, and multiple unlockable starting loadouts for each of them, so the game has enough variety to keep you playing for a long time. Finally, this game can run on a potato, so anyone who is interested can play this, and I recommend you do if you're interested.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most amazing games I have ever played, and it still is in Early Access. Can't imagine how many more hours I will get out of it when it reaches V1.0.It combines turn-based action with rogue speed, and stands tall next to the likes of StS and Into the Breach. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and interesting game, if you like tactics/puzzle kind of games.It's a bit different version of turn based, where multiple enemies will take action at once, if they can. But you can overcome this by planning up to three actions at once. This is definitely a fresh take on the genre for me.And it all being wrapped into a standard rougelite package makes it even better.There are a few different characters with different special skill and starting weapons, and there are a lot of weapons and upgrades you can earn along the run.I've encountered a minor bugs, like freezes.I expect this to be polished more and new content being added when out of early access.Overall a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Just excellent. Simple puzzle-like combat that feels extremely rewarding to work through with the tools you gather. Perfect difficulty where dying almost always feels like your fault, the only complaint here is when enemy waves spawn in you get no indication of where, so it's possible to get stuck then get stuck which sucks but can be kind of played around. But since playthroughs are (or should be) less than an hour, it doesn't feel as bad as other rougelikes that can make you feel like your time is being thrown away. Attractive art, very chill and fitting soundtrack, so easily worth the price, especially on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Shogun Showdown takes the positional gameplay format of such games like Into The Breach and Alina of the Arena and distills it down to the perfect size. Especially for the price, this is a hell of a value. On its face, it's an extremely simple concept. When you take an action, your opponent does as well. Given the small battle arena, this means you need to carefully consider each move you make in order to avoid attacks or an opponent's movement. You can queue three attacks at once which allows you to hit combos giving you extra money or consumables. RNG is there, but it's at the right level so you aren't screwed by unfortunate spawns like in Into The Breach. Fantastic Steam Deck game too!The later stages have a ton of enemy waves to get through. If you don't have the proper amount of damage in your deck, this could lead to very very long battles. Also, the hookshot enemies suck, but that's just because they're easy to overlook and not plan against. Shogun Showdown is a must own at its current price. It's a wonderful experience that gives that big brain feeling. Nothing in it is unfair, it runs wonderfully on the Steam Deck, and the gameplay and style are perfect. Kudos to the devs. They made an excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Games really cool and unique especially for the price, it also has a demo which lets you play a decent part of the game to get a feel. It is something you could probably 100% in a day (as of right now) if you play it a lot but for the price its definitely worth it as a game to quickly pop in for a quick run or two to kill some time. The devs are pretty consistent with content updates making for a generally cool lil community of people.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pinnacle of simplicity and depth combined. Like many others have said, its a theme combination of games like "Into the Breach" (RNG and strategy elements), a Deck Builder and retro rogue-like all in one. It'll be slightly steep of a learning curve initially but damn is it addictive and its ONLY IN EARLY ACCESS!!! This is more polished than some AA or even AAA games have been released with. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Easy to understand, simple to play, and with the combo system and cool moves you can make, I tend to forget that it's turn-based. Cinematic and casual but rewarding for those of us that enjoy customizing builds and making daring moves (that can't actually end up hurting you in real life when they go wrong). Well worth the small price, even at this early stage of development.Out of early access and my review still holds
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Very simple concept, seriously refined excecution. At first sight it seems very easy, but if you try for a no hit run, it quickly becomes harder than it seems. _childDocuments_.review: EARLY ACCESS REVIEW AS OF 19/11/2023:Wow, it's quite incredible how the game just came out 6 months ago - in early access - and it's already THAT polished. The basics are all there and if the game never changed from here, it'd already be a good game and recommendable. Especially noteworthy is how the game manages to bake the learning/familiarization organically into the player experience. I was eased into the game and roped into wanting to play more at all times. Cookies for the devs!Yet, there are drawbacks which'll likely keep the game at tens, but not hundreds of hours of game fun - good but not great. The regular enemies are imo actually already close to perfect as they are. There is the obvious and to be expected balancing and tweaking requirements, defo on the weapons and boss side. Here, I'll only mention my biggest points:- Weapon Enchantments: Apart from some rare exceptions, those are not underutilized. They are very costly and do not do enough.A standout is the "ice"-effect. I don't understand why some bosses enemies are immune to it - that decreases the range of viable builds so much and so unnecessarily.- Skills (i.e. relics in Slay the Spire): The biggest let-down and bottleneck for game-improvement! Some are kinda overpowered, many don't do anything. Most importantly, they don't INTERACT which your builds so much. I think if that could be fixed wholesale, the game would be ready for the next tier, aiming for level 9000.Lastly, all stages feel the same, only the featured enemies change. That's okay, but could be better. Maybe some environmental stuff could come into play, like cover you could erect or lava fountains you could trigger or so? This must obviously be carefully considered to keep things reasonably predictable, but maybe there's something there. Oh, and also please do something more with the music...In summary, this is awesome already and I highly recommend to all tactics-afficionados!

_childDocuments_.review: This is in the genre of 'easy to learn, hard to master'. It's also a roguelite and something of a cardbuilder. Lastly, it's got some minimalist elements to it that I really enjoy.The basic game play is that you have tiles which deal a certain amount of damage and have a number of turns before they can be used again (the marks at the bottom of the tile). Doing one of the following counts as a turn: turning around, moving, using your special ability, adding a tile to your attack queue, attacking, or waiting. Your enemies will be doing various actions as you perform your turns. The idea is to kill all of the enemies on the stage, losing as little health as possible.As far as tiles go, the most I've seen is 6 tiles max at the end of a run--it's less about having a ton of tiles and more about utilizing the ones you have well.I haven't unlocked the last character yet, but the special abilities are: Wanderer--switch places with the enemy in front; Rohin--push the enemy in front of you as far back as possible dealing 1 point of damage to the enemy and the enemy he hits (0 damage if the enemy hits the back wall); Shadow--phase through the enemy in front of you.Your tiles can be upgraded throughout the run. Mostly this consists of increasing damage or lowering cooldown (or some combo like -3 cooldown -1 damage, +1 damage +1 cooldown). There are special effects though. One type of upgrade adds 3 cooldown but you can add the card to your attack queue without using a turn. There are also enchantments (+3 cooldown): poison--deal 1 damage to enemy at the end of each turn for 3 turns; freeze--prevent enemies from taking a turn for 3 turns; shockwave--deal 1 damage to all adjacent enemies; perfect strike--reset cooldown immediately if you dealt just enough damage to kill the enemy (dealt 2 damage to an enemy with 2 life).There are also skills you can purchase during your runs. Some examples are; start fights with a shield -2 health, when an enemy deals damage to you, deal the same damage back, shields persist between fights, inventory slots +1.Consumables are rather basic but nice; gain shield (prevent next damage), recover 3 health, immediate cooldown of tiles, poison all enemies, curse all enemies (x2 damage received on next hit).As far as meta-progression you can unlock additional slots in the shops and you can buy new tiles.The character differences are subtle but enough to ensure unique runs between them. Each character has their own special ability and 2 tiles to start the game.I really enjoy the hidden depth to this game. There are a lot of ways you can build your run around--enemies can kill each other, ranged, close quarters, etc.I've beaten the game on day 1 (normal) but there is still a lot of content for me to get through. Beating day 2 will unlock the fourth character, and I still have a number of tiles to unlock. More importantly, I still need to learn how to master the game.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I know the term 'Indie Gem' gets tossed around a lot. But this game is deserving of that title (and probably a LOT more attention than what it is getting). Gameplay is deceptively simple. After each action, your opponents move. Battles are completed on a series of tiles that vary in length, from 12 tiles to 6 tiles. Movement is done on a horizontal plane. While this may sound restrictive, it means that every battle is a brain scratching puzzle. As you progress through the rogue-like structure of the game, you gain new ability tiles which allow you to handle harder battles. Abilities can be upgraded to near game-breaking levels but never so much that it doesn't feel like a challenge. Also, everytime you beat the Shogun, the game gives you a new day, with even greater challenges like enemies with more health, lower consumable drops and reduced character health. Which gives you more excuses to try and see if that game-breaking combo still works in future runs.Is this the next FTL/ITB? That depends on how much hype it generates. So yeah, Imma add my voice to the hype train. Lets give this game the recognition it deserves!Also, the soundtrack is KICKASS. Here's the link to the artist's Youtube: Oscar di Mondogemello: You're welcome

_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Shogun showdown is an unlikely combination of Deckbuilder (Slay the Spire) x turn by turn tactics with perfect information (Into the Breach) x fantasy medieval Japanese setup (Sekiro).Through strength, finesse and subterfuge, your Wanderer / Ronin / Shadow has to  and cleanse these shadow-stricken lands from evil.Whether you prefer to jump back and forth at the beat of the music, or methodically study enemy move sets during active pause to get the opposition , the game is already superfun to play in EA and likely to improve with final release. (+) "Just right" level of difficulty, with the challenge tiles / achievements providing . After you've bonked enemies through sheer power of blades, or rained a barrage of shurikens and poisoned arrows from a safe distance, it's refreshing to turn into a puppet master, wreak havoc and mischievously let them turn on themselves.(+) Good intra-run variance and diversity of playstyles, rewarded by (+) Enemy variety is well thought-out and is able to counter the player if you have a blind spot in your strategy.(+) Pixel art and music are decent and do a lot for immersion.(+) With already 3 playable characters and 2 load-outs for each, there's already several ways to show the Shogun who's boss. (-) My biggest peeve: . In the best Deckbuilders, sometimes the best choice is not to accept the reward, as it would dilute your deck with unwanted filler. Having the option to refuse the proposed reward and get paid in gold / random potion would have been an excellent addition. (-) Lack of content to be unlocked: after some point your skull currency accumulates without a use case.(-) Limited boss diversity: apart from the 4th boss where 2 options are available and choice of who to face is left to the player, the others are fixed. (-) Some rare occurrences where damage can't be avoided. Would have loved if the balancing made it possible to perfect every run, and know that each time I take damage, it's because of a fault of my own.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun little strategy game with clean design and smooth mechanics. The content is a little on the lighter side, but it's still in Early access so that's understandable. Honestly it'd be worth the price even if they didn't add anything else, but I'm sure we'll get more content by the full release.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: It's an excellent little 1 unit tactical game - very clever game play that's stripped down far enough that it's almost a puzzle game each encounter, but in a good way, and since there is character progression between each encounters, it's much more than a puzzle title overall. There is enough depth, it's easy to get into, and it's just fundamentally fun. My only gripe is that it's too short - with a game this fun I could happily work my way through 5x more content or more. That sort of complaint indicates just how great the game is, because there are plenty of experiences where you end up slogging through to the end, or never get over the hump bothering to get into it! The game not overly difficult, particularly for a roguelite, just lots of fun, and leverages what it's good at rather than trying to be something it's not. Just really outstanding game design. Shogun showdown stands out amid a sea of cookie-cutter generic tactical roguelikes. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely promising; got hooked in minutes. Difficulty curve is gentle enough for a filthy casual like me. Of course you can crank it up and up if that's your preference. _childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best combat systems ever in a roguelike. Everything about the game is great and I can't recommend it more. _childDocuments_.name: Shogun Showdown

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game! Just finished it and had tons of fun with all three characters. The gaming mechanics are simple but really thought through, graphics and soundtrack are amazing and every character has an entirely unique playstyle - seriously the best game I've played in ages.I am a big fan of rogue-likes and deck builders. If you are too this game is definitely for you. Its a nice blend of both genres with none of the parts being too dominant. So instead of being a clone of a different game it feels like the creators did something new here. Another reason I recommend the game is that you can pick different playstyles to play it according to your own taste. It can feel like a mix of chess and STS when playing strategically and finishing with as little turns as possible or like an action game when trying to get the speedrunner achievement - and be quite an intense when doing both at the same time :DI seriously can't believe this is still early access since its already better than a lot of finished titles out there. Really looking forward to the developers adding more content over the coming months.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a lot of fun with this little gem. I stumbled across by complete accident when I bought another game that bundled this in with it. You play as a ninja fighting other ninja masters of different varieties and abilities. You have to strategically plan your attacks and move on the little tiles to make kills and avoid damage. The meta-progression in this game is very fun and I enjoy all the little upgrades I earn when clearing a level and buying items in shops. In a lot of games of this nature I sometimes feel the upgrades and artifacts you obtain don't always feel like they make much of a difference but not here. In Shogun Showdown, you can actually become OP with many of the upgrades you obtain. If you enjoy turn based strategy rogue likes, this game is definitely one to try.
