_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game because I loved Road 96. But I dunno what the hell went wrong with this game. It don't feels like the first one, the "skate parkour qte music thing" totally kills it for me. As others already said in their review, it feels like it suppose to be a mobile game. The world feels empty and the characters are shallow. The only two good things about the game are the music and that it runs very well (for a Unity game). Anyway, for a Road 96 fan I can't really recommend it, unless its on sale for at least 50% of the price. Dear devs, please make your next game more like the original Road 96 was. Because that game was really really good.
_childDocuments_.name: Road 96: Mile 0

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how to feel about this game. First of all I want to make it very clear that this is NOT a bad game by any means and I did enjoy it. The game play is relatively fun, the music is still good, and the story is decent. The issue comes from the fact that this is a step down from the original game in practically every way. This game could have been so much better than it was. Going from an amazing adventure game with multiple paths, good atmosphere and (in my opinion) a good depiction of a corrupt dictatorial regime to a much more linear, skating rhythm game is a heavy letdown. As someone who puts Road 96 in my top 15 favorite games of all time, I can't help but say that I was a little disappointed and you probably will be too. That being said, if you want to know what led up to the events of the first game, maybe get this on sale, and definitely get the About a Girl ebook, it's pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Road 96: Mile 0

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original Road 96 and reviewed it . It told a beautifully poignant tale of a desperate bid for freedom, showing the complexities of human nature through a series of scenes and side-characters that felt raw and believable. Mile 0, by contrast, is its foil. Except for the last scene, it’s shallow, with soulless writing, and vacuous characters – an absurd and immature cartoon that arrogantly and undeservedly dares to bear the name of its grand and heartfelt predecessor, sinking in stark inferiority to its former title’s lofty heights.• GeForce GTX 1660Ti• 8GB DDR4@1330MHz• i5 9300H @2.4GHz• HDD 7200RPMAt 1080p, Mile 0 ran well over 100FPS constantly. I experienced no bugs or glitches, which makes this one of the only positive things I can say for the game.Mile 0 plays a lot like Road 96, and other similar games like Life is Strange. There are small sets you can explore, though they are often linear and lead to cutscenes and dialogue choices that drive the narrative. And that’s fine – games like this are a vessel for a story, and it is the story you play them for. I wouldn’t have minded if this was it, but for reasons unbeknownst to me, they added a minigame to Mile 0 that sadly constitutes about half of the entire game.It is essentially Subway Surfers – a mobile game – you are jumping over, or ducking under obstacles collecting combos and points in what is meant to be a skating session with the game’s protagonists. I didn’t dislike this. I  it. It was tacky and cheap. The achievements are nearly all tied to them so to 100% the game you have to perform well in each, which as a completionist frankly sucks. And bafflingly some of the story is told from within this via some dialogue, yet they’re unwanted filler content: unrealistic and absurd, and littered with stupid quick-time events.Mile 0 doesn’t know what it wants to be, and it ends up being rubbish. On the one hand it’s an arcade mobile game making a lousy attempt to be trendy, but on the other hand it’s the prequel to a deep and contemplative narrative game set against the backdrop of a political dystopia but isn’t clever enough to make you think, and never puts you in a position where you really have to, unlike the first game.Mile 0 ends up being worse than the dystopia it wants to portray, making a mockery of the severity of its own setting. It is immature in all its facets and lost my favour very quickly because of this. The final act, though better, was not enough to constitute a redemption.Mile 0 strikes me as written by a naïve teenager. It screams mediocrity so loud it’s painful, as we’re forced to endure the asinine dialogue between two characters we have no reason to care about. It’s not that there is any real complexity to be read between the lines here either. Rather, nothing much is said. Conversation flows somewhat awkwardly and while this could be forgiven a few times as the natural way in which the characters communicate, it happens so often that one wonders if it’s the best the writers were capable of.The plot of Road 96 was heartfelt and realistic enough to be believable – a wave of teenagers fleeing the border for a new life. This is mentioned in Mile 0, too, but the story doesn’t build a convincing dystopia to escape from; the protagonists live an irresponsible life of petty crime, and the tyranny of the government comes over not as a sinister, evil political machination, but rather a cartoon joke dreamt up by a child. There is not the depth or intelligence here that the first game so benefited from.Some of the side characters from Road 96 make an appearance, which on the one hand I was glad to see, but there is so little expansion on the events of Road 96 that Mile 0 almost doesn’t feel it was set in the same world beyond a few hollow references to the Wall of ’86, and the raising of a few names familiar to the first game – a tragically missed opportunity, especially with the characters who were hinted to have deep backstories in Road 96.Some of the choices strangely affect consequences, too. In one case I was deemed to have lost support for the revolution because I asked about the safety of my parents. Another time, I was thinking on something to myself in one of the game’s scenes, but the thought had consequences. Both implicit suggestions by the game are absurd: that one cannot care for their family  support a revolution; and that one cannot explore an idea without it affecting their beliefs. These false dichotomies are the sorts of conclusions only fools reach, as the intelligent recognise nuance.Only at the end of the game, in the final short chapter, after hours of drudgery through those horrid skating scenes and shallow dialogue, is there  of the charm that made the first game. The camera familiarly pans up from the road, and there a scene unfolds that just managed to stir my emotions, and set the stage for where we meet Zoe in the first game. Just for a few minutes, Mile 0 showed it didn’t  forget the source material. But it wasn’t enough – not nearly – to redeem itself.Mile 0 is stylised, like the first game, although I never found it looked as good. It has a distinctly cartoon feel about it, and while Road 96 did too, it managed to be eerie and beautiful; serene and ugly, all when the game’s narrative required it. Mile 0 just looks low-quality. Save for one or two scenes, it didn’t set the mood nearly as well as the first game. The soundtrack couldn’t save Mile 0 from its mediocrity either. Used to great effect in the original game to draw out emotion. It’s not that it’s unfitting to the game’s genre or setting, it’s just that it has no great writing or characters to complement, and so isn’t elevated by anything. The fact that I didn’t personally like many of the tracks might account for my lack of praise here, but I also didn’t like most of the tracks in the last game either, and despite this could still (and did) praise their power in making the game the great experience it was. For a game so centred around the beat of music, Mile 0 misses nearly every beat that gave the first game its heart. Mile 0 is an absurdly comical game that is not funny, portrays a political dystopia as a caricature, and tells the tale of two teenagers who don’t feel like they understand the slightest thing about the political world they find themselves in. It is not made with nearly the same love or intelligence as the first game, and for so much of its runtime there are no reasons to care about anyone or anything that happens.It is a pitiful prequel to the far superior Road 96. It has all the grace of the average mobile game; the creativity of a party-political broadcast; the believability of a politician’s promise and the charm of a newsreader. So little of the deep, humanist struggle for a better world that made the first game powerful and memorable found its way into Mile 0 until the final scene, where it was too little too late. It wastes your time with boring minigames and hollow dialogue, squandering its chance to give a moving catalyst to the events of the original game with all except the last act, which cannot atone for the drudgery that came before. You can spend your money on better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: is a prequel to , and you take control of two recurring characters, Zoe (from the first game) and Kaito (from ), and the gameplay mainly consists of Musical Rides and exploring White Sands, a gated community in a divided nation called Petria that is controlled by a tyrant/dictator in 1996. To avoid any confusion, I’ll be calling this game  and the first game .✔️ A compelling story that introduces more memorable characters, as well as delving deeper into the backstories of recurring ones from the previous game.✔️ The new Musical Rides offer a fun experience, made even better by the fantastic soundtrack that accompanies them. They are also replayable.✔️ Beautiful visuals with a 90s aesthetic.❌ Most choices feel insignificant and with no real consequences❌ The ending feels forced and out of place.❌ Experienced some annoying graphical glitchesInstead of controlling random teen hitchhikers who were trying to escape the country through Road 96,  has you play two characters; Zoe, the minister’s daughter and an important character in the original game that you encounter on your journey to Road 96, and Kaito, another recurring character who first appeared in , Digixart’s first game, and lives in the slums with his parents who are part of the revolutionists. Both characters are best friends and they usually hang out in a half constructed building.The game takes place in White Sands, a divided community where the rich elites and poor workers live, or as the dictator calls it “the most luxurious place to live in Petria”. Basically, the story is Kaito’s attempt to convince Zoe that the dictator, government, police and her father are corrupt, and that Petria is not a perfect utopia but far from it, and at the same time Kaito and his parents are trying to find a way to escape Petria.Each character in the game has their own spectrum or meter, which is displayed on the top left of the screen. This meter is affected by your dialogue options and gameplay actions, and varies depending on the character. For example, Zoe has a Certainty vs Doubt meter, where choosing to deny Kaito's attempts to convince you that the government is not corrupt and that Petria is a perfect country will move the meter towards "Certainty" (which is represented by the shape of a home). Conversely, choosing to agree with Kaito will move the meter towards "Doubt." Kaito, on the other hand, has a Revolutionist vs Doubt meter.That being said, most of the actions won't have significant consequences beyond affecting the meter. For instance, ripping a propaganda poster or choosing a dialogue option that supports the revolution while talking to a police officer won't lead to any immediate consequences.Unfortunately, there are no branching paths; if Zoe's meter towards certainty is maxed out, it will not influence her story arc. However, it does influence Kaito's story arc, and the game features four distinct endings for him that depend on the meter readings of both characters. There’s also a final “showdown” between Kaito and Zoe, and it was a cringe anti-climatic anime-style fight, and it won’t alter the ending in any way, so it was entirely pointless.Overall, the voice acting in  is well done, and the character animation and lip sync are impressive. While the writing can feel cringe at times, it's a realistic portrayal of teen conversations as I’ve even heard far worse from real teens. The game features four acts, which took me roughly 4.5 hours to complete.Each act of the story features musical rides that are reminiscent of popular mobile games like Temple Run, Subway Surfers, and Digixart's first game, Lost in Harmony. The rides will have you play as Zoe, Kaito or both interchangeably, and you run through a musical track where you collect points in order to achieve the highest score. There are 10 tracks total and they play a role in the game's story and world-building. While they are relatively easy, achieving a specific score is not required to progress in the game. All musical rides can be replayed from the menu. You can also explore White Sands; you can talk to almost all NPCs, there are a few optional minigames that you can find and play, you can spray-paint on posters and certain walls (pro or anti government illustrations), you can collect cassette tapes (songs from the soundtrack) that are hidden throughout the world, as well as stickers of the recurring characters from .The art style of  has a retro-inspired aesthetic of the 1990s. Like the visually stunning , the game's world feels alive and immersive. That being said, I experienced a lot of graphical glitches, particularly towards the end of the game; the weather looked very ugly and distorted, as well as the foliage if you look close enough. While these glitches were not very common, they were pretty distracting.The soundtrack has a diverse collection of music with different genres and styles, and they are great to listen to. My favorite has to be “Land Locked Heart” by The Midnight. Most of the songs are featured in the 10 musical rides.While I was initially disappointed that  wasn't a road trip game like its predecessor, and I fully understand why people do not recommend it, it doesn't mean the game is bad by any means; the story is still engaging, with memorable characters and enjoyable musical rides. The game's soundtrack, much like the first game, is awesome and adds to the overall experience.

It is literally like they stuck a Temple Run mini game into Route 96, except it is a major part of the game. Because of the rides mechanic, I had absolutely no interest to replay the game, especially because there is no reason to, other than to get a higher score on the rides.Play through it once (it took me 3 and a half hours to play through) and then watch the other endings on YouTube. They are all very repetitive, and not worth spending 3 and a half more hours to get.Other than that, a lot of characters do return, and some are found through easter eggs. _childDocuments_.review: Short answer: It falls very short of its legacy, Road 96. If you haven't played Road 96 yet, go buy that instead. In depth:This game adds a new feature, which will be a major part of the progression, namely skate sections. These skate sections works mainly like a Wipe Out/Mario Kart track with obstacles and points you must collect. You cannot skip these except for each section of each skate track, if you fail enough times. The rapid camera movement of these skating mini games also gave me motion sickness at times when you see the obstacles and points further down the track, then the camera suddenly changes to another point of view. With that said, the skating sections do feel quite fluid and well made, and as a game of its own. This would probably be a good game as a tie in, like Persona 4 Golden vs Persona 4 Arena Ultimax or something. The skate sections would probably feel much more justified if they weren't forced on us and were kept out of the main story, with the exception of a few where you are fleeing someone but it would serve much better to optional stuff like clothing, collectibles and stuff like that. However, to me they add nothing but distractions to the story. But I guess when the game is this short, you need something to fill the void. Reflecting on what made me like Road 96 so much:To me this is the feeling of loneliness and uncertainty of what locations I would pass through next, combined with the overall progression of the game. For all of us who have played the original, we know the outcome of this game. There is no secret, no mystery, no conspiracy not all ready unraveled. I think the developer failed to recognize what made original road 96 so great.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Road 96, and enjoyed it.  That said, give this one a pass, even on sale.  Road 96 was an interesting, procedurally generated adventure that was enjoyable.  Road 96 Mile 0 is an unfocused mess.  It tells the prequel tale of Zoe, one of the characters you can run into in Road 96, as well as encounters of a few others you meet in Road 96.  That part is good enough, but each short chapter is interrupted by a totally bizarre, not easily skipped skating minigame that's jarring in its being totally out of place in an otherwise 3d point and click adventure that feels like it belongs in another game.Frankly, this game should have been a DLC for Road 96, sold for a few bucks, and without the stupid skating.  There's less than five hours of gameplay here, including the stupid skating game, and unless you like skating games (I don't), zero replayability, because the skating part is annoying to the point that I have zero desire to replay the rest to see different endings.I loved Road 96, but after this one, I'm casting a very skeptical eye on anything from Digixart/Ravenscourt, which is a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: Mile 0 is a game about playing out the consequences of your ideology. While first playing through, I found some of these dialogue options for Zoe to be a bit… 'save a puppy kill a puppy', you know? "Actually, poverty is GOOD for you, daddy said so!" Or "Hey! Maybe we shouldn't be gulaging children?"Then I started realizing just how often these choices are two-tiered. Nuanced. Sometimes even contradictory in a very honest way. "I don't know if I believe you Kaito…" followed by "…but I'm willing to find out.", that kind of thing.And then- the game's perspective switches. From Zoe, the daughter of an important political figure, to Kaito, a radicalized youth who saw first-hand Petrian tyranny, watched as oil drilling destroyed his neighborhood and displaced his family.Compared to Road 96, which I felt sometimes restrained itself from really seeing its depictions of extremism through, Mile 0 does… not hold back, narratively, even if it sometimes goes over the kids' heads. The most nuanced political opinions are left for older characters to discuss, or passed to the player themselves to draw their own conclusions, based on available evidence.In a way, I'd call Mile 0 a video game like I'd call The Wall a film. In the strictest possible sense, sure, that's what it is, but that descriptor really undersells the intended value as a political art piece. A narrative-driven experience, focusing on airing grievances and dissecting complex subjects through music and style.It's absolutely dominated my brain-space since I've started playing it, and going back to get S+ Ranks in every stage was often frustrating but hardly impossible. But replaying to get a high score, while supported, is hardly the point, isn't it?I'd still suggest playing Road 96 itself first, it'll give you a deeper appreciation for all the odds and ends collectables and cameos. But, for fans of punk as more than just an aesthetic, Mile 0 has purpose behind its pomp.

_childDocuments_.review: Not only a really good rhythm game, but also an excellent prequel to the political story of Road 96.Mile 0 puts you in the shoes of Trombonista Zoe from the first game and her (previously unseen) friend as they live in the gated community Zoe grew up in. The story is mainly about Zoe coming to terms with the reality of life in her oppressive country (or not), thus setting up why she does what she does in the sequel.The game is divided between free roam segments where you mainly pick up collectibles and do minor tasks to go ahead with the plot, and in rhythm game segments. These play similar to Kingdom Hearts Melodies, in that you control your character on screen and have to collect points and dodge obstacles.The control is straightforward with only two inputs ever used, even for the (fortunately rare) QTEs.The story is less deep than Road 96's and has far fewer branching paths, but the rhythm games allow for some replayability as you can try to ace them.If you like rhythm games and/or the original Road 96, pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start by saying I am an absolutely massive Road 96 fan, to the point I would consider it in my top 5 favorite games of all time. I replayed it over and over again, trying to find every interaction possible. I sincerely loved pretty much every moment of it.That being stated, I didn't have that same feeling while playing this game. I am recommending it for fans of R96 like myself simply because of the story, but I felt the gameplay was pretty lackluster. I don't plan to comment on the different endings because I only received one, I plan to focus this review the gameplay itself and the story that I know.One of my biggest gripes are the skateboarding/rollerblading scenes. I am aware that it is a mashup of R96 and Lost in Harmony, however, it didn't feel like it was adding anything, it felt like it was replacing. Meaning, I felt like it was just used as filler. There were so many of them that I was practically annoyed by them once I was getting to the last ones. I don't think they would have bothered me as much if they didn't feel like they were half the game. And maybe that was the point, but it just didn't feel like a Road 96 game, which is what this is titled. This mashup for me personally just didn't vibe the best.I also felt like overall there was less to do than R96. While there were collectibles around the area, it felt so linear in each section that I could barely deviate. You're stuck either tearing/defacing posters, rummaging through garbage, or looking at stuff to give you different backstory text. Meanwhile, R96, while also linear, just had more to it overall and almost felt slightly open-worldly. The last of my complaints has to do with the story. I enjoy finding out more about Zoe and her origins, as her story in R96 was one of the most interesting ones in my opinion. However, Kaito is never mention in R96 at all. Unless I somehow missed it, I do not remember any dialogue from Zoe about Kaito, even in a way of being hinted at. But at the end of this game, Zoe is very clearly affected by Kaito in many ways. However, when we meet her in R96, there's no mention of Kaito at all? It just seems so strange that Kaito is literally the reason for Zoe ending up where she is in R96, but the only backstory she ever gives you is about her dad being the Minister of Oil. Secondly, you can choose to have Zoe stick with her family values/the government or start to rebel along with Kaito's ideals. And for Kaito, you can have him go full Brigade or start to question if the Brigades are good or not. I have only played through this once, but this all seems a bit pointless in the end, because once you meet Zoe in R96 she's completely anti-government anyway, and Kaito isn't even in R96. For the different endings of this game, I suppose it isn't pointless, but for the overall story when you're including R96, it just doesn't really make much sense.To sum up my complaints, I don't have nearly the same motivation to replay this game like I did Road 96. Road 96 was random, you could have a different story every single time. With this game, you have different endings, but overall the main game plays the exact same (or almost) and half of it is taken up by music sequences, which are a pain if you're not into them. I want to see the other endings, but I don't want to go through the main story again to get to them. Which is such a bummer, because I was so invested in the replayability of R96, and I put that same expectation on this game, but unfortunately, it definitely did not meet it.For the positives, I overall enjoyed Zoe's story. I liked learning about how she started with supporting her father and the government, and slowly but surely learning the truth and how to come to terms with it. I am sincerely hoping they release more games with the backstories of other characters such as Sonya & her brothers (S&M), Jarod, Fanny & Alex, John & his wife. I just hope they ditch the mashup of Lost in Harmony and bring back the true roots of Road 96. I have very high hopes for the future of this franchise, and I am still just as invested in the story as I ever was, but the first game is hands down way better than this one, unfortunately. I still think a fan of the series should play it, but don't keep your hopes up as you move through it.
_childDocuments_.name: Road 96: Mile 0

_childDocuments_.review: Road 96 is a masterpiece that can be played over and over again without feeling boring or overplayed. Mile 0 isnt any of those things. The intro: The skating premise doesnt fit the general story of the 96-universe and it leaves a bad taste in my mouth, so to speak. The tentacle thingy in the beginning doesnt make any sense within the confines set by the first game in the franchise. Road 96 isnt science fiction or fantasy. Zoes introduction is also out of taste and didnt fit her character in the least. It felt very removed from the original game. Making a whole section of the gameplay in the trombone style gives of the vibe of, "theres nothing else to zoe than her playing the trombone". She also came off as a low-tier childish anime girl, whihc was very annoying and dissapointing. Onto the dialogue and character gameplay:Whats the deal with having characters talk while you arent controling them and as soon as you control them they stop talking? That is just stupid. Either you only play as silent characters or everyone talks. Then there is the thoughtbubble. I dont wanto read what the characters are thinking. This isnt a comic book. If Zoe has thoughts about the statues they should be expressed in dialogue, not in a thoughtbubble. Then there is the atmosphere. Im instantly meet with cancer and anxiety/ptsd. Road96 is supposed to be a wholesome, bautiful sommer type game. A game like that shouldnt open with a dark and intense dialogue that colors the atmosphere in rather dark shades. Im not saying that there cant be any darker themes. On the contrary. The game needs darker themes to be consistant with the totalotarian-regime theme. But what we get in this game just isnt it. _childDocuments_.review: My heart breaks to give this game a negative review but i can't recommend this game to anyone right now.But why is this so?This game is the prequel to Route 96.You don't have to play R96  before to understand the game but it helps a lot.The story explains the background of Zoe - one of the main plot characters in Route 96 - and let you explore more of the world of Petria.The devs have improved the game in terms of graphics and storytelling.Gameplay is not exactly the same like in Route 96 but that is okay, it's a different kind of game.Your choices matter in the game, so be aware of what you're doing.And again, the soundtrack is a masterpiece and really amazing, i love it.So why i can't recommend the game?This is due to one simple fact:The autoscroller parts of the game are horribly bad!I like the idea and concept of it but the execution is so bad it's making me sad.The camera perspective is absolute bs, the controls are not precise and who the heck had the idea to add QTE to that? At least the QTE is rare enough but still not a good idea in that.I think they realized that the autoscroller parts sucked so they added a lot of checkpoints and the option to skip the parts if you fail too often. So at least you can progress with the story.But since they build Achievements around it and even made a global leaderboard (why that? ffs) I have to judge the game by it and so it concludes in not recommended.I hoped for better of the game but the devs have failed this time.Maybe another game like R96 would've been better as sequel but maybe next time.

_childDocuments_.review: It's important going in to know that this game isn't just a prequel to Road 96 - it's a sequel to their first game, Lost in Harmony. _childDocuments_.review: It pains me to not recommend this game, because I really loved the original Road 96. It's not terrible, it's just that if you're coming from Road 96 looking for more, you'll likely get disappointed. Note: I played for 1 hour and then refunded and watched a full playthrough.For starters, they completely removed the plot mechanic from the first game, it's now a mostly linear story. That's alright, the problem is it feels very hard to connect or care about Kaito (one of the two main characters besides Zoe) and his backstory because there is no previous connection at all. Unless you played a certain mobile game from the same studio released ages ago, and even then I doubt it makes you care particularly, as the mobile game barely contained story elements. Either way, super weird of them to expect their audience to have played that game and refuse to elaborate any further. Like, why are Zoe and Kaito friends to begin with, considering the circumstances?As far as the gameplay, there are very few minigames or puzzles, it's mostly exploration and dialogue like the original, plus the "rythm game" sections, which are just so... mediocre. Turns out, if you take a mobile game's mechanics and port them to PC, AND EVEN DUMB THEM DOWN, it's not that fun to play. It's just so unsophisticated, like a game made for toddlers.The setting itself is a straight downgrade, I get that the developers wanted you to truly feel the oppressiveness of the state that Zoe ran away from, but at the same time they still tried to sprinkle in some of the lighthearted/joking conversation style from the original. It just doesn't work and feels super weird, like they want you to feel tense but laugh at the same time. The original did a much better job seperating those scenes. The dream-like rythm game sections don't help either in creating a serious atmosphere, it's too arcade-y and jovial for that.This also means that there were very few points where the game's pacing slows down and you would get to relax and really have the music and visuals pop, which were some of the best points of the original for me. There's two slow scenes at night on rooftops, which felt really reminiscent and were my personal highlights of the game, but that's about it.The game does get slightly better in the second half, mainly because the story actually starts unfolding, but never gets to the level of the original. You don't even really end up learning that much more about Zoe's story that you didn't already know by what she told in Road 96. Overall, it just feels uninspired. There isn't any of the magic that made the original special. The game is trying to tell a serious story, but it feels like the game doesn't even take itself serious most times. It's more like a bad comedy where nothing really matters. You came into this game looking for Zoe's backstory and some lore and you leave with even more questions, or potentially just utter disinterest because you don't care anymore. I hope the devs can reflect on this and come back strong. The Road 96 universe and characters deserve it, and they already showed they are capable developers with the original. Speaking of which, the original has decent replay value, so for now I'd recommend doing just that if you ever feel like returning to Petria. You're not missing out on anything by skipping Mile 0.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely understand the negative reviews this game has gotten. Road 96 is one of my favorite games ever, and this feels really weak by comparison. It's very linear, short, padded with unnecessary minigames, and your choices don't feel nearly as impacting.BUT the actual story pieces are still fairly good. It provides an interesting and realistic backstory for Zoe, and gives us a far better sense about Tyrak and life in the heart of Petrovia. I do feel like it's a bit over the top (the authoritarianism seems far too overt) but I suppose that was mostly the case in Road 96 as well. Yes, the game is fairly short, but it was engaging enough that I played it straight through in just one session. I would also say that the game didn't have much choice but take a limited scope because it is a prequel. I think there were only two choices in making a prequel: keep the basic format of Road 96 with other teenagers escaping Petrovia, or give a provide some background for an intriguing and popular teenager character from the first game. I think they made the right choice, because even if it didn't allow for as fun of a game it did help fill in the story better and tried something different. Even if I personally didn't care for the minigame filler approach and wish they'd found another approach.The final thing to say is that this game is very generously priced at $13, and an absolute steal at the current sale price of $6.50. I don't see how anyone could complain about the game when offered at such a reasonable price point. (That said, Road 96 is on an even bigger sale right now and selling at an absurd $5, so absolutely pick that one up first.)

_childDocuments_.review: This is the prequel to one of my favourite games of all time: Road 96. Mile 0 is great, however I think Road 96 (the original) is better. Simply because its longer, bigger and has lots of replay value because of the game's procedural aspects. Mile 0 has 3 main locations to go to, however Road 96 has a seemingly endless amount. Because of this there is not really that much of a difference between two playthroughs unless you pick different choices. I do, however think the music of Mile 0 is a step up from the original. The music in Road 96 was some of the best video game music out there, and there is an obvious budget increase in Mile 0. The graphics in Mile 0 are slightly better than Road 96's however both games have fairly good graphics. A new thing that was added was the new rides, they are very fun and one of the game's best aspects, beat by its story. Also you could play either this game or the original first, it is mostly just an origin story for Zoe, who is focused on a lot in the first game. I would recommend playing the first game at some point probably before this, but it is up to you. Also one of the key main differences between this game and the first is that in the first you don't play as the main character. There were 6 or 7 main characters in the first one however the one the game seemed to focus on was Zoe who you play as in this game. However the main characters for this game are Zoe and Kaito (which you play as) It is more of a spin off than a mainline game. I feel like this is sort of keeping the hype up for a sequel to the original. The story as well is sad and funny, with the ending (at least the one I got) being heartbreaking. This is a great game and I recommend getting it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who was tremendously impressed by the first game, which resulted turning myself and my friends into loyal followers and supporters of the series, I am profoundly heartbroken to announce that this game was an utter disappointment. This review will heavily rely on a comparison of Mile 0 to Road 96 and my personal observations combined with my commentary.The first game had a bunch of unique characters, which encouraged the player into playing the game more intensively to learn more about their life stories and their purposes. Although Mile 0 accomplished to point out some of the key elements and details that were only implied (not directly shown) in the first game, it has not made a significant contribution to the storyline.Mile 0 lacks in-game interactions such as unlocking skills and collecting money, along with a variety of interactions. This was an expectation because those interactions played a huge role for the concept of the game, making it less appealing to the player.Musical rides were simply terrible. While soundtracks were fascinating (as always), musical rides comprised the majority of the gameplay time. There were an unnecessary amount of them and were basically the same with different themes. Mini-games that required use of logic while challenging the player should have been preferred, according to my perspective.The success of the first game set sky-high expectations for players. However, Mile 0 was not even close to surpassing the first game due to its limited in-game features, mediocre critical thinking phases, and lack of character interactions. I am still a huge fan of the series and will await for upcoming games. However, Mile 0 should be a turning point for the developers and a call to return the roots.

_childDocuments_.review: Enough people have talked about this not being like Route 96 - so let someone, who has not yet played that game tell you about Mile 0.Mile 0 is a rhythmic game that also wants to deliver on a story telling side, being a prequel to a story driven game. It sets out to tell a story and then uses its rhythmic parts to overexaggerate, probably to show the teens perspective. But is the rhythmic game any good?No. Sadly it's as simple as that. It's not bad, but it sure has no finesse, it brings nothing to the table. It does the typical, letting you drive around and dodging obstacles, occasionally jumping, ducking or pressing A in a closing circle that is  generous at letting you score 'Perfect'. And yes: You can collect 3 Coins in each level. Overall the game isn't hard, which is ok, I don't think anyone was looking for a challenging Rhythmic Game here. Heck, you can even score an S+ without picking up all of the 3 coins in a level, which is good, because #*!@ that last coin in '10 more Years'!I am not a big fan of the rhythmic genre and even I played better games like Sayonara Wild Hearts. IF you are looking for a rhythmic game, play that one. IF you are looking for a game like Route 96... Well, take Life is Strange or any other story driven game. This ain't it.Being a Prequel to Route 96, this game tells the story of Kaito and Zoe living their best or worst live in the autocracy that is White Sands. The two Teens have very different backgrounds which could have been an interesting concept and the story focuses on that point.Sadly the execution lacks. The story is so incredibly Black and White, that it insulted my urge to find out, what really happens in a game. From the get go White Sands is the bad, being a police state George Orwell would have dreamed of and the Black Brigade is so obviously a scapegoat, that I won't even put spoilers over it in this review. And don't let me start on the "skater tag" that Kaito at one point draws, which most definetly didn't just put a skate board over the symbol of the Black Brigade. Ugh. The game also basically features no likable side-character, completely focusing itself on K + Z.Now, the problem is: The game sets Kaito up as one of those angry kids that has every given right to assist the Black Brigade. The first third of the game you play as Zoe slowly realizing this fact and then in the exact moment that you start to play as Kaito you suddenly get told quite obvious that Kaito should be cautious about the group, that supports his people against the autocracy that he deeply hates. It just didn't resonate me and as obvious as the game made the Black Brigade out to be not the solution to the problem of White Sands either, I just couldn't get myself to play Kaito as someone questioning them.What I ended up with was Kaito ?!? It didn't make any sense and obviously just wanted to tell an ending that could work with the beginning of Route 96.Overall the writing had too many flaws to be considered good. Oh, and there is a reason why I barely talked about any major story accompanying the Teen-Drama: There is none. At least none, worth getting talked about.Some minor technical flaws, in one level a crossing just wouldn't want to work until I restarted it, but that's the worst that happened. It was ok enough.While the graphics definetly are a downside to the game, looking incredibly blurred and often enough ugly or unrealistic, points have to be awarded for the use of colour and thematics in the rhythmic parts of the game. '10 more Years' stands out to me, or the skyscraper. However a massive downside has to be the ego perspective which was so incredibly shaky that even as someone who doesn't suffer under motion sickness I had to concentrate extremely for the first minutes.The music was nothing to write home about. The rhythmic music was ok - good, the background music ok. The only exception were some parts, like Zoes reaction to the Fall of '86 or a few dramatic scenes between the Teens, especially the one up the skyscraper (no further spoilers).Mile 0 is not a good game. It's not terrible, but it fails at what it wants to do and obviously at what the fans wanted it to be. However its a quick and okay-ish experience, so if you want your spoonfed backstory to your favourite Route 96 characters, then you can certainly spend your money and time worse.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give Mile 0 a tentative non-recommendation.The issue with creating a 'choices matter'-style game as a prequel is that you're inevitably heading towards a particular outcome, especially where one of the main characters is also one in the prior game. In my playthrough, I chose to play Zoe as the biggest bootlicker in the history of bootlickers, and Kaito as a standard Black Brigade-wannabe. Without giving specific spoilers, this had very little impact on the overall narrative relative to any other set of choices (I can't be 100% certain in that fact but it felt clear that there was only a very small number of episodes very late in the game that had any degree of conditionality to their content).With that being said, as you might expect from Road 96, the narrative is pretty good. Imagine an ambitious episode of a high school drama but set in Petria. Some new characters (Colton!) are very well-written, and the older ones who are built on are done so in a way which doesn't feel jarring.There's a new gameplay system of skateboarding/roller blading through which very limited amounts of the story are told, and the soundtrack is played. Sadly, it's a pretty rubbish system. It's essentially a trivial platformer, and it's clear that to get a decent amount of playtime out of the game, the expectation is that you go back and try and effectively 100% every time it arises. Hitboxes feel janky, forced camera angles don't communicate the information you need, and mechanically the entirety of it is jump/crouch/left/right. Of course, this was largely the case in the original as well, but the original didn't present a style of gameplay which was so dependent on getting things like that right.The final two episodes you play through in Mile 0 are proof of the issue: they're far closer to the gameplay of the original, and they're by far the most engaging and meaningful episodes.I enjoyed Mile 0, but that's honestly because I love Road 96. To someone who hasn't played it before - go play the original, absolutely, if you get hooked, *maybe* pick up Mile 0 in a sale but be aware that you're getting an evening's worth of lower-quality content out of it.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: First, Road 96: Mile 0 🛹  should have been a DLC to the main game Road 96, not a new game 💢⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀     ⋆｡ﾟ☁︎｡⋆｡ ﾟ☾ ﾟ｡⋆ ·:*¨༺ ★ ༻¨*:·. ⋆｡˚ ☁︎ ˚｡⋆｡˚☽˚｡⋆Road 96: Mile 0 take a place in Petria 🌆, It focuses on Zoe's past life and you are playing with two characters only. it's a short but impactful DLC that provides a taste of what to expect from the full game Road 96. _childDocuments_.review: Road 96 Mile 0 was an excellent prequel, and despite it's heavy political undertones with it's themes and ideas, it still turned out to be a wonderful little game with a heavy 90s aesthetic that ought to inspire many games to come, as there has never been quite a time like the 90s. One critique that I would like to pass on to the devs would be the rhythm controls. For future games, while the new  rhythm  game mechanics, especially for the fights, are excellent, I certainly think there should be an easy mode, where these sequences are cinematic cut-scenes as opposed to games. When you mess up, it interrupts and in some regards diminishes the impact of the story implied with the game, which if not done perfectly, can result in you needing to skip scenes after 10 or so tries, which gets very frustrating after a few times.  I'm sure plenty of gamers love the new challenges, but adding modes and settings to make the experience even more enjoyable for both players who love a challenge, and those who love a casual experience which is driven more by narrative, would be best. Road 96 did a better job of this with it's mini games in the background, and the story being procedural. I would recommend that they be blended, and for the dream sequences, these should be optional as games, and should also be offered as cut-scenes only if the player would prefer to have a less frustrating experience finishing one aspect of the game that didn't need to be this heavily challenging. Apart from this small blemish, the game was very well polished, and there were so many easter eggs and new locations. It would've been cool to check out the other locations in Petria mentioned, but I'm sure that might intend to set up foreshadowing, as I'm sure a third installment of the series would include a great deal of procedural open world exploration, which would be excellent.Another idea would be to cut down on the teenage dialogue, which was incredibly cringe. Even my 16 year old past self would tell these teens to either calm down or shut up. It comes off as superficial when everything the characters options are only facetious, edgy comments sourced from teenage angst. More options for polite, considerate conversations and even relatively normal conversations would be great.Personally, I did a Pro-Petria run, mainly because I was so sick of being preached to about how horrible Petria is, and how I have to be hippie who wants to leave and cross the border, otherwise, I'm a complete moron. That entirely condescending message behind the story and my choices took away from my enjoyment with the series, but didn't completely soil the experience for me, but I thought it important to add it in my review for record.Also I was hoping to unlock an ending that completely changed Zoe's Story by picking these options, but what I got was a very predictable prequel with only conventional lines which line up with the story of route 96, which was honestly very disappointing, but I'm sure such a thing could be worked on in the third game if it were ever made, to explore the continuation of Petria's story in alternative ways. It would be cool to see where it went.8/10. a good game, even if short, too many political undertones, which removes it from it's top rating, and lack of innovation on the open world, did it's job as a prequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I played through the game with my friend on his account so ignore the low playtime...I don't understand why this game is getting so many negative reviews. Yes it's a prequel in terms of the story, but the gameplay is definitely inspired more by Lost in Harmony (which is why they included characters from both the games). It's supposed to be a sequel/prequel to both games, so keep that in mind.This game is much more linear than the first, but I don't think that that's a bad thing. I will admit I'm a bit biased since rhythm games are my favourite genre of games, but I do think the rhythm game levels are good, the controls are a bit janky though so be prepared for that. The majority of the game is open-world exploration like Road 96 though so if you like that from the first game then you'll be happy enough.Also the soundrack is just as good as Road 96's one, definitely recommend that even if you're not planning on picking up the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Road 96: Mile 0

_childDocuments_.review: I'm thoroughly impressed! Mile 0 manages to capture the heart and essence of Road 96, while being a unique game. It's a poetic and artistic masterpiece. My first playthrough took me about 6 hours, and there is a lot of replay potential! I loved the skating sequences. They are difficult but fun, like any good mobile game. However, each one has a story behind it! I love how this game uses these sequences for storytelling, it hits you in a way that typical dialogue cannot.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the first game and I was hyped when I found out this one was coming out pretty much right after I finished it. However, while Road 96 was a fantastic game, I can’t really recommend this one. I was expecting a similar, gripping and emotional adventure with a banger soundtrack as Road 96 but it was nothing like it.Probably the worst part of this game is the thing that is also the main feature – the mobile game-esque skating sequences. I think it would have been fine if it was a one-off thing like the acid trip with Sonya in the first game but instead they made it a core mechanic. I really didn’t understand the point, the skating parts were boring as ♥♥♥♥.Another thing I liked in the first game was finding food, money or car keys. Even the cassettes were nice because you could listen to them in your stolen car and the soundtrack was full of absolute bangers. In this game, a) there weren’t really any random items to find b) they were meaningless. There was no use for money, keys or food and I’m not even sure you could listen to the cassettes in this one.Then there’s also the world. In this game, you are confined to a boring, small residential area. Not only that, but the there are only two important characters, Zoe and Kaito. So no fun encounters, no interesting characters, no interesting missions, not much anything.In fairness, I probably wouldn’t be this harsh if the first game wasn’t so good which made this one a big let-down. But even if I hadn’t played the first one I don’t think I would be that into this – I just don’t enjoy mobile games that much.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love the original Road 96, and even loved this game, I don't think it has earned my recommendation.Let me explain, the story is dramatic and keeps you invested, the base gameplay and puzzles are okay, but what Digixart did here with the skating minigames is just... utter horror. About what felt like half of the playtime you play these skating minigames in a subway surfer manner, with occasional quick time events that absolutely suck. (Most annoying to me was the constant camera perspective changes)These minigames added so much frustration to me that I really ended up not enjoying the game, despite the rest being very good. _childDocuments_.review: I usually give games a good chance, but I don't think I can bear much more of this. I LOVED Road 96, and if you really, really love that game you might like this, but its gameplay is quite a departure from Road 96.First of all, the skating minigame after every "mission" is brutal. I'm not into that kind of thing, so having it be central to the game pushes me away big time. Second, I mentioned in my review of Road 96 that I noticed a few funky accents in the dialogue but it didn't detract from the game. Well, this time it's bad. I think every character has a different voice actor from the first game, and very few of them can pull off a convincing accent - so that pulls me out of any immersion. Lastly, it doesn't run very well, and exploring the environment doesn't feel as interesting or rewarding as it did in Road 96. It could be a fine story/rail-based skating game, for those that are into that, but since it ties so heavily into Road 96's lore, I don't know that it would even be that great as a stand alone. I don't know what compelled the developers to make the game the way it is, but it should have been overhauled, or the story completely re-written so that it stands alone and has nothing to do with Road 96. Honestly, even the writing feels worse.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked recommend, but I actually have very mixed feelings about this.The good stuff:it's a nice concept and a good game to play if you enjoyed Road 96 and you're hungry for more.The story is interesting and it develops Petria more - you get to see what it's actually like to live in there instead of just the outskirts, it also features a light free roaming aspect so it feels like you're actually exploring the world instead of just dealing with a string of premade little stories.The bad:It feels very limited in scope and mechanics compared to the original, there's no "permanent upgrade system" that incentivates you to replay the game and find new ways to handle the different sistuationsThe game also tones down the roleplaying aspect: instead of a nameless, faceless teen the game thrusts on you two established characters with their own personalities and constantly switches back and forth between them.You're still allowed to make your own choices, but the choices have been decreased from 3 to 2 as you're only allowed to either act in character or make your character doubt their convictions.The characters are... alright. Zoe quite never clicked for me but I like Kaito - the side characters remain entertaining but there's a shocking lack of depth to them.There's also this bizarre focus on this new "Rides" mechanic, which is some kind of weird rhytm minigame where the actions are not actually tied to rhytm at all.This was actually done in the original in that one Sonya story but now they're a major part of the story and while you can skip them by failing enough at them they're not optional as they're integrated in the narrative.From a purely gameplay standpoint these segments range from slightly frustrating to entertaining, but the effect they had on the narrative was detrimental for me.I understand what the developers were going for, they're supposed to represent the teenage fantasy the protagonists are living where they don't quite take the situation as seriously as they should yet, but I feel like they trivialize the overall message of the game and kinda makes a mockery of the events in the story.One ride in particular felt really out of place, as it turned what's a very low moment for Kaito into a weird ass "cool" trip for no reason whatsoever.Overall I liked the game, and I would give it a barely positive rating like a 6/10, but I'd definitely wait for a sale on this one.I hope the devs will tackle the original concept again and this is just a spin off prequel, cause I don't think the direction this game is heading is the right one.

_childDocuments_.name: Road 96: Mile 0

_childDocuments_.review: A passable but disappointing title that falls short of the brilliance of the original game.Many characters from the original game are either completely missing, only briefly mentioned, or show up for short, pointless cameos. If you were looking for any meaningful backstories or character developments outside of Zoe, you'll be disappointed. It doesn't contribute much to the story, with the exception of introducing Kaito who has no relevance to the original game anyways.For the most part, this game stays true for the Road 96 core gameplay with a heavy focus on narrative over action. That said, there is a new reoccurring feature to the gameplay that sticks out like a sore thumb: the skating sequences. Visually neat, but mechanically shallow, uninteresting, and slows the game down when all I want is to progress the story.  It wouldn't be so bad if it wasn't for the fact you have 10 whopping skating sequences to go through.The nail on the coffin is the god-awful fight scene at the end of the game. What were the developers thinking? It completely destroys the tension of what is the single most tense part of the game with the most overly-dramatic, cheesy Street-Fighter fighting sequence. I know Road 96 isn't shy of trying to get some laughs from the audience, but this instance was so poorly timed and detracts so heavily from what is supposed to be a serious moment.Overall, if you're looking for some more Road 96 content, then this is probably for you. The story is decent, the art style is there, the music is still great. But if you're wondering if this is a "must-buy" for Road 96 fans, it most definitely is not. It falls short on so many aspects while introducing nothing new to the original formula. Buy it if you really want, but know that you aren't missing much if you skip it.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first game, raved for my friends to play it, and was so excited when a prequel was released. I don't mind the skating/fighting/etc. Aspects as some others in the reviews dislike, though it feels like it needs fixing, the drag on the character within the skating parts feels heavy and not well adjusted. I encountered bugs when picking up spray paint where I could no longer find it, but it hadn't been picked up - instead acting as just decoration. The dialogue and choices feel forces, Kaito and Zoe's relationship doesn't feel fleshed out and, especially at the beginning, the dialogue is very awkward. Even a lot of the Easter Eggs felt meh. I will probably do another run through and flesh out my opinions more later (hopefully after some bug fixing). i understand that it can't be too similar to the first game but the lack of exploration, development and more feels like this game should've been polished for at least a few more months before release. I will say, though, the skating aspect of this game brought some very nice scenes, it looked great. I just felt like the invisible narrative hand dragged me through the mud of Petria. I'm incredibly disappointed, in full. If you want this game, get it on discount until they fulfil key improvements to this game. _childDocuments_.review: Most importantly would be the bugs. The rail mechanic works on a whim and I had to replay the final level a few dozen times to get S+ because it wouldn't let me change rails while the camera was next to me under the Tyrak statue so I kept dying.One of the stickers also didn't spawn for me, I played the game twice (once casually and the other making all opposite choices and getting all collectables) and when I was trying to get all the stickers the "Aya's Ghost" sticker didn't spawn and I've other people say the same.The voices from nowhere are also strange. I'll tear a poster with no one around and suddenly there's a voice commenting on it. While other times I go through the trash right next to a dude and he says nothing.The game also feels very short, the original I played three times to completion across a week, but this game I 100% it (minus the glitched sticker) in one afternoon.The more linear format wasn't necessarily bad, just I wish I could skip cutscenes/dialog. I didn't mind not being able to skip in Road 96 as much because it was random and objects could give more dialog choices so I never knew what was coming, but in Mile 0 everything is the same. I don't need to watch Kaito talking to his dad again cause I've seen it before. I don't to hear Kaito tell me about Aya again cause I've heard it. For a game that seems like it's made to be played more than once, it's pretty annoying oversight.I also wish it made it clear what collectables you have. I ended up having to try and zoom in on the stickers and tapes and cross reference them with a guide because I had no clue which collectables I already had. The first game let you so I have no idea why they removed it.The romance hinted between Zoe and Kaito didn’t go anywhere, it shows up for two unconnected dialog choices and never again, so it felt pointless.I also miss the survival mechanics from the first game, I understand why Zoe and Kaito don't have to  in White Sands, but when Zoe hit the open road, it would have been cool to see.The rhythm games are fun, as someone who loves rhythm games and adored the chase sequences from the first game. It caught me off guard going off the original but it was still fun.I especially loved how story choices made the course different, I wasn't expecting it after Road 96 didn't have any choice base impact, so this was a lovely surprise.I love the inclusion of old characters. It was an absolute treat seeing how Adam came to work for Sonya, seeing a shop owner talk about Battle Tanks, and seeing John  was an unexpected but welcome surprise.I loved it when NPCs did react properly. I was talking to a guy and then tore down the poster right next to him mid sentence and didn’t get to learn what he had to say. That was cool and meaningful. I was used to NPCs in Road 96 not really reacting to me so it was a surprise to see something take notice.Something I didn't like about Road 96 that Mile 0 did way better is having your choices mean something. When I played Road 96 I went down a different route every time but always got the same ending which felt cheap, but I had fun picking all the opposites this time to be able to pick different choices in the final scene.The sound track, although having weak points, was amazing just as in the first game.Overall, I did enjoy this game, it didn't live up to the original and I can recommend it, but I do believe it has earned the mixed rating it has.

_childDocuments_.review: The skating sections (or "musical rides," as the publisher puts it) represent a larger portion of the game than you would think, and if that's your thing, then you'll probably enjoy this game. Even what story there is, which is advertised as sort of a prequel to the original game, ends up being mostly a retread instead. There's little new here, other than the skater stuff, which is colorful and trippy (and, as a few other reviewers have noted here, oddly reminiscent of games like Sonic the Hedgehog, of all things), but it's just not really in the spirit of the rest of the game, or of the original Road 96. It's a high concept idea that, for me, just didn't work.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had a lot of potential, but it just fell short. I don't want to discourage everyone who contributed to this game, it's really a lovely story. I really like the unique art style and the soundtrack, and the story is easy to digest and the endings feel right. Though I felt the dialogue and scenes were a bit short and lackluster but I do genuinely enjoy the plot, especially because I played Road 96. That being said, I would've liked to see more content overall. The areas you can go to seem very small and not a ton to do except some short dialogue interactions and the scripted event that ends the area and proceeds the story.  It's just odd. It's also not the most stable during these scripted end-area scenes. I've had the game crash on me during those. The mobile-esque skating minigame is awful. You can't skip it, happens after every chapter and it feels like I spent more time playing the minigame than I did the actual story. Honestly I think the Devs should just add an option to skip the skating minigame entirely. It's probably too late for that seeing as how integrated it is into the story, but would definitely like to see it gone from the next game. Overall I complained about a lot but I'm still recommending it because for $12 it's not that bad, and the story & art are cute. I'd recommend getting it on sale and I look forward to more Road 96 games.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Road 96 there is some fun content in here.. but it's threadbare. The game is largely linear and the cast of characters is reduced dramatically, not that it matters as you'll be interacting with them in only a few scenes each at best. The gameplay is a strange mix between the original game and an on-rails skating minigame. Which is reminds me of a few of the least enjoyable sections of the first game but instead of a few annoying sections, every single area seems to be followed this same minigame. And while the first game had a sort of heightened reality to it, the skate sections here are abstract in the extreme, with giant versions of antagonist characters trying to literally crush or a snowboarding section to represent freedom. This while the minigame allows the art team to put on some impressive visual displays, makes the whole thing seem much more detached from any sense of reality. And the quick transitions and loose controls make it a feel like a chore. I occasionally deliberately died repeatedly so the game would trigger the ability to skip the section. There are some puzzles that operate like the original but there are no scenes with anything approaching a sense of urgency. I never felt like I was in any actual danger of failure at any stage, something that the first game was excellent at. The fact that you could be discovered and 'lose' a run in the first game made the stakes feel real, this game lacks that completely because the story needs to arrive at a specific place with these 2 specific main characters. And another gripe is the lack of any of the exploration and sense of beauty you could find in the original. There's no equivalent of the mountain traverse or seeing the waterfall for the first time. It's just a few houses, and some bland urban areas that feel all the more empty for being much larger. It's like the writer was very interested in telling this specific story and thought that we would all find it so compelling that we would forget about the things that made the first game so special: the interesting characters, the slow release of information about each person, the sense of scale, the sense of threat and danger and the slow moments of reflection.And don't be fooled by anyone talking about nuance in the choice and consequence system, it's paper thin, all it boils down to is your ability to choose or not choose specific options at a later scene. That's it. It's the game equivalent of a toddler wearings it's parents shoes and playing adult.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're interested in some events leading up to Road 96, and the game is on sale, I'd say go for it.Pros: It's short, generally fun, and you get to see some extra lore for the game. The characters are endearing and seeing more about the events prior to Road 96 is a good treat at a lower price.Cons: It's short, and the main gimmick isn't as fun. Meeting the characters and choosing some dialogues is about the same as the Road 96, but the "Ride" segments. while visually appealing and somewhat important for character developments at times, they somewhat lessen the experience overall and add a sense of challenge to the game which doesn't really fit the type of game it's supposed to be in my opinion.I also said short is both a pro and a con, this is because for what the game actually is, it's good that it's shorter. I don't think this type of game would be as enjoyable if it was much longer, unless it was a sonic game or something.It's a con in that it's too short for any substantial story to take place. You get the general events leading up to Road 96 but it's like eating a cheese sandwich when you're craving a cheeseburger. Yeah it's not bad and it fills you but without anything to sink your teeth into it feels empty and generally like a "better than nothing" game if you like Road 96.Ultimately, I do like the game and would recommend it only if you're a fan of Road 96. and even then, wait for a sale. But if you got nothing better to buy, this wouldn't be a purchase you would regret.

_childDocuments_.review: HONEST REVIEW FROM A BIG FAN (No Spoilers)INTRODUCTIONI’m a devoted fan of DigixArt Studio and the original Road 96. The announcement of this prequel had me excited from day one. This review reflects my initial impressions and some disappointments.STORY / ATMOSPHEREExpanding the game’s lore is always welcome, and this addition succeeds to an extent. While the prequel doesn’t introduce many new characters, it enriches the backstories of familiar ones. However, the repetition of interactions with the same old cast felt contrived, merely recycling memories rather than building new ones.The background of the new main character lacked depth, making the in-game decisions feel odd and sometimes illogical, though there were occasional improvements in certain episodes.SETTING / GAMEPLAYFans of Road 96 will recognize the classic graphics and gameplay style, peppered with fun jokes and references, which are the highlights here.The runner setting introduced in the trailers doesn’t mesh well with the game’s serious tone—imagine mixing a poignant story with a 'Subway Surfers'-style arcade.The game’s duration is disappointingly short at 5-6 hours, possibly stretched to 7 by collecting all available items. However, collectibles such as cassettes remain unplayable, which was a letdown. Additionally, the absence of an economic system and meaningful choices outside the main storyline felt like a step back from the original.CONCLUSIONThe quality-to-price ratio is disappointing. This prequel had the potential to be a fantastic game at half the price. I hope DigixArt Studio returns to form with deeper, more structured future releases. As it stands, the game feels uninspired—a sequel for the sake of having a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: This one hurts, I'll be real. It makes me wonder if Digixart simply got lucky with Road 96.Road 96 was a beautiful, fantastic piece of storytelling where the choices really DO matter, and they feel like they matter. It's linear, but the story beats are generated based on your choices, similar to those really old books where it would tell you to flip to a page if you wanted to fight a dragon. The replay value is through the roof, there's a wide cast of characters with unique stories that breathe life into the pitiful world of Petria, the gameplay loop is engaging and interesting because your choices are reflected to you immediately and with impact, and honestly the music and vibes were immaculate.How do you take everything that made Road 96 great and make a completely different game? The story can be completed out of order, your choices don't really feel like they matter until the end, and the characters feel completely stale. Even Zoe, who is supposed to be the poster girl for this series, falls completely flat - and we're the ones playing her! Don't even get me started on the gameplay. Subway surfers rhythm game? Really? Now, this could have been somewhat bearable, but the controls are complete ♥♥♥♥. You collide with things that aren't even there, the timing is broken, and the movement is unresponsive. The music was pretty solid, but the experience completely threw me out of the moment.The missions that exist outside of the rhythm game weren't fun. I think I moderately enjoyed the very first one where I delivered mail like a "commoner" and told every snobby person in the square off and treated the workers like people, but that's it. They throw you in a small location, you interact with two or three things, follow a story objective, and then throw you into the rhythm game. That's it.Road 96 took me about 11-12 hours to complete. This took me just under 4. It's not worth the $13 dollar price point and to be honest, I'm not sure I would even waste my time playing it at the $3.88 it's currently on sale for. If you're on the fence about it - maybe you really enjoyed the original game and want to keep going or see what Zoe's life was like before running away - skip it and keep your fond memories of 96 intact.

_childDocuments_.review:
Road 96: Mile 0 is a Narrative-Adventure game with a musical component created by DigiXArt, the French studio behind the successful Road 96, 11-11 Memories Retold and 5 Pegases Awards winner. Published by Ravenscourt, players will alternate between the roles of Zoe and Kaito, two teenagers with different backgrounds and beliefs. They live and explore White Sands, a luxurious condominium where Petria´s elite reside and where Kaito´s parents work.
Zoe is one of the characters of Road 96. She comes from the rich side of the city and her father works for the government. Kaito, a character from Lost in Harmony, lives in the less privileged area. They're good friends, but that could all change quite soon.
"Their journey in Road 96: Mile 0 will challenge their friendship and everything they believe in. They say money doesn’t buy happiness, nor friendship. These teens are dreamers and they are going to learn where they belong. Will they remain friends?

ROAD 96 WORLD
Understand the previous event of Road 96 and what made Zoe flee from her home. Play as Zoe and Kaito to shape the evolution of their fate. Besides this, you will run into many of the colorful characters from Road 96. Get to experience another side of the troubled country of Petria.

IT'S ALL ABOUT FRIENDSHIP
This is a story about conflict and difference of opinion between two friends. Zoe and Kaito come from two different worlds, but they are unified by a powerful friendship. They will face many challenges, can they overcome them?

MUSICAL RIDES
The musical segments of the game are a real emotional experience that put you into inner worlds of Zoe and Kaito. You will have to make choices and ride and dodge to find your way through these beautiful psychedelic trips.

_childDocuments_.review: By all means Pac-Man Mega Tunnel Chomp Champs isn’t a bad game, it is just valued extremely wrong. $30 Australian is a pretty hefty ask for an online only Pac-Man battle royale. And it’s not that it couldn't work, it's just that how do you sell that idea to people who aren’t already Pac-Man fans. Because even if this game was worth the full asking price (which due to the lack of variety and general content in the game it isn't), that price alone is already a huge deterrent to players. Which this game desperately needs and deserves. Because there is a fun game here. It's just not worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Chomp Champs is fun but overpriced. Customizing Pac-Man is enjoyable and they clearly put alot of time into this game, but it's too expensive with not enough content. Worth getting on sale for a Pac-Man or party game fan.While I do enjoy Pac-Man and the concept behind Chomp Champs is fun and interesting, I don't think this is as good as I'd hoped it would be. While I still recommend the game, I do so with a few major caveats. For starters, you have to be willing to always have at least some Bots in your game. This is a paid online only multiplayer Pac-Man game and for $20/$30 the potential player base is going to be limited. There really is only one game mode and Ranked tracks wins and loses while Elimination doesn't.Do I think the game is fun? Yes, it is absolutely fun. the customization is fun, the music is a remixed happy and cheerful tune that Pac-Man fans enjoy, and the gameplay is an interesting grid based system with fun PvP and power-up mechanics. While I can say I enjoy this game, I don't think it's for everyone and I definitely don't think this game is priced properly. It's definitely a more casual Battle Royale game but I do think that the more competitive older players will dominate this game and leave the intended young casual players feeling a bit disappointed. The ability to que for Elimination with a party makes this a fun group game at the minimum, guaranteeing actual players in the PvP rather than just Bots, so there is potential there. I wish there was a system for making a lobby and hosting players to it, but this is fine for what it is.Overall, it's good. It retains the same basic Pac-Man game play while mixing it up and having a fun PvPvE spin. I enjoy it and I think it's fun, but I do not think the price is set right, something Bandai Namco never seems to nail down with their games.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot, in good conscience, recommend Mega Tunnel Battle. The bones of the game are , but I have some major issues with the following: ‣  To compare, the original Pac-Man is faster and, compared to any of the Championship Edition games, this moves at a snail's pace. ‣  This is a battle royale game, yet there is never a clear sense of environmental danger. The game begins with 64 randomly connected mazes and, as players are eliminated, they drop off, but there is never a risk of being on a maze that's about to disappear - it just replaces your mazes if you're on an eliminated player's field. ‣  Although it has a forced tutorial and a excessive glossary menu, the win objectives are still muddy. I'm still not clear if being killed by another player costs you a life or why there is a fluctuating score in the right hand corner. ‣  You'll be given two randomly selected missions out of a pool of about ten that encourage you to invade another player's maze to complete it for points. Is it worth it? Are there other benefits? Hell if I know.The maze-cherry on top is that this game already seems to be dead on arrival. As of this writing, the game has been out for four days and it's  player count is 52 players on Steam. Cross play helps, but every game I've played has been stuffed with bots. I would love to see Amber Studio and Namco put more development into this and make this into something worth celebrating, but considering this game had life on Stadia before being ported in this state years later, I'm not holding my breath. I'll watch the updates for this game in the meanwhile and update this review should some meaningful updates come along in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a ton of fun, even when you're playing against bots. You recognize the bots by their sort of standard usernames. You can also tell when it's a real player by the way they move and their tactics. When a real players shows up in your game you get a real kick out of it because the action is like a showdown. The level designs and all the different powerups and the fact that you can eat other Pac-Man make it a really entertaining experience.The Pac-Man customizations are really well designed. I'm running around as Klonoa and I love how it looks. The speeds that Pac-Man moves with are excellent. When you grab a power pellet or a power up, Pac-Man speeds up in various degrees. And the speed of Pac-Man and the enemies make it exciting without you feeling like you're in over your head.I didn't experience a lot of input delay. I did notice it depends on which server you're on. You can select to what region of the world you want to connect to. Keep in mind that this is a online multiplayer game where you're always playing over a server. So there will always be a bit more input delay than in a singleplayer Pac-Man game. You can navigate Pac-Man through the mazes just fine though.Finally, I'd like to add that the animations and use of colors make the game look gorgeous. And that this is a fantastic arcade game.I bought an authorized Deluxe Edition key from a official keystore that is partnered with Bandai Namco
