_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Fun game and concept, but terrible presentation, release module and price point does not justify the game's value. Game is not content supported and there's (literally) zero effort to keep this game alive. Of the many Pac-Man experiences I've played this is definitely one of the most disappointing recent outings of the arcade king.I love Pac-Man to death but I think this is the first time I've given a negative review for a game on Steam. I waited a month to give this game a chance but unfortunately I must give out my hardest thoughts to my favorite yellow sphere.PROS:- Fun multiplayer twist on the Pac-Man formula- Decent visuals and nice soundtrack (despite various bits being reused tracks from the Pac-Man 40th Anniversary album)- Crossplay and friend matchmaking- Customization of Pac-Man outfitsCONS:- : Not only did they put this game behind a price tag instead of making it free-to-play, this game is put at a costly price point with little value to justify the price tag (The compilation game Pac-Man Museum+ is at the same price point at this game and it has 10x more value than this game).  (why is this not a free to play game?????) Asking for a price point for a battle royale game in the year 2024 is asking to be DOA.- Lack of content AND support: This game has gotten only one bug fix update throughout this game's lifetime, and has received NO new content since launch (if i had a nickel for every time Bandai Namco released a live service Pac-Man game with only one or two content updates before shutdown I'd have more than 10 nickels)- Game feel is rough and unpolished especially with the UI department. Also memory intensive for a game with simple graphics- Lack of player base makes it impossible to have a match full of human players and not CPU players (because of the price point)- Input lag during online matches- Features originally present in the Google Stadia version are omitted such as the single player Challenge modeDon't get me wrong, I love Pac-Man to death! This is a very fun game with a fun concept, and playing this game with friends and human players is guaranteed to get you sweating and with full tense. However at it's current price module is where I just can't recommend this game. At it's current price point ($20 USD at the time of this review), this game offers very little to justify it's price point. If you do intend to pick up this game, I'd recommend buying it only when its on sale. If not, there's plenty of other great Pac-Man experiences out there; just not this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not trying to simply repeat what everyone else has already said by now but I will say, Chomp Champs probably could be salvaged if Bandai Namco and Amber Studio ever decided to go in and give the game a F2P overhaul with far more substantial content. That is the only way I see people going out of their way to play this game, but it's also something I doubt is likely to happen knowing the state they chose to release it in anyway.What I really think instead is that Bandai Namco should just take the hint that Pac-Man as a live service isn't going to work. Not when it feels like, more than anything, they'd prefer to sabotage their own game's chances of actually gaining a playerbase like we've seen time and time again with these short-lived, online-only experiments. Chomp Champs could've and should've been the easiest win ever for these guys, so to see the game in this state just makes me sad.If you need your Pac-Man fix then Museum+ is a much, much better use of $20. Its 14 included games will easily provide enough incentive to keep you busy for dozens of hours - way more than you'll reasonably be getting if you bought Chomp Champs. Pac-Man World Re-Pac is also good, but a bit more expensive at $30.Bandai Namco, I am begging you to stop bringing new live service Pac-Man games into existence.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty charming and fun multiplayer spin on Pac-Man. I wanted to play this when it came out but it was Stadia exclusive at the time which was about as appealing as hearing the phrase "live service hero shooter with moba elements". Thankfully the evil has been slain and now respectable, hard-working gamers who run games on their own hardware can enjoy this gem.At first it seems like your typical Pac-Man, but there's a bunch of mazes adjacent to each other and you can invade other people's game which is the real challenge, because you're trying to be the last Pac-Man standing. While there are score bonuses for clearing mazes and eating ghosts, your ultimate goal is the cannibalistic act of eating as many of the other Pac-Men as possible which is a bit grotesque if you think about it, but it's incredibly satisfying to close in on your prey and make the kill.The choice to make this multi-platform was smart, it doesn't seem like there's a ton of Steam players (and admittedly the game is weirdly a bit tricky to actually find on steam, I generally keep up on pac-man but I didn't realize this was out), but it was pretty easy to find a game. I don't think I ever waited longer than 30 seconds to get into a game which is pretty good. The matches only last about 5 minutes which is nice since that's about as long as I got in a normal game of Pac-Man. I don't usually stick with most multiplayer games beyond a week but I think the low barrier to starting and stopping makes it as appealing to fit into a short break as any normal Pac-Man game and I think that's key to this game's success for me. It's quick fun that's appealing in the same way as classic Pac-Man, but puts a fun spin. I love the aesthetics as well, the different mazes have a bunch of visual themes, some just general whimsy and some based on other Namco titles, and the cosmetics are very cute (I'm currently using the mouse suit for my Pac-Man). Hopefully this stays online and keeps a decent playerbase, it's a very solid and pleasant multiplayer spin on the classic formula.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long time (40+ years) Pac-man fan that tends to stray far away from multiplayer-centric (online only) experiences.  To that end, I was quite conflicted upon adding Chomp Champs to my cart, with the Steam refund policy being the only reason I followed through with the initial purchase.Having gone through about a dozen or so rounds with the game, I can say that longtime (old/older?) Pac-man fans could get a lot of enjoyment out of this one.  Overall, the game feels generally familiar and fun with it's classically inspired visuals, sounds, and gameplay.  Both Elimination and Ranked game mode lobbies turn around fairly quickly, with no excessive wait times to get into a game.  The release price also seems fair considering what's on offer here.  If I had to put together a list regarding what I thought multiplayer Pac-man should be, Chomp Champs would check the vast majority of the boxes.My only real concern with the game is it's seemingly lack of human player engagement.  In Elimination mode, gameplay sessions were short and fairly easy to obtain a first place finish.  It was quickly apparent that most (all?) of the "players" I was facing in the majority of my games were bots.  Conversely, Ranked games were longer and more challenging, likely due to more human players being part of the game(s).  Keep in mind that these experiences were during the game's launch weekend when player engagement tends to be at it's strongest.While Chomp Champs may continually build more and more players over the coming weeks and months, it's also likely that the small player base may continue to dwindle.  Cross platform may assist in this regard, but ultimately won't solve the catch-22 that this game may unfortunately find itself in:  gamers don't buy/play because the player base isn't large enough, but the player base won't increase because gamers won't buy/play.  Perhaps a free weekend or "free to play" version of the game could help mitigate this.Though I've given the game a recommend based on experience alone, I'd also advise anyone considering Chomp Champs to proceed with caution as the viability of the game may turn out to be short lived.

_childDocuments_.review: PAC-MAN Mega Tunnel Battle is a modern take on the classic arcade game that brings the beloved yellow hero into the realm of battle royale. This game offers a fresh and exciting twist on the iconic PAC-MAN formula.In PAC-MAN Mega Tunnel Battle, players compete against 63 others in a frantic race to be the last PAC-MAN standing. The core gameplay mechanics remain faithful to the original PAC-MAN, with players navigating mazes, gobbling up pellets, and avoiding ghosts. However, the addition of multiplayer introduces new elements of strategy and competition. Players can sabotage their opponents by sending ghosts into their mazes, stealing power-ups, and even directly competing for control of the same maze. The result is a fast-paced and exhilarating experience that puts a fresh spin on a classic formula.Visually, PAC-MAN Mega Tunnel Battle retains the colorful and charming aesthetic of the original PAC-MAN games while adding modern touches and visual effects. The mazes are vibrant and dynamic, with a variety of themes and obstacles to keep players on their toes. The sound design is similarly nostalgic, with classic PAC-MAN sound effects and music that will appeal to fans of the original games.The multiplayer aspect of PAC-MAN Mega Tunnel Battle is where the game truly shines. Competing against dozens of other players adds a new layer of excitement and intensity to the classic PAC-MAN experience. Whether you're teaming up with friends or facing off against strangers online, the fast-paced action and unpredictable encounters make every match feel unique and exhilarating.With its addictive gameplay and multiplayer focus, PAC-MAN Mega Tunnel Battle offers plenty of replay value. The ever-changing dynamics of multiplayer matches ensure that no two games are alike, and the competitive nature of the game encourages players to keep coming back for more.In conclusion, PAC-MAN Mega Tunnel Battle is a fantastic addition to the PAC-MAN franchise that successfully modernizes the classic arcade gameplay for a new generation of players. With its fast-paced multiplayer action, charming visuals, and nostalgic appeal, it offers a fresh and exciting take on a timeless classic. Whether you're a longtime fan of PAC-MAN or simply looking for a fun and competitive multiplayer experience, PAC-MAN Mega Tunnel Battle is sure to satisfy.

name: Death or Treat
detailed_description: Join Scary in the HallowVerse to make things great again! You will play as Scary , the owner of Ghost Mart, leader in manufacturing candies for Halloween. Discover a huge world with lots of rooms, explore new maps in every run while you try to survive the hordes of enemies. It’s not an easy task, every world is even more tricky than the other. Starting with Darkchat, the Storyum lab, Riptok, the most used app sede, Deviltube, leaders distributing storyum, and the last but not least FaceBoo!, the ultimate epic frontier. Will you overcome the callenge and dare to defeat Clark Fackerberg? Choose your combat style Combat is one of the fundamental pillars of Death or Treat . Choose your favorite weapon style (fast, heavy or ranged) and face a real horde of enemies in the purest hack'n slash style: fly through the air and attack the crowd with force, move nimbly and look for their weak point. Collect valuable hidden treasures to unlock new terrifying weapons and spooky skills that will help you in your journey. Home, sweet home: HallowTown Meet the spooky but friendly neighbours of HallowTown, they are a coffin of surprises! Each one of the stores that you will find in HallowTown can provide different profit for your enterprise. You can create new weapons at Frank's Forge, or buy healing potions at DetoxBucks. Our vampire shopkeeper, Joe Bite Them, will help you get new empty slots for your inventory, and the Pumpkin guys will teach you how to craft magic spells. Finally, go to Pumpkin© to trade your ingredients for more candies! A whole handpainted world to explore “Death or Treat” is an action hack and slash rogue-lite 2D with traditional animations and handpainted environments. We work with traditional illustrators and animators, each of them brings their best to create HallowTown in a distinctive style. Each world has its unique look and vibes, so make sure to enjoy every run!

_childDocuments_.review: at first glace, it gives off heavy Hallow knight/ Have a Nice Death vibes.the game looks BEAUTIFUL. the artists did a great job.the music is alright as well.the animations are pretty nice.art-wise, the game is fabulousmy problems with the game, unfortunately, are all about the game feel/mechanicsthe end lag on the end of combos and dive attacks is HORRENDOUS. i took damage way too many times simply because of it. the game has this uppercut combo that can juggle enemies but the enemies stay in the air too long (and not in a good way). it also doesn't help that you can only combo attack once per jump and can't dive attack afterwards. for a game that wants to encourage air combos and such, the player is kinda limited while in the air. enemies need to come down faster, otherwise i feel the juggle system thing should be tossed out. when enemies attack, there's no graphic that lets the player know "this is an attack". a simple red flash/flurry would REALLY flesh that out, because color coding hazards/enemies/projectiles in a game like this is KEY to giving the player visual information, and this game is lacking in that departmentthe dash is SLOOOOW. and on top of that, you get no invincibility frames when using it. for how sluggish it is, it deserves at LEAST that.sometimes i have trouble discerning what is actually a platform and whats only in the background.as you unlock more weapons, you begin to realize how quickly some become completely irrelevant. instead of different gameplay styles, there's only BETTER item choices. which IMO is terrible for a rougelike game. also, the chainsaw's up attack is broken. broken as in: it doesn't have a hitbox.for a rougelike game, ive surprisingly ran into very few items. most upgrades i got were from the potion seller right before the bosses that can give you potions that either increase or DECREASE your stats. some items are simply too weak to consider or just DON'T WORK (the 1-up item in particular)and on a final note, the text in the dialogue box when talking to npc's is SO SMALL. please please PLEASE make the text bigger!i really truly wanted to like this game, but in its current state i cannot recommend it. the game is still young, and hopefully these issue get patched out.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Hm, it looks a bit like Have a Nice Death. Is it a copycat? Just looking similar, but an awful, low-effort game? Let's see... the options are often useful for a first evaluation. We have graphic options, a bit spartanic and including some resolutions, from HD (1280x720) to 4K (3840x2160) to six quality settings, very basic audio options (music and sfx voulume), and a bunch of languages. All in all nothing very fancy. And there are no controller settings? At least my PlayStation 5 controller worked without problems. No keyboard option? Oh, well, enough, let's actually play the game.The game starts with a short, well made introduction movie, even though it doesn't really explain much. We, a little ghost, arrive in HallowTown, a ghost village (inhabited by ghosts, but also quite empty) that seems to have a new drug problem. The citizens are addicted to Storyum from evil Mr. Fackerberg, boss of Faceboo!. Only Mr. Jobs (not looking like Steve at all in his turtleneck) with his music, as well as the old Mr. Joe Bite Them who doesn't look like the current US president, and a few more ghosts (and a pattable doggy) are still here. The overpriced DetoxBucks coffee shop is closed, as is the Pumpkin shop. Frank Smith, looking like Frankenstein's creature, makes you new weapons. You will also meet Mr. Gates from Necrosoft to improve your spells to help you on your way through the HollowVerse to Riptock and Deviltube... you see, the whole game world is full of such references. We choose our weapon and spell (out of three) and the journey begins. Our goal is the Faceboo! headquaters, and we start in the Darkchat factory. We can (double) jump, dash, use our special skill (selected at the start) and our four attacks. Something unusual is that we can walk through our enemies, touching them doesn't hurt us. We are a ghost, after all, but their attacks do hurt, though. Combat can be a bit chaotic at first, because we generally fight a bunch of foes at the same time and we walk through them, and they walk through each other as well, so it gets a bit crowded before you kill a few foes. You have to get used to that and learn to avoid their attacks, especially from those annoying bats. I hate attacking birds in platformers since my experiences in Earthworm Jim. You can choose perks during your journey, and you can shop random potions in Hatters shop - some increasing your stats, some reducing them, but at least the potions are cheap. Bossfights (the first is the mad scientist Stephen) unlock new stuff. When we die (we have a health bar, so we don't die at the first hit) we return to Mr. Joe Bite Them, and can take many of the collected ressources back with us. They are required to reopen the shops and buy items from them to improve our character. This is the main gaming loop - going on a run, killing enemies/collecting stuff, dying, improving the village and our character before retrying. Actually the typical grind.Ghostly 2D rogue-lite hack'n'slash. Not bad, but you have to get used to the combat system.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly surprised to see so many negative reviews for Death or Treat. During my time with the game (about 2.5 hours right now), I've had an absolute blast. Are there problems? Sure, but they don't detract from the overall experience. I'll wholeheartedly agree that the combat system could use a few tweaks; hit/dash canceling and the ability to restart mid-air combos would be a step in the right direction. That said, you get used to these minor problems after a few runs and kind of fall into the game's rhythm.The biggest problem is that the Death or Treat wears its influences too proudly on its sleeve, which seems to be rubbing some people the wrong way. Is it a Tim Burton-meets-Have a Nice Death knock-off? There are similarities, but there's clearly too much love and passion in this project to simply write it off as a simple cash grab. Speaking of cash, that price point's a little high in my opinion - this feels like a $14.99 or even $19.99 title. The price almost made me pass it up, but the art style eventually won me over. Lastly, a suggestion to the developers: This is definitely an Action Roguelike game, so I'd try to get your game listed under that subgenre as well. You're missing out on players like me who may only browse that tag.I play a TON of action roguelikes, and Death or Ttreat is a solid effort. Even though the story's a bit confusing, I dig the environments, the characters, and the combat. It's one I find myself thinking about when I'm doing other things, and given the amount of games I cycle through on a regular basis, that speaks volumes to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Death or Treat:~~~~~~~~~~~~ Your name is Scary, a ghost and entrepreneur of one of the biggest candy manufacturing plants! Your biggest calendar day is the last day of October. You guessed it – it’s the day we celebrate Halloween! But when you arrive at HallowTown, there is no one to deal with or talk to. It's literally a ghost town, and you are absolutely flabbergasted! What is going on? It's all because of a new drug created by the businessman Clark Fackerberg. Are you ready to travel to FaceBoo and face Fackerberg? Be assured the journey will be long and dangerous in Death or Treat!Death or Treat is a beautiful 2D action roguelite platformer and hack & slash game developed and self-published by Saona Studios on the Steam platform on the 12th of May, 2023. As you start the game, you'll be greeted with a short, fun and well-made introduction that will give you an idea of what happened in HallowTown.  Then, you'll spawn in the centre of town, which will be empty except for one store, The Joe Bite Them store! I had a good laugh there, very funny. You can purchase additional slots at his store to keep items you gathered on your last run. At Frank’s Store, it’s all about weapons, and you have twenty to unlock. Pumpkin Gates owns Necrosoft, a very clever and funny reference; there you can upgrade your three magic skills. There are two other stores where you can purchase items that you might need to upgrade skills, gain additional items slots, gain more health or purchase weapons. You will need plenty of candies and items to do so for all these stores. And when you are ready to go on a run, head up to your little friend, Mashmallow to select the weapon and skill for that run.  The game consists of four levels combined into several small stages, and you need to reach the gate at the end each stage. All the stages are full of enemies, each with its own characteristic attack. A few of them will have two types - mele and distant attack - but most of them have one or the other. Any items such as chests, wooden crates and barrels that have a light blue glow always have candy to collect. Every time you kill an enemy, you'll get some candy and maybe a health potion. Every now and then, you will encounter enemies with a red skull icon above them. It means they are harder to kill, but when you start unlocking new weapons and upgrading your skills, they become easy to kill. Don't forget to check the walls; if there are small sparks, you might have found a secret room. Also, at the end of each stage, you can choose which direction to follow; up, middle or in the centre. Most of the time, you have one or two options. When you reach the Hatter’s shop, it means that you will be confronting a boss in the next room. I found the levels harder than the bosses. I easily made my way to FaceBoo in my latest runs but still fell short of facing Fackerberg.You have a normal and stronger melee attack as well as a magic spell.  At the Hatter’s shop, you will have the opportunity to choose between two random perks. The perks will be for a specific action or inventory.  For example, you might have the option of Frankenstein or a giant wolf to improve your melee attack.  Or a choice of perks for your dash and your jump. Maybe you’ll have an additional slot in your inventory.In terms of the controls, they are pretty good as far as I am concerned. Yes, it might take a bit to get used to them, but they are just fine.The graphics and animations are beautifully done, and the soundtrack is good too. I only encountered one crash in all my game time when I was trying to hit the bird that held candies in the first level. I just had to verify the files again, and everything has been fine since then. I used my Xbox gamepad in all my runs, and my settings were all on Ultra, using 3840X2160 on my 4k 144mhz monitor. The game has been translated into 11 languages, including French, Spanish and English. Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Beautiful animations and artwork+	Four levels divided into small stages+	Funny references all the way through+	Fun and easy to get into+	Good number of upgrades and weapons+	AchievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	I found the bosses' fight way too easy compared to the levels-	Experienced one crash-	No trading cards as yetDeath or Treat has beautiful artwork and animations. Really fun to play but lacks challenge, especially with the bosses' fights.7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

detailed_description: Buy the First Turnip Boy Game About the Game Turnip Boy is ready to commit more felonies in this comedic action-adventure game with roguelite elements. This time the career criminal is teaming up with the fearsome Pickled Gang to plan and execute the weirdest heist of all time! Shake down hostages, steal precious valuables, and explore the deep, dark depths and history of the Botanical Bank. To pull off the perfect heist, you’ll need to purchase an array of dangerous and wacky tools from the dark web, including a diamond pickaxe, C4, and… a cardboard box? However, bank robbing isn’t easy, so be prepared for intense shootouts with security guards, the fuzz, elite swat teams and more! A thrilling single-player adventure full of bank robbing, dark web browsing, and fuzz fighting. Roguelite elements to turnip the action. A big ol’ bank to explore and loot. An array of wacky weapons. Take on whoever the bank throws at you in intense shootouts, from security guards to elite veggie swat teams! A large cast of quirky food-based characters, including some familiar faces and new citizens with their own stories and problems. Earn collectable hats to wear and new banger tracks to blast. Discover a deeper history of Turnip Boy’s world and how it became what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: This game became weirdly important to me last year.After a friend first recommended the 'first game turnip boy commits tax evasion' not long after it came out i played it and loved it. then when this game was announced both my friend and i were super excited for it to come out.Unfortunately that same friend died in August last year.she will never get to play this game that she was so dearly looking forward to. _childDocuments_.review: While technically a sequel to Turnip Boy Commits Tax Evasion, don't expect similar game play going into this. Turnip Boy has gone from what felt like an adventure game to a rogue-lite. I am not typically a fan of the rogue-lite genre, of which I have played some games but not stuck with for a meaningful length of time. I stuck with turnip boy because I really enjoyed the original game and the world it built, but I will admit I was a bit sad to see the devs take it in the rogue-lite direction. It's what everyone's doing now and certainly with some rogue-lite games it feels like 30 minutes of game play stretched over 10s, if not hundreds of hours.Thankfully, Turnip Boy Robs a Bank didn't do this, and I finished the main game with 20/23 achievements in around 8 hours.I had a great time playing this game, but there are some things I think I'd change.I will not spoil what happens at the end of the game, but the difficulty spike is insane!!! Seriously, up until this point I felt the game was really balanced and between the weapons and upgrades you can get, I never really hit a wall.The end game is unbalanced and completely disproportionate to the rest of the game in terms of difficulty. Seriously, if more time had been spent balancing this, I thing it would have been completely reasonable to remove god mode from the accessibility settings. Again, not trying to spoil anything but there's a huge chunk of game you have to replay every time you try for the end game.The ending itself felt a little ill-conceived too. I was hoping to find out at least a little about what happened afterwards.Instead of just having a straight up god mode, it would have been nice to see some options to reduce the damage turnip boy takes from hits. Or maybe customise the amount of hearts you get. Speaking of...Offering the player more progression in terms of  health upgrades would have encouraged replayability  to max out the health even further before the end-game. Perhaps more could be done in terms of defensive upgrades tooI appreciate that you can return after the end-game, but things are still in the state they were before the end-game. Reflecting the state of the bank and the hideout to be that of after the end-game and maybe adding some quests relating to what happens at the end in the bank would go a long way to keep players interested after clearing.This was a really fun game, and kept me playing but I almost uninstalled towards the end due to the steep increase in difficulty and was slightly disappointed at the lack of post-game content. I don't want the developers to feel disheartened because I really enjoyed the game, but I would have enjoyed it way more if the end was balanced, and if it wasn't a rogue-lite it would have probably been up there with my favourite games I play this year.Please please please, don't make the next game in the turnip series a rogue-lite. I know it's popular, but not everybody wants it. I'd be up for a completely different genre though. Turnip Boy Defrauds a Golf Club? Turnip Boy Invents Time Travel? Turnip Boy: Turnip Detective? Turnip Boy Tries Go Karting? Turnip boy builds a vegetable hospital? Turnip Boy Brings Back Television? Really there's no limit to where you could take this and I'm excited to see what comes next. Please feel free to use these xDIf I had to give Robs a Bank a score out of 10, its an 8 for me. Enjoyed it.

_childDocuments_.review: follows the story of the previous  game with a lot more gun and melee combat based gameplay interlaced with the humor and fetch quests. If you didn't play the first game, there will be some dialogue that doesn't always make sense, but the game will still flow smoothly, and you will be enjoying the game in no time.The game is split into multiple exploration runs from your home base, where you can purchase progressive and permanent  upgrades to your armaments. Each run is limited by a fairly short timer (3 minutes) that can also be upgraded and extended by a couple of minutes. The idea is that you have that much time to explore and rob the bank and its usual customers before the law enforcement shows up.If you wish to stay and engage with the law enforcement, they quickly show up in great numbers once your time limit is reached. After that, you slowly accumulate a series of stars, one through five, as you manage to stick around longer and longer. Once you reach 5-stars, the bank reaches an Armageddon type situation where you need to get out in a hurry or risk dying.With the money and loot that you obtain, Turnip Boy can then use the funds to take each subsequent run deeper. The game doesn't hesitate to tell you everything you need to know or to do with a series of tasks that you can easily access from the menu should you forget. You keep all of your earnings if you return to the truck (or train) alive to make a getaway from each run. Or if you die, you lose half of your earnings from that run.The individual rooms have the same layout each time for each individual room. However, there are elevators that take you to random rooms to make some variation from run to run. After some progression, the enemies that show up also change and give a bit more of a challenge. Some rooms are accessible gated by in-game combat progression, while others are gated by your heist funds needing to purchase specific items to gain further access.Once again the game is designed with all possible audiences in mind. Aside from the standard difficulty, there's a casual mode, along with accessibility options that has "God Mode" and adjustable damage rates to really help facilitate the ability of each player to complete the game. Of course, the game requires the ability to read and comprehend the nature of the quests.The boss rooms that you previously visited can be replayed, all it takes is for you to go provoke them again. Otherwise, they are optional once you beat them once.I am reading people are finishing the game in 5-6 hours or so. I guess I am about halfway through, and so my progression is a bit slower than average. But I am having a great time enjoying the gameplay and the dialogue, along with the artwork. There are a bunch of side quests, fetch quests, and collectibles to get in this game. And just like the first game, there are a ton of hats to collect as well. So I don't mind putting a bit of extra time in. I definitely plan to play the game to 100% completion as well.This game clearly has similar bindings on controller or KB&M for a twin-stick shooter, it's easy to adjust to either way. It has the same goofy hand-drawn cartoon style of the characters and their movements as the previous game. The music is fun, and the sounds work wonderfully for this game. There is a whole series of unlockable soundtracks that you can earn through one of the side quests.Most players who want to take a stab at this game should be able to progress decently far, if not to completion. I have no idea how the "God Mode" interacts with the time-controlled doomsday situation to ensure game progression and playability. I am sure the developers conjured a viable resolution. If you want to find out, you can do so after starting the game.The game maintains a $14.99 USD base price as the previous game. But this game is much bigger and definitely offers more content and replay value. I definitely think this game is worth the price.  is just pure joy to play, especially if you enjoyed the  prequel. The fundamental focus of the gameplay shifted to a more twin-stick shooter, but the rest of the charm of the game is still ever present. I do like that the developers kept the accessibility options to keep the game's plot progression within reach for almost everyone who can read the dialogue.I can strongly recommend this game for all of my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: I am genuinely sad to write this review.I loved the first turnip boy game, but I cannot give this game a positive review.Where do I start?*This is a mostly spoiler free review, any spoilers will be marked as such*  I don't think the gameplay is bad neither because it's different from TBCTE, nor because I don't like topdown shooters. I think the gameplay is bad because there is just way too much going on.A lot of the main ideas feel like they were added really early in development and never expanded upon. There are many examples for this, such as: The timer. The timer just feels like an annoyance, you never feel any sense of urgency to get back to the car up until you reach the max star rating and *very minor mechanics spoiler* , which is honestly just a very lazy way to make the player stop their current heist rather than introducing a more fun risk/reward mechanic to the game. There are some other minor gameplay issues this game has, such as melee attacks from enemies being borderline undodgeable and copious amounts of screenshake when firing certain weapons, but also another big issue: bosses.Bosses are just DPS races and bullet sponges, all (except for one) spend half of their fight being completely invincible (which makes half of the fight incredibly boring) and the amount of enemies they spawn during that time makes it more or less impossible to dodge everything. Every boss (apart from *mid-endgame spoiler* , which wasn't that bad honestly) feels very same-y. Apart from their sprites, dialogue and some attacks there's nothing that makes them unique. The final "boss" is a whole different can of worms, I'll talk about that in the part of the review discussing the ending.Another big problem this game has is the money system. This part of the review is probably better as its own section: Progression doesn't feel satisfying.  Doing the things integral to a fun and engaging gameplay loop like killing enemies rewards you with not nearly enough money. Instead, 95% of the money I got during my playthrough were from these "pedestal items". This would be fine if I got them just from vaults (dungeons) as a reward, but they are also just laying around in a random area. To make matters even worse, getting into a new area gives better items, which makes sense in providing a sense of progression. However, this makes all previously collected money completely useless, as the values of the items in the next area are multiplied by ten. This once again results in the gameplay being affected (you just run past any and all enemies and pick up pedestal items, any time spent killing enemies feels like a waste of time) and in progression not feeling meaningful, since upgrades feel expensive in one area with worse items and extremely cheap in the next area with much better items. On the topic of upgrades, they just aren't interesting. Upgrades just boil down to "More Health" and "More Damage". The other progression mechanic is an exchange of the money mechanic for story progression which as mentioned above just doesn't work, and the third one is just a way to slap more time on this very short game, more on that later. With this last upgrade mechanic, you can unlock new weapons by bringing the NPC weapons you found in the bank from enemy drops. The problem is that half of the weapons you unlock are complete and utter garbage DPS-wise, not making it worth to invest time in the system.Alright, next section.If you've played TBCTE the story is pretty much what you'd expect. Nothing much I can elaborate on here. It's pretty much "Go to area A, kill boss, unlock progression item, go to next area". There's a bunch of goofy lore sprinkled in here and there and the jokes are pretty funny, but that's about it. The ending however... *obviously spoilers* Why did I put these two things into the same section? Well, some of the quests *NPCs that give you side quests spoiler*  just end up as very grindy and annoying. You have to *spoiler for quests*  what I would get if these were accessible from the earlygame, providing another sense of progression by slowly completing the requirements for these quests, but they are deliberately locked behind a lategame area, which just makes them feel like filler for this very short game. I completed the main story after three hours while completing some of the shorter and easier side quests along the way, but I spent the other two hours completing the side quests mentioned above and the starting weapon arsenal which is once again just a complete grindfest.The *very minor mechanics spoiler*  just make it all the more annoying to find one specific quest NPC.Why is the game so short? I don't mind short games at all, but come on! 15€ for 5 Hours, almost half of which I spent grinding for 100%?The game is trying too hard to be a sequel in some areas of the story *ending spoiler* Why can't I change the aspect ratio?The music still slaps, but why aren't there any specific boss/area themes anymore?If you liked TBCTE for its humor, you might like this game, but it's still watered down by a mediocre at best, somehow both grindy and short playing experience. It fails to establish a proper gameplay loop and somehow actively punishes players for interacting with its mechanics.Thanks for reading this absolute wall of text by the way, dear devs, if you read this, please keep this in mind if you ever make TB3

_childDocuments_.review: Continuing the adventure of Turnip boy, now we team up with a mobster to rob a bank and make a lot of money, but the deeper we get into the bank, the more we discover about turnip’s family past.The game isn’t bad, but it makes a pretty significant change and opts for a different genre than the first one. The first game is more about adventure and exploration, while this one is a shoot 'em up with some roguelite elements, which I found a bit tiresome.Even though the game is casual and short, at the beginning it feels very repetitive because you have to go to the bank, steal as much as you can in a short amount of time (if I remember correctly, at the beginning you have a minute or a little more) before the police arrive and you have to escape, and repeat.Some rooms you encounter randomly depending on your luck, and sometimes that works against you, making it tedious. The humor is more or less the same as in the first game; but there is a lot of overly long dialogue (for the minute of gameplay you actually have) and although it pauses the time, having to talk to 5+ characters who talk and talk and a lot of it is filler, it ends up draining the intention and humor a bit.Another thing that seemed very strange to me is that instead of improving the initial options of the game, they got worse; they are much more limited and brief... it feels rushed. I couldn’t even take screenshots because the option wasn't enabled, unlike the first game.In the end, with all the upgrades and understanding how to advance in the game, it wasn’t so bad, but I definitely like the first one better. Still, if they make a third one... I would play it :P to see what else is in the story, I just hope we have video, graphic and audio options (and screenshots available) as the first one. It was weird to have a background to fill the gap in fullscreen.

_childDocuments_.review: First off you should be aware that this is actually a roguelite and not an adventure, the trailers and description don't really make that clear and may be disappointing to players of the previous game (like myself). I will say that I am really not the biggest fan of rogue style games and this has all the familiar symptoms of one that you would expect: You go on timed runs through a singular building and try to progress a bit further each time. You lose weapons and cash you were holding if you die. Exploring the bank is done via elevators that send you to a random floor and this is actually pretty annoying if you are looking for a specific room or npc. The game play loop is repetitive by design and doesn't change much throughout the game. Thankfully it retains its charming, quirky characters and humour and it's pretty short and casual so I did still enjoy my time with it and there's a good chance you will too if you are a fan of the first game, just be aware of what you are getting into. Much prefer Tax Evasion but still had fun with this.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Funny dialogueHatsRobbing banksAwesome soundtrackSmashing everything for no reason (so fun)Way more weapons than the first gameGreat accessibility optionsTurnip Boy's beautiful faceLGBTQ+ representation!Easy to tell when an NPC quest has an updateNeat auras to show if a character is friend or foeLoooreCons:Less linear gameplayRandomly located rooms (makes it hard to find certain quest NPCs)Powerful weapons aren't added to your weapons cache (if you die in a boss battle, you have to go find the weapon again)Can't skip dialogue when re-trying a boss battle after deathGame won't default to fullscreen (annoying to change setting every startup)No tax documents to rip :(Abrupt endingIf you liked the first Turnip Boy game, you'll definitely enjoy this one. It's got the humor, cute art style, and clever references of the first game. However, this game is played in "runs," where you start in a weapons room, pick your items, then enter the bank and get all the money you can (and talk to any NPCs you find) before your timer runs out. Then you leave the bank, return to the weapons room, equip new items if necessary, and enter the bank at the beginning again. If you die, you return to the weapons room and have to re-enter the bank and find your way back to where you were. I found this aspect frustrating, especially as more of the map is unlocked.Also, some rooms ("elevators") are randomly swapped every time you enter the bank. This means these rooms have to be re-located every time, or may not appear at all. This was frustrating when I wanted a specific NPC or weapon that only appears in one of those rooms.Suggestions:More things to do with money in endgame (I didn't even get the promised piña colada :( )Add a way to more easily access the elevator rooms -- maybe a very expensive dark web item?Add way to access weapons after death without defeating a boss again (or, if there already is a way, make it more clear)Add better descriptions for items to explain their use BEFORE you buy them (like the train ticket or milk)Does Tangerine Dog do anything? Besides get stuck on walls? If not, it should. Like barking at enemies?More detailed map (kept getting lost in the Dark Docks)What happened with the pomegranate and Crancran?WHAT HAPPENED TO THE BANANA????

_childDocuments_.review: is a sequel to the very funnily named . While it has references to the first game, the premise is absurd and silly enough to be enjoyable without really understanding any of the tie-ins to the first game (mostly the setting and characters). Plot-wise, the game works just fine as a standalone, and the sequel is much more centered on gameplay anyways. Overall, it’s a fun time if you enjoy roguelites. If you’re wanting more of the same from the first game, this game has some similar elements but overall feels quite different in terms of gameplay. However, if you enjoyed the humor and fetch quests of the first game, that still exists.You’re a turnip and the veggie mafia recruits you into a grand heist to rob the botanical bank. Not really much more to it than that, honestly! But who is playing a Turnip Boy game for the story? It’s all about the humor and gameplay, really. Overall, if you laugh at the title, you’ll probably enjoy the game. Otherwise if you think it’s cringe you aren’t going to enjoy the game at all.Music is pretty good – I was jamming along as I played quite often. The art is very cute. I had a guest over and she thought the game was cute! I told her “I’m robbing a bank” and she just nodded slowly and backed away. But hey, the first impression was cute! She definitely didn’t see some of the bosses that look really freaky. Overall, the art style is very fitting for the game and its usually quite clear to tell things apart – i.e. what is breakable, where is the exit, what is going to harm you or not. Although some enemies and NPCs blend in and not always clear if I should talk to someone or shoot first. Kinda makes sense though since it’s a bank heist – guess it is part of the job to know who you want to shoot versus spare. is a roguelite action game where you repeatedly rob a giant labyrinth of a bank until you get to the MOTHER LOAD. It’s impossible to win in one run as you won’t have all the required items to pass through the next area. So you’re expected to constantly rob the bank, earn money, then spend that money on upgrades and items that will help progression. The map is a mix of set rooms and elevators that will randomize. The random elevators helps keep things fresh but they get kind of annoying during the mid and late game. This is perhaps my one and only criticism of the gameplay. Eventually you run out of things to spend money on and the elevators have rooms that are purely for making money. They may also have NPCs and it can be annoying to be unable to find a NPC because their room won’t spawn. This could have easily been resolved by giving the player an option to spend money to reroll the elevators. You get a good variety of weapons but you can only hold two at a time. You’re highly encouraged to drop weapons you bring with you in favor of taking some from your victims. The purpose of this is to increase research to unlock more weapons.Overall, the game is not too difficult. There are enemies throughout the bank and I’ve died a few times from being careless. There are also bosses which aren’t overly difficult either. There is a “boss rush” but it’s thankfully been patched to be able to be done over multiple runs and saves your progress so don’t have to repeat it if fail what happens after. No issues.Operating System: Windows 10Processor (CPU): Intel Core i5-3570K CPU @3.40GHzGraphics Card (GPU): NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070Memory (RAM) 16 GBIt’s a fun game. A bit of a different vibe from the first game as it seems to highly prioritize the gameplay loop over the rest. It’s still fun, but  overall I think I enjoyed the absurdity of the first game a bit more. The sequel sometimes got a little annoying with the excessive dialog, but it was still a good time in the end. It’s worth a look, especially if you’re into a short silly game. Don’t expect to get much more than 5 to 6 hours out of this game, including time to grind out 100%ing it. Probably more worth it on sale than full price due to the shorter length. However, the playtime seemed perfect and didn’t really feel like it was padding out playtime for the sake of it.

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE |  | UNMISSABLEI mentioned in my review for Turnip Boy Commits Tax Evasion that I was looking forward to the developer's future content and I'm very happy to say they delivered in a big way. While the first title had more of a walking sim/combat/puzzle focus, this game is a roguelite that narrows in on task-based quests and combat. The story builds on the prior title, and so I recommend playing it first (you can likely still appreciate the story in this title without doing so, but some things won't make sense). Also, this game took about two hours longer to complete than the first (seven hours vs. five hours), so it's nice that they made that change given many reviews indicated they were disappointed by the short length. Simply put, Turnip Boy Robs a Bank is a nice deviation from the first title in that it carries much of the original title's charm, but the roguelite elements made it feel fresh and updated, and there's more content to enjoy. If you enjoyed the first title, this is a great one to pick up, and even if you haven't played it, both games have a lot going for them.

_childDocuments_.review: First game where I wish there was a mixed type of review I could leave, instead of a clear negative/ positive.The game itself is okay, the story is good (as long as you liked the first one, which I loved), but the gameplay is kinda bad. The music is amazing, and honestly might be the best part of the game. I'll probably listen to the sound track outside of it.Even on the hard difficulty it doesn't feel like there's any challenge, because as long as you get a decent weapon you'll steamroll the bosses. They don't even get a chance to do their mechanics outside of the 'immunity' phases beacause you can hit them before they unfreeze. The bosses in the last game were more difficult, especially comparing final bosses.The rogue like parts feels more like an obstacle than fun progression. I wanted to continue with the story but had to keep going back to base to buy random items to open doors. If you prefer a melee style, the upgraded weapons suck ass because the first 10 unlocks are all ranged weapons, which means you're holding onto the 1 good melee weapon you find and only have 1 gun to recycle every time you go back to base.I did enjoy the random elevators, the pictures make you not waste time going into the ones you don't want and it rewards moving through the level quickly and remembering where elevator spawns are. worst part by far was resetting for 1.5 hours after I beat the game to get the correct elevators for my last 2 quests and 100% it. Please let me pay like 1m to pick an elevator that guarantees shows up  On top of that, the "Limitless Line" at the end of the last game is so much superior as a roguelike game, which only makes this one feel worse because I've played it. Overall, I do love the story of turnip boy, and don't regret playing it, but the gameplay just isn't there.

_childDocuments_.review: As a middle-aged woman, I'm clearly NOT the target demographic for this game, but as an enjoyer of shooter games like Super Animal Royale and Deep Rock Galactic, I thought I'd give the new Turnip Boy sequel a try.  Want to watch an old lady play this?  Check out my video: Turnip Boy Robs a Bank is hilarious, the characters are incredibly cute, and although it took me a while to figure out the gameplay loop and start blasting heads, I'm really enjoying going on tons of short raids in the bank.  I've already yoinked over 40k from Botanical Bank and am not stopping, as this mama just unlocked the grenade gun!!As an older person with questionable reaction time, I also appreciate the accessibility options, including easier bosses, auto aim, and even auto fire if I want to sit back and let Turnip Boy fend for himself.  Do I recommend this new Turnip Boy game?  If you like funny shooter games, yes.  The dungeon-like style of the raids offers plenty of replayability, difficulty settings makes this playable for even the biggest of potatoes, and it's hours of fun for around 15 bucks.  Did I receive this for free?  Yes, but I stand by my candid evaluation.  If you don't like it, talk to Mayor Onion.

_childDocuments_.review: 7h 4/10, The last run will be a challenge but unlocking the later weapons will help out a lot 1 There are a few guides, that can be found in the Steam community.  I hope  will be finished, as I prefer written guides to find things you're missing.  No No No No Not really, although during the last run, you want to be quick as it is already hard enough.  No No No, you can play on the easy difficulty with auto-aim and still unlock all the achievements NoI'm so happy to see a new  Turnip Boy game! I wish he would go on a more wholesome story arc... but that doesn't seem to be in the cards for Turnip Boy... After committing tax evasion he now starts robbing banks...  Where will he end up in the future? But I hope this will not be the last we see of him! While Turnip Boy Robs a Bank is a different genre than Turnip Boy Commits Tax Evasion, it still is just as much fun as the last title, and full of the humor we loved in the first title. the story goes further where the first one ends, but you don't need to have played the first one to be able to enjoy this. however, there are a lot of references to the first game, so it is more enjoyable if you have played that one first. TBRAB is a rogue-lite in which you get asked to rob a bank, and while doing so you'll get loads of tasks by other characters that you'll meet in your runs. There is a main structure in the bank that will always be the same route, but there are rooms that will switch between rooms, that way you'll meet so many characters and maybe in later runs find the things/people they asked for. An important thing to do is bring back weapons you found during your run because you can sacrifice them to the blueprint board to unlock new starter weapons which will be so much better than the ones you start the game with. You'll need those for the "final" run, as that one is a real challenge. None of the achievements are missable, and you'll unlock already a bunch by playing through the game, just keep an eye out for the objectives on your to-do list to finish up those. The objective to rob a bank never got completed in my game, but the 38 other tasks need to be completed for the achievements. Focus on bringing back weapons for the blueprint board and increasing the amount of money you can earn and the rest will follow.

_childDocuments_.review: Turnip Boy.Really good game! I didn't enjoy it as much as the first but it was very close. I will list my pros and cons and then compare the two games.Pros:-Great Soundtrack, fits very well with the bank heist theme-Great Writing-Fun Characters-Cute Art-Representation!!Cons:-The elevators. (Trying to get a specific room in order to get all achievements was really tedious)-Money having pretty much no use late game. (Last 2-3 hours the only thing I could buy was the )-No sense of mystery - the first game had me questioning what was happening throughout it, especially with  , but the only similar moment was with , who seemed to have very little impact on the story.-Dialogue for the beginning of a boss fight would replay every time I went to retry after dying. This was especially annoying during the final fight.-Couldn't regain boss drop weapons after -Didn't spend enough time with characters/too much dialogue sometimes. With a fast-paced game like this, lots of dialogue sometimes breaks the immersion. Dillitini suffered a bit from this, and this led to me not becoming very invested in his character.Turnip Boy Commits Tax Evasion was a brilliant game. Turnip Boy Robs is also a great game, but its soundtrack, art style (which is slightly different) and writing all aren't as good - but are still excellent. I am being overly critical because of how good Tax Evasion was - it set the bar so high that anything not up to that standard would leave some people disappointed.The first game's art style and cheerful, relaxing music led to the darker themes of the game being more impactful. However, when players of that game go into this one knowing about all of those themes, it doesn't come as a surprise when a lot of similar story beats happen again (for example the ). What bothered me about the reuse of these and only a few new introductions was that everything felt underdeveloped. In fact, it felt like  was going to have a big story impact  but there was none of that and it felt like a lot of missed potential.If a third turnip boy game is made, I'd like to see a couple more spooky moments sprinkled in amongst the cuteness and more variety in music, like in the first game. I'd also like to see fewer, more fleshed out characters. We don't need dozens of NPCs with two lines of dialogue for the game's story to be told. However, I did enjoy several new additions, such as . They were fun characters and could have huge implications for the world and helped forward the story!This game's gameplay, while being very different, was more fun than the first's. The boss fights were better and the enemy variety was nice, but the lack of puzzles was sad (the only puzzle was figuring out where you met that one NPC two hours ago who now needs that item you just got! /pos).Despite all my complaints (none of which make this a bad game by any means - it is well worth picking up if you enjoyed the first, I just think that there are ways that it could be further improved), I had a great time with this game - I did 100% it!  I hope that you devs continue to make fun games like this and I for one will be getting the next Snoozy Kazoo game day one.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically much much better gameplay wise than the first, but a bit disappointing  story wise. Gameplay is kind of light roguelite, shoot'em up/bullet hell. A bit like Enter the Gungeon if you know it (although much less of a roguelike than Gungeon and much easier too).Gameplay is sooo much smoother, the first one I only played for the story and the jokes (which made it very much worth it) but the gameplay was a bit lacking, the gameplay parts (dungeons, bosses, etc) were not fun at all, even tedious, but thankfully it didn't focus that much on gameplay part so you could just ignore it.Well that's the exact opposite. Well not "exact" because the story is still kinda fun, a lot of jokes are really good, and a lot of the lore bits are funny too... Just clearly not as much as the first one. While the first one got entirely carried by its story and jokes alone, here, if it was everything the game had it would clearly not be enough.Thankfully, the gameplay is soooo much fun here. As I said earlier, I really get vibes from Enter the Gungeon gameplay wise. The fun of finding a cool weapon that is really satisfying to use, and then just tearing through the rooms with your new toy. Bosses are much more fun than the previous one. The timer mechanic is interesting honestly, much less frustrating than I initially expected (and it's not a hard timer, depending on your weapons, you can absolutely stay longer if you're ready for it), and forces it to be quick runs, so you don't get the tedious problem of roguelites where you know when starting a run it could be a 30/45 min run.So, came for the story, stayed for the gameplay.

This game has a more rouge-like style. The main map itself is the same, but there are special rooms in the bank that change each "run." This sequel is a lot more combat focused than the first, but I felt it kept the series fresh and was a good take on the old formula. The game should take only a little longer than the first game, so expect roughly 3-5 hours to beat and 100% the game. _childDocuments_.review: Fun, quirky little sequel to the original Turnip Boy! A few things:- A major complaint I saw from players is that the game is too grindy. I disagree. You're meant to be constantly bringing back weapons after missions to unlock new ones. If you overlook a central mechanic, yeah, you will struggle.- I do feel like some of the charm and plot motifs of the first game are not present, which is a shame, but not enough to make me not reconmend it. If you enjoyed the 1st game, you'll enjoy it.- Controller settings feel a little weird, feels like it was meant to be played on a keyboard- Settings do not save and there is no full screen support which feels really weird for a game made in 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most frequently contentious discourses in videogames is also one of its most uninteresting and that is genre definition. For as long as gaming has existed, people have had seemingly endless patience for arguing over which nonsense term can be arbitrarily applied to which games in a futile effort to quantify the unquantifiable: art. Gamers as a whole have effectively speedrun traditional art history and evolved to its highest (and dumbest) form: Does x game count as a roguelike?This question to the uninformed must sounds like absolute gobbledygook, because it basically is. This question and others like it are so fruitless when treated as actual debates rather than the potentially interesting opportunities for self-reflection on how we consume art they actually are. As far as I'm concerned, genre is defined by the art, not by outside observers. If one piece of art is like another, then it can be said to belong to that genre. Turnip Boy Robs a Bank is undoubtably riffing on roguelikes (or roguelites if you want to be a pedant) and stripping it down to its most basic structure. In doing so, it creates a perfect microcosm of the genre, one where you can experience all the growth and progression contained within Hades in five hours instead of 100. As a followup to Turnip Boy Commits Tax Evasions, Robs a Bank is both an improvement and a regression. Tax Evasion's greatest strength was its charm, with the whole game centred around one excellent gag stretched to the absolute limit. It was witty and cute but was ultimately a pretty basic game. Nothing exemplifies this more than the roguelike DLC added for free after launch, which was so horrendously unfun with its half-baked faux-Zelda combat. While the story was fun, Tax Evasion's gameplay was lifeless, stiff and under-developed.Robs a Bank is almost the complete inverse of its predecessor. Our vegetal protagonist has moved into more serious financial crime, with an amusing lack of motive. He is just as silent as ever, but with the loss of the document tearing gag from the first game, he feels just a little less interesting than before. The story and jokes have taken a bit of a backseat in general, but this is to allow the mechanics room to breathe and I'd struggle to disagree with that move. Turnip Boy has traded in 2D Zelda for Nuclear Throne, now running about the titular bank with a surprisingly hefty arsenal of creative weaponry, blowing guards away and shaking down innocent bystanders.Each "run" sees you burst into the bank, which remains the same each time, outside of semi-randomised elevator rooms. Your main goal is to accrue as much ill-gotten gains as possible whilst progressing deeper into the bank. A time limit of only three minutes keeps runs short and snappy and there's a good pace to the game overall. The time does pause for dialogue (which there's a surprising amount of) and boss battles, so it's not as punishing as it might sound at first. You'll be gathering side-quests as you go, which usually require talking to a separate NPC halfway across the map and most of the time you'll resolve without even realising. Once you escape back to your hideout, there you purchase from a decent enough pool of upgrades before starting all over again.As I said before, it's not a long game. I did every single thing in the game in five hours, but you could easily see the credits within three. This isn't a bad thing though, as one of the most offputting aspects of a new roguelite is the implied time-sink that it will involve. I'd love to play Dead Cells, but am I willing to give away 200 hours of my limited lifespan to truly enjoy it? Turnip Boy Robs a Bank has no such quandary, you can finish it inside an evening and still have time for a few runs of Balatro. This also makes it an excellent introductory roguelite, even more so thanks to the generous suite of accessibility options. Robs a Bank isn't a particularly difficult game, I died only five or six times in total, but every game should have them and it's always nice to see them.The one thing holding Robs a Bank back from being a complete improvement on the first game is its writing. It's still decently charming, some of the NPCs and sidequests are on par with or funnier than the first game, but the central plot was lacking the excellent gags from Tax Evasion. It all culminates in a finale that is almost as silly and over the top as the last one, but doesn't feel quite as earned. It's still better written than more "funny" indie games, but I would have liked a little more of that anarchic design to be reflected in its moment-to-moment writing. All in all, there's little to recommend against Turnip Boy Robs a Bank. It's cheap and cheerful, only as long as it needs to be and it's all round good fun. If enough people buy it, we can only speculate what crimes Turnip Boy will turn his leafy hands to next. Turnip Boy Creates a Crypto Scam, anyone?

_childDocuments_.review: First, before I begin, I feel that I need to give a couple gameplay details. Turnip Boy Robs a Bank is a roguelite adventure, where each round of robbing the bank has a very short timer (starts at 3 minutes). You begin each round in the same location with all enemies respawned, and you need to go back to wherever you last were to continue the story. This gives the feeling of never being safe, and always being rushed, adding up to a level of anxiety I needed to accept in order to enjoy this game.I played, beat, and reviewed the first installment of this series 6 months ago at the time of writing this review. In that review, I brought up three primary aspects of gameplay. I'll look at the same three aspects in this review, as diving into these three aspects sum up my opinions on this sequel perfectly.- Story: In the first game, I raved about the story. It was cute, playful, and the highlight of my experience. In this sequel, the story takes a backseat. There are still adorable monologues, characters, and hilarious dialogue, but this is marred by the feeling of being rushed by a clock that only lasts a couple minutes during gameplay. This got better for me over time as I realized the clock pauses during dialogue and as more whimsical characters are introduced, but nonetheless, the sequel does not come close to the original story.- Action/Combat takes center-stage in this sequel. While I complained about the combat not being polished in the original, the sequel takes large strides to improves this. I actively want to continue playing after getting 100% achievements because the combat improvements, and while Turnip Boy's combat is still not as good as dedicated shoot 'em up games, I enjoyed it quite a lot.- Metroidvania/Map: This is where the biggest improvements were made in the sequel. Traversing the map is the most important aspect of roguelite adventures, and where I criticized the backtracking in the original, this is possibly my favorite part of the sequel. The map is split into visually distinct sections which are all connected with interesting points of interest at every corner. The map still took a couple hours before I started understanding and memorizing, but once I did, my outlook on this game changed drastically, and I no longer felt nearly as rushed to do what needed to be done.Overall, Turnip Boy Robs a Bank is a fantastic sequel to the cult classic Turnip Boy Commits Tax Evasion. I can't wait for the third installment "Turnip Boy Commits Genocide." I recommend playing the first installment before playing this sequel, but I still highly recommend both, and would be happy paying full price for both.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s cute, and it has fun in it, but it’s not as concise as the predecessor, to the overall package’s detriment. 8/10.As a returning veteran of Turnip Boy, this sequel is great fun. It’s cuddly presentation is wonderful, it’s got the humorous hard-boiled narrative spunk that makes it unique, and the gameplay is rock solid. Soundtrack in TBRAB is excellent, and the use of TB’s phone to shuffle the radio at anytime is a great addition. I understand the need for a rogue-like to have farming, I’m not new to the genre. But TBRAB has a gratingly slow burn before the lategame power spike. Please, take it from me, rush the main quests, leave the side stuff for later, or you will feel trapped in this very short game. Another issue I have with this is, unlike TBCTE, I can’t as easily recommend this game to a younger audience, as the dialogue is too crude and it’s themes pushing inappropriate.  Technical performance while good, doesn’t support native 1080p/1440p/4k, but a window size scaler and no borderless windowed mode. TBRAB is accessible, engaging, and is a perfect ‘gamer’s first rogue-like’. It’s casual fun, and well worth the full price tag. It’s so close to being perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the first game very recently. While I quite enjoyed the first title and its spin on a original zelda like exploration, goofy tone and dialogue and cute artstyle, this one didn't resonate with me as much.I want to recommend it for the much improved combat, and the still existing aforementioned strengths such as visuals, sound design, decent boss fights, funny dialogue, characters and situations, but the game is dragged down by the death timer (this game takes the form of a roguelite, killing you instantly after a set timer in every run), this killed the leisurely pace at which I explored around in the first game and always gave a sense of urgency. on top of this, the very repetitive nature of the runs didnt help to justify replaying them over and over again. worse, there are some glaring technical limitations for a 2024 games. this game didnt seem to support 16/9 screens. i am not talking ultrawide, im talking legit regular rectangular screens that everybody got. well tough luck gotta play this game on only the central portion of the screen, forming roughly a square. i dont remember the last game that worked like this, probably gamecube games emulated on PC. also, it would not remember my settings and i had to redo them every single time i launched the game (keybindings, language, even stuff such as fullscreen), this grew old quite fast.couple all of those glaring issues with a 18 euro price tag for a 4/5 hour game at best, it falls short of recommended, despite its qualities and undeniable heart.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not fun.It seems like robs the bank is trying to be a roguelike without really understanding what's fun about roguelikes. It thinks mindless repetition is why people go to roguelikes. I found I was going through the exact same route the exact same way multiple times, maybe stumbling across something new by accident that I wasn't able to get past yet because I didn't have the necessary upgrades.This isn't how I normally play games, but it's how the game encouraged me to play, with the strict time limit that doesn't *really* have room for real exploration and the heavy focus on making as much money as possible.There's also a time limit. I don't understand why you would ever put a time limit on a rogue-lite if you also want people to explore. It's a really cheap way to increase difficulty, and it's a big part of why I started taking the same route. There's just not enough time to explore. It's like it was the only way they could think of to make us replay levels, which just isn't how a roguelite should work.It'd be like if Binding of Isaac killed you if you didn't reach Mom in 10 minutes - it's *possible to do*, but I don't think anyone would enjoy it as much if the game were like that. It doesn't feel like you just weren't fast enough when that happens. It feels like the game is punishing you for daring to explore.The movement is also really, really janky. Turnip boy moves way, wayy too fast, which led me to stumble into enemies and bullets, meaning I took a lot of unnecessary damage. In comparison, the weapon speed is extremely slow and sluggish.In the first game, slow weapon speeds weren't a problem because it wasn't a combat-heavy game and there was maybe one or two enemies per area. That doesn't work for robs the bank, though, given there's several enemies in each room that seem able to shoot and attack much more quickly than you, even if their projectiles moved slower. Worse, enemies are nigh indistinguishable from npcs that you can shake down for cash. I had to find out the hard way when something was an enemy.The UI is also extremely mobile-centric, which is extremely strange to work with on a PC or with a controller. I know that the devs make games for mobile (including the Turnip Boy series) so this kind of makes sense, but I wish they made the UI less mobile-ish. It feels a bit cheap and was also kinda hard to understand.It was disappointing. I loved turnip boy commits tax evasion. It doesn't feel like the devs understand why it was a good game. Even if Turnip Boy Robs The Bank wasn't a Turnip Boy game and was completely divorced from the standards of that game, TBRTB is still a bad roguelite. I don't think they knew what they were doing when they made this.

_childDocuments_.review: The first game Turnip Boy Commits Tax Evasion is a lovely action-adventure game. However... Turnip Boy Robs A Bank plays more roguelike... with swords, guns, and more guns. I love how the art style, the humor, what made you fall in love with the first title makes its way back in the second. The major things you need to focus on is making sure each time you enter the bank, you need to leave with as much cash as you can carry, and try to bring back a weapon or two... cash can be used in the HQ's shops to help you obtain useful items and upgrades... the weapons you bring back with you can be used to upgrade your arsenal so you can take improved weapons in with you at the start of each run.Some doors in the game are only accessible with key cards, and each of these cards are in the possession of bosses. We were expecting bosses to overcome, that was one of the highlights from the first game. I have no issue with the obtaining of these cards, its doable, its done even, I worked my way towards being able to over come each boss, and was rewarded with each key. My issue comes with the late game...As the story progresses towards what I can only assume is the end of the game, you are given a monumental task. Remember those bosses I mentioned? There was four of them, and you will have to fight them all again in one run without dying... is this a problem? Yes and no... no... because if you have been grinding and you have everything there is to have up to that point... you can mop the floor with all four of them in 3 minutes... BUT... after you do defeat them the game's difficulty spikes through the roof because then you are prompted to begin the next phase...A fifth boss appears, this one can not be dealt damage like the previous ones, you "simply" have to dodge it's relentless attacks and minions because remember those four bosses? You have to return to each arena...and carry out the rest of your mission... while the enemy continues to rain hellfire upon you... there is no mercy... you might be lucky to be given one scrap of health but don't worry you will be dead as soon as you grab it so theres no point even...so here is where you will die... and die a lot... and guess what? When you do die you have to start all over again... that's right go beat the four bosses... begin the hellfire phase all over again and die soon after because this part of the game is pretty impossible you need some night five, Five Night's at Freddy's RNG bullcrap...I recommend dropping more health for the player to pick up and maybe ditch the enemies because the boss is already enough to deal with... 6 hearts max is not enoughUPDATED!-=-=-=-=-=-=-I noticed there was an update for the game so I decided to try the final gauntlet again for the 30th time... I noticed that one of the four bosses I previously mentioned had a new move, nice touch. Onto the real meat and potatoes... a lot more health gets dropped during the final ordeal making it possible to reach the end. This removes the RNG factor entirely so if you die... chin up soldier, the game is beetable :) the game is fair, just try again.Seriously though thanks for making the impossible possible because I spent hours on that final run before the update.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not really a roguelite as most of the map is the same (and if you're looking for specific random elevator rooms you're likely to get screwed by RNG.) It does get repetitive at parts as you start running around the map under your short time limit, checking all the elevators and npcs to get your sidequests done. The weapons are fun to use, and boss fights are challenging but engaging.Gameplay may be middling at points, but what sells Turnip Boy is it's humor and world building. It's overwhelmingly silly with many fun callbacks to the first game! Then it beats you to death with horrific worldbuilding. I reccomend.

_childDocuments_.review: Turnip Boy robs a bank is a game that has a lot of charm and good humour, but sadly like Turnip Boy in the beginning falls flat on its face with the roguelike mechanics. For one, the layouts of the actual "map" doesn't change at all, so you're going to go through the same repetitive motions again and again. The randomized rooms you could go to, a third is straight up just npc "hubs" with nothing to loot, and the actual maps have so little variety between them that they inject little variety at all in the core loop. As for money progression, the balance rapidly goes all wonky as items that don't fill up your actual money bag become your actual source of cash, making the money bag size increases practically worthless. The weapons you can get as well just seem mostly on par with each other dps wise which makes it hard to justify using anything other then two or three weapons you like, not like the combat is much difficult otherwise. And to top if all off, I finished the game in 4 hours, likely less once I realised how little time I needed to spend in previous areas with how fast money scales.It's not worth the asking price, with neither the gameplay replayability nor enough charm (as much as there is) to justify the length.
