_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is enjoyable; with beautiful visuals and vistas, a fun (though, partially flawed) combat system, good build diversity and good replayability.However, what is on offer for 49.99USD$ is  a finished game. There are masks, weapons, entire weapon classes, pre-order/deluxe edition bonuses, certain voice-acting, and more absent from the game on all platforms along with a baffling lack of polish in many places. Additionally, the "40+ hours" of gameplay that is listed on the store page is incredibly deceptive, and the average first playthrough will likely only be 15-25 hours even when accounting for a collector's playstyle; for the price point Jyamma Games asks, and compared to its contemporaries, the game is very short.The game may be improved over time, but it is impossible to recommend a blatantly unfinished game, admitted as such by the release of an "improvement roadmap" only 3 days post-launch, being sold at near full price with intentionally deceptive marketing; either check back in 4-6 months down the line, or play if there is a drastic price cut or sale. Would refund if I could.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly I can't recommend the game, encountered too many game breaking bugs and the game is very short for the price, it cost £40 and I got around 10-15 hours out of it, even though the devs said "40+ hours". My listed play time isn't accurate, as mentioned the real play time somewhere around 10-15 hours. Hard to tell as I kept the game open when AFK a lot. In game save file says 15 hours but I was AFK for that a lot as well. Bad habit I have with games. Some of the game breaking bugs: Ladders disappearing, making progress impossible. Enemies just standing there completely unresponsive. Being unable to talk to NPCs. Boss health bars disappearing, UI elements disappearing.Positives:Combat is mostly fun. The parrying mechanic felt nice and responsive, the world is really nice, the lore is great, nice boss variety. Good music, though limited. Nice UI. There's some good ideas like the masks, but it isn't implemented properly.The game has a lot of potential and in march might be great. The devs did do a good job overall.Negatives:The game does not explain things well, weapon rarity, unique elements systems, etc.Normal enemies are weak and boring to fight. I never died to a normal enemy.The game focuses on mask loadouts and switching between different mask/weapon combinations, but I found myself never switching, there's no reason to... It's slow and clunky and just gets you killed in combat.Game has the worst enemy variety of a soulslike I've played. You sometimes fight the exact same bosses multiple times, there's one boss you fight 5 times and another 3 times...Heavy weapons are basically useless because there's no poise, you'll never get slow weapon attacks off since every attack stuns you.Physical builds are very weak compared to element builds and battlemage builds are straight up broken.Tried many different weapons, the movesets are lacking, clunky and boring. No reason to use heavy attacks, it costs far more stamina and does minimal more damage than light, and is much slower.Most of the weapons and most of the abilities in the game are useless, and there's a lot of copies, like 4 of the same ability just with a different element.Final note: They released the game like this, at this price, but it's far from finished and they even released a road map and the game will be in a finished state in March, which if I knew I wouldn't have bought until then.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review early because I want to help decide for those thinking about getting it now as it has just come out. I am only 9 hours in but I have beaten the first main bosses that were in the demo and a few of the mini bosses(?) in the second area going into the third. I did play the demo when it was released and thoroughly enjoyed it as I am a huge fan of the souls and souls -like genres.combat and game play: The biggest thing to note here is that the combat for ALL bosses, most mini bosses, and high-level common enemies rely almost solely on your ability to pary (that becomes painfully aware with the second boss, Vermiglio and only continues to be the case from there). If you are not confident in your ability to pary and perfectly deflect, I would sit this one out. There are definitley bosses that punish you hard if your timing is not impeccable. My biggest issue(?) with the gameplay is the mask loadout situation. It might be a personal issue but I really dont understand the use of swapping through the masks and having the ability to quick swap them. I have not once needed to change my loadout the whole time I have played so far because the game kind of locks you into one combat style that it prefers. All in all I do think this game is enjoyable and I agree with others saying that it is better than Lords of the Fallen but not as seamless and great as Lies of P.I will update this review once completed but so far so good.

_childDocuments_.review: The game still has several issues that need addressing:1. Hitbox inconsistencies:While enemy hitboxes are generally decent, there's a frustrating inconsistency when they are on the ground. After breaking an enemy’s guard and using a special attack, it becomes impossible to deal any damage while they're down, even though your weapon visibly hits them. However, when your character is knocked down, enemies are still fully capable of hitting and damaging you. This imbalance detracts from the overall combat experience.2. Invisible barriers and environmental hitboxes:The game is riddled with invisible walls that break immersion. Throughout the map, there are numerous objects and rocks that seem like you should be able to walk or jump over them, but invisible barriers stop you. For a game that was postponed, these issues give the impression of lazy level design. A good example is at the "Church of Maja," where there’s debris that looks like you should be able to climb on or traverse, but it’s yet another invisible wall. This breaks the flow of exploration and reflects a lack of attention to detail from the developers.3. Camera and corner glitches:The camera often behaves erratically when your character is stuck in a corner, especially during combat. If you get cornered by an enemy or near environmental debris (like at the Church of Maja), the point of view gets completely disoriented. Your character becomes immobile, unable to dash, jump, or even properly move. These corner glitches turn what should be intense moments into frustrating experiences, leaving the player stuck and vulnerable without control.For those who have recently played the latest and more polished Souls-like games, I wouldn’t recommend this one just yet. While the style and theme are intriguing, the game still feels like it’s in development. If you’re looking for a relaxing, visually stunning experience, this isn’t the game for you right now. It has potential, but it needs more refinement before it can stand alongside the top titles in the genre.PS: after playing for a whole while, i still dont recommend this game. If you’re the type of player who enjoys completing games 100%, be warned: this game’s achievements are also broken. Despite collecting all weapons, lines, and aspects, the corresponding Steam achievement didn’t unlock for me, and I’m not alone. Multiple players have reported the same issue, which makes pursuing achievements pointless and frustrating. Given how many bugs already plague the game, the fact that even achievements are malfunctioning is another sign that this title needs serious work.

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased the game after having only recently been introduced to the Souls-like genre and this type of visual style and setting is right up my alley. As someone who's not super good at these types of games, as they tend to make me panic and just smash button randomly, I really appreciate the way the combat feels once you get into the flow of it. The stamina system discourages you from wailing attacks on an enemy, and the parry mechanic supplements those moments in between attacks really nicely. It feels like a back-and-forth, and encourages you to analyze the enemy and understand how they move and pattern in a way that I didn't feel like I could in similar titles. A more seasoned Souls-like player might find the combat slow, but as a relative newbie, it's an extremely welcome pace! I'm still getting my butt whooped by the first sets of bosses, but I don't feel like I'm simply out of my depth. I feel like I can think and strategize mid-fight, read what the enemy is doing. I was hooting and hollering when I beat the tutorial boss the first time, because I felt like I was actually understanding the mechanics beyond just "hit thing till it dead"!!I feel like I have room to experiment and learn, which is really needed because there's a lot going on with the elements and abilities and items in menus that I don't know how to access on the fly. I feel like I need to sit down for a few hours to understand what everything does, otherwise I'll end up moving forward with my trusty longsword and brute-forcing my path to victory with some pesto and minestrone at my side.Something I really don't understand at this point is the weapons, specifically how to gauge how powerful they are and what they fully do. I've a longsword that, by numbers, should be fairly weak, but it has a purple bracket around it and does the most damage of my non-elemental longswords. Not sure what's happening there, but it kills well so I treasure her.My last "critique" is I'd kill for some kind of map. I get dreadfully lost very easily, and at least the early part of the game is in a small city with lots of cooridors and levels. A map would save me lots of headache, but I've been able to bumble my way forward eventually.So overall, loving the game so far! It's feels like a great introduction into the genre for interested folks, and I'm simply adoring the visuals and commedia dell'arte and the immaculate vibes. Highly recommend checking this title out!ALSO when you load a new game file it asks if you want the tutorial or not, which I can imagine is GREATLY appreciated for folks who are pretty savvy in the genre or for people moving forward who want to speedrun this title. Very lovely QOA. Excited to see accessibility like keybinding remapping coming soon too,

_childDocuments_.review: 🎀The inspiration from the Italian locations is really admirable, if you like Maccheroni, Pizza e Mandolino, especially the first area is the most inspired, however this game is full of bugs, not cleaned at all from technical problems, the roadmap states that this is an Early Access, because it is not possible to get stuck in the mines after defeating the giant crab because a sort of invisible wall appears, as if the boss was still alive, to overcome this bug I have to go back to the main menu and restart the game to make this invisible wall disappear.Another bug I found is related to the frog quest, after meeting him the third time and equipping the gondolier's mask, it is no longer possible to change the mask, here too I had to restart the game to overcome the bug.The merchant no longer sells consumable items for fast travel. It is not even possible to respec points from the pg in the theater, the button appears gray and unclickable.The levers to recall the elevators do not work.In some areas, there will be the word "Travel" to allow you to go to other zones, the word floating in the air, not even near an object to serve as a reference. The word only appears when you get close, and the problem is figuring out where it is.The weapon bullset does not exist, everything is identical based on the type of weapon.Weapon feedback is non existent.Little variety in enemy animations, almost all the same.The enemy AI in many circumstances is ridiculous, many kill themselves by falling down, for example, if you throw an object at a dog that is near a cliff, it will jump towards the cliff and kill itself, also works with other enemies.The story is really nice as well as the representation, but this game has never been tested by the developers, I don't understand the rush to release it in an incomplete state maybe 70% because there are too many bugs and the lack of variety in the combat system on the weapon classes.There are dozens of other bugs found.Even though the weapons are fully upgraded, they deal very little damage. It seems that the damage is focused only on magical abilities rather than melee damage. It's not even possible to understand how to upscale or create a build, as there are no descriptions regarding the type of damage.In no Italian review have I seen or read about these problems; no one has mentioned them, probably because they received free keys and want to make this game appear as the "Top" but that's not the case. There are missing collisions in too many areas of the game map, where you either fall out of the map or fall from elevators. No Italian reviewer has mentioned these issues, and this behavior seems biased and they lack coherence , as if they want to cover up or defend a game that's almost completely broken: enemies get stuck, bosses freeze, and boss fights are all about constantly blocking enemy attacks to perform a parry after stunning them by filling the blue bar, which takes a long time. Everything is too repetitive, and many times there's no opening for a heavy attack, forcing you to block attacks continuously. None of this is mentioned in the Italian video reviews I’ve watched recently. All the focus is on talking about the artistic style, while the technical aspects are completely ignored, such as the stiff animations and repetitive combat. Some enemies are in the wrong place, I'm referring to the enemies that jump high, some of which are placed in rooms with very low ceilings, causing them to get stuck with their heads in the ceiling. Others get stuck outside the rooms because of low doorways, allowing you to hit them without being killed, which is very unrealistic. Some enemies perform close-range attacks even when you’re 10 meters away, I’m referring to those with axes, others freeze, just like some bosses, or even the player character gets stuck in game elements. In the map representing Venice, where you need to activate levers to lower the water, there is an area where you can walk underwater, and the character dies only after several minutes because the game doesn't register the water's presence. There are several non-Italian videos on YouTube showing all these bugs.The development of this game is clearly focused on the story, neglecting the combat system, which is really poor, boring and too repetitive. The animations of the enemies are copy-paste.At the moment I do not recommend it, too many problems and the roadmap in the discussions confirms that this game is incomplete, bluntly!

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my first review on Steam. I want to write my honest opinions on the game and give my point of view for advice for the developers at the later part. The reason being: I quite liked some parts of the game, but at the current state of the game I would have a hard time recommending it to my 'normal' player friends.I will give the game an overall score of 6/10 at this time. Following are the aspects I considered for this score:+ I really liked the world and the interconnected paths. At some point they are a bit convoluted and there are some questionable 'shortcuts' (which aren't really shortcuts in my opinion). So exploration and mapping out the area felt in general good. However, if they went just a tiny bit more out of the way, the maps would have turned out an utter mess. Close call, but I'm glad they ended the maps how they did, I think they are currently fine, but on the border of making it too convoluted.+ The combat in general feels nice. Attack patterns of enemies seem generally ok. A few really strange ones, where I'm not sure if it's bugged or intended. However, readable after the first few encounters. The ranged dudes are a bit obnoxious, as some stuns are longer than the recharge of their attacks plus your attack wind up. It can be counteracted, which is good - but a bit more leeway or variety would have made a great deal to not frustrate me so fast. It's not that it's unfair or bad, it's just not really fun.+ The enemy moves and variety are ok as well. However, there are just as much misses as good examples. So this one is a 5/10. I think by design, most bosses share moves with normal enemies. Which is probably because the masks represent battle affinities. I don't find this wrong at all, however, bosses should in my opinion come with a few extras. A very good example of the game is a certain poison lady. You encounter her multiple times, every time adding at least 1 new move. I really liked that. On the other hand, there were bosses with literally 3 different attack moves. Not enough, not good, not particularly fun.- The magic and elemental debuffs are a huge miss for me. I don't know exactly where I am in the game, but I believe I am at least halfway through. And honestly, I have no clue what the debuffs do. It is certainly explained in text and all, but my issue is that I find it not intiutive at all. Honestly, even Elden Ring I would critizice to not properly display tooltips of debuffs. So in my opinion, either add very short and clear descriptions of what debuffs do. Or, which would ultimately be much better design in my opinion: make them more intiutive by using better icons or names. I think the game uses Italian language as a base for the elemental/debuffs, which is also probably by design, but it just doesn't work well for me.- There are bugs currently. Not a huge deal for me, but may very well be for other players. I lost all my things twice, because the game couldn't place my belonging after a death. Once I was stranded on probably a few pixels of a ledge (impossible to get to again), and once they just simply weren't anywhere to be found where I died. In later areas there are environmental parts not assigned to being 'walls' or 'walkable' so I just fell through the ground. I hope this will get fixed, and to be kind here: there have been worse releases.Because I liked the exploration of the maps and the combat in general, I will stand by my 6/10 rating. I can probably only recommend it to certain people however.Following are a few thoughts as a player who has played many Souls games - and games in general. These are things I would probably change if I had the chance to work on a game like this:1. The skills you can acquire are way too much in my opinion. The idea is generally fine, but just as Lies of P had to change their tiers, I think this game should reconsider the skills which you can acquire. The main reason is, that all of them seem to be equippables. So you can skill 30 different things, but only equip a few of them. I would much prefer a little bit of a simpler system, where you chose a 'mastery'. For example a 'parry mastery'. And then you can upgrade this skill twice or something. The more skills there are, the harder it becomes to balance, and I honestly believe the balancing of the current skill tree is quite random.2. Statuses, Trash and Balancing: I have no clue, what my issue is, but there are some trash mobs which are quite honestly obnoxious. They seem to have 10x the health of the guy next to them and they sure respawn every time as well. This might be an effect of me not understanding the debuffs/buffs, but I am not going to respec or change my loadout because of one guy. I just skip these. I don't think this is the intended way to deal with it by the devs, but it is the way I assume most of people deal with it. Therefore it is not a feasible design decision in my opinion. Which also ties in with the next point I want to make:3. Loadouts: Honestly, not a bad idea. I can create a 'template' for my playstyle and switch it relatively quickly. The use, however, when exploring the map or fighting enemies is just.. not there. I think what most of us players do, is just have 2 of them set up nicely, and switch for certain bosses. I might be wrong here, but I've never made use of the 3rd loadout. Reason being: you are also kinda limited because of your stats. My honest opinion: tie the loadout and loadout switch to the weapon change. In 95% of all cases I will switch the loadout to use a specific weapon. Why not tie it all to the weapon, I think that would work perfectly fine.4. Finally, this may be a silly point at first, but hear me out: Give bosses a memorable feature. For example, when the poison lady does her 3 poison bolts in a row, add a voice line before. 'Let the poison consume you' or something. Not only would it be a huge benefit in learning a fight (I think the first of those is almost unblockable until a few tries in), but it would make the boss fights something to talk about. They are a bit underwhelming at the moment. Man, I could even go back to games like World of Warcraft in like 2007, where voice lines indicated moves. Also, if you look at a game like Elden Ring, everyone will know exactly what boss you are talking about when you say: 'I command thee, kneel!'. I don't expect visuals like Radahn or whatever, but I truly believe that memorable boss fights can greatly advertise a video game!I want these games to continue and get better. Maybe add a patch of new content for further community feedback and trying out stuff. I see there is potential and there are good basics here. But as a gamer, there are things lacking and not working out (as intended?). Therefore, even though the review may appear harsh, I only mean to give a fair opinion and some advice for both players who may be interested in the game, as well as developers who follow or develop such games.

_childDocuments_.review: A really interesting twist on the souls-like genre, filled with rewarding exploration, stunning visuals and hidden depths. I was totally unfamiliar with Italian folklore before playing the game, which added a new level of intrigue and novelty too.  But what really appeals to me about this game is the way it tells its story through game play. There is so much more to this game than first appearances. If you enjoy narrative that isn't spoon fed to you and encourages you to piece together clues, you're in for a treat. Combat feels fair and balanced, but if you've played other souls likes there will be some new concepts and mechanics to figure out. If you are looking for a game that does something different instead of just doing an impression of a fromsoftware game you won't be disappointed.Please give it a try and support Jyamma Games because I'm excited to see what they make next!

_childDocuments_.review: So, the game is... playable, the art direction is superb, but on a technical level the game is lacking on every level. From crashes, respawning items  or just unpolished enemy attacks that are incredibly frustrating, like a guy with a ballista that can permanently stun lock you, or the mini bosses with a buff that triples their damage output. Despite that, the game also  has  a lot of good qualities, like the incredible customization of your build with the mask system, the art direction that I mentioned earlier, the level design and overall the game is fun to play. So why the negative review? Because I went on holiday and when I came Back I didn't notice that the difficulty of my run had been changed automatically and proceeded to do almost half of the game without noticing. Why would you do something like this in a souls game? Just Why? Maybe I'll change it, but for now NO.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game that shines best when you find the set ups that works with your play style.You could play it like a classic souls game (ignore the loadouts, path of innovators and just go BONK), howeverthat would take away a fun part of this game.It's true, you can't respec (at least where I'm currently), but that problem is nullified by using the correct aspect: to give you an example in souls like terms: you want your second mask to be a mage but you don't have enough intelligence? no problem: just equip the "mage aspect" and you will have some bonus intelligence.To resume: don't be afraid to experiment; having a lot of options means also that you could put togheter a bad loadout, a bad loadout works bad, if it works bad you don't have fun and your experience is ruined.Don't rob yourself of a funny experience just because your first set up didn't work as intended.The game itself is fun.The graphics is good, the art direction is VERY good (take a close look around in Quinta, and see all the hidden, sometimes macabres, details in that sunny town).Music is out of this world.If you have finished games like elden ring and liked its customization/variability, but are still hungry for a souls like game without falling in the exact FROM SOFTWARE format, this game is for you.EDIT: I went further in the game: you have to beat a strong optional boss, but after that you unlock the respec option, so you can also do that with your attributes.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as Souls-likes go, this one is closest to Lies of P, though I will admit it isn't nearly as polished. There are plenty of issues that could soft lock or hard lock you (according to the community, I do believe this part). There are some bosses I feel should have a minor move-set tweak (and some bosses that really need to be nerfed, according to the community). Personally I only witnessed some visual bugs right towards the end, and some issues with achievements not being handed out. Despite all of that, I think I might have enjoyed most of my time in Enotria even more then my time in Krat. That isn't a objective statement, this title could definitely use some time in the oven. So if your interested I'd definitely say hold off till some of the QoL stuff in the road map drops, think they have it planned out to March of next year. Using that as a guideline of when do jump in would do you well. But even saying that, I need to say it again, I really enjoyed my time with this game. Heck, I even jumped into the Italian VC just to boost my immersion and hear half a dozen people intermediately yell "Cazzo." Fun times.PS - My play-style was to ram my head into bosses and just parry till I won, barely touched mask lines. But a buddy was mainly mask lines and we both could complete the game, so there is some build variety. But you probably should learn to parry at least some attacks.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: today September 19th 2024 devs published an "improvement roadmap" that goes all the way into March of 2025 and includes such things as "new additional mocap animations" and "increased variety of moveset". This is something you'd expect from an early access title. This game isn't just unpolished, it's quite literally unfinished. Wait at least half a year and a big fat discount.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Not a great first impression, to be honest.First thing I was met with is the complete lack of a key rebinding option, and that alone made me ready to refund right then and there. However my patriotism won over, and after firing up Autohotkey and tinkering with it for a bit, I was at least able to give the game a chance with a control configuration I'm familiar with. Yes, developers said key rebinding is coming in the first update or something along those lines, but seriously you're asking almost 50€ for this, the least you could do is release it with all the basic features of a proper PC game.So I finally hit new game after getting my controls in working order, and I'm hit with a voiceless cutscene that barely gives me time to read subtitles, so I try to speedread the whole thing with the predictable result that I understand less than half of it and I'm left feeling like I have to rewatch it. Alright, let's just chalk it up to skill issue. Then the game actually starts, and man... barely anything changed from the demo that I remember. The tutorial still kinda overwhelms me with unintuitive terms, half of which I just give up to remember and decide to learn as I go, and the combat and animations still feel kinda stiff for some reason.HOWEVER, once I got out of the tutorial and into the meat and potatoes, free to do my own thing, the game changed gears. Combat is actually not bad despite the somewhat stiff animations; if I had to draw a comparison to similar "souls-like" titles, I'd say it doesn't feel as good as Lies of P, but miles better than the new Lords of the Fallen. Mixing and matching the passive skills you get from the skill tree with various active skills and equipment combos makes me see a lot of potential for build variety, and you can set them up into 3 loadouts which you can switch to on the fly. The setting and scenery is beautiful, and I think the graphics do it justice; this is a pretty game to look at.They say first impressions are everything though, and I'm not going to lie and say they didn't sour my experience for the first hour and a half, which is kinda important being almost entirely the window of time you get for a refund. I'll probably update the review as I go, and I'll wait to change the rating at least until the key rebind situation is sorted out.

_childDocuments_.review: I am keeping my original review below. Within hours of posting it they pushed an update which fixed the secret final boss. The resistances were reduced and they would no longer spam a full heal ability. Additionally I reverted my character to more of what I had throughout most the game and was able to beat it.This game very much reminded me of the original Dark Souls and the world feeling interconnected was extremely nice. It felt good being able to be an actual battle mage and not  the moonveil or twilight great-sword type.The story felt intriguing and the music in the boss fights is amazing. *Elden Ring players won't enjoy not having infinite stamina while sprinting around but it isn't open world and was always intended as a way to punish you for trying to run through the map without knowing what is around the corner in the original souls games."I was actually loving this game even with all the jank until the end. When you play and reach the end, please just accept the offer. Don't swing. As the game currently stands, I am unable to beat it without relying on jank and RNG according to all the threads I have seen. This is not fun. No amount of skill can get you pass this secret boss without having the appropriate weapon, ironically the worst type in the game, leveled for it. I was super excited to leave a positive review of the game because OVERALL I really enjoyed the experience and I am sure if I would've accepted the offer this would've been a very different review...As soon as this gets patched and fixed I will be changing my review."

_childDocuments_.review: The game made massive improvements after the demo, though a bit of jank is still there. Even then, i think the devs managed to work around it, as the attacks are pretty much always readable aside from a few, and most of those are not like that because of the jank but because of the balancing, I'd say.The game is buggy as of right now, though I've never experienced anything too impactful. For examples, some of the enemies' AI stops after attacking them (rarely, but it happened a few times), the boss music does not play after subsequent tries (unfortunately since the OST is fire) and a few voiceover are missing. Thankfully, all of those seem to be fixable through the right patch, so if those bother you I'd suggest to wait a few daysI've heard of people having performance issues, but I've had next to none aside from some brief stutter in a couple of areas until now, and my PC is not a super computer by any means.TLDR: Clunky but way better than the demo and if bugs bother you I'd suggest to wait for the next patch for bug fixes, otherwise give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Just over 20 hours of game play and I've reached the final boss. This game has been quite amazing.:- The graphics are incredible.- The world is rich of history.- Great weapon variety.- Mask Lines, or spells, are plenty and creative.- Bosses are tough but fair.Overall, I think this game is a must for souls-like fans. Perhaps weapon move sets are not the best, but almost everything else makes up for it. Every boss is amazing, aside from one "mage" boss in the main path which I though was complete and utter BS! The world of Enotria is a healthy balance between true open world and a linear path. The first main area is more or less linear. After the two other main areas open up, you are free to choose where to go, though it is clear you are supposed to visit one of them first over the other.If you have the money, I recommend this great game!

_childDocuments_.review: As an Italian, I really wanted to like this game and I didn't.It's beautiful, the Unreal Engine 5 really highlights how good the level design in this game is but unfortunately, it's not a very good game. Game designers had a good idea in mind but didn't know the basics of how to balance gameplay and overall player experience. I was often lost, not knowing where to go and just simply confused with how this game's progression works.Puzzles completely stall your progression and boss fights sometimes lead to absolutely nothing after spending a long time trying to defeat bosses.It is not a fun game and it becomes stale after the first area. It's baby's first souls-like and it shows. The combat is very boring, parry, parry, parry, parry, parry, stab, parry, parry, parry, parry, that's the whole game.TL;DR: Looks good but it's not a good game at all. Leveling and Loadout system very underwhelming and confusing.6/10 (worth it if it's €15 or less).

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play the demo. People said it was jank. All I know is the finished game is good. It's an indie soulslike, so it's not going to be FromSoft quality... but that said, it stand up on its own and is fun. As usual with these games, give it a little time to see if it clicks for you. Everything is kind of mysterious and the systems can be a little overwhelming at first. Just give it time and you might be in for a good surprise. The most interesting thing about this game is the art direction. It's inspired by Italy and Italian folklore, and so in a juxtaposition to the dark and foreboding worlds of Dark Souls or Bloodborne, you get a sun-drenched Mediterranean landscape. Combat takes place on beaches, in the cobblestone streets hamlets, and in beautiful fields of flowers. Honestly, it felt refreshing to see so much light and color in a game like this. I don't want it every time... but it was a good break. The rest of the game is very standard fare - stamina based combat with committed attack animations, mysterious NPCs, hard bosses, items, maze-like levels (done well, I might add), etc. If you really love the genre, this one is worth picking up... although $50 feels a little steep to me. This would be a perfect $39.99 game IMO. So wait for a sale, or if you have that need for a new soulslike to explore, do what I did and plunk down an extra $10. All in all, afteer about 8 hours, it's feeling like a 7.5/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pretty good souls like! While it's a bit rough to go back to less flashier souls after playing Wukong this games has a solid foundation with a system that lets you actually play around worry free with the new weapons and abilities you get thanks to a stat changing element you can switch on the fly via load outs. It's a bit buggy here and there but on my 4080 I didn't experience anything game breaking or too frustrating.My favorite element of the game was certainly the load out system combined with the lies of P like parry/dodge system. By the end of the game I had ~8 weapons maxed out I actively swapped between while playing (and quickly thanks to the loadouts) to approach each enemy. My builds around each weapon were varied as well, which status inflicting weapons filling in my status inflicting build, elemental on my elemental build, and a tanky poise breaking build with a giant hammer. I never felt like I ran into an item I couldn't use which is an element that's always bugged me in the more rpg heavy souls likes; if I get a new weapon or spell I want to try it out, but in the other games it's simply not an option. All of this combined with some pretty smooth parry/dodge souls combat and some fun weapon movesets.The game is also exceptionally pretty. Each area is unique from one another and they all look visually stunning. The detail that went into the games regions is obvious and there's a lot of love in it.As for complaints; my biggest one is surprisingly less of a general complaint but moreso one boss; magic is weird in this game and the way it tracks you does not feel great. One boss (the priestess) in particular shows this off more than any other with 3 adds that spam high damage magic alongside her own high damage magic. Alone, the boss is already annoying, but with the adds I imagine that a few controllers may be broken by the time the games complete. There are also a few bugs here and there, although, again, AND FOR ME, none of these were game breaking. Just weird little things that either required me to f4 at worst or little ones that were just quirky and weird. Also poise & super armor are a bit hit and miss for me in this game. The worst offender IMO is poise based around melee skills. Some enemies like to attack ALOT, and when you've gotten a skill charged that requires a long time to charge it only to be interrupted by some quick attack it's a bit frustrating to say the least.Overall I recommend Enotria. if you like Souls games I imagine you'll enjoy this. It definitely feels like a more budget souls game in some ways (things like voice acting not existing for every NPC) but the guts of it are fun. Parrying and striking enemies, switching mask, using abilities, all are pretty enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Amendment: I lucked out when playing the game and was able to play to completion. There are other players that encountered bugs like gates to the next area not opening, essential ladders not appearing, elevators and levers not functioning (I did experience this one - but only for backtracking shortcuts), losing loot drops and memoria when bosses die at the same time, saves being deleted, healing items having reduced healing, mask lines becoming locked until switching loadouts, and others - without the demo save.I put all this upfront in that, you might experience the game mostly error free. Or can wait until more patches made.Original Review at Launch, mostly:short: A subjectively fun souls-like with many ways to build without ever needing to grind to be strong enough to progress.longer: I have a stricter definition of Souls and souls-like, so if you have a loose definition (e.g., you consider Armored Core VI, Ninja Gaiden, Hades, or Returnal as souls-likes), then I've already lost you in this review. I'll take the Funny and if you absolutely can't help it, I'll take your points too. Give your clowns shelter under my banner.I normally do not enjoy Souls or souls-likes (stricter definition). I am enjoying this more than my irks and quips. There are a lot of tweaks and polish I'd like to see. And there is a lot for me to yet still do and try out.I'm not one for grinding and in terms of progression. And so far, I don't have to. Among the weapon types that drop, the resources that I've discovered from exploring and defeating enemies in my path, the memoria (experience and currency) I've acquired and the items that convert into memoria, a vendor NPC, the interchangeable aspects that influence stats, and having at least one usable mask option - I've never needed to grind and still have ways to overcome the enemies or bosses ahead.Reiterating: For progression.Now IF I want to try out different masks, I'll probably need to backtrack or acquire them on a New Game+ unless something opens up later to quickly acquire those shards.Other little things: There are some attack combinations that will execute a little faster if you perform them in certain orders, e.g., longsword's light attack into a heavy attack or polearm's light attack into a heavy attack. But that specific tidbit is not true of every weapon class.There is an elemental defense rock-paper-scissors style system for some enemies. I've stubbornly ignored it without issue so far, but it might catch up to me as enemies are surviving more than a stamina bar's worth of attacks now.Some weapon classes will feel nicer than others in terms of fluidity. e.g., the longsword and polearm for example have a nice flow you can get going with them. Versus the colossal weapons, you'll need to be more careful with the timing as a dodge attack can cause that next light attack to be slower than a heavy attack and deal far less damage than a heavy attack. And if you wanted to do a light attack and NOT a dodge attack, you'll have to wait a bit or figure some other way to achieve that. Edit: I am now exclusively using colossal weapons for the 2nd region onward of the playthrough. There are openings - parry can create some, other times you can dodge to get in position at the end of a string and go for the heavy attack. If the enemy is unraveled, I tend to do 40%~60% of a boss's health, but it's getting to that unravel point (and for someone that parries well, that would probably make everything easy - but for me that falls for most feints, oh boy.)The attacks or passives you think would have super armor (hyper armor?) can frequently get knocked down. Not sure if this is the directional force that the devs mentioned (e.g., if you're doing an overhead vertical attack coming down and an enemy does a rising attack that hits you in the face first - you're going to get flinched). Though still not sure about the passives that make it sound like you should have super armor for a brief duration - only to be interrupted within 0.1 to 1 second of getting the buff.I'm not much of a parry sensei. It's nice when I can recognize what an enemy is going to do to get that parry timing down, but I have a shortcoming in that area in any game. When you get the parries down on a foe, figure out the openings, it becomes a nice exchange. I still haven't explored the gems that impact the parry enough to say one way or another on those. There is no guard - which is a hard adjustment for me. There is a partial parry, where you don't deflect the attack fully, but will take damage and may take a little longer for you to regain control of your character - and those can feel stiff if you whiff consecutive parries.I'm not the best person to talk about performance. I tend to adjust settings down as needed to achieve 1080@60FPS and once I have that - I just keep going. The scenery looks beautiful when the settings are ultra and occasionally I'll look at a scene or environment to gasp (sometimes in horror at the gruesomeness of a scene), but reiterating I do tone settings down.At the time of this writing - there are some bugs out there. Some more cumbersome than others. e.g., you unlock an elevator shortcut and kick down a ladder, then the game forgets you've done so and you can't take that shortcut back. Or inventory crashes when interacting with certain parts of the game and once you realize that's what is causing it - you need to return to the main menu first, then go back into the game do interact with your inventory. Or one time when I died, caused a world render issue. My death is that traumatic for the game world and I get it.Story - still piecing it together. So far, I think I'm an unpaid heckler meant to disrupt everyone else's performances.The music that I have heard is amazing. I can't hum it yet, but I love most of what I've heard and there are two places I wouldn't mind leaving the game on just to hear the music so far (title screen, theatre).Not sure if there is missing audio yet. Sometimes, I'll see subtitles, but won't hear anything. Largely for NPCs out in the wild.And then the list of things I'd like to see improved (without completely overhauling the underlying gameplay mechanics):1. A way to jump through menus faster such as D-Pad Left or D-Pad Right scrolling up or down a page (might have to figure how this works for shop)2. Option to turn off Vibration on controller.3. Option to rebind buttons on controller[strikethrough]4. Option to rebind buttons on keyboard and mouse[/strikethrough]5. At vendor NPC(s), having the weapon class listed6. At vendor NPC(s), having a way to increase quantity increments by 10 at a time (e.g., at present, if I wanted to buy 99 nuggets and fragments, that'll be 198+ inputs instead of 20+.)7. Ambiguous effect of Super Armor so far on Greater Inner Might and Armored Bruiser. Interpreted it as being able to resist flinching / staggering, but have gotten plenty staggered with it.And then things that are my own personal tastes that would be an overhaul:A. A pause (even if it is a two step process that obscures the entire game screen)[strikethrough]B. Adjusting colossal weapons' dodge attack - at present - they are a liability without the reward. Slower than a heavy attack, deals about as much damage as a light attack, doesn't have any additional super armor, and even with Trained Arm and True Grit perks - deals less than a heavy attack. Alternatively, the ability to toggle off the dodge attack or a set of weapons that doesn't have dodge attacks would be nice, since I usually just want the light attack after a dodge.[/strikethrough]I digress, enjoying it overall and this is my little review as I pad my time listening to music and pretend like I'm playing the game. (On a seriouser note, I do like the build possibilities at this point without a complete respec. It is also possible to respec stats later in the game, but at no point did I feel like I gimped myself).

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy a parry-focused souls-like, I think Enotria has much to recommend it. The setting is beautiful. It's pleasant to play a souls-like without all the dead-bodies, hopelessness, and intrinsic depression. The combat, while it does have bugs that need to be fixed and can be janky, is generally satisfying and engaging. However, being able to perfect parry is an essential aspect of gameplay, often you get punished for dodging with ranged attacks that encourage you to stay close to the enemy and parry. Everything can be parried, both physical attacks and magical attacks. The game has no unblockable attacks ("perilous attacks" for the Sekiro players or "Fury" attacks for the Lies of P players) which makes combat easier. Also, the parry window is very generous compared to Sekiro and Lies of P and can be increased with certain perks from the skill tree. Moreover, levelling up does make a huge difference in your ability to survive in the game. In addition, the build system, while unnecessarily complicated and difficult to understand at first, makes a profound difference in gameplay. The element of every enemy is labelled, so you are able to choose a weapon and build that maximize the damage it takes. The build system might be too strong, for example having a Radiant weapon makes the 2nd area of the game a trivial exercise. It's true the game has significant faults; there are significant bugs and glitches that need to be repaired. I did have two early bosses who froze after I parried their attacks for a specific length of time and I had a glitch where I fell through elevator platforms that were supposedly solid. I agree with people who claim that the game should have been marketed as "early access" with the final version being released in March after the developers "Path to Improvement" fixes and polishes the game. Some other pros and cons: the game has enjoyable music in addition to the beautiful setting and a con: its story is completely opaque and uninteresting. However, I wasn't play for the story so it didn't bother me that its lore and writing are, frankly, terrible. So, if you enjoy a good parry-focused souls like, you have two valid paths: 1) buy it now and I think you'll still find the investment in money and time worth it or 2) put it on your wishlist and purchase it in March. I hope this review helps you make a decision.

Due to a bug i am now softlocked out of all content regarding elevators that i have to call with a switch. This makes it impossible for me to finish certain quest lines and reach the true ending. currently can't recommend itMost Bad Reviews are about not customizable Keybinds on PC, do not let this deceive you, this is a good game, not for everyone but for what it wants to be. So setting expectations is important.Who is this for:- i would say for people that like the gameplay feel of demon souls and dark souls, because animations are long there is an input delay and you can not cancel most of them. If you only played elden ring chances are you will not like thisWho is this not for?  - people that play with M+K, because ATM no customizable Keybinds (they are working on it)- people that expect a highly optimized game, without any flaws and fail to see that this is a prime example of an indie/AA game - people that can not handle invisible wallsThoughts about the game:It is not fully optimized there are a few bugs and they kinda messed up your reset points for your "souls" if you die, because i can happen that they are in a spot that has no escape (you fall form a cliff, land on 1 pixel that your character can stand, stand there for a few sec than fall further down and your souls are not atop where you fell first but were you fell last)If you do not pay attention to the ailments and "elements" of your enemies you will have a hard time, because you will lack dmg. Also healing is a more deliberate choice.Pretty cool is that i can downgrade my weapons/spells if i want to get the materials back, i will not get my souls back but this way i can experiment more however so far (2nd area) i have more than enough mats to upgrade a good chunk of weaponsThe difficulty so far is i would say average, i killed most bosses in 3-4 tries (i normaly run 20-30 on most souls bosses because i do not use big tactics) In short if you are aware that this is not a triple A, high polished game you will have a great time because so far voice acting is good, the visual design is pretty cool and not done before and if you have a grasp of the combat it is pretty solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I start my review, I want to clarify one thing:  Check the game times of all these reviews.  If it's under two hours, most likely it'll be praised highly.  Obviously the first chapter is the demo area and is the most refined from the game.  But most players once it goes beyond that the cracks start to show.As someone that has reviewed this game during its demo phase, not much has improved.  Stability in frames has in certain retrospects but not without some sacrifices.The game seems unpolished.  The way it was in the demo but poorer in its release.  The blurryness and pure saturation of its orange tones makes the whole game very one dimensional and not easy on the eyes after an hour or two.The buttons for me does not work.  It either has a 1.5 second delay or it will refuse to activate a "bonfire" or what nots.  I swapped to 3 controllers and never had an issue with the demo but it is on this.  I noticed when I went to windows mode it was fine but very inconsistent.People may think its close to Lords of the fallen due to its clunkyness and granted I didn't enjoy LotF I respect for what they tried to do (minus the final boss).  I think most peopled failed with Lords is that they tried to play it as if it was DSIIIThe animations:  This is my biggest gripe.  Different swords to use but its the same type of animation? It shows lazyness. How a short sword has the same speed as a giant hammer is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beyond me. The game has some uniqueness but at the sacrifice of the players ability to understand what's going on in terms of states and specific names tailored to Enotria.  The lack of VA (which in they put in their project update for 2025 to have that changed) and on top of that the same repetitive song for each chapter (that seems out of place btw) is a bit laughable. As for this developers first game to release, it's okay.  I think if they cooked a bit and not half ass a game and then "finish it" by 2025 maybe I wouldn't be so harsh, but its very difficult to be forgiving for a $50 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Dungeon Goblins, Don't normally Give many Reviews but i feel its needed. So to start, if i could give this a meh or Neutral neither Thumbs up or thumbs down i most Certainly would with this game. I may have only 22 Hours but i Finished the game and took my time doing so. First of all Lets talk about Positives: The Story is Very Simple but Also Really Interesting, the music for the most part was actually well Done Despite what felt like a limited amount. The Combat was Actually Fun and i loved the Element status effect system they have created. I think The best thing about the game was Certain Boss Designs in how they looked and i Really like the Picturesque Views In the game. I was Interested in the use of masks with Buffs rather than Gear Sets which May seem simple but i actually liked its uniqueness. Negative Sides: Almost everything i mentioned in the Positives also has a negative to it. Music was Repetitive and at points got so annoying that i eventually turned the music down and Eventually off all together. Boss designs were nice but for some Bosses that's all they had to them and there were many i actually don't even remember because they didn't drag my attention. I will leave these few Light Negative here and move on to the more bigger stuff.Now the Even Bigger issues: Element system was made out to be really important at the Beginning of the game and was suppose to be paired with the fact you can have 3 Changeable mask load outs where you can have different weapons and abilities to swap on the go for rotational Builds. Honestly, it felt useless a waste of time and not needed. Which is a problem when the Centre point and main features of the game Is literally These Two things. At Starting zone i Found a Nice Colossal Weapon with sick element And never changed it until a bit near the end and only for maximisation It really wasn't needed i just Changed it on a whim. Literally all the weapons in the game and all the different elements with Certain bosses having "Weaknesses" to certain elements and it wasn't needed, I beat the game with one Starter zone Weapon and i never changed my mask once, Same mask throughout the game just upgraded. I never felt like my gear was An issue or felt the need to change like in some other games. So it felt like all those weapoons and no need for them. Although i did check out new weapons from time to time to see what they did to find each class of weapon has the same animation swings. One Saber is like every other saber, Every Greatsword is like every other etc etc and each one also had similar stats until literally the last zone when its not even going to be used unless you do NG+ Beside that the moveset's of bosses were Fairly simple but fun but i found a boss or 2 that at times Bugged out Due to the Surroundings. You fight one on an incline and his abilities Just mess your lock on camera up and you cant see Anything and then get trashed or stuck. Besides all these bad points i still feel the game has solid Potential and the foundations of the game are Solid. More optimisation & Balancing of weapons and elements will Go along way and make it even more enjoyable. If i was the rate the Game Overall id say about  Id Probably say get it when its on offer if you aren't sure but i don't Regret Buying this. Its always Nice to Support new Develops that try there hand to push new ideas, Concepts or just Do there own Interpretations on Pre-existing Concepts.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the critisim stated here, with some being valid and some not, I definitely recommend this game. Because Enotria - The Last Song is not trying to be as grand as all the other Soulslikes that have come up in the last years like Elden Ring or Lords Of The Fallen, and you should not expect that of it. Looking at the development team, you can see that this is not the work of a studio with dozens or hundreds of people, but with a small team that wanted to tell their own beautiful story.The gameplay is fun and the english voiceaction is truly on peak. The world is diverse and full of details. The game shines a light on a part of folklore that should deserve more attention, not because of its grim-ness, but because of the opposite. However, I do find it strange that they already know what things they want to improve about the game, with more animations and voiceovers being on the list of things that will be added until March 2025, because it makes me question why they have released it so early and did not wait a bit longer to include these things before the release, not after.Regardless, if you are reading this, I wanna tell you that this is a great game with fun gameplay, hard bosses and a stunning world with lots of little details. I can only recommend it because I can see that the developers truly made Enotria - The Last Song with lots of love, and that is something very rare nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: A soulslike game that stays quite true to the souls formula. The main aspect that is different is the environment, the aesthetic is nowhere near as grim as many of the soulslike games, with much of the game being out in sunny middle ages Italy. The environment, enemies, and bosses, all look pretty cool, and I think a change of scenery for this genre is welcoming. In general, if you like soulslike games then I can almost guarantee that you will like this game, apart from Dark Souls, Elden Ring, etc, I would say it is one of my favourites, I prefer it to something like Nioh for example. Definitely worth your time if you are into this genre. If this genre is not really your thing, or you find it hit or miss (and I would say it can definitely be hit or miss), then judge whether you want to buy it by reading a bunch of reviews first to get a good sense of the gameplay and environment and so on before checking it out, but even in that case I would recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Enotria: The Last Song immerses players in a richly detailed world that reimagines the soulslike genre with vibrant, sunlit landscapes inspired by Italian folklore. From its unique visual design to an innovative combat system, the game offers a refreshing departure from the typical dark and foreboding atmospheres.World-Building and Visual DesignEnotria: The Last Song stands out for its exceptional world-building and breathtaking visual design. Set in a world inspired by Italian folklore, the game transports players into a vibrant, meticulously crafted reality that breaks away from the gloomy aesthetics typical of many soulslike games. Instead, players journey through sunny mountainsides, lively cities, and enchanting skies, each location rich in details that make exploration a true visual feast.Unforgettable Boss Battle MusicOne of Enotria’s most memorable elements is its music, especially during boss battles. The soundtrack is not only catchy but also enhances the intensity and emotions of these encounters. With diverse compositions, the music keeps players immersed, never becoming monotonous, and adds an emotional depth to the gameplay experience.Combat System and MechanicsThe combat system in Enotria introduces innovative mechanics, such as the aspect system and the use of masks, bringing a fresh approach to gameplay. These elements allow for various strategies, enabling players to customize their playstyle. However, at times, combat can feel a bit clunky, with some enemy attacks seeming unintuitive, which can occasionally lead to frustration during battles. Despite these minor issues, the unique mechanics bring a new perspective to the genre, providing players with a refreshing combat experience.Final ThoughtsEnotria: The Last Song is a visually stunning journey with rich world-building and an unforgettable soundtrack that elevates the overall gameplay experience. Despite minor flaws in the combat system, the unique mechanics and captivating locations make it a worthwhile adventure for genre fans. With a few refinements, Enotria has the potential to become a standout title in the soulslike category.

_childDocuments_.review: Enotria: The Last Song is a Souls-like that tries to stand out from the rest of the genre by trying some new things and experimenting. For example, it uses masks that you can find throughout the world that you can get from bosses or defeating enough of a certain enemy that all have certain attributes that define your build. In my experience so far, they all have their use cases and all of them feel viable in their own way. The bosses and enemies have enough variation between them to keep all of your encounters interesting. The game also makes use of staples of other Souls-Likes such as the Stagger bar, parry system, and Bloodborne viscerals. With all of that said, Enotria: The Last Song does have it's problems, the biggest one being, at time of posting, optimization. I have a 3.7 Ghz. CPU, an Nvidia 4070, and 32 GB of RAM and I have to run at minimum graphics.  I also capped my frame rate at 60 but even then I still sometimes dip towards 30. Because I had a humble beginning to PC gaming, this is something that I can look past in the grand scheme of things.Enotria: The Last Song is by no means a masterpiece, but it's a fun game to pick up if you want something similar to Sekiro or Bloodborne. If your still uncertain about wanting this game or not, the developers said that they have a big update scheduled for November that addresses a lot of problems that the game has currently. If you have a good PC to run the game on and you don't mind having a few low poly buildings when you look over a view, you will like this game. _childDocuments_.review: I've just finished the game and there's a lot of potential but also a lot of problems. Early access probably would have been a good idea to iron out some of the problems before releasing it into the wild.The game looks great and and runs great and at the beginning the exploration is good too. But a game like this succeeds or fails though is entirely on it's enemies, bosses and combat, which is clunky.  Enemies and bosses are robotic and not in a good way like Lies of P.  There are lots of new mechanics. Different enemies use weapons with elements which in theory you're meant counter with a weapon using another specific element but I just reverted to a strength build and hit everything as hard as possible. The devs wanted players to parry but I also got through the entire game without parrying all but one or two bosses. Most enemies were just way too easy and predictable.There were also things like lines (ashes of war) which you need to charge up through combat but I got through the entire game without making use of them. It's hard to recommend the game at the moment because they really do need to do a lot of work. If they want to look for a bit of inspiration, look no further than Lies of P. Combat is what makes or breaks these games and in this respect it isn't good enough.  Normally I would immediately go into Ng plus but there's not really enough to justify that either. For example doing Ng plus in Wukong allowed me to fully unlocked my relics and reach full power when I eventually got to Ng plus plus plus. Ultimately it wasn't a big deal getting there but the fact that Ng plus unlocked new weapons and relic perks was motivating. In this game there isn't much point and maybe the devs can address this in their road map! Give me a reason to keep playing. But mostly make the combat better.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game worth buying? No (at least not right now, it's Early Access but they're not saying it's Early Access, so yeah I feel a bit scammed)Is it a bad game? Not really? But there are a lot of things that make me feel like no one actually play tested itOverall solid 3/5 that probably got released now and not next year just for budget reasons so, fine, fair, we have to be realistic.The Good:- Very nice premise, it's trying way too hard to be exactly like FromSoft's games in terms of presenting the story, and it only partly works. The story however seems interesting, the feel of the world is a nice change of pace and overall well designed.-Some minor QoL improvements over other soulslikes, nothing to write home about-Loadouts remove encumberance which I like-Mask lines seem cool (I always play weapons only in soulslikes, but the few I've tried actually seem fun to use if it's your thing)- The mechanics of the status effects are really nice, I'm usually the "this weapon feels good I'm using it for the whole game" so having to change weapons for different elements (and making it feel good) was actually refreshing (BUT, see weapons point below), reeeaaaaaaaly like the whole elements & statuses thing. Great idea, great execution The Bad:- (keep in mind I almost never used Mask Lines which improve upon this point but you still need to use the weapon to charge the line soooooo) Weapons don't feel good to use, like any of them. They are all just ok and there's what, 4 types of weapons? Maybe I missed some I don't know- Enemies also all feel the same, weak mob that sometimes throws stuff, less weak mob you can still one shot by staggering, strong mob you need to dodge away from. They look different, they have different animations but they feel EXACTLY the same, attack timings etc.The Ugly:- By far the worst feeling parry I've used in any game. The developers obviously want you to use it but they made it feel extremely janky, the animations of the enemies don't feel like they match the parry times, I've never used a mechanic before that I felt I got worse with over time- The dodge might even be worse, I'm not sure if it's the i-frames (or lack there of, which obviously is perfectly fine, again would be a nice change of pace, if we could actually parry attacks but see the point above)- The camera was the reason I felt like I died at least half of the time. You can literally not see where you're stepping (and no, this is not realistic or immersive, trust me I teach fighting), it is WAY too often that your character goes invisible because you're too close to the wall, so now we can't parry or dodge because there's no feedback from the enemies or any other animation to indicate if you're successful or not because that changes the time you can use your next dodge/parry- Wall clipping happens way too much. Not even 10 hours in and I'm already giving away my down time where I can hit bosses so I can reposition in the centre of the arena so I don't get clipped into a wall or a step or something, Together with camera, well over half the times I diedA Fistfull of Bad:Accessibility is the worst I think I've ever seen in a game. No key rebinding, second major area is so white it blinds you and you can't see pickups, as mentioned camera is awful. All in all, just, nahA few points more:The game has potential. I'll probably give it a try next year after their mentioned updates, I was looking forward to it after the demo, but if I could refund right now I would (well, maybe I wouldn't because but just for "I wanna see what they do with it" reasons). Good premise, close to a good execution but just missed it. As I said, it would easily be a MUCH better game but budget is budget and I'm genuinely excited for the studio's future games. Just take this game and polish it,  add to it, stick a 2 at the end and it'll be good

_childDocuments_.review: I finished three runs (2 NG and 1 NG+), completing all the quests, endings, collecting all the weapons, and trying out several classes. Final (and honest) thoughts on the game’s quality.I'll start with what impressed me the most, which are environments and world design. I found them sensational, both from a visual standpoint and in terms of design and interconnectedness within the gameplay. From these points of view, they rank among the best in souls-like games.The combat system and balancing are also good: it’s not a particularly complex game, but it requires the right concentration, especially in the first run. I probably would have made the boss fights a bit harder, but that’s just my personal opinion. I like the mask-switching mechanic, although I think the awakening mechanic could have been made more important: switching masks during combat was more for the fun of it than for the actual utility of activating the awakening, as awakening abilities are almost never truly 'game-changing.' Maybe some perks could be nerfed, and the awakening abilities could be strengthened, making this original and interesting mechanic more useful.In terms of enemies, I didn’t find anything particularly wrong or unfair, with one exception: a boss fight in the church of Falesia in NG+. They are four enemies who all use ranged attacks, some capable of one-shotting, and they are often hard to see because they’re covered by the other’s attacks. In my opinion, it becomes too random a fight and less about the player's skill.From a narrative standpoint, I found it enjoyable, both in terms of the main lore and the quests.If I had to point out what convinced me a little less, it would be two thing:1. I struggled to empathize with the NPCs and gods (with a few rare exceptions, like Moretta and Pulcinella himself). Maybe a bit more could have been done with some of them to help players to love or hate them rather then remain indifferent.2. The boss fights. Aside from maybe a couple of them, I found the others not very exciting, both in terms of movesets and visually.However, it’s important to highlight that the most crucial thing was never done wrong: the movesets are always readable and never 'confusing' like in other titles, and this is definitely something to appreciate.But of course, these are entirely personal opinions. In conclusion, I find it a game absolutely worth recommending, which will definitely appeal to fans of the genre. Its greatest strength lies in its wonderful environments and their exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just beat the game. and while yes, we are all coming down from the high from the Elden Ring DLC and then Wukong. I'll just give my thoughts here:1. Game length and time.I beat the game in about 18 hours and explored pretty much everything. I got every mask achievement. I did all of the red portals and beat all of the bosses. Most of these bosses didnt give me any trouble at all once I got the hang of parrying. The game Devs say it is about 40 hours to beat the game and explore everything and maybe I didnt explore every crevice but I pretty opened every door, went through every zone and path and unlocked whatever I could find.2. Combat and Feel of game.The combat feels nice at times and then other times it does not. The game doesnt really feel optimized with some bosses and enemy types. There are CLEARRR victors in terms of the weapons, masks, etc. But honestly it doesnt even matter as the game is not that hard so you can pretty much clear anything with any set up as long as you are parrying. The dodging in this game does NOT I frame. So even if you perfectly dodge there is a slight delay and there is a tiny immunity/no damage timer on it. Also some of the mobs when you are on a cliff would clip hit you and you would clip off the side. So dont lock on and stay as far from the edge as possible.3. Bugs.There are A LOT of random bugs (falling through the floor, getting caught on the edges of elevators and dying, phasing through the floor, UI bugs (on Keyboard and mouse) where you select the quantity of an item to use. A few times while traveling my "runes" would disappear. I had random crashing in the game (just counted and it was 26 times) as well and was taking an unusual load on my PC (I have a pre-built $3,000 computer that runs games on ultra settings no problem).4. Storyline and Music and Locations/Graphics.The storyline honestly didnt really make 100% sense to me and didnt really seem like there was a coherent story throughout. Lies of P had a better story and explanation of how each boss contributed to the story and this game didnt really do that for me.Music for certain bosses was AMAZING. It was like replaying the Witcher 3 with better music. My ONLY problem with this is that there wasnt enough OST to go around and 1/2 the time you are exploring in the open world there is no music.Locations/Graphics. There are 3 Chapters to the Game and each Chapter had 2 distinct feels to them. The locations themselves were done great. They felt coherent there were no random invisible walls. However from certain angles the assets would lose their quality and would glitch out. (again an optimization problem).Level Design: Honestly the level design was pretty good. There were certain times that had me hoping to get to a save point but the way all of the maps intertwine and flowed with each other was really cool.Final Thoughts : Its a solid 5/10 game. _childDocuments_.review: Note: CHATGPT IS USED TO FORMAT AND CORRECT GRAMMER. THESE ARE MY OWN THOUGHTS.After completing one full playthrough of , I’d like to share my thoughts on what the game does well and where it misses the mark. I won’t discuss bugs, glitches, or performance issues as that’s not my objective here. Instead, I want to highlight the bright spots of  and areas where it fails to embrace those strengths.The primary reason I bought  was its environment. I love contrasts in games—joy and sorrow—elements that  tries to portray but doesn't fully embrace. The first region, Quinta, is full of vibrant colors, beaches, and charming houses, but there’s a lack of visible sorrow. Although the narrative justifies this to some extent, a more striking representation of madness would have added depth. For example, using a corpse as a literal puppet could have been a bold choice. This isn't a suggestion, but rather an expression of what I felt was missing.The issue becomes more apparent when compared to . In "Krat," you can feel the chilling consequences of what went wrong. I don’t want  to adopt the same gloominess, but to reflect the story’s impact on its enemies and environments more effectively. The game tells us things are wrong, but I rarely felt it beyond some bloodstains on the ground.After the first region and parts of the third, the game’s beauty is undermined by a lack of attention to its landscapes. There are few areas that offer a breathtaking view of the region, which is a missed opportunity.  succeeded partly due to its stunning landscapes, and while  isn’t an open-world game, it could have provided at least one moment akin to entering "Lyndell, the Royal Capital."The gameplay is, at best, decent, with lots of untapped potential. The biggest issue is the lack of  features. There are many weapons, skills, spells, masks, and aspects, but their functionalities are unclear. The game doesn’t show detailed stats or effects for these elements, which discourages experimentation.A dedicated testing area with max-level equipment could have allowed players to better understand the mechanics and build options, similar to the puppets in the Hotel in .The enemy variety felt lacking, not visually, but in their attack patterns. Most enemies required the same approach, with their speed being the only thing that evolved. The lack of distinct patterns made it unnecessary to remember movesets, diminishing the challenge and depth.Dealing with multiple enemies was difficult due to their AI coordination, as they often covered each other perfectly. These encounters were rare but noticeable.Regarding the  system, I found it more practical to maintain distance than to parry, which seems counter to the game's design. Attacks often started slow and then became lightning-fast, making timing difficult. Maintaining distance and attacking during gaps felt more reliable. Normal attacks also deal posture damage, so breaking posture with light weapons feels underwhelming since fatal attacks don't deal much damage.Enemy attacks often felt disconnected, which hurt the flow of combat. For example, a guard’s thrust attack followed by a radiant slash should reward dodging or positioning, but the slash would hit regardless, making these attacks feel independent rather than part of a cohesive chain. This disjointed feeling was most apparent with the final boss in the fourth area.I don’t focus much on the story in these types of games, and  was no exception. While I read everything in the compendium, the story didn’t engage me. The opening cutscene felt overwhelming, and I didn’t feel compelled to follow the narrative closely. From what I’ve gathered, the story is decent but not particularly memorable.Several features significantly affected the experience: The game feels unfinished, with many basic quality-of-life features missing. Considering the competition, games like , , and  offer more polished experiences for similar prices. While I understand that this is a smaller studio, the current state of  doesn’t justify its cost.
