_childDocuments_.review: Short version: The game is not very good. It starts off pretty fun but it gets worse and worse as you play more. I would personally not recommend playing this game at the moment, maybe wait until it hits the sales at 10€ and some patches have come in - if they come in.Long version:The game starts of fairly well, enemy variety and the early areas are pretty good. Gameplay is not too difficult, the parry timings are very generous and bosses dont deal an absurd amount of damage for the most part. But the further you get into the game the more obnoxious the enemy and boss variety gets. You have to parry some bosses - and im not joking - literally 50 times or more to get a hit in with anything that is not a saber, longsword, or a mace. All the bigger weapons are almost useless, you just cant get a hit in with how slow they are and how fast the average boss is. Normal enemies are recycled as bosses frequently. You fight the same guys over and over again and by the end its just not fun. The overwhelming majority of bosses in this game are just tedious to fight, not difficult, but just a health and parry sponge. Some of the unique bosses are ok, not spectacular, not terrible and just mediocre.It seems like they also copied the worst parts of other soulslikes, mainly the input reading from Elden ring. Some bosses have a ranged punish when you take a sip, and this comes out so fast you actually just cant heal.  The worst part is that it cancels your heal, so you just get stunlocked and die. One later game boss in particular has a 5 projectile combo that can kill you at 2300hp. It feels very cheap, like an artificial difficulty thing. You can obviously work around this by timing your heals when the enemy is doing its 10 trillion hit spam combo but honestly its just not fun. You can also abuse those projectiles by baiting out that attack and then parrying them to build up posture damage, but now we are well into the not-fun territory of gameplay.Overall the balance of the different aspects in the game is very bad. 3 of the skill trees seem to be almost useless, and in the one that is useful there are only a few skills to pick. The player character has no poise with small weapons, and only a little bit of poise with the bigger weapons, but with them you have to trade hits. The "magic" system is pretty much useless. You have to spec in heavily to that to make it even remotely fun, and even then you have to actually hit enemies to charge the spells/skills so at this point its a melee build with extra steps (these abilities start at 0 charge with every boss and charges with hits). Some bosses are impossible to lose to since they are so easy, and some others can be very difficult and there isnt really a logic to this in terms of when you fight them in the game (later bosses are not necessarily more difficult i mean).In order to have fun with this game i think the combat system and overall balance of weapon catgories and number of parries needed for a riposte needs to be reworked - heavily. Most of the masks and aspects also just seem useless so maybe that needs some work as well. Heavier weapons need to deal more damage in relation to the fast ones, and attack probably two times faster (a +10 colossal might have 1000 attack power, and a saber 550, but the saber can attack at least 5 times more often). I regret the time i wasted in Souls Italy and will not be returning there any time soon. If you have to choose between starting your 40th run in Elden ring and this game, choose the 40th ER run.

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of big babies complaining in the reviews about how slow the attacks can be. Yes, this is a souls-like and you have to time your attacks! this is not ninja gaiden. button mashers, move along. I had the same complaints in the demo, but I quickly adapted (that's what you do in soulslikes, adapt). Once you learn the flow of combat, it is anything but slow. dodging and parrying are quite forgiving, giving you many ways to make space for your attacks. the element system is also a neat twist (one I assume a lot of angry reviewers never bothered to learn), giving you options to make fights easier or more challenging as you prefer. levelling weapons and masks is also very forgiving, allowing you to refund materials to use again. And you will; while it would be possible to grind and stumble through with a single build, it's quick and easy to build a mask, line and weapon build tailored to the boss you are up against. The world in this game is bright, colourful and vibrant, which is a nice change in the genre. the Renaissance thematic consistency throughout gives it a standout quality even in it's obligatory dark and moody Souls moments. The (uncommon) music is also a brilliant match for the boss fights that keeps me enthusiastic to jump in and try again. it's unfortunate that outside Quinta, there is mostly no ambient music. The atmosphere in the first city is perfectly executed, with enemies actually playing the music and shouting in the revelry that can be heard throughout. it would have been nice to see that continue in the rest of the game. I have not encountered any serious bugs, aside from a couple instances of frozen enemies, who have always quickly snapped out of it. for general polish I'd rate the game above dark souls itself, and on par with elden ring. Optimisation may be lacking, or maybe my hardware is. I find I often have significant frame sluggishness, even at the lowest graphics settings. That said, I'm playing on a lower end ryzen 5 and a GTX 980, so maybe it's a me problem. I'll say that ER does run much better on the same hardware, and while beautiful, Enotria is not noticeably more graphics intensive than it. The heavy filters many areas have could be part of the issue. Over all I'm sad to see this game get Mixed reviews; at 26 hours in I think it deserves better, and so far has been worth the entirely reasonable $50 CAD that I paid. that's less than the Erdtree DLC that just came out.

The animations feel intentionally misleading to make learning parry timings hard and I could never get them down. I'm a big fan of Sekiro, and despite some people saying the parry window is bigger in this game than Sekiro, I had a MUCH harder time getting them to work. _childDocuments_.review: Finished the game and absolutely love it. Straight off, this feels like Wuthering Waves mechanics with a souls flare. There are 3 character builds that can be flowed through along with special alts that charge from attacking. Personally I have found the combat to be good. The parry window is forgiving, but failing it has big stun potential. The running R1 is very slow which would be my only complaint. It's closer to a charged R2. If you're used to the wuthering waves mechanics and flowing through characters, this game is a blast for combat. The character is a bit floaty, but the hits have good feed back. A strange quirk I encountered was opening the menu in a boss fight causes the boss health bar to disappear. Characters also don't repeat what they've previously said. Overall the game is stunning and it runs well. I've only played with the Italian language, but for me everything is easy to grasp and the voice actors are *chef's kiss*.  My overall thought is this is not a souls like but a souls inspired. Don't go in expecting elden ring or lies of P. The mechanics are VERY different. Not all status effects hurt you, some offer benefits. Sadly the game is short if you're good at souls games. Each boss took one or two tries. There was so much more that could be explored. The Compendium is by far my favorite part. It's a nice little lore book, which I would die for in a souls game. Finding scraps about the world and getting to read them and meet the people is such a wonderful concept.

_childDocuments_.review: Enotria: The Last Song ReviewBy Thom Stone on HIGH Visual variety and fresh gameplay breathe new life into an oversaturated genre.LOW Lack of multiplayer. Some original ideas are underutilized.WTF You call that a final boss?Over the past decade, countless titles inspired by FromSoftware’s Souls have come and gone, but few have managed to stand out from the crowd or even meet the bar that’s been set, especially now that it’s been raised once again by the wildly successful Elden Ring DLC, Shadow of the Erdtree.Enter Enotria — a new and soon-to-be classic Soulslike from Italian studio Jyamma Games that dares to be different by drawing inspiration not only from FromSoftware, but also the rich cultural traditions and aesthetic appeal of Italy.Enotria is a world populated by people trapped in a never-ending play, doomed to perform their roles according to a script they didn’t write. This fate is interrupted by the player in the role of the Maskless One — he enters the scene as a mere puppet, but will ultimately go on to liberate the unwilling actors.This theatrical concept works well as a device to explain the reason why NPCs are stuck in a loop of performing scenes on the shoreline or dancing in the street to a melody that can be heard in various forms throughout the city of Quinta.According to Jyamma Games, the city of Quinta and its surrounding area were inspired by Tuscany, and this can be observed in small details like traditional Italian dishes found on tables, and imposing structures like the Church of Maja where the player must face their first boss. The virtual tour of Italy continues with later areas that are reminiscent of Venice (Litumnia) and Sicily (Falesia Magna).The combat is fast-paced and requires not just skill, but patience.The third-person perspective allows the player to see a broad view of their enemies and surrounding environment which allows them to telegraph enemy move patterns, tactfully dodging or parrying their attacks before going in for a strike, but they must also know when to step back and conserve stamina.Landing an attack charges (at varying speeds) up to four “mask lines” which are special attacks that deal different kinds of damage known as Ardore, which can be especially effective against certain enemies.A crucial piece of the gameplay for players to understand and take advantage of is that they get up to three loadouts which allow them to equip separate sets of weapons, quick items, mask lines and masks. Unlocking certain branches on Enotria‘s skill tree allows the player to select abilities to suit their style, like staggering weaker enemies whenever they successfully dodge an attack. Although the player can only alter the equipment, skills and abilities for each loadout at a checkpoint, they can switch between their loadouts on the fly, which is helpful when facing different types of enemies in a given area.There are many masks that can be acquired throughout the adventure. Some will be received upon defeating a boss, but the majority can only be crafted after collecting a certain amount of mask shards. It was satisfying to piece them all together and make my first mask — the Gardener. I automatically received it after farming gardeners (an enemy type that appears in the first area) and one of its effects is that it makes a certain healing item more effective. Later in the adventure, players can gather enough boss mask shards to make their corresponding masks which allows the player to use some of their abilities as mask lines.Apart from the masks, one of the most important mechanics is the elemental system which functions much like rock-paper-scissors. Certain mask lines or weapons infused with an element will be especially effective against an enemy aligned with another.For example, Vis, a status effect that inflicts dizzying damage, is super effective against enemies aligned with the poison effect, Malanno. Midway through the campaign I fought a god named Veltha, God of Strife who was aligned with Gratia (holy damage) but weak to Malanno, so I maxed out my favorite Malanno weapon and took pleasure as I watched her stagger and suffer from poison damage every time one of my attacks landed. Leveraging this vulnerability didn’t mean the fight was quick work, but it was significantly easier to wear her down than by using the other weapons in my arsenal.The level of difficulty presented by bosses like Veltha (both a powerful ranged fighter and relentless swordswoman) was on par with other Soulslikes, which is to say, very high. Thus, players who are new to the genre will need to learn the basics quickly if they are to progress. When it starts to feel impossible, they can always farm currency from enemies and use it to upgrade their equipment or level up before taking another stab at whatever boss they’re stuck on.Speaking of bosses, most of Enotria‘s were guilty of one cardinal sin or another, and for some, their vices manifest physically, such as the gluttonous cannibal Zanni who had feasted on fellow actors and turned into a balloon of a man with multiple mouths and an insatiable appetite. It was a delightfully horrifying and imaginative monster design. However, one of my favorite battles was the duo boss fight starring Balanzone and Pantalone. Rather than strong and silent types as many Soulslike bosses are, they were a comically dysfunctional pair, often damaging each other when trying to attack me while bickering throughout the fight, voicing their self-interest and avarice.Shockingly, the final boss proved to be the most underwhelming boss fight of the whole campaign. His attacks were fairly predictable and not much changed during his multiple phases, except that a few ranged attacks were added. At no point did I have to significantly change my approach — it was mostly just a matter of pulling it off. While the majority of Enotria is excellent, this mediocre final encounter was just one of a few things that left me feeling underwhelmed when all was said and done.Even though I didn’t need any help on the final boss, there were a few that made me wish I did. Summoning friends and strangers alike is one of the things I enjoy most about Soulslikes, as it adds to the feeling of “jolly cooperation” — a big part of what makes these titles so special to me. Unfortunately, there’s no online or multiplayer of any kind to be found here.There were also a few underutilized mechanics that are unique to Enotria, like the Ardore Burst — a stomp that staggers enemies and materializes platforms and ladders when the player stomps on a gold seal, allowing them to reach previously unreachable areas. Whenever I saw one, I’d be filled with the spirit of adventure and feel excited to see where it would take me. Sadly, they’re all too rare.It’s also worth mentioning that during my time with Enotria, I encountered some sudden difficulty spikes and observed some enemies with odd AI pathing getting stuck in certain places. The devs have since released a patch to address these issues and they plan to release more fixes in the near future.Ultimately, my time with Enotria: The Last Song was fantastic. The unconventional Italian theming swept me off my feet, and the gameplay was pleasantly familiar, yet offered enough differences and new ideas to let it stand on its own. If any Souls fans are looking for something to lighten up the dark autumn days that lie ahead, they should consider this summery theatrical adventure their remedy.Rating: 8.5 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: Enotria is good in the beginning. A lot of cool mechanics and fun learning how to utilize the elements to your advantage.The early bosses are fun, you get to learn the parry properly and they feel rewarding. The environment and art style is amazing, and I did enjoy the lore so far.Now, I haven't finished the game, I think I'm close to half way now and not sure if I'd continue the game. The bosses aren't anything special anymore since they become the "normal" enemy. There are multiple bosses that ends up being the normal enemy not far after you kill the boss version. Now, the boss version is more difficult of course, but the boss looses something when you keep meeting them over and over in the world.The biggest reason for my hesitance is the amount of enemies that stun lock you. I got beyond annoyed during some parts of the game. There's so many ranged enemies combined with quick moving enemies that stuns you and you end up not being able to move. The later bosses also becomes a waiting game. You just have to parry them for 5 minutes, repose, rinse and repeat! They're definitely less satisfying to kill after some time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite soulslike to date. With all the respect due to other games of the genre, I very often felt like they didn't even try to build a world, they just crafted a glorified boss rush with no secondary paths, no interconnections, hardly any shortcut, no looping back to previous areas, none of that. When I play Enotria, I feel like it's the closest to the first Dark Souls when it comes to level and world design, which is a fundamental part of my enjoyment of the genre.I did have some performance issues in a specific late game area, which I pretty much completely solved by lowering the graphic quality for that bit. We gotta be aware of what's inside of our PCs and sometimes we should just accept we can't play all games at ultra quality. Also, this game was made by an indie studio, I'm sure they'll work on making it run better but I won't really be mad at them if the game is not 100% optimized on the first week when much bigger studios took months to run decently. The combat is satisfying and the elements mechanic is well explained and there's a reminder on screen all the time, so it's really not hard to choose the right thing to do in any situation. The game might be a little easier than others, but you can craft your own difficulty by choosing your own challenges, just like in any other game of the genre. I'm playing with a very strong weapon as a main, so I won't complain it's easy since it's exactly what I'm trying to achieve by using a powerful build. The price tag is fair for the quality and the playtime it offers.I recommend this game to people who enjoyed the Souls trilogy more than the more recent Souls/Soulslike titles

Your character parses his general vicinity, slowly, with a fully extent arm. As if to add the last stroke of white to his cloud hes painting. I've never felt so frustratingly unsatisfied equipping and swinging an item named "ULTRAGREATSWORD"This was just one of the many things the combat does to leave you feeling empty and sad you just paid AAA prices for a game that I'd value at 10$ tops. The story is interesting and is delivered in a way that is easy to understand, exploring is rewarding, and the world design is logical to the point where it feels like people could have actually lived there without being inconvenienced by unfortunate level design elements (looking at you, FromSoftware). I love the Italian theme too. Very fun.Enemies and bosses were diverse in design and behaviour and to say that weapon design is unique is an understatement. Even consumable items are beautifully designed to the point where I found myself craving the foods (and not just the pizza)! Combat mechanics were a fun change too, with ranged attacks and magic all taking the form of abilities charged up through melee attacks. Statuses are double-edged (both buffs and debuffs at the same time, like for example, one that both increases the damage you take and the damage you deal), which created new challenges and is something I've never experienced before.My only criticisms of the game are the multitude of bugs. I cannot count how many times the game crashed on me for one reason or another. Sometimes there were days where I couldn't play due to the game crashing before I even loaded in. My greatest adversaries were the dogs and other 4-legged enemies as fighting them would result in a crash at least 90% of the time unless I killed them from range or they found a way to die on their own. I can't help but wonder if part of the problem is my sub-par PC but your experiences may differ. If you have the patience, however, the game is still well worth the trouble. 9.8/10 would play again... but maybe after a patch or two xD

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely very good so far. Barring length being a possible negative factor (I've heard it's on the shorter side), I'd easily put Enotria alongside 2023's Lies of P and LOTF as among the best non-fromsoftware soulslikes. The combat is solid, which is key to making these games work. It's on the easier side for one of these games, but definitely feels like a souls-like at its core. The parry is smooth and very satisfying. Weapons are impactful. Devs worked hard to provide lots of tools to help players follow along with the various changes they made to the souls formula (names for stats are different, new status effects, seperate ability system, etc.). Seems like there is solid build variety.Visuals are clearly not triple A, but still fantastic. And the art design is absolutely stellar. Voice acting is also great.Couple minor issues with gameplay: running/walking feels a little weightless (feels almost like there's a running animation, but the character is just sort of floating); sound design could use some work; optimization leaves a bit to be desired.

_childDocuments_.review: Enotria is an alright soulslike that I enjoyed my time with, even if it doesn't innovate much. It has some pretty good gamefeel, especially when it comes to general responsiveness, especially deflecting enemy attacks, and the way enemies react to your attacks (most of the time).However, parts of the game are inconsistent, where enemy movesets range from fair and fun to unfair and unintuitive to read (such as when in an attack the enemy hitbox spawns). Environments range from gorgeous to somewhat bland. Locations range from excellently interwoven (such as the first city area) to straightforward and linear. The limited number of movesets also makes finding new weapons not terribly exciting.But I know this game was made on a small budget by a small team and I think they accomplished something good and respectable. If you hunger for a deflect-focused soulslike, Enotria is a solid pick.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who likes its soulslikes, this one's absolutely incredible. The bugs, while present, aren't completely horrible and honestly the worst part of this game is that i have to uninstall and reinstall a C++ visualizer which is weird. Aside from all that the combat is fluid and fun (Please don't change Curtis's Roncone that thing's moveset is fine as is) and the upcoming changes to make the game feel even more interesting give me more to look forward to! The art direction is also stellar, using various places in Italy as a base and running wild with them made the setting feel new enough to want to see what was next. And oh my god, the music. Holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the soundtrack is one of the most incredible things i've heard. Curtis's theme is such a great way to tease how creative this team gets with its folk music, and I'm aching for more of it. The bosses are fun to fight, as well (the final one in particular, but the "secret" boss could use a bit more tuning), being perfect little amalgamations of this game's peaks. If there ever comes a sequel or a spinoff, I know it'll be absolutely incredible and will somehow surpass this in quality. My only advice is that this could have been in the oven for a few more months, just to hammer out bugs, remove the weird start-up jank, and flesh the game out a bit more with unique attacks for boss weapons and maybe balancing the game so BRT/ASN builds can shine as brightly as my fellow elementalists and battlemages! This game, for all its faults, is still one worth playing and checking out for yourself. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game from the first minute to the last. Combat imo is solid. The whole *elements* system is fun and I liked it because you can engage with it as much or as little as you want and still get through the game. _childDocuments_.review: "Enotria: The Last Song" is a standout action RPG that draws players into a beautifully crafted world inspired by Italian folklore. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ The game is a visual spectacle from an artistic point of view, the Italian themed landscapes, vibrant warm colors, spectacular vistas, architectures, costumes and music envelop the player in an awe inspiring soulslike interpretation of 'La Commedia Dell'Arte' from Italy, the love and work poured into every single detail is to be commended+ Great map design, each one of the 3 major zones that comprise the world of Enotria is full of secret passages, shortcuts, interconnected paths and loot to find, exploring the game's world is never a waste of time and it is actually quite fun+ A beautiful story that uses famous Italian folklore's characters to weave a memorable tale greatly enhanced by the compendium you can fill up as you explore and defeat bosses, the major bosses in the game all have really good 'last words' after defeat that really enrich the experience of defeating them+ In depth player costumization system, between the masks, the roles, the weapons, the spells and the passive you can tailor make your very own maskless one into 3 very distinctive builds easily swappable mid fightCon:- While the player costumization depth is very good borderline excellent, the enemy complexity is extremely basic, most enemies have very few patterns of attack that are often repeated between variation and sometimes even the bosses, the very basic nature of your enemies makes your character choice less impactful since you rarely have the need to swap masks or change weapons- Imbalanced combat design, Enotria is a parry based soulslike which tries to push the player to be aggressive and yet most of the enemies of the game have extremely long combos, very short openings (sometimes none) and extremely 'random' periods of dragging attacks that makes the most efficent way of fighting them a constant parry\ one light attack combo until the enemy stance is broken for a critical strike- Technical problems are present and can be troublesome, now there is a roadmap for their resolution but i still need to signal the fact that one of the major boss fights (Goddess of Strife) bugged so badly that she just stopped fighting and stood there watching me as i wacked her to 0 hp, couple that with some side problems to fix ( side quest npc are not voice acted for example)- The game lenght is not what advertised, i took my time to explore all i could find and even achived the true ending clocking my first full run at 18 hours which is absolutely fine...but advertising it as 40+ is a bit weirdEnotria the Last Song is a soulslike built with love, passion, heart but also inexperience and overreach ambition and it transpires from every moment you play, every magnificent landscape and beautifully written dialogue or page of lore is diminished by a very basic combat and imprecise understanding of the genre that can cause a bit of frustration. Yet i feel that overall Enotria is a pleasant experience that will keep you entertained for your entire playtrough, despite my gripes with some of its worse aspects i didn't regret one second of my journey in its beautiful lands. If you are a lover of soulslike and have experienced the major players already (Lies of P, Elden Ring, Lords of the Fallen, Nioh 2) or you are new to the genre and want to start with an easier entry level experience, then Enotria will leave you pleasantly surprised and will provide a satisfying, while bumpy, journey in very original and beautiful setting that deserves to be seen.Recommended  6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The TL;DR is that the game is good but it has some problems, buy it after a patch or two.PROS:- Parry system akin to Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, it's very satisfying to absolutely body enemies and they can't even touch you if you git gud.- Art direction is on point, there are three main areas in the game themed on real life aesthetics of location in Italy and I knew exactly where the inspiration came from.- The narrative is fantastic, it's a 3 act play with big finale. The focus is our companion guiding us onward to the finale. However there are other characters with insight worth listening to to deepen your understanding of what exactly is happening.-  The mask & aspect system is novel approach to crafting a build for a souls-like and it works very well with the game's theme. You are part of a play. You are acting out a part (or several) even if you don't know how that part(s) plays out in the end, so swapping between roles and costumes is natural.CONS:- No key remapping? What year is this? They have said this will be fixed, but it's so brain dead I'm keeping it in the review.- Bugs, there are a few that crop up here and there most are harmless, a frustrating one was a crash in the secret final boss when I got them down to like five hits away from death but that literally the only crash to desktop I experienced- The tutorial is at once too much and not enough. The way it presents it's information is by text dump, no bad, cease. I ended up skipping all the information do I could get back to fighting. The tutorial also force buys several early combat innovation perks. I doesn't feeeeel good, let me make my own choices you cowards. Anyway the tutorial is so tedious it gets ignored and core mechanics go unexplained and thus unexplored. The tutorial needs to not treat me like an idiot. If I pick up a mask, trust me to want to find out what it does same with items and weapons, and on that note...- Why the hell can't I alter my loadout without resting at a checkpoint? What needless obstruction is this? AND ON THAT NOTE!- Why are they called loadouts?! Everything else in the game is on theme. Why are they not called characters or some such?THOUGHTS ON ISSUES OTHERS HAVE MENTIONED:- People have complained the game is too brief. This, in my mind, is a wild take. If you run past everything, and first try every boss (skipping optional bosses) I reckon that you could maybe... Maybe complete the game in less than 6hrs or so. No-one is doing this. If we assume your an average player skipping extra content and just beeline for the main bosses your looking at 9-12hrs if we're being generous with your skill level. An average run with exploring is going to take 18-20+ hrs. That's just for one run through. The game is clearly intending for you to make multiple runs. 3 at an absolute minimum by my reckoning so your probably looking at 30-50hrs, your mileage may vary.- The high priestess boss is trash. And you know what they are right, it's not a well designed boss, 3 priestesses supporting a high priestess is an interesting boss fight. Getting spammed by the same holy magic spells from 4 different directions is not.- The true final boss can't be beaten is one I've seen crop up a bunch. There are a few bosses that heal, and yes this is very annoying. However there is a solution. various weapons have a status build up. There's one that specifically prevents healing by these bosses. Don't know about this mechanic because the tutorial is awful and they maybe skipped over the optional area and boss that do it to you.- I've seen a few people complain you can't respec you character. You can, you just have to beat one the hardest bosses of the game. The optional boss is in the second area about a third of they way in maybe earlier than that. Personally I love that that is how you get the ability to respec, but I get why people might not like that very much.FINAL WORDS (I promise):There's no doubt this was an ambitious project with a lot of hype to try and live up to. Especially since it's carrying the vaunted souls-like tag. As much as I've moaned and cringed about the problems, I ultimately don't think they're enough to deny the game a recommendation. I certainly don't think the release of this game was so bad as to say it realised in an unfinished state, perhaps an unrefined state. lacking in polish in one too many areas for a smooth release. Either way it has my recommendation but with perhaps just a couple asterisks on the end

_childDocuments_.review: I set this review as Positive because I believe it would be hypocritical of me to do otherwise, and because there's no way to set it to Neutral, but I do so with a fair warning: if your tolerance for the honest inexperience yet passion of a game dev is currently at the minimum and your standards will allow nothing less than your personal or maybe popular, absorbed and subsequently adopted interpretation of game design perfection, and everything else is a product of filth, unfit to even be looked at or tried, then this isn't a good time to pick up this game as it currently is riddled with a number of small or medium - but noticeable nonetheless - anomalies that, while they haven't personally ruined my gaming experience as I don't mind the occasional break from immersion and even find the comedic side to imperfection as long as it doesn't hinder my ability to progress in any meaningful way, they might for others that perhaps take videogames under a more, shall we say "austere" light and would rather don their tragedy mask upon the discovery that alas, indeed  is amogus, game is a scam because it's more than five to ten bucks etc...If you're like me and enjoy multiple games of varying budgets for what they are with a looser, more permissive - within reason - and personal perception of what quality any given product is supposed to meet, and enjoy a variety of genres including in this case the fairly widely recognised Soulslike, specifically for the style of the combat flow, exploration and RPG mechanics, then you might want to give this one a shot as it presents more than a few intriguing mechanics pulling inspiration from existing recognised combat design, with its unique twists and quirks like a very non-standard host of elemental damage types and status effects and a charming rock-paper-scissor style elemental resistance and weakness system.The world that you can explore looks visually appealing and focused on sunny, colourful environments as opposed to the more commonly known depressing, dark Souls style - nothing wrong with either, just pointing out the difference - and the RPG mechanics specific to this game make use of a rather dynamic attribute system which gives you ways to customise and adapt your build in more than one way on the spot rather than having to stick with just attribute points being levelled with experience points/currency.Gonna make a small remark on the price which seems to be a consistent concern, and for admittedly good reasons in this day and economy. I consider 45€ to be slightly above what I'd consider a fair price for this game. It's also half or less of what a typical AAA costs nowadays, so I do some quick math without much experience as an economist, but given that there indeed has been considerable production value within the hand-crafted elements and real work and passion put into this project made by a yet inexperienced but willing to learn team, if I had pre-existent full knowledge of the entire game, flaws and all, before buying it, I'd still do so, because the value I give it is ultimately the fun I got out of it.I can't wait to see what else this team wants to make release, and want to see them keep working on this rather ambitious, flawed yet charming project and to improve it, treat it as an opportunity to perfect the scene and act every day.

You can add 6 or so skills from a skill tree (a la Diablo 3), the different masks give different stat lines, weapons get upgraded, easy to swap weapons and consumables. - Controls are all what you would expect and in the right place. Attack, heavy attack, dedicated jump button, run, etc. Very, very similar to Elden Ring and the Souls games. I will add more and refine as I play. _childDocuments_.review: Got to play for an hour before I had to go to work today. This is NOT a "review". Just a minor preview of what I played so far. Graphically, the presentation is beautiful. Graphics are well done with your assortment of Nvidia and AMD tech and a wide assortment of graphical options to tweak to your heart's content. Audio is ridiculously well done. Can't wait to get to the more frantic battles and see what is in store for my ears then. Combat is fluid but you need to KNOW and LEARN something right off the bat. There are no shields. You parry or dodge. Think of it like how Bloodborne flowed and you'll get the hang of it quick. Learn to parry though. it's your friend in this game. There is a LOT to learn when it comes to combat. There's an assortment of effects that can be used by you and your enemies. If your enemy is using one kind of "power" then you need to use something that they're weak to and not strong against. You also NEED to have at least 3 builds you can switch on the fly because of these "powers" you can get. They can also effect you negatively so you need to pay attention and LEARN what each does. The game gives them, from what I"m guessing, Italian names and you REALLY need to learn what each does and provides for and against. It requires you using your brain far more than any other Souls-like made to date. You have a HUGE assortment of differnt loadouts you can equip and use and a ridiculous amount of gear as well. Take your time. LEARN the ropes. The game is worth it. Anyway, just a head's up. It's looking great so far. It plays FAR BETTER than the demo ever did so kudos to the devs for making it better. Definitely need to learn more about the loadouts and powers myself but it's a challenge I'm going to welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Some thoughts after more time. A lot of people echo the sentiment once you get to the second area, the greek inspired area, a lot of the tedium of the game comes to the forefront. Feels like I'm not allowed to fight until I perfect parry enemies. Spells have not improved and are mostly just an excuse to imbue your weapon with an element if you desire that playstyle. Platforming feel worse than in the first area and annoying ranged enemies aplenty. I saw another review comparing this game to Dark Souls 2 but with less bugs and required parrying which I think is a perfect description. I would recommend getting this game on sale. It's not quite worth the 50 dollars.Early review upon beating the first boss. Solid game. Looks beautiful and has good music.Combat is slower than recent Souls-likes which was an adjustment. The Parry mechanic works like Sekiro and Lies of P. Your parry animation is slower than those games but the window for a successful parry is much more forgiving as well. Only took a few attempts on the boss to get the timing down. The dodging is like Bloodborne. When locked on you sidestep when not locked on you roll. Biggest plus is the loadouts and every stat holds value because of it so you don't feel like you have to dump stats into the one thing you want. You can swap builds on the fly with up to 3 loadouts you can have at any point in time. Personally thus far the Ardor abilities have all felt detrimental to use in a boss fight and mildly annoying to use against mobs but I think there are talents in the talent tree to help make them more viable. name: Mediterranea Inferno
detailed_description: A treacherous visual novel about friendship, desire, and grief. What’s better than a sensual summer retreat in the South of Italy? Join Claudio, Andrea, and Mida in their travels as they try to recover from the collective trauma of the 2020 pandemic. Three young men in their early 20s reconnect after two years of forced isolation, hoping to rekindle their friendship; an exceptional bond that made the trio truly special! A mythological force well beyond the sum of its parts! Or so they think… As you pick their activities for the day, you’ll discover their darkest fears, their obsessions, and, as the reality of their failed expectations become apparent, their thirst for revenge and retribution. A lazy afternoon by the pool, a lustful night at the club, or even a morbid visit to the local cemetery: you’ll decide how to spend this summer vacation, but wherever you go, something or someone will be waiting, offering an additional, forbidden trip through the arcane inner spaces of conscience. Eat the Fruit of Mirages and fight for your endless summer! HIGHLIGHTS Pick daily activities for the trio and see how they affect the story. A new treacherous drama from the creator of Milky Way Prince – The Vampire Star. A generational story that is as touching as it is disturbing. With music, writing, and art from the game’s author, including hundreds and hundreds of original illustrations. INFO A playthrough lasts 3 to 4 hours, reaching one of many possible endings and showing roughly 60% of the game’s content.

_childDocuments_.review: Play this game if you: Enjoy LGBTQ themes, watch Art House films, can handle some spookies (not a lot, just a little), have unresolved feelings from the pandemic, enjoy weird/unique games that take risks, want to play more games like those developed by Grasshopper ManufactureIt's inspiring that such an artistic, niche game can make it onto a platform like Steam, which has such a large audience and wide reach. But it's sad that in the case of Mediterranea Inferno it still didn't make much of a difference. At least, while I write this, the game sits with fewer than 25 reviews. And yeah, this game isn't going to be for everyone -- it's a homoerotic thriller with a very loud art style and it touches on numerous triggering topics -- but damn if it isn't one of the best games to drop in 2023 anyway. I strongly recommend this to anyone willing to give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Mediterranea Inferno

_childDocuments_.review: Mediterranea Inferno isn't here to offer a pleasant ride. But, it is an honest one. Maybe one of the most honest games available. Mediterranea Inferno approaches issues central to young gay identity, it does not mince words, it does not hide anything. It is mature and vulnerable. I will keep plot points concise and vague, this is truly an experience best ingested blind.Normally when I review my thoughts on a game, it's about what I thought about the game itself, Mediterranea Inferno defies that and while I still think about my experience with the game, it's caused me to also think about my own circumstances and history. As a gen z Homosexual who like everyone else was trapped in a seemingly world ending catastrophe those short years ago, I felt the repression, anguish, and solitude each of the three leads embodied, I feel like many others, that I lost something. Something that I will never truly grasp and never get back. This game provides a deep window into modern gay culture through the lens of a gay author, while also examining the nature of love, friendship, and identity.I saw my own struggles in the three main characters, and even if I don't have much in common with these queens of the Italian nightlife, I have never felt more strongly connected to a cast of characters on an emotional level. I know this review is not very informative in a true tactful representation of what this package entails, but artist Lorenzo Redaelli has created nothing short of a complete triumph. It's difficult, it's raw-- it's beautiful. I feel that unlike a lot of games, this one is absolutely worth your time. It will sit with me for a long time. And it will help put things in perspective when I decide what my own future may hold. .... Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Mediterranea Inferno

_childDocuments_.review: i once went on vacation in Las Vegas with my friends. i was fairly certain going in that i would hate it there and i was right. i'm not built for the strip, a place where almost everyone you talk to is trying to get one over on you. trying to balance what you do around everyone's sleep schedule and hangovers is nearly impossible and at any given point in time at least one person is having kind of a bad time. mechanically, Mediterranea Inferno evokes this group vacation perfectly. every character believes that this vacation has what's required to heal them, if only they can drag their friends through these healing experiences. you can feel the impossibility of making everyone happy and kind of oscillate between choosing a character you most identify with and maybe trying to balance the vacation.the visual storytelling of Mediterranea Inferno is breathtaking. every "panel" is packed with symbols, effects, and jokes and the rhythm and repetition of some of the screens feels perfect. the writing is constantly underscored with imagery soaked with queer, erotic, catholic, and nationalist themes.it's a short, impactful, and heavy work, and well worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a gift, so I had no idea whatsoever what to expect. However, I can definitely recommend Mediterranea Inferno to anyone who is looking for a very experimental queer visual novel horror experience! The story follows three characters who were best friends before Covid, and who lost the beginning of their adulthood to lockdowns. During their time apart from each other, they each turned into different people (not necessarily into better people). This new dynamic creates a lot of tension as they attempt to spend a vacation together.This game exudes SO MUCH style and clearly put a lot of effort into conveying the story. The audio design is so well-done, and the colors, compositions, and backgrounds are absolutely stunning. It's the only game where I've sent someone a screenshot of the Main Menu because I liked it so much. And I really liked the way the developer's Italian heritage played into this story, and I really felt like this game earnestly had a lot of ideas it wanted to discuss (I didn't agree with all of them but I think that's the point of making art or whatever).The characters took a bit of warming up for me, but I was surprised by how much I started to like them over the course of the game. The story has a lot to say and tackles all kinds of thoughts with a lot of nuance and earnestness. The plot can develop in several ways, and I appreciated the variety in each playthrough, even though you only make three or so big "choices" in every run. I really appreciated the game's openness about sex and intimacy, as well as the individual dynamics between the three characters. Understanding how their friendship worked was intriguing, and I found the game quite ambitious in the story it wanted to tell and how well it executed that narrative. The game allows you certain insights into the characters that are very metaphorical stagings of what is going on in the character's psyche while they are doing something instead of really showing you their actions and proceedings, and it's both very insightful for understanding the characters as well as somewhat ambiguous about what is actually *really* happening right now, and I really loved that.However, there were a few things that didn't quite resonate with me. Occasionally, the character designs of the three protagonists were too similar, making it difficult for me to tell them apart visually, and I wasn't the biggest fan of the character art style specifically. Additionally, the dialogue occasionally felt too stilted and on-the-nose, and I felt like the game was jumping a bit with characters in terms of characterizations to get messages in the game across more easily (I had a few moments where I said "This guy would not know what that word means," out loud or stuff like that, lmao), and while the story is totally an open discussion that you can take away what you personally interpret into it, the one thing I personally found a bit annoying was that the narrative was constantly wallowing in self-pity about how hard our generation has it, even more so than I felt was usually deserved for the moments it happened in, and the narrative had such a general contempt for the "past" as a broad concept that it baffled me a bit, to a degree where I'm not sure if I was missing a layer of irony perhaps. But none of these things made the game less interesting and fun to experience for me, and the way I had to limit myself from just starting to discuss the game's ideas at length here really is an indicator for the fact that the game really had meaningful and thought-provoking things to say!Overall, I found the game really engaging, and incredibly visually interesting! The characters kind of grew on me as concepts over my playtime, and the story gave me a lot to think about and will certainly stay in my memory for quite a while.

_childDocuments_.review: i highly recommend this game! i absolutely love the art and story. honestly the mirages were my favorite part, andrea's being my favorite out of the three.edit:going through the game to find every and any little detail or scene i missed made me realize how much i actually like this game. similar to milky way prince, the story was different and confusing at some points, but that confusion drew me to the game more.each character has a story to be told, through every mirage and nightmare there was always something new you'd learn about a character. every character equally relatable as well. the scene where andrea brought the beds together and put himself in the middle made me feel so bad for him. claudio's entire character is depressing, having a terrible father and an amazing grandfather really set the stage for his character. mida is so terribly relatable (in most ways other than the popularity), made what he did and say feel so meaningful. andrea's nightmare really made me feel something, the isolated loneliness attacked me at my core. i love andrea. claudio's ending has to be my favorite.the art is amazing. the mirages and nightmares are amazing. the endings were amazing. i await Lorenzo Redaelli's next project.thank you for creating this relatable and beautiful work of art.

_childDocuments_.review: 2.7h (100% achievement, finished the game) No. Yes (~7 achievements). No. is a visual novel about 3 gay friends who spent a holiday together after the Covid outbreak. It's a game that tells a story through emotions rather than words, describing the feelings that each person goes through.- Provocative story that tells the struggles of the younger generation- Twisted ending- Nice, surreal presentation regarding what the character feels- Content might not be suitable for teenagers- The lights can be blinding to some people- It takes time to reach the other endingsIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 uses a combination of 2D and 3D visuals. The characters look hand-drawn and placed in a simplistic, 3D environment. The color and lighting bring these two to life though, combined with their surreal presentation at times. Despite only using simplified animation, the game does a good job of showing what they want people to see. However, this presentation style can be harmful to the eye, sometimes. Some colors can be too bright, making it hard to see the whole scenery.The main story tells of 3 friends who hang out for a holiday after the Covid restriction has been lifted. The trio was Italian, so expect some Italian words mixed in the dialogues. The story itself tells about two things: the prologue tells about what the desperation of the younger generation and the latter chapters tell the story of each of the trio's struggles during the outbreak, and how it shapes their life.There's some provocative content in here. The prologue itself tells about how adults leave mess to the younger generation and how they force them to clean them up. The game does a good job of delivering this message - I even got emotional about it as I played. Although I understand that it was told from the teenager's point of view, I don't agree with this statement, and it could be harmful to people who are not mature enough for this kind of content. Other things also might not be suitable for teenagers, especially those living in a more closed-off country. It seems to regard drugs highly, pointing out how you can ascend to heaven if you consume a lot of it and how a character will be doomed if they don't do it. I know that there is a content warning on both the Store page and in the game about it, but I think I better add more to it here just in case.The trio has a different share of struggles and focus in life. It slightly shows the difference that you get as you grow up, and how your relationship becomes distant over time. One focuses on carrying on their grandparent's legacy, one focuses on socializing with people, and one focuses on being famous. Despite what they claim, they actually have some scars that they hold deep inside. I like how they show the trio's insecurities. It's mostly shown when they consume the drugs, with the happy version of the person that they would like to be. But flip it back, and you'll get what they actually feel. This was shown bit by bit in the early game, which will be revealed more as you unlock the bad ending of the said character.The game can be confusing to follow. I like the presentation, but once it goes to the actual dialogue, most of it feels empty and not important. You get what's happening to the characters, yet you also get some exposition that can be out of context, especially in the secret content. Moreover, it doesn't have any moral message whatsoever, despite the issues that it tries to bring up. The ending gives a twist, though. The game is pretty much predictable at times, and I am basically just there to see what the game will present me with. The drugs will explore more about the characters and what they feel, and I find it to be satisfying to watch despite the empty dialogues. I thought it would just keep on doing that until the game ends, but the ending tells otherwise. I was kinda pumped up when it happened, and although the finale ended up being boring again, I still had my share of fun playing it. is a visual novel. You are bound to read a bunch of dialogues and sometimes interact with objects to progress the game and reach the ending. You'll be staying in a house for 3 days, and you can choose where you want to go between two locations during those days. Each location will focus on a certain person, giving them a chance to consume a drug to get to know them better.The game has multiple endings. It's achieved by how many drugs each character consumes. I was actually interested in seeing them all, but it seems that replaying the game can take a long time to do, even with the x5 speed bonus that you get after clearing the game for the first time. The drug world was taking too long and the dialogues couldn't be fast-forwarded. The x5 speed only helped a bit with the animation, but not in speeding up the game altogether.I finished the game in 2.2h. I spent the rest of my playtime getting the rest of the achievements. You can replay the game to get the other ending or even content that you missed - you can only choose one out of two locations each day, and each location gives a different content. However, as I said before, it can take a long time to finish it even with the x5 speed bonus.It seems the game only saves the location you are in and not the interaction you had. is a game that will be up your alley if you care more about presentation than story. A game so abstract that you only care what the game will present you with. However, the content might be too strong for some people, and I wouldn't definitely recommend it to teenagers due to the provocative feeling. If you think you are mature enough to deal with all the content, don't mind the flashy colors, and care about experience rather than story, you'll like this game. The game can be very expensive for the price it offers though so buy it when it's extremely discounted.

_childDocuments_.review: Concept: What if three walking stereotypes were also the most whiny, pathetic, unlikable, hopeless and helpless depictions of Gen Z doomers depicted in recent memory?I appreciated what the developers tried to do with the 'economy' in the form of summer coins, having a limited amount to spend and thus forcing you to consider how you spend them in relation to trying to 'reach heaven' through purchasing mirages, but I also didn't feel the need to pay much attention to the system because I didn't care what happened to these little drama queens. There is replayability here in that you can make focus on each character's whims and experience different scenes, as well as an alternative ending only available through experiencing all those scenes. Again... I hate these characters so much that I don't think I could manage a second playthrough.The art is great. The style is quite unique and there are some fantastic shots and scenes in the game. The 'visual' part of this 'visual novel' is excellent. It's just the 'novel' part I didn't enjoy.If you have a negative opinion of yourself or have low self-esteem and also enjoy visual novels, perhaps this is for you. By comparing yourself to these three dorks, you'll feel like a million bucks just by comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if I've ever really had a visual novel put me in a choke hold quite like this one. This is a mean, cruel, violent, terrible, beautiful game, and to say anything else beyond what the trailers show is to spoil. This is real stuff right here.I should mention that this is a game that begs for replays due to its unique game-play loop, which I think is pretty cool, and it's story and setup are captivating enough that it earned them from me without any hesitation. Related, though: If I have any complaint about the game, is that the skip option is locked out until certain requirements are fulfilled. I understand why to an extent, but it does make some scenes that are required viewing and don't change between its runs a little cumbersome. This is the most minor nitpick I could think of for what could very well be my favorite game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s be direct about this. I’m not a fan of visual novels for involving too much reading and not enough gameplay or visual depiction. I’m not the target audience for this niche (gen z, queer, Italian etc). I’m not into explicit sexuality and strong LGBT tones. This game doesn’t hold back aside from showing you the D in full glory. I’m not into art deeply. A lot of symbolism is gibberish to me aside from basic ones. I still got intrigued and ended up enjoying the game, way more than expected!The art style along with the music are the stars of the show. Both worked hand in hand to ensure enough action between all the reading, at least when it comes to visual novels. The game also has some gameplay in the form of taking many decisions that drastically change the story and what you experience. There is a bit of currency management and finding minor collectibles for the achievements. It’s not possible to get everything on your first run but you can keep the progress you’ve made in a new run and then focus on the content you didn’t experience before. So it feels fresh and exciting enough. You can even get all the achievements in around 1.5 run but I still fully completed the second run to see a new ending and it was worth it. The characters are unlikeable for the most part but their emotions are raw and it turns into a horror story by the end. My attention was grabbed and I was interested in seeing what would happen next. The achievements are fun to figure out and they’re not challenging as long as you read the descriptions of the achievements often and pay attention.The game has 3 flaws for the most part: the save system, no skip and two characters look too similar. Saving is a bit of a mess. You can save at any time but it doesn’t save where you were exactly. It saves after starting a new ‘chapter’.  So you have to commit to a full chapter if you don’t want to repeat things. I kept making new saves thinking I had more control but at least I was relieved to find out your progress with the collectibles is kept after completing the game the first time. And a full chapter is not long btw. The game has no real skipping option but there are some other means. A new run skips the early part and goes straight to where the action begins. You can also increase the dialogue speed. I’m glad about those options but I would have still liked skipping or a quicker way to experience what I missed. Think of chapter select or a timeline chart where you pick a specific scene like with some of the visual novels I’ve tried. Two of the three characters (Claudio and Andrea) look too similar in terms of design. I kept mixing the two for a long time. Oh, and there is some typo here and there.This is the kind of game I wouldn’t have given a chance if it wasn’t for Humble Choice’s May bundle. It’s a special game with no real comparison to anything else I played. I’m glad to have spent less than 5 hours to play it. But this kind of game is VERY personal to the individual and you need to be really tolerant of certain themes. It’s not a game for everyone. At least I can say it’s technically sound and it succeeds at what it’s trying to do. It’s up to you whether you want to give a game like this a try.

_childDocuments_.review: + Gorgeous visuals and audio+ Excellent writing is a mashup of neon-soaked theatrical drama, bitingly cynical comedy and grounded, intimate human emotion+ Every single scene has unique art, rather than static sprites talking at each other+ Meaningful choices despite limited interactivity+ Fantastically atmospheric- No option to skip read text, even though you're clearly meant to replay the game?- You have to unlock the "fast-forward" option that lets you get through scenes you're replaying, which didn't happen until after I saw the "true" ending* Very flawed characters you may or may not end up sympathizing with, which could affect your enjoyment* While sex and violence underlie everything, there is not actually any explicit content of either; nudity is censored, as are the sex scenes, and the worst you'll see violence-wise is blood with disturbing sound effects* This is openly, uncompromisingly queer, and if that makes you at all uncomfortable you're going to have a bad timeGoing into Mediterranea Inferno, I was expecting something shallow, but dark and stylish enough to make up for it. Gore and shameless sexuality, but in a fun way. Shock value rather than value, perhaps. And the game  filled with violence, sex and psychosexual horror, brought to life by its phenomenal sound design and visuals.That said, I was pleasantly surprised by both how easy the overall story was to follow and by the unflinching but surprisingly sympathetic portrayal of the leads' inner turmoil. The latter, more than anything, was what made me love this game. The writing approaches its deeply flawed trio and their messy relationships with an unsparing eye, but it ultimately reaches for empathy and shared horror at the world rather than a moralistic condemnation. Yes, they're all terrible twenty-somethings who seem to be preoccupied mainly with themselves, but despite initial impressions, the script isn't interested in painting them as nothing but vapid stereotypes for you to hate, even as they increasingly view each other that way as their friendship unravels. Beneath the performance, each of them is hiding pain rooted in something complex and human.Let's talk about the gameplay for a moment. The boys begin each day by suggesting different activities they want to do. Going along with a specific character's desires means they get the opportunity to experience a Mirage: surreal, psychological dreamscapes experienced in first-person which offer you insight into that character's insecurities, preoccupations, and the lies they're telling themselves. Seeing four Mirages lets a character reach "paradise" in the ending, supposedly, but you're warned early that there aren't enough Mirages to go around. No matter what you do, ultimately someone is going to be left out in the cold.Despite the limited interactivity, the choices you make still matter. Depending on the mental state you've inflicted on each boy by buying or denying them Mirages, their dialogue and actions shift dramatically. Feeding their delusions via Mirages keeps each boy happy, but to get to the real person inside each of them you have to do the opposite: crush their hopes by denying them their escapist fantasies, until you can finally get to the root of their trauma, which is portrayed in a cumulative nightmare sequence at the end of each route depending on who you've failed to bring to heaven. Each ending is different, but all of the ones I found were rewarding.I passed the height of COVID-19 in China. The characters' spiralling mental health and increasing detachment towards reality as they passed day after day in total isolation felt incredibly true to life and relatable to my experiences, in a way it might not be for others—Italy's lockdowns, like ours, were stricter than elsewhere, and brutalized people in ways that can be hard to talk about even now. Still, regardless of whether you can personally relate to the characters' experiences, I'd recommend at least trying this game out if it sounds like something you might enjoy. If nothing else, it's currently a unique experience in gaming. Not to mention one of the only pieces of media I've seen that wants to talk about what the pandemic has done to a generation of the young and hopeful.TL;DR: Recommended if you are the kind of person who watches or would watch Italian art films about toxic queer friends, as that's essentially what this is, except with more player guilt.
_childDocuments_.name: Mediterranea Inferno

_childDocuments_.review: An unflinching examination of post-covid society that is in turns, hilarious, painful, gorgeous and unsettling. The tight structure of choosing which “mirages”—surreal and beautiful fantasies—to gift to each character is compelling and meaningful and the resulting chaos and conflict is both satisfying and shocking.This endless summer of narcissism and crisis is incredibly clear-eyed in how it sees the current moment but is also filled with moments of humanity and lightness. A truly unique cinematic journey, and the most fascinating game of the year. Strongly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for May 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before June 4th, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.An attempt at a visual novel. Mediterranea Inferno starts with the author saying it’s his reflection on a host of problems and has a long content warning. I don’t know if it’s the author trying to be the voice of a generation, but it comes off that way. The game is about three gay men going on a vacation to reconnect after “the Pandemic” and don’t worry they namecheck COVID. I hope the author felt a cathartic release with this, this was intended to be a way to talk about something that bothered him, but comes out as something like I’m 14 and this is deep. The thing is, the pandemic was hard for everyone, and it’s hard to incorporate that into a story, but it’s also not done well here. It’s also hard to tell a story of what seemed like three over-privileged sexed-up gay men who… honestly, I’m not the right person for this game, and that’s a big issue with it being in Humble.But also in general, I just didn’t like this game, it felt more like it was forcing storylines and even after 20 minutes I knew it wasn’t going to work for me. I know a lot of people are going to call this a great piece of art because it spoke to or for them, but if I have no reason to even know who a character is in the first fifteen minutes, why am I focused on a visual novel about them? Pick this up if you liked Milky Way Prince, this is made by the same developers, and I didn’t like that one, so I didn’t like this one. Thus is life. But for me, This is a hard pass.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Mediterranea Inferno was an... experience, to say the least. An LGBTQ+ horror visual novel that feels as though was meant to be the game creators way of expressing how they feel in an artistic way.I'll start off by saying the stuff that isn't blatant spoilers, because its hard to talk about this game without spoiling big chunks of it, so if your interested in playing this game check it out during a sale or a bundle. I don't personally feel that its worth 15 bucks unless your very clearly interested in this product from the get-go. If you like horror, artistic games, and LGBTQ+ matters then pick it up when you feel comfortable with it. The gameplay itself is pretty simple, a visual novel mixed with a point and click adventure game going through hallucinogenic trips that each of the three characters experience during the summer. Each one isn't that long, having a handful of things to find through each trip but also a very clear 'exit' that can be ran to within 15-30 minutes. It also has quite a few endings, a bad and 'good' ending for each character, with a 'best' ending (though fair warning, it really depends on your opinion on what is good or bad about the situations. there is no happy endings here.) The entire thing is drawn beautifully, with plenty of heavy theme through it all. I do have an big issue with its gameplay however.Gameplay wise, it has no skip option. The best you get is a 5x speed option, but only after you've more or less beat the game twice (can probably be done once if your lucky enough on your choices). While this is nice, its unfortunately not really amazing when most scenes will still drag out much too long because of animations that still drag on even at a higher speed.I would still recommend it, but its definitely an acquired taste. If it sounds good to you, check it out. Otherwise...

_childDocuments_.review: mediterranea inferno is like...what if revolutionary girl utena was about a trio of italian twinks whose coming of age was interrupted by the pandemic. i mean that as the highest compliment.the art/music/sound design is incredible, the characters feel like real people, and the symbolism and social/political commentary make it a prime example of games as serious literature. it is a visual novel, after all — but it takes advantage of the medium in some delightfully creative ways that remind me of one of my other favourite LGBT visual novels (if found). it's dynamic and truly interactive, not just clicking to advance through walls of text.i don't think i am precisely part of the demographic being spoken to/about (i was 25 when lockdowns started so it didn't disrupt my social development in the same way as it did for gen z) but as a younger millennial i still found the larger themes of alienation and anxiety about the future to be very resonant. i could see a bit of my own reaction to the pandemic in every character — my relief at being able to stay home and chill, my grief and yearning for the rave scene i had just started getting into, my panic about the impact on my career plans. it's cool to see such a thoughtful and nuanced take on the psychological impact of the covid years on young adults, perhaps especially queer young adults.on that note i also have to reiterate how much i loved the depiction of messy gays — the casually mixed gendered language, the raunchiness, the drug use — and the fact that all of this is presented unapologetically and without explanation. one could say i felt seen! it's becoming more common for media to put forward sanitised, over-explained portrayals of LGBT people in order to get brownie points for "representation", only to end up not representing anything real at all. in that regard, mediterranea inferno is wonderfully, refreshingly honest.that's basically it. i loved this. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I love these evil little twinks.The music, writing, and shot composition of this game absolutely blew me away. The core mechanic (choosing who gets fruit, and, thus, who is left behind) reminded me a lot of my favorite VN: We Know the Devil. Both games are deeply queer and about religious trauma and the complexities of friendship.The mirages were revealing and fun, with only very rare moments of "what am I supposed to do here?". Most of all, I believed in the characters. While some of the circumstances were peak melodrama (complimentary), the core of each character was so believable. As someone who was once the third wheel in a group of three friends, I understood Mida. As someone who struggles to believe in the future, I understood Claudio. And, most of all, as someone who seeks out connection because being alone can feel like staring into the void, I understood Andrea.And of course as a gay with profound amounts of religious trauma and COVID trauma, I related deeply to the writing. Highly recommend for fans of visual novels and especially horror visual novels!

_childDocuments_.review: Mediterranea Inferno, in the vein of the developer's previous game Milky Way Prince, is a gay-themed visual novel with horror overtones, in this case about three Italian twinks on their first vacation together post-COVID. It's not going to be for all tastes, no doubt - beyond the gay focus, the protagonists are deliberately often unlikeable - but even as a late-millennial gay man who is by no means a social media influencer or party boy, I found the themes of post-COVID social alienation and despair for the future relatable, which manages to make many of the horror elements all the more disturbing. Also deserves credit for its visuals, which depart from the standard visual novel style by stylishly combining the 2D character art with simple 3D models. Not everything here works - the game is often prone to stating its themes a bit too heavy-handedly and didactically (the true ending does attempt to subvert this, but in a way that's arguably heavy-handed in its own right), but we need more narratively ambitious queer games like this and I'm excited to see what developer Lorenzo Redaelli does next.one note: as with Milky Way Prince before it, this really needs a better way of speeding through (if not skipping entirely) previously completed parts of the game to redo choices and reach all the endings, there's a "fast" option that slightly mitigates the tedium, but only slightly, and a 5x speed option that would help a lot more if it wasn't only unlocked after you get the true ending (by which point there's a good chance you'll have seen all three of the other endings anyway, though it's possible to reach the true ending after only two of the others).

_childDocuments_.review: This was a strange and artful game. I liked the music, style and how sinful the main trio was - it was interesting to follow around these terribly young, hurt, and seeking people. Even though I couldn't connect well to the politics and nationalism, I found the trio's fears and desires to be relatable. I hadn't thought about the lockdowns in some time - my memory of them is fuzzy and the experience itself felt like a long dream, much like this game. The three character endings were all painful - that specific ending track (Cantica) just left me in hurt silence each time. The levels were interesting - my favorite was the medieval "movie" shoot. I found all eight cards and reached 4 (5?) different endings. I'm still in a state of surprise at what I've just witnessed.

_childDocuments_.review: A gripping, queer, and psychedelic look at the anxieties induced/highlighted by the pandemic as well as the trauma caused by lockdowns. The game explores how we struggle to define ourselves, relate to others, and deal with our society on both a personal and grander scale through the medium of 3 friends going on a ♥♥♥♥-erotic summer vacation.Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Mediterranea Inferno

_childDocuments_.review: I remember buying and playing through Milky way prince, showing a friend, and both of us being moved by it, a wonderful experience. We heard about Mediterranea Inferno releasing and couldn't wait on it. It released, and we expected to love it, and again be moved by it, but for it to hit us so hard and move us so much? We couldn't have predicted that. Mediterranea Inferno is such a stunning piece of art, everywhere from its art, to its soundtrack, to its tale and everything in between. If it sparks even a tiny amount of interest in you, you owe it to yourself to play it. So many games come and go, but Mediterranea Inferno is an experience i don't think i'll ever forget, please play it and let it move you the way it did for me

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, angry, raw. This game explores the struggles of queer youth during the pandemic in Italy through an outwardly flamboyant and hedonistic tone both in its aesthetics and narrative, revealing some real anger and frustration boiling underneath the surface. It might not have the most polished writing and themes, but it is worth playing just to experience a confident narrative from a point of view that is fresh and deeply personal.

_childDocuments_.review: 3 gay twinks on vacation descend into hell after years of hubris catches up to them, but is it their fault? or is it this wretched world that has failed them?I can quite frankly see a bit of myself in all three of the protagonists, which is very frightening to say the least, yet it feels like it is something I personally needed to hear sooner than later, maybe we're all martyrs.Regardless of my personal bias regarding how much I can relate to the characters, this is an excellent narrative adventure game with some dark themes, exciting twists, raunchy humor and compelling structure, all tied up with a great soundtrack and overflowing visual style.Very recommended, GREATLY recommended if you're lgbt+ (it just kinda hurts sweeter that way, maybe).
