_childDocuments_.review: (Obviously thank you Ad.  Awesome Ad.  For giving me this game...  And for helping me see some things clearer.)Ah alright.  I hear you game.  I get your "message", but...  I have counter ideas.  Which I wont share nor tell you because in the end it wont matter.  After all...  We all see what we want to see, don't we?  It's only the certain aspects/events of our lives that can shatter such illusions...Game.  Okay the game is trippy and I CAN tell if you really need to take a "trip" to understand things even better...  You don't.  People who have problems with bright lights shouldn't attempt this game.  The game is rather colorful and I had to close my eyes on scene changes/flashing parts due to it causing eye pain/strain.The game also can benefit from being faster.  My spacebar/mouse got a workout.  I think they dislike me now.  Sometimes you don't know when to click to advance and sometimes you just gotta wait a while.  It's fine for patient people...  But for people you really made this game for?  They aren't as patient.I don't speak a lick of Italian and I am too lazy to translate all the phrases.  I am pretty certain that there was a part in French?  Know what I did?  I made up my own words.  At least write the translation next to it.  Again...  Your target audience will just gloss over it.And please...  Why so much hatred for old people?  Really?  I am not going to lecture you, but damn!  Aren't you being a bit too extreme in telling all of them to just go die?  What if the situation was reversed huh?  How would you feel then?  Spending all those years building and creating things with tears and blood...  Only for someone "bright and young" to tell you to "go die".  Have you no remorse/shame for any of it?I got carried away.  But people need to understand that precious things in life can vanish within an instant and then...  Then you'll never get them back.  Regretting it all the same.Okay back to the game itself: it has...  I guess you can say "multiple endings"...  It's just...  You are going to have to favor a character above others.  Especially if you are after all the Achievements.  It wont be easy and will require you to replay a few times.Story...  Story is about "side effects" from being "inactive" during the lockdown.  Also how unfair the world is too.  You learn jack sheet about the three characters.  Sadly.  All I know is that they are high and mighty and psychotic...  Loving all sorts of "mind altering substances".  If they actually bothered to busy themselves with a hobby and met some OTHER NORMAL PEOPLE...  F it.Anyway.  It's rather simple to figure out the ending and what will take place.  I mean...  Three guys...  Hatred...  Drugs...  Inside one isolated place together...  Come on.  >.>  It's right there.The dilemma here though...  Should you read it?  Well...  What do you want?  Are you a young, impressionable person hating on the world and people in it?  Shaking your fist and swearing at everything and everyone?  Only to wish to escape reality?  This game is for you...  :>Do you want a murder mystery?!  You can figure out the plot just by reading my review.Did you get high and needed something...  More like literally ANYTHING to read?  You are in the right place!  (Perhaps...)Are you a smart thinking, older person...  I don't think you are here at all.As for my opinion: I don't hate it.  I don't think you are supposed to enjoy this game, but rather...  Reflect on some things?  See how far passions get you?  I am capable of trying to think things through first and I get it.  I understand what they TRIED to get across, but at the same time...?It wont be for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game in a bundle and even if I had low expectations for it, this is definitely a diamond in the rough. Sure, the visuals and the linear storytelling is not everyone's cup of tea but it’s a deep exploration of human emotion and complex relationships in a post pandemic world. _childDocuments_.review: Amused, moved, flabergasted how this gem of a game overflowing with singular personality is overlooked. _childDocuments_.review: ✅Very stylish and artsy✅Music➖Abstract➖Narrative can be underwhelmingGame World: Mediterranea Inferno (MI) is a visual novel that takes place in Italy. The game world mostly consists of you simply reading the dialog while the characters interact with the game world. Unfortunately (maybe), the game world is very hard to describe. This is an incredibly artsy title. As such the world itself often feels less like a world and more like a painting. I will commend MI for its unique graphical style below, but I’ll say as far as a game world goes, MI fails to impress - it can oftentimes be challenging to understand what the world is supposed to be, especially during “Mirage” parts, which goes completely drug-induced bonkers. Narrative: The narrative in MI is generally simple but the Mirage sequences can make it incredibly confusing. You don’t play as any character, as the player, you have a third person perspective while occasionally hearing the thoughts of the three main characters - Claudio, Mida, and Andrea. Each of the characters have their own demons below the surface they are dealing with, and the premise of the game is focused on how the COVID lockdowns have mentally impacted the Gen Z protagonists. The story takes place in Italy as the three protagonists are somewhat famous. The lockdowns are lifted and for some reason, they haven’t spoken to each other in 2 years and want to do a weekend get-together. What follows, at the start, is a weekend full of queer debauchery. There are no explicit body parts shown, but the scenes and dialog can get quite perverse. As the player, you choose who you want to give these Mirage items too (more in mechanics), what results is the Mirage seems to give the chosen character more confidence while the others become more mentally unstable. Ending spoilers: Despite my ending, there seems to be many other options available if you choose different characters. Still, the narrative wasn’t good enough for me to want to play it again. While the general story was good enough to tolerate, the Mirage parts took whatever normalcy MI has and threw it off the rails. I would have rather enjoyed to have a deeper, more intriguing dialog without the need for drug-induced craziness. Length: This is a short game, but you won’t see all of the content from a single playthrough as there is a good amount of choices for the player to make. One playthrough for me took me a little under 3 hours. Controls: Being this is a visual novel, the controls are largely KBM and involve simple left clicking on options. Mechanics: The main unique mechanic that MI has in the guise of player choice is the Mirage mechanic. How this functions is that some sort of queer deity comes to your characters and basically says that Mirage feels good and you need four of them to “Ascend to heaven.” The trick here is that a Mirage costs this random currency to obtain, so you have limited options to choose who gets a Mirage. Once a character chooses to have a Mirage, they enter some sort of acid trip that on some level explores how the character is feeling or what they are thinking. Furthermore, inside the Mirage, there are some different paths to take and more options to spend your valuable currency on. There is a type of card hidden in each Mirage that is used to purchase something if you collect 8 of them - implying that it may take more than a single, or even 2x, playthrough to accomplish this. So overall, I’ll say that of the visual novels I’ve played, the Mirage mechanic seems like a unique spin on a normal VN play. The concept seems intriguing, but the execution leaves me wondering if there was a better way to implement this in perhaps a not so abstract way. All the Mirages I’ve watched felt somewhat confusing and nonsensical. Difficulty: No difficulty involved, just choices. There doesn’t seem to be a way to fail. Quality: MI is a very artsy game. The quality here is less of something I would call beautiful, and more like a unique abstract painting. Sometimes the artfulness of the design can get in the way of how things are supposed to look, making me feel confused to what even is happening, especially during Mirages. I don’t really like abstract art, but I feel that MI has done a great job in bringing a unique take to VNs. UI: Simple and yet it seems to cover all of the bases of a good VN. I like how the log of previous dialogs is right there when you access the menu. I did find the save system confusing. There are auto saves, but when I attempted to save manually I had to reload from the auto save to get to where I was. Also, despite there being a manual save, it seems as though you cannot save in the middle of dialog, only a certain points, so once I saved in the middle of the scene, and when I reloaded I was brought back to the beginning of the scene. Performance: No issues with performance, played on my desktop PC. i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSDSound Effects: The sound effects are done well. I noticed it being quite atmospheric. Things like rain, car doors, and background noises are done well. There is no voice acting. Music: The music is pretty good and I’d say the best part of the Mirage experiences. When you enter Mirages, there are some absolute bangers that had me tapping and nodding my head to the beat. Well done. MI has some good replay value. I read somewhere that when you finish a single storyline, you’ve seen about 60% of the content in the game. So I figure you’d have to replay it at least 2 more times - once for each character you didn’t choose, plus another time maybe for the max card trade in, which I’m not sure what that does. All of this extends the 3 hour playthrough up to around ~9 hours, but I do anticipate some possible repetition, especially if you are unable to skip scenes. The game seems like it was meant for replaying because as soon as you finish, you are immediately thrust back into the first scene. Mediterranea Inferno is difficult to recommend. Every unique thing it brings to the visual novel space (art style, Mirage) has clear disadvantages that make me dislike it. Furthermore, it can be difficult to recommend due to the overtly queer protagonists as you really need to take your audience into consideration and hope they have an open enough mind to look past things like 20-year old men having sex with each other. Ultimately, I’m going to not recommend this because to me the core part of a visual novel is having a gripping enough story (duh, it's a book with visuals) to keep the player engaged, and I thought that the story of MI was weak enough to make me not care enough to play it a second playthrough. While the game definitely delivers on art style and music, it's almost like those areas had more effort into them instead of writing an engaging story. You can find my curator page here:

_childDocuments_.review: Mediterranea Inferno is not a game, it's a Choose-Your-Own-Adventure e-book that's been dumped on Steam masquerading as a game.  As a visual/interactive novel, this doesn't feature any notable gameplay, it's just a lot of clicking through badly written dialogue that would never have been accepted or published in print, which poses the question, "How did something this badly written end up on Steam?".To answer that question: When someone hoping to become an author is unable to get published in print, they spend $100 and dump their high school fan-fiction onto Steam, under the guise of a game.This E-book features Choose-Your-Own-Adventure elements where you make some decisions that don't do anything to change the fact this is just an E-Book.  Nobody finished reading a Choose-Your-Own-Adventure book and said "Boy, what a great game I just played!".   Because E-books aren't games.  And neither is this.This is an atrociously written Readers Digest reject tier e-book about European vactioners... the delivery is worse than the premise.  In a sea of garbage non-game E-books infesting Steam, this is one of the worst, and that's including all the Ren'Py anime garbage from weeaboos. The E-book hamfistedly tries to solve social issues and other mental health problems by, uh, talking about them in a garbage CYOA E-book.  Ugh. Trying to address social issues through the medium of video games is misguided and can be harmful.  While it's plausible to suggest the intention was noble, this can do more harm than good.  Game developers are not professionals in areas of mental health and social problems, and when they use video games to pretend they are, this can cause far more harm than good.  It's my opinion that it's improper to use video games to push political or social agendas.Apart from the harm such hamfisted attempts at addressing social problems can cause, this offers zero benefit to PC gamers.  People suffering from health issues or other social problems should seek out professional help rather than going to crap shovelware video games attempting to get sales by exploiting such problems for their own benefit, as is the case here.  Remember, this is a FOR-PROFIT product, attempting to cash in on mental health issues by offering garbage E-book solutions to them.  This is NOT OK. Visual novels/e-books are tedious at best... imagine the best novel you ever read, be that Hitchhikers Guide to the Galaxy or 2001: A Space Odyssey or Twilight (if you have terrible taste in literature), but then translate that to a format where the words dribble out and you have to click your mouse every time you wanted to read the next sentence, instead of just turning the pages. You'd think it was garbage.Now imagine that experience, but with much worse writing (because if these guys could write professionally, they'd be published authors and this would be on shelves in bookstores, and they wouldn't have to pay Valve $100 to self-publish this on Steam), and you have your average Steam e-book.One of the chief problems with failed authors polluting Steam with non-game E-books is that E-books can easily just be presented in a web browser... there's no justification for charging money on Steam for what might as well be a webpage.  We don't spend thousands on buying a gaming rig to spend money on Steam for something Chrome or Firefox could do.Mediterranea Inferno has the laughable price of $15 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the E-Book, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.You can get better quality books and comics for free online or from public libraries, or from bookstores for a fraction of the price of this "game".  Steam isn't a comic book store, neither is it  Netflix, it's for games.  Your gaming rig is not a Kindle.  It's impossible for me to recommend things to PC gamers that aren't really games.  They're seriously trying to get FIFTEEN BUCKS for a hamfisted attempt to cash in on mental health issues by pushing a garbage E-book on Steam.  It's disgusting.

_childDocuments_.review: Mediterranea Inferno is a queer visual novel set in a post-covid world about what it means to be alive right now. The game is surreal, often feeling like a drug-induced trip of some kind, but this works to its favor as it tells the story of three lost youths in Italy. While the visuals are effective for the most part, some of the bright and flashing lights feel intentionally harmful to the player, and the characters look very similar, so much so that I had a hard time distinguishing them in different lighting. The story tackles deep themes and conveys emotions well, and the endings are especially gut-punching. I enjoyed the brazen portrayal of messy gays and the blurring of gender present here, and the religious symbolism gave this often blasphemous story an even more poignant feel. This game is trippy and at times confusing, but it's a beautifully-made passion project with a validating message, and I'd recommend it for those repressed, Catholic guilt-filled gays like me who still don't know how to pick up the pieces in a post-pandemic world.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to talk about this game in any way without spoiling what makes it whole, but why not give it a try anyway. It's a visual novel with branching choices aiming for a replayable cycle of short "routes".More than that, it's a visually striking, aesthetically confident exploration of italian gay culture and post-lockdown (current covid) trauma. More than that, it's an uncomfortable existentialist dive into the psyche of three anxious, troubled youth, scarred by society and themselves. More than that, it's a mirror in which to see ourselves naked and raw. It's a hard play, a tough read, and an absolute must experience. Stop reading this, and start reading it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mediterranea Inferno

_childDocuments_.review: Trippy visual novel on the young adult post-pandemic experience through a queer-esoterism lens, and some anime-like horror elements.The visuals and some of the mechanics to play with the genre staples to great effect. Although personally I mostly appreciated the way esoterism is approached: masterfully merges elements of queer myth and hyper-specific Puglia folklore.The characters are quite aggravating people, which is kinda the point it seems. As a baseline, one might empathise because of the shared pandemic trauma, while at the same time seeing them as the privileged queer youth unbothered by the struggles of the LGBTQ+ community.As a queer person raised in the areas the game takes place, it hits quite more strongly. One can't help but feel conflicted about the characters. They're there, engaging in that predatory tourism that's destroying local communities, while at the same time, given the privileged nature of the characters, having a level of acceptance and ability to express their sexuality that is still mostly denied to queer youth in the area.While one hesitates to think ill of young people whose ignorance is an effect of their circumstances, when you  it does get quite cathartic.
_childDocuments_.name: Mediterranea Inferno

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most beautifully crafted games I've had the chance to play. This game is powerful in its theme, the art is striking and the scenery is smart. Not to mention, the OST is an absolute banger and I can't help but listen to it again and again. The game is easy to play and catchy. It won't let you drop the controller until you've had more of it and soon you finished it entirely. Yet even the end is probably not enough, you'll want to start over. For any player fond of narrative games, this should be a non-skippable must-play.And I just love that the game has the courage to talk about sexuality and to represent it in an interesting manner and context. We need more of this.This is definitely one of those rare pearl that has everything in it.

name: Undead Inc.
detailed_description: As a franchisee of Endwell medical you are entrusted to establish and run a successful medical facility – delivering ever increasing profits for corporate HQ. Establish a local subsidiary of the Endswell Medical Corporation. With multiple locations for your franchise to be located in, each biome will have new unique features that will keep things fresh while offering different challenges. You will need to build and expand your offices and research facilities. Hire & manage your staff effectively to maximise efficiency. To satisfy Corporate HQ you will need to ensure you are delivering ever greater profits, legitimate business will only earn you so much – if you want to truly excel you will need to push the boundaries of science and medicine. Leave ethics at the door and research illegal bacteria & viruses to help develop cutting edge treatments and bioweapons. Stay in control of your operation and make sure business runs smoothly. Manage suspicion levels by ensuring your staff are loyal, bribe or intimidate politicians & local officials, keep the police off your back and stay one step ahead of your rivals. Pushing boundaries can be dangerous – ensure you keep hazardous activities in check by providing staff with adequate PPE and safety protocols, keep external interference away and if needed make sure your director is on hand to keep any mishaps ‘in house’. Losing control is a matter of when, not if… When the time comes, ensure you are ready. Gather any trusted staff, as much money research you can carry and make your way to the extraction point before it’s too late. Anything gathered will be of great use in your next franchise… Remember; All’s Well, that Endswell… Key Features: Resource Management: Manage patients, cash flow, risks, and maintenance. Keep your operation running smoothly and without… incident. Build: Rent office space and expand your medical facilities – even underground. Utilise the space for a range of activities both above and below board. Staff Management: Hire the right staff for the right job. Staff are ranked on skill / cultural fit / stamina determining effectiveness, and you get what you pay for.. Research: Develop new drugs and treatments to help serve your community whilst also secretly researching illegal viruses & bioweapons. Roguelike game loop: When things go bad, salvage as much money & research as possible to help start your new and improved franchise in a new town. Directors: Take control of unique Directors to help run your facility – each come with their own perks, special abilities, and equipment.

Leave ethics at the door and research illegal bacteria & viruses to help develop cutting edge treatments and bioweapons. Stay in control of your operation and make sure business runs smoothly. Manage suspicion levels by ensuring your staff are loyal, bribe or intimidate politicians & local officials, keep the police off your back and stay one step ahead of your rivals. Pushing boundaries can be dangerous – ensure you keep hazardous activities in check by providing staff with adequate PPE and safety protocols, keep external interference away and if needed make sure your director is on hand to keep any mishaps ‘in house’. Losing control is a matter of when, not if… When the time comes, ensure you are ready. Gather any trusted staff, as much money research you can carry and make your way to the extraction point before it’s too late. Anything gathered will be of great use in your next franchise… Remember; All’s Well, that Endswell… Key Features: Resource Management: Manage patients, cash flow, risks, and maintenance. Keep your operation running smoothly and without… incident. Build: Rent office space and expand your medical facilities – even underground. Utilise the space for a range of activities both above and below board. Staff Management: Hire the right staff for the right job. Staff are ranked on skill / cultural fit / stamina determining effectiveness, and you get what you pay for.. Research: Develop new drugs and treatments to help serve your community whilst also secretly researching illegal viruses & bioweapons. Roguelike game loop: When things go bad, salvage as much money & research as possible to help start your new and improved franchise in a new town. Directors: Take control of unique Directors to help run your facility – each come with their own perks, special abilities, and equipment.
short_description: Undead Inc. is a high-risk, high-reward resource management simulator where you establish and manage a local subsidiary of the Endswell Medical Corporation. Build, manage staff, conduct research, and trade in both cutting edge medical treatments and bleeding edge bioweapons.

_childDocuments_.review: Early access despite it not being listed as such. Don't buy it. Wait a while. Too many bugs and weird things to count. I'm struggling to find anything positive about this game. Here's just a sample of problems I've ran into in just 1 hour:-Cannot change language after the first time you start the game. If you accidentally click on the wrong one you're screwed.-Extremely unpolished. This should be listed as early access. There is no way this can be considered a finished product.a-Animations break frequently. Then again, perhaps the T-posing is everyone trying to assert their dominance over each other and their environment.-Very neat concept. Clunky and, honestly, irritating execution.-Employee hiring is poorly designed. You use a menu to hire from different kinds of employees, which are seemingly randomly generated with no ability to filter based on skill levels or some method of paying more for better employees. In addition, once hired they automatically assign themselves to a room, so if you want them to work in a specific spot you have to pause the game, click them, click a button in the bottom right, then click on the room you want them to work in. Would be way better if you could just click the room you want to hire someone for and have the menu pop up for employees that can work there, basically directly hiring for that room, if that makes sense.-Voices for your director/employees is in some AI generated, unintelligible language... or at least I can't figure out what language they're supposed to be speaking thanks to aforementioned AI butchering of their voice lines. What is this, The Sims?-Frequent hangups, like the game just acting like it's frozen at random (especially in cutscenes).-Poorly made tutorial that teaches some extreme basics that you could easily figure out on your own, but doesn't go into properly managing things like status effects, suspicion (employee and other groups), gathering things for evacuation, and other more complex things you would think would warrant a tutorial or something over.-Game is forcibly paused while you're looking at menus (for instance, the one for black market deals. Can't have it open waiting for production to finish making something for one of the deals there).-Employee suspicion rises too fast.-Seems to be a time management game, which is not directly mentioned on the store page (unless you count looking at user-defined tags). Yes, I saw the extraction bit at the bottom of the page. However, it's common for these types of games to mention that kind of thing but let you keep going on however long you want, and from the way it's worded here makes me think that you have some control over how long you can keep playing. Instead. in this game it seems like you're on a hard set timer rather than just having to move on if you let things get out of hand.-No tooltips. Of any kind. In a management game like this. For example, you can't mouse over the status icons on my employees to find out what they are and how they're being affected, instead I have to pull up employee management to figure anything out.-Unsure if it's actually worth $20 for the content provided and gameplay loop.Normally I don't like the idea of reviewing a game this early after release since I feel like doing so is premature, but in this case it feels as if there was zero QA testing done (this coming from someone that has QA experience for both AAA and indie games). The game has a very interesting concept, and I sincerely hope they're able to iron out all the problems... but for now I'm done with this review, I'm done with this game, and I'm going to play something else that's worth the time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Undead Inc. is, for better or for worse, symptomatic of a certain stripe of Tycoon games. There's not a whole lot of player freedom on offer, the early goings-on for any new Endswell Medical franchise you set up are identical from game to game, right down to optimal room placements, and the only viable strategy puts a timer on your progress. You're free to stick to above-board consultation and Direct-Consumer Sales plans, but you'll only earn a pittance from legitimate avenues. The Black Market is a necessity for any sort of proper cash flow, which in turn means you're going to attract attention - and motivates your checking up on employee loyalty as a mechanic. If an Engineer or Scientist sees too much, you'll have to let them go or risk corporate secrets reaching the wrong ears.All of the above creates a loop that's a bit too narrow to allow for the deeper ends of Wannabe Umbrella Corporation's misgivings to really take shape. I haven't played through to the end of the tech tree, but review after review states that zombies, animal-type GMOs or any of the expected perversions of science hardly ever feature prominently. I've played enough to find the interface fiddly, and came to thinking that letting us build or redesign interior partitions in a hollow shell, à la Evil Genius 2, and to build up or drill down as needed, would've been more legible. As-is, the menu bar is cluttered, there's a ton of needless scrolling and it's all too easy to lose sight of a selected underground zone. Add to that concerns with pathing or with employees' needs shifting so quickly most can't even handle the trek down to their workplace, and you've got a design doc that feels sophomoric at best.There's fun to be had, sure - in small doses - but for a good, solid, supersaturated concentration of Evil, see Evil Genius 2.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has gotten a lot of hate, some of it deserved, some of it not. So let’s get the hate out of the way. Con:There is not enough content in the game. You have a game where you’re running a Resident Evil bio-company and you have 5 research trees, With Consumer and Equipment being the most fleshed out, Bioweapons only having 3 options, Infantry and Plant research only having a single option. Disregarding research you don’t have enough content in general, no public relations to help with Suspicion generation, no advance security to keep things safe, no additional directors, no advance staff, no ways to modify your staff whether legally or illegally. The game has optimization problems often leading to game crashes and in some cases corrupting your save game because there’s no manual saving options. People complain about the graphics but for a $20 game it looks pretty good for what it is. What is upsetting is day 1 DLC, DLC that gives you a director that isn’t even that good but is required for an achievement.Tutorial doesn’t give you nearly enough information on how to play the game. While it does give you a good introduction story into the world you’re getting into, you’ll have to figure a lot by yourself. On the same topic, the game lacks tool tips which makes learning a little more difficult. Pro:The setting and story is very good and I’m surprised it took this long for someone to create an Umbrella style type of game. And I would be very interested in how this game goes. The gameplay loop is solid there’s very little issue I have personally with the gameplay (just a lack of content as stated). At the end of the day your job is to make enough money to pay an ever increasing Franchise demand. When suspicions get too much and you can no longer meet the demand grab whatever staff and resources you can get and get out of there. Unlocking perks and making your next run easier. The developers have done a very good job in updating and optimizing the game since it’s released. From game breaking bugs with the police, to modifying the exhaustion gain of staff members. Ideally these should’ve been fixed before the release but I’m happy it’s getting fixed now.Summary:For $20 the game is good mindless fun. Choose a Director, Build a franchise, make money, evacuate, unlock new perks, rinse-and-repeat. The devs are currently working on optimizing the game and I pray they add more content to the game. The game needed more time to cook, needed more content, ideas, and optimization. I wish it came out day 1 but that isn’t the case.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: - the soundtrack slaps, - the premise is interesting, - the foundational gameplay loop feels pretty solid, along with a decent number of random/reactive events which should keep things feeling fresh for a long while. - Game is quite stable (at least for me) and UI/HUD nav is fluid and responsive.The Bad: - if feels like the tutorial covers the absolute minimum basics of the gameplay loop and not a whole lot more. - Some important details can be easily lost, and more important details aren't touched on at all (for example, hiring security guards and creating and equipping items aren't touched at all). - UI feedback is nearly non-existent (if I can't do something, I'd expect the UI to flare or otherwise focus attention on whatever is preventing me from doing a thing, instead of having to hunt it down myself). - Nearly all micro-scale actions are driven through a singular flow of selecting a staff member and then finding the thing you want them to do by panning the camera on the map in order to do it - it would be really nice to be able to do the reverse and find the thing you want to assign someone to, and then assign them to it remotely.The Odd: certain design choices crank the micromanagement up to 11, but also aren't especially well explained/tutorialized, which can lead to a lot of friction when trying to do certain things. For example: - building underground requires someone to be physically present in the room you want to build out (have vision in) while the same constraint does not apply to the surface buildings?- Rooms can only have one staff member assigned to them at a time, which means that no one else can take over when whoever is assigned goes on break unless you keep an idle staff member around specifically for that purpose. - Not being able to do things like set working hours for a given staff member to make the most of their various traits, or assign staff specific sleeping bunks so that they don't pick a bed clear across the map from their workplace that eats up a decent chunk of their stamina just getting to work, can make for an especially frustrating experience.The experience so far has been mostly enjoyable on both micro and macro scales, but certain features or quality-of-life mechanisms I'd expect in a management game, especially one that regularly maneuvers towards absolute chaos like this one, just aren't there, which can make for a very challenging or frustrating game. If you don't mind that, then for $20 this is a bargain.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of things wrong with this game, but I think it's because the game was rushed out before it could be properly polished. Being able to disable it would be nice.Being able to jump to alerts. For ex. when a room explodes or is repaired, being able to jump your camera to said room would be great, at the moment I'm bumbling around like a fool trying to figure out where it is.That also reminds me, the tutorial explains the bare basics but after that it feels like I'm stumbling in the dark. Other reviews mentioned how annoying the staff is due to constantly taking breaks and I agree. Being able to assign staff to specific  quarters would be nice.Patients also have a tendency of waiting in the waiting room for several days due to the staff arriving at work, doing one diagnosis, then taking a 12 hour break. By the time my doctor got to the office half the patients left.The game feels way too difficult at times, or frustrating rather. Having to pay the 90k fee in 7 days feels like a ridiclously massive amount, especially when the black market contracts pay pocket change in comparison to the fee.Don't forget all the money you need to pay for the rooms and staff.The directors are strong, or rather they can do any job and have maxxed out skills, so that helps out early on.Which reminds me, I feel like the DLC director is pay2win, in the sense that it never runs out of stamina and has no exhaustion, meaning it can do any work 24/7.Having to manually assign production is annoying, why can't we set the production to maintain a X number of say Wellcine.I know that it has somewhat Roguelike elements, and that failing and learning from mistakes is normal.But at the moment, the game is just incredibly frustrating, since I have no absolute idea what I'm doing wrong and what was I supposed to do instead.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game isn't perfect. But it's good enough. IMOIt has a cool idea, and for the most part it does a great job of bringing that idea into reality. You are playing a simulator game. A side scrolling simulator. Where you are the director of a branch of a big time pharma company. You need to make a certain amount of profits to pay your investors and if you don't have it you're in big trouble.To do that you need to make some less than ethical decisions. Creating super viruses, and selling weapons and gear on the black market to make money. It's an interesting idea and as I stated earlier, for the most part it does it fairly well.Overall the game is actually really fun and interesting with a LOT here that I just don't wanna spoil. but TLDR:-Decent graphics-Great sound design-interesting gameplay-Great pricebut the bad?-Stability is questionable-U.I. is annoying-Tutorial is awful-no tooltip helpful hints.I think for 20 dollars this game deserves a thumbs up. _childDocuments_.review: Gonna be honest, game is... mediocre. Such potential, amazing idea, yet it feels, like it's completely unrealized. First thing first: What should I do? Seriously. I played 3 hours, researched a lot of stuff, but I still don't understand what I need to do. Make money? Make zombies? Make cure? Second: UI/UX, in particular - lack of it. Take underground facilities for example. Why I need to keep someone there to build stuff, if I was there second ago, and I know, it's absolutely empty. How do I repair broken room, without recycling it?  Why my rooms are exploding? There is no explanation, making gameplay loop pretty uncomfortable. This game is an strong (very strong) early access, yet it position itself as a finished product. If this is a finished product, then I'm dissapointed. But I want to give developers benefit of the doubt (purely because the concept is great), and hope, that they will rework and polish this game to the point, where it would be enjoyable to play it.Guys, come on, I believe, you could do better then this. I WANT this game to be fun, but for now it looks like a demo or early access game in alpha.You have so many games with similar mechanics. Take "Lobotomy Corporation" as an example. To potential buyer: DO NOT BUY, unless you want to invest your money and trust into development.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: "Undead Inc." offers an intriguing concept, but technical issues, frustrating micromanagement, and a poorly executed tutorial severely undermine the experience. With cumbersome staff management, lack of UI feedback, and tedious mechanics, it's best to wait for updates or explore other management games instead. Recommendation: Wait for substantial updates before considering this purchase.-----"Undead Inc." offers a promising management experience in a chaotic post-apocalyptic world teeming with the undead. However, despite an intriguing premise and a captivating soundtrack, the game is marred by bugs, crashes, and frustrating mechanics that hinder smooth gameplay. Here's a closer look:The Good:- Intriguing Premise: The concept of managing an undead organization is undeniably fascinating.- Solid Gameplay Loop: The core gameplay loop is strong, with a decent mix of random and reactive events to maintain player interest.The Bad:- Inadequate Tutorial: The tutorial only explains the basics, omitting crucial details like hiring security guards and crafting items. Mechanics like managing suspicion levels or status effects are not explained at all.- Lack of UI Feedback: UI feedback is almost non-existent. When an action can't be performed, the game should indicate the reason instead of leaving players to guess.- Tedious Staff Management: Nearly every action requires selecting a staff member and manually panning the camera across the map to assign tasks. Assigning staff directly to tasks would be much more efficient.- Excessive Breaks: Workers take 10+ breaks per day, making micromanagement tedious and gameplay frustrating.The Odd:- Micromanagement-Heavy Design Choices: Certain design decisions make micromanagement overwhelming:- Underground Building Vision Requirement: Building underground requires a staff member to be physically present in the room, unlike surface buildings.- Single Staff Member Per Room: Only one staff member can be assigned to each room, meaning that no one else can take over during breaks unless an idle staff member is available.- No Working Hour Scheduling: The inability to set working hours or assign specific sleeping bunks leads to frustrating situations where staff walk long distances across the map to work.Final Verdict:While "Undead Inc." holds immense potential with its creative concept, technical issues, cumbersome micromanagement, and a poorly designed tutorial significantly undermine the overall experience. Despite some enjoyable aspects, the lack of quality-of-life features and challenging mechanics make it frustrating for most players.If you're willing to overlook these shortcomings and enjoy managing chaos, the price tag may seem reasonable. However, I'd suggest waiting for substantial updates or a more polished release before purchasing.Rating: ★☆☆☆☆ (1/5)Recommendation: Wait for updates or explore other management games before picking this one up. For now, "Undead Inc." is best left on the shelf.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like leaving negative reviews often, however, this game is clearly not finished.The concept is really great and I want to like it, however, there are mechanics that just don't work well.1. Staff get tired way too quickly. For instance, your medical doctor will diagnose one patient, and then spend half the day walking to the coffee shop, sit in said coffee shop to relax, and then walk all the way back just to repeat this process. Mind you, every time a patient gets fed up and leaves, that raises the public suspicion meter. Certain menus, like the black market, also cannot be accessed if staff aren't in the room and when you need that sweet, sweet dirty money, you may find yourself in a situation where you can't get said money because your admin worker is on the opposite end of town chilling in Starbucks because they sat in their work chair for 2 minutes.2. The game tells you nothing. The tutorial covers the barest bones, but it's serviceable, however, there is literally no  tool tips. Certain Director abilities tell you jack all and the only way to learn is click the button. Other items you may want more info on doesn't tell you anything because there's no helpful tool tips. The game does have a knowledge base, but it's in the main menu, why? I've never played any other tycoon/strategy that does this? Why do I need to quit out of my game just to go read up on something. The game practically begs us, the community, to make a wiki for it because of this.3. Suspicion rises way too quickly. I thankfully haven't had an issue with the police in my run like many others have posted, but the general public shoots to critical in just like 3 days, all because of my staff are slacking off.The game holds potential, it's a super fun concept and I would love to see this work out, but for the love of God. Please, please fix the UI, add some tool tips, move the knowledge base into the pause menu, and maybe adjust your tutorial a bit to explain some more. Most of all, re-balance the stamina feature, or at best, make a smaller version of the staff lounge so that we can put it in the buildings closest to their work zones. Heck, slap a limit on the small lounges, so that only like 2 or 3 employees at a time can be in them.I truly want to like this game, but right now, I just can't. If the game gets some balance patches, I'll maybe come back.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Informational pop-ups now explain previously unexplained content. Game crashes significantly less than launch. Albeit, still occasionally.     I've played this game since launch. I really, really want to love the game. Conceptually amazing, and the game play loop is fun in my personal opinion. There has been multiple updates improving how smoothly the game runs, crash fixes mostly alongside the addition of tutorials for previously unexplained game functions.     Thankfully I haven't had the freezing or crashes that I had at launch. I was able to complete a run with only a single crash. I hope the developers continue to push out updates and work on the game. Maybe also balance the zombies as it seems the safest way to complete a run is to ignore the "zombie meds" entirely. Also a way to identify Blindspot Hideouts without risking your staff would be appreciated as scouting without a private army is fatal.EDIT: After Patch 5/13/2024 - Much less Crashing, still crashes occasionally.EDIT:  After Patch 5/28/2024 - Just... Freezes, becomes unresponsive. I can't get through the first week without game freezing, actually harder to make it further than the patch from 5/13.. Incredibly frustrated. the added tutorial slide-shows are a welcome addition. Much of the information there I had to learn from trial-error.EDIT: After Patch 5/30/2024 - Significantly less crashes, workers no longer get stuck in queue lines becoming unusable. Have been able to actually complete a run.

_childDocuments_.review: So, ultimately I recommend this game. The game play is interesting and fun, its fast paced and makes it so you can't do everything the same way every time. I also love to hate the procedurally generated maps. Sincerely love that I have to think how to balance out everything differently each time. I'm greatly looking forward to seeing the final product. That said, the black spots are there. Devs.... your overall stability needs some work. Multiple crashes for reasons I can't fathom (my deck hates it and my PC still crashes on occasion), your tutorial covers maybe 50% of whats needed to play the game (how the hell do I heal up my guys, thanks google...) The gang members are prohibitively hard to deal with early on and I got really tired of losing 1 game out of 3 when my director is the only person who can handle groups of more than 2 without constantly throwing security forces at them so I can actually expand. I really hope you're able to address some of the stability and balance issues because I want to see this game be the best it can be.
_childDocuments_.name: Undead Inc.

_childDocuments_.review: Starcraft Silver League player here, this game is surprisingly challenging, subtle, and complex for a first time player. Definitely a bit more challenging than something like fallout shelter. The fact you have to earn the information on how to what features even are instead of a fully fleshed out tutorial + lack of more than 2 save slots + restarting new game every time you die, the procedural generation of levels being truly chaotic and encouraging re-rolling etc  may put off some other players by how unforgiving it is. The UI is decent, but not very user friendly to newbies that aren't used to seeing tabs upon tabs of numbers, names. The tutorial mode can probably be stretched a bit more to explain different concepts and interactions, especially with regards to biomass harvesting and black market research. The game was somewhat unstable and still is, but seems to be improving in the short amount of time I binged this game for several days straight to try to understand it. I think its a great game though it could be a bit more polished and like I said, a more extensive tutorial may give more players a chance to learn to appreciate it as well as add more content without necessarily adding new features. That being said, I hope the dev team considers more DLC or sequel since it feels like a concept worth expanding.

name: STORY OF SEASONS: A Wonderful Life
detailed_description: Put down roots on your new farm in the peaceful town of Forgotten Valley. Forge precious memories as you weave your own generation-spanning tale of friendship, family, and farming. Bring life to the land by cultivating crops and raising animals, find love among the town's friendly folk, and make lasting memories with a family of your very own in this reimagining of a beloved farming classic. Establish your homestead Live a carefree life on the farm growing an abundance of crops and nurturing the land to improve your yield. Raise cute animals that reward your affection with handy produce that is perfect for recipes, as gifts or sold for a profit at your very own market stall. Discover new animals, create hybrid crops and build upgradeable facilities to help you on your way to a dream life in Forgotten Valley. Befriend the residents of Forgotten Valley Find new friends among the charming cast of characters in the tranquil town of Forgotten Valley, and get to know them through all-new events! In this close-knit community, there’s an abundance of memorable personalities, from the mischievous Nature Sprites to the nutty scientist Daryl, that make Forgotten Valley… unforgettable! Tell your story your way Play as male, female, or non-binary, and customise your look as you start your new story in Forgotten Valley. Regardless of how you choose to play, all of the eight eligible bachelors and bachelorettes have romantic potential, so you can truly be who you want to be and fall in love with your heart’s desire. Fall in love, start a family and build precious memories Once you’ve found your one true love, it’s time to settle down and start a family. Watch your child grow into adulthood as the years pass! Will they inherit the farm? Or will they find their calling somewhere else? Help your family thrive across the decades in Forgotten Valley, guiding your child on the path to finding a future that’s right for them. A Wonderful Life for a new generation! Revisit a beloved story as never before, with updated visuals, additional marriage candidates, new animals, seasonal events and a wide array of gameplay improvements. This reimagined version of A Wonderful Life brings all of the heart and charm of the original to a new generation as the definitive experience of one of the most cherished entries in the long-running farming series.

_childDocuments_.review: I will be entirely honest: if you didn't play this as a child, you most likely will not like this game. It's slow-paced, clunky, and unpolished in comparison with contemporary games in the genre. This is not Stardew Valley, Rune Factory, or even Story of Seasons: Pioneers of Olive Town. It is, objectively, tedious and repetitive. ButI love this game. When I saw it was on sale, my heart fluttered. This was my favorite game of all time as a child. I would literally spend upwards of 8 hours (if I could dodge my parents for that long) playing it in the basement, enthralled. I learned Excel just so I could keep track of my crops and animals. I drew so much terrible fan-art that I filled boxes of it. I wrote fanfiction of it before I even knew what fanfiction was. Every secret, every interaction, every obtuse mechanic has been carefully cut into my brain. The world, the characters, they all felt so... promising. So open. So very much like real life yet so very safe. I felt like I was apart of this story. I laughed, I cried. This was my game.I write this as someone who's drowning deeply, deeply in the depths of nostalgia here. If I hear "Breeze Song," I cry. It's that important to me. That's why I modded this game to hell and back. Was it for gameplay? No. Was it for ease of use features? No. It was to bring back the old terrible 2004 graphics, the poorly translated names, and the music. That's honestly all I needed to give this 10/10, best game of the year. They could've literally just ported the Gamecube version to PC, and I would buy it on release day with a smile.So would I recommend this game? Not really, unless you're like me. The controls on PC are wonky, even with rebinding the keys. The graphical settings don't seem to do much of anything, and the textures are still somehow jagged and blurry all at the same time. The characters are one-note, their stories trite. But this is my favorite game of all time, and I think it is for other people too. This was a foundational experience for me, and it expanded the series (and the genre) in ways that I don't think have ever been fully realized - even today. I guess what I'm saying is, that if you are my clone, you will like this game. Otherwise, I think there's other games in the series and genre that have better QoL features, better characters, and better mechanics.But it's my game.
_childDocuments_.name: STORY OF SEASONS: A Wonderful Life

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get to the review, I think it’s important to mention a few things. 1. For those who don’t know, Story of Season: A Wonderful Life, is a remake of the 2003 Gamecube game Harvest Moon: A Wonderful life. From 1996-2013 Marvelous Inc had their games translated to English and localised by the company Natsume. In 2014 Marvelous Inc decided to have the series localised by their American Publishing brand Xseed Games. Natsume owned the rights to the name Harvest Moon so the English name of the series was changed to Story of Seasons. 2. Since this is a remake, I feel it's unfair to the game to compare to others in the farm sim genre. As many are aware, Harvest Moon (SOS) games paved the way to what we now know and love about the farm sim genre. They were a heavy inspiration for the many, many, many farm simulation games we have access to now, with many of its unique features being outright copied and further expanded on in the newer generation of games. In this review, I will only compare SoS:AWL to the original, HM:AWL, and speak of improvements or negatives. 3. At the time of posting this review, I have nearly 100 hours in the game, and completed most achievements, wonders and the encyclopedia. I have a 6/7 chapter farm, so some of my information may be from outside sources. I mention this only for the sake of showing my experience in the game. For context sake, I married Gordy and had an Academic daughter. I use an Xbox 360 controller and have no issues with game play. (I have heard negative things about mouse & keyboard but can’t personally speak to anything). ---Pros:- Huge bag space given from the start of the game (No need to spend $$ to upgrade, rarely will you ever find your bags completely full). There’s also a shelf & outdoor fridge to place extra items. In Year 2, you’ll gain access to an indoor fridge which has even more storage. - Romance & Marry men or women, gender neutral name options.  - You can give more than 1 gift a day to build up friendship, sometimes up to 4-5 gifts depending on the person, and friendship only degrades with one specific person. This makes building friendships & relationships incredibly fast. If you’ve played as many farm sim games as I have, learning everyones likes, schedules etc gets old fast. I appreciate this very much. - You can see everyone on the map from the start of the game. - Profit re-balancing compared to the original. It’s much simpler to make money, a good early tip is sheep are a good profit. - Movement speed and animations are faster compared to HM:AWL, you can also pick up multiples of the same item easily. - Fishing has vastly improved! In the original it took up a LOT of time, you hardly got any fish for the time spent and it was VERY difficult. There’s an actual shadow now. - The game is LONG! There are 10 days in a season,  4 seasons, and 7 chapters of story. Lots of replay value! Try different marriage candidates, have a different gendered child and try raising different skills for different story outcomes on 2nd, 3rd, play-throughs. There’s also 8 save file slots to accommodate this. Cons:- The game starts off on a poor note; launching the game will pre-load in Japanese, on PC. There are workarounds, as others have noted in guides/other reviews, but obviously, the game not being double-checked to be ready for launch day has to lose points in my book. - The hybrid & rare crops system is poorly explained, poorly executed/improved on (can’t bulk make seeds), and in general is very confusing for beginners. If you want to do this part of the game you basically HAVE to either refer to a guide/spreadsheet or write stuff down, thankfully there are really wonderful guides in the community tabs for this game you can check out. - Having chickens sucks. To get your eggs daily you must pick up the chicken, set it down somewhere else and pick up the egg from under its butt. Sometimes other chickens will race to warm up the exposed egg, making you have to pick up multiple chickens. It’s irritating. If not for achievements sake, I would not have upgraded the coop. - In a couple of in-game years, once you have the bigger barn & coop you’ll spend most of your time on the farm. It can take a really long time to tend to your animals, they constantly fall asleep so you have to wait for them to be “available” in order to snuggle up to them or milk. When refilling fodder, if your animals are in the barn (ex. while it’s raining outside), it’s really annoying to refill fodder since they’re constantly in the way. Just minor irritants that add extra time to animal tending. - Mechanics for influencing your child’s job/personality are not introduced to you in the game, to find all the information about this you’d have to look at a guide. This is good and bad, it allows you to explore your son/daughter more organically, but if you don’t get many cut-scenes it can feel like you’re missing out. - As a result of the above, because I didn’t know what to do by Chapter 4 my kid felt unloved because she had no friends. Apparently, I was supposed to run around with her as a baby and talk to people in the town to help her build relationships. She would say horribly depressing things like “I’m too miserable of a human being to hang out with”, and “Nobody would ever love a girl like me”, which could have been avoided if the mechanics were introduced in-game. - Carter & Flora standing in the dig site can prevent you from digging certain tiles, there’s no way to push them or move through them, sometimes you can lose out on items because of this. - Not being able to pick specific body types. If you enjoy being femme, the clothing all comes on one basic body type which resembles a masculine frame. -I personally recommend this game to players looking for a farm-based game that has life sim elements, players who not only want to plant crops, trees and care for animals, but also to marry, have a child and grow old watching their child grow up in a small quaint town, with characters to meet, grow close to and fall in love with. I would acquaint this game to a more ‘traditional’ Animal Crossing vibe, in the sense that if you take it at a leisurely pace you’ll enjoy it. I think if you are looking for a fast-paced farming game, with an expansive map, abundance of characters and features you’re looking at the wrong game. This game requires you to slow down and many things are on the simpler side. If that’s up your alley, you’ll enjoy the change of pace. I’ll happily give the game 4.3/5. The issues I mentioned are fairly minor grievances, and I overall had a very positive experience with the game. I mention them so that prospective purchasers can be aware if it’s something that bothers them.
_childDocuments_.name: STORY OF SEASONS: A Wonderful Life

_childDocuments_.review: If you, like me, grew up with the Gamecube version of this game, you may be overcome with nostalgia while you play it. It's an amazing sensation, but there are a few things that are quite disappointing with this remake. To begin with, the controls are neither "terrible" nor "horrible," but there are certain quirks, especially while completing tasks like Archaeology with Carter standing right next to you. This will disallow player input because he is within speaking distance of you, which can be annoying. However, if you recall the original game, planting, watering, and placing seed was a complete nightmare flicking you to the same spot and being a literal hair trigger input away from missing. It's a lot easier now with so much QoL adjustments. Ignore the bad reviews claiming this as it is mostly certain controllers that don't work properly. Xbox works fine. The game isn't or never was designed for keyboard an mouse, but sure could use some polish.Do you remember the original sprites? They butchered them, Nic, Nac, and Flak. I don't care whether it was for good translation purposes; this is something I am enraged about. Their names no longer roll off the tongue, and the Valley Forgotten Valley? It's FORGET'ME'NOT VALLEY... What on earth were they thinking. Could probably get a mod to change it back.Aside from this issue, there is another one. If you receive a board request for someone and want to give them flowers or something to expand their friendship with them, you can't do so for the duration of the request, so you have to get it out of the way, which can take some time to get everyone's relationship up swiftly rather than taking an entire season. I also don't see the whole issue with some users games loading as "Japanese" or other languages... There is a literal configuration option choice separate from launching the game before you are able to launch the game that allows you to choose all of the correct settings. Animals can't and won't die. This is something I honestly believe should have been included in all SoS games. Remember as a child forgetting to bring your animals in on a rainy day or forgetting to feed them, only for them to tip over and die or even die from old age? That is one thing I wish they had maintained. It provided a deeper meaning to the game as a whole.This doesn't really add anything to the game. It's just the original game with a tiny bit of polish.I can see it now, other players coming here from Stardew Valley and other games and declaring "this game sucks" you know that's going to happen. This game has less to do with it being a competition and more to do with it being a genuine game about growth, being good to others, and getting to know the population. There isn't much to do but talk to people, give them gifts, farm, generate money, and live a "Wonderful Life."There is no multiplayer or anything along those lines. It's an old game that has been rebuilt for individuals who want to relive their youth, as the originals were exceedingly slow with lag and other issues. Many of those faults have been addressed in this remake. Visually it's great, a lot of the slow inventory management and tool management is gone.Now I'll say something. No, this game isn't worth $49.99, nor is any other game developed these days. On sale, I would recommend it but as of now, only if you truly want to support the developer who brought a lot of good memories to your childhood and also something that was a catalyst to what brought you Stardew Valley.

_childDocuments_.review: Tip: Use the 'Launch Configuration Tool' to set the game to English before you start. 2nd Tip: Use a controller. The default keyboard layout is bad.'A Wonderful Life' being so close to my heart, I'd like to offer a high-level review and  info on what is new and what has changed.For those who have never played any version of AWL such a detailed review will not be necessary, so here's my review/summary and we can go into the finer details afterwards:SoS: AWL is a farming simulator set in the cozy 'Forgotten Valley' - keep various animals whilst growing crops, befriending villagers, finding your future husband/wife and over the series of chapters raising a family all whilst discovering new events & expanding your farm.This remake includes features from AWL & AWL Special Edition whilst offering updated graphics, better performance, a new spin on music, some new features and various quality of life changes. You can present masculine or feminine, choose your pronouns & marry any eligible candidates (regardless of sex).I'd recommend this game simply because the GC version had two separate versions (for hetero m/f playthroughs), some design issues and a  less sophisticated sound design, whilst the PS2 (Special Edition) had many improvements, it ran absolutely horribly. Therefore this remake is a necessary one and worth it.They did more here than the infuriating trend of simply updating the graphics and calling it a day. This is refreshing.So for those new, that's all you need to know really, there are some changes I'm ambivalent about, essentially approach this game as a 'casual experience' because there are more safety nets now.That being said feel free scroll down to the comment section on this review. I have put a short history lesson about the series name ♥CHARACTER: Choose your appearance (skin tone, hair, hair colour, body shape, pronouns and can change your clothes)RELATIONSHIPS: can marry ANY of the male/female bachelors. There is sadly no way to set a preference at the start of the game and all candidates can trigger events - a pity if you wanted a platonic relationship.CHILD: You can freely choose if you want a boy or a girl, no need for Mr Pots this time.BULLETIN REQUESTS: You can now do requests for villagers for rewards.SENTIMENT TRACKER: You can now view your relationship with all of the villagers in the pause menu.CAMERA: You can take photographs in game and they're stored in an Album you can view. Added side effect you can see interiors easier.CORKBOARD: collectable photographs throughout the story, I guess.ENCYCLOPEDIA - Records all kinds of items and when you first obtained them. This includes pretty much everything.NEW RECIPES (automatically added to the stove when discovered)WONDERS - Collected for doing various things in game - act as in-game achievements.COOP/BARN Upgrade: You can double your barn/coop capacity to keep 16 of livestock & chickens each!SHEEP/GOATS: These can now be bred.PREGNANCY: You will now need to manually animals into isolation close to birth.CHICKENS: Hens can naturally hatch eggs by laying on a fertilised one for a few days.MILKING ROOM REMOVED: I am not sure why. It's implied there is a tool to milk all your cows at once that exists.TOOLS: Upgrades are now offered over time via Van instead of by order book.FERTILISER SPREADER UPGRADE: Will automatically fertilise a field.FERTILISER MAKER: Now produces 5 fertiliser.FLOWERS: GOOD: Brushing is now the same as washing - no need to push animals to the trough anymore.GOOD: Milk is auto-collected now when using the milker.GOOD: You can bring chickens outside using a bell now.BAD: You can no longer feed your dog - your dog is now automatically fed by Takakura.BAD: Cows now provide indefinite milk output makes it no longer imperative to breed cows. Output will reduce but never 'dry-up'.VERY BAD: Animals can no longer get sick or die. The only consequence is there is a new 'C' type quality milk that cannot be used in cooking or shipped. WHY?!GOOD: Selection only allows watering dry/tilled tiles. Fertiliser cannot be used on a max quality crop. Useful!GOOD: Planted trees auto-block surrounding tiles to prevent planting. Useful!GOOD: Underwater bridge between Spring and Digsite improves ease-of-access.GOOD: You can choose items to sell at your market stall now.GOOD: Shipping bin/order form/collection bin/tool & food storage are all conveniently placed outside and close together.GOOD: Picking up multiples of the same item (e.g. flowers) can be done and putting things into your bag is instant.GOOD: Like SE you need to fertilise your grass - however a tile won't stay fertilised forever, instead grass spreads to surrounding tiles over time to compensate for this. Pretty cool!MIXED: You can see objects in the dig-site as you dig them up - however Flora/Carter standing close by can make it hard to actually dig.MIXED: Forced wake-up at 6AM. Takes away risk of oversleeping.MEH: You can leave the valley to 'visit other towns' but all it does is pass 6 hours. Future feature?BAD: Territory capture: It's very easy now - no time limit and Charlie has lost his skill.MOSTLY GOOD: Updated graphics - (a more cartoony colourful feel. Chickens in particular look very different and you are stuck with cotton-candy pink sheep). You may want to turn down the brightness a little.GOOD: Revised music - a new spin on music. Pity we cannot switch between GC/PS2/SoS versions)MIXED: Localisation - improved translation quality, however the updated names to be closer the literal/spiritual meaning of the Japanese will be jarring to those familiar with the previous localisation.MIXED: Design Changes - Gordy (Cody) definitely had a questionable design originally, the brow ridge arching over his eyes, wide strong features & the weird addition of facepaint however...BAD: Design Changes - Pui (Murrey) BAD: Design Changes - The Blue Bar BAD: Censored names in a single-player game - you cannot name something 'Cass' because that it has a bad word in it.BAD: We can choose slightly longer names but restricted characters - there is no on-screen keyboard with extra symbols like stars, hearts and so on available to choose from. Only non-accented alphanumerical names allowed.--------That about covers it. Loving the game so far even if it's over-sanitised in some areas. Hope all this info was helpful to new comers & devoted fans all the same. Thanks for reading and happy farming ♥

_childDocuments_.review: This is a typical case of wishing there was a rating between 'recommended' and 'not recommended'.As a fan of the original game, 'Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life', I've been enjoying this a fair bit. Quality of life improvements are sparse, but appreciated. However I would find it difficult to recommend this remake to somebody who doesn't already have a fondness for the original game. This remake simply doesn't stack up against more modern farm sims in terms of features. Somebody playing this game with a totally fresh perspective for the first time today would most likely find it lacking and would be better off playing one of the numerous alternatives instead.One aspect that I do find to be a downgrade from the original personally is the visual style. Seeing the valley at a higher resolution and frame rate is nice, but I do miss the more 'earthy' and desaturated look of the original game. It gave it a distinct melancholic and 'down to earth' vibe that fit the themes of the game and I feel this is lost to an extent with this version.That isn't to say I think this is a bad game in its own right, although it's difficult to not see it through my own biased, nostalgic lens. It's a solid farm/life sim, with most of the fundamental stuff that you would expect, but I would suggest waiting for a sale if you don't have an attachment to this game already. It definitely feels like the developers were primarily focusing on appealing to people that do, down to the game using a lot of the original sound effects and such. It can certainly be described as a faithful remake, for better or worse depending on your perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: This game cemented my love for the Harvest Moon series. I've been waiting to play this game again for 20 years. (I'm 35 now). This game is calming, relaxing, beautiful and adorable. This game holds a special place in my heart. It’s MARVELOUS!Initially, I didn't like the slow pace and clunky controls, but now I appreciate the slowness. It makes me be present and enjoy the unhurried nature of the game.The enchanting artwork, especially on rainy spring days, captivates me. I love exploring the village and hearing what characters say during the rain. I love that there’s a ton of dialogue to explore.At first, I really disliked the 10 day season. But it’s taught me to plan carefully and spend each day to the fullest. I like that. Tending to my animals twice a day used to feel like a chore, but now it's a natural and unhurried part of the game. I feel quite attached to my animals. They feel more real in this game than other installments in the series, in my experience.I really enjoy how much is focused on your family life here, in a lot of other games it just feels like an after thought, but here it’s such a central mechanic. And also, the fact your child ACTUALLY FEELS like a child is so cool. The remake captures the original's essence perfectly, in my opinion. I loved experiencing all the stuff I missed as a youngen and all the stuff they have added, including the new ones to marry. It's old and you can feel it, and in some of the pacing and design decisions, you can really feel it. But it's a Farming/Life sim at its simplest, and it's a relaxing joy. I LOVE that I can play it without having to balance a million resources and tasks and social needs in my head--it's an easy rhythm without a huge need to grow... expand… but with an interesting-enough premise to make it worth the pleasant grind.Playing it feels magical, like stepping into a world where time slows down and everything is okay. The entire game is about trying to find happiness in trying and dark times, in hopes that doing so will help you reach your goals. Truly a poetic masterpiece among gaming.I’ve been having a lot of bad brain days lately and this game has been such a soothing break from real life stresses. As someone on the spectrum dealing with depression, this game has been a ray of light. For how simplistic it is, it is so lived in—much more than any other HM/SOS Ive played. This will always be my gold standard. It brings me joy and tranquility. I hope it will bring you peace as well.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: The source of my earliest childhood trauma.They mostly brought over improvements from the Special Edition and helped streamline the "life" aspect of A Wonderful Life. It isn't nearly as memorable or eventful as, say, Friends of Mineral Town, but they tried so many weird concepts that I want them to continue trying to iterate upon. Your life in general is the focus, and they change the dynamic on you with every successive year.However, there are only 10 days in a season, as opposed to the normal 28. This means that A Wonderful Life is not only much shorter, but paced in a way that you have to keep up with more routines. AWL is more grounded than the usual expected formula, similar to Save the Homeland, and some of these aspects are what Stardew Valley wound up remixing in lieu of a more cutesy fairy-tale story that games like Magical Melody or Tree of Tranquility tended to hard-focus on.The Story of Seasons version of AWL does cute-ify the original experience quite a lot. I don't exactly mesh with the oversaturated look, same with Stardew, but SoS: AWL has the unfortunate issue of having this annoying green filter over everything. Many of the animations from the original AWL were removed or truncated for ease of access, which is a welcome change, although I wish they just made the original animations faster instead.I love the character re-designs, and I love the way they improved upon the original, taking ideas from every previous version of AWL and modernizing it. You can romance any partner regardless of gender identity, the ability to decide your child's gender was also simplified from the original. Instead of the original GameCube game having 10 years, this version takes the Special Edition's approach and truncates it to 6 years with an endless mode at the end of the main storyline. You can obtain a handful of additional outfits throughout the game, and if you're ever stuck, they explain about 90% of the game verbosely through an in-game guide. The last 10% were fairly obtuse mechanics that required Google to solve, but could ultimately be discovered organically by the remainder of individuals who still take notes.Most importantly, while this version is basically a port of the Switch release, it runs significantly better than the Special Edition while keeping the quality of life, which makes this arguably the best version to play. If you really want to stick to tradition, the original GameCube game is never far away, but this is a welcome (see: stable) substitute for one of the most notorious versions of the game, which is the PS2 Special Edition.I hope they continue to try out this "life" style of Story of Seasons, or at least remix them in ways that work with their new style, because AWL left a huge impression on me as a kid that no other farm life RPG has done since. Every new game tries something new, but sometimes it's good to go back to what was done before and find out what would work for future games.
_childDocuments_.name: STORY OF SEASONS: A Wonderful Life

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to buy this, feel free, but it's not what your nostalgia thinks it is. Maybe it's my own rose-tinted glasses and just how long it's been since I really sat down and  A Wonderful Life, but this re-release functionally is the same game with less in it.Since it's a crossplatform game now, there's no Mineral Town connectivity, which removes a small optional thing.Since animals dying is apparently not OK anymore, that was removed too, which thus removes the tedium of managing breeding cycles to keep getting milk from cows. I don't necessarily mind that, but nothing was added to fill the time that managing those cycles used to take up... so it's just dead air, now.A couple of building functions were removed or shuffled around. This is OK, I think, it cuts down on loading screens... but again. There's nothing added in place of the time spent running back to your farm to go inside a tool shed, so the game ends up feeling emptier than before.Even with all its faults, the gamecube release of A Wonderful Life is the superior version.This is a purchase I regret. I wanted my little sister to get to enjoy the game some more after our gamecube disc finally gave out on us - just a little too scratched after all these years. But it's simply not the same.

_childDocuments_.review: This ain't it. Basically, if you're on the fence about buying this, don't. Either wait for a sale or watch some gameplay before you commit 50 bucks to it. If you do get it for full price, know that what you're paying for is nostalgia, but beware. Your nostalgia is LYING. Do you remember how much of a craphole little town Forget-Me-Not Valley was? I didn't. This remake shows off every problem with the original that you don't remember. It's a featureless farming game with bare-minimum relationship and farming mechanics, all crammed into a tiny town with nothing to do. The fishing sucks, the digging sucks, and the music doesn't change between seasons. Overall, the gameplay experience felt kind of like being physically at McDonald's, but ordering using one of those new touch screen kiosk things. There's no meaningful interaction, nothing more interesting than menu navigation, that annoying Maroon 5 song you hate is playing on the overhead speakers, and you're beginning to question why you even bothered to enter the place when you could've just gone through the drive-thru. At least eating your limp McDouble alone in your car is more outspokenly lonely than being physically in the building and avoiding eye contact with the homeless guy waiting for the bathroom.It's not a 0/10, but if you want a good Harvest Moon remake, go play Friends of Mineral Town instead. Better yet, if you want a good, robust game that expands on A Wonderful Life's setting and characters, play Harvest Moon DS! No, I'm not kidding.
