_childDocuments_.review: Back in the old A Wonderful Life game days, animals could get dirty. And when they got dirty, you had to manually push them to a nearby water trough just for the option to clean them to appear when holding your brush. Cows would eventually run out of milk and you'd be required to breed them in order to get more milk from them. There was also only a single goat you were allowed to purchase, and once you bought that goat, you couldn't get anymore. That goat would also eventually run out of milk and there was no option to sell the goat, so you would either have to continue caring for this goat for the rest of your playthrough or starve it to death to open up the space.The remake isn't perfect, but it fixed several (but not all) of the issues that the original game had. It made a few new issues in its wake, like the fact that animals will breed any chance there's an open spot or the fact that Blue Tree Crops in particular are a pain to S rank. The lack of dialogue and the slow, grindy feeling you get as you progress to the final years are something that have existed in the original games and while the did add a number of new cutscenes and events, especially those involving your child, it's not a full fix.I cannot say this will appeal to people who prefer the more tradition style of farm sims like Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley or even other Story of Seasons games. I will say that this is the best version of A Wonderful Life and if you ever wanted to give this game a shot, this is the easiest version to experiment with. After all, I finally have tools that are actually upgradable. I can catch more than 1 fish per hour in game now. And most importantly I don't have to hold two (or three if you got the Special Edition) different game boxes up and ask myself if I want to play the boy or girl version while trying to remember all the differences between them.

_childDocuments_.review: As Someone who remembers playing this on console I had high hopes and expectations for the remake of such a classic and one of a kind game of it's time, even now the concept of ageing and watching your child come into adulthood ( and passing away) is still very rarely seen in these types of games.I know a lot of people will dislike the fact that some of the things that made this game a challenge are gone like animals getting sick and die, which made sense with the entire tone of this game i.e the journey of life from the beginning to the very end and experiencing the highs and lows and the hard work paying off in the end . But honestly for me it was still a thoroughly enjoyable experience. a Harder difficulty option however would definitely be a welcomed addition for some :)Despite the real challenge aspect of animal maintenance being absent you can still suffer from neglecting your animals by their products dropping to a grade that cannot be sold so ignoring them for too long will require you to spoon feed them Fodder+ and fuss them for over a month or two to fully recover from it so be sure to give them at least 1 interaction a day ( Especially your cattle animals)I'm unsure if I'm the only person to notice this but fishing did feel like it got stunted compared to the original release, I used to be able to get my farm off the ground by catching Sharsharks so fishing really felt like unless you needed them for gifts, cooking recipes to do  the 100 dishes or any other achievements it felt very lack lustre and wasn't great for making any money which i felt was a shame, the addition to multiple different fish and the option for Ocean fishing was nice  (original had about 7 in total unique fish an 3 sizes) All in all I enjoyed my return to Forgotten Valley and was sure to experience everything this time round to give it the fair justice it deserved, I also loved the option to pick Female in this version but would like some more girly outfits :3 ( Yes it's a farming game but we wanna look cute sometimes too!) As long as it doesn't look like 'I Love Bears' T_TTLDR: If you haven't played this before i recommend it as it is a unique farming experience and lovingly recreated closely to its original counterpart. If you have played before? Come back for nostalgia you won't be disappointed :)

I would love to see more DLC introduced in the future, but preferably more than just bonus player outfits.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like an original Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life game updated with a lot of major game patches (60% base-game + 40% improvement) including improved graphics (from darktone of PS2 to half-Japanese anime theme) and performance which is significantly smoother than it was in the original (60 fps with no crash or lagging), extended cutscenes and storyline, NPCs are more lively than the original especially your family members, step-by-step tools upgrades and a way to earn money which got buff in crops and livestock products (treasures from excavation site also) but got nerf in fishing and foraging so you can't fish for your life like the original one. Even though they change many things, they still use some mechanics like the original game (which I respected) including the weather affecting crops and livestock products. The game also welcomes all player gender (yes, this game support LGBT+) and marriage is not fixed in man+woman like before (but you can't live alone you need to find a partner to begin the next chapter). Rating summary: 9/10 for the player who doesn't play the original harvest moon: a wonderful life.9+(2)/10 for the player who plays the original harvest moon: a wonderful life. 1 plus from more lively NPCs and events and 1 plus from being me back to my nostalgia.Warning ****

_childDocuments_.review: I was SUPER excited waiting 2 years for this to come out, I was ready to get hit with nostalgia....and wow.  I really wanted to love this but I can't. First of all, the game is practically unplayable with mouse and keyboard. On the deck the controls are better but it freezes, Typing names in is a pain and you have to press a bunch of buttons at the same time because there is no keyboard optimization. Took me 4 Minutes to type out the name "Rue" on my deck. Super fun. Looks like crap on the deck too. The game overall looks too colorful and cutesy compared to its predecessor, it's completely lost all of the realistic melancholy vibes the original had. Everything is too bright and cheery with shoddy shading. The models and textures all look so cheap and lifeless. All of the uniqueness from the older HM titles is gone, everything they release is all soft and way too cartoony now. The original game was always supposed to be darker than the other HM titles. It always stood apart from the rest and was very special to me as a kid with it's aging system, it is one of my favorite HM titles. But they sterilized it all and turned it into a cutesy little fantasy town.  Yeah let's make the sheep pink puffballs like they came out of a magical girl anime.... let's also make it so they can't die anymore when the whole original game was based around life and death.... cows ALWAYS produce milk now. They altered a bunch of beloved characters and changed their names for no reason and the perfect town name "Forget-Me-Not Valley" to "Forgotten Valley", change the bar to a stupid cafe, didn't bother adding much dialogue etc. They pretty much dumbed it all down or more specifically, modernized it.The original game had its flaws but it was still meaningful & beautiful. It had more charm and was quirky. This is lifeless modern trash. Play the OG instead. I'm returning this for Rune Factory 4 S which I will be replaying for the 3rd time because that is an excellent game actually worth my time.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this out of nostalgia for Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life for the PS2 and I gotta be honest. Its kinda hard to recommend this for people who never played the original. Some gameplay aspect are still kinda dated for today. It kinda gets repetitive at later part of the game where your daily activity are consisting only to fishing or digging at dig site. And not to mention the valley size are small. Again those are valid criticism and surely will put people off.  This game is more suited toward chill and relaxing / zen-like gameplay. Its the "slow-burn" type of game so don't worry if you not feeling it at earlier parts of the game. And again, don't go into this game expecting Stardew Valley-like experience. Still here? Great, with the negative out of the way, let's talk what I love about the remakes. My main issue with the original games are EVERYTHING FEELS SO SLOW. Picking up flowers is a real chore with how slow it was. Taking care your crops takes AGES too which is a shame considering this is a FARMING game where the farming aspect felt tedious. In the remakes? those are gone. Everything feels so much faster now. Foraging for flower is quick, tending crops is quick.For new players, welcome! This game put huge focus on your life with your family instead of farming. so you HAVE to get married by the end of Year 1. On year 2 you will have a Kid and you can raise them to be how ever you like. Influence them to be a farmer when they grow up, or be musician or an artist, it will affect their life on later years. This game consist of 6 chapters (and one bonus 7th chapter) where there's some kind of time skips between chapters. Your kid will grow older and so do you and people in the valley. You might notice the selection of crops in this game are kinda low, because starting in Year 2, you can cross breed those 1st gen crops and grow a new 2nd gen crops. Oh and you can breed those 2nd gen crops into a new undiscovered 3rd gen crops where you got to name the plant yourself. And  1 season consist of only 10 days. Too short? Don't worry, crops here are multi seasonal so, some crops grow in 3 seasons, and some in 2 seasons so you have plenty of time to take care of those.Most of the game mechanic are keep intact so, whip out those 20 years old guide, some of em are still relevant. Oh and somehow they removed the Animal death. I kinda saw this coming since the FOMT remakes. Also cow now produces milk non-stop where in the OG you have to breed your cow so they keep producing more milks. Now breeding only gives a temporary "buffs" where your cow will give +2 extra milk. This game uses the Chapter system from the Special Edition (PS2), so every chapter only lasts a year (10 days per Seasons, One year = 40 days).The new art style / graphic are good in my opinion. The OG are too dark and this is kinda more saturated (again, just my personal taste. Some people might dislike the new art direction). My minor nitpick are how incosistent the animal models look. They have the original Cow back but somehow the Sheep and the Chicken are taken straight out of SoS: Friends of Mineral Town, so it kinda clashes with the new Cow model. The music are really faithful to the original. I love what they did to Breeze song here and get this, most of the sound effects are lifted straight from the OG games, including the environmental one like the windmill sound near Vesta farm.Since this is now localized by Xseed and not Natsume, some of the villagers name got changed. The new names are sounded more similiar to the Japanese one, like Marlin is now Matthew (in JP he is called Mashu).Is it worth the full price? Kinda. If you really love the original games, go for it. Its worth the full price. If not, you can wait for sales since Story of Seasons games usually goes on sale pretty quick.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest: This game is mostly for the nostalgia. OGs like me who have come from GameCube and PlayStation are thrilled to have this remake. For those who haven't played the original games, it may seem a bit bland or repetitive after a certain point as you ARE limited to a small town to traverse across your character's "Wonderful Life", but that was where some of the original charm came from for me. You grow older with the residents that you get to know, build your farm, and raise a family. I really appreciate SoS rotating back to familiar favourites and breathing some life back into them again. I can only hope that my hands-down favorite, Animal Parade, is soon to come on the remake list!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a first introduction to the game review after a few hours of game play.I have played the original years ago back when Adam Sessler was yelling at it on X-Play that it "NEEDS MORE SEEDS!". Okay, let's begin...## Core Game Mechanics ##Good change/update. The game pacing is faster. You no longer run like a waddling penguin that takes six hours to cross the map. I appreciate this very much - you can actually get a lot of errands done in a single given day, unlike previously.Controls are... Different with a mouse and keyboard but given enough time you learn them like any other game. However, the Stamina mechanic I feel is too generous if it is being true to the origin of the game. At the beginning, per the old game, you had very little Stamina. By "working" the farm, as years go on, your Stamina increases significantly, allowing you to do more - it literally paced the game for you outside of pure monetary means in-game. This mechanic seems gone now. You're really only burdened by the clock of the day, and your wallet. I can complete the dig site, farm, and run around and barely hit half of my Stamina.Graphics look good! Big improvement, if not at times stuttering. Clearly could use some performance enhancements to make the frames smoother in some locations, but overall a non-issue. No crashing so far!Targeting your "boxes" for watering, etc., can (and still is, like the original game) a little jank. To overcome this, however, I realized by aiming your camera straight down your targeting is far more forgiving. Thankfully, the camera completely rotating when you walk into one of your fields is gone from the original game. You can be rewarded by finding random recipies scattered throughout the place at various locations. Some exploration is rewarded, thankfully. ## The Dig Site ##Dig site is the same, mostly. Only issue here is the character hit-boxes block your character. A result of this is you can easily miss-click your action in the dig site, and some squares can be a PIA to target, making this issue a rather consistent annoyance.## Farming ##Works the same as the last game, really. I do still agree with the past criticism of the game "NEEDS MORE SEEDS!" but, honestly, it is fine in the end. Animals are the same, mainly. However, they removed the Sheep and we got Goats. Sure? Take that for what you will.You can pick-up a multi-stack of hay from the silo to fill your feed troughs in the barn. Not sure how I feel about this - QoL is better if you have a lot of animals but it is weird thinking you can grab a stack of 30x hay bales and just do everything in bulk. In a weird way, the manual labor is what appeals to some of us.I wish there were more building upgrades available. (There may be more later on, but I doubt it. Felt like it was a missed opportunity).Start of the game is FAR more forgiving - they even give you an apple tree seed to start! (Whaa?) EZ-Mode.## NPCs ##Interactions were improved a lot from what I remember. Cut-scenes and stories are more fleshed out and a LOT more common. Characters in the past that were hard to "find" consistently seem to be far more available. You now have a set of "hearts" you can track for relationships as well as a sliding bar to see how much people like you. I wish there was a way for you to track what "people liked" for gifts through trial and error, seeing as everything has a journal entry, but now I'm nit-picking. You can be a girl OR a boy!I wish you could sell more via the bin in your farm. I'm STACKING collectibles from the fields, flowers, etc., and can't sell them until I see the traveling merchant which can be a bit of a drag.## Conclusion ##Overall, good game. I am still just starting so some of what I say may not be entirely true late-game. This is also a day-one release review so remarks about performance, etc., may not be valid even by EOD tomorrow - who knows. Keep an eye on patches. The game in the end is true to the roots of the old game, with some added in extra material. However, I feel the extra material is still conservative to what they could do. They could truly expand a lot on this game and still not ruin the formula of the old one and I hope they do.My only main gripe is the clear failure of the Stamina bar. It, weirdly enough, is a core game mechanic that truly helps dictate game pacing. It makes rainy days feel liberating, it makes the dig-site an all-day consuming activity, and makes you prioritize just HOW much you are willing to farm without being fully burdened by your own self-inflicted workload. It also means meals, and Stamina rejuvenating items lose all meaning to the game. In the original you wouldn't catch me without stuffing my face full of Mugwort (Now an Herb) every day for that little extra hit of Stamina. Now, it is a stack of 20x+ sitting in a cabinet waiting to be sold.Oh, and the fishing -- Just get rid of the literal fish in my opinion and make it a shadow or something. It just looks... Weird. If you get the game, you'll see what I mean... Has no implications on the game... It is just... Yeah...

_childDocuments_.review: Hi all,A Wonderful Life was originally a Harvest Moon game on the Gamecube, and though it retains the trappings of most farm games (crops, livestock, fishing, spelunking), there isn’t as much moment-to-moment pressure to maximise your yields.Where games such as Stardew Valley or Rune Factory lock you into an absorbing cycle of equipment upgrades and farm expansion, A Wonderful Life is content to let you potter around town at a leisurely pace. Each season lasts just 10 days.Sounds short but listen there are 7 Chapters that contain different increasing years of playing time.There is no game (so far I know) where you will see how your child turns out when it becomes an Adult!!!Influenced by your actions and your friendships with the community around you, even the partner you have choosen to be yours take a bit part in it.That’s because the game’s focus is  as the title suggests  on having a wonderful life.There’s far more to do after you’ve built up your farm, chosen a partner and settled down.Characters age and change over time! New faces move in and others depart.Some Character are cheery on the outside but may reveal more once you get to know them, as continual heartbreak, unhappy marriages or the pressure of parental expectations are not uncommon themes!Though they’re not always explored in great depth maybe because the Dev thought:(What if a 9 year old play´s this game and the parents, did not yet teach them the meaning of life cyrcle).New to this version are non-binary gender options and same-sex marriage, none of which are any impediment to having a child together (thanks, harvest magic).It´s more colorful too and you can do Orders for villagers and there are Town event´s.You can teach your Dog comments!!! I hoped to get the Khivawa or more Option with the cat.But at least the coat can be Breed and Sold YESSS.^^Oh I forgot there are a some clothes to choose from in Shop, to buy as DLC or later in the process.What can I say more....mmh I hope in the Future there will be more DLC´s.Like Costumes to wear that are cute or lazy.A Town to visit and get two more marrieable Character.I heard if you could connect Game Cube with Playstation there where as a thanks 2 more Lokation and Partners to choose from.And that we can take care of the wild animals around our Village ( in the hope the Godness will appear).Uff already so long... uhm.If you know you can handle stuff like endless repeating like real life.You already loved this Game on Game Cube!And love extrem cute children, animals,  you want to just relax... nod just no grinding or rushing^^Than buy it like me on sale.^^Greetings thx for finally creating the PC Version after Years of waiting.^^ WinkPS: ADVICE ( that I forgot^^ and put just in )When you start the game for the first time, use the configuration tool, the last two tabs are for the language setting!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a Harvest Moon girly since I could pick up a controller, and HM AWL was my very first Harvest Moon game, so to say I was excited to play & had high hopes for this remaster would be an understatement! However, upon loading in the game, I was really surprised by how unpolished the game felt and ultimately, sadly, decided to request a refund for this game.To start, my game booted in another language, and I had to Google how to change my language back to English. While that isn't a huge deal, it certainly sets the tone for a first impression. I also had a difficult time figuring out the controls right off the bat -- keyboard and mouse are an option, but I found that sometimes, clicking my mouse would change an option, and other times, it would serve to confirm an option. Character animations were very choppy and the movements seemed sharp and unnatural, rather than smooth and fluid. It felt like I was playing a HD hack of AWL, not a full remake. I was ready to put all of that aside for nostalgia's sake, however, as soon as I gained control of my character, I found that the quick, jolt-y movements of my character combined with the camera speed triggered my motion sickness and I was unable to continue playing, even after turning down the camera speed (which was really difficult to find -- why aren't settings mapped to ESC?) This was interesting, as I've only experience gaming-related motion sickness when trying to play VR, never from a non-VR game. Being someone who loves farming simulation games, I've played a LOT of really wonderful games over the years. Many of them being worked on by developers from this studio! Having so many incredible games at my fingertips has really raised my expectations when it comes to farming simulators. With all of that experience in mind, it is really difficult to justify paying $50 for a remake that looks and plays like a game from ~2013, not 2023. If you really loved HM:AWL, you may appreciate this game at a lower price-point, like $20-$25, but I would encourage you to 1) take some Dramamine before you start up the game, if you suffer from motion sickness, and 2) lower your expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Story of Seasons: A Wonderful Life is a farming simulation game that was first released in 2003 for the Nintendo. so literary when I was kid I played a lot on PS2. The game was developed by Marvelous Interactive and is the fifth game in the Harvest Moon series. Here is my review of the game:Pros:- The game has a charming and immersive storyline that will keep players engaged for hours.- The farming mechanics are easy to understand and implement, making it accessible to players of all ages.- The game allows players to interact with their surroundings and the people in their village, adding a sense of community to the game.- The graphics of the game are bright and colorful, adding to the overall charm of the game.- The game features a day-night cycle and weather system, making the game feel more realistic and dynamic.Cons:- The game can feel slow-paced at times, with some tasks taking longer than necessary to complete.- The game can become repetitive after a while, with players having to perform the same tasks day after day.- The game can feel limited in terms of customization options, with players having little control over the layout of their farm.Overall, Story of Seasons: A Wonderful Life is a charming and immersive farming simulation game that is perfect for players who enjoy a slower-paced, more relaxed gaming experience. While the game can become repetitive at times and lacks some customization options, the overall experience is enjoyable and highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Im so so in love with this remake/remaster!A wonderful life has been a huge part of my life growing up, being one of my favourite games in this series.So coming from that i had an immense level of nostalgia!They did an incredible job at making the game truly feel like the old one! From the art style, to the gameplay I can honestly feel that im feeling just how i did if not happier playing this and i couldntve asked for more.(seriously they did an amazing job on the graphic remaster, balancing updating them but trying to keep the old colorschemes. i often find myself preferring the originals due to the nostalgic colors but i dont really feel that way with this one)Some things of note:This game aligns with older types of gameplay- tasks are a bit repetitive but days pass quickly, so its a great game for those of us who enjoy feeling comfy, relaxing/zoning out doing little tasks and rotations of gameplay (i.e. picking flowers every 2 days, choosing days inbetween for excavation, etc)This isnt the type of game with constant new features popping up so keep that in mind!it is not boring however, at least in my opinion i havent felt bored once so far. its just a more laid back play style and i feel it lends itself perfectly to making your own routines and playing comfortably. I find my days playing feel more structured and i can play how i use to play games, relaxed, laid back, talking to friends on the side. I love creating little routines for myself in this game, sitting in the square learning when villagers pass by to sell goods, etc. I genuinely love the pace! _childDocuments_.review: This is a modern day Remake of the original Ps2 era Harvest Moon A Wonderful Life. The game stays largely the same in terms of story and characters. A few mechanics have been changed, the game has alot more help and redefined interfaces and a few new mechanics and personality. But it largely stays the same to the original.The game now has a notice board for requests, (Some) characters designs have been changed, Pronouns were added, Clothing hair color and eye styles have been added in its place. Vinnie allows you to combine two crops into a new sub breed and eventually 2 sub breeds into a unique Super Crop that can be named by the player.The game also has a large Empathizes on Family, namely the Players Child of which will be the main focus of the game and has alot of sweet and heartwarming events to experience- Something truly unique from how children are depicted in games.Overall a beautiful Modern Day take on the classic farming sim that started the genre. Story of Seasons Wonderful Life will bring back your Nostalgia of the original and the beautiful graphics will draw you in. 7/10

In this game there are 2 side things you can do, and 2 major things you can do in this game. The major things are what you haft to do in order to get anywhere. 1- Farm (Animals and crops)                                                                                            2-Social (talking to neighbors to get hearts)                                                                                                        --They don't have alot of lines so you will get                                                                                                            the same line over and overThe Side things are fishing and mining, I say mining but its really you going into a cave and clicking square or "x", depending on what your playing on. _childDocuments_.review: They understood the assignment and once again delivered on a remake of one of the classics. Like stepping back in time 20 years ago, but with a fresh look and feel. The sounds are nostalgic.. with some of the sound effects being identical to the ones used in the OG. The music is  different, but oooooh, it just gives my brain a huge dose of nostalgic serotonin. Pretty much every mechanic that existed in the original is duplicated here almost exactly. If you've played this before, your brain might just take over and go into auto-pilot as this will feel in a lot of ways how it was to play the first time. This can be a double edged sword, however, as they haven't really added any content here to have more activities to use up your time. I had always hoped they might add more, as there is still a lack of things to do as the game progresses to later years in comparison to other  and  titles. The game handles smoothly (playing with a controller) and I appreciate more control over the camera. The run speed is MUCH faster which is a huge improvement, and the hunger mechanic doesn't seem to be as aggressive here. You can sell items to Van in a stack rather than one at a time (HALLELUJAH)... and you can also save anywhere at any time. They've added a way to check your affection and friendship with people (rather than kind of guess, because it used to be obscure) and you can of course marry every person who was available previously without needing to switch between games to do so. In fact, gender has kind of been eliminated altogether - allowing you to customise your character however you see fit and then choosing pronouns. There's lots of customisation here, and you're even allowed to change your hair color and style on the fly. Murrey's redesign is kind of atrocious, which is so far my biggest complaint. I can live with this, however, as I'm really enjoying the rest of the design work that was done here. I also feel it's pointless to not let people change eye color if they want, if customising the rest of your look is available at any time. If you loved the original, I'd definitely recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I want to say I played the original on GameCube and I loved it. *I think this heavily gives me a bias towards the game and I am aware of this*SOME PROS: The game is a faithful remake of the original and adds some nice mechanics/customization that before you could not do.It adds some useful QoL updates like the Map of where people are in the village and the encyclopedia. The music and sounds of the game are lovely, I have had no issues with music randomly stopping.The cut-scenes are welcomed and feel impactful to the game.The festivals are a good way to get closer with some villagers and are a good addition. SOME CONS:I do think, especially if you did not play the original, it can seem as if there is not much to do. _childDocuments_.review: I impulse bought this game, and don't regret it one bit. I, admittedly, never played Harvest Moon, I only ever watched my brother play it. I might've played it for five minutes, but I was too young and too dumb for it, so I gave up. With that, though, I'm coming into this game a little blind, so some of my complaints might just be mechanics carried over from Harvest Moon.If you like Stardew Valley, this game will capture your heart for very similar reasons (the romance aspect, similar farming & animal maintenance, etc.), but you'll be sitting there missing Stardew when it comes to fishing or mining. Both are incredibly slow and mind numbing, so I've gotten to the point that I'll just rest my thumb on the button to fish and mindlessly scroll on my phone, just using the vibrations and noises to guide me on when to reel it in. It's just waiting, and not at all challenging in the slightest. It's a little true to actual fishing in that regard, but when it comes to video game fishing, you can do a lot better than the bare minimum. The mining is similarly mindnumbing, you just mash dig on a hole until you dig something up. You just can't look away very long, since some holes don't have anything at all and you have to move to the next hole, so you're sat there mindlessly spamming the button to try to get through it fast enough. I've gotten to the point that I don't bother fishing or mining anymore. Not enough reward for all of that nonsense.All that being said, it's a genuinely good game. I'm not very far in, but I've been playing nonstop since I got it and I've enjoyed every moment, I just wish mining and fishing were a little bit more interesting. I've been playing it on Steamdeck and it works just fine, and once I bumped the resolution up to the highest setting all of my graphic issues were fixed! It's only crashed once, which is less than expected imo.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up on Harvest Moon: A/nother Wonderful Life, so I was very excited for this remake and followed it very closely. So far I'm up to day 10 of Spring in the first year, and there's a lot I like about the game, but unfortunately there's also a lot I don't like about it. Some of the things I don't like are nitpicks, admittedly. 1. Not a fan of the graphics; a lot of colors don't look good together. Most of the game's textures are washed out and very simplified, while some things are darker and richer in color and more detailed in texture. For example, Chris looks horrible because her hair has gone from a yellow-blond to muddy blond, while her pink suit isn't dark enough in color anymore to balance that out. It's hard to explain, but I hope people will know what I am talking about. Again, this is probably a nitpick.2. Like a lot of Japanese games in this genre, it's clear that more thought was put into the console version when it comes to controls. The keyboard and mouse bindings are an embarrassing mess and it's difficult to rebind them. A lot of actions in the default settings overlap, so for example, when I am trying to switch tools with the mouse, I have to be sure I am not facing any animals or people or... really anything, because the game will think I am also trying to interact with it.3. I love that most of the sound effects are exactly the same as the original, personally. But when compared to the newer sounds, (such as re-recorded voices and music) they sometimes stick out like a sore thumb. Some of the older sounds are still crunchy and lower-quality.4. Fishing is a lot easier in this game, thank goodness, but it's also... too easy. I'm glad it doesn't take nearly as long as it did in the original, but now you're guaranteed a bite within one second after casting, every time.5. The game does run as smooth as butter. I was honestly expecting it to run horribly, so this is a nice surprise.6. The range for when music starts playing in certain areas is way too large. The songs you have going on the phonograph on your farm start playing way before you even approach the entrance and it's very distracting and annoying.7. I love the inclusiveness with same-sex marriage and being able to be non-binary. It was always so strange that you had to buy an entirely separate game back in the day just to play as a woman if you wanted. I could understand being locked in with hetero relationships since it was the early 2000's, but separating the ability to pick your gender was just ridiculous.It's a good game. I don't think it's worth $50 USD, though. More time could have been spent on the PC version and making those controls easier to navigate and understand. I'm enjoying my time with it, but they've also managed to flick away a lot of the charm and character of the original with washed-out,  pastel graphics and more cutesy character designs. (Can't believe they've "yassified" so many people, like Gustafa, Cody (Gordy) and Marlin (Matthew.)) It's honestly kinda conflicting to click "Yes" on recommending it for that reason. So, make of that what you will, I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: STORY OF SEASONS: A Wonderful Life

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the original, it was so special being able to load up a new save of A Wonderful Life after all these years and fully throw myself into that nostalgia bubble. I'm only a few hours in so far, but I can say I'm having as much fun as I did at 10 now that I'm 27 (and the quality of life changes that they made are so nice.)If you're looking for a similar game to Stawdew Valley, then this game might not be for you, and that's okay. It's a lot slower than Stardew. When they titled this game "A Wonderful Life" they meant it; there's more of an emphasis on getting to know the townspeople and befriending them (there are quite a few upgrades and items that you receive through expanding your relationships with NPCs). They remember what you gave them as presents and make comments on it. As their relationship grows, their dialogue changes. You get to see the residents grow up with your character and your character actually ages! They get wrinkles, gray hair, and will comment about their age if you have them look into a mirror. You also get to see your child grow up and can influence what kind of job they have.This is definitely more of a laid back farming RPG than what is usually on the market these days. It takes about 25ish minutes to get through one day but there are so many things you can do: dig at the archaeology site, go fishing, play mini-games with an eccentric pair of twins, grow crops and raise animals, etc. You can explore new cooking options and take some psychedelic mushrooms and talk to the smallest of harvest sprites... I will say this game has less features than a game like Stardew since it's more-so focused on the stories of the townspeople. If you're not into the narrative experience I probably would recommend something different.Control wise, this game probably wasn't optimized for a keyboard and mouse and it shows. You can change the control scheme but it did feel annoying and I prefer using a controller. So far I haven't noticed much grief in the way of controls other than not being able to dig certain spots at the archaeology site because Carter and Flora are standing in the way...As far as performance goes I was a little apprehensive about getting the steam version since Marvelous doesn't usually optimize their PC releases but I haven't had any trouble running this game at the highest settings. If you don't mind taking a step back, learning about the townspeople, and taking in the story, I would recommend this game. If you enjoy a more fast-paced farming RPG where the years go by a little faster, I don't think I could recommend this to you. As someone that grew up playing every Harvest Moon game I could get my hands on, I really think this remake does the original justice, and I'm looking forward to living A Wonderful Life.Oh, and if you get this game... don't forget to give Nina a flower everyday.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit #2: Games been out for 6 months now and they still haven't fixed any bugs. The one "update: they did was to fix 1 or 2 items and all it did was break the game even more. There's no excuse for this.Edit: (Changing this to not recommended for the following reasons: The game has been out for 2 months now and there hasn't been a single update to deal with bugs. It's been almost 4 weeks since I've sent an email about the game breaking bug I've personally experienced and I still haven't heard back either.)I bought this game purely for nostalgia because Harvest moon A wonderful life and another wonderful life were my very first harvest moon games. This game is all about relaxing, running around to talk to townies and taking care of your animals. There is not much content here because the main focus of the game is around your family. Unlike most other farming games your not trying to rush around to get everything done in one day and your not trying to be the best at anything.    I'm playing this game with a ps5 dualshock controller, a ryzen 9, 32gb ram and a 2070 super and so far the game runs perfectly fine for me. No stuttering, bugs ect. so far. It started out in english windowed mode and I was able to switch to full screen no problem. One thing I really like is that It actually shows ps5 controller prompts instead of xbox prompts.   The color palate for the game is WAY to bright and doesn't reflect the darker art style of the original, I will say they did a great job with all of the house interiors though.   The horse is ugly as can be, it looks straight out of a nightmare, what were they thinking? Just look at the horse in the original game and then go look at the horse in the upcoming harvest moon game to compare. Seriously fix the horse model.    Lastly the cow model looks great, I love how they kept the original model in mind. That being said they clearly had different teams working on each of the animals. The sheep, horse and cows don't look like they even belong in the same game?? You have a bright pink round sheep with a realistic looking cow with a horse that looks like a 5 year old drew.       The new planting and watering system is the best I've used in a story of seasons game so far. It's so smooth with controller and it automatically goes from square to next square so you don't have to keep lining it up. Not only that but when you pick stuff up, you don't have to put it in the bag before picking up the next item. Huge improvements there compared to the original.    All in all don't get this game if you want a bunch of content. If you want a nice little relaxing story and to watch yourself, family and the townies grow old then get this game. As disappointed as I am with this remake it's still enjoyable to play and is ACTUALLY relaxing unlike other farming games.

_childDocuments_.review: A huge draw of this game is nostalgia, as it is a remake of Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life, originally for the Nintendo Gamecube.  A lot of the game play reflects that it is a remake of 20 year old technology.  The graphics were overhauled and some scenes added, but it is meant to play like the original.  Along with the updated graphics, the controls were made less "clunky" and caring for animals is made easier.  Like all HM/SOS games it does get "boring" toward the end, especially if you are a seasoned player.  This game is meant for everyone and is intended to be relaxing/cozy so it does leave a lot of extra time to get everything for players who are new to the franchise or go at a slower pace.Cons:-Glitch with chickens/eggs.  Eggs randomly disappear/reappear during collection.  -Dialogue doesn't update after year 3/4 which makes later chapters boring-Some cut-scenes are too specific with weather/time/schedule requirements to trigger-Characters are bland and not aesthetically pleasing (Even with the updated graphics characters outside the original Bachelorettes are ugly and don't fit with the aesthetic of the Main Character; they are over-stylized and have niche personalities that aren't interesting.)  IMO, this game has the worst cast of characters of any HM/SOS game.-Not enough story for chapters 3+Pros:-Easier controls+saving compared to original-Updated animal care (no need to push each cow to water spout to wash) and tools -Additional dialogue compared to original-Unique approach to farm sim-Fun and rather addictive gameplay for the first few chaptersOverall, I recommend the game as I did have fun playing it and didn't get really bored until the last year.  It could have used more cutscenes/events in later chapters as the first chapter had so much going on that the drop off was noticeable.  I never finished the Gamecube version, but was able to finish this one.  Not a lot of replay value for me, but I'm happy to have completed a play-through.

_childDocuments_.review: Story of Seasons: A Wonderful Life is essentially a remaster of Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life from the PlayStation 2. If you played the old one the game is pretty true to the original, all the same characters are present with the addition of a couple more. The farm layout is almost the same and the town is not only the same layout, it's the same size as the old game's world, so don't be expecting a whole lot more from the original. There is some new things added into the game. I don't believe goats were in the old one, and there's a few more interactions with townsfolk. And Muffy's name was changed to Molly, which I'm actually kinda glad. The graphics are hard to rate, they are pretty bad that it looks like the PS2 version, but they are also crisper and clearer details on the crops, items and other things; it's better, but still looks old and cheesy.All in all it's basically the same game as the PS2 version, with the notable exception that you can actually make a profit selling crops wholesale. People who owned the original will know what I'm talking about. When the game came over from Japan to NA and Europe it shipped with an error in its coding that inverted the seed/fruit price, so the fruit grown sold at half the price of buying the seed. The only way to make a profit was by either raising animals, using fruit trees that produced fruit yearly, or fishing with a fishing pole. Thankfully they fixed that lol.It's a decent game if you want to relive your childhood again, but honestly I was a little disappointed. I guess I was expecting more added to expand the game to make it new and fresh. I'm going to give the game a positive recommended rating because it's cute and I used to love this game, but $50 is VERY STEEP for a game that is a 2000s era repaint.Yes, I said repaint, not remake.P.S. - The option to play as a male/female character is misleading. You don't really pick a male or female avatar. They give you face/hair/clothing options that are either masculine or feminine and then have you chose your pronouns - he/him she/her they/them - so yeah. That was almost grounds enough for a negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm heavily biased because the original is my favourite game, but this game is amazing and I absolutely love it. I have changed some of the key bindings to suit my needs but they are still a bit wonky.This is definitely a welcome addition to the Story of Seasons series and I am so glad that I can now play on PC even with the keyboard wonkiness. I run most other games at high and I have to run this one at medium without antialiasing. _childDocuments_.review: With only a few hours in and nearing the end of my first Season, I have found this game to be both a huge dose of the nostalgia for A Wonderful Life from the Harvest Moon series as well refreshingly different enough to enjoy in small bursts of play. _childDocuments_.review: In it's current state, the port needs work. The camera controls in particular need revamping. But the gameplay is smooth. Work on keyboard controls. They just aren't very good right now. They lack polish and it's very awkward, plus I found no way of pausing the game to go to options while IN game to change the controls.2. The camera needs adjusting. Make it move with your mouse naturally, not by holding down a button. This might be rebind-able, but as a default, it's clumsy.3. Allow people to change their name and pronouns mid game if they wish. People's lives change, just as your life changes in this game. It would be simple enough to allow people to FULLY customise everything on a whim. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT AT ENDSo, I bought this game hoping it'd be very similar to the game cube version, knowing that it wouldn't be EXACT and I am pretty pleased overall. I have a really great PC, so I'm having no lag issues or any of that - I'm also using an Xbox controller, so I'm not having too many control issues, but I will still say that there are some weird things:When you're typing something in, it immediately reverts to if you were playing with your keyboard and it's a little confusing trying to get it back to the Xbox controller. You have to hit the ENTER bar and then you can go back to using your controller.When you first open the game, you're in WINDOW mode, so you have to go into game settings and display and change that. And then ... You can't partially exit the game to say, go on google for any reason - it will make you fully exit the game instead. It would have been nice if there were more characters added ngl - maybe I'll get some hate for that, but I feel like there aren't very good romantic options in the game overall. Maybe there are more characters in the DLC, I haven't looked yet but, there's that. OVERALL it IS good - the music sounds about exactly like the game cube version, all the sound effects are very nostalgic and I love them, the visuals are overall very good (BUT NOT THE MOTION BLUR). I'm really excited to keep playing, but I AM also hoping that the devs are reading the reviews and will fix things like this. The motion blur is really annoying. I know ya'll are trying to make it as close to the game cube version as possible, but it's a PC game whether we like it or not, and having motion blur is just annoying.EDIT--Previously in this review, I thought there was a problem with the motion blur, and there actually is not. There's a problem with the resolution and frame rate, lol. You can't have this game on max settings, it make it appear to have motion blur when in reality, it's just not able to fulfill the fps you're asking of it. I've got it on the 900 option and it's looking much better now. Also, I thought there was no quick save - but there is! When you're in your house and you go to that side table by your bed, and click the option that says 'journal' then go to 'write in journal' THEN you can save - and that can be whenever the heck you want! So that's def nice. Now that I've played a little more, I am really enjoying it. This is def a nostalgia game - if you're looking for the best farming sim ever made, this probably isn't it - BUT it IS nostalgic, cute, sweet, wholesome, relaxing, etc. If you want a really chill game to play at the end of the day, this is it. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pure rush of nostalgia. I can't believe it's been 20 years since the original. How does that make you feel? Because it makes me feel pretty old.Now I'm gonna start by saying this. If you're thinking of buying this game because you love Stardew Valley or Sun Haven and those were your introductions to farming Sims, I do not recommend this game for you. If you never played the original as a child, I do not think you will enjoy it. I wouldn't play this game if it wasn't for the fact that I LOVED this game when I was 5. It's a very simple game and is nothing like Stardew valley. I'm already seeing Stardew players flock to this game and saying it sucks. They just don't understand. They weren't there in 2003 playing this on GameCube. Now that I got that out of the way....It's pretty much the exact same game but they made a few changes. Some changes I like and others I don't.PROS: The farming mechanics feel way smoother. Remember in the original how much of a nightmare trying to plant, water, etc was? Well they fixed that in this remake. It's so much faster and fluid, and you can change camera angles while in your fields which is really nice.It runs really smooth. I have an i7 6700, 16GB of RAM, and a GTX 1070. i play the game at 1440p Ultra settings and I get a steady 60 FPS. I can even play it at 4k around 40 fps but I like the smooth 60 so I stick to 1440p Remember in the GameCube version it would stutter from time to time? And it was even worse on PS2. Yeah that's not an issue at all here. Which I would hope so, for a brand new game in 2023.You can now fish at the beach. Which I know probably isn't a huge detail but it's just nice that you can do it now. You can go to the city. Now what I mean by that is, you can go to the city and it skips time by 6 hours. so you can't actually go to the city and wonder around but it's a nice little feature for if you need the time to pass. (I just prefer to fish to pass the time to make that bread ;) )They added a bridge over the river so you can get to Carter's dig site straight from your farm instead of having to go all the way around. I really like that.You can customize your character how you want. Though I just made my character look the the OG because I just felt it wouldn't be the same.You can actually sell your produce in the shipping bin instead of having to take them to van. I know you could do that in HM AWL SE but I never liked that version much.You can save the game at any time by pausing it and "writing in your journal" which I really like. Now you don't have to wait to go to bed to save your progress.You can see how much energy and stamina you have. In the original you were always left guessing how much energy you had left. You could open your pack and see your characters stance to see if they were tired or not, but with the stamina bar it's just much easier to keep up with my energy levels. Though if you do run out of stamina, the game will skip ahead by a few hours and you will regain some energy.Van Still comes on the 3rd and 8th of each season and from what I can tell, he sells all the same items.They added an automatic fertilizer machine you can put in your fields. They're kind of expensive but I'm definitely looking forward to using those. I think they added a few other new things but I'm not too sure.There are four Bachelorettes and 4 Bachelors you can choose from. And it doesn't matter if you play as a guy or a girl. You can Mary any one of the 8. It's nice to see the developers being inclusive like that. I think that's about all I can think of for the pros. Now here's the consCONS:THEY CHANGED THE NAME OF THE VALLEY FROM FORGET ME NOT VALLEY TO FORGOTTON VALLEY! Forgotten is the complete opposite of Forget Me Not. Now they're just saying the valley is forgotten instead of not forgotten. This isn't a deal breaker for me, I'm just a little disappointed with this decision. But I'll live.THEY CHANGED THE NAMES OF SOME OF THE CHARACTERSMuffy is now Molly. Celia is now Cecilia. Marlin is now Matthew. And they changed a few other names. Nami is still Nami at least. And most of the other characters names were unchanged. But I still call them all by their OG names anyways. Ain't no way I'm calling Muffy "Molly" ick. The controls could use some polishing up on keyboard but I'm using an Xbox controller. It took me a little bit to get used to the controls but once you get used to them they're pretty easy. If you can't use a controller and you don't like the keyboard controls, you can always change your key bindings. Which is a headache, I know, but it is what it is. The backpack menu is different, like way different. I'm not really sure I'd call it a con BUT you have to get used to it. I hated it at first but now it's fine. It's just that initial shock of "okay, I wasn't expecting it to be like that." I never played animal crossing, but my friend said the menu reminds her more of animal crossing. So I guess if you play animal crossing, the menu will look fine to you The graphics aren't really the best. I actually think the GameCube version had better lighting and shadows and stuff. This looks a little more flat and cartoony. But that's probably what they were going for and I do somewhat like the art style of the game. Not a deal breaker for me though. I think the game still looks nice in its own way.It's $50. I think that's a bit steep for a game that's so simple. But nostalgia calls. So I had to buy it. That's probably why they made it so expensive bc they knew us harvest moon lovers would pay the price anyways. Oh well, it is what it is. I think that's really the only cons I can think of right now. IN CONCLUSION:If you played the original when you were a kid, you will most likely love this game. It's just a huge hit of nostalgia and it feels really good. If you are coming from Stardew valley, you probably will hate this game. It's nothing like Stardew and you will probably get really bored really fast. So keep that in mind. We don't need anymore Stardew players causing this game to have mixed reviews. Don't get me wrong, I love Stardew too, but it's a way different game.So all in all, have fun farmers! And build a yourself a wonderful life!

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a long time Harvest Moon player, so I have been very eager for this release since they announced it. I feel that it will obviously be more enjoyable for those who played the original back in the day for the nostalgia kick, but it is still good enough obviously to have new fans. That being said, those who are comparing it to Stardew Valley, and saying it sucks, I do not feel are giving it a fair chance. They are completely different games.Another thing: people are complaining about the characters names being changed. The reason for this is because Marvelous and Natsume split, due to Marvelous acquiring their own in-house localization team (X-Seed). Natsume still owns the "Harvest Moon" name, which made Marvelous have to rename to Story of Seasons, while Natsume continues to make absolutely trash ripoff Harvest Moon games. A lot of the characters names changed because X-Seed and Marvelous wanted to have the characters names as close as they could to their japanese names. Some of them were already close enough to english names, so those ones are as-is or had very little change.As for having issues with controllers not working, I didn't have this issue. I am using an xbox controller, but obviously can't speak for everyone on that., I was actually really worried this game wouldn't be good at all or have the Harvest Moon feel to it. Especially since the color scheme is clearly different and doesn't have that gritty ambiance the GameCube version has. Personally, I enjoyed the "thicker" models of the characters more if that makes sense. But I so far really enjoy the game, so where it is lacking in that, I feel has been made up by the improvements they have made since the 2003 version. Some of the improvements/changes I have noticed so far that I specifically enjoy are:Lastly, everyone is talking about how this game isn't worth the 49.99. Clearly, it is subjective, I've wanted this remake for forever, so personally I would have paid $100. I've ripped this game apart growing up replaying it so much, but even with the burnout that comes with that, I still really am enjoying the remake now. I will most likely end up with 100+hours. Also, I prefer the old chicken models haha.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough, here are my thoughts.- Beautiful story of growing up, starting a family, and growing old. So rare in this genre, and really well executed!- Certain elements have been made easier/simpler, such as being able to milk cows all the time, not just after they give birth, and having the option to breed goats. - A really interesting cross-breeding system for crops, with a BUNCH of hybrids to discover- You can live out the queer fantasy of dating anyone you want without judgement, and also have a child with your partner regardless of gender- While the tone and overall feel is much lighter than the original Harvest Moon title, I wouldn't consider that a bad thing. You never feel punished for failing to befriend a character early on, either.- While each year is rather short compared to other SoS and farming sim games, finishing the entire game takes some commitment (~150hrs, allowing for time i spent paused doing other things in the background). There's a time skip feature that i used a lot during the last chapter, and that helps a bit when you feel like you ran out of things to do between chores.- Eventually, it's easy to feel like there's nothing else to do. There's ranching, farming, fishing, mining, cooking, and talking to people. But the character dialogue can get stale after 100+ hours, and there aren't many special cutscenes after the first few years aside from with your family.- Also, aside from the few facility upgrades, there isn't much at all to buy in this game. Van's shop has special stock during the first few chapters, but in later chapters he doesn't add anything new if you've already upgraded your tools. Having some reason to keep making money would help this game a surprising amount, even if it was just more outfits or cosmetic upgrades.Overall exactly what i hoped for in this remake. I would love to see a child raising system incorporated into other HarvestCrossings, because there's tons of potential for generation mechanics and dynamic in-game community growth in this genre. Hopefully this remake sparks interest in that, so we can move beyond trying to make the "next stardew." It isn't perfect, and feels a bit like the meme of a detailed horse drawing eventually becoming a child's doodle at the end, but if you want a farming sim that allows you to actually *finish it*, it's well worth the money in playtime alone.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a lengthy and somewhat detailed review, I have marked spoilers especially the major ending spoilers.I'll be straight forward- I don't have a lot of positives to say about AWL.So I originally played Harvest Moon: Another Wonderful Life (Girl version) on an emulator early last year. I got bored with the game by year 3 on the emulator which I should've known better- but then it had been announced that it was coming to steam, so I stopped playing on emulator to wait for steam release hoping it wouldn't be as boring, but I was wrong...AWL originally came out in 2003 for GameCube so it's an old game that's been redone.Game was on sale a few weeks ago so I grabbed it for 20$ and I regret it. It's not a bad game, but it's not for me. By the time I got to year 3 I was bored again, but this time I forced myself to play until the ending anyway.I get it's an old game but even with this 'redo' and the addition of the quest board, the game just feels extremely slow, dull, and boring. Especially after getting to year 3, even with only 10 days in every season the game just felt like it dragged on. Watching your kid grow up and watching yourself get old was pretty neat but that's all the game has going for it.This game has WAY TOO many combos of hybrid plants to do through Vinnie.Let's talk about the animals and breeding- you get no real help on your farm so you're dealing with crops and animals by yourself. Now, I don't know if it's just me but the animals were breeding by themselves like crazy. I sold my last male bull because the cows kept getting pregnant, I sold my roosters because my chickens kept making babies, and my sheep same issue, I had to sell the male because my ONE female kept getting pregnant. Goat same thing, kept getting pregnant so I broke down and sold the male which you can buy a new one through Van.The ONLY male I didn't sell was the duck since you can not replace the ducks if you sell them all.The animals legit breed a high amount and every time I turned around, it got to the point to where I would sell as baby the day it was born so I guess it's good money but it was highly obnoxious.For some odd reason they changed- Marlin's name to Matthew, Cody was changed to Gordy and Muffy was changed to Molly.. Oh and Murrey was changed to Pui. I don't understand the name changes, but there it is.The bachelors? Aren't the best, they're some of the worse pickings out of any game with marriage I have played.. I feel the bachelorettes were definitely much better pickings over the bachelors.This game heavily revolves around getting married and having a kid and telling a story.If you do NOT get married by end of year 1 you leave Forgotten Valley and game ends- so this game forces you to get married to continue playing.POTENTIAL SPOILERS: About raising a child and the affects of certain items it has on choosing your kids future:In this game you visibly watch yourself get older. You go from being young to literally watching yourself grow old with gray hair, which is neat.... This game technically gives you a lot to do, even after finishing the game I realized I still missed a few things and this is one of the few times where I don't feel like restarting just to finish getting achievements. I will add: I've also been slowly playing Animal Parade (2008) and Magical Melody (2005) on an emulator and I've had much more fun playing those games than I did with this game.I hope they remake, AP, MM, ANB, and TOT.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game, back when i was 12 years old, i play this game all day, all night.The game mechanics are straightforward, emphasizing agricultural activities such as planting crops, raising livestock, and participating in village events. However, what truly shines is the depth of relationships players can cultivate with the villagers. Interactions with the diverse cast of characters are meaningful and affect the game's progression, with friendships and marriages significantly influencing the player's experience.Visually, A Wonderful Life embraces a quaint art style that has aged gracefully, showcasing a colorful and idyllic world. While the graphics may not match modern standards, the game's timeless charm and attention to detail in its environments evoke a sense of nostalgia and warmth.One of the standout features is the game's dynamic seasons, each presenting unique challenges and opportunities. Adapting to the changing weather and seasonal demands adds a layer of strategy, requiring players to plan their activities accordingly and optimize their farm's productivity.However, the pacing of the game might not suit everyone, as it leans towards a slower, more leisurely experience. _childDocuments_.review: I can guarantee most people in the market to pick up this game played it back when it was on GameCube, or maybe a very niche crowd playing it on PS2. For those people, I can say with certainty that it's everything you remember and more*. I'm putting an asterisk because the things they add to this game that are different from the original are small, besides the new coat of paint. I'll go further in depth in a little bit.First of all, let's talk about farming. One really aggravating thing about the original game when growing up was that there was so many hidden intricacies in farming that I just didn't understand when I was a kid. I didn't understand why my cows would not produce more milk during the summers. I didn't understand why my animals were all sick if they were in rain. Why my crops were dying because you could only learn what season they grow in from the shop menu. This stuff made the game a frustrating grind for cash using the few things you COULD instead of an intricate balance of learning and doing, just because FINDING the places to learn this information is hard. Luckily in this version, all of that is changed. Information is given to you upfront and accessible at any time through "Takamura's Notes" on the settings screen. But more importantly, they don't give it to you as an info-dump, but rather unlocking chapters over time as you need them.Farming also received significant upgrades in gameplay. Watering is much less of a hassle with the ability to snap to a new tile after watering one, so you're not trying to angle yourself for EVERY crop tile. Trees now create paths between them so you can't accidentally plant crops in ungrowable tiles. Seeds can be tossed as an AOE by holding down the plant action. It makes it much nicer to tend to your farm without taking too much of your day to do.Livestock besides the face-lift to the UI and giving visual indicators of health and affection didn't receive a whole lot more, but being able to know when your livestock have products ready for you, the bells letting them in and out now being MUCH less confusing, and not having to push each one over to the water trough for brushing is very nice. I wish we received more animals, but that's more personal opinion.Villagers, besides getting a few redesigns are almost entirely the same. Dialogue is very similar to the original, the bachelor and bachelorette heart events are almost entirely unchanged, and they all have the same schedules as before. Nik, Nak, and Flak, now Jack, Ace, and Hart, are now actually worth visiting, as they impart cooking recipes for you to use in your kitchen (I cannot understate how insane it used to be that you didn't have a recipe book). Most importantly, actually befriending every villager has been incentivized using a new mailbox system that villagers can send gifts to, along with a bulletin board that gives you quests to both raise their affection easier along with score you some free items. I think the things they added are nice, but I still wish that villagers didn't have only four things to say every day.Speaking of which, all of the original bachelorettes from A Wonderful Life, AND the bachelors from Another Wonderful Life are dateable, with no locks on gender. Clothes also aren't locked on gender, but they've been changed slightly as to be more neutral for genders across the board. The biggest thing though that's new for Story of Seasons here is pronouns, which can be set as He/Him, She/Her, or They/Them in this game. It's polished, it's well-implemented, and most of all it is SUPER affirmed through all the other changes they've made. It doesn't seem like much, but as a programmer, I know that means they had to rewrite a LOT of dialogue to work for They/Them pronouns to work. If you look at other games that allow pronouns, especially like The Sims, it's much more rocky and unpolished. So big thumbs up for them in terms of making the game that much more inviting for the LGBT fans of this genre. (Which is like, a VERY large chunk of its fanbase)In terms of the hobbies you can perform, fishing is not much different in this iteration, other than the fact you don't have to wait all day for catches, and archaeology now has visual indicators that something is inside of the dirt instead of just digging in the same spot ten times in a row hoping that you're doing something. Minigames are back, and not much different, but they're fun nevertheless. If there's one thing I wish they added more of, it's things to do in this category. I guess it's never too late with DLC, but I really doubt we'll ever get anything like that included in there. The biggest disappointment here is the hill to Mineral Town, which now functions as a 6 hour timeskip--which you could also do by literally just sleeping. It feels like wasted potential to not introduce a new area with Mineral Town characters (or new ones!) or new activities to do.Overall, I've been having fun with the game. It's a little brighter and more saturated than before, which in my opinion kinda changes the cozy cottagecore vibe I used to get playing the game as a kid, but the quality of life more than makes up for its shortcomings. It's still the little farming sim that made me feel like I had something to run back to when I was stressed out or tired, and to that point, I think there's merit. But there's shortcomings too. This game is almost entirely unplayable on PC without a controller (and we know how well Steam handles controllers sometimes). The game defaults to Japanese if you try to use the config tool first, which can cause problems for people who aren't the foggiest familiar with 日本語. Maybe with this port there's some potential for modding, but only time will tell.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the different take on farming sim that this game has:1. The majority of the game is focused on life after finding a partner and starting a family2. Creating new plant varieties  by crossing different plants together.3. Improving plant attributes: (improving quality, increasing which seasons and soil they can grow in).4. More variety in livestock types and productsI have never seen another farming sim use some of these neat features. I was hooked on trying to breed the best of each type of plant. (Many of these things are not available until after the first year, since the first year is focused on finding a partner. Get through the first year and the game expands). I didn't feel like there wasn't enough to do with the time available and I didn't feel like it was any more repetitive than other farm sim (I put a lot of time into Stardew Valley). The seasons are way shorter, so each day represents more time. A year is just 40 days instead of the typical 120 (30 days a season). However, I felt this fit with the activities available in this game. I think the flow of time was just right. This game definitely focuses solely on farming and socializing, so there is no combat area or similar things that people have come to expect from farm sims. One of the best Story of Seasons/Harvest Moon games. It is one of those games that I revisit every few years. (I played the original on Gamecube). I thought most of the quality of life changes were great. One thing that I liked in the original better was that milk production was only available after a cow gave birth, and eventually the milk would go dry. So there was a focus on timing and continually breeding new livestock that I though made it more interesting. Now the cows just give more milk after giving birth, rather than ONLY after giving birth. I kind of wish the developer would make "Difficulty Settings" or something to be able to choose some of these features in the original. Overall, still worth the time and I am glad they brought this classic back and gave it a new wonderful life :)

_childDocuments_.review: So I have way more hours for this game on another platform, but my review stands for the PC version too.This is a remake of a much older game that you have probably already played before. If you haven't played the original then I highly recommend you do so before trying out the remake. If you're expecting new additional mechanics with this game then you may be disappointed; it feels like they pretty much took the original version of the game, enhanced it with modern graphics and improved on some bugs or gameplay mechanics that needed some fine tuning like frame rate issues. Unlike the original version, the remake actually smooths out the farming experience to where it's actually bearable to play as a farmer now; planting and watering crops is easier, shipping items is easier, so on and so forth. They did add a feature to where you could accept villagers' requests for items or dishes in exchange for money so that adds more to the list of things you can do in the game.Asides from some character name changes and appearances (due to what I believe are legal reasons) as well as a shift in color scheme throughout the game, I do believe the remake does a good job of sticking to what the original game intended to portray to the audience...except for a few things that could be immersion breaking enough to ruin the experience of playing this game entirely.The beloved aspect of the original game was how realistic the progression of the story as well as its gameplay mechanics were. For one, animals could easily die in the original game if you did not consistently take good care of them. In the remake, animals don't die at all. That is...not how it works in  which is a large component of what players liked so much about the original game. If A Wonderful Life is supposed to capture the realism of life and its brutal nature, why are animals unable to die...? It is immersion breaking to know that you could go days without acknowledging the existence of your barn animals and they still will not die. It also renders caretaking of the animals rather pointless. In the original game, if you did not feed your cow for just one day it would most likely get sick or something...kinda like in real life? Yes, this is just a game, but when you take away an aspect that was already in the original version of the game that aimed to portray reality then that point becomes meaningless to argue. It breaks the immersion that the developers claim they want us to experience and enjoy out of their product in the first place.They also beautified the character of Murrey, a homeless man struggling to get himself situated in society. Though the brutal nature of homelessness for a man was once captured well in the original game, they decided to completely ignore the elephant in the room with the remake when it comes to how harsh life is for homeless men. They actually went as far as to change his look completely from wearing dirty clothes, having nappy hair with bugs flying around his head to having colorful garments, well kept hair and butterflies flying around him. Now tell me in exactly what reality do homeless people have it that good? It is not only immersion breaking but it is completely insulting to the people who have experienced that brutal reality, and it is also insulting to take that away from the audience to be able to familiarize themselves with that reality somewhat through the character like players could with the original game. You cannot sell to an audience the concept of a rural village in which its inhabitants live in for a myriad of reasons such as escaping the depressing and lonely nature of the bustling city life or the poor life choices they made coming back to get them, only to completely ignore how reality works and go as far as to insult the audience in order to do so.It is no surprise that the remake includes same sex marriage and selection of pronouns unlike the original game. After all, the original game was created in a vastly different timeline years ago. However, I have an issue with the way its implementation fails to really curate a gameplay experience for  like the developers claimed. It really feels like the game caters towards a minority group of people with a selection of pronouns or are attracted to the same gender, and this is coming from a woman that likes women. When creating a character I decided to play as a male character for nostalgic purposes, since the original game had you play as a male and that's that (unless you played the version in which you could only play as a female character). Right off the bat they have you type out your character's name as well as select your character's pronouns. The problem with this is that that's all you can adjust in the settings when it comes to gender-based preferences. Throughout my playthrough I had other male characters flirting with me in many instances of cutscenes and there was nothing I could select in the settings to prevent this. That immediately broke my immersion of a game that once did not include any of these features; what if I was a straight male and did not want male characters flirting with my male character during my playthrough but instead have friendly instances with them? Or what if I decided to play as a female and I did not want the female characters flirting with me because I was straight? The developers claimed to add these features and cater the storytelling and character design towards these new features to make the experience inclusive for everyone but failed to really get the inclusion part down. They should have implemented a feature in which you could select your orientation like how you can in Sims 4 and they should have created different cutscenes for this feature, otherwise you are creating a gameplay experience that is far from inclusive and immersive.All in all, I do not think this is a bad remake persay. I think the remake does a decent job at capturing the original game's message and emphasis on family, social interactions, and life experiences and choices. It is also nice that they added the villagers' requests feature which really adds more to your things to do in the daily life of a farmer. However, I think you would be doing yourself a disservice if you did not play the original game first. Though they improved upon a lot of farming mechanics and graphical issues that existed in the original version, I still believe the original version did a much better job at displaying real life through the world design, character design, music and story progression.
