_childDocuments_.review: A well made remake of a classic. The art style is, in my opinion, greatly improved in most respects. The increased choices, options, and more refined mechanics have greatly improved the game.Personal Pros:1. Vastly improved mechanics across the board.2. More customization (not much more, but more).3. Requests by villagers twice a month keep things interesting and motivate you to explore cooking and hybridization mechanics. (The rewards usually aren't great but if you want the achievement you'll be doing as many of them as you can anyway. And some rewards are really worth the effort).Cons:1. The digging minigame can be annoying as the two archeologists block your digging spot by being near it. A mod on Nexus can rectify this though.2. (My opinion) the pink sheep and less realistic looking chickens were the wrong direction to go. I think the game should have gone more realistic instead of more cute. But at least the chickens grew on me a bit.3. Some things are more tedious to unlock, but this isn't meant to be a fast paced game so on the other hand its not that big a deal. Be prepared to fish a lot if you want the best rod. By the time you get it, you'll probably be sick of fishing. Less annoying with the other tools that you will end up using regularly anyway if playing the game right.4. Name changes. Some characters have had their names changed from the original game cube version. I don't know why. In some places it works, but in many cases I feel it hurts the game. Ex. Ruby is now Lou. I liked Ruby better. Tartan is now Vinnie (and for who Tartan is, a name as common as Vinnie just seems out of place).5. There is an option for voice over language. You can choose English or Japanese. However it makes almost no difference. Occasionally character make grunting sounds but most dialogue is purely text and even fewer characters actually grunt a word. I think in my entire time playing I heard exactly 1 Japanese word. Its a nice option but it doesn't really do anything.I know I listed more cons than pros, but I tend to be more critical with things that I love. This game is worth the money and most of my complaints are small.

_childDocuments_.review: So far looks like a good remaster of a much-beloved classic. I've just about finished Spring Year 1 and everything has been very smooth - no stuttering, no long loads, and everything looks very polished (albeit very pastel and bright. I remember the original being very realistic and earthy in color scheme).As others have mentioned, keyboard play is terribly laid out and frustrating to use. Thankfully, you can go into options and rebind the most egregiously offensive default keys to something you like better. Ideal? No, but that's the solution we've got right now. Can't comment on controller play because I've yet to try it.Additionally, on first launch, the game will opt to run in low resolution windowed mode, so that'll be your first stop in options to fix. As for the actual game, a bunch of welcome QOL/modernizations:+Tool use has been significantly sped up and also somewhat automated (ie you can repeatedly press the tool use button and you will auto-select the next tillable/waterable square in range and automatically move to/perform action on that square).+Bells on the Barn/Coop to call all animals inside/outside.+Character customization. Pretty basic set of faces, hairstyles, skin colors. You can change your hairstyle and color in-game any time (certain bachelor/ettes like frequent look changes..).+The cooking interface has been overhauled and is much better. +You can marry any bachelor/ette regardless of your gender selection. Except Rock, he's awful, no one should marry him.+The addition of an achievements system for completionist types.+More cutscenes+Probably more but I'm not that far into the game yet.Definitely an enjoyable return for those that enjoyed it back in the day. It's all here. A decent entry into a Story of Seasons/Harvest Moon type for a newcomer as well - though maybe not as full on features as a truly modern game might be expected to be. It is simple and small in scope, the story about a farmer growing their farm and family over the years in a tiny country village. A very relaxed experience.

_childDocuments_.review: So let me start by saying, this game is worse than the original for the Gamecube. There's less to do in-game, taking care of livestock has gotten more tedious, even the shipping mechanic has changed for the worse. Most items you have to sell through Van now, you can't just throw them in your shipping bin anymore (including fish, herbs, and even low quality milk/eggs). TBH I haven't played the original in years, so maybe that was also a thing in the original too? I just know it's annoying in this game.This version of the game does add some new features like a side-quest bulletin board where villagers can ask you for items. And new character events have been added from the original version. As a lifelong Harvest Moon fan, A Wonderful Life was one of my favorites. Even though this version is a downgrade, I still enjoy playing it and seeing the villagers again is like saying hi to old friends from your childhood that you haven't seen in ages. It gives you a heartwarming feeling to know they're still just living life in Forget-Me-Not Valley. If you're thinking of getting this, but have never played the original, I recommend getting Friends of Mineral Town instead. If you have played the original, and are expecting an exact copy, then be prepared for disappointment. I only recommend purchasing this if you're a sucker for nostalgia like I am, and want to say hi to old friends from a long forgotten valley.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I'd like to mention that I am playing on PC and the controls are not even close to as bad as what other people are claiming. They are pretty normal controls for a PC game for the most part, and if you're not a fan of something, you can just change the controls. I didn't change the controls and I have no issues playing this game. It uses WASD like every other normal game, and you use your mouse. Pretty straight forward.I'm loving the game. It seems almost exactly the same as the old game at the start, but as the years go on you notice more and more differences from the original game. I love the changes they made to it, except I wish they kept the names of the villagers the same and the layout of the farm the same. I noticed they kept Cows the same, but changed the chickens, sheep, and horse. Unfortunately, I am not a fan of the new horse model and would prefer the old model instead of the new one. I am also not much of a fan of the fact that they removed a lot of the buildings for the farm that was in the original game and instead replaced them with tools. It just makes less for the player to do and doesn't make the farming aspect of the game as fun as it used to be.I wouldn't decline an update that lessens how long the horse sleeps when it sleeps, because I end up waiting quite a while sometimes for my horse to wake up. And as a new player, I didn't know you could call your horse so I ended up just waiting for it to wake up, which was real torturous. If possible, it would be wonderful if modding could become a thing for this game.Besides that, this game is very fun if you're a fan of harvest moon games and slow-paced games. Most of the time you are just living a simple farm life, and a lot of the appeal of the game comes from friending all the villagers and uncovering their stories and making your own by having a husband or wife and a child.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Sorry, but as someone who has not played the original but has played several Rune Factory games and Story of Seasons games, I found this experience to be pretty barebones and lacking. Every other farming sim I've played has had more depth. Rune Factory 4/Trio of Towns are better experiences in my opinion. I only got up to the start of Chapter 2 before getting so bored, I stopped, so maybe my opinion doesn't matter, but I go a little bit more into that and why... I'm a guy that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ puts hundreds of hours into ♥♥♥♥ like Animal Crossing and Farm Sims so a game like this losing me at a dozen hours is a feat honestly.I understand that it's a remake of an old game, but when it comes to remaking something "faithfully," I feel like some compromises should be made in adding QOL. As it stands I feel like RF4 and the SoS1 and SoS2 have multiple magnitudes more depth than this game. A lot of little things add up to make the experience a slog. Why do the two mining dudes block you from digging when you're on top of them? Why can you not put Fodder in the bin when your animal is on top of it? Why can't you interact with your animals without pissing them off if they randomly fall asleep? Why does the map not show the current location of villagers so I still have to track them down within the acre? All the other games previously mentioned did this. Why is moving around such a slog? As far as depth goes, all other prior mentioned games have 4 seasons with 30-31 days. This game all seasons are 10 days. Crops and products start at B, and go up to S within one cycle. Gaining friendship with villagers takes no time at all - justifiably since a year is so short and that's how long you have to confirm a marriage partner, but still, it takes so little time to woo a candidate that I felt absolutely nothing. Nothing really feels like an achievement because everything happens so quickly.Perhaps the appeal of this game is that there are chapters and time skips and you get to see the progress of time. That's why years are shorter and everything takes less time, but frankly speaking all the little things and lack of depth as a result made me just stop wanting to play before I even got past the start of Chapter 2. The problem is there's no real overarching goal or thing to aim for I guess? For a while in RF4 and SoS I'm raising friendships/crop levels/gaining money/accumulating resources and the process takes long enough that the progression feels rewarding. I don't get any of that in this game.Last thing worth mentioning is that the villager dialogue during gameplay is droll and starts repeating more quickly than New Horizons which is a feat.Rune Factory 4 has a lot of unique dialogue that makes talking to villagers every day a worthwhile prospect, and the script has the energy and personality to make them likable. It has more farming mechanical depth and it even has combat/dungeon exploring on top of that. More QOL than this game. There's always something to progress that doesn't take so little time it's unfulfilling.Trio of Towns has more depth to basically every aspect of everything, not sure what else to say about that in particular...I understand nostalgia and that this game probably meant a lot to other people in the past, but as someone without that experience this game is REALLY outdated. There are better experiences out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I very rarely write reviews on games but I was so disappointed with this that I had to make one. I grew up with the original AWL on GameCube, and it is one of my most nostalgic childhood games, so I was eagerly waiting for the remake to come out as soon as it released. The graphics are cute, and I liked the character as well as the fact that it's more inclusive now when it came to pronouns & romancable NPC options, but that's about all the pros of this remake for me. Like I said, this game was a huge favorite of mine as a kid but 10+ years later it's so simple that it doesn't compare to any other of the more modern farming games out there :( All of my daily farming tasks were done about 2 hours into the ingame day, so I spent the rest of the day awkwardly running around trying to find things to do. Maybe I would mine for a little bit, or talk to NPCs, but even with that, I had nothing to do past noon.. and then I'd just go to sleep and do it all over again. The controls were quite weird as well, keyboard and mouse had a really odd control system, and when I swapped over to a Switch controller it took a half hour for it to work properly. I did end up getting a refund on this. With how little there was to do, I would have not spent more than $20 on this. _childDocuments_.review: This is a great remake of the classic Harvest Moon game. While it doesn't have the style and panache of modern farming sims, what it lacks in features it makes up for in charm. It's a slow farming/life sim with a story to follow. The town will change over the years [chapters], friends will come and go, and the world evolves with or without you. This adds an element of realism not seen in many modern day alternatives as well as making each interaction/scene with characters special because [at least in your first run] you don't know who's going to be where by the end of the year. So many die, move on, change locations and new characters will be introduced. It's emphasis on community, family and relationships is top notch!While it's got a lot of heart, don't expect to be strategising too much or min-maxing skills/methods to raise money. There's variety here sure, but the scope is limited compared to modern titles. If you find recent games a bit too stressful and overwhelming with too many options on how to farm, this is the game for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to other SoS games I'm honestly disappointed. I never played the original AWL, but the focus of this game is animals, not crops. That wouldn't be a problem, though I prefer focusing on crops, but animal husbandry in this game is an absolute logistical nightmare. Chickens can end up anywhere, including lost in fodder grass in the field, and lay eggs at seemingly random intervals. Inside the barn, meanwhile, your horse will eat any other animal's fodder, sheep are constantly falling asleep on top of fodder bails, and you can't do anything with a sleeping animal. I'm struggling to get anything done, and my coop and barn aren't even maxed out at tier 1, forget about tier two. I know, I know, "skill issue," but ultimately I think this game just failed to find that line between realistic and fun. It just feels more like work than playing compared to other farming sims.On top of that, the game feels way more story focused, forcing you to marry by the end of the first year. I actually like that there's not logging/mining in this game, but they didn't offer any suitable alternatives (other than fighting to get your animals to behave), so you're pretty much stuck spending most of your day fishing and digging for relics once you've fulfilled the marriage requirement. All this also means that everything you get you either just pay for, or comes for free, like your house upgrade.Ultimately, I was really excited about the premise, getting to actually raise a family through a storyline, but the pacing is all off, way too much control is taken away from the player on how to fulfill conditions, and the entire farming aspect of the game was poorly executed. If you loved the original AWL then knock yourself out with the nostalgia, but otherwise, there are way better SoS games to choose from than this one.P.S. While I applaud the gender neutrality of the player, excuse me, but why does my wife get boobs and not me? Patently unfair, tyvm

_childDocuments_.review: Was really excited for this game after months looking forward to it. and even bought the DLC. Was immediately put off by how front-loaded the intro/tutorial is. All the farm mechanics (including soil fertility, etc which doesn't seem to actually follow what they say) is shoved at you as soon as you arrive at your farm. This is fine, but I couldn't find a way to properly recap what I couldn't remember which resulted in aimlessly wandering/clicking things. The BIGGEST issue for me is the UI. I've played clunky games and poorly ported games before, but this one was unbearable. Imagine a typical 2-joystick type camera (like Halo or whatever) where left joystick is movement, and right joystick is orienting the camera. It's essentially that, except left joystick is WASD and to orient the camera you must be actively engaging a mouse button while turning it where you need. I think a setting where you can remove the need to be holding a mouse button and instead have a normal fps style camera/movement control would make the game actually playable. Also, just to note, it took me about 45 min of play to realize that you could even change the camera view at all since it wasn't mentioned in the tutorial that I recall. Other issues: - The toolbars are not at all intuitive- No obvious 'move stack' option or tooltip on transferring items from one place to another- No pause (escape) menu - can go to inventory to pause the game though- Weird pet peeve, but when exiting a building you don't always have the same camera orientation as when you entered- Interacting with some items (ex. wild flowers) only gives a tiny prompt in the bottom right corner. I have a large monitor so it's very easy to miss- Would love to be able to access game tips, save menu, and general settings without going back to my farm house- Kinda weird that they tell you to get married quickly multiple times in the tutorial :-P- Farm doesn't seem to be very customizable (aesthetic-wise) Pros:- Generally really pretty environment (especially the water!)- Characters seem interesting- Intrigued by breeding animals/crops- Character creation is pronoun-inclusive (she/her, he/him, they/them)

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original on gamecube when I was a kid, and I loved the game, even if I didn't know what the hell I was doing. I was never able to get past the second chapter in the original because I just found the chapter to drag on for way too long, and I would keep losing interest. But with this version, every chapter in the game is only a single year. Which, while that may seem like it goes by fast, it's much better than them dragging on for too long. I love the simplicity of this game, but a part of me does wish they had added SOME things that you find in more modern farming sim games. I would have loved for there to be a way to know what events were happening and where. In the game currently it's so easy to end up missing most if not all of the events outside of major ones. Events are important because they allow you to learn more about the characters in the game and feel more included in the community. So when you miss a lot of them it just feels empty. I also wish that there was like, one other activity to do in game during the day. Most days once you've finished taking care of your crops and animals, and talking to everyone if you're the social type, the only things you can really do are fish or go to the dig site. But because the money balancing is really strange in this game, there isn't a huge point in going to the dig site once you've gotten your tablet for the year. And fishing is fine, but it takes a lot of time and you don't get a lot out of it. I just wish that they would have added something else that we could do to fill our days with. Overall I would recommend the game, though you may want to wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: ❀ ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━❀The original game was my first ever game I played from start to end. Hearing about the remake I was just waiting on the edge of my seat hoping it was just as good and kept the nostalgia. My standards, like so many others, were extremely high and reading the reviews before I purchased made me  nervous.At the time of this review, I have put in 46 hours. I play this game on Mouse and Keyboard. ❀ ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━❀This game gives you ALL the nostalgia from the original. Yes, names were changed and I will forever call them their original names but other than that, I think it's .-The cut scenes are amazing, in the beginning it is a lot it seems, but honestly I loved every single one-The controls are really easy to get used to for Mouse and Keyboard, you can change them as well if needed. I ended up only changing one key (the pick up key)-You can build friendship extremely fast, for marriage candidates, you can see all the cut scenes pretty easy if you are in to that before picking.-The map is so helpful to find people in the beginning, but you tend to find out their schedules quickly. -You are able to pick up the same object without putting things in your bag first.-Your bag is HUGE! By the end of year 2 is when I found I needed to start using the storage more due to my bag filling up quickly.-The Hybrid crops can be tricky, but talking with a few people you can learn a bit from it or just experiment and when you understand it, it becomes so easy to just keep going.-You can save at ANY TIME! There is no need ❀ ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━❀Reading some reviews, a lot has been fixed for mechanical things. I never once had it pre-load in Japanese on PC. The only thing in the beginning that took me a bit is to learn how to exit the game, I didn't realize you just had to press ESC and you will pull up the menu. The camera controls took a bit to get used to, honestly got pretty dizzy at first learning them as they are so quick!I do wish you get more things from villagers, like more unique tools and such. But it does make it easy to upgrade your tools since its all in one area besides "blessed" tools.❀ ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━❀All in all, I find myself always wanting to play this game. I absolutely love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: This entire review is just the outcome of someone who, as a kid, only got to game Saturday and Sunday between Noon and 9 while also having to split the console time with two other siblings. The only way I've known to play this game is while on the clock and intense.I absolutely love this new release of AWL mainly because, like myself, this was their first intro to a slice of life farming game and for many still IS the only farming sim game that has such an advance aging system embedded in it. (which is amazing for how old the game is) This is what I think would deter a lot of casual slice of life players. Your farm isn't forever.	For many, this game can start out as a casual play through but the aging system kicks in immediately. If you want to see and get the most out of this game a.k.a make money, build your farm and raise your family; you as a player are going to have to actually think about where you put your assists.	This is where I think the game's EASY and HARD mode activate (if that's hard to believe) Unlike other farming slice of life you have to choose which path you want to focus on. This is because, AGAIN, the aging system makes you need to prioritize your resources. In my opinion, crops would be considered HARD mode due to the many hybrid combinations (HINT: its not just the crops but also the crop quality) but I'd prefer every gamer make their own experiences and conclusions.You can 100% play this game very casually and still have a great experience but you'll honestly end up walking away feeling like the game could've been better (because I have) only to replay and realize how different the gaming experience can be when you focus on how you want your farm to be from the start. Side note: All of this detail is only for building your farm so imagine how the game gets when you have a kid that also has its own growing system that is impacted by who you marry and how you interact with them.Basically if you're looking for a game that will probably consume you for the rest of your life this game is wonderful however its not for everyone because its not one of those games that you can really get "lost in" and benefit from it.

_childDocuments_.review: When this game was announced I was super excited. I played the original a lot on my GameCube and always had fun min maxing how much money I could make within the first year, be it legitimate or with the glitches that existed. That said, the localized translation of the original left... a lot to be desired... I don't think I ever uncovered every record or secret.Now this one is in my hands and not only is there nice localization and some good QOL, I'm once again spending a lot of my time min maxing different files to see how much money I can make based on luck, choices and the like. I love the rest of the game, too, but the simplicity of that first year has always been the most enjoyable for me.That's why despite my enjoyment of the game and raising my child with different spouses as I build up the farm, I was a bit sad and disappointed that the game puts you in a game over if you do not marry. It's the point of the game, yes, but I was hoping that would be changed with this new version, to like, some stasis where you can say 'not ready yet' and it just replays year 1 for you. That first year just goes so so fast and I'd really love more time to properly dedicate to not just befriending the potential spouses, but getting them genuine gifts they actually enjoy. Instead of, yanno, shoving flowers and herbal soup at them every day (what I keep doing every playthrough so far).Or for an option to not marry anyone locally and wind up being the single parent of a kid anyway (a fling from someone in the city that went sour or... whatever), but that's an overly ambitious expectation to have for a remake game, so I'm just being wistful here.The only other thing I think I wish was in-game was the ability to skip cutscenes. I replay year 1 over and over... so stumbling into all the events every time back to back sometimes makes me wheeze.That said the rest of the game is about just as I remembered it and a lot more. I only had the original version, so just 3 spouses (Nami, Cecilia, Molly). Being able to see the male spouses from the other versions (Another Wonderful Life and Special Edition, iirc) was a treat and I do understand and appreciate the name changes to a number of the characters. I think the only thing that throws me out of the loop in terms of localization in this game now is calling it "Forgotten" Valley. I think keeping it as "Forget Me Not" would have a lot more punch to Takakura's opening narration if he said "Forget Me Not Valley, a place that the world over time forgot about" or. Something. It just doesn't ring the same, but it's not a deal breaker. I also miss the alliterative/rhythmic appeal of Nic Nac and Flak. Hybrids are just as overwhelming to me as ever and I'm glad that they kept cows looking the same as in the original! I always enjoyed a more realistic leaning kind of direction with the farm animals and it's why AWL was my favorite out of every game. I was a lil sad that the other animals are super stylized though (sheep are pink and have their afros, chickens and ducks are orbs, goats... well they are certainly goats, the horse is also certainly a horse). They're growing on me. I love my sheeps now. Wish there was a breed that was natural white colored though.All that aside I do enjoy how this game is more or less a relationship with your kid as you raise them, and the farming has a deep system with a lot of stuff to explore in it but is not necessary to have a decent experience. Kids are cute and grow up so fast. :[ Again I'd love a perpetual mode to just 'stall' a year before progressing to experience some of it a little longer.Anyone coming from a game like Stardew need to know that this game does have a specific goal and an end. It's a bit open ended in what you can specialize in to make a profit on your farm, but there are specific factors you have to take in when it comes to making money and how profits can be VERY fast if you're lucky (my file where I dug up 7 golden forks day 1 of spring...) or slow and steady if you're not. Some things can be very obscure and vague (like parts of raising your kid's interest and learning hybrid crops, but there are guides for those, for the most part). It's all those little things that more or less show that this is a remake of a game from a previous console age. If you're OK with something a bit more linear goal wise and want something different I recommend this game. If you much prefer the absolute near timeless freedom Stardew provides, then perhaps not.I'm generally mostly fixated on year 1 cause I know I am determined to have a specific profit before I get married and I've yet to reach that yet. I am stubborn, but I'm having fun while doing it. I'll eventually finish a full life on a file when I quit being stubborn about it but I'm in no rush for it.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is very biased toward Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life, I came into this with very low expectations. I did not enjoy the character redesigns in Story of Seasons: Friends of Mineral Town. Heck, I already did not enjoy the decisions to modify character relationships, families, etc. Specifically for the port of Harvest Moon 64 that became its own game, Harvest Moon: Back to Nature. Gotz will always be Karin's father, Rick will always be Ann's cousin, etc. Though, don't confuse that with me not saying it is a good game, because BtN is great. I speak so articulate because I enjoy the game, but I digress. Lastly, I expected the graphics to be very muddy, tons of creative choices done to hinder rather than improve the core of the game. There was a lot I could have thought of.Surprisingly, Story of Seasons: A Wonderful Life deviates almost entirely from my expectations. It is not without me saying it has any issues at all, but it has far fewer than I expected. I had already been making this list since I started playing, and I am not that far into the game so it will not be nearly as in-depth as many others on here.Pros+ New art style does not look like a smartphone game.+ Town Introduction can now be skipped.+ Gameplay is incredibly more streamlined.+ Through testing out various inputs, it is indeed possible to play with the GameCube controller for all necessary inputs.Cons- Load times are very poor when entering buildings [Steam Deck].- "Takakura's Notes" are shoved down your throat and sometimes spoil stuff that should have been a surprise, as they were in the original.- Poor analog implementation.- Renaming characters with established identities.Neutral° Player can move noticeably faster.° Difficulty is noticeably increased in farming activities, requirements to retain energy, etc.° Bulletin Board from The Tale of Two Towns returns.° Load Screen should have an option to be a black circle transition to make it easier on the eyes.Now, to summarize a couple. The analog is because I wish the game tried to have a speed between "walk normally" and "ludicrous speed" and it does not feel like there is. So if your joystick is sensitive, you will shoot to the moon right away. It is not like you ever need to walk, and when you are in Strafe Mode, it is very controllable. It just feels a bit imbalanced to me, but honestly does not take away too much from the game.Other thing is, I do not like character names being changed at all. For instance, Maria from Harvest Moon 64 will always be how I refer to her (changed to "Mary" from BtN onward) to list a different game for example. I will always call Muffy by her first name too (changed to "Molly" from AWL remake onward). Stuff like this bothers me since they already have names tied to them and in a remake of a game that is most focused on its characters than anything else (well, up to the first Story of Seasons, anyway), it means a lot to me. You get attached to how a certain character is and this practice they sometimes do of modifying a character's title, origins, etc. This stuff bothers me a lot. I don't mind them adding more to the character, but taking away is where I put my foot down. Unlike the case with SoS: FoMT that was more grounded in names, art design and writing, once a text editor comes out for SoS: AWL, I can just change the names back. I am still waiting for a mod of BtN and FoMT that does that someday, but I digress.That is the end of my criticisms. I actually enjoy playing this a lot, these aside. I know it is an old game in spirit, but it is the first time I have wanted to put time into a new release in forever. It is still very fun to play, same as the original. But it adds so much more. Lumina has a drastically better redesign than the effort of AWL Special Edition. Besides her, the male characters they redesigned to be better suited as bachelors are good too. Gustafa feels like a younger version of himself and has a very good voice for his appearance. Gordy feels exactly the same, on top of the emotional distress of his art being more in line with his age. Kind of wish Matthew took a bit more inspiration from his original design when he was Marlin, but it is not a bad take on him. I do wish Yasuhiro Wada was consulted to at least help with art design in both the FoMT and AWL remakes since that would have helped a lot, but I can at least say the AWL remake did a much better job at being faithful to the original than the FoMT remake.I was also surprised the remade music was not unpleasant on the ears this time. SoS: FoMT has a very unbalanced soundtrack with a few good ideas, though I definitely just wanted to replace all of it with the BtN originals. Overall, a lot of the music in SoS: AWL is much better by comparison. I do miss the original intro portion of Breeze, but I can live with it. The new one sounds nice. I actually think some of the NPC House music sounds better in some cases. And I am very picky on music too, so the fact I can confidently say it catches the charm of the originals in a lot of them is very nice to admit.I would like to go on even more, but sadly, I am only in the first week of Spring. Shocking to write this much in such an early part of the game, I know. But I will say I am here to stay for the journey with how optimistic I sound, beginning part aside. And if anybody does prefer things all the way in both remakes, godspeed. Nothing wrong with that. I just personally miss how some things used to be and I will always feel that way. But I have decided I want to invest a lot of time into this remake. It has been very fun to me. Also, this accidentally just turned into a double review since I brought up the FoMT remake a ton.But, yeah. For those who enjoyed the original Harvest Moon: A Wonderful Life, please give Story of Seasons: A Wonderful Life a chance. It will be well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Very slow-paced and probably more so enjoyed by those who played the original Harvest Moon: It's A Wonderful Life on the gamecube or playstation. I grew up playing the original on gamecube so being able to return to a newly polished remake was exciting. I kept getting hit with waves of nostalgia while playing, especially in the opening scene. I would say that if you like slow paced farming games set in small towns you'll likely enjoy the game, but because of the price, I would recommend possibly watching a play through of the game online before buying- or waiting for it to go on sale- just to make sure you really want the game. Aside from my love for the original, which leads me to love this remake, I could understand why someone WOULD NOT like this game. The map is very small and days can seem repetitive if you have no requests or goals in mind. It sometimes just feels like an endless loop of: talk to your favorite villager, forage, water crops, tend to animals, end day, repeat. Which can cause some boring and stale gameplay. To solve this, I think it's best to have goals in mind and keep an online guide nearby as you play so that you can make goals and understand what you need to do to achieve those goals. The game doesn't really give you large objectives to work towards, like stardew valley and the community center, it just kinda tells you to start establishing a life in your new home. The only large goal that I have encountered so far is that the nature sprites briefly mention that they want to bring back the harvest goddess through the spring and wish to do that by making the area nice and caring for it, but after that cutscene, you aren't given any objectives or quests to work towards that goal which is a bit confusing. Anyway, overall, I love the game even though I haven't finished it yet, but I can understand why someone would not like the game, or feel as if it's boring or aimless. Really, the point of the game is to live 'a wonderful life' by changing, growing, and making connections that will last you a lifetime. The messages within the game are very bittersweet, and for players of the original (from my experience), will feel very nostalgic not only for the original, but for the time in their life when they had first been playing the game. Really brought me back to sitting on the scratchy carpet floor of my shared bedroom with my two siblings and staring up at a TV as I played the game for hours on end until my neck started to ache. I remember the dig site by the waterfall was my absolute favorite (and still is!). I was constantly going up there just because I loved how secluded that area felt.In summary, I would recommend this game to those who played the original and fans of other harvest moon games, stardew valley, and just anyone who enjoys small town farm games. The characters within the game are very likeable and have good dialogue that doesn't feel awkward or stale (sometimes can feel repetitive but what can you do? lol). They each have unique personalities and within your first season you'll feel yourself gravitating toward a specific "group" of villagers or a specific villager, which really helps with creating a sense of community in the game! The cutscenes you encounter are cute and enjoyable, with good back and forth dialogue that give really good insight into the characters and your role within the town. The farming system is easy to understand and doesn't feel overly complicated. The animals are easy enough to care for that they don't feel like an inconvenience, but they're important enough that you won't forget that they exist. Progress is VERY slow and takes some patience, so find something to occupy your time with. I recommend the dig site, talking to everyone in town, and fishing. Fishing can feel like a drag because it's slow and the fish don't get you a lot of money if you sell them, but if you keep most of what you catch they're great for substitutes in recipes that require a fish in them. Anyway, I apologize if my review seemed very rant-like, haha. If you do buy the game, I hope you enjoy, and if you decide not to because of my review, but still are looking for a farm type game, I would suggest you check out stardew valley (an all time favorite of mine) or roots of pacha (love this game! got it last week, it's extremely fun and has an immersive plot-line).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great for the nostalgia, though I can't really say I enjoyed most of the changes. Lemme explain:While I'm an impatient person who likes to speed things up, this remake is a little TOO sped up. Each season is only 10 days, which means 40 days a year. You can quite literally finish a whole year in 1 real time day. Not only that, but you can easily upgrade things without trying, all you need is money. No blacksmith, no mines (it's just a digging site that's not always open), also NO CLINIC? HOW DO THE RESIDENTS SURVIVE? THEY JUST DIE WHEN THEY ARE SICK? Also, they added a feature that allows you to travel to another area, which takes 6 whole hours away IIRC, only to get a black screen saying it was a nice trip, you don't get to actually go there. Not really a fan of the game controls either.As for the good, I do like the visuals and how time actually passes and we get older. Although it was a big part of what made the old games special, not having annoying weeds, logs and rocks on the field is a nice change. Also, we can FINALLY water the middle crop, it drove me crazy back when I played the original, best change IMO. I like how you can give residents multiple gifts per day, makes befriending and romancing them much easier. I miss the Harvest Goddess though, wished we could romance her here too but it makes sense why they didn't add that in as you have to get married in the first year. But I'm glad they make you marry in the first year, I romanced Matthew and immediately proposed to him out of pure spite after seeing a cutscene of him talking about his feelings for Cecilia (YOU'RE MINE, MATTHEW.)All in all, I do find the game relaxing and comfy, it reminds me quite a bit of the original and I'm happy to see the characters again.

The graphics are so cute, it brings more colour and life to the game, though there are some differing art styles that are noticeable in the game. The systems and mechanics hearken back to a more simple time in the farming sim genre with new quality of life features that make it easier to re-experience. The remake is beautifully redone and truly gives you the same "feels" that the original did all those years ago. This is a more life sim focused farming game compared to many of the others out there and even some within the Story of Seasons/Harvest Moon franchise. All the usual farming sim features are there but expect progression to feel a bit different in this one (which I personally feel like it makes it stand out from the rest of the pack in a good way). As a caveat though, if you really want your farming sim to be all about crafting out the layout of your farm and hurried schedules of this, then that, then this, and rinse and repeat it may feel underwhelming to you. This one encourages you to make friends with the towns folk more, get married, and not live like a hermit the first few years until you've "made it" like most farming sims cause us to want to do.All in all from the perspective of playing the original and wanting to experience Forget-me-not Valley once again this is a for sure recommend.If you come from the newer age of farming sims expect something different than what you have been used to. It's not necessarily a bad thing but maybe check out a video review or two and see how it makes you feel on it. Although beware as there are a lot of sites seemingly have reviewers that are either not fans of the genre or never played the original. It's worth a try if your curious and kinda want something a bit different from the modern farm sim.

It is disappointing, although now I just tend to think of her as Aro-Ace representation in game. 2. The movement feels a little slippery. Im not a fan of losing a couple hours if you pass out, though I understand why its there. 4. The rise in prices of things in game from the original feels a bit...steep. _childDocuments_.review: I have played a lot of Harvest Moon games, but never got to experience the PS2/Gamecube titles. Though the original crusty PS2 aesthetic of this game is gone, it still feels like a game straight from that era in the best ways possible. It's a very charming entry in the series and I can see why it has a cult following. There are some bugs and optimization issues, but it is otherwise a good PC port. I am playing it on steam deck and can confirm it runs fine. It's a simple entry, even more so than Friends of Mineral Town, but it is still worth it.Edit: So I nearly got 100% in almost 90 hours of playtime. My final verdict for this game is that it is simply the best Story of Seasons game I have played. It does become repetitive around chapter 4 or so but that is about the time I decided to attempt getting all the achievements that I could. The whole thing with you and the villagers aging and watching your child grow really added a depth to the game that I have not seen in other SoS/Harvest Moon games I have played. Though the writing was minimal overall, there were a lot of really charming and emotional scenes scattered throughout that made me care for my little virtual family. I loved the character interactions and personalities a lot in this. I really, really hope they are able to bring these mechanics back in a future title and flesh all of this stuff out more. I absolutely adored this game.

I have no gripe with any of the changes made to the game and completely understand/appreciate those changes. The developers seem to be very transparent on these changes and if you find yourself upset about any alterations to the original, perhaps if you hear them out in the developer log you will be more understanding. On a side note, I watched a youtuber play the Japanese release of this game, (joshplays) and I feel as if he sold this game short. He did not nearly touch on the quality of certain things that I find in my playthrough, so I should definitely recommend people to try the game themselves and be careful not to buy into other peoples lackluster experience. I can guarantee anyone who played the original and has stayed true enough to their inner child, will thoroughly enjoy this game. As for newcomers to the series, I will endorse this game and have you know that this was basically the Life Sim Genre progenitor, so throw some respect on its name.

_childDocuments_.review: Does it have minor issues yes, but just one; the game launches in Japanese. This isn't a major problem as some make it out to be it just takes a little work which I thought pc players were all for and not afraid of.  After hitting play, choose the launch configuration tool. The first tab at the bottom is language, set it to your language, English French, etc, and save and exit. The game is now in your language. The game isn’t a 1:1 remaster it's a remake, and beautifully done, it's been made new generation kid friendly where animals don't die (like every other new SOS game) which again isn’t an issue, you still have to take care of your animals. Graphics are great and frames at least for me and a few others sit at a steady 60 fps, and let's be honest; You don't need higher than that for this type of game. As someone who grew up on the original HM games of the 90s and 2ks, before marvelous ended their relationship with Natsume and Natsume ruined the HM name. This is the game you want. P.S. i suggest using a controller to play as this game was meant to be played using kb&m for entering names only. until more optimizing comes through (if any) it apparently is difficult to use a KB&M

_childDocuments_.review: A port that delivers on all counts - thank you so much! chapter system covering around 30 years, well-paced story about raising a childfun hybrid crops to make lovely, warm, quirky characters changes to characters over the years changing seasons, nice romantic festivalsnice special wedding scenefishing, dig site, exploration, collecting wonderfuls it’s just enough to do to make things interesting, the type of game you enjoy spending time in and want to create a new character immediately after you finish I missed Forgotten Valley. Glad to have it on PC and it has all the charm, with a few good changes from the original versions. Another Wonderful Life has always been one of my most favourite HM games.  This release preserves that. The game pulls together every feature from AWL, ANWL and the Special and makes a lovely work of it.It’s one of the better paced HM games: has a plot spanning 30 years, divided into chapters, seasons are 10 days long but there is plenty to do to keep you going, like making fun hybrid plants and crop mutations – including blue varieties as well as 2nd and 3rd generation cross-breeds. Get sheep for good gold. The cast of colourful and heart-warming characters makes this one of my go-to HM games and am really glad it got ported and remade. It keeps the feeling I always loved about the original games.  One of the standout features of this game is that as years go by – the characters change, age. It keeps the feeling that time flows, unlike in many similar titles. The core thing here is to raise a child  and go through the hoops of them growing up – so if you don’t marry by the end of chapter 1, it’s game over.  You can propose earlier but I like waiting until the guy comes over and asks – it’s a form of reverse proposal I always liked in HM games – so yes, there is one and it’s worth waiting for it on 10 Winter, but make sure to raise those hearts. On the other hand, if you do wait for the reverse proposal, you will miss out on an extra (and lovely) engagement event that happens after you propose, so choose.  You can marry any gender, of course. They also kept rival events from original games. That was always fun.  This release has been adapted and uses three genders properly – they aren’t a gimmick. They work, so I am consistently referred to as a she. You can be a they, if you want. It also makes slight but welcome  changes to the original games, including graphical upgrades, and some changes to marriage candidates.  It adds the artist Gordy as a bachelor (he was previously known as Cody). Gordy’s heart events are just as fun as those of other characters, and introduce his artistic process.  Exploration,  working at the archeological dig, fishing – everything is fun and very relaxed and charming in Forgotten Valley.  In essence  this is the Harvest Moon I love and remember and am enjoying it in the ported version very much so.This game is nearly everything I loved avbout HM games – everything Olive Town nearly ruined for me. I’m glad to be back in Forgotten Valley. This game is definitely the kind of Story of Seasons I want to have and a meeting with an old friend. Comforting and nice to play, heart-warming.  A fine addition to my favourites. Puts a smile on my face. I’m really grateful for this release. And hope to see Animal Parade one day too – the second of my most favourite HM games.  The third and last were SOS and Trio of Towns.  But A Wonderful life was always a stand-out HM game because it has this wholesome, warm feeling about  it, a different storyline that is well-paced and fun to play. Has a heart.Precisely my kind of game, because I seek games with a heart. This is one of them

_childDocuments_.review:
Your new life begins in Forgotten Valley, a tranquil community where your father and his friend Takakura once dreamed of running a farm. As you befriend the valley's residents and fulfill your father's legacy, you'll live a carefree life on the farm growing crops and raising animals. As the seasons go by, you'll find your lifelong partner, raise a child together, and watch them grow up before your very eyes.

This remake of a beloved classic features plenty of new events, enhanced festivals, more recipes to cook, and a cornucopia of never-before-seen crops. Looking for more to do around the farm? Take pictures of your family with the new camera feature, dress up in your favorite outfits, or help your fellow residents with their requests.

Whether this is your first STORY OF SEASONS adventure or you're returning to Forgotten Valley, a wonderful life awaits you.
